name: National Underground
text:
To put it as nicely as I can, everything about this meal and experience was sub par. I once stopped here for a drink on the Pedal Tavern and remember seeing a sign that boasted "best burger in Nashville!" After ordering the cheeseburger, I realized that statement was about as true as the stuff you read on Wikipedia. It was a bland burger, nothing more and nothing less. The fries were good, though. 

The service, to also put it nicely, was pretty bad. When my brother and I walked in, we didn't know if we were supposed to seat ourselves or order at the bar. So, for about 5 minutes we waited at the bar, where there were only 3 or 4 other customers, and finally the bartender came over to take our order. My brother and I, we're pretty friendly, non-pushy people. But the bartender seemed put out by every request we made. I don't think she cracked a smile the entire time we were there.

One last complaint and I swear I'll be done...I asked for a cup of water and then the bartender brought me a bottled water and charged me $2. I asked her if I could get a cup of tap water but she said they only had bottled water. Since when do restaurants literally FORCE you to pay for water?

To sum it up, save your money and appetite for somewhere with better service and better food.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I drink TN Brew Works regularly at local spots all over town. I have a real sweet spot for their ESB-- SO GOOD. Anyway my husband's mother was in town and we decided to finally check out the TN Brew Works Taproom. The location seems a little off the map but once you arrive there are no worries. The taproom was busy but we still got front row parking. The space is really beautiful and has a lot of different nooks and crannies so even when busy you don't feel like you are in a crowded loud restaurant. We sat upstairs because we saw a band setting up downstairs and wanted to be able to hear each other. Once the band started I was so impressed with the sound level. It was very pleasant and traveled all over the building without being too loud or annoying at all. It was so nice. 

Definitely, travel down to Ewing and try this place out. Perfect place to drink beer!

name: Ole Red
text: I enjoyed the entertainment and the food. Our waitress was excellent. I felt sorry for her, she had to walk so far. I don't think the restaurant is setup in mind of the servers.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Great, large portions of food with live music.  Margaritaville is a fun, beachy place with food ranging from fish tacos ($17) to burgers ($16.)  The music is good if  a bit loud.  Service was excellent.  You can people watch from the window tables and they angle to let in a nice breeze.  Lunch is a bit high, but that may be the area pricing as well.  Live music pours from all of the establishments along Broadway.  Nice lunch place!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Best music on Broadway, in my opinion -- you won't hear classic rock covers here!

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
This was one of our more memorable experience, date night for hubby and I.
Star Wars New Hope with symphony was awesome.Watching the movie and the Orchestra at the same time was so cool. If you enjoy these type of performances this is very good. The Orchestra was great, sounds were right on point,beautiful arrangement. The art of music and film was amazing to watch. Thank you Nashville Symphony 
We will return.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Came in on a Wednesday for 2-for-1. Not a lot of variety of beer which is why I gave them 4 stars. 

They had a live band which was over by the time we arrived about and hour before closing.

Parking can be difficult if your coming on a busier night. Other than that i will definitely be coming again. Great beers!!!!

name: National Underground
text: Rude, surly, and unhelpful! Service was not just slow, it was HOSTILE. These people act like you are crashing a private party at their home! Not only did they not apologize for fucking up my order, they acted like I should apologize for asking them to fix it. I spend plenty of time in dive bars with "relaxed" service. But these people were not "relaxed," they were pissed at customers for being there. No wonder we were some of the only people there on a Friday night. Plus, the bathrooms are nasty (even for a bar) and the whole place REEKS of old beer. I could get better food and service at a Quick Trip, and Quick Trip will give you FREE WATER.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Hitting the Town? Start with something at Bridgestone Arena if an event is happening like hockey. This arena is actually really nice with a lot of great restaurants and drink choices inside at reasonable stadium prices. There is actually a bar called the Patron Platinum Club that is open to the public but, a lot of people don't realize it is accessible for everyone. What I really like about this arena is that it is literally next door to all the action on Broadway and is perfect for drunkenly stumbling starting your night on the town. Plus if you are going to a hockey game the Predators are actually pretty decent and puck bunnies are always hot.

name: Nashville Symphony
text: A beautiful space that sometimes offers unique experiences. I went to see a screening of Casablanca where the orchestra performed the soundtrack live! It was incredible.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I'm really impressed with Bridgestone Arena and I like it a lot more than the YUM! Center that's here in Louisville. It's a huge venue with tons of options for beer, liquor, food and vendor souvenir shops. I came here to see the one and only Stevie Nicks, we didn't have floor seats because they were too expensive, but the seats we did have were close enough that we could see, get good pics and good video as well. 

The sound inside of the arena was loud and the acoustics were amazing. It was the escape from real life that I craved and not only did I lose my cherry to seeing one of my idols that night, but also my voice screaming (just ask Scott XD). 

The food smelled great, but we knew better than to get food at an arena because of the up sell on it, instead we had a few drinks. Honestly the beer prices weren't bad, I spent too much money, but for a 16oz craft beer from draft it was $11 and for a 25oz domestic canned beer it was also $11. All the bartenders were very knowledgeable about the products and spirits. Scott didn't think that his cocktails were worth it because we like ours strong, though. At $20 for a double is about the average for any sort of concert venue. The whole staff was extremely friendly and helpful in whatever questions we had when getting drinks, walking around or getting back to our seats. 

One of the major pluses to Bridgestone Arena is that they have a section for smokers & people who just want some fresh air to go outside and be able to re-enter at. This was excellent because between The Pretenders and Stevie Nicks there was about a 20 minute intermission that would have just been boring to sit through, so we were able to get a drink each and enjoy a cancer stick outside. 

Overall I would LOVE to see another one of my idols at Bridgestone Arena again, and soon because we weren't able to explore Nashville too much due to the next day being election day (gotta do my civic duty!), but I'm all. The. Way. Down. I'm blown away (tire pun intended) by this arena and you will be too!

name: Marathon Music Works
text: We arrived before doors opened for a show and the venue bar had BOGO draft beers which was awesome. They have quick bar service and a taco stand inside in case you need a bite to eat. We went to a pretty chill show but a small group of people decided this was a punk/mosh pit kind of show. They were moshing around, throwing beer on people, falling down, etc. Security was nowhere to be found. I tried talking to security and they were not interested in hearing from patrons.  Pretty disappointing after we traveled 3 hours to attend. Aside from the vibe, the sound, service, and bars were good.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: First time here, was pretty pleased. We had a group of 7, but didn't have to wait long for a table, staff very friendly. I got a chicken Caesar salad that was delicious, and more than enough! I went with our waiters suggestion of some Margherita w/o sour mix and some citrus flavor...it wasn't all that great, could've stuck with a regular and been happy. Also, two of our party's food came out late, so they comped their orders! Very accommodating and not many complaints for a chain restaurant.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We ate here on Mother's Day. (Party of 5 plus one munchkin) The restaurant was not busy by any means however our food took approx. an HOUR to arrive at our table after placing our orders. Other patrons dined and exited as we waited for our meals.  When our food finally arrived it did not include my meal. My family graciously waited until I received my food (Cuban sandwich which was very tasty, btw) before they ate and by then all of their meals were cold. Our waiter was very apologetic and swore up and down that he turned in my order with the others and blamed it on the kitchen. My sandwich ended up being comped which I felt was fair. However I was really worried about the fact that we had parked in a pay by the hour parking lot since we waited so long for our food to arrive. When we were finished with our meal we headed to the parking lot only t o find a $40.00 parking ticket. I returned to the restaurant and asked the manager if he would be so kind as to help me out with it since we had waited exceedingly long for our meals. He said there was nothing he could do and compared it to me expecting him to pay for a speeding ticket?! Thank you Margaritaville Nashville for making my Mother's Day one to remember.

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
My boyfriend and I did date night at the symphony last night. It was a wonderful experience. We sat in the Founders Circle and had a great view of the symphony and the movie screen [Home Alone]. The Symphony orchestra and chorus were amazing and the building is beautiful. 

The staff, ushers, and volunteers were all very friendly and helpful. 

There were several bars throughout the venue and the prices weren't too extreme and were affordable. 

It was wonderful that there is a variety of opportunities in which all can experience the symphony and is a highly recommended venue.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
The Bridgestone Arena is where the Preds play, big name concerts are held and I'm sure the occasional Monster Truck rally. But the review is really about the fans rated number one by ESPN. While I am not sure of the formula the "mother ship" used, I'm pretty sure they got it right.
Everyone seems to be dressed in team colors, the anthem is often sung by some recording star, a veteran is recognized for their service all before the puck drops.
The fans taunt the opposing goalie with a verse that questions his ability. Loud music is played when the Preds need a lift. Live bands play between periods. It must all work as they often have the best home record in hockey.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: This is very laid back, relaxed and fun spot for a Nashville show. The sound quality isn't the very best, and it can be down right bad depending on where you're standing. And it's all standing, which is sometimes tough for this old broad. I love the new little attached bar though - great place to relax, chat, and yes I'm old, sit before a show. Good prices and I like the mobile ticketing through ticketfly.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: My husband and I went here on a whim after brunch for Valentine's Day. We had the beer and chocolate pairing flight- it was oh so good! My husband LOVED their IPA and Extra Easy, I enjoyed their Southern Witt. The people working their were very nice and helpful. I would recommend this place for a first date or date night out, regardless of age!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Layla's is one cool dive bar with kickass live music. It's two stories, and the second floor has a great view of the stage but if you want the music to kiss your face than sit up front. Service was great too as both the bartender (who sang a song with the band) and the wait staff made sure your drinks were always full. There's plenty of options around the vicinity but Layla's knows how to take care of its patrons.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: In typical Margaritaville fashion,  this place won't let you down. Food is delicious and our bartender,  Noelle is a sweetheart and was a great Nashville ambassador to tourists like us.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
As breweries go, this place is well set up. Great porch and a nice interior with views of the brewing area.  The music is good to listen to in some spots, but in others (like parts of the upstairs) the sound can get a little distorted. 

Beers are passable and there's generally a decent selection.  They're not going to win any major awards but by Nashville standards they at least brew clean beers.  Thankfully they don't offer a bakers dozen of "IPAs" and have some imagination when it comes to their recipes.  That said, I'd stick to their more hoppy beers and maybe their dark beers. Their more lightly hopped beers are their most drab, and I suspect the pressurized mash filter system they use is primarily to blame--it literally wrings out all the sugars from the grain thereby allowing them to use less grain per batch of beer (so malt *flavor* is lacking). 

So 4.0 stars for the brewery venue, 3.0 stars for their beers..

name: National Underground
text: Expected a larger burger for $11. Seasoned very well. Staff was friendly. I ordered a Sex on the Beach and the bartender faked her way through. Pretended she knew how to make one but it was no where close. LOL! Still good, but a totally different drink from what I ordered. Back to the burger...tasty, but not an $11 burger.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I absolutely love stopping in here for a quick drink and socializing with friends and family. A friend kept mentioning events hosted here and I first visited with family from out of town. The layout is friendly for group outtings. The brewery floor is appealing with areas for guest to view the process without a formal tour. I have become hooked on there Kombucha. As a beer lover it's weird to say that I truly get excited about this place for their Kombucha, it's such a niche in Nashville. They're the only brewery that offers an alternative non-alcoholic beverage adding to the appeal. 
I have yet to try the menu but it's intriguing and unique. Offering a wide array and providing beer lovers a reason to stick around. I could see this as a great date spot for beer and food enthusiasts like me.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: I've been here twice, it is much bigger than I expected. It wasn't too crowded when I went. I will go back if there is a show I want to see.

name: Ole Red
text:
Not bad but not great. We arrived around 6 and went to the roof top. We were wanting a table outside and the waitress was pretty rude about letting us know where we could not sit. Funny thing is that when we left an hour later it was still empty. Not a great start Blake. Let's break it down:

Atmosphere 3 stars - nothing special about the interior or rooftop. The downstairs area has a nice stage but the entire restaurant has a commercial feel to it. I considered it average for Broadway. 

Service 4 Stars - our waitress was very pleasant. She was helpful and attentive. No issue here. 

Food 4 stars - it's bar food but pretty darn good. I consider it above average. I had the trio sliders. The pork was very tasty, the bologna sandwich (yes they still make these) a we really good and clever. Lastly, the hamburger was solid. My wife had the pimento cheese wrapped in mozzarella. Really well done. 

Value 3 Stars - for basically two appetizers and four beers we left with a $60 bill. Alittle high for what you get but considering it is in the heart of broadway, probably pretty typical. 

All in all, it was ok. I would give it 3.5 but yelp won't allow me to do that. It's definitely slightly above average and I would come back.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: So yummy! Great atmosphere. Valerie was the best! So helpful and attentive. Made the experience so much better!!!

name: The Night Owl
text: Surprise of the year! Big time diamond in the rough. Had the special meatball sub and fries with their special sauce, then we played ping pong and drank. Great time, music was loud bring ear plugs. Employees super cool

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: I assume this is a classic honky-tonk dive. I chose this place because the sign out front said "Nashville Hillbilly Music". The music was great - solid musicians, pretty broad repertoire for requests, and the sound was great. even from way in the back we had an okay view.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: There was a 45 min wait when we got there, but we were seated quicker than that. My first margarita was say too sour and not good at all, which is disappointing considering it was Margaritaville. The 2nd margarita, a more expensive one, was better. The food was good and I love the atmosphere. Our waitress was very nice and friendly. I'd go again.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Had a great time with my group at Margaritaville! Fun for everyone - drinks and food to serve all tastes and ages. Thank you so much Valerie for your amazing service and tips. Yum! 

Edit: 
We were told they let lunch goers into the Friday show but this is not true. Just a heads up before you plan to dine before the show... better to just wait in line and dine upstairs at 2 when they open it up

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Not a half bad neighborhood bar. The patio was pretty nice, drinks were just alright though. Tables were hard to come by.

name: UV Nightclub
text: Terrible. Do not go here. $10 cover to see a bunch of ghetto thugs show each other their guns. The 10 cops always outside is your first clue.  If all you want to do is dance and have a few drinks-there are plenty of other cool places on broadway.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Family friendly place on Broadway.  Those traveling with people under 21 will know that it can be difficult to find a place to eat in the downtown Broadway area, especially the later it gets.  While we would have preferred a local non-chain restaurant, we opted for Margaritaville and had a good experience.  The place was crowded, but the wait wasn't too long and there was a pretty good live band playing, which added to the Nashville atmosphere we were hoping for.  The food was decent and service was good.  The server accommodated our vegetarians and made sure their orders were adjusted to accommodate their needs.

name: Ole Red
text: Enjoyable atmosphere, good music/musicians, & a super sweet waitress made this place enjoyable. I was really hoping I would love this place but the menu is limited and our food wasn't great. We got the fried pickles as an appetizer and the Nashville Hot Chicken & biscuit with Fries and tator-tots for dinner. The biscuit buns were great, I actually think I would've enjoyed them alone with butter and jelly more than I did on the sandwich. The chicken was hard to chew and not very spicy. The French fries were nothing to write home about but the tarot-tots were great! They're homemade and much better than the boring steak fries. The fried pickles were good, large portion so easy to share with a group of 5-6! Overall just an ok experience, I'd probably pick a different place next time to get the real honky-Tonk Nashville vibes.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Started off badly when the hostess wanted to seat the two (my mom and i) of us across from the kitchen when the entire establishment was 1/3 full. I objected and we were placed in a better spot. we both ordered the fried chicken. Chicken tasty and lots of it. Could have used more gravy. Server nice and attentive.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
We went to the Bridgestone Arena for the first time for the Womens Basketball Final Four Championship. We actually loved the experience. People couldn't have been nicer. All the employees were so very helpful, friendly and efficient in the job they were doing.
I realized I had lost my camera about 5 minutes after entering the premises. We immediately went to the information counter to find out what I needed to do. My camera was already sitting on the lost and found shelf! Unbelievablel!There was an  estimated 17,000 people in the arena at that time. Some one found my camera and immediately turned it in. Could hardly believe this happened in barely 10 minutes. Grateful.
I love Nashville. 
UCONN ROCKS.....

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
The atmosphere of the restaurant is wonderful! The service has always been up to par when I dine here. The wait is acceptable for an average dinner time, so long as Nashville isn't hosting a special event. 

The drinks are delicious, but can be light on the alcohol at times. The food, although delicious, seems pricey for the portion size. I could get a larger burger at Cheddars or even Applebee's. It seems you pay more for the ambiance of the restaurant than you do the food.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Five stars for her best waitress in the history of waitresses. Food was good, but what really made it was Amy. If you come to margaritaville and don't get Amy, you're missing the hell out. Funny, good person, and real Nashville treat. We were here as a bachelorette and she played along with all our dumb antics. 10/10 would recommend.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Awesome!!! Walked by and heard a great band playing so we went inside. Beth Garner Band was absolutely rocking it!!! Great vibe and a lot of history, if you are in Nashville it is a must see!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: This place ROCKS!!! As a "non-beer" drinker, I was less than enthusiastic to follow my beer snob husband here on our trip to Nashville.  I was WRONG!   The knowledgable staff led me in the direction of several beers that even the non-beer girl could enjoy!  My beer snob husband looked like he had died and gone to heaven! While the beer was obviously a religious experience (from the look on my husband's face), the food is what stole the show for the non-beer chick.  The burger was the best thing I've eaten in a long time and put all other burgers to shame.  I don't know what they are putting in it.. But evidently there are 5 different beers making up various components of the burger.. And the experience was enough to have me racing to book my next trip to Nashville!! A must stop on any Nashville tour!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Stopped here on a Wednesday night when they have a 2-for-1 draft beer deal. Every beer I tried was excellent but the Basil Ryeman was my favorite and one of the best beers I've had. My boyfriend really liked the Tennessee No. 12 Quad. Both were so good that we came back the next day to get some to take home.

All of the staff here was also wonderful. They are so knowledgeable about the beer and made great recommendations. They offered samples of beer they thought we would like.

I would come back here if we're in Nashville again, even without the 2-for-1 deal.

name: Ole Red
text: Amazingly decadent food. I know this sounds crazy but the bologna sandwich is to die for. The chef has it custom made from his own recipe and has nothing to do with Oscar Meyer. The tater tots are crazy good. And anything with the smoked chicken is super good. And the love music is phenomenal. My biggest criticism is that there is no NY location.

name: Marathon Music Works
text:
I recently visited from Michigan to see Clutch in concert at this venue. I found this to be a pretty good venue to see a concert. It's basically a converted warehouse in an old industrial district. There is ample street parking near the venue and we had no trouble finding a spot. 

Security was fairly thorough, but also reasonably chill. We did get to the venue on the early side (the doors typically open about an hour before the concert starts.)  They do have a coat-check, but I left mine in the car so I wouldn't have to bother with it. There is a fairly large bar in the entrance area so you have have a drink while you wait for the main area to open. You can either get a general admission ticket or you can pay a bit more to get a seat in the "Lux Loft", which is a raised area on the side of the stage. It has a good view as well as a separate, private bar and bathroom area. On the main floor, there are two general bar areas and the public restrooms (which have bathroom attendants...) There is also a taco stand that basically sells tacos or nachos (chicken or veggie.) The tacos were not too bad, although one of the taco stand employees was pretty rude (she seemed irritated to be working that night.)

The concert experience was not bad, but I felt they were a little heavy-handed with the smoke machine. Also, the acoustics were not the best despite them turning the volume up to 11 -  and you know there's an issue when you can barely hear Neil Fallon's vocals, since that guy's a vocal powerhouse. The security had to break up one little scuffle on the main floor, but it was resolved efficiently. All in all, it was a really enjoyable night and I would definitely see another concert here.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Good place. Food is good, drinks are real good. Entertainment is great. Huge place gets very crowded sometimes but lots of fun.

name: Ole Red
text: Love Blake Shelton and Nashville but this stop was a disappointment.  Started on the roof and had some ok service and an appetizer.  Then moved to main dining room. Food was sub-par, stick with beer as mixed drinks were very weak. The service not even close to the Nashville standard.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I loved the concert and the arena but won't recommend the Lexus lounge.  It was crap.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Layla was the bartender upstairs and I cannot rave about her enough!!! She was fabulous! My mother and two aunts were with her having a "great time" enjoying themselves at the bar and she did such an excellent job taking care of them, making sure to give them water in between in order for them to pace themselves.  One of my aunts is blind and she watched out for her even making sure to lead them through the restaurant when it was time to leave!  I was so impressed by her patience and caring for them.  Thank you so much!!!!

name: Ole Red
text: Fun and Classy!  Food, music and service were excellent.   I love that reservations are available. This is definetly a great addition to Broadway, not your typical Honky Tonk and I appreciate that very much! I am a local and I will definetly be bringing all of our out of town guests to Ole Red, this will be my go to place on Broadway!

name: Ole Red
text: A great place to visit when your in nashville. Great live music with excellent servers and bartenders. The roof top has a great scenic view of downtown Nashville. We had tacos with chips and salsa. All of the food was awesome with really good sizeable portions. A really great place to go if you love country music.

name: Ole Red
text: WE want to like this place.  We really do because we like Blake and his music but... sterile, slick, unimaginative.  These are the words we used. I think this was my biggest disappointing place we went this weekend. We wanted an Oklahoma honkytonk not what this is. It might make money but we will go elsewhere to have fun. Please if anyone in charge reads this ... go to your roots not what this is now.  We did not eat here so we can't review that. We came 3 times in a 5 day weekend and felt the same way Thursday through Sunday.

name: Ole Red
text: First time in Nashville, was so disappointed at Ole Reds, I'm a Blake Shelton fan but his bar was a horrible experience. Drinks were more expensive, restaurant and bar smelled really bad. Tables were a mess.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Terrible, tiny plate for $17. Not to mention the chicken tenders were so oily I felt sick after . Not coming back.

name: Ole Red
text: The atmosphere is great but we were there when the band was not great! The pickles were awesome but rest of food just average or below average. Of high importance..... only one women's bathroom stall had toilet paper! Good luck to you all!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Margaritaville is nice, but homeless people walk in there. One came right up to my table and accosted me. I got out of there so fast. I wanted to buy a Margaritaville blender, but not any more.

name: The High Watt
text: I really enjoyed seeing Alan Rayman here on 11/29/17. The atmosphere for this small venue was perfect. I also was surprised at the price of beer, $3 for Yuengling Tall Cans! The sound was surprisingly good for a venue of it's size, I was afraid the acoustics would be disappointing. My only criticism is the lack of cooling fans and in the areas where seating was available it was kind of uncomfortable (more of a personal thing..big dude struggles). Overall I would highly recommend The High Watt to anyone and I'll definitely be back.

name: Ole Red
text: Great service!!  Our server was Nira and she is fantastic!!!  We had a party of 10 and she took care of us wonderfully, she was friendly, funny, and helpful.  The food is tasty, the tater tots are yum!!  My kids devoured their lunches as well as the rest of the table.  Live music and the overall ambience is really nice.  Highly recommend Blake Sheltons restaurant on Broadway!!

name: Ole Red
text: The place is nice, the owner is famous and the long lines will make you wander what is going on and you'll NEED to check it out! Stayed in line outside for almost 2 hours, like everyone else who didn't give up. I figured we don't need a table, we'd be fine with seats at the bar or whaterver, so I went and asked at the door, and a security guy said No, this is the only way to get in. Well, almost 2 hours later we get in and the host said there are no more seats in the restaurant, unless we have your name down. What name, why did we stay 2 hours in line? They didn't know about the line outside, like we were in a different world. They almost kicked us out so we went up the stairs to find SOMETHING, and we ended up the Lookout rooftop, which was almost empty, and even had a guy with a guitar playing some nice songs. So we reluctantly asked if we an seat, and they were like Yes, everything is open! Holy crap, why did we wait almost 2 hrs in line when you have empty tables here? (the guys up here didn't know about the line outside either!) Great views from the top and the food was delicious! The funny name nachos made it to Instagram instantly and had everyone around come and take pictures too, they look amazing! Same for the Tiramisu dessert! Too bad that this place is so poorly organized and so unfriendly (told the same security guy on the way out that I came at the door and asked you of other options and no one mentioned the Skylounge, his answer was Go somewhere else if you don't like it). So go to the door and insist that you want to eat or go upstairs, the line is most likely for a Spotify event, don't fall for it. Or go somewhere else.

name: Ole Red
text: Went tonight. The music was great as was ambience. BUT... The food and drink were absolutely awful! We only ordered beer which was skunky ( waitress replaced) and worst nachos ever!! Kettle chips with god awful toppings! Makes we three who went there sick thinking about I! Had sickeningly  sweet bbq  sauce on it, slimy cheese sauce on the bottom that didnt  taste like cheese, some kind of COLD meat on it.. chicken? And guacamole which was ok. I have never had a bad nacho before today! Blake , please fix it!!!!  Dont put on bbq sauce ,make the meat on top hot, put real sharp cheese in it etc. Also we ordered the biscuits which were also awful! And where was the honey to put on them??? Terrible food. Next time we will eat first and order water or a coke . We love Blake Shelton but he needs to know those Two dishes are awful!

name: Ole Red
text: One of my favorite bars on broadway! Came here multiple times on my trip! The bar/restaurant is so spacious, it is 5 floors! The singer/band was always great! I love how everything is dog based obviously because it's called "ole red." The fried pickles were good and you get so many, a whole bucket! The burgers were also very very tasty and good! My boyfriend got a beer and I ended up with a "some beach" which I order two more of after my first! This drink was soo good!!! Definitely have to go here when on Broadway!

name: Ole Red
text:
This is a great spot on Broadway for both food and live music. The musicians are pretty talented and play a variety of music. Occasionally Blake Shelton sings on stage too. 

Service is decent for a busy place! And people watching is a blast.

name: Ole Red
text: Cudos to Blake!   Love Ole Red.  Salads, Hash Browns, quiche and one pound cinnamon bun for brunch were the best we ever had.  The jumbo pretzels!! Omg. Had three during a weekend stay. The drinks were the best on the strip.  The roof top bar was beautiful and as comfortable as your living room. Love love love ole red.

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
This is a very beautiful music hall that you need to experience for once if you are ever in Nashville for a visit. I have been to the Nashville Symphony twice: one trip in 12/2017 and one trip in 11/2018. The hall is always decked out beautifully during the holiday season. The sounds are amazing, and the musicians are just amazing with their skills. 

You know you will always get great experience with Nashville because of the Music City's reputation. I have not been disappointed to both events that I attended: Dave Barnes's Very Merry Christmas in 2017 and Martina McBride's White Christmas Concert in 2018. Both performances were excellent and made me felt so excited each time I entered the Symphony Hall. 

Thank YOU, Nashville Symphony. You will be always on my list to attend musical events whenever I am in Nashville, TN!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: First visit here. I was impressed with how clean it was! FYI- There's a mothers' lounge on the second level between sections 210-212. It was very clean with 3 gliders, a changing station, sink, etc. Great place to nurse my baby during a basketball game!

name: National Underground
text:
I wanted to like this place. I really did. It boasts its little reputation of being owned by a famous musician, being a hotspot for local artists, etc., which certainly makes it appealing. But, I will never eat here again. I ordered the buffalo chicken sandwich, which was possibly the saddest, puniest cut of chicken I've ever seen, complete with less-than-fresh greens on the bun. Also included LESS than a handful of kettle chips. For 11 bucks? Are you kidding me? Service was completely sub par. I somehow got roped into getting a bottle of water - I guess I misunderstood over the loud music. Where am I, a sporting event? NIX the stupid bottle, and give me a glass. Its a restaurant for crying out loud. But more importantly, I never once was asked a) how my food was or b) if I needed more water, or ANYthing else for that matter. And there were about 8 people in this entire joint (should have taken the hint). You can make up for crap food with good service, but unfortunately both were crap here.
            Now, maybe I made the mistake of ordering a chicken sandwich at a place known for their burgers (or so they say on their sign), but still, this was featured pretty high up on the menu, and that's what I wanted. So if that was terrible as it was, how good can the rest of the menu really be? Nashville is a haven for good food, with a multitude of options. So, go ahead and skip this joke of a restaurant if you find yourself downtown. 

Cheers! :)

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The place is a joke. 6.50 for  Coors Light. 12.50 for a watered down lousy margarita. Don't forget the overpriced 15.50 no taste nachos. This place is strictly for tourist with no brain who will spend 30.00 on a t-shirt.

name: National Underground
text:
My office is downtown and I am lucky enough to only visit once a week. On that day as many of my team try to go out for lunch together as possible. So there are usually 3-6 people. This past week we decided to try this place out as many of us had not been there. 6 of us in this group and we went a tick early (11:30).

Service: Slow, I think the girl working was the only one working the front of the house.

The menu is only in chalk on the wall, great if you are facing the wall when you sit down. Seriously get more menus or make it easier to see. 

It is $2, that is right TWO DOLLARS for water. They won't bring you tap water you have to buy a bottle. Mixed drinks at lunch are $8, EIGHT FREAKING DOLLARS for a drink at lunch on a Tuesday. Tea, coke products and the like are $2 and you get refills. 

I ordered a cheese burger, medium rare no bun. I got a fairly decently cooked burger with what looked like an American cheese slice on it. I don't mind paying $11 for a burger but seriously this one wasn't worth it. ALL sandwiches come with a small handful of kettle chips (potato chips out of bag). There wasn't a cheese selection, or bread choice etc. There was a stack that contained lettuce, tomato slice, onion and 2 pickles. One person order a side of grilled potatoes and there were maybe 4 slices but she didn't receive her chips with the sandwich. The potatoes are signed as an appetizer so it wasn't fair to not deliver both. Others at the table felt the food was MEH. 

A lot of folks don't like to spend a bunch of money on lunch, which is why they don't like to eat on that block. But let's compare. National Underground burger $11 + water $2 = $13 plus tip. On the same block burger (bourbon glaze, onion straws and Gorgonzola with fries) $10.95 + water $0  = $10.95 plus tip. Hmm better values can be had elsewhere. 

I am sad that more places don't give a hoot about folks that are stuck downtown because they work there. This place is catering/charging for the tourist crowd because they can. But here is  the problem, I won't go back and I won't recommend it to anyone. When I schedule an event for Nashville my blog post will reflect my feelings of how places treat the weekday lunch crowd. Maybe they have a killer happy hour, guess I won't know.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: We were here for the Predators playoff game against Dallas. Our seats were the second to last row up high and were still great seats. There are no bad seats in this arena. The live music between periods was awesome, and Smashville sure loves their team. It was so much fun!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
We had the best time at Tennessee Brew Works yesterday!  We were visiting from Minnesota and greeted warmly by the staff and got some amazing beer right away.  We played a fun round of Taboo while surprisingly listening to some of our favorite tunes (Minnesota's Trampled by Turtles, coincidentally, and Devil Makes Three!). Mine and my other half's favorite selection was the King's Wit. So good. Was also happy to see that it was on tap at Peg Leg Porker down the street later on when we went to get BBQ for dinner!

P.S: The soap in the women's room smells so good. Please never change it.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I absolutely loved this brewery. 

Traveling: 
It's in such a fun and cool location of Nashville that I hadn't been to before. I like that it's slightly off the grid, but it's also not hard to navigate to from the interstate. It's the perfect pit stop.

The BEER:
The beer is fabulous! Their IPA is my favorite. 
You can build your own six (or four) pack and take as much as you need to go! This was perfect for traveling back up north, because I have a lot of beer drinking friends that wanted to try from this specific brewery. I didn't take the tour, but I'm sure it would have been great, as the staff was so friendly and attentive. 

The FOOD: 
Ah-mazing. I haven't tried everything on their menu, but based on the 3 plates that I sampled, I would confidently say that no matter what you get, it's going to be great. 

Overall, the atmosphere is fun, the beer is top notch, the food is great, the staff is friendly, the bathrooms are CLEAN...

the only thing that left me scratching my head walking out the door was.... why didn't they already have some sweet tea brewed? Ha! I expected to fill up on some good sweet tea in my last southern stop going back up north and was surprised when they pulled out the simple syrup to pour in the unsweet tea. Is it just me? Either way. WORTH IT.

Definitely stop by. You'll LOVE this place.

name: 12th & Porter
text:
One star for our gorgeous server at lunch and one for the fried pickles. 

Nothing but derision for the insufferably toxic "manager", whose function, it seemed, was little more than that of a particularly inept doorbitch, with an emphasis on the latter part of the job description. Nowhere in the universe, that's right, even in Nashville, is it acceptable to come stampeding onto a tour bus with manufactured anger over an issue, that if all my years around the music industry have taught me anything, was due to YOUR lack of attention to detail. 

Also, your venomous, unsolicited late night dining options tirade impressed no-one present.
Looks as though my card was ran twice for the privilege, on top of. 

Sorry about whatever the popular girls did in high school to turn you into such a bitter human being, but leave that sh*t at home, it's unprofessional and no-one cares to see it.

name: Ole Red
text: We went on a busy Saturday night and the waiter was so attentive and got the order down perfectly despite the music being so loud (music was great btw). We got appetizers and the portions were big and tasty. The band, Frank Ray, was awesome! They played music from all different genres that kept the crowd on their toes.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Great food. Great service from Josie. It's not cheap, but the quality and quantity make up for it.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Wifie did not want bbq so we landed at margaritaville. It was good but it really did not stand out and impress me. The seating process was really disorganized.  The music was really loud so you could not hear anything. The food was good - I had the seafood jumbeleia  - wifie had seafood mac and cheese  and baby girl had shrimp alfredo. The service was ok - we did not leave wanting to go back but it was not terrible just not memorable.

name: Ole Red
text:
Blake, you missed the mark! If I'm out drinking and eating, I shouldn't be writing this review... 

A bit clinical, sterile and not what I expected after visiting all the other local bars. I appreciate a nice place, but, Ole Red is in between. Servers are too rushed, food and drinks are slow, lighting is too bright and I couldn't wait to leave. I'm sure the roof top is amazing, but I wouldn't know, DJ? Why a DJ?

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Great arena for the game or concert. I have seen Beyoncé and Jack White with Loretta Lynn here. Great location on Broadway and plenty of parking garage around for major events.

name: Ole Red
text:
Unimpressed - My friends and I wanted to visit Ole Red since they are obsessed with Blake Shelton. Here is our story....

We showed up at about 9:30PM hoping to be seated for dinner. We were told the first two floors were at capacity and we had to eat upstairs at "The Lookout". We went upstairs and then were told the kitchen closes at 10PM and we had to order immediately. Maybe it's because I'm from New York, but a kitchen closing at 10PM is absurd to me. The service was horrible, the table was dirty and the food was gross. The menu was limited to bar type food & snacks. We ordered a bunch to share; Here is our order:

1. Big Soft Pretzel: Only decent thing we ordered; probably was frozen though so that's hard to mess up. 
2. Nashville hot calamari: Repulsive. The calamari was shaped in long, thick sticks and was a bit undercooked and soggy. 
3. Trio Slider: One of the "sliders" is a bologna & cheese on white bread.... okay.......
4. Fried broccoli: Do not order; you will burp it up for the rest of the night. 
5. Burrata: The weirdest menu item ever. It was a sin what they did to the burrata. It was plasticy and filled with some orange/red filling.... appalling. 

Blake, stick to music buddy....

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Came in on night with Jake Durkin playin and Ashley serving.  By far, the best night out in a long time because of the service and the song! Will be back!

name: Ole Red
text:
My husband and I passed by Ole Red right before it opened at 11 and decided to wait with the handful of others at the door to get in for lunch. 

We decided to sit at the bar since it was only the 2 of us. The bartender was very nice and took her time to explain the menu offerings. We really liked that most of their food, sauces etc are made in house. 

We both started with a beer (love the local beer offerings!) The one thing I didn't quite get was that the beer was served in a plastic cup. I get why they'd do that after hours once a rowdier crowd comes in, but not in the early afternoon. 

We both split the nachos and they were SOOOO GOOD!! Like I'm not even kidding. From the chicken, to the BBQ sauce and everything in between, I highly recommend the nachos!! It was plenty for 2 people and honestly we couldn't even finish it between us. YUM!!!

The interior of Ole Red is definitely a step above the rest. The stage was awesome and they had a bluegrass band playing the whole time. There are multiple levels and a rooftop bar, but unfortunately the rooftop was closed when we were there so we didn't get to see it.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text:
I've never been a fan of the atmosphere or patrons here.  As far as Nashville bars go, they should rename this place "Douche Central."  I went there last night against my will, and I'm not sure what I did to piss him off, but the bouncer cut me off after three beers.  He physically took my third beer from my hand.

The long and short of it is that if you want to see the worst Nashville has to offer, from the basic country music wannabe's to the douchebags trying to hook up with them, and get rude service at the same time, this is your place.  It's like a bad high school party, and the prude bouncer is your mom showing up.

name: Ole Red
text: Had to stop in to support our OK boy Blake Shelton.  Downstairs was pretty typical of most of the  places along the strip.. but we went to the rooftop (enclosed for the winter) and liked the whiter vibe.  Our burger was terrific and has good service.  Prob pretty great view in nice weather!

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
This venue is breathtaking. 

I love everything from the courtyard to the statues, to the unique light fixtures and marble covered interior. This is the perfect place to enjoy a night at the symphony or hear a concert. 

I've noticed that they are trying to incorporate more comedians, popular musicians and discounted tickets to get more people in the doors, and I'm glad that they are making strides to ensure this lovely gem downtown is a success. They have multiple bars in the lobby's so you can enjoy a cocktail for a reasonable price. Put it in a plastic cup and you can bring it inside the auditorium. I love that!

Some people don't dress up, but I would suggest you do. It's just the kind of venue that screams class, sophistication, and the arts.

name: Nashville Symphony
text: The Schermerhorn Nashville Symphony was an amazing venue for a concert. We came to the Richard Marx concert on June 14th. Amazing!  The acoustics in the room were on point. The symphony behind Richard Marx was magnificent. The building itself was inspiring with all of its intricate details. It was very clean. There was an outside area for having a drink and enjoying the fresh air yet you were still in the confines of the building. There were bars on every floor as well. Everything you needed was right there. We had box seats on the balcony. Nothing could've been better for that night. Simply priceless!!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: As someone who lives here, I know this place is a tourist trap, but my sister loves coming here on special occasions, so it's where we ended up. We had a great experience. The food was yummy, even though it was outrageously priced, and we were fortunate to sit far enough away from the band that we could hear the music, but still carry on a conversation without having to yell. Our server was fantastic and gave us recommendations as well as kept our table clear and drinks refilled. They've got the piano stairs, gift shop, nice bar, lots of drink options, and live band. Overall, the service and food was pretty good compared to what you could end up getting downtown at a busier restaurant.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
As our Uber pulled up under a bridge we were a little skeptical but wow are the beers good! 

We ordered two flights which allowed us to taste the majority of the drafts. Hands down the best one was the Colts Bolts, an amazing peanut butter/almond/chocolate stout. The vibes were very chill and cozy. There was more seating upstairs and it looked really cute even though we didn't sit there. Service was also great!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Fun place to grab a cold beer and hear some great live music. Worth stopping in for a cold one on a hot day. Beers are about $5

name: Ole Red
text: Pimento cheese dip is awesome. Atmosphere is casual. Great service, good good, great service, and great entertainment. Will be back

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: My friends & I ate here for dinner. The staff was polite & friendly. The food was filling but a little on the high side you pay for the atmosphere. The drinks were delicious & averaged priced.

name: Nashville Symphony
text: Ok the acoustics are amazing.  It's full of snobs but what the heck.  I went to hear Mozart.  They threw in two songs that sounded like Yoko Ono being channeled thru Symphony Instruments...stick to the darn plan.  The Mozart was great...the other two songs sucked.  They seriously sounded like background sounds for a made for TV movie.  Stick to the plan...Mozart and save that crap for after midnight Rocky Horror Picture Show crowd.  If I was Martha, I'd want my money back.

name: Ole Red
text: Disappointing! Food and service. Limited menu and the staff needs a refresher in basics.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
My Favorite Brewery Tour & Tasting In Nashville

SITREP

My hats off to the Tennessee Brew Works, and big props to tour guide extraordinaire Garr for giving one of the best brewery tours I've seen to date, ANYWHERE.

THE SETUP

There are a lot of similarities in tours through breweries (and wineries) for that matter, but where Garr really set the bar was on his most extensive discussion on "the mash" - the process of making the mash, the organic, vegetable, fruit, etc., matter you may use in mash - and the inordinate tedious process it is to clean the machinery of used-mash.

"THE MASHER".  

In fact, Garr was quite proud of their stand-alone "masher" which apparently does all the heavy lifting for the brewers that many other breweries have to do manually. 

Therefore, Tennessee Brew Works has the inordinate capability to add many more flavors to the mash process without it deteriorating the whole brew-making process.

THE BREWS

And the brews were all fabulous!  I tried their Basil Ryeman (quite exotic in flavor!) and the Belgian Farmhouse (hands down my favorite), and was delighted with both of them.  YUM!

THE LOWDOWN

A great brewery stop to listen, learn and imbibe!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Stopped by on Valentines and enjoyed their sampler paired with local chocolates. The beer was excellent and the chocolate choices really highlighted some subtle tastes in the beer. 

They has a great outdoor patio, hope the weather is great next time I'm in Nashville.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
You go here for the atmosphere so it's odd to see reviews criticizing the food. C'mon, It's not a fine dining establishment. The atmosphere is soooo FUN! 

We went to the "Music Row Happy Hour with Buzz Brainard" on Friday afternoon which is broadcast on Sirius XM's The Highway. It is fun & festive. It is upstairs in Margaritaville. 

If you don't wait on line for hours you won't get a table so then it's standing room only. (There is service at the tables but we did not get a table.)
Long line at the main bar but if you go to the side room bar there was little to NO wait. 
Staff & bartenders were all friendly & fun. 

If you must sit or are grumpy or don't have a "license to chill" (JB reference!) then please just don't go. 

Surprise guest Michael Ray played a few songs. 

The happy hour was so fun!!!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Awesome range of tasty beers. Each distinct, unique and very drinkable.  the burger was world class; juicy, tasty and with really good chips on the side. Courtney tending bar upstairs was delightful. Really knowledgeable about their beers and helped match everyone coming up to the bar with the right selection. This is a "must" for Nashville microbrew tours.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Great great beer. And at great prices. Staff was super helpful and not judgey since we were amateurs when it comes to craft beer. Highly recommend the Basil Ryeman! 
Patio atmosphere was great, shared tables. Lucky enough to sit next to some friendly adults. Live music starts almost as soon as they open. Unlike a lot of other places we went to that weekend, it was not blaring loud and did not take over the experience. 
Food was delish! If you like spicy, I highly recommend the frog legs. My dad had nothing but great things to say about the burger. 
We will be back on our next Nashville trip!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I love this arena. I have been here for multiple events, and will give you separate experiences depending on what your doing at the arena. 

Hockey

The Preds games are always a blast. Lower bowl or upper bowl tickets, you will not have a bad seat in the house. A very friendly compound for visiting fans. Since Nashville is such a melting pot, you continually see away jerseys frequent the stands of Residing Nashvillians. A good collection of assorted concessions foods and beverages. Great location because one the games pile out, Broadway is the post game destination. 

Concerts 

Recently, I went to Bridgestone for the Eric Church concert. The night he played was a Bridgestone Arena record for attendance. Everything went smoothly, concession lines were not overwhelming and the crowd behaved themselves. Last year, I attended the FGL/Luke Bryan concerts. It was an absolute blast. Being the Music City I really do believe you see the artists best performances. Example, Eric Church played for 3 hours. 

Tonight I embark in a new Bridgestone venue called Areacross. Where the top dirt bike riders invade the area. Excited to see how this compared to concerts and hockey games. 

PS during hockey games they play live music during intermission...of course right? It's NashVegas

name: Ole Red
text:
45 minute wait, bad sweet tea (tastes like dirty water), burger selections limited and once delivered the burger had blood in meat. Fries were soggy upon delivery and not crisp.

If you are a fan of Blake and want to see it, step in, add a photo or video to your social media story, and then go find you something good to eat elsewhere. You'll thank me.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Tennessee brew works was one of our favorite places while visiting this past week. We arrived around 4pm and they had live music and good seats. They have 2 levels of seating including an outdoor area and rooftop. The place is a bit tough to find but so worth it. We started with the intention of stay for a beer or two. We wound up being there for 4 hours. We ordered a flight and just went at it. My wife and I both really enjoyed the cowboys and hippie. The staff were extremely friendly and the food looked great! The music was also very good. One negative would be no AC, it was hot in there. It can be overlooked after the beers get in ya. This is a hidden gem in Nashville that should be on everyone's list.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Food, beer, and atmosphere were great. All of the staff was very nice and helpful. Only giving 2 stars because the manager was very disrespectful and aggressive to our group when we tried to talk to him about an issue. He kept his back to us while we were simply asking for an explanation. Total coward and does not deserve a position of power. Hopefully he does not hold this position for much longer considering the way he talks to his customers I can't imagine how he treats the staff.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: This place plays genuine country music!!! Laid back real Nashville experience. Good service too!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: One of the best breweries I have ever been too, not just because the beers are great but the food we ordered was delicious as well.  My husband and I got 2 flights, one of the top 5 beers on the menu and one of the 2nd grouping on the menu which cost us $2 extra.  It was worth it because we got to sample all of the beers they had and figure out which ones suited our tastes the best. I liked the "Country Roots" which is a sweet potato stout and the "City Winery Collaboration" which is an ale aged in a pinot noir barrel. We had the frog legs and a cheese plate to go along with our beer and both did not disappoint.  The food here is not like regular pub food. Its elevated and you can taste the quality in every bite.

name: Ole Red
text: Ole Red's food was pretty tasty in general. The nachos were decent, but the quesadillas were amazing! My husband and I also really enjoyed hearing the live music while we ate. It was a fun introduction to Nashville that we enjoyed very much.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Beer selection was good. They also had other drinks/wine for the non-beer drinkers. Food was great! I gave the fish tacos 5 stars. My friends rated the pulled pork sandwich 4.5 stars. Prices were reasonable. Good amount of food and larger than normal wine pours. I would definitely recommend this place and would come back.

name: Ole Red
text: So excited to visit but it ended on a terrible note. After enjoying a yummy dinner on the 2nd floor with my 12 yr old son, we went to the first level at 8:30pm before it became adults only at 9pm to watch the performer. I walked to the first floor bar TO GET A WATER... It was two people deep, with people who had drinks, and were all facing the stage, so I said excuse me and made my way to the bar. Omg, all hell broke lose with two 65+ year old couples who screamed they were in their SPOT and ordered me to "get your drink and get the hell out of here". LOL, yeah, no. Anyway, I told her she was blocking the bar and she yelled she didn't care. There should be someone ensuring you can walk up to the lower level bar without being blocked by entitled people claiming their "spot" and blocking the bar and then bullying them. In retrospect, I should have alerted security/bartender about her foul mouthed harassment but was too busy defending myself, which I didn't need to do. Total bummer experience for my son after seeing Ricky from The Voice rehearsing there during the last season.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: This place was great. Easy to get to, in, and around. Super fast service at the food area. Clean bathrooms. The food prices were much lower that I would have imagined.

name: Ole Red
text: Omg this is the best! Blake Shelton's place is do classsy!!!! We had the best drinks!!!!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
Even after all these years, I am surprised by the number of bars/honky tonks that dot Broadway. Each time I think that I've seen them all, 'new' ones creep up on me. In such a finite amount of space, there seems to be an infinite amount of narrow bars stuffed into 5-6 blocks. And, despite singing this song time and again, I'm always, like, 'haven't I been here before?'

No. No, I haven't.

I hadn't been to Layla's before and I don't know how that's possible. It's been there forever. I have been in Nashville for [redacted] years. We should have run in to each other by now. But we hadn't. Walking in to Layla's, I got the sense that this was the locals' tourist bar. Surrounded by Roberts and Tootsie's, Layla's may get lost in the shuffle but I sort of like it that way. Bear in mind, it will never be empty. You'll just have the ability to move freely, unlike at the other bars I just mentioned. If you have out-of-town friends to entertain and they've been to Nashville before, bring 'em here. They'll get that 'Nashville' experience without the bumps, tossles and woo-hoos that might bring a lesser man to tears.

At Layla's you'll hear fantastic musicians doing their thing. Despite the name, I heard more country than bluegrass. As a native Kentuckian who was with other Kentuckians, I was hoping to hear some blue and 'billy but no such luck. The musicians on the stage, though, were very talented -- as is expected on Broadway. Downstairs is a crush of humanity so I headed upstairs. This is your local pro tip for any/all Broadway bars: never stay downstairs. Upstairs you have more room, a bar you can actually get to (reasonably priced drinks, local beer in bottles and Nashville LITs if you want/need to get lit), bathrooms you can use and, in the case of Layla's, a back patio that spills out on to the alley. This gives you access to the food (grilled/fried to perfection), TVs to gawk at, open air to pollute with cigarettes (don't do this), and the chance to see musicians walk from the Ryman to other bars. This is what I mean wrt a local tourist experience. You get all the pluses of a Broadway bar without the over-the-top frenetic insanity of some of the more tourist-facing establishments.

Layla's, I'll be back with another crop of seasoned out-of-towners.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Female bartenders are rude if you're a tourist trying to have a good time.  My buddies and I were told that we were annoying and loud and told to close out our tab.  After we spent a good amount of money at this place, they were quick to dismiss us.  It's very unfortunate.  I wish I was able to give zero stars.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Great spot to drop in and hangout for a while.  The atmosphere was fun and the local entertainer played a nice variety of songs.  The drinks were strong and affordable in relation to other near by stops.  Barry and Katie kept the bar well and really were engaged with the guests in the bar area.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I'll likely repeat what my wife stated so bear with me as I try to highlight other aspects of the brewery. Oh, here we go, bathroom was clean which is sometimes rare at a brewery. Ha!

The beers we sampled ranged in variety and were all tasty and worthy of individual servings. Parking in the area is a little tight especially on busier nights. We were here on a Friday and somehow found rockstar parking right by the entrance. Use Lyft/Uber and you should have no problems and not risk the OVI/DUI.

The multi tiered patio is a great place to enjoy the beer and has covered and uncovered portions for those like myself that sizzle in the sun. The only negative aspect of the patio is the possibility of inhaling some second hand smoke. 

There was a female guitarist singer/songwriter playing some halfway decent music which made the experience very "Nashvillian". Who knows? She could be the next Grammy winning artist on radio repeat. People watching opportunities are great here as all kinds of people walk/stumble through the doors.

Keep up the great work TBW!

name: Ole Red
text: Ole Red is a beautiful space with an awesome chandelier in the main stage, eating area. The bar is build very well and has a lot of character! The rooftop was beautiful with another wonderful view of Broadway. This place has a swanky vibe, which I did enjoy. However, I was a little surprised being that Blake is the owner. We loved our time at Ole Red!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I've been to half a dozen concerts or events (PBR!) and over 50 Predators games and have sat in almost every area on all three floors and never had a bad seat. The views are great. It is easy to get around and there are multiple entrances depending on where you park. 

The food is good enough - during Preds games go check out the Hot Chicken stand on the first floor and pick up the HOT CHICKEN MAC N CHEESE, oh man it is the greatest! 

As far as Predators games go, there isn't a better environment to enjoy a game. So loud and so fun!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good ribs, great pulled pork plate with 2 Yazoo Hefeweizen. Pretty good country band, despite the young look ! Good experience, if you don't mind plastic forks, knives and table cloths! You will not go hungry !

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Good music and food but the dance floor is always people line dancing and nothing else. Drinks are pretty expensive. They turned the NHL playoffs on for us though which was awesome. Good to go if you like line dancing bad if you wanna party and raise your glass while you dance.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Cool place. Came by for lunch and some music. Good singer and a really nice group of servers and bartender. Good prices and better music. Wings were ok. I hoped they wood have more smoke flavor. I'd come back for the music and cold beer.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great fun! Good prices. The band was fun, free pool and foosball tables while waiting for band and/ or table. I had the stampede sampler, and I would not recommend it. The ribs were good, the brisket was WAY too fatty, and the pulled pork was okay but too dry. I tried some of my moms monte cristo and it was phenomenal! I would recommend that all day. Overall great place, if I'm ever in Nashville, I will return here.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Food is expensive but not good. 
Our waiter was terrible and had a attitude,  the tip was included in bill and the waitress didn't deserve it. Dance floor is nice but not impressed.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Atmosphere was cool.  Bartender Yanet was the most unfriendly depressing person I have ever seen! Nashville is such a cool fun crowd I would highly suggest a super fun, bubbly person behind the bar.  Someone that makes you feel welcome would have set a better vibe for us to stay! Maybe it was a bad day but I work customer service and it's always show time!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Pizza is really good. Quality ingredients. A medium is the same size as a dominos large pizza. Haven't had anything other than their pizza but it is definitely worth it. If you are a ranch with your pizza guy/gal I highly recommend asking for 2 sides of ranch. It is so darn good. Staff seems to be mostly high schoolers on break and hipsters but it's a tight place with good pizza. 5 stars

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: LOVE this place.  Always has great service and fantastic music!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Food was great and very reasonable. Got in before a concert with no wait. Service was good as well

name: Twin Kegs
text:
This is my first dive bar experience. They had Dos Perros on tap. I asked if there was a happy hour and the response: "Our beer is cheap." Very True

The burger was solid, no frill and yummy.

Odd things I liked about the place:
Padded bar: a good place to lean and put a knee on
Shuffleboard 
Karaoke- there wasn't a huge wait to sing

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: To preface, I LOVE Rippy's. It was the bar I used to go to in college and I really love the vibe, but something very strange and disappointing happened last night. I was at Rippy's at 10 sitting on a stool in the corner listening to the music. I had driven downtown and was planning to listen to a little bit of music after dinner and then drive home. While sitting, a staff member approached us twice asking what we would be drinking (reminder we were not at a table or the bar). We told him the second time we were driving and had ordered a drink earlier at the bar so we didn't need a second, and he told us we had to leave. He told us that it was his responsibility to serve us in his section and keep table turnover.  His reasoning is because we had to get a drink or leave. Never have I been treated like this at Rippy's, and I can't explain the disappointment. It is a place to enjoy music as well as drink, and the pressure from a staff to order a drink was appalling, especially after he knew we would be driving. I did not think that there was a rule that at all times in Rippy's you had to have a drink in your hand or you would be kicked out. VERY disappointing, especially with such good memories from a year ago when I went to college in Nashville.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: It was Tues. & they just opened so it was pretty quiet. Waitress was very bland, no personality which is unusual for Nashville. We were vacationing  & we had experienced friendly service everywhere. Food was very good. BBQ ribs, potato salad & fries. Bottom line: 2 Stars for Service, 3 Stars for Food.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: If your in the mood for ribs, this is the place. The flavor is great and soooo tender. We also had the nachos which were also a hit. The queso on it is the best I've had in awhile. Service was extremely prompt and we hardly waited 10 minutes for our food. Live music was a very nice touch. Great atmosphere!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This is a cowboy saloon, well a great bar.  We went here back in August 2017 the week end that the bears beat the titans.  It was an exhibition game.  (The place was rocking, Folk's were backed up into the street to get in). My group did not like it, we were a bit too old for this 25 to 35 crowd.  Sorry we moved on, but you young Folks will enjoy WILDHORSE SALOON in BNA.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The food is good and the music is great. Very friendly atmosphere. A good spot to relax have drinks and listen to live music.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
The only good thing I can say about this joint is the music is GREAT!!  Stayed for over 2 hrs listening to a great band on the upper level.  It's a pretty cheesy place and the food is below average.  The hamburger was atrocious.  Even after plenty of drinks, it was just awful.  Bubba Burgers taste better than this. 
  There is much better bbq in the area.  Try Peg Leg Porker instead.  Best bbq sandwich around.
If you're just looking for a good , fun, larger honky tonk atmosphere with table seating this is a ok spot.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Went here a couple of times during a stay in Nashville and I just loved it. All three or so times we went, they had Square Dancing--not sure if we were just lucky or if they have it every night. It was so much fun to learn the dances together with other diners. Their food is delicious, too, and the service has always been good. I also love the architecture of this place. They have a huge main floor with tables and seating, in the middle of which is the stage with the dance floor. They have a second floor, which is basically a huge balcony with more seating options. The ceiling is very high and there are horse sculptures "running" across the ceiling. It's pretty cool. Definitely recommend going here for some Southern feeling.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
TPAC is located in the James K. Polk Cultural Center which houses a myriad of event venues including the Tennessee State Museum and Andrew Jackson Hall--the place where I spent an evening recently.

I had the opportunity to visit and see - hear "Star Trek: The Ultimate Voyage" a live, retrospective film and music performance. The show featured selected clips from 50 years of Star Trek episodes and feature films while accompanied by a full orchestra. (In this particular small venue, it was a well-balanced half orchestra of about 50 performers.)

"Beam me up Mr Scott" in this instance meant beaming a high definition video onto a 40-foot wide screen behind the orchestra. The players were very dimly lit and did not distract from the video. In addition, the orchestra was hidden in part by a pseudo reconstruction of the bridge of the Enterprise.

The concert featured many familiar tunes written for franchise favorites such as Star Trek: The Original Series, Star Trek: The Motion Picture, Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan, Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home, Star Trek: Insurrection, Star Trek: The Next Generation, Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, Star Trek: Voyager and much more.

A VIP pass (for an additional cost) afforded us the chance to go onstage during  the afternoon (before the performance) and be present for the sound check as well as meet the conductor.

Pretty cool event.

I realize this does not cover much of TPAC...but that will come after future visits.

name: Twin Kegs
text:
What I liked:
1. Trevor at the Catbird Seat (a formidable judge of food) told us this was his favorite burger in Nashville.  The burger was quite delicious - and helped with our hangover from the drink pairings at our dinner the evening before.  However,,,

What I didn't like:
1. The service was terrible - the one waitress was also playing chef as their normal "chef" hadn't shown up.
2. The smoke- beware - smoking is allowed.  Sadly, that over powered the tasty burgers we wanted to enjoy.

Verdict- 
Meh... not worth the trip.  Maybe an evening try would be better, but I would stick to the other strong burger spots in town.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Seating in the dining rooms are first come first serve. We waited about 20 minutes for a table to open up. The waitress was very prompt with waters and our drinks even though it was extremely busy on a Saturday night. 

The Honky Tonk tea was a great drink. The pulled pork dinner was OK. 

The bands were very good and the upstairs bar seemed to be where it's at. 

Overall, fun place with good drinks and decent food.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: We came here Thursday night.  This place is great for kids.  They put two big M on my daughter's hands (minor) just incase someone thought she was 21.   The place is huge with three floors.  The first floor is for dinner and the second two floors you can just sit.  We came at 9pm for line dancing and stayed until almost midnight.  My kids had a blast.  The band Radio Romance was playing.  Great band doing mostly covers and a few original songs.  We had a great time.  My youngest (7 years) had the most fun out of anyone on the dance floor.  She was having dance offs with about ten girls who seemed to love her company.   Great night for everyone.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: Was at TPAC last Saturday for @Midnight Live with Chris Hardwick at the James K. Polk Theater. It was awesome. Seating was comfortable. Venue was easy to find. Parking was easy. Very happy. Staff seemed friendly although I didn't have much interaction with them.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I got the chicken fingers. They were ok the batter was pretty heavy. It was a Friday afternoon and medium busy and the service was horrible. The bartender working had no personality nor seemed interested in working.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Food was not worth it, there are plenty of better places on Broadway. My ribs were tasteless and I wouldn't order meat there again based on the average-ness of everyone's plate. The only stand-out was the fried pickles appetizer--the best fried pickles I had in Nashville, they do the entire dill spear instead of the rounds. I would recommend you go for the music (it's loud so don't expect a conversation), a beer and the fried pickles.

name: Nashville Palace
text: The food was not the greatest.  The live music is great.  Cute place,  but if you came to enjoy for,  skip it.  If you want a nice little lunch place with live music,  nice environment and great music.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Good drink prices compared to the other bars in the area, and place is pretty bumping with life. A lot of space so your are not cramped. Id come her again.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Nashville has delicious food everywhere, this place is great for food and live entertainment. They have two live bands performing each on a separate floors.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Right across from where Predators play.  Good, not great, 'cue...AND LOUD MUSIC.  Bring earplugs, folks.  Save your ears!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Hard to really give a full review of this place as we were there for a private work event. But the venue is fantastic. Love the dance floor, the game options on the second floor (though they are TOO close together), and the table seating. 

The catered food was pretty delicious and the drinks were mostly good as well. I kept trying to get a gin and tonic (and tried 3 of the 4 bars in the place) and it was sparkling water every time. Very different. 

All in all, we had a blast. The dancers were fun to watch, the band (Brother Trouble) was really great) and we had a great time at the event. 

Thanks!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Always Nice To Find Pizza After Midnight!

SITREP

This is a great spot to come to after a long evening of having dinner (Sycamore Nashville), getting cocktails at more fancy establishments (Aura), dealing with more dive bar locations (Red Patio Saloon), and then decompress on beer, soda and pizza.

THE SETUP

Located in Midtown Nashville (not to be confused with Midtown Sacramento, where I live), the Soulshine Pizza Factory has a great late night menu, and is reminiscent both at once of a Sports Bar, Music Venue and a Gourmet Pizza Spot.  We hung out on the 2nd level deck, and patio bar area.

WORLD MUSIC

There was a great band playing when we arrived that way laying down some nice funky Jamaican beats, and expanding into a world music vibe with their music selections.  To be honest, I didn't recognize any of the tunes they were playing, but it was all upbeat and good to dance to.

GIANT FAN!

Oh my god.  On this large patio deck where the band was playing, is this massive overhead / over-sized fan - it must have been about 30-35 feet in diameter (kinda taking the wind out of the sales of my much smaller by comparison, three 5-foot fans I have in my home).  It certainly was impressive

THE PIZZA

Excellent personal pan style pizza - it seemed enough for 2 gals at our table to be sharing, and one was enough for me.  The Jacksonian had chicken, tomatoes and green onion.  The Mississippian had BBQ chicken.   They were total yum.

THE LOWDOWN

Soulshine Pizza Factory is a great stop to chill after a long night of fun when you need something to eat and want to catch a chill vibe with a band, refreshing drinks and great conversation.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: My family had lunch at Rippy's and enjoyed live music. You seat yourself and a server comes to the table. We started with the fried pickles which were delicious. The food came quickly and the waiter was pleasant. The meal was excellent! I had the pulled chicken sandwich and it was flavorful and juicy. This is a perfect place to stop for a bite to eat for lunch if you are with adults or kids.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
