text: Food 2-stars, atmosphere 4-stars.   Weird checkin process.   You get carded, then you checkin, but they tell you it will be quick.  Then you can sit around/drink for hour or two until they call you for a table.    $6 cover on weekends, unless a member of party is veteran of military.     Had Hot chicken sandwich....  would not order again.   Was weird.   Hot habanero chicken, with overly sweet toppings.  Fried pickles decent.   Line dancing and live music very good.   Also, very kid friendly.   I recommend a visit, but think it will leave foodies wanting more.    FYI:   Get impression staff doesn't like the business.    They said 2.5 hrs tonight, even though it didn't seem that busy at all.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great place to go in Nashville and learn to line dance.  Made a fun night because everyone can dance without feeling self conscience.  Cover charge was worth it once you get in a lot to do from playing pool, to dancing,

name: Big Machine Brewery & Distillery
text:
Ok, seriously, I was amazed!  This place the staff is nothing but spectacular. We just happened to be walking by and one of our party recognized Big Machine store and Distillery as affiliated with Taylor Swift.  We went in to look around, and the security guard,David schooled us on the superiority of their vodka and whiskey.  Totally changed my mind about alcohol and quality, and I'm not even a drinker!  
Besides that...The bar staff helped us so much with navigating around Nashville. We were getting overwhelmed with trying to figure out where to go and what to do.  She actually saved our trip!  She told us the great places to go to eat, shop, listen to music and bars to go to.  Nashville is such an awesome place, with incredibly nice and helpful people everywhere, but this place but  Keeleligh was the most amazing of them all!  A complete Gem.  I am so glad we happened upon this place so early in our trip. 
Thank u, thank u

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: As tourists we felt welcome here. My first choice for their 12 bone pork Ribs, fried Catfish strips with fries, and a Bud Light.  Bridal shower singing and dancing to Song of the South makes it irrelevant if the stage singers are good.  'Next time', I wear my denim shorts and tonylama to blend!  An honest honky tonk bar.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Quick review for a quick stop:

Two story building. Three different live bands. One packed, happy, drunken crowd. Go and look at all my reviews... they are long... they are tiresome... they are detailed and intricate. But this place doesn't need that. This place just needs for you to know that you are going to get an amazing Nashville experience

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Second bad experience at this cheesy little saloon. Don't bother there is zero customer service. They are the rudest management team and staff in Nashville. Learn to line dance from YouTube. And a simple drink is a double digit price. Too many other places to spend your money in Nashville.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: After previously enjoying concerts here with dinner and hearing some awesome local talent,  NEVER again. 15 Minutes to sit being the only people at podium Sat as soon as someone noticed us them no waitress for another 10 to 15 minutes with maybe 20 other patrons at tables, we left ....when I informed the manager, he couldn't care less.....won't b back

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
We went there for lunch. We are new to the area from California and this place was exactly what we were looking for. Great southern food and fast service. The host girl was very friendly and welcomed us. Our server was nice and attentive. 
They have kids menu, too. Food was big and very good.
Place is huge. They have pool tables on the 3rd floor which we played with our kids since up stairs wasn't busy yet. ( I am guessing it gets busy at night so no children allowed then )
Nice experience.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Don't come here if you want customer service.... the only ones that are right are the servers and hosts according to the gm... it doesn't matter if you purchase food or drinks.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Ok BBQ not the best in Nashville by a long shot.  They had unsweetened tea in the sweet tea the night I visited, and the waitress did not believe me.  I asked for a soft drink to replace my tea, she later came back and stated she tasted the tea and it was unsweetened and apologized.  Why argue with your customer?

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Busy place on the corner of Broadway. Two floors at least with great live music on both floors. Lots of different menu options. I went with the brisket plate. I chose Mac n cheese and coleslaw which I was happy with. The corn bread was also a really good addition. My brisket was melt in your mouth and multiple people at the table called it the 'best' they've had!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Lunch time on a Friday. Had the grilled chicken wrap and it was great. Band was good as well. Wasn't to crowded at that time but still a good crowd. At this time they had ample servers and the food came out pretty quickly. I would definitely go back.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Way too fun here! Prices werent bad at all and I convinced my friend, who isnt a country fan one bit, to get out on the dance floor. So much life and energy. Id come back to nashville soley for this saloon!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Came for the Friday night concert series put on by local favorite indie radio station Lightning 100.  On a warm summer night this is a really great thing and very, very popular as evidenced by the hoards of people crowding the upstairs patio.  One of the things I love about this place is their support of local music.  Check out their concert listing for great stuff.

Soulshine has a lot of good things going for it such as this weekly event.  It has other good stuff like their beer selection.  

The food and service?  Meh.  We had their nachos which aren't made from your traditional corn chips but rather the pizza crust/dough.  The toppings were good but I hated the pizza crust.  Also, service upstairs on the patio was dismal.  It took forever for me to get the bartender to acknowledge.  Once outside we never saw our waitress so we went back to the bar to order more drinks (we had been sitting outside for over 30 mins) and at this point our "waitress" finally came over and chided us for not ordering from her after hastily introducing herself.

So why am I generously giving 4 stars?  I love their support of local music.  And the fact that this chain is named after an Allman Brothers song.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Just stopped in for drinks and an appetizer. Poor service in the bar. Waitress didn't clean any of the tables the entire time we were there, and when we asked she begrudgingly got a dry rag and ran it across the water rings on the table. Fried pickles were meh. Environment was decent.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Okay, this place is HUGE. It's the first place we went to when I visited Nashville, and oh man, it was FUN! There's THREE different bands playing at once, and everyone is just truly enjoying themselves. It's so loud so you have to shout, but it's fun. Lots of drinking and dancing and singing going on. My friend and I were starving so we got the pulled pork. YUM! I'm glad I got to try some good bbq while I was in Nashville. If there is better bbq I"ll be sure to keep it in mind for next time.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I have been to Nashville twice and both times I have been so excited to eat at Rippy's. Not only is their BBQ sauce the perfect combination of tangy and spicy, and the pulled pork moist and plentiful, but the music and atmosphere of the three story establishment makes it a start to a great night. The food may take a bit longer to get to the table because of the popularity, but it is well worth the wait (30-45 minutes). Also, the fried pickles are a great appetizer. Prices are fair (8 dollars for a sandwich and fries).

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Great ribs great sauce. Probably the best smoked chicken I've ever had.
Good band and attentive servers. 
Loved it

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: My husband and I wound up here on a Wednesday when live music was playing. Food, drink, music was good. What I want to point out was how they dealt with a young country music fan. He wanted to sing and loved Johnny Cash, and I have never been in a place that was so kind, accommodating, and nice! The treatment of this young man was beyond and above anything I've experienced and that alone recommends this place in my mind. On behalf of all of us on the spectrum, sincere thanks.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Live music ! 
Local beers and nice samplers of BBQ. First restaurant tried in Nashville thanks to our Uber driver who recommended the place.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
We had so much fun here. On the Friday night that we were there, they began charging a cover charge at 7:00 (waived for military and first responders- thank you for supporting these brave people). We got there around 7:30 and stayed for a long time. The atmosphere is so much fun that we couldn't bring ourselves to leave. 

There are three floors, all with a view of the stage if you are interested in the live music (we loved the first artist on the night that we were there!). On the first floor, there is a huge dance floor and there are line dancing lessons in between live music sets. The dancing is fun!!! Even if you miss the lesson, it's easy enough to pick up by just watching others. 

I will say that we didn't order any food, so I can't comment on that. I did order a drink, which was expensive and heavy on the alcohol, but delicious nonetheless.

name: CMA Fest
text: Great time as always.  Our tickets were in Section 127 and were great..closest row the better.  Make sure to scan your tickets at various scanners for prizes.  Get a hotel in town!

name: Big Machine Brewery & Distillery
text: This happened to surprisingly our favorite place downtown. It's off the beaten path right beside FGL house. We saw the word sample so we went in during the day and had a vodka lemonade slushy sample. It was so good. The bartender was very knowledgeable with my husbands questions. We had some more walking to do so we left but we went back in the evening to two different bartenders. We decided to split a lemonade slushee because we aren't huge drinkers and it hit the spot. More then the the great drinks there the bartenders and service were great. They were able to read the cues in my body language and communicated to each other wordlessly to deal with a situation with another patron that was loud, in my space, and making me uncomfortable. The male bartender was able to speak with him and diffuse the situation. Thank you so much! When we come back we will make sure to stop in again.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Rippy's was really fun. They had a great band playing and the drinks were not only cheap, but also good. The bartenders are friendly and so is the crowd. I didn't try the food, so I can't comment on that, but I'd recommend Rippy's for a fun night out.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Atmosphere great, service not. Caitlin was our bartender and we did not get one smile from her during the 10+ drinks we ordered. No hi how are you, thank you. She ruined the whole experience for us as we were having fun on the dance floor but as soon as we had to order a drink we dreaded it. Hope we won't get her again.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
We loved it.  Our server Brendon( I think that was his name)  was awesome.  He was extra friendly and really helped us out on what to order.  His recommendations were spot on.  The pulled pork sandwich and smoked chicken platter were the best.  The chili was excellent too!  The cole slaw was good but needed a little salt. We thought it was much better than Jacks Bbq that was across the street.  
The band that was playing were funny and sounded great too.  I would definitely go back !

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Went here this year & once last year. Idk what happened between last year & this year but there's a huge difference, and I don't mean in a good way. Last year when we visited the pulled pork was absolutely delicious, I didn't have one complaint. This year was disgusting. I usually always finish my plate. This year I had about five bites or so and was done. That's how gross it was. Definitely cooked different and more fat & chunky instead of shredded. Waitress also sucked this year. Messed up my whole order, then argued saying that's what I ordered. Definitely won't be back again. Will stick with Peg Leg Porker, Id rather stand in line for an hour there because they are much better.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Hands down this restaurant was the filthiest place I visited down town in Nashville!
The waiter: Tommy gave us the crappiest service we've ever had in our lives!
I have been in the restaurant industry for over eight years and a food server as well. This server took our order after waiting 20 minutes, never came back to fill our drinks ,never checked to see if our food even arrived & the order was completely messed up & he didn't bring 4 items we ordered (not all food we ordered was brought out). The best part of the night, was after sitting there for an hour and 15 minutes he came back to the table and dropped the check off without half of the food even being brought out or served to us. I gave it one star, because the band was good but other than that everything else was disgusting and horrible!
I would not recommend this place to my worst enemy! Hopefully you guys change your management and your server because you will never make it if you keep such a failure of a slop house in Nashville for sure:(

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
For being Nashville for the first time I thought I would have some good BBQ I've hade better in Detroit. Gave you 2 sauces and they were both ok and did not see much of a difference other than one was a little more spicy. The ribs wee good with the dry rub but the pulls chicken was dry. The slaw was bland but the beans were good and only if you like spicy. I figure this is the type of food you get in a tourist town.  I guess you have to go off the beaten path to find the good stuff. 

The one thing I did find disgusting and it wasn't the restaurant it was that whole area it smelled look old stale beer and cigarets not vert appetizing.

name: Big Machine Brewery & Distillery
text: We were in Nashville for my daughters 21st birthday went to all the bars and trendy stuff your supposed to do while in town. Came in to Big Machine because they had a Vodka lemonade slushy on a very day met the manager Jacob and have been back everyday since. I highly recommend visiting,GREAT Vodka,Whiskey,Store and very friendly employees.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Matt Holloway should be fired! My boyfriend and I decided to check out the line dancing. Unfortunately we were unable to find out. We had waited in line to be ID & got wrist bands went inside and got a drink at the bar & started a tab with my CC. We stepped outside to smoke b/c it is a smoke free building and then when we attempted to return the door guy informed us we were not allowed inside. I showed him our wristbands & explained that my purse and CC were at the bar and he stood in front of me to physically block us from going inside. I ended up having to push past him so that I could go get my purse and close my tab out and get my CC back. As I was waiting for the bartender to run my CC the door guy approached me with the manager (Matt Holloway) who were both going to escort me out. I explained that after the way I had been treated at the door I was leaving of my own choice after I paid my tab and the manager grabbed my arm as to assist me out the door. So do NOT waste your time or money at The Wild Horse Saloon unless you want to risk being refused service and forcibly removed for no apparent reason.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Great food. 
Service could use work. Seating wasn't great. High top chair at a regular table is a little ridiculous. But the food. The food. Delicious & affordable. Don't miss this place!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
The bartender was super sweet. She served me quick and with a smile. 

But the bareback.... damn. What did I do man. Just ask you a question. What are you mad about man. I'm from California and didn't know what time a game started. It's cool if you don't know, use words man. Shrugging like a 6 year old ain't it.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Had lunch here after visiting Cooters. Sat outside and Brandi was our waitress. She was very nice, funny and an amazing server even after she got seated with like a party of 20 next to us, it did not impact our service at all. Cathfish and fried pickles were great! That batter is amazing!Brandi  gave awesome recommendations. Can't beat the prices either!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I went to Rippy's with my wife and two closest friends. We were in Nashville for a long weekend. We arrived at the restaurant at 6:00 pm on game night for the Predators. I didn't think we would have a prayer of getting a table and eating in a treasonable amount of time, but we decided to give it a shot. I was pleasantly surprised when were able to get a table right away on the second level. The service was excellent and were able to order right away. Our food came out very quickly and was delicious! I had the 1/2 rack of ribs with baked beans and Mac & Cheese. The food was amazing and I enjoyed every last  bite! I recommend this place anytime you are in town!!

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
We saw Disney's Broadway tour of The Lion King in the Jackson Hall at the TPAC and couldn't have been more thrilled with our experience. The venue is a little on the older side and perhaps a bit small, but I felt like every seat in the house (regardless of the ticket price) would have a great view of the show. The attendants were helpful and made sure everyone was where they needed to be. We were ushered into our seat in a calm organized fashion.

We sat in the left side box with a spectacular view of the stage and he performers. Parking was a bit of a headache, but we definitely plan on returning to the TPAC again - perhaps next time to see Beauty and the Beast!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Would not recommend. We had a table of 9, which we understand is a bigger table, but not outrageous. We waited forever for our food, and when we got it, nothing was warm. It all felt as if it had been sitting on a counter for a very long time. We complained and were told it was our fault for having too big of a table. Along with the food being cold, it wasn't all that great either. When wanting to leave, it took us a good half an hour for our waitress to get our cards back to us--and I would like to mention we were in here on a Monday night! Was not impressed at all!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Usually my expectations for a soft opening are pretty low. Sure a mixture of trepidations and hope that result in a mixed bag as a new restaurant finds its footing and works out the bugs. 

What a joy!  

The atmosphere is great - set up with a stage for a live band on one end, a bar at the other. 

Restaurant opens at 7 am for breakfast, transitions to a brunch menu and then lunch before dinner. 

Food was great (tried their Hot Chicken) and served hot and fresh. Ice Tea was tasty too - fresh and quenching.  Fries were hot, crispy and lightly salted - perfection in my book. 

Service was great - once it gets more folks, will be interesting to see if they can keep up the high standards they've set for themselves. 

Overall, very positive and I look forward to trying one of their burgers next (if I don't hit them for breakfast first!

Went back on a Friday night for a burger. Awesome. Even my daughter (who is famous for not finishing her meals) enjoyed and finished her burger.   

BTW, live music starts a 7 pm.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
I have no idea what the place is like at night, but we had fun during the day. We attended a line dancing workshop hosted here. The service was fantastic and the buffet lunch they served was great. Pulled pork, baked beans, slaw, mac n cheese and brownie bites were on the menu. They have a large dance floor. If you want a good mixed drink I recommend the "hot mess."  

We had an absolute blast line dancing there.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Rippy's may be popular but we just walked out due to crappy service from the staff. It's 4th of July and it's a "seat yourself" type of deal. Well you'd make more money by having a hostess to seat and tell people the wait time when they can't find an open seat. I ordered just a coke and it was bottom of the barrel just carbonation. The heavy blonde bar tender has NO manners or people skills.  She should work at the DMV with that shitty attitude. Worst visit on a vacation ever.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Being in Nashville for the first time, and with kids (8 and 12), this left us with a dilemma.  We wanted to experience the Nashville music scene, have some good food, and go to a lively yet appropriate venue for kids.

In doing research it became clear that Broadway was the place for this.  The avenue is full of restaurants and music and we happened upon the Wildhorse Salon after reading it was kid friendly.  

We could not have made a better choice.  This place is huge--three floors.  First floor are tables to eat at and some bars, plus the main stage and dance floor.  Floor two has a bar, some booths, viewing spots for the stage, and games such as pool and Foos Ball (all free to play).  The third floor we did not get to but it just looks like a vantage point to watch the stage.

We arrived to the place around 4:30.  We sat and ordered the fried chicken, piggy grilled cheese, and the kids Mac and cheese and kids burger.  We started with fried pickles and drinks as well.  I had read that the food here was at best average but we absolutely loved everything as it was all very tasty and filling.  

While waiting for the food there was free line dancing lessons (every 45 min or so) and the first band also came on.  The kids danced and then we ate and it was an absolute blast.

After dinner we grabbed a seat near the dance floor, had some more drinks and danced up a storm as the band played.  The kids even ordered a lemonade that came in a big plastic cowboy boot!

This is the perfect family place if you want good food, Nashville music, and a lively environment that truly satisfies both the kids and adults.  We stayed until about 8pm and it appeared that at that point the crowd was getting older.  I would think any time after 8 or 9 it would not be as kid friendly.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
I love this restaurant. As per Nashville requirement, the live music is generally on point. With the cool upstairs deck open to the main part of the second floor, it definitely has a unique feel. I've been here several times now and have always had great service, even during night ha when it's packed. 

As far as food goes, for the appetizer, the pulled pork nachos are a must! They've got a unique flavor but they're unexpectedly amazing! Next time, I plan to try their pork sandwich. For the main course I've always gone with pizza. Cheeseburger is amazing. The CCR was good, but not as much as others I've tried. Whatever type of cheese they use, I think it's the best in town! The sandwiches are moderately priced (10-15) and the pizzas are a bit pricey for the larger sizes, but the smaller ones are reasonable (10/15 or 20-27 for larger).

I haven't tried any cocktails yet but I've heard good things. The beer was cold, with a good selection of domestics and crafts. Average pricing there.

I recommend Soulshine when friends visit.

name: Nashville Palace
text: This place has really changed over the years! W sat at the bar and bartender took several minutes to greet us or ask for our order. When I asked what they had- he replied "a lot" and walked off. I then asked about moonshine and he told me they don't have that anymore- after we ordered something they did have and wings and onion rings (menu is limited) we sat back and enjoyed the band. The music was great and the lead talented with a great voice! Before we got ready to leave- we tried to buy a T shirt- one of the guys tried and tried to find the key to sell us one- he finally came back and brought 3 koozies (there were 3 of us) and asked if we could come back to get one the next day. That was a shame- never had time to go back

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Went for a private function. While there were bars on all three floors getting a drink was a nightmare. They didn't seem to have enough staff to keep up. Food was good. The entertainment was amazing. LoCash Cowboys played!!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Fall of the bone baby back ribs, live music, attentive sfaff, what more can you ask for? Popped in for lunch on a whim & never regretted it.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
This is the best place to hear old country music in Nashville. Plenty of parking, great bands, friendly folks, and classic country music. The food is pretty good as well. The burger and fries is delicious. For a night out of traditional country music, Nashville Palace is the only place for me.

P.S. - It's handicapped accessible for my 90 year old grandmother to hear great music. She loves watching the dancers two step on the dancefloor. We also bring the kids during the day and early evening, so it's great when family visits in town. TIP: bring earplugs for sensitive ears.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I loved this place. the history behind it the atmosphere the food all enjoyable. I got the pot roast and it was delicious! we also had their burger which they make their own jalapeno bacon. I will definitely be coming back

name: Tin Roof
text: Great!! Chris Young dropped by and ordered a Few drinks and was in the back listening to the live music. Our waitress was on top of the drinks as well. Great spot, good music and laid back, friendly staff. A good place if you're not trying to be too fancy.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
This is my second attempt to get reservations.  I got in their queue 12 hours before tix went up for sale, waited patiently for 14 minutes(once 8am rolled around), still sold out.

Both times were to see an old friend from out of state perform.  I'm sorry, but this ticket/reservation system is a joke.  It says it's a lottery/random spot in virtual line.  So, even with getting in the virtual line 12 ours in advance, I probably lost my reservation to someone who logged in minutes before 8am.

I don't think I will ever attempt to go the Bluebird again.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Not the greatest grilled cheese like we'd been told. Oh well. The sweet potato fries were gross too. 

The bartender was sweet and helpful. She helped me pick a beer that was pretty good since I'm new to beer. It was cool that there was live music. The guy was pretty good. 

Dive bar for sure. But cool.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Sutler's Bluegrass Brunch was a request from out of town guests. We had a great experience when we went last year, however, the $15 bottomless mimosas you are better off getting one off drinks. After I saw several other customers with lighter mimosas, I asked our server (Jenna) for a splash of champagne she went to the bar and added soda (vs. champagne) as my two bartender guests watch her do. Highly recommend the food, but maybe a more understanding waitress than Jenna...

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
This burger joint was expected to be better but I give it two stars. 
Probably was one of the worse places to come and it in Nashville. The only thing that was good was that I came with a group of friends and it was empty, so it was perfect for us to sit together. 

Needs to somehow make a major change or i believe it's not gonna make it.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Proud of the history established in the Woolworth in 5th for Desegregation by the "sit-in"! The restaurant portions are large, our food was good - just be aware the blacked ribs are very spicy! Very attentive wait staff! I would recommend and I would return!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
For all the hype, I was not impressed.

A small group - seven of us - went for a friend's birthday. The birthday boy summed it up - the place needs less hipness and more service.

It started out well enough. A couple of people had ordered drinks when we arrived, and encouraged us to try the Babs on a Budget. The waiter came back after a few minutes for our order, and my husband tried it. Boring Me had some ginger ale. Drinks took a few more minutes to get there, but came in cute mason jars, and everyone was happy.

20 minutes later, the waiter finally returned. He seemed annoyed that we ALL needed more drinks by that time. He brought them back, and seemed to need reminded that we might want to order food. We were getting hungry by that point, so we indicated that we would get an appetizer, but we would order at the same time. As soon as we mentioned the appetizer, he ran off to put in the order without getting our food orders.

A little while later, the pimento cheese appetizer arrived, delivered by the bartender. Pretty good. A little pricey for something served on saltines, but I guess that's part of the hipness of the dish.The cheese itself was tasty.

We were pretty hungry by the time the waiter returned to get our order. And then we waited and waited for the food. We all kept trying those little tricks you use in a restaurant. "I know when I come back from the bathroom, they'll be bringing the food out." 

We had been there more than an hour and a half by the time dinner finally came to our table. There were some apologies muttered in the meantime, but they didn't seem that sincere. Especially since our drink glasses kept getting empty. 

And everything was a mess. He didn't seem to know who had ordered what, or what sides came with each person's main dish. The girl to my left got the kale salad instead of the house salad. There was an unclaimed dish of macaroni. The birthday boy's burger arrived, with a promise that the fries would be out soon. And everything was cold as though it had been sitting, waiting to be delivered.

My husband's gumbo was okay. Really more like chili, and a little cold, but there would have been few complaints had it arrived in a timely fashion.

I have to say that my marrakesh kale salad was the highlight of the evening. Good flavor, good texture. Quite nice.

But my burger, my poor burger. I think Elsie would have been disappointed with her "favorite." It was cold and positively squishy where the juices had soaked into the bun. I ordered the BBQ sauce on the side, and it came on the side - and on the burger. I had ordered the burger medium - I know that's always a risk - but as I finished the last couple of bites, I realized that part of the squishiness was meat that hadn't gotten cooked at all. I scooped out some pink paste, closed my eyes and finished the rest.

The Chris Scruggs band lightened the mood at the end of the night with some killer classic country and western swing.

We walked out feeling better. Until we looked up on the back deck to see our server smoking and having a boisterous cell phone conversation. Which explained a lot.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsie's is overrated. Been here a couple of times with my friends and it's nothing special. Was once escorted out because my friend misfired a mayonnaise packet and the group behind us that it hit asked the bouncer to escort us out and he did, even though we apologized and explained it was an accident. Staff isn't friendly or understanding, bands really aren't very good. Check out ANY OTHER bar on Broadway.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Don't bother... Besides this place probably won't be there in six months anyway. Great concept but the idea got lost somewhere before execution.  Drinks, food and bluegrass, what could go wrong? Well let me tell you... parking is limited but that's not their fault, however everything else was... We waited for an hour for brunch on Sunday at 11:30am which is fine and for a good restaurant I understand that's primetime and that's also not the problem. Bloodys were bland, never saw the hostess seat anyone unless she knew them(we ended up sitting at the bar), people come for the bottomless mimosas and camp at the tables both inside and out but order no food, hmmm, bartender took my half drink and silverware away while I was still using them and the food was completely uneatable. I had the standard breakfast, my most favorite things in the whole world (eggs, bacon & fried potatoes with a biscuit and gravy) eggs and bacon were so greasy you couldn't eat them and the potatoes had some kind of mystery spice that made have no taste at all. Oh and btw gravy was from a jar...disgusting. Sorry Sultler, I was looking for more and was very disappointed. I won't be back.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We stopped by for drinks at Tooties.  The employee at the door would not let my 63 year old father in because he did not have his license with him.  I sincerely appreciate that establishments need to check IDs for liability reasons and for safety.  However, this employee showed a complete lack of common sense.  I am 30 - if I didn't have an ID I would completely understand being turned away.  But, 62...  I feel sorry for this business because they lost the money we would have spent and ended up using next door.  Again, I fully appreciate safety but this person at the door was ridiculous.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Good spot to stop if you need to get a late night fill up. Tried the 5 alarm burger one night and bacon cheeseburger another night. The jalapeno puffs were the best thing we had. Can be a bit of line depending on the time you stop by. Once you order food comes out pretty fast. Staff was hit and miss, 2nd night seemed like they were less than thrilled to be there. I get it a bunch of drunks stumbling in to eat is less than desirable but I think I would expect that during the shift. Good food, not great but not bad.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Big crowds very tight. Several floors of music.  Very pricy for drinks.  Music and history was great.  Great to visit once.  Many other great ones down the hill

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Went here for bluegrass brunch on a Sunday - waited about an hour, but for a brunch place, that's a good sign that people like it! I got the breakfast tacos which were delicious. Service could have been better but it was pretty busy that day. Nice live music while dining. :) Would definitely return!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Live music on top floor great!...over priced drinks ($5 bud light, $8 well) eh guess that's ok...warm beer????!!?? Plus rude top floor bartender who would not take it back right after we bought it??...No thanks. Luckily most of us had a good buzz going by this time and it was our last stop of the night. I talked with another friend who had been there before and apparently warm beer is common at tootsies because they get so busy. They should really take care of that for the price they charge. Plus I should mention it was 24 degrees out, no reason for warm beer that night.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
While the bars around Tootsie's are always bumping, even in the middle of the day, only one consistently has a line. And for good reason. Now while I spent at least a few minutes in more bars than I can remember in Lower Broad, there were some things that made Tootsie's stand out:

A giant fan on the top floor - it was humid as hell that weekend. Like, actual Hell. That fan was a lifesaver and us guys spent time rotating in and out of its blast.

A big open balcony, just to chill out at and people watch.

The best bands I'd heard all weekend. Not sure if we just got lucky, or Tootsie's really gets the best performers, but I was thoroughly entertained whenever we were here.

It just felt like a legit party on the top floor. Like I was at a concert that I didn't have to buy a ticket for.

Yes, it's crowded as hell, but for good reason. Sometimes it's just right to go along with the crowd.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Started out a 5 then my husband got ripped off in the third floor men's room by two guys charging people to use it !sucks check your rest rooms more often

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
My friends and I were killing some time downtown before the Titans/Packers game a couple weeks ago and decided to stop here for a couple hours. Considering it was a Saturday afternoon on Broadway, it actually wasn't too busy inside. We were able to grab one of the booths that they have, which was nice. This is definitely more of a dive (although I've been to some places that were more dive-y than this) but it's not terrible. The beer is pretty cheap, and the bartenders are super friendly.

I went to the bathroom and there was an employee in there giving people soap and paper towels and stuff. That was definitely unexpected in this type of place, but I can appreciate it. I would definitely come back here again, and possibly try some of the food that people seem to think is decent. A good spot downtown if you're trying to avoid the crowds at some of the more popular bars.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great atmosphere of tourists listening dancing to country and rock standards at this historic honky tonk bar. A hefty Jack Daniels on rocks in plastic cup is  $7.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Good old fun. Go for the music and crowd. Pass on the food. Make sure to floor hop. Great service!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Best place on Broadway St.  During three night we try almost all the bars and Tootsie's had the best bands and service.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Sunday night, got in line at 4:55 pm for 6 pm show. Didn't get in to that show, but were 20/21 in line for the 8 pm writers show, which was amazing! Well worth the 2+ hr wait! Food is mediocre bar food but great service in a packed house.

name: Tin Roof
text: Came here for lunch & had fantastic service food was great too. Being from OZ needed a bit of a hand with directions & the young lady was so helpful & friendly. Wen in Nashville nxt I'd def come by here again

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
We have been hearing about tootsies, so we decided to get in, the bouncer on the door said that I can't take my camera in, so I had to go back and leave in the car.
The place is crowded but you can stand or sit comfortably, they have 3 stories, we have been to the first 2 stories, each one had a live music .the drinks are reasonably priced
$7 for a beer. I think you should give it at least a quick visit

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great music and great times. Very chill and a lot of fun. Always something going on and the bands are great. The shots are expensive but what isn't on Broadway. Just stick with beer and you aren't breaking the bank.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Awesome hamburgers, terrible cover bands. Enough said. I tend to eat and run because the cover bands are always garbage (and I simply hate cover bands). When the bands aren't playing, this is a cool place to hang out, drink beers and eat.

For you Predators fans out there, they will give you one free beer prior to the game if you come in wearing Predators atire.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great place to drink hang out and listen to music. We will return on our next visit to Nashville

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: First time I ate here it was great so I was excited when my boyfriend suggested going for dinner last night. I ordered the same dish I loved on my last visit - the zucchini tacos. Unfortunately, they were pretty awful this time around. The zucchini was covered in such large globs of beer batter that it didn't cook through all the way, resulting in a crispy outside and raw doughy inside. Not good. Our server did remove it from the check, thankfully. My boyfriend's smoked meatloaf was ok, but the jalapeño Mac and cheese was disappointing... it was just regular Mac and cheese with a couple jalapeño slices on top. Overall, the service was ok but the food definitely wasn't worth the price point. Probably won't go back.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Can't comment on the food, but my bar experience was very very poor. Ordered a cocktail which had little to no alcohol in it, when I commented on it to the bartender, my partner and I got a very rude response rather than an apology. Shouldn't have kept drinking there but ordered another drink to give a second chance. Same scenario next time... When I politely asked for a little more alcohol in the drink I had, the bartender charged me for a double and almost wouldn't speak to me the rest of the night. I attend bars regularly and know what constitutes as rude behavior from both customers as well as servers... Being extremely polite and borderline apologetic for my preferences, the bartender was extremely negative and generally unpleasant on top of the poor service provided. Will likely never return, especially after reading negative food reviews from other customers.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Paradise Park Trailer Resort
We decided to grab a quick meal here. One side is more of a "trailer parked themed" bar. The other side has a tacky diner theme where you order at the counter and then pick up at another counter in the back. There are several booths and tables. I got a grilled cheese with tater tots and my husband got the single- wide burger with tater tots. It was all very good. It was a good place to grab a quick bite to eat if you are walking down the Broadway strip in Nashville.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Awesome spot to grab food after the bars, the jalapeño cheese fritters are amazing. The staff is very friendly and the crowd is usually heavily intoxicated so it's cool to see the staff so calm and patient when dealing with customers.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
I'm giving 5 stars for the show. 
It's worth it.
We went on a Saturday 6:30 show, with out reservations. There was no cover, but there was a wait... Like we got there at 4:30 and were the last people to get in. I know the website says 28 seats that "no reservations". Can get in on, but they only let in the 1st 20-24, then you can wait for cancellations and get in at 6:15. If you don't have reservations it's all a maybe. So your best bet is to get them (good luck :)) if you don't, show up early, and hour at least.

Nothing outstanding to say about the service or food/drink.  But the show was great, ours was artists in the round.
We sat in the back pew, but it's so small there isn't a bad seat.
Don't forget about the 7$ min, even if there is no cover. Cover is for the artists, 7 is for the house.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Brisket hash was not great. Chicken fried chicken biscuit was described by my friend as "About as good as KFC". Service was great.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The worst of the tourist bars on broadway, 7$ for a bottle of pbr . Directly next door they are 3$. Seems like greedy ownership as this deters the average folk from tipping the band accordingly

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The brisket Mac and Cheese was amazing. Perfect portions. The waitress, her name was Cat, was so personable, fun, and made the experience even better. Will definitely be back.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Loved it! We had a blast. Great music and the food was pretty good too. Fun to go in the back alley entrance like the old performers did. Follow the white footprints.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
The Stone Fox is the first of what I hope are many places to call the Nations home.  A restaurants and live music venue, the Stone Fox is a great place to enjoy some great food and drinks and see some great up and coming local bands.  I have been here for everything from brunch to late night shows to Nashville Outlines, a day-long music bonanza showcasing some of Nashville's best.  

Considering all this place has to offer, it's a bit small and the staff a bit thin, but if you have patience its not an issue.  Some items on the menu are definitely better than others (great sandwiches, but brunch isn't my favorite) but they do make great drinks.  They don't have a lot of parking so be aware of that when coming to visit, and there really isn't anything around the Stone Fox (yet) so keep that in mind when coming out here for shows.  However, again, this is a great live music venue to see some really great new acts before they hit it big.  

The Stone Fox is basically an all-day kind of hangout, and I hope to see more of these in the Nations soon.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Had a blast here. Very loud, crowded, youthful scene. If you like quiet, laid back bars- don't come here. Definitely a scene for bachelorette parties and college kids. Three floors, live music

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great bar for music and people watching.  They have multiple floors with a roof top seating area.  Each floor has their own act playing.  Music was very good, but the food and drinks were not good.  Drinks were served in plastic cups and food was terrible.  Service was very slow.  My advice would be to eat elsewhere and come to Tootsie's for the entertainment later.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: OMG THE BURGER WAS TO DIE FOR! If you want a good burger please go here first! I think that's all I remember though LOL

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
The Good:
1. The potted smoke- though, note this terrine is a smooth texture which I know bothers some people.  I loved the flavor.
2. The wait staff had terrific recommendations.
3. Great, creative Cocktail list
4. The Burger (dunked in cheese soup) - This might be my favor burger in Nashville.  The Ciabatta bun was crispy providing a great contrast to the soup dunk.

The Ugly
1. To be fair, this is more like the mediocre... I had high expectations for the Speakeasy downstairs, but the space is too big.  It feels more just like a bar/holding room for those waiting for their table.  I'd prefer to see something akin to the Office in Chicago if I'm going to a "speakeasy"- small room, no windows, comfy seating for a few, not for 50.
2. The Brussels Sprout Hash- This should be called mashed potatoes with 3 sprouts on top.  I was surprised given the hype around this dish which was sold to us as one of the most popular on the menu.  It was delicious, but did not meet expectations.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Average at best.  Too many better options in Nashville.  

Brought friends from Boston and was embarrassed with the service

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: It was our favorite place as far as hanging out and listening to good music. If you get a chance to catch Beth Beighey and Laurel Taylor, do it!! They were wonderful and seem to be regulars. The food looked good, but we didn't eat there. It was nice to sit on the top floor and have the view of the town. Can't wait to go back soon!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
The name is deceiving. 

We went here before the Maroon 5 concert, after we couldn't wait for one hour to get food at Rippy's Bar-b-que. Bad decision.

This place indeed looked very nice outside and they also had a band playing inside the restaurant, but that's about it. We had the burgers and fries. They were so greasy and have been fried to death. I thought McDonald burgers tasted better than these craps I just ate. Although I was starving, I took 2 bites and threw the rest in the trashcan. The food was definitely a foodie's nightmare. 

Please spend your hard-earn money somewhere else.

2013/#52

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: By far my favorite honky tonk bar in Nashville.   The staff were great and the live music was even better.  Fantastic venue.   I will always return here every time I'm in town

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I'll give this place a 4 overall but it flirts with a 3. First off, it's a very cool music spot and vibe and the band we saw was great! Played a lot of fun crowd songs and the singer had an awesome male voice. The food I would rate a 3. I ordered the pulled chicken sandwich and fries and it didn't blow me away by any means. Not bad but nothing to tell mom and dad about. Had a few beers and 1 Moscow Kentucky mule that was good but at 9 dollars quite expensive. I would come back but it's not at the top of my to do list.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Pretty cool space, despite being divey and louuuud. During the day there is plenty of room to stand and sit. The drinks are pricey, but the bands are good and they seem to have a lot of fun. There were some very cute and endearing Texan girls playing when I visited - they rocked!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Perhaps my favorite bar on Broadway, Tootsie's was definitely a highlight of the music side of Nashville. On each level of the bar there is a different band performing, and were were lucky enough to experience an absolutely killer band on display on the first floor this past Friday night. The band was great and the lead singer was on fire. She had an amazing voice and absolutely brought down the house - this experience was the highlight of my Nashville trip. 

This was one of the top rated bars when I researched Nashville before making the trip and I'm glad it didn't disappoint. I would definitely recommend making Tootsie's a priority when visiting the city.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Heard good things about this place before I visited Nashville. Looked at Yelp on the night we decided to head over, mainly to get the address, but started reading the reviews. Was alarmed by the negative ones which claimed service was awful, but there were so few I figured, "Eh, let's give it a shot." Should have listened to them. We were seated and then not waiting on for a while. We finally ordered and got our drinks pretty quickly, but took over 20 minutes to get the one small appetizer. Took another 5-10 to get our meals. Three veggie burgers and fries and one order of the house chili. All of the veggie burgers and fries were cold and seemed like they'd been plated and left out for quite a while. My fiance wasn't thrilled about the chili but at least it was the proper temperature. The waitress apologized for the cold food and the long time it took because there was a meeting in there and "they told us they weren't going to eat, but then ordered food and there was only one cook so he got slammed." When we arrived, the meeting was over and there were people milling around having drinks and talking, and definitely not eating. In fact, it looked like they'd had maybe had some group appetizers or something, but there weren't signs of a large group having eaten dinner, let alone having JUST eaten dinner. 
The server was nice enough but service was just dreadful. They really didn't seem to have any idea as to what they were doing. Also, the veggie burger was the worst I'd, personally, ever had, and the other 2 on the party weren't crazy about their burgers, either. Would definitely never make the trek out to this place again.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Live good music, delicious food at one of Nashville's oldest and best venues. Kinda small so get there early to get in line so you can enter into a Nashville dream!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
I was pretty excited to check out this famous Nashville spot and even though I only got to see it during the day, I loved it! I feel like you can really feel all the talent that has come through this "lounge."

I love the live music scene on Broadway and this was no exception to the greatness that one would expect! The prices were pretty standard for that of a Broadway bar. It can get pretty crowded, but that is also to be expected anywhere on Broadway. Overall, I love Tootsie's and I can't wait to go back!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This bar was pretty cool but definitely a tourist trap. I honestly had more fun at other bars but you really can't not go here. The downstairs band was hands down better than the one upstairs and so was the crowd. Great country music, few mash ups, and cheap drinks - I mean really, what more can you ask for?

Get there early!

name: Tin Roof
text: Not a club-goer. Ate there for lunch on a whim while downtown. Staff was decently friendly. Waiter was just going through the motions basically. Salad was FAR too small for cost of 8.95. Food was ok. It's a live music bar in actuality so I wouldn't recommend it for lunch.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: If you're a visitor and can get tickets, it's a must do in Nashville. If you're a local and haven't gone, go. A great intimate atmosphere with live song writers and has such great history, not to mention a great tshirt selection. If you can't get tickets you can get in line for first come dibs which is cool. Seating is kind of communal so you get to know the people around you and have a good conversation. Full bar, and food is simple but really good. Not a place where you can go and gab away all night, so if you want a nice first date spot, super intimate choice. Been there 3 times, and going in a few weeks.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I had been to the sutler a few times before for drinks downstairs or Monday night writer's nights, but I hadn't eaten there. This week, I met my dad there for lunch and we were overwhelmingly impressed with the food and the whole lunch vibe. We both live and work near the 12th south/Melrose area, and there just aren't many places for lunch that you could find easy parking, bring a big group or have a business meeting. The Sutler will now be a go-to lunch spot for me, and I'm excited to try dinner!

Being gluten-free, I also generally find my lunch options a little limited. All of the sutler's salads and meat and three plates sounded like delicious gluten free options. I went with the mustard tarragon chicken, and it was fabulous! Filling but light, flavorful and fresh. 

My dad got the hot catfish tacos and I bet he's still talking about how much he loved them. They were basically like nashville's hot chicken in fried catfish nugget form, served in a corn tortilla with some fresh slaw and whatnot. I was really jealous not to be able to try them (for fear of flour in the batter), because they looked amazing and dad was overjoyed.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
This place is a hidden gem! 
Don't let the location scare you away. It tucked away off of a few sides streets and on a corner. The decor keeps your head turning and looking throughout the whole restaurant. I loved the USA sign. 
A few of my favorite things: awesome seating on the front porch, mason jar drinks, large bar, amazing outside seating, cool pallets with flowers and greens and friendly service. 
I came with a group of girls for brunch and were very please with food and service. We loved the bloody Mary's! Breakfast tacos all the way! Our food was fresh and delicious. Don't pass up this little gem!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Every floor had a band and drinks flowing.  It was like A Vegas strip but on floors. Super fun place!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Way too expensive and overcrowded. We wanted the rooftop bar and there were hundreds of people packed in upstairs that we could not get through the crowd. Huge disappointment my well rum and coke was 9 bucks for a very tiny plastic cup. Bartender was rude and unfriendly. Would not recommend unless you're 21, obnoxious, and want to spend a fortune on mediocre watered down drinks.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
We came here for lunch. Had the Woolworth burger and gumbo. The burger came with fries. The fries were over cooked. The burger and gumbo had an average taste to them.  The total cost for lunch was $23 including drinks.

The restaurant was designed to look like the finer Woolworth store, and had a man playing the piano throughout lunch. We enjoyed listening to the music. The customer service was good.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Up until a few weeks ago, this would be a "six star" review. The bar downstairs was our new favorite place in Nashville. The 3 stars here are purely for the environment. It used to have the best, creative, well made drinks rivaling any place like the Patterson House in Nashville. And the pork rind nachos were one of the most unique things in town to recommend. However that has now been removed from the menu (which I understand there will be changes of course.) But the most disappointing things is that they have changed their drinks to be more generic. Gone are the wonderfully creative mixology drinks full of flavor and character. All we are left with is generic drinks mad to look fancy but that you could get anywhere. Such a shame. Very sad.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: My girlfriend was so excited to come to nashville because she wanted to see where some of the greatest country music stars of all time had got there start. We went to the open mic night at 630 and were told we would not be allowed in and that there was another open mic night later that night by the staff so we came back at 815 for the "open mic night." The first open mic night was free but when we showed up it turns out it was a 12$ cover charge at the door plus 7 dollar food and drink order minimum and it wasn't open mic night but rather a blues band that in my opinion was not good at all. The cafe was in terrible shape and falling apart and we were all stuffed packed into this small cafe. I wouldn't even call it a cafe. It had no theme there was no real selection for food or drinks. The waitress we had was very rude and disrespectful. I was very disatisfied with the entire night and me and my girlfriend ended up leaving early. Will not return to this place in the future.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This is the place to be in Nashville. We got two seats right by the band on the second floor. The bands were great and talented. The beer is a little on the expensive side with $6 for the Bud light but you are downtown and listening to music so you can't complain to hard.

name: The Stone Fox
text: My friends and I ate here as soon as we got to Nashville as it was suggested by our Airbnb host. The place is really nice, I dig their decor, and they seem to hold a lot of shows, smaller acts from different cities, which is super cool. Our server was prompt and pleasant. We had Mint Juleps but it tasted too strong. Although we haven't had Mint Juleps before so we weren't sure if it were supposed to be strong.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Came here for bottomless brunch on Fourth of July with a group of seven. We waited for an hour or an hour and half to be seated but I was surprised that we were even able to get a table as there was a ton of people there. I had the breakfast tacos with a side of potatoes which were both pretty bland even after topping it with the salsa that it came with. I doused them in hot sauce to make them edible. The servers were pretty prompt about refilling our drinks and there was a live music so overall it was a good time.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: While at times it can be hectic at the Sutler when Mo's working you don't need to worry. That girl is on it! She recommended the express lunch and it was delicious and a great value! They have a great brunch on the weekends but I started coming for lunch and happy hour. Mo has to be one of the best in the industry and makes my day when she's working!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Paradise Park is a perfect place to go on a weeknight before a show at Bridgestone. While everyone else is jamming up Rippy's or Brewhouse, you can be left in peace (relatively) at Paradise Park.

Standard divey bar on Broadway. Some interesting features include:
- Live band (ok, no different than the other bars, but worth noting)
- Photo booth right up front when you walk in
- Skee ball
- an old beat up convertible demolition derby car that you are more than welcome to sit in and take pics and look redneck
- basketball games in back
- crane games (my favorite)
- decently strong drinks

They do have bar food but...I don't really recommend eating here. There's better bar food in town, so just go there. Keep this one for drinking.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
You will want to come hungry to Woolworths, the portions are huge & the staff are fantastic. We had the reuben & mercy me it was incredible. I am a hearty eater but thank goodness we shared this sandwich. 

The food is reasonably priced & a great value for the quality of food. The extraordinary history of the Woolworths is not to be missed & the pictures throughout the restaurant highlight the fight for equality. 

We liked it so much we are returning before we depart Nashville, a must stop on your tour of Nashville.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
What an incredible, nostalgic breakfast at the counter of Woolworth's on 5th. Wow. Just wow. 

We were fairly concerned with parking availability, but easily found a parking place at the public parking lot around the corner, not even a block away. We made the mistake of trying to park in the parking garage across the street, but were kindly instructed that was for business parking only. Oops. Lol! 

Upon walking into the building, it was exactly like I thought it would be! We were immediately in love with the history and felt a little bit transported back in time. 

We had table reservations but decided to sit at the counter. Jonathon was our server and he was such a dream! He was so knowledgeable and ultra friendly with such a beautiful smile. 

We ordered from the breakfast menu and selected sweet potato pancakes with jalapeno bacon and the Hoppin John omelet. All was delicious! After a second cup of their awesome coffee, we took a few minutes to tour the downstairs area where they feature live music and a second bar area. Theres also another area upstairs, but it was rented out for a private event. 

Such a wonderful experience and we will definitely go back! Highly recommend.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Oh Tootsies.  I don't know why but I found myself here on 3 separate nights in Nashville.  Why?  Well probably because of no cover, 3 floors of live music and a super cool roof top lounge that you can easily escape the crowd and people watch the hustle and bustle down on Broadway.  Each time we had a good time, and saw good music and talked to good people.  TIp, enter from the rear though the alley on a weekend to avoid the line and super packed downstairs room!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
So, this is The Nations, huh? Interesting. After being gone for so long, I have a hard time remembering if certain areas of the city (or, outside the city as this area technically is) had names/designations or if this is an outgrowth of population explosions, search for housing and what not. Whatever the reason, increased interest/activity in urban renewal* is usually a good thing. So, The Nations... and The Stone Fox.

I'd heard much about this out-of-the-way spot long before coming here and am pleased to note that it lived up to its billing. It's moody, interesting, fun, and full of potential. Kudos to the owners for having the vision and concept. And kudos, also, for having a 2 for 1 beer special going on with Bingo on a quiet Monday night. I can dig it. And, I should dig it, given the '70s throwbacks throughout the air and on the walls. $3 well drinks made things go down pretty easily, as well. Being that I was hungry as well as thirsty, I studied the menu for some choice eats. I almost went to town on the black bean chicken chili nachos (right? how good does that sound?) but our waitress talked me in to the comparatively healthy chickpea/beet veggie burger... which I, then, proceeded to make unhealthy by 'Elising' it with bbq sauce, onion ring, pickles, cheddar cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion, and avocado topping. Of course, it was magically delicious. How could anything *not* be with all those amazing toppings. The veggie burger itself was a bit crumbly but that's par for the course with homemade veggie burgers.

Food coma starting, I got my second of the 2 for 1 beer and walked around a bit. The dj was spinning '70s tunes on vinyl. The bartender was doing some interesting things behind the bar. But my attention was held by the deck. This wooden charmer was made for warm weather and cold beer. I'll be back for it. There are a lot of good things going on at The Stone Fox. Regardless of where you live in the metro area, hop on over and give it a spin. 

*Let's keep it responsible.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Loved this place! We visited on a Friday night. We had drinks, pimento cheese, meatloaf and pot roast. Everything was wonderful! Our server was attentive and gave great recommendations. This was a lively spot for a Friday night dinner, not too loud though. We had the most fun, we loved the decor, and history. Overall everything was fantastic. We will be back. Thanks Jordan!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I love this bar so for how old it looks and feels like i am your at a bar from home. Such good music and old Decor. The drinks are reasonably priced and the bartenders are nice.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
The food experience in Nashville has been superb. Spot after spot, I am delighted. The Sutler did not disappoint!! My meal was absolutely mouth watering and The Gambler (drink) was made to perfection!! 

The space is huge... There's a billiards room downstairs as well as a lounge. Seems like a pretty decent spot for nightlife. I will have to revisit when they have live music. The happy hour is great, the food is great, service great... Get on down to The Sutler ASAP!

name: Tin Roof
text: This is one of my favorites! Treat yourself to the Smay and enjoy the scene. This is a great place to go with friends when wanting to grab drinks, listen to music and talk. They have live music events and always a great place to see the up and coming! The fishbowl is always a fun drink too, but the Smay is my favorite drink in all of Nashville

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Historic Tootsies!  While this place reminded me of some of my old hole in the wall bar haunts from college - we had a great time at the 3rd floor bar.

Quick service, cold beer, yummy pretzel bites with cheese and really fun singers on stage.  

Great visit.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Wow!  This HAS to be someplace you visit!  Great historical value!!!  Everyone in this place was polite and talkative.  Great food and service!  Sam made some amazing libations!!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: You've got to put Tootsies on your "must see" list.  Great atmosphere and they get the best talent.  We loved new comer Rachel Curtis.  Watch out for the pimento cheese bites ... my mouth was on "fiya!!!"

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Happy Hour review: 
When looking for dining options downtown, it can be difficult to find something that a local would want to visit, but I am happy to report that Woolworth is a really nice option! This diner-style open concept is unique and gives a feeling of art deco. The projector showing old movies and background music adds to that feeling I'm sure. I love the giant long bar and stools; the overall vibe of the place is really nice. We grabbed a seat around 5:30 for happy hour. They offer drink specials with a daily cocktail for $5 and wine, mules, and martinis for $6. We ended up ordering a bottle of wine for $25 or so and split it between us. For food we ordered the fried pickles, okra, and jalapenos plus the soup of the day which was broccoli cheese. It was a nice snack and everything tasted really good! It was a perfect way for 2 locals to kick off a fun night out (cheaply) adjacent to Broadway. I'll definitely be back to sample more of the menu!

name: Tin Roof
text: VERY cool dive bar. Decent prices. Large beer menu. Cool atmosphere. Definitely would return.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Bridal party came here as a result of a recommendation and were wearing matching tanks. Male bridesmaid attempted to join and was denied because men in tanks are not allowed as a rule. Fine. Put a woman's top on him to allow him in as most of our party was already inside and asked to speak to the manager (picture attached). He said he really didn't care what the rules were as long as he got paid by the owner. So.. TO THE OWNER... stop living in 1854 this is bachelorette central and we want to support your business within reason. Your manager made it very clear that there was no discussion to be had and was Borderline homophobic in his responses to my questions regarding the bars policy. All experinces with this jackass were rude, condescending, and fake. Would not recommend this bar to anyone looking for a GENUINE Nashville experience as this bar only values numbers and revenue.

Note- manager refused to provide me with a real name. Pictures attached to ensure accountability.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: My experience at Woolworths on 5th was good, I had the half fried chicken and it was very flavorful (well seasoned) and crunchy! The side dishes mac &  cheese, sweet potatoes and collards greens were on point as well. My only suggestion, based on the theme of the restaurant would be to play music of that era.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Honestly, we didn't go here for the food, but the lure of seeing upcoming music artists perform. We didn't make a reservation a week out, so we got there at 4pm, braved the cold weather and stood by the front door to get "first come" seating in the overflow church pews for the early 6pm show. We got in and were delighted with the front pew seating we were given. Most of the bistro sized tables were packed with 4 chairs and squeezed into the small performance area. I'd choose bar seats or the tables around the outside walls if I made a reservation. 
My 5 star rating is hugely an indication of the "music experience" provided by this intimate setting and the four fabulous entertainers we saw tonight. I would highly recommend this venue to experience the journey aspiring artists follow in search of making it big.  We actually enjoyed this performance better than our Ryman concert earlier this week!   
Don't miss this place! I wish I was a local so I could come here weekly.
So, food? Fish/chips, burgers, salads and nice selection of beer.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsies is a Nashville treasure! The legacy of this bar and all the great talent that has walked in this place is legendary. The bar in its self is a wonder for the eyes. Both the food and the music is a feast for your soul. The place is filled with happy music loving people with a great staff, strong drinks and an even better story to tell written all over. You can spend hours here just looking at all the priceless memorabilia! If you are coming to Nashville then you must stop by for some true Southern Comfort! As Always, Enjoy!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Room had weird smell. Had to open windows to get rid of deodorizer smell.  Breakfast/ restaurant was just a closed off dark and dingy conference room. But the bar was very good. Comfortable seating good food and snacks!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I was a little scared to check in here after reading some of the reviews but good news y'all: the place has been renovated and is nice now. It is located in a beautiful area set off from everything which worked for me. 
The only complaint I have is the doors need soundproofing - I could hear the light bulbs in the hall! 
My room was newly redecorated and had everything you would want in a room. Nice comfy bed, big TV, etc etc. I didn't spend much time in it because I was here on business and we were out and about most of the time.
I dined in the bar area and enjoyed some chicken fingers and waffle, peach cobbler, drinks, and also had the breakfast buffet in the restaurant and that was nice.
Overall, a very nice property, friendly staff and I would stay here again.
Four stars only because of the door situation.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Bouncers are rude and racist.  There are plenty of other bars to give your patronage to than this place.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: This place is a little too old and used to be four stars. Spending four nights here. After night one, I paid to upgrade to a suite on the third floor. Much cleaner and quieter. I can't hear my neighbors coughing and chatting at 1am anymore. It's pretty worn down and it needs an overhaul, so don't expect much and you'll be fine. No sign of bed bugs, just generally "been around for awhile". That all said, the staff is tops! They act 5 star and have been accommodating and professional; which makes up for an 1990's place on the cheap.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Not really much to write about here just stopped in for a drink while walking around town and the use the restrooms, the music wasn't too bad

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Went during the day to enjoy nice weather on the balcony. They had a good live band playing. I would probably only come during the day if it's nice to enjoy the outdoors!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
This was one of the cleaner, most comfortable bars on the block. 

It is dark in there, which keeps it much cooler than the sweltering heat outside. 

The live music was better than some of the local competitors and the drink prices were comparable. 

This place is probably closer to 3.5 stars.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Burgers were great, sriracha mayo was amazing, the little guitar they served my two year olds fish sticks on was awesome and staff was super friendly. Appetizer was cold but I still enjoyed it. Food came out quick. Valet guy was incredibly nice, should have caught his name.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Excellent hotel!  Very friendly service, clean environment, fast service. Room was very clean and housekeeping was friendly. Great value for the money spent on the room. Convenient for commuting to downtown. Less than $20 can ride from downtown

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I was here for CMA fest over the past week and spend quite a few hours in here a few different days. We had Jackie as our server and let me tell you she was OUTSTANDING!! The food was decent but the service was incredible. :)

name: East-Centric Pavilion
text:
This little venue really surprised me! I never even knew it existed until this Friday. Hidden behind a little shopping center on Fatherland, the East-Centric Pavilion is a little gem of a venue.

Its a pavilion, so there isn't really much to describe. However, the bathrooms were clean, the stringed lights were beautiful and parking wasn't terrible. You may have to park on the road, but that has never scared me. (Parallel parking QUEEN right here) I love a good open air venue. I'd say rent it!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Some of the nicest staff in the Starwood family of hotels. I have stayed in this location on several trips to Nashville and they never fail. I wanted to stay an additional day this trip and use some of my SPG points. They had no more rooms on the club floor that I am used to, but they happily offered me a deluxe room on another floor and still gave me club access with me even asking along with comps for the bar and dinner. Overall great experience. Had some noisy neighbors on this floor, but that's what happens on a Saturday night in Nashville!

name: FooBar
text: I love the comments about it being a  dive bar that is smoke filled and the music is too loud. Well, yeah and if that is not what you are looking for, you will not love this place. It does have a great space for live music, the bartenders are great and I can't say I have ever had a bad time here.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Really awesome spot with GREAT booze and great music. The have different flavors of sip-able moonshines. I personally loved the blackberry moonshine - it was delicious -- it tasted like a very, very strong cocktail. The bartender on the night I visited (Friday, July 29) was awesome. She was friendly and made great suggestions. She talked to us casually and really seemed like she was having a fun night at work. I would definitely return to this bar on future trips to Nashville.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Freaking love this place. Always a good band, a pretty mixed crowd age-wise, great drinks, and a cool interior. Lot of wood and antlers, and the "moonshine" list is awesome. It's a nice break from the douche bag spots scattered down Broadway.

name: Limelight
text: This venue is the absolute worst place i have ever attend. The concert tickets said the concert would start at 930 and would be over by 230 , well we got in line at 9 and waited in the cold until 1040 because the doors didnt get opened until 1020. When inside we were first to the front of the stage to see 21 savage , well as the night went on alot of hood rat girls tried to fight us for our spot and they were pushing, shoving, and threating to beat us up for absolutely no reason. The security also did not do anything when we told then and they laughed with the girls and pretty much high fived them it was absolutely ridiculous.  The limelight was so unorganized and the noise is terrible there system shut dowm multiple times and everyone was just standing around and also there drinks tasted like cheap liquor. They also gave a minor a 21+ drinking pass.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Always packed. It's become a staple of downtown honkytonks...basically, you have to go here if you're bar hopping in town. Usually a good band, though sometimes there's a miss, but never had a bad time here. As a local, it's really fun going here just to watch the tourists drink and dance. LOL

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Went for the weekend, second time there.  First time was great and we loved it.  Terrible service this time.  No towels at the pool, everyone had to keep asking them to bring some out.  No one comes out to the pool area to take drink orders - they are losing ALOT of $ there.  Many people were complaining.  Went to the restaurant to get beverages, restaurant was empty and staff was in the kitchen chatting.  Waited 10 minutes for someone to come out.  Another couple got tired of waiting and left.  Friday they repaved the parking lot and there was nowhere to park.  We asked and were told to park in the back BEHIND the employee entrance, quite a walk.  Restaurant opens at 11:00 for a few hours then they close until later in the day.  Bedding and pillows are HORRIBLE. We each had 2 flat pancake pillows and could have used 2 more each.  Sheets are so stiff they weren't even comfortable.  There was a piece of toilet paper under the sink from the prior guests and still there when we left.  After housekeeping changed the sheets, they were nice enough to leave the used pillowcases on our couch for us.  They do have balconies so you can sit outside if you wish.  We will stay somewhere else next time.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: The new owners replaced American hard working Veterans with illegal immigrants!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
I went to see a famous musician here, during the Songwriter's festival and I have to say, it was not the best place to enjoy music.
Whether it was the line outside, the way they take the tickets, the way they herd you in and everyone fights for a seat.....
Nah........  I didn't like this venue, in fact, I left early.
