I wouldn't go back. I would avoid this place for watching performers.

name: The End.
text: The venue was great. Although it was a bit of a slow night, the bartender was not attentive and seemed indifferent to my service. Saw a great show there, and plan to return.

name: FooBar
text: This is a very cool place. It's in east Nashville but its not to hipster. It's got tons of space and plenty to do. While I was there we played pool, darts, and some awesome game called drunk Jenga. Very worth checking out.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Stop in to say you went to the bars on broadway in Nashville, but there are better places to see live music and have a few drinks. Most people in Nashville will tell you the same.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Nice music venue. It can get a bit too overcrowded which for me takes some of the fun away. They have a full bar with awesome beer choices. The prices are nice too. I've never paid more than 10 dollars to come inside and that's a plus for me. I go to the monthly Boom Bap party and I always have a great time. Be careful at the bar because the bathroom is tiny and almost always occupied. Ha! Any party here, I would most definitely go.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Another awesome bar in Nashville, with great music....very busy but worth checking out.  Memorabilia everywhere and cool to listen to some talented live music.  Friendly service....didn't eat just had drinks.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
We went bar hopping in Nashville, and made a pit stop here. 

The music was great, as were the drinks and the people. The rooftop patio is awesome and the weather was perfect so I very much loved that! 

Unfortunately everything closes at 2:00 in Nashville so the night ended pretty quickly considering we got to Broadway around 12:30.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
Great artist here, left a Paul Simon T-shirt and they saved it for us!!!
Great people highly recommend and not shoulder to shoulder!!!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Always another good bar spot for Nashville! I haven't run into one that I don't like. Only came during the night time hours for entertainment and for drinks. I always enjoy the bands that are here downtown, no matter which bar you are in. This one is no exception to the norm. Definitely make a stop in here, at least for a drink and to listen to one of the many bands that perform here.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Best bruschetta I've had anywhere! My cousin and I always make it a point to hit up the Hard Rock in every city. Staff was very friendly. Great location!

name: The 5 Spot
text:
Dive Bars thy name is Home.

Meaning, like many cool dive bars I would move in and live in this place except for one major, glaring, awful, horrific issue with The 5 Spot:  cigarette smoke.

I love all things hipster (GQ magazine once referred to The 5 spot as "Nashville's Best Hipster Meat Market") I love all things rock and roll and seedy and cool and stuff but for the love I hate cigarettes and cigarette smoking.  It's nasty.  It smells nasty.  It causes birth defects and cancer and a host of other dark afflictions and at The 5 Spot you can still smoke inside meaning the rest of us are stuck sucking in the cloud of noxious chemicals while you smokers get your high.  Ewwwwwww.

Otherwise welcome to a very cool place!  I don't watch the TV show Nashville but I heard that The 5 Spot is featured a lot.  In the world of reality there have been some great acts that have received their start here in the past decade that they have been operating, and in homage to older, golden days gone by there are some pretty neat vinyl albums scattered across the walls.  (There is also a massive Elvis mural in the ladies bathroom that you don't want to miss).

The 5 Spot doesn't just host up and coming musical acts.  It also hosts fun dance parties (images of my friend Matt slamming a pretend sledgehammer down to Peter Gabriel's "Sledgehammer" on the dance floor come to mind) that are themed such as Monday 50s and 60s groove night and the night I went which was Friday 80s dance party along with popular cover acts like a recent Sunday night's tribute to the 1973 Watkins Glen summer concert that had tons of Dead songs, Allman Bros songs and of course tunes from The Band.  Standing up on the bar stool (choking in ciggy smoke) and singing "The Weight" with fellow bar patrons made for a really great Sunday night in Nashville.  My bar stool neighbor that night was from NYC and works in the music industry doing stuff for bands like Emerson, Lake and Palmer.  The kinds of people you will find in The 5 Spot will range a huge gamut from young to old.  A very cool, mixed crowd.

The Jameson on the rocks I ordered was the biggest one I've ever held thanks to the massive cocktail glass it was in and it was a cheap price.  They have great local beers on tap that sometimes run on awesome happy hours, plus loads of ice cold beer in bottles in their coolers.  You honestly can't go wrong here, just remember to bring your gas mask for those times when it gets crowded and everybody is lighting up.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Was here on July 4th! Live music jamming, beers were flowing! Must see spot if visiting Nashville. Yee Haw!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: I love Sheraton. Beautiful hotel, well kept and even though it was big enough to get lost in, they have good service! Got a great rate for the night and I love how they offered cheap shuttle service downtown on the hour! Impressed!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
We took a stroll down Broadway over the course of the weekend, trying to hit up every bar we passed. For some reason this was place was absolutely packed out. Maybe the band playing was a bit Nashville famous? Not a fan of country music so I couldn't tell you. 
There wasn't a spot at the bar nor a single seat in the house was open. The upstairs was also closed. After our group of 4 split up, standing at different spots at the bar, the one on the side & the main one & unable to grab the attention of a bartender, after 15 minutes, we left.

name: The Valentine
text: My brothers and I came to this spot during a guy's trip.  It's a dope spot; HOWEVER, the food is not good.  Grant it, I wasn't expecting much but sheesh! On the brighter side, our bartender was great!  She definitely made up for the horrible food.  Maybe we came on an off night.  DJ is decent and the rooftop is great.  Overall, not too bad.....just don't order food.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Elevators suck, breakfast food is not good. Staff was great, accommodating, friendly and willing to help!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
Favorite bar on broadway -- don't be fooled if it is less crowded to start the night.  Most folks don't walk down to 2nd when there are events at Bridgestone but just do it!

Great musicians, friendly bar staff and moonshine via the Popcorn Sutter legacy.  

There is a back door for busy nights and a 2nd story. 

Make sure you tip the gals/guys on stage !!

name: The Bridge
text: Stayed at the Renaissance Hotel in Nashville for 3 nights this past weekend. We ended up at The Bridge every night, and some of the afternoons. We loved it! Amanda was a fantastic server and always kept us well hydrated and fed :-) We loved the .99 housemaid chips and pimiento dip! Go here to start the night, and finish it! It's cool!

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: We were a bit disappointed, most of our food came out cold and we had to ask for it to be reheated. The service was fine I guess. Don't go in if it's empty is what we learned from this experience.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Terrible. Not a fun place for your bachelorette party. Overpriced. Mediocre food. Dull atmosphere. Lame music. Piss poor service...especially at the bar.

We tried to make a reservation for my friend's bachelorette night the day before and were told there weren't any more and we could try our luck. When we arrived, there were two large tables open with the correct amount of seats in sections that were open, but not busy. We were told the wait would be an hour. Then a group of men without a reservation walked in an were seated at one of the tables. Maybe they're regulars? Whatever.

We go to the bar and get a round of drinks while we wait. Despite there being 12 of us, it took the bartender 15 minutes to even acknowledge us to say "I'll be back." 10 minutes later she took our order. I offered to pay for the round to make everything easier instead of splitting checks, but because I was traveling, my bank's fraud detection kicked in and a temporary flag was placed on my card.

The waitress didn't tell me the first time it didn't go through, but ran my card so many times (I found it later) that a hold was placed on my account. Then she came back, slide my card onto the bar, and announced that my card had been declined, and promptly walked away. She practically yelled it so loudly that everyone in the party began reaching into their purses to pay. When I asked her to run it again, while I called my bank to get the hold released, she said she'd already run it 4 times. 4 times!???!!! Without discreetly approaching me first? After I got off the phone with my bank and the transaction went through, I informed her that while I was still going to tip 20% despite her lack of tact, she said curtly and attitudinally "I'm sorry you feel that way."

We continued to have a terribly long and mediocre dining experience with crappy food. While the waitress at our table was far better than the bartenders, the night was a complete bust. We didn't even go anywhere else after because Hard Rock killed the vibe. I'll not be going back to any of them.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
One of my favorite places on broadway! It has room to dance and socialize. Long bar and enough seating! 
The music is great and fun and friendly people.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Visitng TN for the first time, my friend brought me to downtown Nashville on a saturday night.  That place is poppin'.  The experience to be downtown was so much fun. Everything is new to me so I was checking out the scene.

We went into The Stage. The place was getting busy and filling up. Young & old were all having a great time.  Cort Carpenter was performing.  

I enjoyed the live band, no cover, casual dress & everyone just having a great time!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: One of the best bars in town. Will always visit when I come to town. Great music, drinks, service and talent. A 'must visit' bar when you are in Nashville!

name: East-Centric Pavilion
text: I've been to the East-Centric Pavilion at least 4 times at this point. It's hard to review a pavilion because they are pretty self-explanatory. The magic happens with the group hosting the event. The shell of the pavilion is great. It's open, the bathrooms are clean and the area surrounding it is nice. They have a wooden fence with lights on it and painted bee cutouts. They also have a string of lights on the inside. I hear the management company is easy to work with and the rental price is reasonable.

name: The 5 Spot
text: I'm only recommending this place because of the live music and it was close to where we were staying. Even though the bartender was a total jerk, you could totally tell everyone there was having a blast! Didn't stay too long, but I'd be down to give it a second shot.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text:
Worst meal of my life unless you want to eat out of an ashtray.  Everything tasted waaaay to smokey and was burnt to a crisp.

Onion rings and waitress were good which is why I can give 1star instead of 0.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: We came in Friday & Saturday of NYE weekend. Friday night there was two awesome bands and the atmosphere was fun. However, the service was just okay. The bar has a monster list of flavored liquors but no menu or drink suggestions. The lack of a menu is fine but when asked for suggestions the upstairs bartender (Saturday night) simply said "whatever you want" to every customer who walked up. Both Friday & Saturday night we encountered a young guy working as the bar back who was fairly unprofessional. Friday night I asked him for a round and he just said "that's not me" and pointed at the bartender. Saturday he was arguing with another girl working while behind the bar. Okay, you aren't here to serve AND customer service is everyone's job. He didn't even attempt to get the bartender's attention for us as she was standing at the other end of the bar (not helping anyone at the moment) too far for us to politely get her attention. Saturday night we were upstairs with another bartender who refused to suggest any drink at a bar that had nothing carbonated behind the bar for a couple of hours. We were there for NYE and the band didn't even stop for the countdown. The bartenders didn't acknowledge the countdown except for grabbing a single popper right after the nite drop, kinda. The band forgot where they were and were stopping & restarting leading up to it. Complete letdown on a night where we are out for the sole reason of ringing in the new year.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
This is by far the worst place I have eaten at. I think McDonald's is a much better food and I do not like McDonald's food.  
Server was nice but the service was slow, buffalo wings were microwave cooked cold in center. 
To make it less painful let's say I do not recommend nor would I repeat.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I enjoyed the experience at Nashvilles Hard Rock Cafe and I would definitely go again. I got the twisted mac and cheese, it was delicious, though a bit spicy if you're not interested in that. It was a classy atmosphere, with all the typical pictures, guitars, and outfits Hard Rock is known for decorating the walls. Our waitress was wonderful and helpful, refilling drinks without prompting. She also stated that we could wander around the restaurant and have a look at everything along the walls. Parking is valet, costing 15$ for 0-3HRs but that didn't deter us. Even at 9PM on a Wednesday night the street leading up to the restaurant was lively with people and music, lending to the happy atmosphere.  There was also a small gift shop inside the restaurant for anyone interested in purchasing souvenirs.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: With so many options on lower Broadway frankly on my second visit to Nashville I was surprised to see this place still open. Compared to other places on Broadway one word comes to mind "boring ". Sort of forgotten on a prime corner location overlooking the river. No rooftop bar, bands have not been particularly good, and the food certainly isn't a draw.  When I have been here I feel like I could be in any of the cookie cutter chains, TGIF, Applebee's, etc. Only plus is valet parking, but I usually don't have a car in Nashville anyway. So basically bang a left on 2nd Avenue and bypass this place.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: The logo on their employees shirt about says it all "I see you- I'm just ignoring you"

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: First off, I wish there was an option to give no stars. Honestly one of the worst establishments I've ever stepped into. Not too sure why this is such a big chain restaurant cafe whatever it's supposed to be, it's not. Worst chicken on the block it was more like rubber than anything else. Mac and cheese was cold, burger tasted like cardboard and we weren't even offered boxes to bring home our foul food. Will not be returning ever again for the rest of my years.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Service is vey poor here. Our waitress was very flighty and messed up on several occasions. The first mistake she made was she forgot to replace my side of fries with the mac and cheese side I ordered. That caused me to wait until after my whole meal was done to get my mac and cheese. The second problem was she would just disappear and take forever to replace our drinks. The last and biggest issue was my dad is a diabetic and his blood sugar was very low and when we asked our server to get bread or something she made us order garlic bread which took forever to get. My father could've passed out in that time. Overall food was ok and atmosphere was nothing special compared to restaurants around this area. Only go if desperate!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: First time guest to Nashville and I couldn't have asked for a better experience! After many hours of research and reading reviews, I selected the Sheraton Music City Hotel for our NYE get away. I was welcomed right away by both staff at the front desk. I explained I was new to Nashville and awaiting my friend's arrival. The front desk sent a special surprise to our room to make our weekend stay memorable. All of the rooms have been remodeled! It was like staying in a brand new hotel. The lobby has not been renovated yet but they explained it would be renovated next. I did hear an occasional barking dog but that was only once we were awake and getting ready to leave. We had a mini Bluetooth speaker we listened to as we got ready and slept so we never heard anything through the walls. Bed and pillows were super comfortable! The shower pressure was weaker than what I'm used to but nothing to complain about. I ate at the on-site restaurant twice and had room service once. My lunch at the onsite restaurant was a burger and fries. It was amazing! A lot of food for the price. Service was okay at the restaurant. We also had brunch at the hotel. The brunch is a breakfast buffet (that you pay for) and it was really good especially if you needed a good breakfast after being out late. For room service we ordered a pizza. The pizza was not good, so I would stay away from it. My friend arrived just in time for pizza and asked me if it was frozen... so if you like frozen pizza maybe you will like it. We had a magnificent room view of the courtyard as you see in the photo. We also fell in love with the little charging station on the couch. We took Uber everywhere we went and besides NYE night, it was $11-13 to get downtown to Broadway. I felt 100% safe. The hotel is not within walking distance of anything but with Uber you really don't need much. We booked through Hotels.com and I feel we received an excellent rate. When I return I will definitely stay after at the Sheraton Music City. I was sad to leave Nashville. For two women in their 30's, this was the best NYE we could have asked for! Thank you staff at Sheraton for making it magical!

name: The 5 Spot
text: My numero uno Nashville hangout. Have had many memorable experiences here. Can have a drop dead serious Americana/Country/Blues/ artist at 6:00 and a 80's for Ladies dance party at 9:00. For example, at 6:00 on Fridays they have a Happy Hour with a player named Tim Carroll, blues rock with an edge. There is a different theme every night from Motown to Twangy Country to Gay Dance Party. Halloween, Valentine, New years parties! Also, many known writers and musicians show up. Go to their web site, http://www.the5spot.club/ I could go on all day about the 50+ times I have been there.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Terrible place. Showed up with 12 girls. Wouldn't let one of us in because she had a backpack. Despite the dozens of backpacks seen inside. Epic fail.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Good food. Great time out on the patio with the band they had on Saturday night. A good place to check out if you want good BBQ and Brisket.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: I'm an artist performing all weekend. There is no one to service the room after 4pm. Also I had security knock on my door 2100 last night at 130am to tell me I'm talking on the phone to loud. I travel for work and need to talk to bookers and agents all over the world so the times vary from time zones. I was on an important work call schmoozing a booker for a potential job and I had to put them on hold to deal with this situation. The security not only told me to keep it down he told me that I was loud and that someone was trying to sleep mean while I hear people running and screaming in the hallway all day and night people partying intoxicated I put in ear plugs no biggie but lets not do anything about that lets pick on the sober guy in the room trying to make a sale. I showed the security my room there was no woman booze or anything shady going on I said I'm on the phone he also reminded me of the time. Gee thanks Dad I'll try to get to bed at a decent hour for school. For what I'm paying for the room, this just sucks. The room service food is very dry the chicken especially and they forgot the salad dressing and had to call and have them bring it up.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Came here after leaving another restaurant with terrible service a couple blocks away. It was late on a Saturday night and we were seated immediately. Our waitress was awesome and the food was great!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Was looking forward to eating at the Hard Rock Cafe for lunch but when we arrived they had shut the entire restaurant down for a private event. This was on a Monday and we had checked out the website on Sunday. Would've been nice to see the closure listed on their webpage before we wasted $10 to park only to have to leave and find someplace else to eat. I expected better.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Great food!!! Terrible service. Takes way too long. Waitresses are rude

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I am only writing this review to save people from the nightmare we endured. The display of Rock & Roll art and collectibles is beautiful. I could feel the history. But the service was terrible. We waited on a waiter for 15 mins. After a long wait the food was cold and had no flavor. After looking at the last review We will agree ,.McDonald's is better. Save your money and stomach. Overpriced and Overrated.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Now this is a place to watch a band, have a drink and get your people watching on!

I didn't eat here but spent some time listening to a pretty good duo (coming from a guy that really doesn't like country music), having a beer and watching the pretty mixed crowd. This place is just a well run, good feeling place for a drink and some music. The bartenders were very good, seemed to keep everyone happy with a pretty good smile (one for sure prrrrr). 

I would definitely stop in here when back in town.  Of all the places on the main strip this was a very simple place but the one I felt the most at home in. 

KT

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Older hotel. Stayed in for one night on our way to PA. Large room, semi clean. Walkway carpet was dirty. Curtains had stains on them.  We got it on Priceline so it was the cheapest we could find on a short notice.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Nice spot. Wish they had more of a variety besides country though. I ran into Ron Jeremy here which was weird haha

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This place has great music on every floor and yummy drinks! great place to dance and have some drinks. The bouncers aren't that friendly but they make sure nothing gets out of control. Right in the center of downtown Nashville , stop by and check out some bands and have a good time.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I had a very strange experience here. Due to flight delays, I didn't arrive at the hotel until about 2:30 am. When I walked up to the desk, I stood there for a long while before someone heard me in the back room and came to the front. I said hello and that I was checking in. The person working looked up at me with super angry eyes and didn't say a word. She shuffled through some papers then went back to the back for about 30 seconds. Obviously I was confused. When she came back she asked if I had ID & a credit card. So I handed each to her and she didn't say anything but walked into the back with both. She came back about one minute later and handed me a room key. Still saying nothing. I asked how to get to my room and she said I turn right and go down the hallway. I said thank you and went to my room, excited to relax, after a long day of flying and traveling alone. I open the door to find luggage and a men's suit on the bed and the bathroom door was closed. I was so confused and realized I was potentially alone in a room with a man at almost 3am. I immediately went to the front desk to tell her about my experience. This time I was helped by another woman who kind of tried to laugh it off and gave a crappy reason for the mistake. I was so tired from traveling that I just wanted to get to a room without anyone else in it. However, I had a hard time sleeping after realizing this is an establishment that gives out multiple room keys to different guests for the same room. I woke up early the next day to check out and asked to speak with a manager about what had happened. The morning front desk staff seemed mortified for me, but said no managers were available because they were in a meeting. They referred me to someone else, but not a manager. To ease my terrifying situation of being a lone woman traveler in the middle of the night who goes to find a mans things in her supposed hotel room, he asked me if I wanted a coffee... or maybe a bottle of water, because he sees I already have the water they carry, so why wouldn't I want more. I tell him no, thank you, and by this point I'm clearly shaking from being so freaked out by this weird situation and his lack of understanding how scary it was for me. He told me there was nothing they could do but apologize. I obviously was not impressed and was going to leave. He offered to sign me up for the FREE rewards program to make me feel better. I travel frequently and I have been meaning to do so, so I agree to sign up but let him know it doesn't really make anything better. So they added some points into the account. Not enough for a room though, which is fine because after that, I would have a hard time trusting another Sheraton. I left right after, and don't see myself returning here anytime soon. 

Also, the room smelled musky, they put me on the first floor with a back door leading right into the pool area, and the shower flooded. No thanks.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
How do I start the only reason we went was my granddaughter wanted to go. To say the least it was a disappointment we
Started with the sampler appetizer, actually it was really good hot fresh and was delivered to the table quickly. The noise level was such you could barely order not because it was crowded mind you there was probably less than fifteen people in the place. I know the name implies there will be music but there are limits. We decided on the cheese burgers that were supposed to be legendary, they did resemble the menu art but they were cooked dry and heavily charred needless to say we were not happy. We didn't understand why the parking lot was full and the dining room was empty, we soon figured out at fifteen dollars to park it was a great deal for parking downtown. We won't be back.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Great place to hear live music. They have a limited food menu I've never tried but looks appealing. This is such a fun area of town with all the music venues and restaurants close by. To be in an area with so many businesses, parking is typically very easy to find. There's a paid lot next to the 5 Spot that's pretty reasonably priced. Love that Lady Gaga played here on her Dive Bar tour, because now I can say she and my husband have played the same venue.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Fun place with great live music (not just country). Drinks are a tad bit on the pricey side ($8/ea for jack & coke for example). Overall, definitely recommend stopping by.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Very nice hotel. The 2 queen rooms were very spacious and the balconies were great! Comfy beds, roomy bathrooms. Restaurant and bar on site which was convenient. Staff very helpful and nice. Close to the Opry. Shuttle service is offered to get downtown as well at $10 per person. I highly recommend this hotel. We also got my birth year rate ($79) for 2 nights out of 3!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Best spot in town. We went 2 different times during the weekend. Bartenders were friendly and music talent was awesome. Small and more intimate then most bars on broadway.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I stopped here for a drink, and to hear the band, on a Wednesday evening in early June 2019, which happened to be during the CMA Country Music Awards Festival.  I am a senior citizen and a tourist, visiting Nashville for the 2nd time.  The town was crowded.  I walked into The Stage and immediately a good cover band was playing!  It was easy to get a drink, listen, and dance.  Fun!   No problems!  Easy in, easy out, and ready to visit the other bars on Music Row!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This place is by far one of my favorite bars on Broadway! It has four different rooms, all with different vibes and all with live music and their own bar. Everyone seems to love the bottom floor (main room) but I love the roof! You are right in the middle of the strip and the view is awesome- one of the tallest roofs on the row. They don't have a great craft beer selection, and  they make you wait in line to get to the roof after you've already waited in line to get into the bar. Thus, four stars. But, the bands are always solid, the dance floor is fun, and the bathroom line is always quick, so i'm pretty sold.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
The pool area and lobby are nice.  The room we stayed in was a little dated, but no major complaints.  The room was clean, but I did see a centipede and a millipede in our room.  I understand these things will happen, but I still don't like it.  This hotel is very convenient to the airport, but if you have an early flight you will have to find your own way to the airport.  They should start the shuttle service earlier in the morning.  

If you are looking to swim, the pool area is awesome.

name: Boulevard Records
text:
In all honesty, this was the most disappointing record store I've ever been to. We were on cloud nine after our cream cheese craze at Proper Bagel, it only made sense to cross the street and sift through some records!

But, but...where are all the records? No exaggeration, I looked through the entire selection within five minutes. Shelves were bare, with some categories collecting dust and nothing more. 

The girls working the front didn't seem to care that we were there, nor did I feel the need to bring up the lack of records to them. The only positive thing that I can say is the store was clean, had tons of natural light and had a comfy nook area. 

Again, I would've loved nothing more than to spend way too much money here on vinyl. Especially in Nashville -- the Music City! Oh well, hopefully they begin ordering more product to cater to the young Belmont crowd.

name: The Bridge
text: Stopped in after getting in late in Nashville on road trip from Texas. We had two Woodford old fashion drinks. We ordered salads at the bar. The salads came quick and changes were made to order. Bar team was helpful and great. Watch Astros on TV while eating. Was very enjoyable and relaxing here. Not to noisy. Restrooms were close at hand here and clean.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The Sheraton was the last of several stops on our cross country drop your child off at college trip! It was a great time and his hotel made the last day simply perfect! Close to the airport, excellent customer service, timely shuttle service but most importantly this hotel has Ashley! She is the 5 star representation of the Sheraton Brand! She was friendly, warm, kind and knowledgeable! She welcomed our tired and stressed family and made us feel relaxed and at home! Ruby ended our trip with a beautiful soul and smile!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: This is one of Nashville's best kept secrets.  I have been to Nashville 3 times recently and the talent here has always been the best.  Staff is so friendly and it is the place to visit for those of us that prefer something outside of the tourist traps.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Nice spot, live music was okay. There wasn't a cover when we visited. The bathrooms were clean.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
Three words: Apple pie moonshine. This is the best shot of hard alcohol I've ever had! Bootleggers has many different fun flavors which go down easy. Their shine carries on the legacy of Popcorn Sutton, a moonshiner from the Appalachians. The atmosphere is lively and fun. 

The venue on lower Broadway does not look like much from the outside, but once indoors it has an old saloon sort of vibe. The bar area is nice and the lighting is very fitting as there are makeshift "chandeliers" made out of old moonshine mason jars. 

Even on a Saturday afternoon when they were busy there was good service. The bartenders were great! 

Overall, not the sort of place my liver can handle on a weekly basis but should be a must for tourists. I brought three friends here who were visiting Nashville and they loved it. We unfortunately didn't get to go upstairs and hear live music but I'll be back to check it out!

name: The 5 Spot
text: DONT USE A CREDIT CARD HERE!!! My tab was 82$ and they added on a 97$ tip. I called the manager when I checked my balance and he was completely sketchy and never did anything to help me. So many other cool places to go in Nashville. Don't give a place like this business when it takes  advantage of  people just having fun with their friends.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Cool spot on Broadway. Large selection of moonshine cocktails and fun live band the night we went.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I had the absolute worst turkey club of my entire life here. I attended the CMA music festival, which is a busy time for all restaurants in the area, but that is no excuse for the pathetic slop of a sandwich I received. First of all, when ordering I was straight up ignored at the counter for a solid 10 minutes before the staff even looked my way. After I finally got service, I was given a barely toasted two pieces of bread with a disgusting amount of mayo, one slice of tomato, one piece of browning lettuce, and dried out chicken. There was no bacon at all. If I wasn't so hungry I would not have even touched this overpriced garbage sandwich. I will never eat at this chain again.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Took some friends from Missouri out for drinks and dancing. It was Friday night, so it was expected everywhere we went would be busy. Waited in line to get in, but only about 5-10 minutes. We got beers as soon as we walked in. First floor was super crowded and the band was still setting up. We made our way to the top floor, every floor had different music and bands on them. We ended up staying on the top floor next to rooftop patio. The band was great. Range of music and interacted with crowd.
Pleasantly surprised at how collected lead singer was when a rude bride to be tried to take money out of tip jar and said his tip jar sucked.Glad he had patience, because she sure was on my last nerve.
We decided to go to another bar down the block and immediately regretted it. When we left the stage it was really packed with a bigger line out front. Will definitely be back, we all had a good time.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: The manager Terry was amazing!! She gave my party of 12 her undivided attention when we had a slight issue with our waitress. The way she handled the situation was more than we ever expected. I work in the restaurant business and was so impressed by the way she took care of our party. I cannot say thank you enough to Terry and how she handled her manager position.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Had a blast at our first visit here! Key is a super fun and awesome waitress! She kept us entertained while we were waiting for our food.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: A few of us decided to take a self guided scooter tour from Bearded Iris back to our place in the South area of Nashville. We planned to make a couple stops and when we hit broadway, we needed a watering hole ASAP. Luckily we rolled into Whiskey Bent and got a few seats at the bar. It was early afternoon so it wasn't super crowded. This definitely worked in our favor because the two piece duo was amazing and once they really got going the bar started to fill up quickly. Whiskey Bent was a quick stop for a beer that turned into a great experience. Definitely one of the better Broadway spots.

name: Ray Stevens CabaRay Showroom
text: The showroom is beautiful.. Ray Stevens had as much fun as me and my Girl.. its a really good time.. we loved the piano bar too

name: The Valentine
text:
I'm gonna be plain honest - I'm really not a fan of country music/honky tonks. When I stepped out onto Broadway, I tried to listen for a place that wasn't playing country music, and wasn't too crowded. I stumbled across The Valentine. The building has really lovely architecture, from the prohibition era.

I caught Steve Cunningham and the Cunninghams, a good cover band. They played Prince, Journey, Jackson 5, Queen, and more. I got myself an Angry Orchard cider and swayed along. There are people of all ages there having a good time dancing. It was one of the few venues that didn't get too crazy on Friday evening, and I appreciated it. Staff was very pleasant. Do stop by if you get a chance.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
My favorite "honky tonk" of the trip.   Fun and friendly staff.   The bands that played the night we were there were all fantastic.  Any one of them could be the next discovered big star!  

Drinks were generous and fairly priced.   Security staff at the door was a kick..  Carded everyone regardless of age.   They. made this gals night

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Stayed there for a meeting in summer 2018, and it was fine.

Back for another meeting end of July 2019, but this time it didn't go so well.

Pros: friendly helpful staff and comfortable, well appointed, spacious room.

Cons:
1. I arrived around midnight to discover that they had no rooms available. This despite me being a speaker at the meeting and my room having been reserved by the meeting organizer well in advance. I get it that people sometimes don't show up and a business doesn't want to leave money on the table. But a last minute no-show is charged full fare (so no money left on the table) and a room reserved by a meeting organizer (especially when that meeting is bringing in a ton of business) maybe deserves some special consideration before giving it away.

2. Internet connection spotty everywhere--guestroom, lobby areas, meeting rooms. 

3. Electronic door locks malfunctioning. While I was checking in (finally) the 2nd day of the meeting, a guest needed assistance because both of her key cards had stopped functioning. I didn't think much of it, until the same thing happened to me the next day. Staff were polite and helpful but not surprised when I went to the front desk with this problem. Seems to be a routine issue for them lately.

I stay in 5-10 different hotels every year. This property is well below average.

It seems to me that they minimally need a substantial investment in modern technology (at least the door locks/key cards and internet bandwidth). Management staff might need some retraining or replacing, too.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Hole in the wall, disrespectful and disgusting. Treated me nice but I watched them, I mean security and manager being rude and mean to others and that hurt me, we all left and never coming back.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Super fun and friendly place and they get good bands. I always stop here when in town.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: I tried to bring in my personal water bottle (every other bar allowed me to enter with the bottle) and this particular bar/bouncer did not let me enter the bar. I was excited to visit this particular bar and meet my friends/I have had 2 drinks throughout the entire night. Unfortunately I will not recommend this bar to anyone I know and or this bouncer ruined the experience due to his own personal feelings against me.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: An employee pushed me out of the way very aggressively because I "was not moving" so I nudged him with my elbow and was immediately manhandled by security. This place abuses authority. DO NOT SUPPORT THIS ESTABLISHMENT.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Great new spot, they have it figured out!   Live music, kid friendly, porch upstairs, and games on the TV's!   Something for everyone in the family......I live downtown and it's great to have a spot to take the whole gang!!

Beer- Ice Cold
Food- Simple and Good
Entertainment-  Icing on the cake

name: Robert's Western World
text: Had a great time. The music was the best in downtown area. Food was great and really reasonably priced, even if you have to order at the bar(they'll l bring it to your table). Drink prices are fair  and people are friendly. Get a spot upstairs for a secluded spot to watch the show.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is a 'must visit' during a trip to Nashville! It's a classic bar with a good beer selection and an intimate music atmosphere. I'd recommend going during the day so you can get a table up front close to the live music.

name: Nashville Municipal Auditorium
text: Very cool, vintage place to see a concert! Loved all of the old concert ticket posters that were hanging. Bathrooms were clean and staff was friendly ( both a plus for me!) I will definitely go back

name: Second Fiddle
text:
The bartenders may be fast, but they also like to pull a fast one on you. I paid for two mixed drinks ($7.25 each, not terrible considering the place) with a $20, and the Britney Spears wannabe took my cash and pocketed the change. I stood there a minute, expecting her to get in the change drawer as quickly as she greeted me and made my drinks, but no. She disappeared, evidently under the impression she deserved a $5.50 tip. She tried to do the same thing to another girl in our party with a $7 order. No, you don't get a $13 tip, sugar. Maybe this is standard operating procedure nowadays, but it's not cool and would keep me from tipping at all on subsequent drinks. 

The live music was decent and the crowd wasn't obnoxious. Go in there with ones and quarters and you should be all set.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: If you visit Nashville, you have to visit the Ryman Auditorium. Yes it is old and yes it is a bit pricey, but hey it's a part of Nashville history! There isn't a bad seat in the house and it is kidn of neat being part of a live radio show. We might have lucked out with some great performers, but I could see this place being a great time any night. It's a bit refreshing/odd to only have each performer play 2 songs, but at the same time, you get a good variety. I enjoyed both the imported and regular talent (btw how are the square dancers still chunky after all those moves). Overall, a great experience!

name: Music City Center
text: This place is gigantic, it is beautiful, and I like its modern design. I still don't think it was a good use of taxpayer money though. I hardly saw the old convention center used, so we'll see how this goes. Hopefully it gets put to good use. I was here for the Nashville Comic Con that came in. Maybe more fun things will come to town because of the center is here.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is a perfect place to experience Nashville dive bar.  This is among the many bars on Broadway.  It's close to the Ryman.  All the bars have live music.  No matter which one you pick.  So now you have to pick one you want to chill out in.  This is the place.  During the day you can have kids there.  Now it's a bar. So don't think it has a kids menu.  Basic bar food.  But they have one special that is what I had to get.  It's a fried bologna sandwich and PBR for $6! It was the coolest thing.  They have cheap beer.  Basic beers for $2.50.  They have the air conditioner on high in there and since it was the summer it was welcomed.  Nashville has weird weather.  It was a hot day and sitting inside and watching some players on stage was well worth it. 

I'm sure at night it's a happening place.  So maybe I'll go at night.  But it's well worth it to stop in and have beer.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This is another must do!!! $20 seems a bit much for a self-guided tour, but it is definitely worth it to keep this huge piece of country music history around. They offer AAA discount which was 10% off. We went on a Sunday morning and it wasn't crowded at all.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: A fabulous experience and birthday dinner! Our service was excellent, not a thing was overlooked. We had the hot shrimp and crab dip appetizer as well as the bruschetta, both very tasty! I had the margarita shrimp which was perfectly fresh and light. Others at my table enjoyed steaks, pork chops and pastas. Everyone was very pleased with our meal from start to finish!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This one on Broadway is pretty reminiscent to the one in Birmingham with the only major difference being no outdoor stage. They do have two floors so it has a more restaurant feel, although the second floor was closed off by the time I got there around 1:00am. They open everyday till 3:00am which has it's advantages. The Mad Hatter's performed a mix of Top 40 and 90's music.They serve the best amaretto sours and a little too strong for my taste Vegas bombs. I'd definitely like to come back on a Friday or Saturday night and see how different it is as opposed to a Monday night.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great atmosphere.   Made an evening dinner.   Great music.  Fabulous meal.  The blackened red snapper et toffee is off the hook!!!    Great service , the staff is fantastic.   A new Nashville must visit for me!!!   Loved it!!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I came here on a Sunday night for a late dinner. Food and service did not disappoint. The drinks were great - I too went with the pineapple, cucumber drink and that is probably one of my new favorite combinations. The food is pricey here - so I went with a couple of the small plate options and dessert. I had the bruschetta, Mac and cheese and the duck breast. I did feel like it was a little crazy to pay $15 for three bit size pieces of duck breast, but they were delicious. The Mac and chest was good and you would love it if you love goat cheese. I don't like goat cheese, but I still liked it enough to eat it. The bruschetta is pretty standard here. I really wanted the creme brûlée, but they were out so I settled on sticky toffee pudding with ice cream. That was pretty amazing. The night I came they had an amazing blues singer that I could have listened to for hours. This would be a great date spot for anyone looking to impress.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I can't say enough. Boots everywhere. This place is Nashville, Nashville, Nashville. There is always music and it is always good. It's a great place to stop if all the pop-country cover bands on Broadway are starting to feel like a little much. Robert's is old school. 

If you show up on a weekend night, it's going to be packed. It just is. Still, the staff is great. But you might have to strong-arm your way through the crowd to the bar. I prefer the random Tuesday. More room to sit, dance, etc. and the music is just as good.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Of all the places in Nashville that we discovered, and there were many, this was by far our favorite venue for awesome live music and good, cheap drinks. We went back at least 6 times in a four day trip. I also loved the grilled cheese sandwich - great "blotting paper" when drinking!

name: Robert's Western World
text: We love old county .. Exactly what we were looking for .. Great music And simple food!!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: The music is great! Good beer selection, try the Yazoo pale ale. It's local to Nashville and really good. The tacos were great, but the Mac and cheese was runny. I'd pass on it next time. Overall, great bar pick!

name: Second Fiddle
text:
Oh my gosh, this place is amazing and has some of the best bartenders.

I would like to start off by saying, we asked for a mixed drink which required root beer.  The bartender let us know they did not carry root beer, but instead of making us order another drink, she offered to go next door and BUY us some root beer!  Um, coming from Chicago, this was a once in a lifetime thing and Second Fiddle will forever receive five stars.

The band played excellent music - not one song we didn't know or want to learn because they were such great performers.  The band was so engaging, and the people in the bar were just as much fun.  

The drinks were pretty cheap compared to some other spots on the strip, and the bartenders really know what they are doing.  Great spot.

name: Legends Corner
text: Fun bar right in the thick of Nashville. We like to go in the daytime. Less crowded and not a lot of drunk people. The bands are so good. Old time country mixed with new music.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place is my second home. I've been a resident of Nashville for 10 years but I don't think that Robert's will ever get old. There is history in those hallowed walls. The music and acts they feature are real, genuine country. I love the dance floor. The food is great and fast. The wait staff are kind and helpful. This joint cannot be missed when you're on Broadway.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This is the original home of the Grand Ole Opry.   The building this is a former Church, and you will be sitting on hard wood seats with very narrow Aisles.  Bring a seat cushion.   The show is for a radio program, so there are commercials as breaks.  We enjoyed the show, but HATED the seats.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Music was great! The service and food was a lot to be desired though. We had a group of 10 girls and the waitress was nice enough to put the bill on two separate checks, but the food for the first check came out and then the second check 20 minutes later. The food was mediocure: the fries tasted like frozen bag fries, the hot chicken was very bland, nachos came when we were finished eating.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Went here with my in-laws for my fiancé's birthday dinner. We were expecting great food and atmosphere. Bottom line: food is way over priced, the service was average, the restaurant was very loud. I wouldn't come back here unless I had a discount.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
What a cool place!! The atmosphere is just amazing. Nice big bar area, dining area with a stage and live music, and if that's not your thing, then you can sit outside on their patio and people watch The Gulch. Love it!

Hubby and I got drinks at the bar and I must say, I was not a fan of mine. I got a lemondrop martini and it tasted like pure lemonade. Ok lesson learned, stick to wine...

The beignet appetizers were AMAZING. A puff pastry ball stuffed with cheese, prosciutto, and I think even basil with balsamic drizzle. Just do it. 

Dinner was not great.... I got the scallops. They are served with risotto which I love but this stuff was either over or undercooked (hard pieces) and seemed as though it had been sitting around for a while and someone just popped it under a warming light. 

Husband got the lobster tacos and he was also very underwhelmed, very little taste he said. The meals are not cheap, but we chalked it up to the price you pay for the great atmosphere. 

We got desert on the house since we were celebrating his birthday - berry cobbler and it was delish!!!

I do want to comment on the service also.... not good. Our waitress never came to check on our drinks the entire time we ate dinner and both of us had empty glasses sitting out hoping she would notice. So instead of ordering from her when she brought the bill, we just decided to get drinks elsewhere. 

Overall we loved this place because of the atmosphere and we would be back, although next time I think we would just sit in the bar area, get wine & apps, and listen to the band.

name: Music City Center
text: Rambling layout.  Poor access for disabled. Expensive. Wide range of space.  Lots of stairs and climbing.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Worst bar on Broadway. As a local I can say that this is the most unfriendly bar in Nashville.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Saw Josh Turner here and I must saw that this is one of my favorite music venues. Even if someone has a "bad seat," you're so close to the stage where it feels like they're singing to you.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: If I could give the Ryman 0 stars I would. Horrible experience. Treated poorly by the staff, no one seemed to care except for the events manager Trevor. Ushers Damien and Carol (who are apparently married according to her and take up for one another) were completely vile and I have never been treated like this in my entire life. Did not get to enjoy the show due to their rudeness and persecution. When I complained to the ushers manager I was asked if I "wanted free tickets." I explained that I didn't care about the money I cared about being treated like a human being.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
A classic Nashville honky tonk. The music was loud and pumping. The crowd was dancing and having a blast. The drinks were cheap and strong. I was there on a Monday night. The strip was pretty quiet overall. But not Robert's. Just as fun and wild as a weekend. 

I wouldn't regularly spend a lot of time on Broadway, but I would definitely want to get my fix each time I'm in town and I would totally be okay doing that here.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Cool little venue with some great history. Lots of local bands walking through their door and the bar staff and food a great.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Came to Nashville from Chicago for an Anita Baker concert. The auditorium was huge and beautiful. The church pew seating was nice and  gave you a communal feeling. My sister complained about sitting on hard wood so bring a pillow seat cushion or something if this is your issue. The Ushers were kind and helpful. It would have been nice to had gone on the tour of the auditorium to gain more historical knowledge of the venue. Great place.

name: Robert's Western World
text: My wife and I were in town for an Avalanche game and this was the first of many bars that we visited. We stopped in late on a Monday night and it was lively...but not packed. The drinks were very inexpensive from what we are used to paying. The food was good for a late night bar food...but the band was GREAT!!! I don't know if the music is that good every night...but if it is...don't miss it!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We had a great time here last week celebrating a birthday and holiday family get together. The band was absolutely fantastic. We had a table night next to the stage and it wasn't loud at all. Food was great, drinks were flowing, and our server was attentive and wonderful.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Probably my fave broadway bar. I like that you can be on the second floor and still enjoy the live music playing  on the first floor. 

Also Tara, our waitress, was amazing! Just the right balance of attention. Nice  to Find a place in Nashville that values god customer service!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: One of my favorite restaurants in Nashville. The food is always amazing and normally the music is great too. Great atmosphere and the service is always on point. Definitely make a reservation because they stay busy. The patio is great during the warmer months, but the main dining area is the place to be to see the nightly band.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: You could feel the history in the Ryman auditorium. We saw the grand old opry there last night and what a treat it was to hear the old sounds if country mixed with the new. The seats are like church pews adding to the spirit of the old world. I could pretend I had gone back in time 90 years when the music first started. The mood was jovial and peaceful despite the presence of numerous gun toting patriots. The black lilies were great and I loved it when Larry Gatlin danced with audience members. We were disappointed that there was no mention of Stringbean Akeman and no Stringbean memorabilia in the gift shop. No Stringbean overalls no Stringbean harmonica or Stringbean pens. The gift shop was severely overpriced and you had to show your ticket to get in or out. We enjoyed watching the bossy little singer of the black lilies direct the musicians as she belted out harmonies.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Dont have any other honky tonks to compare to, but great ole timey country music with fiddle and lap steel enjoyed alongside my fried bologna sandwich and PBR.

Mix of locals, sport coats and cowboy hats... good time for all. Drinks arent dirt cheap, but no cover for a great band, so no complaints at all. 



sidenote... Nashville seems to be the friendliest place on earth!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Where to begin...lets say a great visit gon bad. The Rhyman sold us two $20 tickets at 11:04. Because there was a special evnt that day they were pretty clear that they would be closing in an hour. 

What wasn't clear was that self guided tour would be herded into a line to wait 15 minutes to watch a intro video. Once through we had 20 minutes to see the actual auditorium. 

It wasn't long into our final minutes that the lights began to flick off and the guards/etc began to shoo people along. 

Once to the lobby I took a moment to register my feelings on a comment card an then use the facilities. The guard drew the stantion tape across the entrance as I was entering and then began to argue with me about how we had enough time...should have known the place was closing...and to leave now! Oh.. But spend as much time in the gift shop as you like.

I'm very disappointed that the Rhyman would sell tickets so close to the time they needed the building empty and then not have the decency to allow your final tour of the day to take in what they paid for. We weren't overstaying our welcome. 

Also I'm not okay with picking a fight with your guests.

One of the parts of the welcome video that stuck with me is that the guests and fans of the Rhyman are what kept the place from being razed and kept vital.... If what I experienced is any sign. You've clearly lost sight of that.

Final analysis...great history here, but you'll be treated like trash once your money is handed over. Would not recommend.

name: Legends Corner
text:
Wish I could give this place more than 5 stars as they deserve 10!! Being from NY I'm not used to such a welcoming environment so Legends Corner is always a favorite spot to be at when I visit! 

The music is great, the company is great the bartenders are awesome. Even before walking inside you get greeted by such welcoming people! 
This past time when I visited Legends Corner ( weekend after Thanksgiving ) my friend and I were greeted at the door by the kindest, funniest and most inviting bouncer I've come across! ( Ray ) 

When you go into any bar your first impressions are usually with the greeters/bouncers and for me Ray definitely made a FANTASTIC first impression and was a definite influence on our decision to go inside! --- if the bouncer was that friendly and welcoming we were sure the rest of the staff would be too! ( and they were :) ) 
Can't wait to come back and visit again, it'll be my first stop!! -- and hopefully Ray will be at the door again next time! :) 

-Alexandra
:)

name: Robert's Western World
text: If you're going to Broadway, this is the place to go; don't waste your time going elsewhere. Great music, great food, and an overall great vibe. They even have a veggie burger!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Awesome old school venue that is a must see in Nashville.  We went for bluegrass night and saw Gibson Brothers. Fantastic show. Parking lot right there next to building for $10.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I haven't been to Sambuca in years, but joined a friend at the bar on Saturday night. Our bartender was amazing. He ran the bar like the ultimate pro- cool and collected while sweeping in to take orders and refilling drinks as we enjoyed the jazz band. We enjoyed the small plates and I cannot wait to go back and check out the bar upstairs which was closed for a private event. Until then... I'll be dreaming of those Goat Cheese-Stuffed Artichokes :p

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Best place in Nashville for blues and Jazz. The steaks and seafood were delicious. I would say that the quality of this was the very best that you will find. We will definitely go again.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Robert's completed our solid first night in Nashville! After too many cocktails and gorging on high class food at Rolf and Daughters, my friends and I decided to end our night on a high note with $2.50 bottles of Yuengling. While the idea of Broadway isn't really my thing, obviously I couldn't come to Nashville without at least checking it out. With the street performers and endless groups of bachelorette parties, it felt a little like the Vegas Strip, minus the ability to walk down the street with a beer. 

I'm not really into country music, however, I wanted the true honky tonk experience, and I got it at Robert's Western World. The music was great, the bar was crowded but lively, and people were friendly. We made friends with multiple groups of people, most of whom were all in Nashville for the same reason - to persue their music. Definitely different from what I am used to in DC, where everyone works for the government or is looking to break into politics. Refreshing.

I had heard that Robert's was the best spot on Broadway, and while I don't have much to compare it to, I would certainly go back. Cheap beer, good music, and friends. What could be better?

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
My wife and I went to here last night. 

It was pretty dead and the restaurant was very dark, like hard to read the menu dark.  Yes, I get it's the vibe, but still. 

The band was average at best, much better performers elsewhere. 

The was was definitely good.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The video at the intro was a good history of the building. Fans of country music will enjoy the tour more. Balcony seats for a show would be absolutely amazing but be careful on the first floor towards the back,  visibility is limited.

name: Legends Corner
text: So much fun!!  Bands are great and the staff is awesome!!  Loved every minute there!!!  My new favorite :):):)

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great drinks and awesome atmosphere.  they were gearing up for some live music.  too bad i couldnt stay.  i would go back in a heartbeat

name: Robert's Western World
text:
The ambience is geared toward a more mature crowd, with classic country being played by live bands. The night we were there brought in an older crowd. Definitely some talented musicians. 

Drinks were a little slow, but it was a busy night. Maybe staff one more bartender to increase efficiency.

Overall though, a good time and would come again.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Being a fan of country music, seeing the Ryman was pretty awesome.  There was some construction but seeing all of the old architecture was amazing.  I went there for a concert and the acoustics were very nice and knowing all of the legends that performed on that same stage made the place that much more amazing.  We also had a great time in downtown Nashville!!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
As a music lover, I'm fortunate have lived in this great city for over a decade now and have the opportunity to see so many shows at the Ryman, the "Mother Church of Country Music." There is definitely something special about this place. The history, the pews, the stained glass. There is just so much to love about this place. The acoustics are great. Some great shows come though Nashville at this venue, because really,  who WOULDN'T want the opportunity to play here?!

Seeing a show here should be on every music lover's bucket list!

name: Legends Corner
text: A good place to grab a beer and watch some great entertainment on Broadway . Nashville is an extreme party town but watch yourself as their are a lot of cops on the Broadway .

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Well we had a bad experience at Layla's (see review) so we decided to cap the night off here. Walked in and got a bartender fairly easily. Ordered an Irish carbomb and a Jagerbomb. The bartender looked annoyed to make them and minute later we had our drinks. We finish those since they are bombs and she walks off to apparently not take another order. Stand there and get ignored for a couple of minutes. Screw this just gimme the tab so I can back to Georgia. Bartenders in this city lack personality and seem to hate their jobs. The bartender at this establishment was no exception.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Rude rude rude bartenders!!!  Our mixed drinks were straight up soda and the blonde hag said I have a shot in my drink if I paid for it.  Don't bother with this hole.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: If you are looking for a place to eat, play games, shop, and hear live music, then go here.  Several restaurants and lots of different shops, even a grocery store.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place for authentic live country music and cheap food and drinks. Had a wonderful night here during my first trip to Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We wanted a true Nashville honky tonk experience. We got it! It was Saturday night. The line at the door didn't take too long. I can't believe there was no cover! After we got inside, it was crowded and noisy, but a ton of fun! The band was awesome! The cocktail waitress managed to work the entire room. It was a great night!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: What can you say, it's the Ryman. The walls breath good vibrations. The history in here is unprecedented. To think of all the artists that have graced this 125 year old church is staggering. We brought in the NewYear with Old Crow Medicine Show and they didn't disappoint. If you're ever in Nashville, make it a point to at least peek your head in this old school house of country music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Excellent restaurant!!! I went on a Saturday night. The food was excellent and the band was awesome!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
The best chicken & waffles EVER! The chicken was crispy and juicy and complemented perfectly by gravy and a very spicy and unique syrup. The waffle was golden and delicious. Very generous serving.

Bonus - there was also a great live band playing!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Our favorite place on Broadway - Rachel was fabulous as a bartender and server - we had a group of 13 and enjoyed every minute -- the music, cold beer, onion rings and bologna sandwich!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: 2 stars instead of one because of the amazing history. But otherwise to me this place seems totally overrated as a music venue. Very uncomfortable seating for a longer show. Better places to see music in Nashville IMO but the history is indeed amazing.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Had an ok time here. Stopped by to have a few drinks and enjoy music. Music was good, food and drinks were good. But service was everything but. The bartender asked if we wanted to keep and open tab and when we said no he replied "so this is your last drink?" Almost pushing us out of the establishment. Overall just an OK experience. Especially on Valentine's Day.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: This is a great Nashville experience- highly recommend to start your evening here. Just don't sit too close to the stage as conversation will be hard... as it is in most live music venues. Service has always been great- food is a 4/5- usually good but not the best I've ever had.

name: Legends Corner
text: Love love this place.  So much history, good music all the time and a great staff.  It's a shame bars like this are being taken over by country music "name" bars that are all the same machine.    Don't let these gems disappear!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Amazing time and a definite must if you have not been. The staff is friendly and the acoustics sound was amazing!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Very unique venue.  I went to see Jill Scott and had great seats.  However, after sitting for very long, the seats were starting to get uncomfortable.  I loved the intimate setting and the production was great.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Two bartenders told me that Nashville was no longer a country music town. One of the bartenders even said it and then "dropped the mic". Then had two security guards stand behind me after I said this bar was more of an LA bar than a country bar. Perhaps they were right that Broadway was no longer a country location, but I walked 10 seconds down the street and was in an old school country bar and happy. This bar is just like any other bar in any other city. Don't go here if you're looking for a country bar. It sucked. If you want an LA bar with bartenders who are obnoxious and willing to call security guards for zero reason then this is your place. Drop mic and the 20 something douchebag bartenders can promote more candy pop music for $10 a pop and make Nashville less country and more MTV. Johnny Cash (if these loser bartenders have ever even heard of him) would roll over in his grave. This place blows.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Im ganna start this review in a weird way but who cares...i just gotta start by saying that their cheese queso is some of the best queso ive ever tried. Came here for a quick lunch and had a nice time. Got the loaded tots to start and they were great. A little small but a very nice app with amazing queso lol. For lunch got the pulled pork sandwich which was average id say but got queso on the side for the fries which was a great call. 
Bar is cool and has a unique look with stickers and sharpie everywhere. They had some live music which was very loud so we sat in the back. Bartender was a little nasty but she was the only one bartending and had a pretty full lunch crowd. 
Overall a decent spot to stop for a bite to eat at a reasonable price.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Kate is such a wonderful bartender! Friendly, personable, attentive- highly recommend checking this spot out for a brewski and a fried bologna sandwich!

name: Legends Corner
text: When I was visiting Nashville, I heard some good live music coming from this bar so we decided to walk in for a few drinks. Unfortunately the band was taking a break about 15 minutes after we got there but the drinks were good and there was a good vibe here.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I am giving this place a 4 star - not because the food is anything special or tied to the unique Nashville culinary scene, but because we were a group of 12 women for a bachelorette party and they provided nice ambiance, and service.   It is hard to go all-out foodie when you're a group that big, so I think for what we got, it was good.  

They have a huge dim-lit space, a stage with live music and even an area for dancing. Our server was a sweetheart; answered a lot of questions, was attentive, was fun, took a ton of photos of us, split the bill without issue based on what we each ordered (this must be uniquely Nashvillian because they do not do this in NYC- though I never mind splitting evenly).  He greeted us with bottles of champagne, provided by a female not in attendance, so they do, do bottle service. I feel like they made my bride to be friend special which is what mattered. We go ta big comfortable table in the middle of the room.  Menu is big and has variety.

I shared food with my bestie girlfriend to the left - we shared a fresh shrimp ceviche (could have been better but wasn't bad, was fresh.. just lacked some flavor and usually ceviche complexity)...I ordered the blackened snapper etoufee which was good - good portion of blacknened snapper, shrimp, and crab dip.. which was super creamy. Kind of wished they had less of this and more of the dirty rice, which was little but a bit small for portion.  They dish also had crunchy French onions (like the salad topper) which gave what would have been a mushy dish some texture.  It was good - and great for if you are hungry. In highsight, I also would have tried the scallops which they recommended. 

Lots of girls were getting a mixture of sides, or salads - my gf got the portobello mushroom, asparagus and salad... The one scallop she ordered was $7 though which was a bit ridic. She was told it was an add on order for surf and turf.. Idk. Anyway, boo.  I guess being this kind of entertainment place you can expect prices to be in the upper 20s to low 30s for meh to good food. 

They also had an extensive drink menu, including some drinks that were... lol.. "naked" aka less calories.  I guess they try to target women. 

It was great for our purposes (seating a large group) but if coming to Nashville just to eat, I wouldn't go. It's in a nice neighborhood though. Amazingly, the server did not add auto grat also.. which was a kind gesture but that was a surprise with a group so large.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Four of us on a girls trip stopped in for a cocktail.  Travis waited on us, gave us a great recommendation, the strawberry lemonade cocktail and took great care of us.  After we left I realized I was missing my credit card.  We called them but they claimed they did not have it.  Went back  there to double check and as soon as Travis heard I was missing the card,  he started searching all the black bill holders.  He found it!  He made the extra effort and saved my vacation.  What a fabulous employee.  Thanks Travis!

name: Second Fiddle
text: One of best bars in Nashville.  Authentic Honky Tonk.  Jessica and crew are Best Bartenders in Nashville.   Always great artists.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: This is one of the best options in downtown Nashville. Our waitress Amanda was amazing please ask for her when you make your reservations!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
People who actually write bad reviews for The Ryman astound me. They're really just whining.  The acoustics are great. The venue itself is great with lots of character and history. I feel Nashville is lucky to have it. 

Yes, there are church pews. It is the Mother Church, after all. They add to its character. Many say that they are uncomfortable. I don't really find them to be so, but you can take in cushions like you would to a ball game. I saw one guy say he didn't like them because he felt he was at church. Really?  Are we looking for things to complain about?  I've never really felt like a packed sardine in the pews, but I am neither overweight nor were any of the people in the rows I've been in so far. Maybe I've just been lucky. 

The columns are there to support the balcony. I have not found them nor the balcony obstructive of my view. When I saw Weezer I supposedly had an "obstructed view" according to the seating chart, but I saw everything fine. The columns aren't that big. 

I highly recommend seeing a show at the Ryman. You should at least once in your lifetime.  And keep your cranky pants at home. 

Tip:. Free valet for Nissan owners!  They even leave bottles of water thanking you for being a part of the Nissan family in your car!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
In Nashville - So many bars and honky tonks, so little time...

If I had one afternoon/evening in Nashville, this is the place!!

Music from Wendy Newcomer and her band was fantastic!!  

Service was warm and hospitable, ambiance is everything you would expect in a dive bar, we did not try the food offering so, no comments on food. 

Even the patrons were nice - met people from Canada, Indiana and some locals, too.  

Highly recommend.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We attended a show a few nights ago at the Ryman.  I love the history of the venue and love the venue itself.  The wood church pews were actually more comfortable than I expected.  Midland put on an amazing show!  Unfortunately a very inconsiderate couple chose to stand the entire show.  We were in the balcony where no one else in the area was standing.  The 4-6 rows behind the couple could not see the stage at all. People around them asked politely several times if they would sit down. The guy was drunk and extremely rude.  Ryman staff was notified and would do nothing. They have a policy of not interfering with attendees. Really disappointing After driving 4.5 hours for the show.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place is one of those that you want everyone to know about but you don't want it to change. Great musicians, friendly staff and just the feel like you are in a place that knows it's a honky tonk without having to try

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
This place is awesome! Was here a few weeks ago for a Thursday night get away and had a blast. The food is great, the music is great and the people who work there are amazing. 

The band, The Cosmic Collective performed that night and were fantastic! Definitely will come back again for some more fun.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I just got back from my dinner here. We are here for a week visiting and this was the greatest first night place. We are celebrating my 30th birthday and we were lucky enough to have Emerson as our server. Not only did he give us a recommendation on an amazing drink he was great through the entire meal. He helped us know the good places to visit on our trip in Nashville. I am so thankful for him he was funny and so personable and so helpful! He really made our first night in Nashville extremely memorable! We would come back just for him let alone the food and drinks! This place is a must go and definitely ask for Emerson if you want a one of a kind experience!!!!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is a Broadway joint that you imagined and hoped all of Broadway to be. Tremendous "classical" country and rockabilly bands. I had a bologna sandwich for the first time in like 15 years as part of the Recession Special, and I didn't regret a moment of it. It's the one place I demanded to go on multiple nights.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
We came here for a late lunch early dinner on Saturday a little after 5:00PM. What really was a turn off when we walked to the hostess 2 of them standing around and asked for a table for 2 ... they looked at us like we came to their house. Then they said ohh are u having drinks or dinner we are not ready so you can sit at the bar. Just a little tip if you are in the restaurant business weather you are ready or not you should always be welcoming and accommodate your customers. The people that walk in your door don't want to hear anything, they want to be seated and served. Focus on providing them the experience they expect and deserve. 

However our server George was wonder and made the experience great. I had the salmon with asparagus and my husband had the pork chop with Brussel sprouts and everything was delicious. Id say the portions were on the smaller size. The manager came by to make sure everything was good.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is the only REAL honky tonk on Broadway. Robert's has great music, a fun atmosphere, and cheap food/drinks.

If you want to see what Broadway used to be like before it turned into a giant frat party of the exact same bars, serving $8.50 Bud Lights for an endless supply of bachelorette parties... 

Robert's is your answer.

name: Robert's Western World
text: If they have the same caliber entertainment every night awesome. $$$ Drinks tough to find a seat but I guess thats a good thing.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
