text: Walking down Broadway - came across this place after few stops. Ordered 5 drinks and paid in full. Ordered another round of Jell-O shots and hold-behold! Bartender was rude with a 'TUDE!!!! Looks like "Hunter" the bartender even "pocketed" the "amount pay" for our Jell-O shots, after we told him their Jell-O shot tasted like a year old. He was rude and beyond unprofessional!  To top it off, manager and just repeated the same thing he said... didn't even apologize for saying "sorry the Jell-O shots were awful.". Never again. Would never go back! And he claimed "oh good" ... that to us is BS for sure. If he only knew who I am ... visiting his little old bar.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Good place to visit if you are not a police officer.  They will not allow you in if you are armed off duty.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Lovely place. First time in Nashville and tried this place out. Great ambiance. Amazing service. Delicious  food!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The RyMan was an amazing facility unfortunately the Larry Gatlin hosted Country Music Show was horrible LARRY IS WAY PADT HIS PRIME AND TRYS WAY hard on songs especially high notes ! Lee Ann Carter was great but that was about it ! The show was really bad some people left before it was over ! The gospel part was actually the worst ! I would never go to another one of theses shows . They will be artist specific like Dwight  Yoakum

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My first time in Nashville and after going to all the fancy restaurants ie Kayne's Prime this was a surprise. We spent our 27th anniversary here and actually went with the recommendation from the hotel driver as opposed to the concierge recommendation from the Omni hotel.  Keith our server was awesome and recommended the best food the shrimp and crap dip is to die for has a little Cajun/ chili flavor the filet Oscar with grilled shrimp was not on the menu but was better than the filet I had at Kayne's the night before, my wife's salmon Oscar was perfectly cooked. The music was the best jazz even compared to the best from DC.  Hands down go here if in Nashville a great alternatives to the honky Tonks!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
A fun, loud, great honkey tonk right on broadway next to countless "country music clubs." Amidst the massive amount of bachelorette magnet bars, this place stands out as a true country music destination. It can get rather crowded and still have the occasional bachelorette party crash the scene, but hey, this is Nashville, that's bound to happen. 

The drinks are inexpensive and ice cold, and the music is ALWAYS phenomenal. You should definitely make this a stop on your trip to Nashville, or make it your regular bar if you live downtown, the music never disappoints.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: The food was good but unspectacular.  The calamari appetizer was the most disappointing part but everything else was tasty.   I expected more based on all the hype.   The staff was friendly and brought us a free desert for our anniversary, which was much appreciated.  We got the sopapillas which was probably my favorite food for the evening.    We were disappointed after making a reservation very far in advance to be seated nowhere near the live music and instead being in a very generic dining area watching the music on a TV.  The prices seemed high for what we got which is the main reason I would not recommend.  I think people would enjoy the food but frankly could get the same or better for less cost elsewhere.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place to have a beverage and listen to great music.  The food is fun and reasonable.  Had fun and great place all around

name: Legends Corner
text: Best Honky Tonk on Broadway. Unlike some of the other bars, this one is less crowded and chill. We enjoyed the live music and the bucket of beer deal - probably one of the best deals on Broadway (five beers for $25). I also loved looking as all the random country artist memorabilia - old records, guitars, juke boxes, etc. next time I come to Nashville this will be my go to spot.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
great music, i was impressed with the audio set up, i know i shouldn't be cause its nashville and everything, but really, sitting in the back and being able to hear the band perfectly, impressive.

 they have a good basic menu and the food on their is really good, the prices were all over the place, somethings were cheap, and somethings were prohibitively expensive: example $4.5 for 8 HUGE mozzarella sticks (delicious), but $5.5 for a 'premium beer' ( Shiner Bock ). basic french fries were 4.50... so just kinda odd.

 also this doesn't really bother me so much but worth pointing out, even tho the bar was not busy the service was poor, sub par. i didn't count off for that, just really the pricing is what impacted the score.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Awesome band and music. Stopped by on a Sunday night and place was packed. I enjoyed the experience. Only complain is shots were too light. Not enough etoH. Didn't pack much of a punch.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Old-fashioned honky tonk bar.  We tried to go early Saturday night but it was way too crowded.   We stopped in Sunday after brunch and it was not crowded.  We saw local legend, John Shepard.  Nice, corny, old-fashioned country show.  Beers are reasonably-priced, they even have some local microbrews.

name: Legends Corner
text: I travel to Nashville on a regular basis. I have had the opportunity to spend many nights on music row and have had a lot of fun. My favorite place to go is Legends Corner. Good atmosphere, cold beer, laid back compared to most places on the strip and more traditional country music. Give it a try, if you don't like all of the crowds at Tootsies etc. you will like this place.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Our concierge recommended this place. The food was absolutely amazing. The bread pudding was the best I've ever had. Service was spot on and the entertainment was great. You will not be disappointed with this place.

name: Robert's Western World
text: You can't do Nashville right without going to Robert's. I'd give up all the rest for this honky tonk! I really like that they play old/classic country (the good stuff like Johnny Cash). They have a small dance floor by the band and encourage guests to dance! The bartenders are nice, and while it's often busy, it's never body to body like some obnoxious places (cough cough... Tootsies). I love that it's historic and classic Nashville, but not obnoxious and overly packed. Go to Roberts for a great time, you won't be sorry!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: The hostess was so rude and utterly incompetent.  When we got there she insisted that we sit at a couch for a dinner reservation and refused to move us to one of the many empty tables in the restaurant. Tyler, the bar manager, was nearby and very quickly resolved the issue and kindly moved us to an ACTUAL table and provided us with the utmost customer service and was so personable and friendly. The food was absolutely delicious, and our group was thrilled in the end with the restaurant overall. Thank you Tyler!!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great food, great service, great music. I read a wonderful review so I had to try it myself! I had a burger with fries and it was delightful. I thoroughly enjoyed all aspects of the atmosphere provided. I will warn you, there is no cover charge to enter so tipping the band is a MUST. I would definitely visit again. Rock on, Nashville, TN

name: Legends Corner
text: Unprofessional staff. Made inappropriate racist comments against people in our party. Kicked them out for being black and couldn't provide justification for forcing them out of the bar. Take your business elsewhere.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is the real Honky Tonk grill!! We felt right at home here. This joint reminded me of the joints you stumble across in our hometown in Pennsylvania. It's a laid back ambiance with good eats, friendly staff, cold drinks & ear catching entertainment. We snagged a table right up front near the cowboy boot lined wall. I loved this!! The entertainment was what you come to Nashville to enjoy, down home old school country. 

Our cheeseburgers were on point. The best we've had in a long time!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Nashville is Music City. The sound quality at the Ryman could & should be excellent, and it is not, in my opinion. At the recent "I'm With Her" concert, each band did their last number acoustic with no mics & the sound was clear. The amplified vocals had been muddy, hard to get the words. 
Are the sound techs unfamiliar with this very good acoustic hall? Do they just turn it up too loud? Is it the microphones? I really would appreciate having an excellent sonic experience in this fine historic auditorium.
The general ambiance is pleasant. The church pews are hard. You can sit on your jacket or bring a small cushion. If you are tall, you might reserve an aisle seat to give your legs room.

name: Robert's Western World
text: What a fun place! I was told that sometimes celebrities pop in and perform. While we didn't experience that, it was still cool. The band that performed played great music. They went back to Johnny Cash and some great classics. Truly a wonderful experience!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Loved this place. It's hallowed ground. This is the Grand Ole Opry downtown. Took a self-guided tour. Signs about its history, performers, costumes, instruments are everywhere inside, and it's easy to get around. The country musical history here is phenomenal. This is where professional country music and bluegrass began, and stars were made. The Ryman was saved by the performers and fans as money was raised to restore the old building that was crumbling. We learned about the 3 p.m. performance and purchased tickets. We sat in the original wooden pews.  Boy, listening to Announcer Eddie Stubbs, hearing the humor and the songs of Larry Gatlin and his brothers, listening and singing along to award-winning songwriter Don Schlitz, and watching the dreams come true of some young performers, THEN being entertained by 85-year-old Charley Pride who is still jiving was one of the best days ever. We couldn't help but smile. This venue is a must-see.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
The bartender was AMAZING! She had a great personality, was attentive, and definitely was someone every employer would pray for. Her manager; however, was not. My father ordered a drink "neat" -- you know, a drink without ice. Somehow that warranted a 40% upcharge on the "regular" drink. But wait.. if it's between "neat" or "on the rocks" is there a price difference? No. Apparently, in this tourist-focused town you're expected to know that you will be charged an additional $2/drink NOT to have ice (or to have ice). I live in Los Angeles, I've traveled around Europe & Asia, and I'm born and raised in Cleveland, Ohio. No matter how cheap or expensive a cocktail is, I've NEVER been charged EXTRA for requesting a drink without ice! Hilarious.

In all honesty, what was more upsetting was the condescending tone the manager took with me when disputing a $4 upcharge!! $4! That's how much their MANAGERS do not value their CUSTOMERS. I will never return to this establishment, nor will I be paying the amount charged on my credit card--you better bet I'm disputing that $4, nor will I ever recommend this business again. Congrats! You "made" $4 on 1/8 "extra" alcohol without ice with ZERO customer loyalty and ZERO return business!!! This company needs to hire managers that understand customer service.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This is the ultimate dive bar.   They have great entertainment and pretty reasonable drink prices.  Nice happy hour.

name: Legends Corner
text: Nice small intimate bar if you get there early. I found this to be similar to the other smaller bars; good band, good drinks, lots of memorabilia.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Great historic gem. At first I was hesitant about going thru because of the price ( my bride says I am cheap),but after seeing the theater I was amazed. This place is a must see in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This might be one of the oddest bars I've been in but that's what makes it amazing.  Most of the servers were older ladies (which I loved) and is refreshing from all the T&A on the strip.  Reminded me of an old VFW.  All of the photos on the wall are old and crumbling but that adds to the charm.  They had a great band when we were there an old country band with an upright base.  They also sold boots which was a bit odd but again added to that charm.  

We didn't eat while we were there but they had fried bologna sandwiches which had I been in the mood would've been exactly what I would've ordered.  This place is a real gem in Nashville where everything is being taken over by the singer of the moment mega bars.  This is a throwback!!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I wanted a true honky tonk experience. Cowboy boots, southern accents, big hats, dancing that do-si-do, cheap well drinks, and all those other stereotypes. Because when in Nashville, see the Nashville sights, right? While I was on the search for that on Yelp, Robert's came up. 

First of all, you won't find southern charm here from the staff. I just thought I'd let you know, in case it was something you are looking forward to experiencing. The wait staff here was rude af. And I don't mean just one person, but everyone we encountered. Perhaps it was an off day... For all of them. If you're constantly at capacity, and that makes your workers cranky, maybe management should hire more people to accommodate surging numbers in the summer. Or perhaps increase their pay since they have to deal with a bunch of drunk tourists. Just a few thoughts. 

Other than that, it's a pretty entertaining dive bar. Live music is played here, every day. I love that, even if it isn't really my kind of music, it's still fun to people watch and enjoy the company of your friends. It's extremely small, and no doubt constantly beleaguered by drunken people, no matter what time of day it is. They pride themselves on their well-known "Recession Special," which includes a fried bologna sandwich, chips, and a PBR. PBR here is consistently cheap in general, at $2.50, and most of the food is as well. While the food is cheap, you'll find that the quality is also cheap... Definitely lower than typical bar fare. You'll find mozzarella cheese sticks for $5, French fries for $4, and even a hamburger for $6, all very affordable and incredibly greasy; perfect for soaking up a bit of alcohol before you go on with the rest of your night and drink more. 

THE VERDICT:
Cheap food, cheap drinks, live music, centrally located in downtown Nashville. It's an entertaining place to go at night with a group of friends, but not really the place to be if you like tasty food and friendly bartenders.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We visit Nashville about 5 times a year. And every single time we dine at Sambuca. We were there this past Saturday night (11/11) This place has it all. Great food. Wonderful entertainment and top notch service. Arielle is an awesome server. Friendly and knowledgeable efficient and attentive!! The entrees were delicious ! Miso Sea Bass is a must!! Wonderful array of flavors!! The flat iron steak is cooked perfectly any way you want it!! The entertainment the Pearl played very upbeat and fun sets!! We can't get enough of this place.  Hats off the the entire establishment!!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
Absolutely love this place! The grocery store bakery makes the BEST chocolate flan I have ever had - a whole one ordered was $25!!! The people are so nice - I love heading over to Plaza Mariachi for lunch during the week or even on weekends (and I don't live close...lol).

Great entertainment - love the live music and Mariachi band!!

Overall, a great place that I hope stays around for a long while!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I have been to Sambuca several times and it never disappoints me and my friends. The food is great and so is the band. The music has a wide variety of genres so it appeals to a diverse crowd. The dance floor is very very small that to me is it's only flaw. 
This time I had the stuffed artichokes, roasted Brussels and a house salad. It was all delicious and more than I could eat. 
This time the place was full of women, there were only maybe 5 couples in the whole place. 
Me, my friends and all the other women there had a blast dancing. 
It's a sexy,  fun,  safe place and a night there won't set you back financially like some of the other places around Nashville. 
They also have valet parking!!

name: Red Rooster Bar & Music Hall
text: I sat at the bar and I felt like I was sitting at my 9 month old's booster chair.  The stool was too low...  Their original score from the health department was 71, and the follow up was a 92...I wish that I would have seen that BEFORE I ordered.  The shoulder sandwich had more fat that I liked.  In addition, my fries were cold.  After asking for a "fresh" batch, the waitress brought me back a basket of hot fries that tasted like the grease used to fry them in was old. The so-called hot BBQ sauce was anything but.  It was my 2nd visit (trying to give them a 2nd chance) but I won't go back.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
My friends and I were so excited for a night on the town in Nashville after getting off a rough part of the Appalachian Trail. We heard good things about Tin Roof so we went there first. 

THE BOUNCER WAS AWFUL TO US.

He wouldn't let us enter. All of us are 22+, so this came out of left field. We were patient in our response, because we all are of age and have been for a long time. We pulled out many other forms of identification, but he refused to give us the time of day. You might be thinking that he had to help the next people but it was early on a Monday night- there was no one else in line.

It was a terrible way to start the night, and we felt so disrespected and belittled. He was awful. 

Thankfully, Tin Roof is not unique. We still had a great night, enjoying other bars nearby. We will NEVER go back to Tin Roof.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is the home of TRUE country. Stuff you can only hear on Sirus XM channel 59
LOVE this place. Brazillabilly band is awesome!!  So much history in this establishment.
Gets packed...wonder why... Lol ...that tells ya something.
A MUST see!!! If in Nashville stop in.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: After hours the shops close down and the dance floor is open. They play all types of music, although the music is mainly Spanish, but they play all types and it is amazing. The dance floor is large and there are plenty of tables. Me and my friends had a great time. The security is also really good and lines move by fast. The drinks are expensive, but that is gonna be the case in most places. I would definitely come back and recommend it!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I did absolutely zero research on the honky tonk scene before coming to Nashville and I just randomly popped into RWW because I liked the music. I'm not really a fan of C&W, at least not "modern" C&W. I prefer the sounds of slide guitar from the '50's through the '70's and since I heard those delightful notes wafting through the open window of RWW, I figured it would be as good a place as any to have a beer and and a listen. 

The band was great and the beer was cheap. Seriously cheap. A PBR was $2.50. The bathrooms were clean enough and while the downstairs was really crowded, everyone was friendly. All in all, a very enjoyable time!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Best value and most authentic classic country venue in Nashville.  Reliable series of quality musicians that play old time gems as well as a few songs of their own.  Check out their music schedule for what acts they'll feature and when. 
Also: All day every day deal of $2.50 PBR & MHL plus delicious burgers.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is one of the oldest bars out on Broadway & really is a must stop if you want to experience downtown Nashville. The band my girlfriend Julie & I saw was great & if you get hungry they have a grill where you can grab a bite.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Robert's was one the Honky Tonks I wanted to visit. Since I was in Nashville for work, my boss & couple other people recommended that Robert's was one of their favorite Honky Tonk in Downtown Broadway. 

One thing I love about all the Honky Tonks, there is no cover charge but make sure you have cash on you because the bands will walk around with their tip jar (tips is the way the bands make their living). 

Food: We ordered their Fried Bologna Sandwich served with chips ($4.00). You can order their Recession Special which is their Fried Bologna Sandwich, Chips & PBR Beer. Since we didn't get to go to the breweries in Nashville, we got to try a few beers at Robert's. Tried Tennessee Beer Works, Southern Wit & Yazoo, Hop Perfect IPA. They were both really good! 

Entertainment: I forgot the bands name but the gentlemen who was sitting next to us told us they were the best band that performs in Downtown Broadway & he was right. We were able to go to Robert's twice during our trip & both nights we caught the same band. 

If you're in Downtown Broadway, make Robert's your first visit & make sure you order their Fried Bologna sandwich. Happy Eating!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great drinks, great music, and great service. What more could you ask for? This is a chill spot in a hot neighborhood. It draws all sorts of people, which always adds to the experience.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
The butcher in the market alone deserves 5 stars. Excellent meat and seafood selection and helpful.
All of the plaza (except of course the cell phone store, law office, and money changing place) is a great place to pig out and dig into some varied cultural experiences.
We got both the hot and cold platters from the tapas place and it was a good variety, then sampled the pizza, and then hit the ice cream/popsicle shop. Very good all around.
My friend took some of the ceviche home and raved about it. We tried the flan from the market and it was delicious as well.
The art gallery has some really beautiful things to look at. Make sure and check out the rope art.
Great concept and execution. I can't wait to see what moves in to the other spots inside the plaza.
While you're there, get your next meal to-go from Taj Indian Restaurant in the same parking lot. It's the best in town.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
One of the BEST venues EVER!!!
The music sounds soooo good in this venue it's unbelievable. I was here back in 1976 when I was a young gal and I wanted to go back since we are in Nashville alot.
We got Excellent seats, Sec. 3 row G
Amazing!!!! 
Country artist pop in all the time here. We had T Graham Brown pop in and sing a couple songs. Loved it. 
I felt so much closer to the artists and felt their heart pour out when they sang here.
I was however thought the gift shop could have had more things/variety and could have been bigger.. I did not see the GOO GOO bars anywhere. 
I would highly recommend this venue!!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Walked in because I heard "A Boy Named Sue," stayed when they started playing "Copperhead Road."  Food was solid.  Beer was cold.  Service was outstanding.  My favorite Honkey Tonk on Broadway, or tied with Legends.  People were great.  Service was better.  Beer was cold.  Bologna​ sandwich?  Corn Dog?  YES PLEASE!!!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We stopped in for lunch.  It is definitely nothing like the typical Nashville restaurants we went to.  It is dark and mysterious, more like a lounge, with really neat bold colored décor that pops out at you.  (We went on a Monday, so I'm sure the weekend/dinner experience is different) The lunch menu was very diverse and was reasonably priced for the area.  I ordered a soup and salad combo.  The shrimp and crab bisque was very tasty, although I wish it had more pieces of shrimp and crab in the soup.  I ordered The Bib salad, which was very fresh!  I also decided to try a Pale Ale from Yazoo, a local brewery in the area and it was also very flavorful.  Our waiter was new, so the service was a little choppy and slow, but the manager came by twice to see how things were going.  Overall, we had a great experience and I would definitely go back.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
***REVIEW FROM AN EXPERIENCE IN JUNE 2015: I just wanted to let everyone reading my review know that even though this review was written in the beginning of 2018; I went to this place in June 2015 (however I am sure if I went to this place again the review would be similar). A few days ago I was talking to someone about places visit in New Orleans because they are interested in visiting the city. I realized that when I went to New Orleans I went to a lot of amazing places but I never wrote Yelp reviews for them because I did not start writing Yelp reviews until the beginning of 2017. I enjoyed many places on my trip and I wanted to share my experiences with everyone  even though they are a few years old. So I decided to dig up some old pictures and write the reviews.

I would also like to add that most of the experiences I am writing about are places I went to while I was on a guided tour for my trip. I went on a Collette Tour called America's Music Cities. Most of the places we saw and ate at were planned because of the tour. During the tour we stopped at 3 major cities New Orleans, Memphis, and Nashville (and few other stops along the way). I just wanted to let everyone know that since I was on a tour my experiences may have been a little different compared to those who went to these places and were not on a tour (they went on their own) It was an amazing tour and I definitely recommend it.***

I went to the Ryman Auditorium for a tour. The Ryman is a beautiful place with a lot of Nashville history. I loved learning all about it and having the opportunity to see a piece of history. It is known as the Mother Church. The Ryman was a church before it became a home for the Grand Ole Opry (until the Opry moved however some Opry shows still perform here). The is also a mini Country Music Hall of Fame in the Ryman Auditorium where you could see some costumes people wore when they performed there. If you can, definitely visit the Ryman Auditorium especially if you like country music. 

I hope to go back someday and see a performance there. 

Enjoy!
Simona

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
We went to sambuca for our first meal in Nashville. 

Environment: excellent. Live music, great lighting, wonderful service, overall excellent ambiance. 

Food: for the price, it was okay. We got everything that was highly recommended by our server as being the very best, and it was decent- but not worth the upscale prices. We liked our cocktails and local brew, but the appetizers, salad and main course simply did not match the lovely environment. Although, desserts looked amazing, we were too full!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Love the tour and being able to learn the history of the building, of Nashville history and the history of the Grand Ole Opry. Seeing tonight's show (12/23/17). Most of the year the show takes place at a venue at Opryland, so we lucked out coming here midwinter. The posters and photos of past performers here was eye-opening. This old tabernacle is now referred by many as the church of country music. Taking a tour beforehand really is worth it. I had no idea of how close it came to be being torn down. Nice to see how they're preserving their musical heritage.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
I love Tin Roof!!!

I just got back from visiting my brother Nashville and while I was there I stumbled across this gem. I had been recommended to visit Honky Tonk Central, which I did, but I actually preferred Tin Roof. The environment at Tin Roof is casual, relaxed and fun. I also thought they had the best bands!

The bands play a lot of country but it isn't exclusively country. I went on a Wednesday from about 5-9 and on a Thursday night. You need to go and watch the band that plays every Wednesday from 330-7. I have never seen a band that was more relaxed, fun and was able to laugh at themselves. It is a trio and they are super chill and fun. It was the first and only band that I saw in Nashville (or ever, really) that was able to laugh at themselves if they made a small mistake (ex -- singing 90s song and voice cracked a little during a high pitched part...ha!). The mistakes aren't major but it is just refreshing to see 3 young guys having fun and just doing what they love - it is clear that they love it. They were funny and did a mix-up of 90s music when I was there -- Third Eye Blind, Blink 182, Incubus, etc. I had walked by earlier in the day and they were playing country. Overall, they were awesome!

The band that played after them from 7-11 (I think until 11) was also great but very different. They were much more intense (the other band was more relaxed and low-key) but these guys knew how to rock out. They were also really fun but very different energies. They played all country but I wasn't familiar with it all -- I would say it was a mix of older and newer songs. They were definitely talented.

The band two bands on Thursday were also great (one from 8-11ish in the front and the other in the back after 11). There was good dancing in the back when the second band set up for the rest of the night. 

The drinks are nothing fancy, so I am not looking for a craft cocktail when I am here. They do have happy hour specials from 3-7 and it is $1 off certain drinks (wells, etc.). I didn't try their food so can't speak to that.

The reason I took a star off is because of the bar service on Thursday night -- my mom ordered wine and it came in a plastic cup (which is fine) but the bartender only poured about an inch of wine in her glass. Really?! It was about $7 for an inch of wine...lame. I ordered a mixed well drink and it was fine. We switched bartenders later and he was better, however, their shots looked under-poured too. But, the 2nd bartender was friendly and attentive. Our waitress the day before was nice but I had walked to the bathroom and saw our drinks sitting there while she chatted w/other waitresses and they were still there when I came out - she brought them over right after that.

Overall, this is a great spot if you want to have some drinks, dance and listen to good music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: This place is top notch from head to toe. We were seated right away when we arrive. All of the staff was extremely friendly and professional. Our waitress was timely to our table, asking us if we would like anything to drink. The entertainment for the night with setting up as we sat down. They begin playing around the time that we got our food. The entertainment was fantastic! All of the food that myself and two friends got was absolutely divine. We had a few small plates(buck beignets and duck breast), Gorgonzola salad, a pizza, and the filet mignon. Not to mention the cheesecake for dessert. The steak is one of the best I've had in my entire life.  We also had a few Tennessee mules, which were very light and refreshing. The waitress was even able to separate our checks, which made it very easy to pay. I highly recommend this establishment!!!! I came all the way from Florida to have a great experience in Nashville, and this place did it. I am going to have to definitely come back.

name: Musicians Corner
text:
One word: Awesome.

Love this wonderful showcase of local artists. Dogs and kids run around while their loving parents sway to the music sipping on a beer or enjoying a snow cone. This is what I think paradise looks like. 

Bring your sunscreen and a blanket for sure and just enjoy the beauty of the combination of music, nature, food trucks and drinks. What could be better? Maybe a sprinkler.....but then you'll have to worry about mud.....So no, everything is perfect. Enjoy :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is amazing. Owen was probably the best waiter I have ever had and really made you feel at home. The food is affordable and absolutely delicious!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits are melt in your mouth good! For breakfast I had the southern sampler and the country ham was really good. The hash down casserole was yummy as well. Service was incredible and really fast! Loved it.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I should have known better....huge restaurant in tourist area.....red flags I ignored. Four of us ate there for Valentines Day.  One of four entrees was acceptable. Other food.....dry, no flavor. My Reuben had virtually no sauerkraut, and the meat was dry, tough and stringy! Looked like it had gone into the oven and left far too long. Go careful when considering this place for a meal. Settle for Black Forest cake and have your meal elsewhere.

UPDATE:  The on line customer service associate followed up immediately after my above review was posted and asked me to contact the restaurant's GM.  I did so today. He is DEFINITELY interested in providing a quality dining experience and was disappointed to hear about my experience. I'll now gladly give them a second chance.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
This past Saturday 22 of my friends and I went to the Bavarian Bierhause for dinner, beer, and dancing to an oom pa band.

It turned out to be an overall terrible evening all the way round.  Service:  Terrible - 30 minute wait to get the first beer - it took 45 minutes and  two servers with two different orders to get more beer.  To add insult to injury it took an hour to get a check
  The server had to go around and ask each person what they had! Then she processed each check one at a time some people waited almost another hour to pay!!!

Food some sausages over cooked and even burnt.  Some fish raw on the inside.  Many mixed up orders.  People would say this is not what I ordered.  Waitress would reply "this is what they made you".  You won't eat it????

Atmosphere way way way too much back around noise.  You could bafely  talk to the person next to you and no one else. 

Entertainment:  Band played some German songs them mostly US pop oldies.  Sound mixing was terrible band sounded very bad. 

Over all the evening was over the top bad.  22 people  have said we will never  go there again.
Alex Stillwell

Not good for a new restaurant in Nashville where people have high expectatioms at new venues!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
What it is:  A Munich Brew/Beer Hall in the U.S.  It is loud.  It is community seating (tables for 8-10)  Yes-you may be seated with someone you don't know.  No-you can't have a table made for 8-10 for you and your date.  Did I mention loud?  You go there for the atmosphere, to talk with friends and family, to laugh, sing, and drink beer and eat.  It's a place to hang out for a long time and enjoy the experience.
What it isn't:  A place for a quiet romantic dinner.  A place where the food is quickly prepared and served so you can eat and leave and they can turn over the table.  It's not a place to grab a quick bite on your way to the movie.
Seriously the food was great.  Enjoyed the Rouladen with red cabbage and sourkraut.  Sometimes rouladen are prepared differently in different regions.  I prefer mine with cubed bacon inside.  These seemed to be wrapped around a pickle and a carrot slice.  But very good.  Served warm-could have been hotter, temperature wise.  The Jagerschnitzel was good.  Now, wienerschnitzel is a breaded and fried pork or veal cutlet.  I remember Jagerschnitzel being fried without the breaded coating, then the mushroom gravy.  This seemed to be a wienerschnitzel with the mushroom gravy.  The beers were great!  
The band was tolerable.  I'm hoping they'll eventually find a "real" German band and have a long-term contract.  This evening was a guy with an accordion, a guy playing sax, and one on drums.  Some German drinking songs.  But-even Queen and Rammstein played on the accordion isn't German music. 
A flight of beer, a radler, a .5 liter beer, 3 entrees=$110 with tip. Opry Mills rent has it price. 
I will go back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Would of given 5 stars if they wouldn't of forgetten my preserves with my biscuits in my to go order. Being as the preserves are a staple I can't give 5 stars without trying with my biscuits! We're from Texas so I don't know if we'll ever eat here again. Hopefully so we can give them a try

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits best I ever had. Pulled pork was tender however pork chops dry fried chicken very good. people were so nice and the peach jam WOW.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: German beer,brats,bar at the mall. Overall food and atmosphere is good,great place to hang out while others are shopping.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
We have been to City Winery three times, each time for dinner and a concert. The food is fine. The service is fine. The building is fantastic, although directly beside the homeless shelter. It's nice they have valet service. The sound is fine.

Here's my problem...We saw Robert Earl Keen and he was introduced as "Robert Keen Earl." Last night we saw Mac McAnally, 7 time winner of Musician of the Year award, and he was introduced as "Mac McNally." City Winery is getting great acts and there are more shows I look forward to. I wonder how may times they can insult the artists and keep the talent coming.

Chris Knight is playing the venue soon. Please be aware the K is silent.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Nothing to say. Everything is fantastic. Don't think you'll like chicken and waffles. Try and be amazed

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This is a must if you are in Nashville area. The wait will be long but do yourself a favor and wait. There is the smokehouse to spend time in and the gift shop. So unique and a treasure. 
The food is amazing too

name: Loveless Cafe
text: For breakfast, the biscuits and blackberry jam are superior.  For lunch, the fried chicken is exceptional.  Everything else that I have tried is great.  Add to the great food the amazing history, the iconic location and the associated store nearby, and you've got an excellent eating experience.  To me, it's a "must try" for anyone visiting Nashville.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I loved this place!  The food was great and the staff are welcoming!  We happened upon live music night which was very entertaining.  The gift shop is small and reasonably priced. 
Highly recommend!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wonderful service and wonderful food.  Worth the extra drive if you are in town. Prices are pretty reasonable when you factor in the amenities.  Beautiful drive on the way!  The manager came out immediately to great us and help with food allergies.  The bbq omelet was perfect!  Enjoy!  Easy 5-stars!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Where in the world can I begin to write a review? I guess it has to be the biscuits-tender, flaky, fresh as fresh can be, right out of the oven, popped into my mouth before I even have a chance to smear on the strawberry, peach, or blackberry preserves. All you want-all day long. But save a little room for a delicious breakfast. You name it they'll make it. Today I'll just stick to some savory Southern Country Ham and some sunny-side eggs, of course with creamy, cheesy stone-ground grits. Mmmm. But wait. Can't decide; how about a sampler? Or if you brought friends and family...they got you covered--Family Style Breakfast includes sausage gravy too. And be sure to try the Hashbrown Casserole or maybe the BBQ omelet. Oh, you're here for lunch? Fried chicken, meatloaf (better than Mom's...sorry Mom), and finger lickin' good Pork Chops. So much good stuff, I never have room for dessert...but you might, and they got it too. Try some pie and make a note to come on back, y'all.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A must when in Nashville! Great food and service!!! Highly recommend.  We times it just right and was seated with out a wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Everything was amazing!!! The service, food and ambiance was perfection!! Catfish was not to be believed!! Our service was some of the best I've ever had!! Biscuits and jam of course were the best I have ever had and they are free!! You must go here for best southern comfort food in a laid back atmosphere:)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I've eaten here since 1996 wouldn't give it 5 stars due to the popularity of the restaurant and the wait times most encounter, food is pretty good but very overhyped. A must try for non-veterans but go on a weekday.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The Loveless Cafe has a nice concept for a restaurant, neat way to turn a motel into something else.  Came here on an afternoon so no wait for us, sat on a side patio, our waitress was slow and didn't really seem to want to be there.  We each got a drink with a sidecar shot in a souvenir mason jar.  I got the Harvest Moon with moonshine excellent and we also got a strawberry lemonade one too, good as well.  The biscuits with jelly were good, liked the different flavors of jelly.   We then tried a ham on a biscuit basic but good.  The best thing we had was the chicken and waffles, chicken was moist but crispy and the waffle was fluffy and crisp, a must try if you come here.  One of the best experiences was a group of southern women sat next to us and it was a riot listening to them, great people.  They have some nice souvenir shops in the rooms around the restaurant.  Overall it was a pretty cool place.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This place is massive and has a very fun atmosphere. We shared a platter that included a porkchop (which basically tasted like ham), a roast beef with gravy, one of their sausages, red cabbage, sauerkraut, and mashed potatoes. Everything was tasty and had a unique flavor to their seasonings.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Service was really good here tonight. It's the first time we stopped in here. They have a live polka band and had I thought about it, I would've requested to be seated away from it because it was so loud we were trying to scream at each other so it really put a damper on any kind of conversation. I ordered the Reuben  and it was decent. Not the best, but still good, my husband was really excited about the beer!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Been a few times and always loved it. Went shortly before Christmas for dinner and we were not happy with our dinner. Even messaged them on FB about it and no response. We had 2 Jägers and they were not like the times before. Overcooked and the gravy was not right. We will come back and hope the food will be better. Glad we have a German restaurant in Nashville now.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Really fun casual German beer hall. It's connected to the mall, but it boasts more of a touristy feel rather than a quick "dine and dash" mall spot. 

Unfortunately I was here for a work lunch and didn't get to sample any beers, BUT I highly recommend the reuben sandwhich. The marble rye and sauerkraut were good (a little strong but good), and the corned beef was nice and salty. 

Clearly a spot for good heavy German food. You can tell this place must get packed. It had rows and rows of bench style seating. Not the most comfortable, but hey, it's a beer hall.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We were totally unable to book online for an upcoming show. Then, show was sold out and still it was impossible to be placed on a wait list because of problems booking online----we even tried to set up a new account which rejected us and stated, "invalid password ". So, tried calling the venue to see if we could be placed on a wait list. No---not possible---can only be done online. Seriously? We won't bother w/this venue again.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: The experience was definitely European. The service was outstanding and the food was excellent. An excellent choice of German beers both on top and a bottled. A great place together with family for a good meal or friends for a Saturday football game.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best biscuits and fried chicken I've had in my life. There should be no contemplation about this place; just go!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Beautiful venue! The food was amazing and the service impeccable. Daryl and Mark went out of their way to make us feel welcome and answer any questions we had. The wine flight had four selections of wine that were all very good. We climbed the curved staircase to see the beautiful outdoor decks and seating area upstairs.
We made a reservation for brunch on Sunday, July 16, and it was a slow day so we pretty much had the place to ourselves! Highly recommend the eggs Benedict, the roast beef calzone with au jus, and the BLT. All were absolutely delicious and good portion sizes. Our appetizer was recommended and didn't disappoint. The food is high quality as is the service and the restaurant/venue itself is beautiful!

name: Big Shotz
text: Good drinks, good music. Double Shotz are $5. I was hoping for munchies to snack on, but the only food is Jello Shotz. Smoking is allowed, but it didn't get too smokey. Overall, not bad.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is amazing! I highly recommend everyone to go and see this place and have a meal. While you may have to wait, it worth very second of your time. The staff are so friendly and accommodating. The food is out of this world! The hash brown casserole is to die for.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: When I die I want to be buried under the foundation of Loveless Cafe. I've been to Nashville probably 10 times over the years and I finally tried this place with my friend on a Thursday morning around 11a. There was no wait. I strongly recommend you go on a week day so you can get in quick. The staff were extremely friendly and the restaurant itself has that Southern home charm so you feel like you're eating at someone's home. They are known for their biscuits and if you order a plate or platter you get biscuits with it automatically. The biscuits are very good. I would say 4/5. They have a crunchy texture on the bottom and are soft and fluffy on the inside. Our waitress guided us to get the pulled pork and eggs which was the best of both breakfast and BBQ. The pulled pork is hands down the best I've had in Nashville. Their BBQ sauce is also really tasty and has that tangy vinegar undertone I love in my sauce. The portion sizes are HUGE! You can get at least 2 meals out of it. The coffee was delicious and they came around often to fill up our cups. My friend got the hash brown casserole as her side and I got the cheesy grits. The grits are the best I have ever had anywhere! You have to get the grits! Long story short, I love this place and didn't want to leave. It's a must experience if you're in the area.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Not a bad place. I can't complain since we only have two German restaurants in Nashville that I know of.

Stopped here after shopping. If you're at the mall, it is almost impossible to find this restaurant because you literally have to walk through an exit door. Once you're inside tho, this place is huge!

Food was decent. We only had their wurst when we ate here. They don't let you substitute your sides so FYI- you're stuck with your fries.

Kitchen was a bit slow for a not so busy place. Our server was nice tho.

I'd like to come back and try their main dishes next time. They have plenty of beer choices of course.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Holy biscuits! It's been a few weeks since our last visit and I am constantly craving their biscuits-so good! There's really just no place like Loveless. The staff feels like family and you never feel rushed. Take some time to walk around after you eat-the shops are all lovely.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We went around 10am on a weekday and the wait was 40 minutes. The biscuits and jam were delicious. However the rest of our food was not great. Def not worth a long wait. We got chicken & waffles, waffles, eggs & bacon and pancakes. The atmosphere was fun and the gift shops had a lot of cute things. Guess it is more of an experience place but don't think we would go back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
OK 511 reviews let me throw mine in there!

It is good great country ham, went on a Monday morning 8am so no wait.  would I wait for breakfast?

Can't go wrong though for breakfast.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We checked out this place while on vacation in Nashville and it was worth the trek. It is a bit off the beaten path of downtown Nashville, but the drive is somewhat scenic and was enjoyable. Upon getting seated, our server brought us two platefuls of biscuits and jams - and when I says platefuls, I mean stacked up in 5s and we immediately started stuffing our faces. They were so good. 

I ordered the pit cooked pork bbq plate and my husband got the fried pork chop plate. They came out and my jaw dropped, they were so big it was enough to feed me for lunch and dinner (possibly breakfast the next day too!). I thought the bbq pork was good, not the best I had during this trip however. My husbands fried pork chop however was so good. I could have eaten that all day long. 

They also had cute little shops to make this more of a destination to check out rather than just the restaurant - which after how much we ate, we needed the walk. I definitely enjoyed those biscuits and think this was worth the drive.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Absolutely beautiful ambiance. The food however is a different story. The performance was nearly over before we received our food. My husband ordered a pizza. We also ordered the truffle fries and a Kale Caesar salad. The salad was delicious until I pulled a long, stringy red hair from the salad. At that point, I was done! The venue is beautiful but the food service is lackluster. Eat before you go!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Just finished a great lunch here.  It's an authentic and fun German restaurant.  The food was fabulous and the service even better.  I couldn't recommend more.  Andrew was my server and did a fabulous job.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I had high hopes when I first walked in because of the restaurant design, but I was really disappointed in the food. Don't go here if you're expecting real German quality food. This is the worst Jagerschnitzel I've ever had. Bier cheese was terrible too. I definitely won't be back

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Love the venue -- classy, intimate, good wine -- great shows.  I have not had food here, so can't comment .. But since I really think Nashville in general is missing the mark on classy places --- this gets a 5 star for me.  Nashville is a strip of 'bars' and beer drinking joints -- so this is a really great option (one of the few) where you can see a show and drink some nice wine.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I went here for breakfast this morning, and it did not disappoint! We arrived at 9:45 AM and got the last open table before they went on a wait. For a Monday morning, that shows you how popular this place is. 

The child in me was craving some chocolate milk, and their chocolate milk is wonderful! Very creamy and chocolatey. 

The biscuits come out first with blackberry, strawberry and peach preserves. They were all delicious, but I think the blackberry was my favorite. If you fall in love with one, they sell them so you can enjoy them at home or bring back as a souvenir or gift if you're traveling. 

I ordered the bacon and eggs with a side of grits. I've learned that you either love grits or HATE them. I'm a true southern girl so I love them! I must say the grits at Loveless are some of the best I ever had. 

The serving of eggs was huge! I got them scrambled with cheese, and I swear there had to be about 4 or 5 eggs on my plate. I only got half way through before I threw in the towel. The bacon was cooked crispy, just like I like it. That makes a big difference to me when choosing a breakfast spot, as most places never listen when I ask for crispy bacon. 

This will definitely be a go to breakfast spot for me from now on!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I struggled between 3 and 4 stars on this one. My girlfriend and I attended a concert here two nights ago and I had mixed feelings. As far as our food went, it was amazing. We had the burrata, which was out of this world, and also the Brussels sprouts. They were cooked perfectly and seasoned just right. There were no complaints there. However she ordered a glass of wine that she received after our food came out and I ordered a beer that never showed up at all. On top of that the doors were supposed to open at 6 and the show started at 8. We showed up at 6:45 so that we would have plenty of time to eat before. We weren't seated until after 7:05 because we were waiting in a line that wasn't moving at all. Just seemed a little poorly organized which caused the wait on the drinks and wait to be seated. I would go back just for the food and get take out next time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Pretty good, honestly don't understand what all the hype is about.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I don't understand why this place is so praised for their biscuits?? They have this awful chalky aftertaste. My husband can confirm. Have tried them on different occasions and always taste off. Is it the kind of thing where no one wants to disagree because it's so famous?? Disappointing.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food was amazing. The biscuits were unlike any I have ever had. Waitress was so kind, and service was speedy. Can't wait for my next trip to Tennessee. Loveless will be on the list to visit again, because of the current biscuit withdrawals :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Went in early on a Friday morning, had a omelet and biscuits and gravy. Biscuits and gravy were good but not the best I have ever had. The one pet-peeve that I have is un-melted cheese, which the omelet had, and under cooked onions and green pepper. The ham in the omelet was excellent. Prices are a little high, since this place is a tourist trap.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Excellent food and service Lucas (luke) awesome server ....best breakfast near nashville

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is a fantastic place and a must if you are in Nashville at any time. I had ordered the BBQ over eggs which are over pancakes. It was one of the best things I have ever eaten. The biscuits where the best I have ever had. They even have a cute little shop where they sell the biscuit mix and was so good. Later on our trip we went back for lunch and had the BBQ pulled pork sandwiches. It was soooo good. Be prepared to wait because this place is always busy no matter what time you go. However, you can check out the little shop or play bags while you wait. Thats right I said this place had bags that you can play while you wait. This is definitely a must go!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Went during the week with my dad and we both loved this place.  We waited only about 20 minutes,  I heard the wait can be up to 3 hrs on the weekend.  There is a window where you can watch them make the biscuits from scratch.  The food was amazing, I would go back.

The gift shops are super charming too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: OK so you are driving into Nashville from Memphis... BANG you see Lovelace Cafe's sign! STOP at this restaurant! You will not be disappointed! If you have ever listened to some rando on the Internet, listen to me now! The Lovelace  Cafe is amazing, flavorful, and spazmatic!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Definitely will have to come back and take in a show.

Atmosphere:
The entrance reminds me of a theater hall - which it pretty much is. We went the day after Christmas so the crowds were extremely low - like maybe 1 or 2 other groups with ours so we were able to enjoy an empty restaurant. You should be able to park on the street but it can be sketchy. (This place is next to the Nashville Rescue Mission - I think they tow if you park there.) Valet is available as well.


Service:
Since there was not a crowd we didn't have to wait. We didn't even have reservations so I couldn't tell you how the peak hours are.

They sat us near the bar but we could still see everything happening.

The food came out promptly.

Food:
We decided to go with the prefix menu with the wine pairing. I would highly recommend doing so as it was delicious, and the servings were surprisingly large. (Make sure to ask if you've got food allergies as they may substitute some dishes for you.)

However the wine pairings you can leave out. I would suggest if you're familiar with your wines that you just choose yourself. Some of the pairings were a bit overwhelming.

Overall:
I enjoyed the food very much. I was hesitant when this place first opened because it was next to the Nashville Rescue Mission but knew eventually I would have to give it a shot. I'm glad I did.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
We were given free pretzels by the lady standing outside the restaurant (a card to get a free pretzel). They have a gluten free menu for those that need it and a vegetarian menu as well. Amazing. 

I got the potato dumplings with mushroom sauce which were delicious and the wonderful pretzel with honey mustard dipping sauce. 

The apple strudel (warm) is a must. 

The accordion player was excellent. 

Recommended

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I live right down the street from the Loveless so we frequently get carry out because the wait is too long. Expect a long wait, but there are shops that you can visit while waiting. 

As for the food, it's all the southern food that you would expect. The biscuits are delicious and I am not even a biscuit fan in general. The fried okra is great and the breakfast menu is recommended.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great breakfast at the Loveless Cafe.  My wife had the Chicken Fried Steak breakfast, which was melt in your mouth delicious.  I had the country ham, which I had not had before.  It was a bit salty for my taste, but surely was exactly what you would be looking for in this type of ham. The endless biscuits were a hit with the family, and the homemade jam was worth the trip alone.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
This is my new favorite place to go! Had the pleasure of seeing Los Lobos at City Winery a month or so ago. Just getting around to writing the review...

We used the valet service when we arrived which was fast & efficient. Walked in through the beautiful entry into main lobby and were greeted by several friendly staff along the way. We made our way to the podium to check in and were immediately escorted to our awesome seats for the show. Honestly though, there doesn't appear to be a bad seat in the house. We were on the side, second row of tables....

Our server came by within 30 seconds to get our drink order. Since our group was interested in wine, she brought over the sommelier to assist. He was very knowledgeable and recommended a great wine for our party. We ordered food and enjoyed the ambience and said hey to other friends who were attending. 

Food arrived quickly. Everything was really delicious - I loved the mussels and had the steak for entree. It was very tender and tasty...everyone in our group enjoyed the food very much!! Our server was excellent as well so the dining experience was 5/5 overall for food quality as well as service. 

The show began and this was amazing for many reasons. (a) I love Los Lobos - they are an old favorite and they never disappoint. (b) The sound of the venue was first class - excellent PA system was rich, warm and the mix was perfect...you could hear everything and nothing was either too loud or too quiet (c) Having a excellent meal while experiencing this made it over the top great!!! Add in the fact that you have plenty of "elbow room" makes it really fun to kick back, relax, and just enjoy the show!

I love City Winery and will go out of my way to see concerts there again and again!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Danke Bavarian Bierhaus! This place is amazing and you just feel you are having a beer and a sick pretzel in Germany. They have 1 liter beers, Giant pretzels ( you got to have one) and their apple strudel is delicious. So far, The giant pretzel is the most delicious I have ever tried.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Hubby and I came here in October to check out their fried chicken.  We were pleasantly surprised to be served complimentary homemade biscuits and jams which were all delicious!

The chicken did not disappoint either ... the coating was golden brown crispy and juicy.  It's a very popular place for tourists so there was a wait to get seated but they had many shops to keep people entertained.

Very friendly service!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I've been here countless times and have never had a bad meal or experience. The staff is wonderful and the food even better. If you want good home cooking then this is for you. There are options for everyone and an all day breakfast menu. They smoke bbq all day long on the property and it's to die for. The price is more than fair too. The bbq omelette in the picture was $8 and is huge. You can't go wrong with bottomless biscuits with a variety of jams.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is a German themed restaurant, not an actual German restaurant. The beer is the delicious, but the food is not. You will enjoy this best if you have never been to Germany or even an authentic German restaurant. Diuble check your bill, our waiter added the $3 beer cheese sauce to our order, without us asking for it. And for some reason, after i filled out the check, and added the tip, the receipt that I sign had been rounded up.  I will not be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
My friends and I had brunch here on a Sunday morning. The wait time was about an hour and a half, but we were able to order take out to eat at the picnic tables outside and received our food within about twenty minutes--worth it! While waiting for our food, we wandered around the shops. I loved the concept of this cafe and the way that the motel property has been re-purposed. Very popular with bikers, hipsters, families, retirees...this is truly the type of place that brings generations together.

I had a tough time deciding what to order, but after smelling the barbecue roasting I went with the pulled pork barbecue with eggs. This could easily feed two people...so much food! The barbecue was delicious, as was the hash brown casserole that I ordered on the side. I had high hopes for gluten free biscuits, but alas. I tried the peach preserves and they were great.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Everything was very good! The biscuits were great, the jumbo chicken strips, Mac n cheese, fried okra, mashed potatoes and has brown casserole were all so yummy! We got there at 5:30 on a Sunday and waited about an hour. Worth the drive!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I'm not one of those people who gets up early to eat breakfast or that person who just can't get started for the day without a heaping plate of sausage and eggs first thing after I wake up. Hell, most days, by the time I've done my morning routine (check emails, read the latest Cracked articles, read the news, shower/dress), it makes more sense to eat an early lunch and just skip breakfast (unhealthy, I know). This is not to say that I don't enjoy breakfast. I loved chowing down on the dining hall's breakfast on weekends when I was in college. I'm always up for a late night trip to IHOP (or WAHO, if I'm south of the Mason-Dixon). I've even been known to whip up big Sunday breakfasts if the mood suits me (homemade pancakes are my go-to, but I've made crepes and ebelskivers and omelets and more). I'm not a fan of early morning breakfasts, but I adore brunch and I enjoy leisurely breakfasts, and when I'm traveling, I'm much more inclined to fit breakfast into my schedule.

While visiting Nashville a few weeks ago with my best friend from home, trying out breakfast joints was near the top of our list of things to do. The South knows how to do breakfast and Nashville has a collection of well known breakfast places and diners (including Noshville and Pancake Pantry). The Loveless Cafe is perhaps the best known breakfast place and it's famous for a reason: they serve a delicious breakfast. 

To be completely honest, we didn't actually dine in the restaurant...we drove out there on a Saturday (after being defeated by the long lines at the Pancake Pantry) with high hopes of finding a seat. Unfortunately, everyone and their mother had the same thought in mind, so when we pulled in, it was a struggle just to find a parking spot, let alone a spot on the restaurant's waiting list. After hearing the wait could be well over an hour, and unable to handle the increasing grumbles of distress from our stomachs, we opted for the take-out option (having been reassured that it would only take about 15 minutes). 30 minutes later (which was not too bad, because the waiting list time was now almost 2 hours), we had two Styrofoam containers filled with breakfast and, as the weather was unusually warm for January, we were able to to take a seat at one of the picnic tables in front of the restaurant. The food was delicious: the eggs were light and fluffy, the biscuits were airy and buttery, the sausage had a nice snap to it, and the jam was sweet. My friend had some sort of concoction of pulled pork and eggs and hash browns and more and enjoyed every forkful. After dining, we roamed around the property, visiting the little shops scattered about (I happily purchased a bag of biscuit mix and apple butter--both ended up being delicious). 

So, while I can't review the actual dining experience in the restaurant, I can say that the food was excellent and, with its reputation and that whole "the owner was friends with Paula Deen and a bunch of country stars have eaten there" thing, it makes sense that it's a busy little place. If you want to dine in, be prepared to wait for a long time. Take-out is a great option and it definitely is quicker than waiting for a table--there are picnic benches around the property, or you could always take it to go. The employees I spoke to were incredibly friendly, despite the craziness going on around them, and they were quick too. The restaurant is a little bit out of the way, but parking is pretty decent and it's not too far from downtown. 

If you're looking for a great breakfast, definitely drop by...just be prepared for the fact that you may just end up eating breakfast for lunch due to the wait time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This was so amazing and totally worth the wait. My server Skye was super sweet and friendly. The food is so yummy!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We got here on a Sunday morning around 10 am the last day when we were in Nashville and there was a 2 hour wait! Wanting to get on the road, we ordered to go and it was ready in 15 minutes! The pimento and fried green tomato biscuits were recommended by the sweet hostess and they were out of this world! We enjoyed all the staples as well. Stopped in the gift shop and purchased a cookbook and some biscuit mix and we were on our way. 

To summarize - if you are in a pinch for time, order to go.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: One of my favorite places to eat in Nashville! I also love the entertainment aspect. City Winery does a great job of booking desireable talent, and it never fails when I'm in need of showing my visiting friends/family a good time! I would recommend this to anybody. A little higher price point, but the experience and quality food are so worth it!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We are spoiled because we live close to this Nashville treasure. That means we can come during the week and avoid the two hour wait times during nearly every Saturday and Sunday of the year. 

But, if you're visiting Music City and want to try some famous biscuits and fried chicken, then this is a great place to put on your list. 

Located in West Nashville near the scenic Natchez Trace, it is an easy, scenic drive from downtown Franklin, or conveniently located off I-40 and McCory Lane. 

Come on the weekend and prepare to wait. The time will pass quickly as you visit the gift shop, take photos by the famous Loveless sign or play a round of corn hole or two. 

By the time you're done, you'll be ready to eat. This converted motel turned restaurant has charm. The entry is covered with autographed photos from country singer, athletes and local celebrities. 

The staff is friendly and many have worked at Loveless for several years. 

We've enjoyed many meals here as a family, friends and even a couple of business meetings. You can't go wrong. While the biscuits may be what bring you in the first time, it's the charm of this local institution that will bring you back.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Good and bad. Good: atmosphere, personnel friendly, clean, new, music. Bad: 28% tax on food and drink, plus $5-6 parking. So total of extra 50% of our experience was on taxes and parking. AND, extra 20% fees on top of event fee. Plus plus plus...this place nickel and dime's you to exhaustion. Boo!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: After a long drive from NH we made a quick stop in Nashville and a local bartender told us we couldn't continue our journey without stopping for brunch at Loveless. I had the fried chicken and waffles with a bloody mary and my bf had the pulled pork and a moonshine drink. And let us just talk about the biscuits for a second, warm and buttery magic. Coming from New England, this exceeded our expectations as to what Southern food should be. The portions were huge and well priced. Our server was an absolute sweet heart! In a whirl wind trip, they left a lasting impression on us!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Not only are their biscuits ahhhmazing (and jellies) but the place is also iconic! I love the food, but there's so much history there too. Feels like I'm eating in my memaws kitchen! And there's even a gift shop for tourists passing through!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I've been to City Winery about 7-8 times. I've had a review on here before but they removed it because it of something to do with the reason I was here was for an event, which I feel most people come here for an event. I digress. This wasn't my first time. 

We arrived around 6:15pm on a weekday for an event. The event stated that valet parking was free for us, it's normally $6. Usually you can find parking in the back of the lot. This night there was two lanes, a valet lane & an Uber/Lyft lane. We decided to park in a spot down the hill from City Winery. In front of where we parked, it said "IR-G Customer parking 7am-5pm Monday - Friday". It was a Thursday, so we thought we were good. 

We were parked in the car for about 3 minutes when a valet attendant came down to speak with us. He said that we weren't able to park there as they park the valet cars. We could valet up front or park on the street along & behind City Winery. If you've been to City Winery, the whole place is fenced off. To park on the street & walk around is probably a block walk. This part of town isn't somewhere I want to walk a block in the dark when we left. He asked what event we were there for & we told him. He said that valet was free. We asked if we had to drive the car up there to then have him drive it back & he smartly said "yea" and shook his head up & down. 

We asked him about the sign that said IR-G parking & he said that "we have permission to park here".  So it's not even City Winery's property & they're dictating who can & cannot park there. I even looked it up on the property records & they don't own it. So we move the car up to the parking lot proper. There was a ton of open spots & cars that weren't backed in, which made me think other "regular" people parked there. Also because in the past we'd parked in the lot without issue, even when the valet was in force. 

We parked in the lot along the patio & got out. As we locked the car, a different valet ran over to tell us that we couldn't park there. He also asked what event we were there for & he told us valet was free. I asked "if the valet is free, can we not leave it here?". He said, "no". It then dawned on me, if we didn't have them park it & keep the keys, they would be out a tip. I asked him, "can I just give you a tip & we be able to leave it here". He agreed & I gave him $3 to leave it where we parked it. 

That situation put a slight damper on the night but it bounced back with the black bun pork burgers we had & some hummus. They also had some different wines on happy hour pricing, for $7. Not a huge deal, but better than the $10-$14 normal price tags. Two wines at $7 each, the bill totaled $17.40. I didn't think about it till after the fact, maybe some kind of tax? Liquor tax maybe?

They've got small plates on the happy hour menu (that runs from 5pm-7pm). We also had the crispy risotto balls, beer cheese stuffed, spicy mustard & adobo BBQ. I could've ate ten of those things, but instead I ate like 3 of them. I tried one of the duck tacos, I liked the flavor but the meat was a little dry, maybe an unlucky one. 

I've got no issues with City Winery expect for that exchange between the valet. I really don't understand how all these valet's in town can close down & take over public streets or other people's property for their parking. Next time I'll park on the street & pack a scooter to ride over.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: So worth the drive!  Crispy chicken, tender gizzards, best biscuits ever!  Desserts were good, but we were really too full to appreciate them.  I'd skip dessert and have another biscuit myself.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My second visit in late August:

I made reservations for my meetup group of ten ladies here because of the amazing time I had previously at City Winery. I bragged on this place and the wait staff and could not wait to share the Nashville gem with the group. First, the reservation process...I made the reservation on open table and asked to have a tour and noted that I was a Vino file. I expected a call about the reservation which happens nearly every time I use open table but not this time. So I called the day prior and asked if we were touring and why no one reached out. I was told tours need to be made 48 hours in advance but that they would squeeze my guests in if it was not busy. We show up and it was busy with a Nashville Scene event. We were seated and waited for 14 minutes before anyone asked for our drinks and that was after I asked a server to find our waiter. Up walks Jared. SMH. I time everything when I get served in a restaurant like literally on my iPhone I time it. It took 15 minutes to get a round of mimosas so I asked for the manager to check on it and up walks Jared who tells me "oh they are sitting on the bar". Well go get them please Jared. At this point I snagged Darrell and remembered him from the amazing previous service and begged him to be our waiter. He quickly took our orders and was so pleasant to my guests. Thanks God for Darrell! I even had a guest celebrating a birthday and he even got her a slice of blue velvet cake. Jared however was aloof and spent much time with his other two tables. The food came out and all guests were pleased. I then asked the hostess about the tour and she said sure you can tour now it is not busy I'll send the manager. The manager never came. One of my guests stopped the manager and asked for the manager so we could tour and he replies oh I'm the manager. I explain the situation and he says we cannot tour. He said "I don't know who you talked to yesterday but we can't". I'm a vinofile and will not bring my guests here again. I was embarrassed to have talked to highly of this place. What a huge disappointment and disaster

name: The Basement
text:
Oh man. If I lived in Nashville, I feel like I would be here ALLLLLL the time. It really seems like the go-to place for new and emerging talent. Talking to some people on the patio, there is also a fair share of accomplished musicians who decide to drop in unannounced, (I heard Metallica came once upon a time to randomly practice their set). This was our first stop when we got into town, as my friend was putting on a Texans in Tennessee showcase that included a bunch of singer-songwriters either living in, or originally from Texas. There was truly something for everyone - indie artists, country artists, a little bit of pop-rock...and everyone was more than welcome. 

I can't put my finger on it, but you just feel like you're kind of in the presence of greatness in this place. Like one day you'll hear someone on the radio and say, "Oh, I remember seeing them at the basement!" 

Drinks are reasonably priced and pretty heavy-handed if you go the liquor route. The bartender was super friendly and awesome. Definitely a place to visit if you're visiting - even if you don't know anyone who's playing, you'll probably still find someone you like.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wow!  Such a great experience!  We had a large group so we had to wait a little while (but it WAS a Saturday night so we expected it). They did have shops and things to look at and check out on property though, so that was nice. Once we were seated there were no disappointments from there on!  The food portions were huge and plentiful!  It was a great experience and I would love to come back with my family!  Thanks!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: After reading some other reviews I feel that Some people just want to complain.   $5 for valet is reasonable.  This is a intimate venue.  We watched Jason Isbell there last night and the crowd was 412 people.  I was amazed an audience could actually be quiet in this day and age.  The food seemed a bit pricey but it was very tasty.  No complaints about our service, as Ashley took very good care of us.  The wine selection was good, the craft beer selection could stand a few more options, but this place is called the winery....   If an artist you like comes to the winery, do yourself the favor and go watch them there.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Yummy! Long wait , but played cornhole and enjoyed our company ! Food was amazing!!! Pulled pork BBQ biscuit is where it is AT!!! I may have also drank a mimosa for two ... By myself.... Yummy yummy yummy !!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Southern hospitality at its best, and QUALITY FOOD!!! I could not believe my mouth! This place is everything it promised to be, always FRESH HOMEMADE ingredients is what we were told, and they delivered no problem... THE BEST BISCUITS ANYWHERE!!! Seriously folks... as a native Californian, i have never ever ever tasted biscuits so good. I've got a gluten sensitivity, but am not celiac, and these did not affect me at all. The pork loin was tender and delicious, the creamed corn is to die for, the service is friendly, warm, amazing - Susan was our waitress and she was generous with portions and her customer service - before we leave Nashville, we are definitely making the 30 minute drive back out to this place... IT IS WORTH IT YA'LL!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Got biscuits? The Loveless Cafe has you covered. Buttery, flakey and served with strawberry, blueberry and marmalade jam, breakfast doesn't get much better. Come early, or you will wait. As an alternative, you can also order takeout and eat at one of their picnic tables. Country ham, fried chicken, grits, sausage gravy and hash brown casserole are all not to be missed. We got a sampler of pies to go, and I'm already looking forward to dessert. Customer service and price ping both A+. Be sure to stop by their retail store on the way out for some merch, biscuit mix and jam.
