name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is a little diner out in the middle of nowhere.  We went based on the reviews.   We were not impressed.  The mac and cheese was decent.  We had the fries checked fingers and three sides.  We purchased one extra.  We had sweet potatoes which were too sweet, fries green Tomatoes which tasted like they were laying in the kitchen all day.   Not impressed.  Our waitress was super friendly and made the experience enjoyable but the food was mediocre at best.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This breakfast is GREAT! Boyfriend and I got to Loveless at about 9:45 on a Saturday morning. We went in knowing we were going to have a lengthy wait, so when we were quoted an hour and a half I wasn't too perturbed. The grounds are really cute and we were distracted (or I should say I was distracted) by the shopping for about 20 minutes. Afterwards, we just sat in the car with the buzzer from Loveless because it wasn't a super nice day, and listened to Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows on audiobook. Highly recommend.

Our buzzer went off after about 45 minutes, cutting our wait time in half! This was awesome, and I don't know if they over-quote intentionally but I think it's a genius idea because I was so happy when the wait was shorter than I had gotten prepared to wait for.

The place is ADORABLE inside and our waiter was really nice. I had an omelette, my boyfriend had a sampler with a million meats and eggs, and we gorged ourselves on those biscuits. The omelette was really yummy and my boyfriend's plate was very good as well, but at the end of the day, I think people go here more for their lunch specials like fried chicken than a standard omelette, but OH MAN THOSE BISCUITS.

The biscuits are so light, so flaky and delicious. The jams that accompany them are delightful, and I had to tell our waiter to stop bringing them over because I was getting really concerned at how many I would be capable of eating.

This is a really fun, albeit kitschy, breakfast spot. Don't come here if you are a person who will be annoyed at waiting a long time for food that isn't THE BEST FOOD YOU HAVE EVER HAD. Enjoy the experience, and mostly those biscuits. Yum.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I was so excited to try this place out. After living in Germany for 3 years, we were hopeful to find some familiar foods there. The portions were extremely small especially the schnitzel (husbands order)which is usually the size of a large plate, it was more of a kids size . So that made the high priced plate pretty lame. It was also the most greasy schnitzel I've ever had. 
My mom and I shared the roast and it was served with mashed potatoes that were very awful. To top it off, my mom and I got very sick after our meal!!!! 
Then there's the Kasespaetzle which was just okay. They topped it with dried French onion which honestly was what made it good. 

On a good note, the live music is always great! I might return for a beer and atmosphere, but I wouldn't eat there again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Despite the 1 1/2 hr Sunday noon wait at the cafe the visit and meal to the Nashville iconic cafe was a delightful afternoon.  The wait was made bearable by complimentary coffee and lemonade with plenty of shady porches to sit under.  There is a country store and gift store on the grounds.  They sell ham, biscuit mix, marmalade and other popular items that are on the cafe menu.There are a few other boutiques and and art gallery featuring local handicrafts.
The breakfast menu is available all day and dinner is served at 1100 on.  No reservations on weekends but they are possible by using an app during the week.
The food was delish.  Biscuits were free and probably the highlight for me. They serve alcohol drinks as well.

name: Big Shotz
text: Never do business with this place. Owner has horrible business ethics. It's a newer spot and I guess they just haven't figured out how to treat people right. Save your money for a place that's worth it.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
My sister and I dropped in for lunch. She lived in Germany for three years and misses many of the foods she came to love there. This restaurant scratched the itch for her! 

We started with the Bierhaus Wings. Since I was expecting pig knuckles, I was a little disappointed. However, they tasted really great. They just weren't what I thought they were going to be. We had jaegerschnitzel with fries, schweinbraten with red cabbage, sauerkraut, and potato dumpling, and black forest cake. My sister didn't like the sauerkraut, but I did. We agree on everything else that it was marvelous!

We'll go back for sure!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Atmosphere was great food was so so disappointing variety of entrees and some dishes were not really good

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Awesome venue!!! We saw Phil Vasser here in October, 2019.  They are an urban winery that source their grapes or juice from California. So they offer a nice selection of wine including some cabs, francs, blends, Pinot noir, and more. They also offer a nice selection of craft beer. The food was delicious; pizzas, apps, and main entrees.

The venue has 200-300 seats that all offer a good view of the performer. The service was great, and we will definitely be back!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The bar and food service sucked at the Leon Russell show last Sunday.  This is my 15 th show at the Winery and the food and service has declined steadily since I joined last year.  The Shows are outstanding but if you want the whole packages it misses. I love this place for music but the service and kitchen timing need to step it up.  We got our food during the last song.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Food was good.  Beer was good. I might go back for those items.  The service was a bit slow.  Friday night and not really that crowed.  The music was way TOO loud, or poorly projected.  And the room is not acoustically prepared for it. You could not talk at the table.  The waitress could not hear, and neither could we.  And there are lots of questions about the food and drinks.  Having music is nice, but get a better PA system and turn it down.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Every time I go it's an absolute treat. Delicious food (especially the biscuits---OMG) and fast service. Everyone is friendly and sweet. I highly recommend Loveless and even though there is always a wait, don't let that deter you. Enjoy the grounds, shop in their stores or lounge in the yard while you wait--it's worth it! Try the potato casserole and chicken salad. Both are EPIC!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: First off the beer is delish. Atmosphere is amazing. Food is to DIE FOR. We're officially fans and will be back every weekend lol

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is special to our family. Anytime we are in the Nashville area, we make our way to the Loveless for some good Southern cookin'. Breakfast, lunch or dinner, this place has it all. The Loveless Cafe is somewhat of a Nashville institution, so be ready for a wait during peak days and times. Even on a Friday late afternoon, we waited for 35 minutes or so. However, we did a bit of shopping in the gift shops and played a few games of cornhole while we waited. It was a nice to have alternatives to just waiting for a table. Once seated, the service was wonderful, and the food was even better! We had fried chicken, spicy fried chicken and a pulled pork dinner and all were fabulous. 
As a tip- this is off the beaten path. It is at the northern terminus of the Natchez Trace parkway, worth a drive on for a few miles as it is beautiful. It will take a bit of time to get to if you are heading from downtown. I'll be honest, I wanted to eat here so bad, I fibbed to my husband about how far off the Interstate it really was. I think if he heard ten more minutes one more time, I'd have been left on the side of the road in Nashville. But hey, I'd probably be working at the Loveless by now!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We have been lovers of Loveless for 30 years. It's all about the biscuits and fried chicken. We made many a pilgrimage to the restaurant when we lived in the Nashville area for 20 years and make sure to return with each visit back.

The wait time can be substantial. It's best to arrive after 1:00 and before 5:00. If you can, ask for a table in the original house section at the front of the restaurant. The add on area is loud and rushed, resembling the ambience of a Cracker Barrel 

Order the fried chicken or better yet, the fried chicken livers. And don't fill up on biscuits and homemade preserves, you will need the stomach space.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We had high hopes for this place....after living in Germany for 4 years we wanted to have a good German meal  Unfortunately The customer service was horrible and the food mediocre at best    Maybe stop in and have a beer ( albeit warm) but save your money and don't eat

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: Cool space, good drinks, great staff!!! Breakfast served all day which is always a plus.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The grits, omg... the biscuits, omg! I swear in another life I was a southerner who survived solely on barbecue, grits, biscuits, and gravy. 

When I visited with friends during a Nashville vacation, I was more than excited to make the trek here for breakfast. We knew the wait would be worth it. Surely it was. You should also know that this isn't in the heart of the city, but rather on the outskirts -- about a 30min drive from the city. I shall remind you, the food is worth it.

We arrived, put our names in, received a pager that would work on the Loveless plot, which had a few gift shops and other places to sit and relax while you wait. For us, they said 1 hour, we got our table after 45min. 

Needless to say, we got a great deal of shopping done while we waited! The gift shops have cookbooks, biscuit mixes, kitchen decor and supplies, and so many other great items that are perfect for souvenirs or gifts to bring home for family and friends. Meanwhile, the hunger pangs started coming because of the irresistible scent of barbecuing meats wafting through the air.

Every table starts with a basket of biscuits (dreams do come true). They're small, warm, and fluffy. I loved the butter + blackberry preserves combo. I didn't want to overdo it so I had to cool off after 3 biscuits and save room for my entree. I had the pork barbecue with eggs over easy and a side of cheesy grits. I can't describe the comfort I felt as I devoured the tender, juicy pulled pork topped with a drizzle of extra BBQ sauce, which is more than enough to last another meal. Of course I had leftovers, which were great as a late night snack later that evening. The grits were perfect - creamy and cheesy and full of flavor. 

I could eat here for the rest of my life and be happy. Oh, how I wish I could...

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Excellent food! Great friendly service!!! Would definitely come back next time we come through Nashville. Biscuits are out of this world!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best breakfast in all ifNashville. Omelets are awesome. Biscuits fluffy and hot served with fresh made jams and jellies. Atmosphere is laid back. Love the specialty shops.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
This is probably one of my all time favorite places to spend New Year's Eve. I have been visiting my family in Nashville for the holidays for the past four years. This year we spent the evening at the CW. Our venue waitress, Kim, was extremely knowledgeable about the menu, wines and enhanced our experience. 
Marc Broussard was the perfect entertainment for the evening. We shall return!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
One of the best breakfasts I have had! Would definitely come back here!
Service and food excellent!

What we ordered:
-the country ham- their specialty - my friend thought it was alright and the ham was a little on the dry side
-Waffle- great flavor and crunch 
-biscuits- free for the table.  I loved the strawberry and blueberry jam.  I really wanted to love the peach jam, but wasn't impressed. 
-Chicken biscuit sammie- really good
-Granola- homemade they thought it was osme of the best granola they've ever had
- I got a side of gravy to try their gravy.  It's almost as good as mom makes! large pieces of sausage and great flavor. 

Although I was super full, I really wanted to try the Key Lime Pie, but sadly, they had sold out.  So if you go maybe you should try it and tell me what I missed out on :(

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Everything about this restaurant was amazing, what an experience coming to this place was! I went to Nashville for the weekend and of course looked on yelp and trip advisor on the best places to eat (The Must Eats) and well this place showed up on both so me being me and wanting some great food I took an Uber (about 15$ from downtown Nashville) and came to check this spot out. Let me star off by saying this restaurant is not only a restaurant it's the cutest motel with a restaurant and a couple gift shops. It's such a cute campsite area filled with such nice and happy people. The food at loveless cafe is everything ones taste buds can dream of. The biscuits are life changing!! I can almost guarantee they will be the best biscuits you will ever eat in your life, that's how amazing they truly are. It's hard to even save room for your actual meal because they're so addicting you cannot stop eating them and loveless cafe pairs them with four different jelly's so you have to try a biscuit with each jelly so you can determine which one you like the most lol. I could go on and on about how wonderful this place is and how delightful the food was but it's just an experience you need to try yourself.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I had the pleasure of being the celebratory guest of honor at Bavarian Bierhaus and all I can say is what a wonderful experience it was for myself and all 50ish guests that came along. My parents through me a graduation bash and the space and efficiency was unmatched. Despite all the hustle and bustle of the party, the servers in charge of us were more than capable of handling the many orders and requests that came through. From one order to the next on a blank check, every one of my guests was well satisfied with drink and food and no one's order was wrong. I applaud the staff or Bavarian Bierhaus for tending to both mine and my party's needs with efficiency and promptness. No one amongst us was disappointed in the experience despite so many of us and it was overall an enjoyable and pleasant time. Although there were many of us, everyone was treated as an individual guest and their requests met. If you're looking for an open space with exceptional service and fare, Bavarian Bierhaus has got you covered.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: First of all, this is the cutest little place! They have a little market store and novelty barn and hotel. But I came for the cafe! Cindy our waitress was so kind and wonderful! She was quick and had GREAT suggestions! I had her personal favorite: fried pork chops, they were mouthwatering! Not greasy, perfectly cooked! Grits were savory and butter filled, fried chicken was so juicy! The real star was the hash brown casserole! Cheesy goodness right there that makes your soul sing! The complimentary biscuits were warm and fluffy and their homemade butter and preserves were a perfect balance of fruit and sweetness! This will be going down on the must haves list when I travel to Nashville again!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Free coffee is why they're getting two stars!

There is no way this place is worth the hour plus wait we were told when we arrived. Being on a time crunch we opted for take away and decided to eat outside. Our biscuits weren't really cooked. What the hell? The French toast was fine and happily my egg omelette was fully cooked. This is not a must visit and even if I lived in the area I don't think I'd go back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Ok, so the biscuits get five stars! But the food only three. Loveless Cafe is a tradition in the Nashville area, having served their famous biscuits for over 40 years. 

We had to try it and they were some of the best biscuits I've ever had. The main course was good, but not out of the ordinary. My fried okra I make at home is better and I believe the mashed potatoes are instant. 

Still a good meal, but I would maybe go back for breakfast instead to try the biscuits and gravy.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: 4/4 people in my party don't know what the hype was. The biscuits were OK.  Mac and cheese was alittle worse than velvetta mac and cheese.  The fried chicken was dry.  The creamed corn was equal to Jolly Green Giant creamed corn.  And to wait a hour and 45?!?  NO.  We all said that Cracker Barrel would have been better.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
My wife and I went on a Friday night. Half the tables were empty but they seated us with a group of strangers. We moved ourselves ONE table to behind the strangers. For over 10 minutes the wait staff and other employees ignored us.

We left.

We drove to the mall from out of town just for this restaurant.

I don't know if we will return.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
They have lost their edge...no longer special, alright but nothing to write home about.

They have a system to maximize profit and that rather than charm and service trump customer happiness.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Well, would have loved to try this restaurant but, despite talking to a staff member and being assured that we could eat at the bar and not need a reservation, we arrived at 1730 and was told no seating was available and the restaurant was closing in 25 minutes.  What????

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Along with Mission BBQ, this is arguably the highlight of the mall and I would definitely like to explore the menu some more.

The gift shop has some genuinely charming (though often overpriced) things in it. I found a stuffed a dachshund for only 12 bucks. The beer hall style is nice, as is the bar up front, where we ate.

The pretzel, which you can get for free if you stop at the kiosk outside, is fine for what it is - it's not terrific, but it's hard to really mess up a pretzel. The Bavarian Onion Soup was very good, with pretzel bits in it to differentiate it from standard French Onion.

We ordered the King Ludwig Platter to try to get a sampling of everything. The meats were all very good, with the Rouladen probably being the best part and the Knackwurst being the most forgettable of the meats. Meanwhile, while the gravy was excellent, the actual potatoes were kind of grainy (almost like instant).

Our server was very kind and attentive. I'd be curious to see this place once it gets more crowded. As is, I definitely enjoyed myself.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Five stars for the beers and three stars for the food! We came to try this place after missing Bavarian style beer after our trip to Germany last summer. The beers were absolutely on point! If only the food would live up to how good the beers were. I had the traditional schnitzel with fries and was really disappointed. Everything was almost cold when it was brought to our table and really lacked flavor. So I had to knock down a star. When we went there was also a live band playing! It really made the whole place feel authentic like any bierhaus you can find in Germany or Bavaria.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Came here for the first time and really enjoyed it. We ordered off the breakfast menu, but the dinner menu looked great as well. They also have some family style options for both. Biscuits were great, as was everything we ordered. Look for the cupcake of the month.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We were hear last winter and loved this place. Came back this summer and nothing has changed. Biscuits were marvelous! Service was great and prices were very fair. I love this place even if it is packed with tourists every day. Worth the wait any time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Reminds me of my Grandma's cooking.
The fried liver and gizzards were perfectly cooked, the biscuits were irresistible, and deserts were amazing. We also love the staff who sang happy Birthday to my wife.
Hope to come back soon.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Everything was rushed! 
I arrived and waited in the valet line, and from that moment on everyone was in a hurry. 

I got to the table quick service to see what I wanted, so I started with a menu.  Half price wine and appetizers. 
Everyone was getting their apps when I arrived. Three different wait staffers took my drink order. It was a bit confusing lol but they worked it out.

I got the mushroom and goat cheese balls. They were delicious. 
Prosecco was also quite tasty. 
I tried the hot crab dip.. not the best. 
Everyone at the table raved about the pizza! 

I would go back to check it out again. 

Beautiful decor!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
The atmosphere alone is worth the visit. Even the staff are dressed to the German nines. Not nein, nines. Lederhosen clad servers and live polka music make you feel like you're in an authentic German bierhall. 

The German sausages are all sourced from my hometown of Milwaukee from a sausage maker that's been around since 1880! Usingers is synonymous with top quality. If you've never had a bratwurst that snapped when you bit into it, then you've never had a good brat. The menu has some seriously authentic dishes. I may be here every week. 

Make sure to wash it all down with a liter or das boot of the finest German beer before leaving to do some shopping at the mall while you sober up. 

Auf Wiedersehen!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
A friend posted photos of biscuits and jam months ago - and I was like HOLD UP.... TELL ME WHERE THESE ARE.

So when we ended up adding Nashville as a stop on our family vacation, this got added to the list of places to eat.

Glad we did. Biscuits were yummy. Food was all tasty. Such a cute little spot with shops on the property, etc.

We left happy, and I bought a trio of the jams to take home with us.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is such a cool place right in the middle of the hotel and mall. The restaurant is huge and there's an area when you walk in to buy all the German goodies your heart desires. We went a little crazy with the candies and imports that we had to think about how much space we had in our suitcase. There was no wait at all because we arrived during lunch. Our waiter was super friendly (and was actually German). He spoke with my boyfriend for a little which was cute. My boyfriend ordered the big meat plate and said it was quite authentic. He also said he was super full and satisfied. Being that I don't eat dairy, it was a little difficult for me to order but I ended up getting the chicken schnitzel anyways and asked for the sauce on the side. It was heavy but delicious. You're able to sub out whatever side you want so I got the red cabbage which was also really good. I'd definitely recommend stopping g by if you're visiting. I'm glad my friend recommended this place. I'd love to come back for dinner next time I'm in town.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: They have a really nice selection of drafts. It was almost a little overwhelming but the bartender made great selections. While I was looking over the menu a host stopped by, I think her name was Rebeccah, and recommended the chicken fried steak. It was outstanding!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Get a picture with the classic sign at Loveless. A Nashville staple. Order the jam as gifts for Christmas and take tourists here for breakfast on Saturday. The atmosphere is cozy and the biscuits are to die for. If you need a pie to take to a special occasion, this is where to get it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: So I've been here 4 times, all said 45 - 55 minute wait...there is not that many small cafes that I would wait for, for that long...but the 4th time I decided to wait for 40 minutes....walked around the area and shopped at the other stores...very cool stuff...then we were seated...people talk about their biscuits...they ain't lyin!! Please all the food was delicious...so earth the wait, now i know how far Elvis felt after he ate there!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food was amazing. I came for lunch on Saturday and breakfast on Sunday! The portions are HUGE! You will definitely take a meal home. The pancakes were buttery and fluffy. The omelet was cheesy and light. The hash brown casserole, oh my goodness talk about tasty! Overall I think this place is awesome and inexpensive. I love the atmosphere and the wait staff is super fast, efficient, and polite. Can't wait to come back!

name: Big Shotz
text: EVERYTIME I come here it's a good time. Bartenders are always friendly. By far the best bar in Nashville. Drinks are dreamy

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Ahh, yet another place in Nashville "renowned" for their biscuits that didn't deliver. Maybe it's my version of biscuits that they don't deliver on. They make 10k a day, and maybe that shows. While tasty, they remind me of the kind you bake yourself in the little metal tin. However, their preserves, country ham, hash brown casserole, & and country fried steak were very tasty! Very touristy and kinda cool. Worth the trip!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Restaurant is great. Big and spacious! The kids meal was cheap and giant portion and the giant pretzel  with cheese was the best appetizer. Our waitress Morgan was very nice and accommodating. We were with 6 kids and she was very patient and came back to check on us often. The pork shank was huge and crispy. Only thing I didn't like was the crispy noodles because it wasn't so crispy and my daughter didn't like the Mac and cheese but everything else was delicious. The French onion soup was really cheesy. The giant beers were super cold! Would definitely go back!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Lived up to the Hype. I have lived outside of Nashville my entire life and the first time I went here was the past Sunday. The grounds have nice little shops to browse while you wait, places to hang out in the shade so you really don't feel like your waiting. The food was delicious, the biscuits reminded me of my grandmothers. Quaint ambiance. Good food and friendly service made a great afternoon with friends.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place was awesome!! Every server that came by rocked!! Virginia, thank you for the stories you shared with Tammy and myself Friday afternoon. We will be back!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great place and service was outstanding. Kristen was awesome and made our visit very enjoyable- had family style supper and did not disappoint! Not a fan of the Barbeque as it was a little dry but everything was wonderful

name: Mercy Lounge
text: The Mercy Lounge was an awesome venue! We went last night to watch The Boxer Rebellion and were blown away. It was comfortable and had a great drink selection with solid prices. Our only negative was the lack of food served either at the lounge or nearby otherwise we loved it and can't recommend It highly enough!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: What an amazing venue.  Intimate feel, great acoustics, full bar.  Great place to see a concert.  It doesn't hurt I was seeing Stephen Kellogg for the eighth time.  By far the best venue yet.  Just a perfect evening.  I will be looking for more of my favorites to play here.

name: Drifters
text:
I've got to be honest- I'm not a fan.

The food seems very plain and bland to me. Maybe it's all the years of surviving on hot chicken, chicago dogs, and everything doused in jalepenos and hot sauce. I know I'm at least a little biased because growing up, everything my 'rents cooked tasted like cardboard and they had never heard of spice. I could probably live off of condiments.

When I last went, the service in an empty house was sub-par. I was told someone was going to get my refill and then waited a very long time (10-15 minutes) before that ever happened. With a mild esophogeal condition, I can't guarantee dry food will make it down the throat completely without some liquid to wash it down, so I literally have to pause eating if I wait on a refill. I'm normally quite understanding, but felt that a 10 minute wait in an empty house was a little excessive.

Call me a typical American, but I like my food to have flavor.

name: Drifters
text:
I highly recommend the BBQ nachos! This is one of my favorite places to grab a beer. The staff is so friendly, and they have great deals on beer! During the day the place is slower. Make sure to sit at the bar and make a friend. 

Signed,
A Regular

name: Drifters
text:
Went on Sunday to listening to a band. It was a beautiful day to sit outside under one of their umbrellas or canopies. 
They are dog friendly and unfortunately smoker friendly outside. Fortunately, the breeze kept the smoke down. 
A big storm blew in and our waitress informed us in time for our large group to get a table inside.
We got served inside. We didn't care for the smoked wings. The dry rub ribs were tasty.  The fries were nice and crispy and good. The hush puppies were very good. One person on our group got a salad. It was huge and a great variety of veggies, not just head lettuce.  The two for one beer specials were an unexpected treat. Good variety to chose from. 
Super area of Nashville. Easy pay as you go parking lot. $5 for 2 hours. Lots of little shops to explore in the area. 
A bit of a dive bar but great vibe and fun atmosphere. Service was good and pleasant.

name: Commodore Grille
text:
This place is hit & miss! Breakfast can be a challenge, staff is nice the food is good when the want it to be. Had the meat lovers omelette had no bacon even though its was advertised with it. Very little meat, when I showed them the comment was I should've ask for extra meat, thought the name said it all, guess not.
Also it wasn't a true omelette it was folded over unscrambled eggs. Had the country skillet the next morning ask for no peppers of course it came loaded with them. Morons!!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Saw first film in the newly remodeled building today.  The movie wasn't my total cup of tea, but that happens.  What a great new space they have created; will definitely be back for many films!  The inside ticket sales area, however, seemed a bit cramped.  It's located just inside the building from the new main entrance.  On the other hand, the concession area, which I didn't partake of, was large and a vast improvement over the old one.  All in all, a big win for Nashville!

name: Drifters
text: Our first taste of Nashville was a score! Cool grungy atmosphere with unexpected awesome BBQ.

name: The Country
text: Very cool atmosphere, had a writers night when I was there and all were very good. Nice big patio! Try the grilled cheese!!

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Don't ever go here.  Their bouncers have a Napoleon complex and will kick you out for going to the bathroom.  You can be a VIP and get kicked out for no reason.   Take it from a local.  Never go here.

name: The Family Wash
text:
A couple of weeks ago I decided to check out an East Nashville favorite for the first time:  The Family Wash.  I had driven by it several times, heard several great things about it, but for some reason had never made my way in.  Ridiculous, I know.  After a last minute decision to grab a bite, coupled with the fact that there was no wait for seating (I was starving), proved to be a great decision.  First of all, we had an awesome server (Stephanie--if she's there, ask for her, she was fab); Second, an impressive beer selection immediately caught my attention.  I asked our server for her food recommendation since I was a first timer, and she suggested the Shepherds Pie: A GREAT choice, it was delicious.  We also opted the spinach and artichoke dip as an app, which was quite tasty as well.  Rumor on the street is that their mac and cheese is pretty much to die for, but we didn't opt to add more calories this time around. Next time.

So, as I mentioned, the beer selection was impressive.  Several local brews on tap, along with seasonal selections from around the US.  I opted for the Jackelope Red Ale, and it did not disappoint.  In fact, it was really, really good.  If you've not tried Jackelope yet, do yourself a favor and make a visit to their taproom... I have yet to have any of their beers fail me.

After the first beer was served and food was on the table, the night continued to get even better with the addition of live music.  We are so lucky to have such talent in Nashville playing at joints like the Family Wash, and, they have live music every single night they are open.  Pretty awesome.

Don't wait as long as I did to check this place out--you'll be glad you paid them a visit!

A couple of items to note:

Tuesday is Pint & Pie night: A draft beer and Shepherd's Pie for $10 (Normally the pie itself is $11)

Thursday is $3.75 Draft Night 

They are closed Sunday and Monday

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
I dropped by here last week to see my first concert since moving to Nashville. As I had come to see the band, and hadn't heard anything about the venue, I came in fresh with no preconceptions. What I found was one of the best small concert venues I've had the pleasure to experience in my three decades on this planet.

The stage is perfectly set -- accessible to a GA crowd with excellent site lines. The sound system was great, though the drums/bass can easily overpower the higher register instruments and vocals in space like this if not balanced correctly. Decor was appropriate for the crowd, drinks were reasonably priced.

name: Springwater
text: Claiming to be the oldest bar in Tennessee, Springwater is a place you have likely driven by many times, but unless you turn on the road between McDonald's and Centennial Park, you'd never know it was there. The place definitely has an unpleasant odor upon entering and teeny tiny bathrooms, but overall it was a good place to listen to some great live music. Everyone I encountered who works there were very friendly, and there are plenty of seating options amongst a covered patio, a room with the stage for bands and a third room with pool tables. It is the true definition of a dive bar, so if that's what you want, you'll love it. I will most definitely return in the future.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Went here for on Saturday night with a group of 8. The waitress was attentive when we first arrived, and then ignored us for the next 30 minutes. We then resorted to ordering from the bar, which I imagine she did not like, because she then ignored us completely until it was time to pay the bill. We also got pizza and it sucked.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Poor service. Food was basic bar food. No problem with that. Waitress was slow and got our order wrong. Paid with card and left cash tip. Total was 8.70 but when looking at my bank statement I was charged 10.70. Not a big deal financially but I won't be back.

name: EXIT/IN
text: I had my 3rd horrible experience at Exit in last night and I'm never going back. My boyfriend and I both brought 20 bucks cash to see his best friends band play. We brought 5 dollars for the cover and enough to get 2 beers each. We basically wanted to have low key night and not spend much. We were having a great time and walked up to the bar to get our second round of beers. He ordered a miller light and the bartender opened the beer and put it in front him so he started to pull out the money to pay. At that point the bartender said, "it's a 10 dollar minimum". My boyfriend politely said, "no thanks then, I'm good." Then it got ugly quick. The bartender proceeded to tell him that he had to buy the beer and reach the 10 dollar minimum or he would be kicked out immediately. He refused to buy the beer and then we were surrounded by three bouncers to "enforce" kicking us out of the bar. I asked the bartender why he couldn't just ice the beer for a few minutes and sell it to someone else and he said, "No one drinks Miller Light"?!? The whole thing was ridiculous and poorly managed. If I was the owner I would fire everyone on staff and start over. There are too many other great venues in town to put up with this type of treatment as a paying customer. The entitlement and rudeness of the staff seems to be encouraged. I remember going to Exit In back in the day and liking the staff, maybe there is new management? Either way, I will not be back.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: The Belcourt is one of my favorite things about Nashville, and I'm not just saying that because I'm a former employee (I only left because I moved to California). The Belcourt has introduced me to movies I'd probably never have seen otherwise. Most very thought-provoking and so good but without a mainstream following or release. You're more than likely not going to see crap, though you may see something strange. I also love that they do midnight movies. Going to see The Room at midnight, throwing plastic spoons around, and screaming at the screen once a year really gets your stress out. I love the remodeling. At first I was very wary of the remodel, mostly because of the nostalgia from when I was an employee and fear the theatre losing its character. Since a visit to check it out and a midnight screening of the aforementioned The Room, my mind has been put at ease. The '22 Hall looks almost untouched, though I believe it got new seats and other necessities. I think the '66 Hall has a few less seats, but not by many. Looks pretty much the same as well. The Belcourt will always have a special place in my heart.

name: Commodore Grille
text: Came down for a quick bite and a few drinks around dinner time. Food was OK, drinks surprisingly expensive. $10 for a not very generous Malibu and pineapple juice. Manager, Todd, wasn't friendly at all. Do yourself a favor and walk a block for food/drinks.

name: Drifters
text: We ordered the hush puppies as an appetizer which were basically flavorless. I ordered the chicken wings which are pretty big, so I'll give them that but the meat was over cooked as it was super chewy, fatty, and pretty flavorless as well. The skin was rubbery and over charred. My boyfriend had the ribs, which were also dry and flavorless. Definitely not that "fall off the bone" kind of experience you look for in BBQ. I guess their sauce selection was pretty good. They only "allow" 2 students in the bar at a time which is what you make of it. Just a very disappointing experience especially for the price. Would not return or recommend to friends. Maybe enemies.

name: The Family Wash
text: The food was just okay, the food is way overpriced. Music was pretty cool, but the experience was not worth the money. I've been to several other restaurants/bars in Nashville that are half the price and have a DOOR NOT MADE OUT OF PARTICLE BOARD. The building is a complete dump, food is not anything special, so why is it $15 for mac and cheese?

name: Drifters
text: I didn't take a picture of the food because I just dove in!  Everything was delicious.  There was also great live music performances.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
The Belcourt sets the standard for cinema. No 3D blockbusters, but the collection of films that they rotate can not be found any where else.

The theater itself is comfortable with good sound. 

You can buy a beer with the movie, which is awesome. They even have local drafts.

Just go.... Go..... Go...... Go..... And watch movies you never heard of tell a story you never heard. It's good the soul and good for the community.

name: Drifters
text: The ribs!!! Got some just out of the smoker..they were amazing. The smoked pork is perfection. Try the Georgia sauce!

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: This was the worst concert experience I have ever had.  I bought tickets for my brother for his birthday as we are big Chris Stapleton fans.  My brother's girlfriend forgot her ID and the person checking at the door could not have been more rude or disrespectful.  We has various other forms of ID, offered to be X'd and no one in the group drink, we made it clear we had driven several hours to get here for the show.  We could show a photo ID picture through the phone and then had at least 4 other forms of ID to compare it to including a social security card and health insurance card.  I understand rules are rules, but the man working at the door was rude, disrespectful and flat our inappropriate to be a "professional" your organization has employed. I love music and attend several concerts every year and have never had such a horrible experience. If we had to have been denied entry there was a way to go about it with more class and appreciation for your customers. I have attended several events at your venue and will not do so again.  I was stunned that the elderly women in front of me, who clearly had a disability, and did not have an ID as she is unable to drive, was also denied entry.  You should be ashamed of yourself as a business and as a venue.

name: Drifters
text: This place was cool. We were visiting Nashville and heard a band playing on a warm afternoon so we stopped by to see what was going on. We had already eaten, and weren't driven by an alcohol frenzy, so we stopped in for lemonade and an iced tea to watch the band. The waiter was totally cool about it, we didn't feel pressured to order more and it was a nice time. I wish we had been hungry enough to try the food. Seems to be a biker hangout, but at the same time not really. who knows, I enjoyed it....

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
I came here for lunch on a Wednesday with my boyfriend and ordered eggs Benedict with steak, and wow! The steak was phenomenal, cooked perfectly! I loved every bite, and I am super picky about my steak. So kudos to the chef!! I also had the gator bites and they were so delicious! My boyfriend ordered the shrimp platter and he enjoyed it. Another time that we came, he had a burger and loved it too. Overall, the food here is very good, highly recommend having food here if you come for a game, enjoy their food with your drinks, you won't be disappointed.


Update: 12/31/17

I've come here a couple times, but the most recent time I came was in New Year's Eve. I've got to say, I am so glad I did! They had a huge party here, and my boyfriend and I were able to stay somewhere warm and ring in the new year at a fun atmosphere. (We we're planning to walk around downtown before learning about their NYE party)

We even invited a few people to come join us and we had a blast here.

name: Drifters
text: Went there for lunch - it wasn't busy but the food was good - they even make their own BBQ sauces - the fries were good and hot.  Adam was our server and really went above and beyond on service.  Additionally, met the owner - who was a really nice guy and shared a lot about the city.  I would definately go back to check out some of the live music.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: I am a member of the Belcourt Theatre.  I am so glad to be part of this non-profit organization.  The films shown here are wonderful.  I recently saw I,Tonya and was blown away.  Keep up the good work!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
If you're into strange artsy movies, this is the place for you! I'm not and I didn't like the movie or the price. 

This is the place for the non-mainstream movie goers--keep that in mind.

name: Drifters
text:
Behold, the BBQ Brisket Nachos.  So amazingly delicious, you won't be able to stop picking when the plate is almost empty.  Layers and layers of perfectly layered corn tortilla chips with melted cheddar, BBQ sauce and BRISKET.  Must have.

Also had some spicy fried pickles, ribs, and wings that were tasty.. but I'd come just for the nachos.  Service was great and they have awesome happy hour specials!

They also have self service for their sauces.  Of course, I had to try them all.

name: Drifters
text:
I was quite happy when we stumbled upon Drifters. Coming from Houston, TX, our bbq standards are set very high, but we happened to stop in Nashville on the way to Lexington. Coming in around 10:30pm at night, the quality food selections were limited for a late night dinner, but Drifters definitely did the trick.

Drifters wasn't crowded at the time because we came in so late, but it definitely had that local, cool vibe of getting crowded whenever they have live music or an event going on. It's a no frills, nothing fancy kind of place, but that's what makes the place feel so homey. There is plenty of indoor and outdoor seating available, and they even have a stage where live music would play, plus a full bar.


As far as food goes, we tried 2 of their 2 meat plates, and their famous bbq nachos. The bbq nachos are huge and plenty to share! They are piled high with bbq brisket, cheese, pico de gallo, avocado, jalapenos, and a dollop of sour cream in the middle. For the 2 meat plates we tried their pulled pork and sausage on 1 plate, and brisket and pork ribs on the other plate. For sides it came with coleslaw, bbq baked beans, and French fries. Out of the 4 different meats, the pork ribs were by far the best! They came out super tender, well seasoned, and smokey. The sausage and brisket, compared to Houston bbq, was just ok, but we were starving. And the pulled pork was really good as well, it came out juicier than I was expecting. Don't sleep on the sides either! The bbq beans were some of my favorite that I've had in awhile, and I don't normally like beans. If you're in Nashville, come check out Drifters! Solid bbq, cool atmosphere, and live music on Wednesdays.

Oh and I almost forgot, try ALL 5 of their homemade bbq sauces. They are each unique, and go perfectly with their bbq. Half of the fun of eating here was trying the different foods with each of the sauces. My personal favorite was the "New Mexico" sauce.

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
I wish I could give 0 stars. I came with a bachelorette party 14 of us.. a few of us came earlier because we knew we would probably have to wait. We were the first ones in the restaurant. The servers were super friendly and they were quick to serve our mimosas. They took our orders at 11 AM. We were not served food until 1:30PM... well, half of our table got food.. one girl found a hair in her burger, and for two girls they "forgot to put their orders in" and a few we were still waiting on. We called the owner over multiple times, not once did he apologize for the wait or other issues. Once we noticed another table complaining to the owner, we called him over. One girl from our party said this was horrible service, and the owner simply responds, "YOU'RE A HORRIBLE PERSON" and walked away. 

...the servers deserve better than to work for an establishment like Frisky Frogs.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
We love this theater so much.  It's such a treat to be able to come and view all sorts of cool independent movies in such a lovely little theater.  They have all sorts of mini-film festivals and great midnight movies over the weekend, yet hubby and I have yet to attend a special screening event.  We're not Belcourt members but we're thinking of becoming ones.  Since we now have Movie Pass, we have been spending more time here  and I would really love to make it out to one of the special features.

They'll validate your parking if you're fortunate enough to snag a spot in the very small parking lot, but I'd warn to expect to have to park in one of the nearby lots.  The Belcourt seems to get crazy busy during the evening weekend shows so try to head in a little early. Come and enjoy some of the beer and wine that they have on tap!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
Went on a whim with my boyfriend while we were vacationing. We wanted a little break from going out, and came across this while looking for things to do. We were staying at the hostel downtown, and it was only about a 15 minute drive. Very neat theater and left so envious that Milwaukee doesn't have one like it. Glad we chose it over the other standard movie theaters. We saw The Source Family and returned home telling our friends all about it. I would, without question, get a membership if I lived in town. 

The only downside- a girl working at the concession stand. She was visibly impatient as we took a FEW SECONDS to decide what we wanted. We really enjoyed the movie and forgot about her as soon as it started, but we did think back to it later a little annoyed. One of those -I wish I would have said something- moments. The man at the ticket booth was very nice though (: So to the concession women- sorry to inconvenience you at your job.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
The sound is one of the worst I have heard. The stage is in the corner of room and the view is of poles!  

I'll never go there again. Even if it is one of my favorite bands.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: I would give zero stars if I could. All around horrible in everything. The waitress we had was slammed so not blaming her but management needs to really get a grasp on how to run a restaurant particularly on a Sunday game day. Was absolute chaos at this place and poorly ran operations. Food was cold and drinks were terrible. We had to find our own table and carry it to a spot with chairs. We got there to watch the Titans/Pats game and left after first quarter.  Also the men's bathroom was complete disaster. This place needs a complete overhaul or shut down.  Amazes me how a place like this stays in business. Avoid this place altogether!  This bar needs Jon Taffer (show on tv-Bar Rescue) for some serious help!

name: EXIT/IN
text: Saw a great band here.  The drink selections were really good they have the usual hipster PBR tallboys but when I went they had Sierra Nevada IPAs and Barleywines and the like as well.  Really nice venue I would be happy to come back here again to see another band.  Good stuff!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: What an absolutely lovely place! Just make sure you purchase your tickets as soon as possible, get a parking pass and bring it quickly to your car outside, and I mean QUICKLY, because within minutes, cops (lurking somewhere in the dark) will come out and write you a ticket. It happened to us. Belcourt was so nice that they took the ticket and told us "not to worry about it".

name: Drifters
text: Had the sliders the other night.  Pretty good.  I've been in before but didn't eat, however the smell was so captivating I had to go back and try some.  Great place that not everyone knows about, so you can typically find space.

name: Commodore Grille
text:
I went to hear a Facebook friend (and others) sing. Everyone was very talented and/or funny. I ordered the Commodore Grille Steak that came with mashed potatoes. Both were delicious. When the waitress came to take my plate, I slapped her hand (or at least pretended to)... as I was hoping for some bread to sop up the gravy -- ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS!

I am going back in a couple of days and will order the same. Just hope I get the same waitress!

The very chocolaty dessert was mighty fine, too!

I got a glimpse of a potential buffet around a corner - wonder how that thing is....


Update: I have been back twice to see the same and MORE friends perform -- and order the Commodore Grille Steak every time! Always mighty, might fine! And servers are always sweet and friendly and helpful.

Updated 01/10/14: Had just headed some soup at home as I planned to stay in and get some work done. Around 5:00, my sister called from Nashville and told me my singer/songwriter friends (and another new friend) were performing at the Commodore again... so I ate my soup and jumped in the car. About two hours later, I only ordered a drink and warned the waitress I'd be ordering a "CGS" to go eventually. A few minutes later, she brought out a chicken quesadilla for someone else at our table - I was suddenly hungry and just had to order one; not the frontrunner on my search for "the world's best chicken quesadilla" but sitll, mighty good. Of course, I now have CGS waiting for me in the fridge for lunch tomorrow! 

Good food + good friends + good service = a mighty great time (well worth the four-hour drive!)

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
Visited here on Friday night around 7pm.  We did not eat so I can not give it 5 Stars.  

Adam was our bartender and he was very friendly and knowledgeable and attentive.   The beer was cold and live band played a good mix of new and old country as well as good Southern rock songs.  

If you want a good place to go to get off of Broadway, this is definitely a good place to go!

name: Frisky Frog's
text: We came for brunch on a Saturday and ordered bottomless mimosas and they kept them coming. Chicken and French toast was amazing.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
I appreciate everything about this lovely art-house theater in downtown Nashville. It's got a great selection of films, helpful staff, and posh seats. The bathrooms are pretty darn nice, too! In those, the shelf above the sink is perfect for putting down your purse or bag while you get your hands clean. I wish every bathroom included this feature!

My family and I came out to see the Korean film
Parasite at the end of Thanksgiving weekend, and it was an excellent way to wrap up our visit. We had no trouble with parking in the Belcourt lot, and we arrived early enough to walk around the theater and see some of the artwork on sale, benefiting homeless artists and a non-profit organization Poverty and the Arts. Thanks, Belcourt Theatre!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Excellent venue.   Love this place.  Best venue I've been to. Drinks were good and best of all seeing my Nashville favorites, The Dead Deads

name: Drifters
text: Oh my goodness. Best little hole in the wall place I've ever been! Pickles jalapeños, hush puppies, the brisket and the pulled pork. Couldn't have had a better meal! The sweet heat and jalapeño ranch sauces you MUST try! Great little place and I highly recommend

name: EXIT/IN
text: Great variety of sushi that's always fresh and reasonably priced. It's a small place so get there a bit early and expect a bit of a wait. Cozy atmosphere and friendly staff. Loved the ninza roll.

name: Springwater
text:
One of my favorite dives in Nashville. Don't expect anything fancy, but it's a great place to grab a Shiner and people watch or interact with some local flavor. If you get hungry, head through the back door and find Buford, he'll hook you up with a solid burger and tots on a paper plate. It'll hit the spot.
Springwater isn't for everyone, but if you want a slightly gritty, authentic Nashville experience, you will love it. You won't find many bachelorette parties or groups of tourists here.
As the oldest bar in Tennessee, this place is iconic. Taylor Swift did a Coke commercial on their stage and the Black Keys filmed a music video here. 
I would say this is one of the top 10 dive bars in America.

name: The Station Inn
text: I LOVE this place! Great atmosphere! Great Western Swing band!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Came back for another Monday night show with The Time Jumpers. Great sound. Again. That's a huge plus. 
The food was good and priced well. Apps came fast and were pretty tasty. Entrees were well presented and good. No looming pressure from our server which was appreciated. 
Overall, another perfectly enjoyable evening. Someone else said it was bar food. True. But they crank it out and it is fairly priced and we have all paid a lot more for much less

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
I LOVED the new amphitheater! We went to see Needtobreathe with Colony House, Drew Holcomb and the Neighbors, and Switchfoot. We had tickets in the pit (which was standing only), and the view behind the stage was just an incredible backdrop for these awesome bands. 

The Hattie B's hot chicken truck is really cool to have onsite, and I appreciated the availability of beer and drinks all over the facility without having to stand in line. Also, there were several bins for recycling which makes me very happy to see!

The seats in the middle of the theater were padded and awesome! After 4 hours of standing, I was really wishing for a place to sit down. The lawn was awesome too, though! Spacious and nicely elevated for a great view of the stage. 

My "feedback" is this: On the website, the General Admission Pit, listed as PITGA on the tickets, is listed as "orchestra". That was confusing, leading us to be unsure if we were on the lawn, or where exactly we'd be. There is also no information as to if the pit will have seats or no seats for the concerts. Several photos I found on Instagram led me to believe we'd have seats (if that was where our tickets would be) but for this concert, there was no seats. I ended up with a bulky bag holding a blanket that I had to carry around all evening because of the lack of information on the site.I'd appreciate a few more details to help people be better prepared!

I cant' wait to go back to more concerts here; yay Nashville for finally having an amazing outdoor venue that can accomodate large shows.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Nothing special here unfortunately.  was staying in downtown Nashville and couldn't decide what to eat.  place had OK / decent reviews so I decided to give it a whirl.  good location, live music.  it goes downhill from there.  beer in plastic cups and it tasted stale (Yuengling).  the Spicy Chicken Mac & Cheese was sub par.  I'd say one step above Kraft Mac & Cheese from a box.  sorry. just didn't do it for me.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
This venue is awesome and a great addition to downtown Nashville!!!  So happy to have attended the inaugural show with Eric Church.

Great layout, spacious, plenty of restrooms and food/drink options, and just a nice chill place.

Yes drinks are outrageously priced but otherwise it's fantastic.

name: The Station Inn
text: A lot of people moving to Nashville are moving here because of country music and what it brings to the city. I am not one of those people. I don't listen to live music often. When I do, it's more often than not at the symphony hall or the opera (no I'm not 90, some 20/30-somethings like classical music, too!). So it means a lot when I say that listening to the Sunday Night Bluegrass Jam was one of the most wonderful and memorable experiences I've had in Nashville since moving here a year and a half ago. The music was great. Classic and interesting and moving. And the venue was amazing. It seems like it's the last original building in all of the Gulch! Skyscraper, skyscraper, skyscraper, The Station Inn. It's a Nashville legend. And it's still a great time. I highly recommend attending one of their Sunday Night Bluegrass Jams. It's a unique experience in this city. (Go early! We had to wait until people left before we could sit!)

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Usually I tend to avoid bars that are described as touristy, however, I had a great time.

My favorite part was an awesome band they had playing. Their lead singer was a woman named Autumn Reynolds. She had such an amazing voice!! She could sing any country song well, if not better than the original singer. By the end of the night, major girl crush was developed. 

The only reason why this receives 4 stars instead of 5 was that it was slow to get drinks, but that's somewhat expected for a touristy bar in Nashville. The bartenders were very hardworking and made great drinks, but it would be worth it to add another bartender during busy times.

name: Famous Nashville
text:
I love the decor and atmosphere here!  It's right on the river and there are a number of good spots to get comfortable and enjoy the live music or the beautiful view or the amazing local artwork.

I definitely didn't give it 4 stars for the service or food.  We sat at a table upstairs on the rooftop and we were ignored by 3 servers.  It wasn't even very busy.  So after a while (it seemed like 20 minutes) I went to the bar to try to get some service.  There were two other guys at the bar that got served before me and then I just sat there while the three girls just huddled up and seemed to be gossiping.  Eventually one  asked me what I wanted and I ordered two drinks and I tried to order the pretzels with beer cheese. She said they're not serving them now. We ended up skipping food and going somewhere else.

Having said that, it's still worth checking out.  You can relax at the awesome bar downstairs and enjoy live music or can relax in the swivel chairs in the next room and watch the band on tv or can enjoy the amazing view of Broadway, the stadium and the river.  It's a fantastic location that's right next to the Hard Rock Cafe.  The local artwork is also incredible.

Summary:

Design & Decor:          5
Location:                      5
Artwork & Ambiance:  5
Live Music:                   5
Service:                         1
Food:                             ?

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
If it's a weeknight and you are looking for a bit of a crazy crowd,  you might want to go elsewhere. 

It's huge. Which makes it look that much more empty. Of the 3 stories, only the bottom floor was open. It took the band *quite* awhile to go on. I don't know if they were waiting for someone or what, but the groupie with the crazy short shorts on kept us entertained. Beer selection here was slightly better than The Stage, and the waitress was attentive. 

Not my favorite, but the band was pretty good when they got going, and it was pretty nice to sit so close the stage without too many people crowding around.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Food is perfect every time we come! The staff is phenomenal. This is a weekly lunch stop for us and my wife and I make this place a stop when we get out on the weekends. Great food and cold beer!

name: Famous Nashville
text: Great downtown Bar and restaurant. Jessica and Lila were fabulous waitresses and the food was phenomenal. I really enjoyed the Nashville hot chicken and waffles, this is the real thing guys!  Great entertainment, food, music, venue. Truly enjoyed it!

name: The Back Corner
text:
This place is okay- a 3.5. We were there for 2.5hr, though, and felt like we were listening to the same song the entire time, despite pleas to the DJ to mix it up a little bit. I certainly wouldn't go there if you're looking to dance; to sit around and chat it might work. (You might as well just go to 5th & Taylor next door and grab a drink at their bar and enjoy it there or in their beautiful outdoor space if you are just looking to chat.)
Good crowd though- everyone seemed friendly, a nice mix of different types of people, etc. I appreciated that.
Also, there had been a vase of flowers at the front door which I guess we're knocked over- no one working there bothered to clean it up so entry/exit were very slippery on the wet tiles.
The drinks seemed fine, the service "ok", and the ambience pretty good. I say ok for the service because they showed up quickly upon arrival and stopped by regularly, but someone in my group asked them to talk to a manager and their response was "I don't have time for that."

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Very cool joint.  Paid a cover charge to see two great acts perform.  Scott Mulvahill and MountainHeart.  Good drinks, good service.  Safe. Would be glad to go back.

name: The Station Inn
text: If you want to experience old Nashville, not what Lower Broadway has become, come to the Station Inn. You will have a great time and be treated to world class musical talent.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
WOW!

Watching the Time Jumpers jam after a $13 prime rib meal is hard to beat.

This is an absolute must see on a Monday night in Nashville.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: The guy at the front door tonight is a complete jerk called my 50 year old partner "old as dirt" but he needed to see his id.  We brought a guy from. Australia clearly in his late 50's didn't bring his passport refused to let him in.  Then caused a ruckus almost escalating into a fight.  I don't understand what their goal is there but they lost 9 patrons tonight because the guy at the front door was an Uber aggressive jerk with a napoleon complex.  We were there at 1020pm.  Don't go hear if your older than 14 and not wearing a tight skirt.  Borderline age discrimination.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: Its Cheap Friendly and filled talented people. There no longer smoking in the bar. You will see some of the best songwriters in Nashville at Sam's Jams on Weds noon to and Lizards Writers Night on Thursday. Its right on Music Row, who know pop in for a cold one.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: A very nice venue, unlike the venues I grew up going to in Florida. First of all, the food was FANCY! I got a portobello mushroom burger with arugula and a jack and Coke! (Well, Pepsi.) the bathrooms were clean and there were a sufficient number of stalls. Staff was helpful and smiling. The seating was very well thought out, it didn't look like anywhere was a bad place to view the state from. The grass you sit on is soft, but they allow you to bring low-back chairs or a blanket. I want to come back soon to enjoy another show here.

name: The Station Inn
text: I was there last week and loved it. I'm from California, and didn't want the experience of flashy Broadway. I ordered pizza and beer and caught a blue grass jam session. The place filled up real fast. The staff is friendly! I will be back when I return to Nashville. Thanks, Marty!

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Courtney & Daniella are the best bartenders in Nashville! As a local you want to be treated well & you want your bar staff to understand you aren't a tourist! We have been treated so well all day! Both these bartenders are friendly, engaging & fun! 
I recommend this place to locals & tourists alike!

name: The Station Inn
text: Went on a monday night, incredible music and vibe!  Treat yourself and go back in time and visit the Station Inn for a true ole time Nashville experience. You won't regret it!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Went on Sunday brought some friends visiting from Michigan, was disappointed in not getting a table. There was six of us and we noticed two tables with one person obviously saving the table but drinking water? We left and took our money else where and had a great time. 

Here's hoping that someday Honky Tonk Central gets a policy on table saving.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Busy place on the weekends and at nights. Each floor had a different band playing which was nice. It's a fairly typical Broadway bar with multiple stories. A stop for lots and lots of bachelorette parties.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Who doesn't love live music and people watching?!?  The res of the experience?  Meh!  The bartenders were difficult to flag down (They tended to stand on one end of the bar chit-chatting quite often.) and the cocktails were not too tasty.  

As for the other bar patrons?  A few too many individuals who could not hold their liquor.  I do not appreciate have cocktails dropped on me because other people could not hold their beverages straight?  l

As for the bathroom?  Nasty!  I could not have gotten out of there soon enough.  

Would I go back here during my next Nashville visit?  I hope not.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: the band playing there today was so talented, and incredibly entertaining.  Brought many customers on their feet, and was able to keep the customers smiling and laughing with their wit.  Buffalo wings and beers- great.

name: Alley Taps
text:
Great music. Great People. Great Bartenders. 
Met Will tonight and he exceeded my expectations as a superior bartender.  I feel a sense of home here.  This will be a regular spot in Nash.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Brand new music venue for downtown Nashville and a truly great addition!!!   Highly recommend!!!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I've been in Nashville for 3 days. Checked this place out each day and the bands on each floor were great. Lots of talent. Come here for a good time day or night.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
BY FAR the worst experience i've Had in Nashville. We went her for the 2018 new year celebration. We paid 50 dollars per person online for tickets just to get into the bar, which was pretty standard on NYE but when we arrived there was a HUGE line. They had oversold tickets and were not letting anyone in. To make matters worse it was 3 degrees with windchill. Once we got into the bar, they weren't even letting people up to the top floor. The fire alarm went off and none of the staff addressed the problem. After waiting 30 minutes (not an exaggeration) to get our drinks, the bartender didn't even give us limes. 

This was such a terrible experience, and the worst part is they aren't even addressing how terrible they messed up last night. I'm sure other people will be writing similar reviews.

name: Live On The Green Music Festival
text:
Live music, fabulous location, beer and food trucks. Doesn't get much better. 

The FREE Live on the Green music festival series has been going on in Public Square Park for 6 years - and my husband and I have been lucky enough to go to almost every single one. Held on Thursday nights (for typically 5 weeks in a row) the festival boasts some of the best music in town and it's not to be missed.  Last year, they added on a weekend festival to cap off the series. HUGE success as many more folks attended on the weekend. (my only reason for not giving it 5 starts is the fact that they've definitely outgrown their venue. I also wish they would make this event 21 and up, but the logistics of that would be difficult.)

The 2015 lineup is incredible! Passion Pit, Ben Folds, Rodrigo y Gabriela, Moon Taxi. I'm drooling already. 

Over the years, more and more amazing food trucks and beer vendors come out to participate, providing guests with anything they could possibly want to nosh on and drink. 

But with that comes the crowds. We attended the first show of the year last night and were amazed at how crowded it was - so be prepared for that. The event is always a blast - it's always so fun to be surrounded by like-minded music fans, enjoying the summer weather and having a great time. What a great city we live in, huh? 

Enjoy! 

Tips: 
Get there as early as you can (the place starts filling up around 5). 
Many people bring chairs to sit in, but as soon as the shows start everyone stands - making the chairs just a pain to lug around. Bring a blanket instead. 
The food truck lines are unavoidable, so if you have a hankering for a specific one, be ready to wait. 
Porta-pottys abound - no getting around it. :) 
I wish I had a tip for parking, but my husband and I walk to the event, so I have no words of wisdom there. 
Children are welcome, but strollers at this event would be an absolute nightmare due to the sardine-like crowds. 
We always bring our dog - and see many others, so crowd-friendly dogs are also welcome. Your bags will most likely be checked on the way in, so don't attempt to bring in beer - you'll be turned away. 
There is a couple water fountains at the location that are meant to be played in - enjoy them on those hot summer nights!

name: The Station Inn
text:
Awesome place!! Musicians fantastic! Went there for the Sunday Jam. Probably the best experience of our Nashville trip. Talented musicians (aged from 8 to 80) doing what they love. 
Will recommend it to all! 
I'll be back there every time I visit Nashville.
LOVE IT!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great place for live music, drinking, people watching, and just fun. Not sure about the food but I hear the wings are "the best". Never saw so many "Brides To Be" and their entourages. Looks like cover starts at 10pm so start before then and stay. Boots and black are obviously in. Wear anything, might include ear plugs. Yeh, I'm over 50.

name: Alley Taps
text:
Good music
Great Band
Service is slow because it was packed!!!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: If you are in Nashville and want to listen to great live music and have a great time this is the place. If you are lucky enough to have Sebastian be your sever it makes it that much better. That kid works his behind off. Had a great time.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: My favorite place ever! 3 story bar with awesome music and delicious burgers! Saturday morning is packed!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Dark, dingy, but good for live music.  The bathrooms had this overwhelming sewer gas smell - egads.  Cheap draft beers kept us there for 2 drinks, instead of our standard 1 and done.

name: Nashville Underground
text: What a great place with below freezing beer on tap! 3 floors of casual class, and a rooftop view that's not packed with college kids! Good burger and service!

name: Alley Taps
text:
I love the look of this place. The female bartender on Saturday night was awesome. The male bartender on Sunday night was not so great. 

They had a great local gin along with a good variety of other gins which I appreciated. I loved the atmosphere, with very old architecture and hodge podge appearance. There was a couch (living room style) in one of the areas with a tv to watch games which was nice. I like the entrance in the alley way as well. I didn't try any food. This rating is for Saturday night. 

Sunday night, the bartender didn't communicate well when taking orders. For example, they apparently had a 2 for 1 deal on beers. He didn't say anything when my friend ordered a beer. He just tossed a chip onto the bar and walked away. We had to get his attention to ask what the chip was otherwise we would have just ignored its presence as it wasn't necessarily given to anyone. The first set of drinks were very weak. I watched him measure with a shot glass and he didn't even fill it all the way up. The second drinks he didn't even measure, just poured the alcohol in and they were much better. I guess he liked us by then?

Then the live music that was playing was all sad. We requested a happy song and put money in the tip jar. He continued to play sad music and stated that 95% of people are sad (so that is why he is singing sad songs). 

Then , things got weird. Our friend walked into the men's restroom and the bartender and the musician were canoodling or something more sinister. When my friend walked back to the bar, he looked stunned and said we needed to leave.  

So, needless to say, we had an interesting experience.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Awesome music.  The bar is a bit expensive and they started charging us for bottled water all of a sudden.  Water at a bar should be free always. I'm trying not to get crazy drunk and sick.

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text: War Memorial is the worst venue in the city. I've attended several concerts here, and every time its the same situation. If you want to get a drink, including water, be prepared to wait in a 45+ plus line while you miss the concert you paid to see. The bartenders are nice, however they aren't use to dealing with large crowds. You also can't start a tab, which slows down the process further. While at JRAD last night, we waited in line for over 30 minutes at the start of the second set, to be told when we got up to order our drinks, that they were out of all beer and mixers. If you're in the back of reserved seating you won't be able to see the stage. The only thing that would get me to go back to War Memorial would be Jerry Garcia himself coming back to life and playing a one night only show there.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I loved this place. I came here as a tourist and I didn't try any of the food because we had just eaten at Jack's BBQ. Therefore, the only aspect I can judge about the Honkey Tonk is through drinks and music and both were some of the best I experienced in Nashville. The drinks weren't watered down as they are at most bars, yet they weren't too strong so they tasted great. However, the music was the true gem of this place. There are three floors and each floor had great music. However, the third floor was my favorite. I am a country fan, but my boyfriend is more of a classic rock fan. The band that was playing covered country (of course) and classic rock which he loved. It was impossible not to get up and dance even for my boyfriend who never wants to dance. It was very crowded but perhaps because I am 24 I didn't mind it and found it was more crowded at the other bars. Don't get intimidated by the line because there are three floors so it doesn't get as packed as you'd think. Plus, if they have bands like they had Sat night the music is completely worth it.

name: The Station Inn
text: I was lucky enough to enjoy some awesome bluegrass music on christmas night at The Station Inn. What a treat! The Station Inn provided a wonderful, authentic atmosphere and an amazing live music experience. The crowd was full of music enthusiasts as well as tourists. We enjoyed a few pitchers of beer and snacks. The room is laid out so you will get a great view no matter where you end up sitting. There is an open and airy feel in the restrooms (haha! think curtains on the stalls - if you are a person into a super private restroom experience, bring a friend to the bathroom with you to hold the curtain shut more). Aside from the amazing live music, I love love love all of the show posters on the walls!! The mix of older and newer flyers hanging serves as a sort of poster museum. I can not wait to return here on my next trip to Nashville!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
We went to see the Long Players do the Van Morrison "Moondance" album. Got there when the doors opened, thank God, since the place was already partly full before that and the tables filled up real quick. Decided to sit upstairs in the balcony. Good idea given the fact that the dance floor was full of people and the sight lines from the tables on the first floor couldn't be that good. Decent sound upstairs so we were happy with the show. And I can recommend highly seeing these guys do anything. The musicians were spot-on in reproducing the instrumental part of the album. And the rotation of singers made the night even more interesting and enjoyable. The second set was a variety of Van Morrison tunes,some hits and some just wonderful tunes from his catalog.

Two stars? Yeah, because the service sucked! We waited about 15 minutes from the time we sat down for someone to take our drink order, then another ten or more for it to be delivered. Then another 30 minutes before we could order our food. THEN we waited over an hour for it to be brought to the table. Neighboring tables had their food and finished while we waited and waited and waited. reminded our waitress, Stephanie, twice about the food. It finally arrived during the show despite the fact we arrived two hours before the show started. TWO HOURS! That was absolutely inexcusable. And of course, when you wait that long, the food was lukewarm - gumbo that isn't hot just doesn't taste good. And the rest of the food was just mediocre. Not very tasty and none of it was straight out of the kitchen. 

So, advice to the wise - go to 3rd and Lindsley for the music and some drinks. FORGET about the food - they don't know how to make it tasty and they don't know how to manage orders and timely delivery.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I would compare the Honky Tonk Central to a bar in the middle of Times Square in NYC. Very touristy. There are 3 floors with outdoor balconies which is very cool but on a Saturday night the place was packed. The live music on the first floor was subpar. Definitely better places on the strip for live music. I went up to the third floor to check out the live music up there and it was just as bad. 

Drinks are totally over priced. $9 for a tiny cup with hardly any vodka and seltzer. Come on I get better prices in NYC!
