name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: Wax museum tour. Very nicely put together, clean and very decorative. See stars like Carrie Underwood, Blake Shelton, Jason Aldean, Johnny Cash, Elvis, Beyoncé and more. I gave it three stars because of the price.. $24 per ticket and the tour is about 20-30 min long. If you buy online in advance it is $19 per ticket. Also heads up for Nashville Tour books and maps for coupons.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Came in out of the rain for brunch. The service, music and food was great! 
Had a frozé and split the chicken and waffles. Their spicy savory take on this classic was amazing and easy to split/eat. Glad we tried it!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: My husband and Istumbled  across this bar while walking around on broadway. I have to say, we had a great time! I'm not the Biggest country fan, but I enjoyed that there was music for all different styles! The first two levels for live bands (both were great) and then the rooftop area was a hip hop/top 40 area with a dj! I truly had a great time! I ordered some Truly's which were over priced, but I wasn't surprised-ordering them at a bar probably wasn't the smartest thing to do anyways but #basic so it is what it is! Overall, I had a great time. Service and staff were decent and the bathrooms and floors were pretty clean for the amount of traffic coming and going. I would recommend to anyone wanting to have a good time.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: This place was really yummy! My friend and I went at 5:30 on a Friday and it was empty but we didn't watch the show. We just stayed in the main part of the restaurant so maybe everyone was hiding in the show part. The food was good and I was a little sad when my waitress took my food back before I was done with my fries, but I'd go back!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Giving them two stars because they have music. Rude staff ... served us on a Monday night 6/17/2019. We had just bought a round of drinks (4) a good song came on and got up to dance one song. When we came back they had cleared our table. There was plenty of seating so that was not an issue. Bartender was rude and did not handle the situation correctly. When we complains to the bartender about the loss of drinks we were kicked out reluctantly by security who apologized to us .Normally you would have a coaster or a napkin served with your drink so we could of put a clear sign. We did not think it would be a problem because they were fresh drinks $60 down the drain . I recommend going to Ole Red where the staff are trained and friendly . Btw we have owned two bars . You don't treat customers like they treated us. Never going there when there are plenty of nice bars to go to.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This is a terrible establishment. I would suggest avoiding it at all costs if you're a POC. They look at you crazy when you walk in, service horrible, and they will attempt to find any reason to make your experience the utmost uncomfortable. I visited back in February. Gave it one more time this July. It's clear now that this place isn't it!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
Nice cruise up the river on a BIG boat. Didn't do the diner, didn't look like a missed anything. Ordered a beer for the show $14!!! Gee I got to keep the glass.
Update
Wife complained to the Stewart that we should have been told the cost or given a choice. He refunded to a standard beer. Good service from management.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: IN an actual alley that you feel like you are coming in the back door. The place was divey, the food was great. It was a tad dark but it was good food and really nice service.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: BB Kings Blues Club ligger utmed ett stråk på 2:nd Avenue centralt och tvärgata till den stora Broadway. Grannar med bl.a. Wildhorse Saloon, Hooters och Hard Rock Café. Det är turistmagneter allesammans, stora välbesökta ställen med egna souvenir shoppar och ofta med bra live musik på sina scener (då tar vid såna tillfällen ibland inträdde). Roligt att tillbringa en stund här. Bra mat och service, kul inredning. Värt att slå ihjäl några timmar här, men inget absolut måste.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
It's been a week now since I went to the Grand Ole Opry, and I am still thinking about what a great time I had.  OK, let's get this out of the way.  I can't stand Country music and I don't know who any of these people are.  But wow, what a show!  From young to old, from experienced to newbie, it was a star-studded cast.  Talent everywhere, and I had a blast.  

They do things in 30 minute segments, with 3 performers each sequence.  All sorts of different genre - from bluegrass to country to what I would call country/rock.  

The venue is large and well ventilated.  Other than almost freezing my britches off, I had a GREAT TIME!!!!

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: At the foot of Music Row by the Roundabout, Dawg House Saloon is just a nice bar. Its lacquered tables really are spots to get "lacquered, and some do. The pub grub there isn't too bad and includes yummo Six Gun Pizza with 5 meats, 'rooms and special red sauce. The King (George) Strait Pizza is less overthetop with just a couple meats and three kinds of peppers including hot jalapeno. Pork and other sliders, fried pickles and lots of Hot Dawgs are there to. The "Asian Invasion" (is that p.c.?) tempura-fried brat has spiced slaw & wasabi. No beers on tap now, bottles & mixed drinks.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Fun atmosphere, great selection of taps. The building is huge with a variety of areas to sit. Id definitely come here again.

name: Anthem
text:
Went to see adventure club 7/28/13 at Anthem. Tickets were fairly expensive and it was a train wreck getting into the club. It was raining hard and they made you stand in line (with a pre-sold ticket) outside in the rain for almost an hour... Then they wouldn't let you bring your umbrella in so you had to throw it away :-/.

In the club they had massively oversold the show. They sold over 600 presale and then a few hundred more at the door. It was FAAAR over capacity. You literally couldn't move and the temp was almost 90 degrees (I saw a thermostat near the restroom). They could have sold about 300 less tickets and it still would of been too crowded. There were points where you couldn't even get in the main area of the stage because people were stick In The doors... 

Anyhow this club massively over sells shows and then scalps prices at the door. I don't recommend it :-/. I stayed until 2:30 AM and never even got to see adventure club because it was physically impossible to make it through the chest to chest club.

name: Third Man Records
text:
Wonderful gift shop (independent record label) in Nashville for fans of Jack White (the White Stripes). While wandering around the city we decided to add this shop to our list and had a nice little walk over to the shop. It was certainly not in the "high traffic" area, but the walk was really nice. We arrived around the same time as a few other groups so it was a bit crowded. The store itself is very small, but they have a ton of gift ideas in multiple rooms so we were able to semi-spread out and browse without bumping into one another. I noticed a recording area for you to go and record some music and they even had a cool photo booth! 

We looked around and ended up purchasing some Third Man Records gifts to bring back to some friends we know. The girls working the counter were friendly and offered some assistance as needed. So glad we stopped in!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great food drink and service. I was hungry and looking for some food late at night. I loved the german plate.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This place is awesome!  What a surprise to find a place that has the vibe of a neighborhood pub in the heart of downtown!  The staff is incredible, the beer selection is decent and the homemade chips are to die for!  Located in an alley right off the Arcade, this hidden gem is a "must try"!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The music and bands are always good but food is not really what it is hyped up to be, friendly waitresses and employess , they deserve 5 stars , it's the food that is only 2 star

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Alexandria is a phenomenal server and has exceptional customer service  skills. She made my B.B Kings experience perfect!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We were looking to grab some lunch and found this spot. It was not packed but we still had to wait for a table, I don't understand why. We had the ribs (delicious) and catfish bites (really liked the slightly hot sauce it came with). Also liked that the live music included two amazing guys on guitars and not a full on band like many other places in the area.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: We were in town for NYE and was looking for somewhere to grab a bite and listen to live music. We came across this place while walking and decided to give it a try. Food was pretty good. We all had burgers. I had the chilli cheese burger. It could have had a little more chilli on it, but it was still good. I will say though, their homemade chips were awesome! They had live music as well. I would definitely stop in again while in town.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Loved it!! A must see if you are in Nashville. The theatre is beautiful and the bench seats are comfortable.  We had been to the Ryman Auditorium the day before which gave us alot of background on the Grand Ole Opry. The format was interesting and although some of the acts should have retired years ago, it was fun. And...we got to see Carrie Underwood!!

name: Third Man Records
text: They SUCK! They are expensive and think they are so cool. We spent 45 mins in there and found some things that we might have bought regardless but when my son needed to use the bathroom they refused and made us go across The street to a craft store. DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME OR MONEY-many better stores for half the price and nicer people too! If I could give them  0 stars I would!!!!!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: We are from out of town and tried to go to puckets grocery and restaurant.  After being told that it was going to be up to 2 hours wait we decided to come to back alley diner. We should have left.  The air conditioning was out.  They were out of tea and we waited at least 20 minutes for that.  We ordered the pulled pork plate and the pork came out cold.  I wished we would have just waited at puckets.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: The atmosphere is pretty tacky but the food hits the spot and the beer selection is the best in Nashville that I have found. Great for lunch but not dinner. 3 STARS because of atmosphere and the plates showing how many beers people drink freaks me out.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I really enjoyed my visit to Flying Saucer. They had a great assortment of beer, good service, and good food. The best part is that it was all at a reasonable price. I came on pint night (Monday) and was able to sample some local brews for $3 a pint. I would definitely recommend it it will probably return.

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text: Still the absolute best Guinness in town :). Bar tenders are knowledgable, friendly, and attentive. The food is great quality and they have a pretty good size menu. The authentic Irish fare seems authentic to me and is actually really good. Still my favorite pub in town.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I feel like there really should be two Yelp pages for the Grand Ole Opry- one for the tour and one for the actual show.

After attending a show and then later reading the great Yelp reviews about the tour, I definitely wish I had done the tour instead!  The show itself was just OK. Here is my list of things I noted:

-  The Grand Ole Opry is not located in downtown Nashville.  If you are visiting without a car, make sure you arrange transportation

-  The theater itself was really nice-- definitely seemed very modern and the staff was super friendly.

-  The show itself is comprised of a number of acts- I think our show had maybe 5 or 6-- each performing 2-3 songs.  

-  The show definitely targets an older audience.  There is a lot of goofy old-timey country music.  If you can barely stand modern country (i.e. Kenny Chesney, Miranda Lambert, etc), you probably won't like this show.  I'm a huge fan of country, so I kinda liked the O.G. tunes.

-  Be prepared for a ton of commercial breaks-- I was really surprised by this.  I kept forgetting this is a live show on the radio.  It got annoying after awhile.  Especially since we paid $40 per ticket to watch the show.

Overall, I'm glad I checked out the Grand Ole Opry, but I wouldn't come back for another show.  For a tour, maybe.  It was a little expensive- especially after you factor in transportation.  And there are plenty of free music options on lower Broadway.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Music and a beer or two.  We liked the band that night, we did not eat any food at all.  It was a Tuesday night, in town for a conference.  It was not that busy at all.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Well...it wasn't Karaoke as we know it...but, that's ok...could have been a real fun place, but it was over-crowded, noisy and just gave off unsafe vibes...I am not basing this on anything other than my gut feeling....No seating....crowded to the rafters (hey...good for them!) but not really what we were looking for in karaoke....had a beer each and left...if you're into noise and willing to stand, go for it...We'll pass...

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
My kind of watering hole. Outstanding beer selection. Tons of good stuff on tap. Really cool atmosphere with lots tall ceilings and pretty cool decor from wall to wall. I got a pretty damn good SOUR BEER Flight here and i wasn't disappointed. 

Will definitely be finding myself here again the next time I'm in Nashvegas!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Was in Nashville for one night and Belcourt Taps was recommended for a non-tourist taste of local music and food.  Far exceeded my expectations. On a Wednesday night there were a couple of really legit female singers.  And the crowd was into the music which made it fun.  Also worth mentioning, the burger I had was way beyond normal bar food fare.  And very casual place, btw.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: My first time to Belcourt Taps was on a Saturday night. I called ahead and asked for a table of 12! They gladly accommodated us and led us to our reserved tables. We had a great time! The music was fun and the atmosphere was real smooth. I tried their pork fries which came timely, hot, and tasty! There were only two waiters for indoor and outdoor guests but they were on top of things. I appreciated the great service along with great food and music. Will return again. The outdoor setting looked like a great place for bigger crowds too.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
B.B. King's Blues Club was so much fun! It was definitely one of my favorite meal experiences during my weekend visit to Nashville. My friend and I stopped in for an early dinner (around 5:15pm, so no cover charge for us) on a Friday night and were seated immediately, right next to the stage for optimal listening! The Carl Stewart band was playing some jazz/blues classics, and every one of the band members was fantastic (and super friendly!). The vibe of the place is great--high ceilings, fun mood lighting, and pretty good acoustics. 

The food was great, staple, southern fare. My friend and I split a small order of the fried pickles (which came out like pickle chips and were excellent, especially with the dipping sauce! The small order was also plenty for the two of us.), a large order of the ribs (8 ribs, which was plenty for us. There was lots of meat on these guys, pretty solid ribs.), and a side of cornbread (4 warm cornbread muffins, yumyum!). We probably spent about 1.5 hours enjoying the band and our dinner, and spent right around $30 for the two of us. Craaaazy cheap for the amount of food we had!

Loved the music, loved the vibe, great place for dinner! But get there early if at all possible--by the time we left, it was packed!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I'm giving four stars based on the AMAZING music. The live music is literally better than the original artists in a lot of instances. The food was good, not great, and the service was ok. I say GO, if just for the music alone!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I came here for the experience and it was a great choice! Talented performers, venue had great acoustics, and the staff are well trained. I've been to many venues and this is definitely well organized. It is not too far away from Nashville, I took and uber there and back and it was easy to get to. There is so much history, which was promoted during the commercials and found out there used to be a opry theme park which is now a mall located next to the venue along with a convention center!

name: Third Man Records
text:
Every time I come to Nashville, I make sure I can swing by this amazing shop. 
They rearrange and change it around so its always a little different when I go in. 
The employees are always very nice and may I also note, very attractive. There seems to be a plethora of beautiful women and a disproportionately high number of redheads working there. I found both of these things enjoyable. Also great attitudes from everyone. I've never gotten bad service or over heard any of them being rude or "too cool" as other reviews have stated. 
I buy records there each time I go. First time I got The White Stripes' De Stijl, White Blood Cells and Get Behind Me Satan. This trip I got The Stooges eponymous album and Blind Willie McTell Volume 4.
My fiancé went there a few years ago without me and Jack was in the shop that day. They're both from Detroit and my fiancé was at one of The White Stripes first shows in Detroit so they chatted about that. He said Jack was very kind and happy to talk at length with a fellow musician and pose for a picture after. 
I bought a couple T-Shirts this time and last when I went in. I am a small woman so I usually get a Youth shirt sized Large. In addition to them fitting better than adult sizes, I like the special designs they have for the kids shirts.
They have a lot of really cool trinkets and tchotchkes. We got some stickers, match boxes, I got a 45 rpm adapter, some post cards. They had some really cool journals I had my eye on but I was already getting up there in things I was buying so I exercised some self restraint and decided to save some stuff for next time if its still there. 
Theres a lot to look at so don't be in a hurry when you go in. 

Go check it out! 
And tell one of the pretty girls I said hi. 
;-)
~Zoe

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The food here was *really* good. Our server was good too; definitely in overdrive due to the crowds for CMA fest.   I ordered blackened chicken salad which was delicious. My company had pasta which was also very good. We would definitely go back. The music was great, if you like the blues. I do!   It's loud and cramped, so I would be selective on who I recommended this to, but the food was A+.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great service, amazing beer selection, big enough that even when it's full it doesn't feel crowded. I had several local craft brews at the recommendation of the waiter and waitress and all were delicious. I ordered the chips and queso with spicy chili and it was great!  I am not one to enjoy hot and spicy things but the blend of spicy chili mixed with the queso was perfect to me. Had enough bite making me want a drink, but not overpowering that it took away from eating them. They even have me a refill on chips since I had some chili queso left and there was no charge for it. This seems insignificant but many places I've been to in the past year charge $1 or so for more chips. Highly recommend this place...just be prepared for dealing with parking...don't be afraid to valet.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
You will never see a larger beer selection ever again if you go here. The beer menu and taps were dizzying which was awesome.

They even have pre made flights ready to go which is a huge help. I had the $9 Nashville flight and it was perfect to tide me over while I looked over the rest of the menu. 

I didn't have any food but was with someone who ordered a pulled pork sandwhich. It was dry and there was no sauce to go along with it. 

I'll stick to this place for their beer and the cool train station feel. If I get drunk enough I may even buy a plate to put on the ceiling.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Amazing! At 57 I have finally made it here to the place I listened to with my grandfather so many years ago.
Also visited the Ryman too, love Nashville

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Great acoustics but smaller than my expectation!   I enjoyed the venue and would definitely come back again...

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: ate here with the family yesterday for lunch the service was super slow and the food was cold when it finally came.  The turkey burger was dry and hard like it was microwaved.  The chicken cordone blue was overcooked but cold when it was served.  The pulled pork was flavorful and pretty good.  The service was so bad I will not return.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
The only reason you would go here is to listen to the BB King AllStars. Amazing band! 
Don't expect good service, starting with the front check in experience. When you ask for a table with a front view of the band, all tables have "reserve" signs on them, with no one sitting there. My friend and I sat to the side, ordered dinner & several drinks. We noticed that several "reserved" tables were still open & asked to be seated there. The hostess said those were reserved for people who would drink. Now mind you, we had dinner already & several drinks. We told her we had ever intention of still drinking.....she had a terrible attitude. A blonde skinny chick came & wiped the table off, with zero recognition to us. 
Come for the music but don't expect any type of decent attitudes from service staff. They need to learn how to put a smile on their face or move on!!!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great place, first time here and already wishing there was one in NY.  Great beer selections and perfect comfort food. Grilled cheese and tomato bisque was lovely!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: This is our go to for both work and play dinners when in Nashville - it is perfect for groups and it lands with strong drinks, amazing live music, and southern food that hits the spot. Dancing drinking eating and laughing - bring your kids bring your parents everyone will have a blast. Order the fried pickles, gumbo, ribs and catfish. And ask for Amanda she's hilarious and never let our plates go cold or our drinks get dry!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great band! Food was awesome.  Had fried pickles, friends tomatoes, and gumbo which was fantastic.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Went to Belcourt Taps after purchasing a Groupon that included a beer sampler since my husband enjoys trying new beers. Parking was not the easiest but that's extremely common for the area. 
It was Friday afternoon and the waitress greeted us and asked us to please be patient because she was the only waitress there at the moment, which worried me. However, she never missed a beat. The beer was delicious, and the sandwiches we got were amazing. 
The Groupon made it a great deal, that's the only real downside I see is that it's not cheap. Still, for the quality we got I'd say even paying full price would have been worth a freshly prepared dinner, nice cold beers and a comfortable patio setting.

name: Anthem
text:
Visited here not during it's normal operation, but during a private event.

Cool space, I particuarly enjoyed the seating set up on multiple levels, including on the stage and the balcony.  Great size dance floor, and nice incorporation of tech and lighting.  Music was of appropriate volume for me to talk to my party and I thought the drinks were tasty.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
As an Adelicia resident, I really do love the Tippler. I think it's one of the best things to happen to Midtown. It's a great place to dance along to a DJ on weekend nights, or host an intimate writer's round with the best songwriters on Music Row. (Much more sophisticated than many of the other Midtown bars.) I go to the Tippler at least once a week. I love the drink options and have enjoyed many small plates by the award-winning chefs. However, there are just a few things about MCT that really peeve me. 

First, their menu changes almost monthly. I don't mean that they change seasonal menu items. I mean they completely redesign the the way the menu looks, including the paper it is printed on, while also taking off all menu items that originally made the place unique, such as the Duck Burger, the Krispy Kreme Burger, and the San Fran Chicken Sandwich. 

Secondly, their fried pickles are cut so thin, that you can barely bite into them. What I mean by that is they are breaded in a really tasty, spicy batter & fried, but when you bite through that, the prosciutto-thin pickle slice slides right out. It's as if they only use 1 average-sized pickle to fill an entire basket of fries. An expensive place like this should not skimp on their pickles. If they need a lesson in making tasty fried pickles, while also slicing them thin, they should walk a few blocks down to The Row. 

Lastly, MCT always has a special "drink of the day" showcased on the chalkboards on each side of the bar, which is great! But whenever I go to the bartender and ask for the drink of the day by it's name, they look at me like I'm crazy and ask me to explain what I'm talking about. Then I point at the chalkboard and they say "Ohhh. I have no idea. Let me ask". So then, of course, somebody has to come over and teach them how to make that drink and they take their time doing a little taste test of the drink so that the bartender can then explain to me what the drink is. This has happened to me multiple times!! Yesterday, the bartender made a face as if she hated the drink after tasting it & THEN tried to sell it to me. Ridiculous! Their bartenders should figure out how to make the drink special before their shift begins each day. 

These are just some little things that clearly separate MCT from The "Always Classy" Patterson House.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We enjoyed the club very much. Not as crowded and noisy as others and the music was very entertaining. Completely enjoyed the shrimp, and the smoked sausage po boy was excellent. Loved that BBQ sauce!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great service and food. Ended up there on buy one get one free draft night. Drink options were solid and fast. Waitress was helpful and we were both very happy with the food. Got the veggie quesadillas and grilled chicken sandwich. Also side of fries and house made chips. Everything tasted great.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Not a big country music fan but the history and tour is worth the $24 dollars and it is informative and very entertaining. I learned a lot and am eager to see a show. The tour guide was knowledgeable and not boring which was nice. Stop by and take the tour.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Bartender and subsequently manager would not allow a+40yo friend to order drinks and food from bar bc of lack of ID.  Also $15 cover charge for essentially nothing.  Don't patronize this place.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
So we were in town for a conference and want to grab some bites and soak in some of the live music. BB Kings became the destination, so we made reservations. 

The restaurant is very well decorated with tons of jazz and blues legends arranged on the walls with original art work. The music was smooth and well played. 

As for the food, it was just ok I guess. 
We ordered the brisket sandwich, nachos, fried pickles and other items. Nothing special really, just tasted like regular BBQ, nothing that will blow your mind. Drinks were good, it got the job done I guess.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Wow I was told they make great burgers and it's one of the best burgers I've ever had! Many restaurants could learn a few things from their cooks. You get your money and appetite's worth with a large half-pound burger and the meat is tender, juicy, perfectly cooked. The bun was very fresh, though the best part is the secret subtle seasoning in the meat (all I could identify was parsley) which is so flavorful you won't even need condiments (which I normally use but had no need). The accompanying onion sticks were crispy and tasty. This will certainly be my new go-to burger joint and the pub atmosphere is quite comfortable and friendly as well!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I had a great time last night at the Grand Ole Opry. The venue is huge with many nice, clean restrooms available. Inside the auditorium, it was a little bit less grand, at least in the seating area, which is pew styled. The cloth cover on the seats are slightly coming off. My main complaint is that seating in this fashion doesn't give everyone a fair space of room. For example, by boyfriend and I actually took up 1.5 (instead of the fair 2) seats and we were still nearly shoulder to shoulder with the people next to us. Not exactly the most comfortable situation. 

Like many, I came not knowing what to expect and not knowing any of the artist on the list but am all in for good music. I was blown away by many of the artists here-- some rising stars! They definitely gained a new fan! In light of the crammed seating condition, we had a really great time! And the experience definitely opened our eye to the different style of music out there. I highly recommend spending an evening here.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We took the backstage tour of The GRAND OL OPRY!  The tour guide seemed to be as excited to giving us the tour as we were to take it. It was refreshing to see. It was so interesting to see where it all began and how they have tried to keep stars "feet on the ground". They are a family and it shows.  We felt humbled to be there.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Bartender was fucking fantastic. Such a great experience in Nashville. Thank you sir.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Best bar in Nashville if you are a beer lover!  You're guaranteed to find something on the menu you've never had, or even heard of before! Their menus conveniently categorize beers by style which is convenient for those who know what style of beer they like. Not only do the have over a hundred beers on tap, they have many more bottled!  You can get everything from PBR to Wells Banana Bread Beer (which is awesome FYI)!

If you are adventurous like my husband is, you can join the UFO club, where you get a plate on the wall once you drink 200 DIFFERENT beers! However, I prefer to 1) save my liver and 2) stick with a few categories of beers I like best, and even then, I have at least 20-30 beers that I really like here.

Oh, and then there's the pretzels! Warm soft pretzels served with 2-3 dips of your choice. My favorite is the cream cheese and chive, but the queso and spicy mustard are good too! Their food is biased toward German dishes, and to me they are the best options on the menu.

This is our go to bar before Preds games and concerts downtown. Easy parking in the lot down the hill behind the building for cheap, then we walk to the games/shows.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Went to Belcourt taps as part of a day out in Hillsboro at the Pup Crawl event. Stopped in because they featured a dog menu and. We had three pups with us. 

Loved this place!!! Patio was dog friendly and they are going to keep the dog menu going forward, so that's great. Food was awesome as well. I got the stuffed burger special and was pretty blown away. They come with sweet potato, truffle, or garlic parm fries and on a pretzel roll. 

Best part of the whole experience was the management and staff though. Wait staff was awesome, super friendly, and the managers did everything they could to make sure not only that we were happy but that our dogs were too! 

I'll be going back.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
I'm going to give this place another shot, since I wasn't really feeling the vibe last night in general and our server was very apparently new, as she told us a couple times. We sat down and it took about 10 mins for anyone to come by (not uncommon in downtown Nashville in my experience). It was another 10 min wait for our beers once we ordered (again not really that uncommon). Another lengthy wait to be asked if we wanted to order food. When I ordered I was told they didn't have any left, so I ordered a sandwich. Food came out fairly quick, except my wife's food sat on the counter as we stared at it and our server just kept walking by it. Pretzels were very good!! 

When our 2nd round of beers came out my buddy was still finishing his beer. Our server took it from him and then spilled it. Whatever. Then my wife spilled her all but full beer on her own (slipped out of her hand) and server came by again, shrugged and left. Didn't offer to get another one or come by to clean up, nothing, until we asked for our bill. I also wasn't wow'd by the amount of beers. In my mind the more beer they have the less specialty they have in one thing but that's my own personal feeling. 

All of that was honestly dismissible due to our server being on her 2nd night. I completely understand as I was a server at one point and am sure I gave terrible service at one time or another. However what prompted this review was this. I took my food home last night since I only ate about half. I just warmed it up, took a bite, only to find a big ol gnarly black hair in my sandwich. Sandwich was decent to begin, but after that I had to throw it out. 

I'll try and give this place one more shot but that might be the last time for me. Underwhelmed to say the least.

name: Music City Tippler
text: I haven't eaten here but I've definitely partied here. Crowded, loud, hard to get a drink....and totally awesome! DJ rocking good tunes, girls are hot and plenty of them, and has a Manhattan feel. This is exactly the kind of swanky, club scene place that makes Nashville a great place for locals. It's completely different from the tourist mess downtown that we locals try to avoid. Get a few drinks in your system, get a cab, and head here.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
We stopped by here while it was drizzling out and we were waiting for our dinner reservations at Rodizio Grill. We did not know that the Kentucky Derby race was just about to take place and thought that the weather was to blame for the overabundance of patrons. This place is really big and it was jam-packed.

The service left much to be desired as our server could not remember our order and needed correction multiple times. Additionally, the Flying Saucer is known for its extensive selection of beers. On the day we were there, they were out of 4-5 of them, of which my table had selected two. Kind of a bummer, but I wish they're write what they are out of on one of their blackboards or something. Also strange was the fact that the beer glasses come out soaking wet with water at the bottom of them. I appreciate it when restaurants take a minute to dry their glasses before presenting them to patrons.

All in all, if you're looking to grab a quick drink or mingle with the office crowd after work, this is a good spot. But if you're looking to woo someone or have any sort of quiet conversation, I'd strongly advise you to go elsewhere.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Food is ok. Beer selection is amazing. Very loud, and has lots of college-aged kids. I liked this place quite a lot. Played trivia on Tuesday nights several times with groups of friends. Really kind of a great place for bigger groups.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: dude i am deducting a star for parking, which you have to go down in a dirty and shady lot and also pay for it. the beer selection is all right and you do get some award if you drink like all of the selections. the appetizers are all right

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Flying saucer is one the best bars in nashville ESP with the beer selection they have. I highly recommend  the Rocket Tots with the habanero sour cream--TDF. 
And to the girl who yelped that her glass was wet-- if u know anything about beer on tap it should be served in a super clean glass for optimal head and taste-- they rinse each glass on a high powered water blaster before serving. A super smart move. Thumbs up Flying saucer!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This was one of my favorite stops in Nashville. I heard of this place prior to going but didn't know much about it. I was pleasantly surprised. It was beautiful inside. They had a bunch of great acts performing, at least six or seven acts. I loved the bench seating, you could see everything no matter who was sitting in front of you.  It was just a good time and definitely a must see if your going to Nashville for a trip!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: The burgers here are great. They served them stuff and non stuff. Don't worry non-carnivores, they have food for you as well.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Just went in for drinks and music. We ordered wine and the one I ordered they didn't have it so they didn't charge me for my substitute drink. The music was good, bit loud so can't really have a conversation.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
I loved this place, mostly for their amazing wings at $.50 each. They no longer offer them at that price, it's now $1 each and you have to buy a plate of 8.

Went there last Saturday with a large group and service was mediocre. Unfortunately, our favorite waitress no longer works there. 

Without the wing deal, we settled on burgers. They were just ok. I asked for mine pink in the middle but it came out well done. The upside was their fries, totally a winner. 

This place has lost a bit of the charm for me that it once held. The location for the art crawl is great, but at this price point, there are better options downtown for dinner. I can only give it 3 stars now.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: First off let me start by saying that I'm really glad I didn't get the Groupon, especially after reading some of the other comments.  Second, avoid this place if you are claustrophobic!  It's a really small space and the set up is cramped and awful.  I was bumped and jostled by everyone that walked in the door.  There is only one beer menu and a two drink minimum per person if there is live music.  Luckily my best friend, boyfriend and I are lushes; so that wasn't an issue.  The people performing were wonderful!  Which is why I'm giving this place two stars.  We also ordered a couple of appetizers.  We wanted the jalapeño poppers but they were out.  So we settled on the spring rolls and fried mushrooms.  The fried mushrooms were recommended by our waiter as being "the best."  Hardly!  They were hard little balls and had a weird, bitter taste to them.  The spring rolls were a bit better but not by much.  Definitely not worth $7 each.  Besides the misguided recommendation from our waiter, service was good.  However, I am in no rush to go back anytime soon.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I don't know where the other yelpers ate but this was disappointing. I chose the catfish plate. Cute portion of a single catfish filet, dense tasteless hush puppies, lukewarm beans and tasteless cole slaw. If you're considering this place, go elsewhere

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Of the several stops we made on the strip, this karaoke bar was our fave. Everyone was having fun and the stage is set so anyone can get a good view. Just a great time!!

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
I wanted to go somewhere for locals and found this place. Atmosphere was cozy and staffs were kind and really attractive. 
Had a blue cheese burger and pulled pork sandwich with Bloody Mary which was recommended! I'll definitely come back!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: We were given menus but waiter did not come around to take order after 15+ min so we left. There were only 2 tables of customers so it wasn't like they were busy.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: I've here twice and their 6 and 7pm shows were cancelled both times. The waiter kept making mistakes and brought us the wrong items. The food was good, though. Very laid back and casual atmosphere. Also good location. But I don't think I will want to come back here.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I love going to shows at the Grand Ole Opry House! There isn't a bad seat in the whole place. I definitely recommend going to a show if you're in town visiting or if you live in Nashville!! TAKE THE BACK STAGE TOUR!!! It is so cool to see the dressing rooms and all the behind the scenes stuff at the Opry House. Since the Opry House is right next to the mall, they share parking, which means you can either get a really good parking spot or you have to walk pretty far...but either way, it is worth it and you'll be glad you went!!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: My family and I got tickets for a recent show at the Opry. We had such a grand time! There were performers old and young, funny and sweet, and all so talented! Don't wait for a "famous" celebrity to get tickets...we went on a night when we knew only two of the seven performers but absolutely LOVED hearing not only those up-and-coming artists, but also some old-time goodies and are now fans of amazing performers we'd never heard of before!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
This place is out of this world!!  The flying saucer offers a calm & comfortable atmosphere. If you sample enough of the ample beer selections, you may begin to feel like your on Mars. I hope not enough to see Uranus.  
I loved checking out the saucers. I tried to find the PA saucer but didn't. Next time!! We dined on a few apps, enjoyed a side salad & downed a few brews. It was all good!!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This was a great little diner for lunch. I order the original cheeseburger and you can tell that the burger is made fresh. The other girls ordered a chicken sandwich. Both were fresh as well. The fries were great. Overall, it was a great spot for lunch when all of the other places were crowded!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I would 100% recommend taking the backstage tour here. It's so cool to hear about the Oprys history and see where all the back stage action happens including being able to look into many of the artists dressing rooms. Its beautiful inside and the tour ends with a walk out on to the stage

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Well at first I did not want to pay a $3.00 cover because every other bar was free, but my husband thought we would enjoy. It was a great bar, with great music. The BB King guitarist and his band were great, we stayed for ours, ordered catfish app. And crab cakes - excellent, so worth the $6.00 cover. I totally recommend for a great time.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
My wife and I attended this tour this past Monday.  It wasn't originally on our list of things to do in Nashville but we saw a live broadcast of the Opry at the Ryman and whenever we had some free time earlier today, we decided to do the backstage tour as well. $32/person gets you a 45 minute tour partially narrated by Blake Shelton with the rest by a tour guide.  Our tour guide here Kayleigh, was peppy and full of energy and I was impressed by how upbeat she was throughout.  The tour itself started with a video and then proceeded to the artists entrance, through security and into the dressing room area, green room and finally out onto the stage itself for a photo opportunity which could be purchased in the gift shops. Throughout the tour we learned about the history of the Grand Ole Opry as well as what it meant to be a member.  To be honest, my wife and I had no clue about any of this before we came to Nashville but still found it to be a very cool experience.

The bottom line for for me is that I would recommend this tour to anyone in the Nashville area.  It is a cool experience to learn about the Opry and stand on the stage, even if you aren't Country music fans as neither my wife nor I are.  My only regret is that I would have taken this tour prior to seeing the live broadcast at the Ryman as I think I would have appreciated the show even more.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: First time there. Not a big country fan but it was fun. Great to be part of a long tradition for one night. Was able to see Sara Evans

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great food. Awesome shrimp and grits and gumbo. Kids liked mac and cheese. Good music atmosphere and service.  Glad we chose this place based on yelp reviews.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I can say with confidence now, that if you swing by Nashville you at least have to add the Grand Ole Opry to your list of "Things to Do"! It's a country music staple of Nashville and I have been there now 4 times and have thoroughly enjoyed every one of the shows I've been to. The place itself has so much history that I just feel special to be able to see all of it. All of the people you see go through there and perform know how to have a good time and are quick to make you feel like family-- 10/10 recommend!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I recall watching the Grand Ole Opry on TV growing up, so when I had a business trip to Nashville, I just had to stop. It sits in a shopping mall district, surrounded by stores. But walking up to the doors, I knew I was standing on sacred ground, where many legends had once walked. I was never a country music fan growing up, but I grew to love it when I was just 15 years old. This place is such a historical place. I didn't get to see a concert there, but just looking around the inside and outside of the building, I was in awe. If I'm ever in Nashville again, I will definitely be sure to check it out a second time. You can just feel the energy radiating from the walls. Some of the greats were made at the Grand Ole Opry!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: We started with the pretzel's and cheese. They microwaved frozen pretzel's they were too chewy, the cheese was not warm enough it was thick & clumpy. The burger was OK. the fries were terrible, as if they cooked them, then allowed the to sit in the oil to cool off. The replacement fries weren't much better.  I am gonna say if u wanna eat, this is NOT the place to do so. The beer was warm & overpriced. All in all u can skip this place. If u come for the music the let me know.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: What can I say about an establishment I've been haunting weekly for the past 3 years? Flying Saucer is unique because of its loyalty program, known as the "UFO Club" where for every 200 unique beers you drink, you earn a plate on the wall along with a party in your honor (and subsequent amounts of bar tab paid every time you hit the mark) It has a loyal selection of regulars and friendly waitstaff that changes fully about once a year. I honestly love the place, but it is entirely imperfect. The atmosphere alludes to a German beer hall with a couple communal tables (and plenty of single tables), couches, and an open concept complete with garage doors that open during the summer. If you are really interested in craft beer, their Monday $3 pint night is the place to be and their Tuesday-Friday 4-7pm $4 pint happy hour is nothing to scoff at. There are several really good menu items, including cheese fries surprise, the soft pretzels, and the grilled cheese and tomato soup. Their beer list updates weekly with over 50 taps of craft beer from near and far. If you don't like beer, don't come here. You will be disappointed by their selection of other beverages. They have great events like trivia and special sponsored beer releases and glass giveaways. They are a destination for watching preds games. The drawbacks are few but can be extremely annoying. If the place is crowded, service is very, very slow. The restaurant is not staffed for extremely high periods as it is normally a pretty mellow place. If you aren't there to watch the game, avoid going during major sporting events. Overall, it's a great place to eat, grab a beer, and hang out with friends. I wish I could give half star ratings, because I truly think they deserve 4.5 stars.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Was able to have lunch here today.  I ordered bbq wings and buffalo wings and a spinach salad.  The food was really good as was the music.  I definitely recommend this place!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Smoky atmosphere and great people watching. Lots of seating was appreciated as we were wrapping up the night.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I have been to a number of Flying Saucers and am a member of my local here in San Antonio. As this was barely a block from my hotel I ended up here a couple of times due to great specials. On Sunday they had all Tennessee pints for $4. From 4-7 they have a social hour where all pints are $4 so I made good use of that. Like all of the Saucers they have a great selection of beers. The food is the same as all the others, which was a bit of a disappointment to me. The biggest issue I had is that the staff was 100% focused on locals and regulars. It took me flagging down the bartender in order to get my first drink.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: This is the BEST bar in Nashville!! In town for CMAFest and have been here everyday!!! Thanks to Lena and Key (best bartenders) for making memories with us!!!!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: This place is so much fun. Bartenders are the coolest. the music is the best. Food? Don't even talk to me about the food. It's all good.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I was told by a friend to go eat at B B Kings BBQ and they wanted a $5 cover charge to eat. I said I'm paying to eat here and you are asking for a cover NO WAY. I'll find something else. No one else has covers.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Alright, what this place needs are really two different ratings: one for their music and one for their staff. First, I'd give the place five stars for their music. This is a go-to place of mine whenever visitors come to town, or I just want to see an amazing show in the round. Forget Bluebird, you'll never get in. Besides, this place is almost just as good except..

The service here deserves a solid one star. The staff here will actively ignore you. They will walk over to you, look you straight in the eye, turn right back around and head to go talk to the bartender. I've honestly been here probably 10 times in the last two years and have only once had good service, and it turns out that was the server's first day working there. 

The food is decent and the beer selection ok, but again beware of the staff. Sit at the bar if you ever want a drink.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
We go to Flying Saucer almost every Tuesday for Trivia.  While the Trivia isn't the best because of the insane categories (Lamps, Hills, Pigs, etc.), we come back because of the staff, food, and beer menu. The staff typically remembers us, which is nice.

The best things on the food menu are the Bratzel, Prosciutto & Arugula Pizza, Chicken Wings, Pretzels, & Chicken Snack. I literally only order one of those items every time I go. This place has the best pretzels in town by far.

The beer menu is great too because it's large and constantly rotating. I'm a part of the UFO club (drink 200 different beers and you get a plate on the wall). They get a lot of "one and done" kegs so you can try new beers each visit. Love this place.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Here for the first time on our 6 year anniversary date. We are seeing #Move staring Derek and Julianne Hough. Awesome show! If you get the chance see it!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
This is such a great place to visit and experience the the artist and their music . It is such a historical place that should not be missed. There are back stage tour should you should go to see and hear the  whole history of this wonderful place. And if your lucky enough you might experience an induction of an artist to join the family at Opryland. 
A must visit place in Nashville. Its gift store is equally grand. If you buy tickets on a particular night you can get a commemorative poster from the gift store of that night. 
Def worth a visit.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Going to the Grand Olde Opry was quite the experience especially if you pair a show with the VIP backstage tour . The cost of the tour is pricey but I soon learned why . You can book daytime tours for a lot less, but you won't experience the best in my opinion. 

 I went the same night I saw a show so the likelihood of seeing a star or performer is very high .We saw Micheal Ray , Travis Tritt, Riley Green, and Carrie Underwood's husband Mike Fisher. 

You also get to sit backstage on the stage for 2-3 songs of the first performer. The highlight of the tour for me was being behind the curtain with the countdown and that curtain rises and you see all the people, lights , performers and just take in that precious moment. It's a moment you won't forget because it's so unique, special, and unforgettable . You feel like a performer yourself for a split second .

If I had one negative to say about the tour I would say the photograph wasn't very good because of the lighting but other than that really enjoyed being VIP for 30 minutes. 

Money well spent to be an extra part of history. Seeing a show there is amazing as well. I saw a show the Tuesday before CMA Fest and it was a fantastic lineup.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Food was excellent! I had some appetizers in the afternoon here, then came back that same day and had the gumbo and salad. Everything was really tasty and not too expensive. The entertainment was excellent! One of my favorite places so far on my first trip to Nashville, and I'm usually not a blues/jazz fan.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: We came here on a Friday evening for dinner. We ordered drinks, mine being a Cherry Mule which was awesome!!!! The menu wasn't lying when it said "It's really good!"  We left the downtown bar scene on Saturday evening and walked back to the Flying Saucer to once again get a Cherry Mule, only to be told they were out of the ingredients! The waitress suggested the Moscow Mule instead. My husband ordered something totally different, but I went with her suggestion. A few minutes later, she came back and said they didn't have the ingredients for that either! Very disappointed. Should have stayed downtown instead of wasting the trip. So out of the 9 cocktails listed on the menu, they could not make 2 of them.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Just ok. The atmosphere here is really odd. The servers weren't super friendly and had no personality. The music selection was a combo of some decent oldies and some weird, depressing music. 

I was expecting to have a lot more beer choices based on the photos from yelp, but was disappointed. They had a large selection, but when I started looking at overall options of what I wanted to drink, didn't seem like there was anything there I really wanted to try. 

I was hungry and wanted to order food but the place was creepy overall and I just wanted to leave. I did not want to stay any longer than I had to. The whole experience was best described as "strange". 

It was an older building and it felt dark and sad. It's very rare for me to walk into a place and want to leave immediately. The area outside the main building (there were two main seating areas) seemed to have a better feel to it and was more updated, but inside, the plates on the wall were tacky and the tables and chairs were old. It reminded me of something from a haunted/ scary movie or a run down museum. I would NOT go back. 

One positive thing that I liked: The night I went, they were having specials on all pints. So my draft beer was only $3. If you can sit in the outside (covered area) and enjoy cheap (good) beer it might be worth it to go.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: This was not a good dining experience. I understand that the focal point of this place is the beer, but the dining shouldn't be neglected. We ordered the Queso fondue and some tots to share. My friend ordered a sandwich. Her fries were very stale. The celery and carrots that came with the fondue was wilted and browning. My friend's soda was flat and when she asked if she could get another, the waitresses response was, "well, all of the soda is going to be like that". Our waitress ignored our concerns about the  meal and didn't apologize at all. I'm only giving two stars because of the beer selection, otherwise. This place gets one. We should have listened to our cab driver who mentioned that this place had poor service!

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text:
As a karaoke host myself, back in NY, I have found my Tennessee homies!
This place is alive on an early summer Thursday night. I wish there was this much enthusiasm every time I ran a show in the Big Apple. But I'll hold out hope. Can't wait to sing on the stage and try to represent New York.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I didn't go inside but I walked around it's very beautiful! It's near a mall with lots of places to eat and shop.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: Redneck Riviera started in Las Vegas. We went several times a week. Loved the place and they had great bartenders. Affordable drinks and an awesome sequence saddle. We were sad when we found out it was closing. We never found another bar we liked as well as RNR. When it opened in Nashville we knew we would have to take a trip to Nashville. So here we are. Our favorite bartenders Alyssa and Brook left Vegas and came to Nashville to keep working at RNR. They are both great. I can see why Rich invited them to join him in Nashville.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
RUDOLPH Absolutely the worst show I have ever seen. I would've been laughing at it if I had not invested almost $400 on two tickets that were actually in the back of the theater. They were not 2nd market tickets, I purchased them off the official GOO website two months prior to our vacation. Ridiculous costumes and poor makeup on all. We felt sorry for the "actors" there was not a way for them to shine at all. The props looked  like a grade school play. The music was prerecorded too. We heard many people complaining.  We actually left during the intermission. It was a bad choice on my behalf but we always dreamed of going to the Grand Ole Opry.  This should have been for young children but we only saw a handful. Who can afford over a $150 tickets for kids?
Wish I didn't have to pick any stars

P.S.  I have only done reviews a handful of times and all but one was positive

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Saw this place featured on the food network.  We decided to give it a try for lunch that day.  They had immediate seating.  We sat almost right in the middle of the restaurant which made it easy to take in the decor.  We ordered the jalapeno appetizer which was amazing....a little on the hot side but flavorful.  We went with burgers for lunch which were not disappointing.  Definitely filled us up.  The vast variety of craft beers was overwhelming but we did our best to navigate the menu and choose what we thought we would enjoy.  So many options!!! If I remember correctly, you have a limit on number of beers allowed per visit.  I think it was 4, so don't plan a night out on the town and expect to get drunk here.  This is a nice place to meet up and catch up.

name: National Underground
text: Horrible Staff. Horrible Service. Horrible Selection. Horrible music. I would recommend to skip this place. Hopefully it's gone soon

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: The worst. They were supposed to be apart of a 90's bar crawl that I paid money to participate in. We get to Winners and there were no specials and no 90s music. Very disappointing. If you're not going to participate then don't sign your bar up.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Came here with coworkers and had a blast. Everyone ordered alcohol so I asked the bartender to bring me the sweetest, most candy-like drink they had. He brought me the Don't Stop the Carnival drink and after everyone tasted it half the table ordered one as well. It was definitely the best sweet drink of the night. 

I've been before but it was so long ago I didn't remember anything and wasn't yelping back then. Luckily, we all ordered and shared food (my dream!) so I got to try a TON of things. 

I found I love some of their shrimp items, but not all. I actually disliked their Coconut Shrimp which is weird because I LOVE coconut shrimp almost everywhere. The New York Strip Steak had a good flavor but it was too rough for me. I forgot I prefer a different cut. The Pretzel Sticks were just not good to me. They were doughy inside and the dipping sauce was a sharp mustard that I couldn't stand. The grilled chicken tasted a little blackened, which I didn't enjoy. Otherwise it was good. The Key West Quesadilla tasted ok by itself but I know if I could've eaten the sour cream and salsa with it (forgot to ask my coworker for some) it would've been great. 

It was a great experience to have with my coworkers. I think the drinks were the best part of the night but the food was just ok. Nothing really special. Maybe we just picked the wrong things. 

To Try:
Beach Tacos
Island Kabob

Loved: 
- Chocolate Banana Colada
- Don't Stop the Carnival (alcohol) (fav)
- French Fries
- Grilled Blackened Shrimp
- Lava Lava Shrimp (with extra sauce!)
- Ice Cream with chocolate sauce 
- Island Rice
- Key West Quesadilla (with sour cream and salsa)
- Mango Salsa

Ok: 
- 5 o'clock Somewhere (alcohol)
- Corn
- Green Beans
- Grilled Chicken Breast
- Rum Runner (alcohol)
- Sauteed Island Lime Shrimp
- Shrimp Trio
- Strawberry Margarita
- Volcano Nachos

Disliked: 
- Cilantro Lime Cole Slaw
- Crispy Coconut Shrimp
- Conch Fritters
- Horseradish-Orange Marmalade
- New York Strip Steak (medium)
- Pretzel Sticks
- Yukon Gold Loaded Mashed Potatoes

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Great hangout. Great taps with trivia. Small food selection - off on the edge of town- uber to get here not walking to other locations nearby.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Not a popular choice on Broadway since it's a chain but they have great live music just the same.  The perfect margarita gives you the most bang for your buck - all other Broadway drinks are $9, same as this one, but much weaker.  Go here and drink a few and then venture out to the local bars.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We had a great experience. Our waitress, Kiersten, was incredibly nice and friendly. She took great care of us. The 5 o'clock somewhere was a great hangover cure for the morning for my girlfriend. We would definitely come back because of Kiersten's hospitality.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Very nice arena. Came to see Drake and Future and it was wonderful. The arena is along the strip with over 20+ bars so you can have a drink or 4 (like i did) before you head to your festivities. You can check in with your phone which is very helpful. Place has so many bathrooms. Not once did i wait on a 5 mins women's bathroom line. Thank god. And Katie at the box office was a doll. I had a terrible situation with my tickets and she helped me tremendously !

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: This place rocks! Came here based on recommendation and so glad we did. The Basil Ryeman beer is a great compliment to the Impossible Veggie Burger & fries. I don't even know what was on it but boy was it good. Burger & fries was $18- so a little pricey, but enough for 2 people to split. Don't miss Tennessee Brew Works!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Awful service burger was raw when asked to be medium well. Waitress was rude dropped the food ran away dropped the check ran away. They werent even busy. Go some where else.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: I watched a college basketball game here and had some fries. They were average but the game was all right. You can see the brewing plant from the bar which is pretty cool but the tables are pretty full and depraved

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Usually not a big beer drinker but the flight here was too good of a deal not to try. Only 10 bucks for a sampler of five, it's a steal. Forgot their names but the super dark one all the way to the right of the platter was my favorite. It went down pretty well with their frog legs. Ended up buying a case of the Southern Wit and the Extra Easy after my meal. 

Overall awesome experience and a must visit place when coming to Nashville!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Every time my friends and I go downtown to bar hop we always eat here first! It is always delicious.  

I totally recommend the fish tacos..O-M-G! The best I've ever had! The fish has this magical seasoning on it with fresh cabbage and this wonderful sauce, it also has some salsa type stuff but I opt out on that. The tortilla is always warm and I seriously can't get enough. It comes with black beans which I'm not a fan of period not just theirs, I substitute fries instead! 

The only reason this place is not getting a 5 star rating is because of the long wait, which I understand a long wait when busy, but almost every time we've gone(at least 10-12 times) everything takes a long time from the drinks to the entree. 

We always get a shot of tequila and an incommunicado it's the best drink ever! With around 6 different liquors and I think 3 or 4 different juices it is simply amazing! I suggest anyone to try it, it's not too sweet but not extremely strong which can make these dangerous. You could get extremely drunk extremely quick because they taste so good without the burn of all the alcohol. 

We will be back very soon this is definitely my favorite place downtown and more so my favorite place to get fish tacos!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Stopped in on a Friday night, this place was hoppin! It's a smaller dive bar, but the band that was playing, Eskimo Brothers, could be heard from the sidewalk and drew us in! These guys were AWESOME, hillbilly county music, had the crowd engaged, and they were hilarious as well. Definitely stop in Layla's for something a little different from the rock country/cover bands.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Bridgestone Arena ushers go out of their way to make sure you're not enjoying the event you're paying good money to attend. 

My wife and I were in attendance for the Amy Schumer event and had the displeasure of dealing with the annoying ushers. My wife had her phone on the lowest brightness setting and got a notification on her phone and all she did was glance at it (we're out of town, we should be able to look at our phones in case of a family emergency). Two seconds later, some rude usher threatened to kick us out for "attempting to take pictures." We didn't have this issue the night before at the Nashville Predators & Chicago Blackhawks game. 

I'm going to do my best to avoid attending any future events at the Bridgestone Arena.

name: National Underground
text:
Growing up in the Nashville area, there was one thing that anyone from the area rarely did: go hang out on Broadway.  It's just where the annoying tourists went to buy overpriced cowboy boots and butcher the classic standards at karaoke.  Even though the city has changed a lot since then, it's one thing that remains: there remain very few good reasons to go to Broadway unless you just want to play tourist.  National Underground is one of those reasons, because it's so unlike any other bar on the street.  It's never crowded, it's very 'low-key'.  The bands are very good (the band there when I was last in, Brian Wain's Hushpuppy's Daddy, was phenomenal), I've never had to pay a cover, the beers are reasonably priced, the staff are always exceptionally nice, and it just has a really good non-pretentious vibe that is missing from its neighbors.  I've never had the food, but I am anxious to try it.

The reason it's docked a star, then? When you ask for a water, they charge you $2 and give you a 16oz bottle. No bueno, guys.  Fix that, and you'll get five stars.

name: National Underground
text: What a shit show. Waited an hour for food that never came. In the middle of a lovely city this looked cool. What a mistake. Didn't even comp us the iced tea.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Just a tourist-friendly place, in my opinion. I'm not really big on Jimmy Buffett, only being familiar with four of his songs. I like his image and style though, and that's why I chose to come here on my vacation. It's pricey, as one would expect, plus its got a decent gift shop. I'm more than happy to provide for Mr. Buffett's yacht fund (laughs). 

The food was great: I had the Cheeseburger in Paradise, with fries. I'm like Jimmy, I like mine with lettuce and tomato, a cool kosher pickle, french-fried potatoes and Heinz 57. You got to be in that state of mind! I topped it off with two Margaritas. There's not just one, but several different flavors. I chose simply the basic. The waitstaff is very friendly and they seem to love their job, which I value. Check it out if its in the city you visit!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: We loved this bar!!  The bartenders and drinks were great.  The bands were amazing.  We had a lot of fun here!  We will definitely be back to Layla's!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: when I visit Nashville,  I always eat here.  I love the beer, the food and the live singers.  I had a beer and a shrimp dish this time.  the shrimp was perfect, spicy but not too spicy.  I have had wings before and they were perfect.  the bartenders are always friendly and attentive to the customers.

name: Marathon Music Works
text:
I had never been to this venue until recently, and I am almost ashamed of myself for that.  Why haven't I been here before?!  This place is great!  Huge open loft-like space, great sound, great shows...I will be a repeat offender for sure now.
The shows here are relatively inexpensive and they have a wide variety of acts and performances.  They have two bars though the lines can get pretty long.  Unless I missed something its mostly street parking so factor that in when attending a show.  I'll be able to give a longer review after the next time I go, but I attended a Music City Burlesque show here (PS the MCB shows are fantastic and fun, I highly recommend them to one and all unless you're a seriously boring person lacking a sense of humor and are easily offended) and it was a riot.  There was some seating at this particular show, can't imagine that's the norm, but the sound was quality, the space large so you didn't feel like you were on top of everyone, and you get a pretty good view of the stage from any vantage point.  Probably some of the nicest restrooms at a musical venue ever too, as a plus.  But the lines for the bar were very long, and moved slowly, but the drinks were good and reasonably priced so I guess that kind of makes up for it.
I'll be checking out more shows here and will update this review when I do, but for now its safe to say that it's a great place to see great shows.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Great location! Located next to many fun bars and restaurants in a pretty tourist friendly part of town on Broadway. The drinks were good, but not great. However, the service was very good. We visited on a Wednesday evening and had drinks in the bar while we watched live music. The entire bar floor was being serviced by one server, who did a great job engaging with all of the guests and making sure everybody had what they needed. I can't seem to remember her name, but she was very nice. Definitely a fun place to spend your evening in Nashville!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: We stopped in for lunch and were pleasantly surprised at how delicious the food was. We had the Nashville chicken sandwich and the bbq pork, both exceeded our expectations for being at a brewery! The beer was also great! Atmosphere was good as well. The only reason this is not a five star review is because our waiter did not check on us once after we got our food and we had to go up to ask for the check. However, it didn't ruin our experience.

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
This review is for the symphony.

 The Symphony offers a ticket package for young professionals and students at a severely discounted rate. The program is called Wave Length. Being under 30 we decided to participate and buy a complete package for the classical series, which set us back $150 per person. Seriously amazing price, y'all.  The discounted rate doesn't mean that we have bad seats either, we are sitting in the orchestra towards the middle.

The classical series has been excellent so far this year. The musicians are very good and the pieces have been well played. The concerts are on Friday and Saturday nights. If it's a more popular piece, there is a Thursday performance. 

We ended up getting tickets to Handel's Messiah because we enjoyed the shows so much. The guest conductor did a great job and the choir and musicians were amazing. I can't wait to see it again next year. 

People usually dress up for Symphony performances. I would categorize it as "Sunday Best". I usually wear a nice dress or skirt. There is always at least one girl in a full length formal dress. My husband wears a jacket and tie. The center is well heated so don't worry about being cold when you are seated. 

They sell drinks that can be taken into the show. They are a little expensive but that's expected. 

I wouldn't suggest valeting because it takes forever to get your car back.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Came here before PBR at Bridgestone and I had an awful experience.  I ordered a pasta dish that was way way way too spicy. It was obvious something had gone wrong while cooking the dish.  Atmosphere is fun as expected. I just wasn't lucky enough to have a decent experience with the food.

name: National Underground
text:
The waiter was so rude it just ruined our entire experience. As three girls from NYC, we have a pretty high tolerance for rude but having just stepped off the plane, hungry and tired, we were hoping to be welcomed with a little southern hospitality. 

My one friend forgot her ID. After I and my friend showed our IDs, my friend, desperate for a beer, asked if she could show him a photo of her passport. He said no and I told him she was 25. He still refused (which is fine, I respect that), but what really pissed me off was he patronizingly said "yep, it's the law in the United States. You have to be 21 to drink." Thanks, asshole. I had no clue. 

He nickel and dimed us for everything. We ordered water and he came back with BOTTLED -- what?! My friend ordered a burger and he charged her for fries (who serves a burger with chips) and asked her what kind of cheese she wanted -- charged for that too. 

My friend and I split BBQ wings and a veggie burger. Both mediocre. 

Total tourist trap, rude rude waiter and mediocre food. Bye.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
A lot of great bands play here, don't get me wrong. I just don't want to pay $9 a beer to partake while I watch them. haha. Everything food or drink oriented is grossly overpriced. 

I saw the Black Keys here recently and had a fantastic time, it just wasn't quite the same as the Ryman or Cannery Ballroom. The view was so-so and it lacks in character and atmosphere. However, when I saw the Summerland Tour last year we had floor seats and it was so much nicer. If you can afford it, go as low as you can to the floor.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The service was fabulous the margaritas were wonderful. We had the volcano nachos it was large enough for at least four my only complaint was that the toppings weren't throughout the entire dish and it wasn't hot barely luke warm. I would order again

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Bridgetown is the home of the Nashville predators as well as an excellent music venue for large acts.   Bring lots of money as the adult beverages are extremely pricey.   Most of the seating is excellent just avoid the top deck

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Service was great! We had had a long day of birthday celebrations and exploring Nashville, so it was refreshing to sit down and enjoy ourselves. We had a huge table so service expectations weren't high but they were definitely met! Plus they had the balloon artist (who was also on stilts?!) make a birthday balloon hat for our 21 year old! The beer is surprisingly cheap too! Food was great and they were accommodating on my changes.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Great gluten free menu. The service was fabulous and the live music was awesome! Definitely recommend.

name: National Underground
text: Great experience. Had some great local brews and a fantastic burger! Unique vibe, good music, definitely different from most bars on Broadway. The best places are normally hidden away holes in the wall, and this place attests to that! Will definitely be returning.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Really really small and crowded.  If you are here for the band, get to the front of the bar because you can't hear or see the band back at the bar.

name: Nashville Symphony
text: What a gorgeous venue. I was incredibly impressed with the architecture and structure of the building. The food was excellent and the performance was fantastic. Definitely worth every penny!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Though it was a little pricey, our group had such a positive experience.  We walked in as a group of 18 without a reservation knowing we would likely have to split up.  After only a 25 minute wait (while we grabbed drinks at the bar) we were seated all together on the second floor.  The wait staff was quick and attentive.  There was another large party that sat near us and placed their order at a similar time, so there was some confusion with our food coming out.  A few of us had to wait a while, but everyone was so apologetic and even brought out 3 dessert platters for our entire table.  Great wait staff, friendly hostess, and accommodating management.  Get the fish tacos. We will be back!

name: Nashville Symphony
text: Another fantastic Schermerhorn experience!  Registered for "SoundCheck" for students and got some incredible tickets for Mendelssohn's Elijah for $10 a piece.  Best kept secret in town!  For less than the price of a movie ticket I got to listen to over two beautiful hours of orchestral and choral music.  Absolutely incredible-go check them out!  Breaks my heart that there were any empty seats!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Best beer in Tennessee hands down. My girlfriend usually only enjoys bud light but when she came here she loved every beer that they had on tap.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I have a love/hate relationship with the Bridgestone arena. 

I LOVE going to see hockey games here, I hate seeing concerts here! I understand that there are some musical groups that require a large venue for their popularity and/or stage show, but it never sounds very good to hear a live performer at this venue! The only redemption for live shows at Bridgestone is if you have seats on the floor. I have found that that helps improve the quality of the sound and experience.
