The wait staff was awesome!

The sausage, ham and onion pizza not so much. As one of the ingredients was definitely stale. The wings only came in 1 degree of heat and were nothing more than Kroger drummets with Frank's wing sauce.  The kitchen or chef put no thought or effort into that and it shows.

Ill definitely be back, but will give them a few months to mature.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Legit, the Chuck E Cheese of "honky Tonks". It was quite amusing (very clean and large, loved that) and fun at first and then the line dancing lessons started. I wish i knew the girls name (it was a Friday night, blonde girl, hat). The line dance teacher could not have been less enthusiastic. She bordered on mean and condescending to the point where complete strangers were rolling their eyes, complaining and sitting down. People are in Nashville to have fun not to be treated like line dance idiots. At one point I started counting the number of times "the teacher" rolled her eyes. This is also the same girl (along with a number of men) the saloon adds to the dance floor when it's empty to create buzz. Her buzz was basically resting bitch face and a severe lack of authenticity and care. Would be nice if the person representing this place on stage and the dance floor at least faked it. It was discouraging. We ended up leaving and laughing about it, considering that she may have put her two weeks notice in and no longer cared. A word to the wise, and also to this management...you need a better cheerleader...Nashville is about music and show biz...let's see a better show.

name: Big Machine Brewery & Distillery
text: This was the first bar that I had went to in Nashville, and I'm so happy that it was my first experience because not only was our bartender great and our frozen vodka lemonades needed but it was overall just a great place to start our weekend vacation at. At the time my friend and I had went it was slower and we were able to converse a good conversation with our bartender and the people next to us and they gave us all the information on what spots to go too and give us the 411 on the town. I wish I would've came back to the spot before I had left but due to it being such a short vacation and seeing so many things in just two days I wasn't able to but when I do go back to Nashville it will be the first but I go to, this place has my heart

name: Big Machine Brewery & Distillery
text:
5 stars on the delightful whiskey! So smooth and delicious. Their vodka is not bad, either. We stopped in for the tasting and the first gal that helped us behind the bar was great - she knew all about the product and was super friendly. 

However! She departed and we ordered the lemonade slushy from another bartender who should not be working in the service industry! We ordered two slushies with floaters. She produced them and then said they were for another patron. We were confused as we were the only people sitting at the bar, but we said we had ordered slushies as well, so she made two more for us. She managed to spill the second one all over the bar. She cleaned it up but did not refresh the vodka floater on it. No mind, the extra alcohol was probably not needed. So we're sitting at the bar and enjoying and the two original slushies, the ones that were for another patron, were sitting on the bar, lonely. Then the bartender looks at Larry S., who had been sitting there the entire time, and said, "Oh, these are your slushies". So Larry said that we just wanted two slushies, that was all that we had ordered. I mean, they didn't charge us for the extra drinks, but I'm not sure how the bartender screwed up a simple order for two drinks when there were no other patrons at the bar! 

The drinks were delicious and produced no hangover and we enjoyed the nice refreshment on a hot day.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This was my place 20 years ago.  I brought my family and it was terrible. I'm writing this review in my hotel room feeling nauseous and wondering if it's going to turn into food poisoning.  I hope it passes but I will never step foot back in that place.  Nashville has grown and Rippys is no longer on the radar.  Too many awesome places. Disappointing.  I have lots of good memories there.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Great service, fun place, food was so-so. It was good, not great. We asked for hot-hot chicken and it was quite mild, so if you want the spice, ask for the hottest they have! They introduced me to a tasty local beer that I really liked; Hap n' Harry's...a light lager.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: YUMMO is all I have to say! The service was great, the food was great and the beer was awesome!! Live music too, what more could you ask for?!?!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: We really loved it here! Great band! Great drinks! Right in the heart of downtown Nashville... highly recommend!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
We went there 2 times. Once for dinner and a second time because they had a great band playing. 

Dinner. I had the pulled chicken plate. Holy hell you get a ton of chicken. It was awesome and this place is saved for when I go back. I'll now be in Nashville 3 times a year and this place is on the "must stop at" list. They have 2 bars (maybe more I don't know) I was at both. They have different bands playing in both areas. 

Once time we sat and ate and another we sat and drank. It's a cool spot with great servers and great bartenders. Bookmark this place if you are heading to Nashville.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I think Wildhorse has a lot of potential to be a go-to destination for people who want to line dance.  However, I think their charging a cover really deterred people from coming in.  

The night started off fun--there was a good crowd.  We were having a ton of fun but then looked around about an hour and a half later and saw that pretty much everyone had left.  

So just as crowds make larger crowds, the same is true on the opposite end.  We didn't want to be in an empty place on a Saturday Night (around midnight, which should be peak time).  So we left... 

The sight was actually kind of sad -- A good band playing for a completely empty dance hall.  I actually felt bad leaving.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Quite honestly this could probably be a magnificent place for Nashville. Unfortunately they need to work on their customer service. Everyone walks around like they hate their job and it shows in their service. Ordered food to go. Jake helped at the bar. Not the friendliest. Couldn't even offer water while I waited. Floor was a mess. Looked like they drug the trash across it and never mopped it up. Had the catfish. Food was decent but over priced for what your receive.  Of course that may just be Nashville.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We had a semi-private cocktail hour and dinner in the high top area and it was fantastic! The food was delicious and the servers - Seth and Rob - were so attentive and pleasant. We couldn't be happier!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Upon entering the restaurant, the sound of the kick drum and blare of the guitar resonated throughout. It matched the aesthetic that was presented with images of music legends all across the establishment. The live band added a great deal of flavor to the experience, albeit the noise was loud.

Our group ordered the crawfish bread as a starter, which was an excellent decision. The light crunch and flaky texture made the bread a great appetizer. The crawfish also added some variety of flavor to the bread.

Also, our table decided to order multiple pizzas to split in order to limit the cost and encourage trying a variety of types of pizzas. One negative of this restaurant is that it is most likely not meant for small groups because you would be limited to one pizza or having to pay $1 extra to customize your pie. We ordered the rainbow warrior, carnivore, and the alfredo pizza. The alfredo was easily the best tasting, followed by the carnivore and the rainbow warrior. If you are a skeptic of the trend towards adding pineapples to pizzas, then you will not enjoy this one.

One major drawback with the restaurant was its inconsistency in service. Upon asking for my water to be refilled, I was surprised as the waiter spilled water on my leg in an attempt to refill my glass. A simple mistake that could have easily been avoided if the waiter took his time. Overall, the pizza and bread was good; however, if you do not like loud live music or have a small group, this venue may not be for you.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
living in Memphis for 3 years this is not very good Tennessee BBQ 
Staff was a little more concern with their phones then my service 
Sat on both the first floor and second floor and the music was good but I would not recommend the BBQ

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Good pizza. Nice people. I'd go back.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Mom was so excited for the dinner and show to hear all of the classic country legend songs. Worst customer service! Show was so loud! Need earplugs. Barely any songs that we knew. Can't believe my mom paid so much for a show that could  and should have been in Las Vegas! Go see Grand Ole Opry for this price and see some good performers. Couldn't get a refund once show started-how could we know this would be such a bad experience?! ?!

name: Nashville Palace
text: This is my Favorite place when visiting Nashville, the Nashville Palace band is fantastic the staff is friendly and the food is good.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Had the opportunity to dine at NashHouse...  the apps and salad were great but the pork shank was even better!  If you have a chance, stop on by!  #TTFG!  Trust the Fat Guy!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: After being so disappointed with FGL house we thought let's go to a tried-and-true Nashville legacy and that is the Wildhorse Saloon... I had been there over 20 years ago and this place has only gotten better!! It has the largest dance floor and all of Nashville, you can learn line dancing steps and also their food is top notch with awesome service the most friendly atmosphere! We had a blast! We walked in at about 9 o'clock or 9:30 PM on Monday night no reservations nothing just walked right in I had the ribs which were great my daughter had the chicken which was absolutely awesome incredibly tender phenomenal the servers were just awesome and we had an awesome surprise of a live concert going on! Josh Mirenda was performing and he was incredible! We got to meet him and his mom and it was just phenomenal atmosphere! I will definitely go back again the next time we're in Asheville my husband would love it! A definite two thumbs up! Prices were great too!!!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Very much looked forward to trying out this new place--attached to the Cambria hotel--before a Preds game. We are always looking for good options for a pre-game meal, and there are plenty east of the arena to choose from. This place just two blocks west of the arena showed promise but failed in the food. 

Service was prompt, friendly. Beer selection emphasized solid local choices. Thus far so good.

But then the food. The better half found the veggie plate lacking in taste but adequate. the Cowboy burger was another matter--when it arrived it was burnt--perhaps the driest piece of beef I have had in sometime. We were shocked-- the waiter asked "pink or not"-- we clearly said pink. He acknowledged that but then the kitchen had such poor oversight that order preference meant nothing--for a $16 burger. 

Game time neared so sending it back was not an option--a reality well apparent to the kitchen on a busy game night. So they sent out a ruined meal. Shame on them--they not only disappointed us but let down their waiters who were working a big room as efficiently as possible. 

Imagine I will stay on the east side of the arena in the future before arena events.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The best ribs around. My squeester and I came here to eat after partying a bit.....will come back before leaving the area.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Ribs were excellent. Nice dry rub. Always a nice atmosphere with good live music. I've eaten here three or four times and the service is always friendly and fast. Great place to eat before hitting the bars!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Just had a beer but the food did look good.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Ugh, the Wildhorse Saloon is going downhill, quickly, and it makes me sad! This used to be a staple part of our annual Nashville trip, yet the past few visits have been nothing short of disappointing.

For starters, the place is HUGE - three floors, to be exact, but they never seem to have enough staff to keep the place running smoothly. What's the point of a restaurant/bar that big if you are not going to utilize it to the full potential! 

We walked in with a party of 10 and were told it would be a 15 minute wait - 40 minutes later, we were sat. I have no problem with waiting for a table, especially given our large group, however, the issue is how those 40 minutes were spent... waiting in line at the bar! There were two bartenders on a Friday evening and it was complete chaos. Apparently, people who don't want to wait for a table can choose to sit in the open seating area and can order food at the bar... it really messes up the entire system.

Our service was decent, no complaints. I always brag about Wildhorse having the best fried pickles in Nashville - after this last visit, my friends and family think I'm crazy! The pickles were soggy and all stuck together in one big pickle lump.

Pulled pork was fine, yet things just seemed over price. Sad to say that I don't know if I'll return to this once favorite place of mine.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Honestly best service and experience we had in Nashville. Being a bachelor party of 20 was not always easy but the Nashville paLace was the sweetest! Very accommodating and food was excellent. It was not very busy during the day on Thursday when we went but we got to listen to live music and sit on their patio in the sun. Highly recommend.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Food was pub fare, and as to be expected it was okay.

The upstairs has an awesome atmosphere and there was a live concert going on so it was basically like being outside being able to listen to it. You felt like you were outside with all the openness of the bar. The bartenders were all very nice and friendly and talked with us. Everyone at the bar sitting near us were all out of town too and they were friendly as well. Kind of expensive, as to be expected since it was on Broadway. 

Overall, great experience and friendly, quick service.

name: Nashville Palace
text: This is by far the worst place to eat in Nashville. We ordered the Chicken Fried Steak bites, Meatloaf, Quesadilla and Pork Chops and they were all extremely dry without taste. I do not see how people have rated this 4* other than the live music. If you are looking for food, stay away from this place .

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Don't bother going here for an early dinner with kids. The bouncer (that alone should be a warning sign ) will only allow a certain number of people in. They actually closed the door after our kids entered and didn't let the parents follow immediately after because it wasn't "part of the process"... what?!?!  I suppose there is a specific number that's allowed to enter at a time but regardless you can't separate kids from the parents when we were right behind them. After that experience (& escalating to a manager), our group of 20 immediately left & walked a couple blocks over to Martin's BBQ where we had good service & complimentary moon pies during our 5 minute wait.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Live music and line dancing, a fun night out! It's massive and there's tons of seating, I had a great time trying to learn how to line dance and joining in with everyone.

name: The Cobra
text: After living in east Nashville for a year I finally made it to this place. I liked it a lot more than I thought I would! I was expecting a super grunge, dirty, small dark bar. But I was wrong! This place is big! You walk in to the bar area which is spacious in itself, then there is the next room over which has access to the back yard area for smoking/hanging out when it's warm, there is also a few old school games in here such as Pac-Man and a few pinball machines as well, plus a pool table. The third room over (which has a door separating it) is the space for the bands to play. All rooms are spacious and not cramped! There is a great vibe which I've yet to find anywhere else in Nashville. The bartenders were sweet and not too busy on a weekend night. Great spot to hear some live music and hang out with friends!

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
The Tennessee Performing Arts Center (TPAC) hosts some really great events, musicals, the Nashville ballet and opera, conferences, comedy shows and more. The Center houses multiple theaters with varying capacities. The main lobby connect is clean and spacious. There is a snack bar and also several bar areas to purchase beer, wine and even some mixed drinks. There are multiple entrances as well so that you can access the building from either street you are on since the building is so large. There are also several restrooms and the facilities are all clean as well.

In the past year that I've been living in Nashville I've been able to visit twice so far (and bought tickets for a third that unfortunately I couldn't make it to). I went to the 2017 TedX Conference in the Andrew Jackson Hall and the Banff Film Festival hosted by Climb Nashville in the James K. Polk Theater. I would highly recommend going to either of these events if they ever return to the TPAC. The TedX Conference was two days of amazing Ted talks, some even from Nashville locals like Vanderbilt professors, radio talk show host Bobby Bones and celebrity chef Maneet Chauhan. The Andrew Jackson Hall is beautiful and well-kept. The Banff Film Festival originated in Banff, Canada and travels around the U.S. hosting short films that were submitted to the festivals all with the themes of outdoor sports and recreation. 

Even if you aren't so much interested in traditional performing arts like ballet or opera they have so many cool things that would really interest anyone (unless you don't like to leave your house). I look forward to seeing what they have here and I think it's one of the highlights of the Nashville cultural scene.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Came in after Packers/ Titans game,  it is pretty clear that most of the places down here were not prepared for the influx of business.  Out of Miller Lite, what?  Other beers warm.  Server trying her hardest, but the place was packed, tough to keep up.  Food came out fast, how is it that it was barely warm, tasted good, just not hot.  Thinking it would be a better experience if it wasn't so crazy, at the end of the day, we were lucky to find a place to sit down.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
I highly recommend this restaurant.. be sure and get the appetizer
of the spoon fries, OMG..they are to die for!!!  
Service was excellent, the staff very friendly and courteous. 
Food was very good and plenty of it, southern portions are generous. 
Huge TV's all over, friendly, roomy atmosphere. 

We will be back!!

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
I had been here years ago to see White Christmas but I didn't remember much about the location. I knew I was sitting in the highest section and still saw everything, even though the angle wasn't great. When I heard the sequel to Phantom was in town I needed to go back. 

I saw Phantom in San Fransisco back in the 1990s on my honeymoon. My anniversary was coming up the week before Love Never Dies started in Nashville so it seemed a natural opportunity to go check out TPAC again. 

This time I got tickets in the second level, the Grand Loge. I tried to get Orchestra but they sold out by the time I got my tickets. 

I was really bummed that I couldn't find seat views of each level, so here are my thoughts about the two upper levels: Get center if you can. Everything is going to be small and slightly off presentation. The stage is framed, but if you're way up you can see over the top of the frame and less of the rear of the stage. If you're on the side you also see more backstage on one side and less stage on the other. This may make sense conceptually, but for some scenes this will make a big difference. Grand Loge is much better than the Upper Tier. And the front seats are better than the rear ones. The price difference was about $10-20 a ticket to go from upper, rear, side to Grand Loge, center, front. Definitely worth it if you can't get Orchestra seats. 

The building is nice, if a little too modern for my tastes for Broadway. I love the classical theater look better, but this is serviceable. You can buy drinks and snacks to take in as well. I tried wine and water. Both were overpriced, as was expected, but the wine was pretty good, if generic. There are stairs and an elevator. Bathrooms are available in the basement level and inside, once inside the theater. 

(If this matters, there are several Pokestops within range of the theater. You can reach them while you wait. But not once the show starts, please. ) 

As for the show itself - I was disappointed. [SPOILERS] The Phantom was a bad guy who, in the end, makes one good decision in letting Christine go. He's a tragic character who makes evil, selfish decisions and Christine realizes that by the end. But LND starts with Phantom being the exact same evil, selfish person but Christine falls for him anyway...? And what about the child? That never happened in Phantom. If it did, it happened when he kidnapped Christine and she was under his spell. That makes him even more evil! But the worst thing about LND is that the music is boring. Phantom is iconic. LND is bland. The title song was not memorable, IMO. Reprise for more than a second (if you must make a sequel). That's why we are there, right? Obviously, this is my opinion, but as someone who has seen the film, seen real Broadway cast members, knows most of the words to every song and who watched the movie the night before I was so disappointed. 

Finally, about parking. I did valet because I didn't know the area. I won't do it again. It was $25 plus tip. I waited about 45 minutes for my car after I was standing outside. That's after I handed in my ticket at the line inside. There was parking for $10 across the street in a garage. I'll do that next time. 

TPAC is a nice venue, with a good stage and good prices. Obviously shows are hit or miss, but i's great that they are coming bigger shows recently. I'd definitely recommend it and will be going back.

name: Houston Station
text: This was our second event at the Houston Station it was great. Such a beautiful venue and the staff is great...friendly and very helpful.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Love this bar!!! First time in Nashville and it was awesome, on a Sunday too!!! Bands were AMAZING.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Date night at Woolworth on 5th. This is in the old Woolworth's building downtown where my date used to shop as a kid. It was also the site of the first sit-ins during the Civil Rights movement. There's a faux lunch counter as an ode to the past. The terrazzo floors are impeccably restored. The vibe is Art Deco and the background music Percy Faith.

This is another TomKats creation, so the menu has many a splendored thing. I had the predictable fried chicken with green beans (hint: they also own Loveless.) My date had Southern vegetables: okra, black-eyed peas, mashed potatoes. All in the name of comfort food.

Our server was from Athens, Georgia, and too young to realize our interest in the building (check the period wallpaper in the basement restrooms.) You step outside looking for Corvairs and Oldsmobiles. They have valet but recommend parking at the library (which has an impressive Civil Rights Room no one knows about.)

You'll leave Woolworth full--of food and righteousness.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I wanted to love Tootsie's but just couldn't.  It is a three level bar with a stage on all three levels.  It is one of Nashville's famous spots and we were looking forward to enjoying it.  Unfortunately it was just not for me.  It reminded me of a fraternity house and was absolutely filthy from top to bottom.  I would fear ordering anything from their kitchen.  Good looking waitresses with skimpy cut t-shirts and lively music keep the crowds coming in.  You can find space during the afternoon, but come night it is shoulder to shoulder.   If you are looking for a wild time on the strip and don't worry about contact diseases (lol) it may be your place.  The best thing here is the music, but we found many other little honkytonks up and down the strip that were clean and still offered a lively crowd and good music.

name: The Stone Fox
text: I love this place!  Quintessential hipster hangout.  I definitely love the black velvet Burt Reynolds.  The place reminds me of a cross between the old Iguana and what 12th and Porter used to be like for those "of a certain age" who remember when Jodie Faison ran the best places in town.  Stone Fox has a great beer selection and I'll be back to try out the weekend brunch.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
All I have to say is Bluegrass Brunch. Food is delicious, atmosphere is rowdy at 10am. Did I mention they have bottomless mimosas? Great place for brunch if you're looking to let loose on the weekend.

I have also been here for evening cocktails in the cellar a couple of times on the weekends. Very unique atmosphere, nicely designed and laid back. Vastly different from the party upstairs, but in a good way.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Save your money !  Extremely over rated and I have been in the restaurant industry for over 30 consecutive years.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
My food was good ( peppered ribs) but the rest of our party did not enjoy the meal. Fried chicken was very dry, pulled pork can found much better around town. 
The atmosphere was very loud, and the acoustics in here allow you to hear everyone's conversation. Definitely not a quiet meal by any sense of the word.
Waitress seemed tired and annoyed right off the start. Not very attentive, nor deserving of the included gratuity.
Drinks were mediocre at best.

name: SongBird Tours
text: We had so much fun with these guys! It was informative but also very light hearted. They played about 10 songs throughout the tour. Trey and Taylor are both amazingly talented. You need to check this out if you are new to Nashville!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Really fun atmosphere! Loved that there were so many different areas of the bar with live music. It can get a bit crowded depending on when you are there- definitely worth checking out though

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I just ate the best grilled cheese of my life. Also they have live music that is the PERFECT volume. Not too loud not too quiet. Definitely recommend!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Best burgers and homemade hand cut fries on Broadway! More than just burgers on the menu. Fast homemade affordable friendly service! Takeout or dine in!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Lots of bands playing, one on each level and we went on a Sunday! Service was great, we were waited on as soon as we set down and she continued to check on us.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Loved hanging out on the patio and having drinks but 2nd floor bathroom is a bit nutty...the attendant continually barked instructions to those using the bathroom and sprayed huge amounts of glade air freshener into the top "vent" area if she felt people were taking too long (fortunately I just witnessed this vs experiencing it --- guess I was quick enough)! My friends went to the bathroom after and I understand this round the attendant was demanding tips...Get rid of the attendant concept - it's 2017!

name: True
text: This place is fun! We stayed here and Melissa at the bar is awesome. Took us a little while to get our food but the wings were good. Wings are so easy to screw up so that was impressive. I have nothing bad to say about True!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Our chicken fingers were served raw. They did make us new ones, but did not offer any concessions on the first. I was pretty disappointed. I would think food safety would be a big concern for them, but they just played it off like this was normal.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
The Stone Fox is exactly that. A stone cold fox. Too good to be true!

I've been here a few times now. Haven't sat inside yet, because it appears that we only go to the SF when the weather is perfect!  The first time was mid-day, and we grabbed a beer on the back porch, which was fantastic! I love that there is plenty of seating and that there is a little mini garden growing on the fence. I also love that the beer selection - while fairly limiting - was very satisfying. Great options.

The second time I went here, I enjoyed a nice meal on the front porch.  The waitress was a little all over the place, but she was really nice and the food was great. Boyfriend and I split a burger + a kale salad, and both were more than I was expecting out of bar food. I really wanted to try the fried pickles, but I'll save those for another time.

If you're looking for a great porch, a delicious craft beer, and a fun bar (check out their events - super cool stuff going on here!), this should be your new favorite local pub. I know it's mine!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
This is a shining beacon amidst what is otherwise a pretty bleak offering of cool hangouts in West Nashville. Lots of really great beer on tap at totally reasonable prices, and the food is damn tasty. The fish and grits was really fresh and just the right spice level to keep you coming back for more.

While the featuring of local talent is often fun, I do sometimes wish there weren't as many nights requiring cover charges as there are. I got stuck paying a $12 cover on a Thursday night of all nights, when all I really wanted to do was drink some beer. Of course, this was really my own fault. My advice: do your research and check their calendar before you go. 

I continue to be a Stone Fox fan and will be back soon!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Poorly managed line up process that leaves you wondering if they let people continue to line up so they can have a huge line outside. They truly give not one fox about the people standing outside because they are going to fill their club no matter what. 

Another reviewer called them pretentious and that is exactly what they are. Go late if you only want a t-shirt and sit in your car until the line disappears.  Not worth the waiting

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Great crowd, music and $5 pitchers. A can't miss if you are in Nashville.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Any spot with a tribute dish to the all-vegetarian spot where my mom waitressed long before I obtained personhood (holla @ The Laughing Man) has a special place in my heart.

More recently, their veggie burger gained a special place in my stomach. The kale salad made a special place for itself in my wallet... not enough flair in that bowl o' leaves to warrant  an eight dollar price tag. The burger is definitely worth its weight in really good veggie burger worth, though.

Less importantly (but most distractingly), their staffcandy has an imaginary special place in my phone (seriously I want half your phone numbers) and the decor has equal hipster-appeal.

In a nutshell: trendy, tasty food, funky fresh interior, good-lookin' people, and a bonus kitschy venue. Bring your friend from Portland, your thick-rimmed glasses, and an appetite for beets and black beans.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great live entertainment when you walk in and upstairs! Lots of fun and great talent. Best margarita in town :-)

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Fun place during the week-- good place to spot celebs of all genres -if that's your thing. Way packed on the wknd and drinks are pricey but I don't mind paying for a good time once in awhile! And a must go when u have visitors in town!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
The Paradise Park Trailer resort is located in the heart of the action in downtown Nashville. With so many venues playing great music, what sets this place apart is it's delicious bar menu. With bar classics like Burgers and Tater Tots, what caught my interest was the Corn Dogs and Fritos Pie!

While described as a Dive Bar, it was one of the cleanest dive bar I've been too. Even with carpeting, there was no stale beer smell.  On stage there was a cover band belting out 90s and Country classics.

Be sure to stop by and check the Mullet Hall of Fame and hit the picture booth!

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
Great place for quiet study while enjoying a nice cup of coffee, EXCEPT Tuesday nights after 7-8:30 PM. They were holding some kind of presentation in the front room and it was EXTREMELY noisy. It seems they'll be holding it every Tuesday nights. 

Note: The presenter said there'll be Food Truck service at The Well at 7PM on June 19th 

The restroom here is only better than the ones in LA's China Town (if you considered it's a restroom and not a house of horror) 

Tips: Working outlets are in the front room. Wear a light sweater because it's always cold inside!


2013/#33

name: Tin Roof
text: This is the only bar downtown where the tables and walls aren't sticky and old. Very clean, rustic and modern. They have two stages (front and back), and the brands that we saw didn't disappoint either night vs finding a hit or miss band trying to hop around all the other crusty bars. Yes, the other bars are vintage and have character- if it's your first time in Nashville you still should go check them out. However, ending the night at the Tin is probably the best way to go.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Very good food, but my wife saw a kitchen workers leave the restroom without washing her hands, we are never eating there again.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I loved it... thanks to my hosts...I was able to book seats.... 7 venue..... the artists were so down to earth and made funny remarks / conversations an awesome form tof entertainment.  I felt the same vibes as well did watching Nashville ...and grateful thankfull for the chance to experience.  The waitresses were awesome.  The food amazing, though I realised that outlr sweet potato fries may have been slightly burnt comparing them to the lady next door.  Still loved the place,  look forward to some day visiting again.  Thank

name: The Stone Fox
text: This place is decent. Indeed, will return to explore the inside seating area that appears to be recently renovated.  The breakfast food includes a variety of options with plenty of ways to mix up your order do that you can try new things.  I am a northerner so after moving to the south I had to try lots of different preparations of biscuits and gravy and grits.  Therefore I feel qualified at this point to evaluate these dishes.  B and g were good but needed to be warmed up a little. Cheesy grits needed more cheese and pepper.  Omelet was overdone according to my partner; however I did not try it and he's really picky.  I will come again.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Så otrendig så det är super trendigt! Avskalat inredning med lite medvetna sunk vibbar är dekoren här. LP skivomslag från 70-tals pop töntar som Captain & Tennille och Eddie Rabbit pryder baren. Enkla bord och stolar à là amerikansk köksstandard utgör möblemanget här. De verkar ha glimten i ögat här och vet förmodligen att klientelet kommer hit inte för att titta på tjusig, genomtänkt inredning utan de kommer hellre för musikunderhållningen eller bara för att umgås med andra här. Kvällen jag själv besökte var för Jonathan Richman på den lilla scenen. Härligt trång konsertlokal med något hundratal besökare som bara njöt av musiken och showen här. Bra, trevlig och behjälplig service.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
I am currently at the Bobby Jones Gospel show and this event was very misleading from the advertisement.  The tickets that my family & I purchased advertised the show from 1-3pm.  I traveled to meet family from Kentucky and be here by 12:45pm. Only to be told that the doors open at 1pm and show starts at 2pm.

Then once seated in the New Era Ballroom I Ordered the 2 pigs small bites only to be told by the bartender that she didn't know if any of the small bites were available.  She later brought me the small entree and it was ice cold.    Who in their right mind would eat ice cold pulled pork and ice cold corn bread?  

I am very disappointed in the overall service of the restaurant and also the food selection.  What a disappointment to an overly hyped up new restaurant in Nashville.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Go if you can get tickets! I was extremely elated to score tickets to a show. This glorious cafe is a must visit landmark.The club is famous (also featured on the hit show "Nashville") for intimate, acoustic music performed by some established ..some upcoming singers & songwriters... so you might be witnessing/hearing songs here for the first time before they go-on to land their record deal and become famous (Taylor Swift was discovered here).

The singers sing to a small audience (seats about 100 people) The Bluebird has two shows a night, dinner is available at both shows ..Monday nights are Open Mic...

Artists in the songwriters circle who performed that  night were Scot Sax, grammy winning songwriter his songs performed by Faith Hill and Tim McGraw... his wife, Susie Brown and Korby Lenker (who was my favorite... his songs my little life and forbidden fruit... OMG outstanding! ) and a newbie Anthony De Costa.

There is a cover charge of $10 per person for food and drinks... they have a great menu and desserts too.

It was one of the greatest experiences of my life!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: On our trip to Nashville, every one kept telling us "you have to go to Tootsie's," and now I understand why. They had, by far, the best band we saw at any bar on Broadway that week. The bar was packed, but the bartenders were very quick and, like everyone else we encountered, incredibly friendly. The drinks were reasonably priced, the crowd was great, and we had a blast dancing the night away! I would come back to Nashville just to go here again!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I met some friends here to celebrate a friend's birthday, and I just was not wow-ed by the experience. We went on Sunday for brunch, so the place was packed. Despite two people in our group arriving early, they would not let us take a table until the entire party was present. As a result, even once we were all there we still ended up waiting close to 40 minutes before we could sit down. 

The drinks here are really good! I would highly recommend the strawberry lemonade sangria. It is a nice, refreshing, summer drink and they are not shy with the alcohol. Just a heads up, it can take awhile to get your drink. I think I waited about 10-15 minutes for both rounds of sangria that I ordered. 

For my meal, I ordered the Andouille hash, which comes with potatoes, Andouille sausage, peppers, onions, two fried eggs on top, and a spicy hollandaise sauce. They were a little skimpy with the sausage; I only had about 5 or 6 pieces of sausage in my meal, which was irritating since it was supposed to be the star of the dish. The so-called spicy hollandaise sauce was also not spicy at all. The portion itself was also pretty small. For $12 I expected more. 

I would be curious to try The Sutler again for lunch or dinner, and I could definitely see coming back here for drinks. They earned 3 stars for having good drinks, a fun atmosphere, and live music, but lost points for small portions, less than stellar food, and mediocre service.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
HORRIBLE MANAGEMENT!!! If I could give them a 0 star I would. Waited in line in the sweltering weather of 95 degrees with many other fine people, patiently for over an hr. To be told several times by security that we would be getting in, the line ended after us. All the while watching people coming in, being told that they were at capacity, turning people away, and watching grown women with their teenage daughters manipulating the musicians to let them get in early with them, even though they were NOT REALLY WITH THEM!! The security and management team let this happen even though, there were many of us that did NOT get in who communicated to them what had happened. They did NOTHING... they said we could go in and buy merchandise, take a few pictures, but not stay!! 
If they would have told us, we would not be getting in, we would have left instead of waiting. I would NOT support this venue for ANY occasion!! The management is horrible! Did not even offer to compensate or make things right for the 26 people they miscounted that should have been able to get into the venue!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: My review is based on the band I saw here. SO GOOD!! They did rock covers with a female singer. Her voice was AMAZING. We went here towards the end of our night...before we arrived I was getting ready to go home, but just had to stay to hear her sing. It was on the second floor. It was pretty crowded but there was enough space to keep a bit of space between you and the next stranger. Unfortunately, I searched online and could not find the name of the band. I would definitely come here again if in town hoping I would see this band again!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
First trip to Nashville ... So of course we had to check this place out.

This place packed 'em in like sardines. Way too crowded for my liking. Nothing was open up front, so we ended up going to the back upstairs. We liked the music in back much better as well. The gal on the fiddle was absolutely killing it. Very crowded bar but the bartenders did the best they could.

Had a few rounds but soon left after that to check out more of the Nashville scene.

name: Tin Roof
text: Drawn by the music as we were walking on Broadway. This is a big venue and not too crowded inside. Service was friendly and band was playing mainstream music.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I only gave three stars since we didn't eat here.  We came to see The Band Oklahoma and had cocktails.  Our waitress was excellent.  She was also very knowledgeable in the beer selection.  What I really enjoyed was the sound.  Usually these places are so loud with bands however the acoustics here are great.  It was a really good atmosphere.  Can't wait to go back.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Here with a couple of girlfriends, a place I would never have chosen but glad they did, I just liked it the minute I walked in, an upscale saloon with a stage at one end.  The food surprised me, we shared plates and it was all good - hot livers and gizzards on white bread, sprout hash and a shrimp dish, enough.  The cocktails were tasty.  The mood relaxed.  I felt the waitress was a little over friendly, honestly I am just not that interested in listening to them witter on about themselves especially when there is food to be eaten but that's just intolerant ole me.  I really enjoyed my experience here.  We hit the bar downstairs afterwards for another cocktail.  It is large with sofas and more of a loungy feel.   They think it is speakeasy but seriously the music is so loud that is is anything but that.  There were very few people down there and after asking for it to be turned down we were finally driven out - just the totally wrong style of music for 8.00pm .  Price point was very affordable for upstairs and downstairs.  All in all a really nice surprise.

name: Tin Roof
text: We were down in Nashville this past week and stopped at Tin Roof for lunch our first day. We went back every day after that. The bartenders were outstanding especially Ryan, JT, Josh, Ward, and Alex. I would highly recommend checking the place out. Drinks were awesome and so was the food for reasonable prices.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: A dive bar, in a bad way. Pretty junky. We popped over here from Robert's and were nothing but disappointed. Pretty empty, but the bartenders were disinterested and difficult to get their attention. Music was on the low end for a downtown Broadway bar. The vibe tries to be cheeky but the place is so trashed that it ends up feeling actually dirty and not just pretend dirty.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Tried out Stone Fox on a Saturday for brunch. We enjoyed every aspect of the experience: the comfortable patio seating, the friendly server, my amazing dish called the King Rabbit (vegan), my husband's French toast, and the coffee with whiskey drink. Cool place. Will definitely return!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Biscuits were dry and hard, chicken was tasteless, don't get brisket hash and service was subpar. Not worth the money.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: My wife and I went here on our date night and was not disappointed.  The fried chicken entree reminded me of Sunday afternoon meals after church.  The food was excellent.  The atmosphere was very relaxing.  They have done a great job with the place.  The service could have been better as it took our server a while to check on us after we got our meal.  It might not be the Woolworths you might remember shopping in back in the day but it is a very good choice today for a nice, relaxing meal.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Amazing! They were recording nashville song writers while we were there and they did not disappoint! Highly recommend anyone visiting but make reservations FAR in advance or you will be waiting outside. ..

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Atmosphere: The back patio is a great spot to share dinner.  The smell from the smoker and all the trees is great! The only downside is the few mice my friend and I saw scurrying across the ground to get under the house. I'm assuming this kinda comes with the territory with it being in an older area of town. However, I will say its something that really needs to be taken care of.
Drinks: I had The Kate- which was excellent! Extremely refreshing! 
My friend had the White Sangria which was ok but we both liked The Kate better. 
Food: We shared the Stone Fox Cheeseburger with the Marrakesh Express salad and the Meat N Three with the Smoked chicken with Cajun Mac and Cheese. The Cheeseburger was awesome. The meat was fresh and the bun perfect! The Smoker chicken was not at all what I expected. I got well cooked chicken that was unfortunately drowning in some sort of Tabasco based marinade. It in no way had a smoke flavor- all I tasted was vinegar. They should call it spicy chicken not smoked. The Marrakesh Express salad could have been great but the kale was too raw- I would suggest cooking it slightly so it's not so hard to eat. I think it would actually taste better warm. 
Dessert: Coconut tres leches was absolutely wonderful. Would have loved the coconut toasted a little on top but not necessary. 
Service: Good. Not overly pushy but could have been a tad more attentive. 
Overall I'd go back- but maybe sit inside this time :/

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great bar with 3 floors and different bands. Very touristy inside with all age groups and mostly from what i heard rock cover music. It was a good time and fun place to drink and hang out.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Visited this place over the weekend. It was so nice and I loved the rooftop and live music.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Such a fun place! I came here as my first honkytonk experience and it did not disappoint! I saw two bands play and both were incredible. They play for tips so they were taking a lot of requests, but in general I liked all the songs they played. We didn't have to wait in line too long, but the place gets really packed inside. Try to grab a seat just to carve out some space for yourself.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I came with my girlfriends for drinks and a small bite to eat. We came during happy hour on a Wednesday evening so it was half off their signature cocktails, wine and I think draft beer. We got the cocktails and they weren't too bad for just $5 (happy hour price). I got the "don't ask rye" and the "Amarillo by morning". 

Don't ask rye - bulleit rye, peach, sour, red wine. It was surprisingly good. It wasn't too sweet, which is what I feared at first bc of the peach. 

Amarillo by morning - tequila, jalapeño-cilantro syrup, lime, smoked salt. I was told this was going to have a spicy kick, but I didn't taste any spice. I tasted more tequila than anything, which isn't always a bad thing, but I was looking forward to the jalapeño-cilantro syrup taste. 

We ended up eating elsewhere for dinner, but we ordered and shared an app while having drinks. We got the guacamole trio which tasted amazing. There was a classic guac, lump crab guac, and mango habanero guac. Each one had its own unique taste. The chips served with it were warm and crispy. I will definitely get this again. 

The menu looked good, but we just weren't in the mood for it. We mainly went there for happy hour. I'll go back for sure for an entree. I had my eyes on the different types of Mac n cheese. 

Staff were all friendly. The host greeted me with a big smile. Atmosphere was chill. They were getting ready to record something or someone on stage so there was some business going on around us, but it didn't bother us much. We didn't get to make it to the cellar, but that's on my to do list for next time.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: What's not to love about this Restaurant?  The atmosphere is spectacular. I have had breakfast lunch and dinner and all meals were superb. I had healthy options like quinoa and unhealthy options  like fried chicken and they were all amazing.  Woolworths is located in the Downtown area right next to Pucketts on 5th.   If you are coming at night, you can valet for a small fee.  I just prefer to Uber or Lyft because their cocktails are too refreshing to have just one.  There are other parking options available during the day like street parking. But, like every popular city, parking can be tricky, so have a plan and leave your frustration s at the door. Woolworths should be experienced by every local and tourist in Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
One of the many Honky Tonks you'll find on Broadway!  If you are in Nashville, Honky Tonks is a MUST visit and Tootsie's does not disappoint.

There is multiple floors...we mostly stayed on the 1st floor.

The music was great and the bartenders were very fast with service, despite the crowd!  

If you are up for it, try the Apple Pie Shine!  It is surprisingly DELICIOUS!!!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
The venue/restaurant was nice, but I just didn't prefer the menu. Again, the food wasn't my personal preference but we still had an amazing time and the environment was pretty awesome. 

I especially love when you're walking downstairs to the bathroom and the top of the stairwell wall is covered with the bottoms of boots. Hundreds of them. 

Not to mention this place is gigantic. There's also a pool hall underground as well. According to my Lyft driver this place has a historic background, but unfortunately I can't recall exactly what it was. 

Definitely a spot to visit if you're in town for a few days.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Fun, did not kill you in the price of beer, and service was great.  Bands were very very good!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsies is always a great time. This is the first time I've come on a weekday and you can definitely move around a lot better. They didn't skimp on the talent being slow, the band is fantastic.

name: The Stone Fox
text: We went for brunch with a large group so we had to wait awhile. Luckily we snagged the waiting seats on the porch. However, since we waited so long many of us ordered the chicken and waffles, but they only had 3 left! I was confused how they only had 3 left when couldn't they just make more batter? However, I was one of the lucky 3 and the chicken and waffles was great. It would have been better if it was warmer though. Tiny tiny mimosas and bloody marys though for $6. It was almost great.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Super divey bar and pretty expensive. The music wasn't anything to write home about- although to be fair it was a Sunday night. Gets really packed with a fairly eclectic crowd- bachelorette parties to 70 year olds. All in all good to say you've been but not worth it to stay the night.

name: Riverfront Park
text: Never been to a Titans game before so I've never been there it's really nice too bad it was too damn cold

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We came though Nashville and had a hard time finding a place available with seating.  We happened to come across The Sutler and was so glad we did.  The service was quick and the food was fantastic.  I'd highly recommend the chicken and waffles. Not too oily and the waffles were exceptionally fluffy.  If you get a chance. Stop on in!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: You can't bring a backpack in. Purses and shopping bags are apparently fine. Feel free to buy a large purse and put your backpack in, because that's acceptable for some reason.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Full disclosure- I'm one of those people who only found out about the Bluebird Cafe through the TV show "Nashville," which has directly contributed to its skyrocketing in popularity. The history of this venue is remarkable. Countless famous artists played here when they were still unknowns, hoping to get discovered and signed by a record label. It's also common for prominent musicians to drop by and perform here, sometimes unannounced. In short, the Bluebird Café is LEGENDARY. 

Getting seats requires a bit of strategy and teamwork. Reservations are available Monday of the week of the show  at 8 AM sharp. They're very limited, and they go FAST. My friends and I employed a divide and conquer approach, hoping to maximize our chances. Only 1 in 4 of us got through. 

The website was impossibly slooooooooow . One guy was basically out within the first minute- his browser crashed. One girl decided to refresh the page because she wasn't seeing any progress. Never, ever refresh! It was down to me and one last guy, and alas, my wifi wasn't fast enough. The show was sold out within 7 minutes. 

There's a $2 online reservation fee, and a $7 minumum to spend on food/drink per seat. Some shows have a cover charge, but many are free. Don't give up if you didn't snag a seat. They hold a number of spots that are first-come-first-serve, so you can wait in line before each show  for those. 

I assure you, the effort is entirely worth it. This was one of the coolest things I've ever been blessed to experience, and I DON'T EVEN LIKE COUNTRY MUSIC (does Taylor Swift count? JK, don't hurt me). You don't have to be a fan of country music to appreciate the pure, unadulterated magic and raw talent at the Bluebird. We had the pleasure of enjoying a beautiful set from four writers, who have not only penned hits for recording artists, but are also gifted musicians who sing, compose, and play instruments. I felt so inferior in the best way possible. 

The café is cozy and intimate, with the artists in the middle and the audience circled around them. You're  here for the music, not the food, so I won't dwell on that. Their music overflows with passion and bleeds love. One of the songs was so real that it moved me to tears. They performed lively songs too, and had the crowd roaring with cheers. They just completely shut it down. 

We met the artists after the show and got pictures and autographed CDs. Carly Pearce, in particular, went above and beyond my expectations. I complimented her on one of her songs that wasn't on her EP, and she said she would email it to me. I scribbled my address on a crinkled receipt, not anticipating to ever hear from her again. Next AM, I checked my email and there it was- a sweet note from Carly and the song that touched my heart. I definitely have a newfound appreciation for country music.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Perhaps this is a better place to visit at night, but I was not impressed with Paradise Park. The place was dead, even on a Saturday, and the atmosphere was dull. My sandwich was very sub-par, and though the sweet potato fries were good, they weren't anything I couldn't have fried up on my own. Not a terrible place if you're looking for a quick and relatively cheap bite, but definitely not one of the more prime locations in the heart of Nashville.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Bluebird cafe was such a fun experience; however you definitely need to know a couple things in advanced to make sure you get in.  We went during a writers night.  We had to drop someone off at the airport around 5pm.  We assumed this would be enough time to drop her off and then go wait on line for the 6pm show at the bluebird cafe.  When we got there, we couldn't find parking in their lot so we parked in the next lot over, no big deal.  We got online around 5:30pm assuming it was for the 6pm show...it wasn't...we apparently were online for the 8pm show.  It was unbelievable.  Luckily we had the coolest people in front of us and we chatted throughout the whole two hours.  Once the line started moving to get inside, we barely had seats (Yes, 2.5 hour wait and barely were able to get inside). Luckily, we got the last couple ones...We couldn't see very well because had some bars in front of us obstructing our view..it was really cool to listen to though.  The day we went, they had a $7 minimum food/beverage fee and no fee to get inside.  They have traditional bar food/drinks.  It was very good!  I think the whole experience was a lot of fun!  We saw a lot of people who were very good trying to make it in the music business.  We even were lucky enough at the end to see one of the writers who wrote songs for Blake Shelton and Tim McGraw.  It was such a great experience and I would love to do it again soon!

I thought it was nice that the people who didn't get in were able to come inside for a couple minutes, listen to some of the music and snap a picture.  They did for that the people who couldn't get in but were in line!  It was nice of them to do!  Keep in mind, this place is really small so it doesn't fit a lot of people! 

My advice to you is to get there really early, way earlier than you think, but definitely squeeze this in when in Nashville!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
I loved the vibe here! The prominent counter contrasted the huge screen.
And I loved their Brussels sprouts!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I came here with a small group just after 10 on a Sunday for brunch - it opens at 10, and it was already pretty packed! They don't take reservations so you just have to get there early and plan to wait a little bit. The hostess told us to expect an hour wait, but it was really closer to 20 minutes which was a pleasant surprise! We ordered bottomless mimosas and didn't think they were terribly strong, but the price was definitely good ($17 all you can drink). The Bloody Mary bar is also pretty cool. The live bluegrass music was so so so good! They were really talented and we enjoyed them a lot. The biscuits before our meal were a nice touch and super yummy! I was a little surprised at the menu - the breakfast portion is about 10 entrees, and the "Benedict" comes with fried eggs (it's traditionally poached) which was odd to me so i opted to skip that one. My cousin got the breakfast sandwich and she was not impressed at all. My breakfast tacos were awesome, but the potato hash was a little plain. Overall it was good, music was fantastic, service was a little slow but a cool vibe.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: A fun place to listen to live music and eat a basic, bland brunch. The band wasn't too loud and was very fun to listen to! The hash browns were mushy and unseasoned. The eggs Benedict was fine but nothing to rant about. Bottomless mimosas for $17 was a great deal!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
An inviting theme meets live music and credible pub grub in the heart of Nashville. 

If nothing else, Paradise Park Trailer Resort wins the most unique concept of all the Clubs/Bars/Honkytonks on Broadway. The setting is simple - your local trailer park. Faux wood walls, disgusting Beer soaked astroturf, even Christmas lights up all year long... Paradise Park Trailer Resort has the trailer theme on lock down. All you need to bring is a dirty undershirt and beaten wife to complete the experience. Throw in live country music and reasonable drink prices and you are in double wide heaven. 

I stopped in with a good friend to sample the trailer park life style along with a nice IPA and a Burger and was impressed by the friendliness of the Bartender (and yes...he has all of his front teeth). He recommended the #4 which is a Bacon Cheeseburger served with a side of Tots. The food arrived between the time I finished thinking about growing out a handlebar mustache but before I considered options in homemade neck tattoos.  

Paradise Park's Bacon Cheeseburger is a simple, honest, and tasty affair consisting of a 1/3 pound medium cooked patty topped with molten Cheddar and 2 slices of thick cut Bacon, Lettuce, Tomato, Mustard, and Ketchup. A large Sesame crusted White Bun acts as the delivery mechanism and does it's job splendidly. The Tots were an admirable bunch coming out piping hot and seasoned simply with Salt. Wash down with copious amount of a hoppy and floral IPA between bites for maximum desired effect. 

For dessert I tried the Kodiak Chewing Tobacco sampler. Just kidding - that doesn't exist but maybe it should.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
The process of getting tickets is what is the most frustrating process of this website. A huge turn off making people wait like they do and not get anything. You could be waiting in line for 30 minutes and when its your turn it would be sold out. If you aren't going to get tickets why would you still make people wait?

Good luck if you are trying to acquire tickets!

name: The Stone Fox
text: Such a cute place! Great simple food w such character. Great cocktails too!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
i would have thought this would be one of those places with 500+ reviews. this place is one of those once in a lifetime type places in their sense of entertainment. especially their wednesday and saturday night shows.  just happened to be there during a singer/songwriter circle session.  2 hours of songs they've written in constant rotation.  i'm blown away by the talent i was able to witness for a mere 10 buck cover and buying a drink.  i don't know when i'll be able to witness such a collaboration because it's one of those "for one night only" kinda of deal.  

anyway, the place is small - it legitimately is just a cafe that happens to have assigned seating when you get there.  it happened that there was a mix up with the seating and they accomodated our seats to be together and that's awesome.  they have decent local beer selection and a pretty full bar and eat your heart out with standard bar food if you'd like.  you come here for your show though.  don't be picky about who you're gonna see and you might be surprised like i was.  i'm glad i got to witness a bit of history here.  pretty neat.

name: The Stone Fox
text: The Back When 80s/90s Night is beyond fun. The DJ spins all the hits and takes requests as well. Don't miss it. And dressing up isn't required but it does add to the fun.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: This is truly a once in a lifetime experience and if you find yourself in Nashville, I would recommend this over any tourist attraction that you may be drawn to. It is a short drive away from the city, but totally worth it. I pre-planned this and reserved tickets online before we came, so I don't know how it works to just show up for a show. Judging by the popularity - you'd better get in line early. However, I had been on standby a week prior to the show and reserved seats the second they went on sale. Because of my willingness to do this, we got a table so close to the performers that I could have licked them. It is a small venue that holds about 100 people - very close together. However, once the show starts you will be grateful for the intimate nature of this spot. They have food, beer, wine and soft drinks only. I didn't come for the food and I only ordered a slice of homemade chocolate cake to meet the minimum $7 that they ask you to spend per person. The cake was fine, but nothing food-wise to write home about. I went to a "in the round" show, which is basically four singer/songwriters singing their own songs - some which have been published and some not. They tell you stories about the songs, about the business and it really is a very cool experience. Being as close as I was, it felt a little awkward to take photos, but they do allow it - just no video. The whole thing lasted about two hours and I could have sat for another two because it was just that great. I paid a measly $15 for this experience and it was by far the highlight of our trip. Don't miss this one.

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text:
Great, fun place to see a show and spend an evening, but there are just too many issues that keep it from being more than 3 stars.

The good: it's beautiful.  Can't imagine a much more pleasant place to spend an evening listening to music.  The employees were friendly.  Food and drinks were pricey, but not as bad as expected.

The meh: if you shell out a ton of money for the VIP section or for seats (for a seated show), you might be able to see.  Might.  If you're on the lawn, good luck (though we were to the side of the stage and the performer seemed really aware that we were there, so we actually had a better view than expected).  For an ampitheater, it's really flat.

The ugly: the traffic/parking situation is pretty awful.  Other reviewers have covered this pretty well, so I won't harp on it, but yikes.  I mean, if you get a "good" parking spot (near the venue), good luck getting out within an hour of the show ending...  And it's a total crapshoot where you're going to park when you arrive - depends on the random pattern that they're using.  We left early and avoided much of the mess, but our friends were not so lucky.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
The Sutler provides a true Nashville bluegrass brunch experience with live music, bottomless mimosas, and delicious southern food. The atmosphere is authentic and gritty Nashville style, which is a refreshing experience versus the fancier brunch spots around town. Expect to wait - they don't take reservations and this is a popular spot.. you'll have more luck with a smaller party, but even so, it's worth the wait! Especially since you can enjoy bottomless mimosas and live bluegrass while you wait. 
We tried the Breakfast Tacos and the Smoked Brisket Hash, and both were delicious. We were so excited to eat that I forgot to take a picture until we were almost done! Also, our waitress was on point - she never let us see the bottoms of our bottomless mimosa glasses. 
I can't wait to go back again! Two thumbs up.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The new express lunch is fantastic! It was recommended by Mo the main bartendress who is always super helpful and conscientious of customers. You never have to wait if she's working she's full go all the time! Best service!Love the turkey avocado wrap and chili combo!

name: Tin Roof
text: If I could give a 0 stars, I would. The bartenders are very, very unfriendly. I asked for a double and the poured half a single. They charged me $10 for that. DO NOT GO HERE.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Visited with a few girl friends before a concert and I really enjoyed my experience. The restaurant was beautiful and I loved how they managed to keep so much of the buildings history intact. I sat at the lunch counter while waiting for my friends to arrive and had great service from the bartender. Once we sat down, we ordered cocktails and more wine and Brussel sprouts with bacon as a starter. They were amazing- the bacon was thick and flavorful and the sauce was sweet and complimented the Brussels perfectly. 

I ordered a chicken salad which was good but kind of boring, but what really impressed me was my friends food- one ordered the fish and it was awesome. The collards were the best I've ever tasted, the fish was flaky and crispy, and the corn bread and biscuits on the table made me want more. I definitely want to go back to try the rest of the menu/ those hot pots are calling me!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Wonderful place to eat, which is also full of rich history!

We stopped for brunch (I highly recommend reservations!) on Saturday, and wasn't disappointed.  We all ordered different cocktails, and different meals, which ranged from sweet potato pancakes to the steak and potato Hash.  Every entree and drink we ordered was amazing! Cooked to order and fresh. 

Service was also on point/outstanding.  Our server was attentive, knowledgeable of the menu and made some great recommendations for us to try.

Highly recommend a visit while in Nashville!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I came in with my boyfriend on our roadtrip from Texas and LOVED our experience. Krystal was very friendly and so was the security (maybe Mark was his name?). Beer was served promptly in a very busy bar which was appreciated a ton! The music in the front and in the back was a great touch as well!! Mark quickly emptied the bar at closing time and suggested we go to The Diner which was a wonderful suggestion! Thank you Tootsies, we will be back!!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: The food and ambiance were great. The building is beautiful and the fact that the location has a historical significance made the experience even better. We shared the fried pickle and tomato appetizer, which was great. I wish I could remember the name of the waitress because she was amazing!

name: Tin Roof
text:
In town visiting Nashville for a long weekend. Was looking for a place to grab a couple of beers and food and Tin Roof was awesome. Hot chicken sandwich was amazing. Scott was the manager on duty and greeted me right when I sat at the bar. The staff was attentive and the food came quick. Also pretty sure country music star,  
Luke Combs was in visiting which was cool! Tin Roof was great.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Apparently this was a place we "had" to go to since we were in Nashville.  I was unimpressed.  There was a rooftop bar, so that's awesome, but the drinks were insanely expensive ($9 for a vodka soda?!) and we had to wait in line to get in but they didn't seem to be actually keeping track of how many people were inside because it was still too tight to move at times.  The line moved extremely fast- we were almost a block away and got in in like 10 minutes- but I would have rather waited a little longer and actually had some breathing room when we got in.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsie's is whatever right? Just gotta day that they hire the most unreasonable/square minded bouncers I've ever ran into.
Couple friends and I were denied entry due to one friend "not having sleeves"
My friend then continued to put on a long sleeve t shirt and the only thing anyone could regurgitate was "FUCK YOU GET ON THE SIDEWALK BITCH!"
Absolutely absurd in my opinion.
Never going to any place who talks to other people like that...
1 star is entirely appropriate for that type of behavior

name: Tin Roof
text: We visited Tin Roof twice in our short visit to Nashville. To me, that says a lot considering the many great places to go! Tin Roof is two stories and has a small balcony for smokers. It's nothing too special or fancy but the live bands were great each visit and did a wonderful job interacting with the crowd.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Very popular location and a great spot for good live music. The bands at any location  in downtown are not shy for panhandling but they deserve it anyway. Be prepared for the band to ask the crowd for free drinks too , I found that to be very forward lol. The bartenders were laidback and fairly attentive. Love that this place has multiple Floors with multiple bands playing. Definitely going back after dark to get more people watching and band listening in.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I love what they've done with the place. Cool stage featuring live music, shoes hanging from the ceiling on your way downstairs to the bathroom. There is even a cool speakeasy bar downstairs. My husband remembered going to a pool hall down there years ago. The drinks were good. I really enjoyed my watermelon drink served in a solo cup. 
The food to me was rich and heavy. The fried pickles were very good, but beware they include fried lemons, okra, a bunch of filler. I actually preferred the fried okra best. Their pickles were a bit too spicy for me. My husband and any man on the planet would love the heat of those things and the spicy dipping sauce, too. So you can tweek the dish if you want to omit lemons or whatever. I seriously would ask for more okra next time. Those things were very tasty!
Moving on to main dishes, my husband and I split the burger and brussel sprout hash. The burger was served sitting in a cheese soup. It was a bit bizarre and made for a super messy eating experience, but it did taste good. I mean, you slap some melted cheese on anything it's good, right!? The burger itself was ok and the bun was massive. It was like some thick, hard brioche bun. It was ok.
The Brussel sprout hash was quite misleading and disappointing. As you can tell from my picture, it's a pile of mashed potatoes with some roasted brussel sprout flakes on top and a ton of those crunchy fried onions. While tasty, it was sodium overload and not what I was hoping for. I'd rename it potato casserole. 
Overall, there wasn't a healthy option on the menu and only one pseudo salad. Need salads, people!! I'd go back knowing it's more of a drinking, live entertainment type place. Not somewhere I'd recommend as a dining destination.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
My brother was in town for a few days so I made a reservation for him, my boyfriend, and myself on a Monday evening. Parking in the area wasn't too clear, but we were able to park out front without any issues (the street signs say valet during the week however, when I asked the host he said they no longer had valet). There weren't too many people inside so we were able to get seated right away. 

Service was good, our waitress came by just enough to make sure everything was going smoothly and tasted okay. The boys ordered hamburgers, I ordered the meatloaf. The meatloaf portion I received was generous, 2 large slices. It came with green beans and mashed potatoes- I would have liked to see a little more potatoes though. The boys said their burgers were good, and they definitely looked delicious. I do wish they had more menu options, it just seemed a little limited. 

Overall the ambiance was nice (there's a ton of seating so if busy I could see it getting pretty loud) and the food and service was good. More clear instructions on parking as well as a larger menu would boost the stars!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: RIDICULOUSLY OVER-RATED! We stopped into this place on a Friday night and it was packed to the brim. I MEAN.. CLAUSTROPHOBIC PACKED. I was afraid Id get trampled. Getting a drink was next to impossible and that was a problem because it was at least 95 degrees in the pace because of all the people. I waited for a half hour to get a drink before I just gave up. The band the night we were there seemed fun, but I just wanted to leave because I was really hot and really thirsty. Trying to leave was equally as hard because the front area is soo packed with people listening to the band. There needs to be more structure. Its a fire hazard FOR SURE.  Yes.. this place is famous because a bunch of famous people have played/hung out there. Well.. they are not there now and I dont understand why you would want to smash yourself into this tiny and dirty place. Sorry Tootsie's... im not a fan.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: I've been coming to this bar for years (10) it's my favorite bar downtown.. however... I don't like how they have moved the stage bc it makes it hard to get into the bar.. and it was just far too crowded. Maybe we were there at "prime time" but my group stayed for 1 drink and left

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I don't think I've ever had so much fun at a prime tourist location as I had for several hours at Tootsie's. A true tourist mecca, if you're not having fun here you might as well get out of Nashville. It's an institution, a legend, and a true good time. This place has three levels and each level seems to bring a different vibe and attitude of crazy - in a good way. By the time we hit the third floor it was an all-out party on a Sunday at about 2pm. Highly recommend.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: What a cool unique place hidden in a strip mall. I would read about the history before coming here. It's a must do in Nashville. If you can't get tickets online get here super early. The show started at 6:30 on a Saturday, doors opened at 5:30 and I got there at 3 and was 8th in line. Only the first 12 people to wait are pretty much guaranteed in. But it's worth sticking around for no shows. For the late show it seems like you only have to be there at 7 for the 9 show to get in. There were people in line there since 12:30 which seemed a bit much. The show was free with a $10 food or drink purchase. All the food looked really good and I got the queso and chips with a hot choc with baileys! Perfect for a cold day. The setting is very intimate and special with almost every seat in there being a good one. If you can't get in I suggest still visiting it when the doors open and running inside to get some merch!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Love love love this famous bar! The only downside is that it's very squishy inside - it's not that small but so many people go in that it's almost hard to move around. I love that everything inside and out is purple, it's so fun and festive. I actually visited on the day of NYE so it was decorated with tons and tons of purple balloons. The drinks are reasonably priced and no different than any of the surrounding bars. They are nothing special and come in plastic cups. They do have a rooftop which I didn't go up to because it was freezing outside when I went. I believe they have three floors in total. They also have live music playing all the time and the bartenders are really friendly. Located on Broadway in the middle of everything! The line is always super long at night so get there early or plan to wait awhile.

name: Tin Roof
text: We came on a Tuesday night for Lightning 100's beer, bands, and bingo. The green room was pretty deserted when we got there a bit early, but people trickled in as the night went on. They had a $3 leinenkugel special and a $5 blue chair bay rum special. So not bad prices for the promoted drinks, but I didn't look at the other options.
