Our server was attentive and made sure we had what we needed, but if it weren't for the bingo, we probably wouldn't make a habit of coming here (mostly because we're not really bar people).

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Absolutely loved this place! Live Music on all 3 levels, of course bars on each level too! Raw, fun, great drinks. Happy people, perfect gathering place to catch up, laugh and people watch. This is Nashville at its best

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The BEST place for live music, which also has a awesome rooftop to see Broadway!  The view is fantastic. We heard an awesome local band who took customers requests (for a tip). Their talent was very impressive and gave Tootsie's a great vibe! This is a must see in Nashville!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Huge party scene with loud, great music.  The levels and the atmosphere reminded me of the Garment District in the mid 80's - without the smoke and drugs, but with the zoned-out happy people.

Drinks were great, as was service.  

This is the sort of place you need to be in the mood for.  If you are it will be a night to remember!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Reservation process was stressful but relatively easy. The weekend shows go on sale at 8am Monday the week of. I had my calendar set and right at 8am the tickets were released. They went fast! I tried to get a pair of tickets 3 times before they weren't snatched up from me by someone else. All tickets sold out by 8:03 am for the Saturday shows so you have to act fast. They require a deposit of $4 for the free shows. 

On the day of the show, I'll have to admit, it was kind of fun walking by the people waiting in line to get in. Be sure to get there on time or they will give away your reservation! My friend and I were at a 6-top and were seated with a lovely couple, their mother & grandmother. We got lucky to be seated with such nice people and had enjoyable conversation prior to the show starting. Once the show starts, shut yo mouf! They like to have no conversations or whispers while the artists are performing which makes sense as it's all about respecting the artists & their music.

We were fortunate to have four wonderful songwriters the night we went - Jenn Bostic, Sarah Darling, Emily Shackelton and Michael Logen. They would play various tunes citing them being used by professional artists and various movies & TV shows. They are not only all great songwriters but great artists themselves. I believe all of them had CDs they were selling post show. Bluebird is a very small venue which is great because you can hear every word the artists sing and are very close to their circle in the middle of the cafe where the performing happens.

The Bluebird Cafe was one of the best experiences I had throughout my whole trip and I'd do it again next time I'm in Nashville. It also turned out not to be expensive at all. They ask you to spend $7 each (random number) which is easily met by getting a couple of drinks. They had specialty pops like Diet Black Cherry - yum! I heard the food can be skipped so we ate prior to our show. Our server was so nice & beyond attentive. The show run exactly 2 hours on the dot and boy did it fly by! People then hang out to get CDs signed and have little chats with the artists. 

Parking can be rough but check out the secret spots in the back if they aren't any in the main lot. 

One of the artists I saw is now on Rising Star on ABC!

The Bluebird Cafe is a must do for music fans while in Nashville!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Sometimes yelpers just get it wrong... 3.5 stars?? Paradise Park is like having 5 guys or smash burger with a bar and live music in the back & bar. Perhaps it's just Nashville in general, but the musical talent even on a Tuesday afternoon was incredible. 

The burgers are big and juicy -- perhaps a bit on the salty side. But hell, this is supposed to be a fun time with greasy burgers and fries and cheap beer, not gourmet. Would come for a quick bite or a casual night out anytime.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Went to the Sutler for brunch one Sunday morning and it didn't disappoint. We went around 10:00/11:00 AM with a party of 4 and were immediately seated. The inside of the restaurant is very laid back with a country feel. There was a stage with 3 men playing some folksy tunes. Such a great vibe! 

My friends and I were treated to some complimentary biscuits while we looked over the menu. I ordered the BLT with avocado and a side of fruit. I was so happy to get strawberry, pineapple and blueberries vs. apples and melons. They offer bottomless mimosas for $17 and a Bloody Mary bar, but I didn't catch that price. All prices seemed to be very reasonable. Service was a bit slow but overall we still had a good time!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Our second visit to the Bluebird Cafe was in October, 2013. The first time we tried this place, we couldn't get in after standing outside in the rain for hours.  This time we showed up REALLY early (sometime after 4pm) and waited in line (we were 1st in line this time) for the 6pm show. We didn't go online to get tickets because you really need to do that on Mondays from what I understand...and they sell out super fast due to limited number of seats.

But, this time we actually were able to get inside. we ate, drank, and enjoyed the "in the round" music. It was very enjoyable. The food was "okay"...nothing great and ditto on the drinks. But, we had fun and enjoyed our PACKED (yes, it was crammed inside) show.

For people who are coming in from out of town (like ourselves), expect to stand in line outside in whatever type of weather it happens to be that evening, and if you are lucky enough to get inside for a show, then plan to be packed in every seat. However, the staff handles the capacity pretty well once you're inside.

I still feel that the owners and staff could do so much more to make the events more enjoyable and less stressful for the customers. They need to get on top of their notoriety that the Nashville show has given them and get some help with crowds.

I'm glad we were finally able to get inside and see a show!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Stumbled here on a Thursday night around 12am and the place was still jumping. The bartenders were fast and courteous, huge dance floor and live band that played an eclectic mix of music. Dare I say, I don't even care for country music, and even I had a good time. 
There is also an upstairs if you want to sit and people watch the drunken patrons below. There were 9 people in our party and we all had a really good time.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
What a fun night we had dancing to many bands on multiple floors.  This is one of the many places that have been around for a long time on Broadway.  

I liked that there is no smoking.  We started on the first floor, but it was a tad crowded so up we went to the 2nd floor. Great band with a sax, 7 string electric fiddle and other standard band members.  They played popular sing-along country, Bob Seager throw backs, some slow songs and even Beyonce's All The Single Ladies.  They have a good sized dance floor and big bar.  Tables with stools, but you go to the bar for service.  Lots of security so you feel safe.  

We went up to roof top last.  It is part inside and part outside.  Outside they have heaters.  The band there was funky soul with a young version of Tina Turner.  

Enjoyed it so much we did not leave and go to other bars on Broadway.  This is a one stop, all night, don't need to leave bar.  Enjoy!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: your average broadway, neon signed, country music cover band bar.  not complaining since it's everything you expect on this street, just hard to give it 4 stars.  congrats to tin roof for getting many small things correct, good drinks served quickly to a well behaved crowd.  you should probably eat somewhere else then head here for music and drinks.  probably a better place to listen to music than say tootsies, but it also lacks a certain flair.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Let me start out by saying I only come here on Sunday nights.  I've never been here on any other night, so I don't know what it's like then.  But I can tell you this much:  Sunday nights at Whiskey Bent Saloon are absolutely incredible.

Every time I take my first step out of Whiskey Bent Saloon on Monday morning at 2:00 AM, I eagerly anticipate the next Sunday night.  This goes on for the entire week.  Thanks to Whiskey Bent Saloon, Bryan Wain, and Sarah (I'll get to them in a minute), Sundays are my new favorite day of the week.

This place is a bit hidden.  It's not impossible to find, but it doesn't have a neon sign like the more popular venues on Broadway do.  It has huge doors that remain open throughout the night, and the "sign" is right above those doors in brown lettering.

Anyway, back to Sunday nights here.  Starting at 6:00 PM, Bryan Wain and his band play some great rockabilly, swing, country, and blues music for about four hours.  He is one of my favorite local musicians.  Some of his best songs include "Run Around Sue," "Hoochie Coochie Man," "Blue Suede Shoes," and "My Wife Thinks You're Dead."  Usually about an hour into his set, a bunch of the swing dancers from the area (myself included) come in, crowd the floor, and dance our blues away.  After Bryan's set, Brandon Harris and the Good Ol' Boys set up and sing for another four hours until closing time.  They're a more modern country band.  Brandon sings a lot of Vince Gill songs like "Liza Jane," "One More Last Chance," and "What the Cowgirls Do."  About half of us dancers will stay for him, and some people will even get out and do a little line dance.

So that's enough about the music and dancing...this review is supposed to be about the saloon itself, right?  This is a very classy saloon compared to the other saloons and honky-tonks in the area.  Don't get me wrong...it's very country, but also very classy, if that makes any sense.  There's lots of rustic decor there like whiskey barrels, wagon wheels, and even a statue of Jack Daniel himself in the window.  The hardwood floor is slick and very ideal for boot scootin'.  There's no real "dance floor" designated for dancing, but the front third of the saloon is empty and open to dancers.  The back two thirds is a bunch of tables and chairs for relaxing and watching the band.  The right side (or left if you're looking in from outside) is the bar, which stretches from front to back.  It's huge!  They serve beer, wine, and just about any liquor you could imagine.  That's a huge plus in my book since so many bars only serve two of the above.

This place is completely non-smoking.  That's one thing that adds to the "classiness" that I mentioned earlier.  If you do smoke, no worries though.  You can just step right out the huge, open double doors and come right back in when you're done smoking.  They don't even ID here, at least not on Sundays.  You can even bring your kids if you want...I've seen people do it!

One of my favorite things about Whiskey Bent is the bar staff.  Since I'm only there on Sundays, I'm not sure who's full-time or if the staff is even the same on other days.  But Sarah is the best bartender I know.  She's friendly, helpful, and prompt (not to mention HIGHLY attractive ;-)).  She's got brown hair and always wears a black Whiskey Bent hoodie, so if you see her, make sure to order from her.  If she's not busy taking orders, she may even dance with you if you ask!  The other bartender is fine too, but not quite as friendly.  And they always have a cleaning guy back there too helping put away all the glasses and such.  I'm guessing on Friday and Saturday nights, there's probably more.

I know some people can get paranoid about bathrooms, so let me assure you that the bathrooms are clean and fine.  The men's bathroom has two urinals and a toilet, so they aren't huge, but they're fine.

Parking is very tough here.  Of course, it is anywhere downtown.  You either have to find a metered spot on the street or pay.  I usually park at the library garage.  It's down on 6th Avenue, and you can park there for just $4 for the whole night.  Sometimes you'll get lucky and find a metered spot, but don't count on it.

Whiskey Bent Saloon is easily on my top two nightlife venues in Nashville, being tied with the 5 Spot.  Of course, they are two VERY different places with VERY different crowds.  But I can't pick one over the other because of that...it depends on what mood I'm in and what day it is.  Whiskey Bent is my favorite spot on Sunday nights, and 5 Spot is my favorite on Monday nights.  So take your pick!

El fin.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
This is my favorite broadway bar.  I don't like country music or the broadway scene, but the band they had here was great.  Sadly I don't remember the name, I wish I did.  

A bar that specializes in whiskey?  YES please!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: I wanted to give a 4 because I would LOVE the option of a Moonshine flight! There are so many options so it is hard to decide. Molly was great and was able to "guide" us in making the right choice! The Moonshine Margarita with Jalapeño or the chocolate/vanilla combo with a splash of soda.

name: Limelight
text: My people my people. I mean damn. I am in the event industry and the fact that the management was holding up the guest line because they wanted more money, AND I was in line hearing about it, is unacceptable. The bar service was terrible. There just didn't seem to be anyone who knew what was going on. So disappointed.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Room was clean.  Entry was nice.  No coffee stand or shop, so if you want coffee in the morning you have to go to the restaurant.
Room coffee was missing the actual coffee (had cups and everything else).
No bathmat in bathroom.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text:
I've been to Judge's a number of times since it opened. At first I was crazy about the food. Always good, always abundant. In the past year or so consistency seems to have slipped, in both quality and quantity of food. Having said that, when they do get it right, they get it REALLY right. The smoked sausage is about the best I've had. Always had good service at the bar too. There's the good, here's the bad...

You're NOT a music venue. I'm in the music industry, and have been for better than 20 years, and if I want some good BBQ, there is no way I'd do anything other than drive right by when I see and hear an obscenely loud band ripping people's heads off on the patio. Even if I wanted to escape the noise, I'd have to walk through the din to get to the front door. If the idea is to perhaps entice some of the music row types into your restaurant, loud live bands ain't gonna get it done, even if they're great bands, and what I've heard, sometimes for blocks around, isn't so great, just loud. It's enough to keep me away. That's why I can't give the Vinegaroon more than two stars. Please concentrate on being a fantastic restaurant, which I know you can be,  instead of trying to be a venue.

Just a constructive thought... If you are going to have live bands, perhaps make it an event, and just do a couple Fridays or Saturdays a month. There are AMAZING bands in town who will work for pretty little base pay if they know they'll move some CDs and have a decent shot at filling the tip jar. Serious pros too.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Decent hotel with a very friendly staff, but service in the dining room for breakfast was agonizingly slow on 6/10/16. They appear grossly understaffed. If you're in a hurry, go early or make other breakfast plans.

name: The Valentine
text:
Wanted to check out the rooftop - went in late afternoon. 
Great atmosphere - live music, comfortable couches.
Food was great!!
However, bouncer who came on duty & positioned himself at the entrance to the hallway (EXACTLY where the bathroom was) could have had a different attitude.  "Where you think you're going?" is not so hospitable buddy when I've been on your roof for over two hours eating & drinking with my husband.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Check out the live bluegrass jam here on Saturday nights 8-9:30pm! I got to sing a couple songs when I was there this past Saturday night. Really great musicans from the east Nashville area hang out here. Their beer selection was really great and the hummus plate has fresh veggies and warm pita. Yehaw!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: The restaurant is extremely loud. Not family friendly at all, or even friendly at all if you want to have a conversation with the person you are dining with. The food is below average, nothing about our experience was enjoyable or memorable.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Pretty fun place.. Had a good time.. Nice bar lots fun people dancing and having fun. Did not happen to care for the band that much when we where here.. Just to much blending of different songs.. But lots of folks like that sort thing.. So if that's your things stop in here..

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Great rooms and workout facilities.
Breakfast buffet was terribly overpriced and hostess was extremely rude.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The Stage was a great time! Three different floors of fun! The music was on point all night and this was on a Wednesday night so I cannot imagine on the weekend what it is like. I lost my wedding band and The Stage personnel contacted me without delay after I called. They took care of me and the bartenders did the same the night before! Must go in Nashville!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: This is a massive hotel. But it is kept flawlessly clean. The staff is friendly and accommodating. The location, unfortunately, is in an office park. The gym is spotless and all of the equipment seems new and in good repair. There are very few restaurants within reasonable walking distance. The hotel restaurant and bar are, in my opinion, expensive. The only other downside that I can find for this property is that there are no power outlets bedside.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Went to a few different bars on Broadway and this was my favorite. Great music, nice inside venue and I was lucky enough to find a table with my friends and we had a great time. This bar was recommended to me by some family members as their favorite too, so I'm glad I checked it out. 

Only negative was when we went to leave there was a jam at the door. We could not get out and people probably figured we were just trying to get close to the band, but weren't understanding we just wanted to leave. People were coming in and there was a jam of so many of us trying to get out. It was a crowded stand still until the security guards came yelling for people to move. It was scary for a few moments being trapped/sandwiched so tight amongst everyone.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Overall, this is a solid Sheraton. I've stayed at the Sheraton Music City Hotel a few times over the last year each time I visited Nashville. The service is consistently friendly at the front desk and the onsite restaurant and bar are open late! I'm not totally in love with the design of the facility but it is my go to hotel choice in Nashville at a great price. 

It is close to downtown Nashville (about a 10 minute car or taxi ride) without the hassle of traffic and close to the airport if you are flying into town. Check out the great features if you head to Nashville soon. The hotel has on site taxi service, two restaurants and a bar, free parking, indoor and outdoor pool/jacuzzi, gym, and is close to the area airport! You cannot beat this package with standard double rates routinely available at under $150.00 a night with an optional daily meal credit!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Fun, fun, fun!  Place was not overly crowded for a Saturday evening. It was packed but not like sardines. We got there around 7 and were able to score a couple of seats at the bar. The band was great, the bartenders friendly and efficient, and music volume just right. 
My next visit to Nashville wouldn't be complete without a visit here.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Nice hotel. Clean with solid amenities. It could perhaps use a little updating in the common areas. I really liked the courtyard style with the outdoor pool in the center. It made for a nice setting with local foliage. This property has a lot of stairways leading to different levels which is odd. To get to the fitness center, you must walk from the lobby to through a maze of hallways up a half flight of stairs then down another flight of stairs. Very strange setup, but a decent hotel none the less. The shuttle to the airport is always a plus.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Came here for lunch before the Music City Bowl. Service was great and food was good. Would return for sure!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Only impressed with the lobby which was beautiful. 
The front ambassador stated that we were in the updated art of the hotel. Hmmm, phase 1. Lol do you all know what phase 1 means? It means they just began the renovation. The carpet was old and there were no baseboards on the bottom of the walls. No fan in the washroom, the air conditioner was set at 65 and it was 75 in the room. Small refrigerator with no cold setting. No extra towels, toilet paper of shampoo. We had three in the room. Basic TV everything else extra. No breakfast as posted in the first floor lobby. The swimming pools were not clean. Very slimy water. 
Pros:
away from the big city noise 
Takes animals
Free parking

Cons: read above

Would I return: No 
$900 for a run down Hotel

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Wonderful time at Whiskey Bent Saloon tonight, Bre was fantastic!  Great tunes, cold brew, outstanding service!Can't go wrong coming here if you're in town!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: This is a different looking Hard Rock. It was more modern and not the classic rock type theme. Still has the awesome typical outfits and guitars on the walls but the rest was more modern. We really enjoyed that they had the music just loud enough to be overly loud but still low enough that I could actually talk to my husband in a normal voice. Dae was our server and she was really nice. She welcomed us, laughed with us and kept the tea full for my husband. We love Hard Rock and the foos is always fantastic at everyone of them; including this one. I think the only complaint someone might have is the parking lot in front of the restaurant is for vallet only and other must find parking within the city blocks. This didn't bother us since we decided to use the vallet parking. It was worth it.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: This hotel is horrible! I would give 0 stars if I could. They cancelled our reservation for 3 rooms that we had for the weekend without even telling us!! We arrived to the hotel and they told us that the rooms were cancelled because they were booked through a third party and I regularly use Expedia to book and have never had this issue. I think it is absolutely absurd that the hotel never even contacted us to notify us!

name: The Valentine
text: Spent a couple hours on a Tuesday afternoon here and Casey our bartender was awesome and the music was great. New place with a new place smell but I believe it will be a Nashville "go to" place soon. Come by and have a look, I think you'll like it.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This place is always a favorite! Even though it's downtown it's not nearly as touristy as the other bars. The live music is always great! The atmosphere is great too. You never feel overcrowded, but there is definitely a big enough crowd to keep it interesting. Drinks are reasonably priced too. Great place to hear live country music!

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Was in town for a conference and looking for unique/interesting places for some BBQ or Southern cooking. Judge's is a bit of a dive, but that's often what I like. The place has just changed hands and some of the more interesting menu items are no longer on the menu they still have on line. That was a bit of a disappointment but there was still a good choice of traditional BBQ items. I had a combination plate of brisket and sausage. Nicely cooked with a choice of sauces on the table. They even had Yuengling (a nice lager from my neck of the woods) on tap. If your looking for fine dining, this is not it but if you looking for some good BBQ without the price and crowds of Broadway you should give Judge's a try.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: If a good band is playing, like Jesse Caine, this place can be a lot of fun.  Most bands are pretty decent, but there are a few bush leaguers too.  The bar has a good sound system, although the sound guy tends to push way too much bass.  The beer is usually really cold, so that's a plus.  Not crazy about paying the bathroom attendant a buck with every visit, but I suppose it does keeps the bathrooms cleaner than most on Broadway.  Definitely worth visiting.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Our first stop on Yelp Spring Break was checking into the hotel! This was one of the hotels that offered a discount if you were attending the 2014 Yelp Spring Break. Because it was one of the more inexpensive places, my friend and I decided to book our stay here! 

Such a convenient location to the airport! It's literally across the street. So close that the hotel offers a complimentary airport shuttle. When you approach the hotel, you're taken to the top of a hill and kind of given a dramatic entrance. The hotel is beautiful! You walk in and notice a computer area to the left, separated by partitions. On the right is the check in desks. The staff was super personable and really nice. Next to the check in desk and computer area is a hotel bar for your convenience. With a discounted rate of $139 a night, this really set the tone for the trip!

A couple of mishaps that happened in the hotel were as follows. Keep in mind, they didn't ruin the trip at all!

-After getting out of the shuttle from the airport, the shuttle driver grabbed my telescope handle to my rolling suitcase and ripped it completely off of the suitcase. He took me to the front and asked the front desk agent to take care of me. After looking at the damages, one of them mentioned that they had duct tape to fix it! I was like, "oh heck no." I clearly needed a new suitcase and duct tape wasn't going near that. Thank goodness the company I bought the suitcase from completely exchanged a new one out and sent it directly to the hotel. The hotel staff was awesome enough to bring it directly to my room!

-Along those same lines, I was required to send the broken suitcase back, so I sent it through the hotel. Shipping was completely free so all I needed was tape. When I called the front desk, the agent told me that they are too busy to look for tape now. I gave her a couple of hours before calling back and she mentioned they did not have tape at all. That was kind of a turn off as I hoped a hotel of this magnitude would have something as simple as masking tape. I ended up going into the city to buy some tape of my own. 

Once again, I would like to say that these hiccups did not at all ruin the trip. Overall, they were great hosts and the hotel was awesome! The cool part is that the pool area was in the center courtyard and the setting of a previous Nashville episode! This hotel wasn't too far from town and super convenient to the airport. If the price is right on my next trip to Nashville, I will absolutely stay here again. Thanks so much for the great stay, Sheraton!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
A lot of reviews are very dramatic about the worst ever HRC. I thought the employee policy and procedures were followed well. We arrive and was created and she said give her a minute, which means she knows I'm there; a half a second later she seated us. Same thing our waitstaff came by said I will be right back and take your drink orders. She came back quickly and we ordered just a few easy water, tea and spiked milkshake. And some of their famous nachos with steak. I got the toppings on the side, kids don't like that stuff. 
So the staff is managed well but just a few things could be better on attention to detail. A waiter delivered the spiked milkshake and this thing is big and the way he set it down hard and walked off made the brownie fall over in her lap. So thanks for that touch. 
The nachos came out... I was a little Disappointed they were not the mound of nachos I have ordered literally all over the world - from Rome, London, KL, NY, Dallas to LA .... on and on you get my drift. 
It should have been more than enough for 3 to split. Sparse on chips the beans and cheese. We quickly finished the nachos and me and the son needed a little more. We got the classic sliders. Very well presented and tasty. Ground meat with cheese and onion ring and coleslaw. It was good. 
Again the manager helped when we returned the dirty plates - again not a big deal but if you pick up plates and deliver them to a table you should look down at them before tossing them on the table and walking away. 
The manager tried to make light of it and apologized. 
It's a well run HRC. 
I will be back

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: LOVED our stay!  The bed was soo comfortable.  If exploring Nashville wasn't the point of our vacation, I would have spent the whole weekend in bed.  Staff was nice and helpful.  The location was great.  No complaints - I highly recommend!

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: The brisket and ribs were excellent and the service was great.  We'll definitely be back.  Watch out for the Shrmp Diablo......its VERY spicey hot.  Very friendly staff and patrons.  Live music.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
We visited  numerous bars on our recent trip to Nashville and this was definitely my favorite! 

- Not too crowded but busy
- QUALITY live music each time we went (3 times over the course of the weekend) which was a bonus as some of the bars on Broadway had terrible bands.
- Friendly staff
- Very cool country decor, lots of animals
- Clean and not as divey when compared to nearby local spots

Will go back if I ever return to Nashville!

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Came here Saturday for brunch. Bloody Mary was really tasty-- loved having smoked brisket as BM garnish.  Food was quite tasty as well (I had an omelet w/ brisket). Only complaint was the wait time for food. We were one of two tables (arrived and ordered food at same time) but the second table finished their meals and left before our food even came out. Regardless, servers were nice and food was good, so I'd definitely come back again

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
This was where my Nashville Night begun.

A beer, amazing live music and a famous venue.

I especially liked the Keith Urban mural.

I will definitely be visiting here again

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I started to book this location in the spring, but the availability soon filled up and before I knew it, I'd waited too long to decide. Fast forward a few months forward and I found myself in the area, looking to switch hotels. I always play the Hotwire roulette and Nashville is the only place that I've been burned, and it was in the spring. 

When I called and looked online, I found that the cheapest Saturday before Christmas rate was $129. I mastered Hotwire for the first time in Nashville and scored this place for around $100.

I was able to get a slight bit of an early check-in, at around 2pm. It was hard to believe, but they must've been sold out the night before... at least that's the way that they acted when I asked for an early check-in. When we arrived there were several people checking in too, so they must do their early check-ins all at once. The only thing I received for being a Starwood Preferred Member, was free wifi, no upgrade that was mentioned in another review.

The location is not near downtown, it doesn't seem near anything actually. It gives you an office park environment feel. As long as you know that ahead of time (which I did) then there's no need to knock it for that.

A huge plus is the $10 round trip, third party shuttle company that was mentioned while I was checking in. I was prepared to pay around $40 each way for an Uber... so that was a pleasant surprise. 

The room itself was outdated. The decor reminds me of something from the 80s. As long as it's clean, I don't have any issue with the decor. That was a bit of the problem though, the wallpaper it the bathroom was on the verge of nastiness though. Again, I'll make an excuse; I'm not sleeping in the bathroom and as long as the bed is clean, I'm good.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Really fun music venue!  I also found out after the fact that one of my friends from college was here in Nashville at the same time and was just across the street. So crazy! Wish I would have known so she could have joined my party and me. 

Good music, decent drinks, crazy weirdo crowd. (A lot of drunk tourists, but we had fun laughing at their antics).  We had gone to another music venue earlier in the night, and this one far exceeded the former.  Love Nashville.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Motown Monday's after swing is five stars dance party. Be prepared to twist. Nice crowd and mid priced beers.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
This Hardrock is just plain bad.

You set expectations for a national chain in the music capital of the world, and this has to be the worst Hardrock experiences in all food, service, and venue.

Unfortunately we won't be back.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: A great little bar on Broadway! Delicious drinks, great live music and a more local bar vibe. My boyfriend and I stopped in a few times on our trip to Nashville and they remembered us from the night before. Will absolutely be back next time we're in town

name: Ray Stevens CabaRay Showroom
text: Very nice setting to watch a show.  Very good views from every seat in the house.  Nice friendly staff.  Ray Stevens hasn't missed a beat and was wonderful.  So glad we went, we didn't have dinner just saw the show.

name: The End.
text: Man this place is cool but it could be so much cooler. Basically no one is in charge here. The name should be changed to "THATS NOT MY JOB". If you're fortunate enough to catch the bartender/owner actually tending the bar rather than doing God knows what in the back room be prepared. His favorite statement is "we don't have that" and he moves about half as fast as a fart. The lack of leadership falls unfairly on the sound guy and makes them slightly grouchy. If you're playing here be very polite and you'll get good sound. Don't ask the sound guy about anything but sound and set time or you will be quickly told "that's not my problem". Anyways, this place could be great if they got a friendly bartender and a stage manager. It's got potential but poor execution.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Absolutely awesome.....brisket AAA+ - sausage incredible - pork ribs holy mother - cole slaw is the bomb!!!  If you're in Nashville do NOT pass this place up. BBQ lovers unite. Guy Fierre - food network dude  - you have to come check this place out.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Great place to stop in for a beer and great music. Saw a very young and extremely talented girl perform - it was incredible! It's definitely a popular bar but doesn't get as claustrophobic as other bars on Broadway, in my opinion. Nice staff as well.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Confession: In 33 years of living, I'd somehow never been to a Hard Rock Café.  Talk about a deprived life.  Then again Hard Rock has lost in 80s/90s cool back when everyone wore the t-shirts.  Nowadays it's more along the lines of a rock 'n' roll Applebees or something.  Anyhow, we hit it up whilst day drinking on Broadway.  Beer was cold, bartender was friendly, and the rock décor was kind of cool/very kitschy.  I can't say that I'm dying to go back, but I'm glad I checked it off the bucket list.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: On top of great music and reasonably priced drinks, the place was super spacious and I didn't feel over crowded listening to bands the way I did at other honky tonks. Was so great we went back to end our night

name: Limelight
text: I come here sparingly and only on Friday's for the 3-4-1 specials.  Call me bougie, but I don't deal with too many thugs, hood rats, and overly ratchet-fied humans.  Want to see some bad weaves, sagging pants, bad bodied women?  Come here, lol.  They do 4 for one every fourth Friday of the month which is pretty decent.  The drinks can range from pretty good to strong as hell.  I recall once ordering the 8 liquor ass kicker (3 for 1) and I couldn't finish the second cup; it was WAAAAAY too strong!  The specials go on until about 8pm and I'm usually preparing to leave by then.  It gets pretty ratchet later over in the night.  It's spacious, large bar, but come early if you're looking to just unwind and not be among the younger crowd.  It can get out of hand over in the night.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great country music!!! Drinks priced right and best sweet potato fries served. Room to dance and plenty on seating

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Came here with a group of friends and had a good time.  The food was enjoyable, atmosphere was nice, the only downside was the really loud volume of the live band.  I felt bad for my friends and other patrons who were seated by the stage.  The music was fun and entertaining, but the volume of it was almost a bit much as evidenced by the faces of the people stuck to sit around the stage (before the live music started up).

The food was pretty good!  The Buca Beignets were delightful and the Shrimp & Crab dip was tasty.  I really enjoyed my chili-rubbed scallops.  The cheesecake sopapilla was awesome!

name: Robert's Western World
text: The fried bologna sandwich was fantastic and the beer was cold.  The servers were friendly and the band was talented.  The place is a dive but part of Nashville history.  A definite must stop while you are in town.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Good food, good music, nice staff. A lot of space for groups and nice ambiance for date or group night out.

Artichoke appetizer delicious
Chicken Somasas- pretty good
Artisan pizza with sausage- tasty
Mango pear drink-pretty good

Will definitely be back!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: The inside is beautiful! We walked around the building for about 30 minutes before we went to get food. When we went for food, there were a ton a really good options. The food, and amount we paid for it, was great! I had the chicken kabobs with vegetables. It was so well seasoned and the chicken was super tender.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I was here on my birthday and by fortuitous happenstance, we were seated front center to see a group called "Mood Ring", which did 1970's Adult Contemporary style music. Odd, but awesome!

The food nd service were impeccable. Top flight experience!

name: Second Fiddle
text:
Absolutely 0 air in this bar. The bathroom had shattered glass covering all 2 stalls. Line wrapped all the way down the bar. 

As far as bars on Broadway - the music was mediocre but the experience was not worth it. No standing room unless you want to breathe down someone's neck the whole time.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great music.  Thank you John and Lois Shepard for your 40 years of entertainment and making our visit so special.  Bologna sandwich highly recommended!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Salmon Oscar with crab meat, asparagus and hollandaise sauce. Salmon was good, not enough crab meat to even taste; asparagus was almost to the point of being tough.  Did 3 sides. Brussell sprouts were too large to be tender but still tasty, sweet potato was very sweet. Overall about the same dinner we would have had in the hotel restaurant but twice as expensive. No return business from us.

name: Robert's Western World
text: #PorkMcElhinny is an awesome entertainer. Fun atmosphere. Friendly wait staff. Stopped I because of a reference on Yelp and glad we did!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great food in a great location! Close to downtown if you are wanting to go out after dinner. Great patio seating as well. I would suggest making a reservation if you have more than 2 people. But if you have two people it's easy to find an open table by the bar with no wait.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Love, love, love the Ryman Auditorium!!!! You must absolutely put the Ryman on your list of places to visit when you are in Nashville, TN. The 11 minute video prior to entering the auditorium offers the audience the experience of being a part of history. The information and exhibits tell an amazing story, and at the end of it all, you can stand on the stage where so many talented singers have stood and have your picture taken. This is the soul of Nashville, you must check it out!

name: Second Fiddle
text: Nashville at it's best.  Good bands.  I just wish they didn't move out the tables and chairs.  Very limited seating so it's difficult to stay here very long.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I didn't know what to expect when walking into the Ryman Theater.  It was a beautiful experience.  Be careful where you park.  Prices vary widely.  BEWARE of Premier Parking.  Their logo is a script font 'P' on a blue background. You can see the logo above the pay station as you drive by.  They are not required to post the prices, so you won't know the cost until you park, unload the family, and are standing in front of the pay station.  If you think you'll add more time later, think again. A: You can't add more time like a parking meter; your time just starts over again. B: they can engage in "rush hour" pricing.  There are many low cost municipal options.  Plan before you go.  I ended up paying $40 for 5 hours of parking at a Premier Lot.  I called them and was told I should know better.  According to online complaints they will easily ticket you, too.  Do yourself a favor and just stay away from their parking lots.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: It was a great backstage tour of the place. You got to see the entire place and learn about the history of the auditorium.  The new video was really cool. I've never experience something like that before.  It is something that you have to experience.  It would come here before I would go to the country music hall of fame,  there is more history and information here to see and experience.

name: Legends Corner
text: Another Nashville staple.  Crowded and loud.  Go in for one drink and band set, then move to another bar.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We had stopped by here for my cousin's birthday a few weeks ago. The place was pretty packed on a Tuesday night and we managed to order food and beers at the bar before snagging a table. The Chris Casello trio was playing the majority of the night and I absolutely loved them! They are such an amazing and talented band! My cousin had a great time for her birthday and her man even got the band and the bar to sing happy birthday for her. Also, the cheeseburger with chips I ordered was very tasty and delicious, I'd come back just for the food alone but everything about this place was awesome. Being from Seattle, I was definitely out of my element, but the people and the environment are so dang inviting, it's hard not to start stomping your boots around after just a short time! I'd love to come back!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Came here hoping for a little but above par food and music. Both were disappointing. Food was cold and pretty bland overall.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Best deal on Honky Tonk Row. A fun, divey place. The special was $5 for bologna sandwich or hot dog and a beer. Live guitar player was good. Just had fun.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Our visit started off poorly when the hostess said "I need your drinks" immediately after greeting us (referring to our empty coffee cups that we would have thrown away had they had a trash can outside). It just seemed extremely rude. 
Once we were seated, our server Robby greeted us and he was amazing from beginning to end. He made great suggestions and never rushed us. He was very laid back and knowledgable in the best possible way.
The food was very good but the difference in portion sizes between the flat iron steak and the salmon was kind of odd. 
The band playing the night we were there was unreal! A lady named sissy was singing with them but I can't recall what the band's name was. 
The only other thing I found odd was the fact that a restaurant this nice has paper dinner menus. 
Overall, great experience!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Solid honky tonk on Broadway with cheap drinks, great live music and no douche bags. Seems there's a reason this is the spot locals say hit up if you must go to Broadway. And you must!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: The food court was awesome! Everything we ordered was delicious. The guy at the juice bar was really friendly and let us sample a couple of things before ordering. The tapas place was awesome, the worst part was only that they had sold out of two items I wanted to try! We went on a Sunday and there was a Mariachi band playing, a kids story time, two different acrobatics shows, and another three piece band. That was all just in the 2 hours we were there. I look forward to going back for more!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Don't hesitate to hit this bar.  It's not the commercialised bar with high priced food and drinks.  $2.50 PBR and MHL.  Simple burger and fry menu, but who cares.  

Highly recommend coming to this "dive" bar.  As always, they usually are the best.  Great place to sit and chill with a band.  

The only drawback is that it's not great for large groups.  Tables are pub style meant for only a few people but you can push them together.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Food was ok passable. Service was slow and inattentive. We had cheese burgers. Music meh next door at orchid was better. But this place has so much potential to be awesome that is why we stopped.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
One of my favorite music venues in the country. Incredible acoustics, unique decor and vintage Americana atmosphere. The seats are similar to church pews. Staff and security here are very friendly and don't take themselves too seriously. I saw a concert here last night and thoroughly enjoyed the entire experience.

Beer and mixed drinks were $9, which is insane, but whatever, the Ryman is so cool that they can get away with it.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Pretty standard honky tonk that has good music every once and a while. The coolest thing is that they serve a poor boy special- a fried bologna sandwich, a bag of chips, and a PBR.

name: Music City Center
text: A great convention and event center, in a great location in downtown Nashville. Parking is the only negative. $15 on a Sunday to park in the garage for the Antiques and Garden Show in the Music City Center is a bit much.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Wow, I can't believe I have been in Nashville for three years and just got around to coming here! The drinks were great, service was excellent and then there was the food. I ordered bruschetta and three sides, asparagus, au gratin potatoes and carrots (I don't eat much meat) and everything was amazing. The bruschetta especially since they serve it in a dish with warm toast which prevents it from getting the bread soggy. I honestly don't remember what my bf got but he loved it as well! The atmosphere is fun and laid back while maintaining a level of classy elegance. Will definitely be going back!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
My wife and I are big fans of Nashville (the city, not the horrible soap opera). Once a year, we make the 925 mile trek to Nashville for music, food, and the fantastic scene. Our first stop is always Robert's Western World. There's nothing fancy about this place. The menu consists of fried bologna sandwiches, burgers, and various tasty fried snacks. Heck, there's even a veggie burger on there. Though they have a full bar and a great selection of bottled beer, that's not what you want. What you want is an ice-cold can of PBR for $2.50. The music is as good as it gets on Broadway. I'm talking fantastic musicians playing old-time, bluegrass, classic country, and honky-tonk. You will not hear any obnoxious bro-country/pop-country. I recommend keeping an eye out for Rachael Hester and Don Kelley Band. Also, no trip to Nashville is complete without catching a set by John and Lois Shepherd. 

As great as the music is at Robert's, the element that holds this whole thing together is the fabulous staff. As soon as you walk up to the bar, you realize that you're dealing with people who like their job. Though we're just tourists on our annual vacation, they immediately make you feel like locals. It's people like Hope B. (not to forget Teresa and Hank) who make your Nashville experience fun and welcoming, as opposed to feeling like just another anonymous patron. 

Nashville is a great city. As much as we love going to The Ryman, or eating at Husk and Rolf and Daughters, it's Robert's Western World that keeps us coming back. Hank you.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: How can anyone NOT like The Ryman?! Been here several times for concerts and love coming every time. The stain glass windows are beautiful, I love the layout of the venue - very intimate.  They recently re-did the entrance and added a cafe, which is awesome. My only complaint is the parking situation. Valet is crazy expensive and if you want to park your car yourself, you still have to pay to park in a lot nearby. No free parking, boo. If you live in Nashville or are visiting, you MUST attend a show here. It's historical, magical, and awe-inspiring!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place great music and good prices on drinks and food. Thanks for a really good time.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I loved the look of this place as we walked in. It was a Sunday night and a great four-piece band was playing music onstage.
We were really well taken care of, with staff that was attentive but not overbearing. 
We shared an order of Buca Beignets, and they were really great. I had a good, not great, Caesar salad and then the 7 oz filet. The steak was prepared to my liking. It wasn't an amazing cut, but it was good. We enjoyed sweet potatoes and Mac and Cheese as sides, both very good.
We finished the meal with a piece of white chocolate cheesecake. It was rich, but not too rich, which made it a little too easy to eat.
I would give it a 4.5 if that was an option. On the strength of the service and great live music, I'm rounding up.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Great live music and cool decor make this place stand out from some of the other places downtown. This bar had a good vibe going on a Thursday night and we could have shut this place down if not for our Friday morning plans. Next time I'm in Nashville I'm paying a visit here

name: Music City Center
text: Good conference center. Clean, convenient, and newish. The staff is helpful and friendly. The food is above average when compared to other conference centers.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: The night we visited a 70's rock cover band, Mood Ring, was playing. I loved it and sand along with every song! My nephew knew one song. Lol. The service was a bit slow but the place has great ambience and the plating was phenomenal, it makes you feel like someone really took the time to care about your meal. We started with the shrimp and crab dip appetizer. It was excellent with freshly cooked tortilla chips. We had the pork chop, Mediterranean veggie lasagna and the lobster ravioli. The food was good but not as phenomenal as the plating. The creme brûlée for desert was excellent. During the bands break the lead singer stopped by our table to chat and ask us if we were enjoying the music. This was a very nice personal touch. We sat at the back booth which was great because we could all mostly see the stage but not too close that we couldn't have a conversation. Nice place!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Came here with my co-workers. What an awesome experience! Our bartender Hope, was the best. Her service was first class. 

The music was old school country. Bob Kelly band were the best. The decor on the wall is cowboy boots and pics of old country western signings. 

They have typical bar food but you need to try the fried bologna sandwich, which is killer!  

If your visiting Nashville you must come to ROBERTS Western World. I will be back!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: So so so delish!!! Shared a bunch of appys and they were all amazing.  Highly recommend

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: AMAZING! Great food and great atmosphere. Somewhat pricey, but 100% worth it. We were seated in front of the live band. Our waiter was great and recommended what he thought was best, which turned out to be perfect. Went with a group of 5 and it was great.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
We had heard great things about this place and the happy hour in particular so we were excited to check it out when we got a gift certificate to go there. The venue is very nice with a large bar area. We placed ourselves at one end of the bar which was a little bit behind a pillar. The food and drinks were good, but we had pretty bad service. I don't know if it was because of the pillar, but we literally finished our drinks and food and nobody checked on us for 20 minutes. We were all set to order more drinks and more food, but because we had to wait so long, I just couldn't stay. 
The food itself was good; we had a great margherita pizza and some good satay. Wine on the happy hour list was among the better we've seen at local places. We would have gotten more, but like I said we just couldn't keep waiting around forever. Maybe we'll try again at some point, but pretty disappointing.

name: Legends Corner
text: Of all of the bars located on Broadway, I'd have to say this was our favorite!  We always enjoyed the bands and the bartender's are friendly and provide great service.  The drinks seemed to be slightly less expensive than the rest of the bars nearby, although everything on Broadway is pricey.  Can't wait to come back!!!

name: Second Fiddle
text: This place is so fun and you can actually move inside. The band is fantastic, the pizza is good and greasy and the drinks are a good pour! A must visit as you do the pub crawl down Broadway.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Only went in for drinks. Bartender was good.

I understand wanting to entice everyone from the street to come in, but the music was a bit loud. We left after just one beer.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Constantly asks u for tips and make fun of u if you don't give it. Awful. Music may be good but attitude sucks big time. Won't come back here again.

name: Legends Corner
text: The Band was fun . Bartenders on the most part ok. Drinks over priced. Staff and bouncers SUPER RUDE!!  Went there with another couple all in our 40's, enjoing the Tim Mcgraw look alike band. Spent alot of $ on drinks and food, we were all standing up by the bar next to a smelly garbage can, so we moved it aside (3x). Busboy kept moving it back. Then he went and got an over weight (B Team Bouncer) to kick us all out. Is that how you treat your clientele? People come to Nashville to enjoy the Honky Tonks and listen to bands. They should not be treated like 2nd rate citizens. Alot of the reviews for Legends say the same thing. Maybe if an owner or a good manager would be on duty, this place could be better. What would happen if word gets around how bad the Bars in Nashille treat the folks who travel from far away places. What if your business starts slowing down and its not a $ maker anymore, would the Owners pay attention then? WHAT HAPPENED TO THE CUSTOMER IS ALWAYS RIGHT?     Time to train customer Service!!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Came in with my mom for lunch and got the spinach and goat cheese omelette, which came with breakfast potatoes and fruit.  The food was really good, but even better was the build your own Bloody Mary bar!  They bring you a glass with vodka and you add your own bloody mix along with olives, pickles, bacon, and anything else you can think of!!  The atmosphere was also very cool with a live band and our server was very friendly as well!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Ryman is a beautiful place full of history that is well worth a visit. Nothing wrong with the building or tour. 
We went on a $20 tour. 

Neat video. 

Here's what I don't like:
This is Nashville, Tennessee, and 6 of the 10 people in our group had basic pocketknives. This is the SOUTH. 

The utterly stupid security rules don't allow for any kind of pocketknife. You go through metal detectors. My belt buckle set off the alarm. One of our group members had to walk back a mile to the car to drop off our "weapons". (Swiss army knives and a leatherman) 

He missed the tour, at least they refunded his ticket money. 

But that's just ridiculous. Again, this is Tennessee. 

Oh, and they will charge $20 for a photo on the edge of the stage. You can't use your phone. 

I loved the bulding, but the policies really made it feel uninviting and were 100% unnecessary.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
A colleague wanted to try out Sambuca since it was nearby and was a bit different than the other restaurants in Nashville.  The menu looked delicious with items ranging from lobster enchiladas to a red snapper étouffeé.  However, the food itself was just "meh" and wasn't really memorable.  We happened to be there on a night with live music and were seated right in front of the stage.  Although a conversation may be possible if you were seated further back, I could barely hear myself up front. 

One highlight of my experience is the Tennessee Mule, which is served in a pretty big glass (maybe it was more surprising to me since I'm used to those little copper mugs).  The dinner was okay; I might try to come back for their bar and see if they have a happy hour!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Didn't eat or drink here. Walked in, started to go upstairs and was told no one's serving up there. Went to bar downstairs but waited a few minutes and no service. Moved on. Band seemed ok. Typical country band. Crowd was tame and around age 50. Went on a Wednesday around 5:30 though.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Don't go to Robert's for the food or the service.  Go to Robert's to hear great country music and for drinks.  Among all of the bars in downtown Nashville, this one had the best ambience and feel about what Nashville is all about.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
We are vegan and try to find adventure in the many restaurant experiences in Nashville. Madera in the Plaza Mariachi did not disappoint . We had the corn cakes stuffed with vegetables , the jicama salad and the jackfruit entree.
So much flavor, fun, and excitement. all were colorful and full of unusual flavors.
We will return to repeat the experience .
Thank you, Madera.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Best venue in Nashville, without a doubt.

Best venue in the US?  Quite possibly.

So blessed to live half a mile away from The Ryman.  Every show is an experience that you'll never forget.  I honestly could see anyone there and enjoy it... even if I wasn't too familiar with the artist.  The acoustics are one in a million and the building is absolutely stunning.

Tip:  While buying tickets, if you can't get up close... the balcony seats are much better than the far back floor seats.  Definitely!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My flatiron steak was gristly and tasted like a whole bottle of spicy rub was poured on it. I couldn't taste the potatoes or the cheese in the au gratin potatoes for the copious amount of garlic-I love garlic, but that was was too much. My stomach hurt an hour or two after eating, then my guts-still 15 hours later. I would have sent it back but for two reasons- 1. I didn't want date night to be ruined. 2. Courtney, asked if everything LOOKED good, after I had had only one bite of green beans. Then nothing. The coconut mojito was good, though overpriced. The band's selection were decent, but the vocalist was sick, so he sounded bad, which the restaurant manager pointed out to us. Too bad he didn't stay long enough to ask what I thought of my meal.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My wife and I had a wonderful time the food and service was great. The jazz band was awesome, this is my favorite new place to come to in Nashville. If you are in Nashville this is a must visit.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
What a nice addition to south Nashville! From the outside you'd never know how upscale, classy and cool this place is (as you know it used to just be a shopping center Kroger). Inside is beautiful, great art and architecture. A lot of great Latin and Hispanic business, food, drink, snacks and desserts. Great customer service, friendly folks everywhere including guest service coordinators making the rounds and introducing themselves.

Live music that is of excellent quality, clean and new, original and creative. We strolled through many of the stores, my friends grabbed a margarita at the Cuban restaurant, we chowed down on some delicious ice cream at the Paletas Tocumbo.

Stop in next time you are in south Nashville!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Even if you are not into country music, you have to take this tour. It's self guided and will teach you about the history of how music made its way into Nashville. The Ryman embraces all. The 15 minute movie at the start giving the history of the Ryman is very interesting. Very reasonably priced way to learn some Nashville history.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I'm not even a country western music fan, but I loved it. The tour was worth every penny!!!!!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Hot Saturday afternoon and we were looking for music and cold drinks.

We immediately found a booth even though the place was pretty crowded.  Quick service.  Amazing $2 tea and soda in huge cups.  Attentive service and free refills.  Great music.  Fun place!

name: Music City Center
text: While the facility was nice beware of the conference food.  I was served raw chicken at lunch. The breakfast muffins tasted like they came out of a jiff box.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Wandered in and found an amazing place. Good drinks (had the moonshine margarita) and snacked on the chicken 'n waffle nuggets. We were fighting over those suckers. Did I mention bacon? 
Music was loud and great to rock out to. A must stop as you walk down Broadway.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Robert's Western World was exactly what I needed after a long flight. It was the first bar I went to in Nashville, and it had live music and an open kitchen.

It's a long bar with a lot of seating, but it gets crowded (especially with the dedicated cowboy boot rack on the wall). I watched the Don Kelley band here twice, and both times they rocked the house.

The bar takes up more than half the side of the place, which is both good and bad. It's good because there's a ton of bar seating, and it's bad because it's tough to get a bartender's attention.

That said, I ordered the Recession special - a fried bologna sandwich, bag of chips, and a PBR for the low, low price of $5. Was it worth $5? Definitely. Would I order it again? Probably not.

The grill man was doing a great job, but the waitstaff was a bit backed up and food was just sitting on the counter for a while.

The fried bologna sandwich is a misnomer. No part of it is fried. The bologna is grilled. The bread is grilled. But it was definitely a bologna sandwich.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
The ambience, atmosphere and the music make this place truly unique. It's never a dull evening at the restaurant. The food has always been great. I've personally only had the pizza, but what great pizza it was. 

The wait staff were exceptional. Even on a day when they were busier than usual r waitress provided just amazing service in the bar area nonetheless.

Very positive experience and i can't wait to go again.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This place was one of the best spots I checked out while in Nashville. The band "Casello Trio" or something like that was the best band we saw. Three older guys playing rockabilly with obvious talent and skills to spare. I had a few BPRs and was really tempted to try the "fried bologna" deal for just $5 bucks. Its the sandwich, a bag a chips and a PBR for just $5 bucks! Amazing! In NYC this doesn't exist. PBR alone is at least $4 bucks. 

This is the obvious stop for anyone's honkytonk tour ..

name: Robert's Western World
text: My significant otter and I decided to do the Broadway touristy thing during our stay in Nashville and I'm so glad we selected Robert's Western World. Great burgers and fried bologna. Excellent service - one woman was waiting on everyone and making the drinks on our Thursday afternoon visit. She's awesome! Great band!! They played all the classics and sounded fantastic on each.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: My wife and I stopped in late one afternoon after hearing the music as we explored Broadway. The band was playing bluesy covers and sounded great. We grabbed a local beer (Mantra Saffron IPA), found a table and enjoyed the music. It was before the evening rush so the timing was perfect for us. We had a great time. I'd definitely go back.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: This is absolutely my favorite spot ever. It has live music and fantastic food! I've been several times and every time I like it more and more. The music is fantastic! Great Cocktails and ambiance! So far for my Nashville spots this is my favorite!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Ryman is beautiful.  Nestled in the streets of Nashville, it's a well kept, beautiful building full of so much history.  It's so clean and well cared for, you could almost believe it was built today with the throw back style.  It's small - which we loved, and made for a very intimate show (and we were in the back row!).  I'll admit, the whole church pew thing freaked me out a bit.  I worried what if I was next to some seat hogs, or people who were eating popcorn and throwing it all over the place, or what if the seat numbers weren't really numbers.  But, once I sat, the seat was comfortable, I had plenty of space, and most important, we had a great view of the stage.

The sound is amazing - and I am sure that's why it's been used by so many stars.  Hands down one of the best venues to see a concert.

And, I'd suggest the balcony- unobstructed views.  It looks like the orchestra (aside from the first few rows) has a less open view.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Oh course you have to stop by Robert's. Classic country music, cheap beer, and a must see bar. The great things about the Broadway honky tonks is that you just walk next door to see what's up there once you've had a beer or two at the first (or fourth) place!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: I think this is the only bar on Broadway I actually liked. Beer and drinks are reasonably priced. The security was super nice. They threw out a guy who was incredibly inappropriate with my friend. The music was great, and I loved the vibe. Really liked this place!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: I enjoyed the food and vibes here. I got pork tacos and they had this really good peach salsa kind of thing on top which was easily my favorite part. The reason I can only give 3 stars is that the layout is not good for listening to / seeing the live music. The venue goes back very far but is very narrow so only the few people at the front can really see the musicians.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place has an incredibly chill vibe.  Everyone is a mixture of ages and just there to have a good beer, burger, and most important time. Go!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This place was recommended by a friend so my boyfriend and I stopped in one evening while checking out Broadway. The band was playing covers of pop music (not old country) which was okay but I liked the old country band at Robert's Western World better. The interior of Tin Roof is really cool with Christmas lights, neon signs, a comfy lounge area with couches and an overall retro vibe. That's where the charm ended for me. Our bartender wasn't very attentive and seemed much more interested in flirting with the girl sitting next to us (her boyfriend was NOT amused). We had one drink and then headed out. Overall I felt very "meh" about Tin Roof.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Awesome music, lots of food choices., family friendly. This a a great place for Sunday afternoon in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
My favorite bar on Earth

Visiting Nashville and this was the gem on Broadway.  Non stop live music.  And every band we saw was fantastic.  Loved the setup with all the boots and murals on the walls.  People love to dance here and I don't blame them one bit.  
Drinks on this street are brutally expensive but RWW has you covered with $2.50 PBR & Busch beer.  I was also a big fan of the $4 grilled cheese and the fried pickles.  
We went every night and sometimes during the day.  I wish I could go back.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
Great new place just opened!  Terrific for families and kids complete with live music playing & a game room for kids.  Variety of restaurants and choices and shopping all in one area with free parking.

Good authentic Mexican, Cuban and even Greek?? Food.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Tried this place for lunch due to the high reviews. Fun dive bar/honkytonk atmosphere and dirt cheap food. Got the recession special which is a fried bologna sandwich, chips, and a PBR for 5 bucks. Nowhere else in downtown Nashville can touch that. Only one server working the bar when I was there so it took a little time to get her attention and place my order as it looked like she was struggling to keep up with the pace of business. Might want to avoid it if you're in a rush but if you wanna sit for a while, listen to some music, and eat cheap food there's no better option in the area.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: too pricey for what you're given- starter side salad is $9 with no protein. came for the live music but the singer took a break for over 20 minutes and we finished our dinner in the mean time....service is fast. The dill hollandaise for the Salmon Oscar was really tasty but the salmon itself was way too salty and the portion was so small for the price.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Absolutely the best place to enjoy live music! The acoustics are incredible. The atmosphere is wonderful. Sitting in the pews is so fun! My only complaint: do NOT, I repeat, do NOT, use the valet service to park. It is so poorly operated, under staffed, and a huge disappointment. It seriously took them 55 minutes to get my car after a show. No exaggeration: 55 minutes. Do yourself a favor and park in a nearby garage and walk to the Ryman! But don't miss any opportunity to see live music at the gem!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: An absolute must see, even if you are not a country music fan! It boggles my mind to think about the amazing talent that has graced that stage,what a great representation of American popular culture, my family throughly enjoyed this tour! Don't think about going, Just Go!!!

name: Musicians Corner
text:
If I had any doubts about how incredible Nashville is, they were completely quelled by the wonderful afternoon I had enjoying FREE live music at Centennial Park on Saturday. 

I absolutely love the support this city shows its musicians and what a wonderful way to let the community enjoy local artists without paying for a concert ticket!! They also offer a cash beer garden and had 5 or 6 food trucks lined up for patrons to enjoy. They offer this concert series in the Spring and Fall, so be sure to watch for events and stop in for a lovely afternoon!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Went here for a bachelorette party. We had an amazing server. So that wasn't what got the three stars. It's all about the food. It was just not in line with what you expect to get for that price. I suppose you are paying for the ambiance and live music. The risotto under the scallops was very dry. The lobster enchiladas were also just dry and bland. No one at the whole table finished their plate.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Try the recession special. Best fried bologna you'll ever have (except for grandmas!)

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: This was my first time going 1/18/13 for my bfs bday. We did a reservation through the opentable app so we got there an was seated in 10min. Looooove the atmosphere an band that was there that night. So the food was good but highly priced for the small portion. I got a Caesar sald an champagne chicken my bf got the filet. It was good but we left hungry. I'd go back probably just for cocktails though. Very sexy place though.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: So really should have asked to see a manager to give them a chance to correct our experience, but when 5+/- things go badly right from the get-go, you're just kinda over it and want to get out of there. My husband and I came to dine here tonight. We are out of towners and did not make a reservation. It was after 8pm on a Sunday evening however, so it really shouldn't have been too much of an issue. We were greeted by a hostess who was presently snacking on something. Not professional but we all get hungry so no big deal. She promptly asked if we had a reservation which we replied no. She then stated they did not have availability until 9pm but that the bar area was full service. We were more than happy to sit at the bar, order an app and some drinks, and wait for a table. I then inquired if we could have a table on the patio when it became available (which there were several empty already but I understood they may be reserved). Here is when things really went wrong. The hostess stated no because "we wouldn't get proper service" and that they are "very particular with their patio seating". I have never in my life been told we couldn't sit somewhere because we wouldn't get service, nor did I ever tell anyone that in my 10+ years in the restaurant business. Stunned by her response, we took a high top table at the bar. It was a good 5 minutes before we were greeted and then it was very apparent that the bar staff were overwhelmed and we weren't going to get good service anyway. We went ahead and ordered drinks however and she brought my drink but stated they were out of one of the key ingredients and never even asked if I would maybe want something else. Then we went to order the calamari which she stated they were also out of. She did not offer or suggest anything else so we just ordered a salad, had our drinks, and tabbed out. Very disappointed as this is our 3rd year wedding anniversary trip and this place had great ambiance and music.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This is a living, breathing piece of music history.  Johnny Cash, Loretta Lynn, Elvis, The Band, you name it, they've played The Ryman (which played host to the Grand Ole Opry program for decades).

It's a great building with church-style seating.  The museum tour is interesting and - for a fee - you can record a song (either from a list of options or an original of your own) in a small on-site recording booth.

Recommended for any music fans, casual or serious, or for anyone generally interested in a slice of American history.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Greasy burger deliciousness and outstanding old school country. Loved this place maybe my favorite in Nashville. Can't wait to hang again.

name: Legends Corner
text: Great Honkytonk.  Not your biggest not your smallest but the beer is cold and the music is great.  It is a great place to start or end the night

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I used to love this place, but this time it was awful:( the service was slow, food was not good, especially for the price, and they cut their portions, and music was so loud my throat hurts from trying to talk to the guests at our table over the music. Used to be a nashville fave, I won't be sad to never return!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: The music is alright. Not too loud that you can't hold a conversation towards the back, which is nice. The service is great! Our server made sure our drinks were never empty and our plates were cleared quickly. The gator tots are amazing! The smashville burger was just alright.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Mother Church of country music! Need I say more?

To see a concert in the Ryman is to be part of history. This is a must do in Nashville. We loved every minute of our Country Classics show.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Wonderful place! Great food, great deserts, friendly atmosphere. Highly recommended and whole family fun!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great spot for live music! Out of all the bars I visited on my first trip to Nashville last weekend, this bar had the best band playing. Vibe inside is cool and loved all of the boot/wall art!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Visited Nashville for the first time and stopped by this bar first. Band was great and played a variety of music. I'm not a country music fan so it was refreshing as I assumed I'd hear country all night. Fair drink prices and good atmosphere!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This was pretty cool. We did the backstage tour, it was neat to see the rooms, hear some history and get to go on the stage. The displays around the venue are cool, wish we would have known that you have to reserve the make a cd ahead of time, that seemed like it would be fun.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Nice life music. Great margarita. The only bad thing was how to u run out of local beer???!! Such a shame!

name: Robert's Western World
text: I came here on a friends recommendation. She said they have really good burgers. This was definitely true. The burgers were fantastic and fresh. We had appetizers and sides and all were great. Our waitress was friendly and very attentive despite the crowds. They had live music while we were there too. If you have a big party, I'd recommend getting their early.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I took a client to Sambuca for lunch and it was phenomenal! The service was precise and the food was outstanding from the beignets to the sea bass. The flavors were so precise and the ambience was great for lunch. I will be back!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I have been to two concerts at the Ryman so far, and both have been great experiences. As a venue, you can't beat it. It has great acoustics and loads of character. When bands play here, it seems like they're really at the top of their game and put on the best show possible.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We went to Nashville for our first time and found this bar on Yelp so figured we'd give it shot. The line was kind of long but it was worth it! Great bartenders and a great atmosphere. The music was really good and just a great time! We found a seat at the bar and stayed for a couple of hours. Will definitely be going back!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Music and staff were great - location, decor, very good. Food was blah. Macaroni was garnished with brisket, not a lot of meat as implied. Also had the pulled pork nachos and they were just OK.  Overall a good experience but I wouldn't recommend this as a place to eat, especially if you're trying to squeeze only the best into a long weekend. I would gladly go back for drinks though!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
