text: Hmmmm... In Nashville for an event or live in Nashville but can't decide where to go?!? I recommend here!! Much different than other Broadway locations they truly pull off live music & sports well.  They have a good TV setup and their bands are decent.  With two floors, multiple bars, outdoor smoking section, plenty of bathrooms, full bar, happy hour, and a decent menu they hit all my top categories!  We have tried multiple places as a "sports bar" all over Nashville and this is in the top 5 and its downtown as an added plus! Come here for your favorite game and you'll not be disappointed!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
What I liked:
1. This is phenomenal music venue.  The acoustics are strong and even the back of the house is closer than most shows.
2. The line-ups- whether it's the Opry or an up and coming band, there's terrific variety and I've never seen a bad show there - my first was OCMS and several of the Nashville stars- they were all just terrific.

What I didn't like:
1. Many of the seats are partial view- just beware.

The Verdict:
If you like music, any music, it would be a shame not to have seen a show at the Ryman.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Love this place! The food is excellent, the music doesn't blow your ears out (for those of us tag grew up in the 70's) - can't wait to come back!

name: Robert's Western World
text: We come here just about every time we're on Broadway.  Have a PBR, kick back to some of the best music you'll here anywhere and if you get hungry have a fried bologna sandwich.  Great honky tonk.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Even though we don't drink, we still stopped by this place to experience Nashville's nightlife. This place was packed on a Saturday night. People were wild. The live music was not bad but I did wish that the band member didn't come around with a tip jar.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: One of the best places we ate in Nashville. Our waiter, Cory C, was awesome. The red snapper was absolutely incredible and the cheesecake rolls were to die for. The ambience of the place was perfect, good for a romantic dinner or relaxing night on the town. One of the few places we went to that had a live band playing super chill jazz music as well. Overall great atmosphere, great service, and great food.

name: Musicians Corner
text: Musician's Corner is back!  This is a great way to spend your Saturday and there is fun for the whole family.  Musician's corner is a stage set up in Centennial Park where musician's come and play for 3-4 hours on Saturdays through the summer.  If the weather is nice, there will be people and dogs and kids everywhere!  There are also food trucks around the park and a beer/wine garden available.  It's free to get in so bring your family, dogs and children and come enjoy the music!  We usually bring people from out of town for a fun afternoon with some great musicians. Check it out!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Love this place! Best music in town, and the fried bologna sandwich and PBR (though not gourmet) is a classic rockabilly staple.

name: Robert's Western World
text: My mom and I came here after our tour guide George from the Country Music Hall of Fame recommended it. We're from California and it was awesome to get some southern hospitality here. We liked it so much that we came back the next day, and both of our bartenders (Hope and Teresa) were AWESOME. I got my fried pickle fix and the drinks and music were great. For anyone visiting downtown Nashville looking for a great, laid back place, this is it!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Went in for the first time, drawn in by the live music.  

Music was great but bar was a little too cramped for me.  We were also really hungry and it took forever to get some pretty basic food.  

Not sure if we'll be returning here when we venture into the city.  

Depending on your taste in country music, this might be a good place for a couple of beers.  Not the place to grab a meal.

name: Legends Corner
text: An authentic honky tonk (especially compared to some of the new bars on the strip). Good music. Smells kinda weird inside. The staff we encountered were pleasant.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This was such a cool place to visit and I highly recommend it. Of course, it's very well recommended and is therefore a tourist magnet but that's ok - they still deliver.

A Honky Tonk band play in the corner at the entrance with several instruments. The room is pumping. People are dancing in front and having an awesome time. The bar is spread out with people against it watching the band. All the tables but one are taken. We grab it and order a beef burger each, $6. These burgers are excellent, my husband said they were among the best he's had which means they're pretty good.

The bad sell CD's for $15 and will sign them or you can just tip at the end of a set. This is so important to do as they're not getting paid by the bar to perform. You don't pay to get in so think about how much you've enjoyed it and tip accordingly. $3 gets you a beer so no big deal, right?

Check it out.

name: Second Fiddle
text:
Not all Honky Tonks are created equal and after coming to the Second Fiddle I began to understand the differences. 

It seemed like this place catered to a slightly older crowd. The band playing when we came on a Saturday night left much to be desired. The lead singer looked so unamused and there were points where she turned her back to the audience or where she was texting during the song. It was really sad to be honest. 

There were a few people dancing on the dance floor but the music wasn't all that entertaining. 

We left at the end of their set for a larger Honky Tonk to listen to good entertainers and better music.

name: Legends Corner
text: Stopped by for a drink after a concert , was easy to  get in, ordered cold beer, found A bar ranks to rest a few, staff was friendly. Could see this as a fun place on a busy night

name: Robert's Western World
text: ロンリープラネットで紹介されてた所。4時に行ってもめちゃくちゃ混んでる。朝から常に音楽が演奏されてるらしく、いつ行ってもいい。演奏も上手でカントリー調。店員さんが驚く程美人。

name: Robert's Western World
text: Really great honkeytonk atmosphere in there with the live music and southern feel but WAY too small of a venue. May be good if you go by yourself for a quick couple drinks but if you don't get a table you'll end up cramming up against someone sitting at a table/bar making it awkward. I also found I was moving out of the way a lot for people. Not to add this was on a Monday. It's worth checking out but not a place you'd wanna stay at for too long.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
There's clearly a rich & worthy legacy to this venue & it's obviously well-deserved.  Nashville is after all, widely regarded as "Music City," & this is one of its most famous concert halls.  However, that's not to say there's no room for improvement.

Obviously, the acoustics are outstanding.  But as an audience member, there are issues with comfort & site lines.  As the seating is church pews, I didn't know whether to clap between songs or tell the person seated next to me "Peace be with you."  This seating also leads to the unfortunate habit of "manspreading, which wouldn't happen with individual seats.  

Also problematic were the support beams that obstructed the view for many audience members.  Obviously, had the balcony above come crashing down on them, their view would really have been obstructed, but it seems a design flaw that could be remedied.  I suspect at this point nothing can be done because the building is a landmark? But that's unfortunate.

Finally, their camera policy.  I was there recently for one of two Paul Simon concerts.  Prior to the performance, an announcement was made that CLEARLY stated that photography was allowed, as long as it was no video & non-flash.  So, people began taking photos, until ushers started telling them not to.  So, which is it?  If photography is allowed, inform your ushers prior to the show.  If it's not, don't play a pre-recorded announcement confusing 2000+ audience members.

Otherwise, it's a lovely venue inside an out & the Ryman should be part of your Nashville experience.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Hi, I'm Matt and I don't really like country music.  Why on earth did the wife get us a backstage small tour of this place?  Almost all of my country music history came from the Graceland and Sun Studio tours in Memphis, but you know what?  This tour was interesting and our tour guide was knowledgeable and passionate about the Ryman.  I loved hearing about the follow up from stories we heard in Memphis about Elvis and other country singers.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Frequent stopping point for us each time we're in nashville. Fried pickles, bologna sandwiches and cheeseburger on Texas toast can't be beat!! Quick, tasty, and entertaining as well. Definitely recommend.

name: Legends Corner
text: Great atmosphere, great music, friendly staff. We stopped in during a bachelorette trip this weekend and ended up staying until closing time. Loved it

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: An absolute must even if you are not a Country fan. Nice video presentation on the history of the building as well as familiar exhibits. Good fun for the family

name: Second Fiddle
text: The bartenders were goofing off & not paying attention to the customers the doorman called my wife Grandma, the band were poor. This was easily the worst club on Broadway!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The venue in itself is not bad. It intimate. However there are several support columns that will block you view. Now the issue I had was the valet parking. After the show, it was well over 2 hours before we were able to retrieve our cars. And that was because we walked (a group of about 20 ppl) and followed the valet drivers to get our car for a garage a block away. I would so recommend this auditorium but not the valet parking.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Best honky tonk on Broadway, hands down. I tried going to other honky tonks but the music was never as authentic and the crowd was never as lively like at Robert's. I went there on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday night, and every single day the bands were just as good and the crowd just as rowdy. The bands they showcase are always extremely talented and put on an awesome performance. 

The beers are dirt cheap too. I haven't tried their food but it looks good! The service is also very friendly and attentive despite how loud it is in there.

This place is the only honky tonk you should go to. And ALWAYS tip the band and the servers, it's only common courtesy. It's just plain rude for you to not tip the band performing their hearts out.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Yummy yummy dinner, they helped me throw the perfect bachelorette party dinner. Everyone was raving about how delicious the food was for the rest of the weekend! The steak was cooked perfectly, the salmon was pink and flaky, the potatoes and veggies were delicious, down to the drinks and shot included with our specialty menu, fantastic! Would recommend for parties and couples a million times over and would come back to Nashville just to eat here!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
My girlfriends threw me a surprise birthday dinner here and it was a great experience!  It was just three of us, and my friend that called ahead of time said the lady that helped her was very accommodating over the phone.  We sat upstairs on the little balcony that overlooks the stage.  The decor was very elegant and I'm surprised the look and ambiance has remained so nice considering how long this restaurant  has been open (note: it's been at least 5 years since I visited here last).

We had some cocktails and ordered appetizers.  Everything tasted yummy.  But the BEST part was that the live band serenaded me by singing "Amanda" by Waylon Jennings for my birthday!  They were great!  

Our server was very friendly and made sure we were taken care of.  There is valet, but the restaurant does not validate the valet tickets because they are a separate company.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is the perfect Honky Tonk. The gold standard. If you don't like Robert's Western World, then f*ck you.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Frozen hamburgers and fried bologna sandwiches are the limited menu options. $2.50 Busch lights and an assortment of other beer at around $5 each are on the opposite side of the menu. 

All ages until 6 pm and the servers are very friendly to children and adults alike. 

The men working the door are inviting and the have hour long stage sets so you are bound to hear something you like. 

The bathrooms are surprising clean and overall this was a huge highlight to my weekend trip in Nashville. My pre teen asked to return the next day. So we did!

Would have like to see one thing on menu that wasn't frozen or fried.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I had read good things about Robert's Western World and I am happy to say that the reviews are true. Robert's is just what one might imagine a honky tonk should be. Excellent musicians, we especially enjoyed Rachael Hester & The Tennessee Walkers, friendly staff like Kate and good drinks.  We will definitely make a point of spending time at Robert's whenever we come back to Nashville.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
I have been to Plaza Mariachi a few times now and will definitely keep going back. Every time I got there it's a different experience and I think that really adds to the fun of it. You never know what you will find at Plaza Mariachi! 

Plaza Mariachi is a shopping and restaurant venue (mall?) off of Nolensville. It is pretty new and you can really tell a lot of thought went into the planning of this place. The outside and inside are beautiful and very well kept. Parking is never a problem because the parking lot is pretty big. When you first walk in the door, you forget that you are in Nashville. This place has so much culture and personality. It's described as the style of traditional marketplace streets of Old Mexico with Latin history weaved in. In the plaza you will find retail stores, a grocery store, restaurants, a small arcade, and a food court area that transforms into an entertainment center/concert hall. There has always been live music when I have been there. The mariachi bands are incredible. They also have various performing acts. When I was there last, there was an aerial show performing with the mariachi band. It was so much fun to get some delicious food and watch the show. All for free! Well, not the food but you get what I mean. I have reviewed the food places separately but just know that you won't be disappointed eating here! The prices are fair, the food is fresh and oh so good. There is also a full bar if you fancy a drink or two. I've heard of some other fun activities that occur at the plaza so I NEED to get in and try them out. For example, they offer free salsa lessons during the week. I want to say it's every Thursday night. I also have heard that the time to go is on the weekends at night. The food court area turns into a sort of night club with more live music, dancing, and drinks. Where else are you going to get a cool experience like this in Nashville? It would definitely make for a fun night out full of great food, drinks, and music. 

So basically what I'm saying Nashvillians is Plaza Mariachi is an experience to be had. This is Music City and Plaza Mariachi delivers nothing but excellent live music every time.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
Fun place to be at. There is a lot of things going on from grocery to live music, mariachi and ping pong table.

I've been here a couple times now and it's a great atmosphere. Love playing ping pong with the family and got some churros and tacos.

Note: most places have a 50% military discount.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Good for what it is. A honky tonk type bar true to its name. Drinks were cheap but nothing impressive. It was relatively dirty but I guess there's only so much you can do to keep the bar clean when it's packed. There were a bunch of creepy guys around.. my friend had her butt smacked by a random guy while walking by.. but I guess there's nothing the bar can do about that. Not my cup of tea but okay to check out for 10 minutes tops.

name: Legends Corner
text:
This bar is great 
Music and staff was on point.! 
And prices are good,good amount is seats and nice dance floor. No cover,great looking spot.
Can't wait to go back on my next Nashville trip.!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This was my favorite place that we toured in Nashville. I would highly recommend it. This is also one of the 14 stops on most of the hop-on-hop-off tour trolleys if you are a tourist. 

The outside of the building and architecture is incredible once you find out when it was built. We did the self-guided tour, cost about $25. They also have a guided tour were you can go backstage. All tours start out with a video that explains the history and start of the Ryman. The video is presented in a really cool way and not just a video on a screen. I learned a lot about the history that I didn't know. 

Once the video is over they let you wander through the building and look at all the donated mementos of people that have performed at the Ryman. There are also little tv's at some of the displays showing past shows and acts. There is a large display on the opposite side of the entrance doors on the second level that explains the entire history of the Ryman. It was neat to see all the famous and incredible people that have visited. 

There are more display cases on the ground level and a little recording studio that you can test out your singing and guitar abilities at. There is also a little roped off area at the front of the stage where a worker will take a photo of you, the photo is included with the ticket purchase. Most people were just having him take photos with their phones anyway. The tour itself is pretty quick and you can finish it in under 1 hour easy, depending on how long you stand and read everything. The seating is two levels and there isn't a bad seat in the house. 

We did learn that the building was going to be torn down in the '70s but the singers, with the help of Emmy Lou Harris, rallied together to save it. Walking through there I couldn't believe that anyone at any point would want to tear that building down. They still have concerts and acts performing at this location half the year and the other half they are out at the Grand Ole Opry. Everyone that we talked to said the sound quality is unlike anything else. We will be back to see a show on our next visit.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
I went to the Tin Roof 3 times.  Food was good. 

Wait staff awesome. Friendly, helpful and provided get service.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
For Plaza Mariachi to only be a few months old, it's very impressive what they've put together. Obviously, something on this scale... with this vision... took a long time to execute and produce but from most all who have been here, the wait and effort was worth it. For purposes of this review, I am reviewing PM as a destination/venue/center. I think the various businesses that make up PM should be reviewed and rated on their own.

From the minute you pull in to the lot, you'll be impressed. PM stands tall on a hill and its imposing character demands respect. Walking past the cool landscaping and in the main doorway, look up to pay some mind to the impressive chandelier. There are touches like that throughout the venue. From the textured walls to the paint choices to the lighting to the architectural choices, no detail was left untouched. The various hallways bear names of places and add a nice conversation piece to the exploration you're bound to do.

What impresses me most is the diversity of options at PM. Yes, there's a large food court with plenty of South American, Central American and Caribbean styles from which to choose but there's also a grocery store, ice cream shop, radio station, jewelry store, art gallery, a kids' playground, dance studio, sports shop, and other stores to patronize. You could make a day of shopping and eating here. And, being Nashville, there's live music every day in the food court. From emerging artists to local favorites to big names, there's all manner of entertainment to be had. And to the diversity of stores, add a diversity of people. Glencliff's population has been predominantly Latino for a little while now and PM celebrates that and invites people from throughout the metro to come in and see what's happening. Perhaps now Nashville neophytes will finally stop exclaiming that 'there are no authentic 'fill in blank' in Nashville' once they come here. 

There's a ton of potential at PM and it's very cool to see what they've accomplished in only a few months. As more tenants come in and the plaza becomes more of a neighborhood staple and metro destination, I am eager to see how it settles in and cements itself as a fixture of Music City. A couple of final thoughts: PM management/ownership is thoughtful and forward-thinking. This will serve the plaza well. And if you stop by Nina's Nieves, ask for Daniel. After I had an atrocious (review to come) experience at a PM restaurant, I was bowled over by Daniel's enthusiasm, professionalism and fantastic attitude. Plaza Mariachi powers that be need to do what they need to do to hold on to this young man. He's an asset to the organization.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Hot licks and honky tonk in Nashville's premier rocks off joint, Robert's Western World. Hell, tourists will flock here, don't let that discourage you. Locals are engrained into their bar stools here. Seriously, they don't budge even for a dollar!

One of the coolest live music venues I experienced in 2018, hands down. The music was firing on all cylinders. Upright bass, a child prodigy riffing on the electric guitar, and the crowd energetic as can be. 

Things of note that may sell or not sell you on Robert's:

1. Doesn't matter what time or which night you visit, the room will be packed like sardines. Expecting a seat? Yeah, fat chance.

2. Bands in Nashville are notorious for making their living on tips. Confrontational encounters with band members storming through the crowd looking for a quick buck are imminent. 

3. Going to the bathroom will take every bone in your body to power through the audience. Maybe just hold it?

You know I'm a cocktail and craft beer enthusiast. When you come to Robert's, order a High Life or PBR, and maybe a shot of Wild Turkey. You're here for the music and the music only, not pizzazz.

I'm itching to return!!

name: Legends Corner
text:
With so many spots to choose from in Nashville, especially on Music Row, it's hard to say which ones are the best of the bunch. It really depends on the band that's playing, and the crowd in the joint. 

Legends stuck out because it was thoroughly entertaining in the middle of the afternoon and we were still recovering from the previous night out on Music Row. We were able to grab a table and a few chairs in the back, and stayed for a few hours. The decor is a bunch of old album covers on the walls and other memorabilia. 

We got there during the last couple songs of a band playing, so we had to wait for the next band to set up. This next band had a lead, who was an entertainer. Good musician, but also told stories/jokes between songs and really engaged the crowd. The band was good, the music was fun, and the beers were cold. We had a great time! Though it's pretty hard not to have a great time in Nashville.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Beware. This place has got have have the worst service ever. We were there for a concert and literally had to wave our waitress down every time we wanted something. She would just ignore the tables until you stood up and stopped her. Then she would bring incorrect orders to the table and act like it was our fault. Management didn't seem to think this was a problem.  We have been there 3 times and each time the service got worse.  Three strikes. We're done!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: As many years back as I can remember, I have been frequenting the Loveless Café as I have travelled on I 40 east to Nashville TN and sometimes Charlotte NC. Famous for deceased employee Carol Fay's secret biscuit recipe, this place has tripled in size through the years. Biscuits, preserves, and gravy are still good as ever. The breakfast eggs cooked perfectly. The salt pork ham perfectly aged and prepared. The Southern grits extra creamy and also cooked to perfection. But the star of our breakfast table was the tender, crispy Southern Fried chicken half. Oh my goodness, what a wonderful place! Perfect service and plenty of space with the friendliest employees you'll ever meet.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Please... it is so commercialized and far from authentic that whatever it's roots were are long lost.  Better off finding a little diner with big fluffy biscuits and great eggs than waiting an hour and a half for mediocre food and a big bill.  If you want the branded stuff they sell you can find it in downtown Nashville all over the place.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: The beer selection was good. I liked being able to order 1L of beer like you're able to in bavaria. The food was a 5 out of 10.  My weisswurst was decent though it didn't taste like they had actually made the sausage itself and the gravy on my potatoes tasted just like the kind you get out of a jar at the grocery. The potatoes themselves tasted a bit like chemicals...fake garlic perhaps? My husband's meal was better. So you could find something good there if you were willing to endures a few misses first. I would go back to drink but not to eat. Our server was friendly and the atmosphere was fun.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: YUM. To everything. Just be prepared for a really long wait unless you go at an off time of day.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Yep. It's as good as everyone says. I don't think I can even add to the information. 
Awesome biscuits, jam, chix fried steak, veggies. Friendly folks. Worth a trip.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Place is overrated and lame. 2hr plus waiting and the food looks average.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: AMAZING biscuits! We decided to stop here due to the great reviews and it did not disappoint. As we checked in we were told it would be an hour and 15 minute wait for two but we were seated within 45. In the meantime there are little shops to pick up some souvenirs and browse to kill time. The biscuits were awesome along with the peach jam. Our waitress Virginia was also very kind and provided the BEST service we have ever received. Must try if you are ever looking to explore Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Service was fabulous after our 35min wait (which is not too bad considering it was going to be nearly 2 hrs last weekend!).  The food was standard southern classics like fresh biscuits (ok - but the jam was great!), fried catfish (just ok - good hash brown casserole) and bbq (didn't try it).  The food was good but didn't think it was anything special and not worth the 30 min drive out of Nashville or the wait.

Wait!! I just had a slice of their coconut cream pie that we took home. The whipped cream is light and not too sweet. The custard is creamy and the roasted coconut flavour is just right. I'm going to grab another slice right now!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Came here for dinner. The line is long (but they give you a buzzer thing that tells you when you are next). There are gift stores around and cornhole which help pass the time.

Food: biscuits, fried chicken, catfish, ham, pulled pork, pecan pie. Bad: pecan pie, just pass on the desserts. Amazing: biscuits. The outside is almost crunchy and the inside is so fluffy, but not flakey. The fried chicken was really good (not hot chicken).  Also was a huge fan of the catfish. Looks like it was almost deepfried and had a lot of dry rub around it. The ham was pretty salty, but that's just cured ham. I didn't think it was that special. Overall, my favorite meal at Nashville. Some really good sides as well.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We've been on the road and was looking for some authentic southern comfort food that didn't taste like it was sitting in the deep fryer for the last month...this met every single expectation! Shout out to our waiter Owen who helped us make decisions when we couldn't choose what to eat and had a true passion for the food. It was well worth the 45 minute wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Once upon a time - oh, 30, 40 years ago - Loveless was a secret place I took people to when I wanted them to get a taste of the "real southern cuisine." Unfortunately, no longer. It used to be terrific, homey, everything from scratch.
It may be all from scratch now, but it's really become nothing more than a tourist joint. If you haven't ever had good fried chicken, you might think this was acceptable, but you'd do better at a gas stop Krispy Krunchy. 
If you want the real deal, ask around for old-fashioned meat & threes. Sorry to be so brief but there's not much more to say except that it's also quite expensive given what you get - poor service, low quality. If you want really great southern cooking, take the time to visit Lynchburg and go to Miss Mary Bobo's, former home of Jack Daniels. Just make sure to reserve in advance.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Had our team dinner here and it was a fun experience.  The German two person band was good and very entertaining.  They played throughout our dinner with two short breaks during the night.  We shared pretzel appetizers and what looked like egg rolls, but being German, I am sure it was called something else.  Their beer selection was good and the service was excellent.  I ordered the jagerschnitzel which came with mushroom gravy.  It was pretty good, but I prefer more flavor in my food, so German food tends to be on the bland side.  We all shared the dessert which were also tasty.  I would recommend this restaurant for good German food.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Being German, we were sceptical but this is real German food in a real German beerhall. Amazing, decent prices and very good food.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Yes it was Saturday of July 4th weekend. But a 2+ hour wait?? Come on. That's insane. We found out the to-go orders were only about a 30 min wait and decided to do that instead. I got the biscuit sampler, BF got the BBQ pork omelet and biscuits and gravy. Food was ready in about 40 mins. We walked around a bit while waiting but didn't go into any of the shops. Place was mobbed. Ate in the car. Honestly, Cracker Barrel and Biscuithead in Asheville have better food and better biscuits. My fave was the chicken biscuit. After that, the pulled pork biscuit. BF said omelet was just good, not great. Won't be back. Went once to say we were there and tried it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: 3.5 stars. I really want to give it more, because the biscuits are unbelievable and the service is lovely, but I just can't. It's like one of those Nashville places that took off and suddenly the demand was far greater than the capacity. AKA you're stuck waiting more than an hour for weekend brunches, every time. When I visited, it was typically closer to two. Granted, while you're waiting, you can walk around the cute grounds and visit their awesome little market store to pick up some delicious goodies, so that's a bonus. But the inevitable wait, combined with the average and arguably overpriced (excluding the biscuits, mind you) food, just sort of takes away from everything. I'd highly recommend just picking up some to-go biscuits and calling it a day.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food was amazing but the wait is crazy. The staff is really nice. I ordered my food to go and sat outside on a picnic table. The corn hole is a lot of fun too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Definitely a tourist destination, while I'm glad I went to check it out, I probably wouldn't venture there again.  The food was simple, but good.  Biscuits were yummy, but not the best I ever had.  Truthfully, I was happier with the atmosphere than the food.  We went this past Sunday and the wait time was 90 minutes, so instead we ordered take out, had it in less than 30, and ate in one of the other buildings.  It was perfect and much more efficient.  We got some of the Cajun bacon as well, and had BLTS that night, and they were outstanding.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Southern breakfast ? Check ! Biscuit platter lets you taste their famous biscuits AND delish BBQ and three other choices. At 830 on a weekday, no wait and totally worth it. Also- check out the shops :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: When I am asked for suggestions to take guests from out of town for a true Nashville experience, the first place that comes to mind in Loveless Cafe. It is a true staple of the Nashville cuisine. I have to admit, I am NOT a lover of fried chicken, biscuits with gravy etc,., but something about this place changes all that. The staff and service is all polite and adequate. The food is prepared nicely and my guests have always said that the fried chicken is cooked perfection. The appetizer are the infamous Loveless biscuits with a side of there jams and preserves (my favorite). This is not just a restaurant either, the cafe is surrounded by neat little shops selling antiques, souvenirs, and a bike shop. Definitely cannot get bored if you are waiting for a table. If you are looking for a great dining experience and to experience Nashville (Southern) culture, Loveless Cafe is a great place to visit.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I attended this restaurant for a work dinner recently and was sorely disappointed. I was in a group of about 8 people and there were maybe another 10 people there total. It took nearly an hour for our table to be served our orders. I got so hungry I asked the waitress to please bring some bread out to the table to which she replied, "we don't do that". This is extremely bizarre to me and I've honestly never been told this when I've inquired about bread for the table. When the food finally did arrive, I got the scallop ravioli, I was disappointed to find it came with only four measly raviolis. Keep in mind, this dish was about $25. When we finished, eating the waitress then took another 20 minutes to process our payment. I will not be attending this establishment in the future and if anyone is looking for prompt service and a filling meal, I'd look elsewhere.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Beautiful cafe and surrounding shops. Bisquits were good, a little too hard for my liking. The best platter is the sampler with (choose 3) fried chix, bbq shredded pork and fried catfish they all were great! The BBQ sauce was phenomenal! We had the sides corn casserole, sweet potato side and the hash browns. The only one that was ehh was the corn casserole or maybe because it was not too hot.  Overall the shredded pork takes the prize with the hash browns and sweet potatoes.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The Loveless is off the Natchez Trace Parkway a few miles from Leiper's Fork/Franklin TN.  There's not much around it, so it's definitely a "destination" trip.  The café is in a house surrounded by the original 1940's era Loveless roadside motel (the rooms have been turned into shops selling Loveless memorabilia, pottery, antiques, etc).  

If you go, it'll be to say you've been to one of the south's well known attractions and not necessarily for the diner-style food.  The famous complimentary biscuits are "okay".   I ordered a well done cheeseburger, which came burnt and very dry with melted slices of plain American cheese.  The crinkle fries were good, though.

The presentation of the brownies we ordered could use improvement, as we sort of expected they'd be on a plate, slightly warmed, with maybe a dollop of whipped cream or something.  Instead, they were tossed onto the table wrapped in saran wrap.  Fortunately, they were good. 

The Loveless isn't somewhere I'd go on a regular basis, but will take out of town guests who want to see an iconic southern sight.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Noticed this restaurant upon leaving the mall last night. Had no idea it was there but then remembered some small indication of it while walking the mall. My nephew and I decided to try it and ordered the reuben and fish and chips. The reuben ($11) was very good and came with regular fries. The fish and chips came with steak fries which we did not like as much as the regular fries. I love fish but probably would not order this dish again. It was $15 and came with one piece of fish and a lot of steak fries. The fish was ok. Jennifer was our server and we found her to be very nice. We were told the restaurant opened last Wednesday. Unless you park in the side of the mall you probably would not know the restaurant was there. One suggestion I would make is to have better signage in the mall. The doors leading to the restaurant are just plan exit doors that the general public would not use anyway.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
While out of town visiting my boyfriend's family for the holidays in Tennessee, we all came here for a good ol' Southern breakfast on Sunday. Come for the biscuits, stay for the friendly service. And seriously, put peach preserves on those biscuits because holy crap, that's delicious.

Country fried steak and eggs with cheesy grits was really good. The eggs were slightly overcooked, but honestly, not by too much.  Definitely not enough to dock a star.  Those cheesy grits, though...man. SO GOOD. I want more right now.

Don't wait - get yourself here TODAY for the deliciousness.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I'm going to give this 4/5 stars just because it took some effort to get seated. The girls thought I was invisible for about 5 mins, then they suggested take out, then I was seated in the corner next to a large loud table before seating myself... 

Everything looked up right after being seated. My waitress was very friendly & the food was delicious. I ordered the watermelon ribs which were full of sweet zesty flavor, which was covered in BBQ sauce. The meat came off the bone with little effort.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I had a TOTAL blast at a special event at City Winery last Friday! As far as I know, the restaurant was closed to the public that night. We had the entire front area bar, as well as the large venue room. 

There were at least 4 bars placed around the room, which was really convenient, and there was never a long wait in line to get drinks. I enjoyed the cab that they offered that night for the party, as well as one of the "holiday martinis" which was reminiscent of an upscale bushwhacker ;). 

The food was SO impressive. I sampled a little of everything, and found myself saying "mmmmm" on every single item. My favorites were the cheesy grits topped with a shrimp gravy (omg), and there was also a mushroom option which I sampled from my sister's plate that was delicious. The shallot dip with the homemade potato chips was crave-worthy, and the strawberries and cream creme brule hadh me "mmmm'ing" at every bite. 

I can't wait to go back for another show and for another delicious dinner!

name: The Basement
text: Great bar, under a great music store! Been here several times. Good music, and good service. Clean bathrooms.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Of course the main draw is the fact that, well, it's the Loveless Cafe. So, I wouldn't call the food amazing, but it is pretty darn tasty. Especially their biscuits (of course!), of which they are thankfully very generous with. Everything else is yummy and your dining experience here might remind you of eating dinner at your grandmum's kitchen table. :)  The staff were very friendly and attentive.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is overwhelming with southern charm and to be honest, I'm pretty sure its overdosing on all aspects of cute.

However, the options for vegetarians are limited outside of the regular Denny's staples. I ordered the french toast because some variation of eggs just didn't seem like it had enough umph.

And see, I love biscuits, Perhaps more than my biscuit loving, meat eating friends. And their biscuits contain lard. While I appreciate my server mentioning it, he did so with a bit of unnecessary sarcastic zest.

And while I understand I'm in the south and perhaps the vegetarian lifestyle hasn't quite made it down here in the last 20 or so years since I've been a vegetarian, I was a bit underwhelmed by the food and overwhelmed by the charm of the Loveless campus.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: A great place to watch a show, but for the love of Pete, eat somewhere else before or after. This place cannot get itself together on service. When the food arrives, it is forgettable. I've been here at least four times in two years, always with the same result. Unfortunate.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
This review is for the restaurant.  Worst food I have ever experienced.  I love Dolmas (Grape leaves traditionally stuffed with rice and lamb) so we ordered the dirty rice dolmades with Shrimp.  They were so dry they were falling apart and they tasted like dirt.  Hummus plate was ok.  They piled on the one kind of hummus that was the worst and dotted the plate with the others, which weren't too bad.  
The braised duck tacos were terrible.  We all agreed.  The only reason I am giving this a 2 star instead of 1 is because of the pumpkin gnocchi.  If you like gnocchi, this is a MUST.  Delicious...but it did not make up for the poor quality of everything else.  Do yourself a favor and eat elsewhere!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: True Southern cooking.  A spot not to miss when in the Nashville area.  Now serving beer, wine and cocktails.  The vegetables are as close to "home cooking" as you will find these days.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We came for Valentine's Day lunch.  I would not come again for dinner due to the slow service and no compensation from the restaurant for running out of items that came with the meals we ordered, getting one order completely wrong AND waiting a very long time for the food.  The nice couple sitting next to us had their meal paid for my the restaurant because they waited so long for their food to arrive.  That same couple felt so bad that our meal was not also paid for by the restaurant...that THEY paid for our meal!!! Gratitude for the nice couple and shame on the restaurant.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Ohhhhhhhh the biscuits! Everyone is saying it, because it's true! I got the friend chicken and a bunch of extra sides and split my meal with a friend. It was plenty of food plus some! I didn't love the sweet potatoes (just seemed like they had opened a can of yams) but otherwise, everything was so amazingly good. I really loved the green beans! Our server, Jason, was awesome! It seems like he's been there for a long time and you can tell. He knew his stuff, he was super friendly and helpful and added to our positive experience. I'm always grateful when a server will engage a little bit with the table and he did just that! The food is everything people say it is and ask for Jason if you want excellent service to go with it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Had about an hour and ten minute wait. It was worth it. The biscuits were very good. But the chicken and waffles were to die for. Service was exceptional. Price was on the high side but the quality of the entire experience as well as my very full belly didn't seem to mind.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This might be a good place as a music venue, but as a restaurant- skip it. In a party of 4, 2 of us ordered steak. The plating was very nice but the steak was room temperature. The waiter apologized and took them back to the kitchen. In 2 minutes he brought 2 new dinners, again cold! A vegetable side that came out with the first steak, was still warmer than the 2nd entrée. When I called the manager about it the next day, she offered no solution other than if we came back we could have a drink on the house. I would NOT recommend this restaurant.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I've dined here multiple times, and I loved it when I first ate here, but each time seems worse. This time, the service was just awful. There seemed to be only 1 or 2 servers responsible for all of the tables, and everyone in the restaurant seemed to be doing everything - running food, delivering drinks, bussing tables, refilling water, etc. I don't blame the wait staff; there's probably a management breakdown. Our simple, 3-person dinner at 8:30p turned into a 2-hour ordeal. All of the tables around us seemed to be having the same experience. They also greatly reduced their menu. Good luck if you're a vegetarian.

To top it off, one of their events let out around 10:15p, just as we were preparing to leave. You'd think they'd have a dedicated valet for the restaurant patrons, but alas, we had to get in line with the hundreds of people who had attended the event. It seemed to be the final nail in the coffin for us.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I love this place it's just a really cool place to go, if you have eaten here and you are close by do yourself a favor and stop in. It's good food, friendly staff it feels like grandmas southern cooking! So yummy

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Love this place.  Breakfast is amazing.  The jams are delicious.  And the smoke master gave the kids a little tour and a tutorial on how he smokes the meat.  Very nice man .. We all enjoyed talking with him.  Awesome morning!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
"Breakfast at The Loveless Café?"

I had been in Nashville less than 24 hours, and this was the third time I had heard of/and been instructed to eat at The Loveless Café. So, we did!

Since the 1940's, Lon and Annie Loveless have been serving chicken and biscuits right from the front door of their house to travelers going to and from Nashville. Eventually, their 'home' became a regularly scheduled stop of travelers, and as such evolved into The Loveless Motel and Café in 1951.Today, they serve 7000 biscuits a day, and once you've sunk your teeth into the creamy, buttery goodness, you'll know why. They are amazing. They also bring an assortment of fresh made preserves to the table. Yum.

I watch a lot of cooking shows, which is ironic, since I don't cook. Our stove is used to store things, suitcases waiting to be used and shoes waiting to be worn. However, from the myriad of cooking shows, I have gleaned that Tennesseans know bar-b-queue, and after visiting, I am convinced.  Ribs, ribs and more ribs. Ribs slow cooked in a pit. Ribs smoked dry, baked, boiled, broiled, rubbed, doused, simmered and oh so good. The Rib Special of the day at The Loveless, were slow cooked with watermelon; the meat literally falling from the bone. The keys to good ribs, I'm told, are some 'fine swine' and lots of time.

Throughout the ages, The Loveless Café has been a much cherished piece of Nashville culture. In 2004, for the first time in Loveless history, they closed their doors for renovation. When they reopened a few months later, 'folks were standing in line thicker than sausage gravy'.

Today The Loveless has been featured on many shows, including Ellen DeGeneres, Today and Good Morning America. For a downhome  southern food experience, this place makes the cut.

Visit my site at: www.TNBTA.com for cool photos and more reviews....

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great local place with lots of history .Best biscuits anywhere. Always crowded. Their food is worth the wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Always a great experience here. Friendly people, good food, good shopping while you wait. Be sure to stop by the smokehouse. If you're not hungry by then, you will be.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My meal got off to an amazing start with the biscuits and preserves; it was very good. Other than that, your money would be better spent at your local Cracker Barrel. I ordered the pulled bbq pork with turnip greens and mac & cheese. The mac & cheese was beyond disappointing, the turnip greens were decent but below average, but the meat was actually kind of tasty. Overall, my experience was very disappointing considering the hype that surrounds this place. The Loveless Cafe is definitely nothing to write home about.

name: Big Shotz
text: This is the dive-iest of dive bars a midst a row of other dive bars.  The music was great.  The beer was cheap (like $2 for 6oz).  The tables were really sticky.  The smoke was thick.  Anything that wasn't beer (I can't do gluten) was crazy expensive.  My very weak dixie cup of vodka/cran was $7!!   In retrospect I should have just done a couple of jello shots.  Great fun though.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The brunch menu was hilarious. The PB&J is very disappointing, I couldn't even finish half of it. Our server could of cared less about our table. We were out of town guests and it was our first time and he didn't help us with the menu or drink recommendations at all. He seemed in a rush. I was very excited to go there and ended up very disappointed.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Caution: Tourist trap. Biscuits were warm and were good but not the best I ever had. Food was mediocre. Wait time is ridiculously long and I think they do that on purpose so you can spend time in their shops purchasing needless merchandise.  Our service was great though.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great home style comfort food. Really loved the the cream corn and mac and cheese. Chicken was also really good.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I will start by saying I hope they make it and I am surprised they are not more together being a chain(4) in major metropolitan areas.  So to start there was a bit of confusion upon arrival due to the fact that we had a reservation in the restaurant and not the music venue.  Some how within 10 minutes (time it took us to be taken to our seats in the music venue side only to find out that is not where the reservations were for) our reservation for 8 was lost and we were now going to have to wait 3o minutes to get seated.  We finally got that worked out so the wait was only 15 minutes, ok.  The server was very nice but not overly attentive.  We waited for our food for 1.5 hours, then it came out over a 15 minute time frame and for some it was cold.  The food was mediocre at best, the pizza was cold, the duck tacos were gamy and the burger was just ok. Oh did I mention we had to ask 2X to get some silverware for 2 of the people at the table.  After dinner and coffee we waited another 40 minutes to get our bill.  Parking was not an issue for us as we took a lyft but I have to say upon departure and trying to get a taxi the people at the Valet stand were very, very rude.  So my experience was not fun, I did not feel like a patron but more like a nuisance.  I have to say the experience inside the music venue may be better but I do not think I will spend the $$$'s to try again.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Nice place great food and excellent service!!! Gemmall was our server and he was fantastic!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Biscuits: 3.9 out of 5

That's perhaps the most shocking result of my recent trip to this iconic property west of Nashville. I decided to embark on a mission to find the Top Ten biscuits in Middle Tennessee, one of the many foods for which this area is known (hot chicken, barbecue, pork chops, Goo Goo Clusters, pies, etc.). So why not begin my investigation at the most quintessential place to get a biscuit in Music City?

The Loveless Cafe and gift shops have become quite the noteworthy destination for tourists and locals alike, a charming enclave of shops so rustic it's almost kitschy. It had been years since I dined here, long before I was a Yelper, so this time I came prepared to take careful mental notes on the food, especially the complimentary biscuits. Despite their underwhelming size, they come out hot and fresh with a delicious buttery top that's slightly salty and rigid. Almost perfect! And then you consume the interior which becomes sticky, not soft, as you begin to chew and lacks that classic buttery taste. My father the chef developed a 5-star biscuit so perfect it required no condiments. The biscuits at Hominy Grill in South Carolina are a 4.5. Thus I have high biscuit standards, and these unfortunately are nowhere near that caliber.

PROS:
Loveless offers tasty comfort food of reasonable quality and tourists will certainly enjoy their visit. The service is fantastic, in fact the waitress kept my water glass as full as the wait staff at a top-rated Beverly Hills restaurant. The mac 'n' cheese was simple but very, very good and the fried pork chop batter was almost perfect!

CONS:
For a restaurant so lauded by the media, there were many disappointments beyond the mediocre biscuits. The fried okra was mushy and tasteless when it should be flavorful and just as crisp as fried chicken. Okra is currently out of season, but there is no excuse for such a lack of crunch. The pork chop itself was dry. The gravy, supposedly one of their specialties, was perfectly peppery! But the consistency was extraordinarily gelatinous, certainly the type of thickness you don't want in gravy. Perhaps the biggest disappointment of all was the slice of pecan pie, a staple for Southern diners. At $4.29, the small portion I received was terribly bland and tasted like flavorless Jell-O with a hint of pecan. In fact, it is the only slice of pecan pie I've been unable to finish in my lifetime, probably the worst pie I've ever had.

Yes, Loveless is good and it's worth one visit, especially for tourists looking for that classic Southern meal. But compared to the burgeoning restaurant scene that has overtaken Nashville, Loveless simply cannot keep up. I understand how it achieved iconic status. I just don't understand how it maintains that distinction.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Items Selected:
Coffee
Unlimited Buttermilk Biscuits with Housemade Strawberry, Blackberry, Peach Jam
Pecan Pancakes with Maple Bacon, Sorghum
French Toast with Housemade Sausage and Sorghum
Biscuit Sampler - Fried Chicken, Pulled Pork, Aged Ham, Pimento Cheese & Fried Green Tomato with Cheese Grits
Pecan Pie, Chocolate Chess, Banana Pudding
Chess Pie

Conveniently located just off the route from Nashville to Memphis, Loveless Café and the small village of stores around it are nothing short of a Tennessee Landmark, and fresh off the redeye from LAX our arrival at the former hotel preceded its opening by a mere fifteen minutes, a line of six already formed with the sizable restaurant nearly 100% full by the time we left just after 8:15.

Featuring concepts of sustainability, scratch-based cooking, and a menu of Southern diner classics spanning from breakfast through lunch to supper, it was almost immediately upon seating that water was poured while coffee was readied and although the brew itself was a bit acrid without sweetener the refills were spot on and spontaneous, though food did take a bit longer than would be expected as our server was spread thinly throughout the largest room in the house, at times even drawn to the al fresco seating to assist others at a table of twelve.

Sipping coffee with orders placed it would not be long before a plate of Loveless' signature buttermilk biscuits was delivered, and paired with a trio of housemade jams plus requested sorghum and honey it goes without saying that the fluffy golden rounds are indeed quite delicious, though for my money there are better to be found not only in Nashville but also parts of the Carolinas as well as at Yardbird, still the reference standard, though admittedly theirs are not refilled freely on request.

Moving on to entrees, another piping hot cup of coffee poured, it was largely a matter of sampling widely that led to an order of even more biscuits and with each of the four golden rounds topped differently one would be hard pressed to name a winner amongst the group, the crispy chicken and tender pulled pork rousing curiosity of just how good a full plate dinner at Loveless might be while the tart green tomato topped with spicy pimento cheese was as 'Southern' as it gets, certainly not the sort of stuff you see served for breakfast anywhere back home.

Moving next to the French Toast and Pancakes, suffice it to say that both are competent takes on classic American breakfast staples, and with the buttermilk fresh plus the bread homemade the only real question is whether to indulge in Maple Syrup, local Honey, or thick amber Sorghum as the topping of choice, from my standpoint a decision that entailed a little of each before deeming the decision a tossup, the Sorghum almost a bit *too* sweet on the vanilla and cinnamon dipped toast but absolutely delightful when mellowed by the ample amount of toasted pecans added to the pancakes for just a buck.

Unwilling to forgo desserts, 7:45 in the morning or not, what started as a sampler of three miniature pies and puddings quickly expanded to a quartet when the server brought chocolate chess instead of original, and with a pure butter crust serving as the base to both reference standard iterations it speaks volumes that the pecan pie was actually the best of them all, a dearth of 'filler' allowing the caramelized nuts and brown sugar to shine without being overly sweet - a similar degree of subtlety offered by banana pudding that used house whipped cream and softened vanilla wafers amidst thick chopped fruit and a smooth yellow base to deliver an experience that was not only texturally pleasing but also shockingly natural, a quality far too infrequently found in a dessert where boxed pudding is far too frequently meant to suffice.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wonderful food and nostalgic atmosphere. You can browse the store and surroundings while you wait to be seated. You WILL wait. World famous biscuits. Good country cooking. A lot of history in this local and tourist favorite.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I was here for an event during Music Biz 2018. The venue is BEAUTIFUL and the service is phenomenal. I ordered the rose cider and wow it rocked my world.  I would have ordered another but it was a bit pricey for me (recent college grad so definitely out of my price range). Because things were a bit more expensive I was hesitant to buy any food but my hunger quickly grew as the man next to me ordered a margarita flatbread. I decided to #TreatYoSelf2018 and order one as well. I'm glad I did. It was huge portions and tasted amazing.

Overall I really enjoyed the place. I will say it is definitely on the pricier side so I won't be returning unless some fancy man is taking me out. But, it was still amazing. If you're looking for a place to make an impression this will for sure make the mark with their amazing selection and well crafted menu options.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: AMAZING! Food is great, service is great and the place is adorable! Every time I'm in Nashville I make sure to grab some breakfast!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Made the long drive out and although it was neat to see the food wasn't overwhelmingly great. I had the fried chicken, mashed potatoes, and Mac and cheese. The Mac and cheese was very good. I almost think the potatoes were instant at least they tasted that way...not a compliment. The fried chicken was plenty good but not amazing. Now the biscuits were very good but the preserves were the best part of it all. I'm glad we didn't have to wait. I wouldn't say it was worth waiting for. All in all not sad we went but wouldn't go back again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits alone are reason alone why to go to Loveless!  I've had chicken fried steak and both were amazing.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This is quite literally the most popular meal stop in Nashville. Locals and tourists alike flock to Loveless. The bulk of them in search of the famous biscuits. 

Upon arrival, you will be handed a pager (it's a given, there will be a wait). But no fear, there is plenty to keep you busy while you wait. These folks sure have taken space utilization to new heights. Gifts shops, bookstores, deli, arts and crafts; can't fault anyone for maximizing profits. But I wonder if the food has suffered in the process. 

The food :
The biscuits - Served bread basket style, complimentary as you await your order. I will say they are very good. The best? Probably not, but quite satisfying. 

Grits - pretty mediocre 

Waffles - good thickness, texture, and flavor, but becomes stale after about 5 minutes 

BBQ pork - arrived a little cold. Not exactly how you like to enjoy your food. Otherwise ok flavor 

Country ham - touted as one of the specialties; kinda fell flat. The ham itself was on the cold side, and very tough/chewy. 

Unfortunately the name is pretty befitting, loveless cafe.....After my visit, I love them just a little less.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits and preserves are definitely what keeps me and my family coming back. The breakfast is good, but nothing special. My kids love to watch them making biscuits in the window and play on the grounds. We usually go on the weekends but we make sure to get there no later than 8:30am to avoid a long wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: You just has to know what you are getting into. It is a tourist stop, so it is busy. (we waited an hour) While we waited there was some drama with a bachelorette party, which there seems to be a million of in the nashville area. The food was solid to very good, the service was very friendly. I would stop back if I know the wait would be less.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Yes, the hype is real -- the biscuits are ridiculously good. Paired with their strawberry jam, I swear I felt like I was 8 again. Homemade as it gets.

Everything has that authentic, made in your grandma's kitchen taste. Very traditional. Seasoned well, but not overwhelming on the salt. So far it's the best comfort food we've encountered.

Got here at 7:00ish on a Saturday and only waited 10 minutes to be seated. Will definitely come again! Bring your parents, they'll adore it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We were visiting from out of town for the NPAA (Nurse Practitioner American Association) Conference at the OpryLand Hotel, and had great service on a Tuesday at around noon even though we waited 15 minutes to sit.  

I had a country fried steak with white gravy, Hash-brown Casserole, and two eggs over medium.  I combined the eggs and the gravy to top the CFS and it was great.  The CFS was about the size of my hand, or about 10 inches round.   Very very tasty.  My wife had a fried chicken salad, and my daughter had the old faithful chicken wings.  Everyone was very pleased with their meals.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Not a fan of places that Nickel and dime you. They make you valet, as there's no parking lot, and charge $8 for it. They also have a separate wine tax. Additionally, we ordered the roasted red pepper ricotta dip as an appetizer. It was delicious, but they only gave us four chips to eat the whole dip. We asked for extra chips, and the waitress said no problem. When we received the bill, we were charged for additional chips. I have to say, I'm not impressed with their customer service model. That being said, everything we ordered was delicious. However, we won't be returning. I don't enjoy paying fees for every little thing.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The defining example of a tourist trap. Yes the buns are good along with the jams, but that is it. The food is of poor quality, and barely warm. Add this to a long wait, high prices, and an overworked wait-staff and you have a poor dinning experience.  I was very disappointed.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We went two days in a row, it's that good. For breakfast we had the country ham and pulled pork omelet. Both were very good along with the hash brown casserole and biscuits and gravy. The best sausage gravy I've ever had. On our second visit we had the fried chicken with fried green tomatoes, mashed potatoes and gravy and Mac n cheese. For desert we had the key lime pie (the best I've had). Everything was excellent and both times the service was good and very friendly. I will go back every chance I get.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Southern cooking at its finest. It is worth the wait to get some down-home goodness right here. I would give it 6 out of 5 if I could. Lots of celebrities have been here, it has been in business for more than 60 years (that says something), and the diverse mix of people in there was nice to see. I had the chicken fried steak along with eggs and grits; super well prepared with the buttery stone-ground flavor made me perfectly satisfied. Great wait staff too. The wooden floors and windows are reminiscent of the Old South. The biscuits are the best thing I've ever had!!! There is a heat and soft tenderness to them you cannot get anywhere else in my view. Perfect jams as well. Overall tremendous experience. Worth the long drive down Highway 100. Don't forget the sweet tea!!!!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We had my company's Christmas party here and it was wonderful. I was nervous because I'd never been (my usual haunts were all booked) but we were very pleasantly surprised! There was a harp player, which made for beautiful ambience. Everything from the drinks, apps to the entree were amazing. The service too! I will definitely be back for a date with my boyfriend.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing food! Had the biscuit French toast!! The seating on the outside patio is so peaceful and delightful!! Will be back before we leave Nashville!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Service was good. Was a unique setting. We visited for a group event so I can't give a fair review on the food.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Came here for brunch with my girlfriend following church. We had a groupon for basically 2 brunch drinks and 2 brunch meals. The Bloody Mary was good, my gf ordered a drink with pecan vodka and ginger ale that was really good as well. I had the eggs Benedict that was pretty good and my gf ordered frosted flakes French toast. The food is good and service wasn't terrible. Just not my ideal brunch spot. Food meals are a la carte. I can't speak for music venue wise but the brunch here doesn't do it for me.
Not bad at all but nothing to excite me about coming back for brunch. Maybe I'll try dinner/a show next time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Being the only really solid breakfast place in a large radius, Loveless Cafe is always crowded--that's the downside. The upside is pretty much everything else: melt-in-your-mouth fluffy biscuits, solid breakfast food served all day, and friendly service. My wife and I come here every time we drive through Tennessee.

I took off a star because they discontinued their call-ahead option.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Been to this place a few times and it's always great. Food is fast, fresh, delicious, and always on point. Our service from Charles tonight was flawless, You would think we were at the Catalina Wine Mixer! The live music and the energy it creates is the cherry on the strudel.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place became my favorite, for its atmosphere and amazing service. 
We came here 2 times during my short visit to Nashville. We had breakfast and supper. 

The place is very cosy and welcoming. It was a 45 min wait for a table on Friday morning, so we decided to check out the gift shops. Staff everywhere is so friendly! Coming from California, where the only thing is served is attitude . 

Lots of cute souvenirs and home goods. They also ship their food anywhere in the country, which is awesome, because they home made preserves are delicious. 

For breakfast we had country ham and eggs, with side of grits and hash brown casserole. I haven't had southern food in so long, so I enjoyed it. I also got a moonshine shot, which came in a cute jar, that you get to keep. 

Famous biscuits were also good, however I was more excited to try the famous chess pie. And if I could sign up for a monthly delivery of that awesomeness I sure would! That pie is so good! As full as I was after breakfast, I still ate almost a whole slice! 
Susan was our waitress and she was amazing! Very friendly and nice! Thank you Susan!  

Next day we came back for dinner. I had to have some fried chicken before I leave. I got a half with a side of mashed potatoes and green beans. I died and went to a fried chicken heaven! Comfort food at its best! To drink I got a harvest moonshine(?) , it's mixed with sweet iced tea, and so so good! 
But the best part of the dinner was our server Owen! I would like to thank you so much to make this dinner experience so special! Now, every time I will think about southern hospitality, I would think of you! Thank you for great service! You made us feel so welcome! 

Overall, i fell in love with this place and I think it's gonna become a tradition, while I'm in Nashville! Thanks y'all!!! Can't wait to be back!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: My wife was born and raised in Bavaria and I was stationed there in the military, so we love eating German food.  We took five friends and two relatives to the Bavarian Bierhaus on our week long trip to Nashville.  None of our friends/family had eaten authentic German food, so our expectations were high that the food would be excellent.  Unfortunately, we were extremely disappointed in the quality of the food, as well as the lack of authentic German entertainment.  When the food finally arrived, it appeared to have been sitting under a warming lamp for an extended period, as the surface of the red cabbage, spatzle and rouladen were extremely dry.  The food was only luke warm and there was no flavor to it. Everything tasted very bland, which is the same response that I got from our friends and family who joined us.  My wife had the Black Forest Chicken Schnitzel and thought it was very bland and dry, as well. The facilities are second-to-none, which led to our high expectations that the food would be the same.  After spending more than $300 on food, we all agreed that it would be our last trip to this venue, unfortunately.  We would have sent the food back or called for the chef to come to our table, but we had a 2 year old toddler who was getting cranky and my niece just wanted to get home to put him to bed. It is a great concept, but they need to seriously work on their food quality and flavor.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Okay, so I finally made it to Loveless for breakfast. Waited an hour and a half was expected, and there was enough to keep me busy, so that was okay. People were friendly. 

I had some trouble with the menu, ultimately I couldn't find anything I really wanted which is usually not a problem I have. The biscuits were good, but let's be honest, this whole show is about the jam -- which is delicious. 

Waitress was rushed, kind of harassed, but mostly funny about it. 

The breakfast with friends was nice, overall the experience was good. Not really sure why people are so obsessed at this point, aside from the fact that the place IS AN INSTITUTION. Definitely worth it for the history, I suppose.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is definitely worth the drive out of downtown Nashville! The staff is very sweet and accommodating and the manager came over and was a very friendly, interested guy. The biscuits are AMAZING, but that is what they're famous for! The pancakes are huge and are sweet, making them special. The biscuit sampler platter is large, and more of biscuit-sandwiches style than biscuits with various ingredients cooked into them. Definitely try the home fruit preserves on the biscuits! Lots of free parking available and there's a cute market to mosey on over before or after! Interesting history to the place and adorable decor. A great stop!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Came here some time ago, and I have to first say it was the best, most tender, juiciest bbq pulled pork I have ever had. Another thing - the wait time was ridiculous, nearly 2 hours. I ended up having a snack at the shop that also sells the bbq pork, where I had a small preview of the delicious bbq pulled pork. I wanted a second and third helping and just to eat that, but my friends wanted to eat at the actual restaurant.....

And yes, it was worth it, for those dang biscuits. MAN THEY'RE GOOD. I needed extra strawberry jam for them, TWICE. These, along with the bbq pork, are what I remember most. I had dessert too, it was delicious, but nothing comes close to these babies.

Overall, AMAZING, but WAY too long of a wait when its busy. ALTERNATIVE: get BBQ sandwiches next door and buy goo clusters for dessert!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is a Ten!  Wonderful southern food with great service.  Neat little compound of shops too. Chicken fried steak was best ever.  Biscuits were incredible. Not to mention the decadent all handmade desert menu.  Fudge pie?  Only in the south. Do not miss this place!  A bit of a drive from Nashville but so worth it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is tasty - the biscuits are top notch! However, I'm not sure I'd wait the 2 hours on the weekend. I tried the sampler - the pork bbq one is the best!  The tomato and pinto cheese wasn't my favorite.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
The minute I walked in I was so disappointed in the atmosphere. If you've been to a a real German-style bierhaus the atmosphere is rustic and lively. This was more like a cafeteria; white-walled with a few checkered swag valances hanging from the rafters.  The so-called oompa band was playing country; I didn't hear polka until I was ready to leave. Nashville doesn't give you a pass to play country at a -theme- restaurant. (Volkfest has a more authentic band.)
We sat at the bar which served several authentic German beers. The bartender was dressed normally but at least the barback was wearing a German dress. Sitting under very bright lights at a white bar felt like a blandly sanitized environment I wouldn't want to experience again. 
We didn't bother bother staying for food.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I am giving this three stats because of the quality of the pancake and the wait time.  We were told the wait was 45 minutes, but it was more like 1 hour 15 minutes.  The best part was the biscuits and jams they bring out, they were amazing!  I ordered pancakes, plus a breakfast with egg.  The pancakes were extremely heavy, not good at all, I was quite disappointed for a place that is known for their breakfast.  The eggs, bacon and  were very good.

I did enjoy walking around their little (overpriced) shops during the wait.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This place is nothing short of heaven on earth. I just found this place today and I have yet to leave. We came for brunch which was delightfully fresh and flavorful. I had an omelette and a side of potatoes with biscuits. The blackberry jam is simply Devine and has a hint of wine and whole blackberries. The highlight here is the superb customer service with Darrell and Sydney. The wait staff was attentive and I asked a million questions since I love wine and this was my first time. Hayley the bartender treated us to drinks and lovely conversation so come see here. The icing on the cake was when Mike the manager came and asked us if we wanted to see the wine operation. Of course we squirled with excitement!! We have had a magical day of wine, food and great customer service.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I was driving through Nashville and meeting a friend. She suggested this place. It was a Friday night and was a little shocked when the hostess said it would be a "2 hour wait". We walked around while we waited and checked out the gift shop, the jam shop, and the grounds. Our buzzer went off after only about an hour. Pleasant surprise. 
Biscuits, jam, and butter were delivered immediately and our drink order was taken. I had the fried chicken, mashed potatoes, and mac-n-cheese. It was delicious. Everybody else enjoyed their food as well.
Our waitress was great. Very attentive and prompt. Asking if we needed anything, refilling drinks, etc. I would recommend this place and let them know the food is worth the wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We went for Mother's Day Brunch ,,, 2 hr wait,,, drive was beautiful , worth the wait . we got Omletts and French toast ,,, AWSOME biscuits,,, with To die for Jam . Ordered another dozen biscuits to go. 
Friendly service. Love this place.
Remember to look for Bobby flays pix near the door to ur right as u come out .

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Unfortunately, the service was TERRIBLE and the food was way overpriced. The space is spectacular but our experience with the staff was not great.

The staff was rude, did not know a lot about the menu, and we waited almost 2 hours for our food. The chicken was about the size of my fist and cost over $30 after tax. Unfriendly and not trained. A shame because the layout of the place is great.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is one of my favorite food places in Nashville. The country style village and smoke house are classic. If there is a line ... I always call my order in and then go visit one of the shops next door...

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Love them. The food was great. Came out fast and the service was awesome. Dont go that much because they stay busy and it can be hard to get in. But the amazing server told us the best time to come so maybe we can go more often.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Best place to bring friends and family for a good time..loved their seasonal beer and super friendly staff.. especially kudos to Fat Jon.. yes its actually his name.. super fun guy.. and if you are confused what to get... just ask him..

Totally recommend this place...

name: Loveless Cafe
text: IF YOU ARE IN NASHVILLE YOU HAVE TO COME TO LOVELESS CAFE! Best home cooked southern breakfast we had the whole trip. The story behind the restaurant and the motel makes you fall in love with it even more! Our sever Virginia was such a doll!!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: First off, don't think you should charge people 9 dollars to park if they are coming in to eat and drink. Food was ok, prices are a little steep for what you get. Service was fine. Can't say I would go there again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Biscuits and jam were killer. 

We went for our honeymoon and it was perfect!
The food was mouthwatering. I was sad that I was too stuffed to keep eating.

name: Rocketown
text: Oxymorons of Tennessee: You cannot believe that  Jim Crow nightclubs of Memphis, which the bluesmen who played could not patronize -  were also 'great venues'? No 'great venue' maintains a policy of institutionalized bigotry.  Should the government shut Rocketown down? Nope. Yes, @Carrie G: Rocketown's rights to discriminate are absolutely protected by the  Constitution. Should everyone who believes in equality, freedom of expression, and, oh yes,  love and acceptance (Mark 12:31)(Luke 6:36)(Matthew 7:1).boycott Rocketown, and educate friends and neighbors to do the same? YES.  And that too is  absolutely  protected by  the Constitution.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I read an article that said the biscuits are terrific here. Since i am a biscuit lover, Hubby and I drove here from Chicago so I could try the biscuits out for my late December Birthday. I was not disappointed. The biscuits were FANTASTIC. The rest of the food was hearty Southern cooking and it was really good. We were not disappointed that we made the trip. In fact, on our last day in Nashville, we went back to eat at Loveless before hitting the road to head home.
Good food, plenty of it, in friendly surroundings and at a fair price; what more can you ask for?

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
