Oh, the Loveless. How your name is a misnomer.

This place is great. The wait is ridiculous, but that makes the food all the better, and you can always bring a book or a game - you've now been warned! 

I brought my sister here when she was in town, so it was her first time and I wanted to have an awesome experience with her. I'd only gone there once before, and had an epic meal, so I decided to relive it and prove that my memory served the Loveless properly. Oh, it did. 

We had a hilarious waiter (they are all quite friendly there) who gave us crayons despite our age, and was quite speedy on the food delivery. I ordered the barbecue plate, because what else would I order?!?!? Got two eggs over easy and cheese grits on the side, while my sister ordered the country ham plate with tomato scrambled eggs and hash browns.

The meat was very good. Very flavorful and also wasn't so fatty that I felt sick. My eggs were a little undercooked, but such is the way with over easy eggs so I just avoided that part. The grits were suuuuper creamy, so if you like them that way, you'll enjoy these! My sister's ham was amazing, and we had so much food that we boxed about half of it.

Obviously, the biscuits were great. The first batch we had was not directly from the oven, so the biscuits were slightly dry and not wildly tasty. However, if you wait around long enough, a new batch is sure to get around your way and they are definitely worth the wait, served up UNLIMITED and with delicious jam. Yum.

After we drove on the Natchez Trace for a bit, and I'd recommend doing that if you're out this far. It tops off a great meal! I'd love to go again sometime soon - nice folks and nice grub.

name: Rocketown
text: This used be to a great venue back at their old location. Now it is hypocrites pushing a Christian agenda. Allowing certain bands and nixing the ones they " deem inappropriate" and I honestly couldn't tell you based off what criteria. The people who work the snack desks are always polite and friendly, but the security is the most stuck up group of people I have ever met. I've sworn off going to shows here, even if it is my favorite band, I'll pass. Get back to your roots and learn how to run a business. I would give you zero stars if I could.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Love! This place is adorable and the food is delicious! I am not a fan of biscuits yet I ate the entire plate of the ones at loveless cafe! The hype is right and you definitely need to try this place! They also have a store and you can have goodies shipped home to you! It's a little bit of a drive to get to but definitely worth it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I can see why the world famous biscuits are so sought after! I came here with family after spending the last 2 days exploring Music City, and I'm so glad we stopped in. We drove a tour bus in and there was room to park in the very back so that was a huge bonus. When you walk in, there are a ton of photos along with the person's autograph adorning the front entrance. I ordered a southern omelet and I normally am not a huge fan of eggs and if there are other options I will order something else, but the omelet was incredible! I also ordered chocolate milk (my favorite!) and it came with a mason jar cup and two milk boxes. I ended up drinking it straight from the container, but I appreciated that they presented it with a glass just in case. When we left, our waitress had really made rapport with us, asking my grandpa where he had gotten his cane and what it was made from. She was very nice. I hope to one day visit again soon!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We stopped by for breakfast early Sunday morning. I had the fried chicken biscuit which was absolutely delicious.  Definitely the stand out.  My husband had the country ham, which was good, but nothing too amazing.  The hash brown casserole was very tasty and the little biscuit plate they give you is the perfect thing to tide you over until your meal arrives.  The shops are adorable and it's a very quaint little spot to grab a meal and wander around for a bit to walk off the biscuits.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Love this place, GREAT BRATS ! Also love the atmosphere... Certain nights they have live authentic bands/music

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Good german food. Devoured the giant pretzel with cheese sauce. Tried the rouladen and sauerbraten. Good meats and red cabbage. Surprised the german potato salad was cold rather than served warm. Rather noisy so hard to hear a lot of the conversation. Advertised as kid friendly but probably wouldn't take the 1 and 3 year old again. Be prepared to share large tables. Rather pricey with appetizer, salad, meals, and drinks but it was like authentic german food in Wisconsin.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Just wanted to update my review. We have NOT been back yet because we live in a different town; however, the manager contacted me and stated "I want to apologize for your experience last night.  Of course we strive for excellence in every area, and we apparently fell way short with the food.  I am glad you enjoyed some of the appetizers, and that the service was good.  I can't change the past, but I would like to invite you back to attempt to salvage the relationship here, and to prove to you that your experience is the exception rather than the norm.  If you would be so kind as to take me up on it, I'd like to offer you two tickets to a show on me, to come back and give us another try." WOW..... I AM TOTALLY IMPRESSED AND WILL DEFINITELY BE COMING BACK!    #impressive #secondchances #appreciatecitywinery

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Perhaps my expectations were too high.  I think if you're new to Southern cuisine, you may think this place is the best thing since sliced bread.  However, I was just a little disappointed that it was like a more touristy Cracker Barrel (which I actually like better).  After reading the hype about the biscuits, I was absolutely convinced that eating at this place would lead to an unhealthy obsession with biscuits.  Negative.  I was completely underwhelmed.  The only thing that saved it from being bad was the delicious peach preserve topping that accompanied the bread basket.  

Service was kind of spotty - had to wait a long time for refills, the food had a weird timing issue (like I received my food well before the rest of the table).  I ordered a BLT w/ fried egg and a side of hash brown casserole (gag).  I don't think I have a lot of love for the Loveless Cafe.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Come to loveless cafe to experience the southern cooking and hospitality. I got the sampling dish to try out their fried chicken, pork chop and pulled pork. Their food is fresh, tasty and have a pang of vinegar and brown sugar as you would expected. This place is always busy as they have half a million visitors a year.

name: Analog at Hutton Hotel
text: Yes, Analog is beautiful. And for drinks or a show that isn't very crowded, it's probably a fine venue. However, my husband and I were at Analog this past weekend because David Duchovny (yes, that David Duchovny) was there to record a set (he's a musician and novelist, too, did you know?). It was extremely crowded, which made it easy to see Analog's flaws. It's not a large venue to start with, but my main complaint was that there are two enormous columns that run through the venue. The columns entirely block the view of the stage from the several large swaths of the back of the venue. At a show this crowded, where there are only seats for about 1/3 of the ticket holders, having so many places where the view of the stage is blocked is problematic. I couldn't see anything at all, which was unfortunate. (This situation was certainly made worse by the choices made by David Duchovny's team. They reserved the upper floor for VIPs,had several enormous cameras blocking even more of the view, and had several security guards moving around throughout the show in a very distracting and view-blocking manner.) Other than that, the drinks are expensive, and we were charged $12 for valet during the show (we weren't sure where to park around the venue as I tend to avoid Midtown). This wasn't a visit that has me excited to go back - that's for sure!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
After returning from Germany a month ago I was having serious wheat beer withdrawals!! Bavarian Beerhouse to the rescue! 

Ambience : the whole ambience is exactly like the beer houses in Munich. Upon entering it reminded me of the world famous Hofbrauhouse. The long table and benches and family style dining is great to meet other diners and socialize. Even the waitresses wear traditional german clothes. 

Service : We went there on a late Sunday night and the place wasn't crowded. Service is quick and friendly.

Drinks: They have amazing German beers on draft and I had to have my wheat beer. We also got a liter of dark wheat beer which was delish! 

Food: Authentic German sausages and sauerkraut. We just had to get THE CURRY WURST!! it was just as it tasted in Germany. We got the LEBARLASE which is a meatloaf and it truly hit the spot. Got a couple of other sausages which were all great. Try the jalapeño cheddar wurst. 

Love this place and so glad we have an authentic beer house in town now

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Love the atmosphere.   Food is delicious.  Portions are good and they menu is great.  Gotta keep going back and trying new things  Definitely recommend

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We finally visited this Nashville landmark after living here for more than a year. Other than the unique down home feeling, not sure what all the hype is about. We waited about 40 minutes for a table on Friday afternoon around 12:30 pm.  Not bad. We were seated and a basket of hot biscuits and preserves were brought to the table right away.  A pleasant touch. They were good, but not great. They have a strange consistency on the top.  But still good.  It was the main meal that was disappointing. It was quickly brought out after we ordered. I ordered the "special" chicken and dressing with two sides. My husband had the smoked turkey breast with cranberry bbq sauce. He loved it, although he did say it was not very hot. My  meal was less successful.  The "dressing" was white bread with a few chunks (yes chunks) of onion and celery with a little poultry seasoning and chicken broth. The chicken was shedded chicken breast. It was all barely warm. The gravy was served in a side bowl and was cold. (The waitress did promptly bring me another hot bowl.). The sides, sweet potatoes and squash casserole, were slightly warm.  It appears they keep everything in steamers for fast service.

  All and all, I have had better meals at other "meat and three" places.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We had high expectations for what we had heard about this place and it met every one of them! We went around lunchtime on a Saturday and had to wait for over an hour but there are a few shops and cornhole games to pass the time. The pork was everything we had hoped for and the biscuits are the best we have ever had! Highly recommend buying the jams and bacon in the little shop next to the cafe to take home!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: A nice addition to the Opry Mills mall, with an entrance inside the mall and once outside if you want to avoid the mall crowd.  Large beer hall with a stage for live music.  They have a reasonable selection of Bavarian beers with seasonal specialties regularly added.  Food menu looked good and as is typical German fare, leaned heavily on sausages and meat.  We only tried a few small sides, the spatzle, roasted red cabbage and fries.  All satisfied that craving for German food.  If you're a meat eater I think you'd be satisfied with their selection of Usinger's sausages. Servers dress in authentic German beer hall attire, which lends to the festive atmosphere.  A nice addition to the Opry Mills complex.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I normally only review small businesses and try to stay away from chains, but this is an exception.

Valentine's Dinner at the City Winery was a pleasant experience. Seated in the back winery room excluded from the main dining area and the venue was a nice touch. There were several bistro tables for two, for couples that were dining as well. The menu was fixed for the night by head Chef Kristin Beringson was somewhat of a surprise due to the link on the website not working. It featured crab, a nice salad with cauliflower/beets, a lamb tartar, lobster/grits/roasted grape tomatoes, and finished with a fromage blanc mouse with pear dessert. 

Pros: Nice and secluded. Wine pairings with each course. Good service. Portions were perfect.

Cons: Handful of people bringing out dishes which created a few hiccups. Would have preferred fresh silverware for each course. Valet charge (though small at $5, I believe more people would be more generous in tips if it were free)

Overall. My lady and I both enjoyed our time there and would go back. I'd love to check out the full menu. This place is large and pretty unique. It tackles multiple feats and seems to do it pretty well.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: The food was delicious, the beer enjoyable but all this was overshadowed by the WAY TOO LOUD band. They played continuously for the time we were there making it impossible to hear any conversation. I don't mind music making the atmosphere fun, but turn it down and take a break every 20 minutes!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My initial review on 5.6.15 was very ho-hum. That being said, I was very quickly contacted by and apologized to by manager, Emilee. She explained the extenuating circumstances of the day I visited, and was clear, concise and very sincere.

This speaks volumes about the impression they're working on, and the relationship they're building with the Nashville community. I was incredibly impressed with the initiative and honest approach and am genuinely excited to return and experience City Winery once again. This follow-up had been truly rewarding for me to witness--I've told several people how impressed I am with the response from the business.

name: Big Shotz
text: One of the spots around here that I'll refuse to return to if asked. I love a good dive, but this place really had no redeeming qualities, with faux promos that are perennial non-deals...

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
It is so unfortunate that this place has such a high rating on yelp (the main reason we chose to come here). The food was nothing to write home about. Most of the food was perfectly good but nothing spectacular or original. The only thing that comes close to being an exception is the apple pie that we bought and took home- if I were in the area and in the mood for pie I would certainly buy it from here! A classic done well and deliciously. 

My biggest issue besides the lack of excitement from the menu is the complimentary biscuits that come to the table. They come on a plate alongside three of the restaurants jams which were yummy. The biscuits themselves were dry and tough- not what I prefer from a biscuit. If you genuinely like a tougher biscuit then these are the ones for you. 

I ordered the meatloaf with coleslaw and green beans, all was perfectly fine. My meatloaf was covered in too much sauce which had a very strongest ketchup taste. 

Don't get me wrong, the service was fantastic and the food was good, but all home-style and done as boring as possible. 

To note, the atmosphere is very charming along with the exterior little shops that have cute boutique-style gifts and souvenirs. This is an absolute tourist trap and will attract a specific set of people but did not appeal to me and I would not come here again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: There aren't enough words to describe how good the food is a Loveless Cafe. During busy times get ready to wait at least an hour, but it will definitely be worth it. The staff is very friendly and quick. The food tastes amazing and the portions are big enough to have leftovers, unless you're really hungry. The biscuits don't stop coming and they taste amazing with either the butter or jams.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We drove 30 minutes from Nashville to go try this place and got there to find out there is an hour and 40 minute wait to even get seated. Didn't get to try the food because we were not willing to wait a ridiculous 2 hours after driving 30 minutes there. We drove back to Nashville to the tavern and we were seated within 5 minutes. WASTE OF TIME!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Oh my goodness. Loved the food here!! Not cheap though. We moved here from Texas so maybe that's just the prices here in Nashville. We went on a weekday morning and there was no wait. Very friendly staff!! Will return!!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Came here based on the high online ratings. The beer was really good. The food was not good. It wasn't bad either - It was just...there. Everything we had was bland. We started with the giant pretzel and bier cheese dip. The pretzel was so overdone, like a rock. The bier cheese had zero taste. Husband had a brat, I had the German mac 'n cheese with chicken. He said his was all right. To add chicken to mine was $6, and it was the tiniest portion of some of the driest chicken I've ever had. All in all, we were extremely disappointed to have spent $60+ on our dry, bland meal. Maybe we just didn't order the right things...Or maybe we just didn't have enough beer to make those things taste good. We won't be returning to find out.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is a really good breakfast spot. Forewarning you will encounter a wait, but that just makes the food more enjoyable. I loved their bite sized biscuits. Gravey wasn't my favorite though. It wasn't bad it just was not my favorite. The blackberry jam though was pretty delectable. Definitely will return.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We were in town on a recent morning, early for a Predators game and decided to stop in. We hadn't done our homework so didn't realize the restaurant wasn't open for lunch, so decided to just do the wine tasting. The 4 wines - 2 white and 2 red - were of varieties not native to the region, which was refreshing. However, neither of us were enamored of the taste, though I'm not saying they were bad. When we went to purchase some (in order to defer the $10 tasting fee), found the 2 bottles priced at $50! Not competitive!

name: Big Shotz
text: Off the main drag in downtown Nashville with less expensive drinks and shots.  Great live music.  Atmosphere is a bit rowdy and bathrooms are kinda rough, but it's the perfect spot to get the night started before frequenting the more pricey bars on broadway.  We always have a good time here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Not worth the hype. The staff lost their friendliness when I made a comment that my order was wrong. Disappointed because I heard great things about their subpar biscuits. The jam and their sugar glazed ham were absolutely delicious, though.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place has been on my list for quite some time. I really wish I had gotten there sooner. It is a little pricey, but well worth it. I went for breakfast and everything was perfect and arrived exactly as I had ordered it. I had a couple mimosas that were also fantastic and served in Mason Jars. 

The wait was about 30 minutes, but it went by quickly as I explored the gift shops. I've heard about their fried chicken so I decided to order some of that to take home for lunch and dinner. The chicken was fantastic, but the greens were the best I've had other than those prepared by my mom or one of her sisters. If you're on a diet you will need the strength of a bull to not cheat on your diet here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: OMG the best fried chicken I have ever had in my entire life.  One of my friends shed a tear and the other licked her fingers and said "I didn't know people really did that! " it was so good.  They even have all you can eat chicken or meatloaf with great sides and unlimited biscuits.  The wait is terrible but there are shops to pass the time. Only disappointment was watermelon wasnt in season they said so I couldn't get the watermelon moonshine. Highly recommend.  Worth the drive and the wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great service here. Amazing food. They serve breakfast all day too. The waiter was very patient even though we squeezed extra people into the table and separate tickets. A traditional place to go if you are in Nashville. It's nice to get outside of the city and see their shops. Only piece of criticism I have is the sweet tea was not very good and their pancakes are not to die for so stick to the steak biscuits.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
If I could give this place 0 stars for service I would. 

My mother and aunt are coming into town to visit me and city winery has always been on our list of places to go in Nashville. 

A month ago we made reservations for dinner here, but they called and said they rented the whole place out and needed to cancel our reservations. Totally understandable. So we rescheduled and made a winery tour the next day. Well they just called and cancelled that for the exact same reason. 

Two cancellations was already a let down, but beyond that, the staff was incredibly rude and condescending on the phone, which makes me not even want to go to this place at all. They are not trying to accommodate us for their doings at all. If you are going to cancel multiple reservations for paying customers then you need to have public and private times separate and only allow for reservations at those times. This is getting ridiculous. 

We're supposed to go to a concert there that night, but will they cancel that too?

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Been here for dinner and brunch and so good both times! And for some reason there was no wait both times. Great atmosphere and near downtown Nash! Highly recommend.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
One word: Fun! 
Another word: Authentic!
The final word: GO!!!!

With a graduate degree in creative writing, I could go on and on, but I really said everything I needed to say above. 

So, here we go again. 

One word: Fun!
Another word: Authentic! 
Final word: GO! ! I

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Don't make reservations here as the restaurant does not honor them.  The hostess will tel you to wait as if you had no reservation at all.  The food is good but don't be fooled by the reservations they offer.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We came for a songwriters night in the upstairs Lounge.  City Winery has valet parking or there's a pay lot close by. The lounge is a long open room with nice low lighting which sets the tone for an intimate evening. You can sit at the long bar or at shared tables. The menu was upscale and offered several vegetarian options, which you don't always find at a music venue.  We tried the burrata which was served with toasted ciabatta bread and marinated tomatoes. Also had the evening's special vegetable flatbread. The flatbread was served round like a pizza, and was flavorful. The stage is set off to one side at the end of the room and the sound was great. A great place to hear live music and enjoy dinner.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Pretty much blah blah blah food. Not tasty...just your run of the mill so called southern food...which is what?

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Compared to all the food places Nashville offered, I wasn't a huge fan of this place. My food didn't come out hot, and the taste was mediocre. The chicken was overly dried, but the biscuits were definitely delicious. A cute spot, but would not come back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: AMAZING!!! Pimento Cheese & fried green tomatoes biscuit! I will just leave it there. Oh, and OWEN, our server, was AWESOME!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Yummy! Authentic German dishes. Beer garden style seating. Just a great feeling to eat, drink, and be merry. I recommend starting with a giant pretzel. Reuben sandwich and a hot bacon spinach salad for lunch. If you like German beers they've plenty including a tasting tray. Good service too.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I bought a ticket for my dream Justin Nozuka! When I arrived I was super excited for his concert. I purchased multiple wines and pizza downstairs then I  came up to the venue. Once in the venue I ordered more wine and food. After a few songs I had multiple people coming by shushing me, come to find out it was management saying I needed to respect the other customers. What about me...I'm a customer too! I spoke with the manager I guess and she again said this is a listening room yet Justin wanted his audience to enjoy and dance and sing, this is a listening room so we have to be quiet and respect the customers. Again I paid like them and ordered food and drinks. I would not come to this place if you would like to actually enjoy the show. If you wanna go to a show and be quiet go to the library.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Taste: 5
Value: 5

When in Nashville, it was time to see what everyone was talking about! 

Expect to wait about an hour. You can roam around the little row of shops to find jams and things for home or little knick knacks. If it's not too hot, you can find the outdoor spot with cornhole!

Drinks were good. I had to try the moonshine drink which came with a souvenir shot glass. They also make their own bloody mary mix which tasted classic. 

The fried chicken was cripsy yet moist. And the breakfast plate and perfectly salted ham. The star of the show though were the free biscuits and jam! We took a huge box to go!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
My husband was on a self~guided tour of the South and selected the well~known Loveless Cafe for supper. Splendid looking menu but in reality~~not so much. The famous biscuits arrived tough, tasteless, tiny. The homemade mashed potatoes were obviously from a box. The reference to the staff arriving before dawn to make the sides from scratch is puzzling. Opening a box of instant mashed potatoes shouldn`t merit early arrival. Squash casserole mainly overcooked squash, not a lot of flavor.

The fried half~chicken, however, was fabulous!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: They don't play German music. Instead it's a bunch of idiots trying to rap gangster songs and use an occasional German reference. In past was much better with polka music. This is the D- team. I've seen better music on a New York Subway. Make this place fun and authentic. Not a guy wearing a Green Bay packers jersey trying to be funny. He is not. Idiot.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
This really is as good as it gets for German Food in Nashville. There's options for those that don't like traditional dishes and for those on special diets. If you like beer, food, and a great time, this is a winner. 

We prefer to eat in the cocktail area if there are only a few of us, but for a large group the main dinning area is perfect! 

Don't forget desert!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We started with the Reuben  egg roll . Only complaint was that the thousand island dressing was a bit bland. Very good sauerbraten, generous portions.  Not too 'saur' medium tang. We were surprised that it was not served with spaetzel, but the cold sliced German potato salad was very good. Red cabbage also tasty. Monster sized yummy Black Forest cake finished us off.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Service was great and food is fantastic. You feel like you've stepped right into Germany when you arrive. From the music, to family style table, to beer, and even the outfits of the wait staff; it's as authentic as it gets. Even the gift shop features all the German favorites. One of my favorites when I'm in town from Atlanta

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
ENGAGED COUPLES BEWARE! The advertised $15.9K "full service" wedding package ACTUALLY costs almost $70K after fees and charges (with NO 'upgrades')! SEE ATTACHED PHOTOS. 

We inquired here for their larger "full service" wedding package, It explicitly advertises for "80-250 guests" as read in the first line.  We are expecting around 170 guests and felt this particular package was appropriate. We communicated for weeks via email and booked a tour with the staff. We knew that the full service package did not include the bar/drinks which was fine. We chose none of the many 'upgrades' and opted out of extra costs for decor/lighting/drapes to see what the actual starting price came out to.

We thought there had been a mistake and were sent someone else's quote because the cost breakdown line items are completely different than what the package describes, and there was never any mention of a $10K admin fee. When confronted about the $50K difference in price although we chose none of the 'upgrades', their explanation is that each guest over the 80th is charged with the "additional guest" penalty fee instead of over the 250th, as written. When advertised as a 80-250 guest package, the number is false, and it is only priced *up to 80. 

This package called the "Flute" package is their largest package offered, using the largest room of this venue, as well as multiple others - Having only 80 guest spread around this large of a space would be laughable and makes no sense. They're trying to pull a fast one on families who are emotionally hyped. Shameful tactics. It's totally fine if $70K is the budget you have, but City Winery should be honest and transparent about the actual cost vs what they advertise. (Attached are photos of print ad vs official final proposal) 

Choose City Winery - One wedding, for the price of three!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We held a private company event here recently and it was a hit. The appetizers were enjoyed, the drink selection was good, and the staff were on top of their game. They gave us our own separate room and it was the perfect fit.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Waffles and bacon hit the spot and were oh so delicious. The homemade biscuits are mouth watering and salted butter added extra flavor to everything. The jams tasted homey like my grandma was in the back making them. Mary, our waitress, was sweet and helpful with getting coffee to go after we finished. Would come back again!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Great place to go with a wonderful atmosphere! Bar area is nice size and a very nice assortment of Beers from which to choose! My choice for the night was the Grapefruit Beer... YUMMY
Appetizers were really good as well had the pretzel and the flatbread between us and would definitely order again...
I tried some of the sausages my favorite was the smoked then the Jalapeño one.. red cabbage was not to sweet and the kraut was just sour enough!! 
Hubby had the pork chop  with the beef as well.
Tried the Dessert tray with small portions of 3 desserts favorite out of the Apple Strudel, Black Forrest cake and the Pretzel Pudding ? Definitely the pretzel pudding!! They make it in house

name: Loveless Cafe
text: With all the hype I expected better. Yes the biscuits are great. We had the chicken and waffles and basically it was a tasteless chicken breast with the bone on top of a waffle. Nothing special. I had better in MA!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We have been lovers of Loveless for 30 years. It's all about the biscuits and fried chicken. We made many a pilgrimage to the restaurant when we lived in the Nashville area for 20 years and make sure to return with each visit back.

The wait time can be substantial. It's best to arrive after 1:00 and before 5:00. If you can, ask for a table in the original house section at the front of the restaurant. The add on area is loud and rushed, resembling the ambience of a Cracker Barrel 

Order the fried chicken or better yet, the fried chicken livers. And don't fill up on biscuits and homemade preserves, you will need the stomach space.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
What a lovely place! My husband and I took an Uber to visit here. This was the most expensive Uber ride that I have ever paid for and it was totally worth it! The cafe was a part of a farm. The service was excellent!

We had the biscuits with jams. I thought the jams weren't necessary. Biscuits were fluffy and yummy by themselves. I had the Biscuit Sampler Platter with fried green tomato & pimento cheese, barbeque, and fried chicken. They all tasted very good, especially the fried chicken! My husband got the country ham, which I thought it was too salty. We both had hashbrown casserole as our sides. It tasted so buttery and creamy, which was something I have never had before.

We also got the mini dessert sampler with chess pie, fudge pie, and coconut pie. I think my favorite was the coconut pie, which wasn't too sweet.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I visited City Winery for happy hour last week.  I thought everything about the place was lovely--nice ambiance, friendly staff, great happy hour specials.  There are just a couple weird things to note--if you want to enjoy happy hour, you must sit at the bar (not near the bar or at a table in the bar, but at the bar, proper).  This could quickly translate into you not getting a seat if you don't arrive early.  Another note on arriving early--I did, so I could park my own car, which was great.  My friends weren't so lucky, they had to valet for $5.00--not cool in a town where free valet is pretty much the norm.  I enjoyed the experience and will return for happy hour, for sure.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Just a pleasant experience every time. Fresh beer, surprisingly good German food for a place like Nashville, stereotypical but fun oom-pah music, and excellent service. Not quite at the level of my favorite German restaurants in other cities but much better than I ever dreamt of finding here, and I leave every time with a smile on my face. What's not to like about that?

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Superb atmosphere and really good food! Cool little piece of Bavaria right in Nashville. Bier is great, food is superb. I had the Black Forest Schnitzel and the wife had the Bavarian Onion Soup. We shared the Brotzeitteller and all was excellent. Had a couple liters of Bier and she has the Spätlsse Riesling. Really cool experience and wonderful staff. Highly recommended!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
My mom brought us here because of all the hype surrounding the place. With such fame, I expected a long wait but great food. We really only ended up waiting half an hour, and there were a lot of small shops to pass the time.

We ended up sitting on the outdoor porch, which was pretty serene, but the experience was somewhat ruined by the flies. Then, the biggest issue of the meal arose: the service. Nobody waited on us initially, and we actually had to ask for service. After taking our orders, we really only saw our waitress again once or twice, even though we requested more biscuits and needed frequent refills.

The food was phenomenal. Every single thing we ordered was scrumptious, and the biscuits and preserves lived up to their legendary status. The food easily earns 5 stars, but the service was unbearable. Still, highly recommended for anybody in the area.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless is fun & excellent quality.  Their fried chicken is very good, mashed potatoes and chicken gravy fantastic, biscuits great, BBQ brisket great, and the service was excellent.  We waited 1.5hrs and it was worth it.  BBQ. pit master and I talked BBQ for almost the entire 1.5hrs.  It was a great time.

name: Big Shotz
text: Yes, it is a dive bar and off the typical Broadway Nashville beat. However, it is worth a stop. We stopped through on our "Music City Pub Crawl" tour and we came back multiple times after. The $5 "double shotz" are excellent and hit you unexpectedly - the "dirty pirate hooker" was definitely a fan favorite.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I had bought concert tickets here and decided to eat dinner here last minute, as well. First impression walking in: gorgeous ambiance. The lounge area is very open with lots of wood finishings and a round staircase surrounded by wine bottles. Very pretty. 

Our dinner included: fried risotto balls, chicken fricasse, pork belly, lemon olive oil cake, and a few glasses of wine. Overall, I was pretty pleased with the meal, especially the pork belly which was crisp and succulent. The risotto balls were also good and reminded me of falafel. The sweet jam that comes with the lemon olive oil cake was the best part of the dish, but next time I'll probably order the chocolate stout cake which I couldn't stop drooling over from looking at it from the table next to me. 

Dinner here is definitely not cheap. Our meal (for 2) came out to be $140 without tip. Plus, they charge an exorbitant amount of tax since they charge you liquor tax as well. Why the establishment (a "winery") doesn't pay it itself is kind of strange.  Also, valet parking is $5. Good luck finding parking elsewhere. 
 
The concert itself was pretty good, although considering that this establishment hosts many musicians and artists, the acoustics weren't the best. Maybe it was an off night. 

Overall, I'm glad I was able to have the full dining experience here although next time there's a show, I'll probably eat dinner elsewhere first; It's hard to justify the price.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Bavarian Bierhaus is fun!  The bench seating is unusual, but provides for conversation and sharing with others at the table.    They have an amazing beer selection, and I really enjoyed my flight.  And the pretzels are awesome (and huge).

My wife knows more about German food than I do, and she absolutely loved the Rouladen.  She said that it reminded her of favorites from her youth.  I had the Pork Schnitzel and thought it was excellent.  We took home some Appelstrudel for late-evening dessert.

The staff really added to the fun factor.  They are in costume, and are very knowledgeable about their menu.  And the live music contributed to the authentic German atmosphere.  I do not like going to Opry Mills, but the Bavarian Bierhaus makes it worthwhile.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Visited City Winery on July 10th to see the Bacon Bros. I was initially impressed with the upscale ambience and decor. After being seated and realizing our evening was to be spent sitting extremely close to another couple, it was downhill all the way. Our server seemed to get confused at every step. We ordered both the risotto balls and fried green tomatoes as appetizers. Only the FGT arrived... Cold and overcooked. I asked about the other appetizer and was told we didn't order it! They arrived slightly prior to our meal. We both ordered the pan seared grouper. It was overcooked, rubbery, tasteless and on top of what were supposed to be smoked bacon grits. The consistency was more like soup. Again, we were both disappointed. Sides of mac and cheese and haricot verts... again lacking flavor. I asked the server for unsweet tea and was brought diet Pepsi..... twice. Getting our car back from valet was another horror story as we waited in line for 40 minutes! All in all, a $300 very underwhelming evening at a venue I had been excited to experience.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Well I'm in town for work usually hit my "go to" BBQ rib joint before my flight in the morning. Thought I'd change it up and try a different place, lots of hype here. I didn't mind the food and the atmosphere was good live music from the German country side with the long horn.. LOL it's worth a shot if you want a different dining experience. Food was just ok.. nothing to put in a "must have" category first time here so not sure if I made a good dining choice although I did ask the bartender for suggestions. They are ok friendly and keep the beer full think I'll try again and get a different meal maybe.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Delish! Great service and food! Hannah was very nice and helpful. Their biscuits are what KFC biscuits are supposed to taste like LOL.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is definitely worth the wait. Went with a party of 8 and it took approximately 1 hour to be seated. You don't even notice as they have 2 markets on site and cute photo ops. The actual restaurant has a very homey feel with pictures hung on the wall. The food is amazing and the portions are good to share. They're biscuits are great and they bring out 3 different types of jams. I would definitely recommend this restaurant.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Absolutely a must if you visit Nashville. It's like sitting in your grandmas kitchen having breakfast. The food is great, all of it. The country ham is wonderful. The fried pork chops and gravy are my favorite. It can be a wait on the weekends if you don't get there early but there are things to see and do on the grounds and it's worth the wait.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: Bland tasting food at an extortionate price. Incredibly small portions for what they're asking and the menu seemed confused.  I ordered the cheeseburger and was shocked at how small it was for how much they were charging. The milkshake tasted like everything else that was in the fridge. Just go to Hugh Baby's or Steak and Shake!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits did not disappoint! And I would eat the homemade jam with a spoon. Yum. Between the five in our party we tried the pork chops, steak, BBQ ribs, and the fried chicken. Everything was great! And the sides taste homemade as advertised.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: First time visiting TN and was recommended to stop in at Loveless. Food was incredible and our server Barbara was an absolute angel. We ordered half of the menu and had no regrets. Everything was delicious.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loved the chicken, i fell inlove with this place 4 years ago and will come back for sure everytime im in town!! People are very friendly

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I had a friend in town and decided to show her the typical Nashville tourist experience by bringing her to Loveless. We came on a Saturday morning around 10am and had a 45 minute wait. To kill time we checked out their little shops and had a great time looking at all of the cute things. 

When we finally sat down we were greeted with a warm plate of their amazing rolls. The rolls ended up being the highlight of the meal. We ordered the red velvet waffle which tasted just like a regular waffle. I thought it needed some cream cheese icing or something to spruce it up. Then we ordered the fried chicken hoping to experience some of the classic southern cooking that they're known for. The fried chicken turned out to be so dry that it was hardly edible. 

Overall it's a place to try out once but I don't need to go back again, there are better places for southern food elsewhere.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I'm a local, and I rarely come here.  Shame on me, this place is terrific.  Cozy atmosphere. Great food. Friendly, attentive service.  Today I had the country ham, eggs over medium, biscuits, fried okra, and hash browns.  They were all on point.  Rachel was my server, and she provided thoughtful, friendly, attentive service.  Tip for tourists - come in the middle of the day during the week and you can be seated almost immediately.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Make sure to call and see if they're open. Uber'd all the from the city to discover we went on the one day a year they were closed for cleaning/maintenance. Was not advertised anywhere that they would be closed. Great way to start off the morning.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Thank you, Kim, for outstanding service tonight during our show! You were so attentive, sweet and helped us have the best New Year's in a very long time! Food, atmosphere and entertainment was spot on!

name: Big Shotz
text: If you are other them white they will just prefer for you not to be there. Special if you are Latino like me and my wife, I been living in Nashville for 26 years and I never found people more racist them the girl at the door and the other guy she called to tread me and push me, and said racist stuff to us. If they have any cameras at the front door please check it out to see what they did to us!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Went to the Loveless cafe this past weekend on my visit to Nashville. The biscuits were top notch! I rate this four stars because i felt like the Server was rushing us out of there. I know this place probably gets very busy on the weekends, but we were there pretty early and there was still lots of seTing. I hate being rushed...

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Overpriced with an a**hole bartender!  I asked for thousand island on my reuben sandwich & got charged 50 cents extra. A very small 10 ounce beer is $6.50. One beer, a sandwich & dessert was $35. I don't mind paying more at times, BUT it's definitely not worth it when you get sh*tty attitude from the staff. I won't be back.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: My husband and I lived in Germany for several years and loved the food. We have searched the United States for 30+ years for good, authentic German food and have only once found it....until today. The décor took us on a trip down memory lane, right back to a Bierhaus in Munich! The service was great and the food were delicious! Although we sampled several different dishes ordered at our table (and each was wonderful), there are others we can't wait to try! We will definitely be back! This restaurant has earned our seal of approval!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Update: I tried their hashbrown casserole and am in love. Just FYI.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We went out of our way to go here solely because of its hype and reviews. This place is off the beaten path if you're coming from Nashville. 
We had a wait (~30 mins) but entertained ourselves with corn hole and wandering through the shops. 
We LOVED the biscuits and variety jams. 
FYI- a friend I was traveling with asked "do you have a gluten free menu?" and our waitress responded "sweetie, I'm pretty sure we have gluten in our heating and air system"! 
We came to a BISCUIT spot, so we just laughed this off and my friend picked from the menu.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I came here with a few friends on a weekend for brunch. We waited about 2 hours but it was completely worth it. Besides, we were able to pass the time in their retail shop and by playing cornhole. I got the chicken and waffles with a side of biscuits and sausage and gravy. The food was AMAZING. If you're in the area this place is a must try. The service was wonderful as well!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I've wanted to try Bavarian Biehaus since it opened and was so excited to see that it was listed good for kids as we have a 4 year old.  My husband, daughter, and I took the drive to Opry Mills on Saturday evening and crossed our fingers we would have to wait less time at the restaurant than getting off the exit to Opry Mills:)  This place didn't scrimp!  The outside looks just as amazing as the inside. The restaurant was busy but we were able to sit right away.  I do advise when going to sit in communal seating, even with kids.  We sat in the section with table seating and although it was a bit quieter all the fun is definitely in communal seating. 

The restaurant really creates the Oktoberfest vibe.  My husband went to Oktoberfest in Germany and was really impressed with everything from the decor, the food, the music, and rowdy groups of people drinking steins of beer.

We had the Brozteitteller which is an array of meats and cheeses, as well as, a pretzel and rye bread... For dinner my husband had the fish and chips which he really loved and I had the chicken schnitzel w/ spaetzle. My daughter had a GIANT hot dog from the kids menu. Everything was good!

After dinner my daughter got a kick out of dancing with the band which was her favorite part! Will we be back?Well according to my daughter it's her new favorite restaurant!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A true classic. Country ham and biscuits with red eye gravy - it doesn't get any better than that!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Headline: mediocre food (for the price) that's overshadowed by really bad service.

We had a reservation for Mother's Day, but they didn't have a table ready for us so told us we could either wait or sit outside. It was a nice night, so we chose to sit outside, which was empty except for one table of loud, drunk a-holes. Even though the patio was completely empty, they sat us (a family of 4 celebrating Mother's Day) within arm's reach of the other table. I understand that waiters have sections and want tables close together, but seriously, this was ridiculous. For the first hour of our meal, we listened to them (we had no choice...THEY WERE YELLING!!!) discuss the finer experiences in life...you know, like finishing an entire bottle of vodka in one sitting. 

Our waiter was a nice guy but never told us anything about the wine, menu, or specials. Interesting, for a place with "winery" in the name, that they hand you a wine menu that's longer than "The Odyssey" and don't tell you anything about it. Our 4 entrees came out in 3 trips...2 at first, the 3rd about 5 minutes later, and then the 4th about 15 minutes after that. 

The food was good, but nothing special for comparably priced places (~$25/entrée). The pork belly dish MAYBE covered half the plate. It's a small piece of meat with some mashed potatoes and a few peas. It was good (both bites!), but I left hungry. 

Maybe they could use the $5 you have to pay for parking to put some food on the plates.

We won't be back.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
We went with the family for a lunch on Sunday.  There was a very short wait for a table for 8.  

The place is huge. The beer was a mixture of German and local.  We all had different dishes and shared around the table.  Everyone loved their meals and the menu has enough variety that you could go back many times and not repeat anything on the menu.  

Highly recommended!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
All the key elements of the German Oktoberfest theme are here - the fare (large steins of beer, pretzels, meats), the garb (severs dressed in traditional outfits) and the facilities (long communal tables and a performance stage).  Big fan of all the execution and would recommend drinking and dining here to anyone even if they weren't looking to feel like they are in Stuttgart or Munich.  

Dinner dishes are $15 or more (I.e. Half chicken dinner for $17) and half liters of beer in non-happy hour settings run you $7.50 each. Not bad given the quantities of food and beverage you receive.

Will sample a few more meals before throwing on the fifth star but the adults and kids all enjoyed their appetizers & drinks here. Only criticism at this point is of the rouladen which was just OK - not flavorful and moist as grandmother used to make (although maybe I'm to blame for expecting such authenticity and not appreciating the availability of such niche dishes).

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A Nashville tradition that doesn't disappoint on the food.  We are regulars for breakfast, but that's all we come for, so I can't speak of the lunch and dinner. Their country ham with red eye gravy is excellent as are their cheese grits and hashbrown casserole. Love the sweet tea, not killer in the sweetness.  Be early or be patient. After 8 on the weekend, be prepared for an hour or more wait. Fortunately, the pagers they give you work on the entire property so you can go shop while you wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Went again after the Vanderbilt commencement ceremony. This time I was in a large group and each person ordered something different. I got the fried pork chops, which were huge portions (2 big pieces) and very tender and juicy. A friend had the fried steak, which was also very good. I would give it 4 or even 4.5 stars because the food is delicious and the biscuits are always amazing (and the preserves are heavenly). Just be prepared to wait (we waited about an hour).

name: The Basement
text:
While I had a good time here and saw pretty cool bands (like Faux Ferocious), I wasn't into The Basement when I went there. My Yelp rating is more like 2.5 stars. 

I'm really not trying to be a hater, but there was an attitude in that place that soured the night for me. It's a cool looking venue - dark, dingy, rough around the edges, and a little grimy (all pluses for a rock club) - but the patrons and even some of the people working the club that night were kind of snooty. Of all places to be snooty, they were snooty here! 

Perhaps it could have been a bad night, but I got the feeling that this was Nashville Indie Rock Elitism B.S. in full force... Meh... That being said, I'll take the Hi-Tone in Memphis over The Basement any day (just saying).

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The ambience is great. I did not order the food but was shocked at the cost for two glasses of wine.  $32 with tip! wth?

name: The Country
text: Dim lights, dramatic ambiance, authentic country music and stiff drinks, my kind of place. I forget the name of my bartender but she was amazing.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: The hush puppies were AMAZING! Best I've ever had. I wish the chicken strips were bigger, but the sauce was great. I'll definitely be back.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Beer wasn't great (had the kazoo spring) yuck took all I had to actually choke it down. Staff was friendlier to the men  guess what women drink beer too and we tip as well.  Met some cool people in the short time we were there that's about as memorable as it gets

name: The Country
text: No wait staff for the patio. The bartenders are extremely rude and the drinks are average. The patio has potential but the service makes you never want to return.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Wish I could give this place zero stars. They ignored us when we sat at the bar to place an order and finally someone spoke to us... 40 minutes later we still haven't received our food and the staff is horrendously rude. Not worth it y'all! PASS!l oh and then when we got the food FINALLY (what was supposed to be jambalaya and a quesadilla) we had two TINY cups of gumbo.. $40. Not even what we ordered. No refund offered or anything. Management needs to get a grip on this horrendous restaurant.

name: The Country
text: Hard to evaluate bartenders are unresponsive and sully band seems good and the crowd responsive, but come have a pulse of

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
I went here to see Sam Hunt. The show was great. The event venue is fine, it's a large room with a stage. The stage is where it is to allow for the max amount of people. If you want to be close to the stage, get there early. I arrived about an hour and a half before the show and got right up in front of the stage. And there was free parking! I didn't get anything from the bar or go into Mercy Lounge so I am not sure how that is. 
I do think the staff at the Cannery Ballroom need some training. I emailed them about tickets (I wanted VIP tickets), facebook messaged them, and called them. No one ever had the decency to email me, call, or message me back. There was plenty of time before the show for them to get in contact with me. Even if they were sold out, I still would have appreciated being told that.   Working on customer service would be a good way to improve this business. 
Otherwise, I had a great time and the show was great.

name: EXIT/IN
text: Great small venue! It has everything you need to put on a great show. And they have a wide range of artists that come through. A few I've seen are Cursive, Save Ferris and Ingrid Michaelson.

name: Drifters
text:
Drifters has the potential to be a powerhouse BBQ provider here on the east side, but the past several visits have been somewhat disappointing. I'll be the first to admit that they have some great items on their menu, and the pricing is wonderful for what they offer, but the quality of the BBQ leaves a bit to be desired.

During the most recent visit, I ordered the combo with three sliders (chicken, brisket and pork) and fries. Starting with the pulled chicken, I found the flavor to be slightly questionable. I could immediately see that it was dry and not juicy at all, and there was something unusual about aftertaste that I just couldn't put my finger on. Next, I moved on to the brisket and found the same issues - dry and not very flavorful (especially compared to some amazing brisket I've had at some other local places). The final slider - the pork - was pretty good, but nothing too spectacular. What helped was their selection of sauces. We had a sampler of the Georgia, Sweet & Smoky and Sweetfire (which are just 3 of the 9 they offer), and they helped provide some of the flavor that was absent in the meat. The fries were great, though, and I easily could have polished off another order.

In past visits, I had the chance to try the hush puppies, which are really something special. Sweet onions and jalapenos encased in a battered shell and coupled with their Alabama sauce - how can you beat that? I've also had the pork plate during past visits and it's been OK. Maybe we caught them on a bad night for this recent trip, but as much as we love having a BBQ joint here in the neighborhood, we'll probably continue to fulfill our BBQ needs outside of the 5 Points area.

name: Commodore Grille
text: I'm a huge fan of Black Bean Burgers...not a vegetarian just love them. This is by far the best one I have ever had!!! Absolutely delicious...so flavorful. A must try even for a meat lover.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Very intimate music venue...as in very tight space. The acoustics were great but there is literally no space. Overpriced and water-downed drinks. If it weren't for the great entertainment would never come back.

name: Drifters
text:
Food was amazing. Could not have been happier. We came here around 8pm on a Thursday after spending the day brewery hopping and the patio was a great place to sit and relax. The live music was enjoyable and not too loud where you can't hear the person you're with. 

We ordered the hush puppies which were very good, but very filling so I definitely recommend if you have two or more people. 

I got the bbq plate with pork and it was AMAZING. The meat was juicy and the sauce was to die for. The fries -- don't even get me started. So crispy and crunchy and amazing. I cleaned my plate. 

I highly recommend Drifters if you want good bbq and a great atmosphere.

name: Drifters
text: Good spot for a burger and happy hour is all day on Tuesdays so that is always a good thing. I love this place for staying non smoking so that is plus!

name: The Country
text:
Yep, I see a few 1 star reviews for unfriendly staff...I concur. However, this 1 star review is to warn you to not order the chicken under any circumstance. For $8, they bring you one sad chicken wing that was cooked God knows when, that they have warmed up in a microwave alongside a miniature biscuit. If anything, it would be good for a laugh 6 beers in.

Okay, okay, don't order food at a bar and expect a lot. So let's talk about their beers on tap. Hmmm, slightly cooler than room temp, served in a warm glass. Umm, I'll go elsewhere thank you.

name: Drifters
text:
Went here twice. First time had a pretty darn good experience. Great food. We got stew, nachos, and a taco salad. Service was fast, portion sizes were enormous. Live music, pretty nice outside venue. Our server seemed like she was worked like a dog.

Second night I really wanted to try their ribs. Had to go physically find a waiter to take our order after waiting at least twenty minutes. He then came back to tell me they were out of ribs. Took a good 10-15 minutes after that to get our drinks, no service recovery. We left disappointed. Might try going on a weekday or for lunch

name: Drifters
text: A really fun place. Truly a dive bar but with character. The bartenders were really attentive and friendly. We were visiting from San Diego and they really took care of us. They had live entertainment that night and the band that was playing, The Stoves, were really good. We had the Nachos and pulled pork and pulled chicken sandwiches. They were all good. The best part were the sauces. Keller brought over a sample of all of their sauces and I couldn't make up my mind which was the best. We will have to come back and test them again.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
Maybe it's because the Belcourt is where I first saw The Rocky Horror Picture Show (as a 22-year old; far too late, I know), but I have a lot of love for this small indie theater.

In a great location, the Belcourt is all you need in a small theater:  cheap tickets, plenty of seating, a historic home-town vibe, and the ability to buy alcohol at the bar.  It's not rocket science.

I also saw the recent Amy Winehouse documentary here.  Can't wait for the theater to open again this summer!

name: EXIT/IN
text:
So for my 1800th review the Exit/In is a worthy venue.  I saw my Oxford, MS pals the Kudzu Kings here and crazy Kudzu Dave, the bass player, virtually lives at my house in New Orleans about half the year and I've known the folks in the band from since and before the band started.  I was also glad to see quite a few folks from long ago that I hadn't seen in many years show up for the show so that made the whole experience even better.  The venue is spacious while not being too big to lose the ability to have a good view of the performance from pretty much all over the space so it was intimate without being cramped.  They also have an upstairs balcony level area that also adds some more good space to view the show.  The sound quality in the space was also of good quality which isn't always the case in some venues.  I was also happy to see that this space has hosted a LOT of famous and less famous quality bands and they have a pretty extensive list of them on the wall behind the bar.  The bar service was quick and easy but it did take the bartender's longer than average to remember my tab. The Tiki Bar exit that leads to their patio did not have a Tiki Bar but it does lead off pretty near to Cafe CoCo which is an awesome place to grab a snack and more beer after a show!  

Overall this is definitely an awesome venue to watch a show in and it is just a perfect size place to have a great music experience.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Cannot give this place a higher rating. I've rarely had a better movie-going experience, with knowledgeable and hospitable staff, high quality refreshments, gorgeous theaters, and excellent movie selections. You also get a parking pass that is good for 2 hours before the movie time and 2 hours after, giving you time to explore Hillsboro Village without the hassle of street parking. I will be back soon; I would see any movie shown here at any time.

name: Drifters
text: This place is amazing! A little off the beaten path, but so worth it. Huge dog friendly patio with bags and ping pong, and the inside is divey and wonderful. The food is very very good, and the prices are really reasonable (and the happy hour specials even better!). I'm a vegetarian, but my husband is not, and we were both so happy here. I had the fried tofu sandwich with cole slaw and he had the pork sliders with tots. Both left us so happy and full (but not too full to try the banana pudding!). The portion of tots was enormous, but they were the perfect conduit to the delicious BBQ sauces they have. The sauces are all available via BBQ sauce bar--our favorites were Texas and sweet & smoky. The banana pudding was pretty big; my only complaint was that it could have been more banana-y (and even then it was still really good). Highly recommend this place! If only they would pick up and move to Phoenix, AZ!

name: The Country
text:
Went on a Sunday night around 8:30pm.  There was an $8 cover per person.  The the kitchen was closed.  Half the draft beer was sold-out, making the otherwise decent beer selection below average.  The band playing was good, but the acoustics in the place were bad.

Bottom Line:   Go somewhere else.  The acoustics are not good, there is a cover charge, the kitchen was closed and the beer selection was sub-par.

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
Stopped in Thursday night after having dinner in the Gulch. None of our group had ever been. We had originally thought we were going to stop into the Tin Roof, but all they had was hockey on the TV. Walked down to Frisky Frog and the music we heard sounded good and we decided to stop in. Place was not super busy, but lets be honest, it was a Thursday. We grabbed some drinks and sat close to the band. The  band was great! Such a variety of music, including rap. Great music to sing and dance along to. Drinks were good and strong. 
We enjoyed ourselves so much that we ended up going back again Friday night after making some rounds.

name: Springwater
text:
After a day bouncing about Nashville and stopping by  the Parthenon, we wanted - no, NEEDED - a drink.  This place was the closest walk, and it turned out to be a blast!  Very kind bartenders, large beer menu.  It's beer only, but I loved that.  

It states it is the oldest bar in TN, and I believe it.  I know these places like to keep their "cash only" status, but in 2016, it may be time to kiss that vestige goodbye.  I'd still go back, though!

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
Checked out the mercy lounge for the first time last night to see Porches & Girlpool play and I was not disappointed with the music or the venue. It was relatively spacious for a small-medium concert and wasn't overpacked despite there being a decent amount of people there. They also have a fairly affordable drink menu, which is always appreciated. Service was fast and the overall vibe of the venue was cool.

My only critique is that their photobooth didn't work and tends to steal people's money --  that being said, they have a sign explicitly stating this, so using the photobooth is really at your own risk. The staff also was very transparent about this. Overall a fun venue, would recommend checking it out!

name: Drifters
text:
Not bad, not bad at all! Drifters gets a major nod for being a BBQ joint with a dedicated vegetarian menu. Keep your expectations in check, though, after all it *is* a BBQ joint. No culinary wonders for those of us avoiding the offerings from the smoker (however, my guy is a BBQ fanatic and ordered the most monstrous plate of nachos with some kind of BBQ meat splayed across 'em. This looked like a delicious mess, which was confirmed), but utterly basic basics: tofu, which I'm a fan of + Morningstar Farm protein, which I'm not a fan of (and if you're vegan, know that Morningstar Farm is not). 

I ordered the Tofu Dinner w/o slaw, which also comes with fries and beans (not sure if that was meat swimming around with those beans so I didn't taste them. It sure looked like meat shreds). It's a generous portion and although I wasn't blown away by anything on the plate, I can see it being the perfect late night food (yes! they have late night hours!) and it sure did treat my lingering annual hangover right. As did the Bloody Mary.

The staff is nice. The patio is sweet and the interior is the perfect dark, divey BBQ joint kind of atmosphere. I like this place a lot. And I'm just so appreciative of a BBQ place doing something cool for vegetarians that is truly unexpected. What's not to love about that?

name: Drifters
text: Ok I'm from KC so BBQ is kind of a big deal in our neck of the woods. Had the brisket sandwich and tots. Good fresh bun and generous amount of brisket. Good hickory penetration, not too dry. House sauce is sweeter than KC likes but good smokiness. Tots were spot on. Nobody likes a soggy tot. Great hole in the wall vibe, good service, and the soundtrack reminds of all the songs I need to add to my Apple playlist. Nice BBQ break for a KC chick.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
My thoughts on the Cannery Ballroom echo my thoughts on Mercy Lounge pretty much verbatim (they are in the same building after all). I feel like the room near the stage is a bit freer in the Cannery than in Mercy but it's been awhile since I've seen a show at Mercy to know if that's actually true or not. Anyway, for the Cannery as a music venue:
I see a lot of reviews complaining about the drinking area being roped off to a tiny space? I've been to several shows, most recently in November 2017, and this has never been the case. Of course they've been 18+ shows but they stamp you if you're 21 and up and you can go wherever you like with your drink. Maybe at shows where there are very young attendees it's different? I thought this was a bar and all shows were 18+ but I could be wrong.

PROS:
*Good size for working bands and artists to headline (not the kind who play the stadiums--we're talking about up and coming, used to be, niche, cult, local, underground, etc.). You can see the show from pretty much anywhere in the room and navigate your way to the front if you wish fairly easily.
*Easy parking--get there early and park for free on site, get there a bit later and park in a pay lot connected to the main lot for only $5 which is not bad at all by Nashville standards
*Easy bar navigation--they will greet you, serve you, etc. pretty quickly
*If you're a smoker there's an easily accessible deck and they let you in and out with no hassle. If you're not a smoker that deck is far enough away from everything that nothing drifts back in
CONS:
*Acoustics at Cannery (and Mercy) leave a bit to be desired as everything gets 2x louder than it needs to be as it echoes off of every stone and brick surface area. WEAR EAR PLUGS! If it's a particularly loud act try and stand midway back from the stage. On my most recent visit the opening acts sounded great but I moved to the front for the headliner and it was deafening. That in some ways was simply due to the nature of the band and the music they played but better acoustics would've softened it enough to hear the range of the performance a bit better. I overheard someone on my way out telling their friend "you never stand too close to the front, always half back and the sound's better". Maybe for this place but I've been in several venues where you can stand right by the stage or at the very back and whether the loudest of metal or the softest of folk music if the acoustics are right it'll sound great wherever you are. 
*Drink prices and selection: while not as bad as Bridgestone or the Ryman, the FAQ on their website is a bit misleading when it claims "drinks start at $3 and go up". I ordered my share of different beers and drinks and nothing was $3--not even PBR or Miller Hi-LIfe. There were no (or few b/c I didn't see them) craft or import beer options so if you're a beer drinker it's standard mass produced American beers for 5 bucks a pop.
*Entrance procedure: it's odd. You get here and park but if you walk to the door to line up they direct you outside of the gates and down the sidewalk then march you in field trip style once gates are open.

That's about it. I'd see another show here if it's the right act but this iisn't my favorite place to see a band in Nashville by any means.

Cold beer - check

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
The Belcourt is my favorite thing in Nashville. I would like Nashville about 35% to 45% less if the Belcourt wasn't here. 

The new building isn't my favorite. How did it take millions of dollars to make everything look somehow at once cheaper and newer? They've traded the rundown, ramshackle charm of a 1920s movie palace in decay in for something that looks a lot like cinemas in Williamsburg or downtown Manhattan, and they've compromised the original facade's tripartite arches--still used as the theatre logo--in order to build up. Basically, the Belcourt is now a white gallery cube, fitting perhaps because some shoddy local artists now seem to be on lowkey display and because the theatre shows self-described art house films. Perhaps it's just the tone of white and the absolutely pristine nature of the affair, or perhaps it's just the kind of nostalgia typical of millennials to yearn for the original. On the other hand, the new theatre upstairs, the conference room/educational spaces, and the new entryway for the smaller theatre downstairs are really welcome additions. 

The new upstairs theatre allows them to show more obscure, less popular films to smaller audiences--but I'd suggest sitting in the first two rows because the screen is quite small and the height differential between rows is not enough to allow one to see subtitles. The original "1925 Hall" (where the Opry was briefly located) isn't a truly remarkable old movie palace space, however, the continued presence of a decorated proscenium and the old, red, velvet-y seats ensure that even postmodern biopics about David Foster Wallace feel like you're watching them in a 1960s time machine rather than a Regal Cinemas. The second theatre downstairs is newer, likely from the 1980s, but has excellent sound and picture quality. 

The concessions aren't really a step above what you'd get at a normal multiplex beyond a wider selection of beers (the Regals at Opry MIlls and Green Hills Malls have mainstream Trump beers; the Belcourt slyly eschews GOP beers for the impartial PBR and local/Southern brands) and hard alcohol. You DO get $1 refills on any size popcorn, which is great if you have only had breakfast and felt as though that Truffaut movie was going to feed you more than Fido. In fantasies, they serve like kale chips, green smoothies, and burgers. 

Parking at this point is competitive during peak hours. I'd recommend getting to the theatre an hour to an hour and a half before your movie when there isn't such high demand, parking, and then grabbing a beer at the dive bar the Villager Tavern. Your parking pass lasts two hours before and after the film so make use of it. Just don't patronize the nearby chains like Jeni's which have turn Nashville into a monstrosity.

Overall the film selections are outstanding, diverse, original, and often adventurous. Sure, the Belcourt tend to keep some real stinkers masquerading as independent film ("Nocturnal Animals," anyone) for too many weeks, however, between the mainstream first run independent fare (which is often v good) they run anywhere between what I have counted to be two and eleven repetory films a week: on Friday at midnight, you can see a cult classic horror film about a serial killer Santa; on Sunday at noon, you can watch a film celebrating indigenous black culture on South Carolina's coast; on Tuesday night, you can see a biopic with sterling performances if lackluster script; on Monday afternoon, you can see a newly digitally restored "Battle of Algiers" with a seminar led by a Vanderbilt professor afterwards; and, on Saturday morning, you can go to a roundtable discussion of black gay male sexual identity to accompany your viewing of the aforementioned "Moonlight." Really, the offerings are exceptionally diverse and adventurous for a theatre with only screens serving a relatively conservative, otherwise artistically unadventurous blue dot in a red sea. 

While I go to the Belcourt at least twice a week, I don't really see the great advantage to becoming a member. You get 20% off only the non-alcoholic concessions (boo!) and, especially if you're a student, the ticket discount isn't large enough (student and all matinee ticket prices are $8.50, while member tickets are $7; normal evening tickets are $10) to make the membership fees worthwhile. 

I mock the employees a lot but perhaps shouldn't. Some of them are totally the performative media/theatre studies types who turn purchasing a ticket into a one act play about being a FRIENDLY hipster in a dead end job making sacrifices so you can get your parking pass but a lot of them are just chill af. I've gotten free concessions before late at night, and I've also had a ticket refunded for a film I found unwatchable--twice. Like I said, I come here a lot, but, generally, the employees are gracious without acknowledging the fact that I probably go to too many movies.

THE BELCOURT IS THE BEST CULTURAL INSTITUTION IN NASHVILLE.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
This theatre is a non profit venue to watch independent films.  The theatre first started in 1925.  



The theatre also has food.  Most of it is typical movie theatre, but they have bratwurst.  



However, this is my favorite part of the theatre, a full bar!  Yes, please!



I had a mimosa while watching the movie.  



I like this theatre.  It's a good place to watch independent movies and to enjoy a cocktail while doing it.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Awesome time ! Highly recommended- great bands and awesome service !!! Bands were very good ! 
I was a little taken back by the gentleman working in the bathroom - but all good. We will go back later today as it's on the main stretch to our ho

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: While visiting Nashville with a group of friends, Honkey Tonk Central was definitely our home away from home! The service was great (excluding one night with a waitress we dealt with around dinner time). The live bands were awesome, and very personable with the crowd. We always had a great time when we stopped by Honky Tonk Central (which was every day we were there for a few hours at a time!) I would highly recommend Honky Tonk Central to anyone who is visiting Nashville and wants to get a taste of a real Honky Tonk!

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text:
Went for stand up and REAAALLLY liked it. For a dive bar, it's actually fairly well lit and a couple of decent brews (in bottles mind you).

Baller as all heck! Go here!

name: Famous Nashville
text: Food was good. A little pricey but it id Nashville.  Staff was kind and courteous especially at the bar!  Music on Thursday was outstanding!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
In from NH.hittting all the downtown spots. We were looking for a place for dinner and music without all the crowds and better food than what we had at a few of the places we hit. 

Great service friendly and great sandwiches and apps.Band was top notch, Good drinks, beer selection a little thin.

name: Alley Taps
text: The bar is cozy with plenty of room to sit and enjoy the music.  The drinks are basic,  but come for the music.  The Willies on tap tonight playing 20's inspired swing, blues and jazz.  The 7 member band is fronted by Jen Jones an energetic lead vocalist who keeps the band in order. Worth hearing for a good time trading off between country and blues.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
So, great venue. Love having yet another place to hear live music in Nashville, and with AmSouth/Starwood Amphitheater gone, this place was sorely needed. Obviously it is nowhere near as large as the old amphitheater venue was in Antioch, but it is downtown Nashville with a killer view of our humble skyline and within walking distance to all the best that downtown has to offer.

Pros: Our group went for the recent Needtobreathe show and had a blast. The acoustics are great, and the venue sounds like a true amphitheater. Everything was neat, clean, and relatively well designed.

For the cons: You will NEVER get me to pay $16 for a single beer. What in the crow?! Also, the seats in the reserved section need to be rethought. It was incredibly hard to find your section and row, but when you finally reached your destination, not all the chairs are marked with the numbers, and you don't realize upon your initial visit that the numbers that are there are tiny and stuck on little removable magnets on a minuscule sticker on the back of the chairs in front of you. The crowd departure needs to also be rethought. The gates are tiny, and when you have 6-7,000 people departing at the same time, it becomes a complete cluster trying to simply get out of the venue.
