Overall, we will most definitely be back, as we have tickets to another upcoming show in just a couple weeks, but we will be more prepared and most certainly will have had a drink or two before the show. $16, hah! I can't help but laugh every time I think about it. (Oh, it's also $4.50 for a small bottle of water, so be prepared for that too.)

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: This is a beautiful venue! My friend won free tickets but I'm not sure I would've spent money to sit way back in the lawn. Also check the weather before you go- it started raining during the show and there is not many places to run for cover.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: This is a real country bar nestled right in between the music studios. Very cold beer, nice people locals not the bachelorette parties lol. I wouldn't call this a dive it's pure country more like "authentic".

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
What a great place. Tons of seating. Great band. Lots of windows to see all the action going by as well. Great food too
Nice crowd

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Located in the heart of downtown Nashville, Ascend Amphitheatre provides top touring live acts. 

There is not a bad seat on the house. The view of the Nashville skyline and downtown is beautiful. 

This venue is walking distance to Acme, Tootsies, Pinewood Social and many Nashville honky tonks. 

There is also not a bad seat in the house. They rent lawn chairs to sit in, as well!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Went on a Thursday to the 3rd floor & the service was not great. My friend & I walked up to the bar, very close to the bartender, had our money out & ready yet we were forced to watch her put on her lip gloss & walk to the other side of the bar. Just had to laugh. Had a pretty good time dancing to the band other than that.

Went on Saturday & the first floor was so crowded we could not even move so we went to the 2nd floor & there it seemed the bartenders were moving as fast as possible (although it took me 10 minutes to get a bud light, at least she was working as hard as she could & was very pleasant). 

Because it is right on the corner & the bands both nights were good, I would recommend stopping by for the first bar of the night just to experience it and then moving on.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: Stopped here on the trolley tour and was surprised it was so good. Great decor, music and vibe. I will definitely come back again.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Nice amphitheater with ample lawn seating, came here for a Beck concert. Annoyed that we brought in umbrella and lawn chairs that were too high so had to rent their chairs. Plus we had to leave our umbrella and chairs (all 4) that we picked up today from Walgreens. Rent four for $7.50 each. Hope no one steals our stuff!

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Great bar. Beautiful decor and such a great atmosphere. 

Has a great wine collection and out of most of the bars is easy going and relaxed.
If I had to describe it I would say the affordable sophistication on broadway. 
A nice break from the crazy honky tonk outside.
Which is still amazing but some times you need to escape from.

I highly recommend visiting. Xx

name: Famous Nashville
text: Unbelievable brunch - best we've had!  Beautiful trendy bar.  Awesome chicken and waffles and breakfast quesadillas.  #monkeybreadgamestrong

name: The Station Inn
text: We went for the Sunday night Bluegrass jam and it was one of the highlights of the weekend. The performers were fantastic and the talent performing was a joy to watch.  If in Nashville, do yourself a favor and stop in on a Sunday night.  I promise you won't regret it.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I went on the Saturday of Memorial Day weekend. It was packed but I loved it. 3 floors with 3 different bands. I drank a ton and didn't spend much. One of the girls I was with got kicked out for being too drunk, but the guy kicking her out couldn't have been any nicer about it. She had lost a shoe and he searched the bar for it and found it. And nicely led us to an elevator so she didn't have to walk down the stairs. If you get kicked out of a bar in Chicago, they aren't gentle or friendly about it. Can't wait to go back here!

name: Nashville Underground
text:
So, for those who don't know, this spot on Broadway St is owned by the infamous Gavin DeGraw. We were seated right away and had a very friendly waiter. There's an upstairs to this restaurant where I suspect the younger crowd goes to dance. There is a great rooftop lookout that overlooks Broadway (great for pictures).

The food was delicious! Not only was there great music played by very good looking country artists, but there was also plenty of drinks to go around. I ordered a mild hot chicken which was spicy enough for this Wisconsiner. I recommend going lighter when ordering the spicy chicken, since the mild was pretty dang hot. 

I will definitely be coming back to try this place out again...even though I can't decide if it'll be for the food or the cute singers!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Such s great spot on broadway. They invite everyone in they have great bands and they really appreciate their customers. Refreshing

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I'm a local who has always enjoyed Honky Tonk...until....

My friend and I decided to go here on a casual Wednesday night. We got in line for the bouncer to check our IDs. The bouncer granted me entry then proceeded to check my friend's ID while I waited patiently inside. She started laughing and yelled out to me "He thinks your ID is fake!" Apparently, he told her to tell me to "get a better fake ID" when in fact, I have been legal for years and my ID is 100% valid and verified by Metro police. We immediately left after I told the bouncer my ID was real and he called his security on me for no reason. 

Go here if you want to feel unappreciated as a customer.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: A must if you are in Nashville!  Small venue with great entertainment, food and drinks!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Came to see the Time Jumpers and we enjoyed the event. A nice intimate setting for a concert for such big names in the band, but we still had plenty of space to be comfortable. Our waitress was lovely and gave us great reccomendations about other nearby attractions when she heard we were from out of town. Honestly, the food is sub par, but I wasn't expecting much more, being that most people come for just the music anyway. Would gladly return to see another show.

name: Alley Taps
text: This is a wonderful place to grab a small bite to eat and have a drink!  The food was pretty simple things: we ordered the ham and cheese sliders and the bbq sliders and both were really good for bar food.  The drinks were good.  The atmosphere is probably the best thing.  It wasn't crazy packed but there was still enough people to make it fun.  The music was good. Defiantly a place to check out!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Buyer drinker consumer beware. Went in here last night to the first floor bar and ordered two coors lights. So the first bartender says sure that will be $18.00. Wow ok that seems a bit high for two beers but oh well it was good music and busy. Then we order a second round with a different bartender and it was magically only $12.00 for the same two coors lights. Someone is making a lot of extra tips last night from over charging customers!!! Be careful is that really worth losing your job over thief bartender!!!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Great spot to see a concert.  The bar wraps around the entire back wall so you rarely have to wait for a drink, and the prices are pretty fair. The acoustics were surprisingly good, and the balcony tables provide a great view if the stage all around.  Definitely worth getting there early for one of the balcony tables-- but if not, the gently sloping standing room is great too.  I'd definitely come back and see another concert here.

name: The Station Inn
text: Hot, hot, high energy bluegrass music the night we were there. Super-talented musicians. If you have any pretense about you, you'll hate it but if you don't have a problem sitting on mismatched chairs at vinyl tablecloth covered tables listening to musicians wow you, get there in time to grab a table and some cheap beer ($15 Yahoo pitchers) and $2 popcorn. Prepare to enter bluegrass heaven!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Way fun place with awesome bands and several levels.  Better than most on Broadway!

name: Nashville Underground
text: A group of us came in on a Wednesday night. We went to the 4th floor. To be in you have to be over 21. But the bartender carded us again. Customer service was terrible.  The dance floor is amazing but the music is not good and when we asked to change to turn up, the bartender gave us much attitude and refused to do so.

name: Live On The Green Music Festival
text:
How can you say no to free music? No matter what kind of music it is, people love free. But, what if the free music was totally awesome? Like Matt & Kim, ZZ Ward, Michael Franti, Local Natives, Moon Taxi and many many more. 

Sitting on the grass, drinking a cold beer, hanging with friends and listening to this awesome music is exactly why I love Nashville so much. Shhhhh.....don't tell the rest of the country we are so awesome! 

Thanks Lightning 100 for hosting such a great event!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Went to Big Stage Mondays and it was fantastic!  For $10 you see a 2 great singer/songwriters and each introduces a "new face" who also performs.  One and half hours of great music.  What a treat.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Awful if judged by the bathroom attendants. Which is reason enough not to go. They are militant and absolutely offensive and terrible. Will not attend again or recommend to anyone ever. The music is okay/good and the bartenders are great, but the bathrooms make it bad enough an environment to skip for all the other better bars on the strip without bathroom attendants or at least ones like this. Note to management: Fire/get rid of the bathroom attendant who threatens to call security on you for bringing your drink into the stall with you in order to protect yourself from being roofied. As someone who had had a close friend roofied and raped thanks to a date rape drug in a drink at a bar, I do not take well to a bathroom attendant calling security on me (first floor 3:30PM on Saturday, May 21, 2016) because I chose to be safe and responsible by taking my CLEAR liquid drink into the restroom with me to avoid a similar fate. This is absolutely unprecedented and insane. Anti-woman and terrible. Fix this poison at your establishment or you will surely face legal ramifications in  the future. Everything women should stand against. Unbelievably appalled.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Might as well had a full body cavity search at the door and given a hard time and my wife's e-cig was confiscated.  Every pouch and every pocket will be searched while drunk assholes are allowed to be insanely over served and spill drinks all over the place.  Venue is otherwise nice and the sound is incredible.  Hire better people.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: When there are so many places on broadway to see, this place defiantly caught our eye just walking around on a Friday night. 3 stories, different bars and bands sounded really cool. We stayed downstairs and got a seat which was great to have since we were there for live music. Seats are a little old, but they get used a lot. Beers were a little high, but had a good selection. The bartenders were on it, normally takes about 5 minutes to get a drink other places, and I didn't wait more then a minute for a beer. The 2 bands we saw were great! We stayed for about 3 hours and had a blast.

name: Alley Taps
text: Walked in on a random Monday night. Visiting Nashville for work, and I love this place. Unpretentious bar with a good selection of beer and a great lineup of young artists. Came back a second night just to unwind. I didn't eat anything so I can't speak to the menu.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Went to the Ray LaMontagne show and his vocals were off for half of one of my favorite songs. If we're paying money for a ticket, the audio team needs to be prepared. It took a good 3 minutes for them to turn on Ray's vocals. And $15 for a Bud Light? Give me a break.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text:
My first dive bar experience in Nashville, and it does not disappoint.  Walking through the door, I was greeted by a haze of cigarette smoke.  I forgot that smell when Minnesota banned smoking in bars, can't say I really miss it...but I'll accept it for part of the "allure" of this bar that feels lost in a bygone era.
Dimly lit, sad country music playing from the soundsystem, and locals in small groups throughout the room...this is a place to learn something about this city.
No live music playing at the moment, maybe some will happen while I'm here.

Note, $5 minimum on cards, no local beer...standard American fare only...go for the Shiner Bock for 3 bucks. I dig this place, a lot.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: This place was charming and had great music. Decent moonshine prices :)

name: Nashville Underground
text: This place is terrible. Been twice and will never return. Bartender is terrible. He walked by my empty beer probably 20 times and never asked if I needed another one. Terrible service

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Awesome venue. There was a huge line but it moved very quickly. They did a fast check of bags and a pass through a metal detector. They had many drink options, though some could be pricey. The place was packed but emptied relatively quickly as well. The sound was awesome and the stage was well placed and designed

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Off the chain!! Country music!! Friendly  people!! Had a blast!! Gotta come back!! First time in Nashville! Not my last time!!!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Great venue to catch a show. Both big names and local bands alike. Not a bad view in the house and I love the fact that there is plenty of seating!? Whether you want up close and personal or if you prefer to chill in the back, relax and watch a show, they've got a table for you.  It's got a good food menu, full bar and we've never had bad service! Highly recommend!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Although some might deem this a tourist trap, my friends and I could not have had a better time in Nashville!  We started the night at Honky Tonk, made our way down Broadway and down 2nd street then found ourselves back at Honky Tonk because it was THAT much fun.

It has 3 floors with 3 separate bars and 3 separate bathrooms which is great because you don't have to leave the floor unless you want to hear a different band.  Oh yah, there are different live acts on each floor, each with a different vibe.  I really enjoyed their Honky Tonk Tea, especially a decently large cup for $7.

BEST TIP EVER FOR 90 DEGREE NIGHTS: The 3rd floor has the best air conditioning, specifically this area towards the left near the stage/bar area.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
We hosted a corporate event at Honky Tonk Central in July 2014 and couldn't have been more pleased with the venue and service we received. The vibe walking into the bar was fantastic - the place was crowded and the band sounded great. Our party had the entire 2nd floor reserved, with a private band for entertainment. The space was clean, large enough for our group of ~80, and had great views of Broadway from the open balcony and all-around windows.

The appetizer buffet was a hit and the service was impeccable. Thanks to Frank, Amanda P., Kori M., Leah C., Paige R., and Roger G. for being a great crew!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Do not order a mixed drink.  Neither one we ordered tasted like it had more than a drop of liquor on the straw.  And the coke was flat.

name: Famous Nashville
text: So walked in, place is packed, live band playing  band shuts down, DJ takes over. Place empties out. Take a hint. People come to Nashville for live music not stuff you can hear on your truck's FM.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Three floors of fun! It's less crowded than other bars nearby and decreases as you go up a level. The 3rd level music lacked the most. It's large and spacious and the 3rd floor has the best view of the streets but I would suggest hitting up another bar after checking out the view.

name: The Cowan
text: Cool venue! Located in Top Golf, so there is plenty of parking. However, when there is a concert Top Golf is closed off in the Cowan, which means you can get food from their menu. They had 2 food selections mini tacos and popcorn. A few drink options and selected beer options. I got a Coors light in aluminum alittle pricey, but most concert venues raise the booze price. The food tho, the tacos were tiny but hella mighty!  They had steak, chicken and pork (they didn't have spicy steak tho). The steak was Greek style with feta cheese and mediterranean salad style topping. The chicken... geez whoever made this spicy buffalo chicken with a carrot slaw... knew that it needed a bleu cheese dressing made it! I wish tho it had some bleu cheese crumbles.. hint hint. But the Asian pork taco with the crunch slaw.. hot dammm my favorite. I definitely want to go back to eat, I'm mean if they made those mini tacos... endless deliciousness is ahead. The bathroom were clean and maintain well. The security was on it too, from entrance to controlling the mosh pit and drunk concert goers. Definitely would come to another concert.

name: Nashville Underground
text: If you are over 25, avoid this bar. Lousy bar service (check your bill carefully) and the clientele is pretty low end.

name: Nashville Underground
text: This place is awesome!!   We descended on them as a traveling hockey team with a group of more than 40 and these guys took the best care of us!  The food was amazing, the server Dakota was fantastic and couldn't have done a better job taking care of such a big group and the manager Teddy shuffled things around to make it work for us!  Bull rides were so much fun - I can't stop thinking about the Poutine - wish I had time to go back for more!  Will definitely be my first stop if we come back next year!!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Came to Nashville for the week and every day we ended up back here. We had a hard time finding a bar with a good selection of beer on tap and this place had an amazing selection served ice cold. This was by far our favorite bar on Broadway. If you are looking for a more laid back place than some of the crazy bars, but with the best beer selection (not Jell-O shots), this is your place.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Loved the band - Donnie and Sam. Good service and enjoyed the Fritos Pie. Much better experience this go around!

name: Famous Nashville
text: Not a single person in here and our service was still slow as molasses.  This place was dead.  We ordered the hot pretzel app and left.  The pretzel was awful too!  Avoid.

name: Nashville Underground
text: $12 for a Jack and Coke. 'Nuff said. More since Yelp requires it. Average band if it wasn't Nashville. 15% full.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Yummy Food, Friendly Service and Music are Top Notch! 
Catch The Timejumpers on Monday at 8p!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Great acoustics! The bar has a great set up with balcony seating, lower seating, and standing room for dancing. The food was good for bar type food. Overall great experience, we will definitely be back!

name: Live On The Green Music Festival
text:
I have been going to Live on the Green since the start in 2009, when I was brand new to the Nashville scene. 

Every year it gets bigger and better - this is a must for locals and tourists!

So many great bands - whether they are popular, local bands, bands that have almost made it, or well-known bands that you are dying to see. It's always a great mix of music and well, I believe that is because it is put on by Lightening 100 - who is always on the lookout for the best music - new and old! (I swear that I secretly don't work for them - I just love them!)

Anyways, the best part - it's free!!

You can bring your lawn chairs, blankets, pets (although yes - bringing your cat is awkward...please just get a dog instead of acting like a cat can be a dog), friends, cash (for beer of course), and be ready to party!

I would recommend finding parking a little bit further out and then walking - parking is tricky downtown in the first place, but with an event - it's 1,000 times worse. Or, this year - they started parking at Marathon Music Works and a shuttle will take you there and back and there is an after party there too! I haven't tried it out - but I'm sure it's awesome as well.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Great place off of Broadway. Shelly and Daniel are fantastic behind the bar!!!!!!!!!  Live music is great great view from the rooftop

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We only got to pass through Nashville for a few hours, and after we walked around we decided to get food before we hit the road. This was the closest restaurant so we stopped inside. The server was really nice, though a little slow compared to our normal tristate experience. I had the sweet tea which was amazing, and definitely complimented the BBQ pulled pork. What really blew me away was that at 11 am on a Monday, there was a live act covering country songs. I was so excited to see this, I never wanted to leave!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Honky Tonk Central is always crowded and busy during the weekends and the staff isn't very friendly. It's pretty much standing room only and you have to fight your way to the bar to order drinks. They have good music and a "dance floor" area if you can get to it!! Stop in, have a drink, then go to the next bar.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: When the food finally came out it was pretty good! Our bartender upstairs was awesome! She dealt with like 3 large parties with no help! The place actually ran out of wings during the national championship game.....guessing the manager dropped the ball on a lot of things last night!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We had some of the BEST service ever from Heather! She was always always checking on us! She was so sweet and kind! The music was amazing! We enjoyed our afternoon so much! Can't wait to come back!

name: Nashville Underground
text:
A group of coworkers and I stopped in for lunch on a Tuesday.  We arrived after 12:30 and the place was empty.  Not the best sign.  It was so empty that it was "seat yourself" on the first floor.  

Orders around the table varied -- some hot chicken salads, a burger, the hot chicken ramen, chicken salad plate, some appetizers.  Our food came out relatively quickly, although the restaurant was empty, so I would have been mad if we had waited a long time. 

I had the hot chicken salad at a "hot" spiciness level.  First few bites--not hot.  Then out of nowhere the heat kicked in.  Not so hot that you could not eat the food but definitely hot.  The chicken on the salad is chicken tenders.  I must have touched one with my finger and then touched my face because the skin on my face started to burn.  Won't do that again.

Feedback from others at the table--the hot chicken ramen was more like a bowl of noodles.  Not much broth.  The coworker who had the burger said it was "disgusting" and did not finish her food.  The side of macaroni and cheese was "really good" I am told.  The sides are really small I will note.  The person who ordered the boiled peanuts said the peanuts were cold.  That's just gross.  

My salad was fine.  It was a salad.  I thought the chicken was good.  I would order it again--just maybe the medium heat level.  The service was fine.  All-in-all, a solid three-star Yelp experience.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
*This review pertains to their lunch only!

My search for good gumbo in Nashville surprisingly led me here. I work downtown so I wanted something quick and easy, but inexpensive as well. I entered around 1:45pm and sat at the bar, unaware that their lunch ended at 2pm. I was happy to know that I just made the cut! I was greeted quickly by the bartender, who suggested some of her favorite items. I knew I wanted gumbo, but she gave me a sample size of the chicken and dumplings soup. It was sooo good, the best I've had only second to my mother's. The gumbo was delicious but a little heavy with okra. The entire menu is $10 & under, there is plenty of parking, and you have the option to call in your order ahead of time. 3rd & Lindsley will become my go-to this winter for hot food during lunch hours.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: You can't beat this place for BBQ when you are near Pilsen, or even when you're not. Fun, festive atmosphere, and delicious food.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Had really good food.  We got the poutine and fried chicken and it was really good!  The live music always killer and the bar had some good local drafts

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Hole in the wall on Broadway with- hands down- the BEST bands on entire strip. You could go there when they open and never leave until they close and not be disappointed!

name: The Station Inn
text: We almost didn't make it to the Station Inn but I'm so glad we did because it turned out to be the highlight of our trip. If you've had your fill of 'Nash Vegas' and want to experience amazing talent in a low key setting, this place is for you. We visited on a Monday and got to see Val Storey, Carl Jackson and Larry Cordle do their regular gospel/bluegrass show. The welcome was warm, the beer was cold, everyone on the stage was a professional and Val has the voice of an angel. We arrived at about 10, right at the end of the first set and got in with no problem. What an amazing night!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
Small place with friendly staff. More of a local hangout then commercial bar. Had a couple of acoustic singers that were very good. Typical bar food that was all very good. Buffalo chicken wrap
Quesadilla both excellent.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I was determined to go to a honky-tonk bar while in Nashville.
I had a list of places to do Saturday night with my friend but my foot had other plans...  decided to step in a hole, sprain itself and have me unable to walk for the rest of the trip.
Thankfully the hotel I was staying at let me borrow a wheelchair so, Sunday, after brunch, I was able to go to Honky Tonk.

Right on Broadway, which is the main tourist street filled with bars, restaurants and lots to see and do, we went in.
People immediately made way for us and my wheelchair, made space for us at the bar, and were so nice.  The place is super casual, almost dive bar like.  Bartenders are flirty with the patrons, doing shots with them, making conversation, and singing on stage with the band.
Drinks are cheap, strong, and served fast.

Live music was great, even for a non-country fan.  I was dancing on my chair, enjoying the crowd dancing and singing, and having a great time.
The people visiting the bar are there to have fun. They make conversation with everyone at the bar, which gave us the opportunity to meet another guy visiting from Florida, and talk to locals that were just there to hang out and even invited us to some beers while we listened to the band.

This is exactly the type of bar I wanted to experience before leaving Nashville and so happy I was able to.  Even more appreciative that they accommodate me, and made me forget about the pain on my foot and wheelchair while I was there.  

Real fun place to go and chill with friends, people watch, and enjoy some live music.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Worst service ever. They treat everyone like tourists ... as if they won't ever see them again. It's embarrassing to be a Nashville resident with people like this.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Food would only be good if you were drunk. To call it mediocre would be generous. Got the lemon pepper wings... bad. Chicken tenders not very good either. Only good thing was fries, but it's pretty hard to screw those up... although I thought the same thing about chicken tenders, but I was wrong.

name: The Cowan
text:
This was a a huge disaster!  I went to the Cowan last night at Top Golf to see Cole Swindle Pre-Show Punch Launch Party.  Even though it was thunderstorming, raining cats and dog with lightning and high wind warnings...I still arrived 15 minutes early.  It said all over your advertisements that the doors would open at 5:30...great I can stand a bad weather under the tent provided at the entrance of the Cowan for 15 minutes...but that was not the case.  At 530...nothing...there was another event in the cowan that had the place packed.  The thunderstorm had picked up and there was lightning all around...the situation there became more unsafe.  At 5:58....28 minutes after the doors were suppose to open the cowan workers manning the entrance and one man with a sugarland hoodie on told the 60 or so of us hiding underneath the tent were told we need to get out of the tent and line up on the outside wall.  That's when my phone went off saying that Davidson County (Nashville) was under a tornado warning.  Everyone underneath the tent initially resisted the instructions out of safety but the Cowan worker continued on saying no one would be let into the event until the tent was cleared.  Everyone began leaving the tent ...many didn't have umbrellas but waited to get in for a lot longer than we had.  Many people because of the extreme weather and fear of safety left...which is what we ended up doing. We left at 6:03....33 minutes after you said in your ads that the doors would be open.
This event was complete chaos and had a total disregard for concert goer safety.  At NO point was there an alternative given for the safety of everyone there...they forced everyone out into extreme conditions with a tornado warning in progress. 
I have purchased many products from Sugarland including tshirts, Roaming man, flavored moonshine and glasses and have visited the store numerous times in Gatlinburg.  Ive never seen anything with the Sugarland brand on it that would lead me to think negative about your company...until last night. 
Im not sure if it was Top Golf's Cowan venue or your company that makes it a practice to intentionally put patrons at risk for their events during extreme conditions because of a lack of another plan.  I am an event organizer myself and have never seen such poor planning.  I left straight from work with a co worker to see this event...traveled a half hour.  After seeing the gross negligence of both your employee and the Cowen employees I knew that they didn't have any of out best interests in mind.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Ok, famous hot chicken, local brews served below freezing? (Not sure about the science on that one, but it's really cold!) here's the kicker: acoustic guitarist in the middle of the afternoon playing whatever classic rock and folk music I request. Oh yeah, and they have adequate screens showing hockey and baseball. It's like they knew i was coming. Not too shabby!

name: The Station Inn
text:
Our friend lived in Nashville and suggested The Station Inn to see some great local bluegrass. We stopped in on a Wednesday night and had an amazing time. The staff was great, the doorman and the bartender were both very friendly. 

The place is huge, so if you get there early, you can get a great spot up front or be seated with a large group of friends. It is nothing fancy, a bit of a dive bar, but that is definitely more of our scene than some of the other clubs we passed. The walls are covered with posters from years of great up-and-coming acts and I'm sure any act that plays there will be impressive and entertaining. The particular show that we saw was Mike Bub and Friends, a mishmash group of musicians who played wonderfully off of each other and put on a great show. One of the musicians invited to play with Mike that night was Scott Vestal, an amazing banjo player who we had seen years before with the Sam Bush Band. This place gives off the vibe that you never know who might show up to play here!

My only complaint is their very small beer selection. They had only a few beers on draft and mostly cheap domestics. They had $15 pitchers of a local brew which was pretty good and that's what we drank most of the night. 

If you like bluegrass and you're in Nashville, The Station Inn is definitely worth checking out!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This three story monstrosity sits on the corner of Broadway giving patrons a view into the looking glass of tourist town. A couple buddies and I showed up here after lunch and went straight to the top. It seemed to be the least busy as people weren't willing to walk up any further. We hung at the bar waiting for the rest of our group and watched the Masters. I'm not really a golf fan so I was a little bored but as time went on the bar got more lively. Bachelorette after bachelorette showed up with their woo-crew with one goal in mind... get turnt. As annoying as they can be, the bachelorettes got the place once after the band started and the woo-ing was held to a minimum being that it was still only 3pm. Even better than the show inside was the people watching outside. The balcony allows you to look down on a sea of party busses and whatever else rolls down the road. I saw musical acts, tractors pulling wagons of drunkards, and pedal bars regretting not being pulled around by a wagon or monster truck. We had to head out for an early dinner but I can only imagine what this place looked like only a few hours later.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Terrible service and cold food. When we arrived the second floor wasn't very crowded at all, yet the service was still horrible. Seemed very understaffed. Waited 45 minutes for the food and it was cold. Took 30 minutes to tab out. Avoid at all costs!!

name: Famous Nashville
text:
The rooftop bar was cool. 

We had drinks and nachos. Never in my life have I had nachos with no flavor. Between the cheese, beans, corn, tomatoes, etc...none of it had any flavor. It was the strangest thing. Neither of us could really taste anything. Worst $16 of nachos and that's saying a lot as I'm a frequent nacho order-er at football games.

Stick to the drinks.

name: The Station Inn
text:
We're talking about a legit old school bluegrass jam here. Sunday nights. It's free admission and it's so worth getting downtown for.

Every Sunday night his place turns into a dream, with amazing bluegrass artists all coming together. It's pretty magical to watch. It does get rather packed so be sure to get there earlyish. Cheap beer. 

The vibe isn't anything fancy, not that you'd expect that walking in. The Station Inn is everything it's meant to be. True. Real people. Great music. Rustic.  If you're a person who enjoys live music, this is something you need to do at least once in Nashville.

Also... Emmy Squared next door makes a mean pizza for before the show. See you there.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Today we had this AMAZING waiter Kirk! This guy had so much pep in his step, managed the entire floor efficiently and was a TON of fun! He literally made everyone feel special and made the atmosphere so much fun on this Saturday afternoon.  Thanks so much for making our day such a great time. We had no intentions of staying this long, but he made it worth it! Rock that bandana! You made our time there one of our most awesome memories of the trip!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: This is a lifetime memory of great music. The Time Jumpers are so amazing I'll never forget them.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Johnny T. got it right. What could potentially be wrong with Broadway can be found at this place. 

I was bored out of my mind. The music on a three levels was uninspired. I had it in my mind that I wanted to leave right when I entered and I should have followed my instinct. 

Instead, we stayed for about an hour. Paid $13 for two beers ... Twice over. The music was not up to the standard of other places on the strip. I'm sure I'll be back, but it's because of the location.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place is great and has multiple levels and all different kinds of music. We spent the majority of our night here and had a lot of fun. People from all ages were here and drinks were reasonably priced.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Love this place!! We sat on the upper level for a show on Sunday and even with a packed house our server Brittney did an amazing job keeping our drinks coming and checking on us to see if we needed anything. The view of the stage was perfect and the music sounded great! We ordered a sampler platter of appetizers as well and they were all delicious. I highly recommend the fried pickles and chicken tenders! TIP: Get there early to get in line before the doors open to get a good seat and get a Lyft or Uber to avoid the parking headache.

name: Music City Male Revue
text:
My friends and I went to the Saturday 4pm show for a bachelorette party and had the time of our lives!!! I know there aren't a lot of reviews because it's a new show but we loved it and we walked out of there laughing and smiling from ear to ear. It's so fun!

Initially, I was a little annoyed because we bought VIP tickets to the Friday 6pm show but a few days before, they had to cancel that show because there weren't enough ticket sales. They helped to exchange our tickets and we ended up at the table closest to the stage! It was a BLAST! The guys were gorgeous and entertaining. The show was funny, interactive, and a once in a lifetime experience for a girls weekend, birthday, or bachelorette party. The host and the servers were all incredible too!

After the show, Coyote Ugly is the bar right next door. I would highly recommend going there next! 

You and your friends HAVE to do this in Nashville!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This has always been one of my favorite venues on Broadway to see a few local Nashville bands. Probably a little pricey, but it is on Broadway, so that's to be expected.
Mostly good bands playing all day, and the sound guys do a decent job on the mix.
Another good stop on a Nashville trip down Broadway.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Ohh yeah, Best time ever. Looking forward to return visit!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: My all time favorite honky tonk. $8 cocktails with two shots of yumminess in each drink. It cannot be beat. The location is epic, the music is unbelievable, the waitresses are super nice. The cocktails are the best. I cannot stop thinking about how awesome my experience was.

name: Music City Male Revue
text: Was incredibly excited to see this show as my friend was in town visiting. We booked two VIP tickets for a Friday night show and received and email a few hours before the show informing us the event had been cancelled due to lack of tickets sold. We were told we would receive a 100% refund. I therefore booked for the following Saturday night and again a few hours before the show received a notification of cancellation and refund guarantee. I did not receive a refund for almost a month for the first show after continuously trying to contact the organizer. Then after a month I was emailed, and then ignored and have YET to be refunded for my second show which was over $100. Quite frankly this entire thing seems like a scam. Do not waste your money or your time.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I was there two nights ago and was on the top floor during last call. My friend and I purchased our final beverages and were rushed out of the top floor. No worries, we thought, let's just go down to the main floor. We come down the stairs to the security guards smoking weed in the staircase. I'm no cop so I didn't care, but they told us that we couldn't go into the main floor and that we would have to finish our drinks in the staircase and then we could get in line AGAIN outside to come back into the bar which was already closing.  I have a feeling they either wanted us to grease their pockets to get back in, or they were pissed we interrupted their smoking sesh.  I even mentioned hey man I don't care about the smoke or anything and he was like "it's CBD" lol ok buddy, I use cbd oil every day and as a California native with a valid medicinal marijuana card, I can tell the difference but nice try.   ended up having to pound my drink in a staircase reeking of piss to end my night because of these two douche bags, wouldn't go again. There are plenty of other venues nearby with better entertainment and less shady staff.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Unfriendly service and very unpleasant... sorry pick another place and you will enjoy more!

name: The Back Corner
text:
Nashville's lounge revolution continues. We've gotten Nashville's take on Brooklyn, LA and Vegas. the back corner is very Miami Beach. When I walked in I, immediately, thought of Haven (RIP https://www.yelp.com/biz/haven-miami-beach-2). From the LED wall to the music to the drinks to the vibe... I didn't feel like I was in Nashville anymore. the back corner stands out and gives Middle Tennesseans something that's not readily available in this area. If you're in the mood for a little coastal cosmopolitanness (is that word? It's not a word), the back corner is about to be your new favorite place.

The neighborhood gets things moving in the right direction. For as much as Germantown has (scenic streets, fancy high rises, coffee, good eats) it didn't have a nightlife destination. Putting one here makes a lot of sense. Building off the 5th & Taylor imprint, the back corner starts off fancy (but not pretentious) and builds to memorable. Upon entry, the first thing you notice is the LED wall and stage. With a changing display of electronic intoxication, you're drawn into a world far away from Lower Broad. If you can break your gaze away from the stage, you'll notice the upper and lower lounge seating. Intimate, cozy and a bit mysterious, the seating at the back corner lets you decide whether you want to be front & center or if you're rather sit back and take it all in. You can be as public or private as you'd like. If indoor seating isn't your thing, make your way outside to enjoy the fire pit and Germantown night sky. Just do us all a favor and refrain from smoking. Seeing cigarette butts along the patio or by (in??) the fire pit is not sexy and very off-brand.

All the above said and noted, the back corner is not a huge space -- which is a plus and minus. It's a plus because it never becomes the cavernous mess of bass and desperation. The minus is crowds gonna crowd and with a lot of people, the space will be tight. I don't know how to fix that. I suppose a velvet rope and waitlist will keep crowds at bay but neither feels very Nashville. Hmm... Another minus (relating to the size) is that there's only one bar. One bar in a space this cool is a bit tight. I know the space behind the bar isn't huge but I would staff it with 3 bartenders at a time so as to keep up with the crowd. Because you're going to want to drink. A lot. The cocktail program at the back corner is a bit unusual for Nashville -- and very Miami. Expect rum, colors and a boozy punch. Actually, the menu could use a punch. Get on that, tbc. Re drink progression... start with the gimlet. It's pretty to look at and refreshing to drink. All the mixers, juices, etc. are made in house so you're getting quality fare. From there, hit the No. 4 and, then, the No. 2. If you're still upright, drink some water. Water? Who am I kidding? Cocktails! You're in Miami, [redacted]! Well, sorta.

If you need some noshes, 5th & Taylor is serving up bites. Don't come here for dinner. Who eats food? Let the music and booze nourish your body. As perfect as the back corner is for DJ sets, live music (this *is* Nashville, after all) works as well. the back corner isn't the Downtown dance club people have wanted for a (looooong) while. But it is a welcome addition to the city's nightlife scene and, very possibly, you're new favorite place to go. Bienvenidos a Nashville.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Paid to attend their NYE event. Unfortunately the top floor flooded and we were not allowed in. We waited in line for over an hour and were told repeatedly they would get us in as soon as possible before they finally announced they were over capacity and no one else would be let in. I've called multiple times, written emails, and left Facebook reviews and messages and still have heard nothing back. I was promised a refund and they have completely avoided taking responsibly. Awful management/customer service.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Beautiful venue! Tons of concessions (despite hilarious $7 prices for water bottles, $15 "glasses" of wine, etc.) and clean, huge bathrooms. 
Tip - you can bring unsealed plastic bottles of water in. Lots of vendors outside charging $2. Do yourself a favor and grab a couple of those. Giant draft IPAs cheaper than Mich Ultra? IPA it is 

Parking - if you're lucky, there are free parallel spots downtown after 6pm, but of course not tons. $5 parking in the R lot across the pedestrian bridge, just need to walk over the bridge. Smaller lots near the venue $10-$50. 

No umbrellas allowed. Just read the rules first. Definitely did a pretty intense pat down and bag check so don't think you'll get away with sneaking something in. Saw them check someone's hair...  

Lawn area is spacious. Amazing views of Nashville. 
However, the lawn crowd every time I've been to Ascend has been awful. I've been to tons of outdoor venues like this and people are clapping along, paying attention, even dancing during the headliners! Went to two shows in the last week - had a visitor come just to see them. Lawn was just lots of bored people playing games on their phones in the lawn, not clapping, screaming at people who were up and dancing, carrying on loud conversations as if they were out at the park. It was so quiet for such a large venue, even the bands noticed... awkward. Jason Mraz, Cake and Ben Folds - not really your sit back in silence kind of bands. 

Basically, if you want the vibe of a symphony and are fine staying still and seated on your blanket, the lawn is your spot. If you're trying to dance, sing, enjoy a favorite band, you need to absolutely get pit standing tickets or seated tickets or you will be very disappointed. We ended up moving just so I could go stand on the sides of the venue with others who had my same thoughts to dance and sing along, so the crowd of loud talkers on their cell phones stopped flipping out about people dancing and having fun. Felt like a bad picnic of people watching people watch a concert. 

Also - very inconsistent sound. I thought the opener was set at a great volume, but was struggling to hear the headliners. I know there are sound rules for the city but please turn it up enough so people on the lawn can hear.

Will be back, but 100% in a seat or pit.

name: The Station Inn
text:
Nashville has a jewel with the Station Inn.  I have been there 3 times and each visit has been a treat.  I was there Saturday, Feb 21 and enjoyed Larry Cordle.  I took a friend and his daughter and we all had a GREAT time.  My friend bought 3 CDs for the night.

If the show starts at 9pm, I would get there around that time so you don't miss any great bluegrass music.  It's first come first serve as to seating and they have ATM outside to pay for the door.  They have a decent selection of beers and sodas.  Some nice snacks but we did not try their pizza or anything.  You can run a tab for your table and pay with credit card at the end.

My buddy summarized it as a great night to just listen to quality music and forget your worries.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Went there with a few peers from work. Downstairs was vibrant/loud but looked fun. We went upstairs so we could talk shop; have a sip and some
appetizers and enjoy some music. 
***I just reviewed my transactions on my card and realized I was charged twice for my order. Just be sure save review your receipt as they seem to have the going @honkytonk

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Let me tell you something-There are many choices on Broadway, but I feel that Honky Tonk Central was one of the best--I simply had a fun time!

It was a Thursday Night-standing room only-it is a large bar/club with enough room to dance!  There were two different bands playing and they were both very talented!  They had great crowd control and rocked the house!  

There was a nice age mixture in the bar and I made friends and we crawled to a few more bars together for the rest of the night!  

The drinks were a lil off--so I moved to bottled beer to keep myself happy!  

Note:  They do ask for ID - bonus-No cover!  The bands play for tips--so be generous!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
My wife and I caught Beth Hart on a Saturday night.  First...get there early.  We came in 2 hours before the show and still were about 150th in line.  Suppose it depends on the show.  Most main floor tables and balcony tables we full.  There was plenty of  space on the main floor to stand, but we were looking to sit for the night.  We grabbed two high top seats along  the bar on the right as you walk into the venue. Even with being 75-100 feet away the seats and sound was fine.

We split a  veggie quesadilla, chips and salsa, and fries.  The quesadilla was fresh and filling.  Beer was cold and readily available.

The staff at the bar was very busy, but still found the time to quickly check in wiht us often.   

Will definitely go to another show at 3rd and Lindsey when the opportunity arises.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: If I could give this place zero stars I would! My friend's and I were there and the bouncer started picking on this guy that was intoxicated. All he was doing was singing. Meanwhile all these drunk women were doing the SAME THING and he didn't throw them out. We followed them out and my friend asked "why are you throwing him out? He wasn't doing anything" and he said "why don't you stop being a B*TCH and go to another bar". Now call me crazy, but I don't think that was warranted. If this is how the bouncers treat the patrons, you're going to lose A LOT of business! PS- he was a younger guy with short brown hair and too afraid to give his name when asked, COWARD!

name: The Cowan
text: Great venue and even better location.  Tons of parking, easy to Uber here and they are supporting various genres.  Big room with a long bar. Good things coming for the music scene in that area with this bar. I had a great first experience, looking forward to going back.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Great Honky Tonk, we went on Thursday the 7th of nov 
The band was a really great band, I don't know their name but they were a family band from Nebraska???
They were a great band, The type of band that can play anything. Great bar -a lot of fun. Restroom was OK, There is an attendant which keeps it up a bit.

name: The Basement East
text: Came here tonight. The tap option was low but the drinks were good. Mainly beer not many "mixed drinks" options. The food menu was slim, but pretty yummy. If you don't go to eat a meal at least try the gauc. It was so fresh and delicious. It was reasonably and normal priced menu. The patio was nice and lots of seating.parking seemed limited but free.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Worst food ever! Ordered shrimp fritters and couldn't identify a single bit of shrimp me or even the flavor of such as n their shrimp and corn fritters. Waitress just shrugged her shoulders and said, "It is what it it is'.  The band was no better than a small town dive bar band....actually, probably not even as good.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I really like Whiskey Row when I do hit the Broadway bars! The multi-level space provides for a variety of "vibes" on your night out. From live music space, to a club-like room, even to the awesome rooftop, there's a space for everyone on your next honky-tonk bar crawl!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: The "hidden gem" of downtown Nashville! Great food, great music, and awesome upstairs patio!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: LOVED the drinks here and the music! It was a friendly spot to walk in with a decent cover, and my under-21 sister was able to come in as well, which was rare in Nashville at night.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This place was fairly busy for a Monday night however with keeping that in mind, the time it took to get our drinks was incredibly long.  Additionally the service was quite poor, rarely checked in on us and never brought requested hot sauce or other condiments out.  The music was good but the most disappointing thing was the food, an incredibly bland whiskey burger with dry jerky-like bacon topped on it and the fries that could've been microwaved for all I know.  My peers seemed to like the wings they got but based on my experience I would not go back.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Love this place. Great music, decent beer selection from local breweries, fantastic atmosphere

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Not from Nashville but this is what I thought Nashville was supposed to be.  Broadway is loud music and college bars.  This is real music.  Food is great and service is fantastic.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Good little museum but we do feel it is over-priced. They had some great memorabilia, clothing, hand-written letters from Cash and history about his acting career and timeline of his music career. Bathrooms were clean and it was nice and cool inside on a very hot summer day! Gift shop is very over-priced.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Had such a great time and the band was awesome   But after tipping the band to play the next song and paying our check, the bouncer decides to tell us to leave. Smirk and all.. Sorry this review would have been 5 stars but the bouncer deserves nothing. No respect and will not be back.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: AWESOME. If you are visiting Nashville you have to check this museum out. It's well worth the money, and in my opinion is much more interesting than the Country Music Hall of Fame. My only regret is not buying something in the gift shop, but there was so much to choose from I couldn't decide!

name: 360 Burger
text:
Every time I've visited, my experience has been different (good, for the most part). I like that their mixed drinks are reasonably priced; if you want your money's worth, get their namesake. The menu changed a bit recently when the owners changed. I don't really notice any other differences, but the waiter I had mentioned how much better things were. The service seems better and more attentive. 

Burgers have been good if not terribly unique. Sweet potato fries need batter or seasoning. I'm still not decided on the pretzel bun being used for everything. This being Nashville, one of their draws is live music. I haven't heard anything bad yet, but it can get a bit loud. 

Overall, this is a place that you don't really expect to be in Antioch.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
I love the Nashville Big Bang--music is always great (play by requests), and they will play anything so there is usually a good variety. There were a combination of 5-6 musicians that filtered on and off the stage in different combinations.

Big Bang is always interactive and this location is no exception. Great place to swing by for some shots (must get the obnoxious light-up shot glass). 

I will say it is harder to find than most bars on Broadway because it is upstairs.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
Walking down Broadway in Nashville this is a place you could easily walk by and never know it was there. Just a doorway leading up to the second floor venue.
Big Bang is a great name because you get a lot of bang for your buck. 
If you don't know how Dueling Piano bars work, You write down a song on a piece of paper and give it (with a few bucks) to one of the pianists and they play your song.
These guys are talented! They also from time to time have accompaniment from a drummer or guitar player. 
This is now by far my favorite place on the Nashville strip.
Waiters and waitresses also sing and dance in between taking drink orders (they do a great job at both) 
Sadly they weren't open on Sunday (even they have to rest) but if you are in Nashville you need to check it out.

Cover is just $6 after 8:30pm, drinks are well poured and fairly priced.

Get there early for a good seat!!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: I frequent swinging door monthly...but I believe last night was the last.  Spent $40+ on alcohol and food. I then went back to the bar to grab a couple waters...they refused to pour me a water that wasn't a $3 bottle.  I realize SD has the right to not serve a drink but that is so ridiculous!  We left and went to Barlines in the Omni.  They gladly gave me waters and laughed that swinging door acting like that!

name: 360 Burger
text: Great burgers and wonderful selection of beer! Also on Friday and Saturday nights they have live music and the bands that I have seen there are top notch!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Wow, lived here all these years,  family came in to town and invited us here. What an awesome place. Great music at a great price, extremely genuine Nashville treasure. Food was better then our Broadway adventures. Free valet parking was super convenient. For $12 bucks a person, $5-6 beers, great deal.

name: 360 Burger
text: Had my hubby bring home chicken sliders...should have probably went with the hamburger sliders. More bread than anything. Definitely wouldn't order this again. Sweet potato fries were just okay; I've had better.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
I've been wanting to check this place out for a long time.  When our songwriter friend Simon was scheduled to perform I wasn't going to miss it for anything.  You can purchase tickets at the door but I wasn't taking any chances so I ordered them ahead of time.  It was a good thing I did because they sold out.  There was a long line of people waiting to get in and others on a wait list in case people with tickets didn't show.  Performing songwriters included Simon Reid, Sister C, and Michael Ray.  The songs told a story.  It was a fabulous show.

Seating seems to be first come first serve.  After standing in line, you make your way up to the counter where you give them your name and a hostess seats you.  If you want to sit with your friends then you should purchase your tickets together and make sure you get there at the same time.  The service was great!

I started with "The Show Cabernet" as I looked over the menu.  The couple sitting at the table with us had been there before and recommended the Country Fried Chicken so that's what I ordered.  It came with red skinned mashed potatoes and green beans.  The food portions were huge so I ate half and took the other half for lunch the next day.  The food was good and the wine was great.  We will have to make a return visit before long.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Just awesome! Very entertaining and the staff was very attentive and helpful. They really looked out for me as I was by myself. Get there early for a good seat.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: An excellent place to visit. However I think there needs to be more " listening stations" 1  headset and up to 4 songs/videos per decade was very frustrating. We were there on a quiet day,one could only imagine what would happen if a bus tour arrived. Parking close by is  expensive, we found a parking metered space that had no time limit and cost $1.50 per hour, far cheaper than the private parking charges.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This place is terrible could not be worse. Giant lines. Terrible service. Have to wait in line forever to do anything. DO NOT COME HERE

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great place for food and seeing the best local talent. The nice twist here is you can actually hear the performers.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: One of the most amzing collections of anyone's personal life let alone the life of an icon like Johnny Cash.  I think some of the more negative reviewers missed the mark on this place.  Going through and reading about his life and career with all the included memorabilia and personal memories of his life was, to me, like being able to go theough his personal effects.  They allow as many pictures as you want but I felt uncomfortable taking pictures of his personal things there.  It is an amazing collection cataloging the life of a great man and musician and must see if you're near enough to it.

name: 360 Burger
text:
I absolutely love this place!! We started coming here after craving good burgers in June 2013. Ever since then, this place has been a weekly stop for our family and friends. I love every burger on the menu! And I have never been to a burger place that hits how you want your meat cooked right on the nose!
Enjoy live music, this place has it! The service is always great and pleasant. I usually come in with big groups and the servers are more than happy to serve an accommodate! Two of my favorite servers are Tod and  Matt.
Food options are great! I love the pretzel bun, but you can get a regular bun too! Sweet potato fries are da bomb!!! And if you are still hungry after you mama Jana burger, their brownie with ice cream is divine! 
Check out 360 burger!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Best live music in Nashville!!! No, seriously, original artists; heartfelt and soulful, talented artists. I wish our stay could have been longer. Loved loved loved...

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I'm super cheap and was not thrilled when my guests wanted to go to this museum. $20 was certainly more than I wanted to spend for Johnny Cash, and I was annoyed to hear that the Patsy Cline exhibit was a separate charge. (Spoiler alert: I probably would have given this 5 stars if admission was $5-10 cheaper)

I was pleasantly surprised by the exhibit. There are a lot of videos, artifacts, and interesting things to read. And there were several interactive activities that I was impressed by, including one in which you could re-mix one of his songs. The museum held my attention, though I'm not a Johnny Cash fan.

Again, my main complaint was the cost (though that complaint applies to most of the tourist traps). They advertised a "green screen" where you could "get you picture taken with Johnny." I was not pleased to hear you had to pay for this - $20 for one picture! I will say, however, that they edited the photos nicely so it really does look like he's in the picture. My cousin was very pleased to buy it.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Wanting to do a "tourist day" in our own town, my wife and I decided to visit the Johnny Cash Museum on a Saturday. We loved it! It has a ton of Cash artifacts and displays that detail his music, the eras he lived and sang through, and the people he touched. There are some interactive stations where you can experiment with sound mixing, plenty of music stations where you can listen to different recordings of Cash and his close contemporaries, and clothing and musical instruments that the man wore and played on tour. Our personal favorites were the things from Cash's personal home (including his grandfather's piano that was his most prized personal possession) and all the June-Johnny love artifacts (there's even a poem he wrote the day of June's funeral). 

Negatives: The only beef that we had with the tour was that the entrance to the tour was extremely crowded. It loosened up after the first hall but it was initially kind of overwhelming. Hopefully at some point they can extend or build onto the building, which would help with overcrowding. 

Rebuttals to some other criticisms I noticed in other reviews:

1. The Cash Museum has nothing to do with parking prices in downtown Nashville. Credit high crime rates, white flight, and the expansion of the suburbs in the 1950s-70s which made it possible to have a ton of cheap parking in downtown Nashville in years past, but those days are long gone. Its not the museum's fault if parking lots of being turned into high-rise office and condo space. Like any other city, its expensive to park. Either learn to parallel park (free on weekends), or ride the bus. Its $1.70 for a bus ride and they all lead to the downtown terminal.

2. The price of admission is honestly not that bad. $16-18 is pretty typical for museums. If you're a Johnny Cash fan, its worth it. 

3. I saw a lot of complaints about prices in the gift shop. Are y'all new to museums or something? When has a museum gift shop ever had bargain-bin prices?

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: I would give this experience 2.5 stars if I could, because of the two hour trip, I hated the first hour and loved the second. The first hour you're herded into the main boat ball room, which is kept at a breezy -10 degrees, and proceed to put on the most cheesy and staged show I've ever seen outside of Gatlinburg. It's a shame, because it's definitely a talented cast. The highlight of this hour was when the two very pretty singers pulled up a grandfather, sang a creepy Grandpa song to him, and asked if they could be his granddaughters too. He very clearly stated, "No, but you can be my girlfriends. Well, kind of clearly. There was a drunken slur happening there (bottomless mimosas for $14!) They were completely thrown and off script for like 30 whole seconds. His wife was less amused. The food is unremarkable. For the second hour, they let you actually go outside and have normal, real human musicians playing and an out door bar set up. I give the first hour 1 star and 5 to the second.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: I will be going to this bar for the second time in a row on my trip to Nashville. Excellent service by the bartenders and delicious affordable drinks in fun serving cups that they allow you to take home as souvenirs. Hilarious entertainment and fun. The artists are incredibly talented that I almost wanted to sign them to a record label. The Big Bang honors old time rock n roll and makes you remember the good times, while getting a nice buzz with friends!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
I'm a longtime fan of The Listening Room. It has gone through many iterations. My only comment intended to be helpful to the ownership, is that you really need to work on your menu and finesse. I've had mostly not-so-good experiences with food there. I will keep going back and back because I love the place so much, and the great support it offers the writing community. So I would highly encourage everyone to attend shows as they are the best in town, but don't have high expectations for the food yet. Cut them slack as they figure it out and let the food catch up with the outstanding venue. Be supportive of them as they are really trying, I'm sure. Best part of the place is the valet parking! Two thumbs up!

Part Two follow up...I only made those comments to be constructive. There are some very good things on your menu, but I think you can top others. You have one of the best music venues in town both for seasoned pros to the tourists. Keep up the good work!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: This is a no-cover dueling pianos bar on the main strip in downtown Nashville. It has a fairly large seating area and a separate bar, with a small spot open for people to dance. The acts were very energetic and some were quite talented with playing piano and drums, and also being able to improvise. There was a college age heavy crowd though I saw a few other groups with people in the late 40s range. Drinks were meh and about $6 each, service was friendly but they did not have enough staff to keep each group properly served. The poor girl was running around as fast as she could but she had too many tables to keep up with. The music selection was mainly pop, with a little bit of country mixed in. You could request songs (along with a tip) and the higher the tip the more likely your song would be played (if they knew it). We had a decent time and would consider returning, but with so many music places available it would probably be a long time before we find ourselves back there.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: The service and people here were awesome! Our bartender was the best! We returned for another afternoon of fun.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
This place is awesome. If you're looking for a chill place off Broadway and interested in great talent and original live music this is the place.  We just saw Gina Vernier, Jeffrey East and Summer Overstreet. Phenomenal singer songwriters with distinctive styles. You'll be inspired to support up and coming artists.

Drinks were great, food was okay. I ordered the pulled pork, which was very dry without a lot of flavor, but that didn't prevent me from giving the highest rating to this place. 

A must for first-time travellers to Nashville.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Wow this place is a hidden gem! Didn't get any food, but great entertainment and wait staff. Man these musicians are talented.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Great self guided tour, full of so many interesting stories and facts. I wasn't sure if I would like it but I would definitely go again!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I have learned a lot about The Man in Black. I think they did a great job showcasing Johnny Cash life. It was worth the price I paid, but way not get it cheaper. Check Groupon before you go.  If nothing is there they have AAA discount for dollar off.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
We were in Nashville for a whirlwind 48 hours to see a show at the Ryman, so the next morning, we had a bit of time to kill before we headed back to the airport, and I came across the Johnny Cash Museum on Yelp... and well, we just had to go. 

We were staying downtown, so after lunch at Puckett's, we walked on down. You enter into a little gift shop, then at the register you see the admission for the museum. I think it was $14 bucks per person.... then you walk on back. 

I was amazed to see the variety of things in here... from Cash's school report cards, to Morse code manuals he used in the army, to stage outfits, of course all of the records, but some really nice and awesome hand written set list, lyrics and notes to be viewed as well. It is small back there, but there is a TON of great stuffed packed in. 

They have ipad audio stands that you can put on some headphones and listen to Johnny's songs in each decade. His cover of NIN Hurt plays in the background and it never fails to make me shed a few tears. Also very cool, a station where you can listen to Get Rhythm on 33, 78, cassette, CD and MP3 formats, to hear the difference between each one. (Now to go and finally get that replacement needle for our record player!) 

Super intimate feel, so much so that I also shed a few tears after reading a few love letters penned to June... 

A MUST for any Johnny Cash fan.

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: I went to this place because I was told they have live music for late night options. The music was great! I ordered wings and after about 20 minutes I asked where they were and asked if I could just get my money back. At this point I was "reprimanded" by the bar tender and the manager. I was asked to leave as the manager literally threw the wings in a to-go box. The man anger made a scene and told me "I should leave"... It was literally the worst experience I have had in a bar. I felt like a complete idiot.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Wonderful museum filled with lots of memorabilia. Great place for any Johnny Cash fan to visit!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Stopped here on a Tuesday afternoon during 4th of July week. It was a pretty full crowd and the band that was playing was amazing, probably our favorite of the week. Our waitress was very nice and frequented our table and made sure we were taken care of. The place was very clean and nice. Unfortunately it gets really busy later at night and we never got a chance to return. We would recommend it, we had a great time. If anyone knows the band in my photo please let me know we would like to follow them on YouTube or any other social media. Thanks in advance!

name: 360 Burger
text: Great burger place with live music during the evenings.  Had the PB&J burger which was terrific and a craft beer.  Highly recommend.

name: 360 Burger
text: Surprisingly delicious. If you don't mind country music - I'm serious - they serve great burgers and generously-portioned sides. Try the Smoked burger minus BBQ sauce. I'll be back for more

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: My rating is for the Saturday brunch.  The items included: fried potato, scrambled eggs, French toast, bacon, sausage patties, and biscuits.  There were also some fresh vegetables and fruits and yogurt.  Food tasted fair, seating is plentiful and atmosphere is excellent, with great music.  Service is slow and friendly.  Really just wasn't worth $18.  If price was $10, may be a three star.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Meh, I'd skip this place for brunch.  Live music doesn't start until 12 (which is really why we came here).  Food was just ok.  Nothing special.  Ordered shrimp and grits.  Shrimp lukewarm and shredded cheese on grits not even melted.  Lobster bisque was terrible.  For the price, I'd head to Southern Steak and Oyster for brunch.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
We just went there on August 12 and we were surprised there were a lot of people there (to the point that no one was motioning the number of people in or out - could be a fire hazard) .  But on the other hand when you walk in there are many different kinds of t-shirts and gifts in their store.  General admission is $18.00 per person.  
    So much memorabilia it's unbelievable.  The exhibits start out with Johnny Cashs' childhood and his military service in the Air Force.  As you walk through the museum you can hear his music and see different documentaries on his prison performances and clips from his TV shows.  There are walls with all of his gold and platinum records, a history of his musical career, all of his 45 singles that he sold, all of his album covers, his 8 track tapes, and cassettes.

name: Silver Dollar Saloon
text: On a long, all girls weekend in Nashville...the Silver Dollar Saloon is where we had the most fun! If its a Friday or Saturday night you can really only deal with the Broadway crowds, lines, and prices for so long so we found ourselves stumbling down 2nd street this way. There was an awesome band, LOTS of dancing, and the crowd was just right - not body to body but pleasantly busy. I didn't have a hard time getting to the bathrooms or ordering a drink, we even got to stay after hours and chat it up with the band because they weren't hustling us out of there rudely. I had a great time and recommend it if you want to try something besides the main 5[ish] on Broadway. Enjoy :)

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Not a big fan but fell in love with the musuem.  The displays were very interesting and i found myself reading every single page of the man's life history. we were rushing to the airport to pick up someone so had to hurry through and got to see only half the museum. Despite that, i'm still glad we visited!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: This place is everything that tourists love and locals make fun of.  Amazing musicians, all of whom are multi instrumentalists, singers, and killer entertainers.  Is it filled with bachelorette parties, packed on weekends, loud, obnoxious, and filled with out of towners?  Yup.  That's what makes it a really amazing time.  Try it out, bring all your friend stuff and get sloppy.

name: 360 Burger
text: My wife an I had lunch here. The burgers were awesome! Very well seasoned and cooked at the right temp. Even the fries were crispy and hot! Very well portion. Only down side was the price.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Great pace to visit when in Nashville! It's a must to have on your list! Great entertainment and they even include the audience! It and experiments you won't get anywhere else!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: We were excited to stop by here, my sons first pick to do on our trip. Tons of cool memorabilia through the years and sample music to listen to in different recording types through the years. Lotsa history in here on Johnny Cash and the gift shop had a great variety of cool stuff to purchase! Staff friendly and helpful. A must see in Nashville!

name: 360 Burger
text: This place is fantastic. Great burgers. Local music that's gets to the soul of Nashville rather than the stereotype.service is up to par. If your near a ouch it's the best one here. If your driving through Nashville on the 24 its worth the stop.

name: 360 Burger
text: The atmospere was great. You could really tell the meat was organic and grass fed. We were here on singer/songwriter night, good music. The service and envirorment were comfortable and inviting. I really hope that this local resteraunt expands and goes places. P.s. Prices are very reasonable.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: This is probably the biggest waste of money for food in Nashville. I ordered the chilli and fries and the chilli was cold and the fries were lukewarm. The menu has 6 food items, one dessert, and about 40 different beverages. Also there is a $15 spending limit so if you get no beverages you have to buy 3/6 items on the menu. The music is great usually but the service is terrible. Seriously Wendy's chilli taste better than what I ate tonight.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Stumbled upon this gem of a museum while strolling Broadway.  Had the wonderful opportunity to visit just prior to leaving town.  The staff were genuinely friendly and a pleasure to be around.  The museum covers the entire life of Johnny Cash with great exhibits.  Can't wait till our next visit to Nashville to visit again.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: I am in love with this place mad Angela and Donny Lee rock OMG !!! I am HOME!! Great music, epic location and good food and a fantastic time!! I can't wait to come back next year!!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I do love me some Johnny Cash. 
Some tips: go early or on off days. This place can get really crowded and that takes away from the museum. 
It's small and has no re entry. So make sure you see everything you want to before leaving. 
Listen to the music and watch the footage they have. It's pretty interesting. 

That being said I wish that they either picked a larger venue and gave people more room or allowed for you to come in and out over the weekend to see it with less people.  It is also a little spendy for what you're getting. But when in Nashville.....

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I hate to say negative things about a place many people seem to have enjoyed it. I don't think this museum is worth $22, especially when there are better attractions in the area for the same or less money. 

I like Johnny Cash and some of his music but you'd have to be a die-hard fan to enjoy this. Kids will be bored. 

Since i wasted my time and money here, I didn't get to spend much time in the Tennessee State Museum but the little that I saw was much more interesting and fun and free. I heard it has a music exhibit.

Cons:
1. $22 admission! --does not include Patsy Cline Museum!

2.
