Approximately 6 rooms total. 3 of those are just long hallways with memorabilia (costumes, photos, records, letters) up on the wall. 1 room is a looped video about his TV/movie appearances. 1 is just a loop of him making a speech about the American flag. The best room actually has some kiosks where you can listen to the music. 

3. Not that reading a lot of information is bad, but there is A LOT required to obtain the information. Long block paragraphs next to the exhibits. You'd have to stand at each item and read about it to even understand its significance. 

4.Very crowded-- made it difficult to read the information.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Well it's a fun environment the drinks are very expensive and there's limited seating. It's worth stopping by to check it out but I wouldn't write home to mom about it

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We went here 2 nights in a row . Very good talent it seems is always here . Had a large crowd both times. Bartenders were attentive in helping each new person going towards the bar for drinks . We went walking to a few other spots but always would end up back here . Playing country , some rock on request and others. Great place to check out in downtown Nashville

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
While I'm not a huge country music fan, I do like history, and JC (Johnny Cash, not Jesus Christ) is certainly a big part of history - much moreso than I suspected before I entered.

If you have a AAA card, you save a buck off the $15 fee; kids tix are $11 each.

It's not terribly big, but man do they pack a LOT in a small space. Lots of artifacts and very good explanations to go with each. 

You enter and leave through the museum store, which has everything from soap to shirts. We didn't get anything but go ahead and look around.

If I could, It'd give it 3 1/2 stars.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Went on a Monday evening with another, pleasantly surprised by the quality of the song suffragettes singers. I once hear that in Nashville, you could hear star quality musicians at the local bars and listening rooms. You still can, and I plan on returning to Nashville regularly to listen.

For out of staters, there's something like a 15% alcohol tax on top of the regular taxes. Made a nice dent in my wallet, but at least it supports the area.

name: 360 Burger
text: I have been now 4 times to 360 Burger, 3 times dining in, and 1 time picking up a carry out call in order. Every time i have been the service has been great, and the FOOD is AMAZING! The pretzel bun keeps me coming back as well, and the spinach as a side :-) The Sante Fe and Cilantro/Avocado Burger, the only 2 burgers i will ever need to order ;-) keep up the good work guys and gals....i will be back again soon!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Not a single Johnny Cash Museum shirt other than a few random ones on a discontinued rack. The staff was very short with us and rude when we asked if they had more. Displays and exhibits are great though. Still overall a bit of a disappointment.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
A staff that we clearly inconvenienced by coming in to dine and drink. The two waitresses walked past our table and the table behind us four times over a 15 min period and each time they turned their backs in order not to make eye contact to take our order. I get treated better at the Waffle House. Left there and enjoyed a great meal and music at The George Jones.

Management did reach out and stated they would address issues.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Very cool place! Has all kinds of Johnny cash memorabilia, from his guitars and platinum albums down to his bible. If you are in Nashville it's worth a stop!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: If you want to waste your hard earned money on a business that has zero regard for human life then waste your money here. My husband and I came into town to visit friends and decided to visit the museum. We are huge Johnny cash fans. We entered to a very busy room as it was rainy outside. I do not recommend coming on a rainy Day. We waited in line for a while before we actually stepped foot into the actual museum but shortly after we stepped in, my 9 week old started crying really hard. Of course my natural response was to turn around and leave. The rude lady taking tickets yelled at me and told me I couldn't leave that way because of 'fire code.' It made no sense whatsoever. So instead she told me I needed to make my way through the crowded museum with my husband and our baby stroller. It was a nightmare. I walked along slowly apologizing to the hundreds of customers about my sick baby crying. I ended up leaving with the baby and my husband walked through the museum as quickly as possible with the stroller since they wouldn't let him leave through the entrance either. My husband asked if we could re-enter so I could at least see the museum (since we paid 20 dollars per person and 22 for parking) and they rudely told him 'not a chance.' So I went back inside to ask for a refund and before I could even open my mouth the guy at the front desk said 'no way.' I told him I realize we can't re-enter but I would like a refund. He said we will not refund you no matter what. I asked for the manager who eventually reluctantly gave me a refund. When I told her about being treated rudely by the associate at the entrance she not once apologized, she responded with 'oh.' Nashville is a touristy town and you would think customer service was important. Not at the Johnny Cash museum...I'm said to say we will not be returning. We had wanted to visit that museum for years but I'm sad to say we will never go back.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: I went to the boat with my husband last weekend to break up our "dinner and a movie" date routine and enjoyed it for the most part. The boat makes its way from Opryland to downtown Nashville and provides a great backdrop for pictures. The entertainment was good; the music wasn't necessarily what I would listen to but I appreciated the talent of the performers. The food was okay- think tough, reheated frozen dinner rolls and pretty dry roast beef. The cheesecake with cherries and chocolate sauce at the end redeemed the meal somewhat. The service wasn't so great, seeing as the only time I got a water refill was once about halfway through the meal when I called our waiter over and asked for one. They get three stars because of the entertainment and the scenic route. If I had it to do over again, I wouldn't get the $90 dinner ticket- I would buy a ticket for the cruise only and eat dinner beforehand.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Absolutely love this place. They show such respect to songwriters and provide an awesome atmosphere and quality sound. They also select talented artists; surely some greats will have their start at the Listening Room!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: If you're looking for a fun night out Whiskey Row is the place to be! Not only is the music a great variety, the atmosphere is very lively! If you're looking for exceptional drink service look no future than BILL BUTLER he knows what he is doing moving at a very quick speed while also making a quality drink! Highly recommend this place.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
I'm surprised by the bad reviews! We loved this place! It's a little bit more upscale than your typical Broadway honkey tonk, and the food is fabulous. I went out on a limb and got the kale and quinoa salad.. OMG!! So good. Like, please share the salad dressing recipe  

Also, ladies anything and everything you could need for a night out is supplied in the ladies room. Hair spray, deodorant, Tylenol, etc. I thought that was a nice touch. 

Overall, for a Broadway honkey tonk, it's a 5 in my book. Thanks, Dierks and staff!

name: The Basement East
text: Easy parking. Easy entry. Easy access to bars and restroom. Acoustics were great even in sold out crowd.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: The worst place in Nashville. Boyfriend and I went here for New Years 2015. We put our drinks on a table and Nick (the boss) told us to take them off. Which we did but Nick (very short manager) looked at my boyfriend and like he was going to hit him and we asked the manager what is wrong we moved the drinks and the manager Nick said your boyfriend is giving me an attitude. My boyfriend didn't say a word to this man but ok we will move our drinks. The boss kicked us out. The boss wouldn't even listen to me. If you are a manager of customer service industry wouldn't it be smart to treat your customers well? I would never treat a couple this poorly. Nick is the worst manager I have ever seen. I told everyone on the bus back to the hotel. I told them to never go there and spend your money across the street at Honky Tonk where they treat there customers with respect and understanding.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Great find!  Even people not super fans would get something out of this.  Lots of content and memorabilia.  Lots of interactive listening.  Certainly worth the money to visit!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: This was a different experience for us but we really enjoyed it.  Once we arrived, the staff welcomed us aboard and were we surprised.  They had a lunch buffet that was great and a musical show that was awesome.  It was "Country" and anyone could enjoy the music and we enjoyed the musician talent and music while on the showboat.  One significant part of the trip while riding up and down the Cumberland River was you can go outside and see it while riding.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: My friends and I did a tour at the Grand Ole Opry and decided to take advantage of a groupon for Madame Tussaud's Nashville museum which is located in the mall just walking distance from the Grand Ole Opry.  In my opinion, it's well worth it.  We had a lot of fun seeing "wax" figures of country stars, rock stars, country legends, blues legends, movie stars, and some pop stars.  There are some that are freaky just how much they look real (the Jimi Hendrix is great!).  Maybe a couple that are a bit iffy (*cough* Justin Timberlake).  But either way it's fun and relatively cheap attraction and it's impressive how long it is.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Music was great. Cool looking bar. Service was pretty bad. Took forever. After our first round and an appetizer the check was already on the table. Got a second round, she did the same thing. Like just tell us you have been cut and we would have cashed out. Do not like feeling like I'm being kicked out after dropping a $100. Drinks are way overpriced for what you get. Ended up staying because of a terrible rain storm. NO, Zero mention anywhere of a $3 service fee to pay with credit. Got to pay that twice. You can go here for decent eats. A little google search will steer you to better food. But there are plenty of places on music row with better drink prices, staff, and the exact same music.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Beware the hidden charges.  Stopped in for a drink and some music on a Saturday night.  Paid $6pp cover which is fine but what really annoys me is that I noticed the tax on the computer printed bill was 24%!  I questioned the waiter, he went to speak with someone, came back and told me it was correct, stating that there's no state income tax in TN so they have very high sales tax.  It sounded crazy, but I didn't argue.   Today at brunch I realized the tax rate is 9%.  So they have programmed into their computer an extra 15% for no reason.  We were a party of 3, so it wasn't an automatic tip, and it was all on the tax line.  I guess most people are too drunk to notice, but I want to call them out on it.  It's just wrong and I added extra tip.  If it hadn't been for this, I'd give a higher rating.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: great food and service!! I love the high rooftop bar. I would recommend getting here early because it can get busy at night.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
I went to Kid Rock's new restaurant Thursday night with an out of town crew from work.  It was a disappointment.  I ordered the NY Strip medium rare, but it was a tough cut and overcooked closer to well done than medium.  Not worth the price.  The onion rings were soggy.  Our waitress was attentive, and the music wasn't too bad, which is why I'm giving it two stars.

Overall the ambiance felt like Jason Aldean's or Blake Shelton's new joints.  Slick, sterile, and uninteresting.  It's a shame to see authentic Nashville turn into corporate main street.  Kid Rock should have stayed in Detroit with his signature rock-rap sound, and left the country-western honky-tonk scene to the locals.

Sad.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: The gift shop at the Nashville location has the rudest and most unfriendly service personnel I have ever encountered. I entered the gift shop just to look around at the souvenirs, and was promptly followed about by a sales person that not only never cracked a smile, but didn't even utter a single word. Perhaps future training of employees should include instructions on how to communicate with potential cash paying customers, or better yet how to have basic good manners.  Since when did sales people Forget how to make a "friendly " sale? Needless to say I walked out of the store empty-handed and disappointed at the state of affairs today.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: This venue is fun, but I would probably not stay for more than an hour next time. It is important to get here early as seats/tables fill up quickly. The artists who played were entertaining and very good, however, the staff (specifically at the bar) was not very friendly. We had a party of around six individuals who casually hung out at the bar and watched the entertainment, however, each time we ordered drinks it felt like we were an inconvenience.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: This 5 start review is def not for the food bc it would be around a 2 if i were rating the food (salmon was burnt and burger was plain). But the show was amazing. Best thing we did during our 3 day visit to Nashville! A Must do if your visiting.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Lovely showboat tour.  We love the cocktail time on the decks before dinner.  It was tranquil while the boat was moving towards downtown. Dinner was fine. After dinner we all came out on the decks and watch Nashville downtown. Beautiful skyline and city lights.  It doesn't hurt that the weather was great. Later we went back inside to watch the show.  The performers did not disappoint ... great music.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I loved it, I wish the prices were not so high to get a picture with the gorgeous man in black but this is a tourist trap so....overall go check it out, it was so much fun!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
This was such a disappointment, and total waste of a cover charge.  Upon entering you have to walk up a bunch of stairs.  If you could see the inside from the outside, you wouldn't bother.  It's dark, barely any walking room, no dance floor, and we only saw one waitress.  The song they sing for a woman's birthday is completely vulgar.  I'll never go back.
I was really excited about going.  The dueling piano bar in NOLA was one of my favorite memories.  The one in Nashville is just....bad.  Don't waste your money.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: The restroom on 3rd floor was clean but, no, toilet paper. Food was okay. Service was not great.

name: The Basement East
text: Great establishment and did a great job with the Geddy Lee book signing and Q&A.   Huge crowd, lots of us crazy Rush fans lined up early for a chance to be up close and personal with the Big Beautiful Book of Bass author Geddy and get a signed copy.  The staff is awesome with crowd management - getting everyone in quickly, managing the crowd inside and organizing a great event.  I'm sure it's just a good on a music night, but here on a Sunday evening for a author's Q&A and signing, they did a great job and made everyone feel welcomed and comfortable!  Thanks for a fun night!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great bar atmosphere with decent music. Packed on a Memorial Day Monday and fun for it. Cold Yuenglings and tasty, junky fries with chicken bbq & ranch.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Had great expectations for this place walking in. Great venue!! Music and artists were great. The place was full. Service was the worst we've experienced in Nashville. Wait staff took forever to take our drink orders and when we asked for the menus when we sat down, we still never received them so we asked to borrow some menus from the table next to us. We were at the 8:30 show "The Movement", which included two sets of an hour each. We ordered our food as the first set was starting. During the changing of sets, we asked the waitress about our food. She said the kitchen was really backed up. She came back 5 min later and said she moved our food to "the front". When it came out, the burger we ordered was a chicken sandwich. After sending it back, a cold burger returned, but they forgot the mac n cheese. When it came out, it was still hot. Very poor dining experience. I have high hopes the management staff takes some leadership and turns the kitchen and wait staff around. There may be too many offerings given the number of people sitting down all at once to eat.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: While away on a girls trip we spent an evening here! The entertainment was really great and the musicians shared the stage, while taking turns singing and playing songs. They talked and told stories and the evening was very cool. There are lots of bar drink options and typical bar food as well.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: It was AWFUL. The bouncers took our REAL ID's. They would let us speak to the police or anything. I guess we have no way to get home, because they dropped them down a sewer grate. Wouldn't recommend if you're 21-23. F this place. They'll be hearing from us soon!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This has the potential for greatness!  However, there is so much stuff crammed into a small area.  Add a crowd of people and it's unbearable.  A bigger venue is desperately needed to fully honor a great musician.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: This place is awesome! Has great bands all the time and has a rocking great vibe! Highly recommend checking out.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: If you are a Johnny Cash fans, this place will be great. All else, meh. They had almost every piece of memorabilia from Mr. Cash you could imagine in a well laid out order. However, there were WICKED crowds going thru EVERYTHING. I have never seen that many people read the cards of almost every artifact. Combined with a very small (let's say too small) spot made it very tough to get a good feel for things. I thought there was more, but must have missed it. Not a second floor like I imagined. Not worth it unless you are a huge fan.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
I will not be returning to this location ever again. I had high expectations of this place but unfortunately was a complete letdown.
First off my girlfriend's work friend was having a birthday on the 2nd floor and had a table reserved.. 

Some context is I did not know her work friends last name. 

Well after standing in a 30min line outside I find out I have to stand in another line to get up stairs
As I wait for the stairs I notice people going up without standing in line 
So I ask the door attendant "hey, if people have a table can we skip the line" 
He says "sure what is the name" so I give her first name
This asshole literally looks at me laughs and says "ya... you must know her really well" and wouldn't let me through at all

So I missed most of her birthday from the waiting I didn't even need to do because of this jackass...

I will NEVER return here and I do NOT recommend it 

It's hotter than Hades there. The security is obviously doing their job very well 
Considering my girlfriend telling me she was able to just go up the stairs without giving a name or showing ID to get in so I guess this place is sexiest too 

Well it's Welcome to Nashville once again

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
We had so much fun here on our first night in Nashville, that we decided to come back for a second night!

Definitely purchase your tickets online ahead of time. Seats are assigned as you walk in the door, so show up early to check-in and get the best seats. We found that the tall bar-top tables in the back had the best acoustics and best service (those tables are tended by the bartenders who are much closer and able to check in more frequently).

The $15 food/drink minimum per person was easily met with a few drinks each. We tried the nachos on the first night, which were just OK. The food was nothing to write home about.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: We all thoroughly enjoyed our evening here. The entertainment was awesome. I wasn't crazy wild about the meal. It was fun to try fried brussel sprouts but when paired with the brisket and french fries it was just too much grease. There is a wider menu so don't let that deter you from trying it.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Quick review: For anyone visiting Nashville and looking for a fantastic live music experience, Listening Room Cafe should be on your list! Similar to Bluebird Cafe but much easier to get tickets, very inexpensive, lovely interior and outstanding on-stage talent.

Details :

Note - My review is strictly for the music and ambience! I did not sample any of the food.

Before my first trip to the Music City, I received several recommendations to attend an "In the Round" event. Basically, a show where the best up and coming songwriters get a chance to showcase their talent. I had initially tried to get tickets for the famous Bluebird Cafe, but was too slow on the draw so I discovered Listening Room Cafe instead.

My boyfriend and I purchased tickets for the St. Patrick's Day show - $5 each. I ordered them quickly and easily online for a grand total of $13.29 at checkout (with the service fee). So reasonable!

We watched Smithfield, Adam Wood, Casey Derhak and Jesse Lee perform, and it was absolutely incredible! The audience is asked to maintain a low level of noise, which is much appreciated because you want to soak in every second of the talent on-stage. Once the show ended, I could hardly believe that almost 3 hours had passed.

We arrived about 15 minutes early to get a good table. They seat you based on your arrival, filling in the tables from front to back. The wait staff is super attentive and discreet during the show (for the most part). 

Definitely give Listening Room Cafe a visit! Fun fact, Jesse Lee sang for us the hit song "Peter Pan" that she co-wrote for country star Kelsea Ballerini. Just one example of the awesome talent you get to see!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Stopped by here for a drink before a concert, sat at the bar, staff was friendly, place was clean, drinks were cold, ended up with shrimp fritters for an appetizer, they were pretty good, will definitely stop by again

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: What a fun place in Nashville. They have such respect for the performers and it should be that way. Food was good but that's not why we went. Some very serious talent. Would highly suggest going there to see performers you'll see for a lot more in the future.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Oh Whiskey Row. I want to love you so much because you are seriously so awesome! But your staff SUCKS. I was just there, literally 5 minutes ago, with my husband hanging out on the rooftop. We decided to leave after ONE DRINK, and we go down to the 3rd floor and I'm waiting for my husband to come out of the restroom before we get into our Uber, and one of the "bouncers" comes up to me and says I'm being escorted out. Ummm excuse me? For what?! Obviously confused, I ask why I'm being escorted out. "I've been told that you were already kicked out once and you snuck back in. You need to leave now." I tell him it's clearly a misunderstanding because I was up at the rooftop with my husband having one drink and how could I have snuck in past 3 door guys...but he refused to listen to me and said he was just doing his job. I've worked in the service industry my whole life, and I've never been treated so horribly for something I didn't do. It's a holiday weekend, train your staff better. There's 20 girls wearing the same thing I'm wearing. Don't kick out a random, good customer because of a miscommunication. There are too many other great bars, so I will definitely not be back.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text:
This place was a pleasant surprise for me, but my friend had been here the last time he was in Nashville. My friend and I had been to another place earlier in the day, and we were let down by the service and the food. That was definitely not the case here. The whole experience was great.

When you walk in the place, there is a stage and a band playing. Back home that would be a nice touch, but Nashville it is a prerequisite. The downstairs area was crowded, but the bartenders were still attentive. There was no seating available and my friend did not want to stand while eating, so we went upstairs to eat. The upstairs was not crowded and it was a nice environment. There were plenty of flat screen tvs and seating to accommodate large groups of people.

The food was really good and the portion sizes were large. I had the burger with barbeque and bacon, which was delicious. It was not made from a frozen patty, unlike the place we had been to earlier in the day. There was one person who worked there, but I did not get her name. She reminded me of Rosie the Riveter, and she was nice. Unfortunately, she is a Packers fan, but I guess we all have our flaws. She was describing the chicken fingers, and I am now going to have to make a trip back to try them. She also was describing some of the other items, and I have to say that if they are as good as the burger I will come back every time I am in Nashville.

The service was really good. As I said earlier, the downstairs bartenders were very attentive. There just was no available seating downstairs. As a result, we were about to leave the place when the bouncer let us know there was seating upstairs. Vanessa was the bartender upstairs, and she was a very good bartender. She's definitely the triple threat. It was nice because between Vanessa and Rosie the Riveter, it seemed like this is where I would be watching football games every Sunday (besides Bears vs. Titans/Packers/Vikings). One of the guys that worked there took a break upstairs by the bar, and he was telling me more about moonshine. I have to admit that I do not know about moonshine, but after talking with him and Vanessa... I might just try some one of these days.

This place was really good, and I look forward to my next visit.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Had a great evening! Everyone was attentive and food was excellent.i was pleasantly surprised as a lot of times buffets are so so but everything offered was delicious. Music show was excellent and our server George was awesome! Definitely a keeper!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
We visited Nashville for the past 4 days. We kept coming back to Dierks Bentley bar.  We had a blast! Great music with the Dozzi band, which everyone needs to follow on Twitter, Facebook etc... they were awesome and could go everyday and listen to them!!  The bartender Jake was absolutely the best!!!! He took great care of us, very pleasant, kind and was always on top of his job....we love you Jake and we will be back to visit!!   Until next time Nashville 

Brian and Mel from Greenville, PA

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Ok I stand corrected.   So just be prepared to pay 24% above the price of your drinks for state taxes and it's not the establishment's fault that they have to charge that much.

name: 360 Burger
text:
Real nice burgers + happy hour till 10pm + good live music.

I went here the first time and got myself the avocado cilantro burger with house fries. The fries were slightly soggy but the burger was bang on. Medium well done patty on a pretzel bun, oh boy aren't you my new favorite burger joint.

Just to make sure first time wasn't a fluke I went back again after a week and this time I got myself the insanity burger with sweet potato fries. The sweet potato fries were superb and the burger has now become one of the best I've had. 

I will keep going back till I'm around this part of Nashville. Yet to try a couple of their other burgers and hoping they'd turn out as good an experience as I've had so far.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I enjoyed this place a lot. Local museums are always hit or miss, but Johnny Cash just has such a great story and this museum actually has a pretty fantastic selection of memorabilia and actual items from Johnny's life. It's tourist friendly and well organized. And there's a Patsy Cline museum right above it too. Great way to spend a few hours and a little more authentically Nashville than the Kid Rock Honkytonk.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: I walked in & an employee asked for tip money right away. I was there 2 seconds & told me we work for tips bitches! We walked out! She was so rude!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Stopped in randomly. Great music (a little loud, but fun) where we sat on the 2nd floor. Food was good, but the service was great! Sarah didn't steer us wrong and made sure we had a great time. Will definitely go back the next time we're in town.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
The staff was wonderful the waiter was very attentive and the food was great!!!  I've never had a better Porkchop in my life.  

I was a little disappointed that only the main level was open gift shop was not open no other floors were available and I was just music playing on the radio with some videos that show and then the screen.  We were there at about 8 o'clock on a Tuesday night.   The place was not packed but busy enough where we hand a 30-45 min wait.   Tuesday might not be their busiest night but it would've been great to see a local artist playing their own music up on the stage.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Just to be clear, this 5 star rating is not for the food. Or the drinks. Or the service. However, the music we heard here was nothing short of amazing and I think everyone should come, so I gave it 5 stars. It was our favorite part of our Nashville trip and is an experience we will not soon forget.

First, I will say that $5 to watch these musicians is a STEAL. Now, I'm not from Music City, but I've seen a fair amount of live music in my life, but this experience blew all of that out of the water. They had us laughing, crying (more than once), and just plain awestruck. 

If you arrive early, which we did not, you can order drinks and lounge around for a bit. At show time you are escorted back to the listening room where you can order dinner and more drinks. Because they seat everyone at once, the waiters are understandably very rushed. In a effort to be prepared for everyone coming in at once, most of the tables had water and cups on them already. Ours did not, and it took about 20 minutes for us to get some. I noticed that the table next to us had cups, but their water "pitcher" (Jack Daniels bottle) was empty when they sat down. Our food came out super fast (read: it was prepared ahead of time and not very fresh). It was good but not great. We ordered three Old Fashioneds from the bar and each one came out different from the next. I'm pretty sure the first one was just a bourbon on the rocks. Oh well. 

All in all, an amazing music experience. Just don't have high expectations on the restaurant side of things.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text:
We had fun here - but it was quick. Super quick.

But this was our first visit to a wax museum - and I have to say, it was pretty neat. We had some great photo ops and overall, it was enjoyable. Just wish there had been a little more to it for the $19 a person.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We stopped in on a Sunday morning for a Bloody Mary and music. We choose the spicy version that was supposed to come with special spices and their very own pickled vegetables. What we got was a runny bland red colored drink garnished with a lime wedge. Not at all as described in the menu. WORST Bloody Mary ever!! Service was poor. Music was good and we did enjoy that.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
It's Bluebird Room without all the stress of reserving tickets but with all the same talent performing.

I had such an amazing time at the Listening Room - why are there not things like this in Chicago!? Seriously one of the best things I did on my last trip to Nashville. 

All of the singer songwriters on the night we went were incredibly talented. Some better than others and some just mind-blowing. My favorite of the night was Kyle Reynolds! Loved his acoustic boy band but way more talented vibe. 

Beer selection wasn't great but I found one that I stuck with for the night. And prices weren't bad. Also our server was super friendly and attentive which was nice.

name: The Basement East
text:
Tonight was my very first time going to see music at The Basement East!!! I don't know why it has taken me so long to check out a band here...I was the lucky winner of 2 free tickets to see Austin Meade (opening act) & the Read Southall Band - THANK YOU @NowPlayingNashville

The music was great and the venue is simple and easy to navigate.  I highly recommended coming early to grab a seat at the high bar tables... (most of the venue is standing room only). There is a free parking lot and nearby street parking.  I'm not sure If everyone was at LOTG but it wasn't that busy tonight.  I'm not sure how the venue picks the lineup but I thought both bands were really good! Austin is from Texas - favorite song was Savannah! Read Southall is from Oklahoma and describes themselves as Southern Rock & Crunchy Country . My favorite song was "Why?" - Loved belting out the lyrics!  The drinks were great and the bartender was really nice.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
I'd stay away. 

The only place in Nashville charging a cover ($6/head) and they had the worst talent. We hated it and left pretty quick. This place is attached to Dick's Last Resort - which also seemed weird. Everyone in there is wearing a hat that makes them look like klan members.  Hit the other bars and venues instead.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
I wanted this place to be amazing..... 

Lets start with decor and location! The location in downtown is awesome and very easy to find. Once you go in there are 3 floors, the first is a bar the second is a chill vibe where you can eat and listen to music (we were there for brunch) the third (7th flight of stairs) was the roof which was TINY!! 

Everything looked great, LOVED the decor and the music was exceptional, the man and woman who sang were amazing vocalists. Unfortunately we really wanted to have brunch on the roof but with only 3 shaded spots and two out in the sun we couldn't find a spot. We got a booth on the second level and took a seat. 

To make a long story short I will bullet point the positives: 
- The southern fries were delicious 
- the decor and ambiance was nice 
-moderatly priced mimosa's and bellinis

the negatives: 
- other than the southern fries our food was below average 
- two of our orders were wrong, and when asked to bring the rest of my food they brought out my side of bacon, after we were all done eating. 
-The waitress we had never refilled our drinks or asked if we wanted more

I may go back to check out the bar but I've honestly been telling people how bad our food and service was because of the name so many people will want to check it out and I don't want them to waste their time.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We came after brunch on Sunday.  There was a great band and it was not too crowded.  We sat inside (it was scorching hot outside) on the first floor at the bar with a great view of the stage.  Loved the atmosphere with the windows open and the AC blasting.  Beer selection is pretty typical of the bars on Broadway.  We didn't have food.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I expected it to be a little bigger museum, but I guess it was still pretty cute setup. Honestly, Johnny Cash fans would appreciate it more than me. They have few stuff, like his concert and performance related outfits, guitars, his personal letters, and photographs, etc. on the display.  There are many audio stations to listen to his music and couple of videos are shown to tell the story of his life. I saw some old couple listening to his famous song "Hurt" and they were in tears. I didn't understand why they were crying, but then my boyfriend explained me the importance of that song. Long story short, go to this place only if you're a die hard fan of Johnny Cash. Like any other touristy place, there is a souvenir shop inside the museum that sells Johnny Cash t- shirts, mugs, magnets, posters, baby onesies, and what not. You can also grab a bite or drink some beer in the small cafe next to the ticket counter.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Been spending time at whiskey row several times a week since it opened. Im usually not crazy about the broadway bars, but I do play music in some of them(whiskey row included). This place has the best atmosphere of any bar on broadway in my opinion. The food (e.i. whiskey burger) is so good. The drinks are great and the staff I have met all seem personable and professional.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: A bit of a walk from the main drag, but worth every step. We listened to 5 amazing song-writers in an intimate atmosphere without all the craziness.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: We had one goal our first night out in Nashville-find the Dueling Piano Bar. Find it we did, and boy we were not disappointed! We got there pretty early so we had our pick of seats. It started with just two players/ singers, but by the time we left (3-4 hours later) they had four-five of them on the stage at one time. They could play almost anything you requested and if they didn't know it, one of them would go learn it quick while the others continued with other requests. I requested Metallica and they delivered! My family and I had so much fun and while the drinks were a bit pricey, it was to be expected since we were on the main drag of downtown Nashville. I can't wait to go back and bring everyone I know!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Glad I went.  Like everywhere else in Nashville it was way too crowded when I went.  I love a few Johnny Cash songs and albums but you have to be a Johnny Cash super fan to really enjoy this museum.  Expensive for what it is.  Real estate can't be cheap in this area but I'm sure Cash's relatives aren't hurting for money.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Hello! I'm Johnny Cash.

I was quite impressed with this museum. It's not a huge museum and can be done in 1-2 hours but it houses a ton of interesting information and memorabilia. I was also surprised with how high tech it was compared to other museums I have been to - music videos on iPads! How cool. While we were there, an employee was walking around helping people who needed it and answering questions. He's got to be the Johnny Cash trivial pursuit champ - he knew everything! Apparently they have Johnny Cash friends & family that will work at the museum occasionally. 

You can take pictures anywhere within the museum and there are some great photo ops! Like posing in front of the wall of records.

Tickets are normally $15 but I was able to snag a Groupon for half the price or you can use the Total Access Pass for admission. Keep your eyes open to score a deal on entry!

I like Johnny Cash's music but aside from the movie with Reese Witherspoon, I don't know much about him. I learned quite a bit at the museum and enjoyed watching his performances. I was in the theater room alone watching various bits from him on TV shows and such for quite some time. One of the big highlights is the handwritten lyrics to Walk The Line and Folsom Prison Blues. My personal favorite thing in the museum was the Valentine's gift from Johnny to June.

You can't miss the museum - it's a huge red brick building with Johnny Cash written all over it. There isn't a private parking lot but there is a paid parking lot adjacent to the building. 

In my opinion, it's a must do while in Nashville.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
My review is for this bar during the afternoon. 

Whiskey Row is a three story bar that has the tallest rooftop on lower Broadway. When you're walking up the stairs to the top, you'll truly feel it. There are a lot of stairs. The top floor has a great view of all of the Honky Tonks. There's an outdoor area as well as a DJ set up. 

The bottom two floors are where the live music happens. The first floor was loud and lively. There is a lot of bar space and tables to sit at. It feels very spacious and is one of the few square shaped bars as opposed to the very narrow rectangular shaped bars. 

We wandered our way to the second floor and had such a great time. The vibe was really chill. They have drinks and food and lots of large booths and high tops. The band playing was incredible. They were really friendly and talked a lot to the audience asking for requests. Their music was awesome. 

I really liked this bar. There was something for everyone. From the rooftop area to the cozy second floor listening lounge to the rowdier first floor, it's a great spot to spend an afternoon. I bet it's a ton of fun at night also.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Went to Nashville for a girls trip in lieu of me graduating from college. It was a 5 day trip and after going to Whiskey Row the first night I wanted to go there every night. It was so much fun! First floor was live country music and second floor was a dj mixing all the 2000's and current hits. I paid for my first two drinks and my friend paid for our first two shots and with tip it combined to $40. The age group was mid twenties to early thirties. I'm gonna miss Nashville but I'm really gonna miss Whiskey Row

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
I'm sure we were one of the many who couldn't get tickets to Bluebird Cafe so we ended up here. This is absolutely nothing against the performers, who were all awesome, but everything to do with the venue.

Given that the main attraction is music, the acoustics were terrible at this venue. The wait staff clears plates outside in the main area. Even though they were about 10 feet away, when you bang forks, knives, and plates together, the noise carries. It doesn't help that the flooring is a hard surface so it also echoes. It made it really difficult to hear the actual performance.

On top of the entrance fee, there's also a $15 minimum per person for food and drinks. Now, if you have to enforce a $15 minimum, that makes me think that you DGAF about your food because people will have to order it anyway. The fried green tomatoes were the worst I've ever had, and don't get me started on the batter. The chips on our cheese plate were stale. If you absolutely had to come, just stick with drinks.

I wouldn't return, and wouldn't recommend. Too bad because the music was great!

PS The parking was free valet, which was convenient.

name: The Basement East
text:
If you are in Nashville, but not trying to get all in the country scene, check out The Basement East. New Found Glory was wrapping up their 20 year tour and the venue was awesome!! Drink prices weren't inflated -- low end at $2 up to maybe $5-6 which is great because you can stroll over to the food register and grab a a sandwich or guac n chips. 

Venue had a decent sound system that let you hear yourself instead of having to constantly scream.  I didn't have a chance to check out the pub, but I will if I'm back in the area.

Overall, it's a decent venue to see bands and other acts at prices you won't get in an arena/ballroom setting.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
Nice surprise!! 
We ordered some drinks and some of the Ultimate Nacho's while we decided what for what to eat for the meal. The drinks we had were all so good! AND pretty! They had an AMAZING salad! (Heads up the kitchen closes at 10pm) I got the house salad with chicken. It was SO GOOD! The seasoning was so good! I saw someone's salad go past my table and opted for it over a burger because the salad looked THAT good! (If I'm honest I was expecting more bar type food but this was like real restaurant good food!)
I enjoyed this salad on the 3rd floor- with some awesome live music! The drinks was sooo good! Smaller than some of the other broadway bar's, but still very good! We enjoyed the Born Free, Devil Without A Cause, & The Bobby.
The 3rd floor has nice big tables to seat 6 beside a window (so fun to get the breeze, watch people & hear other live music while the band changes out)

This is absolutely a must go to if you are on broadway! This is a 4 Story bar, music on every floor!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I LOVE it here. Local beers and fabulous live music in an industrial space that also succeeds in having a cozy, intimate feel. This was my first stop out on Saturday night and I honestly wish I spent more time here rather than checking out the grimy honky tonks on Broadway. The bartender was superbly friendly and small plates were excellent - especially the smoked veggie skewers and toasted ravioli. The cocktail menu surpasses anything you'd find down the street. Listening Room totally spoiled me with goodness before heading to Tin Roof on Broadway where I returned a gin & tonic because they accidentally poured tequila. But that's a review for another time.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
We had a terrible experience on 5/29 while we were having lunch. We went to the top floor to enjoy the view. As we were eating lunch our bartender peeled her skin from her shoulder and let another customer sitting at the bar lick it off her finger. She then grabbed a lime and put it in a beer. I wish I was making this up but it is true. After we paid our check I spoke with the floor manager , Trevor and explained  what happen. I was not convinced much would be done. I went to the main floor to ask to speak with the General manager and was told she was on vacation. I requested to speak to the highest level manager on duty and was told they are busy right now and I could leave my number. I left my number and have not heard a thing. 
Concerned about health issues here. If this goes on in front of customers what happens in the back?

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text:
This was a welcome surprise on a busy football Sunday. It is just a little off of the beaten path and we noticed a rooftop floor with good sounding music as we passed. So we stopped in, listened a bit on the first floor and then found our way up to the top floor to listen to a very pleasant female vocalist performing solo. The sound level was low so we could listen to her excellent performance while enjoying a couple of very good football games. Granted, if all you want is football, the music might be a diversion. But if you would as soon listen to good music while watching, this will definitely fill the bill. 
We enjoyed a couple of reasonably priced drinks while we listened to the music and were served by pleasant wait staff. All in all, a very pleasant afternoon. We would recommend this for a leisurely afternoon of football (or other sports) and some good music.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
The food was okay but thank goodness the music was amazing. 

We really had a great time! Our trip to Nashville would not have been the same without coming to The Listening Room.

Be sure to order the fried pickles as an appetizer but prepare yourself because they are on the sweet side instead of tangy.

We ordered the brisket sandwich and the two meat BBQ platter. I've never had a shredded brisket sandwich... I'm used to sliced. It tasted good but the texture was too similar to the pulled pork.

On the night we went, we got to listen to AJ Kross. If you haven't heard him he, is an excellent singer and songwriter. Actually all of the performers were great it's just that AJ was a real standout.

We would definitely go to The Listening Room again if we ever came back to Nashville.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
All country music represented during show. Bluegrass, country classics/relics and the "new" sounds from up and coming artists.  My kid said, "mom I like all the music, the old folks and the new ones!" She saw the ad for the Johnny cash museum and she is excited to go there! This a must see venue in Nashville.

Family friendly, clean restrooms and helpful employees make it 5 stars!

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text:
Great atmosphere especially on game days. They have great staff that does a great job of managing the crazy amounts of people they get in there on college football Saturday's. 

If you are in town in Sunday make sure to stop by Spatzmatics after 3pm.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Exceeded expectations! Great atmosphere and great beer selection. Service was great and will return when we are in town next!

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: When I come to Nashville, I love to drink at this place. It's off of Broadway so you're removed from a lot of the tourists which a like. The beers are also cheaper here than on Broadway too. I usually order a bucket of beer and save that way. People I have talked to say they put on a good brunch and to sit up stairs. This place was crowded on the Sunday we came to but we were still able to find a good table. They have a floor to ceiling, wall to wall TV that they put the NFL, NHL, MLB or other sports on. They have food but I just stuck to beers and mimosas. It's quicker to order at the bar than it is to wait for a server too. They have restrooms on both floors too which is nice. They almost always have a live band/DJ downstairs on weekends too. The staff behind the bar are friendly and quick to serve you. If you come here, I don't think you'll be disappointed!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Awesome music, the ribs were out of sight and our waitress Amanda was the bomb. We will be back

name: Music City Tippler
text:
One of my favorite bars in Nashville so far. As a recent transplant from California, it reminds me of the type of bars I would go to out there. There are three levels, the bar on the main floor(there's a seating section and outdoor patios too), the lower floor where there's another bar, DJ and some dance space, and then a mezzanine overlooking the dance floor which is more loungey. Overall, the bar has a classier feel and people are better dressed than you'll find in the college bars down the street.

Drinks and craft brews are good, well-priced and never weak. I've never had to wait very long to get served. People are generally pretty friendly and easy to talk to(this being Nashville after all). And a good mix of people as far as age range and ethnic background.  Music is mostly top 40 and club bangers which I'm not a huge fan of, but it doesn't bother me either. It seems to get people in the party mood so it's all good. There is also a big screen up near the bar that games are shown on.

Nice place to hang if you want to pretend you're not in Nashville for a few hours or you're a transplant from the coast feeling homesick and don't care for the huge country-western scene.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This first time here, immediately felt the divey vibe. Loved the paints and the decor, self seating, was a bit busy but wasn't packed. The music was legit tho, they had rap on that flowed with the vibe of the place, when P.I.M.P from 50cents came on, all The patrons starting singing the first chorus. The beer selection wasn't bad but wasn't a lot for a dive bar, the food was the reason we picked this place. Once we were seated, we got our waters right away, order our drinks and food right away. We drove 2 hrs and was hungry and had a concert to attend. My beer and my cousin old fashion came about 10mins after we order. My beer was good for a local brewery, my cousin's old fashion wasn't as great as some other places. As time passed, we noticed previous customers leaving and new customers who showed up after us getting food. I went up to the bar to see the tap selection and get a tasting of the Rock Bold another local and had to order it from our waitress at the bar. It's been about 45 mins or so when she noticed we didn't have our food, then she said " I am not sure what happened to your ticket but I am going to look into it" at this point. I was beer #2 and borderline hangry mad.  She came back, apologized that the kitchen didn't get our ticket and asked if we were here for a concert. Which we were, she asked if we wanted to stay and wait for our food or go. We told her if it doesn't take long, she went to ask the kitchen and they told her they can do it. So we agreed only if it takes 10 mins, which was going to give us time to find somewhere else to eat. Not even 5 Mins after that our food came out. If it wasn't for the delicious juicy burger on that fluffy crisp bun with melted blue cheese and the amazing garlic seasoned fries I would have given this place a 3. But the food was good, I am sure it isn't just from my hangry stage but the burgers were cooked to juicy perfection and the fries were crispy but soft in the middle with just the right amount of seasoning that didn't over power it. The service was less to be desired but there was only 3 server/bartenders but still it shouldn't have taken 45 minutes to notice we didn't have food or come back to our table.  I definitely want to go back when I am in Nashville again and try the jalapeño poppers and give it another try.

name: Third Man Records
text:
"Your Turntable is not Dead"

This is the slogan at Third Man Records and they are doing everything they can to make sure that it is true.  Third Man's founder, Jack White, came to prominence in the band the White Stripes and has been consistently fascinating since emerging from Detroit in the late 90s.  The White Stripes were a vibrant throwback to Blues and Garage Rock, taking ideas that were from previous generations and bringing them into the modern era.  The same is true of Third Man Records, they are taking a format that belongs to previous generations and updating it to be innovative today.  When the White Stripes were covering Country songs from Dolly Parton and Loretta Lynn it was a cross genre surprise but now it makes the eventual move to Nashville seem inevitable.

For a person who's most famous band is built on a lie about his fraternal relationship to his bandmate it makes sense that Jack White would curate his own history and create his own museum.  The Third Man Records compound is a place of Pure Imagination befitting the Wonka-like figure at it's center.  It has a recording studio, offices, and a performance space, but the most accessible and prominent area is the store.  Rarely has so much of interest been packed into such a small space.  Somehow, without feeling cluttered they have managed to fill every inch of the store with wonder.  There are plenty of records for Jack White, his side projects, his side projects side projects and his legendary friends.  If you don't have a turntable you can purchase one there or buy all kinds of merch items from standard T-shirts and posters to a Third Man Rubik's Cube or fine jewelry.

You can gawk at the technologies that time has forgotten like a 16mm video jukebox and a record your own record machine.  The display case features actual Grammys.  The walls showcase the inventive records that the Third Man team have thought up and then executed with the wizards at United Record Pressing just a few miles away.  Even the bathrooms are cool.  I know it sounds weird but make sure you go to the bathroom while you are there because it allows you to see more of the property.  In the men's room they have a kooky upside down bidet that functions as a shower for the touring bands that come through.  If you are a music fan it's cool place to visit and if you are a Jack White fan you might as well surrender your wallet to them.

name: Music City Tippler
text: Great interior. Very hipster speak easy. Pretentious crowd but that's to be expected opening week. I'll give it some time and come back. Cocktails and light appetizer menu.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: At first was a cool place but the dj running the karaoke absolutely ruined it. My boyfriend and I put our names in for songs at the same time. My boyfriend went a couple of songs later and my turn kept getting pushed further and further down the list behind people that had just got there. I went up ~30 minutes later to tell him to strike my name cause I was done and leaving. He then says I'm up next and proceeds to make an announcement saying- hey if it seems you keep getting bumped down the list it's because new people come in and drop $20s in his tip jar. It'll be the last time I go to that bar and I'll make sure my friends don't waste their time there either.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Hands down my favorite karaoke bar on Broadway in Nashville. Drinks are moderately priced. Karaoke runs smoothly throughout the evening. Plenty of places to sit on bar stools even though it stays crowded and fills up rather quickly. Amateur entertainment at its best mixed with some diamonds in the rough. Lines can sometimes be long going in but they move rather quickly. On my 23rd birthday I sang here (another thing marked off my bucket list) & I'll never forget it

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: How can you not give them five stars!  It made country music what it is today.  George Hays had a radio show.  One of the singers didn't show up and they had a fill in.  Jimmy Thompson played his fiddle and they got a huge response to add country music to his radio program.  And the grand ole opry was born.  It is amazing how many places housed the Grand Ole Opry.  One of the buildings was the Ryman House which was a converted church.  The seats were pews.  They still have pews.  There is a part of the original stage in the current building.  You can stand on it!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
"The Grand Ole Opry is the show that made country music famous."

Country Music would not be what it is today without The Grand Ole Opry. The Grand Ole Opry was where a lot of country music artists started their career. I took the day tour, and I found it enjoyable. You learn about its origins, go backstage, visit the different dressing rooms and see all the memorabilia collected over the years. 

My favorite part was being able to go on the "circle of wood" and take a picture on it as if I was a country music sensation. lol. In 1974, a circle of oak was cut from the Ryman Auditorium, and inserted into The Grand Ole Opry's stage. Hundreds of country stars have stood and sang on that slab of wood -- Johnny Cash, Patsy Cline, Dolly Parton, Blake Shelton, Carrie Underwood and up-coming country stars. The Grand Ole Opry has their own photographer who will take a picture of you on the circle of wood. It is a complete tourist photo trap, so if you are a sucker like me, you may end up purchasing a photo. If you don't like how your photo came out, they can re-take your picture. I recently bought 3 pairs of cowboy boots (everyone owned a pair in Nashville! Refer to that review here: https://www.yelp.com/biz/boot-country-nashville?hrid=tSVO1NK_msqpQ7JhkitFDg&utm_campaign=www_review_share_popup&utm_medium=copy_link&utm_source=(direct) lol), so I had my photo retaken because they did not get a good shot of my stylish Nashville ensemble. lol. 

If I am ever in Nashville again, I will try to catch a live performance. I may not be a country music listener, but I am pretty sure it will be a good experience. And you know I will be in cowboy boots, so it better be good. Yee-haw! lol.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: I like it.. nice place to chill.. drink beer... listen to country.... & watch sports ‼

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Where to start.... this rating would have been a bit higher but our server Heather was such a bitchy Cee-U-Next-Tuesday it totally ruined the end of our 4th of July in Nashville. I was in there with my brother who is a well known beer critic (he was not impressed by the beer) she got a little pissy when we started asking questions she didn't know the answer to ( like that's our fault). She is definitely not from the south as she doesn't have a grain of Southern hospitality that TN is so well known for. EVERY encounter with her ( which was few since she dropped our beers off and checked on us once) she had a really shitty attitude especially to me but was a little better with my brother but he is pretty cute.  She was nowhere to be found so we asked another server if we could order a pretzel. Heather come back to our table and sarcastically says, "oh so you changed your mind about food?"  Returns and tosses our plate of pretzels on the table and walks off. We had to ask another server again for our check. She brought it and disappeared. I asked the guy behind the counter if he could ring us up and said only our server could so we waited for her again. But the final straw that demonstrated her low class pissy attitude was when she saw I did not tip her then followed me out of the bar, stared me down and made a sarcastic remark about "have a great night ". I worked my way through college as a server, my kids were servers and my brother was a server and I am a very good tipper but I'm not rewarding bad behavior/attitude. If I was an investor, I would demand she be fired.   Almost all negative reviews (1-2 stars) for this establishment gave a poor rating due to terrible service and horrible attitudes of wait staff.  So apparently if you're a rude A-hole or bitch you won't have any problem getting a job at Flying Saucer.  Negative reviews seem to have no affect on Flying Saucer management as there are no responses of apology for the bad experiences which is why the bad service continues. 

We watched the other servers and they were friendly, smiling, and attentive to their customers. 

The only thing we had to eat was the pretzels which were fresh, nice and soft and pretty good but needed just a little more salt in the dough. 

Anyone playing the slightest attention could see my brother was reviewing beer and posting reviews. The beer wasn't that great but everything tastes a little better with kindness. 



My advice is skip the Flying Saucer and head 8 blocks to the east and go to Rock Bottom. Their brews and service were much better and the food was pretty good.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
What Nashville lacks is A. Yes, the letter A. 

Belcourt Taps, a once tapas bar, sans the A, and now a beer, food and live music joint, is really a hidden joint in the 21st S neighborhood. On a cold wintry night, to escape the howling winds, I ducked into Belcourt Taps (thinking it was tapas), expecting a plate of tortilla espanola, maybe a bite of fried eggplant with honey, patatas bravas, or any of the infinite little eats that haunt a tapas bar. But lo! it was now Taps and there was beer (lots of local ones at that) and food. And music.

The evening saw three sets of people get up on the little stage and sing and play. I detected two options of vegetarian burgers and after dousing with their bhut jholokia hot sauce (ask for it), I was on fire. The evening was on fire. My skin was on fire. My tongue was on fire. Everyone was fiery red and blazing hot. I clapped and cheered, drank and wolfwhistled. I howled at the moon and demanded encores. Truly, it was a magical night and I returned with some friends a couple of times. And both times, we were impressed and serenaded by the cozy and dimly lit interiors, great beer and good food.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Unless you tip the DJ a hefty amount, or hes got eyes for you, you're not gonna sing. I came to this bar visiting from 4 hours away because I love karaoke. I signed up as soon as I arrived and the DJ was very short with me, even after I put a few bucks in his jar. I continued to watch people who had signed up much later than me sing for about 2 hours before I left unsatisfied and frustrated. Not to mention you couldn't cuss on stage or you'll get kicked out? Seriously? It's karaoke not a church service. To wrap it all up, the DJ needs a serious attitude adjustment, and maybe a reality check. Good job pal, you load up your equipment and play country music for drunk people to sing over. Hop off your high horse. Won't be returning. This place was 2 hours I'll never get back.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: We got there when they opened and had to wait outside. If you don't want to open at 8pm then don't post 8pm on your web site that simple. Then we finally got to go inside and had to wait around while they all stood around talking. The DJ finally gets up and takes requests after singing his own songs. Then he sings every other song himself while you sit and wait to actually see people sing Karaoke. No one is there to listen to the DJ sing. They are there to see karaoke. We finally left after feeling like they were doing us a favor letting us be there and being tired of waiting to see people sing. Left the DJ a $20 tip, bought drinks, were polite, but still felt like they were going out of their way just doing their jobs. We won't be back.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Visited Nashville for a night last month and loved Flying Saucer. The space is great, and the beer list is simply amazing. We tried some of the local beers, and let the bartender make some recommendations for us. The staff was not only very nice, but also incredibly knowledgable about the beers they have, which is even more impressive given the large beer list.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Beer selection is just great. Its always nice to be able to try new stuff. Service was pretty slow and food took a bit of time. The food quality itself is nothing to write home about but  this is the type of place to grab some beers and munchies after work.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: We were supposed to meet some friends here, but they never showed up.  They have a very large selection of beer, but nothing that I thought was extremely difficult to get or rare.  Although they had a much smaller selection, I thought Beer Republic had a much more interesting beer selection. I like the decorum and would give this one a try if I was in the neighborhood again.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Good Beer, great service..got a Groupon for 2 flights and a pretzel, no problem redeeming it beer choices were varied and good, liked all the IPAs that they offered..would return..worth it for craft fans to check out..!!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great atmosphere.  Food was good and  appetizer was great.  Catfish was excellent and ribs were ok.  Fried chicken was disappointing.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Stopped in here for lunch one day while at the Frist and really enjoyed it. The service was friendly and prompt and my food was out very quickly. They have several vegetarian options to choose from and their Hippie Burger, while different from other veggie burgers I've had, was super good. Their beer menu is insanely comprehensive, with something for everyone, and nicely categorized. Great lunch spot, very reasonably priced, I'll be back to try more beers and their cocktails for sure!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
I need more of this in my life.

Did I know it was a chain? Nope. Do I actually care? Nope. In fact, I want the chain to come to Chicago, ASAP. Queue a Fleetwood Mac song here... You would never break the chain... 

Anyway...

This place is huuuuuuge. And the beer menu is huuuuuuuge. If you can't find something you like here, then you must not like beer. If you see the Blackhorse Vanilla Cream Ale available, GET IT. After trying this beer here, I forced the manfriend to drive 30 minutes out of our way on the road trip back north just to go buy a sixer of this in Clarksville.

Flying Saucer, I see you've inched north to STL. If you see this, and you feel the need to expand to Chicago... call me.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I came here with a few colleagues and it was a lot of fun. I had the grilled cheese and tomato bisque and it was delicious! Warning for vegetarians it has bacon!!! As a non-vegetarian it was flavorful and perfect for a summer time dinner. I couldn't figure out with beer to get, there are so many option it takes at least 15 mins to figure it out. I tried their ghost beer flight which is a super cool concept, they have 4 beers that are blinded so the customer or servers have no idea which is what and they are numbered. You can have one like picking a number out of a lottery or try a tasting flight. I would said 3/4 were really good, unfortunately I'll never know what the name of the beers will be. We also learned that to get a plate on the wall required to try 200 different types of beers.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Worst service. Hostess had such a bad attitude she threw our menus down at the table & walked away. Took 3 people on wait staff for us to flag down to ask for service which took 20 min for someone to finally come take our order. Another 25 min to get our drinks. When we got them the ice was melted in them, could tell they'd been sitting at the bar for a while. Go to the hot dog street vendor instead!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: The beer selection here is awesome and changes regularly. The servers are always friendly and very attentive. The pretzels are a must have! They are served warm with your choice of dipping sauces. The regular food there is good too, but I can make a meal of the pretzels.  The only downside is that parking can be a bit of a challenge and you may end up walking a bit.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I thought we could get lunch in a relatively small amount of time. We had 1 hour for my wife's lunch break and we didn't receive our food until 40 mins in the building. Needless to say, we ate our food quickly and tried to pay, but there was one waitress handling way too many tables. Either they are understaffed or need a faster cook. It's never good when the people get seated after you and have their food come right out. The only thing I can say positive is the food was decent. I wouldn't go back.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: One of the better local bars in Nashville! From the writer's night on Wednesday to the best Sunday Funday spot in town with the Spazmatics, you can't beat it! With all the TVs, it may be the best place to watch a game as well! It is a Bama bar, so Vols fans beware on Saturdays. The staff is awesome, and always on point with service and fun times. I would recommend for both locals and those visiting and looking for a good time!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Excellent ambience. Great service. 

Tried their Share Plates. Make sure to try their Hungry Farmer and Loaded Rocket Tots. Awesome!!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: One word... Incredible! We were one hour into arriving to Nashville for our first time. We usually bar hop.. Nope there was no leaving this place. Just wow!!! You have to come, all the best song writers in country music are here actually on stage playing for you. Could not believe it! Kate our bartender is absolutely the best ever. Make a reservation it is packed!!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Went here for dinner last night. Was able to go straight in and get a seat as it was an early dinner. The waitress was nice. The nachos were great, my wife's ribs were great she said, my brisket was good at best you could tell it was dry due to being smothered in BBQ sauce. But overall was a good meal. The music was good sang everything from old country to blues. Will definitely go back.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
After walking Broadway for over an hour, we ended up at BB King's. 

Unlike the places on Broadway, we didn't have an hour-plus wait; we were seated right away. The place is really dark, so be careful walking until your eyes adjust.

I had BBQ ribs and chicken ($20). My son's burger was "average" in his opinion (he is a burger snob). In a non-tourist area, I'd say the food was overpriced, but it was bout what I'd expect in such a location. I was disappointed that the $10 beer special, which included a souvenir glass, was a no-go since they were out of souvenir glasses. Boo.

"The Rhythm Section" was performing, and I really enjoyed their show. I could have put down a few cold ones and chilled out for hours if I didn't have to leave.

A solid 3 stars for the place and the food, with a bonus star for The Rhythm Section.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Wait staff was great, very prompt & friendly, but that couldn't make up for the very mediocre food.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Flying Saucer is my favorite beer drinking spot. I know, its a chain. So shoot me! 

I have been a big fan of Flying Saucer for years. It is just a super chill place to eat, drink and be merry. Their pretzels are an awesome addition while sampling all of the brews. I always park behind the building. They validate, so it isn't too expensive. 

Honestly, the number one reason why I love going to Flying Saucer is because I am part of their Beer Knurd club. I used to only drink the same two or three types of beer but now I am trying all sorts and enjoying the process! 200 different beers gets you a plate on the ceiling. I will get that plate if it kills me!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: The price is right and the food was good. I ordered a burger (obviously) but don't be fooled because they do not cook to temperature.  PBR for $2 and their fries were pretty great.  Off the beaten path and very chill....a great place to get your night started before the insanity that is Nashvegas!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Thought this was a bar... they only have beer. Really? We wanted Long Island ice teas but had to get cider. Gross.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Love this place.  Cheap karaoke and cheap drinks.  What's not to love?  Located on Printer's Alley too.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
I attended an Event at the Music City Tippler last night hosted by Bombay Sapphire and GQ.

I must say the interior/decor and overall vibe of the just about two week old bar/restaurant was a vast improvement over it's predecessor the dull and snobby 
Miro District.

The staff was very friendly and amicable and kept the place very clean the entire evening, I even saw one of the managers wiping the counter in the ladies restroom. 

The passed apps were average for an event of that sort yet not disappointing in any way and although I am not a fan of gin, the specialty cocktails were enjoyable.

I enjoyed my first experience at the Tippler and would love to return on a regular night of service to receive the full experience.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: After years of not going to the Opry, I found myself in Nashville and wanted to relive how fun the Opry can be. I was surprised to find that singers like Bill Anderson have decided to take it on themselves to give sermons on stage about an issue that doesn't exist. The saying of "Merry Christmas!" He acted as if the world is taking Christmas from country music. How ridiculous and what an unnecessary creation of making the Opry politically-charged, when it should be about good solid country music. It was awesome when immediately thereafter another artist came out and greeted the crowd with HAPPY HOLIDAYS. Bill - stick to the music and not the stupid issues dividing people. Jesus Christ isn't worried about Christmas being stolen. ;)

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Food was alright, but what REALLY made the night was the fantastic live music. The band was perfect, completely in sync, meddled with the crowd just right. 

Go for the music, eat some of the food - I had the DEBRIS Burger - brisket, beef patties, cheese, it was worth it. Fries were perfectly crispy.

name: Music City Tippler
text: Used to love this place and gave it a glowing review once upon a time. But we went in a few weeks ago and were shocked to find the interior redecorated (cheaper tables and chairs) & the menu COMPLETELY different. They used to have really cool menus with a huge selection of food and drink- their menus now are just basic and very limited on the food front. It's obvious the Tippler just wants to be a bar now- don't bother coming here for food. The drinks are really great, but it's just a bummer that this used to be a spot for amazing food AND amazing drinks. And it definitely had a classier vibe before. Oh well- on to the Patterson House!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We went pretty late at night after dinner for snacks, drinks and good music.  The ambiance was so much fun and the BB King All Stars (the live band) were very entertaining.  We got some nachos and a side of mac and cheese to snack on that were both very good.  The band was a lot of fun and a lot of people were dancing.  I'm not a country music fan, so finding a great alternative in Nashville was exciting.  The service was great and I would go back.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Great tour along with a lot of information. Groups are small with plenty of time to take pictures.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I was raised on Country, however, love all genres.  My parents use to visit the Opry every few years, but I've never been.  A recent business trip had me less than an hour away, so I had to make plans to bring my wife for a weekend experience in Nashville and the Grand Ole Opry. 

The sound, the lights, the talent all combined to make it a once in a lifetime experience.  

We also purchased the backstage post show tour.  We were fortunate to see Bill Anderson back stage and he spoke to us as he was leaving.  We were amazed at all that goes on back stage.  

We would definitely visit again.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Overall good tour of the facility. We did did to see areas backstage that are normally not seen. We were able to see into and go into some very nicely decorated dressing rooms. Way over priced. Would be nice to have some discounts for seniors and lower cost for children under 18. 45 minute total tour with at least having been covered by watching videos or standing in line to get a forced picture taken.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: My new favorite place! It was our first visit at the opry, and my husband and I loved it. There is no better way to see several great artists all in one night, at such a historical place that means so much to the country artists themselves. We were able to get better seats off of stubhub, and were on the main level rather than the balcony. Although they it looked like any seat would be a good seat! Love love love, and can't wait to go back one day!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Food, atmosphere, live music and service were all fantastic! I had the nachos (delicious) and pulled pork sliders (yum!). The live music added to the atmosphere and made our lunch more enjoyable. Will definitely be back!
