name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Stopped in for breakfast,  a very eclectic menu,  but still can get basic eggs. Had scrambled eggs,  awesome breakfast potatoes and bacon.  Husband had cornbeef hash,  and it was real cornbeef, also very good. Jalapeno bacon good and spicy.  Service was very good,  very friendly.  I would recommend!!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: We went to see the Lewis Copeland Band. My girlfriend and her friend know Lewis from his hometown. We went for the music, but did have some beers while we were there. They have a great selection of beer and serve it in plastic cups. The trailer resort theme is cool and the stage is big enough for the bands. Some of the places on Broadway have tiny stages.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Three stories of hootin' n hollerin' and good times! Take s stroll to the back alley and enter through their neck entrance to avoid the line out front. Lookin' for a good time kinda night? Stay on the first floor and enjoy the live music and the party atmosphere. If you are looking for a bit more fresh air and open space, make a bee line to the top floor and onto the balcony. Live music is also blasting through the upstairs speakers, too.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Great atmosphere.  Bluegrass music added perfect feel for Sunday brunch.  Service fantastic.  Food and drinks pretty good. Had tacos, enchildadas, and both sangrias.  The place to go for weekend brunch.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Blond bartender serving on the rooftop on 8/4 is rude AF. She has no reason to disrespect a group of courteous, paying customers. Won't be returning.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Love this spot!  This is my neighborhood pub, so I usually come here for happy hour or last call.  I think I've only been to like, 2 shows here.  Bigger shows can get crazy packed.  Solid food and a decent beer and whiskey selection.  The burgers are easily as good as ML Rose and you don't have to put up with the aging bros;  just hipsters.  90% of the staff is super cool and I ain't even mad at the one that doesn't like me.  Also, 241 beers on monday is super clutch.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
The food was okay, but execution on the cook fell flat. The speed with which I got my food was amazing. Probably indicative of the food all having been precooked. I got a hot chicken sandwich. The heat was good, but the chicken was over cooked. The fried exterior was too crispy that it took away from the bite and the chicken itself was dry. The Texas toast used for the bread of the sandwich was cold. The sandwich would have been better if the Texas toast had been toasted or at least warmed up a bit. The tater tots were overcooked, but otherwise good. 

Overall, the place was fine for food in a pinch. Might have been better if I was drunk and jonesing for a food fix. I'm on the fence about whether or not to come back.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
This was a special experience. We had just come into town and we were  told  to go to the Bliebird Cafe ! we tried to make reservations in "the queue ". That was a bust. So we just got in line for the 1 and 45 minute wait. It was ok. We just bonded with everyone!  We were literally the last people in. They had to separate us but it was ok just to get in!  I was so close I felt like part of the band!! 
The gals at the door were very nice and the wait staff was fast!  It ended up being a special experience and one of our favorite places in Nashville !!!!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Love this place! It's great food and service...I love the old Woolworths atmosphere. It was happy hour til 8 on Friday. So cool...definitely recommended by us for sure. Swing bar downstairs is so classic.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I came here for beer and music and Tootsie's most definitely delivered. From what I saw they had 5 different bands playing on every level of the bar. I was amazed. Drunk, but amazed. The upstairs bathroom attendant was the shit and kept calling everyone "sexy sassy". My friend paid 7.00 for a rail gin and tonic with no lime haha but that seems normal in a tourist town.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Some say this is the heart of Nashville, every website, and everyone I talked to told me that this is a must visit. So there was no doubt that this was gonna be the first place we went  out to on our first night in town. Because this place is pretty packed it doesn't seem as big as it really is.  But there are like 3 floors of bars, stages and people singing everywhere. In fact thier even singing on top of the bars. The live music here is the star, its pretty much everywhere. This place is is deff a tourist trap, but not one you will regret. If you can get a table or space to sit at the bar its a good time. Not one of my fav places on broadway but deff set the tone for the weekend.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Went to see the Urban Pioneers and the stage, acoustics and venue were awesome. 

I ordered a brisket horseshoe and got about 70% fat on a piece of white bread covered with fries and some kind of cream sauce. I think the idea was to hide that there was really no meat. It was the most disgusting thing I have ever tried to eat. 

They should really not serve food.

Also how can you charge $16 for what is basically an appetizer? This should have been less than $10. Probably about $2 of food. 

The music was great and the setting was awesome. My suggestion is to eat before you go to the Sutler.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We made a point to stop in here over the weekend, glad we did - very cool place! It was super crowded when we arrived, but following advice from other Yelper's we made our way upstairs. Much less crowded and a great band playing! If I had it to do again I'd go earlier in the day to have a better opportunity to look around and hang out without the crowds.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
There's a bouncer at the door checking ID, ensuring that you are 21. Friday & Saturday nights are the most popular and it's wall to wall inside. ....just like walking on the street. 

Seems like the music is pop rock as all the 21 year old girls in the audience know the words and sing along with the band.

The norm is no cover,  and beets are about $5. Male sure you tip the band when they pass their Buckley around!

Always a fun time, and you might actually hear some good music.

name: Riverfront Park
text:
I went here last night for Americanarama (a concert featuring Wilco and Bob Dylan among others).  My husband and I are too old (and I'm too short) to stand body to body with a lot of people with BO, so we opted for the only seated area, on a hill at the back of the venue.  It was a pretty terrible experience.  The biggest problem was WE COULDN'T HEAR THE MUSIC.  The stage was probably a third of a mile away and the speakers were not powerful enough to get the music back there.  They also had an ice cream stand with a huge, loud generator right at the base of the hill of the seated area, which further drowned out the music.  And we couldn't see a thing.  It might as well have been ants performing.  

Add to this that they don't allow you to bring chairs or coolers or umbrellas (confiscated at the gate) and it made for a pretty cruddy experience.  I won't be back.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: My favorite bar in Nashville! Hate to see it have less than 5 stars.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Had a great time here. Their were so many different places to choose from, this one was packed but has 3 floors with 3 different performers. So don't let the crowd in the door steer you way. Go in and go up to one of the other floors. Kayla Woodson was performing she was amazing. Good times!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: DO NOT GO TO THIS BAR!!!! I was charged $20,000. Yes, twenty THOUSAND dollars and they will not answer nor do they have an answering machine so there is no way to get in contact with them which is by far the worst management I've ever experienced.  If there were negative stars, they'd get 5.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Wife and I dropped in on Saturday to listen to music and have a couple drinks.  The guy checking IDs was very nice and professional. However, the hostess was the most dismissive and rude person I can remember encountering front of house.  She literally swiped me away with her hand to get to the person behind me.  The drinks were fine, nothing special.  The music, and really the reason we were there, was great.  Although the sound guy in the back had an old plate of food hanging out by him, which was a little nasty.

With so many music venus in town, and many known for world class customer experience, we probably won't be back.  Not bad for a quick visit after dinner at cinema though!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Went here with a group of 8 for bunch. Food was heavy but delicious. I enjoyed the chicken and biscuits. Coming from the south, the white gravy did not disappoint. Live music was playing and the service was great. Bottomless mimosas were a hit with the group.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: 5 stars for entertainment but 2 for food, it's all about the show!! Was very good and it's a small venue so not a lot of people. We waited in line for 3 hours because we didn't have reservations. Definitely worth the wait

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I was looking forward to visiting this establishment for quite some time having heard it talked up and advertised on local radio. Unfortunately, I was sorely disappointed. To start, the cheese curds are not cheese curds at all - they are mozzarella balls jazzed up with sauces. The dish itself was perfectly fine, but please don't call them cheese curds. I had the pulled pork sandwich and there was hardly any pork on it at all and the bun was just a regular old bun, nothing fresh or baked in house. The sweet potato fries were limp, cold, and lifeless. The coleslaw was... coleslaw. And I had ordered a side of their mac and cheese. Nothing life changing but just fine. My cocktail was good, but the whole experience was marred by the lackluster food and surly attitude from our waitress who even tried to remove my plate as I was still eating off of it. Honestly, I would save your money and pick up some quality BBQ at better local restaurants. This is for tourists who don't know any better and as a local I would not recommend it.

name: Tin Roof
text: Didn't do dinner just drinks and for music.   Atmosphere and decor is awesome.  Band the night we were there was awesome!  Recommend!!!!

name: Tin Roof
text: Looks like a local dive bar. Basic bar food but with a little twist. I had the pizzadilla and it was great. Spicy with the added jalapeños. Craft beer was only $4. Staff was friendly and attentive. Friends had chicken tenders with a honey buffalo sauce and it was great! Def a cool spot to have a beer and quick bite.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Pricy drinks, talented bands playing covers of crappy 80s songs and modern country. Was hoping to see some cool original stuff- found out you have to get off Broadway for that!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Met up with friends to enjoy a nice evening. The food was good and the specialty drinks were enjoyable as well.
The fried chicken was good as were the short ribs. The stand out was the BBQ ribs. Service was good. We had reservations and were promptly seated. Afterwards you can go downstairs to enjoy live music and dancing
It would have received 5 stars, buy the dining room is pretty loud for conversation.
All in all, you should give it a try.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Sat for 15 minutes without even being acknowledged. If you can't handle the amount of people on a Saturday night, hire more servers or train your people.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Very cool classic Nashville bar.  I've been here about 10x because all of my visitors consider this a "must do".  It's always too packed and difficult to get a drink. 
The employees are not very knowledgeable.  One employee checked my friends ID and let him in.  He told the guy he was going to stand by the door because he was waiting for his wife.  While he stood there the bouncer changed his mind and told him that he could no longer go in because his shirt didn't have sleeves.  In 100 degree downtown Nashville.  Nice.  
It's fine if you want to have rules, but don't let someone in and then change your mind. 
It's unfortunate because they always have fabulous performers.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
A dive may describe the atmosphere but the food drink and staff were excellent
Music was good for a Wednesday afternoon

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I'll never go back to this place.  They're so disorganized they don't have a system in place for their 'first come first serve ' night.  Stood in line in 100 degree weather for an hour and a half and didn't get in.  This after the little punk running the door said he counted and said it was fine.  Guess those people I saw just walk up and be let in took our spots.  Oh..but the 'good news' was we were first in line for the next show....2 hours later!!  Ever thought of utilizing the deli ticket method morons so people will know if they're getting in and don't have to risk heat stroke?

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Just because your closing doesn't mean you don't give a F.   Hard work will get you a good job of you make an effort!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Unbeatable intimate setting. It absolutely doesn't matter if you are familiar with the performers.  It will be an amazing experience that any true music lover will treasure for a lifetime.  Gary Burr & Georgia Middleman had me laughing & crying.  Their song writing skills & delivery are amazing so I was a little disappointed when they announced that they were bringing their friend Kenny on stage.  I was so enjoying them that I didn't want the vibe to change.  Their "friend" stepped up from a nearby table to play a few tunes with them.  "Kenny" turned out to be Kenny Loggins.  You absolutely never know who you'll see at the Bluebird Cafe.  Just go.  Reviews on food & service are completely unnecessary.  It just doesn't matter how good either of those things are.  You're there for a musical experience like no other.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Great food, drinks, service. Creative southern based menu with a strong well thought and creative culinary influence. This is a must go place.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Was recommended as this bar has been around for a very long time. Faded photos of stars cover the walls. We walked in off the alley and found seats on a Saturday at lunch. This was CMA weekend. The bar was comfortably crowded. The band played. We learned that the band get to play for one hour, then a different band sets up and plays. We ordered from the simple menu--pulled pork sandwich and fries--very good, delicious chili, and pimento corn fritters--hot and crunchy, but there was no green tomato jam served. I couldn't get the waitress's attention. That jam would have been good. The beer list was extensive, but there were no stouts. As we left we realized that we were on the middle floor. A stairway led to the third floor. We walked down steps and left through the front door which was the first floor. That room was smaller and a band was playing. This is a three-floor hole-in-the-wall bar, and popular with the music scene.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Worth waiting in the cold!!! This is a must while in Nashville!!! So intimate and priceless to be in a room listening to such talented people!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Good food, nice atmosphere.  Worth a visit for sure.  The fries are awesome!  If in Nashville you must come and sit at the counter where it all happened.  You get to eat and experience history.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Can I give it a minus 1 star? 
The hostess was extremely rude. I have never experienced someone at the front of the house treating not only only us ( but another group who was next to us) so poorly and disrespectfully - HUGE ATTITUDE! The message was "go away we don't want your business" ... said in so many words. Management alert !! Train your people! Regardless of how packed you are today, your success tomorrow is not promised!  I was shocked and disappointed at how we were treated. We traveled from California to attend. I am in the entertainment business and no one in our town would get away with treating guests like this and still have a job. I unfortunately don't have the hostesses name but if your interested in following up we attempted to attend Friday July 12th late show. She could have cordially explained the way it "works" there and invited us back another time. Just saying... :-( Maybe put a sign up on the door after your full ?) There are simple solutions to avoid uncomfortable situations in the future.

name: Tin Roof
text:
Came here for the first time tonight, my friends wanted to smoke a cigarette so we started to walk to the patio and there was a barricade saying that section was closed. We asked the doorman where we could go and still have our drink in our hand without having to go out the front(without our drinks). He said we could go past the barricade to smoke. As soon as we walk past the bait cafe one of the bartenders said we couldn't do that, we said sorry but the door man said we could to smoke... he said OK no problem. As soon as we got to the door another long haired bouncer came out cussing and saying "are y'all FUC*ING stupid or can  you not read??"
Then preceded to come out and grab our drinks and thrown them in the trash because we did not appreciate being cussed out as PAYING CUSTOMERS. Will NEVER COME back here.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Woolworth used to be so delicious. However, the recent menu changes and assumed recipe changes were obvious to our table of locals. The pancakes tasted microwaved instead of straight from the griddle and there were brunch items we just could not find on the menu. We asked if anything was different and it was confirmed that the restaurant had gone through a few changes. I feel like tourists will love anything, but it's disappointing when most of my local friends have stopped coming here as the food is just NOT the same. It's even more sad considering the historical relevance of the location. I would hate for this restaurant to go the way of so many places that have a short life span in this city due to tourists moving on to the next "hot spot in Nashville." Just a heads up, the locals do not like these changes. When suggested I'm often met with "they're just not good anymore."

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I found the bar on yelp seems to me is a popular local place. There are two set of artist playing in the bar..i don't know the artist but enjoy the atmosphere.. it's loud but lovely..

name: Tin Roof
text:
My kind of bar. It's where the locals go. I have my favorites back home in Los Angeles and San Diego. Tinroof reminded me of home. They have live entertainment on most nights it seems. 
Most of the staff greets you with a sweet smile, i'd like to say the others were probably just too busy working  
The drinks are yummmy and the queso fries were pretty tasty   
When in Nashville you have many options as far as the nightlife, entertainment bar life go...I'd definitely check this one out!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This place is authentic and definitely not fancy. Great musicians make this place the best Honky-Tonk in Nashville. The bartenders are great too.  Hey when you look up Honky-tonk, this place is used as an example. Seriously, its painted a pinkish purple color on the outside. (only the outside..thank God) look it up. 

Bottom line, you go there for the music. 
Many Greats have performed here, Legends have been discovered here, and tomorrows Legends just may be performing there tonight.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The food is terrible. Chef can't even cook an egg. The drinks suck too but at least the mimosas are bottomless if you get drunk enough anything is edible right?

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
This is a pretty great brunch place!! This was another great recommendation we received on our trip. He cautioned, you will need to wait at least an hour. Come prepared to wait. They do not take call ahead sir reservations. 

Once you put your name in you can look to see how long you've waited and how many more parties are a head of you. 

They had some pretty good deals, such as bottomless mimosas. This is especially great if you are waiting. You can eat at the bar, but it is crowded so be aware. 

The food was great. I recommend anything with their biscuits!!!  The food came out surprisingly fast as well. I felt like we ordered, blinked our eyes, and the food was out. 

The bluegrass music they have playing is probably one of the biggest draws. It was so relaxing to listen to live bluegrass while eating. The restaurant itself had such a nice vibe to it. I can't wait to go back on another trip!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Great burger and fries served within five minutes during busy Saturday night. We had just left Rock Bottom restaurant after waiting an hour and not getting order

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
This is the best restaurant in Nashville! The barbecue sauce is to die for! For reference, I do not like bbq sauce but what they have is completely different, a much lighter and liquidy sauce. Everything was cooked expertly. Probably the best breakfast/brunch I will ever have in my life. Our waitress topped the experience off with great service. 

Corn cakes: So good and filling. The bacon on top had something on it (jalapeño according to the menu) that gave it that extra crispy oomph. And just like bbq sauce, I don't like bacon either! All the elements - perfectly poached eggs, pesto on top of the corn cakes worked harmoniously together like a love song for my tastebuds. 

Corned beef hash: This dish had the bbq sauce! The beef was so tender, it was like pulled pork. I wish the corn muffin was bigger because we were fighting each other to get more of it. 

Sweet potato pancakes: Very tasty and cooked just right. The maple syrup was exceptional, not too sweet. I would ask for a different side because the bacon was the weakest link out of the whole meal. 

This is a must try that I always recommend to anyone I know who may be travelling to the States! If you appreciate good food, customer service like it should be done and history then do visit! I want to go back...

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I'm so happy we decided to eat here for brunch. The food was delicious. Our server Kim was outstanding. She was pleasant and made our experience 5 star. Kim was friendly, knowledgeable of the menu, and had a smile from beginning to end. I highly recommend this restaurant.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: The atmosphere is fun, open floor plan and the historical nods are present everywhere, from the music to the decorum. I really enjoyed the projection of classic movie and music clips on the wall above the kitchen that can clearly be seen from anywhere. The hostess was exuberant, funny, and knowledgeable, but my server wasn't as personable. She seemed a bit overwhelmed. The food...was fantastic. I had the shrimp Po Boy and a refreshing cocktail. The best Po Boy I ever had. Will definitely be returning soon!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: We went here on Wednesday night to the 6 o'clock show. All reviews and word of mouth really built it up. It was a great time. The drinks were a little on the weak side but that's the way they are at a bar. We also split an order of nachos and they were fantastic!! A pleasant surprise!!!They also had nice big napkins, very absorbent. The show we saw was "In the round" and the main guy was Lucas Hoge with three other guys who have wrote songs with him , Eddie Killgallon( from the 90's band Ricochet), Drew Powell ( it was his first time playing at the BlueBird Cafe), and JD Wood. They played lots of real good songs some we recognized and some were brand new. We had a really great time and would definitely go back!!!! I gave it 4 stars because the young guy at the register where they sold T-Shirts at the end of the show was an A$$Hole with ATTITUDE. That is not the way you want to end the experience. Kind of a bummer. I hope the Blue Bird reads this but they probably won't  and probably don't care because this is a gold mine for them  that people everywhere want to experience. If you like both kinds of music Country and Western you gotta go. I highly recommend it.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
I traveled to Nashville and this is the one spot I wanted to spend my birthday at. Tickets sold out online super quick so we decided to go and wait outside in hopes of getting it. I was super excited and got the chance to go in.

This place is a cute cafe that caught my eye when watching the show Nashville. Seating was good because anywhere you sit you can see the stage. They also have drinks and food where the waiter/waitress come around to you. Drinks came out quick and food was good. 

I loved watching all the people go up on stage and perform there own songs they have written and really liked the positivity in this cute place. Staff and owners are super friendly and genuinely love there jobs.

Perfect place to enjoy great music where a lot of the top
Notch artist have performed at! This place is a must when traveling or living nearby!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: The filet steak is AMAZING! I will definitely be back to enjoy it again. Also, Jordan and Sam were amazing bartenders. They helped out with our large party and made sure we were taken care of at all time. They were kind and attentive. Definitely go see them and try the steak if you have the opportunity.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
My mother is a history buff person. So coming here was on her list of things to do. 

I am not always comfortable talking about things that have to do with the segregation or desegregation between people. 

The reason I'm giving this place a 5 is because of the extremely cool lady who was our waitress. She had the most beautiful name (Zakira) and was really friendly! 

I know I can be a weirdo but she was cool with it and even told us how her mother came to naming her. Which was also a really sweet story. 

So thank you for your kindness and letting me add your name to my 'baby name list' (even though I'm 75% sure I'm not going to have kids-LOL)!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Very crowded for it's size (it's huge), and kind of dirty. But it's Nash-Vegas, can't really expect perfection. Come here just to get drunk and hear some good live music. It's one of the first bars you'll notice when you get to Broadway.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
This place is soo trailer park that it lives up to it's name! Lol I gotta say though the food is good and it's the best for your 2am munchies! Tater tots a must! Sliders a plus! The music isn't so bad!!
Very eclectic place! Where u can see the Xmas tree made of green colored tires! And AstroTurf with rocking chairs!
The set up could be better to listen to the music near the band!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsies was everything they said it would be and more! We had a blast! The musical talent on stage was top notch. They really owned the crowd. Our servers were amazing they literally ran back and forth hustling us drinks and were super gracious and it didn't hurt that they were gorgeous. The only thing Tootsies could improve on is their bathroom situation. Everything else has me looking forward to going back next time I'm in Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: You can drink beer and listen to music all day here.  What else could you ask for?  Beers are reasonably priced and music is great!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great bar and have had a blast here but the band playing right now is not as awesome as they think they are. Refused to take a request for less than a 20.00 tip. Not that talented. Playing Sunday around 7:00.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: WARNING!!! If you think you really are in the que to get tickets, you're fooled!  So is everybody else!  In the matter of seconds, the seats were disappearing before I could even hit proceed.  I have been waiting for months for the day to purchase tickets and NOTHING! YOUR SYSTEM SUCKS!!!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Yes, it's real. And yes, it's as good as the hype. If you're lucky enough to secure a seat, GO!

Did not have food, but the music was outstanding. And why people, I'm looking at you, 50 year old women in front of me, can't follow the "no cell phone use" rule during the show is beyond me. Really? You're THAT important that you can't go 90 minutes without checking your texts?? I was "this close" to ratting them out to Don Schlitz!

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text: This is a beautiful venue. It wasn't as large as I was expecting which was a pleasant surprise. There are food trucks and beer vendors but make sure you bring cash! Parking is free but it's field parking so try to beat the rush at the end of the night if you can.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Bar, music, good service. Just as overpriced as the rest of the bars on the strip. Turns out this place has some history, they didn't mention that at midnight on a Saturday. Anyhow, service was great for the bachelor party I went down with. Cool joint, definitely been there a while and has the scars on the building to prove it. This was my favorite joint I went to.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Yes, it's real. And yes, it's as good as the hype. If you're lucky enough to secure a seat, GO!!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This really is the place to come on Broadway. There were 3 separate stages, no wonder there was so much good music. I liked hanging around the second stage on the second level until I got up to the third level and saw that band. They were awesome and singing all the latest country hits which I really appreciate seeing as I'm newish to country music. 

The drinks were average price compared to the rest of the bars on the block too.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
This place has great history around civil rights era. We walked in and felt we went back in time. Sat at the counter and ordered breakfast. I had a biscuit with gravy and a fried egg.  The biscuit was different - not your typical white floured biscuit but it was light brown and fluffy, not heavy or dense. I wonder if folks here are judged by their biscuits?  . Needless to say, it was very very good!  Husband had corned beef hash that was great - nothing we ever had in Boston.  This hash had chunks of corned beef, caramelized onions, crunchy potatoes and black eyed peas. Northeast corned beef is more like consistency of canned dog food - odd. 

The waitress, Kara was so kind and sweet. We chatted about foods from the South and foods from the Northeast. We clued her in on korean fried chicken. She laughed when I told her I struggled with really good homemade fried chicken. She was adorable!

I would go back again in a heartbeat

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I keep coming back to the Sutler for the mimosas, the music, and the service. Cat is a great server who always makes our girls brunch dates so special. They are updating the menu and the additions are FIRE. The sutler is here to stay and has wormed its way into my heart forever.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Food was great, drinks were good. Loved hanging out here. Our server was the best part, though! Super nice and helpful. I think her name was jordon?

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: We had diner there which was very good. service was also good. It has a nice atmosphere and a long bar with many barstools.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: My trip to Nashville was a therapeutic one. The past year was riddled with deaths, terminal illnesses and the end of a 20-year-marriage. I came to create new, positive memories. The Bluebird visit was a sentimental one. I attended the charity event show on Tuesday 1/22. The show was fantastic. I was not disappointed with the music or merchandise. I was, however, extremely disheartened by what happened after the show. I dropped my wallet near my seat and when the waitress brought it to me (at the merch table) I realized $1000 had been removed. The thief left a $20 bill inside. The waitress became defensive and was unempathetic. I spoke with the manager/bartender who was rude, condescending and unapologetic. He did call the police for me but refused to give a statement or have any involvement in trying to rectify this situation. He stated that the Bluebird has no cameras in the venue and I was just out of luck. It was really disappointing and created a terrible memory for me. My takeaway from this is patronize this establishment at your own risk. The talent is phenomenal but the employees just might have sticky fingers. This was an expensive night at the Bluebird and a lesson in human nature and greed.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Visiting Tootsie's was one of my top bucket list items when visiting Nashville and to be honest it fell short. Maybe we went at the wrong time of day (Sunday, Memorial weekend) but it was just not what I expected. We were promptly served on the first level, which was nice, and bee-lined it upstairs where the vibes matched that of a standard corner bar, with less charm. The band was mediocre at best and reminded me of bad karaoke. I guess I just envisioned much more from this Nashville icon.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: What a fun brunch!! Live bluegrass, bottomless mimosas for 17$, amazing brunch options, and fast service!!! Loved the brisket hash, but my favorite was the shrimp and grits with the Cajun creme! The monkey bread is a MUST! Great coffee too!! Would definitely come here again on a trip to Nashville!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Nicole was a great waitress! She took care of our whole party (over 10 people!) and made sure we had an amazing time. We did the bottomless mimosas and she always made sure our glasses were full. We loved getting to know her!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Great Happy Hour! You can get a craft cocktail for 5$ and experience live music. It has three different environments. Upstairs there's a typical Nashville bar/restaurant atmosphere. There's also a patio outside. Downstairs, there's a wannabe speak easy downstairs, it's a speak easy decor with modern music. Downstairs, there's also a billiard room with a ton of pool tables. There weren't as many people in general as I thought there would be, but it started picking up after happy hour. It was quick service and they were very friendly as well! There's also a parking lot which is a plus!

name: Tin Roof
text: I called then at 11am Sunday  8/27/17 talked to this rude bartender on the phone. I asked for the owners number because I wanted to let him know I am calling the health dept on there San Diego location but this idiot says why are you calling me on a Sunday to complain to me about a issue with are San Diego location insaid can I speak to a supervisor non there manger non there I asked for his name won't give it he needs to be fired

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Love this place! The music and bartenders are fantastic lots of fun. We had no problem ordering a drink the bartenders practically flag you down as you walk in and made our drinks fast. All of the performers were engaging and so much fun. It was neat to see all of the old photos of celebrities on the walls.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
"Doors open at 5:30pm" but if you don't have a reservation, you will be waiting another hour at least before all the resos swagger in (we didn't have a reso, and got in at 6:45pm after music started). Actually you may be waiting for 2 hours in the walk up line and not even get in the building. This information was not communicated well enough I thought. 

Also, the doors didn't open at 5:30pm. They opened at 6pm because everyone had to wait for the bartender to show up before people could go in.

The music was quality. The food was decent, but I won't be back again unless I'm hired to play :P

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: My husband and I would not describe ourselves as country music fans, but everyone we know urged us to check out the bluebird when they heard we were visiting Nashville. We reserved tickets online in advance and went in with an open mind. We knew nothing about the singer/songwriters when we got there but left feeling like we knew them. The place is very casual and intimate, and the songs and stories were beautiful. The only downside for me was a few songs were really sad and I lost my dad recently - I didn't see them coming (should have, its country music, lol) and I was a bit blubbery and embarrassed toward the end. Definitely evoked a lot of emotion, which is great when you're not so sensitive! Looking forward to going again, prepared with tissues in my purse next time!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Excellent place for late night food you won't feel guilty about it because you won't remember it. Burgers and cheese fries are sooo good. Live music nightly, like everywhere else in Nashville, and a fun vibe throughout. The place is danky but huge, plenty of room to hang out with friends and sober up while you wait for an Uber. I definitely recommend this place.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Went to Woolworths before a show at TPAC. I called ahead of time to make sure I didn't need a reservation to sit at the bar and have a drink. When I arrived it was packed- that's a great sign! Then I sat down at the bar. It took almost 15 minutes for anyone to come and take my drink order much less just drop a water to me. I've worked as a bartender and I know they were busy- but it almost felt like they were avoiding me.
The bartender was extremely rude to the couple next to me- I get it- busy night, lots going on. But there's really no excuse. Perhaps Woolworth should add more bartenders? Not sure. The fried green tomatoes were great. However, it's not good enough for me to return any time soon.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Did not care for the music being played in this establishment. Too new country for me. Packed with bras hanging over by the bar area. 
Alot has changed since Patsy Cline used to go in here and just chill after the Opry, only reason i went in. I walked straight through to the back and walked out to the ally.
People push you, bump into you. 
Dodn't care for it.
I know its World famous but, I didn't like it.
To loud. Too busy. New country music. Young performers.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I gather this place is historical? I don't know the history but this must be why the place was so jam-packed.  We could hardly get in the door or even enjoy the other floors.  Upon opening the front door we were greeted by an overwhelming "toilet" smell.  Not pleasant.  We fought our way through the crowd and made it all the way up to the rooftop.  None of the floors caught our attention and the vibe just wasn't working for us.  We stayed for only a short while.  Out of all the bars we stopped in on "honky tonk row," this was our least favorite.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: I really enjoyed my time at Paradise Park. It's a super electric bar with AstroTurf for flooring. I loved the live music playing during both of my visits as well as the smells coming from the kitchen. They serve a variety of food that I didn't try. There's plenty of space to roam about as the bar was not overly crowded. Buyer beware - This is by no means a classy spot for a date or romantic evening, but for a small group of tourists, this worked out just fine.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
I visited Nashville for Memorial Day Weekend and knew I had to pop by the Bluebird for Writers Night. Since Monday was a holiday, there was only one that weekend, and everyone had the idea to go early. I got to the Bluebird at 5:30 PM and was one of the last to make it in for the 8 PM show (even though during the initial count, I was #60 -- I think people saved a lot of spots for their friends to jump in later and the performers also had some guests). The wait was pretty long and hot, and there was no shade so bring a fan and parasol and something to do! I'm sure most nights aren't quite as bad.

That being said, the wait was worth it -- especially for 3.5 hours of music and stories. The Bluebird is truly a songwriter's venue. Steve Goodie was a hilarious host, setting the stage well and even performing the most hilarious song. All 8 or so performers were good singers... but truly amazing songwriters. I felt so many emotions that night from writers of diverse experiences, ages, and hometowns.

Just as I thought the show was over, they bring on a featured songwriter -- Don Schlitz! He was gracious enough to entertain us for hours with hilarious stories and songs he wrote, including "The Gambler," "Forever and Ever, Amen," "When You Say Nothing At All," "You Can't Make Old Friends," among others that the crowd sang along to together.

The inside is rather crowded, and I would strongly recommend against getting the garden salad (veggies were plain and chicken was nasty). I would gladly pay $7 and a couple hours of waiting for one of the most memorable musical experiences!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
It's very unusual that I like the food but don't like the restaurant. I try not to be a curmudgeon but sometimes it's warranted. I've been to the new Sutler twice. The first time I had the grilled cheese and tomato soup. It was wonderful. What wasn't wonderful was the hostess who looked down the length of her nose at me and made a face like she'd just stepped in something made by a dog. I had to get her talking just to see if she would actually insult me so I asked her if she'd ever been to the old Sutler to which she replied "No" with the attitude of "as if." I decided then and there that regardless of the food, I wouldn't give them anymore of my business.
Jump to New Years day, 2019. I considered my options, (price, selection, location, parking, etc,) for brunch and rested my hopes on my favorite all around brunch - Lana's Copper Kettle. No-go, not open. Then my thoughts turned to Fenwicks and their lovely sauerkraut corned beef hash - also not open which led me by proximity away from Sinema, (too fancy/dressy,) to the Sutler.
This time there were two hosts, one male & one female who also both regarded my presence with a fair amount of distain. I was eating alone, I'm not twenty-five anymore and apparently not sufficiently hip or cool enough to be greeted warmly. Whatever. I sat myself at the bar and had the Andouille hash. Pretty good. The bartender was nice as they usually are, (tip dependent.) 
As I ate I considered what bothered me about the place besides the cold welcome and I narrowed it down. I knew the old Sutler, I wasn't a regular but I ate there infrequently and saw a few excellent shows, (Victor Wooten solo no less.) It was a dark, comfortable place even as a brooding portrait of Nathan Bedford Forrest glowered over everyone from above the bar. They welcomed business AND working folk, young and old alike.
The new Sutler is a Disney-fied version for the young & hip crowd that offers a carefully crafted veneer of Southern sans the hospitality. When you've been on a pirate ship then ride the Pirates of the Caribbean you feel more than a little cheated. The wait staff all contrived in flannel and jeans, yee-haw y'all. Nothing sours a southerners mouth like a disingenuous pantomime of ourselves. I'd bet a thousand dollars not one person in the bar could guess what a sutler was or more to the point would even care. It's pretty good food but it's an insult to the memory of the real thing, a genuinely comfortable neighborhood bar. Gone but not forgotten.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This is a really fun place to visit with numerous options for listening to bands, one on each floor. It is well known of course, and it is worth visiting. I only got a coke with the intent of listening and we enjoyed our time there. It was busy, but because of the multiple levels and listening choices, we felt that there was lots of room for lots of people.
They have a selection of clothing products, mostly shirts, Ts and sweatshirts. My wife found one she liked and the price was fair.
Overall, I would encourage my friends to try it.
It is not a family venue. It is a bar! But if you like music, I don't think you can go wrong. There are many choices in the area and we felt it was worth our investment of time.

name: SongBird Tours
text: What an awesome tour! So unique and wonderful to get a feel for the culture that Nashville offers. You get to ride around in a bus and listen to talented famous song writers that have had several top chart hits sung by several big names right on the bus with you sharing their uncut songs, their stories and their passion for music. The beautiful lyrics written, the passion and the authentic Tennessee feel was nothing short of wonderful on this ride. We were able to listen to unbelievably creative lyrics sung by Trey Bruce & Paul Jefferson. Their voices were a wonderful as their raw lyrics and it brought extra touch of uniqueness to the tour. They had some wonderful stories and knew a ton about the music industry. On the ride we were able to see famous locations where the stars began recording, cutting and writing their music. We got to hear how songwriters are so supportive throughout the industry and lift one another up, which was inspiring to hear and see. Most importantly they shared their passion and life for music, which was contagious and a privileged to be in the presence of two incredible artists. Our guide (Miss. Jenna Renae) was not only funny, beautiful and entertaining but she had a beautiful voice that blended so well with Trey & Paul. In a world where country songs on the radio all sound similar with the same tune, this tour brought light to original country music writing. Would highly recommend this tour to anyone looking to understand the roots of Nashville and support the beautiful life and passion that the music city offers.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
This review is not a reflection of the amazing performers that we saw at bluebird. The musicians were absolutely phenomenal and I don't even love country music- they were soulful and had wonderful voices! I am in awe of their talent and being so close to them was really cool! Musicians get a solid 5 out of 5. 

This from start to finish gets a solid two or three would be too generous. To begin with the ticket process is as people say another reviews completely annoying. You logon before 8 AM and are in this online queue- that randomizes people at 8 AM and hopefully you get in to buy a ticket but you only have a minute so get your credit card ready.  So you're better off just trying a bunch of dates and hoping for the best!

So we went to a 6 PM show on Thursday night. We arrived at 5:30 PM parking is impossible and you are likely to get towed if you park illegally in someone's life. When you walk up there is a line of people waiting to get in if people don't show up and if you have a reservation you can go in and hostess would check your name on the list. This is where it gets a little aggressive the hostess has an impossible job I do believe that her job is very difficult to try and get as many people in as possible while also Keeping to code regulations etc. I think that bluebird may need to take a page out of Starbucks book and revisit their customer service policies and invest in some training for their staff. So yes take this with a grain of salt this is a stressful situation for the staff they only have a small amount of time to get people's orders before the show starts etc. but with two shows at night every night of the week you think they'd have a better system down. Our waitress downright seemed annoyed by our existence she was short with us and disinterested. She would be halfway across the room before I could answer for ask for one more drink. 

Food: you come here for the music not for the food. My husbands "Nashville dip" sandwich was fine and nothing he would write home about- we ordered chips and salsa as well - chips were cold and stale and salsa was ok but kind of tasted like a cold soup. I then had the caprese salad which was acceptable. I had two drinks he had one and we had an app and two entrees all said and done it was $63. Not bad but not great for meh food. 

The pineapple cider was legit- I loved that!

All of this to say you're cramped in with people you don't know it's a little warm- the staff is rushing around- it's all kind of a mess to be honest. That said it's an hour and a half show and you're on your way- cool experience if nothing else.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: For me this place rocks country! Three levels of bands and bars (a different band on each level). The roof top is a nice view of Broadway and downtown Nashville ... Fun to relax and enjoy some loud country music!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsie's is historic, so I made sure I went by.  After a couple of​ days all of these places somewhat blend together.  No complaints.  Neat place.  Upstairs was great.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: So. Very. Crowded. Do yourself a favor and get to the rooftop as soon as you can...for air! Music was good, drinks were quick, but overall not for those wanting to relax and enjoy anything other than pushing crowds and drink slamming.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Colleen told me to say she is a great server and I did because she is

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
We went here for a friends birthday dinner and it was the worst dining experience I have ever had. First of all we had a large party, so we made a reservation. After waiting for almost an hour after our reservation time we were seated at a large booth. They had placed 13 table settings around the booth. There was absolutely no way 13 people could fit even sitting shoulder to shoulder. After being told, very rudely, that they were trying to find stools for us but there were none. Someone from our party went to the bar and took stools from people who were leaving and brought them over. 

The manager offered to comp appetizers since we waited so long even though we had a reservation. Which seemed nice at the time, but doesn't make up for the rest of the experience. 

Next, after the food finally came out one girl was missing her food. My sandwich and soup came out ice cold and I had to ask for it to be heated again. 

When it came time to pay the checks, not only did they not split them correctly (one guy had to pay for all of our bottles of wine we ordered for the whole table), but the waitress actually yelled at the person who's birthday it was. Apparently there was a HUGE misunderstanding with what he said and she was very insulted. But there is absolutely no reason to ever yell or be rude to a customer, and he didn't even mean anything rude at all!

I had had it at that point and went and to speak to the manger. She said she was thankful I spoke up and she would go do something and she disappeared. But I don't think she ever actually did anything and my friend wasn't apologized to for being yelled at.

Like I said this was the worst dining experience I have ever had. All of the staff were rude and acted like they were better than everyone else except for one woman. I would not recommend this place to anyone.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Definitely not worth the hype.  Worst Management and Customer Service I have seen. 

On a Sunday, my 3 friends and I arrived at 5:40 and waited in line for the 8:00 show.  When we arrived, the staff assured my friends and I and several people behind us that we would definitely make it into the show.  On numerous times, the staff came out to assure my friends and people behind us that we would definitely make the show.  Their assurances were the reason why we took the time to wait for the show.  However, once it came time to get into the show, and after over a 2 hr wait, that was not the case.  The "bouncer" told us that only 1 person could get in from our group because they "ran out of seating."  We were the first group to get turned away.  

Suggestion: why not give everyone in line a ticket so people do not have to mindlessly wait?!  There were so many people who did not wait in line but still got through the door.  

The "bounder" told us that he could let us in to take pictures and purchase merchandise.  So we waited.  From the door, we could hear the stand-up comedian.  I'm sorry, but isn't the Bluebird Cafe known for its music and not comedy?!  When the first act started, we could hear the music from the door the music was anti-climatic.  We were not impressed.  That's why we decided to not stick around even though we could hear the music outside the door.   

After talking to my uber and lyft drivers about the Bluebird Cafe, they were not excited about the experience, I should have been warned about the experience.  They specifically said that Bluebird Cafe was only hyped up due to the show, but it's not worth the wait.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Loud and fun. Crowded in its peak times and a blast. Terrific live music. I couldn't do it every night, but love to go on occasion.

name: The Valentine
text: The rooftop bar served food which was nice. The bartender was friendly. Totchos were really yummy. The chicken was hand battered and yummy, but the fryer oil needed to be changed for sure.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Came in on a whim, and I'm so glad I did. Bartenders were friendly, band was great. Great energy, even in the middle of the week.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The staff was so very helpful.  The rooms were clean.  The courtyard with the pool was amazing.  While it is not located downtown the hotel offered a shuttle called the Monarch for $10 round trip.  The breakfast buffet was ok, nothing special.

name: FooBar
text: I went there on a Tuesday night and the band was slammin'.  I paid $7 for a Jack Daniels neat. I like that there's actually parking in the back too. Check it out!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The stage was super fun! They had a great band when I was there I believe his name was Jerry Jacobs. It was one of the best nights of my life and the crowd was very friendly. What a legendary place.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Stopped here during a tour of the city. First time I've had moonshine. I had the blue raspberry and lemonade concoction which was delicious :) Good environment, live music, friendly bartenders.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
We always love playing at the 5 Spot on our tours through Nashville. Great stage & sound. Come see us on August 16th, 2016!
Watch our music video here:
https://youtu.be/X01MtEiuNP8

Whitherward
www.whitherward.com

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Cool place. Really big, insanely crowded when I went on a Saturday night around 11pm. There was a band playing country covers. They were good. They only have bottled beer, no drafts. Not sure if I would come back, just because it was SO crowded. We went upstairs and it took a long time to make our way through the crowd.

name: East-Centric Pavilion
text: It's a nice venue.  We were there for Yum East, and it was packed with people.  The only complaint was the lack of parking.  And having a few benches for seating would have been a nice touch.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: I usually don't post reviews on here but I am very upset with this hotel.  The AC in our room is not working and the temperature is extremely hot. We had to have someone come assist in the middle of the night and he just in fact confirmed it was not working.  I called the front desk again and I was basically told just to deal with it.  I was very nice to the front desk associate but she did not provide me any sort of resolution or understanding. I will be speaking to a manager as this could have been handled with much more professionalism!!! I am now stuck attempting to sleep in an extremely hot room that we paid a lot of money for.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Good music, good prices on drinks and a good crowd.  Went here 3 nights in a row. Not a meat market.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
Only in Nashville can you hear someone you would pay to see at the 5 Spot. You want the WOW factor. It's only Tuesday and this first band is absolutely crazy. What a great place, good beer, and outstanding music. I will post band info soon.

Alright so YouTube Daniel Nicholls. She was great.

name: The 5 Spot
text: My favorite bar. That's all I got to say man. They put on great shows and the Country and Western Wednesday is a perfect night out in east end.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: I found this hotel and and the staff to be extremely pleasant.  For a family get together, we had a total of 5 rooms over the course of 4 nights. We were on the club level, which was so nice. We had access to the lounge 24/7 so we took advantage of that as much as possible.  Even when there wasn't free appetizers being served, we used the space to gather and order pizza.  The weather was great, so we also spent a lot of time out by the pool.  Staff members that stood out: Kendra, Ballin and Tessa at front desk as well as Terrell in the club lounge. These employees went above and beyond to make sure we had a great experience.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: They serve local beer and whiskey, and most importantly, great music. I love the fruity whiskey and the vibe so much!!! That was really a relaxing and unforgettable night. There were a fantastic band with two singers, one male and one female. We are all fans of country music now!!!

name: The 5 Spot
text:
Popped in here for a drink and to check out the band. This is not a country bar. The band was a little rock a little blues. They were great. The crowd was really into them. 

It was a full house. They have a nice long bar but there wasn't a ton of access since the room was crowded. Be patient. You'll get there. They have a really nice patio out back that wraps around the building. Nice and quiet for chatting compared to inside. 

Definitely worth checking out.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
Low key. The band was rude even though we were the ONLY people in the place. I thought the moonshine really wasn't that good. 

Yes it is a small place. Yes it isn't as full as some of the other bars. The staff was friendly. I'd probably go back if I was a local and wanted to be in a place that wasn't full and listen to decent live music, which I hear there are not many in Nashville (haha).

As a tourist, someone who came in to Nashville for a couple of days and wanted to see and hear some music, skip it. I'll probably never go back.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: I have been to Judge Vs twice and both times the food is good. The smells from the sidewalk are very intising. The BBQ is good, service is mediocre. I think the sides items need some work.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
I came to the Stage twice during my trip to Nashville for a friend's 30th. First day, a Thursday, was fun and the music was good, but the crowd could have been better. It was low key & smaller that night, which I think is why certain people wouldn't take a hint. Also broken glass which never got cleaned up.
Saturday night on the other hand was a great time. It was surprisingly so too, because I'm actually easily claustrophobic and it was so packed you couldn't move without the whole crowd moving, but it didn't faze me at all. The crowd was all friendly and the music was great. I'm definitely going again next time I'm in Nashville.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: This was my favorite spot in Nashville. We were walking by, heard good music, and paused. The doorman told us he works Sunday afternoons just because the bad that plays is that good, so we went in for one drink and stayed for the whole set! The layout is open and comfortable, the Sunday afternoon staff and band are the best we experienced and it was overall just a great afternoon.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: The service was extremely slow. We waited almost 25 minutes to be sat at a table when there were over 15 tables free. Then we were placed on the second floor where we waited another 15 minutes to place a drink order. Over 45 minutes later our appetizers came out and we were missing one of the three (we were told it was sent to the wrong table by mistake). Another 15 minutes later the missing appetizer came out and was brought to the wrong table again before being brought to ours. Over all an extremely disappointing experience.

name: The 5 Spot
text: I've been here twice have been consistently blown away by the music I've heard here. A great place to hear original music (not Johnny Cash on a loop) that is NOT country. Great place to dance, drink, and have a good time.

name: The 5 Spot
text: We took an Uber to 3 Crows only to find out they weren't going to have live music so we walked up around the corner to The Five Spot.  Soon after entering the place, we got to hear a few songs for the cover before the band called it quits for the evening.  We enjoyed some beers and popcorn before giving up and leaving to find music elsewhere.  The bar itself felt quaint and quirky.  Our timing was just off to enjoy the full ambience.   They have both indoor and patio space available.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Best bar on Broadway! Angela - the hot blonde bartender is the best!!!! The bands are always entertaining and the music is always upbeat! Love this bar.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: We had a good time here! Came to Nashville, specifically Broadway, in search of great, live country music, which seemed hard to find on a Thursday night (shockingly!) but this place came through. They had great live bands on both levels and we really enjoyed it. Liked how they had a nice patio and a pretty big bar. Spent some time on the main level people watching over Broadway, they have nice windows for that if you enjoy a good crowd, ha! Overall a great experience!

name: The 5 Spot
text: Nice place and super fun when watching live music. Too bad the bartender was rude and paid us little to no attention!

name: The Valentine
text: Cool bar. Sooooo mannnny floooors! Kind of irritating that the bars on each floor do not communicate with each other so you have multiple open tabs but need to make sure you close out of them all! Great band and each floor has a different vibe for whatever you're into.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: 5 Star service from Meagan on Sunday , July 20th!! We felt like we were family sharing stories about Memphis and Nashville. Thanks for great conversation  and laughs!! Even came back for the excellent band after 3pm.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Nice place, very convenient to all Nashville locations.  We were in town to see Wicked with our oldest daughter

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This was my favorite place on the Broadway strip. The live band was so talented and they just threw you for a loop of dancing and laughing and overall great time. The place was spacious to dance and not feel crowded and the bartenders were nice and fast with service. I would love to cone back to this place again

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Best place we have been to in Nashville! Great service...GREAT music! And we have been here for a week.....

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Nice hotel. Be prepared to walk your ass off if you need ice bc the machines are sooooo far apart. 

That said, is a nice hotel. Cool pool in center of courtyard.

Jacuzzi is 24 hours in gym :)

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: As I'm not a huge country music fan, it was great to hear some rock'n'roll!  They also have a huge beverage selection including top shelf liquors. I would definitely recommend this to people looking for live music outside the normal honkytonk!

name: The Valentine
text: We were here last week. I loved the style of the place and the big tables on the second floor for larger groups is nice. There wasn't however any assistance at all to get a drink or menu. The bathrooms are incredibly small with just two stalls. I do like the multiple levels and the vibe of the place. Nashville is busy and it just would have been nice to get a drink quickly and service. Being new- they have the opportunity to impress and not just be like all the other bars. We will be back just isn't our absolute favorite.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Steady ship in a storm. Downpour out side and Southern Rock inside. Always have a good time, great food and awesome drinks. Haven't been in a Hard Rock in any city that disappointed us.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: I've been coming to Nashville annually for the last 5 years and have never been disappointed.  Well, thanks to Whiskey Bent, the streak has died.  When our group went there last night there was a crotchety old man at the door who asked to see our I.D.'s even though everyone was in their 40's/50's.  Well, since my wallet was stolen a couple weeks ago, I did not have an I.D. and I tried to explain this to the idiot at the door.  I also told him I had been in Whiskey Bent the last 2 nights with no problem.  After getting no where with the old bouncer, I asked to speak with the manager so I could hopefully plead my case to someone who would treat me with a little more respect.  That didn't happen.  My vision of southern hospitality will forever be tarnished after that encounter.  Total bitch on wheels.  She was acting like I was some sort of con artist and actually threatened to call the police on me for trespassing.  Not sure how that was going to play out since I was standing on the sidewalk.  She was bitchy and stupid.  I could clearly understand their position if I was hanging with a young crowd and looked like I could be under age.  Not the case. I just think they could have made an exception but at the very least they should have been more polite to me.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: I like this bar because it has the feel of an old saloon. Great music played here! I like the drinks and the friendly service

name: Ray Stevens CabaRay Showroom
text:
Seeing Ray Stevens has been the big hit of our Memorial Day Weekend trip to Nashville. The old boy, now 80-81, can still bring it. He cut his first record 61 years ago! I remember them all from Ahab the Arab forward. He jokes, he laughs, he moves (I wouldn't call it dancing). 

Our server was fun. The food was not special, but the entertainment was so good that I rated the evening 5 stars anyway. If you can make it to Nashville, see this show!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Nashville, the home to country music.  This city was wild, and it was fun to visit.  So, we visited almost every bar on broadway.  So much to see in a short period of time.  However, employees and I stopped here.  I'm from bay area california, and I am not familiar with country music.  Never listened to it.  Not a fan of it.  But I had to try it out, since I was in Nashville.  

The place was semi-packed.  There were plenty of spaces on the dance floor, but no one was dancing.  But everyone was just drinking and enjoying the band.  

Rating:
Food:  n/a
Price:  3
Ambience:  3
Service:  bartender
Overall:  3

For the experience, it was worth it.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Sucks. Sucks sucks sucks suck. Bartenders are a complete joke who think very highly of themselves and over price drinks.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I hadn't been to a Hard Rock Cafe in many years so my husband and I decided to try this one while in Nashville. It was awful, from the food to the drinks. The music was not rock at all it was pop music which threw me off a bit.

name: The Valentine
text:
We signed up for a pub crawl. Which was more just a wrist band that allowed us discounts on certain drinks at specific bars. The Valentine was one of those bars, after verifying with the bartender that the wrist band did give us the discount, I thought we were all set. Instead at the end of the night when my bill was nice and big, the bartender called the manager over to enter the discount code. 

Well the manager came over and told me I was wrong. The discount code only works for drinks on the 3rd floor of The Valentine. I told him I We had no idea, and that the bartenders have been saying all night that we were good to go. Well the manager didn't care, instead he started calling me a "fu*king idiot" then threatened me and threatened to throw me out of the bar. Then laughed when I said I was giving a bad review. 

Listen I totally understand if you can only honor the discount on specific levels of the bar. It's kind of silly but whatever. But for the Manager to act the way he did, to make threats and to use such disrespectful language... that's just nuts

name: The Valentine
text: Drinks aren't made well. Staff is rude. Music is the only good thing. Give it a miss!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Amazing service! Ask for Nixon he's awesome! Atomic burger was perfect! NY strip was cooked to perfection! Presentation was great! Amazing hard rock atmosphere!! All in all great place!

name: The Valentine
text:
I didn't know this place existed, as I don't frequent Broadway that much. But it was a pleasant surprise for our friends night out celebrating a birthday. 
4 floors of dancing.. what?! It looked bumping from the outside and I was ready to see what it was all about. There were 3-4 door guys checking IDs so it made the line go quick in the cold. We headed up to the rooftop and people were dancing along the way at every level. There were a couple different DJs playing on different levels, too. It didn't take long to get a drink and bathrooms were conveniently located. There were tables to sit/stand/hang out at if you didn't feel like dancing and would rather watch. Everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves and there weren't too many creepy drunks to ward off. Would recommend going with a group of friends if you're on a level and want to dance!

name: Ray Stevens CabaRay Showroom
text:
A Great Experience!  This is a Showroom with a piano bar in the entry.  We were familiar with the Piano Player John Jonethis who is extraordinary! He performs before the Cabaray and after.
     We loved the Ray Stevens show we were a group of 6 and the venue was perfect. We had great seats and the dinner was wonderful! The wait staff is very attentive and the drink prices are reasonable!  
     We returned after the fantastic show to the piano area and things got rockin!  Ray even came out and joined the crowd and sang with us!! Both the performers are great showmen.  I think it is a must see.  We will be sure and see it again the next time we are in Nashville.  You just don't get entertainment like this anymore..

name: FooBar
text: This is my favorite bar in Nashville!!! Great happy hour and good burritos (If you like spicy food you must try the Green Chilli Burrito). The bartenders are awesome and pour a strong drink! The best thing about this bar is that it's never the same...the eclectic mix of people and ever changing genres of music always keeps the place fun. People think of it as a dive bar because of its location but it's actually a big bar inside with a seperate room for live bands. If you want to experience the East side of Nashville, make sure you stop at Foobar.

name: Boulevard Records
text: Shitty selection and ridiculous prices. $30 for Fleetwood Mac's RUMOURS? Really? A complete and utter water of my time.

name: The Valentine
text: Very cool place. Bartender Jordan was awesome. Music was really really good. The place is spotless and brand new. We will be back.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Food was great! The service was better. We went during cma fest and it was very crowded but being able to make a reservation we were seated quickly. Our waitress was very friendly and the drinks were good too!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Fantastic music and service. Moonshine is great. Try the Oatmeal Cookie. Worth the visit.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Great vibe! Fun music. Dancing bartenders. Loving it! Band is awesome! Getting the crowd totally into the music!

name: The Valentine
text: This place was awesome! The DJ (I didn't manage to get his name) played a nice mix of Top 40, throwbacks, and country songs. He welcomed requests and was very open to all of the bachelorette parties. The bartender at the mini bar Christian or Kristen (it was really loud so I'm not sure which one I heard!) was absolutely amazing. Even though the place was packed she managed to remember me and my friends drink order every time we came back. It was our first ever night out in Nashville and this place did not disappoint!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We' were in town for a festival and stopped at the hard rock for a bottle of wine and delicious nachos. Amazing service by our server Krystal and supervisor Anna who made sure to accommodate us and made great convo. We had our dog with us and he became a little sick from the heat, the staff came out with ice cold water and a wet towel to put over himself. They went above and beyond to make sure all of us, dog included, were comfortable. Thank you ladies!

name: The Valentine
text:
Looking for a classy yet casual Cocktail Bar with a rooftop option on Broadway in Nashville? The Valentine has you covered in spades.

The Valentine is a self-described 'upscale saloon' boasting three interior floors of food, drink and live music, along with a rooftop patio located in the center of all the action in Music City, Tennessee. I found myself at the bar thanks to a corporate event complete with open bar and appetizers and would argue there isn't a more distinguished or well appointed interior on the Broadway strip thanks to the giant chandler, prohibition era vibe, and illustrious service. Thanks to the open floor plan design on the second level it is easy to watch the nightly live music without blowing your ears out and the 3rd floor begs you to belly up to the bar to catch your favorite sporting event. The rooftop bar and patio closes any argument on what Bar is the most elegant and chic in the area.

I had a wonderful time at The Valentine and suggest that this is the spot to start any Broadway Bar Crawl.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place, whether you come in for a few minutes or stay a few hours.  Friendly staff, great burgers and beer selection.  Prices are fine, food a great value.  Don't miss the onion rings and the grilled cheese is perfect, gotta try it, don't mock it.  The band is great, their play list speaks to the history of country music, what a talented band.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
"People are wantin' to know who you've been sleepin' with to get on the Opry so quick." -- Coal Miner's Daughter (1980)

Oddly, with all the concerts I see in a year, I've yet to attend one at The Ryman. It's still on my bucket list, but it's bound to happen sooner than later.

On my recent trip to Nashville, we decided to take the tour and I'm so glad we did. The price tag is $20 and well worth it as I learned so much history is just a short time. I was in awe. You start by watching a fun movie that explains the beginnings of the place and how it was the Grand Old Opry and how it was then resurrected - it was fun and was more than just watching a bland and boring VHS tape - I won't give anything more away. As you leave, they give you a numbered map and then you begin the self-guided tour.

I'll admit, I suck at self-guided tours, but I prefer them to having someone drone on about a place to me - unless they are really engaging. So this was probably best for me. I just don't tend to follow instructions. First, I was distracted for a long time by the posted from previous shows that were signed by the artists, framed and hanging just outside the main auditorium. I spent a lot of time looking at the posters, and being sad I didn't see these shows. Shout out to Dave Grohl. 

We wandered for a long time and read everything there was to read and sat in the balcony and lower level (this is awesome because now I know where to sit for shows) and just took it all in. I resisted the urge to buy any schwag in the store as I know I will be back for a show soon.

name: Legends Corner
text: One of my favorite spots we crawled to during our vacation to Nashville. And bonus it was St. Pattys day!!:)

name: Robert's Western World
text: Standard Nashville bar, pop in if you're walking by but nothing to rave about (or complain about) from my experience.

name: Robert's Western World
text: My go-to for real honky tonk music in downtown Nashville. Do my best to go 5-6 times a year. My last visit came a week ago, and my usual cheeseburger and fries were spot on. Swear they are best fries in downtown. The beer is good; the waitresses are attentive, despite the chaos, and music is great. What more do you want?!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: The atmosphere was great. Our server Jade was awesome and sweet. She made sure our drinks were filled and our food was prepared right. We had no issues with our orders. The band they had last night Paulina Jayne (6/26) was amazing. We will definitely be back.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Delicious food, super swanky sexy live music in the background and Jesse our server absolutely killed it. I'm a bartender of 10 years and have super high standards and I've never been happier with a server, really ever. Love the atmosphere and good time attitude. Thanks Jesse for a kick ass meal.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Went to see the Black Crowes while we were in town and the show was phenomenal.  The acoustics were a little sketchy but I'm not sure it was the fault of anyone specifically.  When inside you just FEEL the music of days gone by.  The vibe is fantastic.  I wish we had done a tour to see the venue in daylight to really appreciate it.  Next time!

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text:
Not what I expected from the other reviews or the name. Friends and I went in for a late night bite thinking we would get some good food and some good music. 
Upon entering you could see it was a dive bar, but I am open to trying new things or finding the diamond in the rough. This place was not it. After we came in we headed to the bar to order some drinks and food. The food was cafeteria food at best, and then on top of that they charged a cover but it was just a lady coming around with a basket. Needless to say we didn't stick around long. We had a pretzel that was good, but everything else came out of a jar or bag or freezer from the back. No diamonds recovered here.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: I got a sandwich with Andouille sausage and shrimp. It was delicious with a kick and I couldn't stop eating the crinkle fries. I also tried my friend's southwest quesadilla and loved it! We chose Tin Roof based on the music and a picture of the sandwich ordered. The bartender was friendly and I felt like I made the right choice stopping here.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I went here to get a late lunch (3pm on Saturday) to go, based on Yelp reviews and the fact that their menu prices seemed reasonable for something simple.   Sorry to disagree with so many other Yelpers on this one, but my experience clearly was different than theirs and I wasn't looking for music. 

The place was extremely busy and it took me a while to make my way to the bar/register area. One of the bartenders took my food order, and said they could do it to go which was great. I ordered, paid and waited. And waited...while other people kept getting their food.
