After 25 minutes I got her attention again (after she helped several other customers) and she didn't recognize me at all just asked if she could help me with anything. I asked if she could check on my food order, she asked what table I was at, I said it was a to go order and I'd been standing there. The look on her face told me she had forgotten about it. She brought me the food, and said it had completely slipped her mind. 

The food itself was okay...grilled cheese sandwich was decent but soggy (due to sitting around I'm guessing), the fries I got as a side were crinkle cut fries clearly from a bag and they were undercooked  the fries were definitely not worth the up-charge for getting them instead of chips. 

I might try this place again, but more likely to go elsewhere.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Ryman: The Mother Church of Country Music. You walk in this place and you can feel the history. The seats are wooden pews, it's great! I've been here a few times and every show has been great!
My two favorite shows have been Elle King and Kacey Musgraves "A Very Kacey Christmas." I'm pretty sure Elle King married a couple on stage and then Kacey Musgraves put a beautiful Christmas show on!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Sambuca is chic with lavish decor, made for the young and hip professionals of today. A great place to go and unwind, grab a drink and listen to live music. For you with a immense palate, the food is amazing.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
A visit to the Ryman is nothing of a religious experience for music lovers, and considering the building's history as an evangelical church, that's an appropriate analogy. The history of this incredible venue overpowers you from the moment you walk in, and really comes alive when you take a backstage tour. You'll stand on the famous Ryman stage, see the dressing rooms that honor the building's rich musical past, and hear fascinating anecdotes about the famous performers whose careers were launched in the Mother Church of Country Music.

After the tour, take time to linger in the auditorium and see the displays recounting its colorful history. Run your hands along the wooden pews where thousands of music lovers have sat for more than one hundred years, and soak in the atmosphere that makes the Ryman one of the most memorable places in America. 

Then make time to come back for a show, where the space comes alive with miraculous acoustics, the thunder of more than 2,000 fellow music lovers stomping their feet in unison, and the wonderful call-and-response between musicians and their fans. I took in a Bluegrass Legends show, and came away with a new appreciation for the essentially American style of music that was born on the Ryman stage.

Like Preservation Hall in New Orleans, or Carnegie Hall in New York, the Ryman is a shrine to the music that makes America great. If you're ever fortunate enough to be in Nashville, be sure to make it your first stop.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I was in Nashville for a national convention and decided to break away from the pack and explore this on my own.  Sure glad I did, they call this "The First Church of Country Music" and it's A-MAZING!  Any fan of music, not just country music, will appreciate this living museum.  I wish I would have more time to just walk around and explore and just learn and soak in the vibe.  I got there the last tour, want to say it cost around 15 bucks for the tour.  The tour was cool, we were lead around by some old-school codger who knew his history.  I enjoyed going backstage, getting to peak into the dressing rooms where some of the best musicians ever have graced the stage.  You get a sense of the tradition and importance of this place hearing the stories and seeing the sights, the spirit is still there.  Seeing a live show here is definitely on my bucket list, I hear the acoustics are perfection and it's such a beautiful stage.  In a city known for music, this is one place you have to hit, it's the real deal you all!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
Great place...so much fun. We ate great food and watched an excellent mariachi band!!
We will definitely return!!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This is the only Tin Roof location I ever been to that I enjoyed, it has a great location right in the heart of Nashville on Broadway. The food is not the best but the atmosphere is lively and the service is good, friendly people. After visiting other US cities I am glad Nashville has really friendly and welcoming people for the most part especially in hospitality they know how to do it right.

name: Robert's Western World
text: In the sea of honky tonk's and chaos on Broadway, there is the heaven of Robert's Western World. A savior for the hungry patrons who are looking for some great music and delicious food. The fried bologna sandwiches (and I hope I wasn't just intoxicated) are FREAKING AMAZING! The fried pickle spears (although they burned my mouth horribly) were unforgettable, and the crowd was perfect. This place definitely stands out to me from the 20+ establishments we visited that night in Nashville.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This place is awesome, perfect for any history or country music buff. We came here on Friday might to see Chris Young, Ashley Monore and Michael Ray. What a great show! We had such a good time and all the hosts were so funny! A must do in Nashville if you can get tickets to go. Concessions are allowed in the theater, so feel free to buy wine or beer at the concession stands to enjoy during the show.

name: Legends Corner
text: Decent music. The bands are entertainers not just musicians which is fun. Similar to most spots on Broadway, it has walls covered in albums and cool stuff. Only serves pizza but the pizza was good.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great music, if you sit in the back you can carry on a conversation, and hear great music. Waited awhile for our food, the Sweet Tea, delicious, nice big cups. We are from Chicago Illinois, and have been here for a week and have been here twice. Fried pickles great.

name: Music City Center
text:
I thought the architecture of the Music City Center was pretty cool-looking, with it's curvaceous outward appearance!  It's a convention complex that offers a large 1200000 square footage of meeting space and exhibit options.  You can check out their website's calendar to see what events are coming up.

+cool architecture!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Really really good service and a very attentive waiter. On the weekends (Friday and Saturday) they have a live band. When I went it was Al Green and the hard times. Lol. They were really in good though and had the whole crowd enjoying themselves.

If you don't want to be close to the music there are quieter areas or a patio outside. The place is really nice. The drinks are on the more expensive side but totally worth every penny. They don't cheat you on your alcohol and they have really taken their time to come up with a creative and satisfying drink menu. 

Food was great. They serve small plates and larger meals. I ordered a small plate of Chicken Samosas. They were a tad greasy but the flavor was on point. In will definitely be going back there my next visit.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The vibe of the Ryman, Holy Church of country music was great. The visibility however was less than optimal especially if anyone of any size sits in front of you. The beer selection was not very good but prices were typical of the stadium concession . 

I would definitely come back to the Ryman for another show, just need to choose the upper balcony first row or main floor towards the front

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We bought the combo Ryman/Grand Ole Opry tour.  This Auditorium in downtown Nashville has stunning architecture and beautiful details throughout.  You can see everything at your own pace and enjoy the history.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I've held several events at Sambuca and have usually had a pretty good experience. However last week my husband I went in for dinner on evening and I was really disappointed. The restaurant was extremely slow for a weekday evening, yet our server didn't seem to be particularly interested in serving us. I ordered the filet, and it has to be the absolute smallest filet I have ever ordered. Considering the price point of the restaurant, I was extremely disappointed in the portion sizes. The filet only came with asparagus making it a lot more like a small plate than a true entree. 

Beyond the portion sizes and service, the place was a wreck. The women's bathroom was absolutely atrocious- see attached photos. When we left, the valet line was about 10-12 people long. I realize it's handled by an outside company, but it reflects badly on the establishment for such a long wait. Probably will not return for a private dinner.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Difficult review to write - really was wanted a good experience but disappointed in terms of food quality, cost and frankly service. 

I would equate the food experience equivalent to that of a mass produced event type quality.   The restaurant was filled to capacity (not a bad thing) but the food fit - was somewhat lukewarm, dried, and lacking any serious flavor.   I had the red snapper étouffée- again, fish was overcooked and a bit dry.   My wife had scallops with risotto coins - very small serving and a bit salty.   

Derive was adequate at best - appeared understaffed for the amount of people.  B coffee came after dessert - annoying.   

Drinks were adequate at best as well.  

For the cost ($150 for two - three drinks and normal dinners with dessert) just left feeling like we could have gone to a dozen other local new places and had a much better meal.   

Good place for large parties I suppose.

name: Music City Center
text: Very nice convention and event space.  Some of the best food I have ever had on a trade show floor but then again when I saw that Chef Elaine Taubin former of Lowe's Vanderbilt Plaza is there, it was no wonder.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Needed a perfect place for an important business/fun dinner.....could not have found a better place.....
1) our waiter "Price" was incredible.....great recommendations...sincerely wanted us to have a great time.
2) the band was amazing (thx Nashville!) but not too loud.
3) appetizers, wine list, entrees, and dessert were all awesome!
The chef is incredible......an epic evening!!!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I got here on a Sunday afternoon for some brunch with my buddy. There was live music playing, western swing country music to be specific. Very good ambience owing to the fact that the band was hitting some real nice chords. 

I got the recession sandwich. It included a fried bologna sandwich with chips and a PBR for $5. To me this is/was a steal. I get started on my beer while waiting on the food. Now the sandwich was too salty and I did not like it one bit. I don't know if this is common with frying bologna but I'm not getting it again until proved wrong. 

My friend got a turkey sandwich and he seemed quite happy with his food. A basic nod of the head is what I got when I asked him about his sandwich so I cannot really tell you much about his sandwich.

I will go back again for some beer and live music, but it's not on my goto list for sure.

name: Music City Center
text:
WOW. This is easily the largest building I've ever been in. This place is massive! 

I attended a conference here recently and I thoroughly enjoyed my time roaming the halls of this place. Everything in this building is super clean, clearly organized and "green."

By "green," I mean that they use reclaimed rain water in all their bathrooms. At first glance though, it looks like every single toilet in the building needs to be flushed. It honestly looked like each toilet had pee in it and no other bothered to flush it. It wasn't until you go into a stall and read the sign on the back of the door that you realize it's not pee, it's reclaimed rain water. So don't worry when you go into the bathroom!

Speaking of bathrooms, every single one I went into had an attendant. There was also a huge bottle of Listerine mouth wash with tiny, disposable cups, hair spray and lotion to use. It felt like a really fancy hotel - but it was a huge convention center. 

During the opening ceremony of my conference, I couldn't go 20 feet without someone offering complimentary (came with registration) food or drinks. The food was AWESOME. They had mini brisket and pork belly tacos that were to die for. Two or three bites of food that packed a ton of flavor! And the drinks were amazing too. I couldn't turn around with being offered beer or wine. And the bartending stations (they were scattered all over the place) offered a full bar of items. The specialty drink of the night was called The Red Carpet with watermelon moonshine and some other stuff I can't recall. It was really sweet and it got me really buzzed. 

During the expo hours that food was phenomenal. I was expecting simple things - finger foods during the expo hall hours, but I got food you would normally get at a higher end restaurant. We had pecan crusted chicken, sweet potato tater tots, quinoa vegetable mix, teeny salads with fennel, argula and house-made dressing, pork tenderloin with risotto, baked potato gratin,  cake pops, house made pecan pie, teeny tiny ice cream cones with Jack Daniel Bourbon Honey Vanilla gelato and branded white chocolate bars. So much good food! I don't recall the names of everything I ate, but I everything was delicious!

Major props to all the staff at the MCC - I kept seeing staff constantly moving. Servers, chefs, attendants - everyone was great. There was always someone there to point me in the right direction, offer to show me something, grab my plate, serve me food, even talk to me in the restroom! 

If you're ever in the Nashville area, I highly recommend stopping by this place to check it out! It's right next to the Bridgestone Arena, the Omni and the Country Music Hall of Fame.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This review is for the tour only, I did not have the pleasure of seeing a show here when I visited.

As first timers to Nashville, we decided to get their city pass that allowed us to get into a bunch of attractions for a discounted price. Our first stop was the Ryman. I knew this was the Opry previous to its current location, but didn't know much else. I must say, I absolutely LOVED the self guided tour we were given. The video you see at the beginning is really like a mini theatrical production, and it was PHENOMENAL! I'm a history nerd, so I was relishing all the facts that were thrown at me. The little showcases throughout the auditorium are very well put together and gave me tons of insight into the true significance of the Ryman. My grandma, sister and I got our picture taken in the circle on stage, since my granny has always been a huge fan of the Opry and I think this was part of the Old Lady's bucket list. Overall, a great venue to tour, and hopefully one day I'll get back for a show.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I have been here a few times and every time it's been amazing! The food and service is always amazing followed by great live music. 

*Now the menus are hard to read due to the lack of lighting

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Very cool show but be sure not to talk quietly, act excited, or show any form of life because the man clientele is 75 years old or older and we got scolded for enjoying the show....just don't move or sing along or clap and you'll be fine.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Rainy Saturday afternoon, they were open! Got the "dis" from next door octopus, just rolled in here.  Amazing duck, great appetizers.  A little slow on service - but good place to chill.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Happy to experience the legendary Ryman Auditorium in wonderful downtown Nashville. Located right in the middle of downtown, you can grab some drinks, dinner, or whatever before or after a show.  The auditorium itself is clean, but still had the old feel to it... you can just feel how much talent has passed through this venue. :).  There is seating on both the balcony area or in front of he stage and to be honest you can see clearly no matter where you are seated.  The seating on the balcony area is like bench style seating (no individual seats) so you have to kind of shimmy into your seats since you can really tell how many people will be in the row.  We have some fellows that we're mad we were sitting inside... they were like "how many people do you think can fit here?" lol I'm like "I don't know but we're about to find out since they sold us these tickets in the same row as you." Lol grumpy old men. Lol

All and all, we are So glad we came! If you haven't been to Nashville before, this is a must for your to do list.

name: Legends Corner
text:
So, we took my visiting BiL downtown to play tourist.  We had some time to kill before meeting the folks we were going to dine with, so we stopped in at Legends Corner.   I guess it was too early in the day for waitresses, but our beertender did a pretty good job of tending bar as well as waiting tables.  

The beer selection wasn't very extensive, but we found something suitable to quench our thirst.  My wife was pleased with the Cosmo that she got.  And my beer was good and cold.

Megan Ellis and her band were providing the entertainment.  She's got a great voice, and we liked her a lot.  I know this city is chock full of talented people looking for that one big break.  I hope she gets hers.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Wrap me in red velvet!!! Yes the walls at Sambuca are a bright red fabric to match the Beetlejuice themed design, love love love! The welcoming laid back attitude of staff makes this a Nashville staple. Live music, check. Dancing, check. Well executed cuisine, check. Drinking, HELLO!!! The charm of a place that serves cheese sticks a la cranberry sauce, calls it something fancy and makes me love to pay for it, has my vote!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Nice atmosphere.!!Great Steak!! It is worth the buck!! Great music!! The waiter was fab!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
When an old buddy of mine let me know there was a fantastic show coming up, that just happened to be on my birthday... there was no doubt in my mind what my plans would be. Within the hour, tickets were bought, flight and hotel booked, and finally the day came when I returned to the Ryman Auditorium for the best of birthdays. 

It wasn't my first trip to the Mother Church, sure as hell won't be my last either. This has to be my favorite all time venue, EVER. There is not a bad seat in the house: I've sat right up front, all the way up in the balcony, and a few times somewhere in the middle, and have always had a great view... and the sound...the sound. Almost acoustically perfect, if not perfect, even with just one person on stage or a whole mess of folks. 

Back in another life, when I was hitting up the concert scene across the Midwest pretty heavily, I had the ultimate pleasure of getting in backstage. To see all of the signed photos on the walls, the dressing rooms, and even smoking a cigarette out back on the iconic back exit stairs to Ryman Alley.... you just feel the bigger than life energy of all the phenomenal stars that have played here.....

Some of the best times of my life here. ALWAYS an experience that will create a sweet, sweet memory.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Only there for a beer and a half on 4th of July.  Bartender wasn't too friendly, but it was find for a quick beer and a fun environment.  Also the live music was a little on the loud side for conversation.  At any rate I would return as it seems to be a Solid honky tonk and at good for some beer!!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Sambucca was great for a large meal. We had a group of 12 and they made the reservations easy. Our table was right by the stage for a great Latin rock performer. She was great! Our waiter was very nice and helpful as well. A couple of our steaks were over cooked, which can be hard in a Party but also basic at that price point. We were freezing! The AC was cranked and we asked numerous times to have it adjusted.  My uncle had napkins all over him.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: So much fun!! Great music and great bartenders!! Corone served the best drink I had all weekend!! I don't mind paying for quality drinks as long as it's " quality"!! Very professional and FUN!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Came to see Jason Isbell. I love the idea of pew seats but sometimes I don't want to be crunched with a stranger. There just wasn't enough room for the amount people on our row. But every single employee was insanely nice. And the show was great.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Good music, cold beer, great atmosphere. Doesn't feel hokey like a lot of the other bars on Broadway.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: A great day at the Ryman! A well polished tour guide, with lots of information, and lots of freedom to tour and take photos.

name: Robert's Western World
text: While waiting to enter witnessed a very aggressive foul mouthed female door employee push a woman to the ground and then claimed the customer pushed her first. Need better quality of people at your door

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Would give this place 5 stars if it wasn't for the beyond loud music that makes it impossible to even think. They have both gluten free and vegan options Great waitress and good vibes. I'd suggest if you want decent prices and a place to start your night off.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
We went here 8.4.18 to celebrate our friends 27 Wedding anniversary. We have never been before.
The atmosphere was charming and relaxing..The venue is wonderful. They had a live band "Grant Garland" wow!!! 
  The service was excellent!! 
We had the crab & shrimp dip and shrimp  ceviche  it was delicious and fresh! 
For dinner I had the salmon Oscar- fresh and cooked perfect
The others all had the Jumbo Chili rubbed Scallops and rice pilaf- OH EM GEE!!! They melted in your mouth and so flavorful!! 
We had the most enjoyable time and will be back for sure!! We are still talking about it 2 days later.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Another one of those "If you are visiting town, you just go here" places.
Also crowded, expensive and loud.
Absolutely worth it!
Every time I have been, there is fab country band playing.
This last time, I learned about the rear entry that goes out to the alley and provided easier access to a couple other bar.
Absolutely worth a visit.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Let me tell you about the happy hour! Sambuca 75 and Frose are the clear winners. Cheap, strong, and tasty just how I like my drinks. I brought a friend here that was visiting and she has not stopped raving about it. Well worth a visit and they have live music. Come get some!!!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
went here on a sunday night on my first trip to nashville after reading all the glowing reviews on yelp and trip advisor. despite going in with high expectations, i couldn't have been more pleasantly (i'm far from someone that knows his way around country music) surprised. i know that i'm sounding like a broken record in saying what's already been said about this place dozens of times, but it bears mentioning again, and once more for every good experience that a person has in going there.
- great honky tonk, country, rockabilly, and old school 50's and 60s' rock n' roll
- great fried bologna sandwich and decent selection of local beers at more than reasonable prices
- everyone there, including staff, had an unfazed smile the entire time

it's a quintessential nashville experience

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Perfect after the zoo place to unwind with live music, bar, tacos, playground, arcade and more! Everything is super affordable and the building itself is brand new, clean and has security also! We had such a good time, everything was delicious especially the tostadas and paletas!!! Can't wait to come back with friends and family.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Hey y'all, there's a reason the Ryman is called the Mother Church of Country Music. Located in the middle of downtown, it looks like a God-fearing cathedral from the outside, and it's hallowed halls definitely reflect the spiritual heft of its history. No coincidence there as the auditorium started life as the Union Gospel Tabernacle in 1892 and housed rafter-raising revivals. Its program was broadened by a woman named Lula C. Naff who booked a wide variety of performances in the theater for over half a century.

She's the central figure and narrator of the ten-minute, multi-screen video you see in a separate room at the beginning of the $21.95 self-guided tour. Obviously inspired by similar featurettes at Disneyland and other theme parks, it provided a highly engaging overview of the Ryman's history. Once you exit the room, Jamie W. and I were free to peruse the two floors of the theater which includes quite a few exhibits and a historical timeline (photo: http://bit.ly/2ltIlC6). Lots of spangly costumes and elaborate musical instruments with accompanying videos narrated by familiar country music stars.

It was like a smaller version of the Country Music Hall of Fame (photo: http://bit.ly/2K9o835). Of course we took advantage of the photo opp where we stood on stage in front of the Grand Ole Opry barnyard backdrop (photo: http://bit.ly/2lxF7xa). This was where the Opry resided until 1974 when it moved to its current cavernous home to the east of downtown. But I could well imagine seeing Hank Williams or Patsy Cline perform their familiar hits In the more intimate setting found here. We would love to come back for a real show, but the tour gave a strong sense of how potent country music can be.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This was a referral from the hotel concierge. There is a live band so if you want quiet don't come here. We say way back to reduce noise. Started with free fried pickles thanks to the concierge. Really good thick pickles. We had the hot chicken sandwich which was good. The best macaroni and cheese ever with some brisket in it. Overall awesome food

name: Legends Corner
text: Stopped in before the Preds/Bruins game. Not very crowded. Band was good. Drink prices were on the higher side, but at least they had the beer prices on the menu (most other places didn't). Will come back next time wer're in town.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We came to Sambuca for a bachelorette party and made reservations a month ago and it was very easy. We called day of to confirm and they said they had our reservation up on their second level "rooftop", which is more of an dining area with retractable doors, but when we showed up it was gorgeous! We were seated right away with a beautiful view of the Gulch and when our waitress Ariel (I hope that's correct) she was right away amazing. She gave us honest opinions of what to get, the red snapper and the flat iron steak were both amazing, she was able to split our checks up with no issues and she just made our experience great overall. Thanks Ariel and Sambuca!!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Decent mixed drinks, good live bands, and plenty of space to move. Glad we stopped here, out of the many bars on Broadway!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Great venue with fantastic staff!! I'm still recovering from a broken hip so I was using a wheelchair tonight. The ushers were unbelievably friendly and accommodating. 
Because of the church pew seats they wheeled me to my seat then guarded the wheelchair to insure it wouldn't roll away. We weren't sure what to expect and found the experience better than we had even hoped for. 
I'm not big on giving 5 stars but the Ryman completely deserves it!!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Sambuca is perfect for a special night out. It's a tad on the pricey side, but the food is outstanding. The decor is pretty swanky and hip so be sure to wear something stylish. Don't miss the sea-bass and soapapia cheesecake - it's seriously one of the best meals I've ever had.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I come here for lunch any chance I get because the staff is amazing and the food is fantastic! Even though you cannot go wrong with anything on the menu, I highly recommend the Sea Bass, Brussels sprouts, and best salad!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Great stop if you want a quick bite to eat on your way to a concert. 

My friends and I took the train from Mount Juliet to downtown Nashville. The stop for the train is at the end of Broadway. The tin roof Broadway restaurant/bar is a perfect stop in between the train stop and Bridgestone arena. 

The restaurant has live music, which is great for an authentic Nashville experience. It is quite noisy up in the front of the bar but there's several tables and chairs towards the back that is perfect to be able to chat with friends and still hear music. 

My two girlfriends and I Shared an order of loaded tater tot's and chicken tenders w/ fries, it was perfect for the three of us to munch on with some drinks before the show. The food did not take too long and it was a nice upbeat fun environment.

name: Nashville Municipal Auditorium
text:
It's been years since I have seen a gig at Nashville Municipal Auditorium. From what I hear this was the premiere spot for larger-drawing acts prior to Bridgestone but even years ago when I first came to a show here it was more for raucous acts and a more "engaged" floor audience.
I really enjoyed the show I caught here recently. So why only 2 stars? 

It's just a bit run-down and I don't see them doing anything about that. That though is manageable. What does suck are: (a) if you pay for a seat and are anywhere close to 6" tall you will be crammed in knees bumping the person in front of you; (b) check in through the line is nowhere near as efficient as at comparably sized (or larger) venus (e.g. Bridestone); and (c) concessions are ridiculously priced with little to no variety. You want a beer? Your options are Bud, Bud Light, Mich Ultra or some crappy lime-a-rita Bud, all in 25 oz cans for $11 a pop. Any other music venue in Nashville you can get a quality beer for half the price.

But...I'd come back for sure if the right act is here. There's a reason some acts are going to opt for Municipal over Bridgestone (if they're too big to play a fantastic venue like Marathon or the Exit/In)...and that's because they let folks act like they're at a concert. Plenty of security and good checks to make sure you're safe when entering but they let you mosh in the pit. It's grungier and more run-down but there aren't too many bad seats in the house (view-wise) and it suits a lot of shows.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Love the show at the Ryman. To be sitting on the church pews in the same place that Johnny Cash first met June was amazing. Great place a must check out when in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Easily the best bar on Broadway. Cheap beer, great music, and simple food. Getting a grilled cheese like your mom used to make for $4 a bit tipsy is amazing.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Loved this place. Cheap beers and great live music. Saw the Don Kelley band on 6/17 and couldn't leave until they were done playing. Did a slammin' version of Ramblin Man by the ABB. $2.50 Miller high lifes? Are you kidding me. The sound was mixed perfectly for the cozy environment. All good. Question-Who was playing lead guitar that night?

name: Robert's Western World
text: Fun fun fun!!! That's what I thought about Robert's Western World! So.....I had a layover in Nashville and brought my bf along. It was Christmas night and I Yelped and found Robert's! I used to avoid the Nashville layover, but now I can't wait to return because of this place. I don't know if it was poppin' because it was Christmas, but it was a blast! The drink specials were great and so was the food! Love the hotdogs!!! They had live music and people dancing and some were wearing rhinestone cowboy suits too! Too cool!  People were dancing and just having a grand ole time. I can't wait to return to Robert's Western World!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Great venue with impressive acoustics and big headliners! Great location and close to all the best restaurants Nashville has to offer!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
In late July during a heat wave, we walked up and down Broadway and Second street twice trying to find great music that did not blow your ears off and decent air conditioning. 

Then we heard Rachel Hester at RWW and we spent the afternoon there. She and the band were both very impressive. Classic country, but not too twangy. We were able to dance on the small dance floor and that made it even more memorable. I made a few video clips and after listening to them back home, I realize that they were all extremely talented musicians. I especially liked her rendition of "No one knows my name". I had never heard that song before, but I could not get it out of my head after hearing her sing it. I think she does a better rendition than Gillian Welch.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I went to Nashville for a bachelorette party, which I'm pretty sure is 60% of the people walking through the city.  It is crazy the amount of people in this city that are celebrating bachelorette parties, and just in the restaurant alone were 3 other parties.  We took an uber to dinner, and the driver told us a little about this area of Nashville known as The Gulch.  The atmosphere as soon as you walk in is very nice and welcoming.  It has a L.A vibe to it, and I loved that about it.  It is two stories and has a great bar area as well as a smaller restaurant seating and large outdoor seating as well.  The lights are dimmed pretty low and made my 28 year old eyes feel much older than they are!  

The food was decent.  A bit overpriced for the flavor, but several people I was with loved the seafood carbonara and the salmon Oscar.  I wish I had gone that route instead.  I went with the filet which came with asparagus and a bordelaise.  I love bordelaise usually but this one just lacked the flavor it was intended to have.  They were out of asparagus so I opted for the sprouts.  I LOVE sprouts and they are very difficult to cook and getting them right is an art.  These were decent, but since getting them right is so hard, I'm usually not too picky on the sprouts.  I just expected for the price they would be perfect.  The band was amazing and I really enjoyed having some music in the background while we ate.  It was hard to hear at times, but we were seated so close to the band that is understandable.  Drinks were great and overall a decent dining experience for the city.  Great location and we really enjoyed walking through the Gulch after dinner.  Best part of the entire meal was the fried cheesecake.  That is a MUST try!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
A really solid bar with a gorgeous theme and great music. We stopped in here on a rainy Sunday to listen to a "Hangover Special" band that was all acoustic but pretty good. We sat at the bar and the bartenders were pretty quick at helping us out. The beers are pretty cheap and we also got quite a few $3 jello shots. The second band that came on were lively and we ended up staying a lot longer than originally anticipated. We ordered the loaded tots and my god, the queso melted over these little tot nuggets were amazing. Highly recommend if you want an unhealthy snack.

Love the vibes here, love the food here, love the bands here!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
I'm reviewing the ceviche and pallatas food court restaurants. There are others... Très gauchos look amazing.

Ceviche: Pretty robust menu. I ended up going with the ceviche de pescado. All I can say is... For 12$ you get a massive quantity of food. The ceviche itself is okay. I would rate that a 3. It's mostly shrimp with raw cut up vegetables. It doesnt have a lot of flavor... Not something super authentic.

Pallatas: There was a huge line for the pallatas... And there's a reason. The pallatas were amazing. I got a strawberry pallatas and it was just the perfect blend of sweetness and flavor. Why this review is a 4.

Overall: I'd go back for the pallatas and to try out très gauchos. I would probably not try the ceviche again..  it's just not that great

name: Robert's Western World
text: Well I have walked up and down the street most of the night. I just flew in from Dallas this evening. For the most part I would have to say the live music isn't very good. But right here at Robert's Western World it is the best music I've heard all night. I would definitely come back here if I was ever in Tennessee again. But I doubt I ever will be. Robert's you rock!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great food and music! Just don't expect any service! So and I had to get up and asked for water, then waiter apologized for not waiting on us due to staff gave him too many tables! Save ur money!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Sambuca is one of my favorite restaurants in Nashville. I won't lie I've always stuck to my favorites on the menu, but once I find something delicious, it's hard to try anything else. The shrimp and crab dip for an appetizer is a must for everyone! It is soooo yummy. Also if you want a perfectly done steak, this is where you go. Every time I've ordered my steak they have prepared it correctly on the first try. The same for the rest of the people I have dined with. I personally love the Filet! It has great seasoning and a delicious sauce. The wine is tasty here too. Finally the ambiance is always great with the live music on the weekends. I would recommend this restaurant to anyone in the Nashville area.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Is Sambucha's er "Sammy's" the best food I've ever had - nope.  Best drinks - probably not.  Best atmosphere - it's up there.

Is Sammy's the best experience I've ever had at a restaurant?  You better believe it.  Here's the thing - you are family the second you walk into Sammy's.  Whether it's in need of great service at the bar, a recommendation for a night on the town - or just the family you've never had - Sammy's is the ONLY place is Nashville (make that the south) that you need to go to.

Some say George Washington's crossing of the Delaware is this country's greatest quest.  Well I'd beg to differ.  That stumble down to Sammy's on Friday and Saturday during our Nashville vacation will forever be written in the history books.

Only difference - GW crossed the Delaware a third time - and if my wife lets me back into that city again, a third crossing shall commence at the one and only "Sammy's."

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This place treats patrons with unforgivable scrutiny. The "gatekeepers" at the door are both unreasonable and uneducated as it applies to the validity of a drivers license. Apparently, they are not concerned about their business and give a different face to southern hospitality ~ it's ugly.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: You don't really come to a Honkey Tonk on Broadway for the food, but if you happen to be here when everyone's hungry- the tacos are way better than I thought they would be. Especially the fish tacos that tasted very fresh. But beyond the food the live music was amazing - even mid afternoon on a random Monday, and the staff was friendly and attentive.

name: Second Fiddle
text: While walking up and down Broadway, I knew I had to chose a country western bar and listen to honky tonk before I left town.  I really don't like country music and knew that these bars wouldn't change my mind.  It didn't.  But country music is Americana and I had to experience it live, love it or not.  The bar was long and the live band played at the front with their backs to the window so patrons walking by could see and hear them.  Because they were playing some Sweet Home Alabama when I walked by, I thought it would ok to come in here.  Bartenders were not very sociable and the crowd really didn't seem to get into the music.  Maybe they don't like country either?  Nonetheless, I'm glad I walked in and stuck around.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We were lucky enough to snag seats up front on a busy holiday weekend and stayed for a few hours because: the music was awesome (think Johnny Cash) and the beer was a couple bucks (we decided to be less high maintenance and go for PBR & Busch). My only regret is leaving to check out a couple other Broadway bars just to find bands playing...Third Eye Blind? Yuck. This place was the best and the people watching was top notch.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Been twice. Received awful service both times, treated like I'm not good enough to be there or an inconvenience when I order. Food is meh. I ordered something that was not what I was expecting at all, and as much as I hate sending food back, I did ask and the bartender was infuriated. It's very clique-y here, which if you read any of my other reviews, I don't really like. I think this would be a nice place to go on a date if you had reservations and didn't care about blowing money on small portions...the décor/vibe without people is really cool and swanky, somewhat romantic...I just think there's better places to go.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Really enjoyed this place until I sat next to an article, which I read, about the rags to riches story of the owner.    That story I love.   But, his band played tonight and they are talented, to pass around a tip jar like you are a struggling band  is a fraud.    To make matters worse, Mr. Come from nothing asked who went to the Ryman tonight and further crapped on what he called pop country.   Yes I went.   Music is about acceptance and while I understand the want to maintain traditions there is no need to put down an evolution in music and alienate half the folks patronizing your bar.    Crushing to the soul that you aren't open armed to anything promoting country and music and solid paying clientele.   Any stars from me simply for good wait staff (Ramone's  t-shirt) and a good bologna sandwich.     Overall, the place is worth the visit.   The attitude I got on my visit just sucked.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is where locals go IF they go to Broadway.  Don't waste your time going anywhere else, Robert's has the best music on the strip.  Catch the Don Kelly Band on a Friday or Saturday night to see the best guitar player in Nashville (19 year old Daniel Donato).  You won't hear pop country here, it's all old school country, Southern rock and blues.  You might get REAL lucky if the band happens to let the Robert's staff sing - they are all amazing.  The guy that cooks your fried bologna sandwiches has moves like Jagger (and a great voice/presence) .  The cute blonde bartender just wrote a song for Willie Nelson.  Incredible people behind those counters.  Brazilbilly is great if you like old country, think Marty Robbins.

Don't bother waiting in line out front, go to the back and get onto the balcony.  You can scope out a seat below, especially when the bands change out or take breaks. 
The place gets really crowded, but have some patience - a server will come around to you if you have a table or you can always ask someone sitting on the bar stools to let you in to order, chances are they are regular barflys and will be more than happy to oblige.  

Try the Recession Special, a bologna sandwich, chips and beer for $5.  Or the Stimulus Special with a hotdog instead of the bologna.  The fried pickles are awesome!  And for anyone visiting from Louisville, they have Falls City beer!  Don't see that much outside of Kentucky.

No cover. No smoking. No pop-country.  Usually drunk, college kid free (changes as the night goes on, but nothing like the other Broadway bars).  

Robert's is true Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Don Kelley and company were terrific. We watched them on Fourth of July weekend. 

The lead guitarist, Porter McClister, was simply the most incredible player I have seen in some time. He works incredibly hard and gives his all for the audience. 

Kelley, meanwhile, is really funny. He entertains the crowd with a good sense of humor. 

The bass player's bass was really cool. He was extremely talented.

The bar, itself, was jam-packed with patrons. A host of them were dancing right there in the front. Others were drinking PBR and eating hamburger and fries at the bar. Good experience.

I had a great experience here, and look forward to returning to this particular place. Lot's of fun!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Obviously a place for tourists. Short wine pours. Mediocre food. High school type band too loud for dining. Not a be back.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: If you like live loud music (you can literally hear it from across the street), friendly bartenders, good beer selections, and lots of seating, then Tin Roof is your place. The music isn't quite Honky Tonk when I went, though. Think more college music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I ordered Breakfast Tacos.. Very good!!  I like the atmosphere  and the blueberry margarita

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Not only were the drinks delicious and light, the food was fresh and exceeded my expectations, but the service was unlike a typical dining experience. Our waiter Kenny, went above and beyond to make sure our group had an unsurpassable experience. The manager also helped created a unique experience for our bachelorette party! Thank you, both! We will be back next time in town!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Sit outside on the upstairs patio. It's gorgeous. If you're in the mood for a live band in a lounge setting, sit inside. The shrimp and crab dip was delicious. Also great cocktail selection! The items are pricy but you could fill up on appetizers to ease the wallet.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great food and service. Centrally located near downtown. Prices are reasonable. Only negative is the parking. I would go back!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Excellent venue for the Grand Ole Opry! Saw old Crow and the Gatlin Brothers play the last show of 2018 there.  Big Historic Church converted to a performance auditorium.  Four sets with a variety of unannounced performers makes for an evening full of surprises.  Certainly a "don't miss" event if you visit Nashville.

Note: original wooden church pews still the primary seating.  Bring a cushion as the 2.5 hours can be hard on the backside!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I had to leave a review for this because it was absolutely amazing. I wanted a nice dinner for my birthday and I found this place and decided to check it out. I got the Filet and Lobster and was one of the greatest meals I've ever had. The waiter told me to get it with Gorgonzola Butter (I don't like Gorgonzola cheese but figured to try it anyways) I don't think I'll ever have a steak that's tastes as AMAZING as that one did. The person who was with me even said that may be the tastiest thing I've ever tried.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: What is there not to love about the place? Outdoor seating, live music, delicious food, great service and a nice drink menu. My husband and I just happened upon this place. We were actually walking to a restaurant next door, but because their patio was booked for a private event we decided to check out Sambuca. So glad we did!! We had the cheese and prosciutto beignets, and calamari to start. Then my husband and I split the sea bass with lump crap and each enjoyed a glass of red wine; I had the Clos de Bois Cabernet and my husband enjoyed the Luna, a red blend. Oh, and our entree arrived split on two plates for us to enjoy...very nice of the waitress to have done for us!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Sooooo much history here.  Where everything on Broadway is new and so commercial, Robert's is Old Nashville.  No hipsters in here.  Just good country music fans who appreciate the local musicians.  It gets just as crowded and crazy on Friday and Saturday nights like all the other Broadway joints, but Robert's is pure history.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Someone told me that "there's not a bad seat in the house," and so far I've found that to be true.  I've been to a lot of shows here and sat in various parts of both the floor and the balcony, and I've never had trouble seeing or hearing the performers.  I like the pew seating, but I suspect that's partly because I'm on the smaller side, as people go; I've gone to the Ryman with people who are taller or broader than I am, and they seem a little less comfortable.  Concession prices are in line with what you'd expect.  But the history, the aesthetics, the acoustics-- they all combine to make this my favorite live music venue in Nashville, and one of the best I've been in anywhere.  I hope to do the tour one of these days.

name: Second Fiddle
text: This place is a lot of fun. You can find more authentic places (Robert's, Ryman, etc.), but this place just feels like a good time. The bands that at Second Fiddle were very good with involving the crowd and making it fun.

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text:
Stopped in here after leaving a show at Zanies not really bowing what to expect. Was thinking it was just a corner pub. 
 To my surprise it was much more than I anticipated. They had a live show which was acoustical and the folks inside were super nice. 
 My wife and I really enjoyed this hidden gem.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Awesome burgers!!! Fresh soft bread, the Angus beef is SUPER DELISH! And there is live music. 

We got there at noon and it got pretty packed shortly after. Great ambiance and a good low budget and local menu to choose from!!! Definitely a place to go

name: Robert's Western World
text: I have nothing bad to say about this place. My boyfriend and I stopped in pretty early one night during our stay and had a blast. Broadway certainly isn't for everyone (touristy!) but Robert's Western World felt less touristy than the one other honky tonk we checked out. The band was great, playing old country and interacting with the crowd. We knew we had to try the fried bologna sandwich because everyone on the Internet told us to. It didn't disappoint. It's not gourmet by any means, but it's salty, perfectly grilled, crispy and delicious. Basically like a BLT with thinly sliced bologna instead of bacon. We washed it down with some $2 MGDs and tossed our cash into the band's tip jar. The bartender was attentive and polite. It wasn't too busy when we were there but I imagine it (like all the others) can get packed on weekends and later at night.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My wife and I live locally, and have heard and read pretty good reviews so we decided to give it a try. We quickly found out that this is a bad Nashville tourist trap. The food/drink were priced on the high end, but they have done a good job with their menu descriptions. Unfortunately, the food quality and preparation were both terrible. I would expect this quality of food at your average wedding or cruise. For the record, we got 2 appetizers: dumplings & Brussels, and the flatiron steak and salmon for our meals. On top of that, our wine (by the glass) came out skunked. The service was great, but the live band was below-average (for a Saturday night in Music City). Really felt like we threw away $150 after that night. The first restaurant in Nashville that my wife and I will never go back to.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
My friend and I went here last night.  It was "ok."  I enjoyed the live music, and the bar tender told us they have different bands almost every night.  The atmosphere is nicer than some other bars in Nashville and its geared towards upscale (I said geared towards..not it IS upscale).  
     The food is somewhat greasy and salty, but I guess that goes hand-in-hand with beer.  However, I'm not a beer drinker.  We ordered the lobster tempura (if you want to call it that).  It was a disappointment.  The 3 small lobster tails were dipped and fried in what looked like onion ring batter with panko bread crumbs.  That my friends is NOT tempura.  I ordered the margherita pizza, which was beyond salty.  I could only eat 2 slices...I gave it a second try incase I just happen to eat a salt patch.  My friend ordered their striped bass with vegetable couscous.  The fish that came out was a very sad less than 4 oz filet that had soggy skin.  However, the 3 cups of couscous they piled on her plate was ok o_O.  That is not worth $32 dollars.  About the drinks.. I've "heard" around town that this place makes the 'best' drinks.  If you like mixed drinks that are sweeter than southern sweet tea, you found your place.  I ordered a strawberry mojito, and my friend ordered their 'signature' pink lemonade..blllaaaahhhh!  They should write in the description these are sugary drinks with a pinch of alcohol.  
     I gave this place 3 stars because I enjoyed the environment.  However, the service and the food are not worth it for me.  I forgot to mention..my friend and I had the "dinning experience" at this place.  In other words, we were here for about 2 hours waiting for service and food.  This is not the place for that..maybe I will come here just to listen to the bands?

name: Robert's Western World
text:
If you are in Nashville to hear good live music instead of the same 5 contemporary pop country songs being karaoke'd by every bachelor/ette party, you need to find a way to get into Robert's Western World. This place had hands down the most enjoyable music/band of any bar that I was in on Broadway. 

I can't speak for the food (although I don't know that the grill and fryer have ever been cleaned based on their appearance), but the fried baloney will always peak my interest. The music was great, the other patrons were friendly, and everyone seemed to be having a great time despite being packed in pretty tightly. 

If you want to dance and sing to songs you hear on the radio, go somewhere else. If you want to enjoy good music by quality musicians with others that also have an appreciation for the music, this is the place to be.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Visited for a show. We bought tickets online and the line up of artists were not what we purchased. But we made the best of it since we were there. The singers and musicians sounded great. The comedian was very funny. We went there mainly to see Dustin Lynch.  He came out at the end and only sang 3 songs. We were expecting more of a concert type of event. The seating is in wooden pews and our backsides were aching sitting in them. Seating was tight, we were all squished together. Made it a little uncomfortable. It is a live radio show so there were a lot of plugs for the sponsors of the show. That seemed alittle odd, but guess that is how it works there. Probably wouldn't return there for a show.

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text:
Great place for bands. 

It was understaffed when I got there to run the cover table for a friend's funk band. Bartender and Owner, however nice, was definitely upset since her help didn't show up that night (the waiter/other bartender). I felt so bad I almost hopped behind the bar!

Regardless, the stage is well-fitted for up to a 6-8 piece act and something of a wonder. The tables, however, are set up like a cafe and people end up moving them during the show which does not allow for prime seating. People end up in the back talking near the bar where more seating is available which can take away from the integrity of the show. 

Bathroom is clean and majority of the place looks well kept and cared for. 

Overall it's got a great bit of character. Good drink prices for well drinks and beer as well as decent food!! Go for it! :)

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
With a night to spend in Nashville, I thought it would be best to find a place with live music and food.  Sambuca came up a few times on google so even with an average rating on yelp, I decided to try it out.  Long story short, I am never listening to google again.

Sambuca has a stage on one end with various performers almost nightly.  Tables and booths are facing the stage giving it the proper attention.  My server was super attentive and sweet.  Service was the only "wow" factor I got from Sambuca.  I ordered the beignet appetizer and filet entree, and while they weren't bad, the food in general was only average, to say the truth.  The filet was a bit soggy to the cut.  The butter sauce was not complimentary to the steak.  The drink (sambuca sling-back) was strong with no particular flavor.  Food is overpriced and I was not satisfied from the food to the drink to the ambiance.  This place was unbelievably dark!  Everyone around me had to use their phone in order to read the menu.  Maybe I was expecting too much.. But I'm sure there are other restaurants that can better represent Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Very disappointed!  We couldn't eat there. They would not allow us to stay due to my brothers back pack. They have a No Backpack policy. My brother has to carry this due to the chemo that he is going through right now. When he told the man at the door what he had in there, he said come in you're fine. We were maybe 5 steps in when a woman came up to my brother and said that he couldn't be in here. He started to tell her what he had in there and she said " I don't care you can't come in here with that back pack, you need to leave!

If this is how they treat people with cancer, shame on them!  No compassion!  

My mom taught me it's all about how you say something.  This was cruel. 

So disappointing!

name: Legends Corner
text: I love Legends.  Lefty Ferguson is the best entertainer and his band is awesome especially the keyboard player.  Lefty has a great voice and is the best guitar player.  What a great musician.  He plays on Friday Saturday and Sunday from 10 am to 2:30 pm.  Love him.  Every time I'm in Nashville I never miss going to Legends.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place is the real deal country! They play all real country music not the stuff you hear on the radio lately. The staff was friendly and attentive and the beers were cheap! My boyfriend got some food and wasn't impressed but it is just a bar so can't hold the food to too high of standards. The live music was great and we will be coming back.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This WAS the Grand Ole Opry where history was made. It was fun hearing the stories and taking the tour, seeing backstage, the dressing rooms, etc. The video showing the history of the Ryman was interesting and the spots featuring Minnie Pearl were priceless. They still have concerts there and I would love to attend one of those.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This place is something you definitely have to see, it's an amazing experience, however once you've seen it, or been here, you really don't have to see it again. It's cool that it is still a live radio show, and the acts change from time to time.

There were a lot of people I had never heard of, but are or have been a huge part of the Country Genre Community. The closing group was Alabama, and I actually knew songs they had sang, but a member was sick, so they ended up not performing. That was a bummer. 

My mother went on a tour of the location earlier in the day, I didn't, and when we went to the "show" she told me this was everything that was on the tour besides the performances. So she felt it was a waste of like 30 dollars. Which I would have agreed with if I had gone on the tour. She was also bummed there wasn't a discount for Senior Citizens. Which my mother always looks for and as a 65+ Beautiful lady, she deserves to ask, and should be given one. All Senior Citizens should get a discount here, but sadly they don't. 

Anyway, go, if you haven't been here before, or decide do you like country? Yes, then go see the "show" but don't waste your money on a tour earlier. Are you not the biggest Country Music fan, and/or do you know the acts that are performing while you are there? If not, then book a tour, but don't waste your money on a "Show". That is how I would have decided if I knew what we knew when we visited.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is a must especially if John England & the western swingers are performing. ( every Monday night). The group is the best we've heard this week. Gets the crowd right into a good time either singing or dancing.
 The bar is great and friendly with great weight staff

name: Robert's Western World
text: This was my favorite bar on Broadway. It was a small enough space to feel close to the stage but you are not packed in like sardines. . . like at Tootsie's. The band playing was old school, felt like Elvis era country, I loved every second of it. As one of the oldest bars on Broadway, this music seemed fitting. They also have amazing grilled cheese to help with the drunk munchies.

name: Second Fiddle
text:
Fun place to listen to great music and have space to dance. Worth a return!
Great shots as well!

name: Legends Corner
text: One of my favorite bars in Nashville! Got to this venue around 1am and it was still hopping! The band there played a wide variety of music, including classic rock, country and even some 90s hip hop! It's one of the cheaper bars when it comes to purchasing beverages, so keep that in mind! There are a couple of bars, one up front with the band and one in the back that's not as crowded. Overall, a great time!

name: Legends Corner
text: They had the perfect drinks. The live music was good. And the bartenders were great and fast! I'd return!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Reading Marcia's Yelp and I want to say about the same thing except I was the tourist and we got a taste of the Nashville Country Culture.  We were recommended by Danny at Gruhn Guitar.  No Cover.  The band folks canvas the joint for tips and we bought the CD.  Read later that this is the best souvenir to buy when in Nashville.  We can check that one off.  Great bar service as well.  We got extremely lucky and got an actual table with a seat thanks to a kind fellow that had some extra room.  On the pricey side for a couple beers and 2 shots of Fireball Whiskey but again, it was very worth it because this is exactly what we wanted to experience.  And we were able to do it at 7:30 when Broadway was not full of drunks yet.  Perfect for our taste.  Good old Honkey Tonk music.  A must visit for Tourists and I know Marcia is right when saying probably not an everyday place as it would get pretty monotonous but this Yelper and my wife really loved it.  The eclectic crowd also made for amazing people watching.  All kinds.  Crowded and loud and we loved every minute of it.  A real must see on Broadway!

name: Second Fiddle
text: The band was good and the beer was cold, but seriously... How does a bar named second fiddle hire a band without a fiddle???

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Ryman is must see for any country music fan or historian. You will not be disappointed. Take your time and soak in the smells and aged architecture that they have preserved. Well narrated and lots of artifacts and information available to view.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Mother Church--a force to be reckoned with. Did you know that up until about 30 years ago, drums weren't even allowed in here??

I took a tour of this place with my Music Business program in college, but didn't see a show there until last night. 

The atmosphere is quaint, but charming. Stained glass windows, church pews for seating, incredible acoustics and not a bad seat in the house! It was so intimate, I literally felt like I was on stage with the artist.

Overall, a great experience and a Nashville must-see. Will definitely be back soon and often.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Great venue! The sound is terrific and the staff are very nice.

Drinks are on the pricey-side.

During the encore, they had security guys come to the front... Which was disruptive... And sucked 'cause they took audience members' spots. I was a total bitch to one of them about it and he just took. So I guess that was nice.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: LOVE Plaza Mariachi and all the local goodness it brings to our neighborhood! There is always something fun happening, from live music to salsa nights to soccer or hockey games on the big screen! Try the ice cream shop in the food court- the coconut flavor is to die for!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: we stopped by for lunch this week and tried a bunch of things. i had the falafel plate from kouzina cafe and hubby had steak and fries from tres gauchos (he's from argentine and said their red chimichurri sauce is "the real deal"). then we both got coffees at madera cafe and did a little grocery shopping at mazfresco market. everything we had was great (and also cheap!) and everyone we interacted with was so friendly and nice. the facility is bright, clean (including the bathrooms!), and family friendly. and apparently they also have live music and dancing on certain nights! =O we will definitely be back. i already decided i want tacos and paletas next time. i also noticed that they still have some empty store fronts available. can't wait to see what else moves in! =)

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This place was amazing and located perfectly by so many other touristy spots.  We saw the Grand Ole Opry here and the surroundings really teleport you back in time (those pews are over a hundred years old and the original pews!)

So much rich history in the place - very much recommend doing the tour afterwards so you can see the dressing rooms and get a chance to learn more about the history and past.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We had a lot of fun here! The band was very inviting and adventurous (they were willing to try any recommendation). We just got drinks and sat near the band.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
It's a honky tonk, it's a bar, it's a western wear store!

Iconic spot in the heart of Nashville. They've got a great collection of memorabilia. If you're in the market for gear then you're sure to find a pair of boots or a ten gallon hat to fit your style.

Grab a bite, grab a beer, grab a boot and scoot.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
We love this place!!! Miso sea bass and shrimp crab dip are to die for! 

Staff is always friendly but you need to make reservations in advance (more than 1 day).

Love the romantic atmosphere and the music sounds great. Highly recommend for date nights and birthdays. Birthdays get a free dessert too ;)

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Cool spot with 4 levels, live music, excellent food and cocktails. I had the spicy blueberry marg, ceasar salad, scallops and the cheesecake sopapilla. All excellent!

name: Legends Corner
text:
I would not normally take time for this kind of crap, but the security didn't do them self any favors. 

For my sons 21st birthday we came to Nashville, great time! But the security Gaurd decided to judge my son and thought he was a bum, and told him he pissed in a trash can and kicked him out. Even though he was with us the whole time. Then they let us know that he wasn't allowed into 3-4 different bars 

As far as I'm concerned if somebody  pissed on a trash can they should be reprimanded. My kid didn't and and legends should piss off. Bummer for them.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
On the strip of broadway, in downtown Nashville - where the bars are kind of like the houses in any major city suburb - cookie cutter, but the superficial accents separate them slightly - Tin Roof was set apart the night of Wednesday, Feb. 27.  

Myself and a handful of coworkers strolled in because of the band's teaser - mashup of jazzy reggae - that spilled into the streets.  They were awesome and friendly - if I lived in the area I would make a extra effort to see if they were playing at Tin Roof again.  

The service as received was lovely compared to other locations on the strip.  They were kind, attentive and the drink prices were ok.  

Didn't get food.  The bathroom looked moderately clean - but my judgement was after a few drinks. 

Overall - nothing orgasmic, but I'd check it out again.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Fried Green Tomatoes, Tots, Biscuit Sliders, Chicken and Waffles all delicious and fab service!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Live music on a Monday afternoon?  You betcha...Great atmosphere and cold beer. The cook was a little busy but the burger was cooked perfect and fries were super hot and stayed warm until I finished them off.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Sometimes I give 5 stars rating because the place is so in a class of its own.  Robert's Western World is such a place.  
- It has a long music history.  
- There is live performance of old country music from eras before I was born.  
- The all day beer special is $2.50 a can, tax included.  
- The simple pub menu is headlined by fried bologna sandwich (hint - the bologna sandwich was salty and delicious). 
- The interior hasn't seen a decor update for eons.  
- The place is so divey that the ceiling lights in the ladies washroom don't work; the washroom is lited by a contractor work lamp.  

I think this was the way it has been since a long long time ago, and the way it will be for a long long time.  And I enjoyed it.  I loved that John and Lois still perform here after 40 years.  I loved that they were transparent about their service level/style during weekdays, as they put a note on the menu to tell customers to order at bar themselves.  We did get waited during our visit because the business was slow.  I Ioved that the waitress didn't watch over my shoulders for tips.  She just let me put the tips in a big jar on the bar at my time, because who wouldn't when she ate a completely full filling Recession Special for $5, unless she has indeed been hit by recession, then the waitress would be completely understanding.

If all the nostalgia doesn't make you think Robert's is in its own class, it is the only pub on honky tonk that has a Pokémon Go gym named after it.

P.S.  No cover charge.  Ever

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Very informative tour! You get to see a few different dressing rooms that the artists still use to this day. Also get to learn about the history of the ryman, the mother church of country music!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Service is crap in the middle of the day! No matter if u sit at the bar or a table!  Music is good.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Classic spot on Broadway for some honky tonk music before you leave the city. It's old school and classic country. Great price for drinks and friendly service.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: So sad this was my favorite in town ! But they removed two tables to make a dance floor well after we were sitting and ordered round of drinks.  The manager who was also serving at the bar and not managing the floor or customers could have cared less. She basically said too bad for you . Would not have been a big deal if it was just me. But I had brought in a group to show them my favorite bar. Well as another bar sober in town said you need to manage your business keep your customers happy . Tin roof has forgotten that they could care less if you come back

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text: this place rocks! tonight i saw john carter cash play along with wes orbison and john carter cashs son joseph john cash....it was amazing!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Great cultural place for live Latin Music but most of the food is WAY overpriced for the quality served. Colombian empanadas one order of 8 are $13.95 and they pull them frozen out of a bag. You can go to Cucharitas and get the same thing for half price. The juices are made from concentrates that come from a jug and they charge almost $7 each. I had three juices empanadas and an order of Yuca fries and it set us back $33. If you know anything about Latin food that's rediculous!  The Argentine place Tres Gauchos is cool, but again super pricey for what they serve. I'm not paying $20 for a steak in a food court on disposable plates. I would definitely go back for the music and a beer but don't think I will he taking my family there to eat again anytime soon. There are much better choices for most food options within half a mile for most stuff they serve there at other restaurants up and down Nolensville Rd.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Love this place.
Great place to come and eat, listen to live music and have some cocktails

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Fantastic cheap Mexican food that I was treated to for lunch by my boss. The food is freshly cooked and perfectly prepared I had the chicken sofrito with rice and beans and it was spectacular. This area of Nashville is an ethnic enclave with great international food.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Really! How insulting can you be? Shrimp and  crab bisque came. There were onions and celery. No crab or shrimp. We sent it back. Our lovely waitress brought us a new serving; telling us that they had added an extra scoop of shrimp and crab. It must be a 1/4 tsp of something, mostly onions and celery. DON'T spend your entertainment dollars. AVOID. Very high priced entrees, no problem if there was a value.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We toured the ryman this morning. We did the self guided tour as well as the guided backstage tour. The guided tour was good, wish it was more informative and our tour guide was a little more articulate. We had trouble understanding her at some points due to her mumbling. The video that started the self guided part was the highlight! Absolutely exceeded my expectations. Great job ryman.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Must see in Nashville.

Take the backstage tour to get the best feel for the amazing history and talent that had passed thru here.

My wife is not a huge country fan but even she was impressed with the tour and history.

Only thing better would be attending the Grand Ole Opery show here.

Tip leave enough time.  We went on the 3:30 tour and were pressed for time on the self guided portion if the tour.  They close early if there is concert/event scheduled which is Friday and Saturday.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I had never been to Nashville and decided to make Robert's my first stop on Broadway. The food was cheap, the music was loud and fun, and the place was packed despite it only being 3pm on a Thursday. After hopping around to other places on the strip, this place had a more dive bar feel that I vibe with while the others felt more upscale. I imagine Robert's hasn't changed much since they opened and that this is what Nashville felt like decades ago. Definitely a must stop and a great value. I had the mushroom and swiss burger with chips and my wife got the "Recession Special" (fried bologna sandwich, chips, a PBR, and a Moon Pie). Our total was like $12 which is insane to me considering you're downtown in this area. Keeping prices reasonable encourages crowds to show up and makes it easy to be generous throwing money into the tip jug for the band.

name: Music City Center
text: Sitting in the lot for over an hour and now have to try to follow the direction of ONE person. Poor lady.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Among our stops while on Broadway was Roberts. I was relatively sober here....relatively being the optimal word

~The Good~
This place gets slammed harder than...well you take it from there on that one. It is a much smaller space that its neighbor Tootsies off to the side. It has two floors, both of which serve, and allows for passerby to congregate listening to jams. Drinks were decently priced out. I had a couple shots to get my night going and it was actually a tad cheaper here compared to other spots. The space up top allows for you to exit, as well as re-enter, rather than using the upfront line. This is helpful when all the tourists start flocking in. Music was loud but not to the point where I am screaming, which was nice. Overall a fun little spot... Oh oh, and NO COVER!

~The Bad~
It's just so small! I was elbowing people, people were elbowing me...even my shot glass was elbowing a beer bottle. Maybe that adds to the flavor of this spot.. not sure. Really small and cramped space led for a relatively quick exit for my gang after about 45 minutes of messing around. The music was also not as strong...I love most music, but old-school style country music in a bar seemed a bit off for a Friday night. Wasn't really amping me up like Tootsies louder bands did. 

~The Downlow~
This is a fun, albeit smaller bar on Broadway. Still, drinks are priced well, no one wanted to deck me for dancing like a fool, the atmosphere was still pretty chill and heck... NO COVER on a Friday night. Overall that adds up to 4 stars. Perhaps if the band was a bit better I'd bump it... Maybe next time Nashville ;-)

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My girlfriends and I spent the weekend in Nashville for my bachelorette and we wanted to go to at least one really nice restaurant while we were there. Sambuca did not disappoint! Our server was absolutely amazing. (Shout out Emerson! Thanks for everything) He took the time to explain the menu and all of the drinks. I had two cocktails: The Cock 'N Bull which is their take on a Moscow Mule, and a Royal Basil lemonade. Both amazing. My friend and I split the chili rubbed jumbo scallops and the salmon oscar with brussels. Both were incredible. Perfectly cooked seafood and seasonings. The crispy rice cakes under the scallops were also a nice touch. They also surprised me with an announcement from the band with my wedding date and an amazing flourless chocolate cake with a candle for dessert. The live music was wonderful. I couldn't have had a better experience at this establishment. I've already recommended to a few of my coworkers heading to Nashville next week!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
Great center with delicious food court and in my opinion the best live music in Nashville!! The 5 person mariachi band is excellent -- better than the ones I've heard in California. They've definitely made me appreciate Mexican music that I've previously taken for granted and never really noticed. And the stage is impressively well displayed/built. 

We loved tasting the various Spanish/Mexican-influenced cuisine in the food court. Unfortunately we didn't love the churros at the "Hot Churros" booth (because as Californians we're forever spoiled by Disneyland churros). 

The atmosphere and decor all create a really nice cultural vibe that's refreshing to find in Tennessee. Also, every employee here is so friendly & courteous. 

Worth checking out! Especially if you're tired of hot chicken or the crappy inauthentic Mexican food in Nashville!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
My wife and I were on a week vacation to Nashville, in what was the coldest week they had seen in a decade. This is why we came here in January!!! But I digress. It was New Year's Day and a lot of the places on the main drag were closed, but Robert's looked fun when we went in.

Dave Cox was the band, he plays covers of old country hits, really good. They all play for tips here, so I bought his CD for $10 and thought the hour we spent there listening to him play was well worth 10 bucks for 2 people.

Kind of a narrow place, but an old time bar. No draft beer, which is my only fault, but the waitress was nice and the prices for a Bud were reasonable. The food looked like regular bar food, but we didn't try any.

If you like old country hits (Nelson, Cash, etc....) Check this place out!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This place was great, the bartenders were a lot of fun and had great recommendations

name: Sambuca Restaurant
