text: I love this place!!!  Great spot for dinner or even just drinks and live music.  When I'm in Nashville, this is where I go for guaranteed enjoyable time.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
I LOVE this place! So much so that I went twice in one weekend!

My husband, four year old daughter, and I decided to give this place a try on a Friday night (then revisited on a Sunday morning).  It was a cold night and we decided to venture away from our usuals.  Upon entering Plaza Mariachi we were pleasantly surprised!  First of all this place looks great!  It has the feel of a Mexican marketplace with authentic stores, food, kids area, bar, grocery store, and even a radio station.  

On our first visit I decided to eat grab food from Tres Gauchos which is listed as an Argentinean steakhouse.  This restaurant is located in the "food court" but don't let that fool you the food is very high quality.  I knew this place must be good because the line was long.  I placed and order for the flank steak with a side of Mexican street corn.  My husband decided on Chisme Cafe and ordered nachos and street tacos which he enjoyed.  Everything was delicious and my daughter danced to the Mariachi band while we ate.  After dinner we went and grabbed a Margarita at the bar and headed to the play area.  My daughter was highly entertained by the large play structure and we were entertained drinking our margaritas watching. Upon leaving we stopped at Botanas Lokas and grabbed some delicious churros!

Sometimes living in Nashville I feel like there is not much to do for families.  I am so happy to have found Plaza Mariachi.  It is an amazing place that I will be visiting again very soon.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We couldn't visit Nashville without seeing a show at the iconic Ryman Auditorium. Located right in downtown it's super easy to get to as a visitor to the city. We saw Penny & Sparrow and Drew Holcomb and the Neighbors and had an amazing time! The venue itself is smaller and more intimate and the performers were very personable. When they would break from the music and talk to the audience it was really engaging and not something that would work as well in a huge stadium. The energy of the audience was also something special. My only complaint is the wooden bench seats start to get pretty uncomfortable after a while. We ended up standing in the back to finish off the show, which turned out to be great because I could move to the music!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My husband and I went in on a Wednesday night...which Sambuca says has a happy hour from 4:30-6:30. We had reservations and had a nice spot right next to the kitchen (sarcasm because there was NO ONE HERE) and could hear the band warming up. When we asked about the "happy hour" we were told that only applies to the "Cocktail area." Are you kidding me?!?! The happy hour is displayed on their menu being served to me in the restaurant area. After inquiring about this, the waitress told us we could get the "happy hour" special only on our drinks, but not on the small plates and acted like this was doing us a favor. So by now we know that there is a happy hour which applies to drinks and small plates, but not to the restaurant area. What a joke! We walked out without ordering and we will NEVER come back here to this pretentious, expensive restaurant...and we didn't even try the food.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
If you're going to go to one honky tonk in Nashville, it pretty much has to be Robert's Western World. Don't let the name fool you, it's not some shop full of cowboy boots and hats for purchase. No, no, it's a dive bar right on the NashVegas strip with live music, cheap beers and where fun times are abound!

Robert's encapsulates exactly what you'd want from your honky tonk experience with beers that aren't at overly inflated prices, good music and a nice upper area for big groups. Thanks to my fellow Yelpers for bringing me here in perhaps the biggest UYE I've ever attended.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Absolutely amazing place of musical history!!! Thank goodness they didn't tear this place down. A Southern treasure that should be seen by any music lover of any genre!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Good food, good service, good drinks... Came here on a Friday night in August and encountered no wait to sit outside on the patio. Our server was attentive and offered a great suggestion as I was in between the salmon and the scallops. I took his suggestion and did the scallops and was so pleased I did. The flavors of the scallops, the tomato sauce, and the seasoning used paired with the risotto cake was out of this world. I encourage you to visit The Gulch and Sambucas. Oh and did I mention the $5 valet?

name: Legends Corner
text:
There's a bouncer at the door checking ID, ensuring that you are 21. Friday & Saturday nights are the most popular and it's wall to wall inside. ....just like walking on the street. 

Seems like the music is pop rock as all the 21 year old girls in the audience know the words and sing along with the band.

The norm is no cover,  and beets are about $5. Male sure you tip the band when they pass their Buckley around!

Always a fun time, and you might actually hear some good music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
When it comes to reviews, I have three things that make up my ultimate 5 star rating. What brings my rating of 5 stars to Sambuca?  Well, ultimately it was the overall experience my party thoroughly enjoyed. This enjoyment is courtesy of your incredible server Molly. 

I found myself working in Nashville temporarily for 4 months, and some of my dining experiences were truly not up to par. When we sat down, I was coming off a rough work day and needed a lift. Molly arrived at our table with a smile and uplifting positive attitude. This was exactly what I needed. There is nothing worse than a server who seems like they despise their job. Having served before, I can appreciate and respect everything they have to deal with during a shift.  I informed her of the lousy day that had preceded us walking into your establishment, and that we wanted to have a couple of drinks to get the evening off to a better start. She suggested margaritas, and she was right. It made complete sense, of course margaritas inspire a fiesta in life. 

Molly's suggestions for dinner worked out perfectly too. I was in the mood for some seafood and her recommendation of the red snapper étouffée was just what I wanted.  

First part of the 5 star rating is atmosphere.  Second part was the food and beverage quality. The third part was customer service. Honestly, to me it is the largest contributor of the dining experience.  

I am not sure if your business recognizes its employees for its receipt of positive reviews, but if they do please recognize Molly for making it an experience for us, versus a simple dinner after work.  She is the primary reason I will refer business to Sambuca in the future. Thank you!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Worth the wait. I'm full, I'm happy and I'm going to sleep.

That should say it all. Love it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
One star for good biscuits and a bloody mary. Another star for the gift shops to walk around in during a very long wait. 

I expected at least a 20min wait for brunch Friday for a group of 9. Hour wait seemed long and I would have left except the place is far enough outside of Nashville it wasn't worth it to relocate. 

Finally got seated and ordered our bloody Mary's which were good and came with a piece of bacon. But they took a very very long time to come out. Actually everything took a while. Service is not a strong suit - but rarely is with large parties. 

Now for the food. It was just bad. We ordered various things across the 9 of us and no one liked their food. Hash brown casserole? Sounds great but it's more just strings of soggy potatoes covered in melted velveeta. I thought it'd be like a crispy cake with some onion and peppers and bacon fat maybe. But nope. The country ham? Foul. Super grisly and way to salty. 3 of us ordered the ham and all felt that way. 

On top of the food just not tasting good, we all had some hurting stomachs afterwards. I was looking forward to coming here since I heard great things. But it was a major disappointment and I will not be returning again.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My wife and I hit City Winery last Friday to see Matthew Sweet play.  This is already one of my favorite music venues in Nashville.

First off, it's just awesome to be able to sit and have a drink while watching a concert.  I think I'm getting too old to stand throughout a show.  The service was very good and I was impressed with the wine and beer list.  We were told that they would actually have wine for sale that they personally made (as any winery should) within a few months.  

We weren't sure about the menu because the show started at 10:00, but they were still serving.  We had already eaten, but did order dessert.  It was a peach dish and was very good--reminded me of creme brulee a bit.  The menu appeared to have an excellent selection and you're probably looking at about $20 per dish.  However, there are appetizers and desserts if you don't want to a whole meal (or, you could just drink).

This place is great.  Check out their calendar as they do have a diverse list of acts.  I look forward to trying their food on the next visit and could easily see myself adding a fifth star.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I'll probably be dethroned of my yelp elite status for leaving anything less than 4 stars for this Nashville staple, but honesty is the best policy, right? I'll start by saying that for me, the best part was the experience: the gift shops, decor, and southern hospitality from the staff. 

When we put our name on the list, we were told it would be a 1 hour and 45 minute wait. There are plenty of gift shops to spend money at while you wait on your buzzer to go off. It ended up being about an hour wait. I spent $30 on a ceramic berry carton, a tea towel, and foot cream. All very cute and I use them regularly so I don't regret any of them. 

As far as the food goes, (don't judge me, we hadn't eaten anything and my eyes are larger than my stomach) I ordered two eggs sunny side up, a fried green tomato and pimento cheese biscuit, home fried potatoes, a piece of fried catfish, & biscuits and white gravy. My husband ordered a few of the same things, but also pancakes. 

The good: the pancakes were huge and good. The biscuits and homemade jams were tasty. Not drive 30 mins out of my way good, but definitely the best thing I had. The catfish was tasty and I wish I had ordered the catfish supper plate. 

The bad: the eggs whites weren't completely cooked. I know a little is expected on sunny side up eggs, but I scraped more than I'd like to the side of my plate. The gravy was... weird. My mother-in-law also ordered the white gravy and we both thought there was something about it that was off. I had a couple bites wanting to like it and just couldn't eat it. It didn't taste old or like it had gone bad. It just had a really different flavor than anything I've ever tasted in white gravy. 

The meh: fried green tomato and pimento cheese biscuit. This was a 60:30:10 pimento cheese:biscuit:tomato ratio so I really only tasted the pimento cheese, which was nowhere near as good as my own homemade pimento cheese. The home fries were cut up in little squares and deep fried, probably frozen, potatoes. Similar home fries are available at Nashville biscuit house down the road from our house. 

I guess what I'm saying is that we won't go literally out of our way anytime soon to go back, but if we have friends visit who want to go, we will go back with them and I will try the catfish plate. Otherwise, I'm not in a hurry.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We decided to go here for brunch on a Sunday and the wait was 1.5 hours. We killed time by walking around and visiting the cute shops around the cafe. Ultimately we found out that it would be quicker to order carry out. We found a picnic table in the shade and ate outside. I had the two eggs with bacon platter with a side of hash brown casserole. It was amazing! I will definitely revisit on my next trip to Nashville!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Absolutely amazing!!!!  The drive from Nashville was absolutely beautiful.  Wait was about 45 mins but they have cute little shops to keep you entertained. Went in the middle of June so it was hot and humid. Once you are seated they bring these delicious biscuits and jam. If you arent a big eater than i recommend sharing a plate. Had the chicken fried chicken.. perfectly crisp with gravy on side. Mac and cheese wasnt anything to right home about. Cream corn was quite tasty. Over an amazing dinner. Definitely worth the drive!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Great place to catch a live music show! Fair ticketing and great prices....cheap valet parking. Eats and drinks are somewhat overpriced but getting a great seat for your favorite musician makes it all work out.

Pros- fair ticketing, clean, lots of drink choices, pretty good menu of food, they don't give you grief about taking a vid.

Cons-sort of pricey drinks, they pack you like sardines at little tables and its reminiscent of "family style" seating in fact you share table water, sometimes hard for servers to hear you.

So the seating is 3 tiny tables (if not more!) pushed together and 6 seats at those tables. Just hope you sit next to someone nice! As you will be VERY close, actually its ridiculously close. End seats are the best I think.

The shows never seem to drag out like they might at other venues. They seem to stick to the time very close.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Disappointing experience. We came to the winery with high expectations. The setting and wine were good but the food took over an hour and was less than impressive. The server did her best and comped one of the meals that came out cold and desserts but our bill was still over $300 for four of us. Don't waste your time here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Okay. So many things i want to say but really just go here.  The biscuits are obviously the star of the show.  The blackberry preserves are next level.  And to top it off , the waitresses are outstanding.  Danielle in particular made me feel like I was just part of the family.  She was absolutely awesome. Seriously guys.  Forget a birthday cake next year, I just want biscuits.  Okay that was too far...I'll take both.  GO TO LOVELESS CAFE!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Iconic location.  You could stand and look at the pictures in their main room for an hour.  Incredible menu as well.

I went in and picked up some sauces and spices for my father's birthday and they even put it in a little package with a card for me.

Worth stopping in!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is an event that everybody should do at least once. Yes, it probably is out of the way. Yes, there will be a wait. Trust me though, it is all worth it. There are cute little shops to check out and free lawn games to play while you wait for your table; and you can make the detour worth it by going for a stroll down the BEAUTIFUL Natchez Trace Parkway after breakfast/brunch. As far as the food goes, prepare yourself for mountains of the most delicious biscuits you are likely to find anywhere unless your grandma has been making them for as long as you can remember. I highly recommend ordering the pork barbeque breakfast platter, but you probably can't go wrong with anything on the menu. If the weather is nice, try to get a seat out on the side patio to further increase the experience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Delicious fried chicken. It's so worth the wait to eat here. Don't forget to visit the cute gift shops.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I give them 4 1/2 stars - dinner last night was excellent for the 4 of us at an early-Mothers-Day celebration.  Service was welcoming, friendly and fast.  Three of us had the sampler platter and I had the BBQ pork with sides of sweet potatoes and green beans - fresh and flavorful!
Great first visit and they honored our reservation for 4 on a Thursday weeknight.  
Thanks - we will be back !

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing food and the friendliest staff I have ever met.  A must eat when in town.  The pimento cheese burger is great.  Everything home made

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This place is very unique and must be experienced. When you come,  ask for Kimberly as she is the most professional and thoughtful server we have seen in quite some time. The food rocks too!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Cute little restaurant. As a tourist, saying it is in Nashville is misleading. It was about a 40 minute drive from broadway.  But the drive was relaxing and worth it if you are not in a rush to eat like my mom was lol. 
We had watermelon ribs, ocra, cream style corn, fried green tomatoes and mashed potatoes with gravy. It was all good. We also had a three dessert sampler plate that was delicious. Coconut cream pie, pecan pie, and the banana pudding. My favourite was the banana pudding. They need to turn it into a pie because they do a great pie crust. 
The server Mark was excellent.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I live about 15 minutes from the LC, and honestly I'd suggest finding a Cracker Barrel instead.  The biscuits are flat and dry and everything else tastes about the same as a Cracker Barrel (if not sub-par), but has a much higher price tag.  This is not a spot where locals eat (often).  Every time I pass by I shake my head at the tourists lined up outside.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: It wasn't bad but wasn't good either. Just saying for a place that prides itself on biscuits I ordered the pancakes thinking they would be awesome and I was wrong. My pancakes were dry, flat and tasteless. If I would have known that it was going to taste like this I would have not waited ninety minutes until we got a seat. My husbands country fried steak and eggs were good but nothing to write home about and my father in-laws ham and eggs were really salty and not good at all. Very disappointed in what we had. When I come back to Nashville this wouldn't be a place I would choose again. I just hope the jams I bought as gifts are better.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
So even though I've lived in Middle Tennessee for quite a while, I've never been to the Loveless Cafe until now. Some relatives from Cali came in to visit so we stopped here after picking them up for the airport. 

We arrived there at a time that most restaurants aren't that busy; smack dab between lunch and dinner. However it was still an hour wait here, and I'm actually shocked it was *only* an hour given how many people were there. 

I really liked the building(s) itself. For anyone who doesn't know, the Loveless Cafe and surrounding shops are a converted motel from the 50's. I love places like this; you can tell just by looking at it that it's a relic from the golden age of highway road trips. You almost never see such things anymore, as they've either been torn down or are in complete disrepair because they went out of business after the interstate system was built. 

The little shops were cool. Touristy but charming. They had quite a few interesting items, as well as some food such as jams and cured meats. I had plenty of time to check them out while waiting on my table.

Once we were finally seated, I was quite impressed by the service. Despite being packed to capacity, our server was extremely attentive and very sweet, taking plenty of time to explain the specials and whatnot. I ordered their blue plate special for the day, "Honeyspice" chicken or something to that effect. It was a half chicken barbecued with a spicy honey-based sauce. It was absolutely fantastic, as were the turnip greens and okra that accompanied it. The biscuits, for which this place is apparently known, were quite good as well. My girlfriend and I shared a slice of fudge pie for dessert and it was quite delicious. 

All in all it was a really fun experience, but the wait is long enough that this isn't the sort of place I'd want to go to regularly. However it seems to be a fantastic place to bring visiting family or other people who have never been, and it's definitely a place I think everyone should experience at least once.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This is really a 3.5...bit given the history, 4 is a safe number.

My stars...(5=epic "best of") (4=really tasty and want to go again and again) (3=good and will go back once in a while) (2=fair, might return for a visit if there was some glimmer of hope) (1=avoid at all costs)

Go or No?  Go

Tease:   The Loveless is known for their famous biscuits.  They are amazing...but everything else is just good.

Why I went:  For the biscuits!
When:  Summer 2012

Food:   I was in a group of 6 people.  Everyone enjoyed their meals.  We had a late breakfast/early lunch.  The BBQ was OK.  The fried chicken was good, but not "Gus's good", and all the fixings were tasty.  However, the biscuits were amazing.  They taste different than any I've ever had.  No gravy...just jams and marmalades.  The biscuits are super light and fluffy...and highly addictive.

Service:  Very good.  Our waiter was good.  Friendly enough, but not all that attentive.  He took the order well, but didn't frequent the table enough for refills, etc.  They were super busy...but they should be used to that and still give ridiculous service.  Not bad mind you...just not as good as we were hoping.
    
Hints/Final thoughts:  This is a tourist trap.  But it's a good one.  Just know the biscuits may not please every palette.  It doesn't taste like any others.  But, take them for what they are and they are amazing.  Everything else is pretty much just good.  Also check out the store...there are lots of cool foodstuffs, shirts and trinkets.  While their BBQ was a bit disappointing, they BBQ sauce isn't!  Grab a bottle!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I don't need to  add to  the other great reviews.  Do yourself a favor; just go.   And be sure to stop by the gift shop for jams, hams & biscuit mix. You'll be craving these within days.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
As a music venue, very nice. Great sound, physically spacious yet intimate-feeling. Except for my first experience, for Sturgill Simpson in August which was a crowd of Americana fans and a private event, I have never yet seen the place full, however. it's early, though, and I'm sure it's still getting its footing. It's about a 300-seat venue, which really helps you feel connected with the artist, but a lot of that has to do with the act, as well. It's not really great that you have to share a table for eight with people you don't know for dinner and a show; it'd be nice if there were more tables for two and four, as there are hardly any in the whole house.

The menu, however, is less impressive. Pretentious is okay if you can back it up with taste, but it's just not there. So, it's a pretentious and pricey fail. Since City Winery is a wine venue, it thinks it has to offer only complicated dishes, and I enjoy the occasional highbrow reduction or unusual flavor combination. The friend who was with me, however, does not, and that's okay, too. Sometimes wine is best when it accompanies something simple, and there is not even one menu item that might be qualified as uncomplicated or unfussy. Not one. Take a look at your menu, Chef, and relax it a bit. Give us a variety of options, to appeal to a variety of diners, in the way the sommelier offers the wine list. Everybody will win.

I will say that our server, whose name was Matt, I believe, was very patient and was happy to take time to explain every description and answer every question we had. I ended up with the beet salad, and when that proved too spicy because of the cayenne pepper, I ordered the cheese plate and made that work, although I did not enjoy the horseradish spread that was one of the accompaniments. 

Also, when we arrived, the seating staff said that we were to sit at separate tables, and of course, I wasn't going to have any of that. Our arrangements had us seated together, and I was polite, but had to insist that they check their seating chart notes again. After just a few minutes, we were led to one of the few tables for two, off to the side but still well in view of the music. I was happy that they made the effort to correct the error without any attitude at all. 

I did attend a private event at one of the smaller upstairs rooms that also had a little stage and a bar. I was helping at that event, so did not experience it as a patron, but I did notice that the bartenders were friendly and helpful, and the waiters seemed prompt at the tables. The hors d'oeuvres trays, however, lacked variety and imagination. Anyone can put crackers and cheddar on a plate with strawberries, but to be fair, maybe that is what the client ordered from the catering staff.

The parking is what everybody else says it is, but I have had great luck with the valet staff being exceptional every time. I've never waited more than a few minutes for my car. They really ought to offer the valet as complimentary, however, since there aren't any other real parking options. 

So, it's like this:

Main Music venue: B
Dining Menu: D
Service: B (Matt was a little slow, and rushed us on the check)
Private events: B
Parking: B-
Overall: B-

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Meh. The food is good, but not so good that it's really worth the wait. One in our group got french toast and it arrived cold. Checked it off the bucket list and will probably not be back.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: My last review was less than favorable.  I would still caution anyone to ask what something costs when the wait staff offers you an alternative, as they will always up sale you to the most expensive wines and liquors they have, but I will say my last two visits (yes I continue to go for the music acts) have been far more favorable.  The last two times it seems the food quality is back up.  This does make me happy because the acoustics are better than any other venue for music.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: There are no words! Everything is made from scratch they are kind of out of the way off the beaten path but we'll worth the trip. My husband had the gizzards he loved them the biscuits with sorghum and butter omg a must do if you are in Nashville

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is no joke and worth the effort. Go. Doesn't matter how far you need to travel to get there, just go. Eat the biscuits, order the fried chicken and cream corn. SO good! All of it was amazing... you'll leave full, happy, and ready to come back for more. I will definitely be coming back to Nashville just to eat here again. Instant favorite!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We had to wait on a weeknight, but that's kind of expected with the Loveless Cafe. The biscuits are delicious, and our service was awesome. She was very helpful and friendly. Everything on the menu sounds so great and well-priced. The homemade creamed corn was top-notch! 

I'll have to go next time for breakfast!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Oh my goodness, if you are looking for a hearty (and wonderful) breakfast, the loveless cafe does not disappoint! The peach jam was my favorite, and the pulled pork was fantastic.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I walked in for a quick biscuit and jam experience around noon on a week day. While the blackberry jam was outstanding, the biscuits were a little on the chewy side for my liking. And YES I'm from the south. ;) 

The most disappointing part of my experience here, though, was service related. Our waitress was incredibly rude and snarky. I overheard her making ugly remarks to the cashiers about my party in the next room. We were all extremely nice, but she was not. If you're looking for "southern hospitality" I'm afraid you won't find it here.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: It may be unfair to compare this establishment to the numerous restaurants I've visited in Germany and normally I would let this go. However, the Jagerschnitzel I ordered was the worst I've ever had. I sat at the bar where i was served by Kira, a lovely and very personable young lady. I ordered the Draft Flight and the samples were very nice. The Jagerschnitzel arrived less than ten minutes after ordering which is strange. Preparing this filet properly should have taken longer. The crust was almost impenetrable and the gravy/sauce coagulated. I mentioned my opinion to Kira and guessed that this meat had been prepared prior to my visit and was microwaved for quick service. She checked with the kitchen and indicated that this may have been the case. This place has the feel of a Munich beer hall and groups will have fun here, but the food needs to be stepped up.

name: The Basement
text: Caught a free Fruition and Dead Winter Carpenters show while here in Nashville last night at The Basement. What a treat for an out of towner to catch a couple of my favorite bands at a free show! The basement is as exactly as its name suggests. This little spot feels just like an unfinished basement, only there are great sounds emanating from it making the experience unique. The beers are reasonable and you can't help but drink them just as you would in your own basement. The other great aspect is that the musicians are accessible - luckily the members of Fruition and DWC were friendly! Thanks for a great experience!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We just had lunch at this establishment.  Good food and GREAT wine!  :)  The place is really clean.  The bar tender and server was really nice!!  We could not have asked for better!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I love this place.  We love Biergarten in Epcot and this reminds me of it.  Fun, festive, good food, good beer.  The food is not very gourmet, but I do not believe it is supposed to be.  I got weinershcnitzel the first time, it was very good, spaetzle was a little bland but I liked it anyway.  I don't like that the lingonberries were served in a plastic shuffle cup, it cheapens the place.  The pretzel and beer cheese app is awesome.  Potato Pancakes are like my polish mom in law makes.  We brought her home some sausages and she asked us to bring more next time, which says a lot considering she is polish and eats similar cuisine.  The pretzel pudding is heavy but delicious!!  The band was great, my daughter had a ball.  We went back again for lunch and loved it then too.  Our waitresses on both occasions were excellent.  We will be back.  It's new, has a little ways to go as far as the food but it's got a ton of potential and could turn out to be a new fun favorite place to go.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Food is awesome and so is the service.  There is always a wait but they at least provide distractions with the multiple shops!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Firstly - be prepared to wait for a table on weekends for a long time. We waited for nearly 2 hours to be seated and even though there are little nooks and crannies to explore whilst you wait, we'd exhausted them by the time we were seated. It's very popular!

Breakfast though was GOOD. I had a plate with different biscuits on it which was delicious. The jams and condiments were all outstanding. Would like to return for lunch or dinner one day.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Biscuits & jams were so delicious we visited twice in a 1 week trip (and bought biscuit mix & jam to go!). It lives up to the reputation and is worth the wait. (Just make sure you call 24+ hours in advance for reservations, especially for large groups, otherwise they won't take em).

BBQ pulled pork breakfast platter was huge and tasty. Fried chicken and waffles were okay (waffle was on the heavy and bland side), I subbed in dark meat fried chicken and it was super good. I'd order just the plain fried chicken dish next time.

Blueberry vodka drink with a souvenir shot glass for $11, it was really good... Maybe too good! 

If we lived closer, I'd be 400 lbs. Can't wait till my next trip to TN to return.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This review is strictly for the food at Loveless cafe. We waited more than an hour to eat. I ordered an omelet and home fries and a fried green and tomato biscuit. The food was good but probably not my favorite breakfast I have had in the area. That being said, I think I ordered the wrong thing.

The biscuit was good but not the best I have had in the Nashville area. My favorite thing I had was actually the blueberry cupcake I had for dessert. So delicious! The service was great and our waiter was very friendly. My mom had the chicken fried steak which I tasted and it was pretty good. My husband had pancakes, eggs and ham steak and he really loved his meal. I don't think I will rush back but it was fun walking around the property and shopping in all of the little stores.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Decent sausages but not great sides. Come for the beer and pretzels and not much else.  NO substitutions allowed.  Super slow service.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: In love with loveless! What an adorable place! Had to checkout loveless while in Nashville and I'm so glad we did. Didn't  get a full meal as we had dinner plans but we HAD to try the biscuits and jam which were AMAZING! They were so buttery and delicious along with the 3 samples of jam: strawberry, peach and blackberry, all delicious. We also tried the hash brown casserole and key lime pie. The hash brown casserole was so good, along with the key lime pie. I don't normally like key lime but this was delicious. I wish we would've had time to go back for breakfast or dinner. We did go to the gift shop and picked up BBQ sauce, jam and a few other goodies. Super adorable gift shop and grounds. Definitely worth going. Best biscuits we had while in Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The best fried chicken , home made biscuits, & toppings in the south-The best fried chicken , home made biscuits, & toppings in the south-The best fried chicken , home made biscuits, & toppings in the south

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The all-you-can-eat biscuits are tempting, but definitely not the best. They're not bad, but seriously, just a standard biscuit. The 3 jams they serve are apricot, berry & strawberry. All are very sweet. Again, nothing special. The food was beyond disappointing. Please, do not order the southwest omelette. It's a basic omelette that they ruin by dumping an atrocious amount of pace picante salsa on & inside before bringing it to your table. Of course, it's stone cold from the large amount of cold salsa that was just poured inside. For the price they charge & the crowds they draw in, it's completely ridiculous that they're serving such mediocre food. Sorry we wasted our time & money out there when there are so many other great places in Nashville.

name: The Basement
text:
Oh I adore The Basement. It's such a great place to see local and upcoming bands, and I can't wait to see the artists that I've been 5 feet from make it big. I love that it's musty and dark. I love the grungy nature of the bar and that you really feel like you are in a musicians basement checking out a show from a friend. I'd highly recommend just stopping in on a random night when you feel like hearing a live band that will be vastly different than the artists you'll see on Broadway. 
Of course you need to park on the street and might have to walk a tad and the drink line gets long, but those are minor annoyances when you consider the experience you are there to have.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Decided to stop here on the way out of Nashville after it being recommended by several friends. From what we had been hearing regarding its popularity, we expected to wait for a table. Luckily, with it being a Wednesday morning, we were seated right away. The host was extremely welcoming and made us feel right at home. The decor and atmosphere only furthered that feeling- inside is a quaint, country dining room, one that you'd expect to find in grandma's house. 

Our server, Ashley, was an absolute delight. She was extremely friendly, prompt, and completely made the experience for us. We feel very lucky to have had her although something tells me the rest of the service staff are just as warm and kind. 

The biscuits! I will dream about the biscuits the rest of my life. Ashley brought a few plates out for us during our meal, which we happily inhaled.

I had the garden omelette, which was honestly not any better to me than the ones I get at IHOP or Denny's. not bad by any means, but nothing special. 

All in all, will definitely be visiting Loveless next time we are in Nashville.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Nice happy hour deals before the show time - flat breads and wines for $7.
The wild mushroom flatbread was pretty good, unique combo.

name: The Basement
text: We went on a Tuesday night for "new faces". It was free, the drinks were pretty good and the music extremely fun.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Stopped in to meet my mom for a lunch 1st time going was impressed by the building and set up inside (it does have a strange location) had their selection for Nashville burger week the KLD far burger it was good but didn't get my vote they did offer s smaller portion due to the promotion which worked out fine for a hot day added on the zucchini fries and they were the best I have ever tried will eventually go back to try out some other items

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Awesome food, friendly service and outstanding atmosphere. Do leave room for desert, the chocolate pecan pie was well worth the belly ache from eating too much :-)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless Cafe is a classic southern little diner that never disappoints. It's a perfect southern eatery. The workers are so friendly and really make the experience even more enjoyable. Never had bad service here. The fresh homemade biscuits and jam are what I really look forward too, everything else is a bonus.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits and jam were amazing, the food was top notch, and the waitstaff were all super friendly and laid back and made our time there truly enjoyable.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great service, but the food really wasn't worth the wait. Granted we went on a sunday after church let out, but the food was just ok. Nothing that left me waiting to come back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
11:55am on a Sunday the day before the big eclipse so take that into consideration.  Hostess quoted 2 hour wait.  Yikes.  It's a long drive and we had nothing else to do so went for it.  It only took 1:15 and like all the other reviews will tell you, there's stuff to do as you peruse the small shops.  

Biscuits come out as soon as you sit down along with fresh jam and soft butter. Coulda stopped there.  Really fresh and soft.  

If it's summer when you visit, the watermelon crawl cocktail is total summertime drink. 

Ordered the Southern Sampler which is a choice of 3 meats and 2 sides. 
Fried chicken - A+.  My favorite of the 3
Pulled pork - A+  served on a thin pancake.  Awesome 
Country ham- C. A bit dry. 
Wife had fried catfish, also and A+ super tender.  

Waitress was no doubt slammed the entire time she's there but was one of the best I've ever had.  Great service.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: The beer hall ambiance tries to be authentic and most people here look like they're having a good time. The costumed staff are fast, friendly and appear to enjoy their jobs. The drink menu had several German white wines to choose from and hubby liked his beer. There's even entertainment starting at 6pm. However, the food is bland, dry and cold. The schnitzel tastes like it was made days ago and reheated. The Reuben rolls burst with so much grease I had to jump up and step back to not stain my clothes and several napkins needed to wipe our faces. The sausages and mustards were tasteless. And the fries were like eating strips of cardboard. Yes, we lived in nearby Holland and eaten at many German restaurants in the US, but sadly this was the worst.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Sehr gut fixings, as if I was back in Deutschland.  Great lunch; with my wife, we always enjoy good German cuisine.  We had the Bavarian Onion Soup and split a Currywurst plate.  Joey our server was spot on and of course our meal was topped with Spaten lagers.  All said...highly recommend.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I have to chime in to give a different perspective. Coming from a restaurant lover  from Chicago now transplanted to the south, the food isn't that special. You are coming here for the experience, the eclectic Nashville tourist trap. The biscuits and jam are great along with the fun little shops. But the wait is pretty awful all the time and the food is basic country home cooking. The meat was just strange. Great service though!

We went really early since we have a baby and made it out by 9am. At that point they were quoting over 1.5hr wait on a Sunday. Honestly not worth it, in my opinion.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Near my house but I don't go often because of the long wait. The biscuits, yes, are to die for. The salads are pretty awesome - ask for the creamy peach vinaigrette dressing!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best biscuits. Was visiting for a marathon and came across this place. Not your healthy California fare, but if you like biscuits (these were the best I have ever had) and fried chicken stop here. Fun place and friendly wait staff.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: After well over a dozen trips here I had my worst experience at a Nashville restaurant in years. Mediocre food every time I've been there. Terrible service. I won't be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is always a favorite place whenever we visit Nashville. Delicious food, great service, and a beautiful location. Their homemade blackberry jam is out of this world, their biscuits are delicious, and I have never eaten anything that wasn't good.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Perfect spot for a cold beer with a sausage snack.  Don't forget the pretzels. Enjoy a relaxing afternoon with friends and fun music.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I went to City Winery for the first time the Saturday before Valentine's Day this year. The ambience was very nice except you were sitting 2 feet from tables on each side of you. There was no privacy. The wine was very good, however it was pricy which was expected. I chose to go with the special of the day, "Cab and a Slab". They brought out my steak and I waited 10 minutes for them to bring my guest's meal out as well. When we were finally checked on we were told they had lost the ticket and it would be another 10-15 minutes for them to cook theirs. My plate was then taken back to be kept warm until the rest of the other was finished. I have never had this happen before. The steak was good except it was 6oz's and the sides that came with it were very small portioned.  After a $40 meal I was still hungry. The waiter Ryan was very personable when we first sat down and explained the menu, however we saw him maybe 5 times the rest of the night. I think he was overwhelmed! The table next to us had their plate taken back twice before she was finally served a warm piece of chicken, so we were not the only ones unhappy. We weren't able to experience dessert because by the time we got to dessert we had already been there for over 2 hours and had other arrangements we were late for. When we got the check there was an added alcohol tax on top of the food tax and subtotal. I was always under the impression that the restaurant was supposed to take on that responsibility. To top everything off, there is no parking and valet will make you pay $5 up front, and expect a nice tip afterwards. Just another way this place can nickle and dime you. I have never been so upset with an experience before, especially on a big night like Valentines, where you would expect them to have it all together. I would not recommend this place for anything other than drinks. There are too many other good restaurants in Nashville I'd rather spend my money.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
As good as advertised! We had to wait almost 2 hours on a Saturday afternoon, but the time flew by because they have plenty of casual seating areas and free iced tea to sip while you wait. And of course shopping :) 

Once we were seated they instantly gave us biscuits, and the food did not take long at all to come (we were afraid it might, since the table wait was so long). Everything tastes genuinely homemade, and the environment is friendly and cozy. We will be back!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I had a blast here. The wait was just under 2 hours, but there is so much to do on "property" of the restaurant that it was nothing. The experience was great and I can't wait to go back to try more of the menu.

The drink menu look fascinating, but I at 10 am and didn't want to partake in the moonshine cocktails that early in the morning. :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I won the Bushel and a Peck gift basket and was blown away at how fast it arrived to my door and everything was packaged to perfection (nothing broken, bent or damaged) .  Now I can't wait to try all the goodies in the basket. 
Oh by the way,  I am not just down the street or in a neighboring town.  I am about 30 miles West of Portland, Oregon.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Even on Sunday night there was still a 40 minute wait but it was worth it.   Waiter was friendly and came out with food right away when we told him we were hungry.  The best friend chicken I've ever had with sides of greens and green beans.   The biscuits were really good too.  I'd go back next time I'm in town.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits were fantastic!! Service was good. I wasn't crazy about their pork barbecue. I could've done without the cornbread hoecake they put under the BBQ. Id rather have it on the side. I'd also appreciate a choice of BBQ sauces.  They don't have any at the table so you have to ask for it. Their sweet potatoes had way too much brown sugar for my liking. I can't cay I was crazy about their coconut cream pie but I like the idea of the mini pies.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: It was suggested to us by a complete stranger at a resort in Crossville, he said if you go anywhere in Nashville the Loveless should be at the top of the list, well it was # 3, What a wonderful experience, we were warned that there are sometimes a long wait,We waited approx. 30 mins. After that we were seated promptly on the side patio and greeted a very friendly bearded waiter wish I could remember his name! He took excellent care if us! The food was amazing! Very sizable portions! I would highly recommend this to anyone visiting Nashville that us looking for a home cooked southern style meal! Two Thumbs Up! Can't wait to visit again nex

name: The Basement
text: It feels like the house party of the year in your neighbor's basement.  I make friends every time I go and always feel welcome.  I can't get enough of this intimate spot and love checking out the talent that comes through.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Maybe the hype is about the history of this place and the country store/farm house/home style cooking charm. The food isn't really anything spectacular, not even the biscuits. Maybe just not my types but they're pretty sad to me. Tiny little pieces and no texture but loaded of baking power. Definitely don't come here for biscuits. We had breakfast here, nothing special, meh! pretty salty ham and country fried steak was big, but you tasted so much fried grease after 2 bites and full. 

Came here again for dinner cuz some friends who's never been and wanted to visit this joint. We had the smoked pork chops, although tasty, the texture was a bit funny. 

Friendly staff and food came out pretty quick. But not a place I'd come for the food, especially seeing all the magazine covers on their walls.  I didn't grow up in the south, but surely had plenty share of southern cooking and this is just not the place, but it's pretty cute with the country store and all.  But for food lovers, don't come here for the food.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I visited Loveless yesterday with a party of 7 around 10:30am and despite the crowd we were seated promptly. I was excited to visit the restaurant and really enjoyed the service and atmosphere of it, but the food fell just a bit flat. My omelette was overcooked and the cheese inside was hardly melted and tasted just like craft pre-shredded cheddar. I couldn't finish it- and that was a $8 omelette. The grits I got for another $4 and the complimentary biscuits saved the meal, however. The owner (I'd imagine?) came out to talk to us for a bit and wished me a happy birthday which was very nice. 

Overall, I would probably not return because of the high price that did not match my food quality, but I still had a nice visit. The little shops around it are cute and my friends bought me a set of Tennessee drink glasses to remember the trip.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This was our first time. The service is still a little green but only 3 weeks opened. The music was really nice and interactive. 5 stars. We got the giant pretzel w all sauces. The beer cheese was our favorite, a must try. The food portions are large. I'm not a huge German food fan but I really liked everything. The decor is traditional and very noisy. Overall a winner in my book.  Defiantly go when the musicians are there. I can't say enough about them. We will defiantly be back.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Some people might love this but I found it horrid! Maybe because I have had real German food, but this is not even a close replica. Now I do love German food but my stomach hurt immediately upon eating the fake cheese sauce.  There was nothing real about this food, the potato dumpling was out of box paste, the noodles had no flavor at all, then that same fake cheese sauce was placed on top. With those canned onion rings in top. I tell you this food was bad, bad bad. Even the Hot Dog has a strange flavor the only thing that tasted okay was the pretzel( no sauce) and the sauerkraut.  Maybe the food would have been better had we 5-6 beers, but because we were driving it was not a good idea. Sorry we should have just grabbed a burger somewhere. The music was fun but loud as well.  Should have checked the reviews first
This is in response to owner asking when we went
Wir kamen am 15. Juli 14 um 15.30 Uhr und es gab kein Salz im Sepatzle-Wasser. Der Käse war nicht das, was wir benutzen, also wer auch immer die Soße machte, vergaß den echten Käse. Prost

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Stopped into here during a business trip through Nashville because they're supposed to be famous for their biscuits and gravy. While I did really enjoy my meal, I wouldn't say the meal was much better than I've had elsewhere.  I don't get how the biscuits and gravy are famous.  I wouldn't advise you drive 30 mins out of Nashville for the food. Perhaps the nostalgia of the place is worth it?

I would say that the staff were all super friendly!  Southern hospitality at its finest!  The place does have a nice southern charm to it too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This restaurant boosts on how all of the food is homemade southern cooking and I'm here to tell you it's absolutely not. Most of what we ordered was frozen or out of a can. I think the best thing about our whole dinner was the preserves and biscuits although the biscuits tasted like ones I've gotten from Sysco. 

My husband ordered chicken fried chicken, garlic mashed potatoes, green beans and fried green tomatoes. I ordered the meatloaf, mashed potatoes and fried okra.  My husband did eat his because he hadn't eaten today but I ate only about 1/4 of my dinner. 

I was so disappointed because I had heard so many good things about this restaurant since its revamping several years ago and I thought this would be a meat & 3 with true homecoming. If that's what they call home cooking they need to come eat with our family to see what real southern home cooking is all about.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The country fried steak here is amazing. We love it here & the service is always awesome too!!  You can't go wrong eating here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Best fried chicken and biscuits I have ever had!  Loved the not overly hard fried chicken with just the perfect crunch.  The biscuits that are delivered to every table are light and fluffy.  As they are warm, the butter melts into the doughy goodness right away.  Then add their fresh made preserves and you are in heaven.  We had peach, strawberry and blackberry.  The peach preserves were the clear winner of the three.  I was let down though with the sides.  The hashbrown casserole was only okay.  It wasn't very hot and ended up just tasting kind of bland.  Daughter's mashed potatoes weren't mashed well and she ended up with a very large piece of whole potato in her scoop.  The creamy coleslaw wasn't very creamy and was completely unremarkable.

Our waitress was just as nice as can be and make our experience here just peachy.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My mom came in town to visit and we made a day trip out to Loveless.  I don't think we realized that it would be as busy as it was.  We parked and went in to the restaurant and got our buzzer thingy and were told it would be an hour and a half.  Normally I would have gone somewhere else, but there is so much to do there!! We spent time walking around and visiting the various shops around the restaurant.  The employees were all nice and helpful, and they ship your items for a flat rate--and you can buy items from any store and they just walk it over and put it all in one box!  Really convenient for my mom, who ordered some holiday gifts!  When we got to the restaurant it was hard to decide what to get because everything looked great!  The fried green tomatoes were crispy and delicious, and my chicken fried steak was the best I have ever had.  It was enormous.  The sides were fantastic and the biscuits--out of this world.  The nice little blueberry and lemonade drink with the moonshine shooter was a nice touch as well.  I will definitely be going back!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Great venue. Lovely menu. The food has been the highlight each time I've visited. The wine list is extensive, although I'm not much of a wino. They also partner with a local shelter so I'm inclined to love their commitment to Nashville. This is easily my favorite attribute of the venue. 

During shows you're often seated with strangers. Not an issue for me since I love meeting new people. 

The service is so slow it makes coming here unbearable. I loathe coming to this venue based on service alone. They have table toppers as a feature to let your server know you need something. Unfortunately, it is extremely ineffective. Servers look past the table topper, ignoring your need for service.

While I appreciate their uniqueness as an urban winery and commitment to the local economy/people of Nashville, it pains me to say, don't come here expecting much more than a great show. Expecting anything more would be a disservice to yourself. 

Cheers!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Sadly had to walk out when told at 62 years old I needed to have id to order a drink. What??? Have had drinks elsewhere in Nashville without id. Silliness

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We went for lunch today and it was our first time here. Everything was excellent!!! Fun staff. Neat atmosphere. Good prices. Great food and fun shops to check out. The portions are huge so we have leftovers for dinner tonight. A must see.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: The service was very good  our server Micah made great beer suggestions. We split the king plate. The food tasted like it had been prepared hours ahead and just kept slightly warm   The pork chop was very good even being barely warm. Great atmosphere. Next time just beer and pretzels!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This is all I'm gonna say about this place. 

I was told my grand momma passed.  Nope, she's in the kitchen of the Loveless making biscuits and preserves. 

Yep, they are that good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
There's not a whole lot about Loveless Cafe I can contribute that hasn't already been said...but they are absolutely worthy of another 5-star yelp review! We came with a big party of 16 on a weekend while we were in town for a conference. It was hard to rally the troops to drive out to the middle of nowhere and commit to an hour + wait, but it was well worth it.  While we waited there was stuff to keep us occupied on the grounds.  We played corn hole and visited the shops. Side note: the people in the shops are just as nice as the wonderful staff in the restaurants. The girl at the gift shop let all of us try the different jams and was genuinely sweet at could be.  

We were seated in a back area where we had the whole room to ourselves. It was perfect! Our waitress was awesome and I can't say enough good things about every single member of the staff we encountered. I'm not sure how they did it, but every single order was right and came out at the same time. And of course the food was out of this world! You get a huge serving and everything is perfect. I'm glad I don't live in Nashville, because I would easily gain 20 lbs from eating there so often! 

We were the last diners in the restaurant that night, and did not remotely feel rushed out by the staff. They encouraged us to enjoy ourselves and stick around for dessert...which we gladly did! We had to hit the road to drive back to Chicago early the next morning, so they sent us home with a ton of extra biscuits they had leftover from the day.  Seriously, if you're ever going to Nashville, you HAVE to go to Loveless Cafe!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits, biscuits and more delicious biscuits. Honestly some of the best I've ever had. The brisket was pretty darn good too. My tip is to go early for breakfast to avoid the line. Luckily we arrived early enough and only had to wait 20 minutes. While we waited, we walked around the motel and country store.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I'd go back just for the biscuits, they were so good that I couldn't finish my breakfast.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Hands down one of my favorite places to go! Their biscuits and fried chicken are amazing!!!!! It's an iconic tourist spot but even if you have to wait they have cute shops and games and things you can do in the meantime! I'd recommend anyone go there.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
After hearing about the famous Loveless Cafe for the past 3 months, I finally had the opportunity to try it out. And I must say, it did not disappoint. The Loveless is much more than just a cafe. There is a gift shop, gallery, and a few other buildings. It's like a mini campus. If you love it in the restaurant, you can buy it in the store.

The cafe itself is very kitschy southern comfort. Comfortable enough and if you go during the week, there shouldn't be a wait. On the weekend, good luck. The menu is full of southern classics. They have a good cocktail menu and my strawberry drink was delicious. I even got a little souvenir shot-glass mug thing. They only have 5 beers though, non that are tasty. I would stick with the cocktails, even though they run about $11 a piece. The best part is of course the appetizer of biscuits. Their jam is to die for. I could have filled up on biscuits alone. Will definitely be buying some of their jam. The main courses were also delicious. Lots of side options. You can substitute the fries for any side (and they suggest, almost demand, that you do). 

In the end, you will leave this place unbuttoning your pants so you can breathe. It's a great tourist spot if you have people visiting. Little too touristy for me just to go back on my own. But maybe for those biscuits...

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We had a great meal and ate a lot of biscuits on this trip.  My wife got a nice smoked porkchop and I got the fried chicken.  The service was great.  This was a bit out of the way for us, but ultimately worth the drive from Nashville.  We enjoyed the jams and preserves, so we bought some in the local shops afterwards.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Solid menu and fast, efficient service. Decent German beer selection and reasonably priced.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wait was not too bad but long since it was a Sunday, but ABSOLUTELY worth the wait. Biscuits and jams were Phenomenal! Service and hospitality was top notch! A must dine when you're in Nashville.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Absolutely mediocre. If you want a beer by all means I would have one and then leave and go get dinner! The pork shank pretty much was so over cooked it had a few tender parts and the rest were great toothpicks.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Fun place with good beer but if you love German food you might be disappointed.   The quality of meat was good.  The biggest disappointment was the run of the mill gravy and tiny portions.  $27 for a King Ludwig sampler should have more than a spoonful of kraut and red cabbage.  Overall not worth the money and I probably won't return.  Very disappointed.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The wait was long (1 hr and 30min) but it was worth it. To start, the biscuits and preserves were tasty but it was the fried catfish that earned the 5 stars!! Fresh and fried to perfection!! Server was good too. While this place is kinda outta the way, it is a gem worth exploring.

name: Dirty Little Secret
text: Enjoyed the fun atmosphere with dancers, flashing lights & awesome DJ- Case Bloom. The drinks were good pours & the staff was quick even when it was crowded.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I wanted to like it. Recommended by a friend. Fried chicken was dry and over cooked. They gave me a new one but still the same. The gravy was cold and did not taste homemade. The creamed corn was yummy. The biscuits were also great along with the preserves. Service was great. Manager came and made things right but it was still very disappointing.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I'd never been to this (or any other city's) City Winery before until a recent show (Rickie Lee Jones) brought us out. A few artists I like had played the venue before but I'd never pulled the trigger on purchasing tickets. The price was right for RLJ and we'd wanted to see her for some time so we gave them a try. As a music venue it's pretty solid--we were on the balcony, which oddly had cheaper tickets and from what I could gather a much better view than anywhere on the floor save for the front row. In terms of atmosphere, it's a very chill/laid back show and I could imagine that some artists recede into background music material. Thankfully Rickie had requested no food service during the show and the audience was fairly involved so it felt like an actual concert not just an excuse to eat and drink with music in the background (she did a terrific set by the way).
The food was good+. A bit pricey for what it is, particularly portion size. For example, I ordered the shrimp and grits entrée which was $22; it was delicious. But, it was an appetizer portion at best. If they'd had 2-3 more scoops of grits with shrimp to match it would have been completely fair. The Brussel sprouts are really good, also a bit pricey for the serving size. And the desserts are really good (but again, very small serving sizes). Everything we ate was good but unless you order a burger you're apt to leave hungry if this is your dinner.
There's a good selection of wines but I honestly wasn't in the mood for wine. They have some house specialties, about $10-$15 a pour, and some fairly priced bottles to take home. I opted for 1 each of the 2 local craft brews they have on tap, both of which were good. My wife enjoyed the house white, though.

Parking is interesting--they do valet for very cheap (maybe $10 or less?) but if you go that route it takes an incredibly long time to get your car at the end of the evening, longer than the valet at the Ryman even. Pro tip--there's a $15 all night lot in the parking lot down the hill from the front doors--walk to it after the show and be on your way before the first person in line at the valet is.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Oh my.  Was I in for a treat.  I've been going to this place for about 6months and always ordered the 3 sausage plate until I came with my son and he ordered the Schweinshaxe. It was awesome.  Plus the Bartender Kathleen was very nice and knowledgeable. She sure made the experience better.  Definitely will recommend this place to my friends

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Went for late night snack after the Opry. Really fun environment.

We had the "German" onion soup. Very good.

Had a few Wurst with German Potato Salad and Sauerkraut 

Also the Shnitzel which was moist and crisp the Spatzel was really too salty though. 

I would go again..

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Great spot all around! Great food, excellent service!  Have eaten and experienced numerous shows here. Never disappointed. Reccomend to all.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I give this place a 2 star due to the hospitality Bavarian brieuhouse conducted. Food was wonderful but the staff wasn't something that I would call professional. My waitress Amy was astounding and very pleasant to be around! But the one flaw that I overheard was just rude and hateful. I can't remember the young girls name, she has short blonde hair wearing an ear piece, and wasn't in full uniform, she was speaking with another employee about another waitress. She was saying some awful stuff about my waitress. I felt that everything she had said was just mean. I feel like if they need to speak about anything not on the floor but in the back! Anyways, thanks again for the great food I doubt I'll be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: (Biscuit & Gravy review only) Being born and raised in the south I've had some good biscuits but the biscuits here were not what I expected based on other reviews. Now don't get me wrong, they were good biscuits, but truly special they were not(8/10 at most). Their homemade jam was good(9/10). Gravy on the biscuits was only ok(7/10). I still want to try their other food.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We had a private event here for my daughter's graduation from Vanderbilt.  We used the private room and patio and it was fabulous. We worked with Tianna and she was so helpful to me as I was trying to organize the event with 4 families.  The staff on the day of the party was wonderful (they set up all my decorations while we were at graduation) and the food was delicious.  I would highly recommend City Winery for an event!

name: Big Shotz
text: Worse place I've been downtown and I live in Nashville. I'll never go back. I was there with some people I knew and the bartender was looking at them asking them what they wanted when it was me paying for myself. When I brought it to her attention to listen to me and not them since it was my card she replied with "don't get an attitude with me". I purposely did not leave a tip but some how got charged for a tip on my card.... I guess stealing is ok to her.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Came here for Easter Dinner and was very impressed! The space is beautiful, well-kept and the perfect setting for a relaxing evening. We couldn't decide which wines we wanted, so we ordered a few flights and were impressed by all the wines we had. They recently changed their menu but we loved the food we had ordered.  Their menu is (obviously) wine-focused so everything we tasted matched really well with our wines. 

What really stood out to me however is the service.  All of the employees seemed genuinely happy to be there and were eager to help with any recommendations or questions we had. It seems as though management has really created a great atmosphere for the employees and it certainly showed throughout our dinner.  At the end, we spoke with Rayna who was absolutely lovely and as gracious as could be.  Her demeanor and passion blew us all away.  We will definitely be back soon because of her!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
First of all,
YES, YES, and YES! 

I came on a Friday night around 4:25 so it wasn't very busy yet and parking was not terribly difficult but I can see how it can fill up and become a challenge very easily. There are a lot of buildings on the property and if you don't look at the signs pointing you which way to go, it could be possible for someone to get confused as to where the actual cafe is. 
When walking in the main entrance of the cafe is plastered with autographed pictures of celebrities and country music stars who came and ate. 
It's warm and welcome. The decor is very Country but cute and fitting.

Once sat you get the choice of all day breakfast or lunch. They also have alcohol and some other specialty drinks. 
I got the Country ham platter. 
You can sub out the eggs for a long additional side if you do not want the eggs. I got the green beans "(delicious country bacon green beans), caramel sweet potatoes (not too sweet.. just right), and the creamed corn (good but definitely not what you would expect) 

The biscuits are to die for( softest, most buttery biscuits ever) as is every single preserve I got to try with it (peach, strawberry, and blackberry). 

My portion is huge. I got a huge ham steak, there biscuits, and three sides and I came alone! Haha!

The staff is fantastically friendly. True southern hospitality that makes the state of Tennessee proud.

There is a "motel" part of the property, as well as a barn, a "Hams & Jams" gift shop type, and then an area where you can have events such as weddings.

I see why this place is so popular and I highly recommend it for GOOD, SOUTHERN STYLE Grandma Sue's cookin'!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
After mine and my husband's second visit to Tennessee, we decided to stop by the famous Loveless Cafe that my cousin had been telling me about prior to moving out east.  

From the outside it's not much to look at and you'd totally miss it.  We actually did and had to turn around.  But after going inside and looking up a bit of the story, we found out the cafe was built out of the Loveless family house and preserved to look as it did back in the early days, which made it something special.

The waitresses were all so friendly and attentive.  It really seemed as though they loved being a part of this charming time capsule.  Coming from California, I not my husband are accustomed to real Southern food which seems to be massive, deep-fried and delicious.

My husband ordered the fried pork chops which came with two large chops.  They were so tasty he literally made himself sick because he refused to not finish both singlehandedly.  If I were to have ordered the same this would for sure have been a 5 star review.  I however opted for the white meat fried chicken plate.  I never eat chicken skin, but this skin was fried so well that the skin was not fatty and instead was crisp and delicious.  The chicken however was so dry I could not eat it.  I loved the biscuits which come free as soon as you sit down complete with several homemade jams and jellies.  

I will definitely come back next time I'm in Tennessee and ready to really eat, but I won't be ordering the chicken.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Drove 6hrs to this place as our first stop in Nashville. I'm only giving 3 stars bc the biscuits were worth coming here (the jam more than the biscuits.. kinda overrated and not worth over an hour wait). Waited 40 min to be sat (that's fine and was expected).. sat down and it took 30 mins for our order to be taken because our server didn't know how to multi-task. He was rude too when his tables (4 total) kept asking just to get their drink and food orders taken. He even gave one of his tables to another server because apparently he couldn't handle it. He kept doing things one at a time instead of all at once. I've served before and getting sat 3 new tables is no hassle. Very disappointed with driving all this way.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
SO much fun! This German restaurant is located in Opry Mills Mall and there is tons of seating for however many people are in your party. Big wooden picnic benches line the large space and there is a big stage with live music. Large bar area as well if you want to sit in a smaller space. 

The beer selection is really good, especially if you like German beers! The food was fantastic as well. Large portions and everything was served piping hot. Yummy! I had a wurst platter and it was more than I could finish. Sign up for their email club and enjoy a free pretzel appetizer. Plus 15% off in the gift shop if you check in on Yelp!

Great experience. I would love to bring my family back here!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We had a wonderful time at Marc Broussard (my favorite) in New Years!! Jared, our waiter was AWESOME!! Made us feel so welcome and was just so sweet! Great time!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Went for dinner at this place and it was one of my favourite spots in Nashville. The food is fantastic- I recommend the southern sampler. Our server handled our group of 12 like a pro. If you stop in take time to look through the little gift shops. I scored some candied bacon popcorn. Definitely recommend this place!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Stopped for lunch on our way to The Smokey Mountains. Well worth the out of route!!!!! Loved the grounds and things to do and see while we waited. Best biscuits I've ever had and the chicken strips were amazing! Will come back the next time I'm in the area!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Wow!

My former roommate and I met here for dinner while I was in town for a couple of days. I am so thankful she suggested this restaurant! The food was exactly what I was looking for as an out of towner- down home, country fare. I ordered the pit-cooked pork barbeque. The pulled meat was presented on top of two cornbread hoe cakes with a drizzle of barbeque sauce. The fluffiness of the hoe cakes soaked up all of the juicy goodness perfectly. The dish came with two sides. I chose fried green tomatoes and coleslaw. In true Tennessee style, I enjoyed everything with a glass of sweet iced tea. With the portions being as large as they are, I left with a full belly and a nearly full container of left overs. 

Our server, Owen, was very friendly and accommodating. When he learned this was my visit to Loveless Cafe, he offered a few suggestions of their more popular items. He provided excellent customer service and his humor & hospitality made for a memorable experience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing!!!! The biscuits were unlike any biscuit I've ever had!!! We had a 45 minute wait, but it went smooth because of the shops/activities to do on the same campus. We hope our travels will bring us back!!!

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text:
I stopped in while leaving downtown to avoid the rush hour traffic and only planned on having a beer or two. I sat at the bar and right away felt welcomed by the friendly bartender who had some great recommendations of their draft beer selection. One of her coworkers had come in on their day off (which I always think is a good sign of the vibe) and I ended up talking with them for a solid 2 hours. At this point traffic had long died down and I could have made my way home with ease, but I was having a great time trying new beers and hanging with those at the bar.
I decided to give their food menu a shot, and quickly found several options that sounded perfect (although definitely not the $13 frito chili pie...$13 ?!?!?). I ended up settling on the patty melt with fries. This was an excellent choice and I will definitely be tempted to get it again even though I love trying different items when returning to new spots. Will be a hard decision next time!
All in all, Fat Kat Slims has a good beer selection, tasty food, and even better atmosphere created by their staff. I'm all for going back to check out their live music and hang on the nice big wrapping patio in the Spring and Summer.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Visiting Nashville for the weekend and was taken here by family as this is supposed to be a Nashville staple (plus I'm a sucker for fried chicken and biscuits). Dropped by on a Saturday around 1pm. We had to wait for about an hour before a table became available (we were a group of 6). Here's my take on this establishment:

1. Service: Our waiter was superb; friendly and explained everything to us. The lady who greeted us at the entrance and took our names down was not so friendly. 

2. Food: I got the Loveless fried chicken with two sides (turnips in liquor and caramel sweet potato). The fried chicken was yummy, but by no means the best I've ever had. The sides were mediocre. Sweet potatoes were way too sweet and soggy. Turnips were fine. 
Their biscuits are really good, but I personally preferred them more with butter or dipped in gravy. The gravy was great. Not sure what the hype is about their preserves... tasted good but nothing amazing?
Portions are good. 

3. Price: Good value. 

4. Aesthetics: Casual and cozy. Bathrooms were nice and clean. One thing I noticed when I first sat down was that there was some kind of food on my chair (and it was wet) which I had to clean up (and of course, I chose to wear white jeans just that day, haha). 

Would I go back? I personally don't think the wait is worth it. The food was good but not mind blowing and definitely not worth waiting 1 hour.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Left so full and satisfied! 

Definitely get their country ham, it's salty goodness on a plate! BF got the Famous Country Ham with eggs and I thought why not have a pancake too so I ordered that platter and boy what a mistake. Come hungry cause they start you off with the biscuits and it's all food extravaganza from there. 

Biscuits were interesting, tasted different and my BF told me that it's the buttermilk they must use. As I ate another one I was getting used to it and slathering on the strawberry jam they provided. 

Then our breakfast plates arrived and I saw my mistake instantly. 3 large pancakes along with the home fries, egg, and ham I ordered. The home fries were tasty, gobbled those up with the egg and ham real fast. When faced with the pancake though, couldn't even finish one and gave the other to my BF. I was defeated. Didn't help my BF asked for another order of biscuits after we finished the first. 

Great breakfast! Would love to come back.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Stopped in before shopping. Sat at the bar had a couple of beers, lots of choice on beers. Ordered Rueben tools and a pretzel with beer cheese, tasty but a little pricy for what we received.
Nice atmosphere bartender wasn't too friendly. We read you get a 10 discount out in the mall, yet she didn't offer it and knew he was a veteran. It wasn't a big thing but she should have offered it.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This might be a fun place to have a few beers and appetizers but their food is just mediocre. The waitstaff was extremely helpful and friendly.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: best southern comfort food. So happy we stumbled across this place. Did not have a reservation and only waited 45 minutes. Server Joni was polite and friendly! Yummy fried green tomatoes. Yummy bloody Mary's. Felt like being at grandma's house.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Love that we now have an legitimate Bavarian restaurant in Nashville! Great atmosphere, awesome German food and live music! Join The Stein Club!
Only thing I'd say is that I wish it was not at the mall!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
German food you say- here's your go to!
Great food and beer choices and really cool atmosphere.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
