Wow! What an experience! To begin with, our server was PHENOMENAL! He was incredibly friendly and. Knowledgeable, after we felt like we ordered what seemed like the entire menu, we get our drinks. I had the watermelon moonshine drink and it was basically summer in a Mason jar, the most refreshing drink I have had in a long time.
Our food then comes out, the best part of the entire experience were the handmade biscuits (you can see the kitchen staff rolling them out through a kitchen window). I am pretty sure I have had dreams about these biscuits and the amazing butter and jam they served with. I intend on bringing every guest I have that comes to visit me in Nashville here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Second time visiting the Loveless and it is a truly fun place to visit. Plan to allow a lot of time to get there from Downtown Nashville. The reason for my rating has nothing to do with the service - our server Bama was attentive and pleasant and did a great job. I started with a Lynchburg Lemonade - very lemony - not enough "Lynchburg" but good. I ordered green beans, fried okra and fried chicken. The beans were traditional southern green beans cooked with ham and great. The fried okra was really good as well. The chicken, which is billed as one of their great menu items = way over cooked. I ordered dark meat which has to be really overcooked to dry out and it was really dried out. It was seasoned nicely however. Since I had decided on fried chicken earlier in the day, I was disappointed and hence the 3 star rating. I will say that we took home the left over biscuits and I had biscuit toast for my breakfast the next day which made up a little for the chicken!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Though I've been here many times, today I brought my parents to Loveless Cafe for the first time! Today's visit owes us nothing & my parents are sold on all things Loveless! The food was AMAZING and the staff was absolutely incredible! If you've never had the corn or the turnip greens... they are a must! Everyone was so kind, especially Mr. Keith who took a moment out of his busy schedule to give us the history of Loveless Cafe! The Loveless experience is well worth the drive! You won't be disappointed!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: What I enjoy the most at loveless is the peanut butter pie.  I often want to buy a piece take home but I know this would be bad so I don't.  The fried chicken and the biscuits are other gems but always save room for the pie.  To avoid the long wait get food to go and eat it on the picnic benches outside.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Such an amazing place. If you are on the fence, STOP, jump down and drive to Loveless. I ate at many, many amazing places in Nashville but this one just stole my heart. 

First, they do get busy because they are AWESOME, but do not dismay. To keep you entertained while you are waiting there are plenty of stores and things to keep you busy plus I love that you can chat with the grill master who is making the delicious meats. 

Second, the food is amazing. I had the BBQ Eggs breakfast. So fabulous and sooo much BBQ. I couldn't make it half way through and I'm no slight eater. We had melt in your mouth biscuits and all the sweet treats of homemade jams and jellies. Our server even brought out fresh sorghum. 

Last but not least, the service was just lovely. Truly kind and helpful people who just want to make your visit fun, memorable and especially delicious. Definitely worth the trip!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Arrived just after they opened for breakfast and was immediately seated with a plate of hot biscuits and jam. Food was excellent and service was very attentive.  Great way to start our morning drive down the Natchez Trace.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
THANKSGIVING REVIEW ONLY: so im slowly ordering from every reputable place in town for thanksgiving. monell's was last year and fantastic. loveless was this year and a 4. nothing more

turkey was MOIST. but they give you a few legs with bone so not sure if that makes up part of the 60oz of turkey you get. would obviously prefer to forgo the bone for meat.

sides were all stellar as one would expect. i love the restaurant.

i absolutely love their biscuits but hard to bring back to life in my opinion. i wish they would actually just give frozen raw dough. you get a dozen in an order but they give you 3 tiny plastic ramekins for all dozen which i thought was complete BS. however they will cheerfully remind you "you can buy more preserves at our store!" you're spending $120 on the basic package so i dont think it would kill them to throw in one more set to make it 6 ramekins. you could probably squeeze out 2 servings per ramekin, if you have big folks, then forget that.

THE PIE IS NOT HOMEMADE. they dont state it is anywhere but just wanted to point it out bc its $11. SKIP THE PIE or just order one of their handmade ones. i wish i caught this but honestly, from a marketer, i think its bad for their brand to be selling mass produced pies. to be honest the pumpkin pie was not that great. it was more of a mousse texture. we didn't think it was done but the crust was 100% golden brown.

i would absolutely consider ordering here again for thanksgiving but didn't stand out that far from monell's. both are amazing so its just two amazing places against each other. 

the gentlemen who helped me pick up my order and take it to my car was the highlight of the experience. (not the dude who chimes in to tell me to spend $7 for more preserves)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We visited the Loveless Cafe for breakfast. We arrived at 10:00 am on a Monday and had to wait 30 minutes. The line was even longer when we were leaving. We explored the shops on the premises while we waited. We were given biscuits and jam upon being seated. The biscuits were light, fluffy, and delicious. They are small which we liked because it made it easier to try all three of the jams. Each one was great. We both ordered the fried chicken and eggs with homefries. The eggs were good. Nothing spectacular but still good. The homefries were just the basic previously forzen homefries but the fried chicken was very very good. The coating had great flavor, the chicken remained moist, and the portion sizes were large. The service was excellent. Our coffee was refilled regularly. We never reached the bottom of our cup.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuit is aren't like classic southern biscuits I'm used to (although those are good in their own right). They're like little heavenly pillows of joy. I was expecting a touristy place so my expectations were low, but the food was just good, southern, homey, a little heart warming really. The service was the same.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: What a tourist trap! It is not worth the wait. The only thing good was the biscuits. Everything else is fair at best. I was disappointed in the chicken fried steak and the gravy was plain which reminded me of Dennys. My friend's chicken was dry. You should go to Slow Burn Hot Chicken or The Country Boy in Franklin for some good Southern food that tastes like the region.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
So being a German in the US, I admit that I am extremely critical of German food. I am of the belief that if I can cook it better at home, I've wasted my money. 

So let me start by saying that they did a decent job recreating the Hofbräuhaus, from Munich. This alone made me feel a little closer to "home". I opted for something that I don't make at home because I can either not get the ingredients or it's too much work. Meterwurst has always been a favorite of mine from home but not something that is easy to come by. It was so delicious! 

My husband had Jägerschnitzel - which I do make at home, so of course I had to sample his... I could tell the gravy was instant (but it is a restaurant), but it was good. I still make this dish better at home, but my opinion is biased.  As for my Meterwurst - I loved it!!!

I had a Colabier (coke and beer - don't hate till you try it), and my husband had some cocktail they tried to sell as German, but the only thing German was the gummies. Mine was GREAT! He had an Apfelkorn and I had a Kleiner Feigling to end the meal. 

Let me close this review by saying I will be back. I left feeling homesick and wanting more. I think that says it all.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I have nothing but love for Loveless Cafe. It's one of the few restaurants in the world I would wait over an hour for, but the wait was oh so worth it. I ordered the Southern Omelet with sausage (made and smoked in house). The omelet was huge and overflowing with cheese, peppers and onions. The sausage was very flavorful but not too salty with a bit of a spicy kick. The eggs were fluffy and did a great job of encasing the bulk of the filling. The side of hashbrown casserole was delicious -- creamy with lots of sour cream and cheese mixed in.

Of course, the biscuits were amazing. The preserves on the side were good, but I'm so glad I asked for some honey -- they elevated the biscuits even to an even more supreme level than I ever thought possible.

As long as our wait was, the shops around the cafe made the time fly by. The complimentary lemonade and coffee were great as well.

Everyone should go to Loveless Cafe at least once -- it's worth the drive and time.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: Great atmosphere and bar. Love the 50's diner look. The staff is friendly and helpful.  I'll be back for sure.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Well, butter my butt and call me a Biscuit!!  Finally visited the world famous Loveless Cafe!  I drove there from Clarksville and took the scenic route...just a beautiful and peaceful drive.  Everything on the menu just looked so yummy. My awesome server Megan helped me out (I cannot say enough kind words about her). She just rocked!!
Ok I ended up ordering the Chicken Fried steak meal. As you can see in the photo how big the steak was. I could've put a saddle on it and rode off...lol!!  It was hands down cooked perfectly with the right seasoning. Had 3 sides:  Mac & cheese, mashed potatoes, cream corn which was amazing. I couldn't finished it...but guess what's on the menu tonight. 
Really enjoyed walking around to their other little shops as well as looking at the memorabilia on the walls up the cafe.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is everything I wanted it to be. A bit kitsch and cute and all the biscuits I can eat. They're buttery. They're good. Less flaky than I anticipated but still oh so perfect. I actually like the fact that it's a bit inconsistent in cooking some are a bit more brown or less so. The service is amazing and friendly. If you're not anticipating eating a lot, the a la carte orders (ie biscuits and gravy) are perfect size. 
It's totally worth a trip here when in Nashville. I love the fact that if you don't mind eating at off hours you can make reservations. I stopped by the shops and wanted to buy everything.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Nice location, the shop is great but was not that impressed with the famous food! Still worth the trip through!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Got the Ruben rolls and were disappointing. However the atmosphere and beer were great. Next time I would go for the chefs special.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This place is a decent enough concert venue but the chairs are not made to sit in for any length of time.  They feel like sitting on stadium bleachers after  a while. The staff is courteous and efficient.  I agree that the 25% tax on drinks is a rude surprise, especially when the pour is on the lighter side. The only dish I tried was the smoked bone marrow. It was okay, But the bread must have been very expensive as there are only 2 small thin toasted slices. The menu stated preserved lemons in the dish. I assume the lemon was supposed to be in the gremolata, but there was no citrus or acid notes and the garlic dominated the whole dish.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: The burgers were great. Big portions of fries and onion rings. Our server was very friendly. Will be back!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Went to this place for a drink and it is a MUST!!!  We ended up leaving then going back because it was such a great time! The atmosphere is awesome, the beer is awesome, the food is incredible, and the staff was VERY friendly! If you are in Nashville you MUST go here!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Great venue for a show,  Saw Arlo Guthrie's 50 year show here, and when the first scheduled show was cancelled due to snow City Winery was great to contact early, and gave if the option of a full refund or to hold onto the tickets for a new date. We held the tickets and enjoyed a terrific show. The valet parking was spot on, and the venue itself was overall charming and inviting. The teperature, lighting, acoustics and ambiance was outstanding and the seating at the dining tables was a little tight but comfy.
The staff from valet to host to servers were all quite good and the wine and food were very good and reasonably priced. Overall, I'm sure some come fond little things to be picky about, but I had a great experience and would not hesitate to dine and see another show here in the future, and that's 5 star worthy for me.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: When we finally found it and you get pass the long wait   We enjoyed our trip we are breakfast eaters and they serve it all day   Ham is extra Salty but if you dip it in the gravy wasn't so bad. I had some fried green tomatoes they was yummy.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: The best service I've ever had!!! Not only was the food phenomenal, the bartenders made the experience one to come back for. Jenna was a sweetheart, Kait was a delight and Jason and Josh were absolutely hilarious. Whether it was busy or not I never had to wait for a thing. You won't find better bartenders anywhere. The frisky frog definitely lucked out with them

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: This place is so hipster!  Even still, I enjoyed my visit here.  Our movie was showing in the upstairs theatre which is TINY!  You can't really have a bad seat in this theatre (unless you're a short person).  You'll want to arrive early if going with a group so that you can have seats together otherwise it's highly likely you'll be separated.  We went to a matinee and for two tickets it was $17.  They have the classic popcorn and sodas at the concession, but you can also get hummus and craft beer and other hipster things.  We went with a large popcorn and large coke for $13.  You can get refills on both for $1 each.  There is a very small lot right next to the theatre for parking.  Once you get your ticket they will provide you a pass to place in your windshield (this ticket is good for 2 hours before and after the show in case you want to check out some of the local shops or restaurants).  If you can't find parking there, there is a paid lot directly adjacent to the theatre.  Overall we had a very pleasant experience at this theatre.  There are also several highly reviewed, affordable restaurants and bars mere feet from the theatre should you want to grab a bite or drink before or after your show.

name: The Family Wash
text: The Family Was had a great run on Greenwood Ave. It really was East Nashville's version of the Cheers bar where everybody knows everybody. It makes me sad to drive past this shuttered location, but I look forward to the Wash reopening in their new location later this year. It will never be the same, but perhaps it will still be great.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: So far this venue has been able to book some of the top artists I've seen in a while. I went to one show that was sold out so the venue was very packed and crowded. Luckily I'm able to go back for most shoes so I watched it from side stage where I had plenty of room. Overall it's a good venue with good staff and good shows.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: The Belcourt is amazing. It's so wonderful to have a theater so historic, beautiful, and unique in town. From classics to indie flicks, they have it all. Service is always wonderful and they have so many fun and exciting events as well, including after-showing interviews with directors. So grateful to have a theater like this in Nashville.

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
Giving this place five stars based on my experience the past couple of Thursday nights.   First of all, this place is much cleaner, newer, and fresher
than any of the other bars on the street.  The stage and lighting are phenomenal, and the band, Smashing Pilots is OUTSTANDING!  Geared up in grunge, these guys rocked the roof off the place.  I couldn't believe my eyes or ears... all 90s rock!  Unlike anything else in Nashville, definitely a MUST SEE.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
A friend gifted us a dual membership to the Belcourt for Christmas last year.  I have always loved this place but this year I've attending more movies/events due to the membership.  I cannot express enough how in love I am with the Belcourt!!  

It's a little like a step back in time every time we attend a movie or event here.  The concessions are reasonably priced and they have local beer on tap!!  PLUS members get a discount on tickets AND concessions!  

I encourage everyone to support this wonderful theater!

name: Drifters
text:
I can't really speak about the food, except the tater tots which...seriously who doesn't love tater tots.  

Drifters is a dive bar in the best sense of the term.  No frills, Cold drinks, laid back place.  Great beer list, everything from High Life to a good local craft selection.

My wife and I came because we heard the music floating through the air one night.  Sat on the back patio and listened to Luella Woods and Tim Caroll swap off singing and playing with some killer local talent playing with them.  

This has become our Summer place to come and grab a drink and listen to some music.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Being a huge fan of indie films and documentaries, I absolutely love the Belcourt.  I have never had a theater experience quite like it.  The staff is wonderful; they are passionate about the movies and their fabulous venue and they have a phenomenal sense of humor to boot.  I have only been once so far to see Altered States and we won a float in a sensory deprivation tank!  Now that I have permanently relocated to Nashville, I will be popping in on the Belcourt quite a bit.

name: Drifters
text: Couldn't ask for a better home bar. We always look forward to Summer nights on the porch listening to music here.

name: Commodore Grille
text: You don't go to the Commodore Grill for the food. You go for the music. The menu is okay and the servers are friendly, but there's never enough of them. But it's your standard bar food, and not a very extensive list, so just be prepared for that. But one of the top places to hear songwriters in Nashville.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Went on a Friday evening for happy hour and really enjoyed the atmosphere: nice, clean, and safe. They played a variety of music which was cool. I got the buffalo wings, well seasoned but not crispy. My friend had the catfish and fried shrimp. I tasted a shrimp and it was really good, well seasoned, and jumbo size. I'll be back because you can't beat a bar that offers $3wells with good food.

name: Drifters
text: Awesome bbq with a ton of different choices on bbq sauce. Atmosphere is dive bar like with super friendly staff and great prices on drinks.

name: EXIT/IN
text: Basic medium size venue.  There is an upstairs in the back that you can look out from.  It is especially helpful, when realizing you are going to shows that are inhabited with mostly under 21 year olds who want to mosh at the slight hint of volume, it doesn't even matter if the music is moshable.  They offer an outside patio for smokers, especially helpful since once you come in the venue you can't come back out.  The bar is standard and has a spending minimum of 10$ when using your card.  Sound is ok, but once you are near the front that usually goes out the window.

name: Drifters
text: I used Drifter's to cater my wedding and couldn't have been more pleased. Marc, the catering director was responsive and easy to work with. No weird hidden costs or surprises on the bill, and my guests loved the food.

name: Drifters
text:
Starting off, I have a bit of a background in barbecue and the smoking of meats in general. It's a passion of mine and often partake in the pastime on the weekends. This fact may have affected this review slightly.

Drifter's seemed like the perfect place to go, having a night to go out to eat with a friend who had dropped into town. It was barbecue, in one of my favorite spots in Nashville, and it was......well, barbecue! We arrived to see a very southern-looking, slightly roadhouse-looking visage behind a porch that was overlooking the 5 Points area. It was gorgeous. Going inside, we were told to sit anywhere and we took a seat at the end of the bar.

Everything was great, with signage checkering the walls and not a whiff of pretension to be had in the entire place. Our server was pleasant and directed us to the many local craft beers while we browsed the menu. Not being a beer drinker, I left it to my friend to try a few. But we were mostly ready for what we came for: barbecue! The many different sauces was an exciting prospect, and I was ready to dive into every one of them. 

Ordering a pick-two combo of brisket and pork, while my friend ordered the sliders, our food arrived around 15 minutes after we ordered. My first impressions were that of excitement, and I went right for the baked beans. They were decent, however, the sauce was a bit too thin for what I imagine to be "southern" baked beans; while the beans themselves retained a bit of stoutness that told me this was not the slow-cooked baked beans I was used to.

Next came the sauces! My friend calls us sauce whores because of how much we eat and make sauce. They had 5 different ones ready for us and I wanted to get to them before I tried my pork and brisket. 2 of the sauces were highly vinegar based, which I'm not the biggest fan of, and the atomic was simply untouchable as it was just insanely hot. Settling on the sweeter, tomato-based sauce, I moved on to my main course.

The meat wasn't bad, but I really can't say that it gave me anything worth coming back for. The smoke was there, however, it was somehow just still completely devoid of flavor. The sauces also did not impress me in the least... Were they bad? No, they weren't. Was I blown away? Sadly, there are better store-bought sauces... And I hate to say any of this because I wanted to like it so badly. The place looked like a winner, had great prices and a great view, friendly staff, and good beer; the food was just lacking though. It wasn't bad, just wasn't good either.

Try this place out! Just keep things in perspective. Don't go in thinking you're going to be getting the best and you'll be happy. The fries and tots were probably the greatest part, perfectly cooked and not greasy! I just wish that their beans and meat were as on-point as the fries. I just need a bit more flavor to make the barbecue the way it should be... unforgettable!

name: Drifters
text:
The Drifter sandwich is pretty tasty. It's a great concept. The pork is cubed (not pulled) and the brisket is outstanding.

This is more of a dive bar than a restaurant. I had a very long wait to get my sandwich to go (at a pretty quiet time of night) and was glad I wasn't eating in. The service was not very friendly and the place wasn't very welcoming.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
I absolutely LOVE going to see movies at the Belcourt. Movie watching is definitely one of my main hobbies, and there's no better place in Nashville to indulge in it than the Belcourt. Between their midnight movie series, the Saturday morning series, the outdoor film series, and the endless array of independent cinema they have on their reels, there are so many options for people to enjoy here. 

I'm beginning my membership tomorrow. I know I won't be able to use the student discount forever, so I may as well take that one step into adulthood before I graduate. As long as I'm living in Nashville, I will be a member of the Belcourt. The movies and the staff are what keep me coming back, though I have to admit that the specialty cocktails they create for the midnight movies are a definite bonus! I could go on for much longer about how great this place is, but I think you get the picture by now!

name: Drifters
text: Some of the best BBQ in Nashville. Friendly staff, never have to wait long to be served even on trivia night. The absolute best Brunswick stew in the state, honestly. The prices are fantastic, and there isn't a bad thing on the menu.

name: The Country
text: Best live music off Broadway without all the tourists! Great neighborhood feel with fantastic live music daily! Check them out. It's a must to see in Nashville.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Good atmosphere to watch the game but very slow service. Our order came out wrong and the alligator bites were raw. Really only positive was drinks were good.

name: The Country
text: Well they changed the menu again, no more kale salad  such a bummer!  Definitely recommend coming for Hexagon presents still though!!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: The bands I've seen play at Mercy Lounge were amazing and sounded great in this venue. The one thing keeping me from giving it a 5-star rating is that people at the bar are sometimes loud and obnoxious and really distract from the concert experience. This, of course, is a potential problem anywhere there's a bar in the same room as the show, but it'd be nice if Mercy Lounge tried to separate the two a little more.

name: Drifters
text: Looks a little shady but is actually a fun little place. Lots of good beer. Lots of good food. I had the pulled pork chimi and it was awesome! Corn hole in the back. Live music in the front. Within walking distance of a lot of places if you want to do a pub crawl. Nice place to hang outside in the summers. I keep hearing about the corndogs so I'll try that next time.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
This venue is alright. Far from my favorite place to see a show in Nashville. 

There's a huge line to get in, which seemed a little dramatic, but fine. That's cool. While in line, some red bull girls brought us free drinks which I liked, but when we got to the door, we were informed we would have to finish them or toss them before we came in. Again, I get it, but geez. I had literally just been handed the drink a few minutes before. 

Once inside, good luck. It just kind of is what it is. No place to sit. Just a big open room. Maybe I'm getting old. I probably would have preferred that in my 20s, but I felt like we didn't even know what to do with ourselves. We just sort of stood in the back the entire time, near the end of the bar. 

The sound wasn't great. It always seems weird to me when I'm at a venue in Nashville, TN and I feel like the sound could be a lot better. The speakers weren't well positioned and there was quite a bit of feed back in the beginning. 

I did enjoy myself, but when the show ended, I was more than ready to leave.

name: Drifters
text:
Passing through Nashville on a recent x-country drive and I NEEDED ME SOME Q.  Drifters provided !

Fellow yelpers steered me to this dive and IT WAS GREAT. We had the combo platter.  Ribs slid off the bones, brisket & sausage were also perfectly smoked & prepared.  Sides were tasty classic preparations.  Service was Friendly and Quick.  Food & Service were  5 star.  4 stars cause, although they had a full bar, they did not have any NA Beer.  Doesn't matter, next time in town, I'll be back

name: Drifters
text: We were looking for an alternative to the downtown Broadway scene. We found Drifters on Yelp and decided to try it. We came for drinks and live music on the patio.  The drinks were great and the music was awesome.  The only downside was we arrived toward the end of the bands set.  It would have been nice to have another band come on after.

name: The Family Wash
text:
Called over two months ago to make a dinner reservation for my wife's 40th birthday party.  Party of 11.  I even repeated the date back to the guy on the phone to make sure we were all set. I even let him know it was for my wife's 40th.   

Showed up this past Friday night (11/7/14) with my wife and our friends, all of whom had traveled great distances to join us for the weekend to find out they had no record of our reservation.  Wow.  

They tried to seat...ahem.... cram us at two separate high top tables right by the entrance and when they gave a bar stool to one of our friends, she was told not to put her feet on it because it was broken.  

I'll admit they did try to offer us a free round of drinks but I was not having it.  This was going to be our first meal out together to kick off the weekend and to be seated separately (on broken barstools) was completely unacceptable.  

We walked out and went across the street to the Porter House Bistro.  I'm writing a review of this place next.  We were seated immediately by a wonderful staff and were treated to one some of the best food and cocktails of our entire weekend.  The chef even came out to greet us and took a bunch of photos for us as well.  

The Family Wash might be good for beers, live music, etc., but I will never know.  You blew it, guys.  I will return to East Nashville (hopefully soon and often) and will spend my money elsewhere.

name: EXIT/IN
text: What a little gem on Church street. Plenty of nearby options for pre game (or after party). The venue has great sound quality, friendly bar tenders, and most importantly, some fabulous acts in a the best music venue-dive in town. I saw Cee Lo here - he had two great openers and the crowd was super friendly to a gal flying solo. I would definitely come back to catch one of the many recognizable bands who come through here, and I can't wait to catch a discovery act they find.

name: Drifters
text:
I've been here on Friday nights with live bands, Monday nights for trivia (which I am so not good at) and eaten and drank all the times in between and I really love this little biker-bar-style place in East Nashville.  

The service has always been great no matter how busy it is (and its usually very busy), the food is good BBQ-style smoky goodness and the beer is always cold.  You can sit inside, admittedly a smaller space, or they have a very spacious patio, and the stage for previously mentioned live music is outside.  

I highly recommend their nachos (can be had with or without meat for my veggie-loving brethren) and their spicy black bean burger is a thing of beauty.  The patio can get smoky, and parking is limited in their small back lot, so keep that in mind.  

But there's always something fun going on here, and its become a go-to place with friends, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a good time that its too fancy or pricey.  Drifters is one of those places you cross the river to enjoy willingly.

name: Springwater
text:
We wanted a dive. 

We got a dive.

Beer was cheap.  Cash only.  $5 cover for the bands that were there.  

We came as one band finished their set.  Next band sucked, but we played darts and laughed at ourselves instead.  

Iconic music venue in Nashville.  Although we didn't hit it on the best night for music, if you are lucky, you might be there when it does. Attracts some pretty awesome musicians.  See? http://www.rollingstone.com/music/videos/premiere-the-black-keys-invade-iconic-dive-bar-on-little-black-submarine-20120904

Cool spot.  I'd totally come back here again.  Gritty, smoky, and dodgy.  Dig it.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: I photographed the AMA's this year and this is the venue that I was assigned to on Saturday night. It is a cool little spot, the stage is on the small size and I was front and center with my camera. I was pushed and almost knocked over SO many times. The lighting was great though and the service was good for how packed it was. The drinks are expensive...$7 well shots, so I wasn't too excited about that. But I will probably go back if they get a show worth watching.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Was there recently for the I Saw the Light movie premiere and I have to say, staff were amazingly wonderful. I had a great experience. I'm from out of town, but would definitely see a movie there the next time I'm in the area. I have nothing but wonderful things to say about this place and the people associated with it.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: This local art house theater is a Nashville institution that celebrates independent filmmakers and classic cinema. After decades of being well-loved, the aging theater recently reopened after a major renovation. The result is a beautiful new lobby, updated bathrooms, a well-stocked concession area that serves standard movie fare as well as alcohol, and gorgeous theaters evocative of classic Hollywood glamor. The only knock is that the seats can be a tight squeeze if you're packing extra pounds. Rule of thumb -- if you need a seat belt extender when you fly, you might not fit.

name: Drifters
text: VERY good BBQ. Bevare that the portions are enorm so do not ordet too much. I was done after my nachos (which was very tasty!)

name: Drifters
text:
We went to Drifters because my friend was craving their BBQ chicken burrito.  We went for the food, but this review is really about Marie the bartender and guest manager who went far out of her way to help me.
   
I was visiting from out of town, and it was my last stop before heading to the airport.  We ate outside on the patio.  Super relaxing.  I was wishing I could hang out longer to hear the band that was setting up.

When I got to the airport, I realized I didn't have my hoodie.  Ugh.  It's my favorite one, very unique, a gift from my sister...I must have left it at Drifters.  So I called and got connected to Marie.  She didn't see it, but took my number just in case.  The good news - when I landed there was a message waiting for me that she found it.  The bad news - I didn't have a way to get it!  Hearing the disappointment in my voice, she offered to mail it to me personally.

A huge thank you to Marie!  That was very kind and I really appreciate it!

name: Drifters
text:
Ah, Drifters... No frills at it's finest!
It's tucked right in the heart of five points, but doesn't feel "too" hip. You'll see all kinds here... Old, young, couples, families, dogs too!

The food is consistently good. I always go for their BBQ pork sandwich, my man goes for the pulled chicken sandwich. It's one of my favorite places for BBQ in Nashville - and I'm the kind of person who has to sample BBQ everywhere I go. LOVE IT. 

So the food, it's good. The atmosphere is what keeps me coming back though. The staff is so friendly, the crowd is usually really chill, and the outdoor seating is the best! Especially when a local band is playing, which is often.

For me, summer is Drifters season..... I'll be there quite a lot over the next few months. See you there!

name: Drifters
text:
Great dive-bar scene with plenty of outdoor seating. The food is surprisingly good, but I'm not a bbq fan...so I usually order the veggie burger and it's delicious! Beer is reasonably priced. 
This is a traditional spot for me to hit, as I usually alternate between Drifter's and Beyond the Edge.

name: Drifters
text: I was teetering between 3 and 4 stars, because the service was good, and overall the food wasn't bad. The problem is that I felt the queso dip could use a little more punch to it, and the ribs were very so-so. They do have very crisp french fries, which is one of my favorite things. Also they have a selection of bbq sauces which is nice. I felt several of the sauces could have been left off, including the Texas sauce. This sauce was more of a letdown to me since I moved here from Texas, and was simply not blown away. I have been here once before when visiting Nashville, and I was more impressed on that visit. I will be more scrutinizing of places now that I am going to be using yelp more frequently. Overall this place is worth a visit, and I will return. The great service, live music, and overall quality of the food is good.

name: Springwater
text: I would give 0 stars if I could! The absolute worst venue ever. Is a over 21 venue only but booked a band that was underage. Band and crew were not made aware of the age requirement. They didn't not let camera guy. Band had to leave after set and couldn't support other bands!! Worst venue ever!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
I love the belcourt. I'm so glad Nashville has held on to a little piece of its history in this building. The remodel made it really nice inside but I'm glad they kept the old movie screen because it creates an ambiance that other theaters don't have. I also love the cookie/pastry selection they have at the counter from local businesses as I am not a theater popcorn person but like to have something other than candy. 

Tip: if you haven't been to their showing of Rocky Horror Picture Show, go! It's so much fun.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
I'll start by saying that Cannery Ballroom might not be the most ideal concert venue for everyone. There is no seating so be prepared to stand for 2+ hours. I think that's the most important thing to know. 

The Cannery Ballroom is in the same building as The Mercy Lounge and the High Watt. Since there are multiple venues, they will ask you out front which concert you are there to see and point you in the right direction. Parking isn't bad if you get there early enough. There is a smaller lot with free parking and then a bigger lot for $5. I believe it's cash only but we were lucky enough to get a free spot. We were there Halloween night to see Ghostland Observatory so I figured it would be pretty busy. We arrived at about 8:45 for a 9:00 show. Check-in was super easy. A security guard did a metal detector test and looked inside my purse. Inside, a person scanned my mobile tickets on my phone and we were in. The Cannery Ballroom is one big room. Right when you walk in, the bathrooms are to the right in a separate area. The bar is also to the right and is pretty big. They had about 8 different options for beer and then also mixed drinks. Beers were $5-7 and I believe they were all tall boys. Not bad for a concert venue. The stage was in the front right corner but can be seen from anywhere in the room...I think. It might be hard to see when the room gets really packed. The room wasn't too busy yet so we were able to get right up front. I'm not sure if this was the best choice. The sound was really loud. I know concerts are loud, but this just seemed unnecessarily loud. The building is brick so I'm guessing it has something to do with the acoustics. The crowd was of course pushy and packed but that's what you can expect with GA standing rooms. Like some of the other reviews have mentioned, it gets really warm in this place. I mean this was October and once the show really got started, it was pretty hot. I had a t-shirt and jeans on and was uncomfortable. I could see the singer was just dripping in sweat. I don't think I would come to a concert here in summer. But I'm also a person that doesn't like the heat. 

The tickets were a good price compared to other venues in Nashville. It's nice that you can get right up to the stage if you don't mind how loud the sound is. Standing in the middle of the room might get you better sound but then you don't get as good of view of the stage. Overall, it was a fun night and a nice venue. I would come back for another concert!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
My only complaint is that there aren't more Belcourt Theatres in town! I have been seeing films here since I moved to the area 12 years ago. It's a true art house with a variety of genres and access to limited opening release films. 

If you are into old films, they have lots of classics playing throughout the year and even do holiday specials. It is very family friendly. 

I do miss the old feel to the building (and the funky bathrooms) but it is nice to have more space for events. 

The concessions are on point- local beers, wine on tap, and unique snacks. Some membership levels even have free refills on popcorn and soda!

This is a wonderful place to connect with likeminded individuals who enjoy experiencing films in a smaller and more intimate space. 

Go see a film! You won't be disappointed. 

Parking in the lot is free too!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Mercy Lounge brings in some really incredible acts either before they hit it big or right after.  The tickets are so cheap and the space very small with great sound.  It can get really hot in here when its sold out, but they have a lovely little deck outside that's great for cooling purposes.  The bar is small but the bartenders here are always on their game.  Sometimes for smaller shows or showcases you can sit at a table and relax while you enjoy the music.  When its sold out its a free for all and really packed but compared to other venues its really not that horrible.  Sure its a battle to get back to the bar from your great viewing spot (there really isn't a bad place to stand here) but even if you can't get back to that first spot you can see quite well from anywhere inside.  Seeing a show here is an overall great and inexpensive experience, and usually you want to see the bands playing here while you can before they are playing bigger venues to more fans.  Yeah you feel like a music snob ("I saw them at Mercy last year and now they're at the Ryman") but the acts here are worth the stuffy dark room and rampant PBR.

name: Williams Fine Violins
text: Wow. Speechless. I am by no means qualified even to begin to describe the wealth of treasures in this shop. Completely in awe of the instruments here. The owner is very friendly. Kind of wish I could actually play a violin now.

name: Drifters
text:
Obsessed! 

We landed in Nashville at about 10 pm and the first thing I did was open up my yelp app to find some Bbq! 

So glad we came here. We got a sort of sampler platter with ribs, brisket, hot links, fries and fried pickles. It was SO good! 

Definitely recommend! Chill spot, good drinks, friendly service and lots and lots of yummy sauces!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: I don't really like independent movies which is why I don not enjoy belcourt. It is full of conceited hipsters and college/grad students that don't know anything about the politics and socioeconomic status of this world. The films are ok but the audience just ruins it fo rme man

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Oversold tickets so there weren't enough seats for my party of 3. And no, we didn't care if we sat together, there were literally no seats left. Didn't apologize and were clearly annoyed. Takes days for refund to go through. Wish I hadn't spent $20 on the uber ride over! Love small independent theaters and support the ones where I live, but this one really needs to get it's sh!t together!

name: Famous Nashville
text: 5 star venue !  This is one of the nicest and most fun bars I have ever visited.  The hospitality was off the charts fantastic as well.  If you are looking for a private event space in Nashville , look at this venue!! It's fantastic.  Best rooftop in the city, overlooking the stadium and the river.  Mae will treat you right !!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Lindsey M was just the BIGGEST bitch to us! Just trying to buy a t shirt Lindsey... Calm down and get a new attitude.

name: Nashville Underground
text: I was glad that we wondered into this restaurant. I had the Strawberry salad, perfectly fresh and a beautiful blend of ingredients. Also tried a Music City Mimosa, which I loved, but thought was a bit pricy at $12. My husband had a burger, and he enjoyed it as well. The entertainment was great, both artists we saw had wonderful voices, and I loved that you could listen but they weren't so loud that you couldn't still have a conversation.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Went here on the Fourth of July to listen to the symphony and watch the fireworks. The venue is really nice, and we had a good view of the fireworks. We could hear the symphony well from the lawn area. So why didn't it get 5 stars? One word: $5 water. OK, maybe that's two words. Or one word, a number, and a symbol, but I'm thoroughly ticked off. Out on the street, vendors were selling water for $1 to $3. Here it was $5 at the concession stand and $7.50 at a cart. For $7.50 I'd expect it to include a haircut or a hamburger or something, but no. There was a taco truck at the back, but they were forbidden to sell water. And no, you can't bring in your own water from the outside. Nice venue, but I'll only go in the dead of winter so I won't die of thirst.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great Nashville bar with good music! It's 3 stories which makes it easy to jump back and forth to listen to the different bands. There are also nice balconies to look out of Broadway and take a break from dancing. Would definitely come back.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great place!  We stayed on the first level, LOVED the band that was playing.  Pretty crowded but a fun place to have a drink.  I didn't order food but it looked like they had typical bar type food (burgers, wings, fries, etc).  Drinks were a little pricey but hey, it's downtown Nashville.  Except for one bartender, the rest needed to get the sticks out of their asses.  Not friendly at all, no smile, no "hi, how are you"....nothing.  Just a "what can I get you" with a crappy look on their faces.  I would definitely come back to check out the second and third floors.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Worst place I've been to in quite a while. Perhaps my expectations were skewed given the excellent alternatives. I went with my girlfriend to enjoy some music after a long week of work. 

Overpriced drinks, including one awful rum and coke.....unable to describe what it tasted like as I've never tasted a drink so bad. Not sure what brand of rum they use but it sure ain't rum. Music was average at best.

Also beware although it advertises that it closes at 3am, it closes well before that. I got served a drink at 235am, by 240am I had the most obnoxious, overzealous bouncers pushing me out the door telling me that i had to leave the drink. To make matters worse, I was completely sober and was only starting my 3rd drink. A member of the Nashville police department grabbed my beer and threw it in the rubbish bin, followed by one of the obnoxious bouncers throwing me aggressively out the door. I have not experienced anything like that before. Suppose it's an indictment of the trajectory our police department at Nashville is going in. I'm sure he enjoyed plenty of drinks after hours for his sterling service.

In summary, woeful drinks, terrible staff, brutish door staff and average music.....I would advise to stay well away from this sorry establishment. There are far more attractive propositions in the offing in the great city of Nashville.

name: The Pink Slip Lounge
text:
My reaction was..
Where is everyone?
The lady behind the bar didn't have much to offer in drinks but a nice smile.  I had a Jack with coke.  It tasted watered down:(.  We did have fun playing at the pool table. You just need 4 quarters to play a game.  Other then that nay or eh.

name: Alley Taps
text: Alley Taps is nestled on the lesser (by A large margin as there is nothing else there) traveled side of Printers Alley.  You wouldn't even know its there if there wasn't a sign standing outside the place.  Inside it's actually about 3x larger and a lot nicer than expected.  I did it eat there, but it looks like it's more of a drinking spot than eating spot.  I'm definitely not demeaning their food as I didn't see it.  There are several seating areas, tv's, and lots of bar seating.  At 3pm they have 2-4's.  They actually pour an excellent Guinness.  They have have live bands everyday after 5pm.  This place hasn't blown up yet, but it definitely could with their offering coupled with the new hotels that are popping up.  At its present state this is a great place to come without the tourist clutter downtown.  If they get the tourist good for them.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Not bad.  Only the first floor had live music, but as it was too crowded and hot we went to the third floor.  It had a nice view of Broadway, but piped in music rather than letting us hear the love music on the first floor. Nothing was on tap, no happy hour, and the drinks were overpriced. The bartender was very helpful.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Pulled pork and Nashville hot chicken were both very good. Normally things like slaw are just a throw-in, but the pickles and slaw here were very good. Service is good especially given they just recently opened.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: The best addition to Nashville in the last 20 years. Perfect blend of the beautiful weather and music with intimate lighting and sound. A perfect 10.  Thank you

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Lots of fun. Even if you don't like country music!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Been here a few times to see the Time Jumpers (q.v.). and Tim Akers' Smoking Section (q.v.) There was food and booze. The music was so good I can't remember what I ate or drank, but I remember it didn't suck, in fact I think I thought it was pretty good. Seating is way tight, but again, no tighter than seats at any concert hall. What I remember distinctly is that I had a rollicking good time each time I was here, and I can't wait to get back. When in Nashville, put this place on your list. It's as good as it gets.

name: Nashville Party Authority
text:
We used NPA for our wedding reception and were very satisfied with the experience from beginning to end.  I reached out to four other DJ's before finding NPA, and the others don't even compare when it comes to professionalism and punctuality.  Blair, the owner, is very responsive, transparent, and pleasant.  He amended our agreements with lightning speed and helped make suggestions for the flow of events and which songs to play when.  I can't say enough good things about him.  

Jordan was the DJ for our reception and did a fantastic job.  He showed up on time, kept the dance floor hoppin', and dealt with our drunken guests' song requests quite diplomatically.  We also leaned on him to make announcements for the first dance, cake cutting, toasts, etc. and keep us on a timeline (we didn't have a wedding planner), and this was no problem for him.

Stop looking and just book Nashville Party Authority.  You won't regret it!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This bar has three levels- all with outside decks which is pretty nice. Live music on each floor as well. I will say that I have watched them turn a lot of people away so avoid this place if you have a fake id . It's not my favorite on Broadway but definitely worth stopping in for a drink.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: If you go this bar you probably a tourist b/c that is the only reason I can think that you would pay $5 a beer and wait 10 mins for a drink when there are bars with $6 pitchers and 2 dollar drinks less than a block away.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: My coworkers and I ventured here for a drink on a Thursday night. We went to the top level, which had a nice view of Broadway, and the musicians upstairs were good!

name: The Back Corner
text: , An awesome upscale nightclub with amazing R and B mix by some really talented D j's.

name: The Station Inn
text: This place isn't fancy at all but the people were very nice. The music was unbelievable which is why we were here. We were only in town for 3 days but ended up going here twice. The music was much better than anywhere on Broadway. Don't let the unassuming looks of the place turn you off. If you like bluegrass then this is the place to be!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Great venue! I've seen several bands play and they always sound great! I love the chicken wings! My only wish is that they'd have assigned seats! It's a real drag having to get there an hour or more before the doors even open to stand in line outside to get a seat. I'd pay a little extra to have an assigned seat!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Honky Tonk Central is my favorite bar to visit on Broadway. We always make it a point to go whenever we are in Nashville. I love that it features different bands on all three floors, so you can find whatever fits your mood. If you don't like what is going on on one floor--move along to the next! Each floor also has a bar, tables, and dancing area. I like to get my drink and stand on the patio on the 2nd or 3rd floor to people-watch the characters walking up and down Broadway!

name: The Station Inn
text: Incredible musical experience. Intimate atmosphere that feels like sitting with friends. The focus is certainly the music and the music is worth every penny. I could have stayed all night.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
What I remember about Benchmark is not the band or the beer selection or seating, but the bathrooms. This place had by far the oddest bathroom stalls I've ever encountered. That being said, they were clean and had more than one in the bathroom. Helpful things. 

Also helpful was the giant container of water available for hydration. As a local told my friends and I, "Everyone comes to Nashville thinking they can out drink it. They're wrong, all wrong."

Stay thirsty, friends. This place is A-OK to quench your thirst, alcoholic and non.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Very good food and drinks. We enjoyed the music. Very fast and friendly service. We would definitely come back.

name: Nashville Underground
text: The plates were a little on the small side! But the band was so amazing! Not sure how I felt about the Mac and cheese or corn bread but the fried tomatoes were to die for! Our server was very sweet and took good care of us. The venue itself was really nice and had a great feel to it!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Do not miss the Time Jumpers if you are in Nashville on a Monday night, when they play at 3rd and Lindsley. They are the best live band you have ever seen. Every single musician has won multiple Grammys. They play Western swing and classic country, and it's a joy to hear. Throw everything aside and go here.

Call ahead or use their website to make sure you get tickets, and show up early (7:00 for a 9:00 show, at the latest) if you want a seat. You can't beat the price, it's €15 to get in.

The beer's not cheap and the food's not that great: stick with the burgers and fries. But you are here for the music, and it is well worth your entire visit to Nashville.

There is free parking but it is a bit tricky and you might want to take a cab, you can afford it.

On other nights they have a wide variety of music, usually not country. Call ahead or check their website to see who's playing.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Food was lame. Drinks were expensive and small. Music was so loud you couldn't hold a conversation. Never again.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: We just returned from Nashville to hear The Time Jumpers on Monday I play steel guitar and enjoy watching and listening to Paul Franklin .The whole band is spectacular if you love quality Western Swing and the food is very good and reasonable if you want to eat not to mention VINCE GILL doing his best playing and singing. The first time we saw them at Station Inn but like this location better. Need to get there early if you want a seat.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Good music, pretty good Hot Chicken. Not as crowded as many of the other places on Broadway, but then again, this place has only been open for a few weeks. Overall, not disappointed.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This place is massive, and it's in the heart of the touristy Broadway section so if you dislike crowds this may not be your place.  For the most part though, the bands are excellent and there are 3 floors to choose from so you can get whatever you want.  Drink prices are about average, and table service can be very good despite the crazy crowds (it presumably helps if you pay cash and tip well upfront).

It naturally seems to be mostly tourists that populate this massive establishment, but I'd definitely go back.  I'm a fan.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Great place. Great music. Cold drinks. The band playing was very good. Interactive with the patrons. It made for a great evening.

name: The Station Inn
text: Definitely go here if you are in Nashville. Amazing music (based on the two times I've been), cheap beer. Can't speak to the food as I haven't had it. If there is a cover charge, I guarantee it will be worth every single penny! The only *odd* thing is that the ladies bathrooms have curtains instead of doors outside the stalls. I sort of had to hold mine closed with one hand to prevent a different type of show to other unsuspecting guests ;)  Get here early if you want a seat!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Visit the Nashville Underground for the atmosphere, not the food. Really enjoyed the band. The service was great! Food not so great...sorry for the let down.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Wanted to go Honky Tonk hopping but we enjoyed the music here so much that we never left.  We took a shuttle from the campground to the Broadway Honky Tonks so that we could enjoy the day and not worry about driving back.  We ordered the chips, Queso and salsa which was really good especially the Queso and then later ordered onion rings and tater tops which were both really good.  The only thing I marked them down for was the price of the beer.  Coronas and other beers all seemed to be six dollars each which is pretty high.  Service was A+.  We would go here again and may tomorrow.
The first musicians were good but almost everything was a ballad.  We were about to leave when we found out that there would be a band change in about 45 minutes.  So glad we stayed.  The next band was great.  The front man had a great personallity, getting the audience involved, a great voice and a super band.  They had the place packed and some people dancing.  Lots of middle aged people dancing and acting silly.  So fun people watching.  Everyone was having fun.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Great venue for live music. The food is okay but I'm really here for the show. Get here early. It's first come, first serve for seating.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I had a nice time at Honky Tonk Central. I only went in because I needed a beer to cool off and this just happened to be right near me at the time. I was around 2 pm on a Friday and the place was crowded!!! All 3 floors were packed to the brim so I knew it had to be a fun place. My fiance and I were able to find 2 seats at the bar and the bartender actually saw us right away so major kudos for that! Since we were visiting we decided to try a local beer. We each ordered a Yazoo and paid in cash since starting a tab may have been a mistake. While drinking our beer we enjoyed listening to the band...they were playing some old school country which I loved. 

We stayed for a total of 2 beers each and then continued our journey down Broadway. The bartenders were all really great, but the price of a beer was insane! I guess paying $7 for a beer is okay when you are visiting a bar like Honky Tonk Central.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This is such a fun place to hang out any time of the day! I stopped in around 5 PM, then again around 9. Different vibes on each floor of the building, which is super fun. First floor is loud and rambunctious, second floor has more tables for talking and eat. Also love their little porches you can stand on and watch people. It is pricey, but it's a touristy bar in Downtown Nashville, so it's to be expected. Only dinging this place for the cleanliness, which was less than stellar. Use the bathroom somewhere else.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
my husband and i had a fantastic time here on a recent monday (yes- monday) night.  service was friendly and efficient.  the drink prices are steep, and the servings are small, but when there's a good band playing, it's worth it.  i do think the band makes a big difference in your experience because, while we loved the first band that was playing, the second one was kind of a dud, so we ended up leaving.  that being said, it's definitely worth it to try this place out.  we hadn't anticipated ordering food, but we were enjoying ourselves and starting to get hungry, so we got buffalo wings, fried pickle chips, and a side of fries. the food was actually really good, nothing gourmet, but good.

overall, this is a solid spot on Broadway.

name: The Station Inn
text:
This spot is a Nashville institution and you are bound to see amazing music here any night of the week.  Bar is beer only and food is cheap pizza and hot dogs.  So if you want something else then eat beforehand.  

I showed up about 8:30 for an 8pm show and the place was full, and there is quite a lot of seating.  This is a singer/songwriter kind of joint.  Come here if you want to be captivated by good music!  It's not a very social joint. 

The staff (I think it was the owners), were all very friendly and welcoming!  This is refreshing in a tourism town where hospitality can at times be a little jaded.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I only go here during daylight as it gets way too crowded with bachelor/bachelorette parties after dark. Great music and the higher up in floors you go, the better the experience, in my opinion. Our service was great as it was not too crowded on a Friday late afternoon. We did plenty of people watching and still sat close enough to see and enjoy the local band. There was a group of college (Clemson) boys who gave us plenty to laugh at. 
After drinking and dancing, we got hungry and decided to give the Frito Pie a try. It was really good and I would order it 100 times more. Perfect food to offset the amount of beer we drank. After that, it was very nice to see that the line for the ladies room on the 3rd floor was not long and the single stalls were quite clean for a honkytonk bar. This place is a very well known and they have a reputation for great local music and wild times. Enjoy!!!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Food is amazing! Kid friendly, dined with 6 kids and got the chicken tenders basket and a couple sides. The service is great! Keeley tawtar was our server and she was amazing! Knows the menu very well and was so great with the group of kids. Definitely will be coming back!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great atmosphere and live bands. I was refused a cup of water and told I'd have to pay $2.50 for a bottle. I've never been to a place that refuses someone a cup of water/not sure how ethical that is.

name: The Cowan
text:
As with Craig D, we drove in to see The Fixx at the Cowan, but we had general admission.  It seemed like quite a few of the yellow wristband wearing balcony crowd traveled down to the main floor due to the lack of seats/views up there.

The Cowan is a nice place to see a show.  Small enough to get close, big enough so you don't feel cramped.

Here's the set list:

Set 1 (Reach the Beach (in reverse order)):
- Outside
- Privilege
- Liner
- Changing
- Reach the Beach
- Opinions
- Saved by Zero
- Running
- Sign of Fire
- One Thing Leads to Another


Set 2:
- Stand or Fall
- Less Cities, More Moving People
- Are We Ourselves?
- Chase the Fire
- Driven Out
- Something Ahead of You
- Shaman
- Built for the Future
- Red Skies

Encore:
- Deeper and Deeper
- Secret Separation

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Great tunes and the 3rd floor was rocking!  Broadway and 4th Ave the sounds are booming. Drinks flowing and this band is jamin!  Welcome To Nashville, TN
Honk Tonk Central is exactly that...Central to the fun!
#KatrinaAustinBand was on fire9
Day # 2  #2019RoadTripUSA

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Came from California and had a blast here! Lisa the bartender was then best put here!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Great place for live music. Acoustics & sight lines are good, ticket prices are good for exceptional entertainment! Food is typical bar food, good for what it is. Good beer selection, reasonably priced. Attentive,friendly service. Been 3 times, will certainly go again.

name: The Station Inn
text: After reading some of these reviews, I have to say - some of these tourist have no idea what they're talking about. If you want to see some live music in the evening without fighting the crowds on music row, this is THE SPOT to go! The owner is a really nice guy who loves to jam with his fellow musicians. They're cool people! The drinks are reasonably priced, either $5-$6 depending. Get there early, get a good seat, and don't order the pizza... it smells up the place. Enjoy the show! You won't see anything better :)

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Packer Bar downtown!  We had a great time watching the playoff game. Upstairs is the sports at with good TVs. Music playing downstairs. $4 beers (not bad for downtown).  We loved that we ran into lots of people from Wisconsin.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Honky Tonk has really good music. We usually do a beer or a shot in each level. Great views too!  We've never tried the food but it looks delicious with large portions. 

I rarely give reviews below 4 stars however we were treated pretty poorly last night after spending quite a bit of money. Let me preface this by saying we were sipping water and not even drinking anymore. I have zero clue why the 3 of us where approached and told to leave.  I don't know if we were mistakenly identified. They told us to leave right away.  They escorted us out.  We weren't given a reason. It was horrible & weird.  I have no clue what happened but I felt terrible over it. Not a single one of the three of us were acting foolish and we tipped well. 

We'll give them another chance next time for sure but pretty turned off at this point.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: The BEST place to see live music in Nashville!  Small, cozy venue with really good sound!  You never know for sure who will show up, but it is always a great show!  I can't say anything but I wish I lived closer, so that I could go back on a regular basis.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
This is the first bar we ended up going to in Nashville, mostly because they were one of the few still serving dinner by the time we entered Broadway at about 8pm. 

The live music was great, food was typical bar fare (and therefore delicious) and the drinks were great as well. My girlfriend enjoyed the Blushing Bride shot and Vodka Energy drink slushee so much that we gave Benchmark another visit our second night in the city just to order a round of those again.

Great little dive away from the chaos of Broadway, definitely recommend as a place to start or end the night.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
We came to Ascend Amphitheater for Dave Matthews & Tim Reynolds. I have to say we were really impressed with this venue.  

We were in the lawn and even those seats were really nice.  We had the option to rent chairs, but we didn't bother since we knew we would be standing once the concert started.  Sound was great even from where we were sitting.

There were plenty of restrooms and they were all nice and clean!  

Plenty of food and beverage options as well!

We used Uber, so I cannot comment on the parking. You can walk to Broadway or basically anywhere else you want after the show to enjoy the nightlife Nashville offers. If you want to Uber back right after the show, your best bet is to walk to one of the nearby hotels and get an Uber from there, you will miss the surcharge by walking a short distance and it will be easier to find your ride.

Great little venue and we would definitely come back here again!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Well, first let me say that I did not have any food while I was at Honkey Tonk! But my boyfriend and I had our first experience to Nashville, TN, and we spent 3 nights at Honkey Tonk. The first night was my birthday night!! The band on the second floor invited me on stage and sang Happy Birthday to me, and allowed me to pick a couple songs for them to play. They were AWESOME! But also we went there during the day, and the bartenders were absolutely lovely, except 1. They were accommodating and even took pictures for us. I would definitely come back to this place! Their music selection is 99% country, and 1% everything else. But I LOVED it, because I love country music, and having s good time and singing along to bands!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: I went to see the Time Jumpers(with Vince Gill), it was probably the best 20 bucks I ever spent!  I believe they play most  Monday nights there.  What a place to watch live music, nothing beats a small intimate venue!  Our waitress gave excellent service, even with the show being sold out!  Food was good and affordable. They have a bunch of awesome painted portraits of music legends.  This place is a most do!  It is about a mile off Broadway, but you can get a golf cart ride for tips only, it is called "Joyride provided by the city of Nashville. Oh yeah, their alcohol there is pretty good too!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Unfortunately, I need to give this establishment 1 star due to the inability to reach anyone about an item that I left. I was in for business and out the next day so unable to just go back to pick up the item.

A friend and I have called their listed number continuously for 3 days/nights - no answer. I posted 2 requests on their Facebook page - no comment or reply. Today,  I submitted a quote request for a private party hoping that someone would respond or call me. The auto response to the form listed a different # of which I left a voicemail - NOTHING.

Unbelievable!

name: Loveless Events
text: Beautiful place with a lot of space. The food was from Loveless Cafe and it was awesome.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Hell I don't listen to country on a regular, But this place was great. Other than the meatball bouncer copping a attitude at the door while I was trying to get a hot dog....I understand no drinks outside, just tell me where to put it. Attitude was rectified when I hit him with kindness in verbal judo.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Great group,fabulous bartenders and the music was worth hanging around for.
Dance floor small and the request  for tips for the musician is  sad. Pay them a living wage.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text:
Our kind of place!
A hole in the wall joint with friendly locals, a nice bartender and local singer/song writers. Off the beaten  path (not walkable), in a neighborhood, but well worth the Uber ride.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Just left.  They will entice you to put in money for a song request, then when they do not play it, they tell you that you made the wrong song choice. The people there are so rude.  Do not go!!   So many awesome music venues in Nashville this is not one of them.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Horrible bar.  $18 for a drink, no atmosphere, bathrooms were disgusting, waitresses extremely rude. Tried charging us for drinks we did not order. Do not go here, so many other better spots on Broadway that actually had a pulse. Customer service better step it up if they want to stick around, bad reviews travel fast and travel far. Would have given this place a negative star rating if it were possible.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Like everyone's mentioned there's different floors for different music. My friend and I got some drinks and sat in on the live music on the ground floor before heading up to the rooftop. I don't know if this is always the case but since it had just rained all day, it was very beautiful and breezy up on the roof. With mostly music from the 90's onwards blazing, it was a good dance atmosphere. I'd recommend people to come check out Nashville Underground, but of course as the night wears on, it gets more and more crowded so be prepared to stand in line.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Here on a special Girls week vacation; causin' trouble and makin' new friends with our awesome bartender Shelley who kicked ass!  Our new home away from home.  We will be back for Shelley.  We love Shelley!

name: Nashville Underground
text: I would give this place a zero. The fact that they won't let people in without passports is ridiculous especially when your at a bar. The bouncer sent everyone home without a passport. Valid drivers license for folks that are clearly over drinking age was not sufficient. My husband and I were turned away and bouncer said come back with a passport.  Good luck to you & Gavin. Plenty of other roof tops will let you in with a license.  I only use my passport for traveling internationally.  Was not aware that Nashville Tennessee was outside the USA.

name: Famous Nashville
text:
Had a business meal here the other day.  There were about 35 of us. I was a little nervous as we only had one server for our group.  However, I must say that Kaitlyn the server was absolutely amazing.  She handled our group with perfection making no mistakes along the way. 

The drinks were flowing and the food was great.  I have eaten at countless restaurants over the years and without  a doubt the service from kaitlyn was the best I have had in any large group setting.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text:
If there's any truth to the rumors --- an iconic live music is on the verge of shutdown by corporate monsters. 
If so, I am glad I had the chance to experience Bobby's!
Live music, beers, friendly regulars, and best yet, no problem finding free parking ! 
A must see for Nashville visitors and residents alike !

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
3rd and Lindsley is the perfect example of don't judge a book by its cover. I was so excited to see that DeVotchKa was coming to Nashville for a show. When I saw that it was at 3rd and Lindsley, I had mixed feelings but wow, was I wrong to do so. 

3rd and Lindsley is located on a corner in a strip of a few other businesses. While there is parking out front, don't count on it. I got there about 45 minutes before the opening act and it was already full. Luckily, there is a parking lot across the street. This one is paid but for $10, it's not bad. The concert tickets were only $20 so I was fine with dishing out a little extra dough. Upon entering, the bouncer asked for my name. They have a list so I guess that's how they keep track of ticket sales. It works. 3rd and Lindsley is kind of set up like a dive bar with a stage. The bar is to the right when you walk in. It wasn't too busy yet so I decided to grab a beer there. Friendly and fast service. Beer prices are good. I then went to look for a seat. On the main level there are normal tables with plenty of chairs. The lower level stage area is open if you wish to stand. The nice thing is the main area with all of the tables is slightly raised so if people are standing, you can still see. There is also a second level with seating but the band insisted that everyone sit on the main level. No problem. I was able to snag a seat right up front. I had the perfect view. I was really close to the stage but still had the comfort of sitting down. There was a server assigned to the area and he was really attentive. Not in a pushy or annoying way, just a quick check-in to see if I needed another beer. While I didn't order food, the menu looked decent. When the show started, I was really impressed by the sound. Really clear and the perfect volume. I was so happy I got there early because I had the perfect view. I love DeVotchKa so getting to see them so close up and with such great sound was amazing. I could see how this place could get cramped if it was a sold out show, but this night was busy without being too busy. While it's not the fanciest place, it delivers great sound at unbeatable prices. I will definitely be returning when another band catches my eye.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Tri level bar with three stages and three bars on three levels. Live music every weekend. Lots of variety with their music groups they have rotating throughout the day. Drink prices are a little steep, but strong. Don't ask for a 'long pour of anything, because they make it a double, which is double the price! $18 for a 'double' cranberry vodka! 

The drinks are a little more stiff than most places though, but expensive. Also, be prepared to wait for the bathroom line for a long time here. Single room. No stall, just a room.

Still one of my favorite places to be when I'm in Nashville.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Honky Tonk is located right on the corner of the main tourist strip Broadway.  We walked passed it a few times and after hearing the band we decided to go in and check it out.  It was early afternoon on a Monday and they were packed.  It's a huge bar with plenty seating and tables as well.  It could use a remodel as it was dingy.  Our bartenders were awesome and quick.  I was drinking Patron Margarita's and they were made so well that I kept drinking I enjoyed them so much. 

The patrons hanging out in the bar are mainly tourist and they were all fun and having a good time.  From plenty of Bachelorette's  and every single age group.  This is just another thing I love about country music, no age limits.  You can find every age group who are country music fans.  I guess Nashvilel is the number one destination for Bachelorette's to come and party.  They are everywhere.  I can totally see why.  So many fun roof top bar's and plenty of fun thing's to do along with such great restaurants. 

We had eaten a big breakfast so we did not try any food here and not quite sure I would. It may be a tourist bar but the drinks were very reasonably priced, great service, and the band was awesome and very engaging.  Most folks don't realize these bands work for tips only, so take care of them if you are enjoying their music.  We tipped well, requested a song that they played very well and I even purchased their CD.  They were really good and so engaged with all of the patrons throughout the bar.

We had a fun few hours hanging out drinking and enjoying the fabulous band. Hit this place up as it is really fun.

I could have done without the restroom attendant. I appreciate trying to help folks out but I never go into restroom with my purse so I had to go back to give money for handing me a smidge of soap. Really didn't fit the place.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great bar on Broadway in Nashville with fantastic music on every floor with the third being my favorite floor. It's awesome to look out onto the street from above and enjoy the sights and sounds of what is now to be considered the new NashVegas. The band was absolutely fabulous and the vibe is really chill. After a few hours of being there, had to order some food, nothing major, just chicken fingers and fries. The menu has typical bar food and they were good, not great, but good enough to feed some of the liquor in my belly. It's convenient that they have a bathroom upstairs because heading down the stairs would definitely not be appealing. I would definitely say that if you're ever in Nashville, this is one stop that you definitely have to make because it's one of the iconic bars in town, and you will have a hell of a good time!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Nicest bathrooms in Nashville!  Bartenders Ed & Charity were fantastic! We have a group of 6 visiting from Wisconsin and they both were so pleasant and entertaining. We felt very welcomed! The only thing we would suggest is using plastic cups instead of glass. The drinks served in glassware was nice but seemed risky.
