We all agree 5 stars for bartenders but gave 4 stars because of glass, table set up in dance area and music should have been louder.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: After the trek from Tuscaloosa to Nash, I was super excited to make it down to Broadway. Once we walked around a little bit, we decided to stop at this honky tonk! It looked like the perfect mixture of chill and fun from the outside, and that it was! We were there from 6pm to midnight, as the amount of fun we had made us lose track of time. Tried some local brews, ate some tater tots, and danced a TON! If you are young, but don't mind out hanging with an older crowd, and looking for a fun experience, this is it! Bands were great, large bar, not much selection, but overall a great experience!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Music was exceptional.  The cockroach doing the back stroke on our table at midnight was not.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
We came here since all the places a couple of smaller venues didn't have a table. We didn't care for the food. We had much better food at Hattie B. the chicken felt like it was spoiled before they cooked it. Had to eat when we got back to the hotel. The place wasn't too crowded, that's why we decided to go in. It;s more of a sports bar (upper level completely) and downstairs there's a stage. The bathroom has a pink slanted counter and a lady handing out paper towels and a portable dispensing soap bottle for a tip. The counter reminded me of a strip joint vanity area. lol

 We stayed for a little bit. It was okay. The entire district seems chaotic spring break, vegas new orleans style. We may venture out a bit and try some other places that are less of a touristy trap and where the locals like to go.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Staci (yea with an "i") and Whitney were great! They made sure our drinks were never empty and made the best mixed shots. Even thought they paid me for this review I would recommend the Benchmark!  I'm totally kidding on the paid part. There was great live music and tv's were we could watch the NBA playoff game. They are worth the visit for good service, great drinks and music!

name: Alley Taps
text: We really only decided to come here based on the live music we could hear from the speakers as we passed by and we were very pleased with our decision! Great beer selection and WONDERFUL pizza!!! I was not expecting bar food to be so delicious. The friendly staff and live music were an added bonus. Highly recommend!

name: Loveless Events
text: What a stunningly beautiful venue for a southern country wedding! I was extremely impressed with the space and the lighting was classy. I'm a bit envious that I cannot change my wedding venue to Loveless, alas I am not getting married in TN! Ha Ha.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I like this bar, but I think it is absolutely bs that they make someone stand in the bathroom and put soap and paper towels in people's' hands and don't even pay them. They spent the time to make, print, and laminate signs informing their customers that they DO NOT pay their bathroom attendants to "encourage" tips. I tipped because it is not the bathroom attendant's fault, but I feel that this is not the correct way to run a business. If you want a bathroom attendant in your establishment, pay them. If you don't, I know damn well how to put soap on my own hands. Pick one. Happy to tip, but I don't like the approach taken of hiring bathroom attendants and then guilting people into helping them make approximately no money for doing a demeaning job.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Dueling pianists, often accompanied by bass and drums, play cover requests, spiced with friendly or biting commentary. While there's plenty of fun watching the waitstaff do the time warp, the real attraction is the musicianship of hearing on-the-fly versions of everything from 60s classics to the latest Bruno Mars. Not the extra loud atmosphere of other Broadway bars.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: I had a great time. My first time at a place like this I didn't know what to expect....classical or just a guy playing a piano. Well let me tell you I was wrong it started off with 2 guys on different piano playing one song then going right in to another. They interact with the crowd about songs and requested songs. If you want your song played TIP them. they also break into a full band and the drinks were priced right. Overall a great time cant wait to got back

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Attended this bar on a Saturday night, and the place was definitely full of entertainment. These guys are seriously SO talented-- as most play all the instruments as well as sing, NOT to mention pretty much know every single song the crowd asks for. For me (as I am not into huge crowds or the typical dirty bar scene) this was an excellent stop while in Nashville. Actually went here with my boyfriend and it served as fun, but chill bar date night. The staff was really friendly and helpful, and were constantly asking if we needed anything. Also I liked how this bar was cleaner than a lot of the others and the staff was constantly cleaning up used cups, etc, so things would not get too messy. If you come to the Big Bang-- definitely expect a good time and lots of laughs!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: AMAZING !!!! It was our first time to Nashville, and nothing compares to this place!!! My husband and I came twice during our stay because we had SO much fun !!! Huge shoutout to TYSON who just killed it !!! He was able to play all the songs we were requesting and it was amazing. Also, as a tip, request Kenny's Prince mashup because your life won't be the same afterwards. It was incredibly amazing !!! What a talented group of performers !!!!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
This was my favorite bar in Nashville - which says a lot about me, I think, namely that country music is not my thing!  If it isn't yours either, then make this place your home.  We had a DAMN good time here on a Sunday night, no cover, place was crowded but you could still get a table and drinks fairly easily.  They had three pianists, who rotated so that they could take breaks and/or play the drums.  Most of the piano players were young and cute and funny, but all were extremely talented musicians.  They were making everyone laugh all night, and they could turn ANYTHING into a great piano song.  I was singing along all night!  Yeah it's mainly pop music, some current, some 80s/90s, but let's be real - I love that stuff.  And these guys could turn Baby Got Back into a piano song!  That is impressive!  $20 for a request is pretty steep, but I imagine drunk people are willing to do it.  I didn't feel the need to request anything since their whole song list was like putting my iPod on shuffle. 

There's plenty of honky tonk and country on Broadway.  If you need a break from it, go here. You won't regret it!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Attended the grand re-opening last night and thought the venue was amazing!  The line-up stellar - the place was packed!  We had fried pickles, fish tacos and the nashvegas burger - everything was great! My husband tends to be a 'burger snob' and wanted to go back the next day for another one!  The home-made chips are perfect too!!  

The owner is wonderful - he stopped and talked with guests all evening!  He is very friendly and approachable.

The venue is perfect!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great music, low quality food. My waiter lost my credit card and showed great indifference to that fact. Not good...

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: 4 great songwriters and great drinks. Food is good. Come for the music. Wait staff was very good. More enjoyable than cramming into a bar on Broadway.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
I will have to say this place is pretty cool but I have to give 2 stars because last night my girlfriend and I went and there were maybe 10 other people in there and I tipped them and make a request for a Boston song 

They instead wanted to keep playing rap music because some drunk people kept giving them $20 

It sort of pissed me off. I wasted 2 1/2 hours waiting for my request to be played and it never was..

Very disappointing 

I will not tip these guys EVER again

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great spot! We were immediately welcomed by a friendly and fun staff. Jake is an amazing bartender! I love his upbeat personality and he makes outstanding drinks! We enjoyed the bands both days we were there and food is delicious! Each floor has a different, but cool vibe and I really like the decor. We will definitely go back next time we are in Nashville!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Being our first time in Nashville, we stayed downtown and did the touristy bars along Broadway.  After 3 days of the crowds, annoying bachelor/bachelorette parties, and drunk college kids we wanted to venture out and just listen to some good music in a different atmosphere.  We heard about the Listening Room located just a few blocks from downtown and made reservations which surprisingly was only $5 per person.  They have 2 shows Monday through Saturday nights at 6 and 8:30 pm.  I called the venue to find out what time I should arrive for the 8:30 show.  I was told that the 6 pm show ends at 7:30 and since the seating is first come, first serve, I should arrive at 7:30.  Glad I did because we beat the crowd in and were able to get a great seat.  However, this location has plenty of seating....but if you want to sit near the stage, plan on coming early.  They have a $15 per person minimum once you have been seated....ordering drinks at the bar in the wait area do not count.  The prices were fairly reasonable....My Yuengling was $4 a bottle....cheaper than I had on the strip.  The menu was typical bar food.  We ordered the cheese plate that came with pita chips, gouda cheese, cheddar cheese, and a generous serving of pimento cheese.  Other items on the appetizer menu were hummus, chicken sticks, and hot wings. They also have dinner items as well.  The music was excellent.  There were 4 artists sitting side by side on stage...each one taking turns playing songs they wrote themselves and usually giving a short intro on how they came up with the song.  All in all, we had a great time and would highly recommend to anyone looking to hear good new music.  One final thing....if you are staying in the downtown area....even though it is about 10 blocks from Broadway, I would recommend taking an Uber especially on the way back since this area could be a little shady at night.

name: 360 Burger
text: Our waiter was very pleasant, and took the time to tell us about the menu. The food and drinks were delicious,  and even my toddler enjoyed his kids meal. Service was quick, we are definitely coming back again.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
We had 7 of us from ages 9 to 79 went on a beautiful afternoon.  I choose not to add the food option based upon the reviews here, Opry Mills is where you park so there are plenty of restaurants nearby. 
Things I did not see mentioned.
The keyboard entertainer up top made this trip very enjoyable.  He got the crowd going, I think he name was Casey.  
Had it rained as was in our forecast - the ride would have been a lot less enjoyable and we probably would have been squished.  
There is a short list of food for purchase that we didn't find out about until the ride's end if you want something to hold you over. 
Drinks are pricey but it's a cruise after all.  
"Sunday in the South" theme was not for us, we hardly watched the show.
Buffet - I did a walkby and was happy that wasn't our lunch.
Overall enjoyable smooth sailing to downtown and back.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
On a road trip I stopped at several museums but this was the best.  Price is $17.95 for seniors and we forgot our $1 off coupon you can get at any hotel.  
The place is clean and when I accidently touched the glass by the Remington piece, someone was there to wipe my prints off as soon as I walked away.  I apologized when I saw him at the end of the tour.  Very interesting.  Give yourself some time to really look at all the stuff.  Sooooo much to see.  More than I thought there would be. 
One problem.  I had my photo taken but they were not very good at directing me on how to stand so the picture would look like I was playing with the guitar with Johnny.  Make sure you check out the other photos and ask them to set up the photo exactly like the example.  I personally think $12.95 is all they should have charged me for a printed copy.  I did not need the $5 to down load it.  I wish they would correct that part.  But it is a cool picture.

name: 360 Burger
text:
I was a bit confused by this place.  First, if its a sporty bar place please put on more variety games/sports on their 20 tv sets.  All of them had basketball (same useless channel) and it was not a game. I do not care for basketball but I will watch hockey, NASCAR, golf, even curling but something else, please.  Secondly, Is it a fast food burger place?  Is it a casual dining place?  Now, the burger.  it was ok.   Fries, skip them.  Thirdly, Service was very good.  

I am not sure about this place, odd.

name: 360 Burger
text:
I hit this place up for a friends birthday party.  The food was good and priced nice (hey! Free shake with a Yelp check in!) The HUGE problem was the house band.  We had a larger party and it was impossible to talk to anyone that wasn't directly next to you.  The music was very loud.  At one point the saxophone player made his rounds to the tables and played to people...it was super uncomfortable.
I want to go back to hit up there extensive happy hour menu but I'll be sure to check out the entertainment situation first.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
OVER THE TOP FUN!

If you don't know the name of a song or the artist, at least know a lyric or two...

Throw it out on a slip of paper, a TIP would be nice, since you are requesting it...and the fun begins!

These guys will belt out ANY song ever written. The oldies, the funk, the rock, the blues, the R&B, the hip hop, the pop...there was not a song they could not play by heart on the pianos. A drummer was added and these guys, rather HOT, by the way...they mixed it up and changed positions playing the grand pianos and master drums!

It was a blast! 
Ever in Nashville, this is a MUST SEE!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Just visited Nashville for my second time over and was determined to get a 'songwriters experience. A friend of mine who's been living there for several years directed me to The Listening Room. She said it's a lot less crowded and strict than the bluebird which has to get some sell out months in advance now.

I have to say I absolutely loved this venue, however they do sell tickets in advance online. They're super cheap about $5 or $10 but you're going to want to make sure that you got those tickets so that you don't have to wait out in line like I did hoping to get a waiting list seat. I got the seats the show was great but I could definitely have done without the 1 hour and 15 minute wait because I didn't plan properly, so don't make my mistake!

Now on to the show. Once you get inside they do have a $10 per person minimum during the show which last anywhere from 90 minutes to 2 hours. Serve food in a full-service bar so it's not hard to hit. Food get 3 stars. Nothing special so is recommend having done drinks and eating elsewhere. 

Music was fantastic! When I was there there were three singer-songwriters on the stage taking turns playing songs they've written. Several of them have even written number 1 top hits from people on country music radio right now! They were so talented! The venue is small and fairy intimate but didn't feel cramped. They do allow whispering - my understanding is many others like Bluebird do not. 

Loved it! Will go again!

name: 360 Burger
text: Easily the best "upscale" burger place in town. I had the mushroom swiss, very good, nice and juicy. We also had the sliders, fried mushrooms, and salmon burger. The piece of salmon was huge for the price but I think putting it on a burger didn't do it any favors. It would be better as an entree. The onion rings were not my cup of tea, but if you like the beer batted thick cut kind they are perfect for you. Overall, excellent food good atmosphere and fair price. Definitely give it a try!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
I usually love a dueling piano bar, and I figured being in Nashville there should be some great artists here.  That said, this is more set up like a concert with rows of folding chairs facing the two pianists.  It was a bit uncomfortable, and just plain awkward.  I would have expected more of a lounge/bar feel where the pianos were part of the entertainment, not the sole purpose of the establishment, to the point they did not even invest in cocktail tables.

And, they did not play our request despite the $5 tip.  I will stick to the country music bars next time.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great great room and vibe.  Food is a little full but not bad.  A much more convenient option than Bluebird but it feels similar.  Very nice staff.  Great music!!'

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
So wife and I went on this boat trip and really enjoyed it. It wasn't 5 star food, but it was a fun night out. The weather was great. It was a chance to get out on the water. The show and food was good for what you are paying for. It's just about the experience. And we enjoyed it. 

The only thing I would add as a recommendation. Clean the outside of the boat a bit. A lot of insects and spider webs everywhere. The waiting landing needed a bit of pressure washing too. 

But again, I did enjoy our time and would bring family back when they come visit.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Get the big hit burger - you need to eat this one with your fork! Dig in don' t be shy there is always great music here!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: The Johnny Cash Museum was so wonderful.  Learned such many things about JC that I didn't  know. The time seemed to stop when you're there. Be prepared to spend a few hours poring over the vast articles and music. If you want a nice afternoon getting to know the man in black this is the place to go.

name: 360 Burger
text: I've had to move my review from 5-stars to 3-stars. I still love the food, but the last two times I've been I've waited over 60 minutes for my food, and both times the restaurant was nearly empty. On one of the occasions, some in my group waited over 80 minutes for their burgers. Until I hear that the speed of the service has picked up, I probably won't go back.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I went to The Listening Room Cafe tonight, and the food was awful--greasy nachos with fake cheese and no salsa, unimpressive mac and cheese, and the so-called "house-smoked seasonal vegetables" consisted of microwaved broccoli and carrots with a sickeningly sweet teriyaki sauce drizzled over them. It is 4 hours later and I am still feeling ill.

name: 360 Burger
text: In a nutshell, best burgers, great atmosphere and wonderful management.  Will definitely be back often!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Want some good food and great music without all the hassle of getting into the Bluebird Cafe (not to knock it)? 

The listening room cafe has a large dining room and was really easy to get tickets to. 

There is free parking in their lot for customers ($10 for non-customers) and they let us park there about an hour before the show so we could hit Broadway.

They have a nice menu with lots of options. The pricing is a little high but portion sizes are good. The hot chicken is delicious, but even the mild will take your head off. 

The music is the real kicker. The talent was excellent and the show was all acoustic. 

Definitely a place to check out for a good, hassle-free evening.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
You cannot visit Nashville, aka Music City, and NOT visit the Johnny Cash Museum. This was one of the highlights of my weeklong vacation to Tennessee with the wife, and although I had high expectations of this place, it absolutely surpassed them. An amazing museum dedicated to the Man in Black.
I love that you can peruse everything at your pace. There's so much to see and take in- handwritten letters and lyrics, pictures, outfits, instruments, gold records, personal items from his home, I really can't explain the amount of cool things there are to take in at this museum.
You could walk through in under 30  minutes if you're in a hurry, but to really take it all in, we took about an hour. It's absolutely worth the price of admission, and ANY music fan would appreciate the museum, but if you're a fan of Johnny Cash it's a MUST-DO. I think kids would enjoy it, although most older folks probably have more of an appreciation for what's there, but the kids could still have fun. The store is also very cool, lots of awesome t-shirts, mugs, etc for sale, I could've spent a few hundred bucks there for sure.
This museum is a short walk from Broadway- if you're doing a day in Nashville, I think this is one of the must-do's. Totally worth the price of admission, it's an amazing look at history and life of one of the greatest musicians to ever live. No cheese, no tourist trap, just a great collection of items from Johnny Cash's life. So glad I went and I recommend you go to!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Must see. Pay the money. It's worth it. 45 to 60 minutes. Great stuff. A lot of reading but it's worth it. We were a little hesitant at first because when we first came in the museum there were a lot of people and they were all bunched together but it thinned out pretty quickly. Definitely worth making the time for to learn about one of country's most influential singers.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The music was great, food mediocre. On top of the $7 entrance fee per person they overcharged us for 1 drink I did not receive and they charged a 21% gratuity for a party of 6.....I found it absurd that the 21% was after an additional $20 + in taxes. When I return to Nashville I will come back but only come for drinks. I have never heard of gratuity after tax, especially for poor service and cold food.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: It's was fun, but a little cheesy. Good place to go if you want to beat the crowd for a bit.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Ended up walking out. Had high hopes but sat there for over 15 minutes and no service. Upstairs and patio closed. Bummer

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Went before a New Years Eve concert and thoroughly enjoyed it. Had to leave before I started spending too much in the gift shop.

name: 360 Burger
text: Consider yourself warned!!  Don't waste your time!!  I don't usually leave bad reviews only positive ones, but our experience here was just that bad and I had to say something. We were one of two tables that were occupied in the place at 11:30AM.  Now I know why.  The service was the absolute worst and the food was just ok.  After finally waiting an eternity for someone to take our food order and for it to be prepared, we heard the cool yell order up.  We waited. The waiter went over and stood by our food and texted. We waited. He texted. We waited. He texted. He saw us just sitting there staring at him.  And he went back to texting.  I'm a polite guy but I was angry at this point.  I know how tough running a business is and I try to eat local.  I hope the owner reads this post, and gets his employees up to par. I'll never know because I won't be back.  $15 for a burger, fries, and drink before tip.  It was ok, but a burger for that price should be all that and more in my opinion.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: As a first time visitor to Nashville, this place came recommended, so we made a reservation. The songwriters who performed were pretty darn good. I wish that I could say the same for the food. I ordered the turkey sandwich, which wasn't terrible, but it was cold & the bread was mushy. My husband ordered the pot roast, which consisted of a tablespoon of beef au jus, no vegetables,  & dry baked Mac & Cheese. None of which was very warm. Of course we came to listen to music, but the deal is you pay to enter, & you must spend at lease $15 per person on whatever, or simply pay the additional money at the end w/o eating or drinking. Since we don't drink, we chose from their menu.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: For overall Nashville atmosphere and live music this place is awesome. The singers were outstanding, the food was really good, and the drinks pretty good as well. Overall definitely a cool place to visit. If you are coming with a big party lookout because this place gets packed! Apparently you can try braving the crowd or buy tickets for $5 a day or so early in order to confirm your seat. Overall a really cool place to come and try out. So turns out after eating and drinking here it is even more grand than I thought. It is basically the musical straight version of Nashville's / NYC's version of 58 below. Absolutely beautiful music.

name: 360 Burger
text: Great place for lunch, dinner or a drink after work.  Burgers are great and make sure to try the turkey burger!  I eat at 360 at least 3 times a week.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: My parents came to town for Xmas so I bought us all tickets on Christmas Eve day so we would have something fun to do. The weather was terrible so that meant walking around the boat in freezing rain wasn't the best, I have to imagine this would be really nice on a sunny, warm day. The food was typical banquet style. The best part was the apple cake that probably wasn't even made on the property. I requested the chicken and it came with potatoes and a few green beans. Nothing I'd call delicious cuisine. The show itself was decent, with some talented performers. It was entertaining although it was hard to see from my vantage point behind a giant pole. This is a decent time, but I'm not sure it was worth the money.

name: 360 Burger
text: Finally got to try 360 Burger tonight, it was great. The experience was started with Justin and his welcoming personality, he even helped carry out (we got to go) my burgers and drinks because I was carrying my one year old. The burgers were amazing. They tasted like the best homemade burgers I've ever had. Patties were seasoned very well and it had a great smokey flavor. I got the slippery pig and my wife got the Ol' Smokey (she loved hers as well). We will be back for sure and next time we'll eat in, the inside was very welcoming and had a small stage for live music...sounds like fun! Again though Justin did a great job, I always appreciate excellent customer service and he was great.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Food was excellent and of course the music was top notch. Amazing to hear the songwriters sing their own songs!

name: Silver Dollar Saloon
text:
Walking through the busy downtown at night, we took a break from boot shopping (for me!) and found a place with live music and some fun. 

Downtown is lively at night, so many people out celebrating, shopping, eating and drinking. We found ourselves a tiny little bit of the bar at the end. I ordered a Jack and Diet Coke and my guy ordered a beer. 

The music was great, but we didn't stay long as we had to get some dinner. All in all, it was a fun place with a great band.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
We've been to DBWR twice to eat, once for brunch and the other for dinner. I'm glad we tried the brunch first because if we would've had dinner first we probably wouldn't have gone back. 

The brunch menu isn't large but the options were tasty. There were 4 of us. We ordered 2 Bloody Marys and 2 Mimosas. They had run out of OJ for the mimosas and asked if pineapple juice would be ok to sub or if we wanted a different drink. We opted for the pineapple juice sub and it wasn't bad. For food we ordered 2 breakfast sandwiches, the chicken and waffles and breakfast burrito. ALL of the food was delicious. We couldn't get enough. Will definitely go back for brunch. 

Fast forward to the weekend after the 4th of July we decided to try dinner. We had to find our own seat which was challenging. We ended up on the 2nd floor. The booth had a drip above it probably from the AC being on overload from the hot temps. I'm not sure how our waitress was able to get our order right as it was so loud but she did and was awesome. There was 4 of us again. We ordered the pretzel and beer cheese dip for an appetizer and the fish and chips, mac and cheese, turkey melt and mushroom burger for our main courses. None of us were super thrilled with the food. I only had half of my sandwich. My fiance said Jason Aldean's fish and chips were way better. The mac and cheese was ok, nothing special as well as the burger. I will say that the garlic fries were delicious and I ordered a J.I.M.B.O. to drink which was sweet but good. The pretzel had a little too much seasoning but was overall good. The beer cheese it came with was amazing. Beers at DBWR are cheaper by $1-$2 compared to some other bars on Broadway. 

Overall a fun bar with a good vibe.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: Very cool! Some of the figures legit looked like real people. We did think that it would be a bit bigger but the rooms were very cool. Convenient location inside the mall next to the Grand Ole Opry.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Bought a living social deal to use while we were on vacation in Nashville.  First off.. figured the reason they were on living social... construction blocked the parking lot and the front entrance making it really hard to get to. They have a giant banner on the side of there building, printed on their door, and printed on their menus that Brunch was served Saturday and Sunday from 10 am to 3 pm. We arrived Saturday at 10 am. Was seated and ordered drinks. Then we were told that the kitchen didnt opened until 11 am. ... seriously then why does the giant banner on the side of your building say 10am?????

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: We are Johnny Cash fans and we still learned a lot. There was lots of music to listen to, videos to watch and some fascinating objects from his life.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This was a fun museum. It isn't organized particularly well but the memorabilia and extensive collection is great. Would recommend to anyone going to visit Nashville

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Family and I had a great time. The guys that played were funny and talented. The only draw back was trying to find the place.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Great live entertainment! Wish there was more room for dancing, though. The pianists get better as the night goes on. They also can play multiple instruments. What talent!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Great place to listen to amazing music.  Unpretentious!  It is a treat to see and hear the musicians and then you never know who might be in the audience that will just go up and jam on stage with the performers.  My daughter and I love all kinds of music and this was a wonderful venue to visit in Nashville!
go for drinks and music!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
If singer/song writers are your thing, this is a must place to go.  And it's downtown.
The food is good and the performers are excellent.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: The General is a good attraction for bringing guests from out of town to.  I personally don't care for country music, so Nashville is not my favorite destination.  I can get by with the music because they put on a fairly entertaining show.  The food however, is pretty ruff.  For the price of the tickets a higher quality meal should be provided.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: This place is a really neat concept. It wasn't as busy as some of the other spots nearby, but we did go in the early evening and it was still about a third full. I think it'd be best to come here late in the evening when it's busier. Still, we saved on cover which they start charging later in the evening.  The pianists are pretty talented and they sang everything anyone threw at them. We didn't try the food here, but the drinks were reasonably priced.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Such an awesome place to hear raw talent. Some long lines but worth the wait. We visited from NYC, you can't see musicianship like this up there. Nice beer selection and good drinks. Buy your tickets in advance to make sure you get a seat! Highly recommend to country fans.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I'm not sure about the actual museum because I only stop in for the coffee. The coffee is worth a review. Amazing, but I've always been a Bongo Java fan. Staff is a bit rude, but it's worth it.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Note that this review is primarily judging this place as a music venue. This was my first proper visit to Nashville and I wanted to catch a songwriters "in the round" session. I was easily able to get tickets online for the show and dinner. I would recommend doing the same to avoid waiting in line or possibly being turned away if there are no seats left.

We attended the regular Tuesday evening "in the round" series called The Movement. There were four artists in the 8:30 PM set and another four in the 9:30 PM set. Each artist played a song "in the round" before starting a new round of songs. Sometimes the artists would perform together on a piece. Sometimes this was planned and sometimes an artist just jumped in to provide some spontaneous accompaniment. It was a really fun experience that I highly recommend checking out. Be sure to stay for both sets!

As a side note, we did have drinks (a margarita and a knockoff of an old fashioned) and some side dishes (mac and cheese and mashed potatoes) during the show. Nothing was particularly noteworthy, but as we were both hungry and in need of some libations, they did the trick.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The Listening Room has a cool location and the interior is really cool! Go to hear music and have a drink or three...i would suggest avoiding the food. I got shrimp and grits and I LOVE shrimp and grits. The version I got here, were a few shrimp swimming in a tasteless sea of soupy grits. The musical acts, the night we went, were hit or miss. I will go back and see if it was just an off night for the place. It seems to have a lot going for it...maybe I just went at a bad time.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The only reason this restaurant has 3 stars for me is because the ladies singing were amazing! If I were to return, it would be strictly for the performers. Other than that, the service was terrible and the food wasn't amazing, it was just okay and overpriced. They do have buy one get one mimosas and they were pretty good. 21% Gratuity is added if there are more than 6 people in the group. Since we had such bad service, I was irritated that I had to pay 21%. If it weren't for the service and having to pay 21% of the bill to the server, I would have probably left in a much better mood.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text:
I'd give it two but the guy at the door was really nice guy!
My buds ordered Coronas and I ordered a Bloody Mary.
The Coronas turned out to be a safe bet! Not just cause they're cold frosty and consistent but aft two sips of my Bloody Mary I got the cold consistent eye roll and "what's wrong with you?" Attitude from the bartender girl and her fellow bartender! 
When I commented about all the "stuff" in the Bloody Mary (mushroom, olive, onion, green beans, a pickle, and s strip of over cooked dried out bacon strip! When I questioned the server, her response was "what do you want me to do about it?" I told her simp it out! She rolled her eyes in disgust and then picked it up with out looking away and dumped it in the trash! Like "how's that!" Them proceeded to tell me how people come there for the bloody Mary's and they don't use artificial premise mixes - my advice - lose the server and your own mix!
I was so disappointed because I heard it was Owens's by George Strait and I'm a huge fan! My advice is to make the door guy a manager and get rid of the rude bartenders!the place has a weird vibe - don't waste your time

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Warm bottles of beer. If you are in your 20s you are probably ok but if you are in your 50s, expect to be ignored and served very last.  Would not recommend.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: If you are in Nashville, this should be on your list of things to experience. We are not country music fan. But we still enjoyed the night. Ended up staying for back to back shows. Great talent on both shows. This isn't the loud honky tonk music you experience downtown. It felt classier and very enjoyable. Entry is usually $5-10 per person and $10 minimum on food and drinks. Food and drinks are reasonably priced and decent. Recommend this place.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great music and service. Different singers on every floor. Clean and nice and cool with big ass fans during the summer heat. Had brunch her and drinks the night before. Good atmosphere.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
So, first of all, I have been there twice, and have had 2 different experiences.  The first time was very good - both the venue and the food.  The word must have gotten out, and the second time we went (July 2019) the place was packed.  And...that is what this review is about.

The music was great.  If you have not been, they have song-writers who sing their own music.  Some of it is largely unknown, but some has been recorded by major artists.  That part was great both times.

They cram the tables together, and the place was jam-packed.  The service was the opposite of good - with drink and food orders taking fuh-ever to get out there.  And, the food was not great either.  My wife had a chicken something-or-other that she said tasted good.  I had the brisket sandwich.  It was tough and cut into slabs.  There were ribbons of fat or gristle running through it.  It was relatively tasteless, even though it was advertised as a special rub and smoked until tender, blah, blah, blah.  You will see you waiter to take you order, and then when they want to be paid.

I sent a comment in to the Listening Room through their website.  They never responded.  It's a business.  I get that.  Like an airline, they are going to cram as many paying customers in as they can.  My personal opinion (and it pains me to say it) is that they grew until they broke.  

Nevertheless, the music was good.  Next time I will order a hamburger or something simple for them.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
It's difficult to overstate the appeal & importance of Johnny Cash to country music.  Like all performers, he had ups & downs through the course of his long career, but his legacy is a powerful & lasting one, to which this museum is a fitting memorial.

Which of course means that as it's located centrally in downtown Nashville, it's also a rather crowded one.  I was in town recently for the weekend to see Paul Simon perform at the Ryman Auditorium & never having been to Nashville before, wanted to experience the best of the city.  I figured this was part of it & made a point of including it on my list.  I allowed myself a little more than an hour to experience the full museum (a single floor, made up of some genuine content & a fair mix of "period" pieces, plenty of audio/visual material & text displays to read as you wander through the museum).  

There's a cafe & a gift shop that has a decent, albeit uninspired selection & you're allowed to take photos (no flash) & no video.  This is a must-see stop, as anyone should be aware of the Man in Black & his impact on country music.

name: 360 Burger
text: We went to 360 Burger for the first time last night. It was an early dinner on a Sunday night, so not too many people there. Service was prompt and friendly. The place looked nice and was really clean. We got to watch the football game on the big screen. As for the food... the burgers were great. Really well seasoned. I had the mushroom swiss burger and hubby had the bleu cheese burger. The fries, on the other hand, left something to be desired. They tasted fine, but were pretty limp. I like mine crispier on the outside. When the server brought our check, she also brought us each a fresh drink in a to-go cup, which I thought was a nice touch. We'll be back!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Had 4 songwriters on stage. They all had great stories about their songs, really an awesome mix of talent. There was not a bad seat in the house. The acoustics, food, drinks were all fantastic! The brussel sprouts tho...yummiest!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
As an avowed Johnny Cash fan, this place was a marvellous place to spend an hour or two. 

I particularly liked the inclusion of tablets around the place that allowed you to watch clips of Cash's best music. Just try and stop your feet from tapping along!

The little exhibit showing work from other Sun Records artists (like Elvis and Jerry Lee Lewis), was another great touch.

The museum's staff were also extremely friendly and knowledgeable. 

The only reason this didn't get 5 stars is that I would have wished the place to be slightly bigger! For someone who wasn't such a fan, it might not have seemed quite worth the $16 entry fee. Still, definitely one of the better museums that I've been to - highly recommended!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I took my father here for his birthday and he loved it!!!! Very interesting tour, I liked listening to some if the music they displayed,  and the covers done by many country singers. Definitely a place you need to see if you're in the nashville area.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
We were so excited when we found out that The Johnny Cash Museum would be opening just weeks before our trip to Nashville.  We made it the first stop and our trip and it was well worth it!

The museum is laid out nicely and takes you on a journey through Johnny's life and career.  You can tell that a lot of love and care was put in to the design of the museum and the artifacts that were chosen to display.  It was amazing to see the items from Johnny's personal life, including letters to friends and handwritten lyrics from some of his most popular songs.  There is a video you can sit down and watch about half way through the museum about Johnny's movie and TV appearances that is very informative and entertaining.

Over the past week we have been through about a dozen museums and tours in Nashville and Memphis and I have to say The Johnny Cash Museum ranks very high on our list as one of the best.  I was even impressed with the staff working in the museum.  They were very friendly and seemed genuinely happy to be working there.  The gift shop seemed to have more quality items than many of the shops we have been in on our trip.

I would definitely recommend the museum to anyone visiting Nashville!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Bartender dana had the best personality. Favorite bar we went to. Music was fantastic.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The songwriters played some major hits that we had no idea they'd written. It's a great atmosphere where you can make friends and casually chat whilst listening to fantastic acoustic talent. The food was fairly average and the drinks were light on alcohol. What really made our night was our fantastic waiter Trent! He was always hustling to ensure we had everything we needed. Totally worth a 25% tip! When we go back, we definitely want to be in his section!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Even if you're not a huge Johnny Cash fan, this museum is an interesting place to visit. Lots of costumes and memorabilia presented alongside the chronological history of his music career. All the displays were well done and informative. Can easily see the whole museum in an hour.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: This place was pretty cool. It was my first time visiting a wax museum so I have nothing to compare it to. Costumer service was good, I got som really good pictures. My favorite was the Elvis and Jonny Cash exhibit. The pictures I took look like real people. Five stars.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: This was my second Madame Tussaud's visit. The one in DC was more my speed. Felt more... authentic? This one is located at Opry Mills mall. If you buy tickets ahead of time online you save $5. You'll want to do that considering what they charge for what you get. Wax figures are cool to look at but slow your pace down or you'll be finished very quickly. You'll find all your beloved country stars here- Taylor Swift (yes, she started as a country gal), Patsy Cline, Elvis, Reba, Eric Church, Tim McGraw, Kid Rick.. the list goes on. They have a small "pop" room including Justin Timberlake and Queen Bey. Fun place for the kids. Plenty of parking in the mall parking lot. Walk over to the Grand Ole Opry after!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
First of all, I love Johnny Cash. The story. The history. The trials. The music. 
The museum was everything I expected. Love the time line of his career and the old photos. The wall of his hits and recordings was amazing. 
If you take the time to appreciate everything it will take a coupe hours here. Lots of neat artifacts and photos. If you like Johnny Cash be sure to stop.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Today is the first time I visited the Johnny Cash Museum Store. 
( The Johnny Cash Museum opens Spring 2013 ) 

Even though the store is small it makes a strong impact. This shop is not like any other in the downtown area and it's worth the trip. 

The Johnny Cash Museum Store is beautifully designed using the original brick walls, rich dark woods, glass showcases with a few pieces of memorabilia and beautiful artwork. TV monitors on the walls show Johnny Cash footage from the 50's and throughout his amazing 50 year career.  

The merchandise is tasteful. I picked up a couple of CASH coffee cups and a couple of t-shirts. They sell glassware, hoodies, T-shirts, bags, CD's and many other items paying tribute to The Man In Black and Sun Records.  

One case has gorgeous jewelry designed and made by Tara Cash ( Johnny's youngest daughter ). She uses authentic crystals, silver, copper and other high quality materials yet her prices are very reasonable. You can get a "guitar pick" made of silver with "CASH", "Pickin' Time" and other phrases or a stunning pair of crystal and
hammered brass earrings or a crystal necklace. The variety is always changing.

The prices are reasonable throughout and the atmosphere is nice listening to Johnny Cash while browsing. 

I'm anxious for the Museum to open. It's going to be first class all the way.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
It is a fun time place.  I have been to other dueling piano bars and this one wasn't the best I've seen.

My recommendation is to stick to the other bars in the area the music and entertainment is much better.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great atmosphere & lovely employees! The food is wonderful & is definitely one of the top places to visit in Nashville !

name: 360 Burger
text:
A terrific restaurant!  A friend told me about 360 Burger so we decided to give it a try this afternoon and were pleasantly surprised with the entire experience!  For the namesake we decided to eat burgers but the entire menu offered a great variety of seafood, salads, hot chicken, burgers and homemade desserts.  

We started off with fried eggplant and a couple of draft beers, Blue Moon and Jackalope as we waited on our burgers - cilantro avocado and margherita burger with sides of sweet potato fries and french fries that included tangy aioli for dipping.  These stuffed gourmet burgers were excellent with quality ingredients from the local farmers and growers. 

The staff was very attentive and the atmosphere was relaxed and welcoming with a stage set-up for live nighttime music.  I invite you to visit their website and drop by the 360 Burger soon.  It is quickly becoming very popular and now I understand why it is one more successful restaurant presented by the Swett family.  

The Antioch area is thriving with a very active housing market, new businesses, green space, and future projects being solidified for the upcoming next few years.  The 360 Burger is one more attractive option to eat while on the southeast side of town.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
My advice is to go for the music, NOT the food. And I mean skip everything on the menu entirely, even the drinks which are awful. You are only safe with beer. It is a good place to literally go and listen only to music. (No talking!) Which can be hard to do if you are on a date or with a group. 

I ordered a brisket sandwich that I planned to share with someone. The meat was so dry and hard (as in days old or sitting under a heat lamp too long) that I could not cut it. It was inedible. I was with 7 other people and they all had the same experience. Every single one of us left hungry. (And it isn't cheap!)

On top of that, the service was odd. They were having us essentially serve ourselves by standing at the end of the table and passing things down, pointing to who we should deliver it to. This went for the food and drinks. Then at the end we were helping them bus our table, asking us to pile dishes on top of the tray already started. Just not normal. Very low class. The server was in such a hurry to get us out of the room after the show ended that he knocked over a full drink over that spilled onto several people. 

So if are a looking for a place to sit in silence and listen to some great up-and-coming artists, you won't be as disappointed as we were. Just don't show up hungry!  Not to mention that there are MANY other places to listen to good music in Nashville. Do your homework. Skip this place if you can.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
This was a nice museum chock full of memorabilia put together to tell the story of Cash's life.  We went on Saturday and the museum was packed, wall to wall, which made it difficult to see things and the layout was initially a little disorienting.  One of my favorite parts was seeing the stone wall from his house (that sounds boring, but seeing pictures of it and reading about the history, I found it surprisingly moving.)  I also liked the multimedia interactive exhibits.  Also, I didn't realize he was a visual artist!  I would have loved to have seen more examples of his visual art. 

If you are a casual Johnny Cash fan, I still think you'd enjoy the museum... but try to go during the week when it is less busy.

name: 360 Burger
text: I think previous raters are giving higher stars simply because they want the place to survive, but this place deserves nothing higher than 1-2 stars.  You think it's going to be a great place with the awesome and tasty grass-fed beef and interesting burger stylings, but they miss the mark on just about everything.  We had been once before and it was decent.  Food took a bit long but we figured it was because it was new.  The burger was completely overcooked but thankfully the meat was good so it saved it.  We decided to come back a second time to specify how we'd like the burger cooked because we felt it would save it.  Started off well and the server even asked how we'd like the burger cooked.  It was us and about 5 other people in the entire restaurant.  45 minutes later our food still had not arrived.  Meanwhile, we can see directly into the kitchen and it was not a pleasant site.  Note to 360 Burger, if you have your kitchen visible to the consumers, make sure your cooks are kind, presentable, and actually cooking things!!!!  There was one cook, not rushing to get anything done, simply taking his time.  Then two other cooks show up but only distract the first and eat food they find back in the kitchen.  We also got the pleasure of seeing this cook mouth off to the waitress when she picked up someone's food.  That was lovely.  But the icing on the cake, the very reason we left, was when our food FINALLY showed up on the line (over 50 minutes waiting for 2 burgers and fries) our server can't be found.  She's outside talking to friends!  2 minutes of our food dying on the pass, we got up and left.  We'd already waited nearly an hour and I'm not going to wait for our server to take her sweet time chatting it up with her friends.  Sorry 360 Burger.  We really wanted you to survive, but you can't treat customers like this and expect them to come back.

name: The Basement East
text: Nashville's best place for live music!  Every genre and every kind of vibe you are in search of.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: This show was amazing! The food was delish! I really enjoyed this boat show. Dinner is served around 7, our table was pre assigned when we picked up our tickets so no need to get there super early. Cash bar.  Show does to about 9:45

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Kind of tricky to get to since it's a narrow door between two other entrances. The bar is upstairs on the second floor. There was a nice patio are and the performers were okay. We requested Europe's Final Countdown, the pianist didn't kill it but it was okay.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great food, amazing drinks, and such a fun atmosphere!! Will definitely be back soon!!!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Wow!  Best date night started with a BANG for sure. Great place, I will be bringing any and all house guests here. Just hope that one, or really any penis type song does not get requested when I bring the parents. That happened to the people next to us...ha ha awkward for them funny to us.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: This piano lounge and bar is okay but they charge cover to come in here which is really devious. I think it is nice to come as a couple but in a group some people might not want to oay

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Woman can come in with basically nothing on, men have cutoff sleeve shirt and stopped at the door. Could not get in without buying a shirt. What BS

name: 360 Burger
text: I have been to many burger places in Nashville, but 360 is worth going again n again. Can you imagine Happy Hour everyday till 10 pm , you can't get that anywhere in Nashville. Its in Antioch so not too much crowded but pleasant environment with live music. They have best sweet potato fries in town comes with Garlic Aioli. Burgers come with your choice of meat, best is the Farm Boy which comes with Fried Egg and choice of bread,try Pretzel Bread . My friend likes spicy, he tried Insanity burger and  he said its best burger he had till now in Nashville. I bet you will go again n again.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
My first night in Nashville, I knew this was a must see. I'm so happy we went. Great entertainment and a nice atmosphere. I was blown away by the talent, and had so much fun. It wasn't crowded at all (it was a Tuesday though)  which I prefer. It was intimate, personalized entertainment for the 12 people there. I even got up and did a Charlie Brown dance because they played it on demand. Going back tonight!! 

The location is situated between two other places. We walked into the wrong bar and asked the bartender there, where the pianos were. He flipped me off and said, 'upstairs'. I'm guessing they get that a lot... their bar had carpet and stunk like piss and booze.

name: 360 Burger
text: Great food! I've enjoyed everything I've tried, burgers, oysters and you have to try the bread pudding. Friendly staff and service - 360 Burger is a great addition to the neighborhood! Best food around

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Five stars for the music and zero stars for the service. 

We went on Sat evening for the 6pm show.  The music was outstanding but, after our first drink, the servers largely ignored us. I nearly had to tackle the server to order a second drink - which arrived as the show was ending. 

We liked the music so much we decided to brave the servers again for Sun brunch and music. As on Sat, the music was very good but on Sun the service was even worse. We ordered "bottomless mimosas" which was basically 1 mimosa unless you could catch the server for a refill. We ordered brunch prior to the start of the show but almost 2 hours later had still not received our food. When we complained they said they would comp our brunch and then brought our brunch out in to-go containers???

In summary, great music but absolutely no service.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
We were in Nashville for a week and went to the museum twice. It's amazing! Beautiful and interesting exhibits and enough interactive components to entertain the kids. It's not very big but there is enough to see and spend about two hours (without the kids asking to leave).
The ragged old flag exhibit is really cool.
The people are really friendly and the location is great, you can stroll around downtown in front of the shops and bars after the museum.
If you're a Johnny Cash fan this museum is an emotional experience. If your  not a huge fan the design and organization is enough to appreciate.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: We had a fantastic time.  Got lucky and was seated front and center.  The music was great!  We had a wonderful overall experience.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Mark is by far the best bartender I have ever met! He has a great attitude and mixes great drinks! I would recommend this bar to anyone looking for great live music and amazing drinks! Order his lemon drop shot!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great food and drinks as well as a cute venue. Had a table of 8 and the bartender took forever to come help us even though there was only 3 other people in the restaurant. Went to our table to listen to music and the server took awhile to come take our food and drink orders when we finally got food it was wrong so I had to send it back and it still came back wrong but it was 915pm so I wasn't going to send it back again. Waitress was not attentive at all but was attentive to other tables and we were required to pay a 21% tip for her terrible service because we had an 8 top table. They also have complimentary valet which is nice.

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text: One of my favorite bars in midtown!! Love the whole gang!  Been going here for years and seen them go through a lot of changes. I recommend the blue shot, so yummy! love you guys!!!

name: The Basement East
text:
Oh yeah!

This is going to be awesome, having this venue in the neighborhood.  This is too good to be true. AMPLE parking - so that will never be a problem.  Plenty to eat within walking distance.  *hint* go early, park, walk to dinner.  Perfect.

Venue: 
The Pros: large, cavernous building with a large bar on one end and a fair amount of tall tables to sit and view the band. 
Plenty of space to stand, lean, find a chair, wander. Attentive bartenders.
Good A/C system.  No problem cooling the interior.
Sound is excellent. Good acoustics.  Good sound system. 

Cons: 1 toilet for the women.
The lights behind the performers are bright, bright, bright lights that hit the audience that are sitting up close to the stage - with an almighty glare. There's no way to sit at the front tables and take photos of the performers.  
Hell, you can't even sit and watch the band because the lights are hitting you directly in the eyes.  Those need to be turned off.  There's no reason for them.

Other than that.. We enjoyed it, loved the space, loved the ambience, loved the energy. 

Welcome to the neighborhood!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Every country musician and country rock artist seems to have a bar in downtown Nashville.  Kid Rock's place is ion a great busy corner location on Broadway with multi-level seating and live music.  It's a really big place, and we saw 2 entertaining bands there on our multiple visits.  Loud, fun, informal, and a little tacky....which is what you'd expect from Kid Rock.  There is a large drink menu with something for everyone....domestic beers, craft beers, shots, cocktails, & signature drinks.  Drinks are priced comparably to other bars in the area & its a fun experience for a large group!

name: 360 Burger
text:
Yes 5 stars for a great place, a must go to Restaurant !!!
Had the blackened salmon with avocado and steamed broccoli very good but that was only a very small part of a great experience.
That two bands That I had the privileged listening to made the experience even better very friendly staff nice clean place and music.
Had a great time !

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
I was so excited to hear from our waiter, Travis @ Erch, about the Monday artist showcase here at 6pm. It is the Song Suffragettes- which is women of country who sing and write their own music. It was great. The happy hour 2 for 1 beers were also good! We sat on the front row and the event cost me $5 (for the beer). The food people were ordering looked good but we were just there for the music. This was a great way to hear live music that wasn't just the typical Nashville radio country. 

We came here knowing we could get a. Seat and we were also already parked downtown for the day. We had planned to go to the Bluebird but were told the wait was ridiculous and it was be so very crowded.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I was so excited to visit this bar on my trip to Nashville, as I am a fan of Dierks Bentley and country music. However, I was permitted into the bar and my boyfriend was not. My boyfriend was dressed very presentable, however due to his elastic band khaki shorts we weren't let in. We are from out of town so its not like we have so many chances to come back. Hoping I can try again tomorrow, get permitted, and leave a better review!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
Corny! After spending almost $200 for the two of us, I was expecting more. 

We come to Nashville every December and this was one of the last things that we hadn't experienced. I figured, what the heck, let's do it. Christmas time in Nashville is starting to catch on because it gets more and more crowded and more and more expensive each year. Traffic was horrific, so I was too worried to pre book the tickets. But low and behold, there were several seats available when we got there, right at 6:15 (boarding time).

Parking was easier than I expected. Tons of free parking was available in the Opry Mills Mall lot, which runs parallel to the Cumberland River.  

It was dark and chilly when we were standing to board, but they had an area that was blocked off with an awning like set up, so the waiting to board wasn't too bad. The waiting was the biggest annoyance. 

Once we finally got on board, the buffet was waiting, nice and hot. The food is the only reason I'd give it two stars. The buffet consisted of a ton of vegetables, roasted potatoes, mashed potatoes, stuffing, turkey, and roast beef. They pulled the food and stopped carving the turkey and beef at 7:45.  So you could grub until you were miserably stuffed. And then there was dessert around 8:30... that consisted of peppermint cheesecake and a sugar cookie. 

The wait staff were all hard to understand. I have been on countless cruises and I know some of the waitstaff there, are foreign, but this was bad. On cruises the waitstaff mingle with people close to 24/7, these guys on the showboat only few times a week. 

The Christmas show itself consisted of very few people. The dancers were 3 men and 3 women. I've been to many shows, and this was by far the worst. Who organized this?! Someone who mustn't have ever been to a show before. Literally, the shows on cruise ships are far better.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text:
I was surprised at how much fun we managed to have here. If you're into taking fun photos, this place is awesome. We spent about an hour and a half here. 

The wax figures look insanely real, and although I knew that you could touch them (from seeing other people's pictures), I thought that there would be some kind of restriction (how do they keep them looking so good with people always touching them?). 

This place is located inside a really nice mall, which is kind of random and it was empty on the day that we went (I believe it was a Saturday?). Despite it's country music focus, there was a nice variety of musical stars from all genres. Everything from Billie Holiday to Ozzy Osbourne.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Not one of our favorite places we visited here on Broadway. The computers for employees were on the bar and we constantly had to move so we weren't in their way. The place was pretty busy and we did get service rather promptly, but it's sort of small & we couldn't really enjoy.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
The food was ok, the show was a little cheesy, but after the show up on the top deck, Bob who played the fiddle and sang was very entertaining, I could have listened to him the whole 2 and 1/2 hours, the other thing to beware of, when we ordered the tickets on line, and picked up at Opryland, we paid 100.00 a person and the ticket said general admission, we thought that meant you just sat in what was available, not an assigned table, when we arrived, we were then told, general admission meant no lunch, ok, a lunch cruise you thought lunch was included in the 100.00, at this point not having eaten breakfast since we thought we were having lunch, thought 2 and 1/2 hours without food was going to be rough, so we asked is it possible to get food, told they would check if seating available yes, there was seating available but we had to see bartender and pay an additional 21.00 per person, so a treat for Father's day turned into a nearly 400.00 excursion because no drinks were included either. So, my final review, thought a bit pricey for what you got. And the view of downtown Nashville was nice, but that was about 10 minutes of the trip, the rest was an industrial plant and trees.  I would not go back again, and I visit Nashville about 4 times a year as my daughter lives in nearby Murfreesboro.
DorothyP 
Pittsburgh, PA

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
This place 
I'm a huge Johnny Cash fan and this was everything I could have asked for in a memorial. His piano, clothes worn by him and June, even the chair he sat in for the "Hurt" video. Just epic. And emotional too. It's pricey, as are most attractions like this, but definitely worth it for a fan.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
I am Kid Roooock...well I'm not, but we did stop in to his Big Honky Tonk Bar and Grille while visiting Nashville. I got the burger and fries and absolutely loved it! It was cooked and seasoned to perfection. The place was really hopping on a Friday Night with live music. 

The staff was very friendly and got the order out in a relatively short amount of time. They were quick on the refill of drinks, which is very, very important! The drink menu was plentiful and varied. The decor fit in with the bar vibe and live music. 

Would definitely go here on my next trip to Nashville. Which hopefully be soon, I loved Nashville. See you at Kid Rock's Honey Tonk!

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: Absolute garbage!!!! Went there for late night bar food cause it was one of the only places that served last 2330. Service was horrible as in the bartender was an absolute dick, no thanks have a good night, nothing!!! Took 20 minutes (the female bartender said it would take that long) for 12 wings that cost $14. If you're drunk and looking for food, do yourself a favor and order a pizza.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: So on a spontaneous trip up to Nashville we found ourselves staring at a strip of bars playing various genres of live music. The day was super hot and country is not my thing so we decided on Kid Rock's multilevel restaurant. The first two floors seem to be the main band and they sounded real good but being hot and cranky at this point we went up the stairs one more to level 3. There really was not much going on. A band was setting up. A large bar in the middle.  We waited a pretty long time for a waitress and ordered iced tea which came to us with maybe two ice cubes per glass. He ordered wings which were just ok and I got a salad for $9 which was basically Publix salad mix dumped in a bowl. Pretty disappointed.  However I had my sights set on a bourbon banana cake off their dessert menu.  Through every bite of this Publix salad I was awaiting soft banana cake with butterscotch icing and toffee pieces. How could that ever be wrong??? Well I'll tell you. It was probably in the fridge for over a week and the icing chipped off in pieces away from the half vanilla half possibly banana cake. Oh and Heath bar crumbled over the side. I wanted to cry. Beyond that, the food was pricey for what it was. Service sucked. It was so loud that all you could hear up there was a horrible mix of bands from all the neighboring bars competing and then begging each individual with the tip jar. Oh and be careful leaving. You may trip over passed out college girls in pools of vomit.

name: Silver Dollar Saloon
text: We came here on our last night in Nashville, its a pretty old crowd compared to the rest of Nashvegas but they have a live band and cheap beer, what more can you ask for?

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: I loved this place! We stopped in on Friday night and made a point to come back again on Saturday night! The bands were awesome and we were able to get drinks pretty quickly, except on the 3rd bar, they seemed a lot slower up there. Definitely check it out!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
Big, beautiful place of good times and great music on Broadway.  Several floors of fun each filled with great music and fun.

The rooftop was my favorite.  You can scan the entire downtown area and are across the street from the famous Johnny Cash Museum.

Food menu is limited but it is all pretty good.  Being from Detroit - I will however call out "Bobbie" and ask "WHERE IS THE MAC n CHEESE"??

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I am a huge Johnny Cash fan and I have wanted to visit this museum since the announcement was made in May '12 that it would be opening. My girlfriend Julie was an excellent sport and made the pilgrimage with me on a really crappy weather day. The museum has some great artifacts and is a must stop for anyone who calls themselves a fan of the Man In Black.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text:
Worth the visit. We laughed the entire way through. My youngest danced with Beyoncé on stage, my mom finally got to kiss Blake Shelton, and I got to dance with Timberlake. 

We got a good discounted rate on groupon

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
Pretty cool bar, i know they just opened and they are still working out the kinks. We came on their soft opening night, so I wont be too harsh on the review. The drinks were decent, the bands featured that night were pretty cool. I was impressed, one of the girls from American idol was featured.  The band took a while to set up, but that was because the band was waiting for her to show. 

I like the overall feel of the place its wide open and has an mezzanine area where people can sit and on a nice night they had all the windows open for cross breeze. There is a bar upstairs, downstairs in the middle and off to one side, and another mini bar as you come in, so plenty of places to sit and/or get a drink at the bar. We didn't go to the roof top, but it looked pretty cool from the street, I believe there is another band up there. 

They still had a few things to work on, but I am sure they'll get It together soon, like they only had 2 TVs and no mirrors in the bathrooms.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I've been here twice on trips to Nashville. Both times did not disappoint. Dierks Bentley chooses very talented bands to perform at his honky-tonk. Both times the service was great. One recommendation is to get a table early on a Saturday night and then stay for the duration. You won't have to worry about being jampacked and will have a spot to sit and place your drinks. Our most recent trip brought us there on a Sunday night. Matt from security was absolutely fabulous and figured out how to get my husband's favorite NBA team game on one of the TVs in the upstairs bar. This meant that I could get my live music fix and he could still watch the game. We were so grateful that Matt went above and beyond to do this for us! The atmosphere is fun and the food was good too. Definitely make whiskey row a stop on your list of honky-tonks on Broadway.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text:
My first wax museum experience and wow they are realistic! It was just like I was hanging out with all my favorite country music artists. 
Lots of photo opportunities and you can move at your own pace.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I'm heading home to watch the movie ASAP. Well put together. Makes me want to pack rat all my stuff and open a museum.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
So my family LOVED this show. The talent was fantastic. We were in the front row and my kids were just loving it. The only reason I removed a star was the food. The fooD was not my favorite but honestly, I didn't care that much. The experience was more important to me and we all loved it. 

After the show was over the cast came out on the floor and greeted everyone. They took pictures with the kids and were very friendly. 

We got a nice family photo that they took when we arrived. You do have to pay for that but it was nice and worth it! Nice memorabilia from out trip to Nashville! 

Give it a try and have a great time. See you next time!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Food is good but the menu is pretty standard pub/bar food - sandwiches, salads and burgers. I had a ham and cheese melt. It wasn't anything memorable but it was definitely tasty! The artichoke dip was really good and the drinks were yummy. 

The real reason to come here is the entertainment and atmosphere. The live music here is great! We felt very welcomed by the staff and really enjoyed our time here. We were here on a Saturday night and did not have trouble finding a table. We would definitely come back for drinks and music.

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text:
This was once my go-to place on the weekends, but it got to be so crowded that I phased it out.  However, I was reminded that this can be a great place to go during off-times (weeknights especially) as though it is still busy, its more relaxed than coming on the weekends.

Despite always having a packed bar I get my drinks refilled in a pretty timely fashion.  The food is great bar food, a bit heavy but thats to be expected (drinking and pub food go hand in hand really).  I love their mahi mahi sandwich and they have the best fried pickles in town.

I know a lot of people come here to watch games on TV but I wouldn't recommend it for that.  Again, this place gets crowded and loud fast and despite the projection screen at the front of the bar its hard to see.  Also the outdoor patio sometimes has live music or a DJ so it can clash with anything you're trying to watch.  Unless its lunchtime I wouldn't say to come here to watch anything on TV.

I would recommend starting your night here but not finishing it unless you want to fight for drinks and standing room.  Come on a Sunday night if you want a chance at a table or seat at the bar.  This place can be a ton of fun or horrible, depending on when you choose to come in.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Great beer, food, and excellent staff!! Got a Groupon for beer tasting and an appetizer for 2. I loved the experience, they have good beer selection and the Nachos we ordered were good. I personally liked the way the place was decorated, it just felt artsy and cozy. The place had a couple of TVs in case you want to watch it instead of talking to each other lol. It also had outdoor seating with a smoking and a non smoking area. I went during the day and parking was ok but I don't know how it can get at night. Overall I really enjoyed my time there, like I said, staff was great and beer was even better!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: My first and last time here was last night on New Year's Eve. A group of people kept talking behind us even though we nicely asked them to stop. Then we informed security and they did not address them. When I took a picture of the offenders someone on the row below them tried to slap my phone out of my hand. 12/31/16 The John Prine, Jason Isbell, & Kacey Musgraves show. These people talked constantly from 7:30pm until we got up around midnight and sat in seats on the third row that people already left. It's clear the trashy concert goers were just there to party and not watch performances. My husband and I also spent a lot of money in there getting drinks and snacks. I'm pursuing this until someone from the Opry apologizes to me. That's around. $500 down the drain!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We were in town for a convention and needed a break. Had the best time and the band, sorry can't recall their name, were more fun than we expected. Had me doing a cameo or Mustang Sally!  If we make it back to the Nashville this will be on our must do list! Service was great, food average.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
There's not much more to say than what everyone else has already said, but if you haven't been here yet, what are you waiting for? 

I used to regular this place in Texas- even have my own plate on the wall. Here in Nashville, I'm not so much a regular, and only due to the fact you have to pay to park or catch a cab here. I love the brew selection and the fare. It's a fun place to be. It's kinda like a candy store for the grown ups. 

The place is pretty big and super comfy year round.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We paid our cover charge, sat at the bar and gave the white band a chance. They were decent, but not blues singers. We paid our ride bartender his 9 bucks for a cocktail a d coke and left 21.00 poorer

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
I'd give them a five star if the Friday and Saturday night scene there wasn't so bad.

Don't get me wrong, I'm a member of their club, and am about 70-80 beers in to the 200 required to get a "plate" on their wall.  I love their pretzels, and especially love many of the beers there.  If you go when they aren't packed, you can generally expect a calm, comfy atmosphere.

The waitresses are a mixed bunch.  Some, frankly, aren't great.  Some, however, are awesome and very knowledgeable.

The only problem I have is, going on a Friday or Saturday night will mean fighting for a seat.  Now, prior to becoming a member, this also seemed to mean slow, generally bad service.  Since my friends and I are all members, though, and generally tip well, I feel that that has changed.  To a first time visitor, a Friday or Saturday night will usually entail searching for a spot to sit, waiting a long time to get served, and they'll likely be out of their more common sales that night.

Go on a weeknight.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Great atmosphere and wonderful hot dogs! Very fun - cornhole on the front patio, places to sit, good wait staff. Very laid back and a fun place to come for a beer. They also have $2 domestics every day from 11-7!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
