Like Name, Like Beers, Like, probably have given more stars than the available 5. we always have good time here and the beer collection from all over the world will hell lot of taps to taste.

Pros:
Many Many beer options for everyone

Cons:
Not really any issues, but the place gets crowded during weekends.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
ate lunch here with the family. Beer chilli, chicken wings with sauce on the side and white cheddar mac&cheese. Chilli was thick, meaty and spiced just right, the pasta mellow but tasty - good for kids. The wings could have used more cooking but weren't undercooked, just not impressive. The celery and carrots that came with were largely frost-bitten from cold storage, but we got better ones upon request. 
We enjoyed the atmosphere and live music though I wish there weren't TV screens at every corner showing sports and news. there was no cover charge.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Extremely bad lunch service. If I could give zero stars, I would.  The place was practically empty around noon but it took forever to get our food and the waitress didn't offer an explanation, in fact she never checked back with us after our food finally arrived. We also had to flag her down to get our ticket to pay. Lousy, lousy service and the food was not that good.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Food was ok. My husband's ribs were too dry. I got the brisket sandwich and it was tasty. The tater tots were yummy too. The wait staff was terrible and not very thoughtful from the moment we stepped in. There was live music off and on during dinner which was not bad and the noise was at a good level where  we could still talk and hear each other without difficulty.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
To enjoy this you must be a country music fan to appreciate it. Paid for the backstage tour and then went to the Friday night show. 

I am a fan so appreciated it, but it is expensive. The show was good because it covered the gamut  of country music (old and new) and had one of my favorite artists. Excellent tour guide who knew what she was talking about and was able to answer all the questions posed. 

Only got 4 stars due to price. Not recommend for families with children due to the price.

name: Music City Tippler
text: Went for Father's day and they did not disappoint. My meal was actually free as I am a dad. Slow but good service, nice brunch choices. Food was slow to arrive but everything was good.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: We had a great time here during the day with our tween girls on a visit to Nashville. The host and crown were so fun. Karaoke first for our group but these girls wanted to sing all day.

name: Third Man Records
text: I've been a fan of Jack White for 2 or 3 years now and I have most definitely heard of the legendary Third Man Records. It doesn't seem like much from the outside but on the inside it is unlike anything else I've even seen, or experienced. The store is just breathtaking with how well it merges the new and the old.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I've been to BB Kings several times since moving to Nashville. I guess it's one of those things you want to do if you are visiting Nashville. However, I'll be ok if I don't go again. It's a been there done that kind of thing. We met some friends from out of town there last night and the restaurant could only serve beer since they lost their liquor license. I don't know how an establish such as BB Kings could let something like that happen. The food is pretty decent however.

name: Third Man Records
text:
If you are in Nashville and a fan of music and Jack White, this is a must stop! So many fun things to check out and play with and explore. And loads of great records to pick from, with the majority being recorded live at Third Man Records. There is a super cute old school photo booth, dancing hamster machine, fun sound machines, a vinyl listening booth AND a booth where you can record yourself and have it pressed to vinyl. 

TLDR: GO! This place is the bees knees.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: I have to say that I believe this is up there with the best burgers in Nashville. The bar itself is pretty nice, a decent selection of brews on tap and a nice happy hour, but their stuffed burgers are what will bring you back. The Sunday Brunch includes this whipped cream cheese center that is unbelievable, and they have the classic juicy lucy on the menu for the traditionalists out there. Their spicy fries are knock you over spicy and delicious. I never came before it changed over from Taps and Tapas to Taps Stuffed Burgers, so I can't speak to any differences, but I would say it is well worth a trip!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Took a group for an early dinner great beer selection and your typical pub grub, but everyone was satisfied.   Service was good and everyone was well nourished.   Been to the one in Columbia SC and in Raleigh NC, decent regional chain.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: I went to miss Kelli's expecting to have a great time. I bought a drink from the bar on the right hand side and got mediocre service. I then went to meet up with friends at the bar on the left hand side. As I sat down on a bar stool a male bald headed bartender with a cigarette hanging out of his mouth asked me if I needed a drink. I politely said no I had just gotten one from the other bar. He said "well honey if you're not buying you need to get up." I kindly replied I had already bought one so that's a little crazy and got up. He then proceeded to tell me "well you can go f*** yourself." My male friends heard him say this and made eye contact with him. He then told the bouncers our group made him nervous. Before we could finish our drinks a group of 10 of us were escorted out. Mind you, while this is happening a highly intoxicated female next to us has spilled 3 drinks and has spilled one on another customer, but was not asked to leave. I told the bouncers what happened and they agreed that said bartender has issues and should not be working there. Do not go there unless you like to be disrespected.

name: Third Man Records
text: It's a pretty cool place and worth a stop in if you love Jack White and all the The Third Man does for the world of music.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The hostess with the nose ring is extremely rude. So rude, in fact, we left. We wanted to sit somewhere else since the music was way too loud, and she was not accommodating. She wouldn't explain why we couldn't sit elsewhere when there was empty tables all around.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Skip the $90.00 VIP tour.  Major rip off.  Not much more than the $19.00 daytime tour.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great food and service at a good price. Pulled pork,    baked beans, potato chips and po'boy was delicious. Floors and bathrooms could use an update.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Awesome place to listen to live blues music. Got some amazing brisket and a bottle of wine while my girlfriend had the grilled chicken. The food was an awesome. The band was very entertaining and took song request, except they didn't play any Eric Clapton. But overall I would for sure recommend to any friends in the area! Made for a great dinner to start out evening together!!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: LOVED this place! We went on a Saturday afternoon. Great use of outdoor/indoor seating. The staff were all really pleasant, knowledgeable, and helpful. We only got beers and the soft pretzel app, but really enjoyed everything we got and would definitely recommend it to anyone looking to grab a drink and an app. I'd definitely go back to try more.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: The owner was very rude and disrespectful to my friend. She called her an It and a He/She. Please don't go to this homophobic bar!!

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
After wondering around downtown Nashville for a bit and checking out some of the sights we decided that we should probably eat. We checked out Yelp as well as Google Maps and was able to find B.A.D. We really didn't want to spend a ton of money on dinner - but we didn't want something like McDonalds so we felt this was a good compromise as the prices were reasonable.

We wondered around for a bit before we actually found this location - as they literally are down an alleyway. We walked in and found a seat. They were not busy - but they were not slow either. It was a good mix. Our server came over right away and took our drink order. They did seem to be more of a bar than a restaurant but that is besides the point. They listed out all their specials and unfortunately on Friday nights the only special is $4 fireball shots.

We ordered chips as the appetizer. They make them in house and are amazing. They are cooked and salted to perfection! We ended up doing burgers - I went with the Mega Titan Burger and my other half went with the fork and knife burger.

Our wait time for our food was not long at all. But it wasn't so soon that we couldn't enjoy the chips. The burgers are seasoned to perfection - to the point I wanted to storm the kitchen and steal it all so I could re-create the same burgers at home. The burgers were cooked to perfection as well. They were juicy and just full of flavor. The knife and fork burger comes with chili on top (hence the name) and I hear it was amazing as well.

Our server was great. She was friendly, offered suggestions, and kept our drinks full. She was very attentive to our needs.

If you're looking for a burger in the downtown area - check them out. They're worth the hunt!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I don't foresee ever coming to Nashville without a trip to the Opry. In full disclosure, I'm not a huge country music fan, but I like it well enough due to a stint in rural Texas with limited radio access. We also went into the night not knowing anything about anyone performing. Now that I've been to the Opry, I'm a believer.

I loved how the show was broken into quarters and the way that each quarter contained classic country, bluegrass and a more contemporary act. The Opry was a true variety show and I ended up downloading a few songs as we watched and discovered new artists.

The set and the history and the seating were also pluses. Even though we sat in the first balcony (and I'd splurge for better seats now that I know how great the show is), the acoustics are great and you can see the performers on the big screen.

Yes, the Opry is a little commercial (both the actual commercials and proximity to the mall), but the show is so lovely it's easy to look past that. Next time, I'll buy the tickets that have a backstage tour afterward.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great food with healthy options available. Fantastic waitstaff and great for listening to music rather than the crowd itself. Gets busy

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: The beer selection here is fantastic!  My server recommended Finch's cucumber beer and it was so interesting.  I love when servers give suggestions, I almost always take them up on it and am always pleased.  Love the decor and atmosphere in here, if I was local I would definitely want to be part of their beer club sounds like so much fun.  The pork belly sandwich was a bit dissapointing, however the bread on the sandwiches is amazing!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: Loves the roof . Had a great time with the servers. I went in because they were military friendly

name: Back Alley Diner
text: The turkey sausage soup was definitely worth ordering. The locals seem to be enjoying themselves.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: It's my first time here so I had to go.  We had a group of about 20, and had a very nice guide.  I'm not a big country fan so I really didn't know any of the names.  Even for me though, it was interesting to learn about the legacy of the place.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Awesome place but was a little hard to find (I'm also directionally challenged). We found it and we're happy with the service and food. Definitely recommend you stop here for lunch.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
I'd give it five stars if marks were supposed to be for being as advertised, but I hold five star reviews for uppity fancy places that blow my mind. 

Any place with half price green flash west coast ipa during happy hour is gonna have high marks in my book. Juicy Lucy was good and filling, even though it appeared pretty small.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: We did some honky tonking up and down Broadway during CMA Fest 2018 & this was our favorite stop. It's a more intimate place and the performer, Noah Garner, was very engaging. Loved it.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: The sirens wail on a cold Nashville night. A sign beckons you down an alley way telling you that BAD, Back Alley Diner, is good. What you learn upon walking down the alley is that BAD is actually bad. The bar smells like Dolly Parton's dentures soaked in urine. The money you save on $2 PBRs will be lost tenfold on dry cleaning bills for your clothes, which might as well be tossed into the nearby dumpster. I appreciate a good dive bar, but even I can't endure the assault BAD waged on my nose and sense of worth.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Great family activity with a variety of acts each show.  A must do in Nashville.  Covers history of the Opry. Our show included old school acts, bluegrass, a comedian (awesome by the way... Henry Cho), and some great mainstream acts.  We could only get balcony seats way up in back but seats were great... They set up the seats so everyone can see, even kids.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I arrived in Nashville for the Beachbody Summit (fitness convention), and my friend got me tickets last minute as a present so I could see the famous Opry. It definitely did not disappoint! While I was near the stage, any seating arrangement here would do justice in offering the full allure of the history of why this is such a Landmark. There were some old-school country performers as well as some up-and-comers, followed by Vince Gill. Despite not being a big country fan, I had a great time!! There were places to grab a bite or a drink or a souvenir, it was clean and very comfortable. I definitely recommend checking this out if you're ever here for a visit.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Had such a great experience at flying saucer. Staff was knowledgeable and friendly. They were patient with me and helped me choose a beer selection I would be super happy with. We just came for drinks, however next time we pass through, I would definitely try the menu. Atmosphere was really laid back. They need more pubs like this in Nashville!

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text:
When I used to live in Nashville back around 2008, DM was a great spot to go out at night.  Fun bands, good crowds, great service, the works.

Now, not so much.  My wife and I have been a couple times over the past few months.  This place has really let itself go.  First, no live bands, at least that I've seen.  Instead, they have these DJs who are real mood-killers.  First, they've got their base turned up way to loud.  You can feel it in your chest half a block down the Music Row - on the other side of Demonbreun Circle!  It's almost unbearable trying to get close to the stage to dance.  Not that you'd want to anyway, since the floor used to be packed with all sorts of people, now it's like 1-2 bachlorette parties and a couple creepy dudes.  

Last night, the DJ couldn't seem to stop playing Lonely Island.  Yeah, mix in a chorus/verse for laughs and then move on, haha, good stuff.  But three full Lonely Island songs in a row?  My group literally stopped dancing because of it and left the floor.  Of course, when we went towards the back, we were met with a wall of cigar smoke.  So, not a high score on the ambiance chart either.  We ended up leaving shortly thereafter.

I will say, their pub food is pretty tasty, and their HH deals aren't bad (but don't get the house brews - even the bartenders will tell you that they're terrible).  So for a HH and/or dinner?  DM seems fine.  But if you're looking to dancing in the midtown area, it's either Tin Roof, South (assuming you can stand the heat), or somewhere on Division.  DM used to be so good, and now it's so bad.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Server forgot about us. Band was good during the day. Singer had good voice, sax, piano, drums.  Servers looked like the were unhappy.-zombies. Large place. Probably more exiting at night. Bar menu.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Walked in to some incredible voices singing.  Worth a drink to see what talent shows up!

name: Third Man Records
text: There is such a cool atmosphere here! Ive been wanting to visit ever since reading about it in The Rolling Stones. I even got to record my voice in a vintage vocal booth. For just 20 bucks, I was able to put my original song on a record! So cool!

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text: I love drinking with all the expats on Friday afternoon. But I'm writing to let you know that DM has the best potato salad I've ever had. Skip the fries, get the potato salad. You won't regret it.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
The food and atmosphere were good... but they need to label which of their foods are spicy. Everything has a little kick to it but the Mac and cheese was terribly spicy. They basically poured spicy nacho sauce on pasta. It was almost inedible. That's not southern Mac and cheese. Ick. 

However, my beef brisket was great. Smoky and tender. And the corn muffins tasted just like mama made. I also enjoyed the banana bread pudding and the peach cobbler. Tasted very fresh.

Still. I think there's better places to go in Nashville. I probably won't be back.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: The Grand Ole Opry is a historic place to visit in Nashville.  We came here on a Tuesday before CMA fest.  Not gonna lie but that was a good choice to see a lot of great artists: Darius Rucker, Chris Janson, Charles Esten, Little Big Town, and Carrie Underwood!   They all put on a great show.  There was a pre party before the show with a outdoor concert and plenty of beverage and food options.  It was a blast too.  Inside don't think there was really any bad seats looked like pretty good views from the balcony too.  We sat on the floor about 20 rows back worth the price for the seats.  The concession prices are pretty reasonable compared to other concert venues I've attended. The crowds here are pretty tame and don't get very loud, made a couple people mad because I stood up to cheer on the artists after they did a great job.  The Grand Ole Opry is a great place to see new, old, and great country stars.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: If you have a visitor from out of town, bring them here. Get two drinks and the pretzel and cheese. On your way out, swing by the Union Station Hotel to checkout the turn of the century architecture.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: This place was fun, good drinks.  A bit dissappointed the happy hour only applied to domestic drafts, but the double bloody marys were a hit!  The bad that plays around 1:00pm on Sundays was entertaining, the woman singer had a very pretty voice.  Overall a good time!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great food. Nice music. Great service. Tre was excellent and treated my girls and I with amazing service. Definitely the best place in Tennessee

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
This was the best music  experience  I had in Nashville by far and definitely over the last few months.

You see I'm not a modern country music fan but alas I thought when in Rome do what the Nashvillians would do. So we got tickets to the Grand Ole Opry at the Ryman Auditorium. The only ones left were limited view so I went for the balcony. Turns out our view wasn't very limited maybe just the far corner of the stage and there isn't a bad seat in the house acoustically.

The performers were all top notch and some were surprises even different from the program we were handed as we walked in. Seeing 4 stars from the show Nashville out singing on stage was an added bonus. Later one guy even brought a yoyo out. If you can get a ticket just go!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Located in an old building, this Flying Saucer has a great ambiance. Sit in the veranda if you prefer a quieter table. 
The beer selection is extensive to say the least. My grandfather didn't know what to pick, so I told our waitress what he usually drinks, and asked that she pick something out for him- he was quite pleased with her selection. I've been trying the gluten free thing (have pity on me) so I was happy to see that they have gluten free beers and ciders to chose from. If you don't know what to order, ask your waitress, they're usually pretty knowledgeable and have no problem bringing out samples.
Overall: great place to hang out!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Loved the experience. We were told when purchasing that it was an obstructed view but we could still see just fine!  Awesome entertainers. Can't wait to come back. Hopefully trace Adkins will be around next time. However josh turner and the rest of show were fabulous. Just loved MR Osbourne and the rocky top Xpress,  riders in the sky, Mandy, and  Home Free wow. And please Little Big Town our fav!!!!!  Only thing that could possibly make better would be to have all the old gang alive and on stage. Roy Acuff, porter wagner. Patsy Cline. Loretta Lynn.  Lil jimmy dickens. Grandpa. Minnie pearl. Hank Williams. You could feel the spirits off all the great!!!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Very rude wait staff and mediocre food. Wouldn't waste my money again. Band was good though.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Had a lot of fun here at a Friday night show. The first row of the mezzanine had great visibility  of the singers and the TV screens. A bit frustrating that the acts don't all get posted in advance on the website- if you have date flexibility, that makes planning difficult. 
I have to say the drinks inside the theater were pricey- 4 drinks were $37.00, without tip! But it's nice they let you bring them into the theater.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: We had such a good time here. Maddie (sorry if I spelled it wrong!) from NY was friggin awesome. I'm actually glad we went early and it was slow enough for her to stay and shoot the shit with us. Everyone loved what they ordered. Jalapeño burger, Bleu cheese burger, Boston dog, plain dog, turkey and beef tenderloin sliders, mac and cheese, beans, fries, tots, slaw.... all good. Drinks were cold, food was deeLish, and the service was great. Oh, and I forgot to mention that two of our group of six are 8 and 10 years old :)

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Cheap drinks but serves its purpose for karaoke for the brave and drunk.. Wait was a little long to sing, but the crowd is supportive regurgless if you're good or bad and song choice.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Having grown up watching Hee Haw and loving Country Music, a visit to the Grand Ole Opry was a must during my time in Nashville. We got tickets the day before which was actually lucky as it seemed it was close to being full for the day we wanted to go. We got there early and walked around some and took pictures. The tour started pretty much right on time. It was a large group but overall a decent size to still be able to hear and see things. Out tour guide provided lots of information and explained everything as we went through the tour. You get to go backstage and see the dressing rooms, the post office, and the Artist's entrance. The only downsides were that we were not allowed to go on the stage as there were workers there prepping for a show that night, and because they were getting the lighting set up too, the giant lights were down blocking anyone from getting a good clean picture of the stage. So that was pretty disappointing. But overall I am glad I went at least once.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
If you love beer, you'll love the Flying Saucer.  If you don't, well you are barking up the wrong tree.  They have a sign that says they have liquor and wine, but it is pretty frowned upon. 

The food is quite good for bar food.  I like the nachos as well as the buffalo chicken wrap.

I would definitely suggest coming here every now and then for a beer and a bite.  I only deducted one star because sometimes the bartenders aren't necessarily very knowledgeable about some of the beers they have, which could be due to the sheer number of them.  Nonetheless, I have found that surprising a few times.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I go to a here, I love it here!!! 

But for $20.00 tour to watch Tv on a tour at the Opry House is so Cheesy! I could do this on my couch! So so disappointed ! 

Most of the dressing rooms were closed they don't know why? We barely saw anything! 
Worthless! 
Refund please.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I under estimated this place! I knew the music would be awesome but didn't expect the food to be just as good!!!! The ribs were to die for!!!  And the Mac and cheese is a must! I recommend BB Kings for the entire experience!!! Live music is amazing!

name: Third Man Records
text:
Either you get it or you don't. 

If you are checking Yelp to decide if it's worth a visit to TMR, you probably don't get it (yet).  If you are leaving a negative review because there isn't rack after rack of mediocre used vinyl, you definitely don't get it and I actually kinda feel sorry for you.

There literally would no "Jack White" and no TMR or retail store or anything as we now know it without the involvement of some amazing and wonderful women over the years, and the staff here is no exception.  Don't let some of the reviews talking about hipsters or whatever fool you - these girls are just cool, the kind you can't fake.  

The prices are pretty reasonable, and I'm sure as hell not some rich guy saying that.  And if it helps, do a little research about Jack's personal philanthropy and TMR's continuing charity and community involvement and you'll wish you spent a little more.  Again, the real deal and not something they really publicize.

Don't forget to have a nickel or two in your pocket for the gumball machine!

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: This is the best place on Broadway. It's very energetic and everyone there is super welcoming and friendly. You can request to karaoke a song, or if you're more of a shy folk you can sing along to other artists singing. It's always a great time and good to be at every day of the week.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
What you see is what you really get. Lively, loud, tremendous beer selection, good selection of food options; sharing "starters" is a great idea. Dinner portions are modest....nice to be able to balance liquid intake with solid food consumption--easy to do here. 

Always a bit of a quandary....four or five stars? Contrasted to full-blown restaurants this would be 4 stars, but I'm comparing it with beer emporiums that serve great food, and in this case five stars are well-deserved.

Very congenial wait staff helped us settle in with nearly 2 dozen relatives visiting from all over the US. Politely and continually paid attention to both our food and drink needs.

Absolutely perfect soft pretzels with delightful dipping sauces. Savory traditional Shepherd's Pie. Dynamite house-made Rocket Tots, served, interestingly enough, with a friend egg. Brats are ok. All-in-all, good solid food.

No negatives other than we were told (beforehand when we called) we would not need a reservation, only to arrive and see there was an issue with such a large group of friends....and another large group had, in fact, made a reservation for the same time period. All turned out well since "Emily" and the other staff made us more than welcome. We'll be back.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Nice place for group karaoke. There's a pool table way back. The waitress was very nice. We ordered a couple of drinks and watched the groups that was there perform.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Good service. Ordered the catfish po' boy. Good, but not spectacular. Great, friendly bar service, which is welcome when traveling for work. I'd definitely recommend as a place to duck into for a quick bite and a friendly face.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Really good burger, extremely fast service.  From the outside doesn't look like much but once you enter, it is both larger and nicer  than expected! My husband said "we will be back! Came for lunch and did not have the opportunity to see any live music but it appears they do have it!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great service. Good mixed drinks, too! Food was okay but worth the try.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Belcourt Tapes is a movie, from the makers of Poughkeepsie Tapes. It sucks. This is not that.

Saw a band here once, and was taken drinking here once. From my 2 visits I have little good or bad to say about it. I love that they have live music every night. I think their sound system could be better but I'm not the one performing (and this crowd wouldn't like my sh*t anyway) so it's cool.

Prices are too high for me - let me clarify - in all of the bars in this neighbourhood, compared to what I'm used to (in Buffalo for example) but it's in the trendy part of town next to Vanderbilt so that is to be expected. Collegey crowd when I was there, and hipstery too, but you can get that just from the name. Speaking of which, the first time I came here (with a girl that was too cute for her own good) it was called "Belcourt Tapas" or something. Sounds like a Fox joke, but it's for real. I didn't try the Tapas, but she said she had and told me not to. So not exactly a ringing endorsement. But I think the place has changed hands since then, probably a few times, much like the girl in question.

I received a nice response to my review, and since it showed some excellent customer service, I will give them an additional star. Yelp reviewers are not allowed to accept discounts or free stuff, but the fact that this establishment is going out of its way to try and make people more satisfied is a good sign.

Anyway, I've been randomly ringing doorbells in my neighbourhood again, and I got arrested for it so now I have to go to Bellcourt. Bye.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: This was a fun night out. Good food, good music, good times. $7 cover charge to get in and the music makes it hard to talk but that's not why you'd go here. If you like blues music, looking for some good food and nice drink menu, this is a great place to go.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We came for dinner.  The tables were empty but they let us wait for 45 minutes so they can charge us for "cover". Finally got seated and took 20 minutes for the waitress to stop by because i went to complained for the wait.  I hope the food is worth it.  Terrible service.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: I do not like having to bribe DJ's to not wait an hour to go to the mike.  The bartenders could not keep track of tabs and they seemed very disoriented.  If you are looking for a true Karaoke bar, its not terrible.  But for anything else, there is far better options available.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Music is 5 stars; service is 5 stars; no need for further justification. Drinks are 3 stars....strong but pricey. Ok maybe because where this is equals 4 stars. Food is 1 or perhaps 0 stars. Hummus app brought out partially frozen! Really? The next hummus...acidic and old. Blech! Doesn't anyone check this? Math equals 5+5+4+0 divided by something equals about 3 ish stars. B.B. would be embarrassed I think.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: If your military please stop here, bogo drinks. I would have rated higher but some guy bartender on the top floor, no names here, just tattooed up. Sidenote:RUDE! My friend who couldn't read the *service elevator only* sign walked into the elevator as he was talking to some guys says, "ummm ok it obviously says service elevator only." I hear him being rude and I turn around and say sorry she didn't see that. He just was not polite. Sorry for the rant but I just came back overseas from my second tour and almost wanted to punch his inconsiderate face off. Be kind and don't hire jerks. Another sidenote: Danielle is an awesome bartender!!!

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: My best friend and I were first timers in Nashville, and stumbled upon the Dawghouse  while we were walking the streets. We walked in for a few drinks and ended up spending the rest of the day there because of the amazing staff. Shelby our bartender was amazing, great conversation and such a beautiful light to be around. Everyone was soo friend, the cheese curds and fried pickles were amazing. Cant wait to comeback!

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text:
If you are visiting downtown, put this bar on the list. Very fun karaoke bar. A lot of talent hits the stage, with a few funny drunks in between. Big bar with easy access to drink service all night. Highly recommend even for just an hour or two.

They served pizza by the slice hear as well and it was actually really good. Only downfall to my experience was a drunk guy grabbing woman trying to sing on stage. Security choked him out in front of everyone and then they took him in the back to god knows where.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Absolutely awesome!  Went out of there way to take care of everything I asked. Great food great staff oh yeah

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text:
Wow - there are dive bars with karaoke and then there are dive bars that try but end up just completely sucking. This is the latter.  On a Friday night the place is packed with more than enough volunteers for karaoke, but nope, the "DJ" (a young kid trying to look cool while he "spins" from an iPod...) wants to hear his own choices.  The music isn't bad-- actually some great choices-- but he'll only play the first 34 seconds of a song.  Then switch to something else. Seriously.  Someone needs to hand that guy a Ritalin-laced cocktail...

Yeah the bar is ok and they have Jell-O shots and all, but the reason you go into a basement karaoke bar is for the karaoke... Otherwise just rename it miss kelli's Jell-O shot bar.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Had a great time here on the 4th of July, as prelude to the downtown fireworks extravaganza.  We (me, my 3 young adult children, and son-in-law) got to the Club about 5:30 with plans to stay until about 8:30.  We were quickly seated and treated to great music, first a guitar soloist (Clint somebody) and then the BB King All-Stars.  The All-Stars were a special treat, featuring a dynamic soloist, Larry Springfield, who led the Club in a rousing rendition of the Star Spangled Banner, as well as a number of soul standards.

The music and atmosphere are the primary reasons I gave this 4 stars.  We had dinner there and the food was OK, but nothing memorable except that all of our orders came out from the kitchen either incorrectly or after much delay.  (Since we weren't in a hurry, the delay was no big deal.)  I had the BB King House Salad and Gumbo Ya-Ya, both of which were tasty, but the gumbo came out lukewarm.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This is another "must see" on a family trip to Nashville. We attended the daytime tour and we plan to go next summer for the VIP tour and show. It is an amazing experience. Truly a once in a lifetime!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Everyone needs to experience the Grand Ole Opry while visiting Nashville.  
GRAND OLE OPRY
Old Crow Medicine Show, Shenandoah, Matt Stell, Rachel Womack, Del McCoury Band, Waylon Payne and Jeanie Sealy.  We got good tickets row B seat 4 & 5.  Tonight the show was awesome!  You must do the Opry when in town!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Really cool history. Backstage tour was conducted really well by Kelly, super bright and fun! Got to see some legendary photos and dressing rooms. It sounds cliche, but you could feel the history and the lore when you're standing in the Family Room. 

Videos of Country Music Legends (including Shelton and Underwood) being asked to be a member of the Oprey while on stage and seeing them tear up really resonates with how much stock these guys out into this place/show. My favourite were the stories of Lil Jimmy Dickens, who I only knew the name of prior to visiting Nashville (I know, what a loser I am). 

I walked on stage and calmly said into the microphone, "Hello, I'm Johnny Cash." And as an adult-child I walked away with a smirk on my face because I knew he'd said the exact same thing on that exact same stage, countless times. 

Really liked the gift shop as well. It was very expensive but I walked away with a $34 red and white baseball shirt. Wasn't as tacky and lame as most gift shops, actually had some cool things. I almost walked away with a $9 labeled harmonica for gods sake. 

Only knock is I thought the building was bigger. Tour was very quick (45 mins) and I wish it was longer!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Lame. Put in my song & tipped the dj. Place was empty. Never called me up. We'll never come back.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: WannaB's isn't your "let's go laugh at terrible singers" kind of karaoke bar. This is Nashville. The bartender or any random waitress could probably out sing the majority of people you know. Yes, there will be the occasional crappy singer. Yes, there will be a drunken bachelorette or 3 who try to work through putting a ring on it. However, my experience is that most singers are entertaining and worth the stay. If it ends up not being your cup o' tea, walk to the back and step over to the bar next door.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: One of the best karaoke bars on broadway. Definitely a good time. If you want to sing be prepared to wait over an hour on a busy night. The bartender - especially with the purple hair- is super nice. Bathroom attendant was weird but the bathrooms were clean. Try the frozen lemonade!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This tour was just okay. The guide we had was very lackluster. The experience relies heavily on video clips as you move through the beginning part of the tour. After that, our guide would rattle off some information without any care that the group could all hear him. Some areas were small so we would have to take turns to get into place to take photos. Because of that, it would take a few minutes. The guide would move on before everyone was done, probably because they keep him on a strict time schedule. It was also quicker than I thought it would be and the building was small. I'm glad I went because it is a historical place but honestly, there was nothing about the experience that felt very grand.

name: Backstage Nashville
text:
From the beginning, Dan and Ron were outstanding in their communication with me. My brother in law is handicapped - in a wheelchair and I asked them about wheelchair accessibility. Fast response that they were. They asked to send a note to remind the day before. I did and they were ready for us. We entered through the back door - no stairs, no crowds and we were comfortably seated in the front with the wheelchair right next to the couch before the rest of the audience entered.

Now... how have I lived in Nashville 13 years and missed this until now?  We have waited online hoping to snag a spot at Bluebird, which I must say is next to impossible the last 4 or 5 years. But, don't bother. This is much more comfortable and food quality better as well.  

Talented artists took turns on the stage, with a Tennessee Fireball whiskey shot in between one of them.  The servers were courteous and attentive - just can't recommend this highly enough.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We went on the back stage day tour and it was awesome. $33 bucks scored us a walk through everything including dressing rooms. Randy was our tour guide and he was great!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We have been here several times for different venues and have always had great service, always clean, seats were comfortable with plenty of room to sit.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text:
This place has potential to be a great spot but it need some work. We came around noon on a Sunday to watch some football, eat and drink.  There was a lot of disappointment in my group because of several of the things we attempted to order, they were out of...both food and drink. 

Service was a tad on the slow side but the waitress we had was very sweet and busted her butt with our large group.  The food was ok and the drinks were good. It does get vey crowded during football games. I was told by the bartender that they normally charge a cover on Sunday's but didn't this week due to the new year. If that's true I would say it's not worth a cover as there is no live music or anything special besides tvs.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
A new thing in Nashville.

I only had a (that's 1) drink - an unfortunate result of my rushed midtown boulevardiering - and I didn't go down to the lower bar (whuh?), so maybe I'll update this review.  The Jalisco Luau was tasty, delicately crafted, and intriguing, with just enough spice.  Prices are à la Holland/308/Patterson.

This is the bottom of the Adelicia building - with all the attendant high-end noveau riche / tall men with expensive designer plaid / women with 3-hour hair.  If it wasn't for the friendly doorman/host and laid-back atmosphere, this place could be uber-pretentious.  But it isn't.  An inevitable, and desirable, use of this space has finally arrived.  I hope the plebs don't ruin it.

UPDATE:  Oh gawd, the plebs have ruined it!  Stay at Whiskey Kitchen, you plebs!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Great place to stop in if you want a break from country music - I wanted some more blues and R&B. Great staff -amazing band with amazing horn section ! Both female and male singer tore it up!  

Sooo much fun!!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
What more can I say about the Grand Ole Opry?

When in Nashville, it's definitely a must see. We enjoyed walking around and taking it all in. So many talented singers have walked through these doors. I'm glad to have visited and learned a lot about the history of music.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text:
The Dawg House Saloon was my first official meal when I moved to Nashville and it's your quintessential bar food. I ordered wings and my bf ordered a sandwich. The food came out very quickly and it was better than average bar food but the main reason we will come back is for the atmosphere. We brought our puppy with us and he got five star treatment. Any place that will treat your dog better than you is a great place! 

Their service was quick and attentive but we really appreciated how above and beyond our server/bartender treated our pup. People that love animals are the best people. He immediately had a bucket of water in front of him and the attention of every passer by. We'll be back plenty to grab a quick bite to eat and watch a football game with our pup in tow. The Demonbreun Hill group of restaurants are a great collection of eateries and drinking establishments and we would definitely recommend it for lunch AND nighttime fun. It's compact and you everything is literally connected to each other so if you're tired of one bar, you can walk next door to a different one.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Completely disappointing experience. We walked to Belcourt Taps for lunch one day, waited forever for service and even longer for food. I ordered the Juicy Lucy which according to the menu is stuffed with cheddar cheese and comes on a Pretzel Bun. When it came out I got a regular cheeseburger on a regular bun, nothing as it was described on the menu. There were 4 of us in the group and each meal did not come close to our expectations, which by the way were only held at normal bar food standards so we weren't expecting gourmet, but definitely something that would of been worth the hour wait from the time we placed the order until it arrived. Probably a good bar to hang out but dont waste your time for meal purposes.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
Absolutely loved the food.

I was impressed how big the place was.  It was my first time so I didn't realize it was so swanky and huge inside.

Our server was great and took good care of us. He also told us about the menu and tips on what to order when we come back.  He was very efficient on letting us know our drinks would be out soon and to assure us he was taking care of us. 

I was super impressed and the manager came out to greet us and tell us about the restaurant.  He was really genuine and made me feel like he appreciated us. 

Did I mention everything I had was awesome (chicken biscuit, mac n cheese bites, bruschetta)?

I'll definitely be back!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Good Band Jamie Highdon. Perfect sound. Fried pickles are great. Awesome! Kids welcome. Good drinks.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Dawghouse is always a great place to kick back and have a drink. The bartenders are always nice. Best Sunday Funday in town. They have drink specials most of the time. It is an Alabama Football bar on gameday saturdays, so if you dont like Alabama football or dont want to be around that crowd. Don't show up.

name: Ole Red
text:
Mixed experience. Courtney on the second floor did a great job as our server. She was friendly even though you could tell she was tired; our order came quickly and was accurate. The security staff is very professional and promptly solved some situations that could've gotten out of hand. Unfortunately, hostess team at the rooftop was another story. I put my name on list for a table of 2 and got the confirmation text at 8:06. We went to 2nd floor to listen to music and wait it out. And hour and 15 later I went upstairs to check on table and was told I had been seated already. I never even got a text that table was ready. There was no apology no explanation and no table.  I hate to say the music was a disappointment. There were 2 bands and they both sounded like amateur karaoke. Much better music out on Broadway.  There were 2 other couples next to us and they were shocked as well. 
On flip side, it was very clean, not too packed and we were able to seat on a couch for several hours and watch the myriad bachelorette and bachelor parties.  A different Broadway experience. Good if you're hungry or want a place to chill.

name: National Underground
text: Ordered food and beer.  Had to sign a waiver for "hot" chicken. It was hot but not waiver worthy hot.  Asked for another beer it never came got check left. I am with everyone else not worth going back.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: It has now been over 2 months. After my last post, I recieved an email requesting my phone number from the kitchen manager to which I immediately responded. I still have not heard a word.  It definitely shows that they could have cared less what I went through because they have no intention of ever addressing the issue. I guess lessen learned. When your at Margaritaville,  don't order the food unless you don't mind being sick for 3-4 days, just order the Margarita's!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: While the interior of the building is nice, the patio is great (minus the view), and the employees are friendly, the beer itself is nothing to write home about. My wife and I got flights here, and nothing was very memorable. I had come here intending to get a growler of whatever I liked best, and I left without one at all.

name: The High Watt
text: Small venue with a cool vibe and views of the city. I've never been to a show that was sold out here, most of them have been pretty empty actually. But I love the space, and it definitely has an intimate feel to it. I like that you have to go back through the building and it's somewhat tucked away and hidden. I'd highly recommend seeing a show here!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Bridgestone has me torn in two, I hate seeing concerts here (I blame Nashville, with its spoiling me with excellent musical venues) but I enjoy me some hockey games.  The staff is always helpful, even when the place is crazy busy, and they have a lot of places to acquire food and booze throughout the arena.  So I'm giving you, Bridgestone, 3 stars, because for concerts you get a 1, and for Preds games you get a 5.
 
Unless you can manage to get stellar seats (in which case, lucky you) music just doesn't sound as good at Bridgestone as, say, the Ryman or 3rd and Lindsley.  If you want a decently-priced seat you're most likely sitting in Knoxville (aka your head is hitting the Bridgestone ceiling).  I've been here many times for shows, and even sitting close (on those days when it was lucky me) it just doesn't sound as good.  But I've been spoiled here, and I'm not denying that.  Nashville has so many great places to see acts...even strolling down Broadway on a weekend night you see people playing in the street who are good.  But there's something about Bridgestone that I can't put my finger on...it just doesn't translate into great shows.  I'm hard pressed to go when I can spend the same amount for a nosebleed seat that I do for local music festivals or up and coming acts (that end up at Bridgestone eventually).
 
But for some reason this does not seem to be the case with hockey games, or other events held at Bridgestone.  Maybe it's the energy in the crowd, and fans get riled up to support their hockey teams.  There are entire sections in the third tier filled with rabid fans that make your night more fun.  
 
The arena being downtown, be prepared to park and walk, and pay a lot for the privilege, especially since the paid lots are more pricey on event nights.  The food is typical fare for arenas, but the staff are always nice and willing to help.  I don't beat down the door to get to events at Bridgestone, but I don't mind going.  If your favorite 80s bands are there, it will be crowded but by all means go and have fun.  See the Predators play if you haven't already.  And it's downtown, so once you've paid an exorbitant amount of money to stash your car someplace take advantage and stay out.  I guess what I'm saying is that you won't be upset for taking in something at Bridgestone, but it may not be the best show you've ever seen either...unless its hockey, then its always awesome.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Jasmine and Beth were very helpful!!!! The food was great!

We had a party of 7 and the food was brought out quickly and hot. Everybody left happy and well nourished.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Well the place wasn't initially all that bad. The singer of the band playing told a paying customer to basically "f-off" when she requested a song and to put money in the tip jar.   In all fairness she looked annoyingly drunk, but it's important to always remain professional. Lastly they closed at 2 which was an hour earlier than everyone else and they didn't even sound for a last call.  So we stand at the bar for close to 5 minutes waiting for my card and our check and we are being ignored until one of the bartenders turns and tells us they're closed. I reply that I waiting for my card and she goes t retrieve it. In the meantime a busboy rudely shoves past us and exclaims for us to get out that they are closed. By this point I'm fed up with he rudeness of the staff trying to corral everyone out and telling me to leave before I can even get my tab closed. I don't leave a tip to make my point of being dissatisfied with being ignored for the last 20 minutes of our visit. As we are walking down the street the waitress chases us down to explain she "works for tips".  Well that's funny because I tip for work. Try having your staff not be so rude at closing time.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Absolutely great spot that I have not been here in a year. The food menu is great and the service is smart and friendly. Awesome beer and very great atmosphere !!!!

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Solid solid bar! Great food!!! cheap ass drinks, great bartenders. Did a one hit wonder on karaoke night when i was wasted. I wish this place was around me because I would be there once a week. Awesome Nashville spot

name: National Underground
text: Thanks so much national underground for the amazing experience. Great food and wings I am from california and we had a amazing experience will took great care of us. Great ambiance great drinks.

name: Nashville Symphony
text: Beautiful venue, great acoustics and friendly staff. I went to see REO Speedwagon here back in October and had a great time. Prices for tickets were very reasonable and we had a good view from the orchestra level towards the middle of the room. Drinks were reasonably priced and I believe they had a cafe type place as well but we did not purchase anything. The best part, aside from the concert itself, was the amazing staff. Everyone I encountered was very friendly and helpful! I look forward to seeing another concert or possibly the symphony here in the future!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Tennessee Brewing! Hard to find, worth the effort! Cool old building. Beer was great!  Hot Nashville chicken sandwich was great. The artisan cheese board app was excellent.

name: Ole Red
text: Food was flavorful, music performer was amazing. Great atmosphere, the decor was nice and classy/rustic. The Poutine was really delicious, as was the peanut butter ice cream (a must try!). Our server was busy (as it was 4th of July) but she was as attentive as she could be, very nice and welcoming. One star was deducted because the chocolate cake was not moist, not very good. But would have the peanut butter ice cream on it's own for sure!

name: Ole Red
text: Love live music in a comfy place with no smoke and great drink options?  Come on down!!!  Fun atmosphere, and easy to get to.  So nice to just be able to sit and enjoy great tunes!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Overpriced Sysco food is about the only way to describe it. Our server was terrible and paid very little attention to our table. My wife and I both had two different frozen margaritas and could not taste tequila in any of them. We will not be going back to this location or any others.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Funny thing, sent email nearly 3 weeks ago as requested and haven't heard anything. Must not matter one way or the other.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Nashville's Bridgestone Arena is an extremely well managed sports, music, and event venue. Although it's getting on in age (built in the mid 90's), it's been updated well and offers great concessions (including local craft beer!) in addition to pretty good seating. If you've got the scratch, I recommend sitting in the club level, as you'll have access to better dining options and actually get a waiter for your section, so you can spend more time enjoying your event and less time waiting in line for concessions.

name: National Underground
text: This place kicked me out tonight. The "owner" came up to me and said I was a "homosexual" and that they don't allow that at the bar. I had done nothing that portrayed a homosexual manner. I went up to the bartender and asked if he was really the "owner" like he claimed to be and she said "no, just ignore him." Then he came up to me and again told me to get out, and the bar tender was like "yeah, you need to leave." The guy continued to harass me and yell at me to get out of "his" bar. I've never been in this situation before and don't plan on ignoring it. Gavin Degraw, who I love, is apparently the actual owner and did NOTHING about it.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
While waiting for the 98 degrees concert to start at Ryman down the street (yes that's right!), we decided to get a couple of drinks on Broadway. I didn't want to bother with the overly loud crowds of some of the more famous bars so we decided, why not? Let's try it! We typically try to avoid chain restaurants but we wanted a margarita.

It was actually really relaxing. We sat at the bar and of course they had live music. But they didn't just play country music. They were also really engaging.

My favorite Margarita was called perfect margarita (something like that) it was about $9-10 but it was so worth it. It was so much stronger than their regular margarita and it wasn't as sweet.

This place is huge, too. They have a really big dining area perfect for families.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I just needed some food between bars, so I was glad that they served something solid here.  I got a simple grilled cheese sandwich, which was good...but very expensive for what I expected for grilled cheese.  Maybe they use brie, so it's a bit fancier?  I was bummed there was no live music while we were there, but did appreciate the food.  

At the time it was too cold to sit outside and I didn't get a chance to try the drinks, so my experience was far from optimal.  Wish I could have enjoyed it more, but for how things were that day...I am indifferent about TBW.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Went in about 5pm last night.  The back room was mostly empty except two large groups.  With a room full of empty tables she tried to sit us next to one of the groups.  I'm not talking a table away I'm talking next to.  The lady in the group had to move her purse for us to sit down.  I asked if we could just take a table near by.  With a grunting noise she let us.  She gave us a couple
Of menus and there we sat....and we sat........and we sat.
At least 4 different waiters or runners walked by our table on multiple times.  Not one made any effort to acknowledge us.  In the meantime I fixed their wobbly table, you're welcome.  Two people walked in and sat with the group that was about ten feet from us.  They were promptly asked if they would like something to drink or order some food.  At that point we left.  I told the hostess and the fella she had been standing talking and laughing with at the front podium for the last 20 minutes about our lack of service.  Blank stares was the reply.   Food looked good but we never got a chance to try it.  The restaurant reaches out to me below.   With NO way to communicate with them without publicity posting my email.  No thanks!  They don't care.  Plenty of other places to go in this town.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Decent bar food, but what makes this place great is the music. However, arrive early or prepare to stand all night.  If your not lucky enough to get a table, it is difficult getting to the bar to order drinks.

name: National Underground
text: Best hamburger ever.  The menu warns that service might be slow, but that was not our experience.  Waitress was attentive and knowledgable, and the entertainment was fantastic.  One of the highlights of our trip into the city!

name: Ole Red
text: 1st time to Nashville and really enjoyed having a drink and a starter to share. We didn't get a main dish cause we wanted to keep checking out other places. Live music was good, drinks were good and appetizer was good. Service was excellent. What more can you ask for!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I went to Tennessee Brew Works for the first time yesterday. They've only officially been open about one week and I was really impressed with several things. First...the taproom is a great hang and has a very different and cool feel compared to other breweries in Nashville. Second...the staff was incredibly nice and welcoming. Even one of the owners was on hand to greet every customer in the tap room. Third they have good beers, which I guess is the most important part anyways. I am a big IPA fan and theirs, the Cutaway, was great. Lastly, their did options are limited but good. Pork Sandwich, Kettle Corn, etc...

Overall, good hang and I'll go back.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I saw the Foo Fighters many, many times in the last year. The show at Bridgestone was fantastic, of course, but it was the STAFF and the FACILITY that I was so impressed with. I would be back in a heartbeat. So impressed with how organized and friendly they were in contrast to other arenas I saw shows at this summer. What a refreshing change to the usual rude concessions, angry security and disorganized lineup procedures...or lack there of. Great venue, and well run. Bravo!

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
We finally got to make our first trip to the Schermerhorn to see "The Legend of Zelda: Symphony of the Goddess" event.  The building is beautiful and the Grammy award winning Nashville symphony was a treat to see/hear.  It was also fun to see the posh Schermerhorn overrun with nerds...

They offer valet parking for a whopping $27 so we opted to find our own.  We parked at Pinnacle at Symphony place, which was a very short walk to the orchestra hall.  We paid $15 BUT the Pinnacle closes most enterances to their garage except for the main one.  We did not know this and ended up walking around most of the building before we found that unlocked entrance.

Unlike other Nashville Arts venues, photography is allowed while the house lights are up, so feel free to take your phone/camera to snap some pics of the beautiful interior.

The hall is like a vast maze, but there are plenty of staff that will be glad to help you find your way.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Visiting Nashville and as a margarita drinker, I figured I pretty much had to stop here. All in all, decent, but pricey. The drinks are stromg, but I've had strong drinks for much less. I had the Teriyaki Chicken; it was delicious, but again, pricey. The bartender, JJ, was very nice. He's the reason I gave four stars instead of 3.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: The atmosphere, music and most importantly beer are absolutely phenomenal. They have a great take on different styles of beer. My wife, who doesn't even like beer found one that she really enjoyed (southern wit). This place gives you a great taste of Nashville and is a must see.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
On a recent first time visit to Nashville, our bnb host suggested this place among the many choices on Broadway, and I'm glad she did!  Layla's  is very unassuming, but the music is good, the beer etc is reasonable, and the staff was friendly.  There are dozens of honky tanks to drift in and out of along these touristy blocks, but if you're looking for a calm place to sit, kick back with a cold one, and enjoy some good Ole Nashville music, you'd be hard pressed to beat this little joint!  We went back a second time and were just as pleased.  And, if you need something for comparison, Roberts Western World, next door, is a good alternative if you must...
And if you're wondering why then it isn't a 5 for me? Well, there wasn't a better place I saw...but to be perfect, I'd suggest a little more seating, which they can't really expand, and some killer food...which I didn't sample.  But it's the first venue I'd return to in that area, next time around!  Thanks, Layla & company!  And a special tip of the hat to the band one evening, led by Chuck, who only referred to himself as "Chuck the f*** and his f***ING band"...so they might be a tad hard to track....lol...but they were three hours of pure, talented, and sincere entertainment. So Layla, please tell these guys to get a better way to follow them, 'cause we surely would!

name: 12th & Porter
text:
we love this place!! it rocks!! 

http://www.watchonlinevideos.org/twitter-links-hitleap.html

name: National Underground
text: I loved this place. It's quieter than most other SoBro bars and they have a great burger. Staff was super friendly and the music wasn't country. After honky tonking for two days, a change of pace and style was welcomed. We watched the Hissy Fits play 50's swing rock for over an hour. Definitely going back.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Tommy and Melissa are awesome.  Sit at the bar for great service from these two and a great seat for the music!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Honestly all these honky tonks are pretty indistinguishable from one another. But that doesn't mean they aren't at least a little fun.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: We like to go to breweries all over the country and this one was a great find! The decor inside and out is very inviting and unique and the beers are nothing short of that! You can tell the Brewers put a lot of heart into what they are making!

name: The Night Owl
text: Great space to squad up. They have karaoke and it's always a blast. Pingpong and pool

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
There's a bouncer at the door checking ID, ensuring that you are 21. Friday & Saturday nights are the most popular and it's wall to wall inside. ....just like walking on the street. 

Seems like the music is pop rock as all the 21 year old girls in the audience know the words and sing along with the band.

The norm is no cover,  and beets are about $5. Male sure you tip the band when they pass their Buckley around!

Always a fun time, and you might actually hear some good music.

name: The Night Owl
text: A great local bar, with delicious burgers!  Fun atmosphere, friendly staff.   Fun times!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Went to a Preds game when visiting from LA. This place is awesome. Nashvillans are too nice. I was wearing a Kings jersey and only got some mild smack talk. People, stop complaining about the food, it is not a restaurant.  The popcorn was amazing though. And whoever thought of half of beer during first intermission deserves and handshake.

name: National Underground
text: The burgers are good enough in my mind to justify the cost, and I live 4 blocks up the hill... It's nice to get more music variety. I hear that Gavin Degraw owns the place...

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: attended the CMA awards and was impressed.  The place was clean and the acoustics were great.  Also attended the taping of the CMA country christmas.  Great views of the stage and no echo, the venue could be different for sporting events, but for the two music shows we attended, i thought it was a nice place.  Lower the prices of the drinks and snacks though, geez.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Just in Nashville for a day and found this place on Yelp.  Awesome brewery!  Great decor and great beer selection.  Very nice staff.  Lots of seating throughout.  Had Sunday brunch and it's a smaller menu but is fabulous.  Large size version of connect four was fun for the kids.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Music was very good. Our waitress was ok.  Food was not so great... Thought it was a bit expensive.  The worse was the ladies bathroom.  Diirrttty.  Needs walls washed and painted.  Dirty cover below sink, no paper towel holder.. Floors gross.  Would not go back. Jimmy send in someone

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The volcano nachos could feed an army. The margaritas could knock out an army. Otherwise, nothing too spectacular.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
This place is so cool! We met friends here for a Saturday afternoon beer tasting. We did not do the tour but enjoyed spending time in the tasting room trying out several beers.  

The outside patio area is great and look forward to returning when it's warmer. The inside tasting room area is very nice and cozy. The staff is beyond friendly and very welcoming. While tasting there were 2 acoustic performers that added a great piece to the overall atmosphere. The upstairs tasting room overlooks the brewing operation which was neat to see. 

We tried 3 different beers that were good and served in a snifter glass at $5 each. This trip we missed out on a sweet potato stout that sounded delicious!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I really like this place.  Very nice vibe, lively, friendly cheerful staff and people, good food and good beer (and they have wine), pleasant surroundings, nice music.  

The one drawback is that when they run the credit card you are given three options: 20% tip, 25% tip, or "custom amount".  This really is a turn-off.  I'm glad to give a good tip, but I do not like being pushed, particularly with 20% as the minimum tip.  Particularly since you have to go to the counter to order, so it's not like they are doing a lot of work.

Also, parking is an issue.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: This place is awesome! Most of the time I go to a new brewery and I only like one or maybe two of the beers, but all of their beers are excellent. The place itself is pretty cool, especially the balcony that looks out into the brewery. This place is a definite contender with my all time favorite Yazoo.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Came here to see the Blackhawks take on the Preds in April 2013. Friendly staff, clean bathrooms w the speaker system so you don't miss any of the action, fast moving drink lines, etc. Aside from the loss, I had a great time, even made friends with security.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: MMW is a great venue! I love the industrial/factory feel and that it's a good size with two bars! The sound is great, and I love all of the fixtures and set up of the space. It's great! They have a good variety of shows and its an excellent venue. However, the parking definitely blows. The streets are always crowded so if you don't want to pay to park you have to drive quite a bit. Otherwise, lovely place!

name: Ole Red
text: Very unimpressed. Blake Shelton wouldn't come here. Food menu was odd. However, great service and employees were friendly though.

name: The High Watt
text: This venue offers a great variety of entertainment from concerts to comedic/stand-up shows. The sounds is really great in any room and the space is always cool and comfortable to sit back and enjoy a show. Best part- most shows are either really cheap or FREE!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
We met here with our Green Bay Packers group twice. Really nice place to meet up. 

We Wisconsin (Florida) people made it truly unbearable on the main Nashville strip (Broadway). Too crowded in several bars as Packers fans travel well.

So, we hung out south of the main strip in an area they call The Gulch. The Gulch is an old warehouse district that is being torn down and replaced with high-rise condos, restaurants and a host of micro-breweries. 

This place is a little tricky to find if you don't have it in your mobile GPS, but well worth the visit. They play contemporary music, they have a downstairs, an upstairs with two huge TVs (with sports on) and an outdoor section. 

We hung out upstairs and outdoors during our two visits. I had a hefeweizen which was really good and stuck with that. We had great conversation and really good service. Hope to make it back here in future visits. 

Highly recommend!

name: National Underground
text: THE worst place in Nashville.  So poorly run it must be a front for something. as you wait on line for the bathroom, people are taking food off of plates at the kitchen counter. The manager is a street thug with no manners and hasn't bathed in a while. Food ? They dont seem to keep the place clean and their is no hot water to wash your hands. If you want a crap time thats the place . What a S.... Hole ! So many nice places in Nashville.Stay away!!!!  Ps if you reserve a table with a view for New years. I guarantee you will be ripped off. Dont pay cash. The promise one thing and totally lie about what they deliver.

name: Ole Red
text: Took my mom and sisters for brunch on a Sunday. Live music was awesome! All our dishes were delicious. Spacious and open seating. It wasn't noisy from other people, even though it was packed. Definitely worth the trip.

name: National Underground
text: This place is awful. After ordering a cheese basket, we recieved cheese with a a bite out of it. Such a low value of entertainment compared to the rest of the places in nashville.  Service is OK.  Food selection is lacking.  Do not be tricked by the coupons being handed out for 10% off down the street.  Its not worth it!!!

name: Ole Red
text: First time we've eaten here. The menu was small. We've stopped in for drinks and live music before which I recommend. The Tennessee mule was just a regular mule, but the cherry limeade was good. The southern tater tot poutine was amazing! The hot chicken biscuit with fries and slaw was okay. I would have really loved it if the biscuit was better. I ended up just eating the chicken. The ranch was very good, watery which I usually don't like... but the dill flavor in it made it. I'd go back

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Loved this place! Everything was great, even the food! We got the cheese plate and some baba ghanouj along with a couple flights and a pitcher. The area's very spread out and not too crowded. They have live music downstairs and free board games upstairs. We found a darts area and played darts for a while too, just ask the counter for them! Overall, it's a fun place to spend an evening and the staff is very kind.

name: National Underground
text: I am only giving one star because otherwise Yelp won't let me write a review. Awful. I don't even have articulate words to describe our experience. Just read all of the other awful reviews. They sum it all up. Lesson learned- read the Yelp reviews BEFORE you try a new place.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Layla's was a super fun experience. I love the band, the atmosphere and the drinks. I thought the drinks were reasonably priced and they were not stingy on the pour, either. The bartenders were friendly and made the experience awesome! I will be going back to Layla's when I go back to Nashville.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Had an awesome time at the beerfest did not had the opportunity to catch a game while there.  The beerfest was well organized and the venue was kept very clean considering the hundreds of people in attendance.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Cool brewery to check out, especially if you're from out of town and don't know where to go. We did the flight which was plenty for us to sip on and let us try the different varieties they offer. Live music was playing so we hung out for a while. We didn't try the food but it looked really good!

name: Ole Red
text: Entertainment is good the ribeye was ok. Outback Steakhouse is better! If you wanna check out a spot to hang out and have a drink and enjoy the scenery it's a good spot to stop on Broadway.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Horrible service from female bartenders. They need to be trained better. We were there with a big group ordering a lot of drinks and they didn't appreciate the business we were giving them. I guess we won't be going back there again. They are very racist!!!!!!!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
One of the things I love more then anything in life is music in any form but life music is on top of it.

This place give my the chills when I hear wonderful vocals from people I love just to mention some Bruno Mars, Cher, Kelly Clarkson and do many others. 

Great service, helpful people giving direction, the sound is incredible actually is the best to make an incredible 

Ok food but good drinks

name: Ole Red
text: Great food. The group Aberdeen Green is super great. Waitstaff is so nice - our waitress is from Chicago - and Blake Shelton's touches are EVERYWHERE!!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: This arena is fantastic. Nothing too exciting, but it's always clean and the staff is super friendly, as well as almost all of the guests. Food prices are decent for a large sport/concert venue. Great acts often visit here and there's never a shortage of things to do and see in the area. The hockey is great with live bands between periods. I always look forward to going back here!

name: Ole Red
text: This place is full of yokel tourists and downer doormen! Worthless. Give your money to another dope space

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
The good:
Comfortable seats.
Easy access.  
Has some really unique shows (like Roger Waters Ça Ira).
Acoustics aren't as bad as you'd expect from a squared venue.  

The bad:
The square venue is acoustically challenging and for Roger Water's Ça Ira, they felt the need to augment the sound with microphones... Which is unusual for an opera.  

The bottom line:
The experience was awesome and easy the best performance of any opera in English I've ever heard and one of my favorite opera performances of all time period.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Great Arena! Never had a bad experience and there is definitely not really a bad seat in the place. Only complaint I have is the outrageous prices for the concession stands. Water for $5....are you kidding me? They definitely need to lower the prices but other than that a great venue with lots of great acts coming through. I know they are always busy doing something, which is a good sign!

name: Ole Red
text: The service was so slow the kid at the table next to us started eating his boogers. I don't know why he thought it was a good idea. But it was.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: What a great experience!!!! Chris Rhodes was professional, funny, and entertaining!!!! Even during a rush!!! We had a great time and will definitely be returning!!!! Great place and space if you are out with the family!!!

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Great food and awesome service. Waitstaff worked as a team so you never had to wait for anything. We were impressed with how attentive they were. Good prices and great experience

name: The East Room
text:
My boyfriend's band has played a few shows here, and it's overall a pretty decent venue. There's limited parking up front, but you can park in the car wash next door for free.

They have a pretty open area downstairs with fairly minimal seating, so I'm assuming more dancing happens here than I've yet seen. It did get a bit crowded, so depending on the act you're coming to see, come early if you don't want to lean against the bar all night.

Speaking of the bar - decent beer selection, I think they might have some wine too. But they don't have liquor, so pregame before you come!

There's an upstairs balcony with some extra seating, and this last time I was around they were using it for merchandise. Half this section is curtained off, so it is cozy up here.

I like the casual atmosphere here, and everyone is quite friendly. It's a good place spend an evening and hear some stuff you haven't heard before.

name: Ole Red
text: Food was poor quality...not a lot of options....cheese tastes spoiled and worst off all fruit flies everywhere...absolutely disgusting...definitely keep your options open!!

name: Ole Red
text: I'm not why we had to wait 2 hours to get a seat. They took the wrong number to call us. Had to call twice and stop in to make it right. Multiple order were wrong. I was very disappointed on multiple levels. They do a poor job of maximizing their space. To many places to pick... pick a different location!!!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
I wish they had Bluegrass bands here. That would make them different from the other honkytonks on Broadway.

But that said, I still like the place.

name: Ole Red
text: Employees very rude- won't be back. Walked in and was treated very rudely because this little doorman thinks he is cool. He was too busy talking to a friend to be doing his job. Then treated very rudely bc we interrupted him.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Kind of a lame addition to the other honky tonks on the Broadway "strip" in Nashville. While there was a little more care taken in outfitting the decor of the place to look more like a bar than a lumberyard (see my review for Tootsie's Orchid down the block), the two bartenders we had to contend with were behaving like jerks for most of our visit.  I guess they fancy themselves a place for locals, and my wife and eye stood out a little as tourists, so they came off with a bit of a chip on their shoulder.
