Too many other options on the street to put up with it for very long, so we didn't.

name: National Underground
text:
I'm not too sure why they've gotten the "best burger in Nashville" award because really, their burgers were at best, mediocre. I definitely don't think their prices are great, over $14 for a burger (extra cost for bacon and cheese!) and even a charge for fries! Not just that, I barely even got a handful of fries (9 to be exact) and they just weren't that good. 

The wait for my ridiculous, over 45 minutes and there is was hardly anyone in here. It's constantly loud and I feel like everyone is yelling at one another. Also, it was rather cold in there and no one seemed to want to do anything.  

Overall, I'm not overly satisfied with this place. Not worth it

name: Ole Red
text:
This is my first time in Nashville. Everyone who has been to this town loves it and told me I would love it too. 

Someone told me Ole Red is owned by Blake Sheldon. Because he's one of my favorite singers, a group of work friends and I went to this bar as my 1st bar to visit in Nashville. 

Let's get this part right! The live music was on point. Zach Ray was the best part. 

We stop at the bar and Josh is the bartender. He can't look more unhappy. I asked what one of the wines on the shelf was because I couldn't see the label. He hands me a wine list. We order drinks. I ordered a veggie burger and he tells me to come back in 15 minutes. I come back in 10 mins because our friends parents arrived and they wanted drinks. When I walk up to the bar, Josh says, "your food isn't ready, I said 15 minutes." Me, "Okay, I understand that, I'd like to order more drinks." He just can't look anymore annoyed. 

I had my knife on my belt but it was hidden under my jacket. Chris with Security was actually a nice guy. He asked me to leave because you can't have knifes in there. His manager Jackie rolls her eyes at me, when I ask if i can keep it in my purse. "I'll show you on the front door that you can't have knifes." 

I walked to the front door and all it shows is a firearm sign. I'm not going to spend money at a place that has rude people treating their guests poorly. 

Sorry Blake. Your food was good, music was amazing; however you should take a second look at the personalities of your staff. Friendly faces and attitudes will keep your guests coming back. 

The Whiskey Bent Saloon was a lot of fun. And so was Jason Aldean's.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: This is a horrible place. The band that was playing the night we came on our vacation was practically forcing the crowd to tip them and when people didn't, they accused them of being members of ISIS. The racist and also untalented lead singer was also calling out African Americans in the bar and talking about white America... We raised complaints to the bouncers who laughed and ignored us. Maybe this is normal in the South, but my friends and I live in the modern world and this is just totally unacceptable.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Tennessee Brew Works es una muy linda cervecería que se encuentra en el centro de Nashville, quizás en un lugar medio escondido, pero muy agradable y confortable por dentro.

Es de esos típicos lugares que tienen tanto la fábrica como el bar en el mismo lugar. El espacio es muy lindo y con bastante onda.

Pero lo importante, o sea la birra: probé una muy buena IPA en este lugar, posta que muy recomendable. La atención es muy buena y los precios -dentro de todo- accesibles. Tiene merchandising de todo tipo y distintas birras para llevar. Generalmente hay músicos y bandas que tocan en vivo.

name: Ole Red
text:
Great location and super service are two of the strong points of this Broadway Bank location. Blake is doin it right with his new addition to the Broadway scene. Except this place is obviously two notches above the best of the crowd in this neighborhood. Quality, consistency, reputable and clean....all things not easily found down on Broadway. 

Has the chicken which was good. The pulled pork was delicious and sides did not fail our expectations. Try the Mac &Cheese, biscuits/gravy and bread/butter pickles. Drink selections are well planned recipes but expensive....you get what you pay for. Everything in Blake's place is high dollar, but then again when you're good you can get what you charge. 

The variety of bands is pleasant and the quality of the productions is refreshing. 

Now on to the Tishomingo location!

name: Ole Red
text:
First off Blake Shelton owns or has his name on this place.  Who doesn't love Blake Shelton!?...well except for Miranda now but let's not get into that.  I wanted to go last June but it wasn't open so this trip we took with our 17 year old daughter, her first trip to Nashville! Ole Reds was our first stop! The initial impression was wide open space with tables. There was music playing as in most places in Nashville. We waited about 10
Minutes for a table. We sat downstairs near the stage but they also have upstairs where the bathrooms are located. Not ideal when you aren't planning on going up there but you'll need the exercise since all the food is yummy and unhealthy stuff. Or should I say all we ordered was yummy and unhealthy! They had salads on the menu. We ordered the tater tot poutine and quesadilla. We wanted to eat a little everywhere so started with these two items. They arrived and
the portions were LARGE! The poutine has lots of meat(pork) homemade tots and country gravy! They top it off with a fried egg! The quesadilla was huge and packed with chicken. A guy seated next to us had the potato chip nachos and they were HUGE!!! The food was good, I love Blake and we enjoyed the young man singing. It was a great place so not sure why the star rating isn't better. But I am an elite Yelper and it's a must stop on Broadway!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I won a charity auction for a gift certificate to Margaritaville and came with my BF on a Saturday around 1. Upon entry you hear the live music and notice the gift shop. The walls are covered in faux bamboo and the vibe is beach bum fun like every other Margaritaville I've ever been to. We were seated and ordered margaritas, the spicy shrimp app, and fish and chips.  My margarita was called the perfect margarita and that was accurate. It was potent and used fresh ingredients. The shrimp app came out and it was basically unseasoned fried shrimp topped with spicy mayo. Very underwhelming. My fish and chips came out cold so I got another order and they were much fresher. The fish is not hand battered or fresh or seasoned. I ate all the fries and left the fish. I ate my BFs jerk salmon dish with him and then we went and ate somewhere else. The food here is bland, frozen and quick but the margarita was great.

name: Ole Red
text: We stopped in for an early lunch. They were easily able to accommodate our party of 7 and we were seated promptly. The waitress was knowledgeable about the menu. We had 2 different adult beverages and both were great. There was live music and the band was great. We ordered the cornbread appetizer and it was amazing! We also had the pimento cheese appetizer and it was also delicious. Both my sister and I ordered the 1/2 chicken. This was A LOT of chicken but it was not good:( we wanted to like it but it was over fried. We also had the side order of Mac n cheese and it was nasty. The 3 kids wouldn't even eat it.  Overall, this was a good experience but I would not need to go back if I was in Nashville again...unless Blake was there!

name: Ole Red
text:
The rudest staff ever. We sat at an empty table at the rooftop bar area not  knowing it was "reserved" because there was NO SIGN. The RUDEST person told us if we did not move we would be escorted out by security - REALLY????? Why not just ask us politely to move? 

If this was my restaurant/bar I would be MORTIFIED. I will NEVER go here again!

name: Ole Red
text: We went there on Monday night and it was awesome. Had the nacho's and they were some of the best we have had. The band adairs run was great. Thanks ole red, we want to come back!!

name: Ole Red
text: Let my preface this by saying I live in town, so I only go to Broadway when I have visiting guests who make me. That being said, I was pretty impressed with the food at Ole Red, and will definitely bring guests in the future. This restaurant had multiple vegetarian and vegan items-we had an impossible burger with tots that was delicious! We also had a chicken quesadilla that was huge- two people could definitely share that entree. There is also a vegan version of the quesadilla. The drinks are expensive for Broadway, but on par with nicer restaurants.

name: Ole Red
text: First of all, GET THE TOTS. I don't care if you don't like tots, (because I don't) GET THEM. Our waitress, Megan (I think) suggested them to us and described them as deep fried mashed potatoes and she was right. SO GOOD. Burger was fantastic too! We sat right beside the stage and it was nice listening to the band.

name: The High Watt
text: Saw Brendan James here a week ago. Loved the atmosphere and would definietly return!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Food is not fresh and tasty. It's super expensive. People don't eat if it was given it for free but charged 5 times the regular price. Service was slowest in the world and it took more than 90 minutes. I was ready to leave but the waiter kept saying food is ready and on the way. What a waste of precious time and money :( Stay away. This type of places should learn a lesson

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I was treated to Tennessee Brew Works on Nashville Brew Bus tour during Yelp Spring Break and what a treat, one of the highlights of trip to Nashville with a tour from one of the owners Garr Schwartz, who is passionate about amazing craft beer.
Tennessee Brew Works is only one of three breweries in the United States using Belgian Meura mash filter.
My favorite beer, which my friend who is not a big beer fan, commented holy shit this is good beer is their Basil Ryeman, Belgian style Farmhouse Saison beer, which was one of the best beers I enjoyed in Nashville. 
I can't wait to return to have some more great craft beer on my next trip to Nashville and bring a growler and cooler to keep cool on the five hour trip back to Ohio.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Whether it is a concert, festival or sporting event -Bridgestone has you covered.
Great location! 
Food is good if you need a snack.
Preds Pro Shop here too!!
The bathrooms are newly renovated!

name: Ole Red
text: The only good part was music from Trey Odell and the view. Server was not knowledgeable of what gluten free options they have. Friends fries were cold. Server forgot to put in one item we ordered

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I was excited to add this place to my list to have a drink for my first visit to Nashville.  What a disappointment.  Old decor and I did not think it was very Jimmy Buffety.  We sat at the bar and nearby was a singer.  He was ok. Did a couple of sing along songs.  That was fun. Lots of drinks on the menu.  I was surprised that they didn't have more of a selection of margaritas.  A lot of their drinks had pineapple juice in them and I am allergic to pineapples. I ended up ordering a strawberry daiquiri.  But asked the bartender if there was any pineapple in the margarita.  I know they normally do not - but like I said there was only a few drinks that did not have pineapple in them.   He asked if I was allergic and when I told him yes, he said he would wash a few things before he made my drink.  Appreciate that!  But when I got my drink?  It had a pineapple hung on the rim of my glass. Hmmmm..... As for the drink it had to have been a virgin- could not taste the alcohol - not even a little bit.   Same for the husband - could not taste the alcohol.  24 dollars for 2 drinks that weren't that good?  I wouldn't recommend this place.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Words cannot describe the level of customer service that Shelby bestowed upon me, true professionalism at its finest. You could tell she was an expert at customer service and it showed. If I could pick one waitress to serve me my food for the rest of my life at a restaurant it would be Shelby. I'm literally breath taken and I will spread the word of her legendary service.

name: Ole Red
text:
This place is new and nice. Pretty clean as well. The staff is deplorable and customer service leaves a lot to be desired. The manager actually made a derogatory remark about the length of time it took me to get up the stairs. I was born with a rare muscle disease. I feel like anyone who patronizes this bar is likely to be treated the same way. Will not return and will let everyone I know exactly how I felt.

Bleu Butler

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Great atmosphere. Good beer. Yummy food! 

We couldn't check in to our AirBnB until late afternoon so this was a perfect stopping place for us. 

My boyfriend and I split the burger and the chicken sandwich. Both were unique and yummy, but very filling. My favorite part of our meal was the French fries. The seasoning was super good. 

The beer was okay. The flight was a good value so it was nice to try a few different options, but I didn't like them enough to order a full glass. 

We brought our dog and sat outside. The outdoor seating is nice and the inside is super open. You can even walk through the brewery portion of the building.

name: Ole Red
text: I was so dissatisfied with the service and lack of quality and taste of the food.  Service horrible and takes forever.  Party of six normal no heavy drink orders basic food requests.  All the people in the dinner party said same.....food bad.  Does Blake eat here?  So excited no bummed over it.  People at KOA also said food bad they all went on different days too.  Missed opportunity for a Big Bang but a big flop.  Also several people said his other place just as bad.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
This place is a city. It's just so so big. I remember when Bridgestone was brand new and the city was courting a hockey team. Hockey? In Nashville? Do ya know where you are? This is football country. O course, these were the days when Peyton Manning made sure that Saturdays in the Volunteer state were burnt orange. Well, history has shown that hockey has made a much better home of late in Nashville than football has (no pressure, Mariota) and Bridgestone has stood the test of time.

I don't get the complaints that it's old. The arena is less than 20 years old, people. Wrigley is old. Bridgestone is barely walking. And, despite its relative youth, it's already undergone some pretty significant (and impressive) renovations. Parking is easy.* There are plenty of access points. Three levels give goers the option of a variety of experiences. The on-site dining is choice (and that space has been redone as well). And the arena itself is massive. It's designed to hold a ton of folks but I have never felt smashed in or uncomfortable. I've also never been here for any other reason than to attend a hockey game. I know! I didn't even go to hockey games when I lived in Chicago. But, I wanted to check out some pro sports, Music City-style and until the NBA can figure out that Nashville is perfect for a team, hockey it is (change my mind, Mariota).

Watching hockey at Bridgestone is fantastic. There's not a bad seat in the arena and the good seats are *really* good. The fans are into it, support the team, make noise, and are psyched to watch the action. Nashville's a hockey town. Who knew?** Plus, there's good music, great graphics and a fantastic atmosphere. Again, I've never attended a concert at the Arena. If I had, perhaps my opinion would/will change. But until that happens, I'm more than happy to come here for a hockey game. I'd be even happier to come here for a NBA game. I'm looking at you, Raptors.

*It is. Don't argue.
**Keep in mind, Miami has a hockey team as well. Games/fans are not nearly as fervent... which is to be expected. The Panthers should move to Indy, Cincy or Cleveland.

name: Ole Red
text: Wow It was our First time at Broadway's new restaurant, Ole Red- Blake Sheltons new establishment. Thanks to our waitress Creuna she was awesome. Great band JD Shelborne and food was amazing.For lunch we had the burger and chicken biscuit sandwich. Both were excellent and complimented by great drinks. Very clean place and service superb. Highly recommend when in Nashville.

name: The High Watt
text:
This is a nice little venue to watch some bands.  The sound is great, the bar is small, the price is reasonable, can hold a good crowd.

Why 3 stars?  Because they don't have enough seating.  I was very, very, very lucky that someone gave me their stool.. Otherwise, I would have left early and not seen the two bands playing.

Shame on them for not having enough seating..
Why can't it be more like the Bluebird with tables and chairs and waitresses?
Imagine the business they would do, then!!!!

But they don't think that there are ALL different age groups that attend these concerts and some people can't stand all that long.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I wanted to add to my review that our food may not have been outstanding; but it was still pretty good.  (Our group of 5 managed to finish it off!). I also wanted to add that our server, Olivia, was outstanding!  She was friendly, helpful when we were ordering, and quick to anticipate drink needs & get them our in a timely manner.  She is definitely an asset to Margaritaville!

name: The High Watt
text:
3.5

Yet another cool venue in Nashville. One of the things I like noticing is the sheer number of places at which to see a show and how those places change depending on location and/or artist. There's no need to have a cookie cutter live show experience in Nashville -- which is just another reason to love this city.

The High Watt is part of the Cannery Ballroom ensemble. So, you know where you are and you know what you're getting. What sets HW aside from its partner/neighbors... the ceiling seems higher at HW. The layout is a bit more straight forward in that you ascend the stairs, walk past the bar and directly in front of you is the stage. If it sounds simple, it is... and it's the reason I just can't quite make it to 4 stars. The venue is very small. This is perfect for an intimate night with a favored artist. This is frustrating for a more raucous show and an attempt to either get anywhere near the bar or situate yourself anywhere other than where you first land. There's a small seating area to the left but who comes to a rock show to sit? I don't think HW is the right sort of venue to sit and watch a show and I wouldn't recommend coming to a see that kind of show here. See above re multitude of different venues for different types of shows/artists. Plan wisely and know what you're getting into before coming out. Once you've done your homework, I think you're in good shape for a fun night out at The High Watt.

name: Ole Red
text: Great atmosphere , several great bands. Nice atmosphere. So much food it was difficult to eat. Only negative while all four of us enjoyed everything about the Resturant. There was no place to park and the cost of 25.00 for parking  was steep, for no longer than we were there.

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
Yes, yes, and yes.

The Schermerhorn is a fantastic venue (and wonderful addition to downtown Honky-Tonk Central) hosting all manner styles of music performances. In fact, for some people it is a bit of a surprise in this country-centric music mecca.

We've enjoyed attending a abundance of events ranging from Classic Symphonies performed by the the highly talented, 5-star Nashville Symphony Orchestra to Jazz Concerts & Pop Performances by legends such as The Manhattan Transfer, Johnnie Mathis, Frankie Valli & the 4 Seasons, to Movies...accompanied by the orchestra. That's a treat in and of itself. A live performance of the music while viewing the full length motion picture.

The offerings are not limited to classical or jazz or pop. Music of ALL kinds is presented in the on-going plethora of concerts and events. Just check out the incredible schedule: https://www.nashvillesymphony.org/tickets/calendar . It is truly impressive and offers something for every age: children to senior; every taste: classic to country; multiple venues: in the hall to in the park to smaller, intimate special parties. 

The highly talented symphony is led by world-class conductors Giancarlo Guerrero (Music Director), Vinay Parameswaran (Associate Conductor) and Kelly Corcoran (Chorus Conductor). Ushers and support staff are always courteous and willing to assist in any way possible. (Don't hesitate to ask for directions--the venue can become confusing with its myriad of hallways and transition areas.)

Parking is available in numerous downtown lots. Discounted Pinnacle Parking Garage vouchers(limited) are available prior to the performance and special discounts are given to concert series subscribers. You can also park in the public lot located conveniently across 4th Avenue under the Music City Walk of Fame Park.

I afraid my words are inadequate in describing this treasure trove in downtown Nashville. I heartily encourage you to experience it for yourself.

name: Ole Red
text: Travelled all the way from Hawaii to watch the Gone West Band at Ole Red, waited 3 hours outside the venue to find our that we still can't go inside because they've reach capacity and if we continue to wait, their set would've been done already. So disappointed.

name: Nashville Symphony
text: The Symphony Center is located in the heart of downtown Nashville with available parking directly in fronted the building-about $35-I believe they also offer valet, but when we arrived 30 minutes prior to the show, it was already full or closed. The interior creates a very elegant ambiance with great seating. We had the "box seats" which offers it's own private bar area on each floor. A definite recommend for date night!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Went here for a tour on Saturday at $11! Our tour guide Jason was super friendly, and definitely made it a more personal experience asking where we were from, if we had been on a tour before, and tailored the tour information to our interest. We were able to taste 2 beers that day Southern Wit and a porter, Pie Town Porter. They gave us a pint of whatever beer we wanted and let us keep the glass. It was a great experience, and we stayed for a while and got another flight to taste! Great beer, great people with lots of seating (2 floors), definitely would come back here again for the ambience and beer.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: The most unfriendly staff!!! Not welcoming and very rude! Sad, was excited to experience it as I've heard great things!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: What a fun place! Staff is VERY friendly. I shared the wings and had the sauce on the side. To be honest the dry rub on the wings was so yummy that I didn't even need the sauce. The beer in the picture is Basil Ryeman and it was just what a saison should taste like.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I've been to a few concerts here and it's always been a pretty good experience. 

Lately, they've updated their concessions and now offer great, local beers. I really appreciate that b/c, if I'm going to pay too much for a beer, I'd rather spend an extra dollar and get one worth drinking. The staff is always friendly and helpful. The sound and ambiance is what you'd imagine of an arena (big, loud, dark.) They check purses before you go in but it's nothing too crazy. The parking is less than ideal but that's just downtown, in general.

After seeing a few shows here, I've decided I'm just more of an amphitheater girl. You get a really big show at the arena but there are just so many people and the place is so big, there's not much of a vibe. For what it is, I think it is a great "what it is." Also very conveniently located if you want to crawl around downtown after an event. Leads straight out onto Broadway and all your world-famous honky-tonks.

Fun fact: The Nashville Convention and Visitor's Bureau has a visitor's information/gift store in the arena. It's the funny looking part off the side at the corner of 5th and Broadway (with the radio tower on top.) Obviously, the radio tower is a wave to WSM and the reason that part jets off the side in a weird angle is because it's supposed to look like the building is bowing down and paying homage to the Ryman Auditorium, the first home of the Grand Ole Opry, which is located just a bit further up the street off 5th Ave. Now, go impress your friends!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: I like this place. It's the perfect dive bar. Small and cozy atmosphere. Brick walls, license plates nailed up everywhere. It was busy but not packed. Bartenders were very attentive and the band they had was really good. Very laid back crowd. Mostly young groups of friends, but a few older couples hanging out. What more can you ask for in a bar? Had a great time.

name: National Underground
text: We stopped there on a Saturday morning around 10:30am. The service was the worst I have ever had anywhere - anytime. It was not crowded - maybe 15 people in the place. It was 10 minutes before we saw a wait person, It was another 10 before she brought us any drinks. They ran out of glasses. She only returned once after we summoned her to ask how much longer until the food was out - she said it was going to take a while - 10 minutes more. We waited 20 minutes more. She didn't return, we waited 45 minutes total for the food that never arrived. We gave up and left.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Stopped in before my concert right across the street at the Ryman. I ordered the Shrimp Scampi along with the Uptown Top Shelf Margarita as recommended by our friendly server Francine. The food took a little long but it was a busy night in town and Francine kept us informed along the way. My party and I enjoyed it and will definitely comeback to enjoy a little bit more of the live music and great food.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Came here on a Friday night with some Nashville locals and was shocked it wasn't more busy, but that was fine with us. It looked like the live music had just wrapped up and there was plenty of outdoor seating. Beer was good as expected and I hope to come back and try some others another time. 

Ordered the Southern Grilled Cheese with bacon and WOW was it good. The pear butter added a unique and delicious flavor. The bacon was really thick; it was good but next time I would probably skip it. The food was really good but a bit overpriced; granted it was a very gourmet grilled cheese.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: This is one place we always visit when going through Nashville or staying for the weekend!! The beer is so good and clean and food is phenomenal!!! They are dog friendly and the location and atmosphere is very cool. They usually have locals musicians come in every night and I would highly recommend the tour.

name: Ole Red
text: I was not impressed with Ole Red. After checking reviews, we decided to give this a try. The three of us were seated within 10 minutes and the server arrived at our table soon after we were seated. The menu was somewhat limited, typical Nashville bar food fare. We ordered one hamburger and two salads. Things were a little pricey, but we were in the heart of Nashville's tourist area and realized we were going to pay more. The disappointing part was when our food arrived. The home made tater tots were soft and tasteless. Even with salt, pepper and ketchup, they were not worth the calories. If you can't make them better than what we'r buy at the grocery, don't try.  The burger was ok, but probably was frozen patty they slapped on the grill. The worst impression was made by two of the saddest salads I've ever seen. Old lettuce, mushy cherry tomatoes, and so little of everything that you could almost see the plate through it. We ordered a piece of Nashville hot chicken with each salad for an up charge of $6. Each salad was served with a SMALL thigh. For $6, a thigh!? Top that off with having to ask for dressing three times because each time they brought a container out, it had maybe two teaspoons in it, we had made up our mind that Ole Red would not be anywhere we'd recommend or visit again. So- for over $60 we recieved, two salads, one hamburger, a beer, a tea and a water. And left hungry. Don't bother with Ole Red.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
One of our favorite bars on Broadway. We were there weekday afternoon. Quick service and got to hear a great musician. So many dark, no-light bars..but this one has plenty if you're downstairs.

I had the pulled chicken salad and the chicken was great. The only reason I wouldn't give it 5 stars is that my fiance had the nachos and there wasn't any cheese on them. Weird, right?

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: My family and I were visiting Nashville for the day and we starting to feel slightly parched and hungry. As we walked past Rippys the smell of BBQ drew us in. The bar and grill has a down stairs and upstairs bar and sitting areas. Upstairs can accommodate for larger groups and is air conditioned. The ribs, onion rings, pulled pork and mac and cheese are really good. I normally am very picky with pulled pork and can say this place is good. I personally ordered the sliced pork loin on Texas toast  (aka chilled cheese pork loin sandwich) and was very happy about my decision. Rippys has 2 bbq sauces (sweet and spivey). I liked mixing both together as the sweet had better flavor but I still wanted spicey.  The service was quick and you can tell the wait staff enjoy their jobs. Music is not as loud in the upstairs larger sitting area and is nice if you want to be able to talk without yelling. I highly recommend Rippys.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Expensive, yes, but I thought it was worth it. The live music was phenomenal and the staff was super nice. The ambience was really fun and light. I would recommend it.

name: Houston Station
text:
My husband and I had our wedding at Houston Station on November 25th. We cannot say enough about the beauty of the venue and the dedication of the staff! 
We decided to not use a wedding planner, and Elizabeth and Samantha were top notch helping us plan such a large undertaking. At our first meeting with Elizabeth she had a folder with recommended vendors. We felt the best part about Houston Station is that ALL of the vendors are in the building, they are used to working seamlessly together, and Elizabeth has long standing relationships with them. At our planning meetings, Elizabeth and the vendors were finishing our sentences! That is how much they anticipated our needs.
By the end of the wedding, we felt like Elizabeth and the staff were family. Elizabeth is no nonsense, runs a tight ship, and has the biggest heart of gold. She is a HUGE Alabama fan, and my husband is a HUGE Auburn fan. Of course we were married on the Iron Bowl. 
Elizabeth set up the grooms room with a TV for the game so my husband could watch it until the last minute. Even in the face of Alabama's loss to Auburn, she knew how special it was for my husband, and she graciously played along. 
Clearly, I can't say enough about the venue and the people. If you're looking for an upscale way to do it yourself, go to Houston Station. It is worth every cent.

name: Twin Kegs
text:
Oh...this place. What a gem, this place. 

Ok, first things first. Twin Kegs was recently voted "best burger in Nashville". I might agree with that. The burgers are DAMN good, but I've also not had every burger in Nashville so that's not really a fair assessment for me. BUT it's definitely a top contender! The article I read stated Twin Kegs was voted best burger and listed the price at $4. This is absolutely not true. The burger the bartender recommended as their best seller was $8.50. But, delicious nonetheless. 
The karaoke was certainly a thriller. STEVIE G., please come back! This place gets very lively for karaoke, so if that's your thing, get there early! 
They have a shuffleboard table and I was pretty damn good at it! 

All in all great bar food (don't put it on a higher pedestal than that) and great times had by all. This is a perfect combination to help you forget about the bad grammar on the sign. Don't you mean "Internationally Famous"? :)

name: The Rutledge
text: Great place to hear live music.  The service isn't great, you probably will wait awhile for a drink, but other than that, it's great!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
We were drawn into Rippy's after we heard the music from the street. We got salads, chicken nachos and corn cakes with chili. The upstairs has an awesome vibe with a big bar on one side and lots of tables on the other side. There were three different bands playing (one upstairs, two downstairs). The woman singing upstairs had an amazing voice.  

Our server was super nice and attentive even when his section got pretty busy. The food was pretty average. The chili was good but I was hoping for better corn cakes. The nachos were pretty standard. The view from upstairs is nice and looks over all the commotion of Broadway. A table by the window is the perfect spot for people watching while listening to live music with a beer in hand.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: What a freaking disaster, they make your order food within 5 minutes or they kick you off your table.....then you get to talk to security wannabe "head of security" True and the boys.......bad food, warm beer, thank god they bought the real estate before the boom in Nashville.......

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: My girlfriends and I came to Nashville for 3 of their 21st birthdays. Two of them had temporary ID's because they JUST turned 21 in NC last week. They both had their old ID's that expired last week. Showing the bartenders both their new paper ID and their old ID that just expired, the bartenders would not serve them. I've been 21 since January with a normal NC ID and they questioned mine as well. The bartenders were the bitchiest women and this was the biggest bummer to all of us considering we just got to Nashville today and this was the first place we came.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: The food was pretty good! I recommend getting the crawfish bread, as that was the best thing our group ordered. The alfredo pizza was also very good, but the rainbow warrior left much to be desired. Ambiance was cool, and there was live music on the top floor.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Line dance lessons/dancing in general. Just do it. One of my favorite places!

Downside: bartenders upstairs are slllllow.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Stopped here after the Packer /Titans game.  After finally getting waited on for a drink order, the server came back to inform us they didn't have Miller Lite. She again returned 10 minutes later to take another order.  We ordered both drinks and food at this time.  The reordered drinks arrived and some were warm. The pulled pork, beans and onion rings were barely warm.  Not a place I'd ever return to.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: If you like crowds and loud music then this is your place. Packed in like sardines, not clean. Don't care for Broadway, Just a bunch of tourist traps, go elsewhere in Nashville. Jack's Barbeque down the street has the best BBQ on Broadway

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: So much fun! We went on a Monday night so it wasn't packed but we had a blast learning to line dance and river dance!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
This review is for their room rental and corporate meetings. 
* The food - although abundant - was not good. "Eggs tasted like rubber."  Another said, "we should never come here again, this is just bad." Our vegetarian and vegan had sandwiches brought in from across the street for lunch on day 1 and brought food for breakfast.  
* The AV situation on day one as bar none, the worst performance by a vendor in my career.  I've walked in to rooms and had phones missing, power cords forgotten, missing AV gear, and the like, but in each case the situation was quickly remedied and we got about our day. This had no excuse - there was no one to remedy the situation.  We had 30 plus people in a room and we have no AV equipment to use. I cannot understand how no AV person was present during the meeting. That's frankly unprecedented for anyone who rents meeting space. 
* Day 2 was loud, between a fan belt squeaking (I understood we turned off the AC to stop the noise?) and street noise.  Again, commented on by many but at that point the team had given up hope.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
This review is for food only, not the music, ambiance, or service.

We were kind of pressed for time before a concert at the Ryman and needed a place serving something (anything) vegetarian.  To their credit they served a veggieburger, which is surprisingly not easy to find in the area.

At best it was ok, as were the somewhat soggy fries.  The three stars reflect our server, who was really nice and helpful, the music, and the rustic ambiance which we appreciated.

If you are vegetarian there are numerous really good options in Nashville, unfortunately not in the downtown area.  Allow time to eat and travel to your destination.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Got take out here around 10 PM, lookin forward to a pulled pork sandwich with a side of coleslaw. Look at the sandwich - totally dry. NO BBQ SAUCE. Is this not a BBQ joint?!  If you have to add it yourself, that's fine but LET PEOPLE WHO GET TAKE OUT KNOW!  Also, no fork so I couldn't eat the coleslaw either. What a mess all the way around - total waste of my $8. Then called to talk to someone about it and no one even bothered to answer the phone. Save yourself the hassle and go somewhere else for takeout!!!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The place is big. Nice stage size and dance floor. They offer line dancing lessons. Service was okay and the drink prices were high. Feels more like a club which I'm not really a fan of. I prefer the more dive bar feel.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good atmosphere, good bands, adequate service given the noise, good cocktails. Ribs were average, had worse but had better. Lose another star for using Sweet Baby Rays as one of the sauces provided on the table. A nice honky tonk bar to hang out at but skip there food (or ribs at least)

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Stopped for a quick dinner.  Fast but not great.  Pork loin sandwich was ridiculously small.   At least service was fast. I can't recommend this place.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: A comfortable corner bar that offers good Pub food.  The wings are spicy and meaty. The pork plate is excellent. The one draw back that seems to be common on Broadway is beer is only served in bottles.  We miss the draught beer choice.  Will definitely go again because beer in a bottle can also hit the spot, and the location and music was excellent!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Yes... this place is a little "touristy" but its still a good time. The music is good and they teach you line dancing (if you want.. they dont pressure you). The drinks are plentiful and the food is good. Our group  tried a little bit of everything (steak, catfish, chicken strips, cole slaw, hush puppies, fried green tomatoes, pork chops, and fried green tomatoes). Everyone liked their food and had a great time. MAKE SURE YOU TRY THE DELICIOUS BBQ SAUCE! I dont even like BBQ sauce and I was putting it on everything I could find. I even bought a bottle of it in the gift shop. Its a really big place that gets really busy, especially if there is a show going on.  Get in early and claim a table.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Stopped in for lunch today and the place was dead but we still enjoyed our time here. The live music was entertaining and our waitress did a great job taking care of us and giving meal recommendations. We had a salad with steak & an order of chicken tenders. The salad got two thumbs up and the chicken tenders got one. The French fries were really good, they must have some sort of seasoning on them! I could've just had a plate of them by themselves! Overall we had a good experience!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
As I type this I am actually across the street at Baileys enjoying great service and food. I had to walk out of rippy's because the service sucked so bad. 

We waited at a table 15 minutes before it was cleared from the last guest and when it final was, they didn't wiped it down. Just left all the scraps from the last group.  So the waiter returned 10 minutes later to take our drink order. 10 more minutes to get said drink (1 beer 1 water).  10 minutes later to finally ask if we wanted to order. We told him no paid for the over priced beer and walked out.

name: CMA Fest
text: I've been to the music festival several years and this year was worse than ever. when going down to the riverfront you had to have a ticket to get in and if you didn't have a ticket then you had to stand in a long line and you were the last ones to be let in to the riverfront. Also the first night going to the Nissan stadium my friend brought her small purse and a clear bag and went right in to the stadium then the next night she brought the same thing and they made her put it in the locker. So The thing that made her so upset was that one night they allowed it and the next night you didn't.  Also the bars have roof top seating. Last year we went up there and watched an artist or two and then left this year they were selling seats for 100 per person along the railing. The CMA fest has made it hard to be able to enjoy yourself and I will never go back.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: As a line dancer from the north, I was excited to come to Nashville to show off my skills. Unfortunately, Wildhorse is just about the only place to line dance and their line dancing is surely lacking. They only teach extremely easy dances (which makes sense seeing as they have all beginners all the time), but when the instructor started leading dances to the band she used the same couple of dances for all the songs. It was disappointing that there were tables covering half of the dance floor, because then it would have been much easier for a floor split or two stepping around if the tables weren't in the way. We went on a weeknight and the bands were acoustic, which is not very conducive to dancing! On the weekend they were full bands but still nothing too impressive. The instructor played a couple songs between sets but half the time it was hard to hear and they didn't know anything about what to play.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Out on the town we stopped in because we heard the rooftop band.  We decided to eat dinner, I got the pulled pork sandwich with Onion Rings it was good but could of been a little heartier,  but being  downtown on Broadway everything is smaller.  The husband got the pulled chicken sandwich with baked beans and he absolutely loved it.   But then again could of been heartier.  But overall service and food was good and the band was just average compared to come we had seen earlier.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This is by far the most family friendly dancing place in Nashville.  It is often crowded on weekends and in the summer.  They have a stage which usually has live music, and a large dance floor where you can go up and dance whenever you want.  The place itself consists of three floors, so its huge.  The food is good, especially the deep fried pickles.  A fun experience for the family, but it isn't overrun with only families, so it's really good for anybody.

name: CMA Fest
text: Artist did their jobs!!! Sound crew not so much!! BASE LEVEL IS AWFUL. We have great seats up front and the base is so bad we left early. Everyone around us felt the same too. Literally our insides were vibrating!!! Let me add I go to a TON of concerts and listen to rock n roll and those shows aren't this bad!!! Wayyyy tooooo much thumping base! I really felt bad for all the older people around us. Bad sound!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Die Karte gibt wieder was man erwarten kann.Bediehnung sehr nett und hilfsbereit.
Die Portionen haben amerikanische Größe
und machen satt

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Came in here with some girlfriends late one night, loved the band that was playing upstairs! We had a blast getting on stage with them and singing!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Ok, I am a fan of...

Soulshine's Bushwhacker. It is the BEST Bushwhacker I've ever had.  There's some kind of coconut flavor in there - I'm not sure if it's canned coconut milk, or coconut "beverage" like you can get in a carton. But the concoction of flavors in Soulshine's Bushwhacker are unlike that I've had in a Bushwacker anywhere else - nationally.  It's chocolatey, ice cream-y, coconutty, and YUMMY. It apparently can only be served in a small glass because of its alcohol content - I dunno, after two I wasn't feeling super buzzed.  (Maybe because I also ate??) But run don't walk to have this drink at Soulshine now, it is WORTH IT.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Cover charge to eat mediocre food and $5 bottles. Loud, can't hardly hear the person next to you. My short rib grilled cheese was awful. Meat was bland, dry, jerky like, bread tasted like they cooked it in a whole stick of butter. Had to drown it in bbq sauce to make it edible. Save your money and go to honkey tonk row!

name: Nashville Palace
text: First time in Nashville so I'm checking out some of the spots. Food was pretty average here, overall. No real standouts on the menu. But the waitress was super friendly and attentive, and the food came out quick (a plus cuz I was starving). And the live music was great. At this particular time, there was a folksy gentleman that played some great oldies and stuff I've never heard which was all great. I'll come back.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Just had a beer but the food did look good. Next time we'll take the time to have a bite to eat.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Good pizza -- nice outdoor space.  Gets really loud, unfortunately.  And, I really really wish they had a decent option for some wine.  Everything in mid-town other than The Tavern -- is a bar.  Soulshine has some class to it -- and it would be really great for us to enjoy a nice glass of wine too -- instead of beer.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I was very underwhelmed by the Wildhorse Saloon. Although I was able to get in for a reduced cover charge due to the fact that I was attending with a large group, I regret even paying the $3 to get in. Upon entry, we immediately realized that the place had been taken over by teen and pre-teens for the night. This place is 3 full levels plus a huge open dance floor, but there was no getting away from the underage revelers as they were everywhere. Hey, I was a teenager once and I understand that teenagers want to have fun too, but I also think that this bar should enforce a curfew like other bars in the area. Something about teenagers having easy access to alcohol and dancing with people more than twice their age doesn't sit well with me. Additionally, after 10 pm an adult should be able to go to a bar for a night of drinks and fun with friends instead of feeling like they're obligated to be a responsible chaperone.
In addition, the drinks were absolutely horrible. Their "drink special" for the evening was still over $7 and consisted of some cheap-o whiskey and red apple schnapps. Eww. We ended up just ordering a rum and coke and vodka tonic, which were extremely watered-down and still cost $6.75. 
2 stars because it IS an impressive-looking venue and the line dancing instructors and house bands have the potential to make for an awesome night out (as long as you're not the only patron of legal drinking age). I really wanted to like this place, but I don't think I'd ever return as long as they charge a cover.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Amazing pulled pork sandwich, the best I've ever had. Live music was great. No draft beer but overall a great spot on Broadway

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I had an amazing time watching the Predators first Stanley Cup game here! The music was spot on and Amber, our bartender was a gem! She was the first person, after a few spots before, to greet us. We only waited a minute before her smiling face asked us what we'd love to enjoy. Didn't try any food this go round but I've heard their ribs were to die for!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I give this place 2 stars only because the waitress (new from Houston) and a waiter (who's name I didnt get saved it from being one star. I walked in a side door, the place is at about 25% capacity. I find a place in the side or back room and sit down. Apparently, I broke a major rule by not being sat by a "hostess". After 20-30 minutes I got up and asked a scruffy looking waiter, who's appearance I can only guess was new wave druggie or homeless person, and asked what the deal was, because everyone's ignoring me. He said, with more than a bit of attitude, that you're supposed to wait to be sat, and then explained that it's on the sign. I said that's no excuse and was about to leave but figured I'd give it one more, if even sarcastic, attempt. So I found a "hostess" who was leaning by the door. I had to ask, since she was trying really hard to ignore me, if I needed to be sat. She said yes and proceeded to sit me almost where I already was. I moved right back to where I was. Still took another 20 minutes before anyone talked to me. When the nice waiter asked me I explained the situation and he was more than and even brought me a free, albeit warm, beer. Then, the waitress, who'd walked by me at least 10 times came by and was very nice and sweet (new from Houston). I had one drink, paid for it and left. I don't blame this on the staff, I blame this on the management. This is a training and culture issue. I suggest a change in management, someone who actually understands how customer driven business works. I won't be back. I was here at about 4pm.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Great live music with no covers and decent pizza!
The live music is the reason we went here and the band on Thursday night was good.  There was no cover and the upstairs was the music stage. The pizza was okay, I had the Mediterranean without mozzarella sub with feta. I found it okay tasty but the pizza was a little small and overcooked. They had a good beer selection of local beers like Yazoo.  In walking distance from the Gulch so we didn't worry about parking.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
This was the bar my group and I started off our night as we ventured up and down Broadway. As we pulled up to Broadway to look for parking, Rippy's caught our attention because there was a mob of people standing on the corner to watch the McGregor vs Mayweather fight. We got excited because we saw Rippy's had live performers but then we realized all the bars on Broadway had live performances. I asked for a round of pickle back but they didn't have any so I went to ask for Tokyo Tea which the bartender did not know how to make so she said she will just make me a Long Island Tea (I think, it was super noisey). When she gave us the drinks, it was half filled in a plastic cup and she went to charge me $9 per "drink". The drink wasn't even strong so I just thought it was such a rip off.

This bar has two levels so check that out if you're feeling adventurous. They have live bands on both floors.

name: Twin Kegs
text: OK, this place has really improved so I felt the need to update my original review.  The burgers are to die for - especially the Spice Burger.  The crowd is mixed and the place is still divey (try to avoid the restrooms if possible) but the burgers and the friendly staff make it worthwhile.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This night was probably busier than normal since NHL Stanley Cup game was nearby. Had to tip server before being served so she would serve us. Once we got seated & served, it was fun. Food so-so. Buffalo chicken sandwich was not good; fried pickles were good. Live entertainment excellent. Travel Channel was there doing a story, which was fun to watch.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Ick! Premade slop! Don't waste your time.  The ribs were the ONLY thing good. The sides were obviously premade n stored in styrofoam. Sooo bad

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Fun venue with good variety on their menu.  Walking distance from major venues and hotels, and live music was a plus.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: My husband and I see at least 4 shows a year here and love them all! They bring the best musicals to town. I also attend Tedx Nashville and a few other conferences throughout the year and love the facilities. Only improvement they could make is wifi for the conferences... It's hard to sit all day listening to speakers but not have the ability to open your laptop and catch up on emails. However! The shows they bring to town make me forgive the little wifi indiscretion. Can't wait to see Wicked!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Ah, Scoutmob, always leading to fun new places. We decided to take advantage of 50% off this new spot, and were very pleasantly surprised. 

To start, the interior is very cool. From what I understand, this is a small chain, but it felt like a Nashville local spot. It has an old brick warehouse feel to it, but was really clean and definitely set a good vibe. The music was a bit loud and had some crazy psycho jazz playing at times, but hey, that's Nashville. The big stairs towering through the middle of the room, the stained glass windows, and the beer-bottle chandelier made for some really fun stuff to look at. 

As for the food, it was pretty great. Three of us split a 16" Carnivore pizza. I forget what all meat was on it, but you can use your imagination... It was a lot. While it wasn't mind-blowing or revolutionary, it was very solid, very delicious pizza. They offer white or wheat crust, and have a LOT of specialty pizzas. There were also lots of people ordering sandwiches and they also looked tasty. 

Overall, the cool vibe, the good food, and the reasonable price make this a prime candidate for a "regular" spot. We'll be back for sure.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
True Southern hospitality - from the management, servers, and food. We have been in Nashville for 3 days, and we were waiting for comfort food.  This place exceeded expectations. 

We heard about this place because of the Cambria Sunday funday pool party! Our table of 11, ordered 1 of every shareable appetizer - the spoon fries, bacon queso, and deviled eggs were our favorite! I did the BLT - hangover helper. Hot chicken was great! 

Our server was exceptional, providing us local suggestions and always checking in on us. Great conversation. He was be first man to actually treat us with respect and keep us from getting hangry! Sincerely appreciate everything he did for us! Would definitely come back!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
If you like BBQ, music and an open restaurant concept, Rippy's is the place for you.

Located in the heart of downtown Nashville, Rippy's is a 2 floor restaurant with an open concept - meaning you find a seat when one opens up.  The service staff will get to you when they can and they'll return to you on occasion.

There is a bar on each floor, sit up on top and feel the breezes and see the great views of the city.

Be sure to get their BBQ, it is to die for.  It comes quickly so you won't get to hungry waiting.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Came here for a conference dinner. There are three levels but the crowd was huge so still people had to stand. The bars are at both levels but am not sure if the bartenders aren't accustomed to so many customers because the service was rather slow. The food was buffet and the barbecue meats were amazing, even the salmon. The deserts were okay. Nothing great. The live band and performance and the entire ambiance was so hip and fun and will make you shake a leg for sure!!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: I came here for a conference and really liked the look and feel of the venue. The inside had 3 levels and all with overlooks of the stage. There were plenty of bar stations and the venue was right near the popular broadway area. Worth a visit!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Tried this place while visiting Nashville.  Salads are listed as iceberg lettuce but it was mixed greens. Plastic silverware do not cut pork sandwiches. Upon complaining, the waiter avoided our table.  Over priced for quality and service we had hoped to get.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Went here a few months back and the service was fantastic. This time, the waitress Brandi, was more I to socializing than waitressing. I ordered the biscuit breakfast that was supposed to come with ham, and egg, and potatoes, and why I got was a 2 day old dry biscuit. The waitress ignored us for the whole time until someone at the table flagged her down. When we told her I just got the biscuit, her response was "the kitchen messes up sometimes, I don't know what's going on back there." She didn't even offer another choice, but she took it off the bill. I ordered a Diet Coke, and it was clear I drank it, and she passed the table multiple times and never offered or brought a refill. But she brought the surrounding tables their refills. Also, our baked potato was dry

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Service was absolutely terrible and the food was not very impressive. We waited a good 15 minutes for a server to come take our drink order, and then had three different servers wait on us. I will say that it was very clean and had a great atmosphere with the live music and line dancing!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
You can't come to Nashville and not line dance! We asked around where to go and were led by locals and tourists alike to Wildhorse Saloon, not to be confused with dancing at The Crazy Horse Saloon. That could've been totally awkward waiting in line with the kiddos to get into there! :)

It's a HUGE space! It was the end of our day and a nice change from the squishy Honky Tonks we had been hopping in and out of all day. It was great to just spread out and have tables readily available. The rules were a tad strange.....I believe it's 21 and over with a cover after a certain time, (I cannot remember exactly what time that was though-sorry) and we arrived just before that time, about 15 minutes or so. Despite being with the kiddos we weren't asked to leave however. Ok, whatever. I'm not going to say anything. There was no line at all when we arrived, but quite a long one when we had left about an hour and a half later. 

The bands were fantastic!! I mean really good!! I kept feeling like I was stealing or something for not paying to get into what I would describe as a full on concert with lighting and everything! I mean, this was a show! They were even selling band merch (that's the lingo those of us who have been around the biz use). 

There was an instructor who led the dancing casually which was very easy to follow, even for my 7 year old. She LOVED it!!! Wouldn't leave in fact! Really fun!

There's table service and reserved seating towards the back bar and open, first come, first serve seating on both sides of the dance floor where you can bring the drinks and food you purchased at the bar. We got a table right away no problem. 

I enjoyed some local drafts which were good and fairly priced. I got the girls fried pickles because I felt bad they weren't patrons as we were getting such a great show. They were just ok. It was a huge bowl, one I don't know who could possibly finish. In fact we gave them to the table of ladies next to us we had made friends with. I would say if those pickles were any indication of the quality of food, skip the food and just do drinks and dancing. For that alone, this place is so great! 

The kitschy horses placed all around were a hoot and great for photos! Don't miss the ones on the ceiling! So fun! The kids loved these! 

I say it's a go! 
Come at night! 
Dance and get your 'boot skoot shuffle' on!

name: Big Machine Brewery & Distillery
text: Fantastic tour/tasting led by Tommy for our large group of 11! Very cool place with a more intimate vibe than the big name bars right on Broadway.  We would all highly recommend this tour!

name: Twin Kegs
text: I live in the neighborhood and heard this place was under new ownership and the burgers were worth stopping by! They were right - I had a veggie burger and tator tots that were super great. However, I didn't love they still allowed smoking (I left with my clothes and hair smelling like it) and a pitcher of beer was $18. Previously (at least a year or two prior) the pitchers were only $6. Overall a nice little dive but I'll only revisit when I really need a burger fix, don't mind smelling like cigarettes and want a canned/bottled beer.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: My family and I were visiting Tennessee and we wanted to try a place downtown Nashville. We know someone who works here and decided to give it a shot. We were told that the food was really good and we were not disappointed! I got the buttermilk fried chicken with mac and cheese and coke slaw. The fried chicken was really good, but y favorite part of the whole meal was the mac and cheese! It was probably some of the best mac and cheese that I have had at a restaurant! We also got the fried pickles app and it was sooo good! Definitely worth the extra cals for being fried! We also loved this place because it was just plain old fun! They had live music and they even do line dancing lessons! The instructor was easy to follow and we were able to pick it up pretty quickly! We were very happy with this place!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Extremely dead on a Wednesday night and the singer was HORRRRRRIBLE!!!!! For such a big place to have 10
customers is a shame. Looked like a fun place but maybe it was the extremely cold weather or random weekday.

name: Twin Kegs
text: Best burger in town. The last of the great neighborhood bars in Nashville.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
I've been to Nashville many times over the years, lately I've been eating at Jack's BBQ. For some reason I decided to give Rippy's a try this time around, I wish I would have went across the street and eaten at Jacks.

My wife ordered the Pork loin melt on Texas toast, she ask the server about the seasoned curly fries, my wife was concerned about the seasoning. Come to find out the curly fries are frozen and pre-seasoned. The pork loin was dry, tough and had no smoke flavor. The curly fries were way too spicy for the wife.

I ordered the half slab of ribs with potato salad and baked beens. The potato salad tasted like it was a pre-prepared commercial product, the beens tasted like they opened a can then heated them up.

The ribs were an utter disappointment, they were way over cooked, had no smoke flavor, and no taste from the dry rub. The ribs tasted like they were made the day before and heated up in a steam table, which washed away any smoke or dry rub flavors.

The server was slow, she never even came over to see how everything was, I had to ask for the check. I spent a little over $30 for lunch and feel violated at the shoddy quality food. Next time I'll be eating at Jack's.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Such a great new spot! Awesome menu and good service. Very impressive whisky/bourbon selection! The artwork and design is very nice.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Never been to Nashville and I was told we had to stop in and glad I listened. A huge plus was our teenage kids could join us. The food is excellent, line dancing lessons fun, the band that night was Cumberland Run. Great music. My review would have been a 4 and what made it a 5 was our waitress Jenna. Attentive, friendly and professional. The best waitress I've had in a long while!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We stayed at the Cambria Hotel this past weekend and ended up frequenting the NashHouse for both breakfast and lunch.  We had great burger, amazing deviled eggs, and yummy fried pickles.  We were a group of ten everywhere we went so we weren't an easy table, but every waiter/waitress we had was accommodating, patient, and helpful.  We liked this place and would recommend it to others who stay in the hotel!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Came to this bar to support my friends performance. Her music was great, of course, but dude, this bar sucks. The service was horrible. I had to find a server rather than her coming to my table. We asked for menus, she brought 1, for a party of 3. I'm sitting at the table now, I am waving at her trying to get her attention. We've been here for almost an hour and she's only gotten us 1 beverage. The bathrooms are unbelievably disgusting and you don't even want to wash your hands afterwards because there was no soap or drying materials. The server does not care even care about her job at all. Needless to say, we are leaving her zero tip and not going back.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This is my second visit to a Nashville and this place never disappoints. The love music. The food. The drinks. The lady LOVELY WOMAN who is the bathroom attendant , as well as the service. This place is great! Highly recommended.

name: Twin Kegs
text: I'm a fan of this local dive because it's not only in my neighborhood, but is super chill and always entertaining. Serves beer only and has a decent variety of burgers and fried guilty pleasure snacks. My only complaint is when it's crowded the smoke can be overwhelming, but then again that's why so many people enjoy this place as well. Cheers.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Three stars for dinner and 4 stars for the band/bar area.

The portions were HUGE but the food was fine. I got the pulled chicken and it was kind of dry. For a southern BBQ restaurant I expected the food to be flavorful and smokey but it was simply pulled chicken and the table has BBQ sauce for you to put on the meat on your own.

The bar area with the band was great and had fun vibes. The windows were open and the fan was on, which we appreciated since most bars in Nashville had been very hot and sticky. The only thing keeping me from giving the bar 5 stars is the pushy band singer. Our group was not used to tipping the bands in bars and didn't have cash. When we told her this she got in our faces and told us that she had Venmo. I'm sorry but we just walked up and didn't request any songs and I'm assuming you are getting paid by the venue to be here.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I love Soulshine! It's Mississippi owned, so that's a plus. I've been twice before, once at the Oxford location. Each time the food has been great. The most recent time I had the Marley pizza and bread pudding. Both are awesome! I wish they had a bigger selection of draft beer. I will definitely come back.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I visited the Wildhorse on a site visit to hold a conference in Nashville.  I sampled their BBQ and it was awesome.  The sauces were great and the meat was extremely tender.  This place is known for their fried pickles as well.  I did try one and it was good, but not something that I would eat on a regular basis.  

There are a large number of pool tables and other bar games with plenty do space.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Awesome food and outstanding service! Ask for Shonnie, she's the best! Love this new spot. Highly recommend

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Downtown Nashville is rather dirty, but the best part of it is The Wildhorse Saloon.  A huge venue with three floors including live music, line dancing lessons, a family environment and great food.  

We ordered the fried pickles to start off.  Tasty.   I had the Tennessee BBQ duo and my husband had the Stampede platter.  Their brisket is outstanding - tender and juicy with just the right amount of spice, and the pulled pork was deliciously smoky. They offer three types of sauce - mustard, spicy and sweet all three are tasty in their way.  

The stampede platter offers the same pulled pork and brisket but adds a half rack of tender, delicious ribs rubbed with the right amount of spice and grilled with sorghum molasses.  De-Lish!

If you have kids traveling with you, they are welcome and will have a great time. Mine took line dancing lessons and left with a huge smile on her face.  Cute stuff in their shop too.  Tourist place??  Yes but worth it.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Multi-level restaurant and live music bar. Usually a very fund and high quality band in the smaller lower level bar. We had good BBQ bar food here and really enjoyed the atmosphere. 
Not fancy, but lots of fun. Can get very crowded on first floor, but grab a table if you can.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
I really enjoy this place. 

The wait is never too terrible and there is always room at the bar while you wait for a table. 

On site valet? Yes please! I love not worrying about parking. Valet staff is always courteous and prompt. (ie: these guys haul ass).

I enjoy the drinks at Soulshine but I what I love most is their casual atmosphere, live local music and tons of delicious pizza options! I also really really love that they will customize an order. Yes. I'm that girl.

Sitting outside on the upstairs (covered) patio is my favorite location. I enjoy Friday nights with Lightening 100 and I have never tasted a pizza that I did not enjoy! The names are clever - and I do enjoy a clever menu - and the flavors are always scrumptious. I go in knowing I will most likely overindulge in cheesy breaded goodness.

Also, I really like their logo/the font used for the name. 

Nutshell:
Order the "Sleeps with the Fishes" pizza. Ah.mazing. 
Definitely go. It's a cool hang.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great food which came out surprisingly fast. Especially for how large the place is and how busy it was on a Friday night. The service was on point as well.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: First time at Nash House and it didn't disappoint! Had the best time listening to Hannah Rose and the food was amazing! Chicken Fried Chicken is fantastic!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Music was great.  Drinks were a complete rip off, Rippy's? Rippy's you off, yes. Bring a ton of money.  I got two vodka tonics, $10 each for a small plastic cup...okay, to be expected.  So I ordered two doubles for my son and I as I wanted a larger cup.  Got two 12 oz plastic cups of vodka tonic, $21 each.... we had eight total drinks and our tab was $120 for eight drinks.  Holy smokes a single is $10 and a double is $21...should have called the police for them stealing my money.  Atmosphere was great, music was great but the drinks are a scam.  If you win Powerball, then go here.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We were thrilled with our Christmas Eve Dinner at NashHouse. We enjoyed the Deviled Eggs - 5 ways, biscuits and jam, and our entrees. The real winner was the banana pudding . The live music was a wonderful touch and we appreciated that it was family-friendly. Our waiter was fantastic and promptly took care of us!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Pizza was really good.  Lots of great beers on tap.  We went on a Sunday afternoon, so it was pretty calm.  Service was consistent and friendly.  I've had some trouble finding decent pizza since I moved to Nashville, but Soulshine is going in the right direction.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Was here on a Friday night of Labor Day weekend.   First the place was not filled but they had no wait staff.  We seated ourselves and waited for someone to come and serve us.  Took 30 minutes.  Had to keep reminding them that we had no service.  When we did get service, was the worst ever seen.  People dropped off food but no silverware or dishes.  Had to ask several people continually for silverware of which they said they ran out of! We got salads and no dressing.  Once again had to find someone to get dressing.  Not sure we will return.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great place to visit while on vacation! We sat at the bar for drinks our first afternoon in Nashville and Matt, our bartender was outstanding! He was friendly, professional and gave us tips on where to visit while in Nashville. He took his time explaining all about Nashville to us and the drinks were great! Excellent place!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great music horrible staff! Purposely ignored my friends and I until kitchen was closed so they wouldn't have to put in any more food orders. We wait 45 min and know asked us even if we wanted a drink.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Very much looked forward to trying out this new place--attached to the Cambria hotel--before a Preds game. We are always looking for good options for a pre-game meal, and there are plenty east of the arena to choose from. This place just two blocks west of the arena showed promise but failed in the food. 

Service was prompt, friendly. Beer selection emphasized solid local choices. Thus far so good.

But then the food. The better half found the veggie plate lacking in taste but adequate. the Cowboy burger was another matter--when it arrived it was burnt--perhaps the driest piece of beef I have had in sometime. We were shocked-- the waiter asked "pink or not"-- we clearly said pink. He acknowledged that but then the kitchen had such poor oversight that order preference meant nothing--for a $16 burger. 

Game time neared so sending it back was not an option--a reality well apparent to the kitchen on a busy game night. So they sent out a ruined meal. Shame on them--they not only disappointed us but let down their waiters who were working a big room as efficiently as possible. 

Imagine I will stay on the east side of the arena in the future before arena events

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: 3+ Super new place, it was pretty quiet on a Tuesday night when we were there, which worked out as we had a large group. I had the Nash burger, which was pretty good - could have had a bit more flavor. Friends had the catfish, which looked delicious and they enjoyed. The corncake came out like a super hard disc and we were quite sure what we were dealing with. The manager corrected that and got new ones served, which were better. Overall, the meal was pretty good, service was great and I appreciated their commitment to doing a good job. The place has a huge TV and stage right up front. It should be interesting to see how it pans out.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Very good barbecue place staff was very friendly and our food came out really quickly. Prices are good for the amount of food you get.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Really disappointed.  The restaurant was dead... only. A few diners, yet wait service was slow and dinner took forever.  I ordered Shrimp and Grits. Very disappointing.   Grits were okay but sauce was way too strong and peppery (which I typically love).  Not much food for $25!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
We were there for a work lunch.  The place is massive and full of funny full size horses that make for great photo ops.  The stage is large and they had good live music for us on a Wed during lunch.  They also do line dancing and line dancing lessons there throughout the day.

Now the food...they set up a buffet for us.  There was salad, pulled pork, baked beans and rolls.  It was ok.  The baked beans were great.  The spicy sauce that you can put on the pulled pork is nice and spicy.  The salad was not very fresh.  

They may have another menu that has great food, I'm not sure.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: I would have given 5 stars. But. The kitchen forgot to send out the appetizer. However,  the food we did get was absolutely fantastic. Zack was our waiter and was very informative, willing to go the extra mile to ensure you got what you wanted. I look forward to my next visit. In a town with hot chicken on every street. They really can compete with the best of them.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The service and food was just ok. The ribs were overdone and small for price. I left hungry! Great music venue and drinks.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The service was horribly slow. It took an hour to get a side of fries for the table. Food was good it just took forever to get it. Live band was ok but all the songs they played were slow and depressing. Did not enjoy my time here.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The food here was GREAT and the atmosphere & decor was a lot of fun.  The only thing preventing this from a 5th star is a few minor service issues, but everyone is entitled to a bad night on occasion.  I would definitely go back if I ever find myself in the Nashville area again.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The Wildhorse is a good time. Went on Saturday night, kind of early. Line dancing lessons in between band sets. Everyone gets out on the floor. Mix of country, pop, and hip hop to line dance to. The band was phenomenal (Adairs Run). My only criticism - we started out on the 3rd floor, where I'm guessing there is no wait staff. The glasses, bottles, plates, half finished just sat and were never cleaned up. We eventually moved downstairs, but it was a little unsanitary.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Just happened upon this place after sight seeing in the area. Walked in and heard music so I was intrigued. Well they were having a live broadcast for a radio station and featured a couple of entertainers. My friend and I took a seat and enjoyed great music while eating lunch. I had a mushroom burger with sweet potato fries. Both were exceptionally good. Fries were crispy and cooked to perfection. I would definitely return for both the food and the entertainment!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great place for family fun and line dancing , the food is excellent, got vip service roped off for us , saw a horse at the bar and i will post that photo soon.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: We walked into Rippy's tonight and sat at a high top table by the windows. We sat there for twenty minutes and no one came up to us to ask us if we wanted a drink. Finally my friend got up and stood at the bar to order. The blonde behind the bar would not look at her. She did all she could to avoid her. My friend then stood right in front of her and when she asked for the frozen jack and cola's, she said we only sell those on the roof then turned and walked away. Ummm what if we wanted something else then!? We weren't going to the rooftop when it was raining outside. It was completely rude and uncalled for. That's how you treat paying customers!? If ever in Nashville skip this spot! There are plenty of other places to go to.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: One of the worst experiences I have ever had at a bar. Hadn't had a single drink yet and was kicked out during a lowkey afternoon after having been there for 20 minutes. Felt completely disrespected by the manager when I asked for an explanation of the situation. Spoke to some people sitting at the bar who said they thought the food was horrible as well. Definitely plan to skip this one.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: We ordered through Door stop Delivery. We waited a while to receive our order and when we got it, it was COLD! The breadstick tasted like they had been sitting for awhile. The pizza COLD.
