WE are not far from the restaurant and it should not have been delivered cold for the price we paid. They upcharge their menu prices for delivery,which we already pay a service fee and delivery fee. I am very disappointed!! WILL NOT BE BACK

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
This is a bar you MUST visit at least once during your visit to Nashville - especially if you're having a night out on the town. Located conveniently on Broadway, Rippy's is a fan favorite. The live music and beers are constantly flowing - and with that comes the singing and dancing of all that love and adore Nashville. Their rooftop is probably my favorite feature, especially in those summer months. And right across the street is Tootsie's, so after your wrap up your rooftop singalongs, you can stumble (I mean ... walk) onward to the next hot spot. ;)

Please note -- I would not opt for this place just for dinner. Choose a 5 star meal in Nashville (there are plenty!) and THEN make your way to Broadway for your shenanigans.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Food was pricey and mediocre at best. Would not recommend . Server was friendly, but wouldn't go back .

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: I was in Nashville for the first time and only for 2 days. I didn't have too much time to explore in the evening but had to at least try to see the Broadway nightlife. We walked around a bit as we could hear talented musicians from just about every venue. We passed by Wildhorse Saloon and heard amazing music coming from the inside. We felt as if we had the privilege of attending a free concert. The music was great and the drinks were very reasonably priced. They also had one dancing lessons every couple of hours. Great quick exposure to the Nashville scene.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
So I'd be lying if I didn't say this is a pretty cool venue.  It's huge, with tons of seating and a large space for line dancing.  We were seated on the main floor, because it wasn't particularly busy on the Sunday night we chose to go, but the upper floors looked pretty big, and the balconies for each floor were lined with chairs for viewing the dance floor and stage.

Every hour and a half or so, they would invite anyone and everyone up for a line dancing lesson, and then after would bring up the band so you could continue your newly learned line dancing moves.  The musicians on this particular evening were really good; we stayed long enough to see both their acoustic and full band set and enjoyed them both.

OK, so the venue is cool, dancing is neat, bands are good, so why only two stars, you ask?

All these good things cannot make-up how lousy their menu is.  It's a small menu, choices are limited and prices are high.  My husband and mother-in-law got their chicken and biscuits ($16) and both had to load up on salt and pepper to make it edible.  I ordered a pulled pork sandwich ($12), which was bland and dry and could not be saved by their (disgusting) BBQ sauce they have sitting on every table.  I've had better BBQ pork sandwiches in southern Ohio for under $7.  Also, my sandwich came with a horrible hodge-podge of french fries.  There were curly fries, and waffle fries, and some sort of seasoned fries.  Literally it was all of my least favorite fries thrown together and served to me lukewarm.  I was NOT happy.  

I'm clearly an idiot, because I decided to order a dessert to try to fill me up, since I couldn't choke down my fries or sandwich.  We got their chocolate toffee mousse cake.  The "toffee" part of the name is referring to a minuscule drizzle of caramel over a sickeningly rich slab of chocolate.  I was splitting this dessert with my husband and we didn't even finish it.

Our bill for two bland entrees, one deceptive dessert and a tip for mediocre service was $45.  We didn't even drink because, GET THIS, a cocktail is $16.  I DON'T CARE that it comes in a souvenir glass, I'm not that kind of tourist, and it just puts me off.

Come for the dancing, come for the music, but don't come for the food.  You've been warned.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
I give 5 stars for the history in this place. Country legends have performed here for many years and at one point this was the place for aspiring musicians. If I remember correctly, Randy Travis worked here many moons ago. Reba performed here, among many others. 

It's decent in size and good for large groups or parties. It's also close to the airport and Opry Mills. If you are next door at the "Cooters"  Dukes of Hazard Museum, then it's worth adding to your stop. 

As for the food, I have nothing to rave about. This place needs vegetarian options badly.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I thought the whole wheat crust was delicious on our pizza. The crawfish soup is to die for! The service was good, but not out of this world. The Pig nachos were delicious as an app. Everyone left feeling full and happy. I would go back for sure.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Came here on a snowy Tuesday night - wasn't packed at all.

Ordered a full slab, beans and coleslaw.

The beans were pretty good. Coleslaw ok. Ribs were pretty dry and didn't really fall off the bone. I wouldn't say tough - but borderline. Certainly not great.

The live music was pretty cool, though they pester you with the tip bucket (and they ask you twice if you don't have cash on you) which fan seem a little unfriendly.

I'm sure this is great when it's full of great people and music but tonight it really wasn't a hit.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Another brunch in Nashville, The Sutler calls it Bluegrass Brunch on Sundays. I ordered a coffee along with chicken and waffles. We arrived a little after 10am, party of 8, and we did not have to wait. Always a plus! Chicken and waffles were delicious! Our server was very attentive. Check out all of their brunch menu with many options for food and beverages. I have not been there for dinner, but I have heard great things. Keep it up!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Wait a minute--affordable pub style food in an unpretentious atmosphere that gets you in and out in a reasonable amount of time on lower Broadway?! Yep. Want a great burger, tasty chicken tenders, salty fries or a host of other satisfying options pre- or post-drinking or event you've found the right place. I'm always looking for good, quick fairly priced food in this area when I come to an event at Bridgestone or elsewhere in the neighborhood as there is so much of the opposite in abundance. Lower Broadway is tourist central and they know it--and hence charge for it. If I'm going to a concert or event of my taste I don't neccesarily want to get deafened by music I don't care for or go bankrupt for a sandwich and a drink prior to the show I came for in the first place and Paradise Park Trailer Resort had me covered.

I had the bacon cheeseburger with fries and a side of mac 'n' cheese---I know, a lot of cheese salt and carbs but I was starving and hadn't eaten all day (and this hit the spot). You can make that a double but after seeing the generous portion they served me I was thoroughly glad I had kept it to a single patty which is more than enough to suit a reasonable person. The patty was juicy, the cheese was melty, the bacon crisp---fresh lettuce, tomato, onion, pickle and a great bun with some good sauce and bam! The fries were super salty but tasty, fried up in peanut oil (ala "Five Guys") with a bottle of vinegar to coat them if you so desire. I added the mac and cheese which was delicious, real cheese with cheddar flavor.  My wife opted for the buffalo chicken tenders and was surprised at how meaty and good they were for bar tenders, they came layered on top of tots which were crispy and great. All of that for less than $25 (on lower Broadway)! So many places in this neighborhood charge twice what they would if located anywhere else in the city so it was refreshing to eat something good before a show and not be gouged for it.

There isn't a waiter service---we made our way in through the bar having passed up the actual restaurant entrance so it took us a minute to realize you placed your order up front at the counter but that works great here. They call your number (fast service), you grab your food and you're on the go after you take your time enjoying the meal. Gaze at the "mullet wall of fame" , velvet paintings and various trailer park motif if you want. There is (or at least was when we were here) an open mic style music thing going on in the bar area next door but unlike some of the neighboring joints it's not cranked to 11 drowning out your conversation and appetite. I realize this is "music city" but as someone very selective on what country music I can handle this is often a deterrent in hanging out too long in the touristy section of town. Thankfully we have Paradise Park right here for something different that locals can dig. I have a lead on similar such options in this part of town and will be checking those out soon as well.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Great homemade bloody mary! Brunch was OK, but baked cheese grits are worth a return visit. Service and music both great as well. I would go four stars, but the food was a bit sub par.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
What an awesome, iconic spot in Nashville. If you don't know the history of this place, it's worth checking into - they have a good synopsis on the menu, which of course I neglected to get a photo of! This was one of the major sites of peaceful protest in the American Civil Rights Movement, and is really a famous place to visit for that alone.

Of course, the food is what lured me in, and it did not disappoint. We had our college-age kids with us over a weekend, and we needed a brunch spot on Saturday. The city was packed (holiday weekend), and we could not get a reservation anywhere. Fortunately, these guys had bar seats open, and it's a great bar to eat at so we took a shot. Good move! We had the corned beef hash, which was really tasty and had huge chunks of corned beef in it. My daughter had the fried chicken salad, which I didn't taste, but she said it was amazing (and it looked to be the case). I ordered the sweet potato pancakes, which I usually don't do (carbs-o-rama) but they were very likely some of the best pancakes I have had in my life. I'm not exaggerating. If nothing else, order one plate of them for your table and share - you will not be sad you did. 

We had a lovely brunch Bloody Mary (great) and Greyhound (also great), some coffee, and a lovely time chatting with the bar staff. Would definitely go back here, for sure. 

Only reason I took off a star is because I do feel they're just a tad overpriced. Coffee was $3, for example. Not grossly so, but enough to where I would not eat here that often if I was local.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
This is a great casual place to get really creative and above average bar food. They have a decent beer selection, but their cocktails are just okay. The atmosphere is a little kitschy, but it works. The servers didn't really know much about food and especially didn't know anything about the cocktails or beer list. 

We ordered the fried pickles and okra, which was pretty standard but very good. I LOVED the bacon popcorn. 

The grilled cheese was good, but I was not a fan of how it came sitting in the soup. Next time, I'd ask for the soup and sandwich to be served separately. I also did not love the tomato soup because it was much sweeter than how I usually like it- this was just a matter of preference, since a few people at my table loved it. 

The roast beef sandwich was really yummy, but a little mild on the horseradish and blue cheese - some people may prefer that! 

Overall- I think the food is great. What this place needs is a ramped up cocktail program, and it would greatly improve the experience.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Great brunch guys! The atmosphere is a bit off but the food and service are great. I like the tofu options and the chicken and waffles are good too. I am excited about trying more of their dishes. This one is on the short list.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I gave the Bluebird 3 stars because the food and service was really great. The song writers, so disappointing! If I want to hear shitty pop country, I'll listen to country music radio. I was expecting my visit to inspire and show real country coming from people's hearts. Instead, I listened to overplayed pop songs about being "the girl next door" and "baby daddy drama" seriously. Shits weak! I saw better music at the local dive for free and didn't need to make reservations. All in all the Bluebird is unfortunately overrated.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I love this place but coming in for brunch is quite a hassle. It's always so crowded which is clearly great for the owner but there isn't much place there hang while waiting an hour + for a table. The food is fantastic and 98% of the staff is great but when it comes to the hostesses, it needs improvement. Theses ladies don't smile and have attitude when asked about things. 
If you're going have a community table please close the gap so you can get more people seated. Don't let the customer keep an empty chair in between them and the next person just bc they do not like sitting beside strangers! It's a community table!!! Also, can you please start carrying moscato wine? Brunch is perfect with moscato! 
Cudos to great food, drinks and atmosphere!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: We attended the CMA Fest last weekend and immediately saw Paradise Park upon our arrival. It looked entertaining and enjoyable but unfortunately, we did not have the best experience. Although, the instruction sign was clear on how to order and pick up food, there was a negative vibe with no greeting or further direction from the front cashier. Thinking it may have just been a bad day, we continued to pay and wait for our food. We realized the number display was not working and instead, the cooks were calling out numbers for food pick-up. We weren't sure how long it's been this way or if it was actually normal, but it seemed a mess to us. Food was being wasted from not being picked up or given away to other customers for free. Our order number did not match the order given to us and we had to wait for almost an hour for two hotdogs, and fries. The food itself was amazing, and the rooftop atmosphere would bring us back. Just hoping after the planned remodel, there will be a better experience.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Easily one of the top bars in the South. You can go there anytime of day and listen to some amazing music. You don't need to be a country fan to enjoy Tootsie's and Nashville. The staff is excellent and the prices are cheap. I had 3 beers and my bill was 9.00 on a Monday afternoon. Fri and Sat nights the crowd is having a blast.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Wow - this place is truly one of a kind! I'm so happy we were able to get tix and experience the Sunday night singer/songwriter session. All of the artists were phenomenal and I enjoyed the quiet, intimate atmosphere with everyone giving their full attention.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Bought tickets to the hot chicken and jorts fundraiser event which was really a good time and good way to say goodbye to the place. Only problem is the next day I noticed the bartenders had taken it upon themselves to leave a $20 tip on a $12 tab. Currently disputing with the credit card company. Hopefully these awesome people aren't hired elsewhere in the city.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
nice service, good beer and top music!
the rooftop its verry nice! i love it! we go there on 11 AM and its play a live country band! thats cool!! i definitly come back!!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Giving 3 stars because i have attempted to eat here 3 times but haven't had the chance- worst parking situation in town.  The $3 for valet says, "yeah, we know it's garbage but we don't care"... It screams amateur for a restaurant that should average $50/cover.

If you are the landlord reading this- designate some parking for your businesses... It's a key to success with multi-use.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Two words: bottomless mimosas.

The food is priced correctly and the mimosas were strong! Bottomless for $17 is really quite the deal, and I'm so excited I found this hidden gem in Melrose.

I had the the andouille hash with their complementary biscuits and, OOH GIRL, the food was delicious! With great live music, amazing service, and reasonably priced food and drinks, I'll be back numerous times.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsie's is a must
Every floor is lots of fun
Rooftop is a beaut

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
We love performing at The Bluebird on our tours through Nashville. Steve Goodie is an amazing Sunday host and it's the best listening crowd in the country!
Watch our music video here:
https://youtu.be/X01MtEiuNP8

Whitherward
www.whitherward.com

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Really cool vibe! They have different cocktails upstairs & an entirely new menu downstairs. Get your first drink at the bar and then venture downstairs for your second. If you're going for dinner, go early and ejoy the cool basement vibe. It's upscale but casual. Most weekends they have live music. So glad this great venue is in the Melrose neighborhood!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
When it was much warmer, a group of friends and I came here to enjoy the Bluegrass Brunch, which features live Bluegrass music on Sundays from 10AM-3PM. We came around noon and the wait was about 30+ minutes but they had plenty of outside seating for us to wait at so it wasn't bad. 

Once inside, we were able to snag a booth right by the open window, which was perfect. Our server made great recommendations and was attentive. The live music was a nice touch and not too loud for us not to be able to talk to one another. 

Since I'm an unapologetic lush, I immediately zoned in the Bloody Mary Bar, which allowed you to pick your choice of vodka then have your gander at whatever fixings you want. I went with my beloved Tito's. The Bloody Mary Bar is located to one side of the stage and had a good variety of hot sauces, seasonings, celery, olives, and dried meats like pepperoni and salami. Honestly, the only thing else I wish they had was slices of bacon. They also offer $15 unlimited mimosas, which was very appealing. 

Honestly, I don't recall too much about the food. Let's just say we had a boozy brunch. I know I ordered an entree but by the end of finishing my Bloody Mary loaded with all my favorite fixings, I don't think I ate very much of my actual food. 

Overall, I would come here on a nice day to grab a seat by the open windows and enjoy an afternoon brunch.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: I would give this less than one star if it was an option. This bar is super cliché, and while it could be a cool concept it is poorly executed. The staff here is terrible. The guys at the door are super douchey. Don't waste your time choose bar that better fits what you're looking for. If you want a true Nashville experience with live music go to tootsies. If you want bad food and bad service come here.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Great atmosphere with okay food. I ordered the Cheeseburger with Fries and it was okay but no where near the best burger in the world. After I ordered I noticed that the cashier did not ask how I wanted my burger cooked. That is not a good sign.
 But this place serves food late night and has live rock music which are a big plus.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This was my favorite spot to drink and see/hear live music in Nashville. Very happening place with very attentive bartenders and awesome live music. The bar itself looks old and kinda nasty but if you're here to have a good time it doesn't really matter. They have multiple levels with bands on each floor. Would definitely return if I ever come back to Nashville.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Place is filled with pretentious hipsters who are too cool for anything. I assume the chef is too cool to cook since I am sitting at the bar for over an hour for a glorified grilled cheese with turkey. But at least I am now getting 2 beers at a time? 

The Sunday Brunch gets great reviews. The Thursday sandwich dinner-not so much.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: We just stopped in for a quick lunch, it meets the perfect description of a dive bar. The bar itself had, of course, great live music. There is a separate dining area so you can enjoy your food in a quieter area. We were pleasantly surprised to find that the burgers were amazing. No complaints here!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place was pretty rowdy and full of 20 something's looking to get drunk. I couldn't even hear the music over the screaming bachelorette parties. If you're looking to get bombed this is the place. Lol

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Reservation system is the worst.  Waited online in the queue for 18 minutes (exactly as instructed) and when I was redirected to the site to make my purchase, was greeted with "sold out".  This is for a week night show.  VERY irritated.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
We were so excited to go check this place out until we finally went in and were so repulsed by the smell of rotting grease? Beer? Something rank! We turned right back around.

Thinking they should replace the green carpet through out the bar with something a little more sanitary. :(

name: Tin Roof
text: Had Donatello's Toast for brunch and was extremely surprised at how good it was . The atmosphere of this place was phenomenal. Extremely unique , free arcade games and board games while waiting . Very unique and food was delicious.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Ate a burger here yesterday and am now dealing with the WORST case of food poisoning ever. Seriously guys, if you're thinking of stopping in here, do yourself a favor...keep walking.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
I.love.their.brunch.

The boy had chicken and waffles and I was so annoyed! You know when you order something and then realize after it comes that you should have gotten what your dining partner ordered. Yeah, that was me. I kept trying to steal his food. Not that what I ordered was bad, his was better!  What I ordered was the BBQ pork omelet. My problem with the item was that there was too much pork in the omelet and that they seemed disconnected. I think I would have liked it better if it was BBQ pork served with two fried eggs, eggs over-easy or scrambled. That way the items could mix in harmony. What ended up happening was that I unfolded the omelet and ate the pork out of the middle with the potatoes. Even so we were on the back patio and it was great. Relaxing, calming, and sipping on a mimosa in a mason jar, I was content. It's almost two totally different venues when you eat out back. Next time I plan on trying the enchiladas. I hear wonderful things about them!

Beyond brunch we went for the Kentucky Derby. The place was packed, the bartenders were hustling, and the ponies were racing. Mint Julep in hand I watched my horse not win. (wha whaa)

Overall I'm a huge fan of the Fox. I left feeling like, but why, why must you be so far away from me?? I would come here every weekend if I could! Instead I have the honey drive me. (It's on a short list of things I will drive too.) The prices are great and they really pack the schedule with things to do, see, or listen to!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We spent the weekend here with friends - finally decided to go to Tootsie's hearing that it was a famous place and fun.  We went up to the 3rd floor looking forward to having some fun.  The bartender "Taylor" that waited on us had attitude from the beginning. We ordered our drinks, one with just a splash of cranberry - she made it with a lot of cranberry.  then we gave her a $50 bill and she gave us change for a $20 -  when we asked her to remake the drink the way we asked and then corrected her on the amount of money she gave us back - she rolled her eyes and gave us attitude- and I don't mean a little bit of attitude.   She then started talking back to us being rude and obnoxious - we asked her name and asked to speak to a manager.  She proceeded to call security and they refused to bring us a manager - and escorted us out without hearing our side of the story and getting us a manager.   As a couple in our 50's and not trouble makers we've never been treated in such a manner and under no circumstances will we EVER step foot back in that hole of an establishment or tell anyone to go there.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Typical honky tonk. Bar goers say it's one of the best bars with live music on Broadway. It gets really busy on the weekends. And it has rooms with live music.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Great local hideaway.

Came in on a Wednesday had a pint,, $3 porter unheard of!

Live musc was just what I needed


4* just because of the $5 cover but hey, everyone has to eat !

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
A cool place to hang out and listen to some music.  I wish there were places like this in Miami!  Alas, the culture is very different down here!

If I am ever in the area again, I'll be back.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
I love the Stone Fox, and I especially love that it's in my neighborhood! I've visited twice now within a couple of months and look forward to going back again. 

Both times I have received excellent, personalized service. They're quick with suggestions and information, as well as explaining the different beers they offer to my husband. 

If you're there for happy hour times, be sure to ask for their Small Plates menu, because the flatbread pizza is where it's at! Their homemade chips are pretty much the best, too.

We're not much into the live music scene, so we make sure to visit when we know they are not performing. Our latest visit came during a sound check, and I know for sure that our choice of times to avoid live music was spot on, as you can't hear anything but the music when there. If live music is your thing, then you definitely need to go during those times, because the music we heard sounded great, but we were there to visit with family. The sound check didn't last long, so it worked out well for us. 

I hope to visit soon on a weekend for brunch, because I hear that they serve an excellent brunch. They serve chocolate gravy. Can it get any better than that?

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Awesome spot on Broadway! This place is small but was pumping with a great band on a Tuesday afternoon, female singer was standing on the bar performing!  Bartender was attentive, quick, friendly  as soon as we walked in. You share tables with other guests but it's fine bc everyone's happy!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Gourmet food with a come add you're ambiance! ! Nevertheless, I 'd urge to let them know to go easy on the salt! ! Amazing and exceptional menu !!!!!! Yummy !! Highly urge the trout! ! Yet tell them to go easy on the salt, all of my friends loved it, but it was a little salty, other than that, great setting! !!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Loved loved loved bluebird cafe!!! The music was wonderful, the group had such amazing chemistry. I am hoping to come back again soon.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: This was an awesome nights. The wait staf was great and ver helpful. They even moved our table for a better view. The artists were friendly and honest with thier stories and songs

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
When I went here we heard really good things about this lounge from the desk clerk at our hotel. I was excited because it seemed a like a very cool place. When we got there there was absolutely no place to stand downstairs. The place was completely packed with people standing right next to each other. You could literally see the sweat in the person in front of you. It was hot and very uncomfortable. The drinks were pretty good if you could get to the bar. We only had one and then left because we couldn't handle the zoo. 
On a positive note however, the music upstairs was really good. The band was high energy and really got the crowd going. If we could have gotten our drinks amongst the mass amount of people we probably would have stayed to listen to them.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Entertainment was 5 Star. Dillon went above and beyond to make sure the group I was with was safe and had a great time! He was also the one that greeted and wished us a good night when the bar closed.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Anywhere that breaks the rules and stamps my hand at 7.00pm instead of the stated 8.00pm is A-OK, this meant we were paid and guaranteed entry in case it was a sell out but could go off elsewhere until 10.15pm.  A small but perfectly formed venue with tables and a lounge area.  The sound for Meadownoise was great as was it for Tristan's release party.  A packed venue with a front and back patio for a gasp of air.  The menu had enough to please the veggies including , Mac and Cheese $9, Bimibap $10 and Fox's Hot Chicken $12 and Fish and Grits $12 for the res of us, The cocktail list was lovely and   well crafted, I guess I am saying I had preconceived ideas that were way off the mark.  This was a delightful surprise, a young crowd on the whole but a good vibe is a good vibe, wish it was on the East Side.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Came here for the fried pickles that other reviewers mentioned, only to find that they aren't on the menu. Ordered some cheese fries instead. They were ready in 26 seconds but I was eating raw potatoes. Also, the band was incredibly brazen, demanding $30 to continue playing the song they strummed a few notes of. Someone caved in to their incessant bullying, and then the lead singer announced that they didn't even know how to play the song and would wing it. He sounded awful - I feel bad for whoever wasted their money to hear "Africa" tonight!

Stop in for drunk food late night, otherwise keep on walking down Broadway.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Fast service, but drinks are really small - barely cover the bottom of the cup.  Maybe that's good, considering that most people around the area bar-hop, and it's not their first drink. Good fun music and fun crowd.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: We made our way into the bar around 430 on a Friday afternoon. The band playing was excited to see our bachelorette party walk in, and immediately invited the bride up on stage. The main singer was encouraging the playful banter with the bride, but eventually flipped on a dime. He flipped after the bride took his hat and put it on her own head. Apparently that was a trigger point for him because he immediately put his hands on the bride and physically shoved her off the stage. Half of the bridal party left the bar immediately while the others finished their drinks. While the other half was still there, the singer told the bar "f*** those girls" as they were still standing there. While walking on Broadway to the next spot, multiple groups came up to show their sympathy for the situation. They had all left after watching that incident play out. Overall, the singer was a very poor representation of a bar that came highly recommended. Hopefully, the bar recognizes this and takes the appropriate action to address the disrespect of their hired entertainment.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: A classic, but also a shit show.  I think there are three stages, one way in the back, one upstairs, and one near the entrance.  Crazy big and busy.  Definitely a must stop for an out of towner.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Great spin on corned beef hash! Best flavor with a combo of hot sauces (Texas ketchup and ones name I can't remember that taste like Tabasco). Has corned beef chunks, sautéed bell peppers and onions with skillet potatoes, black-eyed peas, 2 eggs cooked of your liking and I chose a corn muffin. Worth writing about.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: We came in the other day as we always try to do when we come downtown. Love the food and the atmosphere and that it doesn't cost an arm and a leg to get a beer! But this time the bartender Tawny, was fantastic, she had such an outgoing and fun personality. I tend to be critical seeing that I'm a long time bartender (which is awful, I know) but her service was on point. I hope to see her again next time we venture out!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: We were looking forward to a nice meal while in Nashville and unfortunately did not find it here. I truly cannot write anything good about the meal, staff, or cleanliness of restaurant.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
This place is awesomeness except the seating 
Which holds 75 they turn away business 
Every 2 hours I'd love for them to find a bigger 
Place but from what I'm told they like doing 
Business this way anyways the band's are 
Always great and the service is awesome

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Well, crap. I wanted to like this place, but it's really not worth it - at all. First of all, service is rude - from the get-go. We were in line, and dang if someone who works there didn't just cut everyone off and order a bunch of stuff. Here, you order up front (from someone who wishes they were anywhere but there), and then go find a table. We did that, and while my husband was watching our stuff, I went over to the other side to the bar to get us each a drink. So, instead of the usual 2 drink limit per person, there's a 1 drink limit per person. Each of us had to go get our own drinks - even though we're over 50. This is just a dumb business plan. Food was only o.k.. He had the chili, and I had the Paradise Patty Melt. There was supposed to be a "board" where your number would be shown to let you know your food was ready. Wasn't working, but the kitchen staff didn't seem too concerned. Customers were looking around - wondering whose food was up there getting cold. Unfortunately, this will go on my list of places to never go to again in Nashville.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Came here on the recommendation of the Blue Collar Comedy Tour Bus (or whatever that thing was called).  We were told that it was the best burger on Broadway, so we figured we'd check it out.

This is more of a fast-casual type of restaurant- you place your order at the counter in the front and then pick up your food in the back.  We went on a Saturday before a hockey game, so it was pretty busy.  We probably waited about 20 minutes for our food.

We sat down on the bar side of the place.  There was a live band, playing hard/classic rock covers.  While it was a nice break from country music, I wasn't really a fan of the band that was playing.  However, I did enjoy the meal.  My husband and I both got a singlewide burger with sweet potato fries.  This meal was a good value for the price and quality.  I'd definitely come back for the food.

I had to give three stars, however, because I just didn't like the atmosphere.  The band was too loud for a place that was more of a eating-type of a place.  And it just wasn't a very comfortable place to eat a meal.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: The line scenario is a joke. Lie, cheat and steal to be in line 1 or you just wasted 2 hours of your life standing in the sun. There are plenty other places for great live music. Would not recommend the experience.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I have visited once before and had a great time.  Unfortunately your reservation system is crap and site does not process the demand adequately.  Half loaded pages, table selection, bogged down, etc.  Terrible experience that obviously causes frustration and now general disinterest in your bar.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Don't take your backpack, they won't let you in. Seems silly, being smack bang in the middle of Broadway you're going to get a lot of tourists popping in, some are going to have bags from shopping (what's the difference?) - we weren't staying centrally to drop anything back. It's a small backpack, no bigger than a large handbag really. I just use a backpack now because handbags hurt my back. 

Maybe next time Tootsies! I've heard great things about you!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I would give it 4 stars but I didn't really know the cultural and historical importance of this place. The place is very cool looking, and the music is excellent, but I personally didn't think it was worth waiting 1.5 hours. There was a $12 entrance fee plus a required $7 purchase minimum. I wish I was able to appreciate the venue, but it's hard when I didn't grow up listening to southern music.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: They need to train these servers. The host/wait staff is a hot mess. The hostess grunted at us and threw our menus on the table. The server was incompetent. I asked what blancos tequila they had and her response was "I don't know, a bunch I can't pronounce." GIRL BYE. She didn't offer to go check or ask or even write them down so I could read them myself. She suggested I just order the tequila that someone else at my table had ordered. Still have no idea what it was. And when it came out, I sipped mine which was disgusting then compared to my friends which tasted normal so either my glass was dirty and still had sanitizer in it, they started pouring the wrong drink or someone just put something in it. Cool. I would have sent it back but we were ignored the rest of the night. This place sucks.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Prepare yourself because this place get's pretty packed, but I can definitely see why. The talent is through the roof, this place has several levels. The view from the rooftop is absolutely amazing. This place pretty much represents what Nashville is all about. The entertainment, drinks, and the crowd equal a great time.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I had to wipe vomit off my shoe after leaving this place. Tourist trap. The music was descent but the bar staff were very rude and inattentive. Ew.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Had a ladies night with BINGO (mondays) at 9 and 2-4-1s til 10 and we had a great time. Although I didn't order any food, my gal pals really enjoyed the Pimento Sandwich and the chicken tenders basket. I was all about the drinks, well drinks to be exact for the 2-4-1 prices including beer. Both drinks I ordered, a whiskey & ginger and gin & sprite, were surprisingly strong :-) And at 2 drinks for $5 i made out pretty well! BINGO was really fun and with a packed house, there was definitely excitement in the air...who doesn't like prizes from Grimey's??? I'll definitely be going back for the food!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Totally divey, but cheap beer and the band actually had some talent to speak of. (Playing electric guitar with glass slide, good. Going around with a bucket and hitting patrons up for tips, not so good... just sayin)

Drank a local beer called "Jubilee" and chain smoked in the front window with some friends while listening to live music. I consider that a win.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
The vibe of this place and I didn't mesh.  It had a hipster/preppie thing going on and there was a large party that was a little tipsy.  I got the impression from the look on our server's face it wasn't the usual.  The hot chicken was ok, and husband's gumbo wasn't anything exceptional.  Felt the beer was a bit limited given other options in town.  

Fun renovation and great location for the area.  Happy I tried it, but probably won't be back.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This was a great venue to visit for a night out. The three floors have all bars and room to dance and live bands that will make you shake rattle and roll. The bartenders are on it and you don't have to wait long and some bands even take requests. Such a good time and lots of talent

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Food was great! Atmosphere was great! Bartender was awful. Not only not great at managing a busy bar but bad attitude! If you don't like your job DON'T bartend.  Especially in Nashville.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Woolworth was an interesting experience. I ordered the gumbo and deviled eggs for my appetizer. The eggs were great but my the rice in my gumbo was not fully cooked. The waiter replaced it in a timely manner. I enjoyed the short rib for my entree but it was a little salty. 
    Although the food left more to be desired, the service was spectacular.  I also enjoyed the facilities.  Don't forget to tour the mezzanine for some superb photographers of Nashville's history.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Definitely a happening place. Crowded, multiple floors, multiple live bands. It gets a little too noisy and crowded at times. The bar doesn't sell bottled water or iced tea, so if you don't want alcohol you're stuck with soda. 

There are girls all around selling beers, with not so subtle signs asking for tips.  

Definitely go up to the various levels to decide what band you like best.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Really enjoyed this place. They have a nice roof top bar that's great when the sun goes down and it isn't as hot. Very attentive bartenders and the music was good too. Good crowds and fantastic people watching

name: True
text: True is a good size open space great for listening to live music several nights a week located on the 5th floor of the Cambria Hotel.  The bar is set in the back of the room opposite the stage, with windows that open to allow for outdoor seating on one side of the bar.  The patio also houses the hotel pool, so it gives off a party atmosphere during high season.  We stopped in to listen to some local music and have a drink and appetizer.  First off, they had me at Guinness on draft!  Definitely a check in the plus column.  It was happy hour, so we ordered two drafts and the fried green tomato/mozzarella small plate.  The appetizer was nicely presented with alternating layers of tomato and cheese with a green goddess drizzle.  My only suggestion is that instead of the raw red onion slices on top, I think peperocini would add much more flavor.  We had a nice time and my husband paid the bill while I was in the bathroom so I didn't see the receipt until we'd left.  Now for the check on the negative side.  We had been charged full price for our drinks and appetizer, although we had ordered off the happy hour menu for all items.  So we ended up paying about $10 more than the bill should have been. (we also bought a drink for someone else which added to our bill).  So definitely check your bill before paying to make sure they honor the happy hour prices.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: If I'm going to say anything I am going to say that the bread is absolutely amazing. Best bread I have ever eaten in my entire life. For my meal I had the fried chicken and it was OK as far as fried chicken goes. The drinks at the bar were delicious and the atmosphereis really neat! Our server was great too!.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: I went with a group and was kicked out for no reason and offered no explanation other than a very rude "have fun somewhere  else" by the security. I was ejected so quickly I didn't have time to notify the group I was with that I had to leave. I have a few folks that can vouch that I was in no way being belligerent or doing anything to warrant the way I was treated. This was my worst experience on Broadway so far and I'll be "having my fun somewhere else" permanently.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
A friend and I went to here on a recommendation while visiting Nashville. 
It was a few flights of stairs to get to the bar. On the Saturday night we visited it was JAM PACKED. Literally could barely move at all. Despite this we someone managed to get beer very quickly. 
We did notice the patio seemed fairly open. We walked towards it but were told by a bouncer they only let a certain number of people out there at a time. We waited in line and watched others make the same error we did it only took a couple minutes for us to make it outside. 
The view was incredible. It was a panoramic of the Nashville skyline. Across the street was where the Predators play so there were larger than life posters of attractive hockey players. 
There was a large bucket with beers you could purchase outside without going back in. I paid cash but I cannot remember if they accepted cards there. 
We couldn't hear the music outside (which had been very good) but we could breathe. Awesome place overall.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Good bands...couldn't really get over the no weapons sign on the door or being wanded, the chilly was good but drinks more than the competition.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: If the food was cheaper, I'd give it a 5. This is the place to have breakfast in Nashville! I'm not one to pay for "ambiance", but this place has it. The food is good, service is excellent, but I lucked out and sat next to a regular, who attends the place consistently. Also, there was piano playing in the background. What a treat. This place is a treasure. And read up on the history, so if you don't know, now you know.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Disgusting service and good. Do not eat here. I was recommended by some friends and it was a horrible experience. Absolutely awful.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I wanted to like Woolworth on 5th. I have been to every other Tom Morales restaurant in Nashville and Franklin and have liked them all. I hope tonight was just a bad night for Woolworth on 5th. The hostess was aloof. When we arrived 5 minutes before our reservation, she coldly said "Have a seat and we'll call you when your table is ready." The chicken was dry and the order was wrong. The manager stopped by and asked how it was. No discussion when I said "OK." He said "Great," so I guess OK is the goal. Fortunately, Nashville has many restaurants with loftier goals.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Such a great bar and authentic.  Bartenders are very attentive and musicians are great.   Bathroom attendant was aggressive and uncomfortable.  Drink there.  Don't pee there!!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The food was not good. The meatloaf has been thrown on the grill to be reheated. The mac n cheese was hard and not good at all. It was greasy and the brisket looked like dog food. The service was amazing, super sweet girl. She cute too. The food was garbage. Sorry sutler. Local Nashvillian not impressed

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsies rooftop is fantastic when the sun is shining! Live music was fun inside and the bartenders were helpful.  Friends got food and they really liked what they ordered - quesadilla egg rolls and chili cheese hot dog.  Classic place check it out if you're in Nashville for the weekend/downtown.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Loved this place 
Had the best time and great music.
I saw five or six bands here over three days.... all were great and the place rocks !

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Love what they are doing with this historic spot. My feeling echo previous reviewers. As a Nashville native I'm thrilled that this spot and all it represents can now be enjoyed by everyone in the community. 
On the morning of my visit I went with three friends, we each ordered something different. There was fried chicken, pot roast, an entree salad and the sweet potato pancakes. All the food arrived hot from the kitchen, correctly plated. Our server was pleasant, professional and knowledgable about the menu. The menu itself covers the basics but not much more. Choices are limited. I can see the value of keeping things simple given the reality that Nashville has a shortage of cooks and wait staff. In the end, I was glad I went and I think most who care about this city will be glad to support their efforts.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Annoyed with this place. Came for my bachelorette with 10+ girls and bought drinks for hours. On the way in and out the bouncers told me to go get a free bach shirt and after waiting 20 mins on the way out the manager told me the new promo ended 20 mins ago and wouldn't give me a shirt. When I told him his staff sucked at communication he agreed that they said that but that they were wrong and too bad. Changed my whole experience

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: 3 great bands playing in one place (different floors). Rooftop was very nice also. Must visit if you're looking for live music

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Went for brunch, have to say, food was excellent, music was awesome, our bartender (we sat at the bar) was super friendly. Met some nice people that came and went at the bar, great bloody mary's and think they have some special on mimosa's, I see on someone else post that it is bottomless mimosas!  I will definitely be back here, really had a nice brunch experience. Crowd was from 16-60, really nice energy, they really have a nice place going here! Much better feel for Nashville than the Broadway experience, great place to bring out of towners!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Best food ever!!!! I had the roast beef and it was out of this world amazing! The atmosphere was incredible. Also the history of the place was so inspiring! I can't wait to go back for breakfast.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I didn't eat here, but I was able to go inside. Very cool set up, great history, and awesome to get to visit in person....(I have seen it on the tv show Nashville). It was a must go and see while visiting Nashville because of the tv show. The manager was ridiculously friendly too!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The staff and chef need to eat their own food. Yet another Nashville restaurant serving crappy food at high prices. The Waldorf Salad was disgusting. Presentation was beautiful but I spit out my first bite. It tasted like a vinegar salad. I sent it back for one without the dressing and it came back tasting worse. They must have tossed the fruit in straight balsamic vinegar and it was also extremely spicy. The server acted like we were a bother so I boxed it up and threw it in the trash when I got home. My husband had a burger that tasted like it had  half of a bottle of salt in it but at least it was real beef and other than the sodium was tasty. The fries were great (salted to the extreme) but really, who can't cook fries? The server allowed me to have one glass of water and never offered to refill it until I finally asked for some more. The atmosphere is awesome but the greeting and seating leaves a lot to be desired. The music was the highlight and why we went but if I ever go back, I will not eat.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Pretty cool place! I love the boots on the ceiling heading downstairs towards the "speakeasy" style lounge, which is my favorite area of the venue. Perfect for a chill night out with good music, food, and not too bad of pricing.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Must try the sauces, they are fabulous. Had the carrots and roasted beets as well as the sweet potato soup...both were yummy. The squash sandwich was really good too. This all coming from a veggie. Not disappointed a bit.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Lol. Love this place but despise this place, ew.

This bar is so gross... but so awesome. Green carpet that has people's lost dignity soaked in it, beer in bathtubs, and the wood paneling on the walls makes me want to take a shower. However, the bands that play here know how to rock a crowd. This bar is one of a kind and my experience here is awesome. I also ate here two nights in a row around 2am (yikes). They have good late night food that's generally fast and priced well. 

Not sure if I'll be back, but this is a sober review now y'all

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great music and great times. I love visiting Tootsie's. Always a wonderful experience!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Such a cool bar. If you've never been in a trailer or trailer park, this is your chance. Service is usually quick and the music is the same as all over on Broadway. They give out free beer before the Preds games if you're going to the game. That's a win right there. I've never had the food here but I definitely don't go to Broadway to eat. From what I've seen, it looks decent. Just like the other bars on Broadway, this place fills up on the weekends. There's always room in the back area by the restrooms. Getting back there can be a challenge though.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
3 levels of live music
no cover charge
BUT must tip the bands that play
Nice character of the bar with old pictures all over the wall and thousands and thousands of notes handwritten on the wall.
Have a patio out on the 3rd floor with a nice view of the broadway
Drinks are cheap
Crowd is fun
Busy even on a Tuesday evening.
If this is your first time in Nashville, a must drop by for a drink and listen to some good ol' country music

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Most lively bar on a Tuesday night. And I mean lively. Rooftop was packed shoulder to shoulder. Singers here were really, really good (and we didn't love EVERY singer on Broadway). 

Walls on floors 1-2 are littered with history. What's really cool, unlike Legends beside it, is that a lot of the photos are of country music legends of old actually singing INSIDE Tootsies. Most authentic bar on Broadway for sure. 

As a male, must wear sleeves after 7pm!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
We came to the Monday night showing at 9:30pm. This show didnt have tickets you could reserve in advanced, but was first come, first serve. Knowing this, we arrived at 8:15am to stand in line. We were the 1st people there. While we were waiting outside, the earlier open mic show was still going. We knew that the cafe would be cleared out after open mic to make way for those of us waiting for the next show. While waiting, a couple walked up and asked if we were in line for the show and we said yes. They asked when the doors were supposed to open, so we told them 45 minutes from now. The woman got upset because it was raining and cold, so she went inside and the staff allowed them to get a table but also didnt make them clear out before the next show. Meanwhile, the rest of us stood outside in the rain. The staff should follow their own policies about who gets in at what time.

Secondly, I asked the door man if the cover change could be paid with a card. He said " we prefer cash. We will run a card if that's all you have, but we won't be happy about it". Nowhere on the website does it say cash is preferred. They finally let us in and I go to pay my cover and the cashier woman says "I can't take your card, you need to pay cash". I told her the other guy said card was fine and she replied "well, I have no mechanism to run your card with. There's an atm at that bank over there." I asked her if we could choose a table first and then get cash at the atm since we had been standing outside in the rain for an hour to guarantee a good viewing spot and she was pretty exasperated at this idea but let us do so. Apparently the card machine stopped working right before they let people in, but she never explained that or apologized. She was super rude

Lastly,  apparently on Monday night they have a reduced menu. This is not mentioned online. The choices of food are limited to 1/3 of the menu that they have on their website. We didn't eat dinner in preparation for being able to eat at the cafe and based off the choices of food they list on their website, so to limit our choices to chicken strips or fish n chips was just misleading and annoying.

The band gets 5 out of 5. They were funny and incredibly talented. The best musicians we heard during our time in nashville. The cafe staff however could use some customer service training and learn that the patrons are the ones who keep you in business.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Band was great, room was packed. The atmosphere was awesome! That was until it came to interacting with the employees. I sat at the bar and it was literally impossible to complete my order with bartender, Tony. Initially, it took quite a bit of time to get him to even acknowledge me. As i began to order I was cut off and he walked away. Then, a few minutes later, came the first thing I was able to say. Then quick walk away. This continued for another 30 minutes until I was finally able to order to other items of food. When I noticed the people next to me who ordered a similar item get my food before me, I waited a beat, then had to ask for my food.. which apparently was never prepared. After this I went to the merch counter to get a couple items. The best way to describe Molly at the merch counter starts with a C and ends with a T. I have never had anyone be so blatantly rude to me by asking a simple question about a t-shirt style - to the point where she wouldn't even look at what shirt I was talking about. She rolled her eyes at me, gave me serious attitude and snarky responses. 

This place would be great if they restaffed with polite, customer service driven individuals. I don't plan on ever going back to this place.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: If you're looking for a perfect brunch place, this is the one. I absolutely love their bluegrass brunch, it's such a cool atmosphere and everything is absolutely delicious. We try to come any chance we get!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Naturally I had to visit one of Nashville's most historic spots. Woolworth lived up to all my hopes with its rich history and delightful food. If you don't know this is the location of the Nashville sit ins during the Civil Rights movement. Those original stools are still there today.

Woolworth gives you a great experience with interactive service and food that will have you coming back for more. I tried their salmon and it was perfectly cooked and came out in 20 minutes. They also have a great drink menu so be sure to check that out as well!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
We were here last night and had a blast.
The band was very talented and the atmosphere was awesome.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
If you were planning to go to Nashville I highly recommend you put the Bluebird Café on your itinerary.  It's one of those places that you drive up and go, "this doesn't look so special", however it had to be one of the most spiritually wonderful and intimate cultural experiences I think I've had traveling in the US. 

It combines all the great things about Nashville into one place, wonderful music, spiritually enchanting, pretty good food and all-around soulful fun time.  It is very much a great date night, but will be great cultural experience for the kids too. It is what Nashville is all about, not to commercialize country music you hear on the radio today.

Be sure to book your tickets weeks before you go. As we were told we completely lucked out being able to get in the same day we thought about going. The place is always booked up, but the secret is to getting there early on the day you want to go. Be sure to look at the website for times  http://www.bluebirdcafe.com

They take a total of 10 extra people, first come first serve after for the 6 o'clock show (Doors open at 5 PM). There's also a later show.  The trick is getting there around 3:30 PM and getting in line.  Dori and I got there around 3:50 PM and we were number 9 and 10, however 11 through 15 got to come in as well sometimes they make special accommodations. However by 4:30 PM there were 50 people in line.  

The folks that showed up to play, were accomplished musicians as well as accomplished songwriters for some of Nashville's greatest singers. I have to say, John Scott was there, and was absolutely fantastic. I have paid hundreds of dollars for tickets for other singers, that do not compare to him.  His presence and his music was incredible. Be watching for him I think he's going to be big...

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I literally just had the best chicken sandwich of my life... in fact I'm only halfway done eating it and had to stop to leave this review.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Attended a networking event at the Sutler. This was my first visit. We partied downstairs in the cellar.  I was thoroughly impressed with this setup.  A cozy little gem I've been missing out on.  The bar is huge. It practically stretches the length of the room.  The bartender is fantastic and pleasant. He can make anything you dream up. I didn't get his name but he was cute :-) The wait staff was wonderful, friendly, attentive to the large group, and provided great service all night.  We ordered I think every appetizer on the menu and they were all delicious.  Our event took place on a weekday night during happy hour.  As we wrapped up, there was a bad setting up to perform. I was so in love with my new discovery that I hung around to hear what the band was all about. At least I tried to. The band never played and it was almost 2 hours after their supposed start time. A little disappointed I finally left but will definitely return to try and catch the next one. The Sutler is a beautiful and inviting hang out for great libations and spirited laughs.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Eh... overrated. Three floors. Expensive drinks. At least the bartender was super friendly and pretty!

name: Tin Roof
text:
BOUNCERS SEXUALLY ASSAULTED MY GIRLFRIEND!!!! 

!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

If its friday night and you and your friends are looking for a night out, I beg you avoid this place at all cost. I can not stand for a business that hires employees which such vulgar, demoralizing, rude and sexist attitude towards its customers.  First of all, my girlfriends breasts were touched and frisked by a large black male around  6'3" (seemed to be a bouncer, very beefy man with a beard). This all happened while we had first entered the building. We walked through a group of bouncers who had the smell of alcohol on their breath. They proceeded to catcall at my girlfriend, which infuriated me. While walking through their group one of them grabbed my girlfriends left breast. Fuck them There is nothing more unprofessional than employees being intoxicated on the job. Apart from employees being drunk and having wrapped their hands around my girlfriends breast, they also threatened and insulted me when they accused me of  having a fake ID and I argued in my defense. After all this, I tried to leave and as I did the employees tried to "kick me out".  On top of all this the venue is shitty and gross. Do not give your money to these scumbags. Friday night was ruined.  An added note, this place does not mess around with fake ids, but they do take bribes if you are trying to get your Fake back give them 40 bucks. -- ILLEGAL

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Everything on broadway blends together after a while. But I really liked tootsies and here's why

1) great music-- I liked their variety better than some of the other places on broadway 
2) great service! The management found my wallet that was stolen the next day and were very helpful and cordial dealing with me 

Otherwise, be warned this place is quite popular so it DOES get very crowded so weigh that when choosing a place to go on a typical Nashville night. Overall a great time

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Bring lots of cash if you plan on a long drinking stay. Drinks are extremely expensive.  Alcohol drinks are a minimum of $9 a drink.  That is for non call booze. No food just liquor. It is truly a tourist trap bar with. name recognition. 
Have a drink and move on to the next tourist trap. All prices have really increased since my last visit. 
Only 2 stars because of pricing of alcohol and lack of value. As I walked into the door I and other customers are instantly chased down to get a drink order. Appears they have been trained to make sure everyone buys one of there small expensive drinks. 
Buyer beware of this property.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Now you can't just walk into this place without taking a few minutes to learn its history. This place has seen everyone from Pastry Cline to Waylon Jennings to Willie Nelson (who got signed after playing there). Being open almost 60 years will do that for you. It's named after the owner and it still has her friendly charm. When we stepped off the downtown sidewalk into this place there was a crowd of people with a beer in one hand and giving us a high five with the other. I knew this was a place to have fun. The first floor is a little tight on space, but you learn to make it work. The second floor was just as rowdy and fun. On the rooftop, you get half covered and half open air space. Your view is of all the neon lighting up Broadway. A full bar is ready and serving the first two floors and bottled drinks are offered on the rooftop. There are pictures of anyone who is someone in county music on those walls. And it feels like your neighborhood bar, where you could hang out all night singing and drinking. It is a Nashville must.

*Insider's Tip
-Take the time to hang out on both floors and the rooftop. They will all have a different band playing.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I love the Sutler.  Best late night food! Good music. Fun pool lounge downstairs.   Mac n cheese is yummy

name: World Music Nashville
text: An excellent music school and shop with dedicated teachers and staff. All ages welcome, a real asset to the Bellevue community!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: LOOOUD but fun!  I was bewildered by the fact that the singer on a Saturday night was using her phone to remember song lyrics.  Moonshine was great.  I know because I can't remember.  That's how you know.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
I love this Honky Tonk bar in downtown Nashville! I had the BEST time here!

Since we were only able to spend 1 day in town, I wisely chose 2 spots to get my "country" on. I wanted a good ole' dive bar with great music, cheap beer and a rustic atmosphere. Whiskey Bent Saloon met all my criteria! We arrived at 1230, shortly after the music started, when it was pretty empty. That didn't last long because the band was fantastic and quickly drew a large crowd. Even though it was busy, the bartenders were great! For some silly reason I wanted a bloody mary (what the heck? It's not Sunday!) and she made a really good stiff drink. WooHoo!  Mike was enjoying his beer and we moved to a table on the floor. Who was playing? I didn't know but they played great music! We laughed, we swayed, we drank! 

Whiskey Bent Saloon is as good as it gets!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Jenna is an amazing waitress. She is a true professional of the craft. Her service alone will make me come back!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Great service and an amazingly broad selection of whiskeys and bourbons. I wish my liver could stand to stay here all night and try them all.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Came in with some girlfriends, so fun!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Rock Til The Drop New Years Eve 2018-- paid $150 per ticket, 9pm-1am. Plus: Fun crowd and good choice of premium liquors. Minus: stood in line for 45 minutes to get to the prepaid rooftop, 7 tables--standing room only, one bar with three bartenders, and limited snacks. The Hard Rock did not seem at all prepared. The shoulder-to-shoulder action was much like any other on lower Broadway. Note: the note drop and NYE show is now at Bicentennial Park. Nothing new to see from the rooftop.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Came here with a group of friends while visiting Nashville, and we had a great time. The drinks were decently priced and it was easy to get served (aka not overly crowded, which can be a big issue at some Honky Tonks). The band that was playing was actually good, and they drew us in with country music, but it was clear that they were not actually into country, so they kept covering old rap and hip hop. Not my style, and not what I expected, but the rest of the group was pretty into it, so we stayed for at least an hour.

When it's warm outside, it's REALLY warm inside- the further to the back you go, the hotter it is. There's a small upstairs area that I would imagine gets roasting by the end of the night, so I'd stick as close to the front (and the open door) as you possibly can.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I went here on a date, it was nice, the food wasn't bad! :)

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The Sheraton at Music City is a well-kept hotel with convenient access to the Nashville airport and highways, serviced by friendly and attentive staff. There is ample free parking for guests, and a sizable outdoor pool and gym. Having ordered room service, I can highly recommend the buffalo wings but would caution against the steak as it was a low-quality cut of meat (not as advertised) and the accompanying French fries arrived soggy. My room was clean and orderly, and hallways were quickly cleared of any room service trays and bags of garbage. I took advantage of the continental breakfast in the Lounge, and was pleasantly surprised by the substantial and well-prepared food options. Besides your typical coffee, milk, juice and cereal bar, the buffet included pastries, well cooked bacon, fresh fruit and delicious sausage/cheese/egg breakfast sandwiches. The lady responsible for bussing the lounge was polite and efficient, always quick to serve and assist the guests present. I highly recommend you consider this hotel when you are planning your trip to Nashville, customer service is top notch and the location is very convenient.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Awesome honky-tonk! They have bison mounted on the wall, big barrels to represent whiskey (or crackers, or checkers), and a good amount of space to sit at. The Sprite was given to me quickly and I had a good time with the tourist visitors.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Fun, live music. Loved that they had a girl singer in the band. We had a large party and had a little VIP treatment for the deck upstairs, a little more private and the bartender helping us was very helpful and attentive.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Well-rounded CLEAN Nashville hotel that will be nicer than you expect BUT didn't get 5 stars because it's not the W in downtown Chicago & doesn't have free coffee available in lobby which is key to the success of my family vacations. *Note beer & coffee loving foodie IT husband (on that same note they need more local craft beers on tap.) WiFi costs $9.99/day if you don't have Starwood Preferred or aren't in the lobby. 

Love how all parts of the hotel have smelled amazingly clean! The large fitness center & indoor heated saltwater pool & jacuzzi were surprisingly clean. Our room was lovely & clean. There is ample parking & a cheap ($10 round trip) shuttle running downtown. 

I can not comment on value because we came for free as part of a work conference. Although we weren't terribly impressed with the restaurant (see my seperate review), the catered in house meals were better than expected. So far we have had pastas, breakfast, hamburgers & hotdogs. 

Staff have all been helpful & kind, especially housekeeping. Make sure you request a crib early if traveling with small children on a weekend. We got last one on a Friday at 1 pm. The balconies are a nice plus. Great location for Opryland pursuits. The beds are comfy. There is no microwave or refrigerator in our room. 

Overall, I haven't stayed at a Sheraton in awhile but I'm enjoying this stay & would recommend to relatives in town who want to avoid fuss & headaches of THE Opryland hotel. Thanks for the great family memories!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: We loved this place! The live music was great, the bartenders we super attentive and the prices were slightly less than the other bars on the strip.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I stayed here for the BlogPaws conference. I was not stoked to get here as Sheraton is not my favorite, but I was pleasantly surprised. The rooms were standard for a Sheraton, but nice enough. Room service menu about standard -- nothing special. 

But the service is what makes this a 4-star instead of a 3-. I'm pretty picky. I want what I want when I want it, and the team at the Sheraton accommodated every request. Ryan at the front desk checked me in, and greeted me by name every subsequent time he saw me. That's a touch I would expect from a much higher-end hotel.

I think another time I'd pick somewhere downtown, just for convenience, but this was perfectly reasonable for what it was.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: We stopped by for a drink and watched the band. It was pretty crowded on the night after Xmas. Not sure if the people are mostly locals or out of towners...it was cool but I was not super impressed. However I did get to see some crazy country dance moves.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
We took our youngest daughter to Nashville.  Many of the live music venues are bars, so she couldn't get in.  We thought Hard Rock Nashville would be fun.  We've always had good experiences with Hard Rock, except for this visit.

The live music there was really cool, but the service left a lot to be desired.  Even though the place had a large number of empty tables when we walked in, we got greeted by a snooty hostess who thrust a pager at us and simply said "45 minute wait".

It was about that long of a wait.  I found myself and family standing virtually alone in the front lobby with all the other guests getting seated.  I finally walked over to the hostess and asked how much longer It would be.  She looked at my pager and said she had paged us but that the pager must have been turned off.

We were literally standing 20 feet away.  Why didn't she care enough to walk over to us and at least check on us?

The table she sat us at was right next to the bar, kind of in the way of the bar patrons.  I asked for another table and was told we couldn't be moved.  

Food was just OK.  I had the margarita flatbread.  It was really salty, heavy garlic and was very skimpy on tomatoes.  My wife got the nachos.  Skimpy toppings.  My daughter got the cauliflower burger with parmesan fries.  She liked her meal alot.

Overall, 3 stars mostly for something that can be fixed...service

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
To the two married dudes who were hitting on girls all night and paying for all of their drinks at the bar the weekend of June 5. Gross. I may be describing quite a few...not just two. But the two of you. Ew. Totally EW.

That said, this didn't feel like a sleazy place. Wouldn't have felt uncomfortable unless I wanted to.

Other than the interesting people watching, I had a great time at The Stage. Really liked the staff, they made the rounds frequently to clear bottles and glasses. And that was a lot to keep up with. The music was good. Probably not the best that I heard on Broadway...but heck music is going to be hit or miss in Nashville, and all a matter of preference.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Stopped in on our way to myrtle beach! Food was absolutely delicious, we both had Jack Daniels burgers! Decor was modern and nice, was busy but they got us seated right away! & we had the BEST waiter, on his name tag it said "Yas qween". Good time! Only thing I have to say is that I expected a little more music memorabilia for Nashville!

name: FooBar
text: Hey pretty cool bar. That plays good music. But if you get the tattooed bearded bartender, he will ignore everyone at the bar and joke with his friends all night you literally have to scream at him to get you another beer completely incompetent. What's the point of tending bar when you're not going to tend to anything

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Great experience here. Staff was responsive and helpful, and the stuff they offer kids to do is way more than just a few crayons and a piece of paper.We used our hard rock coloring book at many restaurants after this trip!

Food was good, drinks were amazing. A really nice place to stop in Nashville especially if you're with kids and don't want to bring them to the local honky tonks.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Such a fun bar!! Very nice people that work there. The bands were amazing!! Thanks for a wonderful weekend Stage!!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Very nice place, very clean and worth the money. They have two restaurants inside the hotel and room service. This will be my place to stay whenever Im in Nashville

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Wow. Really had a bad experience tonight. Made reservations on line for dinner on the roof top during karaoke which I included the specifics on the reservation. Called to even make a change with the number. Arrived tonight and told that the rooftop is private party only for $15 each. Hard rock could have called or even done a better job explaining but the hostess was so rude we left and went elsewhere. Why wasn't it advertised anywhere as a private party. We are on vacation and made plans around this. Very disappointing for a well established place. Unfortunately our family has a goal of visiting all hard rocks in the US. We are calling this visited. Really sucky.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This place was totally awesome!!!! Absolutely loved it! Cute atmosphere and the bands were awesome!!! My favorite place on Broadway!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Came here late night Monday. Nice gathering of people from tourists, students, to musicians who had just finished their gigs. What was really cool and unique about this place was the freedom in how the stage band could interact with the audience. The lead singer even invited some of the musicians and singers in the crowd to join onstage. We all enjoyed some guest performances!

The bar staff took care of everyone and were friendly to chat with. Will return when back in town. Thanks for a good time!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: The food was really good when we got the food. It took a long time to receive the food. The waiter was very absent-minded. They did not know what they were doing as far as waiting tables. I'll food was cooked to specifications. The waiter seem to think that comedy was the way to wait tables. Apparently he was mistaken. This was an extreme disappointment.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Had lunch with parents here, had lil rock burger and ribs, was pretty awesome! But my dad ordered ribs and thought its steak Hahahaha, that was pretty funny

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: One of the best honky tonks on lower Broadway along with Whiskey Bent! Their beer prices and drinks are still reasonable compared to all the bars that Dierks Bentley, Shelton, FGL and Aldean are opening!! These places are a downright rip off!!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Was having a great time with 7 people.  Late in the night we order drinks from 3rd floor bar and the female bartender rudely she doesn't want our 3 dollar tip on the 4 beers she opened.  Will never go here again.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
So this will be my third review of Whiskey Bent Saloon. It used to be a solid five stars. The bartenders, bouncer, and band were all great when I first started going here. Since then, the staff has changed. This two star review isn't meant to call out any particular people, but in hopes that Whiskey Bent can improve and maybe even become the bar it was several years ago. For starters, the drinks are way too expensive. I don't want to pay $6 for a beer when top shelf liquor costs the same price at other bars. The bartenders also need to speed up their service. If there are only three people at the bar, it should not take more than ten minutes to get my order.
