Finally, the bouncer needs to accept all legal forms of ID at the door (e.g., passport, global entry card, etc.), not just a driver's license. Not everyone has a driver's license.

Fix these three main issues, and I'll give WBS at least a four star rating, or maybe even five, depending on how much improvement there is. I still enjoy coming here on Sunday nights because the band is awesome, but if it wasn't for them, I'd probably just stay home or go elsewhere on Sunday nights.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: 3 stars cause I enjoyed the rooftop outside patio view and live band. Outside patio gets a different menu verses dining inside you get a bit more option. Basic american food. It was okay. Our server was new and she didn't know anything about the menu or if it was even on the menu. Our food took forever to come out. And we just ordered wings. They do have valet parking if your not wanting to look for parking.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Fun bar! Try the blackberry and/or Blue Raspberry moonshine cocktails. Great, relaxed atmosphere. Friendly bartender and musicians.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The hotel was beautiful! The rooms were clean and very roomie! The staff at guest services were very friendly in helping us choose things to do around town. Definitely will stay again when in town.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
A group of 9 (finally) 21 year olds stopped here for our first bar in Nashville this past weekend & we had an absolute blast. While it was pretty crowded (like every bar on Broadway during Summer) we ended up near the front of the stage which only makes it more fun.
The band we saw was so great (Johnny T) & a lot of fun. Drinks were normal priced for Broadway & bring lots of cash because these bands deserve it!

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Gimmie that sixth star. This place is fscking unbelievable! Their smoked wings are, bar none. The best wings I've ever had.five of us got the brisket, pork ribs, beef ribs, chicken and sausage. It easily would have fed double. The food is incredible. Go here right now!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
the bartenders are attentive. however I can't say much else good about the place. the doorman security staff are absolutely ignorant and rude.. for example I was trying to walk upstairs one of them stood there in my way with his leg on the stairs and would not move

the band was unimpressive partly because you couldn't see them with a column standing in the way. we stayed in line about a half an hour to get into the place it really wasn't worth it.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: This location is not within walking distance of anything you will need during your stay.  The hotel staff are very friendly and always eager to please.  This location would be perfect for large scale events or venue style gatherings.  For a one night stay in Nashville I would recommend checking what is close by.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I chose this hotel for the 24hr hot tub.  This may sound strange, but given that I was going to be on the 3rd leg of a long road trip, I chose to pay double the price of the newly renovated Four Points Sheraton in order to be able to soak my road-weary joints after an evening out seeing Nashville.  
Imagine my surprise when I discovered a locked pool door since their policy (but not their website) changed 2 weeks ago.  I was back in my room at 2am to practically participate in the activities next door which were as audible as if room divides did not exist. This frisky couple was up and back at it at 8, and then thanks to the obviously lacking walls, conversations were also shared between rooms.  
When I arrived I couldn't park in a close or well-lit spot due to conference guests, but at night there is a driveway guard who checks your name to insure you are allowed to drive up (and considerably more available spots). 
The courtyard is pretty, and our breakfast server was fantastic.  
I really wish they had walls, and that they updated their website when situations like 24hr hot tub access change.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I am not exaggerating when I say this was the worst dining experience I've ever experienced. I must've been there during a perfect storm, because I can't believe anyone could give this place 5 stars. It was completely mismanaged. They were out of so many foods, I thought they were joking. The food I order at every hard rock (so I know what it should look & taste like) was a joke: dried out hard chicken chunks, no sauce on my pasta... I wanted to send it back, but our waiter disappeared for 15 minutes, so it was basically cold before I could even get it fixed and start eating dinner. During those 15 minutes, my friend still hadn't gotten her NACHOS, that she'd ordered initially, and should've been out with my food. The waiter finally showed up with her nachos, but they weren't what she ordered. He said he'd fix it, but disappeared for another 20 minutes. Meanwhile, the rest of the group was done with their dinner. They finally brought out her nachos & my remade pasta, apologizing that it was because they ran out of chips. They couldn't tell her that earlier?? Offered to get her ANY other food as she sat there watching others eat? We talked with the manager afterward & got our dinner covered, but it still wasn't enough to make up for the disaster of the evening. Did I mention it was my friend's first time ever at a Hard Rock? Yeah she'll never go back to one.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I was surprised to see this hotel only has a 3 star rating on yelp.....I definitely think it was above average.  First of all, it's BEAUTIFUL. Decor and woodworking and interior design are on point. It was very clean. 

PROS:
Cleanliness
Decent beds and pillows 
Cheap shuttle to downtown 
Nice pool weather permitting
Good fitness area
Multiple elevators 
Spacious rooms

CONS:
Expensive subpar breakfast
No fan in bathroom 
Found old dog toy under the sofa....have to wonder how well they clean 
A little farther out from the city than you'd think 

I personally think the pros outweighed the cons!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Great place to people watch & rehydrate/refuel.

Service was prompt & efficient. Can't go wrong with fast food! Sit outside on a nice day or inside & watch the footy at the bar.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Went to The Stage this past weekend during a bachelor party, this place is a lot of fun.  Drink prices were actually the cheapest of the 4 or so bars we went to on Broadway.  I think I paid $4 for a bottle of Bud Light.  The live music and atmosphere here is fantastic.  I'm not sure of the band who played on Saturday (06/15), but they were fantastic and very entertaining.

Word to the wise, there was a line to get in which I thought was worth the 5 minute wait, however the inside was PACKED towards the front of the bar where the stage is within The Stage.  You will have trouble moving through the mass of people, but if you like a less crowded area head towards the back.

Great times were had, and memories were made.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: My girlfriends and I visited this place on a Saturday night and it was really cool. Just like any bar on broadway on the weekend, the bar was understaffed and slow and we were packed in there like sardines, but this got better as you went up each level. There were 3-4 floors (can't remember exactly) and each one was its own bar with a different talented band. The top floor is where we spent most of our time, posted on the rooftop at a table overlooking broadway. We loved it and I would love to come back.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
Make sure that when they ask you where you are from, you don't actually tell them. They are asking what bar you are coming from and if you answer wrong they won't let you in. Stupid considering no
One was in the bar.,

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Having a great time, no cover,  and sodas were free for my dad who doesn't drink or they didn't charge.   The alcohol drinks are a little expensive but you have to drink whisky in TN if given the chance. Have a wide variety of liquor/whisky and a few good beers.   Wish they had a couple local drafts.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: There's great fun to be had at The Stage. I love country music and don't even mind the new pop-country songs. The cover band that played the night was great--played song after popular song--and kept the energy alive. I went for my sister's bachelorette party so we got pulled on stage to sing Brown-eyed girl and that made my night! Great place to come to with a big group on friends. Not a whole lot of places to sit so wear comfy shoes--or boots to be more appropriate.

name: FooBar
text: I somehow remember enjoying this place more before I lived here. It's really close to our house so I'm sure we'll be back. It's just really smoky inside and I'm not into dry cleaning my winter coat because "let's just go have A beer" when I can have multiple beers at my smoke-free house with no dry cleaning bill.

name: The 5 Spot
text: When this place advertises to close at 4 am, don't believe it. Walk in the door, "we're kicking everyone out! Y'all need to leave!" While there's 30 ppl standing in the bar. They wouldn't even let us stand inside to call another uber while it was 20 degrees outside.. #notafan

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Great live music, bartenders were attentive.  Small venue but awesome. No food which is fine. We went on a Friday night before NYE and the place was busy but not too packed.  Had the apple pie moonshine and loved it.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Nice presentation of the food but the food it self wasn't that great. I ordered a chicken sandwich and the chicken was hard as a rock. My first thought was "is there something in my food" but no it was the chicken. How am I supposed to enjoy this when I can't even eat it! My waiter was overall nice but the person who seated me wasn't as friendly. 

Glad my fries were okay it's something that always I could eat but I don't think this is a place I'll visit again.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Staff is less than accommodating.  Didn't have our reservation.  Then questioned our reservation before admitting that they made the mistake.  They have no official transportation to downtown.  I would not recommend staying here!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
I think we came here everyday. Both in the afternoon and at night, and the stage did not fail us. 

If you're hoping to be impressed by some live music, come to the Stage! We even heard an electric violinist and she was truly the cherry on top.  

people in the front are always starting a dance party and on the back you'll have the chance the sit down and relax. Either way, you will love this place!

name: The 5 Spot
text: My partner and I had came here randomly walking around five points and was not disappointed. We had a chance to see local funk group called Funk Good Time which was absolutely amazing. They really know how to pump the crowd up. In addition the crowd was quite diverse with all ages and ethnicities. I had an amazing time there and would definitely go back. At the time when I went I had to pay cover but regardless I would recommend

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Rude!!! Dont go here, waitresses are rude and snobby. Drinks are watered down. Go next door to Tootsies.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: On Sunday night, their Valet came flying out of the driveway in someone's car without stopping and almost hit me.  I honked my horn, and the guy jumped out of his car screaming!  He called me a "FAGGOT"!  He's lucky I didn't shoot him when he leaned in my window screaming at me.  He told me "FUCK YOU FUCK OFF!"  Then started mocking my southern accent.  This guy has some serious anger issues and needs mental health treatment.  He needs to be fired before he gets your business into some serious liability by crashing a patron's car or assaulting someone.  I mean, he easily could have hit a pedestrian and killed them the way he was driving.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We have been to many Hard Rock cafes and will continue in other cities but I will never go back here again.   Visually we had twenty plus tables open and yet waited 35min to be seated.  Once seated our server ignored us for another 15 minuets walking by twice.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
I was on a long weekend trip to Nashville from Maryland (13 hour drive). While my wife and I were walking Broadway on Sunday, we stopped in Whiskey Bent Saloon. Not only was it one of the nicest bars we walked into in Nashville, but I found a tshirt that caught my eye and I just had to have it! Unfortunately they didn't have my size and we returned home with no shirt :( I was hooked on that shirt though so I emailed them and asked if it would be possible to order one and have it shipped to me. It was a long shot but I figured, why not try?

The next day I received a phone call from the manager Zeke who couldn't have been more accommodating. I paid for the shirt and shipping and got it in the mail 4 days later! However, when I opened the package, I was slightly disappointed when it was the wrong color. Could have easily been my fault as I didn't specify a color to Zeke on the phone, but non the less, wasn't excited about it. 

I contacted Zeke again and BOOM!, he comes through once again! Another 4 days later and the right color arrives in the mail! I know, it was a stupid tshirt and he could have said he didn't have time or not even returned my message. But the customer service I received from Zeke and the Whiskey Bent Saloon was second to none. Hard to find that nowadays. HIGHLY recommend!! Can't wait to get back to Nashville next year and enjoy a cold one at the Whiskey Bent Saloon.

-Ryan

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: We were staying for an event on property. We had booked 2 double beds for our room, however upon arrival we were given a King room. When we stated we booked a double, the response was we're completely sold out--which explained why while we were waiting to check in we were hearing the FD staff calling for roll-aways to rooms, and then also stating it was their last one. So they had oversold our block--not our fault, shouldn't have been our problem! Thank goodness the other 2 people that were to be traveling with us had stayed home or we would have had 4 people in a King bed! This agent did the best she could, apologized, and even told us to help ourselves to anything from the shop before heading to bed. It was very late at night, there was no manager on duty, so we requested that they call us in the morning about this matter. That never happened. Due to weather conditions when we were leaving our flight out was canceled, so we called the hotel to see if we could book another night. The front desk girl who answered was so rude, I don't know why she would work in a hospitality position or customer service, she clearly doesn't like helping people. She said there was no way they could get us another night under our group block rate--even though the block was still going on. When I explained our already unpleasant experience at check in, she gave me an attitude and when I asked to speak to the manager, she said there was one, but that I couldn't speak to her! I work in hospitality and in hotels and this is the kind of employee who should find a new industry. Here we were stranded in an airport needing another hotel night and she had the opportunity to be helpful and compassionate and instead made sure to give a loud sarcastic "Have a Nice Day!" before hanging up when she heard how dissatisfied I was and that I said I'd be sending a letter to Sheraton about our experience. Our group had more than exceeded the block of rooms and brought in a huge amount of revenue to the hotel for the weekend and this was the final experience we had with them. I gave it a 2 because the event staff were very friendly, and the bed was very comfortable. However on our last day when we were exhausted and wanted to sleep in after a busy weekend, housekeeping started knocking on our door at 7:30am!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Great music, fun servers. There was about an hour wait, which we expected on a Saturday night. When you first walk in, it's really hectic and the staff seemed to be really scattered and flustered- They even forgot to give us a buzzer at first! 
We waited at the bar and probably should have just ordered our food to eat there, because it was a little longer than an hour wait.
Once we were seated, our server was fun and gave us really good input about the menu. our ONLY complaint about the menu was that the brisket was sold out. (it was only about 7:45) 
They then ran out of glasses- just as I had ordered another drink. I was almost done with my meal by the time I got my new drink. You would think that a large restaurant like this would be prepared for a huge rush. 
Other than that, the atmosphere was fun and it was a good place to start our night.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
The Stage is a fun, casual bar. We stopped in on a Friday afternoon for a reprieve from the heat. Apparently there is a bouncer checking IDs at the door, but I walked in without getting my ID checked. Since I didn't have my hand stamped they still checked it at the bar, though. The beers are about $5 or $6 a piece, even for domestic, which seems a bit ridiculous to me. I guess that's what you get for going downtown, though. 

The live music is what really sets this place apart, though. While we were there, the band was playing some well-known country songs, but based on other reviews it seems like they play other genres as well. The only drawback of the music was that it made it difficult to have a conversation with the people I was with. 

If you are looking for a fun, casual place that has a definite Nashville vibe, I would recommend The Stage. Whether you're a local or a tourist, you are guaranteed to have a good time.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Worst customer service I have ever received from Sheraton Music City Hotel and I haven't even made it to the hotel yet. I booked it through priceline.com and made a mistake when it came to the dates. I booked for 1 day prior then what I needed. I called the hotel directly to make the change and I was first told that I was out of the window to make any changes. This was strange to me because I booked not even 5 minutes prior to calling. I was put on hold and was then told since I booked through a third party there was nothing they could do for me. So I called Priceline and their solution was to call the hotel and have them move the date or authorize refunding the reservation so I could re book the reservation. The priceline representative told me the manager Kate was rude and said that they would not authorize a refund and would not allow me to change my reservation. I asked the priceline representative what could be done and he forwarded me to the customer relations department that was going to try and help me as well. She spoke with another front desk manager who said they would have to speak with the revenue manager Mike. I had to call back to see what the resolution and Mike offered to move my reservation for a mysterious amount that they couldn't tell me what it would be until I got to the hotel to check in. I'm hoping this is just a bad dream and someone from priceline.com or Sheraton Music City Hotel will contact me and help me get to a resolution that makes sense. If not this has by far been the worst customer service I have ever been subjected to.

name: The 5 Spot
text: A 4-star dive bar!  Not smoky inside, which is a huge plus.  No country music here, more of a place for local jam bands/punk.  Drinks were cheap and staff friendly.  Not a bad time.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Terrible service. My friends and I waited 20 mins for a table at lunch time, which was great, but waited another 30 minutes for a server to take our drink orders. Even after flagging someone down and being told it would be taken care of, we were left waiting and eventually left. Would not recommend.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Great music nice rooftop bar. I had the Music City Mule, which is a blood orange flavor and it was delicious!

name: The 5 Spot
text: A friend and I went to the 5 Spot on Motown Monday; however didn't stay for the Motown bc it didn't start until 10pm and it was 8 pm when we arrived. We did, however, get in some free swing/jive dance lessons before the crowd arrived at 8:59pm. (Cover charge after 9pm) The place was jumping and we had a blast! Food from the "permanently parked" food truck outside was very good and hit the (5) spot!!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: A place worth going to. Great live music. And it's just fun.

name: The Valentine
text:
Two might seem harsh, but nothing about this place was above expectations, and there were a few things that were below expectations. The bartender was nice, not complaints there, but the cocktail/drink menu had approximately 10 drinks. Of those 10, only 3 contained whiskey, I would have guess if there were 10 drinks on the menu that at least 7 contained whiskey. Anyway, of those 3, the most appealing was variation of a Moscow Mule... which came in a styrofoam cup...really? For $14 I get a styrofoam cup?

It was a decent venue, not too crowd (and I sort of understand why). Music was good, but nothing any better than anywhere else on the strip. Overall, I'd say it was a decent place if you don't want a large crowd, but overall certainly nothing special.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Let me disclose first that hotels are more alike than different to me - I'm pretty much in-and-out of my room to sleep & shower and spend more time exploring whatever city I'm in. Okay, Las Vegas hotels are a little different.

But as far as Nashville hotels go, this Sheraton Music City is pretty solid. Since I knew I was renting a car, I didn't want to double my room price and pay for overnight parking by staying downtown. Having said that, I left the car at the downtown Omni a couple of times since Melissa & Shannon were staying there, and Daniel of the Omni staff took good care of it each time. Cool.

Back to the Sheraton: This place is huge, it took me a day to get my bearings, and every room has a balcony. The only hotel amenity I actually care about is WiFi, which is free in the lobby here but also free in the room if you're a Starwood member. And the entire place is smoke-free & dog friendly. 

And finally, this Shearton is really quiet, the hallways are really long, and returning really late one night I'm pretty sure I saw two little girls down my corridor holding hands and beckoning, "Hello Danny. Come and play with us." For one brief moment, I wondered why Daniel from the Omni was parking cars at the Sheraton. But then I went into my room and called it a night.

name: FooBar
text: a dungeon of hipsters who really need to get over themselves, and the space is pretty gross and crowded.  I wanted to give it 0 stars but Yelp does not permit that.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
Moonshine bar!! This bar is a must for a night out on Broadway in Nashville!! They have a full bar but what makes this bar special is the moonshine selection!

A COUPLE TIPS FROM A LOCAL!!!
-There are two floors to this bar, on weekend nights the second floor is much less crowded, has a full bar (same as downstairs, and has live music too! You can also smoke on the second floor...I don't know of many bars on broadway that you can smoke in.
-When you come in, try the moonshine!! My tip for anyone I bring in from out of town is to try any of the fruity flavor moonshines with Sprite, you get the flavor without the burn from drinking it straight!! Then you can still say that you drank moonshine when you were in Tennessee

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Hello, I come here regularly sunday evenings to listen to Brian Wayne band and dance. It really has not disappointed me. I am a dancer and its a good place to dance. The people are friendly and the band is exceptional. I recommend Whiskey bent to any swing dancers or music lovers.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I thoroughly enjoyed my night out here.  There were two bands that played. I can't remember who they were.  The only recommendation I would have would be to figure out how to switch bands faster.  The service was great and it was easy to get a drink quickly the way it was set up. For the amount of people in and out of the bar it was very clean. The bathrooms were clean most of the night. Up until about 1am. They constantly had staff walking around picking up empty drinks and taking out the garbage.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
I tried. Really, I did. I just didn't get it. #simoncowellshrug*

I knew what I was getting into. It was Saturday night. It was Broadway. It was a honky tonk. BUT. I had friends in town and that's what one does when one has friends in town. One goes to Broadway and hopes that one doesn't have too terrible of a time. When I am in these situations, I try to hit bars I've never been to so that I can get an experience as well. So, The Stage it was... along with every other tourist in Nashville.

The crowd wasn't so much the problem. This isn't my first rodeo. I know to expect crowds on Broadway. The problem was that it was boring. The elements were there (people, music, booze, roof top) but there was no excitement. It seemed as though everyone was going through the motions. I am fully aware that places are within their rights to have off nights. I suppose that I was there for one. To be even more clear: I'd say The Stage is more Texas than Nashville so if that's your thing, you may enjoy it more than I did.**

Not wanting to fight the mosh pit downstairs, my friends and I made our way to the roof. It was just as crowded but the roof cut out allowed for more air and a bit more room. For a Broadway bar I was surprised that the sound was so bad. I couldn't hear the band on the stage behind me. From the hoots and hollers, I got that they were a cover band, but I couldn't tell you the style. From the way the singer was slinking (at one point, bent over), I have my suspicions. The bar wasn't as chaotic as I feared. We got up to the bar fairly easily and the bartender did his job without rolling his eyes or grunting. That's a win on Broadway. But, that was it. It was a full bar of out of towners doing what they thought they should do in a Nashville bar. As a local, it wasn't my thing. We stayed for one drink and left. No cover (thanks!) made that an easy decision.

*Because Kanye shrugs -- like Kanye ' are cancelled. 
**Whereas Layla's is more Kentucky than Nashville and I enjoy it more for that reason.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Amazing music and great vibe.  Been here twice in a 2 day period.  First time was great food, great service and great vibe on a Friday night.  Music was perfect and they were very accommodating for high top table and joining them together. 

2nd time was not as pleasant. It was over 1hr and 15min wait for food with little to no explanation except over hearing an explanation to another table.  At first I thought it was just a large table ordering before us.  But as we saw two tables leave we realized there was a bigger issue. 

All in all it may be a one time issue but unclear and no explanation provided. Might consider amending with an explanation.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: I had a really terrible experience here--the bartender took my order two separate times, then got people's drinks but not mine. When I asked her where mine was & why I hadn't gotten it yet, she told me that she wasn't going to serve me because she didn't like my attitude. I am NOT the type of person who is rude to service workers, ever, nor was I belligerently drunk, so for her to behave so unprofessionally was appalling to me. I would submit a formal complaint to the bar, but let's be honest, they're an incredibly popular tourist trap that will do business no matter how rude their bartenders are, so I doubt they care about losing one persons business. I can only hope that others will see this review and take it as a warning--there are much better places to go on Broadway with a much friendlier staff.

name: Legends Corner
text: The first Honky tonk we encountered on Nashville's famous Broadway. This one is on the corner, kitty to Bridgestone arena. Decent cover bands,  pricey beers, nice staff. Time to hop to the next bar.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I had to hit this spot up multiple times on my week-long vacation. The platter....oh the platter! I with I could find sausage like that where I live. And the pulled pork was, of course, amazing. A shot of crown is cheaper than a shot of Jack Daniels because "It's the best whiskey there is"...this is clearly a Tennessee thing.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This honkytonk was listed as a recommendation on the Grand Ole Opry website so it was the first stop for me and my family for lunch upon arrival. I was very disappointed considering there are so many other honkytonks to choose from. Immediately upon walking in I was approached by waitstaff but was not greeted w/hello but told I could not bring in outside drinks (I was holding an empty soda can). I disposed of the can & ordered a few items off the menu. The food was basic fast food. Nothing spectacular at all. Tried to enjoy the music but the band playing was horrible. They were not even playing country music and were not shy about passing a tip can around in your face even before we heard them play. Wish I had gone somewhere else! Don't waist your time here when there are so many other options.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Even as a local this is a really fun place to get away for a night on the town dancing to great fun music.

Cheap beer .  fried balogne and burgers after a long night make it a must do anytime were downtown.

Also, generally less crowded than some other popular honky tonks too.

If I'm feeling extra wild i sometimes even end up coming home with a brand new pair of boots!

name: Second Fiddle
text: Great spot that wasn't too crowded and music was great. Good bartender service and band not to pushy about tips.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Best band experience I enjoyed on Broadway. The band with pappi on the fiddle made for a great time. Everyone dancing and enjoying themselves. Will gladly return on my next visit to Nashville.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Cheap beer and some of the better live music on Broadway. Happened upon Tin Roof my first night in Nashville and I keep coming back for the fun atmosphere and good music.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Food and service horrible but good vibe in music, and it is pretty chill in here compared to the big boys on Broadway in Nashville

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Plaza Mariachi opened about 2 miles from my house and it's now my favorite spot in town! It's such a great option for flexible dining or large groups and a great way to kill a couple hours. Their entertainment program is slammed each week with Mexican Bingo, Salsa Lessons, and much more!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: EXCELLENT food. Well balanced, fresh, and full of layered flavor. Yes it's pricey, but worth it. Environment was low key and classy. The wait staff, manager, and host were very friendly and accommodating. The band was fantastic. Happy hour is 4pm - 7pm Monday - Friday during which the drinks are about half the price.   You should make a reservation early even on a Monday.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This was a great place to sit and have a beer and listen to some live music. The food was just ok and the fryer was broken when I visited for lunch. The beers available are of a good range.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: It was so nice to see a performance in a smaller venue rather than a stadium. The Ryman is legendary, but the pew seats are sort of uncomfortable and it was very hot for the first half of the night.

name: Legends Corner
text: Loved the vibe in this place -- quite hopping for a Saturday afternoon in January so we found a place to set our beer and listen to some excellent country tunes --wish I could remember the country singer!!  He was very good.

name: Robert's Western World
text: The best honky tonk in Nashville.   Try the fried bologna sandwich and drink lots of beer while heRing the best western music of all time!

name: Robert's Western World
text: My favorite spot in Nashville. It's all about old time country and blue grass and the house band (Don Kelley's) is just the best. Between the crazy talented bass player Joe Fink and guitar prodigy Daniel Donato, you are in for an amazing night of fun music. The Don Kelley band is there Monday - Saturday from 6 to 10pm. Be sure to tip these talented guys what you'd pay for a great night of music, because all the bands on Broadway Street only get paid in tips. They'll pass a bucket around regularly and remember to fill it! Oh and be sure to try the fried bologna sammich - it's the best on the planet. YUMMY!

name: Legends Corner
text: Fun bar lots of good music.. Not a overly crazy crowed.. Which is nice if you just want to sit back and enjoy music and cold beers..

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is actually a fun place. It's pretty small and they had a good band playing which strangely didn't bother me. There's an upstairs which isn't big but you can carry a conversation over there. Tragically I didn't try their food which I know it's what you have to try. I was surprised to the bar and the grill located next to each other. I would recommend this place as one of the bars to go to if you are ever in Nashville.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: This place is amazing!! In Nashville from Michigan and we had the best time!! Had the caprese appetizer, crab and shrimp bisque (OMG), the lobster enchiladas, and my friend had the margherita pizza- all were soooo so good. The absolute best part was dessert- cheesecake sopapilla. The best dessert I've had in my entire life!  Not exaggerating! The band was amazing too- The Chris Weaver Band, so great!! Loved the atmosphere of this place too, great decor, classy but not snooty!

name: Robert's Western World
text: We didn't eat .  We came for the music, and it didn't disappoint.  Nathan Belt and the Buckles.  Need I say more?

name: Second Fiddle
text:
Nice place to grab a drink & listen to live music. 

There are many bars on Broadway in Nashville, Second Fiddle is one of them. It was not as populated as other bars, say like Honky Tonk and Tootsies but it was fun. Will go there again if I visit Nashville.

Pros:
Music: Nice live bands. Good music.
Crowd: People seemed to be having fun. Not overpopulated like other bars in the area.
Staff: Bartenders and servers were friendly and fast. Don't need to wait long to get your drink(s)!!!
Ambiance: Real cool. Liked the pictures of classic country singers on the wall.

Cons: will tell you when I think of one :P

name: Second Fiddle
text: I hope I get this right -- we walked in on a Saturday in late January and Jake Maurer was playing -- really enjoyed his voice.  Good venue!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Very fun bar, good music, multiple levels. Food was better than expected. Our only complaint was the A/C was not working well. Hope they fix that. Otherwise, great fun!

name: Robert's Western World
text: We at 8 pm on a Saturday night. Bar was crowded but managed to find a table. Sweet potato fries were on point! Great authentic Nashville bar feel. Note - there is a back entrance through the alley behind Tootsies.

name: Second Fiddle
text: It was the 2nd fiddle but the 3rd honky tonk we stopped at. Same deal as all the others with some kitschy-er decor.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I really loved this place!  Robert's Western World is my new favorite bar in Nashville.  Ha!  Not that I have a lot to compare it to but this place was so fun.  It was crowded but not overly so.  The music was fun, live, honky tonk ish stuff!  The decor is very fitting of an older style honky tonk bar. 
I most enjoyed listening to the music and dancing with others in the front.  They also have a short order food menu.  The grilled cheese is pretty tasty, I must say.  

Oh, and it's free!

Go check this gem out if you are in the downtown Nashville area.  :)

name: Robert's Western World
text: One of the old classics.   Nice bartenders with good service even when it's packed.  Great music and classic atmosphere.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
This was the first bar on Broadway we ended up hopping into, solely because the music coming out of it was stellar. While this bar doesn't have as much room to dance as others, I felt that each night I visited the music was miles better than anything around - and isn't that the whole point of Nashville? 

Great bar, great music, great atmosphere. One of the top spots on Broadway.

name: Music City Center
text: I am so thankful that we have such a nice convention center. The only reason I gave it three stars is because of easy parking. This is the second year that I went to a hair show at this facility. Last year was worse than this year. There are plenty of bathrooms. But 3 hours into the show , they are nasty. It is embarrassing to me because people come from all around to be at this show. And this is what we show them? And I know there is a lot of body heat in 1 big section. But people were walking around fanning themselves. Come on???

name: Robert's Western World
text: I spent several weeks in Nashville recently and stopped by Robert's quite a few times.  They have great music, great burgers and fries.  My only complaint is most of the waitress staff is less than friendly.  None of them seemed like they wanted to be there, let alone get you your next drink.  other than that great place.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is the honky tonk look that you've seen in the movies with the boot wall and all that. I know beer is cheaper in other parts of the city but you have to roll through this at least once.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My wife and I were so excited on our first night in Nashville but Sambuca truly underdelivered I'm sorry to say.  It's all about perspective right?  My college kids would have loved it.  My foodie wife and I found the entire experience average at best, though our waiter was kind and attentive. Tuna special came out cold, twice.  Hanger steak was comparable to something I could whip up in short order.  Oh well, live and learn.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Loved loved loved this place! I liked it more than Tootsie's. There's something so charming about this honky tonk that makes it stand out in my mind. Perhaps it's how cheap the food is ($5 Recession special - sandwich, chips, AND PBR - unheard of in Chicago) or maybe how great the music is or how wonderful the service is. I don't know. Something about this place helped to make my Nashville experience!

Try the fried pickles! They're delicious and the best fried pickles I've had (also less than $5?!)

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
My family and I went here in the forth of July.  Loved the live music.  The band played country and rock covers and added their own flair.  

The chicken and waffles appetizer had a nice presentation but the flavor was a disappointment.  My daughters enjoyed their chicken strips and fries.  My son had a chicken quesadilla with queso dip that he raved about.  The brown sugar and chili dry rub wings were impressive.  The house special spicy chicken sandwich was great.  The food, band, atmosphere and staff made this a great spot to enjoy a lunch in Nashville with the family.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Went there on Sunday morning. Perfect ambiance, relaxed music, great drinks! Will be back!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Fine cheeseburger and sweet potato fries and ice cold beer. Can't get any better than that!!!!!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: This place is incredible! It is such a vibrant and entertaining place to go not only just to enjoy some live entertainment but also enjoy really great food too! The prices were very fair and there was a wide assortment of food available. There were even a couple places that served delicious desert foods! We were very impressed with our visit here and we loved the live band performing too! This place is great if you want to just grab something to eat or if you want to shop around. Plaza Mariachi truly brings something unique to Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Food is mediocre but the beer selection and great service make up for it. The atmosphere is very fun and great for groups.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Incredible acoustics! I've been to a ton of music venues in Chicago but this was incredible.

I went to the Grand Ole Opry at the Ryman and it was a great show. A bunch of artists went up and sang a few songs. I loved the musical variety - all types of country music went up on that stage.

I definitely recommend stopping by here if you're in Nashville. Catch a show of something if you can!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
"They say the neon lights are bright on Broadway
They say there's always magic in the air
But when you're walkin' down that street
And you ain't had enough to eat
The glitter rubs right off and you're nowhere"

So the song may be talking about the other Broadway, regardless, the neon lights *are* blinding on this Broadway too. We headed there in hopes of catching some live music at a honky tonk during our stay in Nashville. Figuring we'd end up on Broadway, I bookmarked a few places that interested me. I've gotta say what caught my attention at Robert's was mentions of boots and bologna - a combo you don't see everyday.

Broadway was madness when we arrived; we quickly abandoned our plan to hit Tootsie's and The Stage after seeing the line. Robert's, fortunately, had a very reasonable line around 11 and even better no cover, so we popped in. The bar was crowded, not so much there wasn't breathing room. It wasn't long before we scored seats at the downstairs bar, with the grill in front of us and the boots lined up behind. 

If you're like us, and not country fans (at least not contemporary country), Robert's might be your speed. Robert's bills themselves a traditional country venue; they played some originals, but much of what Nathan Belt & the Buckles played we recognized and liked - covers of Johnny Cash, Jerry Lee Lewis, Peggy Lee, Roy Orbison, and Buddy Holly. As an added bonus, Robert's didn't seem as crazy as some of the other bars.

If you're not picky, the best drink deal to be had is $2.50 bottles of PBR, High Life and I think Bud Light. If you're into bologna, which judging by the cook, lots of people are, the fried bologna recession special is for you. It sounded weird and kind of gross to both of us, but after watching a bunch come off the grill, manfriend was quite tempted to try one.

A little divey, but a lot of fun; I'd recommend Robert's if you want to hear some good music, drink and eat on the cheap, and not have to scream or play charades with/at your companions.

name: Legends Corner
text: I loved this place! It was one of my favorites in Nashville. The bands were pretty decent and fun. I don't understand the complaints about drunk people and shitty music. HELLO! It's a bar! And it's Nashville! No complaints here.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: For what this is - essentially a Latin American food court in a Vegas-style atmosphere, this place is top-notch! Don't come here expecting fine dining, fancy wine lists or white table cloths. Rather, dress casually, bring your friends and family, and come hungry! The standout options on this visit were the spicy mixed seafood ceviche, street corn in a cup and cold Dos Equis lager. You have to visit different vendors for different foods, but the potential hassle is avoided by just sitting back and enjoying the varying entertainment at the huge stage at one end of the food court. On our visit , there was a Mariachi band followed by fire breathing dancers. Very family friendly in a creative environment.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place for old school country! If you want to dance a little- don't plan on it on Friday or Saturday night! Gail, the bartender, is fabulous! She's on top of things! Shes friendly, attentive and takes great care of her customers! If in Nashville, this is a great place to check out!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Limited menu but I think they do everything well that is on the menu. Ordered a bologna sandwich with fries. Very good! A friend ordered a cheese burger and said it was also delicious. We also had fried pickles which were very good! Service was pretty good also.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Great place to see a show and soak in American history. A few tips: The address says 5th Avenue, but the entrance is on 4th. Park a block or so away and pay $1,  rather than $20 right next to the Ryman. If your seats on on the second floor, odds are you'll be walking up some steep stairs, If you aren't a fan of stairs, go for first floor seats. Seats on the far left or far right do keep you from seeing the entire stage. Peace y'all.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Really enjoyed the dimmed lighting and cozy booths. 

The menu is diverse with something for everyone's tastes.

I had some sort of crab pasta dish and a few glasses of white wine and the whole meal was very delicious. 

The live music was also good. Will definitely be returning.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great restaurant! Loved the live music, loved the food and loved the drinks. We also had great service from the waitstaff which was much appreciated. The only thing is it was a bit dark and loud so it was tough to talk or see the other girls in our group but it certainly put us in a good mood for celebrating!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Although I'm not a country music myself, this place was pretty cool. We took the self guided tour which started off pretty cool. It was this high tech presentation that talked about the history of the building and how it came to be. Pretty neat stuff.
After that we were free to walk around the auditorium and check out the surrounding. Then you have the option to take a photo on stage, it was $20 for like 4 photos. We didn't buy it, but not a bad deal, I guess.

Overall, it is a pretty short tour, unless you are a huge country music fan and want to spend more time. It is a neat experience, plus it's right in the downtown area, so if you are there, check it out. The tour is about $20 a person, no backstage access.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is a must if you're in Nashville. A true "HonkyTonk" and you won't be disappointed with the live music that generates from this place nearly 24/7 with some of best musicians in town. Oh, and they have beer and booze too !

name: Robert's Western World
text: Stopped in for a couple of beers and to hear live music. Eileen Rose was playing and was awesome!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Total tourist here. Went in around 6 on a Friday and loved the singer and band, as well as the $3 price tag on drafts. Hung around for a half hour before moseying on.

name: Legends Corner
text: Been coming to this bar for 5 years now and tonight I had the worst service since I've been coming to Nashville. All three bartenders were very rude and cold when ordering.  If you pay almost 10$ a drink you would think the servers would be friendly. One bartender rolled her eyes when my wife let her know their sprite was out.  Sad I've seen a lot of bars go down hill and close because of bad service.  Hope this one doesn't get to that point.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I'm really glad we checked Yelp as we were coming out of the Country Music Hall of Fame. For cheap eats and great music, this place was perfect at 1pm on a Friday). The bar had a good selection of craft and domestic beers including Lagunitas IPA. I was very happy to see a veggie burger on the menu, and it was good, served with cheese, lettuce, pickles and tomatoes. Frozen commercial crinkle cut fries rounded out my order. The bartender was pleasant although not chatty and remembered lemons for my water.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I am all about getting more for my money, so the recession special is where it's at.  

$5 for fried bologna sandwich (what else would you want after a day on Broadway, anyways?) with chips and a PBR.  Granted, we upgraded to include cheese for another $1 each per sandwich, but it really did make it taste even more delicious.

It's a dive, but for a beer and a bologna sandwich, it's the place to go.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Excellent food.  Excellent drinks.  Excellent live music.  I was very impressed with the entire experience.  Located in the gulch, very modern setting.  I would definitely recommend and come back.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: What a cool place to see a show!  Just saw Sturgill Simpson here last weekend.  This is an older building/venue with church style (pews) seating.  It's pretty intimate with a small capacity.  Because of that, every seat feels close.  The volume is perfect - not eardrum splitting, but still loud enough that you know you were at a show.  There is a full bar in the lobby area and beer/water stands inside.  16 ounce tall boys (Bud, Lite, Fat Tire Amber and Coors light are $8, bottles water is $4) are nice and cold and served with a friendly smile.  The ushers are helpful and friendly too.  They have a souvenir shop near the entrance with lots of great stuff - shirts, hats, CDs. and all the other trinkets you would expect.  Again, this is a fun spot to see a show.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is my favorite music joint on the Music Strip.  
I am most happy when I stumble upon any Rock-a-billy band playing there.
With over 160 reviews, no need for Juicy to wax on.

The place is cool, laid back and has a welcoming vibe (if you're cool). 

It's not your cleanest, but not the Dive as some light-weight reviewers would have you believe.  It's a bar people! With live music and no cover charge... you do the math!  As a lover of dive bars, this joint would not rank. 

It's a true-blue Honky-Tonk. It is not a Barrelhouse. 
I usually go between Noon and 8 pm.  I don't like crowds.

Where else can you get a "Recession Special" meal for $5 ??? (see photo)
It's PBR + Fried Bologna Sandwich + your choice of Goo-Goo Cluster or Moon-Pie.

Does life get any better?

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Always bet on black.

When given a choice between touring the Johnny Cash Museum and the Ryman Auditorium, go with The Man in Black.

Since I've never caught a show here, I can't rate this as a venue. I've heard the acoustics are amazing, so I'm inclined to believe my rating would be higher. I'm not the churchgoing type, but was looking forward to touring "The Mother Church of Country Music"; unfortunately, it was a letdown.

The Ryman offers two types of tours, self-guided tours for $15 and backstage tours for $20. We opted for the backstage tour, which worked out to around $50 for both of us when you include the stupid service charges. Reserve your spots in advance, tours do sell out and I don't believe they're offered when there are scheduled shows.

We were cutting it close and arrived right on the dot for our tour; it felt like we were late, our tour guide had already done introductions as we walked up to the group quickly pointing and asking where we were from. Maybe our disappointing tour was the result of our guide's style or maybe that's how they all are. 

True to its name, our backstage tour was just that - backstage, for the most part. Aside from the old pictures, nothing in particular makes the dressing rooms stand out as Ryman dressing rooms; after seeing two, we got the picture. Our tour felt rushed and sometimes confusing; our guide talked fast, had my parents been with me that would surely have been an issue. Even more annoying, our guide started talking the minute he starting moving toward our next stop; if you're not right next to him (impossible since most spaces required being single file), you're missing stuff. 

As quickly as our tour began, it ended. I don't think it could've been more than an hour, but our guide noted we were well over the allotted time. It's not clear that it's the intent, but I think it would make sense to do the self-guided tour immediately following the backstage one; since you're already in the theater, you don't have to pay for it. That will expose you to the Ryman video and the timeline of artifacts and historical moments associated with the auditorium.

Bottom line: Beautiful auditorium with a rich history, mediocre tour.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Great location, great sound. Great bands. Smaller venue with big name bands. What more can you ask for. Oh, Christmas lights! they should have up lights for ambiance and decoration:) Love the location. If you want to go out before or after there are tons of places.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Of all of the options on Broadway, this is consistently my favorite.  Everything about it is perfect.  No pretense, just fun, great live music, friendly bartenders, cheap and delicious food, all in an incredible party atmosphere.  Get the fried bologna sandwich and a basket of onion rings.  Eat, smile, rinse with a PBR, and repeat.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The venue itself is a ten! I would like to say that your security officers could use a lesson in hospitality. The pudgy, mid forties, brown haired, guy you had working outside this evening was less than desirable and treated the group of people I was with terribly. Instead of asking us to not take photos he flashed his "ego" light vigorously at us with no explanation and upon us asking why it was not allowed he became very hostile and shouted at us. All he had to do was say, "ladies, photography is not allowed". Then again, he's a forty year old security guard- probably used his "aggression" to compensate for his lack of character.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: So not worth the money! Atmosphere is nice, but the food is just ok. $35 for a cheap Flat Iron steak is just insulting. You can get much better food for a lot less money.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great food ....great service....great atmosphere!!!   Enough said !!!  Ask for Teresa...she is the bomb !!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: My boyfriend and I went to Robert's Western World a Tuesday afternoon in January. It was really quiet but the staff was extremely friendly and there was good music. I got a  cider and a hot dog and they tasted as expected.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My all time favorite happy hour spot in Nashville! Great prices, menu, and atmosphere!!! Kaycie is hands down the best! She always delivers incredible service and very kind. She is the reason Sambuca's hang out spot. She feels like one of the girls.

name: Music City Center
text: This place is huge! And beautiful. The building itself is said to be shaped like a guitar (I didn't see it). There are plenty of places to sit down and get some work done, individually or with a group. Indoor and outdoor seating, even on the second and third floors. My favorite part was that the exhibition hall actually has some natural light! I came in December and there were lovely Christmas decorations everywhere. There are a few art installations and the country music songwriters showcase.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Completely ignorant and spiteful server. Asked my daughter three times for her ID just so she could drink a lemonade. Sent the manager over to check my daughter's ID when we, again, explained to her it was just lemonade. Asked about our food after waiting for fried pickles for 45 minutes and the server's response was "I have no idea." Definitely will not be coming back here. A shame for the performers that the wait staff is doing nothing for the atmosphere.

name: Robert's Western World
text: My first ever fried bologna sandwich was a memorable experience. Great bar with a very different vibe from the rest of the Nashville strip. Stop in here for some old school country western.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Cool place with good live music.  Very nice setting.  Bartenders were awesome!  It's not cheap, but the drinks, food, and service were excellent!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Stopped in for a drink last night, our last night in Nashville. We had fried pickles and a fried bologna sandwich. Yummy! Great band and a really fun place

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Wow, brought our family here to see the tour and they had so many people on the tour you couldn't get inside the rooms, or hear anything. The guide was speaking at the front of a long line each time, and although we complained that we could not hear she did next to anything to address the issue. Then the guide left us (we had someone with a wheelchair) and didn't explain that there was a video we should be seeing. As it turns out, the video should have been the first part of the tour. Total waste of time for us and such a shame as we were excited to show our family the rich history of the Ryman. Our tour guide's name was Adele. I hope the management addresses her performance as a guide. Apparently there's also a souvenir picture that comes as part of the package. It would have been nice to have that clarified as we are just now getting those details from another guide after 1 hour 45 min here of a 1 hour tour. 

After speaking with the manager regarding our experience, they refunded our ticket price. We paid parking twice to avoid a ticket in the process of clearing things up with the manager.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: So much fun! Came here on a random Sunday night, live music was fantastic, the vodka was strong, the fries were cheesy and Brandon, our waiter, very accommodating! Fun fun times :)

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I have never been to a venue so poorly run as this. One magnetometer for a venue this size. Several block long line because of this. The entire mass of people funneled through one set of doors. Ridiculous. 

Ryman, learn from the other venues in the area.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
great music, i was impressed with the audio set up, i know i shouldn't be cause its nashville and everything, but really, sitting in the back and being able to hear the band perfectly, impressive.

 they have a good basic menu and the food on their is really good, the prices were all over the place, somethings were cheap, and somethings were prohibitively expensive: example $4.5 for 8 HUGE mozzarella sticks (delicious), but $5.5 for a 'premium beer' ( Shiner Bock ). basic french fries were 4.50... so just kinda odd.

 also this doesn't really bother me so much but worth pointing out, even tho the bar was not busy the service was poor, sub par. i didn't count off for that, just really the random pricing is what impacted the score.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We stopped in for lunch during our trip to Nashville. The band was great, and we loved checking out the cowboy boots all over. Our only disappointment was when we ordered our food-cheeseburger and fries/onion rings. After putting in our order, the lady came back and said that their fryer wasn't working. We wished we had known that when we arrived as we could have gone somewhere else. At that point, we were stuck. I guess I should be thankful that we saved the calories! I hear this a great spot to visit at night, and I will have to go back and try it next time!

name: Robert's Western World
text: If you only visit 1 honky tonk THIS! is the one to go to!!! While on our honeymoon this was the place we visited again and again. The music was ALWAYS amazing and old school country, none of that Florida Georgia Line bull crap! The staff was fun and attentive. And the prices were right! $2.50 Miller High Life's! And ya gotta get a fried bologna sandwich. Holy delicious! Get here ASAP!

name: Robert's Western World
text: first bar we went to because of reviews whilst having girl's trip in Nashville. great vibe and music. pretty packed and there was just one bartender, she was very quick and attentive. tried the recession special - fried bologna sandwich with moon pie & potato chips. really delicious. definitely best bar around that Broadway strip.

name: Robert's Western World
text: "Roberts" is definitely a place to have a good time. I did feel that the bar itself is a bit congested and tight on space. Besides that, everything else was pretty cool. Good drinks, great music, positive vibes. Staff were friendly and attentive!

name: Robert's Western World
text: The music venue is wonderful and they have a lot of varieties of local beer which I loved !

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Ryman was one of my favorite things we did in Nashville. We did the self-guided tour which starts with a short video that details the rich history of the Ryman and how it has evolved through the years.

You can can walk through the auditorium and see the beautiful architecture, stained glass windows, posters from shows in the past, and artifacts from artists who have performed there. It is such a cool feel for a concert venue - such rich history and i love the pews for seating. Oftentimes they are setting up for a show on the stage which will happen that night which is cool to see. We ended up being able to see a show and it was amazing! Great acoustics!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Our waiter at Jimmy Buffets Margaritaville told us not to miss stopping in to Roberts and he was right. Best music on the street and I popped into every honky Tonk.  Crowded, everyone dancing, the band was entertaining and talented- bought a CD.

name: Robert's Western World
text: My fav spot to be on Broadway. Can get a crowded. Simple old fashion country music, cheap drinks, friendly staff and good cheap bar food. The fried bologna sandwich is really good. Definitely a fun place to be!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Because there are already forty million reviews, I won't bore you with my typical in-depth review. However, it's good to know that this is an older crowd, real country/bluegrass unlike the other whiny/rappy junk you'll find on the rest of the strip and, the drinks are cheap.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Awesome Sweet Tea. I ordered the cheese burger and Onion rings. AMAZING!!!!!! Very reasonable prices, would recommend this place if you are ever in Downtown Nashville .

name: Legends Corner
text: Ended it up here as of our barhopping spots  downtown, glad we did. The bartenders were extremely friendly, made good drinks, and the live music was really good. Not only did they play today's popular country music but also country music from back in the day , they played a mix of everything. Another's place I definitely recommend if you are downtown Nash!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Robert's Western World was everything I thought a Honky Tonk would be... a tad edgy, dark, filled with nostalgia and history, crowded and absolutely rockin'. It took a few minutes for us to find a seat which was made a little awkward as everyone was staring me down because I had the kiddos with me. Children are allowed to enter, stay and have a ball until 6pm, then it's strictly 21 and over. Honestly, this was THE best way for me to show them first hand what Music City is all about!! People wouldn't think Nashville would necessarily be a destination for children and I'm here to tell you that's absolutely false! We all equally LOVED honky talk hopping and Roberts was at the absolute top of our favorites list! A must stop! The girls LOVED Eileen Rose & Silver Threads who played while we were there. They were incredible! I highly recommend trying to stop by when they're there. They are regulars! Check the band schedule on Robert's site. They played it all....Janis, Patsy Cline, Cash (obviously) and some fab originals such as "Rose Garden" which is one of our favorites. They were so insanely talented!! That guitarist blew my mind!! He could've easily been Stevie Ray Vaughn, Kenny Wayne Shepherd or Satriani. Wowza!! 

Make sure you bring cash to drop in their artist's bucket. They live on these tip and it's the least you can do as there's no cover charge. The girls begged me to purchase the CDs the band was roaming around selling. I think I paid $5 each! It was the best souvenir we bought our entire trip! We still listen to them daily!!  

The bartender was a doll. You can place order at the bar and she will bring it to your table. I had some local drafts, Yazoo for about $6 each The girls split pickle spears and sweet potato fries they gobbled up in two seconds as well as moon pies for $1. Typical bar food. PBR & fried bologna sammys are the supposed "thing" here however. 

Definitely put Robert's on the very top of your Broadway stops list!! It was an absolute blast!!

name: Music City Center
text: Poor layout! Needs more eating establishments/coffee stops.  Stairs are awkwardly placed and too spaced out! Not my favorite!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
My husband surprised me with tickets to Ray LaMontagne! The concert was awesome! We enjoyed to opening show as well--Kacy and Clayton.

I knew The Ryman Auditiorium was the original Grand Ole Oprey but I didn't know it was an old church. It was very cool to see the old wooden pews that were curved toward the stage. The back of the auditorium was stain glass windows. 

What a special place to visit. They offer tours as well as concerts, have a snack bar (you can bring food/drinks into the concert), and hold holiday services.

Ambiance: Excellent, you should go!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Solid choice in the Gulch for a nice meal out. I was here for my friend's birthday dinner and they delivered! 

Service was phenomenal. Our lady was so attentive, was able to make recommendations (great recommendations, btw), and even brought out a complimentary dessert for my friend for her birthday! 

They have live music all the time. The Chris Weaver Band was there this particular evening, and while I didn't care for them they seemed to be a hit with most people dining.

Food was good. I got the filet, medium rare. It came with a blue cheese butter and asparagus. I asked for the butter on the side as I'm not a blue cheese fan. Tried a bit, not terribly overwhelming as most blue cheese infused things are (to me). The filet was a touch over cooked, but still very tasty. Asparagus was perfect, great flavor with a snap to it. Ordered the bruschetta as a starter for the table and that was definitely killer! I would order it a hundred times over. 

Ambiance: lovely. Thanks for a nice evening Sambuca!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Maybe I don't go at the right times, but it's never lively. The food is just meh at all the restaurants. The stores are highly over priced. I do love the market and the selection they have.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Honky tonk at its finest. One of the only places worth going to on Broadway. Guitar solos that will give you goosebumps and live music performances that fulfill Nashville expectations.

There's usually a line to get in because it's popular, but it's worth the wait. I've been a couple times and both times only had to wait 30min max. If you have a couple beers elsewhere before you go, you'll barely notice the wait.

Once inside the stage is to the left in the front of the venue and bar on the right hand side. Grab a PBR (yay!) and soak in the music.

They also have food here - it was late and I was itching for 4th meal and ordered a burger and fries. Actually quite good late night bar food! Worth it!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Really cool place.  They also show you videos of Ryman (the old and the new).  Really cool to see the original flooring and seating. It seems like no matter where you sit you'll have a good seat of the stage!  Very clean and awesome experience.  A complimentary photo is included with the ticket

name: Robert's Western World
text: Absolutely LOVE Roberts and our Kick Butt waitress Rachael!! She is the best! Make sure you go and spend an hour or 7

name: Legends Corner
text: Great crowd, great music, and great bartenders. This was by far my favorite place on Broadway. We went to Tootsies, Second Fiddle, Big Bang, The Stage, etc. Enjoyed the people watching, the drinks, the live band, and did I say the bartenders here were the BEST!

name: Second Fiddle
text: A okay honky tonk bar where the drinks are poured strong and the bands play for tips. No complaints.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: All I can say is amazing!!! We had a happy hour group of 10 people all coming in a different times  ordering food and drinks at different times but the service we received from Sydney was amazing, she did not miss a beat! You must ask for her next time you're in.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Had an important business scheduled with a confirmed reservation for over a week. Got an email the afternoon before that simply read - your reservation has been canceled. Called restaurant and couldn't find out anything or get any info except "we took a larger group reservation". Pathetic customer service. Will never go there again. Be careful if they tell you that you have a reservation. They don't honor them.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I love this venue. When we went this time, we sat on row H in the balcony to see Gregory Alan Isakov. It was a good view even being pretty far back on the balcony! And the sound was great up there, know sometimes that is a concern with balcony seats. We would purchase balcony seats again in the front couple of rows if possible for our next concert here.

They do provide valet parking for some shows, but there is plenty of parking for 12-20$ everywhere around the venue. The place is classy and easy to navigate. Overall we had a great experience!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: An absolute must. Building is a time warp. So very worth the price of tour. Starts with film that's is so cool. Really enjoyed this stop on our trip to Nashville. Disappointed at the tours ending I and others didn't realize pics on stage  included in price. Person standing next to camera (I thought she was with the people setting up) stood on floor looking bothered and annoyed.  Her job is to take pics so I feel like that was a crappy ending to a beautiful day.

name: Nashville Municipal Auditorium
text: I am honestly not one to leave a negative review but I am beyond frustrated at this point. I have gone to the box office multiple times to purchase tickets for an event and have never had problems until this week. Today was my 4th time arriving at the box office during the listed hours of operation. Each time I have gone in the past week have been at different times between the hours of 10:30am-4pm. Each time I have arrived at the box office, all of the doors have been locked and no one was in the box office. I arrived today at 10am and spent 20 minutes on the phone trying to get ahold of someone to see if they would be open during their listed hours. I finally got someone on the phone who was helpful and kind but told me that the box office would not be open until 2pm. I understand that hours change, but the least management can do would be to post their correct hours, or take them down completely.

name: Robert's Western World
text: My favorite spot in Nashville. It's all about old time country and blue grass and the house band (Don Kelley's) is just the best. Between the crazy talented bass player Joe Fink and guitar prodigy Daniel Donato, you are in for an amazing night of fun music. The Don Kelley band is there Monday - Saturday from 6 to 10pm. Be sure to tip these talented guys what you'd pay for a great night of music, because all the bands on Broadway Street only get paid in tips. They'll pass a bucket around regularly and remember to fill it! Oh and be sure to try the fried bologna sammich - it's the best on the planet. YUMMY!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
If you're looking for something different in Nashville, check out Plaza Mariachi! I went on a rainy day so it's nice that everything is indoors especially with unpredictable Nashville weather. I went on a Friday so it was super lively. There was even an aerial dancer, someone who danced with fire, and loud live music. Like others have mentioned there's also a dance floor and things seemed kid friendly (around 7-8pm at least).

On to the food: Lots of food choices from Mexican to Argentinian to sandwiches. They also have a few places that sell desserts like churros, ice cream and boba. I got three tacos and all were awesome! Overall a fun experience and something pretty unique for Nashville.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
Excellent venue! 
You can tell all the attention to detail.  

The food court has lots of options. 

The stage is beautiful with lots of room for dancing or other events. 

Shops and a market also round out the space.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Fun to tour and learn the history. A place were souls were saved and bluegrass was born.  Sat in the old wooden pews and took in The Grand Ole Opry.  So cool to see so many stars from different era's and the fun they had interacting with each other and performing in a place that they love.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
My oldest would give Plaza Mariachi 10 stars if he could! We were looking for a fun place to take our boys the night before the new school year. I found an amazing review about Plaza Mariachi and we were hooked! 

It was a Monday night and not very busy. There was still live music on stage in the food court area. There are halls that portray streets that run off of the food court. In these hallways are shops and art studios. Such a neat place!! 

For food we had a feast of oysters with a chimichurri sauce, salmon atop veggies, and an amazing dish that had potatoes, pico, steak and cotijo cheese all mixed together. 

After eating and listening to the lovely lady on stage (Luna Morena), our boys wanted to go to the arcade. They had a blast and blew through their $15 arcade card. The two oldest split the card and they got about 8 games out of it. The youngest played in the jungle gym.

We are all looking forward to a return trip!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
This place is awesome; I love Nashville! Having read the reviews, I was hesitant to come here. After the conclusion of Vanderbilt Commencement 2017, we had lunch at Bricktops and ended up at Sambuca for dinner. 

As you walk in, you are met with a lively crowd which is ready to listen to some live music. Luckily for us, the Chris Weaver Band was in attendance and played everything from TLC to The Band. They absolutely killed it tonight!

Anyway, the Tennessee Mule drink was awesome and fairly alcoholic. We shared an order of the beignets filled with prosciutto and mozzarella cheese. For our entrees, four of us had the blackened red snapper on dirty rice. This dish stood out immensely! It was perfectly seasoned and a substantial portion. 

Come here for a good time!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Man, I love Tennessee. Two things people here don't mess around with are their BBQ and their blues, or music in general. 

I insisted we come here, and so glad that we did. No cover charge, and the place was pretty big. We happened to come through on a Saturday when there was a pre-season game against the Falcons and a car show in the middle of downtown. Broadway was hopping and so was Robert's. We grabbed our beers and waded through the crowd to the upper level. 

The band came on shortly thereafter, and 18 year old Daniel from Memphis was guest starring with the band. Holy cow! I've been playing guitar for YEARS and this kid made me wanna hang up my strings in shame. The whole band just rocked. I sang along to Johnny Cash and other favorites. I was hoping for some Folsom prison blues, but ah, next time. 

Decent prices for a drink and a recession special for $5. I don't eat bologna but if I did, hell, I'd be all over it and a bag of chips. Which it comes with. And a PBR. What?! 

I mean, I don't think you're coming here for the food anyway, but if you were, you could eat a fried delight for a Lincoln. 

Amazing music, amazing vibe, amazing Nashville.

name: Music City Center
text:
The building is great and the architecture is superb.  Place has plenty of room to have multiple events and nice views of downtown Nashville is nice!
Only pitfall is with all that great architecture there are people SMOKING outside on the patio areas and they are dropping cigarette butts all over the place - NASTY! 
It would be in there benefit to make the outdoors area a SMOKE FREE ZONE!  Bad when you try to sit at a table out on patio and about 25 cigarette butts are all around you; STINKS!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Stopped here for some drinks and music around noon on a Friday.  We were able to sit at the bar and order some drinks.  The drinks weren't cheap but they were good!  The singer that day was amazing and I could've easily listened to her all day.  The bar staff was great too...very friendly and offered their suggestions with no problem.  I would definitely come back next time we're in Nashville!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Solid breakfast. Very good biscuits and jam. Average coffee. Nice people and interesting history.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Incredible southern cooking. The chicken gizzards and livers were the best I've ever had and the moonshine Marry was an amazing drink. Enjoy!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Although the wait is long, the biscuits and jams really do live up to the hype! It's a Saturday well spent! I highly recommend the fried chicken and macaroni and cheese.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
It's like eating at grandma house.  The first item they bring out is the biscuits. They are DELICIOUS.   I tried the blackberry preserves with them and it was my favorite. 

I ordered fried chicken with mashed potatoes and fried okra. Overall the meal was good but not overly special. The outside of the chicken was really tasty but the actual meat was bland. The mashed potatoes were good and you could taste the butter in it. Don't bother with the fried okra. It tasted like the frozen stuff.  

Service was excellent once we were seated.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
i'm afraid this restaurant is losing its edge.  I will begin with the positive.  The cole slaw,  mac and cheese and the hash brown casserole were pretty good.  However, the green beans were sour, so I had to substitute something else.  The turnip greens were not very good, either.  If you order hoe cakes, they will charge you for them, but the server did not tell me that.  I thought the hoe cakes came with the meal.  Wrong!  The sweet tea was not good at all.  
This is about the third time we have eaten here in the last few months.  We kept thinking it would improve, but it hasn't.  Their breakfast is probably better.  The pecan pie was good.
I hate to see the quality of this restaurant go downhill.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I have live in the Nashville area since 1979, but have never ventured to the Loveless Café. There is a ton of hype out there about how this is the "be all - end all" mecca of Nashville country cooking...hmmmm

Party of 8 and none of us have ever darkened their doorway. It's a Thursday night and it is past 7:00 so seating and waiting was not an issue. Below I will list items ordered and the general consensus of all:

Fried Chicken - good - not great - good. In another lifetime I was the manager of a chicken restaurant. It takes at least 13 minutes to cook chicken fresh - we received ours in 10. Due to moisture content the dark meat was good. The breast - a little dry, but not bad - time to change the grease...
