Meat loaf - good
Chicken livers - good, not great - slightly over cooked - time to change the grease...
Chicken gizzard - general consensus was that the breading was too sweet - again - time to change the grease...
Pulled pork - very good - huge portion!
Grilled pork chop - good
Biscuits - good - really don't understand the hype and the "top secret" recipe. Great starter to the meal, but definitely not "OMG!"
Mashed potatoes w/gravy - good - gravy seemed to be from a packet...
Cole slaw - very good
Cream corn - EXCELLENT!
Mac & cheese - very good
Turnip greens - too sweet - somewhat disconcerting...
Slow cooked green beans - "unique flavor" not necessarily good...no one wanted to take them home...
Caramelized sweet potatoes - meh...
Fried green tomatoes - good, but mostly breading - sliced too thin...
Cucumber and onions - excellent
Fried okra - good - again...time to change the grease...

Personally - I won't be back - too far and to me not a "destination" restaurant. Better - or at least equal - food can be found closer to home.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wonderful breakfast! I had the Chicken & Waffles (so good!) Others in the party really enjoyed the hash brown casserole and omeletes. The biscuits and jam are 5 star!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Country ham is not edible.  It was so salty even for some one that likes salty food. Biscuits were good but not great as others have mentioned. Grits were super rich from the heavy use of butter.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Absolutely the biggest tourist trap in Nashville. Just awful. Flavorless pork pounded flat, fries, worst Rueben ever, and two beers. $87 including tip. If you are into dropping substantial cash and having instant diarrhea from the low quality grease, then this is your dream restaurant. Enjoy!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great environment and great old fashioned food.  Portions are great and the biscuits are FANTASTIC!!!  They are very friendly and when we asked for orders to go they were very accommodating and did not skimp on the extras that would have came with the dishes if we were eating in house.    Yes the wait is long because it is that good.  We sat on a picnic benches and walked around the shops... we even played a little game of cornhole/bags.  It's a great way to spend an afternoon.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits are sometimes good, sometimes not. It used to be consistently amazing when the biscuit lady was around. Good fried catfish. Good cocktails with moonshine. Good fried chicken gizzards with gravy.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This was located off the beaten path. About 30min away from downtown. It is a drive but well worth it. If you're looking to feel like home and really get that warm feel, then this is the spot. Upon entering in the late afternoon, we were quickly seated. The server Owen was the best. Super attentive and helpful. He brought out warm fresh biscuits. It came with 3 different jelly spreads. Blackberry, strawberry, and peach. It was so good. The biscuits were hot and fluffy. with the homemade spread was a match made in heaven. Then we ordered the sweet tea as drinks. For our main dish I went with the half order of the loveless country ham, scrambled eggs, grits, and bacon. The country ham had a nice smokey taste to it. A thick cut and it was delicious. Better than any ham I've had before. Finished this off with the made from scratch banana puddin'. It was served cold and was a great way to end the meal. I'm so full yet so happy. The service here was also amazing. 

Recommendation: Country ham, biscuits, and banana puddin'

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best Biscuits I have ever tried in my life! Simply exquisite! And they make sure they bring plenty for everyone in the table! The staff was very very nice as well! The whole experience was very nice!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This has to be the best Listening Room I have ever visited.  I have been twice and now I I am hooked.  The small plates and Flatbread are outstanding as well as the acoustics. My next move is to become a Vino club member.The short ride up from the Huntsville area is well worth it

name: Loveless Cafe
text: An exceptional cafe with a really homey feel, I felt like I was coming home, and I don't feel that way often enough. Very homey and down South interior, our waiter was highly attentive and incredibly sociable and kind. I was really impressed with the service. The meatloaf tasted like it was made straight from my family's secret recipe, it was incredible. The fried okra tasted amazing and the pickled salad I had was delicious as well. I was in a hurry to get in and get out this time around, I'm looking forward to returning and relaxing for the full experience. 10/10, would absolutely recommend.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If you don't eat here you will regret the fact that you are alive. Food? Perfect. Service? Perfect. AMBIENCE? Perfect. Love u, loveless.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Beer was good - or else it would be 1 star. Nothing else was, which is a bummer bc it seems like it has a lot of potential.  Not only were they playing the most horrendous dance music (this is a German restaurant, not a club), I had a hair buried in the bottom of my very bland Spaetzle.  The beer cheese was very watered down, and the "spicy" mustard was just yellow mustard.   As a Donelson resident, this bums me out bc we are already lacking restaurants.

name: The Basement
text: If you want to go to a hole in the wall tiny dive and listen to live music at any time, go here. The seats are ripped up, the people on stage will have a beer with you and the people in the crowd are musicians or locals having a brew with their girlfriend. We came in the middle of the day and the bartender was the sweetest person on Earth, but not pushy. The lady on stage almost seemed offended when I gave her money - there was no tip jar out which I thought was a bummer for them. Maybe people just try their stuff out here and don't expect money.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Had to stop here since it's known as an iconic place to eat in Nashville. I was already expecting the wait to be 2 hours long, so that part didn't bother me a whole lot. Except that our dining experience wasn't really worth the wait. 

The food was good. Most of it was pretty basic that you can find anywhere but there were a couple of dishes that were done really well. However, the sweet tea was not sweet at all and was actually watered down horribly. After a few minutes when some of the ice melted, it tasted like you were drinking straight water. My biggest complaint though had to be all of the bugs. We had an outside table and I kinda knew to expect some bugs since we are Tennessee in the middle of summer. But we couldn't even enjoy eating at all because of all the flies, gnats and mosquitos. There were 2 yellow jackets that even flew into my purse! I'm really surprised that being such a busy and popular place, they don't put a screen around their outside dining area.

That being said, it's definitely a place to visit at least once. They have a little country store, complimentary lemonade and water set up outside, and other little shops to visit while you wait for a table. Our server was very friendly and the food was good. But probably a place to just visit once.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food was awesome! We ordered the fried chicken and the meatloaf and it was the best fried chicken and meatloaf ever! All of the sides are good also! The biscuits and the preserves that come with every meal are so yummy!! Highly recommend buying more from the store behind the restaurant. The service is very friendly and food came out in a timely manner. I would definitely go back next time we were in Nashville!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We've walked by this beer joint several times since it opened and haven't checked it out even though I'm a beer nerd.  So, we went in today while out walking the mall and sat at the bar, I got a German beer and my wife a cider, which she said was very good and they said was exclusive to them.  After some discussion we decided to snack on some fries, these came with "beer" cheese, and "bacon".  Well, the fries had obviously been cooked hours before our arrival and kept in a warming tray which made them limp and lukewarm, the so called beer cheese was, as far as I could tell, cheese wiz out of a can, and the bacon was bacon bits out of a jar.  The server after checking in with us approximately ten minutes after they were delivered by the kitchen runner offered to replace them, needless to say we did not eat many of them, he did not offer a comp. Since we live across town from OpryMills I won't be disappointed that I'm not close by this place as we won't be back.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Loved everything Beers, pretzel& beer cheese, sausages, schnitzel but the MUSTARD is outstanding!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Our bartender was awesome, so friendly and personable, as well as the host and concierge. We didn't make it in to a show, but I've heard great things. I just wasn't interested in the performer unfortunately. 

They have totally customizable flights from their wines by the glass menu, which is really nice. I do wish they'd have a few suggested flights on the menu as well though to keep the tastes complimentary.

We ordered the brussel sprouts, which were pretty good. We got sold on the wild mushroom flatbread. He said it was award winning. It was fine, lots of rapini and pretty salty. Another guest gave us the last couple pieces of his margherita flatbread and I liked that one more. I wish we would've tried the duck pizza instead, to be honest.

There were a lot of enticing menu options. I'll definitely be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The gourmet's Cracker Barrell. 

This place is tremendous Southern cooking.   Bring a heart monitor.  If you're a Southerner, you'll swear your grandma is in the kitchen.   

The ONLY reason I don't give them a 5 star rating is that they're just so hard to get into.  Hour, 2 hour waits are common.  You may have to hike a quarter mile to get there from the back of the parking lot(s).  On the weekends, there's no good time to get in.   The first time you come the shops are enough to keep you occupied, but they lose their charm after a few times.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Really good onion soup! Very nice staff and people in general. Beer was tasty and cold. Can't wait to watch the music. I'll be back.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I was not impressed. I decided to park on the street because I don't mind walking instead of paying the $5 valet. The atmosphere was great and we were seated immediately. Out of the six items on the menu (it seemed) they were out of half of the things on the menu. I wasn't very hungry so I got the brisket taco. They were $11, micro mini in size, little flavor, cold, and the brisket was tough and dry. The risotto balls were great. It took forever to get our checks. I won't be back. There are too many decent restaurants in Nashville to choose from.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
What an interesting and picturesque place. Attended with a work group, and was happily surprised at how much variety is on the menu and as advertised, a great wine selection.

3 stars comes from a bit of a bar issues and the seating arrangement.  When ordering $15 scotch, the bar should know the difference between 'neat', 'on the rocks' and 'one cube'. Several of us had to send back our drinks due to being served incorrectly.  Note to the bar, I can tell by the taste and aesthetics when you just strained the ice out vs pouring the drink correctly, neat as ordered.  Secondly, when you have 8 full size grown men sitting shoulder to shoulder, it makes for an uncomfortable night.  It would have been nice to have a larger and more comfortable table for our group size.

The food was great, everyone loved their orders, and service was prompt.  Overall a good experience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I spent a day in Nashville and was going to head out of town and grab breakfast along the way. We saw the sign on the highway and decided to check it out. So happy we did! The biscuits and jam were the best things ever!!! Out waitress was so sweet. The food came out fast and had generous portions. They even gave me a coffee for the road! Everyone should definitely check this spot out.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loved having bbq and eggs for a classic southern breakfast. The biscuits here are absolutely jaw dropping as well! I do wish I could just get one pancake off the menu rather than only stacks of 3, but the great food makes up for that. Service was outstanding as well, and it really is a good southern dining experience

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Ok Folks, listen real close. If you're visiting Nashville, you have to put Loveless on your list. This place will not disappoint. Tonight I had the smoked pork chops, caramel sweet potatoes, and turnip greens. And it was just like Mom's. The biscuits are life changing, so leave plenty of room for them (they come out as an appetizer). There is plenty to see while you wait for your table, so stop by and enjoy Southern Hospitality at its finest!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Why is this place famous?

The biscuits are good, but they're not magical. Butter and salt. 

We had biscuits and gravy, and the sausage gravy was standard, boring fare. Nothing to it really. 

We'd heard that this place is always crazy busy, so we came first thing in the morning. We were here 15 minutes after they opened - third family in the door - and the service was still terrible. The server brought gravy and said he was going back for a fresh batch of biscuits ... and then got distracted or something. So we got warm biscuits and then had to ask for fresh gravy. My husband ordered a side of cheesy grits that came out later, and sans cheese. 

The side of fresh fruit was good. 

All in all, if you want to check off a tourist destination, fine. (Be prepared: it's priced like a tourist trap.) If you want a good breakfast, go somewhere else.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Breakfast review...Pricey, have to say that right off the bat.  We ordered a la carte for the most part, to try different menu items.  My scrambled eggs were good, not overcooked, the in-house, smoked bacon was really delicious, grits were smooth and the hash brown casserole was tasty but I thought it had a little too much cheese in it.  I know, I know, can there ever be too much cheese?  I  would have like to taste onion, maybe even some green pepper.  The biscuits were very tasty and personally I'm glad they are small.  The country ham was thick (we like it on a the thinner side though), not over-salted and had a great flavor.  The service was excellent, waiter friendly, bringing out a plate of biscuits and 3 servings of homemade jams. We arrived at 7:15am and the cafe was half full.  When we left at around 8am they had a wait.  Though the line was moving, I would suggest making a reservation, even that early!  There are cute little shops surrounding the cafe.  All in all a good experience and we will go back again for other breakfast items and for lunch/dinner.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great food, service, ambiance. Wat there at least once every 10 days. Staff is the best. Have to wait a bit? Just visit the cool shops on property!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best pulled pork I have ever had.  The sides were amazing too...  I highly recommend the hash brown casserole and mac n cheese, which were both excellent.  The biscuits were good but nothing special, although they bring them out complimentary so no complaints.  The jams they serve with them, however, were very good.  Expect a long wait...my wife and I waited 2 hours, but planned ahead and took a scenic drive down the Natchez Trace parkway so no big deal.  Probably not someplace I would eat often but worth at least one trip.  Good place to bring friends or family visiting Nashville.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
We really wanted to like this place since they are getting some music on the books that we like, and want to see, but I will be hard pressed to return. We have been to City Winery twice now. The first time we went, we did as the website had suggested which was to come between 6-7 for dinner before the show. WAY too early, as it was awkward to be in the music venue with all these empty tables around you. It just felt weird. The food wasn't that great either. The only thing we ordered that we liked was the truffle fingerling potatoes. The flatbread was soggy, and the cheese plate was underwhelming and expensive for the stingy portions.  We were disappointed that a winery boasting such a large list doesn't sell any bottle of wine for under $40. 

The second time we went, we ate dinner beforehand and decided to just have some wine during the show. We ordered a 2010 Malbec that she opened right when she got to the table (in the dark - you can't see!) and poured for us to taste, BUT we were never shown the bottle until she had poured it out and walked away. It was 2011. Not a big deal for inexpensive wine, but if I had been buying a $200 bottle that was wrong, I would have been incensed.

When we got the bill, (it had slipped past us on our previous visit) we noticed that they charged the Liquor By The Drink tax that EVERY other restaurant in the ENTIRE STATE builds into their pricing, but City Winery charges it ON TOP of your already overpriced drink. So a $40 is really $46, a $15 whiskey is $17.25 plus sales tax etc...it is in small print on the menu, but you feel gouged already, and then that tax just seems like a big F-You. 

Paying for rude valets who don't even unlock the door for you, much less open it, plus overpriced food that isn't good, and really overpriced drinks just made us feel nickeled and dimed. Unlike others, we did have good service inside the venue. Again, I wanted to like this place - the upstairs patio has beautiful views of downtown and it's a nice space, but we just feel like it's not worth what you end up spending for an evening there.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I'm from California. There no place like this back home. This is one of the best meals at the best price I've ever had. Had fried chicken, mashed potatoes and gravy and creamed corn. Trust me if you are anywhere near this place, get over here.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Bier selection is great.  Food is very authentic.  Had the Leberkase brotchen and it tasted just like what I had for breakfast every morning when I lived in Germany as a kid.  My new favorite place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: What an awesome place! Cool decor, great fiod, fast service! A must go to!!! My best friend and I started our roadtrip here and it was a Friday morning. I was surprised at how busy they were but the service was fast. The food was phenomenal especially the biscuits!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I met up with a friend for lunch on a weekday and was so surprised at how big the restaurant was. Their food was okay, nothing that made me feel like I needed to come back. I was a little surprised that you couldn't substitute side dishes but it wasn't a big problem. The service was great and I'm sure their beer menu is awesome!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Absolutely a blast for fun, excellent German cuisine! Group of 6 enjoyed the in Opry Mills Mall dinner with live music and great beer and food. Very open and loud! Great service and servers all dress authentic. Food $15-21.00. Would highly recommend! I had Black Forest schnitzel! Yum

name: Rocketown
text: It's a good venue. I've been to both the main room and the little white building across the street. The main room is amazing. I went for a CMT taping of Crossroads so they definitely had a great setup. Many times venues overdue it or even under do it so the sound quality of the bands is very mediocre, but not here. Excellent.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We visited the Loveless (again) during one of the busiest times of the year for Nashville! CMA week. We even arrived at 9am. Waited ZERO minutes for a table and was promptly served those amazing melt in your mouth biscuits that I crave the other 364 days of the year when I can't visit. Our meal was perfect! I always recommend the Loveless to anyone visiting Nashville. Most folks go the "long way" there but it is quite a bit nicer to drive Broadway away from Nashville to see some beautiful homes along the way instead of freeway. I've sent hockey teams to the Loveless in the past and they are still talking about it. And hoping to have another tourney there this year (me too! I wanna come back). Thanks for consistent excellent customer service and food quality. I never fear recommending the Loveless to folks! See you soon!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best home style cooking you can get! It seems to always be busy but it's worth the wait. Plus they have little stores to keep you entertained while you wait. Everyone is very friendly and have southern hospitality. After getting seated and ordering, the wait for your food isn't that long. And if anything is wrong they will make it right. Pies are to die for! And FYI the moonshine are very strong!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Just freaking good. I had the fried chicken (1/4 white meat - amazing), turnip greens (amazing), and mashed potatoes (really, really good). And of course, biscuits with blackberry jam that was to die for. This is one of those places where you just have to stop caring temporarily about things like calories, sodium, etc., and simply go for it.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Brunch this morning. Good food huevos rancheros and build your biscuit. The decor is awsome and concert venue looks great. It has a warm fire place right in the middle of the room. Will return for dinner and drinks.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
To begin, the food was four stars. We had the fried chicken and catfish, with creamed corn and caramel sweet potatoes. All of it was very good. The jam was also delicious! 

The reason I rate loveless three stars is because of the hostess and the lady working the cash register.  Not only did they lack southern hospitality, they lacked any hospitality. I am hoping it was just an off day and not a usual occurrence.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits are heavenly, sides are flavorful and fresh. We had the fried chicken, I felt that the crust was a bit dry, but overall, a great meal. Great atmosphere and a cozy gift shop. The jams and jellies are to die for!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The single best biscuits I have ever had in my life. In fact the only downside to the biscuits themselves is the fact that I don't live in Nashville and they have ruined all other biscuits for me. 

The atmosphere of the restaurant is quaint and clean and the service from our waitress was fantastic. Unfortunately there is quite a long wait on the weekends but it is well worth it and they do have outdoor seating for you to wait on and some neat little stores nearby to peruse. 

In conclusion the biscuits are so good that I will someday return to Nashville just to come get these biscuits again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Went for lunch, arrived quarter to 12, around 15mins wait then people started to arrive. Friendly staff esp our server Mark. The biscuits are really good. Too much food, we brought home some. Love the strawberry preserves.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Be prepared to wait a long time with a lot of tourists on weekends! But then be prepared for some of the best southern food ever. I have never had anything that I did not like. This place is definitely worth all the hype, and the biscuits are delicious.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I love the atmosphere and we always eat here before seeing a movie at the opry mills regal. The fish and chips are my favorite. I prefer sitting in the bar area because it can get really loud. I prefer the guy entertainment over the girl because he sings du hast by Rammstein and we always request it. Love it! Lol!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Just WOW! From the moment we arrived, everything was perfect. The decor is modern, but homey. The venue has wonderful sound and allows for the most intimate feeling. The food is....ahhh, simply delectable. They have a wide variety. Ask about the specials. I bet you change your mind five times trying to pick the best item. 
I have nothing but praise for every aspect of City Winery. Don't miss a chance to dine here, and if at all possible, take in a show.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
One of our good friends who LOVES food came into town so I brought him for a taste of the Loveless Cafe!  This is an update so check my first review for more details.

When we sat down at 6:50pm, we learned that their daily special (Chicken and dumplings on this particular Wednesday) was out already.  My friend wanted to try it so that was a minor disappointing start to our meal but with so many other delicious options, we weren't sad for long.

Some updates on the food experience:
Pulled pork - tender, flaky (shreds apart), smokey and flavorful.  It was much more moist this time!
Fried chicken - crispy, moist but lacked flavor inside with good seasoning on the outside
Fried catfish - squeeze a little lemon on the top, a little dip into the tartar sauce and yes, the bombness in your mouth.

A lowlight was having undercooked hush puppies served to me but the server quickly replaced it with another requested side (creamed corn).  Fried okra, Mac 'n Cheese, and sweet peach tea rounded out the meal.  Note to self for future orders, I don't like their turnip greens - a bit bland with a kick of pepper/spice.

Tip: It's always good to call ahead for a shorter wait time.

Extra: my friend is really into smoking stuff so we stopped by their smoker and were allowed to take a peek into how they make their smoked meats.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Big birds flying across the sky
Throwing shadows on our eyes
Leave us...
[Loveless], [loveless], [loveless]

Having read of "bottomless biscuits", we were disappointed by a lack thereof, apparently not part of the slow service and separate charges for a change in teas (but not for refills after the switch, but given the speed, it wasn't worth mentioning because our time is valuable) despite no mention originally.
$37.79 before tip for:
biscuit sampler with chicken and hashbrown casserole (satisfying)
breakfast sampler (tasty)
two sweet teas, and a peach iced tea (the latter was excellent, the former eh)
fudge pie (tasty but nontraditional)
No creamed corn until 11 (foolish)

If we hadn't also planned a Belle Meade visit as part of our morning, I would've been a bit disappointed about trekking out here (if this is still considered Nashville, you folks really take some liberties with the zoning). Apparently they were on Throwdown, and management changed at some point recently, causing the commercialization that kinda ruined the charm for me.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place was really good. A colleague told me about this place and I gave it a try. The food and the service was superb. The hash brown casserole was my fave

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Great venue. Food options aren't great in choices or pricing. I'll be back, but I'll eat first.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: One of my all-time  favorites and a must for out of town visitors! Average wait is about an hour but the shops on property will help that pass quickly. I have always preferred breakfast here but I've never had a bad meal.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Good Food, Great Staff, can be a little oud and overwelming at times though. The first time we went in we ate at the floor table, community style, and the place was rockin. The 2nd time, we ate a wall table, hightop, leggs dangling. The last couple of times, we have sat at the bar Hightops, and it's quieter, more comfortable, and enjoyable.

Recommend for a date night for sure.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Very good food.   Service was phenomenal.   Sophia was so nice and helpful with the menu and recommending drinks.  We will be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Traditional American breakfast options, nothing spectacular. They are famous for their biscuits and homemade jams and I have to say they didn't disappoint, which for someone who's never liked biscuits is saying a lot. The steak, eggs and home fries were okay but under seasoned. The French toast was also pretty bland and traditional.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Possibly the best breakfast restaurant I have visited. Great history, atmosphere, and traditional southern breakfast. There was a wait but well worth it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I went for lunch with my wife. The food was very good. it's traditional southern fair. Portion sizes are large. I had the fried pork chops and my wife had the turkey sandwich. Everything tasted good except the fried green tomatoes. They were breaded with a cornmeal and flour mixture that was heavy on flour. I know they are difficult to bread with a heavy cornmeal mixture but they are so much better that way. We will be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is incredible! Worth the drive and worth the wait! You must try the pie! So save room!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Very nice area to get away from the crazy city atmosphere with some great southern meals.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great biscuits.  Friendly service.  Amazing biscuits.  Good breakfast.  Everything was enjoyable, and if it were near where we lived, it would be on our everyday to-do list.  Our cholesterol is glad it isn't, but this was some good good comfort breakfast food.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We kind of stumbled into this place by accident. What a great accident. This gem is off the beat and track and is just so cute. We had a 25 minute wait but killed time walking through the little shops on the property. Such fun all American trinkets. The food was delicious and service was with a smile. The biscuits are so yummy with a variety of jams and the ham was so fresh.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Food is like eating at Mom's kitchen. Tasty and all is fresh!  We had meatloaf, waffles, and pulled pork and they were all tastyyyyy!  Get to them early and shop around the shops..

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Normally I don't rip restaurants, but passing your cost of business on to your customers is WRONG! An excise and lbtd tax on top of sales tax? This is a joke, right? No, it's not...mediocre food and paying for another meal in tax? Don't think so, never again!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Average breakfast with a 2 hour wait no matter when you go. This place has a great reputation, but I was unimpressed. The ham was too salty for me and the sausage patties were dry, but I guess that may be how country ham is supposed to be? Whatever the reason, it's rare that I will leave food on my plate, but I just couldn't eat the ham. Biscuits were good, but "best biscuits in Nashville" is a stretch. It's a cool location with a few things to do (like giant Jenga, free lemonade, and some gift shops), but its out of the way. I would recommend other breakfast places closer to downtown Nashville (Fido, Tavern, Jacksons, Noshville, or if you're looking for more of a low-key country breakfast, Pancake pantry whose wait times are comparable to Loveless).

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Let me start.
Could not find the place from inside the mall.
Sat at the bar took 15 minutes for bartender to serve us.
Beer selection and quality excellent.
Food so so ,wifes burger overcooked.Fries ice cold bartender brought out some new ones on a different plate.not much better.Plates sat a long time before they were removed.
suggestion get a pretzel and drink the great beer and forget the food.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Eat here every time my parents come into town because my mother is obsessed with their southern food! Have waited no less than 1.5 hours for a table on Sunday afternoons but well worth the wait. The biscuits alone are worth any wait! They are to die for!!!! Pretty sure I could eat the whole plate of them myself. I've only had fried chicken which is so good. The breading on the chicken is so darn crispy! Banana pudding is good, but can't say I love the other desserts. Definitely a fun atmosphere and have always had excellent service. It's one of those iconic places you have to try when in Nashville!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: So lets start off with the fact that this was my mother's birthday. We walked in and greeted the first person we saw. He told us to go by the concierge desk. They were not warm at all. The immediately directed us back to the initial desk. At this time the awkward gentleman said that he would be giving us the tour. The sommelier was extremely lack luster. He had the wine already picked out.He also seemed forced to have convo and not very personalable. We paid for a wine tour I definitely expected this experience to be a tad more elevated and exciting. I'm not exactly sure why they charge so much for a tour that lands you only between the wine cellar and the front door. Having been in service industry for many years, I find this experience and level of service to be underwhelming. I honestly only gave it 3 stars because my sister was able to talk to the staff about our experience same day. They did their best to make it right.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Friendly and good service. Pretzel was to die for, onion soup was amazing. Worth the trip.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We absolutely loved this restaurant! It's super busy on the weekends, but if you catch an early brunch or lunch during the week, it's perfect. It's definitely a place we will continue to visit throughout our lives.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits here rival anything you have ever eaten! They are incredible and they never stop bringing them to the table. Served with homemade peach, strawberry and blackberry preserves. As my cousin so aptly put it as she bit into her third biscuit "this is my church"!!! The coconut cream pie is my all time favorite from anywhere I have eaten. The custard is thick, rich with just the right amount of coconut and sweetness. The meatloaf is juicy and the tangy sauce they put on it is so yummy. Not a ketchup paste at all. Loved the green beans and the white beans too. And the pulled pork. This is a must go for every one

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We opted to get take out and eat at nearby picnic table rather than wait the 1 1/2 hours. It was a Saturday, so I suppose that explains the long wait. We waited about ten minutes for our food.

The biscuits were really good. I wouldn't say they were life-changing, but I really enjoyed them and could have eaten about a hundred. I got the sampler plate with two orders of fried chicken and BBQ, with creamed corn and fries on the side.

The fried chicken was awesome, not the best I've ever had, but definitely in my top 5 all time. I wish they would have served it with honey, but that's just me being extremely picky--I'm sure I could have asked for it. The outside was super crispy, the fat had been rendered down, and the inside was moist. The BBQ was really good as well, with a great smoky flavor. I really liked seeing the open kitchen around the BBQ pit.

The creamed corn was delicious. The cashier recommended it, and that was a good call. It was creamy, flavorful, and better than any other cream corn I've ever had before in my life. The fries were your standard fries.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We were able to visit on a weekday, so we didn't have to wait in line which was a huge plus. The biscuits were delicious, complimentary and hot - plus three jams to try. I had a typical breakfast - eggs, bacon and grits and my friend had chicken and waffles with a side of hashbrowns. Personally, I love grits and I thought these were amazing. Everything else was great too and the store was cute. That being said, I gave it 4 stars since it is so far removed from Nashville and it did feel slightly overrated.

name: Big Shotz
text: Awesome bar I came across while I was in Nashville for my birthday. Cheap beers and great entertainment. They have awesome Jell-O shots there! I went to this bar a few times while I was there!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great comfort food. Great service. Cute little place! While waiting for a table we explored the shops and buildings around the property.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is second time we visited this place with same great friends.  First time we thought they had some things to tweak.  Today all the details have been figured out.  Phenomenal service by Jeremy.  Food was awesome,  potato pancakes were as good as my moms. Beer is the best in town.  Music was authentic.  Thank you for a great time and the personalized service we received from the waiting team at our table of seven.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This is a great place just outside of town. Most of the food is greasy, fatty, and pure goodness. If you're looking for healthy options, this is probably not your place. But if, like me, you occasionally like to eat way too much fried food and wash it down with sweet tea, then this is worth a stop. 

I've found that it's a nice place to bring out-of-town guests. In fact, that's the only time I ever go. But there's lots of country music references and decor, which is very Nashville. 

The wait is normally long (an hour on average), but there are shops and corn hole boards, etc to pass the time, especially if the whether is nice.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Last night, we went to our favorite restaurant to have a small celebration of life. Just four of us. As always, we were greeted by 3 smiling faces and, quickly put on the waiting list. (At that time, it was 35 minutes.) 30 minutes later, our buzzer was buzzing.  We were seated and greeted by our server, Owen. WOW!!! They were BUSY. Owen is an amazing server and we were delighted to be in his area. Each of us discussed how the food placed in front of us was perfect. Absolutely perfect. Yes, we are regulars. Yes, I notice everything. I have worked food service for over 35 years. Everything was perfect but, we wondered why we were not greeted by a manager. They always greet each table. Well, I got my answer. After leaving the ladies room, I passed the kitchen. The tension was visually clear. The manager we were hoping to come by our table was in the kitchen, yelling at the staff. I wanted to tell her how much we loved our night and thank her. She had no idea I was even there. Cristy truly let me down at the end of it all.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I was surprised with this place! I didn't expect it to be anything great, but it was good! The atmosphere is amazing. Inside is beautiful, wood tables, pretty bar, & then they have a neat music venue where you can eat & listen to music. They also asked you if you would like to try a little of the wine of the night when they seat you, which I thought was a nice touch. 
Our server was great when it came to picking a wine. He asked what I liked & then suggested one, which was very good. He did get a little overwhelmed with other tables & forgot to check on us a couple of times, but hey, it happens.
The food was good, but not as good as it could have been. We had the Crispy Risotto Balls & they were not that full of flavor. Somewhat bland, as well as the sauce that came with them. The Alfresco's Cavatelli was good, but it seemed like it had been sitting out for a minute because when it arrived it was cold & the pasta did not seem cooked well. Also, it most definitely could have used more flavoring or sauce. 
The menu is somewhat confusing & all over the place. I think I need to go back & try a few more things & speak to the waiter more about the menu options. I most definitely will be going back for the atmosphere and wine selection!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: By far, worth the drive! If you're visiting Nashville this place is a must be in your To-Do list! Very good service and fabulous food!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is a bit overrated. I love the decor and the history behind loveless cafe, but the food was sub par. The service was excellent though. I had the Country fried steak and to be quite honest, i've had a lot better. I hope this was an isolated expierence.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I don't know why it's taken me so long to write this review. You'd think out of all the times that I've been and had to wait an hour and a half before being seated that I could find the time to write one up! But no, I've usually found something else to do. They do give you a little disk that vibrates when you're ready to be seated. The Loveless has a few gift shops around that you can browse in. Some of the gifts are really cute but touristy expensive. Now...good lawd the food. Biscuits are made from scratch and are light and fluffy. They come free with your meal along with 3 preserves. If my memory serves me correct they're strawberry, blackberry and orange marmalade...or peach. I don't know. They're all tasty though! I ALWAYS order a side of cheese grits! I'm telling you I drive clear across town for their grits. So freaking good. They serve breakfast all day. I keep telling myself that I'll try something else then never do...because cheese grits, yo. We've tried a variety of things and have never been disappointed. They have excellent bbq, hashbrown casserole, fried potatoes, country fried steak...it's all good. This restaurant is the epitome of classic southern food. Service is kind of hit or miss. You've got the servers that have been there awhile that found their niche and are on a roll. Then there are the newbies that shuffle through things. They're all right but don't give you the "Loveless experience". Parking can be a bit rough depending on when you go. I've never NOT found a parking spot but you might have to walk a ways. No biggie. After eating all that fried food, a bit of walking might do you some good!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I've heard wonderful things about Loveless Cafe so finally made it out there. We went on a Friday morning to avoid the weekend rush. It was a beautiful 20min drive outside of Nashville and managed to get in after a short 10min wait. It was busy on a Friday so I can imagine the craziness on the weekend. Good news is of you did have a wait there is a outdoor area to walk around and buy keepsakes, souvenirs, etc. 

The biscuits were good but not as I had imagined. I had such high expectations. The trio of preserves were delicious and paired nicely with the hot biscuits. We didn't order anything special--eggs and bacon/sausage. Very average or typical to any breakfast joint. I would have been happy with my coffee and biscuits. Service was good!

The biscuit mix you buy in the store is quite good and you only add buttermilk. Very similar tasting to the real thing. 

I will return--and try lunch but during the week.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great place to eat and walk around and do some short shopping. The jam with the biscuits is amazing. The hostess and waitress were both knowledgeable and employees loved their job. The chicken and waffles was perfectly cooked the skin on the chicken was to die for a must try! I also had a blue moon it came in a mason jar and was super smooth.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I took my folks here for brunch while they were in town visiting.  The biscuits are incredible (and bottomless) -- well worth the wait and drive.  I had the fried chicken and biscuits and will definitely be back.  Be ready to wait at least one hour, but there are some shops to browse in while you wait -- we brought a deck of cards.

Very reasonably priced given their demand and the food was very good.  Friendly service, great spicy, strong bloody mary's.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Food is good.... More of a tourist spot
Had dinner sampler ( catfish, ham, fried chicken with hash brown casserole n Mac cheese) 
Catfish-- great light batter
Fried chicken- crispy. Could use more seasoning
Country ham- salty 
Biscuits - great with the blackberry jams

Drink
Blue moon -- great with the moonshine 

Is it worth the wait? Depends

name: Loveless Cafe
text: WOW.  Don't go anywhere else in Nashville for breakfast. Or lunch. Or dinner. Every little thing we had here was incredible. Tammy, our waitress, was a total pro!  She was so sweet and I never ran out of coffee or water once!  Service was quick but we were never rushed and had a great relaxing breakfast with plenty of leftovers to take for snacking later.  What a gem!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Had to do it, too many friends recommending the biscuits etc. 
Flew into Nashville and went straight to the Loveless Cafe. They clearly have this thing figured out - multiple parking lots, mail order hams, a general store, and an art store. All are there to keep you entertained during your looooong wait for a table. 
We arrived at Loveless around 1100 and were told our wait would be 70-80 minutes for a table. No problem, figured it would be worth the wait. Like everyone else, we cruised the stores and wandered around. After 45 minutes, we were buzzed. Yes, they have buzzers to let you know when your table is ready - and they work anywhere on the compound. 
We were seated and quickly met by our waitress. Service was good, fast and efficient. Drinks, biscuits and jams were on our table in 5 min or so. We ordered and had our food in 10. Everything was good, not spectacular, but good. 
Would we go back, you bet. Would we wait another 45 min for a table? Ummm, doubt it. But, again, the food was good and you have to go once to check it out.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Amazing southern cuisine! We dined at Loveless for breakfast, which was absolutely delicious. I ordered the Biscuit Sampler Platter with cheese grits. It came with 4 slider size biscuit sandwiches of pulled pork, fried chicken, medium rare steak, and ham. All deliciously seasoned and cooked perfectly. The cheese grits were also really tasty. This meal really hit the spot.

My boyfriend ordered the half order ham & eggs with hash brown casserole. After he tasted my pulled pork, he wished he'd ordered the pulled pork & eggs. Regardless, he enjoyed his meal and I couldn't help but sample the delicious hash brown casserole.

We were visiting from out of town, so we were excited to buy their cookbook, available for purchase in their gift store.

I'm still thinking about just how tasty this meal was & can't wait to make some of the dishes at home!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Great food, great music, great fun! Our family ended our reunion vacation with 19 of us eating here on Friday night. Kids and adults alike had a great time - and we now have a 2-year old who yells "oy, oy, oy!"

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Everyone raves about this place,  however I wasn't impressed.  The famous biscuits were OK.  I have definitely had better.  Our waiter wasn't really friendly and some of our food was burnt.  We were kind over the place and didn't bother to say anything.  We ate less than half the food.  The shops are a little over priced but a cute set up.

name: Rocketown
text:
I was skeptical when a friend first suggested that I check out Rocketown as an event venue... and boy, was I wrong. 

Rocketown is the jam. 

With room for up to 1500 of your friends , the main venue space has fantastic built-in lighting and sound system so that your don't have to outsource for these additional costs. The attached complimentary parking lot and available surrounding street parking are a luxury to have for a venue space, especially one that is located Downtown! 

I love the expansive and industrial space that makes up the main room. It just beckons you to make the space your own whether you're producing a concert, wedding, conference, fundraiser, or really, the sky is the limit. I planned a community outreach fundraiser for 1000 here and had the best experience! We brought in food sponsors, adult beverage sponsors, and various nonprofit booths into the massive space and it felt and looked fabulous. Did I mention Big Wheel drag races out in the parking lot? Only for Yelp Helps, folks....

Throw in the fact that there is a generously sized stage, up to date bathrooms, and multiple entrance points and you have a ton of room to spread out your own event concept. You also have the option to rent out the smaller "White Building"which is across the way as it is more suited for events 500 or under. The Skate Park is also available for rental and use too.

A cozy "living room" setup greets when you walk into the front doors and you may be surprised to see a fully operational coffee bar filled with java, snacks, and other refreshments. I should set up my "office" her once a week because it's a nice environment to get some work done or relax. You'll see anything from students and creative types to professionals sipping on a latte and working on projects here. They also schedule art exhibits, open mics, and other events within this space from time to time.

And, I can't say enough about Mary Virginia Settle who is the dedicated Director Of Operations here. From the first time I reached out to inquire about using the event space to the cleanup of our event, this lady is nothing short of fantastic to work with. She's always looking out for everyone's best interest and not afraid to roll up her sleeves to help ensure that your goals are met. I wish that I could work with people like her every day!

TIP: As if there isn't enough wonderful things going on here, the work and community outreach that Rocketown does for the youth in our community is admirable. They have afterschool programs, summer camps, and other events throughout the year that help kids off the streets. Rocketown is a 501c3 nonprofit so you may also make donations or contribute to this wonderful place!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
First impression: really cool space. Warm and inviting---intimate for a concert setting, but not too shoulder-to-shoulder, if you know what I mean.

I won tickets to a Lord Huron secret show today, and we ventured here for the show and lunch. My boyfriend and I both ordered the burger and substituted sweet potato fries and zucchini fries, respectively. Service took a while, our burgers came out lukewarm and flavorless... and the substitutions were not made. I was supremely disappointed--the burger looked AMAZING... and the taste didn't match. The show was amazing, and that was the saving grace for the afternoon.

Valet is $5... mostly, the experience was meh. I wouldn't mind going back fo ra show, but definitely won't plan to eat here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This was on our list of places to visit while in Nashville!  Even though it is out of the way it was so worth the stop!  Quaint setting and amazing food.  I could not choose what I wanted so I got the biscuit sampler!!!!!  Best decision - the chicken was amazing!!!!  Their hash brown casserole is a must try!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is all about country BBQ, but the food does not deliver. My husband ordered pulled pork and fried chicken, with sweet potato and fried okra sides.  I'm vegetarian, so I was there for him; the menu had no veg entrees, although it did mark the side dishes that were flavored with meat. I ordered a speciality salad and sides of fried green tomatoes and mac and cheese. Salad was a pile of lettuce, overpriced at $9, fried green tomatoes were good, the other sides were mediocre at best. I thought perhaps my husband was at least enjoying some really great BBQ, but he reported that although the chicken was perfectly cooked, it lacked flavor, and the pork was nothing special.
We waited forty minutes in sweltering heat to get a table, and we had a reservation. There are great restaurants in Nashville, I can't imagine why anyone would choose to go here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wow. The biscuits were as amazing as all the previous reviewers stated. And I got a salad, which seems a sin at a great little cafe such as this... In my defense, my husband and I have been visiting Tennessee for almost a week and the good southern cooking is starting to give me more of a souvenir than I want. The salad was only so-so. The peanut butter pie I had afterwards made me have an audible "mmm" with each bite. The pie alone would warrant a plane ticket back to Nashville in a heart beat. Worth the wait. Worth the hype. The Loveless Cafe is wonderful.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Sunday evening @ 7. Very few patrons. We had a party of 6. 20 minute wait. I assume they were short servers. Our server was in a rush to get our order. They were out of fries, cheddarwurst. Sauerkraut was cold and tasty like the can was just opened. We are from an area with a Genuine Hoffbrau house. These people should stop pretending. Waiter explained nothing and obviously in a hurry to leave.

name: Big Shotz
text: Cheap double shots that taste great, fantastic music and service! If you're visiting downtown Nashville for the first time like I was, this is a great starting point for Broadway night life. It's a quiet, small dive bar with a large variety of drinks and shots (particularly if you love fireball). Wish I'd found this place sooner in my Nashville journey!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Fantastic service. We went in on a slow night because there wasn't a show scheduled for the evening. We had a fantastic wine flight- Classic CW flight- and enjoyed their happy hour Margherita flatbread. 
The bartender and Sommelier were extremely personable and knowledgeable about wines. They were also very friendly and great conversationalists. Excellent experience.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Hey look, this was a great venue for a great band-- the psychedelic furs. The band played great, but their performance was squelched by the incompetent sound person. The bass was way too boomy, and the whole sound was a pile of mush! I don't want to be hypercritical, but this was the worst sound that I've heard at a concert since i played at my junior high. On a positive note, the hummus plate and the duck tacos were delightful!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Fried chicken OMG. Biscuit OMG. Definitely the best biscuits I have ever had and top 5 fried chicken. The biscuits were so warm and fluffy and add their homemade preservatives and you have biscuit heaven. The fried chicken was so good, the skin was crispy but not too oily. The meat wasn't dry, and it tasted really fresh. So good!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Absolutely off the charts.
Got the pulled pork plate.. With baked beans and slaw
Everything was awesome!!
The only thing that would've made it better was corona light.. Had to settle for bud light

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Mmmmmmm biscuits.....and killer jams (blackberry is my favorite). A must stop for breakfast and cute gifts!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wow!!! Most amazing biscuits ever! I got the country fried steak with fried green tomatoes, and it was the best I have ever had. Our waitress was the nicest person!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Waited an hour and a half only to sit out on the patio and be extremely hot. The saving grace was the hash brown casserole.

name: Big Shotz
text: Best place to go to in Nashville!! The bartenders are awesome and they have great deals !!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: One word: AMAZING. Outside of downtown Nashville but worth the trip. Everybody was super friendly and even though there was a 2 hr wait because of the 4th of July holiday, we were patient and it was worth the wait. Highly recommend it.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
In regards to City Winery and their concert menu, it doesn't make sense that they have such a limited menu compared to their dining room. The cheapest wine is $8 for 5.5 oz. with tax it comes close to $10. That's ridiculous for such a small glass of wine. 

A friend and I tried the beet & bacon flatbread because we didn't have much money to spend. The combination of the cheese, beet, bacon, arugula, balsamic vinaigrette and some other ingredient just wasn't quite right and we weren't up for trying the mushroom and something other gross combination. 

The seats in the house aren't too bad, we were sitting in the back. Their sound guy had the instruments up louder than the vocals making it hard to hear the 2 bands that played. Their lighting was alright. 

The server at our table didn't show up very often and so we had to sit a while longer than we wanted to just to wait for the check. 

Also if you don't want to pay $20 cash for valet you have to park on the street and walk a while. 

Overall I think this is a great space for intimate shows, but I think it's outrageously overpriced when you're already paying a large amount for tickets. This place is obviously just trying to get every penny squeezed out of you.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Just landed in Nashville and this was the first place I went. Entered the business and immediately felt the local vibe.  The menu was amazing and I decided to go with red velvet pancakes, eggs, bacon and potatoes.  Perfect breakfast! The velvet pancakes were like a piece of cake. Oh yes the biscuits were served as appetizers with jam and honey, a must.  The only reason this place is not a 5star is because the prices are a bit high for breakfast. Maybe I'm just cheap, this place is great!!!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Worth the drive. Made the mistake if eating 3 of those wonderful biscuits BEFORE breakfast and was stuffed afterwards. Great food! We had a 25 minute wait but there are other buildings/shops to look around in while you wait to be paged. Very homey place. It's like eating at home and being served by your mother.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Don't buy the hype. 
The wait is too long and it's nothing special. You can get the same experience and quality of food from Cracker Barrel. If the wait were less than an hour and a half and it wasn't outside town, then I'd say go for it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: What's not to love? If your a fried chicken and southern hospitality fan...this is the place for you. It gets a good crowd, but it's a big place and there is plenty of parking. The service is always welcoming, quick and pleasant. The food is plentiful and delicious. I am getting a hankering for some chicken just writing this review! It's a nice drive in the country to get to Loveless. Overall a pleasurable dining experience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
One word (that has been said a million times before): BISCUITS!! Worth coming here alone.

My chicken fried steak was fine...nothing amazing, but hit the spot. I also liked the biscuits and gravy that my sister ordered. Service was super friendly!

Didn't love the desserts weirdly enough. Expect a long wait, but there's lots of fun little shops on property that make the wait bearable.

I'll be back!

name: The Basement
text: Two guys making out in front of the stage this weekend. Mikes reply when my wife brought it up was very put-offish. Something to the effect of, if you don't like it leave. Enough said Mike. We won't be back. Too bad, we've seen some good shows there over the years. But, there are many places in Nashville to see good original music without dealing with rude owners and the gay scene.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
OMFG the biscuits. THE BISCUITS, PEOPLE! 

I went here for breakfast on Sunday with my husband and two of our friends. We arrived around 8am and there was already a wait. We only had to wait about 15 minutes for a table for 4, but we must have just barely beat the rush, because while we were waiting to be seated I overheard wait times of up to 45 minutes for other small groups.

Moral of the story, if you are going on a weekend: ARRIVE EARLY.

The first round was biscuits with homemade preserves. The strawberry and blackberry were the true standouts here; we all agreed the peach was just okay, if only because it is more mild in flavor. I could have only eaten biscuits and left a happy customer.

Honestly I ate so many biscuits that I couldn't finish my cinnamon raisin french toast and sausage. Our breakfast entrees were good, but again....THE BISCUITS.

Come here for the biscuits, maybe even take some to go. You won't be disappointed.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Had not heard of this place until they had a Groupon.  You don''t need one to get a great meal for a great deal.  The roasted broccoli and beet salad was great.  The turkey with blackberry aioli sandwiches are great.  The server was excellent. And they have valet parking that I'm a great fan of. We didn't go for a show or concert, just for lunch.  That's enough for me to go back again.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Had a flatbread and was really chewy and tough. My friend dishes didn't look good either (trout and steak)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: There honestly isn't a bad thing I can say about this place. The wait was long - an hour and a half- but they combatted boredom with outdoor games, lemonade, shops to browse, and free snacks. The wait breezed by, and it was worth it. Once inside, our waiter was very friendly and attentive. The walls are decorated with thank you notes and signed portraits from Oprah to George Strait. Our biscuits were excellent and the preserves only made them better. All of my food was well seasoned and delicious - I had mashed potatoes, beans, greens and creamed corn. Everyone enjoyed their food and we plan on going back. Definitely stop if you are in Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
BEST THING I ATE EVER.  My husband quoted on Facebook, "Lord, If I could eat any more, I would!"

This is a must do when visiting Nashville.  However, we need to pace ourselves better because we're always too full for dessert.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This new place is great. Wonderful staff and managers making sure your experience is superb. Wonderful food that is traditional and plenty of it. And the beers on tap are the exact selection a German joint should have. Can't beat four varieties of Hofbrau. Highly recommend making this a lunch or dinner stop soon!

name: The Basement
text: The Basement is an intimate (code word for tiny) bar and music space below Grimey's records on 8th avenue. If you can't find a spot in the small dedicated parking lot, there is plenty of street parking in the residential neighborhood that surrounds it. One important thing to know about the Basement is they typically book two main acts a night. The good thing about this is if you're going to see the first act, you know the show will start and end on time. As the wife of a musician, this is big. It's a huge annoyance to think a band will start at 8 and they end up not starting till closer till 10 and before you know it, you're not leaving to come home till well after midnight. The bad thing about this two main acts a night is if you've come to see the first one and paid your cover, you'll have to leave and come back in, paying another cover for the second show. But, I also understand they want to pay the bands. There's not a lot of tables and chairs, so unless you're there super early, prepare to stand. Again, not a big deal as it's a small venue so there's really not a bad area to be.

name: Rocketown
text:
My coworker used Rocketown to host his wedding and reception. Before coming here, I was worrying if this place would have enough parking spaces for 300+ guests, considered its downtown location. The groom convinced us not to worry about parking and he was right. Parking was plenty for 300+ guests (don't leave any valuables in your car). Rocketown itself, was a large and spacious venue. I went to several weddings before in different venues and this one was probably the largest.

Since the Chinese/Vietnamese food in Nashville is below to average. My friend hired Happy Valley (chef and servers) from Atlanta to come down to serve the guests. I've never thought they would have a kitchen in here, but they did. All of the food came out fresh and steaming hot! The stage was spacious and great for playing live music (He hired singers too). The sound system was awesome. It was like watching a mini live concert. In addition, this place is well-kept and clean, even the restrooms were so clean (A++++). They had more than 5 rooms so we didn't have to wait in line. This was the first time I didn't have to wait in line to use the restroom at a wedding (I went in more than twice. Blame it on the alcohol!). 

My only complaint is the place was a bit too dark for a wedding. I'm not a fan of eating in the dark. It was hard to enjoy the food. I couldn't tell what dish they put on the table until I took a closer look. Also, most of the photos came out very dark (with flash!) like we were at a club. Other than that, I think this is a great place for hosting weddings and receptions. I would recommend Rocketown to friends and family for hosting big events.

2013/#69

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Read about this cafe as one of the must things to do while in the vicinity. So I trusted the reviews and blogs and drove for about a half hour out of Nashville to find this place. I had been warned about wait times and being a Friday visit, I didn't want to take chances. Also the owner had just mentioned that they now take reservations in non-peak periods through OpenTable. So got a reservation and its a good thing I did, cause when I arrived, there were a lot of people waiting outside. For me, didn't wait long, about five minutes and I had a table, thanks to the reservation. So definitely consider making a reservation.
First impressions, its off a highway, and sort of like a small neighborhood with gift shops all around the restaurant. Its definitely popular, found a ton of people there.
When the server arrives, they get you a biscuit sampler, and three different kinds of jam. My favorite was the strawberry, but the biscuits were really wow, just delicious and so soft. Had to leave in a rush, so got the pancakes and left in a hurry, but the biscuits definitely make it worth driving over.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Eh. If you haven't been you have to go. It is a tourist thing to do in Nashville. Overall it is overpriced for ok food. 
100% for tourists. 
Cute grounds though. Decent amount of things to do during the 2/3 hour wait for breakfast on the weekends.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Every time I travel to Nashville, I come eat at the Loveless Café.  It's a good atmosphere, the food is always good and I love the atmosphere.  I travel down the Natchez Trace Parkway often and I don't know which I like the best!  They're both at the top of my "good" list.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I enjoyed my time at the City Winery. The menu is limited, but nice. Also, the items are a bit pricey for dinner. However, there are more affordable items like the appetizers. We ordered the Margherita Flat Bread, and it was delicious! The portion size was large enough for a dinner portion. The parmesan truffle fries were yummy as well. I was disappointed to see they did not have sangria on the menu. However, when I told the bartender, she whipped me up something on the fly, and it was incredible!! They need to add it to the menu!!! The service was great. We also saw an improv show that evening, and it was a great time. I would love to go back for another show. It was a great venue and nice place for a date!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Worth the wait!  My fiance and I were in town for one night, and a Food Network junkie friend recommended the Loveless for breakfast.  We were warned ahead of time of the wait, so we were mentally prepared.  They have a great system using a pager that works all around the grounds, which include shaded benches, gift shops, coffee and sweet tea stations (complimentary).  We were pleased that our wait time was actually about half of the quoted time.

We were greeted by a very friendly and enthusiastic waitress named JD.  My fiance is from the Midwest and knows his way around a carb-laden breakfast menu.  The SoCal native in me doesn't know red-eye gravy from grits.  JD was more than happy to educate me.  With her advice, I decided upon everything "southern"; cheese grits, biscuits and sausage gravy, fried green tomatoes, and eggs and bacon.  

My review may not be truly qualified, as I have no basis for comparison of southern food, but, oh my, was it delicious!  It was a bit of a fluke for me to be in Nashville in the first place, and I will probably never return.  With that knowledge, I savored every bite, plus about five extra bites that I should have resisted. 

My fiance enjoyed his chicken fried steak, hash brown casserole, and plenty of warm biscuits.  

Make your way to the Loveless if you find yourself in Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Was excited to go here. It felt rushed,the food mass produced and bland and the seating was in really tight quarters. The service was friendly however. Go somewhere else

name: Loveless Cafe
text: What can we say that hasn't been said?  This place is amazing and still serves up a true southern specialty of good food and hospitality.  The chicken is a must with its crispy tasty exterior.  The sides are home made and delicious and the biscuits are fluffy like pillows.  Stop in, order it to go and eat outside or in the car or take it home. You will be glad you did.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Biscuits, biscuits, biscuits! This was my first stop during a trip to Nashville due to many recommendations and we were not disappointed. I ordered the country ham with fried eggs and grits, which was great, but let's be honest, it's all about the biscuits here. I could eat 6 of those puppies with every meal. 

The only thing we didn't like was the location. It's far from the city center and took a long time to get an uber but we passed the time in the restaurant gift shop.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The best breakfast ever!!! We had the country fried steak and eggs with the hash brown casserole.  The steak was so amazing and fried perfectly and the hash brown casserole was Amazing.   The biscuits were the best biscuits ever served with their homemade preserves that were so good you had to use all three flavors. It was worth the drive while we were visiting in Nashville !

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place was great!!!! Friendly staff and if there is a wait, and I'm sure there will be, you can walk over to their market and gift shop to look around. 

Biscuits are served with every meal and they are yummy! I ate so many I barely had room for my meal. 

I had 3 sides as a meal and they were all very good. My husband had the smoked boneless pork chop and it was delicious. 

If you are in the Nashville area- you should stop here for sure!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Prepare to wait, then prepare for cholesterol city! 
If I were to return to loveless, which I hope to one day, I will prepare by starving myself for a day or two before hand just so I can enjoy all the delicious delicacies without the insane guilt. 
Yes there will be a wait but there are retail opportunities to bide the time and if the weather is tolerable, there is outdoor seating to enjoy while you wait. 
I had the catfish with creamed corn and Mac and cheese. There are so many sides, I would recommend your party orders a variety along you in order to sample all. Everything was delicious, no exceptions. Even the Bloody Mary! 
This is a must-try when visiting Nashville.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
The best thing that we ate was the Ruben roll and that was even over fried!  My husband's beer he describes as creamy, but I don't like beer so I can't comment.  The bad of the meal:  everything else ... which includes the over cooked and under-salted smaller pretzel which the Manager wouldn't take off the bill after a few bites!  My Pork (as they don't offer veal) schnitzel was OK but was tough, dry but don't ask for extra gravy cause that's additional!!  The crispy-fried pork shank was just OK too, but barely ANY gravy with that either!  I tasted the pork shank and thought it was tastier than my schnitzel!  It is enough to feed 2 people I would say.

Other reviews of this place say negative things about the sides -- we agree!  The spaetzel, sour kraut and potato dumpling were not worth the time nor calories ... and of course, no gravy!  So I'll go there and say that the German place could be considered the gravy Nazis!  Sorry guys...

If we came back, and that's a BIG if, we'd just have the big pretzel, beer, and Ruben roll (requesting that it not be over cooked).

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
We decided to try Bavarian Bierhaus because of beer, brats, and beer cheese soup. We first saw this place in September while randomly going to Opry Mills but decided to go at a later time. That time was two weekends ago on a Sunday afternoon. 

We didn't wait long to be seated but for some reason, waited a really long time for service. Like, really long time. 15-20 minutes for someone to come by. We could only see one server and she wasn't coming anywhere near us. I finally flagged down the hostess and asked about our server. A couple of minutes later, she came by.

We decided to get a beer sampler and she explained to us what beers it came with and answered any questions we had about beers we were thinking of adding. I got the Bier Cheese soup and a plate with two different sausages and Chris got the schnitzel. 

While we waited for our food, there was a polka band that we enjoyed. I genuinely like polka music, so I was really digging them. They did some rock covers as well as played actual polka songs. I enjoyed them already but as I drank the beer (really good beer, by the way), I enjoyed them even more.

I haven't had Bier Cheese soup in years, and theirs was amazing. Of course the sausages were good. I was really digging everything: the polka, the beer, the food, the boyfriend. Speaking of Chris, he rather liked his schnitzel. 

As we were leaving, the hostess apologized to us for having to wait for our server. Honestly it only felt like a hiccup in an otherwise pleasant experience. I told her everything was amazing other than that.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Going the extra mile is what sets you apart. Thanks for letting us in and grabbing a drink half an hour before opening!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
When a hostess tells you it's going to be a 1 hour 45 minute wait for breakfast on a Thursday morning the normal reply is "no thank you" except for when your looking to sit and eat at a historical landmark like the Loveless Cafe. Well 90 minutes later we had our table and we hit the ground running with hot biscuits right out of the oven. Along with that came a potpourri of delicious jambs and sweet butter. We all had something different and each raved more than the other of how good the food was. 
Don't leave Nashville without putting this off the beat and path on your list.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Yup. Down-home cooking. We had a huge party and they accommodated us easily. Jason our server was friendly and professional. And my chicken was delicious! Cucumber salad was the absolute best - I recommend that to go w/the chicken. It is as good as others say!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The lunch started with biscuits and homemade jam. Great stuff. They told us the wait would be 1 hour and 15 minutes, it actually only took 45 minutes. While waiting we got a chance to explore the shops on the property. I had the smoked turkey breast with cranberry bbq sauce. Large portions low price. The wait staff was friendly and kept my ice tea filled. 

We had a good time..

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Skip this is place!! The food was BLAND and the wait staff was less than friendly. There are so many other places to eat in the area - choose one of those!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The 3 stars is more so for the amazing show we enjoyed last week. The winery is beautiful but sadly I wasn't impressed with much else. I've heard so many great things about the food/chef and having eaten before the show, we decided to grab an appetizer, The Salt n Vinegar Frites. Upon placing the order, they came out faster than our drink orders. To some, this would be great. To foodies/food bloggers, this only can mean one thing. This was not made to order. The fries were seasoned to perfection with a less than accommodating side of another perfect garlic aioli. But they were cold. This baffled us. There could not have been more than 150 people at the show and upon glancing around to see if others had ordered food, I did not see a food order within the surrounding tables. There's actually preparation that goes into complete dishes with components. We only ordered the fries.... and they could not be made to order? In efforts to not disrupt the show, for our sake and others, we ate our fries that probably would have been the best fries we ever had, had they been prepared properly. Upon entering the restroom at a later time, I noticed a white table napkin on the floor of an occupied stall. That white table napkin was then picked up by a server from the floor, placed on the sink while she washed her hands and then taken with her when she exited the bathroom. I didn't want to even imagine....I think between the two, this was enough for me not to return. Sadly.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We visited 6/29 around 11 am, we thought we were hitting it early and during the week but when we checked in it was an hour wait, we had come specifically to have lunch so we waited. There are some small gift shops, a postal shop to ship goodies home and a local artist shop with something for everyone. They also had some corn hole games set up around the area as well as picnic benches so that did kill some time but not a full hour. When we were being seated the wait was up to 1 1/2 hour wait!!! So be prepared for the wait! Once seated we were approached immediately and given a plate of fresh homemade biscuits and preserves, quite genius way to stave of the hangry's! My husband ordered the biscuit sampler, they had many choices, he went with bacon, sausage, pulled pork and fried chicken, he thought they were all great but the pork and chicken were his favorite! He also wasn't able to finish as the portion was large. I ordered the catfish dinner with okra and hash browns and can't brag enough, the catfish was probably the best I have ever had and I am a southern girl who has had some catfish! I ate every bit and it was a large portion, it was so light and crispy, not greasy at all. The sides were delicious. We would definitely go back, I would order the same thing too! The food was definitely a 5 but the wait really is a consideration. Definitely a tourist favorite but you will see the locals for sure!!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is a really fun restaurant! My Fiancée and I stopped here a few weeks ago while at the mall and we were very pleasantly surprised with our meal overall. The staff was attentive and our food and drinks were brought out promptly. The drink selection is good and they have a variety of German brews and wines. The menu is what you'd expect from a German restaurant and the pretzels, sausages, and schnitzel were very, very good and quite filling. It was a great meal overall and it will be our go-to if we ever want German food!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I went to Loveless Cafe around lunch time for breakfast. The wait was initially forty-five minutes, however, since we were coming from Chicago that was no big deal. We decided to wait and peruse the gift shops that were filled with delicacies and kind of  pricey apparel. We were buzzed back into the restaurant before the estimated time. It is very chilly inside so make sure you bring a sweater! The menu was simple and easy to navigate; I ordered the biscuit sampler since they are known for those.
