The platter came with biscuits that were shared with the rest of my table as an appetizer. A sweet and decadent plate of blackberry, peach, and strawberry preserves... as well as honey (which you can ask for). The biscuits were scrumptious to say the least and my favorite was the strawberry preserve, but all of them were tasty! The coffee accompanying my meal of my choice of the 4 biscuits (fried chicken, green tomato and cheese, and steak) and grits. The grits were the best I have ever had. I added honey and butter even though it came perfectly flavored already. Out of all of biscuits, chicken was my  favorite because of the moist and crispy texture that complimented the warm soft biscuit. All together five stars for the great service even though it was a long wait, the enviroment is very southern inspired and the story sheet they give you provides a great back story. Very great experience, do not forget to take a picture with the sign!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Great atmosphere and vibe.  Plentiful wine list (among the deepest in Nashville) with many reasonable choices.  Have been a couple times now and while the menu is limited, there are some stellar items on there including the Napa cabbage salad and burger.  Staff has been friendly and knowledgeable thus far.  Have been to one concert and looking forward to going back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Went to Franklin and Nashville to visit family.  The first morning, they took us to the Loveless Cafe.  The food was great and the portions were HUGE.  They are famous for their biscuits and, of course, the gravy.  I had pork chops and eggs.  It came with biscuits and gravy, and it also came with their hash brown casserole.  Everything was delicious.  I would say you must go here if you are in the area.  You won't be disappointed.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
For once DD&D had it right on!  The chicken is awesome, the biscuits like none I have ever had before, and the fried green tomatoes divine.  

The only caution I would have is to get the EARLY.  We got there around 1pm and had to wait an hour for a table but it was well worth the wait.  Wouldn't mind going back to try the bbq some time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I love this place. I've been here a few times and it's really quite delicious.  It's tasty comfort food with the best biscuits ever.  Typically, there is always a wait so be prepared.  The vibe is country comfort and the food represents that.  Today, I had the fried
Chicken and some pork chops with peach jam-mashed potatoes and Mac and cheese.  The crispy skin on the chicken and the moist tender inside was simply delicious. I forgot to take pictures because we were so hungry and the food smelled so great.  If you find yourself in Nashville and looking for good comfort food, come to the Loveless.......the biscuits, try and eat just one!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Overrated. Great biscuits and ambiance but slow service and waaayyyy too noisy and a long wait always. Prices higher than expected. Not too impressed.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This would have to be one of my favorite restaurants. The food is fresh and good. The atmosphere is great. I would definitely recommend this place.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Good: 
A beautiful space, located in an up-and-coming area you wouldn't have wanted to visit 3 years ago. You walk in and immediately feel at home. The whole club, from bar area to bathrooms to the showroom, is intimate without being cloying. 
It fills a huge gap in this city, which has needed an upscale club inbetween tiny 75-100 seaters (eg Bluebird Café) and larger halls (Ryman). 
Very clean, great bathrooms, nice bar area. Lots and lots of wood.
They're making their own wine next year, and the gigantic barrels are eye candy if you like good vino. The wine lists (there are 2) are comprehensive. Some very reasonably priced , but that's because they charge YOU the liquor tax. Be forewarned.
Food is better than expected. Risotto balls, recommended by our waitress, were excellent (though I'd go for spicier mustard). Pork tacos ditto. The steak was two lovely pieces of meat - though the chef has a heavy salt hand. (Maybe they're salting and letting it sit to tenderize? Still, it shouldn't be that salty.) I don't recommend the mussels, and the cheese tray is absurdly small for what you pay, but the ravioli was gorgeous. The burgers are very good, and there's a vegetarian option too.
I'd recommend the meze platter, except that we had it our first visit (opening night) and it was large enough for four. Last visit it had shrunk considerably. 

The bad: 
Five dollar parking charge? Really? The attendants make it clear that your $5 goes to the venue, so you're expected to tip on top of it. But there's NO street parking!!
Getting seated is a work in progress. I've been here 5 times so far, alone, with family, with business associates. Each time, we arrived at 6 pm, when they opened. Each time, wait staff weren't ready. Each time, there's a meaningless cluster of hosts and hostesses? standing by the entry doors, doing anything but paying attention to the customers. Each time we were sent to the "concierge" for tickets and information. Forgive my being snotty about it, but how many City Winery employees does it take to seat someone? If it happened once, all right. But every time? 
Food service is slooooow. Don't come hungry. I don't know if the wait staff are over-loaded or what, but when you go out for an expensive evening like this, you expect better service. My waitrons have all been nice, but far from the kind of competency I experienced at the NY or Chicago clubs.
Food is expensive for what you get. (Online menu prices changed?) Our party of four had a bottle of inexpensive wine, 3 Tito's vodkas, and two beers, plus mains and 2 appetizers) was $310 before tip. I think that's expensive. Portions aren't big enough for leftovers. If this were The Palm, I'd expect it, and I'd be satisfied knowing the quality would be wonderful AND I'd have enough for another meal next day. 
The wait staff are friendly, but scattered. Ask for salt and pepper. Ask again. And again. Finally ask a bus boy, who brings it eventually. My wife's burger arrived with fries, everything looked great, but by the time salt and ketchup arrived everything was cold. This is not unusual here, but I can no longer excuse it as growing pains.
And they don't pay the liquor tax?!?! This is the only restaurant in Nashville charging the customers for it - even Kayne Prime, home of 50 cent charge per blue cheese olive in your drink, doesn't charge liquor tax. Really, between food prices and liquor tax, I would not suggest eating here.

The ugly:
Sound problems. It carooms off the back wall so you can't hear vocals at all if there's a band - of the 3 we've seen, this was a problem with all of them. It's all right for an acoustic act like Taj Mahal, but something needs to be done. Who opens a club in Nashville without consulting a sound engineer? Everyone in my party, each time, was disappointed in the sound quality.
Seating is, to put it bluntly, horrendous. At first glance, it's very pretty - until you realize that a) no matter where you sit, you're not facing the stage, and b) chairs are tiny, and tables are about a foot shy of the standard 2 or 4 seat table length. What this means is that no matter how much you pay, or what you reserve, you're going to be miserably uncomfortable. My wife is petite, our daughter is likewise, but even they complained that they couldn't eat without elbowing one another. 
The sideways-only seating means you don't get to enjoy the show the way you would with concert-style. I understand you can't do the concert-style and serve dinners, but I'd love to see this place change up so half the table is facing the stage. The other half could just turn their chairs around for the show. As it is, no one was happy with the seats.

All in all, I will continue to attend when I'm in town, because they're bringing in a lot of acts you wouldn't normally see in Nashville. But I'll dine elsewhere. And I'll try to get validated, even if I'm not a "vinofile" (because I resent paying $75 a year for what I would get), and I'll avoid ordering liquor.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
So there are those "spots" in Nashville. You know, the ones that ALL the tourists know about before they get here? And HAVE to go to in order to get an "authentic" Nashville experience. This is most certainly one of those spots. I can't tell you how many times I've been out and heard tourists talk about how they have brunch plans at Loveless the next day. 

Most of those "tourist" spots don't get high star ratings from me. They usually evolve with the rise in tourism and then loose their special local flair. This is not one of those places. I grew up about three minutes down the road from Loveless. I can't remember the first time I came here, because I was so young. But I do remember the motions. The delicious biscuits and crunchy fried chicken, the walk to the back of the property to look at the bicycle shop, and then over to the country cafe to buy some rock candy and a biscuit mix.

This place is Nashville. Its out in the middle of no where (Transplants and tourists.....you'll have to drive away from downtown). It's authentic, unique and special. The menu is simple for GOOD. The drinks are simple but GOOD. And the experience is actually and experience. 

Go there early. Play some yard games. Look at all the LEGENDS pictures that have dined there. Buy some freaking rock candy at the store. And do yourself a favor and get the biscuit mix. It might not be as good as they are at Loveless. But when your back at your non Nashville home....you'll crave a Loveless biscuit.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Southern cooking at its best!!!  Not sure how anyone would rate this place less than a 5-Star visit.  Food is great, atmosphere is great, and service was great.  Biscuits Biscuits Biscuits!!!  That is all I need to say, and don't forget the jelly.  I think I ordered almost everything on the menu because I couldn't decide what I wanted and everything looked good.  Great place for a tourist to stop by.

name: The Basement
text: Very, very small... dark... FANTASTIC venue for live music... after you've browsed the used records upstairs at Grimey's. I paid just a few bucks to get in The Basement, bought a beer from a cooler tap, sat down 3 ft from where three outstanding, never-heard-before, blues bands played back to back. One was from Australia, the other two... were not. All three were remarkable. Don't miss a chance to check out this venue when you're in Nashville.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: Wow, what an experience! The hostess, Rebeccah made me feel at home from the moment I arrived. The beer selection was amazing, almost overwhelming. Thankfully the bartender was very knowledgeable in helping satiate my thirsty palate. After a handful of beers, it came time to choose food from the expansive menu. I settled on the patty melt, and was blown away! The meat was expertly seasoned and grilled to a perfect mid-rare. All in all, Fat Kat's was a great experience, and I will be returning for sure.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: Stopped in to see what the talk was all about. I used to come in here when it was the pour house. I will tell you, the remodel, upgrade, stage and whole new vibe and atmosphere is fantastic! I can't wait to come back and hear some music and hang out.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My husband and I were in Nashville and this was about 30 minutes from our hotel. We had to check it out after all the great reviews and it didn't disappoint. The food, coffee, and the service was excellent! The biscuits were the best we've ever had. You get a plate of them for the table while you're looking over the menu and they are served with 3 different preserves. The blackberry was our favorite. My husband ordered the Pit-Cooked Pork bbq and two eggs. It's served over two pancakes and comes with a side, he chose grits, which he said were amazing and also more biscuits. It was $13.99 which is more then we typically spend for a breakfast entree but he said it was absolutely delicious. It was so much food he got a to go box and ate the rest later! I got an omelet which also is served with biscuits. It was $7.49. Needless to say we left with a to go box of biscuits! Right next door they have a little market called Hams & Jams and they also have a gift shop. That was fun to walk through when we were finished eating. Next time we are in town we will definitely go back!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Decent. Beer is solid, got some big ones too. It's a bit hokey pokey, its German themed if you like that. met a guy from Germany and brought us our beers and food. He explained everything and was pleasant. We live about 25 minutes north, so we come down to the area to try things out. I'd be back again. We had snitzel chicken with gravy. Good stuff.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We've been going to Loveless Cafe for about five years and have always ordered the breakfast. On our last trip We decided to try the other fare. I had the breaded pork chops, one of my favorite dishes, with Mac and cheese and mashed potatoes. My wife ordered the BLT sandwich with American cheese. We also ordered the fried green tomatoes as an appetizer. 

The green tomatoes were excellent. The rest of the dinner was so bad we couldn't eat it. The pork chops were so over cooked they were like shoe leather. The mash potatoes had so much white pepper they were hit. The Mac and cheese was tasteless. 

My wife's BLT was cold and the cheese was hard and dry, not even melted.  Oh well nothing ever stays the same. I could see if one item was off or bad , but two entire meals were not eatable. No need to return to this place. They do just fine without our business.

name: Dirty Little Secret
text: It's all fun and games till they want you out.  A group of friends and I (10 women) had table service on a busy saturday night...we were having a great time till the manager decided we were done with our table and they abruptly removed ALL of our drinks - because they had another group coming in (this was midnight) telling us our TIME WAS UP.  I'm sorry, but when you just dropped $1200 on two bottles of vodka in 2 hours - no one said that came with a time limit.  To make matters worse it turned into a scene out of COPS - the bouncers, yes more than one,  started man handling us,  physically accosting a few of my friends and rushed us out the back of the building.  No women in their right mind should EVER ENTER THIS PLACE unless they have their own private security team.  Shame on you Dirty Little Secret - I wouldn't have expected this kind of service from a Nashville establishment - maybe you're practicing for the Vegas Night Club Scene.  Ladies - BEWARE

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Pretty cozy place to eat. The staff is great and inviting. They give each table biscuits and some homemade jam to try out. I had the country fried steak with hash brown casserole and fresh fruit. The steak was made well because the meat as well as the batter were seasoned well. Didn't really like the hash brown casserole because it was too cheesy. Kenny, our server, kept checking back with us, which I appreciate. All in all, a quaint place to have a meal at.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Was told this is the place for fried chicken and biscuits while in Nashville. Biscuits are heaven!!!! So good. Mac and cheese was lacking. Fried chicken was good but mine was a little too crispy around the edges and did have a touch of the burnt oil taste to it. But ........ we did eat at about 7pm or so as well.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Very nice restaurant with friendly staff. Food was very appetizing. Live music was entertaining. Oh, beer if you want some. They tapped a keg while we were there and everyone that wanted a free beer got in line and you also got to keep the glass mug, offer good until the keg went dry. 

Located in very nice mall (Opry Mill).

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Awesome place with fantastic food, servers and music. Going again tonight.  The sausage triple platter is especially good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The first time I've felt that anyplace was worth the hour and half wait to get in. There wasn't a single thing on our plates that wasn't delicious. Service is top notch, and even management chips in to make sure everything is running smoothly.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Excellent! Most friendly service, authentic German traditions, delicious food and beer straight from Germany! Love it!

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: Fat Kat Slims is pretty average, kinda pricey for the quality of food the serve. I don't live in the area and I won't be back if I am. Nothing to write home about, service was awkward and kinda slow. Had a cool aesthetic but other than that not remarkable at all.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Better than the reviews say, if that's possible.  World class Southern fare.  Make this a stop when in Nashville

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I don't get it.
I don't get it all.
The biscuits are BLAH boys.
The cheesy hashbrowns were epic.
Its a cool looking roadside place , but otherwise its average to poor for breakfast.
No love lost the Loveless.

name: Rocketown
text: Overall it's good that they're here for teens and young people.  Decent facilities and plenty of parking.  I don't like however that if you drive there to purchase advance tickets they still charge you the convenience fee you pay if you order online.  That's ridiculous!  I also don't like that they've compromised and book bands that are clearly in opposition to Christ.  Like I said, overall it's good they are in Nashville.  They bring in a lot of bands faithful to the Kingdom, and provide a good hangout for teens.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This place should be avoided at all costs for Mothers Day Brunch in the future.  1pm reservation we arrived for at 12:45pm. After 47 minutes of being shifted from line to line we were finally seated.  The selection of food rivaled a Shoneys buffet and the waitstaff were inattentive at best. Family of 4 paid $240 for what would have been better served for $50'at Cracker Barrel.   Manager said "yes, we need a new system because this happens every year and at Easter!"  Trust me when I say, there are better places for special occasion brunches like Mothers Day and Easter.  On a scale of 1-10 it registers a form 1 and that's only because the location at least was accurate.  Just a horrible Mothers Day brunch.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Unfortunately, the valet most likely ruined my experience here.  For starters, there is NO parking available except for some abandoned buildings across the street from the rear of the winery. However, the valet claims to own ALL of these spots and was EXTREMELY rude and even aggressive towards our party for attempting to park.  The valet loudly threatened me that if I didn't try to park on the street he would call a tow truck while I was inside their restaurant. 
Seeing as how others in our party were waiting inside, (and at this point there was no way I would let the valet near my car) we had to park around the corner and leave the car in front of the Rescue Mission.  
When we got in, the bar staff was friendly and we ordered some drinks and appetizers.  We had the fries, the duck tacos, and something else I don't remember. The fries were not memorable, and the duck tacos might as well have been dry pulled pork because that was what it tasted like. 
We did not see a show there so I admit I cannot rate the music venue space.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great atmosphere, service, and food. Visiting from NM and decided to stop in. Worth the stop!! Be prepared to eat when you go in!  Biscuits prior to your meal will keep you going back for more!!!

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: Went to fat Kat Slim's tonight. Had a great time. Great food. Great service!  Huge chicken fingers!!!! Definitely check out the specialty cocktail list they know what they're doing!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
They have lost their edge...no longer special, alright but nothing to write home about.

They have a system to maximize profit and that rather than charm and service trump customer happiness.

The regular employees try to tone down the eagerness of the summer student workers and seem to enjoy watching people wait...

Chicken fried steak was more grease and batter than steak...heating pie was done in a micro wave, nothing country about a micro wave.

Their beer selection is pretty weak...not having micro brews is a micro aggression.

name: Big Shotz
text: Poor service here. Make sure you check your bill as the bartenders add drinks you didn't have. The bartender was confrontational and cussed at us when we asked about charges . Music sucks there as well. VERY Loud to cover poor voice. Wil NEVER go here on next trip to Nashville

name: Analog at Hutton Hotel
text: Their New Year's eve DJs were soooo good. And the vibe in the venue was so welcoming and fun. It was the perfect way to ring in the new year and I admit that I am a professed hater of that holiday but the staff made me feel safe and appreciated. I never had to wait for a drink, even the line to get in moved super quick. The bar was so packed but this girl with black hair and accent was buzzing around making drinks at the speed you only see on reality TV show. Smiling the whole time I just subbed to insta page to follow the shows they have and can't wait to go back again. Thank you, Analog for having such a beautiful well orchestrated music venue. Rare in Nashville ....

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Classic southern comfort food. I had their fried chicken with mashed potatoes and gravy as well as macaroni and cheese. The country ham is excellent too. Almost all of their menu items are homemade and you can tell. They're famous for their biscuits and preserves! They are usually very, very busy, so definitely be sure to plan your visit. I don't recommend coming on a Sunday unless you're prepared for a long wait. The best time is around 5 PM on a weeknight right before the afternoon rush! Great service as well.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I visited City Winery while visiting Nashville.  I looked up the winery and was hoping to see a show as well, but they were sold out!  Upon arrival, we were greeted by the hostess and seated at a great table in the middle of the winery.  I loved the industrial space and the decor was made you feel comfortable.  

Our waitstaff-Peter was so knowledgeable and friendly.  I decided to start off with a flight of wines - that cost $20 - this was a good choice.  I had two whites and two reds.  My favorite was the Pinot Noir. 

Food - We decided to try the: Margeherita Flatbread; Calamari; Pulled Lamb Sandwich; Potato salad and seasoned fries.  Everything was good except the Calamari.  I explained my thoughts about the dish and the item was removed from the bill.  

City Winery is a great place for a group; date night or a special occasion.  If I lived in the area-this would be my go-to-spot for sure!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: First off we were seated with another nice couple whom we never met before at the same table.  Wasn't what we expected but ok it Christmas no need to be that way.  Then first course arrived.  There was 6 small pieces of pickled red and orange colored beets.  All less than 1/2" in general size strong vinegar on them. Like not diluted at all. Then a chunk of cheese in the middle on top of about 10 small blades of fancy lettuce. Also the lettuce was a bit soggy. There was on chunk of cheese in the middle on top of the lettuce.  Tasty little piece of cheese. It was less than 2" in diameter.  We were supposed to divide this into 4 portions between me and 3 other persons.  First off it was extremely awkward to take and try to divide such a small portion for a Christmas meal that cost $35 each person.  Food wasn't cooked properly, potatoes raw in middle and waitress was so rude when I asked for more salad.  She said "That wasn't enough for you?"   Anyway we tried to eat the food and not be completely angry for her treatment, dry turkey, cold food and pushy rude behavior.  Food was slop not fit to eat and I showed the manager the potatoes in a napkin infront of several people going directly to her. I wasn't going to pay for that crap.  They were busy and several seen how I was disappointed.  Never again going there. Save your money.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Worth the wait time! Biscuits yummy!! Homemade preserves delicious. Watermelon ribs excellent!!! Best ribs ever!!!! Must go asap.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits galore! What a cool little compound. Had a bit of a wait for breakfast, so we meandered around from shop to shop for about 45 minutes. We were seated, served and had paid the check in probably less time than we waited, but when we rated our favorite meals from our time in Nashville, Loveless and Farm House were definitely the top two (though we couldn't decide which was our fave).

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
For the ultimate southern food experience, this is the place! We had a 30-minute wait, but it went by quick as we walked around the grounds and peaked in to the simple shops there. And the wait was totally well worth it.

Everything we had was awesome! At our table, we got the cat fish (essentially, fish and chips), the chicken tenders (which were more like chicken filets) and the pork chops (while two pork chops would have suffice, there were three). The servings were gigantic, not to mention 2 sides each, and we definitely SHOULD HAVE split just a couple of dishes, but we wanted to try so many things that getting several items was essential! We all loved it all. No complaints. Everything tasted so good! I was completely satisfied and I feel like I got some true southern food exposure.

This place lives up to the hype. Definitely worth the effort and whatever wait is required!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Dear Loveless Cafe,

My new husband and I ventured into your establishment late Wednesday afternoon to have some lunch after horseback riding.  We are visiting Nashville on our honeymoon and were told that Loveless was a place that we must stop.  While we enjoyed the nostalgia and the staff, we were disappointed.  The food was not that great.  Matt ordered the blt with fried green tomatoes and I got the chicken hands as our waiter called them.  The best thing about our whole meal was the squash casserole.  My chicken was bland and dry and matts blt was nothing better than what I could have made for him at home. What was most disappointing was going to both gift shops and seeing every little trinket from coffee mugs to quirky ornaments was made in China. When your company is representing Americana....it is a shame and a poor trust in your country to not produce in America.  So sad that this piece of American history chose to commercialize in this way.  Then hidden back in a corner and under advertised was the shop that held the true treasures, Tennessee local artists!  You company should highlight these people...they are what make your establishment what it is.  Being that you are locally owned, you should completely understand this market.  Overall, when we come back to Tennessee, I doubt we will come back to Loveless or recommend it to our friends and family.  Once was enough for us.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I stopped in this location for a quick late night wine flight. The bartender was very friendly and the wine was good. The venue is beautiful like the others. They allowed us to check out the event space even though they had a concert going. It looked amazing. The upper balcony was a great viewing area. This visit, along with the other City Winery locations I have visited, was outstanding. You can tell there is a quality standard within the brand and it is maintained very well throughout.

name: Drifters
text: Took over 50 minutes to get our food, DONT COME HUNGRY! you'll never get your food! Totally disappointed!

name: The Country
text: Unfriendly staff and cannot make a drink. Might be ok for a beer. Was not there to see the live music. In from out of town- did not display the Nashville hospitality expected. Pass on this one.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: House drink Mr Frisky was horrible. The gumbo was nothing more than gravy over rice with some shrimp pieces tossed in. I gave it two stars because the fried shrimp and alligator was good. The Cesar salad was boring. We went here on a recommendation of a couple we met on one of our outings well they don't know good gumbo at all. Service was slow definitely won't recommend this place

name: Drifters
text: HIGHLY recommended. Small place and a small menu but they do what they do well. Appreciated the many vegetarian options too. Plus, service was top notch, super-friendly.

name: The Bowery Vault
text: As a performer I highly recommend the Bowery Vault. The Owners Vero and Emily are extremely accommodating in terms of setting up and take down as well as giving performers the best sounding performance. Now if they just serve some JD.......

name: Drifters
text: Outstanding BBQ!  The pulled chicken, brats, brisket, and pulled pork were great.  The sides were great.  The fries, coleslaw, and beans were delicious.  Great variety of BBQ sauces.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
2013/014

We came in to see "Chasing Ice" a few weeks back, and enjoyed the movie as well as the comfy seating. 

I like small theaters, as I'm not into going to see a movie for the ambience of hundreds of people around me for a first run movie. I honestly didn't notice any of the architectural details of an historic place; you see one indie theater that used to be historically- and cutlurally-significant, you've seen them all. 

They do offer the kind of foreign and independent films that generally attract a more subdued crowd. However, at the time I saw the movie, the women behind us kept slurping/whispering throughout the entire movie. I kept glaring at them, only to find out that my husband knew one of them. Oops.

Given the blue laws of this state, I was surprised to see them offering alcohol.

name: Commodore Grille
text:
Great place for food and music. My husband is a musician so we went to play at the open mic. The songwriters featured are always great. We will be back for him to be featured in Dec! The drinks are great and the spinach and artichoke dip is amazing. 
Debbie, the MC, is fantastic!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: One of the friendliest staff I've ever encountered.  Special shoutout to the head of security Eron, who is a pro and is extremely cool.

name: The Country
text: Friendly atmosphere the Friday night song writers night was great, (i think it is held the third friday) they hosted a variety of local talent. For more info on the talent night  check out Hippie Chick Twang on Facebook her and her son were the hosts and she was a very talented songwriter and guitarist.

name: EXIT/IN
text:
Ticketfly's online ticketing was completely down for an extended period, and whoever manages this venue seems to very rarely answer the phone, so I went to Exit-In when another show was going on in hopes that the venue would be able to sell a ticket to a show held the next day (thus also avoiding the huge percentage-wise fee for purchasing online, so I was ok with the inconvenience of making a trip over there). But the box office couldn't even sell a ticket to their own venue for a show held the next night. I was referred to two other locations which apparently can't even sell tickets while the Ticketfly website remains down.

Have been to one of more concerts at this venue previously and found it sort of so-so in terms of layout and sound quality, but had never heard of a concert venue unable to sell tickets to its own shows held the next evening, was kind of annoying as a customer as this information is not made clear from the website and this is a very unusual policy for a music venue - if someone from Exit-In reads this, please note in your FAQ or elsewhere on your website that tickets for future shows are not sold at the ticket window, as I think the common understanding is that the selling of tickets to current and future events is a core feature of most venues' ticket window or box office if they have one.

***
Update: Thank you to Jeremy for the fast response to this (below). I still think it's sort of lame that there isn't a way to buy tickets in advance of showdate at venue without relying on a web interface which as I recall regularly charges over 20% in fees not even displayed to customer until checkout, and that same interface now appears to have suffered a pretty massive hack and presumably/possibly may have exposed customer payment data in the process (not sure of this but it seems to very often end up being the case in these situations). But you and other staff I have interacted with there have always been professional and courteous on the venue's behalf. Thanks for taking the time to respond and for doing it in a professional manner.
 
****
Annnnnd update yet again. Can we talk about how stupid I was with this previous review? Venue I had gone to to try to buy tickets was Mercy Lounge/The Cannery, not Exit-In; related venues, I think, but not the same. Sounds like I might have run into the same problem regardless, but Exit In is a way better venue than this previous review allowed for. I think 5 stars in terms of actual venue quality is fair, and again I appreciate that someone from the venue replied with such class. Still  of a fan of the online ticketing interface used, but 5 stars for the venue itself (and for its staff!).

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Best venue for weird chicks pushing their way to the front and saying "excuse me" followed by 7 d-bags with sunglasses at 10pm in a dark room. Also, the sound is average if average is the sound of your record player playing on the first floor when you're on the second. Bartenders are good...not counting the bad one. Want to go to a concert at the ass end of a horse stable? Come here.

name: The Family Wash
text: Pint & Pie night was well worth the extra day in Nashville.  Great atmosphere!

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
Somehow I've never reviewed Mercy Lounge. I notice I've covered most of the other music venues in Nashville but slipped up with this one--and some of my earliest Nashville shows took place here. Before I even lived in the area I took a few roadtrips to Nashville to see shows here when bands I really liked were playing. It's mostly a solid place to see a band with a few notable issues.
First---it's a great size and decent layout for a mid-sized (popularity wise) band. It's an intimate, up close kind of place. Bigger than the End, smaller than Marathon. They have on-site parking (huge plus) for only $5 (not bad at all). Drinks are cheap. Easy in and out and I've seen some pretty great shows here.
So what's not to love? Well...even if you're not an ear-plug fan (and I've made myself become one anyway over the past few years to save my hearing and still keep going to shows) you better become one at least for the night if you're headed to Mercy. That's because the acoustics in this place are outright deafening. One of my favorite bands played here a few years ago and though they are a fairly loud band this was the loudest I've ever heard them and I've seen them 10 times in 10 different venues over the years. Here I could barely make out a word of the vocals (and they have clear vocals typically, a very narrative song-writing is important kind of band). I left with the worst headache of my life. Plus there are some posts and polls in odd places so if it's an active show watch out. And getting to and from the bar with a drink at any point can be cumbersome.
That all said, I saw one of the most active shows by one of the loudest bands around here not that long ago and it worked really well with little to no issues for me. Sound was clearer than in previous visits. I've noticed some great shows coming to Mercy in the next few months so I may have to revisit, particularly for the more singer-songwriter style events.

name: The Bowery Vault
text: Today, I had the good fortune of discovering The Bowery Vault. To say this artfully curated vintage clothing shop has charm is an understatement. It's a time portal. Hang out, have a beer, try on some (affordable!) clothes, hope you catch a talented band while they're on residency. Either way, GO THERE.

name: The Country
text: Awesome music venue. Great food and music. Great drinks as well. Always good fun here and you never know who you'll meet!

name: Drifters
text: Marie is the best. Truly the best. Worth the 30 hour drive to hangout with her and have a drink at drifters! Make sure to get a cold yuengling and a good order of hush puppies. No better a place to escape from the Tennessee sun! This is the spot.

name: Drifters
text: What a fun place... great vibe... friendly staff... tender ribs and brisket... no sauce needed! sides were outstanding, especially the hush puppies, slaw and beans... good drink specials. Leinenkugel Summer Shandy on tap was a bonus! definitely recommend!

name: Drifters
text: Traveling through Nashville with only 2 days to visit, we wanted to go to the best BBQ joint in town. Drifters had 4.4 star average, with a few other places being 4.5-4.7 stars but it was on our way back to the campground after a late trip to Jack Daniels Distillery and was open till 1am so we decided to try it. I am very glad we did! The atmosphere was as laid back as you'd want to see, we ate outside, where there was a band playing at a decent level so we could still have a conversation. It truly felt like we were at a neighbors back yard bbq. We ordered a couple of beers, bbq nachos and a sampler plate. I am not a big fan of sausage but the smoked sausage on this plate was amazing! The bbq nachos with the brisket were by far the show stopper though! Please do not waste tummy space on the fries and sides! We did end up trying a few of those other higher star places but was disappointed by them after eating at Drifters. If you're passing through or in the vicinity and have not been there, go and order the nachos with the brisket, I promise you will not be disappointed!

name: Drifters
text: This is one of my favorite restaurants to go to in Nashville. Especially if you like a nice day out with some BBQ, this is the place to go!

name: Drifters
text: Great food. Good deals, two for ones most days. Also have a great outdoor space with ping pong and corn hole. A lot of fun!

name: Drifters
text: This place took so long to deliver any service what so ever AND when we finally did get our food it was cold. Never again.

name: Springwater
text: Bartender was too busy to be bothered on his computer. Seemed super annoyed. I get it -- we aren't locals at the dive bar, but it's your job. Gave him $20 for $13 tab and never brought us change. Super rude and acted like he had better things to do. Place is a dive bar, which I love, but the smell of natural gas is overwhelming. Save your time and your money and go to Villager Tavern or Santa's.

name: Drifters
text: This is a dive bar, first and foremost. Having said that, the barbecue is great!  Tried the BBQ sampler, but switched out the fries for the hush puppies and the black beans for the standard baked beans. The ribs are dry-rubbed and were very good. The service was fast and friendly. Highly recommended!

name: The Local
text: The music and beer selection here are good. We went in on a Friday night. It was pretty quiet, not a huge crowd. The reason for our low review is upon checking our credit card statement we found the bartender gave himself a higher tip than the one we gave him for two beers. It's pretty shady to change the tip amount on the receipt. I don't know that we will be back. But if you go, pay in cash!

name: Springwater
text: What a treat.   Gritty, pool, darts, loud music, $2 PBR.   Stop in, mingle, have a cold one.

name: The Local
text:
1. Best French fries in not only
Nashville, but the world. 2. Gina is the best bartender I've ever had. She gave us some secret ingredients we asked for and even squirted my mustard for me. 5 star service for sure. Come see Gina on Monday's and Tuesday's!

name: The Bowery Vault
text:
Ellie and Emily were excellent hosts for a Thursday night open mic.  They are also the most friendly people we met this week in Nashville, I mean everyone in Nashville were friendly, just Emily and Ellie were extra!  

Cozy and very good sounding stage.  Rich and decadent espresso.  Unique vintage clothing for men and women, with affordable pricing.  Very cool rock bike leather jackets made by Bowery Vault.

Will be back!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Nashville's best theatre with an array of indie options. At times, Vanderbilt professors lead film discussions. Plus, this theatre is non-profit.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Going to see Declan McKenna tonight. I have two spare tickets for attendee. Not for sale. LGBT friendly. General admission. I'll finish review after I see the show.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
We attended a show there last night for the first time. My husband is a disabled veteran who walks with a cane and has a service dog so events like this are hard one him.
The security staff were amazing. We were treated like they were watching out for a family member. We entered first, didn't wait in line, they brought him a chair until the doors opened. They provided us stools, told me where each guy was going to be in case we needed anything. Security checked on him throughout the night. We even were walked out of venue safely, behind the crowd. 
I can not say enough about how caring security was. We will be back!

name: Drifters
text:
Too bad I can't give Drifter's zero stars. It was THAT bad. My husband got the kielbasa hot dog bun sandwiches w sauerkraut. He wigged out when he tried the sauerkraut. Who makes 'bad' sauerkraut? It's already fermented, but we all know what regular kraut tastes like. This didn't. It was just plain weird and icky tasting.
     I follow a keto way of eating and find there's usually something on any menu I can order. So, I went w the large dinner salad with added brisket for $12.79. The salad was a big bowl full of bland iceberg lettuce, about eight super tiny squares of chopped tomato, and maybe 10 thread-bare pieces of shredded cheddar cheese. The brisket was beyond horrible. It was cold, greasy, and mostly in hard chunks. I was fairly hungry, so I tried to make the best of it. I tossed everything w my balsamic vinaigrette and ate it all. Within two hours after returning home I became violently ill. I vomited all night and the next morning until 10:00. I thought my organs were going to come out. I was also sick on the other end.
     I didn't notify the restaurant because first, I figured they simply didn't care about the quality and taste of their food, and second, I thought if they didn't care, why would they care if one of their unimportant customers got as sick as a dog from eating their slop.
     Seriously, don't eat at Drifter's BBQ in Nashville on Woodland.

name: The Bowery Vault
text: This place is so awesome and welcoming! I bought an authentic leather jacket and I can't wait to wear it. At night, this place turns into a music venue. I will have to come back and check it out. Definitely worth a spot to stop by!

name: Drifters
text: The best wings in Nashville without a doubt - a great selection of bbq/hot sauces - amazing burgers, too!  The staff is fantastic (especially Sarah!); also, a dog friendly patio!  Usually the live music is decent, as well.....highly recommended!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: I like the Mercy lounge for a small venue.  The sound and lighting was respectable - which is a must to see live music.  I enjoyed that they had an outdoor patio so you could sit outside and view the Nashville sky line for a bit if you wanted.  The bathrooms were a tight squeeze, but manageable.  It did take a bit of time to get a drink, but when you're trying to serve that many people with only a few b-tenders, what else do you expect.  I was saddened in the beer selection and the fact there were no drafts on tap!  Really you're a bar for brew's sake!  So we opted for the $3.00 PBR's which I guess is a good deal if you're 21 and broke LOL.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: This place blows. Took 2 hours to get our meal and that's not even an exaggeration. Did the bottomless mimosas and got served straight OJ. Would never recommend under any circumstances. Fuck this place

name: Springwater
text:
The final stop on our dive bar hop was Springwater. Why the hell it has taken me so long to come here I will never know. 

It's so dirty and divey that it made my heart skip a beat when I walked in - in a good way. That was love I was feeling. The first room has pool tables, characters ranging from maybe homeless to that dude might be lost, a random dog chilling in a booth, and 70s bucket bar seats lined up in front of the fairly short bar. We grabbed a seat and got us some cheap cold Miller Lites and started immediately talking to the bartender and the people around us. 

In the back room a band was playing and it is dark and loud back there. I greatly preferred listening to the band from the other room but your interest in the band may vary. There are some tvs above the bar to watch that sporting event you want to keep up with also. Bathrooms are small but definitely not the nastiest I've ever seen. Small patio too but you can smoke inside so not sure why the patio is there - perhaps for some fresh air or to watch the characters driving around centennial park at night. 

People watching is the best. The night we were there an entire wedding party came in including the bride in her white dress. A guy wearing a shirt saying "in dog beers I've only had one". A dude bruh trying to drunkenly hit on my friend but repeating himself mercilessly. It's got everything you would want. So you gotta go!

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
Mercy Lounge is obviously a major player in the Nashville music scene. The focus is definitely on the show - the sound quality was awesome, and the local bands were surprisingly great. Admission was a super reasonable $10. Even though the venue is serious about their music, the space and the crowd give the impression that this is just a regular hangout with no pretenses. Bartenders were responsive, always looked your way despite how busy the place was, and somehow understood what you said despite the fact that they probably couldn't hear you at all.

We did have a funny time counting the number of minorities... it totaled 5 or 6 that night, across several hours, for a packed room across a huge space. Not so great, but I do realize it's Nashville..

Worth a visit as a tourist? Yes! It's not a visit to Nashville without live music. Mercy puts on great shows that feel representative of the talent that Nashville has to offer.

name: Commodore Grille
text:
Basic place. Convenient being in our hotel. 
Service was mediocre and the food was fair. I did like the live music, especially the songwriter nights. 
Good place to grab some drinks and listen to some music if you want a relaxing night at your hotel.

name: EXIT/IN
text: Great Venue. I did get a refund for the past show that was cancelled. Thanks!!! Will see another show here.

name: Drifters
text: One of my favorite hangs.  Always somewhere to sit, great live music on the weekends and I dig that they have a pong table out for people to play.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: There isn't really a whole lot to say about this little spot, but you can expect some serious Nashville charm, live music and a cold beer.  You get to make your mark by placing your "stamp" on a dollar bill and adding it to their collection.  Thirsty?  Like beer?  Stop on by!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Briefly stopped in here to grab a beer and listen to music - loved this place! There was a great band playing and it wasn't too packed so we could really enjoy ourselves. Will definitely be coming back!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Pretty cool place for tourists like myself. My niece and I had a good time. The drinks are SO expensive at this place that it's worth it to go to a place like Roberts just up the street for cheaper and better everything. This place is cool but make sure you bring your wallet.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
This is for the music, we have been here for 2 days and stepped in and out of a few bars and the music here is top notch! 

Cozy little bar with great music!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Had my first visit to Nashville a few days ago, and my nephew told me to be sure that I stopped by this bar. Best recommendation ever! Walked in to amazing music (Kassie and Wilson performing on a Friday afternoon), Laura behind the bar made us feel like regulars returning after being gone too long. It was a struggle to leave, but we were in town for a wedding and had to keep on schedule. Managed to sneak back to Broadway after the wedding the next night, and we did the stroll looking for a place to stop and listen to the music. I wasn't surprised when we ended up back at Benchmark, perched on barstools as the charming Vanessa and more fantastic music made the evening fly by. Can't wait to go back to Nashville, and I guarantee that a couple of visits to Benchmark will be on our schedule!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
If you are a bachelor/bachelorette party, this is a required stop for a Nashville night out.  If that sort of scene bothers you, I'd probably visit Honky Tonk Central either during the day or just not come at all.

My husband and I visited three times during our 5 day stay in Nashville.  The first time was for lunch (nothing to write home about- pretty much the same bar food they sell everywhere else), the second was for a few quick drinks, and the last time was on our last Saturday night in town.

Daytime entertainment is, like most places on Broadway, mostly acoustic.  Some acts were better than others.  On the Saturday night we visited, we were able to snag two seats at the bar, so we sat tight for hours (especially since there was a big screen TV in front of us, playing the Final Four games).  All the times we were there, there were no cover charges.

I liked this place because you have three floors of music and it was pretty wide open (unlike Tootsies) so even though it was packed, you never felt claustrophobic.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: I saw Isaac play here a couple of years ago.  We loved his music and have even enjoyed following him on Facebook.  I recently caught a video of Isaac playing at the Benchmark ... got me revved up for a long overdue return to Nashville.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Was there recently and said what has happened to the lower Broad I once knew. I saw three people vomiting and many stumbling drunk. The police stood by and seemed not to care. Nashville has tons of musicians but only a few will make it to the next level. Most who play here will not. The food was just alright and the toilet gets a D at best. Go to the Blue Bird. Better neighborhood.

name: Nashville Underground
text: We are locals and we LOVE this place for the most amazing breakfasts!!  Why wait in long lines at the other breakfast places when you can walk right into here and be served immediately!!  Bartenders are awesome.  The "Bloody Mary" is amazing and you get to make it yourself with all the goodies they have set out for you.  It will not disappoint!!  Highly recommend for a great downtown Nashville weekend breakfast!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
First experience at 3rd and Lindsley was a good one. 

Since I had a group in town who wanted something fun to do, other than Broadway, I found 3rd and Lindsley. We had a great time. Saw the first show, which was Justin Forrest who was a grand surprise as well. I didn't expect great blues. We didn't eat so I can't comment on the food but our drinks were delivered quickly each time. The place is clean and staff is helpful, friendly and efficient. Not only will I go again, I can't wait to go again. Its a great deal, a great place and the entertainment is over the moon.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great atmosphere. Great food. Fast service for being so packed. Love this place so much! Best place in Nashville!

name: Alley Taps
text:
We were so happy to stumble across this place as we were walking around the downtown area. It's adorably located in the middle of a large brick alley- we would have missed it if it wasn't for the pop-up sign on the street. The atmosphere is really fun! The entire place has a prohibition-era theme with a long bar, a stage for live music, and lots of decoration. 

They have 2 for 1 drinks for Happy Hour during the week, and we were pleasantly surprised the strength of the drinks. The female bartender was generous and polite. If you are looking for a hip place to grab a good drink or craft beer, you should definitely look for this hidden gem! When we return to Nashville, we will be back! Thanks Alley Taps!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This bar/restaurant is massive and located right on Broadway. There are 3 floors with live music with people of all ages. The drinks were average priced.

I didn't eat here personally because of the night scene- didn't seem too clean of a place to eat at. There are bathroom attendants and great bartenders.

ATM charges $6 to take out money, so if you want cash on you- I suggest taking it out elsewhere! The bar accepts cash and card however.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
I attended my first concert this week at Ascend and was thoroughly impressed. The view is outstanding from any seat or the lawn. The sound system is crisp, clear and easy to hear anything from all spots. The location on the riverside and the base of the pedestrian bridge is unique and enhances the experience. 

If you have the opportunity to see a show here; do it!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: One of my favorite bars in Nashville. What makes it my favorite you ask, Isaac Mathews.  Awesome singer.  If you haven't seen him play you are missing out.  One of the main reasons I go there is to see Isaac.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
I made reservations for 4 with opentable.com. Life got in that way, and I used the site to delay our reservation 30 minutes. When we arrive, I learned the site and the restaurant weren't communicating, and our reservation was cancelled. It was a slow, rainy night so we were sat right away. No big deal. 

The live music on the first floor was so loud conversation was impossible except for what we could fit in, in between songs. It's okay though. We spent most of the time with our mouths full. The fried green tomatoes are delicious. We actually ended up ordering a second serving after our party devoured the first in a matter of minutes. Crispy meatballs were exactly what you'd expect. Calamari was a bit too chewy for my liking. But, the bacon on the charcuterie tray, oh my gosh, that bacon. Goodness gracious. Everyone should try it! It's the perfect blend of crispy and chewy, salty and sweet. You just need to try it for yourself. I'd recommend washing it down with a Tennessee Mule - they don't skimp on the Old Camp. Forgo the banana pudding unless you like crispy wafers. They're not my preference, but they might be yours. 


So they advertise as the tallest bar, whatever. The second floor was closed. The third and fourth floors are office space you can't actually get to. The roof top has corn hole, and I'm told they'll be getting more games soon. They play pop music up there too which someone might appreciate. I prefer country; it is downtown Nashville after all. 

A little forewarning, don't take the stairs, only use the elevator. I thought I'd go down the stairs instead of waiting on the elevator, and ended up locked in the stairwell because the doors lock automatically. I knocked the the rooftop door for almost five minutes before finally getting someone on the phone who could come let me back in the bar. Talk about a scary movie moment! 

Overall greatness: food = yes, bar = no.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Don't go for the food! 
  Frozen filler hamburger  patty , dry chicken and cheap prime rib.

name: The Pink Slip Lounge
text:
I stopped in at the Pink Slip while staying at Hotel Preston and had an A-OK experience.

The Great:
+ Live music
+ Local beers on tap

The Average:
o Fair prices
o When they made my Manhattan correctly, it was a quality drink.

The Poor:
- The food was underwhelming. I tried the bruschetta (overpriced, underwhelming) and the pizza (doughy, bland) and regretted the decision.
- When they made my Manhattan incorrectly it was terrible (different bartender, different night).

It's a cool spot to have a drink and catch a band, but eat before you get there.

name: Nashville Party Authority
text:
I just wanted to thank you for the great DJ service that Nashville Party Authority provided - and also specifically offer kudos for the great job that Josh did feeling out our group and helping folks to have a good time! He definitely kept the dance floor moving.
 
The country line dance instructor was perfect for getting our folks out onto the dance floor as well!

Thank you for the great work!

name: The Station Inn
text:
I was looking for the quintessential Nashville music experience and this was it.  I went to see the Roland white band and had a blast.   The place itself is really low key with some folding chairs and picnic bench seating.   The food is so-so serving pizzas and things of popcorn.  But that's not why you came here.   The atmosphere is great. Doors opened at 7 and we had time to get settled and chat it up with our neighbors for the evening.   Turns out we got some great tips on places to go things to see in town thanks to a bluegrass talent scout we met.  

The band was great.  tons of interaction with the crowd, kept things lively.  I enjoyed every track they played.   

If you're looking for a place to listen to music away from the chaos on Broadway come here its worth it.

name: The Station Inn
text:
$? no way..
we paid $9 for a small pitcher of coke. that is absurd..
other than that it was 'jam session night' so there was no cover.

the music was amazing.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: What a disaster. Despite having tickets and being here two hours before show time, there are no seats. People are squeezed in like sardines. The fire department should be called.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I had an amazing day at this honky tonk. People underage are welcome here during the day and we sat and listened to the band for about 2 hours and I could have easily kept listening to them enjoying my soda. The band was super friendly and played a range of classic and modern country songs. If you don't like the band on one floor, there are 2 others you can try. We never switched floors because we loved the band on our floor but it would've been easy if we wanted to hear other bands as well. High recommend this place and we will probably go back tomorrow!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Good music and fun atmosphere. Food just average, nothing special. I don't think people go there for the food, they go for the entertainment and the drinks. Three floors with live music on each so you can't ever say that you're bored.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Honky Tonk! This place was very fun. Three floors of awesome music. A great view of the strip on the top floor. With three bands playing its easy to find one that suites you best. Also the crowd seemed friendly I was able to make some cool friends at this bar.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Cool bar to hang out in but it can get super grimey. Can get really douchey at times but the three levels are cool to check out. If you can hang out near the balconies and oversee Broadway it's a good time. Really it's 3.5 stars from me.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This is the largest bar in the area - three stories with different bands on every floor.  As you go up the floors, the food selection, bar selection, quality of the bands and spirit of the crowd diminish significantly (no food on the third floor and no cocktails).  On the plus side, the bands are good and fun, take requests for songs, and try to excite the crowd (especially on the first floor), on the minus side - they walk around the tables with their tip jar.  I understand the importance of tipping, but the jar is already big (more like a bucket), sitting at their feet, and anyone who wants to make a request for a song or go outside has to pass by it anyway.  So they look like street performers when they ask for tips.  The honky tonk tea (a version of a long island iced tea) is good, the lemon drop is lacking.  The atmosphere, however, is great - it's loud and fun, with people tapping their feet and singing along.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I have never in my life been treated with as much disrespect as I was treated this evening. My friends and I entered Honky Tonk lured by the music, and proceeded to the bar. I ordered a round of drinks and left my card with the lovely, friendly bartender. As it began to fill up, my party decided that it was time to go. At no fault of the bartender, it was difficult to close my tab. I couldn't get her attention, so I tried to wedge in so that I could signal for someone to close our tab. Numerous witnesses attested to the fact that a young female patron was staring me down as I did so, even going as far as to call over a "friend" or boyfriend of hers to push me and actually pull my hair. Once he pulled on my hair, I did in fact turn to him and confront him. His female friend attacked me and I do, in fact, have scratches to prove it. He called me a slew on horrific names and spoke to me in such a way that I wished his own mother could have heard, as she would have been disappointed and appalled. I know, as I am a mother myself. I turned to the bartender who noticed the commotion and asked for my tab. Once I did, I felt a complete drink being dumped on my head. Witnesses will say it was the original young girl patron, I however thought it was the man because as I turned to him he gave me a smug grin and a wave. I reacted as only a woman assaulted would react. I screamed and was held back by my friends. The bartender motioned for the other female to be removed, however, the insanely disrespectful and horrific "man" commiserated with a large bouncer and this is where my main issue takes place. A MAN, a large man, employed by Honky Tonk turned to me, a drenched (from the drink,) hysterical crying (from shock,) mother and started physically pushing me out of the establishment. He even went as far as threatening to put me into a cob car himself if I didn't comply. He didn't know that my own husband was law enforcement himself and was inside trying to defuse the situation. As I cried that my card was still inside, he used his large body to physically push me out. My husband attempted for 20 minutes to get my cc back, and was told it was "lost." My friend went in later and a full 30 minutes later was given the card but with charges on it that I did not authorize. My family has been in the restaurant/bar business for 40 years and I have never, nor has my family ever seen such Unprofessionalism. We plan on contacting the better business bureau, as well as a lawyer for the the physical harm that has come to me. I encourage everyone to stay away. Any establishment that would allow this to happen, is not one that should stay in business.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
This may be the busiest bar/restaurant on Monday nights in Nashville. The reason? Simple: The Time Jumpers, Nashville's country big band that should be on every music lover's list. Attending one of their performances has been on my bucket list for several years. So glad I made it. Seeing this band in person you understand why pretty much every performance of theirs is sold out.

Not a bad seat in the house, good sound on the night of our visit and the crowd is respectful of the performers. It's very likely I'll be back to see this band again even though it requires a 600 mile flight.

Average bar food. Nothing spectacular going on here. With the kind of crowd they command on Mondays alone, not to speak of other nights, a little surprised they aren't kicking the food quality up a notch. It wasn't bad, it was just OK bar grub like burgers, your requisite appetizers. How not make a *great* burger instead of an average one? Mostly a beer crowd from what I observed. When I ordered a Zinfandel they brought me some God awful kind of blush wine that I requested sent back. I had asked to pay the tab for a party of five and they complied without complaint. Service was above average to my eye for this kind of venue.

If you come, come early, particularly if you're seeing the Time Jumpers. Parking is pretty limited. We found a spot up the street 50 yards or so. Not particularly inconvenient, just very limited. Overall a great smaller live music venue well worth your visit.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great prices for good food in downtown...try the nachos plenty to share

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: 3rd and Lindsley is an interesting spot to catch a show. I particularly like heavier rock shows at this location as the acoustics and set up here are intimate but clean, comfortable and a little more upscale than some such shows typically get. To top it all off, this place actually has food with waiter service---and it is pretty good! It's nice to stop in for a band you really like but that isn't the normal crowd-drawing Nashville act, get in when the doors open, sit and order a meal and a brew, and still have time to get in the pit near the stage after a good meal. Parking is odd here as you're likely to end up in one of the many neighboring businesses which close before this place usually opens but luckily they're all mostly cool with that.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
I saw a small little show here. Never have been here before, I was hesitant hearing some negative reviews.

Personally I had a great time. They can get some really decent acts for being so small. It was packed when I went so the bar service was really slow and hard to get to, but the beers were pretty cheap so I can't argue about that. 

I'd come back again.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Went there to go see the talented and incredible Brit Stokes. Anytime I come to Nashville I always look up two of the best,Brit Stokes and Isaac Matthews. Not only was Brit and the band so good but the food (nachos preferably) was incredible. The waitress was top notch and she worked her tail off the whole time. It's only fair and suiting that you tip the band well, tip the waitress well and go see Brit Stokes at this really cool and classy joint. I felt like I had quality seats at a top notch concert. Do yourself a favor and go to Famous Saloon and order the Nachos and enjoy the shows. Great food, Great Music, Great times. I'll be back next time I'm in town.

name: Nashville Underground
text: This place is absolutely gorgeous and stands out among all the other restaurants/venues in Downtown Nashville.. the staff, food , drinks EVERYTHING is top notch!! You feel like you are stepping into another city when you walk in. Nashville needed Nashville Underground

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Another awesome Broadway Street Honkey tonk!   Huge bar, food service and great music.  
Huge TV for the sports fans!!  
Didn't have the food here but the wings smelled amazing!!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Typical bar on Broadway..etc it is 3 stories tall on a prime location...corner lot of 4th and Broadway..It looks sort of New Orleans style with all the windows and doorways with little balcony areas...

But again,...its just a bar...
There was a major accident a few months back..someone fell to their death...I was afraid that would happen...
But if you like loud, rowdy and drunken excitement..then have at it !!!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Nice place.  Good service and food. Nothing fancy. Hot chicken nice and spicy, and that was only medium! What would 'ring of fire' be like?

name: Famous Nashville
text: This is what Nashville needs. It's a stylish, classy bar atmosphere with top-notch service and really great food (bar food + some more creative options like Avocado pasta!). I love that it is located off Broadway, because it IS different than the sticky sweaty honky tonks we are all used to - and I do love those too. Famous Saloon picked our group up from the Gulch in a private, pimped out shuttle bus (more like a party bus) and drove us to them. We had a fantastic dinner and the best bartender/server, then we danced the night away: first downstairs to country music and then upstairs on the rooftop with a DJ. This is a very cool addition to our bar scene!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Our first time here and we could not believe how rude this bartender was to me. We order 4 drinks, my husband did not hold his drink when handed to him bc he was too busy getting money from his wallet, so I reached out to get the beer that was set on the table. Next thing you know this CRAZY, RUDE, UNPROFESSIONAL bartender snapped at me "You can't do that!!!! You can't get the beer until he paid first?" Dumb girl, then why where you trying to handed to him? Such rudeness, she shouldn't be in this industry if you don't have a customer service mentality!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Not the friendliest place. As a local, this is one of the worst bars to visit or play at. The staff isn't very friendly and they could care less. Good luck getting a drink.

name: Famous Nashville
text: This is one of those gems of a place that we just decided stop in on our way between two destinations.. loved the view from the rooftop bar! Great place to stop for a drink.... or 6

name: The Cowan
text: Nashville has some goofy music venues, but The Cowan has a couple of good things about it compared to others.  As a musician who has played a number of Nashville clubs, I like that The Cowan has a real stage with a back-stage area.  Many places treat the stage as an after-thought.  I also like the size of the room.  It's what I would consider mid-sized.  It's not small like Douglas Corner, and it's not too big making it difficult to fill if you're not well known.  They have a nice balcony.  Thankfully it's on the north side of downtown.  I get tired of everything being on the south or near south side.  The only suggestion would be to have some tables and chairs on the main floor.  Unless you're a dance band, you don't want a large, wide open floor.  Give people some tables and chairs if they want to sit down.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: My favorite place for live music in Nashville.  Great atmosphere - nice stage area and intimate setting without being crowded.  Good acoustics.  I've loved every show I've gone to here.

name: Music City Male Revue
text: Amazing show!!! It was exactly what I wanted for my bachelorette. The guys are true performers, they're hands on and really fun!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
This venue is amazing.  That being said, I went to 3rd and Lindsley with a purpose, to hear Christone "Kingfish" Ingram play some blues in Nashville, TN and Kingfish put on one phenomenal show!  If you've never seen him, you should.  You WILL be a fan!   I was fortunate enough to meet and hear this young man when he was just 15 at a blues club in Clarksdale, Mississippi, and had the pleasure of sitting next to his sweet momma.

As an additional bonus, at 3rd and Lindsley, we sat with Ms Thornetta Davis, and her handsome husband James.  She's the blues Queen of Detroit!  We were blessed beyond measure that night!

Thornetta even sent me one of her CD's (because it was my birthday night) and it's so great that we listen to her and Kingfish all the time when we're riding on the bike.
I hope someday they get together and sing, I can travel!

Our bad experience was our server.  She charged for premium, without asking, and took so long to bring the drinks they were watered down when we received them.  My husband asked for a Guinness, and after 30 minutes went to the bar to just cancel it.  Our server saw him there and grabbed the Guinness and popped the top.  My husband said he'd just canceled it, and she said she couldn't put it back.  When our bill came, and we saw all the charges weren't correct, we asked for a manager.  He gave my husband $2.50 cash for the beer, but nothing about all the watery upcharges.  

If you go,  watch your credit card VERY closely... or be very wise, pay cash.

name: The Station Inn
text:
Bluegrass jam venue.  Musicians form a tight cluster and mostly jam and play for each other.  Most customers don't seem to go to listen to music, but treat it as a backdrop for conversation.  I had to move with my folding chair to behind the musicisions to hear anything.  Outside of being bumped by a guitar case, nobody seemed to mind me being there.  Food is has good  pizza with a good selection of beer.  An
Enjoyable evening once I got dialed in to how it works.  I don't hear much live bluegrass where I live, so I was happy to hear
The real thing again.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: I've been coming to Nashville on a regular basis (at least four times/month) for three years.  Benchmark is consistently a fun, friendly atmosphere where you can find amazing talent.  So much better than the vibe on Broadway, around the corner on Second Ave. you'll find great, friendly bartenders (Whitney Love and Co.), good bar food, music that will keep you in there for hours.  At the top of that headline is Isaac Mathews.  Isaac is friendly and interacts with the crowd and will amaze you with his pure tone and talent.  Bobby Tomlinson joins him from time to time and adds to the fun and talent as well.  You won't be disappointed if you come here for a drink, an hour or a night.  Ask Isaac to play "Like a Cowboy".  You won't want to leave.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
We visited Saturday night and it was a fun bar.

Positives.

Guys, you need to check this place out. I'm married but noticed there were plenty of attractive women and they outnumbered the guys probably 2 to 1. It's one of the few bars I've ever been to that wasn't a sausage factory!

Even though the place was packed and appeared understaffed the Bar Tender on the 3rd floor was prompt and polite.

We ordered chicken tenders and fries (a little overpriced but that was expected) and they were on the table in record time and they were fresh so the kitchen staff was on top of their game!

Drinks were good and reasonable for the area.

Awesome views of Lower Broad from the balconies on the third level. You can see all the action in the area and get some fresh air too.

There was a decent house band that played a great variety of music from old time country, new country, pop and rock.

Large TV's throughout the bar to watch sports or whatever. They had the Game 5 of the Predators Ducks on to watch while we were there.

I wish I could give 5 stars but there were a couple negatives.

The lower level was so over crowded you couldn't move, that's why we immediately made our way to the 3rd floor.

The restrooms were absolutely nasty, urine on the floor and the sinks filled with empty cups and beer bottles.

The staff for the most part was polite and attentive. Unfortunately there was one or two security staff who had "tough guy attitude". Let me be clear, most of the staff including the security was very nice and were even helping try to keep the place clean but the one that stood out was about a 400 pounder who had a terrible attitude, he was vaping in the bar and it was blowing right in peoples faces. At one point in the night he was throwing things away that a bachelorette party had left on the table next to us to save their spot while they all visited the restroom. I tried to tell him they would be back in a moment and he just gave me a dirty look, yelled something at me and continued to toss their stuff out.

All in all it was still a great place and of course very touristy but I could recommend it to locals too.

name: The Station Inn
text:
The Station Inn averages out to a "high 3," but I ultimately had to round down because of the insulting food quality. The "pizza" is minor step up from the stuff my sister and I used to make when we were kids and ran our own "pizzeria" and made "deliveries" to "mom's room." The "pizzas" were basically Wonder Bread and ketchup, topped with melted string cheese. Gross. It's not much better at Station Inn, where you're basically eating oven-baked cardboard, canned tomato "sauce," mystery meat ("sausage"), and Kraft something cheese. Enough irony for you? OK, I'll stop.

The music, on the other hand, is terrific, and I recommend staying for a couple hours and getting a full and wide gamut of bluegrass sets. Other reviewers here are lauding the "authenticity" of the music, but I'm not sure I can actually speak to that. For one, "authenticity" is very much a "cultural construct." Is there really an obvious delimiter for breaking off the inauthentic form the authentic, the inorganic from the inorganic? And what of musical genres themselves, given what we know about hybridity and cultural mixing? Last, I've been sour on "authenticity" as a concept in recent years. Like "neighborhood," it's often seeped in artifice propelled by urban real estate development, and live music venues are frequent nodes for cultivating this mystification. Don't believe me? Read David Grazian's Blue Chicago ethnography about "authentic" jazz clubs in Chicago, where proprieters (sp) purposely rip seats and make internal decor look cheap so the place feels more "authentic." I was so outraged reading the book that I had a hard time getting into live jazz/blues music for about a year afterwards, so distracted was I over whether venues were trying to pull an 'authenticity ruse' on me.

Bottom line: the music here is great, authentic or inauthentic, and the food is downright horrible. If you come here after a good meal, well, that's the way to do it.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Very poor service. Waited 30 minutes for a server after being seated. Two waitresses continually walked past us and just ignored us. My wife asked one of them if someone was covering the area and rudely replied Yes! I will get to you. Ten minutes later I asked another server and he got us somebody from another section. Was not super busy in there not sure what the issue was.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: So surprised by how much I liked Honky Tonk Central. To be honest, I had never been to Nashville and wasn't all that excited about Broadway. But, I LOVED this place! We sat on the second floor. There were a ton of tables, servers to keep the drinks flowing, and an amazingly talented band. I don't love new country music, but this band was so talented and engaging that I let my "Steve" drink settle in and I embraced the atmosphere that is Nashville. I was sad to leave. This place is so much better than Tootsie's or any other of the "must do" bars on Broadway.

name: The Basement East
text:
Wasn't a big fan of the brunch we had this morning. Great music but super loud.The breakfast burrito was bland and basically filled with undercooked sliced potato. 

The Pub Mary was way too salty. I liked that they took a risk with it and used fresh tomatillo, but for every sip of drink I had to take a hit of water.

Very overpriced for what it was.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
