We had a great variety of food and everyone agreed that the food was yummy and plentiful.  When I arrived at the bar, the tables were decorated beautifully and the furniture was arranged to accommodate our group.  The two people who worked during the time of our party were attentive, helpful and efficient.  There were almost 90 of us.  If you are having a private party in Nashville this would be a great location.  They are easy to work with and our group had an enjoyable time.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Oh man, this was my favorite places in Nashville! The live band was playing a little of everything. I heard Sublime, Aerosmith, Tom Petty, Eminem, Pearl Jam and the very best Led Zeppelin. I only had beer here but the bartenders were on top of it. The place was jam packed yet the line went quickly. I highly recommend this place.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Everything about our visit to this place was "meh".  The service we received from the bartender made us feel like we were a bother to him and he paid us almost no attention. We got draught beers, which were fine, and we ordered the hummus plate. From the pictures we'd seen in reviews, it looked like a thoughtfully crafted plate. Our was not so beautiful- I wish I had taken a picture. There were a few pieces of pita, several green zucchini pieces, and three piles of the chunkiest hummus I've ever seen. It tasted okay but the presentation was pretty gruesome. There was also no live music at 4pm on a Saturday (which I realize we could have researched further online before choosing this place) so we weren't doing any listening at the Listening Room! Maybe if we came later in the day we would have felt more welcome and better served.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Paid way too much for so little. Love Johnny cash! They truly got you - for the store. You had to line up for tickets with everyone buying stuff from the store. I think I'm just used to more organization and this was just not laid out well at all. 
Line entry goes back toward the bathroom!! Nothing blocking you from walking straight and not seeing the turn toward the opening. Next ya walk in and be careful not to do what we did - we went down the narrow pictured wall and turned RIGHT to the stone wall and followed that right OUT THE DOOR AND DONE. Nothing showing you you had to walk LEFT To more displays. It was wayyyy too crowded. Toooooooo crowded. 

Better organization would be awesome. And less about the store and more about the musician. Not impressed.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
Great show!  Very talented actors and singers!

The food was good and we didn't have to wait to eat.  We were served as soon as we walked in!  A nice Christmas dinner with turkey and ham.

Fun adventure to go on while visiting Nashville!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Good music tonight at BB King's:  Eight O'five Jive.  We received good service.  The BBQ chicken was excellent.   My husband had the brisket and he loved it.  The BBQ sauce was delicious.  The fried pickles were very good.  I have no complaints.   I will definitely come here the next time we get to Nashville.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Visiting from out of town and found this restaurant last minute on a Saturday night. Seated quickly, food arrived quickly. Our waiter Eddie was FABULOUS. And everything we ordered was great. Reasonably priced, especially given the quality of the food. My teenage son had the bacon wrapped meatloaf, my teenage daughter had shrimp and grits. I had the chickpea and avocado appetizer with salmon added and it was a full meal. Great experience all the way around.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I had a wonderful time touring the Grand Ole Opry. If you have a AAA card you'll get an additional discount. The tour is a little over an hour and they start it off by showing a 10 minute video with Blake Shelton explaining the history. You get to see areas where they have filmed shows (Nashville, most currently), all of the dressing rooms and you get to go on stage too. It was an amazing experience.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Found Belcourt Taps after doing a Google maps search of the area. Stopped in for drinks and dinner. What a little gem this place is! Great beer selection and seriously good BBQ Ribs. I mean phenomenal fall off the bone tasty, tender Ribs! Actually talked to the man who smoked them out back. Lucky enough to be seated at the bar next to the owner who was wonderful to chat with. 
Now to top all that off they had a line up of young musical talent that was excellent! 
To sum it up; Great food + Great service + Great drinks ++ Great music = We'll be back!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Seriously terrible. "Ms.Kelli" is the rudest business owner and cares more about putting her boobs in men's faces than she does anything else. The place is gross. Also, tons of underaged people seeing as it's extremely easy to sneak in the back. Don't waist your time. I feel terrible for the nice bartenders having to work under such poor management.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
This little hidden gem is amazing!! Their awesome sandwich board signs on the street is what caught our attention. We even snapped pics of it & decided we were going to hit up this spot later. 

We came in to wait out the thunderstorm and happened to get a table by the little stage. The guy performing was awesome.  It was a Saturday night & one of the specials was $2 PBR so naturally, I had one ha. I wasn't too hungry but felt I needed to eat something so decided on their pulled pork quesadilla & a side salad. Both were extreme filling and super delicious; sadly, I couldn't finish my food. 

If we had more time in our quick visit, we would have come back but the next time I'm in town, definitely hitting this spot up!!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I've been here before and loved it but tonight the server Mary ruined our night.  We had company in from all over and wanted to show then a great time in nashville. Mary was rude immediately upon engaging our table and the disservice continued throughout our interaction.  She brought my mother-in -law's food out 30 minutes late with no apology just a snarky remark. Despite our lighthearted interactions she never acknowledged us with even a smile.  We may come back again for a great drink selection but Mary has greatly soured the taste.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great place, good food, reasonable prices and great service.  A locals place tucked away in an alley.  You can't go wrong here.

name: Anthem
text: Went to this shitty bar with a group of friends for a birthday party. There was only one white guy in the group of minorities and it just so happens that he for his cover waiver... No wonder why the bar is closing.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Had a grand time here seeing Carrie Underwood. The staff were helpful and very friendly. They really cared about the music. The atmosphere was great and the seating was very comfortable.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
I'm not sure how people can NOT like the Flying Saucer. There are maybe the best hot pretzels I've ever had, dipping sauces, seats aplenty, booze, and a long-term beer drinking contest.

This outpost is right next to a sumptuous train station-turned-hotel that is definitely worth a look. There was plenty of seating even though football playoffs were on (the projection screen isn't the sharpest, guys), and our knowledgeable waitress helped me find an absolutely delicious strawberry beer that I had never heard of.

Loved it.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: First time at the Nashville Saucer was a huge success. Parking was close, door greeter showed us to the kiosk when he realized we weren't locals, we got a table for two walking in late on a Saturday night, drinks were served fast & cold, and football was on a big screen right in front of us. Really couldn't have been better!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
First time in Nashville, so we had to go to the Grand Ole Opry. It took us hours to order the tickets, the website did not work properly. Finally it worked, but on a different night we initially wanted, because the website did not allow us to go to that night. Perhaps it was sold out?
We picked up the tickets at the Ryman, and the show turned out to take place at a different venue. We did not know this, we are not from around here and the website or the confirmation email had not mentioned that at all. The girl at the Ryman was really friendly though and offered to help us with everything.

The show itself was lots of fun! Good music, entertaining people, the commercials in between hilarious.

The tickets were very expensive and due to the venue that was 12 miles away, we were forced to pay $30 to get there. In the intermission we payed $6 for two cokes. Expensive evening.

But we had a good time.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text:
Nice local american themed bar with a good crowd and awesome live bands. 
Stopped here while bar hopping around town and had a real nice time. The beer was cold, the staff was great, and the band was awesome. Prices were reasonable and they had a nice local variety of local brews.
Deff worth stopping in for a beer or 5 lol!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Not a bad place. Printers alley is pretty cool and every time I am around I end up in this place. Nothing spectacular about the bar. Not the best kareoke singers in the world but definitely a small town kinda feel at this place.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: It's The Grand Ole Opry. How can you not give it 5 stars? Well I'll keep this review short. We came here during a visit in Nashville and was lucky enough to score tickets to an amazing show. It was being headlined by Carrie Underwood and featured Charlie Daniels as well as other guest. We had seats towards the bottom of the side balcony which gave us perfect view of the performers.  I loved the history of the Opry from when it was built in 1974 and was almost destroyed in 2010.  It looks great now and it's like stepping into a country music museum.  Seats were comfortable and the acoustics sounded great. It's a 2 hr show with 4 main singers being hosted kinda like a radio show, but that just adds to the nostalgia of the experience. This was possibly the best part of my trip to Nashville. Make sure you check out a show if you are in town!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: When I first walked into BB's my first impression was I liked how classy the decor was and how it wasn't tacky! The place is huge inside and makes you feel like your in a real blues club! I went for lunch and had the catfish bites and beef brisket! The catfish bites were very delicious and the brisket & BBQ sauce were also very tasty! I bought myself a bottle of the sauce to take back home! I wish I could have went there for dinner because the menu and crawfish bites look awesome for dinner time! Overall I really liked and enjoyed my experience at BB's! I recommend this place to locals or people who are passing through!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Love this place!  Very chill, great music, just wish they were Newcastle fans.... ;). Best place in Nashville.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The best ribs ever. If they have live music it's even better time. The spice on the ribs was so awesome with the flavors. All the food was really good. Mac and cheese and chicken fingers for kids. Would highly recommend.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: We found this on a whim after a conference at the convention center and couldn't have been more thrilled. We had five people and ordered burgers (veggie and otherwise) and the chicken Philly and LOVED them. They were flavorful, quick, and well priced. We are coming back here in April and will be eating here again. Highly recommend taking the walk down the back alley to find it.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Horrible service. Horrible owner. Strangers are allowed behind the bar. (Why hasn't the ABC been alerted about this? It's illegal!) Go elsewhere.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
Really cool bar that we stumbled across for the first time tonight.  It's the only non-smoking bar I've found downtown that isn't a chain.

Prices were reasonable, scene is low key, environment is casual, and the food is pretty good.  Glad I found a bar downtown that isn't so crazy!

Will definitely be back!!!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The service and live band was amazing. Our waiter, Josh was extremely helpful with the food selections since all the items on the menu sounded amazing. Service was even better then the NYC location. Highly recommend the BBQ Salmon dish and the strawberry daiquiri!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
This place is a beer-lover's heaven. If you become a regular, I recommend joining the UFO club. Once you've tried a certain number of beers (200 I think? Or maybe just everything they have?) you get your own plate, *ahem* saucer, on the ceiling. 

The food is good too, but the beer is what you really want here. 

Highly recommend.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
This is a fun place to watch country music. We came on a Saturday night and watched a show from 7 PM to 9:30 PM. They had several musicians and the music is excellent. It is a nice auditorium, with comfortable seating.  The doors open at 6 pm and the staff keeps the audience entertained until the show starts at 7 pm.

The grand old Opry does sell out on weekends so I recommend getting your tickets several weeks in advance.  The parking lot does get full from the outlet stores traffic so I recommend using a taxi or Uber.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Such a cool place with an insane beer list and good food. They have couches in the front where you can chill. They have a program where you drink 100 beers (3 per night max) and you get your own plate on their ceiling and...some other stuff, I hope? Watch out for the bacon-wrapped jalapeños, they are spicy af. Green chile stew is good and comforting to me. The tots are weird, not like real tots. The pizza is good. Sorry I keep using the word "good". Just trust me, you'll like it. So check it out!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great atmosphere great music the pork pulled pork tots we're phenomenal Great Taste. Also got the shrimp po boy it was good.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: When in Nashville...since we were here we figured we might as well actually go to the 'Opry, took a chance and got tickets the day of the show, not the best seats but worth the price ($45) The performers were all really talented and we had a good night, really nice to see a show where music comes before egos..a nice experience..if we ever get back to Nashville, I'd do the Opry agin...5th star missing because I thought a beer only cost 9.50 at a NY Yankees game.!!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
The worst. 
Most overrated. 
Waste of time and money imaginable. 
Portions are tiny and expensive. 
Definitely at tourist location set next to coyote ugly as well as hooters. 
You're already looking at Yelp so do yourself a favor and find somewhere that's not terrible to eat.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Decent food, abysmal service. We had the soft pretzel, beer cheese soup and veggie pita. No one greeted us when we walked in or seemed to even care that we were there. Once we found our way to the table and ordered, we saw neither hide nor hair of our waitress once she found out we only wanted 1 beer. Unmerited pretentiousness.  We won't be back.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Visited our first night in Nashville and had a great time! Great music, great food, and great service!

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
We came to Nashville and found exactly what we were looking for in Back Alley Diner. Stopped by for a late lunch, and it is a little hole in the wall bar with a nice attentive staff, quick service, cheap prices, and great food. 

It isn't your run of the mill frozen to plate bar food - the jalapeño poppers were the best we'd ever had and we could've definitely devoured another plate of them. My best friend and I both got the southwest burger and it was perfectly cooked and came out so quickly. 

If we were local we'd be regulars - they have great specials on drinks and food every day of the week. Will definitely be back on our next trip to Nashville!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Simply amazing. My wife and I saw Carrie underwood and many more with great seats less than 40 yards from the stage for 60 bucks a ticket. Where I am from lawn seats almost 1/4 mile away are 100 bucks a piece. Great venue with amazing history.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text:
Best inexpensive way to escalate a good time.

I love it when a place tries to cram many different bar staples into one venue. I love the cramming because it brings all sorts of different patrons into the bar searching for a good time and as my motto states, "I am a personal tour guide to a good time".

Located in Printers Alley or as my drunk friend so loving called it, Harry Potter Alley, Kelli's Karaoke is 100% all Karaoke all the time. This may discourage those looking to dance, but the patrons don't try to out sing each other with ballads, like other established Karaoke bars. This bar caters to the upbeat and the tone challenged.

Kelli's also has inexpensive drinks. Our group ordered multiple rounds and did not break the bank. In addition, the bar itself contains a huge case of multiple flavored Jello shots that are hefty in both size and taste. 

In the back of the bar you will find decent restrooms and a billiard table. In the front you will find an ever small dance floor and decent size stage for singing. TIP THE DJ OR YOUR WILL NEVER SING. I watched for over an hour, before I asked my boyfriend if he paid the DJ. Needless to say, I got my 15 seconds of fame, after a couple dollar please and thank you.

We danced, we sang, we met great strangers, and we drank. At the end of our experience we found small vendors outside ready to sell cigarettes, walking taco's, and chilli dogs to satisfy all in our groups' post drunk urges. Best note of the night were the taxes that line Printers Alley to take us home without wait, for I could not walk very far with this taco that night.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Summer, 2014... Went to BT&T the other week when my GF and I went to the Belcourt Theater to take in some NASA goodness going on there. I have to say that the service was EXEMPLARY. Their selection of local brews was excellent. I love the fact that they seek out and promote local brews. The food was... well, it wasn't great. My burger, despite being stuffed with bacon and topped with blue cheese, was dry as a bone. Not quite vulcanized, but well on its way. The potato salad was BLAND. Even my girlfriend's fries were flavorless. Come on guys, ever hear of lightly SEASONING food as you cook or finish it? I will say this...I really did like the place itself. I liked the waiter and barkeep. I thought the place has a great atmosphere. The food needs a little work, though. Make that adjustment and the place could be a regular spot for me. I will indeed go back for another try, though. After all, everybody deserves a second shot.

Fast forward to 1/9/2015... Once again, GREAT beer selection and atmosphere. They have also revamped their menu and it is MUCH improved. Kudos to these guys for doing that. This is now a place where I can do more than just take in the selection of finely crafted, local brews and live music.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
The live music atmosphere was AWESOME and so was our server. Only two complaints:

While the music was awesome, the volume not so much. You can hardly hear the person right next to you attempting to talk to you, much less the server attempting to take your order. Maybe it was just this particular night, but part of me even felt bad for the server, seeing as to how she basically had to get right next to our faces in order to be able to hear us. 

Second, the food was OK, but not great, especially for the price. I got the pork chop, & for $21, I expected alot more. The fried pickle appetizer, however, was definitely one of the best I've ever had. 
Overall, returning for the music and appetizer might be in the future, but didn't like enough to hurry back.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: My family and I bought four tickets to the Backstage Tour. Maybe you're not the worlds biggest country music fan. I'm not gonna sit here and tell why you should like the genre. You can still enjoy this building for what it is! It honestly feels holy or hallowed. You notice that when you walk towards the main entry and look up at three impressive and understated chandeliers overhead. There's not a ton of chrome or bling in the design. I think impressive and understated is a great way to describe the venue in fact. It's both fancy and homey at the same time. I hope we can all understand that it's more than just a venue. It's significant culturally as well as musically. I can't attend a concert in the short time I'm here and going through the Backstage Tour might even be preferential for someone in my category. The tour is about an hour and it covers all the big chunk of the Opry's history, including all the various locations and iterations that the show and its home has taken on. To actually walk on the stage and see what the artists are looking at is wild. You can see where Dolly gets her fan mail and take pictures of her dressing room. (Yes, she's still a main stay at the Opry.) While the likelihood of me getting tickets to a premiere show here are slim, getting to enjoy a backstage tour and taking pictures from all angles of the Opry is still a big treat. The tour itself is partially automated through pre recorded clips starring Blake Shelton alongside a live guided tour from an Opry employee. It's quick, it's easy and the photos are precious! The Opry tour is a great way to spend an afternoon in Nashville and it's easy to get to as well. Thank you for the fun tour Grand Ole Opry House and thank you Music City!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: This is a great, fun spot to head to with your girlfriends for an evening of cheap margaritas, jello shots and karaoke. I'm not one for singing but I certainly enjoy watching! It's a bit of a dive bar that allows smoking...which I'm not a fan of. They could do better at venting the place as it became unbearable after a couple of hours.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
I would give the Flying Saucer 5 stars based on their pretzels and cheese alone. AMAZING. I literally dream about these. 

Plus they have a fantastic beer selection and laid - back atmosphere. Good deals: Monday night is $3 pint night and there is always a $3 fire sale beer. 

Service is hit or miss but I always keep coming back!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Everyone refers to this as an experience ... and it was, in the best, possible way imaginable.

WOWEE!!!!

Great talent, polished performers.

We won two Cracker Barrel rocking chairs - still figuring how to ship the other one back to Canada!  LOL.

They allowed us backstage for about half an hour and I can honestly say that I was backstage, at the Opry, with John Anderson singing!!!!  

I will be back.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: 11/27/2015 in town for the Turkey Day weekend. Caught the band 'Nashville Nobody's '. They were great !!! Friend ed hem on Facebook. They r the regular house band at Tequila Cowboys - downtown Nashville. They also travel a bit too. They sing a wide range from pop to southern country- and more. CHECK THEM OUT  online too  Facebook, Reverbnation too I think

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Walked around the Opry grounds. Great photo ops.. However I wish the sign was all lit up! The R was out when we visited tonight, lame!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Great, fantastic, wonderful, a 'must do'....

Visited from the UK; Nashville itself. Had a few dodgy spots, but the Opry was a living legend - not that cheap, but you get 2 1/2 hrs live music, much of which is from top notch and well known musicians.

You can't go to TN and Nashville without going there - but book your tickets online in advance if you can to avoid disappointment  - top night out; in fact so good we went back the next night !

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Had so much fun at WannaB's during a girls trip to Nashville. The people were nice, the atmosphere was fun and supportive and they have a great karaoke selection. Will definitely be back at an upcoming bachelorette party.

name: Third Man Records
text:
This place is really, really cool. Several cool vintage music pieces, small items and records recorded at the place.

This is a must stop for any music lover!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: My first visit to The Grand Ole Opry. We purchased tickets months ago without knowing who was performing. I was initially disappointed when the headliners were posted, but after downloading both The Steel Woods and Charlie Worsham albums, I could hardly wait.  Parking was confusing as there were no obvious signs pointing to the main entrance, and after walking around Opryland (which was enjoyable) we found the Opry.  Easy to get in and the lines moved quickly. This was a Saturday night show. Seats were awesome.  The show was worth every cent. I accessorized at the souvenir shop and I'm looking forward to my next visit.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Food was delicious!! The staff however needs work, my waitress literally sat at the table with us to take the order which is unprofessional. Also, when i walked in the hostess mean mugged us and ignored us for 5 minutes and was reluctant to help us. Our waitress was kind of short with us until we inquired about alcohol then she lightened up. Gumbo& spinach dil were on point though.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
My girlfriend and I were looking for a place to eat dinner during CMA Fest.  The wait time for most super Yelp-friendly places was an hour+ and we didn't have that kind of time, so we strolled into Back Alley Diner (BAD food, BAD drinks, BAD service is their tagline.... for Back Alley Diner, not because it's bad).

We walked in and it's kind of a hole in the wall bar.  We seated ourselves and our waitress came to see us.  We ordered beers and mozzarella sticks as an appetizer.  The mozzarella sticks were typical TGI Fridays style mozzarella sticks.  Nothing to write home about, but not bad.

For dinner, I had the hot chicken sandwich and my girlfriend had the catfish po'boy.  The hot chicken was probably my favorite hot chicken I had while in Nashville (I tried to order it pretty much everywhere).  It was crispy on the outside, seasoned wonderfully and tender on the inside.  It balanced well with the mayo and pickle on the Texas toast.  Really, really good.  The catfish was good, it's a big portion.  Good breading.  The homemade potato chips she got as the side was really what she raved about though.

The only thing costing it a fifth star was that it took quite a while to get our food considering the place wasn't very busy.  Took about 30 minutes after we ordered to get the food.  All in all, very pleased with the experience and would definitely return.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: You have to love country western but for a gal that wasn't really into it, I had alot of fun and foot tapping along with the great singers and songs that were performed.  Shouldn't be missed if you're in Nashville.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Best fried pickles I've had. Hot wings whee above average. Ribs where average. Overall the food was okay.

Music on this particular night was quality. Overall this is a fun place, but didn't come for the food.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I just had dinner here with a group of friends for a bachelorette party. Our waiter, Colin, was spectacular, the music was stellar, and the food was great! The food may not be particularly spectacular but it's good, downhome, southern bar food and exactly what you would expect and more. I had the catfish poboy, which was delicious, and we had MANY drinks. All of which were delicious. If I am ever in Nashville again I will certainly be back.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Always a great time here. Stacy and Kristen are great (and both absolutely beautiful, to boot!)

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We went on the backstage tour. I loved seeing the dressing rooms and the family room. The tour guides were very informative and helpful. I would love to go back to see a show sometime.

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text: I normally go to the dan mcguiness in cool springs due to convenience of location for me, but was in the Gulch and so figured I'd venture up the hill and check out the Nashville location. Was very happy to find out was nonsmoking and was very happy to see that it had the look and feel of a pub as is advertised. Service was amazing, had a great array of beers available, some local crafts as well as the typical Irish fair of beers available. Had the spinach and artichoke dip while I was there(yes not very Irish but was looking for a quick snack), and the rest of the menu looked amazing, and would have had more if not for having dinner plans already. Bartender was very nice and attentive, customers in the place as well were great company to have. Overall a great experience and will definitely be back at some point soon.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
This place is off the beating path... It is literally in a back alley.  

Once you get passed that and the "dive" bar aspect prepare yourself for some great food!

We had the fork and knife burger and the gargantuan double burger. The double burger was too much food but it tasted amazing !!!!   The gf loved her fork and knife. 

We added wings as an appetizer and they too were delish !!!

Overall this place was a perfect 5. Amazing food and a great atmosphere.  It is not for the snooty but if you like good old fashioned back end charm with great food then put this on your radar !

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: A really fun place for BBQ and music in Nashville. I know it's a bit of a tourist trap but if you're bringing your family with little ones, this would be an idea eating place vs ones of those on Broadway with all of the homeless musicians and drunks. I had the slab of ribs and thought it was pretty good!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I went on a Tuesday and It was packed.  Standing room only for 20 minutes then the bar opened up.  The food and the music was good. I had the hickory burger snd it was good. The music was the best part of the whole thing.  I didn't mind the cover charge,  just wish they had more seats that night. I would go again and would recommend it. Just go early to get a seat.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great beer selection (but you know that). Decent food (but you know that too). What do you not know? Getting a glass of wine of any type, is damn near impossible (but hey, it's a beer pub). And another thing, did you know that it's really loud? Yeah, you knew that before you got in the door.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I was excited to find a hidden little dive bar downtown but ended up leaving fairly disappointed. Our waitress was not the friendliest, and after my order came out wrong twice I finally gave up. I got the hot chicken sandwich and it was average at best. Definitely not true Nashville hot chicken, more so just greasy. My friend got a hamburger and it looked like a frozen patty. Not all it was cracked up to be.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: .We had no idea .What a great experience we had at the Friday night Opry.. It was amazing that it was so casual and the performers made you feel like you were just hanging out. The experience far exceeded out expectations!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Very casual. Live music and excellent burgers. Loud so not for intimate conversation. Very friendly service but it gripes me when food for the whole party comes out over an extended period.

name: Third Man Records
text: Worst customer service from Cam. I'd spend my money elsewhere as long as he works there.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: This was my absolute favorite spot on broadway. We had a good time at other bars but this place is the most fun I have had in a long time. We walked in at about 8pm and were the only ones in the bar. We were disappointed at first but sat down to have a beer. Once we started singing people POURED in and we were glad we claimed our spots because the place quickly became standing room only and also completely filled up! The rest of the night I spent singing, laughing, drinking and making memories. If you are looking for a good night and great time in Nashville please just dedicate one night to this place. You will not be sorry.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: The Pork Stew was AMAZING, but the portion was so small that I thought it to be a practical joke played on me by the waitress. It was still one of the best stews I've ever had though. A well balanced, spicy, and rich dish. The cheese topping was a wonderful addition, and because the pork was spicy the cheese did not bland the dish down. The stew was served with tortillas on the side, which was odd, as it's as far removed from a traditional carnitas based dish as possible. Increasing the stew portion, and adding bread as a side would make this a popular $20 dish. I would definitely recommend it to my friends and family, but please don't sit too close to me as I may have to steal some from your plate when mine is finished.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
AWFUL experience! My group of 6 sat down at 11:15. Our food arrived at 12:15-- cold as ice. We could not send it back because we had reservations at 12:30 for another activity in town. When I spoke with the manager, he was very rude. He gave us a 25% discount on our meal. Seriously? We waited 40 min on brunch items only to receive the food very cold & we got $3 knocked off. 

I will NEVER be back!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: The building is nice, it has a patio out front. They have a neat bar and some good beers. The service staff is nice.  Just going to drink here is a cool vibe. The food and menu are not good. Under cooked apps, for tacos they used pita bread cold out of the package. In the past we have given the food a try and have been disappointed. No more. May drink there in the future, but will not eat there again.

name: Music City Tippler
text: Great spot in the heart of the midtown action. We had a great dinner. Ambience is very cool and service was great. It picks up later with live music as they clear out the dinner tables, so go early enough to eat.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Enjoyed my visit here. It is in a dark alley, but once you walk in it is full of life. I had the black bean burger and fries and a few cocktails. I enjoyed it all and have found myself thinking about when the next time I can go back!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Had a great time! The live music was great and so was the food. Had the ribs with the cole slaw and sweet potato fries.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We did the Grand Ol Opry day tour.  It was 45 min tour showing back stage and the stage with the center from the original Ryman.  I felt for 30 dollars they could have had better content about the building and musicians.  However they started the tour with a introduction video of Blake Shelton giving the history and then split the group in two.  While we waited they had us seates in the benches and asked where we were from and told cheesy jokes.  This was a missed opportunity to give more history and content.  The tour felt rushed and did not give that much history or relatable information. The video with Blake gave the most information. For those who are deep country music buffs, as in know of the 1920 - 1950s music then this might be fun.  But they barely brought up current musicians or any stories about them at the opry.  All I know is what mail box Keith Urban is because the tour guide loved him.  I believe if they can introduce more stories of current musicians and fill in the wait times with more history rather than jokes I would have felt better about spending 30 bucks.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Good place to watch a game. Lots of TV's. Or, come for the 80's band, they're a lot of fun. The service is slow, at best. But, my husband had a great hot dog there!  About what you would expect at a sports bar.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I have visited This restaurant twice and it has been great both times. The only issue I recall is a mix up of our food. But other than that great place great atmosphere! Can't wait to visit again!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This was a good place for a quick bite at lunch hour. It had a fun staff and good environment.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Spent a week in Nashville, attended a Grand Ole Opry show, had a backstage tour, shook hands with Vince Gill, Eddie Montgomery and best of all Dustin Lynch was invited to join the Opry Family, as well it was Trace Adkins 15 year anniversary. An awesome show in all regards, I recommend for anyone who loves country music to take time to attend a show.
Ps. On the backstage tour I seen the backs of Tim McGraw and Trisha Yearwood walk out the back door away from where I was literally 15 feet from me... such a lost opportunity

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Amazing! I have never been to a bad show. By far the best sounding music venue I have ever been to! I highly recommend a backstage tour as well.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Ms. Kelli's kicked my friend out for wearing a shirt with no sleeves. Mind you, this friend of mine was male, cut, and showing off some 'suns out, guns out' and looking good while doing it. If a Nashville bar is trying to stop a man from showing his true colors (and jacked arms) then I don't want to be part of their clientele. I walked in with a tank top on and was easily let in. This kind of sexist behavior should not be tolerated in such a progressive city.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I love this place. We went to the Cirque Dreams Holidaze show. This is our second time going to this show. It was amazing once again. We will definitely check it out again next time we are in Nashville!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
I used this venue for a client launch party last night.  I can't say enough great things about the staff at this venue.  Kelly and Amanda were so incredibly friendly, helpful, and flexible.  The ENTIRE staff at our event was friendly and fun.  They showed my client and our guests an amazing time.  Southern hospitality at it's finest.  

The BB King All-Stars Band was AWESOME!  They really helped to make our event a fun experience.

Great venue, Great food, and best of all... GREAT STAFF!  I can't wait to host another event in Nashville at BB King's...  THE BEST!!

name: Music City Tippler
text:
The Tippler is a bit hidden in terms of where I normally jaunt for a drink after class or work but I've been here twice now and have been equally impressed each time. The inside is pretty large and there is a dining area separate from the bar. It's dim lighting and fairly average noise level, I recommend it for catching up with a friend or for a date situation. 

The first time I came here I was SUPER impressed by their cocktails but could only handle two because they were a wee bit strong. The next time I was debating between a cocktail and wine, and opted for wine. At first I thought I had made a huge mistake since their cocktails were so great previously, but when my wine came out it was fabulous as well, so disaster averted. This place definitely has their drinks on par.

I recommend the chicken biscuits AND the churros (omg) for dessert. Normally churros bring back memories of overpriced, lukewarm chewy breadsticks that I bought at the state fair from a man missing an unusual amount of teeth. These churros were so much better, and have replaced all nightmarish memories of churros from my past. They are clearly homemade and come out with a salted caramel dipping sauce that is sooo good. 

I also really appreciated that the manager on duty (Emily I believe was her name) came out to our table to check on us and see how everything was. She was very friendly and offered to give us a tour of the restaurant which I really appreciated! We were too full to take her up on her offer, maybe another time. Emily also let us know that they are coming out with a new seasonal food and drink menu sometime in February, just another reason to go back!

So get a few drinks, order the churros (obvi), and you are guaranteed a good experience at the Tippler.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Perfect for a beer enthusiast! The building itself is worth a stop. It's beautiful! Our server was great and very knowledgeable, which is awesome because there are SO many beers to choose from. We split the bratwurst plate and tried out a couple of new beers. The food was good and was just what we wanted to go with some beers. If we had more time in Nashville I'd love to have gone back in the evening and sampled a few more brews.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
(This goes out to the previous whiny reviewers) This is a beer bar! Come here if you like beer, good beer, flavorful beer, beer that is so good it doesn't need to be served at 33 degrees! Order some good beer! Then, order some snacks so you can drink more beer. We liked the pretzels and the tots. Do not come here looking for a good dining experience. It's a BEER BAR!

The fact that I have checked in here more times than any beer bar in my own home town shows you how much I adore this bar.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Best place to eat great bartenders and servers. Like one big family. Love this place.

name: Third Man Records
text:
Yes.

I love everything about this store, from the overall aesthetic to the small boutique feel of it to the great things that Jack White is doing to promote and re-issue important music. 

The color scheme of the store and of the 45s and 12" albums that are available in the store brings a great uniformity that makes everything feel so much more organized and sensible. I love that the only things available at the store are things that have been released on Third Man. If you are looking for releases by all your favorite bands, then this is not your store. 

I wish that more labels would do this, have a store front. Imagine if Kill Rock Stars or Merge, or Matador had their own store. I think that would be fantastic. 

That this is the only place one can buy certain singles and full lengths is great. Despite its size (incredibly small, one room) there are so many great surprises. I picked up a recording that Gibby Haynes did that I didn't know ever happened. 

This is so much more than a store: it's really representative of a mission. 

I can't say enough good things about this place. Get there.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This is a must if you're visiting Nashville. We bought tickets about a month before our visit for the backstage tour and the 7pm show.  I wasn't sure what to expect but it was fantastic! The backstage tour was pretty interesting and it was neat to go on stage. It lasted about an hour and then we went across the street to the mall to eat but I would've preferred to try the food trucks in front!  The drink prices are high! $12 for a single, $22 for a double, $9 for beer and $5 for water. We saw that Carrie Underwood was on the line up for this show so that was pretty exciting! I don't think the line up is finalized until the week of. Definitely worth the money and if I'm ever back in Nashville I will definitely do this again!

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text:
They just re did their menu and it's MUCH BETTER!

The bartenders, Shelby, Key and Maddy are super sweet and make great easy drinks. 

Service is quick and I'll be back :)

Also on Sunday's there's an 80s band called The Spazmatics; worth it!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Got the brisket. Incredible. Plus an amazing blues band to accompany my meal. Magnificent.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
This place was an awesome find in Nashville. It has a LOT of beer. Probably at least 2-3 dozen on tap as well as in bottles. And it's not cheap beers, but an extensive selection of craft beers, with international and seasonal options. If you like beer, this is the perfect place to try a variety. Sadly, I was not there on a Monday, but apparently all of their beers are $3 on Mondays! 

Not only were the beers good, but the decor was also very creative. Their spacious main bar area has saucers lined all over their walls and ceiling. They also have a nice lounge area with couches and plenty of natural light, as well as rooms with pool tables. I loved the interior design in both areas. This place is a bit of a way from the downtown attractions on Broadway, but it's totally worth the (relatively short) trip!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text:
Best part about this bar is that it is very clean inside and they have weekday live music starting at 11am. Our bar tender Calla was super nice and very friendly. She was busy yet had time to be personable. The music was good. A bunch of solo musicians happy to play together for music fans. People of all types and ages inside this morning. Started off with a couple of cold beers. No bottles, only cans and draft. Got a bit hungry and made a bad choice of getting a small bowl of chili. Didn't figure it was going to be poured from a can and put in the microwave. $10.00 for the can of Hormel. Not really a fan but then live and learn! I only sat in the downstairs area but they do have a second level. Not sure if there is live music upstairs later in the day and into the night. 
Metal bar stools are not so comfortable if you plan on hanging out for a while but then no one really stays long cat any one place on Broadway.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Found this place while strolling around from my hotel. Delicious burger! Great little bar.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
This can be no less than 5 Stars. This is the birth place of Country Music. So many legends have passed through the Grand Ole Opre House.

Well on in Nashville on this day and after finishing a project for work, I noticed a place to eat and by golly it's across the street from the entrance to the Grand Old Opera House. How can I not go in.

The parking lot is massive. The entire complex is like an amusement park. Hotel, water park, shopping, movie theater and of course the Grand Old Opera House. 

It's late afternoon and it's 96 degrees and I have to walk nearly a mile from my car to the building. A lot of posters of singers along the way and of course country music playing through loudspeakers. 

It was closed on the day I was there so I could only see the outside and the gift shop.

I admit I prefer rock music but don't frown on Country Music. Rap music and the like, nope, not for me.

Anyway just being there was a good experience. I would love to go for a show there one day. 

"The Grand Ole Ope" a piece of history. You must go there.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text:
WOW!!! What a FUN venue and fun staff!! Be sure to ask Stu at the bar to sing for you! If you're lucky (or tipping well!!) he'll serenade you and the whole bar!! JJ manning the Karaoke booth is ALSO a star!! Ask him to sing Walking in Memphis!! So talented. Also the blue fishbowl drinks are amazing and dont taste like alcohol at all, so be warned!!! Drink is slow and steady or else you'll be the FIRST one on the karaoke stage! And don't worry, you'll sound great....
JJ and Stu opened a WHOLE HOUR EARLY for me and a group of 10 who were coming from a holiday Christmas party- so accommodating!! They have basically every song too, so pick anything! We sang everything from Mama Mia! to Pat Benetar to Christmas Songs to I'm Proud to be An American! So stop on in and have yourself a drink and a sing! On the other side is Tequila Cowboys too! So you can bar hop without even leaving the building!

name: Third Man Records
text: Great gentrified and redone building rescue turned into ultra hipster bait shop with lots of exclusives and rarities.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This place was absolutely amazing! I loved learning the history of this place and why it's so important to country artists! The prices are alright but highly recommend if you are in Nashville!

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Came on Sunday! Great band and atmosphere!!! Only bummer, I had went shopping earlier that day and left my purchases in the restroom by accident. Unfortunately, not even an hour after I left and someone had already stole my stuff and trashed the shopping bag in the trash Not DawgHouse fault but it still sucked.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We were looking for a non-country place to enjoy some food and live music and this was one that came up our first night to check out. The po boy was OK, not amazing. The bbq was good according to my husband. The service was wicked slow despite being a Monday and not packed to the rafters.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
My husband, nephew, and I like country music, but it was our nephew's wife and 9 year old daughter who REALLY wanted to visit. It's not inexpensive, but our AAA discount brought the 4 adult tickets down $8. After spending a little more than an hour on the tour, we realized that what we paid was well worth it. 

We had to go through a metal detector and bag search. Then Lynzee, our tour guide, led us to a small auditorium for a 3D movie that required no 3D glasses. We recognized more of the performers than we thought we would, and knew more about the history of the Opry and its stars than we gave ourselves credit for. Now we were excited to see the auditorium itself and all of the dressing rooms. 

Lynzee took us backstage, showing us the path the stars travel, from the parking lot, past the Minnie Pearl statue, up to the metal detector & security guard. We walked to the "Post Office" where the stars receive fan mail - address your letters to the star of your choice, in care of the Grand Old Opry, Nashville, TN. They'll get your letter. We saw the names on plaques of all the musicians inducted into the Grand Old Opry. We sat in the family room/waiting area to learn more about the building and look at photos on the wall. One large mural had the water mark from the 4 foot flood. 

We walked past the dressing rooms, each with a guitar pick painted on the floor, with the number of the dressing room on each. Next was the stage, and we were able to stand in the circle behind the microphone, posing for a photo ($25 for 8x10, 3 5x6, and digital code to download the image), staring out at the auditorium that accommodates 4,400 customers. It is definitely a holy place, with cushioned benches resembling church pews. We had no time for the evening performance, but we hope to return to see the musicians play in this Grand Old Opry.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Enjoyed the free live music in the early afternoon before this area got super busy. Specials included 2 for 1 drafts and a few 1/2 priced appetizers. Server has a list of local drafts but no description of each of them. The food as decent, we enjoyed the pulled pork nachos and catfish po'boy.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We took the backstage tour with Randy and had the best time! Not a hard core country music fan, but found the tour to be fun, informative and interesting.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Never been before.  Tonight the 7 of us went to see the 700 show then the 930 backstage tour.  It was great.   Our tour guide was awesome and even better she was from bklyn/Staten Island like us.  She was a great tour guide and extremely nice.   My friends son got kelsi ballerini's autograph so that was even better.  Never did a tour like that before.  We were all glad we did

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
First time at "The Grand Ole Opry" it was pretty unusual. We were expecting it to be downtown by the Ryman Auditorium....Not the case...this located Right across from a Huge Mall and Super touristy. Do not let this deter you from the show! Once inside it is an AMAZING VENUE...very intimate and nostalgic..GREAT SHOW
HOWEVER EAT BEFORE YOU GET THERE.

DO NOT EAT HERE AND drinks are REALLY EXPENSIVE

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: First time in Nashville and this was our first stop. Steve, our bartender, was amazing!  Had a bunch of great stories, treated us like he had known us for years and most importantly the food and drinks were awesome!  I am a bbq snob and the ribs at B.B. Kings were some of the best ribs I've ever had!  We are here four more days and will be back for sure!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: This was my second visit to Nashville and this is my favorite by far! Noah Garner is an excellent entertainer! I highly recommend that you check this place out when he is there!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: As a beer lover, I was very Impressed with the amount of taps they had on the wall. The beer list was amazing. I went with a local vanilla stout that was dark and creamy. As for food I picked my own pie. I chose applewood smoked bacon, bratwurst and avocado. I was surprised at how good the pizza was for a pub type place. It was not greasy and the crust held up. It's a personal sized pizza so I almost finished the whole thing. If you're splitting with someone definitely order an appetizer as well. They gave thick slices of bratwurst and avocado which was nice and the bacon had good flavor. The only reason I'm taking 2 stars is because they don't have high chairs. I understand it's more of an adult establishment but since they do allow children I feel they should be available. There were plenty of kids when we were there. Other then that it's definitely a good place for beer lovers who want a good selection.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: This is such a fun place, but the bartenders were absolutely horrible. When I asked for drinks I needed to provide 4 IDs for all the people who were drinking, but it was only two drinks for two people. The people I was with ordered 3 drinks without question. I understand that it can be hectic and there are young people that show up but this was completely unreasonable.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: This evening was quite the eye-opener for what type of establishment Belcourt Taps is all about. I was there for an hour before I witnessed a truly horrific incident. I saw a man cornering a woman and yelling at her for calling him a "d**k." The owner, Rose, walked over and automatically said, "I don't care what you said I'm on his side." She allowed the incident to escalate and did not shut it down. As a man in this society, I would never corner a woman and start yelling at her. This is unacceptable and honestly hurts to witness. Afterwards, I was outside listening to the conversation of the owner and the woman being yelled at, and she stated "he [the man yelling at the woman] makes her millions and y'all [the woman's boyfriend and friends] make me nothing." If a business owner only cares about money and not her customers then I'm sorry, I will not be coming back and do not recommend Belcourt Taps to anyone.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great beer selection and solid bar food.  Consistently awesome service.  Never stupidly busy.  Go here to get away from the mania of Broadway and have a civil conversation with friends over delicious beers.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
Let me start by saying the interior design of this place was awesome. My first impression was an instant feeling of not being cool enough. 

We were seated quickly which was nice and greeted by our server. We couldn't hear a word she was saying it was so loud. We had to repeat our order a few times and she finally got it. The menu was rather small and they were out of a few things. The server told us some items were out of season, why put them on the menu if you opened last month? Guess what? The menu is paper, reprint it. Or have some specials to make up for it.

The food arrived after quite a while and it was kinda funny how small my plate was. Ordered scallops and there were 3 quarter sized scallops over half a handful of lima beans. It was tasty but as an entree, left me starving. Other people in our party were less than impressed with their bland panera like paninis. Two of the guys didn't even finish the sandwiches since they were so bad. These are clean your plate kinda guys we are talking about. All in all. It was overpriced and underwhelming. I never mind paying good money when going out. I do mind when we go out, order a full dinner and drinks and everyone is ready to go to another restaurant because they are still hungry. Step it up tippler, too many amazing restaurants in Nashville to mess around.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: I'm sure this place is better for drinks than food, but we went at lunch on a Saturday and were one of only two tables of patrons in there and service was still horrible. Took about 45 minutes for two burgers to come out and they were not good. The one bartender/server that was working was kind and apologized for the wait, but still, it was ridiculous and the food wasn't worth it. Only giving two stars because the guy was nice.

name: Third Man Records
text: The Disneyland for Jack White fans. I wouldn't call myself a Jack White expert, but I'm definitely a fan and have enjoyed listening to his music both during his White Stripes and solo career. Third Man Records has been on my list of places to visit while I'm living in Nashville so when I had a friend in town that wanted to go, I was pumped. Third Man Records is in Sobro so parking can be a bit tough. Luckily, we got dropped off for the day so it wasn't a problem. The outside is pretty cool. Sleek and modern. It makes for a nice touristy photo. If you don't already know, Third Man Records is a few things. First and foremost, it's Jack White's independent record label. The Nashville location (there is also one in Detroit) is the headquarters for the label and also a record store and music venue. I NEED to make it to a concert at The Blue Room. It's sounds awesome. The record store has a lot of interesting things. Yes, it has a lot of records but it also has books, clothing, old record players, instruments, and more. If you're a Jack White fan, stock up! There is plenty here and it's all at a reasonable price unlike other souvenir places. Another cool addition to the store is an old machine that lets you record your own record. It was broken when we were there but the worker explained it a bit. You can record a short song (I think about 2 minutes) for $20. Now that's a unique souvenir! If I was actually a singer I would totally be into this. Or it might even be fun just to do with a group of friends. You can say you recorded a song at Jack White's studio. They also do small tours if you want to learn more about the label and studio. We just wanted to check out the store and get something for a friend. While the store isn't huge, it's definitely a Nashville must!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: Their signature cocktail was really good. It had peach juice and whiskey. They are apparently known for their whiskey and their whiskey did not disappoint. I'm not a shot person but was able to take two ad their whiskey is really smooth. They do have like music, so it is loud.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: One of my favorite spots to go in Nashville! Friendly staff, good food, tons of TVs, and a great atmosphere! Best Sunday Funday spot in Nashville!

name: Third Man Records
text: Very psyched we got to stop in here on our weekend in Nashville.  Had to curb myself with all the schwag available.  Staff was also super cool and nice.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
Honky tonk in Nashville is a bucket list of mine.

I crossed that off during a 28 day road trip and a pit stop at Layla's. After walking up and down Broadway deciding which place to venture in to, we picked Layla's and it didn't disappoint. We got a chance to get out of the humidity, relax with a couple of cold hard ciders and listen to The Risches play for almost an hour.

My only complaint (and the reason for the 3 stars) was there wasnt wifi access for those of us coming from outside the US. We unfortunately are traveling with a very limited data plan so any chance for free connection is a double plus bonus score. Otherwise it was just the right amount fun at the right time during this epic trip.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: This was an awesome place to have a beer! There's a ton of seating inside and out, live music and fantastic beer. I would recommend grabbing a flight to figure out which beer is your fav. They offer several great beers, all of which are completely different. Check it out, just be prepared to wait on the train if you go down Fogg Street.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Skip the beer, this is about the food. I was part of a Nashville tour of local establishments, and this was our last stop. I was hungry and ordered two dishes and was not disappointed.

You can see and get close to the brewery and it is the cleanest I have ever seen. Service is adequately prompt, the staff is friendly and the decor is wonderful.

When we were there, the stage was occupied by a young lady solo artist who sang wonderfully. This is Music City, after all.

They have a great outside deck, but the view is not great. It will get better when the road construction is finished.

First, I ordered the frog legs. They must have come off a bullfrog. These were the best frog legs I have ever eaten. They were tender. moist and meaty. A light texture crust covered the meat, but it was nice and crunchy. The sauce as akin to Nashville hot chicken, but not firey.

Fish tacos were next. The presentation was nice, but I was taken aback by the fact that the fish was basically a fish stick. Put aside your early childhood memories of this kiddie staple. The stick was a nice size, was moist and tender and the coating was wonderful. Chef was a genius in creating this dish because the shape of the fish stick was perfect for wrapping in a tortilla. Topped with a nice slaw and sweet sauce, this dish was a "keeper".

Go there.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The food was the only thing keeping me from giving one star. The service was nearly non-existent. Our waitress was not around after we placed our food order. Other tables came in after we had ordered and got their food long before us. When the food did arrive, only half the table was served, then two more dishes came out 10 minutes later and we waited for the last dish another 10 minutes. When someone asked for ketchup, she rolled her eyes and argued with another about the lack of dressing on her salad.  She should be working for the DMV, she'd fit right in.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Food and drinks were good.
However, the waitress took absolutely forever with our order, we never recieved silverware and had to take it off neighboring tables. Alsp got charged double for every drink we recieved even without asking for a souvenir cup.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Just left this place. Was hanging out trying a beer sampler and having a sandwich. A couple of young guys and the bartender which clearly was their friend decided it would be funny to make fun of me for smelling and tasting my beers. That's funny because to me I actually like the smell and taste of beers and really enjoy them. The food was good but that bartender was terrible she really needs to figure out where she works and what she is serving. I'm sure my LA hat did not help me out either but I would expect some better hospitality from  a brewery.  6:38pm 11/12/17

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Great tap room great beers and really great food.  Not at all your typical bar food - much better.  Love the hot chicken.

name: Ole Red
text: Extremely understaffed!!   So many tables were open on main level, but wait was over 45 minutes.  We got seated upstairs, great view of the band, but we only saw our server ONCE!  It took us going to the bar to get her to come the first time, we got our own silverware, then continued to go to the bar to get our drinks.

name: National Underground
text: Extremely slow service, poorly prepared food and over priced. This is what happens when someone wants to play music for a living opens up a restaurant.

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
Schermerhorn Symphony Center is absolutely beautiful.  The acoustics are top notch.  The Nashville Symphony has classical and pop series. Other artists go there as well. The building itself is a true symphony hall and it is wonderful and very classy.  You can check their website to see the schedule:


http://www.nashvillesymphony.org/tickets/calendar

name: National Underground
text: New management, new bartenders and servers, and a new grasp on what this bar/restaurant can do for Nashville. Everything seems to be ran much better than before and we had an excellent time at their Bluegrass Sunday Brunch. I recommend trying this place out again if you had a bad experience before.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Really cool place!  We loved the beer, atmosphere and the nachos.

name: National Underground
text: Awful, slow service. Messed up our order multiple times. Up charged without being told. Over priced for what you get. DO NOT go unless all you want to do is sit at the bar and drink.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Very casual spot for lunch. Really good bar food though. WARNING: the buffalo chicken tenders and hot hot hot! Delicious though. Keep a beer nearby.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Good venue,  Great food,  handicap assemble,  Great music.  I had the chicken quesadilla,  it came with guacamole,  Pico,  and a line flavored sour cream. Delish

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Sucks balls, let waaaaaaay too many people in for their whiskey jam...think country hipster convention...I went home and killed myself after

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: We sat allllll the way up top for the Stanley cup game 2 playoffs!!!!  .. almost at the ceiling ... but still felt like a "5th team member!" The fans are bananas! Those chants were hilarious and surprisingly chanted by EVERYONE in SYNCH!!!!!! This  was an amazing experience ...national anthem .. amazingly performed by non other than ... freaking  brad paisley!!!!

name: Ole Red
text: We were excited to visit here on our first night in Nashville. Very disappointed in the music talent on the night we attended. Was my least favorite of the weekend.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: From the jambalaya, to the live music, the bar, and the souvenir shop with all the Parrot/5 o'clock themes - this place rocks! It feels like such a relaxed place with a great vibe to it! I missed it in Las Vegas, but was glad to make it here in Nashville! The prices are a little bit high, but the waitresses were fantastic, and the value you get for the money is amazing!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I love this place. Its an awesome looking arena from the inside and out. What a great place to catch an NHL game. Nashville has the friendliest NHL fans in the league. I love coming to games here. I have friends near by in Brentwood so I catch a few games a year here. I met Amy Grant, Vince Gill and Carrie Underwood here, I got expensive tickets. One my fav venues in all of sports and its literally right off Broadway so you can hit up the honkey tonks before or after the game. Nashville traffic can get bad from time to time thou, you are warned. Other than that I would recommend this place to any NHL fan or anybody that wants to a rip roaring good time and Nashville natives are super friendly, people will actually talk to unlike cities like NYC or Chicago.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I was craving something other than beer and bbq. Jimmy delivered with a decent margarita and the best ever coconut shrimp / orange marmalade. Only reason for not getting a 4 is the boring "island" loop they play on every tv. It was fine the first 10 times .... but come on. At least have some in the bar and some on the floor with a game on.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Stopped in for dinner.  Very busy and lively.  25 minute wait for table.  It's a Saturday night so busy was expected.  Spent a little time in the gift shop and saw a couple things we wanted for the game room/bar.  Decided to have a couple drinks while we waited for the table and get trinkets later.  Bartender was exceptional.  Ordered two frozen margaritas- they were out of limes.  He told me that he'd get some limes to us.  10 minutes later, here he comes with a cup and freshly cut lime - way more than we needed -  went back to him and added some to his tip.  He was really good.
Got out table and waited almost 30 minutes for our appetizer - which also arrived with everything else.  I had ordered a steak, which was so bad it wasn't worth eating.  Well over cooked.  Waiter didn't come back to check on things until we were almost finished - everything else was OK.  
Waiter said manager took my meal off and never offered to make another one.  Now I'm a little pissed.  Paid our bill and on the way out, I addressed the manager about his lack of presence to find out he never knew about the issue in the first place.
Needless to say, I decided not to buy the cool stuff for the bar because why would I want a reminder of such a lousy experience?
It's Nashville, it's Broadway, I guess the standard shouldn't be really high, but for a chain establishment - it should have been better.
On a food note, I don't have to rearrange the walls in the game room to accommodate new parrot head stuff!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Quiet possibly the friendliest and most spacious restaurant on the Broadway strip. The waitstaff (a lot of waitstaff) are there to make sure your every need is met to an extent. I also enjoyed the fact that even though they have two stages (one in front for small acoustic sets and one in back for full bands), they use one at a time as not to overwhelm costumers with music. The steak quesadilla's are to die for and even if you feel like you've been forgotten, one of the many waitstaff is sure to ask "How was your meal?"

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: A little dive-y. Has karaoke, which is why we were there. It's not crowded at all - even on a Friday night. We were there with a group of ten people, and there wasn't a wait to sing! Typical beer selections. Not bad, but it's basically a place to go for karaoke!

name: Ole Red
text: Loved this place! The food and service were both top notch. The tater tots were the best ever

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
Layla's is probably my favorite bar on Broadway. It's non-pretentious, and doesn't get *too* full, though it can get a good amount of people on the dance floor.

They don't do draft beers, only bottles. They have a decent selection though, which is nice.

There are tables along the walls, and some bar seating.

I saw the Eskimo Brothers here, and they were one of the best live acts I saw that week in Nashville.

I was only here for a few days and went to Layla's twice for drinks and live music. Couldn't help but come back a third time to pick up a t-shirt. It was the last one in my size, so the bartender just plucked it off the wall. It had a staple hole in it, cost $20, and smelled like beer, but it's probably the most authentic souvenir I brought back with me.

name: National Underground
text: Saw some old reviews on here that weren't so great but heard it was redone and much better so I decided to try it. THIS PLACE IS GREAT. It's right on broadway and has a great unique vibe. I had a burger and it was delicious. Can't recommend this place enough. Great beer selection too!

name: Ole Red
text: The music was good but the food was NOT good and there were fruit fly/gnat things flying all near our food. So gross! Our waitress was very unfriendly. We hardly ever write bad reviews but it was just such an unpleasant experience. We won't come back here

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: I wish they would have posted on their website that they were closed for renovations.   Very disappointing. Made a special stop to watch the Richie sisters on the way home to Wi.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: Great place to see a concert in Nashville. I have seen Gwar and the Dropkick Murphy's at this venue and the sound was great. Highly recommend this venue

name: National Underground
text: No Southern Hospitality here! After one employee invited us in from the cold for drinks, a friend and I were immediately confronted by another employee asking if we were going to buy food or drinks.  I told him that we are waiting for the remainder of our friends to get their ID's checked and then we will decide what we wanted to order.  Immediately the bouncer told us to leave because we were not paying customers.  Rediculous.  Poor customer service. Rude employees.  Definitely will not return.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Ken and Chris in the merchandise store were SO nice!! Ken was super helpful and friendly and Chris was so sweet and generous I walked out with a pineapple pin! Made my night!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Great vibe- locals and some sporadic tourists. 

It's a great place to hide from the downtown scene. Would recommend to any beer aficionados.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Would you like salt with your steak / salad?
Ordered the $26 steak it had so much salt I could not eat it. Manager took it off the bill. She got me a salad which had as much salt on it too. 2-Stars. Nov 2016

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I like this arena and all but almost three weeks later I'm still pretty annoyed about my last experience there.

Wanting to watch the Canadiens warm up, I asked an usher if it was cool if I could go down to the ice. She said no I had to wait until 5:30 (6pm puck drop) and yet all these people were taking good spots. So I asked the usher one section over about this and he told me to head on down. Still not sure wtf that was about. I've never been restricted anywhere and she was clearly the only one following such a rule. Had I waited until such a time I would have had no place to stand and warmups would have been well in action. And since I managed to get myself a puck that would have REALLY sucked if I hadn't been able to go down there.

Still like the arena overall, it's one of the only places I've been where sitting in the upper bowl does not translate to jam as many people in small seats as possible width wise. But I think they have raised their concession prices a bit too high. Not that it stopped the legion of douchebros in front of me from reeking of shit beer, so I guess maybe robbing fools is better than appealing to the masses...I mean I can't argue...if you wanna overpay for light beer instead of go to a bar literally across the street who am I to judge.

Lastly can I just say please don't put those ads with Mike Fisher eye level for doing your business in a bathroom stall. Totally can never look at the guy ever again. Or listen to Carrie Underwood.

Props though for letting people hang around during the crazy tornado warning thing.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: My hostess Cori was such a delight! She welcomed us with such a big smile and even shared things to do in the local area. She was such a great start to a wonderful evening of food and fun!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
First, we have been to Margaritavilles all over the country. so, our expectations were set by our previous experiences. The restaurant full but not overcrowded. We found a tble near the band and dance floor. After about 10 minutes our table was bused from the previous customers. Ordered food and drinks. My $9 Landshark arrived about 10-15 minutes later. We ordered our go to, Volcano Nachos with grilled chicken added. The nachos arrived and we noticed there was no Guacamole on them. After several minutes we were informed that the kitchen was out of Guacamole. As we dug in, we discovered that 3/4 of the chips were topping free. Under the crown of melted cheese there as a scoop of chili covering about 3 inches. next to that a scoop of cheese goo covering about the same area. The grilled chicken that we normally get turned out to be small cubes of pressed chicken mystery meat. (smaller than a crouton). My wife finally said she didn't want to wast the calories eating this.
The music was really good. the 3 piece band was engaging and tried to get the crown involved. The night before we were in the bar and the duo playing were also very good. 
The entertainment is why I gave them 2 stars.
First bad meal I have ever had at a Margaritaville.

name: 12th & Porter
text: Great place in general and specifically. Came for a concert, saturated for the beer.  Great environment, haven't tried the food but it smelled good.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Smaller venue then most Margaritavilles. Friendly staff and good music that took requests. Good drinks (of course). No food taken in, sorry.

name: Ole Red
text: What a great experience, both times the bands made you want to dance and sing along! Lots of fans going, so you don't sweat. A fun experience, just what you think of when thinking of a fun bar in Nashville!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Stopped in for a couple of Bahama Mamas during Memorial Day weekend. Interior design was very tropical and authentic. The bar area had large bay windows that were opened to the street. The restaurant location is a corner spot right in the heart of all the action on Broadway Avenue. I didn't eat anything but had a great time, loved the drinks, decor, and location. Definitely stop by and get your favorite beach drink and sit in the bar area/cocktail tables.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
For this location in the prime spot off Broadway, the service was great. Walked in was seated right away listen to
The live band and ordered our food- fish n chips and pretzels.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Great venue. Love music and chill vibe. The grilled  cheese and fries were great. Also loved the hot chicken sandwich (giant, could definitely be shared). Lots of good beer selections including some unique ones like beet beer.  Looks like the outdoor section is super cool but it was too cold this weekend to sit out there!  Definitely check it out.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
Full disclosure: Booze and band only.

The doorman said the band could play anything. The band could not play "anything", only the favorites. The bartenders were nice and the price is right considering the location and amount to drink. Big plus, they have Yuengling!

It wasn't crowded and the acustics were pretty good. If you just want drinks and music, this is the place to go.

name: Ole Red
text:
A 20 minute wait, yet 15 tables open...this place won't last long!

It took a while to flag down a waiter, at least the drinks were good.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Out of the local breweries this one has the best menu and options for snacks and non-drinkers alike. I really appreciate that. I do love a good brew, but I like having something special for my non-drinking friends as well and their kombucha is really good! They also have reasonably priced snacks. 

I adore the seating situation. Tons of outdoor space in the shade, sun and in between, and also a cool fenced off area inside the brewery. On perfect weather days it can get a little crowded but the set up feels pretty fluid and the lines move quickly.
