As a local brewery they have a few 'regulars' on the menu - if you are a stout person try the Sweet Potato Stout, it is amazing! But honestly through sampler trays and sampling from my friends 'trays' (aka glasses) I've never had anything I made stink face too. Thats pretty rare.

Parking is actually fairly decent across the street, a little bumpy and tore up, but easier access to park then the other local breweries in the area.m In fact, if you don't mind a walk, just mosey on down the street/across the tracks to try the others! Ask a local, they will know! ;)

name: Ole Red
text:
Prime location on Broadway, alongside all the bars/nightlife/must see tourist stop! We actually ended up in this bar because 1)they allowed my kids in who happen to be way under 21 and 2)offer vegan options on their menu!
The place is quite spacious and set up to allow everyone a great view of the band playing that night.  Bathrooms are impressive, as well, albeit up one flight of stairs.
Drinks were on point and the food was good enough. I was a bit disappointed that my impossible burger substitution for the bbq pulled pork did not have sauce on it or shredded. Wouldn't have considered it a substitution so much as just a burger...

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The waitress Liz is phenomenal. Very pleased with the food. Service. And drinks. If downtown, and need a cold beer and some grub. Go see Liz.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Takes over 20 minutes to get a drink from any of the bar tenders, also not a set last call time and as soon as they called for last call they would no longer serve anyone in my party that was there. The only reason they are even getting a star for me is the band. The bar tenders are extremely rude, service is disgustingly slow and they don't have the words customer service in their vocabulary. Will not be going back and I'm extremely disappointed that my large party was treated that poorly, I will make sure that any other large groups do not visit this business, they can spend their money at a better bar with actual customer service.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: This place feels like my home away from home.  I've worked in here since 2002.  It's not too big and not too small. It's located right in the heart of downtown.  If you're lucky enough to have a hotel room in downtown Nashville, you can walk to the arena without a problem and then spill out into broadway and 2nd ave. after your event.  I believe the building is aging gracefully as they continue to add new features.  On the south end, there's the new "Tavern 96" which faces the Country Music Hall of Fame and new convention center.  When inside the arena, be sure and check out the "Krazy Kyle" sign in the 1st level at the north end.  That is my spot!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: This is a really nice spot to hang, plenty of table games and tvs to watch sports. I really enjoyed the summer wit beer!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I am at The Highway Happy hour which is great but bartender and wait staff are rude. Highway needs a venue that is better for their fans. Margaritaville just doesn't get how to treat people and increase sales. Why wait in line for 3 hours in the sun without being able to buy a beer. Siriusly

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The hubby and I are trying to hit all the Margaritaville's across the world!  This one was quite big since they have a large second level.  The food was good but bummed they no longer do their drink sampler.  That was amazing!! I only gave it three starts because he went there two nights in a row and the second night we sat in the bar so we could listen to the live music.  The bar was very crowded and I didn't think a lot of was done to manage the craziness!! I was sitting at the bar eating and had people leaning over me all the time.  I did end up claiming to the manager and then left pretty quickly thereafter.  I do love Jimmy, so the food, drinks and music did not disappoint.  I think this is our 15th one we have visited.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: Sucked. Waited for an hour with nothing going on.  No seats, no tables, etc. Don't do it!!!!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I was enjoying myself. The concert was grooving and my hips were moving. But then it happened. Some arrogant jack hole spilled his beer on me. Also, the seating sucks. If you can't get floor seats, don't go. It's that simple. Also, the sound quality is poor.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We were very excited to come for a friend's show but between low quality food that is barely above McDonald's quality, overly expensive watered down drinks, flies everywhere and some idiot stilt walker wandering around and blocking the stage... We will not be back. Out of all those the stilt walker is the one thing I could really not forgive. Really inappropriate to have a side show when people are singing their hearts out on stage.

name: Ole Red
text: We ordered the 1/2 bucket of chicken with mashed potatoes and biscuit. The wings as an appetizer are tangy and bring a little heat. The pulled pork and tatie tots are a delightful meal. Love the music and enjoyed touring the top deck ! Great scenery.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: As a sports nut, I had to go here and get some pics. Located downtown, so parking is a hassle just to snap some pics. Still, it is definitely worth the trip!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Buffett, I love you.  I've been to Margaritavilles all over.  This is unfortunately, the worst.  I know I'm in Nashville but I don't go to Margaritaville to hear country music.  I go to Margaritaville to hear Buffett or at the very least, trop rock.  Not in this location.  Here not only do you get live country that blares out, but it overrides the videos of Buffett.  If I wanted country I could go to the dozens of places all over downtown.  I don't want country.  I want either Buffett or trop rock. I've given up on ever being able to hear that in the Nashville Margaritaville.

name: The Night Owl
text:
Friendly, fast service and clean local bar. Delicious traditional wings and chilli cheese fries! If you are craving those... this place will not disappoint!

There's a huge bar when you walk in and to the left is additional seating and the band stage. They have their own parking lot and we always find a spot. We've enjoyed the local musicians here also 

There's also a ping-pong table and pool table in the back. Several TVs also for those looking for a hangout to watch a game. lt's non-smoking now which when Spankys, the smoking was deterring!

Now this is our go-to local bar!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
I visited this location having never been to a Margaritaville.  Was looking forward to having some island inspired (in an American way) food.  

A friend and I met up with our group (8 total) for dinner, we were a little late due to the parking mess in that area.  They had been seated pretty quickly after arriving on a Sunday evening.  Only drinks had been ordered.  We added our drink orders to our waiter.  Other group members reported that the waiter had said they were out of a many items.  Overall, I can't remember how many things they were out of, but it was quite a lot.  

Our group orders - one young lady isn't able to get seafood mac and cheese without seafood, seems....fishy.  Another young man gets wings with two sides.  A few minutes later, waiter returns to say they're out of wings (the young man had attempted to order several other things that were also out that night).  Later, he returns to say they did have wings.  Manager follows up to tell him they did have the wings.

I settled for the BBQ chicken sandwich with fries. Everyone's food comes out and manager (there may have been two, or one in training) says "enjoy!"  My friend and I that had been late did not receive our meals.  Manger asks what we had and clearly has to place the order again.  Our party had pretty much finished eating by the time we got our plates.  We were going to ask for them to go at this point, but I was ravenous enough when the plate was placed in front of me that I devoured it in about 5 minutes.

Chicken was moist and bbq sauce had nice flavor.  Cheese was not worth the calories, but I ate it anyway, along with the bacon.  Fries were satisfactory.  I took the bun completely off the sandwich bc it was enormous.  No report from anyone else's food.

Manager did comp the late meals along with the wings of the young man.  Apologized we were not able to eat with our friends.

Did not take part in the libations, can't give a review of that.

Wish I would have tried the nachos - saw a couple of plates of them walk by and they were heaping!  They do add chili instead of just beef which always makes me a little weary and is probably why I didn't order them.  If you have friends that want to come, go ahead....but I'd rather find something local.  However, I have to commend the manager for comping 3 out of 8 of our meals.  Cannot complain of a free meal on my graduate student budget right now!

name: National Underground
text:
So here for lunch on a Monday. Place is just ok. 

Partner got the hot chicken said it was super good. The potato salad is good. Taste like it has ranch dressing In it. Chicken definitely the best value 

I got the catfish. Came with the good potato salad as well. The fish was good only complaint would be for $11 I kinda expected a bit more than one small piece

name: Ole Red
text:
A first Nashvillle trip.  Desired to look up Blake Sheltons new place there.  Weather hasn't been TN weather..  30's... 
seated by stage, performers were on break, hostess kind, atmosphere multi ages, 
High top and regular tables, 
Ordered crazy named quesadillas and pulled pork sandwich.  All was fresh and tasty.

Service A+
Prices A+

If ever return (warmer time) would re-do visit!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: The beer is great. Don't order the charcuterie meat plate. I'd love to tell you what's on it, but the waitress never told us. There was something that resembled corn beef hash with peppers, some ground up meat, and some type of soft sausage. Yes, soft sausage...just what we all want to put in our mouth. I can't speak to the rest of the food, but it looked good.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
Cool joint but watch out on Friday night's.
First visit was great but on Fridays the bouncers become very arrogant. I stepped out for a smoke and bought a Gatorade from a hot dog stand which offended the staff outside, so they allowed me no reentry, after I paid for my full beer on the bar and my meal which I didn't get to eat. I asked to speak to a manager and was instead threatened. I could see if i was being a drunken loudmouth, but being sober and only having a sip of my beer, with being treated like that is completely unprofessional. Way better venues in town.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Stopped by in Aug 2011 for a drink at the new Margaritaville in Nashville. I have been to a lot of the Margaritaville places around the world, This one was not as fun as some of the others. Vegas, Turks and Caicos, and a couple more. It is nice place for a drink and talking with friends

name: Ole Red
text:
We stopped in early evening Saturday . We went to the 5th floor and decided to grab some food before our night was to start . We were set at a nice table and had to wait for quite a while do someone to come and check on us . We orders simple drinks and waited for 20 minutes to get our drinks . We said ok it must be an anomaly and it will get better .Very limited menus and the first item we ordered Peel and eat shrimp they were out of ... ok well we decided on a few other items . Pork Belly and grits , some picketed shrimp
And the slider trio . That order took almost 30 minutes to show up . So when received the portions were. Wet small and 3 people had a snack and 2 drinks for $120 ... what in the hell ... I live in Nashville and take guests to Broadway a lot and won't be seeing Blake's place anymore .

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
I've been to Margaritaville many times while I've lived here in Nashville and it comes with both pluses and minuses.

Positives:
- The vibe.  Beachy, fun vibe with great decorations and a fun gift shop for tourists.
- The music.  There are some great, live bands that pass through here and it's always great to listen to local music while you eat/drink.
- Nice people.  The bartenders and waiters/waitresses have always been very friendly!
- Great for under-21s and under-18s.  It's a great place to bring kids and teenagers if they want to experience Broadway/Nashville music after 6:00PM.

Negatives:
- No-so-great, high-calorie food.  The food isn't awesome.  Their burgers are dry, overcooked, and flavorless.  Their fish and chips are dry and taste like old fryer oil.  I've never been impressed with any of the food there and it's impossible to find anything close to healthy.
- Expensive.  Not only is the food not very good, it's also expensive.  Definitely not close to worth the cost.
-Syrupy drinks.  While there are some unique drinks that are pretty good (try the loaded Landshark - a Landshark with a shot of tequila and lime), many of their beachy drinks come from a mix and are syrupy/too sweet for my taste.  Also, my last cranberry vodka had salt in it (??)

Summary?  Great place to get a drink or two and listen to music.  I wouldn't go for the food, though!

name: Ole Red
text: The food here was incredible and HUGE portions! The entertainment so fun!!!! Definitely a MUST SEE!!!!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We were thrilled to find a Margharitaville in Nashville, mostly because we know they have a good gluten free menu! This place was great when we were starving today as it was an easy walk from Music Row. We were served by the very knowledgable and helpful Samantha who answered all our questions about the menu and took great care of us. Thanks Samantha! Gluten-free cheeseburgers are excellent, we haven't tried the Volcano Nachos yet as it looks like a little too much food for us. Fun place with lovely staff and good food!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
This brewery is located in the Gulch. It has a good reputation and is served in many local restaurants and bars. The taproom serves delicious food, and live music, complete with rooftop patio. 
For more brewery info visit: travelptswithacraftbeerproblem.wordpress.com

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: My husband and I had a great time! Our server, Ethan, was the best!  He suggested the grilled Mahi-mahi for my fish tacos and boy did he know what he was talking about!  It was wonderful!  The live entertainment was great, even if it wasn't Buffett music.  It is Nashville!  It was a great place to go and sit down and not be so crowded you couldn't enjoy yourself.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: I've been to TN Brew Works twice now, and am looking forward to future beer drinking and overeating.  I had the house burger, and damn I was surprised how good it was!  One of the best burgers I've had anywhere.  They had live music playing inside, and a spacious outdoor patio with 2 levels.  The surrounding views are, shall we say, raw industrial with a bit of stalled construction work.  Aside from the unique location, TN Brew Works is legit.  The beer is great, food is great, and service was excellent.  My suggestions (besides the burger of course) are the Basil Ryeman and Southern Wit.  Please enjoy.

name: Ole Red
text: Skip the lobster roll.  It is literally just plain lobster sitting on a bun. The brussel sprouts, kale salad, and salmon poke salad were all very good. The ambiance was nice, and we did enjoy the live music. Overall, a nice place to eat.

name: National Underground
text: Strolled in this place on a warmer than usual winter Sunday and ordered some of their chicken nachos.  I was very pleased with them.  There were way more than I could eat and lots of gooey cheese.  I wanted just straight queso, but they didn't carry it so this was the next best choice for me.  My friend ordered chicken and waffles and gave me a few bites.  That chicken was to die for.  Very tender and moist.  I was impressed since I don't normally appreciate white meat pieces.  There were two folks on the stage playing some bluegrassy-country music and they were a joy to watch and listen to.  The wait wasn't too long for the food, but couldn't even get in the place the night before.

name: Nashville Symphony
text: We loved our recent visit to the Nashville Symphony to see Harry Potter with live music accompaniment. The seeds, the orchestra, the humor of the conductor, and even the snack bar was all exemplary. Great way to introduce kids to the joys of a live orchestra.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: I came to Nashville for fun girls weekend before my best friend moves away. Came to this bar to enjoy live music on the rooftop at about 4 pm on a Friday....bouncer SNAPPED my REAL Arkansas drivers license in half because he thought it was fake. Ruined the rest of my weekend. Can't go out with a snapped ID.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
#excellent

     I'm glad to have finally made it out here to this brand spankin new brewery.  This place is located just on the border downtown Nashville and sits in the midst of aged warehouses.  As I was following my GPS, I began to wonder if I was being taken to the wrong location. I drove through questionable alleys of what seemed like a ghost town. 

I finally arrived and found the facade of this new brewery to have quite the design. The design is very industrial contemporary with a slight rustic feel.  The designs are very eye appealing. A lot of natural wood is used for the table & walls which give this place warm feel.The peeps here have converted a very large rectangular warehouse into what is now Tennessee Brew Works. About 15% of the space is used for patrons to come and enjoy some brews @ a fair $5 a pop. The rest of the place is where all of the magic happens. There seems to be a lot more space here that's unused but is likely awaiting further expansion or storage.  

I visited during the 2nd weekend after the opening and was pretty impressed.  It's very simple, the staff is very friendly and attentive. The owner Garr made his rounds and came to speak with my buddy and I for about 15 minutes providing us insight the brewery's inspirations and processes of developing recipes.  I was thoroughly impressed and felt extremely welcomed by all of the people, here. 

There is a filling area for growlers which hold about 5 beers or 62ish ounces. You also have 2 bar areas, one upstairs & one downstairs where can purchase your brew & start your tab.  On the front portion of the inside of the building, you can see the exposed second floor & of course you can look down to people watch. There are long tables upstairs and a separate area close to the brewing stations where you have barrels that are used as standing drink tables. Also on the second floor, you can walk outside on a catwalk where there are even more drinking areas. Pretty cool stuff. Oh, and the front patio is pretty darn sweet. 

I tried two of the beers, I tried their IPA which was pretty darn good, the IPA had a surprisingly darker than normal IPA color. I also enjoyed the very flavorful Extra Easy Ale which had a nice bitter taste. I loved both beers and can't wait to go back and try the others.  

Food? They only have flavored prepackaged popcorn to offer though I am sure food trucks will make their rounds here at some point.  Might I suggest pork rinds from a local joint?  Mmmmmm, yes, you should sell them here, TBW. 

I loved the site and the staff here @ TBW.   The craft beer is fantastic and the location is convenient to Peg leg which is around the corner for some good ole BBQ.  

I certainly recommend this joint if you're meeting your buddies and enjoy great craft beer.  Certainly a spot to hit up if you're getting off work or making this place one of your stops during a night out on the town hopping bars.  Open till 8PM Thursday - Saturday. Tours to come, soon.  

Can't wait to get back!

name: Ole Red
text: Went to Ole Red tonight. Great music and good food. Had a great time and the band playing was fantastic.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
As with all of jimmy buffets places you will not be disappointed! Came here for the music row happy hour featuring buzz from the highway and had a blast. 
Show starts at 3pm, doors to the second floor open at 2pm but if you want a seat upstairs you need to line up between 1130-1200 outside. When we got to the second floor we ordered some food and drinks and waited for the show to start. They had a few bucket specials so thats what we did. Food wise we got the nachos to split which were very good. Not to expensive and id say each app of nachos is good for 4 ppl to split. 
Show wise id 100% recommend it. We got on the radio and buzz and his staff were great. The wait staff and bartenders at margaritaville were also very good.

name: Ole Red
text: After standing in line for quite a while, we were Very disappointed in management and "corporate policy." We were in town for a concert and celebrating my friend's 35th Birthday. Her license expired at midnight, but she had a printed state of Tennessee temporary license along with her just expired license to show she is 35. If you are going to have a business in Tennessee, you need to know the Driver's License procedure and be prepared for this type situation.  It has all of the markings, etc on it to make it official.  EVERY other place we went to let us use it with her  expired license in hand. We were so looking forward to going here.  We were such @blakeshelton fans.  I have always said if there was one star I would like to sit down and have a beer with it is him.  I feel like if he knew, he would have been disappointed too.  They need to look at state of TN licensing and make a change to their corporate policies that Amy, Andrea and Chris were not so nicely pointing out. I did not get ugly, I just explained the same thing I am writing here.  The bar is in Nashville...just send the corporate employees down the road to learn the state system.  They even brought Chris the bodyguard down who was very rude, when again I was just explaining the TN process.  There is another location opening close us in Gatlinburg.  Hopefully the policies will change by the so others won't be as disappointed as we were.  By the way you lost about $200 in sales last night and we are in Nashville a lot. I know this makes no difference to corporate or the managers, especially the one there last night. #disappointed #blakeshelton #olered #nashville

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Nice open space with seating on two floors, live music near the bar, great service and really good food. The portions are HUGE! I love how creatively they use lime in the coleslaw and sour cream. Great burgers. Sweet potato fries and a nice gift shop to boot! It's five o'clock all the time at Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Best service yet thanks to Bowie.. In town for the Preds game got us in and out.. again big props to Bowie..

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
I want to start off by saying if I could give this place 0 stars - I would. The wait to get inside wasn't too bad maybe about 5-10 minutes the problem is the AWFUL SERVICE once you get in! I went with a party of 6 and we waited at LEAST 30 minutes standing RIGHT NEXT TO THE BAR WITH CARDS/CASH in hand!! The bartender named Eric was 100% just downright rude!!!  He was so rude to all of us, that we actually just left and spent lots of money at other bars right next door/ down the street. I will personally tell everyone I know to never go to this bar and I hope that Eric finds a new job that is not in customer service very soon.

An update to this: I reached out to the management team (as they asked me to in their response below) over a week ago to discuss this and nobody responded back to me- can't say I'm surprised. Avoid this place at all costs.

name: Ole Red
text: Good food and outstanding music to go along with it.  Whiskeys may have been watered down slightly only thing that may have been better.  Overall, good food, good time

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I have visited 5 breweries in Nashville this weekend. Tennessee Brew Works is by far the best. The beers were really good, but what sets it apart is the staff. The people working here are naturally friendly like friends giving advice and being helpful. Whereas some of the other breweries felt like I was part of a business transaction. 

The stage up front had great music and the 2 story taproom with dart boards and seating inside the brew room was great. The outside 2-level seating looked great but it was a little too hot/humid for us to be out there. 

Go here over the other brewery spots. You will not regret it.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Alright for concerts, a lot of the big stars like Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars will perform here due to the venue's size as accessibility. Hockey games here are fun, and I've seen the Preds play and WIN quite a few times which was a treat. Snacks and drinks are a tad costly - I believe my can of watery pee beer was $9 and I remember my stale popcorn or nachos always being on the pricey side as well. Your bags will be searched upon entry (I didn't mind - but just be expectant of that). The crowd control to get in and out of the arena is not very good because of this, so expect a good wait and cramped lines. We've tried different means of entry each time and haven't found any to be better than the next.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Really good.hardly had to wait for a table.and the food was great. Try the chimichurri steak.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Since this venue opened I have lost count of events I have gone to see here. May not be the biggest place, but it is indoors and the best artist come here to play. We usually have a family member drive and drop us off nearby or we get everyone in a spot and get a van with a driver to drop and return for us later when we are ready to leave Nashville. No complaint about the beer prices. I figured out years ago to wait to party after concerts instead of missing the show while in the line for the ladies room. Once the concert is over your downtown and the next phase of the night begins then. That's when you get your drink on if that's your thing. Do I miss Starwood? Of course.  But it hasn't slowed anyone who loves live music or sports. Even family entertainment like the circus and Disney on ice. Bridgestone always has A - list entertainment!!!

name: 12th & Porter
text:
HOLY GUACAMOLE!  Their nachos prove that there is a God.  I can't tell you what's on them, even though I reviewed the menu I don't know that everything that was on the menu showed up on top of my nachos but they literally were the best I've ever had.  I seriously think about them ALL THE TIME.  The wine was good and decently priced and the waffle fries weren't very flavorful. GET THE NACHOS. 

Also, we came to hear Tessa Violet and the show was amazing. The bartenders on the stage side were great, attentive, and enjoying themselves.  Sound was great, and would highly recommend.  Show up a little early to eat the nachos then go for the show once you've finished up. 

OH, and be prepared to stand in line. It literally wraps around the building into a back dark alley. 

I love this place and would definitely recommend it!! :)

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Lager Fish & Chips was really good, especially with lemon. Nice atmosphere with good live entertaining band, but long wait. It's was worth it.

name: Ole Red
text:
Blake Shelton has referred to me as an old fart, and he's probably right, but the band at Ole Red's featured a lot of the classic music we old farts love.  Ole Red is being billed as an upscale honky-tonk which seems to be an oxymoron.  Nevertheless, it is a very nice bar, and we really enjoyed ourselves.  We were entertaining some of my wife's cousins from out-of-town, and everybody had a great time.

The staff is friendly, and helpful, and more importantly, they seem really excited to be working there.  My wife tends to judge any establishment by its Cosmos, and Ole Red makes an excellent Cosmo.  I was impressed with their beer selection, and found a very tasty IPA from East Nashville.  Go figure.  

We had tickets to a show at the Ryman, and we planned on having dinner shortly before the show.  So we thought we'd split an appetizer to tide us over until dinner.  The waitress suggested the nachos, and they were delicious. They also were served on a platter the size of Oklahoma.  Six of us were not able to finish them.  And none of us felt like dinner before the show, or after the show.

We do not go downtown often, but we are sure that the next time we have out-of-town guests, we will introduce them to Ole Red.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: So I still love this place. Just wanted to update on the food. The first thing I had was the grilled cheese & it was pretty good but nothing too memorable. Well now I've had the sweet potato poutine & the fish tacos. AMAZING! Not really poutine but I don't care. So good. My friend also said best burger in Nashville. Better than Pharmacy.. Which whoa, I'm trying it next. Or maybe the sandwich with the ham. Decisions, decisions. Plus, they have new games. Love the darts and giant connect 4.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I was honestly surprised at all the negative ratings about this place.  We had a great time in here.  We wanted to stop in because we are Jimmy Buffett fans.  The food was good -- wife had a club sandwich and I had the fish tacos.  Everything tasted great.  We also ordered margaritas (I mean, it's Margaritaville) -- they were very tasty.  There was a live musician up front by the bar which is pretty typical for a place in Music City.  The musician was covering lots of different songs, took requests, and gave a nice vibe to the place.  The highlight of our visit was our server, Kiersten.  She was on it.  She made us feel like family while we were there.  Took a nice trip into the gift shop after lunch and chatted up some of their staff -- bought a T-shirt and some trinkets.  Staff was nice and friendly, and we left happy.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
We stopped by for the SiriusXM Musical Happy Hour.
Great service from Kelsey. The margaritas were very good and a nice selection of local beer . The food was okay but not special. We enjoyed the show.

name: National Underground
text:
Terrible. I'm not a big review person, but I had to write a review on this pathetic excuse of a establishment.

Avoid at all cost. Terrible service. Overpriced. Not a good burger.

name: The High Watt
text:
We drove down to see Run River North and Lighthouse and the Whaler, and had a fabulous time. The space was sufficiently open for dancing, the stage was conveniently bar-height, and the sound was excellent.

The bar is conveniently located - you can sit and watch the show from there - and easy to move in and out of. The bar staff was very friendly and attentive. The only thing that would make it better would be a wider beer selection. Sierra Nevada Pale was the sole craft beer option. Other than that, though, it was excellent.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
This is my favorite venue - in the south - by far! Bridgestone always has the biggest names in music every year, from George Strait, Garth Brooks, Kelly Clarkson, the CMA Awards, Keith Urban (big country fan here!), Springsteen, Billy Joel, and countless others. 

Pros: 

The vendors on each level, they even have one off of the floor so you don't have to go up to the 100 level. 

You can see the stage from just about any seat in the house.

Tavern '96 off Demonbreun 

Cons:

The seats are small and crammed together, if you're not a stick figure or always wind up sitting by, in front of, or behind "that person", you will be shifting around to try to get comfortable. I always hope ticketmaster gives me the "pick your seat" option so I can get an aisle seat to have a little leg room. 

The escalator to go to the upper levels. There are two escalators, both going up before the show, down after. Be prepared to wait getting out, the line to get to the escalators takes a whiles There are stairs as well but you have to walk around the arena to get there.

Both cons are worth putting up with to see whoever's playing the Bridgestone!

Parking garages are close by, the closest being part of Music City Center off Demonbreun across the street, then another one is two blocks away at the library and the Renaissance. I've always received an email with the option to buy a parking pass for the Pinnacle but both of the lots I mentioned are closer and are around the same price, although it helps to buy it if a big name is playing.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We went in once.  The food was okay, had the 1/2 chicken in BBQ sauce or style, the breast was okay, but the leg and thigh undercooked. Bill was pricy, mostly because we had 4 drinks, at about $11.00 a pop, and just average (barely adequate) margaritas which were on the specialty menu, not great, and definitely less than expected for the price charged.  Paying for the name Jimmy Buffett.   Waitress was the best part, Annie took good care of us.  Music, fair to middling.  Would not spend time to go again, better places.

name: Ole Red
text:
Great food.... Go for the chicken both hot and not are great.... Best music on Broadway...

And tater tots are definitely a must order

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Damn good burger! Perfect set up for a beer and some food. The 1927 IPA was one of the better I sampled from the 5 taster flight they offered. Would highly recommend this spot for a good hangout spot with friends.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I came here for a convention for the work I belong in. The arena itself is pretty decent but I largely gave it 2 stars because there being a soup kitchen a couple blocks down where people would die for a warm meal and clean water. Meanwhile upon trying to go through the entrance, the security was making everyone entering throw their food away and they were taking people's water/drinks away. But the worst thing was they were taking the water bottles and just dumping them on the pavement, not even on the grass. The pavement appeared as if it had been rained upon. This was disgusting to me.

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
We stumbled upon the symphony center while we were walking on our back to my friend's house.  We got lucky since they were having an event for school kids at the venue so it was open.  We went in to have a look-see and was amazed by how beautiful the center is. The architectural design as well as the decor is fabulous.  I was particularly drawn to the lighting fixtures which were amazing and beautiful. 

We definitely got lucky that day because the symphony hall was open and the orchestra was rehearsing so we were able to listen to them.  They sounded great and the acoustics in the symphony hall was amazing.  I really wish I had time to catch a show or two at this venue on my stay in Nashville but time was short.  I will definitely catch one next time I am in town.

The staff members, volunteers I think, were very nice and accommodating.  They answered any questions that we had.  Bathrooms were well-maintained and very clean... a definite plus, if you ask me.

name: Ole Red
text:
Most impressed with the menu. 

Vegan & Vegetarian options. 
I will say the cornbread was SWEET like pound cake.
Atmosphere was great, very entertaining. 
Nice customer service at door and from the waitress. 
We sat right by the stage and only walked around a few minutes. 
There was dancing as well. 
We didn't walk upstairs this trip but definitely will next trip.

name: Ole Red
text:
Food was surprisingly great. Burger was cooked a perfect medium rare as ordered. Fries were good. Staff & service were excellent. Great live music & festive atmosphere. Adorable little details throughout the restaurant (see photos of bathroom signs). 2nd floor gives a great view of Broadway. 
A must see in Nashville.

name: Ole Red
text: Awful, Do not recommend, we are locals, and decided to give Ole Red a try.  I know that they do not rely on a revisit (since most that visit are tourists) so they really don't care about the quality of the food or service(sad), but we will not come back or recommend it to any one visiting.  First the service was obnoxiously slow, and they weren't that busy ( around noon on Sunday) we waited so long for drinks, that we went up to the bar to get our own (the table next to us did as well, several times, they were from out of town and complained the whole time about the service)  When we finally got to order our food, we both ordered the Ribeye, $30.00 a person, with one side.  Well it was the worst cut of meat I have ever had in my life, it was ALL fat,!   I understand it is not a steak house, but I have bought better steak at Aldi then this!!!! Thirty dollars for this?  Mine was way overcooked ( I wanted medium rare) so I sent it back, It was $30 after all,  I was eventually brought another, which was rare, still mooing on the plate, but didn't say anything, it wasn't worth it to us.  It was a struggle to get the sever to come back, (that's why we got our own drinks), so we paid the tab and went elsewhere  The one good thing they had was  the Cauliflower (Ill give them that).  Also they had music playing and it wasn't over the top loud, so kudos on that as well, but overall your food and service sucks! I normally do not leave reviews but it was just that bad.  Save your self the trouble and go somewhere else!!!!!

name: Ole Red
text: The food is sooo good. I don't understand why this place only have 3 1/2 stars. The service was fantastic and friendly. Wait was only 5 minutes at 12 noon on NYE. Life entertainment was good. I would say it's a little loud but hey I don't mind that one bit. Would definitely come back when back in town.

name: Ole Red
text: When I think of what Blake Shelton's restaurant might be the first thing would be a dive bar.  Of course I was partially wrong, it is a dive bar with some major modern features.  It did not disappoint. The ambiance was amazing with a great band and the food was some of the best I have had.  I recommend the wings because they have just a little bit and they fall right off the bone.  A must have is the homemade tater tots.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: The beers were interesting and enjoyable for the most part (especially the basil) and the consistent live music added to the ambiance. Emptier than expected for a Saturday night.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
More than anything, I really like the feel of this place. Brewery/taproom/bar/live music venue, TBW has pretty much everything you need for a beer-fueled good time. I hadn't heard of this brewery before coming to Nashville but I'm mighty glad that it's on my radar now.

To begin with, as you approach the venue, you're impressed. Rather than go for an industrial 'gritty' feel, TBW welcomes you with patio seating, gorgeous wood and plenty of open air (is that a rooftop?). TBW is a celebration of one of the key elements of beer drinking: doing so with a group of friends. Yes, the craft beer movement is a serious one but it should also be fun. The fellas over at TBW remembers that. Step inside and, again, you have ample seating, a second floor/balcony access and plenty of posters letting you know of upcoming shows. A cold craft beer and live music sounds like a pretty excellent night in Nashville. And, what of the beer? I'm glad you asked. Expect inventive flavors that, if you come here during a tour, are expertly explained and generously sampled. I am not much of a basil fan (read somewhere once that it's a carcinogen and whether or not it's true, it's stayed with me for all of these years) but it was an unexpectedly tasty treat. A saison with fruit notes, the spice from the herb elevates the beer in to something I'd never tasted before (and I drink a lot of beer). The Country Roots sweet potato stout was also a fun drink. It respects the region while offering a twist on the usual stout (coffee and chocolate notes). Since the beers (while I was there) hovered around the hoppy and bitter (not my flavor profile), the last beer I tried was the Southern Wit. This is a white ale with conspicuous sweet fruit notes (orange, honey and pear). It went down very easily and would be a perfect spring/summer beer. Are you sensing a pattern? The brewers at TBW take this stuff seriously but have fun with their creations. You should as well.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: We were visiting Nashville for a few days and we decided to find a nice local pub to spend one of those nights... Boy what a mistake that was, I probably should've listened to the uber driver when he said that the downtown bars are "nicer to the outsiders". The lady bartenders were very rude to us from the beginning and they were not shy about it either. One of the ladies got irritated because I found a fly in my drink and she had to remake it, really? A few hours in they decided to express their feelings by cursing at us, we decided to take our business somewhere else because the lady bartenders made racist comments and the manager "turtle" did nothing when these allegations were brought to him. Definitely not worth you money or time!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Loved it! The beer selection is awesome and their food is on point! Ample space on the patio and dog friendly as well! They have a small lot in the back for cars, but it might be better to park on the street-the alley is super narrow.

name: Nashville Symphony
text: For Father's Day week we were in Nashville on business.  On Father's Day my husband was taken to the Nashville Symphony: The Baseball Project with Hall of Fame Dave Winfield as narrator and host of the event.  Also in attendance was former baseball Manager John McNamara  .  Along with these two icons were vintage and historical footage from Cooperstown.  The had singers who sung classic baseball songs as the symphony performed.  They also reenacted a baseball game as you would hear it on the radio or sitting in the stand with symphony playing the organ riff you hear at every baseball game to making sounds that sounded like a crowd.  The also did a tribute to Babe Ruth, Joe DiMaggio, Jackie Robinson and Roberto Clemente.  Additionally they had a vintage baseball team that plays by the original baseball rules in the lobby between intermission and before/after the show.  We really enjoyed it.  Great Job! Nashville Symphony!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
This outstanding brewery near the Nashville Gulch is a great place to enjoy some delicious craft beer, good grub and wonderful music. Dropping by during a recent visit to Music City, I enjoyed two fabulous IPAs -- the hoppy 1927 and the citrusy Hippies & Cowboys -- along with their solid Extra Easy, a malty pub ale. Paired with a tasty Five Beer Burger, the brews were by far the best I've had in Nashville.

Brew Works also serves up live music almost nightly -- the evening I was there, I enjoyed a terrific performance by a local bluegrass band. The small taproom practically puts the musicians in your lap, but you can  escape to a second-floor bar and dining room if that's not your speed. There's also an outdoor balcony with great city views. The location is an industrial neighborhood just east of the official 'Gulch,' so it can feel a bit isolated if you're walking over on your own. And while parking onsite is limited, I had no trouble finding a spot about a block away on the street. 

Tennessee Brew Works is a gem that combines great craft beer with great music. A must for any beer lover visiting Nashville.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
We are beer lovers and are so happy there is finally a quality beer and food spot!!!Love the sweet potato stout! Also,
The staff is very friendly and knowledgeable about the beer and food. We always take our out of town friends here and these guys at TBW never disappoint.

name: Ole Red
text: Great food, great experience!  A must visit in Nashville! Service was excellent and environment was open and welcoming.  Server came by several times and was very sweet. Menu had good offerings and came out of he kitchen quickly.

name: Ole Red
text: Very enjoyable eating experience in the heart of Honky Tonk Nashville's famous downtown Broadway. More of a pleasant dining music alternative to the louder places on Broadway. Ole Red has very talented performers. Victoria our server was great. The Potato Tots are amazing and huge. The Kiss My Country Ass Quesadillas delicious. An overall great place to visit and revisit.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Really great bar food! Sampled several good beers too! Nice live music. Bathrooms out of soap and paper towels ... hence the four rather than five stars. Maybe this was a fluke though. 

The grilled cheese with pear butter, goat and white cheddar was to die for! The smoked pulled pork sandwich was mouthwateringly delicious. We also liked the hot chicken sandwich. The fries were just ok, but the house made ketchup was excellent with a sweet balsamic flavor. There was a beer called the quad something, wow, loved it! Very smoky and rich. It packed a punch at 10% ABV.

name: Ole Red
text: The fried chicken was great. We had the 1/2 chicken and briskets and it was plenty for 2. The music was loud but not overpowering. We had the  normal seasoning. They also have Hot that is a Buffalo Wings sauce. The 4 stars is for the meal along with a quality music show.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Lively place, for a Thirstday afternoon/evening. Good beer and fine hushpuppies. Active dartboard. Fun & friendly informed staff.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Went here for a private party. Extremely packed. 

I'm only reviewing on everything but the food because I didn't eat although the nacho plate looked delicious. 

It was packed so I stood over by two waitresses who were complaining and cursing across the room at each other. So unprofessional, I was surprised the owner let it slide multiple times. Although he looks extremely young and not really sure what he's doing. 

The staff are all pretty rude. I wouldn't come back.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Pulled chicken + baked beans + collard greens = heaven! This place is so great! The band was tremendous, the waitress at the bar was an A+ waitress, the meat was hot and smokey, there is Bridgestone Arena across the street, and also the prices are solid. A must for Lower Broadway!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Oh my gosh! I couldn't say enough positive things about this place! It just made me so happy. Keep in mind that I am a bit biased since anywhere that plays country music automatically gains a few stars for me. ;]
    Don't be turned off by the first impression. We were a little confused since we thought we were on our way to a bar, but when you first walk in it's a restaurant. The second and third floors are bars. Both of the top floors overlook the huge dance floor on the bottom level which is obviously line dancing! The dance floor is right in front of a huge stage where there is live music. 
    Scattered throughout the place are these life sized horses that look a little like cartoons. They are really fun to take pictures with. The bathrooms are very clean and I met an attendant named Barbara who was the sweetest lady. 
    The drinks are little pricey, but worth it for the atmosphere! There are two bars on either side of the stage and of course big bars on each of the top levels. They do have a souvenir shop also. 
    There is unfortunately a $6 cover, but I will definitely be going again despite this. Even one of my co-workers who does not like country music had a great time!

name: Nashville Palace
text: We only went to this bar at night after dinner, so we only had the drinks and listened to the music.  Loved to listen to Dennis Payne and his band.  The staff was friendly and the drinks were good.  We spent several nights of our vacation coming here to listen to the music and have a drink after touring during the day.  I believe Roberts Western World on Broadway is the sister bar/grill to this bar.  The menu and decor is the same.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Well,,,,service was fast but my ribs were cold. It took longer the get the heated ones back than it did to get them the first time.  While waiting I ate my two side dishes. So when I got back the exact same ribs, complete with the first bone I ate still on the plate, I didn't have any sides left to eat with my meal.  

I suggest you keep walking if you want good food.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Our Uber driver recommend Rippys for BBQ and the honkey tonk scene. It was seat yourself and, as packed as it was, we got a table right away.  We had pulled pork, pulled chicken and ribs. Dinner, including the sides, was great. Loved the fried pickles. Service was fine. Bands playing upstairs and downstairs. Music was ok. Downstairs was packed - difficult to walk through.  Would recommend.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Food was basic bar food. Nothing great. My bf had his first fried bologna sandwich. Waitress was fast and the band was fun. Loved watching people dancing. This place is bigger and a lot less crowded than the downtown location.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I went to Nashville for a quick girls trip and tried this place out the first night for drinks, dancing and food. The ribs were amazing!! Great sauce!! We tried Peg Leg Porker that got great reviews on yelp, but their ribs weren't nearly as good as Rippy's... and we had to save a table for nine of us and wait for at least 40 minutes in line at PLP.

name: CMA Fest
text:
We planned our Tennessee trip months ago without planning on being here during the festival.  Wow we got lucky what a great experience!  Loved all the exhibits, bars and performances.  We saw Big and Rich  6 rows from the front all free.   Cool to watch Keith Urban sign a cowboy hat for a young wrangler and we bumped elbows with Blake Sheldon popping in on a jam session.

On top of all this downtown was filled supporting their Predators!  Way to go police and fire support to make this a safe experience for us out of towners.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: After doing the bar crawl one night in Nashville, we finally landed in this place and loved it so much we came back the next night. I was on a trip with my sisters and we were looking to line dance. Apparently dancing isn't very big in Nashville, everywhere else we went, people were just sitting and listening to the live music. This place was perfect. It is huge with a really large dance floor and amazing live music. We loved the line dancing lessons and then practicing on the songs after to perfect our steps. Really clean bathrooms!

name: Twin Kegs
text: It's definitely a dive bar, but I picked up a burger to go; I must admit, it was pretty darn good! (and greasy)

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Love this place- all of the food is amazing- my favorite pizza is the buffalo pizza though- it's beyond delicious!  Such a fun atmosphere and live music - it's a must for Nashville and you need to try it out!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: BBQ was good, not amazing. There were live bands all night which was cool. Its definitely laid back. Not a must go kind of place but not regrettable.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: CMA fans do not go! Our waitress had the worst attitude and was upset that we asked for separate checks. She just decided to divide it evenly between everyone. Food was just ok. The windows were open and it started pouring down raining on our table and not a single person came to help up clean up. Our food was soaked but luckily most ppl had finished eating. Spend your money on better food and service somewhere else.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: In town for a conference, read the reviews and stopped in. Love the atmosphere, live music. The drinks are very reasonable and the food is the delicious. The people really showed a Philly girl southern hospitality while enjoying watching my Eagles play. Definitely will be back .

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Food was fair but the waitress Mercedes D. Was horrible. She couldn't put a smile on her face. We had a group of 9 she could have made a great tip but when the food came with the wrong order she said she " didn't ask questions" hmmm isn't that what a waitress should do if an order is wrong. Crab apple!!!!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This is a huge location and we stopped by in the afternoon and they had line dancing classes during the day.  Instructor was engaged and friendly.  A must stop by for a Nashville visit.  Several floors and plenty of seating.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
This place is becoming one of our regular stops. As a transplant, we first ventured in to see a football game on a Sunday. The bartender was super accommodating and provided superb service including turning the game I wanted on one of the big screens at the bar. The manager also stopped by to see how we were doing and even put the audio for the game on the overhead speakers.

Pursuant to that, we've stopped in for a few business dinners or when we have out of town guests. The vibe is great and you'll regularly catch some live music. I spent a decade in NYC, so I have a different preference for style of pizza, but they do a good job here. The food in general is pretty tasty and reasonably priced. 

Our last couple of stops have been venturing out when the weather is nice to take advantage of the huge 2nd floor outdoor loft. It's really an awesome spot to chill and enjoy some sunshine and a nice breeze. There's always some good local music and Travis the bartender goes above and beyond to take care of you. Looking forward to our next stop!

name: Houston Station
text: I co-chaired a school event at Houston Station and could not have been more pleased.  Beautiful venue, perfect layout, thoughtful details like wifi and plugs everywhere.  Elizabeth was a dream to work with.  Our crowd loved the beautiful old brick, wood floors and heavy timber beams.  So much charm that decorating can be kept to a minimum.  Perfect place, easy to work with, very helpful.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: We really like this place.  When we went Broadway was CRAZY packed and starting to fill up with a pretty rowdy crowd.  We discovered second ave and liked how it was a bit more laid back and not as packed yet still had a lot of great honkey-tonks to choose from.  Although the Wildhorse charged a $6 cover it was worth it.  We hit the 7.30pm show with 2 way crossing and were surprised to see a fair amount of families.  We arrived at 6pm and was warned it would be a 1.5 hour wait but there were seats available at the bar so we had drinks.  We had a great server (Savanna?) once seated who was very attentive and the food was pretty good as well.  The show was really good up on the stage although after playing for about 50 minutes they took a 30 minute break!!  30 minutes was way too long but we stuck it out.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
I like coming here for the drinks & listening to music on the awesome patio.. but the food & service are not so great. I had the Mississippian pizza & tried the Bob Marley as well. Both were meh. I think the crust was the biggest problem, it was pretty soggy. 

Overall, I would not eat here again but I'll be back to drink on the patio!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
This place is pricier than others on the strip but you go here for the eye candy. Upstairs has open balconies that look down the strip so it has a very outdoor feel. It's slammed on weekends, I had lunch here, BBQ and it was OK but nothing at all special. The staff seem to be hit and miss, they're not big on serving overseas guests as they don't tip the 20% that Americans usually do, I know as I'm british and she had an attitude when she heard my accent but I showed here my Cali driving license and she warmed up. 

If you come to Nashville you have to stop in and make for the upper levels for a few drinks, you won't be disappointed on the view and the hang. There's better food around if you want it. The bands as all on the strip is also hit and miss, you get who's out on the night but then walk around and see who's on. Lots of kids, cougars and trendy dudes you'll have fun here. It is what it is, but it's 3 stars at best.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I feel bad bashing this place because of a band member that was out of line. This place had great service, great food and a fun atmosphere! I would go back in a second and recommend it to friends visiting town. I even tipped our waiter extra because he was great with our huge party. Thank you Justin for getting back to me about our bad situation - appreciate it!!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: We were celebrating a milestone event.  I was very appalled by the way the hosts treated my Sister-in-law.  The waiter was efficient, the food was mediocre at best, pricing was reasonable if you like their food.  As we were leaving the establishment, two male hosts aggressively approached my Sister-in-law accusing her of (dining and dashing).  They demanded to see the receipt which she graciously showed them.   I felt like they humiliated her and should of apologized.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I asked the bouncer if they sold water bottles and he replied, "Hot blondes only". Keepin' it classy with that southern hospitality.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: What a fun place! The B-B-Q was excellent, we got to square dance, and overall the whole environment was enjoyable! We are not in Nashville to often, but we will be back!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Terrible live music. Worse food. And the beer is ridiculously overpriced. If you come out of a hockey game or concert, keep walking.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Food was terrible.  We ordered the hamburger and pulled pork sandwich, both were bland, as was the Coleslaw.  Bartender is RUDE!  Asked her to check status of our food since it had been over 30 min at that point.  Her reply?  'I'm not allowed to check the status'.  Huh??   I must say the music was fabulous.  I suggest going to hear the music but go to Acme (down the street) to eat.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This was an interesting place. The dance floor seemed small for the amount of people wanting to line dance but it worked out. We got a decent table to watch the show and our server was awesome and on top of keeping our drinks filled. I had several appetizers and they were all good. Their wings were a pretty good choice. The band was good also. It's a good place to go if you want to watch a bunch of tourists attempt to line dance. Overall it was a fun time

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good  was not so good , and the drinks were ridicusly overpriced,  I guess is to be expected on Broadway but I think it's to much , the food price is not so bad , but I personally didn't like the food so much my wife had a BBQ wrap and that was better that my pulled pork sandwich

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great place to go hear some music and get your line dance on! The food was okay, but it is definitely not the main attraction. The music and dancing are definitely the main draw here. They have great sound and lighting and host some of the best that country music has to offer. A must see if you are in Nashville.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Barbeque was awful!!! Baked beans and turnip greens were marginal at best. Music was loud, but lacked quality of sound.  Too many musicians in this city to get a better sound which reflect the quality of sound and talent in this city. Wait staff not attentive, but to her credit she was working the bar too.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: TPAC is a wonderful venue where I have seen many Broadway touring shows, ballets and plays. I recently saw Beauty and the Beast there, which was top-notch. The facility has comfortable seating, plenty of restrooms (although could use more for women during intermissions) and helpful and friendly staff. Parking is available by valet or many surface lots and parking garages in the vicinity. If available, I highly recommend parking in the Library garage, as it is just a couple blocks away and the most reasonably priced parking you'll find in Nashville.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Pretty good place to stop for a quick bite to eat and a drink before going out onto Broadway.

My friends an I had the pulled pork on corn cakes, they were very good! 

Good price and location. We sat on the upper level by the open windows looking out to Broadway. Quick service and there were was a lot of seating. A bit loud, but fun to listen to a live band during dinner.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I loved it !! Nice place, good music, clean, service is ok.
I didn't eat just had drinks 
They have line dancing with an instructor which is very easy to fallow we enjoyed it very much. 
We got to see David Oakleaf he was great 
I would recommend you visit wildhorse saloon for some line dance fun

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Nice atmosphere and wonderful live music. Only problem was the bartender, Daphne, was extremely rude. We left after one drink after she gave us attitude. Every other bar on Broadway was welcoming and the bartenders exuded southern hospitality. Very disappointed with the service here.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The pimiento cheese was the best I have ever had! I also had the house salad with smoked salmon, which was also delicious.  The amount of salmon was huge.  The service was great and knowledgable.  The band that was there was sort of annoying because the songs were all played at the same tempo and they made super cheesy jokes- but it was a Monday nightProbably not the A list.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Jenny was our server tonight and we were a difficult crowd. We came in at different times, had multiple checks and picky people. She smiled and served us quick and well. She was a great server tonight!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: We went to Rippys last night with our volleyball team last night.  We sat upstairs and there was plenty of room and tables that made it easy to accommodate large parties, live music both up and downstairs and the team had a great time dancing.  Food was great, and service was great, especially considering how crazy this place was.  We were a party of 30, there wAs another team with Pri ably same amount of guests, as well as several smaller tables and food came out in a fair amount of time and tasted great. Our waitress, I think her name was Elizabeth, handled our crazy group like a pro and even allowed us separate Checks (greatly appreciated).  The restaurant was great, with a fun casual environment, great food, and room to dance.   Will definitely be back.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Band playing on the first floor and another on the 2nd floor...I'm definitely a fan! If you want that Southern vibe, this is the place to go. I had the full slab of ribs and they were fall off the bone tender and smokey! they rate up there with one of the best in my opinion. I love that Fireball; had a shot right before my ribs came. Upstairs, the music got even better! You've gotta try the Cinnamon Toast Crunch Shot.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Would love to be able to review the food here, but I can't since I couldn't get any.  My boyfriend and I came in here one night and, after being told by one mostly disinterested staff member that our best chance of getting served was to sit upstairs, we went upstairs and sat at an empty table.  We looked over the menus, chose what we wanted and waited for someone to come by.....or acknowledge our presence....or glance in our direction.....or......anything.  After at least a good 20 minutes of sitting at our table and watching staff members attend to or clear nearby tables, we did not receive so much as a greeting, let alone an offer to bring us anything to eat or drink.  And yes, they were busy, but if a waiter has time to bus the table next to ours, they have time to look in our direction.  I am virtually certain we left our invisibility cloaks at home, so I cannot fathom why the staff opted to ignore us, but we were completely ignored.  Pathetic and ridiculous lack of service.  We eventually just got up and left, still completely unacknowledged.  Would not recommend.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
My teenage son and I arrived in town starving on a Friday night and Yelp!found us a gem!  We chose Soulshine because of the combination of live music and pizza, and both were excellent.

We shared a 12 inch CCR pizza on wheat crust -- chicken, Canadian bacon, small bacon pieces, and a ranch sauce.  Delicious.  The chicken was white meat chunks that were moist and tender.  The wheat crust was thin and crispy just the way I like it.

Based on several reviews that the Crawfish Soup "was to die for", I tried a cup.  I wish I would have gotten a bowl.  The reviews were right on.  The soup was creamy and savory at the same time with the just the right number of whole crawfish tails at the bottom of the cup.  It was spiced with the perfect amount of cayenne -- subtly cajun without being too much.  Reminds me of another favorite creamy cajun treat, the fettuccine alfredo at Jazz, a Louisiana Kitchen, in Kansas City.

Soulshine Pizza Factory is highly recommended, especially on Fri/Sat nights when there is live music with no cover charge.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: There should be a 6 star for this. Johnny Neel from the Allman Brothers playing tonight. The guy before him was awesome. This is the reason why I love Nashville.  You would pay to see this and here its free. Of course this place has great pizza and plenty of beer options but again WOW Music City.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
This was another "when in Rome" moment for us.  We were at the Wildhorse on a Monday night.  The live music was great.  We sat in the upper horse-shoe area and loved watching the spectacle of people line-dancing.  It is totally a tourist trap but silly fun.  We sat there for about 4 hours, just drinking, ordering appetizers, and enjoying the live music from a great vantage point (kinda felt like Statler and Waldorf, the old men in the Muppets).  

The bars in the district area have a lot that still allow smoking.  Dive bars are fine to me and the music was really good from all of them, but at some point in the night, I didn't want anymore smoke (I believe Wildhorse is all-ages / kid friendly so there is no smoking allowed) and to sit down in a place relatively clean.  Wildhorse fit the bill.  Well worth the $6 cover, especially because I don't remember how much the drinks were... but I think $11 for a very strong vodka/cran and a pretty sizable beer).  That doesn't seem awful to me.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Hmnn, not sure how to feel about this joint. Oh wait, yes I do. They are racist. They have a live band, which is cool, but what place doesn't in the neighborhood? This is not the place to give your business to. 

Yeah... let's go ahead and avoid places that yell out racist slurs towards asian tourists. Probably not a good idea. Seriously in disbelief. 

Here you go, let me hand you guys this L.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This is our go to place as soon as we get into Nashville each time. I like their second floor bar area. Good music and fast service. Try the nachos with pork.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Been sitting here for almost 2 hours. If somebody could come to take our order that would be great.
Tried to get somebody's attention, and the staff member said he doesn't take care of our tables and walked away.
Horrible service.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Not impressed. Stopped for drinks in the afternoon. The band took 30 minutes to set up. The bar was tacky (sticky). $15 for a draft beer and a not very good 7&7. Ok I guess.

name: Twin Kegs
text: Great old school atmosphere. Kind of run down and dirty, but I saw the bartender cleaning, so I don't think it is grimy, just old. Bartender was very nice, and the people that were there that seemed to be regulars, were very nice too. I had the BB (Bad Burger) and it was very tasty. They also had 3-4 porters/stouts, and I like dark beer, so this was great. The even had one of my favorite beers, Left Hand Milk Stout.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
We are staying at the hotel next to the Nashville Palace and driving past it for the few days we are here, the place is always active. So we decided to check it out. 

We loved it and enjoyed ourselves so much that we are going back tonight. The bands were great! Didn't have to fight the Broadway crowds and spent half of the money we would have downtown. Draft beer is limited on choices, but other than that drinks were great and can't beat the price!

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Historically, I have loved this place. Basic bar food and great country music. 

This past visit was a huge disappointment. The music was so loud it hurt ears. It was pretty obvious when we walked in because everyone was seated as far away as possible and several people had their fingers in their ears. No excuse for this in this town. 

We left because we couldn't take it. Sorry.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Catfish tacos are AMAZING.  Perfectly blackened and seasoned catfish.  A must have. Get a little extra sauce to dip the fries in

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
First of all, they charged us a $6 cover per person, which was surprising, but we thought, ok, maybe its worth it.  We figured it covered the cost of the band, but then again, there's a band at every saloon and they arent' charging for a cover fee.

next problem:  there was a private party renting out half the place, so we had to listen to company xyz speeches to their employees and watch them all act like idiots square dancing and dominating the whole dance floor and stage.  another reason to not charge us cover charge, if theres a private party and the microphone and dance floor are being dominated by a private company then why are we charged a cover.??  we will return to nashville but NEVER to this rip-off joint.

Then we ordered nachos with pork, there was about two tablespoons of pork and most of the nachos had nothing on them.  a $12 ripoff.  Same deal with the salad, the chicken on it was ice cold like the whole salad was sitting in the refigerator, not hot fresh grilled chicken.  Basically a bowl of iceberg lettuce for $11.  ripoff.  Next came the wings, we requested sweet barbecue and they came out plane.  Now i've never had plane chicken wings in a restaurant before, usually they are coated with sauce and delicious.  Well these were plane, looked like they just threw them in the fryer and served them without any sauce or flavoring at all.

Our server was indifferent, probably making so much money off tips from the drunk tables she didn't really give a hoot about us.  The bartender (while we were waiting for a table) was semi-unfriendly, my wife doesn't drink alcohol so when i ordered a beer for me and a pepsi for her we got a sneer.  

Lastly: a couple showed up with an infant baby in a carrier.  now this place is really really loud, and they just put the baby on the table right in the center of the place where the music was crazy loud...  We said something to the management that this was inappropriate, that in infant should be in a loud place like this and they did nothing, said it was "parents discretion".    Well some parents have no common sense, the poor baby was subjected to this loud place.... the two parents went up on the dance floor and left the baby with a grandparent- so we dropped a little note on their table- reminding them that the childs hearing could be damaged and that it was far too loud in there for an infant--- common sense aint so common anymore.  On our way out, we mentioned to the guy who took our cover charge that they shouldn't allow infants in there, he had nothing to say either.  So we left $70 poorer scratching our heads about the entire evening

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: For a bar in Nashville, it's nothing too special. A decent bite of ribs, an okay beer selection, and mildly helpful service. The band was just a couple dudes covering random country songs. All-in-all, there are better places for food, service, drinks, and entertainment in every direction.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Went there tonight and had to wait over an hour for a table, even thought several tables were available.  Horrible customer service and very disorganized.  Food was decent but took a long time.  Possibly worst restaurant/entertainment experience ever.  Would never return under any circumstance.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good music and great food. Isn't that all you need? Rippy's definitely has both. Their BBQ is excellent and the buffalo wings had my whole party wanting to go back for more. I was truly impressed with the food. It's not typical fried bar food, but actual BBQ. The live music was great on both floors, but I honestly can't say that I saw a bad band throughout the whole strip during my visit. All bands on the strip work for tips and walk around with a tip bucket, which is a little weird, but it's normal around here so no harm. This is a definite stop for anyone's trip to Nashville. It's located on a very busy corner and gets packed late night on weekends. Luckily they have 2 downstairs rooms and an upstairs that is pretty big. Conveniently just a few steps away from Bridgestone Arena. Well done Rippy's

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Nashville- you GOTTA get to this brand new hot spot in the heart of Downtown... Truly unique eatery with a vibe - the name says it all!  This is a tasty Southern menu and spectacular live music venue.  We ordered deviled eggs 5 ways and the meatloaf - wholly unique and absolutely delicious!  Treated to two terrific songwriter performances and had an amazing Sunday evening.  Extensive bar, great coffee options, doesn't get any better!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
I liked this place.  Good music, and a nice roomy floor plan.  

The food was served rapidly after ordering, and was delicious.  Drinks were reasonably priced and made quickly.  Service was good.  

You'll find a large rooftop here, with music on all levels.  Wood floors, tables, and bars, and stairs.  I was here on a Tuesday afternoon and it was pretty packed, so I am sure it's even worse during the weekends. 

I tried the pulled pork and a salad, both of which were fantastic.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Always packed, had lunch there. Pulled pork wasn't the best, lacked a lot of flavor for being in the south.

Great sides. The Mac and cheese and the backed beans were amazing, whereas the coleslaw not the best. 

Brother had the ribs and he said there were amazing

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Beautiful venue. Slow service and horrible BBQ. Dry brisket that taste like dirt with lots of salt. We sent it back and they brought us Ribs. Again it was dry, chewy and taste like dirt. We took two bites. Manager demanded we pay for what we didn't eat. We refused and left. We won't be back.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Large and really nice restaurant and bar with a dance floor and stage.  They were giving line dance lessons that were really popular.  We would have drank here, but we never saw a server in the.bar area.  We never got a food menu either.  We waited maybe 20 minutes and then left.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: We stopped here for a quick lunch. Average bar food, good service, we did enjoy the live music, the duo were actually very good and fun to listen to while eating. Not the bars fault we could not stay longer since our parking was about to expire and it is very expensive to park downtown.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: We were looking for a family friendly place with good food, beer and good, live country music and that's exactly what we got! We were able to get the full Nashville experience with an early (4ish) dinner yummy bbq pulled pork and brisket), front row to a wonderful band with our kids. Def would recommend this place.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This was one of the worst places I have ever been to. This was the first place I have been to in Nashville. My party arrived around 12 and ordered lunch straight off the menu and not one order was delivered to our table correctly. Then at about 2pm the rest of our party joined us at kickoff for the semifinals of the college football playoffs. Unfortunately, we will have to rewatch it because all of the TVs only worked about half of the time due to bad satellite reception that the staff refused to fix. Our waiter said "I guess it'll come on when it comes on." To top things off, it was New Years Eve and so they had at least 7 staff members blowing up hundreds of balloons with long strings  and putting them all over everyone which tangled everyone up and got all in the food despite numerous complaints from several parties. We stayed for around 6 hours to try to watch the game and ended up live streaming it on our phones. We came in excited with high expectations and were thoroughly disappointed and will not be back.  Bad management. Bad service. Mediocre food.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Pretty good bar.  Lost 1 star due to lack of Guinness on tap.  The live bands were good, and the food was decent.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: We went to see Paw Patrol Live on our first visit to the Tennessee Performing Arts. The theater was a lot bigger than we had expected it to be. My wife and I grew up in NY and attended many Broadway shows and this theater definitely rivals a Broadway theater in size and spectacle. The volunteer staff at the venue were all very friendly during our visit and they made sure that our kids had a wonderful time. We look forward to attending future shows at TPAC for years to come.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Live music and ribs.. that's all I wanted and that's what I got! The service was quick even though the place was packed. The ribs were decent - great hangout place when in Nashville.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Visiting our daughter who just moved to Nashville, were told a 1 hour wait for a table, waited the 1+ hour in the waiting area with drinks/appetizers (the fried pickles were great) and then seated at the counter like seats facing the dance floor while there were tables obviously untaken.  When asked if there was anyway we could have a table (There were 4 adults and 1 child) we were refused saying they were expecting a party of 20..thast party never came and the tables remained empty and we remained and ate our VERY MEDIOCRE dinner, tasteless.

The restaurant staff never smiled, were rude on several occasions and need to find other jobs. They were very bothered to have to do anything for us and believe me we are very easy people.  Not sure what their problem was. My daughter wrote on the receipt the details of our distasteful service and visit and asked that the waitress please be sure the manager sees the comments.  I am sure she never showed it to hi or her.

The ambiance and music were terrific and the décor....we loved everything about the place except 2 very important features...the service and the food.
