We will be back in Nashville several times a year in the future but will NEVER frequent this place again.  Those waitresses who services us really need to leave if this place is to continue to be in business. Sooooo atypical of the wonderful southern hospitality we experienced everywhere else.

Manager...please track down who worked there last Sunday evening around 7 PM and address it accordingly.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We were so excited to eat here after hearing how good it was from others and reading other reviews. There are only 8 other tables here and it took over an hour for our food to come out. Half of our food was undercooked and cold. We asked for a manager and he asked me what I wanted him to do about it. There was no explanation or apology. I have been a server and bartender for years and that is not how you handle your guests. Needless to say, we will not be back. I really hope they read this and improve their service.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Nice place to hang out, watch football, and drink beer. Open space is good for chilling. Food is pretty good. Wide selection of local beer.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Stopped in on the way to Navarre, FL. Everything we ordered was on the money. Great food and found my personal favorite beer from Bearded Iris. My family and I had a great time. Music/entertainment was great, the food and atmosphere was equal. I highly recommend stopping by!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Food was mediocre. 5-7pm was filled with too many kids. Running and horsing around on the dance floor. I'm sure it's probably better later at night.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Pro. Music and ambiance...have a drink but don't eat

Con : Like many other patrons, my family and I suffered the result Of poor service and mediocre food. We were seated at 6:45 our reservation time right near the stage. We waited 20 min before we finally asked for a waiter and drinks. Later asked for silverware, asked for more refills, ask to have our order taken and 2 hours later got our food. The waiter apologized but the manager didn't seem to care though we got a 1/2 discount that we asked for. This was the first time in my life I didn't leave a tip. I normally tip 20-30% and travel 3-4 days a week so I eat out A LOT! Many people got up and left mad.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The Wildhorse is a good time. Went on Saturday night, kind of early. Line dancing lessons in between band sets. Everyone gets out on the floor. Mix of country, pop, and hip hop to line dance to. The band was phenomenal (Adairs Run). My only criticism - we started out on the 3rd floor, where I'm guessing there is no wait staff. The glasses, bottles, plates, half finished just sat and were never cleaned up. We eventually moved downstairs, but it was a little unsanitary.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Mediocre food. My  Friend and I split the pulled pork platter, Mac and cheese, and cornbread. It was alright the pulled pork was dry the Mac and cheese was ok. Nothing spectacular. I honestly expected a lot more because it was recommended to us by somebody who lives down here. Next time I will definitely do more research, because all we wanted was delicious juicy bbq and rippys didn't hit that mark.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: We did a group event here so did not order off menu. Our buffet had pulled pork and Berkeley brisket - both good. Overall good food and decent venue.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
This was one of my top bars when I visited Nashville (and I went to most of the ones on lower Broadway when I was there for the week). 

The food menu is substantial and there are lots of choices. However if you go you should order the fried pickles (world famous as they say), the fried green tomatoes and a beer of your choice. They have a beer brewed specially for them and I tried  it...two thumbs up.

In addition to the food I found all the staff friendly and helpful, there was a good crowd and either free line dancing lessons or live music on the stage all day long. The bar is multi levelled and very spacious.

Highly recommended and worth a visit if you are in Nashville.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Went there after it being recommended by several out of town visitors. It was great, split the sampler platter with a buddy I was down with. It's multi-storied much like the rest of the town. Service: Melody our server was great, attentive and friendly to my very annoying group. Food: OHHHH HELL YEAH! All of it, delicious. Sampler came with some rib, onion rings, kielbasa thingies, and a bunch of other stuff. It was all delicious. I'll be going back if I'm ever in town again. Restrooms were nice and clean too, which is rare for a bar on a strip. Enjoy!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Slow service but the ribs are awesome! the music and atmosphere are what you would picture Nashville to be.  Combine the two BBQ sauces for perfection.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: The house bbq sauce is delicious! Gotta try it on the brisket sandwich :D everything made from scratch here and the live music is awesome! Definitely recommend this place

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The new Wildhorse is only surviving off its old reputation. It is a shell of its former self. Smaller menu, higher prices and horrible service. I am curious if management has changed as well. All of the servers appear to be if not disgruntled then unhappy. The building is still very cool and a must see for anyone visiting. I would order a drink and then find another place to go.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great location for groups. We had the 3rd floor to ourselves. Fooseball, shuffle board and pool. Great food - awesome salad bar, pulled pork sliders, fries, ribs, s'mores (with real fire!), fried pickled and even chocolate covered bacon! We learned how to line dance and listened to a live band. It was a great night out!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Would you like some good Ribs with Live Music?  Then stop at Rippy's.  If you are a soda drinker you may feel like a Second Class Citizen.  The liquor drinkers our waiter were served like First Class Citizens.   Annoying.  We had to flag him down to stop at out table why he had stopped at the liquor drinker table five times.  They were less just across the aisle.

       There are Two Floors and they both had a 'Live Band'.  

         This restaurant is across from the Bridgestone Arena and just down the street from the Ryman Theatre.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Came here on vacation with friends. We were watching a football game and the band began to set up. Well, we discussed this with management and informed them January 1 is a big day for games! We are mid game wnd about 40 people are here for the game NOT the band- THEN for no reason bc he said "I wonder if the band is aware no one here is here for the band" and the band member turns around and told our friend to GO F YOURSELF!!! You're in a dive bar band and.... Ya most people come for the bar or game and you're here to promote yourself. Get used to it.. Youre small town. Ugh, So rude! The band here "Brian James" has a long haired dude that is a complete DouchE! Beware of this terrible band. Otherwise the bar and food were fine.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I got the chicken tenders and fries, the tenders were pretty good but they will probably be better if you get them a little well done. The fries were good but would be better if they were hand-cut nothing is better than hand-cut fries at a BBQ place. Our service was fast and good! Would recommend!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Dropped in and had the chicken fried steak girlfriend had the Shrimp and Grits ..  Dessert was the Nash House Pie...  our server Amy was great!    The service was was and got to meet Andy the manager... We will be back

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This place is fine. Like most restaurants/bars on Broadway, it was a fun environment with live music. I would come back for the music, especially because the volume levels were good. Not too loud, but I could hear well. They're getting dinged on food. The Mac and cheese tastes like Stouffers. They put their meat through a smoker, which is good, but the taste was a bit strong for me. Come for the drinks or the ribs -- best friend's dad got them and fell in love.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
My friend and I went to Rippy's while waiting for a bar crawl to begin. We got there before 9 and were somehow able to snag a table.

The top level is an amazing - open air bar with seating and an artist almost always playing. The band while we were there were great! They played all covers and the mostly inebriated people would get really into most songs. Cue Wagon Wheel! And yes, the place is full of overserved people but what was interesting to me was it was people of shapes, sizes, sorts and ages - including groups of friends, couples, and families. Rippy's seems to be the place for everyone. 

Beers are mega expensive. More expensive than other places on Broadway for the same beers. However even with that, I had one of my more enjoyable Broadway experiences here because of the music, open air and actually being able to get a seat for an hour.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Stopped in to do some shopping listen to music and get another drink all this walking the wife is having me do is driving me to drink.

name: Twin Kegs
text: About my favorite place in my neighborhood now. I have watched this place blossom. Have gone through some personnel changes but have a really friendly staff. Drawing a more diverse crowd than when I first started going. Beer selection has expanded big time. And you hear the cliche "best burger in town" alot. But this place truly lives up to that billing

name: Nashville Palace
text: I can't do zero stars but this place is so unforgiving and anti freedom. If you have a confederate flag don't come here. General Lee is next door but don't exploit your freedom here. The band was amazing the service was fabulous but the management will will stifle your group activity. Visiting from Cali. Californians and free thinkers, this is not your stop. Kristen was the only bright star here.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Is this my favorite Nashvegas spot? Could be based on my past experiences. Two bands, one cutting up with Merle Haggard... Drinking @lagunitas..yup my favorite #ipa and bar!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Food options are as reviewed previously. Lots of fat, salt, cheese, etc. I ended up choosing the grilled veggie plate, which had a nice variety of different things, but was a little oily and salted. Service was fine. Tables are pretty close together. We went very early (5) and it was half-empty, so we didn't experience the crowded, loud part of the deal. Table liked the spicy fried pickles (you can order all pickles instead of sampler), steak, trout. I won't rush to go back based on ambience or food. The "speakeasy" (sigh) downstairs looked like a cool space, but it's hard to get into it when you're in a strip mall off Franklin Pike.

name: Tin Roof
text: The queso is a must have, gotta have!!!! We ate it with chips, put it on our sandwich, pizzadilly, and everything!!!! OMG amazing!!  Service was a little slow, prices were moderate

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Hands down one of my favorite places on Broadway. Although it's just a hole-in-the-wall, it's a great bar environment - especially before a Preds game (if you wear Preds gear, you'll get a free beer ticket). $6 Natty pitchers, fun bands, and spectacular service makes for a great time. The food is pretty good too.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Food-
Normal bar food, nothing special. 
HOWEVER: get the sweet potato fries and you won't be disappointed. I like to call them "crack fries" yes they are that good. 

Music-
The best sounds I've heard! You have to go at least once!

**SO worth the wait, if you can't get a reservation a week in advance to sit at a table be prepared to wait outside an hour to an hour and a half prior to show time to ensure your seat at the bar or in a pew.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: From the moment we walked in we felt like we were home. Great food, atmosphere and staff. This place steeped in history as a counter where sit ins occurred in 1960. The hostess's parents actually were at the sit ins. Wonderful experience!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: My wife, I and our wheelchair bound daughter went to the Bluebird for the first time last night for the Monday night "Open Mic".  Although we had the obligatory wait outside for over an hour before they opened, it was actually enjoyable and gave us a chance to speak with and hear the stories of musicians and others who had come from all over the United States and beyond to visit Nashville and the Bluebird. The Bluebird staff of Elliott, Britton, John and others were absolutely fantastic. They checked on us outside periodically and got us in out of the rain and seated as soon as they could. Although the small 85 seat room was packed, the service was very good, the drinks very reasonable and the beer extra cold.  We did not order any food, so can't speak to that.  There was no cover charge or minimum expenditure for the 6:00 open mic show, and the show was quite enjoyable - certainly can't beat that!  By the end of the night, we were on a first name basis with the staff and many others who were there.  Certainly an evening well spent. Highly recommend it to others.  Recommend that you do your research regarding the procedure for the night of the week you plan to go (as they all differ) and follow it carefully. Get reservations if you can and be sure to arrive extra early to be safe. Enjoy your memorable evening at the Bluebird and say hello to Elliott, Britton, John and the gang for us.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Loved this spot! Definitely my favorite bar in downtown. Came here on my first night in Nashville and had a great time. Being a fan of rooftop patios, this place was a must and the views of downtown are great. It is multileveled and has live music on each of the levels. Only downside was how packed the rooftop was when we were there. Ps... The moonshine is strong- watch out!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: By far my favorite honky tonk bar in Nashville.   The staff were great and the live music was even better.

name: Tin Roof
text: I decided to get the sandwich named after the place. It was the first time I had a peanut butter and chicken sandwich. It was great. No idea it could be done and I was definitely surprised. They have mastered this combination and if you're curious about the Tin Roof special you should definitely check it out.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text: What an amazing place! First time here. Big heart's for change. Plus 20 different coffees to choose from and great sandwiches. All their profits go to ending poverty around the world. I will visit here every time I'm in green hills. Check them out!

name: Tin Roof
text: Really enjoyed this bar. Bartenders are attentive and fast and make a great drink. Band was awesome and the atmosphere was great, my entire group had a really great time. Those who wanted to dance could dance and those that wanted to chill had room to do so. I also loved that the band didn't just play country music like every other bar on Broadway. Great bar, I will go back when I'm back in town.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Loved everything about this place. From the moment you walk in there's a fun energy throughout the 3 floors of this bar/restaurant/live band venue. The bar is great and the food options are pretty good. But I think a lot of people go here for the historical significance more than the food 

With such a rich history in country music, you've got to visit this spot if you're anywhere near Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: By far the best Honky Tonk in Nashville.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Fun atmosphere, cheap food, cheap drinks. Worth stopping in, although - like most spots on broadway - not worth staying all night.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This was probably one of the funnest bars I've ever been to! I loved that it had 3 levels with a different band on each! So fun to go to and listen to live music. I also was a huge fan of the rooftop bar overlooking downtown Nashville and the rest of Broadway. 
This place was also very dirty though. It's not one of those bars that I would bring a child into to listen to live music, I would only go here if I was with my friends. 
I will be back though because it was so much fun!!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I'm a huge fan of the show "Nashville" and it was a dream come try to get tickets to the elite Bluebird. Yes the process of getting tickets is awful and difficult, but once inside it is worth it. Food and drinks are very good. Staff is friendly and helpful. The atmosphere is very welcoming and it is great to see new songwriters. I could spend every night in here if possible!! Can't wait to return for a third time(: Hopefully I'll run into "Deacon" one day there (:

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsie's is always a great time!! With three floors of music, you can move around just to hear a different band play. The best part is that each floor still seems pretty intimate so you feel like you're really jamming out with the performers! They try to get you involved which is nice compared to the other bars that have one band and a huge dance floor. Yes beers are a $1 or 2 more expensive here than at other bars but it's worth it to me because I think they have some of the best acts. And you never know which celebrities can pop up on stage!

name: Tin Roof
text: Won't be back. Was very disappointed...they took up chairs at 1047. I went to the bathroom and the guy took up m chair...as my friend was sitting there and my beer was right I front of my table. I could understand if it was packed and they wants to keep the flowing but it wasn't.  They made the people next to us get out of their chair. Im confused???

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: I cannot say enough about Rachel and the staff working tonight. I have never been to a bar that started out with 20 people and turned into 120 and the bartender executed her duties as diligently and as balanced as she could behind a bar by herself. Watching her fill pitchers and serve shots at the same time while calming the natives was nothing short of phenomenal. I would recommend this bar and Rachel to anyone who has patience and can see the momentous amount of hard work and dedication it takes to be an amazing bar tender. I cannot say enough about Rachel and her bar skills. We're from small town Ohio and she made us feel right at home from the first moment we arrived.

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text: Terrible venue.  Hard to see stage. Worst venue I've ever been too.  Paid $50 for lawn seats and for a show that starred an hour earlier than advertised. At least the sound is decent.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Just went here for drinks (prior to dinner). It was OK. The place was pretty dead but I'm sure it's a hot spot at nights. Customer service was not bad, bartender was nice and drinks were fine. But that's all I can really say. One thing I wasn't a huge fan of was when I was there, at the bar, the garage or windows were open and people were smoking outside -- I could definitely smell it while hanging out at the bar indoors. 

Can't say much about the food, didn't have anything.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
It's really sad to say that I will not be coming back here for their food. It just doesn't taste good. I've been here at least 4-5 times and I am always disappointed. I only come because they are the only
Place in this side of town that has a happy hour until 7.

The ambiance is really nice. I love sitting at the bar and their cocktails are pretty good. So cocktail wise, it's great! But man, their food is not good at all. 

So come here during happy hour to drink since the ambiance is so cool! But that's it. Don't come here hungry.

name: Tin Roof
text: I've been to the Tin Roof in Charlotte, NC many times, so it was kinda fun to go to the actual Tin Roof - as I imagine this was the original.  It looked identical to the one in NC.  It was fun, good music, dancing, busy yet still places to sit down and converse.  I'd come back for sure.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The only reason this bar is not slammed on a Saturday night is because the service sucks.  Literally disappointed everytime.  Leroy Powell is the only reason we come here. Amazing music, poorly managed.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Absolutely yummy buffalo strips!  Flaherty and got and the handcut fries were great also!  Love the trailer park theme and three live band was really funny. It's great that you can go to the restaurant area listen to the music but still have a conversation

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsies definitely lived up to its famous reputation! Great cover band playing on this Sunday night. The bar was jam packed with a lively crowd, and the singers gave a great finale singing and dancing up on the bar.

name: The Stone Fox
text: John was really great. He was friendly, attentive, and probably cool with the Oxford comma. I also can't believe the great bands that play there. I really wish I would have bought a house closer so this could be my neighborhood bar. Did I mention the food? So much to choose from and I haven't been disappointed once. I can only hope to get snowed in while visiting so I have an excuse to take up a longer residency.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Was so great for breakfast we went twice. Best sweet potato pancakes hands-down ever had in my life. Hope I can replicate them at home. Service was top-notch. If you're from the north and you remember the old Woolworth store and diner counter this is just like it. Surprisingly great experience what a fab find

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
This is a hard review for me, because The Sutler has such highs and lows. 

The highs? 

1. Great happy hour. Upstairs (The Saloon): M-F 3-7 - 1/2 off draft beer, wines by the glass, and signature cocktails. Downstairs (The Cellar): W-F 5-7 - 1/2 off draft beer, wines by the glass, and signature cocktails. Downstairs (The Cellar): W 7-10 - 2 for 1 wines by the glass. Also - the Cellar is pretty big, so it's not as crowded during happy hour as lots of other places in Nashville (where you walk in at five and half the tables are taken)!

2. Good drink selection. Good beers on tap. Good cocktails. 

3. Decor. Especially downstairs in the Cellar, the Sutler is really cool. Comfy couches, big chairs. Definitely a great place for happy hour with a lot of people (I've gone with groups of 7+ and we can always find seating). 

The lows?

1. The parking. It used be bad (when you could park behind the McD's and walk over), and now it's even worse. With all of the construction and building on 8th, they have about 40 spots for The Sutler, Sinema, and everything else in that shopping center. If you're going after 4, good luck. (I have Fridays off, so I went at 3 last week and parking then was a breeze.)

I haven't ever eaten, so I can't speak to the quality of the food. The menu looks pretty typical Southern (burgers, fried chicken sandwich, steak sandwich, tacos, nachos, queso, meatloaf, but they have a salad or two if you're looking for something a bit lighter. 

I'd also like to try out the Bluegrass Brunch sometime (Saturday and Sunday 10-3). 

If it weren't for the insane parking situation here, this would probably be a four-star review for the happy hour alone. Seriously, where else in Nashville does the happy hour last until 7 and has plenty of seating? Nowhere, that's where.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Ein muss für alle Nashville Serien Fans.Ist bloß etwas schwierig Karte zu bekommen zumal man von Deutschland aus bei der Zeitverschiebung gut planen sollte. Mit dem Onlineausdruck aber unproblematisch.
Es ist eine sehr spezielle Club Atmosphäre.Wir hatten nur Getränke weil die Veranstaltung um 9 pm losging.Aber alles ok

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Music was awesome. Food was hot and tasty. Pretty much self-service after you get your food and they leave you be which is nice. It was a nice place to grab a quick bite and it was quieter than the other restaurants near by. Wait was only a few minutes and staff was decently friendly. We would stop by again. Decor was ok but nothing special.

name: Tin Roof
text: Went in prior to the bowl game and it was the wrong Tin Roof. However we're glad we stopped in. Ladies working were very nice and helpful. Tried the hot wings and chicken quesadilla. The wings were very good and my wife liked the quesadilla. Would be a regular if I lived in Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Came to Tootsie's for a bachelorette party bar crawl. Despite it being a larger bar with 3 levels, it was still incredibly crowded!? We were wading through crowds to move around, to the bar, from the bar, away from the bar. 
Aside from that, it has live music, which is always fun. The bands playing that night were fun, and we spent most of the time on the third floor. It was annoying though that they said that it was $20 to make a request...seems a bit steep. The venue itself is a total dump. The floor is sticky and grimy. I didn't end up paying for any of the rounds of drinks at this location, so I can't comment on the price, but it seemed have a a lackluster selection of drinks: mostly cheap beers and well drinks. 
The bouncers were also a bit annoying. They opened up the patio area behind the band, but were oddly (and obnoxiously selective) about who could go to the patio. We were standing on the raised area besides the roped off patio area, and they told us that we had to step away. However, there was a couple standing beside us, also outside of the roped off area, and they were allowed to stand there...seems a bit arbitrary. The clientele also was a bit obnoxious. They seemed completely oblivious -- and even a bit rude -- to people trying to pass through. I know that it can be a bit annoying, but just be courteous and move out of the way so people carrying drinks can get by...
Overall, it was fun and part of the quintessential-Nashville experience, or so I'm told, but I don't think that I'd go back if I visited Nashville again. It's a one-and-done deal for me: been there, done that, and it's time to explore some place else.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Cool hangout. Food is nice craft burger style. Interesting flavors from local goods . The Stone Fox burger was nice. Overall the experience was nice for a weeknight. I will go back

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Great brunch on Saturdays, the food and atmosphere are great.  Friendly staff, great wait staff.  Loved the Nashville Hayriders, get them back!

name: Riverfront Park
text:
Not to be confused with Y-Front Park which is where I usually run around in my underwear.

This beautiful rark in Nashville is right by the river. You never would have guessed that from the name right? 

It's absolutely gorgeous and spectacular with massive Bridges spanning the water and even a pedestrian bridge in the middle of it. You can see the huge imposing Stadium right across from the park, and it basically is situated in the area at the very end of Lower Broadway when you get down to the river. You will not find many parks with such beautiful urban and natural scenery combined. If it was a little bit more well-lit and safer at night I would give it a 5.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Place is terrific, the food is decadent and delicious.  The fish was my favorite, but burgers were very good too.   I particularly liked the music teach of the Saturday nighs I wentt.  Glad to see the old Melrose area coming alive.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I don't get why this place is so dang popular.  It's ok but I've been to better rooftop bars with live music before.  It's got a cool view of the strip so worth checking out the upstairs patio.  The live music acts are pretty alright and there are about 3 stages.  This place gets soooooo crowded that it's not enjoyable after awhile.  Drinks are mediocre and it's kind of dirty.  But you gotta visit there once to see it and then move on to other cool bars on the strip.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Rude bartenders there. They look bored and don't make you feel welcome. Just horrible!  Wanted to get the first time experience, but very disappointing.  Note to owner:  too much competition out there to let this happen.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Fun bands. Games. Multiple bathrooms. Multiple bars. They serve food on the other side of the building. Huge place and awesome for a Saturday night party

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Waited in line 3 hours tonight to catch the 9:30 show.  IT WAS WORTH EVERY MINUTE. Don Schlitz was on stage and was joined by some random "union" picker.  Mr. Schlitz put on a heck of a show and the picker just might have a future in Nashville. 

Special shout out to Joe Salvo.  He is professional, good natured and one great doorman, as well as, being the most "photo bombed" doorman in Nashville.  Also props to Vonda ---- quick, professional and efficient service. 

The baked Brie was awesome. 

Folks -- the "picker" was Vince Gill. The Blue Bird Cafe is a must see.  I can't put it any other way.  I just can't think of where else you can see such superstar talent (Mr Schlitz and Mr Gill) for only $12 in such an intimate setting.  

We stayed in Nashville (on our way home to Texas) because we wanted to see the Blue Bird Cafe ----- it was sooooo worth it and I am so glad we did. 

Also, I am happy to know that the reservation system is improving.  The current system is a bit of a pain (back to waiting 3 hours in a stand by line), however, they are fixing it.  

I can't wait to come back on my next trip to Nashville.

name: Throwbacks Bar & Grill
text: LOVE this place! The food is OUTSTANDING!! I can be a picky eater and everything I have tried on their menu is fabulous. I live in Atlanta, and frequent Nashville and this place is ALWAYS on my must to do list! For food I would suggest the wings.. I have never had better.. the sauce and the way they are cooked is incredible! The chicken salad wrap and the fried mushrooms were among my favorites to! They almost always have a live band on the weekends which is a plus. The owner Steve is always there, and pays special attention to making sure everyone is having a great time! A go to place if your in town looking for a relaxed bar.. ( the drink specials don't hurt either :)

name: The Stone Fox
text: If this business was more geared toward customer satisfaction than assuring that they maintain a hipness that included aloof, rude,  and incompetent staff, I might enjoy it. I've sent many friends who've visited Nashville there, and always hear that the food is mediocre and overpriced. I didn't even get as far as the food because of how incredibly unfriendly the staff was when just trying to have a drink. Will never go again, nor would I ever recommend it.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: First off, the service was horrible. The waitress was extremely rude, and we had to get up and ask for things like silverware, napkins, etc. because she didn't bring these things to the table, or come to check on us. On the other hand, the food was great. So we had fried okra and pickles which were tasty! Also had macaroni and cheese with chicken. Delicious! I enjoyed the local music night.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: A must stop for all when In Nashville as a tourist.  It's more for the history and live music than anything else.  It's the perfect place to end the night as most of the older tourists were there and gone.  the prices aren't bad depending on what you're used to.  Some of the reviews mention it's tourist trap, well unless you live in Nashville you're a tourist too, and a trip to Nashville isn't complete without a stop at Tootsie's.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Ummm this place has beer. There's not much more to say. It's cheap -ish, it's very divvy, you can write on the table if you're bored, and the night I was there they had some mediocre live music. I'm not sure I would eat here, but if you want cheap beer, this is your place.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
First time here.  Good start upon arrival...pleasant server and came to the table quickly.  Ordered drinks and reviewed the menu.  Server offered some good suggestions.  Unfortunately, we then waited 40+ minutes before our server finally came to the table and said they'd lost our ticket.  They said the meal was comped and would come out quickly, but others continued to get their food.

Food was good and I like the atmosphere, but wouldn't rush to go back.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Burger was really good. Bun to meat ratio a little off. Meat was seasoned well and good quality cheese.  A/C was cold inside. Staff friendly.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Okay, so as a tourist, I HAD to go to Tootsie's, right? 

I tried to go at a quiet time, but apparently that time doesn't exist. The crowd was huge and the space is small, which led to many uncomfortable moments since everyone seemed to have been overserved. The band, of course, made up for the discomfort and played a slew of popular hits, and the crowd couldn't get enough.

All in all, I'm so happy I went, but I probably won't return.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I would not recommend Sutler to anyone at all. We went in on a Monday night and the restaurant had only a few tables filled up. Our service was terrible - it took close to 20 minutes to get the drinks that we had ordered and about that same amount of time for the server to return and take our order. The appetizers we ordered came out with our meals. The meals were not good at all. My fiancé ordered the trout and was not prepared to spend the rest of the evening picking bones out of his meal before he could eat it. Several at the table also ordered the "grilled veggie plate" which turned out to be mostly grilled lettuce with a roll of thyme on top that was still on fire. No one finished their meals due to the appeal and taste. It took us approximately another 20 minutes to find our server and check out. Mind you this place was NOT anywhere close to busy. I was extremely disappointed.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsie's is a Nashville staple and somewhere you should visit if you are doing the tourist thing on Broadway. I really like that they have added a rooftop bar area with live music and drinks. But eeesh. When I was there with out of town guests it was packed to the gills and they were only letting people go up if others were coming down. 

This now creates 3 levels of music which is nice, but man. Overall it's just so crowded that it can be difficult to enjoy the scenery. But... get there early and I'm sure it is much more enjoyable!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I REALLY want to like the Sutler. They have done a great job with the decor and I love the downstairs bar.We live in walking distance to this establishment, so I was very happy to see The Sutler reopen.  We have visited the Sutler at least 6 times, and each time find the staff to be on the "high-falutin'"  side (thats a nice way to say snobby).  We recieved better treatment at the OLD Sutler!  On our last visit, my 3 friends approached the upstairs bar at the same time, and once they got the attention of the bartender, was told by her "I need some breathing room". I suppose we had to wait for her to find her Zen before we could order drinks. Since there are no cocktail waitresses for the bar area, several of us in our party of sat without drinks for at least 30 minutes. Having been in the service industry a very long time, I looked around and saw other tables with empty glasses. Lots of lost revenue. This place needs some trained professionals behind the bar and hostesses that are not rude. The downstairs is great, but no one is in a rush to serve you if you sit at the bar. Too many garnishes to prep, I suppose. Other reviewers have commented that the staff is dismissive - We have had that experience as well.  I wish the Sutler would get it together - it may be growing pains but if you want my business and  more importantly for the high falutin' staff, my tip, you are going to have to earn it from now on.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Warm beer. Okay music. Too crowded too early and the bands in different sections blended together. Not all it was chalked up to be! Had much more fun at several of the other bars

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Best stopping place for a beverage in Nashville. Service is hard to get, cause they are so busy. But for a great watering hole, Don't miss this well located bar. Go to the rooftop...

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I'm so disappointed in this place! I went to Nashville on vacation and when I found out that there was a bar that was purple I was so excited to check it out. We weren't let in two nights in a row due to a backpack (okay that maybe understandable) and then for having a camera. This place is not tourist friendly.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I came here for a reunion event

The Good:
So I really liked the feel of this place - it has a very speak easy vibe to it and it was great for socializing in groups (the basement was of course super spacious) and there were plenty of great sofas to take advantage.

I also really liked the the glasses they served things with and their great drink selection.

The Bad:

- Parking for this place is a nightmare
- Definitely need more staff to help out (I only got drinks and that was an ordeal)
- The outside has horrible decorating - if I didn't know better this was a weird shop on a strip mall.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Excellent venue.  Small intimate performances but some really really talented musicians.  Space is limited and getting a comfortable seat will benefit your night.  Nice drink menu.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Not a huge fan of Stone Fox as a "music venue". Bartenders seemed nice, but made sure to take care of the regulars first.

name: Tin Roof
text:
Pretty cool place to grab a bite and some beers and listen to live music or watch sports!

Vegetarians, they have some options for us: cheese dip, cheese fries, jalapeno poppers, salsa, guac, three different kinds of quesadillas (and you could probably vegetarian-ize any of the pizzadillas), three sandwiches (pb&b, grilled cheese, and a veggie sandwich), and salads!  

Happy hour is Monday - Saturday, 2-7, with some pretty good deals!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
I give the venue 4 stars and their food 3. The restaurant itself is cool. It's very relaxed and there's a stage so they probably play music at night.

Came here for a Sunday brunch. Got there around 10:50 and there was already a wait. we got seated around 11:15 and left around 12:30. By the time we left, there was still a line waiting to get seated. Advice: call ahead of time.

I had biscuit with jam and added fried chicken with it. Honestly, it was okay. Nothing special. They didn't have anything on their menu that was unique. 

It's not a bad place. Decent food. Decent service. If I knew I had to wait longer than 30 mins, I would go somewhere else.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: We really enjoyed the food and atmosphere here. The live music was pretty good. Jenn the bartender was fun. I had the grilled cheese and my wife had the 5 alarm burger. Both were delish. The tots were pretty good. It was not crowded but we were here in the middle of the afternoon. Good place to eat for cheap with good food and service.

name: Tin Roof
text:
Tin Roof became a go-to lunch spot for the BEST CHICKEN TENDERS IN ALL OF NASHVILLE. No foolies. The accompanying crinkle fries are just divine.

The service is pretty good overall, although there is a completely incompetent and rude b that works on Fridays and is usually on the new side. Brunette, ponytail, sour expression: avoid her at all costs.

The quesadillas are also amazing (the shrimp is very bland, so can't recommend that one). The Shroom is probably my favorite, but the Buffalo is good, too.

Do not order the nachos: TR does not have any ovens in the kitchen, so it's cold ingredients on chips. That ain't nachos, people! The hubs and I ordered them once and sent that sorry sh*t back.

Went to TR once at night, on a Friday. I was told it got stupid busy by 11, and that is a minor understatement. The crowd is young (I am not), so let that be your guide.

Again, best chicken tenders in town, if that's your thang.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place was packed. It has three different levels and great music. The drinks weren't too expensive and it was a lot of fun talking with the members of the band who came around to chat. They were taking all kinds of requests and wanting input from the crowd. The bartender was nice and always looking out for us when our drinks were almost gone.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Awesome spot and not terribly expensive! The staff is REALLY what makes this place! You feel at home when you walk in and are grated by there hosts. Sandwiches are fab, filled chicken salad is awesome. The soups are bomb!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Bouncer put a crack in my legitimate drivers license by bending it back and forth, then told me it was a fake because it had a crease. I asked him to stop bending it (Maryland ID does not bend) and presented him with a credit card with my name and my teaching ID, both of which he ignored. Cop verified that it was real and let me in, no apology from the bouncer. I will be writing a letter to the manager and asking to be reimbursed for the cost of replacing my ID.

Update: the manager reached out to me the next morning and did agree to reimburse the cost of a new ID. He was very apologetic and agreed that the bouncer had used excessive force when bending it.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
We had a total of 12 people visiting for Christmas and they requested a downtown day. I figured it would be difficult to make a reservation for 15 people during the holiday weekend but we were lucky enough to snag a table at Woolworth's. Parking was easy and they had our table prepped and ready on arrival.

Service was a little slow, but that was to be expected with such a large table. Fortunately, the food was still hot. 

We are a difficult crew to feed with vegatarians and one member with severe food allergies but everyone was able to find something and most everyone liked their food. The most popular and well-liked dish was the sweet potato pancakes.

Woolworth's also provides a nice jumping point for a downtown tour. When you exit the restaurant, you can walk through the arcade and then past some of the newer hotels like Noelle and Bobby. You can then turn to walk through Printer's Alley before making your way to Broadway. 

Great location, great food.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place rocks ! 3 levels of bars & music ! Friendly servers music is live and rocks! No cover charge this place is creative & fun let your hair down spot ! Performers are great .

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I get it and agree with the history and the music and all that. My only suggestion is close it for a couple of days and give it a good cleaning. It was a dump when we were in there with garbage on the floor... To be fair we were there on a busy Saturday night in August so prime time. I do think they can do a smart renovation, to keep the history in the walls and charm, so they can get rid of the 4x8 sheets of poorly installed plexiglass everywhere. Ole Red and Kid Rocks' place are just as fun, but modern and clean...

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
So, this one felt kind of like a tourist trap, but I actually left feeling really pleased with my meal and experience!

We ended up at Woolworth's for dinner with a group on Friday night. We had initially wanted to grab dinner in a trendy section of town but after being quoted crazy long wait times, we got on Open Table to see what our options were. We were able to snag a table for 5 at Woolworth's in 15 minutes.

When we arrived, there were only 4 other tables dining here. Not a great sign for a Friday night. Also, the place is huge since it used to be a department store, so the size of the space made it look even more empty.  The man who sat us was really friendly, and our server was also great.

The history of the place is really interesting and they include a print out so you can read about it which I really appreciated. 

After we ordered drinks, the server came back around and checked on us. Myself and a friend had ordered the Parlor Punch which I was a huge fan of. It had a huge sprig of rosemary in it to offset the sweetness of the prosecco topper and I just thought it was a really interesting and refreshing cocktail. Our server checked on the two of us specifically because she'd been getting mixed reviews of the drink and said it was either a love it or hate it thing. While I loved it, my friend didn't care for it. Our server insisted he swap it out for something he'd prefer even though he gladly would've taken the hit and finished it. She brought him a sangria and he was thrilled. I really appreciated not only checking back on us but insisting on doing whatever it took to ensure we enjoyed our meal to the fullest. Major kudos for that.

I had the short rib pot roast which was really delicious. The short rib was perfectly tender and fell off the bone by the forkful. It was atop a bed of mashed potatoes and green beans, both of which were okay. I had a few bites of my boyfriend's patty melt which was also quite good, as were the fries. Two of our guests had the meatloaf and they said it was really good. I will say that our friend who had 2 appetizer plates as her meal was not as thrilled with her choices, but those of us who ordered entrees were quite pleased.

Overall my expectations were pleasantly exceeded. Service was truly above and beyond in the hospitality department and we were able to enjoy a solid, southern meal for probably 1/2 the price of the places we had been trying to go that night.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I have not eaten yet but our server is wearing a Trump 2020 hat while working at a historic touch stone for black history.  I am very uncomfortable having this man serve us. We are a big group and they are putting a 20% tip to a man who supports our president who has demonstrated bigotry

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Free Brad Paisley concert! Great music before and after the show - he even bought the crowd beer!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Loved every minute of this place. Great vibes, and good atmosphere. 
Mo, my bartender, was sweet and professional and on point the entire time I was visiting. Excellent drinks!  Every drink she made was more delicious than the next. Mixed perfect and delivered with a smile every time!  Thanks Mo for all the great recommendations from off the menu and also for around town!

Give this girl a damn raise!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Felt very much like a tourist trap. Way too crowded and nowhere to sit. There are other, better places in town if you want live music. It is worth a stop because of the history though.

name: Tin Roof
text: Didnt try the food so I cant rate this place based off that, but loved the atmosphere and live music. Everyones friendly, no cover. highly recommend!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Coolest bar on Broadway Street. You could spend the whole day at this location going up and down three floors listening to live music. The rooftop bar is pretty epic as well. It's absurdly crowded most of the time but well worth the experience and vibe.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Went in for the bluegrass brunch. I can definitely understand some of the complains about parking, because with the spaces it shares from the nearby businesses, you had better be prepared to park a little way's away. None of that is a serious obstacle (if you're used to city parking), but plan accordingly, and I can definitely see why it would be tricky to get in here late at night.

Once you're in, I can see why this place is a community institution. There's a goodly amount of seating, the music is very enjoyable, the menu is affordably priced, the food tastes good, there's a nice drink menu, and the service is damned prompt. One of the things that struck me was that we were taken care of by multiple servers, meaning that they all just look for what needs doing it and do it (I'm hoping they share tips, too; they earned them). The biscuit benedict was extremely tasty, as was my girlfriend's chicken fried chicken biscuits. The bottomless mimosa was appropriately bottomless (I think they refilled it something like six or seven times) and there's a substantial whiskey menu to pick from as well. All of the brunch entrees seemed to hover in the $9-$14 range, and while the drinks were a little bit pricier, not unjustifiably so.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The staff is so quick and friendly, the music was awesome too. Can't wait to come back!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Do not go.  Rudest waitress I have ever encountered. As I stood up to walk away because she scared my daughter, another waitress told us she is like that all the time. She threw menus at us, slammed down the water. The manager simply said he could give us another table. He didn't look too shocked either.  Why keep someone employed working there who is actually harassing and mean to your clientele.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Visiting from Michigan and we had a blast! Fun to see so much history on the walls. It ended up getting too crowded for us on a Thursday night. However, the waitstaff was really awesome and attentive.

name: Tin Roof
text: The band member told my younger sister to take her shirt off. I will never be returning.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: The filet special was absolutely delicious - 6 oz filet covered in savory bearnaise sauce over sausage and potatoes. They give you huge, shareable portions. Recommended!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I visited "The Sultler" Thursday evening 1/3/19 with 3 other couples after an evening at a comedy show. The experience from the outset was terrible as we walked in and saw a sign that said seat yourself, we proceeded to sit at a table that sat 8 and after 10 minutes no wait staff came to us! We then decided to scrap formal dining and go downstairs to get drinks, play pool and eat finger food. When we got downstairs we approached the bar and watched the bartender while the bar down and ignore us for approximately 5 minutes. My long time friend (30years) went to ask if we could play pool on a table that was open? We were told that there is a list that you sign with your phone number so that staff could inform you when a table was ready. The same pool table was still empty after 5 more minutes! So my friend with his spouse asked a staff member why is this table still empty with a group waiting and as they spoke another table became empty! The staff member told us we had to wait and was extremely short and dismissive towards us, even laughing in amusement and walked away in mid discussion! The obvious thing is all 4 couples were of color (African American) And everyone who was being attended were white! The overall experience was shameful and embarrassing! I would strongly advise you not to spend your hard earned money in this place! They are stuck in an America that is long dead!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Amazing experience! From Iowa and I loved sitting in the roof top and enjoying the sun and a great view up and down Broadway.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Great choice for good food in a little historical spots.  Tried the shrimp and grits and it was fantastic!  Great service at the historic counter.

name: Tin Roof
text: tin/tin Came here for a sorority date party. Reasonable prices for beer. Friendly staff. Bathrooms were clean yet vulgar. 2 ply toilet paper, ample paper towels. Very cold and refreshing water.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I love the Sutler! Between 90's Night on Thursdays to Bluegrass Brunch on the weekend and the weekday Happy Hour this is always a great place to gather with friends for drinks (I recommend the Kentucky Mule) and quality food. The service has always been wonderful and attentive, and they always seem to get great live music performances.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
I had a great time at Tootsie's during our most recent visit to Nashville! We got there around 1pm on a Sunday and headed up to the third floor. The sun was shining and it was a great day with a slight breeze. 

There was a band starting at 1, Lady and the Gents, and they absolutely rocked the place for 5 hours. Getting there around 1pm we were easily able to get a table and we did not move from that spot until 6pm. 

They had the college games on, and the drinks were flowing. I would say the only drawback is that they did not have draft beer and that the drinks were on the expensive side. I can say my wallet did not like Tootsie's. 

Overall a great experience!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Yet another fun stop on the Honkey Tonk Strip! This place has no cover, just like all the other bars on the strip. There are multiple floors, but i ran straight up to the rooftop. It was a fairly cold night, but the heat lamps make it a comfortable place. There is a great view of the strip and Bridgestone arena. The inside just past the doorways to the roof was very crowded, so it was difficult to approach the band to tip them or request a song. People were friendly and having a great time, so it was no big deal to push through. This kinda affected being able to approach the bar as well. However, when I was outside on the rooftop, there was a waitress walking around and taking orders on the floor. There were plexiglass boards on the walls showing who had performed there in the past, very interesting, and a very fun time!

name: Tin Roof
text: Amazing service and live music! Came on a Sunday night and it was awesome! 10/10  @carone

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This was my favorite bar to goto on broadway st. All of the bars have similar pricing so expect it to be $6 beer night at all of the bars in the area. What set this one apart from all the other honky tonk bars on the street was the live bands and atmosphere. This bar is three stories tall with a bar and a live band on all three. We found a nice spot next to the second story band and enjoyed the experience. They were playing country music and even taking requests. The third story also had a balcony that overlooked the whole area. Most of the bars on broadway st. are very similar, but this one is a little notch above the rest. 

~Bmo

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: This place has a cute vibe and great bluegrass music. We came here while visiting for brunch on a Saturday with a group of friends. They do not take reservations so be prepared to wait. Overall, the food was just ok. I tried the biscuit Benedict, a few friends got the shrimp and grits, and my husband tried the hash. The biscuit in the Benedict was hard and the food came out semi cold. The hash potatoes were the same way (cold). The shrimp and grits were apparently amazing tho!

name: The Stone Fox
text: Great neighborhood bar with amazing live music! Good food and good drinks! Cool staff :)

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Okay, I'm perplexed. Cool space, rich history, pretty dang good food...what's missing?  Nothing we had was so special we couldn't get the same somewhere else. The crowd was light but it was a Sunday dinner so the room energy, both staff and diners, was at best, subdued. The wait staff is supposed to encourage and sell the menu at different stages of the meal...drinks, then apps, then entree, then dessert and then the check. I never felt compelled to stay any longer than the entree. We did try a couple of apps but our server brought the entrees before removing any of the used plates and that made for some awkward teamwork to clear and make room for even more plates. Two things they need to work on, timing, attention to detail and representing this place with pride and a higher level of passion. If this doesn't happen Woolworth on 5th is sunk. 
I think they should have returned it to its former glory and capture what it really was, a southern lunch counter instead of some crafty southern gourmet trendy bar restaurant and event space. More chrome, sweet waitresses in dresses, southern style plates, amazing pies and coffee, a place to gather, a place to meet up and dine. Woolworth is none of that in all its redefined trendiness.. a little more authenticity rather than austerity would go a long way in making it successful for the long haul.  Right now it's just another trendy restaurant in a town full of them...and it's clearly not the leader.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: This place was great. We went with a group for a friends birthday and they were very accommodating and the food and drinks were great. Above all of that our server, Keena was maybe the best server we have ever had. EXCELLENT.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
When coming back to Nashville I try to avoid the touristy spots and attractions. My boyfriend had never been before so on this last visit we hit many of those said spots and it was actually fun. With that said, I've never considered Tootsie's touristy. I mean of course it is but it's also a local institution, iconic  and legendary.

A really fun place to relax, have a beer and enjoy some of Nashville's finest local performers. Employees (including the bartenders) work for tips only so it's important to be generous.

This honky tonk is epic and a must visit whether you're a tourist or a Nashville regular. Always a good time.

name: Tin Roof
text:
***Tin Roof is an okay casual bar and grill for nearby residents or workers, but there is much better food elsewhere in Nashville that is more reflective of the local cuisine and ingredients***

Tin Roof looks like a garage from the outside with all of the aluminum/metal (lots of aluminum/metal on the inside too), but it is actually a spacious dining establishment for casual food (sandwiches, wraps, pizzas, and quesadillas) and live music.  The restaurant has kind of a kitschy feel with all kinds of retro decoration on the walls (not sure if the decoration is authentic or not).  There is even a Breathalyzer on the wall.  At lunch, Tin Roof draws a young, hip and casual downtown Nashville crowd. 

As mentioned, the restaurant features casual food.  It is American bar and grill food with mostly bar and grill ingredients integrated with each plate of food (even quesadillas and pizzas).  Tin Roof appears to specialize in sandwiches and they have a great variety of them including standard, found-everywhere sandwiches like an Italian sub and a turkey club as well as more hard to find items like a Reuben made with turkey. 

All of their sandwiches can be made into wraps so I took their buffalo chicken tenders sandwich and turned it into a wrap.  The kitchen tosses chicken tenders in your choice of sauce and I opted for the traditional buffalo style hot sauce.  I had them remove the cheese and add lettuce. 

The wrap was good.  It did not feel full enough though.  I would have preferred a tighter wrap with not necessarily more chicken but more crisp and cool shredded lettuce to provide a satisfying contrast to the hot sauce chicken.  Still, the lettuce was fresh and the tortilla was not dry or stale. 

I thought the chicken tenders were nicely prepared.  The batter had a great crunch and was not too heavy.  The chicken itself was moist.  The hot sauce was nothing particularly unique, but it was satisfying enough if you like this type of heat.  They generously applied the hot sauce so it was a hot sandwich.  Ranch sauce was provided on the side for dipping.  I would have preferred a blue cheese sauce, which I think would have been a more satisfying compliment to the chicken.

Sandwiches come with fries, but they are the crinkle cut, Ore-Ida style fries so I had them substituted for tortilla chips and salsa (the menu indicated that their chips and salsa are made fresh everyday).  Unfortunately, I found the chips and salsa to be disappointing.  The salsa did not have much heat or spiciness and while the chips were thin, they had kind of a stale crunch (it might just have been from how the chips were fried).

Service was very pleasant and the food came out quickly.  Unfortunately, servers were hard to track down at times--understandable perhaps given the size of the restaurant and the huge plastic cups used for water, soft drinks and such. 

Prices are reasonable though it is not a significant amount of food served at lunch. 

Tin Roof is a decent and quick lunch spot and a good option for people who work or live in the area.  If you are visiting Nashville though, you might want to seek out other options because there is much better and more local food elsewhere in Nashville. 

I believe free street parking is available.  I do not know if Tin Roof has its own parking lot.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: This is a great place to experience a lot of different things. The atmosphere was very nice and retro. I love the different food selections and even the lunch promotional that they had. The food was seasoned and had good portions. My only change would be to ask for the chicken to not be as fried as much to the point where it is dried out. Definitely worth another visit!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
I was in Nashville to celebrate a birthday and asked my hotel for a recommendation to take a group. Made reservations in advance and received a text alert the day before and day of as a reminder. Great so far.....

Then we got there. Atmosphere was good, place wasn't very full for a Friday night so didn't need to worry about disturbing anyone. But I have to say, we received the absolute worst service I've ever repay a restaurant. The waitress was young and very inexperienced. Took our wine order then disappeared for 10 minutes because we had a question about on if the wines. My group finally flagged another waiter down so they could at least order drinks. 

She finally comes back with two bottles of wine but no wine glasses. Then tells us it took her all that time to determine that they didn't even have the wine we had the question about.

She didn't bus the table hardly at all throughout the entire meal. We finally gathered them up and stacked them in a corner of the table and even that wasn't enough of a clue for her to take them away.

At least the food was ok, but in talking to others after that night, this place is getting a reputation for poor service. With so many other great choices in Nashville I'd recommend you eat somewhere else.

Very embarrassed and disappointed. Suffice it to say, I won't forget this birthday.....

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: So glad we chose Woolworth for a late breakfast. The food was delicious and the staff were attentive. We sat at the counter where, as you will be reminded by the pictures displayed around, others made their mark in history. A "must add" to your list of places to experience while in Nashville!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Wow,First when I walked in it was great with the service. They wanted my money, okay..... How RUDE multiple staff members were to my son because he was eighteen (had nothing to drink) and at the strike of 7:00 out he and all went and we understand the rule, but to be that cruel. We only went to listen to the music and spend time with friends and family. Lost any future business...you suck!!!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: This manager of this restaurant, Woolworth on 5th, who worked the night of December 11, 2019 is discriminatory. I did not get a chance to eat because of how poorly they treated me before I was even able to order. I live at the corner of 5th and Church so I walked there last night wanting to have a boozy milkshake & eat dinner. I was not feeling well all day yesterday and I pretty much stayed in bed all day. I had received some pretty upsetting news earlier that morning so not only was I feeling under the weather but I had spent the day crying. I don't know why this gave the manager the right to tell the waitress not to serve me based on the 5 seconds I had been in the restaurant & the fact that he had not even spoken to me nor did I even see who this person was. The waitress came to my table poured water for the table then asked if I would like anything to drink? I responded, "Yes I would like to try the Affogatto." She then said, how about something else like a juice or something non alcoholic? I responded with, "Why?" She then tells me that her manager told her not to serve me. I'm completely confused now because I have no idea why I could not be served unless the kitchen was closing, but then she interjects with, "You haven't been drinking?" At this point I'm absolutely baffled at why she or anyone would even make this assumption. I respond with "No, why would he even say anything like that?" First of all, I rarely ever drink, and when I do it is normally no more than 2-3 drinks because I do not like the way alcohol makes me feel after any more than that. I did not have anything to drink that day nor the prior 4 days to the date this event happened. I have an alternative style of dressing, so was because of the way I looked any reason to start making assumptions about me? She said she was going to get the manager, but whoever this person is, is not someone I want to waste any of my precious time on this earth on. Not only that but at that point I'm upset about being judged unfairly, so I get up and walk out of the restaurant.  I'm not going to give business to someone who makes a bad decision based on the way a person looks to determine weather or not they are to be served or not. Sorry but my friends & I would rather eat elsewhere then to be subjected to this type of discrimination.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Great Experience

It's not the original Woolworth's (from what I understand) but the history is still present. As a history nerd, this was a definite stop for me while in Nashville. I expected the typical tourist trap but the food was actually quite good. We had a group of six and everyone said their food was good. Not typically the case for a "tourist trap." Service was also very good.

The reason for the four stars is for a few reasons. I think my expectations were tempered thinking it wasn't going to be good, the competition around it with so much great food in Nashville hurts it a little, and the food really wasn't quite at the level of great. I still think it's worth the trip and the stop, especially if you like history like me.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: My friends and I went to Nashville for the weekend and decided to get brunch before we left Sunday. We found The Sutler on google and I'm so glad we did! This place was awesome! We got there about 5 minutes after they opened and that was just in time because it was already full. If we had more than just the 2 of us we would have been waiting a while. Now that I have been there I would do the wait. They have live music and great food. The complementary biscuits were to die for; I could've eaten 20 of them. They also have bottomless mimosas. We opted out because we had drive. I got the beef Benedict and my friend got the avocado toast and I can't say anything bad about either. Delicious, she also got a side of hash browns which I wish I would've gotten instead of the grits. The grits were ok but were a weird consistency for my liking. Not to mention, the place is cute as heck! 12/10 recommend!!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The food is amazing but Kristin and Virginia are the best parts of this place! They work so hard and make sure you're taken care of! We loved them!

name: Tin Roof
text: Don't waste your time coming here to eat. Beer was not cold, server was not at all friendly and the food was sub par. The bar has some cool decor and a decent patio but that's about it.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Came here with friends and their small child. We got a booth by the window in the front one Saturday morning so we could listen to the music. The menu was somewhat limited and our waitress seemed really bothered that she had to take our order and bring us our food. I wouldn't come back. Also, this place seems popular with large parties (like bachelorette parties).

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: No visit to Nashville is complete without a stop in to Tootsie's!  This is the original and it's still serving up drinks with the best of them!  Sure it crowded and loud but that's part of the fun!  We didn't wait long for all our drinks all night!  Great fun and great band.  They've even got a rooftop bar and patio!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: This is where Taylor Swift was discovered. Bluebird is an iconic and legendary Nashville music venue. I really loved it here, the wait can be long to get in and its crowded most nights but you can catch some really great talent playing here. I would recommend this place to anybody visiting Nashville. The staff at the Bluebird are super cool and have a very laid back vibe. I would visit again when I am back in Nashville. Two thumbs up for the Bluebird Cafe, hopefully I catch this place when T Swizzle comes back to Nashville.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Food and service was awesome. Great selection of brunch items. Will definitely go back for the sweet potato pancakes!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Yes, it's a Dive bar- astro turf, plastic cups on the floor, empty pitchers on floor and I even found a wooden bracket on the ground because I stepped on it walking by! The tat tots are good and if you are drunk the food is awesome lol but not bad for a snack of tots or fries:) if you want a packed dive bar with live music GO here! There is only one huge problem for me about this place- the shots (served in small plastic cups) are $8.50!! If you are with three people that adds up fast! This place should have no shots over $6...it's a dirty dive bar!!  The bartenders aren't super friendly but with pitchers of beer selling at 6 bucks - they probably are over it! When I was there I noticed 3 bartenders so it was super easy to get a drink but shocked when I learned three small shots were $30. If you are with a lot of people and you feel like shots find another place- a dump like this serving in plastic cups is not worth it.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
First time in Nashville, wanted to discover all good stuff I heard about this city and bars with live music ...And YES, I confirm that I had a great experience there. They do have multiple stairs with a live band in each...plus a roof deck. I am
Not a real country music fan but I loved it!!! Strongly recommend to hop there and have some good time!!!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Located in a strip mall. Stop in here for a drink before heading out to an event. We had 45 mins to enjoy a drink but it took 30 mins to get our drinks. One of the drinks never came. 
Our waitress seemed overwhelmed. We believe she didn't put our order in until one in our party went and asked her.
3 of the drinks we wanted were not available. They ran out of the beers. It was Friday around 6:00pm.

The music was good. The wall behind the stage is really cool- it made with cowboy boots. 
This place has  potential- the management need to evaluate if there is enough staff to meet the needs of the customers.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Sweet Tea shine with Lemonade was amazing. As was the coffee shine. Brandon and Jennifer were such awesome bartenders. Left with a a new fave ball cap. Loved the chandeliers too. Great place. Must check it out!

name: FooBar
text:
A great dive bar for all the degenerates.
Pool tables, darts, mexican food, flatscreen TVs with DirecTV, and live music and DJs.
Staff is friendly, but they're not gonna put up with anyone being a jerk, either. I like that.
Only things I would like to see improvement with is parking, it's kinda rough, and making some DJs who play there that think the people outside the building need to hear them turn down the volume just a little bit. Gets frustrating to have to scream at each other and say "WHAT?!" back and forth all night at the bar to your buddy sitting on the barstool directly beside you.
Other than that, this is my number one watering hole.

name: The Valentine
text: I first walked in at 4pm on a Sunday afternoon and there was literally no one on the first floor(no band, no guest, and a bartender drinking a beer) we went up to the second floor and no one was there, the third floor had a good amount of people but there was no bartender.... We waited a little and still no one came. It was really awkward

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: If you've not been to The Judge's Vinegarroon in a while, the new management has made a lot of changes, and they are not for the better.  The first thing you'll notice is that their parking lot is chained off.  There is no parking, so come on foot.  You know those amazing chunky, fresh, hand cut french fries they used to serve?  Those have been replaced with thin shoestring frozen fries that aren't nearly as good as McDonald's.  The fried corn on the cob was chewy and cut on the diagonal, which made it pretty, but really hard to hold.  Prices have been substantially raised.  The regular sauce has also been changed.  It's now thin and runny, but I thought the flavor was pretty good.  Fortunately, the beef brisket is pretty much unchanged, and it's still really good.  Unless the new management addresses these unwelcome changes, I wouldn't recommend going here, unless you want to pick up an order of brisket to go.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Fun time. Stopped in for a quick drink. The bartenders were a lot of fun to talk to. I would go back. next time for dinner.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
This was a great hotel and I'm glad we stayed here. We were in town for Yelp Elite spring break and decided to stay here because the downtown rates were crazy expensive. We got a rate of $139 per night before taxes, with the Yelp rate. 

Pros: pool (looked beautiful but we didn't use it), big and nice rooms, lovely lobby. They also have a 24-hour indoor pool and hot tub. 

When we arrived around 330pm, our room was not ready, so the hotel gave us two free appetizer vouchers. 

Cons: I really would have liked at least 1 quick-service place or a place to buy juice or essentials. We mostly ate snack bars for breakfast and headed downtown for lunch and dinner. 

I would definitely stay here again if in the area, it was convenient enough to take Lyft or Uber everywhere.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: This was my first visit to a Hard Rock Cafe and had my doubts, but I was very, very surprised at how good the service and food was. It was my sons choice and we had a great time! Remember this is a very loud very busy place to dine! If you are wanting to kick back and relax this is not the type of restaurant for you! But if loud music and good food are go! My son had the cauliflower burger and raves about it still! While In Nashville I wanted to try Nashville Hot Chicken and this one was flavorful and not to hot! Aleta our server was great and a big shout out to Sam "Stone" for stopping by twice and not only checking on us, but talking to us and making us feel welcome!!!

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Have been here several times always good and good value for the money , but this last time 8-23-14 was very disappointed . The special that was 3 meat choice for 10.00 with large portions went down to 2 meat choice  @ 10.00 and small portions ?? What's wrong with that pic ? Was very disappointed , we won't be back ...

name: FooBar
text: This is a really cool bar. The bartender was nice and did a great job. She was pretty busy but that did not stop her from speaking to people and getting drinks promptly.  If you are looking for a great local place this is it. I will be back.

name: The Bridge
text: Watching live music that was great and our waitress Judy was amazing. Definitely will be back here and hopefully Judy is our waitress again!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Lovely place to stay. Short Lyft drive to Broadway and Opryland. Pool was beautiful and our room was spacious and had a balcony overlooking pool

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Was super excited to see Nashville's Fourth of July fireworks at their rooftop party. But it was not a full viewing of them.  The building obstructed nearly half of the show. Very disappointing.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Nashville is just a fun place to be. The Stage is a lot of fun. Good music, live music, drinks and fun people. The bartenders are quick and the drinks are strong. It's a pretty large venue so is definitely great for bigger groups! I would say this is one of the bars you need to check out when you're in Nashville.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: We absolutely love this place!!!!!!!! Great beer, staff and music!!!!! Can't wait to go back!!!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We had lunch here as we were passing through and the staff were extremely accommodating. We had a large party with a lot of kids in it and not only were they friendly but they were also extremely generous with my children. Great beer on tap made from a local brewery wish I could remember what it was called.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
We had a great time in here! My fiance and I rolled in around 4:30 PM on a Monday afternoon after I heard one of my favorite songs  being covered by the band playing at the time. They were completely solid and we rolled in where we had a quick beer a piece before heading to Jack's BBQ for dinner. 

The Stage, I assume, has to get crazy crowded during the nights, and I can totally see why. They have plenty of table top seating and bar seating where you can sit and enjoy the music being played by what ever band that is serenading the crowd. Drinks are reasonably priced, and not overkill like a lot of the downtown Nashville strip tries to knock up prices. Not Stage though. 

Bathrooms were clean -- I felt that was worth mentioning. 

Anyway, solid place and would love to return for a night out on the town.

name: The Bridge
text:
While staying at the Marriott we stopped here for a late night snack/meal and was pleasantly surprised how nice everything was.
First the all glass atmospher is very cool with a Manhattan/posh style. The serve is also excellent and very friendly.
Got the spicy chicken sandwich which was a little on the small side but decent. We then split the brownie a la mode which was very yummy and filling. 
Bar wise we had a couple glasses of wine. Bar menu isnt huge but everything they have seems to be nice and all speciality drinks made well. 
Overall a nice spot to stop in for an end of the night drink or a quick bite to eat.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
I'm updating my review now because my original review is from four years ago, and a LOT has changed since then. Before it was a solid five stars, but since then, WBS has taken a turn for the worst. The drinks here have always been overpriced, but I tolerated it before because 1) it's downtown, and all the downtown bars are expensive, and 2) the atmosphere, management, and music more than made up for it.
