However, the prices have still increased, even though they were already too high to begin with. Last night, I ordered a Shiner Bock, and it was $6. SIX DOLLARS for ONE beer. I can go to a bar in another area and get a fancy cocktail for that price. Heck, I can go to the grocery store and get an entire six pack for that.

The management has suffered as well. Four years ago, the bouncer always knew my face and didn't need to ID me every time. Now there's a new bouncer who still sees me nearly every Sunday, yet he still has to ID me every time. I understand that they may have changed their policy since then, so I won't knock them too much for that alone, but the bouncer is still incompetent for another reason. A few weeks ago I went in and used my global entry card instead of my driver's license as my ID. I've done my research, and this is an acceptable form of ID under federal and state law, as it's a photo ID issued by the US government. However, the bouncer would not accept this ID. I explained the above to him, yet he didn't believe me. After about five minutes of arguing (I didn't have my DL on me at the time; I'd left it at home), I called a friend who was inside to come out and help me. She's the wife of one of the band members and sees me nearly every week at WBS, so I figured she could talk him into letting me in. It eventually worked...after another 5-10 minutes. But the bouncer said that I had to use my driver's license next time, or he wouldn't let me in. This guy needs to get retrained on what a valid photo ID is. Now I'm wondering if people without a driver's license can get in with a passport or a state ID. If not, I feel sorry for them.

The bouncer isn't the only incompetent employee here. When I first started going to WBS over four years ago, there was a wonderful bartender there every Sunday named Sarah. She was friendly and prompt at getting my order as soon as she saw me. She was also very attractive, if that matters . She would even come out and dance with me when she wasn't busy. I don't know if she left or got fired, but she hasn't been there for several years now. The current bartenders are just crummy. When I went last night, I sat at the half empty bar for several minutes before getting a morsel of attention from a bartender. I made eye contact with them several times, and they just ignored me completely. Eventually after about ten minutes, one of them finally noticed me and took my order. It seems like they're always in a rush, even when there's only like four people at the bar. When I do finally place my order, I feel like I'm being rushed. WBS seriously needs to hire some competent and friendly bartenders like Sarah was.

The final thing I'll bring up is the band. The only time I come here is on Sunday nights for live music by one of my favorite local bands, Hushpuppy's Daddy. Recently, I heard rumors that this band may lose their gig at WBS. If this happens, I will be very disappointed, as they're the only reason I even go to WBS anymore. They're one of the few bands that plays classic country, rock and roll, jump blues, and oldies music downtown anymore. Walk down Broadway, and you'll mostly just hear 2010s pop country.

Whiskey Bent Saloon, y'all better step your game up. If you fire Hushpuppy's Daddy, I will not be back, even if you do hire more competent staff. The only reason I'm rating you two stars instead of one is because the venue itself is still nice (it's still very spacious with nice hardwood floors and cool decor), and Hushpuppy's Daddy hasn't been fired...yet.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Another music bar on Broadway that had talented musicians. It wasn't too crowded and the bands were great!

name: FooBar
text: If you're on yelp looking for a bar, do not come here. It's not the place for you and you won't like it. Locals only

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Just try the Atomic burger medium rare and you will be hooked.  If Alexsis is your server you will have a great experience!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Our server Mary, who is a newbie, ROCKED IT! 
We had a party of 7 and are demanding.  The manager Faith was also phenomenal... I traveled from St. Louis and expect excellent service and food.  This place did not disappoint. Well done Mary!!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: No cover, live band, I'm in! This was probably my favorite bar in downtown Nashville.  The band they had playing was entertaining and diverse in their music selection. There isn't much room to sit or anything but who comes to these places to sit anyways?! The drinks were pretty good and about 10-12/drink so pretty standard. Would absolutely recommend this place to anyone visiting Nashville and I certainly can't wait to return!

name: The 5 Spot
text: Cool dive bar in East Nashville. Went on a Saturday night. $5 cover. Chatted a bit with the door guy, was a friendly Australian. The people here are eclectic. A little bit of everything. No one bothered anyone and just enjoyed themselves.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: It's 26 degrees out and this bar refuses to close the door as guests sit in winter coats, hats and gloves. The drinks are overpriced but the current band is incredible.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Well, this started well. The hotel looked nice and our room was clean as well. We stayed 2 nights. 
About 20 minutes into our stay at the hotel on the first night, the power for the whole neighborhood was cut due to weather. Understandable. One can't predict these things and it's something that could happen. The hotel had no generator of any sort, no way to have any light inside the room. No candles or anything of that nature either. So, between 7pm and 4-5am on the next day we basically stood in complete darkness, using our phones as flashlights... Until the phones died too. Not only that, but the air conditioning was obviously not working either. It was miserable. I was, however, prepared to let that go. 

On the following morning, after a long concert the night before, I thought I'd sleep in and check out right before 11 am (the set check out time). I was awaken by knocking on the door and the door suddenly opening. I had the inside latch on, therefore whoever was trying to come in was not able to do so. I jumped up in a panic because I thought I overslept and I was late to check out. I found my watch and, to my surprise, it was only 8:50am. I couldn't go back to sleep since my heart was pounding out of my chest, so I started getting ready and getting my luggage together. It wasn't even an hour later when the knocking on the door continued and someone, once again, attempted to walk in. It was 9:45am, over an hour before the set check out time. At that point, I was quite upset. Why on earth would anyone, housekeeping or otherwise, want to come into my room when I've paid good money to be there until at least 11am... Without being asked to do so?! 

I then packed all my stuff and left. So, I stayed the two nights, of which I sat in the dark on the first, and the next I was interrupted by staff and was not able to rest. I could have slept in my car and probably had a better and more relaxing time. 

Once I returned home, I wrote customer service an email and described my experience. I had to provide a condensed version due to the 1,000 symbol space constraint. It's been almost three weeks since then and I am yet to receive any kind of response. The fact no one contacted me and at least apologized was even worse than the actual experience. 

I used to like Sheraton and would seek the hotels out anywhere I went on vacation. After this experience, I would not pay another penny to stay there. If you have the chance, find somewhere else to go, you probably would have much better time!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Had THE pleasure of stumbling into The Stage during the day while shopping with my boyfriend on Broadway. It was very early on a Sunday (maybe noon) but there was already a fantastic band playing and we sat at the bar.

Bartender was a sweetheart and our beers were cold. What more can you ask for? Also, this place is like a music history museum. Just gorgeous and rich.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: My favorite of the places we hit up on Broadway for my bachelorette party.  We heard 3 different bands on the different levels, and each one was great.  I loved the rooftop bar, and the drinks were reasonably priced.  Keep in mind there is no cover, so the bands only make money off teh tips they receive - tip them well and make a song request!  I definitely will be back next time I'm in Nashville.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
You can't come to Nashville without experiencing the live music. That would be sacrilege. Jamie W. and I always attend a show at the Grand Ole Opry when we're in town, and on our last visit, we pressed our noses against the window at the Bluebird Cafe. This time, we were determined to find a place on Lower Broadway despite the armies of party-hearty drunkards that stood in our way at the doorways. This one appealed to us the most because there was no cover charge and there was a lot of space where you can get a view of the band (photo: http://bit.ly/2N9liIC).

We ended up on the mezzanine where we could look at all the activity below including all the couples doing the two-step without falling down. This was one of the rare times that we ordered bottles of Bud Light as we swayed to the twangy tunes though they alternated with more urban pop songs to make everyone happy. We went upstairs to find yet another stage of musicians and another bar but with a vista view of Lower Broadway down below (photo: http://bit.ly/2Jeltjt). We ended up hanging out for a couple of hours like we were Nicole and Keith or something.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: I booked our summer vacation through Booking.com here . As the hotel is under renovation and they didn't tell the third party we were woken at 7 all week . We would not have booked there had we known about renovations. They blamed third party . Third party said they were not informed. Manager offered us a meal which was ridiculous as we had spent a lot of money staying for a week .third party gave us a 15% discount to make it right as they could . Vacations were meant to relax when you work 60 hour work weeks .

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I saw a super star yesterday at the Stage Anna LaPrad is the real deal. At 3 in the afternoon the joint was loaded. Really cold beer and good whisky. All the bands we  saw very very good .As far as playing for tips nobodies putting a gun to their heads to play there. Relax and enjoy!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Loved this place. Went to several places on Broadway and heard the best band and fiddle player here. Wasn't crowded but so much fun.  I will definitely return. Give it a shot!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: If I could, I'd give the hotel even more stars for one simple reason: Ashley. Ashley made my stay amazing through her exemplary customer service. She consistently went out of her way to lovingly accomodate all hotel guests; she is customer service at its finest. What a pleasure.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: My brother suggested I check this place out on my trip and I'm glad I did!!  The 3rd floor is a cool place with the rooftop bar.   We were there on a weeknight and it was rockin!  Definitely put on your places to go!

name: The 5 Spot
text: I came here once for Motown Monday night. I wanna go back! It has an interesting mix of demographic here at this dive bar. Doesn't feel like a weird dive though it was lively especially as it got later. Love the throwback music and the fact people actually dance. (Some of it really entertaining. Great people watching here.) you can't beat the happy hour prices! Seemed like a good beer selection too!! The bartenders were on top of it and friendly. Major plus. Didn't try any of the food but I'm assuming that's just like any dive bar food? Maybe next visit. They have something going on almost every night it seems. There was a line out the door as it got later, clearly a popular thing to go to on a Monday night! My friend and I got there early like 9ish, no line and not crowded at all yet. I'll be back! Duh.

name: East-Centric Pavilion
text:
The East-Centric Pavilion was a wonderful host to events at the Tomato Arts Festival, providing a gathering space away from the central 5 Points excitement, but in support of the nearby shops. Early in the day, a cornhole tournament was run in the adjoining yard, and beers were served from bars set up under the pavilion. The bluegrass band set a festive tone for an exciting day ahead.

The area is well maintained, the landscaping and design a vast improvement from before. This space promotes community gatherings, local small businesses, and non-profits, in a location convenient to many of East Nashville's newest merchants. 

Looking forward to updating this review as the East-Centric Pavilion hosts more events!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Such poor service at the Pride Festival!  This isn't just a rant against Nashville's trend to profiteer off of alcohol sales at their local festivals. Though the trend towards having only one alcohol sponsor for these festivals is both disturbing and irritating, many providers can pull it off adequately. But Hard Rock's monopoly at this festival has demonstrated a new low in service. If you're going to be the sole provider of alcohol at these events you shouldn't be so blatantly capitalistic to be providing such few locations, options and bartenders as to maximize your profits. P.s. Festival planners... it's only a matter of time before we Nashvillians revolt and just start bringing our own alcohol!!

name: The Valentine
text: I visited The Valentine during the CMA Music Festival and that's when the place had live performances by Aaron Tippin, Darryl Worley, Ronnie McDowell. The entertainment was Fantastic and love the place too. A great place to go when visiting Downtown Nashville.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I really enjoyed coming to the stage to hear live music and enjoy some beers. They didn't have a cover on the night that we went. The layout of the space was great: a large open dancefloor/seated section facing the stage, with a bar to the side. I think the openness of the venue makes this place lively without being cramped. It was a really fun time to hear a local band play country covers. I think the stage attracts great talent, so you will be getting a great musical experience no matter which night you come.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Food was awesome! The chicken mac and cheese was VERY good! Service was very good also. Good music, good food, good service..can't go wrong!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: If you want to wait forever for your food, get a stomach ache and over pay you should eat here. Their Nashville hot chicken sandwich was disgusting it was over peppered, greasy, and just plain gross. Our server was nice but whew it was just a eh experience. I normally love hard rock! We go to our local one a lot but this one was just blah.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
This place is just old school and cool.  I honestly wish they allowed smoking here because it would remind me of the way neighborhood bars used to be in the 90's (and probably before, but I was not old enough to get in).  This is not a trendy place (thank God) so you don't have to get all dressed up and there is not fancy food or crazy prices.  Just come as you are and hang out with other people that have come as they are to listen to some great live music.  I have been there twice, both on Saturday nights.  The other night, the Mark Robinson Band was playing and they are a fun Blues Band.  The sound was great.  The time before was older country music and it was also fantastic.  I am looking forward to trying the Friday night 80's dance party which is the first Friday of the month, I believe.

The food was "popcorn only" the two nights that I was there...microwaved in a bag....so that could get better, but there was only one person bartending and doing the popcorn, so I get it.  I heard there is a food truck sometimes.  They pour good drinks, so can't complain.

There is a cover charge so be ready!

name: Boulevard Records
text: Love the environment - very clean and small.  A nice stop on any tour of the area.  No Tears for Fears :(

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: We really enjoyed our stay here. We had a King Suite with the view of the pool from the 4th floor. The room came with a dining room table, full couch & two chairs and desk & chair. The room was clean and bed very comfortable. The lobby is Grand with nice staff to greet you. The price is good and I didn't notice any children running around and this was good for us as we are seniors. I will definitely stay again because the price is good, near airport and short drive to downtown. The only thing I was missing was a Gift shop.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Vegan?  They were able to confirm that the veggie burger is vegan, however they had no idea if their buns / bread options were vegan.  I had to order the burger without a bun because they were not able or willing to verify this for me.  Very disappointing.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I went to this place last night. One of the best bands I have seen in 10 years  they were very entertaining, which is odd for a Tuesday night. I went for a beer and stayed for the band and did 15 shots. Lol. First time in my life I stayed at a bar because of the band.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: 3.5. Good music, no cover. Was easy to walk to from the [ahem: "ho-tel, mo-tel..."] Holiday Inn [Express]. Enjoyed it with the boy and his cousins on a not-too-packed weeknight one our way to the midwest Thanksgiving.  The crowd was weird though (mid-40s plus and early 20-somethings...not really any late20s to early 30-somethings).  Drinks were good and strong though, even if it didn't have a noteworthy bourbon list.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The second stop on our Broadway bar crawl. No surprise here "the stage" is the main attraction here. The musics loud, and everyones "got a cup in there hand". This place makes you feel like your at a concert, everyone knows the words to all the songs. The band was great here, maybe the best we heard in all of Nashville.  Simple concept here but surprisingly fun.

name: The Bridge
text: Great place for a drink. The views are so special and the staff is very friendly. Doesn't feel like you are in a hotel lounge.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
A real honky tonk. No food, just music and alcohol. Another one of the Broadway must visits on a visit to Music City. Music all day. Stop in for drink or two and see some good sounds. Not much to say about a bar only establishment. 

You want to say you've been there.

name: Ray Stevens CabaRay Showroom
text: Just saw the show tonight. Highly recommended. You will start the evening with a smile and leave with a smile. Stevens is still the consummate entertainer and you won't spend a better evening.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Overall it was very good. They forgot to make my husbands food but our server was very nice and the manager took care of us.  My salad and Mai Tai excellent!!!  Tour kids also always have fun at Hard Rock.  The kids were given amazing activity packs.  Nice touch!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I'll start by saying that I've stayed in Nashville twice over the last year and stayed here twice.  I'd stay again if I ever come back.  At first glance it's on a hill and you drive through these gates to get there.  Once inside the lobby is pretty nice and everything has an inviting feel to it.  The rooms are clean and the bed was a pleasure to sleep on.  

As far as the location, it may seem kinda far away from downtown, but I'll say this.  The entire weekend I was here, no matter where I saw starting from and where I needed to go literally everything was 15 minutes away when I plugged it in the gps.  And you can't beat the price.  Staying downtown was ridiculously expensive compared to this place, and that's without including the $20 parking fees most places can surprise you with.  Parking is fee here.  If I'm coming to Nashville again, I'm most likely staying here again.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: The Whiskey Bent Saloon on Broadway is our go to saloon when we come to Nashville reason being is none other than TARIA LONG!!!! We LOVE Taria and the boys! She sings from the heart & has an amazing voice, plus, her music is very relatable. Taria & the boys are fun & get you involved with their show/music. Make sure to get a copy of her CD "Everybody Wants Some". Whiskey Bent Saloon invites you in and treats you like family. The saloon is clean with friendly bartenders, top shelf liquor and ice cold beer! You can't ask for anything better then cold beer, good liquor, friendly staff and of course TARIA. Make sure to put Whiskey Bent Saloon & Taria Long on top of your list when visiting Nashville Tennesse they don't disappoint!

name: Ray Stevens CabaRay Showroom
text:
The facility and entertainment is excellent. The food quality is not up to par with the overall experience

Bar service is prompt, courteous and reasonably priced. We spent an hour before seating time enjoying the piano player and drinks. After the show we returned to the bar for drinks, music and dancing. Ray Stevens also came to the bar and sang additional songs and danced. We were seated for dinner promptly. The dinner theater is comfortable with tables on three sides of the stage. We started with a nondescript salad of lettuce, a couple of grape tomatoes. The dressing was store grade. We had chose the beef entree from fish, chicken and beef for our meal. The meal was similar to what you'd get at a banquet. A few green beans, a few potatoes cubes and the meat was covered in a brown gravy. While it was good, it was at best ordinary. Desserts cost extra and also ordinary. The show was very good. Ray sings many of his old hits with high energy and is entertaining.

name: The Valentine
text:
Music and atmosphere were awesome, service and food left something to be desired. 

Went with a friend and sat on the rooftop patio, grabbed menus and from there no service. 
Went to the bar to order drinks and food, asked about specials but told there were none, even tho I found out later there were. 
Got the turkey club, the amount of bacon on it was the smallest I've ever seen. Says it comes with avocado but really it's brown guacamole. Flavour just wasn't there. 

Despite the food they have a great selection of alcohol and you can't beat the patio!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Recently spent a long weekend in Nashville and after quite a bit of deliberation decided we'd stay at a "nicer" hotel instead of the many nearby motels that'd cost half. Overall, this particular Sheraton was pretty disappointing. Our room had that weird old musty hotel room smell to it, and we got a real odd handicap accessible room which apparently was all that was available which seemed sort of unlikely given just how easily in the day we were checking in. A friend got upgraded to a suite which was laid out super odd, it was like it had the same amount of furniture as a normal hotel room, but instead just had enough room in the center to set up a boxing ring or something. I don't get it.

The hotel bar was absurdly expensive for how watered down the drinks were, and the hotel food was pretty terrible for how expensive it was. Overall, a super mediocre experience and considering how much we paid (compared to the rest of the Nashville area) it was pretty disappointing.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This is amazing honky tonk! It has such an awesome vibe and my favorite thing is they have the cutest security and bouncers. I mean honestly 10/10. They always have great music playing and there's always something new to see. It's similar to other bars on broadway but this one is a must see!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: We visited this place around the New Years Eve time frame and had a blast! The service at the bar was very friendly! In addition, the staff members who came around were incredibly funny and quick to clear away any empty glasses (and answer all our questions about their trendy cowboy hats :P ). We had a party of around nine individuals, who were able to all hang around one of the tall tables with a few stools without feeling cramped. The bands playing were very good and played a lot of popular songs! Overall, I would absolutely recommend this venue and look forward to visiting again during our next Nashville trip!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Key was capital A AMAZING!!!!!! Absolutely loved her spirit! Thanks for helping us today!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Another Nashville spot I was at a few times and feel I can write a review. Every bartender we had was amazing and their choice of bands or musicians was amazing. Every bar on broadway has music, but this place has exceptional talent and great bartenders. I was at countless bars on broadway but I have this place saved to make sure I get there again. Do yourself a favor, save the time and stop in here.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: 12/27/19: Service was SOOO SLOW! Food was cold and chips for spinach dip were stale. WORST experience! DO NOT GO TO THIS HARD ROCK!

name: The Valentine
text: Great bar. Had a group of friends for NYE in Nashville and went into Valentine the night before NYE and had a great time. The bartender Katie was great and our group had the best time. Will go back here when I am back in Nashville. Also there was another bartender on the rooftop that all my friends were raving about how she was so great but never made it past the 3rd floor.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Wonderful time had at the Stage. The music with all the bands was just incredible to say the least. We visited in the afternoon and late evening. Surely less crowded in the afternoon. The drinks were good but little on the pricey side. That's expected with the bands playing. Had a great time with friends.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: One of the best Honky Tonks/ Bars on Broadway! Great music and even better drinks. Molly Bird kills it behind the bar! If you're looking for a fun place with a friendly staff, look no further!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
So I used to be a Hard Rock Fanatic! Anytime I was in a new city I would get the same thing Nachos and a Hard Rock Collectors mug.  Times have changed.  I am now a diabetic and I have to watch what I eat and drink.  With that being said, it was my birthday so I decided to lax my diet for the night.  

This was my first time to Nashville.  So I wanted to see what Hard Rock's contribution to Nashville's role as being the Mecca for us country music fans were.   Not impressive. It was more like all the other hard rock hotels where it was more about rock and roll than country.  When I got to the restaurant, I had to go to the rest room so I went right in and the toilet was disgusting. Somebody had diarrhea and clogged up the toilet.    I went out and informed the lady at the podium and she gave the illusion that she knew it and they were just leaving it there asking me "well is it overflowing?" What difference does that make?!?! Do you think people want to be thinking about somebody's bowel movements while they are about to eat in a restaurant? Like get real!  

Going back to the diabetes issue, I can't believe with every body moving toward healthier choices, Hard Rock still decides to hang on to 2,000-3,000 calorie dishes still. NO healthy choices at all.   I mean I was laxing my rules a little bit but I couldn't in good conscience eat that many calories.   So I just got chips and salsa and a hurricane. Now I usually have a hurricane and am able to get a buzz.  Not here, I got nothing!  It was like 95% juice and 5% liquor.  I tasted the vodka at the very end  which means the bartender didn't mix it up right.    

Will never return to this Hard Rock again! and until Hard Rock gets healthier choices,  will probably never go to any hard rock again.

name: The Valentine
text: Valentine has lost its appeal on Broadway. They built a solid group of locals with plenty of money to spend with a great place to gather and turned us away. They have let go of great bartenders with a great customer base and brought in new security that do not know the regulars and treat all of us like out of town strangers. 1 star for effort and great atmosphere but they are going no where quick

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: It's a nice place with friendly staff, good drinks, and it's located right downtown.. We were in from out of town. Try to stop at hard rock in every city we visit

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
My review is based on the gift shop in front of the Hard Rock Cafe...the building is very small but stocked full of Hard Rock collectibles and shirts and all kinds of other souviners.

 There is a section on the floor where it used to be the silver dollar saloon. There are several silver dollars in the floor. It really is cool to see it.

The staff is fun, friendly and helpful.

Highly recommended..

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Hands down my favorite bar on broadway. A great place to day drink. It's smaller and it definitely gets busy as the night goes on. You'll always hear some great music in here! Drinks are great as well.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I absolutely love this hotel! It's beautiful, has a full bar, restaurant, indoor pool, beautiful outdoor patio and a large pool. 

The hotel has recently been updated and it is better than ever! 

The customer service is top notch! Ebony (I think that is correct) is amazing at the front desk! 

The rates are fantastic! I honestly don't know why anyone would want to stay anywhere else when visiting Nashville. It's about 15 minuets from the crazy traffic and downtown area; with free parking and WiFi! 

Every time I stay there I have such a good time.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: My wife and I have been heavy rock fans since we first got married. We travel to Hard Rocks all over the country, Las Vegas being one of our favorites. Of course that was until we came to visit the Hard Rock Cafe in Nashville the other afternoon. We live in Knoxville so we visit the Nashville cafe quite a lot, maybe 3 times a month, but one thing really stood out this past time and it was our server, Ali. Besides the exceptional service that she provided, she took the time to actually have a conversation with my wife and I about our travels and life as well as her goals, ambition, and passion for her job. While having these conversations and making us laugh our socks off, she also managed to run around making sure everyone else outside was well taken care of. Being in the food industry and working at the Hard Rock cafe myself years and years ago, I was more than impressed. By the end of meal we were ready to adopt her ha! This being said, our new favorite Hard Rock cafe has now become the Nashville Tennessee restaurant. I highly recommend everyone to go there and request this young lady and listen to her stories, you wont be dissapointed! We will be coming back more than 3 times a month now and with friends and family. Thank you Hard Rock Cafe for making my experience well worth it.

name: Legends Corner
text: Another must stop when in Nashville... If you want to stay away from the tourist trap aspect wait until later in the night to go... Start on Lower Broadway and work your way up.   The history and great live music is worth the stop.  Plus, you never know who will pop up and jump up on stage.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Food was good, but nothing over the top. Favorite order was onion rings & mozzarella sticks. However, the atmosphere was excellent!! Definitely a great time to enjoy a local dive. The staff made you dee right at home, and the music was fantastic. Traveling through Nashville, this was a perfect stop.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: The food was so delicious and our sever Matt was beyond attentive. Matt answered any questions with the smile gave us great suggestions and made our dinner that much more memorable. The restaurants ambience was romantic with a jazz band that was playing in the background. The food was cooked to perfection! We didn't have one bad experience with Sambuca's from start to finish, it really was special. Next time we are in Nashville at the Gulch we will definitely be going back!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I just love this place. Never a bad experience. Sat on the patio and enjoyed terrific music, service, food and cocktails. Can't beat that.

name: Robert's Western World
text: The best honky tonk on lower Broadway.  The food is great and the music is always top notch. Unfortunately, it has become very crowded.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great service. Try the goat cheese stuffed artichokes! Amazing. We caught a great blues band, and got sat right away at 7pm in Saturday night. (Although to be fair.. The entire city of Nashville is out waiting for fireworks in the rain)

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Great venue for music. Lot's of history. A must when you are in Nashville!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: This review is for restaurant. Had Calamari Fritti and Cheesecake Sopapilla while listening to live band. Food was okay nothing special and fancyish atmosphere. What was not okay was seeing the way staff handled other customers who were not happy with the service they received. Instead of addressing this away from dining area, the staff continued this feedback session with the customers to the point where the customers were loudly cursing. Intimate atmosphere ruined. Gets worse. I guess there was some mix up with receipts among waiting staff. Guess where they have their arguments? Right in front of customers. Get your act together!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
While deciding what to eat ( my wife has cranky spells when she gets hungry) we popped into Roberts, ( heard they have fried bologna sandwiches) and who doesn't love that. While we agreed we would split one to "tide her over", she ate it all but one bite! It is def a cozy place, but then again most of the bars are on broadway........ but hey, that's what we are here for !!!! 
Cheap beer, and the bologna sammich was ALL OF THAT!! - def worth popping in on as you try to figure out what your gonna do next ..... only to look up and realize you spent the whole night there! Caelin was the best .... she kept us in drinks we never got parched!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Best place around! Where else can you buy boots in the afternoon, listen to great music and then nosh on a fried bologna sandwich (a must - soooo yummy). Their country music is more traditional and wonderful, so much talent on the stage. I also want to give a BIG shout out to Hope who served me yesterday. I forgot my purse, called them later and they put it in a safe place. Thanks Hope!

Don't forget to tip the band!

I don't think there is a better place on Music Row and certainly one of my favs in the US. If you have a bar/music bucket list, make sure you put Robert's on it.

name: Robert's Western World
text: It's kinda one of those places you go in Nashville because it's so iconic.  It's in the hub of all things touristy on Broadway, but this place itself is as authentic as it gets.  Great live music.  I would definitely recommend it as a must-stop if you're doing the Broadway Street Circuit.  This and Acme Feed & Seed may be the only two places I recommend on Broadway

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I have always had a great time here - the choices of love music are great -- and they have one of the better wine lists around. There is room to dance a bit and the outside seating is really great.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Seen the Gatlin Brothers and toured the behind the scene dressing rooms where johnny Cash and Minnie Pearl would hang before the show. The original 1892 and great restoration plus don't forget the movie they show it was fun.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Arguably one of the best places on Broadway! Upstairs is semi-open so you can smoke. Plus no matter which bar you went to, you got quick service. Nothing beats that. The staff there is great and be music was even better. A great mix of country and classic rock. Cannot recommend this place any better.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: What an amazing piece of Americana history. This is a must see, even if you aren't a country music fan. The amazing names to have graced this stage is bigger than a phone book. Really a gem.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great atmosphere and beer. It was also nice to find a place playing something other than country on Broadway. I know I know it's Broadway,  but I still love it

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Color me impressed with Robert's Western World!  I came in here with a friend as we were both eating dinner next door at the BBQ joint, and could hear what was going on inside of Robert's and we wanted to be part of it.

Being a fan of music, mainly ROCK music, I was hesitant to walk into a place that had the words "Western World" in its name, because I'm not a huge fan of country music and I think of Western country music as being the twangy music that I just can't stand.  However, my perception was dead WRONG.

When I walked in, there was some young kid, maybe about 20yrs old or so, wailing, and I mean absolutely wailing on his electric guitar that was behind his head.  I was like 'what the...??"  This kid was a wizard on that guitar and what I was hearing wasn't twangy at all...the kid was shredding it.  Come to find out the house band is legendary and the band leader is known to mentor up and coming guitarists and plays with them live in this bar.

We didn't order food here as we had just eaten, but those fried bologna sandwiches looked fantastic.  Also, were I'm from, you put down a $20 on the bar for a couple of beers and any change you get goes to the bartender.  Not here.  I ordered two beers and got $15 in change...WHAT? 

Then I thought the fun was over.  The band announced they were going to play a George Jones song....I was like, "ok, here comes that TWANG that I can't stand!!!!!!!"  I was wrong...that band made that song their own, updated it, and it was awesome.  The musicians were fantastic...then they put their take on a Merle Haggard tune....and it was AWESOME.  

What a wonderful experience here...the decor is fantastic, and this place qualifies as a DIVE...but one you never ever want to leave!!!  

Highly recommended.  Don't forget to tip the band!!  (and the staff!)

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Your average bar with live music.  I chose this place since it had 4 star reviews.  IMHO it did not live up to the reviews.  We ordered BBQ sandwich and quesadilla.  The BBQ was cold and the quesadilla was average.  We went in the mid afternoon so perhaps they were not staffed to meet expectations.  The service was average with only one server.  The music was live.  Don't think I'll return here unless I just want to drink beer.  Suggest you skip the food.

Still wondering how this place got so many high ratings.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We just left...band was playing Purple Rain and other Prince tribute songs....there was also a Black Lives Matter documentary playing on the TV's. Not the Nashville I know...not going back!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: The atmosphere was quite amazing for live country music bands and an energetic audience. We loved the finger foods as that was what we mostly ate. Our server was a hot little college chick who forgot about my wife's quesadillas, but altogether we still had a great experience. The kiddos were dancing to the music and cheers of "whoo hoo" came from our group. Three stars for the food as it was average. Also, the bar ran out of draft beers, so that sucked because I didn't get my Goode Island drink, lol! Overall, a memorable event with some family

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
My parents and grandparents used to go to shows here, and my spouse and myself have been attending for around 15 years.  This used to be hands down the best place to see live music in the state; but thanks to its proximity to the bars on lower Broadway and the recent push to attract tourist dollars, it's now more a place to hear the drunks behind, around and in front of you whoop and holler instead of letting you see or hear the show.  People drink all day on Broadway and then show up here for the concert, where they buy more beer and mixed drinks to keep their good time rolling.  The venue is now way more about booze and drinking than actual music.

It's really too bad.  People used to be respectful and you felt you were getting your money's worth (tickets here are NOT cheap).  But now you'll be treated to the people nearby screaming, "singing" along, and having loud conversations about whatever they had for dinner or what they plan to do after the show.  Heaven help you if you actually ask them to talk a little more quietly, keep hands/feet in their own space, or whatever - "they can do whatever they want," "this isn't a library" (actual quote) and the kindly older folks who serve as ushers here have no real power.  There are usually one or two security guards, but they won't do anything about the obnoxious behavior of others unless one of the drunks actually takes a swing at somebody.

The worst thing, though, is when you spend $$$$ on seating near the stage only to have security let the people who've bought cheap tickets at the back of the floor flood down and stand in front of you.  This may be why many folks prefer the balcony.

No way I'd even consider going here on a  Saturday night anymore, under any circumstances.  It's heartbreaking to see this place turned into just another tourist commodity, but so goes a lot of Nashville these days.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I've been on a mission to catch as many great shows as I can this year (2017) and though I've caught some great ones all over Nashville from large venues (Bridgestone) to tiny (The End), I've somehow missed the Ryman completely. I've seen shows at the Ryman in the past but not since moving to the area a few years back. Partly that's been avoidance because I hate the parking situation at the Ryman, part of that is the artists I've been wanting to see simply haven't played the venue. However, a favorite artist of mine was set to perform here and I bought my tickets as soon as I could and the performance reminded me of how great this venue can be.

Pros: (1) Historically significant spot that every Nashville visitor (or resident) should visit at least once--do the tour for the history, see a show for the experience; (2) Acoustics are phenomenal--the sound here is just perfect--no distortion, no fuzz, just clear bright sound that sounds great at a sound level that is totally audible at every note but that isn't so loud you need earplugs; (3) for the most part, not a bad seat in the house--if you're not directly behind a post you can see the stage from everywhere you may sit. Toward the end of the show I recently saw  we were near the back of the bottom level but with the way the room is angled we had a clear view the entire time. Toward the end of the show many of us began walking down the aisle to catch the encore from the front which showed just how great the view is from the center front but those tickets are typically noticeably higher; and now (4) valet parking that is only $20 (free if you drive a Nissan due to their sponsor). That sealed the deal but though drop-off was seamless and painless, pick up of the automobile after the show took a bit long.

Cons: (1) Pick up time for valet as mentioned could use some work, there is some confusion as to what the official process for pick up procedure is as well since what we were told at drop off was not what we were actually supposed to do; (2) concessions as they are at any of the "name" brand venues of the city are a bit ridiculous ($12 for a beer, $8 for a soda); (3) seats are a bit hard after awhile as these are old school church pews without a cushion; (4) this venue while perfect for some styles of music isn't suited for everything--if it's an active show with dancing, moshing, movement at all this doesn't work

So check it out, it's worth a visit!

name: Legends Corner
text:
Another superior spot on Broadway, Legends Corner is a little louder but a little deeper. I loved that we found a table on the "mezzanine" where we could see over the folks on the ground level but the music was still clear.

I'm not quite sure why the band had to cut out at exactly 10:15, but okay.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: This place is amazing! There is such a great variety of shops here! I found chicha morada, which made me very happy. I can't wait to come back on the weekends for live music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Stepped in here before going to see a show at the Station Inn which is across the street because they only serve beer over there and I'm more of a hard liquor kind of girl...
Very nice live band playing but didn't catch the name. Female lead singer and female backup were both great. Again with the cover songs tho...

Shimmied up to the bar. Ambiance is chic and dark... The crowd was a little off-putting, maybe a tad too snotty for my mingling taste. Angie the bartender was great tho and did me a huge favor by making me a slammin' espresso martini. I was on the road all day and badly needed caffeine to perk up. Espresso martinis, when done properly are probably one of my favorite things in life. I don't usually order them tho because being a bartender myself I know what a bitch they are to make. She glady obliged my request and it was delish!
My bf got a fancy $12 beer and then had major martini envy when he saw/tried mine. Place wasn't cheap but I guess that is to be expected in this part of town. Only had one round and left but it was a good one!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Went to the Ryman last night to see Sam's Place, hosted by Stephen Curtis Chapman..... One of the best events we have attended.!  We felt like we were joining in a small gathering of some of Steven Curtis's close friends, singing their favorites and enjoying just being together!   Such a special place and a wonderful series....can't wait for the next one. We bought the whole series and gladly would have paid twice the price for this event!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Sunday 5/14/2017 Had an amazing dinner out on the patio on a perfect early evening to eat outdoors, which happened to be Mother's Day! From start to finish, it was a lovely experience. Our hostess sat us promptly when we arrived at our reserved time. Our server took our drink and appetizer order, then came back to take our dinner order. All four of us had a glass of wine and the table shared two appetizers. Dinner arrived in a timely manner and was delicious! A nice variety is on the menu for both beverages and food.  No dessert for us this time, we were stuffed. Nicely sized entree portions for your money. Service was very good and the manager came over to our table to introduce himself and make sure our experience was on par. It was!  Live music was happening inside, but since it was so nice outside, we opted for the patio this time around. We will definitely come back. With so, so many in town vying for our food/entertainment dollar, everyone has to keep their game up and stay on their toes. So far, Sambuca is doing just that!

name: Robert's Western World
text: This was a pretty cool first time to Nashville spot to visit! True honky tonk and lots of character. I had the $5 recession special which was a pbr, bologna sandwich and a bag of chips. The sandwich was actually pretty good. It was 3 thin slices of bologna on a buttered toast with lettuce and tomato and a mayo packet. Definitely worth my stop in. I would suggest you sit upstairs in the back of your in a group so you can hear each other talk. Band was loud but not to loud. Enjoyable.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: This place is amazing and as all the businesses open it's just going to get even better! Awesome child fruit cups, live Latin music, restaurants, and fresh hot tortillas. I'm so excited to see such an awesome development in the area!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
We visited today and chose a guided tour at $30 each verses $20 for a self guided tour (includes the self guided tour and a movie explaining the history of the Ryman). We are glad we did. The tour was interesting and informative. We would have been disappointed to pay $20 each just to see the movie and walk around the seating area. 

Our experience was very good, but this is not a cheap visit. It cost $14 for two hours of parking and $60 to tour. 

We look at us as a one time thing, although seeing a live show there would be awesome, and a charitable contribution to keep this place going for generations to come.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Robert's is a fun Broadway stop for Nashville visitors. It's more accessible for all ages(meaning not a ton of young wild kids), and great for enjoying live music. Drinks are also really affordable. Most hover around $5-9 which is great for this busy street. It does get packed so you may want to try and beat the crowds before 10 to get a seat or be comfortable.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
DON'T GO TO THE RYMAN!!

I went to a see Tedeschi Trucks Band Concert there (or so I'd hoped.)  

When I entered the venue, my ticket was denied and I was told to go to the box office. 

The box office staff were rude, arrogant, disrespectful and completely unconcerned that I'd paid $120 for a ticket that they'd already sold to someone else.  They told me that I was "out of luck" because someone else was already sitting in my seat.  No help to find me another seat, and when I expressed frustration, they called security.  30 seconds later, a Metro police office and 3 beard security guards surrounded me.  All the sudden, I'm a criminal.

The Officer lost his temper, put his hands on me, and escorted me off the property. He actually threatened to arrest me. 

Until they find box office staff and security who respect human beings, DON'T GO THE RYMAN!!  Oh, and STOP DOUBLE SELLING TICKETS!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
We had the guided tour which last around an hour, we went backstage and our guide was informativ, after the guided tour, you do self guided one because not all the stuff is covered in the guided one. The only thing that made the visit unpleasant, is the girl that was taking the photo( that was 7/8), we approached her to take a photo for us, she didn't talk or greet us, so we had to ask her to take a photo for us, she said ok without a single smile, it felt awkward like we came on wrong time. no smile, no talking.
Anyway, you can get a parking close to the auditorium on the weekend for $10.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Ryman was the greatest music venue I've ever been to. The intimate setting and the church style set up makes for such a unique concert experience! I caught a Leon bridges show, and even from the back of the room I had great view of the show and the acoustics were great. The story behind this place takes it to the next level. Even if you only have a day in Nashville you have to stop by here.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: A very nice, all around experience for the entire family.  A great food market with fresh seafood, meats and a bunch of other goodies.  It also has various shops, a nice restaurant and a killer food court area featuring vendors offering an interesting variety of other foods.  The venue is spotless, the live entertainment is incredible, the food we tried at various vendors was excellent.  There is also good security throughout the plaza.  I am especially addicted to the ceviche at El Ceviche Loco.  It is soooooo good.  It's an overall fun and delicious experience.  Check it out.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: we went here for happy hour drinks and they were incredible! the atmosphere was really nice and this would be a great place to go for drinks and music, unfortunately none was playing at 2pm on a Thursday (obviously). the only reason I'm giving this 4 stars is one of the girls received her drink with green leaves in it and the waitress sat it down and said to disregard them that they were from another drink the bartender made.. they should have never served that but remade it. with that said I would still go back and try their food with hopes they take more pride in making sure its served without other ingredients.

name: Robert's Western World
text: A gem for tourists, this place has cheap fried food, fireball on tap, accepts credit cards, and awesome live music. However, my first trip was also my last since it definitely reads tourist by way of the customers, crowds, and location. Broadway is a must see, so don't let this review deter you from going in just keep in mind that you might have to wait for a seat  to sit next to what appear to be frat guys from out of town. But hey, the bartenders are lightning quick and the live music is likely better than anything you'll find in your hometown.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Behold! The future of eating is here and it is GLORIOUS!!!!!!! The place is huge and the dining options are extravagant. Also the entertainment is something akin to a Disney experience. My family and I ordered a meal of shish kebabs and steak fries then we were beset by music on the stage and fire dancers performed for us. All for free. THIS IS HOW U EAT!!!!!!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Easily my favorite bar in Nashville for the following reasons:

1) The live music was amazing every time we went

2) It's the only bar in Nashville that sells beer for less than $5

Great place for your first Honky Tonk experience.

name: Music City Center
text:
A pretty typical conference center. 

I wasn't crazy about the main ballroom being on the top floor, but ended up working out. Everything was clean and organized though cell service on Sprint could get spotty. There was free WiFi provided by the conference. 

The location is great- close to Broadway and all the hotels and I'd pick Music City over Opryland any day.

name: Robert's Western World
text: First time at this great honky tonk. Had 3 kids with us and got a seat upstairs no problem. Food service was slow but staff was very friendly. They lost our food order initially but ended up giving us another order on the house. Great music and atmosphere!

name: Second Fiddle
text: Definitely a must on broadway, they always have good bands and great bar tenders.

name: Music City Center
text:
This is a great place for trainings and huge gatherings. I am here all week for training and conferences for a huge company. I am excited! Here is so much room. You would never know from the outside. 

Everything is super clean and bright. Who knew they could cool down such a huge building. They keep it nice and cool inside. There are plenty of stands for snacks and drinks. The bathrooms are not as big as I would have expected. The lines are long.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I love Robert's!  Karen is by far the best bartender I've encountered in all my years of coming to Nashville! Great bar, great music and excellent service!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Nothing bad to say about this place. Fried bologna was so good I wanted to have 15 of them but I held on because my wife would have killed me, or the bologna. Yeeehawwwww. Great live music, great drinks and with great prices.  Would recommend this place to anyone looking for a good time in Nashvile.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Very cool to walk in the steps of the greats. We did the self guided tour. Ask for AAA discount and save about $5. The video part during the beginning of the tour was awesome. Very entertaining. The tour was a little rocky. They just basically let you lose in the auditorium to roam freely. Was kinda lost and didn't know where to go when let lose. Pretty cool experience.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Good place for dinner while enjoying live music... (Jazz swing on my visit) More upscale and has really good food.
Very comfortable seating in dinning area and great bar area that is still in viewing and listening distance from the band. Outside seating also available.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Fun with great music and a good greasy burger and fried pickles and delicious sweet potato fries!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Our favorite joint on Broadway!  Cheap beers!  Great food!  Also one of the few places downtown that still plays all the traditional music!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: There is a Tin Roof in Memphis so I had to see what this one was all about. Well... I really enjoyed the food here. I ordered street tacos and corn on the cob. The street tacos were pretty good, but the corn was out of this world!! It was sweet and salty. It had cheddar cheese and some other type of sauce on it. I never had anything like it. The bartenders were nice and the door attendant was kind enough to get my friend a seat to sit at the bar. It was crowded because of the Superbowl viewing. There is a second level for seating as well. I enjoyed my time here.

name: Legends Corner
text:
Cool corner bar on Nashville's Honky Tonk strip- crowd gets more lively later in the evenings.
Next touristy gift shop.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
If you're looking for the authentic Honky Tonk experience in Nashville, Robert's Western World should be one of your first stops. Like a great jazz club in New Orleans, Robert's is the perfect spot to hear country and bluegrass music on Broadway. The house band that was playing when we dropped by was as good as any I've heard, and had the audience locked in throughout the entire show. 

The long, rutted bar that runs along one side of the narrow space beckons visitors to pull up a stool, order a whiskey or a beer, and soak up the music and the atmosphere. The beer selection was nothing to write home about (they at least have Lagunitas), but that's not really the draw here. Nashville's wide-ranging music scene offers dozens of great choices, but Robert's Western World is one of the truly unique places that makes this town the center of the country music universe.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Husband and I wandered over here on a Friday afternoon in June. We'd already eaten lunch, so we walked up and down Broadway, past all the bars, before we picked one that was playing the best music. To us, that was Tin Roof. It didn't hurt that a friend had also recommended this place!
They had reasonably priced beers, but the best part was definitely the live music! When we were there, that was a band playing all different type of country music covers, from those popular in the 60s and 70s to more current pop-style country. They harmonized well and also did a good job of keeping the crowd interested & participating. They genuinely wanted people to make requests. 
I know a lot of this review is of the band, which changes, but I also noticed that Tin Roof had great acoustics! Likely, any decent band will sound as good as they can in there!
We had a lot of fun spending a few hours here! They had a decent selection of beers - local and otherwise - on tap. We tried a couple local beers from Little Harpeth - Yum! I preferred the Chicken Scratch, my husband the Iris IPL. We had one of each, so it was perfect.
Next time I visit Nashville, this place is at the Top of my list!!

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text: We had a great time and saw some wonderful music, but based on our experience this evening, it is clearly not a "listening room" as we had anticipated. There was much talking and laughter by those in the audience, including other performers,  during people's sets, especially during solo acoustic guitar playing.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Blew into Nashville for a little country music and stepped off B'way for a Mushroom & Swiss Burger @ Robert's Western World based on several Yelp reviews that talked mostly about the music. 

You gotta love the live country music here in the Mecca of country jams. Great country-blue grass here at Robert's today. Dark, cool air conditioned atmosphere was a nice backdrop for my burger & IPA...and tasty fries...very nice. 

Definitely lived up to Yelp's 4.5 rating.

name: Music City Center
text:
This was my first time at the Music City Center. I'd previously been to the Nashville Convention Center a few years ago for the Nashville Auto Show and I have to say this place is a needed upgrade. We stopped in on a Saturday afternoon for the Antiques and Garden Show of Nashville (we scored a couple free tickets from Yelp). We parked over on Lea Avenue, a few blocks away, free parking, woohoo. We'd at at Bakersfield then made it over to the center. 

We entered down at the 5th Avenue south and Demonbreun entrance. I figured that the antique and garden show as going to be so big it wouldn't be a too hard to find, however, I think I miss judged how large this place was. This place actually takes up 3 blocks. They've got 2 streets that run underneath the building, pretty neat. We randomly entered down a hallway that had a few rooms with a multi-level marketing company. We realized we weren't in the right place and asked one of the information desks where we needed to go. We needed to walk pretty much to the other side of the building, to level 3. The stairs leading up to the 3rd level have small, little terraces. The were locked that day we were there, maybe because it was only 20 degrees outside. 

We made it up to the show, the room was pretty large, it wasn't the biggest in the place, but I did peek though some open doors on the way to the show and some of the rooms are HUGE. I really like how they have so much natural light. The windows on this place are vast and the ceilings are so tall. The design of this place is very futuristic on the outside, with some of that filtering though inside. This place is a a true asset to Nashville, no matter how much they had to spend on the place. It's sad that the bees on top of the building died over the winter.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is one of the spots I hit when I have out of town visitors. It gives a good taste of the town in a venue with good music and good service.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Disappointing to say the least. I came with a large group and we had a limited menu due to the number of people. We waited over an hour for somebody to take our order. Our food arrived over another hour later. Servers ignored us and nobody acknowledged what was happening. When we reached a breaking point and complained, the staff mocked us and were not told to stop. The food probably would have been very good if it were not cold after sitting out. I would not recommend this restaurant due to lousy customer service.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Music is the best.  Service is the worst.  Have been a patron for over 10 years and just can't take it anymore...will not go back.  Rude...

name: Legends Corner
text: Came here 2 nights in a row while I was in Nashville.  Came here first on Christmas Eve during the day.  It was pretty empty as expected, but still had a decent amount of people there.  That didn't stop Buck McCoy (the performer at the time) from being so much fun and incredible!! We had a blast.  Then the next day (Christmas Day) while walking up and down Broadway trying to find a bar that was open, we saw that Legends was only one of 2 bars that was open.  To our delight, Buck McCoy was there AGAIN and this time the crowd was double the size.  We were still able to get a seat and a drink no problem.  Definitely a fun environment there.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This is an amazing venue. I've been to a couple of shows and also did the tour. Yes the acoustics are great. Choose your seats carefully so as not to be behind a pillar.

name: Robert's Western World
text: The best honky-tonk for more traditional country (not new country) music. The drink prices are better than the neighboring honky-tonks, too. And the service is always great.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Went here on a Saturday night with a friend and my boyfriend. All of us have out of state IDs. The bouncer gave all of us a hard time, but especially my boyfriend, who has a Florida ID. The skinny, scruffy bouncer then proceeded to break my boyfriends ID without looking him in the eye or admitting he had made a mistake. This is a ruinous and disrespectful way to treat first time customers. We would've forgiven this transgression for good music and a good atmosphere, but we were instead greeted with a terrible cover band and worse patrons. Would not return.

name: Legends Corner
text:
History is there, music is good. Beers are expensive, as is typical of a tourist trap. However, the shortest, bearded doorman has Napoleon complex. Tread lightly on Titans game day when around as a fan of opposing team. 

Update. This guy is still not nice.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Disappointing experience. Previously visited the Tin Roof by Vanderbilt, which lead us to visit this location - however, much different experience. Took 45 minutes for nachos and a quesadilla. The nachos were cold. Waitress never checked on us - so we had to get our napkins and silverware. Huge disappointment. 

The bathroom doors, while having a lock, don't lock. And the music is so loud you can't talk to anyone.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great food good service always live music a must go excellent atmosphere always lively

name: Legends Corner
text:
How could you not give this place 5 stars! Heart of Nashville, great place lots of amazing talent and fun. I travel to Nashville on business often and always pop into here, Honky Tonk Central and of course Tooties. 

Definitely stop in if you are doing the Broadway crawl!!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My friends and I enjoyed our dinner here almost 3wks ago. Although, the live music was a bit loud, but they sounded great. The steaks were cooked per individual temp request, accompanied with a side of our choosing. We also ordered appetizers which we devoured! The cocktails were on the strong side but tasty according to the ladies ;) our waitress and her assistants did an okay job serving us. As a note, it is not as dressy as they claim it to be, most customers were dressed casually. However, you won't be out of place if you decide to dress semi-formal. One more thing, it is very dark in the restaurant, tables were only lit with 2 small candles, therefore, making it hard to read the menu.  They brought a special dessert on the house to celebrate our friend, which was a very nice touch!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Best venue I've seen a concert at even though its pew seating so if your row if full it's pretty tight.

name: Legends Corner
text:
I'm a big fan!!!! So far, my favorite stop on Broadway. We had a lively band of live music. I super duper enjoyed the music, the drinks, and the fun! There was line dancing friendly atmosphere and tons of fun. 

The bar is pretty long, so there's plenty of seating that allows for a view of the show. There's a second bar in the very back. Not super inhabited, but nice to have the optionality. They also had a screen showing the show in the front in case you aren't far enough forward to enjoy the show!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Excellent music, fantastic burgers, and outstanding service by Rachael R.!  I came to town for the Jimmy Buffet / NFL draft weekend.  All of downtown was packed and the energy was great. My friends and I went to more bars than I can count and found ourselves visiting this establishment the most.  We were served by Rachael on our last two visits on Sand we were equally amazed each time with her lightning speed, friendliness and accuracy! 
I highly recommend this place to all who visit the Nashville downtown area. The singers were incredible and every visit was memorable.

name: Musicians Corner
text: I LOVE Musicians Corner!!! It is my favorite part of summer in Nashville. Musicians Corner is a FREE music series in Centennial Park. This summer the shows are Fridays 5-9 pm and Saturdays 12-6 pm. Fridays are dedicated to acoustic music and then Saturdays are a nice mix of artists. It is outside so the experience can depend greatly on the weather but it's definitely worth enduring a little heat or rain. There is one big stage at the front with a small stage off to the side sponsored by Lightning 100. The smaller stage features artists in between the big stage sets. I have enjoyed every single artist I have listened to at Musicians Corner. They get a nice mix of genres and actually rarely play country music. This is great for someone like me that doesn't really like country music (don't hate me Nashville!). However, when a country artist does play they are still great to listen to! I think live music from talented artists is always good. The seating is just open on the grass so it's nice to bring a blanket or lawn chair to sit on/in. There is some shade under trees if it's a super hot day. There is also an awesome selection of food trucks in the back. I'm guessing they rotate every weekend but you can usually count on the staples of bbq, tacos, shaved ice, ice cream, and then some other unique trucks like Korean and Vietnamese. Thirsty for a drink? They have you covered! There is a small "bar" that serves a few beers, wine, and I believe mixed drinks. What's better than listening to some great music while sipping a cold one? If you really like the music, they have a vendor that sells the band's merchandise. There are also a few other vendors/sponsors along the back. You can score some free swag if you like collecting pens and frisbees. Parents, you might be happy to hear that there is a children's section. They usually have some fun games set up for the kiddos and have people supervising the area. Overall, I'm super impressed that this whole experience is free and so well organized. I definitely will be going every chance I get!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Ryman is such an exquisite and beautiful place to go enjoy a show. The acoustics travel through the auditorium with such grace and the rows/pews are well arranged. 

I do not necessarily agree that there isn't one bad seat in the house, as I would not want to be all the way in the back of the main floor due to the balcony blocking half the stage. Again, that may not "block" the performance, but it's not as visually appealing or welcoming. I have never sat in the balcony or sides to comment on those seats. 

Merchandise set up for shows is a bit chaotic and does not easily allow patrons to preview what is for sale before waiting in line...but I do not see anywhere else to set this up better. And the entrance is a bit hectic, but they do a good job for such a small venue. 

Price of food and drink are to be expected for a venue. 

Love the intimate setting and will be back for more shows in the future.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: AMAZING. If you're going to Nashville this is a must visit! We saw a Tuesday evening show and it was amazing. This venue is smaller and we had seats that were "limited view" but it was still amazing and I would definitely go again in those seats. The venue is small so I don't think there is a bad spot in the house. Plus this is such a historical site you don't want to miss that!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My sisters and I had dinner tonight on the patio at Sambuca.  Drinks, appetizers and dinner were fantastic!  We started with the beignet and garlic bread appetizers and then had scallops, shrimp & crab scampi and salmon oscar.  Everything was fresh and delicious.  Sambuca was the perfect place for a fun evening in the Gulch.  We'll be back!

name: Musicians Corner
text: Awesome music and a beautiful park with great places to sit, ample shade, and some beer vendors on a hot day.  What can be better than listening to music in the park on a beautiful summer day?!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My fiancé and I have gone here for special events 2 years apart. It was the same experience each time - incredible. Because of this last experience, I feel the need to do a review. Tonight our young server was above and beyond. Halfway through the night of great live music, we started to notice an older gentleman making appearances at the tables. Eventually, our original server was nowhere to be found. The older gentleman, who we assume was the manager, had taken over and covered for the server who had fallen ill. At no point did the server disclose he didn't feel well, and continued to give 5 star service. We thought it was very honorable that his manager took over all his tables and sent him home to recuperate, with a seamless transition and continued great experience. We can't wait for the next time. Twice I've had the best steaks I can find in Nashville. 5 stars, only because I can't give 10 stars on Yelp. The food, live music, location, and staff are top notch. Thank you Sambuca.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Ryman is one of the famous stages in Nashville. The history of the Auditorium dates back many years.

Did not come for a show but I wanted to see the site itself.

Huge auditorium, all brick. Built like the historical sites in Philadelphia and Boston. 

Great place to see even if you do not come for a show. You can hear and feel the historical vibes.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: It was graduation day for a couple of universities so they were booked up. In light of the fact that all were reserved parties, they were incredibly under staffed. The service was very slow, the Bloody Mary bar was not maintained, the food was mediocre at best.  Oh, and they ran out of one of the appetizers within 2 hours of opening. They were ill prepared for what they most certainly knew was going to be a busy day. I was embarrassed that I chose this place to celebrate our sons graduation and will not return.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I love this place with a fiery passion.  The tour can be interesting, but I really suggest going to see a show at the Mother Church. Any show, any artist, it doesn't matter.  I went to the Chris Stapleton show this past Friday and was blown away.  This venue is spectacular and Chris was as well.

The acoustics will blow you away.  It is almost as if you don't necessarily 'hear' the music as much as you feel it.  That is what makes this place truly special.  Crowds are usually fairly tame as the church Pugh seating makes it difficult to get up and move around too much, although some will try.  

The new renovations go very well with the venue and have only added to the charm.  Go to the Ryman for a show, you'll be glad you did.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Only true authentic place on Broadway. Cheap bar food that is out of this world. Cheap beer and cool place to meet the locals!

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is my favorite bar on broadway. Classic honky tonk style country music. Bands are great and the bartenders are fun. The loft is a secret treasure.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
You can honky tonk this place and experience the "old" country music . The country music with the twang. 
The environment is pleasant , homey, and a mamma and poppa store. 
The hamburger is basic and fries the same. 
What's bonus of this place is its environment.
Def worth the visit .

name: Robert's Western World
text: A little disappointed with this place. The music was okay, we found much better music in some of the other places on Broadway. As for drinks, the selection is not that extensive for hard liquor. I wanted some johnnie walker black and they didn't have any. Overall, it was just okay the night we went there.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Authentic Nashville! The only place we locals go on Broadway. Some of the best music and cheapest beer in town. Make sure to get the "Stimulus Package." You won't be sorry.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
One of my hands down favorite bars I've ever been to! We got a recommendation to come here and were really excited as we heard its pretty old school Honky Tonk. On a Saturday night there's dancing in the front and it's absolutely packed so be prepared to be packed like a sardine. We managed to get a table near the bar but it was really hard to 1) find the one bartender and 2) catch the "waitress" as she would come at completely random times since she was overwhelmed. 

The old school music makes this place. The fiddle solos alone are great enough to make you swoon! I'm not even a huge fan of old school country but these bands had me tapping my feet. I also loved how cheap beers were- 2 beers were only $7 (PBR is $2). My only regret is not getting a recession special (fried bologna, chips, and a PBR for $6).

Absolutely love this spot! Stop in!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I went with some work colleagues and had the grilled red snapper ettoufee and the sopapilla cheesecake. Both were delicious! The band was excellent fun too!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Saw Shinedown there this week....seating leaves a lot to be desired (too crowded in the pews) our seats were under the balcony ( it was like a scrunched dugout), that with the warm temperature in the place made me so claustrophobic I had to go stand in an open area at the back. Probably won't go back.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Excellent meal, service and music.    Everything was cooked to perfection.   Service was at our pace.  Never rushed nor slow.   Our server, Emerson offered great selection and was very attentive.  Chris Matthews band was a nice variety and relatable with the audience.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: So I felt I was in the world of Mexico in the Plaza Mariachi. It was a happy feel good vibe inside and the best night life I have encountered in Nashville and surrounding area. It was the perfect end to a busy day at the The 21st Galactic Expo. Watching the dancing     was supremely fun.  I loved going inside the little dress shops too. I really want to visit this place in the day time and go to the little restaurants and boutiques with friends.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Went with a group of 8 the evening after Thanksgiving.  Were promptly seated at the table that had been requested days before.  We were upstairs with a view of the stage.  
The band was good and did get loud at times.  However, they were very entertaining. You are charged $2.00 each on your tab for the entertainment.
Our waiter, as well as back up support, were perfect.  Waters immediately.  Waiter knew the menu and he also advised of the specials.  He was good with keeping up with each tab.  
Food was good for all.  One or two even said theirs was great.  Linda Lou had the Sea Bass and loved it.  I had the ahi tuna seared with a bowl of the shrimp/crab bisque.  Ahi was perfect.  The soup was bland.  
Good selection of craft cocktails and craft beers.  
We will go back again.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Tried to go to Tootsies but it was so busy I couldn't even get a drink so I ended up next door here at 2nd Fiddle.  That was the best decision made.  This place is great. Good music, good drinks and great bar staff (Jessica et al). I came in here on my own and was soon talking with a bunch of people. Everyone was super friendly and just made you feel welcome. It became my go to place on Broadway and is now easily my place to go and hang when in town. Thanks all for a great time!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
3.5 Experience 
Nothing Spectacular. We hit this place for Happy Hour. 
Half price drinks and apps!
