The wait time was a bit long for drinks, but worth the wait! Aloha Sunrise was super delicious the only thing better would have been drinking this on the beach! 

I ordered the shrimp and crap dip- it was tasty! I didn't taste the shrimp, but overall good! 
It was very fresh.

The band was interesting- not what I had pictured and played a range of music. Not to loud either. 

Running a bit late to meet the girls, I grabbed a parking spot on the adjacent corner ($20). Good if you are going to be in the area til midnight, but you may wanna cruise if you are just popping in.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Really good food and excellent experience. They had a lot of good performing acts. Authentic Mexican food too

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I loved the atmosphere and how quickly we got our food!! The live music was lovely and the food was good. Didn't necessarily like the Mac and cheese but the shrimp and crab soup was lovely

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: 4.5 stars.  It's a pretty cool indoor plaza.  It's like, a big Hispanic shopping plaza.  This was my second time at this plaza.  I came when they first opened and thought it was pretty neat.  You walk in, and it's like, a big food court with different vendors from different places.  There's also a game room, and a bar.  There is live music, and entertainment in the middle of the food court while you eat.  There is also a grocery store inside, and different kinds of shopping stores inside this plaza.  There's even a radio station in there.  Great plaza to check out if you're in the Nashville area.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Ryman is an event unto itself and not to be missed.  Steeped in music history, the Ryman is the birthplace of bluegrass and the heart of country music.  If you're visiting Nashville, put this at the top of your to do list.  It doesn't really matter who's performing the night you're there.  Consider it a bonus if the performer is someone you actually want to see.  They're all good (they have to be in order to get a date at the Ryman).

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Live band music! Delicious food and wine.  It will be my go-to place when I am in Nashville.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I hadn't been to this place in years and now I have stopped by twice in a month for happy hour. Good special on their drinks with some good prices. They also have some good music. One time with a live band and the other with a DJ.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great dive bar with good music and reasonably priced beer. We loved the music enough here to stay for a couple of beers.  Would definitely go back!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Here for chinese new years celebration plenty of food options that look good havent chosen a place to eat yet but asking people about their food options everyone says all the food is great and good portions...would recommend this place because it has plenty of options...

name: Legends Corner
text:
The Good: Music and people watching.

The Bad: Beer was not cold; area behind the bar was dirty.

The Rest: stopped in after dinner at The Southern for an after meal beer and music. Had a bottle of Laginitus IPA and it was warm :( Music was good. Crowd was moderate. I left after one drink.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place is great.  Cheap beer, grill at the bar and awesome music.  Great small bar where everyone was friendly. The staff was super even when slammed. $2.50 Busch lattes and good music..best in town. We will be back!

name: Legends Corner
text: My wife and I started out here, music was great but a bouncer (named Chris) was on a power trip or it's just shady practice to keep people out after they order drinks. Luckily we went to the stage on broadway right after and enjoyed the rest of the night.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: I had the pleasure of visiting this fantastic American city for 6 days and had a beer (Or three) in almost every one of the honky tonks on Broadway. For a number of reasons, this one makes the top 3. The quality of the musicians and the standard of the bands was immense. The bar staff were friendly and knew their stuff. I didn't eat here but the food that I did see arriving at tables looked amazing. Very clean toilets. Another bar upstairs and a cheeky little smoking area. Good screens for sports fans as well. All in all a great place on the strip. I indulged in 6 visits in 6 days! Enjoy live music? Enjoy The Tin Roof.

name: Robert's Western World
text: My mainstay watering hole during my trips to Nashville.  I try to avoid Broadway with the exception of a few places. Roberts, Second Fiddle, Layla's, and Legends. Sometimes Tootsies.  All at the corner of 5th and Broadway.  The place has all the charm you'd expect from and old school music hall and bar.  Go there for the early shows to see real Nashville. Stay later to see the house band, Don Kelly, cover some outlaw country classics. While the food selection is limited it is awesome. THE BEST fried baloney sammich or an awesome cheeseburger with all the fixings. No fries, chips! Good selection of beers but it really is a PBR kinda place.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Amazing live music. Their ocean water is great. The Broadway superstar is good too but the raspberry was a bit syrupy.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Love this place!!! Jessica the bartender is so sweet and fun. Always have a terrific time. Steer clear of all the gimmicky places. If there is a big time country singers name on the door u can pretty much know it's crappy. Places like this are what makes Nashville amazing. Thanks Jess!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: From my understanding, this place is not always open, but I was here in early December and was lucky enough to see a show. The music was great and the energy of the performers was fun, positive, uplifting, and just made you want to dance. Surprised by the performance by Luke Brian at the end of the night. This experience really turned my NY/NJ daughter of an immigrant attitude toward understanding the love of country music! The establishment is actually quite active on social media, surprising! The whole of the building was not as much as I had anticipated; I thought to show up an hour early to tour the building, but you definitely do not need to do that. Also, the seats are mega uncomfortable, but it's fine. All seats are not created equal, some places do not see all parts of the stage. And don't even think about sneaking to an empty seat mid-show, they will find you. It was very interesting to hear the live radio advertisements being made.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place was just incredible the live band was amazing the drinks were good the atmosphere was awesome. Would recommend coming here if you're a outer Towner like me.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This is for sure see on anyone Country bucket list. However don't expect more, by paying for guided tours than self guided. Yes you get to go back stage. However it is very rushed, and for what you pay, I felt like you should be able to soak it all in. So much history and wonderful music I wanted to share with my 15 year old, but was off and running and back to self guided in less than 30+ minus I would guess.
Giving a little more info to what you get for your money would be s great thinf.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Very enjoyable tour of the historic theatre. We paid extra for the guided tour, and it was worth it for the behind-the-scenes access.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
So much history at the Ryman! The exterior and interior still resemble the church it originated from, giving it a lot of charm. There is something comforting about sitting in a church pew and listening to some great music. 

I rate the Ryman a 3 because you have to be careful where you sit. The main floor has many pillars holding up the balcony that can directly impede your view if you didn't choose your seat wisely. My suggestion is to  sit further up on the main floor or get balcony seats because if you sit under the balcony, your view will be impeded at some point during the show. 

Despite this, the Ryman is a must and it has never disappointed me!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: After reading some recent negative reviews, I almost didn't go to this great place. But since I was staying at the Thompson Nashville a half block away and it was raining intermittently, I decided I'd rather walk than drive. The place was excellent, from ambience to service to food and live band. Anastasia was our server and super pleasant and helpful. The steaks and seafood and desserts were so good. I'm a bit of a foodie, but not hypercritical, and they did a nice job, about $80 per head after tip and that included entree, several drinks, and dessert but we didn't do appetizer bc we didn't want to be too stuffed. All in all a satisfying, enjoyable visit. Thanks, Sambuca!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Madison Square Garden of Country Music, such a great and historic place. The tour is outstanding and I highly recommend to everyone who goes to the Nashville area. We went on the self guided tour, and saw everything that we wanted, including going on the stage. Have to get back there to go a show.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Was fun visiting there. Music was very good.  Food was ok and i guess one doesn't go there mainly for the food. All said and done, go there and enjoy a beer and the music. Staff was very welcoming.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: So I'm giving Sambuca a 5 star rating because of our server (Tyler). Here's the story....we had drinks at Sambuca in the afternoon. After leaving, one in our party realized she had lost her credit card. We called Sambuca. The person who answered the phone seemed un-interested in our plight so we got back in a cab and returned to Sambuca. Tyler ( who had not been informed of the phone call) looked through all of his receipt books until he found it! He then refused a tip! Thanks Tyler!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
This place was recommended by friends. However, the service was AWFUL!. Our waiter, Ken, neglected us all night. After bringing us our initial drink order, no one checked on us for over a half hour. With long empty drink glasses, I had to flag down another server and ask them to find our waiter for us. When he finally came by, he apologized for the delay, took our second drink order, and assured us our food would be out soon.

After being seated for over an hour, he brings out -- our entrees. I asked what happened to our appetizer? He apologized for forgetting and offered to get it for us. But, it was too late by then.

Since it was my wife's birthday, I asked for some cake with a candle (which another table near us had received earlier). And, we also ordered another desert to share. But another half hour later, it still hadn't arrived. I flagged Ken down from serving another table and signaled for him to bring my check. He offered to bring our desert boxed up to-go. But, I just told him to cancel it and bring the bill.

Viewing the bill, they at least didn't charge for the appetizer they forgot or the desert that never came. But, considering the poor service, I would have expected some kind of consolation, such as comp'ing a round of drinks or something.  

The experience ruined our birthday celebration. I will never return.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
What a wonderful event we had at Sambuca in Nashville!!!

We had a rather large party for dinner - a gathering of family in town for a wedding - and we couldn't have been happier with the setting, the food, the music, and the way we were taken care of by our server Jesse.  (Everytime someone left the table, Jesse would fold up there napkin into a beautiful rose :) )

We had a variety of four appetizers and each one was better than the next.  I don't think you can go wrong there.  As for dinner - it was the best sea bass I've ever had.  My husband gave me a bit of his scallops and they were awesome too.  All 15 of us loved our dinners.

A special thanks to the manager Casey who visited us to be sure we had everything we wanted, which we did.

Thanks Sambuca!  You will be on my list whenever I visit Nashville!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Roman Auditorium is the true birthplace of the country music variety show...that is before the Grand Ole Opry was completed. The round stage, in fact, was donated to the latter to provide some continuity when the music moved elsewhere.  A great tour and colorful history should be on any Nashville list.  It's well worth it.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Ryman is a must see if you are in town! I do wish we booked the guided tour to hear more about the history.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is the Broadway honkey tonk you want to visit.  

It is as old school as it gets in the land (street) of new neon bars that us locals recommend.   

Go in for the classic country and stay for the grilled food -- grilled cheese, fried baloney sandwich -- you must check out the food menu! 

**you can't miss the "recession special" on the menu for $6 - PBR + chips + fried baloney sandwich

name: Robert's Western World
text: Stopped here for lunch while traveling through Nashville with family. The food was good bar food. The pork chop sandwich was tasty and hot, and the onion rings were outstanding. It's no-frills food and the menu is pretty small, but that wasn't a problem for us. The service was fast and extremely friendly. It's definitely got a cool dive-bar type feel. The live music was excellent, authentic classic country (shout-out to Rachael Hester and the Tennessee Walkers, who were nearing the end of a 3-hour set when we got there). It's relatively small inside, but there is a small balcony if you can't find a place to sit on the ground floor. I would highly recommend this place and would definitely come back if we're in the area again.

name: Second Fiddle
text:
Such a great experience to visit this bar. The band (on the night of 8/7/13) played classic country songs, and the singer was talented, yet funny enough to entertain the crowd. He came off the stage and walked around, partly to collect tips but also interact with the people in the bar.
The bartenders were friendly, and prompt in serving drinks and snacks that we ordered.

With numerous Honky Tonk bars on Broadway in Nashville, The Second Fiddle will surely be my first recommendation to anyone that is in town and wants to listen to authentic country music. There is a little dance floor for those of you that are looking to swing the hips. The interior is cool, with antique radio receivers and instruments decorating the walls.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Want an authentic country music bar that seems to have bachelorette party repellant hanging over the door? So did I, and that's exactly what I found at Roberts. Reasonably priced, good crowd of all ages, and great old country tunes. Loved my time here.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Yes to the Bologna Sandwich!  Simple...but delicious. My husband ordered the turkey and Swiss.  He regretted not getting the fried bologna...like I suggested he should. I let him have a bite...but I didn't share. I wanted it all to myself. It was so good!
Don't make the same mistake my husband did.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
Plaza Mariachi is a great concept and i was very excited to come here for the first time on a Friday night. The interior is very nice, new and clean. I wasn't able to fully explore but spent most of my time in main food court area. Overall, I wasn't blown away by my experience but will highlight the hits and misses. 
The food court is really nice with a big stage and live music. I really enjoyed the ambiance and the music was fantastic. That was definitely a highlight of the night. 
Our first stop (obviously) was to grab a drink at the stand set up in the food court. They had wine, palomas, margaritas and beer. We ordered a margarita and a paloma, and I liked the paloma a lot more than the margarita but unfortunately the grapefruit juice was out of a can and not fresh. The margarita was also missing something... I can't quite put my finger on it but I really didn't like it. 
Everyone was raving about Tres Gauchos and it had by far the longest line in the entire place. We were pretty hungry so we stopped at the tapas place to get a snack, Las Tablas. Unfortunately they immediately told us they were out of most of the menu so we were limited on what we could order. Luckily we were able to get some manchego cheese with honey and patatas bravas. Both were very good. 
I decided to skip the slow moving line of Tres Gauchos and opted for Botanas Lokas instead; the Mexican snack stand which had tacos, street corn, candy and other small bites. I tried the chicken, pork, and barbacoa tacos and liked them. The street corn was fantastic and I liked the pork taco but the other two were just OK. Honestly, I would have much preferred the taco trucks that are right down the street on Nolensville Road. 
I sampled some of the meats from Tres Gauchos, and wasn't a fan. Not only did you have to wait in line a long time to order, it took another 20 minutes or so for the food to come out. Expect to wait if you eat here! The chimichurri options were good (especially the spicy one) and the steak was definitely better than the chicken which was overcooked and didn't have much flavor. The street corn was not good either, but the empanada was delicious. They aren't on the menu and may have been a special of the night. 
The pistachio ice cream was very tasty for dessert and overall I still like the concept and think it has potential, but some of the food was a definite let down. I'd come back but would make different selections.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I was really excited to go here for our nice dinner out for my bachelorette weekend but was left hungry and extremely disappointed. Our server was the only bright light in the whole situation. 
We sat down ordered drinks, and received them quickly, our mixed drinks were delicious. Then we ordered our salads, soups, apps and entrees. Salads and soups came out quickly but after 30-40minutes our apps (bruschetta and the goat cheese stuff artichokes) still were not out. When they did arrive after we complained on not getting them, the artichokes were room temperature at best but we were hungry so we ate them.
Then our entrees didn't make it out until almost an hour after we ordered them. Once they arrived we were ready to dig in only to find that they were cold. The flat iron wasn't cooked and was raw, the Au gratin potatoes were totally uncooked. My risotto was tasteless and was hard and room temperature. We were so hungry but we all barely ate our dinners because it was cold and frankly inedible.
We complained and after going back an forth they comped all the food but we still left hungry and disappointed in what was supposed to be a nice dinner out to celebrate my bachelorette.
We paid for the drinks we ordered and took good care of our server because it was not a fault of his.
They really need to get their kitchen together, the kitchen will be the demise of this place.
If I were you I would think 10 times before going here for dinner.

name: Robert's Western World
text: If you want blues and Country music, you must come here.  It is a dive bar with a grill.  My top two of bats if you are coming to Nashville.  Well unless your not a country fan.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This was one of my favorite stops during my week in Nashville! Great live music on every floor, and a great place to hang out. It WILL get crowded as the night goes on, so we got there a little earlier in the evening since we wanted stools

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Truth be told, I was skeptical that this somewhat snobby LA girl was going to fare well in a honky tonk, After all, I've never owned cowgirl boots and only know a handful of mainstream country songs...Carrie Underwood, Keith Urban, and anything else that makes the LA radio waves....you get the picture.  Anyway, I walk into Roberts and I'm blown away, not only by the diverse crowd (age, gender, race) but by the super cool old school band that was playing!  Tons of people dancing (old and young and both really good).  The availability of seats and the super sweet waitress.  I went ahead and ordered two Recession specials, one for me and one for my boss, because I was being funny. ($5 for bologna sandwich, PBR and a bag of lays). Our waitress advised me to upgrade and add cheese and grilled onions, so I did just that.  I don't think my boss and I have ever scarfed down something so quickly!  That fried bologna sandwich was scrumptious!  The music was fabulous and the atmosphere was sheer fun for a Wednesday night.  
I know this side of Broadway is not the "cool" side, but it was a great time and when I come back, Robert's is on my radar!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Sambuca without a doubt has one of the best happy hours in Music City! My friend and I decided that we needed to try it based on the prices alone. Many of the happy hour cocktail prices are between $5-6 each. I had the Sambuca 75 for my first cocktail which was a mixture of vodka, champagne and a fruit puree. It wasn't too sweet which I liked. For my second cocktail I got the Tennessee mule which was also good and not overly sweet. My friend and I split the bruschetta which was a light appetizer with a tomato mixture and crostini. 

If I had to pinpoint the patrons here I'd say mostly a 40s and older crowd but the atmosphere is nice. There was live music which wasn't too loud and we could still have a conversation. The food and drink was all good, the atmosphere was pleasant and the service was excellent. The server knew her drinks and I liked her recommendations. 

I'm not sure if I'd come back here just simply because it wasn't exactly my type of scene but the happy hour is very very good!

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text:
Ooooh, another great, cozy venue to sit and chill and listen to some great music in this city.....
People don't stand up in front of you.
Most seats have excellent viewing and listening.
Drinks weren't terribly expensive.
Bathroom was clean.
Acoustics were very good.

This is one of those places you like to bring out of town friends to.
This one and the Bluebird.

name: Legends Corner
text:
This bar is still great 2 years later. 
Music and staff was on point.! 
And prices are good, good amount is seats and nice dance floor. No cover,great looking spot inside and out
Can't wait to go back on my next Nashville trip.!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Just shy of being a dive bar (imo) I'm giving this place 5 stars for what it is. Awesome cheap food (grilled cheese, grilled bologna sandwiches, fries, etc.) 

We had a problem with our food being given to another table? And then not getting all of our fries, instead getting too many bags of chips. Their method has no madness to it with different servers bringing different things instead of a server to a table. But that doesn't really impede your experience if you have the time to wait, because they're more than willing to fix their mistakes and really nice about it! 

Live country music! I'd definitely hit this place again next time in Nashville!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This would be an absolutely brilliant place to go to lunch. Their recession special is a steal. Unfortunately it requires you either be unemployed or have an hour and a half lunch break and work right next door in order to obtain it when there are 21 other people in the place.

They will keep you in beers until your food heats up in the fryer, and there's generally a good musician playing, although you could luck out like I did on my last visit and have the epitomy of "guy just trying to make it i the music business" who would be charged with murder if any of the singers he was covering were still alive today.

Slow, music, good divey place. It's the sort of place you like to dislike, and like to prove your dislike by patronizing. Or something.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Probably my favorite place in Nashville just because they have cheap beer, old school country music and fried bologna sandwiches. 

The quality of the music is always off the hook. Simple place, but simply awesome.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
A must stop on your Lower Broadway barhop.  Since there are tons of reviews about this place, here's my brief thoughts.

Free admission.

Decently strong drinks.

Cowboy boots on the wall, perhaps for sale?  I couldn't tell.

Always a good band, usually with a upright bass which is, of course, festive.  Tip the band - no admission so go ahead and give them some bucks so they can pay rent or buy some beer.

Totally packed out on the weekends but on weeknights much more manageable.  Plus if you are a tourist you don't have anything to do the next day right?  Drink up!

That's all you have to know.  Then you can stumble out and hit up another honky tonk.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This is the worst bar ever. My friends and I went here and we just turned 21, and the bouncers after a long while of us being in there kicked us out of the bar because they thought we were faking our age and thought our ID's were fake even though they were very much real and the bouncers thought we looked "too young" to be in there. I explained to the bouncer that what he said to us about looking too young even though we were of legal drinking age was "discriminating" and he kicked us out because he thought we were lying and because he got called out. He then towards the end proceeds to snatch out drinks away when we paid good money for them. I felt extremely disrespected and I'm very disappointed my friends and I were treated this way. Do not recommend and do not go here.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
A genuine Honky Tonk bar with live music and quick serving bar keeps. The cheese burger probably saved my night, as it's hailed as the best burger. It was good for the record. Music was great and the environment was fun. 

Visit this place if on the Boardwalk.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great burgers and sweet potato fries! Live music playing all the time. We went for lunch, so good crowd...not sure if sorority scene comes at night. You don't want to miss this stop!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Everyone should see a show at the Ryman every time they visit Nashville! It's amazing! The setting is so small and intimate. There isn't a bad seat in the place. It's a truly wonderful experience!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Cool concept, nice temperature, inviting atmosphere, and very good food.  Not may cool shopping options.  I love the food market also.  I will come back with family and friends on the next time.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Holy Grail of music venues. The nostalgia, atmosphere, and acoustics were just unbelievable. It sounds so good here. We came here to see the Local Natives and they sounded exactly as they do on the album. It really was as if I were listening to them on my music playing device! The staff here is awesome. They do not police people around like I have seen at other venues. They have ample restrooms and bar areas. I never waited to use the restroom or did I wait longer than two minutes in line for a beer. The ushers were very helpful by making sure everyone knew where they were going. Seating was by old school church pews, but they were surprising comfy and they are well spaced so no elbow touching and shoulder grazing with the creepy unknowns. This is hands down the best music venue I have ever attended.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
***The Grand Ole Opry and Ryman Auditorium are two very historic parts of the Nashville music scene; while a lot of the music is old-fashioned, the Grand Ole Opry is still a must experience if you are a music fan***

Ryman Auditorium is one of the country's most historic and well known music venues.  Ryman is located right in Downtown Nashville (next to bar and lounges that explode with live country rock music).  It is also the original home to the nation's longest running radio show the Grand Ole Opry and even runs the Grand Ole Opry for a select few shows of the year before the Grand Ole Opry relocates to its newer and bigger home--the Grand Ole Opry House.  The Grand Ole Opry House is near the Gaylord Opryland Resort (a few miles outside of Downtown Nashville).

I went to the Ryman Auditorium for a Grand Ole Opry performance and it is a unique experience.  You can purchase tickets at the box office the night of the show.  If you get there early, the Ryman Auditorium has a small and very crowded gift shop, which sells lots of Ryman Auditorium and Grand Ole Opry souvenirs.

Ryman has a few concession stands that sell reasonably priced food with generous portions though the quality is mediocre.  The concession stand here serves hot dogs, chicken tenders, popcorn, various candies, caramel popcorn, bottled water, soft drinks, and alcohol.

The auditorium itself has a lot of history.  With the decor as well as the memorabilia on display, you can feel the age and the history of this venue.  You can feel it in the seats too.  The seats are actually long hard wood benches.  They are not very comfortable and they can be a little tight depending on who is in your row and how many layers of clothes they are wearing.  The venue has a mezzanine section (some seats have obstructed views) and a balcony.

The show has a fairly interesting setup.  The show is broken up into four parts/acts and each part is hosted by a Grand Ole Opry member, who also performs the opening and closing song for each act.  The host then introduces performers for each act.  The hosts tend to be more well-known than a lot of the other performers, but there is an incredible variety of performers as at least eight different artists/groups perform each night at the Grand Ole Opry.

Since the show is a radio show, there were also sponsored ads performed live by the show's standard radio announcers.  The ads featured brands like Cracker Barrel, a dollar store and a boot retailer and some of the ads were even unintentionally kind of funny.

The show was interesting even if you are not a fan of country music (there was a mix of more modern country music as well as some very old timey country music).  In addition to the wide variety of acts that performed, the hosts and the performers had a very familiar camaraderie that resulted in a lot of comedy as well as a very casual, intimate and family feel.  The familiar and jokey banter made me feel that like I was just spending a weekend with these artists at a large gathering.

In terms of the live music, the venue was nice.  The acoustics were very pleasing and the music really fills the big space.  The acts themselves were good too though how much you like it depends on how much you like this style of music.  Still, for non-country music fans, it was fun seeing country music legend Vince Gill and American Idol star Lauren Alaina perform.  It was also a unique treat to see Tennessee's state song Rocky Top performed by the artists who originally recorded that song.

Service was very good on my visit; the staff was friendly and polite.

Ticket prices are reasonable and can be a real value depending on who is performing though there is very short notice on a lot of the performers.

Live music is a major part of the Nashville experience.  There are definitely more contemporary and exciting music elsewhere in Nashville, but Ryman Auditorium and the Grand Ole Opry are still very signature elements of the Nashville music scene.  Though this style of music as well as some of the commentary that occurs throughout the show is not for all tastes, the Ryman Auditorium is still a very unique experience and a must visit if you are a music fan.

There are several pay parking structures around the Ryman Auditorium.  I believe the parking structure adjacent to the Ryman Auditorium is $10 per vehicle.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: A beautiful and intimate venue. Beyond classy. Always a great time.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
This isn't fine dining, but its fun and has a great atmosphere.  The food is pretty good and they usually have a pretty talented band.  Its a fun enough place, that it should be more crowded.

My only complaint about this place is that the mgr. has the waitress seat people in some of the worst side tables, even when the place is nearly empty and the other tables were not reserved.
The table was so bad, we dined at the bar and watched the band.  I won't go back if they don't start changing this.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
No Passport Needed

From the time you step out of your vehicle and walk the few steps from the parking lot to the main entrance, you begin to feel there's something different about this place. Perhaps it's the neat decor in what was once a run-down food store in a strip mall. Perhaps it's the lively music constantly being piped outdoors...and that music continues indoors as you step into a beautifully decorated mini streets scene. Maybe it's the alfresco cafe with its enticing aromas just to your left before you enter.

Questions? There's an Information booth right inside the main entrance. And there are plenty of assistants and Security Personnel throughout the area to guide you to ... to wherever or for whatever you need ... the bathrooms perhaps? (Located in the street--hallway to the right of the large stage in the Food Court.)

Walking into Plaza Mariachi, I was immediately transported to some of the tiny villages and small shopping areas I've visited all over the world. The lighting, the ambiance, the sights and smells are both subdued and vibrant at the same time. The decor is absolutely spot-on with gaily decorated wall art, plants, and paisajes (landscapes). Please take time to look and admire the effort that went into the planning of this amazing venue...a little slice of Latin America - Mexico right here in Nashville!

Entertainment? They've got it. Live music much of the time with acts ranging from Mariachi Bands to solo performers to trios and more. The acts are ever-changing and also include daily performances by jugglers and acrobats performing above the Food Court... maybe right next to your table! (Check the calendar on the website.)

Food? Yes they've got it. Try some mini tacos (teeny 3-inch bites reminiscent of tapas style) at Botanas Locas (Crazy Snacks). Or, walk across the spacious Food Court area to the Tienda Bar for a cold cerveza. Maybe you're in the mood for a steaming cup of hot Madera Coffee? If so, go ahead and grab a Cuban sandwich while you're there - they're located near the back (or is it front?) of the Food Court, opposite the stage.  

Maybe you're in the mood for a cold, refreshing, and healthy, fresh-made Zoomito Juice (I had a tantalizing apple, carrot, and cilantro) or a bowl of cold ceviche or... tapas at Las Tablas Tapas? 

I grabbed a generously filled, lightly spiced Gyro with Lamb and Chicken and grilled onions at Kouzina Café, then sat down to listen to a rising Colombian star, Marcela Pinella....oh my!

Maybe you'll want to play with the kids at Tito's Playland (arcade)? I'm sure they will!

The side hallways (aka streets) are filled with an eclectic collection of stores: an Art Gallery, a Cellular Provider, a salon, Insurance Company, a Radio Station broadcast booth (Activa 1240), clothing stores, ice cream (oughta have something sweet to sustain you on your journey), along with many, many, many more.

On your way out, you might stop by MazFresco Market, the International Grocery Store, and pick up something to take home - fresh fish or meat, while choosing from a wealth of Latin American fresh baked goods and packaged products. 

¿Listo? Ready?

Púes, ahora tienes tu oportunidad de hacer un viaje a América Latina justo aquí en Nashville. ¡Cierto! 

(Well, now's your chance to take a trip to Latin America right here in Nashville. Really!)

By the way, the Mariachi Band today played a full set of lively Mexican music...and ended with their version of "Rocky Top!' How appropriate for this marvelous mix of cultural creativity.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Had an early Sunday dinner at Samba recently, which was an altogether enjoyable experience. Live music was very nice, service was good and the blackened red snapper étouffée was off-the-hook tasty! Will be back.

name: The Basement
text:
SOUND:  Honestly it sounds great!  

CLEAN:  No, it always feels sticky like whatever you touch or graze by, maybe bring some wet-naps haha!

DOOR:  I don't know, I've only ever been "on the list" with a guy that plays drums with bands.

SIZE:  I think it can pack a lot of people in, and there are some random tables and chairs.

TIP:  Go early if you want a SEAT. 

DRINKS:  I feel like they are pretty affordable, usually $5 or more. I haven't had a liquor drink, I usually get a beer and it's always been great.  Not sure how good the liquor drinks are and how the pours are.  Not sure I could recommend anything other than a bottle of something.

Overall, if there's someone you want to see here you should definitely come by!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
[TLDR]A former roadside motel converted into a country-style restaurant serving stick to your ribs entrees, breakfast all day, and the best biscuits I have ever had [/TLDR]

I have been reading about this place for many years trip reports and local assessments on Roadfood.com, most especially about the biscuits, and finally made the trip down here this past week

The food there is very good.  Not great, not mind blowing, but good.  In terms of what is available on the menu, it is very similar to Cracker Barrels; but I think most every item (except the mac-n-cheese, which was surprisingly meh) here is a notch or three better than what you'd find there.

The option to dine family style is available here for groups of 4 or more

While the food did not blow me away, the biscuits most certainly did.  Moist, fluffy, delicious -- perfect.  These are served as the free bread basket and you can ask for as many refills as you'd like, and every plateful includes three different homemade jams - strawberry, blackberry, and peach, and all three are wonderful - plus real butter.  For the best experience, I'd advise ordering minimally - a little protein of your choice and a veggie side or two, or maybe a bowl of sausage gravy, and just let those biscuits be the focus of your meal.   A little tip: ask for extra jam with your biscuits, as they tend to be a tad stingy with the portions on the jams, and trustme, you'll want more.

If a place like this existed locally, we'd absolutely be regulars there.

One caveat - this place is VERY loud, even when not filled to capacity.  It is very popular and you should expect a wait to be seated even during non peak hours

5+ stars for the biscuits, everything else was 3 to 4, so overall 4 stars

Recommended

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The staff is awesome. They are super friendly and will take good care of you after waiting so long for a table. Expect to wait 2 hours or more for a table. Have no fear. They have things to keep you busy while you wait. Like a couple of gift shops to explore, a huge barn to hang out in on cold days and the property is enough to enjoy the scenery. Your table will be ready in no time.

The food comes out fast. EVERYTHING IS AMAZING! The fried chicken is my favorite with cheesy hash. I love this place. If I am ever near the Nashville proximity I will make the trip to Loveless Cafe. This place is made for foodies. Must go!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I have had this on my "to try" list for a while now- my hubby HATES to wait and was hesitant to come.  We got here at 8:30 on Saturday morning and we got a front parking spot AND were escorted right to our table as we walked in . 

My 2 year old got milk, pancakes, and bacon- which he refused to eat.  Hubby took them home and said they were great.  Hubby got the sampler platter and said everything was great.  I got the city ham with egg whites (and didn't really care either- my ham was burnt and my eggs were wet and not very appetizing), but the biscuits and preserves were amazing and so was that hash brown casserole.  

We had a great breakfast and would come again for sure.  We also enjoyed walking around afterwards.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing southern comfort food. Good service. If you are visiting Tennessee this  is a must!!! Highly recommended. Will leave you stuffed lol. The biscuits are sooooo good and always served warmed. Freshly baked out the oven. Do not forget to ask for honey. It has to be requested. Big menu to choose from. #carbNation

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Lots to love at the Loveless Cafe. As the Mrs. noted, the bowl filled with pats of butter is a great harbinger of good things to come. As in, good things to spread that butter on. As in delicious biscuits. Also accompanying those biscuits is their signature strawberry, blackberry, and peach preserves. And when we finished those off, our waitress Robin brought us more, which we boxed up and took home with us.

Mrs. ordered the pork chops, which came with three, two of which went home for a future dinner. Her caramelized sweet potatoes were quite good, and the creamed corn may be the best side they make. It's certainly one of their most popular. I had the grilled catfish, none of which survived to go home in the doggy bag. Wonderful seasoning. Mac and cheese was fine, the southern grits outstanding. 

Adult beverages are available. Their featured drinks center around local moonshine which comes in a little take home souvenir mug. I opted for for the sweet peach tea moonshine and loved it. There are also many dessert choices. Mrs. had the Blueberry and Peach cobbler, of course warmed and served a la mode. I had the honey chess pie. Both most satisfying. Robin took good care of us. We had a minimal wait time, maybe 10 minutes, but there is a gift shop and general store to occupy your time which beats just sitting on a bench. 

The only knock against the Loveless may be that it's just so far from the city, you really have to go out of your way to eat there. But it was undoubtedly worth the trip.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Worth the trip and the wait.  Plenty to do while you wait with shops, etc.  Lots of places to wait.  The biscuits truly are amazing.  You'll get a big platter of them when you are seated.  I had catfish sandwich on texas toast.  It was good but the star is really the biscuits.  Had 2 sliders, a fried chicken biscuit and a pulled pork biscuit.  Pulled pork was a+++ .  Definitely go check this place out.  Wait was about an hour on a rainy saturday for brunch.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: After reading the Wikipedia entry on this place, maybe my expectations were too high (read it sometime), but the biscuits were not that good.  The country ham was way too salty (I am from the South, I know what biscuits and ham are supposed to taste like).  It was pretty much standard Waffle House fare.  One saving grace - the preserves that go ON the biscuits were great.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
OMG!!!  What an amazing breakfast!!!!     Came on a Wednesday morning at about 10 AM and had just about a 15 minute wait for a table of 6 which I didn't feel was very bad at all!!!  Waitress was very nice and the food came out in a very timely fashion considering it was somewhat busy.  
The biscuits came out and were the best I've ever had.  Warm and moist. Served with sides of fresh apricot, raspberry, and blackberry.  
The little country store was soooo cute.  
A must stop when in Nashville!
Definitely try the cheesy hash browns and the BBQ, so yummy!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best fried chicken and biscuits. We've gone for breakfast too and had the best experience. The environment is nice and cozy - especially in the smaller dining rooms. I can't wait to go back for a quiet morning with a warm breakfast. The shops are fun too. I had to buy some jam to take home.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits were amazing! Our server brought us a plate of warm biscuits, which were great, but then brought us a plate of MORE biscuits straight out of the oven... heaven! Especially with butter and preserves. I had the catfish dinner plate with fried okra and fruit. I thought the catfish was well done, as well as the hushpuppies. Unfortunately, I was not a fan of the okra. the breading was very thick and heavy. My boyfriend got the pulled pork sandwich and fries.... (of course I had to try!) and both were delicious. Loved the fries. Can't wait to come back and try the breakfast menu and the desserts.... they look amazing!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Don't order the pancakes unless you like dry thick pancakes then the waffle was a beautiful golden brown as it should be but it was so thick and Doughie waffles should be airy and crispy really a waste of my money and time

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I would definitely put this on par with a Cracker Barrel with larger portions and an extensive  history.  Being that we went midweek in the evening there was little to no wait.  My food was decent.  The biscuits were quite tasty (I may have evaluated about 4...)  I was not blown away by my overall experience but I am open to going back again to try the breakfast.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
There's a lot of good things going at Loveless Cafe, to start, let's do a list:

1. Southern hospitality. We asked our server what's sorghum and without explaining she went ahead and brought 2 containers of plain sorghum and then a bowl of butter and sorghum and mixed it on the table to show us how it should be eaten. Try it if you like molasses or just try it for the sake of trying. Always courteous, shows up at the right time, and splitting checks - no problem. 

2. History and photos.
3. Kitsch and charm.
4. Overall good showcase of southern food: my picks were the butter and fruit jams, biscuits, fried chicken, creamed corn, hashbrown casserole, and slaw.

Country ham (as warned by our server) is VERY salty and a bit tough. Something that I thought would be amazing would be the Banana Pudding was just ok, not much vanilla wafers. Pulled pork was said to be smoked for over 12hrs gave me too much of a high expectation. Fried chicken was good, moist and lightly battered.  Food was on the salty and sweet side. 

The souvenoir shops always leave a slightly bad impression. It's a double edge sword. It's hard to take it seriously as dining, when it is part tourist destination. A long sleeved t-shirt printing of bacon striped jacket - that is pretty sweet!   I know it's all part of the show and indeed they looked like they were doing pretty well selling overpriced goods, so good for them!

Thankfully, we're given a wait time of 35min, just enough time to explore the grounds. As a package, LC should be experienced at least once: 3.3 stars.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Bbq was very good. The biscuits and gravy were very delicious and the people were very nice. I bit of a wait for the table but worth it. There's shops around while you wait so there's something to do. They also serve moonshine drinks and beer, wine and tasty stuff. Its also very pretty around the restaurant lots of roiling hills and nice trees. I recommend going there.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is an excellent place. We went on a Saturday and, honestly, did not expect to get in anytime soon, but we were up for the wait. We have wanted to go for some time now. While waiting we toured the little shops on the campus and found several very cool Christmas presents for friends and family (NOT the corn pone stuff at that Country yatta yatta joint). The service was excellent. The food was wonderful and the biscuits to die for. One of the 10 best breakfast joints EVER!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Yesterday was our third trip to the loveless cafe and it won't be the last.
It was all great as usual
The biscuits were so heavenly and I love the peach preserves
Fried chicken was excellent
My husband got the combo plate chicken, fried catfish and meatloaf.  The sides were all great
The pie so many choices we got the chocolate cream and pecan Excellent
The store was also great
Lots of choices love the biscuit mix , country ham and all preserve choices
Until next time dear friend

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Gemaal, was the best waiter. Very attentive and always on cue with all our needs. We did the five course meal with the wine pairings and it was incredible. I will make this a must do meal every time I'm in Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
So I wanted to love this place so much since my Nashville friends talked about it. This is way far out from the downtown Nashville scene. We arrived at 8 am on a Friday morning and it was about half full (look at that, eternal optimist). We started with biscuits. The biscuits were delicious...For about 30-45 minutes. We then ordered biscuit sliders since we couldn't decide what to pick. The hash brown casserole was really tasty! 

So after our meal, we shopped at the cute stores, which I highly recommend checking out. However, it was about 5 minutes into shopping when our stomachs exploded. Luckily, there are bathrooms on site! I'm glad we tried the food, but I think my stomach isn't equipped to process it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is extremely busy and has had over an hour wait every time I have been here. Which is not too often because the food is really not that great. Yes, it's cute and I like the gift shop, but it's a restaurant. Good food at a good price should keep people coming. On a positive note, servers are really friendly and sweet.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Fantastic.  Can't wait to go back.  Expect a long wait.  We showed up at 1pm and it was still a 45min wait.  Split the Southern Sampler Plater with my wife (fried chicken, catfish, and ham as meats/hash brown casserole and marinated cucumbers and onions for the sides).  Also ordered side of sausage gravy to go with the amazing free biscuits and a pimento and fried green tomato biscuit.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Ignore that guy who said the sound sucked for Psychedelic Furs. I imagine he must have been smoking something gone bad. The sound was perfectly mixed, the seats were fabulous, the ambiance on point, the food was spectacular- risotto balls, pasta and steak had our whole table gushing with every bite ("This is SOOOOO good!"), and the wine, wow, the wine. This place has a sommelier and he knows his shit. The recommendations were perfect. Thank you Nicholas and Josh for the stellar service! And to those whining about the price, all I can say is "duuuuuh!" It's an upscale joint, y'all. If you want to pay less for your food and drink, go to a honky tonk.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We asked "the locals" for breakfast recommendations and this place took the cake, hands down! We were not disappointed!! 

My husband and I and another couple ordered Family Style. This was an all you can eat family style plate table service that included: hash brown casserole, sliced ham, bacon (too smokey for this Northerner), eggs, grits, and the most delicious homemade biscuits and preserves!

I could have eaten a plate of biscuits and preserves all by myself or at least wish I could have if I wasn't filling up in all the other deliciousness! 

Now, there was a wait but here are little shops to visit and free lemonade stand...to be cont...

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I took my mother here for Mother's Day and we ate dinner there before the show and watched Citizen Cope perform afterward. I read on help before that the food wasn't very good and it was true. My mom and I both ordered the burger, which was just okay. However, it's the safest option on the menu so if you're going to eat there then order the burger. We ordered the potatoes Au gratin and they were undercooked. It was disappointing. My mom ordered the Chardonnay on tap and it was just okay. Luckily mom is happy about anything and liked her food and wine. I just expected more for the price. Also, the $20, 2.5 glasses of wine option consisted of maybe a typical glass and a half of wine. It was not much at all. The food overall was a 2.5/5 stars. 
    The waitresses and staff were fine. They could step up their customer service skills and friendliness just a tiny bit more. 
     The music was the best part. Excellent artists. We sat in the middle on the floor and it was still hard to see. Not great acoustics in the place. 
    All the negativity aside, it was a beautiful venue and great concept. If they could improve their acoustics, rewrite their menu, make some staff changes, this place could be the talk of the town.  

 All in all I suggest
1. Bringing $5 cash to valet
2. Order the burger if you're gonna eat there 
3. Save money and eat somewhere else
4. Drink wine there 
5. Sit close so you can see and hear (it's worth spending a bit more) 
Enjoy your time

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Big breakfast, chicken and BBQ menu!   All the food and service was superb.   Plan on a short wait but there's plenty to see and do around the complex.  Smoke house and shop have lots to see.  Several shops with unique gift items from the area, or Loveless recipe products!   Our meals were all very good and large portions.  Fried chicken is to die for!  BBQ and even breakfast all day met everyone's desires.   A cool stop when around Nashville, highly recommended!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Worth the 40 minute drive from where we were staying. I fugured there would be a wait but,  we got right in.  Very friendly staff. The place just makes you feel like you are eating in someone's dining room, so welcoming.  Hot biscuits the minute you sit down and they were amazing. Breakfast was great too though tourist prices. Everything was fresh and well prepared. Cool grounds to walk around too in order to get rid of a few calories before the trip back. Highly reccomended.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I've eaten at Loveless many times, and have had quite a few different dishes, but I'll try to touch on some highs and lows. Long waits are to be expected, especially on weekends and at traditional meal times.

I'm a meatloaf connoisseur. It's one of the dishes I use to judge a restaurant. Theirs is good. Not the best I've had but far from the worst.
The mac n cheese is pretty standard Velveeta and elbow macaroni. 
The creamed corn tastes more like a corn pudding to me...a bit too sweet and custardy. 
Fried green tomatoes are not good. Thin and tough.
Mashed potatoes are good.
Hash brown casserole is decent.
The BBQ pork is good. Not great, but not bad. 
Fried chicken is very good.
Breakfast is always good, though the grits are a disappointment. And the biscuits just haven't been the same since Carol Fay died a few years back.

They have a liquor license. Try the Bloody Mary, then go over to the store and buy a jar of the mix for $10. It's worth it.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Went back after a poor initial visit. Sat down on the main floor for Steve Earle and had a much better experience. The service was attentive, and while we didn't have a full meal, the apps we did order hit the spot. Most importantly, the sound in the room was fantastic, especially great for Steve's solo acoustic set. Will definitely be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best breakfast I have had in years! We went during the week so the wait was only 15 minutes. I ordered the sampler and everything was perfect, the gravy was great, but the highlight was the biscuits and preserves. Service was incredible, the staff friendly, and the atmosphere homey. It was so good we bought a pie to go, some preserves, and a dozen biscuits (they gave us the biscuits). Only problem for me is they are near Nashville and I live in California but they make Tennessee very tempting!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is a very fun atmosphere, the food and booze is great. Its a bit pricey but makes for a fun night out. Get the pork knuckle.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
So for the first time in a long time I can say these words: believe the hype. This place is as good as every one says it is. If you're in the Nashville area you must stop by to have a meal here. 

Yes, the wait will be incredibly long -- so don't come starving or you will give up and leave. We had over an hour long wait, but it was well worth it. Plus. there's an entire property to explore, which includes two gift shops (one featuring free samples of food items and appetizers), cornhole games, picnic tables, and more.

The food is absolutely delicious. Tastes like a meal at grandma's house. I went here for breakfast/brunch on a Saturday. However, I really really wish I had a chance to experience for dinner. I look forward to making this one of my regular stops when visiting Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Ya gotta love the Loveless. The wait is worth it! The food is perfect, every time! The offer up amazing food, great service and a fun atmosphere. I've eaten at The Loveless countless times and I'm always impressed!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A must see for Nashville. Gift shops, restaurant, resort, and breakfast all day! Moonshine shots, unlimited biscuits with three types of jams, and outdoor seating if you want. Service was good and prices are great. This was recommended by a tour guide and although it's in the mountains, it was worth the trip!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: First off, I'm a southern boy through and through.  I love good southern cooking more than damn near anything else around. That said, I'm no stranger to good food and most of the time, they're not reinventing the wheel when you eat at southern food joints.  When my friends picked me up from Nashville to head to their home in Alabama, we stopped here for dinner.  Their biscuits, oh dear god, their biscuits.  Damn.  I ended up getting smoked pork chops/loin that was glazed in their homemade peach preserves.  This is damn near holy divinity.  As my chef says "god spoke to me".  I really do think, if there was a god, he'd tell you to eat here.  I had enough leftovers that I took with me, I had breakfast for two days straight with the addition of a couple scrambled eggs.  When you walk in, you see a wall/walls of autographed photos from the Nashville scene in there.  I'm looking forward to my trip back to Nashville just to eat here......at least once.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Be prepared for a loud, lively experience! Unfortunately, I went there thinking I was going to have a nice, relaxing diner! (Not the restaurants fault!) I had the fish and chips and wasn't pleased - but hey that's what you get when you order non-German foods from a German restaurant. My hubby had a good experience though!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This is a great concert venue . They have great sound so you can truly hear the music! However DO NOT EAT here!! I've learned my lesson after giving it TWO tries!! I was hoping to give them a second chance after my first experience wasn't so great, but unfortunately they failed me again . Both times we had terrible service and both times the menu was not full of great options. For instance there was not a single steak or chicken dish on the menu . There was " bone marrow" who wants that?? Call me a redneck but no thank you ! I ordered the Napa Slaw( that's right , slaw) for dinner because there were hardly any options. They had pizza and my husband got that , it was over cooked . Here's the deal, go, drink their amazing wines, but go to dinner somewhere else first!!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: A beautifully created night spot. It's a perfect 10 on the "cool" rankings. However I probably won't be back and here's why. I went to a show there recently in the upstairs portion. For "regular folks" like me, drinking the the basic house wines are plenty adequate.  That way you can get your cost per glass under $10 and not feel like you're getting ripped off too bad. Well, the waitress explains that they don't offer their house selections upstairs. You have to order from the rest of the wines starting at $40 and going way up from there. This is BS and they know it. They don't offer their cheaper menu to patrons of a show because they know those people are a captive audience. They aren't going anywhere and they are going to order something, so why not put the screws to them and remove the cheaper portion of the menu? Great business sense! Well, you got me once but that will be the last time. Additionally, my tab came out to $59 after I ordered only the one $40 bottle of wine. They were trying to run us out of the place the second the show ended so I didn't dispute it. I just signed it and left. Too bad because it's such a neat place. They won't miss me as I'm not their target customer. The whole thing was a racket.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
If anyone has ever given this place less than 5 stars, YOU A LIE!!!!!

Incredible experience - went on a weekday for dinner. No wait. Drink orders were delivered with warm, flaky biscuits and a trio of preserves (blackberry, peach, strawberry - ranked in that order). Server was so polite and helped me and my elderly father navigate the menu/side options and offered to bring us another side if what we ordered was not to our liking. Pa ordered country fried steak, greens, and hashbrown casserole (a must) while I got the BBQ pork atop cornbread hoe cakes with coleslaw. Cannot go wrong with their BBQ! We passed on dessert because Pa couldn't stop eating biscuits and wanted to drink the blackberry preserves. Left stuffed, well worth the stop!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Walked in at 10 minutes to closing without even realizing and they still sat us, the hostess was a bit begrudging and so we finally figured it out. The waitress was wonderful and still super helpful. It's definitely a cute little kitschy spot and certainly novel. There's two gift shops and two event spaces. There's a cornhole game for the kiddos and face cutout picture props too (no idea what those are actually called). To get the last star: get rid of the funky odor upon entry, don't be snarky when taking Mamés but kindly alert patrons you close soon, and maybe moisten the biscuits a wee bit. They were good but so dry. Overall: if you love kitsch and history, check it out.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Just went there last week . I have been eating there since it was really a cafe , over 30 years ! It has always been great until now .My server was a white guy with a shaved head and husky build . When he dropped off my water after a 15 minute wait , I was ready to order . Obviously , he did not want to take my order . I asked him a question about the sides when ordering and he literally just turned and walked away from me without saying a word . He proceeded to do what he wanted to and came back after several minutes . He was extremely rude , at a level I don't think I have ever seen with a server . The fried chicken came and was good except that the breast had an area of blood inside about 1 1/2 x 1 1/2 inches and was raw . The server did not ever return to check on anything or fill my water . I asked the hostess as she passed by for the manager . He was an older white man working in the kitchen area . I told him the situation with food and server . His only response was "do you want another piece of chicken?" in an annoyed manner . I said "no" and asked him not to send the server back to my table .  He said the server was the only one who could take payment and walked away . That was it , no apology for anything or any caring for the situation in any way . I regularly take groups there for business related meetings as well as family/friends . The server made no comment whatsoever when taking payment . He never at any time asked me if I needed anything or gave me more drink . I will never go back . By the way , I did not say anything to the manager until after the meal was eaten . I also told him I did not want free meal or anything like that . I did not want anything free or anything like that but the offer was never given . I paid full price for everything . I think this is the first time that I have not tipped a server . I am also in the service business.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Among the many delicious things that are on their menu, the thing that stands out most is the biscuits which is what they're most known for.  What stood out to me about these biscuits was fluffiness of the biscuits and the buttery taste that is well complemented by the jams they serve.  Everything else on the menu is generally cooked well, but the typical southern fare.  As far meats go, I have had their quarter dark fried chicken, pork chops, and pulled pork barbecue and was not disappointed.  However, I have heard that the chicken has been hit or miss from reliable sources so order the fried chicken at your own discretion.  I find the best time for a meal here is breakfast.

Another thing that stands out is that even though the place is a restaurant, they also have a barbecue pit and a souvenir shop where you can buy their jams, biscuit mix, bacon, and other tourist trap souvenir items.  

Service overall is generally pretty good and friendly, the food arrives fairly quick, and they are kind enough to give you a small plate of biscuits as a complimentary appetizer.

The only downside here is the wait because after 10AM on a Saturday, this place becomes very packed and an hour wait is not uncommon.  Easter Sunday is the worst since wait time typically exceeds 3 hours by 9AM.  

Food: 4
Service: 4
Price: 4

name: Loveless Cafe
text: It's the Loveless!!  It's sooooo good!  Best friend chicken in town.  And the biscuits!  Oh my the biscuits.  Don't eat before you go so you can load up on them.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place was one of the places recommended by magazines/sites and trip advisor. We didn't think much of it because it just seemed like any other southern eateries, but I am so glad we went there. This place was recommended by every local we met, they couldn't stop talking about it and after we ate there we understood why! The place is very homey and cozy, though casual. I loved the ambiance and it's set up! Our server was extremely nice and he suggested pretty much our entire menu. As soon as you sit down he brought us some fresh biscuits and jams and they were both delicious! The biscuits were fresh, warm, soft, and creamy! Jams seemed like they were homemade. Everything we ordered on the menu; fried chicken, grilled and fried fish were fresh and so so tasty! (we all liked the fried chicken better at Hattie B's but here it was delicious too). Sides we ordered were fried okra (YUM) and creamed corn (again YUM)! I am so glad we went there and it's definitely a place to visit when in Nashville!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
What stupidly good fun: Proust, everyone!! 
The food here is actually pretty damned excellent for a small chain and the vibe is like 24/7 Oktoberfest---this German lass is officially smitten! The authentic dishes/beers/sauces are expertly executed and laid out and the service here was quite superb from start to finish. 

And hello, there's fun entertainment too!! Yes indeed, I'm the cheeseball who will gladly do the chicken dance while chomping on a big sausage and slurping a boot of the good brews. It's family friendly while still being good all-aged fun too, which is truly tough balance to find, but somehow this joint manages to do all that in spades.

Also, if you're LUCKY....and if you're a lush like me....you'll get called onto stage to do a complimentary shotski. So you've been warned, fellow party people: come here to get sauced and bossed and stuffed full of schnitzel! Das all good!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: If I could give them a 100 stars I would. In February I decided to have a small and intimate dinner party to commemorate a milestone birthday. I sent my inquiry and Alex responded. I went down, looked at the space and fell in love. It was quaint and intimate enough for what I wanted to do. Alex was amazing from start to finish. She saw my vision and helped me achieve exactly what I wanted. I was working on a budget and while I went over, $700, it was definitely worth it and the ideas that Alex added, made a super classy and more special touch. On my actual date, this past weekend, Alex was out of town, however, from my arrival to my departure, from valet, to the Sommelier, Blake and our dedicated waitress, I can't find one complaint. I opted for buffet style, southern style dinner and when I tell you the food was amazing, hot and tasty. Delicious, is definitely an understatement. I will definitely be visiting the City Winery more often and I am also planning a wine tour and will be joining their wine club. Never have I been blown away, by such professionalism and their attention to detail is and was unmatched. THANK YOU, City Winery, Alex, Blake and Ms. A for making my 40th, one of the best moments of my life. There isn't anything that you could have done to make me any more happy, satisfied or make this experience any more enjoyable.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Be careful your bill can add up quickly.  I've lived in Germany 3 times so my view might not be fair.  I have a hard time paying $3.50 for 2 slices of Rye bread when it always came with the meal in Germany.  
The Schnitzel was large and tender, pretzels large and hot, potato cakes yummy and Bier cold.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place just doesn't have good food. I've been here three different times and each time I've been let down. The skinny........wait 1-2 hours and have bad food.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We had a great breakfast at Loveless.

The biscuits are perfect! Tender, buttery, salty. The home made preserves are delicious. We may have left with a pint of the blackberry preserves.

I had fried pork chop breakfast. Don't get this is you plan on eating again that day. It was great. Two well seasoned pork chops with gravy on the side and two over easy eggs. Comes with a side of your choice.

My wife got the ham and eggs. The ham was a bit salty for my taste but with the gravy and egg yolk it was delicious. 

The service was good and friendly. I really can't say enough good things about this place. You should go too!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Totally worth the ride and wait. Biscuits are amazing. I ordered the fried chicken with cream corn and mac & cheese. Incredible. I'm not a big cream corn fan but the waitress, Tammy (who was super sweet), suggested we try it and it was great! We LOVED it. The barbecue sauce was so good that we all bought our own bottles to take home from the gift shop. The fudge pie was tasty as well. Oh and the Hams and Jams gift shop is adorable and full of great items. If I ever come back to Nashville, it's to come eat at Loveless Cafe.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Average food, super slow service, overpriced for the tourists.  Nothing to see here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Love me some Loveless!! Always great food and customer service! They have every kind of mouth watering southern soul food you can think of. They serve bloody Mary's & fun cocktails as well. It's definitely a family style restaurant with lots of fun gift shops. Restaurant still fantastic after all these years. Be prepared to have long wait time if you go at certain times & days of the week. Lots to do on grounds tho while you wait so just make sure you have a snack or are tithed over. Thanks Loveless for all that you do!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Yes I am a fan of Loveless and get silly when walking in the front door. Could be the checkered table cloths that triggers instant salivation. Mmmm we're talking fresh made biscuits and peach and strawberry preserve as starters and lots of down home meat and three to follow. Yessireedy Yesindeedy I love this place. While on a holiday from Australia I came saw and ate here and I love it for its down home vibe. It's usually crowded and it's typical to wait for a table to be ready. No problem cos there's a grocery and gift store perfect to kill time and stock up on some neat gifts and souveniers. While waiting to be seated I got me some grand souvineers that travelled well from Nashville to Sydney and back again. Got a nifty red guitar-shaped fly swatter and an oven mit. Still got em and have swatted a few Australian and Nashville flies too so these work just dandy. OK back to the food. Delicious. Smoked ham, turkey, fried chicken and all the usual suspect sides. Got tourists and visitors? Take them to Loveless.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Fabulous way to lose a lot of money quickly. Staff seems too cool to help you and everything is overpriced. It's a necessary evil given the great acts that come through.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Delicious and wonderful as always. The biscuits and blackberry jam are the best ever!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Holy smokes, everything was so delicious that I ate too fast and had to go to bed after :)

I got the biscuit sampler with bbq, fried chicken, country ham and sausage as my four options. On top of the biscuits they brought to the table, I had a lot of bread in a short period of time! My boyfriend got the chicken and waffles, which were huge, full of flavor and completely worth the trip outside of Nashville.

Make sure to check out the various gift shops on the property and the barn. It was set up for a wedding and looked gorgeous!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
A must visit in Nashville and worth the hour and a half wait! If you have to wait there are lots of little stores in site to visit. The food is delicious... I mean the biscuits.. THE BISCUITS! To die for. You can even see them make them! 

...if you're lucky, you might spot a celebrity. I heard they frequent this cafe.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: BEST Biscuits, Fried Chicken and Creamed Corn I've Ever had!! I stayed in downtown Nashville and drove nearly every day to go to the Loveless Café.  It's worth the drive.  INCREDIBLE!!!!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Joe was an amazing host! City Winery made our bachelorette weekend start off with a bang

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is one of my new places to frequent. The food is really good and the place is huge with a great atmosphere. They have fun musical performances. The woman who sings and plays most days is really fun and talented. Kevin is one of the managers and he's a really nice guy who cared about our experience. All of the servers we had were quick and helpful. Check it out! Get a brat!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
5 STARS JUST FOR THE AMAZING BISCUITS

I don't care how long you have to wait, how many hills and weird turns I had to take to get here, AND HOW FREAKING COLD IT WAS. These biscuits made it ALL worth it.

It's a Southern institution that I am shocked is actually not more popular than it already is. 

That said, I would skip the fried chicken (it was tasteless) and just go for the fried catfish, the creamed corn, the baked beans. Although the pulled pork was great too.

YUM.

name: The Basement
text:
I've seen a lot there over the passed decade. Great shows, good people. This Saturday night at a show with Weekend Jimmy we noticed a male gay couple that was being very publicly affectionate. About midway through the show, they started frenching...Now I'm no prude, but any self-respecting bar would put a stop to anything like that ; gay or not. But, that didn't happen. It just got worse as the show went on. Rather than make a scene, we left. Sent Mike an email and his response was basically "we'll miss you; or not".

So there ya go. Nashville's gay scene would be embarrassed.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My family and I went here for breakfast on a weekday. Love the experience; the store owners are very nice, the decor inside the cafe is great and the staff is very friendly. The biscuits were delicious and we all really liked the hashbrown casserole side, but other than that the food was pretty standard - and a bit pricey for your average breakfast. All in all, we were happy with the stop, but would probably try a different breakfast spot next Nashville visit.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food is spectacular and the service is outstanding. If you are looking for good homestyle southern food then look no further. The price is a bit steep but you get what you pay for. You get to keep the moonshine side car jars, and the portions are huge. And the 14 hour slow roasted pulled pork melts in your mouth. Don't go to Nashville without eating here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
You can't go wrong here...southern cookin at its best. 

The hospitality was spot on. 

We order family style (fried chicken, grilled pork, fried okra, Mac and cheese, and hash brown casserole)...you know...health food...for the soul. 
The dessert was coconut cream pie and apple pie...oh then there's the biscuits. OMG!!!

We also tried their country fried steak...really good. 

So that's it.  If you want real southern cookin, then you need to go here. 

Don't debate it...just go. 
If you have a long line just stay; that means it's with it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Yes, the biscuits and jelly were amazing but that's about all for me! Both are def made fresh. I've never had anything like them. They're complementary with some orders but you could enjoy them by themselves with coffee for breakfast- filling. I ordered the chicken and waffles. The waffles were too thick & that made them hard to enjoy. The chicken was huge! It's definitely a good choice if you have a huge appetite that early in the morning. 3 stars for the biscuits but I wasn't impressed by anything else. The drive is out of the way even if you are driving into/out of Nashville. The staff was decent. Stopped by around 9am  on a Friday morning so there wasn't a wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Enjoyed the ride through the local area via GPS too.  The food is superb. Pimento cheese and green fried tomatoe biscuit is awesome.  Sausage omelet was also excellent.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I loved the winery when it first opened up.  But I think it has gone down since then.  I have never felt like I was a cheap person, but their focus on trying to nickel and dime you to death is glaringly obvious.  $5 to self park yourself in their lot?  Who does that?  Then there was the food.  I've been to a number of shows there and thought the food was good.  Ordered a burger the other night and the bun had to be at least 3 or 4 days old.  I worked in restaurants for 15 years.  No self respecting kitchen would send a bun out like that.  And if they couldn't tell, they should seek another career path.  The thing was as hard as a rock.  Next is the wine.  Even buying their cheapest house wine by the carafe comes to $10 a glass.  I hate to tell them but BOTA box wines are better than what they make. Then to further their cause in pursuit of eeking out money, they've started making some shows like this one a Vinofile only show which means you have to pay $75 to be a member to even buy tickets.  I had to laugh because the venue was only 40% full.  

It's sad, because this place could be so awesome, but it appears whoever is running this place can't see the forest for the trees.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is awesome.  On our first visit, my husband took a picture of the sign and fell in a gulch (LOL).  He had (and finished) the sampler platter, I had the fried chicken.  You really can't go wrong with anything here.

The second time, I drove straight here from the airport (ok, I picked up my daughter) and headed over.  They knew I wasn't from here because I ordered iced tea (not sweet), but food is great, everyone's nice.

I will be back there in a few weeks - can't wait!!!

name: Big Shotz
