text: I have been coming to Nashville for 6 years now and I always come to Big Shotz every single time! If your looking for a fun and friendly environment with great life music this is a great place to go. This year I went and I had more than a great time. My favorite bartender Brin was truly amazing . Very helpful and kind! I will def be back because of the staff! Drinks weren't pricey and the music was great! If you want to dance your butt off upstairs is a lot of fun to. That opens later in the evening ! I will be back in two months and this will be my first stop! Thank you Big Shotz for making this trip so memorable! Thank you Brin! I'll see you for my birthday in 2 months

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I'll start on a positive note; the venue is beautiful! There is a huge wine selection, including 450 bottles, and several wines made in house that are on tap and served by the glass. The cocktail list is also good - I have the La Fleur and it was wonderful. The server was attentive and friendly and knowledgeable about the menus. The food, was very subpar. We were really excited about the menu, so we ordered lots of apps - the burrata, duck tacos, charcuterie, pork belly. All were mediocre at best. I ordered the filet and it was less than average. I didn't have the highest expectations, because it's not a steakhouse, but for $35 I expected a little more than average. The filet was not tender, little flavor, and appeared to be  less than the 7 oz advertised (not confirmed). Overall, I would go back for drinks (it's a winery, it's what they're good for), but not food. 3 stars because the server was great and drinks were good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Biscuits.  Don't even question giving them a try with their blackberry jam/preserves - what have you.

The portions are fairly large.  I had the fried chicken salad with ranch.  It didn't even look like I made an attempt after my attempt.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I drove across the country for my bucket list/birthday/I bought a new car/hey why not and stopped here on the way from Raleigh NC to Los Angeles.Spent half my budget on gifts and food. Well worth it. Everyone was really nice, the biscuits were delicious, coffee hot and I just might make the drive out again. MMM. I love you, Tennessee.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Good food and fun destination. Love the little shops surrounding the diner. And it's a good thing, because you will wait a bit for your table. Nice to have the shops to browse, and they have corn hole games set up on the lawn.

Food was good, but no "WOW" factor. Just a good meal well prepared. The raves about the biscuits are a joke. They are indistinguishable from frozen store biscuits. 100% Pop-N-Fresh.

Be prepared to get rushed, they are ALL about table turnover, and will attempt to hurry you along. And will get very snotty if you linger.  Our waitress was very attentive, and friendly, but got chilly very quick when we pointed out she got our order wrong. I also asked for hot sauce, waited a long time, and had to remind her, which got me some eye rolling. 20 minutes after seating us she was so adamant about moving us along she practically handed us our coats. 

Frankly, the homey vibe feels like a sham, they are all about volume, volume, volume, and turning tables as fast as possible. Sadly, this place has the "Too famous to fail" attitude many successful places have, that they don't need to take care of you because the sheer volume of business they get makes the quality of the dining experience irrelevant.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Excellent southern food! Plan to spend all your calories for the day on the biscuits! It's worth it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Lunch, desserts and service were all very good, 4+ stars, I'd say. The reason I'm docking them 2-stars is their posting of No Weapons signs. It seems to have been proven over time that a good guy with a gun is not a threat to anyone. I'll not return for that reason.

name: Rocketown
text: I went to Rocketown for a  rock/metal concert, which was placed in the white building across the street. Room was spacious enough for the number of people there and everything sounded good. There's a good bit of parking nearby.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Authentic German food. My wife and her family came with me here and they have all been to October fest in Germany and said that the food was spot on. I highly recommend the Black Forest schnitzel. It was delicious. Also happy hour is from 8pm until close daily. Get a 1L beer then. It's a good deal. Service was great too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I love this place! Our waitress was extremely friendly and helpful with recommendations. 

While waiting you can walk around and visit their little shops and take cute photos. 

The food was fantastic! 

It does get busy though so be prepared to wait for a little bit or go at a off time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits, peach preserves, blackberry preserves and grits were delicious. Country ham has the fecund farm flavor which was great, though unexpected. Cheese grits and scrambled eggs were not that good. Great ambiance and history. Store had lots of menu items for sale. The bisquits are so good that I could easily gain weight by eating them everyday.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I love this place! Our waitress is always so nice and helpful. We never have to wait because we go on off hours, early dinner/late breakfast.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We love the food here. They have the best biscuits you will ever eat.  I always order the fried chicken and hashbrown casserole and my husband always gets something different and has never disliked anything.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Really enjoyed this venue , food, and service. We will definitely return! Had 1/2 carafe of wine, the risotto balls and a flatbread. All were very good, brought out promptly and reasonably priced. Didn't mind the $5 valet as that seems cheap to me and love not fooling with parking, worth the money everyday. It was slightly odd sharing a table with people since we had 2 tickets but it was a table for 4. However, we chatted and had a lovely time. Think we may have found our go to date night spot especially when a favorite is in town. Love living in Nashviile!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Cracker Barrel if it did not go corporate. You are a fool if you pass up a visit here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
My boyfriend and I took a trip to Georgia for Thanksgiving and we made a pit stop in Nashville. I was looking up some cool places to check out and the Loveless Cafe was one of the top places to visit/try out.  

When we first arrived, we parked in front of the Loveless Cafe country market where they had specialized gift, hams, and signature jams. As we walked to the cafe I spotted "The Loveless Cafe" neon sign...I definitely had to take a few pictures of it. You know me :) 

As we entered the cafe (which is the white house)  there were photos of famous musicians and actors all along the wall they even had stockings hung from the fireplace welcoming the holidays! Right as we got in the waitress right away showed us to our seats. I was amazed by all the decor and art on the walls. They had a lot of cool Johnny Cash portraits and pictures. The table covers were blue and plaid patterns and the place  mats gave you a little history lesson on the cafe and how it got started. 

Looking at the menu there was a variety of things to try. You got your fried chicken, sandwiches, salads, homemade size dishes, and much more. Since we were in the south we had to try the ice tea! It was bombacious! I had read on the travel blog that the Loveless Cafe had amazing biscuits so we asked our lovely waitress to try them. We saw that they were small biscuits and they give you little cups of jam.

Loveless cafe is definitely comfort food for the soul and a place you should stop by if you're in Nashville!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Service was great. Everything was delicious. The biscuits were amazing, especially with the preserves. I highly recommend the peach glazed pork chops, fried chicken, catfish, and country ham. The pork chops had grill marks so the charred taste balanced perfectly with the sweetness of the peach preserves. Everything was cooked perfectly and had excellent flavor and the portions were very filling. We would definitely eat here again if we were in the area.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
First off, our server was great, that's it. Let me start off by saying, I have always wanted to try this place. I am a huge foodie and eat out a few nights a week, City Winery has been on my list of places to try out and is a convenient drive from my house. 

A few weeks ago I decided I wanted to go to a great brunch to bring in the New Year. I looked around at all my options and decided on City Winery because of their menu. I made a reservation and my boyfriend and I were so excited to check it out.

When you walk in, it's a nice environment, what made our 4/5 star experience into less of that was the buffet. The $30 per person hotel breakfast buffet....it was decent and mayyybbbe worth $15.....

The thing that really got me though, was that I had no idea it was a buffet until we sat down. No where online did it say it, nor when I made the reservation...or even when they called to confirm the reservation the day before!!! They only had the buffet option and no actual menu. 

I came here to try the menu, not a buffet and am very upset I was not told beforehand. Every single person in the place was just as upset as me and it ruined the way I think and will talk about this place....and my first day of 2016! 




UPDATE - A manager contacted me today and issued me a refund for the buffet. I will go back & review this place again when I am able to have a true experience there.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I had some pretty bad biscuits while in Nashville but this was amazing!! So good! And I bought the BlackBerry barbecue sauce without even trying it and it was amazing

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Been in Nashville four years and finally I decided to drive 40minutes to try the talk of the town. I had the southern omelette which taste amazing. The biscuits is definitely a plus too. Now I can see why it is a place you have to visit if you are ever in Nashville.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Good wine selection, and enjoyed a show there last year. Gotta say it was a little weird being at a concert and eating but was lots of fun. Being front row is crazy good, actually touching the stage the whole time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Endless homemade biscuits? What's not to love? Gets super busy. Now taking reservations on weekdays! Otherwise I highly suggest going between meal times. We tried at 11:30 on a weekend and were told it was a 2 hour wait for 4 people. Left and came back around 4:30 and only had to wait 30 mins. Totally worth it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I had a wonderful experience at Loveless as a solo diner. The employees were friendly and efficient. The biscuits were divine. The CHICKEN was so freaking crispy and flavorful...I can't even. I had prince's hot chicken the day before, which was ok...but if you have the chance to eat this. Choose this! Broccoli and rice casserole was so comforting I wanted to curl up with it on a couch. Well with the drive out of the city. Perfect when coupled with a tour of Belle Meade!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Worst German food ever. Wow. Left enough of an impression we had to write a review.

Spaetzle is limp, greasy and tasteless. Gravies are run of the mill, out of a can quality. Lacking in flavor, authenticity and value the owners should take stick in taking advmathe of the tourists. I mean $20 for a chicken schnitzel that is flavorless, small and not authentic. Even if you are a starving tourist, just pass this this restaurant. For this price go to the equally over priced aquarium restaurant but at least there uses higher quality ingredients.

Three positives, nice staff, a solid german and jaeger beer selection. And the chef who is on his game in that he actually came out to speak to us about our experience. If ownership goes back to its roots of a "german" experience and stopped sourcing low-grade ingredients they would easily hit the ball out of the park since they have one of the hardest things in the service industry under control -- good employees.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text:
1. Grumpy bouncer sets your experience off to a bad start immediately.
2. Cheeseburger came out very dry and simply bad tasting. McDonalds or Wendy's has more flavor in their 99 cent hamburgers.
3. Same goes for the patty melt but add soggy bread.
4. Picture of the Mac and cheese attached in which the flavor was below average and the quantity was laughable. About 12-15 pieces of macaroni.

Bottom line: you will never go here for the food, maybe they have good music but eat somewhere else first.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Food and beer are great! The service at the bar not so much! I felt like we were bother them.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Love this place! Eaten here about 3-4 times and have never been disappointed. The schnitzel is incredible as are the pretzels and desserts! Great environment and lovely staff, whom speak with a german accent no matter the color tone of their skin A deffinate must for ppl who like food

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A staple in the Nashville area that every out of towner should experience! Great atmosphere and terrific Southern food!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
After so many had told me to go check this "Nashville staple restaurant" out, I decided it would be a great opportunity to take my mother who was visiting from out of town. I knew this was a popular tourist attraction, so I wasn't surprised when we arrived at 9:20 there was already an hour+ wait. 

They have a few stores surrounding the cafe and some sitting areas and cornhole games. 

We waited around an hour and a half and then waited another 10 minutes to be greeted. Our server, Ethan/Evan, never introduced himself, never gave us a welcome, all he said is "what do you want to drink?" That was it. We thought that was a little weird, I guess we were expecting a little more from a restaurant that is so highly raved about. It took about 15 more minutes to get our waters and other beverages. We then ordered an appetizer and went ahead and ordered our food, again very little interaction with our server. They have little mazes and word searches on the tables (presumably for children) but thank goodness they had these to distract us from the almost hour wait for our food. The appetizer came out the same time as the rest of our food, always disappointing. Someone else delivered our food, not the server. But the server, NEVER ONCE asked how our food was, did everything come out okay?, can I get you a refill?, nothing. He brought over a few napkins. We asked for more biscuits and he told us when more came out he would bring them, he did this but again never saying anything to check on us. 

My mom ordered the Santa Fe Omelette, she was left very disappointed. It has very little flavor and had way too many onions stuffed inside. 
I had the biscuit platter as "an appetizer", the pimento cheese and fried tomato was my favorite! The others were good, but nothing I would drive another 45 minutes too again. 
I got the breakfast bowl and I was very pleased with my bowl, delicious, warm, plenty of food, great flavor. 

Overall, the loveless cafe was greatly overrated in my opinion and we were left very underwhelmed. I would not recommend this to people coming to Nashville, unless you are looking to spend your entire morning/afternoon for decent/good food with poor service. Disappointing experience, such a shame for what I had heard about the place. (Side note: I was a server for 8 years so I understand when a server is busy and overwhelmed, but this was not the case) 
I post this so that Loveless Cafe can help rectify the issue with their employees and remind them that service is key to a successful business, and that hopefully in the future no one else has the same experience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I first visited this cafe about 10 years ago.  I had been thinking about it and wanted to return to it.  G and I decided to meet here for dinner one Friday night.  It's about halfway between his residence and Knoxville and mine in Memphis.  I got there, and it was about a 45 minute wait, which was fortunate, because he was 45 minutes late.  



The cafe started in 1951 with the Loveless family basically selling fried chicken and biscuits out of their house.  



They have a BBQ pit, so they obviously smoke their own meat.  



It used to also be a motel.  However, the motel quit operative about 20 years ago.  The old motel parts are used for retail.  You can buy plenty of souvenirs, some edible and some wearable.  



They start you off with biscuits and their famous jams.  The biscuits were great.  They also serve breakfast all day.  I had to restrain myself from eating too many before my meal.  



They have some drinks.  I had a whiskey and water.  One friend ordered a shot of moonshine.  It came in a cute mason jar cup.  He said it was "strong."  



I love combination plates, so that's what I got.  With as much food as I got, it was worth the price.  I think it was the most expensive item on the menu at $17.55.  The Southern Sampler Platter comes with your choice of three meats (Fried Chicken, Catfish, Country Ham, Meatloaf or Pork Barbeque) and two sides.  I chose the fried chicken, because that was one of their original items.  I also got the country ham, because it is proclaimed on their neon sign outside.  And finally, I got the pork barbecue since I saw the BBQ pit outside.  All the meat was just plain perfect.  The pork was on a cornbread pancake.  



I also got to choose two sides.  They have tons of choices.  I ended up getting the greens and the mac n' cheese.  Both were good and typically country.  I would have liked to try the fried okra, but I already had too much food.  



For my meat, I did't choose the meatloaf, because I knew G would order it.  he did, and it was good.  It was covered with a tangy tomato sauce.  He got the vegetable of the day, which was squash.  It was surprisingly good, too.  I wasn't tempted by it when I heard it was the special, but I was jealous when I tasted it.  



They have desserts, but there's no way someone could eat anyway after eating here! 

The other intriguing thing on their menu is their family style supper for groups of 4 or more.  It's all you can eat for $17.55 a person.  The table has to agree upon two meats and three veggies.  It also includes a regular drink.  

It is so good that it would be worth a three hour drive.  Seriously.

name: Big Shotz
text:
This place is kind of awesome, if you're in the mood for the ambiance it provides.  Big Shotz is located just off of Broadway, the touristy bar strip in Nashville.  Big Shotz is definitely a dive bar with live music, cheap drinks, and a grubby feel.  If that's what you're looking for, Big Shotz delivers.

When you first enter Big Shotz, be prepared for some cigarette smoke.  The interior is dark and looks pretty worn out.  Seating consists mainly of high-tops with some of the most beaten up stools I have ever seen in a bar.  These tables overlook two stages:  The back features a large stage and video projection screen, while the front has a smaller stage by the large doors and windows that open onto the street.

I visited on a Saturday afternoon and there was a small crowd listening to a duo play music.  Once inside, we discovered that the drinks were dirt cheap!  Beers were $2 for draft and $3 for bottles.  Shots were similarly inexpensive, though none of our group had the nerve to try the infamous double-decker $5 shots at 2:00 PM.  The bartenders were nice.  

Overall, this seems like a great place to kill some time if you are looking for a dive bar with ultra-cheap drinks.  I can't stress how inexpensive this place is compared to the competition around it.  It's a little dirty, but some of that is by design (I.e. the terrible barstools) in the so-bad-it's-good sense.  This is probably a great place to get hammered at night, too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is a great tourist spot! We love getting little souvenirs from their shops before or after we eat. We pretty much always get the chicken fried chicken, and the only one time it was undercooked, we were given replacements (cooked perfectly) and sent home with free dessert. It's a super friendly and welcoming environment and the servers are always warm and kind! The biscuits are to die for and we loooove the sides -- especially the creamed corn and fried green tomatoes.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Big Rig Blunder
We recently drove the Natchez Trace from Mississippi and I wanted to take my husband to Loveless Cafe. The only problem was that we were in a motorhome and were towing. I emailed ahead of time to ask if they had parking for a large rig and were assured that they did. Unfortunately when we got there the signage was unclear (and the road is very busy) so we ended up turning down the next street which had no outlet and we had to back up and turn around. When we got back out to the road we spied a dirt road across the highway and thought we could pull into that to get turned around. NO! It was someone's driveway and it was a dead end. Now we were stuck. Upon seeing our dilemma the operations manager ran across the street, hugged the very concerned property owner (not the first time this has happened apparently) and helped us to get turned around and into a back lot behind the gas station where there is lots more parking that you can't see from the street. We were assured that they were in the process of revamping their signage.
Once we got inside we found out it was 1 1/2 wait!!! I dug in my heels and told my husband that we were not going through all of that only to leave but after waiting 20 minutes I realized I was starving and not going to make it so I ordered food to go ONLINE (they have an awesome website for placing your order to go) and picked it up 20 minutes later and ate it in the motorhome. The Fried Chicken was just as I remembered it and my husband loved his brisket. 
The moral of the story: If the wait is too long (which it often is) go online to order and eat at one of their shady picnic benches.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
This is our first visit to the Nashville location, but we have visit the City Winery in both Chicago and Atlanta.   

The concert we attended was upstairs in the lounge area instead of the main stage. It was a beautiful atmosphere, beautiful acoustics, and the food was delightful!!! You have to visit if you are Nashville!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Tourist trap. Chicken was dry and had no seasoning or salt. Bbq was ehh. Chicken fried chicken was literally burned so bad we had to send it back and the gravy tasted like the jarred gravy you buy at the store for emergencies. The service was prompt but not friendly. Just cold. Felt no southern charm at all. 14.00 for a fried chicken drum and wing..mashed potatoes and a bowl of fried okra. Could have had the same meal at cracker barrel for 8.99 and had better biscuits and gravy.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We went to breakfast here on a Friday morning around 9 so we were able to avoid any major waits. We waited about 10 minutes for a table, which is not bad at all. I once tried to go for lunch and it was 1.5 hours (more common, from what I hear). The breakfast food was very yummy. I did love the biscuits and the jellies that they had. The hashbrown casserole that is raved about was also good. Overall, it was yummy food, but I am eager to try their lunch/dinner options. Good service, fun atmosphere. Worth the trip as a "bucket list" item!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing dining experience as usual at loveless!!! Great food and drinks, I had the fried chicken , Mac and cheese and corn.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Food was good- I wished  it would have been served hotter but flavors were great - the Rouladen were dry :(

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We loved the food, drink, music, and atmosphere. Our waiter was pleasant but extremely slow. We had show tickets, budgeted 90 minutes only to find ourselves 70 minutes into our evening and just getting our meals. Getting our bill was another endeavor. So we did feel rushed to eat and leave. Plan double your time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Fun vibes, service is outstanding, biscuits were great. They serve breakfast all day and in hindsight, I should have taken advantage of that. The food on the lunch menu had too much gravy and cream sauce for my pallet.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
We were here a few weeks ago and have to admit that it was better than we expected.  We are German, so it's hard to come close to to the real thing when we're out, but since my parents live in a place that doesn't have as many German restaurants as we would like, I brought them here to try it.

The food was very good - filling, and although not exactly authentic, still really flavorful.  I had their version of French onion soup, some schnitzel and then a potato dumpling and all were very good.  The beer was really good and the atmosphere was very fun and enjoyable, with a duo (a couple, I think) who played while everyone ate.  

It was very convivial and I would highly recommend it, especially if you have a group, as you can sit at large long tables and share conversation easily.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: After a second trip here, I'm convinced my initial rating was too low. The biscuits and peach preserves were just as delicious as my first time here, followed by the exceptional cheesy hashbrowns... so good! I went a different route, and tried the french toast, and I was not disappointed! Cinnamon and sweet just the way I like it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
If your in the area, be sure you make the Loveless Cafe one of your stops !
You made need resets, so get that done !
Tim was our waiter and he could not have been any better!!
Fresh, hot biscuits with homemade peach, strawberry and blackberry jelly are delivered to your table as soon as you are seated .
You really can just stop there!!
Be sure and ask for some sorghum syrup too.
WOW
WOW
WOW
Very delicious!!
We did order, and this is what we tried:

Fried Chicken, cream corn & fried okra 

Fried fish, turnip greens & okra

Meatloaf with garlic cheese mashed potatoes 

It was all so good. To be honest, we were full from the biscuits.

They also have fresh homemade pies .
We had to try ! Lol
Key lime pie and also banana pudding!!!
You can't go wrong, just do it. 

When in Nashville, make that short trip to the Loveless Cafe!!
Go get Full

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Great wine and atmosphere. Service was excellent, food was ok.  I will go back for wine and small plates.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Great brunch! Can't wait to go back! Had the Poke Bowl, Little Gem Salad...fabulous! Great service staff, never a bad time!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wow!  Southern home cooking at its best!  I go to Nashville once a year and this is the best part of the trip.  The food and service are amazing and the cool little shops are a must to check out.  Also, it is right next to the best bike trail in the Midwest...the Natchez Trace Parkway.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wow oh wow. AMAZING AYCE southern breakfast. The biscuits here are a must!!! The restaurant is on a huge plot of land, so lots of open space also to just hang out / roam around after your meal. There's also a gift shop where you can buy their biscuit mix.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Ok... at the suggestion of many, I finally made a trip (out of my way) to have a late breakfast here.  Yes, the biscuits are good, but not amazing.  Most breakfast platters are over $10 (a breakfast sandwich can be had for under $10) and you will get way more food that you could really want or need.

They have expanded into the retail game by operating a gift shop and a few other stores on site (former inn rooms).  Nothing that I just had to have, so I left without buying anything.  

It not overly touristy here, but getting really close to that level.  I will say the food is good but come with an empty stomach to get your moneys worth.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best southern food I've ever had definitely get refills on the biscuits service was lovely fast and felt like home. Some of the best fried chicken!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Do yourself a favor and make sure you top here for breakfast, lunch, or dinner or all three.  To many amazing items to list.  So individually great and the opposite of all chains.  Has the amount of ratings and scores for a reason.  Loved it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Once you have been served and eaten here at Loveless, you realize why there is a line out the door.   Phenomenal staff / service and the food is off the charts.    Loveless is so good, that I actually requested them to cater our wedding dinner for friends and family.   Huge hit.    Thank you Loveless!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wonderful wonderful wonderful.  The southern corn was amazing.  Wish I had bought the peach jam when I there.  Get a chance buy some.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This has been my favorite grub spot since moving to Nashville. I had the watermelon ribs and they were to die for! I've eaten my fair share of ribs and these were some of the best I've ever had. Their desert was very good as well. 

Per the other comments, yes the wait time can be long, but once you try their food you'll understand why folks are lined up.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place was excellent it is a little bit of drive but nothing too crazy maybe 15 mins outside of city. The biscuits really are the best I ever had and the service was family friendly. Cannot recommend any more to check it out.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Incredible biscuits, country ham and sausage gravy! The jams were really nice too. It was neat and clean and the service was good. It's definitely worth your time.

name: Big Shotz
text:
Pretty cool area.  Bar smelled like piss...Literally.  Bathroom smelled like puke pie.  There were 2 other people there and the bartenders were not friendly at all.  You'd think that a bar with no customers would try a bit harder.  Walked in and stayed for 1 drink to be polite and the bartender wouldn't close out our tab until we tipped her first.. So yeah..... good work, guys...

Also,  I don't rate places low regularly if you look at all of my other reviews...

name: Big Shotz
text: Bartenders are terrible. Very rude when you ask what's in a shot. The male bartender tried to fight the group I was with (which we are all bartenders)- he gave us koolaid as a shot. Do not go here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
If you love a good, no a great biscuit, then look no further. Nestled deep in the hills of Nashville is this throw back to simpler times. What was once a family run hotel and cafe is now a delightful dining and shopping destination. From the outside of the Restaurant you would think it would be a long wait but walking in the doors you realize to how spacious it truly is. Did server was super friendly and welcoming. When I asked for a kids menu she was more than happy to oblige. She actually recommended it since their portions were so huge! Mom chose the chicken fried steak while I picked the kids catfish with baked beans. While waiting for our order our server brought out a plate of delightful tiny biscuits with a trio of fresh made jams. 
Everything was delicious! As we were walking out I made a u-turn back to get a mini coconut cream pie for later. Have to say i was not disappointed! Just wish I would have had a few more biscuits!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place has great biscuits and jam! The hash brown casserole is amazing too! I think there's a lot of hype for this place, they can upgrade their menu a bit. Had the BLT with fried green tomatoes and it was plain, the bread was blah too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is the bomb! My first time in the Nashville area and my daughter recommended it since her in laws are regulars. Omg, the biscuits were out of this world. Hands down the best country breakfast I have ever had in my life. I dream of the Applewood smoked bacon and grits and biscuits with blackberry jam. The eggs were so fresh. What a cute place! The gift shop was so adorable, I picked up a few gifts to take back home to Denver. Until next time, when we meet again.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This place is awesome...  best food?? Probably not the  "best," but pretty solid. The atmosphere is really cool...   Yeah yeah, I know it's hokie but it's still fun. I'm giving this place a high rating because of the total package and not just the food. Like I said, the food is good and they have some cool items like the big pretzels and the Speatlze (sp?).  Of course it's touristy....and that's perfectly fine unless you're holding an American German food chain restaurant to authentic German standards?? Honestly, I haven't been to Germany, and I'm sure it's not super accurate. But to hell with it, this place is fun!  do it!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
This review is just for the restaurant part of City Winery. I didn't go see a show there, since I'm under 40, and their lineup makes me depressed just looking at it. 

Unfortunately their food made me even more depressed. The menu (like the music lineup) is straight out of the '90s: pretend fancy and bland, dating back to a time when people were probably just easier to impress. I'm vegan and only went to eat there because they had a promising-sounding vegan entree listed on their online menu, but our waitress explained that they took it off since nobody was ordering it. So I ended up paying $17 for a slimy portobello mushroom with a bit of couscous on the side.

I'm not against paying $17 for an entree when it's good. But there are much better restaurants in Nashville to spend your money at, and after picking up my car from valet (which you have to pay $7 for, by the way) I wished I had gone to one of them.

P.S.: Don't waste your time writing to management. They won't write you back.

P.P.S.: The Black Crowes? LOL.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Back home in Tallahassee, FL, we don't have any authentic German restaurants. So when my Mom and I saw the Bavarian Bierhaus restaurant while shopping at the Opry Mall, we decided to dine in. When you walk in, you are greeted by the sound of the live band playing Bavarian music. You immediately notice the staff wearing authentic outfits and the open beer-garden design of the restaurant. I was thrilled to see the menu and to enjoy their food. 

Boy, was it delicious! We split the Bierhaus Wurstteller, a plate containing 3 links of different bratwurst sausage, red cabbage, sauerkraut and whipped mashed potatoes. The food was just amazing. The bratwurst had so much flavor and the sides were a perfect pair. Our visit made us really wish we had one back home. When back in Nashville, I will be sure to stop in again!

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: Went for the soft opening, newly renovated with the appearance looking like an adult only Steak 'n Shake!  Love it.  Bartenders were awesome as always seeing a few familiar faces from their other business Hemingway's I believe grand opening is in couple weeks check it out !

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I don't know exactly what it is about this place but I'm a huge fan. I suspect it's because of how much it reminds me of Biergarten at Epcot.

Be warned, this place is loud, by design. It's the only thing that I really consider a drawback. It wouldn't be the same if it wasn't, but keep that in mind. You aren't coming here for a quiet meal.

For starters I ordered the Spaten München Munich Hell based on the waitress telling me this was the most popular. Google would seem to tell me it's just an average German Beer, which is probably true, but I liked it. 

For appetizers we had the Pretzel with the Sweet Mustard. This thing is huge and was easily shared by two.

Dinner was München Weisswürste which is two sausage and ANOTHER Pretzel. (We had pretzels for days after this).

The food and beer were great and I look forward to coming back.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Where to begin?  This place is pretty cool as well as VERY loud.  It's connected to a large shopping mall, so our expectations weren't much.

They were B-U-S-Y when we were there.  Our server was stretched extremely thin.  Our drinks ran out.  He disappeared for long periods of time due to having to take care of so many other people.  But the main reason I'm giving them only three stars is because our food was forgotten.  Some other lady brought it out with an apology.  When our server finally did come back around, he seemed surprised we had received it.  It was cold.  Tasty, but you could tell it had been sitting up in the window for quite some time before it was brought out to us.  

Our fear was that had we complained, it would have taken yet another eternity to receive the remade portion of food.  It just wasn't worth it.

This place is neat.  It's touristy.  It just fell short for us,

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing amazing amazing. The wait is worth it, plus there's cool shops and corn hole to kill the time. Biscuits and jams are incredible. Had the pulled pork w/ creamed corn and Cole slaw and it was all great. It was so good we went back a week later and took the in-laws. This time I had the chicken fingers and they were just as good as the pork. If you're in town and can afford a few hours for some good southern food, this is definitely worth stopping by.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The Loveless Cafe did a fantastic job hosting our large family (32 people). We had a wonderful experience. The staff was friendly, courteous, and incredibly efficient. They took our order quickly, had a very short turnaround, and checked back frequently. Compliments to the kitchen staff as well, the food was excellent! Everyone enjoyed their meals. The biscuits are some of the best I've ever had. We were just about ready to order desert when a severe thunderstorm knocked out the power. The staff handled that well too. Quickly split the check and processed all of the individual payments. If anyone in our family are ever in the Nashville area again, we will be sure to return!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Great day for a meal.  I had the Catfish plate.  Four pieces of catfish with a couple hush puppies.  Then for my two sides I had their amazing sweet cream of corn and hash row. Casserole.  You also cannot forget their amazing biscuits as well.  I had a few with a mixer of butter and sorghum, yummy!!!   Washed it down with their freshly brewed sweet ice tea.  I also had a cup of their country white gravy for my catfish!!!!

This was some good country eaten today!!!!

name: Drifters
text:
Coming from Australia, we weren't sure what we were getting ourselves into for a late dinner on a rainy Sunday night from the look of the outside of this place
Once inside it's a simple place with bar, table and chairs as well as TV screens around the tops of the walls with different sports shows.
The food and service was great! I had the Pick Two Dinner Combo (brisket & chicken) and my husband had the BBQ Sampler Platter. Tasted sooo good!
We would definitely recommend this place!!

name: Springwater
text: This place is awesome. We drove into town for a show that was a whopping $5 cover. Cheap beers, good vibe, fun atmosphere; no complaints! Cash-only. No liquor, if it matters to ya. I love how old school it was with the vending machines everywhere. Jukebox had killer tunes. The sound system for the stage setup was perfect. Loved the back room area where the bands load-in and it had the bench seats; so great. Played pool all night/morning. We had a blast. I will def be back! \m/

name: The Country
text: This place has had the worst customer service I have ever received. After having to leave the venue 4 hours early because of random threats from a man at the venue (who was showing his gun to fellow party-goers on NYE promoting others to request he got kicked out), we tried to discuss options with the managers to refund us at least a portion of the $200 on entrance fees my group paid just to leave within an hour of arrival. We were not able to get ahold of them via email or phone after many attempts. Biggest waste of money we have spent on what was supposed to be a celebration of my new engagement. Very disappointing.

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
What a nice venue this is.....
Plenty of parking (pay), lots of room to walk around, plenty of bathrooms..
plenty of good air circulation.

I went here for an event.
It wasn't a music event, it was a food event.
The place was lovely..  spacious.
I got there early enough that I got a free parking place, and didn't have to pay for the lot adjacent to the bldg.

I wouldn't mind going here to see a musical venue, one of these days..
It was very nice for a food event.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Me and my partners played a "rock gig" at this place and let me tell you, the place was B E A utiful. This joint really knows how to throw a rock show. A little smelly in some areas of the venue but nothing a little Lysol and complimentary breath mints can't fix. Only complaint is there weren't enough chairs, I feel like I threw my back out LOL haha gotta go!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
What a great place!

My BFF that lives in Nashville lives within walking distance of this place and has recently discovered its greatness.  I am so thankful that she took me here.

One of the first bonding moments I had here was with the dude working the front ticket counter who was wearing a band t-shirt for the band Anvil.  We swapped stories of meeting the band (I when they came to Austin and he when they came to Nash at The Belcourt) during their promotion of the documentary Anvil, the Story of Anvil where he told me tales of the staff taking the guys honky tonking down on Broadway street.  Because this is the type of stuff The Belcourt has:  independent doc film screenings and indie movie showings that host Q&A's with film makers, actors and in this case musicians.  And who knows maybe the actual staff will take you dancing downtown.  :-)

Build in 1925 as a silent movie house The Belcourt has been lovingly preserved for all to enjoy--thank you for that!  It was even home to The Grand Ole Opry for 2 years back during the Great Depression.  I love it when communities take the time to preserve their movie art houses.  You should definitely take a glance at the architectural touches inside the theater.  

You can get alcohol here in addition to traditional movie theater fare like popcorn and soda AND you get free parking for the adjoining parking lot after you buy your movie ticket so be sure to go back and take of that before watching your film.

You can join as a member to get cool perks.  I am on their mailing list even though I don't live in Nashville just to keep up with what they are programming and showing.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Not bad for a Thursday night,but inconsistent with the mixed drinks and pricing. Good mix of music, friendly crowd.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: A super cool little independent theater that I do not frequent enough. They play classics sometimes on the weekends as well. Oh and THEY HAVE A BAR.

name: Drifters
text:
Goodness gracious, I love Drifters.

We now have Edley's down the road from 5 Points, but where else can you get barbecue and Tex Mex together? This is a beautiful combination, my friends. I highly, highly recommend their pulled pork chimichanga. That sucker always has me coming back for more. If you're not of the meat eating persuasion, however, they have plenty of vegetarian options. I've never been disappointed by anything I order there.

Their patio is perfect for warm nights outside and there's also a ping pong table in the back. You're also likely to be there during a drink special! Be sure to take a look at their calendar as they have rotating weekly drink specials.

name: Drifters
text: I've been to this place a few times and it is one of the few places in town that gets the right amount of smoke in the meat to not hurt the flavor. I've had the wings, pulled pork, and tonight I had the ribs. Each of these did not disappoint. The only thing preventing a 5th star is the service. Each time I've been there's been some kind of problem .Technically this should be a three star review, but the food was good enough to overcome the poor service. Tonight our server was a very attractive woman who really knew the store. But when she brought our first round of drinks where we were sitting outside, she dropped the lemon  of one of them on the not so clean picnic table where we were sitting. She actually attempted to put that dirty lemon back on the glass it fell off of. That is horrid and appalling. Our faces made her see that she was grossing us out so she removed the lemon but did not replace the drink as she should have. This kind of service is unacceptable. The outside tables are like the outside tables that many have in his or her backyard. Would you want anything in your drink that just bounced of a table that has been exposed to the elements? Hell no! Drifters is great other than the weird service you get from time to time. East Nashville is the kind of area where the Carla from Cheers mentality rules the day. But it's fun and well worth the occasional headache.

name: Experience Nashville Tours
text: Definitely a high energy, informative tour with Kaysie. She really knows her Nashville history. She shared a lot of great stories  while showing us the important sites around town. After her tour, we took part in a group bus tour - it was more expensive & way less interesting! Given the chance again, I'd choose Kaysie's tour every time! Great time for a fair price!!

name: Springwater
text: People that use the term "dive bar" should not be aloud in here! Its simply just a "real" bar! for "real" people! I love it!

name: The Country
text:
I loved this aptly named, distinctly Nashville bar and live music venue in Midtown. We visited friends for Vanderbilt homecoming and I'm glad we opted out of the downtown melee to be here. Despite the homecoming crowd, there was good service and plenty of room thanks to a spacious, warmly lit patio. I wish I caught the name of the band playing - they were really good. I didn't have a chance to try anything on the menu but there is a great selection of local brews. 

I especially loved the brooding, industrial chic decor with all its details and custom touches - machinist stools line a long steel-edged granite bar, reclaimed Jack Daniel's barrels serve as the sink base in the bathroom, and wall art features original U.S. patents for different musical instruments. I would love to have a venue like this in DC, but The Country rightly belongs to Nashville as a great homage to Music City.

name: Drifters
text: Drifters is a "dive bar" style BBQ restaurant / bar that occasionally has live music. You can sit inside or they have a good size outdoor section that is dog friendly. The staff is incredibly nice, always have a great experience. Their ribs are fantastic however they run out so availability is hit and miss. That said, in my opinion, the Drifter's burger is probably the best burger in Nashville. I highly recommend Drifters and would give them a 6th star if I could.

name: Drifters
text: Food was amazing for being BBQ nachos, but the service was a little slow as sat there for awhile before anyone acknowledged we were there.   Overall a good experience though.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: The biggest pro is that the Belcourt shows great movies, films you can't find playing anywhere else in a 3 hour radius. This includes even bigger name Oscar runner films as well as indie, foreign and artsy films. It's a neat looking building, good preservation, good location. Concession choices are better than most. On the down side--parking pass comes with a ticket purchase but there aren't really enough parking spaces available for every ticket purchaser. We got there on our recent visit to see a 2:30 pm matinee film and though we were 40 minutes early we were out of luck on parking and had to use the pay lot across the street. Also, though the inside is nice and new looking it doesn't look like the historic building it is (much more modern) and the seats are pretty uncomfortable. Also, I am curious on the NP status of the building--will it remain an NP now that the restorations are done? I assume ticket sales cover the costs of doing business now. Great films are a cultural contribution but I'm not sure it's on the scale of feeding the homeless or educating youth in the sense that donations are due to them once restoration is complete. Anyway, nice new building, excellent film selections, good concessions, clean restrooms, decent location, and nice film series/midnight movies, etc.

name: The Family Wash
text: Very Cool place with great food, music, and people. If your looking for a place that is away from the craziness of downtown Nashville, this is it.

name: The Family Wash
text:
What could I say about the Sheppard's Pie that hasn't already been said? The consistency of the quality has changed over the years I have noticed. Occasionally I get a dill seed, or whatever it is, stuck in my teeth! 

I really dig the windowed off from the music room so that you can watch a band and still have a conversation. I wish more clubs would do this! 

I had a bad experience coming here once where they made me and a dear friend wait outside for 15 minutes outside in the cold before they opened the doors. It was pretty off-putting and my friend, who was from out of town, requested specifically to eat at this restaurant as we had had a good meal there the last time he was in town. He didn't wanna go back there the next time he was in town. 

Over all though a good place to occasionally eat when I get a hankering for the Sheppard's Pie!!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: I've seen a handful of good shows here but nothing about the venue ever struck me as special.

name: Drifters
text:
Drifter's is a cool little spot in the 5 points area just outside of Nashville. The hood has a bunch of food and live music options and is definitely worth a visit. 
We sat out on the patio to watch the live music and WTF, no country music. Darn! 

Our food was tasty but nothing special. We were looking for a real down south vibe and Drifter's was more of hipster joint with more mustaches than cowboy boots. I can get that at home.

I should have known when I saw the vegan menu.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
My favorite place to watch movies.
It's so great, I became a member.
Good variety in movies, comfortable seats, people don't bring their children, and it's never over crowded...

This place rocks and I am SOOOO glad it's nearby.
I also love the neighborhood and usually go wander, after a movie.
Lots of parking (free), conveniently located to restaurants and cute shops and it's clean......

My favorite theater.

name: EXIT/IN
text: A classic venue, dark, dingy and always packed for the shows I go to.  We strolled in at 9.45 pm on Saturday for Mogwai and they came on at just after 10.00pm, perfect.  We managed to stand on the steps stage right which is great for 5.'0 peeps.  The wall of sound from the Mogs was great and very very loud, A good time was had from everyone.  Bartenders busy and efficient, bouncers, busy and polite.

name: Commodore Grille
text: The food wasn't bad for a hotel restaurant, but the truly amazing thing was the music! I know it shouldn't be a surprise being in Nashville, but the music was great from a group of writers and great singers! Great ambiance, and getting to see one of the great country music writers Will Rambeaux and Co play was a treat and a pretty spectacular welcome to Nashville for a first time visitor!

name: Commodore Grille
text: Convenient, casual and clean. Plenty of parking. Our team had a  casual corporate after hours dinner. Service was slow and not overly attentive. Food was typical Bar n Grill offerings. Live music was a nice touch.

name: The Family Wash
text: It's not often you walk in a door and feel like you just came home, but that's what happened here.  This place is the very definition of funky. No contrived "upcycling" here. No contrived music or food. All real and gutsy. If you need for your plates to match, your music to be quiet, and your kids to be perfect, don't come here. It can be loud, and the meatloaf is better than mine. And mine is GOOD. We also had the gorgonzola chips.  I'm not a great fan of blue cheese, but these are addictive. The service was great and the music outstanding.

name: Drifters
text:
Amazing food and great ambience. Was wanting good barbecue after a long flight from Los Angeles. 

My girl read some good reviews about Drifters and we set out GPS as soon as we landed. It was on the way to our hotel.

We ordered the fried pickles, hush puppies, corn dog and the Hickory Smoked Sampler Platter (pork ribs, beef brisket, pulled chicken and French fries).

The ribs are amazing. The meat pretty much falls off the bone. Some of the best barbecue I have ever had in my life! If this place was in LA, I would eat here every day.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Cool joint.  Nice place to see live music.  Nashville can be a tough spot to compete for attention.  Mercy Lounge certainly holds it's own.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
I am in love with this  THEATER !!!
Noel and I went here to enjoy "The Interview" with Seth Rogen and James Franco. The theater is very nice. 
I love buildings from the past !!!

I purchases my tickets online, and had them set to pick up at WiLL CALL
the parking lot to the side is machine pay but if you go to the ticket window they will give you a code to put into the machine so you can park for FREE..I didn't know this, so I paid $5..now I know ..and I will remember !!!

The concession stand had many choices !!! Full bar stocked with alcohol and beer, including draft. The food choices are not your normal movie theater. We bought two large sodas and buttered popcorn and it cost $18.50.  The movie tickets also cost me $18.50 for both tickets. $37 for a great afternoon out with my lovely daughter...plus the $5 for the parking but the end result PRICELESS MEMORIES with my daughter..

There is theater rooms to show four movies at one time here. They show a lot of independent films. You can become a member and support the theater. Check out their website at belcourttheater.com  

I hope you go and enjoy the show!!!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Came here after a rehearsal dinner. We enjoyed the change from country music that we had been listening to all day. Best part was the fact that they had a patio so we were able to head outside as a group and have a conversation while still listening to the band without having to shout over the music!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: I really don't understand how this bar has gotten this many good reviews.  The mixed drinks are WEAK so weak I'm concerned they water down their booze.  It's always uncomfortable temp wise.  I don't know where the friendly staff everyone keeps talking about is they must not work on the nights I'm there, but the thing that pushed me over the edge was I was trying to buy tickets to a show and they were supposed to be $20 if you bought them in advance well the website kept trying to charge me $25.  I contacted the bar and the person who got back to me was friendly but not able to resolve the problem so I just don't get the tickets for the price they advertised.  Instead of coming up with a solution so I could get the tickets for the price they were advertised for I was told I would have to pay $25 cash at the door which would have been fine with service charges that's how much I would of had to pay if I bought them in advance my problem is not the money it was them not honoring the advertised priceand not caring that I was getting overcharged $15.  So I'm keeping my $60-$75 for the 3 tickets I was going to buy and the $60 that I would have spent on booze and giving it to a business that  does right by it's customers.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: This theater reminds me of the theater I worked at while in high school. It was one of the best jobs I ever had. I can really feel a close knit, caring atmosphere along with workers who care about the customers and the movie experiences. There are so many events and promotions, as well as a great rotation of independent films. I love going there so much!

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Who would have thought that printing your own ticket to a show at the cannery would mean a wait outside in the rain for hours. But people and some of my friends who had will call didn't have to wait at all. Something is wrong with this picture. Lesson learned if you go to a show at the cannery go through will call. I guess the employees scanning a printed ticket need some help learning how to use the scanners. What a joke!! BTW the show was great even with the completely asinine employees running the doors.

name: Drifters
text: Nashville is bursting with great BBQ restaurants, such as Martin's and Edley's, but Drifter's shouldn't be mentioned in the same breath. My meal, a plate of dry, under-seasoned pulled chicken, oily hush puppies, goopy cole slaw, and sweet sugary baked beans left me disappointed and feeling ill the rest of the night.

name: Drifters
text: We loved this place.  Good BBQ, good music, great beer selection, cool patio.  We were just passing through Nashville for one night, but if I lived here or nearby this might become my new favorite hangout spot.

name: Commodore Grille
text: What can I say..the Commodore is the first place I came to when I first visited Nashville. The friendly, warm people I met convinced me to drop what I was doing and move here. Literally graduated high school and moved here at 18 after a songwriting camp held at Commodore/Holiday Inn. The food is a little pricey, but it is always DELICIOUS. Last time we all went as a big group and I was playing a show that night. Anyone who ordered a cocktail felt it was very weak, so we all decided to just drink wine or straight liquor. Best place to bring someone to experience good local and acoustic musicians/songwriters. Parking can be validated now which is a pain but there's ample space which I love. Always recommend:)

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: The place is cold and austere...and the seats are uncomfortable as well as small screens. My 55 inch seems bigger than some of these screens. It pretty much sucks.

name: EXIT/IN
text:
this is a great place!!!! we love it!!

http://www.watchonlinevideos.org/dailymotion.php

name: Springwater
text: It is a cute older bar so don't expect fancy modern architecture. Other than that I love the friendly service and the friendly customers. Beer prices are great $4 for craft beers and $2 for Pabs during happy hour from 2 to 5pm. It is cash only. So if you are at the park and need a nice cold beer stop by.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Absolutely awful establishment!! Waitresses didn't come once to our table. They served tables around us, and completely ignored our table! The staff was a complete embarrassment. The food was awful. I ordered a panini and got one slice of turkey. A disgrace of a business. I will NEVER go back and I Recommend No One ever go back!! Am embarrassment of a restaurant. Hope the GM and the staff all go out of business and jobs!

name: The Country
text: I have not eaten at The Country, so I cannot review based upon their menu but it does look a step above typical bar food offerings. I am basing my review on the facility, staff and parking. My husband's band played here, and it was nice while loading in all his equipment there's an alley right next to a side door. Inside was big, clean and offered plenty of seating. There's also a very nice patio outside with great tables and benches to enjoy the music. The staff were all very friendly and I really loved the orange cream martini, which tasted just like an orange cream ice cream bar. What really earns a 5-star rating, though, is the parking. The Country is right next to Centennial Park, an area that is often parking-challenged. However, they have a dedicated lot and it's free! I'll give you a moment to let that comment sink in. Yes, free, convenient parking does still exist in Nashville!

name: Drifters
text:
Marie is the best bartender to grace this planet. She takes care of everyone in a timely manner and makes the best drinks. Her music taste is impeccable and she looks out for everyone in her bar. 
Drifters has great food and a great happy hour! Cheers in East Nashville.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: I couldn't be more grateful for Belcourt Theater. This place gives me option other than big boxes cinema like AMC or Regal. Belcourt also have the personality of its own, looking at the movies that they are showing. Every time I watch a movie at Belcourt, it reminds me of what movie-making is all about. Sure, big box office money is great - but, for an artist, money is not everything. There is character building, story telling, pacing, dialog, etc. From my perspective, I believe Belcourt has found a happy medium. Parking can be horrendous, but that's expected. As for constructive criticism, it will be best if Belcourt can announce showing time at least 2 weeks in advance, so people can have ample time to make plan. Currently, I can consider my self lucky if they announce their showing schedule at the same week. Oh well!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: From NY.. ive bartended for 24 yrs.. these 2 bartenders are 2 of the best I've ever seen.. and the wings are amazing..

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
I've seen a number of shows here and I've enjoyed them all. The sound is incredible and that's the part that really matters in a town with so much competition with live music. The space is massive and the bar area is well laid out servicing all areas of the venue. 

Sunday shows by Lightning 100 offer $2 Yuengling bottles- Lager and Black & Tans. Not too shabby!

Keep an eye on their concert calendar and definitely check out a new or favorite artist.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Nice place to stop and have a beer. We were passing by early in the day, so we sat outside and people watched. There was live music playing next door that we were able to enjoy. The beer was reasonable. The nachos were just ok. The staff was friendly. I bet this is a fun spot at night.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This was my first Nashville bar experience and it didn't disappoint! I loved the atmosphere of the first floor bar with the live band playing in the corner. The bartenders were all very friendly and for as busy as it was, always stopped by to make sure we were doing ok. I gave it a 4 star because the mixed drinks were just ok and pretty pricey but that was expected for this tourist attraction.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We had a blast here on St. Pattys day which happen to fall during our vacation. It had 3 levels and each level had a different bands, also had green beer. Good vibes, and decent dance floors! What more could ya ask for?

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: A really great space to see a show, beautiful venue, however the Live Nation security folks take their jobs a little bit too seriously and are very invasive. Shining flashlights and basically acting like military commanders. Calm down guys, I'm just here to enjoy some music.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Just dropped in there during day and I loved the atmosphere! Someone came to attend to us right away and it was pretty good service. They had a live band playing and they were pretty good. I was disappointed that they didn't have any beers on draft, but they had Shiner Bock in a bottle so that kept me happy.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Cool country bar. I mean theres over 20+ to choose from. All country and all sell liquor so you cant be too picky. Had a live band. Only thing I didn't like was how they didn't have a bouncer or security at the door because a panhandler came in asking for money. Im not oblivious to times being hard but thats not really cool in a packed bar so they need to keep someone at the door.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great bar to stop in for some music. Didn't leave the first floor, but understand there are another floor or two upstairs with different acts. Decent selection of beers and prices weren't terrible for Broadway. Bar staff was very friendly, and the two bands we saw were both very lively and talented - great for a cold January weekday afternoon.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
When my friends told me to meet them at Honky Tonk Central after I landed, I didn't realize that was the name of an actual place. I just assumed that was just what they called the downtown area of Nashville.

It turns out Honky Tonk Central is a huge, three-story tonk bar with live music on every floor, and fantastic people watching. I wouldn't say it was mind-blowing in any other sense, but it's a good first stop to set the tone and kick off a trip right.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: The bartender lost my card, found it on the floor and charged me twice. I've been calling all week and left a post on their Facebook page to try and get this resolved. No one picks up the phone and no one has responded to my post. I don't live in Nashville, and they've made it impossible to solve a problem like this.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Stopped by Honky Tonk for a few drinks before lunch. Went up to the second floor to sit by the open balcony.  Really pretty view of Broadway. 
We had a cool bartender Lindsey from Detroit. She was cool as hell and kept us laughing while we had our cocktails. I had 2 graham cracker shots which were very good. I also had a honey b drink wine high was pretty good. 
There was live music as well and they took requests. We had a good time.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Dive bar of dive bars.  Pricey beers, but live music all the time.  We split a burger and onion rings, not bad.  Wouldn't dream of ordering a salad there tho, can't believe they are on the menu.  Great atmosphere for listening to music, and people watching.

name: The Station Inn
text:
OMG OMG OMG OMG OMG OMG - I believe The Station Inn was literally one of the top things that we checked out when we were in town.  This dive bar was opened back in '74 by a group of six bluegrass pickers and singers (Red Smith, Bird Lee Smith, Jim Bornstein, Bob Fowler, Charmaine Lanham, and Marty Lanham).  It was originally located near Centennial Park, but moved to it's current location off of 12th Avenue.  They are internationally known to be the place to go to hear Bluegrass and Roots music (I wholeheartedly agree!!!).  The venue is first come, first serve; basically, if you see an artist/group you want to check out, you go stand in line, pay cash, and find a spot at either a table or pull of a folding chair.  We were so lucky to find two available seats by the stage - best seats in the house! :D  We saw Willie Watson (Americana folk singer, who sang and played the rhythm guitar with Old Crow Medicine Show) which opened up with Mandolin Orange (a traditional acoustic/electric duo from Chapel Hill, NC).  I was SO AMAZED - Mandolin Orange was very cute, laid-back, and easy listening, with their violin, mandolin, and guitar.  Willie Watson was ridiculous with his 1930s folk/traditional songs, with him rockin' out on his bango, guitar, and harmonica.  The venue itself is dark and people seemed to be having a great time with bar food (pizza, nachos) and beer.  There was one fellow who was quite intoxicated, and Watson actually sent him a message (in a nice way) to have a seat and not to block the audience views (the dude actually got sour and left).  I highly recommend checking this place out when you're in town/area - it was filled with mostly locals, so you know it's legit!  There's a free lot in the back, but just be aware that people tend to double-park (but, it shouldn't be a problem, since all stay until the end of the show). :D

+Bluegrass/Roots music :D
+first-come, first-serve basis in terms of seating
+tight parking (high possibility of double-parking)

name: Nashville Underground
text: Great atmosphere, friendly wait staff, good food and fair prices. A solid choice down on Broadway. Definitely a relaxed bohemian type vibe with lots of couch seating areas

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Cool bar, always playing music. I believe they start around 10 or 11 AM. The place is also on 2nd Ave. so its a little calmer than broadway, yet still really close if you want to hit up those places. Bar tenders were really nice and observant.  Next time I'm back in Nashville, I will definitely stop in a few times.  I heard the egg rolls were really good, the locals (musicians) were eating them...

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Yep, after living here 5 years we finally got to 3rd & Lindsley,  Kicked ourselves all the way home for waiting for long..but hey, we travel for work a lot, we're old, Mad Men was on, I had to wash my hair...w/e.  

Crikey, did we enjoy the show!  We got there at 7 for the 9:00 Time Jumpers show.  We ended up sitting with a couple visiting from out of town as the seats were very slim pickings...but that was fine.  

The food was bar food...the service was fine considering those servers were working their tuckuses (tuckesi ?) off.  You don't go there for the food anyway, silly.  We didn't starve.  And, dinner for two, 6 beers = $48?  Can't complain.

The show...The Time Jumpers were amazing.  Such tight sound and just plain old FUN.  Dawn Sears' voice leaves you with a lump in your throat, seeing Vince Gill in that setting was a real treat, Paul Franklin's steel guitar is like watching magic happen.  It was pure delight.  

The venue was better than I expected it to be.  They had us crammed in there pretty good, but that's how it's done.  The restrooms were clean and available (a plus).

We had a blast and can't wait to go back.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: For our first time in Nashville,  this ended up being our go-to place for great live bands all throughout the day and night.  After visiting other bars on Broadway,  this is where we ended up time and time again.  Nothing fancy,  but a lot of fun.  Go here!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Walked in, looked around, walked out.

Too many old people dancing. What was it, a Wednesday?

EDIT: It was a Wednesday. My bad.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Had a great time!! Cool place mixed crowd and great music. We went on a Friday afternoon. All tables were filled but it was not crowed. Next time I am in town I will definitely visit again.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This place was perfect on a Saturday night when everywhere else was getting crazy packed!

There were three floors - each one with a live band and plenty of seating.  We ended up spending most of our time on the second floor listening to a great band, and eating some really good chicken tenders with the most amazing bar-b-que sauce!  I would recommend that sauce to anyone, it was great!

A little more updated, this place didn't feel like the floor was going to cave in at any moment like some of the other older bars on the strip which was reassuring.  They also have a great view of the strip on the upper floors, which makes for great picture opportunities.  The doors also open in the summer (we were there in the winter) which I can imagine would make this place even better - you wouldn't feel so caved in like so many of the other bars!  A must see!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: loud, the only drinks options were things you could pretty much get at any bar. This place is full of noisy tourists. Usually isn't a place to sit. Not my scene I guess. The environment was kinda stressful.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Literally the worst bar experience in Nashville. Impossible to get a drink, and horrible service. They don't know how to run a bar, especially not a 4 story bar. Paid good money to get into their NYE event and we got nothing that was "included". Ended up having to wait outside the bar for an hour in freezing cold weather, and they wouldn't let us past the 2nd floor even though our tickets included all 4 stories. Will never go back and would never recommend.

name: Nashville Underground
text: A lot of restaurants on the strip, Nashville underground a great spot. The chicken sliders are to die for, great spot!

name: Alley Taps
text: Stumbled upon Alley Taps while visiting for a birthday. The atmosphere is very relaxing and inviting. When we walked in we were the only two people in the bar. Dave and Kyle were our bartenders and they were amazing! Both were genuinely interested in talking to us and had great recommendations on places to check out around town. Kyle made us an incredible raspberry margarita, without a pre-made mixer. Because of Kyle and Dave's kindness and hospitality, we'll be stopping in one more time before we leave.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Went here for New Years Eve last night and I'm pretty disappointed. Waiting in less than 20 degree temperatures for half an hour and being let in one by one. Why sell that many tickets and not have everyone allowed in? I will avoid this bar from now on.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Came here after the stage on Broadway. It was a Thursday night on the day after Christmas but the place got pretty packed as the night went on. The band was great and played a lot of my fav country music. The crowd was mostly mid 20s-early 30s Everybody seemed to be having a good time and dancing.

name: Nashville Underground
text: My friends and I LOVED their roof top bar. It was so fun . We drank , ate and danced the night away. I will definitely come back to this place next time I visit Nashville. Also they have the best fries I have ever had !!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: This place is awesome! Went to see Natalie Stovall and the Drive, the sound was amazing! Only issue was we never got a menu or even asked if we wanted a drink...everyone around us got service but no one even looked at us....I would come back though! :)

name: The Station Inn
text: Great place to catch some music. The beverage options weren't that great, but a place like this isn't about that (or the discomfort of metal seats for extended sitting). But the band and divey atmosphere in a pretty modern neighborhood was worth the $15 cover and made for an enjoyable Friday evening

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Had some friends visit Nashville for the weekend from Wisconsin. The bartender thought my friend's driver's license was fake and tore the holographic film off her ID, thanks to the bartender she now has to get a new driver's license. 

Not to mention, the bartender had a horrible attitude! There are plenty of other bars to go to in Nashville!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Hands down one of the best places to go to in Downtown Nashville!!! This bar has 3 different floors, and had a band playing on each floor. Open patio windows to Broadway Street. It was the coolest!!!

name: The Station Inn
text: For $12 per person we experienced world class bluegrass.  If you are truly a music lover and want to experience polished, professional musicians in a intimate setting go here.  Make sure you eat before you go. Just popcorn and pizza available for food.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: The best place we visited the evening after a noon Titans/SD game.  Friendly bartenders, reasonable prices, good apps.  Outstanding female vocalist as well.  WIll most certainly be my go-to spot in BNA

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This bar does not have happy hour I'm not sure why it is listed as having it, otherwise good band we were just here for drinks

name: The Station Inn
text: Great place to relax and listen to music.  Super talented musicians and cold beer!  Didn't seem to be super touristy when we were there on a Monday.

name: The Back Corner
text:
The Back Corner is what Nashville has been waiting for...New York City meets Nashville. It's located next to 5th and Taylor and is less
Broadway more Flatiron. DJ, mixology, and swanky lighting. Lounge feel with great small plates from 5th and Taylor. Perfect spot to host a party or kick it on the weekends.

name: Nashville Underground
text: The food is great! Literally one of the best burgers and fries I've had in Nashville. Service is hit or miss, hence the 3 stars.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: During the day there's a crowd. At night it is packed! The place has three floors and has a lot of fun things to offer. You can look down on Broadway from the third floor, watch sports on TV, get food/drinks at the bar, or just clap along/cheer to live music. I came here expecting a good time, and I got it. Only got a drink, but the experience was great, and there were a lot of tourists (as expected).

name: Famous Nashville
text: Out of many drinks both times I was here. Most recently on a Friday, they were out of pretty much all house wines. They ended up giving me what they had left of a house wine- was awful.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
We just saw Styx w/the Nashville Symphony Orchestra and really enjoyed the venue, sound and vibe.  This was our first visit to Ascend and we were really delighted with the entire scene. 

The lawn area has many great vantage points ... If you are near the front of line and you sit in very front on lawn you will get a great view of the artist and stage ... If you get there a bit later go to the river side of the lawn where it seems that area is last to fill up but still great views.  

There are about 10 picnic tables that are available but I would recommend bringing a blanket and beach type chairs to sit on.   Our venue had food trucks and we loved the wood fired pizza that was about $12 for a 4 piece pie.  The beer is the usual fair of bud with some craft ones as well.  25oz bud light was $11 and I was told the craft beer was more pricey-  $14, so you may want to pre party or bring a wad of cash.  They had plenty of alcohol drinks as well.   

One note, the line to get in forms down 2nd towards Broadway and gets long ... we noticed many folks coming in from the opposite way up 2nd in a much shorter line merging at the entrance with our line so that could be a short cut for future concerts.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Great place if you want to be completely ignored by the bartender in a nearly empty restaurant. Walked out with my time wasted and not so much as an acknowledgement of my existence by the staff. Pathetic.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Sooo I've had the most wonderful experience at Nashville underground! The service from Courtney and Daniella was so friendly and personable! 
These two really made my friend and I who are locals have such a fun day!!! 
They are great and I recommend you all come to see them!!!

name: Alley Taps
text:
A hidden gem in the heart of downtown Nashville's historic Printers Alley. They have Guinness on tap and it's a Steelers bar!! (Original owner is from Pittsburgh)
The wings are mouth watering and the hot dog on toasted Hawaiian bread will knock your socks off.
Great ambiance, friendly bartenders and dozens of craft beers.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Very cool nostalgic venue, But felt so sorry for the servers.  When you let everyone in venue at one time, they just cannot keep up.  She worked so hard to keep us happy!  Thinking maybe more staff would be helpful.
