I didn't eat, Because I felt like reviews on the food served were not good.  My husband had a burger, He said it was ok.  He has had much better, Just using good locally sourced meat can make a world of difference.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I LOVED the atmosphere here! The have love music on all 3 floors and when u enter u can just go to whichever floor u want. We went to the 3rd floor to get the best views of Nashville from their balcony. I also love that they have a kids menu and that my kids were welcome there. Their food was amazing! Their fries are especially awesome! Definitely would go back again!

name: The Station Inn
text:
If you love bluegrass, this is the place to go!  We've been here twice & both times the music was unbelievable.  You have to like being in close quarters with other people to enjoy this place.  It is usually packed!
Don't miss it!

name: The Station Inn
text: You MUST go here. I strongly suggest you look at their website in advance so you don't end up catching the last five minutes of what seemed to be an incredible acoustic/folk show like we did. It's only beer & wine and seating consists of standard chairs or some old bus seats against the wall!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This is a reality check for ALL of downtown Nashville. I get it. It's hip and cool to be down here. But magic has not found its way into your well spirits. $10 for a well and diet...... shut up. 

That's crap. It's extortion and anyone trying to claim otherwise is on the take or wasted. Great bar. Great music. But your prices are way off.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Very poor service. Waited 30 minutes for a server after being seated. Two waitresses continually walked past us and just ignored us.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: This is a great fun place to take your friends and family if you want to have a chill night but also have great drinks and great entertainment. Best chicken tenders ever!! The waitress, Brigham, gave great recommendations and was so attentive even on a busy night.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Pulled pork sandwich was good. Bloody Mary was under dressed, and without a chaser. Live music and quaint setting to listen to the performing artist. Kaley Hill was awesome.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Ascend is a great amphitheater I always have a good time here. My son got me a box seats for my birthday and I was super excited because normally I would be on the lawn which is not bad either. When you have box seats you have a table of four and you actually have service, unfortunately there was only one waitress because they were short staffed so we ended up having to go get our own drinks and food I would just say for the premium seats it's not acceptable to be understaffed at the price you pay for those seats.  Hence the four stars.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This is exactly the place you want to be if you are looking for a standard, "honky tonk highway" experience in Nashville. The band on the first floor is jamming out every night. It's gonna be the same set of like 10 songs that everyone wants to hear and requests. One of the nights we tried to get them to sing Taylor swift and it took multiple Venmo attempts to get it done. And I spent every day of the weekend in Nash ending up here. 

The bad. They card every single person that walks through this door even if you look like someone's grandpa. The alcohol selection may not be refined enough for the classier person. There are a LOT of bachelorettes.

The pro. There are a lot of bachelorettes? Depends on your opinion of them. It definitely gets a little rowdy here (first floor comments only) but not in an out of control way as far as I can tell. I didn't stay out late any of the nights I was here so the before midnight crowd is respectable but I can't say anything about the after midnight crowd.

name: Alley Taps
text: Showed up at 5pm during the week. Completely dead, which is fine... supposedly happy hours. Ordered a drink and after it was made the bartender informs me it's $10 minimum for credit cards...."but it's 2 for 10$$ so you have another one coming...". Gee.. thanks. No band. Happy hour. Yet a two drink minimum. Awesome, not

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Actually had a nice time at Honky Tonk Central on Thursday night, August 9th, with one major exception. I ordered a beer and a cocktail from the bartender, I paid with a one hundred dollar bill and she gave me a twenty dollar bill as my change. When I tried to tell her she was wrong, and after entirely too long of trying to convince her of her mistake, which included me asking for a manager or supervisor and her saying that there was not one,  her only excuse was, "oh, you're from California, you should be use to being overcharged." Being an industry professional, I know that bartenders should never try to grossly overcharge a costumer. This alone really hurt my Honky Tonk Experience.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Here in Nashville on vacation, and I had seen good reviews for another restaurant next door. We accidentally wandered into this one thinking it was the one I'd read about but THANK GOD FOR THAT! It was amazing. My husband had the hot chicken salad. And I ordered the Ramen.... Holy hell it was soooooo good. You also get to pick your level of spice for everything. We went with hot because we are lovers of all things spicy. The server said that it runs hot but we went ahead with it. THE HOT IS HOT PEOPLE! I can handle high heat but damn. Still worth it, you could still taste the amazing broth and the noodles were perfectly cooked. One of the best meals we have had here in Nashville.

name: Nashville Underground
text: The only area that was "busy" was upstairs, and they had one bartender running bar and floor and it took 15min to get my tea because she had to run downstairs to get it, by time we got our appetizer, we got our food also  and it was ALL wrong and the food was so cold, the fried green tomatoes were soggy, they ignored all our bruger requests. Very disappointed! First time In Nashville and we picked this place to eat! Next time I'll be looking at reviews! Would have done 1 star but the bartender was sweet!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: The drink price reflects the location and the name. $9 for a small vodka cranberry is steep BUT the entertainment and overall vibe here is worth it. There were some really great performers on stage here and even though we went on a Sunday night, the whole place was still lit. This is a classic Broadway experience and I would definitely recommend making a stop here while visiting.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Avoid! Blatantly rude, unfriendly staff. Too many other bars and live music options in Nashville to waste your time and money here.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: They were out of vodka, all they had left was their well spirit. I understand they had a busy weekend, but Monday night guests shouldn't suffer for this. Our bartender was "embarrassed".

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Beautiful venue with a view of downtown Nashville and the river and bridge. The general seating in the grassy area was perfect for dancing and enjoying the night.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: One of my favorite venues I've ever been to in TN.  It's an outdoor venue so it went perfect with the concert that I went to.  The views of downtown were beautiful from this venue.  The front area close to the stage is called the Pit... from what I saw, there weren't any seats there.  Everyone there was standing, but not like it really mattered if there were seats anyway.  Everyone, everywhere was standing and dancing cause it was such an awesome concert.  We got our tickets in section 103 row S.  It wasn't far at all from the stage.  Got a great view of her, and they also had big screens on each side of the stage for you to be able to see her.  Our section had seats to sit down in if you'd like.  The lawn area also didn't seem bad at all.  It's in the very back and you have an option to bring a lawn chair or towel to sit on.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Loved this bar before today... had a disrespectful bartender that said we were in high school. If we're in high school why are you letting us sit at your bar? Just rude and didn't pay any attention to us. The guy before her was amazing though so props to him. P.s NOT IN HIGHSCHOOL just on vacation let us live our lives

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: The food wasn`t very good, too crowded and people started to get drunk & stupid early. We were there when the doors opened @ 6pm for a concert at 8 @ TBshakedown and by 6:30 the stupid started. Strong smell of smoke that was not cigarettes. It reads that 3rd and Lindsley is for all ages, I don`t agree with that at all. I guess if you buy tickets to go there, get drunk and act stupid then this is the place for you. Don`t get me wrong, we like to have a drink or two & have fun, this wasn`t that kind of venue. We want be back.

name: Nashville Underground
text: The food was great but our service was terrible. Our server wasn't aware of the drink specials so my friend who got hot chicken was suppose to get free beer but wasn't aware and also was charged more for her drink when she asked the server prior to ordering it. I ordered a pulled pork sandwich but needed a plate since it was served in a basket so I had to wait 15 minutes for a server to come and then I finally asked another sever who brought me one 10 minutes. My food got cold but I was so hungry, I just had to eat it. The band that was playing was amazing and overall a decent experience my best suggestion is to have more than 3 servers on the floor on a Saturday night. Pictures are our tenders with Mac and cheese, hot chicken and a pulled pork sandwich. I would say 3.5 stars but the food was really good.

name: The Station Inn
text: Some of the best music you'll hear in Nashville!  Small, old place with simple tables and reasonably priced drinks ... and a fantastic studio quality sound system.  This will be a must see on every future trip.

name: The Station Inn
text: The Station Inn is a classic, hole-in-the-wall venue featuring top-notch live bluegrass. It sits on the edge of downtown Nashville in a neighborhood known as the Gulch. The Ridgetop Ramblers were playing on the night we visited and the five members are all excellent singers and musicians. Fully enjoyed their set. We arrived about an hour before the music was set to start and the place was already very nearly packed. They serve beer only, no wine or cocktails. You can get a little thingie of popcorn for $2, though. By the time we left (around 10pm) there was a solid line of people out of the door hoping to enter the sold out venue.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Don't get me wrong: Honky Tonk Central has a great location, a great balcony to people watch, and great artists singing at every level. It's just the rest of it was a drunk, sticky, smoky, disgusting mess the night my friends and I came. I was not impressed.

name: Nashville Underground
text: We had 1 free night during our conference, and wanted to go somewhere casual downtown with good food & live music, that wouldn't break the bank. These guys delivered! It was a Tuesday, so not at all crowded. The music was great, & not so loud you couldn't carry on a conversation. We tried several different things on the menu, but we all tried the hot chicken, & it was amazing! We went for hot (there was 1 level higher, & we didn't go there), which I found to be hot but not painful (varying opinions on that in our group), & not so hot it masked the delicious flavor. I rarely order fried chicken in a restaurant, because I'm worried it will be too floury, too greasy, or bland. This was perfectly crispy, not greasy, & certainly not bland - wowza! Fried green tomatoes were also perfect - thick slices of heirloom tomatoes, light breaded & perfectly friend, with a tasty sauce lightly applied. They had a good selection of draft beers, including some local favorites. Our server, Ben, was delightful. Super helpful without being pushy or intrusive, made great recommendations. I'd definitely return next time I'm in Nashville! Compared to the other places we stopped in on Broadway, it felt more personal, less "commercial country."

name: Nashville Underground
text: Party of 25 girls here for a bachelorette party. Came in for the bull riding attraction at 4:30 pm on a Saturday. Nearly 100 degrees outside, so we really needed some water first in order to begin to enjoy ourselves. 40 minutes at the second floor bar and still couldn't get anyone's attention. 2 bartenders staffed at a bar this size on a Saturday night...not their fault, but certainly management's. Went downstairs to a bar equally understaffed. Found a waitress and asked for a manager, who said she couldn't find them. Very subpar service and a disappointing experience. With 50 bars on Broadway, I would choose another.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Rude is the word of the day. Don't mid it being busy but the bar tender could have been ten times nicer!!!!

name: The Station Inn
text: Loved the Sunday bluegrass jam. Nashville institution!

name: The Station Inn
text:
Came here on a Sunday night and loved the vibe and the music.

@Merlin C, I think the elite status got to your head. It's asinine to "round down" the  rating because of the pizza. The place dubs itself as a music venue (as it should based on the amazing music) and clearly offers the pizza as a snack to the beer and music. It's like rating the Metropolitan Museum of Art in NYC 3 stars because their cappuccino at their cafe came out a little too frothy.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Why haven't I left a review for this place. I've been a handful of times. Face palm. 

Great outdoor venue. Cheaper than most and just as comfortable. Maybe minus the scorching heat at times.  Same decent food and drinks as all the other venues. 

I haven't paid for seats yet. I've always sat in the lawn and brought blankets to sit on. It's worked just fine and you get to enjoy the music and your company

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Super packed tourist destination
Atmosphere / decor - 3
Service - 3
Food - NA
Location - 4
Value - 3

Overall 3

This place was packed every time we drove past it so we decided to check it out. This is very clearly a tourist destination so if that's what you're looking for this is a great place to go. The drinks are really expensive ($9 for a well tequila shot). There was some live music and a few floors which is cool. If you can snag a seat by one of the windows you get a nice view of the strip.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
This venue was great!  Small enough to feel close, seating for almost all.  Fantastic bands like the time jumpers(which Vince gill is a part of!). Little did we know the counting crows would be there watching and two girls from the voice would be there and would sing too!

Food a mediocre but who goes there for the food?  

Get there 2 hrs early for time jumpers.... Place fills up!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
With 3 levels of live musicians, rotating throughout the day, you can pick your music mood as you go. The atmosphere changes with the bands. Mixed drinks had good reviews from our group, like the "Graham Cracker" rumchata drink. Drinks were about $10 each. We stopped by for the music midday on a Friday and the bands were all great. Old country favorites, a few new popular sonhs, and some classic rock - we sang along in our seats. Food smelled great but we didn't eat here.

A few bachelorette parties came through and danced. The space is large enough that you could sit to enjoy the music and eat with your family, or gather around the band and dance like wild, without bothering each other.

Musicians here, and in many other local places, will play to the crowd. A $20 tip gets any song you like.

ATMs on every floor. Easily-accesible sibgle stall bathrooms on each floor. Balconies to view Broadway. Stores to buy cowboy boots, souvenirs, etc. right across the street.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Stopped in with the intention of having just a beer or two. Went to the roof top level and met Bobby Two Times the bartender and ended up staying for several beers while the wife had a few tequila drinks. He was one of the best bartenders I've met in quite some time. I'm a native of middle Tn and have seen Nashville change dramatically over the past decade. It was refreshing to meet a bartender who could still carry a conversation, mix great cocktails, and even give pointers on where to find some great international food selections. Most want to just take your drink order and move on to the next customer. He was able to do that but also continue the conversation with myself as well as other patrons. I will definitely be returning!!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: This is a really cool venue. They bring in such talented musicians. Definitely check it out.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Walking down Broadway at night, I saw lots of live bands and bunches of girls having their bachelorette parties in the various bars and establishments in this area.  It was interesting to watch for a bit, but not the vibe my bf and I wanted as the last stop of our road trip over Memorial Day week.  

As we reached the end of the street, I decided to pop in here because I thought it was Acme Feed, and I had read online that it's a really good place.  Didn't realize until after we walked out that it was actually Nashville Underground, oops.  But I'm glad that we came in by accident.

Multiple floors, each with a slightly different vibe.  Ground level was a country band that was pretty good.  The second floor was closed for a private event.  We went up to the rooftop bar and saw a cool dance floor with a DJ who spun nice tunes, although it was kind of empty.  

Lots of different kinds of beer on tap, and I was happy to finally try some local Yazoo Gershwin beer at the rooftop bar.  It was so refreshing and delicious.  Probably the best tasting beer I've ever had.  I really liked the flavor.  Very nice and drinkable on a hot night.  

Outside was a nice view overlooking Broadway.  Then we realized that there was another floor above us, so we went up to the top-most rooftop bar.

That part was split into two sections, both outdoors, with another bar in between.  We were able to sit down on some lawn chairs and chill with our beers to enjoy the music and see the pretty night lights from the skyscraper nearby.  What a fun way to end the evening without all the craziness of the party animals going nuts in the other bars.

name: Alley Taps
text: A friend recommended this hidden gem on our first trip to Nashville. It's hidden in a back alley and felt kinda speak easyish. Friendly bartenders, great drinks (loved the Oatmeal Cookie Moonshine), and the entertainment was on point (of course it was). They had a blues band playing a wide variety of tunes with a Little Rock and roll thrown in. Super down to earth crowd. We even felt comfortable enough to get up and dance a bit, even though were the only ones tearing it up. Overall a great time and we will definitely be back!

name: The Station Inn
text: This place is a lot of fun on a Sunday night.  We arrived around 8pm for their bluegrass jam.  There is no cover charge, and it lasts until 10-10:30pm or whenever the crowd dies down.  There is a circle of musicians playing bluegrass music in one corner, and a bunch of seating facing them.  It's nothing fancy - just a dive bar with your standard beer and limited bar food - no liquor.  People come and go, and the musicians are just jamming rather than performing for an audience.  It's a bit tough to hear them from afar as the microphones are not on (or at least it seems that way), and it gets loud with people chatting and trying to compete with the music.  I wish an announcement was made for everyone else to quiet down.  We sat about 10 feet from the musicians and had a hard time hearing them sing.  All in all, it's a great place to hang out on a Sunday evening.  Metered parking is free on Sunday evenings.

name: The Station Inn
text:
Hands down, best time I had in Nashville!

I'm not into bluegrass music, per se, but when in Nashville you do as the natives. Though banjos twanging may not be my thing I do love live music. Especially live acoustic music.

We went on a Sunday night which means Bluegrass Jam Session night! There is no cover but it's actually quite priceless. Artists sit around in a circle-ish form playing various songs. Performers will come and go at their leisure, joining mid-song sometimes, playing different instruments and singing their hearts out. I was amazed how well the sounds meshed together when I'm sure some of the players had never been there before. They did a great job of passing the baton and letting everyone have a little solo jam session to highlight their skills.

On the night I went, there was a young lady of probably just 14 or so. The group of adults were so welcoming to her and they were very encouraging, as well. I loved the open & accepting nature of the more seasoned jammers.

The jam session starts at 7pm with audience members coming & going but I suggest getting there prior to 7 to ensure getting yourself a seat.  There isn't much fancy beer but they do have the usual PBR, Bud, etc plus a couple of local brews. A pitcher of Yazoo Pale Ale is $15 which is a great deal and better than Bud...though a pitcher of that will run you just $11. In addition to drinks, they serve food but it looked a bit sketchy. I would just get food prior to hanging at Station Inn.

I saw people of all sorts, all ages, some on dates, big groups of friends, some families including father & son, partners or performers sitting solo - it's a real come one, come all type of place where no one can really feel out of place.

It's dark and a dive but dang is it a delightful deal!

name: Famous Nashville
text: The prices were a little high BUT my Bloody Mary was amazing, worth it for sure. The DJ they had on the roof top was so so good. We had a blast here!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Having three floors was definitely a great set up, and there were plenty of different music types. It provides a great view of broadway and you could spend a majority of your night here because there are so many options for great music. Although the service at the bar was pretty good, a gin and tonic was $9 and they tried charging for cups of water, so that was a little disappointing. I would definitely recommend it to anyone visiting Nashville because of the wide variety of options.

name: Music City Male Revue
text: Came here last weekend for my friends bachelorette party. We were all very excited, but it turned out pretty disappointing. Maybe because it is so new and they are still trying to get things figured out, but we expected it to be a little different and more entertaining for the amount of money that you are paying. Maybe less of a musical and more hot men with less clothing would be nice!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
I have been to 3rd and Lindsley a few times now to see the cover band Guilty Pleasures.  This place is a pretty good place to see a band.

So you come in and there is a bar to your right.  Also note if you walk directly to your right there is a bathroom there.  Typically less busy than the other one.  There are tables throughout including upstairs in a couple of balcony areas.  

The stage is at the back and you have to go down a couple of steps to the floor which I suppose is a dance floor or mosh pit depending on what type of band you are seeing.  Bathrooms are off to the side of the dance floor, multi-seaters, but still can get a line going.  Depending on how packed it is, you need to plan ahead.

Drinks are stout depending on the bartender.  I like stout.  I noted they do have Tito's vodka and they have a section of top shelf liquors for those that don't want the rot gut well drinks.  I don't want those. 

Overall, I have had some fun times at 3rd and Lindsley.  Go check out a live band and get your dance on and drink on here!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: We went to the Monday songwriters show.  It was amazing!  I had bought my tickets a few weeks in advance and having never been to Nashville I wasn't sure what to expect.  There were 4 songwriters who had written for huge stars and told really interesting stories.  We walked from Broadway.  We did eat there and it is typical bar food.  I was happy to see they had a number of vegetarian options. I had the veggie quesadilla which was huge.  It came with a number of fresh vegetables inside and was better than a lot of vegetarian bar food we ate on Broadway.  The last day we were in Nashville our uber driver who is a musician at night told us we had to go to songwriters at 3rd and Lindsley and was happy to hear that we already did.  It's a great way to spend a Monday afternoon.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Came for drinks only.   Bartender was amazingly friendly.  We came early so there was no live music.  We had just arrived in town.
Wish we had come back later.  Regrettably we went to kid rocks to have a terrible food/bartending experience with music... 
When in Nashville and you want to experience southern hospitality...  Come HERE!!!!!!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Our waitress was awesome. The venue was packed, all seats full. Service was timely, cheerful and downright delightful. The drinks and foods were very reasonably priced and tasty. 

We saw Tim Akers & The Smoking Section last night at this venue; to say the band was amazing is a gross understatement! I have not yet had enough coffee to think of the appropriate words to describe this band of 16 or so musicians. 


Tim and his band @ 3rd and Lindsley combined to make a wonderful 33rd wedding anniversary celebration for us.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Open seating, food was ok. Mostly people or there to drink and have a good time.
We were there from 12 noon till around 145, struggling singers!

name: Famous Nashville
text: Worst. First and last time there. Ordered food, came it to pick it up, and they all had no idea what I was talking about. Super lazy employees. The guy just came over and told me 8 min. I asked why. He said it just came though. After 40mins of waiting. Total garbage. The building should be shut down. Ain't got a GED between the 4 of the idiots there. I said I wanted it cancelled and the guy just walked away. It's a joke there and way overpriced.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Came here during a bachelorette party for some lunch. We went to the second floor and sat down and listened to the awesome live music that was happening at the time! 

We ordered some beers and fried pickles to start. There were 8 of us and more than enough for all of us to have plenty of fried pickles so that was great!
Not all of us ordered lunch but those who did got some wraps and I got a salad.

The food was pretty average nothing over the top stuck out but it was very good and the overall experience was definitely worth stopping by! 

Definitely somewhere you should come if you're visiting Nashville even if you're not coming for food, it's awesome how there's live music on the different levels and a great place to just take it all in! Plus the windows give you a nice view of broadway so you can take it all in!

name: Famous Nashville
text:
Great rooftop bar! 

My friend and I came here to grab a couple drinks before the Stanley Cup Final game 3. There was a country band playing on the first floor. We took the elevator up to the roof and found two seats at the bar. They were running a pretty cool special: anyone in Preds gear could get two for one local beers. Love the support of the hometown team. 

I liked the atmosphere. It wasn't as insanely packed as the other rooftops. The bartenders were all nice. We headed back downstairs after a couple drinks to check out the band. Great vibe. Nice TV setup at the bar. I would definitely hit this place up again.

name: Johnny Cash Museum

name: Johnny Cash Museum

My wife and I really enjoyed visiting this museum as we are both Johnny and June fans. We even met Johnny Cash's younger sister Joanne who happened to be visiting while we were there! Visit this museum while in downtown Nashville. Not a huge museum but you can spend hours there checking out all the exhibits.

name: 360 Burger
text: My first time to 360 Burger will unfortunately be my last time. I had been given a free meal promo card to try them out and so I finally did.  The Turkey Bacon Club that I got (which, ironically, is the most expensive sandwich at a little over $9.00) was not $9.00 quality.  After eating about 3 bites, I realized that the bacon was not cooked properly and not crispy at all.  The "fresh turkey" was fresh out of the Oscar Meyer luncheon meat package alright--Publix and Kroger Delis have tastier turkey. It certainly wasn't quality and worthy of shelling out almost $10.00.   And the bread wasn't thick texas toast, but seemed more like sandwich bread and was very small.  I was very disappointed,  to say the least.  Had I paid for this meal, I would have probably asked for my money back.  I'm totally grossed-out and nauseated from the sheer thought that I consumed semi-cooked pork.  The burgers may be good as some of you say, but I will never find out due to this experience here--it has not left the best impression on me.

name: Johnny Cash Museum

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Great museum for any Cash fan. I think it's a little pricey, but you are in downtown Nashville. I would definitely recommend it to any Cash fan.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
So cool and an awesome tribute to a great artist.

I've always liked Johnny Cash but don't know his music that well, besides the more famous songs like Ring of Fire, Folsom Prison, Walk the Line etc. I've seen the Joaquin Phoenix/Reese Witherspoon Carter/Cash interpretations in the Walk the Line film and they're excellent.

I don't really like museums much, just as I don't really like reading books much although I enjoy biographies. This museum is like a Cash biography.  

This museum allows you to become familiar with Cash's music decade by decade with listening stations dedicated to the 50s, 60s, 70s, 80s, 90s and 00s. What an interesting performer! He was exceptionally talented and profound with his messages. What's also great about this is that it makes me wish I'd had the chance to know him. And June.

I enjoyed the film too - and for once I didn't fall asleep watching it. It's become a habit of mine.

Cash fan or not, it's worth a look.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Awesome time going through the Johnny Cash museum. Went in not knowing too much about him and came out as an expert. Loved learning his history and seeing all the success he had in his life. They even had a small display for the movie with Joaquin Phoenix and Reese Witherspoon. (Which is a great movie) we finished the day taking a greenscreen shot with Johnny Cash!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: The best museum I have ever been to.  However I am a huge Johnny Cash fan and I may be a bit biased. I took my Dad when he was in town and he really enjoyed the museum as well.   Personally I enjoyed the last section of the museum where they show some of Cash's interests such as photography and art.  They also had an incredible collection of handwritten lyrics and notes to June.  It was a beautiful homage to the Man in Black.  Would recommend to anyone who has even the slightest interest in Mr. Cash.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Damn it is hard for me to write a less than stellar review of this venue. I have been a patron since 3 locations ago in Cummins Station, I have performed on their stages and listened to others perform my songs, it's always been a good time. Their previous location on 2nd Ave was one of my favorite places to hear live music, eat great food and drink delicious cocktails. I am not sure why they had to move, I expect either the rent went up or the building is being replaced with another high rise. The new Nashville. The previous room was big and square; even at the back tables you had centralized sound and view. The new room is shallow and wide. 

Today was the first time I visited the new location on 4th. Looked promising from the outside, but the interior is cold and sterile, and while it was mostly empty, I expect people sitting at the far side tables would not have an optimal listening/viewing experience. Friends of mine were playing, and it was my first time having brunch at TLR but their regular offerings are so delish I didn't expect a problem.

Well...muchos problemos. Starting with service, which was virtually non-existent. Took forever to flag down a server and even get a menu, and the place was nearly empty. The offerings were limited. What my friend and I received was barely edible and personally my own breakfast at home would have been preferable. Coffee served in a paper cup at a sit down restaurant that actually owns real dishes. Creamer served in a plastic cup to be dumped into the other cup. The appetizingly described potato hash on the menu, promising a fresh hash of potatoes, peppers and onions underneath two sunny side eggs, was ore-ida frozen home fries that tasted like they were baked hours ago - overcooked, cold, hard. The eggs on top were virtually snotty, whites barely hardened, and served ice cold. Requested tabasco served in yet another plastic cup that I waited 10 minutes for as my breakfast got colder. I had to get up and ask for it at the bar when it didn't come. My friend's fried green tomato BLT was gummy, bacon flabby, toast cold and hard, french fries also cold and crispy as cheetos. Not a good kind of crispy. We would have sent it all back but it took forever to get any service at all and we were starving at that point.

Brunch just felt like an afterthought, and after speaking to some of my friends at other tables who had also just eaten, it seems everyone agreed.

Didn't drink today but looking around, the drinks did look good and they have two for one bloodys and mimosas. Next time I will just sit at the bar and drink my brunch. TLR does feature some of the best performing songwriters in Nashville and the sound system is just as awesome as ever. I love you guys, and I hope dinner service at the new location will be just as amazing as it has always been on 2nd Ave, but brunch needs serious work. Too many other options in this foodie town.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
This was easily the highlight of my visit to Nashville. General admission is $17, and it's worth every penny. 

it's not a very big museum, but it's full of stuff. There's stations to listen to his music, and there's a back room that shows a film about Cash and features his work. 

There's so many things on display. There's a ton of outfits, hats, and boots that he wore on TV or in concert. His gear from his time in the military is there, furniture from their home is there. There's hand written lyrics sheets and love letters and the awards he received. There's even a door from prison on display there. I love Johnny Cash, and it was awesome to get to see some of this stuff first hand.

I also really liked that there's no guide, so you can stroll and read at your leisure. I like the no-pressure situation. 

On the way out, there's also a gift shop. There's shirts, books, albums, jewelry, and all kinds of things boasting his picture or his lyrics. I ended up buying my girlfriend a bar of soap that smelled like mint called Aloe, I'm Johnny Splash, because two puns are better than one. 

There's also a cafe here. We didn't get a chance to pay it a visit, but I think it's pretty cool. If I was from the area, no doubt I'd hang out there more often. 

If you're a fan of Cash or of country and rock music, be sure to stop here next time you're in Nashville.

name: Johnny Cash Museum

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
Went on this dinner cruise during a trip to Nashville and had a wonderful time! 

My boyfriend and I went on a Monday night and at first were a little worried because when we look around all we saw was really OLD people, we were the youngest ones there and we were over dressed compared to everyone else. 

Before entering the boat, there is a person there taking pictures and we were able to take one infront of the General Jackson which I thought was pretty cool. 

When we actually entered onto the ship everyone spread out and it became more intimate for us. We took tons of pictures, the sun was starting to set it was just wonderful. The river was absolutly beautiful and the staff was very welcoming when entering the ship. 

 I found a waiter and ordered a bottle of white wine for my table to be there when we were ready to be seated. About an hour we were outside and on the upper deck having cocktails and watching the band that was playing. On a loud speaker they told everyone to enter the main dining room for dinner.

The dining area was huge and looked very elegant! There was a large stage in the front with the curtain still up.  We shared the table with about 8 other people. This was nice because everyone was interacting with one another and we got to meet people from different places. 

When we got to our table our bottle of wine was warm, however, one of the servers realized that it was sitting there awhile and took it back and brought us a new one nice and cold. They poured us both glasses of wine and ice tea. They immediately brought us our salads and bread. I also noticed that there was a small menu on the table just in case you wanted to order more appetizers. The salad was very fresh and the dressing was very good. After salad was done they brought us dinner which was also very good but I think it could have been a little more hot. But this was understandable due to the fact there were tons of people to feed at one time. 

After dinner, we had about 30 mins to break away from the dinning area and they brought us to downtown Nashville where we were able to take even more pictures. The whole city lit up at night was just gorgeous and we went right under the bridge which was also lit up. When we went back into the dining area our dessert was already on the table. They forgot to bring my boyfriend and myself coffee and it was a pain to get them over to serve me. I also wanted to order Ammerato but before I had the chance to they have already walked away. 

During dessert the show started and it was excellent! They actually pulled my boyfriend on stage and made him do the funky chicken infront of everyone with the rest of the entertainment staff which was both hilarious and fun. We wound up having a great all together and is something you should do of you are visiting Nashville. 

The only complain I have is that the wait staff is very slow and rarely check up on you to see of you need anything and when they do come by the give you your food and leave quickly, if this is fix it definitely has the potential to reach 5 stars.

The second floor was more of a nightclub feel and we danced for hours having the best time of our lives! And then the rooftop, the view is hands down best in the city! Make sure you try their specialty drink called Tequila Mockingbird!  I'm giving this a perfect score because I will definitely be back!!!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I love the Listening Room Café! I started coming here after tickets to the Bluebird became impossible to get, and I must say that I am impressed.  It is your typical songwriters round, where songwriters perform a song and tell the story of how it came to be.  Some writers are just starting out and some have lots of hits that you will recognize.  Definitely a lot of talent at this place. Every show that I have ever been to has been awesome.  The drinks and the food are both pretty good, the only complaint is that sometimes service can be a little slow.  Overall, the Listening Room Café is a great way to spend a night in Nashville!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Lousy food.  Limited menu.  Every item had egg in it.  Server gave himself 20% tip because there was 8 of us even though he messed up the orders and made several promises that were not kept. Music was good but, everything else sucked.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Listen.  I feel horrible giving one star for anything but this was terrible.  The only thing I liked here was the music, specifically Taylor Dukes. She was phenomenal, but literally everything else was very bad.  My girlfriend ordered a beer and her glass had lip marks on it. I quietly told the bartender and asked for a new one.  I watched her pick up a different glass, hold it up to the light, and put it back to get another one.  BOTH GLASSES WERE DIRTY. No bueno!  We ordered a couple of small plate dishes.  The ravioli was OK, but really, how can you mess up fried ravioli.  The chicken tenders were so dry and cold we asked for another order but don't worry, the new plate was cold too.  After about $30 in small plates of bad food we were still hungry so we ordered two sides of mac and cheese that they basically threw on a blank white plate. Zero presentation, it looked like I went up for seconds at a potluck.  We left immediately and drank a glass of red wine to try and kill any possible foodborne illness that may have been lurking. Thanks but no thanks.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I love going to museums, but this one is extra special.  There are many types of displays and I enjoyed them all.  They have many items that were owned by Johnny Cash and a few that were owned by others who had some connection to Johnny Cash (e.g., an Autoharp that Mother Maybelle played!!!).  I also enjoyed all of the video displays that give an experience that is more unique.  One thing I really enjoyed was a small area where Johnny is projected on a flag while he says "Ragged Old Flag".  There really is something for everybody here--personal items, costumes, guitars, awards, etc.  All of the items are beautifully displayed and you can get very close to everything.  The museum is very well laid out, so it did not feel crowded at all.  It felt intimate, classy, and very respectful to the memory of the great Johnny Cash.  It exceeded my expectations and they were already pretty high!

I went with my husband who is not really a fan, while I am more at the super fan level. :)  I figured he would be trying to move me along, but he really enjoyed the museum, too.  I was surprised that I learned some new things about Johnny Cash.  I think I heard a worker say it takes most people about 45 min to go thru, but I spent at least twice that because I wanted to soak it all in.

The museum store had so many cool items!  Everything you can imagine!  T-shirts, caps, signed Johnny Cash photos, old tour books, books, I could go on and on.  The folks there could not be more friendly and helpful.  I enjoyed chatting with them.

Don't miss this great museum!  It is just off Broadway near other landmarks like the Ryman and Tootsie's.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: A great place to hear music in Nashville. We saw two singer-songwriters on Saturday evening, and while only one of them really had music we liked, the whole experience was fun -- a great way to spend a few hours in Nashville (if you like music). The bar was more than adequate, and the facility tried to make sure the audience kept conversation to a minimum during the performance. We'd definitely go back.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great place, great music. Thanks Nicole for awesome service. Wishing Dierks was here!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Top 5 places to see in Nashville and well worth the time.  Attending a corporate event with a special performance by Tommy Cash.  Lots to see in the museum.  A must see!

name: 360 Burger
text:
Been here many times -- very interesting burger menu!

I've had nothing but a great experience here every time I've visited.  The wait staff is super friendly, informative, and really seem to enjoy working here.  The food is delicious -- I've enjoyed my meal every time I've went.  As a salesman I take many prospects out for lunch, this is perfect for a laid back lunch and always pleases my clients.  Great place!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: It's time for another Cafe to develop legendary live music from songwriters and aspiring singers.  Love the fact that you can get a reservation and that the seating area is large enough to handle popular artists following. Locals should support it if they continue to want local support vs. a conventioneers watering hole.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Update: the management didn't reply to my email. I just walked past on my way to Roberts and an African American guy wasn't allowed in as they didn't like his shorts! I told him they don't like bags for men or tank tops and we laughed sadly at this racist, homophobic and sexist bar. Avoid and cross the road.  

Wow. Only bar on Broadway to have any issues with. Only door staff who were rude and out of order. I walk in with my tiny back pack on. It's been stormy and has my Brolley in. "No back packs" I point out three women nearby with giant bags. "They are purses" I then say ok I'll take my money elsewhere. This "man" with a 80's moustache says I won't get in anywhere. I point out I've been to 5 bars today and carry on. It's like the review below. Double standards and basically sexism. Don't allow women in if they have bags or you are a sexist bar. 

I'll be avoiding like the plague now as this obviously isn't owned by people from Tennessee. As they have all been polite and nice.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: I didn't think I'd like this place. I'm a pianist myself and sort of a music snob and I thought this place would be kind of hokey. I actually enjoyed it a lot! The pianists are very talented and had great personalities for this job. I was expecting to spend $20+ to get in because I'm from New York, and the piano bars in NYC are more pricey, so when I heard that it was only $6, I was thrilled. I didn't request any songs and only had one drink while there so our stay wasn't pricey at all. I really enjoyed my time at Big Bang!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
One star is appropriate. Four of us went for New year's and got there around 7pm to head up to the roof. Around 10:30 they came up pushing wristbands or we couldn't stay until midnight. Not happy, but ok it's New year's. Asked about champagne toast and fireworks and was told by two different people we would get champagne and have a view for the $50 (each) wristbands.

You know what happens next. Midnight rolls around, no bubbly, fireworks behind the tall AT&T building and can't see them at all. Get our bill and find out our domestic beers were hyper expensive, even compare to LA. Extra drinks in the receipt we didn't order, but bar was packed and didn't want to wait any longer at 12:30am.

No food after 9pm, so suffered through to them pay more to just stay. Had fun for the night, but would never, ever, ever go back. 

Beware, all about the $$$ and not a trustworthy place.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
One of the best places to see music in Nashville. Love seeing the singer/songwriters behind the hits. 
Atmosphere is great. Plenty of seating and reasonable drink prices. Plus the food is way better than the average honey tonk.

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text: Great loud music. Very big dance floor. The DJ was average, but everyone seemed to be enjoying the music and having a good time. Our bartender also poured really strong drinks. This would be a great place if you're looking to dance. They also had a lot of tables to the side if you wanted to sit down and chill.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: The food was good service good music good drinks great . A lot of fun . If you are hungry on Broadway it's a good place to go.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Food not great not much better than McDonald's!  Bathroom dirty!  Men's room smelt of urine per husband.  Staff great and music great but disappointed in rest! Get drink only there!!!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Good atmosphere and perfect venue to listen to live music with great food!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This museum in the country music capital of the world is a treat! I loved the interactive exhibits and films throughout the museum highlighting Johnny Cash's long and distinguished career. I learned a lot about his philanthropy with helping promote prison reform, his film career as well as his music. There are costumes and lots of memorabilia too. Upstairs is a separate Patsy Cline Museum. We really enjoyed this museum. The layout & the exhibits were great!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Nick deckard will take care of you, even on a busy Saturday night! This man is beyond words for service. Makes genuine eye contact between tables to make sure you are doing alright! The standards of customer service is set high by this individual, give this guy a raise !!!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: They have the most AMAZING songwriters!!!!! They have the WORST food you will EVER eat! The cheese on the cheese plate looks like it can from a Chernobyl Nuclear Farm. Seriously if you let it sit there for five minutes it turns neon. It really bothers me because I want to give this place my money but the SIX different times I have ordered food here (I tried something different each time) I have taken one bite and stopped eating! Come on guys...it is not that hard to make decent food. This stuff is terrible! Skip the food and plan to order at least $15 worth of drinks per person (It is well worth the investment.) If the food were even a tiny bit better people would be more likely to come for more than the music and this place would be packed EVERY night. PLEASE, PLEASE, PLEASE, fix your food problem! Even the wait staff complains about it!!!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I would recommend the food, but not the service. My party ordered burgers that were very good, however, the service did not match quality of the food. Our ID's were checked an unnecessary amount of times and they nearly broke my ID trying to see if it was a fake. And the drinks themselves being over priced and taking far too long to get to the table. Most likely will not be returning.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: My friend and I were recommended to visit the listening cafe. We got tickets for the 6:00 show and arrived 5-10 minutes early to be seated for the show. We order a couple drinks and a couple appetizers. The waiter recommended the fried pickles so we ordered those. They were great! Sweet pickles with a mild kick in the ranch dip. Perfect combination! The singers (3 of them) on stage had the best voices!! They played great acoustic music that they all wrote themselves. Backing the music with stories on how they wrote each piece. It was such a wonderful experience and I'd definitely go back!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Yikes. As a resident of Nashville, this place is awful. And if I was a tourist, save your money and go elsewhere. We went to brunch today at 10AM. They had a "special" menu which meant no buffet and less sides. It had to be printed off twice, because when I went to order they noticed not everything had a disclaimer, so had to reprint and I had to reorder since they cut items off the menu. We sat there for an hour before anyone played on stage... which isnt that the whole concept? 

Finally the food - no flavor and terribly overpriced. My friend had the CB Slinger, which was just a salt bomb of chili and burger. They got the eggs right but the dish was convoluted mess. I had the Egg + Pulled Pork Benedict. The side of potatoes I got were the saddest looking shriveled up things that looked like that had been under a heat lamp for 3 hours. The hollandaise sauce was for a lack of better words "gloop". 

We waited 45 minutes for food. An hour for the artists to go on stage. The food was terrible. Some of the worst I have had since living in Nashville. McDonald's breakfast would've been more satisfying than what they are slopping up at The Listening Room. So many better brunches and live music spots. I'm just glad I went to this place before I took any out-of-towners... would have been embarrassed.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
This was a really interesting experience and the songwriters were really talented. I wasn't sure what to expect but it's a very toned down performance where the songwriters play their songs in acoustic and discuss them. Kelly was the best of the four in my opinion. Not a lively show by any means but no real complaints about the music or songwriters talent.

I was less than pleased with the organization. Before the room opened it was a crowded push toward the doors and I could see others getting visibly frustrated especially since the show started a little late. 

The worst thing was the food. Do not eat here. We ordered wings and Mac n cheese and it all tasted like cardboard. To make matters worse, there is a $15 minimum and the wait staff was visibly overwhelmed taking food and drink orders for everyone in the room. The drinks weren't great either, I'd recommend just sticking with beer to fill your tab.

TL;DR The music was solid, but I couldn't look past the terrible food and poor organization. I will not be coming back.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
Love this bar. 
Love the huge stage, the sound, the bans that have been here last 4 nights, I could see myself here every night if I lived in Nashville.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
2 stars for the food
5 stars for the music venue

The Listening Room is downtown Nashville's response to the Bluebird Cafe: A showcase for singer-songwriters. 

Tips:
- Tickets are cheap, so order them in advance, even if you are uncertain of your plans

- Eat before or after the show

- Although there probably isn't a bad seat in the house, Tables are assigned first-come, first served by checking in at the hostess stand, which is straight ahead as you come in the main door, so arrive early

We went to the second show on Valentine's Day. They had a special prix fixe menu, plus limited a la carte selections. Although pleasant enough, our waitress made mistakes placing our order, which, considering the price, was quite disappointing. The food is NOT the reason to patronize The Listening Room.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Great music and atmosphere! There are a few different floors and are all really amazing. The roof has heaters if it's cold out which was great.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This was a great spot. Great music. Servers and hostess were super friendly and the food was fantastic! Really enjoyed the atmosphere. Total win.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: In our opinion, this is THE place to take guests to in Nashville. We often go ourselves, but it's an exceptional place to introduce visitors to the true vibe of Nashville.  They have incredible songwriters rounds that give you an up close look at the writers behind the hit songs. You can chat with them after their shows and feel really connected to the music. You might also have the chance to meet up-and-coming artists, as well as major artists. The food is great, service is stellar, and the booking agent knows what he is doing!!! The Listening Room is a true Nashville treasure.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Love this place! Great experience to be had in Nashville--A must go if you're in town visiting. Always a great time: good food, great service, and a fun, upbeat environment.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: As good as it gets!  I have visited the Johnny Cash Museum twice now since it's grand opening. Bill and Shannon Miller have created this heartfelt display of "The Man's" life. Starting from his childhood years in Dyess, Ar., through his personal life and entire career. Each display includes an IPad with information about the items you are viewing. The set up is high tech impressive yet easy to understand and follow. There are so many personal items of interest that provide a good look at particular times in his life....stage costumes, guitars, furniture, handwritten items, video presentations.awards and documents never before seen by the public. This is a state of the art Museum to honor a great man, music icon, devoted daddy, granddaddy , brother, uncle and friend whom his mother named J.R. Cash. A walk through this museum takes you back in time in the life of Johnny Cash. It is a MUST see! And, be ready to shop! The gift shop is classy and full of CASH goodies... Cash IS back!  Now, go see for yourself!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Bouncers wouldn't let my friends in "because their pants were too baggy". Very disrespectful.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: Talk about amazing and life like!!  Such a neat experience!  This was one of our top favorite places we visited when in Nashville.  My kids are still talking about this place!  So much fun!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great atmosphere and food. Bartenders are awesome and very attentive. Jake took care of us and made our experience vey enjoyable. He likes to have fun with his patrons and is one of the best bartenders I've encountered in my many travels. Will be going back to visit Jake again on our next two nights in Nashville.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Ashleigh in the rooftop bar is the best bartender in Nashville. Will get you anything you want and fast at it

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: Madame Tussaud's Nashville was a pretty cool experience. Tons of country music stars, pop music stars, and my personal favorite a section dedicated to The Beatles.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: The Asian bouncer (Paul I think) was super friendly! My experience was better because of him! Highly recommend this place.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Food is not why you go on this showboat. However, the boat ride was fun, moving out to the Nissan Stadium area was great, and seeing the massive crowds by Broadway was unbelievable as we moored. We had no trouble getting chairs right up along the railing to be up close and personal with the fireworks over the Nissan Stadium and river, and to be able to avoid the crowds with a nice river cruise back, entertainment the whole way if you wanted it, or a nice breezy spot on the aft of the boat if you didn't (that was what we went for). Either way, as long as you go in for the experience and not the food, this will be a night to remember!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: An okay showboat offering. The food was good and the show was nice save for a couple off off-key moments and missed cues. But it's a new show and the performers will get better deeper into the season. The wait staff is friendly but all were language challenged and placing drink orders was a bit challenging. Also they were frequently nowhere to be found. I'd ordered the optional Hot Nashville Chicken, which is one of the spiciest things I'd eaten in a long time. And I could not get a water refill. Luckily my wife let me douse the flames with her glass. Other patrons at our table also had trouble getting drinks and getting them accurately. There's not very much scenery on the trip with industrial back lots being some of your views. Due to water levels the captain didn't take us to the downtown view and we got back early. A fact that they didn't communicate to the buses, so there was a long cold wait to leave.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Very big and exciting place.  The music was par.  We heard better in other places on broadway.  The servers were very attentive I was hoping for more from kid rock.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text:
Went to bar on Sunday with a friend for brunch, ordered the mimosa tower (2 bottles of champagne w/oj in large tube with a spout). The bar filled up quickly, but the bartenders and servers had it under control. We both ordered the crab benedict, it was tasty, but big enough for us to share. We also received the food fast. A friend joined us maybe an hour after our food came, and when she ordered, it took a very long time. One of the bartenders told her the kitchen was backed up, and apologized. All three of us work in a bar- we understand what a pain in the ass brunch can be, so our friend sipped some of our mimosa during her wait. (No big deal)
Overall a great experience, great prices, and great service i will be back.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I love the Grand Ole Opry - it is a classic Nashville venue and I love that it's modeled after The Ryman. I've been here a few times for the Opry shows and really enjoy the fact that they have so many performers in their performances, it makes it more enjoyable and fun, in my opinion. The parking lot can be a bit dangerous for pedestrians but luckily, it's massive so there's plenty of parking. Staff is always helpful if you have questions and will tell you all about the history of the Opry. Great place to bring kids too! Love this place!

name: Music City Psychic
text: I went in with a friend for fun while visiting the bars in the area and I was very pleased. It was the most accurate reading I've ever gotten. She was great and if I lived in the area I would definitely go again if I wanted a more thorough reading.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
Meh is right. The wife and I stopped in here for a quick bite and drink before a TPAC show. Everything we'd've rather had was closed down the Arcade Alley, so we opted for this as it was right around the corner, and only about 2 blocks from TPAC.

Seating wasn't a problem, as the place was about 1/2 full (we were there around 6). We grabbed 2 spots at the bar and enjoyed their happy hour specials, which on this particular day (Thursday) were 1/2 price apps and $5 drinks from a designated list of cocktails. We opted for cheesesticks, wings, and chili cheese fries for our snacks and standard margaritas on the rocks for our drinks.

The cheesesticks were fine, nothing either impressive nor offensive. The 'marinara' that came with it was standard salsa, straight out of the bottle. Meh. The chili cheese fries we didn't get to experience, as they came out and told us there was no chili, so we just got regular fries - they even forgot the cheese... The wings were the worst offenders, though. Very tough and cartilage-y, sparse meat, no real flavor or seasoning. I ordered them tossed in buffalo sauce and they most decidedly were not. Couldn't tell what it was, but it wasn't hot wing sauce. Overall, the food was very subpar and we're glad we got it all for 1/2 price.

The margarita I got was made with (admittedly) a well-portioned amount of liquor, but muddled with Orange Juice. Yuck. Some folks may like it, but this was my first marg made with OJ, and it was not a good look.

At the end of the day, we left full, but not overly pleased. The service at the bar was sufficient, however, and quite friendly, so no complaints there. We'll try elsewhere when next we're in the area.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Fantastic burgers and even better fries especially! The diner was not busy at the time we went so we had very fast service. The bar also has a lot of character and is a great place for a late night dinner. The location is a little sketchy but it lives up to it's name as a "back alley diner".

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We were in Nashville and decided to check it out. 5 dollar cover per person wasn't good with a party of 9 but girl at door worked it out . Pork nachos and hummus is amazing. Service is great . It's a very loud place so nor so good for kids.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Last week, I came in and I immediately loved the vibe! It was super busy but the hostess Adora was very attentive and friendly.  We were seated promptly and our food was great! I waitress was a little overwhelmed but she continued to check on us the entire time! (Wish I remembered her name!)

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Definitely worth the $20. I think it was a great tour for the money, they accept AAA and give a couple dollars off each ticket.  Our tour guide was great and now I can say I sang at the the Grand Ole Opry even if it was you are my sunshine. 

Seeing the dressing rooms, the green room, and standing on the original floor was a wonderful experience.

name: Hotel Indigo Nashville
text: This slightly overpriced place feels sort of thrown together. The lobby is impressive and nice, however it feels sad at night when they have live music, but no one is there at the bar to watch. I'm not sure if that is the case all the time or not, but it is not a lively scene. The building is old and has been remodeled, which I can appreciate, but I just don't understand some of their decisions: They have a Styrofoam tile drop-ceiling in the hallways, which makes it feel like an office, minus the florescent lights. There are also  crazy powerful fans blowing though vents in the wall right by the elevator, which was loud, annoying, tacky, and totally unnecessary. The room was nice enough, but with some quirks/imperfections. The laminate/fake-hardwood flooring did not even meet the baseboard at the edge by the wall, leaving a gap of about half an inch. I just stared at this in disbelief. I just can't imagine a hotel manager saying "oh, thats' good enough." If you had a contractor do this in your home, you would be unhappy, especially if you were paying $230 a night to sleep in your house. And this could be fixed in 10 minutes with $10 worth of corner bead from home depot. I just don't understand the apathy, given that the place is supposed to be fancy. The fancy white leather rolling chair in the room was all stained and discolored. Also water stains on the fake hardwood floor.  There was only one nightstand for the kingsize bed, and there is room for another. Oh, and there is this weird child-sized door in the wall that leads to the furnace, which was completely covered in dust and high-voltage stickers. Very weird decision. At least put a lock on it. Totally gross and probably unsafe if you had a curious child in the room. When we went down to get our breakfast we were actually super impressed...it appeared that this was the most impressive continental breakfast ever: scrambled eggs, biscuits and gravy, sausage, bacon, hash browns, etc. We thought for a moment that hotel was going to redeem itself in our eyes, until a server came by and gave us a $37 bill. No free breakfast. No free coffee. $230 a night. Oh, parking is also $20 a day, and the parking garage is kinda gross, and is not exclusive to the hotel. We also waited for valet but no one showed up.  Oh, I almost forgot;  The front desk also charged my debit card over $500 after we checked in, even when we had already paid through hotels.com. This drained my account for a day until I could figure out what had happened, leaving us with only $23 in cash to spend on our first day in town. We had to just walk everywhere and look at restaurants that we couldn't eat, and we visited the gift shop of the parthenon, because we had no money to pay the admission fee. All the while I was calling my bank and trying to figure out why my money was missing. This pretty much ruined the first half of our visit.  When I finally got it figured out I went to the front desk and they acted like it was no big deal, as if  it happens all the time. They said the charges would be reversed in about a day, but then guy at the desk called my bank and they reversed the charges in minutes instead. In short, I thought this place would have a little more character and charm than a chain hotel, but it doesn't.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Being an avid country music fan, I knew I had to make a trip to the Opry while visiting Nashville. The venue, though its nothing too fancy, has such a rich history and has been well preserved. 

The show itself was fantastic. Very entertaining and  little down time between acts (something that you dont get very much at concerts nowadays). Even if you aren't fond of a particular musician, they're only on for 15 minutes. That being said, I can see why it is a disappointment to some who come to hear a particular act and only see them for a short time. But the Opry IS a radio show and that's how it works.

Cons: The woman we spoke to on the phone when ordering tickets was quite rude, and I am not one to take these instances too personally. She acted as if we should know the answer to questions we were asking and gave us an attitude when we inquired about standing tickets as opposed to the seats. However, everyone else at the Opry was very welcoming, so I would say that their staff is attentive overall.

The traffic pulling out after the show was a nightmare. We expected it to be busy and congested, but the Opry parking staff that was directing traffic had no idea what they were doing. Crossing pedestrians while cars were moving, allowing cars to stop and wait, not moving taxis along etc. It would have been easier to pull out if the parking staff wasn't confusing everyone.

Overall, neither of these instances were anything close enough to ruining our experience at the Opry. I would recommend it to anyone who loves live music and wants to experience a historical venue. Just a couple of things to note before you go.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Fantastic spot for the Beer Lover. Cool ambiance and good service. The "chalkboard" had some great and rarer choices. They had most of the well known gold standard American IPAs etc

The food is decent. The menu choices are spot on, just not very tasty.

I was hoping for at least a better pretzel - it was wilted and seemed like something you could buy frozen at the grocery store.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
First let me say the band playing was phenomenal!! 

The food was to die for, I got the Chicken Fried Chicken with the Mac and cheese and the creamed collards on the side. They were to die for!! The chicken was juicy and we'll seasoned, the collards were different from what I'm used to but I have never had them creamed, they had maybe bacon and carrots in them and it was surprisingly delicious!! The Mac and cheese was the only thing I was not really enthused with as it was not baked but it was good for what it was. 

My boyfriend got the chicken and rib combo as it comes. I was able to taste the ribs and they were good, fall off the bone with good flavor to them.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: I can't speak for the bar or music, but this is NOT a place to go for lunch. Super slow and terrible food. My "Chicken Philly" was made with lunch meat and burnt to a crisp on one side. My friends had a burnt boca burger (clearly nothing special about their veggie burger) and a dripping club wrap (dripping with what we weren't sure since it was also made with lunch meat). Their only redeeming quality was the fries - those were good (and they were an up-charge). I got half price for my half burnt sandwich.... I guess that's fair. :-/ Just don't go for lunch.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
The beer selection is awesome. 
The management oversight is weak. Tonight they ran out of pizza at 7 pm. It is Friday night. 
Last nights silverware was delivers with the previous patrons left overs. 
Did I mention the beer selection was awesome?

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Fun place 2 for 1 beer special's included the craft beer selections ...Crowd was a blast ...Nice crowd for a Thursday night, very friendly staff!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I LOVE this place!! My dad and I work in the same office building downtown and this is our usual Friday lunch spot. I usually get the club sandwich with fries and let me tell you...those fries are hands down the best ever. Crispy and seasoned on the outside, and soft on the inside. yum! Will have to go back in the evening to say how the bar is but it is always busy! 5 star service every time and some of the best food downtown...GO!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I LOVE SAUCER. They have SO many beers. And I'm the kind of person who hates beer, but the beertenders and beer goddesses were super attentive and helpful. Also really prompt service. The place has a young vibe after 7PM, and I love it!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
May of 2012 I surprised my boyfriend with a trip to Nashville for his birthday because he LOVES him some country music. I swore I would never revert to country but with all those love stories and twang beats I am fan now too. 

Lucky for me when I booked our tickets we had Carrie Underwood, Brad Paisley and Scotty Mcreary singing that evening. The bench seating was perfect and the sound was amazing. I didn't feel like I was in a huge concert venue. 

I went the extra mile and bought the VIP backstage passes. If I can remember I think the cost was around 75-100 each. 

Good Points
-You get backstage and learn about all the country stars who have been there and see the dressing rooms. 
-We had the honor of meeting Carrie Underwood and Scott Mcreary ( 1 minute but I took it) 
-You get to go onstage during the opening of the music and see what the stars see. 
-They only sell each concert 10 VIP tickets so it's more personable and not overcrowded. 

Bad Points
-No CAMERAS ALLOWED in the dressing room hang out area. So when I met Carrie underwood ( Yes we snuck away from the group and walked to where Carrie was and got a photo w/ her) Needless to say we got yelled at by our tour guide NOT for sneaking away but for using our camera. My issue with that is I just payed you almost 200 dollars to walk back stage for 45 minutes and you aren't going to let me take a picture with an awesome country singer who was happy to take the photo w/ us? Crazy.. That's the only reason why I didn't add on the final 5 star rating. 

-We could not find the tour guide!!! We went to check in at the ticket booth and NOONE knew where to send us. Finally after 15 minutes ( which meant our tour ended in 30 min) we walked to the gift shop and had to have a nice guy call on the walkie talkie to see where the tour people were. 

Other than that if you love country you MUST visit this place. It's a great memory we will keep forever. You can tell for every country singer on that stage it is a true honor to them to be invited and a dream come true.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: We needed lunch so we found this on yelp. It was a little hard to find as it is down an alley. Lunch was so so. I have a shell fish allergy seems the kitchen that day couldn't promise no contamination with fries etc. so I had the bean sausage soup. Crackers only no crusty bread for patrons. Soup was salty. My son had a hamburger and fries. I had sweet tea that was tasty. So so food. The waitress looked like she had been there a long time slightly unstable but nice enough. Next time I will try another place. I think local office workers go there for lunch.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
We were staying at a near by hotel and decided to check out the Flying Saucer for our first official meal in Nashville on a Sunday afternoon. I love the relaxing environment and the extensive list of beer options. My friend and I shared an ordered of Loaded Rocket-Tots as well as Prosciutto and Arugula 12" pie. The tots were crazy delicious, it is a must try. The pizza were delicious as well and is enough for the both of us. 

This place is such a great find, we were glad we came here for food and beer.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I just ordered BB Kings for the first time today and oh my god this is such a good burger. I got it to go and the service was friendly and quick! Thanks guys :)

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text: Good food. Not my favorite crowd after hours.

name: Anthem
text: I have only been to Anthem to attend Yelp events but both times I have been I have enjoyed myself immensely.  The staff are incredible.  The drinks and unique and tasty and reasonably priced.  The bar bites are always yummy.  They have an excellent happy hour.  And this is one of the rare clubs in Nashville, so as the night gets on it gets rather dancey in here.  There's plenty of parking and lots of space to explore with friends.  I need to come here on a random weekend night to really experience this place but what I have seen so far has been really awesome and different for the Nashville landscape.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: Honestly-if you're coming to Nashville with any sort of group-so yourself a favor and rent one of these buses. Be a local Nashville Celebrity for a second. Don't short yourself thinking you don't like singing 90's out of an open air bus in the afternoon. You need it. You want it. Just do it.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Best ribs I love the location in Memphis tn
The one in Nashville charges to sit and eat 
The Memphis crowd is #hip

name: Back Alley Diner
text: SO GOOD! I love the authentic bbq & sweet tea at all of these little "hole-in-the-wall" places! It really is in the back alley of the shops along the mall so pay attention you might miss it, haha we did the first time we walked right by it! Had the sweet tea and some delicious burger with bbq sauce and onion straws... You could tell the burger patties were made by hand and all the food & sides were delicious!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: The food here is below average. Salad out of a bag I think with bottled salad dressing. Chicken fingers and fries dry as a bone. Yuck! If you're interested in beer only this is your place. But eat elsewhere.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Overall the restaurant was great from the moment we walked in the door. If you you enjoy a live band  and the blues this is the place to be.  I would like to thank you for having us Nashville!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Vast beer selection, but the poor service doesn't make up for what this restaurant/pub offers on the beer menu. We were in a group of seven, and everyone ordered the equivalent of deli sandwiches. The food took well over an hour to come out, and the entire order still didn't come out together. The worst part was that our server NEVER came by to check on us or offer an apology for the ridiculous delay. The quality of the food was terrible as well, but that was to be expected.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Stuffed burgers, craft beers, dog-friendly patio, What else do you need? A few things I can recommend. Better parking, locally sourced food items, more loyalty from a couple of employees. I have been really surprised that the restaurants on both sides have been packed but this place isn't. From what I gather it is probably from the days of yore when they were a not so successful tapas restaurant with a very similar name.

First I had the Hells Kitchen burger. First word that comes to mind is "DAMN!" It was just the right ratio of spicy to taste, lots of cheese and cooked perfectly. Topped off with the pretzel bun I would call it my best burger yet in Nashville.

Craft beer selection was good but not great. Selections from Czann's & Brooklyn brewery on draft made me happy. Would loved to have seen some local craft taps. 

The patio has been my go to spot due to being with friends that have dogs. They have dog bowls that they bring out with water for the four legged friends. 

Parking in this area won't get any better so be prepared to walk a ways. Although the burger was pretty fantastic the sides were just ok. As you will see from any of my reviews I love fresh fries.
