When you are taking the extra step to do truffle, garlic parmesan, and sweet potato fries I don't see why you wouldn't take the other half step to go fresh with these items. Fresh and local is always better. I would also love to try their burgers with locally sourced grass fed beef. 

Finally the staff... Patio staff has been EXCELLENT. They do have a bartender there though that was antagonizing and making fun of a musician that was playing the other night. As far as I'm concerned this is disrespectful to your boss who brought them in, to them as a customer, and any fans that the performer may have brought in. All of which are responsible for your paycheck. If you disagree you should never show it in front of customers. I also heard that this gentleman is rude to customers and couldn't believe it with how well I had been treated at this establishment.

To wrap this review up. Check this place out, sit on the patio and bring  your dog. You will make new friends and have a relaxing time.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Music is great and is the only reason I gave 4 stars instead of 3. The BBQ sliders tasted good, but they were lukewarm. The fries were bland and stale towards bottom of the pile. The service was ok. Overall, it's a great experience, but I would skip coming here for dinner. Just enjoy the music with a beer.

name: Anthem
text: Nashville needs a place like this, but Anthem does not hit the mark.  First of all, they opened the doors one hour after the advertised time.  We bought VIP tickets and were supposed to get VIP bathrooms, bar, and private viewing area.  They were not policing for non-VIPers in the area, so in addition to over-selling, there were people in the VIP area that didn't have VIP tickets.  It took over 20 minutes to get a drink at the bar, and worst of all, there was ONE bathroom in the entire area, for men and women.  So, after standing in line for 20 minutes for a drink, you could stand in line for another 20 minutes to use the bathroom.  Don't waste your money.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: One of the better clubs that I've been to in a while.  They have a happy hour on Saturdays until 7pm and don't charge a cover before 7pm.  They have two stages, four bars, and closed circuit TVs throughout.  The menu offers a wide range of southern style food, including ribs, white cheddar mac n cheese, and banana bread pudding.  Plus, the live entertainment not only entertains, but encourages dancing and crowd participation.  This spacious, smoke-free club offers a refreshing change from crowded, smelly bars typically found in downtown Nashville.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This a hidden gem. Great food and drinks for a great price. You can tell nothing is frozen. We bring everyone we know in here. The service is always great, no matter what the sign says ;)

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Decided to check out this place as a continuation of my brother and I's search for the best hamburger in Nashville. This is a really cool area near Vanderbilt (I had never been over here before) and most of the businesses are outfitted in what look like regular houses. I thought that was a pretty neat idea. There's lots of outdoor seating but we went on the nicest Saturday in February so we were forced to sit inside.

The inside of the place is pretty small, only maybe 15ish tables (two are pretty large). All of the tables are painted with different things. Ours was one of the larger ones that was painted as a record, but we saw one nearby that had a painted version of Kenny Rogers' face (I thought it was funny). Service was decent too, the guy we had (didn't get his name) was super nice and checked back multiple times throughout the meal.

I had the sliders, which were topped with bourbon onions, dijon mustard, and cheddar cheese on little pretzel buns. There was a little bit too much mustard for my liking, so that flavor kind of overpowered everything else and the bourbon onions should've had more... bourbon? Didn't really taste that. I had the side of truffle fries and the flavor in those was SO damn good. Very earthy and tasty, would definitely have those again in a hot second.

My brother had the Macho Burger (stuffed with buffalo chicken and blue cheese) which he thought had a pretty good zing to it. My boyfriend had the Belcourt Black Eye (stuffed with bacon and blue cheese) and also had good things to say. They had regular fries and coleslaw, respectively, and thought the sides were just decent. Overall, everything was pretty top notch.

This is a great place located in a really cute area. If you're going here, be prepared to walk because parking is the WORST. We had to walk probably 4-5 blocks to get there. Although, it's right by a park and it was the nicest day in a while so it seemed like everyone was out that day. There's metered parking (although all of them seemed to be expired... wasn't sure about that) along the street and free street parking if you walk. Overall, I really enjoyed my experience here and wouldn't hesitate to go back to try some of their other stuff!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Flying Saucer is the best bar in Nashville.  They have so many beers!  Every time I go, I try something new and exotic.  If you are into beer, this is a must visit in Nashville.

Living in Franklin, we have to make special trips to come down to FS.  Usually, it's before a Predators game or concert.  The food is pretty good.  It's a German heavy menu and you'll do well to stick the brats and kielbasa.  Both are really good.  Also, the soft pretzel appetizer is fantastic!

I started on their UFO club a few years ago.  You get a card and they have a system that keeps track of the beers that you drink.  Once you hit 200, then you get a plate on the wall of the restaurant.  I'm closing in on 100, but it will take me a while to complete the task.  Some folks have gone through the program nearly a dozen times.  Crazy.  

I love visiting this place for the variety of beers and the unique menu.  If you are doing something special in Nashville, park and eat here.  Then leave your car and go to your show or game.  The beer selection is awesome and the waitstaff is very helpful and friendly.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Really like the concept of Flying Saucer.  Join the UFO Club, get a swipe card that keeps track of your beer purchases.  Kind of a rewards program (max of three credited per 24 hour period), try 200 different beers and you get your very own plate posted up on the wall or ceiling.  Excellent selection of beers, probably 40+ on tap - all great choices.  We also had a pizza which was very tasty.  Great service!  Will have to keep going to Flying Saucers - wish they had one in Charleston SC!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I stopped in to try the buffalo wings while passing thru Nashville. They are definitely above average. I found them to be are very good--crispy and non-breaded--and come with celery sticks and dip. The ambiance is that of old tavern but without the smokey stench. I recommend the B.A.D. For the price, I give it 5 Stars.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Cheap, delicious food. Service was very good. Only real complaint was the A/C should have been a little colder, kinda stuffy in there.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Waited an hour past the start of the show for the doors to even open. Terrible time management and efficiency given there was no one around to manage the people. Everyone was annoyed by the time the doors opened. Not worth it.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
I do respect the niche that this place is trying to fill in Vanderbilt campus vicinity. That being said, the layout of the restaurant is really cluttered, and I have trouble really being able to relax in here. The burgers are definitely decent; however, I think they can stand to knock them all down by about $2. 

To their credit, they manage to find some hokie-but-fun musical talent to play in the evenings, and the beer offerings aren't bad. However, since you're the kind of person who takes time to read Yelp reviews, you can do better.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Delicious food. Great beer choices. Pretzels were awesome. Mustard is super spicy but worth it!!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Absolutely loved being here! It was everything we had hoped and more.  We were fortunate to see Dierks Bentley, Kacey Musgraves, Rick Skaggs, Daily & Vincent, Terri Clark and more. It was a great night of music at a great venue.

Seating was great, can't imagine a bad seat in the place.

Liked that cabs were lines up ready and waiting after the show made it easy to jump I'm and make it back to our hotel room.

name: Music City Tippler
text: Steak isn't supposed to taste like onions, but the ones here do. Probably the loudest restaurant I've been to in Nashville.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Wonderful experience. Performance was the best. Seating was nice. Staff friendly. Overall a great entertainment choice, I would recommend to anyone coming to the area.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: i was recently in Nashville for business and went to BB's for a light bite and to listen to tunes. what a change from the dives on Broadway. The beer was cold and the music hot! The BB King All Stars are absolutely incredible and it was nice to watch without having beer spilled on you or being pushed around. Great time!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Kinda divey but full of locals and no.loud music. Great beer and  burger. In fact, it's mostly a beer, burger, barfood joint that appears to be more of a bar.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: It's truly a hole-in-the-wall kind of place, but they've made it their draw! Drinks are unique and diverse. Food is tasty and affordable. I'll definitely be going again!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Visited Nashville mid-Summer to do the tourist thing and decided to go to dinner downtown at BB King's Blues Club. Reservations made the day before (thru Open Table) somehow got lost (the place was packed!) but the hostess seated my date and I soon after arrival anyway. A funky table on the side was upgraded to a table front and center of the band's stage along with a great waitress (I don't remember her name but she had multiple cool bracelet's on each arm!). 

Had a coupon from hotel for a free appetizer but basically you get $10 off of your meal. I ordered a cup of gumbo ya ya but a bowl came out instead... oh well, it was enough for two people so it worked out because it was free and delicious! The mixed drinks were "okay"... seemed as though they were a little watered down with the ice. The two bands were great they played songs (I never heard before to several that I had including a great Prince rendition) which everyone seemed to enjoy, several couples (including us) were on the large dance floor and the waiters/ waitresses that navigated around the dancers with food/drinks along with a few lone wolves provided the additional entertainment. 

The restaurant's location was great (2nd St) and it happened to be a few short blocks from the hotel-provided shuttle pick-up spot (5th St) so parking was not an issue. Would visit again, try some different drinks and would definitely start off with the gumbo ya ya!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Do not go in this bar they will take your money and beat you up and there is nothing you can do cause when the cops come they will lie about it.

name: Anthem
text: I've never been treated better at any club in town. The amenities, the shows and the decor are second to none when it comes to dance clubs.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
We recently went to Nashville for the first time for the Final Four championship.
Just had to go to the Grand Ole Opry. We went on Friday night and really enjoyed every minute of it. The show consisted of  the old and the new,  performers and music. A great variety. The acoustics were great and don't think there was a bad seat in the house. We got our moneys worth for sure. Every employee we encountered couldn't have been nicer. They were happy that we were there and we certainly felt welcome.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text:
I'm starting to realize that most of the bars in Nashville are slowly transitioning into a chill rooftop bar experience. I don't mind it because I prefer that over people bumping and grinding on each other. My friends and I came here on a Saturday night so of course we knew Broadway was going to be busy.

The bar consists of three floors which seems like the higher up you go, the more laid back it is. We managed to find a table and we got to hangout for a while without people constantly bumping into each other. There was live music playing which is a common thing in Nashville. The person performing was very entertaining and talked to the crowd which was a plus. 

The only downside is the drink prices. I know every bar is going to jack up the prices but I thought 6 dollars for a Coors light was a bit steep. At the time, I didn't care because I already had a strong buzz. Looking back now, if I was 100% sober, I probably would have passed up the drinks. 

I'm loving how Broadway is changing their bars up and Redneck Riviera is no exception. It's a nice place to go to if you're looking for a location where you and your friends can casually have a cold one.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I came to Nashville for a girl weekend for my birthday. We happened to stop by this restaurant. The brisket was very good and our waitress Alexandria was awesome. She was very informative, caring, helpful and I would hire her in a minute. The band was terrific. I highly recommend this place if you come to Nashville

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: I need to come here again once I have decided what song I can sing and not sound awful or make a fool out of myself. It's cray how talented people in Nashville are. I need to up my karaoke game for sure.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
The food was okay, I had the ribs , they were just okay. 

The cornbread was good.  The drinks were on the weak side .

name: Third Man Records
text:
very friendly and helpful service 
i felt like alice in wonderland
jack has created a beautiful place i enjoyed every minute i was there

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Are you a fan of blues music? Are you a fan of good BBQ? Are you a fan of alcoholic beverages? Then BB King's Blues Club is a perfect location for YOU! Service, excellent. Food, tasty but not anything special. Drinks, made RIGHT. Music..... hands down the BEST PART. We went on a random Wednesday night and got to see the legend, T.C.Coleman! Couldn't have been more excited to see this amazing band preform. I was on the edge of my seat during their opening set where every instrument got their own solo (even the bass guitar!). The worst part was the long intermissions the artists took, but it's hard to complain when they are playing from 7pm to 12am! We arrived for dinner around 5pm and did not have to pay cover since we ate there. Awesome experience if you're a lover of good music! Long live the king o' blues.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: The beer selection and ambience is pretty nice. The food was average but as another reviewer said about the tots appetizer, the egg totally turned me off. I can do a runny yolk but not runny whites. Be sure if you order this dish to specify the egg to be cooked more thorough-- I believe it would taste better and look more appealing! Overall, I will come back!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
If you like beer this is the place for you.  Their selection is amazing.  We spent most of our time looking at all of the plates on the ceiling which are awarded to people who drink 200 or moor beers at their various locations.  The food was decent.  We did their loaded tater tots for an app and then each had a sandwich after that.  The staff was friendly and very knowledgable about the beer selection.

Also, we did not partake but there is an entire section of couches, love seats, and picnic benches with wait staff service.  

Its just outside of the downtown area and walking distance from the Music City Center so its a great location if you're there for a conference.  Go.. drink.. enjoy.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text:
Oh Printer's Alley. You are home to those fantastic gritty, late night Nashville adventures and I love you for it. Ms. Kelli's is never my first stop.... I always somehow end up here and that's OK with me. 

Who doesn't love a musty basement smell, cheap jell-o shots, karaoke, and flashing lights? They have a dance floor in front of the stage and drink prices aren't bad. It's not my favorite place to karaoke, but it does the trick in a bind. 

However, the last time I went the karaoke guy forced us to get this really annoying app to sign up for karaoke (not sure what happened to just putting your name and song on a piece of paper). Not gonna lie, it was difficult to set up after a few drinks in, and our group gave up after a while. Why you gotta do that to us Ms. Kelli?? Otherwise, it's a fun time and not bad for what it is!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
This was an amazing experience. First time at GOPH and I was able to see one of my all time favorite country groups, Rascal Flatts.  Hunter Hayes and Shaw Brothers were there too. 
Had a wonderful time with my friend.....great night!!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: The name is spot on "Back Ally"  hard to spot.  Find it. Great food. Great prices.  Open mic was great. Katlyn, our server that evening was funny and super helpful.  The ace is a true find for sure.

name: Third Man Records
text: Fucking awesome. Great collection of records and random stuff to look at. The girls that were working were really sweet and gave my daughter a free puzzle. We bought records & a toddler hoodie. We got the chance to meet Jack the day before at his Walk of Fame thing and we love him and this store and Nashville. You must go here - it's worth the stop.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Try the grilled cheese burger it was great and very filling. Another cool place to go downtown close to printers alley.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: BB King god rest his soul would be EMBARRASSED to have his name on this place. Let's just leave it at that.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Cool little place to get good laughs and a few drinks.  Plan to have dinner somewhere else no food served here.  The DJ is cool and the karaoke list is really good almost all your favorites.  A little dance floor is in the front and adds to your fun.  Can get a little snug because of the people and little room for dancing.  Overall a good place to have a great time!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I'm so blessed to able to come and see this place so much history here. We went the day before coming here to the "Ryman Auditorium" which helps understand the whole history. We did the backstage tour also it was amazing to here all about that takes place in getting it all ready for a performance. We actually start from the beginning of how the guests begins his walk through the facility. So step by step we did the same walk through as if we're the guest. It was cool feeling and you appreciate it every time you see them on stage. Definitely recommend going through the backstage tour and later that evening go for the performance. There about 7 performance that night. We enjoyed every moment..

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Christmas Eve, not that crowded.  But our server seemed over worked!
We ordered our dinner and it took FOREVER to get our food.  One of my party got the pulled pork plate - do they not serve bread with this?  It was also like warm.
They tried to deliver calamari to us - we did not order that.  They delivered fried fish and shrimp to us - we did not order that either!  Took another 10 minutes to finally get our ribs and chicken platter - 3 bones?!  That's it?!  And they were burnt too.  The chicken was good but a very small piece.  
We were going to get dessert but decided not to after all that.
Did they offer to comp or anything?  No.  our server was snippy too.  
Will not be coming back here.

name: Third Man Records
text:
To the two beautiful ladies working the place, the day before Jack's Lazaretto album came out: thank you very kindly. You two were fiddlin' with the record booth for a long time (I was waiting my turn a while, up until past closing) and you both handled that and Jack's guests with so much grace. I don't recall your names, but you with the pretty eye-shadow and beautiful diction- keep talking, singing, writing, whatever you're preferred communication: you share beauty and wonder and it's a delight to the ears. And to the other wonderful woman (with the dazzling stockings and warm-golden heart): you curated an amazing evening for me by recommending bingo night at the Stone Fox. Me oh my this California boy had a wondrous time talking with the hipster knitters and fun-time bingo players! It was my only night in Nashville and I can't imagine a better impression of your fine city than the one you two left for me.
Oh and this: next time you're shooting the breeze with Jack who I heard was saddened by something: just remind him that Fate may be what our brains are hard-wired  to look for in patterns and all that, but it doesn't change the truth that it was designed in the first place by that holy King of Rock 'n Roll, our good God. Hope he sees that, and maybe writes a song about it.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Pretty cool experience to see a show at the Grand Ole Opry while visiting Nashville! This is coming from someone who is not really a county fan but does appreciate all types of music. I went to the show not even knowing any of the artists and really did enjoy myself. The auditorium is beautiful but does have bleacher style seating just FYI. Country fan or not, it's pretty cool to be in a place where so many legends have been and a definite must experience place when in Nashville!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Absolutely TERRIBLE service from the front of house.  What is the point of offering reservations if you can't keep them, and then telling people who walk in with a party of 13 that they have to wait for 45 minutes and that you couldn't care less.  I have never been treated so poorly.  High prices, gimmicky atmosphere, and horrible customer service?  I don't think so!  We happily spent our money at the Brazilian steakhouse a couple doors down where they have great food and even better service.  I will never set foot in a BB King's establishment and will tell as many people as possible about my experience.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Love the blues!!!!! Love B.B. Kings!!!!!! Memphis New Orleans and Nashville!!!! The live music is amazing and true!!!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This is a great little hidden place we stumbled upon. The service and food were awesome, it had a great atmosphere and the prices were quite reasonable as well. Highly recommend it and I'll be sure to return.

name: Third Man Records
text:
I love this place! The theme of the facility design is a exciting play on your visual sensory and every detail looks like it was intently picked out to leave the passerby intrigued or bewildered. I recently got to take a private tour (courtesy of Yelp during its 2014 Spring Break event in Nashville, TN) of the entire facility beyond the lovely shop. During the tour I got to check out everything from beautiful metallic crown moldings, eclectic artworks, furnace elevator, wall mounted animals, vinyl records with liquid inside, and some many other unique sights.  

The facility has an analog/straight to vinyl recording studio that had a huge view of the Blue Room (aka the multi-purpose music venue where live shows are recorded on site), a dark room for developing pictures, outdoor patio area, massive indoor merchandise/record shipping area that literally has a quirky road-side motel theme, a hospital themed company lounge/break area, and some amazing business offices (including the mysterious Jack White's office door). 

I was a little disappointed that the vinyl recording booth was out the facility for repairs prior to the Jack White and Neil Young appearance on Jimmy Fallon's Show. Despite my dreams of cutting a cheesy record on the go to mail to my parents, I could not complain after finding out about that type of awesome happening. Overall, the tour and visit to the shop was amazing. I plan to come to show at the TMR venue and visit the shop the next time I get a chance!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: 5:00 on a Friday in January couldn't be a better time to eat here, walked right in.  Great food, great music

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: No complaints about anything. Everyone wad nice, food was good and made quick and a large variety of beer

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
The cost was $24 a person. A little pricy, but traveling from California.. Probably never will come back so we paid it. 

The tour itself is enjoyable. You get to see backstage and learn a lot of new Information. Our tour guide was great. She was funny and made the experience that much better. 

If you're in the area I recommend spending the $24. It's about a 45 minute walking tour.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We arrived to a practically full house but scored a table in front.  Trey, our server was awesome, the music too!  Not too loud but totally danceable and FUN!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: This place overall was great. There was live music on Saturday when we went to have dinner so we had to pay a $10 cover even though we were dining there. Although the live music was great I was shocked we had to pay a cover while we were eating dinner. The food was much better than we expected, but the service was not so great. We waited about 15 minutes before our waiter came over to offer us drinks, thank goodness we got drinks at the bar while we waited for our table. And to order dinner and pay our Bill was a struggle getting our waiters attention. Be aware that on a Saturday night for two people the wait was on hour. We had a gift card that was printed online from a family friend before our move to Nashville and it seemed like non on the staff knew how to redeem it. Overall the music and the food made for a good experience but I'm not in a hurry to come back.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
My impression before stopping by here was that it would be a kind of dark, cramped beer bar.  Boy was I wrong.

A beer bar, yes indeed.  A phenomenally well presented and organized beer list the likes of which I have rarely seen elsewhere.  But so much more.

Located just behind the Frist and Union Station, Flying Saucer is a rather large, very comfortable bar I'd be at a heck of a lot if I were a Nashvillan.  Comfortable couches and chairs on one side, traditional tables & high tops on the other.  Great, cheap beer and food everywhere.  Plus a separate room for live music and pool.  Just a great chill spot.  Best pretzels I've ever had, too.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text:
While in staying in Nashville we were searching for a place to hang out and have some reasonably priced drinks during the day. I checked yelp and found this place was right across the street from our hotel. How can you go wrong with a place that has Happy Hour every day from 11-7?! 

We managed to rack up quite the bar tab, but for the amount we ate and drank, it was more than worth it. We will definitely visit them next time we're in town.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I stopped in with two friends to have a beer or two and listen to some live music. The place was empty except the bar area which was about 50% full. We went to sit at a table and were told we could only sit at a table in the bar area if we were eating. Really?  The dinning rom areas were completely empty and half the tables in the bar area were empty. Needless to say we only had one drink, left and won't be back. Very stupid seating policy.  People are more likely to stay if they can sit at a table and talk instead of all facing away from each other while sliding off a bar stool. Very bad management on this one.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Very cool spot with tons of beer choices. Draft, cans, bottles, nitro... We're pretty picky about our beer and we both found something new we enjoyed, including a kelp and sea salt gose! The food was good but not the star of the show. We had a yummy cheese fries appetizer, the Pork Banh Mi and Marcellus Wallace (cheesesteak). Both were good, but again, not the reason we'll come back... but we will come back! The patio was gorgeous and the bar area was loud and fun on a Friday night.

name: Third Man Records
text:
Third Man Records produces, records, and presses some of todays and yesterdays  best albums, unfortunately their customer service and shipping times do not have the same quality. I am disappointed and frustrated with not getting orders on time, especially when you are forced to pay two day shipping charges and it takes them weeks to get your order in the mail. I understand it is still a small company and shipping firm but the site offers limited products and most of those products are housed in one location, it shouldn't be to hard to bundle two LP's together and ship them. The real issue that gets me is after waiting a week and half after placing on order there is still no shipping conformation, which prompted an e-mail to see whats going on with the order. After another twenty-four hours there is no return e-mail informing me about the status, so this then prompts a phone call. After a short chat with Third Mans sales rep it is told that the company is extremely backed up and there is nothing they can do about it. This unfortunately is not a reasonable solution. So instead of giving the record company the money they rightfully deserve  it is now going to Amazon, who has already shipped the albums the day I purchased them and instant digit copies for instant enjoyment. The icing on the cake is when I call Third Man back to inform them that I want to cancel the order they say that can be done, but when I start asking about the refund procedure they hang up the phone while I am mid sentence, thats what I call customer service. All I know is if I call the job done half way through, I would not have a job. So Third Man Record keep putting out the music its great, but get a new shipping department and watch your customer service people, because if you call the company ext.3 watch out for the person on the other end. 

No Thanks, MV

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Such a cool little spot.  Awesome vibe, great beer selection, great bar staff and live music all the time.   Keep it up Belcourt crew! You guys are awesome!

name: Third Man Records
text: So....I'm embarrassed. I thought Third Man Records was a record store. Oops. It's a record label with a cool record shop attached. So...it didn't have the record I wanted, but I learned a lot about Third Man Records and their artists and had a fun time exploring the shop. So I'm an idiot (to be fair I'm new to Nashville), but you learn something new every day!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Great  Beer Joint, excellent grub.

Beer selection is amazing over 85 drafts, plus hundreds of bottles.   

Great staff and service.

Food was really solid had a great Banh MI sandwich.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I'm giving the tour 3 stars only because at the end, the photographer who hands out the picture that was taken on the stage circle was a bit cranky when a couple didn't buy the photo. He threw the photo on the table and then passive-aggressively announces that he guessed that they didn't like the photo. The photo cashier was in a mood too.. Whenever she gave the credit card bill for my husband to sign, she just grunted and flicked her fingers to the cup of pens indicating that he can grab one to sign the bill. I mean honestly, it was so nice to experience the typical southern hospitality in Nashville all weekend --until we visited the Opry, which was a huge surprise. 
The tour guide was nice and friendly, though the tour seemed very rushed. I think the people at the end of the tour need to be retrained or sent elsewhere, behind the scenes.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This is a great family friendly show. Came for my birthday and was a great gift. 28 July Comedy was hilarious.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great place for lunch. No cover charge until the evening hours so go in and get out of the summer heat!  Good eats but a bit pricey for bar food. Had I stayed in town for the night I would have been back to feel the place with a bad but onward I must ride, ride, ride.  Definitely worth going to though. Good atmosphere.

name: Third Man Records
text: Horrible service, do no use their film lab. It's a rip-off. Over charged and still didn't get every thing I paid for, plus it took them an extremely long time to get my pictures back. Never going back!

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
Good burgers, nice staff, chill atmosphere. They play country music on the stereo. They have a bar and four local beers on tap.
It seems to be mostly non-tourist.
One last thing: it really is in an alley which is pretty empty, but it's not hidden, they do have a sign on the building.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: If you haven't been to BB Kings before, it is probably going to be exactly what you expect. Large, noisy and crowded. We went on a Friday night in May in Nashville. The place was very busy but we were able to get a table without too much of a wait. My date had the brisket and really loved it. She said it was done exactly right and the sides were all perfect. I had the porkchops and I must say I was disappointed. They were saying and overcooked. I realize that can happen in a busy restaurant and it did this time. The live music was great and we had a really good time. The servers were very attentive but don't plan on having a lot of conversation in this  noisy restaurant.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great music. Great Brisket but it took 1 hour &10 minutes to get our meal after we ordered. A heads up from the bartender would have been great. Probably will not done there again but the music was good

name: Back Alley Diner
text: We should have known better - B. A. D.  says it all. Bad food. Cheap, but bad. To start, they were out of at least four items on the menu. The cook carried a trash can into the kitchen by the rim, then went about cooking without washing his hands. Then the cook left before he cooked all our food. Yes, just left. Maybe that was a good thing. One of us got under-cooked chicken. The broccoli and cheese soup was pasty, and where was the broccoli?  The catfish was bland. The menu was misleading. The onion straws were all fried crust but no onion. Spend the extra $5 and go to a restaurant you'll actually enjoy.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I had a tour of backstage because I wasn't able to get to a show while I was there. The tour was awesome! Our guide was funny and very knowledgeable. We got to see everything backstage like the artists do-- it was great! I learned a lot about the history of the place & about country music.

Only downside and why it's not 5 stars is because of the price. They tell you to buy tickets online to reserve a spot because tours are crowded, so instead of being $18 it was over $20 for a ticket and the day I went the place wasn't crowded at all. Even $18 is kind of expensive for an hour tour, when we couldn't even see every dressing room, only about 5, and that is what they're known for.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: decided to go here before an event at TPAC - had a heck of a time finding it, definitely BACK ALLEY!  food was quite good if nothing special, just a true diner.  drinks were good and very reasonable.  the ambiance is great and the service spot on with very friendly wait staff.  would definitely head back here when in Nashville and don't want to deal with the crowds in other spots

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I was so excited to try this place- great reviews, cool location, and fair pricing. The atmosphere is excellent- very inviting. I would love to say that I had a great experience, but it was the exact opposite. Forty minutes after ordering a cheeseburger and a salad, I inquired about their whereabouts. Our waitress came back and said they moved our ticket up and were STARTING on it. Seriously disappointed in the fact that it took an hour to get our food when there wasn't even a wait to be seated. After watching several more orders come out, hoping they were ours, and watching the tables all slowly clear out, our patience had reached its last. Then arrived our food- cold burger and limp fries. No more B.A.D. Food for us.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: My family was passing through on a cross country road trip and we happened to stop by. My son is 7 years old and he is not a fan of loud music, but he enjoyed the live band that was playing. He even almost danced!! He food was amazing, my wife thoroughly enjoyed herself and the creamy greens were to die for! Brandon was our waiter and he was soooooo amazing! He helped us have the best experience and our family loves him so much we had to let his manager know that he's got a star on his hands! The Mac and cheese was hyped up and I tried it...I thought it was bland. But my substitute of creamy greens was amazing! Please try the brisket, it's delicious!

name: Third Man Records
text: This place is a must do stop. This is Jack White's Studio and record store. There is the coolest antique recording booth that Neil Young and Jack White stood in and recorded an album together and they sell it there in the shop. We loved it and bought some albums and cool tee shirts. Parking is tough around there but we got lucky and parked right in front. Loved our time there!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Karaoke dive bar...that about sums it up.  Cheap drinks and loud singing.  I went with a large group on a Saturday night.  Maybe we were a little early for the crowd or it was an off night for Ms. Kelli's, because we were about the only folks there (we left around midnight).  Everyone had a great time!

name: Third Man Records
text: I love Jack White, and all his projects. When I walked in with my wallet in-hand, I tried to not buy everything but it's so hard to resist. There's Jack White merch to White Stripes memorabilia to various concert posters, and Third Man shirts. Oh..I can tell you it's worth the paycheck! I walked in and was transported into a world of Jack White. I'm still trying to collect the whole White Stripes anthology. (All I need left is De Stijl, Get Behind Me Satan, and Icky Thump) This place definitely has magic stored inside it, and I am definitely revisiting back in the near future (as if I haven't visited already 3(00) times)

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Went for a concert so did not get there early enough to take the tour but just being at such an iconic place is one check off the bucket list. :)

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Well disguised as an outbuilding behind the Union Station Hotel and next to the Frist Museum, the Flying Saucer pub is what you are looking for. Whether you want a comfortable place to chill, drink beer or have a solid meal or snack, this place delivers with good food, great beer selection and tons of personality and ambience. 
We enjoyed 2 huge and delicious piping hot pretzels with ample cheese and mustard dipping sauce, enough for 4 people to share through at least 2 rounds. The burgers are large and the fries are light and crispy. 
While the place is a serious pub and caters to grown-ups, we came on a Sunday afternoon and found many families with kids enjoying the place as well.
Whether you want a place to unwind after work or want to get away from doing the tourist thing on Broadway, the Flying Saucer is a very satisfying stop.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Two songwriter nights a week- fantastic stuff! I'm a huge fan. Beer selection is much better than your average bar. Good amount of tv's. Bartenders are great. Prices reasonable. Checks all the boxes for me. Although I could do without the Browns on Sunday :)

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: Very friendly staff! We came early to ride the Honky Tonk Express and waited in the air conditioning. The manager was happy to let us wait inside and even answered some questions about the Honky Tonk, even though they contract out that service and he wasn't sure of the answers. The band sang customized songs to our bachelorette using her and her fiancé's names and our hometown (Chicago!) to personalize the lyrics! Highly recommend for any bachelorettes out there looking for memorable snapchat stories and videos. No idea how the drinks are since we didn't stay long, but the service was impeccable!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
My absolute favorite place to go for a live music show. Even better than Broadway for me. 

The Opry is small enough that you can feel the presence of the artists on stage. The performances span generations, with performances by a variety of musicians. The acoustics are wonderful. And you never really know what to expect until you experience that show.

If you go to Nashville, you must go to the Opry.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Probably one of the best places to see in Nashville! What an amazing experience! All the history in this place takes your breath away if you are a true country fan! The knowledge of the tour guides is endless. And the videos are amazing. I'm still in awe.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
Came here for dinner after a long night of walking around trying to find somewhere that didn't have an hour wait to be seated. The Wednesday night deal was buy 1 get one draft free! So we were pretty stoked about that. 

Live music for the majority of the evening which is always a treat. Our server, Paige, was really friendly and accommodating with our large group of people. 

As far as food goes, it's the standard southern comfort food: burgers, shrimp po' boy, catfish sandwich, pulled pork sandwich, etc. Everything was decent quality and I don't think anyone really had any complaints about their meal. 

One thing I I unfortunately would not recommend are their signature drinks. For the first two rounds of drinks we stuck with the beer deal and margaritas. Then we got bold and tried out really cutely named pop-star themed drinks. Literally tasted like straight alcohol with no good flavor which was really a let down. Stick with the beer and margaritas !

name: Music City Tippler
text:
Upon entering Music City Tippler in Nashville's Midtown, I thought to myself, this place, contrary to many of the very Country bars on Nashville's Broadway, could do well in NYC. Well, go figure, it's actually sisters to NYC's very own Tippler that I reviewed months ago. So, it was no surprise that I liked the place. 

You can notice similar aesthetics in the decor, the bar, and the cocktails. Country music not particularly your thing? No problem, because you won't hear much, or any, of that here. Playing hip-hop, top 40, and some club bangers, the vibe here takes you outside of Nashville, but keeps you around all the sweetness and politeness. Ideal, right?

To drink, I had their Del Rio (Vida Mezcal, St. Germain, lemon, maple, The Bitter End BBQ Bitters). Mezcal never really seems to disappoint me, and certainly didn't in this drink either. You definitely get the smokiness, which is pushed further with the BBQ bitters, but then a nice sweetness from the elderflower and maple.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I loved the Grand Ole Opry House.  I am not country fan perse.  There is certain country acts i like and ones I don't.  But the Grand Ole Opry House is something everyone should see for historical value and pure entertainment.  We have been twice in our life and truly enjoyed it.  If you go to Nashville this is a "MUST SEE"

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
God awful place. The food is complete trash and that is sampling four plates and one appetizer. 

Terrible service and a Long Island ice tea that looked like a weak apple juice.   

The tables are so close together your elbows practically touch your neighbor and they sit four to a table sized comfortably for one so you end up semi holding your plate sitting at an angle to your table while music that no one would call jazz or blues assaults your eardrums in a small club that apparently needs the same volume level as the local amphitheater 

Believe this one; ignore the idiots ranking this place four stars.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Came in before our movie at Belcourt. Service was great, she was very friendly & recommended items. Food came out quick & was great! Beers were tasty & enjoyed the live music on writers night.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Mrs Kelli's is so fun and a great atmosphere. It's always a good time with karaoke and drinks!!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The food is actually pretty solid BBQ and it's perhaps the coolest music venue outside the Opry itself in Nashville.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great service! Our waitress took our order and brought out our food right away. It was definitely the busiest night if the week. ND vs LSU bowl game evening and she still killed it!! AMAZING! Ask for Kaley, she's the best waitress at the place.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We took an amazing tour of the grand ole open and had a wonderful tour guide. It was informative, interesting and we had a great time. It was husbands 2nd visit in the lady couple weeks. He visited there while on business and brought me today to celebrate our birthdays. We're staying in Memphis but it was worth the 3 hour drive.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Really cool spot w/a great selection of beer! Kind of regretted trying to make it dinner as the menu is pretty limited and basic, but it keeps you from heading elsewhere! Speaking of heads, the bartender seemed like he was suffering from a head injury because he couldn't remember basic things but was friendly. We were only in town for 3 nights but came back a second time!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Love this place. I can't wait to go back. This was my first time. 

There is a medal detector when you enter, so leave all those items at home. 

Check out the gift shop first before it gets busy. There are things you can buy here that you can't buy at Opryland. Take pictures soon as you arrive in front of the cutouts before the line gets long and it gets dark. 

All seats are assigned so there is no rush to go in. I'm not saying be late, but you don't have to shove your way to the front of the line. 

If I recall correctly you can bring both food and drink to your seat. Check out the popcorn stand. They had lots of good food trucks, but we opted to eat before we arrived, not knowing the lines and options.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Came here last night with a group. We didn't do it this time but I would recommend taking the tour because you really get to see some interesting things inside and hear some great stories. We happened to see Charlie Daniels last night. He's 81 years old. I must say he put on an incredible show! His age has not slowed him down a bit! This is a must go if you're in town.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text:
From
Out of town and wanted a hole in the wall bar! Beers cheap:cold, atmosphere awesome, great band! Kelsey bartender was great and the others too! Definitely will come when we come back into town! Cheers

name: Third Man Records
text: Great idea and I'm sure Nashville is proud to house it... Shop is very small, high potential for ANNOYING; kids, families, and amateurs playing the two available guitars.  I no longer care about vinyl, my BOORISH ears are fine with mp4.  Tshirts are over priced.

name: Third Man Records
text: Pretty cool place. Really small store but packed full of cool old timey gadgets and vinyl, music memorabilia etc..to buy. worth a visit if you're in the area.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
I'm giving Back Alley Diner 5 stars because I have never had anything but the best experience. This past Saturday a group of friends and I (there were 15 of us total) ate there before the Nashville Art Crawl (we've been doing this regularly for the last year).

Saturdays are a great day to go because they have $.50 wings and $2 PBRs (a fantastic combo if you ask me). I get the buffalo ones and my husband gets the tabasco ones which are somewhat hotter (you can also get them plain without wing sauce) and they come with either ranch or blue cheese dressing. I LOVE these wings. Seriously, I think they're the best! Every other wing I've tried in the past year is compared to these and so far, none have been better.

I really can't speak much for their other food because I love their wings so much, I haven't been tempted to try anything else. Except a few months ago, I did try the pulled pork quesadilla and it was very good.

The service is exceptional. We always have the same waitress (it's a shame I can't remember her name) and she's very attentive and accommodating for us (big groups can sometimes be a challenge).

It's a simple, casual place with good food and great prices. I'd definitely recommend B.A.D.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
If you're a country music fan visiting Nashville, checking out the Grand Ole Opry is a must. During the winter, all Opry shows are held at the Ryman Auditorium, but the Grand Ole Opry tour is still available! 

The tour is about an hour and starts with an informational video about the history of the Opry (featuring Blake Shelton)! I really enjoyed the tour and our guide did a good job of covering a lot without losing our attention. We got to see the star's dressing rooms, mail room, and we even got to stand on the stage! It's $18 to take the daytime tour, and I felt like we got our money's worth.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Fabulous time at a divey bar that allows smoking inside! Polite and attentive staff with a fun party atmosphere to boot! The karaoke hosts were nice, helpful, and fun to talk to (unlike some places I have been). My only complaint was the lack of PBR in cans, but that seems to be a standard here. Thanks for a good time.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: The bar is fine, nice and attentive bartenders, modestly priced.  But you come here for karoke and that part is a total mess.  Karaoke attendant is indifferent at best and so never gets the crowd to engage, enjoy or support each other.  A robot would have more charm.  The sound (particularly when you are at the Mic) is terrible.  Overall, not a fun karaoke spot but good place for a quick beer and shot on Printers Alley.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Don't order food. It takes an hour to come out and only 10 patrons in the bar area. The staff is very unorganized. We came on a game day. TN vs Vandy and the bar is 4 minutes from the stadium. There was only 1 staff member and should have been multiple on a such a large day like today. I've been here once before on a non busy night and it was still extremely below average.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: First time ever in Nashville and we wanted to hear some Blues music but we were apparently too early on a Saturday (5 p.m.) in January because the place was pretty slow.  Tried the ribs with beans and cole slaw and they were delicious but not finger-licking delicious.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Nice and Quiet...... Got the Special Burger , one of best burgers I have tasted ! Cooked perfectly, moist and bun made it all come together! 
Just a good solid burger ! You won't be disappointed.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I know nothing about country music. Nothing. If you told me Patsy Cline sang a song called "I Cried In My Beer 'Cause I Miss You My Dear" I would totally believe you. So it is with this complete lack of knowledge that brought me to the Grand Ole Opry House.

And it. Was. Awesome.

We weren't able to score tickets to the evening show, but my friend and I were able to take the behind-the-scenes tour they offered. (Tip: Use promo code AAA w/ your AAA card and you get a few bucks off)

The tour began with a brief video on the Opry and its roots at the Ryman theater (downtown). We were then ushered past the celebrity entrance, the dressing rooms, the historic studio (where Hee Haw was filmed!), and finally on to the stage. Standing on the circle where so many historical people have performed was amazing, even if I didn't fully realize the magnitude of how many artists have taken that stage. Our guide was so cute and sweet - her bubbliness really made the tour fun for me. 

If you're in Nashville, I recommend this tour! It's only about $20 and you really do see a lot. 

Two thumbs up!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Excuse me while I fly to Nashville for my date with Garth ! 

When a dear friend and frequent travel buddy of mine asked me if I wanted to go to Nashville I quickly looked on the internet to see which iconic musicians might be playing in town.  Since it was months away from the travel dates there were nothing advertised yet.  I checked every month until I saw Garth Brooks headlining at the Grand Ole Opry the week we would be in town. YEESSS! Quickly tried to get tickets for the date we were arriving.  Unsuccessful.  Sold out already?!! Well there is a late show...so, with not many seats left, I was able to secure two seats at the very top of heaven.  Hope we can stay awake after traveling 3 time zones and a few planes.   Best I could get.  What I didnt know was...

There really isnt a bad seat in the house!  The Grand Ole Opry House is now home to the thoroughly entertaining Grand Ole Opry, a live show with multiple acts, played like a radio program.  Comedian, Emcee/Radio Announcer, of course lotsa country music to entertain.  The Grand Ole Opry actually started at the Ryman Auditorium decades prior.  When the show outgrew the Ryman it then moved into this home.   The Opry House is located on the property shared with the Opryland Mills Mall, and right behind the grand Gaylord Opryland Hotel.  So thankful the hotel has a shuttle to the concert  as, even after driving past it three times earlier in the day was still not seeing the Opry House!  The acoustics are great.  The seats, while on hardwood benches, provide great viewing.  During the winter the Grand Ole Opry moves back to the Ryman for the season.

And as it turned out the late show worked out the best.  The entertainers were already warmed up.  There was no rush to get out and make way for another concert.  Even Garth Brooks said he was having such a good time with the lively late crowd.   And as he came back for his 5th or 6th encore it became apparent the Grand Ole Opry was the very best place to be.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
After having such a wonderful experience at the New Orleans BBKings we came upon the Nashville one and decided to go have a drink and listen to the band that was playing.
The Hostess asked us if we were dining, we told her No, we had just eaten but we're going to have drinks only.She said $5 cover and you can only sit in the bar.We paid and happily walked in.
After seating ourselves at a low four top, this angry gal comes over to us with a totally pissed of demeanor and says we CANT sit here.We asked why? she said this is dining reservations only.We explained the hostess told us that we could.
She (the Angry one) did not try to re-seat us and basically kicked us out saying "you cant sit here"She was never nice and she just didnt care and offered not to move us.
  We went back to the hostess and told her we were kicked out and wanted our money back.She said give me a minute let me get the manager to refund you your money.The manager comes to refund us and it's the same gal that kicked us out! Again not friendly, and acting bothered, she asks us if we are the ones who want a refund! Well Duh!! You kicked us out. SMH
At this point we were both blown away ..such a far cry from the New Orleans BBKings.
I told the gal they could learn a few things about customer service from their New Orleans club meanwhile my husband had enough and nicely stated they needed to work on their communication skills and attitude .She promptly shouted back at us with an attitude.
Anyway, its of my humble opinion this person is not management or hospitality material. We are huge followers of BBKing and blues in general, so to say the least we were extremely disappointed to be leaving..We didn't get the gals name but she has a blone afro.
 Just know, if you are told you can sit in the bar, what that really means is you can only sit At the Bar. At which there was no room or we would have.
It''s our First day of our music and food vacation Nashville.Their loss is someone elses gain onward and upward! Lots of venus around town to explore..

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I didn't think I'd love it this much since I'm not even a country music fan. It was terrific and so entertaining! It's not just listening to live music, but also you get to enjoy square dancing, yodeling, comedy, and trivial questions for free prizes. I laughed a lot, and was in awe of the wonderful performances.

We arrived about an hour before the first show not knowing what to expect. They had many places there to get a quick bite to eat even before entering the building. There was a Yee-Haw Brewery truck as well as other diner type food trucks. There's even a shopping mall across the street with lots of food options. Go early and just walk around. It's actually a very relaxing walk and entry through security. You also might want to get your cocktails before the show. I say that because a rum or whiskey drink will cost you $22. I was in shock. That's more than stadium prices. I mean really! The drinks were good with plenty of alcohol but not worth the sticker price.

The show was amazing! It was a mix of old and new country singers. Some famous ones like Trace Adkins, Jon Conlee, and Hunter Hayes. There was a young girl from Canada who sang her heart out during her first Opry stage debut. Madison Kozak got a standing 'O' for her performance. She had the voice of an angel. The Riders in the Sky comedy group were so entertaining. I loved them! This particular show was broadcast live on radio channel 650 AM and on SiriusXM. It was such a cool experience.

Our seats were front and center on the mezzanine level. I'd get these same seats all over again. Everyone was so friendly (staff and patrons). The Opry brings together people from all over the world. I can see why country music is popular now. Don't hesitate to get a ticket to a show while you're in town. You won't regret it. It was worth every penny and it was the highlight of our trip. A must when in Nashville.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Dogs allowed outside. Looks big on the inside. Drink slushees with different and interesting flavors.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
A must see when in Nashville!!!!
We bought a Grayline bus tour package that included a back stage pass at the Opry House. It was fantastic!!! We spent 90 minutes or more with a guide seeing what it looks like behind the scenes.  We got to look inside the dressing rooms to the stars of country music. The hallways were lined with beautiful pictures of country singers and performers young and old. The Opry House has a tradition and rich history in country music that we were not aware of and we soaked it all in. The tour ended with a picture taken by their photographer that you can purchase as you leave. Would highly recommend.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The customer service at the bar is stellar! I visited this BB King's location twice in one week and wasn't disappointed either time. The first visit, I ordered the hot chicken which I guess is a staple of Nashville. The second time I visited the restaurant was over crowded due to performances. I was allowed in at the bar to make another order. I'm thankful for the service.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great band! We were very impressed with the music. The food was fine, loaded tater tots, how can you go wrong? The rest of the food was ok, lettuce wraps not much chicken, meatloaf was fine. It is loud, part of the experience, but just keep that in mind.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This place was nothing short of amazing. You get a free photo with a guitar in the spot on stage. Where many great legends played music. I was so impressed  you will learn and see so much .I have no complaints at all.

name: Third Man Records
text: One thing I had to do on my trip was going to Third Man.  Third Man is pumping out great releases on vinyl.  Loved strolling through the shop.  Had a lot of cool things besides records.  Must go if you're a music fan.  Definitely,​​ if you're a Jack White fan.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
I was lucky enough to be staying next door at the Union Station Hotel, so this allowed me to indulge in a few or three or more beers...LOL

The theme of flying saucers is unique and there are saucers hung all over the walls.  If you are a regular - you should join the Flying Saucer Club! 

The beer selection on draft and in bottles was vast and covered anything you could've wanted:  Lagers, Stouts; IPA's, Sours, Pilsners and German style beers.  I started with a flight and the continued to dive into a few other choices during my dinner.  

The food options were great too as were good too!  Burgers; Sandwiches; Potato Salad and Fries.

Our server was knowledgeable and friendly.  

If I lived in Nashville, I would be a regular for sure!  If you are in town- swing by and enjoy this cool place!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Super nice people and an amazing patio area. Perfect little dive bar. Beautiful atmosphere and also awesome music

name: Ole Red
text:
Poor service from host through lunch. 
We had a large group (13) so they made us split up. They refused to even seat us near each other even though there were enough empty tables to put both groups next to each other. We were all seated by 2:50. Not even during a lunch rush. The party of 6 had menus when they sat down and had their drink order take right away and good order fairly quickly. The party of seven had no menus  for over 20 minutes and only after we asked 3x. No one took our drink order until after we had been seated for 30 minutes and I spoke to an employee standing by the doorway to the elevator.  We did not actually order our food or our first beverages until 3:25.  My first beverage was made incorrectly. Our waiter said he knew that but did nothing to correct the issue. 

A trainer came over to inform us our server was in training and today was his last day of training so he was trying to go solo. She told US we needed to give him a hard time for the errors. I told her that is not our place. She needed to address it and she may want to give him more support in training. 

Food finally came around 4:00. The party of 5 was completely done eating. So we're the smaller parties they say at the two empty tables near us. Most things came out correctly except for the smoked chicken. Two of us ordered 1/2 orders. Both orders came out full. The manager eventually reduced our food bill (not including any drinks) by 50%.  We finally got our bill about 4:35. But our waiter did not fix what he charged for the chicken so we still paid more than we should have.  

We finally got out of there about 2:45. Almost 2 hours after being seated. We did package up our leftovers and shared with Nashville's homeless. Saw a lot of need along Broadway. 

All in all, not the experience I expected and not a place I would suggest to others without a lot of warning about what could happen.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Food was good and the service was also good. Margaritas were definitely out of this world!! Didn't have a long wait either.

name: 12th & Porter
text:
Things have changed here. Especially since the brains behind their establishment quit last year. They had a girl there that did all their booking, organizing - basically she ran the ship. She left and things went downhill quickly. 

The bottom line - there are bigger and better venues that have moved into Nashville. This place will also be a well known because they have been around for years. But if I were an artist, dj or anyone looking to book an event, this place wouldn't be on my radar.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Cool beach vibe. Lot's of margarita choices. Items on their menu can be made Gluten Free which is a plus. Staff was very friendly, food arrived quickly and was very good. The live music was great.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Nashville makes other cities look second rate. The Bridgestone is so awesome and the location plenty of parking decks within walking distance and right on broadway means it is close to plenty of great restaurants. Love the atmosphere downtown and the arena is clean and plenty of friendly staff.

name: Ole Red
text: This is for "The Lookout" which should be called the Watchout. IT IS NOT OLE RED. We made a reservation but didn't realize The Lookout was not part of Ole Red. We were whisked through Ole Red which looked fun and had a great menu. The Lookout is like a lame hotel bar and does NOT play country music. Our server was wonderful but she had to shoo people away from our table when we arrived. People who continued to stand behind us the entire time and blocked our view. AWKWARD. The food was overpriced and not good. The wine was warm. The table was dirty. The view was okay, I watched people at the bar across the street having fun and wished I was there instead. The worst part? The stench of rotten trash blowing up from the street to the table. Is this a "thing" in Nashville or were the garbage collectors on strike? Every dumpster was overflowing. I became nauseous from it and we had to leave. So sad that this was how we had to spend our last night in Nashville, we were having a great time until this.

name: Ole Red
text: This review is about The Lookout which is the top floor of Ole Red. It has a different menu. When you get tired of bar food or just want a superb meal, this is the place to go. We are seafood lovers and this was some of the best we have ever eaten including at the gulf. They have a raw bar and you pay by the item. We ordered two Alaskan King Crab Legs, a dozen raw oysters, a dozen boiled shrimp.  We also got their special huge pretzel with great warm queso dip, which was very good . The seafood was amazing ...  Most of the reviews on here are for the main floor food. Don't stop there. Go to the roof top. We can't wait to go back. Delicious! We were a group of four and had plenty of food. View was also great.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Ok, I'm not a huge fan of beer, but my husband really wanted to try this place and now we are both hooked! 

Trying the Basil Ryeman and when in season Walk the Lime are both musts! I am obsessed with the Basil Ryeman and it is definitely my go to beer there! 

I wish they would open a store in Murfreesboro where we live! I believe they have started serving a small array of food, but they always have Moose Head Kettle Corn and try it or you'll be sorry you missed out. They pair so well with the beer!

It's an awesome place to chill out. They have a lot of room inside as well as outside. They typically have some kind of live music and there is a dart room in the back. 

Reasonably priced and the staff is very knowledgeable as well as friendly.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We had a great time on Broadway, the music strip in Nashville, and enjoyed a great dinner at Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville. My wife had the chicken Caesars salad, but my son and I enjoyed the steak teriyaki. It was phenomenal. Best of all is e service. They just did enough not to be annoying, but helpful. And they have a guy on stilts who makes complex balloon designs for the kids. A MadHatter top hat with a fish. never severe that great. We enjoyed the dinner and also enjoyed the live music. The restaurant is on the best entertainment strip in Nashville. Loved every minute of it. Average pricing made it even more enjoyable.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: We've been frequenting this place pretty much since they've opened up. At first we thought it was just another standard brewery but over the last year they have really upped their game. We love the food and brews here lately and plan to frequent much more often.

name: Ole Red
text:
Amazing food and staff here...I went here a few days ago while on vacation and man i want to go back!!! It was so good!!! 

If you don't know what to get share the red neck nachos with the table and the bucket of champagne chicken oh my wows you'll be in a food coma for sure but they are so good

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Came to grab some dinner and had such a great experience with Chris! We ended up in the middle of the dinner rush on top of the Music City bowl and he handled all of his tables like a true professional. Great food, great drinks, excellent service!

name: Ole Red
text: We wandered into this venue and were treated to a very enjoyable lunch. Food was great and not run of the mill. Service good. Music good.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: I like this venue in so much as I like the bands they book. Parking is terrible. There is no security inside the venue. I and several friends have experienced being basically assaulted during concerts here on the floor, and not because of moshing. Would love for this venue to have floaters on the floor taking care of belligerent fans. Also, the sound kind of sucks. But, you get a great view of the performer.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Came here last night for blue grass night. The beers were two for one, not including flights. The beer was delicious. We ordered food too. The burger was just ok in my opinion. I didn't love the sauces they had on it. The fries were very thin and delicious. The atmosphere is great!  Nice outside patio that is dog friendly. Will be back!!!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Just have to give kudos to our waiter, Chris McKenna.  Went above and beyond in service, and made our visit the best meal on our vacation this entire week.  The restaurant was great too.  Ask for Chris McKenna to be your waiter.  You will NOT be disappointed.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Venue: Margaritaville

Decor:   Nice

Service:   Pretty good, Friendly

Environment:   Pretty size restaurant

Food:   Lot of options:  American, Seafood

Prices:   Not too bad

Debbie Downers:   This location, the beverages are slightly higher than the chains in the south and Caribbean islands

Conclusion: All in all, Margaritaville is an excellent option to hang out on the town.  Lots of people, plenty of seating, place gets jammed pack.  Unique house beverages, good food and service.  Definitely a good chain to have right on Broadway in the heart of it all.

Overall: B

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Worst service I have ever had at a bar and the most disgusting bathroom I've ever been in and I'm a plumber.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: The beer - I had the sweet potato stout - was pretty solid. I'd definitely drink again. The music was enjoyable, folksy, not overbearing, pleasant. Tight seating indoors,  but ample outdoors. Food was...okay. had the sweet potato poutine, grilled cheese and BBQ nachos. Poutine was the best, but wasn't actually poutine at all. Grilled cheese was decent, but not very cheesy. The BBQ nachos were disappointing...loaded with cream and sprouts, with only a hint of BBQ flavor.

name: Ole Red
text: Let me start off by saying we are Not big drinkers so a night out for us consist of two  to three drinks and we start to feel a good buzz. So it's our first time to Nashville we head straight to Broadway on Saturday night. Want to get a good buzz going and enjoy the atmosphere and town. . The place is beautiful, very modern. Sat in the second level bar had the Buckshot and 2 jack and cokes to follow.  All I have to say is SUPER weak drinks!! Paid about $75 and felt Like we drank water!!!

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Ive been here two times and had two different experiences. The first was on an early Sunday afternoon. It was great! It was not crowded, had cheaper beer, and an outdoor patio with plenty of seating. The last time was during a Saturday night. It wasnt so good. It was very crowded and people were hostile. I was shoved and pushed the whole time. Some people seemed hateful and irritated. There was a fight that broke out also that I nearly ended up being in the center of accidentally.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Come for the beer, stay for the food!!!! This is a must do on any Nashville visit. The beer is what originally made me want to visit the brewery. As a home brewer and what my wife calls "a beer snob" the beer was the main attraction. It did not disappoint. There are flavors and a variety of beers for everyone. Two that stood out were the Basil Ryeman and the Country Roots. What I did not expect was the unbelievable food. It was hands down the best burger I had ever had. The brewery is a short Uber ride from the Broadway bar scene and you need to visit. The staff are more than helpful with service and recommendations.

name: Ole Red
text: Hate to complain, but the food just wasn't good. Nobody in my family enjoyed it. The music was great, and the service was average. Could've gotten better food at McDonald's to be completely honest.

name: National Underground
text: Tried medium spicy chicken and burned my tongue so badly that I wanted to cry. And I love spicy food. They brought me a second serving of non spicy when I asked though which was ok. Beware when eating chicken even if advertised as medium....it's not.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Whenever Sue and I are traveling, one thing we love to do is check out local beer.  It really gives you a sense of a place if they have a local beer scene.  I don't know why.  It just does.

This was the only official brewery we were able to get to on this trip.  We did drink a few other local beers while in Nashville, but Tennesse Brew Works was the only place we were able to go to and it did not disappoint.

First off, the day we were here was beautiful.  It was in the 60's and that made it the perfect spot to sit outside on their deck and relax with a beer in hand.

The place was rather crowded.  There is a beer bus in Nashville that takes you around to breweries and I believe we arrived just as a bus dropped off a group here.  After a few minutes we were able to get to the bar and order a few beers.  I had the Southern Wit (a Belgian style white), Sue had the Natchez (an American Pale Ale with rosemary).  With beers on our person we made our way upstairs and to a table outside on the deck.

After a few minutes a few people joined us at our table and we struck up a conversation with them.  Very friendly atmosphere here.  A few of the other tables had some games going (Jenga and such) and it was just very laid back as you would expect from the south.

Look for this place.  It is a bit off the beaten path in the Gulch, but worth the stop.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I love this place, we had suite tickets which included free food and drink.  The food was absolutely amazing, but I did have to knock this rating down to 4 stars because I found a very long piece of hair in my salad.  Otherwise, the food was over the top good.  The chicken was moist and had an awesome flavor.  

They had tons of deserts, unlimited popcorn, beer and wine.  If you are going to go see a hockey game, this is the way to do it!

name: The Night Owl
text: Great music, food and all around vibe.  I play music there on the regular.  As far as that goes it's a treat.  Very comfortable room, not too big, not too small.  Great spot to go hear local talent, which in Nashville is world class talent.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Definitely a tourist trap but worth a stop in. 
Margarita's are ok. I have had better. Landshark beer is their staple as well. 
I didn't have any food. 
They had live music going at noonish which was cool. 
Of course better options for traditional Nashville feel all over Broadway.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Place was a bit of a dive, but the artist was good. Disappointed in the beer selection and it was all bottles. Bartender was very nice and charged my cell phone for me when she heard me say my battery was low.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Just went to our first hockey game here, and found the arena just OK. Frankly, having seen Nashville Airport , the Country Music Hall of Fame, and so many other sites around the city, I found this arena surprisingly lacking in upscale amenities.  We were in the upper bowl...this one was very steep and cramped...there was little room on the landing, seats were very narrow, and the rows were very closely spaced. The seats themselves were comfortable, but the stupid cup holders were too small to hold anything (at least they could not hold the reg size soda or bottled water we bought)...who designed this?? The men's room near us was also very small and cramped...it had three urinals, three sinks (no mirrors), and one entrance/exit.  As a result...LONG lines. Finally, and I can't honestly say I remember too well, but I can't recall seeing ANY auxiliary scoreboards/displays other than the large central one. Please correct me if I'm wrong, but I don't remember seeing a single out of town score?

Most importantly (for me at least), the food was expensive and completely nondescript...we could have been anywhere in the country. The only local nod was some BBQ nachos, and these were only available at a few scattered locations. Otherwise, you could get PLAIN burgers, hot dogs, fries, nachos. No dressed up anything! SO BORING! As expected, it was also pretty bad. 

The game experience itself wasn't anything special either...what was memorable was what had to be the worst introduction/rev up to face-off I have ever seen at a pro game. After warm ups, the teams clear the ice, the lights dim, and the announcer cranks up the music. You then watch a montage on screen for  ten minutes while they send the Zambonis out to resurface the ice. Then they lower a giant Preds head, crank the music again...and you watch another montage. Then the cheerleaders come on and slide by while the music is still cranked. Finally, the players from both teams kind of infiltrate the ice while the announcer plays the player introduction montage (but the starters are already on the ice so it's not like they spotlight them). At this point, your ears are bleeding since they ironically (you are in Music City after all) don't understand the meaning of crescendo and everything has been at "11" for twenty minutes. 

It is hard to say anything about the game atmosphere and fans since the Avs put three on the board in the first period alone. However, even though they announced that the game was a sellout, there were many empty seats at face off, and it never really got loud, even when it was still a game. The announcer definitely could have done a better job psyching up the fans...as it was, it seemed he just preferred to play the usual rock anthem snippets and unending crowd cam shots. I do have to say the usher in our section was very nice and polite, however.

Can't say anything about the parking, as we stayed at the Renaissance and walked. The Hilton did seem like it would be more convenient, however.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: My favorite brewery in Nashville by far! Beers are delicious, workers are so kind and helpful, and that chicken sandwich is the BEST I HAVE EVER HAD. Such a cool atmosphere, if I lived in Nashville I think i'd come every week!
