name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Finished the night at Layla's after visiting several overly packed bars with so/so music. We are not 21 anymore, and do not have what it takes to push through the traffic! I wish we had went to Layla's to begin with. Jeremy made our night! He is so much fun to be around!!! The band was awesome too! Wish I had gotten the name! Good prices, good music, great atmosphere, amazing service! If I am back in Nashville, I will be here!!!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I drove from ATL to Music City for 2012 Grammy Nominations concert   I parked on a street not far from the Arena.  The area was empty but as I walked closer to the Arena there were many police officers.  Entering the arena was very easy, there was a large group of concert attendees but the line moved smoothly.  I got lost in the Arena and walking past my section all I saw were large black curtains blocking the entrances to the aisles. There were two women sitting at a table and they asked me if I needed assistance. I gave them my ticket and one said that due to last minute stage changes, they were going to give me seats that were closer to the stage. This may have been done because the show was being televised live however I still was happy that I was closer to the main floor without paying floor seat prices. It looked as though if I were to sit in other sections of Bridgestone I would have a pretty good view of the stage.  I have to say that everyone I encountered at Bridgestone was nice and helpful.  Leaving the Arena the police officers directed traffic and ensured that the large crowds leaving the Arena crossed the street safely. I do agree with some other reviews that the sound at the Arena could be perfected but I had fun.  I hoped to return this year but the Nominations Concert returned to LA.  If the organizers decided to have it again in Nashville I would go.  The Arena is also a good option when you want to see a concert at Philips but the good seats go fast!  Check out the ticket options for Bridgestone!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Great venue location! I visited Nashville for NewYears and saw a show at Bridgestone.  From a music perspective it had great acoustics and more than ample room to handle a ton of rowdy electronic music fans!  All of the venue employees were accommodating and friendly.  Beer was expensive but what do you expect at an arena?

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Music was great. Didn't know what to expect walking in, but such a hidden gem amongst the big name hot spots!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: You remember right after 9/11 when TSA made everything really slow at the airport?  You appreciated the effort to secure your flight/trip and therefore,  obliged to the inconvenience?  Well,  tonight felt like that.  Except it's 2015. We bought Frontseat tickets for a show.  Arrived earlier than the opener.  Waited in a massive line (?).  Didn't mind the delay for the metal detector.  You know,  safety and all.  But after all that wait for a pre-purchased ticket,  we had to wait 45 minutes to get a drink.  There were 2 bartenders for a 50 ft bar packed 4 ppl deep. Ridiculous.  The show was Amy Schumer.  She would be disappointed with the wait for a drink.  So was I.  I can handle overpriced at a show.  But  waiting 45-an hr for a $12 beer for an expensive show is too much.  I'll select a different venue next time

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: This is a very laid back establishment, but almost to laid back. There is two different parts to this bar: Winners and Losers. Winners is set up for those who are wanting to eat, and relax (yes, you can get beer on this side too however, it is more geared towards eating) Losers is more of a full bar atmosphere where you can order shots and get a little rowdy! Unfortunately, for us, there was not much to see. Perhaps it is because we arrived on a Saturday around 4pm so the venue was rather boring as we were the only ones in there. The best part about this bar is it is not on the strip, near Broadway, so the prices are more reasonable. I think I paid $16 for a bucket of Millet Lite bottles? All I know is it was less than $20! The bartenders are very friendly and easy to talk to... I will admit it is nice to be able to talk to friends and the workers without having to repeat myself or scream at the top of my lungs to get a beer or even just say Hello. Very relaxing atmosphere, and if I am back in Nashville, I will have to go during a time that I am hungry and ready for some action. Come to think of it, there was not a band playing perhaps that is why it seemed so quite? I do realize it was rather early to be out, but when in Nashville on a Saturday, and day drinking I expected a little more to be happening than two empty quite bars.

name: Ole Red
text:
Popped in to check it out and listen to some good music. The singers/band we heard were excellent (Chad Bearden and Casee Allen), and interacted with the crowd well. The bartender, Cass, made our visit even more enjoyable. She was attentive, efficient, and offered fun conversation in between helping other guests. She didn't mind us, the visitors from Delaware, bending her ear a little. It appeared patrons as well as other staff enjoy her jovial personality. 

We liked the layout of Ole Red. Nice and comfortable. Great sound system, and the aroma of leather filled the air.

name: Ole Red
text: Great place to spend the afternoon w drinks, food and lots of Nashville fun!! Love this restaurant!!

name: Ole Red
text:
Our visit was mid-week and in the afternoon. There was no wait for a table, and the live music was in full swing. Our waitress, Nira, was amazing. The energy in the place is great, and the food turned out to be amazing. 

Drinks are expensive ($12 for an average sized mixed drink), but delicious. My first time ever eating fried pickles, they kind of blew my mind. They come with 2 sauces. A white one, which is more spicy, and a red one, which is more sweet. 

Each of our entrees were delicious. The bucket of chicken is a great deal. The half order would be nearly enough to feed 2 people. I also spotted their nacho plates, and they are ENORMOUS. You will need 4 people to finish one of those. 

Oh by the way, Blake Shelton came in. Overall this was a 5 star experience with absolutely 0 to complain about.

name: Marathon Music Works
text:
1) Empty, cave-like acoustics.
2) Rude/pushy staff. 
3) Restroom "attendants". 
4) Overpriced food. 
5) Far from ideal setup for a music venue.

MMW is basically a huge, open factory floor. All of the amenities are situated against the walls of this giant empty room. The stage and the fans end up being in the approximate middle of this room, between four steel pillars. Inside those four pillars, there is barely passable sound reinforcement quality. If the crowd is large enough to crowd outside of those four pillars, those outside of that square area will experience sound quality that is atrocious.

The rules and policies of this venue are apparently to treat all patrons like unruly criminals. It's almost as though the management is implementing unwarranted sports arena/stadium policies and attitudes among it's staff. 

I have attended one show here and will NEVER attend another at this venue. My experience was of a fairly innocuous nature, but was generally unpleasant, and certainly not enjoyable. Many of my friends have attended other shows at MMW and had even worse experiences. DONT GO HERE!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: they had a YEAR...read that again...A YEAR notice that we would be arriving with a large group (80+) with multiple confirmations prior to our arrival. Yet upon our arrival, at the prescribed time, we were told the room was not ready and we would need to wait....A YEAR, then there were not enough seats as we had requested...the poor bartender had to bus tables (which was great for the people waiting in line for a drink) the food was beyond sub par! The chicken was dry and like shoe leather.  This was the low-light of our trip to Nashville! Avoid this place like you would avoid the plague!  Terrible!

name: Ole Red
text: Dinner tonight- after a bit of a wait we were seated. Server wasn't as attentive since we didn't order alcohol as the table behind us did. Food was good - Hot Chicken was properly hot, pickles good. Hubs burger was good too but the tots were slightly disappointing.  Good music made up for the shortfalls!

name: National Underground
text: I've never been treated so badly in my life. We ordered a sandwich with bacon and French toast. the sandwich came with no bacon and we told the waiter and after waiting 30 mins for the bacon,  we ate it without the bacon.  The French toast never came,  even after an hour that we were waiting there...  When the check came, it was charging me for the French toast and the additional $2 for the bacon we never ate and waited forever for.  When I asked the waiter to take these two items off my check since they never came,  he laughed at my face and said it was only $10 (and that I was being ridiculous for asking for this...) it wasn't only this,  I can't even put it in writing how awfully disrespected I felt.

name: Ole Red
text: We were looking for a quick meal after the Country Music Hall of Fame and before the Grand Ole Opry. We weren't expecting much but were pleasantly surprised. We had the half order of the Champagne of Chicken (can get hot or not). A half order is a half  chicken so consists of 4 pieces. Two of us split a half order. It comes with biscuits and gravy.  We ordered one side which was huge and shared among 4 people. We got the "not hot" chicken and we all agreed it was the best fried chicken we had ever had. The live music was awesome but was very loud so don't plan on having a conversation.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Great place to watch concerts!!! Parking is easy and you're right on Broadway! What more can you ask for right??

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I walked in on Valentine's Day around 8PM, and it  was we pretty empty .  I was surprised that maybe 8 people in the back dining section and the hostess said it would be a quick service.  I ordered a salad and burger.  I waited over an hour to get my food.  I was so hungry.  Little did I know that it would take an hour and 45 minutes to eat here.  I would not return, especially if I was in a hurry.  I would have left after 30 minutes after ordering, but I didn't want to be rude.  Very disappointed!

name: Marathon Music Works
text:
Awesome piece of space on Clinton Street.
Enough parking for everyone, lots of other shops nearby to wander into.

Went to a concert here one night and had no trouble parking, getting into the venue, ordering a drink, getting a seat, watching the show, getting close to the performer.
The sound was awesome, (as long as you're not right up in front of a speaker), and it's non-smoking!  Big + in my book.

Getting tickets was easy. They have a box office open during lunch hour all week long.  You can either order your tickets online or head over to the box office and save yourself a few bucks.

I'd like to see some more bigger names in there. 
I appreciate small venues with larger than life performers..
And I also appreciate the fact that they have seating for those willing to pay a little more, rather than standing and watching the whole concert.

Two bars, good variety of shows, plenty of parking, good sound system, good lighting...
non smoking.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The staff is friendly, and the music is decent. The food was edible, but not worth the price. A vegetarian salad with little more than lettuce was $15. My mom had a cheeseburger and thought it was okay. The margarita was fantastic though! People beside us ordered nachos and it looked like the kitchen used a full bag of tortilla chips, so the portion quantity is definitely not small.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text:
My husband and I took a short trip to Nashville after Christmas in December 2018.  This was our first stop when we arrived in Nashville.  We had no idea where we were going or what we were doing.  Looked like a dive so we happened upon it.  It was the afternoon so it was pretty dead.  We sat at the bar and had the best bartender Elaine!  She gave us lots of tips on places to go and things to do.  So friendly and lots of great drink specials!  They had vodka Capri suns!  Mmmmmmm!!!  We asked tons of questions and spotted some celebrities!!  This was a great local spot and glad we happened upon it at the start of our vacation!!!

We did the Thursday night whiskey jam as well.  So much fun!  We saw a ton of great bands and very cool atmosphere.  Well worth checking out!!

name: Ole Red
text: Really liked this place.  Liked the decor and loved the tractor that is hanging from the ceiling upside down.  The two guys that were on stage were really good.  Sang a good variety of songs and different artists.  They didn't have to compete with the other places on Broadway.  Most of the other places on Broadway have open air bars and the music flows out into the street.  It can be a bit much as they seem to be competing with each other and just becomes noise.  I had the Cherry Limeade. Delicious!!!  Husband ordered the Champagne of Fried Chicken and I had the pulled pork sandwich.  The fried chicken comes with biscuits and gravy.  So good! True southern biscuits and gravy.   Lots of fries chicken and it was really good too.  Pulled pork sandwich was good too.  Came with coleslaw and I chose a side of tator tots as my side.  They were different - ok.  Lots of people recommend them in other reviews.  Debra was our server and she was great!   I would go back and explore more on the menu.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
My first stop in Nashville. Took a scooter there from the hotel. They have a great beer selection and the folks are ready to discuss what goes into the beers which I very much appreciate. The people are awesome! Friendly as can be. After some beers I asked for the food menu and as always asked the bartender what was good. He suggested the cheese burger and said it had won awards. I almost expect that everwhere I go but I decided to trust him and give it a try. The burger was awesome! Amazing flavor and cooked perfectly. The shoestring fries crisp and yummy

If you are in Nashville and want a good beer and burger look no further

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Fun place for someone not from here! No cover and average service!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Tennessee Brew Works has a very cool atmosphere for any beer drinkers! A combination of indoor and outdoor seating and multiple bars make this a neat place. I was underwhelmed by their beers but they have a large enough selection that you can find one you like. Go for the beer but you'll probably enjoy the atmosphere more!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Our server Whitney was awesome.  Very attentive and friendly even though it was very busy.

name: Ole Red
text: Good location for people on vacation looking for entertainment with a meal.  Non-stop live music.  I only had a burger that was just ok so I can't speak for the rest of the food on the menu.  Not a  good place for conversation as the music was constant and very loud.  The service was very good.

name: 12th & Porter
text: The place is nice, food is good. But I'd rather put my nuts in a rat trap than go back and deal with security and how it was ran through out the night.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Had dinner at JWB Grill on Friday night and thoroughly enjoyed the food, ambiance and service. Our server, Jessy, was wonderful, and went out of her way to make it an elevated dining experience. Highly recommend checking this place out.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I suppose the food options are more varied than the bars on the strip but only if you arrive early enough to try them.  We arrived late so the only things available were burgers.  We arrived minutes after the time and they would not budge.  In fact, we watched as they served other customers their full meals and we were only offered burgers.  We would have stuck around, but the drinks we ordered took forever and were very weak.  Not impressed.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I would probably go back again if the skinny male bartender covered in tats wasn't such a dick to my friend and I.

name: Ole Red
text: Great food, large stage with excellent music. Wait staff very fast and attentive. A must stop when in town.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: This place is awesome! I have been to many arenas and we went to go see the Predators play while we were in town. While huge, it is organized and there is always someone there to ask if you need help. It is clean and bright which I really liked. Inside the arena, seats are comfortable, while still you can tell they pack in as many people as you can. Sounds was great! We only got sodas and some fries but lines moved quickly and not over priced for "over priced" event food. After the game getting out was a breeze!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Excellent service and great food! They have live dancing lessons and great live music! Order the French fries! You get a combo of 3 types! The fried pickles were very good!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I stopped by here for lunch on a Monday afternoon. The place wasn't too busy and I managed to find a seat at the bar quickly. I loved that there was a duo singing and playing guitar, they were very talented and were taking requests of all sorts from patrons. I ordered a Yazoo pale ale by recommendation from the male bartender and it was very very good, light flavor and very smooth. I then ordered a pulled pork sandwich with fries from the female bartender near by, she was a little standoffish and only checked on me maybe twice while I was there. Other than that, the experience was well worth it while listening to great live music. The food was pretty average, though. I'd definitely come back to grab a beer and see another set of musicians onstage.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Soulshine was found by accident when looking for food Saturday night but was so so good!  I had the gluten free Godfather and it was delicious!  Add a side a ranch and it's so good  plus there was live music which is so Nashville and I loved it!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
We had a large bachelor party stop by for some beers and pizza. The service was the best I've had in a long time. To be able to keep 20 drunk males going with only one server is always impressive. She went above and beyond to help us. 

Kitchen sink pizza was good! Great wings too!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Too big to be fun.  This place was a little too polished for my taste.  I had fun but definitely prefer smaller places with better music.  Oh, and did I mention that it's owned by the Gaylord??

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Partied here with a friend two weeks ago(will upload pics later) and it was pretty decent. This was my first time going since living here in Nashville. Drinks were ok, food wasnt too bad, but good Lord it was CROWDED! Atmosphere was fun and people were pretty cool. SIDE NOTE: 1.  Not a place to get dressed up for. It was hot as hell and comfort is very advisable. 2. GET THERE MUTHA EFFIN EARLY....and I do mean that literally if you want a decent seat or to find a park anywhere in the area.  We went  about 6:45pm and it was shoulder to shoulder.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
1- line dancing instructor was super hot- what a butt!
2- live music by some unknown who was nice enough to take pictures with us tourist types
3- pretty great food
4-free line dancing lessons with a hot guy
5- creepy horses by the bathrooms for photo ops
6- un-manned gift shop
7. three levels of awesome
8- only one level was open when I was there because of private parties
9- what more could you want than horses on the ceiling?
10- If I lived in Nashville I'd be here all the time.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: The pizza was amazing, and Leah (the bartender and server) was incredibly friendly and attentive throughout the evening. Some of the best pizza and service I've had in a long time!

name: CMA Fest
text:
Well......

I avoided the steep parking charges by riding my bike to the festival and locking it up right in front of where the cops patrol parking.....   So, I saved about $65.

I got a seat (you use the same seat every night of the festival) near the exit gate so coming and going was a breeze.  Same level.
The seats in LP field are made of steel...
So when the temperature is at 95 degrees with 200% humidity, you stick..... superglued would be the better word..
And you sit next to the same people every night...
The person sitting next to me overflowed into my seat, every night...
so when you have hot sweaty flesh sticking to you from the person next to you .....    it's a wonder I didn't throw up.

I did it once.....
It was good enough for me.
Now, I sit in my front yard in my beach chair and listen to the concert.
Sound travels nicely, along the river!!!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good bbq ribs! I love the outdoor seating!!!!!!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Funky little place with pretty good pizza and a lively atmosphere. We dined here in July of 2016 before heading to Titan's stadium for the Guns and Roses concert. They had live music starting as we were leaving. Big outdoor dining area upstairs. Neat little place.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Not very impressed with them. Server was nice enough but I had to seek him out to pay our bill in which I ended up giving the money to a bartender or we would've been late for our Ryman show. The menus didn't have prices for drinks either. They were $9 each before a tip. The drinks we had were a Lynchburg Lemonade and Peach vodka drink. They were good but served in a plastic cup half the size of a real cup. Granted I realize they were paying for entertainment and we didn't pay a cover to get in, but the bands had been switching over at the time so we didn't even get to hear any music. Oh and they had a bathroom attendant who gets a tip along with the server.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Loved the atmosphere! Food was alright. Had the turkey blt. I have had better. The BBQ pulled pork nachos were awesome! Great southern taste if you are looking for something different

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: My husband and I came into Nashville for one night. Decided on the Wildhorse Saloon as I remembered hearing that it was good food and a good atmosphere. The atmosphere was good, the band that was playing was really good. Then we got to the food. The fried pickles that the had and the  locally brewed beer was the only thing that I enjoyed. I order brisket and pork, figuring I could have some good barbeque while in the south. Food came and the brisket and pork were very greasy and tasteless. The fried potatoes were over cooked and inedible.  Plus on top of all this we waited like 40 min even receive our food. Out waitress was pleasant though not very attentive. All in all I was not please. If you just want some good entertainment and have some drinks you'll be fine. Just will never recommend eating there again

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
I've not seen an actual play at TPAC but the set-up looks like it is a great venue for that and there are few if any bad seats in the house.
My wife and I recently saw a rock concert here and for the type of show that it was--theatrical, engaging but not in need of huge audience participation movement (dancing, moshing, etc.)--this was a solid venue. We were near the front and had a great view but I could see that those behind us and up in the balcony likely all had a solid view. 
Valet parking here is not too pricey ($25) considering you'd spend that or more in most of the parking garages in the area on a typical evening and this way you don't have to trek through one in the middle of the night.
Concessions looked okay but pricey (though not more than say Bridgestone). For a rock show this place was a bit disorganized--we lined up in several separate lines only to find out that none were ours (a general purpose ticket-holding line is what we needed, seemed like it'd be the easiest to find). Performance time listed on the tickets was actually the time they planned to open the doors to the theater room and it wasn't until that point that we were even told which line to get in.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Good margaritas but they should be for $14.  Wings are terrible but the ribs were fantastic.  Go for the line dancing and atmosphere.   Food is mediocre at best but this place is a Nashville landmark.  Have fun - "ya'all."  ;)

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The food was not that great.  I'd rather go to another eatery known to the locals, Peg Leg Porker, Jack's, etc...the bartenders here were ungrateful and looked agitated taking your order.  The music was not great- more fun at another bar without a cover (even just to eat).  This has clearly become a Nashville go to...begrudgingly.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
We wet here on a Sunday afternoon, it was rainy out and Broadway was pretty quiet.  

We sat in the back where the band was playing, they were pretty good and they kept us entertained.

I got the pulled chicken sandwich and it was very good.  I like the fact that it is served without bbq sauce on it (you add your choice when it comes to the table).  

The food was good, service and location were all great.  The reason for the 4 star is because they sell RC cola products, yuck!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: So awesome! Didn't get a chance to try the food but the ambiance was awesome. Great for a very chill night.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Roger is the stereotypical d-bag bouncer. They cancelled line dancing multiple times, and as a tour leader that effs my game plan. If you're going to be a dick, Roger, and ask us to come back in an hour to linedance, don't be upset with us when we come back and you've cancelled again. I'm sure it wasn't your decision, but your overly aggressive bullshit is just gonna send us elsewhere. #fireroger

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
A TEN! A TEN! A FREAKIN TEN!!!!

Came to TPAC on June 21 to attend the Martini and Marionettes show. The show itself was in the Andrew Johnson Theater, on a lower level. When we got there, the crowd was buzzing around the food table and standing in a long line for drinks from the cash bar. 

The off thing to note was that there were no Martinis to be found. Liquor drinks, Yes. Martini, no. They were announcing before the show that it was OK to bring in your food and drink to teh show. Then once you sat down an automated message came on saying no food and drink. I lol'd. 

The show:  WOW!!!  That was an awesome show!!!! Phillip Huber was able to make the marionettes come to life on stage. The moves they made and the expressions they had were just so unique and well timed. Each character that came onto stage had it's own personality and skill set.  It was absolutely amazing!!! If Huber ever comes back, I want to be there!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great family experience. Pulled pork sandwich was amazing! Excellent customer service! Awesome location on the strip with live music.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Popped into the 2nd Ave icon but was disappointed to find they don't play live music until like after 6pm. Had a delicious Bullitt Rye and went back to Broadway.  Wall to wall talent.  Seems they'd use that celebrity stage rep to showcase local talent.  Sure would make it a more enjoyable pit stop.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Very very slow and poor service. Food delivered was incorrect and server indicated that the food runner couldn't be tracked down to correct it. Definitely did not have a customer is always right attitude. I very seldom complain or have issues with service but this was extremely poor experience. By no means was there southern hospitality experienced from staff. 

The live classic country music was very nice and enjoyable. 

Food is ok but not exceptional. I like simple food which the menu is primarily comprised of. 

I am not sure whether I would ever give this place another try. If I did, I would likely sit at the bar. 




Overall, this could be a god experience of staffing is adjusted

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Great service, good food and awesome live bands.  Kid friendly, line dancing.
We highly recommend the Wildhorse Saloon over the George Jones Restaurant.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This place is a must! We tried a few times to get in and the third time was a charm. The place is huge and they have a dance floor, full stage, multiple bars, and three floors. We got there around 4:45 and got seated immediately but when we left around 6 o'clock the line was out the door. There were three different singers when we went, the first guy wasn't the best I've heard all week, and I don't know how the others were. Our server was great and came by frequently and gave great recommendations.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
This bar is on the corner in Broadway across from the Bridgestone arena in the heart of downtown Nashville.  I has two stories with the upper deck being an open/covered patio w/ a small stage.  There is at least one stage downstairs as well.

This place is pretty touristy, but for good reason: you should go there.  Plain and simple, it rocks.  There will be live bands to be there on there multiple stages most evenings.  This is Music City, after all, so every one playing and singing here will be trying to make it big, so the music will be top notch making for a great and rowdy experience.

The food is decent here and not too pricey.  Not the best barbecue I've had in the south but was a perfect compliment for the entertainment.  Drink specials seem to mostly include domestic bottle of beer and maybe some mixed drinks.

Side note: the first time I came here Ronnie Dunn popped up out of nowhere, took the 2nd floor stage and played four songs (June of 2013).  Afterwards he spent at least an hour being mobbed by riff-raff and hooligans (my wife and I included) for pictures and autographs, and he was very cooperative.  Seemed to be a somewhat normal occurrence here.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
My boyfriend stopped in Nashville on a Sunday so naturally at 7-8, most places were closed. We settled on this place because we wanted to try some "southern" bbq since we're from Michigan. Honestly? It sucked. The waitress had a section of over 10 tables, so our service lacked. Not her fault at all, as I've worked food industry and 10 tables is at least double what someone who cares about service should make their servers do. My rum and coke was watered down. Our pulled pork sandwiches were so dry that I nearly choked on the first bite. They had one standard barbecue sauce that we had to drench our food in.

This is the kind of place that tourists need to avoid. The only reason they had a full house was because they were open, and they had a nice upstairs patio to suck people in like we were.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
We entered expecting the same , lively club of 10 yrs ago. We entered and waited at the end bar for service which never came  I had to find the bartender for service
 I paid 11.oo for a cocktail and coke
 The dance floor filled with about 20 min for a dance lessons and left after the practice
The band was excellent.  There were maybe 20 people total . Dissapointed in my favorite club
We used to drive up from Knoxville just for them

Victoria Nellums

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This place is terrible!! Don't waste your time. What a tourist trap! The BBQ is dry and not cooked in-house. Live music is a draw but the food and drink leaves much to be desired. If you're in the mood for BBQ, it's much better to go to Jacks and hit up a live music spot afterwards. Prices here are extremely high as well. I would not recommend this spot.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Food was great and you can't beat the atmosphere...however, the best part was our waitress!!! Hayley from Pennsylvania was quick, helpful, and honestly pretty funny! We had a blast with her. Definitely coming back.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Can't rate the food or drinks. We never got waited on. It was a Wednesday afternoon. Not that busy. Bye bye.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Ambiance was cool and line dancing lessons were fun but totally underwhelmed by the food. Whoever said the fried pickles were their best ever has no taste, Hooters has way better fried pickles. Burgers had no seasoning. Service was good

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
It holds its promise. Very nice venue, fast service,
Line dancing and great bbq. We had the brisket, cheeseburger, chicken tender and grilles cheese. Just great. And our waitress was really nice. 
We also had the famous fried pickle in apps. Really gwood:)

name: Nashville Palace
text: Out of downtown near the Grand Ole Opry. The food was basic bar food, although the chicken strips were large slices of chicken breasts. The place has a funky fun feel and the crowd likes to dance. Saturday night was Nathan Belt and the Buckles, a real rockabilly sound with lots of 50/60's country hits. Any singer that can do Roy Orbison is good with me.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
I've been to several shows at TPAC in both Jackson Hall and Polk Hall. The venue itself is absolutely phenomenal. Great seats in all sections no matter what theatre you happen to be in. I've seen 3 Broadway touring shows and 1 solo performance show at TPAC. Tickets are affordable depending on what show you happen to be seeing. The only downside is that they have no student rush and rarely ever is there a lottery rush, so no discounts unless you're in a large group. 

Other than those tiny exceptions, TPAC is an excellent structure and one of the finest theatres in the state.

name: The Cobra
text:
Geographical Location: Up & coming (kinda feels a little sketchy)
Are the floors sticky: No (thank goodness), however you do feel like you think they are going to be.
Is it loud: HECK YES. bring your ear plugs to soften the loudness
Parking is a little sketchy too, and you will likely have a little jaunt.
Variety: It's a good thing! There's a cute quieter smaller more intimate room but still with big noise (on the right as you walk in), the "lobby" where the front door is has a couple games and a couple booths and separates the different rooms.  The room on the left (when walking in) has the bar and more music. I didn't venture to that room, so I don't have much to comment about that. Would I recommend? In general I probably wouldn't just come out to hear music but if my friends are playing their music there, then definitely!

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
We have seen several shows here now.  We particularly enjoy the Tennessee Repertory Theater (now Nashville Rep) and the Nashville Ballet.  If you've read my reviews, then you've probably guessed my biggest complaint: parking.  We tend to pay $20 for parking at every event.  However, I've recently read that the library offers special $5 parking during off hours and weekends, so we are keen to try that next time.  We also prefer to purchase tickets online in advance to skip the lines.

The theaters are cozy without being crowded, the staff is courteous, and we've sat in just about every section and have not found a bad seat in the house.  We don't usually partake in concessions so I can't really comment on that, and based on the lines after the show, we have no desire to try the valet parking.  The bathrooms are inconveniently located, which is the only complaint I have about TPAC so far.

TPAC is definitely a recommended Nashville experience!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I was here for a work event on a Wednesday evening. The massive location highlighted a sparse crowd in the restaurant on the first floor. Our private party split the second floor with another party. The second floor had a stocked bar, restrooms, shuffleboard, foosball and pool tables. There are a ton of seating options too. Some of us conversed at the high top tables and others say around the balcony handrail to watch the line dance lesson. Even with half a dozen people participating, there was live music and a couple employees leading by example. I bet this place is rocking on the weekend.
Food was pretty decent for BBQ brisket served buffet style. I'd skip the mini pies for dessert though, they didn't taste like much.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: As expected the place was packed... my buddy Adam was manning the bar and serving like a boss. I couldn't sit outside because of the crowd but inside was nice and friendly. The beer is cold and the Tomato and basil pizza was fine! Love this place and always have a good time here.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Best. Place. Ever.

I had the pleasure of visiting the Nashville Palace on a recent trip to Nashville. We were staying nearby and checked the Palace out on the basis of a recommendation. We loved it so much we went back a second time before we left. It is located in a strip of stores that include the Willie Nelson Museum, where I also spent a great deal of time but that's another story. Anyway, the Nashville Palace is a honkytonk of vintage variety frequented by locals. They feature live music - Western Swing, anyone? You can dance if you are so inclined, and the food is great at a great price. AND THEY SERVE MOONPIES FOR DESSERT. The next time you find yourself in Nashville, definitely make time for a stop at the Nashville Palace. You will not be disappointed.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
The barbecued have chicken was surprisingly good today. My expectations were surpassed and I give them credit.  The service was also good but a bit slow, we set upstairs it was not very busy but it didn't seem to take it while for our server to deliver.

The music setup upstairs is not as good as the music on the first floor in my opinion.  

Of the honky-tonks in Nashville Rippys is one of my top two but somehow seems to be overshadowed by some of the more popular joints down the street

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
Oh TPAC, you never let me down!

With 3 different auditoriums, TPAC can host popular comedians, broadway shows, smaller theatrical productions, concerts, operas, the ballet, and everything in between! I appreciate the variety of offerings they have, and always enjoy coming to shows here. 

They also allow adult beverages in the show, and will pre-order drinks for you so you can swing by the bar during intermission. So convenient! If you are in Andrew Jackson Hall (the largest one) they recently opened a bar INSIDE the auditorium. That just rules!

You can park for free at the capitol just off Charlotte down the hill a bit, and I always do that to avoid paying to park :) 

My only complaint is that their bathrooms aren't super accessible or convenient, and I feel their signage is small. The restaurants also seem to be crowded no matter when you go. 

I appreciate you TPAC, and am excited to see which shows grace your stage this year!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: A regular stop for us when in Nashville best part about the place is the music by Paul Pace. On 5/31/16 the bartender was very attentive, kept drinks filled and even helped us order something that wasn't on the menu. It is a bar so don't expect 5star dining, but you should enjoy your visit!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Ribs and side dishes were amazing!! Beer was cold and the music was great!!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great music in two spots downstairs and the covered patio upstairs.  The BBQ is great - one of the old standby's on Broadway.  Friendly staff.  They do have TV's if you are interested in sports.  The patio on the roof is a good spot for music and broadway people watching.  It can get a little crazy before big events at Bridgestone.  And remember to tip the musicians - that's really how they make a living.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Ribs and.sausage were fantastic! Music was good, if not a little loud! Great service!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
What a disappointment- I was expecting a 
country bar/restaurant. When we arrived they had line dancing lessons - awesome!!!  When the band came out to play - I'm assuming that it will be a country band (HELLO- we are in Nashville) that we could use our line dance lessons. Nope, I was wrong, it was a rock band, granted a good rock band but we were expecting country music. Won't be back - will tell my friends not to bother!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Desperate for a place to sit on memorial day weekend, 

We went up to the second floor, the smell of fresh vomit greeted us.
Sat down, a rush and haggered waiter took our drink order.

Sat around for a few, ate some wings and onion rings, it was just not a good night to be there, bailed quickly.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This was our lunch stop on our honky tonk walking tour. The music was pretty good, the bartender was attentive but the food. Yes! Get the rib wraps, probably the neatest (as in less messy) way to get your meat, smoke, sauce and coleslaw. Paired with turnip greens - so flavorful my mouth is watering right now! - you have the makings of a memorable meal experience. The place is bigger than it looks on the outside, so don't let the crowds deter you; c'mon in!

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Noel and I decided to grab some lunch before hitting the mall...I hate going to the mall and fighting the crowd shopping, much less trying to eat..so we went to Nashville Palace for a quick bite before our RETAIL THERAPY Section..

I decided on the restaurant..I knew before we went in that its a Touristy TRAP but HEY, sometimes you have to give it a go...I am a local now, 4 1/2 yr resident of Nashville..but sometimes I like to blend in with the tour-eestas...

We went into the Nashville Palace and it is a little dark like a bar...there was a guy singing on the platform sitting on a barstool strumming his guitar...at first he wasn't have bad but as the 45 minutes slowly passed by he was featuring his song choices for one older man...he knew by name  BERT I think it was and he was wearing out the genre with oldies but goodies ...but they were like the funny songs not really anything worth listening too over and over..they were all sort of the same after you get through the first 3-10...lol !!!

Noel ordered the Mushroom Swiss with fries and I ordered the hot wings with blue cheese for dipping..and the burger was just PLAIN...and small and the fries were slightly cold..the wings were okay but sort of over cooked. It wasn't bad but it wasn't that good..my biggest problem was the FLIES...they had the window/garage doors opened and the flies were so darn bad...they were so darn  aggravating...to the point of maddening...I will definitely NOT eat there again for the sheer fact the darn flies drove me away..

I want to eat somewhere where they appreciate you and treat you with inside dining free of bugs and in the air conditioning. If I wanted to eat with the bugs, I would EAT outside on the Patio...I will NOT EAT here again...
The service was slow, but heck she was the only one working. She had to be bartender and waitress to the whole restaurant including the patio..on a friday afternoon around 12:30...they should have had her some help.

As all my reviews, I ask if you want to go here .go here..your opinion and experience maybe way different from mine..I just choose NOT to dine here again..

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great time at Rippys!! The music was fantastic, I don't remember the name of the group Singing but they were very talented and added to the ambiance of the restaurant. I had the chili and it had just the right amount of spice while maintaining great flavor. The chili came with corn cakes that were much like pancakes made from corn meal. The staff were wonderful and attentive, this was a great lunch spot.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: So my initial experience was pleasant.  I was sitting at the bar by myself and found out I had friends meeting me here. So I asked for a table. The host did not want to give me a table because he said I had to eat dinner. I sit back at the bar and realize there are plenty of people at the tables just having drinks. Not to mention it's a Sunday afternoon and the place was DEAD! Then my friends come and they get a table, saying exactly what I just told the guy.  First negative experience I had in Nashville. Don't want to throw race into this but I am a minority and my company looked more like the locals.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: We came for drinks, no food. I cannot comment on their food because we didn't have any, but the menu looked great and the drinks were fantastic! The artist playing was absolutely awesome. They were teaching line dancing lessons while we were there. It was a lot of fun and a very kind, friendly and fun atmosphere. Definitely a must see when visiting Nashville!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Overpriced barbecue, the only reason I walked in the place was Jack's is closed on Sunday. The pulled pork had no flavor. And they offer no combinations. And did I say overpriced?

On a side note, the place was empty, server (Victoria C #448) made us move to one of their tiny two place tables. Guess what, still empty when I left. 

And one last thing barbecue sauce, only two, one too sweet and one too spicy.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Great atmosphere. I tried the Apollo Po Boy and it was great. Fast and friendly service. Great artwork and music instruments on the wall. Good value for the money. Definitely will be back here soon.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Went in here two separate nights performers were all fantastic.. If you get hungry you have to try the pork loin sandwhich.. Phenomenal !!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Had the pork loin melt with coleslaw on the sandwich with the potato salad on the side. Potato salad was a definite pass... way to sweet. It needed something to break that sweetness up like some onion or more salt but just way to sweet. The sandwich was very tasty. The pork was great. I wish that had given me a little more slaw on top and used thinker Texas toast but overall a good sandwich. 

The music and view upstairs was great while we dined. We thought the drinks were a little overpriced but that seems to be par for the course on this street.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: It was a decent venue whilst without a cover. I had the Jalapeño Burger, which was pretty decent with the spicy table sauce. Between the two sauces, the darker sauce was favoured by my table. The stampede platter was well-received by 2 people at my table, but one person said that, despite the different cuts, the taste was very similar and got tiresome. Beer and entertainment was fun to watch. Overall, a good experience.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The food was better than I expected! We went at lunch with 3 kids & it was fine for them. My daughter had the kids brisket & it was awesome. Enough for an adult. Pork sandwich was good too. Fried chicken was not so great. Ok margarita.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: We stubbled upon Soulshine by accident, we were very impressed would highly recommend.  our server Trent was awesome! We had a mix of appetizers and some drinks. The music was great, had a good variety of performers.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
I really appreciate all the different shows that TPAC is able to bring to Nashville. Over the years seen a few shows here, from Madama Butterfly, Les Misérables, the Nutty Professor, & Lisa Lampanelli, Robert Irvine Live and tonight Matilda. They've got a lot of different content presented throughout the year. 

The TLAC actually consists of actually 4 different sized auditoriums, the Andrew Jackson Hall (2,472 seats), James K. Polk Theater (1,075), Andrew Johnson Theater (256) and War Memorial Auditorium: 1,661 across the street. I've been in all 4 of the theatres, tonight we were in the Andrew Jackson. The theatre is huge. When you're in the orchestra, it's hard to see all the seats that are above in the balcony. The staff is there to assist you to find your seat and most of them are retired folks from the community that are very sweet. 

They've got a bar in the back of the Andrew Jackson Hall called Bar Seven. It's pretty much like the other little bars in TPAC. The prices aren't cheap, but they're not crazy. I wouldn't get drunk here, obviously, so prices are okay. I've posted a picture with the prices of the drinks at the cash bar (they also take cards). 

Parking isn't too much of an issue. They've got a few parking garages that charge around $10. They've also go valet up front that is $18. That's kind of high, but a bargain compared to what Schermerhorn Symphony Center charges at $27! I honestly have never had a problem finding street parking down the hill. If you show up 45 minutes to an hour before showtime, you'll probably find a parking spot fo free!

TPAC is pretty good about sending emails with what is going on, without going overboard. You can buy tickets online and the site is easy to use, with picking out seating a breeze. Nashville is lucky to have such a strong artistic community. With TPAC leading the way.

name: Twin Kegs
text:
The cheeseburgers go two different types of cheese. Two!! It's absolutely what makes their burgers so special. It's not my favorite burger in Nashville but it's in my top ten. 

So the reviews are correct. This is your typical roadside dive bar. It's not clean, it's not disgusting, but it's not clean. They have plenty of games to keep you occupied and the beer runs frequently. If I lived on that side of time I would probably go more often but since I'm on the east side I would rather go to Dino's for a burger and a beer. If you love dives, this is the place for you!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Melody was awesome. Stumbled in randomly right before a big concert on the street and somehow snagged a table. Melody kept the drinks coming was personable and so adorable!!!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: It's very loud! We had the bbq & wasn't worth a return trip to get again or to recommend. Very bland & uneventful This place is your typical bar period. It was very crowded so if that's not your thing, skip it. The dance floor can be overwhelming! Yet another tourist trap in downtown.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Pulled chicken sandwich w curly fries, super yummy! Good drinks, friendly staff, good place to stop for Nashville experience!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I worked here for a few years. I still tell people they must go here for the fried pickles, line dancing, and horses on the ceiling, despite how things ended. I myself have returned a few times to certain private events and other random nights out and it's always a good time. 3 floors and 5 total bars here..very grand. FAMILY FRIENDLY WAHOO...it's the only place I can think of that is 100% family friend in town..there are a few places that are all ages during certain hours, that I would feel as a parent Id have to be really cautious and monitoring my kids with...BUT, not at Wildhorse...kids are welcome and they will have a great time. There's also games like pool, air hockey, and a little arcade so the kids (or your inner kid) will have a blast. Honestly, I'd say get here at like 6:30 or 7 and stay all night to just hang..but PLEASE tip your waiters because they are working really hard and have to run up and down not only 3 flights of stairs, but a basement where they fill up huge bins full of ice. This was a really fun, but challenging job..so tip tip tip them. ;)
They are now doing renovations and I'm excited to see how it turns out. It's over the top tourism, but my gosh they always have great SOLID live bands, (though I've yet to play heehee), and the food is probably the best for the price you'll find downtown. Try the pickles, the brisket, and a giant margarita...and bring your boots cuz if Skyla is working, you'll get the best dang line dance lesson in town, y'all !

name: Nashville Palace
text: This was our last night in Nashville and we wanted to experience some live music with our three kids. We were a little apprehensive at first, but the manager noticed us right away checking out the place and made a point to encourage us to stay for a bit. So glad she did! The kids learned a line dance and had a blast! Food and music was great! The manager even got a guitar for my daughter to hold to pose for a picture. Very welcoming atmosphere, thanks for a fun time

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Originally, had such a good experience. We went back to get shirts. Joey, the bouncer was so great, over and above, both times we went. Zach was also a good bartender and had good customer service. When we went back for our shirts because we loved it so much, Amber was extremely rude. Exhaled because we asked for shirts and had someone else get them for her. Her attitude completely put us off. Both being in customer service we were extremely disappointed. Five stars for our first experience but one for our last.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good ribs and cornbread. The collard greens left little to desire, very watery for my personal taste. This place was good and worth the stop.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I came here while I was in Nashville. I had the 3 meat combo of pork, brisket, and sausage with 2 side orders. Good food at reasonable prices.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Stopped in here with my nephews hockey team and families (large party - ~30 total) on Saturday night and it was perfect! They accommodated us well and we got to sit mostly together near the stage. The entertainment was great, line dancing was a blast and the staff was (mostly) friendly. The third floor had a bunch of games that kept the boys occupied while we all drank and enjoyed the music. However, The food is limited and wasn't great. Everyone raves about the fried pickles but I didn't see what all the hype was about, they just tasted like normal pickles to me. The four star rating is mostly because the food wasn't great and our server suggested a drink to us that was $16 because of a souvenir glass that we weren't informed of. $16!! For one drink! If you are offering a guest a special drink, you need to let them know so they aren't blindsided. I would've ordered something else if I knew the price.

name: Twin Kegs
text: We've been here a few times and it's great for what it is: hole in the wall smoky bar with really good burgers.  It's been awhile since we've been there so we decided to give it a shot last night.  First, we ordered a pitcher of Miller Lite. It was flat.  Then the server asked us if we were ready to order. We were waiting on friends. When we finally ordered she said "our cook left and I'm not sure if/when he's coming back".... what?  She said she could cook up some tater tots for us though.  We won't be going back...

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Good pizza and great music on Sunday nights! Apparently if you know how to play an instrument you can come and jam w the band! Anyways great ambiance, a lot of space! Definitely will be coming back!!

name: The Cobra
text:
This place has everything. Beer, music, pinball, a photo booth, live music, a cat and of course.... waiting to use the bathroom for 5 minutes only to see two gentlemen exit shortly after one another from said restroom. Weird right! Oh well, at least the honky tonk was playing, the booze was a flowing and the arcade was warm. 
Be sure to pop in for some tasty jams and a crack at the Rob Zombie House of a thousand corpses pinball machine!! Rad!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good food, reasonable prices, and great entertainment. I had the pork loin melt sandwich and onion rings and both were 5 stars. My wife had the pulled pork and coleslaw - both good, but not great. Entertainment was very good and the staff friendly and efficient. Well worth your time and money!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Ok.  If you seen how the Wildhorse Saloon was back in the 90s compared to NOW..........It's CHANGED A LOT and I would say for the worse!  I didn't move to TN until 2004; after moving, I decided to try out the Wildhorse Saloon and I was a bit impressed because I was getting introduced to line dancing and I was just dancing for the fun of it.  It seems after going to other clubs around Nashville or Middle TN such as Kickers Country Club or Silverados (which was an awful place) or travelling outside of TN, my days of going to Wildhorse Saloon was DECREASING a lot because these other clubs were different and they were honky tonk places and the line dancing was a bit better!

The young kids being out on the floor was/is a HUGE PROBLEM because they are running around the floor while dancers are dancing.  Parents, you need to be around your kids and set some boundaries!  Too many teens coming out on the floor and staying on the floor while dancers are dancing is ANOTHER PROBLEM.  Wildhorse Saloon, you guys need to set some boundaries!

The dance floor, from what I'm hearing, is decreasing.................WHY???????????

It's more touristy and more of a restaurant and concert venue!

I haven't been to the Wildhorse Saloon in months and the only reason I would go back is for CMA fest because those country music fans KNOW LINE DANCES!!!!!!  Other than that, I don't go back!

name: Nashville Palace
text: Was on a road trip across the states when we decided to stop and hang here for the night. We ordered chicken wings, a mushroom Swiss burger (add jalapeños), and a local IPA. Wings and burger were pretty solid, as in I would order it again. The service and the music at the place is what sold it. Our waitress was polite and helpful. So if you're looking for a nice place to sit back and enjoy some good food and some of the Nashville vibes, check this place out. Shoutout to Josie and her service!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
If you want to see the band, you either have to make that explicit, or maybe you just seat your self. Hard to know because the hostesses stick their nose in an iPad and hardly look at you when you come in, let alone talk to you. I know all these places are just for tourists, but does it really have to be such an assembly line?

As for the food, we all had the ribs with sides. The potato salad and turnip greens were good, but the ribs were pretty tough and bland. Underwhelming.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Like all the other bars that I've been to while in Nashville, this one does not disappoint.  It has the usual multi-level floors with a different live band playing at each one, along with open air seating.  If you happen to sit right by the edge where you can peer down to the street, it's a great view of Broadway street and you can people watch.

The service is good, our server was very attentive and I felt like I never had an empty bottle of beer.  I didn't get a chance to try any of their food but may do so the next time around.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: I came to TPAC for the first time a week ago for a concert. It's a massive place situated downtown. I was in the James Polk theater. Loved that they offered concessions and alcohol. It was nice getting some adult beverages before the show. The staff was really friendly. However, there are two things I didn't like about TPAC: bathrooms + parking. The bathrooms are downstairs and feel like a sauna. Seriously, every woman in the bathroom kept complaining about how hot it was and it was miserable to wait in line to use the bathroom. Parking is crappy. There is not designated parking area so you have to pay to park in one of the nearby lots. I spent $25 on parking - that's crazy. That's almost the amount I paid for my concert ticket. Bleh!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Food was absolute garbage & the waitresses were hard on the eyes. Sound quality was amazing!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Went in on a company event. Nothing special. All day long people bragged about this place it I didn't find it impressive. Maybe if you go when it's open to public it's fun.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Super basic atmosphere. Music was enjoyable. Had chili with corn cakes. I though corn cakes wold not be pancakes but something to pick up with my fingers.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Our group had a wonderful time at the Wildhorse. We wandered in during our detour down 2nd Avenue which is a good take in itself. Once you get off Broadway things are a little more civilized. 
We found 4 seats at their large, comfortable, and elegant bar. The bartender made a wonderful version of the Old Fashioned which I enjoyed. They also had decent wines by the glass. We hung around for the line dancing lesson which was a lot of fun whether you participate or just watch. 
This place is notably clean and quite large so there's plenty of room to sit  or dance. We liked the atmosphere at the bar where everyone was talking to each and sharing tips about where to go in Nashville. I will definitely go back to the Wildhorse next time I'm in town

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Our waitress Tayla was great, the food was great, and staff were friendly, professional and fast

name: Nashville Palace
text: We had a group of 10 and sat on the patio for their 1st day of serving brunch and we were thrilled we did! The apps were delicious, the bacon Bloody Mary was top notch, and the servers/band were all very welcoming and kind. To top it off - the prices are great!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The wait was long, the food was cold, and if we hadn't waited so long to eat we probably would have left.  We ordered wings, fries, and a wrap,  the only thing that came out warm was the wrap which should not have been warm  quantity not quality

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Meh. Bbq wrap was kind of dry and very oily. What's the worst thing? The amount of plastic used. Plastic cups, straws, disposable silver ware. Just an incredible amount of waste. Salad comes in a paper bowl. The only thing that doesn't get thrown away is the plastic basket your food comes in.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
We come to Nashville all the time and we were looking forward to eating at someplace we've never been before. 

The music was great, food was awful and service was non-existent.  We made reservations for 6pm and arrived a few minutes before. They sat us right away and next to the stage which was great because Haleigh Martin was great!  It took 10 minutes before the server came to greet us after the had walked around our table numerous times without stopping to at least say hi.  When he finally stopped by, we ordered fried pickles, our meals, and a couple bar drinks.  The pickles came out quickly and dropped off by another server. We had no plates or silverware to eat. 20 minutes later still no plates, silverware, no drinks from the bar and the server was checking on every other table but ours. We stopped the manager to let him know of the issues were having and his response was "You are more than welcome to leave". What?!? He then proceeded to tell us they were short 2 servers so service is a little slow.  A little?!  A) That is not the customers problem and B) if you are short servers then you close sections and not continue to seat customers beyond what your staff can handle.  The manager did state he would take care of our meals, not what we were looking for but he did offer. 

We finally got our drinks and our meals. My son's girlfriend for a burger that was dry and she had to drown in ketchup to eat.  My son ordered the Smoke Stack Burger which was a huge mess but decent. I ordered their brisket meal that was over cooked and dry. It comes with fries, slaw (which was good) and their version of cornbread, which let's be honest is a glorified pancake that is burnt beyond recognition (Picture attached).  My husband got the Chicken Fried Chicken, the only good meal we got, it was so good he ate every bite.  


We never saw the server again after he dropped off our meals, we did order another round of drinks and yet again they didn't come out until we were done eating and ready to leave.  

We asked for our check. When the server finally dropped it off, all food was on the bill.  We called a different manager over this time because we couldn't find the first one we talked to. We repeated our issues from before as well as the meal issues.  We agreed to pay for our drinks (obviously) and my husbands meal because the rest of the meals were below satisfaction and not eaten.  This manager looked over at my son's GFs plate and said "doesn't look like she had a problem". Really?!? Do you not see it drowned in ketchup and less than half eaten?  She didn't even eat the fries.  

I would never recommend this place to anyone.  Even when others in our hotel would share where they've eaten and asking for suggestions we would tell them to not waste their time!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I visited the Wildhorse Saloon on a Friday night at 5:00, excited for some dinner, entertainment, and maybe some line dancing that others on here haved raved about. Our experience was almost nothing but disappointing.

First off, the downstairs tables had an hour wait. We were told the upstairs was open seating, so we opted for that. The entire "saloon" was swarming with kids. I've seen less kids at a Chuck E. Cheese. It was so bad that the on-stage entertainment played The Itsy Bitsy Spider on two different occasions. He was getting visibly upset because he didn't know enough songs that were age appropriate for all the kids who filled up the dance floor.

In terms of service upstairs, that was next to non-existent. Even though we were ordering food, we had to do that at the bar. Then we had to just watch the bar for our food to be ready and go retrieve it ourselves. We ordered a bucket of beer as well. The bartender mandated that we bring the bucket back right away because he didn't have enough. The other members of our party also had to raise up their arms from across the restaurant to verify we all had wristbands on. If management wasn't too cheap to hire waitstaff to serve the packed establishment, all of this mess could have been avoided.

The only saving grace for this place was the food. We ordered the Nashville Hot Chicken, which was quite good and packed with flavor. I had pretty low expectations for the food by the time our meal arrived, but it ended up being pretty good.

All in all, though, we left very disappointed. The ownership either needs to market this place as a kids destination or as a fun place for adults to dance and have a beverage. They can't have it both ways.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: I'd give this place a negative 5 if I could. Don't waste your money for the $6 cover charge or your time. Service is awful...oh, wait! There is NO service. The place was booked with private events on the multiple floors and there was no seating... unless you ordered a dinner entree per person, which we didn't want to do. Sat at an apparently open bar area and were kicked out because we were sitting in front of the private party area. Apparently, the only seating was in the bar area. Luckily a couple was leaving as we were relocating. Waited in vain for a waitress or waiter to take our order and finally went to the bar to get cocktails. No one picked up dirty glasses left at the table by the previous party so finally took them to the bar. This place has terrible to NO customer service and the attitudes of the hostesses and waitresses is disgraceful to supposed Southern hospitality. Find another place for dinner, dancing and/or entertainment.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We really enjoyed the food here.  We came here every day for a meal.  Breakfast, lunch and dinner are all good.  The Hot Chicken and Pork Shank were awesome!  Great service from Mikey, our waiter.  He made sure the grilled chicken and kale salad was just the way we like it.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Good Music, but had to get our own drinks, server ignored us. She went to all other tables in our area, but not us. Other servers did not approach us. Appeared to be local patrons, servers knew, those folks waited on promptly. We  didn't get drinks right away, but after 20 minutes, my husband went to the bar for our drinks and complained to bartender about service, but said nothing could be done  about service. Walking distance from our Hotel, but we would go again for the music, but be prepared to get our own drinks,  soda price reasonable.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Nice atmosphere with live entertainment, food was good but nothing memorable.  Had a group of eight on Friday night so it was great to find a table open as they have multiple levels and plenty of seating.  Service was good with a friendly waitress and support staff to help out made a great night for everyone.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Not well organized, we sat ourselves, asked another table for their menus and when we finally flagged down waitstaff, we were ready with our order.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I've got to admit. I'm not much of a Pizza guy, but Soulshine is great. I've been a few times and the flavors are great. It's definitely worth checking out. Their second floor balcony is great as well.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Totally paying for the atmosphere here.  Brisket resembled beef jerky and tasted the same.  Full slab of ribs are the size of a half-rack elsewhere.  Live band on each level but good luck hearing one without the other...and neither was good.  Sort of like going to a Chucky Cheese and watching the rat sing out of tune.  Not a fan.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Went for a burger and had the brisket. Was a decent price and tasted okay. The service was good and the band playing was great.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Come here for the atmosphere and fun but not the food. I got the 3 meat plate- the sausage was nothing special, brisket tasted like roast beef, and chopped pork was definitely reheated from the day before. Huge waste of $22. I brought my 8 year old daughter and she loved it. Line dancing was fun. There was an hour and a half wait for the first floor but tons of open tables and hardly anyone standing around waiting. The second floor was open seating but you had to order food at the bar and hope it made it to you since there aren't servers or numbers. The food runners walk around lost trying to figure out where food goes. They need a better system for that, like numbers. The music and overall set up is great, and there are kid friendly activities upstairs.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: This place was absolutely amazing! The service was the best we've ever had since being in Nashville for 4 days. Definitely a must have if you like cheaper than regular Nashville beer and if you like great food! I got the 5 cheese pizza and it was so melty and delicious and the pizza crust was the perfect thin and airy consistency. My husband got the pulled pork nachos and they were everything nachos were supposed to me. Every bite had the deliciousness on it. The pork was tender and delicious, and the blue corn chips were just the perfect addition!

name: The Rutledge
text: The service certainly leaves a LOT to desired. A little disappointed, I really did expect much more atmosphere. Small balcony earned a star and comfy chairs/strong drinks earn two more.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Very crowded and loud music...but it's Nashville!  Friendly and fun atmosphere. Great ribs and good service. Listened to some amazing talent.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Love! Charming throw back country music atmosphere. Loved all the memorabilia on the walls, you can tell there's a lot of history there! A real honky tonk. Live music was great, (we came specifically for a writers night) they also have a nice big patio. Our server was very friendly and the food was surprisingly excellent! Had a grilled chicken sandwich with sweet potato fries. The grilled chicken was seasoned so well, one of the best chicken sandwiches I've ever had. The fries were delicious too! Very fast service with fair prices. I will definitely be back, I can't wait to bring friends and out of towners here as well!

name: Nashville Palace
text: Bad restaurant service, very slow. Food is not good. Music was too loud and it was difficult to hear singers. Music band was good, however, music producer needs to work on balance music sound and artist singing. For 69$ a person I Do not recommend!

name: Twin Kegs
text: Great place! Cheeseburgers, jalapeño poppers and beer- what could be better. Oh yeah the shuffle board table.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Like several other recent reviewers, I was brought in the door because of a generous Scoutmob deal. I didn't hate Soulshine Pizza, and I might be willing to give it another chance one they've worked out the growing pains of a new business and staff. 

The remodeled building looked great, and the twisty staircase to the bar upstairs was a nice touch. The staff was also very pleasant and friendly. Still, any restaurant needs to rest on the laurels of its food. I have to say, I've had better pizza for less money.

I was surprised by the lack of beer knowledge on the part of the servers, especially because they had a fairly extensive selection. My server did not know anything about the beer selection, other than the names on the list. When I asked about this, he explained that the waitstaff is not allowed to has drinks at the restaurant, even on days they are not working. 

This policy really perplexed me, as just about any restaurant will take the time to train staff about the wine, beer and cocktails served. If done right, server training should include samples in my opinion. For a restaurant that prides itself on beer selection, I really think they're shooting themselves in the foot with this strict policy.

I ordered the Boudreaux pizza, minus the crawfish tails. The Andouille sausage was a nice topping, but the pizza was overall just okay. While the $9.99 price tag was not outrageous for a personal-sized 8" pizza, the next largest size (12") was almost double that, and a large (16") was darn-near $30. That's a lot of money for a pie. I would have enjoyed a $8 take-and-bake from Papa Murphy's about as much while having plenty of money leftover for a better selection.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Our first stop in Nashville after a long travel day. Super friendly staff, cool artwork, great music and great food. The cheese and garlic breadsticks were great - huge portion. I had a Wild Bill pizza - grilled chicken, garlic ranch, mozzarella, and wing sauce. It was spicy and awesome. My wife liked it better than her pizza, which was also really good as well. She had The Mississippian bbq sauce, grilled chicken, sun dried tomatoes, and pepper jack cheese. Super tasty food - a great welcome for us!!

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
When you first enter the building, the Andrew Jackson venue is to your immediate right. The James K Polk and Andrew Johnson Theatre are further inside the building. The public space is spacious enough for you to come early, grab a drink and await your show. Though I'm not sure how early the bar/snack vendors open, it was nice just to get there early to cool off from the summer heat!

I was a little confused because it was hard to find the restrooms. Since it was my first time, perhaps I missed the signs. I found a sign for them as I approached the entrance to the Polk theatre and was directed to take the stairs to the lower level. If I were there for a performance at the Andrew Jackson venue, I would have had to ask for directions. My assumption is that you would have to walk up to the mezzanine and go down the stairs.

The Polk theatre was very nice, the seats were comfortable and it seemed every seat would have a full view of the stage.

The $20 valet was busy as I walked up. The TPAC website also offers you a chance to reserve parking at City Center for $10 if you sign up online. I saved a couple of dollars by parking at the library.

Looking forward to my next visit and I'll definitely be updating this review!

name: Nashville Palace
text: Was visiting Willie Nelson & Cooter's place's when the music from the Palace caught our attention. Stopped in for a quick cold one with my wife and adult daughter. Seven hours later we left with memories worth 10 times what we paid for. The staff? Phenomenal! My daughter has special needs. Some people don't mix well with this population. Our waitresses,  bartenders and the bands and fellow guests could not have been any better, nicer or more accommodating. The food was great. The fried pickles were the best I ever had,  ever. Fried yucca? Try it. Beer? ICE cold. Get away from the downtown crowd for an evening and try the palace.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: Amazing performances. My husband surprised me by taking me to see Beauty and The Beast. I took a friend of mine to see Cinderella. I seriously almost cried both times it was so beautiful lol. The tickets weren't expensive either 130 for two people. I ordered my tickets online which was very quick and easy. They also have a great concession stand with lots of food to choose from. I also bought a beautiful Cinderella graphic tee. I would definitely go back to see both of those amazing shows. The way Cinderella would change into different costumes right before your eyes, even hair style changing was simply spectacular! I will always be a girly girl and enjoy the Disney princess shows no matter how old I get lol!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: The shrimp and grits was excellent! Flavorful and delicious. It was a nice treat to come during a Wednesday evening with live music (no cover). The restaurant is pretty big. It's close to the Music Hall and the JW Marriott where I was staying while attending a conference. My Ring Of Fire Margarita was OK--not spicy and a little too sweet for my liking.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Best Ribs in Nashville period. Beer is cold, music is always great, but the Ribs are #1.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Ordered 2 kids meals. It was pretty much mediocre. I had a cheeseburger. Decent size but tasted like an imitation burger.  My husband ordered ribs and sent them back. They tasted oven baked. No seasoning and the fries were half done. The greens looked over cooked and soggy. We will not eat here again

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Typical honky tonk, live bands, decent food. If you go to Rippy's make sure you sit at Jennifer Miceli's bar, she's amazing. Some of the other bar tenders come across as rude but she isn't one of them. She's always smiling, friendly and attentive. She is very easy to talk to and makes the bar so much more enjoyable. I hate going to the bar if she isn't working, by far my favorite bar tender!!

name: The Cobra
text: I used to love this place, fun games, cool crowd, DJ, but the last two times I've been the whole place smelled like a dirty toilet. Last night we went for a couple drinks and to play darts and I could barely stand the stench. We played a quick game and left. I asked the bartender if he knew it smelled like a toilet in here, he just shrugged and said "well it's Cobra". I'm all for dive bars but it doesn't have to smell that bad. Open a door, light a candle, clean up. I'd rather the floors be sticky than inhale piss air.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
