Went here a few times while in Nashville, it's a fun place, but staff can be a bit rude (which is disappointing on any vacation) Food is mediocre, typical bar food. Pretty touristy place, so don't expect to mingle with the locals here if that's your MO.

On the positive side, they've got a nice open rooftop area. Would go back, but proceed with caution.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Wish there was a 0stars option. Entirely too pricey for such small drinks ( they taste okay)
I'm a cigarette smoker and the pulled pork and chicken literally tasted like my fingers smell after a cigarette. So basically smoked human flesh. The sides look to be canned and taste as such. Had baked beans that looked like refried beans and Mac n cheese that was the consistency of mashed potatoes. Will never waste my time or money again.

name: CMA Fest
text:
This is our second year at CMA Fest. This year was much different than last year. It was still fun, but it seems that the concerts are turning into concerts that you can only enjoy if you pay for a pass. We usually listen to the free concerts and grab a couple of beers, but this year it was almost impossible, due to the fact that the people who bought a pass got into the "free" concerts first. So it would fill up within an hour. 

I don't know if we will be back next year because we enjoy cheap fun & this seems to be turning into even more of a money pit.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
We  went to TPAC for the very first time on January 11, 2018 to see JERSEY BOYS.  The show itself was TERRIFIC!!   

The venue, left a lot to be desired.  First of all, it was rather warm in the lobby, but I attributed it to all of the people walking around. 
Once inside, it was actually hot.  My husband spoke to the box office about it and they told him they had not turned the air on that day.  January 11th was 67 degrees at 7pm, plus that many people in a theater and no air conditioning??!!   Everyone around us was fanning themselves with their programs, it grew warmer and you began to smell perspiration, cologne, beer and frankly it was DISGUSTING.  The woman next to me had to leave her seat and go stand all the way in the back because she thought she was going to vomit from the heat and smells.  My husband said he would not return because the smell of beer was gross.  This is NOT what I expected from this venue after having paid $100 per ticket including fees.

Second, I have never been to a Theater where drinks and food are allowed inside the theater.  I was shocked at how sticky and dirty the floors were when locating our seats.  Plus my seat looked like some kind of liquid had been spilled on it and left to dry.  By the time we left the theater, there were cups, wrappers, napkins. etc. littering the floor.  Terrible.

Again, the show was AWESOME but very, very disappointed in the Venue.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
I wish I had time to write a more detailed review about this place but I wanted to share a quick tip with fellow Nashvillian yelpers:  CRAWFISH SOUP.  Must try.  Fabulous.

The pizza I had was good, too.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
After a big Spring Break party for Yelp, my friends and I decided to go down on Broadway Ave to enjoy the vibe and the strip of Nashville. Originally we were to meet at Robert's but it was so busy. We decided on our next location, Rippy's. 

Throughout my trip, I've passed it a few times and loved the look! This two story joint offers a lot of room! The bottom floor has a bar area and a stage for live music. One great thing about Nashville is the live music and this place was no different. When we visited, a trio was singing on stage and sang some wonderful country tunes. When I walked upstairs, I was surprised to see that the place was jammed packed! This was more of the "nightclub" version of the place. Huge outdoor windows offered a lot of fresh air. Whether or not you go upstairs or down, the beers are pretty reasonable. A Coors Light goes for about $6. 

One of the highlights of this trip was being able to meet MTV star, CT. I don't know if he worked there or not, but I saw him behind the bar and asked him to take a picture. I'm a huge fan of the shows he's on and love that guy in general. In a place like Nashville, I was certainly surprise to see him there, but super thankful I did!

At the end of the evening, I thought we had a great time. The place is perfectly located and has a super chill vibe that would bring joy to anyone's day. When I'm back in town, I'm certainly making my way back to Rippy's. Thanks for a great time folks!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great music and a fun place to be.  The food service is a bit strange in that you order and pick up yourself at the bar.  But the food was good "bar food".

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
We'd been to many of the bars/clubs along Broadway during our stay in the city, and hadn't gone in here because the bands playing when we passed by didn't seem very good. But, our tour bus guide today suggested we stop in because it's supposed to have more history than any of the other places. Yup, lots of history on the walls, but we weren't impressed by any of the three bands on the three floors. They've also got the most expensive beer prices in the city ($6 for a Bud Light bottle!). It was really crowded when we went in, considering it was mid-afternoon on a Thursday. We decided to go directly upstairs instead of standing and bumping elbows with the crowd downstairs. As we got to the stairs the bartender comes out from around the bar and grabs my arm and says "do you want a drink?". Not knowing the layout, and thinking this may be the only bar in the place, I get our beers from her. We saw her do that a couple more times with people going upstairs. Turns out there's a bar at each floor, and she was just grabbing the orders (and tips) from the people passing through before they got to the next floor. If I were the other bartenders I'd be pissed.

If you're on the second floor you get the sound of the band there, but you also hear the band on the first floor. Very poor acoustics.

If we knew before what we know now, we would have walked in, taken a couple of quick pictures, and then visited any one of the other places on Broadway that seem to have better bands, better acoustics, better prices, and less crowded.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place was awesome. We spent 5 days in Nashville and went here 3 times. Entertainment was great every time on every level. Service was slow on the upper patio we had to ask the waitress for a drink after 4 tables of people who sat down after us were served. Drinks were well mixed (strong like we like). People watching is also amazing there too. Bartenders on lower bar level we found to be more attentive.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Best place to eat after a night out on Broadway!!! They stay open til 4am! One of the best burgers & tots I've ever tasted!!

name: The Stone Fox
text: A pretty hip joint. Great mood lighting and the place just glows. Perfect for people watching and not pretentious. Drink specials are cool. Decent bar. Cool for live music from Nashville hipsters. I think a pitcher of PBR is $9.

name: Tin Roof
text: Depraved place with live music but there's like two areas that is very crowded. The bathrooms are very dirty and it is dificult to even line up. The drinks are all right.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Amazing.  I was very skeptical when we went in.  But wow. Chris was our server and though there for only a week knew his products very well.  I had the big Blt sandwich with side salad with the jalepino  ranch dressing.  Extraordinary and even though the sandwich was large it held together and the favors were balanced  the salad dressing which is home made was excellent.   Long story short the drinks were properly proportioned and yes  the drinks and dinner while on the higher price level were actually priced correctly for the quality and portion.   I will be back

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Very nice. Ask yourself how often can you eat in a historic place? The waiter was very helpful, gave some samples of local beers to choose from and gave some nice explanation about the building and it's history. And now comes the best : all of the above combined with great food ( i had the ribs :-) ) but see for yourself

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
I am currently at the Bobby Jones Gospel show and this event was very misleading from the advertisement.  The tickets that my family & I purchased advertised the show from 1-3pm.  I traveled to meet family from Kentucky and be here by 12:45pm. Only to be told that the doors open at 1pm and show starts at 2pm.

Then once seated in the New Era Ballroom I Ordered the 2 pigs small bites only to be told by the bartender that she didn't know if any of the small bites were available.  She later brought me the small entree and it was ice cold.    Who in their right mind would eat ice cold pulled pork and ice cold corn bread?  

I am very disappointed in the overall service of the restaurant and also the food selection.  What a disappointment to an overly hyped up new restaurant in Nashville.



Update:

So basically the Manager contacted me from my Yelp review and "promised to make it right". However what was promised was never received.  I will never + my inner circle will never return to this restaurant.  It sucks because I love the history and culture BUT it's not managed by the right people!!!'

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Food was very good. Service at the bar was really bad. The bartender was rude. The waiter disappear for a long time. Service needs to improve.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
I went to Nashville for the weekend and was able to book tickets for the Saturday night show.  I absolutely loved it!  We watched Dennis Matkosky, Greg Barnhill, Chris Nathan, and Gary Nicholson.  They were all amazing!  I felt like I was at an MTV Unplugged thing or something, except much closer!  =)

So a couple tips.  Tickets went on sale the Monday before the show at 8am (local time).  Tickets pretty much sold out within 5 minutes.  I recommend getting to the website a minute or two before 8am and keep refreshing until you see the button to buy tickets.  Don't ponder over the seating chart too long, because others are too!  Click a table and reserve it as soon as you can!  They charge $2 for each reserved seat and you pay the entrance fee when you arrive.  

So the night of the event, there is a small parking lot with free parking.  We parked in the lot next to it because the lot was full.  Our car was still there, so that was good.  There is one line for reserved seats and another line for waiting list.  Make sure you stand in the right one!  They don't open the door until the show time.  

There's a $7 minimum for food/drinks.  Not bad at all!  We had the sweet potato fries, and they were delicious.  

I would definitely go back to Bluebird Cafe.  Great set up, great entertainment, and great people!

name: The Stone Fox
text: My new favorite Nashville restaurant! It's a chill ambiance with great food. Their pickles are homemade and just like grandma's. The veggie burger, fries, and chocolate cake were incredible. Great little restaurant bar.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This place was a lot of fun when I was in Nashville for the Half Marathon in Apr 2014.The place was jumping and each of the 3 floors had live music - a real pleasure to experience as an out-of-towner.  The bar has a nice outdoor balcony on the top floor.

The band was a little pushy asking for tips and wanting patrons to pay $20 per song request.  Other than that, the place was a lot of fun and I'd go back again.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Get there early! No, no time is too early!

Wish I could be here every night of the week. It's in a dinky strip mall that looks older than it is (1982), but man, the ambiance is incredible. It truly is a special place! Songwriters share their music and it is magical. 

I recommend you attend the Alive at the Bluebird series benefiting Live Hospice. It's a good cause.

Food: you don't go for the food, but if you have to eat, chicken fingers weren't bad. Dont recommend the BLT.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Going here raised my expectation of what Mac & cheese should taste like. I'm not trying to be dramatic, but it's sort of life changing. 
The triple guacamole appetizer was excellent as well.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: This place was super busy at 11am. The hostess quoted us for 80 minutes, but we only waited 40 min, which was an awesome surprise! When we sat down, the server came over quickly and brought us a basket of biscuits with an assortment of jams. We ordered cocktails and water, which were delivered within a few minutes. And after we ordered our entrees, our food came out in about 10 minutes. I ordered the brisket hash and it was very flavorful. I was very impressed with the quickness of our dining experience, considering how busy they were for brunch!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
This is MY bar, and no I don't mean that I own it, but I love it like a child I sprung straight from my womb. I have never had anything other then an amazing A+++ time here. 

Conversation that happens almost everyday:

Me: Where do you want to go for dinner? 
Husband: Hm, what do you want?
Me: I want to go to Stone Fox

And off we go. Honestly, this place is the best. The food, the amazing (and strong!) cocktails can't be beat, the staff is friendly and attentive... the back patio is great for enjoying good weather, the bands they book are TOP NOTCH... what more could a gal ask for? Throw in a few friends (which are easy to make here and I've met MANY!) and it's a recipe for a rollocking good time. Thank you Stone Fox for being so awesome. I love you and will see you tonight.

name: Tin Roof
text: Visited on a Thursday evening. The place was full of obviously inebriated and loud students. I felt out of place. The food was not very tasty and the servers were not very pleasant.  It seemed to me that they paid more attention to the college students and ignored the more mature individuals.  I don't think I will be back.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: This is an experience not to be missed.  I am so glad we got to experience it.  We had my father attending with us so we went to the early show on a Wednesday night.  The reservation system is easy to use.  We got onto the site 8am one week prior to the day we wanted to attend.  We had no issue getting three seats at a table. The staff was friendly.  The history of the place is wonderful.  It all went by so fast.  There is a minium drink per seat but easy to meet with one drink.  The fee was $2 per seat to get tickets on their reservation system.  I also got a very cute comfortable tshirt long sleeve for $30.  I didn't know it as the time but it has "Shhhhh" on the back.  Make time to experience this place while in Nashville.  There is not enough parking so be prepared to walk.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Don't expect good service unless your sporting an ironic mustache or are roommates/dating a server. Completely ignored at the bar with only one other patron sitting there.  Three decent beers on tap and a pbr handle. I'd drive further for better service and live music if I had a choice.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Thought I walked into a bad bourbon street bar. First floor band didn't play any country - bad covers of twisted sister, Adele, and Cranberries. Performers kept yelling about how much they were getting tipped to play these songs and they didn't even really know the words. Over priced bad juke box. I've always heard about the greats who played at Tootsies. Really disappointed that the new generation is tarnishing a country music institution.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Solid burger, good fries and tots, perfect for a casual meal.  Great atmosphere with live music coming into the room through connected bar (we were there for lunch).  Would definitely return on our next trip!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Best bar for fun and live music on Broadway!! It's a blast to have drinks upstairs on a sunny day. It's always a must visit. You never know what kind of amazing talent you will see!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: 1 Star. Came at 3:30 pm on New Year's Eve. Sign said it opened at 5. Waited at a pub for 1.5 hours. Came to stand in line until open and worker said it did not open until 6. We waited in 19 degree weather. This is not how you treat fans and customers.

name: The Stone Fox
text: $8 cover per person on a Thursday night.  Didn't appear to be busy or have a band.  No thanks.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This is such a gross bar, and it's so stressful inside because it's packed, but we had a great time singing along with the band on the second floor that was playing on Friday night.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: After what happened to my Daughter's boyfriend, I will never step foot in this racist owned establishment ever again. I will speak badly of this place whenever I am asked about it. I will strongly encourage all of my friends to stay away from this place. Great message from Tootsie's management, racism is alive and well in Tootsie's!

name: The Stone Fox
text: Great food, hipster vibe (meh), but poor service. The food keeps me coming back time and time again.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
My friend was looking for this place all night, easy to get in and out of with the bottom
Bar well within reach. Didn't wait long for a table, if you are going bring a sharpie so you can leave you mark. Very unique crowd and had a girl singing on the bar, overall great time

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We went to Tootsie's on week night, so the crowd wasn't big, which disappointed me. The Apple moonshine is REALLY good but not real moonshine. One of the bartenders made a drink for me with the moonshine that was good and she was really friendly and I even helped her sell a few of the drinks to some girls. The band upstairs was terrible, but the band on the first floor was really good and really entertaining. The history of Tootsie's is really what is cool about this place.

name: The Stone Fox
text: My husband and I have decided this is our favorite "neighborhood" bar/hangout. They could get 5 stars out of me if they had earlier weekday hours for us parents that have to do "day dates ."  Beyond the fact that this place is just cool, the food is great (also local,) staff is friendly & fun ensues at the Stone Fox! We love their Sunday Brunch (chicken & waffles rock) good craft beers, and nightly live music. They let our grumpy 1 yr old run around pushing barstools till he tuckered out; priceless!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Dangerous and ignorant establishment. Security was a joke and didn't care that people were getting cut with glass, fighting, and kept continuing to do so for hours. Our group notified the security person on the floor we were on (3rd floor on 05/26) that ONE group was continually starting fights with random people and he just laughed. When we questioned why he was laughing he then decided to call someone that would actually do something. 

Our group and multiple others left because they didn't feel safe and despite knowing what was happening for hours, the security up there did nothing. Wouldn't recommend going here unless you're looking for trouble.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
We went here with a bunch of Yelp Elite people on our yelp elite spring break. they have a few floors, try to see if you can get on the top floor as they have great bands playing there and there's also an outdoor portion. There's no cover which is great, but apparently the bands don't get paid, so when you see a jar or hat going around, try to contribute.

I would come back here if ever in the area, it's very conveniently located so it was our second stop on our bar crawl.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Went on a Sunday afternoon and had the BEST time! It was insanely crowded but spirits were high and it just felt like we were joining in on the fun. It took a minute to get drinks but considering the crowd I didn't mind.

The top level/ roof was awesome (it was pouring rain and they had to close some of the open doors) but they cranked up the air conditioner which was an appreciated perk.

The bands had a lot of energy and played a lot of crowd favorites. I'm so impressed with the way these musicians hustle in Nashville!!

name: The Stone Fox
text: Sat at the bar 10 minutes with the bartender text and talked to the delivery guy. Never even acknowledged me. F on service

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: My husband and I tried it around 9pm on a Friday night and the food, drinks and service were all excellent! We happened to catch the Sutler Saloon String Band and they were fantastic as well! The guacamole trio appetizer is bomb. We also split the gumbo and brisket tacos and were impressed with the explosive flavor of both. I recommend their mules and their specialty cocktails...we loved everything we tried. My only complaint is that it's pretty expensive, but we did know that going in.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Again with the tourist trap places where a ton of old people hang out, trying to be young. 

Don't get me wrong, I'm not an ageist. Being in my (upper) 30's, I know that there is a time and place for certain bars and clubs for me, and I also would like to believe that I act accordingly (prior to a few adult beverages). Tootsie's was another place that was recommended to us by our taxi driver. He must work for this bar and Legend's because both were awful. They were jam packed with an older crowd, like no standing room to breathe....let alone grab a beer. Ughh...

There was a bouncer standing out front with a velvet rope, as if this place was THE place to be. We did have to wait until a couple of people left prior to going inside. We quickly assessed the situation, and left immediately. The band was playing death metal to adults my parents' age. 

It was all just a bad dream...I'm convinced.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: The atmosphere is worth it, the bar is fantastic, I'm glad people really have a discovered it, because you can usually get in no problem. This is my go to place for events downtown, close, but not overcrowded yet.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Ok first off this building is amazing.  I love that they restored as much of the old Woolworth that was left. I hate that I was so hungry that I forgot to take photos of our breakfast orders because they were beautifully presented and they tasted even better than they looked. I had the corn beef and hash with a scrambled egg and my breakfast companion had eggs your way which came with potatoes and bacon. He is not a potato lover but these were so good he ordered more. Definitely worth the trip to eat in this wonderful piece of history. I know I will return next time I will try the lunch menu.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great honky-tonk! The wait staff is super efficient. I had a veggie burger that came out super good. The band played some "real country" songs that were marvelous.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: This bar is so bad, it's good. It's name is so fitting especially with the big guy with blue overalls on working the door.  Green carpet flows throughout the building and I'm pretty confident it is full of many nights of regret. If only the walls could talk... Lol  :P. There was a live band and tons of people dancing, drinking and enjoying life.  Best part, there is a car (yes a car) parked in the middle of the floor... you can get in the back and dance or whatever. Makes for a great photo! The drinks were sub par but you should definitely come for experience.

name: Tin Roof
text: One of my favorite bars I've ever been to. I've been to Nashville twice and both times I went multiple times. The bands are always great and interactive. The food was delicious and fast. The drinks were great and so was the staff! Highly recommend

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Was incredibly excited about experiencing the legendary Bluebird and had an overall great experience. Only downsides were the food and the seating. The food menu didn't offer too much, but I ended up getting the chicken salad club. It was a cold sandwich and was surprisingly pretty good. It was served with their homemade chips which I did not like. They could definitely work on the food, but then again, that's not what you go to the bluebird for. 

I got my ticket pretty last minute, so I didn't have many options on seating. But I was not aware that I would be seated basically behind a pole. The staff gave me a second option right off the bat (because there was one more empty seat), but it ended up being fine looking around the pole. Just be mindful of making reservations early on so you can get a great seat!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We stopped in for a beer and listen to a few songs. The place was packed, which is the norm. It was a good crowd, even though it was shoulder-to-shoulder, everyone was nice and not pushy. $5 for a Coors Light bottle but no cover so it sorta cancels out? Good spot to start bar hopping down the street.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Shame on you Sutler. I ordered the chicken and waffles and my fiancé ordered the chicken fried chicken biscuits. The chicken was so over cooked there was barely any meat and the meat that was left was so dry it would practically turn to dust once you bit into it. Pictures attached. One of the tenders wasn't even edible and NOTHING was done. The chicken should have went from the fryer to the trash. Even when the manager or who I thought was the manager walked by and saw me blatantly taking a picture of the"chicken" nothing was said. My fiancé's chicken also met the same fate and we were charged $30+ for food that wasn't edible, most expensive cornmeal waffle and biscuits and gravy I've ever purchased. To top it all off, I would have to go to the bar to get drinks 50% of the time. The ONLY reason I give 3 stars is the outstanding service the bartenders provided. If we would have sat at the bar the entire trip I would have been a 5 just for the hospitality they treated us with. My fiancé was so excited to come here for her birthday and the bartenders are the only people who made the experience enjoyable. Long story short, don't order anything with chicken, and stay away from their "Mexican" food.

name: Tin Roof
text:
Just your standard bar, but the food is a step-up from your regularly bar food. 
I hear you may run into a celebrity here, but I haven't seen any.
I would recommend going to an OUTDOOR concert here, inside is a little too small for a large concert crowd, although they do have a stage inside.
Went to Bingo on a Tuesday evening, hurry because it fills up fast, although they move VERY-VERY slowly... so plan on drinking a lot or bringing fun friends to be entertained because the Bingo alone doesn't cut it as entertainment.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I have been enjoying The Sutler for several months now.  It seems to get better every time.   The food reads like a normal menu, but it's the specific way in which they prepare the food which makes standard classics like Reuben's and BLT's become unique and eclectic versions of themselves.  Today, we had the brunch, and it was by far my favorite visit yet.   The brisket hash with collared greens was perfect.  It balanced sweet with saltiness and a little spicy kick.  Just perfect.   Sunday brunch includes a Bloody Mary bar, bottomless mimosas, and a bluegrass band.  The atmosphere is well thought out.  It can be upper echelon or a fancy dive depending on the attitude you carry for yourself.  Perception is everything and this place will challenge that view. It's completely Nashville, perfect for locals and visitors alike!

name: Tin Roof
text: It s a good bar with decent beers. But on Fridays and Saturday night mostly have a DJ and plays a lot of popular songs. But it does get extremely crowded to a point where u can't move

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: 3 floors, 3 bars, 3 different bands who are all amazing.  Drinks are pricey but you are paying for atmosphere.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Perfect late night food! It was my first time in Nashville and I ate there both nights, which normally would be embarrassing but it's really the only quick late night food available on Broadway. I got the patty melt and the sweet potato fries were the best I've ever had! Be prepared to wait in line when the bars start closing but it's worth it!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: i liked the live music here and the appetizers were all right. It was a bit dim and crowded- the only drink i got was belgian ale and it was all right

name: Tin Roof
text: I just had to change my original post. Tin roof is good for multiple things the perks I've experienced over the few times I've gone: going out and dancing/partying in the upstairs bar area, catching/playing a show (writers round) downstairs, and the Monday night social.  It's a great way to network and hang with other songwriters& artists. I judged this place too quickly off of one visit a couple months ago and for some reason I could not find a way to delete my original review. I still have yet to try the food! Prices seem good, drinks are pretty strong!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Ok, well I've got a purse full o pork, I'm from New York and I didn't know what song I was dancing to but it was an amazing time. I would highly recommend this venue for a variety ( 2 floors of live entertainment) of musical fun.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
When I told people I was going to Nashville, everyone said you have to check out Tootsie's for a view of the Honky Tonk (Broadway) aka the place were everyone gets lit, & for good drinks.  I was not disappointed!

I believe that this bar is 4 stories high?  & with a rooftop bar with a great view of the strip.  I do not know how the gals made it with their high heels!

Each level is madness, with bartenders serving too much alcohol & live music.  It was epic!  To be honest, I do not remember much but I remember getting fat shots, like half a cup full, & having a blast!

name: Tin Roof
text: Tin Roof is actually a very cool place to grab a bite to eat and a beer. We got dropped off by Uber right in front and we were able to sit outside period ever very easy menu which is very reasonable. I ordered the Cuban sandwich and the tater tots off the starter menu which came with bacon bits and ranch dressing, pretty damn good. They have a good beer list as well as some good mixed drinks. Great atmosphere, kind of a younger crowd especially as the night goes on but it was fun to people-watch on their patio. Our only issue was our waitress seemed to disappear as they got a little bit busier and had to track her down to get a bill, which was screwed up, but we just wanted to move on by that time. Otherwise seem to be a good place and everybody enjoyed the food

name: Tin Roof
text: This place is petty close by to where I work, so we pick up food or drinks regularly, typically whenever I go to pick food up it's a male bartender with a bad attitude. I was pleasantly surprised with the excellent customer service today. It did take the girl a few minutes longer than it probably normally would to greet me, but I understand that she was busy. She was so nice whenever I was finally greeted and even gave me complimentary tea to makeup for my wait time! Thank you blonde girl working behind the bar today!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Beware of new doormen and bouncers with attitude. I stood up on bottom
Of stool
To get my sisters attention, and one of the security grabbed me and said "sit the fuck down". I wasn't even drinking. Then on the way out the door man said they were going to kick me out. WTF! The bartenders were awesome and band was great. Your a little to big for your britches sir.....

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
So I was warned that Tootsie's was not worth the hype.  But as I was at another establishment on Broadway, a new friend told me that you had to go to Tootsie's at least once as it was one of the original honkey tonk spots.  I wanted to explore so we went.

After entering, the ground floor was wall to wall people, my Aunt needed a bit more space so she suggested we should go up to another floor.  As we walked towards the stairs, I saw a black pouch on the ground and asked the woman standing over it, if it was hers.  She was so excited that she didn't lose it, she bought me a drink.  After getting my drink from her, I headed upstairs.  My Aunt found a table and we enjoyed the band up there.  We had a second drink.  The second floor was crowded but a bit more manageable than the ground floor.  There was a third floor but we didn't go up there.

The band was great, the drinks were well made (I don't know the prices as I was being treated to drinks for my birthday), and everyone in the joint was fun and nice.  I had a great time and am glad I hit this spot before leaving Broadway for the night.  So I say, come at least once to Tootsie's and you may have a great night like I did.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Hm... not as impressed as I thought it was going to be. I LOVE comfort food and this didn't really hit the spot. We ordered the pork belly appetizer and for entree, ordered the pot roast and pork chops. 

Pork belly: Delicious! They did a great job balancing all the flavors - the fattiness/richness of marinated/roasted/broiled pork belly, with a fresh salad in a tart salad dressing, pickled pears, and goat cheese, plus watermelon chunks for a bit of sweetness. This was on point for $12.

Pot roast: Solid. The meat was very tender, the mashed potatoes were silky and buttery, it's a classic comfort dish that is hard to mess up. They did it well here for $32.

Pork chop: Not good. The meat was overdone and lacked flavor. The stuffing they put on top also didn't help add any texture or flavor. The black eyed peas and cabbage it came with were too sweet for their own good, and although did add flavor to the pork, then overpowered it. This was not worth $30.

All in all, the service was great, the restaurant feels a bit bare (albeit its historical nature), and the food was okay. Wouldn't say that this would be a place that I'd come back to if I were to choose another restaurant during a Nashville visit.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We didn't think brunch was our thing until we came here this morning! The Bluegrass Brunch is a must go to! Great atmosphere. Great food. Great mimosas. Their biscuits are superb! I got the sweet potato pancakes and he got the chicken and waffle. Both were delicious. This is our brunch spot from now on. Others don't even come close to our experience here.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tooties has some great live music no doubt, just like all the other legendary honky tonks on broadway. So this review is for the venue and the atmosphere, since you gotta choose which bar to visit by some criteria right? 

Tooties has two bars, one that you can see from the broadway entrance and one up the stairs in the back. That means double the music acts on a given night. You can really see the age of this place. It is ancient, and there is barely any place to move about even with two bar sections. Despite the lack of space and the throngs of crowds, the bartenders are like hawks. They target you and make sure you have a cold budlight in your hands at all times. If it wasn't for how cramped tootsies is, I would like it a lot more.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We went because the website advertised LIVE Karaoke Thursday nights.   We got there excited to participate and were told they stopped it.  The live band of two were good. Had appetizers and drinks that were good. Very disappointing.

name: Riverfront Park
text:
My travel companion loves to walk everywhere in order to really get the sense of a city. If it wasn't for him, I would have never seen this little Nashville gem. One thing is for sure: I was happy we visited this park at night. It was so hot and humid in Nashville, visiting this park during the day would have been a nightmare. 
What drew us to the park was the light cast from the pretty changing colors of the psychedelic elevator which brings you up to the the Shelby Street bridge. I saw it off in the distance while we were driving around, looking for a good spot to take skyline shots of Nashville's skyscrapers. I also saw the bridge next to it and I was like, "Oooo, I wanna go there!" I got all excited about it and was yelling it out, pointing at it like 5 year olds do. What's cool is that my travel partner gets the same way when he sees stuff like that and it automatically turns into a quest for him. We were so excited that we didn't even notice that when we got there, we had literally parked the car in the middle of the road and left it there in front of the elevator. 
The elevator was all glass and I'd say the ride up to the bridge is about 4 stories. I immediately ran up to the elevator with my friend and as soon as the elevator started going up, I realized that the height and the speed with which the elevator was climbing was not pleasant at all! I had to cover my face and not look out of the glass. The inside of the elevator also smelled like pee. It was gross. The city of Nashville should clean it out!
Walking up to the Shelby Street Bridge was amazing at night because of the way the spotlights illuminated the bridge, it really showed off the architecture. The only complaint that I would have is that the bridge is the best place to take skyline shots, and all of the bright lights on the bridge seriously mess with your nighttime photos. I had to hold my phone out from the bridge as far as possible in order to get a decent shot. The bridge is also a place where local teens like to go and smoke cigarettes, and no doubt, they like to party and chill there. This didn't bother me, but I noticed that they really don't have personal space issues and thought nothing of walking really close to me to get around me while the bridge itself was not busy. My travel partner saw this happening as well and did not like it at all. 
The rest of the park is very clean. Under the bridge there are plenty of picnic tables for visitors to have lunch on better days. Looking at Yelp photos, it also seems like this is a place where outdoor concerts happen and I couldn't think of a better location. I really enjoyed exploring this part of the city. When we walked back, we took the stairs down and stayed away from the stinky scary elevator. Make sure you check this place out!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I'm not sure what was going on when we first walked in, but it felt odd. Once inside the space, it was super cute! It is a very large space... it wasn't busy. The hostess was PERFECT! We were seated at the time of our reservation. Zach was attentive and was patient with our party of 8. The kids loved the macaroni and cheese. The meatloaf, shrimp and grits, and turkey were all good. The fried chicken was fantastic. Get the fried chicken! The kids got milkshakes for dessert and multiple people at the table said it's the best milkshake they've ever had. Several reviews mention the food to be underwhelming. This was absolutely not the case. It's southern fare. It isn't fancy. It was great!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Oh my! What an amazing time we had watching Scott Collier and the midnight special! He is so awesome with the crowd! The bar staff was wonderful! They were always ready to serve! We can't wait to come back!

name: Tin Roof
text: My new favorite bar in Nashville! The cheese fries are so addicting. I met some other customers the other day who refer to tin roof as their second home. Bartenders were very outgoing and made my experience here awesome!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
I came here on a Friday night with my boyfriend for the food as we were hungry and this place was empty. I didn't think any bar type of food would be any good, but it wasn't too bad. The place is run down but the customer service was good and the food was decent.
I don't remember what I ordered but the burger was dry and they're known for their tater tots from what the cashier said so I ordered that. Everything was mediocre at best. The sweet potatoes fries weren't good at all. Would highly recommend staying away from those. But definitely go with a juicy thick burger if you do get anything from here.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Ay yi yi.  This 30 year old is no longer cut out for the packed to the gills bars.  However, Tootsie's is kind of a big deal, with its historic list of big-name acts.  When in Nashville, it's a bucket list item.  The walls are littered with celebrity photos of all eras.  Simply put, it's the perfect place to spot great talent before they go big.  There was no cover to get in, but be prepared to wait in line.  Some girlfriend's and I waited about five minutes, and then we slowly worked our way through the masses to the bar.  Drinks are overpriced, but remember where you are.  We were lucky enough to grab a table while the former occupants were talking about leaving, so we parked for a while and enjoyed the music.  Because of the crowd, which leaves no room for personal space, don't expect to have a conversation.  Go for the experience.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: 5 Stars.   This is an iconic location with significant civil rights history.    Aside from that, the food is great!    It is not high end, but simply outstanding "comfort food".   The decor is super-cool retro and the service is outstanding.   Don't eat lunch on Broadway, go here!!!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The talent at this place was through the roof. I honestly felt like I was at a concert and could not believe the musical talent that was set before me. I was pretty much in  heaven because we ordered a delicious pitcher of red sangria, a chocolate dessert in a cup, and live music. It was the perfect evening. Also if you want to venture downstairs there is a Pool Hall Downstairs, and another swanky bar attached to this place. This place had me at Hello!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Wow!  What a great experience. The Thursday night we were there we saw Jessie Lee, Paul Sikes, Ash and AAron. I think I have that right. Sorry if I don't. Our group was split up because it is so hard to get the tickets on line -we just took what we could get. No one in our group cared once we got there. Every seat was great. My husband and  I sat at table 9. It was almost like we were part of the show we were so close to the artists. They even sat there drinks on our table. The music and background behind the songs they sang and wrote made it an once in a lifetime experience. The artists stayed after and we were able to speak with them and take photos.  Highly recommend!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Bring lots of cash if you plan on a long drinking stay. Drinks are extremely expensive.  Alcohol drinks are a minimum of $9 a drink.  That is for non call booze. No food just liquor. It is truly a tourist trap bar with. name recognition. 
Have as rink and move on to the next tourist trap. All prices have really increased since my last visit. 
Only 2 stars because of pricing of alcohol and lack of value.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Came in for my first visit, and I was both HANGRY AND THIRSTY!!! Was Greeted by an attractive girl at the bar who seem to have a chip on her shoulder she never wants mild never watched big knowledge me other than what can I get you to drink I ordered my food and she put it in and then disappeared and gave respite to new bartender.... New bartender delivered my food to an empty beer which had been empty for probably 3 to 5 minutes somewhere in that area remind you I'm at the bar. A bar of 10 seats maybe. They delivered my food seven minutes ago it's still sitting in front of me ice cold as it was when I got here and I still haven't gotten anyone to come over and asked me about it. This will be my first and last trip here at the Sutler no matter how good the food would've been if it was hot like it should've been!!! HORRIBLE SERVICE

name: Tin Roof
text: visited late Saturday night.  can the locals get any nicer!  funky atmosphere.  Younger crowd.  I'm looking forward to going back.  If you need a late night hot dog, they have you covered.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Plan ahead and order tickets & be patient when you still need to wait in line to get in. Great live music brings in the crowds. They're so well known, they'll allow you to have your photo taken inside if you're unable to get tickets & entrance.
Awesome spot!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Can't rate the food , but would rate business zero based on "security" / door detail.  My 37 year old friend was turned away as her ID was in the hotel room (with no plans / intention of ordering alcohol-if they even have it?   I was then turned away for a "bad attitude " as I thought it was bogus they wouldn't let her or I  in to order a take away burger......guess we aren't the right color or sex

So Weird.  Other Bartenders in the area said food was decent, but 2 girls couldn't get past the angry door men.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place is fun! Super crowded downstairs but that's the place to be. Drinks served quickly and music was great. Saw a couple get engaged there actually! Fun stop.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Outstanding! Very cool place to hang out on a Sunday. We arrived around 1130 and were told by the hostess the wait time was 75 minutes. We left and hung out at the coffee shop, Fenwick's 300. The wait time was slightly longer than the estimate however we didn't mind since the coffee shop was equally enjoyable. Our service at The Sutler was prompt, courteous and our orders were accurate.  I had the Classic Breakfast and my friend had the Smoked Brisket Hash.  Our food was served timely and hot which was surprising given the amount of people.  The Bluegrass Band was decent, made for pleasant change of pace.  The atmosphere is very relaxed. Out of the 3 meals in Nashville, this restaurant was the favorite!

name: Tin Roof
text:
I gotta say, I love my dance bars and Tin Roof delivers phenomenally. But my review is not for a classic Saturday night out. I'm here to tell you about Tuesday night bingo night, hosted by Lightning 100.

First, I'll tell you to arrive an hour early for guaranteed seating. I arrived at 7 (starts at 7:30) with one other friend and had to share seats with another table. i will say that the fellow that we joined was extremely welcoming to a newly minted bingo player like myself which adds to my liking of the event.

Great prizes and plenty to go around. This is how I picture bingo nights going and I will definitely be back. Why  4 stars? The slow service. At one point I stood up to have my drink refilled. Not good. The bar is trying to make money off us right?

Other than the slow service, I loved the chill atmosphere and would definitely recommend.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: 4 floors of madness. Just madness. The first floor was crowded, people were singing on the bar, but you just have to elbow your way through! In the back near the alley there is another stage with live music. We got a beer and got a spot behind the stage and watched them sing songs by request for a while. The upper floors were just as crowded and music was being played on each. It was cool to check out!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: This is one of our favorite finds in downtown Nashville!  The first impression was with the hostess. Lateesha,  she was so amazing.  Her contagious personality is a rare find and we loved her!  Our waiter was on point, the food came quickly and was beyond our expectations!  I would highly recommend Woolworth.  We will definitely be back and will suggest this to everyone!  Thank YOU for an amazing Saturday morning family brunch !

name: Tin Roof
text: Great local bar! Has a great happy hour and laid back feel! Their quesadillas and fries and queso are a must try!

name: Tin Roof
text: Their pour here is close to a double.  The bartenders know what this place is about.... heavy drinking.  I haven't eaten hear so I don't feel safe giving it a 5.  This is a prime pre-game spot before hitting downtown Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great music and fun atmosphere. From looking at the outside and venue this wouldn't be my first pick but we had a lot of fun!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Fire hazard -----Too crowded to be fun.  


Not worth the wait in line to shove past throngs of obnoxious bachelorette parties to wait for a beer. Typical of all Broadway bars. Check it out during the day to say you've been there, spend your evening elsewhere, Nashville has better nightlife than Broadway.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Omg nothing on the menu under 15. The burger was bland and the fries were limp and cold.  Dim lights did nothing to enhance the evening.  Selection is better at lunch when prices are less.  Ok for lunch but a total miss for dinner.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Food was decent, only real reason i gave this any stars. 
1. Host had a bad attitude through the get go, and we werent sat for 6 mins. Take into account there was no line of people waiting to get sat. We were eventually told by some other employee that to just seat ourselves which we did.
2. Sat down and didnt get served for a solid 11 minutes. No waters, no anything. If it were busy no big deal, but half the restaurant was empty, so idk what was up with that. When our server finally showed, she took our entire order, brought just my drinks not my husband, and forgot our appetizer entirely. Burgers were actually pretty decent. We reminded her of our missing app when entrees were dropped and i could tell she just forgot to ring it in. Not a huge deal she said itd be out in a minute. That was a lie of course. 
3. Finished burgers which were nice, app finally came out but we were already full. Told manager to either take it back or just leave it, as it didnt matter. He did comp it so grateful for that. We received no refills on drinks didnt even ask. We could see our waitress paying more attention to the tables right beside us. Everyone else was helped but we were left alone. 
Overall: this was a truly disappointing experience. Wont be back again, even after it was hyped up to us.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
I've been here twice now for brunch. The place is adorable, servers are friendly, drinks are great, food is pretty good. I just am THIRSTY throughout the entire experience. I feel like it's such a hassle getting a water refill in this place. Usually this doesn't bother me, but during my first visit I realized that when you've eaten a few bites of their super spicy chicken and waffles and realize you won't have any more water for 20 minutes, you start to contemplate putting your face under the bathroom faucet for relief. Luckily my brunchmate let me drink his water too. 

My second experience I wised up and went for the classic breakfast plate which was great. Runny eggs, flaky biscuits, sausage and hashbrowns...but no bev refills (coffee or water) for like 20 mins at a time. I think honestly they just need more than 2 servers on weekends. I hate to be so harsh, but seriously, especially for brunch, we need to rehydrate and caffeinate, Stone Fox! I will try you again, but maybe try for a less crowded time.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsie's is always on my list when I'm in Nashville!
Crowded and loud - shoulder to shoulder ... exactly what I expect for a Legendary Nashville Honky Tonk!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Awesome experience!  MUST see!  Make a reservation FOR SURE!!  The baked Brie is off the chain and I don't even like Brie!  Good service, amazing music.  Recommend this to EVERYONE!!!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: One of my favorite places on Broadway! Love all the beer on tap and the games they have available. Good place to day drink and play some golden tee. They did take out beer ping which is a bummer:/

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text: The Well has gotten massively popular since it opened around a year ago. Its perfectly located in Green Hills. The coffee is great (my go-to drink is a honey latte, very smooth and the sweetness balances well with the espresso), service is nice, seating is pretty easy to find, and it's not too loud (plus, whoever mans the playlist does a great job). There are certain times of day where parking can be really difficult (around 10am-11am on weekdays) but it's open everyday and for pretty good hours. They also sell pastries and sandwiches, as well as other merchandise like mugs, T-shirts, and household decorations. All profits are contributed toward providing clean water for regions of the world that need it, which is pretty awesome.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Super cute place, very trendy and hipster. 

But please. For your own good. 

Do NOT eat the chicken and waffles. They made my boyfriend so sick.
I did not enjoy my enchiladas- they were cold and tasteless. We paid almost $40 for a lame meal. 

Only go to this place to drink.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Super cool bar downstairs. Food was great I had the wedge salad with steak. The bartender down there was really friendly and helpful. I'd certainly go back and try more.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
This is my favorite place in Nashville.  It's so amazing to watch and listen to amazing songwriters and hear their stories.

You need to make a recommendation a week in advance.  Tickets sell out in less than 5 minutes and there have been times I didn't get a table when I refreshed the page right at 8am.

When the artists are playing, you're expected to be quiet and listen.  Because of this, you don't get to talk to the other people in your group very much over dinner, but you'll have a lot to talk about after. :)

As far as food goes, you're expected to spend at least $7/person for some events.  I've had a few items off the menu and they're good, but there is a lot of amazing food in Nashville and people come to the Bluebird for the music rather than the food.   If you're looking for an amazing meal, I recommend going out to dinner before or after the Bluebird.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Stopped for breakfast and did not have to wait over an hour like other local spots. To our surprise, got seated quickly and the food was really good. Service was great too. Friendly and personable. The atmosphere was neat too, great history. Would recommend!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Visited The Sutler on Saturday for Brunch. It was extremely, busy the wait was going to be 30 minutes. I asked the hostess if we could sit outside and she said sure there isn't a wait for outside. We had the pineapple orange Sangria, which was very refreshing. Elle was our server and she did a great job informing us on our food and the wait time for drinks as the bar was backed up. She politely brought us some water while we briefly waited. The food was served nicely and the Chicken Biscuits and gravy were over the top! This should be one of their signature dishes!  We will definitely be back!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I got the Dime Store Burger, which is basically a cheeseburger. I ordered it medium well, but it came medium rare. When we got a medium well burger it was charred and unseasoned. I also tried a bite of the fried chicken,, and it was also very dry and had little seasoning. It is not worth the expense, and I would not recommend it to anyone.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: historic, cool, comfortable , classy.   Woolworth on 5th presents a wonderful dining experience.  immediately greeted at the door, you look around to see what they created.  either a table, booth or bar seating each authentically   relaxing.  a southern influenced menu. we enjoyed the outstanding oven roasted Brussels  Sprout starter.  now the challenge which wonderful item to order.  the fantastic Short Ribs were so delicate with the most amazing sauce.  the truly southern Fried Chicken was crisp, tender and awesome.  sides dishes of mac & cheese, collard greens, potatoes paired perfectly.  ended with Chocolate Pudding served via jar.   combined with an attentive waitstaff ,  such a pleasant meal !!!!!!!!!!!!!!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
1. The place is a in a funny little strip mall outside of Nashville, across from a mall and suburban hell - as I like to call it. 

2.  I didn't eat here. I might have had dessert, I don't honestly remember. I had some beers, don't remember what the beer list looked like. Really, who *actually* comes here for the drinks and food?!?

3. Getting tickets/Getting In: You need to get online and get the tickets two weeks ahead of time at like 8am. I'm serious. We forgot and waited til 4pm and it was sold out. They do have a waitlist though, so call and get on it. We were told that there were often late cancels and no shows and there are pew seats that are first come first served. We were prepared to get there at like 730 for the 9:00 show, but around 2:00, they miraculously called me with two open seats at an awesome table ( I could have touched the one guy)! Once you get there, the line on the left of the door (when looking at it) is for people with tickets. The line on the right is for people without tickets. Do it right and get tickets, and you'll be happy you did.

4. Music: We came on a Sunday which is Artists in the Round. It was 4 older song writers who sat around in a circle and took turns playing songs they wrote. They were AMAZING. They told stories of getting their songs "cut". Some of the ones that I recognized were cut a bunch of times by different artists before actually getting recorded or on an album or something. Seriously, these guys were *LEGIT*. I recognized a bunch of them, and every. single. song. was AMAZING. These weren't up and coming song writers, they knew their country music. 

5. I officially love country music. This is my MUST DO/MUST SEE/MUST GO in Nashville. No ifs, ands, or buts.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
In regard to the atmosphere, I tip my hat. Walking into a very fun, friendly, and classic saloon feel. The food and drink menus were interesting. The beer selection is okay, mixed drinks were good and the food was so-so. Dishes ordered were the burger, Mac and cheese, boiled peanuts, shrimp, salad, and mashed potatoes. Of the food ordered, the shrimp and burger were good. Everything else was C- at best. Dessert ordered was bourbon pecan pie and was delivered fresh from Kroger's freezers. 

In regards to the experience - it was terrible. We called 3 days in advance for a 10 person reservation. We're given strict guidelines of "if entire party isn't present at the time of the reservation then the reservation is cancelled/bumped." We abided by the guidelines, everyone was present and accounted for 10 minutes before seating time. When seated, they crammed 10 adults at a table plated for 6 comfortably, 8 pushing it. We were sitting on every corner and with drinks, waters, and plates, it was like a Tetris game from hell. Food was overflowing on the table and no one was comfortable. 

The seating arrangement we had probably impacted my enjoyment of the food. However, if reservations are made, seat your patrons appropriately. The wait staff was even frustrated with the seating because it impacted their ability to place food, drinks, and maneuver around the table because we were stuffed in the middle of the floor.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
This review references the dining experience - did not stay for music.
Got there before 6 on a Saturday. No parking. Waited a bit for Valet ($3). 
Had two beers (which they were out of both IPAs advertised to be on draft), served with warm glasses, before we had to ask for a food menu, then had our food before we had silverware, but service aside....
The food was supremely disappointing. 
Fried pickles for appetizer, they were only about 25% cucumber pickles, the rest were peppers, green tomatoes, maybe a green bean or two, and several fried lemon slices??? so bizarre and just a taste people would want. 
We also saw an appetizer come out with a mason jar of spread and a sleeve of saltines. Come on. Try harder Sutler!
Hubby had the brisket "horseshoe" which was grossly messy - he ate it, and paid for it the next day with several trips to the bathroom. 
I had the brussles sprouts and the mac n cheese - brussels were too burnt/crispy where they left a bad taste in my mouth for hours, the dish was mostly mashed potatoes for $8 and the mac n cheese was just way too rich. Not in a tasty way.

I hate to be such a hater but, I have much higher standards than this place achieves. I don't know what it's trying to be but... it's not winning. 
Later went to Treehouse for drinks and definitely wished we had done dinner there!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsie's really is one of my favorite places off Broadway. Each floor has a stage and a band playing on it. It was a packed house, but we found a spot on the second floor by the back entrance behind the band. They band was a lot of fun and played a lot of country faves. 

The bathroom attendant was the greatest! She was so funny. 

This place is a must if you're headed out to Broadway St.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Stone Fox is a home run for me. The atmosphere, the food and the service were all top notch!

My supper club and I went for Brunch one Saturday afternoon and although it's located out in the middle of no where, it's well worth the drive! I had the breakfast tacos with dill sauce and I have to admit I was a little nervous for a Mexican breakfast food to have dill sauce on it. Never fear though, Stone Fox knows exactly what they are doing and it was absolutely delicious.

If you like a kick of spice, their take on the Bloody Mary is the right brunch drink for you. Not only is it ascetically pleasing, but it packs a lot of flavor in that tiny mason jar.

I seriously can't wait to go back and try their lunch/dinner items.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Go, go, go, go, go. Quit waiting around. Go.

Awesome venue, superb eats, very quick/friendly service, great prices, and very enjoyable ambiance.

The wife and I stopped in for a special holiday-date and could not have left more pleased and impressed. We had a reservation, were seated promptly, and immediately greeted by a helpful server. We ordered a drink and appetizer, and those were whisked out very quickly.

I opted to try their fresh seafood gumbo. Stupid delicious. Getcha sum. Honestly some of, if not the best seafood gumbo I've had in a long, long time. The wife got a cocktail that she enjoyed, but thought it a bit overpriced at $14.

We then turned our attention to dinner, and opted for the quarter-white-meat chicken with green beans, mashed potatoes, and mac-n-cheese. It was probably not more than 10 minutes after we ordered before our food arrived at the table. I had JUST finished the gumbo, and out slid our food!

At the end, there was not a morsel left on either of our plates. Each item held its own with deliciously prepared and seasoned flavors. I must admit however that the mac-n-cheese was a star. Something was just spot on with the dish that made us both want to carry home VATS of the stuff. The chicken was also a bright spot. Perfectly cooked, tender, juicy, and lightly-battered deliciousness. Needless to say, the bone was licked clean (as it should be). All for $11.99? Yeah, we'll be in again soon... mouth watering.

Well done, Woolsworth. Can't say enough good things!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
All I need to say is that I got too messed up to even check in properly until later on the next day...Yup, Tootsies was a great host to us Phoenicians for two insane nights... who is ready to get your crunk on?
~The Good~
Woof. This place gets slammed, and for a good reason. Already half buzzed; I went into this huge joint viewing multiple levels of bands strumming live tunes. Dazed and having fun, I knew it was time....time to dance. The dance floor on each level is actually just widened space adjacent to the bar...and it's always packed. Packed with bachelors/bachelorette parties galore, this place is Party Central. It felt like a Vegas club- Nashville style. On the top level you can also go outside to a party area with tables which outlook Broadway. You can see all the hijinks going on down below and inside ;-) You can also see the Johnny Cash life-size doll on the building off to the side, looking like he's ready to jump. That was a trip, especially whilst drunk as a skunk. Drinks are served appropriately; the bartenders are relatively attentive and did a good job serving me in a timely fashion. The music was up to the bands, but they delivered great tunes and did a wide variety of hits from country to pop to even some rap. I can't honestly say I remember everything about those couple nights...primarily because I was too busy having fun ;-) This is definitely a place you must hit up, when in Nashville.
~The Bad~
STEPS.... GAH! Steps at the entrance are god-awful. It's unfortunate, but since we are talking about a multi-level club servicing a ton of people, let's just say there will be steps. Drinks are served out of small plastic cups...I get it; they have a ton of customers. But couldn't you spring for some glassware and save the environment a tad?  Those are my two major complaints, other than that this place his hella-fun
~The Downlow~
When in Nashville, come here on a packed night and get ready to party. No cover! I love it! No cover and tons of rocking live music. There will be crowds of people, but nothing that will overwhelm you. This place would get 4  1/2 stars, but will be rounded up for being such a good host to me and the other Phoenicians...plus no one died, that's a plus right? 5 stars for the great and unflinching live music, fast bar service, overall atmosphere and for no cover whatsoever!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Online ticketing system is ridiculous... how can 4 different shows all sell out within 3 minutes of the 9am opening window? Why keep people waiting in a virtual line if the tickets are sold out? After this experience, I will not bother again... a waste of planning and time.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Beware if you are visiting!

You can't throw a stick without hitting a bar with a live band in downtown Nashville, but we got lured into this place and instantly loved it's chill charm.  The bartenders on Friday, October 27th were FABULOUS!  We liked it so much that we spend almost $500 on drinks and snacks and generous tips.  So, why not go back!!  Right??  We LOVED it there.

So, yes, we returned on Saturday and everything was going swimmingly.  Much busier on a Saturday, lots of costumes and insane energy.  We headed straight to the bar to be greeted by a bartender who remembered us from the night before.  Of course, she was awesome.  I wish I was better at remembering names.  

THEN, my brother accidentally bumps into some young twit with a nasty mouth.  She told him "NOT to touch her!"  As if.  She was nothing at all.  She was throwing such ugly attitude and acted like she was going to get in his face so I stepped in.  She then started insulting my age as if we didn't belong there because we were too old.  How did Paradise Park Trailer Resort respond?  They kicked my group of 7 out!  About $700 later.  

Every place in Nashville had such lovely southern charm except for this place.  Makes sense.  They only want trailer trash there.  Got it!   When we return, and we will, we will spend our money elsewhere.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This place is a classic Nashville stop for a reason. I strongly suggest going up to the 3rd floor - it has a different vibe than everything else. We went out here after going to grab some delicious BBQ at Martin's. We ordered a bucket of beers and hung out listening to the music. 

BRING CASH! (There's also an ATM on the 2nd floor.) You can pay for your drinks with card, but you'll want to be able to tip the band. They're amazing musicians and all of them are working so hard. I felt awful that I didn't have cash or a bank card. Make up for my mistakes!

name: Tin Roof
text: Had the most amazing food on broadway and the band was amazing, fell in love with the place and would highly recommended!!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
The Bluebird is definitely a must for any fans of the show Nashville. Although a very small music venue in a random Green Hills shopping center it is amazing inside. It is a listening room, so it is meant to enjoy the music not to carry on any conversations after the music starts.

My friend and I got tickets on a weeknight for 'In the Round' where songwriters/musicians sit in a circle in the middle of the room and take turns playing original music. 

Although it was free to reserve the tickets online it was a $15 cover the night we went and they require all patrons to purchase one item (my friend and I ordered wine). Tickets are available at 8 am exactly one week in advance from the date you are planning to go. You can expect that any given night may sell out in minutes, especially if it's someone well known. It's possible to show up the night of to get one of their few seats for first come, first serve but you would need to show up pretty early to do so. 

Overall great experience and I highly recommend it!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: If you are going to the bluebird for the menu then you have completely missed the point. Not that it is bad, but you go for the music and the vibe. It feels like an absolute Nashvilles staple, with a writers-in-the-round set up, reasonably priced drinks, and a fine food menu. It is great for couples or small groups, or if you just love music.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: When I read about the history of Woolworth on 5th, I said to my wife that this is a restaurant that we have to visit.  This restaurant location and particular the counter, is forever linked to the Civil Rights Movement.  It is at this location where protests occurred in the form of sit-ins that made it possible for all Americans to be able to have a seat at the welcome table of restaurants across the country.  It felt good to be eating in a place, where those who fought for my freedom, protested.  The restaurant now serves as a testament to their efforts to overcome racial injustice with racial equality.  By the way, and I have to mention that the food at this place tastes awesome!  I highly recommend Woolworth on 5th for any occasion.  I also highly recommend it as a place to visit to connect with those who fought for our freedom!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
If it's a weeknight and you are looking for a bit of a crazy crowd,  you might want to go HERE.

If you like to breath, you should still go here - but you might not want to stay too long.

This place is tiny. The stage is tiny. The singer was actually standing on the bar, while the band was on the tiny stage. There are some tables with stools. You should probably just drink PBR. It was a serious blast, with the whole place singing along. Very different than The Stage and Honky Tonk Central. It was our last stop of the evening, and I really had a good time here.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: So we never actually made it through the door, but did get up to the body guard and were immediately turned off.  As you can see from photo's this place looks pretty cool - so we were excited to visit, but after waiting in line for over an hour and just about to get through the front door - we were very disappointed in the way were treated, I understand it was busy! But have some respect, the guys in the front spoke to us very rude and disrespectfully which I did not appreciate.  Made me think twice about entering the doors and giving them my service.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
This was a place we were told not to miss when headed to Nashville. Was surprised how far from downtown it was and in a strip mall on the side of the road, but everything about it was well worth it.

We came in for an In The Round fundraiser for the local hospice program and got tow witness the round robin of top of the heap acoustic artists and songwriters including Pat Alger, Kathy Mattea, The DonJuans, Jelly Roll Johnson and Bill Cooley. Wow!! Stories were traded and songs sung individually of shared by all. 

Service was good and drinks done well. As live venues go, it is small and intimate and makes you feel as part of the show. Make sure to make reservations as they will sell out quickly.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Walk into tootsies for my first drink and to open a tab. 

"No, I don't have time to get you a water." 
                                - x blonde bartender on 2nd floor on 1/28

My thoughts, "guess I'll just find a bar that cares at all about its clientele."

The appearance of people spending their money on Nashville soul. 

18$ doubles of house liquor

 Impossible ripoff with no soul or humanity.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
We went on Saturday 8/26, it was also the night of the big myweather- mcgregor fight on tv (which they had on the tvs upstairs and downstairs). Im not sure if this was why I had the experience I did (unusual volume due to the fight), however nights with risks like this should never occur anywhere at any time. While we were there at about 11 pm, the bar was so crowded it was literally the most people you could possibly fit within the space, ie, people standing upstairs in rows of persons like almost like in lines of people shoulder to shoulder breathing on the necks of those in front of them. No way to even WALK through that area! Downstairs was similar, perhaps a hair less crowded - however as we were standing there after getting our beers it became more crowded to resemble the upstairs. 

I hesitate always to leave a bad review, from what I could tell the service (bar) and bouncers were polite and provided good service. I write this review because this place is a death trap, and the management needs to change policies immediately to protect the lives of their staff and the people visiting. My friends and I had severe anxiety while inside of the bar and we skedaddled as soon as we could tell it was unsafe. Situations like the station night club fire could have had many less losses of life had the establishment practiced safe fire code and not overpacked their capacity. As a patron, always be aware of safety and overcrowding and visit bars that have your safety in mind.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Whiskey Bent is my favorite place to be on a Sunday night! Hushpuppy's Daddy is a great band with a mix of old country and 50's and 60's rock. If you like to swing dance or just to watch, you should be there between 6pm and 10pm. The bartenders are great too! Everyone is friendly.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The hotel itself (lobby) is beautiful. As a tall person, I enjoy the high shower heads. In terms of convenience: If you enjoy having a close distance(only to the airport) then you'll love it. Nothing else is convenient. There are no stores within walking distance. This hotel luckily also doesn't have a gift shop. There is a shuttle that takes you downtown or to markets, but that's it. For anyone reading this and thinking "Hey I liked that hotel" or "Quit hating" or whatever, I've heard the same complaints from numerous people during my stay here. Unless you're planning on intentionally inconveniencing yourself and your family during your stay in Nashville, don't stay here.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This bar wasn't so jam packed on this lovely Sunday night, which was nice. Cool country theme decor and a great sized stage! No cover charge after 6 was a plus!

name: The Bridge
text: This place has delicious food with beautiful presentation. I would never have expected this from a hotel restaurant. I ate the California salad all three nights I was in town! It was so clean and fresh tasting. Also tried the hummus plate, french fries and pizza and all were delicious. I highly recommend this place.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
For the brief stay for YELP SPRING BREAK Nashville, this was a nice place.  It had cocktail hour, free shuttle to the airport.  

It's distance from downtown made it expensive to trek using a cab which I only had to do once when my phone died and I couldn't use UBER or Lyft.  However, the rooms were wonderful, the pool was close by (although I guess there was another pool indoors which I didn't see).  But it was a perfect spot away from the busy Nashville Downtown.

I think this was designed primarily for business visitors since it's location is close to the airport and near to some big businesses in I might consider the Nashville suburb.

Maybe I can say, this are one of the few delights I had in my visit to Nashville, the events I attended were so so and I didn't feel the welcome vibe we had when I did YELP SPRING BREAK Las Vegas several years ago.  Hopefully, lessons learned.  

Now if they only can do Spring Break in Europe...

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Service was the slowest I have seen. We ordered and it took and hour to get the food on a Thursday night when it wasn't busy at all. My wings were ice cold and I sent them back. Not worth eating. The menu is limited and not worth it. With So many places to go don't waste your time at Hard Rock. .

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Fair to middling at best. As much as I wanted to love it, it just didn't deliver. Tried 5 different meats. All had a good smokey flavor but were either overcooked or tasted like they were cooked days ago and put in steamer or banquet tray. The scorpion app was good. Brisket wrapped sausage jalapeños and bacon wrapped shrimp jalapeños. The smoked mushrooms were great. I was hoping this would be my go-to BBQ joint, but nope still searching middle TN. I was torn between 2 and 3 stars since its about a 2.5. They get a 3 for having Blue Bell ice cream. Will probably give this place another try in hopes that I hit them on an off night.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
I had the BEST time at this bar during my recent trip to Nashville! This place will be the highlight of your vacation especially if your a drinker! 

I am fm NJ and came across this place while searching for a location for Whiskey Tasting! Sure enough, after searching and searching, I finally found one, THIS PLACE!  

Before heading down there i called the place and talked to the manager of the bar via email and let him know I when coming down and the number of people in my party (which was only two). 

When we arrived at the bar around 5pm, on a Tuesday and it was pretty empty. The decor was very interesting and fun. I went to the bartender and inquired about the Whiskey Tasting and this very nice girl (who was new) was not aware the bar had a Whiskey Tasting. I told her who I spoke to through email and she politely excused herself and got us another bartender. Another bartender came to help us who was also very nice and brought us two Whiskey Tasting sheets. On the sheets she put 5 large shot glasses on it (ten all together) and told us it was only $20 per person  for regular whiskey and $25 for premium Whiskey. 

Either way your getting 5 shots of Whiskey each for that  prices is just AMAZING! 

I wound up getting the premium and my bf got the regular. So we able to try 10 different whiskeys all together!
