She would pour us the shot and explain what that specific bottle was, how they made the whiskey, where its from etc (very interesting!)  After pouring the shot she left the bottles in front of each shot glass so we knew what we were drinking, which was very nice of her. One of the shots were moonshine and she also took the time out to explain the history of moonshine and what was so special about this specific bottle she was letting us try. We allowed her to pick out most of the bottles we tried because obviously she knew her stuff and we picked out maybe three of them. 

When my boyfriend and I tasted d the moonshine she laughed because it was very strong which she knew. She then gave us some really tasty berry mix in a different glass to pour our moonshine in because there was no way we could drink that straight which again was very nice of her. Every time we finished a shot she would take away the bottle and put it back behind the bar. 

For the next few hours we took our time tasting the whiskey and drinking some beers. The bar slowly started to get more crowded throughout the evening and before we knew it the bar was packed! I was so happy we got there early because eventually when we looked around there were no more seats at the bar. Keep in mind i was here on a tuesday. 

That night they had a live performance from a man named Brandon Giels, totally entertaining. He would play his piano upside down, blindfolded, played with his boots and even lit his piano on fire. He was so enthusiastic and extremely fun to watch! At this place they also have bar snacks just incase you get hungry. I wound up getting a pretzel it's warm cheese which was great after drinking all that whiskey. 

We left this bar feeling very nice and couldn't be happier I found this place! If your going to Nashville I highly recommend coming here! I will be back in the near future and will absolutely be making another stop here. Keep it up Whiskey Bent Saloon!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Just left this bar and someone stole my jacket while I was there and the wait staff was very inattentive.   They told me I needed to leave because my jacket was not there and kicked me out of the bar.

I had to walk home with no jacket on in 30 degree weather. Needless to say I will never be going back to this bar again.  Too many better places in Nashville to go.

name: The End.
text: Dank and  overpriced but great music, nice crowd, and a homey culture dive bar like experience.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: good servers and service. good atmosphere. its loud, but the normal and fine loud because its just everyone talking. the food was alright, nothing special, but definitely not bad. but the expensiveness doesnt justify the food or amount. $12.95 for 5 chicken tenders. they were ok, but the breading sucked, to crunchy and to much. the menu doesnt say how much. i didnt know how many tenders i would get. i looked at getting wings as well and didnt know how many i would get. and the parking is awful! theres a small lot in front, but its only valet, and thats $10! then theres nothing else until a parking garage that doesnt tell u prices, and a small lot that is $27 for 4 hours. overall, if they had had a parking lot, it would have been a good enough time from start to finish

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Beautiful hotel.  Fantastic service! I returned from an outdoor concert with a group, COVERED in mud, and we were still welcomed to join in on the fun at the bar by giggling staff members.  Our room was spacious with a great view of the courtyard. Would definitely stay again.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The airport is 5 minutes away. Downtown Nashville is 15 min away and there are zero stores or markets within walking distance. Their gift shop is puny, so be sure to bring your own snacks (they have a fridge but no microwave in the rooms)They only have one restaurant, which is pretty good. Their showers were comfortable to bathe in though. Their bar is thinly stocked and pricey [a Makers sour cost $13.00]. One last thing. Breakfast isn't complimentary, or cheap. Prepare to pay $15 for their breakfast buffet

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I travel a lot, and ask very little, yet when I check in I ask for a quite room (I know this is relative to where the hotel is located, but there are nosier and quieter locations in a hotel).

I knew this hotel backed up to the freeway, so I asked to not be on the freeway side.  This is a big hotel, so there are plenty of rooms (80% or so) not facing the freeway, and I checked in early.  The guy who helped me said you are not on the freeway.  In the room all I heard was freeway, it was most exposed side.  I had a meeting right as I checked in or would have asked to change my room.  I was very polite/friendly when I checked in, yet he just blew off my request.

name: The End.
text: Has a super cool vibe. But it is so small and so dirty! There wasn't even soap in the bathroom.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: I didn't want to give this place even 1 star. The prices in everything is outrageous $3 for a 20oz drink. We booked our room a month in advance and when we arrived to check in the front desk tells us that we have been downgraded on our room. We had no other choice to stay because we were there for training.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
On a recent 5 day trip to Nashville, checked out The Stage a number of times.  I liked this place a lot!  The bands here seem to be a little different than the more party-style bands at Honky Tonk Central or Tootsies. 

No cover (at least not when we were there) and drink prices seemed to be about average, compared to other places on Broadway.  If you come early in the day, they have tables and chairs set up and kids are allowed in until 6 pm. The space is pretty wide open and they have an upstairs loft area to sit.

We saw a few different bands play but my favorite was the Wes Cook Band.  I think Wes must be about my age because he was playing all the country songs I listened to in my teenaged years.  Loved him!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This place is absolutely fantastic, great bands, great atmosphere....and unlike tootsies they don't wand you down like a criminal or have no weapons signs everywhere...this is the south leave us alone.

name: Turn One
text: Best dive bar in Nashville. The sweetest bartenders and the regulars are entertaining and welcoming. Lots of karaoke and open mics too. Even the door guy is a charmer!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: This bar is a well-needed break from the hustle and bustle of Broadway. The bartenders are real people - super friendly and give great suggestions!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
This is a standard conference hotel. We stayed on the 4th floor and it smelled like wet towels the entire weekend. 

I took the kids to the pool, which I do not recommend. The pool looked like it hadn't been cleaned in a few weeks. There was LOTS of hair floating around, bugs, dirt, etc. The clientele at the pool matched the unkempt conditions. 

Our room was perfectly fine. Clean, no problems, low noise. Free Parking, which is easy to find as well.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
First off, the people who work there are outstanding! Everyone asked if we needed help with a smile on their faces. 
The room was fine, clean, nice linens, just what I would expect. 
Here are my complaints. For a GIANT hotel, 2 handicapped spaces out front. The hotel is so large I had a hard time getting around. It was a hike from the lobby to our room, then another hike back down to the freezing cold pool. We were the only ones foolish enough to get in it. I asked a lady walking by if they had a wheel chair available and the VERY nice lady said yes, she would get it. IT was nice, but belonged to another lodger! They were so sweet about it, exchanged it for another one (after they tracked us down). Easy mistake to make. 99% of the time I can make it to the room and pool without one, but hate unloading mine from the back of the suv. 
THEN, after traipsing around, we thought we would just have room service. Uh oh, no menu in the room. We called and said we wanted a burger to split with extra fries. Neither of use want to eat a lot before we go to bed. So we got an "Angus" burger (read: no flavor), 10 French fries, for $35.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: I recently traveled to Nashville for the first time with a group of friends. The music was great. Wandering around from bar to bar we found Bootleggers. It wasn't too crowded, you did not have to fight your way to the bar, and they had a good band. We stayed until they closed at 2. Would definitely return.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Wonderful experience and will definitely be returning. Took advantage of an incredible room rate on Priceline. Actually the best rate in town on a Monday night. So nice to have a balcony and although cold out I look forward to returning and using the pool. Additionally they serve dinner u until midnight and the bar stays open until one. Had cocktails served by a welcoming bartender named Michael who was happy to offer peanuts and snack mix because we arrived after the kitchen had closed. He didn't rush us on drinks even though we were the last thirsty customers. 

TIP: our room was a lengthy way from the elevator  and with luggage, you will break a sweat. Mention to the front desk a request to be as close to elevator as possible.
Bonus: Free WIFI and free parking

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The bands here should all have record deals. Plenty of room for dancing to the outstanding music! I almost feel guilty for seeing a free concert!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Cool place.  The band that was playing was legit.  Great vocalist, and the guitarist was on fire.  So much fun.

Drinks were not too expensive.  

Lots of space inside, which was nice.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Got the banana berry pina colada, brownie sundae, and a side of fries after a late night. The drink and food were okay. Cool band and very laid back atmosphere.

name: The Valentine
text: Gorgeous space. Great for large parties and brunch menu was on point! Highly recommend the hasbrowns!

name: The Valentine
text: So I went here on a whim to have a few drinks with a friend I hadn't seen in a few years. There was a nice crowd and a beautiful and amazing singer with a banging band performing. This woman was outstanding. Now mind you I am not a country music fan at all, but I can't help but love good music especially coming from a great singer. To my surprise it was Haley Vaughn from American Idol! I do not watch television aside from occasional movies. I found out it was her when I did a Facebook search of her name. Haha to think I actually sat in on someone that once debuted on the big stage. I can't forget to mention that the Valentine had good service, attentive bartenders, and strong drinks. Gotta love it!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Let me start out by saying The Sheraton Music City has the potential for greatness. The lobby, check in area, outdoor patios, and pool were nice and inviting.

But my complaints start with check in. First, my friend and I arrived late morning to the hotel. We anticipated that our room would not be ready right away, however, because we were heading straight to a conference we needed to know when we could drop our bags off before heading out. For some strange reason, the hotel staff gave my friend and I tons of attitude when we tried to ask what time we could go up to our rooms. Is it that hard to give us an answer? Finally, the desk staff said it would be ready by 3pm. Meanwhile, my friend and I ended up having to check our bags with hotel security since we needed to make our Conference downtown.

Once we did make it to our room, my friend and I were extremely disappointed with the lack of cleanliness. We found clumps of hair in the corners of the room and in the drawers! The rugs smelled like wet rags, and we could never tell if our room had actually been cleaned when we returned for the night. Two or three times we had to call the front desk for clean towels. Also, this particular hotel has crazy old electrical outlets in the rooms because none of my device chargers fit! I had to go to a cafe to charge my smart phone each night...insane! 

Hands down the worst hotel experience I've ever had.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Great experience! Their customer service is outstanding! I bought a living social deal but had to cancel one of the rooms. Tessa at the front desk helped me figure everything out and made it work smoothly. The staff was very friendly and the hotel was beautiful. Rooms were comfortable and the courtyard with the pool was very pleasant! I would definitely stay here again the next time I visit Nashville!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: We stayed here the last week of July and although a little pricey, it was well worth every penny. The landscaping is beautiful, the lobby is gorgeous with a wishing fountain in the center a lounge and business center and a gift shop to the side of the check in counter, staff was very pleasant, courteous, accommodating and friendly, all rooms had a balcony over looking the gorgeous pool, my only complaint and very small one at that was the ice maker was broken on my floor so it was a long walk to get ice, other than that the next time I'm in Nashville this will definitely be where we stay! Absolutely loved it. Oh yeah and very accessible to downtown and other Nashville attractions!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: The "Moonshine Margaritas" are to die for and moderately priced. Wonderful little spot and always great music.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: First time in Nashville, blown away on a Monday night. And the football coaches conference was in town, could not get any better!

name: The Bridge
text: This bar is outstanding! What a beautiful venue! I love the large glass windows. It's neat to see what's going on outside while enjoying cocktails or a bite to eat. I visited the bar a couple times while there. The bartenders were friendly, and welcoming. There is a variety of seating that is comfy and cozy. They have live music in the evening, and I throughly enjoyed the band on Saturday night. Great place to go for drinks and a bite to eat! And, the sangria was absolutely delicious!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Came here on a Saturday nite.

Had a fun time in this bar. The bf and I were in Nashville for only one night. He's a 
Real-Deal musician. The kind who has made a living doing it so we wanted to see some great live music while in Nashville. This place wasn't our scene but we badly needed alcohol in us after driving from Philly for 14 hours. 
The Bartender in our hotel recommended this downtown area and row of bars. Honestly, I avoid this kind of place like the plague but wth? 
The bouncer was polite, and smiled which was a nice first impression, I guess living in BK the last four years has me sort of jaded. 
The main bar was pretty crowded and there were some douchey frat type bros that stepped in front of me while I was politely waiting to order...where's the chivalry at??? but there is another full service bar in the back. The bartender there was friendly and she definitely poured a good drink. I don't recall how much the drinks were so probably average.

I thought there was a pretty mixed age range but my bf remarked that it was an older crowd - however he's a young'un so everyone's old compared to him. The band was energetic, pretty typical cover band. I wasn't interested enough to find out their name or anything. They had people dancing tho.

We left after one drink in search of something with a little more depth to it.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: nobody in vip section so we go upstairs to vip and we are told minimum drinks to be there ok then waitress doesn't come back and we have to get drinks ourselves then told to leave vip section at 1030   thus place doesn't care about customer service or anyone that doesn't throw money at them

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: My husband and I were staying at this hotel for a marriage retreat and from the beginning they were so pleasant and the bar was excellent. Their restaurant has delicious food and the rooms were clean and cozy.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text:
We stopped here in our road trip and we were mind blown by the hospitality. It was a quiet evening so we managed to have the best out of the staff. 

Food is great. Plenty and tasty. We ordered a mix of everything and if you love BBQ there's nothing here that will disappoint you.

Looking forward to stop by in our next trip to the area.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
My friends and I recently visited Nashville for a bachelorette party.  We visited whiskey bent during the day on Friday and really like the music, plus it seemed pretty clean comparable to the others in the area.  We came back Saturday night completely prepared to wait in the line.  When we finally got to the front of the line after patiently waiting for 30 minutes (We had a group of 8 girls), we watched as the bouncer on the left of the door let a couple guys in in front of us that weren't waiting.  I asked the bouncer on the right and he said "they know people inside".  which I was fine with. I understand the owner probably has friends and they would get preferential treatment.  But then we continued to wait, and another group of 4 men were let in in front of us.  At that point I jokingly stood in front of that walkway next to the bouncer on the left and said "no one else comes in this way until the bride gets in"  to which I was told "they are paying me".  At about that time, ANOTHER group of 4 MEN,  came up,.  The bouncer told them it would be $40,  which they slid him.  I wasn't moving, but the guys physically pushed me out of the way to go in , and me and my 7 female friends were left standing outside waiting to get in. 

Don't get me wrong,  I know things like that happen, and I know bachelorette parties in Nashville are a dime a dozen.  But bachelorette parties spend money.  LOTS of money.  And the guys paying the doorman $10 to get in, are probably going in to get free drinks from their buddy at the bar. Not to mention they were GUYS.  aren't bars supposed to want to have a higher woman to man ration? My group decided not to wait any longer watching people pass us , we walked down the street to another bar and gladly spent our money there. 

Whiskey Bent is a good concept, it has good music, a good location, and pretty good drinks.  But you need new management and new staff if you are going to blatantly allow that amount of "bouncer paid" walk ins.  2 people is one thing.  10 in a row is just ridiculous.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Customer service was good and the rooms were clean. However, the walls are so thin I could hear the conversations of the people next door! It especially sucked when they were getting ready to go out at 11pm blasting music and having incredibly loud conversations the entire time.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Stopped in here for a quick couple of Jack & Cokes the other day.

No complaints.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Great rooftop bar! 
I'd prefer to give them 3.5 stars. 
Went on a Sunday night, there was a band downstairs and another one on the top floor, it was nice to have a choice of so much space. There were heaters on the outside deck so even though it was chilly, we stayed nice and warm.  Unfortunately, they stopped serving food pretty early, so we had to go somewhere else although we were enjoying the view and atmosphere.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: We stopped at Bootlegger's as part of a guided tour of Nashville. Live music flowed from the establishment out on to Broadway as the band played Chattahoochee. It took a while for the bartender to take our orders, as he had just been bombarded from everyone on our tour bus. While I waited to get my drink, I took in the country chic decor, complete with mason jar chandeliers. A group of soldiers stood nearby letting their hair down (so to speak),  delightfully enjoying their day drinking. This is one thing I love about Nashville. While other cities may turn up their noses at such behavior,  Nashville establishments welcome day drinking with open arms and a "Come on in here, Y'all" mentality. I ordered the sweet tea moonshine because seriously, you're in Nashville. Why would you order anything else? This was not the authentic, take the hide right off your tongue moonshine that your friend's, friend's cousin makes illegally in a homemade still using God knows what, God knows where. No, this is not that. It will barely deliver a buzz. I think it was really just sweet tea. None the less, if you want a cool place, with cool decor and good music to day drink with your friends, Bootleggers is  a chill place to go.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Where to start? Ok, the staff is very friendly, albeit uninformed. The rooms not only need to be renovated but they NEED TO BE CLEANED. Not exaggerating, I wouldn't touch the light switch in the bathroom with my bare hand so I used a tissue each time. I took pictures of that and the carpet. Really disgusting. So many things combined. The TV on demand only worked about half the time, the clock radio was flashing and I could not get it to reset or to change the time so I just unplugged it, the side lamps by the bed emit an electrical buzzing sound so I just didn't use them...The room service WAS SO SLOW and the night before I had to wait 90 minutes just for someone to find a room service menu to bring to me as for some strange reason they don't keep them in the rooms. I think they mean well but the hotel itself is not managed properly. Silly things like no butter on the toast or on the tray so when they bring the butter later the rest of the food is cold. Then they have "Adagio Spa" listed on their website. Well, I left a message and never got a call back. So I went online and found another number for them and it was some clueless girl who wasn't even sure there was a spa at the hotel at all. Then when she figured out there was it comes out that they don't really have "a spa" there, but a room where THEY CAN DO MASSAGES. But as there is no staff on site they will send whoever is on call and therefore, no appointments were open. Really annoying and badly planned. Trying to see how to attach photos as the photos I looked at before I reserved were much better than the real thing. AND I paid twice as much for my room as I should have given the CMAs were this week and I guess some people were still here.  But seriously, out of all the airport hotels I could have chosen, this was not the best choice. I think if I ever had to stay at an airport hotel again here I would just go with something like an Embassey Suites, at least you know it is low budget and probably better managed.  Really disappointed.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The Stage is a subpar bar with the best looking staff on Broadway. Go see those fellas for yourself.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: One of the best dive bars in Nashville. Music is sweet! Not loaded with crazy kids. Love this place. Bartender is one of the rising stars of the country music scene.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: My family went to Judge's on 08/30/2014 and it was very disappointing  the food was cold the ribs were small but cook nicely the brisket was half fat and the mac 'n cheese dry and cold right out of a box. The staff I don't know what to say it was bad bad and more bad.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Don't use the ATM machine. For the second  time now it's given me a receipt and no money. Worst part is when you ask the bar manager about it he tells you he'll give you a number to call. Really doesn't give a shit. He finally gave me my money and said, "Here. Now get the fuck out of here". Is that the professional way to handle the situation? Note: it was only $20 that I took out in order to pay the cover charge at the door. I'm sorry but if it's a repeating issue then it's no longer the ATM company's fault it's the club's wrong doing for keeping a faulty machine in there. More so, if you're going to charge cash only cover charges then you need to provide an ATM that works and doesn't dispense invisible money. Why is it still in there? Is it owned by the mob and there's nothing you can do about it? Get a new frickin' ATM. It's really not that difficult. And fire that belligerent, apathetic asshole of a bar manager and hire someone who takes customers getting ripped off seriously. Way unprofessional on two levels.  I expect more class from an establishment that's considered a staple of the music East Nashville scene. As a result I didn't stay, didn't spend money there, will probably never go back and now I'm writing this shitty review. Congratulations. Not giving a shit is so worth it.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Clean room, nice staff, got extra tea bags. Will definitely be staying again.

name: The Valentine
text:
Don't go here. The bouncers, security, and front door ID checkers are violent and abuse their power. I watched a guy (patron) get punched in the back of the head as he was leaving the venue  by a bouncer standing outside of the door. Then when the guy turned around to defend himself, three people from security took him to the ground and tased him... twice. This was excessive use of force, especially for people who aren't even police officers, and an abuse of power. Outsiders tried to help but were confused as to what was going on. Multiple people saw this whole encounter, but these bouncers think they can get away with it because they're attacking drunk people. It was really messed up. There are plenty of other bars on this strip with professional security. Beware.

Also, the drinks were awful and overpriced.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Very very nice beds and pillows and rooms. Really sweet staff. But the walls are so thin that any noise from next door is going to keep you up all night.

name: The 5 Spot
text: No complaints. It's a live music spot which I like. Patrons seemed to be nice enough. This particular night, there was no cover charge. They have alcohol too.

name: FooBar
text: Hate to be a party pooper, but total bummer night. The sound in the venue totally destroyed a couple of my favorite bands. More than half of the songs would have passed wonderfully as a shreds video. (Google it) Waiting over 15 minutes for beer and then having the bartender first whisper in his coworkers ear and then give me completely incorrect change kind of feels like a scam. The dudes on the street selling newspapers are running a better business.  I pray to all the gods of music that neither a band I love nor a friend's band ever have to play here again. Amen.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: This is the second hrc i have eaten at food was as good as expected and so was the service. Granted not busy at all while their. Prices were on point for a vacation spot.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Great atmosphere. Sat out on outdoor 2nd floor area. Service was good and very friendly. Bad part - food horrible. Ordered nachos and spring rolls. I could have gotten better at Taco Bell (I don't even like Taco Bell). Very disappointed in the food! Will not go back. The band was country. I know we're in Nashville but we're at the "Hard Rock" cafe. Expected rock band.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Went on a Sunday around lunch and it was dead. Radio played bizarre music, including children's dinosaur sing along something. Food was ok (not bad, not great). Service was good. Felt like the items on display were minimal and boring. There was nothing exciting about this location. Even though its chain, I was hoping for something special. VERY small gift shop area. For the price, go somewhere else for your meal.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Awesome service and great music. Highly recommend the moonshine drinks. Get there early as it seemed to get packed around 7pm.

name: The End.
text:
The End is Exit/In's grungier little brother who lives just across the street. But don't underestimate it! The End tends to host more DJ sets and music from heavier metal bands (so don't f* with it). 

I've been to some really great shows here. It's a perfect place to check out bands you're not familiar with, since the cover is usually really low and sometimes free. Inside is nonsmoking, but there's a generous outside smoking area with tables and chairs too. That side door is perpetually flying open, so some of it does carry inside. 

The bar is beer and redbull only so there's never a line or a wait for a drink. The parking lot is limited, but street parking is generally easy to find. I live in LA now, and I am so jealous of the amount of free street parking I had when living here. Enjoy it, Nashville!

Venues like The End make me so homesick for Nash. Music shows that are so accessible and enjoyable are the hallmark of the city. You really can't beat it.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Unfortunately I wasn't moved by the burger here. Our server was nice though and we received great service.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text:
My guy took me here on the first night I arrived. When we arrived, we were told the Kitchen closed early. The Night shift didn't show up, what a bummer. We decided to just have one drink and eat somewhere else then.

The two girls working the bar were funny and told us about this Smoked Dulce Vida Tequila they had smoked in house. I was so intrigued, we had to try it. She brought us a taste and it sold us on those drinks. Like a fine cocktail in a BBQ restaurant, it impressed me enough to want to come back the next day. 

So for lunch, we met at Judge's and sat at the bar again. We ordered a 2 way and a 3 way so we could try the different smoked meats. The flavor is beyond smokey and delicious. I'm a fan of brisket and loved the portion they gave me. It was so good, I barely added any sauce. 

Food was on hit. Those smoked margaritas are great and we loved this spot. Although I didn't finish it all, I took my leftovers back with me and finished them later. ;)

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Sheraton Music City Hotel is a good location for our last night in Nashville. We have a 6:00 AM flight and we need a hotel near the Airport. It is only around 5 minute drive and they also provides hotel shuttle starting from 4:00 am.

Rooms are dated. Still the old layout like most of the Sheraton in North America. Hopefully some renovation in the near future as it is just depressed to stay in a dated room.

No free wifi unless you are with their reward program and for Gold members and up, high speed connection is complimentary.

Since the weather was bad, so we ended up having a drink and a light dinner in the lobby restaurant. The price is reasonably for hotel meal and the food was a lot better than I expected.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: While in these trying times I can appreciate that clubs wish to maximize profits, still, at $8.50 for a whiskey drink, the customer would surely expect a decent pour in the Jack Daniel's & Coke he paid for. Total rip off; won't be coming back here. Ever! But the music was great!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Memorabilia was alright, though I expected more from the Nashville HRC...

Food was basic. Nothing exciting, and overpriced, if anything.

Waitress wanted to sell us stuff; said she'd get some accolade if we bought more stuff. She seemed to lose interest after only one person in our group said yes.

I had never been to a HRC, but always saw the shirts and figured there must be something special. After the Nashville trip, though, I feel that is a serious error. I wouldn't go back to the Nashville HRC. And frankly, I have no interest in visiting another one anywhere.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: I really liked this place. It's something new in the city of Nashville. They have something going on every night on stage such as salsa night and so on. However it still needs some improvement but overall it's a nice family hang out when an event is going on

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Gotta say, we love country music, but we sure learned a lot on this tour. We both remember watching The Grand Old Opry as kids along with Hee Haw, but I didn't know Bluegrass music started here. And, I really like Bluegrass too! 

The Ryman has a wonderful history that is presented exceptionally well through a back stage tour. Our friend Anne told us it was a must and we trust her opinion. She hit a home run with this recommendation! The transition The Ryman has been through is quite a story told very well. 

I must say I had my reservations before going to The Ryman since we were scheduled for a show at The Opry and a back stage tour the following night, but Wow... it was awesome! A piece of history that everyone should experience, including those not in love with country music! 

Our tour guide, I think his name was Justin, was outstanding and provided so much insight and character into his presentation! I highly recommend him for your tour. This was my favorite part of this trip to Nashville.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I saw Alt J here in September. I was in the second row of folding chairs. Not only were the seats incredible - minus the fangirling drunk 20 year old guy in front of me - but the sound was better than most venues I've been to and that's saying a lot. The staff is nice and gets the crazy girls who run up to the stage out which is also nice because no one wants to see you twerking.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Definitely a must-see. It's the mother church of country music for crying out loud! You can honestly feel how special this place is when you make your way into the auditorium. Being a former musician and singer (... for my high school band and chorus...), I definitely feel and understand the special place this landmark has in music, country or otherwise. It's very small, making for a more intimate environment. The "balcony" comes down pretty far, so I don't recommend sitting in the back section of the ground floor area if you actually want to see a show, but if you care more about listening to the music, I don't think it matters where you sit. Just walking around you can hear how different it sounds.

I recommend getting the Total Access pass at the visitor's center. You can visit 5 attractions for a fixed price, and you have a choice of different places (technically 4 because the Parthenon is a preset choice). This pass is $50 as of today, and a great deal if you use it correctly, especially if you want to see a lot of major attractions.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Good band, nice bartenders, good service on a thursday. Try the ring of fire as a shot. Yum.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Honky-Tonks, Live Music, Boot Stomping and Yee-Hawing are the crux of Nashville's historic downtown center. Broadway Street is like the Times Square or Fisherman's Wharf of Nashville; so yes, it is the 'tourist' area; but one needn't say it like that's a bad thing. As a visitor, you have to visit the tourist areas to get a feel for what I think of as the 'origin' story of a city. In San Francisco, it's the wharf; filled with ports and history, fresh seafood right off the boat and sourdough bread. In Nashville, it's Broadway; filled with honky-tonks, live country music all the time, history and legends. Our second stop in Nashville, was Robert's Western World, a fantastic honky-tonk with walls covered in memorabilia, cheap drinks and my first basket of fried pickles!

The Don Kelley Band was our 'band du jour' and they were amazing. They have been playing Roberts since the nineties. With an authentic country sound and unabashed honky-tonk vibe, they will make you want to get up and dance--or at least stand up and holler. Either way, they are a party waiting to happen.

If Shaun White and Stevie Ray Vaughn had a love child, Daniel Donato would be his name. Like a thunderclap from a clear blue sky, this 19 year old guitar player will bowl you over.

For a complete review with tons of photos, visit my site at: www.TNBTA.com

Cheers!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: If you want Mexican ambiance come here . I love here . Makes feel like I'm at my family Mexican parties

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The mother church of country music does not disappoint.  Every seat in there allows for the perfect musical adventure.  It is a cozy venue as well and you are immersed in the history of the place .  It is an amazing place to catch a show and you need to do so if you have yet to have the opportunity.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Acceptable bar food at a reasonable price. Not much choice...basically burgers and fries. Music was good given it was lunch time.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I did the self guided tour because it was close to closing and it was anticlimactic.  They charge for pictures on stage in addition to the tour cost.  

I'm sure if I had made it there early enough to do a guided tour it would have been better.  The place is beautiful in it's historic way.  I have a friend who is a songwriter and had a song played on the show Nashville in the Ryman so it was nice to view the auditorium from that prespective.  I'd go back again with others, but probably not on my own.

name: Robert's Western World
text: decideyournight.com kept recommending me to go to Robert's Western World and I'm glad I did. The fried pickles ARE TO DIE FOR!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Sambucca is a solid place for a night out. On my last visit there was live music. 

I ordered the pasta and my companion a steak. Both were tasty.

I had the sticky toffee pudding for dessert...it was a solid decision.

name: Robert's Western World
text: If you are visiting Nashville make sure you stop in for a burger and listen to some great country music. The night we were there the band was great. They had a 17 year old guitar player that was amazing. Food is cheap and the place is just plain ol' fun.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Really quirky place,  even for a place on Broadway. This has an older country feel and was my favourite spot in Nashville. The food was okay and drinks were cheap.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Overall terrible experience. To think we had a group of 20 to 30 people at a private event and the management lady was just unprofessional and completely rude. Not to mention had terrible communication skills. Complete waste of money and time. Stay away.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We had a great time here. The music was fantastic! Hope was our bartender and she took very good care of us while we were there. No cover charge to get in, just don't forget to tip the musicians and bartenders. This place is honky tonk legit, I would recommend going here before one of the touristy bars on Broadway.

name: Legends Corner
text: Lots of fun! We had quick service and the music was great.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Save your money. Not worth it. And if you have a party greater than 10, they will have a set menu for you and have you all pay a high amount. There are so many better places in Nashville to try for a better price. The lasagna was dry and cold. Please guys...save your money. Side note, the music is way too loud.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
DISCLAIMER: My review is based on my OWN personal experience and opinions ~~it has NO bias intent towards the company/business, the owners/managers or their employees. Please let YOUR OWN experience and views be your guide for enjoyment !!!!

Just got back from the Chris Daughtry Concert on Nov 16th, with my daughter Noel celebrating her 19th birthday. We had such a great time. The opening act was Bobby Church Band and then Daughtry put on a 2 hr show with encores..it was amazing..Rushing out tomorrow to buy his new CD/Album  "Baptized"...if you don't have it yet....GO BUY IT !!! Amazing entertainer...the best concert I have been to in years..

name: Robert's Western World
text: The food was GOOD, the beer was COLD and the music was GREAT!  It is a honky-tonk and it is FUN!   Nothing fancy...  but a GREAT honky-tonk dive bar.  Stop in and enjoy life!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Not a bad place seats are just uncomfortable and narrow. Definitely a every now and then event place.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Hot mess! This is a great alternative to the honky tonks up and down Broadway. If you're looking for a place with live music that plays a little bit of everything, this is your place. There's plenty of room to dance and the bar is pretty accessible.

There's also an upstairs area where you can enjoy drinks and food without all the chaos that is taking place downstairs. From here there's a great view of Broadway. 

Back in the day, their location on Demunbreun was my favorite spot for live music. It's nice to see they can bring the same good times to other locations.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Authentic honky tonk surrounded by tourist traps, apparently one of the few places on the strip still frequented by locals.  Fare is simple but good and more than reasonably priced.  Service is friendly if not always fast. Good for a late night but and some music.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Pretty mediocre live music on a Saturday eve...almost 30-40 minutes without any music when bands switched...cocktails were decent but nachos not upto the mark..either too soggy or completely bereft of any topping...so what could make this experience  worse? As we munch on the badly done nachos in a no-music background at around 11pm, the staff comes and makes everybody at the bar stand up since it's  supposedly  their time to pack up the bar stools..so highly unprofessional!

name: Second Fiddle
text: Live band.  Great bartenders.  Can't ask for much more in a bar.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This place was packed! Typical bar scene. Drinks were cold and refreshing after walking around Nashville on a 95 degree day. Band was good and up beat. Would probably stop by again. 4 stars since we didn't try the food.

name: Nashville Municipal Auditorium
text:
Went to see JOE & Fantasia for Valentines weekend.....

I absolutely hate this venue! It serves its purpose for hosting large sold out events but staff wise and seating are a hit or miss everytime. Price wise, well it just depends on who is going to be there and what day the concert falls on. Ours was on a Friday. Once we got inside  we headed to the concession stand to grab a hot dog and nachos. The girl behind the counter made our food with NO GLOVES on! which we were not having! So it took about 20mins to get our food. Seating is pretty much whoever gets there first if your not sitting in the floor section. Any higher seats are first come first serve.

The staff knew nothing about helping you find your. Plenty of security there so no drama. 

Will i return..?? probably not, i just think there are better venues for artist to show at.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
I'm really surprised there aren't more reviews for this place. Maybe it's new?

While walking through the crowds on Broadway, we were drawn in here because of their unique band/stage set-up. There were windows people could climb in to and be behind the band... some of the singers obliged people with selfies, etc. That looked fun enough, so we went on in.

The fun continued with pretty great bar service downstairs, and shots served in paper cups labeled "Medicine Cup" and with dosing lines. This was especially awesome because we were in town for a health related conference. The fireball shots and mixed drinks helped us have a reallll good time.

The band was awesome and played a mix of country and classic rock songs, and the place was crowded pretty early, which seemed like a good sign. Restrooms upstairs were large, clean, and simple. 

If I ever make it back to Nashville in my life, I'd be sure to hit this place up again.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Really like this place, great music, pretty good food, friendly waitstaff... out of all the options on Broadway the Tin Roof is a great place to stop

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This review is on the Ryman as a historical landmark to tour during the day.  We were only in town for a few days, and wanted to take in a show at the famed venue, but the only act that was performing while we were there was standing room only, and my bad back keeps me from being able to stand straight up for more that half an hour at a clip, so we took a pass, and came back the next day just to look around. Even if you aren't a huge fan of country music -- like me -- you have to have a healthy respect for the building's history and historical significance to American music in general.  It's part venue, part museum (gift shop included), and you're permitted to either look around on your own, and read the plaques in the cases, or take a guided tour, where the docent gives you some anecdotes about the Grand Ol' Opry, and the decades of entertainers that have graced it's stage.  Absolutely worth a stop, even if only for an hour.

name: Legends Corner
text: Great venue for music. The people who go this bar are really friendly. I also get a hot girl's number when I come here so it could be my place. It is one of my favorite bars on Broadway other than Tootsie's and Robert's Western World. I would recommend you to visit if you come to Nashville, the entire street of Broadway just walk it and find the bar or music venue you like I would recommend checking this place out it always has good live music.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Awesome place! My wife & I are visiting from out of state & two different friends recommend this place. The bartender Carolyn was very attentive & had a great attitude. Highly recommend!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Came here for a conference event.  The live music was great, service was awesome and the hot chicken and jalapeño mac 'n cheese were really good!

name: Legends Corner
text:
Not much to say here that others haven't said, other than, it is definitely a tourist trap, but the tourists are those in their mid-50's who want to be in their mid-20's, and think they still look like they are in their mid-20's. I went in, since our taxi driver said it was somewhere "everyone goes". he must get a lot of soccer moms and grandmas who want a good time while they visit Nashville, because this place was a hot mess!

Albums cover the walls and the bar doesn't serve any good beer. There is a mini stage in the corner where a live band plays. The band was decent, but that's about it.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I stopped here on the first night of my stay in Nashville. It was such a cool experience! A true honky tonk dive bar filled with people dancing, talking, live bluegrass music, funky wait staff and life.

There is never a cover charge but the band does come around with a bucket collecting tips. 

I ordered the garden burger and the fried pickles. The fried pickles were out of this world! The garden burger was stinky but i mean who orders a garden burger at a bar anyway?? In retrospect I would have gotten the fried bologna sandwich (as part of the $5 "recession special"). (See update below!!!)

Def check this place out! So much fun!

Update: I went back here and this time I got the fried bologna (the $5 Recession Special) and all I can say is WOW. Tasted like a grilled cheese but instead of cheese was cooked bologna. So so good. Highly recommend!

name: Robert's Western World
text: We went to about five honky tonks on Broadway on our trip to Nashville.  It's kind of something that I think you need to do when you visit Nashville. I had read somewhere that this was the best and most authentic of them all. And it was one of the best. The band was good and interacted with the patrons well. I liked all the boots on the wall. It was a nice touch.

name: Legends Corner
text: This was my favorite honky tonk bar... On a Saturday night, Legends was filled with young and cute country boys in dirty jeans, cheap drinks and great live music. On a Tuesday night, it was filled with elderly couples dancing and romancing to country music... with cheap drinks. It was a great time, and I'll definitely be back when I'm in Nashville.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great, fun time! We went on a Thursday night and there was plenty of space. Service was very friendly and fast and the BBQ brisket nachos were a hit with everyone at the table. Amazing band and fun atmosphere! Would definitely return and will recommend to anyone that also comes from out of town!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Awesome. Beautiful space, lots of food and drink options. Excellent place to watch World Cup.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is a great bar to hang out for good country music, some drink and a simple meal.  They don't offer draft beer but have fine bottled beer.  The Recession Special which includes a small sandwich, a bag of chips and a RBL for $5 is a good deal.  The inside is cool and dark.  The vibe is nice.  The bands performed there were the best we had on Broadway.  Some customers went on the stage to sing and boy, they were good!  We recommend this place to spend an afternoon and/or night.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This was my favorite bar in Nashville. The music is the best. It's real honky tonk, old school style country music. Many places claim to be a honky tonk but they only have terrible cover bands playing pop music and modern country music. Places like that are a dime a dozen in Nashville but, Roberts is the true gem of downtown Nashville. Awesome and attentive staff that chatted us up during our visit and some damn fine sandwiches on the menu. Can't beat the $2.50 Miller High Life either. Make sure you go early and check out the house band. They really get everyone dancing and singing. 

Bottom line, I spent a week in Nashville and should have just went here every night. You should do the same. Do not go to the other over crowded bars just go to Roberts!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I made reservations for this Sambuca outing in honor of my friend's bachelorette party. This restaurant has special meaning to her because she went on several dates with her fiancé there while they were dating. We had a really special night. Some rad blonde girl was belting out some killer tunes with her band that were totally mood appropriate. We had calamari and the shrimp crab dip for appetizers and both were pretty good. The bride got the salmon dish and she LOVED it. The other dish that seemed to be a hit at the table was the filet with the Gorgonzola walnut butter. YUM. I (and one other pal) got the ribeye and it was unremarkable. The other guest got the lobster enchilladas and she wasn't all that keen on them. So to sum up, we had: excellent appetizers, a few solid entrees, good cocktails (apparently there is a berry dragon cocktail that everyone loved), and killer tunes. The ambiance rocks. Worth the trip for sure.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Loved our server. Cumcumber pineapple drink was delicious. My entree was the scallops with risotto -- So perfect. Scallops were cooked perfectly and paired great with the risotto and asparagus.

name: Legends Corner
text: A fun honky-tonk with cool decor. The drinks are cheaper next door at Robert's however. But if you don't mind paying a little more and listening to covers of less traditional country, it's a good time.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: An Absolutely great place to visit.  The tour was really very informative and filled with an energetic video before you walked through the auditorium.  Really a great place to visit.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: FYI buy a beer do not buy a mix drink.  They Do not now how to pour a mix drink.  Do yourself a favor and go down to the whiskey bent saloon for a real drink.  $7 for a coke with no alcohol.  I wonder why no one was drunk when I was there at midnight.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: For me, while the food was fine and the wait staff attentive, the atmosphere was just weird.  Dimly lit with blood red accents and one of the worst bands I've ever heard.  In 'Music City' of all places, you don't expect (or I don't expect) to hear the 'easy listening' top forty sounds of the '70's delivered in the most bland way possible. Think Seals and Crofts, Bee Gees and ELP played by a band in a nursing home.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Not my best experience. The band seemed in the bottle for a Monday night and my wife and I got sick from there French Onion Soup Special. Sorry but thumbs down all around on this one!  Should have known better.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: First home of the Opry and amazing history!  The video at the start of the tour was very entertaining and informative!  Awesome spot!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I visited the Ryman on a venue tour because there were no performances that we wanted to see while we were in town for the weekend. And while the tour was interesting, this really is a place that you need to experience, not just go look at. Therefore, I'm going to make an effort to see a show at the Ryman the next time I visit Nashville. Its acoustics is suppose to be superb making it one of the best places in the world to see a show. 

The museum tour starts with a video with the history of the Ryman and how evolved from a gospel tabernacle to the Mother Church of Country Music. The rest is a self guided tour of the auditorium, where there are selected artifacts from its history. It's fascinating and this place is full of history and stories. Definitely worth a visit, especially if you can't get in for a performance. 

Really looking forward to seeing a performance at the Ryman the next time I visit Nashville. Review will be updated, and I'm confident I'll be changing my rating to 5 stars!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Went in on a Friday night and the band was bloody brilliant! The double bass player (which in my opinion is a dying art in this electronic world) was amazing. Unfortunately, I didn't catch the name of the band, but they played proper old school country honky tonk...which was just what this uncountry, english girl was looking for while in Nashville!

Not only that, the $6 burgers were fantastic. One of the best burgers I've had in years. Beers are $4, and there is no cover charge. However, be prepared to fork out a few dollars every hour when the band comes begging. I quickly learned that if the bar didn't charge a cover you're going to pay about $5 per hour per table of 4 people (less if you don't love the band, but you still have to remember that these talented musicians don't get paid a penny to work in these bars because the competition is so stiff). The band on Friday night (later on) recommended a tip of $10 to $20  per hour, but I think that was wishful thinking!

We went back on Sunday night, which was much quieter and the band was good, but not as good as the Friday night band, but the burgers and service were just as good. This was our favourite bar on Broadway without a doubt.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: live music at lunch time, Chicken tenders are amazing... Best lunch downtown

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
The food looked better than it taste!! If you are not a fan of dill be careful ordering the dishes with dill, it can be over powering. The drinks and Appetizer's were very good! Our server Jordan was excellent and he did everything within his ability to assure that we enjoyed ourselves. 
My future visits will consist of Appetizer's and Alcohol. Can't go wrong with this combination.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Every time I come to Nashville I have a great time at The Second Fiddle. This trip proved no differently. I was in town with my husband in mid September. Brandi Thorton was awesome on Thursday night, her voice is unbelievable. The bartender had a really big fantastic smile & she was very nice to us. We've been coming in for years & we were pleasantly surprised to see Megan when we went back on Friday. All the staff is friendly & kinda silly (one guy behind the bar was hilarious) and seem to get along well (cutting up, working hard, laughing and smiling all night) which makes it an even better place to be. Seems more like a family working together. This is not a Honky Tonk anybody should be skipping past when visiting Nashville.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This is the tour to go on while in Nashville.   It is a beautiful former church turned concert hall.  A film starts the tour to tell the history.   And what a rich history it had.  Walking through the building feels thick of spirits of the fine country musicians in time gone by.

There is an opportunity to get on the stage for a photo.  I didn't look to see how much that cost but many in my group did it.  The gift shop is very nice and full of treasures. 

The Ryman is still used for concerts and events.  It seems like a very nice venue for music.  If you are in Nashville check it out.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I don't love the new construction (just doesn't fit with the aesthetics of the previous design), but this is my favorite place for a concert. With the exception of the last 6 or so rows on the main floor, there's not a bad seat in the house.

name: Second Fiddle
text: My family and I went on a Friday afternoon.  It was not busy at all.  My card was overcharged by the bartender when adding the tip.  It could have been an honest mistake or it could have been skimming.  I had to call the establishment.  They apologized, but should have offered compensation for the error in my opinion.  The overcharge was not excessive, but it's the principal of the matter.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Good ole music and good cold beers. Cheapest beer on the Broadway strip. Come and cool off and sit for a spell ya hear...

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great drinks with the best server named Evan. Happy hour more than worth it here. Great  music by the Jacob Reynolds band.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We went to Sambuca to celebrate our daughter's 16th birthday.  The food was all very good.  The place is expensive but we knew that going in.  All of the entrees were great:  Shrimp and Crab Scampi, Filet and Lobster tail, Salmon Oscar, Blackened Flatiron, and regular Filet.  The only thing we found underwhelming was the side of Dill Havarti Potato Tots. The ONLY warning: be aware of the live music, and ask to be seated away from the stage if you want to me able to chat.  But if it's just my hubby and me, we will probably want to sit there and enjoy the live music.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
In my opinion the obstructed view could really be a lot worse. I mean it's something I will avoid in the future, but if I found really great ticket prices for a show I really wanted to see I would definitely not have issues purchasing them because of this fact. The Ryman's amazing acoustics more then make up for the lack of being able to see who is playing fully. The place  is unique and definitely a must for any person who appreciates sound. Plus it's old school, no usher was under the age of 60. 

My only qualms are with the weirdness of live music crowds in Nashville. I still cannot get over it.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I'm sure this is a great place to see a show, but the hour tour for 25 bucks is a rip off.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
After walking around Broadway for about a good hour to find a place to eat, we landed here. They had good live music and the servers were cool. 
My friend and I ordered the Mac and cheese, hot tater tots, and chicken and jack quesadillas. My favorite of all the 3 was the Mac and cheese (soooo good). We also had A shot called "F-n-8", not that good, it was too sweet. The bathrooms needed a touch up. I'd go back to have the Mac and cheese again !

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
My (awesome) job hosted our annual Holiday (Christmas) party here this year. The space is nice, but not amazing. The service was alright. And the food was.... blah at best.

Unfortunately this just isn't the place I would recommend or spend my time. I got a three course meal - started with a crab bisque - the cream wasn't cooked down enough and wasn't really edible. The second course was pretty good though- medium rare filet was seasoned and cooked well. The side of asparagus was ok, lower quality veg and the au gratin potatoes were salty, cold and were over cooked. 

Nashville is an awesome city- and there are so many places with great food or music. Dont waste your time or money going here. Sorry!

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place has one of the best burgers on Broadway! It's super cheap and you get to listen to great live music while you're there. There's just something about Robert's that draws you in; we ended up staying for more than 3 hours. The crowd tends to be older but everyone is usually really friendly and fun. We sat upstairs and had a great time drinking and dancing with everyone around us. The bar tender was nice but not the most attentive, we often had to ask several times to get something. But, I would gladly come back.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We really enjoyed the tour!  It was around 45 minutes and very informative.   We are not huge history bluffs but this was interesting!  Great history on The Grand Ole Opry.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Came here based on the rave yelp reviews and I have to say, was disappointed!

Very divey and quite dirty. Hard to get drinks at the bar as extremely overpacked (yes, many bars are overpacked in Nashville on a Saturday night, but this one was moreso than others, no elbow room whatsoever)

They had some very disgusting deep fried food with an open kitchen in front of the bar, so you could see the guy removing frozen nuggets from a fridge and deep frying them in front of you. And frying up bologna sandwiches at the same time. Bizarre.

Waitresses were friendly and drinks were quite cheap though. Live music was good.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We live in the icon across the street and have always enjoyed sambuca's until the last visit. We had a birthday celebration and several preteen kids. They ordered from the small plates and we chose outside since they were with us. It was a very large group and several ordered drinks. I did not see the bill but when I reviewed later we were overcharged 60 something dollars. I wrote a letter to the manager and have been ignored. I enjoy the food there and the atmosphere but cannot believe I had no response to my communication. Will NEVER go back

name: Robert's Western World
text: This dive honky tonk bar is the read deal! We came during the afternoon and listened to live music and are a recession special of a PBR, fried bologna sandwich and chips for 3.50. They also have burgers and hot dogs. This is s music institution. The food is mediocre but the atmosphere and music are five stars!

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is a true gem of a honkey tonk on Broadway.  It was recommended to me by both visitors and local's.  Great music and standard bar, cheap eats too, burgers, etc.  I'm rating it only 4 stars because I found the evening bar staff to be a little bitchy and neglecting.  I'm sure they are all jaded by the constant tourists, but it wasn't the most welcoming of service.  Overall great experience though!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great place for live music and a great bite to eat. Very very good food, and they have a great variety on the menu. Great location in the gulch and great staff. Definitely recommend!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This s*cks to choose "a-ok" (3 stars) v. "Yay! I'm a fan" (4 stars). Yet, based on our experience... :( 

I was SUPER looking forward to traveling back to Nashville and trying the fried bologna after seeing it highlighted on a Food Network show. And how perfect - getting to do so while listening to some live classic country after a weekend in Brentwood. 

The fried bologna was okay; just not as great as it had gotten built up in my mind. There was a little too much bread v. the amount of bologna. Hubs' burger was evidently also okay - although it looked really good!

Perhaps what most negatively influenced the experience - in turn generally impacting the overall experience - was service. Our gal was nice, just not the most attentive server in the world. Had it been a shoulder-to-shoulder Friday or Saturday night, I'm confident it'd been less of an issue (we'd have understood); however, it was an early Sunday afternoon with many open tables and spots at the bar. That being so, I don't want to have to carry my arse across the place to ask for refills. Get your "bar eyes" on and take care of your guests! 

We'll try again. It's Robert's Western World in d'town N'Ville for God's sake.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We had an 8:30 reservation and were able to be seated early, 8:00.  The five star review is fir the food and service.  Our waiter was great.  The veggie lasagna is amazing, different than a traditional lasagna.  My husband enjoyed the ribeye, but it only came with one scallop. The waiter offered to bring one more scallop, as the dish only comes with one scallop.  The downside is where we sat.  We sat upstairs in the glass rooftop room. It was unbearably loud.  I could not wait to leave because of the noise.  I was hoping for a more intimate experience for an anniversary dinner. They do have music, bands that play. If you go, make sure you ask about seating if you don't want to be in the loud rooftop room.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I made my first trip to Sambuca on 12/10/14 and loved it. I met a group of ladies for happy hour and had a great experience.
First, it was not busy on this particular evening, so we had a very easy time finding seating. The bar area has several couches and over-sized chairs and tables in addition to regular tables/chairs and seats at the bar. The entire restaurant was very clean and decorated very nicely. The atmosphere was very warm and welcoming; all of the staff I talked to were extremely friendly and seemed happy to be there. This being Nashville, you can always find someone singing/playing and this place is no exception; a singer with a nice selection of Christmas music. Parking is also ample and very easy to find; there are 2 pay parking lots 1 block away - I paid $2 for 2 hours - completely reasonable. 
Good happy hour specials with a fun selection of drinks and appetizers; the food was excellent. I had the mac & cheese with prosciutto - a small plate but was more than enough for me and it was delicious.
I will definitely be back to Sambuca!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I am not a country music fan so the history of the Ryman doesn't thrill me as much as it would someone who loves the music. I did enjoy the movie that started the tour as it gave great background information. I wish the backstage tour was available today, but it wasn't. Worth a stop, whether you are a country music fan or not. Oh, and one of the best part was that they have a Tennessee appreciation deal going - by one, get one - for their regular tours.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I came here for a Melanie Martinez concert and let me just tell you that it was a very overwhelming experience. I had purchased the VIP package and found out that there had been a huge mix up with the VIP seating. I will say that the employees were doing their best to handle the situation and I really appreciate that. They were calm and courteous, but were not able to help that much until we kept badgering them. It would have greatly helped to have been updated more on the issue. We ended up having to sit far in the back but we got refunded. The place was nice and clean. The main drawbacks were in that it felt sort of unorganized. There didn't seem to be much streamlining, although it is a pretty big place, but the lines for purchasing merch from the artist and other lines were all over the place. Overall it was fun and there isn't much else to say. A lot of this will depend on the artist performing and their personal team, so the employees handling the events here can only do so much, but they could step it up.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Went to celebrate our wedding Anniversary & it couldn't have been better. 

From our waiter, Jesse, who went beyond the definition of server to make our night special, to the Stacy Mitchhart Band, playing us a funny song for the occasion, the entire night was fantastic. 

The Bucca Beignets appetizer was a perfect way to start along with a glass of wine & a Cock'n'Bull (their take on a Moscow Mule)

The Spinach salad and the Crab/Shrimp Bisque really wet our appetite for what was to come. 

We had the Miso Sea Bass, which had an Asian zing flavor with the bed of apple & cabbage stir fry & the 7 oz filet with the Brussel sprouts. Both were prepared to perfection. 

We finished with a White Chocolate Cheesecake that really topped off a perfect night.  

Overall a truly superb evening out. Thanks to the Sambuca team for making this Anniversary dinner a tough one to top for years to come.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Hands down my favorite music venue we visited in Nashville! I am not a huge fan of modern country myself, but as someone who has switched from classic violin to country fiddle, I've definitely found an appreciation for honky tonk and that's what you're going to find here. 

The bar itself is small and long, pretty no frills, and lots of quirky, fun, and unique decorations adorn the walls. They have a bottom floor/bar as well as a top floor/bar. Lots of tables for seating and room to dance up front near the band! We found it was easier to get a seat on Wednesday night than it was on Thursday night and one of our Uber drivers said that was pretty true to his experiences as well. When we arrived on Thursday, the place was packed (shoulder to shoulder) and we couldn't move in or out. Kind of just got stuck in the flow of traffic. Wednesday was great though! 

Food is bar food. I had some french fries. Friend had a burger, chips, and mozzarella sticks. No one tried the fried bologna sandwich- we didn't realize it's like THEIR THING. I guess someone will have to try it if we ever head back. I'll update and let ya know. Otherwise, it looks like there's 600 other reviews... someone has probably tried it ;)

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
It's all about the people !

My wife and I were exploring the Gulch on our last day of vacation in Nashville. It was extremely hot out so we stopped in to have a couple of iced teas when we were greeted by Dawn. She seated us with a big southern smile and within minutes we were sipping our tea and talking with her about how great Nashville is and why most folks who live here never leave.

Time had slipped away through pleasant conversation about travel experiences when I realized we had a flight to catch and asked Dawn if she would call us a cab to get us back to our hotel. She gladly made the call but almost 30 minutes had passed and no taxi in sight. We were running out of time and were stressing about the possibility of missing our flight.

Without the blink of an eye Dawn insisted on driving us back to the hotel in her car. My wife and I were shocked by her generous offer and took her up on it. I tried to offer her gas money, but she refused and said it was karma. We have been around a little but never experienced kindness and generosity as we have from her. 

We were in a town full of celebrities, but never knew what it was like to treated as one.

Kudos to you and your great city, Dawn !

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Well with five stars says it all .. great music great drinks and great food .. trifecta all at one location ... I highly recommend this restaurant for you and the spouse....

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
As you can see from all of the other 1 star reviews, Sambuca has a service and management issue. How is their food? I have no idea, here is why:

Reservation was made for 12:15, we were seated promptly. Some chairs were broken, odd start, but we switched them out and were ready to order. 

12:20 - Waitress stops by and does the usual 'I'll be right back for drink orders'

12:50 - Yes THIRTY minutes later she's back to take our drink orders. She said sorry it was swamped in the kitchen. Odd comment from a waitress... this is when we started suspecting our waitress was doubling as a line cook. We place our drink and food orders at this time, the hanger is beginning.

1:00 - Band finishes and we realize we've been here nearly an hour and don't see food on anyone else's plates. We chat with the table behind us and they explain they've been waiting 1.5 hours and haven't had food. We worry, we had a 2 o'clock appointment to be at.

1:01 - We see a manager, let's call him Brad. Brad just got done talking with a couple who was very disappointed with the service. Brad explained that the kitchen was understaffed and offered to take their names and talk to them later.

1:02 - We flag down Brad. Explain that we've been waiting a while and haven't gotten anything besides water yet, and are fearful we're going to miss our appointment. Brad says when is the appointment? We say 2. Brad says 'you might get your food by 2'. THAT'S NOT GUNNA WORK Brad. We got here at 12:15 and at 1:02 you're telling us our food MIGHT get here in an hour? I would understand if we ordered a freaking paella with a molten lava cake, but we just got breakfast basics.

1:03 - We explain our concerns to Brad and he offers to check in with the kitchen the get an estimate. At this point I should mention we were told our tip was included so they didn't really seem to want to please us.

1:10 - No sign of Brad returning to our table (but we do SEE Brad, boy is he dodging us). No one is eating around us. we went and got our waitress and explained that we know it's not her fault but we have no confidence that our food is coming and that when it does it will have been worth waiting for and missing our pressing appointment. We leave and go to ADELE's up the street who sat us immediately and fed us - which is all we ever wanted!

In sum, how is the food? Unclear. Is it cooked by double agent waitresses? Potentially. Is it worth finding out? Nope.

name: Robert's Western World
text: When everything else is too crowded you can get a place in Roberts, however, not the first choice for prime music And Nashville and honky tonk atmosphere!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I've been going to this place for years! It's always spot on. I had my husbands birthday dinner here (upstairs, overlooking the Gulch) and we just recently went for Mother's Day Brunch. The food is always delicious and the service is GREAT! We opt'd for Sambuca because our kids had never experienced dinner with LIVE music and luckily we were seated right up front, that was a real treat for them to watch.

Happy Hour: I haven't been to HH in a few years but it was always great Martini specials and good food, I'm sure that hasn't changed. 

Parking: this is the reason for the -1 star! It started off with free valet, then it was 3 bucks, then 5, then 10 and now it's 12 or 13. Really? It's not the most expensive restaurant, but it's not cheap either, I think they should validate your parking or at least subsidize the price.

Overall, very nice place anyway of the week to listen to some good music (outside of country music, thankfully...since you can get that anywhere in the Ville) and good food and drinks.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
What can I say that hasn't been said.  We took a self guided tour which was just perfect; it wasn't crowded which was nice to really look around 
The ticket purchased included a photo on stage.  
Beautiful theatre rich in history.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Bang for your buck: 7/10
Quality: 10/10
Service: 10/10
Ambiance/Location: 10/10
Overall: 9/10

A Nashville staple! This is a must see when visiting the home of country music. Our only critique is the price. It's a bit on the pricier side for a self-guided tour, but it's worth forking over the cash to get  this slice of history!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Bad experiensce for us. Limited food menu is way overpriced. Ignored by our waiter. The only thing we liked was the music. Never again!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
At the Ryman for Live From Here with Chris Thile, courtesy of a Christmas present from my hubby's younger son! 
It's a classic old auditorium with seating resembling old wooden church pews, 4 people to a section. Although we couldn't see the far right of the stage, but there doesn't appear to be a bad seat in the place!
Tonight's guests are David Rawlings, Courtney Barnett and comedian Neal Brennan. We had a great time!

name: Musicians Corner
text:
This is GREAT! Free concert out in the park. Doesn't get much better. I happen to just be walking the dog and noticed a line of food trucks.

First big plus for having the food trucks. There were easily a dozen and with the exception of maybe two trucks short lines and great food. 

There were a few little shopping booths set up as well as a play area for kids. 

The music wasn't spectacular but I couldn't think of a better way to spend an afternoon sitting on the grass listening to some local tunes. AND did I mention it was free? All I needed  to pay for was my feed from the food truck.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This place hosted my favorite night on the Honkey Tonk strip! on Wednesday nights they always have a named "Reckless Sidemen" and they are amazing. So, enjoy some food, drinks l, and dancing here! Have a good time! Now, when I say dancing.. this place wasn't packed and rowdy, but  there was space to  could bust a move. I really enjoyed the jalapeñorita A LOT! The cool cucumber taste with a hot finish was actually subtle and the most sophisticated drink i've been served in a plastic cup. The hot chicken had a great spicy flavor, but was a little too hot to enjoy for me personally. The hotness actually made the nachos taste sweet! I think there is another band upstairs, but I didn't check it out. I highly recommend coming here!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I would love to give Sambuca a 5-star rating, but our server (I think his name was Keith) was not good. He gave us a 20-minute explanation of the menu (a few highlights/specials would have been sufficient). He only came back everyone once in awhile to check on us (and didn't look like he had many tables). All of that could have been overlooked, but the way our dining experience ended was just completely rude. Booking on Open Table, it was clear that we had a two hour limit. He pulled my friend aside and said "I need this table in 5 minutes, so you need to pay your tab." We had already got the tab and were paying. I understand why the policy exists, but between the 4 of us we spent over $300 for dinner/drinks. It seems a bit like a money grab to turn tables quickly versus having an enjoyable experience. The band (Patton James) was AMAZING!! I would go back again, but would likely sit in the bar area where we wouldn't be treated so rudely. Sad, it's a great place, and the food was amazing! I hope the manager takes this opportunity to teach the staff how to politely turn tables...especially those spending a ton of money.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This IS Music City. The heart of Nashville can be found beating at Robert's Western World where locals and tourists mingle together. Come during the day, and you'll hear singers and song writers. Come at night, and the band will be playing some of your favorites and some of their own stuff. I heard the food is good. Drinks are basic but good and rails are strong. People are dancing and talking and all having a good time.
