We went at night and the next day because we loved how authentic and genuine this place is unlike some its neighbors. You can't miss RWW.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is by far our favorite spot in Nashville! Small, crowded, dancing & most importantly GREAT honky tonk music! This place brings in the characters so it's great for people watching and letting your hair down.
We always creep our way to sit at the bar in Becky's section, they are crazy busy but she makes sure to take care of you no matter what if she can see you! 
If you can't find a spot, there are stairs in the back righthand corner that lead up to the balcony... not a lot of service happening up there usually, but a trip up and down the stairs to grab another beer is worth it! 
Oh... the food. I am about to tell you the food is not good.... but I'm also gonna tell you that we end up eating here every time! haha! Its kind of like the burger you used to get in the school cafeteria.. I don't know if they have anything but a burger or not.... but we always stay long enough we NEED that blah hamburger and let's be honest.... who cares at that point, I'm just glad we can get food without leaving!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Weekend trip to Nashville brought us to staying in the Gulch and I have been very impressed. Sambuca has a great vibe. Dim lighting made for a elegant evening but the live music was worth it! The band and lead singer was phenomenal! Food was incredible and was worth every penny! We had the popular appetizer, salmon, and the polenta entree! Fantastic evening!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: This is one of the best meals that I've had in a long time. Robbie absolutely killed it. The service was perfect, his suggestions were on-point and the food was incredible. For a great date night, I'd suggest sitting outside upstairs as we did. Do yourself a favor and order the shrimp dip app and chili-rubbed scallops for an entree. Unreal.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Our waiter at Jimmy Buffets Margaritaville told us not to miss stopping in to Roberts and he was right. Best music on the street and I popped into every honky Tonk.  Crowded, everyone dancing, the Don Kelley band was entertaining and talented- bought a CD, worth the visit to hear them play.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We had came here on a Friday afternoon as our first spot. I really enjoyed the music but the service was not the best. The waiter we had was attentive to every other table and left us hanging a majority of the time. However the live music was awesome and I would come back for the music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Great place, so glad I found it...
I had the BLTAE. Bacon lettuce tomato avocado and egg

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Stopped in for cocktails . The Sambuca 75 was very intoxicating and delicious. The service was great. We were the first to open the place so it was very quiet, which was nice. We did not eat so I can only speak for the cocktails and the service. So try the drink next time you are there. It is like a cosmopolitan in a way but with a kick. Enjoy!

name: Robert's Western World
text: We went in for a  late night fried bologna sandwich and ended up staying for the music. Broadway is overflowing with hokey honky tonks filled to the brim with drunk tourists, but Robert's Western World seemed different somehow. Of the four or five bars that we went to, this was easily my favorite. Not a bad sandwich, either! The fries weren't great, though. I'd say skip 'em for a second sandwich.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Great show with Michelle Obama & Stephen Colbert. Only complaint is that after the show started, there were pics on the large screen behind Michelle that did not come up on the smaller screens we looked at . We had to duck our heads  if we were gonna see those pics. Only people in front area and balcony I guess  got to see those.  I think this was a mistake made on Ryman's  part.  Guess they couldn't fix it once the show got rolling.
But still a great show in a favorite venue.  Always. I love my Ryman outings and always forgive  the little things. We are so fortunate to live near here.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Sunday around noon. On the stage a good mariachi band is playing. There are boutique stores and restaurants, some just beverage joints. There's a Latino market on the north entrance and inside you can get Mexican food from a steam table -- it's pretty good. Attached to the market is a Colombian restaurant called La Sobrasura Colombiana. The lady speaks no English but I manage to order the Picadas. I am surprised at the $19 cost, but when I get it I understand -- it's huge, way too much for one person, and it's almost all meat -- four kinds of meat! I imagine it's an inexpensive alternative to a Brazilian steak house. Plaza Mariachi could use more restaurants serving food, and fewer boutiques. It will probably grow, but right now it's mostly the curious walking around not knowing what to do with themselves. I'll be back and check out more of the food options, especially at La Sobrasura!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Recently I was at the Ryman for Marty Stuart's Late Night Jam on  a Wed. night in June 2019.  It was wonderful.  I love that the Ryman is so close to Music Row, where all the honky tonk bars are located, all with live music all the time.  This historic theater has good proportions and a good, small-to-medium size, allowing for lots of connection between performers and the audience.  It feels intimate.  One thing to be aware of:  seats on the ground level, in the rear, have vertical posts as obstructions, detracting from one's enjoyment of the show.  So try to avoid getting a seat in the rear half of the lower level.  This theater embodies the history of country music.  It's a national treasure.  Highly recommended.

name: Second Fiddle
text:
First stop on Broadway this afternoon. It's a loud venue, but they sound mix to the back of the bar. So fight your impulse to sit up front and center if you're a true live music fan. 

I have a standard amaretto on the rocks, so I can't tell you if the bar tender is any good. This is a place to have beer / shots. Maybe don't expect anything classy. 

Had a bathroom run... no toilet seat covers and the toilet seats make you feel like you need them. But that's pretty standard for most popular bars.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Lots of fun and authenticate environment. Great food and definitely recommend. Can't wait to go again. Shop the markets and enjoy the shows.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great girls weekend to celebrate a birthday. Amanda was so helpful with the menu and drink selection. Service was on point! Definitely a go to place when you're in town!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I came early on a Saturday night so I didn't experience the "Sardine Experience" people were talking about. I got a local beer (Yazoo Hef) which was awesome and so reasonably priced. They have PBRs for 2.50. Coming from the Bay Area, that price is pretty unheard of. The band I saw was extremely talented--they apparently had an original song that was featured on the show Nashville. I don't watch the show so I don't know much about it. 

Anyway, I know folks say this is touristy but I enjoyed my experience. You can't deny the great music, cheap drinks, and awesome vibes.

name: Second Fiddle
text:

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place is just magical! Only place I'm willing recommend on broadway. Gives you the feeling of old Nashville when everything around is changing so much. The live music is always fantastic. Just read the incredible life story of JesseLee Jones (the owner), he is truly a Nashville legend and you can see him play! Also had the pleasure of checking out Sunday Morning Gospel--a church service on Sunday morning with a gospel band, no alcohol is served from 10:30am-12pm. They even had free coffee and coffee cake. Very special experience, I will be back!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Terrible service just like the Orlando location. They weren't busy but just ignored us while we waited for a drink. Music was great and fun but the staff here has no business on Broadway in Nashville.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Sunday Brunch here was fantastic!!

Stephanie Athington(sp?) band was unbelievable. Highly recommend if you like the classic Sinatra,Bublè and others. 

 Highly recommended! Stephanie's band is unreal! Well done, please bring them back Sambuca!

name: Robert's Western World
text: My husband has been talking about this bologna sandwich for YEARS. I finally got a chance to try it and it was perfect way to end a night on Broadway. The music and crowd were great, and overall the bar was a fun experience.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: It's the Mother Church of Country Music-that in itself creates feelings of history and reverence. We visited last night for the Alabama Christmas show, and were incredibly disappointed when Alabama cancelled due to illness and they did not replace them with another headliner. Also-the Christmas show was only 3-4 Christmas songs. The church pews are of course, appropriate, however hard as rocks! The Humana advertisements were absolutely ridiculous in number-we all should have left with refunds from them since there was no headliner. Anywho-it's the Mother Church of Country Music.

name: Music City Center
text: Such an awesome venue.  Been here three times in the last couple of years for different events.   Beware of the Dublin Donuts located inside the center.   Staff is very very very very very very rude.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great drinks, great people, great music! First time in Nashville & this is a must stop. You will not be disappointed grabbing a cheap drink overlooking the best view we've seen so far.

name: Music City Center
text: This arena is used for concerts, sporting events and exhibitions. In fact, the weekend we visited there was a National Volleyball tournament, a log home show and a concert! The space is open, clean and visually appealing. Great venue in downtown Nashville.

name: Legends Corner
text: Great music & great beer; atmosphere is worth coming to & is a spot that hasn't been commercialized. Would recommend as a top 3 spot

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text: What a great spot for live music. You can tell that this place is rich with history and culture. It has a bit of a spooky, haunted vibe. The stage is stellar, as is the sound. The bartender was super friendly and accomodating. The food was meh; I probably would not recommend eating there. However, all of the cool things about this spot make up for it.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Cool place nice music drinks a little week. Great roof top in the middle of downtown.

name: Legends Corner
text: Honestly if you want to have a good time, don't come here. They are nasty, awful, bitchy bartenders.

name: Robert's Western World
text: A great place to escape the summer heat on Broadway. There's always great live music and the staff is super friendly. Don't miss the balcony / second floor. There are more seats and a separate bar up their with a view of the stage. It's not fancy, but definitely fun.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
You won't find a bad seat in the house at the Ryman.  You can see the stage from wherever you are, and the sound is great each and every time I've ever been.  It's a smaller venue, so it's perfect for people that don't care for a massive amount of people or have anxiety issues with large crowds.  
The only negative I have about the Ryman is that the old wooden floors underneath and in between the church pew seating was very thickly covered in filth.  They were swept--but desperately needed cleaning.  If large people are in the pew and women have to put their purse on the floor,  it's just nasty.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: When my friend from Austin came to visit me in Nashville, I was looking for activities we could do around the city. Touring the Ryman was at the top of my list! We went on a Saturday afternoon for the self-guided tour. It was so worth it! I didn't know anything about the history of the Ryman, and the self-guided tour starts with an entertaining and informative video. I had NO idea that the Ryman was almost torn down and was vacant for years after the Grand Ole Opry moved from the building! After the video, you can walk around the Ryman, sit in the pews, take photos of the amazing architecture, including the gorgeous stained glass. In the stairwell of the auditorium, there are several panels that detail the history of speakers and performers at the Ryman over the years! Once you get down to the first floor of the auditorium, they have dresses, guitars, hats, etc. worn by famous performers at the Ryman. The self-guided tour is $20 - but it's worth it! It's one of the most fun things I've done in Nashville! I learned a lot about the city, the Ryman, and country music! (There's also a guided backstage tour that is $30.) Tons of fun! Highly recommended!

name: Robert's Western World
text: We visited multiple times while we were in Nashville, and Robert's is definitely the best music venue in that area. Free cover, cheap beers/food and good music. Service can be slow, but everyone is nice and it wasn't a problem. Tip the musicians because it's free cover.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
DID NOT SEE A SHOW. ONLY DID A TOUR. 

The tour starts out great with a well done video of how the Ryman started and became what it is today. After the video, the tour takes you around the auditorium to look at memorabilia and watch a few videos. The costumes were neat, but the price of admission was too high for how little there is to see.

If you're not a huge country buff and know little about the Ryman, my recommendation is to save your money for a better attraction.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I. Love. This. Place. 

Such a amazing venue, the history here is incredible. For shows, I would suggest getting balcony seating unless you are looking at the first few rows.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I was so disappointed in Sambuca this trip. I've been several times before and enjoyed it. However, this time was awful. Our waiter, while nice, seemed like he was yelling at us and called my parents "brother" - my mom was uncomfortable. The drinks were probably the highlight of dinner. We ordered and when our food arrived it was so average. My salmon was barely warm and the Brussel sprouts were almost raw. The rest of the table ordered steaks and they were so over seasoned no one could finish. The band was fun as usual but seemed too loud for dinner. I have no plans to return to Sambuca unless under new management or chef supervision.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
The Good: Quality of food; experience; service; selection.

The Bad: notta

The Rest: One of my favorite stops in Nashville. They have a great selection and I never had anything   On the menu I didn't like. I dined as the host of a party of 11 and the service was exceptional.  We had several appetizers in addition to main courses and desert and everyone was pleased with their meal. Following dinner, we stayed for a while to listen to the live music and were made to feel welcome. Final bill was under $1k for a party of 11 with appetizers,  main courses, deserts, and drinks. Great vegetarian selection as well.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We've spent 2 days up and down Broadway and by far the BEST atmosphere and service was here at Robert's! Karen took such great care of us yesterday, we came back for more. We will definitely be back here each visit and this is my most recommended stop for live music, beer and that fried bologna sammich. Find Karen! She will take care of you!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Happy hour is the bomb, bartender was a stud. Get the basil lemonade cocktail and the crab dip. Half price from 4-7 I think

name: Robert's Western World
text: Loved this place!!! Super old school country music & great simple food.   they have live music, bar & a great little menu. When you first walk in, it's like you are being transported to a different era. There is a wall of boots, that are not for sale lol. I made that mistake ‍. Most of the boots have autographs of country singers. That night they had a great three man band that played old school country and some fifties music. The food was great! Supper simple menu like I said, but so good. They even had recession combos that included fried bologna sandwich, potato chips, moon pie & beer. Combo 2 was a corn dog, chips, moon pie & beer. The food was great the music was great. It was great seeing everyone have a good time. Love it!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Perfectly average! Not too loud, decent music, plenty of seating, a kind bar tender. Literally everything you would want out of a Honky Tonk! The best part is beers are actually the cheapest here out of anywhere on the Broadway strip, at just $2.50 a glass. Not being a beer fan myself, I just had a glass of water, but the bar tender still stayed and chatted with us for a while and wanted to hear all about Chicago. When a girl spilled her drink near us on accident, the bar tender quickly whipped up another one for her, free of charge, which I thought was so kind and out of the ordinary. Definitely worth a trip for some genuine service and laidback country tunes.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Bouncing between a three and a four.
I came her for Lizzie concert and initially I loved the scenery, the organization the building looks great and very beat and clean. However for the actual location being for a concert i can't say it was the best experience.

Bathroom are always going to be long lines however, these bathrooms were cleaned frequently they were nicely designed and truly felt safe.

The bars were horrible. Over priced drinks for poor and slow service. Minimal options, the bar service felt like I waited for an hour for a bootlegger

name: Robert's Western World
text: We weren't looking for super loud, obnoxious party crowds. This was perfect! The price is right, the AC is strong, the classic country music was spot on, and the crowd and staff was down to earth and sound. Also--I can eat a recession special every day for the rest of my life... $6 goes a long way! #friedbolognasandwich

name: Legends Corner
text: My husband and I were heading back to our hotel when we decided to stop in for one more drink. The bands were switching out so we got lucky and scored a table right on the rail of the upper level. Amazing atmosphere and we totally enjoyed the energy of the place. There's no table service, so you do have to go to the bar for your drinks, but that was fine, we were only coming in for one, right? Nope, ended up staying for a couple of hours! Clean bathrooms, friendly bartenders, and an excellent band.

name: Legends Corner
text:
They only let in certain people they only want in. 
The bouncers will pick people out of the line they are scared of and will not let them in for whatever reason. Call it racism call it being scared of actually having to do something but it is a fear they have. As a native of Nashville to be told your friend is not allowed after going in EVERY bar on broadway is a little stupid to anyone trying to talk up their city. Because if the city is talked up and gets positive reviews the club or whatever it is that is being positively reviewed is making more money because of the positive reviews and in this case should not receive positive reviews. 

Workers will turn down any guys they think might actually be as strong as them and will mess up their little lie of a story to get them a better tip so ignore

name: Robert's Western World
text: Very cool looking venue. Waited 15 minutes at the bar and couldn't get service. No band even started setting up in that time. So we decided to leave. Everywhere else around there has more accessible bars with live music starting more frequently. Somehow this place is slightly hipper, which means more crowded and less customer service focus.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The experience of the Ryman theater cannot be simply put into words. There is an energy that fills the place. Not sure if it's the history of the legends that have graced this stage or the emotions that the place brings in each person that walks through these doors. We've came here about 3 years ago before the updates. The transformation is pretty amazing! 

We have sat on the floor seats and balcony and both views are fantastic. They do offer drinks, and they are very expensive. But hey you are not there for the drinks. 

The best part of this place is when you can take a tour. Just DO IT! It's such a fun experience. The tour includes visiting back stage and on stage access.  

This is a memory everyone needs to experience!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
We loved it! Not as loud as the other honky tonks

Brought our toddlers and they seemed happy

They card you as you enter so be prepared 

Clean

Great cheese curds
Lovely workers

Good solid music

Highly recommend

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Homophobic owner announced that girl on girl dancing was allowed and encouraged, but  boy on boy dancing was prohibited.
Dave Tanner, a regular guitarist and vocalist there, has also written a homophobic song about Tootsie's, which he calls a gay bar. This is Southern discrimination at its best. Stay away and don't support. It's a shame because the music was amazing until all the homophobic slander started.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Sambuca looks like a Las Vegas lounge transferred to the down to earth town of Nashville.  It is the epitome of incongruity.  As we are not particularly enamored with Country or Blue Grass, the opportunity to listen to Stephanie Adlington, an accomplished jazz crooner, was exciting. Entering into the bordello like ambiance of Sambuca was odd, but great seating was available on this Sunday night and we thoroughly enjoyed the music. Drinks were light on the alcohol, service was spotty, the food mediocre at best, but the music was great.  The surprise of the evening was when I asked for bread.  Sambuca does not serve bread.  No bread? What restaurant doesn't have bread.  I asked them if they had croutons, but the server didn't get my joke. I offered to go to Piggly Wiggly for a loaf, but that didn't go over well either. As Marie would say, "Let them eat cake."

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Love the Ryman Auditorium. Yes, the acoustics are superb, but there are some tricky sight lines at the ends of the balcony and under the balcony. I recommend paying a bit more for the better views of the stage, but you'll hear well from anyplace in the auditorium. The place is steeped in history and deserves all the accolades. Enjoy!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
It's the Ryman. What more does one need to say? If you are a music lover and an artist you follow is performing here, I can't imagine that you'd have a bad time. Coming here just for the sake of coming here, however, is a bit more of a mixed bag. It's nothing about the venue; it's just sitting through a performance (or, performances) you'd never attend otherwise. That's what happened to me for my Ryman experience.

I had friends coming in town and they (well, really, just one) were on fire to go to the Ryman. Sheepishly, I admitted that I'd never been. I'd meant to. There were shows I would have seen. But I don't make it out to live music venues as much as I once did so I never quite got the spirit to commit to coming to a show. But this would have to be different. On a Saturday in mid-November the show was... the Grand Ole Opry. Hmm. I can appreciate the history and kitsch but this was wasn't my first choice of first show to see at the Ryman. But things were what they were so I attempted to buy tickets and... gone? Really? Three weeks before the show? Hmm. I called customer service and somehow the rep was able to find five seats together where there weren't any before. Magic. Not only was she incredibly helpful but she was quite polite as well. It was a wee bit shocking for a customer service interaction, sadly enough. We were to be seated up top but that was fine with me. Sound travels up and I was there for the sound, not the sights.

We arrived 25 minutes before the show and... chaos. Pure chaos. There were no stanchions. There were no discernible lines. There was only a crush of humanity without the ability to form logical ways by which to enter in to the auditorium. Making things worse, I had to pick up my tickets at will call. Thing is, people were just standing around, not moving. Taking initiative, I started asking who was waiting to pick up tickets. Then I started push... making my way to the counter. I devised the brilliant idea to ally with an older woman. I was the muscle, she was the sass. People parted for her like the red sea and I kept her moving. #teamwork We got to the counter (passing many people who weren't waiting for tickets; they were just blocking the way), got our tickets and resumed waiting. 

The doors opened at exactly the posted time (I can appreciate that) and we made our way inside and to our seats. Once inside, the process was pretty smooth. There's no excuse for the mess outside. None. Drinks are overpriced and weak but you know to expect this. The venue is as stately as advertised. The sound is the stuff of legends and the energy is palpable. I just wish I'd come to see an act I was pumped about. It was cool (read: kitschy) to sit for a live broadcast of such a long-running show but (for me) the novelty wore off. Plus, I think I was one of 10 locals (including the performers) in the building. The Titans-Patriots game was the next day and the Mother Church was full of Patriots fans. Maybe the locals knew better?

I'm glad I came. I'd come again -- but next time I'd come see an act I really wanted to see. Last tip: back row on the upper level had padded seats. As anyone who went to church in the south can tell you, church pews + sitting for a long time =/= comfort. Go for the padded chairs.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Sambuca has a great atmosphere, location, service, and menu (food + drink). 

It has multiple levels and two great outdoor seating areas, a stage with great live music, and an overall cool vibe that I'd recommend as one of my "go to" spots in Nashville. 

You can't beat the filet with added toppings but they have other great dishes and seafood options which seem hard to find in Nashville. 

They have a very professional staff that is helpful, friendly, and knows the menu front to back.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place is a must stop in when in Nashville.  The entertainment was rocking, fun and well, entertaining!  Interactive and just the right amount of loud!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
All I can say is wow! 
I came on a Friday evening and had good Mariachi musicians providing us a wide genre of songs in the traditional Mariachi style. Then we were entertained with two very talented aerial Acrobats (I think that's what they're called.
Eating out with a vegetarian couple can prove challenging in an Hispanic area, but this place provided options and everyone was happy.
I enjoyed the decor and cute shops. I could imagine my students really enjoying taking selfies and learning about quinces and first communions.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This place is so steeped in history that you almost can't help but get caught up in the nostalgia. I had no interest in going here but my wife insisted. She really got this one right. 
This building is over 100 years old and anybody who's somebody has played here or wished they had. The list of singers, actors, shows, etc. who have occupied the stage is amazing. The Grand Ole Opy is only one of many who called this the ultimate stage.
The acoustics here are incredible. The only thing I have seen like it is the Hollywood Bowl. You can barely see the person and yet you hear them very well. A photographer was barking instructions to her subjects at stage front and we could hear her clear as a bell walking above the balcony seats.
We tried to book a show after our tour of the theater, but they were all sold out. So book ahead and rest assured it will be a treat!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
We went to the Ryman on our visit to Nashville, and it was incredible and memorable. Great live show. Many acts included in a series of four mini shows. 

In addition to seeing the show, we also took the self-guided tour of the auditorium and really enjoyed it. The Ryman offers a very interesting tour highlighting the history of country and bluegrass music with numerous exhibits housing artists' costumes and instruments. A movie shown in their theater, traces the history of the building. I'm very fond of country music and enjoy listening to the greats-- Johnny Cash, Merle Haggard, George Strait, Patsy Cline, and while this is our very first time visiting this venue... sure this won't be the last.

No tour is complete without dropping by at the gift shoppe. All things Mother Church (the Ryman was originally built as a church, hence the reference) and Nashville. From collectibles, records, décor, and clothing they've got it!

"Country music has become the music that best represents the reality of American life." --Brad Paisley

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
The butcher in the market alone deserves 5 stars. Excellent meat and seafood selection and helpful.
All of the plaza (except the cell phone store )is a great place to pig out and dig into some varied cultural experiences.
We got both the hot and cold platters from the tapas place and it was a good variety, then sampled the pizza, and then hit the ice cream/popsicle shop. Very good all around.
My friend took some of the ceviche home and raved about it. We tried the flan from the market and it was delicious as well.
Great concept and execution. I can't wait to see what moves in to the other spots inside the plaza.
While you're there, get your next meal to-go from Taj Indian Restaurant in the same parking lot. It's the best in town.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Great honky tonk on Broadway. The only bar in downtown we actually met some locals! 

We came in for a Shiner and their fried bologna sandwich with mayo and tomato. The bologna is actually grilled though not fried.  I saw this place on diners drive ins and dives and glad we made it in.  I thought the sandwich was very good. Not every meal has to be gourmet, sometimes a simple meal can hit just the right spot. Especially when there's some good live country music playing in the background.  I hope this place sticks around for ages.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: All in one place, good food, good dessert, good cantina for drinks, live entertainment, and if you want a variety grocery store they have it too and some stores to buy cute nicknacks! Tacos, churrasco, churros, margaritas, salsa music on Thursday!!!! Beautiful plaza filled with color and Mexican decor makes you fell like you're in a another country!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I had truffle fries for an appetizer.  Great stuff with cheese and bacon.  My meal was pork braciola and that was tremendous!  It is a rolled tenderloin stuffed with spinach, cheese and a white bean.  All covered in a marinara sauce.  Sides were potatoes augratin an a brussel sprout warm slaw.  The brussel sprout was done perfectly.  Really good meal that was unique and flavorful. 
We had stout chocolate cake which was good but not an OMG experience.
Atmosphere is very pleasant and service was excellent.  Waiter was knowledgeable and interacted with us on a personal level.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
You are here for the biscuits! That being said, the rest of the food was a big southern mass of tasty awesomeness. 
You do not go here if you are on a diet, worried about unclogging your arteries, or planning on running a marathon that day.  The portions are big, covered in classic southern gravy and very very delicious. Eating to the point of explosion is a likely experience (especially because the biscuits come first!) 
Stopping by the gifts shops is very necessary. Do it

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
2nd visit to loveless cafe in about 6 years. Not sure why we dont go more often when we visit our family in Nashville.  Sad to learn that the biscuit lady had passed, but they are still going strong and the biscuits continue her legacy.

The wait was about 1 hour, but they have multiple shops , free lemonade and water and coloring activties, and cornhole boards for the kids.

the gentleman in the smokehouse even let my young niece and nephew come inside and see inside this work area and showed them  where the bbq comes from.

The foods was delicious,  we I had the country fried steak with hashbrown casserole,  with 2 eggs.  others had bbq, country ham, meatloaf and pork chops.  Everything was so good and the service considering how busy they were was outstanding.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: An interesting place to try in a touristy area, but not a restaurant that would be in our regular rotation of places to dine. Mom had the goulash that was not like the Hungarian which we typically encounter. It was not a bad dish though, but a tad too salty. I started with beer cheese soup that was not anything to write home about. I ordered the pork shank on the recommendation of the waiter that was a huge portion, but somewhat lacking in sauce. The Black Forest cake is not baked in the restaurant according to our waiter who seemed devoted to serving the customer but was a good way to cap off the meal. I ordered a liter of authentic German beer from the tap which was a decent value at $13 and shared it with Mom. If we are out in Donelson or at Opry Mills, I might go back but won't drive across town on a special trip to eat there.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Loved it. Food was pretty good. Soccer on tv so that was a plus. Polka band was awesome. Would have given five stars but it was pretty expensive. We will come back though.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Blane was awesome! This place was truly amazing. Our waiter was phenomenal. You MUST try the Brussels sprouts.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food was amazing and our waitress was incredible!  Great atmosphere.  Worth the drive.  If I'm ever back this way is for sure come back!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Can you please expand the business to New York? I miss the biscuits there! So buttery, so fresh, absolutely delicious with home made jam! We had more than enough food to take home for the next day breakfast! I definitely will go back the next time I go to Nashville.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
First time here and had a lovely evening. The upstairs venue is very nice, acoustics are fantastic, food was great and the service was excellent. There were some people at reserved tables but that wasn't an option for us when we purchased tickets online.  The smallest table size is for 4 so we were seated with two other people.

Valet parking was $6.  Surprisingly, there was only a 5 minute wait to get the car after the end of the show.  Our show was sold out so it was full but, rather than everyone stampeding toward the door at the end, at least half the room was just hanging out still eating or drinking so that helped regulate the flow.

There is a public lot immediately adjacent that was charging $10 - so not much difference considering a tip for the valet and we may do that next time.

Based upon some of the other reviews, it sounds like it's hit or miss but we will definitely be back for another show.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Take advantage of the whole experience. Browse the shops, take photos, and play some corn hole. The biscuits were perfect and the country ham is wonderfully savory. We think the fried potatoes are better than the hash browns casserole. I could have sipped on drinks all day. The Blue Moon is so smooth that it's dangerous.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Since City Winery opened, I have experienced many great performances there. As far as venues in Nashville go, it is one of the most intimate and one of my favorites. That's the good part. However, I find the food quality/service to be inconsistent. 

A friend and I attended the Labyrinth screening last night. It was General Admission, and my friend arrived a few minutes earlier to secure our seats. I gave the lady at the door my name, and told her I didn't need an usher since my friend was already seated and I knew my way around. One of the ushers started to walk with me, and I said that I was okay to find my seat. She seemed agitated and asked if we had menus. I said my friend probably had one. She started to walk with me AGAIN, and I simply said "can I just have a menu?" Then she huffed, said "fine!", shoved one in my hand and I walked away. Later I realized she only gave me a drink menu, not the dinner menu.  I should have spoken to a manager then, but I didn't want to cause a scene. I don't understand the big concern/rudeness over showing me to my seat!

Next, the food. The event ticket came with a prix fixe menu, which was fine with me. It was posted on the FB page and sounded yummy. However, the pasta entrée was pretty bland. The dessert, a crème brulee, was great...except for the fact the restaurant didn't have enough spoons to go around and we had to eat it with a fork. I usually enjoy the appetizers here, but you never get what you pay for. $3 for a flat soda (which was never refilled) was the icing on the cake. 

I wasn't going to post anything, but this type of service is ridiculous. I think this could be a top-notch venue if servers/management would just be polite and listen to their customers. I know several folks asked questions on the event page about times, menu, etc that were ignored. I will continue to see shows here if I like the artist, but I'll make sure to eat before!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
My family and I recently went on a trip to Tennessee, and during this trip, I made it my personal goal to eat as many Southern biscuits as possible. The Loveless Cafe was my first stop on a trip to severe heatburn that was worth every painstaking moment and choked down Tums.

So let's start with the biscuit. Warm buttery and flaky as any good biscuit should be.  To accompany it, I also ordered the fried catfish, okra and sweet potatoes, along with a bloody mary made with the cafe's own bloody mary mix. I have to say it was the spiciest bloody mary I have ever had. My husband had an iced tea drink with moonshine that came with its own, little moonshine glass you could take home. Very cute.

But what the Loveless Cafe is known for is their banana pudding. Now by this point, after eating all of the above, I had no room for it. But we ordered some to take back to the hotel, and having never had banana pudding before, I have nothing to compare it to, but it was delicious with chunks of real banana in it. Overall, I was incredibly stuffed and pleased, and the only reason I am not giving this five stars was because I'm not sure it was entirely worth it.

Yes, the food was good. Yes, the atmosphere was awesome. But there was an hour wait. They have some cute little shops in the compound for you to bide your time, but so does Cracker Barrel, and honestly, I'm not sure this is THAT much more delicious than Cracker Barrel, so I'll leave that up to you. If you feel like checking it out and don't mind waiting, go for it. If you're just jonesin' for some quick biscuits, go to Cracker Barrel.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The 10% off coupon is for their online store not the restaurant :(

I went for breakfast and ordered the country fried steak, hashbrown casserole and coffee. Breakfast was good but not memorable. Hashbrown casserole:  I expected something different. It was just hashbrowns saturated with cheese. I did enjoy the biscuits but was not blown away. I actually enjoyed the jams more. $17 for breakfast is a bit much but the portions were so big that it was 2 meals.

name: Rocketown
text: I cannot say enough wonderful things about this venue, the team of amazing people behind it, and their "leader" Mary Virginia Settle. Everything I needed was taken care of! Mary Virginia even took care of some things I didn't realize that I needed. Amazing venue and even more amazing people running it! My wedding reception was perfect! Easy! I was able to hand off a lot of decisions to them without worrying. They know what they are doing. I highly recommend Rocketown! Oh, and tip these wonderful people well. They deserve it for their hard work and attention to detail! Love!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
My friend and I were visiting Nashville for the first time and taking the Belle Meade Plantation tour about 15 minutes away. They have a restaurant at the plantation but we were looking for something local in town. 

The Loveless Motel/ Café came highly recommended and was said to have some stores to shop while you waited for a table. We were not disappointed! The wait was an hour and 20 minutes but there are three or four shops, and you can get a small snack while you wait; sometimes they're even giving out free samples of salsas or dips that they sell in the stores. The food is well worth the wait; it's basically Cracker Barrel, but fresher, local, and more friendly. Of course the history of the motel is nice to read about, too!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This is definitely a "must see" if you are visiting Nashville or even just live here. Great place to take friends visiting from out of town. You'll definitely have to wait a bit but I went around 9:30 am on a Saturday and it was less than 45 minutes. So not bad - plus, there are a lot of things to occupy your time while you are waiting. Mainly little shops to walk through which sell biscuit mix, jams, Loveless Cafe branded shirts, etc. The staff at the cafe is really nice and the service is good. You are greeted at your table right away and the service is quick and consistent throughout. Water and coffee are always filled. The star of the menu is definitely the biscuits and jams that come with it.
Delicious! But at the end of the day it is just a cafe - the eggs and bacon and other breakfast items taste pretty similar to what you'd get anywhere else. I got the veggie omelette which wasn't amazing but also ordered it without cheese so that may have been part of it. But I am not sure if people are really coming here for the food, but more for the experience at an iconic place in Nashville. And of course - those biscuits! Definitely worth checking out.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
MAN did I love this spot! We stumbled on it by chance and I'm so glad that we did.  One of the manager's at the Johnny Cash Museum suggested it.  The fact that he threw it out there despite the fact that there were other eateries much closer that also provided down home Southern cooking said a lot.  It was well worth the almost 30-minute drive and the additional 1.5 hour wait.  Fortunately, you do not have to sit around idly while you wait.  The property was an actual farm and each of the buildings has been re-purposed.  So it is fun to walk around and explore the property until your table is available.  The barn is a nice venue for private functions like wedding receptions, parties, etc.  One of the other buildings is not a country store reminiscent of a Cracker Barrel but better! They keep your cup full with free coffee over in the country store and some samples of some of the food products made and sold on-site.   One building is the main kitchen and dining building.  Another is a store where you can purchase Loveless paraphernalia and other items.  There are also games like the cornhole beanbag toss and horseshoes to keep you occupied while you wait.

For breakfast we had the pancakes, waffles, biscuits, grits, eggs, bacon, and sausage.  EVERYTHING was soooooo good.  I wanted to try some of the lunch and dinner items but I simply didn't have enough room in my stomach.  Not only was the food great but the service was also excellent.  I forgot my server's name but he reminded me of Ashton Kutcher and even had a sense of humor as he helped me to decide on my food options and continued to check-in as we were eating to make sure that everything was to our liking.  If you are in driving distance of Loveless around breakfast time (or you just love breakfast food), do pop in for a bite.  It will NOT disappoint! I can't vouch for the lunch or dinner items yet but I WILL be back next time I'm in town!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
If you love to eat, this has to be one of the best places to go.  Today was our second trip back to this restaurant and it was every bit as good as our first trip here.  This is definitely going to be on our list of restaurants every time we come to Nashville.

William

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
What a wonderful restaurant! Loveless Cafe is a favorite among Nashville natives and tourists alike! I have been frequenting Loveless since I was a young girl, and I just love taking our out of town guests for an unforgettable brunch!

Loveless is probably 30 minutes away from downtown, so if you are planning to travel from anywhere in the city, plan for a drive. Loveless is EXTREMELY popular, so you must get there early in the day to avoid a lengthy wait. 

If you must wait, Loveless Cafe has taken some steps to keep you entertained. There is a gift shop for browsing, Cornhole boards for playing, and lovely grounds for walking with loved ones. Sometimes the wait for a table can be as long as two hours, so plan for that possibility!

However long you wait, be prepared for the southern comfort food of your dreams. Small fluffy biscuits served with butter and 3 homemade jams are served first. And for the main course I recommend going with a table of at least 4-5 people and sharing one of their family style breakfasts. 

I would also COMPLETELY recommend the hashbrown casserole. (This is my favorite side, and my mouth is watering just thinking about it!) 

I have only been for brunch, but if dinner is anything like their breakfast food, you are in for a treat!

All in all, I would wholeheartedly recommend Loveless to friends and family! You won't be disappointed!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I was not impressed with the Loveless Cafe.  Most items on the menu are fried or heavily buttered.  We couldn't find the waitress with a Geiger counter, so trying to get a refill on our beverages was an exercise in futility.  I understand the "down-homey" allure of the joint - they broadcast a country music radio show in the barn adjacent to the restaurant.  I have been told the radio show is hit or miss - unfortunately, it was a complete miss on the the night I was there.  They had some decent local beers available, but aside from that it was only cheap domestics.  The wine selection is not very good at all.

Everyone raves about the biscuits - I've had better.

It's probably just not my scene, but I found the Loveless Cafe to be wholly overrated.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: My spouse and I were excited to bring our in-laws for dinner and drinks someplace none of us had been before.  The restaurant appeared relatively busy, though there were no patrons that appeared to be waiting for a table.  We approached the hostess to ask about a table for 4 and what the wait would be.  The hostess did not look up to address us for several minutes, and when she did stared at us blankly.  She asked if we had a reservation.  We did not and inquired about the wait for a table for 4.  She stammered, stating that she truly had "no idea what the wait would be" but that right now, they were full.  I asked for any sort of estimate.  Again, she could not answer.  I noted that several seats were open at the bar and asked if we could sit there as an alternative.  The hostess struggled and appeared reluctant as she followed behind us to the seats.  Again, most seats were unoccupied at the bar.  After being seated for one or two minutes, I noted a table for 4 that was empty but assumed that there was likely a reservation for it.  However, after enjoying a flight of red wines and some parmesan truffle fries with lemon aioli (quite unique and delicious) an hour and a half later, the table continued to remain empty.  We left disappointed with that and many other tables empty.  Very upset and disappointed that the hostess (the primary job of which is to welcome and seat patrons) was so unwelcoming and unwilling to offer alternative options to us.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place definitely lived up to the hype. Have always heard about it and had never tried it. Finally got around to it. The biscuits that they bring out are to die for. The jellies that they bring with them were probably my favorite part of the whole meal. The blackberry was incredible. The main course was great, as well. The creamed corn was probably the best I've ever ate- home or on the road!! Hashbrown casserole usually has onions in it, but not theirs. A refreshing break from everybody else's. The mac n cheese was exceptional. The meats were good, but the veggies were really what impressed me. The service was impeccable. Never had to wait on anything. We plan on coming back this trip for breakfast. Can't wait for those biscuits and blackberry jelly!!!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Went to see Cracker here last night .  While the venue is beautiful, it is not a good place to see a show.  the tables are to close together and there is room to spread them out a little.  We ordered the duck tacos and two beers .  the duck was very under seasoned and the beers are a minimum $6 a piece.  the vocals cut out during the opening act, and the vocals during Cracker were awful.  Cracker brought out two female back up singers for a few songs and their voices were muddy and anything but crisp.  Johnny Hickmans backup vocals were muted and muddy all night.  Then the service.  What a mess.  I had to get the attention of a floor manager  after waiting over 15 minutes to place an order.  Then the waitress came along about 10 minutes after that.  Then during the show, our friends we went with were trying to get her attention, 4 times, she never came.  My wife got so fed up, she went to the servers station bar and ordered beers.  Then when the waitress came back, she seemed annoyed we did that.  Its a mess of a venue really.  Really pretty , great acoustics, but the whole premise is clunky and awkward.  Will not be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place doesn't disappoint. Came from Southern Indiana to eat here and stay a couple of days in Nashville. I recommend the Sampler Platter. My wife's garden salad with fried chicken looked delicious.

name: The Basement
text: What an awesome night to conclude our Nashville trip with friends.  We took an Uber there and killed some time upstairs in the record store, Grimey's.  The drinks were  heavy pours and delicious.  The venue is small but really does give a feel of a basement.  I loved the decor and the vibe.  The cover charge of $5 gave us a very full entertaining night of four bands all with their own unique sound.  My particular favorite was Craig Haller.  Make sure to check this out if you are in Nashville. It is definitely more enjoyable and relaxing than the crowded Broadway Street venues.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Food & service is really great. Worth the long lines? Not so sure.

However, if mom & dad are coming to town and you need to fill the schedule with some good country cookin, this is your spot! Plenty of kitschy shops to browse and buy jellies or trinkets while you wait. Toss some bean bags outside or just enjoy a chair under a shady tree. 

Once inside, you won't be disappointed. They're known for the biscuits, which I assure you are the bomb. My wife & I ordered the breakfast pork chops & country fried steak respectively. While both were good, the pork chops blew me away. Juicy & delicious with an awesome crunch. There was enough food to feed 3 people on that one plate. Plenty of leftovers for dinner.

Perhaps the best part of our visit was the service. These are the most efficient (and super sweet) servers I've seen. Never waited in anything. 

Would I cruise out to this place from Nashville for breakfast? Probably not. It's a pretty big time investment with the drive & wait. With that said, it'll be high on my list of places to visit when I have guests in town.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Simply delicious. The biscuits are to die for. The environment is welcoming. Don't be surprised if you have to wait for a table. The food comes out fast though!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Not impressed. Bisquits are ok, pretty average tho. The wait time was long. They ran out of bisquits, had to wait 30 minutes to get more. The ham tasted like pure salt. KFC still has the best bisquits.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Jason was our server and absolute delight! The food was delish!!! Best biscuits ever! He warned me on the country ham and he was correct it's very salty. Thank you Jason. He did bring us a sample to try and it was very good but yes salty. If you like smaller portion I must say share a plate as portions are huge.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits and blackberry jam, yummy! Great home style food, recommend any of the chicken dishes and the hash brown casserole is a must. The wait for a table is worth it, and wait can be minutes or over an hour. Stock up on jam in the store while you wait!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The breakfast is so great!  I love their biscuits!  I feel like I was in the old time at the former motel.  The place is perfect away from the big city.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The breakfast was awesome. We went back a month later. I had the watermelon ribs, they were not that good. I will go back for breakfast but don't think I will for dinner.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Their breakfasts are lacking but I LOVE their lunch and dinners. Make sure you have plenty of time because it could take ages to get a table.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
On vacation with 10 friends from Chicago.
We are foodies and have all worked in the food industry as servers so we have tolerance and yet...

We had researched where to get great fried chicken, great smoked brisket and great biscuits.
Loveless was decided for biscuits.

We drove 1/2 hour from our resort because of the recommendations.
We came in the evening on our first night (a Monday) and waited about 1/2 hour. Perfect. Really a fine wait time for a popular place. 
A few people went to the gift shop.

They seated us at two different tables a 6 and a 4. Not ideal for our first night together but we were hungry.

Our server brought out the biscuits. Meh.
I don't get the hype. It was bread with the jam on the side. Maybe biscuits just aren't my thing.

I ordered the sampler which was one egg, ham, sausage and bacon. DRY salty ham, dry sausage and overdone bacon. It *did* come with a hash brown casserole that I LOVED. I ate it all (I was starving. I'm pretty sure I make the same potatoes at home with frozen potatoes, dream of chicken soup, onion and cheese.

The fried chicken was underwhelming and not what I expected  from southern fried chicken . It was more the texture of shake and bake.

In my opinion, not worth the wait or the drive. 
There are MANY other wonderful places to eat in Nashville.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I just don't get this place.. I truly don't.

4 stars for entertainers.  0 stars for venue seating. 0 stars for food.

They have mediocre food, the tables are situated such that you have to block the aisles with your chairs so you can see over the heads of the people in front of you...
They turn the tables sideways - not straight on in front of the stage...
So all the people looking east and west have to pull their chairs out to face north, to watch the performer...

Terrible layout.  Terrible food.
Good artists.

Caught Damien Escobar, last night....   probably my 12th concert at City Winery...
I enjoy the venue, but just too much wrong with it...
It's really too bad that this place is so mediocre.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I totally enjoy this place.  We have visited here the last two trips to Nashville and have had a great meal both times.   Both my wife and I really thought the catfish was outstanding and I loved the hot chicken which I understand is a down south favorite. Side dishes were plentiful and the biscuits with preserves were awesome as well.  Save room for the peach cobbler and ice cream.  You will have leftovers for sure to take home with you ..

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Great German Food and atmosphere. Try a bite of everything especially the beer and sides

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My girlfriend and I tried City Winery for a Griffin House show in mid-November one Wednesday night. Mostly we wanted to see the new concert behemoth of SoBro (I still hate the name SoBro). 

First off, the atmosphere. This place is beyond superlatives beautiful and tasteful, all at the same time. They've made it obvious it's a nicer place without overwhelming the concert-goer seeking to just enjoy a show with a nice glass of wine. They'll start making their own wine here in 2015 so we'll be interested to go back and see even more of this gorgeous venue.

The wine. I'm just starting to understand different types of wines and an amateur at best in describing what I want in a wine. The waiter was well-trained and did not lead us astray when we were making our selection from the multiple wines on tap, available for a glass, and those available by a bottle. We tried a couple of these before we left and weren't disappointed. 

The food. It was good, not great. I had the leg of lamb pizza, which was tasty with a good mix of spices, crunchy pine nuts, and melty cheese. She got the Chicken Fricassee which was good but reminded me of much less expensive items I've had elsewhere. The food was tasty and good to munch on during a show or for dinner. I'm probably going to have dinner elsewhere the next time we visit City Winery, however.

Pros: Amazing building and predictably great wine selection.

Cons: Food was kind of expensive and didn't blow me away. The parking was pretty terrible. They offered paid valet or you can park on the streets, which is not the best option in this neighborhood.

Overall: This a relaxing, romantic place to take a date for a concert. You will win friends  and influence people if you bring someone from out of town in for a concert. If you can stand the parking situation and high-priced food, you'll be elated to make this spot one of your regulars!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
If you're in the area - drop everything and go here!
We were driving cross country and I read about this place online and got a recommendation to try it out. 
The biscuits are great, I'm not a big fan in general but these were really good and their homemade jams area amazing (bought some for home in their store next door while waiting for our table).
I had the pulled pork platter with the cream of corn and some potato side that were just incredible, the best meat, sauce and sides I have ever had (it's sad, i know).
My BF had the chicken tenders with fries, also great dish though I think that trying the local favorites is always best in these places. I asked our waitress what to order and went by her suggestion and I was happy I did. 
We will definitely be back next time we're in the area.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: By far the best restaurant in Nashville. Their biscuits are AMAZING. I actually wanted to take their biscuits and gravy to go, they were that good. If you are only in Nashville for a day, this is the restaurant to visit. Definitely worth the drive.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Far and away the most gorgeous small concert venue I've ever seen.  Worth it just to see the room. Acoustically perfect and not a bad seat in the house. And they're also a pretty serious restsurant, catering to oenophiles and craft beet lovers. The  flatbread pizzas and the desserts were outstanding. And if they were any indication, I've got faith in the rest of the menu too. This ain't your basic bar grub....they'd do just fine as a restaurant even without the music.

But who am I kidding, right? Toss Buddy Miller and Jim Lauderdale out on the stage, and you've got yourself the moral equivalent of doggie heaven.

This place will ruin you for seeing a concert anywhere else ever again.  As the old saying goes, "How you gonna keep 'em down on the farm after they've seen Paree?"

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Truly enjoyed this delightful surprise and Opry Mills Mall! Not at all the usual cramped, crowded normal Mall restaurant types. Very open spaces, large seating on benches,  German style seating so you were placed at tables with different people giving you the opportunity to make new friends. The pretzels are absolute heaven so light and fluffy and crisp! The food was delicious with very generous portions! Most definitely worth the venture to find this delightful place ! The night we were there they even had a polka band that did a fabulous job! We went on a Friday night, and due their communal seating they were able to seat us very quickly,  which was very refreshing on a Friday night in Nashville!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great food, fun watching biscuits being made, and an interesting store to browse. Fun for the whole family.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My feelings about City Winery are kind of all over the place. I've gone there some times when the service is perfect and it's a wonderful evening. Other times I've gone and the service leaves a lot to be desired.

For concerts, anywhere on the floor is a good view. The tables get a little cramped, but that's no big deal. 

City Winery prides itself on being a "listening room" and I feel like they've been emphasizing "shut up and listen to the show" a lot more recently, but I went to one show where some Vinofile members were loud, drunk, and rude in the front row, and when people complained to the management, nothing was done. They never approached the couple, nothing. They just let everyone else's evening be ruined. 

Very recently, when I dropped off my car for valet, they reminded me that I need to tip on the way out because "the $5 goes directly to the building and the valets don't receive any of it." It was just offensive - were they saying I look like I don't usually tip? Or if you feel your valets aren't paid enough, well... pay them more appropriately? Of course I was going to tip, and of course I did tip, but the lecture about tipping to start off my evening was very off putting.

The most recent show I saw there, the waiter would not stop interrupting us during the show. I'd never had this problem before, as the service is usually super discrete. This show, however, the waiter would come over and hover about the check or talk to us while the artist was singing. It became very annoying. Every other time I've been there, the waiters have been awesome about waiting for applause breaks or encore breaks to handle checks and refills.

Having said all of that, though, it's still a nice place to see an intimate show.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I was raised in a family of good Southern cooks, so anytime that I eat at a meat and 3 I have high expectations. Loveless exceeded them. The biscuits were perfect. They were light and fluff and buttery. Everything I love in biscuit. Everything my friend and I had was wonderful. I especially like the hashbrown casserole. It was was full of sharp cheddar cheese, but not greasy. The green beans seemed to have a little vinegar i them, just like my Aunt Rita's green beans. 

We went on a Thursday night and there wasn't a wait. I imagine on the weekends its really busy. 

The service was great. We got our food in about 5 minutes and our glasses were always full. 

The Loveless isn't the kind of place I would go all the time, but it was fun. It is a little out of the way and kinda touristy, but it was good. The biscuits are so good!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Most of the staff was rude and incompetent. The place smelled like fish. Convenient parking, I have to admit. I think that this would be a good place to see acoustic performances or poetry reading. It's a strange place to see a rock show, and the staff acts like they're annoyed that you're there. Since this is a chain, is it like a slightly more upscale Hard Rock Cafe, just without the memorabilia?

name: The Basement
text:
This place was fantastic... We came here on a Tuesday night  and it was perfect... We were able to experience 3 different music groups and they were all amazing! The service was great! The space is very small but everyone was super friendly and it didn't feel awkward at all... People of all types, personalities and styles... Awesomely eclectic group of people! 

Was missing one star only because it's a bit out the way and you can't walk to anything else from it, but it's only a $5 cab ride to downtown which was totally worth it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Excellent sausage and biscuits. We had to get ours to go. Sunday 11 am had a two hour wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The Loveless Cafe was an amazing experience! My mom and I toured the entire place and had a blast. The food was also very good! The hot biscuits you are severed were amazing!! I had the cinnamon raisin french toast which was good and my mom's omelet was good as well, served a little too cold for our liking though. The hash brown casserole is a MUST try!! Overall good food and I would go back!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great biscuits! Peach jam taste like cobbler, so of course I loved it! The grits are sooooo good. I can only review the breakfast, and it was pretty good. Definitely worth a visit at least once. FYI: we waited an hour to be seated and was told it would be an hour and 45 minutes, so be prepared to wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Our first time here....OMG!  This is comfort food at its best. They brought out fresh hot biscuits and jam the minute we sat down, and they were deeliciouuusss!  The fried chicken strips, mashed potatoes, cucumber and onion salad were perfection. Chess pie and pecan pie were just average. They arrived cold and would be better at room temp. It's priced a little high and it's a 30-40 minute drive from downtown but worth it. Nashville treasure should be tried once by all; you won't need to eat again for 24 hours!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazzzzzing fried chicken!!! I can say the best I have ever had. This place is a must go/see when in Nashville. Everything we ordered was amazing and everything we didn't order looked amazing too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Don't go expecting the a best meal of your life experience. If you're local you probably know not to waste your time. I would mark this more as a tourist attraction. There is always a wait, so don't arrive hungry. The biscuits are made fresh, but I wouldn't call them amazing. I would call this an average southern style restaurant. You can go to Cracker Barrel and get the same food.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I eat at city winery for brunch. It was the best brunch i have ever had. I had the biscuit Oscar!! So good cant wait to come back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Yummy!  Good ole Southern cooking. Fried chicken was delicious, peach jam excellent, sweet potatoes delightful. What can I say about the Hoe Cakes?  Unfortunately, they sat there while I ate my whole meal because I thought they were pancakes (I was with a tour group and didn't know the menu). Not to shabby.  Nice environment. Would visit again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We had breakfast at the Loveless cafe and loved it.  We had the "breakfast #2" and it was a wonderful choice although a bit pricy for five of us.  It aloud us to try the things they are know for, cheese grits, ham and the hash browns. Our server was pleasant and the hostess spot on in her estimate.  This helps because I drove out early to place our name on the list before returning with the group.  Great food!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits, biscuits, biscuits! That's all you need to know- moist, buttery, absolutely incredible. If you want more go for the sides: mashed potatoes, coleslaw, fried green tomatoes. The restaurant has a whole plaza of little shops to visit while you are waiting for your table or for a takeaway order. To save time when the wait for a table is long, get takeaway and eat on the tables outside.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Food was absolutely GREAT! Huge portions of homemade food, biscuits are to die for! First time and will definitely will be a repeat customer. 
Our waiter Jason keep us in biscuits, butter, sweet tea and we never had to wait on anything!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is a MUST if you are visiting Nashville! It's a bit off the beaten path but is super quaint and features homemade goodness throughout the whole menu. We were so impressed, we are here twice during our short visit. The biscuits and fresh preserves are amazing, the chicken and dumplings was the best I've ever had, the chicken strips were juicy and mouthwateringly good, and all the sides were fabulous! The service was prompt and full of southern charm. After eating we walked the property and visited the little gift shop, which is full of mixes, preserves and sauces that they use in the restaurant along with a lot of cute little souvenir type items. Make sure to stock up while you're there and if you forget anything you can always order it later from their website. Overall, I would definitely recommend this cute little slice of southern charm to anyone looking for amazing food and a fun memory!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits were the joy of my visit to the Loveless Café, paired with the bowl of butter and jam varieties to put on them.  I ordered the country ham which was a little too salty for my taste, but everything else was delicious.  My husband ordered fried chicken and waffles which he devoured.  Luckily, we arrived right when it opened, so there was no wait for us, but our friends who live in Franklin said they once had to wait 4 hours!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This place was a pleasant surprise! Great beer options, fun atmosphere, and friendly staff. Totally legit German food! Items on the menu prepared the authentic German way and small "American touches" like beer-cheese dip for the pretzel appetizers! Short 10 min walk from Gaylord Opryland.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless Cafe is way on the west side of Nashville.  It has a storied past and is still a great place to eat!  They have a wide variety of traditional southern fare.  The service is great and the atmosphere comfortable.  My brother, who is a notoriously picky eater, ate everything on his plate!  I'll definitely be back the next time I'm on that side of town (or I might even make a special trip if I'm not there soon).

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great biscuits!! It's fun to watch them make them and boy are they good. Small in size and served warm so it allows you to eat too many! We had the pimento cheese omelet, added mushrooms and ordered hash browns as our side. It's very cheesy and filling. We couldn't even finish the hash browns. We also ordered the four biscuit combo plate. The fried chicken was amazing!!!!! The fried green tomatoes and pimento cheese are good but very rich. The bbq was also flavorful but again it's a lot of food. The cheese grits were delicious and I should have just had those. The staff was efficient and sweet just like the tea. It's fun to visit and it's a place to mark off your "restaurants to try" list.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We've been coming to Loveless Cafe when in town after discovering it 42 years ago-- before it reached landmark status. It has stood the test of time. Yes ,there are long waits occasionally , but if you go with that in mind you'll be rewarded with an unforgettable meal. Today I ordered the fried pork chops. They are crisp, tender and sooooo huge I could only finish half of one ( you get 2). Comes with 2 bowls of gravy, white and brown ,on the side. I had mashed potatoes and thin crispy fried green tomatoes ( superb) with it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Been here several times. This was my worst and most disappointing experience so far. I ordered eggs and ham and fruit. My eggs were supposed to be over medium but they came out pure water. The whites weren't even cooked it was all liquid. Not even close to over medium. I end up not wanting eggs. The ham was so salty I couldn't taste the flavor besides the salt. I didn't even eat the fruit but it looked good. Anyways, they ended up taking the eggs off my meal which was originally $11.99. But they still charged me $10.50 for the ham and fruit which really I think is DISTASTEFUL considering they messed up my meal. They asked my mother if she wanted toast not telling her that it wasn't included and charged us $2 for that. Just stuff like that I don't think shows well of the business. $90 is a lot for three people for breakfast, especially since a few of our meals were messed up and they didn't take care of the bill. Sounds cheap to me.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Reservations are a must for breakfast. The ham, biscuits and blackberry preserves are enough to make me fly back to Tennessee. The country grits tasted a lot like my mother's.  Lots of memorabilia all over.  Cute little shops around the property.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is awesome! Long wait but lots of seating and  to see while you wait. There is a BBQ shack in the middle that hands out free samples that are to die for! Also lots of cute shops! Bring a bottle of champagne and ok to drink mimosas while you.
 Fried chicken and biscuits were divine. Worth the trip and the wait!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Foods pretty good. A very busy tourist attraction, so the wait is always pretty long. They have really good fried pork chops, the steak and biscuits could use some more flavor. Daltons has better steak and biscuits for sure!!!

name: The Basement
text: Cool venue.  Very small and cramped, but cool vibe for sure.  Not a wide alcohol selection, but got the basics.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Went and saw Marty Stuart last night,  the place is top notch.   Sound ,service,food was top notch,  we will be back.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Great beer, awesome pretzels and bier cheese! Red cabbage is very tasty. Great restaurant feel. One of a kind place. Best place to eat dinner before an Opry show. Will be back!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place was on my must do list when when we went to Nashville.  It was a little out of the city so it's a good idea to have a car to get there.  The drive was very pleasant, we saw a different side to Nasvhille.  I had no idea there would be such a huge crowd when we got there.  We went on a Sunday around 10am and there was an hour and 20 minute wait.  The nice thing is there are little souvenir shops in the complex where you can shop while you wait.  I loved the souvenir shops...it was probably the best souvenir I got from Nashville in general...very unique!  While we were going to the different stores, they had free lemonade and water that you can grab.  I really liked the lemonade.  After all that, we still had about another 20 minutes to wait, so we just sat in our car for the remainder of the time.  

Once we were finally called in through a buzzer that was vibrating, we got seated!  The service was outstanding!  They kept coming over to make sure everything was okay and to refill waters, coffee, etc.  We got the complimentary order of the amazing biscuits and they were great!!  I ordered the fried chicken...it was okay but I would probably not get it again from here.  Hattie b's makes it way better!  Everyone else felt the same way about their food!  I definitely think this is more of a place to get the experience as opposed to actually come for the food if that makes sense!

All in all, it was okay.  I definitely think you should try it at least once if in Nashville, but maybe not much more than that (unless you are really into biscuits)!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Had to wait at Sunday lunchtime, but wow, was it worth it... Every bite was delicious southern cooking, like my grandma used to make. Now that we have gorged on chicken & waffles, fried chicken, numerous delicious sides, and some pie---- we are rolling out to car to nap... :)

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My friend and I met up at City Winery for the Hotel Nashville show. This is a super vibing place from outside. 
They do have $6 valet parking, a good sized parking lot out front for $10, and apparently free parking somewhere around the back? I didn't drive around to check. I got there right at 6pm and the parking lot was full but it started to clear out rather quickly. 
Walking inside you definitely get hit with a great ambiance. We had to go upstairs for the showcase. The staff was very sweet and helpful. We sat down and I went to look at the menu... well that's kinda what made me unsure. I do get that it's more upscale and the food and most of the wine prices didn't really bother me. What I don't understand what makes the wine from city winery so expensive? I guess whenever I go somewhere I like to try what comes from the area. This case I didn't and settled for a beer, in which case I got a German import at the same price as I could have gotten for a PBR... to me, that's milking it. ‍
It's a very cool spot and I will at some point go back back for a tasting. The food is delicious, and definitely worth what you pay. 
The sound is great, every artist illuminated the stage. 
As for a winery, well I'm still trying to figure that one

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Adorable space, great story, good biscuits. But the catfish, oh my god, was it disgusting. It was chewy. The texture was so off putting but I didn't want to send it back and wait any longer than I already had so I tried to suffer through it. I ate a third and had to stop before I got sick. The fried okra also had no flavor.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We were told by family members we just had to eat here. Boy am I ever glad we did! Hands down the best turnip Greens I have ever had. And then biscuits melt in your mouth. I have the fried catfish and it is to die for!!! Stop here, it is worth the wait time!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Favorite restaurant in the known universe. Been going for 50 years and go every time I'm in town since I don't live here anymore. Love this place!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is at the back of the Opry Mills  Mall  where we were able to find a parking spot so we said let's give it a try -- hubby as in the mood for a beer-- nice atmosphere like  German beer garden with long tables and a large bar area .  Our server Megan was very polite and attentive asking often if all was ok with food and drink.  I had the Reuben which was awesome and hubby had chicken schnitzel sandwich with ham and cheese which he really enjoyed. For dessert we shared a warm apple strudel with Carmel sauce and whipped cream it too was awesome . Although passing thru Nashville( tourist) I would recommend this place and would eat here again for a future visit ..fun place great atmosphere good food moderately priced

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
All restaurants go through the whole, we've just opened we have learning to do, thing. So that's pretty much what this is based off of. I will go back once they get themselves a little more together.

As we're walking in, first impressions are everything right, there is a couple complaining to the hostess about someone never coming over to take their order.
