The hostess apologizes and say's they can do something about it. The couple was so over it by then they declined and went to eat else where. This happened and we haven't even sat down yet. GREAT......

Hostess was very friendly. When we sat down the benches were very awkward. I'm a small person and I had to sit on the edge of the bench to even reach the table. It wasn't very comfortable and the table and chairs didn't move. My beer was great. My mother ordered the Reuben sandwich. She said it was really good and it looked really good. My Dad and I both ordered Brats. The brat was great, the bun was meh, and the fries were awful. The fries were actually awful for all three of us. They were cold, soggy, and really looked like they had been sitting out for a long time. I ordered a side of the german potato salad. It was wonderful!! Our waitress was ok.

I think I would prefer just to grab a group of friends and drink some beers at this place. Maybe that will change though in the future.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Made it to the Winery on a visit to Nashville. First, we were definitely surprised to see the restaurant was not packed as most restaurants in Nashville are on a Friday night. The waiter was good, attentive with drinks and stopping in to ask if we had questions. We ordered a variety of appetizers for our family: Mediterranean, house bread with butter, crab cake, mussels, and cheese board. The hummus, Mediterranean dish, and cheese tray were delicious, but the other food was sub par....the house bread was cold, and the pickled veggies had so much vinegar they were painful to eat. The mussels were bland and had no juice. The crab cake was stringy and had a blackened crust. We also ordered a chocolate cake that was dry, so I assume it was old, but the chocolate icing with crushed coffee beans were tasty. Overall, we were not impressed. Will not be returning.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We were in from out of town and looking for something different.. We found this cute little place and loved it! How cute! The food was great and staff was extremely friendly! Highly recommend it

name: The Basement
text:
This place was awesome! Super great venue if you're looking to get a little variety and want to hear each individual artist, rather than just the cover bands on the strip. The venue is small, but intimate. Definitely more of a young, hipster-y place. 

Go on Tuesday Nights! It's free "New Faces" night! You never know quite what you're gonna get!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I really really great food and beer!! It was however EXTREMELY loud and we asked to be seated away from the stage. I should have expected live music being a Saturday night, but it was so loud that we couldn't hear our waitress and she couldn't hear us. I couldn't talk to my friends, only lip read. After being moved to the other side of the restaurant, it was still loud but it was at least tolerable!
Our waitress was very friendly and knowledgeable! The beer was cold and refreshing! The food I just can't get enough of. I'm of German descent and this was very rich, authentic, comfort food, just like home cooking. I wanted to take pictures but I completely forgot when our mouth watering dishes were placed in front of us!
I highly recommend Bavarian Bierhaus for a fun atmosphere and DELICIOUS food and beer! Just ask to be seated away from the stage if you want to have any conversation.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
So, my husband is first generation American with two *VERY* German parents, and a very German family, in general. We spent a few weeks last October traveling around Europe, including several days in Munich. We frequented many a beer hall (including the infamous Hofbräuhaus, which is essentially what Bavarian Bierhaus is going for), so we were excited (read: hopeful) to try this place!

Large open room atmosphere, great German decorations - loved the hops hanging from the chandeliers, as I remember seeing that in many restaurants in Munich - totally took me back! Bench seating, but they don't seat you with strangers, which honestly was part of the fun of the beer halls in Germany, but I get that we as Americans aren't generally used to that, lol. 

Service was nice, and menu was exciting - we saw several dishes we recognized from both my German mother in law's kitchen, and from our time in Germany. We ordered a pretzel and some bier cheese - the cheese is worth it! Really tasty. We also ordered two .5 L dunkel's, which were lovely and definitely tasted as they did in Munich.

I had intended to order the jägerschnitzel, as it's one of my favorite German dishes, but chickened out at the last minute, because I was terrified they wouldn't do it justice - especially the spätzle, haha. I was right to avoid it, but more on that later...I opted for the brats in a blanket, and my husband ordered the wurst plate, with a weisswurst and Oktoberfest brat, sauerkraut, and spätzle.

Food comes out, and my brats in a blanket are...hard. Overcooked for sure. The smoked brats had decent flavor, but just way overcooked. Fries were good, though! I dipped them in leftover bier cheese, totally recommend. My husband's reports on the wurst plate - weisswurst had basically zero flavor, very bland, but the Oktoberfest brat was good. Sauerkraut was sauerkraut, yay! 

Now, about the spätzle...it's from a package. Hands down. Like, the kind you can buy in the international section of your local Kroger. If you've ever had real spätzle, it's almost like a German dumpling and a noodle had a baby - they should be slightly dense, buttery, salty, and delicious. These tasted like...rubbery eggs. Really, really disappointing. I get that they're feeding the masses here but I make it at home from my mother in law's recipe and it's so simple to prepare, and 100x more delicious than the freeze dried stuff they're serving here. 

So...in conclusion. Come here for beers and a pretzel. Entree food was mediocre, at best. Service was great and prices were high, but eh, that's Opry Mills for ya. I might come back for that apple strudel, though...!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is a must go. It's about 30 min outside of nashville but absolutely worth the drive. The service was spectacular from the hostesses to the servers and even the bakers making the biscuits (you can even watch them do it!). The portion sizes are perfect. Not too big and not too small. I got the country fried steak and a side of the hash brown casserole. The casserole was insanely good. You must get it if you go!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I rarely give a restaurant five stars, but Loveless Café earns it. I do my share of traveling and this is hands-down the best breakfast in the United States, especially if you like southern cooking. Once you check put the strawberry, BlackBerry, and peach jam on your biscuits you will be hooked. The hash brown casserole is wonderful as is the sausage gravy. Everything tasted so fresh Like breakfast should taste. You will want to get there early as we were told by the restaurant to arrive at 9:45 and there would be no wait. However when we got there at 9:40 it was already 40 minutes, but only took about 25 to get to our table. This is a great place out in the country and you will want to visit.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My friend recommended me to this spot and I was happy that she did.  I was a little surprised at the wait time of an hour, but there was plenty to do walking around the grounds.  When we got seated, the staff was hustling and bustling.  As I looked around to the full dining room, everyone seemed so happy.  That is what good food will do.  I had the sampler with hot fried chicken, pulled pork, and catfish.  So good, every bite was top notch.  I watched them making the biscuits in the back and frying up the chickens across the way.  It is worth the hype, just try to be patient, your belly with thank you, your cardiologist, not so much.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
What's not to love, it's all the delicious biscuits you can eat. The country ham with redeye gravy is delicious. Ask the waiter for honey to go with your biscuits...fabulous. I think this place is a must see, 500,000 people a year visit, that kinda proves the point.

The service is top notch, and so is the coconut cream pie!

name: Analog at Hutton Hotel
text:
They hosted us for a private event during a recent conference and did a great job.  The space is really cool.  Would be good for a private event.

The specialty cocktails are creative.  They use the block ice.  Service is hands on and if you tell them what you enjoy to drink they'll make suggestions.

We had passed food items, not sure of "normal" menu.  All that I sampled was yummy.

If you're in Nashville it's a little out of downtown, but worth it.  Enjoy!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The most famous restaurant in Nashville and rightfully so. Best biscuits in TN. There's always a crowd and well worth the wait. Come out Sunday for lunch when they have a special brisket special that's phenomenal. All the preserves go well with the biscuits

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I wanted to hate this place and assumed it would just be another kitschy tourist trap in Opry Mills, but left liking the place. They have a nice selection of German beers and they are available in 0.3L, 0.5L, 1L. the beer prices, even by Nashville tourist standards were very high ($7.50 for a half liter, which is roughly a pint). I was excited to see currywurst on the menu having eaten it on the streets of Berlin and falling in love with it. While it was nowhere as good as what I had in Germany, it was certainly better than any I've tried in America and certainly better than The Pharmacy's sad attempt. I will certainly eat it again. The wife had a wurst on a roll with potato salad and said it was very good. Overall, a decent experience and, while overpriced, a nice addition to Opry Mills.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This is a MUST in Nashville. It's important to go into it knowing that it's all about the experience. If you go during a busy time, you will wait.  Even if you go early, you will wait... but it won't be as long. If you have a larger group, you will definitely wait. Don't be surprised or frustrated by this. If you're impatient, then don't try to eat here.

Go when the weather is nice so you can pass the wait time checking out the store, playing corn hole and wandering around the grounds. It's a bit of a drive, so go when you are in the mood to enjoy the drive to and fro.

The food is classic southern and will not disappoint. it it a little overpriced? Sure. But you're paying for the experience just as much as anything. You'll get delicious food, and it will be a large portion.  You will leave stuffed and happy.

Again. Know what you're getting into. You don't go here for a "quick bite." You make an outing of it and enjoy taking your time driving out in the country, socializing with those in your party or strangers who are also waiting on a table, and eating a delicious southern meal in a charming old building that has been a part of Nashville for years and year.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I've been here a few times but took my girlfriend here for the first time a few days ago.  We got there around 6:30 on a Thursday night and only had a few minutes wait.  Our server was very friendly as well.  I ordered a bbq sandwich with fried okra, and my gf ordered a three side plate.  She chose fried green tomatoes, hashbrown casserole and mac and cheese.  

We always sample each other's meals and everything was cooked perfectly.  My only complaint but it's a small one is that the bbq sandwich really needs more bbq.  Other than that, we enjoyed all of it.  We split the banana pudding after, then went in the various shops and got a few things to send to family for Christmas.  It's not expensive, it's great southern food cooked right, fast and good service, and of course they have their amazing biscuits.  I'm a huge fan of the Loveless Cafe and definitely recommend it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: So good we came back twice. Once for lunch and once for breakfast. From the service to the food to the collar greens my husband couldn't stop raving about. The ones he loved so much he ordered a side with his breakfast the next day. Special place, wonderful food with true southern hospitality.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We are in from out of town for the CMA Music Fest and this place was recommended by family that lives in the area.  The wait was over an hour, but that was because they were busy.  There are a few shops on the property that you can visit while you are waiting.  

The food was excellent.  The biscuits are great when they came out warm.  The preserves they served them with were all good.  I enjoyed the peach the best, but the wife enjoyed the blackberry the best.  

I am a big fan of country ham and theirs was great.  The omelette that my wife had looked good and was packed full of vegetables.   

The server was very friendly and made good suggestions without being pushy. 

If you are in the area and are willing to wait this is a recommend for me.  

One thing we saw on the menu but we did not do since there was only 2 of us was the family style all you can eat.  Looks like a good way for 4 or more people to eat all they want while paying the same price that a regular meal would cost each person.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I'm not sure if it's the hype or a staple in many travelers to do list, but waiting 1.5 hrs for some over priced biscuits is not high on my agenda. 
They have a neat set up where you can visit their store or play corn hole, but can't say I'll be visiting this place again. One and done.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I came to this place exactly a week ago at the end of our stroll through Nashville. There was a 1-hour wait for my party of 8, which we didn't mind because the beautiful scenery outside and that warm humid breeze... and the fact that is place is a must-go-to when in Nashville.

The atmosphere is nice, the inside looks like a house converted to a restaurant so it does feel homey. We ordered the Family Style supper. We chose endless fried chicken, fried catfish, okra, fries & mac and cheese. 

I feel I must mention that the service (at least ours) was bad. Once we were seated and our drinks were brought to us, we didn't see our waiter again for about 15 minutes. You might think: "Because of the high volume, duh!" No, NO. We saw the other guy waiting on the table next to us go to them at least 8 times to ask if the food was good, if they needed something, if they wanted more drink. When our waiter was taking our order, a glass of water got spilled and he was completely unfazed by it. He didn't offer napkins or to call anyone to clean it up so of course we had to take care of that because it was going to be another almost 10 minutes before he graced us with his presence.

Finally after sitting there half hour with lions roaring in our bellies, the biscuits and jelly came out. They were the warmest, freshest, softest, scrumptious biscuits I've tasted in a long time. Break one in half, spread a little butter on it, some honey and then you can take a bite of heaven. 

Unfortunately for my waiters timing we were all still on our first biscuit when all the food came out. Give us at least 5 minutes w/ the biscuits please!?

The food was so good, you would have thought grandma was back there making the mac & cheese herself! Everything on the table was just right, it was helping us cope with our waiter's service

(This review was written about a year ago but I didn't publish it so instead of "exactly a week ago" it should be "almost exactly a year ago")

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Overall (and probably very unpopular) review: 
not worth the hype

((Lunch/Dinner review - NOT breakfast))

Good: no wait when we went (late lunch); biscuits delivered right to the table with fresh spreads. They were warm and delicious, light and fluffy. Seriously good.  Our server was helpful but not overly attentive or pushy-perfect. She was prompt with our drinks and food delivery, a great server (sorry I can't remember her name!) And you will not miss with the pimento cheese bacon burger. Holy wow. The sweet potato side was super sweet but delicious. 

Meh: Meatloaf was lacking. We expected much, much more in a country restaurant setting. Cracker Barrel's is better (and cheaper) and that's not saying much. 

Bad: Old, stale French fries. Flavorless and half crunchy, half soggy. Asked specifically for new fries, extra crispy and fresh... was delivered the same blah fries, just double fried (old fries dunked a second time in the oil). 

I'm just glad there was not a wait. We would have been much more disappointed, I'm sure.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Heavenly!

Walking into this HUGE space was like walking into my happy place. It was a little commericial in the front, but the prices on the retail were slightly better than when you order from some place like GermanDeli.com, but way more than if you have access to a base commissary. We loved the walls of steins you see, but didn't try that program. 
We were seated quickly since we purposely came before the Saturday rush. Our waiter, Fatjon, was fantastic! He was prompt, courteous, and funny. 
Between 4 of us, we have all the traditional plates: jägerschnitzel, saurbraten, rouladen, and the giant pretzel (plus beer). It's rare that I don't have some sort of feedback about food, but I have not a single thing to say besides it was fabulous. The flavors were great, thick sauces, spot on preparation, and absolutely delicious! If I didn't know I was in a very Americanized place, I'd have definitely felt at home in German. 
Con: The cost is a little steep. It was $122 for the 4 of us, so I'll stick to making it mostly at home, but nevertheless...we'll be back!

name: Drifters
text:
Drifters has great BBQ! And this is a great feat considering this type of food is hit or miss in Nashville.

A large birthday party I was attending decided to eat here after realizing we had no reservations on a Friday night. Woops! But Drifters had some open tables and were able to accommodate our big group quickly. 

We had to try the BBQ brisket nachos, and they were exceptional! They have a variety of BBQ sauces in bottles on your table, and the sweet and spicy was my favorite. I also had the pulled chicken burrito, and I loved it! Decent salsa and good fillings. I sampled the wings, and they were great too, I like that they use a dry rub on them. Their menu is great, and I had a specialty vodka cocktail that was tasty too! 

All around a great meal, Drifters will be my stop when I need good BBQ!

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Fun venue. The bands were great, the bartenders are fast. People are very laid back here and you do not get crushed. It was super warm with all the people so dress in layers.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
The Belcourt is a Nashville mainstay and a cultural treasure. As a local student, my Nashville routine wouldn't be nearly as enlightening without it. Come for the limited releases and programming, and stay for the profound sense of community and ability to drink while watching a midnight screening of Tommy Wiseau's magnum opus. 
The new renovations did not bring the sterility and identity crisis I was expecting either. The theaters were immaculately renovated and screenings are beautiful graphically and sonically.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Entirely too hot summer day to do anything outside so we opted for a movie. Belcourt was the perfect spot. We appreciated the free parking and the helpful cashier inside. The building itself was beautiful; very modern upon entry but the integrity of the older building was maintained within the theater itself. There isn't a bad seat in the joint and the popcorn was delicious! Plus, you can get a refill for $1! Their selection of films was a welcomed change from the other theaters around town. This place is a gem!

name: The Country
text: I have mixed reviews about this place. Great area.  Great remodel.  It can be a bit empty at times which makes it kind of boring.  Although, when there are people there then its rather fun.  I'm sure its tough to have two bartenders as it appears slow a lot, however, it'd be nice to have more people tending bar when its busy.  It takes a while to get a beer.  Also, they need to change the name.  The name really takes away from the chances of this place becoming popular.  All in all though, not bad.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Came here last night for the first time for a concert. Love the wide open concept of the venue but unfortunately, the parking situation is a MESS! Not only is it super cramped, but they only accept cash. It's 2015, they should have a card reader for their lot attendants. Instead, we had to search around for 45 minutes for a parking spot/lot that took cards. Will be steering clear of this place for concerts until they get their parking situation fixed!

name: Drifters
text:
Arrived here late after our flight landed and we checked into our rental down the street. The wait staff was nice and brought our drinks promptly. It was a bit tough to get water refills, though.

I had the catfish and the brisket. The catfish was done correctly, but the piece was really small. The brisket was tender but a bit too "mushy" for my taste - as though it had been sitting in water. I loved the "sauce bar" - lots of options, and all very flavorful. The hush puppies were the surprise-and-delight piece of my meal - the sweet onions and pickled jalapeno made for a super unique flavor, and the dipping sauce they came with was great.

One side note: we were there for over 2 hours on a Friday night and there was no live music. A band was setting up as we were leaving, after 11pm. We had hoped based on the reviews that we would at least hear live music coming in from outside, but either there was some confusion or a scheduling error.

name: Drifters
text:
Chose this via Google Maps, figuring what's not to love about bbq... and it's Nashville, chances are it's gonna be awesome.
A)This is situated in a hip little neighborhood and is on one rad corner. If you want to keep eating or drinking when you're done here, there's plenty.
B) It was a Tuesday early evening. Weather was splendid on the patio (inside seating and bar as well). Live music was just starting and did not disappoint. 
C) The BBQ was drop dead amazing. I ate every last bite on my plate and would've taken a bath in their made-from-scratch sauce (of which there's 5 varieties). Some of the best, smokiest, most scrumptious brisket I've had. Even the beans, which I don't normally touch, were devoured. AND the coleslaw!
D) Add to that 2-for-1 happy hour drinks and what more could you possibly want?! Except of course maybe a server who gives a damn, which in deed Drifter's delivered on. 
Happy beyond what I even expected. Returned two days later for a Round 2.

name: Drifters
text: Right at the hub of the Five Points area, this place had the feel of an old garage with a covered patio. Not much on decor, but the service was prompt & friendly. I was in the mood for a sandwich, so had the Drifter, a nice pile of brisket and pulled pork. Pretty tasty, a tad on the dry side, but fixed that with plenty of sauce. Cole slaw was really good, and the spicy pickles were a nice surprise. Dinner companions dove into a plate of brisket nachos, which they really enjoyed. Saw others playing corn hole on the covered patio, even though it was raining outside.

name: The Family Wash
text: I have been visiting Nashville quite a bit for the last two years and found this place based on recommendations. When I first started going here the food, service and music were great; however, lately seems service and food have been on the decline. It takes days for them to call you back about a reservation but that's after having to call several times and leave more messages. Also the last two times I visited they ran out of my favorite, meatloaf. This time around same deal with service but they did finally have the meatloaf. Clearly the quality has gone down. Don't know if they changed cooks recently but def a change in quality. I feel that based on my experiences that management and owners really don't care about the feedback cause business will not be an issue as they can still pack em in, although when I went this past Saturday night there were several empty tables. Good food and good customer service go a long way nowadays. Best of luck.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
The Belcourt... We looooove the Belcourt! It's a great theatre and I feel so lucky to live blocks away from it. 

We're members and try to catch as many shows here as we can. The staff is always friendly and I love their concession stand. The prices are reasonable and everything is good. The seats in the theater are comfortable and the screens are nice. 

There are always great movies playing. We love catching the old classics, the films we've never heard of, favorite movies we know and love, sneak previews of movies not yet out and current movies that we'd rather not drag ourselves out to the mall to see. 

The Belcourt is awesome. That's just all there is to it!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Hoping the band is better than the service. Security turned me away to use the restroom. Okay, fine. But then I saw the same guy turn away a 4ish year old little girl. Not impressed...

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: They were great before the revitalization, and they are still great. This place has it all: art, popcorn, soda, beer, snacks, screenings of old, foreign, and new movies! I am right at home. The seats may not be high-backed or reclining, but they are comfortable and I am happy here.

name: EXIT/IN
text: I've seen several shows here now and I really like the venue. It's located near some of the best bars in Nashville--places that serve great bar food, cheap but quality drinks and even allow cigar smoking. The venue itself is a good size with mostly standing room well suited for getting up close to enjoy the show. The drinks are fairly priced here as well. The only downside is that parking is pretty non-existent for the venue itself though there is an overpriced lot behind it, but if you get here early there is plenty of free weekend and evening parking on the street further down.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: There's nothing not to love about a historical building loved by its community and turned into a classy and amazing movie theater slash art gallery.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
The Belcourt is a beautifully renovated piece of Nashville history: the Grand Ol Opry was held there in the 30s. With a well-rounded roster of movies that encompasses everything from "arty" and mini-mainstream films (Inside Llewyn Davis), to seasonal, topical and director's series, the Belcourt satisfies every moviegoer's desires in its twin theaters. There are also concerts and occasional children's plays staged by Olde Worlde Theatre Company.

In the summer they show movies outside on the side of the building, with the audience in the parking lot. If you are an insomniac, the Midnight Movie series will be just your cup of tea. It is one of a very few Sundance Film Festival affiliated theaters, which means that it screens those films long before they show up anywhere else. Their largest fundraiser (the Belcourt is a non-profit) is a red-carpet event with cocktails, appetizers and other fun things that accompany the screening of the Academy Awards in the theaters.

As the Belcourt is a true community project, their concessions reflect that spirit, selling Olive and Sinclair chocolates, Yazoo beer, and other local goodies.

If you live anywhere near Hillsboro Village and enjoy movies, it is worth it to get a Belcourt membership for $45. Not only do you get first notice of movies and events that quickly sell out, you also get frequent discounts AND free parking. 

The only possible con to the Belcourt is that the lobby is fairly small and can get congested before/after movies and events. But hey - grab some popcorn or wine (yep. You heard that right.) find a seat and enjoy the ride.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Great, historical theater! Lots of unique events and arthouse films. Love it!

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
I've been here many times over the years for random shows and I've always had a good time! It isn't my favorite sound-wise but depending on who's playing, it gets the job done. You can always count on good people watching here, that's for sure. 

If you're seeing a well-known band, plan on getting cozy with everyone around you. It can get a little packed. There is some seating, but it's very limited. There's a balcony that's great for getting some fresh air, having a beer and taking in a pretty good view of the Nashville skyline. 

You can pretty much always count on drink specials happening here and the bartenders are great. While we're on the subject of drinks though, I have to point out the floor situation in this venue. There are different levels that go up to seating and then back down to the main standing area. BE CAREFUL, hahaha. There have been so many times that I've seen someone completely wipe out because they didn't realize that there was a step there. If that happens to you, luckily there will be enough people standing there to help break your fall and save your tailbone/face.

name: Drifters
text:
Totally love this place. Amazing BBQ, hefty portions, cold beer, brisket nachos are a MUST! And good prices. 

Went there on July 4 after trying a competitor on Main St-you know who you are! They were out of pork and chicken at 6:00 pm. Come on, what BBQ place runs out of BBQ on July 4!

name: Drifters
text: BBQ was very disappointing. Got the sampler platter, and most of it was dry. Left off the sausage, but waitress was nice enough to give me a discount off the bill. The rub was good on the ribs, but none of it was smoked that much. Staff is nice, dive bar feel is nice. But the food was definitely not good.

name: Drifters
text: Adam was our server and he was so informative about the menu and also other places we should visit while we were there. The BBQ was really good but the sides we just average. It's a cool hole in the wall bar if that's what you are looking for... Adam made our experience exceptional!!

name: Commodore Grille
text: We had nice dinner while watching up and coming singers and song writers, great entertainment. I would recommend.

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
I really like the atmosphere at Mercy Lounge. Its a cool room and it sounds good up there. I also like that there is a deck so its easy to escape outside. It can get a little crowded in there for big shows and its kinda hard to get a drink, but that's to be expected when you have popular bands play a small room. 

The only complaint I have is that the online ticketing kinda sucks. There has been several times that will call has had trouble finding our tickets and one time ticketweb sent tickets to the wrong show, names of artists weren't similar and the date was different. Not really sure how that happened.

name: The Family Wash
text: So after moving to Nashville I was introduced to The Family Wash.  It was one of my favorite places as I enjoyed the food, beer, and live music.  Unfortunately after returning from a long business trip I returned to a changed establishment.  One of my favorite items on the menu was the Meatloaf Sandwich.  My friend and I ordered the same thing and it looked as if they took one portion and put it into a blender, then making the sandwiches with this monstrosity.  It just isn't worth the wait any longer.  Go to Mitchell's Deli for good beer and robust meatloaf sandwiches.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: You so cute and cultured Belcourt.  So Indy and hip.  I love your full bar, thank you.  Oh and your parking lot. Thank you for that too.

name: Drifters
text: There BBQ is amazing and I LOVE GOING HERE. but... Recently had one of the waitresses steel a  pair of my sunglasses then lie to my face after  the next time... Only a week in-between I called the day after I forgot them there. Yes my fault. But when I called "'they didn't have them " but she stole them. After me calling and saying they didn't them.  I show up today. Full on front lie to my face about they were a roommates, when I could give a reason and " show " that they were mine. Just not cool.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: My wife thinks that the two stars are generous. Bad experience for us. Went to see The Devil Makes Three last night.  Waited in line for half an hour or more and opening band was playing when we got in.  The room was crammed full, hot and there are no seats.  Maybe I'm too old for a venue like this but I wanted to NOT stand up in a tightly packed crowd that makes you feel like  you are the one being canned, while strangers push past spilling their drinks while trying to dance.  We stayed for about 20 minutes before we left.   Didn't even see the Band I came for and it was just a big disappointment.

name: The Local
text: Great venue and music, but can someone address the announcer tonight. She was wasted and couldn't say the name of the bands right. Not cool...

name: Frisky Frog's
text: This place does not deserve one star.  As someone who works in the restaurant Business I understand how busy and crazy things can get but this was unacceptable treatment of PAYING customers.  We ordered our food before most other tables in the resultant, and after saying something the manager came over and apologized saying they were short staffed so we brushed it off.  But then ONE HOUR later we were still not served.  Finally, after two and a half hours of waiting half of our party received their food which most of it was cold.  Then after they were all done eating the other half was served their food except four people at our table, whose orders were not put in at all.  After insisting we speak to the manager he ignored us, and then called us horrible customers.  We were just asking to be treated as paying customers.  If this place truly wants to reinvent their terrible reputation then they need to replace their manager and hire more staff.  I will NEVER recommend this place.

name: Drifters
text:
There are very few things that frustrate me in life. Vegetarians are up there on that list. 

I was headed down to Nashville for a girls weekend early this fall & had a vegetarian in the group. As a self-proclaimed food aficionado I am pretty big on keeping people happy when it comes to dining options - and I spent hours looking for vegetarian friendly spots in Nashville leading up to our trip. God, what a difficult task in Nashville! Most places that I came across had one or two items that catered to vegetarians, but for the most parts the menus were sparse. ...and a person can only eat so many veggie burgers in the course of a long weekend.

Luckily for me (and the vegetarian in the group) I stumbled upon Drifters. The menu had plenty to offer in terms of Tennessee-style BBQ & it had an extensive vegetarian section. 

We got there right when they opened, so we had no problem finding prime real estate outside on the back deck. Our waitress was friendly & knowledgable, especially when it came to the beer selection. I was happy that they had so many local beers on tap.

We started with an order of the hot fried pickles to share and they were certainly delicious. I did a BBQ combo that I wasn't in love with, but it did keep me full for the rest of the day. A couple of others in the group opted for the chicken tenders which they gobbled up. 

For whatever reason though my vegetarian friend opted for veggie burger -  A VEGGIE BURGER. 

Vegetarians... they kill me.

name: Commodore Grille
text:
I came to The Commodore to play a round (May 7,2015). I was not expecting what happened! This well-trained wait staff was awesome! Our food was not only delicious (everyone agreed, and there must have been 20 of us!) but even plated like a high end restaurant! The prices were reasonable. Staff is excellent and friendly. And the entertainment is great, too! (Nod to Debi Champion!)
I will be back! Thank you!

name: The Family Wash
text:
I'm really surprised that it has taken me this long to review one of my neighborhood favorites, The Family Wash. The Wash has been one of my favorites since I moved to the east side 3 or so years ago. This little place has great food, great beer and a nice rotating selection of local musical talent. Plus, every December they have a jazz group perform A Charlie Brown Christmas, which might be one of my favorite things ever. They get double points for that. 

The Wash is fairly small with limited table and bar seating. I recently found out that they take reservations, which I highly encourage. The inside is a mish-mosh of thrift store finds, vinyl, Formica and twinkle lights. It feels more like you are hanging out in your friend's basement than at a dining establishment, which is a good thing.

The Family Wash has one of the absolute best deals in town: the $10 Pint and Pie night. Every Tuesday you can get one of their signature Shepherd's Pies along with a pint of beer. Since I'm rather frugal, I usually go to the Wash on Tuesdays. And the majority of the time they have a wonderful beer selection consisting of local favorites and solid craft breweries. 

My favorite way to order a pie is the traditional meat pie with added garlic. They take roasted garlic, mash it up and put it in between the potatoes and the cheese. It's PURE heaven. The portion is really big and I always tell myself I'm only going to eat half and save the rest for later. But I'm delusional and most of the time I eat the entire thing. It's hard to have will power when something is just that good.

name: Springwater
text: Dive is an understatement. Walked in with friends, walked right out. Still stink of cigarettes.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
Oh, Nashville, what we would without the Belcourt? Well, now we know, because it seemed like they were closed FOREVER for renovations. But it's open now - and I'm so glad. 

The Belcourt is, quite simply, THE place for indie, foreign, and classic films. And now it's ever snazzier than before. Wine, beer, and concession goods. Snazzy theaters. The best films. You might even run into a celebrity or two! 

The cons? The upstairs theater is TINY - and the seats are totally flat. Good luck seeing anything in that theater. And the parking lot is SMALL (they give you parking pass to put on the dash of the car when you buy your ticket), and street parking in Hillsboro Village SUCKS.

I love you, Belcourt. I'll be seeing you a couple times a month for all time.

name: Drifters
text:
Great, local, inexpensive, good beer selection great BBQ, and veggie/vegan options. 

Friendly staff

Lot of extra spicy sauces

Good music 

Quick service 

Nice and air conditioned ! 

Would definitely recommend

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
I miss the old theater! I mean, the new renovation is nice, but it lacks the character and charm of its previous incarnation.

They're still doing a great job, though. 

I first came here in the early 2000s and saw Life of Brian. And now I'm looking forward to seeing Tom Waits' BIG TIME on the big screen.

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
The acoustics here are terrible!!

That said, it is a nice big space and I appreciate that there is an outside sitting area with pool table.

name: Drifters
text: Went here on a Friday night and got right in.  The happy hour drink specials were worth the trip alone!  My husband and I split the sampler and all of the meat was tasty!  We tried all of the bbq sauces and did have a favorite but can't remember its name.  I also had the banana pudding, but I wasn't a fan.  The staff was very friendly too!  I'd come back if in the area.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I love this place!!! You have to come here and meet the bartender Crystal! Best ever :)

They have good live music, lots of debauchery, and strong drinks.

You can request songs from the bands that play live, just make sure you tip!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place is an eye catcher! 3 floors with live music and bars! I would've given this place 5 stars if it wasn't for the service that we got on the 3rd floor bar. I was with my boyfriend and his best friend, who is black. Which doesn't matter right? Then how come the two blonde bartenders served EVERYONE else around us and didn't bother to acknowledge our presence. One blonde bartender was older and wearing glasses. She was having a great time talking to two men from North Carolina who were RIGHT NEXT TO US. The other blonde bartender made drinks for people who came to the bar after us and then got on her phone and talked to the servers while we were STILL waiting patiently. When we FINALLY waved her down she gave him a smaller size drink than my boyfriends (they got the same thing) and then didn't even hand him the drink but she put it on the edge of the bar on HER side for him to reach over and grab. This is disgusting. I hate to think this happened but it did. Y'all should be ASHAMED.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Gina is the greatest bar tender I've ever had!! She served me the best Miller Lite's all night long!! Oh and she's beautiful!!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Please read what happened to my friend at Honkey Tonk Central....absolutely awful: 
https://www.facebook.com/marshall.gregory/posts/10205989182234258?fref=nf

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Well ya see now I went down to the Honky Tonk Central in good ole Nashville.  Let me tell you this place was wild as young buck lookin for a philly.  From what I can remember there was tig ole bitties bouncing around everywhere and the music was just about damn near perfect.  My one and only one complaint was there was a huge empty bottle of tequila on the bar which made me more frustrated than a dinkleberry stuck to my sole butt hair... turns out it was the damn tip jar! God bless merica

name: The Pink Slip Lounge
text:
Ok so let me explain right off the bat that this is JUST a hotel bar. If you are going here as a destination then you are probably going to be a little disappointed. 
It's located inside The Hotel Preston, which is a recently remodeled property right next to the Nashville Airport

The main reason it's getting 3 stars is because it has live music, and there were a couple of locals that seem to be regulars...even though it's a hotel bar...that come here and dance. I'm a pretty nostalgic kinda guy so I love it when old people get drunk and dance like they are young. Without this ambiance I would probably have to knock it down to 2 stars.

With that being said, if you ARE staying in the hotel, and don't really wanna venture out then definitely stop in. It connects to the restaurant and you can order limited offerings from the restaurant at the bar. We didn't eat, but the people around us who got food seemed to be pretty pleased with it and it looked above average.

There is a pool table, a dance floor, the stage is actually a pretty decent size, and the band they had playing did a really good set with a nashville pop twang sound covering 70's and 80's classic rock. 
The drinks are on par with what you would expect. $4-$5 per beer and $5-$6 for a glass of wine. They have an average beer selection. The bar isn't overstocked though and they have a pretty limited liquor selection.
They do have a happy hour though which I would definitely check out if you are staying at the hotel. 

The bartender also really knocked them up a star. She was a super friendly middle aged woman. After asking her for the check after just one drink...she asked us about our plans and told us: "come on back down to the bar if you don't find anything better to do around town." After that I asked her what time the bar closed and she just laughed and said "we just kinda close when everybody leaves." maybe 11...maybe 1"

name: The Station Inn
text: Got a pitcher of Yazoo for $15, grabbed a seat, and listened in awe to the bluegrass band of the night. A definite must stop whether you are visiting (we are from california) or a local. Great talent on stage, relaxing environment (great for a chill date or to catch up with old buddies). The sound system is really great. There was a $12 cover charge when we went on a Friday night... 100% worth it. The decor was fun too with posters of various bluegrass concerts and festivals, dim lighting, and laid back seating/tables.

name: The Station Inn
text:
I would venture to say that the Station Inn is the most authentic music venue in Nashville, and I just love it. This was my second time here and my second time in Nashville. 

Both times that I've been we've seen a great bluegrass band - the first time it was Fireball Mail, and this time it was Blue Mafia. Get there early for shows like this, the place fills up so quickly! Cover for both shows was around $15, cash at the door. On Sundays they have a bluegrass jam. Unfortunately they didn't have it happening when we were there last weekend, but I would have loved to go to that too. Occasionally, you'll get some famous talent stopping in as well. The Steeldrivers still play here!

They have a few local beers on tap and sell beer in pitchers, and they also have cheap delicious popcorn too!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Went today (a Saturday) between 2 and 4. Great band. Great crowd. Ordered beers from the bar on first floor. Bartender had my card for 3 min tops. I grabbed it as soon as she brought it back, even left a respectable tip. Just a few hours later I'm getting fraud alerts from my bank. Very disappointing. I won't be back. Management needs to get control of its staff.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Was there for a bachelorette party. They really made us feel special. They let us reserve a table for 16 ladies in the back room with an amazing view of the river. They held a VIP booth area for us right next to the band. The manager really helped to make this all happen as easy as possible. The only thing that I would warn you is not to get the spicy chicken unless you like your food really really hot. Over all the experience was amazing and I would defiantly come back again.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Good buffalo wrap, nice music, it was cool to be on the 2nd floor with balconies and open windows during lunch time.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: The door man was so southern and nice. We got our drinks fast and although packed you didn't have to run into people every time you chose to move. The music was good as well.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
We went here for a day drink - no judgment from y'all - and it was certainly okay.  Really, just fine. For those of you from the East Coast, you know "fine" is not how you want to be described.

Now, I can't comment on food, but what I saw looked decent...the service was a little rough around the edges.  That's why this place gets two stars.  No, it wasn't crowded, and the beers on tap were plentiful, but the bartender was not paying all that much attention.  It might have been too early in the day, but there was also not any live music, nor was there any semblance of a server at the patio tables. 

The rooftop deck offered amazing views of Broadway, but from my particular visit, this was the only plus to the place.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I had so much fun that I we went twice in one day. We ran the Country Music 1/2 Marathon and this seemed to be the unofficial-official after race spot! Wr had lunch there and it was the typical bar food...nothing to write home about but after a long race, who cares. The drinks were great and the atmosphere made up for the food.
We returned later that night as we were bar hopping. Had a great time!
I would definitely return next time I'm in Nashville!!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Loved this place, only been once, but it was almost a Holy experience. Coming in from Knoxville, treating my sister to a birthday concert in the form of seeing Chris Whitley live.  I'm a huge Chris Whitley fan and saw him years back kill it at a show in St. Louis. On the way into town, my sister's car broke down, but we still made it to the show. What could have been an awful experience turned into a great one because everybody we encountered took good care of us and displayed true hospitality, patrons and staff alike. This is a small, intimate venue for serious music lovers. I didn't know this at the time, but Chris Whitley was dying from lung cancer and would pass away only a few months later. This place has, or at least had soul the last time I was there. Gotta hit it up again soon!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
If you want to be in the heart of Broadway and hear some awesome live music at any time of day on any day of the week, go here. At night, they will have 3 live bands going on 3 floors. You can walk to the river from here and be in the heart of the action.

This place is massive. Bartenders are fast, lots of hot people dancing and going on stage with the band and the music is always good. They leave the doors open so you can hear it from the street.

The best part is the balcony overlooking Broadway where you can drink and people watch. Huge windows overlooking every corner of the street. Some of the balconies have a background of brick walls from the building across the way and with the wind blowing and the music going, that feels pretty nice. Not many places, if any, on Broadway that have that.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Walked in w a group of 5. Got carded. Walked up to the bar. Got carded again.  Went to a different bar in the same restaurant.  Got our drinks.  As we were sitting at our table, we got randomly carded for no reason AGAIN! At that point, I'm out. I'm not going to profiled(and I don't need explain WHY)) anymore today.  Never going here again

name: The Station Inn
text: !!!An amazing set of cosmic variables aligned to create a magicle backwoods night at the station inn. Randomly stumbled upon it through an ad hoc waiter recommendation. The "Pizza and Yuengling" sign signaled good vibes instantly.  For 2.5 hours, we experienced the best banjo-tastic bluegrass music I've ever witnessed. Next visit to nashville, "Station Inn" WILL happen.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Just visited Nashville for the first time and this was my favorite spot! We ate there for lunch and then continued our drinking there at nighttime. Such a lively atmosphere and great musicians performing. Relatively Pricey cocktails but well worth it.

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text:
How is it that I'm a live music junkie, have lived in Nashville for almost a decade, and only been here once?  Serious life fail on this one.  My first concert here assured me that I will be back pretty regularly.  Beautiful space, great staff, great sound...again how has this not happened before?!  

Be prepared for lines to get in and get beverages (oh wait, like all other concert venues) but the staff are really great and things move along quickly.  It sort of reminds me of the Ryman but larger, and with a standing-room-general-admission area that can be a real blast given the right band (in my one experience it was awesome).  

Its right downtown so come early for the whole park-and-walk of downtown Nashville.  Tickets are usually reasonably priced for this venue.  I cannot wait to go again.

name: Famous Nashville
text: We had a great time at Famous! Beautiful decor! The guitar pick art is a must see... The truffle fries were amazing, but the last time we were in they didn't have them  The lower level is live music and the roof top bar has a DJ.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Favorite place to go to during my weekend in Nashville! My group always ended up starting and ending our night here.  We visited this place 4 times in one day.  There's lots of space, and the crowd gives off a really nice vibe!

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: I was looking for a fun dive bar, and thought I found one. This place has only bottled/canned beverages and no liquor, which I was not expecting. I would have liked it better if I could have a draft beer or cocktail.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We came here towards the end of our night and just stuck to the bottom level, it was good. The band was great, it wasn't super packed so you had space to move around and dance and it was a pretty chill relaxed spot. I would try it again, if we had more time to check the other levels it would be worth a shot, seemed like a good place for entertainment

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
The family and I was there for the first time to see Ward Davis and it was awesome!! Great intimate venue to watch live music!! Not a bad seat in the house. I was looking at the up coming shows, and they have a fantastic lineup. Any and all kinds of music is represented, so you will definitely find something to get down to. I can't wait to attend another show!!

Foods ok but the beer is cold!!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
My husband and I came here during CMA fest for a quick beer before heading to LP Field. Although the bouncer was super nice and let my husband take his Pita Pit purchase from next door inside, which was a perk, the music was pretty crappy, which was most definitely not a perk.

The place has a decent selection of beer, and seemed to have a lot of space/seating, but there was definitely a better vibe at a lot of the other venues on Broadway. Maybe it's just that 2nd Ave thing.. I mean, after all, it is on the same street as Hooters and Coyote Ugly.

name: The Station Inn
text: Please GO TO THE BLUEGRASS JAMS on Sundays. It is almost a religious experience, it's transcendental. It was one of the most amazing and soulful experiences I ever had in my life.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Won't play Beyoncé. Made everyone boo at me for requesting with $20. If you want to hear the same freakin songs you hear at every other bar on the strip great. Don't ask for anything original or they'll shoot you down.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I am giving 2 stars bc I came here and had a great experience the first time - nice workers great servers and friendly patrons ... 

I went back a year later and apparently they hired some horrible rude people.  I was here for a friend's bachelorette last night and when I got out of the bathroom I asked a worker how to get back upstairs twice because I couldn't hear him over the band.  He grabbed my arm and said to walk outside with him.  I said I was walking upstairs where my friends were and he yelled in my face not to talk back to him and to walk outside.  

He walked me outside.  I explained what happened to the bouncer and walked back into the front door.  What a rude inconvenience.  Loser with a Napoleon complex - cut your man bun and don't be rude to paying customers.   I went back inside only to get my friends and leave.  You know how to lose business.

name: The Pink Slip Lounge
text:
We had dinner, last Friday, in the Pink Slip Lounge and the ribs were incredible!

The were above and beyond the best ribs I've had in Nashville or any place for that matter.

The rest of the meal was good, too, and we really enjoyed the prompt and courteous service.

Thank you for a great evening at The Preston!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Nice dive bar...music is on all day all the time...haven't tried the food but people seemed to be happy. It's a great happy hour spot. Grab some friends, request music and enjoy listening.!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Atmospheric, good service and cheap beer. Best thing about it was My One and Only, an extremely talented husband and wife duo.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: As promised, I went back last Saturday AND Sunday nights.. Caught Tim Bridges and The Honky Tonk HitMen on the 3rd floor, Sat night and then on the 1st floor Sun night. AMAZING performers.. If you want a little preview you can watch some videos on YouTube.. Search Tim Bridges 2224... Or AMKing925.. I recorded the band..

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: It's a bar, 3 floors, 3 bands, lots of folks....lots of folks. The balconies are pretty cool. Dirnks were on par with the rest of the bars in the area, overpriced and weak. Can anybody make a good gin and tonic in Nashville? Anyhow, yeah, it's a bar, and it has bands. Bouncers may have roid rage is the only thing I'll say. Some little twerpy kid wasn't happy about something and got in the bouncers face and the bouncer, all 300lbs 6'5'' of him felt it necessary to headlock, take him to the ground and handcuff him. Looks like that bouncer wasn't allowed to be a cop, thank goodness.

name: The Station Inn
text: Legendary bluegrass venue in the Gulch neighborhood of Nashville! It's a dive with $11 pitchers of bud light and $2 baskets of movie theater style popcorn. The music however is at a very high level. Friday and Saturday nights at this place are a real party! I just saw Scott Simontacchi and Ryan Cavanaugh kill it there this past Friday night! Lots of players from the ABC Show, "Nashville" play here. Go check it out FO SHO.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Drinks are expensive, but the music is really great. I love how there are three floors with three different bands playing. I definitely plan on dropping back in the next time I'm in town!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: My friends and I were enjoying ourselves at Honky Tonk this past Saturday night along w every bachelor and bachelorette party in USA. A guy from one of these parties pushed me off a stool, which resulted in me falling into another customer. A waitress whom I had noticed was incredibly annoyed all night by observing her scream at customers to get out of her way - proceeded to call me a rude bitch. Two things I have to say about this...1. I have been in the service industry for over ten Years and therefore have an incredible amount of respect for people in this business. 2. I have dealt with some major jerks myself - but rule #1 - you never curse at a customer. The door guy extinguished the situation and he could not have been nicer. He also mentioned to me that waitress had been in a bad mood all night. Get a new job if you do not have patience for a packed bar. You're working on the hottest street in the state for gosh sake. Star for nice doorman and star for great music.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
An above average spot. A really nice bar. The band was good. One thing about this place that bothered me was that they didn't serve Gerorge Dickel. Tennessee only has two whiskeys, Jack Daniels and George Dickel. One can get JD anywhere, so since we are in Nashville, only about 80 miles from Tellahoma (where Dickel's made) it should be an option.

 The first day I drank Dickel was the last day I drank Daniels..

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
A triple decker bar. An impressive live band. Large dance floor. Fun night! A must stop for all those looking for a good time.

This was my first taste of the late night Nashville strip scene and it was a great way to start off the weekend. Live covers all night and a rowdy crowd made for some great laughs.

Holler 'N Swaller!!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Great concert venue. We saw Casey Donahue Band! They were great. The best part of our experience was having Candice from CA as our bartender. She provided drinks the entire night and was attentive. AMAZING BARTENDER. Will come back again because of her.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Saw Pretty Lights here and it was amazing! Having the skyline in the background was wicked. Recommend comfy shoes, big mistake on my end after a night standing on a hill but I can't wait to make this trip for another show!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
I want to give them a better grade because the are a bonafide Green Bay Packer bar- but I can't. I'm here for the Sunday Night Football game on Nov 4...
The bar service (from the kitchen) has been slow,and because 'the kitchen (upstairs) is overheating' the back door is standing open & the 53 F degree, rainy breeze is blowing through the joint. 
If I had wanted to attend an outdoor game and freeze my a$$, I'd have paid for the privilege. 
Despite complaints - beyond me- the door remains wide open. 
Get it figured out.

name: Alley Taps
text:
Definitely not 4.5 stars. Pizza reminds me of the pizza I had in school. Not wood fired.

Originally gave this place 2 stars. I have since realized I was way too generous. This place has good live entertainment but that is it. Bartenders don't know their menu. Food isn't good. 

Very disappointing.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: I have only been one time but this venue exceeded my expectations! I went for the Halloween show of Pretty Lights and was very impressed with the venue and the staff! Easy security that got us inside fast even with a long line! Lots of options of drinks. (yes you will pay around $10 for a beer but thats the same at like every venue) It is bleacher style seating that has an incline towards the stage so no matter where you sit you have a great view! It was raining most of the time during the show but the crowd was amazing and the staff did a great job watching out for everyone! Would return again soon!

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text: This venue was neat, with its historical monument feels outside and clean and classic look inside. It's located in Nashville and there is free parking from 6pm-1am by the library which is right across the street from War Memorial Auditorium a quick minute or 2 walk. Check in was easy and quick, the security attendants were helpful and friendly from doing their security search to helping us find our seats. There were several pop up bars available downstairs, upstairs and one in the bathroom hallway. They have a concession both with snack and beverages available too. Our seats were clean and comfortable with a great view of the stage, with the U shaped seating and standing option by the stage there really wasn't a bad seat in this venue. The best part was their music selection during the line up change, man Nashville knows their music! We almost forget we were at The Used concert, those songs had people dancing and singing. The restrooms were located down in the basement area which was a walk from our balcony seats and 2 flights of stairs. But they were clean and well attended for a busy concert event. My only issue was walking into the building, it could have a bit more lighting and I was wet from the rain and was like a ice rink. I slid my way into the entrance.

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text: Probably one of my fave venues due to the layout. No matter where you stand/sit you have a really good view. Nothing to block the stage like at other places. Also, well ventilated. You may not think that's a big thing, but who wants to stand around sweating your butt off? I can stand right in the middle of the crowd and still be comfortable. You can easily get drinks right inside the room or at the stand just out in the hallway. Only problem is the bathroom is in the dungeon. No problems finding parking nearby. WIll definitely be back if they bring in more good shows.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We did some day drinking and stopped by honky tonk for some appetizers and got to listen to the band on the second floor.  Prices were reasonable . Nachos and wings were good

name: Nashville Underground
text: Awesome experience! We had a party of 8 and made reservations. We were seated right away near the live entertainment. Our waitress was extremely helpful with drink choices as well as entrees. The food was fantastic especially the hot chicken and fried green tomatoes! The banana pudding was enough for us to share and was delicious!!! The operations manager,Teddy, was super nice and showed us around upstairs. The outdoor spaces were very unique with outstanding views. We thought the decor was top of the line and created a hip Nashville vibe. We're looking forward to returning to Nashville and Nashville Underground.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: The entertainment and ambiance was good.  The food was okay.  The staff was unfriendly.  Be sure to check out all three levels and have fun!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I can't believe the stupidity we  encountered, at 27 yrs old I've never Been turned away but the idiot in front " big e" pushed us away forcefully.  If you want to be assaulted and mishandled then  this is the place to be.  "Big e" assured that 12 of us would not be visiting honkey tonk central again,  tootsies is the place to be.

I can't stress enough the improper treatment of large groups by the honkey tonk central
Employees especially "big e":  it is exceptionally inappropriate the treatment myself and my family endured at the hands of the honky took central team.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Good music. Had fun until.... Security staff are assholes!!!! We got kicked out after being got told once to get once off the bar stool once. Which I understood and got off. We spent over a couple hundred bucks in there. Fuck those stupid big headed security dike bitches! Assholes!!!!!!!!!!! We weren't out of line. Respect they need to learn the word. BT you need to check your staff!!!!!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Horrible service and attitude from staff.  This is a bar, not a restaurant. I'm absolutely shocked that anyone gave over 2 stars.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Awesome venue! There truly is not a bad seat in the house. I love going to see shows there. Their Nashville Sunday night is super fun to go to! The food is pretty good and the waiting staff is real quick and attentive considering how large and crowded it can get in there! If you get a chance to see a show here do it!!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great place to go if you're from out of town.  You can feel the Nashville vibes!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Wise! 

Zeota Road! If lucky to hear them here: consider yourself blessed ~~

SetUp: 2 beauty gals with madTalent + fiddle from SouthDakota (!?!) now, killing it. 

brother crushing it too on all the guitars (Parachute and GBrooks - calling Baton Rouge) -- they pulled in one of bestBESTbackup guitarist: Jay! Really killing it for all ages and such.... Feel lucky to have heard 'em here first...

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Always a long wait and I had a rude bartender on the first floor. Music is good on every floor but service is better upstairs.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Good venue for a fun concert. The refreshment prices are way over the top expensive!  $7.50 for a bottle of water? Are you kidding me!?!

name: Famous Nashville
text: The Chicken N Waffles are so good here. Music is good, beer is cold, friendly wait staff.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Atmosphere is great. Service was okay. Drinks are way over priced. The hot chicken is ignorant hot. The chicken and biscuits was bland and rubbery.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Friendly service. Food was good. Music was great. Only request would be to turn it down. Would be even better if not so loud.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Food was good, better than most for bar food. They were short servers but told us right away so we ordered from the bar. Fun place, good food for a casual night in Nashville

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text:
With mixed emotions, we have to give this place five stars, and would have given six if that was an option. Our dilemma is that we really do not want everyone else to know about this place. We selfishly want to keep it to ourselves. You see, what makes this place so perfect is that it already has the best clientele, best staff, and best vibe. 

If you are looking for a touristy "honky-tonk" experience, there are plenty of downtown options for you. If your idea of bar food includes things like a $25 bowl of squid ink infused gluten free ramen, there are plenty of options for you in the Gulch. If you want to swill $6 drafts while your senses are assaulted by a shockingly loud and untalented house band, Soulshine Pizza is just the spot for you.  

All kidding aside (mostly),if you want to grab a few beers in a low-key, safe, friendly little bar where a guitar is routinely passed around so that the patrons can sing a tune, this is your spot. The crowd here is eclectic and warm. Just don't tell anyone else, OK?

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Merry thank goodness you guys have been fun Erin tthank morning I hope was love u I you have to do get be w

name: Famous Nashville
text: My favorite bar on the Broadway strip.  There was country music live downstairs with a great rooftop. The rooftop overlooks the river and they played current hits and hip hop. So if want a little different feel from the honky tonk hit the roof at Famous Saloon.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: For fans of outdoor venues this is a beautiful backdrop along the river. Definitely one to plan to arrive early and soak up the sunset before the show. Take advantage of the food trucks because the food in venue is pricey and tends to be at front of venue. One weird thing is you can't lean against the wall along the walkway. There is a phone charging station and we were leaning against the wall waiting for phone and had to stand up. Trust me, it is like an alarm goes off as soon as you touch it. Funny but didn't ruin an evening just different. The sound was great and the walk over bridge from the parking at stadium saved us time missing a lot of traffic after the show. We were driving back to hotel and heading north. One thing to note is food is scarce after 9 on weekdays and construction makes the evening drive a pain heading north.

name: The Station Inn
text: The entertainment was fantastic. I really  enjoyed the show but the door man was quite rude. I was told to stop talking to my wife as if I were distracting others. Though I  asked those around us after the show if I were being disruptive or disrespectful and nobody said  i was. Being told to stop talking quietly to my wife was definitely a  mood killer. I was having a  great time  until then. Will not be back.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
Off-Broadway!

We liked what we heard as we were walking by, so we went in. Luke Lander was singing, and we stayed for a couple of hours. We really enjoyed his music. 

Beer was colder and more reasonably priced than at honky tonks on Broadway. We had eaten at Pucketts, so food was not an option; however, several others were eating and their food looked good.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Today we had this AMAZING waiter Kirk! This guy had so much pep in his step, managed the entire floor efficiently and was a TON of fun! He literally made everyone feel special and made the atmosphere so much fun in this Saturday afternoon.  Thanks so much for making our day so much fun. We had no intentions of staying this long, but he made it worth it! Rock that bandana! You made this day!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Was there and saw an AMAZING band. RodeoGypsy. They mentioned they were playing the next day there too so we went back...... that being said the music was where the positives stopped. Service was straight terrible. Over 30 minutes every time you ordered a drink at the table. If you went to the bar the bar tender would take your empty and then not say anything... you had to ask every time for another drink.... was just really weird.  It was like no one that worked there actually wanted to be there

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: A great little bar of of the overly load and crowed Broadway honk tonks. This a great little place with good service, good drinks at a fair price and you don't have to yell in the waitresses' ear to order. The entertainment was awesome, even asking for requests. This was the 1st time the two of them performed together. They did the requested songs great, unrehearsed and using their iPhones for the music and lyrics. Just waiting for her big break, the female singer will go on to become a country star someday. I think her name was Jessie and I am sure I will recognized her when she hits it big.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
We really enjoyed Honky Tonk Central. We stopped in for music and drinks. We watched a few bands on a few floors and they were all great. 

The drinks are strong and the bartenders did a great job with the big crowd on a Saturday night. 

My cousins went earlier on the day and got the hot chicken. They said it tastes really good but will light you ON FIRE it's so hot! lol. Be ware! They didn't offer different levels of hot like Haddie Bs

name: The Station Inn
text:
I went with a group of people to watch Bluegrass at the The Station Inn.  What a great experience.  Normally there is a cover charge but on this night there was not.  

As noted in other reviews, this place is a dive with an assortment of chairs in tables.  You have to find your own seats, which can be difficult.

The bar is towards the far end of the room across from where they band plays.  The service is fast and friendly--easiest to open a tab.  They do serve food like pizza--we had eaten so just had some popcorn (which fit the atmosphere well.

This night they had a Bluegrass jam that was excellent and no surprise you can hear the music really well.

The Station Inn is definitely worth a visit.

name: The Station Inn
text:
If people are showing up here for great food and fancy drinks... they're not using their Yelps correctly.

The beer was flowing, the pizza was cooking (there's something about the smell of a frozen pizza cooking...), and the tunes were carrying.  My only complaint would be that several tables around us apparently showed up for Chatty Cathy Hour.  Talk to your buds, sure, but if we had to hear about "Steve's ex-wife" from turtleneck who never once turned in the direction of the music... whew.

Once we moved closer to the jam circle (Sunday.  What a lovely thing.) we had a lovely, lovely time.  I'm looking forward to proudly hanging a framed version of the Station Inn poster I took home on my wall.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I saw a lot of reviews complaining about poor service. I had nothing to complain about. I experienced great service and entertainment. The appetizers and drinks were pretty good too.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Wow so fun!! Impressed with the artists and venue all of it!! A mist do when in Nashville. Cozy venue great drinks atmosphere is wonderful! Thanks to a local couple I met at Lukes on Broadway that led us here!! Awesome!!!!

name: Famous Nashville
text: $13 for a red bull and vodka. What happened to Nashville. That's insane. This is a cool spot a little bit off of broadway but come on, Manhattan level expensive. 2lb wings were okay. Nachos okay as well.

name: Nashville Underground
text: This is the worst service I have experienced so far in Nashville, Would recommend anywherer else but here ,bartender downstairs bar obviously needs to find a new profession, visited 8-31-2019 10:50 AM

name: The Pink Slip Lounge
text: My fiancé had to do some paperwork for a job here, so I waited upstairs.  A sign advertised that the Pink Slip would open at 3:00 today.  I even walked over to the front desk to confirm this was accurate, and she said it was.  It is now 3:21 and the door is still locked with a bartender appearing to clean glasses inside.

name: Nashville Underground
text: I am one to praise restaurants but I am severely disappointed. I had to ask for a side of honey mustard several times and when I went up to the bar to ask again and the bartender was beyond rude. Its a side of honey mustard, no bid deal but when treated with such disrespect, I asked for the manager. He blew it off which only made me more upset. My party of 11 dealt with similar issues.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Thank you for being the exact opposite of the establishment diagonal to you. You guys welcomed me with open arms after my racist experience at Whiskey Row. I love you guys for that

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We experienced the worst service while trying to visit. The waitress was extremely rude from the moment we sat down. My friend had asked about the seasonal brews, since on the menu it states, "ask about our seasonal brews," and she got real snarky and rude saying, "she doesn't know why that's on there, it shouldn't be." My other friend tried to order an iced tea with her meal and she had to make a comment about her Long Island ice tea not being a real ice tea, it would make it taste differently, when all she wanted was a tea with her meal as well. While ordering one of my friends asked how a drink was and she stared at him and just wrote that drink down and walked off. She never checked on us to make sure we were ok, only stopped by to make rude comments. My boyfriend had a medical emergency and we were trying to leave and not disturb anyone. I hurried over to get our waitress and waited beside her while she helped another customer. She ran up to me screaming in my face that we had tried to dine and dash on her without paying. I had never even left her sight. When I got my receipt I was looking it over and the waitress again thought she had the right to get into my face and ask me what I was looking for. She tipped herself $18 on my card and $10 on my friends. This by far, was the worst service I have ever experienced. My family and I have been long time customers of the Honky Tonk Central and I don't believe we will ever return now.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: My family and I stopped in for a couple beers. Upon leaving, we stopped at the restroom at which time our waitress RUDELY approached and accused us of only leaving her $9 to which we actually left her $24 on the table. After swapping a $5 from her for a $20, I returned to our table because I did not believe her. There laid our original $20. Not only was she rude our entire visit but then she tried scamming us, guess she took us Nashville first timers for idiots. Very disappointing! Will not return.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great onion rings (bun not heated on hamburgers). Yummy drink - Purple Heart but $11. Band was good. Not a lot of people in the place at noon. When she came around with the tip jar - we put a $5 in and asked for Wagon Wheel. She promptly told us that was a $20 song?!?!?!?!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Our 3rd favorite bar we visited in Nashville! This bar has your popular country tunes being played live by a kick ass band who keeps the crowd going. The bar is large and smack dab in the center. The bathrooms are a bit run down but oh well. Nachos looked tasty but we came here pretty full. The beer prices weren't the cheapest on the strip but this place has great vibes during the day, even on a Sunday!

name: Alley Taps
text: Sweet prohibition style bar underground Nashville, 100+ yr old building and really cool. Great bar & live music venue!

name: Nashville Underground
text:
We came in around 5:30 on a Friday night. We were heading somewhere else, but accidentally walked through this door and decided to stay. 
The atmosphere is pretty typical of the Nashville Broadway scene. It was pretty cool and there was a live duo playing. 
Once seated, we were each given a water and menus. After about ten minutes, a server came over and asked if we were ready to order. I requested a beer list which she produced and then left again. A while later she came back and we ordered food and drinks at the same time. 
After 13 minutes (yes, I timed it) I went to the bar to retrieve my own beer. The server was standing at the bar and I asked if the beer sitting at the bar was mine. She said yes and handed it to me. 
I ordered the shrimp and grits and it was great. My wife had chicken and waffles and she said the chicken was among the best she'd ever had.
