No one ever came by for drink refills or to ask if I wanted another beer. Also, I had to take a silverware roll from another table since there were three of us at our table and only two sets of utensils. 
As we went through our meal, I noticed something in my beer. I fished the bug out and showed it to our server. They took the beer and one entree off of our bill and apologized profusely. What sucks is that I had already drank most of the beer before I noticed. 
I don't expect much on Broadway since fine dining isn't really the reason people are there, however, everything except the food was sub-par at Nashville Underground. Maybe it is better for night life than it is for dining.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Horrible service. Went there during the late day and decided to try it again two days later at night and the staff cared more about talking to young women than letting tourists in to listen to the band. DON'T GO HERE.

The band was great!

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Great BBQ burnt end's and friendly staff.   The Mgr (Teddy), goes above and beyond to service guests.

A++

name: The Back Corner
text:
I live in the flats across the street. Nothing that TBC has done is wrong. The catwalks and open floor bar are pretty cool. But after stopping by for 6-7 times in the past 6 months, I can honestly say the people who choose to come here don't know how to be chill and meet new people. 

This realization came to a head tonight when I finished up at a work party (researchers, medical people, etc.) Uber nerds who don't know how to talk to people..... yet they were way more relaxed and chill than the people at TBC every time I've been there.  It's a clique posse circle while people watching place with zero interactions outside the people you bring with you. 

If you have a small group and want to dance to club music and look at people while ignoring them, this is totally your bar.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I have been here multiple times, day and night, in the winter and in summer. This place is a staple if you're going to visit Nashville.  They have multiple stories of bars and live bands, and it's always a fun time! The only complaints I have about this place is that it gets super crowded and the prices are a little more expensive than the average bar down there.  Overall, this is a fun place to go and hangout with your group of friends!

name: Famous Nashville
text: Shelley is the best bartender!  Great time. Great drinks. Great music. In the heart if the Broadway district.  Good music. Sarah,Beckie and Andrew are awesome!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This bar is a fun place to visit. We were on a bar hop tour. The music was good and everyone was having fun and dancing. They had the game on so it was nice to watch the game, enjoy the music and have a couple of drinks. 

There were a couple of reviews that mention the venue. I will say that the venue is huge and lots of space for a lot of people. I posted a picture of the crowd!

Overall: I will give this place 4 stars. Fun atmosphere and good music.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Well, the server has ignored us twice. So... all I can say so far is they are good for music, but if you aren't drinking, they aren't going to wait on you. 

To be continued...

We were ignored again. My husband had to track down the server to take our order. 

Don't wait until the last minute and get mediocre bar food from here. Come early and sample one of the better food opportunities Nashville has to offer, then come here for the music. 

Oh and don't order a margarita, not even a top shelf, they suck here.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I was a tourist which maybe made me love this place even more than the average joe, but how could I pass up the chance to go to a place called "Honky Tonk Central"?! We were not disappointed and had a blast! It seems to be a big place for bachelor/bachelorette parties too because we saw several from out of town.

I had the key lime pie drink which was excellent and truly/dangerously tasted exactly like key lime pie. The bands cover popular country music songs and it is just a lot of fun over three levels with windows open and a casual, welcoming ambiance. The fried pickles are so yummy! I had my share visiting Nashville and I liked these best. 

The staff is super friendly as well. One server we had, Josh (I think his name was), was awesome and made a friend with everyone that came in. I loved the vibe and the bar tradition of "hollerin' and swallerin" -- fun, fun time.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: This place is the perfect venue for an aging concert goer like myself. If you come early, you can sit at a table with service and everything. They get a wonderful and wide range of acts, from up and coming local bands, to 90s artists, and festive cover bands. The shows start on time, the space is very well designed, and there's just an amazingly intimate feel. Whether at a Moon Taxi, Yacht Rock Revue, Jewel, Wild Feathers, or the Long Players, it's a an evening well spent. The Sunday night Lightning 100 broadcasts are a particular favorite. Those things run like a Swiss clock, and on a school night, I sure appreciate that.

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text:
I've been to most of the popular music venues in Nashville now so it's hard not to compare one to another and see how they stand up to each other. The War Memorial Auditorium is a perfectly fine place to come and see a show, but just not my favorite due to some reasons I'll list below. Although it is an indoor concert venue you enter through a security check outside and then into the courtyard with the 'Victory' statue. The location and the exterior is the most unique thing about the auditorium. The inside, however, does not wow. My friend and I saw the Haim concert here, and that was awesome to see them! 

Pros:
-They have multiple concession stands and bar areas for snacks/drinks
-We had a good experience with the staff, from the security people to the bartenders
-Because the auditorium isn't very big and the seating is in the shape of a 'U' it is easy to see the acts no matter where you sit

Cons: 
-The bathrooms are in a basement so if you have seats on the upper level you have to go back down two sets of stairs
-Although historic, it really needs some updates like little lights on the stairs so that you don't trip and fall! 
-As with any concert venues there are lines, lines and more lines for everything

Overall, if good acts come here I'll go back. It's a decent venue with good seating and acoustics.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Do you enjoy the outdoors? Do you enjoy music? Do you enjoy venues that are easily accessible to downtown and there are multiple parking/transportation options? If yes then I'll see you down at Ascend since that's where I'll be listening to every music act/concert I can here!

I've been to two shows here (The Lumineers and Ray LaMontagne) and I enjoyed my experience at the venue both times (although the Ray concert was super weird but that's another story about him as an artist)

Other pluses to Ascend are that security lines are efficient, they allow you to bring in sealed plastic water bottle per person, they have concession stands and multiple bathrooms. If you are coming from out of town to see a show here then you can walk to Broadway after and continue the fun after the show since all the bars are close by here. 

The only negative thing I can think to say is that with this Tennessee weather there is always the chance that your show will get cancelled due to a thunderstorm or severe weather (of course this has nothing to do with the venue). However, on a warm summer evening Ascend is the place to be!

name: The Back Corner
text:
This....this is what I've been waiting for in Nashville! I'm not a honky tonk kind of girl and I don't enjoy overcrowded bars with bad live music so this felt like a breath of fresh air! For one, having a DJ that is spinning house music is almost unheard of around town so definitely keep that up...please! The other really redeeming point to this lounge is that the drinks are good and they are inexpensive. I'm so used to going to new bars and paying $15 for a bad drink making it very difficult to order more than 1 without taking out a second mortgage. The Back Corner actually has drinks under $10 and they are delicious! 
The vibe in there is relaxing and cool. It's easy to go in there, make yourself comfortable, drink a couple cocktails and just chill for hours. Next time I'm going hungry because the snacks looked pretty great!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Monday nites with the TIME JUMPERS still the best music deal in the country! And they start playing at 8PM now so the show's over about 10:30. We arrived just after 6 and found the last table on the floor...full house. But, there's not a bad seat in the house because of the intimate size. Way too much good to say about the band...these guys - including Vince Gill but not fronted by him- play some of the best western swing/blues/rockabilly/ country to be found anywhere..and for $20!  The food is pretty good, drinks too, and reasonably priced. Excellent waitress. Eclectic crowd all ages. Wish we lived in Nashville so we could go every Monday nite.

name: The Station Inn
text: Sunday bluegrass night was fantastic. It's free, which you can't beat, but really what makes it so special is the amazing level of talent. On my last visit, I was pleased to see the performers were a mix of all ages and genders, including a young girl, who was fantastic.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Just came here to drink and listen to music, but it was great for both. We rented a floor for a business party a few months ago and had a terrific time. 

This is the first time we have been back. We stopped in for a beer and had several. The service was quick. The music was awesome. It was crowded, but we found a couple of stools. One of our favorite places in Nashville for just good ole party music and drinking.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great music, cold beerGreat crowd. Who could ask for more! You n the strip 3 flora of music. Shame I cannot post the video!  A must stop.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This is a tri-level music haven, filled with all the local talent! The balconies scattered along each level give a great view of all of Broadway! The music is fantastic and gives plenty of opportunities for dancing and indulging! Highly recommend this for daytime or nighttime! You can't go wrong!

name: The Station Inn
text: In a world of staged experiences and photo opps it is so refreshing to enjoy a concert and fellowship at "the real thing"...

name: Nashville Underground
text: I am visiting from FL, and it is my first time in Nashville. My boyfriend and I actually had other plans as far as where we initially planned on going to eat and just so happen to come across this chill laid back hot spot with live music entertainment. We genuinely enjoyed our experience here at Nashville Underground. Our server Mariah was very nice, sweet and attentive. We received our food in a timely manner. The alcoholic drinks were pretty solid!! I highly recommend trying out the drink "Smashville" especially if you're a tequila drinker like myself. SO GOOD! The food is your usual bar food. But I must say everything we had tonight was good, we had no complaints. Our server recommended the Mac and Cheese (which is a popular side dish) we loved it!!! They also have a rooftop bar, so go check it out! The restaurant/bar overall is such a cool, chill spot to be at to just kick it with good company. Keep it up Nashville Underground, and thank you for welcoming us!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Fun place to learn about Johnny Cash.  Not so good for kids as they would be bored

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This is a must see for any Cash fan.  Great memorabilia; plenty of concert footage, videos, history and plenty of things I bet even you didn't know.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I'm not a huge Johnny Cash fan, but this museum was right off Broadway and we heard good things about it so decided to check it out. It was pretty cool to see all his stuff and learn more about him, though I expected it to be a little bigger than it was. There was also a room where they were playing video/music on a large projection screen but it got a little drowned out by the bass of the band playing next door. We got $1 off each person for being AAA members. It was still a little overpriced for being sort of small. A fun stop nonetheless.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
This museum is one of the best I've ever been to.  We just went there on Wednesday, May 11 and I was surprised there were a lot of people there in the middle of a weekday.  When you walk in there are many different kinds of t-shirts and gifts in their store.  General admission is $18.00 per person.  
     So much memorabilia it's unbelievable.  The exhibits start out with Johnny Cashs' childhood and his military service in the Air Force.  As you walk through the museum you can hear his music and see different documentaries on his prison performances and clips from his TV shows.  There are walls with all of his gold and platinum records, a history of his musical career, all of his 45 singles that he sold, all of his album covers, his 8 track tapes, and cassettes.  
     There is a small theater in the back of the museum where you can see a history of his acting performances ranging from Little House On The Prairie, Columbo, and film he did with Kirk Douglas called Gunfight.  They even showed a clip from his Saturday Night Live appearance.  Pretty funny stuff. 
     There is plenty of room to walk around in the museum.  It is very spacious.  They do allow pictures in there but no videos or flash photography allowed.  If you go to Nashville you have to see this museum.  It is great.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: A very special venue where the music, not the crowd, gets top billing. I really enjoyed the moving performances last night from Rivers Rutherford, Bobby Ham Rick, et. al.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: the food here is pretty great as well as the music and the rooftop portion of it. the only downside is the bouncers are very rude which is never a good thing. hoping they chill out a little bit over time

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Had a great time here, and I'll admit it helps that I really love Johnny Cash! From the love letters to June Carter Cash, big boots, guitars and his report car showing he did well in typing this museum is everything Johnny Cash.

Don't miss the room in the far back to the left. They play Johnny on the big screen and it's almost like you're watching him live.

I liked this more than the country music hall of fame, believe it or not. A definite must do in Nashville!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: They need to hire more bartenders or open the other bar. I know you want to make tips but if you can't handle it, get more bartenders! Waited more than 15 minutes and just walked out.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Wow, listening room amaze me for their talents! Honestly, I am done for those noisy music at broadway, living room shine my eyes, highly recommended to try

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Went there for brunch during a bachelorette party. The service was horrible to say the least. Upon arriving our server took our drink order, 25 minutes later we still had not gotten our mimosas or bloody marys. Mind, they poured the mimosas out of a pitcher so they didn't have to do much to "make" those. After getting our drinks, our orders were taken. The food was so-so but almost everyone of us had a something missing or wrong with our order. Additionally our orders didn't come out at the same time. We were a large group but their excuse was they only had 3 egg pans which just seems ridiculous for as large of a place as it was. 
After we were done eating and waiting to pay they kitchen sent us some hashbrown casserole which was good but at that point it was too little too late. On top of that gratuity was already added because of our party size. Overall I would not attend this place again for drinks/food. The band playing was good so that is a bonus. They were not understaffed when we went and we expected more from a place that wasn't busy.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: You need better door management! It's mid day, you're not busy, but he wants to be rude!? Wow! No..we weren't drunk. Hadn't even had a drink?! Just wanted to listen to music and try your bar?! Wow! I'll make sure everyone knows how I feel. Love Dierks, but won't ever go back to this bar?!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great place to watch great music. I will definitely come again next time I visit Nashville. The singers were all awesome. Service was also good. Can't beat the price to attend.

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: We came here with several friends and had a great night! The band was hilarious and talented, the food was yummy (the wings were a bit too saucy), and the drinks were priced very fair! I suggest it for anyone looking for a good time!

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text:
If you love Country music, Pop, Blues or Rock n roll this is the wax museum for you! Definitely worth the $19 (If you order online) entry fee. It's 24 if you walk up. They also have a $39 VIP package that includes a tee shirt and a VIP lanyard. 
Definitely worth the trip! Friendly staff and nice atmosphere.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
I was pre-disposed to love Big Bang because it's just like one of my favorite spots: Pat O'Brien's Piano Bar in New Orleans. Except that there's a cover (only $6, well worth it), the booze is cheaper, every woman in the entire crowd is married (unless they are the bachelorette), and the guys on the piano are younger, and funnier, and will basically play anything.  

We heard a lot of country classics, some Billy Joel, Janis Joplin, and some 80s hits...all songs you'd probably expect from a piano bar. But they also rocked out with very decent versions of songs by Eminem, Kanye, Lady Gaga and even threw in a Conan reference or two. The bartenders were fast and friendly and get up to dance on stage every once in a while, all in good fun.

The piano players are the stars of the show though; these guys are definitely talented, and they know how to work the crowd. Bohemian Rhapsody brought the house down, and Proud to Be An American degenerated into a chant of USA! USA! USA! All I know is that you haven't lived until you've seen 18 drunken louts* dancing together to fun. until one of them faceplants. 

And a good time was had by all.
___________

*Yes, they're with me.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
You go in then down and up.  Left right down and up.  It's a maze.  Because of the building size they had to squeeze all the memorabilia into one building.  It's good venue but perhaps one day move it to a much more roomier place.
5 stars for what it has to offer.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: $15 for two hours of parking, $18.65 for admission, and $25 for the t-shirt! As a record collector, I liked the audio, the 'mixing studio' and vinyl record exhibits. There were some real Sun records to drool over. Many exhibits had placards in Johnny's own writing and there were lots of costumes and guitars. The main drawback was the crowds. They don't restrict how many people are in there at a time so I couldn't even get to alot of things. There is no flow, so people will just stand and block an exhibit for ages.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
This concept is so great, but the execution was disappointing.

We ordered tickets online for $12 each, a very reasonable price.  We arrived about 20 minutes before the show was set to begin.  There was a line wrapping around the interior of the building. We were told to wait in line to get "checked in". So we waited, then later they stopped checking people in and started calling party names. This tactic worked better, and they asked everyone to remain in line for courtesy purposes, which we appreciated, since by that time we were at the front of the line.  We ended up being seated at a table right up front, but far right of the stage.  We had waters waiting on the table for us, but a server never came.  We had to go to the lobby to get drinks since the bar inside was booked with table orders. At the lobby bar, I asked for a cocktail menu (since I had seen some interesting drinks recommended on Yelp), and the bartender told me that he didn't have the ingredients to make the cocktails from the menu but he could make me something and he asked what liquor I prefer. So, he made me a drink with vodka and club soda (which I don't like) but I drank it anyway. I appreciated the effort, but really would have preferred a cocktail from the menu. 

We eventually waved down a server to order food. He was very friendly, but not very attentive. The show was set to start at 8:30, and we got our food (including the appetizer) at 9:40.. and our silverware ten minutes after our food. We had to wave down other people to bring the things that our server forgot. Everything was bland, the food really didn't have any flavor, and I bet you can guess what the temperature of the food was like. We had pot roast, with macaroni and green beans (they were out of multiple side choices). The green beans were terrible. Our appetizer was fried green tomatoes, cold and bland, served with a tiny bit of some sort of mayo. Our friend at the table with us said the burger was terrible.

The show was really good. The musical talent was fantastic, and each of them had interesting stories and quips to go along with their songs. The ambiance and environment was excellent. 

If you decide to try out The Listening Room, I would suggest skipping the food and have low expectations for service. You will definitely enjoy the show!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Bartender was rude & said we "wasted alcohol" & gave us snotty looks all night. Terrible wait staff..

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: We had been wanting to find a live music venue that isn't crammed full and in your face since moving here in 2016 and we have found it here! Our trip last night was a birthday present for my husband. Everyone was friendly. Service was prompt. Priscilla was our server and she was great! She even took a photo of us in front of the stage. Drinks are priced really well. Food was pretty good. Music was great. We look forward to our next visit!

name: Silver Dollar Saloon
text: This place is huge. The bar must be 75-100 feet long and they have lots of good draft options and live entertainment. Walk all the way to the back and look out the window for a good view of LP Field. My only gripe with this place is that it's just so damn dark. Very depressing, unless the toothless lady is there to cheer you up with her dance moves.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
The food was very good, beef was nicely done. Drinks reasonable. Nice ride down the river. The show was EXCELLENT!! Loved it. 
Highly recommend, it was fun.
Little pricey, but hey, touristy thing, well worth it.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Favorite bar on Broadway! For sure need to stop in, loved the Dueling Piano. Request whatever song you would like and sing along to this comical version! NO Slayer request, though! lol Good drinks and great atmosphere!

name: 360 Burger
text: The prezel buns are great but the burger is meh, the services is meh.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
My teen sons and I enjoyed this museum. It is very professionally done, and my kids learned a lot. In addition to a LOT of personal and professional Cash memorabilia, it also has sections on the Carter Family and the other members of the Sun Studio Million Dollar Quartet
The layout is VERY confusing. The exhibits are narrow, and as you wait your turn to read the letters Johnny wrote to June, you will be forced to listen to tourists speculate out loud on how long Johnny spent in prison (he never went to prison).
We arrived midday on a Saturday, and it was jam-packed, with about 50 people waiting in the lobby. The entrance is VERY poorly designed, with three cash registers serving people trying to buy tickets to get in AND those buying gift shop merch. I have never seen this done in any museum. Gift shop should have its own separate register. There was a lot of confusion about this for folks pouring in off the street.
Other than that rocky start, it's a great stop in the middle of downtown Nashville and a well-deserved tribute for someone who would be on the Mt. Rushmore of country music.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Paid in advance for a Luncheon and River Cruise.  The boat was down for a repair but the staff promised a refund on the cruise portion.  The food was buffet style and nothing to rant about.  I have contact them twice and no reply.  The entertainers were very good! Huge waste of money for the food and cruise portion and too bad their management can't follow up on the promise to refund.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
We came here on a whim after seeing a show at the Grand Ole Opry.  We were planning on just grabbing a drink and heading out.  We ended up staying for four hours!  The guys on the piano were unreal, for lack of a better word.  We were rolling laughing and singing.  There wasn't a beat missed in 4 hours, they just kept alternating pianists.  
 
We went on the night of the Alabama versus Auburn game, and the dueling pianists were taking cash for dueling the school songs.  It was fantastic.  It's a very crowd interactive scene.  

The bar service was very quick.  And drinks were cheap and strong...

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
This was a great Cash Museum. Self- guided tour. Lots to read about his history, lot of things to see from guitars to clothing and even some furniture. 
The little coffee shop was great with the 2 classic bean brew! And, of course, the gift shop. 
Thanks for the great reminders and trip down memory lane.

name: 360 Burger
text:
"Eat, Drink, and Be Local", it says on the back of the 360 Burger t-shirts.

I am not a drinker, so the offering of a selection of craft beers does not resonate with me and my dinner experience. But the time, money, and space that would have been taken up by such things were better spent on the incredible burgers and other sandwiches coming out of the kitchen at such an unassuming spot outside of Nashville.

With a name like 360 Burger, the specialty is not a mystery but the secret that sets this particular place apart is one that is becoming a trend throughout the country: a commitment to fresh, local ingredients. Fresh ingredients, prepared correctly, simply taste different, and in the best way possible. Those who know and love food, especially burgers, cannot be disappointed.  The beef for the burgers at 360 is touted as "certified grass-fed, DNA-trackable beef". Once again, taste the difference. The beef is expertly prepared, no matter which burger is being delivered to the table, and the flavor that comes through is one that cannot be duplicated at a national chain, much less a fast food restaurant that is accessible on every city block. The added touch is the selection of breads available for each burger, ranging from a classic brioche bun to a delicious pretzel bun to Texas Toast or a fresh croissant. Burger King may tell people they can have it their way, but 360 Burger delivers on that statement in a far bigger and better fashion.

The Bacon Basil Pesto burger is one of the more unique flavor combinations on the menu, no matter which protein it is paired with (burger, salmon, turkey, or chicken). As a traditional burger, the unmistakable basil pesto is accented by the smoky Applewood bacon and the woody flavor of the Swiss cheese. 

The Farm Boy is touted as "breakfast on a bun", and that statement is not a joke.  A breakfast burger with ham and a fried egg, pulled together with maple cream cheese on a croissant, the concept is easy and the flavors are bold but the execution is a problem. The croissant is massive, making an already large burger almost unworkable.  Don't get me wrong, I like a big, messy burger experience. Very quickly, though, the Farm Boy goes from a sloppy burger to a knife-and-fork diner garbage plate, trying to assemble all the pieces together bite by bite, rather than retaining the ability to eat the sandwich by hand. The burger is served on the croissant by default, but Texas Toast is a better option in this instance. But it is delicious no matter what!

Carnivores don't just feast on red meat, and the Blackened Salmon is the best option for those who want something a little different.  Let's face it, salmon is easy to screw up, as is nearly any fish. The salmon at 360 is seasoned and prepared perfectly, and that is what counts. With a brioche bun, lettuce, and tomato, what is already far more than just a fish sandwich is taken to another level with a fresh, rich garlic aioli and is paired beautifully with the buttery salmon and its Cajun seasoning. The Blackened Salmon burger is the best overall option for those seeking a healthy meal packed with a variety of flavors.

If eating healthy is not a priority when you walk through the door, forget the menu and order the Slippery Pig. The foundation is what is generally known as a "Juicy Lucy" burger, in this instance stuffed with Monterey Jack and Cheddar cheeses along with bacon bits, then topped with American cheese, more bacon, and garnished with leaf lettuce and tomato. Everything a burger seeks in a burger is present on the Slippery Pig. The pretzel bun and the brioche bun are both excellent choices for the Slippery Pig.

Side items may not be a featured dish at a restaurant of any kind, but are worthy of attention when they are so good that they stand out when placed next to an equally impressive entree.  The sweet potato fries are some of the best I have ever had. Obviously made fresh and not frozen, the fries were crispy and go well with a side of ranch. If your conscience will not allow you to pair a giant burger with a deep fried side, the fresh steamed broccoli was quite good as well.

The service was fast, friendly, and attentive. The atmosphere was modern, bright, and features a permanent setup for live music performances that are a weekly fixture. Parking is plentiful and convenient, and the establishment is located next to the Game Galaxy Arcade, sure to be a hit with any video game loving Millennial like myself.

Overall, 360 Burger is a gem, and sure to be a hit with every foodie that is in the greater Nashville area. Sadly, it is six hours from my home in southern West Virginia, but with more and more travel in the works in the coming months, every trip to and through Nashville will include a stop at 360 Burger. This place is not just a restaurant, it's a destination for those who consider food to be a personal passion, because those at 360 certainly do, and the evidence shines through on every plate.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This place is an inspiring place to go specially if you're an Artist/Musician...It easy to get in. Inside there's a lot of his memorabilia from his childhood and how he enters the music business, there's lots of things to read about so if you're going here make sure you spend at least two or three hours...They had a little gift shop...It would had been great if they had a coffee shop and if the place is bigger...Everything is cool and a recommendable place to go for museum visit...

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
In reality, I would rate this place closer to a 3.5.

I came here a couple of weeks ago with some friends and my husband. The place is much bigger than I had pictured. When the musicians started, the place was full, but there was still space to move around. I liked the place already. Not being big (or adventurous) drinkers, I just ordered a glass of white wine while my husband ordered a Corona. There was but one option for vegetarians so he ordered that portobello mushroom sandwich while I ordered the shrimp po'boy. I'm usually a sucker for po'boys. 

I actually really like the look and feel of the place. I love the concept of respecting the music and the musicians; that talking (out loud) is not "proper etiquette" in the middle of a performance. The food had arrived in a timely manner, as well as the drinks. To be honest, I wasn't the craziest fan of the food. In fact, before writing this review, I had to go to their website and review their menu, just to jog my memory of what exactly was it that I ate. So, one word to describe the food, unmemorable. What I DO remember are their homemade chips. I'm one of those people who eats all of her main food but barely touches the sides. But this time, there were some main entree leftovers and the chips were completely polished off. The only downside was that the chips seemed unevenly seasoned - some had just a dusting of the seasoning, the others tasted like there was an accidental dumping of the seasoning on them.

I would've rated the place a bit higher based on the ambiance, music, the concept, the great service, and the delicious homemade chips. However, before coming to the cafe, one has to purchase the tickets for a specific musician one came to see. We had bought the tickets to see someone else and ended up with four musicians on the stage, none this specific musician. While I mostly enjoyed their music, I still didn't get what I came to see. I really didn't like that - there was no offer for a refund either. No apologies for this little mishap. The tickets were cheap ($5 a person) but great service would've gone a long way in this case.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Just back from CMAFest. We returned to Swingin' Doors for the legendary Bloody Marys. Wow-wish we hadn't. The drinks were still great (though overpriced), but the service (especially the manager) was very disappointing. It's a tough (but profitable) week in Nashville, I get that, but the rest of town was shining with great service - Swingin' Doors not so much.

name: The Basement East
text: Good venue. Drinks were cheap and there is plenty of room to hang out and not be crammed against people. The cover on Friday was $10. I thought that was a little high, $5 seems more reasonable. The band was ok, but I probably wouldn't go back here and pay a cover when there's plenty of free live music at other bars.

name: 360 Burger
text: I have been coming here for over a year and have found the service and quality of food to be of the highest quality.  Justin, Brandon and the rest of the staff always give me a warm welcoming hello.  It kinda reminds me of Cheers..."sometimes you wanna go where everybody knows your name'!  I've only been there a couple of times when there was music, but the artists were always on point!  I highly recommend this place to friends and family!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Really fun vibe! $6 cover but checked in on yelp for $2 off. Lots of oldies and the whole crowd gets involved. There was one pianist that we really loved and had the voice of an angel. Would come back again for fun pregame with a small group

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: I was once a frequent visitor of the big bang, until the last experience I had there. I ordered two rum and cokes for me and my girlfriend. However, mine was missing the rum part. I noticed this upon first sip, it was only coke. I'm very understanding and get that during busy times people can often be forgetful. So, I politely informed the bartender that my rum and coke was missing rum. The bartender had the courage to question my judgement on this, then took my glass, took a sip of it. I wouldn't be giving this review right now had he simply just made me another one without questioning the customer. I wouldn't go to this bar unless you want to put up with bartenders that treat customers like 3rd class citizens.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Loved the concept and the artists playing then we went. This was our first visit to Nashville and a friend told us to check this place out. The food was nothing special and service was average. there are much better places to eat, but if you're into country music, the round table act is a must see.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Been here for 1 1/2 hours and having a blast!!!!  Should be 20 stars!!!!!     Music is awesome. Can not describe how great. Funny. Perfect sound. Great entertainment.  I need more stars. A must go to in Nashville

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Did not even get in the door. Made my friend dump her water that she's carrying around because it's 100 degrees out. Told me I could not come in because I had a backpack. It's a small backpack that's a purse. Needless to say, won't ever go to this damn place. No loss, plenty of other better places to go in this fine town that are okay with water bottles and backpacks.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Great Museum if like you Johnny Cash, this is a must see when you in Nashville...  Lots of memorabilia and you have countless opportunities to listen to The Man in Black....

name: 360 Burger
text:
Food was fine, service was fine.

I literally signed up just to put this comment on here.

Every time I've been here it's been relatively slow. Regardless if the house is packed or if we're the only ones there.
I don't typically mind because the food is good - especially for the area (Antioch). As far as the best burgers in Nashville? - No, definitely not.

For the time crunched lunch goers - I recommend ordering it to go. A group of 4 of us went around 11:30 and didn't get our food until 12:30 - needless to say we had to get it to go. Worst part about it was all of our orders had something wrong with it and we didn't notice until we got back to the office.

If you're looking to try it out -- definitely go when you have some time to sit and wait.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: The street of this museum and the front of entrancy museum smell so bad .... plenty of hangover not super cleaning after the wild night.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Eeehh. This was not a great experience for me. 

With out of town guests, a group of us decided to do a touristy brunch at the Listening Room Cafe. We came in around 10:30am with live music starting at 11:30am. Our table had about 7 people and the place was pretty empty with the exception of maybe 5 other tables (the place is pretty large). 

They offer a buffet for $18.00 that looked very similar to a continental breakfast at a Holiday Inn. No thanks. So we sat down and looked over the menu. I decided on the veggie flatbread with bacon instead of french fries that come with it normally. They offer bottomless mimosas/bloody mary's for the reasonable price of $15.00 if I remember correctly. I did not partake but had a sip and they were pretty solid. Not all orange juice and mixed properly. That's where the good ends. 

We waited an hour for our food. Then they broke restaurant rule #1. They brought out 3 entrees and then we waited at least another 10-15 minutes before the rest of our table got their food. Seriously? No one had silverware either, so we had to wait be able to eat our brunch. I was very cranky at this point and starving. Much to my chagrin, I discovered that my veggie flatbread was not a pizza, but rather a clump of veggies and a tiny bit of hummus in a thick bland pita, and made like a sandwich. Huh? Since when does flatbread = sandwich?  On top of that it was bland and boring once I started eating. The bacon was OK and they brought out french fries anyway. Unfortunately, the poor food didn't stop there. The burger was just OK, the chicken and waffles had completely unseasoned and dry fried chicken that needed salt. It was a huge portion, so I ate some of that since my flatbread was not good and left me hungry. I was not a happy diner. NOTE: One person ordered the pancakes and said they were very good, so all the food wasn't a let down, but I can't speak from experience.

I must shed light on the performers who were very good and entertaining. They were the only saving grace of this meal and sounded awesome. It was definitely neat to be able to enjoy their music at this venue. Should I ever return, I would not eat here but would get drinks and listen to the music. The place has a cool vibe and would be fun to do without the pressure of a meal.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Bartenders were kinda rude. There were wrappers and napkins all over the sticky floor around the crowded high tops. We visited on a busy Saturday night, but I've worked in plenty of bars and restaurants that we took pride in keeping spotless regardless of volume. The endless scrolling photos of bartenders in skimpy clothes twerking on the TVs was exhausting. This isn't a club in NYC or Vegas. People are visiting Nashville for a reason, so a bit more authenticity to the city's roots would be nice instead of promoting the chicks that are slinging your bottled domestic beers (cause they don't serve a single draft). The band sound-checked for like 30 mins and then hopped off the stage and didn't play any music. Overall, pretty disappointing experience. 2 stars cause the decor was nice and I like Dierks lol

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Go here for the music which was excellent but do not go here for the food. I had their signature smoked pork steak which was way over cooked and very tough and overpriced. The pecan fried okra had no taste of pecans what so ever. But the music was outstanding which is why I gave them 3 stars. The music and music venue was worth 5 stars but the food was barely worth 1.

name: 360 Burger
text: Just got home from my first experience at 360 Burger. Here are the pros: good burgers, worth visiting again just for that. Sides are decent. Beer selection also decent - lots of local brews, so good on them. Go Nashville! Cons: woefully understaffed, friendly servers, just not enough of them. And the worst part was: the food took 30 minutes to come out. Two burgers. Thirty minutes. That's way too long. I *might* go back, but a word to the wise: don't go hungry.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This bar was so much fun! Michael, the security guard with the beard, was so awesome and made our experience with our bachelorette party soooo much fun! He's the best!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Great atmosphere, Great food! Great live music! Danielle W. Is a great server and really cute!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
I came here with a bachelorette party, and was convinced to purchase a package deal ($50 a person) by an event planner. The musicians were fantastic. But that's the only fantastic part of the place.

1. The package deal shots were not drinkable. 
2. The champagne wasn't good enough for a post prom high school bash.
3. The event planner put the wrong name on the stage call-out, upsetting our bride.
4. The server never brought the appetizers included in the package deal.
5. The average age in the bar was mid-40's--not appropriate for a bachelorette party.

When I complained to event planner, I got no response. I do not recommend this piano bar to anyone. Musicians, go find a better bar! You were great!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Finishing up the 6:00 Show tonight at the Listening Room! Great entertainment . Love that they know each other and change things up as the evening progresses! 
Second time here and truly enjoy them!! Keep up the great work!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
I did not try the food, which if what I'm hearing is correct, is a good thing. We came strictly to have a drink and experience a rooftop bar, and lo and behold, we ended up picking the "highest rooftop bar in Nashville." Of course, we didn't find this out until after we climbed all those stairs and THEN saw there was an elevator. I wanted to die.

The view, however, was stunning! You can see plenty of noteworthy buildings from your perch on the rooftop.

I can't fully give this place 5 stars, because I didn't try the food, nor did I pay for my drink--one of my coworkers did--and he kept pretty mum about the price. I'm sure if I had a better gauge of the flavors and prices I'd be able to rate more accurately, though.

But to me, as my first experience ever in Downtown Nashville, it let me impressed and with a sense of awe over how colorful and musical this city is.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: We sort of stumbled onto this place looking for somewhere to get a quick bite to eat before a concert. We just made it in time because about an hour later and this place was packed as well. We ordered some burgers and tots and I have to say I was very surprised good burger but be warned it is huge we could have split one and the tots were super crispy...just good bar food. The bartenders were also great super friendly they were very understaffed but they got the food out fast and drinks steadily coming the whole time. We would stop by again for a late night snack or before a football game. My only problem was the band...they were good played country music like you are suppose to in Nashville but as most bars in Nashville they play at a level where no one can speak come on its only 7 not time to party just yet lol.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Ordered 3 vodka Redbull drinks. I was handed 3 shots of Fireball. I never drink Fireball and this is not something I would've ever ordered or mistakenly asked for. I was told, "That's what you said, I've already ran your card." I turned around and handed those shots out and went to another bartender. I also don't prefer to be pushed out of the way by men with girls on their shoulders for bottle service. My tab is worth more than that one little bottle delivery. Also, maybe your security guards would be more of an asset if they were snorting white stuff up their nose in the corner. Just a recommendation.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Service was great honestly food  is the reason for the 3 stars restrooms I am glad I waited u til after we had lunch but then I almost lost mine when I went in

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Stopped in on Friday afternoon after everyone cleared out to head over to the game.  Bands playing on the first and second floor.  The fourth floor is home to the highest bar on Broadway with nice views and comfortable coaches to sit on.  The Mac and cheese comes in an iron skillet and is pretty darn good.  The rooftop bar is great for beer and basic drinks, very limited on mixed drink capability.   Definitely should be a stop on you list.

name: Live Oak
text: Gotta say this is THE PLACE for a Patriots game!  The appetizers are yummy and just want u want to watch the Pats do what they do!  So do your job and head down here!!!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Such fun and very educational! Loved the many different areas with video theatre style learning spots. Great location and has a little shop and cafe too!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
We stopped in to the rooftop bar and had a great time. The music was great and our server Austin was AWESOME! He was pleasant, really helpful and treated us like royalty. He's the biggest reason we will be stopping back in here again next trip through Nashville. Truly the best time we had in Nashville. 
**We did not eat, just had cocktails and listened to good music. The view from this rooftop is really great.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: If you're a tan you have to come.  Location is very centered around 5th and very nice shop goo. Tastefully done.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Terrific live bands!!  Stopped in twice and enjoyed the bands both times.  Was extremely crowded on Wednesday night so not sure how a weekend evening would be.  

Drinks were good.  Didn't try the food.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: HOLLEE was amazing! Great service and made us feel more welcome than the other 11 rooftop bars we had been to. We loved her! Best rooftop in Nashville!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
My husband and I decided to spend our anniversary aboard the ship and I've got to say we were very pleased. Neither of us have ever been and neither of us like being around large crowds of people. 

We walked in to a buffet that had the best food we've ever eaten. There were two buffets and you could serve yourself from both sides so because of the 4 lanes you didn't stand in line long at all. You then seated yourself at your table (which someone explained where the table was as you walked in the door). The only thing we didn't like about this is we didn't have our own table and there was no sweet tea (there was unsweetened tea at everyone's table). But that will NOT stop us from going again and again. 

We left our table after our meal and before the show started so I can't speak about the show. We explored the boat and stood out back and watched 9 guys on stand up jet skis do flips on the waves the boat was making, for my husband and I this was a great show for us.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Too expensive! It was $17 bucks to see a couple of rooms of memorabilia. Worth stopping if you are downtown and need something to do, but wouldn't make a special trip there. If you are a hard core fan then maybe you would pay but for a causal fan like me who has seen Walk the Line and Walk Hard, then you will be underwhelmed.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
Stopped in here as my friends and I were touring Broadway and the various bars on the strip. Of all of the ones we visited, this one was the best.

The place was fairly well packed when we walked in. We lucked out in that people were just leaving a table as we walked by, so we were able to snag a table. The place is pretty big, with a long horseshoe shaped bar as well as an upper level with additional seating. We stayed on the ground floor and my buddy left to get drinks.

Since I don't like the taste of alcohol, I always request a drink that tastes the least like alcohol as possible. This place delivered as I got a blue concoction that tasted like fruit and whipped cream. It was one of the best drinks I've ever had and that is really saying something as it comes from someone who doesn't like to drink.

The band on stage was rocking out and was very good. They were a bit on the louder side and it made conversation a bit difficult. However, people were dancing in front of the stage, they were dancing in their seats, and people appeared to be having a good time.

My friends and I stayed for about a half hour. There were sports on the television screens. If people left, we saw more people come in. If I lived in the Nashville area (I don't -- I live in Oregon), I would enjoy coming in here to grab a drink, maybe give the food a try, and have a good time. I do have to say that the band provided a lot of the energy and enjoyment and I'd be down to see them again and hang out a while if I am ever in the area again.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This looks like it's going to be the new hot spot on lower Broadway! One of the managers let us take a peek inside yesterday and it is incredible!!! My friends and I can't wait to spend New Years Eve here !!!!!! Welcome to town whiskey row !! Side note: their food and craft cocktails look out of this world!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Ask for Jake! Sexiest bartender in Nashville! Best cocktails and service! He's beyond the best on Broadway!
Amazing food, music and vibe. Check them out, y'all!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: I was pretty disappointed in this Honky Tonk. We started on the 2nd floor and ordered some nachos from the bar. Once a seat opened, we moved to a table. We had servers walk by us several times and never acknowledged us or asked if we needed anything. We sat at a table with dirty empty glasses from the previous customer. I finally stopped one and asked if there was a server for our table. They apologized and gave some excuse as to why nobody has checked on us. It took about 20 minutes to get the nachos and we had to go back to the bar to get ourselves another drink since as I mentioned nobody ever asked if we needed anything.  My sister and I are both Kid Rock fans and she has asked me to get something from there. I was again disappointed that they only had a few shirts and sweatshirts to choose from. Would of been nice to have a bigger selection of his items available. I guess this isn't a "gift shop" it's a honky tonk.  With all the space, one would think they'd invest into more souvenir items.  The music was good and we enjoyed the band that was playing. This is a place I can say I went there but would not be my go to spot for return trip.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: We popped in here for NFL Draft weekend on Saturday night, since the nearby bar our event was at sucked! It actually worked out, because this place had a kick ass band on the main floor, and they rocked it!! We got there too late to eat, but the drinks made up for it. Great vibe, fun people, and it's right on the main strip. It has 4 floors I believe, with a different band on 3 of the levels, but none of them rocked it like the band on main floor. Definitely a go to spot.

name: 360 Burger
text:
Really good food here. Service is variable. They often have live music, which is sometimes the reason that I don't want to come here. It's a small place and it gets entirely too loud. Even worse when it's something you don't enjoy (country music, in my case). Too loud to have a conversation at your table. 

The good is always good. Best sweet potato fries I've ever had. Definitely beats the pants off anywhere else I've tried them. Great burgers, spicy chicken sandwich is also very good. Local beers on tap.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: We tried Kid Rock's on our visit to Nville because the music sounded great from the street. We were there on Wednesday night around 7pm, so it was crowded, but it wasn't a huge party yet. We ordered drinks from the bar (good service at the bar!) and waited a few minutes for a table to open on the second floor. Once we found a table, we were approached by Hayley B. No smile. No greeting. We ordered our meals (the food was bar food - perfectly fine) and then we ordered another round of drinks. When she brought the drinks back to our table, it was pretty crowded with dishes, etc. She left the drinks and walked away. My sister-in-law, while rearranging dishes on the table, accidentally knocked her drink into her lap. She hadn't even taken a sip, so the drink was full. Haley B walked by our table and saw us trying to clean up the mess with our dinner napkins. She kept walking and offered no help - not even a bar rag. When she returned to the table 10 minutes later, my s-i-l ordered another drink, and Haley B, knowing that the original drink had been spilled, charged her full price for another drink. Admittedly, the spill was my s-i-l's fault, but come on. Lousy, lousy service from the minute she approached the table. We enjoyed the bar. The band was good, the food was fine, the vibe was good, but if Haley B is an example of the service - there are a lot of other options in Nashville. Had we had a decent waitress, my review would've been a 3-4 star review.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: LD, our bouncer/security personnel was amazing!!! There were many people outside and he kindly walked us to our uber so we arrived safely. Thank you so much LD!!!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: We came here for a pit stop, we had been walking around and just wanted a place to sit. When we got here it was emptyish, we couldn't go to the second floor or roof top because they had a private event which is pretty cool. But the guy singing was so good! He was playing acoustic and had a great voice. Slowly but surely the place started getting packed. We still got all the drinks in a timely manner. The shots were soooo good! We really liked this little bar. Staff was friendly and quick even after they started to get busy. Will stop here again when we are back in town.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I got the shrimp and fish platter and it was amazing! You get 8 shrimp and 1 catfish filet. The filet is breaded fantastic! It's so light and crunchy! Some of the best catfish I have had. The shrimp are always breaded great and very crunchy! I'm a big seafood person and what I tasted was GREAT seafood. I also had some of the dry rubbed wings and they tasted great as well. Really love the rub on the wings.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: My husband and I walked in and we were greeted right away and I asked for a menu and a glass of water. A half an hour later my husband had to go ask one of the four bartenders for a drink. We were there for several hours in which we had to flag a server down every time... and we were sitting at the bar. The Spazmatics came on and the place became packed. We were having a lot of fun. The wait staff was much better when busy. Then the electric went out... it was soooo hot. The wait staff basically decided to stop serving. Needless to say we really tried to give this place a go. But after 4 hours of really crappy service enough was enough!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We had an amazing visit to BB Kings. Two of us ordered ribs and one ordered a pulled pork sandwich. The ribs were some of the best I have had! The cole slaw was delicious and the beans had some southern kick. There was even a solo artist playing that night who was very entertaining, wish I could remember his name. I would highly recommend anyone make a trip to BB Kings BBQ!!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
So by the number of meals I've had here, I ought to earn a plate (Saucer?) on the Wall!

Fantastic selection of brews (and a limited selection of wines and other spirits) with a good food menu well prepared. 

Ambiance fits well into Union Station and aside from various promotions (trivia and themed nights) occasionally live music in the evening. 

Friendly staff (where most folks know my name) make it an enjoyable place to take the adults and work colleagues.

name: Third Man Records
text: I've been waiting to visit this place since it opened. The Third Man Records building is everything you'd expect from Jack White: old-timey Americana, with wax figurine machines, vinyl records, a recording booth straight out of 'O Brother, Where Art Thou?', a listening room, coin powered mechanical musical monkeys, and even books of poetry and a collexion of album reviews from White's new(-ish) Third Man Books publishing house. The staff are knowledgeable, courteous, and very personable!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We went to see Carrie Underwood & the other artists on August 10th. We got there early to get parking before the 9:30 show and went to keep ourselves busy before hand. The show was great, it's so cool to hear and see other artists I hadn't known before- there was even a comedian! Loved it. We got really good seats for $70 each and they were even comfy & roomy because of the bench style. The key is going for an artist that you know and then it'll be worth the money no matter what, because you'll hear stuff you know and stuff you don't!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Well worth the $20 for the back stage tour!
They tour every 15 minutes, for a 40-50 minute walking tour.
The tour includes walking on stage, through auditorium, dressing rooms, mailboxes, member plaque area, sound proof auditorium, and stars entrance.
The building has a lot of character and the tour guide has a lot of great information to provide.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great pizza, best enjoyed in groups. Great beer selection. Some go to study others to explore, try 'em for sure!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: What an experience! We were so excited that we were able to get tickets to a show the day before. It was a 9:30 PM show but it was well worth it! It was Darius Rucker, Kelly Pickler, Craig Morgan, Lee Greenwood, John Conley, Chris Janson, and Trace Adkins. The show was phenomenal and felt like a once in a lifetime experience. It was a salute to the troops night and the whole room was filled with patriotism! It was awesome! Next time we are going to do the tour!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: If you love beer this is the place to be. And if you don't love beer and you want to try it out this is the place for you. Plenty of beers to choose from. Over a 100!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
I like this place. It's a cool, chill environment to hang out with friends. It does get a bit noisy at night, but that's all the fun. Their selection of beer is amazing, but I wish they carried more Light craft beers. 
The food is real good. The goat salad is amazing. I wasn't thrilled with the nachos, due to the grease, but that's also cause (I assume) it's real cheese, and not that "nacho cheese" stuff. very tasty and always good times!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Went with a group of 11 ladies all wanting to have a good time however when I ordered a Coors light and a water I was charged $12!!! Thought the price was way too high so we decided to leave. As we were headed out we asked two employees how much do they normally charge and they both gave me a different and lower number. I asked to speak with a manager and was told they didn't know where he was. As we were leaving we ran into a man who said he was the manager and yes that price was wrong and he would bring us a voucher for each of us for a $1 beer. He never came back with them. Sadly they lost a lot of money from a big group. I will never come back to this establishment or recommend it to anyone else.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We first walked down the Broadway which was very busy so we turned into 2nd street and found the B.B.King's. It was not to busy and we were seated right away. But we had to pay a $5/person cover for the live music (not all bars in Nashville take a cover) - one thing right away - the group was worth the 5 bucks. Service was ok - I think it's not easy to do a good job in this environment (often very loud and busy). I ordered the tuna sandwich - and I have to say it was really done to the point - nice rosa. I was in a lot of so called gourmet restaurants where the chef was not able to do it that way - so compliment to the chef. My son had the catfish tasted ok - so overall (expect the tuna which was superb) the food was ok exactly what you expect in a place like this. But I do not like this papers where the food is served on (that's to fast food style). I would come again because of the music, not to busy and easy seating and ok food and drinks.

name: Third Man Records
text:
Earnestly quirky & trendy, & clearly catering to a specific clientele, this Nashville record shop is a bit off the beaten path if you're thinking of walking from the downtown area.  This tiny, but extremely crowded & popular shop is overflowing with randomness.  Fans of Jack White & The White Stripes will be pleased.  Fans of more diverse genres?  Less so.  You're there for a reason & it's to support the output of this label, whether it's its output of releases on CD & vinyl, patches, matches, t-shirts & stickers, or decidedly more unique opportunities, like the chance to step into a soundbooth & record your own noise for posterity.

It's worth a visit if you're interested in a more spirited & playful side of Nashville & the staff are friendly.  Just go early if you can, to avoid the crowds.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
We came here because other place had 1 hour wait on a Saturday.  They said we'll seat you now. Ok so maybe it wasn't our first choice but, oh boy, this place was good. It's a burger place. You want a good burger then go. You won't be disappointed.  Go drinks too. Great Atmosphere.  Go. Take a chance. You'll like it.

Live music sometimes.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I wasn't aware that there were more of these across the country.  I am glad there are.  Maybe I can get back to another one soon.  As far as chain tap houses go, this is close to the top of my list.  Great beer selection and knowledgeable staff.  Very cool atmosphere.  Plenty to look at and talk about inside.  Their beer club is a really neat addition for someone who can visit often.  It was super hot in Nashville, the AC in here was cranked.  It may have even been a bit chilly for some, but what a welcome relief from the heat and humidity.  Check it out!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Amazing! Rolled into Nashville after 8:00, made it here before last call for food at 9:00 and enjoyed delicious burgers and 2 for 1 drafts. We'll be back.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Atmopshere- Good, the bf and I stopped in once for drinks and a 2nd time for food. Loved the music (live band) and the decor. beware, they do charge a $5 cover after a certain time. 

Drinks- Great, good prices

Food- Not so great, I ordered the pasta primvera with mac and cheese (because i can't resist mac and cheese). The primevera didnt have the variety of veggies im use to and was super bitter. The mac and cheese made my mouth dry. It was just awful. I took it home and tried it the next day, still nasty.  I just expected a better tatse. My bf did not enjoy his fried chicken either. 

I would still come back simply bc of the drinks and music. BB Kings gives you a break from country and and puts you into a world of jazz.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
If you are in Nashville and don't see an Old Opry show you are missing a piece of Americana.

My daughter and I were doing Nashville on one of my business trips.  She always wanted to go. 

We hit the bars of course (all fantastic) but decided since we were in town it was worth the price of admission to see what the Opry House was all about.

We were not disappointed.  I recommend you get a ticket and eat at the BBQ restaurant walking distance across the parking lot.

A great thing to do with your adult kid on a family adventure.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
We recently attended a very well attended event at the Flying Saucer and we were impressed with both the service and food. I was also reminded that I had never eaten here before.. 

We started with the soft pretzels that comes with your choice of two dipping sauces, we chose spicy mustard and queso. These were awesome! I had the buffalo chicken wrap and fries which was great as I could taste buffalo sauce but it wasn't drowning in sauce, so the wrap held up well. My mom had the hippie hollow which is a vegetarian dish of pita of greens, hummus, and other things she omitted. She got this with the side salad which was not only a decent size but a pleasant surprise of romaine, black olives, red onions, and "Italian cheeses". Another surprise was that unlike other places there isn't an up charge to replace the side with a salad. 

As I said the event was well attended but the three ladies who were working were pros. They carefully navigated the crowd and we never wanted for anything. Food was correct and hot. We did ask for water refills from the runner who dropped off my mom's meal since she was coming back with mine. She delivered. Only to have our server come behind her with two more glasses of water.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: DELICIOUS!! Super reasonable prices and a lot of food. Literally in a back alley. It has lots of character and everyone was ver nice. Definitely coming back!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Good vibes, good service, good food and good signature drinks...off the beaten path for a little something different..

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Great local hangout. What I like about this spot is that it's a no judgment zone. Everyone sings carefree and it's a good time. This is my second time visiting this location and the vibe was consistent both times. I would definitely recommend to anyone looking to not take themselves too seriously and have a silly good time!

name: Third Man Records
text:
This place was a really shop. Lots of neat items and you can tell that Jack White has created a really neat environment there. My only gripe was that the vinyl selection of was limited to mostly third man records and live albums made there. When I think record store I was expecting more selection.

Still really great place to check out in Nashville!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: You can't go to Nashville and not take in a night at the Grand Ole Opry. I mean, this is the place where country music began and even if you're not a country music fan (although, how can you not be? aghast) you can still tolerate it for a few hours. The night I was there, Trisha Yearwood showed up unexpectedly along with Garth Brooks and it was awesome. The food, the beer, and the bottled water are what you would expect from any concert venue. Go early because the Opry shares their space with the mall and parking is hell to find. Even if you sit in the nosebleed seats you can see everything because they have two gigantic TVs however, I recommend buying your ticket early enough so you can be as close to the stage as possible because almost all of the performers walked along that area and met the audience.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Really friendly staff and some great food! The catfish po'boy was great and the price was on point. Great location near Vanderbilt University and Music Row.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I will be the first to admit that by no means am I a country music fan, however I couldn't turn down the opportunity to tour one of the most famous concert venues in Country Music history. While visiting Nashville I decided to book a tour of the venue and am very pleased that I did. The tour started out backstage, allowing you to see the artist entrance and even the Opry Post Office where members of the Grand Ole Opry get their mail. We learned that the lowest mailbox was reserved for the shortest member of the Opry, Little Jimmy Dickens, who stood 4'11 before he passed away in 2015.

Another interesting location was Studio A, which is located behind the stage and has been home to shows like Nashville and Hee Haw. Next up was the dressing rooms, we were able to see each dressing room that the stars would prepare in before their Showtime. Each dressing room has its own unique theme too. While I did the day tour, I was told that sometimes during the evening tour you might even see a star or two backstage. We also had a chance to see the large community room where most of the stars hang out after the show. The only thing left to see was the Opry itself, we were carefully lead out to the stage to to see where all the performances of the legendary broadcast have taken place. One highlight was the ability to stand in the circle of the original stage from the Ryman theater, where so many legends have stood before.

The tour was about an hour and concluded with a stop in the gift shop. My recommendation would be to opt for the evening tour before a show, however some of the tour may not be available but you have a pretty good chance of seeing a country music star!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Great way to spend a Sunday night!! 1/2 off bottles of house wine..don't mind if we do! Service is great and everyone is so incredibly nice. Live music and the Caesar salad was great! We'll be back!

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Just like any other karaoke bar, tips make the wait to sing significantly shorter. $20 basically gets u up in the next couple people. Crowd was a great mix of people and were all supportive of the singers.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Pretty good for a back alley, but anywhere else I'd pass.  We ate here because our first three or four other choices had an hour or so wait and we were all tired and hungry at the end of a long travel day.  The menu consisted of about 50% hamburgers, a few salads, and some other items so you might think the hamburgers would be really good, but that wasn't the case.  Our party of 5 all had burgers and no one really enjoyed.  The next day, we found the "world's best burger" according to the sign in the window. Didn't actually try it, but window signs never lie.   If interested, it's on Broadway between 5th and 6th.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Went here this past Friday night with some friends for a bachelorette party. We got there around 10:30 and it was pretty busy. I do enjoy a variety of beers, but I am by no means a beer aficionado. The guy who helped me (wish I would've gotten his name!) was super friendly and I told him the type of beers I liked, and he offered up a suggestion. Can't remember the name of it, but it was a grapefruit type beer and it was awesome! I wish I would've gotten the name of it because I really enjoyed it. Love the atmosphere of this place and the penny wall where all the taps are located was really cool. We only stayed for about 30 minutes (not a good place for a bachelorette party necessarily) but I would love to go back again to try out some different beers they have on tap.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
Not crowded at all on a Friday night which is a welcome change to all the other places that pack a 1 hour wait around downtown.  We were welcomed with friendly smiles and the staff was very nice.

I got the Boston salad which was really enjoyable. They cook the chicken fresh so it's warm and juicy on top of your salad...forget the cold dry chicken most joints toss onto salads! I love how well seasoned and tender my chicken with my greens.

The boyfriend got the fried catfish po'boy. The fish was really crispy but in my opinion, a little under seasoned. Or perhaps under sauced because I thought a side of the remoulade with the sandwich was a perfect fix. Would have been better with more lettuce too.

I do have to say, the hushpuppies are the best I've ever had. Mix the two sauces into the same bite...mmmm. Could eat it all day!

For a drink I got the pineapple upsidedown martini, which was really good in that it really did taste like liquid pineapple upsidedown cake...unfortunately I don't do very well with super sweet drinks so I only for half way through. Glad I tried it though!

The boyfriend loved his margarita.

Would definitely come back, hopefully on a Tuesday when they have songwriter night or Saturday when there is live music.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This place is cool. Really is off an alley!  Anyway had that jalapeño burger and a whiskey (good lunch ha-ha) and it was really good. Good atmosphere and food and a nice little bar.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We were at the Grand Ole Opry on May 5,2018. It was an awesome show and experience. The people in Tennessee are very hospitable and friendly. Being able to see the live radio show in person was a dream come true.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text:
WannaB's!  Yea!  So, every bar and restaurant on the strip (Broadway) in Nashville has live music.  Every single place.  It's a town chalked full of aspiring musicians - some of them pretty decent, others... meh.  Oddly, some of the best singers I heard on my visit to Nashville were to be found at the one place where the singers were the patrons.  Tourists, business men & women alike, all throwing down their best efforts on their favorite songs.  

Particularly impressed by the gal behind the bar, who OWNED a country song while still cracking beers and closing tabs.  Serious multitasking.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I was thoroughly unimpressed with this place. The food was average, and the service was terrible. The server had a total attitude and did not do her job properly. She forgot to take one person's order, and got snippy with people. Aside from the service, the menu was lacking. Only one dessert option. Most egregiously, they charge for soft drink refills. Really? Outrageous. I won't be back.

name: Third Man Records
text:
I would call this the best gift shop in town.

Jack White's studio company. Awesome gift shop. A vinyl recording booth, waxomatic, jukebox, a photo booth, and two turntables with records to sample. Have a number of vinyls recorded and cut in the building. I bought several myself. Prices were shockingly reasonable, a third of the store was on sale. No expenses spared in maintaining Jack White's vintage theme.

name: Third Man Records
text:
With so much to do in Nashville it is refreshing to see Jack White doesn't charge an admission price. Even if you don't own a record player this place is worth a visit. The artifacts are plentiful and the staff is helpful. 

Well worth a visit after you chow down on some Nashville hot chicken.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: What's there not to love! If you like country music this experience mustn't be missed.

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text: love the fish and chips special on thurs. great place to sit outside and drink a beer. great fried pickles and chicken tenders.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: How disappointing.  Our waitress rushed everything along and low and behold messed up our order.  For a beer place, you'd think she know something about the beer or at least the food.  Neither succeeded and the attitude was a bit over the top.  After she totally botched our order, there was no apology, no "I'm sorry", no nothing.  Only a couple of sad bratwurst on a plate. Spend your time  and money elsewhere.   I was expecting more.  Even the beer menu is nothing uncommon. The place was empty.  Deserverbly so.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Cozy spot with good food and personable service.

My girlfriend and I originally intended to eat at Double Dogs down the road but the wait was insane due to Sunday football games, so we wondered up the street and chose Belcourt taps since it seemed empty and the menu outside looked good. 

First impressions: Dim lit, very moody interior which I liked. The tables are painted, ours had a dog on it. Interesting art on the walls. Limited open seating.

The place was nearly empty when we arrived around 1:15. The bartender Josh quickly made his way over with some menus and took our drink order.I have uploaded pics of the menu for other Yelpers to look at. I chose the buffalo chicken burger and my girlfriend made her own burger that was hardly as interesting as mine so I immediately forgot what it was. We also ordered a side of loaded fries.


The burger:

Ordered medium on a nice fluffy bun, lettuce, tomato, blue cheese, great beef, and buffalo chicken. The burger was large enough on its own to satisfy any appetite. You have the option of fries, beans, or cole slaw as a side. Fries were hand cut and quite good.

The fries:

The loaded fries were COVERED in cheese, pulled pork bbq, bacon and sautéed onions. My girlfriend usually despises onion and she happily ate the fries, they were that good.

All in all, I'd gladly come back. I have heard the live music is great and with a cozy atmosphere and good burgers, there is no reason not to check it out If you have the opportunity.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
We're not hard core country music fans, but this visit was certainly on our bucket list. It lived up to all our expectations, and then some. The format is great: eight performers, each doing 3 songs, with one intermission. You get a good flavor from lots of different country styles, and it's fast-paced. We're now fans of three of the performers we saw that we'd never heard of before. The venue is clean and has a great feel and decor. 

The only issues we had (hence the lack of a star) was with the seating and ticketing.
