The seats are church pews, which is fine unless you're sitting next to large people who take up more than their share of the seat allotment. It's best to get an aisle so you only have to worry about that issue on one side.

We ordered our tickets on-line and received an email with a file to print out the tickets. Unfortunately the file was corrupt and I had to call customer service to have another email/file sent to me. The customer service rep even finished my sentence when I said the file was "corrupt" (she said). I asked if this was a common issue, since she wasn't surprised, and she admitted that resolving corrupt file issues was a major part of her day. That was bad enough, but when we got to the Opry house the tickets I had printed out (from the good file) couldn't be scanned and we had to then go to the ticket office to get them replaced (another 10 minutes). All-in-all, the ticketing process was the worst we'd seen in the three years we've been traveling the country. They know they have issues, so they need to take steps to correct them.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Incredible beer list-the largest variety I have ever seen in one bar. I arrived in time for happy hour and enjoyed a few $3 pints. Wine and liquor selection on the poor side, but the fantastic selection of beers makes up for it. I found the prices to be very affordable as well. The vegan options, which included a wrap and pita/hummus plate, were excellent. A very nice surprise.

Atmosphere was great-overstuffed couches and chairs with vintage decor and nice lighting. Power outlets near many of the seats. Our server had silvery/purple hair and was very friendly, helpful, and patient. I would definitely come back here the next time I am in Nashville.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Last night was bacon-wrapped jalapeños, stuffed w spiced beef, chorizo and cheese...100% worth the heartburn during the night! Absolutely delicious. Tonight, loaded rocket-tots, again w jalapeño, also bacon, and cheddar jack/goat cheese, green onion, and topped w a fried egg. Oh, my! And of course, a huge choice of drafts and other spirits.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great music, great southern style food, and very friendly staff! I wasn't expecting to visit a place like this in Nashville, considering country music is king around there. Went in with friends on a whim and was treated to some fantastic blues musicalong with a great beer selection and friendly wait staff. I would highly recommend this place if you're looking for a little something different from the country music scene in downtown Nashville.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: First off, the Opry is the legendary roots of country music, so you have to go and bear it. I enjoyed being there, but the show was soo old. I get it's about the legends, but wow, we need to move on. They did have a few younger performers, but it was very slow and boring. It was also extremely annoying that after each group they had a commercial for one of the sponsors that the host read. It got to be ridiculous that people were laughing. That was painful. Charles Easton (sp ?)  played as did a guy called Zach Williams. They were fabulous! But each group only plays 2 songs, so it was fast and a disappointment for $200 for 3 of us. Glad we went once in my life, but don't feel I need to go back.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We always visit the Grand Ole Opry  during every visit. It is the heart of Nashville, reasonable prices and every seat is good!  Concessions are expensive, wear causal clothing and comfortable shoes.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
This bar reminded me of a bar I would find in LA, so don't go here expecting a unique Nashville experience, but it was definitely a cool vibe (being from CA I really enjoyed it but we didn't stay long since we wanted to see Nashville). 

They have great beers on tap, modern feel, a lower level that has a second bar and dance floor.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Food is cheap.  Venue is divey and a great Nashville-esque experience.   Live music was playing when we got there at 8 p.m. on a Saturday.   It was an up and coming bluegrass band that knew how to entertain a crowd.  Will definitely be coming back.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
We took the backstage tour and it was really cool. It was my second time taking this tour and each time it was different and I learned more each time. 

We bought tickets online ahead of time to make sure we got a reservation because they fill up quickly. We forgot to print the actual ticket though so we went to the box office and they gladly printed them for us. 

The tour began promptly at the time slot we reserved and lasted about 45 minutes. The best part was the end getting to go on stage and look out towards the crowd.

They also take your picture on the stage at the center of the iconic wooden stage circle. You can buy them after the toe for $25 which gets you two 4x6 and a 7x9 and access to the digital copy as well. We ended up getting the wrong code for the digital copy so we got someone else's digital version. We called the next day and they were able to give us the right code over the phone which cleared up the mistake pretty quickly. 

The Grand Ol Opry is also walking distance to Gaylord Opry too, so put these two together and it's an awesome day!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: As a fan of country music, I found this venue to be thoroughly entertaining!  I love how they preserved the legacies of the early country stars (i.e. Minnie Pearl, Hank Williams).  The dressing rooms are cool,  the video introduction by Blake Shelton is enlightening,  the staff is super friendly.  I'd definitely visit this place again!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
I was excited to try this place while visiting Nashville, but unfortunately I was underwhelmed.  We went on a Wednesday night.  The place was packed.  The server even warned us that kitchen was backed up so our food might take a while.  We arrived at 7:30pm ordered by 7:45pm and got our food at 8:55pm.   When we did finally get the food it was just luke warm as if it had been sitting in the pick up window for quite some time.   While waiting for our meal, we decided to try some of the over 50 beers they have available.  All the ones we wanted to try were sold out! :(  

Our server could have been more attentive at the beginning, but  was so after the place started to clear out later in the evening.

Overall, good beer selection which is why I gave it 3 stars, if they had still had the ones I wanted, I might have given them 4 stars.  They definitely lose points for  having just okay food and slow service. 

Go on non-busy night and hopefully they'll have your favorite beer  in stock and maybe, just maybe you'll have a better experience than we did.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This was the most terrible service I have ever received at a restaurant. We made our reservation 5 hours ahead of time. When we got there, they said that they were sorry but they were not going to have a table available. We waited for 15 minutes and they finally placed us at a table. Our order was taken and two of us ordered catfish. 15 more minutes later, they asked if we wanted something else because the fish was still frozen. The food was ok, but didn't make up for the lack of service and the fact we were an hour late for our event. It is our first time in Nashville and next time we will not be coming back to this restaurant.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Came on from Chicago. Went to this place. The service was really bad one server was really rude will not go back.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: It was great. We had some trouble finding it because we thought it was in the arcade. It is just a few steps away. The staff was very helpful and the food was fantastic. The coleslaw is very spicy. The ladies had drinks and loved them.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Came with a group of 32 women in my industry for a party during our convention.  Everyone loved their food and the venue was fantastic too!  They were willing to divide our checks and everything cane our hot and accurate.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
I came here for a conference and thought it would be a great time. To my surprise the only thing that occurred during this experience that was positive was the live music. 

Our group of seven all thought that the service was lackluster. More specifically, we experience a significant amount of delays in service from food, water, and the bill. I have also never experienced more "no" responses from a waitress than this. 

A significant disappointment were the sides. If you ask for a full portion it takes about 35 minutes. They claim the macaroni is made to order but we could not tell. Especially with the small cup side we received. 

Dessert? That also took about 35 minutes. The waitress didn't inform us that it would be such a delay but luckily we all were enjoying the music so the time passed faster than watching paint dry. 

Let's not forget that the servers continued to come to our table with the wrong order. This is extremely disappointing when you are starving and have been waiting for 30 or more minutes for your meal.  For some reason it seems that we had an extremely long wait for everything. 

As I said , this experience was lackluster and nothing that I would recommend. The two stars are for the live band. Oh yeah, the drinks were watered down and unfulfilling (especially my Long Island which was basically juice/coke).

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Highly recommend the backstage Opry tour! It was well worth it-especially for lovers of country music. I learned so much about the history of the Opry as well as learned more about country music that I didn't know I didn't know! 
The structure of the tour was awesome - to walk through this beautiful historical building in the same way via the same steps an artist would enter, such an awesome idea! 
It was absolutely incredible to stand in the same spot as so many of my favorite artists and historical country musicians have stood! Seriously LOVED every second of this!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I was in Nashville recently for CMA Fest week. We stopped in BB King's for dinner one night. I had been here once before (and it was awesome) so we thought we would visit again. The food is so delicious, and it's fun to have a live band. Overall the food and drinks are pretty reasonable for being in a touristy area. The staff is super friendly and helpful. I would come back again and recommend it to anyone visiting! Definitely get the nachos with chicken!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Amazing. Awesome. Wish I had more stars to give this. If you love country music, this venue is a must visit!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: All three of the flying saucers are great.  They have a German and American food selection and tons of beers on tap.  The location downtown is great being next to union station.  You can also get your parking validated for $5.  Once you drink $200 beers in their UFO club you get a plate on the wall with your name.  With a limit of 3 beers at a time that will probably be a 5 year goal.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: When in Nashville the Grand Ole Opry is the venue to see.  Since we were out of towners without any ability to be picky on our travel dates we ended up seeing the performances of people completely unknown to us.  The music was not my taste but I still managed to have a good time with a help of an adult beverage and my friends.  We took the backstage tour and our guide was high on Red Bull and very fun.  They allow you to take a picture on stage during the tour which must be a thrill for true country fans.  I also want to add the vibe is very casual.  I saw one lady wearing heels but most were in pants or shorts.  The Gaylord Hotel has a free shuttle to and from the Grand Ole Opry which is great.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This place offers light, sing along entertainment with few recognizable musicians/songs. The grounds were kept trimmed and offered plenty of paths to choose from on the grounds. I liked the evening ambiance.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
BB Kings did me well in Memphis, so we stopped by in Nashville and were discouraged by the $5 cover charge just to stop in and eat dinner (it was past 10pm). Meanwhile, the band was very good and the locale and scene offered an alternative to the honky tonks and country style bars that litter the region. A positive: the $5 charge does keep some of the rift raft out and the college kids. 

On the other hand, the food is so-so, not great, nothing to complain about either. It's typical chain food, maybe a little bit better. Our server (who was good) recommended the meatloaf, which I was reluctant to order as I wanted to order the fried catfish (which I ordered a few years back at their location on Beale St in Memphis). The meatloaf didn't taste like homemade meatloaf. The green beans that came with it tasted like they came out of a can. It was edible and even enjoyable while we listened to a great band. 

The kitchen was very slow- took 30 minutes to get our food. My friend ordered the pork sandwich, which he enjoyed the BBQ sauce, but wasn't wowed. Jacks (also downtown), he said, blew it away. 

If you come to BB Kings - it's for the music and atmosphere, not the food.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I am impressed!  Very large bar and restaurant.  Place has a cool rustic look with a large stage.  Looks like it has been here along time.  I'm enjoying these delicious hot wings and a local IPA, Yazoo.   Really impressed at how nice this place is.  Too bad I didn't arrive when blue music is being played live.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: We were taken to DawgHouse by Patrick with Joyride. We were having an amazing tour and wanted to stop and have a drink. Patrick took us to his favorite bar.  We loved it.  Very relaxed and laid back. Thank You Key! You took great care of us and made us feel at home.  Your personality kept us entertained and we went back 2 other times!  Again, Thank You Key!!!

name: Third Man Records
text:
Terrible customer service.

Third Man Records has an expensive mail-order subscription series called The Vault, where for $240 a year, you get exclusive "limited" LP & 45 RPM vinyl records, plus a book, DVD or T-shirt, four times a year (For those of you who might not know, Jack White has made a large part of his fortune catering to worldwide vinyl collectors/fanatics.)

I've been a subscriber of The Vault since its beginning in 2009, and have occasionally had to contact customer service when a package arrives damaged. Over the years, Third Man's customer service has been ok resolving the issue and sending replacements, for the most part.

Until recently.

Now, customer service (specifically a passive aggressive asshole named "Cam"), basically tells you to get lost if you question their seemingly sudden reluctance to send replacements. And I quote:

"If you have a differing opinion, I would recommend discontinuing your membership, which I would be more than happy to help you do."

No prob Cam, tell Jack I'll spend my money elsewhere.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
This is one of those places that you just have to stop in front of and take it in because you can't believe you are actually there.

Unfortunately it was sold out the night we arrived in Nashville so we only got to admired everything on the outside and what we could see on the inside.

This is a must for any music fan, and even if you aren't a country music fan, you'll still appreciate it.

It is on the same property as Opryland and Opry Mills so be prepared to search for parking for a few minutes, then having to walk.

You can get many photo ops in and around it but cannot take video once inside.

Don't forget to stop in the gift shop.

I can't wait to come back and see a show.  Maybe it won't be sold out next time!

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text:
my fiance and stepdad hung out here for an hour or 2 while we shopped, eventually we met them here. very entertaining and the people here were talented. seemed to have good price on beers since they drank a few of them. we love the wall in the bathroom people wrote on :) 

stayed here for awhile just listening to people until we went back to hotel to get ready for dinner.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: For those of you who like karaoke, this place is a gem.  The KJ's there are respectful and smart, and don't put shitty people up for their third song when others have been waiting.  This place is great, if you don't like fun times go elsewhere.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
8/13/18 -- After walking all over Nashville, we stopped in to B.B. King Club right about time to eat.. lucky us.  Not starving, we decided to split a meal.  But first..... our timing could not have been better. Plenty of room, for the place had only a few tables filled but we went to the bar anyway.  The Bartender was super nice and had a very good attitude of "touristy people".  Which we were !!   This was our first time to Nashville.  

We ordered some cold beers and ordered the Fried Chicken w/ cheesy pasta and fresh veggies.  Delicious and definitely enough for us to split.   
The Chicken was moist, nice crunch on the batter and the veggies were perfectly cooked...... firm and not mushy at all.  

A guy was playing before the main headliner.... good, but acoustics were bad for a single Artist playing a guitar .... and I didn't get his name.  

We were getting ready to move along.  The restaurant was filling up with people and then the Bartender said.... " you might want to stay for the group that was setting up to play".  It was the Stacy Mitchhart Band.  We'd never heard of him.... but, we stayed and we are glad we did.  More instruments, more diners (the place was packed) and they sounded really good.   

Good food, good Blues..... enjoyable evening !!!  What more could we ask for.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: The best place ever great food friendly staff very clean bar love to hangout there . Biggest T.V I ever see to enjoy watching the game , if you are sports fan this the best place to go . The good thing you can bring your dog and set outside, t.v's everywhere games on the side great bands every Wednesday and Sunday

name: Third Man Records
text:
I'm sure if you're a hard-core Jack White fan going here the first time feels like a pilgrimage...if that sounds like you, make sure to visit at least once when in the Nashville area and you'll probably give it 5 stars. I'm a moderate fan of White's but it's easy to see he took time to curate every inch of this somewhat small storefront to his studio-- every decorative piece on the wall or a shelf and every item for sell seems hand-picked by him.

As an overall record store, the selection is small-to-moderate but fairly priced. The coolest items for sale  the third-man in-studio live LPs, all about $15 each so you can search to see if your favorite act has recorded a set in the studio attached to the store and pick it up. Friendly service, some cool books, LPs, shirts and things to buy and some neat things to look at. Stop by the photo booth to get a memento of your visit if you're so inclined and you're out the door.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Was walking and saw a little sign and decided to go check it out. It's in a back alley and hidden. Which is what makes it so awesome! We sat down at the bar and the bartender lacy was so sweet and talkative made us feel so welcomed! We got the sizzling burger and the home made broccoli soup and they were hands down the best I have ever had! I highly recommend it! And lacy made one of the best margaritas around! 100 stars absolutely awesome check it out! Or you will regret it!

name: Third Man Records
text:
Great stop on our Nashville-Memphis week. We are huge Jack White fans - just saw him a few weeks ago in BKLYN. 

And seeing the shop and getting to do the behind the scenes tour was oddly like willy wonka and the chocolate factory for music!

Really enjoyed the guide and discussions. A real highlight of our trip south

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Used to be very special into the 1990s, then after that went to crap due to all these NO NAMES being able to be on stage and cant sing and granted memberships for 1 hit wonders.  Back in the "Real" days of The Opry a person had to pay their dues to even be considered for a guest spot, nowadays they dont..I forsee The Opry CEASING To exist in 20 more yrs

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I love this place. They have awesome food and great drink specials, and every server and bartender I've ever had has been awesome and so nice. It's right by work so it's fun to go to happy hour after work. The BAD never disappoints!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
If you want beer, you'll find it here.
If you want some Irish-style bar food, you'll find it here.
If you want one of the better trivia's in town, you'll find it here. 
If you want your name on a plate on the wall after drinking 200+ beers, you'll find it here.
Now go!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text:
Loved that they had wine and the beer was reasonably priced. Good music as well! 

But why do they only use plastic cups? And plastic STRAWS!? It's 2018, ya'll. Most plastic isn't recycled and seeps into groundwater and ends up in your fish! It's not just about the environment, it's about the future of our children.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great service, phenomenal selection of brews, quality food and an atmosphere that offers something for everyone.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I am a definite frequenter of the flying saucer.  My husband and I are a part of their saucer club and we are slowly but surely working our way through the 200 beers (we're around 45 at the moment).  It has been so much fun selecting random beers and giving anything and everything a try, something I would have never done otherwise.  Most of their food is pretty good but some of it is a miss; their pizzas, wraps, pretzels, brats, and beer cheese soup are all great, their new buffalo chicken wrap is my current favorite.  Items that have just been okay are the chicken sandwich, rocket tots, and spinach and artichoke dip.  Also their service can be hit or miss too, we've had a great server on a extremely busy night and a really slow one on a dead afternoon, it just depends.  Anyway, we love coming out here for some great atmosphere, food and to try some beers.  Of course the beer selection is massive at 300+ and ever changing, it's a beer connoisseurs dream.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Totally awesome. I'm a country music fan but I think even if you aren't, you would probably enjoy it.

The live to air show and old school country legends performing make you feel like you've stepped in a time warp, but they do have a lot of modern acts too. We got to see Johnny Reid make his Opry debut, which was quite exciting.

Crowd is definitely older, very older (60+) but there are a few youngsters in the mix. 

Delicious homemade kettlecorn sold outside. 

Show runs from 7pm-9:15pm and you can park for free in the nearby shopping center parking lot.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Walking up to this place I was a little skeptical about what I was about to walk into. Literally in an alley and shady looking. To my surprise once we walked in it was a cute diner and the food was great!!! The waiters were super nice and friendly. Drinks were very good too. Absolutely good surprise. Loved it !

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
I knew I wanted to visit this place before I even arrived in Nashville! We made reservations but our table was directly by speakers so I choose to just sit at the bar ( which was more fun to me) ... The cocktails and food were great ! If you order a shot , take your receipt to the hostess then you'll get a souvenir glass..

The night I was there a 15 year old kid was having a birthday so they let him go onstage to jam with the band . He played guitar with so much soul . It was amazing .. 

All in all I had a great time there and will be sure to visit again !!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I have a coworker who has been raving about this place for months, so I finally decided to go, and let me tell you, it is sooo good! There's a surprising amount of space - there's two floors! It was crowded too (we went at 11) but they had plenty of waiters, and we barely had to wait for our food. I ordered the soup (chicken, broccoli & cheddar) and a sandwich (turkey) and it filled me up and I loved it! We were in and out in about 40 minutes, which is perfect! I saw so many good looking things on the menu, so I'm definitely going back for more!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Food was on point, music on Tuesday night was awesome.  Grant Garland band!
Tre is an enthusiastic, hard working, sweet guy! Met the needs of all 9 in our party. Pleasurable night out in Nashville. Would definitely do it again!

name: Anthem
text:
I attended the soft-opening of this snazzy new multi-faceted business earlier this week and was impressed with the concept. 

Previously this space housed the club Mai but a complete over-haul has happened with this newly minted space. Not only does this place offer a club atmosphere but also a restaurant, lounge, and venue space too. 

Due to it being a soft-opening and not being in the complete swing of things yet, I will update more when I revisit soon!

The official Grand Opening is tonight, Saturday, February 16th.

Yelp365#26

name: Belcourt Taps
text: This was my first visit - I joined a couple of friends for drinks.  I love the cozy feel of the interior and the place overall has a good vine.  I definitely plan on going back.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
The music is great! High quality sound and musicianship. We were here on Saturday night for hours! Our first server was Trey who was Awesome! He was attentive, helpful, friendly and our food arrived in a time,y manner. We had the fries with beef and gravy on them and the fried pickles to start. Many rounds and a new server later (sorry I don't have her name, I think she helped us bc I caught her eye but I didn't get her name) we orders the house salad which was Huge for the price and very good, the buttermilk ranch was delicious and not so thick that you felt guilty eating it. And we ended the night with the brownie dessert.
We didn't have an actual main dish so I can't comment on those but I can say that we had a great time, listened to hours of good music and everyone was friendly.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Was in town for a night and got a ticket to a Friday night show ($70) which was located in the nosebleed section (up and to left of stage).  They have giant screens on the walls to give you a better view of the stage but it takes away from the intimate experience (even though they can fit 4000 people in the venue). The seats are actually wooden pews with a cover on them and there isn't much leg room. Definitely no where to dance if you were thinking about it. 

There was no musical guests playing that were famous. The headliner was an artist by the name of Randy Skaggs who got fame in the early 80s supposedly but I hadn't heard of him. 

Anyway the venue is beautiful on the inside. Looks like an old grand house of worship. They do sell concessions including beer, wine and mixed drinks and the prices are in line with a concert venue.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: If you want to sing this is the place to be!! I've been to Nashville many many times and I always always chose wannabes as my go to spot for Karaoke. The staff is friendly the song selection is incredible and it's usually not too terribly crowded. Channel your inner country star and head on down to wannabes you'll be glad you did!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: This was my first time at BB King's and we had such a fabulous time! The food was delicious (we got the blues burger and hot wings) and the music was incredible!! We saw two different bands during dinner and they were both phenomenal. Our server Brandon was fantastic, made the whole experience more enjoyable, and took great care of us all night. We'll be back!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: By far the best burger (In my opinion) in Nashville. Fries are to die for. They seem to have something going on everyday of the week and a great happy hour! The staff is always great and is a cool laid back vibe! Don't let this place fool you! Love this place!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
SO COOL ! Loved the experience ! i've been listening to GOO since i was a kid 50+ years..
Loved it. the only thing I din't care for was the constant sponsor announcements especially for Cracker B......So anti LGBT organization .

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Located a short drive away from downtown, but worth the drive. I am not even a big country music fan but I enjoyed the tour. Our guide, Emily, was very knowledgable and willing to answer any questions. There was a  band rehearsing so we weren't able to stand on center stage which would have been awesome.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Pleasant surprise!  Went here on 11/28 with my girl and we both enjoyed it. The ribs were some of the best I have ever eaten;  fall of the bone perfection and great flavor!  Crawfish popper appetizer was unique and very tasty.  Excellent live music, people dancing, and an overall great vibe in this place. Long live the King!

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Loved this little place. Recommended by the old "friend of a friend," this placed proved to be a nice late night stop. The proprietor was a fascinating woman who produced music and employed up-and-coming singer's and musicians trying to get their foothold in the Nashville music scene. 

Our bartender was a skilled singer and friendly as can be.  A waiter, however, who was hanging out after his shift, (apparently he was a musical virtuoso of some measure) was a bit toasted and acting like an jerk. I guess his provocative behavior was meant to rile us up, but we are a pretty un-rileable group and devour a#%holes like this as if they're light bar snacks. It was amusing as hell, like free entertainment!

While it was too late to sample the food, the vibe was fun, the creative energy was almost palpable, and the people were interesting and entertaining. It was a pleasant surprise all around.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Flying Saucer gets 5-stars even though it has faults because it's just that fun.  Traditional pub style, they have an amazing beer selection which always rotates in new drinks.  They even import a keg or two of a certain beer, and it's only available until it's been drank, giving a sort of exclusive variety.  Pint Night on Mondays is super fun too!

As bar food goes, it's pretty damn solid.  Both the pretzels and the sausage are really tasty and are sure to please everyone at your table.

There are some downsides, though.  It's pretty loud, so can be hard to have a meaningful one-on-one with someone.  Finding a table can be tricky (you might have to be a vulture and wait for a party getting up).  You have to be a little creative with parking, too.

Overall though it's a great place and I'll be back with my group.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We had dinner and entertainment here as part of a large group in town for a convention. Although the food was buffet style for us all it was all great. The live music and atmoshere was good as well

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: What a great day of entertainment!! We started with the tour which gave us amazing insight into so many unknown facts and the way The Grand Ol Opry works. We even got to go on stage with our group and see what the singers see - what a view! Then the evening was full of talent - many different genres were in the line up. Comedy, classic country, new country AND Alabama!!

name: Third Man Records
text:
This little hidden gem is worth 5 stars!
=== === ===
Ok, the place is rather tiny for a record store, but there are tons of interesting finds inside. 

You can find strange recordings from people you'd never think would have recorded anything. I picked up two small albums of Elvira for my hubby. Anyway, there's also a recording booth where you can make your own 2 1/2 minute record which is pretty fun. You can also make your own guitar figure out of wax via a machine while you watch. 

If you're a music lover, especially music on vinyl, this is a place that you'll want to check out. There are also some videos on YouTube of this place where musicians will take their turn in the recording booth. Pretty cool to check out.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We visited B.B King's Blues Club on a Wednesday night and we heard that we should make reservations. So we did on Open Table for 7pm and the band started at 7:30pm. We were sat right away. The band was AWESOME. Great soulful music! The food exceeded all expectations. We ordered catfish bites for an appetizer and they were delicious! For entrees I ordered the bbq chicken and rib platter and the meat literally fell off the bone. So amazing! The service was even better. Our waiter was slammed busy, but we still had our drinks full at all times. If you visit Nashville make this a stop!!!

name: Music City Tippler
text:
(Note: Was really torn between giving them three or four stars. The point would be docked if I compared Tippler to its neighbor, Patterson House, only a five minute walk away.)

As a huge fan of Patterson House, I was very excited about Tippler arriving in Nashville. At first glance, the place did not disappoint. I love the ambiance of the place, and the fact that it has space---always a good thing in Nashville where it seems like every decent bar is crowded every night.

Some notes:

- Tippler should win on food since they offer a full menu, but they offer only a very, very limited (around four items, if I remember right) menu for people at the bar and for those who want to stay outdoors. I get how this could be easier service-wise, but it was a big limitation for me and the husband both times we went.

- Tippler should win on novelty since they serve draft cocktails, but they only serve three or four different kinds. When we were there, they had already sold out of the one that sounded interesting (at 7 pm), and there's nothing novel about a mojito or a vieux carre, which were their other offerings. Their standard cocktails run $12-13 each, but so do Patterson House's---who have a larger bar menu.

The food itself was good but unremarkable. We tried a sampling of the bar food and also had entrees another night. (I have to say that the salmon was very good---I like my seafood salty though, so you have been warned.)

I don't mean to bash on Tippler because I actually really like it---and intend to go back repeatedly! But when there's another option close by with amazing cocktails and really good bar food, they need to do something to make themselves shine. If they improve their bar menu and draft cocktail offerings, I think they could really be something.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Food and service were both great! Beer was cheap and location was unique. Definitely stop by if in the area.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
Dear Tippler, thanks again for a magical evening. Our group of 14 was seated promptly for our reservation, and it was uphill from there! We started by ordering drinks and a few appetizers for the table. The folks on our end chose the hummus and chicken biscuits. The bean mash was served with some gourmet leathery pita for dipping. We rationed the nickel-sized chicken biscuits between a few of us. Served in an iron skillet, and on iron biscuits, these $10 morsels truly made a impact. Dinner was uneventful, and as our plates were whisked away, we were informed that our table was so nice that they had booked it for another group! We were asked to wrap up and move. After paying a well-earned service charge on each of our bills, we were allowed to stay in the restaurant.

The maître d did offer us a nice spot upstairs, and we moved on with our evening. The area we were moved to even had its own TV! The TV was not on of course, and when we asked to turn it on we were told there was not a remote. Being a former Boy Scout, I decided to turn it on using the power button. A waiter was then kind enough to come by and turn it off for us a few minutes later, saying that they did not want it on. My mistake! As the night wore on, we began to enjoy some of the well-priced beverages. In fact, complimentary bottles of champagne and fine glass flutes were brought to our table! We just were not aware it wasn't for us. Told that the owner was coming in and wanted our table, we were asked to move along again. But not before we were allowed to pay another service charge! This time our host recommended a nice spot for us out front, right next to the valet. As we left and were "you're welcomed" by the the hostesses, we knew this was an experience we would never forget. Thanks again Tippler, to show our appreciation our group of 14 will do our best to make sure your restaurant tables aren't in such demand in the future.

name: Third Man Records
text:
What a unique record store for vinyl junkies! Lots of fun stuff to browse and one of a kind vintage "toys" including the automatic recording booth! Worth the $20 to record a little something silly or sentimental. I travel for work and I was missing my cats...and my husband haha so I recorded my wedding vows and I can't wait to give it to him for our 3 yr anniversary! 
There was an amazing clearance sale when I went in and I got a $100-150 Verameat necklace for...FIVE DOLLARS!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: I thought Ms Kelli's was pretty cool for what it was- a karaoke dive bar. I like that it's dark, kinda grimy, and not pretentious at all. My group of four had no problem finding a table on a late Saturday night. However, a member of the group had to bus and clean the table before we could settle in. There appeared to be a pretty mixed crowd. Tourists, regulars, random (awesome) folks out for a good time (us), and a few strange ducks. Overall the vibe was nice but you have to scream in order to speak to people. Beer was cheap but the Jello shots weren't very strong, IMO. I didn't get to sing and I realize now after reading other reviews it's probably because I didn't tip the KJ. I think that's kind of shitty, but whatever. I feel like I'll be back again....

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: I was there on a Friday afternoon before karaoke.  We planned to have lunch and one drink and ended up staying for 3 hours. Travis Bishop and Wesley Cash played acoustic guitars. ...outstanding original music! Rhonda,  our bartender was friendly,  professional and made it all the more fun!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Not my favorite experience and I was really looking forward to coming here. I ordered the catfish creole which wasn't too bad at all but for the price, eh.. Can def tell it was previously frozen and not fresh. The place wasn't busy at all for a Saturday but that didn't bother me, there was a pretty good band playing. However my experience with the waitress was less than ideal. Not sure what her name was but she had long hair with the side buzz cut. One of my friends chair was broken and it took her forever to replace it. I ordered a drink and it wasn't very good, so I asked to replace it and she was ok about that, however I was water vaping and it creates a small amount of mist and she came over and told me I cldnt smoke it, so I turned it completely off yet I still put my mouth to it to get the taste. It was off, no light, no smoke, Nada yet she came over to me and said "I see your will using it and if I have to tell you again" (this was a bad idea on her part) my friend cut her off immediately and said, it's off, what do you mean? There is no smoke or anything. How someone going to tell me what I can or can't put to my own mouth!? I was less than pleased to be talked to like a petulant child, "if I have to tell you again", seriously? Her approach was aggressive and abrasive and I wasn't a fan.  It was B.B. king and we were not roughy nor loud nor rude. So why I have to get treated like I was about to be thrown out!? Lol Why because my friends chair was broken and my drink taste nothing like the description?

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: What a night we had here! Came with my mom and sister for the first time, visiting from California! It was a well run process. We saw the late show, 930. We waited just a bit for the doors to open and for them to clear out the first show but then we took our seats and were happy to find them comfortable and church like! The sound in the theater is second to none! You will not be let down here if you are looking for the soul of country music!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: Pretty cool bar on Broadway. It has multiple floors including a rooftop bar (which I'm starting to learn almost every Nashville bar has one now LOL) with live music playing all over. We stayed for a while to listen to one of the bands on the rooftop play and it was nice and relaxing. They also had huge fans blowing too, which was a huge plus after being out in 90 degree weather all day.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Well, you put your name on the lit and you see there's 15 in front of you, so you wait, watch and sing along with others. However, when you check back after 10-12 songs, you find out you're only 8songs away?  Whatever, we'll wait it out. Then another 5 go by and you inquire again, to be told you're 5 songs away, and get this:  "ask again and you won't sing at all". After we dropped $200 bucks in here, I left a poultry tip for the wait staff and suggested they get the rest from the rude kaoroke person and we left. I'm sure there are other places that know math, and understand customer service better than this place.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Aside from being in the Nosebleed seats we had a good time. Really overpriced concessions though 5 dollars for a water and no drinking fountains anywhere . Music was good

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Dined last night (12/18) with a group of friends while enjoying heir $3 pint night! Although we had a great time, the servers were very rude. My friend mistaken another waitress for ours and she replied with "I am not your server and you should know that," while rolling her eyes and walking off. That is terrible customer service if you ask me. So beware of the server with brunette braided pigtails and glasses!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This was the highlight of our week long trip to Nashville. The two hour show was fast paced and the entertainment was great. There are about seven groups that perform three songs each. When Larry Gatlin and Bill Anderson did their shows, you could tell they were the consummate professionals. They engaged the audience, told stories, and jokes in between their songs. The whole place was fun. However, we did not take the back-stage tour.

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text: I stopped in here with some friends for a drink in the midafternoon, mainly to take advantage of their large patio section. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay on the patio, lazily drinking our beers and whiskeys while smoking stogies. Our waiter did a great job checking on us and keeping us in drink. None of us got any food, but the menu looked good with lots of the normal bar offerings and many of the usual Irish pub type items as well. They also had a good selection of whiskeys (as they should), which we wholeheartedly took advantage of. One thing that was odd was that my whiskey was served in a plastic cup. I'm not sure if that was just because we were seated on the patio, but it was a little strange. Other than that, we had a great experience here and would certainly recommend it.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The music was great and the atmosphere was ok but I was not impressed with my BBQ/pulled pork sandwich. I have had much better.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Stopped in for some live music and A drink. Out-of-towner, so I can't speak for its authenticity of the joint, but we digged it. 

Didn't have food, but the bartender was extremely friendly and patient. The band playing was enthusiastic and were having a good time which you could tell was reflecting onto the crowd. People were dancing. Atmosphere was on point.

Ended up staying for a couple hours, so anytime I come back to Nashville, I'll try to stop in! Oh, and we got took home a souvenir pint glass for I think only $8.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I wanted to write a long diatribe about the commercialization of country music and the way the Opry has been turned into a gigantic strip mall and has lost itself the way Time Square has, but I can't. While I'm not a country fan, I had an awesome evening at the Grand Ole Opry.  My wife - a huge country devotee - had spoken of wanting to visit Nashville and more importantly the Opry since we met and our fifth wedding anniversary presented the perfect opportunity.

Our show consisted of about six or seven acts, and culminated with Lady Antebellum  (the only act I knew) performing for about 30 minutes.  

All in all, the music was great, the atmosphere was fun and the night was a complete and inexpensive hit.  Whether you enjoy country music or not, you'll certainly appreciate all the musicians presented. I highly recommend visiting the Grand Ole Opry.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Really cool to come to this historic place and see country music stars and legends perform. My complaints are that we had to stand outside in the rain because they would not open the doors early and that there were so many commercial breaks.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Incredible place to make a part of your trip to Nashville. My boyfriend and I went through a tour and saw a night show. It was amazing to stand in the circle that used to be a part of the Ryman. Gave me chills. I really liked how we got several tour guides. It made the tour smooth and enjoyable. 

The show was incredible. We saw artists from different generations and it just makes country music so much more special. Venue was so hospitible and clean and just pure country.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: The prices are really good and the serving size is generous. I got the catfish poboy and it was so freakin hot it seared my tastebuds. Let it cool chef!  The flavor was ok and the hilushpuppies were really good, though a bit raw in the middle.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Getting into the Ryman is a disorganized mess.  Too many people and zero staff.  Once inside and seated the show is amazing.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
This was hands down the worst service I have ever experienced in my life.  First, we arrived at 530 PM and the hostess laughed at me when I requested to be near the band.  She sat us off to the side of the stage saying all the tables were reserved even though there were many tables where one could actually see the band.  I walked back up front and pleaded my case again as not all the tables in front of the band had reserved placards the hostess says they were reserved and told me no to a move to another table. While we stayed over an hour and a half only half the tables were ever occupied.  Go figure...

Decide to just move and sit at the bar since it was only half occupied.  Waited 10 minutes, finally snagging the bartender, I ordered drinks. Another 10 minutes, drinks arrive.  After 30 minutes ordered a second round of drinks and appetizers. Finally get the drinks after 15 mins, which was okay I guess since the bartender was having fun socializing with people at the other end of the bar instead of doing her job.  During this wait we discussed with the sound man why the volume was so low from the band and he said to keep the noise down during dinner!  At BB Kings BLUES CLUB??  REALLY???  I guess it's beyond reality to go to a Blues Club expecting good loud entertainment and NOT a QUIET dinner.

Another 25 minutes goes by and I finally get a chance to ask about the appetizers once the bartender came within earshot. She says "I F'$%^ed up..sorry ...never put the order in"  I would not recommend her language to an irate customer.  She dropped off two more drinks as I canceling the food order and stuffing cash in the glass to pay my bill. I wanted food not more alcohol.   Left at that moment and never going back.  Since I live in downtown Nashville that is a shame since I do enjoy the music but not at that level of cruddy service.

The bartender apologized at the end of my ordeal. She should ..it was her fault, she single handily ruined this venue's reputation with me and my friends.  It should not take over an hour and half to get people seated and fed on a Sunday night. 

DO NOT COME TO EAT DINNER. The only saving grace was the live band, the HighJivers ...they were fantastic.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Every single time I've come here I've been met with smart ass inept staff that is always to busy or too stupid to answer a simple question.  Bartenders are ass holes the waitresses are bitches.  I literally can not stand this place. I'll never come back.  I don't know why I ever did.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: We went to 4 different Karaoke bars in Nashville and the majority of the people who sang at this one actually had some talent and were entertaining. At the other places people just yelled into the microphones and couldn't sing. This was a fun place to go to even though it wasn't crowded the few times we went.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: I have been waiting for the "rooftop" bar to open for a few months and was disappointed when it turned out to only be open on one side with garage doors but that's not even the worst part. Finally made it over there to try it out and they are charging TEN DOLLARS to go up to the "premier lounge" at 2 pm on a Saturday..... the downstairs bar wasn't that busy so I can only assume the upstairs "lounge" was COMPLETELY empty. 10 dollars is insane and a terrible business decision and after reading the reviews from the World Series games I can see it is just a pattern with the managers/owners. My experience turned me off and will not be going back or recommending to friends.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Probably a great local spot. Has all the proper trappings to be as such. But to find out, I guess one would need learn what the secret handshake is. Hey can not blame wanting to keep club closed. Neighborhood bars vanishing... but then again so are neighbors

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: We came here late Sat afternoon for some drinks with friends. It was our first visit. We had a great time. Such a relaxing and laid back place. Great drink options. Soooo many beer selections. Fair prices. The Tennessee Tea was delicious. We didn't try food but the menu looked pretty delicious too.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Each time I visited Belcourt Taps I had roaches crawling on the bar counter right in front of me by my plate of food. They also love like to cancel gigs at the last minute and not notify the artist.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
The Grand ole Opry is one of Nashville TN's most famous tourist attractions. It's fame stems from the fact that country music was pretty much born and breaded here. It was interesting to see this famed institution.

Many of country music's iconic famous stars got their start here. Or so I've read on Wikipedia and tripadvisor. With that said, since I was in nearby Brentwood, TN, I figured that it would be in my best interest to venture up to Nashville and see the Grand Ole Opry concert house "just to see it", among my main reasons for going. It's basically a concert hall that gave country music a legitimate birthplace here in Nashville, TN. While I am not a country music fan, some of the popular music that streamed into the mainstream consciousness within the last 10 years have come from the country music scene, at least some of which are from "American Idol". I arrived here on a casual Tuesday evening from a drive originating from Huntsville, AL. At first, I could not find the Grand Ole Opry since it was kind of tucked away. The Opry Mills shopping center you will see when driving up on the interstate and there is a dedicated exit sign for the Grand Ole Opry. How neat is that? For the most part, it was nice seeing the Opry house for the first time ever. 

And while I did not attend a country music show, due to my choice of music, I enjoyed my time here, "just to see" the Grand Ole Opry in Nashville, TN. The Grand Ole Opry is located at xxx Opryland Drive, next to the aforementioned Opry Mills shopping center and nearby the Gaylord Opryland hotel and resort. They really go all out here, since it's Nashville's most iconic institution and I don't blame them. There are pretty much 2 separate parking lots: one for the Opry Mills shopping center and one for the Opry itself. I realized this when I parked my rental car at the shopping center, walked over to the Grand Ole Opry, and found out that there is another separate lot nearby. Oh well. There is no admission fee accessed when you're just visiting the outside of the Opry house, but certainly there is admission fee charged for shows and guided tours. They accept major credit cards, so that's always a great thing. Ticket prices for the country music shows can vary from performer, so do check with the box office or the Grand Ole Opry website for more information and show times. I do admit that it would be something if I were to stick around and see a show at the Opry. Since I was on a schedule - even on vacation, my time spent here at the Grand Ole Opry was to admire the fact that I was here and to enjoy the moment.

Being a tourist can be swell, but can be limiting as well. It was nice to be in the presence of famous people, or just places to be inspired by, to be honest. Being inspired here is a great thing. I did enjoy the 2 large guitars that were by the entrance to the parking lot. I saw many people were posing by them and taking photos. Many selfies and group photos to be had! I took some myself and admired the building for what icon it is. The building itself was as grand as you could get, while maintaining a cute homespun flavor to it. I'm sure many world class performances have been held here at the Grand Ole Opry over the decades and will continue to do so in the future. While I don't regret trying to schedule a show during my travels to Nashville, TN, there's always next time for sure. If you are a country music lover, this place is most likely the place to be. I'd recommend coming here, just to be a tourist and see the Grand Ole Opry. 

4 stars solid. The grounds are well maintained and there are benches to sit on in front of the doors for weary travelers and those whom need them. It was a privilege to ge here for sure. Keep this place in your travel schedule.

Support local!

B

name: Third Man Records
text: Good folks doing good things for Pietown and Nashville in general. The shows, merchandise, and customer service are always top notch at TMR, happy to support this business.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Slow service, slow (bad) food. 
Had two bites of my burger to know I didn't like it, just to have my server never return until she dropped checks. Making me pay for the burger I didn't even eat. 
They need to learn to staff appropriately to give service that is necessary. HORRIBLY DISAPOINTED.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: If my husband and I get a sitter you can probably find us at Belcourt Tap at some point in our evening. We love it here! Please note this is not a review of their food as I have never eaten here, however, the music here is amazing! When I moved to Nashville over a year ago I tended to go to the more touristy spots at first until I discovered Belcourt! I have heard some of the best music of my life here (cough, Chris Canterbury), and they have a good beer list too! This bar has a neighborhood feel and different performers every hour until usually 11pm, 7 days per week. If you have never visited Belcourt please do but just don't tell the tourists:)

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: I was called a faggot by the door man. I walked inside and was immediately told they were closing when there was an hour left. There was urine ALL over the floor to the bathroom. It is a ratchet place and the service is very poor. Go across the street or look elsewhere on Broadway. I wouldn't recommend this to a DOG.

name: Third Man Records
text:
I am in Nashville for business and just had to visit this spot. If you're a fan of Jack White, then this is the place you need to see.
Many bands have recorded here (i.e. Weezer, Weird Al, Neil Diamond), and you can actually record your own singing voice in that same booth and have it copied on your own record! There is another booth in the store where you can listen to many vinyls issued by Third Man. Unfortunately during our visit, most of the machines were out of order. 
Keep in mind that there is very limited parking, and is located in a part of town that can get sketchy at night. If you're in Nashville, definitely visit this place!

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text:
So I went to the Dawg House Saloon on NYE for the Super T show thanks to some nice friends of mine.  It was a good time.

First, I think this place used to be something else but I cannot remember what exactly.  There's a patio out front, a big square bar when you walk in, a stage and dance floor in the back, and tables situated all around.  For NYE they had everything decorated and looking festive.  

As for the band, they were fun and the dance floor was big enough for everyone to shake their ass.  Sound was good I think - at that point the booze was taking over and it seemed fun to me.  Let's be honest, it all seemed fun to me.

They also have TVs and some people I know go there on Sundays to watch football and do their Sunday funday up right.  I think they also have some food to help you not have tooooo much fun.

Give it a try, it is new and if you like bars I can't imagine you won't like this!

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: It's amazing how much terrible service really stays with you. You always remember places where they treated you like trash. Anyways, went there for my friend's bachelorette and we were greeted by two of the rudest bartenders. A girl with purple kool-aid hair, at the time, and a red head. They do not acknowledge you and make you wait 10 minutes for a drink only to come over and wave her hand while saying "what do you want?" And don't you dare discuss drinks with your friends because then you're all "talking to her at once" and she "just can't." She literally walked away and left us standing there waiting for another bartender to get us drinks.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
My Husband and I were heading to Nashville and even thought we are not big country fans, we can appreciate good music and wanted to cross it off the bucket list. I got $48 tickets in the balcony, 3rd row.  Spectacular seats!  We ended up being at the side of the stage, about 9 rows back.  The seats are pews, which is nice, but not much leg room.
The show itself was SOOOO good!!!  We really enjoyed ourselves!  It was funny, and the musicians were all top notch!!
Bobby Osborne played "Rocky Top" and the crows loved it.  We had never heard that song before, but the fans sure did.  All of the performers were really good and I like that they didn't only play their songs, they played songs that influenced them as musicians.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great choice! Loved the music, good food and superb service!  Friendly folks and a good vibe will keep us coming back for more.  Try them out if new to downtown scene, very different and more sophisticated than Broadway crazies.  Ribs are best, fried pickles and cold local brews combined with sweet gal server was perfect!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: I second Tim K in saying that Colt was great! The bars were insanely busy after a Preds playoff game dumped out onto Broadway. Even though he was super busy on the roof, Colt was super attentive and came around to make sure we had full drinks. No other bar on Bway had bartenders going out of their way to help. The rooftop was a great atmosphere to put down some drinks with the guys and play some giant Jenga too!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Fantastic concert venue. We came to the Opry tonight and had the pleasure of hearing Carrie Underwood along with many other talented musicians. This was my first time at the Opry and I hope to go back soon. 

Sign up for the email list and get their coupons too, we got a dollar off $5 or more purchase of food, not including alcohol.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
My girlfriend Julie & I spent a few days in Nashville for the 4th of July. We stopped in BB's a few times but never ate. This review is mainly about the quality of the live bands & happy hour.

The happy hour has great drink specials every day. You really should make it a point to head here for happy hour (11AM-6PM).

The live bands playing at night were great. It was a great respite from country music. We saw a soul band & a blues band. If you want a temporary exit from twangy county music then head over here.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: It was great. The your was interesting if you're in to tours. The beer was good. The atmosphere was the best part. A couple of Tvs for sports, board games, live music, and yours every hours. At times it seems like there's a lot going on but it flowed well. Great spot for a good time with friends or a date.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Three stars is pretty much on the money. I don't understand a Margaritaville in Nashville but I also am probably not the actual target demographic of these places...see: my dad who sometimes makes me think he can't find anything else on his XM radio other than Margaritaville. 

So we've of course been to the one in the Caymans and on Key West. Since clearly these are out of the way places, I didn't get in the way of my parents having their experience here. 

I was kind of hoping to avoid listening to music...or at least if I was going to have to listen to covers, NOT "Call Me Maybe" gone country. It's somewhat loud in here and I imagine as the night goes on it's louder. We were here prior to a hockey game but it was still pretty busy. 

Since I procured my family a free app coupon I decided I was worthy of the 5 o'clock somewhere which is a take on a Hurricane, which somehow in five years of legal drinking I have never had before. It wasn't bad. I imagine it's one of those things where you're like "oh this barely tastes like alcohol, I'll have another" and then suddenly you're hitting on someone you shouldn't be hitting on. Wait what.

For that free app, we had the spinach artichoke dip. It wasn't bad, I certainly wouldn't have let anyone pay full price for it though. 

I wasn't feeling like having a full on sandwich or anything but there aren't really any smaller sized options. I guess a cup of soup but I had had soup for lunch and it was like obscenely hot for December so that was out of the question. I decided to just get the chicken quesadilla app and if I didn't finish it then whatever. The rest of my family had burgers or a chicken sandwich. The burgers were liked all around, although my brother got the diablo one and complained that it wasn't spicy enough. But I don't think he understands that poblanos aren't that hot.

The quesadilla wasn't bad, there were some spots though where the chicken was a bit tough. Nothing you can't fix with a good bit of salsa though. 

Even though like I said it was pretty busy, we were there only about an hour. Service was great. Would I come back on my own? Probably not. In my case it's really one of those places where once is enough for the experience but if I were asked to come again, I wouldn't say no.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
As avid brewery connoisseurs and current Nashville locals, we were extremely and pleasantly surprised with our experience at Tennessee Brew Works this evening.

 It was a dreary, rainy night and as we pulled up we were fairly apprehensive about the string of dark warehouses and quiet alleys. It all changed quickly as we walked into the "Tennessee Fill Station" (or some name similar) portion of the building. The fellas working there directed us to the "Tennessee Tap Room" (or some name similar) portion of the building that overlooked 2 stories into the "Tennessee Brew Works" (or some name similar) portion of the building where the brewing takes place. I've added the specifics because this is the first group audacious and clever enough to pull off all three portions under one roof.... and to still comply with Tennessee's archaic liquor laws! If sticking it to the man isn't enough reason for you to check it out.... keep reading. 

The tap room is super neat and cleverly laid out with patios, long & community-oriented tables, a flying bridge or "catwalk" and a steady stream of live, local music. It's largely non-smoking (which is enough to convince me to cross the bridge from East Nashville) and has a few TVs to cater to the football crowds. 

Biggest fortes:

- The staff is amazing. The smiles and enthusiasm when they start talking about their beer are a sweet relief. They're excited! They're adventurous! They aren't pretentious. Real People.
- The beers are fresh & different. They keep it local. They aren't afraid to venture from the norm. They add their own zing and flair.... and for that, I respect them.
- They appreciate the food & beer pairing concept. They're bringing in great food to compliment their brews. It's a movement.

If you've managed to read all of that rambling- you can ignore any other reviews and just go ahead and get there.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: $1 PBRs until 6pm - can't  beat that plus live music! Very talented artists playing. The bar reminds me of a local joint, although it's in the middle of broadway. No cover, great to to stop in during late afternoon. Will update if I get a chance to come at night!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We shared the volcano nachos and they were pretty tasty. My son got wings and he enjoyed them. We had to sit upstairs and it kinda took away from the scene. I would have rather been downstairs with the live music. I enjoyed the Margarita flight and it did not disappoint.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: I walked in to an amazing set by an all-female bluegrass outfit (with the owner, Layla, on drums) and soon the talent segued into a tears-in-your-beer and honky-tonking country four-piece.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The worst!!! We waited in line for 2 hours while they let ppl cut in front of us...when we finally get in...order drinks and food it takes 23 min to get our food..nachos....all bottom of the barrel chips...server says NOTHING!!! ...and still no 2 beers and a marg....never come...I do this for a living...there is no excuse for food to beat drinks...if this is happening the MOD on duty is NOT doing their job helping and backing up the staff....drinks come..we order shots....wrong shots came out not what we ordered...then we get charged for 6 shots!!! Sorry wrong again.... Nothing to fix the problem...then give us the wrong bill!!! We pay bill because obviously we are not here for customer service...and it's a few dollars cheaper...don't think we would have gotten much better. Surprising how a establishment can treat their guests this way and expect them to come back....wait it's a tourist spot so why would they care. Seriously you couldn't last on your guest services...good thing your a "TRAP" makes me wonder if our "stellar" service is because of poor management and training. Good luck..hate to think a big corporate restaurant like you can take out honest wholesome business with good service and honest and integrity. Never again

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: We were excited about the fun vibe and great music in a laid back atmosphere on Broadway! Bartender was not friendly--yelling at customers and not real accommodating. Had to leave to enjoy our laid back vibe elsewhere.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Ordered burger and wings. My husband and I split them great portions to split. Best burger we ever had! Made with short ribs. The wings were great.  The sauce was excellent little sweet and a little spicy.  Oh yeah the beer very good. Excellent service order at the bar and they serve you. All round great service.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Food is awesome; better than you find in most restaurants.  
The beer is spot on as well.  My only complaint about the beer is that you can't always get growlers filled if the beer is a limited edition. 
Location is okay, construction all over the place so parking is limited.
Great atmosphere and wait staff.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Sat in open seating at the bar, purposefully picking a table near the large open window at the front of the restaurant. I came with my mother and we were looking for drinks and a quick bite to eat. We ended up going with the margarita flight and a quesadilla. The margaritas were amazing and the quesadilla was delicious. We ended up getting a second flight of margaritas because we couldn't settle on just one from the selection. Our waitress was sweet and attentive. She had a lot of recommendations both for drinks at Margaritaville and other places on the strip. Live music arrived about 20 minutes after we had and had a good sound and playful interactions with those in the bar. Our bill was approximately $50, which initially was shocking but I left happy, full, and feeling good from my drinks so it was worth it. Overall a nice experience; good drinks, food, and environment.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
It is not too many arenas and stadiums across the world that I land as a five stars.  It really is a lot that has to work in making this happen.  The first but probably most important reason why a stadium or arena gets a five star review is due to accessibility to it.  What I love about Bridgestone Arena is it knocks it out the park with accessibility.  Meaning, you can drive to the nearby garage to park there. You can park for free at Nissan Stadium (formerly known as LP Field)  and walk across the Pedestrian bridge (10 min walk) right to the arena.  And you have the bright lights of Broadway where the arena is on.  So before the game or after the game, you have a surplus of sports bars, live music venues and barbeque joints to check out before, during or around the game.  IT WORKS!  All what I have said is before talking about the arena itself.  I'm sure the concerts here are great.   The hockey games here is a great watch.  Seats are decent but getting in and out, the concourse, the food venues..all good with me.

Grade: A++

name: Ole Red
text: We just had a drink and dessert here. My husband had the fried pie. It was apple. He said it was too much like Mickey D's....and that it needed  some cinnamon. I had the ice cream sandwich which was a sugar cookie with vanilla ice cream and marshmallows. It was good.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Great food good times if your looking  for a great time this is the place hands down the staff are professional and always taking care of their customers tell unsweetened tea comes in a huge glass and the food comes in huge portions the customers are nice and will hold a great conversation with you as well.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: 2nd night in Nashville we wanted something a little different and not so touristy honky tonk of broadway. We heard midtown is the spot. This place is like a dive bar you would see in a college town. Everyone is fairly young, well alot younger then broadway. Love how they have karaoke here. The vibe is fun, very laid back. In the battle between Winners and Losers (the bar next door) this place deff wins!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
This was probably the most dive type bar we visited this past weekend for our girls trip in Nashville but I tend to like smaller bars so I really enjoyed my time! 

We stayed downstairs because 1. we wanted to hear the extremely talented band & 2. because upstairs felt about 20 degrees hotter. But overall the experience was very fun & relaxed.

The only suggestion would be to go with a smaller group because it felt smaller than the other bars we had been visiting so it was hard to find a spot for all 9 of us.

name: Ole Red
text: Wow! Great new addition to Broadway. The venue is amazing. Ate at the rooftop Lookout. Ordered almost half the menu between the five of us. Love the small plate concept, got to try and share so much. Cocktails are fabulous. Prices are extremely reasonable, especially for the quality. Service is spot on. Can't wait to go back and try the rest of the menu.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We didn't eat here but all the food on the plates looked very good and had big servings, we just stopped in the check out the store and use the restrooms.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: Jazmine Sullivan concert. She is singing her heart out. She's great the venue does not have good acoustics

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text:
Winner's is hands down my favorite place to karaoke in Nashville.

While there are some aspiring country music singers scattered throughout, I feel more comfortable singing my random crazy songs here with a group of friends. A lot of downtown karaoke bars are 80% amazing singers, 20% random drunk people. I like that I don't feel that I'm the only bad singer out there when I visit Winner's! 

Plus, you never know who you will run into at Winner's. One night a random dude came in and sang "Friends in Low Places" with someone from our group who was on stage; it turns out the guy is a well known songwriter in Nashville, and he WROTE that song. Wow.

The prices are reasonable and you are sure to meet some new friends! Plus I love the patio out front and the randomness that ensues! 

Note: karaoke is only on Friday and Saturdays :)

name: Ole Red
text: I haven't been this disappointed in a restaurant for a very long time. Ole Red's is a burger and beer joint. My burger came in undercooked and wasn't really very flavorful. My wife made the same statement, "We waited for this??!" I tried the Nashvillian burger and she had the Ole Red burger.  Neither is anything special. Service was extremely average for 4:30 on a Saturday without a big crowd.  I gave it 2 stars because the apps were good and it's a cool location. Go here if you want to say you've been to Blake Shelton's restaurant. His music is a lot better than his restaurants food.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Food and drinks were really good! Service wasn't! At one point we couldn't find our server. But the live music was really good! If our server wasn't MIA we would have stayed the whole night!

name: Nashville Symphony
text: Had a wonderful night with husband and 2 of our kids at Cirque de la Symphonie with the Nashville Symphony. An amazing show! This is a great, comfortable concert hall. We sat in a Founders box and it was very comfortable with great views. We have come for different concerts here and they are always very enjoyable.

name: Ole Red
text: Stopped in here while on a quick trip to Nashville! Very instagram-worth spot with cool sofas and fun decor. We had the pickle flight and nachos, along with several cocktails. Nachos were so good--made with homemade potato chips?!? Take me back!

name: Ole Red
text:
Wow ... impressed. Super yummy food with huge portions. Homemade Tater Tots and great pickles. Pulled pork has a thicker smoke flavor, but good. Grits had great texture, well made. Everything was fantastic ... come with a huge appetite. I ate maybe 1/3 of my lunch, but couldn't take it as we are bar hopping. I told the server I cut it in 1/2 and to eat it. Lol

Very cool establishment... great music !

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Good beer and good food! Fish tacos were great. Large seating area in and out. Bit of a walk from dwntwn but worthwhile.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The food, service, atmosphere was amazing. We came here for my girlfriends 21st birthday and it was simply incredible. Live music, great staff, and great food. Everyone in here is having a great time. Would definitely recommend this for others

name: Ole Red
text: If you are looking to go somewhere where customer service is not a priority, this is your place. Extremely rude and unprofessional waitresses. Every other place on Broadway had accommodating waitstaff. Highly disappointed in the lack of training that seems to be happening in a place that has potential.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I had some crap dip as an appetizer, it is delicious and later on my server told me that I had picked the best appetizer on the menu. Check it out guys. It's worth it

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Getting a table here was a little difficult. There was no wait but the servers couldn't decide where to put us so we ended up just going to the bar area. Kiersten took great care of us. Came here to take my friend for his first marg! Prob will just sit at the bar from now on, they seem very attentive and friendly.

name: National Underground
text:
This establishment is truly the worst. (And I'm not just saying this to fit in with the 50 other 1-star reviews.)

For starters, the owner is an absolute jerk off who has no problem getting wasted in the bar and kicking you out if you disagree with him. I've seen it happen at least twice. They should bite the bullet and place a sign over the door stating that differing opinions are not welcome. 

I've also been privy to him taking advantage of drunk people and telling the bartender to add drinks to the tab that weren't ordered or that were "on the house" for other people. 

Then there is the "manager." I can't count how many times I've seen him berate paying customers, get into loud, heated arguments, and throw people out. 

And let's not forget the aforementioned bottled water debacle. 

I'm not sure how or why this place stays open through Nashville's boom. I would come fairly regularly for a while to give it a chance but I eventuslly couldn't do it anymore. 

I certainly hope this is not the impression of Tennesseans tourists leave with.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
My 8 girlfriends & I decided on Margaritaville on a Thursday night around 6pm because the menu looked like there was something for everyone. (2 vegetarians, 2 who loved seafood, all of us who love tequila etc.).

We put our name in for a table & it was ready in under 10 minutes which went by so fast because we sat outside & enjoyed the live music playing. Our waitress was phenomenal, 9 hungry & thirsty girls seemed like a breeze for her. We let her know right away we wanted separate checks & she had no problem with that at all while many restaurants make you feel extremely guilty for asking. 

I ordered the veggie burger with fries which was good but I have had better. My margarita however was one of the bests I've ever had but I can't remember the name.

Service was excellent & ticket times were running quick for it being so very busy. While it was pricey for me, ($30 including tip), I would still recommend this restaurant.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The Margaritas were yummy!  And I have never liked Margaritas. Lol. My mom had the regular on the rocks and I had Mango over Paris which consisted of peach snapps, tequila and mango pieces small enough to fit through the straw right into my mouth. Ingenious!!
