The staff continued service during the performances, but it was more difficult to get the staff's attention (as you would expect).  My suggestion is to arrive and eat early, then sip a drink during the music.

The reason people come to the Bluebird is to hear live music.  I've heard all of the legendary stories of epic performances in the "listening room" setting.  However, on the night I visited, the artists left something to be desired.  I don't want to criticize anyone who performs and puts themselves out there for others to listen to.  However, I will say that the group we saw was not up to the standard that I expected from the venue's reputation.  The other guests with me had visited the Bluebird multiple times, and all agreed that this was the worst performance they had seen.  Without going into specifics, the music was more juvenile than I expected, and the constant pandering to "Nashville" TV fame was extremely annoying.  I get it,  you're on the show... You don't need to remind me every 5 minutes!

I read an article online that described happiness as someone's expectations minus her reality.  Under that framework, Bluebird Cafe didn't measure up on the night I went.  However, I would go back and hear a different set of artists perform.  To summarize, only visit if you have reservations, and hope that you hear a strong artist or two.  Without the good music, there's nothing to fall back on.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Hashtag; Serena, I'm sorry. 

This 5 star rating is a rating of my actual experience here, factoring in alcohol,  and not an overall assessment of the establishment as a whole. As i was in no position to do so. 

Let me preface this by saying this was a 2am,  3 sheets to the wind, stumbling home stop for a burger after partying down for a few hours. 

The joint is done up real cool, I like the divey feel, and how the band's stage is situated so you have to walk past it to get to the rest of the bar. Feels like you've got a rock'n soundtrack to the beginning and end of your time there. 

The Staff:  In all honesty I don't remember much, BUT I do remember the lovely bartender Serena (sp?) being galacticly tolerant and gracious to me despite my drunken jackassery. Seriously, I was a L7 wanker. Serena,  let me publicly apologize for whatever rude or absurd ramblings I subjected you to. (I was able to recall your name because one thing I do remember is going ON AND ON about how your name reminded me of the show FireFly and Serenity).  

The Food: The bacon cheeseburger we had was AMAZING! .. and i think there were some tater tots, but I can't be sure. 

Overall, it's totally worth stopping in and trying it out.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
This is a pretty good meet up spot. The food, its average. The atmosphere, I really like. I came here to meet girls for drinks one evening. The cellar was super loud and difficult to hear people across the table. I ordered the trio guac. The pineapple one was my favorite. Like I said, good not great. 

Brunch was definitely the better option for me personally. I'd recommend asking for a table not next to the stage is available. They do have $15 unlimited mimosas. Not super strong, but hey! They're $15! I ordered the enchiladas. My friends ordered the breakfast tacos and the chicken biscuit with gravy. I didn't try the tacos but she said they were pretty good. I liked the biscuit and enchiladas. Brunch also comes with biscuits and a jam or sorghum butter. I wasn't a fan of the jam but the better was great!

Overall, I'd come here again. Not my first choice but they have a decent happy hour.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Your luck with getting a reservation isn't too high! I was online in the queue waiting long before 8am, randomly placed in line at 8am, and by 8:08am the tickets were completely sold out. So sad! I know it would have been amazing. It would be better if the site recognized and honored who first was on the page rather than randomly placing people. Oh well!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Reservation process is ABSOLUTELY AWFUL. Don't waste a minute with these guys. I rearranged my flights to make sure I was online at 8am CST and got into room at 805 - May 10 was already SOLD OUT!! So frustrating. It's one time my wife is in Nashville and I did everything they told me about to get tix. The game's rigged. Don't waste your time.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Went to this place with my wife for an evening meal.  We were not greeted by anyone, even though there was only a small crowd that night.  Still, we decided to give it a try.  After a lengthy wait for some sort of acknowledgment that we were there, I went up to the bar to get some menus.  The bartender ignored me and continued to flirt with several young ladies.  Two young couples came in and were attended to very promptly.  At that point, I decided that we were too old for this place and got up and left. 
We will not be back.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: They claim they have the best burger ever. I didn't think it was anything special. The decor is cool and the girl at the register was really sweet. The burger wasn't bad and it was a good late night snack. I just peeked into the bar half, so I can't really judge that aspect of this place.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Aaahhhhhhh!!!!! Now this is what Country's all about "Ya'll"!!!!!  Unbelievable....can't believe I'm witnessing what I'm seeing!!!!  This place is INSANE!!!!!  Wall to wall people on all 3 floors!!!!!  I LOVE IT!!!!!!  Amazing place in glorious Nashville!!!  .  As someone local told me...."Nashville's got such soul...I love it!!"  I couldn't Agree more!!!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Hands down the worst experience I've ever had in a bar. Bartender stood, leaning against the wall, watching the band, while chewing on a straw, and ignored us. When I asked if we could order drinks, she said "Yes, what do you want?" However, she never took a step toward us. We had to ask for a beer list, which was placed near us, but not given to us, while she looked every where but at us. I asked her if it was too much trouble, and she just said, "No, I asked what you wanted." We just left, and didn't get to enjoy what sounded like a great band. We have been touring the state, eating and drinking, and tipping very well for good service. Not here, though!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Honky Tonk/Bar.
This place has a special place in my heart because it's the first Nashville-bar I walked in to. And I was not disappointed. It's divey with great music and bartenders.
I prefer the first floor but it can be really crowded.
Don't forget to try their applepie shine!

name: The Stone Fox
text: This review is for Bingo and cocktails--we had SO MUCH fun!!!  The bingo guys made our night!  Thank you so much for putting this on!  The music was great and the calling was a colorful delight.  We were never thirsty and the trip home (yay, Uber!) is a happy blur, so the staff is aces in my book!  I'm certainly not sporty, so I had no idea we had cruised into Nashville during the Music City Bowl, so this trip had more than it's fair share of surprises--This night was a GREAT surprise!  The Stone Fox's bingo night WAS right up my alley.  Thanks everyone!!!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Well worth the wait. We got there Monday for open mic and although we were 1 1/2 hours early we didn't make the cut..............to our great fortune. Later we arrived 2 hours early for a 2 hour show (haven't done that in quite a while) having no idea what a treat we were in for. This place is tiny and they will find a way to cram up to the limit of allowed by law.
It's "Blue Monday" and the house band is playing out of this world. I recognize a bad ass bass player that played for Ashley Cleveland when she was down here in Austin (the live music capital of the world) and in the back I see someone familiar. HOLY SHIT, it's Joe Bonamassa on a guitar in the background. He just happened to "pop in" and join the set. The band later asks a couple of other famous musicians to come on stage and play too.
Sometimes miracles happen and you happen to be in the right place at the right time.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
This is a place that I've never thought of eating at but it was AMAZING! I will definitely be returning. The food was well prepared and the service was excellent. The ambience was southern and lovely. 

Our group of four enjoyed  the humus and hot chicken bites. I ordered the grill cheese dunk with the tomato soup, savory and delectable. I cannot say enough. 
The cocktails were creative and love just about everything about this great gem of a spot!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We went here for brunch yesterday.  We ordered chicken fried chicken with biscuits and sausage gravy.  The gravy was watery and had no sausage in it.  It was ready too quickly to have been prepared in any way other that microwave.  The chicken was dried out and tasteless.  My husband was served eggs that were full of cracked shells.  Very disappointing meal.  Bloody Mary's were great but for a bill of over $100 with drinks we should have gotten edible food.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Stone Fox: I wanted to like you! I might try coming back for another show, but I'll just order drinks from the bar.

I try not to judge a place from an experience with 1 bad server. However, ours informed us he was leaving so we would have to close out, and did not change us over to another server. This is after he took 20 minutes after we ordered a pitcher and he informed us they were out of PBR drafts so essentially we were SOL. 

Uh...couldn't he just have given us over to another server? 

When my boyfriend went up to pay at the bar, the bartender was snotty & informed us we would have to chase our server down (God knows where he was at this point; even though he had conveyed quite the sense of urgency that we had to pay RIGHT NOW). 

I completely understand wanting to leave at the end of your shift, but that doesn't mean taking the frustrations of the day out on your customers.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: This will now go down in history as one of my favorite venues in the country. The acoustics are incredible. Such a warm, intimate environment. We hit up the Bluebird for Open Mic Monday and Mike Henderson band. Open Mic was fantastic. The talent in this town is unbelievable. Then Mike Henderson band was phenomenal, playing blues covers and getting the house rocking. I'm so happy we stopped here!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsie's is a very lively place!

I only had a short stay but had a fun time. Tootsie's has 3 floors of live music, so get the benefit of choosing which you like best! You can also duck out onto their balcony, which was my choice to just converse with friends outside the crowd. Drinks were expensive, but you are paying for the experience.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: This place was the worst dining experience I've had thus far in Nashville. I'm a little bit of a food snob, but it's hard not to be when you have so many great restaurants around you. The Sutler is definitely not one of them. It took us 3 HOURS from start of meal to checks, mainly because our server was non-existent throughout the meal. We waited 45 minutes at the end because we couldn't find her to ask for a check. The food is absolutely awful and it's a shame they get away with charging what they charge for it. I've had better meals at Roberts on lower broad. About the only saving grace was that the bands playing from Belmont we're really great. Still, I'd never come back and don't waste your money on the horrible food.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Well, this was certainly an interesting spot on the Nashville Broadway tourist trap...err... bar circuit.  I visited Tootsie's over Christmas when the weather was unseasonably warm.  I had a good time and got to experience what brings people to Tootsie's.

To start, Tootsie's is a multi-level bar that features live music and a large upstairs patio that overlooks the Bridgestone Arena and Music City Center.  It's part of a strip of bars that feature music and cater to tourists in the area.  

The interior of Tootsie's is unremarkable.  The decor is what you would expect, and the place has a more run-down vibe than some of the newer bars across the street.  I don't mean that as an insult - Tootsie's has a dive bar vibe, and that's a good thing because it is a change of pace from a lot of the other bars nearby.

The top floor is where I spent most of my time, and the deck offers a great view of the street below as well as the Arena across the way.  I enjoyed being on the patio, and there was a live band that played on the top floor.  It was a lot of fun to hangout, to the extent that the rest of the bar was a bit of a letdown.  Because of the unusual weather, Tootsie's was crowded on the day I visited, but the staff handled it well.  There wasn't a problem splitting tickets, but the waitress did forget one beer.  She apologized and gave it to us for free, which was great.

The food and drinks at Tootsie's are about what you would expect for the area:  They are serviceable but overpriced.  I understand that you are paying for the music and atmosphere, but it was a little too touristy for me.  Some of the bartenders were trying way too hard with their appearances, while the guys were lackadaisical unless a pretty girl needed a drink.  My whiskey shot came in a sad little plastic cup that was *barely* half full.  For the exorbitant price, I expected a little more liquor or at least a shot glass so I would feel l like I was getting my money's worth.  My beer was too warm, which is probably a problem with the lines from the keg to the well. The food was bar quality.  My only complaints were the price relative to the quality.

Overall, I enjoyed Tootsie's for what it was - an overpriced bar with a great view.  I would recommend it if you are in tourist mode, but there are far better places to go unless you just want to be on Broadway.  It wasn't my scene, but I can see why others might enjoy it.  It's certainly better than some of the alternatives in the the area!

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text: I was worried about seeing a show here with all the negative reviews but it was awesome. We went about 2 hours early to do the free whiskey tasting and the $5 wine tasting before eating at café fontanel. Nothing was overly crowded and we were able to get right in all three. Cafe fontanel was just ok for me but nice to have a place onsite all within close walking distance. We took our beach chairs that sit on the ground into the music venue. There really was not a bad place you could sit. We were there to see Trampled by Turtles. The music was fantastic and the background of the stage was gorgeous. We stayed till the very end of the show and getting out was no problem at all.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: The history, the atmosphere, the nostalgia... The service exceeded my expectations. I had goosebumps just knowing the history. My lunch was delicious. If you're into history, good food and great service, you should check this place out. Sit at the counter for the full experience.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I wanted to wait a couple of days to see if my anger subsided in regards to my treatment at Tootsies.  I came here with a group of friends expecting to have a good time on Friday February 12 2016, not expecting to be singled out because I am African American.  We got into the line that was set up outside the bar, and the line seemed to be moving fairly quickly.  As I observed the security person outside, he seemed to check a person's ID and then let them in the bar without any type of trouble.  Once I got to the front of the line, I observed more of the same, the bouncer was letting everyone in without being searched with a wand.  Once I got to the front of the line, he asked to search me with a wand, when he had not searched anyone else ( with the exception of the guy standing right in front of us ) previously.  The thing that incensed me the most, was that the person he searched was in a group of four, and he only searched the one guy out of the group right before he asked me to dump everything out of my pockets.  It seems like he was making a scene about searching the guy right before me, so I could not say that I was being singled out, when it was obvious that I was being singled out.  How could he explain that he let the other three guys in without searching them?  Was it the way I was dressed?  I hope not, because I was wearing tennis shoes, skinny jeans (that fit), and a grey Chicago Bulls hoodie.  I am sure that I appeared to be thugging out in my group of mostly Caucasian friends.  I am seriously angered, hurt, and upset that I was treated this way.  No one deserves to be singled out to be searched, especially on the basis of their race.  The other people in my group ( who were mostly Caucasian, one was Hispanic ), were not asked to be searched at all.  I will never go here again, and will recommend to anyone in the Nashville area to not support an establishment that uses such practices to single out people due to their race.

name: Tin Roof
text: Came for lunch at 11:50am it now 1:40pm... we ordered french fries and buffalo wings the moment we sat down.... Slowest service on Demonbreun for lunch. Make sure you have a few hours to blow if you decide to go to Tin Roof

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text:
Lived in Middle TN all my life, so I have fond memories of Starwood (and now Ascend). Fontanel has a lot of work to do before they begin to meet expectations..

Good: Didn't take that long for us to get in and out of the venue as others experienced. But, we did get there an hour + early.

Meh: Based on the number of people filing out early, we left before the encore to ensure we didn't sit in line forever. There's one way in and one way out.

Bad: The GA seats suck. They are not only on a slight incline, but also to the left of the stage. Literally all we could see was stage equipment. If anyone stood up, and I'm talking many feet down the 'hill', you couldn't see a thing. The best view of the event was over near the porta-johns. 
'Bathrooms' had very little lighting. It's hard enough to use a porta-john, but in the dark it becomes downright treacherous. 
Food was expensive, tall boys were $9 and a small mixed drink was $11. 

We paid $50 for these tickets and it was the worst venue we've ever been to. We will definitely not be back. I don't care who it is. No bueno.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I couldn't believe how small this place was. We got there an hour ahead of time and luckily made it in on a Thursday. We actually got better seats because we were the latest ones in. The talent is amazing. It was a great experience. I definitely recommend it if you're visiting Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: HORRIBLE PLACE!!!!! I had to talk to the manager twice and NOTHING was done. Service is horrible and the bartenders are B's I had one tell her coworker not to sell me anything because she didn't like me RUDE..... manager's did nothing. Don't bother

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text:
I've only been to the Woods Amphitheater at Fontanel once so far, for the Barenaked Ladies/Guster/Ben Folds concert.  Having grown up with an outdoor amphitheater in St Louis, I've had lots of experiences with outdoor concerts.  Woods at Fontanel was fine--there were pros and cons to the theater that made the concert we saw there both great and not as good as it could be.

The Pros:
-Nice variety of concerts and performers--there really is something for everyone.
-It's a small space compared to the amphitheater I'm used to, so there's really no such thing as a bad seat
-The sound was great throughout the entire concert.  Consistent, loud enough but not too loud, and a nice balance of instruments and voices.
-The vibe.  Everyone is relaxed, easy-going, and there for a good time.
-Free parking.
-Food trucks and fun contests on the way into the concert space.

The Cons:
-If you purchase actual seats, there is no slope to the grass to allow for stadium-style seating.  If the people in front of you are standing, there is no way for you to see the stage.  That's a major problem in my book.
-The seats are placed VERY close together, uncomfortably so.  I need some space, particularly when it's hot outside and the concert is sold out.
-Getting out of the parking lot after the concert was a mess.  There was no one directing traffic, so it took us 45 minutes to finally leave the venue.  
-Porta-potties instead of actual bathrooms, and running water sink--without soap.    Gross, especially in the summertime heat and humidity.
-High-priced snacks and beverages.  This is to be expected at a venue such as this, so it's not a huge surprise, but it did keep us from buying dinner or a beverage during the concert.
-The delicious Cafe Fontanella is closed by the time most concerts let out; given that they serve pizza and alcohol, the restaurant would make a killing if it stayed open later into the evening on concert nights.

I'd return to the Woods Amphitheater at Fontanel to see a band I love (like BNL), though I'd think twice before attending a concert just because.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: What a cool place, well worth the 1 1/2 hour wait outside. It was quaint,  food was great ,and so close to Sons n Britches, the great group performing that night!!!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I came in tonight with a group of 15 ladies; I was over charged an extra drink, when I wrote that on the check my entire party was kicked out. I was love to talk to a manager about this, so I don't have to go through my bank to clear up the misunderstood.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Having moved to the nations recently, I was really pumped about this place and have given it chance after chance.... Tonight my husband and I got the 'meatball with macaroni ' .... Meatballs seasoned with Greek seasoning (they put this is everything) and macaroni in red sauce. It was terrible and I give up on this place. We left and got White Castle. I give it two stars because it's a great atmosphere. They need to find a new chef.

name: The Stone Fox
text: I like to think that the Stone Fox is an upscale dive bar. It's an old repurposed house (like many other fine establishments in this city) and has ample seating, indoors and outdoors. The patio is a nice place to enjoy an evening drink. A rich collection of local craft ales, and regular beers, tantalize the tippler at their tiny bar. While their food selection is quite good, I was left hollow at their brunch choices. The portions were tiny, and nothing to write home about. There is a place for a live band, and dance sessions erupt periodically. The crowd that hangs out here is "different", by which I mean no suits or pretty clothes.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Brought in 2014 at this place and had one of the best nights during my visit to Nashville by far. The place was rockin' so ordering drinks was a bit of a thing, i let my much more attractive friend Marlene stand at the bar in my place to get attention first (i'd like to think it worked).

Everyone there was hella cool, very nice to me although most people are nice to you when they find out you're from New Orleans and they're all just as drunk as i am, i got an incredible amount of compliments on my attire from people left-n-right. There was one guy who liked what i had on so much he asked if it was cool for him to put on my jacket, hat and scarf and take pictures (drunken good times). 

I liked the fact that there was nice space for a dance-floor, a stage plus an outside area that was perfect for taking those much needed breaks after straight minutes of drunken boogie-ing inside. 

And whoever the DJ was there on NYE 2014 was wreckin' it! He was playing oldies but they were hella groovy and kept everybody moving! I really enjoyed the vibe of the place that night, i'll forever have those good memories to hold.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I came during the day when I had a break during a conference I was attending. It was hotter than the sun out and the bartender quickly came and asked what we wanted to drink. Since I needed a minute to look over the drink menu I said I would take a water for now. Little did I know they only had bottles and you would be charged. I've never been forced to buy bottle water in the US, only abroad so it already set me on the wrong foot. The place was cool, but I just didn't get the hype. I think the waitress/bartender was a bit rude and it just overpowered my true feeling of this place. I'm hoping to check it out again and maybe have a better experience.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Best place for live music good food and best craft beer & cocktails. Not to mention their serious collection of aged scotch/whiskeys!
When you visit head down stair for a game of pool in the parlor or a lounge cocktail in the speakeasy. Something for everyone!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
I was really excited to try out this cool new spot for Mother's Day brunch yesterday.  The place seemed hip and right up my alley food wise, with some innovative and different things on the menu.

My family were the first patrons to arrive and besides us, there was one other couple there for a good 30 minutes before anyone else showed up.  I expect great service when there are more wait staff than there are patrons.  Our waitress was nice enough, but not too quick on refilling drinks.  I sat there with an empty water for quite sometime.  I'm willing to overlook an empty water glass.  What I'm not willing to overlook is waiting 30 minutes for food in an empty restaurant and then getting served freezing cold breakfast tacos and petrified iceberg cold potatoes.

I wish I could say that was the worst of it, but that came when a kitchen staff member walked out, plunked down my food (cold) and walked off with no food served to my husband.  We sat there for 5 minutes before the waitress walked over to ask how everything was (I guess she failed to notice my husband had no food at all).  We mentioned the fact that we were missing his food and she walked back in the kitchen only to come out and inform is that the waffle machine was broken and he would have to order something else.  There was no apology (she did take it off the bill but never offered any apology).  It was unbelievable especially since the food had already been served.  He ended up ordering something else and it was fine, but the experience was already ruined. We were treated like a complete after thought.

I usually give restaurant more than one shot. But they blew it so bad here that I definitely won't be back.  It's sad because I love local, fresh, and innovative places, but the food was mediocre at best and as I said before, COLD...and the customer service was atrocious!  Happy Mother's Day to me!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Had Sunday Bluegrass Brunch at The Sutler and it did not disappoint! Awesome service staff; ours (Rachel) was incredibly friendly, attentive and kept our mimosas full. Food came out very fast and was exactly what we ordered, despite some picky vegetarian substitutions on my part. The biscuit Benedict was amazing. The bluegrass band was top notch and added to the super authentic honkey-tonk atmosphere of the place. We wished every restaurant/bar in Nashville were more like this!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
The food has been great: Tasty, seasoned well, served hot, on time. 
The food has been bad: Bland, cold, sloppy, slow.

The service has been perfect: Friendly, timely, professional.
The service has been terrible: Short, slow, forgetful, careless.

Sometimes a 5, sometimes a 1. 

Consistently inconsistent. 

Good luck, when you go.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsie's is a legend in Nashville, so you sort of have to take it for what it is. Live music, unfinished wood floors, people every-freaking-where you turn, and crappy beers. It's fine, but not my scene. Our friends in town were excited to visit, and it seemed they enjoyed singing along to the music. The many bachelorette parties and hook ups on the prowl around us also seemed to be enjoying themselves. 

I hopefully won't be back, but only because it's not my scene. If you like a dive bar and live music and don't mind insane crowds, you'll probably dig it!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: After asking around for must have a beer at during out crawl in downtown Nashville, we made it a point to go in here. Walked in, walked right out.. Not because it sucked, but because it was SUPER busy. Didn't want to become sober waiting for a drink. Haha.  They must be doing something right! Maybe next time:)

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: If it were not for the wait in the hot sun before we were let in I would give this place 5 stars.  We went on open mike night.  I loved hearing all these aspiring stars.  No stars showed up to play.  I wonder if that really happens.  But this is a must do in Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: 3 Hughes floors of great food and drinks. Some of the best musicians are always here as well

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
On the plane ride over to Nashville I sat next to a local who told me that her #1 must do for visitors was a trip to to the Bluebird Cafe. Sadly I hadn't made a reservation beforehand, so I convinced my friend to take a chance on the no reservations show on Sunday. 

The Cafe, a 90-seat music club that opened in the early eighties, is famous for intimate, acoustic shows. Some performers are established singer/songwriters, and others perform hit songs written by other artists. We arrived about 45 minutes early for the show to a SUPER long line, but luckily we made it inside right before the cutoff (seriously -- we were numbers 88 and 89)!! There is no cover but there is a $7 food and drink minimum per person. I ordered a few beers. The food that I saw and tasted was nothing special. I'd eat beforehand and stick to drinks.

The space really was intimate and people were nearly sitting on top of each other. Groups were sharing tables and some people were seated up against the walls. We were just a few rows back from the band, Two Story Road, a husband-wife duo with some amazing credentials. They played a mixture of covers and original songs and were pretty incredible.

The shows are only an hour at The Bluebird, but it is for sure worth the wait. If you are going to Nashville I would see if there's a show you can buy tickets for ahead of time (I think they release them 1 week in advance and they sell out almost immediately). Otherwise, get there about an hour before and be prepared to wait for a great show!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Thanks be to the chef/s at Woolworths. The chicken was skinny and tasty. My spouse had the pork chops. Truly great food. The price was what I expected, but the quality service and great food will make this a great date night for the Ryman. The history of the building was enough to fill my heart. I only have two thumbs to hold up. Bravo.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
I have found my new neighborhood bar! The Stone Fox! 

I have been hearing a lot of great things about The Fox over the past months, but have never made it in. All I can say is that I shouldn't have put it off for so long. 

What I like about it so much are the two patios. One in the front and a larger one out back. Great for these nice Spring/Summer days. The smoking policy on the porches can leave you gagging while eating dinner, this knocks my rating down at least half a star. You shouldn't be able to smoke where other non-smokers are eating. Just saying. 

For a place I consider mainly a bar, their food menu is solid. They also have a few vegetarian options that are quite good. I chose to skip it dessert, but it sounded damn good. Maybe next time. Their draught beer selection is...alright. About 10 rotating taps, but not nearly as beefy as it could be. Though I am never disappointed in the limited selection. 

Also, check out their music calendar. Tons of live music almost every night. 

Solid neighborhood pub. I cant wait to get to know you better Fox!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
What's NOT to like about the Bluebird Cafe? Other than the fact that purchasing tickets is akin to an Olympic event where time is of the essence, which I didn't deduct stars for, it's a fantastic listening room with a calendar of A+ performers. As mentioned, it's a listening room, and the audience respects the performer/s (who they are in close proximity to considering the limited space) by not talking when the performance begins.

P.S. Try the coconut cake. You'll thank me later.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
$5.50 for yuengling?  Big deal, I'm on vacation!  Stick a few bucks into your pocket for the restroom attendant (and I love this), very European and keeps things nice and tidy!  Absolutely LOVED the music, the crowd and was everything (and more) than I expected.

The crowd danced, sang and had a ball!  I do love a crowded venue!   DH had a great time and he's not a country music fan!  Cannot wait to return!

name: Tin Roof
text: My favorite bar in Nashville. There's always something going on, happy hour is everyday from 2-7 and has really cheap beer! Also if you get a chance, the cheese fries are amazing!!!!! I'm obsessed. Only complaint is have of this place is that they run out of their draft selections quite often but for the price, you can't beat it!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: It's worth the wait to hang out on the first floor with the live music! Get the fried string beans!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Love the rooftop- been here multiple times. But this last time was a little different... We had a friend in from our home town. And when the boys bought their drinks the waitresses gave a stink about no tip, loudly to each other, then up front to our friends. I'll tell you- it was a Tuesday afternoon- girls? With that attitude? That's why you got no tip, and that a why you work the weekday shift. So don't come to my out of town friends for money when you chose bartending as your current profession. Thanks for the first impression. Good day.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Gourmet food with a come add you are ambiance! ! However,  I would recommend to tell them to go easy on the salt! ! Awesome and unique menu! !!!!!! Delicious !! Highly recommend the trout! ! However tell them to go easy on the salt,  all of my friends loved it,  but it was a bit salty,  other than that,  great atmosphere! !!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
My friends and I were SO happy to get lucky enough to snag tickets online for a Sunday songwriters night here! It's quite the online process and kind of luck of the draw to get tickets, so we were pumped.

The place is very tiny inside which I wasn't expecting to be AS small as it was, but the tables are laid out with enough room to get by. We were seated at table 1 which was a 6 person high top and not the most comfortable, BUT - we had a great view of the stage.

Service here was phenomenal. Even though it's a listening room and you have to be super quiet, the servers did a great job of staying on top of if you need anything while still respecting the singers on stage.

Food is sub-par, but I kind of expected that. I would recommend grabbing dinner somewhere else beforehand and just ordering a drink or two to meet the $10 minimum required on a Sunday night show. I got the chicken tenders with fries and they were just...meh. My friend got the quesadilla which didn't look too great either. Other friends got a salad, and it was just nothing exciting.

The experience was great and the songwriters night lasted pretty late - it was about 8pm-11pm. 8 songwriters playing 3 songs each plus a special guest at the end. They start on time and move through without breaks, but expect to be here for a while!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Good place to bring guests from out of town. There is live music, a bunch of cowboy boots nailed/glued to the wall, decent cocktails and bunch of southern style foods. They recently started brunch which is pretty good - the biscuits are the best part. The main meals are OK but if you focus on the drinks and the music they'll make you feel good. The downstairs lounge is hip and full of  post grad people, mostly normcore not super hip but people that are cool to be around.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We were not impressed with this spot as we were "honky tonk" hopping down Broadway. The band was mediocre and constantly asked for tip money. Let your music do the talking! Also, the drink prices were much higher than other locations. 12 bucks for two miller lites!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
A very casual spot.  So casual no one is in a rush, not even the service.  I think our server was related to Phoebe, from Friends.  "Do you know what you want to drink?" 
"No, do you have a drink menu?" Booze arrives 15 minutes later.  I'm sitting 5 feet from the bar. 
"Do you know what you want to order?"
"No, do you have a food menu?"...Oops, again!  Brunch was very good.  Get the deep fried French toast!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Waited 2 1/2 hours to get into the cafe - such an amazing atmosphere. I have been dying to visit this place ever since the show Nashville came out. The staff was fun, and the open mic night was very entertaining. I think we saw a few stars in the making!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsie's is the most notable of the bars on Music Row. That shouldn't mean overcharging for beer. 2 beers coming to $14.00??? I expect that in high priced city bars. Not on Honky Tonk row in Nashville. Other than the drink prices, the music was great, as was the atmosphere. Unfortunately, we went elsewhere after 1 drink. Drank for cheaper elsewhere and heard great music elsewhere also.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I go to Nashville a lot !  The only reason we go to Tootsie's is to get the VIP booth with the one of the most fun and amazing  bartenders! Angel makes our whole crew feel like family! We never have to wait for drink and she's constantly making us laugh with her amazing personality.!! I would highly recommend going there just to see angel!! Thanks Tootsie's for making our Nashville experience that much better !!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: First time to the bluebird.  We went on a Tuesday night and got there very early and stood in line. It was a rainy night so we got in easily and sat in the pews.  We ordered drinks and some food to eat before the show began. The fish was hot and   very good, I can also recommend the nachos and the blt sandwich. We heard four writers / singers who was all very talented.  We enjoyed it so much, we came back for music in the round the next night and again stood in the line. This time we waited a bit longer but we were seated at a table, next to the performers. We were so close I could have shared our nachos.  Again it was some great music from some young artist.  Recommend highly.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I'm giving this place 3stars because the food wasn't too good, I ordered catfish and red beans and rice the fish was fried too hard,the beans and rice was dry ..the staff was friendly even though when the waitress asked me how was the food I told her and she didn't try to make it right, I will not return here again

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Enjoyed our server Jordan! Friendly and happy! I am notoriously indecisive so I love asking servers what they like from the menu. Her recommendations were very delicious! Enjoyed the overall feel of this restaurant. I always have friends asking me where they should go when they come to Nashville so this will definitely be on the list of recommendations!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Service was very friendly and kind. Food was horrible and we found a piece of plastic in the salad. Will not be returning.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Good breakfast spot but make sure to come early. The place gets packed very quick so if it's a big party try to be there when the restaurant opens. The food was good but a little cold by the time it came out. Overall it's a great place to have brunch!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Time of visit approximately 11:30 PM
Date of visit 1-26-2019 

Where is the fire marshal in Nashville Tennessee?? 

 This place is out of control. They have no standards to the number of people they allow to come inside. 
On vacation and we visit this place, there were so many people in the downstairs of this place where the band was playing it was dangerously out of control. As my girlfriend and I stood in one spot for over 15 minutes getting pushed and shoved we felt completely helpless as we were yelling for help begging for someone to help us get out of this place. I kept pointing at the female bartender asking for help and they laughed and thought it was funny. Both she and I lowered our heads and shoved our way to the front door as we were getting hit by people and pushed we finally made it to the front door. I tried to speak to the man working the door that was an older gentleman. And he stopped letting people in momentarily but he was then told by someone to start letting them in again. We left this place and I told extremely large security guy working the door that led to the upstairs of this place that what they were doing was against the law and they are not allowed to do this due to various fire codes they are breaking. I told him this was not safe for anyone in this establishment and that I would be reporting this. He then asked me if I owned this building, I told him no. He then put his hands out and said arrest me then. 
 This is a message for the fire marshal of Nashville Tennessee you should get a hold of what's going on in this establishment it's out of control and someone is going to get hurt very seriously. This is unsafe, dangerous end it is only a matter of time before someone gets seriously injured or worse. 
 For the last time let's not forget this is against the law! 
I will never visit this place again. Pathetic is biz Int excellent description of this establishment. Unprofessionalism from the employees is an understatement.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Definitely would not recommend the food here we order a cheese burger and fries and dip trio which was a joke the dips were blah the salsa tasted like paste picante and the guacamole had no flavor the fries that came with the cheese burger were salted to death so I guess this place isn't famous for the food waste of money .

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: We are very happy with our food and service by John. It's New Years Eve and there is w special menu. We chose the garden greens and Filet  mignon. Everything done to perfection. Dancing and drinking were downstairs in a large hall. Great music provided (big band). Lots of happy people, surprisingly many young people and some terrific dancers. The bartenders were on the job. Drinks flowed real quick across the bar. The only criticism of the night was too few chairs for attendees. Lightning valet as well. Good job Chris.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Since we heard this spot is the main spot to hang out on Broadway, we of course decided to make it our first stop on a night out. From the minute we walked in, we were instantly uncomfortable. This place is packed to absolutely capacity and it's nuts to even move around here. The front entrance was so clogged with people waiting to hear the show down there, you literally had to shove your way to get to another floor. Once on the second floor, it was just marginally less packed but we were able to get a bar spot.

The best part of this place is how helpful the bartenders are, as they actually wave you down and ask if you need anything. Usually this is the opposite so its pretty surprising they were able to keep on top of that. There's a cop standing around eyeing everyone down and even though I'm over 21 the guy made me feel like we were doing something wrong. The band playing on the second floor was mediocre at best- I am not a voice coach or anything, but the guy was off key. I think the main attraction was on the first floor but there was no way we were able to squeeze in there.

Prices are OK but this place is just too freaking busy at night.

name: Tin Roof
text: The fries are great but I'm not so sure how I feel about  the chicken tenders having purple everywhere

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Bluegrass brunch... 10 out of 10, would recommend!! $17 bottomless mimosas is definitely a bang for your buck. Our waitress was Virginia and she was amazing! We'll definitely be back to see her!:)

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Horrible service!!! Don't come here. People are so rude. We are from California and people are so much nicer on the west side

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
I don't know what it was that turned this rabid former country-music-despising woman around.  Was it the incredible hospitality I encountered everywhere I visited in Nashville?  Was it the land of "no cover charge with talented musicians"?  I don't know but Tootsie's gets some of the credit.

I visited on a business trip in Nov, 2014 and it was their anniversary.  What a night to pick.  Kid Rock stopped by to play in the wee hours.

Returned home to Denver, looking forward to a return trip with my country-music-loving husband.

We visited a few times on our trip last week.  There's no mystery as to their popularity.  Three floors of live music at all hours of the day and night and no cover charge.  We paid $6 + tip for a bottle of beer and you tip the bands. The three times I've visited, I've heard country, rock and pop...all covers and all a fun crowd.

When we left at 9P on a Friday night, there was a long line waiting to get in.  We arrived at 7 or so and it was just starting to get busy.  By 8, it was packed.

name: Tin Roof
text: Had a mixup with our cocktails being poured from a bottle of pure water that had been used to train new bartenders on....

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text: HORRIBLE ACCESS.  60 minute line to get into parking lot.   Inept parking assistance and piss poor logistics.  Getting out was just as AWEFUL!   Spent more time in car lines than at the Boston concert.   Shame on the Fontanel.     Won't come back.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: First time to Tootsie's and it could not have been any better! We stayed on the first floor and Kassidy was beyond amazing, so kind, and an absolute rockstar of a bartender! Thank you! Also met sara and angel as well. All three girls were super cute and so friendly! Thanks girls for a great time!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Look, the Stone Fox is great. We eat here every week. Everything on the menu is tasty, the specials are always good, and the drinks are well-done and well-priced. I've never been to a show here, but it's one of the best bars and restaurants on the west side.

Update: it's a pretty good venue.

name: Tin Roof
text: I've been coming to this Tin Roof for a while and loved it, was happy when they renovated. The last 4 times I've been there, someone on the DJ side has tried to fight me or shoved me. I'm military and can't respond because an arrest would mean the end of my career that I've worked very hard for. Each time I've been an adult and asked the individual to stop. Typically I get a response like "get out of my face." I then proceed to tell the bouncer, who goes and tells the guy or girl to "stop." You can imagine how effective that is. Tonight it happened for the last time. I talked to the manager and told him, Morgan, who was very nice and understanding, that I couldn't come back for fear of an altercation leading to the loss of my job. He told me he gets it, he's sorry, several bars have closed that have led to a "rougher" crowd at Tin Roof. I get it, but to summarize this review: if you go here, it's fun, the bartenders are mostly great, but the clientele lately has been troublesome and you will run the risk of fighting someone. It's sad because I want to come back, but my friends and I won't be anymore. There must be consequences to being an aggressor...currently at Tin Roof Demonbreun, there are not.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsies is not fancy but it is fun.  Where country music is at the heart of Nashville.   No better place to feel the soul and history of country music other than the original Ryman.   Friendly atmosphere and if you are fortunate enough to be able to rent the vip area behind the band you just might get to meet  some big names in the Nashville music industry.   I had the opportunity to meet Rhonda Forlaw Adkins and she was kind enough to invite us to continue to share the space when our time slot was over and hers had begun.  For my visits to Nashville I may visit other establishments but Tootsies will always be my favorite.

If you are into old country and the history of country music this is the place to be.  There may have been Murder on Music Row, but not at Tootsies Orchid Lounge.   Been there. Done that.  Bought the T shirt and I will be going back.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Well I thought i was too old for places like this but... apparently I am not. It's like a 3 floor bar with music on each floor plus big crowds and a lot of sloppy stuff going on. But that's sort of what the broadway area seems like on the weekends in general and you could do worse than Tootsie's where the bartenders seem to be able to hear over the din at near superhuman levels. Truly baffling.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Not too touristy. Lil dive bar with live music. Comfy. I liked it here because everyone is welcome and you can walk in in a t-shirt and shorts. Very comfortable.

name: Tin Roof
text: Went in at 10pm on a Monday night. No smile/greeting from bartender. He started by stating they had $2 Tecate and $5 margaritas. Had to pry information out of him. He was not listening to me as I ordered, so no surprise he messed up a 3 drink order. Acted as if he was doing me a favor by allowing me to order and bring back a pizza from a few doors down when his establishment had no food offerings at that hour. In just over an hour of sitting at the bar neither bartender bothered to check on us. Music was good, and we liked the decor.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Their BlueGrass Brunch is awesome! Live music during brunch along with bottomless mimosa's...so you can't go wrong. Virginia was wonderful. She was so attentive and made sure our brunch was not only delicious, but served with a smile. This is a must brunch spot in Nashville...but it wouldn't be complete unless you have Virginia as your server.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I've tried to eat at The Sutler twice in 3 months. The first time they were closed for a private party. Today upon entering we were told they weren't serving from 3pm to 5pm. I wish they would put this information on their website. It's 42 degrees and Christmas time! I'm
Not happy & they won't get a 3rd try from me!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: We did the hop on hop off trolley and they mentioned Woolworth which was a fun touch! I made the reservation early on Open Table for dinner on a Friday, but there seemed to be plenty of open tables. Food is pretty big portions, my parents were able to split the Caesar salad and chicken and it was tons of food for them- always good! We all got burgers which were pretty good- I love bread and the bun was really nice and fluffy. We had the Brussels sprouts, fries, and mashed potatoes sides- all good! The fries are the thin kind that look like steak and shake fries! We also got the bread pudding to split between the 5 of us and it was AMAZING! Made with biscuits- it was devoured:) The screen in the background and music definitely add to the experience as well.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
This was a cool unique spot blocks away from Broadway street. It was quite empty on this Friday night and the ambiance is very casual and diner-esque, but our group of girls were ready for a night out. There's a cool projector area where they old time music videos too, so that was fun to look at. 

We ordered some brussel sprouts to start, which were not the best in my opinion. The sauce was tasty though, but the crispiness of the sprouts could have had some improvement. I also ordered the crispy pork belly and fried chicken salad. I didn't realize how big these portions were, so I definitely didn't need both. The crispy pork belly was delicious though! I wasn't a fan of the watermelon and large amounts of cheese in the rest of the dish, however. The fried chicken salad was also huge with lots of fruit in it- I wish I noticed this when ordering because I don't like fruit in my salads. The chicken was very dry and had to be doused in hot sauce and ranch. I had a good amount of my friend's rib dish, and this was delicious. The sweet potato fries were soft and addicting, and the cole slaw was also a tasty addition to the tender ribs. 

Overall, the food was a hit or miss, but very heavy and filling nonetheless. You definitely get your money's worth in portions! Service was quick and great as well for our large group.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: So first I suggest arriving before 10AM, if not prepare for a wait. My group and I got her at 10:10 and it was already an hour wait. Good thing that they moved rather quickly so we weren't waiting for an hour. Their.sangria pitchers are at a great price but depending on who makes them depends on how strong it actually is. You can get a good 3 cups out of it. Their bottomless mimosas aren't bad, just make sure you keep the receipt. The food tasted great but was a little cold. Not sure if it was because of it being busy or if that's a regular thing. The biscuits and gravy are good enough to share if you're not too hungry. The live music adds a great element to the environment. It's not overly loud but keeps it entertaining, really gives it a great southern vibe. The waitress was a little rude but everyone else was pretty nice. I definitely recommend just make sure to tell them you want you're food hot.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great live music and service! A Nashville must see!!! Cold beer!!!!!!!! True dive bar.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I came here for brunch this past weekend and we had a great time. We were originally quoted a 25 minute wait time but we ended up waiting a little over an hour. We didn't mind because we're pretty understanding that if people don't leave then you can't sit new tables. Plus the $17 bottomless mimosas helped speed that wait up. The food was pretty good. They had great southern options for brunch. The chicken fried chicken biscuits were decent. The white gravy is a little flavorless. The Benedict and chicken and waffles were delicious! 

I for sure recommend this place. The $17 bottomless mimosas and great brunch options make it a nice choice. Be prepared to wait on weekends though.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I ate at The Sutler a few months ago. The atmosphere is great, the food is good, the music is awesome, and the drinks are yummy. My boyfriend and I were extremely turned off by the hostesses though. There were 3 of them at the front, yet it took a while for them to service us, and then they had poor attitudes. We felt unwelcome but still gave it a try. 

Today, we returned to try to have some lunch and drinks. When we came in, again there were 3 employees at the front. It took a bit to get their attention, and this time, the one who I was speaking with turned to her coworker to talk to her while I was asking about the wait. They were complaining about either a guest or another coworker. I was shocked that this happened, and we turned around and left. We enjoyed much better service at ML Rose down the street. 

The hosts and hostesses are the face of the restaurant. There are too many up there for this to be a regular occurrence; they should be friendly, welcoming, and helpful.

We live a 5 min walk from The Sutler and would love to have this be a go-to place, but the service at the front is so awful that we likely won't be trying again unless something changes.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Not too touristy. Lil dive bar with live music. Comfy. I liked it here because everyone is welcome and you can walk in in a t-shirt and shorts. Very comfortable. It is really humbling learning how many famous people got their start here. Ie: Patsy Cline

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Tim and Sarah made our night!!! Loved their midwestern hospitality especially from some northerner gals! In town for #cmas and enjoyd chix tenders and leinies summer shandy!!! Find us on insta feed!! -#sarahandannietakenashville

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I'm extremely saddened about this review. This restaurant turned had become a part of my top 5 places to eat for to the food and the history. Tonight, that changed. To my knowledge, a lot had changed since my last appearance which was in October. The menu changed. The MENU CHANGED. How and why, Sway?! They no longer sell their rich and flavorful gumbo. The small basket of biscuits/cornbread/ho cakes are gone. Even the peach cobbler was taken away. The Mac and cheese is no longer a side! Which is foolishness bc how on ear are you a southern restaurant. The fried chicken isn't even what it used to be. It's more "crunchy", which typically is a good thing for me but something wasn't right with it. They decided to add "Nashville hot chicken" flavor which is not something I thought they should have added. I originally order the friend chicken but couldn't even enjoy it so I went with the short rib roast. It was pretty decent. Tender but not much to go with it. Barely any mashed potatoes or green beans. According to the waitress, the menu was changed to alleviate some costly meals which I find to be false due to the chicken plate being the same price as before ~$16 and the short rib which by the way was a small plate around ~$16. I'm really disappointed that they changed things up. It's barely a year old and boom change menus. I don't think I'll be back. All that history.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsie's was recommended by many friends, so I felt the need to check it out while visiting Broadway. Found seats at the bar and was quickly welcomed by the bartenders. The band that was playing was WONDERFUL (featured a full group with a killer fiddle player). I don't mind spending money on a good time, but the drinks were VERY expensive, even for the area ($9 for a TINY shot of moonshine, and I believe $8-9 for a Coors Light). Be sure to check it out, but watch how quickly you order your drinks!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Love this place!! The vibes are excellent, it has interesting decor and cool live music in the evenings. The drinks are really affordable and happy hour here is ALWAYS full so expect to take some time finding parking. Pro-tip: their fries are the best in town.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Have been here twice now. Great food! Good prices. The first time here had a waitress that was rude and always seemed " bothered" when asking her for items. I believe her name was Virginia?  Then came back and had wonderful service. By one of the sisters.Her name was Brianna I'm pretty sure.  I think her and a twin work together. 100% a great place to eat and have a wonderful honky tonk time.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place was very fun. Multi level bar with live entertainment on every level. Fair drink prices and pours. We enjoyed this place. The bartender had a Rangers cup behind the bar. Yeah!! Let's go rangers!!

name: Tin Roof
text:
Lost my credit card, still charged me for my entire tab.  I gave up after several attempts to get redress from management and staff.

Was towards the bottom of my list even when I was still a howling wildebeest of a Vandy grad student.  It's a bit like Fireball.  Terrible even when you were in college... now even less appealing.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Good drinks. You climb a ton of stairs to get to the lounge. Half way up the stairs you will find the bathroom which was surprisingly clean. Upstairs there is nice live music. The band was ok. There is a nice outdoor patio. It was quite cold that evening but no one turned on the heaters so I saw folks start turning them on themselves. Drinks were just ok. Would recommend if you are into country music and just want a place to grab a beer

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: 3 floors of quality live music and frosty cold beers. This is what I was expecting from Nashville and Tootsie's delivered fully.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Second floor is a real fun time. The Andy Gibbons band plays all your favorite country songs and they are a so personable. Nice band to chat with in between sets.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Sure, the place has history, but if you're really want to hear good current country western writers and singers visit the listening Cafe. Good food plenty of seating excellent prices great bar service and you're sitting right next to Nashville's next big stars

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The world famous Tootsie's was packed on a Tuesday night. The band was okay on the second floor. The beer was cold and quick to be handed out. Another spot to see when you are in Nashvil

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: One of the coolest place I've ever been in my 66 years! Don't pass on the opportunity to go to this truly historic venue!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The bartender complete left the vodka out my vodka tonic. She was fun to look at but don't expect  any alcohol in your mixed drink if ordered after 10:00 pm. I recommend sticking to beer at Tootsie's

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Absolutely a must visit if you're in Nashville. We sat at the bar, and Martha was great. We had the nachos, cupcake wine, Corona, and another drink and it totalled to be around $50ish dollars, which isn't bad.  You are sat very close to other people, but everyone is so polite.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We went here to eat on Saturday June 9th at 11:30 am and got seated right away. The restaurant wasn't very busy at all. So didn't think there would be a problem getting waited on. But I was wrong we set down at the table and was looking at our menus and another couple got seated and waited on right away. Then they got their drinks and still nobody waited on us. Plus their waiter walked right by us 4 times and made eye contact with me but nobody ever waited on us. So after 20 to 25 minutes we got up and left. I told the waitress setting there doing nothing as we walked out she lost our business because nobody waited on us. Mind you our menus where still open on the table and we left them there as we left and I told the hostess as we left that we never got waited on and you lost my business. She acted surprised but as we set at our table waiting to get waited on she walked by us 2 times.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
I really want to love this place because it is so popular, but I think that is my problem with it.  We had a hard time finding a space where we could really go to just enjoy the band.  I love Nashville for the country music.  The night we were there, the band downstairs was playing a lot of rock n' roll, but upstairs was my problem, the band was playing backstreet boys.  I know the musicians get tipped to play songs, but the terrible music continued, which I hated, because both bands were excellent.  
Our bartenders were great, very attentive and friendly.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
I had an absolute BLAST in this outstanding Broadway club during a recent visit to Nashville. The Amanda Daughtry Band kept our group rocking until the early hours with covers that ranged from Garth Brooks to Queen -- and the country band playing the main stage wasn't bad, either. 

The third floor bar may seem like a long walk up, but the open-air patio, great music and spacious dance floor makes it worth the exercise. The beers were a little pricey, and the selection fairly weak, but with music this good, who cares? Hard to imagine a better place in Music City to rock out to great tunes.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I chose this hotel because it was the cheapest on Expedia without being super sketchy. It was definitely a good choice! About 15 minutes from downtown, it's easy to uber or take their shuttle. The shuttle is actually run by a third party so you do need to call the front desk to arrange pick up. It comes to the hotel on the top of the hour and it costs $10 round trip per person or you can pay $15 per person and have unlimited for the day. 

The room was super nice, plush pillows and beds, plenty of space. We had a room with a balcony over looking the pool which was nice. We tried to go down to the pool one night because we thought there was a jacuzzi, but it turns out the small circular pool is actually a children's pool, not a hot tub. They may have a hot tub at their indoor pool, but we didn't go looking for it.

I ordered room service my first night in the hotel. I ordered the chicken piccata and a glass of Riesling. They said it would take 45 minutes or so, but it actually came in about 20 which I was pleased about. It was arranged nicely and came with everything I needed, including a glass of ice water. There is a $7 room service fee FYI that is not annotated on the menu. The chicken was a little salty and not the best I've ever had, but it was decent for room service.

Check in was super easy when I arrived and there's plenty of free parking. This hotel is a great place to stay when you're visiting Nashville!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Stayed here for my recent training in Nashville. My room was closer to the pool elevators, which took some finding. It's a large square, so the more expensive room have balconies or patios facing the courtyard, the less expensive have balconies facing parking lots. Still a decent view. The outdoor pool is open until 9, and there's a nice gazebo and plenty of outdoor seating around. Beautiful. the bar serves food late if you miss the restaurant closing. If you are a Sheraton member you get access to the club on floor 2 for a free breakfast, otherwise, you'll be spending $17 in the restaurant. OUCH. 

My coworkers and I had the privilege of meeting Sarah in sales, who was hosting an appetizer and drinks thing in the lobby. It was awesome, and Sarah is the best around. I would definitely recommend her for your business or private function needs. She recommended all the great places we went while in town, and more that we didn't get to. She's a gem. 

My room was clean, but the maids didn't come the second and third days-weird. clean sheets, fluffy towels, I was happy. Bathroom was spacious, more than enough hangers for my work clothes. The iron worked- a major plus- and my balcony had two chairs and a table for my outdoor needs. 

The shuttle driver was AMAZING. He liked playing trivia with us, and made sure we were to work and to the airport on time. He was a wealth of information and made our stay complete. 

I can't wait to come back. Wi-Fi is free in the lobby, paid in your room unless you are a club member-then it's included.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Hard Rock Cafe Nashville has the best veggie burger in town. Add grilled onions and pepper jack and it's on!

name: The Valentine
text: Stop by last night after hearing how nice the place was and was not disappointed. The staff was super nice and attentive to us. Love the chandelier, tables, bar tops  as they all seem to be a good balance in the room!! The whole place seemed way to nice for Broadway but I'm not complaining. Finally a place to listen to music without stepping in who knows what. Wish the best for them, me and my girls will return this weekend!!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Typical.  If you want the typical Hard Rock chain and to get away from Nashville, stop in here.  You won't even remember you are in the Music Capital.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Ah yes, the hotel in which we stayed during our trip to Nashville. It got the job done, but we were left pretty disappointed by our stay. 

It's worth saying first, that this hotel is super pretty. There's a pool and a courtyard that's just lovely, and the lobby is very elegantly decorated. 

Our room was nice too, for the most part. It was clean when we got in, the bed was soft. There wasn't a fridge, which was a bit of a surprise since that's a pretty standard thing, but it wasn't a huge deal.

The issues at this location had to do with the service. It started out with television problems. None of the channels had any volume. Irritating, but alright. Naturally, we called. The person who picked up the phone seemed bothered by the fact that we'd called the desk.... When that is their job? Not quite sure why talking to us was such a big inconvenience. Anyway, they sent someone up to fix it eventually. The volume worked, but then we didn't have any local Nashville channels. Kind of annoying when it's storming and we're trying to make plans, but can't get any weather forecasts or alerts. 

Then, we didn't have a welcome book. You know the one. The one that comes in every hotel room, that tells you about the hotel, what services are available, places to eat nearby, etc. There wasn't one. No big deal. So again, we call the annoyed desk. They were ridiculously condescending and tried to tell us it was on the desk, like I was not in my room staring at the desk as we spoke. I mean, it's a hotel room. It's only so big. And my stuff is all in a suitcase. It's not like it's a quest for the lost ark to search for a damn book. Eventually, the guy on the phone fluffed us off and said "if another book turns up, they'll send it over", because apparently there's a welcome book shortage in Tennessee. We left a note for the maid to ask for one, and like magic, one was on our desk when we came back the next day. 

So much for Southern hospitality, eh?

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Absolutely terrible. Food is gross. Watch for huge spider webs on the ceiling. The food took over an hour.  If we knew there was one hr wait for food, we would not have stayed. The manager stated our food was only in the system for 26 minutes.  There was no solution just bad food.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: One of my favorite Nashville bars!  Great bands and no cover.  Bathrooms are clean too.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Not the service I expect from a sheraton.  Check in was smooth, room was decent,  nothing spectacular.  No fridge.  When we got there we had some issues with the tv, no volume on most channels.  After a conversation with am obviously annoyed front desk clerk they sent someone to the room who then fixed the volume but managed to make all local channels disappear.  Normally not a big deal but as it was a stormy weekend full of weather warnings would've been nice to know about them.  There was no property guide in our room, you know the one with amenities, room service menu,  local attractions, etc.   The same inhospitable front desk clerk told me I must not see it and insisted it was on the desk.  It was not.  He pacified me and did said he'd look around for another one and send it to the room. That did not happen.  Though a note for housekeeping on the first night accompanied by cash and the guide appeared.  All in all pretty property,super comfy beds,    just be advised the staff could use a refresher course in guest services and hospitality.  When I return to the area I'll try the other sheraton in Nashville before trying my luck with this one again.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Front desk staff at Check-In (August 3, around 2:30pm) did not smile, I don't even think they gave us a greeting. Even though we were SPG members and booked directly and VERY early in the year, we were given a ground floor, handicapped room, and no, we couldn't change it. When I told the lady I had a tax-exempt form so I could have federal taxes removed, she said, "it's already been charged to your card". Luckily the manager overheard her and said he could take care of it. But no smile or greeting from him, and he made it seem like a chore. The hotel is EXTREMELY outdated, and has a stale smell throughout (think of the hotel from "The Shining"). The room was very outdated except for the TV, which is newer and big. The only staff who was nice was the bellman. If you passed any staff in the hallway, they did not smile or say hello to you. The toiletries are extremely cheap and no good. Luckily, we brought shampoo and conditioner from the Marriott and used those. The food at the Old Hickory Grill was outrageously priced and had no taste whatsoever. The quality of it was the same as the free breakfast buffet at a Choice hotel. I was waiting to be seated for a good 5 minutes on the last day of my stay, and NO ONE would help me. A server went past me THREE times, completely ignoring me. I will NEVER stay here when I visit Nashville again. Please don't think I'm a negative person. I have NEVER written a bad review for a Marriott hotel, but unfortunately the conference I was attending was held here. Please take a cue from Marriott and do everything they do. In fact, I just stayed at a JW Marriott the week before, and you all charged the exact same room price. This is utterly outrageous.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: This is a very comfortable bar for dancing or just kicking back with a brew. We caught a bit of two sets and found it to be an energetic space. The servers are very attentive and the decor is pretty funny to see.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
This place is the ideal stop along Broadway!
There is no cover so that in itself makes it to the top of my list!

The bands are always great and the drinks are fairly well priced and always taste wonderful.

The bartenders are quick and friendly.

The bathrooms are clean.

I am not sure what else you could ever want from a Broadway bar, but this is about as awesome as it gets!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
This is a smaller and more laid-back bar on the Broadway strip. It has pretty unique touches to the inside like mason jar chandeliers. I have to say that this place is unusually clean, compared to all of the other bars on Broadway. As like much of Broadway there is live music playing all day. 

It's a really narrow and long space so it's really easy to start a dialogue with the performers, which is cool. Seating-wise, the bar is looooooong, and there are several tables that can accommodate four people each. 

The bar's specialty are moonshine drinks. Not really my cup of tea, but they do have several different flavors that you can choose from. 

This is a great place to sit and relax for a few hours with a group of friends.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Great spot for drinks and great music!  Ambiance was rustic and the bartender was nice.  Merch was overly priced, $22 for a low quality trucker hat ...did I mention great drinks though?!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Stayed here for 2 nights on a marriage retreat. The food was absolutely terrible! Everything was stale, dry or just completely lacking flavor! Most of the rooms don't even have a mini fridge. The only good thing I have to say about this place is that the beds are comfortable and the rooms seem relatively clean.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Got the brisket which was very good but the fries were cold and not good. When the check came lots of extra charges were added. Even after review, when the check came back again there was still extra drink charges. Waiter did not want to fix the bill. I wonder if he gets extra money by adjusting checks after customers pay. Looking back I regret leaving him a very good tip and wish I would have contacted the manager in case he had a thief working for him.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Went to Motown Monday but all we heard was swing, which was a total let down. Also bartender was a complete weirdo, refusing to serve me a club soda along with my bourbon on the rocks. Waste of a $5 cover charge.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The main reason I gave this hotel 2 stars is because it claims to be a 4 star hotel but it's more of a 2 1/2, 3. The room we stayed at was very old not updated at all the wallpaper was peeling off in places. The shampoo, conditioner and soaps were all Sheraton's generic brand. The sheets and comforter were also very old. The only good thing about this room was the location which was near an exit and our patio led right to the pool. No fridge or microwave. Also we had booked a 2 bed bedroom and they gave us one with a king size bed which we had to make work. Very disappointed, next time we will stick with the Hyatt hotels.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
It was my first time ever going to a Hard rock cafe even though there was one in Memphis but never bothered to go. This hard rock cafe is located downtown and it's very lively. Going in the restaurant, music of original Nashville roots are played and its quiet unforgettable. 
I ordered a grilled salmon from the menu and our food took a while to come out but I have to say...that that was the best salmon I've ever eaten and to this day, I still want to make another trip just for the salmon.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Sweet bar with a great covered outside area. Reasonable door cover, drink prices and GREAT music most nights of the week.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Stayed here last night. Nice hotel. Check in easy. Friendly staff. Good location. The problem with this place is the people that stay here on weekends. If you are trying to get some rest ...,forget about it. Drunks, parties, loud people at all hours of the night make me not want to go to Nashville on the  weekend again. Not much security presence.  People making a lot of noise down by the pool also way after closing time. Rooms are clean and nice and they are pet friendly.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Very sub-par. We went for Sunday brunch and it took about 20 minutes for us to get seated and over an hour for us to even get drinks. The place wasn't even crowded, there were only 4 other tables full. The band was okay but the server was very nice but very slow. My friend got a drink from the bar but they ran out of orange juice so the cup was only filled half way, but they still charged him full price. We were told after we got our food that they ran out of fruit for one of the orders but then a half hour later the server came out with a mini cup with a few sliced strawberries for us. The food wasn't very good and was way over priced for how much we got. The only reason I am giving it 2 stars is because the roof top view was pretty nice. You can see the river on the left and the rest of Broadway on the right. Unfortunately we won't be going back.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We had fajitas and burgers that were very good we had a great server Braz. He actually got on stage and sang with the musician that was playing.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I like to go to the hard Rock Cafe in different cities to see the differences in decor and memorabilia. I just like the vibe of the place. There was a live singer when I was there--it is in Nashville after all. I had the Guinness bacon cheeseburger--it was really good. It had a sweet sauce that I enjoyed. Server was very nice.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Came here with a large party and they were accommodating. Everyone ordered different type of mixed fruity drinks that they offer that were all extremely good (try the pineapple or strawberry mojito). The food was extremely good.
