Had the tres fajitas that came with chicken, steak and shrimp. Next time would stick with the chicken and shrimp which were both very flavorful. The steak was a bit tough. They were accommodating to my allergy and gladly offered corn shells in place of flour shells. Service was great and for our waitress to handle a party of 11 plus 3 other tables at the same time, she did a great job. Would definitely return and if you are coming with a large party would recommend a reservation to cut down on wait times on busy days!

name: The Valentine
text: Like the decor and the long L-shaped bar.  Did not go upstairs, but the seating and view of the band looked to be good from up there as well.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text:
Really good onion rings.  
Everything else was a bust. 
Dry meat is a bummer and Sutter Home wine. Really guys?

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I love the stage for the live music but after being told by a bouncer that they "didn't need any more business" I don't think I will return. Rude and disrespectful thing to say to people waiting in line to just get inside your bar in 30 degree weather. I won't be taking out of towners here anymore.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: This hotel was terrible.  We stayed two nights as part of a group staying for a hockey tournament.  For starters, it took a full week and a half to get a hold of the person in charge of booking the room for us through our group.  I left four messages before she finally called me back to accept my reservation.  When we arrived, they had us in a room that was not what we reserved.  That part worked out, but again, not what I had reserved.  The hotel is in dire need of updating.  The carpet in our room was worn, and the entire hotel had a musty, old smoke smell to it.  The staff was not helpful or friendly.  I was hoping for the southern charm that we experienced the night before in Memphis, but it was not to be found.  We made multiple calls to the front desk for items we needed to have brought to the room.  I had to call three times for blankets, and housekeeping did not leave us any clean towels when they made up the room after the first night.  Breakfast was included in our package, and it was inedible.  Cold, rubber eggs and tasteless other options.  Overall, very disappointing experience, especially considering the fabulous experience we had a the Sheraton in Memphis the night before!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Apart from it being a smoking bar it's a great place to enjoy some great live original music on Thursday night at 7pm and a moonshine. Most popular flavor is Sweet Tea. Good location on lower Broadway Nashville. Lots of girls enjoy having their pic taken against the wall of moonshine American flag.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: My favorite bar downtown. The music is always amazing, and it is never too crowded that you can't enjoy it. The bar staff is great and always welcoming. I come for the jalapeno moonshine bloody and margarita. They don't serve food but will allow you to bring some in.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Very fun place to go watch and listen to live music in Nashville. Great staff that was very friendly. Def worth the stop on Broadway!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: This is one of those must hit places when you're on a bender on Broadway. It's always packed with good music and good people. I find it pretty amazing how well the staff keeps up with the orders given the volume of people that they serve.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
I've only been here once, but I really liked the atmosphere. It's a very chill place, with lotso moose heads on the wall as if someone likes to go hunting... Other than that I like the stage, but more importantly the music was THE best I've heard on Broadway. If you ask me, it gets old pretty fast listening to all the country singer wanna-be's. Don't get me wrong, I appreciate country but I'm not a die hard fan so it was nice to hear an artist singing more alternative songs. 

About the beer... yeah, nothing's on tap, and a bottle of beer will run you about five or six bucks. Meh. Not the greatest deal but what the hell I go there for the music, not the beer.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Always solid music and what you would expect of a Nashville honky tonk. The weekdays more acoustic shows are much better than the crowded weekend full band in my opinion. Prices R above average but that's what you can expect from a popular Broadway honky tonk.

They must do when visiting Nashville

name: The 5 Spot
text:
Two words: Motown Mondays!

I travel in and out of Nashville for work during the week and I typically ask locals what's fun to do in town. Based off their feedback, I was recommended to check out Motown Mondays at The 5 Spot, and in all honesty, this place does not disappoint. Drinks here are cheap like $6 for a PBR can and a shot of Jameson; $7 if you're looking for a little more craft. The music starts around 10:00 pm and the crowd gets bumping around 11:30 pm.

Disclaimer: If you're not a dancer, enjoy classic hits from the 50's to the early 70's, or like a good dive bar, then this place isn't for you. Also, if you have work the next day, you probably will have a hangover.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Stopped in here for a quick drink as we ventured.  Ordered a vodka redbull for 9.75 and watched her pour skol vodka and use energy drink off the gun,   Not worth it

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: By far the worst hotel experience I have had.  So many bugs.  Bugs and hair in first room and roaches in second "Club Level" room.  Front desk staff telling me to just take some Benadryl for reaction to 1st room.   Told us they wouldn't charge us due to our experience then Charged us for both nights even though we left after one night, when disputed charges on credit card they denied giving any money back then credit card company pushed the issue and they refunded us one night.  Awful

name: FooBar
text: I love the FooBAR. The bartenders are great, the people are chill as hell (especially the ones on the back porch), and I've never had a bad time, just good ones, a handful of great ones. I love the FooBAR TOO. It's always something interesting going on in there if you like to rock. People bitch that it's loud, but it's a rock bar, so ah, yeah, it'd better be loud. It's cheap, it's nearby, and it's as East Nashville as it gets.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Consistently one of my favorite places on Broadway. Not overly hyped, laid back crowd, reasonably price drinks, and the music's always great. Stop in!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
When this venue is elbow to elbow and the staff can still make you feel that it's all about you, is a sign of great leadership. 

The service provided this New Year's Eve was simply amazing for my party of six!  I will always look forward to their ability to exceed expectations. 

Thanks Zeke P. and the WB team for making your guests feel like friends.

name: Ray Stevens CabaRay Showroom
text:
I have been to the CabaRay twice, once when it first opened, and again this past weekend with my parents, who live in Ohio. If Ray Stevens isn't enough to get you to come out (and believe me, he is plenty reason enough) the food and staff will seal the deal. I'd like to tell you about this past weekend, as it was hands down the best experience I've had anywhere. 
We bought tickets for Friday night (so we thought, my husband made a mistake on the date, and we had tickets for Saturday instead.) When the staff discovered the mistake, they bent over backwards to accommodate us. Our VIP table wasn't available, but they got us in one right next to our chosen table, and it was still incredible seats. They initially didn't think they had enough food, so they refunded us the meal price, then came up with incredible meals for our whole table. I cannot say enough wonderful things about the staff, and the building.
The building is beautiful, from the gift shop to the chandeliers and the place settings. Ray made all decisions himself from what I understand, and he has impeccable taste. The food is tasty, and the CabaRay wines are delicious. The dishes, the tables, the centerpieces, and the setup of the dining room are elegant, and accommodating to anyone, regardless of disabilities (my parents are elderly, and did not have an issue with getting in, and being seated comfortably.)
Now, for the show. There is simply not a better showman on Earth than Ray Stevens. I am generally a fan of metal music, but since I grew up with Ray and his music, it will always have a place in my heart. After more than 60 years of doing what he does, he still sounds exactly the same. He does all his hits, impeccably, and the show is exciting. He tells jokes, plays instruments, sings, and just shows the world why he has had such an incredible career. You will not be disappointed. He is a super nice guy, and takes time to meet everyone, sign autographs, take pictures, and hang out with the audience after the show in the piano bar.
If you're visiting Nashville, please don't pass up the opportunity to see and experience this in person. It is worth every cent and then some. If you live in Nashville, go...and go again...you will not be disappointed for a second.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
I have frequented many a Hard Rock Cafe throughout the world and I can say that this experience was not one of the better ones.  My colleagues and I were in town for a conference and we decided to explore Downtown Nashville for dinner.  We originally wanted to experience Demos or BB Kings, but the line for both were very long and we were hungry.  We ended up at the Hard Rock Cafe and were seated immediately.

I will say that the service was very good and friendly (never really had a problem with service during our stay in Nashville) but the quality of the food left a lot to be desired.  I was in the mood for some nachos and ordered the Nachopalooza.  My colleague ordered the spinach dip and my other colleague the potato skins.  Each of us expressed disappointment when we received our dishes as there was nothing special about any of them.  I asked for a side of salsa for my nachos and was informed that they do not have salsa - very strange.  I ordered a draft beer which was not as chilled as I would have liked, which added to the negative experience.

I suppose there was a reason why the Hard Rock Cafe had immediate seating while other places in town were packed to the max.  I would not recommend this place to anyone visiting Nashville - plenty of other locations to experience the local fare.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Loved that they had wine and the beer was reasonably priced. Classic rock cover band was also awesome! 


But why do they use plastic cups for water? And plastic STRAWS!? It's 2018, ya'll. Most plastic isn't recycled and seeps into groundwater and ends up in your fish! It's not just about the environment, it's about the future of our children.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
We were running behind and most restaurants were on a 2 hour wait.  We decided to go to Hard Rock because big name chains typically always give you exactly what you expect food and service wise.  No less and typically no more.  We arrived last Saturday evening and decided to go upstairs for the live band.  Band was awesome and the food was exactly what we wanted.  The service was far from acceptable though.

We thought it was weird that customers did not seem that happy and that during prime dinner time, the crowd was clearing out (though the 1st floor wasn't).  After waiting 15-25 min for our first round of drinks, it became very obvious what the issue was.  Everything took a ton of time.  We actually ended up walking up to the service bar and grabbing our 2nd round of drinks ourselves since our server was constantly walking past it.  We were there for quite a bit of time and not even a manager touched the table to ask us about our experience.

My wife and I both come from the service industry and typically always give people the benefit of the doubt.  This was not acceptable though.  There were not many sat tables and they had plenty of staff capable of helping each other.  The bar was empty and bartender was completely free to run drinks.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: This place doesn't offer the kind of live entertainment that you see around town, but It's still a cozy place to eat. TVs at every booth showing great Rock music videos. I had the Atomic Burger, and it wasn't all that "atomic" (fine by me). The fried jalapeño was hot hot! But the burger was delicious! This was my birthday lunch outing and they offered me a free ice cream dessert, which was melty under a pile of whipped cream. It's a good place, but they have these restaurants everywhere, so I wouldn't recommend it while in Nashville.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: This was a terrible experience.  We made reservations and were taken to the bar to sit. Then as a party of 6 we were taken to a table meant for 4.  Our waitress was not attentive and it took many requests to even fill our water.  We waited over 1.5 hours for our food. I have been to many Hard Rock locations and this one by far is the worst.

name: The Valentine
text: First off- this is not a review for the bar because I didn't even manage to make it in. It was a warm rainy night in Nashville with a group of 20 or so. 9 of us decided to head to the valentine to check it out. HUGE MISTAKE. As we are walking in, the first 8 managed to make it in and I was the last one walking in and I was on my phone, telling people where the location was. I held the door propped open for (no exaggeration) 5 seconds. Only to have the door pushed closed on me, forcing me out of the bar. I was confused and walked back in the door to meet up with my group. There I was greeted by one of the coolest bouncers (which is such a great career for this 30 year old) with a choke hold, picking me up off of the ground with his two bouncer butt-buddies walking me out of the bar. As this action was for no apparent reason - I began to go bizzerk, calling these two every name in the book (as they woke-heartedly deserved). The Valentine deserves these three fine gentlemen and they just as much deserve  a rewarding career in the bar bouncing industry. I will follow up this review with a call to the manager. Ruined mine and my groups night, and lost them out of money that I'm sure their owner wouldn't be proud of.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This place is great. Bands are first rate. Sound is same. Have to mention the customer friendly restrooms. No attendant wanting to splash Aqua Velva on you. And my pet peace, the door of the restrooms open out so you don't have to grab the dirty handle on the way out. Kudos

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Definitely a tourist spot. However, when you're showing someone Nashville for the first time it's a must on the Broadway tour.

While we were there we took in a band who performed requests and on the spot could play and sing anything that was thrown at them.

It's a nice venue with friendly servers and decent prices for beers.

name: The Valentine
text: Great new bar! The rooftop is AWESOME and the venue is really cool. All of the staff and bartenders are super nice too. Solid music.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I flew in from mass and it was my first time being in Nashville and going out. We decided to start at the Hard Rock Cafe and it was the worst decision we have made so far on this trip. We sat at the bar and the bartender Lindsay was completely unprofessional and had a disgusting attitude. The way she was dress with her breasts hanging out and with an unpleasant attitude towards me and everyone I was with. She was rude to us the second we sat down saying "what do you want" not even a hi how are you or anything. Then started to complain to other customers next to us how she got 3 hours of sleep.... excuse me? How is that any of your customers problems? Completely and utterly the worst and nastiest waitress I have ever came across. We had then told her we did not like our strawberry mojitos because they were literally strawberry liquid with barely any alcohol and she continued to roll her eyes saying "what do you then instead". Not once was she pleasant at all and was a miserable wench who does not deserve to work at a nice restaurant like this. I will not be returning to this Hard Rock Cafe or any other for that matter.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
There was a moment, during my meal, that the video for Prince's classic 1980s track Kiss came up on the television screens placed throughout the restaurant & many of the diners, myself included, simply stopped eating & watched, until the final notes played out.  

Music, like good food, is a communal experience & whoever it was that thought it would be a good idea to combine the two was really on to something.  While Nashville is known for country music & few songs in Prince's catalog are in the country genre, no other guitar crackles with the same dry, tart twang like his, so it's understandable that so many eyes shifted to the video when that memorable song came up in their rotation.  It's part of our musical DNA at this point.  It's familiar.

And I happen to appreciate the familiar.  I've been to Hard Rock Cafes from NYC to San Francisco & all points in between.  I've visited locations in Dublin & Paris.  I go because I enjoy the music memorabilia on the walls, sure, but I also appreciate the consistency in quality & service that I've come to expect after so many visits.  

At this location, I thought I'd try their take on a Nashville regional specialty- the "hot chicken sandwich," & I was not disappointed.  I was in a bit of a hurry with the Paul Simon concert looming, so I didn't get to take a survey of what rock & roll items were on the wall, outside of a shovel used to plant a tree in honor of Ringo's 72nd birthday (I later went & found the actual tree in a park across from the Country Music Hall of Fame), I did make a point of visiting the Rock Shop.  They have one inside the restaurant & a separate on in another building just steps away.

If you're like me & a little more rock & roll than you are country, this is a great option for lunch, dinner, drinks, or just a good time in general.  Fun & family friendly, it's always reliable.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I've been to several Hard Rock cafés and though they seem the same in many ways they are different. This one has a waterfront view and of course it is in Nashville "The Music Capitol of the World" and it is exciting. They also have valet parking and it's a very reasonable price $7.00 We learned the hard way that it cost more to park in public parking. Our wait or was Nixon and he was very friendly. He not  only took the time to tell us about the Local specials he also let us in on the special taste and the one he liked best. Karla decided to order Nixon's favorite and that's a good thing. I say any Hard Rick Cafe is good but so far Nashville is the best.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Where do I begin. My family and friends decided to visit the "famous" Hard Rock Cafe today in Nashville and from the moment we sat down at the bar I was baffled by the bartender, Lindsay. From the start she was complaining, lethargic, and was dressed completely unprofessionally (her breasts were hanging out and hair was all over the place). Every word that came out of her mouth was negative and her actions were not any better. We ordered 4 strawberry mojitos and she sarcastically replied "great" rolled her eyes and told her co-worker to make them because god-forbid she had to muddle some mint. Following that moment she never came in to check in on us and we were sitting right in front of her struggling to drink this sugar cocktail. I never have sent back a drink and I was honestly afraid to tell her I didn't like the beverage. So of course as predicted she rolled her eyes and gave us a bad attitude about how she should have made the drinks and said "what do you want now." I don't know who hired this woman, but she is absolutely the WORST bartender I have ever met. We came to Nashville to have a nice get away from work and we can understand work can be stressful, but you should never bring your own problems into it. We will never be coming back to this establishment ever again.

name: The Valentine
text: I was a little disappointed by this place as I was ready for a delicious cocktail since it's listed as a cocktail bar and it's definitely not. The live music down stairs was a bit too loud so I enjoyed the roof top a bit more. I settled for a corona as the beer selection on the roof top is pretty minimal. You cannot go wrong though with sunshine overlooking broadway and a cold corona. I think I would have liked this place better if I had different expectations going in. Overall, I would recommend the rooftop and a beer.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Cool place, it was nice to experience a different ambiance of live music that wasn't in the downtown area during my visit. The cover charge was only 5$ and the bands that performed were great!

name: The Valentine
text:
This is our favorite place on Broadway. 2nd time here in 24 hours! This place has a little bit of everything you could want in Nashville within its 4 floors. Great live music (of course) on the first floor-especially enjoyed Ryan Tolson last night- excellent service on all floors and totally different
 fun atmosphere and great view of Broadway with a dj on roof. Came back tonight for dinner because we saw the menu last night. And last of all, love the atmosphere/decor in here. My favorite is the huge chandelier hanging from what looks like reclaimed wood ceiling. Super cool place. Check it out

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: When I first moved to Nashville my girlfriend turned me on to this bar and it became my favorite place to listen to live music downtown! Shawna Hornbeck instantly became my bartender & love visiting whenever I stroll thru town!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: All you need to know about this place is POOR SERVICE. Had a reservation and sat for 20 mins before getting up and asking someone to come greet us at the table and take our drink order. After another 10 mins of no service we got up and went downstairs to hostess stand thinking maybe we could sit in the main dining room instead of upstairs but the 4 employees standing at the hostess stand were so stressed out they didn't even talk to us. We left and went elsewhere. They were not even busy but the staff acted like there were people waiting around the block to get in. I will never visit again! Don't waste your time!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Right on the main strip, and a few doors down from Tootsies. Lots of good country music from talented but struggling musicians. We stopped in for a beer. This was an older crowd on this particular Monday. The strip, itself, is very touristy.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Excellent place to stay! We arrived early and were able to check in by 1230 pm. The front desk was staffed by friendly agents, who took their time with each guest and assisted with everything needed.  

The lobby, elevator, halls and rooms were immaculate and in very good condition.  There was an all-over air freshener in the lobby that smelled faintly like men's cologne - which I absolutely enjoyed!  The beds were super soft and cozy, with deep pillows and down duvets. 

The outdoor area near the pool was very relaxing, well maintained and afforded enough room with several guests while allowing for privacy.  The outdoor pool was well-maintained & clean with plenty of lounge chairs, tables and pool toys for the kids. 

The hotel arranged our ride to downtown Nashville, which was entertaining and convenient.  We ended up checking out a day early and, once again, there weren't any issues or problems. 

This will be my go-to hotel next time I visit Nashville!

name: The Valentine
text: So on opening night it appears they are not ready to open. Small  things overlooked that I'm sure for the price tag they paid for this place was an oversight.  Stage is awkwardly placed,  second level has poor view of the acts. Handrails falling  apart  tables are simply  poor craftsmanship. Basically some laminate flooring as a table, very underimpressed. Knowing who backed this place I would expect way more,hopefully they put on the finishing touches over the next few weeks. First impression leaves something to be desired. On the bright side the staff they hired is super friendly,  very engaging bar tenders. They will probably do just fine once they work out some kinks

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Worst place in Nashville! Go anywhere but here. Rude staff terrible service not a good Nashville experience

name: The End.
text: Well this place is definitely a hole in the wall/dive music venue. A venue where the artists playing may literally be sitting right next to you at the small bar or on a couch a couple of feet away (yes, this happened the other night at the royal thunder concert). I can't think of another venue I've been to where the artists mingle so naturally with the crowd and then completely rock out. This venue is definitely a heavy rock venue and you shouldn't have too high of expectations as it's a small place. The prices of drinks are a little high and the old guy behind the bar does the minimum but gets the job done as soon as you ask for what you need. It is dark and dirty in here as others have said before but a "rock/grunge/worn out" kind of dirty. The sound was actually not bad which I was surprised about. There's a vending machine for cigarettes (which of course I wouldnt recommend using) and earplugs in the back by the bar. This is a place to catch some small but talented acts in an intimate venue. This place is across from exit in and parking is typically limited in the lot but there are street parking opportunities available. So if you're a fan of smaller live music crowds, check this venue out as it may be the place for you. Just keep an open mind and as always make sure to rock out!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: The most expensive bar I have ever been into.  That includes New York City and any Ritz Carlton.  Just stupidly expensive.  I was an idiot for starting a tab so I did not realize.  The location is nice.  That's about all I have to say.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
This place was awesome during the day and on Friday night but was awful on Saturday night
 I was told by the locals that Michael Scott is here every Saturday night and he is the worst live music we have heard since we got here 3 days ago.  Love the bar but leaving because of the band!

name: The Valentine
text: Great music by both bands. We were there during happy hour so the prices were great! $3 beers and appetizer specials. Brussels sprouts were amazing! The pretzel sticks were soft and the Gouda dipping cheese was excellent!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Love this place! The bartenders were knowledgable and skilled! We went there every day for a jalapeño moonshine shot and their white lightning margaritas! It is more low-key but provided us with great entertainment and even better drinks! Keep it up Bootleggers!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: NOT ADA COMPLIANT. we could not get around this hotel, there are steps to the main restroom, carpet that makes wheel chairs extremely hard to use. there are steps leading to the first floor rooms. there is a ramp but it is way too steep and when we went down the ramp my friends who were in chairs went to fast and got stuck. going up the ramp is a whole other story. also the only way to get to the indoor pool is to go down a set of steep sets. we had to carry our friends wheel chairs down the steps to get to the pool. if you have any type of disability do NOT stay here!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I went to The Stage this weekend while in town with some girlfriends. We were there on the early side, arriving around 8 on Saturday and the place was PACKED. The band was playing covers of semi-recent hits, which was really fun and they got the crowd engaged. It only took a couple minutes to get attention at the bar, and the woman who served me was amazing. I watched her prepare the 2 drinks I ordered while also opening 4 beers for someone else and communicating with other servers - it was like watching a beautifully choreographed dance. My G&T was solid and served in a heavy duty (reusable) plastic glass. It was a bit crowded and I felt like I got (unaggressively) touched by ~150 people moving about the place during the 45 minutes we were there (which might be normal for the Nashville night scene), but was still a good place to stop for a little honky tonkin.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
A total blast!!! My friends and I headed down after dinner for Motown Monday looking for some fun to get into.

I did not know what to expect walking in- I just knew I wanted to dance the  night away. Thankfully, The 5 Spot got the message and we were on the same wavelength. Arriving around 10, the place was already packed. Early arrival is highly suggested for this very reason. 

Snagging drinks from the bar (Mondays feature 2-4-1 drinks, haaaayyyyy). Though it was packed, I felt the bartenders moved quickly to get orders taken and drinks out. i think I waited about 3 minutes for my drink and the bar was 4 deep. 

We made our way to the dance floor where we danced our asses off. Mondays feature music from the 50's, 60's, Motown, Soul, the list goes on. A nice refreshing break from the trill, ratchet music flooding every club, everywhere. The dance floor was filled with people dressed in period attire, which was pretty cool. Regardless if you think you are a good dancer or not- just lose yourself in the music, the moment (ok, almost quoted Eminem there, ha!) Check out their back patio to cool off, meet people, and enjoy your drink.

The 5 Spot features a different theme each night so there is something for everyone. I would suggest bringing cash with you for the cover. Also, keep your eyes peeled for Riddim n' Spice Food Truck. This chromed out, slick truck slangs Caribbean cuisine, blasts fun music, and a gaming system featuring the classic, Mortal Kombat. I ordered the smoked jerk chicken tacos. DANG! Fresh corn, smoky meat, and hand tossed tortillas made for perfect bar food.

An overall great experience, unexpected for a Monday night. Will definitely be one of my hang spots when I make Nashville my home!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Out of four bars we hopped into on out night out this place was the busiest. In fact it was so busy, I'm surprised the Fire Marshall hasn't closed it down. We literally could not move there was so many people in this place. 

That said, the band was one of the better bands we saw. They were your standard cover band mixed it up quite a bit to keep everyone happy. Their  fiddler jump up on the bar at one point and was really ripping, which was pretty cool.

Very mixed crowd here, but I'd say more over 30 than under. Again, super busy, but when you do finally get to the bar, the bartenders were very quick.

Only three stars because it was just too crowded.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Service was abominable.  We should have known we were in for a disappointment as soon as we walked in - the host was nowhere to be seen, then we noticed her just lollygagging around even though we (and multiple other people behind us) were waiting at the host stand for TEN MINUTES.   

Finally taken to a table.  Introduced to server.  Waited 15 minutes to get our alcoholic beverages filled (mind you, the restaurant was only at about 1/3 capacity with plenty of servers to be seen....)  Then inexplicably, our server got switched out (we thought it was a shift change... no... he was still seen in another section of the restaurant).

Server barely checked back on us, so when our meal was delivered totally incorrect (and I would blame the kitchen.... except when we mentioned it to the server, you could see on his face he messed up)... then we waited TWENTY MINUTES for the new item to come to the table.  Folks... it was a SALAD.  Brought over with ZERO apologies, my guest's food was well-consumed by then.  Still charged full price despite the huge issues.  Ugh.

As far as a Hard Rock goes --- not nearly as much memorabilia as I've seen at other locations, which was a huge disappointment in a place billed as MUSIC CITY.    hmm.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
The worst Sheraton hotel we have ever stayed in. We arrived on a 90 degree day and the A/C in our room was broken. The room temperature was 75 and after 3 hours of the room set at 60 it was 78 in the room. 

After taking a shower to cool off, we discovered that the tub drained at the slowest rate possible. Took almost 3 hours for the tub to drain and it only started at my ankles.

The entire hotel looked like it was put together by 3 year olds. Moldings were not caulked, drywall wasn't finished, wallpaper was peeling. 

Do your self a favor and stay somewhere else. SPG should be ashamed of ranking this as a category 4.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
Have you heard of Motown Monday's? 

Well if not, let me tell you about it... you may have been born in the 90's, maybe even the early 2000's but let me tell you, you know a LOT of Motown and it's the best music for dancing. 

Yes it's a DJ, and yes you're in Nashville, but this place is worth it! You'll see amazing dancers pick up and jive with folks they never knew and your jaw will drop to the floor. How did they do that move? How are they so well coordinated? Impressive doesn't begin to describe the dancing at 5 spot. 

If you're in need of a break, head to the back patio for some fresh air and a moment to think to yourself, but then lace up your shoes and get back up there because this will be the best Monday night you've had in a long time!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Much like Hard Rock in other cities.  A solid choice. A little bit on the pricey side, but consistent and flavorful food.  I'd recommend sticking to the burgers.  They have never let us down.

name: The End.
text:
Great little music venue! This is the spot for locals so if you want to see something off the beaten path & not country, head here. It was very cool to see all of the posters from bands who have played there before, like town favorites The White Stripes. 

We came to check out some local metal and found it to be a thoroughly acceptable hole in the wall venue. They are 18+ but do have a bar (beer only) and even had Yazoo! (Which they promptly ran out of after our first round). They take debit cards with a minimum. 

The woman's bathroom was clogged and uninviting so I used the men's bathroom. It was actually cleaner than I was expecting given the abomination I had seen in the girls bathroom. It wasn't an issue with less than 40 people there, but if it were busy I can see that being annoying. 

Overall, staff was friendly, beer was cold, price was right ($5 cover) and the sound was good. It was a bit of a bummer that the 9pm doors were more like 9:45 while we waited on the bartender to open the venue - but to be expected with a small run operation.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: I flew in from Maine to Nashville to get my first Hard Rock Cafe experience and it was also my last. From the moment we walked in the door the bartender, Lindsay, was aggressive, pushy and completely unprofessional to us. If I could give her no stars on this rating I would have. She was complaining to other bartenders and customers about us right in front of us. She had a lazy work ethic and to top it all off we were trying to leave and she gives us a dead pen so we had to wait even longer to get out of there! The drinks were not satisfactory and when we told her about it she huffed, puffed, and rolled her eyes. She exclaimed "what was wrong with them should have made them myself, what do you want now." AND her breasts were all over the place. I don't know what kind of business the Hard Rock Cafe is trying to bring in, but I will make sure all of my family and friends do not go there even if it is the last resort. Trash experience.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I wasn't sure what to expect after reading other reviews but overall very happy with our 3-night stay.  

Lobby - looks great and nicely decorated - see pictures. The only drawback was that the sitting area closest to the door meant that there was a permanent draft if you sat around long enough. 

Rooms - included a safe and mini fridge but no microwave. The safe is on the top shelf in the closet -  which is tough when if you're vertically challenged like me! Our room had a balcony overlooking the front entry which is a nice option if you want fresh air circulating. Starbucks coffee available in the room, includes 2 bottles of water. $5 extra for the larger bottles of water. 

Pool - great option for the kids after a long day of sightseeing. Adults, bring your suits too if you want to relax in the jacuzzi. 

Location - about a 10-minute drive to downtown which is about a $10-12 Uber ride if you don't want to deal with parking meters. The Sheraton shuttle is $10 (per person!) and leaves on the hour. I've stayed at Holiday Inns that will take your family anywhere within a certain distance for FREE so I was really surprised with this rather high per person rate. There's plenty of parking on both sides of the hotel and it's well lit so I felt safe going to/from the hotel at night. 

Dining options within 2-5 miles: 
- Monell's on the Manor (southern comfort food served family style). Highly recommend! 
- E. Milano's (Italian/pizza) Check in on Yelp for free cheese bread 
- Homegrown Taproom (local brews + food/sandwiches) Nice nearby option if you don't want to head downtown. 
- Jack in the Box (if you want fast food)

Otherwise, if you prefer to stay in, our friends said the breakfast buffet ($15/person) and pizza at the hotel was good. 

Overall - this hotel is a great option if you want to save more than half off the downtown hotels. Kids like having a swimming pool to end the day but the lack of a microwave and the high per person shuttle charge keeps me from rating the hotel as a 5. These are a couple factors I consider when traveling with kids. 

TIP: Sign up for the Starwood Preferred Guest for free WiFi.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: If you are looking for Classic Country from the 80's and 90's, this is the place to be EVERY THURSDAY night from 6:00-10:00! The Randy Nations Band, featuring the vivacious and extremely talented vocalist Taria Long, will not disappoint!! While you are there, purchase her CD full of original songs! We moved to Nashville in July and make it a point to go as often as we can!

name: The Valentine
text:
Came to Nashville and hung out here for hours... because of the music. There were some amazing bands playing & we didn't want to leave & they had a booth that seated our group of 8, which is difficult to find.

However, the staff left a lot to be desired. They were quite inattentive and several had attitudes that weren't warranted. 

We were the only table the staff DIDN'T wait on. We had to go get our drinks at the bar, while other table got waited on. They would literally walk by us like we weren't even there.

The place was cool enough, drinks were Broadway priced, the bathrooms could use some updating like real locks and dispensers that worked but whatever. It is what it is.

name: The Valentine
text: This place is one of my favorite bars in Nashville!  Bartenders are very friendly and attentive, the lighting is cool, and the love bands are always great!  I love how many floors they have and that each floor has a different feeling to it. The rooftop is awesome, as you can see the Broadway fully from it. Love this place!

name: The End.
text: Extremely small little venue behind a pizza place. The manager/owner/whoever was there right before a show was extremely rude. Yelling at my friend for no apparent reason. Definitely not interested in coming back.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Best hotel experience I have ever had, and I travel A LOT. I've never experienced such caring, attentive staff in my life at a hotel. Given my choice, I'd stay at the Music City Sheraton every day, but that might add up! 

5/5 100%

Food is amazing, too!

name: The Bridge
text:
In contrast to all of Nashville's crazy places, The Bridge was a nice calm place for a discussion. Yes, The Bridge did have life music, but it wasn't blowing out your/my eardrums. It is a really good place for a relaxing business discussion. I only ate the California salad, which was very good. 
And then there was the service: Excellent!

name: Robert's Western World
text: This was a great place to have a beer and listen to some great music.  I think it was the Don Kelly band. They played classic country, a little blues, and a little southern rock.  Very nice bar tender and a good crowd for a Saturday night.   We will definitely come back when in Nashville.

name: Legends Corner
text:
First bar we came to while in Nashville for a very short weekend. It was PACKED on a Friday night and the band was playing a bit of country and some top 40s hits. They were phenomenal. The drinks were reasonable and the service behind the bar was pretty quick considering the amount of people that were tightly squeezed into this small venue.

Definitely preferred this place to Robert's Western World, and would love to come back if I am ever in Nashville again. Just another one of the many gems on Broadway. Yeeehaw!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great live music atmosphere, chicken tenders and tots were awesome. Fresh chicken, not processed. Fun times.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This place Rocks!!!  What a great venue to see a show. Do yourself a favor and see whatever band is playing.  It won't matter who it is.  You will have an amazing time.

Quick tip:  Buy your tix at the venue to save extra fees.

Quick tip 2: Bring ear plugs.  It can be really loud and they don't sell ear protection.

Quick tip 3: Save your money on the backstage tour.  The one at the Grand Ole Opry is much better.


Rock on Nashville...this place made my trip!

name: Music City Center
text: Impressing building , modern , clean , spacious , green roof with bees but i dont feel free inside ...

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I am a Nashvillian, and this is my favorite place in Nashville to see a concert. I see a lot of concerts, averaging about 15 - 20 a year at the Ryman alone. The Ryman only seats about 2,300 people, and I love the aspect of seeing huge names at a relatively small venue. I am not a big fan of giant arena shows. The sound is amazing, and the building is full of history. I am not a country music fan (at least not what is called country these days), but I really appreciate all of the historic touches. The bathroom/merch/bar/gift shop area was recently renovated and expanded and looks excellent, and there is so much more room in that area. Anyone who visited previously knows how crowded it could get out there. I haven't tried the new cafe but I have heard good things. Some people complain about the hard pews, but they honestly don't bother me. I am not such of a sitter at shows anyways. You can't find a bad seat anywhere in the balcony, and the only seats on the main floor that I don't like are the back 6 - 7 rows. The balcony will often cut off your view a bit from back there. You definitely should put seeing a show in this venue on your bucket list.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: My first concert at the Ryman was John Mayer in 2003 before he was big, and I loved every second of being there. Music has never sounded better or more authentic. My husband and I went on our first date to see Bon Iver here and we return for multiple concerts every year, bringing family and friends to experience this wonderful place. It's my favorite spot in all of Nashville to listen to music.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: A National Historic Landmark and Mother Church of Country Music, the Ryman is a Nashville icon. It is such an intimate venue with its church pews and close balcony. There are truly no bad seats! The building itself was a church so it has a kind of aura about it. Couple that with the people that have performed on that stage and it's humbling to stand there. I walked back by after dark and even more stunning in the lights. There is a reason this place is known around the world. It was a great place to see a concert. It really shows you the history of the Grand Ole Opry and what it was and what it meant to people and the building is beautiful. Worth a visit even if you are not a country music fan. Don't leave Nashville without visiting the Mother Church of Country Music!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
History Comes Alive
The tour only takes 1 hour, but it is like stepping back in time. The tour starts with a 10 minute historical film. You are then free to roam through the theater/auditorium. If were to come back to Nashville it would be to see a show at this intimate setting. Book your trip to Nashville around a show!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Roberts is fun little bar with live music of course, good service, plenty of bar stools line the bar and there's a good amount of tables as well. We only had a beer and left but only because there's so many spots to see.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Quintessential Nashville! The real give away is all the locals and older folks who come in here as regulars. I was with a big group on a packed Saturday night; we were in the back and had great service. Music is always good.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I loved this place! It's a classic honky tonk and it was packed when we stopped in on a Monday night. There was a band playing, of course. The service was really great and the food was so cheap! This is where I tried fried pickles for the first time and they were SO GOOD! And only $4.50! It was a fun stop!

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text: James G pretty much sums it up for me.  A charming little place, no frills, $8 cover tonight and then a min of $4 per person for food/drink to sit at a table, no problem, though the wine was vile, food comprises pasta with red or white sauce or nachos.  The music was nice, the service efficient and one more time for the record no frills.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We visited on a Wednesday night 2 weeks ago.  A super-fun cover band was playing downstairs so we sat down for a beer and appetizer.  Ordered the chicken and waffles app - it was good bar food.  Nothing extraordinary but decent experience all around.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I love the Ryman. It's easy to buy tickets at the box office. They'll let you park in the lot for free to run in and purchase. I like that the Ryman is small. You don't have to arrive early to wait in line and trek 4 miles to your seat. Concessions move quickly and are located on both floors. Bathrooms are big and clean. Seating is comfy and acoustics are great. Everything about seeing a show at the Ryman is convenient and pleasant. I look forward to my next experience there!

name: Legends Corner
text: Cool venue. The band was really fun. Great prices and they even make it easy to charge your phone at the bar.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Small bar on Beale. Cheeseburger was dynamite. Pork sandwich was a little dry. Love the atmosphere. Live band always playing. Bar servers were very nice.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Since the seats are pews it can get cramped just FYI. Staff was nice and show was good.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
This place is in the Gulch section of Nashville and is worth the trip from downtown. The atmosphere is really comfortable and we were lucky enough to have a live band play the night we were there.  The sound is just right where you can hear your friends and enjoy the music without having to scream to them.  We were dressed in shorts and nice tops and fit right in, so I'd say business casual attire is fine.  We sat in one of the side booths and it was perfect to see the stage and room, while still feeling a little private.

The food is fabulous. The menu is really diverse and well priced.  We had the smoked salmon and fried calamari to start and then scallops and red snapper with a side of tater tots.  Everything was delicious. The tater tots were a little bland considering there was dill & havarti cheese in the potato mix...  for drinks, I had the frose which I highly recommend if you like a slushy type drink on the sweet side. 

The dessert menu didn't really jump out at us, but we tried the Creme brûlée which was just ok. The presentation was really nice (same for the apps and dinner plates).

Our server, Natia, was really sweet and informative. She helped with suggested recommendations and didn't rush us in away.

Food-4.5 
Price-4
Atmosphere-4

name: Robert's Western World
text: One of my favorite music venues in Nashville. The house band rocks! (or should I say countrys!)  food not so good, unless you like balony between white bread. Tip the waitstaff, I think they don't get any hourly wage, so depend on you to tip, and I guess the owner becomes even richer that way.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Tried some really good local Bourbon called Old Hickey. To bad it's only sold locally. I would buy this at home. Has a cream/caramel smell and taste.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Had the onion rings at 2:30 this morning and they were awesome! Heartburn has unfortunately set in quite heavy, but was well worth $3.75 after Makers and great music all night, it was a good way to cap off the night.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: I am so excited to have finally visited plaza mariachi! It's definitely a cool place and a great experience. There are lots of boutique shops, a hair salon, market, and even an art gallery! The food court is definitely the center of all the activities. We went on a Saturday and walked in to a full on show with arial dancers, jugglers, and a full band. We really enjoyed the show and the atmosphere just enjoying a little slice of Hispanic culture. We tried several of the food places but was slightly disappointed, otherwise this would be a 5 star review. The food was very mediocre and actually priced a bit more than say Mexican food trucks or other restaurants. We had gordidas and quesadillas from the hildago stand, this was probably the most average taste. The carne assada was extremely chewy. Although I did appreciate the three sauces they put out self serve style. The tres gaucho place had more pricier fare, we got some potatoes bravas which actually was the best part of the meal. We also got a side of corn but was very disappointed that for $4 we only got half of corn. We also tried the churros place, but the churros were too over fried and the chocolate sauce was just Hersey's syrup. Lol.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
A legendary venue. We used to joke that you would buy the album of the opening band, only to find upon listening when you got home that they didn't sound nearly as good outside of the Ryman.

If you have any chance to see someone here, do it. You won't regret it.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Friendly folks for sure (Caron is awesome!). The food menu is very very limited. Ordered the chicken fingers with Honey-spicy sauce. The chicken was authentic, but the sauce was pretty water-y. Shots were pretty expensive, but the band was ok.

Will I go here again? You won't have to twist my arm, but I won't twist yours either.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: LOVE LOVE LOVE! Must go here for a fancy night out in Nashville. We had reservations for my birthday and they sat us within our reservation time. Everyone that came over to our table wished me a happy birthday which was so sweet. I had the burrata which was SO GOOD. The flavor of the balsamic tomatoes was amazing. I then had the shrimp and crab scampi, which I shared with a friend and I am glad I did because it was super filling. They even split the dish for us which was so nice. My friends all enjoyed their meals, mainly ordered seafood and no complaints. We had the fried cheesecake for dessert which they decorated beautifully for my birthday which was so nice. The best part about the place was the friendly service you received from everyone there. The live music was awesome too and not too loud for dinner. The only negative was the place was super dark and it was really hard to read the menus. My friends are I are all 24-25 years old and I felt like my parents when we had to take out our phones to use the light, but other than that, I had an amazing time and the food was delicious!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Enjoyed a great meal, the live music was great and the speakers throughout the restaurant were mixed perfectly for sound. I sat at the bar and still felt like I had a great seat for live music, good drinks, and the food was fantastic.

name: Second Fiddle
text:
I was alone on a business trip. The bouncer actually sold me on coming in! I still wasn't convinced until, while standing near a table, the bartender came out from behind the bar to take my order!!! Amazing!! Band was great! At least as good as next door at tootsies is not better. 

Keep up the fantastic customer service!!! You'll have lines out the door in no time!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: The band was great and the food was amazing! It was the perfect night out for a girls weekend away. Our server absolutely went above and beyond for us and was very attentive. He forgot one of the appetizers, and comped it for the table. I will be back if I'm ever in Nashville again!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Sooo I blacked out here
Which means it did it's job, folks.
Good music! (I think)

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: My favorite music venue in Nashville by far!! The acoustics of the building itself were amazing and it felt like such a personal/intimate experience. The seats are wooden pews but they really weren't bad to sit on. The view was great. The concession stand lines weren't long. The prices for food and beer were not outrageous. I would love to go back in the future!

name: Music City Center
text: A really impressive (and huge) facility right in the middle of Nashville's awesomeness.  I went to the Opening Weekend festivities so I haven't been to an actual conference yet, but this place could handle even the largest of events.  MCC is big-time.

name: Legends Corner
text: Great place on lower broadway. Wandering in at midday on a Saturday to find an entertaining young lad called Lefty Ferguson doing his thing. Very friendly crowd. I found it to be a better daytime place to go rather than nighttime, but I would certainly recommend a visit.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Nice bar with live music. We stumbled upon this new place while exploring downtown Nashville. There was a free Gin Blossoms concert that night as a grand opening. We stood feet from the stage and met some awesome people while waiting for the band. The only downfall was you couldn't get to the bathroom or the bar due to so many  people. This was to be expected with a great band though.

name: Music City Center
text: I've come to this venue for multiple events, and multiple times. My favorite event is Wizard World comic con. The hall is huge! Lots of room for vendors and convention visitors. The structure stands on several levels as it was built on a hill and can be a little confusing at first. It's important to note where you are going and ask someone if you get confused. Otherwise, you can wander for a long time in this massive building.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: From start to finish, this place was top notch. Had some French Martinis to start, then apps. EVERY dinner was fabulous.  One had the scallop with orzo, another shrimp and crap scampi, the sea bass (OMG), and the salmon. Not one complaint from our table. The service(from Jesse was great) was impeccable and the waiter attentive and entertaining. Don't miss it if you come to Nashville

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Just got to Nashville first time down on Broadway went over to the Tin Roof  had the shrimp and a baked beans and it was awesome will have it again

name: Robert's Western World
text: In an oasis of new age country music cover bands and Sysco box food this place may be the only venue reverent enough to claim the title of 'Home of Traditional Country Music'. Burger was what it was suppose to be and the Traditional music was exactly that.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: My wife and I went on the tour. It was amazing to learn the history of such a historic building. I highly recommend the guided tour. It was worth every penny. Going backstage shows you many things hidden from the public either expected or unexpected. Don't miss the movie they show, it's worth the 5-10 minutes. Note: There are many steep stairs in the Ryman with low ceilings in places. May not be easy for people with mobility issues.

name: Robert's Western World
text: My favorite bar in Nashville. A fun mix of locals and visitors, the bands are awesome and play a great mix of old and new songs, but mostly the classics like Patsy Cline, Johnny Cash and similar. Friendly bar staff, and beers range from $2.50 up, with Fat Tire and similar only $4.50! Cocktails were mixed nicely and very reasonable. I loved the bacon cheeseburger and onion rings, and their special is a 7-piece fried bologna sandwich. Fried pickles are delicious, too, with ranch dressing, of course. Simple food and inexpensive food and drink, but really good food that's affordable. Great bands play for tips, so bring your $5's for the tip jar. I'll be back again soon! Possibly tomorrow! Saturday night can be a different kind if crowd, mostly tourists, but other nights everyone is friendly.

name: Legends Corner
text: Spacious honkey tonk. Live music was great. Drinks were cold. Crowd was fun. There is room for dancing and prices were reasonable.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great venue for solid country music. I didn't eat anything but we had a great time drinking and listening to music. Hope upstairs is the best bartender !!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We had a private event here and everything was delicious, meats, sausage, pasta, salad, desserts to die for, appetizers, everything was so good and tasty and flavorful. They had a band as well that played all variations of songs from different eras and languages as well and the upstairs had a great view as well as patio to lounge on, overall this was a great spot to enjoy a nice dinner

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place! Loved the rockabilly country band they had. Drinks were reasonable, atmosphere was warm and friendly. It was a great place for us out of towners to experience something different. We had a good time. Would recommend to anyone going to Broadway.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Robert's Western World was our first stop in Nashville ahead of our long girls weekend.  At first we were a little unsure about this place, the crowd tends to be a little older, but you MUST look past that because it is a really good time!  We went upstairs (the downstairs was crowded) and managed to sit at a small little bar table.  The bartender was cute, friendly and very attentive.  We all wanted a quick snack so decided to go for the burgers, and they were SO GOOD!!! I love that the burgers are served with a good ol' bag of lays chips. Such a nice touch that I don't see very often.

The bands they have play here are amazing too!  I was jamming out to almost every song that was played, and they definitely knew how to keep the crowd engaged and having a good time.

Stop by Robert's if you want some cheap beer & burgers & good live music!

name: Musicians Corner
text: We showed up for the food trucks and Robert Randolph and the family band. We got there during the second half of the event and half of the food trucks were packing up for the day. They said they had to get to their next event. I was shocked that they wouldn't be there for the entirety of the day.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Fun place!  Great music and the staff is awesome.  The food:  burgers.  Really good burgers.  Don't expect a quiet experience.  This is a place where you will be lucky to find a seat at the bar and enjoy your greasy burger along with some live music.   As far as your options on the strip, this is probably the best.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Went in for lunch, we were only ones in there due to weather. Waiter was super friendly without being overly intrusive. Bisque was delicious, grilled chicken sandwich was good, would have enjoys it more if bread had been toasted.

name: Nashville Municipal Auditorium
text: I've attended Beer, Bourbon, and BBQ a couple of times at this venue.  It's ok, but not my favorite place ever.  It very much has a "warehousey" feel to it...and also smell.  Parking is a little rough, especially since it seems that Nashville has taken to covering many of its downtown meters with red 'no parking' bags.  It was appropriate for this event, but still not my favorite place to hang out.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Perfect lunch spot! Super inexpensive compared to other local restaurants. App, burger, and two beers for under $20!!! I had a burger which was good- it's nothing special but it's delicious! We tried all the apps- none disappointed. Mozz sticks were my fav. $2.50 PBR's and MHL. The staff was super friends and accommodating for our large group. I will definitely return!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Amazing food really nice service service loud music and active crowd! Country my favorite!!! Nice place and friendly staff! I'm from Michigan and I loved this place!!!!!!!    :-)

name: Robert's Western World
text: I tend to avoid downtown but if i have friends in town that insist on going to Broadway this is one of the few venues we will be sure to take them by. Realize what your getting... It is a honky tonk for tourists. you will see some locals, like me they are usually entertaining guests. It will likely be crowded. Dancing is limited, although late night when it thins out a bit and the stragglers are well and truly drunk you can see some interesting "two stepping" attempts. Beer and booze prices are in-line with downtown and the service is usually surprisingly good.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Saturday brunch favorite Sambuca did not disappoint. The live music by Garcia and Scott, coffee alcoholic drinks and the shrimp and grits made this a brunch favorite. I like to bring guests to Sambuca because of the ambiance and great drinks but I brought a date to Sambuca for brunch and that was a sure way to win mega points. So save this one for a good date spot. Our waiter was phenomenal and took the time to explain the menu. We ordered shrimp and grits and chicken and waffles. The shrimp and grits were spicy and the sauce had layers of flavor. The grits were whipped and creamy with little pieces of sausage mixed in. The chicken and waffles were huge! The chicken was juicy and covered in gravy that is homemade goodness. The waffle has the right mix of fluff and crisp edges to make this a masterpiece. The live music was lively and they engaged the crowd with commentary and original songs. Five stars for the service, food and the talent on stage. I'll be back!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Great tour! Must see in Nashville. Our tour guide Kylie was very knowledgable and had great energy!

name: Robert's Western World
text: In the first place this bar has a really cool name, my name is Robert so I could be bias but it what it is. This place rocks man, one of the better bars on the tourisy Broadway strip of honky tonks and bright lights. If you are Nashville you must come to this legendary bar its awesome baby.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
We loved the Ryman!  We paid extra for the backstage tour, which was basically a tour of the rooms and stories about the pictures.  You couldn't take pictures, which was a bummer, but this is the only way you can see backstage which is absolutely worth it.  The tour itself paled in comparison to the one we got at the Grand Ole Opry, but the building is just awe-inspiring. 

You can imagine the women and men sitting, fanning themselves and unfolding dinners as they watched the early shows, and hear the laughter and cheers resonating in the wooden pews.  This place is a treasure.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Love this place, one of the oldest honky tonks on Broadway is that hey have a dance floor. So, if you love good, live country music and want to dance, this is the place to be.

name: Music City Center
text:
Now I know why those boots are made for walking because that's all you're going to do in this place. It is huge complex that takes up over 1 city block.

I was here for a work convention for work. The backdrop and architecture and interiors are clean and aesthetically pleasing but the food is terrible. Perhaps they have a price variation and it was my job that ordered on budget or there is only one quality of food option. Either way the food was miserable so in conclusion looks great but go eat at a regular restaurant after you're done with your work event

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Great great place!!! Came in for some music, appetizers, and drinks.  Did not disappoint!  
The live band was great.  We ordered popcorn shrimp that was tasty, the chicken and waffles was sweet but good, and the nachos were my favorite. We ordered beer and I had jack n coke... Let me tell you, my drinks were stiff and tasty .  This place is definitely a good time.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Gotta check this place out for the best talent in music in town! One of my favorite places on broadway!
I rate this place on the top of my list because of the entertainment. Seating is limited. It had great fried foods when you've been drinking!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Phenomenal first experience at a honky-tonk.  Service was decent, but tough to get the bartender's attention or a table.  It was all worth it though; their regular Monday night country swing band was great.  We also loved the recession special (fried baloney sandwich, Lays chips, and a PBR to wash it down).   We tried the fried pickles and hot dogs as well.  As a true inner city kid, I wasn't sure how I'd fit in however, I think I've found a new niche!

name: Musicians Corner
text: We had a great afternoon of trying new foods and listening to some great local musicians.

name: Legends Corner
text:
Really enjoyed all the Honky Tonks on Broadway.  Legends is on the corner and seemed to be less busy than some others.  There is also a side entrance that seemed fast. 

Music is country of course - but a little bit more rock and roll - at least the weekend we were there.

name: Second Fiddle
text:
Got snow delayed traveling home and ended up wandering into this place because it seemed lively despite the city being pretty much closed. 

Beer was cold, music was fantastic and service had a smile. What more can you ask for?

name: Second Fiddle
text: Great live music and local beer! Not too crowded either! Perfect spot to get started on a Friday night!

name: Robert's Western World
text: If what you are looking for is a straight up honky tonk on Broadway, this is your place. Entertainment is twangy goodness. Fried bologna sandwich special was an exceptional deal and good when trying to absorb a bunch of liquor.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Oh my gosh! Such a fun honky-tonk. We stopped in for beer, music and lunch (in that order) and OF COURSE ordered the Recession Special: A fried bologna sandwich, chips and a PBR. This was literally the best fried bologna I've ever had - I know it's been years since I've had bologna, let alone had it fried but there are simply some things you just don't forget.

Like I'm not going to forget that for just $5 I had a great lunch and listened to a great local singer's gig. Sit at the bar for a good view and plenty of attention from the staff.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: A bit overpriced, and in our party all of the proteins were highly overlooked. That said, the service was good, drinks were decent, and the food was pretty good. Great atmosphere and music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Let me start by saying my meal was delicious, but my family didn't have the same experience. First off, our server gets to our table by saying we're out of a lot of things. Not a way to start your meal at a fine dining place. 
 We both ordered filets and mine was medium and my aunt was medium well. Mine was more well done than hers and it was supposed to be less cooked. They had to recook her steak longer, and her Brussel sprouts weren't good, so she ordered spinach instead. They ended up charging her for spinach which I think was pretty distasteful especially since THEY messed up her meal. Who does that? For dinner we ordered the berry cobbler which is supposed to come with ice cream. Half the reason you order it. It came out without ice cream (non of which our server forewarned us about) and they were out of ice cream. Had we known we would have ordered a different dessert. How do you not tell your customer that? Lastly, the bathrooms were DISGUSTING. I went in a couple times and there was water all over the counter. The toilet paper was never in the holding or it was sitting on the ground with toilet paper all over. Personally, a gross bathroom at a steak house speaks volumes and is awful. It should have been well kept. Overall, the place is beautiful and the music is fantastic and the food is tasty, but for a fine dining experience what did they do to keep me as a customer? Not the best.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Best country music spot in town. Good music every night. Food is ok but, the music is great.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Had dinner with a friend on 02/05/13 and enjoyed it.  I had the flat iron steak with a Caesar's salad and it was tasty and a good portion.  The service was not spectacular, but the jazz band was pretty good and not too loud.  It was pleasant in it not being too busy as well.

name: Legends Corner
text: Great time we'd. July 3  2013 in the afternoon one of the best Acts on the strip ... An afternoon of great talent and a cold beer or 2  great female singer with a great as well as comic guitar player ( he had us chuckling a few times) .. Drummer good voice great chops .. Unfortunately having sound issues but the bass player worked through it to give all a great show... Add the fact the server was very attractive young lady right on the ball with our drinks... We did the bar crawl Sat,Sun, wed afternoon and saw some great acts but this had to be the best highlight of the week for us ...Legends will be on our favourite list on our next visit...  Recommended to add to your stops ..

name: Robert's Western World
text: Love this place!!  always my first stop when I'm in Nashville. Great atmosphere, nice people and good music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great atmosphere off the beaten path in Nashville. We went with a larger group and sat right next to the stage, but everywhere in the place has a good view of the band. Great service - friendly staff & most importantly, delicious food! I would definitely return for the champagne chicken. :)

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: There was a 70's band playing last night which was fantastic. The appetizers were delicious- buca beignets being our fave. The filet was cooked perfectly and the berry cobbler was oh so nice- the ideal bite to end the evening. We'll definitely be back.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Coldest cheapest drinks in Nashville! Nicest servers! Just go you will love it the Sammie's are interesting!

name: Second Fiddle
text: This is a nicely laid out bar, plenty of room inside, nice and clean, wee decorated. The service was good and the bands are great. This one was a bit less crowded than some of the others on the street.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Love their food!!! The atmosphere is so fun!! The only problem is that if you're on a date, you can't really have a conversation Bc you can't hear anything but the loud music! When it's warm, we love sitting outside! It's our favorite spot for date night!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great experience On a Tuesday night ! Awesome music, awesome vibe! Definitely a lot of tourists! Bar prices are typical I guess, I'm not a fan of paying $6 for a beer, but the bartenders were super friendly! Overall great crowd and the band was AMAZING!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We had a nice time at Sambuca for my best friend's bachelorette weekend. For 9 girls, they sat us in a great table next to the balcony, overlooking the stage. The music was really fun and  a nice added bonus to the dinner. The food was really tasty. Our only issue is that we waited forever for the entrees- about an hour after our appetizers. The kitchen obviously did not time out their large parties appropriately and the kitchen was backed up. But they were apologetic and offered us dessert on the house. Would recommend!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Went to see Stephen King.  Got there thirty minutes before show and line wrapped around building.  15 minutes to get in.  Had to stand in trash in alley.  Other than that it's the Opry and worth seeing a show if you have never been.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Me and a large group of friends went here for lunch on our weekend trip from Georgia. We were there for 3 hours before we got our lunch. The amount of time we ended up spending there ruined our day. Overall, bad experience.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Open to all ages until  10.00pm. That makes it great for those 19 year old boys that are visiting.  No smoking, cheap burgers  and bologna sarnies in a basket and a cold beer circa $5.  Plus good ole fashioned country music without people falling down drunk like some of the other notable bars.  Home of Brazilbilly and a rocking good time.
Always a stop when we have out of towners.

name: Legends Corner
text: Pretty messed up being a first responder and veteran being treated like a criminal for wearing a motorcycle vest.  We are a riding group not mc was treated like a criminal.  Let you bogus bouncer see in my vest. Proved no weapon but still treated like a criminal.  Nothing like putting your life on the line every day and being treated like a criminal. You people are joke and should be ran out of business.  We voluntary left business after being treated bad.  Shame on you. I did as you ask and still complied with rental cop. Tried second time to come back without Scarry vest still deined.  Bouncer were good but supervisor horrible.  Demand apologize

name: Robert's Western World
text: Love this place a Nashville classic. Great grilled cheese. They sell cowboy boots too. Always good music. Long honky tonk style bar.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is the only bar on Broadway St in downtown Nashville to experience real Nashville rockabilly live music! Cash only and prepare yourself for a great time. Upstairs level has its own bar.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Got recommended by hotel concierge. "Only" time they had was 6:30 Saturday we were told so off we went.  Walked in to a basically empty room that never did get more than half full the entire time we were there.  All I can say is it was the worst meal of our recent visit.  Don't go, run away. Eat at Cook Out if you are desperate.  Food was expensive service was slow and two out of four orders were cold when they arrived to table. Sent calamari back "we will re-make that right away", about 5 min mater the same microwaved plate came back to table - now a bit warmer but totally inedible.  When they cleared our table we could tell server was embarrassed but they still charged us for the food.  The place can't decide what it is - if fine dining then why TVs on walls?
We had great meals the entire rest of our visit at a variety of spots - avoid this one if you are in town.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Definitely a place that should be on your list if visiting Nashville! Great entertainment although seating is on pew benches. So can get a little uncomfortable

name: Legends Corner
text:
Stopped in here as I was touring Broadway and taking in the sights. They had live music in the window and I thought I would give this place a try.

Place is dark and smells like a bar upon walking in. The band playing wasn't too loud, but plenty loud enough that they could easily be heard in the back area of the bar. One of my buddies flagged down the bartender and ordered a few drinks. 

I am not sure what my friends got, but I got a 7-up and strawberry vodka. It was not very good. Very likely it was cheap liquor that was used, although the small drink was $9.00 on a Wednesday night. To be honest, I don't really care much for the taste of alcohol, so I'm a poor judge of what a good alcoholic drink should taste like. I have had alcoholic drinks that I like, so it is possible, but this one wasn't it. Even my buddy said he didn't think it was that good and cited the cheap liquor used in it.

The bar has a floor section closer to the band and a back section with a few steps to a raised area. We sat there and the band sounded great from there. The bar's back area is like a museum of sorts, with an older jukebox encased in glass. I know jukeboxes are terribly common, but it was like being in Back to the Future Part II and Marty looking at every day 90's gear like it is a museum item.

We left after the single drink. We were probably there 20 minutes. It is a quaint place. Probably worth stopping in at least once to check it out. Not really a place I would hang out for long periods and continue to drink, but it would be nice if you were short on time and wanted quick entertainment.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Recently moved here from San Diego and seriously missing good Mexican food! I was so excited when I found out about this place. I've never seen anything like it. I came here during the week so it wasn't busy at all. The shops were fun to look at and got to see two performances. I think it's really cool that they do that. I want to go back and check out more events. Can't remember the place I ate at but it was pretty good. Definitely need to try out the other places.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Great venue to see a show. You'll want to be there on time because the seating is not specifically labeled so if you are late someone might be sitting in your seat and everyone has to shift over.  The VIP was a little bit underwhelming. First of all the staff were very generous and helpful. The food was not well-maintained and just sort of over cooked as the evening went on. The desserts were delicious. Drinks are much smaller than you get if you are not in the VIP so in order to have a conversation you have to keep walking across the VIP to get a drink and walk back and get a drink and walk back. I think they're trying to control people taking drinks out to give to someone else but there would be many ways to do that without making the service for VIP worse than the service for other people. It is not a lounge it is a hallway. The doors to the hallway say emergency exit only. To make it worse they want people to walk across the entire building and then back to get to the lounge even though there are simply doors and stairs to the area. They have this completely wrong. When you exit at the bottom of the stairs there are two staff members standing there. When you enter at the top it is strange but nobody is standing there.
