They need to put a VIP lounge sign on the upstairs and the downstairs where staff were standing and just pay attention to who goes in through those doors. It is absolutely ridiculous to think a person downstairs on the same side as the lounge would cross the entire theater go up the stairs cross the entire theater go in the door get a drink then when they need another do the whole thing again. Four trips across the entire theater to get a single drink. There are no chairs in the VIP lounge.  I rate locations according to their primary purpose and in this case it is music and music presentation was fantastic and the staff were very helpful. But I won't give the same rating about the lounge.

name: Legends Corner
text:
This is one of the best bars in Nashville hands down.  The servers are excellent and attentive even when its busy.  The live music is always good, though I would recommend going when Buck McCoy is playing as he is exceptionally talented and funny.

All in, this bar shows an authentic Nashville bar experience that is only a stone toss from the Reiman Auditorium.  Go now, thank me later with an appropriate drink.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Roberts Western World is 5 Stars.  The best of broadway, an old school honky tonk that has great music, loose women and amazing fried bologna sandwiches. You cannot beat the Special Doggone for $6.50. Premium Hot Dog, Chips and Buuuuusch Light. The service is second to none and Justin was amazing. Also he is super best buddies of Jason, Josh and Leif.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Amazing acoustics. Only bad seats would be behind a pole/column. In that case the seats would be cheaper for abstracted view. I was standing near the FOH boards/audio for the Janelle Monae show.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
This is a great little marketplace in the heart of Nashville off of Nolensville road not to far from the Nashville zoo.

It's kinda in the hood, but I love that area because it has so many of my favorite Asian, Arab, and Indian markets. It's a melting pot of ethnicities which makes it very special in my opinion

Plaza Mariachi is a huge complex containing little shops, restaurants, and Hispanic markets. The live music and entertainment is also special. It's a great place to go and try food and shopping from many diverse Latin countries. 

Go check it out and make a day of it. I'm sure you'll enjoy it as much As I did!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I was really impressed with the Ryman. I'm not necessarily a country music fan, and had never heard of the Ryman before arriving in Nashville, but I took a chance on the tour and really enjoyed myself. The introductory video was awesome and very well done (and I never ever say that). I really wish I could have caught a show here. If you bring your ticket stub from Ryman to the Johnny Cash Museum, you get $2 off. My only complaint is that I think $10 would be more appropriate than $20 for admission... but I'd vote you visit this over the Cash museum, if short on time.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Lots of activities, beautiful vibe, looks like little mexico vacation spot. Lots of parking, beautiful design

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: What a great place to check out while in Nashville. It's a great historical spot and a must see if you have time to tour the area. I found it to be a little pricey but then again it's a touristy place. You start out going upstairs to watch a little video on it. Then, you get to walk around and check out different memorabilia that is showcased. You can even get your picture taken on stage. There is also a gift shop as well.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I have been here twice with a large party of work friends. The place is huge and can accommodate any size group you have.  We even got a special menu for my party of 18.  The service is great and the dining room is set right I front of a really cool stage. Music acts have been really good and play a mix of country and rock and other styles. The food is pretty good but the larger groups I've been with usually stick to shareable appetizers and they were great.  A good place to take a large group from work or a large party celebrating

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We have been here a few times. It is always fun, the music and shows we choose have been great. The food choices and wine are just top notch. The over all atmosphere of the place is fun and relaxing.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best breakfast ever! Worth the wait. We waited about 45 minutes. While we were waiting we walked around the property where we samples peach cobbler hot tea- so good. Hashbrown casserole is an absolute must. Biscuits were amazing. Everything was delicious.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We've heard so many great things and people told us we had to go. So we stopped by on our way back home from our Nashville trip, even though it was 44 minutes out of our way. Got there and there was an hour and 10 minute wait. I was told there would be a wait so it was expected. They have little shops you can browse around to kill some time. We were seated and staff was friendly. I ordered the Loveless Fried Chicken (half chicken), green beans and mac n cheese. They brought out biscuits and I tell you i took one bite and it threw me back to being a little girl at my grannies table. The chicken, in my opinion, wasn't all that great. It was dry and didn't really have much flavor. The green beans were good and the Mac n cheese were mediocre. But, honestly, I will go back just for the biscuits alone.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Beer was good; food was not. I was very exited to see a new German restaurant in town especially after my trip to Germany. Although the food choices were familier the quality wasn't the same as what we had in Germany. The pretzels just didn't quite match up, the schwinebraten was dry, and the kartoffelsalat was cold (usually served warm in Germany). I'd be able to over look all of that because the space is huge (great for large parties), the staff was friendly and attentive, and the beer was delicious, but it was soooo expensive to not have excellent food too that I doubt I'll be returning.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best breakfast I have had! The biscuit are so darn good! Loved the stored. The jams, meats and chicken are the bomb!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This was the first time I have ever waited 1.5 hr to eat at a restaurant.  Service was great.  I had the fried chicken which was very tasty, crispy, and juicy.  My husband had country ham (which was too salty for his taste), scrambled eggs (which tasted like fluffly foam), and hashbrown casserole (which was too cheesy and heavy).  The biscuits were different, but I wouldn't say they're the best in the world.  I really liked their peach preserves.  The food came out very quickly.  So many people were turned away after hearing there was now a 2-hr wait, but more came to wait.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My wife and I came here back in the winter for the first time and absolutely loved it.  We came back to experience the great food and atmosphere but were severely disappointed.

They have changed chefs, which means a new menu and the food is lacking (to say the least).  The cheese plate was good but not enough bread.  We also had the Brussel sprout salad but it is bland, very bland.  Anytime we see bone marrow on the menu, we order it but this was nothing of the sort.  They loaded it up with saved lemons (really?) and the bread was soft, big and purple.  No capers, no garlic, no sea salt - do not order this dish.  We finished up with the duck flatbread which was the best thing of the night we ate (and that isn't saying much).  

With all the local, incredible good choices in Nashville, we will mark this place off our list.  Don't waste your time and your money; we came on a Tuesday night and there was literally 4 other tables filled in the restaurant - no one at the bar, no buzz and nothing to be desired.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Exceptional food, comfortable country atmosphere, friendly folksy service...what's not to love??? The biscuits haven't been topped anywhere - smooth and silky. The gravy, jams and jellies were all homemade and complimented the biscuits well. 

We'll definitely be back!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Loveless Cafe is absolutely delightful and one that shouldn't be missed by anyone visiting Nashville. The restaurant is located outside of Nashville on Hwy 100. The restaurant sign is clearly visible from the highway with its blue color and neon lighting.

There are several building structure within the "compound" which houses the restaurant, the market, bbq pit/smokehouse, local arts store, and other buildings. The restaurant itself in nondescript and unassuming with a short flight of stairs leading to the main entrance. The inside of the restaurant is warm and inviting. It feels like visiting a Southern home where you are always welcome. The walls are decorated with pictures of famous celebs (country music stars, I think but not too sure since I didn't really look too closely at the photographs) with autographs. 

The servers were friendly and accommodating. We came around 10 in the morning so it was not too busy.  Our server was quite attentive and didn't need prompting for any refills.  My friend ordered waffles while I ordered fried pork chop. The biscuit was complimentary along with the different jams and preserves.  The food that we ordered was amazing but the biscuit was exceptional.It was not greasy but soft and flaky...delicious.  I wasn't fond of biscuits before but their biscuit turned me into a believer :) Such a great example of how good Southern cooking is and a reminder of how much I miss it. If there was one thing that I regret though is that we didn't order the fried chicken liver :(

I heard that wait time can be long on the weekends so it might be better to schedule a trip during the week. Overall, this was definitely worth the drive over from Nashville.  If I am back in the area, I will definitely come back to eat.

Prices were okay and reasonable. They have a parking lot that offers free parking.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: When in the #Nashville #TN area, this quaint little place tucked away in the burbs is a fantastic find if you're after country style dining. The old charm of family meals is reason enough to venture out yonder. I brought my wife and two grandkids here for Sunday brunch on our way back to #LittleRock #AR after a fun-filled #FourthOfJuly #roadTrip in 2014. A cultural icon, the Loveless restaurant is built into a vintage 1950s motor-hotel complex. Far from a tourist trap, Loveless is a local favorite. We make the extra effort in our travels to find places where locals eat. We had our usual favorites: chicken & waffles, bacon, eggs done to order, fresh fruit, buttermilk pancakes, sausages, and (of course) freshly made grits with lotsa butter. The Bride had #mimosas and I had #MoonshineMary (#BloodyMary w moonshine) -- both served in  mason jars. The servers were fun, attentive, and very friendly. This is home. Plenty of free on-premises parking. Prices are reasonable. You may wait a spell but with customers trekking from all parts #USA and the World, it's worth the wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Full of love cafe!!!!! We came here for breakfast and had the best experience.  Love how attentive our handsome waiter was to our every need.  He was also very quick to recommend other items on the menu that he felt we would enjoy more.  He was right and we left full and in high spirits.  Till next time!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Very nice music venue! Not a bad seat in the house! I love being able to pick my seat when ordering! The food is equally good! Service great as well!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Does it get better than Loveless Cafe? No, probably not. 

When I lived in Nashville this was one of my absolute favorite places to go for breakfast. Sure, it's sort of a hike from the city, but the drive is scenic and the biscuits are worth it. So are the preserves. I still dream about the preserves actually. I could totally go for some right now...

Anyway, everything is really good here. I won't lie to you, dear reader. You will probably have to wait. You may have to wait for a very long time to eat at the Loveless Cafe. But trust me, it's worth it.

Everything I have had there has been wonderful. I've had omelets, I've had pancakes, I've had breakfast ham, and various other side dishes. They're all good. And in Nashville, we know our food. If Loveless Cafe is that busy, it's for a reason. 

You can always check out the nearby shops when you wait. Pro tip: the preserves are sold there. Buy some.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is one of my favorite places to take out of town guests to. It's cute, quaint and just one of those Nashville places you have to experience. I will continue to go but I have to say the last three times I have been my fried chicken has been dry and overcooked, like it had been sitting under the heat lamp to long.  I still love you Loveless so please start frying smaller batches of chicken so they don't sit to long! I would rather wait a little longer for my meal and have it fresh and just right! The sides and biscuits are right on point so I'm hoping I just went on a few bad "chicken" days :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Came in for a late lunch and was told it was an hour and 20 min wait. Almost left but got sidetracked looking in the shop and we were actually seated much sooner. Biscuits and preserves were delicious and brought promptly. Food was amazing. Delicious fried green tomatoes. Everyone else had fried chicken and I had BBQ. I could only eat half of mine as it was a large portion with the sides. Delicious coconut cream and peach pie for dessert! Worth the detour!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Love this place! Menu, food,service, atmosphere and history make for a great meal and experience. Biscuits are awesome and the asst Jams are amazing!!!! Love places like this......they get it all right!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Such a cute set up with the little shops surrounding the cafe. The wait was awhile but there was also a lot of people there as well. Very good food and service. I ordered the BBQ and eggs. I recommend it. The bisquits and jams was so delicious. Worth the stop.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We had a wonderful afternoon here today! We were seated right between the bandstand and an opening to the patio,  so enjoyed a lovely breeze while we ate. We sampled a flight of beers,  then my husband had the pork schnitzel and I had the wurst plate with jalapeno cheddar wurst and smoked bratwurst, sauerkraut and rye bread. The beers were good and the food was delicious, but the atmosphere was outstanding! We'll definitely be back!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I gave this place two stars for the following reasons.

I want to emphasize that the food tasted good. The pretzel was amazing. The server was somewhat irritated by the loud music and translated that frustration towards our party.

I feel that the prices are way out of line for the amount and quality that you receive. I do not understand why places like this cannot prepare authentic food. They always Americanize it in same strange way.

I will not return, simply based on the prices.

This the private response from the manager. I have changed my review from two stars to one.

Mark, we are sorry especially that your server conveyed her sense of irritation to you. That is unacceptable with a server. As for the prices, they are comparable to the region and given that we prepare everything from scratch and import all but one of our beers, they are the lowest we can get them. We try to keep them as low as possible.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We wanted to give this a try and we are so glad we did! Emily was fantastic! We sat at the bar and she was very busy but she moved right along with it. We are only here a few days but will be back at least once. It is so refreshing to see someone who loves their job and makes every customer feel welcome!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I was so looking forward to this meal but I'm terribly disappointed. It was average (or below) in every way. I don't believe the chicken was even brined!  So sad. We have better southern food in Minnesota.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Any restaurant that brings in Usingers sausage is solid in my book.

POSITIVE:  
+tasty sausage
+tasty schnitzel
+Good biers 
+I dig what looks to be like a locker room for beer steins.  
+traditional looking uniforms for the wait staff
+went at lunch.  Was happy to see the waitress point out the meterwurst as an option for 2 people to split for $10.  Guess they understand that they're in an outlet mall filled with cheap MFs like me


IN BETWEEN: 
-/+  spaetzle seemed a bit off.  I get that it's mostly flour and egg yolks, but these seemed closer to scrambled eggs.  Still buttery goodness though.

NEGATIVE:
-Waitress was attentive I guess, but she seemed like she hated her job and wanted to blow the building up.  Look, I'd hate my job too if I were still in food service, and I hated working at an outlet mall back in the day, but at least throw on a fake smile.
-Maybe I missed it on the menu, but how bout some veal as a choice for the schnitzel?

BOTTOM LINE:
Hope this place sticks around.  I'd like to come back next time I'm in town.  Hopefully when they've got some live music or during Oktoberfest

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
We managed to get ticket for 2 of the 3 sold-out Jason Isbell shows here in December. We were really pumped, because I managed to get great seats on the first night (4 seats back from the stage). The wife is a huge fan, so she was incredibly happy about the seats and the show. 

Unfortunately, we happened to be seated next to a VIP investor in City Winery, who didn't happen to know dooku about the talent on the stage. Typical bloated businessmen with trophy wives (one of which was Googling Jason Isbell during the show and blurted out that he had "Played with the Drive By Truckers"). You know these kind of businessmen: hang out at cigar bars, eat at Mortons, and live in the Governors Club. Thankfully however, they realized that they didn't really care for the artist on the stage (other than the fact that someone told them how "great" Isbell is, and they had to see him for prestige reasons), so they left half-way through his set. Bonus for us, we ended up front row!

Onto the place itself!

1) Service. Our server was great! In fact, I don't think there is a bad server in the place. They manage to be unobtrusive yet attentive at the same time. They also manage to maneuver through the seating area without disrupting the show (the same can not be said of bloated businessmen!).

2) Venue. The venue is really classy, clean, has a great feel and even better sound. Given the tasteful use of recycled and new wood both inside and out, the backdrop for the stage is a bit corny (City Winery logo on plywood set against a gray Corian panel),  But who cares. You get a great show!

3) Food. This is where they need some help. We just had a few appetizers. Risotto balls and truffle fries. Neither was all that tasty. They weren't bad. They just lacked flavor. Maybe the entrees are better? But the prices aren't that bad. You'd hope they have some better stuff to go with the great wine options. Speaking of which...

4) Wine. Well, wine is their schtick, so let's talk about it. We tried a few of the "on-tap" wines. The Syrah was good. The Malbec is better. They sell by the glass, by the carafe or half-carafe. The prices aren't bad on these, UNTIL YOU SEE THE CHECK!!! This may only apply to the the house wines which are dispensed from barrels, but they charge you separately for the Liquor By The Drink (LBTD) tax, which is 15%. I'd like to say I KNEW if it only applied to tap wines, but our server (who was otherwise great) served us tap wine on our second night instead of the bottle wine I ordered. To do the math for you, if you order the $42 carafe of Malbec, you'll be paying $53 after 15% LBTD tax and another 9.25 % sales tax. ANYWHERE else in Nashville, brewers, servers and distillers include this tax into the price of a served drink. There's a tiny footnote on the back of the menu that mentions this tax. So, if you don't like surprises, be sure to ask your server if the tax applies to all beverages, or just barrel wine.

If I could sum it all up under pros and cons:

Pros: Great wine, great service, great venue, excellent staff all around, good prices on food.

Cons: Wine taxes are brutal, food needs a bit more flavor, valet parking when the show gets out looks to be a real CF. But I don't see a solution to that last issue.


I'll be back for sure. It's a great new place!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food was good and wait was short.  The only thing overrated was the bisquits.  They were still good, they just didn't live up to the hype.  Definitely a Nashville must.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Really famous restaurant but I don't really think this could category in Nashville restaurant since it take 25 min drive to there. Food is good and fresh but kind of too salty especially the county ham. It is a nice place if you don't mind the drive and get some beyond average brunch.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is quickly becoming one of our very favorite restaurants in Nashville. The portions are gigantic. We have had really good service each time we went and they have a great bar with tons of beer choices. I love the beer  cheese soup and of course the Jager schnitzel is amazing. There is nothing that we have had here that was not good.

name: Analog at Hutton Hotel
text: I love this venue. It's beautiful, classy, and hip, but not so much as to make anyone feel unwelcome. Rare is the venue that has spaces to chill and chat without being overwhelmed by people or music. On top of that, the sound and the staff have been wonderful every time I've been there. Analog strikes just the right chords all around.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Where country ham and eggs are the norm, I found it to be very good but not exciting as expected. The biscuits are hot but not flakey nor tender, I would call them mediocre at best. This place is a solid breakfast or lunch venue not sure if I would take the trip out of Nashville to hit it again in the future.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Visiting the Yelp Spring Break Nashville 2014, we went off the beaten path for this experience on a Saturday morning. Told that there would be a wait of over an hour, I had no qualms. Travelling all the way from Alexandria, VA, I had a hunch it would be worth it.

It has been a long time since my childhood, growing up in Florida, that I tasted truly authentic southern cooking. Ham steak, sausage patties with biscuits and gravy, grits...mmm.

The bonus is there are many things to keep you entertained while you wait. It's a village of family fun to entertain everyone. Antique and boutique shopping, complimentary sweet peach tea, quaint areas to bide your time while playing bean bag toss (AKA the "corn hole" game which made me blush). And Pumpkin Butter samples!

When we were finally seated, it was by the general manager, who enthusiastically made us feel welcome. The waitress was also a sweetie. Service is key here.

I can vouch for the:

Complimentary Biscuits and (3) Jelly Sampler
Ham Steak
Pimento Cheese
Biscuits and Gravy
Omelets
And Creamed Spinach

If I were to visit Nashville again, this would be a destination!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing true southern food. Great priced and wonderfully kind wait staff. You can't visit Tennessee without stopping here. Prices are very reasonabke, portions are huge and best of all moonshine and chess pie are on the menu!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
What I liked:
1. The biscuits- I wish I could give 100 biscuit stars.  Living in south I feel like somewhat of a biscuit connoisseur  at this point, and it's safe to say these are my favorite- extra buttery and only made better when loaded up with Loveless homemade jam.  And, get this, they are unlimited! 
2. The atmosphere- Yes, it's touristy and a little cheesy, but worth the visit if you're in town for the weekend.

What I didn't like:
1. Very long lines on the weekend.
2. Per above, tourist hell on the weekend.
3. The rest of the breakfast is average and very greasy.  

Overall Verdict: Go if you're in the mood for biscuits or doing a quick trip to Nashville.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: My husband and I just got back from the Bavarian Bierhaus ~ and we were extremely pleased. It was a lively night with the lovely Lynn Marie playing her accordian. The food was excellent - the beer even better.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I've been wanting try Loveless since moving to Nashville back in December but have been deterred by the long typical long waits for one of Nashville's most famous breakfast foods location. However, I recently figured out that the secret is getting there before 9:30 on the weekends prior to the rest of the crowd. I had the Famous Loveless Full Country Ham platter and soon discovered it was famous for a reason! My girlfriend eyes lit up over the enormous portion as our server delivered my country ham to the table. The slice of ham was very thick and cooked very well, i preferred my country ham a little bit saltier and cured a tad bit longer but this is nothing I couldn't solve with a salt shaker. The biscuits and homemade jams were served to us before our meal came out and were the perfect fix to settle our premeal hunger. I will be ping back to try their cured bacon and smoked sausage in the near future.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great food... well worth the wait would defiantly come back !!!! Great waiter Luke...drink was really good not strong Lynchburg lemonade with souvenir mini mason jar :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great place!!! Such a cool atmosphere. The biscuits are to die for. The wait was over an hour at 9:30 AM, but it was worth the wait!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best biscuits ever. Fried chicken would delicious. Grits and corn meal was Soo good. Would do the 3 hr wait again for this.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: One of my all time favorite restaurants. I have not been here for a few years and it is good to know things haven't changed. Same great food!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We had a little bit of everything at our table: pancakes, chicken fried steak & eggs, and fried chicken, fried fish, and pulled pork with sides of turnip greens and Mac and cheese. Started off with a plate of biscuits. Wow. We may not eat again today. Everything was great. The waiter was very good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The Best!  Just moved here and have already been there 3 time.  Chicken, gizzards, livers are outstanding, sides are homemade and the biscuits are world famous! 
Staff is super friendly (say 'hi' to Susan!) and attentive AND it's reasonably priced!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I have to say that everything was fantastic from the fried chicken, mashed potatoes, and mac and cheese that my girlfriend ordered to the chocolate chip and pecan pancakes that i ordered. The sweet tea was delicious, the service was quick and polite. and the prices were fantastic. I really enjoyed the building it was located in as it complimented the southern cooking that they provided. It had a lot of nice boutique shops on property but did not visit them due to time restrictions. The only negative is they used fans to cool the dining area which was near the kitchen sot it was very hot. I wish they had some air conditioning. Overall i would return there if I am in town again cause the food and service was great.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: What's left to say about the Loveless Cafe that hasn't been said already? A staple of the area and an absolute must visit every time I'm in the are. Had the smoked turkey with cranberry BBQ sauce and a side of hashbrown casserole and fried green tomatoes. All were excellent. And still the absolute best homemade jams I've ever tasted (try mixing peach and strawberry.) The wait sucks, and I don't blame anyone for skipping a second-trip because of it, but there's enough to stay busy in the area if you're with friends or family.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We were visiting Nashville and had read about this place, so made the drive before heading home. SO glad we did.

The biscuits themselves are out of this world, warm, fluffy, and straight from the oven. Served with a couple of housemade jams. YUM.

I ordered Loveless' famous salt-baked ham with red eye gravy, cheese grits, and two eggs. And several glasses of sweet tea! The sweet tea was so good, we went to the shop afterwards and bought a gallon to take home with us!

I already want to go back and visit for the biscuits alone.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Insanely popular and worth the trip 
BUT
The wait can be likewise insane (we waited 2 hours).  My suggestion: Wake up, eat breakfast, then send one person to put your name in.  If the wait's a half hour, join them.  If it's not, judge appropriately.  We were told 90 minutes and it took over 2 hours.  TAKE THIS INTO CONSIDERATION IF YOU ARE TAKING KIDS.  There are some distractions there, but not 2 hours worth.
The food is fantastic, but if you're overly hungry from waiting to have your first meal there, it clouds your enjoyment.
I had the biscuits and t he biscuit sandwich platter and just about licked the plate.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Amazing atmosphere and pretty good food- check out the Reuben rolls which were great but really tasty.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Southern hospitality at its finest! Everyone we ran into here was so sweet and helpful. The food was great. You have to try the cheesy hash browns had the meatloaf and turkey breast. Both were excellent! We were sat right away and our food came our quickly.  We played corn hole after dinner! It was perfect. A must in Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Just as good as I had dreamed it would be. We went on a Monday which was a holiday and waited about an hour but it was worth it! Biscuits and jams are incredible, wonderful ham and pulled pork, amazing side dishes and incredible service. We had Jessica waiting on us and she was just lovely! Thanks Loveless Cafe!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Food was great - no complaints! The only thing that soured our trip to Loveless was the hostess "Brooke".  Totally unfriendly and a really poor first impression of the restaurant. Watched her interactions with other guests and it was the same. Rude and unwelcoming. They could so much better! 
Enjoyed the food though! Would definitely recommend.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I had to go w 3. Just bc your name is famous doesn't mean you can give slow and almost snail paced service. The wait was 25 minutes but once seated the wait was an hour. Sitting here w an empty glass and haven't seen server since he first came to take order.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Excellent food and great service!  We will defiantly be back for the fried chicken and homemade biscuits!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I have been 100% satisfied from the first visit to the last!  One time an order didn't  come out correct. Hey it happens, I mentioned it to the staff and they went above and beyond what would have made me happy. 
Beers are HUGE.. and tasty, wait staff is knowledgeable, chief is worth his salt and management are on top of things. A winning combination!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My wife had the turkey breast with cranberry barbq sauce and I had the smoked pork chops, both were excellent. Best turnip greens I've ever eaten. Trust the staff they know what's good!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I have been to the Loveless Cafe quite a few times, and it never disappoints. This time, I took a few friends with me that wanted to experience some southern breakfast foods and they fell in love! The wait staff was wonderful, the food was great, and the mimosas topped it all off. If you're showing someone around Nashville, don't miss out on this awesome place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is a great stop food was amazing service is great everyone was friendly it's always packed with people we were lucky to only have a 30 minute wait . Our table ordered fried pork. Hops fried chicken kids cheese burger and kids chicken strips every thing tasted great the sides were wonderful and there biscuits are some of the best I have had and always served hot ... If your going through Nashville stop in they have shops you can walk through while you wait or you can sit on the front porch

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
After a year of living in Nashville (and 5 minutes away) I finally decided to dine at the Loveless Cafe. 

While I had a positive experience at Loveless please be prepared to wait at least 40 minutes. I've attempted to dine here 3 times but finally pushed my impatient-ness aside. While waiting for our table we perused the gift shops and sat on the property's front porch. I was literally taken back to being a kid visiting my grandma's house and various other small towns in the deep south. Yes, my friends if you dig Southern charm this is your place!

After much anticipation we finally got in and promptly order sweet teas which were perfect. The superstar of Loveless is supposed to be biscuits however I found them just good not great. But you still have to give them props considering how many they make from scratch everyday. The homemade jams: apricot, blackberry, and strawberry are some of the best I've had and definitely elevated the biscuits.

My friend and I both ordered the fried pork chops. I ended up getting the home fries and she got the hashbrown casserole. I wasn't a fan of the home fries, it tasted like the potatoes you got in grade school but the hashbrown casserole, my God was so good! I was totally envious of my friend. Portions of meat were massive, there's no way you'll be able to finish it all. All in all very tasty.

Looking around the rest of the joint, the other food looked so delicious. I definitely would love to come back and try it all. Waitress was super friendly but was scarce due to the place being packed so I can't be too upset about that.

Great restaurant if you're craving true old school Southern fare but come hungry!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I recently went to Nashville for business purposes and was very eager to go to the Loveless Cafe after seeing them on the Food Network.  The service was excellent! The wait staff was friendly and made us feel warm and fuzzy.  The biscuits are definatley to die for! 

I ended up ordering the sample platter and was unfortunately dissapointed.  The fried chicken lacked adequate seasoning in addition to the fact that the wings were extremely small.  The pulled pork was blah. The catfish was pretty good though.

Overall it was okay, but I probably wouldn't go back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
First, the biscuits are made from scratch and come with delicious jams- and they just kept coming.  I was pretty full by the time my breakfast arrived.  Others in our party were  equally impressed with their lunch meals.  

Everything was wonderful and our server, Kramer, was excellent.  Highly recommend the Loveless Cafe!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I had a friend visiting from KC, and we both love live music, so we got VIP tickets to City Winery last night.  Wonderful venue, great music, very entertaining, but then there was the service....... We were sitting at our table for over 20 minutes before we were approached by our waiter.  And that was the one and only time he came to our table.  My friend and I had to track him down to get service the rest of the evening.  And the venue was not sold out, actually is wasn't crowded at all.  When we finished with dinner, we had to track him down to get coffee and dessert only to be told the kitchen had closed.  Bigtime thumbs down on service.  Won't be going back any time soon.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Bavarian Biernope...

I had such high hopes for visiting this place. I had reviewed the menu before going and hoped they had even a little of the good German taste I grew up on with the German Sausage Festivals with the German Communities back home.  Sadly, I was seriously disappointed.

The interior of the establishment is ok for a German/Bavarian Beer Hall. It is a bit more modern than the old world style I would expect from the exterior theming and the costuming of the staff, but it is light and comfortable for the most part.  The benches are a bit narrow, but that is ok.  The menus are straight forward and easy to order from, the selections fairly simple and not a lot to it. It's about what one would expect, and a one page menu does well here.

To start, my friend and I ordered a giant pretzel with beer cheese.  The pretzel was indeed massive and more than enough for two hungry folks. The cheese however was lackluster, but the mustard that came with it was awesome. Kind of sweet, and fantastic with the good and soft pretzel.

My friend ordered the Kasespatzel.  She said it was a safe choice and was ok.  She ate about half of it and got the rest to go.  She also ordered the beer cheese soup and also said it was good.  Her favorite dish however was the potato salad.

I ordered the Bierhaus Wursteller.  I won't ever do that again.  I had high hopes and we both wanted to try the various sausages, plus the sides sounded good.  We were wrong.  We both tried all of the sides and the sausages and agree... the sides, all of them, were bland and almost flavorless.  The potato dumpling and bread dumpling were both cold and looked to have been scooped with an ice cream scoop. The potato dumpling was almost gelatinous in texture and congealed.  The red cabbage was bland, and the sauerkraut was terrible. A good sauerkraut is strong and bold... this was the complete opposite and I was afraid I was eating coleslaw instead.  Then there was what was passed off as sausages.  While they weren't so terrible as to inedible, I have honestly, no joking around, had better sausage from Jimmy Dean and cooked in the microwave.  There is no way one could say this was anywhere near authentic.  I know it was at least cooked in a grill since two of them were heavily charred almost to the point of burnt, but the taste was nowhere near my expectations or hopes.  For the most expensive dish on the menu... epic fail.

We both ordered desserts hoping they would be the highlight of the meal.  To that end my friend ordered the Pretzel Pudding and I got the Strawberry Tort.  She indicated the Pretzel Pudding was good.  The Tort meringue was entirely too sweet and too hard. Though the strawberries were delicious.

If, and that is a strong if, I ever come back, I am doing nothing but a beer flight or two and praying the beer is better than the food.  After spending almost $100 this evening for dinner, I feel we'd have gotten far better food from McDonalds, and I freaking hate McDonalds.  I'll give it two stars being generous because the staff was nice and courteous, but the food was terrible.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I really loved this place - it was my first time at a City Winery! I'm a music teacher and love attending live concerts but not so much the types where I have to stand the whole time, or deal with screaming crowds, jumping up and down to get a glimpse of the performed. PLUS - I love wine! 

This was the perfect setting for me: delicious wine, cheese boards and flatbreads, and an intimate concert. We saw Josh Kelley, who I was obsessed with in college, so it was a nostalgic night for me. Great venue and inexpensive. I love that they have a decent wine list, too. I wasn't a fan of their own wines, but opted for a much nicer bottle that was totally worth it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I'll hit a couple of highlights and two lowlights.  First, they serve great southern food and you'll leave full! Lunch/dinner food is what they're best at.  Breakfast isn't anything special as you can get the same thing most places and for a little less cost.  Breakfast is not worth waiting for if there is a line.  We've been going there for about 13-14 years or so and have always enjoyed our food.  They used to can their own jams on site and jars were about $7.  Not cheap but as an occasional thing it was okay.  However, they now outsource their jams and they don't taste nearly as good.  Plus you're paying over $10 for a jar - OUTRAGEOUS!  Wait times are terrible. Rarely will you go without having to wait, maybe later in the evening.  We've had wait times over 2 hours. Because of this we just go a couple times a year.  I've always wanted to try their watermelon glazed ribs, but it's a specialty item they serve only on Wednesdays (maybe Thursdays but I can't remember).  We've been three times on those days but every time they've run out before we got there.  Overall they have really good lunch and dinner fare, great hashbrown casserole, giant portions of chicken tenders, yummy fried green tomatoes......

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Strong coffee, cheese grits (why don't more people talk about these? I LOVE good grits, and these are some GOOD cheese grits!), hashbrown casserole, ham, biscuits, eggs and zero wait - a really great way to start a Southern morning. Clearly the trick is to get to Loveless Cafe early on a weekday morning. We ate beyond our fill and were ready to hit the road for 8 hours without another food stop. So very glad Yelp led us to this place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We arrived at 7:15 on a Tuesday morning. It was like a ghost town. My 4 year old nephew didn't understand why I was so shocked to not see anyone there. We were seated right away as we were the first ones there. It took a while to order, even saw an employee get their meal before we ordered. 

We got the kids pancakes and the sausage, egg, and cheese sandwich. Of course we also got biscuits. The kiddo loved his pancakes which were way too big for a toddler. He barely put a dent in one pancake. My sandwich was odd. The eggs were served on top of the sandwich of sausage and melted cheese. I had a hard time prying the bread open to get the eggs on. The server said that's always how it's served. I've never seen that anywhere. 

The service was slow. This was evidenced by the next diners coming in, grabbing menus, and seating themselves. 

It's not a place I choose to go, but would rather stay local.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: After visiting the Hofbrau Haus in Vegas, I was leery, but the food is delish! Great place! Loved the Jaegerschnitzel. The mustard served with the pretzel is fabulous. Didn't want to stop eating. Oh yeah, and there's German Bier! Very happy!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We decided to try Loveless as it is a huge tourist attraction in Nashville.  It is about a 30 minute drive from downtown Nashville, but the view is pretty.  Loveless is quite the complex- the restaurant, gift shop, shipping office and barn for events.  We went on a Monday morning and the wait was about 30 minutes.  The service was great, but I found the food less than exciting.  I had a garden omelet, and the mushrooms were canned and the veggies chopped very small.  The biscuits were more greasy than dry and crumbly.  I was glad to check out a major tourist stop, but I would not go back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Biscuits and jam. Enough said. 

Completely amazing. Such a fun thing to do in Nashville and always worth the wait!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The quality and quantity of reviews speak for themselves. There's nothing more I can add without being repetitive.

Some of the best scratch cooking I've come across on my travels.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
The venue is amazing, but the food and wine recommendations (keyword: recommendations) was not so great. 2 appetizers, 2 glasses of wine and we were out for no less than $60. Ouch. 

Will go back for music, but not for food or wine.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Jam/jellies are amazing and some of the best parts of the meal. You can buy jars if them and some good jerky in the store on the property. Food's normally great, but if the wait seems too long, might want to try a slower time, since a longer wait time means they're getting slammed, and the fried chicken can seem a little rushed and the kitchen overwhelmed/backed up because of large parties with large orders. A close drive from the local cemetery, which can cause rushes, as good southern food like they serve at the loveless is often called comfort food (which I agree with!).

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Well.......


Not sure how long they will last with the restaurant concept.
Place isn't busy..
Waiters are hungry.
Interrupt conversation when they come to the table.

Didn't have to use the valet as there is plenty of self parking.
Food.. I'd say 3.5 stars.
BUT.. their music venue seems to be strong.

I did not partake in a music venue.  Instead, friend and I went to dinner and 
were not swept up with any excitement over our food.

Doubt we'll eat here again.
Would like to check out some entertainment, some time.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The charcuterie board was one of the worst and the burger not only was a hockey puck but came with extra calcium added bone fragments. The bun easily classifies as freeze dried for astronauts.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Stopped at the Loveless Cafe on our way from Lexington, KY to Dallas, TX. The cafe was warm and welcoming with good home cooking and friendly service. We loved the complimentary fresh baked biscuits with homemade jams. The bacon burger with pimento cheese, the catfish fried in cornmeal batter and the hash brown casserole were all delicious. Although the soup and fried okra were served less warm than we preferred, our server (Mark) was delightful and attentive which made it easy to overlook a minor temperature issue that was not a deal breaker.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The food is really great! The truffle fries, risotto balls, hummus and tacos were all bomb.com! Can't really go wrong here and the bartenders are super attentive. Love the atmosphere and would like to go back for some live music!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Legit Southern sides and the best biscuits and homemade jam. Friendly service. Great experience every time!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
What a neat environment! The food was fantastic but I was more impressed with the grounds. The Loveless seems to be an old multi-building motel and they've turned it into a down-home restaurant with neat little shops and games.

The small biscuits beat everything else to your table and, if I were a cheap-o, I could see myself just eating those!  Not sure which made them taste better: the biscuit recipe or the jams that they come with.  Amaze-balls!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Being from the "north," biscuits aren't a go-to dinner or even breakfast staple, but they should be. Oh my goodness, these quick-bread kings were probably loaded with saturated fat and lard but they were some of the most delicious pieces of bread I have EVER tried in my life. And the jellies and preserves they were paired with made them even more amazing. 

What goes best with lard-based biscuits? Fried food, of course! I even took my fried quota to the extreme for this meal because I ordered fried catfish AND fried green tomatoes. Both to die for! I washed it all down with a southern-style lemonade cocktail with nothing other than moonshine. Even if it were brewed in a bathtub it was still very, very yummy! I applaud you because I didn't taste a single trace of soap. 

The one question I have is how can food made with so much love be made by a restaurant named "Loveless"?  Even though you probably caused me to gain two inches on my waist and three on my hips with your delicious fried Southern cuisine, I have nothing but love for you!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is like heading home and being served food by your mother after years of travel. Warm. Welcoming. Wholesome. We had to wait a couple minutes to be seated. Almost immediately, we were met with the famous biscuits, which were just as delicious as the articles suggest. I ordered a barbecue pork sandwich with a side of okra. The okra went fast. The sandwich was delicious and tender. Our server was incredibly attentive and kind. 

I'm don't live in TN, but absolutely imagine myself going out of my way in the future to come back. Is this the best food I've had in my life? Probably not. But the combination of the atmosphere and hearty food create such a content aura, it's hard not to give this place 5 stars.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Rissoto balls are excellent. Scallops are fantastic. Great place to be able to have good conversation due to the dining area being small and quaint.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The Loveless Cafe is amazing!!  For a number of years now, every time we drive anywhere close to Loveless, it is our dining spot!!  The quality of the food (texture, flavor, variety, etc.) would be hard to beat - and the menu (including breakfast all day!) is filled with a wide variety of some of the best down-home 'Southern cooking' to be found except at yo Mama's table!!  The Loveless is famous for their biscuits, and a plate of these, along with delicious jams, is brought to the table soon after customers are seated.  The meals are not inexpensive (but not very expensive, either), but the helpings are HUGE!!  Very easily, two could share one meal and be quite full.  Actually, this might be a good recommendation, for this is the only way to have any room for some of their delicious dessert items!!  The only 'detraction' for the Loveless Cafe is that this place is so popular that there usually is a wait (up to an hours) for a table, but that is a great compliment on what they provide their customers!!  Try to arrive between 2:00-4:00, and you usually can be seated immediately.  Oh, yes - spend some time checking out the very numerous autographed photos of celebrities who have dined at the Loveless!!  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: On our last day in Nashville we rented a car (must have since Loveless is about 25 min from downtown).  When we got to the cafe, I was expecting a wait but not a 1 hour and 45 minute wait.  Usually I do not wait at any restaurant more than an hour but since we could drive around we left our name.  When we came back we got our table and we are glad we ate at Loveless.  Our waiter was really good.  First he brought a plate full of biscuits and jams which are amazing.  He recommended the blue plates special which every Saturday is a BBQ chicken and also the fried chicken for which Loveless is famous for.  Both were really really good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Another must stop destination for those wanting to have the Nashville experience.  It is exactly how you would picture the South and it is situated in some incredibly beautiful country.   The service was friendly and the menu full of heavy Southern favorites.  

At the suggestion of the waiter I tried the Chicken and Waffles.  It was fairly good but within minutes I was down for the count and searching for the nearest hammock.  I've never understood that dish.  The biscuits were as good as advertised.  They were plentiful and came with plenty of jam options.

name: Rocketown
text: Not a good place for gay people and their friends: http://www.queerty.com/nashville-club-fires-staffer-wearing-i-support-same-sex-marriage-shirt-20130122/

name: Rocketown
text: Best tap water in all of Nashville! I was very impressed by their ice to water ratio. It was SO worth the 50 cents!! I bought 10! :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless cafe has some of the best biscuits ever and there blackberry jelly is superb. Their food in general is amazing. It just taste great

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Our server was a little slow, but she's only one person so I won't condemn the entire staff. Besides the long wait, our food was just ok. I've had better German potato salad, and the pretzel was really over rated. I was not expecting it to be so hard, so that threw me off. The jalapeño cheddarwurs is really delicious.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Such a historic place around Nashville. First time there and it was a great experience. I loved seeing all the autographs from celebrities on the wall. Only downside to Loveless is the wait. My party of 3 arrived at 2pm and still had to wait an hour. The food and service was still excellent though once we were seated! Biscuits were delicious as well as the jellies. I got fried chicken and scrambled eggs with hash brown casserole and it was so amazing. The chicken was fried to perfection and felt like I was at home. A must when you visit Nashville!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: First time at the Nashville location. I saw Anthony David perform. Everything was great atmosphere, service, our seats  and of course the artist! Kudos!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
how do I even begin to review the best breakfast of my life. it was so good we went back during our trip. something we never do since we want to always check out and explore everything, not do a repeat. I found this place when searching best breakfast in Nashville and I thought it'd be our first stop after we landed, picked up our rental car and headed on the gorgeous drive over. shocked to find out there was a wait on a Friday early afternoon but it was less then the 45 minutes they said it'd be. we walked around and investigated the stores plus it was a gorgeous day out so it was fine. a wait is never a bad thing, means they are doing something right! 

it was so good, so delicious we came back Monday morning! no wait since we came around 8 am this time. just as delicious as the first time. first time I ever had grits and I am now spoiled for life.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We had a lovely Sunday Brunch meal at the Loveless recently. Our server Evan was great and our meal overall was very good. We started off with their great coffee and the famous biscuits with preserves. The biscuits are light and fluffy and lived up to the hype. I opted for the blueberry pancakes and eggs and my wife had the Music City Platter which consisted of French toast, eggs and hashbrown casserole. We thoroughly enjoyed our meal and recommend this Nashville establishment.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Biscuits were phenomenal, and they keep 'em coming! Fried chicken was absolutely delicious too, though 2 pieces of the dark meat was enough for me as I still preferred the biscuits with their peach jam. Ice tea is nothing special though.

Bought peach jam to go and their biscuit mix - I'd definitely go back if I'm ever in town!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is an absolutely fantastic place! The food was amazing, and our server Owen was the best! All of his recommendations were on point, and he made us feel so welcome. I would recommend the Loveless Cafe 110%

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Southern comfort food at its best. Laid back and friendly. Great local eats. Do not pass this place up if traveling to Nashville. They are often busy so plan on waiting upwards to an hour. That said, the have corn hole on site. That's right, corn hole! Also, if they had a nice family friendly bar that would really help with the wait as well. Lastly, when you order grits ask for pimento cheese in them...you WON'T regret it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Yes, the biscuits here are consistently tasty. No one disputes this fact. But is there a biscuit on the planet that is worth a drive out to the boonies followed by a 2 hour wait to eat what is essentially a glorified, overpriced Cracker Barrel meal? I probably won't do it again, but the tourists seem to think so. Aside from the biscuits, the food and service were decent, but certainly not worth raving about.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I had some friends visiting and decided to try city winery's brunch. 1) parking is confusing 2) our server was barely present. 5 people to eat brunch took over 2 hours. Food wasn't fabulous, I had a French toast which was bland and soggy. The drinks were decent but I wish there was more variety. Probably not my go to for brunch, but enjoyed our afternoon.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The loveless cafe is a fabulous restaurant for real southern soul food. I went here for dinner and I got the Southern sampler platter with fried catfish, fried chicken, and bbq pork(my choice of 3 meats). It also came with 2 sides and I highly recommend getting the hash brown casserole and the creamed corn. The portion sizes are very large and be sure to come hungry because there are free hot biscuits with homemade jams. Personally, the peach jam is my favorite. The only downside about the loveless cafe is that there is usually about a half hour wait, but once you settle down at the table, it'll be worth the wait!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: An absolutely great place to stop and take a step back in time!!!! It takes awhile but worth the wait and there is plenty to do while you casually stroll the property!!! Creamed corn and BBQ Pork!!! Yum Y'all

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Loveless Cafe was definitely a treat, I would rate it 4 or 4.5 star. 

We arrived at the worst possible time (NOON) on a Friday. We ended up having to wait about an hour and 15 mins to get a table. It was definitely worth the wait but still a bit of a pain in the ass. You can kill time browsing the nearby Loveless Cafe shops and get a free coffee next door. 

We were giving some biscuits and preserves to start out (yum!) and I had fried chicken which was served with choice of two sides (I tried green beans and squash). The chicken was absolutely massive and I couldn't finish it. Definitely the best fried chicken I've ever had, although it's not a favorite of mine so I am no expert. 

Service was great here and the decor and ambiance are lovely. Prices were very reasonable (my meal was about $12). 

Overall very fun and satisfying experience :)

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We stumbled on this one afternoon and it didn't disappoint. Having lived in Bavaria this wasn't 100% authentic but it was close enough to satisfy. The atmosphere and staff where great too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Holy cow! This place is awesome!  The biscuits are divine!!! You might just get lucky and see a famous Nashville celeb!  We were lucky to see Alan Jackson on our last visit!  I've only ever gotten their breakfast, but it's been superb every single time!   We always stop in when in town. The atmosphere is great too!  Be sure to grab some apple butter from their store! You won't regret it!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: My husband loves German food. His lunch was great, the wait staff was friendly and attentive. The pretzel and beer cheese is a must!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Awesome crowd and a very good variety of beers. You can get a beer sampler plate with around 5 types of beers. Being and Indian, Eating here would be a hurdle as most of Indians won't eat pork and beef. But still a good place to have some beers and enjoy some live music.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Yummy! We arrived just shy of 9 am on a Saturday (July 26th).  We were on our way to drive the Natchez Trace.  They only had a 20 min wait, so we had just enough time to shop before being seated.  FYI-The wait when we were called to be seated was 45+ mins.  The biscuits were delightful.  I loved the samples of homemade jams they brought with them.  I think my favorite turned out to be strawberry, even tho they are famous for their blackberry - which we'd already purchased a jar of.  Service was quick, friendly & efficient.  Our coffee never went dry.  Our waiter was never too far, and was very helpful to the more needy couple next to us.  ;-)  I had simple scrambled eggs, and half & half bacon & sausage.  The hotel had told us about their wonderful sausage.  It was indeed very good, but one can't pass up bacon either!  The hashbrown casserole was TDF!  Tho my husband didn't like it too much.  But he was not complaining when our waiter dropped off more super fresh out of the oven biscuits.  It was a fun place to visit with very good food & we'll definitely go back if we're in the area.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: They had me at warm, soft, and FREE homemade biscuits. I got the pulled pork omelet for the sake of originality. I loved it along with my chocolate milk.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: What a treat!  We bought tickets for the amazing Marc Broussard concert on New Years Eve.  This fabulous venue includes great wines, a fun and unique menu and helpful staff.  Our concert ticket included a dinner reservation so we came an hour earlier and had dinner before the show.  Our food was great, festive and our waitress was very attentive. On a very busy New Years Eve.  The Marc Broussard concert was excellent and the City Winery venue was the perfect spot to showcase this talented band and blues singer.  The size of venue made for a fun, personable evening and great memories!   Plus we ran into Delbert McClinton in the crowd and enjoyed chatting with him as well!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Food was incredible! Jared, our waitress, was absolutely amazing. So friendly, had great recommendations and felt he truly cared about us and our experience. Cannot recommend him or the restaurant more!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Met a few friends for happy hour.  This was my second time at City Winery. The first one was Mother's Day Brunch and it was beyond amazing.  This time I had one of their specialty flatbread with shrimp and an amazing vodka sauce.  I also had the fried Brussels sprouts with feta cheese (to die for).  My wine selection was Riesling.  Our server was pretty awesome.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We had to wait an hour and a half on New Years Day but the food was well worth it. Our order came out really quickly once we were seated, the food was amazing (you have to get the biscuits) and the service was excellent.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
About 30 min outside of Nashville. Went on a weekday around 12:30pm and the wait was about 40 minutes. There were enough things on their property to roam around and purchase that 40 minutes ended up going by rather quickly. 

The service was phenomenal. Our waiter was so sweet, friendly and attentive. He must've kept refilling our drinks at least 3x that we had to kindly ask him we didn't want to keep drinking coke! Lol. The food is really good. My country fried steak was a bit salty but I ate it anyway. The ham though was the winner. They refill the biscuits so don't worry, if you want more, just ask! Be sure to walk around and purchase some souvenirs. Everyone there are so nice and overall, it was a lovely experience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I love this place. Was here years ago and still as good as ever.  Can't decide what you want to try get the Country sample, choice of three meats and 2 sides.  and of course bicuits! they may look small but they pack a mighty punch.  Delish!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is pretty good! The biscuits are amazing and so is the chicken! If you aren't too full then the desserts are heavenly as well. Every time I've come here I've had a great wait staff. To avoid the long wait come on a week day after 7pm. Everyone knows this place is good so the wait to get in can be pretty long.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Probably our favorite stop in Nashville! We went for breakfast and made reservations just in case it was really busy, but we were seated immediately so that was great. The tables all have these adorable blue and white checkered tablecloths and there's lots of light and interesting art on the walls. Our waitress came up right away and took our drink order, and was super friendly. They served the OJ in mason jars, which I love! She brought a plate of their famous homemade biscuits out with homemade blackberry, strawberry and peach jams. Those biscuits were to die for! I got pecan pancakes, bacon, and the hashbrown casserole. My husband got the pulled bbq pork with eggs, hoecakes and grits. We split a fried green tomato and pimento cheese biscuit too. The food was out of this world! The hype about this restaurant is completely true and we will be back the second we come back down to Nashville!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Coming from California and specifically the Los Angeles area it's impossible to find a good German restaurant. I was delighted to see this beer house and was impressed with the food service and the beer. It looks like a beer Hall out of Munich if you like authentic German food this is a good spot down to earth good quality.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I was shocked at how awesome the biscuits are here. Melt in your mouth kind of good. And then you add anyone of their 3 jams and then it's like a symphony in your mouth. We had the fried chicken, barbecue with 3 sides and it was all absolutely delicious. Needless to say we have a family favorite restaurant here now. #myloveless #greatfood

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Read about this lovely cafe on yelp and was not disappointed!! Loved the ambience, food, and service! I ordered the half fried chicken with mashed potatoes and mac & cheese...sooooo delicious!! Service was great!! Didn't have to ask for refills they were always ready with a new drink, super friendly, and just a great first time experience. Inside the decor is so lovely and makes you feel like you're inside someone's home..waiting as they cook you some delicious southern food! Also visited the market gift store outside and bought some goodies to take back home to Cali with me :) Hopefully we have time to come back here before we head back home! Lovedddd it :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Yummy and delicious fresh biscuits with homemade jam to start.  
   Ordered the three item sampler.  The Country Ham was a little to Salty for my taste, but I was told that is characteristic for that type of ham.  The Chicken Breast came out hot but was dry.  Now the Fried Catfish was perfect and was so good.  I highly recommend it.
     Try the Apple Crumble with Ice Cream.  It is served warm and was definitely a winner.
      Pernell-Kyle (P.K.) Sylvester of the Nashville Predators Hockey Team was there with a film crew doing some shots.  Go Predators!

name: Analog at Hutton Hotel
text: Cozy haven with exceptional vibey atmosphere. The sound crew does a great job handling sound for the room so it's a great place to catch live music. Plenty of great seating options, whether you prefer cozying up to the bar, spreading out at a table, or snuggling into a cozy booth facing the music. Great venue all the way around for intimate shows

name: Dirty Little Secret
text: This place is hot! Great music, mahalo d.j.s, management and staff keep it iNcrowd. Live band dance music has fresh deep sound. Must try to get iN when in Nashville.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Never eaten here before. The food is actually very good. Very different tastes than the normal. Food is a tad bit on the greasy side but it is good for the price. Staff is very friendly and the restaurant is set up beautifully. Would definitely recommend coming and trying it out. Don't go if your on a budget tho. $42 for two sandwiches and two teas. It's a bit pricey.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I went there last night with a group to see Johnny Swim play and it is a great venue to hear/see a band and sit down (the older I get the more I like the idea of sitting down).  The venue area is spacious but intimate and our seats were great.  

The wine selection was good and the pours were above average sized.  I didn't eat, but the food coming out of the kitchen looked and smelled great!

Valet parking is $5 and although most people valeted, the line to get the cars after the show moved quickly. 

It's a unique venue and worth going to to see a show!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I had to meet the head chef, Dennis, due to many food allergies, he had options for me and food was awesome. I would recommend this restaurant to anyone. Our waitress Erin was helpful and was knowledgeable about the food.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
First timer. Menu is very to the point and priced as you would expect for mall/tourist prices. We were seated immediately. Our first table hadn't been cleaned so the hostess promptly found another without fail.
We were very excited about this and we were not disappointed. The Kartoffelpuffer appetizer was fantastic. The wurst plates , with 2 sausages(your choice), potato salad and sauerkraut( forgot our bread, no harm no foul). Great tasting grub and not as heavy as you would think.
They were out of the beer we ordered, so that's why a 4 star rating...

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Well worth the wait. And when they say the wait is over an hour, they mean it. We visited on Sunday after the Fourth of July, which likely resulted in higher traffic levels.

The biscuits were truly amazing and they provide homemade jams. I had a spicy Bloody Mary with a shot of moonshine. I regret not selecting rum instead. The moonshine was too strong. 

The place is very touristy, and has many shops to kill time as you wait for your table. They even have a shipping center to send away things that you purchase in the shops.

If I return it'll be during off hours. Not sure I enjoy waiting that long for food.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Food was good but the pork shank got all of us sick sooooooo that kinda sucked but overall it was good. The service was great.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
"Better than sex biscuits" is not an overstatement. 

Damn, Loveless Cafe definitely has the best biscuits in town! 

The biscuits (6) came with the breakfast meal I ordered. They came with 3 different types of jams (strawberry, peach, and blueberry). After having the blackberry jam at Urban Grub, any other jam seems average to me. Initially I ordered the Breakfast Steak and 2 Eggs but they ran out of the Rib-eye (at 8:00 am!! boooo!!!), so I changed to Pit-Cooked Pork BBQ and Eggs instead. I had my eggs fried - medium and a side of hash-brown casserole. I wasn't a fan of the BBQ, however my friend loved it alot and ended up eating most of it. I never touched the hash-brown because of how cheesy it was. My fault, I should had gotten the potatoes instead. The only thing I like in this dish is the eggs, they were cooked to perfection.

My friend had the Southern Sampler Breakfast (Country Ham, Sausages, Bacon, and Red-eye gravy. The country ham was so salty that it was hard to taste anything after that. They should add this "country ham" to the hypertension risk factors list. The sausages were so dry. We tried to pour the red-eye gravy over it because we weren't sure what was the gravy for...it didn't help. I wouldn't order this. 

The portions are huge. I could barley finish half of my dish after eating all of those yummy biscuits. Breakfast for two people were more than $30, which is pretty expensive. I suggest share the platter with someone and order A La Carte on the side (for 2 people). 

I got here around 8 am and there were no waiting lines. I will be back for those heavenly biscuits and try the fried chicken next time! 

2013/#58

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: A fun atmosphere and nicely decorated for Christmas. I can imagine it can be a hoot during Oktoberfest. The food is nice and tasty. We had a giant, hot pretzel served with beer cheese and an applesauce/mustard spread which was excellent.  For the entree I had the jagerschnitzel which had a good crispy coating on a bed of spatzel cooked perfectly. The potato dumpling I got as a side was a bit dry inside and the gravy unexceptional.  My wife had the Bavarian (French) Onion Soup and enjoyed it. We finished with the desert sampler and liked all three items.  Service was friendly and prompt. The gift shop had a nice selection, but unfortunately didn't have Ritter Sport Peppermint which I wanted to pick up for a friend (they did have about 6 other flavors).

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
A wonderful destination in Nashville. The food is authentic, the bier is excellent. The atmosphere is festive. 
As one who travels often to Bavaria, Bavarian Bierhaus gets my highest reccommendation.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Let me start by saying that I am writing this as someone who didn't grow up in the south and therefore doesn't have any nostalgic feelings for southern cooking. I'm writing this primarily for people that grew up on the east coast or anywhere other than the south.

First, the good: all the food is good and the biscuits are amazing. That being said, be warned: even if you typically like butter on your biscuit, do not do it. Stick with the preserves that come with said biscuits. That combo is absolutely amazing, but the biscuits themselves are so heavy that butter really doesn't work on them.

The breakfast food is generally solid, if a little unremarkable from the perspective of someone for whom the nostalgia for southern home cooking does nothing. If you expecting a direct correlation between how endlessly busy this place is and quality of the food itself, you might be disappointing, even though it's not particularly bad.

The somewhat disappointing: having had some great BBQ in Nashville at places like Edley's, and knowing Loveless' legendary status and seeing their BBQ pit as we approached, I went in expecting to be blown away by the BBQ at Loveless but it was quite the opposite. Not bad, but not great or even memorable - just ok. Main culprit is the sauce which is just sort of average.

I'd just say that it's worth going for the biscuits and for stuff like the art gallery in the back, but My advise would be to stick to the breakfast menu (including the chicken and biscuits) and don't go in with elevated expectations due to the long lines. It is largely just ok and there are certainly better BBQ options if that is what you are looking for.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I went here on a Saturday, so it was super crowded. The wait was about 45 minutes, so my friend and I ordered carry out instead. I got the half dozen biscuits. They come with three types of jams: strawberry, apricot, and blackberry. The jams were delicious! But I think the biscuits were a little overrated. Don't get me wrong, they were good but I'm not sure if I would travel out of the city and wait 45 minutes to get them. The coffee wasn't that good, and then I found out that they have complimentary coffee in the gift shop. 

My friend got the fried chicken biscuit and the pimento cheese n fried green tomato biscuit. I had a bite of both and they were pretty good! They seem small, but they're pretty hearty.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: WOW!!  Absolutely amazing food and a fun atmosphere!!  Loved the live band and watching people try to blow the alphorn. So glad we went in!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This is a quite famous cafe at the northern end of the Natchez Trace Parkway and for good reason.

The biscuits.
The biscuits.
The biscuits.

I still think about those biscuits. Wish they'd brought us more. Wish I'd eaten mine slower. Wish my husband had visited the restroom earlier so I could have nicked one of his.

The rest of our breakfast was great, too. I enjoyed their country ham (half a slice is plenty) and the cheese grits were not to be missed.

But those biscuits tho.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Everyone told us to go to Loveless Cafe.  The food is delicious.  We each had the special of Chicken and cornbread stuffing.  If your in Nashville you have to make the trip, you won't be sorry

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Always a favorite for me!  All company I have visiting will go to Loveless after which I take them often down the Trace for a ride. Back to the Loveless, they have food for every palette of every age and culture. You will not be disappointed. Historic area with someone famous eating there most every weekend and sometimes during the week.  Great venue site for parties of any size and any occasion.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Fun spot and great food and service. Stopped in on a rainy Wednesday morning about 0800. Great coffee, biscuits, preserves, country ham, fried chicken, fried green tomatoes between the two of us.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Wow! We came for the German Christmas supper. The only thing I didn't like was that they didn't have rolling chairs and someone to roll me out to my car. From the start of the evening to the end was a great experience. The ambiance is great from the decor to the staff attire it is a welcoming and friendly environment. 
The food was great. From the pretzel we had as an appetizer to the strudel there was nothing that was not great. Roasted pork, ham, mashed potatoes pretzel stuffing, Brussels Sprouts and Red Cabbage composes the supper, and it was all amazingly good. I can't wait for my next visit, and since I joined their stein club, it will be sooner than later.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Don't know if you've eaten at the Winery for lunch recently but the menu is great, service exceptional and it's just a nice place to escape to in the middle of the day.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loved all of my food! Great atmosphere and it was cool to see pictures of all the celebrities and their autographs. Staff is also really nice!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits are definitely to die for.......the wait is far to long....the food is just ok.....i think back...back....back  in the day it was better but it is just average food at a small place with over crowded dining rooms ...the place is just tired......just to much hype....you can find much better in nashville....or you can be disappointed  and still  say you ate at the loveless cafe

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
As Tourists , someone suggested we try this place, as entertaining , with  great food  too. Well here we go again, They do have entertainment , as scheduled , ( Just Not Tonite )  anyway , we enter this massive biergarten  style plotz , The waiter " Fatjon " I kid you not, I inquired as to his nameplate,  he was very nice and made several suggestions. So I ordered the schnitzelspechzelschwine platter , along with katuffullpuffin , We enjoyed their large pretzel with a sweet style mustard, Onion soup was pretty good. But the meal, was lacking flavor, as well as the pancakes, very bland. I was not impressed. I was thinking German world in Epcot was better. Never the less, lest try the strudel. I am more accustomed to flaky strudel, not a doughy layering.
 But if ya like beer with your mediocre food, then is the place they have several varieties. You can even leave your own personal beer Stein here to boot ,

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great food and excellent service. Try to go during non-peak times to avoid lines, but it is well worth going to Loveless.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Great atmosphere, music, and wine. Service is a little slow but the food is worth the wait! Highly recommend this place for great live music and great food in one setting.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I had been to the Loveless Cafe before, but this was my husband's first visit. He was a little concerned that it was so far away from downtown Nashville, but once he got there he loved it! We made a reservation through Google maps, but still had a wait of about 15 minutes. While we were waiting I enjoyed looking at pictures of celebrities on the wall and we looked over the menu. After we were seated, MawMaw came over and greeted us and continued to provide great service during our meal. My husband got the Southern Sampler Platter and thought it was wonderful. I got the fried liver plate and I could have fed a family of four with all of the livers on my plate! Everything was absolutely delicious!
