After we had stuffed ourselves we checked out all of the shops and picked up a couple of gifts.  The Loveless Cafe will always be a stop on our trips to Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I absolutely love this Cafe!! I live in Texas and have driven cross country a couple of times and have ALWAYS made time to stop at Loveless! I found it by mistake once and it was the best accident that has ever happened. I make a trip every year and always stop to eat here. 

The different jams they make are delicious and I always buy a pack of them to take home and to gift to friends and family all over. The service is always fast and extremely friendly. The servers are so welcoming every time and are always helpful with questions or suggestions if you want to try something different. 

The food gives you that home cooked feeling. It reminds you of your childhood when grandma used to cook your favorite meal for you when you'd stay the night with her. I absolutely love and adore this restaurant and will always make it a staple in my cross country trips!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We had an absolutely wonderful time at the Bavarian bierhaus,  food and service was on point.  The entertainment was excellent and had the crowd involved.  We will be back when friends come back to Nashville. Brought back memories from my time in Munich.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is my favorite breakfast place in Nashville Tennessee! I came here five years ago and couldn't wait to get back for their homemade biscuits and jams. Really cute and fun old-fashioned ambience. Wonderful staff. JaDee was our waitress and she did a wonderful job by welcoming us nicely and bringing out the nonstop biscuits and jams and with that sweet southern hospitality brought some coffee to go for a long drive. Great place for families! Delicious food and great conversation to be had! Don't miss this place on the way to and from your destination when you go through Nashville!

name: Big Shotz
text: Dive bar with good music, but insanely understaffed. 20 minute waits for a beer. Was fun, but irritating.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Everything I imagined it would be. We had the family style breakfast and it was great, though I think we just did one go around with an extra basket of biscuits. The country ham is wonderful. People are really nice as you'd expect. It is very, VERY busy. We went on a weekday, late morning and waited about 45 minutes. The clerk in the shop next door said that wasn't too bad, sometimes it's 2 hours!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great staff, great food, and the Blue Moon is sooo good!! I recommend the catfish, fried chicken, meatloaf, mashed potatoes, and the blue moon drink (alcohol). I would give 5 stars, but I thought the ham was too tough. I usually LOVE ham, but I wasn't a fan of the ham here. Everything else was amazing. Great place to bring the family!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Well, biscuits and jam were brought to us when they sat us. That was the best part of breakfast. Scrambled eggs tasted powdered,  my 2 sausage patties were so dry and tepid I truly think they were cooked the day before....and the music pumped in was the Beach Boys........what?? At a Nashville "southern cooking" restaurant?? What a great disappointment.   And $71 for four breakfasts....yeee-ouch!!!!  Been there, done it, won't be back. Hello Waffle House?? Can you hear me....

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The city winery has a fantastic ambiance. The food and drink selection are extensive and delicious. The only caveat would be the timing. The service was friendly and engaging, however the service was unbelievably slow. Our reservation was set for 6:00pm and we did not receive our bills until 9:30 pm. I would recommend the pumpkin risotto goat cheese balls for an app and the brussels were a hit. Overall a good dining experience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Can't say enough good things about this place. The food is amazing. I've never had a bad meal here. The service is attentive and friendly. If you like BBQ you will love it. The pulled pork is probably the best I've had. 

Now as for complaints, and I wouldn't even say that it's a complaint, is the wait. Expect to be there awhile. I've never waited less than an hour. I can honestly say I believe it's worth the wait but I fully understand how this could be frustrating. What I do like is that there is plenty to do while you wait. Cute shops and lawn games definitely make the time go by. If I you have the time to spare it's worth the trip.

Fun fact. The Natchez Trace Parkway is right over by Loveless and it makes for a lovely afternoon drive.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Went for lunch during the day.


Having lived in Germany, I wasn't expecting much for a place in the mall.

Initial impression- trying to look like a fest hall/Guest House.

Seating is fest style, large tables you will share with other customers.
Atmosphere- kind of dull ( it was lunch, so no live music, but could of had some music playing)

Server- was courteous, but not very attentive.
 Drink glasses went Unfilled, did not check back to see if needed anything (or refills).

Food- I Ordered schweinebraten-rotwein., with a brotchen on the side.
Scweinbraten-rotwein was good, very moist, not over cooked.
The spatzle was like paste.
Brotchen was old, inside was as hard as outside.

Secondary impression- 50/50.
Staff was pretty "zombie" like ( going thru the motions).

Price was not unreasonable, but bordering on not worth it for what received.

Since this was my first visit, I will give benefit of the doubt. 
Maybe it was an off day.

I will try it again, and order another menu item.
Maybe Jager Schnitzel, and see how that compares to my expectations, and experiences from the past.

Did not have a beer, but did check out the selections.
I really expected more selections, at least bottle wise.

But in a bier garden in Germany, there is usually not a large selection either.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Food was good, service was great. Entertainment package is worth the $. Valet team was terrible. Couldn't help us get a cab, pretty much ignored us since we didn't have a car there.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The best breakfast/brunch in the Nashville area. The customer service was phenomenal as well. I'm in the hospitality industry and our server Mark was the best! If I'm ever in the area I will be back, also recommending this to our family and friends. You will not be disappointed!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Hands down, THE BEST food, beer and service we've had in Nashville while visiting!
Our bartender Betsy treated us like family, making sure we ordered exactly what we had in mind, and picked out the perfect beer selections for us. The Manager, Andrew, came to our table and had an actual conversation with us, not your typical "fly by" by management. Great overall experience!
Update: we loved this restaurant so much we dined there again tonight...two nights in a row! Kathleen took GREAT care of us, plus the entire staff is amazing! Food was perfect!! Thank you Andrew!!
BTW...the Apple Strudel and The Pretzel Bread Pudding is out of this world!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: New Years Eve fixed menu...kinda blah to be honest. Food was a bit tasteless. Servers were polite and accommodating and the place is tastefully decorated and beautiful.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Oh my. We are stuffed. If we die tonight it'll be from carb overdose as it was embarrassing how many biscuits we ate. This place was phenomenal. We're from Texas so we are not unfamiliar with delicious southern cooking but this was good stuff! Our waitress, Virginia, was so friendly and the epitome of a sweet southern girl. I had the bbq pork plate with cream corn and mashed potatoes. The pork was delicious. The bbq sauce was a little sweet for my taste but that's a regional preference. The cream corn was delicious and reminded me of my grandmother's! He had the fried pork chops and eggs. The chops were perfectly crispy and hot out of the grease when they arrived! We even had a side of sausage gravy to eat with our biscuits. The gravy was great and they weren't stingy with it either, which is always our biggest complaint with restaurants and gravy. Overall, it was all delicious. I wish we would have saved room to try the pie but there were just so many biscuits.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
From this point forward all other country cooking is forever put to shame!
Catfish = about the best I ever had
Green beans = best ever
Turnup greens = as good as ever had
Buscuits and jams= as good as ever had
Meatloaf= excellent 
Pecan pie= best ever
And yes I ate all the above! And then some!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
This place has the potential to be a great spot in Nashville. It's lacking in customer service and food menu, but with changes made I think I would come back.

There is a nice amount of parking out front, as well as street parking. There is a beautiful outdoor dining area, that is dog friendly, and has a mini golf setup. Inside there's plenty of seating, from booths and tables to bar seats and couches. 

We had to approach the bartender, as there were no servers walking around, and no menus visible. I was expecting more from the menu, it didn't really compliment your typical wine dining menu. 

My friend ordered a salad and I ordered the burrata. The salad did not look very good or fresh at all. The burrata was pleasant, though they were heavyyy on the balsamic. There was no music, it was kind of a dead space but could turn into a great brunch space or event space with some changes!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We live close to this legendary restaurant!  We are lucky to be able to visit often and even order to go!  For locals, this is the best option for busy families. 
We've invited friends from out of town to eat with us at Loveless. All meals are fantastic!  Be sure to arrive early during peak times as it can get very busy. It's so worth it!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Adding the fifth star after today's lunch.  Service was top notch, with a big thanks to our server Alesha, and the food was delicious across the board.  Rouladen was enjoyed by several in our party and personally I really appreciated Bob's prior response on Yelp about how they prepare that dish.  Great beer selection and definitely will be back in the future for the earlier morning Bayern games.

name: Big Shotz
text: We came, we danced, they held my ID hostage... My cousin plays in the band here so I hesitate to leave a negative review, but I have to let y'all know what this place is about. We ordered $35 worth of drinks every round about 4 times in a row. When I was ready to slow down, I went to the bar and ordered an Angry Orchard. She delivered the bottle and then informed me she couldn't close a tab under $15. "Oh, but I've spent over $100 already." Doesn't matter. Her manager came around and gave me more sass than I've ever been given in a professional establishment (and you know I love some sass, but like... not when you're the manager of a bar). Y'all. I had to buy two more drinks as we waited for our Uber in order to get my freaking ID back which was being held hostage. When the manager could have shown maturity she showed hostility. Can't recommend this place with a good conscience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I was in Nashville for a business trip. Something big was happening so I ended up staying out near the airport. I was with a co-worker. I was looking through the Interwebs looking for someplace interesting with Southern comfort food to eat at. Loveless Cafe kept coming up as a place we had to go. OTOH, it had every sign of being full on tourist trap. Finally, the positive reviews won out.
Driving in continued to screen tourist trap. Spending a short time in the waiting room screamed tourist trap.
Fortunately, the food didn't.
We had an excellent meal. I'm nor normally a biscuit guy, but these really are nice with some butter and jam. The dishes we tried were pretty much perfect, and the pie lived up to billing. The only thing that didn't wow me was the moonshine. It was just a bit too sweet and smooth. It tasted a lot like Dutch Genever. That's hardly much of a quibble.
Even though it's a big place, it didn't feel overly large and our server was a nice, earnest, young man.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I was so looking forward to loving this place- but sadly, no. 
And I was so looking forward to seeing one of my favorite bands- Toad the Wet Sprocket. Again, sadly no.
This was my experience:

1. Bought VIP balcony tix $60. Seemed reasonable at the time, now I feel dirty. 

2. Ordered the $15 burger. Asked for it medium rare, came out medium well. Tasted more like a $5 burger. Couldn't talk to our server about it because he was busy with other tables. Only ate it because I was starving.

3. The band comes on stage after the the opener- the opener dude was good especially if you like hearing the same sad song over and over again. He was however, funny between songs- whatever he said because the audience on the floor laughed. 

4. Toad takes the stage. Expectations high. Unfortunately, I was highly disappointed. The sound/acoustics sucked. And maybe it's because I was in the VIP balcony seats- it was very difficult to hear and understand the vocals. The band was too loud and the vocals were buried. 

5. Toad played a lot of their new stuff off their new album. Not a lot of the stuff that made them famous. I was surprised at the lack of their older and more popular music they DIDN'T play. 

6. Because of this experience, I probably will not eat or see another show at City Winery for a long while and Toad has broken my heart. I left feeling empty (crappy burger) and not just in my stomach and wallet- my heart as well. I spoke to a few others standing in the valet line and they agreed. They didn't play nearly enough of their older stuff.   

It hurts me to write this, but $60 on tickets and $50 dinner (burger, two glasses of wine + tip) and I feel dirty. I took tonight off from work for this. Not worth it what so ever. Not at all. Essentially I lost money.

Good bye and good night Toad the Wet Sprocket and City Winery. You both were a HUGE disappointment.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: You got a problem with fried chicken, country ham and biscuits done flawlessly? Yeah, well I got a problem with YOU.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This place is super unexpected in Nashville, a real honest German hoedown in the middle of Tennessee. The beer is awesome, it's actual legit important Bavarian beer and I loved the Hef and Oktoberfest. I've been here for a special event and at the bar just for drinks. The food is decent, I'm not the biggest on German food but the pretzels are super good and huge. The live music is great and on a busy night it really feels like you're in European Beer Hall. This is not somewhere I'd go just for food or drinks unless I was really craving the whole experience, or happens to be at Opry Mills and craved a beer. But it is fun and the staff is great, I'd give the overall experience 4.5 stars.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Coming from Toronto this restaurant provided a lot of firsts for us. Biscuits, grits, fried green tomatoes, moonshine, barbecue, and hash brown casserole were great ( well to be honest we each only took a sip of the blueberry moonshine and that was enough!) but we loved the food and loved the experience. The drive back to Nashville was amazing along the Natchez Trail. We will return when we are lucky enough to come back to Nashville.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I haven't been to Germany or an actual German Bierhaus but this seemed as authentic as I could imagine. My fiance & I watch a lot of Travel Channel & Food Network & we've watched a lot of episodes featuring German Restaurants & famous German dishes. 

It was very hard to choose what we wanted to eat - Käsespäzle, Jägerschnitzel, Schweinbraten or a Giant Pretzel?! We ended up ordering the Bierhaus Wurstteller ($21) -
Oktoberfest Brat, Smoked Brat, Weisswurst, Red cabbage, Sauerkraut & Bread dumpling. We were going to order the Jägerschnitzel but we were soo full of the brats & beer we didn't. The brats were soooooooo good - I honestly wish I could just eat this dish every single day.
Oh & their dijon mustard on their table was also sooooo amazing - I literally dipped everything in it.

If you're in the area or at the mall, this place is a MUST! Happy Eating!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I am a regular at City Winery.  Their show selection keeps me coming back time and time again.  In the past few months, I have seen a rock show, an acoustic show, a band I loved in the 80s, a funk show, and attended a wine tasting.  
I have a few reasons why this is one of my favorite venues in town.
1-valet parking right in front (7$) but free for VinoFile members, which is their annual fee membership club. Parking at many music clubs in Nashville can be a pain, to say the least.
2-seated! If you have a ticket, you have a reserved seat (unless otherwise noted for the occasional standing room only show.)
3-upscale dining.  The chef does a great job with seasonal ingredients.
4-shhhhhhh You can actually hear the artist as most patrons respectfully keep their chatter down.  That being said, of course their are exceptions depending on the type of show
5-they are actually a winery, and their locally produced offerings are on par with higher end wineries from notable winemaking areas
6-its just plain cool
If you are coming to town, check their show schedule.
If you live in town, check their show schedule.
City Winery is a dining and music jewel in a city that's got lots of gems... but this one ranks up near the top for me.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Loveless Cafe is a Nashville icon. They are so good and have branded themselves so well that tourists and locals drive to the outskirts of Davidson County to eat here! 
My family loves this place and it has become a frequent request when they come into town. The portions are very large and we always have leftovers. 
I think they are best known for their biscuits and they are extra special to me because my grandma use to make similar biscuits that she'd cut out with an old tin snuff can. I've never been able to replicate them. Loveless does a pretty excellent job of it. 
Their pork is also delicious! They give you so much, it's nuts! The menu has many options of country comfort food.
Be prepared to wait, the line is always long but it goes by quick because there are lots of things to do on the grounds of the Loveless Cafe complex. There are cute shops, corn hole, Benches to relax on. It's a lovely place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If you want genuine southern food, definitely come here. Being from Massachusetts my family and I aren't really used to this southern food but it was very delicious. They said the wait would be 25 minutes and it was 10 at the most. While you are waiting you are free to walk around the property and explore. The food was truly southern and the staff was attentive and friendly. When we accidentally dropped out pie out of the to-go container in the bathroom, there just happened to be a worker in the bathroom and she ran to get us another pie. Great food and great staff!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is amazing! The biscuits with their jams were fantastic. We ordered cooked-in pork and fried chicken. Well done! The pork was shredded and surprisingly not as oily as I thought it would be.. maybe because it didn't have a lot of fat. It was served over pancakes which were cooked very good! The fried chicken was one of the best I ever had. There was something different in their breading. :) Their mac and cheese was also creamy -- very nice! Cheese melted and coated over the pasta the way I liked it. Creamy corn is also a recommendation for the side. Apple pie for dessert was also quite heavenly. Will come back. :) What a great intro to Southern food!

name: Analog at Hutton Hotel
text: Amazing spot that people need to know about!! The renovation that has happened in Hutton Hotel is spectacular and Analog is beautiful! We were able to go during one of the shows and the sound was great and there isn't a bad seat in the whole place! We snagged a table and the service was very attentive and prompt even though the place was really busy! The bar ended up having a slight computer problem but they were able to get it back up and running in no time, which was really impressive that they handled it so professionally. The drinks are really delicious!! I got one of the cocktails with ginger beer, which is on tap and it is a spicy ginger beer, which I love!! Really great experience and I can totally see myself becoming a regular at Analog!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The trek out to Loveless Cafe from Nashville is so worth it! We came out here to try the biscuits and were amazed by the scenic drive and the bucolic setting for the Loveless Cafe. I felt like I had stepped into a time warp where motels were the epitome of charming places to stay with your family and hang out all day. 

They had a restaurant, a small gift shop, and BBQ. We got here for a late breakfast and were charmed by the ambience. They also served their famous biscuits with three types of jam! It was a great experience for breakfast. Very filling and way better than the typical diner food. 

Service was fantastic and full of Southern hospitality. It being a hot day, the server also offered to give us water for the road. So thoughtful and it made me love the experience of eating at Loveless even more. I brought home some biscuit mix from the gift shop, too!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
*Review is for the wine and light bite pairing class only*

My friend and I had both never been to City Winery and decided to check it out when we read the description of a wine and light bite paring class which sounded quite frankly, absolutely delightful. The event listing was a "Wine and Picnic Pairing" with the Beverage Director 
 of City Winery Jenelle Engleson. She pairs local wines with a menu specially created by the one of the chefs. The theme was supposed to showcase how wine and food can be paired for outdoor events/activities. 

We arrived a little bit early and there wasn't really anywhere to wait before the group was to go into the dining room for tasting class. My friend and I just stood in the lobby before it was time and looked around the venue. There was a concert that night so people were filing into the room for the show. Their restaurant is to the left when you walk in and is an open and exposed area but upscale. They have a patio outside connected to their restaurant. 

When it was time to do the class we were lead back and upon entering each handed a glass of sparkling wine to kick off the event. There was a long rectangular table in the middle of this pretty dining room that was set with burlap and candles and each place setting had five full classes of wine plus a couple of empty wine glasses, two complimentary tickets to an upcoming music show of your choice and a review paper and pen. We could sit wherever we wanted and it was a communal experience so you could introduce yourself to the people sitting next to you. 

When we got started Jenelle introduced herself and the chef who designed the menu. They had a station setup for all the treats and they did an introduction where the chef described each food we were about to eat and then the group could ask him questions. The menu consisted of a curried chicken salad in a tart (my favorite), potato salad inside the skin, a BLT skewer and a yogurt parfait. Although all the food was incredibly and although it was marketed as "small bites" this was enough for me to have for dinner and be okay. 

During the wine and picnic pairings I had an epiphany. This was the first time where I actually really realized that the right wine does bring out the flavors in the food. It was so incredible. For example, I took a bite of the chicken salad tart and the wine that she paired with it. Then she told us to take a sip of this sparkling wine that she said also went well and the flavor suddenly changed. I thought that wine pairing was kind of just this fantasy idea of a way to sell you alcohol but it actually really enhances the dining experience. I was so glad I did this class! 

I cannot say enough great things about Jenelle. She was knowledgeable and made learning about the wines approachable for someone like me who really just knows the basics. I ended up buying a bottle of the wine I liked and she brought it right over to me and was very nice and friendly. 

Overall, so worth the $30! My friend and I plan on doing more of her classes. I also cannot wait to use the complimentary ticket passes to come back and see a show here!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This was just okay. I waited an hour and 10 minutes to be seated, which I don't have a problem with had the food been as amazing as I had heard. I ordered the chicken & waffles, which came with biscuits also.  The biscuits were delicious - light, soft and the homemade jam was a nice addition.  The chicken and waffles was pretty sad though. The chicken was extremely dry and the waffle was something I could have made at home. This was a very disappointing visit. I can get better at a local dive diner here in Pittsburgh.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
The building is beautiful and has a wonderful ambience which places you in the movie watching mood. There are all your standard movie theatre fare served and a bar.

No matter what your favorite style of film (cult classics, documentaries, foreign films, and movies you will see nowhere else) they will be playing here.

I absolutely love The Belcourt Theatre!  

Go once, I am positive that you will be hooked!

name: Drifters
text:
If I wrote this after my first visit, I think it would have been a five star review.  I think Drifters has potential to be a four star joint but it's uneven in presentation and the food.

Pros:
Service - fast, friendly, and funny
Fried pickles!
Amazing Happy hour prices and duration
Outdoor seating
Ping pong tables and a friendly ping pong league
Local beer on draft
Wonderful Vegan and Vegetarian options

Cons:
BBQ - I've had the sampler plate several times and like the sausage and ribs but the pulled pork and brisket are just ok.
BBQ Sauces - Not really a huge fan of any of them.  Not terrible but not great
Hush puppies - just ok.  Perhaps since we're so far from an ocean but they're not worth ordering

We've been a bunch and I might return but it's more for the location, service, and prices rather than the BBQ.

name: Drifters
text:
I really expected more from Drifters just by the reviews I read so I was a little disappointed. The fries are delicious, the nachos are good the tortilla chips are just a little over cooked for my liking. That's preference though. Overall it's a decent place and being a bar it's open until 3am so if I ever need fries late, this place has my back.
If you're into bbq definitely come and try theirs. That's obviously the biggest thing here, being a vegetarian I didn't try much, I'm also the worst pickiest person alive. My sisters boyfriend loved it and all the different bbq sauce options they have. The queso is really good I definitely recommend. Parking all around that's free or cheap. Would recommend eating outside because once it gets busy it's super cramped.

name: The Family Wash
text: Enjoyed a few beers at this eclectic place while listening to great live music. Food looked awesome, although we didn't have anything to eat, and bartender was super friendly. Would love to go back and try something the veg pie !

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: This is my favorite place in Nashville. I like the popcorn and membership is a great deal. I have been sold out more times in the last six months than the previous six years. New Nashville means lots of independent film lovers, I guess.  Still, go to The Belcourt! As a bonus, i once saw the Mayor seeing a matinee in pajamas here.

name: Drifters
text: Ahh, Drifters. I will start off by saying that the BBQ is only mediocre and overpriced. However, it is good enough to serve as good drunk food when the opportunity creates itself. This place is not about the food, it is about the people and moderately priced booze. Plus, they feature great music in their outdoor space on weekend nights. While Drifters has a fairly large group of employees who tend bar throughout the week, they are all the kindest and most attentive that you will find anywhere in East Nashville. The same goes for the clientele-everyone I've come across at this place is very nice, interesting, and not stuffy (which can be an issue at times at other East Nashville joints). Bottom line-when you're at Drifters, you feel at home. Great drinks, great people, and your tab won't break the bank.

name: The Family Wash
text: I was excited to try the Family Wash as I love me some chicken pot pie and live music. The scent of thyme had my mouth watering as we sipped beers and waited. I loved the vibe of the place-very intimate and eclectic-but alas, I was not wowed by the pot pie. The crust was simply a round of puff pastry, and the filling bland -not even close to the yumminess of a homemade pot pie. My hubs had the bangers and mash, which he thought was tasty, but overpriced for the amount of meat he received. Overall, if going for the live music, it may be worth it, but next time, I'll stick to drinks. Service was good.

name: Drifters
text: friendly, upbeat, attractive staff with healthy skin and smiles.   good service and great tunes on the speakers.  not too loud and not too quiet.  some football too on the screens.  haven't tried the food but id be willing to bet it's out of this world.  exposed rafters are a classy touch, with a fully exposed HVAC system sitting pretty up there too, with nothing to hide.  I think this is my new favorite bar.  can't wait to try the food.  I hope it's served in disposable containers, even if I order it for here.  namaste!

name: Drifters
text: I was only in Nashville for a night, and I'm so glad we chose to eat at Drifters.  I'm a vegetarian so I was super excited to see I could get a tofu bbq sandwich!  My boyfriend ordered the brisket and was also very satisfied. We were there on a Monday, so although there wasn't any live music (we went to Broadway for that anyway) it was trivia night.  We had never done trivia before, and the host was so nice and we had a lot of fun.  I would definitely recommend it!

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
I attended an event at One event space at Cannery and had an amazing time. It is the third floor of the Cannery Ballroom. 

Pros: wide open space. Definitely room to play and host any type of event. There is a smaller room off to the side that can host a bar and some high top tables. There is an elevator and stairs to the venue. I don't know what the venue provides, but it appeared to have limited restrictions on decorations. 

Cons: there is no patio. Only a small stairwell for those who need some fresh air. There were several events also occurring that night throughout the building and the signage was terrible. The lines were a mess and we had no idea where to go. 

Overall, it was a great place to attend an event. I don't have knowledge of prices. I would suggest looking into it for an event. The capacity is 400!

name: Drifters
text: Excellent beer selection. The half chicken and ribs looked amazing. Was not in the mood to eat, but if I did THAT is what I would have ordered. They have ping-pong and cornhole. Great outdoor seating.

name: Springwater
text:
How could I have not written about ANY of my visits to this place!

I fully agree... this is the BEST Dive Bar in Nashville.  
That said, Nashville's not my favorite city.  
The whole town's a little too clean and flashy AND worst of all,
way too 'Country'-fied for my 'Big Easy' Gimmie- the-P-funk desires. 

When we first went (2008), the Springwater only opened at 4 pm. 
SO, in my vast knowledge of 'Dive Bar',  I truly felt they where cheating. 

As y'all know I take this genre very seriously!  I am very happy to report #1, because I just noticed they now have a website and #2, my Annual, Nashville, Birthday Bar-Hopping Bash is next month... they now open at Noon!

This place is cool and dirty. 
I have never failed to have . . . 
a great time, good conversation or low bar-tab when visiting.
(*I do believe they are cash only, pay as you go) 

GO!

name: Drifters
text: Three stars. BECAUSE of the service. Beer was good, ambiance was good, food was good, service was horrible. We have been driving all day from Texas, we wanted somewhere to hang out an relax. Our waitress was rude, it took us a while before we got any service, though the joint was almost empty besides the bar area which the bartender was taking care of. I would have given more stars if my waitress wasn't so rude.

name: Drifters
text:
2.5/5

I was passing through on a road trip, thought to check it out for dinner.
The atmosphere is charming but the brisket was drrrrryyyyy and I had to smother that sucker in so much sauce to get a sense of flavor. Waitress was lovely and the blues band was great.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
1) no chairs.
2) speakers aren't hung so sound will travel to the back of the room. speakers seem to be closer to the stage and sound does not travel to the entrance of the room.
3) no chairs.
4) A line that first begins outside the chain link fence, outside the property?  Really?


I was the second person that walked into the ballroom and I went directly to the stage.  Had read reviews and determined that the front stage area would be the best observation deck.
Wrong.
People began squishing me in and crowding me so tightly, I got nauseous.  No air ventilation. I began sweating. Rocking..  
I had to find some air.
I left the front of the stage and wandered over by the bar, by the bathroom hallway.
The lights went down, people were swaying, sitting on the floor, against the wall, some were crammed in the window sills, trying to take a load off their swollen feet...

I found air and a seat in a window sill. Two other people came along and begged to share the window sill with me.

The music began, but none of us wanted to leave the window sill.  So we sat together and listened to the band, in the other room.

Face it, this venue is highly restrictive.  If you need to sit, if you can't stand people crowding you, and you have to sit in a window sill, just to sit down....  
I don't think you're going to be very happy.

Music?  Honestly, I can't remember.  Sound?  Muffled from the other room.
Temperature?  As long as you're not in the crowd, it's nice.. I felt the A/C working.
Bathrooms?  Never got a chance to see them.
Staff?  Never conversed with any of them.

No matter how much I love music, and no matter how much I would travel to the ends of the earth to see my favorite band perform... I would not return here.
Not unless they got some chairs for us to sit and enjoy the bands performing.

DO NOT WEAR HEELS.

name: The Country
text: Loved this place!! Came by on a Friday night after dinner to check out some music. Once we were convinced by the music we stayed for a while and got great drinks and even some delicious peanut butter pie. We stayed for 2 sets and both were amazing! The place itself is also super cool. The only downsides were service wasn't too great and it seemed a bit quiet for a Friday night, but we enjoyed ourselves anyway!

name: Drifters
text: Prestiegelöst lokal honky tonk bar med avslappnad stämning, kall öl och god mat. Hipster vibbar existerar inte här. Kom som du är, blandad publik. Vänlig personal som hjälper dig gärna, eller bara pratar bort en liten stund om de har tid. Jag blev t.ex. till min BBQ-rätt erbjuden ett par kryddstarka BBQ såser som inte fanns framme i den vanliga sortimentet på borden (där fanns det 3 stycken att välja emellan). Han som serverade mig frågade om jag skulle vilja pröva några starkare varianter och skyndade in i köket och kom ut med 2 behållare med söt/stark resp. stark/stark BBQ-såser.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: The worst restaurant experience of my life. We waited over 2 hours for brunch that came out ice cold. Tables who came in and ordered after us were served before. The server was fine but manager could care less that we had a poor experience and would not offer to make our experience better in any way. Would not recommend ever and if you're on any type of time crunch absolutely do not stop in.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: The Cannery Ballroom gets great shows.  That's hard to deny.  And the prices are good--both in terms of tickets and not unreasonable at the bar.  People complain that the stage is in the corner, but I personally don't think it matters (There are bad seats (aka those to the side) when the stage is in the middle of a rectangular room too).  The warehouse-like feel is also really cool--modern as opposed to honkey tonk.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: I've been to Cannery a few times and each time has been a good experience. One huge plus is the parking lot that is adjacent to the building. Parking is $5 and I don't have to walk a mile in the dark to the venue. The room is huge and I don't feel claustrophobic in there. The bar is pretty big and has always been well staffed when I've been there, so getting a drink isn't that hard. The stage and the lights are great and they book some great shows there.

name: EXIT/IN
text: Love this venue, my favorite band Paper Route only plays this venue when they are in town, which makes it great. Very nice small place which makes shows much more intimate. Really enjoy this place and wouldn't miss a show here for the world.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Great place for artsy movies. You won't find any mainstream movies here! I'd recommend seeing a movie during the week or daytime if possible. It's close to Vanderbilt and in a busy area. Parking is extremely limited. Staff were friendly and helpful. It's somewhere that I would go back to, but only for a matinee during the week.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: This bar is one of my favorite bars, ever! Great service, awesome prices, delicious food. The bartenders were eager to help you with your order. Security even held the door for anyone walking in or out. I will definitely be going back!

name: EXIT/IN
text: Saw an artist named matt Sperrazza past Thursday.   He was one of the best acts I've ever seen.  Def coming back.

name: The Bowery Vault
text: This place is amazing! Came across it while visiting Nashville. They are hidden in the building behind Mickhey's Tavern. Such a cool place. They have great vintage rock and roll gear and an amazing stage with full back line. Was blown away by this place, never seen anything like it even in LA. MUST GO and experience! Vero and Emily who run this place are badass!

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Would've given 1 star, but 2 stars because they have bottomless mimosas, bloody Mary's, and service was good. Honestly, the hash browns were just a sorry excuse for French fries. They were totally tasteless and unseasoned. The "cream cheese grits" were actually grits mixed with cheddar cheese, bacon, and peppers from what we could taste. Overall, not a fan. Not coming back

name: The Local
text: Great neighborhood pub. Bartender Tyler took great care of use. Cocktails had a great mix. Appetizers were good. New place with nice decor. Definitely will be back.

name: Drifters
text: We picked this place on a whim because we wanted to replace the bad taste of our last rib experience elsewhere. Our bar tenders Kellen and Matthew were attentive, friendly and made great suggestions for both food and drinks. The ribs, fried pickles, hush puppies and pulled pork chimichanga were outstanding. We had a great time and we'll definitely be back.

name: Drifters
text: Trying to find a meal to appease both a vegan and a person that will eat any animal walking is always a tough challenge.  Look for further, Drifters is the place to be!  I didn't expect any greatness considering it's a BBQ joint and they had a tofu sandwich as an option.  Boy, was I wrong!  First off, being able to eat fried pickles that do not have milk or eggs is a real treat for me and I am glad these were the ones I was able to eat.  They were so damn good!!!!  The tofu sandwich had that same nice, thick and flavorful breading on it making it a super amazing sandwich.   I was super impressed with them and hope to return there again if my travels ever take me back to Nashville.

name: Drifters
text: Great food.....great service.  Very friendly atmosphere.  Marie behind the bar is the best!!!!

name: The Country
text:
Love this bar. Great draft beer selection with fairly consistent rotation of certain handles. Attentive bartenders. Only tried one sandwich (All Nighter I think it was called), but it was great.

Live music most nights which can be a little overbearing. Outdoor patio seems like it will be great in warm weather.

name: The Family Wash
text: I would actually give this place 5 stars for the shepherd pies because they are awesome.  I'm giving this poor review solely based on the service, which always sucks.  Every time I've been here (I'm done BTW) everyone from the hostess, the wait staff and even the manager have been snotty and rude.  I keep going back for the food and hoping things have changed or gotten better, and this last trip will be my last.

name: Drifters
text: I consider myself a serious foodie, so I was surprised to find that this place was just awesome. Cool vibe, easygoing, service was super friendly and attentive yet not clingy. Ribs and smoked wings were excellent! Maybe a little too smoked, but still juicy with an awesome caramelly thick crust. Ooh, the hickory flavor! So good! Sauce choices were varied and spectacular- perfect since I'm not a big fan of sweet sauces. Sauerkraut and cold slaw were excellent. The music was great, too.

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
An excellent venue for music and other cool events for all the hip artists of Nashville! Good looking people and great sound systems they have in place. Makes the band experience exactly what it should be.

The small Parkin lot gets full fast. Don't pay for the other lot, parallel park on the well lit Palmer PL which is one street over & save a few $

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
Parking was very close to the building and only 5$. Security was fine. They did their job. They offer canned beer inside. Bathrooms are clean. I like not having seats, yet I think I'm getting to old not to have seats, if that makes sense. My feet started hurting towards the end. It also became very apparent to me that all those times I pretended to be looking for someone at the front....no one fell for it. Being 5'1", that got old real quick last night. I recommend locking arms with your party and ignore them and their excuses about why they need to cut in front of you. But the group that did it to us got kicked out for lighting up. Just because someone sings about weed, doesn't mean you can light it up right in front of security, dumb@$$es. So, seeing karma served on a plate right in front of you is always fun.
All in all, great experience. Pretty venue inside!

name: Commodore Grille
text: Live music was good service was trash drinks were just as bad. Don't know if it has to do with being the only Spanish and black person in the restaurant but our service looked at us for a good 20min before come over asking us if we were good and walked away before we could answer. Then when she comes back to take our order finally she starts taking the order of the table next to us at the same time pretty much ignoring us. Folks who sat down 20mins after us get their drink while we wait. When drink finally come they taste horrible and she brings the wrong beer. That one star is for the singers they were great. The server was Cindi and we was also extremely rude

name: Drifters
text: Went to this place based on reviews. Some what of a slow night, with practically everyone on the porch for the live music. Still not very busy. Service was the worst. Server even said at one point, "is there anything else I can get you at one time because I'm running back and forth a lot". Ummmmm it's your job. Food was mediocre at best. Would not recommend. 2 stars only because the baked beans were awesome.

name: Springwater
text: A delightful dive bar. Complete with mildly aggressive bouncer, poorly felted pool table and awkward punk band playing in the back. I'd return at some point.

name: The Local
text:
This bar.. oh this bar. It has so much potential; the patio is BEAUTIFUL. The inside is fine.. it's nice. No hard feelings toward it. They serve an assortment of beer, which is beautiful. The food is also good. I have no qualms with it

BUT. It's too damn loud... EVERYWHERE. I have a hard time talking to my friends outside from the farthest point away from the music

Sometimes there are random nights that they are hosting events and it's 10-20 dollars to get in and it doesn't feel like a "local joint." 

This bar could be good but feels mismanaged and trying to be something they are not.. they could just be a great local bar with live music to get a beer out that doesn't make you deaf.

name: Springwater
text:
This is the only "dive bar" where one can drink a Pabst for $2, while sitting outside on a new smoke-free porch and view the Parthenon. 

Assuming the latter the greatest architectural achievement of the ancient world, there is a certain 'frisson' as the French would say that the lowest of low places, to quote Garth Brooks, in the city where 'low places' bring millions to folks who compete for trashy women, drunks in pick up trucks, etc,  and all are commandeered by a funny looking old man who endowed a University, Vanderbilt,  which is finally winning football games, by hiring a black coach.

 At a buck a toss on the JUKE BOX, one can get the greatest range of music selections one desires, from Brooks, to Bob Dylan, to Miranda Lambert, to Rolling Stones, and even the latest from Loretta Lynn, if you really want to go that far back

. Younger writers have mentioned bands, and I've heard there's JAZZ on Sunday, sometime,and junky bathrooms, and friendly wait staff,  but the biggest attraction of the place is its HUGE parking lot, covered with gravel, which reminds me of the days when I first started my research on DIVE BARS, in the state where they were INVENTED. LOUISIANA.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: I'm a member and It's nice to have a theater in this town that shows independent movies but the headache of actually trying to get a parking spot in that tiny convoluted parking lot and end up having to pay metered parking at the lot below that does not always work and then finally getting through the 15 min concession line only to find out that they oversold the movie and there's not a single available seat left is not worth it any more. One or twice, OK but it's like this Every. Single. Weekend. My husband already cancelled his membership. I might have to, too. Not worth the stress.

name: EXIT/IN
text:
The rudest door staff/ security I've ever encountered. Spent more time talking with each other than anything, and then ignorantly kicked out a whole group of people who had been in line to pay for merchandise since the show had ended, claiming that he'd already said something when that wasn't the case. Another staff member chimed in to accuse our group of also being racist as a joke with each other, while talking over our attempt to tell them we'd been waiting patiently with money in hand.  Bar staff also didn't seem to know what they were doing. Had to explain the description of a well known drink, and both times I received it, there was a huge difference in the amount of alcohol served... 
I can get over the long wait time to get in and the inconsistent cocktails, but the staff there has no right to talk down to it's paying customers solely out of arrogance and I will not be returning unless there is a staff change.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Security guards were so helpful and went above and beyond my handicapped sister and I!! So grateful for how wonderful our experience was !

name: The Local
text:
Umm, can I get an Amen for The Local!? It is a perfect spot for a casual date, meetup with pals or solo hangout. There is absolutely no reason there should ever be an empty seat here. The happy hour specials are terrific, the peer selection is awesome and the food is top-notch (in a dive bar kind of way). Those fries are the stuff that fluffy, potato-loving dreams are made of!! 

But, in the fair Music City, I must also draw attention to the fact that this is one of my favorite places to listen to local, up-and-coming acts perform. The space is intimate, and yet with the gorgeous patio you don't feel penned in. I love that I can listen to the live tunes even if I decide to grab some fresh air outside. 

Are you coming to a Vandy game? Tailgate here! Are you seeking shelter after a sunny day at Centennial? Chill here! Are you bored with the blah food options on West End? Seek refuge in a burger here! Are you missing your college days but can't stand to go to a college bar? Grab a brew here!

Honestly, The Local checks every box!

name: The Bowery Vault
text:
We were visiting Nashville for the weekend and found out about the Bowery Vault from a friend that lives in town. Really glad to have gotten the recommendation, as this turned out to be one of our favorite spots in Nashville. It's super interesting (local artists, beer, vintage fashion, and even a selection of cassettes!) and really authentic. Really got to feel the local experience as opposed to a lot of the more tourist-y areas in town.
The owners were super friendly, and we quickly made friends with some of the other regulars. Really wish we had more time to swing by more!

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
I've seen a prior review mentioned it being in a "bad area" and I have no no no clue what they're talking about.  It's perfectly fine.  And it's within close proximity to the convention center and a less than 10 minute walk to the broadway party district.  

Very cute place.  Great servers.  But it got HOTTER THAN BLAZES by the time the show started, the A/C system is apparently not designed to keep up with the heat generated by the crowds.  

And also, I don't know how they haven't been sued b/c they have loose rugs (with no sticky backing) laying around the place and I tripped TWICE on these things that were all bunched up and almost killed myself (didn't see them with a crowd of people around me).  I don't know how someone hasn't got injured on them yet!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Not a fan of the tip "shake down" as the singer stuck his collection drum in our face as he paraded the room begging for cash because "Honky Tonk don't pay us". Well, we all know by now that no bar pays their bands but every other music club we visited had a jar discretely placed on the stage....and we know what it is for if we like your music.

name: Alley Taps
text: Excellent new bar in Printers Alley...great atmosphere in a very unique location. Small food bites and very friendly patrons!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: This place is a great music venue, and a good place for drinks, although a bit on the pricey side. However, I do not recommend eating here. I ordered the cheeseburger and fries, and my 2 friends ordered the patty melt. After 30 mins of waiting, the food finally can out.  The meat tasted like dog food. There was a funny flavor, and I think it gave me food poisoning! The only redeeming part was the fries, and you know those are frozen. The same went for the patty melts. All in all, stick to beer and wine, or fries. The mixed drinks are weak and you'll have to order a lot to taste anything.

name: The Station Inn
text:
Perfect place to hear some authentic bluegrass picken away from the noisy mega-honky tonks downtown. Intimate venue with no smoke smell that is much more family friendly (at least for teens) than anywhere else we went - the focus is on the music and not the drinking. It was absolutely perfect for what we wanted to do, give our music crazy 16 yo a night on the town.

The owner plays a stand up bass and emcees when he and his buddies play and it's obvious they are having a blast. They book other acts and the cover varies depending on who's playing but we thought the "house band", who also play Sunday's for bluegrass night, were amazing.

Prices were reasonable and the food is decent comfort food - the pimento cheese is especially good though. Overall the perfect place for anyone looking for great music and friendly atmosphere.

name: Nashville Underground
text: This place is amazing! Everything from the wings, Mac and cheese, ribs, and YES the banana pudding!

name: The Station Inn
text: Picture some of the best music you have ever heard in a VFW hall. With folding chairs and all. We went for the 9:00 show and saw Heather and Shannon Slaughter. Their music was amazing. In any other city you would have had to get tickets in advance and paid twice as much. If you are visiting Nashville stop by and for sure you will hear a great night of music.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: This is a really good venue.  It has easy access to the interstate just off the Shelby Ave exit ramp and over the bridge.  There's parking nearby and if you use www.parkwhiz.com you can get great parking a block away for $5 or $6.  The facility is nice as is the layout of things.  The box seats they offer are awesome.  You pay a high price but you get free parking a block away; access to a private lounge and private outside courtyard.  The lounge has a free buffet provided by Margaritaville and a live band performs while you dine.  The lounge also has bathrooms.  You can go in and out of the lounge as often as you want.  The box seats are located between the chair seating in the front and the lawn in the back.  What's great is you have four chairs and a table with plenty of room.  Plus the box seats are a couple of feet higher than the people in the chairs so you can stay seated the whole time and still easily see the stage.  Or you can stand the whole time and not have to worry about people behind you complaining.  This is because there is a walkway between the box seats and the lawn and the lawn is a little higher up the slope.  My only complaint is how much concerts cost these days.  I don't think this has anything to do with the amphitheater, it's just artists are charging ridiculous prices for their shows.  Then on top of that you get ticket brokers buying up tickets with even higher ticket prices.  But if you do get to see a show there, you'll enjoy it.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Rather a disappointment.  The sound system was lousy. I think the band was ok but the sound system muffled them terribly.
Service was friendly but slow. I had the pork chops which were over cooked and chewy. The garlic mashed potatoes were tasty but a bit over the top on garlic. My husband had the Nashville hot chicken with medium sauce. Not impressed. The fries were tasty. The cole slaw was good. Our friends had burgers and thought they were good. But not great. 
The roof top bar was nice. 
They really need to step up their game on the quality of the food.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: To be completely honest, we ended up here every single night after we made our rounds at the other bars in Broadway. It has 3 levels, all with different vibes, so the wait is never long and it is never too crowded inside. There is always lots of energy and plenty of seating and room to dance. I liked the fact that there are all different age people here, I spoke with plenty of people my grandparents' age. There are also lots of bachelor/bachelorette parties which always make for a good time. Overall, if you aren't sure where to go on Broadway, Honky Tonk Central is a safe bet!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This place was nice and super country "typical Tennessee"  upon entry we were carded then we headed to the bar,  we got drinks very fast even though this place was jammed packed on a Saturday night.  

This is a 3 level country club,  live music playing,  very enjoyable atmosphere.  Everyone is super nice. 

Drinks are great. Place is clean. Great spot to visit when walking thru Broadway.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Don't fall for their advertised "deals". Was told there were 2 for 1 deals but only to find upon closing out that I was charged full price for not specifically wearing Preds gear. I live in Nashville and was, indeed, out supporting the Preds. I really wanted to love this place (nice bathrooms, not super packed), but unfortunately will not be supporting this bar. Locals beware.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
We saw Eric Church's acoustic performance at the inaugural performance.  Incredible show!!

Beautiful venue with a nicely sloped open lawn area for GA.  Bring a blanket and arrive early so you can save your spot -- also, if it had rained recently you're going to want a blanket to sit on before the show and stand on after.  There are no bad seats in the lawn EXCEPT for the two giant light stands that are about 50/60 feet tall -- if you sit directly behind one you're going to have a bad time.

I see a lot of other reviewers complaining about how expensive drinks were.  Ummm... really?  What did you except?  $4 2-4-1s?  Of course it's expensive!  It's Nashville!  At a brand new venue!  Personally, I felt $12 for a 25oz domestic beer was a very reasonable price for a stadium/venue.  Also, sneak in a flask, drink beforehand, don't be a rookie.

Had a blast and can't wait to come back.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great music but the bar tender on the second floor lost our friends credit card while on vacation.  She was not helpful in finding it either. We didn't have a tab and just paid for a drink. The rest of the staff was descent but clearly this girl wasn't the brightest bulb in the bunch. Just make sure you keep an eye on your bar tender as it could of ruined someone's vacation.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Nice bar, good music. We stopped in for lunch. We had nachos, which were good. I had the chicken salad sandwich...very good! My husband had the pulled pork sandwich...could have been more tender. We were there for the music and drinks not so much a 5 star meal so it was worth the time and money.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: What everyone else said, AND you can even talk politics here without fearing for your life. Mostly intelligent, and definitely diverse, points of view can be had for no charge. You get (at least) what what you pay for here, where "Cheers" meets "Deliverance," and Music Row Democrats mix with Skid Row Republicans.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: The food was the worst in Nashville.  I enjoyed the entertainment.   Frankly, the only reason we went was to see The Time Jumpers.  The music was exceptional.  I mean, the very best musicians in Nashville.   We missed dear Dawn.  We went to the afternoon songwriter show & enjoyed it.  Very limited menu.   The meat in the patty melt had an odd texture & was under seasoned.  The brisket was inedible.  We tried to order something easy at the evening show because we had to arrive so early to get a seat.  Epic fail.  Go to the shows.  Eat before you go.

name: The Station Inn
text:
This is incredible. You never know who you are going to see here, performing or watching!

This is a legendary venue so you have to make a stop by. Sunday is a bluegrasss jam and you just get in as long as they have room. Beer is inexpensive.

They know they are a legend so you can buy old concert posters, t shirts, postcards, etc.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Gigantic three level party bar. Lots of live music. Lower level is often loud, fun and packed. Level two was a lesser band, but room to sit and hang out. Third floor was also fun. This is one of the larger, more touristy spots, but it does a lot of things very well and it worth a visit. 

Food was so-so, but it this is a bar about music and drinking, so go for that.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Great bar for the locals and tourists. Beautiful decor. Great service and food. Best thing is the roof top patio. Best in town!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
What an AWESOME TIME!!! 
Best entertainment on Broadway!
Food was Good for what I would consider bar food.
Staff was great through out our multiple visits.
Honky Tonk Central is a must!
Be sure you ask for Crystal, BEST bartender there!!!! If she's not there look for Kelsey she's a close second!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Walked in and get stuck every night. Stay put to the first floor. There was a great live cover band that knows their country songs . Beside the music the Honkey Tonk Tea was awsome. Drink it away like its lemonade and get drunk as.......... ;-)

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: The place to go!  We had drinks, food and listened to the band.  Everything was great!  It was super busy on a Saturday evening of course but Monday evening was great.  The bands were great!  They were a lot of fun and played lots of different types of music to get the crowd into it.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great party atmosphere! But bar service sucks!!!!!! The bartenders sure know how to ignore you even if you're waving $100 bill. That's exactly to happen to my friend and I; we waited about 30 minutes to get served. HORRIBLE bartender service!!!! About 2-3 bartenders present with a full house. That ratio is incorrect!

name: Famous Nashville
text:
The service here was SO SLOW. 

We were seated at the bar and initially, our first two drinks came quickly. However, once we tried for a second round the bartender was nowhere to be found. She kept walking past us not looking our way. We finally asked her to get some more drinks and she told us she would be over in a minute but never came back. Spent the entire time at one end of the bar talking to the same people, walking past us to type on the computers, and then would return to the same area. We ended up ordering from a different bartender about 10-15 minutes later. 

There was a growing number of impatient customers standing at the bar to my right who were holding out their credit cards trying to get service. I overheard one guy saying he had been waiting 20 minutes. Another woman gave up and left. The guy directly to my right ordered 3 rounds of beers for he and is friends when a bartender finally came around  because he said he knew it would take too long when they wanted more. 

The music here was actually really good but it was a bit too loud to have any type of conversation. 

Also the bathrooms are INCREDIBLE. So pretty and clean with tons of mirrors. That's the only thing I liked about this place.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Good vibe, lot of energy for a Sunday ! Live music and cold beer what more could you ask for in Nashville

name: The Pink Slip Lounge
text: My wife and I stayed at the Hotel Preston where this lounge is located. We went on a Sunday night for dinner. They only had one guy working the whole place' He had to bartend wait tables and I think he was also cook. They didn't  have the meatloaf that we both ordered. My wife had the turkey club (subpar) and I had the steak, just awful. We had to get our own drinks. At least Emiljano the poor guy working there apologized and didn't charge me for the steak. This guy needs some assistance and should get a raise!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Day or night or even the afternoon you can always find good entertainment hold beer and some nice grub. Gina the bartender is super friendly on the first floor. Not much different than many of the Broadway places but this place is also a lot of fun.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
A must-visit for locals and tourists alike. I've seen several shows here--it's ALWAYS packed. Decent beer selection and okay food assortment, but you're not coming here for a meal. The acoustics were great for the shows I've seen here. Parking can be annoying (random people standing out in what appears to be a business lot, charging $6-$10), but what can you do? Welcome to Nashville. 

I love coming here. I'd definitely recommend you make it out too. Dive-y, but a classic Nashville haunt.

name: The Station Inn
text: Not a dive bar. Total opposite of it in fact. If looking for an up tight sort of experience this is the place for you. Make sure you drink with your pinky out to be able to fit in with the clientele.

name: Alley Taps
text: Great place and awesome staff but the owner doesn't play for employee parking which is pretty ridiculous

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Stop by here every time I'm in Nashville. Great live music with hot singers. Love it!!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Went to this place for drinks at the end of our bar hopping extravaganza. The place is pretty cool and they have live music. The Kentucky Bourbon Ale came in a smaller glass than expected. Other than that, good to go.

name: Live On The Green Music Festival
text: Who doesn't love live free music?! No one, that's who. LotG always brings in awesome bands to play. Therein lies the only problem. It's such a hit that everyone and anyone shows up so it's always crowded. I remember when it first started, there was maybe only a handful of people so no matter when you came you could still stand right up in front of the stage. Now you have to practically camp out if you want to be close, otherwise you're way in the back. I always have a good time. Cold beer, food trucks galore, great music. Summers in Nash don't get any better!

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text:
Bobby's is a local bar that reminds me of that show "Cheers"  by the time you leave, everybody knows your name.  It's the only bar I have ever felt comfortable going into, sitting at the bar and drinking a Beer by myself.  The locals that hang out there are super friendly and make you feel right at home.  It's mostly a older group during the day and during the evening, but the weekends when they have open mic,live bands etc etc it's a totally mixed group.
If your just a down to esrth, nothing fancy kind of person..you will love Bobbys.   Don't forget to bring your guitar, you will always be welcome to play, sing, dance....whatever is entertaining,  is welcome at Bobbys!     Rebecca Marks from Cali....

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: While in town for a conference I stopped in here and was pleasantly surprised. I love that the bar was old time with wooden floors, made me think of my time living in New Orleans. There was a live band called Smoke N Gun and they were amazing. Alexia's voice was great, it made it hard to leave the bar. I thought the service was decent and I enjoyed my honey lager.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Famous Saloon came in and saved the day for us after our original rehearsal dinner venue cancelled on us 2 weeks prior to our event. Amanda was so sweet and was a joy to work with. We used the Green Room and our guest couldn't stop raving about how much they loved the space. The decor is very unique yet very Nashville. The food was amazing as well! And of course everyone had a blast on the rooftop patio after our dinner was over! Thanks for helping us have an amazing night before our wedding Famous!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: A friend's family came into town and wanted to go to Lower Broad so we started at Honky Tonk Central.  It's great to have a different band on each of the 3 floors!  We ordered food and the burgers were really good and huge!  Two people could easily split one plate.  The bartenders were friendly and prompt.  Overall a good experience.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Went here today and explored all 3 levels and settled up top. Got an awesome server named Colt. Quick with the drinks, very personable and great dude. Band was really solid and made for a nice afternoon of boozin. Took care of Colt and before we left he hooked us up with a shot as thanks. Will be back.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place has poor management, called three days before. They told us we had the upstairs bar! Get here and there says no! Some douche with long wanna be red hair facial hair was rude to us. Told us they they did not staff up! Walked out this place sucks!!

name: Famous Nashville
text: Very nice bar. Upscale looking, we enjoyed some cocktails and a really talented guitarist by the name of Andrew Vanetten. I highly recommend you check him out!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I was told this was the place to go in Nashville. It certainly is the biggest bar. Three floors, all 3 with a different live band. Music is good.  Food is average. Prices are average. It's definitely worth checking out. 

From a fun standpoint, it doesn't blow away the competition. In fact I think I enjoyed some of the other bars more.  I say I think because I was quite intoxicated and running amuck.  

All in all, this is one of the best watering holes I visited while on my drunken travels. But I do recommend visiting all of the competition as well.

name: Famous Nashville
text: The bartenders are wonderful but the band stopped at 10:00pm the bar stays open longer. I would have stayed later if the band had played longer.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Oh Nashville, you country music loving bunch of people.  This bar is loud, rowdy with goofball college kids, and there are three floors of it.  They have a balcony for drunk party goers to hang off and shout obscenities down at the people passing by on the street.

This mixture is everything I dislike in a bar.

However it's a place you have to go when your in Nashville.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
After 5 or 6 shows here Ascend has solidified its place in my mind as a top venue in Nashville. Nestled up against the Cumberland you will be treated to beautiful views of the river and the sun setting behind the stage. Excellent premier acts regularly book the venue, taking the opportunity to play a festival like atmosphere and making the general admission lawn seats one of the best entertainment deals in Nashville. The sound is clear and not spoiled by the surrounding traffic like you would fear and the sight lines are excellent if a little long from the very back. Restrooms are large and easy to get to. Pro-tip: the ones in the very back at the top of the the hill tend to be less crowded in my experience. 
Beer and food are comparable with other places which is to say expensive. Expect 12 to 16 bucks for a 16 to 24 ounce can of beer. Entrance and security are not too terrible but avoid bringing large bags. If your on the the lawn I'd recommend a blanket for sitting between sets, but you should expect to be standing while the band is on stage if you want to see. You can also bring a small beach chair or rent them at the venue for a pretty reasonable fee. Parking at Nissan stadium is the way to go if no other major events are happening as you can pretty easily hoof it across the veterans bridge and drop right in to the venue avoiding the downtown traffic doomcluster. Overall I'm always inclined to grab tickets to an Ascend event. Metro really did a nice job creating this venue and giving us another great location for shows.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Absolutely loved the girl on stage and the bartenders. We wandered to here new to Nashville and after a drink at Benchmark we left but ended up back there. Just the comfy home feel was awesome.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Spent the majority of our downtown time here on a bachelor party the other weekend. Good barfood (especially the tots) and friendly service. Good bands and a wild good time in a great location with terrific views of Broadway.  Don't worry about the line it moves fast but plan on a few minutes in the bathroom line if you are there on a weekend night! Hope to make a return to this great place.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: I love concerts at Ascend. After the Ryman, it's my favorite music venue. I love that it's outdoors and that the set up is very accommodating. The way it's designed allows for good views from pretty much anywhere you are on the lawn and in the chairs. It's also pretty affordable and they have a good selection of food and drinks. Of note, there is usually a taco truck or some food truck on the far side of the venue so if you don't want stadium food there are other options, you just have to look for them.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Im sad to know I'm giving 2 stars, but honestly I've had & is Way more places with better food. We ordered calamari, marinated grill chicken and shrimp and grits and boy o boy when the food came  she originally said to us " ooo don't touch the calamari because it's hot" since my baby was already digging in, I had expected it o be hot. As she left I reached in for a calamari and honestly if You want a Soggy, Cold, Bad batter Calamari then go right ahead. My husband and I didn't enjoy it at all and we never finished it. 
Secondly I'm someone who don't eat Pork at all, & while reading the menu I didn't see that the Shrimp and grips had 'pork' and as I started eating the grits was too SOUR , I don't know why and then finally I bite into something weird and just not a taste that I'm use to. So I go look at the menu online to read that's in it again the. Asked her " hey is this sausage Pork? " & her reply to me was " I don't know, but for you I can say Beef ".  I was really bothered by that response because I especially am bother I ate pork when I Don't eat that in my life! and she didn't even offer to go FIND OUT or take it off the tab since I BEARLY ATE ANYTHING! but I will Never go there again. 
And Lastly, the ONLY Thing I could say was good was the Fries.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: I and three others, out of a group of 6 friends who ate at Benchmark last week, fell ill after eating at Benchmark B&G. The only thing in common to the four who suffered abdominal distress was the bar food we ate there. This included the chicken wings and the cheesy nachos as well as the fried pickles. We were all laid up within a few hours and for most of the next day as the bad food worked its way through our systems. The wings were delivered hot on the outside and cold on the inside and were not finished because we weren't sure they were cooked but before we returned them, a cockroach crawled across the wing basket as we sat at the bar. The bartender quickly removed the food and comped the food tab. The nacho cheese was a strange milky consistency that had little to do with cheese. Not sure which of these three were the culprit but stick to the beer and wine if you don't want to lose some weight. Music and staff were good.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Close to down town. Parking can be rough if you don't know that 100 feet away they have a free lot. Great bands. Above average bar food. Friendly staff. No bad seat.

name: The Station Inn
text: I've always wanted to visit, and it was 100% worth it! Get there a half hour before the show starts to get a good seat and a drink without waiting in line. We saw Larry Cordle and it was an awesome show- an intimate venue with great sound, a casual and laid back atmosphere, and good bar service. A must-see for bluegrass and country fans.

name: The Station Inn
text: I feel honored to have stepped foot in here. We tried the last time we were in town but were unaware of the fill up policy and came too little, too late. We got there nice and early this time and enjoyed some great blue grass with some fun surprise appearances. Get your pitchers of light beer and your frozen pizzas early and sit back for a great show.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Visited Nashville and went here, don't be turned off by the name - had non-Honky Tonk music and good variety. Drinks are a bit steep ($18 for cheap wine and cider.)

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
If there's one word to describe Honky Tonk Central, it's probably "consistent".

During the "winter storm" of 2015, it was the only place consistently open every day. There was always great live music (mostly acoustic when the sun was out). The bartenders are nice.

I had to eat lunch here out of necessity, and it was surprisingly decent for bar food. The fried catfish basket was a lot of food, and was nice and flakey. I also substituted the fries for onion rings.

They had a problem with beer delivery due to the weather - they only had Yazoo Dos Perros, but that's not a problem because Dos Perros is delicious.

Sadly, I was unable to attend one of the crazy nights here because they never opened up the second and third floors again after the storm while I was there.

So basically, to me, it was a low-key, family-friendly music bar with acceptable food. Which I guess is not everyone's experience with the place.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Good music, but sub par food. Tater tots and onion rings tasted good, but the burgers were very ordinary, and none of the food items were hot or even warmed up. I'm rating this place 3 stars only because it has live music on all the 3 floors of the bar, with a nice view of the intersection from the balcony, which is great for people watching. Good for music and drinks, but not food. Not too bad on the price.

name: Nashville Underground
text: We happened upon this restaurant on a sunny 60 degree day in January and everyone was so welcoming! Suggested we look at rooftop dining so we did and enjoyed the beautiful river view and delicious diverse menu. Will go back for sure!

name: The Back Corner
text: Probably my favorite new dance spot in Nashville. I have been searching for a venue with an amazing DJ and cocktails. You will find both here

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text:
The Good:
1) Great Dive bar for music.
The Bad
1) A/C I found inadequate when I visited. 
2l There is only beer available nothing else, no wine no liquor.

I would go for the music, otherwise I would head elsewhere.

name: The Station Inn
text:
If you are looking for non-touristy, Nashville music, this is the place! The Sunday night Bluegrass Jam was recommend to me by the staff at the hostel I was staying in and I am so happy I decided to check it out. 

Coming off Broadway, this was a totally different and more authentic Nashville experience. The atmosphere was very cool in that everyone sits together at long tables to listen to the music. I liked how people came on and off of the stage as they pleased to play their instruments. 

I will say, I had not eaten dinner before coming to this venue and the food is not good. Do not come here to eat, but if you're looking for great music, this is the place.

name: Famous Nashville
text: This establishment is fails to accommodate  for its crowd. I regret wasting my money here. They have no accommodations for men

name: Nashville Underground
text: After being in Nashville a few days we stopped by Nashville Underground for dinner. It was the best we had had! A few of the other places only had sandwiches so it was a great to have a full menu of choices and it was delicious. Great live music too!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: It was one of the more packed bars in the area but my review is mainly for their huge order of nachos which is good and filling. Can definitely feed at least two people. We were able to find a spot at one of the tables and were worried we wouldn't catch a waiter but we actually got one pretty quickly. Make sure to make eye contact with the waiter otherwise they will probably not come by.

name: The Station Inn
text: The lively music and cheap beer made this the perfect end to our trip. A must do when you come to Nashville!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
