I know it was busy in there, but there were empty tables, so they were not THAT busy. We told them we were in a hurry because the concert we were going to was going to start soon (we had been at the restaurant for over an hour and still didn't have anything to eat) So they brought our check out to us, saying this way we could get out faster. We got our check BEFORE our food even came!? I have never experienced anything that tacky. 

FINALLY our food came, and what do you know? She forgot my order. Even told me she messed up putting it in. So everyone I was with ate, and paid their checks, THEN my food came. I had to eat it pretty fast. Though it was decent, not worth the hour and 15 min wait for a bowl of soup and grilled cheese!

The manager tried to smooth things out by giving us complimentary shot glasses, it did not make up for the awful experience. He didn't even come over to the table to check on us, or apologize, just had the shot glasses sent over.

Lastly, as I was pulling my wallet out to pay, which our waitress, Ashley, stood next to the table waiting for the payment, which made it really uncomfortable.... comes over to me and apologizes to me for being so rude saying "well you know my boyfriend cheated on me and blah blah blah..." So unprofessional! I work in the service industry, and rule #1 is you don't bring your personal problems to work!!! Your boyfriend issue is NOT my problem.

Sorry about your boyfriend Ashley, but you should not have let it ruin our night.

I will not be going back.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Neat little place in Printers Alley. I can't comment on the food, but I enjoyed having a couple beers at the bar. It was pretty bright and colorful at 5pm during the week, so I'm going to say it's probably safe to say this may be a good family dinner option.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Stopped here for dinner on Saturday with the boys from the bachelor party. Doorman told us "Get the ribs!" and the host said it's the best thing on the menu. We all got the ribs, and they were phenomenal. Very soft, slid right off the bone, perfect sauce. I got French fries and Cole slaw as sides and loved those too. Fries were seasoned great, nice and crispy, and very hot. Some of the guys got Mac n Cheese and said it was perfect. Live music was great, not too loud (which is why we didn't eat at a bunch of other places). Didn't want anything too rowdy for dinner. Would definitely come here again for dinner before a crazy night on Broadway!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: WOW - great beer menu!  So many great beers and only so much I can drink, what a shame.  The menu looked like good bar food but we didn't eat here - 4 stars for the stellar beers and proper glasses.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Always wanted to go and I had the chance. Always loved the country and bluegrass music.. Had the best time with the best music. Was able to hear some new upcoming artist. No matter were you sit you had a great view.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Worst service and worst food I've had in years. Don't order the nachos. I am embarrassed for Nashville that this place is in business. See my photos of the nasty ketchup bottle they finally brought out after we finished our burgers.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
This is a somewhat disturbing walk down a darkish alley towards an unknown destination. 

Not to worry; once you get in the waitstaff is pleasant, efficient, and worth a look = ). I shared a pulled pork, fries and onion strings with my wife and topped it off with a solid margarita. Add in her sweet tea and we maxed out around $20ish. 

In the end it wasn't a wasted night, but we probably could have found better. It was another "experience" in another "dive bar" that looked to have a somewhat local following. 

Don't plan on making a big night of it if you're going here this is run of the mill bar food in a run of the mill locale.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
I thought the food was mediocre.  I got a "cheesesteak" sandwich that tasted like a cheap panini I could have picked up at a local grocery store.  You have to order side items separately, which is typical for many nice restaurants and I am okay with if the main course is impressive enough to stand on it s own.  This one wasn't .   The cocktails were tiny and massively overpriced.  I accidentally spilled my first cocktail (1/4 left) - and the waiter cleaned it up immediately but never offered to replace the drink.  He was a super nice guy, but perhaps a little frazzled.

My sandwich was delivered almost 15 minutes after the rest of the food at our table, and they were fairly unapologetic until I asked to have it removed from the bill, which they did, kindly, but did charge me for an extra cocktail in its place.  At that point I was too embarrassed to complain).  My husband and I spent $150 ($180 including tip), for sub-par food and cocktails that should have cost 1/2 of what they did.  

Also- ambiance seems to be having a bit of an identity crisis.  Is it a hipster restaurant, a sports bar, or a nightclub??  In my opinion, a restaurant is better off choosing one and being really great at it - not trying for all three.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Seat yourself....we sat down, 15 minutes later our waitress came up and we asked for menus. She sarcastically says, "well everyone came in at the same time". Horrible service. Never coming back here.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Loved the area on where bar was located but we ordered simple drinks, Titos Soda and lime. The bartender took a while to get them to us and then they were cranberry and titos. When we told her no cran, she returned our drinks in a shot glass and seemed upset. Great local bar but bartender needs to crack a smile and not look upset when she mistakes our order.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: In Nashville for the first time an wandered in based on Yelp reviews. Way to go, Yelpers!  Great space. "Just Right" sized portions of the kind of breakfast food I needed after a night out in Nashville.  Would love to come back at night...

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: A cool experience while you are in Nashville, especially if you are a country music fan.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Love love love the atmosphere.  They have cool seating areas if you are hanging out with friends and don't want to sit at a table or the bar.
The vibe was great.
Good beer and food as well.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Loved the jalapeno tots and the hippie hollow pita. Good service. Great selection of craft beers. Decor is memrable and inviting. Doesn't feel like a chain at all. Great place to stop for a beer or a meal

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This was neat and interesting. Though I think it was slightly over priced, it was still fun to learn more about the history and what it means for the singers to be a part of the grand opry. The tour is about an hour.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Not good for gluten free folks. Was not able to eat. had to leave

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
I usually try write good reviews but I just can't with this place. We have tried it out twice hoping it would be better the second time around but it wasn't. 

The nacho appetizer can be explained in one word...awful. The queso was practically cold and the pork tasted like it was on the verge of being spoiled. My boyfriend had a burger and he said it was okay, but it certainly was nothing to write home about. The restaurant (indoor and outdoor) is a has a nice ambiance and vibe but (big BUT) the food and beer is in my opinion overpriced and subpar. Honestly, I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone I liked.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text:
Awesome new bar on Broadway that will definitely hold its own with the established ones!  They hit the jackpot going from a hole in the wall in Vegas to a multi-floor bar with a rooftop deck and they even have their own line of whiskey.  Bands and DJ's nonstop and the staff is friendly and very interactive!  You MUST visit Blair if you go here; she goes well above and beyond the role of "bartender" and lives and personifies the entire brand.  Won't surprise me if she owns the next one that opens; she is that good!  The bar does not cater to just the guys either; a bachelorette party stopped in for an hour or two during my visit and was made quite comfortable (DJ Sinister having a lot to do with that).

My only ding is the food; it is definitely bar barbecue and not barbecue joint barbecue.  Of course, most people won't come here to eat but for the entertainment and cold drinks.  Get you some hot chicken before coming.

RNR is a must-stop on your next trip to Nashville and will hold their own with the established big dog honky tonks!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great music and friendly staff. Trey was our server and he told us we couldn't go wrong with anything on the menu. He was right!  We had the chicken, ribs and brisket and everything was fall off the bone with great flavor. If I'm down in Nashville I would definitely come back here

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I was visiting Nashville from San Antonio as part of a national professional conference and one event planned for us was the 87th anniversary concert for the Grand Old Opry!  Brother, I'm in!  I like country, really like the classic country and my folks are from Harlan County, Kentucky, home of Loretta Lynn, so this place has always been a mythical kind of place to actually visit.  It lived up to the billing!  WE had very good seats and it was just a special place.  I was surprised at how much comedy played a part in the show, the emcee, Little Jimmy Dickens, kinda cornball, but I was laughing as was the crowd.  Honestly, can't remember who all I saw there, Jim Ed Brown, Jason Aldean, Ricky Skaggs, Steve Wariner, Casey James, Bill Anderson, Tyler Farr, Rodney Atkins, and many, many others.  This was a real show, guess it was going out live on the radio and they have an actress portraying Minnie Pearl to get the crowd whipped up.I went both nights, Friday and Saturday and the Friday show was by far the best, but maybe that's because I was just so completely awestruck and in reverence for being at this mecca of music.  I want to say that those tickets cost me 50 bucks as part of our group rate.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: The environment/decor at BAD is really unique and was my favorite thing about the place.  It is probably great for a happy hour, but I only came here for lunch and my rating is based on that experience.  The menu is typical for a bar and does not have a lot of variety, but if you want a sandwich or a burger, then you will be fine.  I had a burger here myself and it was alright.  The staff that work here are very friendly and provided great service.  I would like to see what it is like during a happy hour, that seems like it must be the best time to go here in this unique place!

name: Music City Tippler
text: A great hidden corner of Midtown.  Live music, interesting people, and inventive cocktails,  The Tipler is a Nashville gem.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Stopped by here the other night before going to a film at the Belcourt Theater. Service was terrible, the server was slow, looked like he had not bathed in days and when he did get around to bringing our drink orders got them wrong. Now for food. My wife got the burger which was nothing to write home about and I got the nachos which were terrible. Nashville has plenty of clean, well-managed and good restaurants. Spend your money at one of them and not this place.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Just alright. Good beer selection (if a little overpriced), but I don't care for the atmosphere. I like to have my drinks outside in the summer and there's no patio and they hardly ever have the windows open on that sunroom-ish area. The food isn't anything special. The pretzels are pretty good, but nothing to write home about.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Exactly what you think.  I had a blast, even by myself, going backstage and taking pictures of everything.  It's crazy to think that you are standing, or sitting, right where some of the greatest country Gods once stood.  Standing in the circle on the stage is almost magical, with the lights shining down and all the other tourists staring at you while you take your picture.  It's pretty cool and quite informative.  Definitely something I would do again with other family members.

name: Third Man Records
text: Super friendly staff. Great prices. An absolute must for vinyl enthusiasts and Jack White fans. Lots of fun things to do and see.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
Cheap drinks! We came upon this place when walking to the WarMuseum. Bloody was thin but good. We decided to come back for some food bc of the reviews. 

First off, our waitress was rude as hell. Second, the wings suck. Like seriously I can't even eat them. One bite responded by "gross!" 

But the drinks are cheap! 

And whomever commented about live music- no live music here. 

Someone's a liar. Come for cheap drinks at a cool hole in the wall. Save your appetite for elsewhere. Yesterday we had amazing wings from Mojo's!

name: Third Man Records
text:
Jack White is a very cool cat.   From his Tesla radio tower perched atop the Lego colored building block shape of his recording studio Third Man Records this is the House That Jack built.  And you don't just have to stand outside and gawk.  You can come inside.  You are invited.

Does this mean that once inside this childlike fantasy land you can climb into a large wooden chair with Jack White himself dressed as Santa Clause and perch on his lap while telling him what you wish for (him, serenading you while playing an electric guitar sans Santa Clothing)????  Unfortunately, no.  You don't get to see Jack.  Or really the recording studio either.  What you get is to step into a front room filled with some memorabilia of days gone by like the actual Lego pieces used in the White Stripes video "Fell In Love With a Girl".

But don't distress, fun is still to abound.  Because Jack has a very vintage, very wooden, very art deco recording booth that still works.  And for a $15 contribution to preserving history you too can become a recording star by shutting the almost sound proof door and making a 45 second record.  It will be stamped with Third Man Records.  And when you are done you can put the said record in an old rusty mailbox outside and mail it to the love of your life.  In fact, if you are too shy to sing into the microphone (dear God is Jack listening to these recordings??) you can just speak a heartfelt message or poem.  Let's just hope the person you are mailing the record to has a record player.

In addition to the vintage recording booth there is also a vintage photo booth you can take pictures in.  I saw Jack on an episode of one of my favorite TV shows (American Pickers) and he ended up buying some antique stuff from Mike Wolfe (who has a store in Nash) so the guy has great taste in antiques.

Of course you can buy albums (some rare) and t-shirts.  Third Man Records put out some cool, exclusive stuff in the music world (become a member for the best access).  And they also have random events at the studio so you will want to do like me and stalk, I mean watch, their website for more information on what's happening.  Swoon!!

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Came on a Monday at 11pm after the previous bar closed early. Place was pretty empty (no surprise) and no drink specials but they were yummy nonetheless! Awesome bar staff as well!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I liked my experience here a lot, it's a fun beer hall with diverse selections aplenty.  But as far as the food goes, it didn't have me going gaga.  Maybe I didn't order correctly but I expected more in that way from all the rave reviews. But the beer was great at the staff was knowledgeable.  The pretzels were a huge hit at my table.  A great stopping point to chill after seeing sights or for a fun night out.  If I was in town again I'd definitely stop by, but I'd have my meal somewhere else.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
One of my favorite places to visit Nashville. 
Have also been to the one in Memphis, Raleigh, Addison & Columbia. 
Super menu for even a Vegetarian!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I am not a fan of country music at all but this was a fun place.

We took a backstage tour and my concept of county music has changed a bit.  

It only costs about 23.00 for a show.  No matter what your stature as far as stardom.  If you are Carri Underwood you play for 23.00 a show or around that much.  If you become a member you must play so many times a year.  Everyone can get a chance at the Opry.  Every star just uses a locker in a community area.  The stars are very down to earth and not like other stars with special

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Get the pretzel.  Do it.

Really cool chill place to drink beer (and eat pretzels, obv) in Nashville.  Not that far from the city center, but far enough that it's a lot less fratty than downtown could be.

Friendly staff, cool seating (couches, benches or regular tables).

And pretzels - do it.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This place is literally in a back alley. It has that bar type of look on the inside. Dark and grungy. BUT they have great drink prices and specials. The food is pretty decent for bar food. Typical stuff such as burgers, chicken tenders, etc. If you're looking for cheap, this is definitely an okay place to check out. I wouldn't go there too often but if i needed something cheap to eat that was decent, this would be a great place to check out.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Food was very tasty.  The Reuben was excellent and I especially liked the jalapeño sauerkraut.  The Cobb Salad was fresh & tasty.  The Quesadilla were on special & were very tasty.  Definitely recommend this restaurant to others.  Our server was pleasant & attentive.

name: Anthem
text: Gorgeous place. Great & professional unpretentious staff. My SUGGESTIONS to Anthem for regular Saturday Nights: Upgrade  the quality of the sound system, hire a DJ that doesn't play 20 second snippets of every song possible, & please leave it up to other less cool venues to play Shaggy & Coolio.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Over 225 draft beers and a limited but pretty good menu. I ordered the quesadillas and enjoyed them. Nothing out of this world, but good food.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Visited on Saturday May 24 around 4 and the place was kind of quiet , but by the time we left, the patio was filling up and the place was getting lively. We went for a Groupon deal and will definitely be going back! The bartender/server, Sammy, was very helpful. We had a beer sampler flight each. There were 5 generous samples of beer. We also had the cheese dip made with sausage and sriracha I was afraid I might be too hot for my boyfriend's tastes but it was perfect. My favorite beer was the Curious Traveler Shandy. All of the beers were exactly as described by the bartender. The location was great and the décor was fun. All in all a great neighborhood bar we cant wait to visit again.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
About as bad as it gets
Big party on a Monday night
First ones in the place
Drinks took forever 
Dinner came out sporadically where 1/4 of the group got dinner at a time. By the time 1/4 of the table finished eating another 1/4 would get their food.
The waitress tried, but the kitchen couldn't figure out how to get food out.
The only thing that keeps this place in business is the music.
Enjoy that and eat elsewhere

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Simply one of the best venues. You can practically feel the history as you enter this place. Free parking is easy because of the mall, and there's really not a bad seat in the house. A must for both locals and tourists!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: By far the highlight of the trip. I was most excited to see Carrie underwood.. Much to my surprise the other artists outshines her. Lee greenwood got everyone singing along. Carson peters and iron mountain shocked me (a child with amazing talent), Lauren Alaina shocked me with her enthusiasm and sweetness( the girl can sing too), and Charles eaten ended up being quite the performer. A great time

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text:
The reviews are a little harsh....and I get the complaints haha. This was the first place I went to while I was in Nashville.  I love karaoke and it was the first place I found...and it was in famous printers alley.  
Honestly. It's kinda what I imagine a tennessee karaoke bar to look like. Smokey. Kinda divey. Kinda bleh. Felt like a great place for a budweiser and terrible karaoke singing. I got to sing 10 minutes after outing in a song. Not too bad.

This place ain't classy...but there's a charm to places like that sometimes. Open wayyy late night too

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great food and service. I highly recommend the arugula and prosciutto pizza. The loaded rocket tots were on point as well.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Music is everywhere in Nashville, and good music too. The band at BB King's was lively and talented, but had some odd choices of song, including one seemingly titled "I'm Going To Marry My Mother In Law." SO corny and just plain weird. $5 cover just to get in the door in the evening.

The venue is the best part of BB King's. It's large and doesn't feel stuffed or stuffy. There is a dance floor in front of the stage which you can use if you dare, and lots of tables situated facing the stage/dance floor. Servers move deftly throughout, bringing food and drinks. It was a little awkward being walked by the hostess through the dance floor, in front of the stage and all the people at their tables watching -- to our table. 

My friend and I just ordered dessert because we had a craving. They have a peach cobbler on the menu, which is served a la mode and I believe made with real peaches! However...it was NOT a cobbler. It was a streusel. Real dessert-lovers know the difference. Very sweet and big enough to share between two people and still satisfy that sweet tooth.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I'm giving a one star because zero isn't an option. Nashville has a lot to offer, but don't waste your time with this. Not worth the money, and the staff are rude, in stark contrast to my other experiences in Tennessee.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Back Alley Diner continues to impress us. We have been back several times since my initial review, but Saturday night we tried some different things. The wings were on special, so we ordered some buffalo and some Tabasco wings. The buffalo has BBQ sauce in the mix, so it had an awesome smokey flavor. The Tabasco had the perfect amount of heat. Both were cooked perfectly, crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. Hubs stuck with the catfish po boy, but I went with a salad. It was great! Quality lettuce and toppings and they were very fresh. Cold beer as always, and some nice live music. We will keep on coming back!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: We found this on Yelp and decided to give it a try. Busy but not too crowded on a Friday night. The wait staff was great. If you like craft beer you need to try the Jackalope Bear Walker. All the food was great and I really liked the homemade kettle chips. It had a local feel and a relaxed fun atmosphere. If you like places off the beaten path you will not be disappointed. No negatives. I just don't give many 5 stars.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
This was a great experience! We went for an early dinner on Saturday... No wait! Even with 6, we were seated right away. The decor was fantastic! I loved the brick walls and the wood bar. Beautiful.

Our server was very nice, but the service was sort of slow. The food was very good. I had the catfish po boy and most of my family ordered the burgers. Everyone was happy. 

I tried the Blues Brew too (I guess it's a custom beer for them) and it was tasty too! We would go back if we're in the area.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Pretty much everything about our visit to the Grand Ole Opry was perfect.  The staff is friendly and helpful.  When you are walking in there is a big guitar with Grand Ole Opry Written on it and they are sure to have a staff person there to snap your photo on your cell for you.  Thank goodness they haven't tried to take your photo and sell it to you.

There is a bar just past security where you can purchase drinks and bring them in.

The show was great and the seats comfortable with very good viewing.

We went to the 7pm show so exiting the theater was crammed.  Felt much like cattle being pushed through a maze.  They only allow themselves 35 min to clear, clean and reseat the theater.  

Parking can be difficult so be prepared to walk a bit.  Actually parking further out isn't a bad idea because after the show there is major traffic congestion.  If you park towards the back of the lot you can scoot out much faster.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great place to eat at. Very friendly environment and the food is great. I had a bacon Swiss cheese burger and it was so yummy. I would so come back here again.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Loved it! Not a bad seat in the house. Prices are reasonable. Great shows, consistently.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great food, great employees and great drinks for a great price. You can't go wrong with the jalapeño poppers, burgers, wraps or chicken sliders. Will be a regular for sure!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Good atmosphere, good food, drinks, music (live), slow service. Will give it a second round.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Great place. Good deals for happy hour. Great food. Staff is nice and friendly. Great atmosphere. Good place to go for lunch and just kick back. Go check it out!

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text:
We had absolutely a blast here while watching the USA (YEAAAAAAAAAAAA buddy) v Ghana game. There was a great crowd watching the game with us. Amurica was definitely represented. Actually, Ben Franklin and Honest Abe even stopped by. Although it was definitely packed, we were able to watch the game reasonably well with the GIANT screen outdoors. The bartenders were also able to handle the crowds pretty well. Buckets of Coors light were $20 and singles were $4 (har ha nice to see buying in bulk saves right)? In regards to food...pretty typical. Although Freedom fries never tasted so good...

Overall, such a fantastic experience. Such an enthusiastic group that embraces the mo' spangled the mo' better. Words to live by.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: It is absolutely unacceptable for this business to treat their customers who are not like them poorly. It is not acceptable to be rude and disrespectful to customers,

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
The Opry is called the 'home of American music' and 'country's most famous stage.'  They're known to offer and present 8 or more artists on each show, and gives the audience a sample of each artist's musical style.  There's also a gift store next door where you can pick up souvenirs, clothing, and music - Nadia, one of the helpful and the most sweetest staff there, gave us a brief history as well as the tour of the Opry we should check out and the upcoming shows that are coming up for the weekend.  Nice plaza to see the venue itself and take pictures next to the guitar monuments. :D

+features a variety of performing artists
+ask for Nadia in the gift store

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: We just hung out in the lower level bar area. Drinks were cold. Service was great. Had some good live music. Musicians interacted great with the bar patrons.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great music but way to loud for only 16 people in the downstairs area. WARNING A friend with us ordered a mixed drink and had a black bug in drink. She sent it back to get a fresh drink, still had a bug but this one was frozen in the ice. Pay attention when ordering you drinks and food!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: 50 cent wings on Saturday, and for 50 cents these are really good wings..if you do opt for the wings don't forget to order a side of fries, those are delicious too! Oh and $2 PBRs...perfect for anyone on a budget and looking for a low key kinda place with live music on a Saturday night.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
I like beer, it makes me a jolly good fellow
I like beer, it helps me unwind and sometimes it makes me feel mellow 
Whiskey's too rough, Champagne costs too much, vodka puts my mouth in gear
This little refrain should help me explain as a matter of fact I like beer

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Beer, Beer, Beer! Awesome staff and great selection of craft brews. This is our go-to spot for new brews and meeting with friends.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: We went last night (a Wednesday) so it was dead besides the twenty of us.  We did have a lot of fun because we love karaoke but be weary of the fact that it would have been a pretty lonely place if we didn't have a large group; there were literally two other people there.  I would hope that it is busier on the weekend.  The bartender and DJ were both really nice and made us happy but I was hoping to see and hear more people.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Thankfully, I have been here several times or I might have been turned off by my most recent visit. The food was fine, but our server was really cranky. Not at all friendly bordering on rude. Maybe she worked closing the night before and really didn't want to be working a lunch shift....? Still, it had a definite effect on our dining experience.

This is the first place I ever went to in Nashville and I loved it from the first minute. I've been back every time I have found myself in the city. It's huge but still cozy sort of. Great central location, next to the Frist.
I almost always get the pretzels and dip and they are always delicious.
They of course have a spectacular selection of beers.

Eat, drink, and be merry! And hopefully your server has gotten a good night's and doesn't look like she is shooting daggers out of her eyes at you.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Went for a friend's Birthday party tonight. Was not impressed. Band was extremely boring. Service was AWFUL, and they added gratuity which she did not deserve. I am a great tipper and this girl was just  downright bad at waiting tables. Wouldn't have given more than 3 dollars. They put a 7 dollar gratuity making a 45 dollar tab for 1 yazoo pale, a coffee,  6 wings (which were slimy and cold), a 1/2 order of under fried pickles and a bowl of what was supposed to be peach cobbler but was basically lukewarm peaches in a bowl with ice cream... Save your 50 bucks that I personally feel I was ripped off for, and walk 2 blocks to Bourbon Street which is where we went after. Better music. I didn't try the food but the drinks were cheap and the menu looked good and much cheaper than bb's. Anything is better than that lame experience we had at BB kings. I assume all these good reviews are from tourists, this is not a good local spot. AVOID.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Good Lordy there's a ton of history here! And you'll learn almost all of it if you take the backstage tour, which I highly recommend. 

I haven't made it to an actual show yet, but the backstage tour was amazing! You sit through a short film on the history if you wish, and I suggest, and then you head on back and there's tour guides along the way to answer questions or give you stories every here and there, but it's pretty much self guided. You see the entrance where every star walks in, and their mailboxes, where you can write them a letter if you so choose. And you get to see all of the dressing rooms and the common area where all the stars hang out. And they don't mind if you sit on the couches where who knows who has sat there before you. 

The headliners dressing room is the only dressing room you can actually walk in, but you see all the others as well. Tour guides will tell you stories old and new and let you know who likes to use which rooms, but they're all themed so it's not too hard to figure out for some.

Then you take a step through the curtain and walk on stage. And then head to the front microphone and stand in the circle where literally every Opry star since the beginning has stood.  That in itself is amazing, for country fans or not, to appreciate. You then walk across the stage and learn about the soundstage next door where the film the show Nashville, and out into the auditorium and into a gift shop.

The price is decent ( I think under $20 a person) and worth it in my opinion. You can take as much or as little time as you want since its self guided, and never be afraid to ask questions, the tour guides are amazingly nice and knowledgable. I would easily do another tour again!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Who am I kidding, Saucer has pretty much become mine and my husbands favorite bar, sometimes the servers can be a little slower, but usually they're pretty good, we come here as much as we can, usually on Wednesdays for Pint night.  I love you saucer, and I'll see you soon.

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text: Best Fish-n-Chips in Nashville! (The secret is they make their own beer batter.) It's a great Irish Pub and they have good food! Not a lot of sunlight- but its an Irish pub.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Really enjoyed the show, yes they do commercials that a lot of folks don't know exist between curtain  shows. Hey, they have always done that. It's still a wholesome family show with Humor, Bluegrass, Country, Modern upcoming stars and traditional country. The backstage pass was a a great deal to see the things that happen behind the scenes. Wish i'd been aware of the celebration add-on (Needed one for a birthday). Great experience for my family. would definitely do it again.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: The tour was amazing.  Great education and knowledge by the brilliant Vinny.  He is super enthusiastic and makes the tour a great experience.  Got great pictures and my sister enjoyed it.  Would recommend it to anyone visiting Nashville!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
I can tell this is a bar I would really love and the only reason it's not getting 5 stars is the music that we had to deal with when we were here. From what we understood it's normally a BLUES CLUB, but unfortunately due to CMA weekend (we accidentally planned a whirlwind road trip during the same weekend), we had to deal with some more mainstream Taylor Swift-y music that was just not good. Actually, I'll go ahead and say at least one of the acts was actually ANNOYING. Whiney girls are not my jam.

But, the service, despite being obviously overwhelmed, was awesome. We sat at the back bar and were basically the only people (and youngest, so we got some stares) there for most of the time we spent in this place. The drinks were good, the food was good, the bartender was cute and attentive and appreciated our disappointment in the music, and we were actually able to GET food and drink during that incredibly insane weekend. 

We got the appetizer sampler and a side of mac and cheese. I don't eat wings, but I ate one of these and can say, as a non-wing-eater, I wouldn't eat them again, but the catfish bites were so melt-in-your-mouth-amazing, I could eat a whole plate of those myself. The mac and cheese was also fantastic, as were the fried pickles (I'm a serious pickle judge), so I'm anxious to get back and eat the fried treats this place has to offer. I'd definitely come back on a normal trip and spend some time listening to blues and enjoying the delicious foods.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
I love this place! I visited on a Saturday night and was able to listen to an amazing band with a lead vocalist that was off the charts. I hate I didn't catch their name. 

Unfortunately, the wait to sit a table of two was over an hour so if you're hungry I wouldn't come here last minute. 

Luckily for us a spot at the bar opened up. Our bartender/server was exceptional! He made me a virgin drink that looked like the real thing and it was delicious! Also the Yazoo Creole plate was very good too. They didn't have many dressings for the salad so that was a bummer and the gumbo was pretty much vegetarian and not what we were expecting. 

Outside of that, it's a cool spot and I'm glad I was able to experience it.

name: Third Man Records
text:
It's Matty C coming to you live with yet another 5-star Friday.

Bear with me, Third Man Records holds a very special place in my heart. Jack White has essentially fronted the entire vinyl revival of the past decade. His bands White Stripes, Raconteurs, Dead Weather, and his existing solo project have deeply impacted my personal life. 

I've been wanting to visit Third Man Records when I began collecting vinyl in 2011. It's a hobby that I've invested countless hours into, as well as tons of cash, but that's neither here nor there. This past April, his Rolling Record Store stopped in Jacksonville (think food truck but for records) and since Nashville was on our list of cities to visit this year, you know I had to make a pitstop at the infamous shop.

I could go on endlessly, but many reviews have covered the bases. In my opinion, the shop is an homage to those who love music, history, equipment, memorabilia, and of course, the art of listening to records.

By far, the coolest aspect of Third Man is the listening booth, which is filled with rarities, B-sides, 7"s, and LP's waiting to be listened in its proper form. I could've stayed in there for hours. Rather I could've spent an entire day in the shop, listening, gazing, wandering and spending my life savings away.

Quite possibility one of the quirkiest record shops I've ever stepped inside of, yet one of the greatest out there. They also house live shows and performances, as well as the record plant that presses vinyl and records artists across all genres. This is the end of my love letter, and I hope our paths cross again.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Watched a hockey game here with friends for some brews and food. I got a chicken sandwich, which was made really well (try their housemade spicy BBQ sauce). The French fries are to die for! My friend got the burger and wasn't that impressed with it. All in all, cheap beer and a good atmosphere to watch a sporting event.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We saw rascal flatts, Chris Jansen as well as some other acts here. There really is no bad seat in the opry. It's a must see experience, the backstage tour was sold out so if you'd like to do that book way in advance. Also easy to park.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Backstage tour was really nice. I enjoyed the history, and the new film they show at the beginning.
If we go again, I'd stay for a show as well. After the tour, I was definitely in the mood to see more.
NOTE: They take a professional photo for you on the stage. You can view it in the gift shop. We got distracted in the gift shop and forgot to check the photo. :)
Another thing to mention, as we were driving there, following our GPS, it looks kinda odd as you drive into the area where the G.O.O. is located. It's located in the middle of a warehouse-looking area with a big mall across the street. Not what I expected, and at first we thought maybe we were in the wrong place. Didn't expect a historical venue like that to be right by a big mall, but I guess that's commercialism. ;)

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Go here for the music experience. The live band and music were good. I enjoyed the performance over dinner. The food was just okay. It's just Your typical bar food. I'd recommend sticking to the basics here like chicken wings and burgers. The items outside of that were not good. The drinks were terrible. The mixers they used taste like cough syrup. Once again I'd recommend sticking to the basic mixed well drinks. I do have to give credit to the white chocolate bread pudding. The breaded part was a little stiff but The flavor was so good. Overall I'd go back here but more so for the musical/ downtown Nashville experience. I wouldn't go here looking for amazing food.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Absolutely loved this place.  We went night after night on our trip to Nashville to hear the music played by their house bands and performers.   The food was really good too.  I had the pulled pork bbq sandwich and it was on par with one I had at one of Nashville's famous bbq joints.  Servers and bartenders were friendly and had good recommendations for things to do in town.  I am already missing this place and wish we had one in Philly

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great bar food at a great price! The staff and owners are always on point. We typically do lunches and happy hour things here and they are very accommodating.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Great show. Saw Cassadee Pope and Charlie Daniels, as well as others I can't recall. Three songs per set for five artists. My first indoor concert in years. I prefer outdoor/festivals.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
After some careful research and recommendations we chose the Music City Tippler for our dinner while visiting Nashville for the weekend with friends.

What a mistake.

The menu was entirely different than what was posted on the web site and by different I don't mean a change of seasons or an update. I mean they were serving the late night menu of light apps and sandwiches for dinner service. We were the only people sitting for dinner at 7pm on Saturday night. It was almost surreal, we were wondering if they lost the kitchen staff the night before? or maybe earlier in the day?

Our open faced salmon sandwich was served on a hamburger bun. Not a nice restaurant prepared bun but a real grocery store white bread generic hamburger bun.

The entire time we were having dinner, someone was running a lemon press or some sort of grinder/slicer over in the corner of the dinning room. Not sure why? we were the only people there.

maybe the chef had the flu?

Stay away.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great club with great music!!! It's a family friendly restaurant with wonderful staff, specially Jean-Paul Mendes (Director of Operations) who made us feel very welcome.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Grand Ole Opry is the most well known music venue of Nashville. 

Located about 15 miles away from the downtown Nashville area.

I thought it was located in the most random place. In the parking lot of the outlet. Pretty weird. I am sure they built the outlet around the venue. I felt like that took away from how epic the venue is supposed to be.

Parking is shared with the outlet. The front entrance area is cool. I liked the huge guitars. 

The venue itself reminded me of a huge church. Cool place to visit even if you do not watch a show or do the tour.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Nice atmosphere! Nice and just right for dancing freely and listening to great jazz. The wait was about an hour but we paid the cover charge of $5 and got to stand around and still listen to music while we waited on our table. One we got our table, we were right in the front. The food was great! Now my Gumbo Yaya had to be sent back the first time. All the rice in it was raw! It was inedible. The loaded Pull Pork Tater Tots were great! It's a huge portion and maybe 4-5 ppl can eat out of. When i got my replacement gumbo, it was great!! The BB King Allstar Band was great! They interacted with he crowd and gave greeeaat music to dance to! BB King was open to kids after 8 PM! There were kids there this night and they were on the floor dancing! Like i said, it was a great experience overall!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I really enjoyed this spot. It's ideal for groups of people to grab some great bar food and an EXCELLENT selection of beers. Servers were nice, and I ended up leaving a full and happy man.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
We arrived here for dinner on a Friday night. We had to pay a $10 cover charge because the band was playing (even though we were eating dinner)! 

I had the brisket sandwich. It was okay. Nothing exceptional about the food. I was with a large party and paying for myself (my bill was approximately $50 - including cover charge). This was pricey for 1 person. 

The band was awesome & entertaining! 

The drink "love on the delta" was good.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
BAD = NOT GOOD... IS AN APPROPRIATE NAME FOR THIS DINER

The food is nothing to write home about.  They need to get a better bread supplier because the buns they used for the burger and pulled pork sandwich had a weird texture.  We had an extremely RUDE WAITRESS who was impatient and didn't want to serve us.  I made the mistake of changing my order when she was writing down my order (mainly because I can't have lactose products) and the look she shot me was chilling.....so make sure you know exactly what you want when you are ordering .  After I told her I was lactose intolerant and wanted to know what entrees did not have milk or cream in it, she shot me a look....If looks could kill I'd be dead now.  With such a chilly waitress we didn't want to stay a minute longer so we ate quickly and left as soon as we could.

My recommendation is to find another restaurant that serves good food and has a friendly wait staff.  We had high expectations from the reviews but were very disappointed with our experience at the B.A.D.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
So many friends had raved about the Tippler, and I was really looking forward to trying it now that the grand opening crowds have subsided. I went last night (just for drinks--no food), but unfortunately, I can't give the Tippler more than 3 stars. 

I'll lead off by acknowledging that I'm a drink snob. If I'm going to pay a premium price for a cocktail, I expect it to have premium ingredients, premium preparation, and premium taste--and my standards are somewhat exacting. The menu told me that the Tippler would do reasonably well on the first criterion, with most of the core spirits of the $20-$30 per bottle variety you wouldn't be ashamed to put in your own liquor cabinet. Unfortunately, when it came to preparation and taste, I was underwhelmed.

I tried two drinks--their variation on the Mule, and the Black Manhattan. Both were decent, but nothing to write home about. With fancy drinks, I enjoy savoring the complexity of flavors, particularly if they change over time. Unfortunately, both of these drinks just tasted flat and no better than something I'd concoct at home.

On the plus side, the bartenders were friendly and attentive. On the minus side, despite it being a Wednesday night, the bar area was crawling with young people acting young. (UGH, I sound like an old man.) My issue with it was that it took away from the ambience; you have a place with a posh interior and fancy drinks, and a bunch of folks acting like they're at the Tin Roof. Oh, and the bar only has back-less stools, so after a while my back got sore. (Yes, now I REALLY sound like an old man.) Anyway, in fairness, I know they have other rooms, so I probably should have just gravitated that direction.

I ended up going to Patterson House after I left, and I was night-and-day more satisfied--and for about the same price, too. Between the selection, the ambience, and the flavor profiles, Patterson House flat-out wins. Like I said, I really wanted to love the Tippler, but at the end of the day it was just okay.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Awesome beer and ale selection.


Awful food.


Just awful.
Plus, we sat at a table for around 20 min while the waitress served people who came in and sat down ten min after we did.

She said she didnt know who had our table, but that she'd be our waitress.

The egg on the jalapeno tots was undercooked to the point of having clear whites.
Not much jalapeno either.

The pretzels were great, as was the beer.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Must see for all country music fans. Love the gift shop, souvenir is a must after the show! I'm sure everyone has this at the top of their list to see!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Sadly we came on a Sunday afternoon and there were no tours or shows happening. We did however, get to walk around and see something so large and famous. We took a bunch of photos out front near the huge guitars and looked in the windows of the performance hall. We then went to the gift shop and bought souvenirs like a couple of tourists. Despite not tour and not being to see the whole thing, we had a lot of fun! I would recommend anyone come if you haven't seen it and want to experience something so historical and cool. Even just the few things we did while we were there made it a good time.
Word of note, however. We wanted to go to the resort next door and look inside the hotel and maybe eat lunch. When we drove to that side of the property, the self parking was $20! We didn't want to spend that much on parking just to be able to go inside and look around. They had no other parking options available so we gave up and left instead.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: The pretzels are worth trying. I am not normally a pretzel kind of gal but they are light and flavorful. Perfect with my beer.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
At first I was skeptical of the place before I got in, but I was glad my friends suggested this place. Loved the atmosphere in there. They have daily specials and Saturdays they have live music but not sure when it starts. 

I had the buffalo chicken wrap with with fries and it was great! The fries were delicious! Our waiter was friendly and attentive even with the place being completely packed. Portion and price of the food is reasonable too. They don't overprice their food like some Nashville restaurants do.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I must say this was a great spot to visit on my vacation to Nashville there are so many other places to choose from but i'm so glad i came here, live music, excellent food, two bars, oh what a wonderful time. Great dessert selection, bread using my absolute favorite. Great art work. This spot is a must!

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
I don't like writing negative reviews, but my experience at Belcourt Taps left me little choice. My wife and I went there on a Groupon for two beer flights and an appetizer. We experienced the following issues:

1) The waitress was unaware the restaurant was doing a Groupon and didn't seem sure how to do the beer flights. As a result...

2) Our beer flights were 10 random beers (well, 9 beers and a cider) without any labels or information as to what they were. Rather than two sets of five beers, it seemed like they told the bartender to just pour 10 arbitrary brews and scatter them throughout the tray. If the word "taps" is in your restaurant's name, you should probably know your way around a keg.

3) The nachos were so low-quality that if I had made them myself, I would have been disappointed with my handiwork. The queso was goopy, lukewarm and clearly store-bought and the toppings were only on one side.

4) Maybe this wasn't their fault, but the band they hired to perform was quite bad. Picture Dolly Parton getting her wig plucked to the tune of a stale guitar and you've just about got it.

Restaurants who offer Groupons are like attractive thirty-somethings on Tinder. If they have to put themselves on that particular medium, they probably don't have their crap together.

Lesson learned.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Bartenders are the best!! Great spot to watch sports, and have a great time. Being a local here in Nashville it's definitely the first bar I'll go to to start my night. And it always has to be my last spot before I go home. Great food and a fantastic atmosphere. Can't go wrong with this place at all.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Off-Broadway, "locals-only" kinda place in the Arcade Alley! Everything on the menu is tasty & fast. I love the hummus, veggie burger, soups, chips, burgers, wings ($0.50 Saturday's & $2 PBR!!), chicken wrap, & the fries have saved my life a few times. If you play your cards right, they'll let you pick the music or tv channel. It's a Live Music Venue too so come for the writer's night.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
I'm visiting Nashville from California and BB Kings was recommend by several people. 

I will now be one of those people spreading the word about how good their food is. I tried the ribs, both the wet and the dry. I actually preferred the dry ribs. They were full of meet and I left the bone clean! The coleslaw, beans, and corn bread are perfect sides that really seal the deal. 

The only downfall was we had to pay a $5 cover even though we weren't buying any alcohol, so that was another $15 we weren't expecting to spend. 

But overall, great environment and outstanding taste! Highly recommended!!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We wanted some music off of busy broadway so we decided to try out BB Kings blues club.  The wait staff were very friendly and attentive.  The food was very tasty and portions were large.   I got the the pork nachos and they were absolutely amazing!   We listened to the band called "the all stars" and the music was the best we heard in Nashville!   Definitely will be back to BB Kings next time we return to Nashville!!!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: It was really cool to be at a historic place that holds so much significance for music. We didn't do a tour, the stage was being put back together from the holiday show. We walked around the grounds which was really well maintained. The store and gift shop has many cool things to look at and purchase. The staff was friendly and greeted us promptly. Enjoyed our short visit here. Next time, I would love to see a show!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: We only stopped in for drinks. The selection is amazing! So many beers on tap! The bartender was helpful with questions. The decor is quirky and entertaining. It's a great spot to meet with friends. My only suggestion would be to add some gluten friendly food items for those of us who can't tolerate gluten but would like a snack. Small issue but just a suggestion. We loved this bar

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I did not expect to like this place at all.  I'd hear vaguely of the Grand Ole Opry, but didn't realize it was a real place.  I was completely ignorant of country music, and only went here for my wife's birthday because she is a huge country music fan.  Thus, we visited Nashville.  I was pleasantly surprised both with the city as well as the Grand Ole Opry  

They do a great job of keeping the Opry House in good condition.  The staff in particular was great and clearly enjoyed their jobs.  Food/drinks were much better than expected, including several craft beers available on tap.  The show we saw was diverse in terms of the acts, and genuinely engaging.  The host layed on the 'Grand Ole Opry' dogma a little thick for me, but the music compensated for it.  We stayed for the backstage tour afterwards.  It was extremely cool to hear all of the stories about the place, and also to see the performers heading out; you really tour the exact same space!

Completely understand why this is a must do.  We'll be back!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We stopped here for some lunch the food was ok.  They have a stage and theres always someone performing the entertainment was good.  The service was fast.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Ate here for lunch. Had pulled pork platter that ranked up with the great establishments in Kansas City. Very impressed with good and service. But thoroughly amazed at the quality of the live music even at 3 in the afternoon. My only complaint, if you view it that way, too many items on the menu to choose from. Guess I will have to make a return trip.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: For this country music geek, this was a huge check off my bucket list! This was my first time to Nashville and my first time to the Opry! It was a magical experience!  The pure energy combined with nostalgia made for a great show!  The new building is very nice. I was a little worried that it wouldn't be as special not being in its original location but It didn't matter a bit once I was there! They have a food truck and snack bars available as well as bar. All items you purchase there can be taken into the show. I highly recommend arriving early and purchasing your tickets ahead of time because it gets very crowded!! Also, don't take more than you need in with you. The only reason I'm not giving it 5 stars is because of the seating. It's all bench type seating (like a church pew) and it was uncomfortably crowded. Like, we couldn't put our arms comfortably to our sides crowded. A little awkward especially if you are seated next to a larger person. However, I would definitely go again!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Review is for the Grand Ole Opry Backstage Tour: 

This is a nice tour to indulge in the history of country music. It's a really laid back walking tour led by your tour guide. It's not boring/cheesy and you'll learn a little about the Opry's history and walk the path of the singers who perform there. You'll see videos along the way, hosted by Blake Shelton. And you never know when you may see a celebrity there!  (Hunter Hayes was there when we were touring.)

Parking is free because it's the mall parking lot, which is right next to the Opry. We walked right up for a tour around noon on a Tuesday in July, but be sure to check the website because I believe tours times change based on events going on. You can book ahead online to guarantee a tour.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
When i travel I like finding out-of-the-way places brimming with local character; in essence, the anti-chain. B.A.D. nails it.

Wandering around the area in the early afternoon on a hot Saturday, my son and I saw an amateurish sign on the street talking about how BAD the place was. We had to investigate.

The A/C was working well and we sat at the bar. I had a fried catfish dish, my son had a burger. Both were good. The staff was friendly (and quite attractive, I might add), and did not pick on me for being from out of town. Lots of visual stimulation on the walls - signs and other stuff that's fun to look at. After getting fleeced at Opryland, it was nice to get a decent meal at a fair price.

Recommended.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This was a gem of a find in downtown Nashville. Delicious food, I had a vegetarian black bean burger, one of the best! Everything was fresh. The full bar, great beers, urban eclectic atmosphere at a very reasonable price made this one I would return to in a minute.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: This place is a hidden gem! We read reviews and man we're we satisfied. My husband and I had the Southwest burger and it was amazing, the broccoli cheese soup was to die for, the Cajun chicken sandwich was great too. We are from out of town and will be sure to come back when we return to Nashville!!

name: Music City Tippler
text: I have to say first and foremost I only experience The Tippler from a private yelp party perspective, so I can't really comment on what the place is like under normal circumstances. It was pretty cool inside though, 1920s sort of feeling, dim sexy lighting and ample space. I thought it was a neat place to have a private party, we took over the downstairs room that has a wee stage. The bartender who was in charge of us down there was also extremely upbeat and very obliging. Thank you mr. bartender for putting up with us and pouring some strong drinks. I should have gulped a giant glass of water with my second Golden Yelpy. Anyway I'm not sure I'll find myself back at the Tippler anytime soon because I rarely go out in this area of town but I feel like it's a pretty cool spot for midtown, I'd rather go to Tippler than the Red Door Saloon, let's put it that way.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Hey.... I was in a group of 8 people and we had waited practically 2 hours from the time we put our names on the waiting list to the time we got our food. Two of us got the southern fried platter and we did NOT get the hush puppies we ordered because they "ran out." For people who waited TWO hours to eat , that is not acceptable at all! Furthermore , the catfish tasted like saltwater and their Mac and cheese ( the substitute for our hush puppies) was just pasta with shredded cheese on it .. shredded cheese that this establishment didn't even bother to melt ! Wow . So disappointing . This is shameful. You should charge for the music and definitely not the food . That was 2 hours of my life I will never get back . Don't go here .

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Dive bar.  You get little cheap plastic cups and if they get busy they make you go to the bar to get drinks from your table, but of course it's packed and hard to get through.  Not worth the effort.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: We received very poor service.  Server walked by us 3 times-  we had to go to the bar to place a drink order and ask for food menus.  The bartender asked us where we'd be and said someone would be right over.  We were outside in the nonsmoking area and the server walked by three times again, taking drink and food orders from neighboring tables and completely ignoring us.  We are locals, but won't be back.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This is a very good place to go to listen to music whats cool is there are different singers every night. Fun place especially if youre in to country music.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I have been here before but the band was just alright so I decided to visit again with associates and the band was amazing with a good vibe it was my sister birthday and we had a blast the band sung happy birthday to her and she was shocked lol... Ok I ordered the catfish and shrimp which was delicious and for my drink can't really say I tried a little of everything but all was good to my satisfaction. Everyone there In our group was very pleased with everything except we were  there at 530pm on Saturday and it was free but waiting on others in our party we ended up walking in at 6pm and had to pay a cover charge which we will know next time lol. It's a great place to visit.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: very good burgers. I had the aloha burger and my wife had the turkey burger. Nice cold beers and service very good and friendly. Had the pork quesadilla for appetizer... great prices nothing over $10. As their motto says BAD is GOOD...,We totally agree. check it out.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: this is a hidden gem-behind union station hotel-you can get food-yes good food after midnight-fun staff and plates on the ceiling-it really was actually pretty cool-i would tell you to go and i will be back

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
My sister in law and I were out for a walk and discovered this gem.
It was pretty busy for a place well hidden. We ordered the hot chicken wrap. It was HOT but good. The fries were crispy and well seasoned. 
 I am sorry we did not get the Jalapenos but I wont make that mistake on my return trip. It will be very soon. The service was great.The lemon drop martini needed a little help but worth ever penny. Tuesday nights have 5.00 margaritas and martinis!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Here is why I gave the opry 2 stars instead of 5... While the show is always top-notch, the parking situation at this location is HORRIBLE. It's a deal-breaker. You will most likely park in an already crowded mall parking lot (next to Dave and Buster's and a high movie theater with an IMAX...)...  here's the thing, you can probably find a spot. that's not the problem. The bad news is that it takes FOREVER to leave. Shame on the Gaylord company for not hiring event staff to help with parking. We sat for a half hour and never moved. not an inch. finally, the traffic moved enough for me to turn my car around and go the other way (fortunately, I knew of the other exit from that area or we would have been there, stuck in the parking lot for at least an hour, maybe two). If being stuck in a lot is appealing to you, I highly recommend.

name: Anthem
text:
This venue had mediocre music that didn't have mass appeal. Don't get me wrong, it looks nice. Unfortunately, that's the extent to which I'll compliment this place. It was apparent as soon as I walked in that most of the 10 people who were there all night knew each other. Maybe it's because I went on a Friday, which is Latin night? For the most part, the place was dead. The very few people who were there had a snooty air about them...the ambiance in general was very pretentious. That sort of environment is maybe ok in Miami or LA, but in Nashville it just doesn't work. 

There was nowhere to sit...not because there weren't available seats, but because if you wanted to sit in a booth, you HAD TO RESERVE IT? WTF IS THAT? SINCE WHEN DO YOU HAVE TO PAY TO SIT DOWN SOMEWHERE? CALL ME CHEAP, BUT I'M NOT WILLING TO DO IT JUST YET. 

12th and Porter across the street is a way better investment.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I'm a beer knurd and home brewer and love the variety. I always get great food and service too!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Do not ever park in that lot, they scam you big time. It takes forever to get out. Park at the mall instead and get out fast and free.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I was visiting from out of town and came here for a sandwich and a beer. While the sandwich, beer and atmosphere were all great, when the bill came, my impression of the place tanked. My bill was $12.28 and my server brought me back $7.00. When I mentioned that I thought she didn't give me the right change, she patted her apron and said "Oh, we don't DO change." You don't "do" change, but you charge people in increments of less than a whole dollar?! So each server is, in effect, stealing from each table?? I was stunned. If she had 20 tables in a night and took .75 extra from each that's an extra $15.00 in her pocket. If you don't want to "do" change as a restaurant policy, then charge your patrons in increments of a dollar - had my bill actually BEEN $13.00, I would have been fine with it and would have tipped at least 20%. As it was, I got out my phone and figured out that $1.84 was exactly 15%, and left her $1.12 to make up for the .72 she stole. If this is a restaurant policy, it's appalling. It left a horrible taste in my mouth, and I've told no less than a dozen people about it. Change your policy, Flying Saucer, and quit stealing from your patrons.

name: Third Man Records
text:
Make your way to Third Man Records if you're a rock 'n roll or Jack White fan! It's almost like a shrine to the musician that he made for himself. You can get knick knacks like wax guitar figures or even pins and chocolates. On the more of the expensive side, they also have unique records and a well-curated selection of music you can buy or play in their on-site music booth and record player. It's very fun to experiment with the sound booths and listen to tunes and bands that you haven't heard of before! 

Another experience you can try is recording your own voice on vinyl! It's more expensive and I wouldn't spend that much if you're not a singer. They have a music booth here that records directly to vinyl. I personally didn't choose to do so because I didn't want to spend money on something I wouldn't use. I don't sing professionally (aside from bad karaoke! and in the shower!). The store also has cool vintage items like old guitars and relics from Nashville's past that you can look at. It's like a time capsule, mini museum. 

However, the space is very small, and you can tour the shop in a matter of minutes. It's too bad that the store is a bit further out from the downtown area, so you once you're quickly done - there's nothing else to do in the area. There are only warehouses surrounding it. It's quite random and a little sketch! (A couple folks came up to me in the parking lot to ask random questions and eyed our car). Just park your car in their designated lot, which can fit no more than a handful of cars, and you'll be fine. We didn't buy anything, but it was fun to experience what it would be like to be Jack White for an hour!

My favorite of all things, funny enough, is the building's exterior! I love the design and the sleek black brick and vintage font! You can't miss it. There's also a photo-worthy radio statue on top of the building. Photos abound!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This is one of the best concerts I have ever been too! The venue is breathtaking but not anywhere I would expect! The prices for drinks and food don't cost you an arm and a leg! But the best part is that there honestly is not a bad seat anywhere! It feels so intimate. I also highly recommend the back stage tour! It truly is one of the best parts & you learn so much about its history & the members! You  only need to take the tour once, but we will 100% be back for a concert every time we visit Nashville!

name: Music City Tippler
text:
Give your happy hour a little more sparkle and go visit this place! The drinks were great , the ambeiance was devine and the food DeLish'!
I tried the chicken sammies/sliders, the brochetta, the fried mac&cheese, and the spicy tuna appetizers... watch out ya'll this food is AMAZING! 
I will definately be back!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Thought it would be cool to listen to Blues while enjoying dinner so we made a reservation here.  When we got to the restaurant (which was more like a bare bones glorified bar) we were told that there was a five dollar cover per person to sit and eat dinner.  I mean, is that even a thing when you are having dinner? Nowhere on there website does it mention this.  Had we known, we would never have gone there (so many good venues to listen to good music for free in Nashville). Since we were already there we decided to give it a shot.  

The waiter came to take out order.  I had seen in the reviews that patrons raved about their Shrimp and Grits and my mouth was watering to give it a try.  My sister planned on ordering the Cajun Catfish topped with shrimp.  We had each already ordered a house specialty drink and were enjoying the very good band that was playing.  

Upon ordering our meals we were told that the restaurant was out of shrimp.  So we both had to find another dish in a limited menu where over half the dishes contained shrimp.  If we hadn't paid the 10 dollars in cover fees and ordered drinks we would have walked out at this point.

I ended up ordering spicy Chicken Fried Chicken served with Macaroni and Cheese and grilled veggies.  My sister ordered a chicken pasta dish.  My meal was actually very good and something that I would usually never order. My sister did not care for her dish.   

During the hour and a half that we were there the band took two 20-30 minute breaks and ended early, which given the cover charge was ridiculous.  Upon complaining to the manager we were able to have the cover refunded, but he was so rude he would not look at us or answer us while opening the cash register to do so.  No apologies, no nothing.

To be fair if I had to rate my actual meal or the band that we were listening to or our Waiter (he was very apologetic) I would have given it a higher review.  But the 1 Star is for our overall experience.  I would never recommend this place based on the experience we had.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text:
If you don't mind a little smoke, and want cheap beer and drinks while you get your karaoke on, then Ms. Kelli's may be the place for you!

The biggest plus?  The DJ keeps the place hopping between singers with some great tunes that will have you dancing on the dance floor up front in no time at all.  And with $3 beers located in a large bucket right next to the dance floor- you will be sure to be strutting and singing!

But if you want to sing- you better be ready to tip the DJ or else you will sit and sit and sit.  And please don't go asking the bartender for some "high falutin'" drink  . . you're gonna be disappointed as standard mixers and beer are the de riguer here (along with some jello shots, or so I hear!)

Printers Alley has tons of karaoke choices.  But Ms. Kelli's is one of my favs . . . .even if I smelled like an ashtray when I left the joint!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
The flying saucer is cool. It's the only bar I've seen in Nashville so far that actually has beer on tap. Not sure why that is. Maybe a Tennessee thing? Anyway, if you love craft beer, this is the place to be! Dozens of beer on tap, and many more in bottles. They also offer beer flights so I had the Tennessee flight. 5 great local beers. 

The food is good too. Had a polish sausage that was excellent. Oh yeah, they have pool tables too. Great place for beer lovers!

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Solid place to go listen to some music. 

Small intimate just what I was looking for. 

The Caesar salad was actually really good. Great dressing. On be the smaller side but perfect with the chicken. 

Would not recommend the house white wine, but I loved the B nectar cider. 

Pro tip sit at the bar if you want fast service.

name: Third Man Records
text: As Vault Club Member and a Third Man distributer for my record store Santa Ana Spin I have to say it was so epic walking up to this iconic building. As a musician I had to try the Third Man Recording Booth and it is one of the best things in the record shop world! Even if you're not a musician you can record spoken word or stuff like that! They're listening booth is one of the best also and you can listen to pretty much any White Stripes album or Third Man artist. It's a super organized and the staff is very friendly and informative! A must check out store if you're into the revival of vinyl!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
The name Flying Saucer definitely made me think of a UFO but there is nothing extraterrestrial about this place and I did not see any aliens. However, the saucers (plates) on the wall are a sign that you're at the right place since the whole wall is decorated with them. 

The place--
The building is absolutely huge and this is the perfect place to come with a huge posse. You could have a group of 10 people and be fine in this place. Since it was just me and a friend I felt like I should call more people just to fill up the huge table we were sitting at. 

The service--
It did seem they were a bit understaffed when we came since there was one server tending to multiple very large tables and we had to try and catch her attention for about 10 minutes at the end when we were trying to leave. Otherwise, she was very nice and we did not wait to long for the food. 

The food/drink--
Beer lovers can rejoice, this is your haven. Food-wise what we ordered was very simple. We each got the house salad and then split the nachos. The jalapeno vinaigrette was good but definitely had a kick to it! The nachos were pretty standard but good. 

Parking--
They do give you a discount if you park in the lot below but I think because we had been there for a few hours (to the Frist then to Flying Saucer) we still had to pay $4 for parking. I would only come back to the Flying Saucer if I had another reason to be in the area otherwise I do not enjoy having to pay for parking! 

Overall, a fun place to grab some beers and socialize.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: negative stars!!! Sister and Dad were both harassed by bartender and bouncers simply after my dad was trying to help people behind us order drinks since they were being ignored. This woman didn't serve us once before during the 5 hours we were there (the other bartenders did and were very nice and knew us by name when ordering drinks). She decided to throw a big scene and yell every swear word in the book TO MY 50 YEAR OLD DAD!! Also to mention we were having a nice family outing to watch some good football. We will never go back and we sure spread some word about this place... not in a good way! No one should EVER speak to anyone that way. Absolutely uncalled for and pathetic. She should be fired ASAP

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text:
I've agreed to elaborate on this review after the owner messaged me saying I *must* be mistaken:

 However, those two stars up there, they are still for the bartenders ONLY. Otherwise this place sucked with JayJay as their karaoke DJ. He is still a crook, and the one thing the owner neglects to address is the fact that I paid this KJ $10 to move up in line and it didn't work. He swears up and down that favoritism wasn't a factor, but I can only go by the experience we had. The same people  going over and over and over and over.......and over again, as evidenced by the precious video cited. 

Yess, we did finally sing AFTER I paid him off and waited even longer only to watch the same people go up again. Why did I not leave? Why did I sing anyway? Because I would have felt guilty making my friends wait so long without salvaging the last shred of fun left here, also I would've been extremely angry if I lost $10 for nothing. We sang out of principle and spite.

No matter what is claimed by the business owner, the fact remains that we had a terrible time. I was in Nashville for 5 days and this was the only establishment that did not measure up to the rest in terms of customer service and quality. If you read through their reviews, this is obviously not an isolated case.

It wouldn't be fair to the other places if I up'd their rating based on what the owner's reaction was, and not based on our experience. Other places earn their stars without bias, and that's how it should be. 

Next time I'm in Nashville, I will give it another shot out of principle but I will not bribe the KJ again just to sing. I will wear the shortest shorts I can find and see if that works.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Amazing! The grounds of the Opry house are filled with fun and elegance. They have a new attraction now so make sure to get to the Acuff house for a tour before you head backstage! 

I did the backstage tour with Will. He was wonderful. He was funny and extremely knowledgeable about the property, people and process. He took it from a general tour to an experience. I'm new to the area and can not wait to come watch some concerts! Amazing place

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
***REVIEW FROM AN EXPERIENCE IN JUNE 2015: I just wanted to let everyone reading my review know that even though this review was written in the beginning of 2018; I went to this place in June 2015 (however I am sure if I went to this place again the review would be similar). A few days ago I was talking to someone about places visit in New Orleans because they are interested in visiting the city. I realized that when I went to New Orleans I went to a lot of amazing places but I never wrote Yelp reviews for them because I did not start writing Yelp reviews until the beginning of 2017. I enjoyed many places on my trip and I wanted to share my experiences with everyone  even though they are a few years old. So I decided to dig up some old pictures and write the reviews.

I would also like to add that most of the experiences I am writing about are places I went to while I was on a guided tour for my trip. I went on a Collette Tour called America's Music Cities. Most of the places we saw and ate at were planned because of the tour. During the tour we stopped at 3 major cities New Orleans, Memphis, and Nashville (and few other stops along the way).
