I just wanted to let everyone know that since I was on a tour my experiences may have been a little different compared to those who went to these places and were not on a tour (they went on their own) It was an amazing tour and I definitely recommend it.***

A dream come true!! I love country music and for the most part the only music I listen to. As I have mentioned I was on a music tour in different cities of the South but I was most excited to listen to the music in Nashville. 

I was so excited to get the opportunity to go to the Grand Ole Opry and little did I know this would be a night that I will never forget. We saw the show and the backstage tour after the show. 

We had wonderful seats on the lower level near the center of the stage. Many great artists performed throughout the night (see pictures to see who performed). Towards the end of the show a special guest who wasn't on the setlist walked on the stage. It was TRISHA YEARWOOD. Trisha started to talk about how it was last minute and she wasn't originally going to perform (that's why she wasn't on the setlist). She mentioned how she didn't even have time to call her band because it was so last minute. She continues talking and to this day I remember the last sentence or so... she said (and I believe these are her exact words) "...but luckily I live with a Grand Ole Opry Member so please welcome my husband Mr. Garth Brooks" then GARTH BROOKS walked on stage!! It was absolutely amazing and an unforgettable night. Only a few of the Opry employees knew that they were showing up so it was a shock to a lot of the employees as well. Anyway, Trisha and Garth performed many songs together. I didn't know a lot of the songs because they were older but it was still such an amazing experience. I also got the opportunity to get closer to the stage to take a few pictures (you can see where I was sitting in the other pictures vs. where I was when I got to get closer to take pictures of Trisha and Garth). The staff didn't mind that I got closer to the stage as long as I didn't block anyone's view. I posted a few of them and I am sorry they are blurry..my hands were shaking with excitement! 

I also heard when I was there that Garth hadn't been to the Opry in about 10 years so it was even more cool that he showed up that night!

Now onto the backstage tour! The tour was awesome! I learned a lot about the Grand Ole Opry, the history of the Grand Ole Opry, and Grand Ole Opry Members. I was able to see many of the dressing rooms and learn about each of the rooms (they all have different themes). Lauren Alaina was still in her dressing room when we were getting our tour and she showed us her dressing room and talked to the group for a little bit. Looking back at the experience now, I wish I would have gotten a picture with her! It was a fun tour with a lot of information. We even got the opportunity to go on stage and stand in the circle! 

It was a truly an amazing and unforgettable experience. I definitely recommend that you go to the Grand Ole Opry. After all, you never know who may show up (or who you might get to meet)!!

Enjoy,
Simona

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: My boyfriend and I are in Nashville for the first time. Before we left my boyfriends father asked us to send him a picture from Redneck Riviera because he absolutely loves John Rich. On our first night out we went straight there in hopes of having a great time and getting our picture. We were greeted at the door by a bouncer who asked for our ID. He checked my boyfriends ID and instantly said it was a fake. My boyfriend offered to show him more proof of his age but the bouncer refused to look at it and told us to leave. My boyfriend is 24 so he was understandably frustrated. A few friends came over and asked why he wasn't being let in and the bouncer said that he had a fake ID and I who barely said anything at this point, "have my ass wrapped around my ears". After being insulted and belittled I had no interest in being at this bar but my boyfriend spoke with the manager Eric. He refused to even look at his ID and blindly followed the bouncer. I've never in my life been treated with such disrespect by an establishment. Needless to say this really put a damper on what should have been an amazing first trip to Nashville. I strongly suggest avoiding this bar at all cost if you don't want to be told you have your ass around your ear.

name: Ole Red
text: Sorry Blake but your service sucks! Went to the roof top bar and couldn't even get waited on. Even asking for a server no one came over. Disappointed

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: This place is HUGE! I don't think there is a bad seat in the house. There are plenty of restrooms around the corner for each exit, which is not the case for other places. There are also many concessions to chose from out side of every exit. This place is conveniently located and very clean. There are several entrance/exits which is very nice. I was surprised at how cold they can make this place for the training we had, even though it is a hokey station, it just so big. Great place!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The food was good but a bit expensive.  The margaritas were fun and plentiful! The best part was the music! I'm in love with all the live music in the area. It was a Monday night and the main road was still alive it music when we headed back to our hotel around midnight. I can't wait to come back to Nashville!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We only went to the bar here to listen to the live music. They had a couple of guys playing acoustic guitars -- they took requests and interacted a lot which made it fun. I got a strawberry blended margarita which was delish & we shared a slice a Key Lime Pie which was heavenly. The waitress was friendly and attentive. We had a great time here!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Hockey night and so a little slow. Service was just okay. The food was not worth the cost at all. Dry sandwich.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: This was a rad arena. Came here to watch my LA Kings play. My team got shelled, but the crowd was amazing. They have a very passionate fan base. The food here, compared to back home in Southern Ca, was amazing! They need to bring the menu to staples center.

name: Ole Red
text: Let's start out about how excited I was to try Ole Red since I'm a huge Blake Shelton fan. His restaurant has to be as great as he is right? Unfortunately I was totally wrong, I've been twice & both times were very disappointing. Both times I sat upstairs on the rooftop & the service was HORRIBLE!!!! If your ok with waiting 30 mins before someone even acknowledges you and than another 30mins to get your food this is your place. Not to mention both times our waitress never checked on us and both times we had to flagged down someone else to bring our check. Don't waste your time.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Needed a place to hangout while waiting on another reservation, reminded me of why I hated bars in college. If people are belligerent at 8:15pm, something is wrong.

name: National Underground
text:
As other reviewers mentioned, the man that I am guessing is the manager  really does spend his time running around harassing customers and yelling at staff. At first we did not realize he worked there as he was wearing an oversized baseball hat, oversized graffiti T-shirt and chains (he looked like he stepped straight out of a rap music video) and when he was not picking fights with customers or staff he was lurking in a corner smoking behind the bar 

We were waiting in line for acme and saw this place didn't have a line or a cover so we decided to give it a try. We were a group of 4       professionals and their spouses and we spent quite a lot of money ordering drinks before we sat down in a corner of the bar to quietly mind our own business and listen to the music. The place is nothing special but our drinks were only watered down the normal about for broadway and the band was decent. 

Not 15 minutes into our visit this manager physically grabbed me by the arm as I was walking to the restroom and proceeded to yell at me, refusing to let go of my arm. Since he was dressed like a gangster rather than an employee and I couldn't hear what he was shouting I just broke free and ran away from him ... but he followed me back to my group and started physically assaulting other members of my group and yelling at them. It turns out that one of us had a small water bottle with them and he was trying to take it away because, as other reviewers mentioned, this place charges for water, even if you just spent a ton of money buying top shelf liquor. When he was done berating and assaulting us he grabbed the water bottle from the table and wandered outside with it. 

While we awkwardly finished our drinks we watched him yell at other customers and his bartenders. We left as quickly as possible and will never ever return. I hope someone sues him for assault.

name: Marathon Music Works
text:
I like catching shows at Marathon Music Works.  This is a very cool venue that shares an old car factory building with Lightening 100 and Corsair Distillery.  It's fairly trendy and even a sold-out show is comfortable to attend and it's easy to find parking.  We paid $5 for a lot, but you could easily park on the street a block or two away.

My wife and I saw Trampled by Turtles and Apache Relay there on Saturday.  It was an excellent show and Winston Marshall (Mumford and Sons) played banjo for a couple of songs (it's ok to be jealous)!  We also caught Yonder Mountain String Band there earlier this year.

This venue is standing only.  I'm probably getting old for this type of place, but you do have a lot of younger folks in attendance.  That also lends itself to a lot of stupid in the crowd.  The good news is that there isn't really a bad spot in the place.  If you get sick of fighting for a spot, then just retreat to a corner somewhere and enjoy the show.

There are two main bars in MMW and they have a surprisingly good beer selection with even a few craft choices mixed in.  I was a bit surprised by that.  With this being a small venue (it was sold out for TBT), the lines are short.  

This is an excellent venue to see a concert.  It's fairly intimate and everything about it is easy--parking, sight lines, and drinks.  You will stand for the entire show, but everything else is great.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Note I'm posting this before he end of Game 6. What a shame that the operators of the arena soooooo OVER-PRODUCE the artifcial sounds played during 100℅ of the breaks. 

Why not allow the fans the respect of non-led chants?? EVERY BREAK WE ARE SUBJECT TO A FAKE ASSAULT ON THE SENSES which belittles the fans and wrecks the game.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Pros: Great GF options, awesome server, friendly service, affordable prices, short wait on a busy weekend night. 

Cons: food was just mediocre.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: There are other places on the strip to go.. Skip it. The drinks are weak and basically all ice. Food is mediocre. The wait is long. Not worth it.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We are having a great time, good food, great drinks and best of all our waiter Jesse stevens. He is the best. Stop by and ask for him he will make sure you have a great time. Thank you Jesse Stevens!!!

name: Marathon Music Works
text:
I road tripped it up to Nashville from Atlanta to see Dweezil Zappa here on 1/21/2017, since I'm a huge fan of his tribute band and they put on an amazing show when I saw them in Atlanta about 2 months prior. I was a little concerned after I bought my ticket and saw the reviews of this place that said that the sound is not very good. 

I ended up being pleasantly surprised. If you read my other reviews then you will know that I am pretty picky about acoustics. I have to say though that I was not disappointed at all by the sound inside of Marathon Music Works. Sure, it isn't the prettiest venue in the world, as the inside of it looks and feels like (and might even be?) a warehouse. But I don't go to concerts for the attractiveness of the venues. I highly recommend Marathon Music Works to anyone who is an avid concertgoer.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We've been to Margaritaville in Vegas and were hesitant to stop in since there were so many other honky tonks. The main reason we stopped was to get a couple landsharks on tap. The dance area was very spacious and the music was good. The bartender was very quick to get our drinks refilled and always had a smile. Everyone seemed to be having a good time. Seems like the bar could be expanded or have a 2nd area for service I had to squeeze through a crowd for drinks.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Valerie was the most kind and fun server.  Very accommodating for our large high maintenance crew.  Great atmosphere and lots of fun!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Great beer, and had one of the best burgers ever. Get it with the egg on top. I'm drooling just thinking about it.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
My wife andI were on vacation and we tried a lot of tap rooms.

I ordered an IPA,good stuff.

The bartender was cool. good times with my wife.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
My wife and I stop here everytime we visit Nashville. The space is very cool and the beers are solid and well-priced. My wife's favorite is the Southern Wit, which is a nice take on a wheat beer. They also had 2 rye beers on tap, and ryes are a special favorite of mine. 

During our visit in June of 2014, we got to sit on the deck (there are two, and upper and lower) and enjoy the weather and the beer. There happened to be a music and food festival that day, and siting outside enjoying the weather and music was awesome. This is a very cool place, and we'll make sure we're back in the future.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Bland, bland, bland food, over priced also. Two Margaritas and one appetizer, almost 30 bucks. Margaritas were almost all ice. Quesadilla was tasteless and one tables spoon of sour cream, quac and salsa, when we asked for more salsa we finished the Quesadilla before the second table spoon of salsa was brought to us, would never go back and would not recommend to anyone. Ended up going to a local Mexican restaurant and had margaritas half the price, lots of food, bill was much cheaper and service was outstanding.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: If Roberts is all jammed up and a$$es to elbows, this is a solid honky Tonkin second choice. Good prices on bottled beer (no draft) and they usually have some talented musicians on stage. Last time I was here, I was treated to a tap dancing man with a zz top beard in full overalls. But I can't promise he'll be there all the time. In fact, if I could, Layla's night edge out Roberts in my honky hierarchy.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Best bluegrass kickass music I experienced in Nashville, great environment, great crowd, highly recommended.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Great venue, absolutely love watching the predators here! My only real complaint is the lack of leg room in the upper section (300 level). Super annoying trying to keep your knees off the person in front of you. Love the concession options, there's literally something for everyone! However, the drink prices are extremely steep.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Loved the vibe and the beer! Super neat space with refreshing craft beers. I had the Belgian wit which was nice and light. Perfect for summer! There was a large outdoor space both upper and lower patios. Looks like dogs were allowed outside - which I love! It is a bit off the beaten path so it took us a minute to find it but was totally worth it!

name: Ole Red
text:
Hands down the worst meal we had in Nashville.

As a vegetarian, we had made reservations here so that I could try the BBQ mushroom sandwich. I was pretty pumped. There were only two of us with reservations for lunch. It was not packed at all and yet, every aspect of the meal was a mess.

First, we were seated by a window and there were these tiny gnat bugs flying everywhere which was kind of gross. The window was closed.

Second, we ordered the red and white sangria. They were not good- just straight wine with a few pieces of fruit in it. We swapped these out for margaritas which were much better, but definitely from a bottle. Our waitress left the sangria on the table. She didn't bother clearing them.

We ordered fried pickles as an appetizer to share, I ordered the BBQ mushroom sandwich and my mom ordered the hot chicken sandwich. Our pickles came fairly quickly and were ok. They were sliced thin and long so the breading kind of came off of them. I've never seen fried pickles like that. They were ok but messy.

45 minutes after we placed our order, we were starting to get restless as our waitresses hadn't given us an update and we had other things to do that day. Around this time, she informed us that they were out of the BBQ mushrooms. This was at about 1:15 now so early in the day! I was very disappointed and really annoyed it took that long to inform us. I decided not to order anything else as the cauliflower steak didn't seem appetizing and I can get a veggy burger anywhere. It took the waitress another 10 minutes to come back to check on my order and at that point, my mom just asked for hers to go. We waited another 15 minutes or so and now my mom is annoyed also. We had been there over an hour. 

The store manager did bring us the check at this point and made a fuss about waiving the BBQ sandwich and the Sangrias, the sandwich we never even got and the Sangria which we didn't even drink! um, thanks??

Trust me, you can find a much better restaurant in Nashville! Don't bother with this one!!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Good food but the server Karah was Great!  Always nice to have a server take care of you and she is super friendly!!!

name: 12th & Porter
text: The new ownership has really nailed re-opening 12th n Porter.  the concert room is renovated and they have great acts performing there all the time now.  The drink selection is great, and the FOOD IS STELLAR!  One of my new favorite spots for lunch or dinner in town,  the Candy Fries are amazing and the menu us full of delicious items.  I won't be able to order the same thing every time like I usually do at my other favorite spots!  So glad this place is open again and killing it!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: First time I've been to a Margaritaville. My expectations weren't high because it's only rated 3.5 stars, but it was a Friday night and any place that was 4 stars or higher had a long wait. Wish we had waited! The staff was friendly, which was the best part aside from no wait at 7:00 on a Friday night - that alone should say something! The food was no better than what you would find in your local bar/pub, but it was priced about twice as high. My final bill with tip for 6 people, which only included one beer and one margarita, was close to $200. That was with no appetizer, either! I love Nashville and have been there a few times, but I won't be back to this, or any other Margaritaville. Sorry Jimmy... You all dropped the ball here!

name: National Underground
text: This place blows. No tap water. Ordered a sandwich, got a salad. Waitress had a weird demeanor. #1 burger in Nashville? #1 burger in nowhere!!!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Love this spot!! Some of the best bands I've heard in Nashville play here. Wide variety of drinks. The staff was kind and fun! More authentic/real than some of the other places in the area. Comfortable atmosphere and definitely a must-go next time I'm in Nashville!

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Awesome double decker patio, great spot to share a drink on warmer nights. Excellent food as well!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Can I say we had the best waiter ever - Chris. Very friendly, helpful and accommodating which hey I think is a rarity at most places anymore. Nice restaurant on Broadway. Very clean, open, and not too loud. If you're getting an appetizer go for the $16 nachos...they will not disappoint.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Best time ever.  Enjoyed the band and the people. The afternoon bartender was from the Boston and very personable.  When we came back the second day he asked where my Blackhawks cap was, as he was a Bruins fan.  Really enjoyed the night bands   Good time I recommend.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I had a good experience at Margaritaville - Nashville. I didn't have high hopes for the food, but my jambalaya was quite good. The margaritas were a bit weak, but the service and entertainment made up for it. The atmosphere is ok and it seemed to be a decent place to bring the kids also. Margaritaville is worth a stop if you've never been to one, but probably not a place you want to go to over and over again.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Music and margaritas were great - my cheddar BBQ burger was ok...nothing special. In fact, my homemade burgers taste better. The sweet potato fries also left room to be desired. Thankfully, the Fins to the Left and Tropical Waters were tasty. I probably won't be back though...

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
This was my favorite of the breweries in the gulch area. This brewery had a lot of space to hang out inside, had an outdoor patio with plenty of seating as well. If you walk upstairs to the top floor they have plenty of fun games to play along with a separate bar to order drinks. Here I went with a wit they had on tap as my drink. For some tapas I went with wings, a cheese plate and frog legs! If your
Gonna be in town got to try frog legs at least once. The beer was fantastic and this is a great place to come hang out, watch the game and drink beer.

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
The Schermerhorn Symphony Center is just as beautiful as the music the Nashville Symphony plays. It's always a treat to attend something at the Schermerhorn. I'm honestly surprised that this building was built in 2006. The style makes to look like it's been here for a century, albeit, well kept. The the Neoclassical design with the large columns at the entrance makes it look very stately. Inside the theme continues & there's a grandeur to it all. 

The 1,844 seat Laura Turner concert hall is equally impressive. I really don't think there's a bad seat in the house. We saw Kristen Chenoweth a few weeks ago & sat on the upper, side balcony. We were able to see everything, including the symphony from above. The sound in that hall is amazing. I prefer the side balcony to the seats down on the floor because the seats aren't the theatre type seats & have more leg room. They've always got a bunch of volunteers helping to assist you in finding what floor/door you need to go to find your seat. 

My only issue, and it really isn't with the symphony, & that is parking. The valet at the Schermerhorn Symphony Center is $27. We've never done it because of the price but there's always a long line in front of the building. It almost seems like the just park all the cars in front, I'm not sure how they do it, but it always looks like a madhouse when people are arriving & leaving. We usually stick to finding a spot along Korean Veterans or park at the R lot at Nissan Stadium & walk over the pedestrian bridge.

name: Ole Red
text: After a hard day of working in the morning and a tedious 5 hour drive to Nashville, my friend and I were looking for a mellow place to drink and relax. Ole Red was that Safe haven in a sea of loud crowds. So thankful for the 5th floor and the amazing view that was provided . As an extra bonus, we got a GREAT cardio workout walking up all those flights of stairs. AND THEN BRITTANY OUR WAITRESS was outstanding!!! She was personable and treated us like we were her number one guests for the night. Thanks Brittany and Ole Red for this experience, much appreciated!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
I like Margaritaville, I like all of them, and I'm not a chain restaurant fan usually. But something about those baby blenders with a huge straw and a frozen strawberry margarita inside does something to me.

 I only order the fried pickles, which are a must. My friend and I started our day here at around 11:30 (him the fins out margarita in a blender, and me strawberry marg in a blender) and listening to music and drinking margaritas at the bar this past Sunday. Good spot to stop at, Jimmy Buffett does it right always.

 Don't forget to write on a dollar and stand on the bar to staple it on the wall!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Stopped by on a Wednesday evening after checking out the different entertainment for the evening. The Bluebird Cafe didn't look as promising tonight, but Margaritaville did.  Decor was neat. Very touristy feeling inside.  Wasn't too crowded. I had the shrimp wedge Louis. It was HUGE! But it tasted great! Nice and fresh veggies and the shrimp was not grilled to death. Server was fantastic.  Entertainment was good, but I prefer their own music to their covers. Definitely recommend.

name: Ole Red
text: Blake knows food! The Redneck Nachos and Chicken Champagne bucket were amazing.  More than enough to feed 3 adults and a preteen. They also had great live music. Amazing experience!

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: We enjoyed the patio the weather was so beautiful so we wanted to be outside. We went on a Tuesday night and the band was pretty good. The beers were pretty cold and the bartender seemed burned out, but overall it was ok.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: My wife and I visited with our son and it was great. The staff helped us have a great experience. The beer was great and the food was on point. we are definitely going back and would recommend this to anyone who wants good beer and food and good service

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
To be fair I'm  not generally a chain restaurant guy. They usually are what you expect and consistent. The reason we chose Margaritaville was the variety of the menu, our 2 daughters could not decide what they wanted. Additionally, we had eaten there during CMA a few years ago because my wife wanted island style drink. Our meal consisted of spinach dip, seafood mac and cheese, a side salad, fries, 2 bourbons and a  chicken quesadilla. The total for this $70+ not including tip. Service was fine. Based on the fact seating was less than 70% full the food took way to long to get out. Our server kind of acknowledged it by the fact she said I'll go check to see where your food is coming. When it did arrive the mac and cheese was barely warm and the chicken quesadilla was burnt, to the point not only was it not edible and it smelled burnt. Not sure how you even send this to a table. In a city built on service and entertainment you would think a manager would swing by once a customer asks for an item to be removed from the table and bill. The night before we had been at restaurant across the street on the corner (place with a great bar and counter service)  that manager came by greeted us then again to check to see how our meal was. Margaritaville will continue  to survive because of its cute theme.

After I posted my review I was interested in seeing what others had to say. It seems our experience is similar to others. Whomever is responding to these reviews continues to say the issues will be addressed however it seems like similar issues again and again.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
When my friend and I decided to drive down to Nashville for a long weekend away from Chicago, we decide to do an afternoon of brewery tours. 

I've been to almost a dozen throughout Chicago and Milwaukee so I know how beer is made. I usually go to brewery tours so you can learn about the beers that each brewery makes and you can try a few of their favorites. So when I say I hated this tour I really mean it. 

First of all, this brewery is hard to get to if you're walking and don't know the area. Google Maps tried to make us cross train tracks that had no crossing twice. When we finally found our way around the train tracks, it was down a bunch of dimly streets. Not a fan. I did not feel safe. 

We arrived and they didn't even check to see if we had actually booked a tour and just sent us to the back where the tour was starting. The tour ended up being a quick 20 minute tour of their machines and the process of making beer. It was supposed to be 45 minutes but apparently there was nothing to say. Nothing was said about the beers they make and a little history of this brewery was given, but not much. It was boring.

Once the tour was finished, we were given a token for a free beer. Yay. So I ordered a beer - the IPA - and it was as boring as the tour.

I would've appreciated the opportunity to try more beers on the tour but I guess they don't that. I would've also appreciate learning more about how they make their different beers. 

Overall, this was the most boring brewery tour I've ever gone on. In fact, it was the most boring alcohol tour I've ever been on. It was more boring than the winery tour I went on with my parents when I was 7 - I couldn't touch anything and I couldn't drink anything and I didn't understand anything. 

If you're visiting Nashville from Chicago or Milwaukee and have been on a few brewery tours before, I wouldn't stop here. It will just disappoint you.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I've loved the Bridgestone Arena since I was a child, when it was called the Municipal Auditorium and my first concert was the Osmond's in 1973.  Yeah, so what...I'm 137 years old.  I look really good for my age.

I recently went to see the farewell tour of Elton John.  Now I'm just gonna remind you again, I am 137 years old.
Elton John was playing as long as I can remember and he's only 49.99999 years old now.  If you've never experienced him in concert, sorry 'bout yer luck. 

The Bridgestone has the most spectacular sound system.  It is extremely loud, but it was also extremely clear.  The instruments as well as the lyrics were crisp and clear, as was Elton's voice when he spoke.  His concert being his farewell tour also tells of his journey, and it was very inspiring.  I really can't express how much I enjoyed this particular concert , or how much I have enjoyed every experience I've ever had at the Bridgestone Arena.

name: Ole Red
text: Was excited to go to Ole Red cause I am a Blake Shelton fan. When we got there my boyfriend tried to order an Ole Red beer and they were out. How can you be out of your own beer. The service took a long time at one point we waited for our bill for 20 minutes. Food was good. The tater tots were the best ever.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
I was there with my husband and son for dinner and the food was very good...all but the crab dip. I would pass on that one. My husband had the jambalaya and loved it. My son had the shrimp and crab mac and cheese and really liked that too. I had the chicken sandwich and it was very good.
Service was a little slow but your on vacation right?!

name: Ole Red
text: Very commercial with a full stage, video and light show. Not the Nashville I was looking for. But Ole Red's saving grace was the roof top patio bar. Love it!

name: Marathon Music Works
text:
I researched this venue prior to the 311 show this past weekend, and, as I had not been there before, was pleased to see it was indoor. I falsely associated this with climate control. 
It was HOTTER THAN THE THIRD CIRCLE OF HELL; I saw people ill from over heating, myself so hot, I downed 3 bottled waters, too scared to drink alcohol. 
We sadly left the venue before 311 even finished because we felt too miserable. I was only wearing a short dress, and sweat was literally dripping down the back of my legs.; nude would have been too many clothes. 
The only source of circulation in a sea of sweaty bodies were a few massive fans about 20 feet up that only could be felt right underneath once the venue got crowded. 
I am not sure how this has not been cited as a health hazard, to close in so many patrons in the south, during the summer, with no friggin' air conditioning, but this was my first and last trip there. 
One star, because the layout of bars and bathrooms accommodated the crowd nicely. 
It was also nice to see a big band like 311 in a more intimate setting.
However, a venue so little invested in the comfort of their patrons, that they couldn't somewhat maintain even a healthy temperature, left me wasting money on tickets for a show I couldn't enjoy and a 3 hr. drive to do so.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I stopped by here earlier today with my wife for some afternoon drinks.  We had decided to come to Tennessee Brew Works because we are getting a pint glass from every state (and most major cities) and thought that their logo was perfect for Nashville.  Upon arriving to the Brewery we noticed what a nice outdoor space they had.  However the below freezing temperatures precluded any chance of us utilizing this space and so we went inside.  This brewery has two floors although we mostly stayed on the first floor.  It was simple with a stage in the front, a bar in the back and then some tables made out of barrels and high top stools around them.  You could also see into their brewing facility from here and if you want to go to the bathroom you have to head through the door towards it and get a good view of it.  Even if you don't have to go, it's worth walking in there to get a good view.

As I often do whenever I visit a new brewery, I ordered a flight here.  At Tennessee Brew Works you get to choose 5 pours for $11.  I ended up choosing the Basil Ryeman (saison), Pie Town Session Porter, Extra Easy (English Pub Ale), 1927 (IPA) and finally the Cut Throat Rye IPA.  The first one that I tried was the saison which had that funk that most saison have and it tasted pretty good.  Up second was the Session Porter which I actually thought tasted a little watery.  My wife contested that but to each their own I guess. For my third beer I tried the Extra Easy which was great.  It was a good representation of its style and was smooth and went down quite easily.  Fourth was the IPA which was bright and flavorful with a slight touch of hops at the finish.  Last but certainly not least was the Cutaway Rye IPA which was extremely hop forward leaving quite a bitterness on the finish.  If you asked me there may actually be too much hops in it.  Out of the bunch I would have to say that the IPA was my favorite with the Extra Easy being my second favorite.

The bottom line for me is that I would head back here again in the future.  Tennessee Brew Works occupies a cool space and I thought that their beers were good too.

name: Ole Red
text:
Great atmosphere but food and drinks left us disappointed. It drives me crazy when bars can't keep their seltzer carbonated. My second drink was improved slightly after I mentioned it, from complete flat to mostly flat - my goodness !
My daughter's  burger was too greasy for her - and she loves greasy burgers
My sons pulled pork was excellent 
My salad was soggy and you could tell us was pre- chopped  hours prior , my salmon came out rare 
Such a shame 
Our last meal in Nashville - a low note . Bummer

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
As I make my way through all of the hockey arenas in the NHL (this is #27), I have to say this is in the top 25% for sure.  In addition to being a nice looking arena, conveniently located in the downtown core, I found the stadium easy to get into.  For one thing, they have multiple entrances and have well marked and well regulated "no bag" lines so for people who aren't carrying the majority of their worldly possessions with them to a hockey game, you can get through security very quickly.

It is quick and easy to get to seats and signs mark things well.  For this event, I had nosebleed seats.  They were padded, which made them comfortable, but a little on the narrow side as two of my friends attending had trouble getting their butts in without twisting sideways!

The sound system is nice...clear and not deafening.  The Jumbo Tron is very nice as well.  The only weird thing that I noticed was that between periods, there was no "on ice" activity, such as a puck shoot giveaway or a pee-wee league match.  Maybe that was just the game I saw (where the Penguins beat the Predators) but it was weird.

Exiting the arena was quick and easy, so that is another plus.  I'm a fan!

name: Ole Red
text: Our experience was great and Kayla, the waitress was FANTASTIC!!!!  I would tell Blake Shelton personally how good she is.  Very friendly, attentive, and a hard worker

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: 5 STARS! We really enjoyed this little bar. We walked in after hearing the music from the sidewalk at around 1 PM. The band that was playing was a great honky-tonk three-piece band. The vibe in here is definitely a hole in the wall honky-tonk feel that you need to experience and hopefully you'll get to hear some great music like we did.

name: Ole Red
text:
Delicious brunch on the rooftop lounge!
We read mixed reviews for Ole Red and The Lookout, but decided to make reservations for the brunch on a Sunday. Everything was great! Walking out of the elevator and getting the first glimpse of the rooftop bar/lounge/deck area started our visit off on a positive note. The décor and arrangement are inviting and balances casual with classy, unlike many of the other establishments on Broadway. We were promptly seat on the outdoor deck and presented with the brunch menus, which are in old vinyl record album covers...cool!

They have a nice variety of "brunch" drinks including my new favorite, The bandit-(Bourbon and coffee liqueur cocktail). The others in our group enjoyed the various mimosas. The one misstep in our entire visit, which would normally have me drop a place a couple stars was the quality of their regular black coffee. It was awful, weak, and definitely cheap!  The food was delicious! While you're waiting for your entrees you can help yourself to a display of fresh warm biscuits, muffins, parfaits, and yogurt.  The entrees we tried were: The Hot Spiced Nashville Omelet-filled with pimento cheese, smoked pork, and caramelized onions (delicious), French Toast Casserole-very good & very sweet, and the biscuits & gravy, which were enjoyed. The parmesan ranch breakfast potatoes which are served with most entrees were cooked and seasoned perfectly!

Overall The Lookout Brunch was a great way to start the day! Good food, drinks, service, and view! Even if you're not having brunch, check out The Lookout for drinks when you need a reprieve from the craziness of the street level of Broadway.

name: Ole Red
text: Great atmosphere , several great bands. Nice atmosphere. So much food it was difficult to eat. Only negative while all four of us enjoyed everything about the Resturant. There was no place to park and the cost of 25.00 for parking  was steep, for no longer than we were there.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
My first predators game since moving here!!! 

Much smaller arena than the Excel back in mn. I loved it. Easier to see well even higher up.

The sound system was great sounding, loud clear but didn't hurt your ears! Definite plus for me!! 

Seats were pretty cozy and it was warm enough:) which I greatly appreciate!

name: Ole Red
text: We lucked out and were able to be seated in a hr. It was fun to hang out here. The drinks were good and the atmosphere was fun. The wait staff was friendly. When we received our food we were pleased. The pulled pork had a strong smoke to it and was very lean. The burgers were done correctly and the homemade tater tots were crispy and not greasy. Would we stop here again, wait a long time for dinner??? Yes, we'd all do it again.

name: Ole Red
text: Visited this place for lunch and I heard the food was good.  I ordered fried pickles, sangria and cheeseburger.   I left so full because everything was delicious.   I almost ate the entire basket of pickles.  Bring your appetite when you come to this spot! Also the entertainment was great too! This spot is a must if you are in a the area.

name: Ole Red
text:
Go for the atmosphere (and the gravy).

I had an absolutely wonderful experience at Ole Red entertainment-wise. Recently-formed duo Southerland was performing and did an excellent job. It also felt surreal to be in Blake Shelton's place, such a cool vibe.

Separating the experience of being in Music City from the restaurant experience, I had the half "champagne of chicken," a big bucket of fried chicken and biscuits, with gravy. The chicken is good but nothing to write home about, more breading than meat to be honest. The biscuits were kinda dry and just not the best. But the gravy that comes with it was sooooooo good. Mouthwatering. I would have rather just eaten an entire vat of that.

Good place to come hang out, kind of expensive to actually eat lunch/dinner, but so is everywhere in downtown Nashville.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
What??? Plastic cup margarita? Jimmy does sell margarita Glasses in the gift shop. Was told it was Sunday and they don't wash the dishes. Only drank the one because well was vacation.

Hope the resort your building actually has what is pictured in the menu. 

What the fuck Jimmy? Not like Vegas at all.

So now for the food- volcano nachos great! Quesadilla was cold and the fried pickles were burnt. The waitress said "they told me to ask if that was ok first" they removed the pickles from the menu.

What the fuck Jimmy?

name: Ole Red
text:
The music and our first Bloody Mary were perhaps the best things about this place. We opted to do shared seating which I did not mind at all. There were 3 of us and we ordered the bbq nachos and double decker ham and cheese. If you like large servings this is the place for you. The nachos were a pile of potato chips with toppings and the sandwich was huge but tasteless. I would have been better off with a burger but was encouraged to get the sandwich instead. I should have stuck with my original plan. 
We took a few bites of both dishes, ordered another Bloody Mary which was not as good as the first one and we were finished. 
I might go back for the music and but I'd skip the food.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
This place is the best - food review first, drink second. 

As a local, I've been working my way through the Nashville hot chicken scene over the years. Recently I ordered the hot chicken sandwich here - the chef personally came out to ask just how hot I wanted it. I wanted hotttt. And. He. Delivered. I LOVE the beer at this place, but y'all, the food is out of this world. I've also never had a bartender pair a beer with my food (wine pairings, yes. Beer pairings? Never). She hooked me UP! Best meal I have had in Nashville in a long while.

But the reason everyone comes here (and it's in the name) - the brew. These guys are doing it right. As an outdoor enthusiast, I love that they have a beer that supports the state parks in TN. As a native, I believe in supporting local businesses - and I love supporting one that actively and intentionally supports others.

Well, and, duh. The beer is phenomenal. Highly recommend.

name: Ole Red
text: Paid for a double of watered down liquor. Bartender denied having served me until I showed her the receipt.  Rip off central.. I will not be back

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
We stopped last night, Saturday, at 7:30. The bouncer greeted us and was joking with us. Douglas Riley was playing mix of AC/DC, Tom Petty, Neil Diamond, Garth Brooks, etc. The band was really good and interacted with the crowd all night. We got a seat up front near the band which made the night. We had a good group of people sitting near us.

The drinks and shots were $9 and they offer several Rumchata shots.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
I absolutely love this brewery. It's a bit rustic with a touch of class. A flight only cost $10, and I was able to sample all drafts available. My favorite was the basil beer which had such a unique taste to it I was really blown away. I also like that this brewery has board games upstairs and darts, so if you're in a playful mood you can have your beer and play the games. There is outdoor seating as well, but it was so hot and humid we opted to remain inside.

Overall, a winner in my books!

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Very cool place away from the touristy bustle of Broadway.  Quality bar food, very attentive service and a very good live band.  The band covered everything from Willie Nelson to Radiohead.  Our party of 4 had a great time and plan to head back for their Whiskey Jam session on a Thursday night.  Very good spot and more authentic musically than the Broadway scene.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
This all-purpose venue is a hot spot for Nashville. It is a favorite of big name musical acts (especially those that fall into the country music genre) as well as being the home of the NHL team, the Predators. There always seems to be all sorts of sporting and special events scheduled for this space. 

Truth be told, I have only visited Bridgestone Arena to attend music concerts. It is a GIGANTIC arena which translates to there not really being a bad seat in the house. This allows for a bathroom around every turn and a concession stand/bar just around the corner from whichever section one may found themselves assigned. 

What I really appreciate about Bridgestone is the location. It stands right on Broadway Street. For those unfamiliar with the area, this is a strip of restaurants, honky tonks, small stage venues, and karaoke bars that appeal to those looking to keep the party going into the wee hours of the morning. If catching an Uber home to hop straight into bed sounds more appealing to you, the mass exodus of those attending an event at the arena can quickly turn into a traffic nightmare. 

I have always had luck walking a few blocks away from the hustle and bustle to make a quick getaway.

name: Ole Red
text: Just stopped in for some drinks. Our bartender RICHARD was so nice and told us a lot of history for the downtown bars. Enjoyed talking with him! Music was good also. It was a kid that had been on the Voice.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I read all the up and down reviews online, but I wanted to give this place an honest chance. The server was very friendly! The decorations and theme was a bit weird for me.. I ordered the quesadilla and the crab dip from their menu, and both were underwhelming.  This place is located directly on broadway so I'm sure they get a decent amount of business, but unfortunately they won't be getting mine any time soon.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Stopped by for lunch, our server, Jolyn was fabulous!! The fish and chips were great with the margaritas! Always love the music

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Best fish tacos I've ever had, and I was born and raised in Southern Calfornia - where fish tacos are abundant in authentic and fast food form, from very fresh to food-poisoning-in-waiting.  

You get two good-sized tacos of Mahi Mahi (or tilapia) seasoned in a cajun influenced way, in a corn tortilla ... with large chunks of grilled fish inside, cabbage, and a white sauce drizzled over it all.  In-freaking-credible!  It comes with a side of black beans and an almost milky tasting rice.  Amazing.  Out of all the fantastic foods I tried and loved, these fish tacos are something I'd come back for and try to recreate at home.  

We also ordered the fried pickles.  Just do it!  

Skipped the drinks because I was driving, but there's live music up front by the bar...open air windows to the outside - we were lucky to get to listen to Eric Von.  He's awesome!  He'll play almost anything you request (someone requested Lady Ga Ga's Pokerface as a joke... and he made a country version of it that blew her lame song out of the water and back again!)  

Prices are a bit on the high side, but it's Jimmy Buffet's Margaritaville.  I wasn't expecting $4 tacos.  But for the quality and portion, the pricing makes it worth it.  The fish tacos were I think $16.99, but they don't skimp on the fish.  They take care of you and your belly in Nashville!

name: Ole Red
text: Only giving this place two stars because the servers are nice .the food is inconsistent, one day it's good and one day really bad . First day food was good , second time it was terrible! The atmosphere is fun but it's the same u can find anyplace. Just don't bother . You'll be disappointed. If you do go , stick with apps. only .

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: The food was solid but a bit overpriced. Didn't care for any of the beer, but they do allow dogs outside which is nice.

name: Ole Red
text:
We stopped by on Friday for lunch. There was no wait and we were seated immediately. The Bulleit sours were very good and strong.

We had the Nashville burgers with the pimento cheese. The rolls are thick, the burgers cooked perfectly, with thick slices of tomato, onion, and pickles. The steak fries were very thick and the tator tots were crunchy with a smashed hash brown-type of filling.

The service was very good, the food was hot, seasoned and cooked well. There was a female singer who auditioned for the voice, she was performing her new original songs. My only downside is that we had a wobbly table and chairs and no signage or tee shirts of Blake that i saw.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I was going  to give a 3 but remembered how fun the audience was and all there chants at the hockey games. The arena itself is beautiful!  The seats are AWFULLY small. Like I had bruises getting up and down in my seat. I'm not the smallest of butts but let's be real everyone said how small it was. Crazy small. Predators were so fun to watch here.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Fiends that live/have visited Nashville suggested this place and I honestly don't know why. Wanted a change of scenery from the honky tonks on Broadway...big mistake. Simply a college dive-bar with karaoke....pass #mediocre

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Bridgestone Arena is the best arena we've been in. It has a escalator going up to the second floor.
We had a very good view from our seats. I don't think there's a bad seat in the house.
Getting into the arena went fairly smooth and the employees were courteous and helpful.
A can of Coors beer cost me $13. 
The cost of the food and beverages are ridiculous.
We are hoping to go to the CMA next year.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Food...not good.  So the best thing about Soul Shine Pizza is the venue.  They have a nice upstairs patio.  The band was pretty decent and it's a good place to listen to some music and visit with friends.  

They have a good bar selection, but the food was pretty bad.  We were there for a party and so they brought out a bunch of stuff...a couple of different pizzas, nachos, breadsticks and chicken wings.  The chicken wings and buffalo chicken pizza were ok.  For the most part, the pizza was awful.  No flavor and greasy, which is a bad combo.  

Maybe I would repeat Soul Shine Pizza just for a hang out spot.  But I definitely wouldn't bother with the pizza.  

I have 2 GF quotes from this outing:
"Best thing here is the diet coke"
"Not worth the calories"

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I stopped by Soulshine Pizza Factory in Franklin for a quick lunch. I ordered the homemade tamales topped with chili and I was blown away by the freshness of the tamales. I will definitely add Soulshine Pizza Factory to my list of restaurants to dine.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Food is ok, nothing amazing...dont just come for the food. Overwhelming dance floor and stage and plenty of seating. Open atmosphere, seems to be a good bar..just not great food

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Great pizza, and even better music.  Came here on a Saturday night during a bachelor trip to Nashville, I would return every trip through the area.    Saturday night was a blast here.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Pork Loin melt was reallllly tasty. Great recommendation by the staff. Music was awesome. I sat near the (open door) entrance and froze to death so I left earlier than I would've.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Good ribbs and great music. Had a good time while having a good meal. This place is right int he mix of all the other places in downtown Nashville. They had two guys on stage playing. Made the meal go by fast. I had the ribbs and liked them. I have had better, but they were good.

Visited November 2011

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: We had a party of 5 from California and Louisiana out celebrating a 16th wedding anniversary. As we were leaving my mother was stopped by 2 different male employees accusing us of not paying. We just had multiple people from our table fighting over who was going to pay the check! The employees were extremely disrespectful and verbally attacking my mother. There is a certain way to ask. Don't treat paying customers like criminals.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Mr. Rippy and Mr. Goldberg, you own many lucrative establishments in Nashville. You have the money. Fix your female bathroom. It's been broken for months.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
lololololololololololololol

i did the cupid shuffle here on a wednesday night.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: My fiancé and I went here last Saturday. This place is big, clean in the area, I think. We ordered salt and vinegar peanuts, chicken wings, and BBQ ribs. The peanuts were ok, but chicken wings and BBQ ribs were very good. The ribs were glazed with honey I think.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Service was slow. Our waitress never checked up on us and we used cash to pay and left shortly after getting our food. The place wasn't busy and we only ordered a side of fries... it was a disappointment.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Sooo this was an impulse buy to have dinner and live music.  Seating was scarce. The food was mediocre and the music was worse. All of the meat tasted watery ... on a good note, the bartenders were both pretty and efficient.  Doubt I'll go back.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Cool atmosphere/decor. Service was fine for lunch. I've only been once but found the pizza to be very average and overpriced. Too much competition in Nashville to be average. Won't be back.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Touristy? Yes. But that doesn't have to be a bad thing. 
The atmosphere is actually pretty damn fun (even if you're just watching line dancers) and the food is surprisingly awesome. Packed with flavors and grease - exactly what you'd want in Nashville.
Sadly, my favorite sandwich in the world - their Western Monte Cristo - was taken off the menu which brings my review from a 5 to a 4.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Had a good time, went in to listen to music and have a drink. The bartenders were friendly and the place was homey.
Service was quick and pleasant. Music started so I decided to  order the food...it was bar food but between the music and atmosphere it passed. I had chicken wings, quesadilla and sweet potato fries...all were good for the bar.
Had  a good time...good music, good service,  good customers and it was clean.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
The barbecue is great overall but the fried pickles are what brings me back. They're deliciously salty, dill pickle spears with a crispy battered outside. Seriously. An entire pickle. Fried. 

The service is commendable (even at midnight) and the food always comes out popping hot. No complaints here.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Super basic atmosphere. Music was enjoyable. Had chili with corn cakes. I thought corn cakes wold not be pancakes but something to pick up with my fingers. It was an OK place, but there is so much to explore in Nashville.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Yes! Yes! Yes! I got the pulled chicken sandwich and some others in my group got the pulled pork sandwich and pulled pork salad. They all enjoyed theirs. My pulled chicken sandwich was on point. I was happy that they smoked it dry so I could add sauce at my discretion. The sandwich and one side were reasonably priced. I will go again when visiting Nashville.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: I've been here many times before and enjoyed it! I'm only giving 4 stars because their concessions stand is pretty gross.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: They accused me of having a fake ID the moment we sat down at the bar upstairs. The bartender and bouncer both bent my ID and scrutinized it then came back and told me it was fake. I have used my ID at countless establishments and never had a problem before, including nearly every bar on Broadway. I am from a different state, Maryland, so my ID looks different than what they are used to getting. I would never recommend this place to anyone, which is a shame because the live music really was pretty good. I did not appreciate them demeaning me and accusing me of being a liar. There are much better bars along Broadway and I would take my business there in a heartbeat.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Went for the CMA FEST, my mom and I had lunch there where we ordered a pretty good amount of food. The "World Famous Fried Pickles" we're good but nothing I would order again, the Caesar salad was yummy, the Chicken wings were my favorite and the moonshine margarita was marginal. Overall the dining experience was nice with good  few really great live artists. 

Since our first experience was good we decided to venture back following the CMA Fest concert, let me just say I was excited to line dance and drink! I patiently stood at the bar for 40 minutes and waited to be served, I was looked at once and said, "hi" and the very rude bar tender said, "Oh no honey, I have to go back and serve the other side of the bar" at that point I gave up! I shook it off and went out to the dance floor where they were teaching a line dance. They taught a VERY basic dance then the lesson ended. It was the only time the dance floor was full then they said "OK lessons are over." Needless to say we were disappointed and headed off to a different Honky Tonk on Broadway. This place needs more bar tenders, more dancing, and a staff that isn't stretched so thin! I missed the Bobby Bones book signing because the waiter took 25 minutes to come back and grab our credit card for the bill.

I will say this, the place has potential it just needs a little help!

name: Nashville Palace
text:
I am in town doing an automotive program in the Opryland area and wandered down to see the cars in front of Cooter's and heard the music that was coming out of the Palace at about 4:30 on Monday afternoon. While not a huge country fan, I recognized the quality of the performer (that turned out to be Nathan Belt) and decided to enter and order a drink at the bar. He was really good and I stayed for his entire set plus another 30-40 minutes of the next act, Ike Johnson and The Roadhouse Rangers. I WILL be back this week, maybe even tonight ...

oh, had the wings (not the hot ones, but had the hot sauce on the side), excellent !!!

A great venue for QUALITY local music!!!!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: We stopped by here for happy hour before going to some other bars hearing they were good. We go in to find a poor happy hour but we didnt mind because we were told there was a band playing. We went upstairs to find the lead singer just talking the whole time asking questions  which was annoying. The beer I ordered came in a chilled glass and anyone who knows beer knows that waters down the beer. The nachos we ordered were horrible. We get that its a pizza place but the nachos were 9.99 for about 15 chips. We pay the same price at other places for huge plates that we cant finish. We definitely felt like we didnt get our moneys worth here! The amount you should get for a side. The salsa tasted like straight marinara and the gin and tonic my girlfriend ordered was too strong to drink. Hope the pizzas better.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Really so many better places to eat and to enjoy good music and dancing.  I paid the cover, then waited for my table.  During my wait I felt like I was on a bad cruise with the cruise directors trying to get people to dance.  I was there for an hour and did not hear one, not one, country song.  I heard the Electric Slide and a Saturday night fever song!  This place is now nothing more than a tourist trap.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Visited Nashville.  Tried this place. Had pulles pork.  It was dry and tasteless.  I don't normally complain about a meal but this is an exception because it was that bad!  Tsharrish@aim.com

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: My daughter and I ordered the large Mississippian and got nearly three yummy meals out of it!  The foundation of this pie was a thin crust that was fired to a well done char and paired beautifully with the sweet sticky BBQ sauce.  Somehow the melted mozzarella & pepper jack had the perfect chemistry to pull this pie together with two chicken toppings (pulled & grilled) and tasty gems of smoked bacon.  Leftovers were most welcome and left us longing for even more!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
The bands which play here and staff are quite kind. While security can be a bit aggressive, I can understand that they don't want anyone falling off barstools or the balconies, creating liability issues for the bar. Sometimes the patrons, at least the ones on Saturday night this last weekend, are rather crazy, but all in good humor. While some individuals were incredibly rude, I take this as part of the tourist scene and not the fault of the establishment.

I love that they have two live bands, one on the second floor and the other on a base. It helps well with crowd control.

I could also be biased in this case, considering I saw two Chicago Blackhawks players on the stairs when I was about to go home. The things you see during a hockey convention weekend...

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
My Fiance and I are from the Washington,DC area and were getting married in Nashville next April. We decided to have our Rehearsal Dinner at the Wild Horse Saloon. We gave them a deposit and signed contract back in May. On July 16th at 11:00pm, we received an email stating that someone else had bought the place out and we can no longer have our event there. We are now without a venue for out rehearsal dinner. This event was planned for approximately 125 people. We have yet to receive our deposit back. Please respond if something similar has happened to you. 
Rachellauren87@gmail.com

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Great pizza place near our hotel. Group of 8, each ordered something different. Two of our group went to pick up the food and didn't know they had walked out without an order. The manager ran after them to let them know. 5 star service based on that alone. Food was good, sandwiches, calzones. Crawfish soup was spicy.

name: CMA Fest
text: This was my first year, and I had an awesome time!! Four days of free country music was amazing. If you don't like a band at one stage, there are many other stages nearby as well as bars and food trucks set up. It was crazy hot but definitely worth braving out the weather. I honestly didn't notice until we were all slightly burned at the end of the week. My boyfriend surprised me with tickets to Nissan. It was an amazing lineup. Definitely worth the money if you like country music, as this has most of the big names. Parking is atrocious. I preferred using Uber/Lyft (lyft offered discounts to those attending cma fest) and avoiding driving and crazy, expensive fees. Most places accepted cards but there were also plenty of atms set up as well. I would definitely, definitely go again!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I have a feeling that when I left this place with a five star feeling, the perfect weather and free tickets that I won had a lot to do with it, but Soulshine was a great place! Had a personal size pizza, priced just as I expected for a "non-chain"/more gourmet place. Also tried the Lemon Wheat beer that was on special and I loved it. Especially the $2.50 price! Live music, patio, amazing ceiling fan to cool the place down, great food....everything I could ask for! Go Friday nights after work for Lightning 100's live broadcast!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: I LOVE THIS PLACE. We got there at 8:30 and had missed the 8:15 line dancing lesson, so we put in our name and we're seated within 10 minutes. The food was amazing and very large portioned. My friend and I could've easily split something and still been full. I got the hot chicken sandwich with mac & cheese and was amazed. So tasty and filling. My friend got the pulled pork sandwich and was equally satisfied. I tried some of her fries and those are great too! After we ate, we started to learn the line dance that was being taught and it was so fun! David Oakleaf and his band were great. I am coming back! Also I'm 19 and was stoked when I found out this place was not limited to 21+.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The tables are sticky, and don't get the Mac and cheese because it is Stouffer's (you can get this in the grocery.)

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The music and line dancing is fun. Pure Nashville. They teach us lay people how to do it so it's a good tom even if it's your first time. The food was good too. Drinks are overpriced and not that great. The service was very poor though. It was like we were imposing on our waitress just to get our drinks and food.  Might've just been a bad night for her. Still worth stopping in.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This place was awesome. My sister is 16 yrs old and loved this place. They teach you how to line dance and we went on a night with a live band. Since we were staying at the the Opryland hotel our cover charge was waved. The gluten free menu was pretty lame and not existent. They have gluten free options but it is hard to be 100% sure. Our waiter was awesome even with the noise level and all. It was a very fun Nashville memory.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Pros: Convenient location, decent atmosphere, interesting decor
Cons: Apathetic (bordering on rude) staff, disappointing food, really loud

My first experience at Soulshine didn't start off so well when I asked a passing waiter if we could have a seat at the last open table, where the leftover food and plates from the previous guests was still sitting.  He kept walking and said, "yeah you can just move that stuff over there" and pointed to a service desk area.  Really?  I'm your guest, not the bus boy. 

Soon after, as we were sitting down, the same waiter grabbed the beer list off of our table and handed it to the two young ladies at the next table.  Umm, I was wanting to look at that myself, thanks. 

Our drinks came quickly and the food came out reasonably quickly also.  But the hummus we ordered tasted like some pasty lime-flavored goop that came straight from a package.  

The pizza I ordered sounded great on the menu, but what I got was comparable to some frozen pizzas I've had.  The toppings were OK, but a little bland, lacking in flavor.  The crust was pretty awful.  It tasted chalky and frozen.  This was disappointing. 

Beyond this, our waiter was just very lacking in customer service skills.  In addition to the rudeness mentioned above, when it came time to get our bill one of the members of our party stated that he already had a tab at the bar and asked if his part could just be added to his tab.  The waiter literally rolled his eyes and said, "I don't think so, but I'll check."  

Despite a fairly negative first experience, I'll give it another chance.  It seems like an OK place for happy hour and the overall vibe of the place isn't too bad.  There was live music, which is a plus, but for those seated in the music area I imagine there's not much chance for conversation as the music was very loud. 

Probably not a bad place to go for happy hour drinks, but I'll probably give the food a pass next time.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Had a delicious pulled pork sandwich and some bud lights. Hit the spot with a good country cover band.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: One of my favorite stops on the strip. The music has always been great, the food (especially the pulled pork sandwich) is awesome, and the servers are usually pretty friendly and on top of keeping you happy.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Not. Good. Insert pizza snob rant here.

What else was not good? We ordered the garlic bread. The waitress gave us what appeared to be a cheese pizza cut in strips. When we tried to reconfirm, "this is the $1.99 garlic bread?" She assured us it was. Then our bill arrived and there is it, $8.99 for cheese and garlic bread. THAT WAS NOT WHAT WE ASKED FOR! Oh and she brought us the wrong beer.  So it may have been an off night, I get it, I've definitely been there. 

To continue, this place is not for me. I am not a fan.

So who should give Soulshine a chance? I think this place is perfect for families, kids and group outings. The decor isn't bad, the windows out front is pretty darn cool but as I said, not for me.

name: Houston Station
text:
Attended a work function here not long ago, and was pleasantly surprised to see a new event venue choice for our fair city.

I like it, but doesn't get five stars in my book. 

Pros:
It's different.
Cool decor/vibe with lots of exposed brick, wood floors, and rough wood.

Cons:
In the middle of nowhere, (yet right in town, I know - just a sort of no man's land).
All around it is DARK.  If your event doesn't have valet, I feel for your guests.
No signage whatsoever.
Street names in that area don't agree with GPS, and since there are no signs, you go around the long way for no reason.
Area around feels sketchy, don't know if it really is or not.
Main entrance has stairs, if you have folks on your list with wheelchairs or climbing issues they are sent to a different area that I never saw.  Assume it was an elevator somewhere.

A co-worker of mine was following me off 4th as we turned onto the street, and the railraod tracks there had a big wash out/hole that he literally got his car stuck in.  It was so dark, I didn't even notice  Oddly enough, there were some area natives that appeared out of the darkness and offered to help... and once he got over the "fear factor," they literally pushed his car out of the hole.

Interesting, and I'm sure I'll visit again.  If I could, would actually be in between 3 and 4 stars, but was feeling a little generous today.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great music location and it's right on the corner. It is multi level with music up and down. We had food and drinks. All of it was reasonably priced and good to the tongue. Downstairs is a bit more intimate as far as being close up to the band. The service was fast and the waitress was nice and cute as well. I will go back before the trip is done.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Surly Security Harasses Mature Patron

I had a particularly troubling night at this Broadway institution. The "bouncer," of African American descent (not that I see color), had orange hair and a surly frame.  Mind you that no "bouncer" was necessary as this was an establishment that I was visiting purely for a nice rack of ribs from my favorite ribs maker, Freddy.  I digress, after looking at my ID, the "bouncer" then questioned my age, which is unwarranted as I clearly give off a mature and worldly vibe.  (I was wearing a Goorin Bros. world traveler hat, gentlemanly summer coat, and a crisp argyle pocket square). He then proceeded to bend my ID to test the validity, and in the process left permanent creases! Can you believe that he questioned my age! I implore you fellow Yelpers to look at my profile picture and see for yourself my mature face.   
 
After explaining to the "bouncer" his blatant mistake in a demeaning way so that he would learn a lesson, he shoved me back a few feet, and snapped a picture of me with his cellular device. He then promised to circulate the picture to his colleagues and announced that he has banned me for life!

Instead of dealing with his mistakes at hand, he resorted to using his illegitimate power to brush me aside! Sad! 
 
I'll be taking my hard earned American dollars to other fine establishments downtown such as Lonnie's, Brass Stables, or Big Bang.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Great service and good pizza. Several choices on the menu. Live music was a plus. Will come back on my next visit to Nashville.   I sat upstairs. The band was upstairs. If your not into that you can sit downstairs and hear just enough music for background ambience.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This place was really fun. The dancing and music was very cool. We are having a great time. Food was not 5 star but who comes here for the food right.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This place is one of the cooler more modern bars/restaurants in the area! We walked in on a Thursday night, and got carded (but you're able to be under 21). There was no cover and there was an awesome feel to this place. There was a band on stage, which was LEGIT, with lighting and everything. I felt like I was at a concert. There was tons of tables and bar space, as well as room for a dance floor, which is not typical of these bars. We got beers and headed to the second floor to watch the band. There were seats, but certain spots were blocked for a private event, oh well. They also had pool, shuffleboard and foozeball. There was no bar on the second floor open so we had to go down to the first to get more drinks. Really cool place, and the food looked yummy!! Would definitely come back.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Soulshine is a fantastic pizza stop in Midtown, just near Vanderbilt's campus.

The place always seems to be busy, they have a ton of pizza options, and lots of great beer available. Wait service could be improved, but overall it's a great go-to for non-chain pizza. Plus, they're open way late!

They often have great live music, and I love the two-story setup. Definitely would recommend.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Had such a fun time at this place! 

There was a fabulous band playing, and the line dance instructor was very easy to follow and had an enjoyable personality. Line dancing exceeded expectations. 

The food was fine as well. We didn't go there for the food though.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The service was great. Food was Delicious and not a long wait since we were all hungy. Beer was not too cold. Entertainment was great and under 21 allowed.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This was the first bar I went to when I got to Nashville and I enjoyed it a lot. I actually went there 3 times in my stay. They had great live music every night I went and the size of the shots they poured were overwhelming in a good way. Check them out if you have the chance.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I've heard so much great stuff about this place and so I was surprised with how underwhelming it was. Not bad... just, not great. We met friends there for drinks and sat for almost a half hour before being served. Good service after that, though. This place has a great patio, too. But you'll pay for it in the end.... $$$. All in all, an average experience.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Three stars is fair.  Decent food, reasonable prices, friendly service, live music (though on Broadway in Nashville that's not all that unique).

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Not the best place for CUSTOMER SERVICE. We weren't acknowledged until I raised my hand. He looked over and mumbled something. He was absolutely horrible. He was unfriendly and didn't seem to care to check up on us. Food was a-ok. BBQ kinda try, flies wanting to dine with you, and the live band was meh. I started sweatin'. I don't think they had AC. Very disappointing.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: (6/23/2014) Our conference organizers rented out the Wildhorse Saloon in The District for the opening reception, what a party! Had a line dancing lesson, then a set from a house band, and a fairly generous, if unexceptional buffet.  Space is vast, three levels around a dance floor overlooking the stage.  Would be a great mid-sized venue to see a band.  Several bars are strategically located around the place, waitstaff is attentive and keeps track of you even amidst the craziness.  Pretty good selection, more upscale than in the honky tonks down Broadway.  It's touristy, it's splashy, it was fun.

name: Nashville Palace
text: We stopped in the Palace for drinks and some music and had a blast.  Nothing fancy here, and we didn't try the food, but the beers were cold and the music was authentic and well played.  Servers were friendly, too.  Definitely worth a visit!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Hit or miss on the food and service

The first time we are here the food was awesome.  The service was very good.  The music was great.  However, it was mid day, mid week, and they were really not busy.  We ate ribs and fries and everything was really good.

The second time was a completely different story.

It was a weekend so I called ahead.  I asked if there was a wait.  The answer I got was "it's first come first serve."  That didn't really answer my question to so I rephrased: is there anyone waiting for tables?  The answer was "no". This turned out to be a white lie just to get me to drive overs there.  The reality is that no one was "waiting" because it was just wall to wall people with everyone milling around playing the role of vulture jumping on any seat that opened up.  It was total chaos, and In my opinion that was a very dishonest way to get us in the door.

Once we did finally get seated (no where near any music stage) our server wasn't exactly warm and friendly.  There were a number of us so we ended up splitting in two tables (one of 4 and one of 5) across the room from one another.  She served both tables and oddly enough one table's food was awesome (pulled pork sandwich, and pork tenderloin melt) and one table's food was ehhhh at best (okay ribs, onion rings and fried mushrooms with golden outsides and undercooked veggies on the inside).

The best part was our waitress tells us at the end that she was nice enough to not put the 18% gratuity for parties of 8 or more.  Which is really funny since she treated each table completely separately taking our orders at different times, bringing the food at different times.

If it hadn't been for our good first experience I might have given them 2 stars.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Really cool place.  Local musicians, great menu, cool building, but the location can make things a little difficult.  Not their fault though.

Usually sit upstairs and it's a great place for a date especially with the other locations nearby to visit afterward.

Always sit in Trent's section.  Always does a great job and takes great care of his patrons.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Walking around Nashville all day can make you very hungry. I stopped in to refuel for a quick bite. Everyone was incredibly friendly. Our waitress had shared with us that she was tired and does not usually work the day shift. We put in an order for a bbq brisket appetizer and ordered lemonade. They have this deal where you can purchase a plastic boot drink and will give free lemonade refills and the boot is yours to take home. Unlimited refills sounded like a good idea, with all the walking we were doing around Nashville. It costs about $10.
