After receiving our drinks we seemed to be waiting a good thirty min for our appetizer. It almost seemed like they had forgotten that we were there. We notified them and our appetizer was on the house! The bbq beef brisket was really good and flavorful. It was nothing that I had really tried before. I am from up north and we don't eat much brisket. 

They also have a gift shop attached to the restaurant lots of tees and southern gear.  Everything looked incredibly clean, including the bathrooms. I enjoyed all the horse décor throughout the restaurant. This seems like a really happening place. We sat in the bar area but, there is a restaurant area with a stage and a huge area to dance.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great environment and big dance floor. Loved the souvenir boot glasses you can take home and their Mac and cheese is delicious! The corn too!! Great for families and everyone is friendly!!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Thirty minute wait on a Saturday night. But it went pretty fast. Great service And good food. Food came out pretty fast! The apple moonshine will hit you fast!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great music to enjoy any day of the week.  Friendly and attentive waitresses serve with pleasant smiles.   Substandard food.   Don't recommend coming here for a nice meal.  Salad served in a dixy cup/bowl.  Plastic cutlery. Curly fries no better than what you get from the frozen food section at supermarket.   Great BBQ sauce at the table. Live music made this dining experience worthwhile.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This is strictly based on the upstairs bar and music.  Everytime I come to Nashville, I have a great time at this place.  I mean the whole block is awesome, but this place in particular is my favorite.  Much more intimate than some of the other music venues in the area, plus the band always plays a decent variety of music.  Crowd has always been great too.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I would say food is pretty good but not great. Super fun at night, live music on the weekends. Would recommend going there for a lively atmosphere  and more of a upbeat kind of place. Pepperoni bread is great and so are pork nachos.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Ok this place is amazing. I have seen some post that day it's a little "dirty". Hello ITS A HONKY TONK!  Ribs were great beer was cold and also seen some well behaving children so it was kid friendly. Had the seasoned curly fries and also Mac and cheese. They had a roll on the plate that was like crack!  Music was fantastic. Was like going to a concert and you just have to tip!  Highly recommended.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Wenn du country music magst ist das der perfekte Ort für dich. Nicht so überteuert wie die Bars downtown. Burger für 6$ und n Bier für 4$ . Nicjt vergessen ein paar dollar scheine als tip für die band mitzunehmen. Would go there again.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Good food. Great ambience. Awesome dancing lessons an s dance floor. Very energetic. Good for kids. Can get crowded so get there early or expect to wait. Had the brisket and was really good. Spicy bbq wings were amazing with the spicy bbq sauce. Would highly recommend for music an fun!

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: Not my favorite theater, but I like that it was small and that the chairs were comfy. Not fond of the bathrooms being downstairs. The customer service there was excellent!!! It's a small and cute venue.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Three levels, multiple rooms most with love bands. Definitely a cool summer place to hang. Food was pretty good 4/5. Gratuity was added on 6 people, not reflected on the check, strange... Service poor. Pretty standard any city main drag restaurant, hit or miss

name: Twin Kegs
text: My fiancé and I recently moved to Nashville and were looking to find a dive bar similar to one we liked back home. We passed this place constantly but just got a chance to go this past weekend. We walked in with a group of 5 and easily found a seat and got our beers. We ordered a few appetizers and burgers and everything was awesome. It was karaoke night, which we hadn't expected, but we had the BEST time. The crowd was in their 20s-30s for the most part, and everyone was friendly and interactive. The bartender was amazing and was running the whole bar by herself without any issues. I think her name was Hannah? She was probably the best bartender I've ever encountered. It's nice to go to a dive bar but receive fantastic service. This place will definitely become a regular hangout for us!

name: Twin Kegs
text:
Twin Kegs definitely has the best bar food in town as well as the cheapest beer! The only drawback is sometimes it can be hit or miss. The karaoke can be overbearing if your not into that stuff. Great food, just a gamble at times depending who may be working. 

Staff is all very friendly, some just handle the pressure of being busy a lot better.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Super fast service, perfect pricing, and really good food. The ribs were pretty damn good and I could roll around in their delicious onion rings forever.  This place isn't the best BBQ joint I've ever been too but if you find yourself on the strip, it's definitely worth a peek!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I had been to Nashville with a friend last year, and we were going to eat at Rippy's, but he decided he didn't want to listen to live music. (I know, you are in Nashville FOR the music.) So we didn't get a chance to eat there. I went back on Sunday, 5/7/17 with my nephew and his mom. The music was great, and the food was good. I got a pulled chicken salad, and the corn cakes. Both were good. They weren't the best in the world, but I would go there again and I would definitely recommend this restaurant to others.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: First off let me start by saying tonight would have been my first enjoyable fight night if all of the proceeding didn't happen. Brooke our server was taking great care of us and was not at all upset with us coming in at 4pm to stay until the fight at 11. When our friends came though everything got combined on to one tab that I personally split up at the end... you can see the pictures attached. Also we got autograted without our knowledge. I would have appreciated it being written down somewhere or us being warned since we were all bartenders and know how to take care of other service members. Nothing was an issue until a Middle Aged Caucasian security guard kicked out one of our Hispanic friends for reacting after he was pushed by the guy who was plowing through the crowd. This guy had previous been fired from Broadway Brewhouse for the exact same act to the exact same guy... fishy... following him being told he was "lucky they let him get his things" the security staff did not let my friend pay for his tab and just told him to leave. Upon hearing this I spoke to the manager Steven who took care of this problem and covered his tab after we pointed out that this seemed to us like a racist attack. The fight made it crazy inside so through trying to talk to the kicked out friend outside and still trying to hold down our table inside some other group members were having problems getting passed security to get back upstairs to our table. This caused a problem when I split our bill at the end. Not only was there a random bud light that appeared on our check but now we had the check of a friend who was told they couldn't come back up to sit with us. So in comes "manager" number 2. As whoever this man was walked up to our table in his trucker hat and rippys tshirt he immediately took an aggressive stance when my boyfriend and I put it to his attention how poor their customer service had been towards us trying to correct a misunderstanding all night. He fought with my boyfriend over at 37 dollar tab, picture also included but note this tab is not autograted like the rest. He claimed that WE should have done a better job in trying to get our friend past security and that since WE did not do a better job it was our responsibility to pick up this tab. I would have had no problem doing this except for the fact that we had been treated poorly by this man now as well and we were the last people standing in the restaurant. All of our friends had given us cash and left and it was not until I was looking at the check again did I realize that they had put an autograt on. I then broke up the pretty much fight that the manager was having with my boyfriend to say if they took the autograt off we would still take care of our server and pick up the whole tab. He sent our server back with a new adjusted check without the 37 dollar tab because the autograt was 56. After we finally got our tabs split and paid for I was very upset, almost to the point of tears that I should be dealing with something like this on a night that should have been fun and relaxing. All in all I have come to the conclusion that I will never be back to Rippy's nor will I send any of my bar guests there. On Monday I will be contacting someone above the people who were inside the building tonight, and that their security is racist.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This place is huge. We got to watch a live performance, mostly because it took so long to get drinks and food. That being said, the drinks were delicious and the food was also.

name: Twin Kegs
text:
This is one of the last dive bars left in Nashville. It's always been one of the best. It has shuffle board, allows smoking, and has some perfectly mediocre karaoke. It's great. What really sets this place apart though is the burger. I usually have their BBB (Big Bad Burger) it's two patties with traditional fixings and bacon that they put under the cheese. Today, I had the single patty BB and it was as good as always. It's a perfectly seasoned patty that I believe they cook in a frying pan. It just tastes like exactly what you want from a dive bar burger. It lingers. 

I tell anyone who will listen that Twin Kegs has one of the best burgers in town. Despite all the new fancy burger places popping up, this one still holds its own. Highly recommend.

Check out my instagram @tennesseeburgergram

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
A review solely based on the music would say "5 stars all the way - great mixture of artists -especially if you stay for 3 or 4 hours like we did - you won't be disappointed. And, if you're lucky, they'll pull the adorable 9 year old girl up on the stage to bust out the tunes like a 20 year pro." 

And the review that factors in service and food would go something like this: Despite us spending so long there we were definitely earning our keep in the drink department - that was until our waiter's shift ended an no one eveeerrrr came back to check on us for more drinks. Our first waitress was a little rough around the edges but I can roll with that. Maybe they were just trying to tell my parents and I that we had had enough to drink: "cut 'em off!" 

As for the food - the reviews are right - meh, meh, meh. I had the pulled pork salad and was disappointed in the lack of flavor and moistness in the meat. My bloody marys were a-okay. To add some kick, I took it upon myself to add a dose of the tableside BBQ. 

All this to say, Rippy's is great if you're thirsty and want to hear music. If you're hungry...just keep drinking till that feeling subsides.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This review is based on the food and service -- not the bar or music. Ordered the brisket sandwich, coleslaw, and lemonade. The lemonade was the worst I've ever had. The brisket and coleslaw was very mediocre. The service was mediocre and unfriendly.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This place was alright. You have to order towards the back and then find a seat. Which can be a hassle if you are going with a group of people. They do have extra BBQ sauces at the table if you need to add more flavor to your food. The ribs that day were super dry and everyone at my table ended up just taking the food home because we just were not satisfied at the moment. It was however great for our  midnight cravings after a long day.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Excellent food, service, drinks and band! My new favorite on Broadway. The spicy chili wings were crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. I recommend the Tropical Hootie drink...delicious! The band upstairs was amazing! Can't wait to go back!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
My wife and I stopped into Wildhorse to take in the tourist trap ambience, and grab some dinner. The wings were just ok, but the bartender, Bernie, made our evening a true delight.

If you go to the wildhorse, seek out Bernie, and ask him to make you a Jedi shot!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This rating is based off atmosphere only as I didnt eat here. Went for line dancing and the band. $6 cover, worth it! Stayed for a couple hours learning the dance and watching the band. One of the highlights of my nashville!  Mustttt go!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: First time in Nashville, and first time stopping in to Rippy's. Five of us ate, and none of us were IMPRESSED! Overpriced mediocre food. Service was borderline insulting. Waitress brought an ice tea to the table, we all looked at each other wondering why. When she came back I stated we didn't order this, she immediately got an attitude. Later when she brought the right drinks, I commented why is the wine in plastic cups? She replied, It's Carlo Rossi, does it really matter. Seriously, there are too many places to eat and drink along Broadway for this type of service. We will definitely return to Nashville, but will skip Rippy's!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The upstairs patio is a great spot to see the strip but unfortunately the band was amateurish and the pulled pork was mediocre at best.  With so many choices it's not worth going here.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Super laid back environment with great live music, pizza, and beer. The roof top is great for a Sunday funday or any other good weather day...for that matter. The service has never disappointed either.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Ribs and chilly. That is DEFINITELY the way to go! My friend had the fries and chicken sandwich and she said it was awesome. The best part was the live music, and also the ribs. I expected them to be dripping in BBQ sauce, but they were dry rubbed and so juicy. The meat came right off of the bone and there was barely any fat on them. If You love ribs, you will love Rippy's.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: We have been here to see a plethora of productions! I have gone with family and friends both on various trips! Every show that we have seen has been incredible! The auditorium is beautiful and the facility in general is always clean! The wait for Valet parking can be very lengthy sometimes, but there are quite a few people! This is a blessing to have in Tennessee! I will definitely be back soon and I would encourage anyone to go!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Awesome meal great music. Well worth the wait to get in.  Make sure you're before 7pm to avoid the cover charge

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I was excited when I saw the menu at Soulshine pizza. We started with a shrimp nachos appetizer, which was good. Then my wife and I ordered a 16" pizza; she had "everything but the kitchen sink" on one half, and I had the Athena on the other. My wife asked for no sauteed onions or peppers on her half. Unfortunately they must have thought that was for the whole pizza, because my half had none. To make matters worse, the pizza had almost no sauce on it. As a result, my half was nothing but mozzarella and feta cheese with black olives and a few small shrimp. I was very disappointed: my pizza was dry and almost tasteless. For the first time in years I am not interested in eating the leftover pizza. I would have returned my pizza but my wife liked her half, so I give Soulshine 2 rather than 1 stars. On the plus side, the service was good, but parking is a pain, even during off hours.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Place was dead on the first floor late last Sunday evening, however that gave us the opportunity to learn about some of the places to catch while in town. Bartender was super knowledgable and engaging. Just what we needed at the time. Will likely give it another chance at a later time.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Worst place I have ever been . We were there last Friday. My friends and i called 3 separate times during the week wanting to set a reservation for about 15. Each time they told us oh yeah we will be able to seat you. We showed up Saturday night at 730 (after calling 2 hours in advance like they wanted). It took over an hour and a half to get a table. We went up to the bar and started drinking but it was an absolute mess to get a table. Finally we pushed one together ourselves on the patio. The waitress asked me if we needed anything like menus, I told her a bigger table and we had already been waiting an hour and a half. She told us she couldn't help us and walked away. After we got a table, it took a ridiculously long time for any server to help us, she got our drink orders and disappeared. I ordered pizza, and it was so loud from the AWESOME live band playing that I honestly didn't think she heard me. It took another 45 minutes to get food and the pizza wasn't even that good. Sure the chick was nice, but there is no reason that this whole situation had to happe. I am extremely disappointed I'm the staff and do not think I will ever be returning after that experience.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: The shows are fine. Basically hit or miss, but the valet is absolutely ridiculous. Do not valet or it will absolutely ruin your night.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great food and music! Food is surely worth the price. I had a pulled pork and it was amazing. Really big portions so come hungry. Nachos are also great.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Always wanted to go here because of the history.  The food was very good.  Mother Maybelle's ham dinner was some of the best country ham I've had.  Music was too loud is the only complaint.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Stopped in here as part of a work function recently and was fairly impressed. The Wildhorse Saloon is set up with a floor level and two higher levels in a -- you guessed it -- horseshoe kind of shape. On the top floor are pool tables and other games to be played.

The day I went they provided a buffet style dinner. I liked pretty much everything I came across. The beans were excellent, the pulled pork and brisket were both very good, even the coleslaw was great. I'm usually somewhat of a picky eater, but I had two plates because the food was so good. 

The day I was there it was packed. Unfortunately, although the establishment can accommodate a LOT of people, it means many of them will be standing. I was lucky to get a table on the 3rd floor mezzanine. Others were not so lucky. To see the stage or the ground floor dancing, many people were standing against a wall behind me. As I looked around, there are tables around the horseshoe railings and there are tables away from the railings, but nearly enough for the number of people that can be in the building. Lots of people were standing against walls because they didn't have any other choice -- there was nowhere else for them to go.

The staff was friendly at the 3rd floor bar area, although as noted in other reviews, the staff prefers a line to be formed rather than people standing along the bar. I guess that helps with a "first come, first serve" set up, why have a 15' bar top if you only need 4' to form a line in front of?

Maybe it was the event, but there was NO hard alcohol served at this place. It was kept to beer and soda, but again, that very likely was at the request of the company holding the event.

At one point a young woman appeared on stage and asked if anyone would like to learn some line dancing. She is very good at this and it seemed that people picked it up rather quickly under her tutelage. Later on, a band came out and they put on a decent show. The acoustics can be a little wonky in the building -- or maybe that's just because of where I was at, which was directly in front of the stage, but up so high -- but I enjoyed the show. Staff routinely checked on me to grab my plates and see if the people sitting with me wanted another beer.

Overall, this doesn't seem like a bad place. If it gets really busy though, you may find yourself with nowhere to sit and enjoy the show. I overheard other patrons talking to employees who said that they sell tickets to some of the shows. I'm not sure how that would work unless they limited the sales to match the number of seats available. I'm glad I got a table, because it would have been very difficult to eat and drink standing up against a wall -- which unfortunately is what I saw a very healthy chunk of people being forced to do due to the limited seating at this place.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Visited Nashville with a group of 6 to experience the nightlife. We tried all the hot spots on Broadway. Made our way up to 8th Ave and found this hidden gem! Excellent live music, well crafted cocktails, and perfect fried pickles! We had very attentive server named Paul, that made us feel right at home. We never had to look for him for another round, he had them to us before we even had to ask! I can imagine this will not remain a hidden gem for long, NashHouse can be a destination all on its own.

name: Nashville Palace
text: A great honky tonk!  Really enjoyed the music!!Don't change a thing.  Good food, relaxed atmosphere, not overly crowded for lunch, and good traditional country music.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Went there for dinner with my girlfriends. Fun vibe, right on the strip. I had the catfish strips, they were more like full on fillets. They were delicious!! And you got plenty of food for a very decent price. I love this place, would definitely go back!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We came here after a big lunch at Hattie B's that was a mistake.  Not because the food wasn't delicious but because we were stuffed.  Started with the biscuits and jam which was sublime.  The fluffy buttery biscuits were amazing.  The jams: Strawberry; peach; blackberry; tomato; grape; and butter were so good.  Then we had the deviled eggs with: bacon; pimento mayo; pickles; chow chow; and I forget what the other one was.  Delicious but then we started to hit the wall.  Had a nice Tennessee pilsener which was light and refreshing.  I ordered the Southern Burger which was a pimento cheese burger with a fried green tomato on top.  It was really good but after two bites I was so full that I had to call it a night.  Ditto for my Daughter who got the enormous pork shank which she said was delicious as well but she couldn't finish it.  I'd come back here just for the biscuits alone.  Servers were nice and friendly.  Live country music was great as well.  Lot of fun I. The Gulch.  Check it out.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great time all around. We came for the line dancing lessons so the 12 year old in our family could experience Nashville at night. Loved the atmosphere. Amazing live music. We didn't try much to eat since we were mostly dancing. Very crowded. If you're trying to get a seat fast definitely sit at the bar where there is open seating.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: By far one of the worst meals I have had in a very long time. The first dish we ordered was a basic hamburger, and the patty was wafer thin and burnt to a crisp. I could crack it like a potato chip. The lettuce was wilted and stale, and the french fries were soggy and cold. The other dish was eggs Benedict with crab meat. Could not taste crab at all. Also ordered a bloody Mary, which seem to have no vodka in it at all. I was told dismissively if I wanted to add fixings to it, I had to take it over to the bloody Mary bar, which was covered in flies, due to open patio seating. We never got utensils, we never got napkins. We are locals, and I often have guests over and refer them to restaurants on lower Broadway, but I will make sure they skip this place.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: only thing they really have going is the food. it's good. today went there for friends bach party, 8 of us. we were told we'd have a 45-60 min wait. fine we went and sat in the bar area. we were at tables on dirty tables the entire wait - not one person coming up to the tables. making us have to go to the bar to get which isn't a big deal but going up taking turns so we didn't lose the table. (1 hr being there) finally got a table.. got our food and drinks ordered.. server seemed good at first. food took probably about another 45 mins to get. yes it was good so worth the wait. we're done shorty after... waiter is no where to be found for at least 20 mins ... finally found told him we had to go. said he was closing out another table and he'd be back. 20 mins later finally back and got to close us out. we were there literally for a good 3 hrs just wasting our day away. also- they add on gratuity of 20% so our server towards the middle/ end obviously knew and decided not to give a f about us anymore. smh

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
This was honestly one of my favorite bars in Nashville which is so funny because I was not a huge fan of going out in the first place. In fact, the next couple days after visiting I couldn't remember the name of this bar so whenever it came up in conversation I called it "Pleasant Surprise!" 

Why did I like it? Well it was a rooftop bar right next to Bridgestone Arena and overlooking the downtown strip. It had awesome, attentive staff constantly working to make sure everyone's experience was fun yet controlled and safe. The food and drinks, while I didn't have any myself, were tasty looking and quite affordable. It wasn't insanely crowded like a lot of the other bars. And the live music was amazing!!

The band playing the night we went was sassy, funny, and extremely talented. I was completely sober, out hours past my comfortable bed time, and in a bar with loud music and crazy tourists and bridal parties yet I was happy as a clam because this band up on stage was one of the most talented live performing bands I'd seen yet. They played all the way to last call (yes we stayed till last call) without a break and anything from The Killers to Lady A. 

Clearly Rippy's knows how to hire them so if you're in town and looking for a great night out with talented live music, a view, a breeze, and some pretty good food definitely make a stop by.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I came in here for like the 4th time in the last 10 years. First off, the music was good, but the amp might have been tuned up a bit too high. The bar tender was nice and friendly, but my God, the prices here are comparable to NY. This is Nashville, ten bucks for a small whiskey and coke in a plastic cup is over the top. I was told "welcome to broadway prices" and I sighed. Is this city so completely blown out? It's TN after all......So, as for the food....we got the 'pick two meat, pay extra for the brisket, and pick two sides' and I was completely dissatisfied. The brisket was dry and thin, the pulled pork was satisfactory, the Mac and cheese might as well have come from a box, and the turnip greens were ABSOLUTELY horrible, tasteless and soggy. All around, 37 bucks for a shared meal and two drinks, not bad but tourist prices and the BBQ was not at all even remotely decent. I probably won't ever come here again except for a drink and live music. Has the standard for TN BBQ gone down? I get that it's "Broadway" but I should think the price of drinks and food is wayyyyy out of hand here!

name: Nashville Palace
text:
We used to like coming here.

My wife and I travel to Nashville a couple of times a year. The Nashville Palace was on our list of "must go" places, due largely to the music played on the stage in the smaller front bar room.

Times have changed.

We stopped at the Palace three times on our last trip. On a weeknight when there were maybe 20 people in the place it took almost 40 minutes to get an order of onion rings--which were lukewarm and grease soaked by the time it got to our table. The bartender was nice, but kept disappearing somewhere. Getting fresh drinks was a constant struggle.

The band was so-so for a Nashville honky-tonk. They were too loud for the space, their drummer was much too rock-n-roll for the format and they used an electronic toy to augment the background vocals. For the first time in our travels to Nashville we did not enjoy the music at the Palace.

The second time was an afternoon when a great solo act was on stage. this was our best experience of the three. the guy on stage was entertaining and the bartender kept our drinks full.

The third time was the worst. The band was great! However, we got NO service at our table. None.

If we had been drunk--we weren't--or had been a couple of jerks I could understand getting less than stellar service. All we did was sit down at a table, then got ignored.

After three hours of fetching our own drinks we had a talk with the bartender. We didn't get much of an answer from him, so we paid our tab after the band was done and left.

Bottom Line: The Nashville Palace appears to be changing their approach to service, food, and entertainment. And we believe the arrow is pointed down in all three areas.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This place is a tourist trap. This was the last place we went to during our bar hoping on a Friday night. There was a 6$ cover to get in. This was the only place that we had to pay cover at the whole night, so we were not too excited about that. The place is pretty huge inside with lots of seating and a massive dance floor. Drinks and food are overpriced. It is pretty much only good if you want to line dance all night.  Don't waste your time or money with this place. Downtown Nashville offers much better bars.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good music and the pulled pork was excellent. The fries were a little weak. Overall good choice

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Don't ask for water with your drinks they charge two dollars for a small plastic cup of water. Oh but wait she said you get free refills. Really!!!!! Wha charges for water. I guess this place

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I normally come here just for happy hour, but I noticed they added a hot catfish taco to their menu so I was slightly intrigued. Let's just say I was not disappointed. You only get two tacos. The kale peanut slaw was a delicious addition. And the cup of tomato soup was good. My girlfriend had the crispy zucchini tacos and she enjoyed it. I've been wanting to try the Mac n cheese, but I'm trying to prepare my stomach for it. 

Also, the staff is super friendly and helpful. Our waitress was attentive and sweet. I ended up leaving a tumbler in there for about a week and they kindly held onto it.

name: The Stone Fox
text: I wrote a review 6 months ago and it was a bad one. I went two weeks ago and boy have things changed! Great food great service great EVERYTHING. Definitely will be back now!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Went with a group of friends last night to Paradise Park and had an absolute blast. I specifically want to highlight the customer service from one of their employees -- Kolby. We chatted with her for about 20 minutes -- she was incredibly friendly, helpful, and made us feel right at home as a bunch of tourists coming from out of town. Would go back again without a doubt!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Quick summary: Don't go to Tootsie's; their shady waitresses will steal from you.

Longer version: My waitress here changed the tip I left on two separate charges. If you're guessing that her tip went up instead of down, you'd be correct (she added approximately $20 between the two bills). Truthfully, I probably would not have noticed her shady behavior had my credit card company not tipped me off to the extraordinarily high tip, no pun intended. 

I tried to call Tootsie's a couple times during normal business hours, but nobody answered the phone. Instead of resolving things directly with them, I am now in the fun process of disputing the charges through the credit card company. It's not a lot of money at stake, but it's about the principle of her blatantly stealing from customers that makes it worth it for me. Hopefully, I will eventually reach a manager at Tootsie's to help resolve the situation (and/or maybe get the waitress fired); I will update this post if I am able to resolve it directly with them.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Okay, if you have seen the show Nashville, you probably want to stop here! It was so much fun. We arrived around 3:30 and waited outside to see if we could get in for the 7 showing. We were 12-15th in line and we made it in along with six other people behind us! We were excited. It is a very small venue, which makes it very intimate. Although the wait outside was long, we had a ton of fun with the people by us in line. So the time passed quickly. The band sounded amazing, told stories and talked about their songs. It was exactly what we were looking for! We did not get food or drinks, but we did buy shirts. They were 26 each and the perfect souvenir for our Nashville trip!

name: Tin Roof
text: Lunch. No Service after 3 different employes looked me in the eyes. My story. I paid to park my car (meter) then went up to the bar to drink and eat lunch after 13min and no service I look around. Only 3 people at the bar. The employee is sitting at a bar stool talking to a guy. Looks at me then looks away. 2 other people that work behind the bar also did the same thing. I was so upset I got up to leave.  Instead I put more money in the meter and walked back in. Same thing.  Could not believe it. I ate next door it was very good Chicago pizza I think. Never will I go back

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Me and my boyfriend visited the Stone Fox on a Sunday around noon. We love trying locally owned restaurants, and we were impressed upon walking in with the cute decor. 

The good impression pretty much ended there. When we finally got out waitresses attention I ordered the BBQ omelet with a Bloody Mary and he ordered the chicken and waffles.

The Bloody Mary took about 10 minute to get to us and was mediocre at best. Tasted mostly like pickle juice. 

The food took another 15 minutes to find us and judging by the temperature must have been sitting out for awhile. I ate mine because I was starving, but my boyfriend was not as desperate. 

His egg and waffle were cold and his (seemingly frozen) chicken was burnt. He ended up just sending it back and not getting anything to replace it. We have been together for 3 years and that is the first time I have ever seen him send food back. 

Again, it took forever to get our server's attention for the check and she seemed irritated when I asked her a question about our bill.

We are polite people and we weren't mad because the food was bad. We just expect a certain level of service from a server and this place didn't cut it. 

I don't usually write reviews, but we were especially hopeful and then fully disappointed after trying this place. It could have been, and I hope it was, a fluke. But I do not think we will be returning and I would not recommend it to friends.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: We attended the New Year's Eve show last night and were amazed at the intimate venue and the caliber of seasoned musicians and songwriters. Everyone was very gracious and there was never a wait because we had purchased tickets. Looking forward to coming back!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place is trash.  The drinks are over-priced, service is slow, basically just a tourist trap.  From a nearby scuffle, my wife got elbowed in the lip by some guy.  After we left in our crowd because of this scuffle, I realized she had gotten hit so I went back and pointed out the guy who did it, security told me she would have to come back to the bar, show them her lip and then they would maybe remove the guy.  Considering they threw out the other guy in the scuffle, it made no sense. Security is a joke.  Take your business elsewhere, there are so many better options with better music.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Poblano pepper entree would have been a 5 star if not for the large amount of undercooked garlic cloves. If only it had been roasted it would add a sweetness instead of bitterness to this dish.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This was our first time in Nashville, and we spent all day here!  The service was amazing - you cannot walk in without being hunted by the bartender - and the music was the best by far!

The people were great as well, everyone engages in the music and has a good time.  This is our go-to spot next time we come!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I love tacos. I love mushrooms. Why not try the smoked mushroom taco?! I did NOT like it, and I like most things. Something about the taste, not sure if it was the smokiness, but something was off. I was so hungry though that I just sadly ate it. The chips and salsa helped me power through it. Plus the 3 cucumber cooler cocktails that I was downing with it. They were pretty dang strong, which I was pleasantly surprised. 

I was with a party and we were downstairs in the cellar. Really cool vibe but loud music and very dimly lit. Pretty sure I had to use my phone light to see some things on the menu. Thursday nights after 9 in the cellar turns into almost a club type area playing 90's music.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Just like that Coldplay song! Paradise Paradise...Paradi...ah crap never mind.

This place is obviously gimmicky but I liked it. Drinks were cheap enough, I think. The music was pretty good. There were a lot of people.

And then they all just cleared out like someone farted at the gym and you knew you just couldn't face another 0.75 miles on the treadmill with that vapor hanging over your head and stinging your eyes and the back of your throat. You know that situation. You just gotta get the hell out. Even if that means that you won't get to obsessively stare at the little dots as they painfully light up the perimeter of that fake quarter-mile track that you're pacing around.

Not sure what happened at Paradise Park but that kind of happened, so we left. I think we would have stayed longer otherwise.

Side note: don't look up at the vents. I said DON'T! JUST DON'T!

You won't listen to me. And you will get airborne toxic mold poisoning just by looking at the thick, black layer of god-knows-what that's just sitting up there.

You should have listened to me. But now you're ruined.

name: Tin Roof
text: If I could give this restaurant 0 stars then I would. The customer service was absolutely terrible. I sit down with my friends & it takes the waiter, a tall white male with long strawberry blonde dreads, 5 minutes to come over & take our drink orders. One of my friends was on the phone when he asked for our drinks so she did not hear him & instead of waiting just a minute he walked away with an attitude. He comes back with our drinks & we sit there looking over the menu when my friend accidentally spills my water all over me. We ask the waiter for a towel, he stares at us for a good 30 seconds, grabs a towel, throws it on the table in front of me & walks away with the same attitude he had before. This is when we took the liberty of paying for the drinks & walking out, assuring him that he performed terrible customer service, which he proceeded to roll his eyes about it & chuckle. We felt extremely unwelcome & I would highly advise anyone not to go to this restaurant & to steer clear of this particular waiter.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
i've been wanting to stop here since they opened. i did once but they were really busy and we just had a quick drink at the bar and bounced. last night my husband and i checked it out. our waiter was super nice and genuine. when we asked about beers he wasn't sure about what the types of beer were but he went and asked which was great. we both ordered and our food and drinks came out quickly. my husband had ordered the jackalope bear walker but we are both sure judging from the pour, color and taste that he actually got the ky bourbon barrell ale, which he was fine to drink so we didn't mention it. 

the food was good but overall the menu seemed really overpriced for what you are getting. i had the chicken tacos. the chicken was prepared perfectly. i really love the marinade. my husband had the reuben and mac n' cheese. he like the reuben okay and the mac n' cheese we both ate and liked. it looked like there was chili on the top of it though and i wasn't a big fan of that. 

i really like the atmosphere and our server. the food was good but not anything really fancy and overpriced. i would have liked to try some other things on the menu but didn't want to pay that much for it. i really struggled between a 3 or 4 star rating. 3.5 would have been ideal. also, parking was kind of problematic - maybe because of sinema. and on the way out it sounded like the kitchen and waitstaff was arguing when we passed the open kitchen. good but maybe underwhelming?

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
This place felt a bit too much like a fraternity house basement. And I'm not saying I'm too good to hang out in a fraternity house basement, just too old. 

There were also far too many angry dudes who looked like they were drinking straight out of their own personal pitchers of beer in order to get up the courage to punch someone (probably me) in the face. 

But at least they had Buck Hunter.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Over crowded. Girls on top floor so rude & full of themselves couldn't take care of problem! We are visiting from San Diego & we were so excited that they had a photo booth with THEIR name on it upstairs... We put in $5 & it counted down then cleared out to original screen! Brought to the bitchy long hair blondes attention & she was more concerned about her phone & the guys working that she couldn't give us customer service & either refund our money or even give us a drink!! In a customer service business it's pretty sad that they didn't take care of the problem or even put an out of order sign on it! It's Thursday & We are here until Monday too & we WONT be back!!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We stopped in with a group of 8 for a late lunch on a Friday afternoon and the place was pretty much empty, which was surprising since the place was so cool. It has a huge garage type door so that it has open air dining, and since it was beautiful out, we really enjoyed it. We got the guac, the fried pickles (they were great) and the spicy nuggets for an appetizer. The nuggets were Hot, so if you like spicy food definitely give them a try. The pulled chicken sandwich was really good as well, and packed some heat. The general manager came around as we were ready to leave and offered to take our picture as a group up on stage which was very nice of him. He explained to us about the boots hanging on the wall, and even gave us a tour of the downstairs where they have a Speak Easy and an entrance to a billiards area that opens at 4. It was cool to see the history of the building and he went out of his way to show us and explain everything which was a great start to our trip to Nashville.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
We went here for the food only, so I cannot talk about anything else.  The cashier was nice, but the food was less than desirable.  Everything we ordered was overcooked: the burger, the chicken...  YUCK.  

While we weren't expecting amazing decor, considering the name, the seating is really old and falling apart.  This was more than wear and tear.  All the tables were dirty, like no one ever bothered to wipe them down. 

Do not recommend nor would I eat here again.

name: Riverfront Park
text: We passed along through here and it was oookaaayyy. The park just seems kind of dingy and gray, and not much of a view. There's a lot of renovating and construction going on right here, so it was just meh. I'm glad I didn't have high expectations and was just passing through, or else I'd be pretty disappointed!

name: The Stone Fox
text: We went here one night for dinner and the service was pretty horrible. She forgot to put in our drink order twice and the place was empty. Food was pretty good but they were out of a lot of food and drinks on their menu. Environment was pretty fun though. I wouldn't come back to eat here again but maybe to grab a drink once in a while.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
You know that place you went to in college to get a bite at 2 am after the bars closed down? Fortunately, you can relive that experience at Paradise Park. Located on Broadway, in the middle of all the bars, it's one of the few places that serves food into the early morning hours and seems to be full of those trying to soak up large amounts of alcohol consumed over the last few hours. 

Actually, the food isn't that bad, when comparing to McDonald's type restaurants. It's close to a Waffle House experience where you see the cook slap your burger on the grill after you order. This isn't a nice, sit down restaurant with table service. It's cheap food meant to be consumed with and after alcohol and when you compare it to other establishments that are similar how can you complain? 

The buns are even better than you get at a fast-food place. Their BBQ sauce isn't bad - at all. And, the burgers are edible as are the fries and sweet potato fries. I ordered the turkey and shockingly enjoyed it. It wasn't some packaged turkey, it tasted like fresh shaved turkey and came on bread that had substance. 

Come with the right expectations - and you won't be disappointed. And, remember it's a perfect fit for those looking for soak up alcohol, rather than a good, Southern cooked meal.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: We had made reservations very far in advance and arrived a couple minutes late due to our taxi getting lost.  After we arrived and gave the hostess our name, she had already given our reservation away.  As we were walking away, she told the line of people 5 spaces just opened up (our reservation).  We were disappointed she could have let us in, but turned us away before our seats were even taken.

name: World Music Nashville
text: Would it be ridiculous to call this the "best music shop in Nashville"??  If you are the average player, I think it may be.  If you are planning on spending tens of thousands on pre-CBS Fenders previously owned by James Burton then yeah, go to one of the famous Nashville shops.  Otherwise, these guys are the deal.  I come here on business from California and pop into the different shops when I have time, so I have been in most if not all.  A guy named Brandon helped me and the dude was knowledgeable, patient and super helpful sharing his knowledge with no pretension or arrogance.  He let me try a few guitars and amps and I learned a bunch from him.  He spent maybe 35 minutes with me and closing time came and went during this time without him saying a word about it.  Also, nobody in here pulled the "...yeah I should be a (touring/session) musician but the (record company/Industry) screwed me and now I am stuck selling guitars to you, and blah, blah, blah..." which you sometimes get in Nashville.  Their selection is fantastic and it's really laid out in a way that encourages you to play instruments through their amps.  Great shop.

name: World Music Nashville
text: Just had a recent visit into World Music and have nothing but high praise for the staff. I have an acoustic guitar, not purchased from them, that needed a little setup work and not only took care of it while I waited but the staff person shared good knowledge on general maintenance and upkeep of my new instrument. Price was more than fair. Very obliging, offered to let me play anything in their extensive inventory. Great, helpful people! This is a great business in a city with an abundance of music stores, these folks really stand out, My next guitar will certainly come from WMN.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Great place to eat before TPAC. Food was good and very fast. Service great as well. Nothing bad on the menu. No domestic draft beer but several IPA options. Sit at the counter if you get a chance.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place is the most fun with great entertainment.  Don't miss Jakes Maurer he is my favorite. Always a fun time.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: This is a great place to listen to great music. My family and I have been coming here for years. since the show Nashville, it is impossible get get show tickets anymore. The way you reserve tickets now is nothing but Stupid!!! I have tried my last time to get tickets for a show here.there are plenty more places to listen to music in Nashville than here!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Food never disappoints, especially from their new menu. Can't beat their mac and cheese! Downstairs has a cool lounge vibe, and you can order off a limited menu down there as well. They have a fantastic happy hour until 7 that includes half off wine, beer and certain specialty cocktails.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
The energy was wild and made this place electric with excitement.  "Country roads!! Take me home!! To a place!! Where I belong!!" coming from the lungs of everyone on the roof.

Live music on all 3 levels, but the roof seemed where the party was. It had a little more room to breath with a cool (60 person capacity) observation deck overlooking Broadway. It was built for some good day drinking. 

It should be a tour stop on your own personal adventure.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: While the music was great everything else about this establishment was terrible. The drinks were absolutely overpriced which is not quite a terrible thing for the location. What was deserving of a one star review was the apparent direction from management/ownership to evacuate all patrons within 5 minutes of actual last call. Any plea to finish a beverage within the coming 5 minutes after turning on all the lights falls on deaf ears and large biceps that are clearly unreceptive. Go and have a ton of fun, tip the amazing bands graciously, and evacuate well before last call.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
If you want a soy chai latte with a side of religion, then you are in the right place. If you don't, you can ignore the religious undertones.

The chai latte was good, it hit the spot. The decor is homey, feels very upscale barn inspired and seems like a good place to study. They get an A+ for best transformation of an old fast food joint. 

I definitely will not drive to Green Hills to get a drink here but if I am in the area, I will absolutely stop by.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The view is great, but the drinks are absurd. I understand paying $10 for a good vodka drink because of the location, so I got a vodka Sprite. What I got was a Dixie cup of straight Sprite. I even let people around me try it, literally laughing out loud that I paid for it. I went back and wondered maybe if she had forgotten the vodka, and the brunettes response was shrugging her shoulders and said "um, I never under pour" and walked away. Have you ever worked in customer service or at any bar? Maybe y'all should try your own drinks before you keep ripping us off.

name: The Stone Fox
text: I don't want to be too harsh, the food was just OK, but fresh for sure.  best ranch dressing definitely homemade.  took a long time to get food but we didn't care. back patio is nice, love the pallet garden and lights.  I'm sure if you go to see the music it gets even better. glad you are in the neighborhood. the servers were very nice and attentive.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Several floors to bounce around on, each playing different live music.  I liked this place even though it was almost impossible to move around.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Good experience when in Nashville because of the history. Lots people, pretty crowded, and loud. Recommend going to the 3rd floor there was more space. Great musical acts!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The world famous Tootsies is a fun place on Broadway.  Beers are kinda pricey at $6 each, but you do get entertainment.  Each floor has live country music depending on what style you like.  The first floor was the most fun and can get packed.  Found this place to be most fun in the afternoon it's more of a laid back vibe.  The rooftop patio was nice but always packed.  A lot of good artist singing here, even the door guy rocked it out!  This is a must stop when in Nashville on Broadway.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Sooooo many good food places in Nashville, do yourself a favor and don't waste your time at this one. The bluegrass band was great and The bartender was nice. The mimosas transfer from bar to table so that's awesome and convenient But that's about it. The food comes out very fast because it is not fresh. The table service is also extremely slow and our server messed up our order and tried to blame it on the kitchen. If your priority is cheap mimosas and listening to music do it,  but there are such great food places nearby don't waste your time here if you actually care about food quality. 1 hour plus wait for a table, and not worth the wait.

name: Tin Roof
text: Food is pretty decent; however, we had to approach the bar to get a server to our table and 3 people sat at the bar right by us and we're waiting for about ten minutes while the bartenders were standing in front of them on their phones not even willing to help. That's not the way to treat customers if you want their tip...

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: We had the best time at the bluebird! We caught the 8:00 show on Sunday. (Waited for 2 hours outside to get in but it was so worth it) We heard a ton of different singer song writers (Anne buckle was amazing!) and then had an hour of Victoria banks who told some really amazing stories and put on a great show. Food was good. Company was great. We loved the bluebird!!!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
It's not amazing, but it does have booze, is staffed by hipsters, and most importantly:

A black velvet tapestry of Tom Selleck in his Magnum PI prime.

I don't think you need any other reasons to go here.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Great Beer. Cool, laid-back atmosphere with Live Music.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I had the fried chicken salad with sweet potato fries on the side. Delish! The fried chicken bites were amazing. My friend got the brisket sandwich and really liked it. The bartender was awesome and had us try the assortment of sauces. The Texas Ketchup was seriously good and I am going to buy some online because it was that bomb. I'd come back here for sure. Also had a Bloody Mary and the Bearded Iris IPA. Recommend both!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: This place has a really good Happy Hour. Half off drinks! You can never pass that up. I tried my friend food she had the grill cheese and it came with some tomato soup. When I tell you that soup was sooooooooo good! I have to order it the next time I visit. The basement area is amazing and so chill!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: First time in Nashville and we heard this place had really good food , it didn't disappoint the ambience was great had a great burger and BLT

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The female fiddle player is insanely good! Her blonde singer counterpart, however, is not. She's the one who demands money even though her fiddle-playing colleague deserves all the money.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
What a great spot for experiencing a show!  It's small and very intimate and I really liked the unique set-up of enjoying a performance in the center of a bar/café/restaurant.  Every seat is a good seat in this place.

It is very popular and very tough to get into...we planned ahead and I thought it was worth the time spent in trying to make this happen.  The staff is friendly just adds to the great experience here.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Went around 1030am on Saturday morning.  Got a table on 3rd floor.  Was pretty empty then but was packed by noon.  The group playing on 3rd floor was awesome. The waitress was very good and we were happy to get there early enough to get a table.  Was a mix of older crowd and younger crowd and the band did well with that.  Bottle beer was $7 for Mich ultra but I guess that's how they afford the bands since there's no cover.  We happily stayed for 3.5 hours before heading to the airport to fly home.  Definitely worth checking Tootsie's out.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
If you are visiting Nashville, you go here. Doesn't matter if you want to go, if it is your scene....this is just one of the places you go.
It is crowded, expensive, and loud (live music!!). But it is loads of fun!
But it is basically one of the quintessential places to go out downtown.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Last night I walked into the sutler to place a togo order, it was my birthday(8/22) and I wanted their delicious burger dripping in cheese sauce. It's my favorite burger in town. It was busy, so I patiently waited for the bartender. She asked me what she could get for me. I said burger, mac and cheese, and collard greens Togo. Then she blatantly stops me with a traffic cop hand, asks me if I'm with the person next to me at the bar, I said no but I just need a burger, greens and Mac n cheese Togo. She proceeds to wave her finger at me as if to pause our exchange, doesn't take my order, and proceeds to take two more drink orders from other people at the bar. 3 minutes later she's back, and she's acting like she still doesn't have time or patience for me. I had to tell her 5 times in all, because apparently I was talking entirely too fast for this fast-paced short-order bartender to comprehend that I wanted a burger, collard greens, and Mac and cheese Togo. She offered fries, and I obliged. When I came back for the food, there were no napkins, utensils, or ketchup offered or included in my $30 order. I asked for them, and she gave me this look like I crapped in her cereal. She warns me it could be a few minutes because they ran out upstairs and she would have to go to the downstairs bar to get them. This is when I started getting upset, because the last time I was there I tried to order a burger in their downstairs lounge, and got denied my food order because food was only available upstairs....while I watched some other guy at the other end of the bar eating a burger!!!! Why would you need Togo cutlery as far away from the exit as possible?! It's for people that exit your establishment with their uneaten food! So she sends a bar back down to get them, 3 minutes later he's back, and she  still doesn't have the time or the ketchup for me. Now the exchange is complete, and I walk out the door. I'm still confused as to why food can't be delivered downstairs, it's like they don't want to profit, they'd rather tell their guests No. Let's talk about the food. 
    I wasn't aware that they had changed their Mac and cheese, no more broccolinis:( I wasn't aware that they had stopped putting fried chicken skin atop their collards:( they do their fries like five guys, except it's like their fryer can't handle it so we had like 3 pounds of oily/soggy shoe string fries. Or the best soft McDonald's fries you could imagine attempting to enjoy. Don't sacrifice quality to satisfy your bubba guests.
     The burger, the burger, the burger. I asked her for an extra side of cheese sauce FOR THE BURGER twice during our altercation. I'm giving her the benefit of the doubt, because she might be new. I haven't seen her before, and she was kind of moving in slow motion. She might not have ever had the chance to try the glory that was their burger, that deity-like cheese sauce and those wickle pickles on there, oh my god it was so good. I found the order ticket from the computer in with the French fries and she ordered an extra side of cheese sauce for the Mac and cheese....which wasn't in the bag. Neither was the burger I wanted. The burger I got was this little ratty cheese burger with melted sliced cheese on top of peppers on an old moldy bun. I'm not one to complain about mold on bread, but this was an ugly looking burger. In their defense, in regards to my photo, I ripped the burger in half and then took the picture.  I still ate it, fearing a 20-30 minute wait, or the attitude,  If I were to step back inside their establishment. Ive spent around a thousand dollars in that place since they opened, and I'm starting to lose appreciation for their inconsistent standards of service and food quality. It's a great tourist trap, I'll give them that.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Guitarists and fiddlers dancing on bar tops? YES PLEASE!! Tootsie's is the best bar in Nashville. The music were amazing, the patrons were friendly and the beer was cold. Great place.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: If you only go to one place on Broadway, go to Tootsie's!!  The bands are great and it.s lots of fun! And there is a 2nd band upstairs.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place is amazing! We actually never made it upstairs, only staying on the first floor, but we had the time of our lives there! The music was awesome, the beers were cold and the atmosphere rocked! If you don't like crowds this probably isn't the place for you but we loved it!

name: Riverfront Park
text: I decided to come down here for a quick short walk before work after it rained a whole heck of a lot. The water had risen up the steps and then you realize, yeah this isn't that high compared to the flood of 2010. It's nice to have this relatively quiet space downtown, which can easily be used for events also. Good work Nashville. Outdoor green spaces for the win!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Very disappointed with this place. I was soooo excited to do their "bluegrass brunch" and even though it was on the other side of town, even though the locals tried to persuade me to a different place, I wanted to try this place. The restaurant was really cute and pretty busy on a Saturday afternoon. We were seated in Emma's station and we ordered the bottomless mimosas for $15. I asked if we could have ice in them and it seemed to baffle her. I said, can you just bring 2 pint glasses with ice then and we'll dump our mimosa in there. Her response was "I cant serve you 2 drinks at once". Um...what? 1st of all, yes you can, but thats not what I was asking. We decided to share the brisket hash with sweet potatoes, peppers and greens. It was served lukewarm and the brisket was overcooked and super fatty but the rest was really flavorful. It really had potential. I got a side of the andouille sausage as well and that was really good. Emma kept up on our mimosas but they were super weak. They mix them in a pitcher to make it easier on the servers but the oj/ champagne ratio is off....big time. We basically paid $15 for bottomless oj. We also got a side of biscuits which were very good with a sweet butter and grape jelly. I wouldn't come back here. Food and service were pretty forgettable. Ohhhh yeahhh....AND...they say Bluegrass brunch on Saturday and Sunday but thats a big ol lie. There is only live music on Sunday. See pic...totally makes it sound like the live bluegrass is on Saturday as well. This is the reason we came here in the 1st place. Very deceiving.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Worst system EVER!!!!  Never waited in line so long w/ no communication. NOT WORTH IT!!!!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This place is known for being just across the alley from the back door of the old Ryman Auditorium that used to house the Grand Ole Opry.  Performers would come over between acts, have a few drinks, and then head back over to perform.  Thus, many, many famous people have visited this club, and the pictures on the wall bear the proof.  But, there is more than just history being served here.  

We came in to check it out, and ended up enjoying the cuisine.  Tootsies actually has a pretty decent Black Bean Burger for the vegetarians in the crowd, and both my wife and I found it to be very tasty.  It was a good value, too.  The burger itself had a good texture, a good flavor, and it really hit the spot.  It comes with seasoned fries that are pretty good, too.  Just note that all the condiments come in little packets instead of bottles, so, if you like a lot of catsup, mustard, and mayo,  you're going to have to open a lot of packets.  The prices is pretty good, too.  

If you like dining in history, and you like eating vegetarian, this place fits the bill.  We also enjoyed the friendly, helpful staff.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
RUDE, we didn't even get to eat b/c when we walked in with our babies(us and our friends had their baby too) they practically rolled their eyes. When we went to the hostess to ask for a table she said "we don't have high chairs" then put our name down. She said it would only be a few minutes wait, then she disappeared and reappeared to tell us that they were not seating anymore people b/c they were too full.
WHAT?! what kind of restaurant turns  waiting customers away? Needless to say we WILL NOT be going back. So if you have babies or a kid(s) don't even think about going to this snobby place.

name: Tin Roof
text: Maybe it was just the time and day I went (Fri night, midnightish) but the place was packed  shoulder-to-shoulder. It was so crowded you couldn't do anything. I didn't get what the hype was, but maybe it's cooler other nights of the week.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
First timer. Went with a couple girlfriends for brunch on a Sunday and it was fairly busy. Our waitress was nice. She disappeared for a bit, but she came back and apologized for it. 

We started off with mimosas and they offer $20 carafe that serves 4 people. Always a plus when they have some kind of special on drinks. 

I just had the biscuits and gravy and deviled eggs. I'm not a vegetarian, but none of the other items seemed to pop out at me. (I was hoping for either some kind of salmon or turkey sausage dish, which there was neither) The biscuits were fluffy and the gravy was tasty. They offer unique topping deviled eggs, but today they were only serving the traditional kind, I was a little bummed about that, but it was still good. 

My gf's had the chicken and waffle and the biscuits and jam with chicken. Neither complained about the food, nor raved about it, so I'm just assuming it was decent. We were busy catching up about other stuff so that could be why the food was never commented on. 

Everything was just okay.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: One of the best places in Nashville. The hot fish tacos are the best thing I've had so far, although the grill Bologna sandwich is is close second. And the sweet potato hummus with a side of pickled onions and jalapeños is also excellent. Very cool space, too.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: With local recommendations- we went for breakfast. The staff was SO friendly and personable! The meal was great!! (Jalapeno bacon especially) we will be back!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Visited from Chicago last April. The staff at Toosies really stood out and set the bar higher than other bars on Broadway. Overall, It's a great city and I can't wait to visit again.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Slow slow slow. 1pm Saturday.  Food ok. Good band.  Get ur chit together.  I dont mind waiting but it appears that the cook is in need of some help and a better mrthod of orded delivery

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Always a great time!  Bands have been consistently great every time we come to Nashville.  Absolutely,  a place to have a few drinks and enjoy the music.

name: Tin Roof
text:
This place took a solid 15 minutes to get a drink on a slow Thursday night on the more quiet bar. Didn't stay too long past that -- due to the change in venue that we went for. 

The overall feel for this place was good though. Seems like a decent staff as long as you don't mind waiting awhile did your drink.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: If you're visiting from out of town and want a fun bar this is it!!  Three floors with a different live band on each floor, rooftop bar, bar food and drinks!

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
UGH! Why didn't someone call me and TELL me this was a non-profit. I would have put my 'non-profit judgy-ness' hat on instead of the usual 'Grr...I'm a grumpy consumer'  hat on. I'll totally give the place snaps for warm/weird vibe but really, do I need the crazy lady in the corner making laps around the place pan handling while we are working? 
I'm sure this is mecca to the Hillsboro High students who are a block away and, in fairness, the hot chocolate was bad arse...warm and spiced with I dunno what? Crack? Vanilla? Cinnamon? At least two of three anyway.  But seriously nutty chick, if I can't get my work done, we're both gonna be homeless so lets give that stuff a rest.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Cool atmosphere, neat history, food is over-priced + over-rated. Service is average. 

Example: $15 cheeseburger. 

Grass-fed = good. 

Previously frozen + sliced American cheese + tasteless pink grocery store tomato + huge bun = are you kidding? So what if there is a (average) fried egg and half a (average) sliced avocado? And no way did this patty start out at 8 ounces, as the menu claimed.

name: The Stone Fox
text: I love this place for beer! It is a great place to hangout and relax with a great beer selection. As for the food, it is just mediocre. It isn't bad but isn't great. I have only been for brunch though.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
The Bluebird Cafe is a listening room and it's well-reknowned for a venue for a songwriter's performance.  I thought it was amazing that we were able to hear the 'heroes behind the hit' perform their own songs, and song that have been recorded by chart-topping artists in all the genres of music.  It was cool as they have 2 different setups, dependent on which artists you see - they can either perform on stage or do an 'ITR' (In The Round).  We had the latter, so the songwriters actually sat in the middle of the cafe, and the tables were placed all around them.  Technically, there are no 'bad' seats, but I wished we were a little bit closer to the singers (we had Table 20) - for anyone who is claustrophobic, this can be a little challenging!  We got to see Thom Schuyler, Fred Knobloch, Jack Sundrud, and Jelly Roll Johnson (best harmonicist EVER!) - they played either as a quartet or as an individual.  The songs were just plain awesome, and the vibe was more of a laid-back atmosphere.  The guys had a great sense of humor, shared stories, and played their bits.  The only 'downside' is that you have to make reservations online (can be quite stress-ridden as I almost fainted from trying to navigate the site and it was slowed down as I'm sure hundreds of other people were trying to get a spot), and you are required to spend a minimum of $7 per seat on drinks/food - I just had a ginger ale and their housemade chips with chipotle mayo sauce - pretty safe, and it was pretty good (the chips were cold, though, but the combo was good and salty).  Our server checked up on us and was was very sweet.  You line up to your left, and the right of the entrance are for people who don't have tickets and who are offered any available seats for no-shows/cancellations.  When you walk in, you pay with cash and are seated.  I really enjoyed the experience here and I'm so glad I was able to check this place out! :D

+purchase tickets online (high anxiety!)
+highly suggest 'ITR' (In The Round'
+$7 minimum on food/drinks

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
I am a coffee freak.  Seriously, I might have a problem.  And the biggest problem for purveyors of my beloved caffeine addiction is that I drink my coffee black.  With my love of this fantastic beverage, I would be about 500 pounds if I added cream and sugar, so oil sludge it is.  So to give me a good cup of coffee can be challenging.  Most coffee tastes burnt.  

But one day while out and about and wanting desperately to enjoy coffee I happened to spot this little place in Green Hills, and I cut someone off (sorry random person) to turn into the parking lot.  First of all its adorable in here.  Kind of like a barn.  Lots of people studying (as coffee shops are good places for that) and friendly people behind the counter.  And a wishing wall for people to post about raising money for charities and mission trips.  Overall really cool just from the visual.  

And then came the coffee, which was utterly fabulous.  Buttery delicious not-burnt-not-crap coffee.  I was in heaven.  And they have great little food options as well.  It's a little pricier for coffee, but I promise you its worth it, and I can't wait to have an excuse to go back.  I recommend grabbing a delicious beverage from here and then going about your shopping in Green Hills.  Way better than Starbucks.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: It might be 3 pm outside, but people in here are partying like it's 3am. Holy bachelorettes. If you're looking for a fun, loud, honky-tonkin good time, this is the place. People complaining about crowds, bouncers, and bathrooms must not go out all that much, or maybe don't know where exactly they are. It was packed inside and in the mid 90s outside, but somehow thanks to fans and AC, it wasn't too hot. The bathroom was actually really clean when I was there. Yes, the beer prices are steep, but you are paying for a full experience that includes awesome live music and being in a Nashville institution. We had the most fun on the third floor. The crowd was drunk but happy, and the band was a blast. We saw tourists, college kids, 30-somethings, some people in their 60s, and packs of bachelorettes. After dancing, it was nice to go onto the roof top and look at the people on the streets. It's a must-do for tourists.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Food exists here. There are things you can put in your mouth and chew on.

Will you like that food?

No. 

Why?

It is disgusting. We got terrible chicken fingers and a grilled cheese sandwich. I sent my grilled cheese back.

Read that again. I sent a grilled cheese sandwich back. The reason, yes you guessed it, they forgot the cheese. 

You have to work hard to screw up a grilled cheese sandwich. 

Next, the buffalo chicken tenders taste like they were still using yesterday's fry oil. I think leaving this menu item there will suffice.

My advice? Go somewhere else your conscience and colon will thank you.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Voted by our entire family of 5 as the best meal in Nashville. Something for every person on the menu and the flavors.... oh my gosh .... my very picky tastebuds were super happy. 

It just tasted like the food was actually crafted with thought and love instead of cranked out for the tourist crowd. The chef has done an amazing job of keeping a simple menu with phenomenal tastes. 

The building itself is lovingly restored and the staff were all kind and attentive. Sivon, our waitress was so kind! Food runner Zack made sure the kids were fed first - so important! 

Sweet potato pancakes were AMAZING. The biscuits were also our fave of the trip. Husband said the fried chicken was also best of the trip (he ate fried chicken all over the state). 

Special note to the proprietor.... it was amazing and refreshing to see the love in restoring this special place. As the city gets more and more modern, it was beautiful to walk into a restored place of history that was obviously curated with love and attention. Beautifully done.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Place has great history went there for breakfast corn beef hash was great I really enjoyed the seafood gumbo the sweet potato pancakes were surprisingly very good we were unsure if we wanted them or would like them and when we got them we weren't disappointed I definitely suggest checking out the Woolworth

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: The food is pretentious and over priced. They've tried to make upscale diner food without success. The fried chicken was nothing special and the mashed potatoes were the worst I've ever eaten. They had a chemical taste. The green beans were also strangely flavored. The bf had the shrimp and grits and said the grits were bland. The only reason I'm giving 3 stars is because of the excellent and friendly service and my best friend's complicated order. .

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Had the honor of catching an intimiate show at the world-famous Bird on my last trip to Nashville. Initially I was expecting more of a bar-scene, but was suprised when I realized it was just that, a cafe. A very personal setting where I got to literally sit right behind the performers. Now, I'm not a country music fan, but I very much enjoyed this. 'When in Rome.' Or at least 'when in the Athens of the South.'

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: It's crazy how you keep a place open when you have an issue with a toilet leak from the 2nd floor pouring down to the first level where people were walking in and it just kept pouring down. After at least an hour of it coming down they closed the first level realizing that it was a sewer issue. Shane on the establishment for staying open and keep people walking through sewer water. It's all about making the money shame on you. I actually have video of this happening and they just kept the place going and the music playing. Totally disgusting!!!

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text: I like to separate my Church and Coffee, and for that, and only that, I'll ding a star off The Well. Discounting that, The Well is a great place to experience some really interesting coffees from around the world, brewed in tender and slow processes (such as Aeropress) to maximize the experience. They have a nice sit-out which, on a cloudy Fall day, or a sunny Spring afternoon, makes a great place to hang out. Free Wi-Fi everywhere makes this an attractive place for students, but I also go there to write at times, and get a break in scenery from the Fido-Frothy Monkey routine!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great bar with live music! Stays open late. I would recommend trying to get a table on the rooftop, the view of downtown Nashville is amazing! The history alone is worth giving it a go!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Walking into this place, it just feels like Nashville, and it feels good. There's a country band playing, but you don't feel like you have to yell to talk to your friends. We ordered some awesome appetizers, the popcorn blew me away! Great vibe in this joint, they have a super cool downstairs bar that is always packed. In fact, I would definitely suggest making a reservation, cause the Sutler is always busy! I went with my wife on a Tuesday, and it was crazy! We had a good time, especially when the food came out, I ordered the trout and it was kickass. Our waitress was super sweet too. Check it out!!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
A must, must do in Nashville! Super friendly and funny staff - as a party of 8 arriving around 11 AM on a Saturday, we got seated immediately; definitely got lucky, though. When I had called about a week earlier, I was advised to have a party of that size arrive right at opening.
