Bloody Mary bar was fantastic; the bacon was great and all the fixings seemed fresh and continuously replenished. I loved getting to dress up my drink myself! A few at our table had bottomless mimosas which were a hit. The biscuit dishes were highly enjoyed, as well as the breakfast tacos and enchiladas. Smoked brisket hash sounded great but it wasn't a standout. I cleaned my chicken and waffles plate - they were so yummy! The brown sugar butter is super good. 

The live music made everything great and the decor and energy of the place were absolutely perfect! Will definitely come back someday!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: (6/21/2014)  So apparently one of the more famous "honky tonks" in Nashville.  Reportedly, some of the early famous first customers were Willie Nelson, Patsy Cline, Mel Tillis, Kris Kristofferson, Waylon Jennings.  Place is right behind the Ryman Auditorium.  We had to stop in, just to stop in.  Got a rail drink and a Bud, for $14, would call that on the high side for prices, but I guess we were downtown.  It was Saturday night, it was crowded, it was loud.  All the surfaces were sticky with booze, as were the drunken and rowdy bachelors and bachelorettes (apparently if you're getting married in a 300 mi radius you have to blow your wad in Nashville??).  I guess all I can say is that I've been to Tootsie's World Famous Orchid Lounge.  Period.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
I've been to Stone Fox twice now for brunch, and it's awesome. Every time I am visiting Nashville we make it a point to go to brunch here. There usually isn't a huge line, but it's typically full. This seems to still be a hidden gem brunch spot.

I'm not the biggest Bloody Mary drinker, but I love their Bloody Mary. Definitely worth trying out. They have good Saturday morning deals on mimosas and Bloody Marys.

The food is great, never had something I didn't like. They have a decent selection of items. 

The atmosphere might be the best thing about this place. The stuff on the walls is really cool, including a giant mental hanging of the United States. They have all different tables, chairs, plates, and cups.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I loved how a lot of things were the same like the floor and the counter looked. I took my mother for her birthday to relive old memories for her as a child. I wish we would have seen more pictures of how the place looked in the past on the walls upstairs however the upstairs was mostly about the civil rights movement than the actual restaurant itself. The food was also disappointing we went for Brunch and ordered sides. The gravy was cold the biscuits tased like the kind I make from the freezer section and they didn't have much of a brunch breakfast selection. I also got a Bloody Mary and it was ok. I think Dinner maybe the better choice on when to go for food. Our waiter was nice however he knew nothing about the history of the restaurant or the pictures upstairs only that there was some...

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We came to Tootsie's after running the TN Ragnar, I had never been to Nashville before so I was very much looking forward to visiting a few bars in the area.  Tootsies was fun, it of course was packed with people.  We ended up on the top floor where we saw a few good singers but it was chilly from the fans or wind being blown.  We decided to leave because apparently the gentleman MCing was extremely rude to one of my teammates.  I'd probably give it another cautionary shot if I returned to Nashville in my life.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Maybe we came on a bad day but at least for breakfast, would not recommend this place. Service very slow, limited menu, sweet potato pancakes too sweet to eat. Not enough gravy on biscuits, jalopeno bacon burnt. Will need to eat again soon. Is cool for the history.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I cannot praise this establishment enough, especially the service. Shan, our waitress, was phenomenal. Our mimosas never once ran dry. The food was amazing and the attention to detail was impeccable. I definitely recommend the chicken fried chicken biscuits and the biscuits Benedict! Also, request Shan, as she is the best!!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Freakin Fantastic Honky-Tonk Friday Fun!

SITREP

Something I noticed about the venues in Downtown Nashville along Broadway - they like their levels!

I mean, you can have a music venue on one level, then a full-blown bar on another level, and then a music venue AND bar on a top level.  Sheer size overwhelmnent!

THE BAR

Let's start with the easy stuff - I just defaulted to my go-to of Sam Adams which ran a cool $4, plus a buck for the tip.  After that, things got a lot more complicated...

THE SETUP

And to be honest, I may have been a bit buzzed to know at any given moment EXACTLY what level I was on since I was following my local Nashville buddies around, and like a passenger in the car, you may not be paying attention to where you're "driving to" and "how you're getting there" cause you're too busy looking at "the scenery" along the way!

A CROWD SURFING ADVENTURE

It was like a human ocean, and sometimes you'd get got in the currents and eddies head to the bar, or to the restroom (which is how/why I almost ended up getting sucked into the women's room because I was got into the vortex of 5 blonde rocker chicks - had to "extract" myself....).

IT'S A SMALL WORLD

Back to the stage, oh my god, the scenery!  I don't know why we eventually left the room where all the girls were dancing in front of the band, behind the band, and AMIDST the band members (oh wait, I was WITH girls, that's why), but that was just fun to see!  

And crowded!  It was virtual rainbow land of Asian women, African-American women, Caucasian women, all emblazoned in different dance attire, shaking their booties to Def Leppard, then Nine Inch Nails, and then the bands' own country tunes.  It was amazeballs! 

LOST AGAIN

This place is HUGE to the first-time stranger, with it's labyrinth of halls and stairs, kinda like an Escher Bach sketch where you may not really be leaving the floor you thought you were.  

When we were walking through 1st level (but I think, it COULD have been the 2nd Level if that's the level the bathrooms are on - and THEN if you're trying to orient yourself from the rear entrance - where we came in - that's not necessarily the same as the ground level from the front entrance), it was like a roller-coaster ride since we kept going UP, and then DOWN, and then UP, and then DOWN again as we were crossing over one dance pit, then to another .  See my confusion?

ADDITIONAL DISCOMBULATION

We would go outside after haggling with the back security guard so that we could be assured we'd get back inside.  [He was a bit distracted at the time too since he could not find his smartphone.]  The girls were taking a smoking break in the back alley and after an hour we corralled everyone back up, and mosied through the back door into Tootsies to THEIR back door where our awesome Nashville hosts - Chris, Nickie and Marti - worked their magic and got us in.

THE BANDS

I listened to 3 throughout my Tootsie adventures and they were definitely strong in the countrified rock and honky-tonk genres, but very gifted in parlaying their talents towards Heavy Metal and Industrial.  

THE LOWDOWN

A most excellent musical rodeo ride in Downtown Nashville!

name: Tin Roof
text: This place was awesome to go to. Alex was probably the coolest bartender, and made our group feel welcomed to the city. Bob franklin really has a great running business. If you like a great atmosphere, and a staff that matches that you'll have to go there.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Everything (Music, Food, Staff, Song Writers) about this place was phenomenal. We definitely enjoyed our time here.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsies hires individuals who impersonate officers and carried concealed weapons without a license ?! What a responsible establishment you folks have been running. We were contacted by the "head of security" and were reinsured that "this officer" would be talked to after the incident that occurred earlier this year. How ironic that it comes out this man has been IMPERSONATING AN OFFICER and Tootsies continued to allow it! Justice has been served! May he gets what he deserves and may Tootsies step up and actually provide a safe establishment to their guests.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great variety of old country and classic rock.  Very fun place to hang out and get the party started.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I came because of the series Nashville but I would return on its own accord.. This place is amazing and quaint! Small and intimate it's the perfect venue and everything sold was very reasonable.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text: It's a very nice coffeehouse. It has a wide open space and a nice patio. I got the Mocha an it was very good. What makes the place pretty awesome is the profits from sales go to help stop poverty and underprivileged areas.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: This is still one of the best places in Nashville.  Good food and good beer selection. Friendly service and the atmosphere is fun with awesome decor.  The parking is starting to be a problem though which sucks because that was always a big reason we would go.  Hopefully that gets fixed.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Avoid the bartender who looks like she's on steroids, she becomes perplexed when it doesn't involve a juice a monkey concoction !

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Not sure how I haven't reviewed Tootsie's yet since it is a Nashville staple. However, it's also a tourist trap and I cannot stand it. Every time that I've been there, it has been crazy packed (no surprise) and I can't even enjoy the fact that I'm there because I'm packed like a sardine in a can. The musical acts I've seen there are pretty decent, which is expected. However, the staff seems incredibly overwhelmed all the time, thus putting them in a bad mood. I tend to avoid this bar but I guess ya gotta experience it just once to say "I've been to Tootsie's"!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Obsessed!!! The food- atmosphere- and wait staff were amazing.  I can't wait to come back.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: The service was very good, the food and setting was average. I was not happy when I got the bill and found out they were charging $2 for rocks (aka ICE) in my bourbon! Bottom line: extremely overpriced for what you're getting and I wouldn't come back.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Great food along with an amazing vibe reminiscent of the classic 1960s restaurant. Love the nostalgic video and movie screen showing clips from the era.

name: Tin Roof
text: Great music and pretty good appetizers. Not amazing but a great atmosphere to grab a bite to eat and listen to live music. A good experience overall. Glad we found it.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We love The Sutler! We really love that it's off the beaten path. The space is really nice, good seating for all to see the show going on as opposed to all Broadway honkey tonks. Drink selection is really good. Do not recommend the nachos, too small. The walk down to the restrooms has a bunch of hanging cowboy boots which was really cool! Also connects to a pool hall downstairs.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: The hamburgers at Paradise Park are GREAT!  Tastes like a burger you would make at home.  All the toppings are fresh and the meat is MEAT.  I highly recommend this place.  It looks like a dump from the street, but the food is so so good.  I am so glad we decided to eat here. as it was our last day in Nashville.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I went here for brunch today and the food was amazing. Crisp bacon, scrambled eggs, creamy grits, soft French toasted bread and a special complementary bowl of hash!!!!!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: First time there and have to say I was not disappointed. My son told me that some famous artists occasionally just show up there. Boy was he right!  After Brad left I went upstairs and listened to this great band covering everything from Garth Brooks to Led Zeppelin to Sublime and everything in between.  It's a must visit if you're in Nashville.

name: Tin Roof
text: I am not one for negative reviews and especially not one to put down a bartender or server of any sort. Last night was an exception. As I was waiting to get a drink for my two friends and I, one of the bartenders had to ask what I wanted three different times in a three minute time span. He was obviously intoxicated and I still remained patient with him. After the first drink he made he took a shot with someone next to me. Still waiting for my other two drinks he took two other girls' drink orders. He made the second drink and had to ask me again for the third drink order. As he was about to make my third drink (or so I thought) there was a man behind me who he knew. The man behind me was talking about how he has better hair then the bartender. The bartender then leaned over so close to my face where I could smell his vile breath and asked me obnoxiously who has "better hair" between them two. I asked where my third drink was (it has been atleast ten minutes now since I first told him my order.) He made me my drink and I gave him my card and told him to close out. He walked down to the cash register where I kept watching him and watched him swipe my card. He then found a bunched up napkin next to him and I watched him throw it at a guy in front of him messing around with him. He then started pouring them shots and I watched him take two shots with them. All during this time he had my card in his hand waving it around. I asked the other bartender to please have him bring me my card. The other bartender was no help and also seemed to be intoxicated. I then asked him where his manager was and he told me he would go get the other bartender. The other bartender came back with my card and I told him I wanted to speak to his manager when he then replied "Why are you in such a bad mood?" And I said "It has taken you 20 minutes to get me a drink." And as I was walking away he called me a "fucking bitch." This was my first drink of the night and it was also my last. I do not associate his post with the whole business as I have been here before and have had great experiences, but this one particular bar tender was very degrading to your business.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsie's is Me and my boyfriends favorite bar in downtown Nashville. They have the best bands, especially on the top floor. It is small but it is wouldn't be the same if they opened it up more. It's very original. Love all of the pictures on the wall ! Katrina is a fiddle player that plays with most of the bands there. She's badass. Give the band $100 bucks to play the devil went down to Georgia & you won't regret it. She's the "best dam fiddle player there's ever been".

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Their food has never been good. I was served a steak sandwich that was almost raw once, and a chicken sandwich that tasted like bad meat. The only reason I gave them any stars is for the good atmosphere

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This spot deserves a solid five stars because it's a lot of fun, and an entertaining spot for a drink. 
=== === ===
This hopping spot is on the Broadway strip and doesn't look like its very big from the outside. However, there are a couple of floors and music and drinks on each. Much of the bar is standing room only, even though there are quite a few seats, if you're lucky enough to snag them. We ordered a drink each and pushed past people to the second floor where we were lucky enough to find a seat. 

Live bands play in each area which is pretty cool to experience. As it were, we sat down where they were holding Open Mic auditions. Basically, singers get up and sing with the band and if the owner thinks you're good, you might just get hired. That was pretty awesome to watch! So yeah, if you're in the area, stop in and enjoy some live entertainment and a few pricy drinks.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
Green Hills needed a coffee shop.  It needed it bad.  Like an addict needs their fix, Green Hills needed a place for people to load up on Caffeine and chill out.  Finally, it seems, that day has come.  The Well took over what looks to have been an old Burger King.  In the hipster rating system, this gives it an automatic 10 points on a scale of whatever number is cool that day.

There is a lot to love about the Well.  From its truly reclaimed nature, to its altruistic mission statement and on to its smiling staff.  What is really great about the Well though is its location.  Located (finally something is) on the OTHER side of Hillsborough (or as the Green Hills locals call it, "the rough side") it has a sort of Zen that is lacking in the greater Green Hills area.  

Whats most important about a coffee shop?  The coffee of course.  It is good here, really good in fact.  The pour overs are good, but their house dark coffee is also astonishingly good.  Perfect temperature and well crafted.  The food here is an after thought, there isn't much.  Were they to add a set of artisan breakfast sandwiches they might win some kind of hipster award.  Think, guys in too tight jeans weeping, and girls with ironic makeup rocking back and forth slowly.  

I think the thing I like most about this place is their committment to be a not for profit coffee shop.  They donate (or so their sign says) all of their profits to charities.  It takes a pretty special kind of person to wake up this early and make coffee for people not to make any profit at all.  For this reason, and many more, I give The Well my stamp of approval.  It might not be worth a damn, but honest people, doing good work makes me a little warm and fuzzy inside.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I enjoyed a very juicy burger that was excellent.  The service was really nice and prompt.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
The Seafood Gumbo Was One Of If Not The Worst Soups That I Have Ever Eaten. Three Days Of Excruciating Heart Burn and Possible Food Poisoning.  The Braised Short Ribs Entree Were
Good. ( Reason 2 and Not 1 Star) Service Was Friendly and Good. Overall ( Except the Gumbo) Good Not Great.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Went to The Sutler for drinks and a show. The Sutler was clean and the waitress we worked with was very friendly. The drink specials are the way to go. During happy hour most drinks are 50% off. Very happy with them music, Alyssa Brown was playing when I was there. 

I ordered one of the dessert mugs. I was pleased with the dessert, but not super impressed will probably not order again. My friends enjoyed the cucumber drinks and the whiskey drinks as well. 

The Bathrooms are downstairs and the elevator is not easily accessible. This was especially hard if you had bad knees!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Had an awesome breakfast here. Sat immediately at the counter and loved it. Great service and even better hospitality! Hands down the best sweet potato pancakes ever.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This is a great bar! I had to stop in since it's a Nashville icon, and it didn't disappoint. We sat on the mid level, the music was great, service was great and the food was delicious! We didn't have high hopes for the food, so we were really happy when it was way better than the bar food we expected. Definitely a must see.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Who plans a vacation around a TV show? My wife. We don't even like country music. 

All I heard about was this Blue Bird Cafe and how hard it is to get into. We followed the directions on the website on logging in at a certain time. No luck, they went fast. I'm talking seconds.

My wife now just wanted to see the outside of this place. We roll up early the doors are locked and nobody to be found. Place doesn't open for another 2 hours.

Then we find out they let the first 20 or so people waiting at the door in. We're the only ones there. We rode it out and I'm glad we did. 

FYI the wait list line started to build an hour before the doors open. By the time the door opened there were more people in the wait list line than could possibly fit into the club. Get there early. Real early if you want in. 

4 musicians in the round. Food was better than expected and the drinks were reasonable, 

I'm a fan and I would come back to the Blue Bird. I think I might like "some" country music now.

name: Tin Roof
text: Every time I visit your establishment your bouncers suck. For the fight, I go back to the restaurant and they tell me I can't go in. I just want to leave and can't get out. They want me to fight a huge crowd of people to leave when I want to leave early. I paid for this shit. This is why I never come here. There is always a problem with your bouncers

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We had a fantastic evening at the sutler good music, food and drink.  We ordered the sweet potato hummus (4/5 stars) the raw veggies (5/5 stars) the grilled veggies (4/5 stars) and the popcorn - which was the best popcorn I've ever had.  It was apparently popped in duck fat, rolled in bacon bits (and grease)' mixed with deep fried jalapeños, and then drizzled with honey.  The popcorn was so good...  I had a bourbon barrel aged ale that was really nice.   Compared to prices in my home state the meal was totally reasonable, especially given the quality of the venue, the service, and the music.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
On one hand, its the Bluebird Cafe.  You have to go.  But on the other hand, waiting outside for 3 hrs in the blistering heat is no joke.  We were first in line (though others came shortly after us) so we got the best seats in the house, but I was pretty annoyed that the first show is not even the headliner and you don't get to stay for the second one.  But then to get into the second one you have to arrive somewhere near the end of the 1st show line, but somehow time it right so that you're first in line for the second show.  I dont even know how its done.  

I don't know that I'd do it again, or even recommend anyone else to do it.  But it was a very Nashville experience.  Food was decent at best, drinks were meh, and band was good but not my fav I saw in Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Cool history. Awful business. Ive known several people to work and play here over the years and they have all said how horribly they treat people. Sky high prices. No room to move. This is a tourist trap plain and simple. If you want to see Nashville for what it really is, don't go here. If you are here to spend too much on drinks, not be able to move, support bad businesses, and get bad service then go here.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Have been to bottomless blue grass brunch twice and had a great experience 

Go early! It does get crowded - I found the golden time to be 10:30-11:30 - I have heard there can be an hour to two hour wait. 

Ordered the andouille hash last visit and it was very good!! 

Pros:
$17 bottomless mimosa
Live music 
Great food/great prices
Cool decor 
Parking in front (but if you plan on drinking, call an Uber!) 

Cons:
Can be understaffed at times and staff can seem overwhelmed 
Can have long wait times 
If you don't want to wait, there are limited other brunch options in the neighborhood 
Do not take reservations

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Kassidy was the most awesome bartender we've ever had! She was a sweetheart and was the reason that we stayed.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: My favorite place on Broadway. Don't get me wrong. This place is a dump  (in the best way possible!)... it wasn't obnoxiously crowded.. drinks were well-priced.. live music... good beer selection on tap.. they have an AWESOME signature Green Tea shot... skeeball, popashot basketball, buck hunter (which actually all work)... clean bathroom... short lines for drinks... and amazingly greasy and wonderfully horrible for you food. Burgers were awesome, I had a killer spam sandwich, and the tater tots were crispy to  a t. We bar-hopped around Broadway, but ended up back here both nights. Get the Green Tea shots!!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I have never heard the music or eaten the food upstairs. My review is limited to the downstairs lounge area, or the "Cellar."

We love coming here because of the speakeasy vibe and the friendly bartenders. The cocktails are also delicious, and they change up the cocktail menu from time to time so be on the lookout for new drinks. 

My only complaint is that the bartenders don't appear to have been trained on some signature classic drinks. I ordered a Penicillin, a pretty common cocktail, and the bartender had no idea what I was talking about. So that kind of sucked. But the drink he ended up making for me was absolutely amazing, so that made up for it.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I'll just say it - this place is weird.  I like the classic feel but not the modern pricing.  The food simply doesn't live up to it.  I had the pork chop, it was ok, not anything special.  We had multiple servers, multiple people stop by and ask us if everything was ok (before food arrived), even gentleman wearing dishwashing aprons came by to interrupt our conversation.  I get it, this place is nee.  But I don't know, just an awkward dining experience overall that will prevent me from returning.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
This place is so awesome.  I came to visit Nashville from Los Angeles for the first time and everyone who had been recommended this place.

I was informed that I needed to buy tickets way in advance because they sell out fast.  Long story short, I wasn't able to purchase tickets (they do sell out within minutes) so we opted for the stand by seats.  The night of the show, my boyfriend and I barely made it in.  Our uber driver (who missed the exit twice), basically made us late but the second we pulled up, we jumped out of the car and the host was waiting outside to accommodate the stand by goers.  We were the last people in.  And by some strike of luck, we ended up getting some of the best seats in the house.  We didn't have to sit on any pews.  We weren't pushed into any back corner (although that's not a bad spot since the venue is small and intimate - any seat there is good).  We ended up sharing a table with a group that was just a few feet away from the performers.  It was awesome!  Sometimes it all just works out.  No tickets and being late equated to only having to pay a cover charge ($20/ea) and sharing one of the best tables in the venue!  So, if tickets are sold out, don't fret, you still have a great chance of making it in!

Once we were in the place, we were relieved.  The performers (true talented artists who write their own music) circled up and each took a turn to sing and play their hearts out.  Now, I am not a big country music fan, but I can appreciate good music and pure artistry and I witnessed it here.  Some of the music made me cry cuz it was just so heartfelt.  

If you want a relaxed and quieter atmosphere where you just wanna listen to good music and kick back, come here.  It's great!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I had heard about the Bluebird Cafe ever since I moved to Nashville. On a Thursday nite I stopped in to listen to the music. I had not even gotten to the door when I was stopped by an immature doorman who asked what did I want? He had been talking with several people who left as I walked up. I replied I had stopped to listen to some music. In a rather rude manner told me they were at capacity. Perhaps they were but the manner he communicated was not very respectful. I don't plan on going again.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Broadway is a tourist trap and a must do. You can listen to live music anytime between 11am and 3am at most venues. Kids are allowed in any place before 6pm so long as smoking isn't permitted (Tootsie's is one of these family friendly places.)

We went at 2 in the afternoon with our almost three year old and the first floor was full, so we took the first table on the second floor and had a view of the band. Food section is minimal, drink selection is wide. 

We ordered chips and dips (undoubtedly canned salsa and queso), chicken fingers and fries (delicious, though previously frozen), and the bbq pork sandwich which melted in my mouth and was smokey goodness. 

So why the four stars for what seems mediocre? Because it's exactly what we were looking for! Music, food and family permitted. 

Also, during our visit I had to go to the restroom which smelled fresh and clean with underlying bleach tones. I was surprised and pleased!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Even though it is a bit pointless to review the bluebird i will give my opinion anyway. The bluebird is what it is. A highly touted, famous, live music venue. While this makes me proud being a Nashville, green hills native, i do believe it is over hyped and over rated. At the bluebird fun is out. You will sit in these wooden chairs, no talking, you must buy at least two overpriced drinks and i would eat before you go. The thing is Nashville is loaded with live music venues, most of them showcasing artist who probably wrote the songs that made the bluebird artist famous. If you are visiting Nashville for sure visit the bluebird if you can, but dont believe for a second that this is the best and only place to hear live music ,and most are free.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Thank you ABC for bringing this gem to the main screen! Yes, I am a fan of the show Nashville and yes I knew this had to be on my lists of stops. 
Unfortunately I was not able to secure tickets to a show but I was able to get on a Nashville TV Show inspired tour which took us to The Bluebird prior to it's opening one night. It was amazing walking in, I felt like I was on the show. They did an amazing job in replication. 
Hearing the history from the owners was such a treat, the place has started the careers of so many, the concept is amazing! 
I hope to come back into town and get to see a show but even walking in and seeing it was a great experience!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Absolute best part of the trip! Luckily I planned ahead and was able to get tickets ahead of time. Picked table 23...which I highly recommend bc it is out of the way and sits up a little higher so you can a good view of performers. The songwriters (Gary Harrison, Carson Chamberlain, Michael White and Rick Huckaby) were excellent and a very talented group of songwriters. I would pay to see them again for sure. The bartender was very friendly and quick to make our drinks. The food was delivered quickly and was delicious. I definitely will visit again in the near future.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: A must if you go to Nashville.  We enjoyed a night "in the round," where four singer-songwriters​​ took turns playing their songs for us.   A very nice server brought us drinks and nachos while we listened.  Service was amazing.  The experience​​ was even better.  Get tickets a week ahead online.

name: SongBird Tours
text:
We sat in the "spit-zone" on the front row for the tour with Bill Diluigi and Trey Bruce. :)

The bus is comfortable, the ride smooth and the tour is well thought-out with a nice review of historic sites, studios and places of interest in and around music row. 

We really loved the writing and singing of Bill Diluigi and the personal and family inspirations for many of his songs - Bravo!

After your tour go back to the Songbird website to read the "Meet the Songwriters" bios and accomplishments of these talented guys - (they are humble and understated on the tour.)

Nice review of the music industry, challenges and opportunities for songwriters and some great history of music city.

Everyone in my group from teenagers to grandparents had a great time on the Songbird bus.

name: Tin Roof
text:
Cute hangout close to the gulch area of Nashville. I went during the day for a quick drink so it wasn't insanely busy. It just happened to be right across the street from my hotel. I did see it get packed at night however. The drinks are pretty cheap and so is the food if you're looking for a snack. We happened to be there during happy hour and they had $4 well drinks and $3 drafts which is awesome! They also had a $5 chicken quesadilla. 

It's in a good location next to a line of other similar bars and hangout spots. This location is less busy and more low key than the location on Broadway I would say.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Not your mothers Woolworth cafe.  Expensive with mediocre taste.  I had Mac and Cheese.  A side order sized portion was $13.  Lots of cheese but no flavor.  My wife's turkey was a very salty turkey roll.  The waitress tried to tell us it was Southern flavor.  Doubt it seriously.  There is a reason why other places have waits and this place has empty tables.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Listen, I heard this was the hardest place to get into, on Nashville! We were lucky enough to get in without a reservation. Cute place. Small, but man, it's The Bluebird Cafe! Bucket list checked!!! But, we were very very disappointed in the fact that after an hour, our food never came out. I only ordered a salad and my friend ordered a tender basket. 1 hour and still no food. The excuse was they ran out of Caesar dressing. I don't think that actually happened, not after an hour with out any food. The 4 other people at our table got their food within 15-20 after they ordered. I'm definitely not disappointed in the music because, hey, it's The Bluebird Cafe!!! But very disappointed that they couldn't get our food out. Or at least get my friends food out. We waited 2 hours outside to get in (5:45 time started) we got in at 8:00. We were definitely starving when we left at 10pm....

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
We were thirsty and trying to kill time before a show at the Ryman. 

Go to Tootsie's they said, hey Legend's looks ligit. Turns out my husband and I aren't really "bar" people. We walked in and right back out of both of those places. Too crowded, too loud, no southern charm.

Well Paradise Park is lacking in charm but it was definitely more peaceful than the other places because we actually got to sit at a good size table and have a drink. 

We decided to come back to grab a bite to eat after the Ryman. They now had the bar fenced off from the concession area which helped reduce the sound a little.

I ordered a corn dog and a New York dog. The hubs ordered the 5 alarm burger with cheese fries. 

Corn dog is hand dipped and very good, crispy crust that's not too thick. That's all I should of ordered because I was stuffed after eating it.

I tried a couple of bites of the New York dog. The bun was fresh but did not hold up to the steam and sour kraut. I didn't care too much for the weenie as it lacked any flavor. Good thing I wasn't all that hungry because I wasn't disappointed that I couldn't finish it.

Hubs really enjoyed his burger. The patty had a good crispy edge. He thought the cheese fries were really good too.

So, probably one of the least fancy places on Broadway but this is where we felt like we fit in the best.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
One of those "famous" dive bar places to check off the list. Aka tourist trap.

Expensive beers. Check
General Filth. Check
Long lines at the bar. Check
Cover bands. Check

Walk in. Have an overpriced beer and say you have been there. Then find another less crowded bar in the tourist zone.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Awesome service, food and music! Went for a Saturday late brunch around 2pm. My favorite was the chicken and waffles. Hostess was honest about wait time and very friendly. We were able to start drinking the bottomless mimosas at the bar while waited to sit, which was neat. Also, they have this cool waiting list program that texts you a link and you can see what # you are on the list. Pretty neat!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Great atmosphere and cool venue for music, however the drink prices are high and the good is overly spicy without any warning

name: Tin Roof
text:
We love Tin Roof on Demonbreun! This is our go
to spot when we're looking for some quality live music and fun environment. We always make sure to bring friends here when they come into town.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Had an awesome time -- on a Monday night. Lots of people, fairly priced drinks and just an awesome vibe to the people there. Loved it!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Went with some friends to celebrate his birthday, had a great time and the atmosphere was very authentic Nashville. Multiple levels of bars and live music on each floor. Didn't wait longer than a minute for a drink...great time!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Arriving the grounds seemed great but then the smell of stale smoke awaited us inside. We were upgraded to a pool view only to find a comforter that looked like a cat had been clawing, a dirty shower head and moldy or dirty door. After talking with management, Tessa, she agreed to refund our money in able for us to stay at a nearby and nicer hotel. She was the best part of the stay! Do yourself a favor and stay at the Marriott next door for a modern and clean hotel. This one is in serious need of renovation.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Best on East Side if it were not for the smoking I would give it a 5, I use to smoke and always went outside. They have a great patio.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Came here for a couple drinks and appetizers with my friends. For $10 a drink, we weren't very satisfied. Our drinks were all very weak and tasted like they had no if any alcohol in them. I ordered the Margherita flatbread to eat, and it wasn't the best. The cheese on it was way too thick and the crust was super hard, kind of felt like chewing on cardboard. The rooftop is also a lot lower than a lot of the other rooftops in the area. I would recommend going to one of the local restaurants instead of here.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: This was our first time in Nashville, we stayed at the Sheraton Music City. The room was clean and very comfortable. The staff was very friendly and helpful, especially Nolan. What a great guy with a wealth of knowledge about the area. This was a trip for our 20th wedding anniversary and wouldn't you know we found a nice anniversary card in our room signed by the entire staff. I recommend staying here if your travel plans take you to Nashville.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Relaxing, clean, and quiet.... but only 15 minutes to Downtown by shuttle or cab. Gorgeous outdoor pool setting, safe and friendly feel, would definitely recommend to travelers for business or fun!

name: The Valentine
text: We were walking down broadway and Cullen Greer drew us inside the Valentine. We will definitely be back and hopefully to hear Cullen Greer play again.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Hit there for Lunch. Had a band playing  which was cool. Hefty brisket sandwich.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Visiting from the north and not a huge country fan, but this is hands down my favorite bar that we visited. Large stage with larger dance floor. People of all ages. The band playing at the time was amazing and played music of multiple genres. Relaxed atmosphere and decent drinks. A must go to bar in Nashville for music lovers.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Honky Tonk/Bar.
A good dive bar with good live music as it should be in Music City.
Nothing much to complain about...

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: This stop was more out of convenience. It was on our walk back to our car and we had stopped at a couple of places that had too long of a wait so we decided to try this place out. It was maybe a 10 minute wait? Not bad compared to the 45 minute wait at the other restaurants. It's overpriced food but it's because of the place and location. It is expected. We decided to just share the sampler. It was actually pretty filling for 2 people. It was well worth the $20 we spent. If you want somethin to share and on the cheaper side this is the way to go. Our waitress was sweet and everyone we encountered was very nice.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The bar itself was pretty cool. It is one of the larger venues on Broadway & that is great if you get tired of fighting twenty somethings for space to stand on the floor. The mixed drinks were poured very "heavy" and I was always able to get a bartender's attention at the bar pretty quickly.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Food was great very clean bathrooms clean portions perfect had the famous skillet was very good wife Had steak was perfect

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: It's 4th of July, things are crazy, and Tisha and Greg are STILL taking great care of us at the bar while pumping out drinks like a well-oiled machine for the rest of the restaurant. I always appreciate personable bartenders, but they have kept us well entertained despite a high demand. Tisha is the kind of gal I'd love to employ, as she took initiative where her coworkers left her drowning, and also managed to realize we had an incorrect check, and took care of us to make sure we were paying an accurate tab. I'd sit at their bar top anytime!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Excellent band playing! People dancing! Great drinks! FIREBALL!

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Some of the driest pork, I have had in years.  Needed a steak knife just to eat the brisket but of course there's no knives. The brisket was closer to jerky. Five and half dollars for warm beer is a bit much too.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This place is so good to have the ideal Nashville experience. There are endless bars and venues to stop in on Broadway, but this one stuck out to us in particular because of how welcoming it was from the outside. The host outside was so friendly. The stairs inside this place to get to the top are brutal but the rooftop bar is so worth the hike. I love that there are stages on multiple levels of this place so you can decide where you want to enjoy your time here. It's a decent sized space and was very crowded but honestly what else should you expect from a great bar in Nashville on Music Row? The drinks were strong and the place was loud but I think that's everything you want in Nashville.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
I have lived in Nashville for 14 years now and have heard about the 5 Spot and how awesome it is for years. Living on the other side of the river I just never got myself over there until recently when a friend suggested I go on a Saturday night when they had a Hip-Hop dance party with different DJs. 

First of all, my boyfriend and I had to wait in a long line out in the cold to learn that we had to pay a $10 cover at the door, so we had to hit up the ATM inside since we aren't avid cash carriers. 

Second of all, the place was so crowded and full of smoke. I know it's a bar and all but it is also a music venue and I guess I am not used to trying to enjoy music of any kind while inhaling second hand smoke. It was awful. 

Anyhow, we didn't have that great of an experience. I may go again on a different night with a different crowd and see if my feelings change about this place and then I will update my review.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
This place was a blast! The band was great and we danced our butt's off. It get crowded just like any of the bars off Broadway get. It was a mixed crowd but everyone there was enjoying themselves.  

There was no cover and drink prices were typical.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
I love people that rate this place 3 stars cause of the music and then they go on to explain how they know the band gets tipped to play these songs "the back street boys" lol. Well, if you know that, then tip the band and ask for a song or two you like. Cheapos.

Great bartender, great sound (upstairs), deck was great, drinks were strong and one of the better places we went to.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Awful. Badly in need of a refresh. Experience started with a front desk clerk who barely made eye contact, and was exceptionally indifferent and rude. The experience continued with a handicapped-accessible room that is so poorly designed that the walk in shower floods the bathroom floor....every time it's used. 
The icing on the cake was the visit from a good sized cockroach this morning. 
All this and more for $300 Per night. When I calmly explained these issues on checkout this morning- no apology. Amazing. 
Starwood/Marriott corporate: You need to take a good long hard look at this one. Disgraceful.

name: The End.
text:
This place is a total hole-in-the-wall, which is exactly what you need sometimes.  People saying the bartender/owner is rude must be putting out bad vibes because he was perfectly fine.  Is he complimentary or jolly? Um no, this is a dive, but he gets you your beer and tells you your total.  What more do you people want??
Only beer here, although a pretty good selection, so don't expect to order cocktails or shots.  
It's a small venue that's perfect for checking out smaller acts. A "sold out" crowd packs nicely in there without feeling like you're suffocating. The sound is good and the bathrooms are not horrendous, although they were unseasonable warm last weekend but whatever. 
A-OK in my book.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Thoroughly enjoyed the spicy Diablo shrimp (wrapped in bacon and a smoked jalapeño), super-tender brisket, snappy sausage, and beer on a random Monday night. Ahhh, beer...the excellent selection on draft immediately betrayed the "dive bar" edifice despite the Jaegermeister shot machine lying fallow on this night in the corner. Blackberry cobbler was well-conceived, but something about my portion tasted distinctly of BBQ sauce, and not on purpose. Personally, I think they're trying a little too hard to compete with the kitsch collection on the walls at TGIF's around the corner, but foodwise there would be absolutely no reason to go to TGIF with this place literally steps away. In my opinion, the appetizers are 20% overpriced and the entrees are 25% underpriced, and should include a side...but maybe the Judge knows best. I'm not local so I'm not sure where the pit expertise is coming from, or headed for, as this relatively small joint in an out-of-the-way location seems like too small a venue for meat this intense and labor-intensive. Perhaps it's a small chain under many names. If it isn't, it should be. Good stuff, I look forward to coming back the next time I stay at the Loewe's, and I will take Chelsie's recommendations once again.

name: The End.
text: This is the little sibling of Exit/In located in a much smaller building across the street. Again, no parking directly here but depending on the night street parking is usually plentiful. This place is a true dive but that's not a bad thing if you're just here for a loud rock show. The bar is beer only and somewhat pricey but not too bad. The owner/operator as mentioned in other reviews is silent to gruff depending on the night but again, not bad for a dive bar I suppose. There isn't a LOT of room in here so if it's a sell out crowd I imagine it is packed but the shows I've seen have been a bit light on attendance (even when it's a great touring band) with friendly fan crowds.

name: The Valentine
text: After 3 days that we had checked it out too many bars on broadway So last night we chosen this bar bcoz the band that playing sound awesome.First we want to stay there enjoy the music,drink or whatever that why i opened my card...,but later we were ignored by server! we tried to looking for her to pay my bill after The band left..,finally she came and asked for another drink but we're leaving..,So i paid $13 buck plus tip Then i checked my account in the morning they charged me overprice.The bar is wasn't busy at all!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: First floor very clean and neat.   Excellent bar tender and they offer Italian natural spring water! Great option

name: FooBar
text: It was pretty good, the bar staff was very friendly and even remembered who I was when I went to close my tab! The band "Kid Freud" did a good job as well. Kudos! Anyways, no complaints towards this establishment except they could have done a slightly better job in the "WOW" factor department.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Hasn't let me down yet. If you want to have a funky goos time. Then this place will tickle your fancy. The 5 spot offers a diverse crowd, a variety of DJs from around the country mixed with live entertainment, and people that actual dance. I could go on forever baby (*home alone rip) Smaller venue but that adds to the essence of what this place brings to Nashville's jolly ole "Honky-tonk" scene. Blah! Cool place, great vibes, and normally its a food truck somewhere close afterwards. Check it out. Peace

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We stopped here while on vacation in Nashville and it was a great choice! The service was very friendly and very good! Both our waitress Shavera and the manager Molly were awesome! My husband and I split the ribs and it was a huge portion! They were falling off the bone and they were amazing! The prices are a little higher but they are this way at all of the Hard Rock Cafes. You expect that when you go there.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Awesome music venue! Went on $2 Tuesdays, $2 cover and $2 Yazoo on tap. Best time ever in Nashville. Great music, fun times!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I had a lemonade made from scratch right on the spot by the bartender! That alone was so awesome for my experience at The Stage to be one for the ages! The live music was really good; it's refreshing to hear a fiddle from up close and also for a band to play "traditional" country music! There is a big crowd but it is a great time!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: I was wary of this hotel because I had pricelined the room and didn't know what treatment I might receive.  I had NO reason to worry--they treated me like royalty--gave me an upgrade, threw in internet.  The room was beautiful and the king sized bed was amazingly comfortable.  I enjoyed both pools and used the fitness room (which is excellent--seriously) frequently.  Suggestion:  if you can, upgrade to the Club membership--breakfast and substantial appetizers (along with sodas and snacks at any time throughout the day) are included.  Loved this RESORT. :)

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: This is a review for the 4th of July VIP and Parking area that is held as an event. The charge for VIP roof view was $65 per person and the parking area was $10 per person. I paid $50 for 4 adults and 2 children. Needless to say, both tickets were a hit and the area was packed. HOWEVER, NO one was able to see the fireworks. Many people like myself waited hours to enjoy the fireworks and were not made aware of the blocked view. When I asked for my money back, I was told that I signed a "contract" saying I understood the view would be blocked. I never signed anything of that sort and simply walked in and bought my tickets and that was the end of it. There was NO mention of the very limited view. I have pics of the "view" or lack thereof, and plan to post them on tripadvisor. I encourage you to go there and see it. Hundreds were ripped off on July 4th. I am very upset all my out of town guests were so excited to experience the 4th of July in Nashville, but were left with a bad taste in their mouth for the treatment at the Hard Rock Cafe. I wasn't the only irrate person that night. A couple dozen VIPs walked out very upset!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Got a renovated room on 4th floor just by asking for one. If you concerned about all the reviews of smelly carpet rooms it's true until they finish renovation going on now. Ask for renovated room.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Spent a few hours here enjoying live music and bourbon. Staff is friendly and the prices are good. Nice atmosphere and a good view of the stage from most tables.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Loved this bar so much, but came here on my birthday. Bartender accidentally poured me a different drink. I politely told her I do not drink pop. She poured my drink out and cut me off. .. won't come back.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
This is the type of place to grab a drink, not eat dinner. 

I came here with a large group, so I understand that there will be time delays with wait staff. But our waitress took over 30 min to take our order. Not sure if they were short staffed but then it also took a long time for drinks to come out and food to get there. And when the appetizer came out, we got the spinach and artichoke dip which I sent back because it was cold. Even the second time around it was still cold. I just gave up. 

On another note, I went on a Wednesday which are live karaoke nights. That part is a blast, and since it's Nashville majority of the performers can actually sing pretty well.

name: Boulevard Records
text: This is a cool little record shop near Belmont. They have a decent selection of new and used albums. I'm looking forward to the concerts they hold at the shop (during fall and spring).

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Don't Do It!

I have been to Hard Rock Cafe's around the US in most major cities. This one is the worse.  

There was a large party with at least 10 kids in it. Instead of seating them all together, the parents were seated in an elevated section near the door and their pre-teen daughters were seated next to the kitchen..and our table.

Not only were they running around and overall barely supervised but the manager just walked back and forth as though it was no big deal.  I love kids, but on a Sunday afternoon on Labor Day weekend, we just wanted a simple meal with a normal level of activity for a family resturant.

Lastly, our waiter put an asterisk on the bottom of the recipe...next too the 18% gratuity recommendation.

That gave us a good belly laugh!

As for the food..nothing special.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: When you see this sign run! Best I can tell, they committed a federal offense tonight! It would appear they created a charge on my credit card. I've ask that federal government step in, shut this scam down, make arrests, and enforce federal offense laws. To me they have committed an act of OVER BILLING! I have contacted Chase as well as Visa networking in efferant to avoid such auctions. They don't seem to understand it's a federal offense. Subsequently, hasn't a statute of limitations. Each instance is three to five years in prison and $10,000 in fines. Stay clear unless you plan to be hustled!!! They won't even use Vaseline!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The rooftop was my favorite spot. Great live music, talented band, cheaper drinks, and the ability to escape from the crowd as needed makes this a great place to start your night. The lower levels were a bit crazier, but still awesome as a whole.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: My wife, son, and I have used the long term parking/shuttle service a few times now. It usually is running behind a bit which isn't normally a big deal. But we waited 30 minutes for a shuttle and when it arrived they took southwest employees over us. The southwest people had just walked up while we waited that whole time. "Sorry we have to take them first." Cool, I enjoy waiting. This will be the last time I use this service.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
Had a super fun Sunday night here the music was great, the band mixed it up with rock & country. The lead singer that night (6/16) was super sexy had a girl crush on her. 
Delicious moonshine infusions, tried a cherry margarita & grape on the rocks with a side of club soda which I suggest so you can really taste the yummy flavors. The white lighting is deadly. If you have an early flight the next day be careful it makes for a painful ride home as I found out today. 
Don't run out when the tip jar comes around it's noticeably rude & $ 2 won't kill ya. Your`e going to have a great time here

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We got a burger here with jalapeños and my fiancé got bbq sandwich with Mac and cheese and beans. Everything was tasty any my fries were delicious. Service was quick and my waitress was pretty funny kept us entertained throughout the evening. I would certainly come back again.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The hotel is very nice and well kept. The bed is extremely comfortable and the room was large and extremely spacious. Had the king suite with a view of the pool! The staff were all very nice and every time we came in contact with staff they always asked if we needed anything and if all was good. Would book here again if ever in the area!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I had a very strange experience here. Due to flight delays, I didn't arrive at the hotel until about 2:30 am. When I walked up to the desk, I stood there for a long while before someone heard me in the back room and came to the front. I said hello and that I was checking in. The person working looked up at me with super angry eyes and didn't say a word. She shuffled through some papers then went back to the back for about 30 seconds. Obviously I was confused. When she came back she asked if I had ID & a credit card. So I handed each to her and she didn't say anything but walked into the back with both. She came back about one minute later and handed me a room key. Still saying nothing. I asked how to get to my room and she said I turn right and go down the hallway. I said thank you and went to my room, excited to relax, after a long day of flying and traveling alone. I open the door to find luggage and a men's suit on the bed and the bathroom door was closed. I was so confused and realized I was potentially alone in a room with a man at almost 3am. I immediately went to the front desk to tell her about my experience. This time I was helped by another woman who kind of tried to laugh it off and gave a crappy reason for the mistake. I was so tired from traveling that I just wanted to get to a room without anyone else in it. However, I had a hard time sleeping after realizing this is an establishment that gives out multiple room keys to different guests for the same room. I woke up early the next day to check out and asked to speak with a manager about what had happened. The morning front desk staff seemed mortified for me, but said no managers were available because they were in a meeting. They referred me to someone else, but not a manager. To ease my terrifying situation of being a lone woman traveler in the middle of the night who goes to find a mans things in her supposed hotel room, he asked me if I wanted a coffee... or maybe a bottle of water, because he sees I already have the water they carry, so why wouldn't I want more. I tell him no, thank you, and by this point I'm clearly shaking from being so freaked out by this weird situation and his lack of understanding how scary it was for me. He told me there was nothing they could do but apologize. I obviously was not impressed and was going to leave. He offered to sign me up for the FREE rewards program to make me feel better. I travel frequently and I have been meaning to do so, so I agree to sign up but let him know it doesn't really make anything better. So they added some points into the account. Not enough for a room though, which is fine because after that, I would have a hard time trusting another Sheraton. I left right after, and don't see myself returning here anytime soon. 

Also, the room smelled musky, they put me on the first floor with a back door leading right into the pool area, and the shower flooded. No thanks.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: We stayed on the club level which is a great bargain that includes breakfast and even appetizers. You also get a room that faces the courtyard with a usable balcony. Start your morning with a cup of hot beverage over looking the beautiful landscape and pool. The room was very clean and pleasantly quiet. You know how hotels these days fill the bed with pillows, well here they do too but they are a variety of firmness. In the bathroom were not just the usual shampoo, conditioner and soap but also a scrubby puff, shaving lotion and other specialty items. It's little touches like that, that sets this hotel apart from the crowd.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
I was overly optimistic when going into the restaurant after hearing that this one had "a ton" of Beatles memorabilia. Super disappointed when I went upstairs to see mostly just posters. They did have some Ringo & John Lennon items, which were pretty neat. But being a fan of them, I was happy to see they had any Beatles stuff at all. 

Onto the food! 
I had ordered a BBQ bacon cheeseburger and a sweet tea to drink. I wasn't expecting it to be great, seeing as the restaurant chain seems to be declining of popularity and quality more each passing year. Luckily, because of the low expectations I had, I wasn't too disappointed. The burger was cooked well, however, it was FULL OF HOT GREASE. So much grease that when I brought into it, it squirted all over my hand. I was wearing my 7 week old daughter in my baby carrier at the time. If I wasn't leaning forward when I took a bite, it would have burned her precious head. The burger ended being so greasy and messy that I had to take the bun and toppings off and eat the meat with a fork by itself. It was a let down. The fries and the sauce on the side were the best part. My 2 year old LOVED the sauce and stole all my fries to dip them in it. 

My 7 year old ordered the cheese pizza and fresh fruit. It came on a guitar platter, which was probably the highlight of his meal. The pizza was so thin, it could probably be a wicked good frisbee if you tried!

Our server at first was really upbeat and excited because they were doing some sort of competition between them. If we bought a Hard Rock Cafe glass, it helped her reach a goal. But when none of us did at first, she seemed annoyed. My mother in law ended up buying one, though. Do hopefully she wasn't bitter about the rest of us not buying one. I'd rather find one in a value village or goodwill for $.50.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: A nice, smaller bar on the strip. A little less crowded (at least on a Tuesday night), and that's how my old bones like it. The bartender was nice and helpful when selecting a drink (they don't have a drink menu, no biggie). The music was good, but again I never mind turning it down a bit, but hey, it's Nashville I get it, so they certainly don't lose points for that. Overall, nice place that I would certainly recommend if you are looking for some whiskey and music, and little less of an early 20s party scene.

name: The Valentine
text: We are Nashville natives and are always looking  for something that is not centered around country music. The DJ  here rocks! He reminds me of clubs we visited in Las Vegas.  Whoever the DJ Is on Saturday nights ....keep him!!

name: Legends Corner
text:
Nashville...lots of guitars in various incarnations on the walls.

Plays Adult Contemporary versions of songs while still having a C&W vibe.

Not too crowded.  Friendly service.

Corner of the busiest street in Nashville.

Besides my friend Cat loved it !

name: Robert's Western World
text: The mixing for the live band is incredible. It sounds like you're listening to a record. There's a nice selection of beer and a full bar. I didn't get the food, but it looks good.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: It took over an hour for our food...which was mediocre and cold at best. Definitely don't come here to eat.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Stopped in here based on a recommendation and we weren't disappointed. Drinks were nice and cheap and service was nice. They ran out of Yeungling, which was kinda disappointing, but they have a good selection of other beers. 

The live music was really fun and upbeat and VERY loud. The crowd was positive and enjoying it as well. There was nearly an hour gap between when one band went off and the other band went on and I wish they had put some music on the speakers while they were swapping to add to the ambiance.

The place itself it pretty cool decor. Really interesting posters and such all over. We were on the lower level and the only table we were able to grab was under the A/C. It was cold under there, but the A/c kept dripping all over the table. It was musical drinks to make sure it didn't drip into the drink. 

Probably wouldn't stop in here again, but glad I can say I've been here.

name: Music City Center
text:
Recently went into Nashville and stumbled across here for car parking.
Great rates non event time and easy underground structure with great payment options.
We walked through the centre and it is massive and seemed clean and welcoming.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Ryman Auditorium was another stop on our tour and I really enjoyed the introductory video on this music venue which was apparently done by Disney and super informative.  I never heard of the Ryman before stepping foot in Nashville but it has a great history and is apparently still a very coveted venue due to its intimacy factor.  Don't skip it!

name: Robert's Western World
text: I mean, seriously, a can of cold Busch Light and a fried bologna sandwich for $5!!!!  Awesome deal, and the sandwich was great!!! Friendly staff

name: Legends Corner
text: Always a good time at legends...always a great band on stage and though it may be packed 99% of the time, it's worth it..

name: Robert's Western World
text: No service at the bar. Eventually moved to a table and got service, but came with an "I don't wanna be here attitude" from the server.  Band only covered Chuck Berry songs. So we were outa there....

name: Robert's Western World
text: Classic joint where there are as many false starts by the band at the door as there are patrons. Solid grub if you're feeling peckish, and $2.50 for some domestic cans if you're feeling parched.

name: Legends Corner
text: Loved the band they had the night I stopped in here with friends, we danced so much!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Not very crowded.  Nothing special to speak of, therefore, stop in, drink and hear the band.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Good food & drinks, great service, even better band! Went with a group and were seated immediately. We had a great time. If I lived in Nashville, I would most definitely come back!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Good food and really fun to go there. Beer was very tasty and live music was awesome. Get the catfish sliders they were the best!

name: Robert's Western World
text: I typically hate country music, but this place is legit. Great snacks, a genuine and amazing bar vibe, and a great time overall!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great ambience, had dinner reservations stopped in hot happy hour before dinner. Ordered the crab and shrimp dip, and a Sambuca 75. Happy hour is 11am-7pm but happy hour with small snacks is 4pm-7pm. My dip was $5 or $6 and my drink the same either $5/$6. I sat at the high top bar where I could view the jenerators, who were awesome! The seat for me I felt I needed to be taller because the bar stools sat low. Closed out my happy hour tab and headed right to dinner. For dinner I had a Caesar salad and the ink squid pasta. The salad was a little salty to me but tasty and the pasta was lightly flavored but satisfying. For dessert I ordered the berry cobbler. The pastry part was sweet. The berries were warm and comforting with ice cream on top. Sweet but not too sweet.  I love The restaurant the vibe is great. Around 7:30 they dim the lights inside. They have a second floor for additional guests or large parties. They also have outdoor seating it's also a close walk the Nashville wings mural. If you're curious.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Amazing food, great atmosphere.  Our waiter, Tyler, was very helpful, knowledgeable and friendly. Love this place!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
My favorite music venue of ALL TIME!  Every show is an amazing experience and it is truly a magical place.  Artists aspire to play the Ryman and I have not attended a single show where the artist has not commented on how special it is to have the privilege.  

There really isn't a bad seat in the house and the sound is amazing.  Hatch Show Prints are a Ryman tradition and they add a special touch to each show.  If you want one, get there early!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Doesn't get much better in Music City than the Ryman...it's a beautiful building with a terrific history. Sit in the balcony or front of the floor for best views.

name: Music City Center
text:
The new Music City Center is incredible! The space is unique, beautiful, has great views, and was built with extreme thought to being environmentally friendly. 

I attended the Greater Nashville Association of Realtors conference here shortly after it opened, and it blew our conference experiences at the older Nashville Convention Center out of the park. The rooms are all super nice and parking in the garage is very convenient. Our lunch, which in years past had been borderline awful, was prepared by the MCC's chef and was really impressive, especially for a big catered event type meal. Dessert was very tasty too, which was chocolate mousse and one other option served in martini glasses. 

For your coffee needs, Bongo Java is right next door inside the Omni Hotel. If you're not a local, the center is right downtown so you can take advantage of everything Downtown Nashville has to offer.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: We've been twice so far and we love the atmosphere and good food/drinks. We plan on making this a go to spot!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Went here with some girlfriends while we were in town for the weekend.  Not only was our waiter extremely helpful, our meals were amazing!  Patton James was playing and we all found the band very entertaining.  This place made me wish I lived in Nashville.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Maybe I just came here on an off night, but the Tin Roof is on a long street of bars and live music venues- and this place wasn't enough for me to stay for a drink. On a weekend night, the place was 3/4 empty, and full of a older (50-60 y/o), drunken crowd. The bright lights are cool, the name is catchy, and people seem to like it, but I wouldn't spend more than 30 minutes here.

name: Robert's Western World
text: If you're looking for a great atmosphere, live music and a fantastic house band with some of the best country musicians(great guitar and bass player), friendly venue and the best fried bologna sandwich ever, then this is the place. Be forwarned, its small and crowded, but fun and they dont get in a hurry; if you want beer or liqour or snack for a fair $ step on up, cuz they aint gonna ask ya.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I was in town for a conference and after checking Yelp, decided to stop in. My only regret is that I had already eaten by the time we decided to visit this place, so no fried bologna sandwich for me. It was, however, a charming little joint with a great band and positive atmosphere. It felt like a real Nashville experience. Of course, I'm from CA, so I may be way off there, but still... I enjoyed my experience..

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
How very cool it was to be here. I love, love, love live and country music so stopping here to walk around the venue and sit on their wooden benches where many folks got to see so many legendary singers perform. Think of the young kids of today going crazy for One Direction or whatever and go back in time and think that the same energy and excitement and happiness was felt for Elvis Presley (my meant-to-be husband), Johnny Cash and Patsy Cline when they graced that stage. Some people usually just see a band once or twice.This is where so many once in a lifetime memories were made. 

It cost $14 to get in. You're asked to sit down to watch a 10-minute video about the history of the Ryman with Trisha Yearwood and can wander the venue. There are tickets for a guided tour as well and you can go back stage.  Sing and record a song for $20. My cousin's girlfriend sang Patsy Cline song and it sounded amazing. I was going to do it. I sound pretty amazing in my car.  Also, you're able to take a photo on stage. There were people dressed in their best country outfits having their photo taken with their guitars and boots. Head on upstairs and see how massive this place is. Pretty amazing that it originally was a place of worship. The cases all around the venue hold clothing and photos of past performers. The rear wall of the beautiful arched windows definitely reminds you of church windows. Around halls outside the main area, the walls paint you a timeline of events as mentioned in the video. And there are signed Ryman posters that were signed by the artists - Kid Rock, Robin Thicke, and dare I say it, The Jonas Brothers. These posters reminded me of SF's Fillmore. It was a great experience. Next time, I'll record a CD just to say I sang "Live at the Ryman!" But I would love to see a live show here sometime.

name: Music City Center
text: I was here for a work event and it was a wonderful space for it. There were 25,000+ of us and most of the time it never seemed that way since there is so much space inside the MCC. The building was clean; inside and out. All the staff I encountered were friendly. The bright natural light from all the big windows was wonderful; and I loved seeing the decorations, especially the rocking chairs, nice southern touch!

name: Legends Corner
text: Great band tonight, Smoke and Guns. Danced hard!!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I was amazed to see such a historical place in person. Learning about how the Grand Ole Opry came about and the numerous musicians it helped to showcase was great. I loved seeing Johnny Cash's black suit and June Carter's pink dress on display was the highlight for me. I loved being able to walk around on my own and see the space for on my own. The price is pretty decent too for what you get, I'd recommend for a very informative and fun tour.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We were on the honky tonk tour of Broadway in Nashville, couldn't bear to miss this spot. Exactly as the other reviews have highlighted, likely very crowded as the evening marches along (we stopped in rather early). Definitely a destination on the strip!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Started out my night at Robert 3 out of the 5 nights I was in town. Amazing musicians, very friendly service, and an unbelievable cheeseburger. I was told their fried pickles are life changing but the fryer was down all week so I wasn't able to try them. Next time for sure. 

I hit up at least 12 bars this trip and Roberts easily  stood out as my #1.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: The atmosphere at this place is awesome. Great concept for a restaurant with amazing booth seats. Service staff not the most responsive, but otherwise a great place to eat and hear live music.

name: Legends Corner
text: The good, we saw a great band on Memorial day.  Great female singer and band.  The bad - no drink service.  This was not too annoying since we weren't craving a drink but you had to fend for yourself at the bar if you wanted something to drink.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Our server was Amazing! I think his name was Jesse. He was very friendly and helped us through the menu. The food was amazing. I had the goat cheese stuffed artichokes, which he recommended. He also brought out a birthday cake for my friends 21st! I have nothing bad to say about this place. Atmosphere was great with the live music they had playing. Thanks for a memorable experience in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text: If what you are looking for is a straight up honky tonk on Broadway, this is your place. Entertainment is twangy goodness. Fried bologna sandwich special was an exceptional deal and good when trying to absorb a bunch of liquor.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: You just gotta see this place. Its just a small little place but there is so much musical history here. If you go to Nashville this is a must. They have some Hatch prints on display and different memorabilia on display. It was cool bc we just saw Loretta Lynn that morning getting her star on the walk of fame, then we came here and saw a couple of her dresses.

name: Robert's Western World
text: For me this was a breath of fresh air. We had been on the road for a few weeks and just wanted some good music. Jesse did the job! I could have stayed there forever just listening to Jessie Lee Jones Brazilbilly band crank out the oldies of Bob Wills and Marty Robbins (Roly Poly!). Loved it. Went around 3:00 pm so can't say what the night crowd is like.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Just go. It's amazing. Best bands, went 3 times the week I was in town. Great service too.

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text: Want to play a legendary venue in Nashville? This is one of them. Their Tuesday night Writers night host Donnie Winters is one of the best in town. It has the stage sound system and everybody gets to 2 songs. The acoustics are great. Drinks are cheap, staff is friendly and you never know who will walk in there. Many people who became big started at Douglas Corner. To warm up or have a smoke there deck in the back. I played there 15 times.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Don't let the fact that this establishment looks like a trendy upscale bar and lounge keep you from coming here for dinner. Their food is actually amazing. It only took me at least five years of coming to Sambuca to figure that out! 

My friends and I used to come here to hang out for drinks after dinner usually somewhere else in the Gulch. Sambuca has a great ambiance and amazing drinks. I loved their pomegranate martinis! One night we were hungry and got a few tapas/small plates and thought, man this is good food!

Fast forward a few years later and we're now all married. My husband and I decided to make a dinner reservation for one of our birthdays. We were blown away at how good the food was! My husband had a really amazing steak here. The live music was a nice added romantic feature. 

I would definitely say this place is worth checking out whether you are looking for a place to hang with friends or for a nice dinner.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We visited while in town in a bachelorette. Everything was fantastic!  Our sever Matt really brought our dining experience to the next level. We couldn't have asked for more!  Food was delicious. Great entertainment. And awesome service. Next time I'm in Nashville, we'll definitely visit again!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
This place is a GEM

Great professional service

Excellent menu

Very welcoming ambiance 

Even the customers here were nice/friendly

name: Music City Center
text:
I've been to a few extremely large convention centers now. Nashville wins for the prettiest I've been at if it does feel a little small. This said there're some really big problems with the staff.

Got there on Sunday morning for a garden show, just wandering from the world's smallest and best hidden Dunkin Doughnuts (very good, nothing to complain about,) and as I'm strolling aimlessly as I'm lost I wander up to an ask-me desk with two employees trash talking Asians, loudly to the one person at the kiosk, or perhaps at each other who were just hanging around there. I get my directions from the one person who's working (not the two who are just leaning there,) head off, more trash talking at volume that can be heard quite a distance.

I'm not Asian nor part of an Asian defense league as a note. Just loud unsolicited random racism was uncalled for.
