3rd floor, sit down for a few minutes as I'm hauling a baby and otherwise tired. There's an employee sitting in the sitting area looking disgusted. I don't know what his problem was, but he was taking a couch and glaring. Eh, not at me or mine but dang. He glared for as long as I felt like sitting and when I left he was still sitting there sprawled out.

Walked past some rocking chairs, there's a large coffee spill.

Two hours later I'm done with the event, walk back to the seats, oh hey coffee spill. I mean, it could be a new one...

All this said, nothing bad happened, there were people there on it, I don't know what's going on and perhaps the casual racism was directed at a group of asians who were there, perhaps the guy glaring at the world had just had his family murdered by asians, I don't know. The only not on top of it was that coffee, unless that was two spills.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My girlfriends and I ate here for a girls-night-out. We split 5 or so plates among the 7 of us, and had one person pay and we split the bill later. The food was all delicious and it was really fun to sample a little bit of everything on the table. It was fun to have live music on stage behind us.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We stumbled upon this place on our last night in Nashville. . . Wow!  The Mad Hatter band playing was absolutely amazing.  Very entertaining.  Staff was very friendly. Drinks were reasonably priced.  Highly recommended stopping by if you're in downtown Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Even on a Tuesday afternoon at 4 there was live music.  It was absolutely a hoot!  There is a definite dive bar atmosphere, bottled beer only.  We had the yucca fries which were very thick cut and softer than french fries, but quite good.  A great venue.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Loved the red walls, and the overall atmosphere of this place. It was a little disappointing to have such a great environment but not the best service. The server in the bar area was less then attentive, I would have loved to have tried the green brûlée but never had the opportunity to order it.

name: Robert's Western World
text: LOVED IT!!! Came here on a recommendation and had a great time. Nice late night bites and live music, will return!

name: Legends Corner
text: We stopped in for the live music.  No tao beer, only bottles was disappointing.  The service was even more disappointing.  The location (kitty corner from Bridgestone Arena), the live music and the atmosphere bring it up to three stars.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great honky tonk bar! Fun live music. Delicious fried bologna sandwich!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Amazing, as usual!

We weren't expecting the Music City Bowl (yes, I live under one very un-sporty rock) so we were surprised to find Broadway even crazier than usual upon arrival.  No worries--we hit up Robert's around lunch time, snuck in the back door, found a few stools at the grill, and had the best beer and breakfast in recent memory!  Even my food snob companion was blown away by the recession special--it is practically all he talks about when asked about the trip!!!

Great music and unbeatable, tasty bargains!  The lady working the bar was super nice and they have the cutest can cozies of all time.  You totally need this in your life.

Thanks for the great time!

name: Robert's Western World
text: A true Nashville honkey tonk. The fried bologna sandwich is a my favorite and wash it down with a PBR

name: Robert's Western World
text: This was the first place I fell in love with when moving to nashville.  There is a bass player named Joe that plays there often.  It is a must see.  This is a great place to start and end you night when going Honky Tonkin.  Oh...and they are a bar!

name: Robert's Western World
text: This is one of our favorite Nashville bars.  They always have a great band playing.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Arguably the best honky tonk downtown, and the preferred choice of many locals when we dare venture to Broadway.  I've heard they serve food, but I wouldn't know anything about that, as I don't make a habit of eating whilst honkeytonking, which seems counterproductive to me.

name: Robert's Western World
text: The place is small but if there's a line it's worth it. Great beer prices and the fried bologna sandwich is awesome. Depression special is the way to go for lunch or if you need something to soak up the beer. Traditional country music playing at all times and the servers are very nice.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Fantastic music!!  Good food and a great atmosphere.  I will be back the next time I am in Nashville.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: The architecture was stunning.  You can tell people really took the time and effort to make this place special. Live music all day. Fantastic food. And the popsicles were amazing. Most food was tapas style so u can try many things.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Honestly this was not the best experience. I planned a dinner for a 14 girl bachelorette party. I had worked with the manager to setup a pre fixe dinner that was 38 dollars each. I also had arranged for the brides aunt to have a round of drinks sent over. The service was good but the food was absolutely terrible. Myself and a few other girls had  to have their meals sent back as they were not edible. The meal i got as a replacement was not good either. I sent the manager two emails to explain my frustration and have yet to hear back. I expressed my frustration to our waiter and he did take off a 4 % gratuity charge but that really did nothing for us, as it wasnt his fault and we all still tipped 20 percent. I will be back there soon and based off  the way they handled this, i will not be returning.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
My girlfriend and I did the tour. We were able to walk right up and purchase tickets for $22 each. She had been dying to go and I obliged and actually had a really good time. 

It starts with a 15-minute interactive video that was my favorite part. It is truly a unique experience. 

After that we toured the facility on our own and there was a lot of cool memorabilia to see and take pictures of. The whole feel in there is like you're in a church, with all the seating being like church pews. You could tell there was a lot of history in the building. 

There isn't really that much to see and you shouldn't need more than an hour to do the entire tour. At $22 I think they are priced too high for how small it is, it's worth about $15. However, it was really a lot of fun!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This was a stop on our Nashville City Tour.  I was not familiar with it until we showed up on the bus and went in to see it.  It is best known for being the home of the Grand Ole Opry from 1943 to 1974.  And if you are a fan of County Music and Bluegrass, and who isn't, you are sort of making a pilgrimage when you visit.  As we walked around we saw a lot of pictures representing a lot of history of the Nashville sound.  We were told it is still used occasionally today to host the Grand Ole Opry at certain times of the year.

When it originally was completed, it opened as the Union Gospel Tabernacle, and Christian revival meetings were held there.  Although it was originally intended as a house of worship, through a sequence of unforeseen circumstances it eventually came to be used for speaking engagements, concerts, boxing matches, etc. in order to be able to pay for the upkeep on the building.

After moving in and having a long and successful run at the Ryman, the Opry moved to its new and modern location at Opryland and the Ryman was almost demolished.  But because it was such a key part of the history of Nashville, the community and a number of investors raised the funds to have it restored and it is still in active use today.  I thoroughly enjoyed being able to go inside and learn about the history and importance of this building to Nashville.  Check it out if you are in the area.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
We did the regular tour at the Ryman (not the backstage tour) and I really enjoyed it. They explain the entire history of the Ryman (I didn't know any of it) in an entertaining way. The video at the beginning of the tour was my favorite. I loved the parallels between the origins of the Ryman (as a church) to present day (as some people hold music in a similar regard), and as a place where anyone can gather and enjoy the spirit of music. The facility itself is not much to look at, but the history is pretty mind-blowing when you see who has been there and what the stage has held... Helen Keller, Charlie Chaplin, Harry Houdini, Jackie Robinson, Johnny Cash, countless rock stars and country singers, the birth of bluegrass, the list goes on and on and on. It was really amazing to think about. 

The perimeter of the Ryman includes some exhibits with old costumes, video, and artifacts that were pretty cool. Overall the video at the beginning was my favorite, along with the hallway full of old Hatch Show Print tour posters (amazing!) and the area with the display of all who have graced the stage at the Ryman. Super cool for any history or music lover.

name: Legends Corner
text:
Legends Corner is a fun bar located on Broadway, however it can get a little bit crowded at times. I stopped by twice while visiting Nashville and both times there were live bands playing on the small stage located in the front of the bar. There is an open area which was pretty crowded with people listening and drinking both nights, however there is an area up a few stairs near the back of the bar which was less crowded and even had its own bar. This is where I spent most of my time as it was easier to relax, while still hearing the music.

Another plus is the side door, which makes entry much easier during peak times. The Broadway entrance can get backed up pretty quick on busy nights so the 5th street entrance usually had much lighter lines which made getting in much easier. I recommend a stop on your visit to Nashville, who knows you might see a rising legend before they become famous!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Solid upscale dining/live music combo! The blackened snapper was perfect and the scallops were cooked just right. Bottle of pro secco was reasonably priced and the service was great!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Took husband on Friday for a surprise date night...what a wonderful evening out! From Shevar (the gentleman who greeted us) to the excellent service of our waiter, Aaron and bartender, Frank. Aaron was fantastic walking us through the menu and helping us decide on one of the best meals we've had in awhile...btw, the beet appetizer was incredible. Can't wait to get back there SOON! A+++

name: Music City Center
text: Great space, food, and hospitality. Attended a conference here as a Nashville native and loved every moment. The food, drink, and rooms were superb. Definitely come check out music city center if you get the chance, the environment is unlike any other in the region.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: If you expect to eat here then grab a snack before you go.  We have been here 30 minutes and still haven't had order taken.  Thank goodness the music is good.  Will go to another place to eat.

name: Robert's Western World
text: The Heartbeat and the Soul of Nashville. America's Greatest Bar! This bar makes your favorite bar look like Applebee's!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
This is my go to lunch restaurant. I love the atmosphere inside, and their patio is equally marvelous. The lunch menu has lots of options, you can mix and match a variety if salad, soup, sandwich options. The best part? Apparently no one else in Nashville ever thinks to stop in for lunch! I have never had to wait for a seat, and the restaurant usually only has a few occupied tables. Makes it a fantastic place if you need something conducive for a conversation with clients or colleagues. 
I'm not as big of a fan for dinner - still love the atmosphere, but the menu just isn't my style at night. If I could rate lunch and dinner separately I would give them 5 & 3 stars respectively.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Wow,  Great food!  Is it a bar? a night club? a restaurant?  We were a little concerned with the live music every night, thought it may be too loud and drown out conversation, but we were right up front and the music was to a perfect level so we could carry out a nice conversation.  And the music was great.  Perfect blend between Jazz, blues, and piano bar.  Very fun and a different dining experience than anywhere else in Nashville.  The only reason it's only 4 stars is because you can't do 4.5 stars and the service was a little off.  The server was great, but the food came out a little quick before the wine, so we felt a little rushed, maybe they are turning tables??  I noticed that when we made the reservation on open table, that the restaurant said there was a two hour limit for our table??  a little weird, but still great fun!  Will go back for sure.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
FIRST:  request Jesse as your waiter. 
SECOND:  order & enjoy
THIRD: the music (if they keep  it at an enjoyable volume) is a highlight. 
FOOD.  Miso Sea Bass.  Filet Mignon.  Duck appy  Roasted Beets  veggie lasagna  polenta - enjoyed all

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great dinner. Had the scallops, was expecting creamy risotto and it was firm only downfall. Service was great.

name: Legends Corner
text: This is a great bar with some really good folks working there and great live music.  Drinks are reasonably priced and served up quickly.  It has a good vibe and is worth a stop if you are in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Fantastic! Great service, great music. The burgers were good and the atmosphere was terrific. I liked it so much, I went there twice in the same day.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Overall, I had a good experience. The restaurant itself is very nicely decorated and has a great atmosphere. However, I think the live music kind of cheapens it/makes it difficult to actually have a high class dinner. The music is good, but it's really loud and is only a few feet away from where everyone is sitting.

The food was good- the chicken puff pastry appetizers were wonderful and I highly recommend them. The margarita shrimp entree was a little lacking in the flavor department. The snapper was very well-liked by my boyfriend but it was a little too strong tasting for my liking. The berry cobbler dessert was also delicious.

Overall, I would go back but I would go early, maybe around 5:30 when the band isn't playing. I think the band starts around 7, so if you don't really like listening to it while you eat, you should get there early. It's a very good restaurant but just not great!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: So much fun!! Great music and great bartenders!! Corone served the best drink I had all weekend!! I don't mind paying for quality drinks as long as it's " quality"!! Very professional and FUN!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I did the backstage tour and I do not regret it. You go through the dressing rooms and walk across the stage while a guide gives you some valuable info. Afterwards you are free to walk around and see the exhibits around the walls. It is beautiful perfection. What a piece of history. You do not want to miss this.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Robert's is my favorite Honky Tonk in Nashville! They have some of the most talented country performers on Broadway street.  For under $4, the baloney sandwich is a solid deal.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: M- yes we had a good experience here the food was pricey but it's quality was appropriate. I did have a fall down on the bisque it was flat needed a bit of chicken base a dash of sherry and a sprig of dill. Also a bit of meat may have justified the price. The music was also very good and added to the atmosphere. Filet and lobster were very good as the scallops. Service was stellar

name: Legends Corner
text: Legends never fails to entertain. The bands are always good and know what to play for the late night crowd. Always super fun and upbeat.  Drinks aren't that expensive and it is a staple of the downtown scene right across from Bridgestone and Rippys.  I do not think they have food, or if they do, I am not sure that is where I would eat with so many other options.  But again, always a ball and a must stop spot on Broadway.

name: Robert's Western World
text: By far the most fun we've had.  No need to go anywhere else. The music was great. We will definitely make this a regular stop. Nothing else on the Strip came close.

name: Robert's Western World
text: An awesome find on Broadway! Cheap Busch Lights, live music, and a dive bar atmosphere in the heart of the city. This place was much more laid back and affordable than anywhere else I found on the strip.

name: Legends Corner
text: This place was AWESOME!! It was our first time visiting Nashville and if anything made an impression, it was this joint! We walked up and I saw a kid singing on stage through the window, then saw another kid on the drums. When we asked if there was a cover charge, we were told "there's never a cover charge!" and had a friendly exchange with the bouncer before going inside. The atmosphere inside was exactly what you would want from a bar in downtown Nashville. People were happy and engaged, and the kids on stage with the band that was playing was just the coolest thing to see. Definitely going back next time we visit!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Typical Nashville atmosphere. We were able to bring two kids in for late lunch weigh my parents. Managed to bring the stroller too. I should add this was a Saturday afternoon before any eric church concert at the arena. Food was average for a broadway street bar. If you want good bbq go to Martin's about a half mile away.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Nice small intimate bar if you get there early. I found this to be similar to the other smaller bars; good band, good drinks, lots of memorabilia.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I stood in the presence of greatness watching Luke, an 18 year old guitar prodigy. His guitar licks were magical as he poured his soul into that thing. He played some Stevie Ray Vaughn and gave it his own flavor--I shouldn't have left, but thinking I was missing out on some great music on Broadway, I left. Every other place we went to was filled with people acting a fool dancing dreadfully to empty cover music. When I stopped back at Roberts to get more of Luke, there was a verrrrry long line. I'll be back tomorrow!!!! This is Real Great Music at its nitty gritty best.

name: Legends Corner
text: This place was fun, not too crowded and the bartender was fun. Upper level area was overlooking the bottom floor and was substantially less crowded. The bathrooms were clean despite how busy they were on new years day. The only drawback was the female singer they brought in, her voice was not that great.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place, especially after 1am the music was amazing & the fried Bologna sandwich with cheese was outstanding & under 4 bucks. Soaks up the moonshine just fine. Don't miss out on going here when in Nashville. Tip the musicians ppl. Don't get itchy butt & run out before paying for your entertainment it's rude.

name: Legends Corner
text:
This bar was a lot of fun. Kinsey Rose was playing. The band sounded so great outside we stopped in for a couple beers until her set was over. We've been listening to her on Amazon since then. 

Service was quick, beers reasonable priced. Good selection.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Robert's is awesome! I was in Nashville with my boyfriend for a 2 day stop during our roadtrip, so we weren't really looking to go hard on Broadway (the bachelor/bachelorette parties were too intimidating). We went into Robert's on a Friday afternoon and it was pretty packed. We managed to get seats at the bar and enjoyed our cheap beers and the band playing. This place is absolutely perfect for anyone - there was a bachelor party there being rowdy, but tons of couples too, of all ages, just looking to have a fun afternoon and listen to some tunes.

Have to give a special shout-out to Gail, our waitress/bartender. She was a gem. We are from NYC and you basically have to wave $100 in the air to have a bartender even consider coming over to you. Gail kept checking on us (and remember, it was fairly packed) to make sure we had everything we needed, and made us feel so welcome. She is amazing and so representative of why Robert's is such a nice place to be.

Looking forward to my next Nashville visit, where Robert's will definitely be a long stop!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Robert's is a great place to experience Broadway! I had quite a bit of fun here-really decent old school country music, boots lined up against the wall, and cheap (enough beer) It's exactly what I pictured a Honky Tonk to be like. A little crowded for my taste but hell, great things draw the masses. I don't know anything about authenticity, but if you want to experience Nashville like you pictured it, then please come here!

name: Robert's Western World
text: This was our new "treasure" on this second visit to Nashville.  It's a for-real Honky Tonk.  First the beer is very cold just the way I like it.  The waitresses are super friendly and most attentive.  Even with large crowds, I NEVER had to wait for a drink.  These gals are ON IT.   Discovered from Caroline, Keri,and Hope that this used to be boot store.  Very interesting.  I cannot complete this review without giving a shout-out to their fry cooks.  One guy in particular --can't remember his name--but he'll know I'm writing about him because I specifically told Caroline and him (the fry cook with black rim glasses)  that we were so so impressed with his cleanliness and his work ethic.  I thought he was a part owner the way that he was always busy, stocking, restocking the cook station and wiping and cleaning up around the station.  He cooked and he delivered to tables.  He must have changed gloves about 10 times in the 40-50 min period I watched him.  Now the food was not outstanding but tasty for bar food and I know it was prepared in a sanitary setting and the prices were great!   Now--the bands and musicians they had were OUTSTANDING.  We enjoyed watching them and their talent was unmatched on the stip.  We will visit again!!

name: Legends Corner
text:
Exceptional live music and a nice staff--these are my qualifiers for Nashville bars and this one meets the test. 

The bartender did charge me for my club soda and lime, but he kept them coming as long as I was there. He also didn't give me a hard time about not drinking. 

The live music was great and the band was top notch. I think I am only giving this 4 stars because I enjoyed another bar with live music on the strip more, however this is a great place to stop while in Nashville. Give it a try--I ensure you won't regret it.

name: Music City Center
text:
State of the art facility. directly in the downtown area, LEED certified, visually consistent with the feel and vibe of the city - this convention center takes the cake. 

The directional signage is clear, prominent and readily available. "Ask Me" kiosks with personnel manning them round the clock make it easy to find out where to go and how to get there. 

There are also many opportunities for marketing signage via led screens and tv screens throughout the building. A nice option for local venues, Restuarants and attractions. 

This is a building that makes you want to look up and not down as you get your steps in. There are design features, historical gems, music references and city secrets all through out the center. 

Whether you are hosting an event or attending an event you will not be disappointed with all the Music City Center has to offer.

name: Legends Corner
text: Dive bar with great live music and personable/speedy bartenders...ended up here on NYE bc the line was moving fast. Out of all the honky tonks we went to on Broadway, we had the most fun here.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This was a cool multi-story bar on Broadway. We stopped in to hear the band playing and had a few drinks. We got some queso to hold us over until dinner time...it was okay. The service was pretty bad though, and our waitress was MIA. The band sort of made up for that, and they did have TV's on with the games. There were also Bud Light promo people working this bar so we ended up taking their survey and got free beers. Fun spot, just need to work on the service!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Let me start from the very beginning:
I was trying to make a dinner reservation for a group of ladies the Monday before the Saturday evening that we wanted to dine here the same weekend of the Music City Marathon. The lady that I spoke with on the phone to make the reservations was extremely nice and helpful with ways to get around the city, things to see, shuttle services, etc. I requested to be seated on the patio if possible (wish was granted, & awesome by the way). 
So, we arrive at our dinner reservation right on time, we were escorted to the patio near a lovely fountain. We all ordered some fun drinks. If you get a cocktail, expect to pay $12.50 a pop for it. I got the Sambuca Sling. Worth every penny. 
Apps, we ordered the beinets and crab dip. They were both fabulous. I ordered the champagne chicken entree with havarti tater "tots", that were actually more like potato logs. lol. Everyone ordered something different & everything was fabulous. Service was very friendly & quick. We were given a complimentary dessert for my friend who was celebrating her bachelorette party. 
I mentioned that the cocktails were a little pricey, but my bill ended up only being around $50 before tip, so as a whole it really wasn't a bad price for the quality of food/drinks/service they have.
If you are planning a trip to Nashville, you must come to the Gulch & go to Sambuca for dinner. Sit on the patio if possible!

name: Robert's Western World
text: It was lunchtime and we decided on stopping here. The hospitality was the best on all of Broadway. Karen, our server was always on hand if we needed anything. Nina, cooked my wife and I two delicious cheeseburgers. The wait wasn't too long at all. The music was the most honky tonky of any establishment we stopped at on our journey in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
5 stars is 100% due to the bologna sandwich.  Hands down the best grill man (Benny) in the USA.  

I come downtown just for this late night post drinkin pleasure

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Robert's Western World was excellent.  No other place on Broadway held our attention so long or made us so happy.  The music varied each night, but all acts were top notch and entertaining.  We saw both rockabilly and country acts over three nights.  It was fun to see folks dancing and having fun.

The service is relaxed and friendly.  The food is surprisingly good too. It's a small menu of fried and grilled items, but we ate there more than once.

We tried other places, but nowhere came close to Robert's for us.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I think this is my favorite place on the strip!  We've been to Nashville twice & both times, I saw the same band.  I was glad because I loved them the 1st time!  It is hard to find a seat sometimes, so wait your turn.  High top tables with stools are all you will find here!
I remember from the 1st time, how good the food is too!  You will see some great locals dancing their tails off almost every song!
Don't miss this stop!

name: Legends Corner
text: Bartenders seem a little uptight.....not a fun bar....plenty of fun bars....keep walkin......

name: Robert's Western World
text: This was a great place to hang out at!  The music was fantastic, and the staff was prompt, and very friendly.  No matter how busy it got, someone always walked around to check on people sitting at the high top tables, including myself.  I was really impressed with how friendly the staff was.  Since this was my first time here, I have no idea if the music is always this good, but the band they had tonight was absolutely amazing, and it was a fun place, with great energy.  Everyone around me appeared to be having a good time as well.  I had a burger, and it was your standard bar burger.  It was good.  I didn't get to try many of the other more exciting items, but the next time I am Nashville, I will for sure visit Robert's again.  This is a great spot for experiencing the great music that Nashville has to offer, in a great environment with a super friendly staff!

name: Robert's Western World
text: What I wouldn't do to go back to this Honky Tonk bar at 1am. I went on vacation roughly two weeks ago and wanted to visit a little slice of home. Robert's Western World was the perfect reminder of why I will always be a Tennessee girl at heart. The deep-fried pickles with ranch dipping sauce...delish. Absolutely delish. I'm a sucker for fried pickles and I'm ever-so happy we decided to her them. I got the mushroom swiss burger with a side of sweet potato fries, and if you're looking for a great place to walk into for a night of boozing or just wanna visit some nostalgic Nashville...this is the place. The food was amazing, the people were great, and the live country music was the perfect charm. Even if you aren't a country music fan, this place is a must-go. You won't be sorry!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
We didn't stay long enough in my opinion. 
The first thing we heard when we walked in was the band explaining to a customer that they wouldn't play Zac Brown band - only old country. It was one of only a very few places that gave me the flavor of the old Nashville - or at least what I imagine it as. 
It's nothing fancy, no roof top bar, and not named after a star (Kid Rock, Jason Aldean, Luke Bryan, etc) but that's what will make me go back.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Ryman Auditorium is the best place on the planet to hear acoustic music.
The tour is nothing really to write home about but the sound and the gut feeling you get when you walk in this venue is something that will stay with you forever.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Don't eat here if you want to stay past 2 hours for dinner. They will politely ask you to move to the bar. So disappointed!!! Won't return.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Hands down my favorite place in Downtown Nashville! I've been three times, each time a year apart, and it continues to be my fave. You can listen to fantastic country here and I'm not even a country music fan. The place is always packed with all ages but does tend to skew more toward the older crowd. The little dance floor in front of the elevated stage is usually full of all ages dancing and two stepping. The servers have probably worked there a long time and take care of their customers. It's filled with old memorabilia that looks legit. I like going to other popular places on the strip as well but this place is just different in a really good way that I hope does not ever change.

name: Legends Corner
text: Legends Corner is a solid choice for a beer on Broadway.  They have live, interactive music and cold beer (they must keep it in a freezer or something).

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Had a very nice evening(12/16).  What a way to celebrate with my employees and friends. Thank you so much service was fantastic.  If they would have me, I would definitely have another party there next Christmas.

Thanks Again,

Scott Baker

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: A must experience and concert experience. Love the history the, the vibes, the Holy Grail of Country Music. Concerts are fabulous, go when you're town a must see!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
I absolutely adore Plaza Mariachi, and I hope Nashville as a city sponsors more cultural endeavors like it. My friends and I went on a Saturday during Dia de los Muertos this year. In the food court, there was a joyously raucous band, the well-known and well-loved Stephanie Urbina Jones and the Honky Tonk Mariachis. Stephanie made the whole food court feel like family as patrons swayed dancing to updated classics and children were serenaded by dedicated songs on stage. Afterwards, there was also a brilliant circus performance involving both fire and acrobatics. For an additional fee, patrons could enjoy a 9pm boxing match in the food court as well. This is certainly a hub of culture and the place to be on a weekend night.

In terms of the atmosphere, I felt like I was back in San Antonio. Patrons stroll through pueblo-esque small shops and a marketplace before entering the food court. While modest in size compared to similar Texan experiences, Plaza Mariachi is definitely a new Nashville landmark everyone should make time in their schedule to frequent.

The actual strip mall outside Plaza Mariachi hosts a slew of intriguing restaurants, like Win Bubble Tea and several other specialty dining experiences. I am personally partial to Taj Indian Cuisine where the owner also specializes in Indo-Chinese dishes on the menu. 

With a prime location amongst other dining experiences and a truly fantastic marketing/planning director, Plaza Mariachi is a must-see in Nashville.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Our server Matthew Was incredibly friendly until he realized that we were just ordering wine and appetizers and then his entire demeanor changed. He was short dismissive and borderline rude.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is a really good little hide-away bar on Broadway. The frontage is deceiving since the building goes clear back to the alley. There is really quite a lot of room. And there is a second bar on the second floor so getting seated upstairs is not a problem.
The real surprise here is the food. They have some very interesting choices and the prices are extremely reasonable especially for a tourist location. We heard some really good things about their "fried baloney sandwich". I am not a real big fan of baloney, but we were strongly encouraged to try it by some fans of the establishment.
The music is a little milder than some of the groups on the row, but I would recommend musicians earplugs for those sensitive to loud music. I thought the mix was a touch off, way too little vocals and too much guitar, but to each his own.
Overall, this is a real gem. Delightful service and food with free entertainment. What else can you ask for? And if you come in with a holier-than-thou attitude, lose it before you come in. This is a good old fun county place!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I went here for the first time this past weekend. Had it in my list but hadnt had the chance. Was not disappointed! I had the blackened filet with the bacon sauteed green beans and the prosciutto mac and cheese-it was all amazing. I wanted the sticky bread pudding for dessert but it is a very popular choice so they were out. Ended up ordering the Sopapilla; it was really good. The portions were on point. Definitely going back.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
The Don Kelley Band was fabulous. Joe Fick is SO good on the bass, and Luke McCreary is an incredible guitar player--and just 19, I think they said. 

We didn't eat here, but the food looked good. Decent beer selection.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
We decided to walk around the Gulch one Saturday evening. I had never been and wanted to explore and try new places. We asked around and people suggested either Sambuca or Burger Republic. We ended up walking over to Sambuca.
We got lucky, we didn't realize you had to make a reservation. We sat at the last open table in the bar area. Place was packed and had live music. 
Once we sat down, it took a minute to get greeted; which was fine. Servers were very attentive once we got greeted. We ordered wine and beer and looked over our menus. Server suggested a couple items and helped me pick my dinner. I ended up getting the hickory smoked prime pork chop with prosciutto mac & cheese. Oh my gosh, it was DELICIOUS. My date got the  Filet over the bed of asparagus with an extra side of maple bourbon sweet potatoes. Neither plate disappointed. Everything was so good.I am typically not a fan of sweet potatoes, but I couldn't keep my fork out of them.
Our server kept checking on us and was so glad that we liked what she had suggested. We stayed and listened to some music after dinner.

If you haven't been, I suggest you do. AMAZING food and ambiance.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Whoever knows me knows that I'm the farthest thing from being a night crawler, but Robert's Western World sucked me in for a couple of hours last Thursday night! 

My friend and I made our first visits to Nashville, and Acme really wasn't cutting it for either of us. I wanted good ol' traditional country music, and I'm so glad that we checked out Robert's!! It has a great mix of younger and older customers, and I met quite a few people who were easy to make conversation with. I'm also not a dancer, but Brazilbilly and Nathan Belt got me dancing up front like mad until 1am.

It's not your typical dark honky tonk like many of the other places are on Broadway. The atmosphere is not pretentious at all, and while being someone who gets anxious in large party crowds, I can see myself hanging out there alone. People are nice, especially since it's not just groups of younger people, so don't be afraid to ask others if you can sit down next to them if there are open stools. Do yourself a favor and check out Robert's!!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Go. Doesn't matter who's playing. Just go. The Ryman is an American institution and if you have a chance to see anything or anyone play on that stage, do yourself a favor and just go. It is, in so many ways, a truly religious experience.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Great place for music, maybe not so much if you're hungry. Breakdown of my review. 

Atmosphere and music: 5/5
The music was amazing as this is part of Honky-Tonk "row" with Tootsies Orchid Lounge and others. The band was fantastic and really set the mood with skills and amazing showmanship. 
They got the crowd dancing and bobbing their heads every time they played.

Drinks: 4/5
Good drink specials and the service for drinks was pretty quick. PBR for $2.50 is pretty unbeatable. 

Food: 2/5
Took over 30 minutes for orders of sides to come up. And when they did, the chicken tenders were overlooked and dry, while the yucca fries were not died enough. The yam fries were okay but nothing spectacular.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My expectations may have been too high for this place. Great concept, poor execution. Took my boyfriend for his birthday. Showed up at reservation time but waited 15mins for our table even though the place was half empty. Gluten free options. Food was just fine nothing remarkable. Salads and salmon. They gave a free dessert for the birthday which was nice. Music was good not stellar but the band took a very long break which dampened the atmosphere.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: The 4 out of 5 star review is based on The Broadway scale. I will admit, I only go to Broadway when I have visitors in town. It's hard to rate them on the same scale as other bars because it's obviously a very touristy place. Everyone knows that. So my expectations are real for this area. I surprisingly had never been into Tin Roof before. I usually pop into the well known bars and then my friends pick where they want to wander into. We heard some fun music coming from Tin Roof so we ventured in. I was digging the inside of this place. We were here on a Monday night so it wasn't packed. This is the best way to experience Broadway in my opinion. The weekends are a bit too crazy. I'm not sure if it's always like this but they had colorful Christmas lights hung up on the ceiling. It added some fun colors to a usually darker scene. What I really appreciated most about this place was the fact that they had drink specials. Broadway can be so overpriced because hey, they can. My friends were a little tired of paying $10 for basic rail drinks so when we saw a $5 rail special at Tin Roof, we were excited. We hit it, and we hit it hard. Maybe the deal was actually a little dangerous haha. We just ordered vodka sodas so they were as good as rail drinks can be. Served in a plastic cup but that's what you get on Broadway for obvious reasons. Glass + Broadway does not end well. We were able to get a table right up front and the music was what also kept us here. The band was really fun! They were doing a mash up of different pop hits from the 90s and early 2000s. A blast from the past! I'm not a country music fan (don't kick me out of Nashville!) so I appreciate when bars mix it up. I can't comment on the food because I would never really order food on Broadway, but they have it if you need a bite to eat. Overall, it was a fun experience and I will no longer pass by this place when on Broadway!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Very authentic music in a pretty inauthentic stretch of bars.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Sambuca is one of my favorite place to go after work for happy hour. I'm normally in a small party of 3 or 4, but yesterday I went with a group of 22! I was not expecting them to be able to seat us together, but we were able to slide some couches and chairs together so that worked out well. 

I almost always choose the shrimp & crab dip. It's cheesy warm goodness with chips is exactly what I need to hold me over until dinner later. 

My new favorite drink is the Cock N Bull, which includes vodka, lime, and ginger. The ginger is what makes the drink so delicious so of course I got two! 

I've always had amazing service here and never had to wait long for food or drinks. There is also plenty of street or garage parking in the area which makes coming to this location a no brainer!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Super cool! The band playing there on Tuesday night played some old country classics like Hank Williams and Conway Twitty. I didn't like the food a whole lot but that is the atmosphere, it's not supposed to be 5 star dining! Very affordable food and drinks. They do only bottled beer, no drafts.

name: Legends Corner
text:
Overall Nashville is a really fun town to visit but is getting really really expensive to go. Although it's on the Strip, Legends Corner Bar still seems like it's true to its history. The bar actually a little bigger than it looks it has an upstairs and a downstairs but they had a really great band playing and they took request as well but as we found out the next night when we went back it was the same set over and over again which is okay.

The bartenders were attentive and friendly even though it was getting pretty busy they seemed to enjoy their jobs and had fun. They were pretty quick I'm getting the beers out to you and it seemed they liked to serve the beers in six-pack form which pretty much is going to separate you from 40 bucks so it was still kind of pricey.

They had a lot of memorabilia up on the walls in the bathrooms did not seem nearly as run-down as you would expect them to be in a restaurant that gets his kind of volume. They had quite a staff of bouncers I think I counted six which was a lot for a Friday afternoon. However seeing as how we just got kicked out of tootsies maybe they had the right amount after all lol

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We were very impressed by the decor and set up of the winery.  It was a pleasant evening with friends, amazing food and even better music.  I would recommend the City Winery only to those who want a low key evening though.  I wore jean shorts a tank and a kimono with boots for a bachelorette party.  I felt underdressed and would have felt more comfortable in a summer dress and sandals.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Reminded me of beer fest in Munich, great pretzel! Great beer, especially the helles!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Perhaps the worst food I've ever had in Nashville....maybe even Tennessee.  The steak was 2 small pieces and was not even remotely warm when it arrived.  The chicken was marginally edible.  Out of one of their tap wines.  Will not be back and will spread the word to avoid this place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A Nashville classic - perfect country food just like your grandma makes  Biscuits and pork chops are to die for.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Giant chicken tenders, people!  Seriously, they are the largest chicken tenders I have ever seen in my life AND delicious too.  This would be a great meal to share for sure.  Our server was very friendly but just a little slow (in moving).  They weren't all that busy so I'm not sure what was up?

Great little spot to stop on a road trip!  Cute little shops around the place too.  Obviously I liked the shopping because I easily spent 50 bucks on stuff I really didn't need.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I don't understand why people are so obsessed with this place... it's mostly new comers, but I've met some lifetime Nashvillians that love it. It's just good southern food. It's about on par with what I can cook at home... there's nothing special about it and the biscuits are just lard biscuits. Look up a recipe and make them yourself. Honestly, I think it's about the same as Cracker Barrel only more expensive and you have to wait for 2 hours to get in. Notice I'm not saying it's bad food, because it's not. It's just not worth the price, wait, or hype. 

If you want wonderful, impressive southern food: find a good hole-in-the-wall Meat and Three or go out to Monell's.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This is my first time visiting Nashville and my second day in the city. I am in loveeeeeeeeee with this winery. So much so that I could cry from how kind everyone here has been. The wine is great. The decor is sexy. The people make it all worthwhile! I was helped by Mike, Hayley, Daryl and Sydney. I want to pack them in my bag and take them with me to Atlanta! The mimosas are divine, KEEP them coming. I will be back! I will bring people with me!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great Southern food.  Good biscuits and preserves.  Blue Plate Special was ribs...excellent.  Baked Beans had nice kick, and sweet potatoes were delicious.  Finished meal with a peach cobbler a la mode...perfect.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Always a great meal. The biscuits are dynamite( obviously) and the pancakes are my absolute favorite.! My husband gets the brisket omelette and swears it's the best breakfast place in Nashville. Tip--!get there before 8 to get a table, otherwise the wait can be very long, but totally worth it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
As far as Southern cooking goes, Loveless Cafe isn't even in my top 15, but the experience was enjoyable and it's definitely something you should do at least once when visiting Nashville.

Biscuits:  Decent. Don't know why everyone is so crazy about them. Pretty small, so plan on eating at least two. The housemade peach preserves are awesome. Overall: C+

Fried Chicken (white meat):  Light, crispy, flavorful crust. Meat was tender and juicy. Overall: A-

Hashbrown Casserole:  Sizable portion. Thick and rich. Slightly better than what you'll find at Cracker Barrel. Overall: B

Collard Greens:  Relatively bland. Lacked a traditional saltiness from the ham hock. Pot liquor goes well with the biscuits. Overall: C-

Green Beans:  Same issue as collards. Overall: C-

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
This revue is for the concert venue only. 

I like City Winery as a concept and venue. There isn't a bad seat in the house. However, show tickets are pricy for Nashville and the menu is also inflated. I also need to add that the acoustics are terrible, which is sad for a room that was built for the specific purpose of performances. It's also the most expensive ticket in town for a show (more than the Opry). 

The food:
I have no problem paying a premium for excellent cuisine, but I've been there three times, and the entrees just aren't exceptional, nor are the wines (and they will add TN liquor tax to your bill instead of including it in the menu price, so that glass you ordered went from marginally reasonable to rather pricy). Expect 25% by the glass tax (between TN liquor tax and regular state and local taxes). The next time I go to a show at City Winery, I'll eat first and have a glass of wine when I get there instead of dining in. 

Parking:
Parking is VALET ONLY at night; be prepared. Make sure you understand the time on your ticket; it may be when the concert venue opens for dinner, and you could have an hour or an hour and a half before the actual show. 

Bottom line: as a local, I wouldn't go to City Winery except for a show, the performer would need to be someone exceptional, and I would to go with the expectation that the sound is going to bounce all over the place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: So so so good. We went Monday around 9 and didn't wait at all. Hash brown casserole is amazing. Pancakes are amazing. The biscuits though. Beyond words. So good. Pace your self! They bring those out first and by the time you get your food you're stuffed. Adorable venue great staff.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Great wine, really delicious filet, and a cool atmosphere. We had a great time here for a low key dinner during a bachelorette. Service was excellent.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Definitely the highlight of our trip.  Went on a Monday around 10 and there was no wait.  Best biscuits we've ever eaten.  Friendly staff and even solid gift shops.  Recommend anything involving a biscuit from this place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: OMG!!! I want to live in their kitchen! This is real southern cooking. Not only is the food AMAZING but the staff will treat you like family...the members you like :-) I will most definitely be coming back to Nashville just to visit them again. Don't leave town without visiting these guys. Yes it's a bit out of the way, but the drive is well worth it. It really is a hidden gem.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We loved it! Is it the greatest restaurant in the South, no, but it was a perfect stop for my first trip to Nashville.  I ordered the smoked pork chops and Mac and cheese and it was OFF THE CHAIN.  Sooo good! The preserves with biscuits were generous and super tasty. I am also a sucker for a road diner with a history! Oh, and the artwork was awesome!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
The best thing that we ate was the Ruben roll and that was even over fried!  My husband's beer he describes as creamy, but I don't like beer so I can't comment.  The bad of the meal:  everything else ... which includes the over cooked and under-salted smaller pretzel which the Manager wouldn't take off the bill after a few bites!  My Pork (as they don't offer veal) schnitzel was OK but was tough, dry but don't ask for extra gravy cause that's additional!!  The crispy-fried pork shank was just OK too, but barely ANY gravy with that either!  I tasted the pork shank and thought it was tastier than my schnitzel!  It is enough to feed 2 people I would say.

Other reviews of this place say negative things about the sides -- we agree!  The spaetzle, kraut and potato dumpling were not worth the time nor calories ... and of course, no gravy!  So I'll go there and say that the German place could be considered the gravy Nazis!  Sorry guys...

If we came back, and that's a BIG if, we'd just have the big pretzel, beer, and Ruben roll (requesting that it not be over cooked).

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A friend who's a local told me that if you have one meal anywhere in the greater Nashville area, that the Loveless Café's the place. He was absolutely right! Pork barbecue, fried chicken, catfish, and the sides (especially the creamed corn) are just spectacular and the staff was so accommodating I even took a few biscuits home.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Flaky, soft, freshly hot biscuits? Crunchy crusty, yet moist fried chicken? Perfectly cornmealed and seasoned fried catfish? Tucked away next to a gas station out of the Nashville city? Yes, definitely the best way to start my New Years resolution of 2014!!

This place was poppin' late afternoon of New Year's Day. Screw your New Years resolution when there's food this delicious around!

We loved the biscuits, fried chicken, and fried catfish. Sides were okay. We weren't too pleased with the overly cheesy hash brown casserole, but we loved the cucumber salad, fried green tomatoes, and hush puppies.

An amazing place with that southern charm that makes you feel like you're eating in a local home, just be ready to wait at least 30 min to and hour if you haven't called in before hand. No worries, you can stroll around their cute stores and get some loveless souvenirs!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
3 stars because I like the vibe of German restaurants. Service definitely could be better since we were sitting at the bar. 

Food was good and authentic. 

Of course, great beer too 

20% chance I give it a second try

name: Loveless Cafe
text: It's famous for a region. Plan to drive out of the city a bit, wait awhile for a seat, and eat stunningly good Southern food. Order anything--it will be excellent.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Came on a Thursday morning at 9am no wait to get in super fast service had our food very fast as well and it was insanely delicious! Had the moonshine Bloody Mary comes with cured bacon and a souvenir glass! Southern sampler, biscuit sampler, and biscuits and gravy! Everything was delicious and cooked to perfection!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The venue is beautiful! This is a great listening room. Service was a bit slow. I cannot comment on the food, but the wine was OK. Not the best wine, yet not unpleasant. I would return for another event.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Every time I visit Nashville this is always my first stop. Being from Chicago, I don't get good southern food often. I always get the Southern platter with a choice of three meats and two sides. The complimentary biscuits are amazing and so are the berry preserves it comes with. The catfish is perfect, turnip greens were delicious. I can't find anything to complain about except for it being so far away from where I live.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best meal I had in all of Nashville. The people here are so nice as well. You need to put it on your list of places to visit if you are in or near Nashville!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Upon approach one might think this place is "cute" or "nice"... boy looks can be deceiving. Let's start with the highlights, although they over work their waiters (a grueling 17 hour shift... yes you read that right 17 HOURS) Jason was incredible, a true glowing star in a dark and cruel place. Also they had the worlds best beverage, you know it and you love it... rootbeer. We had to wait for an hour to get seated and the place is sooooo out of the way. Everyone think the biscuits are soooo great but the true winner was the hash brown casserole. Not a very child friendly place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
That cafe is located like 30 minutes from downtown, and even though it is on a highway.
There is always a line. We had to wait 40 minutes on an afternoon on a weekday to get in. Once you got seated, you are served biscuit and jam. Their biscuit is from heaven!
I ordered the country ham with egg ( perfect) and fried chicken liver and gizzards ( so so). Their prices are good and the service is good as well.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: It's good! It is not great. The atmosphere is awesome,  great wine selection. The tartar appetizer is spectacular,  but they were just short on the rest. Don't get me wrong everything we ordered was good, again it's just I've had better.  It's decently priced and service is very good! It's worth trying.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: First time stopping for dinner. Hit the spot. Was craving country cookin without having to go to Cracker Barrel and they did not disappoint. We sat with Owen and he did an amazing job. Great server with great personality. Food was amazing. I had a vegetable plate and he ordered brisket.  I had to get hash brown casserole, it is to die for. There was so much brisket on the plate. Great value.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Omg! These people know how to make biscuits! I have to say the recommendation to mix Sorghum Molasses with butter and dip the biscuits in them was a delicious idea. The service was incredible. And if you haven't been here yet, their Hash-brown Casserole is OUT OF THIS WORLD! The wait can be grueling but I've never felt so rewarded than after eating at this place. Love, love, love Loveless Cafe!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Great food! Good beer! They are still working on kinks with service but overall good!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is extremely popular...after having read about it and seeing it featured on a variety of shows for years, it was crazy to actually experience it.  I didn't think that a place could be so popular that people would actually drive out to basically the middle of nowhere and enjoy great food...wow, this place was great!  

Loveless Café isn't very close to downtown Nashville and really is in its own spot.  This place is so popular that it's actually its own amusement park.  We arrived somewhat early on a Sunday morning and the wait wasn't bad (about 20 mins).  The food itself was incredible...very rich and very Southern.  Well known for their biscuits, they are definitely incredible...rich, decadent and extremely buttery.  The accompanying jams were great too.  I had chicken fried steak and thought it was excellent...definitely a heavy meal that will keep you satisfied for hours!

If you can make it out here, definitely visit this spot...great food!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Great night last night...tons of energy in the building to watch Yacht Rock Revue.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Tasty food if you don't mind heart attacks. Very long wait. Very busy. Cool shops and buildings all around it. Fun experience. I'd go back, but it wouldn't be my top choice.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Loveless cafe is a must if you are in Nashville. Yes it's touristy but the food was well worth it. I got the country fried steak with hashbrown casserole. The steak was giant and amazing! Had to take half home. Biscuits come warm and with three delicious jams. Drinks are pricey though. Not sure if they were with it. 

I hear it gets pretty crowded though and there can be a huge wait. We went on a Friday morning around 9am and got right in. I guess all the wild and crazy partiers from Broadway were still asleep so try a weekday and early if you can.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Ok, this place is worth the out of the way drive. We were a party of 4 and had an 1.5hr wait. We considered going somewhere else but then found the cornhole stations (you check out the bags at the little postal office store, leave your ID with the clerk in exchange). After shopping for jam in the adorable Loveless themed shops, playing a few games of bags and sipping on some cream sodas our buzzer went off and we practically squealed with excitement. 

This down-home diner didn't disappoint. We were immediately served a plate of buttery biscuits and jam (pro tip: skip the jam and butter up that biscuit!). I ordered the waffle and everyone at the table agreed it was the best decision. The waffle seems to be somehow made of the same delicious dough used to create the biscuits, it was delightful. Highly recommend. 

We were heading out on a 6hr road trip post visit and our sweet server loaded up a to-go box with MORE biscuits without even asking. If you don't buy the biscuit mix at Loveless you can buy it at the airport on the way out of Nashville. Get thee to Loveless and bring your appetite!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Waited over an hour but it was SO worth it. Food comes out very quickly! Creamed corn and coleslaw are my favorite sides. 

Skip the coupon mentioned, it's for online orders only.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: On vacation from California and came here for breakfast. Best biscuits I've ever had. Hash brown casserole was my fav. Service was awesome. Highly recommend.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Delicious biscuits with preserves.  Well worth the 30 minutes wait on a Sunday afternoon.  The blue plate special, smoked brisket with two sides was ginormous and so was the barbecued pork.  My daughter enjoyed the moist and well seasoned meatloaf.  Will have to come back for the pies someday.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is fantastic! The People are friendly and brings the customers back to "service with a smile". Country fried steak, eggs, cheese grits, bacon and biscuits. All great! Loved the grits...
Came on a Monday morning around 10am with 6 people. Did not have to wait...
Also loved the Peach Jam.. Bought a few bottles to take back to NJ!
If you're able to go... Definitely go and have some breakfast here!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: AMAZING experience!! Kirsten was an out of control AWESOME server! The food, drinks & pie were crazy good too. Wish we were local so we could pop in whenever. Definitely check it out if you're in the area!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We had a phenomenal time last night at the Greg Brown show at City Winery. This was our first time there and it will not be the last.  The food was amazing and the service top notch. I have to specifically call out Kim for being so helpful with our menu choices and never letting our drinks run dry. Kim was also so sweet to my mom and a huge thank you goes out to her!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Certainly a solid breakfast option and one that stood out among the plethora of breakfast-centered restaurants in town. The whole place has a very home-y, comforting feel. The biscuits are amazing - my only complaint is that they are too small! But no worries, they will bring you another plate if you ask. The food was good with generous portions. Perhaps not the BEST omelet I've ever had, but I would definitely return next time I'm in town. Be sure to check out their gift shops for cute (if somewhat overpriced) souvenirs to take home.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Paid for a "premium table," which unfortunately came with less than premium service. Ordered a bottle of wine upon arrival which took several reminders and more than 20 minutes to arrive. Food was average and expensive. All this would be a wash if the music listening experience was top notch, but it wasn't. Wedding DJ music bled in from the adjacent private event space, so for the first half hour of the show, the live act on stage was competing with Cool and the Gang.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Must visit for tourists! We visited on a whim right after we arrived in Nashville but were too tired to search for a place to get dinner. We must have hit a good hour because we got seated right away. We were taken care of by Owen, who was EXCELLENT. We split the sampler plate with pulled pork, fried catfish and fried chicken. Everything was delicious. We ended up trying their breakfast later in the trip and it was also good. The biscuits really are as great as they're made out to be. We checked out the gift shop and brought some preserves home with us. We will definitely go back next time we're in the area.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
This place is huge!! We sat at the bar for some quick biers!! The liter is humorously huge but hubby got one. The bartender was great and gave mine in smaller glasses( same liter)as I'm not a fast drinker and also don't have the muscles for the liter!Lol! 
We had sausages, fries  and the pretzels as we watched soccer( US vs Martinique)...
Great atmosphere, friendly service and awesome servings.
We shall be back obviously!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: MY pastor came from this neck of the south so I went and visited his best buddy there who took me on some country bumpkin road out to this place! I loved it,talk about good ole hometown southern fried cholesterol! You got it here.The waffles were huge,fried chicken steak great.It's old school,dixie do it right! Wear a checkered tablecloth and go grits and pancakes too! It's been a long time but i have a book of matches from this place right here on my desk....sort of brings a little "Earl Pitts" tear to my eye.....if you get my drift! Every food lover should eat here once! It's a tradition! I salute you Dixie!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
"I just want his dignity, that's all. I want him hopeless, loveless, finished off! I just wish him ill, very very ill." -- Addicted to Love (1997)

I love a good biscuit - small, large, fluffy, flakey, sweet or buttery. Bring them on. Loveless has been on my bucket list for ages and until recently, I've never been able to get my group to drive the distance/time it takes to get there - because truly, it isn't really in Nashville. It is on the outskirts and takes time to get there. Thankfully, my fellow biscuit lover and bestie, Tanya C was on this trip with me and she knew this was the place to go!

Be prepared to wait, but know that the wait is well worth it. Not to worry, there is plenty to do to pass the time. This is a converted motor hotel and they have converted the buildings into different shops - so there is so much to see (and enough places to spend money). Art, cookbooks, food, clothing, tchotchkes, and then some. If you aren't in the mood to shop, then there are chairs, picnic tables, more chairs, benches.

We drove in and parked (parking is plentiful) and got a pager. They gave us a wait time of an hour 40 - wow. Okay, let's wander! If you don't want to wait, you can place a to go order (yes, they have an app) and eat at the picnic tables (no seriously, this is brilliant). 

We were seated before the allotted time had elapsed - excellent - and were seated at a table close to the front door. Wow, the place is massive. Much larger than I had originally realized. During our wait, I looked through the menu too many times and had a hard time deciding what to eat. After much internal debate, I opted for lunch. Knowing that they just bring you the biscuits for free (with the jams), and that was the main reason I wanted to eat here, my entree was second fiddle. 

First the biscuits and jam - blackberry, peach and strawberry. That's the order of my love of them. Why did I NOT buy some? WTH, Lindy? I could have eaten my weight in these little tiny biscuit gems. And they didn't weigh anything - light and fluffy and no bigger than a 50-cent piece. YUM. I ordered the friend pork chops - delicious. Crunchy, while juicy on the inside. I had the hardest time deciding on my sides - I opted for mashed potatoes with gravy and creamed spinach. I also ordered a side of country ham. Everything was amazing and somehow I ended up with all 3 gravies (brown, white and red-eye).  I think the creamed spinach was my least favorite thing I ordered and it was not bad.

Unfortunately, there was no stomach space for dessert, but based on the other tables it looked good. Next visit, I'm getting the fried chicken! Did I mention I'll be back?

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Very cool venue.  You can have the full menu in the dining room or in the actual concert venue itself.  They have select wines that are on "tap" which are prepared especially for the winery, as well as a decent selection of bottles as well.

We split a couple small plates, which were tasty (went with the arancini balls our server recommended, as well as the brown butter pumpkin gnocchi).  Our server in the dining area was great, but the server in the concert venue was a bit frazzled and hard to track down.

Be aware that the concert time that's advertised is actually when the doors open,  not when the concert begins, and there may be an opening act.  Our show was advertised as 7pm, but we had to leave at 9 to get to a show at the Opry, and the main act hadn't even come on yet.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Good service. We had about 25 people and they were helping us when we needed anything. They weren't very interactive with us. Like they wouldn't talk with us. But they are very busy so it's understandable. But that could be improved with just a small conversation and some jokes.

Food was great! Biscuits were the BOMB. And they just kept bringing them back. We took 4 dozen back and they were gone in 30 minutes. Cream corn, fried chicken, mashed potatoes, and many other sides to a great country brunch.

This is a great place to go. I'd love to go again if possible.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I will never return here again. I have only been three times, but will never go again because our last experience was so awful. The food is good, but the wait times can be long and service can suffer due to the restaurant's popularity.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Great beer, authentic German food served in a big beer hall. The staff is friendly and attentive. My fav is the leiberkäse sandwich and the Flammekuchen. You can't go wrong with any of the selections. It's also a welcome Oasis within opry Mills Mall.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
My hubster found this place on the food network about famous places to eat. We stopped in from taking pictures at Percy Warner park ( separate review). Super cute cafe located on the same lot as a quaint old school loveless motel and loveless famous ham gift shop. 
It was cozy and super friendly. Down home cooking at its best!! The biscuits were 
A. M. A. Z. I. N. G!!! They serve 3 home made fruit preserves that were yummy as well. 
Hubster ordered the 1/2 fried chicken, fried okra, green beens and turnip greens. I ordered the French toast and bacon. Now I L. O. V. E. bacon. The bacon was slap your friend good so were the green beans and I had a food-gasm from the turnip greens. They were perfectly cooked with ham hock and vinegary goodness that make you want to suck the juice out of the greens then chew!! I could have eaten a whole pot of those. The French toast was perfect, the eggs were done right. My daughter ate a ton of the okra. So if a 1 yo eats it then you know it's good. The biscuits, OMG. ( I'm hungry now). 
Cool thing too was a Antique car club came by and chatted a bit. Saw an old dodge and a couple of model A's and T fords. Amazing food and experience. A must go if you can.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We moved to Nashville a year ago. Loveless is where we take all of our guests visiting us in Nashville for the first time. Last Saturday (8/27) I brought my entire family (10 of us) to Loveless. The food was great as usual, but it was really the personal touch of our server Diane who really made the visit special. 

Diane: You made this daughter proud to live in Nashville. You also made my 88 year old dad feel so welcome and special with your wonderful attention and service. Thank you so very much!!!!!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The quick story-go anywhere else, anywhere.  The house wines are overpriced and watery. The service is beyond horrible, and the food is so overpriced and overlooked you're gonna want to hurt yourself for not following this review.   The long story, we dined here in the summer for the first time for dinner.  Anticipated to view the city while, if not dining, having drinks.  The upstairs, outside was closed for a private event, no one was allowed.  The downstairs where the main Restsurant was wine barrel themed. Noisy as noisy could be.  One server for the ENTIRE large set of tables.   He was pushy and we felt pressured and rushed.  That time in the summer we vowed NOT to go back.  Unfortunately, we ended up there the other night because someone in our group forgot how terrible it was. Hoping it would be better, DISAPPOINTED again!  The server was so busy, we felt like it was a hit and run accident.  He suddenly appeared, asked if we were ready to order.  We were ready to order but weren't quick enough I guess and he fled to do something else.  He didn't return.  The hostess took our order.  The truffle fries ( they were short cut and few) were good, risotto balls over cooked.  Flatbreads were overlooked and the duck flatbread was barely edible.  Cavatelli pasta was undercooked ALOT and lacked any flavor really aside from hot pepper. The bill for the extreme basic meal for 4 was 200 dollars.   And he poured water on my ring and hand!!! How do you miss the glass 2 inches away!!!!! Thankfully it wasn't coffee!!!  Never going back.  Will go to The Butcher in Germantown (fabulous duck and you can buy it and cook it at home additionally if you like) or go to Bobs steakhouse at the Omni.  You may pay more but everything is perfect .

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Food isn't all that and our server was a complete weirdo and is probably in the wrong business.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
We've been going to City Winery since they first opened and enjoy the music venue set up. Service is good, the food is usually good. The only problem is the ladies restroom. Each time there has been some type of problem: toilet overflow, lack of TP, and always problems with paper towels. Went last night and still no TP and the paper towel dispenser was hanging open, no extra towels in the shelf and a big wet roll on the counter- thought I was at the local gas station!
Doesn't a manager or attendant ever check the ladies room for problems or cleanliness?
Come on folks- for what you charge for parking, food, and beverage, you can afford to fix the paper towel dispenser or hire an attendant to hand you towels like House of Blues.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits, oh, the biscuits!  We had the fried chicken, biscuits & gravy, and pork belly biscuit with egg and everything was amazing.  The aroma of the smoked pork belly was fantastic.  I also highly recommend the fried green tomatoes.  The mac & cheese was good, but not stellar.  The place was packed and they were very efficient and personable.  I will be back for sure.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Homemade biscuits and jams, slow cooked & smoked brisket...uuuummmmm....uuummmm...good!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The last time I ate here I was a kid but it still looks just the same.  The place is a tourist trap in a lot of ways but it still has some charm to it.  The biscuits are still great while my steak was less than acceptable as it had far too much gristle in it.  The rest of my food was just good Southern food and the staff was friendly and attentive.  This is much more than just a Cafe as it was also a motel that has since turned all those motel buildings into different shops and art displays along with a big ole barn in the back they use for different events.  This place provides a lot of Disney level ambiance and while you can find some better Southern food at other places this spot is still worthy of a visit just to experience the grounds and the biscuits are usually among some of the best in the South.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Unbelievable food.  Fried chicken, country ham/biscuits, fried green tomatoes and creamed corn were fantastic, BBQ pulled pork was good but just okay.   The service was even better, Meagan was probably the best server I've ever had, and I eat out a lot.  A lot.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We visited on Friday afternoon, around 2.  There was plenty of parking around the back of the property (I can see how it could be challenging at times or for handicapped).  The wait was estimated at 35 min, at that's what it was.  Greeter Michelle was smiling and friendly.  Our server Lucas was very nice and easy to talk to, and his service was excellent.  We ordered 1/2  fried chicken and 3 side order plate.  The food seemed to take a little long, but the biscuits (4 out of 5) kept us busy (don't eat too many), and jams were great!  Everything was very hot and delicious!  We will return.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Great home cooking. Try to eat there often. 
Can get breakfast anytime. 
Wait staff very pleasant. 
Feel like u r on a mini vacation when to go there. 
Great jams and biscuits.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Greeting- yes
Vibe- farmhouse tourist attraction
Price- nice
Service- good
Parking- free lot
Food
 best biscuits
Great jams
Fried green tomato sandwich is tasty
Fried chicken is good
Fried okra was dry
mashed potatoes are cafeteria style
Banana bread pudding is very southern
WIGB? yes

One of my go to places when in Nashville

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I attended a concert at City Winery on July 9,2015. The layout, decor, and overall space is promising for a concert. They of course have an incredible wine selection, upscale bar food, and descent amenities to offer you during your visit. Although the positives for City Winery are plenteous, I would say there are a few areas they kept me from giving them 5 stars.

The first opportunity I found was with the valet. Although I read previous post about the price, which is $5, my concern was simply with the staff. These people are your first experience with the venue and they were very unfriendly and uninviting to my wife and I. Yes, you took my car and brought it back to me at the nights end but try and be as upbeat and excited as the workers inside the facility. Secondly, would have to deal with the food. I will openly admit that these opportunities fall solely on personal preference and not solid data but I believe there were some concerns. First, if you are offering a special, only allowed for the restaurant and not the stage area, don't put it on the projectors and show it to me every four minutes. Secondly, 98% of the food offered was not sharable but was also too large. I understand I'm at a restaurant but at the same time I am not. I have experienced in other locations shareable, medium size dishes worked better. Lastly, I didn't enjoy my food. My wife and I purchased the truffle fries and risotto balls for an appetizer then a hamburger, which was a burnt on the outside and raw in the middle, and a chicken dish which my wife enjoyed. The dining is attempting to be upscale and new age but seemed to miss the mark with each selections. The fries come with a garlic mayo which does nothing except take away from the fry. The risotto ball, which should come with marinara sauce, is accompanied with BBQ sauce and spicy mustard. Both offering nothing to highlight the flavors of their counterparts.  You can see the definite potential with City Winery but these are just a few areas where attention could be shown. 

Lastly, on a side note. If you are going to a concert and truly care about your view and sound quality, I would definitely recommend forgetting the front sections of sits. Although this is usually my section of choice, the venue and atmosphere of food, wine, and conversation with your neighbors really demands you sit in the second section and back. 

Thank you City Winery, Victor Wooten and friends for an amazing night. Honestly, despite the few comments here in this review I look forward to returning and recommending your venue to others.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Might be my favorite restaurant. Absolutely wonderful. Be prepared for a long wait but there is lots to do while you cool your heels. The biscuits are exquisite and the hash brown casserole is legendary. Just goooooo!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Not trying to be negative but I was not impressed with this restaurant.  Thought it was overpriced for what we got.  Waiter tried to push more and more drinks on us and seemed to be on a schedule of turning tables.  Food was good but experience was not as good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Let me start off by saying that our server, Matt, changed my life. Not only was he friendly and easy to deal with, but his meal choice has altered my view on the world. We started off with biscuits.
