I've never been a huge fan of anything that doesn't involve meat. I feel like eating biscuits are a waste of time, but not these biscuits. They were amazing. I crushed about 2 of them before we even ordered. Anyways, I attempted to order fried chicken off the supper platter. My boy Matt, said that they offer a spicy version of this dish. Hearing that Nashville's all about hot chicken, I jumped on that opportunity. After destroyed about 2 more biscuits, our food arrived. I gave it a once over and decided it was too hot to eat, so I started off with a dab of the mac n cheese. My mind was immediately blown. The noodles were soft and the cheesiness of the dish was perfect. Pleasantly surprised, I went after the chicken. It was an explosion of flavor in my mouth. It was euphoric. My immediate reaction was to rip off all my clothes, jump in a deep fryer, roll around in the breading and pour the spices all over me so that the chickens could see how good they taste. I reluctantly gave my wife a piece, so she could enjoy a little bit of heaven. This is by far the best fried chicken I've ever had. Dear Mr. and Mrs. Loveless, I love you.

Edit:
One thing I forgot to mention is that you must take the excess breading and spice from the chicken and mix it in with the mac n cheese to complete the experience. God Bless the USA.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Nice atmosphere, mediocre food. My wine drinking friends sermed to enjoy the wine. Excellent service.  We sent a salad back that was soo horrid I'd be embarrassed to serve my dog. But they took it back with no hesitation and without charge. My "medium rare" lamb was so rare it was barely lukewarm.  Again...they took it back for more fire. When it came back...hardly more cooked... it was only tolerable. An attempt at some "interesting" flavor combinations was mostly unsuccessful.  Someone is trying too hard. 
Sapphire Restaurant in the Factory succeeds in the style in which City Winery currently fails. 
I won't be back for the food.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits were good and so was the food!  Enjoyed the hash browns casserole was the best!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: You need to go here and you need to eat the biscuits!!!! Definitely one of the best meals we had while visiting Nashville. We had to wait a little but well worth it. You will not be disappointed :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place was great! We received a recommendation from a local to definitely check out this cafe and we are so happy that we did so. The people there are so friendly and the cafe is very quaint and has a lot of charm. The food is sooooo good, we can't stress that enough. We aren't from around here and we loved getting to experience some of Nashville's greatest foods. Also, they give you a lot of biscuits and jams to eat with it and it was amazing. If you are coming to Nashville or live there and have never been, definitely check out this place! It is so worth it.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
When you order a draft flight, BB designates 4 beers (Bavarian Bierhaus, Hofbrau Dunkle, Paulaner Hefe & Spaten Munich Hell)  and you get to select 2 others for $15. That was a good deal. I ordered a Reuben and subbed German Potato Salad for the French Fries. (I just could not order same old FFs at a German restaurant-to wrong.) The meat, was lean and very good just not as much of it as I expected. This is NOT piled high, NY style. :-(  There was more sauerkraut than meat on the sandwich so the bread was wet (soggy) when served. Not soggy good, soggy bad. I pulled the soggy bread off.
We went for lunch, around 11:30AM so the place was quiet and still empty like. It's a large place. You eat family style (long tables) like in Germany at Oktoberfest. 
I would eat here again. The beer list is extensive and worth more investigating.:-)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My office is just around the corner from Loveless. I get by about once a month. My favorite is the half order of country ham plate with eggs, hash brown casserole and eggs. ALWAYS a winner--with the unending biscuits! Makes for a great morning!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
For the weekend we stayed in Nashville, this was by far the best food!
Great fried chicken, awesome banana pudding and service that was like eating with close friends.
Go to the gift shops, buy some jam(we did), and then get a few gifts for all your friends.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The biscuits!!! The biscuits I say!!!! Simply amazing, baked to a warm buttery perfection topped with homemade jams...I could eat 1000 of them!

I had the eggs and BBQ breakfast, scrumptious! The BBQ had a little rub on it and the sauce is near drinkable! 

The property is really cool too....get ready for a coma!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I just love this place!!  I was coming here for 10 years before I moved to Nashville and now I live only a hop skip and a jump away!!!  The Pork Chops are Wonderful....the Biscuits are GREAT....and I love love love the Coconut Cream pie!!!  10 stars!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If your staying in Nashville and deciding if you should drive all the way out, the answer is yes. The biscuits alone are worth it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Hands down one of my favorite places to go! Their biscuits and fried chicken are amazing!!!!! It's an iconic tourist spot but even if you have to wait they have cute shops and games and things you can do in the meantime! I'd recommend anyone go there

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food is good, especially the biscuits! Decore and food is basically exactly like a Cracker Barrell. Still go for the experience of eating there.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A wonderful place to eat anything.  Great fried chicken with brown or white gravy. Unbelievable sides.  Great greens. Excellent coleslaw. Fried green tomatoes are definitely worth ordering.  One of the best bloody Mary's ever.  We loved the place   Our waitress. Cindy. Was amazing.  She was extra helpful and she was very nice.  Hats off to this wonderful place. Cute store. Impeccably clean bathrooms.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We were here visiting from CA and excited to try this new place.  My husband and I grew up with German Food and it looked authentic.  The food was AWESOME.  It was so good, we came back a few days later.  Love the beer selection!  Our waitress, Jennifer did a great job and was very helpful. Would definitely come back if we are ever in Music City again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
My guess is that I've had breakfast or early dinner at Loveless Cafe at least 50 times. I became a customer at the age of 16 as a freshman at the Vanderbilt University, and I continued throughout my wild days as a student and as a teacher at the university. 

Just went back and Loveless still serves up a lotta love.

Best biscuits and the best country breakfast I've ever tasted, What I really like about Loveless Cafe, besides the savory eats -- the customers cannot be put into a class, or party, or ethic group. It attracts truckers, artists, musicians, tourists, good country people, foodies, and no-nonsense Nashvilleans, and nobody cares, as the delicious food brings everyone together.

This is where politicians of different parties should break bread. Simple good food cures all.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I've had every entree on the menu & always VERY satisfied. Great folks & WORTH THE WAIT ESPECIALLY HOME MADE DESSERTS. 
 Country ham and biscuits awesome in the even know how to do chicken livers properly

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is way overhyped.  Save your money and go to Biscuit Love.  Food is blan but served in large portions.  Biscuits are mediocre but sauce was good.  Other than that not much else to say.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I hate to say this I think it's overrated. Don't get me wrong was food was good & our server was great but I personally I was expecting more. Still go & experience if you'd like but you won't be blown away. Sorry!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Growing up, my Mother talked about how one day she wanted to go to Loveless Cafe if she ever made it to Nashville.  She passed many years ago and when I moved here in 1991 it was very emotional the first time I made it, I cried thinking how much she would've loved the experience.  I've been many times since then and Loveless Cafe is always a treat!  I love breakfast the best.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Everyone told us we had to go here, which is 20 minutes outside of town.
It was so worth the trip. The Biscuits arrived (Warm) with three types of jam. One was yummier then the next. The portions were big and worth every over stuffed bite. Southern cooking, with LOVE at the Loveless Cafe.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I've been to both the upper venue room and the larger venue room in the lower level and they're both great. I went to two concerts: Greg Howe which was a three piece upstairs, and The Aristocrats downstairs which was also 's the piece band. Both rooms have great sound and the food menu is decent. I had the Margherita pizza which was good. I don't recall how much it cost, but it got the spot. I don't drink wine so cannot comment on that part, but the menu seemed large. Great venue

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Unique restaurant in an old fashioned motel with gift shops in the sleeping rooms. I seriously could have just eaten biscuits and homemade jam and been totally content. Delicious! My hubby ordered a breakfast omelet (they have breakfast all day) and I ordered fried chicken with caramel sweet potatoes (yes, caramel) and coleslaw. The only knock is I felt that the chicken breast was on the small size and for the price thought there should have been two. Next time I'll order the fried chicken salad because it was loaded high with fried chicken and get the sweet potatoes as a side. Fun and casual for families.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Some of the best home style cooking I've had!!! We were a party of 4. Was about a 30 min wait on a Monday! The service was awesome! Lady was sooo sweeet and the food was amazing...the biscuits were beyond soft they were delicious! Get the sweet potatoes...soooo good!!! Who am I kidding it was all good! Well Worth the travel from Texas!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Love it here. It's kinda kitschy so I thought I was just buying into tourist hype (as I'm wont to do on occasion), but seriously everything was delicious. Nevermind that I don't understand the ham thing. I had the biscuit sampler and the hashbrown casserole and it was really great. I'm obsessed with the fried green tomato pimiento cheese biscuit. And the BBQ was surprisingly good. Two thumbs up!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I was excited to try this place after reading reviews and receiving recommendations from friends.  I was disappointed to say the least.  We had a party of 6 and all got different plates.  Not one of us said "I'd come back".  It was okay but not what I had hoped for.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Landmark restaurants are always tricky. Sometimes they're just good, but nothing to write home about. They're famous because the locals love it, or it's tradition and because it makes some people nostalgic. Other times, it's well deserved fame that makes you wish you lived there so you could feast on those dishes to your little heart's content- that's Loveless. 

Sweet lord, Loveless. I will fantasize about this place until I can come back. When people think of outstanding, southern home cooking this is it. This is stick-to-your-ribs, bad for your arteries but good for your soul food. I will never be able to have a conversation about Nashville again without mentioning Loveless. 

So what was so good that I am love rambling about this place? 

-THE BISCUITS. 
I'm pretty sure angels sing when these come out of the oven. In Pluto's theory of forms, everything on earth is a copy of the perfect form of something in heaven. And I'm pretty sure Loveless biscuits are the ones they have in heaven. They are fluffy, and fresh and perfect. Obviously you need butter and preserves, because you wouldn't want to cut corners on this delicious experience. 

-BBQ pork omelet 
(AMAZING. One of the best omelets I've ever had). I ordered it because I knew I couldn't get a BBQ pork omelet in NYC or LA or even in carnivorous Chicago. When in Rome, right? Best decision I've made lately. The pork is so juicy and flavorful, and there was just a hint of BBQ sauce, so the smoky flavor carried the omelet. It was perfect. 5 stars. Will order it again every time. 

- The hash brown casserole 
AMAZING cheesy, potatoey, fatty goodness. You couldn't dream up better breakfast potatoes. These are an absolute must. They are the cherry on top of each bite.  

-country fried steak 
My friend got this and it is the ultimate country fried steak with gravy. She couldn't stop smiling while she was eating. If this is your thing, you will be so, so happy.  


I thought the fried chicken was good, but I'm not a big fried chicken person so I probably wouldn't order it again, it wasn't  life altering, like the biscuits.  

The service was outstanding. You feel so welcome and taken care of. That Southern hospitality gets city people like me every time. 

This place is a must, an absolute freaking must. When I am old and gray and look back on all the delicious food I have eaten in my life, I will think of Loveless. 

Peace, Loveless & Nashville forever.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Bland Americana anyone could make better at home. Spinach salad came with a thick gelatin-like dressing that was full of sugar and inedible. Chicken for the schnitzel was not tenderized as is the procedure for schnitzel so it was tough. Sauce was bland with no Swiss flavor. Only the red cabbage was tolerable.

name: Big Shotz
text: Off the main drag in downtown Nashville with less expensive drinks and shots.  Great live music.  Atmosphere is a bit rowdy and bathrooms are kinda rough, but it's the perfect spot to get the night started before frequenting the more pricey bars on broadway.  We always have a good time here.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: From the moment I walked the atmosphere was good. Me and my boyfriend was impressed they had a live band but you didn't have to scream to have a conversation. The band was very interacting with the children. My waiter was good also always checked to see if we needed more drinks. The amount of food you get is decent but it cost extra to get bread. It's $1.00 every roll you get. The spaztle was overcooked I was not impressed I didn't even eat the extra spaztle I got. The schnitzel was dry. The gravy didn't really have taste. I think it took a huge turning point when the male manager told me I wasnt german. He said just cause your mom is Germany doesn't make you one. Do you speak German? Uhhh yes I am mixed with African American and German. I was born in Germany. I can speak, read, and write in German after that I was ready to go. I didn't even take my food home

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I have only ever been here for shows.  And even though it hasn't been open long I've been to several.  I know there's a restaurant and bar space out front (the live music venue is in the back) but I haven't eaten there or even sat there so this review is focused solely on the gigantic slice of heaven that is the stage in the back.

Despite the large space the venue manages to be intimate, and the artists they book are not only talented but may not be your usual fare.  Many of them are older, classic performers, with amazing stories, or newcomers with some serious lyrical soul.  The acoustics are fantastic as well, and there's something about being able to just sit and enjoy some great food, drink, and entertainment without needed to dance or run around.  Its relaxing and enjoyable.

The staff is incredible in their ability to move around quickly without blocking your view of the stage or having to shout at you to ask if you want another drink.  And the drinks and food are just wonderful.  I am a huge fan of their beet and bacon flatbread and their burger.  They have so many delicious wines to choose from, as well as other alcoholic offerings, but if you love wine I recommend a bottle or two for a good show.

Most of the shows start by 8pm and are done by 11pm.  The servers are great at getting your tabs to you before the end of the show so you're not scrambling.  Its really just an overall fantastic dining and musical experience.

They offer free valet most nights, and even at soldout shows are great about getting your cars quickly.  The whole experience is just so laid back and enjoyable, and I've never had a bad time.  I highly recommend taking in a show here and coming early to eat.  The tickets for the concerts are usually more than reasonable, as is the food.  It's a great way to spend a Nashville night.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Unique place. Had multiple little gift shops to wonder thru while you wait. Get the breakfast! Great experience.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
We went on NYE for the Marc Broussard concert.  You can actually eat inside the concert hall if you want.  They open the doors well before the concert so you have plenty of time eat.  You will be seated at a large table with other patrons.  If you want to eat alone before entering the concert hall there is a small dining area and bar outside the concert hall.  It's small so you will need reservations.  

The beet humus was just ok.  The kale Caesar was wonderful.  Simple but one of the best salads I've ever had.  My wife had black eyed soup which was very tasty. 

The have one variety of most popular reds and whites.  We did a red flight.  It was acceptable but not what I would consider middle of the road.  They do have a large wine menu outside of what they produce.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Once seated, take your time and enjoy the biscuits (and accompanying preserves) while silently paying homage to the Biscuit Lady (may she Rest In Peace).....then order absolutely anything and be thankful ....IT IS ALWAYS DELICIOUS!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
They have good food and biscuits. That comes recommended. 

My issue is that I have a dairy allergy, and unfortunately Loveless Cafe failed me with my dietary restrictions. I notified my server about my allergy. She went and grabbed a manager just to be on the safe side. 

He told me he would double check, but I could order pancakes or waffles as the batter comes as a mix and is dairy free. Skeptical, I agreed to a waffle. After I ordered a waffle the sever asked me if I was sure about that as she claimed it contained dairy. Contrary to what the manager told me. She went to double check and read the ingredients list. Low and behold, it DID contain dairy.

Not only did a manager lie to me, but things could have been much worse had I been deathly allergic.

I ended up ordering just 2 eggs and some bacon as almost everything on the menu was not dairy-free friendly. 

Naturally, they cooked the eggs in butter even when I was told they use oil. Within 20 minutes I wanted to die. 

I can say this, they really do live up to their name. Loveless...

name: Loveless Cafe
text: From the minute you walk in, you're made to feel at home. This is my go to place every time I get to Nashville. The staff, the food, the down home, great feeling. Best food in Nashville. Makes you motneant to leave...the restaurant and the area itself. I LOVE the LOVELESS.

name: Big Shotz
text: Dive bar that draws you in with advertised $2 drafts and charges you $3 per draft. Just be honest. I'll pay$3 for a draft but the false advertising makes people feel scorned and bitter.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Great food/service every time we go. 
Biscuits are awesome!
Go early for breakfast as there can be a wait for a table as you get closer to 8:00 am, especially o. Saturday & Sunday mornings.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Soooo good. Going back as often as I can!  Food hot and tasty. Fast service was seated. A lot of history hanging on wall. Take home desserts a real treal

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My wife and I were really looking forward to trying this place because there were not a lot of wine-focused restaurants/bars in the region in our opinion.  This one had a pretty good history.

When we got here, we walked in and while it was a visually pleasing space, it was really quiet which sort of takes the air out of your sails.  When you advertise that music is a focal point of your location, I would think having at least something playing in the Barrel Room would be part of the experience. It's rare when there is no music whatsoever playing even in the background in a restaurant.  It just makes it so that all you can hear are people eating, talking and clanging their plates.  That could be by design but it just kind of made us tired after 15 minutes.

We walked up to the bar and sat down and were greeted by a very friendly bartender.  My wife opted for one of their White & Rose' flights and I selected their Domaine Skouras.  Their wine list lacked some very basic options like a Pinot Grigio, Albarino and they only had one Chardonnay.  My wife tried all the wines in her flight and really couldn't connect with any of them so we decided to pull the plug and move on.  It could be that it was just an off night but we do wine places all over the U.S. and this one just couldn't hold our attention.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: I am a local - 6th generation.  I know southern food when I taste it.  My family has released several published southern cook books over the years. The food is good!  The menu and the prices remind me of our local restaurant Arnold's Country Kitchen.  They serve food until 9:30 pm at Fat Kat Slim's, and this place is worth a try. You can get breakfast, lunch, and dinner. I am thankful this restaurant is so near by where I live.  I am glad to see another meat and three where they can get you in and out.  The service is friendly, and the owners (a husband and wife team) were present during our dining experience.  I appreciated their southern hospitality!  They have the best martinis in town...I had the spellbound.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If you are in Nashville you have to stop here just for the warm biscuits alone.  We were in Nashville for a conference and someone recommended this place and we were so satisfied with everything.  First you are met with a plate of warm biscuits with three different jams, butter is already on the table, before you even place your drink order which was amazing as we hadn't eaten lunch.  Everyone loved their entree from the BBQ chicken special to the pulled pork on hoecakes and their special fried chicken.  The only bad thing, if this is a bad thing, we had no room for dessert and staying in a hotel meant taking dessert home was out of the question.  If we are ever in the area this is one place we will not miss.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Fried chicken: amazing
Catfish: amazing
Smoked pulled pork: amazing
Turnip greens: amazing 
Hush puppies: amazing
Fried green tomatoes: amazing
Marinated cubes&onions amazing
Biscuits: none finer

The service was bright, fun and thorough. I never had to look around or hunt for it because it was there before I knew. 

They say road to disappointment is paved with expectations.   They are wrong.  

Whatever you expect, this place will exceed by a mile.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
It is entirely possible that the Käsespätzle I've eaten at an Austrian restaurant back home is an outlier. If that's the case, my review is pointless.

But the Käsespätzle I got here wasn't even playing the same sport, much less in the same ballpark. It was glorified mac-and-cheese, and not even that glorified.

It came out in like 5 minutes, which was weird. There was nothing Bavarian about the seasoning. Just noodles... and lots and lots of cheese that looked like melted velveeta. 

Again, maybe the Käsespätzle I've had before isn't normal, but it had a very distinct taste and appearance, and this wasn't anything like that. 

Look for the reviews of stuff that was actually really good before ordering, and skip this item.

name: Big Shotz
text: This is a little hole in the wall bar off Broadway in Nashville, A good little hang out if you're looking for good cheap drinks and a not so crowded and busy atmosphere. They have girls going around selling jello shots, they sell moonshine pickles, their drinks are good and very reasonably priced.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I enjoyed this place.  I stopped by for an early dinner one night.  It was rather empty at the time so I was seated and served quite quickly.

The restaurant itself is really large.  Lots of room!  Be prepared for the German style long tables though.  If they are busy, I would imagine you would be seated beside others :)

They have a wall for beer steins, so I gather you can purchase them there and leave them there for some kind of drink discount.  Since I don't drink, I didn't look into this.

The food was good.  It was something that I would go WOW for but it was decent.  I would go back and try something different next time around I feel.  I think it would also be a good place to go with a group of friends.

Some of the waitresses tend to ummmm....hang out a little on the cleavage department.  Okay if you want to see that while you eat...me....it is not necessary and will not contribute to the size of your tip.  That all depends on service and food.   The service was good and she did get a good tip though haha.

name: Big Shotz
text:
Warning, to Tourists and Locals. 
Do not step foot in a lowdown bar called "Big Shotz". Today, l found out that the night l was kicked out, 3 more people were shown the door. Only l was drinking Soda-Coke. Never accidentally bump into The Blond Snobby Lady? "OWNER" there. 
All l did was turn around and accidentally walked into her. Maybe she was standing too close to me. Oh, my l did not know That l had been impolite to The Queen 
of Nashville. I did not know anything was wrong. Then she says with a attitude and raised voice "Do You Always Run Into People and do not say excuse me?"

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Okay food average at best breakfast. The biscuits were delicious but that was about it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Out on a culinary adventure in the hills of Middle Tennessee to find a staple that is almost 70 years old. After a little drive, I am here at the Loveless Cafe off of State Route 100 in Pasquo (southwest of Nashville). You can't miss it because of the iconic neon sign that welcomes you. Wow this was like going back in time to the 1950's. As I walk in the front door of this home from 1951 I feel like a lonely traveler on the road that Lon and Annie welcomed back in the day. You can tell that there was a lot of love and generosity in the home which later became the restaurant. As I walk in the door the smells are amazing. The aroma of home cooking floating through the air invites you to have a seat and make yourself at home. As I take my seat the waitress walks up to the table like your mom coming to ask what you would like for breakfast. I find out that she has worked here for more than 20 years. She was the true example of southern hospitality. Now I am anxious and excited to try the food. Almost immediately after taking my order I see her coming back to the table with a plate of hand made biscuits that look like soft and fluffy pillows with a trio of homemade jams. The jams were the perfect combination of sweet and tart made with love. Even with it being a busy Sunday morning, my food arrived before I was done with all of my biscuits. I ordered the Famous Loveless Cafe Country Ham with two over easy eggs and red eye gravy and the hash brown casserole on the side. Would they pass the test for good southern cooking? OMG that's all I can say. I give the Loveless Cafe 4 guitars. On busy days be prepared to wait unless you have a reservation. Fortunately, you have stuff to do while you wait as you can explore the grounds and gift shops where you can even by the jams you get to eat in the restaurant.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Similar to other reviewers, we went a bit out of the way to grab brunch here. About a 25 minute drive from my place off West End in Nashville, we waited about 40 minutes to be seated. The biscuits and jams were DELICIOUS. The breakfast selections my friend and I had (French Toast, and Waffle) were good sized and tasty, but nothing extraordinary. 

Definitely a good meal, a bit heavy, and worth checking out if you have time in your schedule for the drive out and for the wait!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food was mediocre. This is a fun place for a photo op, but I cannot vouch for the food at the cafe. I will say that I enjoyed the nearby gift shop. If you're traveling and want to bring back goodies (e.g., jams, sauces) for your loved ones, this is a great place to find those goods.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Just a neat place to go.  With platters you can get a sampling but they are ridgid on swapping sides or up charging for things like ribs.  BBQ is smothered style but the watermelon and cranberry BBQ sauces makes up for it.  Amazing sides.  Banana pudding that keeps the local cardiologist in business and is the gateway to heaven.

A complex worth a visit when all the shops are open.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
If you haven't been to Germany you wouldn't know the food is not quite the quality as real German food. We've lived in Germany for 9 years and I am European. 

Now the food is ok but since this is suppose to be German we left the restaurant a little sceptic. I ordered a Jägerschnitzel and we shared a Flammkuchen. Now don't get me wrong it's ok and it looks authentic but the flavor was wanting. 
The bacon on the Flammkuchen was too hard and it looked as if it was pre-made bacon. It's supposed to be Speck and white onions. The parsley garnish completely dominated the flavor. There's usually no parsley on Flammkuchen. 

Jägerschnitzel was fine if you don't know how it's suppose to taste like. This was just a pork chop with some tasteless breading. The mushroom sauce=Jägersauce was just brown gravy with seemingly canned mushrooms as a garnish. It didn't taste right and it didn't taste like mushroom. 

When you order a schnitzel in Germany the kitchen sounds like a construction zone because the chef hammers the pork down to almost hair thin so it cooks quickly and the breading stays crispy. The breading has subtle spices and full of flavor. The sauce is suppose to be more dark red/brown and flavored of  mushroom, wine and cream. Mushrooms are the key ingredient in a jägersauce not the garnish. If you have a German restaurant it would be important to an authentic German restaurant to at least get the schnitzel right- and unfortunately this wasn't right. 
The fries were great and had a subtle dusting of spices. 

The atmosphere is nice and I love the decor. It has the Hofbräuhaus feeling. 
However in Germany our bill would be half the price and the food twice as good and the beer as cheap as mineral water.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Loveless Cafe 
8400 Tennessee Highway 100
Nashville, TN 37221

We had a late breakfast here and absolutely loved it. This is the real deal, down home true Southern cooking at its best. The biscuits were genuine home made and you can watch the whole process in the back! Great food and service. All the bacon, sausage and hans are made right there. The jams and jellies are fantastic too!   I would recommend as a must anytime you come near Nashville. 

Urban Cowgill 
Dec 2015

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
The food and ambiance was amazing! The service... extremely slow. Wine glasses empty, never offering another round, dirty appetizer plates stacked on the table forever. Our reservation was at 7, we got our Che ha ag 9:30. Everything seemed to take a very long time. 
Everyone's food was so yummy ! I had the lamb sandwich, I can't wait to have it again! The risotto balls with punkin and goat cheese were a big hit, as well as the calamari. 
Another annoyance is when the music starts in the venue, and you're in the restI would go back for sure with hopes of a better service experience.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Great German food.  Fun music and very like a German beer hall.  Good beer and great dessert.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We went 2 days in a row while visiting Nashville.  One of the owners was working and checking on the guest. He spent alot of time helping his guest and we had a great time. I really loved the jagersnitzel  and cheese  soup

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Nice atmosphere but don't stop for a quick drink or bite! Stopped in on a Saturday at 3pm and sat at the bar. After going unnoticed for 15 minutes sitting AT THE BAR, my wife went to stand at the register to get the attention of the poorly trained (or managed) staff. The one girl behind the bar was far too busy running checks(?) to acknowledge patrons. The beer on the other hand was excellent (I had the Schnickelfritz). If management can train the staff properly this could be a nice experience. Use caution if in a time crunch.

name: Big Shotz
text: If I could give negative stars I would. Came in to support a friend that was playing in the band. The bartender came up very rudely and says "yeah?" As he was biting his nails. Ok well hi. My husband and I ordered two beers and his response was "what?" Ok can we have "blah blah blah" walks away still biting his nails. Stops and keeps biting and spits his nail in the trash. So that's gross. Walks over to people at the bar does a shot while staring me down and still hasn't given us our beer. My husband and i walk over and say "just cancel our order" and his response was to just laugh and let us leave. I work in the bar industry and I have NEVER experienced such rudeness and unprofessionalism in my life!!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is a fun place! The pretzels were amazing! That alone would earn a five stars. I would recommend this place. That being said it wasn't my favorite food choice.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This was my second time visiting Loveless Cafe. The first time I had a great experience. Tonight I was extremely dissatisfied in the food and service I received. I ordered the country fried steak. What came out was a poor execution of a southern classic. The steak had little to no flavor. The breading was bland and soft. Country fried steak should have a crunchy and well seasoned breading. When Cracker Barrel has a better steak then that is a problem for a restaurant claiming to be a purveyor of southern cuisine. 
I took a grand total of three bites from my steak.  The waiter never questioned why I didn't eat my steak despite my lack of consumption. This is something that a trained waiter should look for. It seemed that the waiter was non-confrontational and didn't want to deal with it. I even handed them my plate with the almost entire steak still on it. 
I doubt I will return to Loveless in the future. Nor will I tell my friends to go as well. 
I encourage Loveless to rethink what they are serving customers and train their waitstaff to look for signs of a dissatisfied customer.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A little ways outside of Nashville but worth the trip! The drive to get to Loveless is beautiful. Expect a wait, especially on the weekends, but spend the time waiting browsing the 5-6 gift shops and beautiful grounds. The biscuits were to die for! We went with a group of 9 and everyone left satisfied, if not stuffed.

name: Big Shotz
text: I was just abused by the bouncer at this location.  I'm no spring chicken and I questioned needing to see my aiD and walked away, he said "go F*** yourself ".  Needless to say this guy shouldn't be anywhere near the public!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Great food, unfortunately, horrible customer service....
I made a reservation for 12 people about 3 weeks ago. It was my birthday this past weekend, so I made sure that I made all of my reservations well in advance. We were about 12 minutes late for our reservation, however I called in advance to let them know. Once we arrived at the restaurant they had a table ready for us, for 8 people. I let them know that I made the reservation for 12, and they said that they didn't have our table in the system and it would be a 30 minute wait.. They then tried to blame us, saying that we were 20 minutes late for our reservation. Mind you, we were NOT that late, and I called in advance to let them know.  Once we finally got seated, we basically had no service. They switched waiters 3 different times, and no one came to our table. At the end of the dinner, we asked the manager for some sort of compensation for the inconvenience and horrible service, and he refused. He said that we should not have gotten there late and the general manager will not give us any compensation. I refused to tip them, and I let them know that I will not be back again.

It was very disappointing because we have been to the City Winery in Napa and we actually love it. I did not expect such horrible service in Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is very cute. The wait was around two hours for a party of five on a Sunday at 10am. Everything that we ordered was great and the little stores are a nice touch. Nothing was overpriced. Was a nice place to spend a Sunday morning.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is awesome! This is the 2nd time I've been. 

Great food! I went with a group and we ordered family style and it fed the 8 of us to beyond full. 

The service was great too! Friendly waitress! She was busy, but still was personable and kept our drinks full. I think her name was Rachel! 

The only down is they don't let you keep the left overs that are on the table, a lot of waste.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If you are in Nashville this is so worth the drive! Best breakfast by far! Biscuits, jam, country fried steak.....oh so good! It is so worth waiting for if there is a line. Little shops are very cute also! Was number one of favorite food venues while we have been here!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
The 615 wine is excellent. The sound is excellent and there's not a bad seat in the house. Jose' and Caitlin were nice and helpful. I actually had an issue that wasn't their fault but they really bent over backwards to make it right. In the end I had a lovely time. 

The menu does not have a lot of basic dishes, so if you are picky or will have a picky person in your party, I recommend checking out the menu online beforehand.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless cafe was on my list of places to eat while visiting Nashville. It's not far from Belle Meade so squeeze in a lunch or breakfast before your tour. My son and I LOVED the chicken and waffle. My daughter and husband like the spicy chicken daily special. He is still talking about the hash brown casserole a day later. With the wait!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: As a venue this place is amazing. There's not a bad seat in the house and the acoustics are awesome. The food is mediocre and expensive. The wine can be hit or miss as well. Also, this last time we were here it was freezing cold to the point that we kept our winter jackets on for the duration of the show. I'm not sure if they keep it cooler on purpose on account of the wine but it was a little unbearable.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Had a wonderful breakfast!  We were seated within 5 minutes of arriving, around 10:30 on a Friday.   The country fried steak was bigger than my face!  The homemade biscuits and jams were outstanding. We are so glad we listened to the amazing recommendations for this place. We will definitely be back!!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Easily the best burger in Nashville. 
Our server Kim took care of us and she couldn't have been better. Spoke to our kids as soon as she came to the table, and had perfect drink recommendations for stressed parents. 
Will be going back for the burger ASAP!!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My favorite breakfast spot in Tennessee! Came here the first day I arrived and it was so good I had to have it again before I left. By far my favorite biscuits and preserves I had while on my trip. Even bought some jars of my own to take back home. I had their Music City Platter with the Ham and it was amazing! Massive portion was sure to keep me filled until dinner! I'll definitely be back on my next trip to TN

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
A Nashville native told me that "Loveless Cafe" was a "must visit" place to eat during a recent trip to Nashville.  I must agree!  There was a long wait, but we were able to quickly pass the time playing corn-hole, browsing the shops, and sampling the complementary peach tea!


I ordered the meatloaf, and it was excellent!   I can think of any other restauarant that has meatloaf that is any better!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Just ok , it's a neat little place but if you base ur review just on the food it's just ok 
Prob won't eat here again 
Wait staff was friendly and helpful and kept out drinks full didn't have to ask for anything 
For five stars for the staff 

Ok on the food 
I ordered the hot chicken plate with Mac and cheese and turnip greens 
And biscuits of coarse 

Hot chicken was good but wasn't hot had like a luisiana hot sauce over it  good but needs more heat 
Mac and cheese was average little dry 
Turnip greens was good but it was hotter than the hot chicken 
Couldn't hardly eat the greens for it burning my throat 
And the famous biscuits was just a biscuit nothing impressive I've had better biscuits at Hardee's 
In all it was a disappointment cause I've wanted to eat here for two years and when I came the food was better than what I can cook at home

My wife got the dark meat chicken plate 
And she said was not good at all

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Food - everything that we got was excellent.  Our family tried the schnitzel (both pork and chicken), both which were crispy on the outside and tender inside.  The salmon was tender with a crispy skin.  The mashed potatoes on the side were smooth and creamy, and homemade pickles on the side.   We also tried the spatzle instead of fries--it's an egg noodle.  My wife thought they might be homemade, but not sure.  

Ambience - This place is very family friendly.  It reminded me of being at Disney.  Even though many people were having beer, it doesn't feel like a pub/bar.  It's brightly lit, again taking away from the pub feel.  It's a giant area, and there were many couples that were seated by themselves at tables meant for around 8.  

Dessert- we had the sampler.  The black forest cake was very good: cold, tasty whipped cream, and did not taste like it was from a box.  The apple danish is sort of a warmer/moister version that I'm used to, but very good and worth getting.  Lastly, the pretzel bread pudding: too hard and not moist.  Not sure if we got a bad piece, or it's supposed to be like that.  

Beer- We didn't have any, but most people around us had beer.  Many had the samplers, which consist of 4 smaller glasses.  

Price- a little more than expected, about 20% more.  But it's in a touristy mall, so it's expected.  

Overall, a pleasant surprise.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
We went to a pod cast show at the beginning of December.  My biggest complaint is that I purchased VIP seats that turned out to be at the literal back of the room--like literally we were against the back wall.  They made some noise about it being on an elevated section and what not but it was in no way better to be at the back than the front.  The balcony seats honestly would have had a better view.

I agree with the other reviewers about the wine, but it was definitely overpriced and nothing special.  We both enjoyed our food but it was a limited sampling to be sure.

Buyer beware--if you're going for a show, avoid the VIP seating (or pay better attention than I did because I honestly had no idea this would be at the back of the room) and sit closer to the front.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This location has great atmosphere and has fast become one of the best venues for the small and intimate music that Nashville is known for.  I highly recommend it for a fun show, as they have a good wine and cocktail list.  HOWEVER, I equally recommend that you eat before you arrive.  The food started out as reasonable quality when they opened, pricey but not bad for a music venue, but wow has the situation deteriorated.  I attended a show and ordered dinner this past Monday night, and what a disaster.  My $15 hamburger took a full 45 minutes to arrive and was so overcooked I could hardly eat it.  The waitress offered to have it re-cooked, but the music was starting, and I sure didn't want to wait another 45 minutes.  When I inquired about a half-hour into the wait what had become of our food, I was astounded when she answered, "I know, it's slow, I'm sorry, but the restaurant is really busy tonight."  This was a reference to the other half of the house, outside the music venue, and to be told their food took priority was just ridiculous.  I am confident it was not her fault, as I could see no one around us had food either, and we had arrived early, a full hour before the show, to avoid this exact problem.  Diners beware and skip this if you can, but the music and the bar selections are good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I loved Loveless!
#mesocheesy #tooeasy #ilovelove

If you've got some time to kill, head 30 minutes outside of Nashville to the Loveless Cafe. It's known by many in the area as having the best gosh darn breakfast in all of Tennessee! Yeehaw! And biscuits are their jam!!! (get it...? biscuits have jam on them...? sooo....biscuits and jam...? yeaaaaa).

The menu is so expensive it's nearly impossible to pick which delicies to scarf down. My usual thing is I want to try as many things as possible at new places so I went with the Biscuit Sampler Platter for $11.99. You can then choose 4 biscuits from: Fried Green Tomato & Pimento Cheese, Barbeque, Country Ham, Fried Chicken, Bacon, Sausage or Steak. I went with the Ham, Chicken, Sausage and Bacon because meat! All were good but let's be real, bacon makes everything better. Actually the plain biscuits with some jam preserves were the best thing of all - even better than my meat between the bread.

If you have to wait for a table, they have some cute shops outside the restaurant. Even if you don't have to wait, they are worth a stop in after dining. I bought a couple of floofy headbands for myself while there.

Loveless Cafe was a fun place to go, but the hype might have slightly exceeded the experience for me. I'm glad I went, think everyone everyone should go, but it's not a place I could see myself driving distances for again. Been there, done that.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Incredible venue with the best atmosphere and service! The food is delicious.  The wine is perfection.  And, Soplia is awesome!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
4.5

Before I get too into this love letter, I have to say that the address has always been a concern of mine. For tourists interested in coming to LC or new transplants eager to see what the fuss is, y'all should all know that this isn't Nashville proper. You will drive a good ways away from the city limits to come here. Whether you want to call it Bellevue or Pasquo, it's all the same to me. You just shouldn't call it Nashville. Doing so, you're going to be surprised why you're so far away from all the other Nashville attractions you've read about and want to see.*

Logistics out of the way, The Loveless Cafe is everything that's wonderful about living in the Nashville metro area. To begin with, driving to it on Hwy 100 from the city is something that's pretty in every season, but early fall is my favorite time to do so. The winding road and turning leaves leave no doubt that you're in the southland and you're about to enjoy some fantastic eats. The drive really prepares you for the experience. Once you arrive... yep, you're here. TLC is an old motel. I think that adds to the charm. It looks like a movie set. Having the cafe and motel unchanged (where it counts) since the '50s is a testament to the power, honor and necessity of tradition. I am so pleased to know that no soulless developer (from out of town, no less) has been able to destroy what should never be touched. I wished the city of Nashville followed suit. So, charm, drive, motel... you're caught up. Park out front or along the back and get ready to do some serious eating.

This ain't the place to be if you're on a diet or (unfortunately) have dietary restrictions. This is heavy, sugary, fried Southern goodness. A steady diet of the stuff WILL kill you so only come here on special occasions. Give your name to the nice people up front and take your seat. Pro tip: don't come here on the weekend or for brunch. That's amateur hour. Come here for dinner during the week and you won't suffer through the pain of waiting behind a family from Modesto eager to take a group selfie with a gingham tablecloth background. I have to let folks know how to do things...

Okay, you're seated. Get ready to eat all the food. Remember, no diet/restrictions. Start with sweet tea and keep it coming. Next, say 'yes' to the biscuits and keep them coming. You're going to want to try all the preserves AND the butter, so save (at least) a biscuit half for each type. They're canned on site and they're delicious. I can't choose between the peach, strawberry or blackberry. They're all addictive. Okay. Strawberry. But I wouldn't turn any of them down. Next, you're here for dinner so go all in. Depending on the day of the week, you'll be able to choose from a special menu. I don't need anything special because if you're going all in on a Southern feast, you gotta go for the chicken. Get the half fried chicken. It'll come with the back, breast, wing, and drumstick. You won't be able to finish, so eat half of the half. Why won't you finish? Well, you're going to consume a gallon of sweet tea. The biscuits are coming to your table as fast as you can eat them. Oh, and you get sides with your chicken. The choices are awesome so choose wisely. As much as I wanted to go for cheese grits and greens (man, I could go for that now; I'm hungry), I chose the fried green tomatahs and mackincheese. I was very happy with both choices. The tomaters were crispy, nicely-breaded and flavorful on their own. Plus, the serving was generous. You're not going to receive one lone, sad tomato. The mac was a bit creamier than I like (I prefer the southernized, post-church baked and a wee bit crispy mac) but it was tasty nevertheless. I wanted to end with peach cobbler but I couldn't be a hero. I was stuffed to the point of discomfort and I had a long drive back to the city ahead of me. I am pretty sure I was food drunk. It's a thing. Next time, dessert. Next time.**

*Seriously. Look at a map. Does this look in town to you?
**Next time to be determined upon consultation with my physician.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Came here to grab lunch on my way through Nashville while on a road trip with my husband. We came at around 1pm on a Saturday afternoon and wait time was minimum an hour and a half. 

I ordered the Southern Sampler Platter since I read great yelp reviews about their fried chicken and country ham and wanted to try both out for myself. The Southern Sampler Platter allowed you to pick 3 of their meats so I picked the fried chicken, country ham, and pork barbecue with 2 sides (I got the mac & cheese and mashed potatoes). All I need to say is GET THE FRIED CHICKEN!!! The chicken meat is juicy and moist and the outer skin layer is crisp and not the least bit fatty. Yummmm!!! The country ham was a little tough, not tender at all, and extremely salty in my opinion. The pork barbecue was ok- not terrible- but definitely worth a bite. The macaroni & cheese was pretty good and the mashed potatoes with the brown gravy was delicious as well. However, I didn't love the red eye gravy that we also got on the side for the mashed potatoes. And last but not least (or I should say first off in the meal), the biscuits here are amazing with their homemade jams!!! I don't love bread and biscuits but the jam here is finger licking good!! Be sure to try it out!! 

On the whole, this restaurant is an awesome brunch/lunch spot and if I'm ever in Nashville again I will definitely come back here!!

name: Big Shotz
text:
While wandering around the chintzy Broadway/District area, walk right past Big Shotz and don't stop in.

The "shotz" that they have are all pretty disgusting and taste like a hangover waiting to happen. While cheap, I just don't think it's worth it. They come in a small cup (larger than a shot glass but much smaller than a solo cup), so it's hard to enjoy your drink while also listening to the music.

The venue is also not well-designed. The bar area is very small, making it difficult to get your order in. We were also trying to stand near the band and kept having to move over so staff could access the back rooms for more beer/liquor bottles. Just not a pleasant experience overall!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My husband and I loved this place. It was s little bit of a drive from downtown Nashville but absolutely worth the trip. The manager and our waiter Owen were so welcoming and did a great job. The biscuits and jam were so good I could have just ate them. The southern sampler let us try a little bit of everything and the banana pudding at the end was awesome. Portions were large so doggie bags were needed. I would definitely eat here again!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I went to a concert there where they offered a general admission standing area for the first time. Don't do it! There wasn't a seating map online so I figured GA is always in the front, right? We were shoved in a back corner, roped off like animals. And they had put a (limited) bar for us in the GA area too, but it was in a front corner instead of behind us?? So it took up more of the standing room that people would want to be in. Made no sense. Everyone else at tables got fancy glasses and they were giving us plastic cups. We asked to upgrade to a table because we had no idea it was going to be like that and they told us they weren't allowed to do that for anyone else anymore, they had gotten in trouble with a manager or something. Probably because they didn't have enough tables for everyone from GA to move, but then we stood there the rest of the night with empty tables right in front of us. People were sitting on the floor against the wall all night, it was a joke. They stressed that it was a new thing for them so I really hope they don't keep trying it. Honestly the whole vibe of the place was weird too because there are constantly servers everywhere and I wouldn't recommend it for an artist you're really excited to see

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Place is very popular so be ready to wait, but they do a pretty good job of moving things along. You get all you can eat biscuits which is pretty nice, not the best biscuits in the world but they get the job done. I guess their chicken is supposed to be something special but I found it to just be all right. Same with the country fried streak it was just ok. I will say the sides were amazing, great cheese grits, Mac and cheese and hash browns. Good food but not mind blowing, I didn't see what the big attraction was.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
First, this venue has promise. I came for a multi-day corporate team event, so I haven't been for the nightlife or a la cart dinner yet. It has a large bar on both floors, ample space for patrons and/or large groups, and a nice looking interior.

A few of cons:

1) After parking my car in one of several available parking spots on the lot, a valet ran out to tell me I had to valet my car - which meant I had to give him the keys for my car to sit in the same spot all day. Huh?
2) The upstairs area is open to the entryway and multiple times in our meetings we were interrupted by loud groups of women squealing, something like "Like oh mah gawwwd!!"
3) The food was mediocre and healthy options were extremely limited. Fried chicken fingers aren't for everyone at breakfast, for example.

Some promise:

1) The main dining and concert areas are nice.
2) Wine on tap.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
my FAV biscuits!! worth the drive. 

PROTIP: order biscuits to go and eat them in a park or at home! they will still be warm 20 min later (Which is what i usually do) 

the breakfast food is aites to me (but i dont like heavy breakfasts to start my day). 

tourists: watch out for the drive. this isnt technically located in "nashville" but 20 minutes west of nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Fried chicken and grits at 9am on a Monday?  Why yes, I think I will.  

My husband and I saved Loveless Cafe for last on our 5-day trip to Nashville.  We decided to go on the Monday we flew out so we didn't have a wait.  Luckily, we only had a 5-minute wait and got to chat it up with the locals.  

We were seated and presented with a plateful of warm biscuits, butter and three different jams (strawberry, peach and blackberry).  

The server, who was as sweet as the jam I was enjoying, recommended the fried chicken.  I ordered eggs, fried chicken and grits.  It was the best fried chicken and grits I've ever had.  In fact, the biscuits are the best I've ever had as well.  The chicken was crisp and simply coated, juicy and moist inside.  The grits were super creamy, salted perfectly and had the right amount of cheese.  

I don't ever remember what my husband had because I was too consumed with my delicious meal to be bothered.  

What I thought was going to be an overrated and overhyped meal turned out to be one of the best meals of our trip.  I'm so glad we made the trek out to eat at Loveless.  No matter what the wait is, this is definitely worth it.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: This place was a big disappointment.  Waited over 30 mins for the fried chicken... both orders were bloody enough to spill on to the plate... poor waitress had to handle it... Sucked

name: Big Shotz
text:
AVOID THIS PLACE! The staff is absolutely horrible. They overcharged me and were incredibly rude when I tried to question the bill. They even got a bouncer involved, embarrassing me into just paying it. The following day my credit card company called and saw multiple charges that looked fraudulent. They advised me to cancel my account and get a new card (which I did). 

Too much energy was required for just a dive bar, and there are so many better spots to choose from in downtown Nashville. I truly don't know how they stay in business and I certainly will never be a returning customer.

name: The Basement
text:
Maybe we're idiots, or maybe we're not. Puja P had her heart set on seeing a show here but we hovered under the Basement's "USE ALLEY ENTRANCE" sign having no idea where to go. The front door was locked. The alley gate was locked. We heard merriment and saw Christmas lights underneath the balcony floorboards but could not imagine how to get in. 

We'd been an hour late to the start of the show. Was it already over? That would've been in line with our experiences of everything in Nashville closing after 10pm. It was only after admitting defeat that it occurred to us that you have to walk literally DOWN THE BLOCK to the BACK of the house to get in. Jesus. In New York City, alleys are adjacent to houses, not behind them.

While Karry L used his sexual prowess to hail a cab, Puja P and I cut across some backyards to briefly check out this newly imagined entrance. Sure enough, there was the bouncer, who told us: "I just got a text message from the bar, he said to stop charging the cover so you guys get in free." Woot! 

(Later on, Puja P tells me that he didn't get any such text message. But how do you know?! The cover was otherwise $5)

Just from hovering inside briefly, it looked like a cute, intimate space, rough around the edges in a good way. The bit of music we heard was a girl + guitar deal. There's a little outdoor deck for nicotine escapes, which explained all the noise we'd heard standing outside. Then Karry L appeared, hangin' out the passenger side of the cabbie's ride. We should've figured out the ingress situation earlier.  

Worth a visit as a tourist? Yes, I think so. It still isn't located in the most convenient location if you have other destinations afterward and don't want to drive or get a cab, but at least now we all know how to get in. Because you've gotta start somewhere.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If you're visiting Nashville and you don't go here, did you really visit Nashville? ALSO- if you're from the Nashville area and have never been here, can you even call yourself a local? I love breakfast food and you can never go wrong with Loveless. Definitely worth the long wait for those amazing biscuits

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The food wasn't all that bad. I order the garden omelette, it tasted good but need to add seasoning flavor to spice it up. 

The place is nice to see a lot of famous people photos with an autograph.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The service and the food are outstanding. They managed the 45 minute wait with appropriate discussion and options for walking around their facilities. The fried chicken was outstanding (not as good as Bubbas in Dallas) and the biscuits were tasty as well. It is about 30 minutes outside of Nashville but worth the experience!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
We came for Burger Week, yes, rather strange timing, but I'm so glad we did. The burger was excellent, cooked perfectly, and I loved the mozzarella, fried onions and what I think might have been thousand island dressing called aioli. When anything is served on a pretzel bun, it's like having a treat for dinner, because I savor the bun separate from the burger. I wish I had known about the fresh sauerkraut on the side because I would have skipped the hot bacon spinach salad (which should have been in a bowl). 

So that was good enough, but then the pretzel bread pudding put it over the top. Anyone who knows my reviews, knows that I love a bread pudding. This gets 4 forks (top rating) for sure on my blog: https://breadpuddinglovers.blogspot.com/. It's luscious.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Yum. Those biscuits, That peach jam. My mouth is watering. The biscuits are the star - they are soft inside with a slightly thick exterior, they melt in your mouth with the right touch of salt. 

We waited over two hours for a table on Memorial Day. There were plenty of shops to look in and the view is nice enough. They had free beverages all over the grounds for guests who were waiting. I think it would serve them well if they'd set up a place to sell biscuits to guests who were waiting. They'd make a killing and guests would be less agitated as they waited. Our waiter was kind but a little over bearing. He went beyond the usual southern hospitality and I thought he was going to pull up a chair and eat with us. The fried chicken was delicious, hash brown casserole was tasty, cat fish was good. Nothing was bad but nothing - other than the biscuits - blew me away. It is well cooked southern food in a fun atmosphere.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
This independent theater has been setting the gold standard for years, and the recent(-ish) renovation has only made it more impressive. Buying tix online is easy, and then you can just check in at the ticket counter. You can, of course, take a chance and just purchase tickets day-of, but often it's a packed house. So do yourself a favor and buy in advance. 

The theater is pristine and has all the trappings of a traditional "art house" cinema in a modern setting. Restrooms are immaculate, and the lobby is fresh and bright with loads of windows for a healthy dose of natural light. Concessions are top-notch. I'm talking a wide range of craft beer and wines, yummy snacks and ice water offered without being pushed to buy a spendy bottle.b

Though not worth a ding in stars, I don't find the chairs particularly comfortable. So if you are coming for a long flick, bring a sweater or jacket to cushion your behind; you can thank me later. 

Otherwise, go! Enjoy! See something weird or different to scratch your intellectual and artistic itch - you know you wanna head over right now.

name: Drifters
text: Amazing corndogs and fries. One of the best corndogs I've had actually. Really good smoked wings and bbq sauces. The bartenders are some of my favorites in Nashville.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: The Belcourt is amazing! Everyone there is so nice and friendly, the concession stand isn't too expensive and every film I've seen there I've loved. The history is so rich too, and I feel special being there even though they recently remodeled, it still has the charm it did when I use to go there back in the mid 90s with my grandmother. Definitely one of the best places to see a film in Nashville.

name: Drifters
text: Very happy about the amount of vegetarian options! Got the BBQ black bean nachos and they were awesome. Ate hush puppies for the first time! Server was awesome and patient since we hung out for almost 3 hours.

name: Drifters
text: Nice casual atmosphere. Young vibe. Went on Sunday evening , no brisket, no ribs, they were all sold out, very disappointing. Wait staff was slow.

name: Drifters
text: Great BBQ in a relaxed environment! They have a good selection of sauces, reasonable prices and friendly staff.  We tried a little of everything. We had the sampler dinner, hand dipped corn dog, smoked wings, and a BBQ sandwich.  Everything was hot and delicious!

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
It was pretty dull inside, however it was a Tuesday. $2 off chicken and catfish tacos on Tuesdays for happy hour I believe 2p-7p. Also half price select appetizers like my cheese squares! Everything was really tasty & fresh! 

Whenever I'm near Music Row again, they can have my coins.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Happy new year!  What a cool spot to party.  They have a awesome amount of talent coming through here on stage.  Besides the drinks being a little higher in price, I have nothing bad to say.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Each time I come here I always wonder why I come back. The service is terrible. There were only 4 other people in the bar at dinner time on a Sunday and it took at least 50 minutes for us to get two sandwiches and the last sandwich came another 10 minutes after that. The sandwiches were supposed to be panini's but the meat (turkey and bacon) was not warm and the bread was lukewarm. It was supposed to come with ranch, which none of them did and the waitress seemed annoyed when we asked for a side of ranch. I've been here multiple times because I live down the road and the experience is usually the same.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
The Belcourt is flat out fantastic. It really is.

I love that they show everything from edgy documentaries to cult classics at midnight. They also have some incredible events like Oscar viewings, concerts, comedy, and the latest Wes Anderson film. It's a historic site, so the interior is very classic with the red curtain and updated but still unique. They also serve alcohol and food! Score! 

I love the Belcourt and need to frequent them more often!

name: EXIT/IN
text:
I've been here MANY times since 2000 and the venue is pretty good. Always has great bands come through. From legends to nobodies just starting to make a name. 

Cons: the staff has become increasingly rude over the years. Shitty beer selection.

name: Drifters
text: Hands-down the best barbecue I've ever had. The ribs came right off the bone, the pork was flavorful and the sausage was just sweet enough. For my first dining experience in Nashville (and all of Tennessee), I couldn't have asked for a richer experience. They were even dog friendly, allowing our little pup to eat and drink with us on the outside patio. Live music was performed outside, which added the final touch to an incredible evening.

name: Drifters
text:
Great little place! 

We are on the road for a few days and looked for a dog friendly place. Found this through Yelp and headed in.

Great food, beer and service. Very friendly and accommodating for our two large dogs.

Highly recommend. Thanks!

name: Springwater
text: Hog Heaven next door was not impressive at all and neither was this place. Its a super divey bar. Its also cash only....it's 2018....I don't want to spend $4.00 at the ATM to get a drink.

name: Springwater
text: Great beer bar dive with a shockingly good sandwich shop out back. Get a beer and let Bruno hook you up with the best Reuben in Nashville.

name: The Country
text:
I'm giving this one star because of the s***** attitude from the bartender. It was our first time there last night (Thursday.) Myself and 4 girlfriends met for drinks and sat on the patio. There may have been a total of 15 people there max--so they were not busy. He didn't say hello, didn't smile, and seemed put off when I asked if they had champagne (which was $10 a glass--too much) and he acted like it was a lot of trouble to tell me the seasonal beers on tap. No thank you after I paid and left him a tip that he didn't deserve either. He was also rude to my other 2 friends who ordered a drink. 

The place is gorgeous and it's a great patio so it was disappointing that the service was poor. 

Also, it stunk inside as if they mopped the floor with old, dirty water.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: I was so excited for the show last night, but the venue is so disappointing. Everyone was just crammed up to the stage, which is in the back corner. We made it close to the front, but there was no hope of making it back to our spot after a bar or bathroom run. So, we hung out near the back and we couldn't hear anything. The speakers do not fill the room. They are half way up the room, pointing towards the stage. I saw a handful of bar stools around the giant bar. Speaking of which, we never had to wait for longer than a few seconds to get a drink. So that was a plus. Also, there were plenty of restrooms. Another thing this place has going for it is close parking. We were lucky enough to find a free spot in the actual Mercy Lounge lot, but they have a pay lot that is in the same area. I don't usually mind to pay to park downtown to have to keep from walking in weird areas. Overall, I was so excited to see the band last night. I am a huge fan, but I just wasn't able to enjoy myself as the venue is such a bummer. I don't know that I will back to a show there, unless there is some kind of seating.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
The Belcourt is the best theater I've had the chance to participate in. Their Midnight Madness movies are exceptional in addition to the quirky new/obscure films they continually show. 
You better come to the Belcourt at least once if you want to experience Nashvegas.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
Incredible theater! They play all the best movies whether it be classics, the never-before-seen, and new indie flicks. 

Never before have I seen an entertainment venue such as this do such a spectacular job at preserving their history and going out of their way to educate and accommodate their guests. I've attended a few showings here (Boyhood, Rocky Horror, and Citizen Kane) and each had a speaker or some sort of film expert preface the showing so that we could really indulge ourselves in the experience. 

They strive for excellence and deliver nothing less. I hope to see the Belcourt thrive for many years to come.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: I'm in love with the velvet curtains and open space with a high ceiling.  It feels like I'm time traveling.  I've also found that the doormen and bartenders are very friendly.  I like exploring the city but have to admit I can't stop coming back here!

name: Commodore Grille
text:
The sangria was watery and tasteless, but at least it was only $10 a glass.

The waitress first informed me that "we don't have sangria here". When I informed her that it was red wine like merlot, fruit, and usually triple sec and/or brandy, she eventually brought me a water glass full of ice and a thin dark liquid that tasted faintly of fruit. The bill at the end of the night had an "open liquor" charge of $4 and a $6 "upcharge" for the sangria that the Grill refused to alter. The nachos had barbecue sauce! and service was poorer than average. What a joint.

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
Absolutely awful for brunch. Maybe better for night life, but they should stop trying at brunch. Which should be one of the easiest meals of the day?? We had 22 of us for a bachelorette party so called weeks in advance for a reservation at 10 when they open. Showed up at 10 after, and doors were still locked. Got a dirty look and an eye roll when we knocked. Had to call to have them open the door. Said we have a reservation, was told they dont taje reservations and we could "push these tables together" ourselves... 

ordered bottomless mimosas for almost the whole party, 2 of the pregnant ladies of the group ordered virgin bloody marys, the server first brought over single mimosas, after telling her that's not what we ordered, she then went to go make the virgin bloody Marys as we watch her pour vodka in a glass...  we tell her we need 2 virgin ones. She had her mind set that someone ordered a regular one as well? No one did.. food comes out, eggs Benedict was a hard boiled egg, 2 orders did not come out. Waitress takes her order again for an omelet with green peppers and sausage, everyone is done eating by the time that one comes out as an omelet with bacon and jalepenos and a runny egg center. This guest did not eat at all, but did enjoy the bottomless mimosas. 

We asked to talk to the manager who was the girl that was slamming food on the table and rolling her eyes as we were knocking to get in. Not friendly and blaming everyone else for the issues. Always saying "I'm sorry, but they didnt tell me about the reservation." "I'm sorry, but they dont tell me anything" "I'm sorry but I didnt have time to push the tables together." "I'm sorry but it's just me and the server today and it's her 3rd day"... take some responsibility. Look at your reservations for the next day you work before you leave for your shift.. put the tables together the night before or come in earlier.. have better training for NEW people. No, it's not the servers fault it was her 3rd day. Luckily she was super sweet despite getting a few orders wrong. 

Also asked to speak with the owner I think before we got our food to find out after we got our food that he left. He knew we wanted to speak with him, and left..  The most helpful person there was the chef's husband who came in to help(but doesnt work there) and actually listened to our concerns and who we had to get the rolled silverware from while we already had our food. 

Just absolutely awful, thank goodness for the bottomless mimosas and we still had a good time because of the ladies we were with. Definitely a memorable experience (not a good one, though) to many of our first trips to Nashville. Please do yourself a favor and go somewhere else for brunch. Pinewood Social was absolutely worth it and super cute place. Way better of a place to hang out.

name: Drifters
text: Super moist pulled chicken and several great sauces make for a very tasty meal ! Food 5 star, Service makes it 4 star.

name: Drifters
text: Love this place.  Dive bar but friendly and fun. BBQ is fantastic.  Out of brisket tonight though.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Awesome show, but have never been so hot at an indoor concert, everryone complaining, people left early.  Wasnt because of a sold out show, because it was unbearable when it was only half full. To me, the sign that the venue cares about the patrons is if the restrooms are taken care of.  This was not the case. A mess.

name: Drifters
text: Went in on a whim on a slow cold day and ended up staying for over 2 hours chatting with the staff and a couple of regulars. Could not have had a better time. Everyone was incredibly friendly, funny, helpful and laid back and the drinks were refreshingly well priced. The only food we got were the hush puppies but they were fantastic. Can't wait to get back. Kudos to Marie, Patty, Adam and Ben for such a great afternoon.

name: The Local
text:
I've been to some dives and Nashville and this place has beyond the absolute worst staff I've ever met in my entire life. 

When I addressed the issue of a transaction with the owner he accused me of making up the issue I was having along with trying to tell me it wasn't possible his rude bartender who was half asleep could have made a mistake. Not sure what happened but these guys tend to wake up on the wrong side of the bed. 

The issue the customer is always right, these guys don't seem to comprehend that. Good luck with that in this town.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Shows great movies. Prices a little high, 10$ for a medium drink and small popcorn. Seats also pretty small and close together. If you don't mind price and seats then it's great time to see great classic movies in a theatre setting with others.

name: Drifters
text: Nashville's version of Cheers! Everyone knew everyone and welcomed those that weren't regulars. Our bartender Marie was fantastic! She was right on top of what we wanted and suggested when we didn't know. Oh the tater tots are soooo good with all the dipping sauces ....yummm

name: The Local
text: Came in for lunch at around 2:30pm. Cute industrial/rustic interior. There is a stage for a live band, but we visited during the week at lunch and the jukebox played good country. Our service at first was great, however we encountered shift change and our food was brought by a new girl. And she never came back lol. I abandoned the idea of ordering a second drink, as it was empty before I even finished my meal. The food was good, quality was met with cheaper prices than in the downtown area. I had the cheeseburger and my boyfriend had the pork sandwich with sweet fries. This place is definitely more of a bar than a restaurant and I would recommend coming in for drinks rather than making it a dinner stop. I think that if we sat at the bar we would have had more attention.

name: EXIT/IN
text: I love this venue.  There are a lot of fancier and bigger places to see shows in the area, but this is just the right size for me.  It's no frills but nothing missing either.  The bar has a good selection and you can get to it quickly easily without missing any of the show.  There isn't a long wait for the bathrooms.  You can see the show really well from just about everywhere.  On top of all that the staff is really friendly.   I'm looking forward to seeing a lot more shows here in the future.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Great music venue, albeit on the smaller side. It gets crowded, which sucks for short people like me, but the acoustics make up for it.

name: Drifters
text:
Top notch rubs for ribs n chicken. Good service. No tough eating bbq meat...this is the kind you want- the soft yummy kind.  A zillion sauces to choose from and they explain
the sauces well too.

If I can say anything helpful, 
1. try to keep smokers away from the doors and windows so us sponsoring fans eating your delicious food dont have the smoke taste mingle with your AWESOME bbq taste. When i eat this stuff you make, its so good I want nothing to interfere with my enjoyment of it. This has become a religous experience for me.
