2. Try to anticipate demand for weekends and holidays because I came a few times when you ran out. Since your food is too damn good, I cried when I had to eat ??horsemeat?? somewhere else. I cant handle withdrawal from your food its so good I want a IV of it please? That includes your quesadilla.
3. Your service is fast and excellent. Keep up the soft meat and excellent taste...its paying off... your chicken isnt dry.... I know what good BBQ should taste like.  - the BBQ meister..... Ive been here 5 or 6 times allready...

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Take it from a local, who was raised in Nashville.  This bar has been absolutely cursed from the get go.  Frisky Frog's owners were crooks, and the new owner of "Live Oak" (Gavin/Brennan?) is absolutely clueless on how to operate a bar. He drives around on scooters all day, and is constantly drunk. Do yourself a favor, and stick to the staples, Tin Roof or Dawghouse!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: I've been to local movie houses in Atlanta and L.A.  and despite the reputation those towns hold as movie towns, the Belcourt outdoes the competition. It's due to the fact that their movie selection is bar none along with the pricing as well. Parking is amazing and so is their selection of concessions. I can't say enough about this theater and how it feels like home. I'll always go here instead of a corporate theater like AMC or Regal.

name: Drifters
text:
Beer selection: 4/5
Sauce: 5/5
Food: 4.5/5
Atmosphere: 5/5
Service: 5/5

Stopped here for lunch before shopping at Fatherland. We wound up finding parking on the street (for free) but the majority of the parking (lots) around here are pay lots. It's situated back from the main road a bit, behind another building, but there's a sign pointing you in the right direction and it looks like there's a few bars and restaurants right across the parking lot.

On Sundays all day they do bogo happy hour on beers... count me in. We both ordered BBQ platters and the bbq itself was so tasty, food came out fast, and I loved that it came with 3 sides (small sides, but I like variety). They have a sauce station to select your own, so we tried the Georgia, sweet & spicy, and New Mexico. All were super tasty with a nice kick, but I liked the sweet and spicy most, like I figured I would. 

The daily side of Mac and cheese was disappointing -- dry and not too flavorful, but slaw was nice and creamy and beans were tasty. 

Atmosphere is a cool dive bar vibe, and it looks like they have a little dog friendly patio situation, it just wasn't the right weather for it this weekend.

We'll be back!

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Best place in Nashville to see a local band or up and coming act. The venue has a great setup and the shows always sound great!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
The Belcourt Theatre is a true gem in Nashville. Showing great quality films that you won't see in every theatre around. The venue is clean, updated, generally great. Seating is traditional seating, no loungers, no recliners but seriously you are there to watch a movie, you can nap on your own sofa! 
Ticket process works so smoothly and they do give free parking vouchers of the Belcourt spaces with the ticket purchase. This is a popular area so parking spaces go quickly.   All the staff was very hospitable and professional.
Will be keeping an eye out for future films to view here!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Walked in with a friend who hadn't been here for twenty-five years. He said it's changed!  The theater is very nice. It's very updated, yet keeps its historic appeal. And the surprise is that the individual movie rooms have the decor of the era e.g., the 1925 room and the 1966 room. Several movies run on the same evenings. A concession counter provides the usual movie foods and adult beverages. The counter people are pleasant and informative about the venue. An elevator is available to see the art display upstairs and to enter the offices. This theater is a gem in the community.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
One of Nashville's gems.  Every time I see a movie at the Belcourt, I'm reminded of how lucky we are to have this special place as both a part of our history and a part of our daily lives.

I love the variety of films here, as well as the low prices and friendly, laid back staff (who know their stuff about the movies shown at the Belcourt, a huge perk).  I am also a patron of the Nashville Jewish Film Festival and get to experience how the theatre opens its arms to the films and events year after year.  The Belcourt is a one of a kind theater and a place where everyone - employees, customers and Nashvillians - feels happy and excited to be a part.

The only drawbacks to the theater are the parking (though the lot is quite large, it often fills up quickly during popular films), the tiny ladies room, and the expensive concession stand.  I can understand paying competitive prices for concessions, but $4 for a cup of drip coffee is a bit much.  Nevertheless, I will continue to frequent The Belcourt whenever I'm in the mood for an indie or art flick.  This place truly is a local gem.

name: Springwater
text:
Buford is gone.  Smoking inside is gone.
Cold cheap beer and good AC.

name: The Local
text:
A perfect spot for an after-work drink. Now that the weather is getting nicer, the outdoor patio is perfect. The Local is farely large, with a roomy interior and lots of outdoor seating as well. There are tons of beers on draft, and almost always a band playing.

Most recently, the space was being used for a benefit for Miss Amazing, a really great organization showcasing the beauty of girls with disabilities. Love that the Local supports such a great cause!

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
First off, the door staff is horrible and mean.. except for ONE security guy checking bags- he was a very polite, handsome black man. But hands down the most memorable person at the venue was an especially discourteous, scruffy looking white guy checking IDs like a junior high hall monitor who'd rather pull a girl's hair or make her cry rather than smile at her and was working the night of 10/7/18.  The guy clearly has an unchecked, undeserved power complex and seems to hate his job as much as he hates the patrons happily showing up to spend money at his place of work. Perhaps if he's so unhappy with his current position he should find gainful employment elsewhere, something in the lucrative Port-O-John industry or a sewage treatment facility would be more appropriate, that way excited concert goers aren't subjected to the wrath of his hyper-inflated, false sense of importance covering a crippling inferiority complex that's obviously made him physiologically incapable of human interaction that doesn't involve rudeness or blatant misogyny on display toward women in line that was consistently derogatory or belittling. His over the top rudeness has no place on Cannery Row or in Nashville. We have a courteous city and his poor attitude doesn't reflect that fact but diminishes it, and it probably makes other women extremely uncomfortable, and personally it ruined my entire evening with friends. No thanks to whoever hired this self loathing, woman hating, half premature ejaculate in human form, half bottom dwelling troglodyte getting his kicks by scowling at happy patrons from his post at the door and savoring the only power he'll ever have over what HAS TO BE his only opportunity to be near actual human females throughout the course of his pathetic daily life and the only women he will ever have the pleasure of disappointing in his small, anger-filled, micro-existence on this planet. 

The artist was fantastic, it's a shame I'll be seeing them elsewhere to avoid the a power hungry little impotent gatekeeper and ruiner of good times checking IDs. Unfortunately I missed his name, but who would ever want it anyways? No more shows for me at cannery for awhile.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
I've seen a handful of shows here. The staff is always wonderful, from the box office to the security. Depending on when you get there, parking can be pretty easy. If you're there just before the show starts, don't bother with the parking lot. Drinks are reasonably priced and they have a great pop up burger joint out front called Boutique Burgers. 

If you're in town visiting try and catch a show at any of the venues attached to it. You won't be disappointed.

name: Drifters
text:
While Drifters claims to be The BEST PATIO in Nashville it does not claim to be the BBQ in Nashville. 

The Patio is nice, the staff is friendly, the music is good.

The BBQ Is terrible. 

Maybe it was just a bad night, but I was all ready to enjoy "The Drifter", but instead I found a soggy bun covered by tasteless brisket and pulled pork. 
 
The nearby "Sweet and Sour" BBQ Sauce helped this somewhat, but I still felt like I was putting Ketchup on a bad Steak. 

All I can recommend here is the live music on the patio. I'd come back for that, but that's all.

name: The Local
text: Love the local vibe. Local musicians and song writers  this is probably one of my favorite spots in Nashville so far!

name: The Station Inn
text:
I'm an out-of-towner who dropped in for the Sunday Night Bluegrass Jam. Based on the crowd there, I don't think they really need one more 5-star review to draw more audience, but I'll give them one anyway.

The place was actually surprisingly comfortable - lots of chairs, cool, no unpleasant smells like some of the classic old-time venues have.

The music was excellent, and seemed to get even better as the evening went on and various musicians came and went. They were already jamming before 8:00 when I got there and didn't stop til after 11:00.

If you are really there to hear the music, I would recommend getting there early and finding a spot close to the musicians. There are no microphones for the bluegrass jam and with a lot of chatter in the audience, it is hard to hear the music if you are sitting halfway back or all the way in the back.

name: The Station Inn
text: Great atmosphere, great drinks and snacks. My favorite is the "thing of popcorn." We went in a Sunday night for the Bluegrass Jam. It was relaxing and fun. Everybody just piles in and enjoys the music and company.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Very cool set up. It is 3 floors with a different band playing on each floor. We sat on the top floor because it was the least crowded, our waiter was on top of everything, always asking if we wanted refills before we ran dry.

name: Famous Nashville
text:
What a gorgeous bar. The live music talent on Thursday night was seriously incredible. 

Reason for the rating: Since when do you serve 12 year old scotch in a plastic Dixie cup? For such an aesthetically appealing place, how in the world could that be how the owner would want customers to experience a "nicer" establishment? The orange slices on our $10 old fashioned's were so old that they were covered with a white "old bar fruit" slime. We found it completely bizarre but it is indicative of why the bars surrounding this one are packed to the brim with people while Famous had us and only us there. It was so awkward that we weren't quite sure how to leave without openly offending the workers. 

There's a reason you're not doing the business you feel your upscale bar should be doing... it's all in the details that aren't being executed by the bar staff.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Decent music and bar service.  Almost empty bar and stage which is odd for a bar this close to broadway, might have something to do with the horrible bouncers.  If you are sitting on the couches, please keep your feet on the floor vs tucked under your legs with boots on the seat, its HIGHLY frowned upon!!!

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Great venue. Acoustics are incredible here. For everyone complaining about the drink prices -- use your brain. The domestic beers are $11.00 for a 25 oz. beer and $13 for Import/Premium. Which means you're getting two beers at $5.50/6.50 a piece. Which is pretty average for any bar or venue on Broadway, especially a nice, new venue located directly on the water at the end of Broadway like Ascend. Were you expecting $5.00 tall boys? Let's be realistic with our expectations here, folks. 

I do agree with the coordination and logistics of some of the tents/food trucks though. I would imagine those are some of the kinks that will be worked out over time. 

The grounds are incredibly nice. I appreciate the security presence coming in. I do think the removing of your water bottle cap if purchased is a tad overboard. 

All in all, a wonderful venue.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: If you are looking for a great dive bar with a local Nashville flair, this one is work checking out. The servers are friendly and the beer is cold. Check out their events as they always seem to have something going on.

name: Famous Nashville
text: The lunch was excellent, drinks, chicken tenders and salad.! The music was two guitar players that were fantastic

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Three levels of bar and live music? I had a great time! When we went the second floor was closed for a private party, but we perused the packed first floor and the moderately packed third floor. The band was good, the drinks were reasonable- I'd go back, and I've already recommended to a friend who was in town visiting!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
One of the better and more lively bars on Broadway. It is at least 3 stories with some outdoor areas and balconies on the 2nd and 3rd floors. 

It's not the cleanest place, but it's downtown bar central so it's to be expected. 

Live music, gets rowdy on the weekends. Much calmer during the week. 

I think this places draws a younger crowd than some of the other bars in the area.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: On our first visit to Nashville we stopped at the Honky Tonk for a drink and we decided to stay a little longer because the vibe was great!! Tom Bridges and his band was playing and they incorporate the crowd like no other band I seen. It's great for all ages!! The bartenders are great. We spent a week in Nashville and we kept on going to this place because it was a great time no matter what day of the week.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Good music and a fun place. First time in. Big place. Lots of people. I for sure will be back.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
Bushwackers!
So, I was introduced to these at a BBQ place in Auburn, AL after a football game one Saturday. Alcoholic milkshake, basically. And on a hot Nashville day, who doesn't want that. Every time we saw a place that sold them, we stopped & got a couple to cool down. 

Also, I got mistaken for someone that worked there. A lady came in, on my way back from the rest room, and she stopped to ask if I mind if their party (at least 15 people) could push some tables together. I said sure & walked-off, didn't bother me any. Hope it didn't create any trouble:p

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Great dive bar feel with live music.  Going to The Stillery next door for dinner but the music pulled us in here first. Bartender was wonderful and the drinks were good.  If I lived in Nashville I would hang out here.

name: Alley Taps
text: Great bar!  Kinda speak-easy like!  Down an alley off the main street!  Great atmosphere and excellent service!  So happy we accidentally found this place!  Didn't try the food, but the bar service was beyond reproach!  Will definitely be back when we come to Nashville!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: The corner location and volume here draw the crowds, but the restroom attendants and urinals where your shoulders touch your neighbors' sent us on our way almost as soon as we entered. Much more of a 20-something college-town bar, hence the gimmicky, misleading name I suppose..

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We went in here to get some relief from the scorching temperatures outside and get some water. We sat near the back and ordered water. There was a man in the restroom handing out soap and paper towels for tips, which I find extremely annoying but paid him anyway because he's probably struggling. Our waitress came up and asked us if we wanted to order anything, but we told her we were fine. She then came up again and showed us the menu as if we had to purchase something even though the place wasn't nearly full at 11:00am on a Thursday. Finally, so she'd leave us alone, we ordered a Jack & Coke on her third attempt. It was in a 6 oz plastic cup and it cost us $10. This place is kind of a joke if you just want to get water and listen to music. Be ready to spend your money.

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: Really good place, but the property is going to be redeveloped soon. Go there quickly if you want to give it a try.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This was one of the recommended places to go to in Nashville.  It is a great time: 3 floors of bands, bars, dancing, fun. With that said, it definitely gets crowded.  We went here on a Sat night, and it was packed on all floors. 

The girl's bathrooms were filthy esp by the end of the night (you know what kind of filth).  The bands they had were great and got people to dance.  I was a little scared for my life bc when we were on the 2nd and 3rd floors' dance area, the floor shook when someone jumped much more when everyone was jumping.  It's probably the norm here.  Also be careful of the balcony.

It took awhile to get drinks.  I was just glad they had my sweet tea vodka and unlike any other bars in other states, I didn't get a strange look for it.  I would recommend to go if it's your first time, but be warned if you care about sticky floors and tables and bathrooms.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Super fun place with GREAT music!  Server Chris was so awesome!  Nice and super attentive!  Love this place!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: They had the Warriors game on!! Winning in Nashville. :) drinks were reasonable and you can't beat 3 stories.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great place to go listen to music. Three levels of bars with each level having a different love band. Prices on beer is pricey at 4.00 a bottle for bud light. I would go back again.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Stop here every time in Nashville. Whoever is playing here is better than the last. Little dive bar away from the chaos of Broadway

name: Nashville Underground
text:
I am rating as a 3 star only for the fact that our service was horrible (see below for reason). As for the atmosphere and the food they were great. We sat on the roof top (up the stairs after elevator ride) and had the chicken sliders with Nashville fries and they were so good. I would definitely go back again and hopefully will get better service. 

As for the service we went to have brunch with friends (roughly 13) and it took a little bit to get our orders in which is understandable, but after we ordered my girlfriend never got her first drink and we were completely done eating before the waitress came back to ask if we wanted another round. We let her know she never brought the first out more than once and we ended up getting one beer after 2hrs. When we went to get our check she had rung up 3 beers on our check (which she took off after we reminded her she only brought one). Hopefully our next time will be a better experience.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Two words: Pokémon and Symphony. My childhood loves came together tonight at Ascend Amphitheater in beautiful harmony. The venue was clean, organized and the staff were helpful and friendly. The sound and lights were top notch and so was the reserved seating. Concessions were a little pricey but I had Ben and Jerry's for $8 which really wasn't too bad. This was my first time at the venue and I'll be returning.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Disgraceful place. 
Ordered a vodka by 215 am, was obliged to throw it by 2:30 am.. the place closes by 2:30 instead of 3 am.. be aware. Bouncers and servers have the worst attitude. Our party got several drinks vodka, whiskey and rum, bad quality all of them..

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: No drink specials,  but a wonderful atmosphere and an extremely talented live band.  I wouldn't mind paying so much for drinks if the band got a cut,  but you are supposed to tip them on top of drinks. Pricy,  but a good time and seemingly a staple of Nashville. I loved loved loved the songs the bands played. Very hot country songs.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Three floors of bands and bars.  It is a destination.  If you don't like the bar or band where you are, go up or down a floor.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Close to our hotel, so fun and packed with great people and wonderful music. My friend attempted to sing on stage every night we went :)

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: If you visit only one place on Broadway, make it this one! The service is amazing in spite (despite?) the crowds. Everyone was super friendly; sharing tables due the size of the crowd was fun. The music was outstanding and really made you feel like you were in the middle of the C&W experience. This is a gem and not to be missed.

name: The Station Inn
text: One of the most authentic-feeling places I've ever spent time in. The vibe is true Bluegrass. I used to go to the jams on Sunday's all the time. Amazing. Space is limited so get there early, and the only food they have is popcorn and pizza.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: I love live music, I absolutely love Nashville. This place is awesome they have live music all the time (THE MUSIC IS GREAT) and they also have raspberry WOODCHUCK CIDER on tap, that's like finding a tugboat at the airport. The staff is great and friendly

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Not bad for bar fare.  You really go for the atmosphere anyway.  Will say though, the wait staff leaves a lot to be desired.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: 3 floors of live music...shoulder to shoulder..if you can handle the crowd, this is a great place. Very cool to look out over the patios here down over broadway.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: This was one of our favorite places on a recent girls trip to Nashville. Great venue for live music. We went on a Sunday night when they air the show live for radio. A local recommended it to us when we said we wanted to hear good bands playing their own music. Sean McConnel was main act the night we were there and did not disappoint.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
We dropped in here during a recent trip to Nashville.  What an awesome place to drink a few Beers and listen to music.  I know there's 100's of these joints around town, but this was around the corner from our hotel and was a ton of fun.  There were multiple levels, I think at least 3 maybe 4, I can't remember exactly.  The band on the main floor was a ton of fun.

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ZhA88ILcgEP9DNwZDx7f0A?select=So23CpKLJ7aYIlj3Bwxrfg#So23CpKLJ7aYIlj3Bwxrfg
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ZhA88ILcgEP9DNwZDx7f0A?select=OYjeqpbup17ahf9Z1DullQ#OYjeqpbup17ahf9Z1DullQ

The girl playing the Violin was awesome.  She jammed and had the place on their feet all night long.  It's too bad I can't remember the name of the band....funny thing is that one of the guys in the band playing the night we were here was playing at one of the bars in the airport when we left the next day...awesome, that's why I love Nashville.

Return Factor - 80%

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: First time to visit this place. Very impressive atmosphere with great service, music, and food! Definitely would recommend this venue to anyone who visits or lives here!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Bartender heather was horrible!!  No smile slow service!  You can look good behind the bar but service should match!!!! 
Live music was nice but didn't say because of service!! Two thumbs down!!!!

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Very nice, new venue.  Staff was super polite, as was security.  Plenty of (expensive) food and beverage options.  We were seated promptly for our show (Flight of the Conchords).

The seating seems to be severely flawed however.  The stage is so high up, that sitting close isn't really worth it.  The act generally sits 6-8 feet back on the stage, and the seats begin about 6-8 feet FROM the stage.  We sat in the third row, and it felt like sitting in the 13th row.  We could only see the top half of the act.  Felt like the stage should be lower, and the seating more on an incline.

With the venue being outdoors, if you aren't in the first 4 or so rows and it rains, you're gonna get soaked.  It started getting really windy during our show, and all the cloth covers on stage were blowing wildly (revealing all the techs and computers working the magic), as were the speakers hung with cables above our heads.  I trust the engineering to a point, but I must say I was pretty nervous as the GIGANTIC speakers were swaying about 20 feet above my head.

It's a decent venue - nice because it's new, but lame because it's an outdoor  stage with a lawn and folding chairs.  Would much rather see a show at the Ryman, TPAC, or even the Bridgestone Arena.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: One of the main bars on Broadway where they have 3 floors and 3 different bands playing. The bar gets VERY overcrowded and mainly had a very young crowd. The beer selection had regular beers, nothing crafty. The bathroom lines are also a nightmare. It was fun to pass by just to say you went to Honkey Tonk Central, but definitely keep it moving to the next bar if you want to avoid amateur hour with all of the 21 year olds.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: I want to give you 5 stars but tonight was so much different than before.  We always get really prompt service and tonight we saw so many tables with food and we didn't get our food till show started and we were the 5th group in the door!!! The music was awesome.  When I return I will probably eat at home and sit in balcony.  This was my first time sitting in lower area and I did not find it enjoyable.  Our waitress was either under trained or over booked with tables. It took forever to get in our food order and the almost an hour to get our food.  That is not our previous experience!  If I had dinner I might not be upset but since I waited a. hour to be there when doors opened at 6pm I assumed I would be served promptly. All our other times this has been the experience so I don't know if it is where I sat or who served us. I enjoyed the music so much.  I would have enjoyed it much more with some food.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: This is an ok place to hear music, but it's so incredibly hot and uncomfortable. I find it pretty insulating to your guests when you know you have a problem- which our waitress acknowledged at the beginning of our evening- and choose to do nothing about it.  Seating is extremely limited at this place anyway, but if you want to stay under 90 degrees, do NOT sit upstairs. The whole place is under air conditioned, but upstairs is a sauna. Also if you don't get there as the doors open, they won't even have a bar stool available for you.  They move them all away so you have to stand through the show.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place is really depraved. This is the worst broadway bar. It is jammed pack and sometimes it is dangerous on the third floor. I watched some american idol person here and it wasn't that good.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place simply blew my mind. 3 stories tall and live music on every level. Had a great time, next time in Nashville, I'll be back!!!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
I'm giving this place 5 stars because as a music venue its quite possibly one of my top 3 places for seeing a show, especially since the place underwent a drastic makeover since my first time checking it out.  It has amazing acoustics, lots of seating, and an overall ambience of just plain awesome.  

My one caveat here is that the food, while good, won't really blow your mind.  It's bar food people, and that's ok.  It's good for bar food as well.  Sandwiches and appetizers, which is really all you need when your focus is on a concert.  And it may take you a while to get your food, and your drinks, if you are fortunate enough to snag a table for a Sunday night show (Lightning 100 puts on Nashville Sunday Nights Live at 3rd and Lindsley every Sunday, with some great up and comers and local favorites...doors open at 6pm, shows at 8pm, so if you want a seat, COME EARLY).  At my last visit I noticed each server had a very large section to take care of, so keep this in mind when ordering.  They bust their butts, so give them some patience.

But onto why you come to this essential Nashville establishment...THE MUSIC.  Oh my GOD the amazing music, and it's so intimate in here.  It's like being totally immersed in the whole musical experience.  It's so much fun.

Your best option is to come early, get dinner, have drinks, and wait for the show.  Bring friends.  Check out an artist you may never have heard of because someday when they play Bridgestone Arena you're going to be happy you did.  Again, it fills up in here quickly, and parking is pretty limited at the place itself, so be ready to walk from the surrounding streets.  It's not expensive at all for a night out here (tickets are usually around $10, and the entrees on the menu are about the same).

I have only ever been here for shows so I'm not sure what it's like on a regular music-free night, but for all the shows I've been to here I've had a great time, and I will continue to come here and check out whatever performers they have.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Enjoyed honky tonk the location was great the music was both both in the day and later in that night. The bad at night was phenomenal the definitely were crowd pleaders. The food was a bit to over fried and bland for my liking. Next time I'll stick to beer and liquor and enjoy the show.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Sweet spot, beautiful interior, and excellent vibe.  Live music was kickin' and the bar tenders were super friendly.  One is now, actually, the mother of my child.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Restrooms suck. Has nothing to do with the lady in the restroom. HTC has not been keeping up with their stalls, they do not lock and I did not have a place to put my bag. Also the crowd is not so clean in the restroom they think it someone else's prob.  If a place is not keeping up with their restrooms, what else are they missing.

name: Nashville Underground
text: This place was recommended for their burgers and I was excited to get one!  Salty, I mean saltier than the ocean!!!  I ate 2 bites thinking maybe I got a pocket of seasoning but that wasn't the case.  They took it off the bill, which was appreciated, but certainly wouldn't recommend getting burgers here

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
We had time for just a few songs (and drinks) on Broadway before heading over to Monnel's to stuff ourselves silly and ended up at Honky Tonk Central due to there being enough room without having to wait in a line. 

We could easily tell upon entering that this bar catered to the out-of-town crowd. Hints: the layout, a half dozen bachelorette parties sprawling throughout the three floors of the bar and the general "lets get shitfaced" vibe.  We found a perch at the bar and ordered our drinks - ginger and Jameson and a Bloody Mary. Yes, it was 5 p.m. and yes, I wanted a Bloody Mary. Yes, the bartender could have looked at me a little less like I had two heads. The drinks were standard - nothing to write home about yet no complaints. Unfortunately, we must have arrived at a bad time on the schedule because live music was only playing for about 50% of the time we were there - est. 1.5 hours. 

Lucky for us, the remaining 50% of the time was filled with a drunken shitshow of a fella from Columbus, Ohio who seemed to take a great interest in my boyfriend and me. Visual: fairly sober us trapped by spitting, red-cheeked, and offensive him. The bar probably should have cut him off. Don't get me wrong. I am down to get down, it's just that in between making offensive statements he probably could have wet himself without thinking twice about it.

In conclusion, great bar for your standard tourist-style Nashville visit. Sometimes all you want is a vodka cranberry, glittery cowboy boots and drunk cohorts.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Great place to see a show!  I have been several times, and always had an amazing listening experience.  Will be going back for more!

The salad I had was very average, so I won't be ordering food here again, unless maybe to try a sandwich or something.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Awful got kicked out for no reason had multiple witnesses that said I did nothing and the security still kicked me out will not go to that place again  way to go guys  have fun with the person that actually threw something off the balcony that will  probably cause  an issue in the future you just lost a customer

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: This was the first bar we stopped at after landing in Nashville on Friday afternoon. We were greeted with a friendly bartender and 2 amazing live singers. Food was bar food, but was good! Drinks were super cheap!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great atmosphere and view from third floor. Menu was kind of limited and drinks were pricey. Music was good with different live bands on each floor.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great service and the guys performing live music were great. Ranch dressing was also good. Very pleased

name: Nashville Underground
text: Fun place to be during CMA Fest. Went for drinks and to hang out on the rooftop bar. It was very nice. Loved that they have self serve water. I heard there was a bathroom attendant which is cool. We played cornhole up on the roof. Wish we tried some food.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Incorrect information.  This place closes at midnight.  We were very excited to visit but unfortunately came to a closed establishment.  For all of the fun that Broadway offers until 2-3 AM, it is not worth it to head here.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: My co-workers and I went for lunch and this was the worst dining experience I think I have ever experienced. We arrived about 11:50am and did not get our food until almost 1:00pm. There were several people who arrived after we did but received their food, paid their tab, and left before we even received our food. Customer service was very poor. We were basically ignored and had to wave down one of the waiters who still did not come over when asked. She told us to hold on but started clearing tables around us rather than assist customers. The floor manager came over and basically told us some BS about them being busy and all the orders went in at once even though we were there before several people and our order was already taken and in the kitchen however, those that arrived after us received their food before we did. Then the kitchen manager came over and said "can I help you" ugh sir who are you!?!? He just walks up to our table and don't even introduce himself or nothing. Then he explains that I don't know if they told you but they brung the wrong order out. Really? So I guess they continued bringing the wrong order to everybody else. We didn't order steaks or anything. We had wrap, sandwich. And quesadilla. It does not take long to prepare those things. And on top of all that, the waiter never came back to give us refills or anything. Just poor terrible service. I'll never go back!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: My favorite bar on Broadway! Three stories with a different band on each gives you plenty of room to spread out and still enjoy live music. I also liked how much open air space you get to keep the place from getting too overheated. Great drink specials and an overall good Broadway honky tonk experience

name: The Cowan
text: Saw a great show at the Cowan but very disappointed by the VIP tickets I purchased - not worth the money. The show was better seen on the main floor. That being said, if you don't get there early enough (we arrived 45 minutes before the VIP doors opened) people reserve stools sitting against the balcony railing making it hard to see the show if you don't score a stool for you and those in your party. They advertise a separate bar for the VIP or balcony section but I didn't see the advantage to it. Overall, if you want to see the show and don't want to run the risk of not getting a front row balcony stool, I would suggest you save the money, purchase floor tickets and use your savings to buy yourself a couple drinks.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Okay service. Day band okay but entertaining. The people watching was the best. I get it they all work for tips.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
It was mid July and pretty hot. It also just rained so it was also pretty humid. The sign read cold beer and I could feel the a/c as the door opened and I stood outside. I was sold and went in.

A pint of craft beer was $6 (expected). Service was okay but awkwardly slow for not being busy. A guy behind the bar walked by me no joke 6 times while I stood there with my card without acknowledging me. There was a pitcher of water on the bar with cups so I can't complain that much, I pounded about 3 of those as I attemped to regulate my body temp and stop the intense sweating the TN weather brought on.

The live music was decent. Plenty of seating. The food that came out didn't look great, I wouldn't eat here. Grab a beer and cool off if you feel like you have to be on Broadway Street. I personally would rather get kicked in the face over spending much time in this area.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: 2 bottles of Miller lite 15 dollars (hope that includes her tip) plus having to wait while the bartender waited on every one around us and still having to get her attention they need a negative star rating won't ever come here again

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
If your a true music fan and go to Nashville, 3rd and Lindsely is paradise. We saw Vince Gill perform here with his Western Swing band for fifteen bucks! He came thru Chicago where we live a few months later and tix were $60! 
Top Nashville talent plays here, you never know who is going to drop by.
Cheers
Danno

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great bar for mid day music and drinks! Staff is quick and friendly! Only issue is the restrooms, could be a like for a mile! But I would highly recommend  this place anytime of the day to be honest! The blackberry moonshine gets you! :)

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Pretty awesome bar! Great music and service. My sister got called up on stage which was hilarious!! Definitely recommend stopping here if you go come to Nashville!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Music played by experts. Thought we'd stay for a while and then book. We ended up staying the night and wanting more. Now we have a place to hang out on Monday. Well worth the $20 to get in.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Still the best music value anywhere! If you go on any Monday to see the Time Jumpers - all superb musicians - be sure to get there early to get a seat. And only $20! We were fortunate this visit to have the guy at the door ask "you wanna sit down front?" (Wait, it that a trick question???) He led us to a table right against the stage to share a table with a lovely couple from Indiana who'd been in line since 3:30...we felt a little guilty but that quickly passed. Vince Gill is the most recognizable performer, but he's just one of the boys in this group of studio musicians. If you aren't really a fan of excellent western swing/country music when you arrive, you will be a convert before you leave...good drink prices and variety might help lubricate your attitude. Selfishly, I'd like to keep this little gem a secret, but how can one not openly proclaim wonderfullness!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Great food and service! This place is really big and you can get food on any floor plus it wasn't very crowded for a game day! The food was delicious and it was reasonably priced! We will definitely be back!!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Thought this was a good place once upon a time but this time around the entertainer was talking and cussing at customers more than singing. Shut up and sing Isaac!! And you know what?? He wasn't even that good and the mic was wayyyyy too loud. Distortion loud. It was very off putting. And apparently anyone with an unfavorable opinion will get harassed from the business. Pathetic. Not recommended

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Went to this place with friends during a weekend in Nashville. It has three floors with live music on each, and patios surrounding the area (which is great if you want to get away from the smoke that pervades most bars in the area). There were about a million bachelor and bachelorette parties, and not much selection for beers. That said, we had a great time - lots of fun music and happy crowd.

name: Nashville Party Authority
text: We used Blair, with Nashville Party Authority, to DJ our wedding reception in July at the Hermitage Hotel.  Blair was simply AMAZING!  He was a true professional, from the very first meeting, to the very last song.  We only gave him our first dance song, and mother/son and father/daughter dance songs, and he chose the rest!  He said he reads the crowd, and plays songs accordingly.  And that he did!  We had a very small reception, with 60 people, and EVERY SINGLE PERSON danced ALL night long!  Countless people, including my Mom (the Mother of the Bride!  You know how picky they can be!), came up to me all night and said he was the best DJ they had ever seen.  He helped to make our wedding reception absolutely perfect.  It was a dream of a night.  Blair was such a pleasure, offered great prices, top notch service, and I would recommend him without the slightest bit of hesitation.  Blair, THANK YOU!  You were amazing!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Last night we had tickets to see The Mavericks AFTER 2 reschedules.  I don't know if this venue oversold this event or what, but there were only 20 tables (if that many). We got there before the doors opened and there were a 100 or more people standing not able to get a drink or something to eat.  There was a smaller balcony in the corner but we were told that was for the band.  There were so many angry people leaving and getting their refund, but the management didn't seem to care that there were unhappy people.  I won't return, I don't care who is playing.

name: The Station Inn
text: Went here twice over the weekend, one Friday and one Sunday night. Fri heard the Tennessee Mafia Jug band, Sun was a big bluegrass jam that a friend played in. This is not a hoity-toity place. You get pizza, popcorn, or beer and that's pretty much it (well, there are some assorted packaged snacks and soda). The lack of options is somewhat refreshing. Place is something of a holdout in a built-up modern neighborhood. Relax and enjoy the music, that's what this place is all about!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Excellent spot to listen to some live country music!  Tater tots with chill and cheese were really good.  Only downfall is that it can get a little crowded

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
awesome place and we love it!!!

http://watchonlinevideos.org/dailymotion.php

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
One of the best places to listen to music in Music City! 
The revamped room has tables and standing room, with not a bad seat in the place. 
I highly recommend the Sunday night shows, sponsored by Lightning 100, but you'll want to get there early and have dinner to get a good spot. 
Edibles include sandwiches, burgers, wings- your typical bar food. Nothing terribly fancy, but you can also find a salad or fish dish if you're eating healthy.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Love this venue. We came here tonight for the first time and we were so happy. The service was great, there is seating upstairs and downstairs (upstairs has a better view of the stage) - there is also a section for those who want to stand in front of the stage. 

While waiting for our show to start, we decided to order dinner. I ordered a burger and salad and my boyfriend had fish and chips. Unfortunately, the food wasn't that great. Salad was pretty much lettuce and a ton of bacon bits. Although we weren't fans of the food, our waitress was awesome and always checking on us to make sure we were taken care of. 

We plan on coming here again. The staff was great and the venue wasn't huge so you could really enjoy the music you were listening to. Highly recommend checking out a show here!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Great find for live music in Nashville. The only difficulty was finding the place, since it was dark and in a fairly industrial part of town. Bobby Long was playing live that night and couldn't have enjoyed it more. What a great live music spot with ample seating!

name: Famous Nashville
text:
Saw the good Yelp review and that it was "Off Broadway" so tried it. Glad I did. Was Thursday afternoon so not crowded. Just wanted good burger and good music and got both. Oh, and great friendly service from Shannon (think that was her name). Ordered blue cheese burger. You know there burger is good when they ask how you want it cooked!  It was hot juicy and delicious!! And the fries were those thin kind I like and were served hot. 

Solo singer was Nashville good but only got to hear a couple of songs before he was done. Duo act that followed was just ok I thought (wished I'd gotten there earlier). 

Shannon checked on me often (maybe too much but rather more than ignored)

name: Nashville Underground
text:
My party stopped here during our Sprocket Rocket Party Bike tour.  We got the sprocket spot as recommended by our driver.  Please save yourself some money and do NOT buy this shot.  It was disgusting and thick like cough syrup.  It tasted like melted red jolly ranchers.
NOPE.

name: The Station Inn
text:
Great towny cute spot. Wildly talented bluegrass artists perform here. They offer vigorously buttered and salted popcorn and beers. 

They are weird about running cards, but hey at least they take cards at all. I didn't mind too much.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Honkey Tonk Central was a very fun atmosphere, the band was singing current country hits and they took song requests for tips. I must say, my group was disappointed with the service, they were not attentive at all. The drinks were also very overpriced. You can find the same menu items for cheaper all along Broadway. Rock on, Nashville, TN

name: Alley Taps
text:
This place was such a gem to find!!! Broadway was way too crazy for my taste, and a Lyft driver had mentioned that his friend's band was playing here that night. I'm so happy to have stumbled in. The music was fantastic (Just Whiskey), the drinks were flowing and the ambiance is cozy. What I really love about this bar is that the front part of the bar has no TVs, while the large back room does. So it seems like a great place to hang out and watch sports with a crew, or have a more intimate drink with a friend or date.

The bartenders were spectacular, they have specialty coffee drinks, and an excellent beer list. Just the perfect bar!

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Ascend is a nice facility in a nice location, with good bands, BUT "SECURITY" IS INVASIVE & possibly illegal.  They opened my wallet & fondled the contents... two different employees at the same show. 

1.  At the entry gate, gate screener didn't just search my bag.  She took everything out and opened every container inside, including my WALLET!  Yes!  She put her grubby unbonded hands inside & moved my money, credit cards, etc. around.  I had done nothing wrong, unless you count buying a ticket to the event.  It was an unnecessary invasion of privacy!  Even police are not allowed to open a person's wallet without consent, and these gate workers are NOT cops!  STAY OUT OF MY WALLET!  

2.  During the show, a man sitting next to me was smoking.  Rather than directing him to the smoking area, which is what should have happened, they made him stand up & empty his pockets, then patted him down.  When they didn't find anything on him, they ordered me to hand my bag over to be searched AGAIN because the stupid kid rent-a cop thought we were together when we were not!  Kid stood right in front of me so that I couldn't see the show & shined a bright flashlight in my face as he opened everything in my bag AGAIN, my wallet AGAIN, and when he didn't find whatever it was he was looking for, he told me I was under surveillance & threw my bag back at me & my stuff fell all over the ground.  I had no flashlight to find everything, but luckily my neighbors helped me gather my things & put them back in my bag. 

This place has always has eerily strict security, but is now a full-blown police state manned by wanna-be cops who have obviously been empowered by management to perform illegal searches while treating people like crap.  Innocent people, btw.  I did NOTHING but buy a ticket.  I followed all their rules & still had my wallet taken out of my bag & ransacked twice at one show.  I will NEVER NEVER N.E.V.E.R. be back & am going to let everyone in my many music-related forums know that Ascend is NOT the place to see jam & rock bands!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I've never been kicked out of a bar!! I only had 2 drinks and was not drunk. Went into the stall with my beer bottle because I didn't want to leave my beer at the bar unattended and get roofied! While I was peeing the bathroom attendant started screaming that I was going to be kicked out due to bringing a beer bottle into my stall. When I came out of my stall she wouldn't even give me soap, just insisted that I be escorted out. Seriously?! After a beer bottle into the bathroom stall?? (No I didn't
shatter it or anything) A gentle reminder of your policy would've been sufficient. Completely unprofessional bathroom attendant and then security.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: This venue is very nice with not any bad seats and a beautiful view of the Nashville skyline.  The women's bathroom was plentiful of stalls and therefore the wait very short.  The big negative I and the group I was with saw was that it needs to be no smoking, or at LEAST have a designated smoking area.  Come on, this IS 2015.  It really was a downer to sit next to a family of smokers (nicotine AND marijuana) while trying to enjoy Earth Wind & Fire/ Chicago.  Not only did it stink but we did not feel good about breathing in all those carcinogens.  I would give it four or maybe 5 stars if something is done about the smoking issue.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This bar is a joke. They treat their guests with their thuggy security thugs like criminals. The security staff is rude abusive and just downright rotten to the core customer service wise. I was with a group small one of 4 people two of them went on the dance floor and the other person went to go get them and we were about to leave when all of sudden by accident I close my eyes but not because I was drunk I was 110% sober. In fact I was so sober then there was more people in the bar that they should have focused on throwing their ass out instead of mine. When asked or told this is wrong going down the elevator the supervisor or what not in a blue shirt with a stupid buzz cut and about five seven and height told me to shut up. What a jerk. You don't tell guests to shut up when asking a simple question as to why you're being kicked out when you've done nothing wrong. They also did not care that I was the only source of a ride home for a young girl legal age of course to get home an hour and a half away which is why I close my eyes because I did not want to go to the stupid bar to begin with but after the way I was treated I will not be going to this stupid Honky Tonk at all. You guys might want to fire your head of security or your security company for allowing their engines and themselves to treat your guests like common criminals in their Thug Like manner. I wish I could give this place zero stars because that's really what you guys deserve. I hope you go out of business. Have a nice day

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Love it. Stayed here for pretty much 30 hours this past weekend when my best friend and I spent a weekend in Nashville. It is super touristy, but as a tourist it was just what I wanted to do when I went to Nashville. 

Live music on every level, windows open letting in warm air, and a friendly crowd looking to have a good time and enjoy themselves. We found that our favorite level was the third because it seemed to be less crowded than the other two. I love it and will definitely spend just as much time here on my next trip back to Nashville!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: A few years ago this place was great, but since the boom in Nashville the staff is absolutely terrible. Incredibly rude and treats you horribly. If you can avoid this place, do. They act pretentious and you don't have the true Nashville experience here.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
5 STARS! When ended up doing the backstage show that they offered during the middle of a Saturday. The song writers were great and even featured one who wrote a few George strait tunes. We loved the seating and the feel on the inside as it really made you feel backstage and really close to the artists. The stories that they told about the song writing was really cool and they all perform their songs. 

When we first walked in we were greeted with a shot of Fireball, free on the house, which was pretty cool and really got the vibe going. I would have to say that if we ever come back or have friends visiting Nashville we will we will highly recommend them booking this backstage show opportunity. They have food available as well but we did not order.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Was enjoying a long weekend in Nashville.... until we came here! Rude staff, especially the bouncer(gave me a real hassle). My drink was decent at best, the only thing they've got going for them is the name and the music. Otherwise I would not waste your money here. Don't even get me started on the rats!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: A must visit when coming to Nashville and for anyone who appreciates American music and its history. They have an amazing collection of memorabilia. The stories associated with Cash's personal items were very interesting. A++

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Food was horrible, entertainment was like a bad cruise ship performance. This was a Thanksgiving dinner cruise and the meal was not what I consider traditional Thanksgiving. The servers did do a pretty good job.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
The Johnny Cash museum is everything a Cash fan could ask for. The exhibits covers 100 percent of his life and give an in depth look into the Man in Black. The items on display give such an intimate look that you couldn't find anywhere else. I am in debt to the Miller's for bringing this museum to fruition giving me something that I could appreciate this much.

If you are a Johnny Cash fan this is a must do on your bucket list!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Terrible management. 2 times trying to come in we have been treated very poorly. One time we tried coming in at 11pm because the door was still open and the nba finals were on and they very rudely told us they were closed from the table they were all sitting at chatting. From my experience working you are not closed until you lock the door and if you are you apologize not rudely reject people. Then the next time the manager and girl at the front door were not friendly at all! We didn't realize we needed tickets because the sign was posted on the front door who I was covered by people waiting in line so we waited in line for a long time in the wrong line. And they made it seem like it was our fault. After that I suggested they post the notice about the lines elsewhere where it could be seen and the girl completely ignored me and did not apologize. Also someone in our party asked if they could use the bathroom because we were at the front of the line (the wrong one before they sent us to stand in the correct line) and they refused even when she offered to leave her cell phone at the front desk. This was just terrible service. There are so many places to go in Nashville stay away from this one! You will be much happier! Take it from us! The only good thing is the singer's are very talented

name: 360 Burger
text: Yup. They got BEEF, and some good one at that! Now it is located in a dead-beat strip mall but that means PLENTY of parking for us burger freaks! When u walk in its got this whole Western motif goin on with the rustic wooden walls n furniture and bar and all. I have NO idea why its called 360. Our server was very efficient and helped me decide on the mushroom Swiss and my cousin on the avocado one. The fries were very unimpressive but thier bun was ON POINT and once u get all up in that beef patty, u know that cow was alive a few hours ago. It's fresh all right! I liked my burger though my cuzzo was a tad bit unmoved by the entire dining experience. He says M.L Rose is better, but I think 360 got it going on, even more so than M.L Rose AND Burger up. No fancy gimmicks like stupid truffle fries. Just got ole fashioned American Cheeseburgers!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: You don't have to be a Johnny Cash fan to truly enjoy this museum. There is a lot of history here and it was actually more informative than I expected. We came early in the afternoon and while we were finishing our visit, we noticed that it got very crowded, so I would definitely recommend coming as early as possible. Overall this was time and money well spent.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Had a blast here when I visited in march!  Honestly we just chose this bar cuz it was freezing rain outside and since we were a bachelorette party we cut the line and got in asap.  But this bar was such a blast!  My friends crushed a couple rounds of pickle back shots and loved them.  I had a couple peach moonshine shots and I wish I had a bottle of that stuff.  Staff was attentive and forgiving of the intoxicated crowd.  Bathroom was disgusting (wet, sticky, and no TP, and only one stall.)  But that was all forgotten by the amazing live  band that rocked the house and got everybody dancing.  The main singer had an amazing voice & vocal range, and did a great variety of music (loved hearing some alt rock in nash!  Sorry not sorry I'm not a country music fan.)  Honestly she even made a country music song feel good.  The crowd ranged from a young lad out for his 21st bday to grandparents and everything in between.  A very comfortable environment.  The sort of place you'd be comfortable checking out solo or with a group.  Yes it was crowded but when I pictured partying in Nash this was the the scene I imagined.  There isnt much great live music in my home town and I really enjoyed my night at swinging doors.

name: The Basement East
text: Great live music addition to the east side. I went in back to back evenings this spring and saw a fantastic Prince tribute on a Friday and an amazing Allman Brothers cover band on a Saturday. The crowds were light, presumably because it was Bonnaroo weekend, but the space has nice high ceilings and seems like it could handle crowds nicely. Awesome selection of beers on tap and the bartenders were knowledgable and friendly.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This place was awesome! I love Johnny Cash but I love him now even more after having learned somethings about him I didnt know before.  Like how much of a humanitarian, activist and renaissance man he was all in all.  I enjoyed alot of the personal mementos of his, notes, the ad he took out on billboard asking why the radio programmers were not playing the ballad of Ira Hayes, the family crest he drew himself, I mean really this place is super cool.    The museum shop was ok but you know they even have original pressing vinyl of the man black himself, so if you are a collector well you can yours there!....for about $250...

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I love museums.  Im a fan of country music so of course when I heard there was a Johnny Cash museum I had to check it out.  The museum is small but it was well worth it.  You can listen to some of his music and check out the memorabilia they have on display.  There is a lot to know about Johnny Cash and this is the place to check it out.

name: The Basement East
text: Great place for brunch on Sunday's! Super relaxed, great music, great service. We will definitely be back. Food was delicious, the portobello mushrooms were amazing, along with the mimosas. Mallory and Alex were great, very attentive and personable.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: The wax figures will definitely amaze you. They are so detailed, you would think they were actually real human beings. Trust me, it's fascinating. A must see.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I can't say if it's always as good of an experience as we had, but we had the best time! I wasn't sure what cocktail to order so they helped me come up with something special to order for me. I had the cheeseburger & fries which were very tasty. But nothing compares to the experience. Baylor Wilson & friends were performing when we went and they were AMAZING. Loved our time here. So amazing. The talent was unbelievable

name: 360 Burger
text: I'm really really bummed. I went to call and place an order for my favorite salmon burger on a pretzel buns with waffle fries and was going to get some honey wings too, after a killer workout. The guy on the phone informed me that they've changed their entire menu and I'd have to go look online to find it. My fiancé was leaving from a meeting and was going to just stop in and pick it up for me as a treat...but I couldn't find one single thing either familiar or delicious sounding. Not one appealing thing. It all sounds like really greasy and gross. I didn't see much of an appetizer choice, and they got rid of the wings..in lieu of their wings you can get breaded boneless ones but I'm not about that. I am soo sad and disappointed. Adding new items is great but why do a complete menu overhaul? Everything was so good.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
My friend discovered this place when I came to town for a visit so we could get some traditional Nashville music/performances in, woo-hoo!

To start, it really sucks. You are outside, in-line and it was cooooold that day. Not fun and the reason I am giving 4 stars instead of 5. You then have to stare inside where people are eating and drinking and are warm and will them to leave. 

Once inside the venue was great! We didn't eat here but the drinks were boozy and creative. I really liked the options. Service was fair, but I did just go up and get my own drinks a few times. 

The band, Amber's Drive, was excellent! Great group of 3 guys but one of them had the most impressive voice and I think he should do 90% of the singing! We had great seats and bought the band's CD afterwards. 

If you are looking for something fun to do in a nice place with decent drinks check it out!
My friend purchased the tickets, but they were not costly, I think around ten bucks or so, a great deal, too!

Just be careful if it's cold outside cause you'll be waiting.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
If I could give no stars for this place, I would. I was part of a group who made reservations to come in on a Sunday morning for brunch, and the service, food, attitude were all below acceptable standards. I was one of the first people there and placed my order for the brunch buffet and bottomless mimosas. Thanks to APPALLING service, I got two tiny drinks. When I tried to flag our waitress down, I got a surprisingly snarky response. I'm not used to being talked to like I'm an 8 year old, especially when I'm paying for the pleasure. 

The restaurant ran out of food for the breakfast buffet, so many members of our group were waiting on their food or unable to get basic menu items. My mind was blown by how poor an experience it was. The person who made our reservation complained about the shortcomings, and apparently got blown off. No love for this place. I've seen better service at IHOP.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I was really looking forward to this museum. It was crowded and much smaller than I thought it would be. It's well done, but really small. Does a good job of telling his story and giving examples and historical items. I was just let down because I wanted more.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
GO HERE. If I came back to Nashville and could only do one thing, I would come back here. 

Ticket: Getting tickets was a breeze, ordered online, showed up early as recommended and was seated at a table for 2 front and center of the stage.

The Entertainment: The three girls who sang the night where there were incredible. I couldn't even speak I was in such awe of their talent. They were Carole King Jrs. in the making - amazing voices and song writers. 

Dining: I was very pleasantly surprised! Sick of BBQ and Fried Chicken, I took a chance on the mushroom sandwich and it was FANTASTIC. On top of that - the had Harpoon Ciders. We were very excited to get our hands on some Boston brews while on vacation!

name: 360 Burger
text: This food experience was very disappointing. I was looking forward to eating here, but my expectations were shot.  We ordered wings for an appetizer with bbq sauce and half honey hot. I specifically told the waitress that I wanted my wings to come out before my entree.  I didn't get my wings until after I was done with my meal!  It looked as if they poured a whole jar of bbq sauce on wings.  You only saw sauce, no wings.  I ordered a cheeseburger and onion rings.  The burger was bland.  I was expecting a well seasoned, well cooked, juicy burger, but I received a dry and flavorless burger.  I was disappointed with my food.  The onion rings were ok.  For the price, I expected more.   I would not recommend this place.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
We went for a brunch cruise and the food was terrible.  Very disappointing.  The eggs were weird, waffles hard as rocks, the chicken was cold and tasteless, we paid good money and when the cruise was over we had to go out to eat because we could did not enjoy the food on the boat.  The performers were very energetic and had great voices but sorry very cheesy.  The big fake smiles were hilarious but I noticed many of the older people really enjoyed it.  One lady was so emotional she cried.  

The boat seemed older but it was nice, we were able to walk around and it was nice being on the water.  I would not suggest the brunch honestly, not sure if the dinner option has better food and maybe a younger crowd.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
My boyfriend and I spent a few nights in Nashville and booked a dinner cruise on the General Jackson Showboat at the suggestion of our concierge.  This was a waste of a perfectly good vacation evening.  I cannot speak to the views as we took the boat in the late fall and it was dark the entire time (and there was not much of a view until we pulled into Nashville), but what I can say, is that this is best avoided unless you seriously don't have anything else to do with your time.  First, our waiter was inattentive, hard to track down and generally seemed like he resented having to wait on us at all.  Perhaps our much much older table-mates had a better experience with him, but ours was dismal.  It was impossible to even get a re-fill on our drinks over the course of hours.  Second, the food was abysmal.  Dinner was Prime Rib, period.  There were no options.  And this was not good prime rib, it was the cheap, salty, grey, gristly nastiness that you might expect to find on the buffet line of a rundown strip club in old Las Vegas.  No thanks.  Even the dessert was inedible.  Believe me, I have a sweet tooth, so would generally be inclined to eat my dessert.   If you cannot make something that I can stomach more than one bite of, you are definitely doing it wrong.  I think it was supposed to be strawberry shortcake, but no other strawberry shortcake I have ever had featured overly sweet strawberry jam-type goo over a tasteless hard puck of a biscuit.  Disgusting.  Finally, the show was energetic and had a decent premise - an overview of the music of Tennessee (Appalachia, Nashville and Memphis).  The performers were good and it is due to their efforts that this receives more than one star from me.  The execution of the show however was cheesy and there was a definite undercurrent of Southern Republican ethos to it that I could see making some people uncomfortable.  

I would not do this again.  If you do book this through a hotel, be advised that your shuttle driver will have your tickets (they will not be held at will call like you might suspect).  This is relevant if you miss your shuttle (like some other people we ran into did) or opt to drive your rental car to the boarding location (like we did), which will require you to find out which shuttle was meant to be yours and hope you can catch it when it arrives so that you can get your tickets.

name: The Basement East
text: Ended up here on a recommendation from our lyft driver. I really liked it. The crowd is definitely hipster and younger than I am. And at first that bothered me, but as it started filling up, more people like me arrived. We saw four bands for an incredibly low price. I cannot believe how inexpensive live entertainment is here. The only drawback to me was that there weren't many places to sit. None of the acts we saw were country. Which was a good thing for me. I like country, but after all of the honky tonks,I'm good for a while.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Dinned here for Brunch this past Sunday and have mixed feelings. The atmosphere is great if you are in the mood to listen to live music. The food is PHENOMENAL - truly, everyone enjoyed their meal. The service, however, was less than to par. Our mimosas were forgotten and you could tell they had our server running all over the place (not sure if they were understaffed or under trained). I will definitely give this place another try in hopes of better service!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Amazing! This museum was in our plans for our 12 day vacation, it was over the top. My favorite part of our vacation and I would definitely return. It's a MUST SEE!!! Good for children (mine were 9/12), younger might not understand it or be able to slowly take in all of the information. My parents loved it as well, mom was crying when we left.
Puts you there w Johnny, in his life. Not only has tons of artifacts, but pictures, movie scripts and letters and songs....pay stubs and interactive devises. 
The gift shop has so many options and items that I struggled to just buy a few items. I love Johnny Cash, love his music and his story.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Music was great. Drinks were delicious. (Which should be rated a 5!!)

I would highly recommend eating before hand. Our food took over and hour and all five meals were cold when they were finally served. Also, one meal came out five minutes after the rest (and it was STILL cold!!). The food was a major let down.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: If I could give this place a "0" I would. We were celebrating a 21st birthday here, paid $12 for a shot, and got screamed at by the bartender. To be fair, a shot was bought for the birthday girl and she had not seen her ID yet--that was our fault..but we did inform the bartender she turned 21 yesterday while we were waiting for her to find her ID. The bartender did proceed while this was happening, however, to say "I don't give a shit" and proceeded to tell us how she had "3 college degrees." Then told us she was the manager (blonde, short hair). When I tried to calmly talk to her, she told me not to speak to her like a child. This did not have a to be as big of an issue as it was. It was blown way out of proportion. She yelled at us because some of us were drinking water and sitting at the bar (there was NO ONE in the bar). I have worked in food service before and this customer service is awful--if you serve alcohol you should not be someone that INSTIGATES bar fights. On a positive note, the live music was wonderful! I believe he said his name was Isaac Matthews. By the way, I have 3 college degrees...and don't work at a bar. Do not waste your money here and don't you dare try to get hydrated here!!!!

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: I visited the museum with my younger sister and we had a blast! We took tons of pictures, and enjoyed an hour of learning about great artist from different genres and eras.   $25 can be pricey so I would recommend looking for different coupons, and maybe asking for a buy one get one free price! Definitely a good pit stop if your in Nashville doing tourist things!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
As someone who does NOT listen to country music this was quite the experience for me. My friends dragged me here (against my will) for dinner and a show. The food was pretty good and the music was great! 

I don't remember the name of the guy who was performing but he played a bunch of different songs. They were all different and there were even 1 or 2 songs that I would have happily listened to on my own!

I highly recommend this place if you're visiting Nashville!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
I've been here twice on separate occasions. I love the music, dueling pianos but I don't like that after I checked my bank account they have charged me for 3 separate checks only 1 which is mine. Jason/Jamie contacted me within a few hours after I posted about my situation and took care of everything which is nice to know they care about their customers. Angry orchard draft is &6. Delicious. 
Get here early if you want a good seat though we got lucky and got seats after people left. Just became a matron of honor and hope to bring my bachelorette here next summer before her fall wedding. Which I saw this place is great for bachelorette parties. 
6 dollar cover on Saturday and free Friday.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: From the moment I walked in, I felt at home. There is much more I could write, but come on in and ask for the Chef..you'll be able to see by the smile on my face. Makes work a bit easier when it's always a killer show, amazing staff, and pitch-perfect sound.

name: The Basement East
text: Had to wait in line for about 20 mins...brrr!Standing only...no tables!!  Drinks were reasonably priced. But enjoyed all the bands that perform. Larkin & Poe rocked it out!!  Wishful thinking...but it would be great if they had some kind of heat for the deck.

name: 360 Burger
text: We got two burgers and some queso con carne with pita chips. The burgers tasted completely off, like something was wrong with it. The meat seemed old and we could not even risk eating it. The queso had literally two pieces of ground beef and came with tortilla chips (far from the description of the item on the menu). It was a waste of $30 and we got it to go so we were out a whole nights meal. NEVER. AGAIN.

name: 360 Burger
text: I honestly do not know what to tell you. After months of waiting for the right time to try this place out and the expectancy of a great grass fed burger I'm left speechless. From the moment  me and my two children stepped foot in the restaurant I could sense this place was starting to disappoint. There were no host or hostess at the podium, there was a awful band playing extremely loud music in the far left hand corner and to top it off the dining area was poorly illuminated. This place reeked of disaster. I approached the bar and asked, "can we be seated" and we were guided to a table that had the light flickering on and off intermittently. So as we sat there for nearly 12 minutes I prepped the kids and stated that in three more minutes we are leaving if we do not get our drinks. At long last, on the fourteenth minute we had a waiter. They must have had two waiters for about 30 people. I couldn't believe it. Our burger experience just kept growing worse. We received our appetizer promptly after all it was just queso and chips. Our main grub now that's another story. The only upside is this, they did make good on the 50% off appetizer that is offered through Yelp and because of the extra long wait for our burgers they did give us a free appetizer. But that's where it ends because I have never in my life tasted a burger without texture and mushy before in my life. Ugh just thinking about it now just... I don't know if they can be called burgers or not it reminds me more of a patty made from soggy bread totally disgusting. Oh, and by the way if you show your Yelp coupon be prepared to be  stalked, followed and repeatedly asked ,"how is everything?" All in a vain attempt to win you over. All I wanted was a good, no great burger!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Only wish we had found this place earlier!! Our goal was to just stop in for one drink at the different bars on Broadway but when we found this place we spent our whole evening there. Great music, great staff. Everyone from the door guy to the bartenders are musically inclined. Get there early for a good seat!!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Always a good time. Live dueling pianos - Music is 80's to present. Standing room only on weekends so arrive early if you want a table. Avoid getting into the piano playing tip wars (e.g. Rocky Top vs Sweet Home Alabama).

name: 360 Burger
text: The service was really slow. Food was fairly decent but nothing to rave about. I had higher expectations considering the Swetts pedigree. Pharmacy Burger & M.L. Rose are better options for affordable gourmet burgers.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Dueling pianos excellent, all 8 or 10 of them. Worth every tip they get.  Its Nashville for Gods sake what's not to love about the place, its talent, restaurants, hospitality.  I truly hate to give a 'negative' but here goes. The wait staff......ok that's about it. Not too friendly, I'll leave it at that.  I visit at least 3 times a year and hope to continue doing so. Well worth a try when on Broadway St.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: This place was the highlight of my Nashville trip. This place totally encompasses everything Nashville is about. The music was amazing, beautiful, and so entertaining. I thoroughly enjoyed my time here and if I lived in Nashville I would come here every weekend. I will say the food is nothing special. I wouldn't come here to eat. I would get a few drinks and maybe an appetizer because the food wasn't all that good. I got the Hot Chicken and it didn't taste anything like Tennessee Hot Chicken. It wasn't spicy at all. My boyfriend had the Pork Steak and he thought it was good but not worth the money. Also, all of our food came out cold except our Fried Pickles appetizer. (Which was good) BUT I would still come here in a heart beat because the music made my heart happy.  there's a $10 minimum per person so getting drinks here would be perfect for me.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Absolutely the best meal in 3 days in Nashville. The meatloaf was - to die for !  Don't pass this location up - stop in and enjoy !

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: If you are under 75 and can walk on your own (without the need of a walker)...think again. The lunch cruise we went on was seriously an older crowd. The singers on the show were basically anyone who didn't make it in Nashville all dressing up like their favorite singers and hoping the crowd doesn't notice they aren't them.
