Good iced tea and pulled pork but I wouldn't be excited for the rest of this buffet lunch. Incredibly boring ride overall. I think the cruise on Gilligan's Island was more fun. Save your money and go to the Opry where they can really sing and don't have bedazzled microphones.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Food was not good at all, burnt short ribs, and dry chicken. They did not have sweet tea, which was shocking for a southern dining experience. We attended the Nashville nights event and some of the performers were talented but all they did was sing covers of country songs. There was nothing organic and it didn't really feel like Nashville. The boat is beautiful and the ride into downtown was great. I would never waste money on the food again.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
The museum sits in a very touristy part of Nashville that made us a little leery of going into it.  We were afraid it would be something cheesy and overly commercial. We were completely wrong.

Any fan of Johnny Cash will truly love this museum.  It's a little small, but beautifully put together with so much to see.  What really made it different for me were all the the things he and others saved and held onto for so many years.  Things like hand written letters to fans, army discharge papers, responses to job inquiries, just really neat things to see and read.

Then of course there was the incredible library of live performances and TV appearances that you could spend hours watching.

name: 360 Burger
text: Good food, slow service. Took forever to get a drink. Took 1.5 hours to order drinks, food, eat and get a check. Far too long for a burger joint.

name: 360 Burger
text:
So glad I finally made it over to Antioch to try 360 burger. I spent the morning at Percy Priest Lake Beach. Since I was in the area, I stopped by 360 burger after I heard good things. Wow one of the few times that a restaurant exceeded the hype.

 Two words: Pretzels Rolls. Amazing. As a Philly native there are few things I enjoy more than a  soft pretzel. Its one of my must haves as soon as I land in Philly. So I'm skeptical when people try to duplicate it. But 360 burger's pretzel rolls rock. The mix of salty and chewy was the perfect compliment to the juicy delicious burger. I got the basic cheeseburger with grilled onions.

 IT wasn't basic it was very well seasoned. And it was huge, I took half of it home. The sweet potato fries and aioli mayo were delicious. They were thin cut and crispy but not overdone. So many times when people try to do thin cut fries they overcook them. I was very impressed that these sweet potato fries were perfect. Also got a ton of the fries. Ended up taking about half of them home with my half of a burger. 


My waiter was friendly and attentive (disclaimer, I came in for a late lunch on a Friday afternoon and the restaurant was not very crowded.). Anyway, he offered my a water to go, which I always appreciate and he got e a lid so I could take the aioli home. 

There was a decent draught selection and I enjoyed my Sweetwater with my burger.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: On vacation fom St. Louis... this is hands down my favorite venue in Nashville!!! Myself, my husband and several of our friends came here back to back night and had an amazing time. The entertainment, atmosphere, service, and management was SUPERB! I will most certainly come back anytime we are in the area!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Visited the Johnny Cash Museum on August 6th 2017 and loved, loved, loved it. It's a self guided tour with displays from childhood. Very well done time line that provides a lot of relevant information about Cash, the times and the music. I spent about two to three hours and left feeling very differently about Cash, in a good  way.  It's a must see when visiting Nashville. The gift shop was over priced, as expected.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Awesome place for music and orange moonshine drinks.  Great Sunday funday!  We highly recommend, must do in Nashville

name: 360 Burger
text: Great food, friendly staff.. one of my favorite places to grab a burger in Antioch!  Check it out some time, you won't be disappointed

name: 360 Burger
text: The service was terrible we waited 30 minutes for our beer and ended up cashing out since the food was going to be another 20 minutes. I have been here before and the food was fantastic but they need to fix their operations.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Drinks were decent and the band was good! Service was slow. The wings say "grilled" but really come out fried dry and with very little meat. Sweet potato fries OK but how do you really mess those up! Go for a drink and check out the America flag bar, skip the food.

name: 360 Burger
text:
Im giving them 3 stars for sone reasons:
The place is nice but a little bit loud for lunch, a little bit pricey. 
The hamburgers are really good, good flavor although the selection is poor.
We tried the fried Oreos with Ice Cream and they were really good.
I ordered mine medium well but came well done, but the server offered me to re do it the right way. Beside that, the server Tony did a great job. I will definitely come back for another try.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Well our experience began on a Wednesday morning. We sat down at the bar with plenty of room still available at the bar and at tables. My husband and I ordered a drink then the bartender asked our 17 year old daughter what she wanted. She ordered a water. She was then asked for her id. We were told we needed to leave the bar because only 21 year olds can sit at the bar. So we grab our drinks and move to a table in the back. Again there, we were told we couldn't sit at the table if we weren't going to order food. The place was empty. We were spending money but the rudeness of the staff was not needed.  If you have an under age child in your party, beware!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
We came on a Saturday afternoon and had a great time. It didn't take long for a table to clear up to get seated. There was live music on both floors but we listening to 4 great female singers who did a lot of 90s music on the 1st floor. Heather was a very attentive server despite it being pretty busy. The artichoke dip was excellent! I definitely recommend it! 

The one thing that is obviously completely out of the control of the management and servers is the lines for the bathroom(s) both had about a 4 person wait but I think that can be expected in a busy establishment.

In short, come enjoy a good time, good food and good service! Don't come for the bathrooms

name: The Basement East
text: I love venturing out to the Beast! I haven't been in Nashville long but love finding venues like this one.  I've seen some local bands and also a couple favorites from New Orleans! I can say from each time the crowd was a comfortable size and you can't beat the drink prices. Shot and a beer specials are allllways welcomed and for the price I always seem to get a good pour. Drinks and sound are the only things that matter to me in places like this so I'll be there first to complain at a venue where speakers are blown and / or the drinks are pricey and weak. Sound seemed to be pretty good quality and there was a good mix of different ages in the crowd which I always think is awesome. I haven't tried any food yet but from other reviews I definitely will! I've yet to spend any time there when it was completely open with the patio but overall I really dig the space. Will definitely be back!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: We did not eat here. We did visit this place 4 times while we were in Nashville.  The party vibe in here is amazing.  We had so much fun at this bar. The band's here were the best that we experienced in downtown.  Very energetic and really good. All the staff here were very friendly. Probably the sexiest bartenders I have ever seen.. tight pants, tight shirts and very tan. We visited all the floors. The roof top bar was very nice. Next time we may try the food here. It was an amazing time.  Make sure you check this place out while your in this town.  You will have a blast.

name: The Basement East
text: I collapsed from heat stroke due to no air conditioning during Billy Sheehan's bass solo. I drove 600 miles to see that solo. I had to go lay down for the remainder of the bass solo (and an additional song, "Ghost Town") on one of the dinette booths until I gained consciousness.  It was THAT hot.  To add insult to injury, the paid parking next door ended literally 4 minutes early and they promptly gave me a $60 parking ticket...on top of the $10 I already paid for 4 hour parking.  F this place.  F it hard, F it long.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Great bar to checkout along the Broadway strip. Stopped in here for a few drinks and to listen to one of the bands playing. 
The bar is a multi story building with a bar on each floor. There is also a cool rooftop bar which offers a nice view of Broadway.
Bartenders and staff were nice and helpful. Didnt get any food but it looked decent.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Pretty Cool place. There are a lot of places inside to listen to a blurb from a show or song.. I was a little weirded out by using "community" headphones. Lots of interesting stuff... including a video of Johnny Cash clips from various movies and tv shows. $14 to get in isnt bad either.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
This review is strictly about service. The content of the museum was awesome.

Make sure you ASK for your AAA DISCOUNT or any other discount. 

I found out after purchasing multiple tickets (from my Mom who purchased tickets after me at the counter) that they offer a AAA discount. I went back up and asked if they would honor it as I had literally just finished paying and the supervisor/manager refused and was pretty nasty about the whole thing. Shame.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I don't like country music so much, but have to say, this was so fun, and so low-key. We went to the 6 p.m. show, heard some great music, and honestly, the food wasn't horrible. We had the hummus, fries, and fried pickles, and my sisters ordered some sort of chicken puff pastry things. As a pregnant person, I have to say that the fries and the fried pickles were exactly what I would want for a visit in Nashville, haha. The waiter was great, the music was outstanding, and I'd definitely come back.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I have mixed feelings about this place. It is a rather large place with tall ceilings so the sounds are not as good as they may be in a smaller place. We enjoyed the music, but the rest was so-so. They had $7 cover and $15 spend minimum per person. We only ordered drinks, which were okay. The biggest disappointment was with the service. They are poorly trained. The servants check in with you every 5 minutes even though you still have a drink that you are drinking. They interrupt people with these check-ins and picking up glasses/dishes in the middle of song performances, making distracting sounds, etc. This place should definitely try to work on how they approach service otherwise I can see them going downhill despite good talent on stage.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
Kid Rock's is the place to go because there is plenty of room (no wait), great service (I am going to marry Austin), yummy local beer selection.

Not sure what was better the music (on the second floor) or Austin (our server). I thought Austin posed for this beer but he said NO!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I went to Whiskey Row last night, but was not allowed in because my boyfriend had on Timberland boots. He was told it was no longer allowed by corporate and not part of the dress code because "too many blacks and minorities are wearing them". I asked them if my boobs were hanging out, if that would be apart of "dress code" and could go in, and I was told yes. So it's acceptable to not have a shirt on, but not acceptable to wear shoes? This is one of his favorite places to go, however, we will not be back due to "corporate's" discrimination.

name: 360 Burger
text: While the food is pretty good, the service is terrible. I've been there numerous times and the service just seems to get worse everytime I've gone. The last time I was there, I actually ended up walking out since a server never came to our table after sitting there for 10 minutes watching them talk behind the bar. There are better burger options around.

name: 360 Burger
text:
I'm giving this restaurant a 2 because the food was delicious (I had the mushroom Swiss burger with sweet potato fries), but the service was a big negative. The man who served us didn't write any of our orders down and messed up 4 out of 5 of them in their own special ways: burger cooked wrong, wrong fries, wrong toppings, you name it. (Not writing down orders and getting them correct is very impressive. This was not.)

He had to come back to have us repeat our orders 3 times, and still got things wrong. When he brought us missing things we requested, he brought them out one at a time, and made up excuses why he brought the mustard but not the refill. 

We really thought there just had to be hidden cameras somewhere by the end of the meal.

You can probably imagine that he got the checks wrong, too. All in all, it took us an hour and a half to order, eat and pay for 5 burgers. There were only a few other tables there.

IF I ever go back, I will write my order down for this particular server: no exceptions. I probably won't go back, though. It's unfortunate, because I had high hopes for this establishment when I heard about their local beef and produce.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Definitely our favorite bar in Nashville! We went on Super Bowl night and both bands we saw were awesome! It was very lively and the bartenders got our drinks quick. Kinda expensive but I figure that's all of Nashville. We loved the music and would definitely come back!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Don't recommend coming here for the food. Absolutely horrible hamburgers and fries.  The hamburger didn't even taste like beef. Super loud. Couldn't even hear what our server was saying let alone carry on a conversation at the table.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: We absolutely loved our time at the listening room. The time flew by as we listened to the  songwriters of Nashville! We ate dinner before attending the show, so we ordered a few cocktails and the homemade donuts. The donuts were hot and delicious!! Would highly recommend the vanilla cinnamon ones. The harvester rose cocktail was also a personal favorite! It is a drink that would suit all tastebuds. We will certainly be back!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Best bar in downtown! Bartenders are always smiling and having fun, the music is steps above that on the main strip, and the food is incredible! ( they have a daily meat n' two that will make you feel like you're at grandma's Sunday dinner).  We have gotten to be out of town regulars and tell all of our friends to come here!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Jake was great! Great atmosphere and band was really good. Definitely recommend it to anyone visiting Nashville.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This is the Best bar in nashville. The food is amazing. We can not wait to go back. Next time you are in Nashville visit this place.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great place to hear up-and-comers in the country music business.  I had the pleasure of hearing Bobby Pinson and Friends on a Saturday night.  Great time, even when the band blew a fuse and the lights went out. The food is average, but the music acts are great.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
I wasn't sure whether I was going to give a 1 star or 4 star review so it got the middle of 2 stars. 
The 1 star review comes from the restaurant owners for screwing their customers at the check out. Apparently the servers have no clue and management will make no concessions for an added charge to every bill. The first line of the bill lists a "tech fee of 3%" not a surcharge for patrons using a credit card! WTF is the fee for. Nowhere else on Broadway did we ever incur this bogus fee. They should notify the customer upon entering the restaurant.  
Now for the review of food and atmosphere. Everything was very good in that area. We heard some good music from the sidewalk and that brought us in. Got some drinks and they were good too. Our server was nice and around when we needed her. We then ordered some food and that was quite good for a Broadway bar/restaurant. I had the  half yardbird and although it was a small chicken, it was a perfectly juicy single portion. The other foods ordered was a hamburger that was really good and a chicken ceasar   wrap that was better than average. All the food came out fresh and hot though the kitchen was pretty slow. 
That music was fantastic and probably one of the best bands we had seen the whole visit.  
My opinion to give the owners a taste of their own filthy medicine would be to come in for 2 hours, don't order anything but TIP THE BAND $20 AND TIP THE SERVER $20 and see how long  this stupid Tech Fee lasts!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I cannot believe that when you drop $200 at an establishment they don't clear your table and leave you to sit with it for an hour! So disappointed! I'll give that the music artists were good so this is no reflection on them. Went as a family, five of us, adults, and at first thought "this is great." Food was delivered quickly and the show was underway. It ends there. After that we sat with our dirty plates filling our table for an hour after we finished eating. Maris, our server, (table 54) walked by us over a dozen times without ever acknowledging our plates or servicing to remove them. She did stop by two more times and asked if we needed anything and was happy to bring us more drinks but never removed a dirty dish in the process. Yes, we left with our table filled with dirty dishes. (See photo) Paid $60 for five tickets and dropped another $125 in food and drinks (not including tip that was excepted). We will definitely think twice before going again. Sadly! There are plenty of great options in beautiful Nashville to drop $200 and get a great experience!! (11/23/18 6:00pm show)

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I thought this place was great. Now I only went for drinks (8pm to 11 on a Thursday night) with my bestie, but we had a great time. The live band played an assortment of county, 90's throwback, and a lot of requests. We came early enough where we got a seat at the bar and we never had to wait long to order a drink all night and our tab wasn't crazy expensive at the end of the night. Packed house, could move, all in all good spot on broadway!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Enjoyable, and I'm glad we stopped. The information about the span of Cash's life and career was good. The place was very crowded (went on a Sunday), making it difficult to really enjoy the exhibits. Price was high, $16, for a relatively small exhibit. 

Coffee shop up front (Bongo) was great!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: We went here on a girls weekend from St. Louis, MO and had a wonderful time!  The atmosphere was fantastic, loved the valet parking!  The singers/songwriters were very entertaining and hung around after their show.  The service and food was amazing!  I have had fried/breaded pickles before, but these were so different and delicious!  It was a great night out with at an amazing venue!  I would recommend reservations as it gets crowded.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Very nice.  Big time tourist magnet.  the food was very good . Its a buffet so keep your expectations in line.   The Music City Nights show was very good, talented performers.  I am sure this cruise is not their ticket to stardom, but they did a nice job.  Would definitely go on again

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: We tried brunch here today and we were less than impressed with the food (music was fabulous though). We had checked the menu online and it showed numerous brunch ( rather than lunch) items but when we arrived the menu had far fewer options. The waitress pushed the $18 buffet but a quick look at it was enough to not be interested. It looked like it had been out for hours and defiantly not impressive enough to warrant the price tag. I ordered the CB slinger $16 and my husband ordered a pulled pork Benedict $18. Both came with soggy flavorless hash browns, mine were even partially frozen. If you can't make a decent hash brown, you have no business serving brunch. My husband's meal also came with undercooked bacon that tasted like someone poured a bottle of liquid smoke on it. Overall they have a great atmosphere, but the food bordered on inedible which is unacceptable especially at that price point. If you just want a drink stop in for some great music but I would avoid the food.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great place. Was here for the opening last night and came back today. Awesome live country music. Food was great. Our sever, Nicole, was the BEST EVER!!!  Very personable and knowledgeable of the place. Suggested many items on the menu but was complimentary of all their items. She has a bright future ahead of her. Hang on to your dreams always Nicole. They will never come true if you don't. If and when I come back to. Nashville I will definitely come back.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Really enjoyed spending about 90 minutes here.  They have an extensive collection of memorabilia, and I learned a lot about Johnny Cash.  If it had been less crowded, I would have given it 5 stars, but we went on a Saturday morning when it was very crowded on Broadway, so I would suggest finding a time to go when it might be a little less busy.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Entertainers was good. Had great costumes!!! Sexy ladies and flat bellied Cowboys.  Pulled pork brisket with BBQ sauce, real mashed potatoes, and pecan pie all were good.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Cool museum esp. if you are a fan. They have a green screen area where you can take a photo "with Johnny." Super nice staff. Wasn't particularly impressed with the gift shop - nothing too unique. 

Admission is $18 which is a bit pricy considering it's a small museum. Use your AAA card and get $1 off!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Amazing show great performers, good food. Drinks were pricy but hey you get to keep the glass lol! Beautiful Nashville skyline at night

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: A great museum! Lost of information, pictures, outfits, and records. We spent an 1 hour here, and learned a lot. The staff were friendly and has lost of souvenirs.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
We watched the midday performance of "Taste of Tennessee." The staff was excellent and very friendly. This is a great way to kill some time and get to explore Tennessee at the same time. The food was tasty and they had cake set out and ready. 

The show was fun to watch with very talented singers performing. The scenery was probably my favorite part. It was nice to go outside on the boat and get to see parts of Tennessee. 

If you're not a local, I would recommend trying this. For me, it's a one time thing. It was enjoyable but at the end I was ready to get off the boat and get into some cool AC.

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text:
Obsessed with maintaining a high female to male ratio of guests.  If you're a group of guys trying to enter, do not attempt to go in together- stagger yourselves going in.

Chuck "the owner" is an egotistical idiot in a Ed Hardy shirt - you can't miss him.  He'll have his doorman bounce you once you've racked up a nice tab, for just about anything.  

The DJ's are subpar.  

There are many other places in the Gulch that you'll have more fun spending your time in.  Nothing to see here - keep moving.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Incredible experience.  Highlight of our  Nashville trip. Maybe the best fried chicken and southern home cooked food I have had in my life.The entertainment was lively and cutting-edge. Appropriate for a variety of ages. The crowd the showboat attracts were so much fun. We just could not get enough and were so sad when it all ended. We made friends on this short voyage that will be long lasting and can not wait to head down the Cumberland again in the future for an awesome steamboat adventure aboard General Jackson

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
2.5 Stars. 
I came here inadvertently after failing to find cheap parking for Bakersfield. Why are the public parking lots $30??!?!?! Luckily, Listening Room Cafe had complimentary valet, so we chose to dine there for lunch. The restaurant is very open, with tables facing a large stage. At first, I was pretty excited to hear some live music. It was too bad, however, that all 3 singer/songwriters were just okay--nothing too impressive. The food and service wasn't much better. Although our hostess quickly seated us, we had to wait at least 15 minutes for a server to even take our order--and that was only after we flagged her down. Furthermore, our server perpetually had a frown on her face and didn't even smile once. I don't think we saw any of the staff look friendly. They just looked really unhappy and bored to be there. Not a good sign.

I ordered the All American Scramble (omelette with cheese, kielbasa, and gravy sauce) and it was just okay. For $13, I was expecting something much better, but the omelette was kind of dry and one note. The restaurant was also serving a buffet option for $18, but by the looks of it, it wasn't worth the money. Very small selection of food items. 

Overall, I left feeling very meh about the Listening Room Cafe. For what it is--a live music venue that serves food--the Bluebird Cafe is much better.

name: 360 Burger
text:
So glad this place is in Antioch!  The area needs more great local places like 360 Burger.  The food is great, the pretzel buns are awesome!  Fries were delicious, whatever sauce they bring with the sweet potato fries is to die for.  We shared the peach cobbler dessert, which was also delicious.  

Our server (Taylor) was great, the whole staff was attentive and friendly.  You can't get service like this at most places. 

Prices were great, a 1/3 lb burger with any toppings you wanted, fries and drink was $7.99.  I had sliders, fries and a drink for $6.99.  They have quite a bit of happy hour choices and prices were cheap, but we missed the timing by an hour.

They have live music Wed-Sat, from singer/songwriters to jazz.

The location is in an abandon strip mall, so plenty of parking.  I am hoping that with 360 Burger coming, more places will take notice and move in next door and surrounding retail spaces.  An Antioch dweller myself, I know people are anxious and ready for good businesses to come in.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: The music was great. I enjoyed the the steak as well. The wings, however, really stood out to me.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Don't waste your time. Food was wildly mediocre and the show was just ok. Your money would be much better spent going somewhere in downtown Nashville with live music and good food.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
I am not a huge country fan, but this place was amazing.  The Listening Room Cafe is a another place like the Bluebird Cafe, where country music lovers can listen to some of their favorite country songs.  The singer here are mostly the songwriters them selves.  

It is a little pricy for me...but well worth the visit....or two.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: This location definitely stands out on broadway! It's loud and big!  We decided to check it out and have an early dinner and grab a couple drinks. We sat upstairs by a window. It was pretty packed! It's almost impossible to hear too so if you want to socialize don't eat here or pretty much anywhere on broadway for that matter.  Our server was fine - the place is so busy so you order and they drop off your check - then if you want food they'll bring another check.  We had 2 drinks at $10 each and chicken tenders and the chicken sandwich. The food was hot and fresh and the music was loud! Good experience - I would return!!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Walked in and felt like this was where the "older crowd" hangs. Also the music was way too loud that we left as our ear drums were ringing...

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Drinks were diluted and service was slow. Pretty relaxed atmosphere and staff seem to be carefree and fun.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Cool atmosphere with live music for lunch.  Food was average but service was horrible.  I felt bad for the other waitress because everyone kept asking her for things... basic things like napkins and utensils.. great location , hopefully service will be better

name: 360 Burger
text: The best kept secret in Antioch.   Great food and beer selection great live music.  Also a great place to watch sports.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
This is the answer to, "Where should I go as a tourist in Nashville when I don't like country music?"

There really was something here for everyone. The performers really knew how to play to the crowd and I didn't see a single request stump them. Their jokes bordered on semi-innappropriate, but that's my style, so it made me love them more. The crowd was a little older than most other places we stopped, which is a nice change if what you are really after is to sit and chill while listening to music.

We stopped in for one drink. We ended up staying for several hours.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Band was great. Food was good. Still working on bringing service to where it needs to be.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Didn't know the Thong Song. V disappointing. Played Journey several times within the same hour. 3/5

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
For those of you used to cruising, you know the General Jackson. The ticket price is just the beginning. Drinks, photos, tours, meals, and show all will cost extra.
Plenty come to Nashville wanting to experience something of the history of the area. A river boat ride, country meal and country music show meets that groups desires. The musicians are studio quality and the meal is mass produced. There is plenty but nothing stands out. The staff is friendly and helpful.
I would not have done this if it had not been initiated by friends.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Wendy on the 4th floor... theeeee best! Like holy cow. Things get crazy and hectic and busy and this girl keeps her cool, doesn't miss a beat, remembers everyone's drinks, and serves them with a smile! For out of towners... she's a beautiful introduction to southern hospitality! Actually all the bartenders on the 4th floor on a BUSY SATURDAY NIGHT we're phenomenal... but Wendy was a star. Rock on sister for your killer customer service!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We came to Whiskey Row for brunch - The food was absolutely delicious and our waitress was Savannah. She was amazing.  Totally on top of things and very knowledgeable about the menu. I am vegetarian and she was very capable of helping me choose an awesome meal. She was pleasant and kept on top of your drinks and keeping our waters filled. We will definitely be back.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Just came here for a quick Almond Vanilla Iced Latte and it was just what I needed on a hot day. I actually didn't go in the Johnny Cash Museum but I did relax outside the cafe to get some cool air. Although just being in the place, it made me want to check it out next time..they had some really cool Johnny Cash memorabilia. But as far as coffee goes..it's really good and the barista's were nice!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I'm not a big Johnny Cash fan, so two hours was more than enough time to spend here. That and four hours of parking cost $30 and we still needed dinner. Tickets are $20 pp for a self guided tour. 

I thought the costumes and movie memorabilia were cool. I think the exhibit about his influence in Hollywood was the most interesting. I didn't know Johnny had been in so many movies and special guest star on so many tv shows. My favorite dress was what June wore to the White House. 

Overall, very interesting information about him, but just one visit is enough for me.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
A bit over priced for it was. I went because I had a living social. The prices on some of the things on the menu seemed a little absurd to me. The waitress really had no knowledge of the menu because they had a new chef and was trying some new things put... did they not have a tasting? 
2 for 1 mimosas- not worth it. Crappy orange juice or something but not the best mimosa I've had. 
The coffee was served in paper to go cups. Idk if they are new to the brunch and coffee game, but it was weird being served in a paper cup when there were people with mugs around us. 
I had the biscuits and gravy to eat, which was just alright- nothing to rave about. 
We went in around 1015, and it was pretty dead, but it started to pick up at 11 when the live music started. The music was great entertainment and very enjoyable. All in all, not sure if I would go back.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
if you want to be blown away by some of the finest art in the world, you would travel to Musee du Louvre in Paris.

If you want to see the most incredible gardens you'd probably choose The Butchart Gardens on Vancouver Island or Cheekwood if you are visiting Nashville or live close by.

If you want to learn about the history of Rock and Roll, definitely head to The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum, located in Cleveland, Ohio.

An Elvis fan? No question - visit Graceland - Memphis TN.

Want to stroll the entire history of Country Music and every artist you can imagine? The Country Music Hall of Fame in Nashville is your destination.

BUT-
If you want to :
View the largest public collection of Johnny Cash memorabilia.
Experience a timeline of audio formats / video footage spanning his incredible career of 5 decades.
Read the Man In Black's personal handwritten thoughts, song lyrics, report cards, walls of awards, and many more interesting items. 
Get a glimpse into his personal life beginning with his childhood.
 
Find out why Johnny Cash is one of the most important musical and historical figures of all time. 
THIS is where you go. 

It's an incredible museum people of all ages will enjoy. 

You can spend an hour or an entire day being entertained by state-of-the-art audio and visual elements. The museum is self guided. 

Take the time to visit. You'll be happy you did.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
I booked tickets online the day of and it was easy to do. I think the seats are first come first served because we arrived 30 minutes late and got seats in the back at the bar. It was fine though, still could see the stage well.

What I didn't understand was that once you get there, they make you order a minimum $15 worth of food/drinks per person. We didn't have dinner so we got the pulled pork sandwich and chicken fingers. Pulled pork was ok but chicken fingers were dry - terrible. 

But I didn't go there for the food so I'm still giving 4 stars. 

The music was excellent! There were four performers and they took turns performing. It was nice that before each song, they gave a short story about what the song was about. Fell in love with Lena Stone and Adam Criag ... they were amazing artists! The show lasted about an hour and half. 

I would go again if they didn't force people to order food or drinks.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
The party at this place on a Saturday night was awesome and just what my group of friends were looking for.  I was in town for a bachelorette party with a group of 12 girls.  We started on the 2nd floor which had more of an upscale country bar vibe.  The band that was playing was great and there was plenty of room to dance.
We later moved up to the rooftop where the scene was completely different -- much younger.  The music was a DJ mix of early 00's and today (not country) which was definitely different from the country scene downstairs. This rooftop area honestly made feel more like I was back in NYC than in Nash.  Great view from the roof, but it was super crowded so it was hard to get to the railings to have an unimpeded view.  

The stair climb up to the roof top was a little on the tough side.  There were a ton of security guards all over the roof top.  I can definitely see why, however.  Lots of ROWDY people.  We had a good time nonetheless.  

I would definitely recommend this rooftop if you're looking to get away from the live country music scene for a little while.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
We were just looking to kill some time before the show at the Ryman so we thought we'd check out the Cash museum. He was a pretty interesting guy so it's got to be an interesting museum right? Nah, not really. I'm not a museum fan anyway but when my husband said "This is a waste of $15" I thought, "ok good it's not just me".

Maybe it was just too small and too many people, maybe there were too many "digital" displays and not enough memorabilia, maybe watching "Walk the Line" before visiting the museum is as bad as watching a movie before you read the book. 

Ok, I learned a little about him that I didn't know but was that worth $30 for my husband and I. I'ma say no.

 
Side note: They sell beverages and since our hotel didn't have vending machines we were quite thirsty so I asked the girl if I could drink it inside. She said no, which is expected of a museum  (even though everything is behind glass). I said "oh ok, I didn't know since y'all sell them". Her reply was "oh well you can buy it and take it in you just can't open it". Thanks...

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
What a wonderful experience when you are in Nashville! The singer/songwriters were out of this world. And seriously, I'm not a singer/songwriter kind of person. It's not really my jam, you could say. But they had so much talent I was just in awe. 

We had the absolute worst server ever, but it couldn't even dampen the experience. We still had a great time. The manager was very nice about the whole thing and gave us a discount for the poor service, so I appreciate his ability to see something wrong and try to make it right.

This is a must if you are visiting Nashville. You are guaranteed to hear some real talent, and if you're a country music fan, maybe a song you've heard on the radio! The singer/songwriters are working in Nashville and have sold songs to other bands and singers. Really awesome stuff.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
So this would be excellent as strictly a bar. Back to back nights of walking into the establishment and there's absolutely no seating in the main area. Which this wouldn't be an issue, but we were told they only served the full menu of food on the first floor. Everyone at the tables were just drinking. No hostess. The setup is just bad. Like I said, if it was a bar it would be excellent, but the "amazing steaks" can't even be eaten.

I don't think it would be a huge deal but we went in back to back days and absolutely zero room to sit down and enjoy a meal. Don't serve food if you can't even serve people. There's a standing room at the top if people want to enjoy a drink. I actually saw no one eating because drinkers were occupying all tables.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Music was nice, food sucks , drinks weak, And since yelp wants this to be a longer review I just have to fill in some areas here, I cannot tell you it's a great place to go, the band on the first floor was good, very danceable, the band on the second floor was pretty good, the pretzel and beer cheese was OK the artichoke dip sucked, place looked a little grimy or actually a lot grimy but it was OK it is on the strip, and that's what you can expect from a tourist bar

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
The Listening Room is an awesome local venue for live local talent in Nashville. Best to make a reservation, but walk ins get seats too! 

Prices are fair and the serving staff are friendly and efficient. 

The food is decent - Te fried green tomatoes are delicious and the hot chicken is one of my favorites in the city (it's very smoky flavored).

name: Live Oak
text: We came from Chicago for Thanksgiving weekend, this place did not disappoint. Great bartenders and great owners. Served up a delicious Thanksgiving dinner while showing Da Bears play to a WIN I might add... we will definitely be coming back next time we're here!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Packed, band average. Couldn't get service after 30  minutes so went down the street.
One toilet for a whole bar full of people- just say no and head down to a smaller venue

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
I visited with my husband and my visiting from out of town friend on Saturday, 1.13.18; it was my first Whiskey Row experience. We got seats at the bar pretty quickly and stayed a few hours. I'd say we were there roughly from 2-6pm. 

I couldn't have been happier with the service we received for most of our stay. The team of three bartenders whose names I don't remember (pretty sure one was Maddie) worked seamlessly as a team, checked on everyone with great frequency and were incredibly friendly. We wouldn't have stayed nearly so long if it weren't for them. I personally am not drinking (the rest of my party was) at the moment and just had club soda and lime and they were happy to refill and even talked me into a few refills. 

At some point in our stay, we decided to get an appetizer. Our bartenders were happy to place the order. The food came out quickly and was delicious. Even as the place got more and more full, our team of bartenders never missed a beat and never sacrificed friendliness for efficiency. 

The band, Dozzi, came on, and we enjoyed them immensely. The bartenders told us they (band members) had all been sick and are usually even way better. I can't wait to see them again. 

Around 5pm, the night shift of bartenders began to arrive. The ladies we had been with all afternoon continued to provide amazing service as they got ready to cash out. It was more than 30 minutes before the new team even asked us if we were doing okay. The shift change was saddening. While the night team were efficient as far as serving people walking up to the bar, they were not so great at checking on those of us sitting at the bar. They also were not nearly as friendly. 

Had we arrived to this team of bartenders, we certainly wouldn't have enjoyed our time nearly as well or stayed as long as we did. 
We have certainly bragged about our day shift team to everyone in the following days. If ever I were to walk by and see those three again, I would definitely go in. 

There is only one bathroom stall (unisex) on the first floor, and the line gets long. There are multiple stall bathrooms on the second level, but a sign or something to indicate that might be beneficial for your establishment.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Seriously this place sucks, we waited an hour and a half for appetizers and it came out cold and burnt. We were one of two tables ? Server was awful, little blond with red lipstick on 5/1 / 18 2nd floor . Tacky live music band walking up to tables asking for tips... WTF??? So many other options, go somewhere else!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Fun place. Stopped in for a drink and to listen to some music. Good location right on the broadway strip. I'm sure it's exponentially more fun at night. But a good time nonetheless

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: This was probably one the word nights of my life. The general jackson showboat was said to be an amazing venue for family's to come and see sights and go on a nice evening Christmas boat ride with a meal and show down the Nashville river. Me, my granddaughter, and my two sons, one of which are autistic had flown in from Florida that day, and we thought that this would be an amazing way to start our family trip. We booked the evening cruise so we thought that it the sun would be going down, but when we got there, it was pitch black. You couldn't see the sights all you could see down the river was some lights right above the port-a potty factory.  The cruise was 6-9 pm, and at 6:00 it was already pitch black. My granddaughter wanted to get the fried green tomatoes as an appetizer but when I asked if the were hand fried our waiter said that most of the food was shipped in and frozen, she was very disappointed and upset. Our main course was the "Sam's Club Special". It consisted of bacon stuffed chicken, broccolini, and cold potatoes, the chicken was like chewing rubber, and the whole course was very disappointing, and for our desert we had a peppermint cheesecake. It was the only decent thing on the menu, even though we knew it was shipped in from a food distributor. It was now 8:00 pm and the show hadn't started yet, for the past 2 hours we had nothing to do but stare at our plates and twiddle our thumbs. The show finally starts and I look back to see my 11 year old granddaughter asleep on the table. The only person in our group that liked the showboat was my autistic son, overall the show and performers were very well talented and deserved more than a debut at the general Jackson Showboat. Me and my family were so appalled by the lack of good service.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
The Broadway bar scene is definitely not my thing on a Saturday night.  I don't know what I was thinking.  Perhaps if Broadway were shut down to vehicle traffic like Beale Street in Memphis or Bourbon Street in New Orleans, I'd have liked it a little better.  The problem is, I don't like overly crowded bars, cover charges, smoking, or music that is too loud to hear the person next to me.  Okay, now that I sound like an old lady...

Big Bang was a god send!

Even though it was very crowded, we managed to find 2 stools (and a table!) and we were served immediately.  We each had a beer and enjoyed the dueling pianos.  They did an awesome job from beginning to end and really put on a stellar performance.  They got the audience to interact.  Even the "security" guards got involved in little side shows of their own.  And of course, they recognized all of the birthdays and bachelorettes in the house.  They didn't give attitude when someone requested a song they didn't want to play, they were good sports and put on a fantastic show.

It was a great way for us to relax, have fun, and get away from the crowds outside.

We didn't pay a cover charge, but there was a bathroom attendant.  Sorry, but I refuse to tip someone who hands me a paper towel and squirts soap in my hand.  I am able to do those things myself, and I shouldn't have to pay for it just because you removed the paper towels and soap from the counter.  I know some bars and clubs have to do this to keep their bathroom from getting trashed, but Big Bang doesn't appear to attract a trashy club crowd.  Besides, I only went in the bathroom to blow my nose!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
As much as I am a huge fan of Cash's music, this museum was a bit disappointing. It's small, doesn't have many items to show, it's expensive for the value you get ($17) and overall a bit of a tourist trap. 

And I feel that the real problem is that most people who come in, enjoy it not because of what it has to offer, but because they're fans of Johnny Cash to begin with. I think the museum gets away with it because of the volume of tourists who want to visit.Surprisingly, we waited for 30 minutes in line just to get tickets. But we were ultimately disappointed.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Too loud and no COUNTRY music!!! Chicken sandwich was burnt and service was hit or miss. We won't be going back.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: ' Because your mine, I walk the line.' I am not big on country music, however I enjoy a couple of Johnny Cash tunes. We purchased tickets on Groupon and we were really excited to check out this museum. I have to say it was a tight fit entering the museum it's just not that big and there are hoards of people. I'm not big on looking at other people's clothes and admiring stuff like that but they had more than that. They had a lot of Johnny Cash paraphernalia and tunes blaring. We got to see his record collection and awards and some more personal touches such as letter to his wife. We got some Folsom Blues coffee after and that we enjoyed. The Johnny Cash museum was self-guided and it was interesting to learn more about The Man in Black. Oh, and I started to tear up upon exiting when they had the video for 'Hurt' playing. Yea, that almost had me balling because that song is just so raw and emotional.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
I am SO disappointed in this place. I will actually never come back. We went on Saturday around 2:00; Hollee was our server on the second floor. It wasn't crowded. We were in a party of 8 for my bachelorette party. 

We ordered a round of drinks and 3 appetizers at 1:00 PM. The drinks are expensive, which is totally fine, if the service matches. The service was horrible. We got our drinks after 15 minutes of waiting. No one brought water or came to check on us. 

We waited for an hour and a half for our appetizers. Every time we saw Hollee, we asked for an update and she said the food was COMING. Three times, we asked. Three times we were told the food was coming. Then, about almost 2 hours after ordering, she said the food would be on them and it was coming out now. Then, a manager came over and said that there was going to be no food and we were going to have it taken off the check. Well, obviously it will be taken off the check. It only makes sense - we didn't get any food. We even asked if they could still make it quickly and she said no ...

They discounted the drinks, but the entire bill should have been comped. This is the worst service I have ever had. There is NO EXCUSE to lie to customers about the status of their food, avoid them, or ignore them. We never were asked for a refill; someone from our party went to the empty bar 3 times for drinks because we weren't being asked for refills or new orders. Then, the management team had the nerve to say our food was comped. In order for something to be comped, it has to actually arrive. Food never arrived; there for it would have been illegal for us to be charged. 

The managers of this establishment never returned my phone call from Saturday afternoon. I am still waiting for them to contact me to further correct this experience. There are far too many other wonderful establishments with the exact same vibe and a far better experience. Try FGL House or Luke's instead of encountering such horrible service and a terrible experience.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I loved it here! It's a really cool place with some really unique memorabilia from his life. It's not overly huge but well worth it. There's a decent sized shop in the establishment as well along with a small coffee shop. It's reasonably priced and I would definitely go back.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Came in here because I heard the good music. It looks like a very family friendly place (which it is) and the food there is excellent! Only the best of bands play this place. The music is always the best!

Now I came in when it was busy so I can understand why it took 45 minutes to get our food. The waitress was very kind and respectful anyways. I ordered the Fried Catfish Dish and it was AMAZING!!! It wasn't too greasy and wasn't too dry. The catfish was very flavorful and crispy. It came with fries,hush puppies,and coleslaw. The fries were decent. Nothing special. The hush puppies were really good and made from scratch. And the coleslaw was also very tasteful and yummy. And that is why this place deserves 5 stars. Don't get mad that you don't get your food or drink right away,the place is usually really busy so you can't blame them. Next time I'm in Nashville I will come back! Thank guys!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: In from the ATL.  Place wins for vibe, atmosphere and location.  Burgers are a tasty treat and good quality.  Go here for tasty burger!  O-Straws on side, Texas burger, local brews on tap.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: If you are a country music fan, this is a must-see. A visit to Nashville without seeing the Opry is like traveling to Paris and skipping the Eiffel Tower. My face alternated between slack-jaw wonderment and cheek-busting smiles for the entire show, except those few moments when my eyes got a little misty. There were country legends and innovative new acts performing, everyone playing just two or three songs, with lots of banter and joking couching each performance. It was traditional, but not musty; entertaining, but not cartoonish; artistic, but not self-indulgent. I'll go back every time I'm in Nashville.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Had a dinner reservation here and canceled it at the hostess desk. Hostess came across as uninterested and bored. Didn't like the way she treated the customers in front of us (felt like was dismissive). Wish the initial experience had been good enough for us to come all the way into the restaurant to find out about the rest.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Im not sure why the yelp reviews for this place are so low. Its well rated elsewhere. Ive been here atleast 4 or 5 times and never had a bad experience.  The crowd is typically educated, not rough.  the dj is good. The service is good.   I was able to sing a salsa song which I was impressed that they had it, and people seemed to enjoy dancing to it.  Even on weeknights its pretty busy, never empty. You should visit!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: What a fun place to have dinner! The music was lively and the performer was great! I ordered the nachos with pulled pork, I got a huge heaping helping. They were absolutely delicious, definitely enough to share. The drinks were also delicious. I would go back for sure.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We were not country fans but we might be now. We new nothing About the Grand Ole Opry.  Didn't even know it was a live radio show.  A way cooler experience than I thought it would be. We saw a collection of old and new recording artists like Ashley Cambell and the White Family. Not terribly expensive either.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Wow, what an incredible and historic spot.  Rather than just being a venue to watch a music show, this is actually an experience!  We were here for about two hours and saw an incredible show, which showcased different kinds of country music, great presenters and even square dancing.  The place is huge and had the most incredible sound system...all music came out crystal clear!

This is such a unique and amazing experience and I recommend everyone to visit if you can...not a disappointment!

name: Third Man Records
text:
As someone who believes in what Jack White is doing, I stopped in because I traveled from NY to see his induction in the Nashville Walk of Fame.  

JW is single handedly reviving the vinyl industry and this store represents his complete devotion to this.

The place was crowded with other people who believe.  The staff was very busy and did their best to accommodate everyone including people who insisted on taking their time up with chit chat.

I bought a vinyl copy of "Elephant", five 7" records (I don't have a record player) and some other things because I believe in this artist and I support him.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
The crawfish poppers and shrimp and grits were great. The made in store chips were good too. My only complaint is way too much food overall. The portion size was huge. Consider splitting dishes or skipping the appetizers.

Good acoustics, albeit loud and the bands that night were good also.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Stopped in to see Steve but Jasmine was tending bar. The bartenders at BB's always hit it out of the park. Jasmine is very friendly and energetic. Steve always has something new up his sleeve. Some of the best mixed drinks you will find. You will always enjoy the Music in BB's. The menu has a full range of food. You will always find something you like.

name: Music City Tippler
text: Went for drinks later on a Friday night. This place was packed! Interesting mix of people, and definitely a change of pace from most night spots in Nashville in that it was a club vibe. Drinks were good. Try the house made fireball-delish! The drink special was preacher's daughter... Bible Belt y'all.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
I have a real fondness for BAD. This is the first place that we are when myself and three of my friends touched down in Nashville. 
The food is pretty good while not the best in town. I wouldn't recommend this place if you're searching for a revolutionary culinary experience.
BUT! 
This place was never packed (when many many other places in the area were) and if you want somewhere that looks rad, has awesome service and you and your friends can have a great time, BAD would be good (sorry for the pun) for you.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great place for a burger.  It's literally in the alley but bright and fun inside.  There is no breakfast on the menu.  All good. Burgers and chips were just fine.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Three stars only because the tour seemed rushed.  We got the total access pass which was wonderful except at Opryland.  You could only make your reservation for the tour in person.  Why?!  So we arrived way early for the first tour on a Sunday,  which in my opinion was a waste of time.  The actual building was amazing to see.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: What a rich musical and historical treat!  You made it this far to Nashville do not skip a night at the roots of country music.  You will not be disappointed.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Didn't eat here, but the staff was awesome and the music was great. Recommend if you are into Blues Music.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Saw the building from afar and thought it was a church, but when we got closer, we saw people eating and drinking inside so we thought to check it out. The interior seemed decorated and furnished with tons of seating options to choose from. We picked what looked to be comfy couch corner and immediately sunk to the floor- the cushions definitely lost all fluff awhile ago. 
We tried the local flight to see what brews Nashville  had to offer which was pretty good, then ended with a couple draft pours of our choosing. My terrapin IPA from Athens, GA that was on special was super yum- had a hint of citrus to it! But my friend's porter was awful- it tasted so bitter with some sour that we felt like it had gone bad or we got the bottom of the keg? We left it un-drank. 
Our waitress also had a bit of an attitude, but we're attributing that to the full tray of glassware she broke minutes before our arrival.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
The personnel working the hostess stand are nearly incompetent. We paid cover for 4 people and walked in. We went to sit down at an open table and a waitress cleared it off for us and wiped it down. Just as we were ready to sit down someone (maybe a manager) told us that we couldn't sit down and there was a wait list we needed to add our names to. Guess who managed the wait list?! Yup! The hostesses!

So we put our names on the list, went to buy some drinks at the bar. There were 4 seats open at the bar so we tried to sit there. The female bartender, who would barely take our order, told us we couldn't sit in 2 opens spots because someone who was dancing was sitting there.  (Where I am from when you leave your spot, they put a water out with a napkin over it to save your spot, this was not there.) 

When the couple came back from dancing they saw that people had gathered around their spot and just ordered from the bar and went back to the dance floor. So they weren't even expecting to get their seat back. Nor did the bartenders tell them that they had turned away two couples by saving their seat.

If my boyfriend didn't have his heart content on seeing lives blues music I would have told them all where to go. I am a paying customer just like everyone else. 

Let's talk about that, too. They advertise that they have no cover. Tonight it was $10 per person. So just expect to pay something at the door even if you have heard separately.

It's sad that a legend's name is on this establishment.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I've been here twice and have only visited their gift shop. They sell some nice souvenirs.

If you're a fan of country music, you will have to check out this place! I will have to come back here for a show one of these days.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Historical. You absolutely have to go if you're in Nashville. Check out the mailboxes and the dressing rooms.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
The moment I walked into this place I had a smile on my face...probably because it reminded me of that old show in Disneyland...the Bear Jamboree?  However there were no furry characters in this spot (unless of course Charlie Daniels counts). 

The Grand Ole Opry is filled with music history and live country to kick up your heals to.  Definitely round up your posse and spend the money for the tour.  I felt it was much better than the Ryman tour (even though if you have time I would recommend that too).  We came back the same night we took the tour for one of their live shows which was such a great time (it really doesn't matter who is playing...it is a great experience).  Honestly this is a "must do" situation in Nashville that you won't regret (unlike all the fried food you will consume in this town).  

This is not the O.K.-Corral so gallop straight to this venue!

name: Anthem
text: They will not serve u water. The bartenders say they dont serve water but they will give u a dixie cup to fill up in the bathroom. They also say if u can afford molly then u can afford $5 for a bottle of water. Thats definatley not a policy u see in any other clubs like LA, Vegas, San Diego or Miami. Other than that it would be a cool spot but they def need to change this policy and improve on the sound and lighting system.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: What can you say?  It is the Grand Old Opry.  Had a great time, listened to some fabulous music, watched some tremendous banjo pickin', fiddle playin' musicians.  Well worth the visit.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Awesome burgers. No buffalo chicken. Catfish was good. Club sandwich was ok. Chicken tenders were pretty good. Fries are breaded so good if that's the way you like them.  Seating was perfect and no wait but busy and fun atmosphere.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: A must see if you are in Nashville - so much music history!! Highly recommend!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Horrible service, they got my meal wrong then argued with me about it and had the audacity to bring it back to me.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Our tour guide, Linda, made this trip fantastic! I've wanted to come here since I fell in love with country music at a young age.  

We started off with a movie by Blake Shelton and then moved through the parts of the Opry House.  It was amazing to see backstage where Nashville is filmed at times, and then move through each dressing rooms, the post office box area, and each special place.  I loved hearing how Trisha Yearwood was a tour-guide, and Alan Jackson delivered mail.  Dierks Bentley got his start as a stagehand.  Just amazing tidbits you didn't know and that made the tour memorable.  

Our guide was knowledgeable, funny, and personable.  The building, and history, speak for themselves and you are in complete awe of the sense of legacy.  The only bad experience we had was as checking out with our photos we asked if we could get just one and the woman told us very nastily that no, we could not.  A simple question, asked nicely, deserves a much nicer response!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Sopped by chance. Great cozy singer songwriter venue. Great food. Met the owner Rose, very sweet lady. Has a real heart for the songwriters. Do you want a corporate owned type bar? No, not the place. A must stop.  Awesome

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
If you are a fan of classic country music, you have to attend a show. Worth the money! Even the Backstage Tour is a must-do to check off the bucket list.

Side Note: It's surrounded by an outlet mall and Chuy's. Kinda sad that the exterior is so commercial but the experience inside makes up for the lacking thrill outside.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Wow.  Super cool place.  Service is deplorable at best.  The bartenders either need a bar back or 2 more bartenders on.    While the bartender is very nice, there needs to be more of them.   Haven't tried the food because they've been too busy for us to order.

name: Third Man Records
text: One of the most creative and inspiring spaces ever put together. The staff is incredible and the music is endless. Attending a concert of movie in the Blue Room is a must if you have the opportunity. Don't forget to make your very own record!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Wandered into Belcourt Taps for a beer last night and was treated to some pretty good local music. It's a chill, divey-ish bar that serves food, has a full bar, and has several local beers on tap. And live music EVERY NIGHT. My first visit (just for a beer) was pretty good - I would definitely try Belcourt Taps again (maybe after a movie at the Belcourt - right across the street). Maybe next time I'll hang out longer and try their food and listen to some live music!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: This is one of my favorite honky tonks in Nashville. The music is great and very entertaining. Plus you can start a tab and you get your card back, just in case you forget to close out. Gotta love the fiddle, if not... you are in the wrong town.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Went on a Thursday night. Service was very attentive and eager to make dinner suggestions. We thought the food was very good.  Wife had ribs, I had BBQ salmon. Ribs were really meaty, more than she could eat. 
House band (BB King all stars) was just awesome.  Got to love the horn section! Just a great night!!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We had been to the Ryman Auditorium a few nights before, and while we enjoyed the show, we HATED the hard wood pews with no leg room between the rows.   If I had to do it over again, I would have skipped the Ryman despite the good music.  If you only have one night to view a terrific show with good views from all areas, and comfortable seats, go to the Grand Ole Opry on Opryland Drive.   You won't be disappointed,

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
I didn't dock the rating for this, but don't think you are going to this blues club to hear blues. Went twice this weekend and heard a mix of slick and bland 70s and 80s soft rock. 

Stopped on Friday night. This was the only place charging a cover. After we paid to get in, we found that there was no place to sit and we couldn't even get to the bar to get a beer. Didn't stay long because there are many choices in the area. 

Went for lunch the next day. It wasn't crowded but the service was extremely lackadaisical and very slow. The food was okay. The best thing I had was a tasty hummus platter, generous portion. 

We gave it two tries because of the iconic name, but I wouldn't go back.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
The Tippler has a very smooth Al Capone style to it.  The Roaring '20s have some nostalgic appeal, and this place has done a fantastic job of recreating that feeling and that appeal -- but in Nashville and not New York or Chicago.  The ambiance for a good drink, a night out with a significant other, or just an encounter with a flapper are all present at the Tippler.  

The bartenders do very well from premium cocktails, to beer and wine.  Additionally there is a menu that goes beyond small bites and into the realm of hearty enough to make it a drink at the Tippler, food at the Tippler, and then finish it off with more drinks at the Tippler to complete your evening.

There is a coat check and a valet.  People will be dressed to the 9s and others will be in jeans and a hipster t-shirt.  They take all types at the Tippler -- including you.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The food is delicious! The gumbo is on point. However, the wait staff could use some pointers on hospitality. I thought being in the south people were supposed to be friendly but that doesn't seem to be the case.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The food was very good. Had ribs, tender and fall off the bone yumminess! Music was great! Service on the other hand was not very good. We were seated at a dirty table and it took forever to get it cleaned up. Wait staff seemed to have trouble finding a towel to clean the table with .Another thing that was disappointing ,we received our appetizers and entrees all at the same time. Service definitely needs to improve. We would go back, hopefully the service will be improved upon.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Have you seen The Babadook?  The Exorcist?  American Idol?  Have you been scared?  I have a horror story for you:

Being on a budgeted vacation, we thought the Groupon for Belcourt Taps was a great deal.  Little did we know, we were in for a bit of a surprise.  

Walking up to the taps we were horrified--no, screw that...earth-shatteringly afraid--to see Guiness and Blue Moon as twenty percent of the options available.  While deciding a bartender even told us not to pick the shandy outright.  That gave us, like, seven other options to choose from out of five or so.  We picked a few different IPAs, a saison and a few others we both forget.  We sipped them politely but as we left the establishment we found ourselves being completely honest, as all people do in the company of absolute naked truth: We hated all of them.  Not a single one hit a resonant note and we were ecstatic to finish them.  

The nachos were below par as well.  They were cold and they exuded a terribly proletariat attempt to disguise "refuse" as "finger food."  The toppings should be cold, yes.  The pico, the sour cream, the olives, et al.  But should the cheese be cold, dear reader?

Should the cheese be cold?

We lie awake in our hotel at this hour thinking that.  They gave us a two room with two beds.  We were charged extra for that, but mind it not, dear reader.  The extra weight from our sorrows of this trip shall be supported by the extra queen-sized mattress, as we lie awake, winking at the ceiling, wondering where we went wrong.  

Will anything cold ever be good again?  I'm sipping a microwaved, scalding hot $1.50 Fat Bottom Knockout IPA with relish, absolute decadence in comparison, knowing full well that both things that are cold and local beers will never be the same.

Nothing will be.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Amazing music, and incredibly awesome staff. Specifically Alexandria. I can on a Thursday night and she was awesome. The music was something you won't be able to experience anywhere else. I love it.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
Once enjoyed this place.  Today's burger fell apart and watery, the bun was old and cold.  Wife 's salad was also old and whilted. 

Likely to skip this place next time we are heading to the theater. Music was good.   Back Ally Diner needs to be better to compete against new establishments downtown.  There are other choices.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
In honor of Mardi Gras I had the shrimp etouffee and cheesy grits. It was a spiritual experience. I left with such a deeply satisfied feeling. Seriously, it was so good it was mood altering. 

I don't drink but my friend liked the bar bourbon he was served. The place is a well-kept dive, the staff a bit punk/goth but friendly, the service was fine and I am now working on how to replicate that dinner because it was so excellent and I live so very far away from there. 

We went early in the evening and the live music had not started yet, so the place was pretty quiet, with BB King playing in the background of course. People who live in Nashville are lucky.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Save your money and buy a ticket to an actual show. Tour was rushed and was mad up mostly of videos you could find online at home. Only giving two stars because at the end you did get to stand on stage.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We took a tour of the Acuff House (limited time offer) to start off our day, but it can be done anytime because it's self-guided. It take you into the house that the Opry built for Roy Acuff 30 years ago. It was filled with mostly images and memorabilia from his life. The Backstage Tour at the Grand Ole Opry was led by Karen, who did an outstanding job as our guide. They take you to several spots that you can snap photos of and see where the stars spend their time. The tour moves quickly and you're not able to really soak in the history too much, which is a definite drawback. Nonetheless, they do a terrific job in the time they're given and it's a must-see if your around Nashville.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
We've been coming here for a lonnngggg time, in fact, every time I visit Nashville we end up here at some point.  And, there's good reason...

BEER.  That's the main reason!  They have a huge selection of beer that they rotate seasonally with a large amount being draft.  They also have a gigantic selection of bottles, you will be pretty busy picking out that one beer you just gotta have.

Service has always been spectacular, never had a bad experience.  Wait staff knows their beers and are helpful with their recommendations.  

The layout is very comfy...the front area consists of a long stretch of couches and love seats to relax on that are overlooking the walls lined with garage doors...when they open those up on a nice day it's like sitting on your back patio, but better!  The inside is this huge cavern with a 150 foot bar and plenty of seating.  Great place to see a game, too.  They have lots of TVs and Projectors to keep your attention.  Additionally, they have a separate game room with pool tables.

Lining the walls are hundreds of saucers where only the very drunk and vigilant get a spot.  Join the club, starting drinking a lot of beers and get your name on the wall.  This was one of the first spots I ever saw with a drinking club.  I'd have a few plates if I lived in N'ville, which makes me glad I don't.

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text:
This pub's main strengths are decent bar food, well-behaved clientele,  a beautiful ambience, and location, location, location. 

We ordered a full order of fish & chips. Being from Milwaukee, we're not easily pleased in this department; and neither of us really cared for the rather bland tasting Harp lager batter of this order. There was no TRUE "Beer" flavor in the batter, it barely registered strong enough for my taste. Perhaps I'm used to the stronger Northern preparations where the bottle of brew smacks you in the forehead. This was just not enough for me.

It WAS better than most fish & chips I've had in TN, however; and the lemon tartar sauce was hands-down perfect. If you're not a fanaticist, you will be pleased. If you are, it's in the "okay" category. I weep, I weep for my hometown. 

Adding to my calorie-fest, we split an order of Bailey's Irish-cream cheescake with chocolate sauce and chocolate graham crust. It was indescribably good. I had't really looked forward to it; preferring my cheesecake a little plainer, but this one changed my mind. Live wild, I say. Wild! ;) The flavors were perfectly complementary and not overdone. The amount of Bailey's was just subtle enough not to be too sweet.

So, this place is what you call RELIABLE. Reliable for decent drinks, decent staff, decent food. 

The staff was a wee bit harried that night, but it was CMA fest- and they handled it VERY well. You can ALWAYS bring an out-of-towner in here. They maaayy see a stah!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Awesome beer and live music. Super knowledgeable staff! Located a little bit of a walk from the downtown full of typicaly honky-tonks, it's nice to get to a place that's a little more original. TV's for the sports guys was a plus for our group. If you love beer, this is a must when in Nashville!

name: Third Man Records
text:
This place is not very big but definitely unique. Some people might be expecting a big record store and this place is not it. A colleague, who is a big fan of Jack White, wanted to stop by and get some record albums. 

We came in after having lunch at the Peg Leg Porker down the corner. The store is laid out beautifully - open and clean. It also have many interesting machines from the past that are still functioning. There's a small recording studio like a phone booth where you pay to go in and records some music onto a vinyl. A photo booth and a coin-operated monkey band. A bit of fun carnival nostalgia.

 Next door appears to be the Third Man Record's recording studio with a beautiful metallic door. Visiting a place like this has been most enjoyable.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
They don't call it Music City for nothing. Waffles and waltzes, honky tonks, juke joints; music 24/7; mostly country music, which is my kind of tune-age. We stayed near the downtown area, and Broadway Street, is like the Times Square or Fisherman's Wharf of Nashville. Everything is there; The Ryman, Country Music Hall of Fame, Johnny Cash Museum, and so on...I was lucky to have a Nashvillian show me some sights not on the tourist map, and Belcourt Taps was one of those. Let me say, up front: it was simply Awesome, with great burgers and even greater music.

Belcourt Taps has lots of beers, Fried Pickles and Fried Green Tomatoes, but, let's be real--who in Nashville doesn't serve these items? The real charm of Belcourt Taps comes in a other ways. 1) The ambiance, complete with a front porch and easy, friendly service. It really feels like you've stepped into someone's living room for a spell. 2) Their crazy, amazing STUFFED burgers. Honestly, the burgers alone are worth the drive. 3) The music. For me, this is what made Belcort Taps stand out and above any Broadway honky tonk or juke joint.

For pictures and a more thorough review, check out my site: www.TNBTA.com

Cheers!

name: Third Man Records
text:
Super fun. The place has an especially exciting, creative energy. 
Everyone there was so friendly. Jess is the delightful person who showed us how to use the record booth and the song came out GREAT! There's a ton of cool stuff in the store too. So glad we stopped in! :)

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: Fun place to hang out and get away from the crowd.  The place is very busy and it requires patients to get a drink because of the crowd surrounding the bar.  The karaoke is fun to listen to and the atmosphere is very fun.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
What a cool spot. 
I'm a bit disappointed to find out that this is part of a chain, but this fact aside, I easily fell in love with the beautiful building and interior, which allow for lounging with friends at a laid-back pace.
