The weekend we came in they had a super large convention going on for sorority sisters.  No not young college students.  This must have been some kind of reunion after 40 plus years cause the average age was 60 and up. They seemed to be having a great time.  So due to this our first night we had two full size beds instead of a king.  The next day they did give us another room with a king size bed but it was a hassle to pack, leave our luggage downstairs until the room was ready later.  The front desk staff seemed as if they were at their wits end of having much patience.  Not the most friendly.

The beds had nice comfy sheets, comforters and pillows, and the bed luckily was comfy.  It looked to be fairly clean until I saw streak marks all over the shower and bathroom mirror.  Not to happy with a quick clean job.  For the money you pay here, I think we paid $160 a night, I guess I just expected much cleaner rooms.

The pool was pretty and they had a nice bar downstairs.  I just think you can find nicer hotels than this one in the area.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Simply a really great bar.  Always fun, different music.  $5 beers and drinks ( a la 5-spot name).   And staff that clearly enjoy their jobs...

name: The End.
text: Walked in and it seemed like a really cool underground sort of punk venue, which is my favorite kind of show and place, and then waited 40 minutes for two beers. Single old man running the bar for a sold out show - wasn't his fault, I felt bad for him because he was completely in over his head but there was an entire bar length of people waiting ages and ages and ages to get served.

name: The Valentine
text: Wouldn't let me and my husband in the door bc he had ripped (buckle) jeans, then let the girl behind us in with ripped jeans. When I asked why he said girls could go in with ripped jeans but guys could not. Go somewhere else. They suck.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I see that this place receives mixed feelings from its customers, so I'll throw a mostly positive one into the hat.

I love the fact that the hotel is away from the hustle and bustle of downtown, even though I spent my weekend there (distance wasn't bad at all). The lobby, restaurant, and bar were absolutely beautiful. I did stay in the midst of a renovation, but could hardly tell except for when the elevator stopped on the 2nd and 3rd floors.

My room was quite spacious and accommodating. No complaints there.

I was accidentally given a key to an occupied room (no accidents), and the lady at the desk seemed shocked and told me that their system does that from time to time. It was resolved quickly. I also had to walk quite a ways to get to my room, though. I guess that just comes with being a large hotel. Not much they can do.

P.S. - I booked through Expedia and got a rate about a third of the usual rate.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Literally left my baby's carrier inside at closing time and asshole security on Tuesday, January 2nd 2019, wouldn't even let me in just to GRAB IT so I could carry my child to our car and home. NEVER COMING HERE AGAIN! Can't believe the guy at the door was such an asshole he would't even look for me. He just sat there shaking his head. I had to run my freezing child to the car with my family because he was to lazy to help. Screw this place they are NOT family friendly!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Touristy places like this are often over-priced, and nowadays can be found in almost every medium or large sized city.  This location isn't a must go to place for locals, and probably gets most business from out-of-towners.  The food is decent, and they actually have some parking (which is rare for most downtown Nashville restaurants).  My biggest issue I have with the Nashville Hard Rock is the volume of the recorded music.  They sometimes have live acts, but their recorded music is played so loud you literally can't have a conversation with others unless you're almost shouting.  You might actually become nauseous.  For this reason we've only been here a couple of times. Don't think we'll go back any time soon.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
We stopped into numerous "honky tonk" bars along Broadway and this was my favorite.  It might be because I was totally in love with the band performing on the top floor.  They were great!

Three total floors, with a heated rooftop bar as well.  Despite the very chilly temperatures we could comfortably stand right by the open garage doors.  There was plenty of room on the second and third floors to enjoy the great live music - no fighting through a jam-packed crowd, finally!!!

Staff was great and the beer selection was better than I expected.

Definitely the highlight of my bar-hopping!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: It is my first time in Nashville, absolutely love "Whiskey Bent Saloon"!! Great energy, awesome live music entertainment. The entertainers will take any music request at no charge (if they know it then they will certainly play it). Guns N Roses hands down my favorite. My drink was made pretty good too! Now this is my kinda bar. Fun, upbeat, lots of good vibes, and just really good engagement. I'd definitely recommend! Thank you for a great time Whiskey Bent!

name: Legends Corner
text: Very cool bar with really good live music. Right in the start of the heart of Downtown Nashville this is a great place to stop and check our all the photos and history on the walls and have a good drink for a great price!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Always such a great atmosphere.  Live jazz music which is never to loud and the food is delicious.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
I love this place. It's so small and squished and smells like grease and beer. True classic Nashville spot. I have found myself here multiple times as their beer is cheap and they have cheap food too! 

I'm all about the Miller High Life's for $2.50 and there's something called the "Stimulus Package" which is a MHL, all beef giant hot dog, and chips for $5.00. Lol . Absolutely awesome. Love it so much.

There's always decent bands in there as well. Bands in Nashville can be annoying sometimes when the lecture customers on tipping. We're all grown adults, we understand you work for tips. We get it.... makes me roll my eyes. I found that happening here a few times and if I was a server or owner would not let the band make my customers feel like that. 

This place is definitely one of my faves and I will be back next time I'm in Nashville.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: This place is pretty cool and I really hope that they can make a go of it. When you walk into it it kind of reminds you of walking into a Mexican themed at Disney World. There was obviously a lot of thought and effort that went into the look and ambience of the mall. My friend and I decided to eat at The Madeira Cafe that is located inside the mall, and a separate review has been left for them. They had very interesting food counters as well as little retail stores, and a small Grocery and bakery that was located in the front of the mall. We got to see a live Mexican band which was very entertaining, and if I hadn't eaten and painful I would have loved to have gotten something from either the ice cream counter or the bakery. If you are in the Brentwood area this would be a cool place to check out if you're looking for something to eat, a place to rest for a bit, or place to pick up some snacks or groceries.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We stopped by late Saturday afternoon for a snack and to listen to the band. The Southwest quesadillas was a large portion with chips, salsa and sour cream and the chipotle bbq sauce and roasted tomatoes made it unique. Nice spot to rest upstairs and enjoy live music with reasonably priced food and friendly service.

name: Red Rooster Bar & Music Hall
text:
Calling this joint a bar and a music hall is like calling a used condom a miniature shopping bag. If you were born with perfect hearing and you didn't like that, this is where you come to lose it all. The music too loud, the drinks bad, and the fresh-out-of-teenage crowd that shows up are like buzzards over a dead kill. 

Man! I am sounding like a buzzkill given how many times over the past few years I develop amnesia and decide to give this cocky place another shot. I always regret it! There is always a crazy line with someone throwing up, another taking pictures of that, someone else punching someone else into the puke pool and the cops running in with their Tasers on. It feels like you have just entered the set of an action movie where someone laced everyone's Coke with cocaine!

Once inside the music is so loud your sinus problems disappear, because your eyes would have melted and leaked everything that they had been diligently holding back for all those years. You wander in blind and bump into some poor sob of a waitresses carrying tubes of colorful intoxicants. All of them come from the same vodka company - Vomit. At the end of the night, the floor of this hallowed dance club is covered with a strange slime that the establishment scrapes off and sells it to 3M, the makers of glue and other sundry. 

I guess the lack of a good multi-tiered sophisticated dance club like those in bigger cities forces youngsters to flock here for their weekly groping and grinding fixes. So here is a message to all you tycoons wondering what is the next big thing - a good dance club that's in sync with the times.

Sorry if I have offended anyone with this review. You should get back to studying anyway. You have an exam tomorrow.

name: Music City Center
text: I love this place. This is my 2nd convention here and both of them were a blast. Wear comfortable shoes because this place is huge.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My favorite place in the Gulch! Great atmosphere and entertainment. My waitress, Ariel was fantastic! She recommended some delicious appetizers. The fettuccine carbonara was amazing and the coconut mojito was refreshing. I highly recommend this restaurant.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We stopped in here on a Tuesday around lunch time and it wasn't busy. They had live music talent that's actually talented. Why aren't there more reviews here ?!? I would've taken a picture of the Hot Chicken Torta sandwich but honestly it was too good and I inhaled it. My wife had the same problem with the Chicken n' Waffle nuggets. They have a children's menu also.

name: Second Fiddle
text: This may have been my favorite place while visiting nashville. The music was out of control amazing both nights we went here. The bartenders are fantastic and pour great drinks. Cool Atmosphere and while crowded, it didn't seem too crowded which is good since I don't do crowds ha

name: Robert's Western World
text: Fun little place on Broadway! Enjoyed the music, definitely a little older crowd. The drinks were very reasonably priced and wish we would've tried the food. It was pretty busy but we still found a place to sit and got our drinks pretty quickly. Really enjoyed all the fun decorations and authentic atmosphere. Not bad!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We went here on a Saturday night, it was pretty packed as was expected. We waited for 25 minutes for a table, while we waited we sat at the bar and had drinks and listened to the live band, both were excellent!! We got to our table on the 3rd level and it was so dark up there we had to look at the menu with the flashlights on our phones!! lol (no joke) The server was great, had a real upbeat attitude, the food was delicious as well!! I would highly recommend this place , and plan on going back...

name: Robert's Western World
text: My favorite spot on Broadway, no bro country here. But don't take it from a guy from the south side of Chicago, go yourself.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I have so often heard "what a great venue" applied to the Ryman. If you like paying $16 for 12 ounces of wine, sitting in church pews, and waiting in a ridiculous line for a bathroom then that may be the case. But start to finish this was a rip off and a hassle at every turn. I've learned my lesson seeing shows at the Ryman.

name: Robert's Western World
text: It was Friday after Thanksgiving, 2014.  There were 4 of us and it was our first time in Nashville. We wandered into Robert's, and instead of staying for one drink, we stayed for a few hours, and had a great time! The music was great, the drinks were cold, and the food was outstanding!  Especially the burgers and fried pickles!  The bouncer was great!  He made sure we were seated in a good spot to enjoy the live music, and checked on us periodically to make sure we were happy.  And WE WERE! Excited to go back next year!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This 5 star review assumes you are not constricted by sitting anywhere under the balcony. Make sure and get a seat in the first 10 rows or anywhere in the balcony.  Sound and sites await. Super venue. ..the sound veritably echos through the ancient timbers.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
There is no substitute for Bennys bologna..  The man is a walks on water next that grill.  

He was not in this visit, but sandwich was still okay.  Not the usual great

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
We had been here about 5 years ago and decided to try it again. It was excellent the first time and were a bit hesitant about going back....afraid we would be disappointed from our first experience.......WE WEREN'T!
Kenny was our waiter and everything he suggested was excellent! From the filet to the wine pairing, dessert and the music. We will be back!!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place was recommended to me by a friend - and I'm so happy I listened. Nicest staff, great drinks and food and amazing music. It was definitely one of my favorite stops in downtown Nashville. I was very impressed by one of the waitresses especially; in a completely packed bar, she couldn't have been better or nicer. I will definitely be coming back here next time I visit Nashville.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: They had a great band playing tonight. Lively crowd and very fun!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Stopped into this bar, restaurant while visiting Nashville during the CMA fest. Saw the band playing I. The front and thought we would have a drink. This places really surprised us. Two band areas one in the front and one in the back, it also has room upstairs and the inside is amazing with character. We ordered a couple of drinks and an appetizer. You must try the loaded tots. Truly delicious, they have queso bacon, onions and more. So good. Our waitress "Anna ". Was very friendly and was able to suggest a few drink items that we enjoyed. You can pass right by, but don't pass it by, good value, great music, delicious drinks and tasty eats.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Uptown funky chic...this micro chain is located in the Gulch section of Nashville ...far from the boots and ball caps of Nashvegas. Situated adjacent to two upscale competitors (Watermark and Octopus restaurants ) Sambuca carves out  amazing jazz club atmospherics with succulent menu choices. Salmon , scallops, filets , chops and some thoughtful apps/ small plates will nourish most discriminating palates. Signature cocktails, such as a basil infused vodka mojito makes early or late night rendezvous' on couch sided tables très bon....
Try the southern inspired tomahawk cut smoked pork chop with prosciutto mac and cheese ..enough for two.
But tis the quality of exceptional musicians that make this hallmark unique. Jazz combos playing crossover R&B, funk, motown at a listenable level makes for a full evening out, including dancing.
Our friday was graced with the the silky vocals of Herchel Bailey, grandson to Country Hall of Fame member, D. Ford Bailey,  who crooned his way through renditions of Marvin Gaye, Stevie Wonder, James Brown and Bruno Mars...
Sambuca is more than an apertif, it is an entrée of delish

name: Robert's Western World
text: My son and I were on a road trip,family golf, etc. stopped in here for a drink. This is the most authentic fun place you can go in Nashville. Don't miss it. Went back several times

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Hostess was efficient (not warm), and the server was nice enough.  We should have researched a bit more before going in and sitting down.

The menu was limited and the prices outrageous for what we were expecting.  It seemed like a minimal effort menu for a maximum $$.

We opted to get up and leave, because we could not see paying over $20 for roast chicken!  Our son was ready to order the $50 prime rib, but we informed him we would get this at J. Alexander's, instead.  Really, this place is no Ruth's Chris (and certainly not Jeff Ruby's).

After reading some other's reviews (mind you, after the fact, on Open Table), it was hilariously summarized as a place to go if you're having a mid-life crisis, and trying to rekindle something with your spouse, except since it's so loud, you won't succeed in having any worthwhile conversation, due to the odd smooth jazz renditions of Michael Jackson.

I suspect the reviews are high because people probably feel embarrassed that they went there and spent far too much money, trying to look like they know upscale dining and entertainment.  Alas, Tin Angel was our more than satisfying back up plan.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Good music and fun atmosphere but I asked for about 4 drinks from the bar after being turned down the 4th time bc they didn't carry an extensive cider and beer list I gave up and settled on wine. I got the champagne chicken I thought the food was ok. It sounded way better on the menu than the food actually tasted. I would go bAck but more for drinks apps and the band rather than a nice dinner. On a plus note they advertise gluten free options clearly on there menu and it's nice having options.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: They where super accommodating for our 7 month old at nearly 8:30 at night! Relieving since many restaurants in the area don't even have high chairs. The food was good! But the service was meh.. We asked for a Cocktail menu for another round of drinks and extra salad dressing and never got either... But it was tasty. The buca begneit (spelling?) was the best!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: One of the best steak I ever had. Miso Seabas was insanely good. It was a perfect Valentines dinner date indeed. We'll surely come back soon...

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
This place is just amazing ! The food is great , the drinks and everyone is so nice. Such a fun place 
I highly recommend to anyone who wants to enjoy the Hispanic culture. Date night would never be better !

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
We were greeted at the door by an incredibly snarky hostess who told us we had to be away from our table within a certain time as they had a second booking.
The food was tasty, sadly cold!

On the upside, Jesse our waiter-- absolutely lovely and the wine selection absolutely fabulous! 

Our tip-- ask for Jesse!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: My friend and I hesitated about this tour because we know very little about country music. Decided to pay for the self-guided tour (which by the way was discounted with my military ID). The movie before the tour , the history about the Ryman and the musicians all over the auditorium were incredible. I was actually surprised by how many people I actually knew. Not sure if the backstage tour is worth the extra $10, but the self-tour was worth every penny!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We made a 6:30 reservation to listen to music and have some drinks for a girls night. They sat us right in front of the stage. The music was good, but loud if you wanted to have a conversation. We were waiting on our one friend and wanted to have some drinks and hang out before dinner. Our waitress kept coming over to see if we wanted food every 5 minutes and we told her we just want to drink and will order food later. Around 7, she came over again to see if we wanted to order and said we are booked solid tonight and have a 13 top VIP  table coming at 8:30 and will be sitting where you are. She said if we weren't done we would have to move to the lounge area upstairs. I don't think we should have been warned about being kicked out an hour and a half before another table was coming because we weren't as "important".  After that I didn't even want to give this place our business and that comment immediately ruined our night. Anyways our food wasn't good for how expensive it was. My friends chicken was dry and the beignets were cold in the middle. Our waitress was nice, but pushy and I do feel bad for her that she was the one telling us we would have to leave at 8:30. That comment should have came from the manager and not been put on her. So if you plan on listening to music and enjoying your night...this is not the place unless you are a "VIP". I would never recommend this restaurant!

name: Robert's Western World
text: You come for the great country music, but it's hard to imagine a better fried bologna sandwich.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Traveld from Chicago for friends birthday and they took away my 22 year olds friends I'd because "it didn't look real". We are all clearly of age and why would we travel 8 hours for nothing... Asked to talk to manager and they told us we weren't allowed to speak to a manager without police supervision. This was on the last day of our trip (Sunday) and it was 6:30. We were just trying to get dinner. Will not return ever again. I suggest going to the tin roof on demonbreun..

name: Legends Corner
text: Great bands but no draft beer. Service is great and fast, even in a Saturday night. Be prepared to tip the band if you like them, Legends doesn't charge a cover so you can too the band!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Pretty descent spot on Broadway. Good music and a fun atmosphere. I would have preferred better beer but still a 4 star establishment. There is a pretty good amount of seating down stairs and some fun bar sports up stairs. I'll probably hit up again next time I'm in Nashville.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: They offered a Mother's Day brunch.  Being from out of town we didn't know any better. Well, I could tell they don't normally offer Sunday brunch because it was poorly done.  First of all once we were sat it took a good 15min before anyone approached us for drinks.  It was not very clean. The restaurant looked like it was trying to be a fancier place but was struggling big time.  Lots of little and big things that needed attention. Food offerings were only ok.  There was barely ever any fruit out and what was out was picked over.  Two pluses were that the orange juice was very good and they had a band playing that was very enjoyable.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: AMAZING brisket Mac n cheese! Great vibe and got to listen to some really awesome music from Blue Honey! We were visiting Nashville, but will definitely return if we are in Nashville again!

name: Legends Corner
text:
The Legends Corner is pretty damn literal. The bar is located on a corner, and many legends have played here.

The place is on a slope so there are two entrances on two different floors. There are two bars, but when I went, the upstairs bar was closed. The downstairs bar was crowded as a result.

The stage is small but there's tons of room to stand, and some tables.

There's also great memorabilia everywhere, from said legends. There was a signed acoustic from Johnny Cash, a 5-neck guitar I can only assume was from Rick Nielsen, and lots of other cool things.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Loved this place.  Spent three nights in Nashville, visited many places, ended up here all three nights.  Great old school country music, my understanding is they play all pre-1979 music so no bro country - you can find that just about everywhere else.  Great bands, great music, friendly waitresses, the Johnny & June mural next to the bathroom is awesome.

name: Second Fiddle
text:

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
This is a great place to go for dinner, drinks, or just a night out with friends to listen to live music. The band during our visit played jazz, and appeared to be very talented. (The music is a little loud for conversation, so request to sit away from the stage if possible.)

For appetizer we ordered the Buca Beignets. They were delicious. As our meal, I ordered the Salmon Oscar, with a side of sweet potatoes. Both were very good. The salmon might be the best I have ever tasted. Nice, crisp outside but very moist and flaky in the middle. My wife ordered the pork chop. She stated it was well prepared and tasty. 

Overall, a very nice choice if you're looking for a higher rated dinner establishment. I think the drink prices are a little high though. In my humble opinion, I don't see a need to charge $12 for a standard margarita. Let your food fare warrant the high price, and treat the guests to average drinks. Regardless, we had a great meal and will probably be back. A solid 4 rating.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Ambiance, entertainment, service and food were amazing! Jesse went above and beyond and provided us with exceptional service. The filet mignon melted in your mouth and the lobster tail was cooked perfectly! I would definitely go back!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We were mainly here for a local live band that was performing over dinner time. The speciality cocktails, spicy blueberry margarita and strawberry basil lemonade ware both refreshing and tasty. The goat cheese stuffed artichokes we're prepared perfectly over crostinis. We split the sea bass, unfortunately it wasn't very good. The fish was over cooked, chewy and fishy. The brussel sprouts weren't anything special. They were mushy and didn't have any flavor to them. For dessert, we tried the cheesecake sopapilla. The outside was burnt and the cheesecake inside was over cooked. Overall, the meal was disappointing but the atmosphere, live music and drinks were great. I'd recommend it for drinks and apps but definitely not for dinner.

name: Second Fiddle
text: This bar is awesome as I was just in here for about an hour in Nashville. They had an awesome bartender. Plenty of standing room and decent prices on beer. Love this place, definitely one of my more favorite places on Broadway

name: Robert's Western World
text: Idiots bar backs are druggies. Pay for your food wait an hour and they kick you out before you get your food. Bouncers are clueless. Bouncer and manager backed the drug addict cook thank god I can afford to walk away with out my 50 dollar food. Idiots. .

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: This place is a must see if you are in Nashville! The food is amazing, the people are very friendly, they always have live entertainment....its so great. They even have a kids play area, fun little shops, and a full grocery store complete with a bakery and butcher. You will not be disappointed in this fun place!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Classis country. Hank and more.  Great atmosphere- wall of signed pictures on one side and shelves of cowboy boots on the other. Truly old school.  Had lunch as music played. Burgers and fries were good and hot as it's cooked right there on the grill.  Enjoyed lunch and the classic country music!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great music and tasty food. Quick, friendly service. Loved the chicken and avacado quesadillas. Great spot on Broadway.

name: Legends Corner
text: This place was so fun! My husband and I spent a Monday night here and it was awesome. There was a great cover band playing and we ended up staying till close. There were good vibes, good music, and a lot of fun to be had...the drinks were a little watered down, but it was a fun spot.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Started w queso and chips. Chips were thick and cold. So probably not made here. Queso was just ok (not world famous).  Chicken tacos were spicy hot. Removed jalapeno and still very hot. Nashville chicken sandwich was awesome. Good flavors. Tator tots hot and crisp. A little heavy on salt.
Music awesome!

name: Legends Corner
text:
Not sure what the hype is about at all. There is a lot of drunk tourist and the drinks are over priced even for Nashville. I went there multiple nights in attempt to hear decent music and never did. Cover bands playing crap versions of crap songs. The bartenders are very good at ignoring people. The security guards or bouncers are very good at throwing random people out. I'm being sarcastic. The bouncers are a joke and are the douche bag over assertive type. 

Seriously there are so many better places in downtown Nashville for a good time. Try Roberts or Tootsies. Avoid this place unless you are a drunk tourist.

name: Legends Corner
text: Legends, along with a few other honky tonks, on Music Row are FUN!!!!  We had a the best time ever in Nashville!  We had so much fun at these honky tonks that play awesome live music, that we never made it to any other place that we had on our list!  And, I don't even drink alcohol!

name: Robert's Western World
text: As one of the very talented singers stated as some folks left the joint "don't leave, they don't understand you out there, we understand you in here." She couldn't have been more right. You will not be disappointed by this classic honky tonk! Cheap drinks & eats (and delicious!). The live music could not have been better or more authentic Nashville. My husband and I kept coming back for more and stayed as long as we could. It was a knee slapping good time!

name: Legends Corner
text: FUN!  We walked around Nashville for 2 days and kept coming back and checking in here.  I love the atmosphere and the friendliness.  I love REAL Classic Country music and it doesn't get any better than this.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: your average broadway, neon signed, country music cover band bar.  not complaining since it's everything you expect on this street, just hard to give it 4 stars.  congrats to tin roof for getting many small things correct, good drinks served quickly to a well behaved crowd.  you should probably eat somewhere else then head here for music and drinks, but if someone in the group is starving, they can definitely find a decent meal (stick to the quesadillas).

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Here right now - ordered scallop risotto - the scallops were good but the risotto were gummy balls of rice. Considering it was $36, s bit disappointing. My friend got veggie lasagna - oddly sweet and grossly crispy! We also got calamari - chewy and gross! The goat cheese artichokes were extremely yummy- best thing we had! Would not recommend unless you are just having drinks on the outdoor patio. The "risotto" ball is pictured below.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Ryman Theatre: 

$25 to enter just to look around is a little ridiculous without live entertainment. It's cool to see--once. The theatre is beautiful with a lot of history but wasn't worth the $25--each. I loved all of the history and photographs with descriptions on the walls. My daughter took about 20 steps into the theatre and was ready to leave when she saw everything. It's definitely a must see but like I said--once. We love country music so we had to go to the heart of it, we were not disappointed with the ambiance.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Went to Roberts Western World last night for a quick bite to eat ... service was ok but it was slamming in there, burger came out hot and fries also hot. It was exactly what I expected, decent food very edible...limited menu but really the ambiance was what was killer. Great music great time !

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Awesome, awesome, awesome music!!!! Absolutely love this place.  Is it the cleanliness??  No!  Do the bathrooms suck?   Yep, pretty much.  
Friendly staff, great band and nobody here cares!!!  
Tons of TVs for the sports fans and did I mention awesome music on a Sunday night?!

name: Robert's Western World
text: I can't tell you what the food was like cuz I didn't have any. The women at the next table had the fried baloney sandwich (think BLT) and loved it. On the other hand the beer was cold and the music was hot (western swing). Robert's has a fun vibe. Come in the afternoon, or after dinner, and swing your ass to some great live music.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Grill closed. Gospel music playing live on stage. Guess that's ok if you are into it. Wish I could of tried the food.

name: Legends Corner
text:
We had an EXCELLENT time at Legends, the live music artist, Buck Mccoy was excellent!!! I can't say enough good things about this singer from his song selection, to his stage presence to his cd of original music. 
As for the bar itself, the girls behind the bar are quick and attentive. You don't have to wait long fir a drink and the album covers and discs on the wall brought back memories. I'm old enough to have played a lot of them when they were new.
All in all a great experience!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
We ate here while passing through the Gulch.  My wife and I enjoyed the place.  Our waiter was very nice and informative when it came to the food and the local scene.  Our lunch was good and so were the drinks.  My wife really loved the strawberry mint cocktail they had for lunch.  We will be going back for sure and would love to try their dinner menu.  

The staff was even nice enough to split our lunches so we could share.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This was recommend by a friend who grew up there as a great little Honkey Tonk to get a drink, something to eat and listen to some music. And, we did. 

Cool place. I'm sure many musicians pass through each day. The one that was playing when we were there was pretty damn good. 

The decor is what I expected in a divey place like this. A lot of local signs, stickers and cozy-quaint with the grit of a good ole place. 

Had a burger and a some vodka sodas. Burger was great...flat top grill greasy. Yum!

Our bartender was awesome. I love a bartender who has worked so long in a place that you feel like you're walking into their own house. 

Definitely stop here for some good music, cold drinks and great service.

name: Robert's Western World
text: The music is alway great. It's a fun bar to hang out. People are there to have a good time.  Drinks are not pricy,  staff is friendly. And u can eat if you want. It's right downtown next to a lot of other places.  I always.  Always come here.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great pickles and burgers at a great price. All with some great live country music and down to earth atmosphere.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
One of my favorite Nashville restaurants, 
The food is always on point, The service was JUST RIGHT, and the ambiance so perfectly romantic
And they have live Jazz at night
I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone in the Nashville area!

It is however, a LITTLE on the pricier side... My group of 4 ate for $170 + $30 tip and we all had immaculate entrees, several drinks, TWO appetizers, and TWO desserts!!!
Not bad AT ALL, and completely worth every penny :)

Will return!!! OVER AND OVER AGAIN!!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: My favorite spot on Broadway. The honky think band playing on the weekend and the regulars dancing make it an experience not to be missed. To me, this is what Nashville is about.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great music. Food was pretty decent for bar food.  But heck, it's Nashville and folks are here for the tunes.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We had such an enjoyable experience. Loved the hostess that sat us at the table. I think her name was Alicia? Maybe Ashley? She deserves a raise either way. When I informed her of my girlfriends medical condition she went above and beyond to make sure we were accommodated. She even helped us find some fun nightlife!! Definitely recommend!!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: The four stars are for the amazing wedding that I got to witness happening in the upstairs party room and the great live music that we got to enjoy from the balcony seats where we ended up. Food was alright- our waitress was sweet, but like they say.. you aren't going to the same place for live music as where people send you for the food. We loved that we were all able to talk during dinner and really enjoy our couple of hours at dinner but you're here for the music and the location. But you already knew that

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great music, especially after 10:30, great drinks, and great service. Rachel is the best waitress we've had so far in Nashville!

name: Legends Corner
text:
What can I say - this is one of my favorite Honky Tonks.  The music is consistently good and well mixed.  You can have a conversation while it's playing, which sometimes is key.  The barstaff is the friendliest in town.  I know if I try to list them all I'll miss someone, but Brooke, Kara, Casey, Nicole, Nikki, Tara, Mary Coul, Barbie, are awesome!
There are two spots to see music - floor level and upper floor.  Try for a seat in the upper level to see and hear great.  It is mostly acoustic music in the morning until 2:15, then bands until 2-3AM.  Tip both the bands and bartenders - that's the Nashville way, and how they earn a living.
My favorite days and bands - Monday afternoon, Kinsey Rose, Tuesday afternoon Hali Hicks, and Thursday nights don't miss Becki McLeod.  Kids are allowed until 6pm

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Solid venue for a show.

My love and I attended a David Byrne concert at the Ryman and had a great experience. The entry was fast and easy and the concession lines moved very fast. I believe the Ryman is and old church that was converted in a music venue. By the layout you can definitely tell but the acoustics of this place are amazing. My only recommendation is to definitely get seats either on the balcony or far enough up on the floor that your view isn't blocked. I dodged the columns but would have liked it more if we were further up (we were row M). But still solid  venue, with friendly employees and super clean bathrooms! Hands down one of the best shows of my life.

name: Legends Corner
text:
When we got there around 10:30 on a Saturday this place was super packed. Come to think of it it seemed pretty crowded in the daytime too. Anyway we were told to go to the side entrance the lines wasn't too bad. The band playing had a great violinist and we were all awed by her because she was definitely rocking it. It was a nice to touch to have the TV screens showing the band as well so those of us at the back had a nice view. 
There were a couple of bars at the back so getting drinks was  not hard at all. They also have outdoor area at the back where you can take a break from the crowed and get some fresh air.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Nutshell:  Simple, well done food, great prices, and friendly service.

Our group stopped in after the Blues v. Preds game on a Tuesday night.  The music was going strong and they had a full house.  We headed up to the balcony to find a place to sit.  The whole place has an old time honky tonk feel, unlike some of the newer establishments along Broadway.  We were starving, so we headed back to the bar to order drinks and food.  The menu is surprisingly really good, they have way more than just microwave burgers (unlike some other places I've been to)  I decided on the hot turkey & swiss sandwich with chips and a soda.  All in all it was under $10, which was great.  They have a grill behind the bar and then delivered it up to us.  I was expecting a very basic sandwich...I was wrong!  It's a simple sandwich, but super tasty.  The bread was toasted, the turkey was juicy and flavorful and piled high, and it was well constructed and not sloppy.  It hit the spot, which is the main thing.  It's worth a stop in for the music aaaaand the food.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Even if you're not a huge music fan, this is a must if you're a tourist in Nashville.  I would imagine seeing a performance here is the best way to experience this unique space, but i give five stars for the self tour!

The space is so uniquely intimate (in the age of stadium tours, its tiny!), it's amazing to walk around it and imagine how cool it must be to see your favorite band here.

The building is a microcosm of the history of Nashville, American culture, race relations, all focused on what happens when you bring people together.  The historical exhibits make you stop and think a bit about all of those things. And that it's still today an active concert spot is amazing!

And from a wow perspective, don't skip the movie intro to the tour. It will delight you!

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text:
We went here for my husband to play at the open mic. I called 199 times before I got his name on the list... which meant he didn't play until after midnight. If you don't want to play late, don't bother if your call doesn't go through before like 1:10. 
It's really cool that they keep playing until everyone who called and wanted to play get their chance. There were some awful acts and some amazing ones. So be prepared for a mixed bag. The drinks were okay and the food was not very exciting. 

If you want to hear music or play and are okay with stomaching some out of tune playing/singing in order to hear some good stuff, check it out.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Par-Tay with the G's!

SITREP

My yelp-buddies Chris G. and Nickie G. (NO RELATION!) organized a wonderful outing to Robert's Western World (RWW).  Little did I know I would lose my Nashville-Virginity at this wonderful den of iniquity!

THE SETUP

As you walk down the hill along Broadway, and head into the "strip" where RWW is amongst many other equally notorious & delightful establishments on both sides of the strip, RWW is easily identified by the neon-illuminated guitar sign.

And even though it says Honky Tonk on the sign, when you walk in the concept is REALLY brought home to you as your skirt right by the front of the stage where any one of a number on Honky Tonk Bands is playing for the enthusiastic crowd.  You can hang around a dance a few numbers like I did, or head straight-away upstairs where the darker, more secret bar is located with great domestic bottle deals!

THE CROWD

I swear I felt at home in this crowd even though I clearly sounded too much like the Peter Jennings & Tom Brokaw dialect of generic North American-speak.  And when girls here call you "dahlin", my heart melts automatically.  [Here's looking at you, Ms. Marti M.!]

THE ALLEY 

Right behind this second bar is the alley where you can step out and enjoy a smoke, have a chat with cute girls in black jeans, and then amble back in, or go next door to any number of other establishments that you can also access from the back (like we did with Tootsies).

THE LOWDOWN

RWW is THE stop to get your Nashville Honky Tonk on!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Exceptional Bourbon mule. They make their own finger reduction!!  Outstanding!!  Get the beniets. You will not be disappointed and I never leave reviews. H

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great location! Great food! Great live bands! Great ambiance! What more can someone ask for? I had the lobster bisque, chicken fried oysters. Scallops for my entree with a side of brussels sprouts. Two drinks which consisted of the Sambuca 75 and Cherry sour. The cherry sour was right on time! A little bit too much salt for the food which was why I didn't give 5 stars (I realize that's my NY/NJ palate talking so I'll let it slide). Other than that definitely good eats. I will visit again the next time I'm in Nashville! :-)

name: Second Fiddle
text:
The second Fiddle 
Kelcy was the barmaid today and she was so kind and really fun.
"Big country & The Hee Haw Rejects".  We walked in as they were playing a 
song called Tennessee whiskey.

Well we ordered some whiskey on the rocks and she gave us two beers to back that up, lol, it's only 3 o'clock in the afternoon, it's going to be either a very short evening or a long night.  We were there for a couple hours, turns out it has to be one of our favorite places that we've been in Nashville! Acoustics were fantastic and love the decor, I WOULD go back.

name: Legends Corner
text: I can't imagine how good the music is during the weekend or evening because we are here at noon on Monday and it's fantastic!   Really didn't think it would be any good on a slow Monday.   Crazy.  As far as the bar, it's a bar nothing special.   But if you want to have a drink and listen to good music it's worth the visit.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Great service and drinks. 
Blackened flat iron steak with buffalo trace bourbon. 
Our server Kevin was great and the king of up-selling ( in a good way). We pretty much ordered anything he offered. We had the crab dip appetizer and additional drinks most likely because of his stellar service. He should be recognized for this as he is definitely generating increased revenue. 
This place was great. The food was amazing on all counts and the live music was great. Not too loud. 
And of course the service tied it all together. Great place.  Definitely 5 stars.

name: Legends Corner
text:
I recently walked to Legends Corner after the Elton John concert at Bridgestone.  It was about 11pm on a Saturday and the streets were full, so we ducked inside.  A band was playing, and they were really good, but my ears were still sensitive from the concert, so we got a drink and sat on the patio to people watch as they went by us.  Although we were the only two outside most of the time, a waitress still came out to check on us.  We could still hear the band and we even clogged to Rocky Top.  There is absolutely NO WAY that my feet will be still when I hear it.  

The most interesting thing that we saw all night was when we sat on the patio on Legends.  A woman, walking all by herself, was very intoxicated and holding a $20 bill in her hand, very visibly.  She walked down the alley next to Legends, and a man kept eyeballing her, clearly ready to take her money, and who knows what.  It was a gut feeling I had, I guess.  I called her to come over to the patio railing and started a conversation.  She explained that she'd been with friends, but she'd gotten too drunk to get into the next bar.  Bouncers said no, and her friends went in and left her to fend for herself.  

The man that was stalking her had turned and went in the opposite direction.  My husband and I told her about the man following her and told her she needed to put her money away, and try to walk closer to a group of people.  Although she was highly intoxicated, she was cognizant enough to realize what we were saying.

Women, don't walk the streets of Nashville at night by yourself.  It's not smart or safe.

name: Robert's Western World
text: All of the food was reasonably priced and the burgers were yummy! We got to listen to John Shepherd and he knew every old country song that we threw out at him! He was very entertaining and listening to him prompted me to check out the history of this place. I found out he had been playing there for over 40 years! This place is always busy at night and everyone is always entertained! A must stop in downtown Nashville!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Our office just had our staff Christmas party at Sambuca! What an amazing place.  We were greeted immediately upon our arrival and taken to the private room we were having our party in.  The decor was very festive.  Within minutes the staff proved to be very accommodating and friendly.  They remembered everyone's name and what they were drinking and we had a group of 60 people.  Everything we asked for they made sure we got it.  I haven't even mentioned the food yet! Everything we had was delicious and with the variety of appetizers everyone had plenty to choose from.  We have been going to different restaurants for Christmas for 16 years and this was by far the best place we have ever been too!  Thanks guys for a great experience.

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text:
I didn't really research this place and just kind of assumed a "cafe" means there are coffee products served. That is not true, but this is very much a singer-songwriter bar where musicians will be performing. Sound is solid with a packed house and the musicians are very talented. 

Food is your standard bar food, and the bar was your standard bar in terms of what you can expect from beer, wine, and liquor. But you aren't coming here for the food, you're coming here for the music. 

For what its worth, the $1.50 coffee (pretty certain it was Folgers) was for the entire pot of coffee. So even though it wasn't amazing coffee, it was amazing service.

name: Second Fiddle
text:
Fantastic live music and fairly uncrowded for a Friday Night. Had so much fun there!

Only thing is that the drinks were pretty expensive, but definitely worth it for the music!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great beer, great atmosphere, GREAT MUSIC!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Every other review talks about the acoustics in this place and yes, they are fabulous and yes, you feel up close and personal with the artist no matter where you sit. Going to a show at the Ryman is truly a must if you're in Nashville for any amount of time. 

I came with a few girlfriends just to experience the Ryman, and we bought tickets without even knowing the artist because the reputation for this venue is seriously that good (turns out Jake Bugg is quite good too). There is parking on the backside of the building for $15 or you can brave downtown and try to find street parking for less. 

If you're looking kick up your romantic evening to the next level, the Ryman does sell food items like chicken strips and hotdogs. They have a good drink selection with a full bar and one of the highlights of my night was a 16oz pour of red wine. 

The seating is sort of in pews, but you do have an assigned seat. The waits for food and drink weren't too long and the staff were very helpful and accommodating. Also its convenient that the Ryman is within walking distance of Broadway if you wanted to get your drink of before or after the show. Looking forward to more shows here!

name: Legends Corner
text: I loved "Legends Corner"! It was nice to walk into a bar and hear country music in the heart of Nashville of course. Loved the energy, the bartenders were fairly quick at getting everyone's drinks which was pretty awesome given that the bar had been pretty packed and busy for the most part. The bar itself is super chill and laid back for sure. Loved spending my first night in Nashville with you guys!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If you are a first timer to the Loveless be advised that the food is great but the wait is always long. I'm not sure there is ever a "slow" time - we arrived around 1:45 today and still waited a long time. We did notice when we came out around 3:30 that the parking lot was less crowded so that may be a better time. It took about 30 min for our food to be served after ordering so don't go if you're in a hurry or you are an impatient grumpy old man! Definitely the best things on the menu are the fried chicken, biscuits and fried green tomatoes.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
4 stars for events
1.5 stars for food.

I swear, I don't understand why the food is so bland here.  Does the chef not taste his food?
We were here for dinner, the other night and both of us made faces after the first bite.
I swear...  I don't understand why the food is so bad, here......

I like the concerts. 
I do not like the food.

I usually have to ask the bartender/barmaid to put a little more sweetener in my mixed drinks..
They're bland, too..

I don't know how this place stays in business with the food part of the establishment.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: It was delicious. We waited 45 min for a table. So we were starving by the time the food came. The service was fast. We ordered fried chicken and sample platter. The meals come with endless biscuits and jam. Both bbq pork was a bit dry. The pies were too sweet for my taste. The fried catfish and fried chicken were yummy. Will definitely visit again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The Good:
- The biscuits and preserves are great.
- The steak biscuit platter was excellent.
- The side dishes are generally good. The grits left a lot to be desired.
- Our server was very nice and attentive.

The Bad:
- We ordered two moonshine drinks, and only one had any alcohol in it. 
- The Bloody Mary tasted like moonshine, water, and a splash of hot sauce mixed together.
- Flies. Everywhere. There were at least 20 flies buzzing around our table from the minute we first got there.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I was in Nashville for work and several co-workers mentioned this place was great for a weekend breakfast.  We arrived at 10 am on Saturday and waited about 1:15 for a table. The food was good, but heavy. All of the homemade jams were delicious with the fresh biscuits (try mixing the blackberry and peach jams together for even more deliciousness). We ordered a side of sausage gravy as well, in order to try that with the biscuits, and I almost liked that more than than the jams. 

I had the pulled pork on top on cornbread - it was huge! All of the entrees were a good size so you may want to consider sharing, especially if you want to enjoy more than one biscuit. 

This place is worth driving out for, but make sure to allot some time for the wait. You can entertain yourself at their shops while you wait or relax at one of the many tables they have around the restaurant.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Okay...I always try to say something good about a place...it has nice...hmmm...nice chalkboards. I have been to brunch twice and both times the service and the food were striving to be average. The only reason I went back the second time was because someone gave me a groupon...still felt like it was a waste. I have not been for a music event, so don't use this for anything other than a brunch review...but a $15 Manhattan for brunch is way too much $$...go to Sutler...much more fun and much better food, value, atmosphere...albeit not chalkboards.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits. Fried chicken.  Homemade fresh jelly. Loveless lives up to the hype. It's worth the trip whether you live in the Nashville area or are visiting from out of town.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The biscuits and preserves live up to the hype! The biscuits are small but very tasty and especially delicious with some preserves slathered on top. I loved the peach preserves so much I picked up two jars from the gift shop to take back home. 

The breakfast is pretty good as well. I tried the steak and eggs and the steak was just okay, nothing to write home about. The hashbrown casserole that accompanies breakfast, however, is divine. 

I would say the only downside is the wait. Thankfully I knew from experience to get there early and was happy to say we were first in the building. It's definitely worth getting up early to have the first taste of those biscuits.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: One of my favorite places for fried chicken.  Wait time is crazy long, but you have lots of stores/activities on the property to keep you busy.  Definitely worth the experience.  We also tried the salted ham for $70+ and when we opened it, we found lots of mold.  Pretty scary, but I think that it's normal and I just cut it off.  We split the ham 3 ways and it would have been nice if they could have cut if for us.....but they said they could not.  For a restaurant, you would think they would have no problem.  So we ended up hacking at that thing in the back of our minivan with a knife.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I enjoyed my meal at the Loveless Cafe. Fried chicken and biscuits! I loved the strawberry preserves and bought a jar! Arriving at 9, the restaurant was not as crowded as shown on the many travel and food shows that feature the place! However by noon a tour bus full of senior citizens pulled into the parking lot and the place quickly became packed. I purchased some items from the general store and walked around the grounds stopping at all the shops in the back! The waitress and hostess were courteous and cheerful! I liked looking at all the celebrity pictures and reading the articles throughout the restaurant. The strawberry rhubarb pie was good but in my to go container the strawberry juice spilled out.   Next time I am in Nashville I will return to the Loveless Cafe!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
For $3 + tax, I was able to get a grilled chicken biscuit and two additional biscuits with their jams. And I was full. The biscuits deserve a 4/5.

The restaurant is not technically in Nashville proper - I think it took me 25 minutes to get there and if it wasn't renowned, you probably wouldn't stop here. It's a cute restaurant with super sweet staff and service. The restaurant is more sizable than I expected and since I came here on a Monday, I didn't have to wait. I did hear a tip - if it is packed, get it to go and sit on the picnic tables. 

There are two shops with their jams and some adorable lunch sacks and pot holders.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Just go... always great and such a cool one off. Liked it better before the gift shops and performance hall but food always a winner

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Luke was our waiter and his customer service was spot on!! So friendly and helpful, food was delicious, chicken biscuit was one of the best!

name: Big Shotz
text: Awesome chill cover band here when we visited . They played some good jams. Our friend we were with says this place normally has legit bands, so we'll go with that statement.  The 5 dollar shot menu on the screen flashed so fast that it took me 10 mins to stare at it and try and decide which ones I wanted to try because before I got to read one, the screen changed !  Bartenders were friendly but I think one was new cause she was slow and got my gals order wrong when she went up and ordered

name: Loveless Cafe
text: They had me at biscuits and mimosas! My husband and I brought a large group of family and friends here for brunch while everyone was in town visiting for our wedding back in December. We knew there would be a bit of a wait before we got there since it's a Nashville staple so we warned our group up front. No one seemed to mind much because they are all still talking about how delicious it was and insist on revisiting during future trips to see us! Btw, you must try the CHESS PIE! Even if your stuffed... it's so worth it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Six of us went to The Loveless around 1:00 February 15th for lunch on a Friday afternoon. 
The waiting list was long. We got our names on the list and were handed a pager so we could roam around the shops or sit outside until a table was available. 
We were seated about 45 minutes later. 

I haven't been to the Loveless in years, so I was hoping it hadn't changed too much. 

Complimentary homemade biscuits and homemade jelly with butter. CHECK
Quaint dining room and friendly server. CHECK
Good food. CHECK
Eat until you're uncomfortable. CHECK
Very reasonable. CHECK

Nice experience...YES. We'll be back more often!

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Was invited to this venue for a friends surprise birthday party and my husband was also playing in the band for the r&b brunch. The parking was very confusing and there seemed to only be one valet outside which caused the already jammed parking lot to get even more backed up. He was a nice young man though and offered to help me unload the cupcakes from my car. 

Once inside I loved the atmosphere. It is very pretty. The selling of individual seats seemed unnecessary and very confusing for the hostess...it took a few minutes to figure out what area had been reserved for our party but the young lady was very kind and helpful. 

When I ordered my food I got the burger with fries. Easy enough...right! Can't go wrong with a burger. I heard the waitress tell my friend (who also ordered the burger) that their medium rare was more like rare so she recommended ordering up a temperature. I got my burger well done, plain with no cheese. Mayo, mustard and ketchup only. When it arrived it was so charred I couldn't even finish one half of it and it was smothered in cheese. I also had no condiments so it was even more dry. I would have asked for some but never saw the waitress again. The fries were delicious but I was very disappointed in the burger. 

Overall my two stars are solely based off of the room decor and the fries. 1 for each.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Went for our anniversary dinner and Tammy was the best server we've ever had! Entire Menu was tempting and the biscuits were, of course, amazing. Can't wait to go back for more brinner (breakfast for dinner)!!! Love the ambience every time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Last night my boyfriend and I landed in Nashville for a Bonnaroo vacation, and immediately wanted a classic Southern meal to kick off our week. Loveless Cafe is our favorite spot when in town, but last night our server, Owen, truly made the experience exceptional! Not only was he kind and courteous, but his recommendations and introduction to molasses butter was to die for. His customer service and attention truly made us feel like we were over a friend's house for dinner. Thank you so much for another great experience and for the mini mason jar as a little token to take back home to Los Angeles! XO

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Excellent food, the German Potato Salad was amazing. A true German dish. I had the chicken schnitzel sandwich. The chicken was so tender and delicious, the Swiss cheese and ham a nice compliment. The prices are excellent.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: The location is great for a business meeting. The atmosphere and character seems a bit forced. Food is mediocre, with some items much better than others. Beer selection isn't as expansive.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great food, great quality, good service once inside makes this a staple for nashville. My only issue was the 90 minute wait to get in! So,many people wasn't to try the chicken that theirs almost always a long wait. Luckily they provide iced tea and seats for the wait. He chicken gizzards! Haven't had those in years!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best f ing biscuits ever! Trust me I've had lots of biscuits! Jams really fresh. We had a 45 min wait. But they have little shops to check out. Food was worth the wait. It's one place I've been to that I wish I live closer to so I could go more often.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Fun experience. The entire location is cute and have a great ambience. 
There was some wait in the morning on a sunday, but go early to put your name down then walk around the area. Great selection of southern brunch items. Staff was attentive. Would go again for the amazing biscuit and jams!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Yep, this is the destination as a go to in the Music City area. Kinda out of the way and a long wait, but interesting southern food, and breakfast all day. Go ahead and have the country ham, it's southern and good. Visit the shops and converse with the other waiters from all over the country. A classic place that goes with the Opry. I understand that you might see a country singer there at times. You'll love more not less!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Welcoming at the door was warm and inviting. Our bartender was very knowledgeable. We had the Bavarian Bierhaus light Helles beer to drink. We also ordered the Bierhaus Wurstteller to eat. We subbed the sauerkraut and red cabbage for green beans and German potato salad. Everything was excellent and perfectly cooked.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits are amazing. The food was really good. There is a very long wait but I would definitely recommend the wait.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Got sick from the crab bennedict which tasted stale and they didnt seem to care.  Will not be going back.  I have an iron stomach and it still took me down.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Nashville Iconic Landmark!  The food is pretty good, and they have some neat things.  It is a tourist trap, but worth going to (at least once if you are from out of town), and occasionally if you live in town.  Fried Green Tomatoes, jams, and or course the Biscuits.

The area now has other goodies around it... arts and crafts places, entertainment venues, and the terminus of the Natchez Trace Parkway, just a hair down the road!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits are the best I've ever had and I now know why people actually eat sausage gravy.  The homemade preserves were excellent as well.  My only regret was that I couldn't try everything on the menu.  Will definitely be back.  Be prepared to wait during peak meal times, but they do give you a beeper so that you can shop in their stores while you wait.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Everything here was good prompt service yummy sausages wonderful pretzel, decent sauerkraut good potato salad and felt like  German  the big beer houses in Germany fun place

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
It was a hour and 10 minute wait to get a table for 7 people on Sunday at 11:30. At least we could kill some time by browsing the small shops nearby but the selections in the hams and jams shop was pretty small but they have jams, honey, peanut brittle, popcorn, nut mixes and some souvenir items. 

The food was average, which is why I rated it 3 stars. It was nice to get complimentary  biscuits and jam. I ordered the French toast with a cup of fresh fruit. The French toast was thick but there wasn't anything "extra special" about them. My friends had the omelette and pancakes and they rated it 3 stars. Good food but nothing special for foodies.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Happy hour 5-7 were great although possibly need some sort sauce on duck sauce rest was great! Wine selection tasting was great

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Headed for the Natchez Trace Parkway, we had to stop and try a meal at the iconic Loveless Cafe.  My wife had the fried chicken, dark, with a side salad.  I got the barbecue plate with pinto beans and fried okra.  The chicken was perfect, full of flavor and moist without being greasy.  The barbecue was very good as were the beans and okra.  The biscuits were outstanding.  The service was very good, very prompt and efficient.  Reasonable prices.  This was a good start to our journey on the Trace.

Like the Terminator, I'll be back.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
4 people for a 7:00 reservation.
As I got out of my car at Valet, I was informed that CITY WINERY was charging $5.00 for parking, and that did not include the tip. When I asked, the valet person told me I could pay them on the way out.  
Arrived about 6:40 and had some great cocktails at the bar. We were seated at 7:00 and informed that the restaurant was closing at 8:00 for a private function..WTF!!  That information could have upset somebody on a date or out for a nice evening, but we are long time food service professionals, and figured out that the event probably started at 9:00.  Nobody ever pressured us to "order up," but at 8:15 they started moving tables and chairs around us.
We started with the cheese board and the Falafel.   Both were about as predictable as tap water..it's good when you are thirsty(hungry), but not very exciting.
Around the table for dinner we had:
The trout---apparently very satisfying.
Chicken fricassee--the grits were bland
Waygu beef tartare--over processed, DRY, flavorless beef.  The sweet corn and charred scallion relish didn't help. I think they forgot the mustard seed aioli and the cured egg shavings.
Hummus plate--nice hummus.   I'm positive that the peppadew feta was replaced by the peppadew ricotta because it had none of the sharpness of feta cheese.  I did not see the pickled eggplant, and it was replaced with some kind of sweet honey like concoction.
Buratta---it was a glob of bland watery fresh mozzarella, with none of the buttery flavor you might expect.  It did melt nicely.  It was in a small cast iron serving dish, with halved cherry tomatoes and some mild green peppers.  it lacked the pickled garlic and sunflower seed pesto that the menu promised.
Speaking for myself, nothing came to the table piping hot, even in the cast iron serving pieces. 
Nothing was an assult on the taste buds (except for the tartare) , nor was anything memorable.  The menu reads a lot better than the actual food tastes.  I am not sure if the missing food items would have helped.
I realize that the weather has been bad, but if something is on the menu and not going to be on my plate, let me know and I can work around that.

We were asked about seeing a dessert menu, but it was difficult to think they were being sincere about offering it as they picked up tables and chairs around us.

When I picked up my car at Valet, I was never asked for the $5.00.  Not sure what that was about.

It was a pleasant evening because the people I was dining with made it pleasant. 
The food was stunningly adequate.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
This was my second time at City Winery. I was disappointed the first time. But since I had to go to an event next door my friends and I thought we'd give it another chance.  Well to bad so sad. I ordered the most expensive think on the menu the ribeye, thinking there was no way to mess that up. I ordered it medium. It came out rare. I sent it back and it came out rate in the center again. I sent it back a third time. To the credit of the management he was embarrassed at the experience we had and  didn't charge me for the steak  or my cocktail. 
But I don't think I'll be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
So I had been recommended Loveless Cafe for their 'amazing biscuits.' Let me just say: they're good, but not amazing. I definitely wouldn't come and wait in line in the morning for them. The blueberry jam though was TO DIE FOR. And fortunately you can buy it on site! 

The coffee is decent, the omelette was good. The veggies in it were fresh and still had some crunch, which I love. The country ham, which they are also famous for, was really good too. 

The service was excellent. My waitress was very friendly and helpful and always made sure I had just enough coffee :)

Overall, giving it 4 stars because it was good but not quite amazing.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I thought this would be a really kitschy place, but it was actually pretty authentic to food in Germany! The ambiance is really cute, service was good, and there was live German music on a Friday night. It's a tad expensive though, minus the one star.

name: Big Shotz
text: Good music. Nice atmosphere. The "double shots" are made from cheap liquor.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I am and always will be obsessed with Loveless Cafe. The preserves, the biscuits, what's not to love? I visit it every single time I am in Nashville and I never regret it. I love the Loveless fried chicken with a side of mashed potatoes and macaroni and cheese. I am not a huge pie fan so I have not tried the pies, but everyone has told me that they are SO GOOD. I am also a fan of their waffles. Really, you can't go wrong with anything at Loveless Cafe. I drag every person I know to eat there and they never regret it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: It was excellent food!!! I loved the biscuits they served and al l of the things that they put on them!   The chicken was very good as well!  The service was great to!   It is a must go to place if you are in Nashville!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wow this place was impressive.We ate a great breakfast of eggs, generous portion of crisp bacon ,hash brown casserole and of course the biscuits. What I enjoyed the most was the fresh preserves . Loved all three, but the blackberry was great! This is not your ordinary cafe!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Hash brown Casserole, homemade biscuits  n homemade jam, country fried steak n eggs w sausage gravy, biscuits n gravy, all amazing!!!!!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We're in town from Texas, so we used our phones to find somewhere to eat. This places is about 35 minutes from where we were staying but 35 minutes was nothing compared to the trip from Houston, so we decided to give it a try. We will for sure come back.
Biscuits amazing.
Fried chicken amazing.
Hash brown casserole amazing.
Did I say chicken was amazing?

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is classic southern food, if your visit the Nashville area you need to go. The breakfast, lunch and dinner are great. The biscuits are the best! They are a meal in themselves. The service is awesome as well.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: So much food on that plate. Chicken and dumplings were delicious tonight as were the sides. Only wished we had room for dessert. Ate too many biscuits before the meal.

name: Big Shotz
text:
This place deserves 0 stars. Warning to Tourists and Locals. This place because of lack of manners by The Owner and 
One Male Manger is the worst place l have ever been in.  
The Monday night l went to the bar and was thrown out-3 others got the boot too. 
Read the reviews on The Facebook page called "Hot Shotz." As l was writing my review for HS on their Facebook page, l read a review from a lady tourist from Mississippi. She was reporting what happened to her the night after l was there. She was with her boyfriend and was grabbed in the Arse while she was sitting at the bar. She complained to the bartenders. They said they could do nothing because it was their boss who had grabbed her-The Male Manager on duty. He has a glass in his hand. He dropped it on purpose and glass went everywhere. 
The night l went to the bar it was not busy. I accidentally bumped into A Blond Lady who was built like a football player. 
I could have gotten hurt. I did not know 
l had run into Owner- "The Queen of Nashville." The Queen said to me-"Do You Always Run Into People and not say excuse me?" She had a extreme attitude and did not say she was The Owner. 
I thought she was a mean drunk. I said are you drunk?" Because it seemed like she was taking it to far over me accidentally running into her. A normal person would have let it go. She said  "l am not drunk, l am the Owner." I have never said this to a Woman before but l said exactly what l thought. I could not control what automatically came out. I said like Bette Davis-"What A itch." Her reply- she said 
"l can kick you out for anything since l am The Owner. " She set me up and wanted to let me have it. Then she said get out. 
I said are you kidding-I am not drunk (only had 2 small Cokes.) Then l said let me talk to someone and l will leave."  She said "NO." The Queen grabbed my plastic cup of Coke out of my hand and throws it into the bar area. She had lost it-could have hit the bartender. Then The Queenie als her good Old Boys- her Posse. Get her-The 2 Bubba's come up on either side of me and both grabbed a arm. They were throwing me out. I thought is this real? 
Or am l in a Hollywood Movie staged in The Old West? I started to fall-they continued to drag me out as fast as possible. The whole bar stopped and watched. I was thrown out into Freezing 19 DEGREES weather. I tried to ask the  guy at the door to help me. He told someone he was lucky he was deaf in the ear l was talking to him. So l went to the his other side. 
Then The Queen calls the police. She told me you can't stand there-you are still on my property. I wanted to call the police but Of course my phone was dead. Not one person coming out of the bar would call the Police in my behalf. 
One lady who came out did talk to me. Her advise was to leave. She knew the owner and was afraid she would press charges and l could be arrested. 
I have reported this Bar to The Nashville Mayor's Office Assistant /Claudia H. 
She is sending a report to The Nashville Tourist department. The tourist Dept does not Nashville to appear like this. 
I filed yesterday this business?? with 
The Better business bureau, posted a review of the bar on their FB page, and last Twitter. You do not treat Customers like this. Especially a Virginian. 
Too bad the bartender and The 2 Musicians were great. I went in because of The Music.  
Another review from 2015 from Yelp,        a Customer review said The Owner started a fight with her Girlfriend at the bar while she was there. The police and a ambulance had to come. The picture is still with among the pictures posted here. 
Be careful where you go in Nashville on Broadway and nearby. Read the reviews of places. The above could happen. Some bars are old. Somehow they pass the safety code. But watch out for tiny steps that are not marked well as you go in. 
I am no longer a local-No more Broadway bars for me. They like their money and could careless about the safety of their customers.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great breakfast today and the service was top notch.  The biscuits and country ham make it worth the trip over from Smyrna.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great restaurant. The biscuits a awesome and they just keep coming. I have only eaten breakfast there but the rest of the menu looks great as well. It is a tourist attraction so I recommend going early or be prepared to wait.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Absolutely the biggest tourist trap in Nashville. Just awful. Flavorless pork pounded flat, fries, worst Rueben ever, and two beers. $87 including tip. If you are into dropping substantial cash and having instant diarrhea from the low quality grease, then this is your dream restaurant. Enjoy!

Speaking to the owners degrading comments, please let me apologize for forgetting about the horribly expensive, dripping (literally) with grease, Rueben Egg Rolls we had as an appetizer. So sorry. Hope the math adds up for you now since you called me a liar.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
A local friend recommended this location for Sunday lunch, boasting about the ham and gravy.  What she didn't tell us was the average 2 hour wait.

We spent some time running in and out of the shops.  Samples were amazing and we got some pumpkin butter to take home.  We still had over an hour to wait.

Once we were seated, service was fast and attentive.  We all loved our homecooked food and didn't eat again for the rest of the day.

If you are coming here, be sure to have plenty of time.  We would have preferred to not take up so much of our limited Nashville time...but we have some great memories of this unique place.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Kimberly is the most amazing server I have ever had her kind attitude and over all demeanor made my night! Loved the half chicken as well

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Second time here and as good as the first time! Virginia helped us celebrate a birthday by totally embarrassing my 21 year daughter by asking her to come to the center of the restaurant and having the whole place sing to her.  Eggs, biscuits and Hashbrown casserole is perfect after celebrating 21st birthday on Broadway!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Food is good but we have had better. We actually prefer Monell's food for both breakfast and dinner overall. 

But no one can compare to Loveless biscuits and preserves! They are simply the best. 

3 star for food. 5 star for biscuits! 4 overall.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Ok I still love seeing shows here. Seriously. It's a great listening room, and still a great place for intimate shows. But wow has the service gone downhill. 

I've had odd experiences with the valet service the last several times I've been to City Winery.

At a show in December, the valet left a phone charger in my car. Why were they in my car long enough to charge a phone? Or if they weren't in my car while the phone was charging, why were they using my car as a mobile charging station?

At another show in December, I got the, what I've now learned is common, speech about tipping.
