Don't think I'll ever forget this day of darts, billiards, drinking and freezing our asses off!

name: Frisky Frog's
text: I've always loved this place for Saturday or Sunday brunch. The food is cheap and I have never had bad services. I am sad they are rebranding and changing their menu. I was not too impressed with the new menu

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Listen. You buy a movie ticket, likely from the same person you bought a movie ticket from last time, and this person also gives you a parking pass, so you can keep your car in that lot right next to the theatre where you already parked anyway but didn't know if you were gonna pay for it. You can then walk straight into one of its cozy-ass theatres as planned to see that artsy foreign- or independent-movie you can't see at AMCs everywhere--or, GOD, just like, The Favourite, even though all your hippest friends are all, "it's so overrated"--OR you can make one of several pit stops: 1) at the fully accessible restroom, 2) at the fully accessible elevator to the 2nd floor, 3) back at the desk for assistive devices for no extra charge (for anyone hard-of-hearing or visually impaired), or 4) at the bougie concessions stand, where you will find, as promised, more than popcorn. You can stick to your New-Year-New-You Mediterranean Diet as planned and get a hummus or charcuterie plate with the red wine du jour. Or you can spring for a specialty cocktail or craft beer on tap to wash down those Milk Duds. You decide.

name: Drifters
text: Best bar in Nashville!! They have the best nachos i've ever had. i definitely recommend coming here and eating their BBQ, too. They have an amazing staff as well!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: I went Sunday night to see a movie and had a phenomenal experience. I love being able to order the cocktail of my choice before finding my seat for the movie (or even getting up mid-way through the movie to snag a some popcorn and an old fashioned). The staff is always friendly and I had a particularly good 1st impression/encounter with two of your staff this past Sunday. I asked them their names at the end of our brief interaction, "Anthony" and "Dillon". Both were friendly, engaging from the moment I first walked in the door, to the moment I left! They treated me like I was one of their friends, and not just a first-time patron. Thank you Anthony and Dillon for all you did to make my experience this last week a special one. I salute you!

name: Drifters
text: We came here because we needed a dog friendly restaurant, and this olace exceeded expectations. Food was delicious and the staff was super friendly. They have a really nice outdoor patio that's perfect for pets. It's overall a very nice atmosphere

name: Drifters
text:
Brisket was good but the fries were not hot and a little overcooked. Service was excellent. Had the pulled pork chili as a started and it was good but the Brunswick stew was not good. 
Had the brisket dinner with 8oz of chopped beef brisket. It was tender, not stringy and had a good flavor even without any sauce. However the side were just so so. I would come back if for nothing else but to have the brisket.

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
Frisky frogs is straight trash. We got there on a Saturday at 11:45. We ended up leaving at 2pm because our food wasn't even cooked yet. The bartenders had food sitting on the bar and were just sitting there talking when customers had already been there for 2 hours. There were three other tables that had been there for 3 hours and still hadn't gotten served. Frisky Frogs is the biggest waste of time in Nashville. We are visiting for our friends birthday and all we wanted was some breakfast food until we went down to Broadway street for the day. This is my first post on yelp because Sometimes people can overreact but that was the most ridiculous restaurant I've ever been too. Do not waste your time on this place. If I could give this rating negative stars I would. Please don't waste your time. 
Bubs approved.

name: The Bowery Vault
text: Amazing little shop, stage and hangout. They have loads of fashions from $5 up. Vero was there to help me with styling. The changing rooms and overall decor made it super comfortable. Plus it's a stage wear shop and if you're feeling bold you can jump onto the stage and test out your look right away. So happy to have this addition to East Nashville.

name: Drifters
text: What a great find in East Nashville local atmosphere ! terrific barbecue and great service  a real gem!

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Fun but horrible service- not the staff's fault- poorly managed obviously!  Not enough help- you would think that at a Patriot's bar - on a weekend when the Pats are playing the Titans AND hosting a huge tailgating party for Patriots fans they would have the smarts to have more than 2 bartenders on and a scant amount of servers on‍! ‍

name: Commodore Grille
text: So I ordered buffalo wings and I got 6 wings, I'm from buffalo and if you got 6 wings in buffalo we would say forget it.   They were good but 6 wings for the price of 10, forget about it don't buy wings from here it's a RIP off.

name: Commodore Grille
text:
They didn't have sweet potato fries unfortunately but their side house salad was really good! Their regular fries were average, a little lackluster. I enjoyed the atmosphere. They have live music and if you go on Sundays at 8 you get to see Marc Allan Barnette and he is amazing! Highly recommend going to watch him. 
My husband got the brisket on biscuits which were cute and the biscuits were nice and flaky. He said it tasted good too. 
It's very dimly lit in there and the servers seems to be really busy. The other food on the menu looked really good too!

name: Drifters
text:
I really, really, really, really, really like this place and for so many reasons, but after eating there this afternoon, I have come to realize this place is like any other place IN THAT dependant on cook and waitstaff...   it can be a great experience or a shitty experience.  Today was a shitty experience.

But I will not hold that against Drifters. I will hold that to the staff waiting on me and cooking my burger.  they failed miserably today.

Bummer too, because today is National Hamburger Day and I had chosen Drifters to spend my hard earned money.

name: Drifters
text:
The music made me curious. I am not much (well, not at all) of a dive bar kind of guy. Eating at said dive bar? Forget it. But, the strains of melodic chords will pique my interest almost every time. Add to that musical curiosity, the siren's smell of smoke? Forget it. There were only so many times I could pass by Drifters without walking in.

So it came to pass on a late summer Thursday where I couldn't take any more and had to have some of what I was smelling/hearing. The dining room wasn't too crowded and football played silently on the tv for the few who were watching. I sat down and discovered that Drifters was in the middle of a drink special. Yes, please. Tonight's special was a 2 for 1 sweet tea vodka concoction. 2 boozy drinks for $5? I can do that. I came in thinking about an American Blonde and soon was fist-deep in plastic cups and cheap booze. This was starting well. 

Because I decided to go all in, I started off with a basket of fried pickles. They came to the table screaming hot and with copious amounts of ranch dressing. No, this was not a meal I could sustain on a weekly basis but as a treat... pass the grease. For my meal, I decided on the BBQ pulled chicken sandwich with a side of fries... and another side o' sauces. On every table are a basket of sauces -- 7 in all -- that will make the trip to Drifters worth your while. SEVEN! I love sauce almost as much as I love juice and strange-colored soda. This was gonna be fun. I tasted the meat on its own first to make sure there was good flavor going on. There was. If I'd had two sandwiches, I would have eaten one plain. That's how good the smoke was. Now, it was time for the sauces. I would try each I was sure of with a bite of meat and dip my fries in the ones I wasn't so sure about. My favorite (to the shock of none) was the sweet & smokey. With a molasses base, it was a forgone conclusion. The Texas & Drifters had the tangy vinegar kick that I look for, but I prefer that flavor profile with more of a texture basis (ie slaw) than meat & bun provide. Georgia had a nice, subtle heat by way of the mustard/pepper base and New Mexico kicked it up with the unabashed pepper profile. I only dabbed Sweet Fire and stayed the h#ll away from Atomic Buffalo. My colon thanked me for the wise move. And guess what happened to make this mess o' BBQ eatin' even the mo' betta: an entire set of '90s hip-hop started to play over the speaker system AND my waitress came up to my table, rapping.

Why don't I come here more often?

name: Drifters
text: Bummer. Would only go back here if I was 12 beers deep and in need of some not good food. I went today with customers and coworkers. I ordered wings and they came out black. And when I say black, I mean burnt. And when I say burnt I meant BURNT. Super dry. I was so pissed but just sauced then up and ate them because I was in a time crunch and didn't want to cause a scene in front of the people I was with. Super unhappy with this place. Will be a while before I ever give it another shot. May never go back. Fried pickles were alright. Other people I was with were upset with the amount of grease on their pork and brisket.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Worst service. Took 1 1/2 hours for a medium burger, after asking 6 times where it was. Waitress argued with us about order, then realized she did take it & blamed the kitchen. Rolled her eyes & complained numerously that her job was difficult. Each time we asked for a manager, a different security guard came to talk to us. There are too many other good places to choose from , don't waste your time

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This place is a nice swanky joint downtown of Nashville. I can't believe there hasn't been a review for this place.

First off, myself and group of friends were attracted to the beautiful country live music coming from this place. Nice building and nice set up. So it wasn't hard to decide to eat here.

The menu was amazing! Lots of delicious meals and appetizers. Which I wish I had the chance to try all I them. The deep fried catfish was my choice. It was so succulent and perfectly seasoned that I left no crumbs else on the plate.

The service was good! Our waitress was quick, the food was quick and the music was good. Can't complain! One thing that would be nice if they had free appetizer like chips to hold us over while waiting.

Overall, if you are new to Nashville this is a must try place. Love this restaurant and bet it rocks on with its live music!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Music and drinks were great.  However, clean up a little. The main floor in this place smells like a morgue that lost power and refrigeration for 6 days.  Go to 2nd and 3rd floors for breathability, where it is less musty.

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text: Saw Haim and Lizzo here. This venue was wicked. Drink prices were outrageous. The bathrooms are on the bottom level so if you need to go while the concert is going on it may take a while. They served food but didn't purchase - just a nice perk. The concert was hands down top 5 best concerts I have ever been too and that's saying a lot. I sat front row at Fleetwood Mac and I was in the very back row in balcony for this one. Still top 5 of all time.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Rooftop DJ and service was great. Bottom floor... the most disrespectful and rudest bartenders I've encountered in all of Nashville.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Bad. Just bad service is terrible, food so sub par I think they got it out of the trash

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: I have been stopping here for 15 years. This is the kind of place that all big stuffy bars try to be. Just a cool place to hang out and chill.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Didn't eat just drinks food look good. 46 bucks for 4 bloody Mary's and build your own. Another tourist trap.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: What a wonderful experience. I loved every second of Counting Crows this past Friday night. What a wonderful addition to Nashville. The backdrop of the amphitheater is the beautiful Nashville skyline, took my breath away! The size is perfect and no matter were you are you are always close to a bar, food, and restrooms!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Came here on the recommendation of a local musician. Fun place for live music styled like a music hall. Saw the band the Time Jumpers. They've performed with Willie Nelson, Miranda Lambert, Amy Grant and Vince Gill. Very fun and lively blues country and western music. Enjoyed it immensely.

They performed for a couple hours, favorites were "Don't roll your bloodshot eyes st me" and "All that's left".

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Attended a private party here the day before the 2015 CMT Music Awards.

Live band, good food, cold drinks.

And a great view of the action on Broadway from the 2nd floor balcony.

No complaints.

name: Famous Nashville
text: A bunch of country music artists incapable of writing a song. Menu items featuring out of season produce. Pretentious as it gets. This is essentially a dressed up dive bar.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: While my concert was amazing and the location was awesome, I am HIGHLY unsatisfied with their policy on confiscated items. This is an email I sent directly to their livenation account: I just left a concert and my items were STOLEN. Your policy on throwing confiscated items in grass is ridiculous at best. All I was told when I asked about it was that "you had the option to take it to your car" and NO ONE gave me that option. In fact, I was told that they would keep it in a secure area and that they NEVER have problem with theft. Which is strange because almost EVERYONE who came there couldn't find their belongings. I had an item that was fairly unrecognizable so I attached a keychain that had sentimental value to me so I could recognize it. Thanks to your lying employees and incompetent policy, my items are gone for good. This email is to thank you for your careless actions. Oh, and one of your security SNATCHED a set list from a PAYING fan's hand. Keep in mind who keeps you in business.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: The music 5 stars! Amazing venue! Time Jumpers on Mondays are such a treat to see and you cannot beat the price!  Food is bar grub and service is on the slow side just because there are so many peple packed in and it seemes a little hard for the server to get through. I was cold and wished I brought a sweat shirt. If you have a large party you might need to go early to sit together, but small parties of two can probably sqeeze upfront right before the show without a problem.

name: Nashville Underground
text: I thoroughly enjoyed NYE at nashville underground! The line may have been a little lengthy, but it was New Years so I understand. What really made the night was that our bartender Eden introduced herself and remembered what my husband and I were drinking all night. She served us with a smile even though they were slammed. I really appreciate her service and hope to see her there again soon!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Here for the 2nd time this week to see North Mississippi Allstars.  Ate here last night.  Good bar food. Great concert!

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text:
War Memorial has an interesting mix of acts....I've seen popular 90's rock bands, one of Jack White's newest projects, and a variety of other bands. It's definitely unique! 

I really like GA because even if it is sold out, it's never too crowded. You can hang in the back and dance or mosh in the front (if it's happening). If you prefer to sit down, they have an entire balcony with seats. Sweet! 

My only complaint is that the drink line out front is always long and you are jostled around while waiting because it's pretty packed right there at the entrance. They typically have some beer stations in the venue that makes it a bit easier though. 

Overall, the shows I've seen here are always a good time!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Great music. The appetizers were delicious but the Prime Rib Sandwich was AWFUL!!!! Very fatty and tough. I would have given it more stars if the sandwich was good and the wait staff more attentive. Couldn't find the waitress for over 30 minutes to get our check. Seems like they may have been short staffed though. I will still go back.

name: The Station Inn
text: We went here for my birthday on a Bluegrass Jam Session night and it was amazing! We had such a great time and they sang happy birthday to me! It was wonderful. Nothing fancy - just beer and good music.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Acoustics are a little loud but they have a great calendar of shows.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Killer nachos. The live music was great. We went in the middle of the afternoon but it seemed as though it would be a great place to party at night with 3 floors packed full of people. The prices were the same as anywhere else downtown.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Typical bar food fun atmosphere with a variety of bands playing on each floor they have some neat local beers . Our waitress was very nEach band that plays walks around every few minutes asking for tips . We did tip every time . It was little off putting when my friend gave 5 dollars and requested a song and the response was that will be 20. All ages allowed I I saw kids ranging from infants to 13

name: Nashville Underground
text: Nashville Underground is the biggest extortionist scam in Nashville. At the end of our night, they gave us a receipt with nothing broke down upwards of $200 and refused to specify what cost what. Poorly ran, no help from management, and refused to speak with us about specifics. I'm very skeptical of their honesty, and warn anyone who considers spending time here to be very frugal and knowledgeable of what they are purchasing.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Come by and have a few drinks listen to the bands on one of the three floors have a bite to eat and enjoy yourself. You never know who you will see here.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I was here for a private party and during the party and food was great and so was the service.  After the party the service downstairs wasn't good and very slow.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place is awful and racist. I asked the bartender (a blonde chick with a terrible sport's headband and sparkles in her hair) for a water and because I intended to bring it to the bathroom attendant she insisted I pay $2.25. I fully intended to tip her and the sweating attendant never asked me for the water. This chick clearly thought that serving beer makes her better than those that clean bathrooms which is totally wrong. It was offensive. I find a place that employs people like this to be downright offensive. Bottom end this dumb bitch lost out on a tip because she's an idiot and will probably work in a bar for the rest of her life.

name: The Station Inn
text: Local flair, loved the Bluegrass, highly recommend.  A place you definitely want to see succeed.  My wife and I will be back, very casual, and everyone was into the music!

name: Alley Taps
text: Good selection of beers.  Excellent happy hour.  Live music is better here than on Broadway downtown.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We checked into our hotel and headed straight to Broadway. Honky Tonk Central's open-plan three story bar appealed to us, as we wanted to see the city and get a bite to eat. We sat on the 3rd story balcony and enjoyed a couple drinks with our lunch. The portion sizes on the food were pretty impressive. However, the drink prices were as high as the third story balcony we were sitting on.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Me likey!  Kudos to an awesome staff who made this first time visitor welcome!  Ok, so I'll make this longer.  The band was also funny, and sang a little Justin Bieber.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: What could be nicer than seeing an old 80's band from your home country (OMD) sitting on the grass with a tarp pulled around you to protect from a light drizzle supping a pricey glass of wine with the one you love.  Sing a long we did with the Nashville skyline behind the stage.  No brolly's aloud, chairs avail to rent and a good view no matter where you are. A great addition to the city

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Sexually profiled by an African American bouncer here. Luckily someone let us in. Do not hate on gay people or "pretend to be gay" not to let a beautiful 21 year old in. It will bite you in the ass. 2015, you ignorant POS.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: went to a Wild Feathers show in this space. Arrive early for a decent experience. They put down a TON of tables, which can be a fight to arrange, especially if there are more than 4 people in your crew. If you are around one of the trafficked areas of the bar, you are going to HATE your show. People are moving around like crazy. The bartenders are slightly slow in my opinion, making pretty typical drinks in a mediocre timeframe.  Can't speak for the food though.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Terrible place to go with an extremely rude staff.never got the drinks we had ordered and they made us wait outside in 11 degree weather with the doors locked due to "overcrowding" when there was hardly anyone inside! Save your money and go elsewhere!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Our  Annual girls trip was to Nashville this year. We had a blast at Honkey Tonk. We enjoyed the best bands, best service. Everyone was so friendly! We visited other bars, but always ended up back at the Honkey Tonk. Hands down our favorite of Nashville. The bands were great, engaging with the crowd, so much fun! Already planning a return trip with my husband!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: First off...the food is awful. Straight from the freezer, to a fryer, to your table hopefully warm. The service was great though. If you are going on a Monday for the Time Jumpers get there early like 6:00. The tables start getting full about then. Eat before you go though.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place is freakin' awesome! The bands are always great! The food is awesome! I have to say, this is my favorite bar in Nashville!

name: The Station Inn
text: Beer only, but cheap beer! We shared 2 pitchers for $14 each. Very cool live music. Just beware that there are some patrons there that think they're at their own private concert at the Grand Old Opry. My fiancé and I were having a conversation and were publicly shamed for talking. The music is good but not like stop all conversations good.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Went there on Saturday with 3 friends.  Made a reservation online and when we arrived we were told we couldn't be seated and our reservation meant nothing.  Exact words of the manager.  He left and a very nice security guard came over and told us to go upstairs there were plenty of tables we could help ourselves to.  We did, and were told someone would come over and serve us.  30 minutes later I go up to the bar and was completely ignored.  So after 5 minutes I went back to our table and finally someone came over.  We were told we couldn't put in an order for 45 minutes and it'd be much longer after that before our food would come.  We left.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Passing through Nashville and decided to check out Broadway.  After checking it out for a bit, I decided to get something to eat and stumbled upon Nashville Underground. I have to say that the food was fantastic and the service was even better. My group sat at the rooftop bar and was served by the one and only Bobby Two Times. I have one word for this guy... phenomenal!  Next time I'm in Nashville, this will defiantly be the place that I will stop at.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Horrible service. Went there during the late day and decided to try it again two days later at night and the staff cared more about talking to young women than letting tourists in to listen to the band. DON'T GO HERE.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Came in around 4pm when it was slow, Elizabeth the local bar tender was awesome and insightful giving us tips of local things to do! The food was amazing and the drinks delicious! Major thanks to Elizabeth. The men's bathroom faucet does need to be fixed...pointing in the wrong direction .

name: Nashville Underground
text: While walking to another spot we saw a sign on an exterior wall advertising beer below freezing. Had to go check this out and YES, their beer is very, very cold and the live music was great! Many different bars and areas to socialize. More than one rooftop bar and a corn hole area. This place is huge!  Happy hour pricing too!  Manager Joshua swung by to make sure we were happy which we were. My favorite find of my Nashville weekend.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Awesome atmosphere and fantastic music! Drinks are great. Burger and pulled pork were delicious! Will definitely be back. Staff are excellent and very attentive

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Was only here for about 30-45 minutes, but I knew I had to write a review because the atmosphere of this place was really very cool and unlike any other bar I had been to.  There are three floors to this bar, and on each floor there is a different band.  What is nice about this is you can still hear some great live music, but because there is so much square footage you are not be sardine smashed with the rest of the people in the joint.  One bouncer here was a bit of an angry man, but other than that had a great time.  I would recommend my friends stop here for at least a drink in Nashville to check out the three floors of music.

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text: The Auditorium is a great venue. It can be difficult to find parking.  Also, the food that is sold inside is very unhealthy

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: In town for the weekend and stumbled on Bobbys for a PBR tall boy.  The dive bar theme with live music was great and not overstated.  Much cleaner than a dive bar in Philly. Bartender was friendly and served up limes with Coronas.  Great dart board.  Plenty of local characters at the bar providing advice to the band.  Worth a look in.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: 1st time going to Ascend Amphitheater. I went to see Charlie Puth yesterday (8/28/2018) and the staff did amazing job for helping people to find their seats and being patient w/ customers asking about the merch (like looking at sizes). My ticket was close to the front. And it was a very awesome experience. The staff did the chairs amazingly spaces so we (as fans/audience) can stand or get through. For advice, just be careful of being overheat/sweaty. It was like 92 degrees on a hot summer day.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I wish that I could be in the town longer to be able to know how consistent this place is...but having been there three different times, I'd say it is middle of the range. This past Saturday night the David Ray band was playing and although there was a group of drunk women that kept running into my mom and I...overall it was a good experience. The music was good, the singer had a good personality, and he could actually sing. It was super crowded, but you would have to expect that on a weekend night. We just went again tonight and I was really looking forward to it, but ended up leaving after a couple minutes. I love music and like live music loud, but this was just way too loud and even I couldn't handle it. There weren't many people in there anyway, and no one was dancing at all. I can't say I don't like this place, because I'd probably try it again if I was staying, but only on a Friday or Saturday night and if the music was good. I think that would like to try the other floors as well to have that experience next time. Hopefully next time I could update the review with a better score :)

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
I have been to this venue many times and it never disappoints. Whether you're a local or a tourist I'd highly recommend a visit to 3rd and Lindsley.

 I have seen many different musical acts from all different genres. It doesn't  matter if you're sitting in the balcony or standing right in front the stage the sound is always good great.
  
 If you're up to dinner before the show, it's also not a bad place to eat and everything on the menu is very reasonably priced.
 
 A couple more things that set  3rd and Lindsley apart from other venues around Nashville are parking is usually always free and almost all of their shows are all ages which makes it more family-friendly.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Fun place!  Stopped by mid-day on a work day.  Great band.  Fast service (drinks only - didn't eat).  Nice crowd.  Nice accommodations.  We may be back tonight!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Whoever the bouncer working the door was tonight is going to end up with a boot down his throat. I hope you people know it is illegal to take someone's ID especially from someone out of state? Your meathead moron bouncer took my girlfriends ID because the idiot thought it was fake. Not everyone is from hillbilly central. The police will be contacted and charges will be made.

name: Alley Taps
text: Such a great place tucked away in Printers Alley.  Great whiskey selection, fab jukebox and loved our bartender Amber!  Nice hideaway!

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: Certainly in my top 3 bars of all time. Great live music. Fun/authentic/local feel. Dirt cheap beer with dollar bills on the wall and a friendly bartender who is cracking me up. So glad I happened on this place!

name: Nashville Underground
text: This was my favorite meal in the four days we were in Nashville. We stopped in on Friday night because everything else was packed. The band was excellent and the food and drinks were even better!! Check out their bbq chicken and collard greens

name: Famous Nashville
text: Went here with my bros and it was an interesting place. Great atmosphere and the food was decent. The only issue is that they totally messed up our order. We received several items that we didn't order and were missing a lot of items. Service was a little slow but it's a busy place in Nashville so understandable

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Welcome to Honky Tonk Central! If being in the middle of lower Broadway with a dozen honky tonks surrounding didn't feel like you were in the middle of it, this three-story mega bar is actually named Honky Tonk Central. 

Different bands and performers are playing live music on every level. Although they don't have a rooftop per se the 2nd and 3rd floors have mini European style balconies that overlook the street below. 

Tough to differentiate this bar from the dozen other honky tonks lining lower Broadway but it certainly has a fun scene!

name: The Station Inn
text: Great live music venue, we heard a bluegrass band for a $10 cover. They only have beer (no wine or liquor) fair warning

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We stopped in here for a beer and a bite and were surprised at the quality of food. We had the hot chicken sandwich and a house salad. I usually don't order a salad at a bar, but the vegetables were crisp and nicely presented. The chicken sandwich was fresh and HOT! It should have come with a warning! So good!

name: The Back Corner
text:
TBC is a great addition to Nashville's nightlife! A mix of dance club and lounge bar, it seems to have everything you might want for a good night out, including an outdoor patio with fire pit. There's no cover, which is a huge plus, and the staff/bouncers have always been polite. 

I've never been here for an actual show, although I've seen the DJ play some tunes and play videos on the large screen. There's also random couches on stage and apparently it's perfectly fine to sit on them while everyone is staring from on the floor. Music can be a hit or miss at times, but when it's good, you know everyone will be dancing!

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Really fresh chicken! We had no trouble getting a table on a Thursday night, our server was Morgan and she was really nice. 
Kitchen forgot tomato on one burger but she took care of that right away.
They have some pre made slushy drinks and I tried one wich was ok but not awesome. I think my problem with it was that they used some vodka I didn't like but if you are not super picky (like me) you might really like it.

The thing with "build your own hamburger" worked out really good for all of our burger eaters. They where super happy. I would go back any day for my buffalo chicken fingers. Also appreciate that you get a bunch of sauce!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: A fun place to eat, drink, and listen to music. Different live bands on every floor. Tables are far enough apart you're not sitting other people's laps. Food is typical bar food, but a bit better than most. Drink prices reasonable. Servers super friendly. Music a little too loud, but that's probably just me.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I spent more time in this bar than I'd like to admit.  The bands were all pretty good on the first and second floors.  Beer was reasonably priced. It was constantly very loud and very full of very drunk people.   Definitely a dive bar scene.

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text:
3.5

I was torn between a 3 or 4 star for this venue. I went to my first show at the War Memorial Auditorium on a Sunday for the Conan & Friends tour. I LOVE Conan so I was on the website buying the tickets the minute the pre-sale started. We carefully picked our seats and thought we had the perfect spot. After paying for the tickets online, they were emailed to us and we just had to print them off. 

Finally the night came to go see my beloved Conan. We followed the directions on the WMA website and found the free parking they suggested. It's Capital Hill Center parking and is free after 6 pm. There were plenty of spots and it's only about a block down from the venue. The show started at 8 pm and we arrived around 7:30. The line was out the door and wrapped around a bit. However, the line went quickly and they had Conan Brand Reps walking around and handing out pins. Gotta love free stuff! When we got to the front, a security guard checked my purse and did the wand scan thingy. A lady then scanned our tickets and directed us to our seats. We wanted to use the restroom before the show started so we followed the signs to the basement. This was the first negative. There are only one set of bathrooms and they are in the basement. If you are seated in the balcony, it's kind of a long trip. There was a small bar down by the restrooms so we decided to grab our drinks here. They had a decent selection of beer and mixed drinks. I was able to get a tall boy IPA for $8. Not bad. We headed back upstairs to find our seats. Another negative I noticed. When you first walk in, the main bar is right to the left. There isn't a lot of room and when the line gets backed up, it's hard to move around. The front area gets crowded fast so you find yourself pushing your way through the crowd and lines. I wanted to check out some of the merchandise but didn't want to go through the sea of people again. Our seats were in the balcony and were easy to find. Up some stairs and to the left. We were on the left side of the stage in the middle row right in front of the stage (if that makes sense). We had the perfect angle to see the performers, or so we thought. The auditorium is older so the seats are old theater seats. They were comfortable enough and I think the stage is visible from all seats in the balcony. I did notice the floor seats were just padded chairs they put out for events. I understand why they need to do this but I know those seats were not cheap. I could see people being disappointed by this. We were lucky enough to have the row in front us stay empty. This gave us a very clear view of the front of the stage. The show started and everything was good. We could see Conan, the sound was good, and of course the show was hilarious. The big problem came when one of the comedians performed and his show was based off of a powerpoint. On the back wall of the stage, there was a big screen. At our angle, the big screen was completely blocked by the huge speakers they have hanging from the ceiling. Everyone around us craned their necks trying to see what was on the screen. Without any visuals, we couldn't understand his jokes and missed out on an entire set. I also felt bad for the comedian because no one in our section or the section across could laugh at his jokes. While our tickets were not the most expensive, they also weren't cheap. Next time I will choose a center seat in the balcony, even though that would put me farther away from the stage. If I didn't need to see the screen, the seats would have been perfect.

While I listed some negatives, I rounded up to 4 stars because I know it's an old building (built in 1925) and I'm against tearing places like this down to build new shiny ones. The architecture is beautiful and you can feel the history of the auditorium. I liked the fact that this venue has seating because I get so annoyed with standing in GA crowds. While it's not my favorite venue in Nashville, I would go back for a performer I really liked.

name: Nashville Underground
text: I went to the Underground for an office holiday party. As a vegetarian, the only thing I ate here (or all day) was their truffle Mac and Cheese. I got a horrible case of food poisoning and ended up in the ER.  Even worse, when I tried to contact the restaurant (three different people), not one returned my call or emails. I won't go there again and I let the party organizer know also so they don't plan any more parties there. I would avoid it at all costs. Or if you do go, avoid the Mac and Cheese.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
We made a reservation for 7pm on a Friday. When we checked in, the hostess said to go to the 2nd floor because it was "less crowded" with no direction on seating. The 2nd floor didn't have tables, so we went back downstairs. There was no one at the hostess stand, so at this point, it was a free for all. Don't bother making a reservation, because it doesn't mean anything at this place. It took 20 minutes to get a waitress, and the food was just okay. 

The only reason I'm giving 3 stars is because the band was good.

name: The Station Inn
text: Me and the fam came here for a weekend trip, had a blast.  The blue grass music was great.  Drank some good beer what else can you ask for.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: A quick in and out drink. Tried to hit up all the bars on the block for a drink at least. If it was good we stayed. Had one drink and listened a bit and moved on. Nothing horrible but nothing special either. Was nice that they had the windows open. VERY small bathrooms.

name: Famous Nashville
text:
The first 10minutes sucked. We sat at the bar. Waited. Waited some more. Watched what seemed to be the lone bartender struggle to service her customers at one end of the massive bar. (If she was our bartender we likely would have left.) Then came along Austin; a great guy, who provided great service to our group for the next 3 hours. He kept the drinks flowing and was genuinely personable. Even the other bartender/server (didn't catch his name) was helpful - he provided us with recommendations on where to get tattoos without getting ripped off by local parlors taking advantage of tourists. 
Other than the service; I like the "lounge" decor of this place. Over 7 years, we haven't been to a bar in Nashville quite like this one. 
As far as the entertainment; in all fairness, we were here during the day on a Thursday so I wasn't really expecting a 5 piece band. However the duet that performed provided good background music. Nothing particularly unique about the guys who performed.
The one thing I thought was very odd: the bathroom on the main floor. Single occupancy. Uh. This wasn't a big deal on a Thursday afternoon but I can only imagine the problems this would cause during peak hours on a Friday or Saturday night.
Overall, I say give this place a try. We'll be coming back, and we hope to have as great a time as was had during our first visit.

name: The Back Corner
text:
Totally agree with Johnny T - this place is a mashup of South Beach meets NYC in Nashville. Modern art in a repurposed warehouse done surprisingly well. It's a little hidden - right behind 5th and taylor

Went on a Saturday night
Pros:
Late 20s were the majority
Great Live DJ 
Swanky atmosphere
No cover
Good looking crowd before it emptied out
Mixed ethnicities - globalism in full effect

Cons:
30 minute wait to get in since it was "near capacity" - PTSD of NYC's meatpacking district began to kick in
Ran out of beer - no tap, just a small mini fridge
One to two bartenders at peak hours
Bar is oddly designed - inefficient and awkwardly located
No dress code
Music system could use some work

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Friendly wait staff and bartenders. Great off the beaten path location if you're looking to get away from Broadway. Drinks were reasonable and friendly environment

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: All three stars are for The Time Hoppers: they're awesome! It's a great way to spend Monday night in Nashville. Better to attend the show thirsty instead of hungry... the beer is cold and the food is terrible. Also probably safest to stick to beer; the table next to me sent back two mixed drinks!

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: My daughter and I went to the Niall Horan concert last night. It was a great night! Weather was perfect for an outdoor concert. The show was sold out. A worker said she had never seen it so crowded. The staff handled the crowd perfect. We did not have to wait long to get in and the line was crazy long. We also were given the option to pay $10/ticket to enter through the fast lane. We did take advantage of this option. The staff helped us find our seat and was super friendly. Great experience!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text:
Took a Sprocket Rocket tour at 1pm (if you don't know what that is you should look it up, we had a blast) & they gave us wristbands to go into this bar during our break. The wrist band got us 8 beers & 8 mixed shots for $40. Not too shabby at all!

We only went in the afternoon but the band there was great & we had a blast. We ordered fried pickles & the queso dip & we loved both for a drunk snack.  While the service wasn't the most friendly we had all weekend, they still were doing a good job working hard to get our drinks and food out quickly.

It seems like more of a dive bar so if you are looking for a typical Broadway experience I'm not sure how it would compare to the rest of the bars considering we only went during the day. But if you would like to get some day drinking it I think this would be a fun little place to experience.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Cool bar and fun environment but very sexist. A group of friends and I were in Nashville from out of town and one of the guys was told he couldn't dance with his female friends near the pianos because it was "females only". Extremely sexist.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: My mom, stepdad, and boyfriend Started our journey on the main level and moved up to the rooftop (my mom is handicapped so they let her use the elevator while we took the stairs). Went to the bar on the roof to order a round of drinks & was greeted by the bartender with one of the worst attitudes you could have in the service industry (I myself am a bartender). Decided to leave after a guy was persistently trying to sell drugs to my parents and the couple in front of us was half naked dry humping and security did nothing about it. Proceeded down the stairs while we were greeted by another security guard who told us my boyfriend was being kicked out for "stumbling down the stairs"... FYI he was walking slow with me down multiple flights of stairs since I was in heels! After bantering back and fourth, we decided to leave and although I will be back to Broadway St, never again to DBWR. Couple be a cool place if you had better employees!!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The music was great!! Abby Cone is a new favorite.  I highly recommend the handheld smoked turkey with avocado.  Great place for a night out in Nashville.

name: 360 Burger
text: First time here. Was promptly greeted and told we could sit wherever we liked. I pulled up a seat at the bar and Matt (awesome bartender) took our drink orders quickly. Service was outstanding,  the burgers were truly amazing. 5 star all the way. Fries were fresh cut and crisp on the outside, perfectly tender inside. The bun with the burger was obviously sourced locally or made in house because it was by far the most fresh and tasty I've ever had. Clean place, friendly and knowledgeable staff, cold beer. Will be back weekly. This place rocks! A much needed change for the Hickory Hollow area.. Swing in and check 360 out.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The music was absolutely great! We were only looking for a place for dinner with some music but ended up staying 2.5 hours just to listen to more! The food was good too. I had the mushroom "burger" which was probably the best selection at our table (out of the chicken strips, wings, and turkey sandwich). Service was awesome as well as beer selection.  Four stars instead of five for the small menu and the food could be a bit better.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Long time fan of Johnny Cash. The museum located downtown and is small and very pricey. You can spend a lot of $$ visiting attractions in Nashville. Look for the groupon ticket and go for half price. The museum has a good account of the life of Johnny Cash and the progression of his career as a musician. I learned a lot I did not know about him.  The collection memorabilia is  outstanding.  We stayed 2 hours and I could have stayed a bit longer.  The parking lot next door is about $9/hour costing as must as a visit to the museum. Take a roll of quarters and park on the street, meters only allow you to pay for 2 hours/ for $3.00

name: 360 Burger
text:
I never ever write these things, but as I sit in the drive thru of Burger King after dropping 33 bucks on unedible food, I thought I would tell my thoughts.

I chose this restaurant because I read really good reviews on here. We were the only people in there at the time so there was no excuse for the service and dinner we had. We ordered fried pickles while we looked over the menu. Well we never even got them and the waitress was dumbfounded when I brought it up. My medium well burger was so well done that it was like a dried hockey puck and so was my husbands. The french fries had obviously sat around for quite some time after being burnt. I mean it was horrible! 

Our waitress never came to see if we liked anything and when we got our bill, the fried pickles were on there. So i dont know who wrote the previous stellar reviews, but they were either delusional or employees. The sad part is my husbands company just built a new facility down the road and I guarantee they wont be eating there. What a shame or sham?

name: 360 Burger
text: Me and a cousin ate at this restuarant last Monday May 19th. I ordered the Bleu Cheese burger in the pretzel bun(waitress suggestion) with sweet potato fried. She had the All American with Onion rings. My burger was tasty, the sweet potato fries had a bit of an old taste to them but tolerable. My cousin did not like the Onion rings. I tried one and it seems like I was eating more breading than the actual onion. Nonetheless the food was good. Our waitress, petite blonde with tattoos, was exceptionally attentive and very sweet. I will return :-)

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: The food was  pretty good but the service was terrible.  We ate on the roof top and we had to go find our own condiments and the bar tender eventually brought us our drinks because our waitress was MIA.  I have never seen so many waitresses and bar tenders not working and taking selfies. Then before we left they turned off the country music at this country bar and started playing Justin Bieber.  No thanks!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Best music venue on broadway. Never too crowded and the bartenders are amazing! You'll have to hear Robert Meza play to believe it !

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Amazing musical artists, great service. I would recommend this to anyone visiting Nashville.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Mediocre food at best. I ordered a pizza which tasted mostly like a frozen pizza from the grocery store. Limited drink menu. Sat upstairs and got poor service. Ex. I had to go to the bar to get my own water refill and at least once there was no one behind the bar so just had to wait for someone to show up. Pretty sure it only stays open based on the need for more restaurants to cater to the large tourist crowd.

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: I came because I had a living social offer. I'll come back because the food as service were great. A Thursday night at 7 isn't the best time to get the usual feel for a Nashville Bar, but it was the perfect time to really experience the food. I travel a lot and eat in restaurants ranging from dives to coat and tie only.... Here, the menu is limited as you would expect from a bar. I ordered the Sweet and Spicy  burger and my wife ordered the Sweet and spicy chicken sandwich. Both we're cooked well and tasted great. I'd put them up against ANY burger I've had in Nashville including at the Pharmacy. The fries were actually potato wedges which I prefer anyway. The musician was Adam (didn't catch the last name) but he was really talented. The only reason I wouldn't give it 5 stars is that they were out of Guinness.... The Stone IPA was a great backup option. They have an impressive (10 tap?) collection of craft draft. To sum up, this place was awesome and I'll be back!

name: 360 Burger
text: I hadn't been to Burger 360 in a while, but I recent made a visit. They've made several changes, such as menu and style of food. In my opinion, these changes aren't the best, and I'll probably never go back.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Song Suffragettes were awesome.  Would love to review the food, but we still don't have it over an hour after ordering.....

Food finally came out, definitely was not worth the wait.  E-mailed management the day after expressing disappointment.  Never heard back.  With how long it took to get the food, I expect a reply in about 6 months or so....

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
The museum is amazing! The interactive stands to play hits at your leisure is great. There is a vast collection of hand written and other memorabilia from his life that really help tell the story. 

I did not, however, appreciate the cashier Courtney blatantly making fun of my mother to her coworker for asking questions about a shirt purchase. It was extremely rude.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Great museum if you are a Cash fan! 

Took us about 30 min to buy tickets and get in and another hour or so inside the museum.

There is a TON of things to see and ALOT to read so you cN stay longer if dedicated. 

I am definitely a fan of his music and really enjoyed my time here. Would recommend anyone coming to Nashville stop by.

name: 360 Burger
text:
I'm not sure where the "360" comes from, but the burger part is very clear. 360 Burger is about burgers. Beef, chicken (grilled or fried), turkey, salmon, you call it. Pick your bread and then either choose one of the predetermined "local favorites" or go with the extras you want.

Beer and "happier hour" specials are priced at a nice round $3.60 and I got here in time to get two beers (small ones, but still two of them) in frosty mugs for that nice price. Spirits, wine, mixed drinks are also on the menu.

I went right to it with the "certified grass-fed beef" and the local favorite that they call "Pimento and Pig" which is a good scoop of pimento cheese and two big slices of bacon. With my side of waffle fries, this was a big sized meal and was quite tasty!

It's Nashville, so of course there is a stage with local music. And the ladies waiting tables are all very attractive. Because. Fortunately, I got here on a night that the music hadn't started yet which meant that I could enjoy my meal in a bit of peace.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: so much fun! you need to check this place out. the muscians are great and the crowd is fun.

name: The Basement East
text: I've been to several shows here. The venue could be really cool but yall should really tell your sound guys to take it easy on the general volume of everything (could easily be 10db less), and the level of the kick drum and the bass are constantly too high. Also a little less reverb on the vocals would go a long way. And I'm not a crotchety old person, and all my musician friends agree. I know the current fad in live sound is to make everything loud and rely on the subs to make the vibe happen, but most music doesn't need that.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Great place to spend a few hours. Come early if you want to sit. Fantastic music, interactive crowd, and very tasty house drinks what more could you ask for.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Love this place!!! I had the opportunity to check this place while on a cross country road trip. The day prior I went through the Elvis Presley museum/house and while this one isn't quite as big and elaborate, this still do a great job at telling his story line while also providing items of his for display. My only complaint is that I wish they would have regulated the amount of people who were allowed in. It becomes a little too crowded.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great food and atmosphere, been twice csnt wait to go back!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Terrible service!! It was noon  and 3 people were in the bar and we couldn't hear each other! No live music which was fine, but when we asked the bartender to turn it down she was extremely rude and condescending.  Never going back!

name: 360 Burger
text: A little pricey for burgers, but hands down the best burger I've had in a LONG time! The sweet potato fries are to die for and there are many burgers to choose from and all I've tried have been delicious. The restaurant itself also has a cool, laid-back vibe. They have trivia nights and live music nights as well as a full bar and drink specials. If you're craving a burger it's a must.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: The captain and the staff of the General Jackson were extremely accommodating to our party.  The food was very good, but more importantly, the entertainment was fabulous.  We never expected the show to be so good.  We spent $135. for each Captain's Table ticket, but it was well worth it.  You get VIP treatment during the entire cruise, which includes first to board and meeting the captain for a little history of the ship, front row seating on the top deck in front of the band, a free cocktail, escorted to your table for dinner by your own waiter, another private tour by the captain, which includes the bridge, and a free General Jackson tee-shirt.  A must see while in Nashville.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I can't speak highly enough about the service and the atmosphere. I loved the old structure mixed with the new sounds.  Food wise, my group split a lot of shareable items.  The fried pickles had the perfect about of "fry" and sauce.  The artichoke dip with the garlic pita had the perfect amount of seasoning. The meatball slider could have used a bit more spice and the fritters could have used a bit more shrimp, but we had just eaten a most amazing Tennessee Hot slider. I must say though, my favorite item was the side of grits. Maybe it's more nostalgic than anything, but I've never tried grits as good!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
Please do not waste your money if you are looking for a fun time. This is a very touristy trip with marginal food and the show is over the top cheesy. The servers had terrible body Odor and the boat was dirty. Too many other great options out there in Nashville for authentic country music and the river is not scenic at all with dirty water and manufacturing industry lined shores.

The singers were talented but again, one of the cheesiest shows ever....felt bad for the performers.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Your experience at the Listening Room definitely depends on the performers that evening. All the seats are good, but your service will really depend on where you are sitting. The food is really overpriced for the quality, but that is to be expected at a cafe like this. There are better venues for live music in the city, but this is a historic option. Be sure to check out the line-up before you buy tickets!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I've been to the  Listening Room twice when visiting Nashville. I really enjoy this venue. The room is large with comfortable seating. My daughter usually buys tickets beforehand, but both times we went, it was not sold out. The singer/songwriters are always super talented and it's nice to hear the background about why they wrote their songs. They have a decent draft beer list. Haven't tried the food, but I honestly come for the music. I would highly recommend coming here for some wonderful entertainment.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
UPDATE: I spoke to Kevin via email regarding the extremely poor service my table received. Kevin spoke with the GM, Chase and stated that they would "be happy to refund the balance of my tab." I emailed back thanking them and gave them the necessary information in order to get a refund. It was now been 10 days since that email. I have called as well as sent another email. Surprisingly enough, I still do not have a refund. They have yet to give me a call back or answer my emails. 

WARNING. DO NOT COME TO THIS ESTABLISHMENT. They do not care about customer service and just want your money. I will be warning all friends and family about this.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
It was terrible. I was with a group that had made reservations for brunch well in advance. There was practically NO food on the buffet. I got a tiny pancake. I had also ordered coffee... it never came.

I was one of the lucky ones though... some paid for the buffet and got a piece of fruit only... some got nothing, but insisted on not paying.

There was only one other table besides our group, so the restaurant wasn't even 1/2 full. I have no idea what they would do if any locals actually came to their Sunday brunch... I imagine not much different though.

My bill was $25.00 with a 20% gratuity. $30 for a pancake and water... I should have refused to pay. The owner of this restaurant owes some serious refunds to the people in my group, and I can assure you that none of us will ever return!!!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Food is deceptively good.  Does not look like anything special from the website and other reviews but sweet and spicy fried pickles and fried green tomato sandwich with pimento cheese?  Yes please!  Bloody Mary's are fire and the music is incredible.  Oh and they take reservations for large groups.  Love

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I came for brunch with a large party expecting the buffet.  The buffet was small and resembled a hotel breakfast. So I decided to stick to the menu. Had a fantastic turkey and apple sandwich with the best sweet potato fries I ever had. I also tried the gravy from a buddy of mine, pretty good as well. The sweet tea didn't taste much like tea. The service was ok, the waitress seemed like she was working, but the infrastructure isn't ideal. Ok experience, better if you like live music.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
If you don't like this place you're an a-hole. 

This is a must for anyone into Johnny Cash / music / rock n roll. I've never seen so much stuff / info in such a small space. This is literally one of the most well designed museums I've ever seen. Everything from Johnny's personal letters to his awards to his clothing to yearbook photos to parts of his house were there. Detailed descriptions explained everything. Honestly was amazing!!! Plus it's across he street from the goo goo store.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
This was a great place to stop...the artifacts and stories were outstanding and the venue itself is really kept up.  Very well lit and clean.  The gold records, grammys, and record covers were really neat to see.

The last stop on the self guided tour is the "hurt" video and the awards that went with it.  That video is a work of art.  If it doesn't give you goosebumps then you are dead inside.  The gift shop was mostly standard fare..but there were some hidden gems (autographs/one of a kinds) if your willing to step up and spend it.  A must see for tourists for sure

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: So,  first time here.  We asked at the door who would be playing tonight, the answer we got from the lady selling the tickets "Oh, country music, the usual stuff".  Turns out we bought tickets for a benefit for some Christian ministry.  Not cool!  Also,  the board on the sidewalk advertises a $10 cover.  Cover is actually $12.  Also,  there is a $10 food and beverage minimum on top of the cover which we found out about once we were seated.  While this may very well be a lovely place,  clear and open communication would greatly improve visitor experiences.

name: 360 Burger
text: Very disappointing.  We arrive at 1:15 on a Monday between hockey games.   There are 3 people in the restaurant when we arrive.   We had 30 people in our group and the gentleman said we needed to call ahead even though no one was in the restaurant.   He sat us anyway because we were just going to come in individually if he didn't.  They took our order in a reasonable amount of time (we were all sat at different tables rather than one big one which was fine with us).  We were told we couldn't order off the lunch menu even though we were there at lunch.  There were 3 at our table and 2 drink orders were wrong.  The food came and it was correct except the dressing on a salad that was supposed to be vinaigrette and they brought blue cheese.  She asked for vinegrette and they just brought vinegar.   The burgers are good but nothing special.  The molten chocolate cake was very good.  With our big group we didn't even fill up half the tables.  We will not visit here again when we are back up here for our next hockey tournament.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I expected a better band at this place.  Seriously.  Doesn't have to be country... but these people were awful.

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text:
Oh my. I hate to do it but I'm going to have to drop a couple stars on this place. My group and I decided to stop in on New Years Eve and see what was gong on. I had fond memories of dancing and fun there a few years ago so I thought it would be a decent choice for us. WRONG. The rack room side was waaay too smokey and the music wasn't continuous. The dance side was honestly just kind of lame and tacky. Too many girls in sequined-out dresses and stilettos wobbling around and the DJ, although energetic, was playing pure crap. It appears that the average age of Blue Bar patrons are in their mid-late twenties and thirties. So why was he playing "music" that would appeal to 18 year olds? Some kind of booty-bass, thisismyfirsttimeataclub kind of music. Maybe I'm just old now, but I would much rather hear stuff that has actual lyrics and a good beat to DANCE to, not just drop it like it's hot. Also, there were NO TABLES ANYWHERE. There used to be high tables that you could at least stand next to and sit your drink on. The only way to have a table that night was to be part of  "Jason's" entourage and then you would be allowed access to the lounge part of the dance room. LAME. Wonder how much he paid for that crap? 

I realize that this was NYE and maaaaybe not what's typical for a Saturday, but I probably won't be back to find out. Boooo.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: My friend and I were in Nashville for the weekend and we recommend to this place by our tour guide we had that morning.  This was exactly what we came to Nashville for and it was right downtown.  There were 4 singer/song writer performers that night (we went on a Saturday) and they were all great!  A nice change from the bars on Broadway where you are all cramped and sweaty.  We got a table in the front row and reservations were only $5 for the Saturday show.  Well worth it in my opinion.  I only give it 4 stars as the food was nothing exceptional - stay away from the apple slaw as it was terrible!  Also, if there happens to be a bachelorette party in the room, they tended to be a bit noisy and not really interested in the performance and were sometimes a distraction.  Other than that, if you are looking for some live music from actual songwriters this is a great place!  We had a great time and would recommend it!

name: 360 Burger
text: This place is awesome! One of the best locally owned restaurants in Southeast Nashville. All of their food is locally sourced which makes for fresher and healthier product. Their burgers definitely rate an A in my book. I've had a few better, but not many. Their BLT sandwich is also something to enjoy. They've got good sweet potato fries and fried pickles. Live music and a full bar, but still very family oriented. Smoke free.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: I've been to other wax museums but they don't hold a candle to the madame. Technically, no one should hold a candle near wax statues, but I digress. Lots of fun to be had here! Celebrities from days past as well as contemporary ones make this a well rounded experience. I wasn't a huge fan of the staff members making us take a bazillion pics in a couple of places so that they could try to sell us memorabilia at the end, but it's a business, so...*shrugs*. Still totally worth it!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
A really fun & affordable place to hear live music in Nashville! This was the first stop for my friends and I right after landing at the airport, and it was definitely one of the highlights of our trip.

You can purchase tickets online in advance or at the door, and they'll seat you based on when you check-in in person. Get there earlier = get a table closer to the stage. The food/drink service was pretty fast considering so many people arrive all at the same time, and the draft beers were a great deal at $5 each for a lot of local beers.

The food was just alright - I'd recommend eating somewhere before if you have time (we didn't). But the atmosphere is really intimate and it's awesome to hear up-and-coming singer/songwriters. It's way better than going to any loud honky tonk on Broadway!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Nice but crowded. You can move at your own pace but plan for an hour to see everything. Bit $$$ but its a tourist attraction.

name: Silver Dollar Saloon
text: We were in Nashville from 12/28/12-1/1/13.  My Husband and I stopped in the Silver Dollar for a cocktail on Sat 12/29 while we were checkin out downtown Nashville.  It was pretty quiet.  The bartender was friendly and the band was pretty good.  So we come back to town on New Years Eve with my whole dance team and I cannot say enough about the service that we got from the bartenders (all we had to do to get a drink is raise our glass) and the band that was in there was fantastic.  Keep up the good work!!!!  We loved the place.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: During a long weekend trip to Nashville my wife and I and another couple sought refreshment in the Swingin' Door on a couple occasions. It is less than a block off of Broadway which reduced the bachelorette party traffic and the drunk males following them. The downstairs is fairly small with maybe 6 tables and a few barstools. During our visits, the bar tenders were always attentive with slight waits if a group came in to grab drinks. Two of the three performers that played during our times here were very good. We never ate here so can't comment on the food. The bathrooms were kind of gross. Overall, a decent place to grab a few beverages and listen to music.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great fun. Perfect venue. And food was good. I went for the music so good food was a bonus. I had the fish tacos. Very yummy.  Get the coleslaw !!

name: The Basement East
text: I ordered the F Bomb sandwich (see attached) with a side of chips and guac and it was delicious. Unique and flavorful, also the guacamole was terrific. It's hard to find a good guacamole and I could've eaten theirs all night.  I didn't expect bar food to be so tasty but I recommend it and intend to try their Sunday brunch.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: So excited that this finally opened up! Great location on the corner, the entertainment was excellent. The second floor was closed for a private event and there was only one bathroom on the first floor which I was in line for 20 minutes...the table I was with was halfway done with their food while I was gone waiting in line which was ridiculous. I waited 15 minutes for my waitress to bring my beer.  On the bright side, the artichoke dip and fried pickles were great! I also had the chicken and waffles which were some of the best chicken and waffles I've ever had-they were breaded with cornmeal and had a thick sauce...to die for! Def have to stop by when I come back to Nashville

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Absolutely fantastic. I went here with a group of six for brunch on Sunday. Reservations weren't needed as there was plenty of room. There were four guys playing acoustically from 11-1, and they took turns singing / playing their songs, and played for two hours. Such great music, very mellow and chill vibe. The only thing people might not like is you can't really talk or have conversations with your friends, since it's rude to the performers, but we were hungover and didn't want to talk so it was perfect. Most bars have the bands come around with tip jars and we were prepared to give them all our money because we loved them, but they didn't even do that.

Food / drink: Some of the best brunch food I've had. My friend and I split the fried green tomato BLT and the monte cristo and both were delicious. BLT was my favorite, monte cristo was very heavy, but that was expected, and still great. Two for one mimosas/bloody mary's. Service was wonderful, and I wish I lived in Nashville if only to be able to come here more often.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Fun night out to hear good music in an awesome little venue. The set up is basic but perfect for the environment.  We went on a Saturday night.  I bought the tickets ahead of time online. The tickets say to print but it isn't necessary. When you arrive they check you in with your name.Tickets were $5 with a minimum $7 food/drink per person.  We each had a drink and shared the buffalo chicken dip. I could have done without the dip but for the price it wasn't too bad.  All of the performers were extremely talented and put on a great show. It was a perfect low key night for us after a night of partying the night before.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great place to hear music and plenty of room to accommodate guests. I would go back here on my next trip to Nashville. Try the vegetable and chicken soup. May have been the best meal I had in Nashville. It was that good!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Color me unimpressed. Wings were pretty close to lousy. Drinks?  No bitters or simple syrup for old fashions. I suggest you try one of a million other over priced locations on broadway.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Had Sunday Brunch here - upon entering, we were told that we had to wait at the bar despite having reservations,  because the chef was backed up. There were about 50 empty tables, so that was bizarre. My bloody Mary was great though - don't do bottomless, as the glasses are half the size of the $6 pint and not worth the $15 price tag. The menu was much more scarce than the website, plus they gave my friend and I each a different one, which had to be corrected. Our food was okay (my friend got Shrimp and Grits and I got the Veggie flatbread) - glad we had a groupon. The singer played from about 1130-1, and it was a nice intimate setting for her performance.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Great Johnny Cash museum with loads of memorabilia and information. Reasonable admission and easy to get to if you are in downtown Nashville. I learned a lot of new information about Johnny Cash and liked the way items were displayed and how the rooms were set up. Lots of items in the gift shop too! We got there soon after it opened on a Thursday morning and pretty much had the place to ourselves.

name: 360 Burger
text:
This place is great! Our first burger stop in Nashville - burgers were cooked perfectly and delicious. Atmosphere is laid back, not a huge place so it feels like a hometown dive (but isn't). Met the GM and head cook - super nice and made great conversation.  

The beef/cheese dip with fried pita is AMAZING. Simple but delicious. 

Good beer selection too. Will absolutely be back regularly!

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text: This review is solely due to how rude the manager was at the end of the night. They do not close at 3am. They very rudely kick patrons out before 2:30.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text:
I love this bar! Right off broadway but not full of drunk kids. Great singers...like Jimmy Charles! He was amazing..sang a lot of goodies but not the same ole songs you hear at every other bar, plus he sings his originals!  Best night in nashville! 

The jalapeño burger & tots are delicious!  Margaritas gone down smooth.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Best burger I've had in a decade. The King Burger rules. Beef, ham, egg, pulled pork. Fantastic.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Entertainment was amazing food was horrible had the pull pork which was super dry. Mac and cheese was super dry.

name: 360 Burger
text:
I am extremely disappointed in the entirety of this establishment.
From food. To service this is a genuine one star rate. 

A bit over a 40 minute wait for mediocre food. 

We arrived and were seated quickly enough but things went down hill from there. 

Waitresses scrambled in the most disorganized and misguided way to wait tables.
We were waited on by two people  whilst one woman waited nearly 30minutes to be waited on at all. 

Appetizer took extremely long to come out. And was just a simple order of fried cheese. 

We then waited 40 or more minutes for poor burgers. 
They were dry and over done. 

One order even specified medium and was still prepared well done. 

Overall just an extremely poor experience and I probably won't be returning.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
I can only speak to the brunch experience at the Listening Room, but it left much to be desired. First, we barely listened to live music. When we called ahead, the manager confirmed the online listing that said the music goes from 11-1, so we made a reservation for 11. When we arrived a sign out front said the music started at 11:30. Our server confirmed this, even though on the wall inside it listed the first musical act as starting at noon. But we thought, well if it's at 11:30, that's ok. It didn't start until noon, and well after we had finished eating.  

The food options were overwhelming and overpriced (I guess to pay the musicians?). If you're going to have an $18 buffet and very limited additional menu options, make the buffet something more than eggs and bacon set up in hotel pans in the back. Also the math on the bottomless mimosas and bloody marys didn't make a lot of sense.

I had family in town, so it was a shame we wasted a meal at this place.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Take the title "Listening Room" very seriously. Not a good place to socialize with your party. With that being said excellent food and drinks as well as entertainment. Fried okra is delicious and something you gotta try!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
My parents, my kids (ages 10 and 11) and I went on the Friday night dinner cruise to celebrate my parents' 45th wedding anniversary and had a wonderful time.  We had a great table right next to the stage, close enough to the performers for one of them to reach down and give my son a fistbump which we all thought was pretty cool.  The servers were very attentive and knowledgeable about the experience as a whole.  The food was so-so, hence only 4 stars instead of 5.   Salad appetizer with ranch or italian dressing.  Entree was a baked potato, asparagus, steak and shrimp.  Chicken tenders and fries for my kids.  The steak could have used a little more seasoning and I would have loved some cocktail sauce to dip my shrimp in since it had no other seasoning on it.  Mom loved the asparagus.  The key lime pie was awesome.  My parents got a free slice of pecan pie each with "happy anniversary" written around the plate in caramel sauce.  Very nice touch.  The show was great too and I am not a country music fan at all.  It was a good mix of genres and very entertaining.  Even my kids loved it and want to go back.

I highly recommend taking the dinner cruise to celebrate a special event.  Let your server know if it's a special occasion and the host will announce it at the beginning of the cruise.  My parents got a special round of applause for having been married for so long.  That made their evening extra special!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: By far our favorite place on Broadway.  Beer was really cold and the bands were really good.  TVs had the games on there was a great mix of 24-65 year old people all dancing. Tuesday night band was really good.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Racist establish that uses arbitrary dress code policies to keep certain groups of people out. When asked to see their dress code policy we were told we were being "hostile" and refused to provide the dress code policy.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
My husband and I found ourselves wishing that we had visited the museum after the Country Music Hall of Fame. You can easily do both in an afternoon. That's because they are sort of the opposites of each other. CMHF is expansive but only gives you a broad look at a lot of  artists and only has a few Johnny Cash items on display. 

The Johnny Cash Museum felt small, and packed with objects (which could use a bit more space to breathe), but it provides a much more in depth look at his career. The interactive features were thoughtful and unexpected, such as live concert footage next to a display of guitars, photos etc from the same era. An old radio with an interactive display of songs that he may have heard as a child on it. Such a great idea.

The quality and variety of the items in the collection is outstanding: lots of handwritten notes and significant items like personal photographs and lots of cool memorabilia related to Folsom Prison Blues. There's lot of stage outfits and instruments as well....and a few odd things at the end. 

Because the objects don't have a lot of room to breathe, you have to be patient and take time to absorb the text panels (compellingly written; I am a fan and i still learned a lot) and to take the time to listen to the many tracks, films and interactive features throughout the museum.
