Otherwise you might feel that you're gone through the whole museum too quickly. For the same reason, when going with family you might want to consider your children's attention spans for the same reason, might be better for older children or teens.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Came to WR for lunch and after dinner drinks on the same day and had Michelle as our server for both. She was fantastic!!! So was the music. Loved the band both times!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Okay so here's the deal,  I love, love, love the Listening room for their music.  I've seen several shows here and they are amazing!   $5 ticket for talented musicians?!  Win.   HOWEVER, the food.   I had never eaten here before.   We were a party of 5 with three underaged teens.  $15 minimum for food, ok fine-but the food was truly awful.  Not one thing we ordered was good.  The hummus plate,  stale crackers and bland dry crumbly  hummus.  Not a good start.   Cup of soup? Meh.   Turkey salad was probably the "best" of what we ordered.   Turkey lunch meat, and some kind of pre-cooked bacon.   Two burgers at our table, inedible.   Way over cooked, no amount of ketchup to save it and bun was stale.  The Mac and cheese- I have no words. Just don't order it.   Turkey apple and cheese sandwich- again stale bread.   EVEN THE PEPSI WAS BAD!   I would have rather paid more for our tickets if this is what they pass off as dinner.   So music 5 stars- food- 1 maybe.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great talent and good venue.   Just don't get the entrees. They are not very good. Stick with the sandwiches and smaller fares. Other than that, really enjoyed the artists and the sound is amazing. Small enough to feel like you have the best seats anywhere you sit.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Really enjoyed the night. The guys on the stage were very talented. Played all the Requests that came to them and didn't beg for money all night. I like that they rotate singers so there is always music. I didn't eat there and only drank beer. Menu I saw only had pizza. One negative... A bathroom attendant?!  Really?  Is this a Nashville thing?  I didn't go to the bathroom at any other bars but I will be disappointed if I find someone sitting in there bugging me while I pee. And I always feel bad for them!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
In general, my husband and I aren't big bar people, especially in downtown Nashville.  We're just not into overpriced, watery drinks, loud music, smoke and obnoxious drunk tourists.  The Big Bang, however, is one that we often frequent whenever we're downtown enjoying dinner or hanging out after work.  

We've never been into the place when there ISN'T a huge crowd and a happenin' vibe.  Despite the crowds, we can usually find a seat with a good view, and the waitstaff is quick and attentive with our drinks.  If we can manage to arrive before about 8:30pm, there is no cover charge, which is awesome.  After that time, cover is $6/person - not bad at all for the entertainment you receive while there.  Drink prices are a little steep, but not terribly unreasonable, and the bar staff supplies a heavy pour.

The entertainment is the real reason you should visit The Big Bang.  The dueling piano players are AWESOME and incredibly talented; each plays the piano, bass, and drums in addition to rockin' the vocals.  They are versed in many styles of music and play to the masses - whatever is requested, in any genre, can be performed by the band (especially if the request is made alongside a $20 bill).  You can and should tip the band members, who work incredibly hard for their money to put on the best possible show night after night.  

We love the energy and vibe of The Big Bang, along with the friendly staff and patrons.  It's easily one of our favorite places to catch some great music in Nashville!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Went here for a night out in Nashville, the food was amazing and I had an awesome bartender! Jasmine was friendly, intriguing, and all around a great representation of the company! I will definitely be back again!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
LOVED this place. I was visiting Nashville for a short trip and had a local show us around the bars in the area. This was definitely the best one. We stopped here first, and ended up coming back again to end the night. There are two pianos set up facing each other, which two pianists  play duets all night. If you want the artists to play a song, you give a tip and request the song. The request sheet is actually blank - I was really impressed with how many different songs the guys knew! I really loved how different the genres were from song to song. It went from country to hip hop to rock and everything in between.

The only downside is the selection of beer is not great. There were probably about 10 options of beers, bottles only. Not bad selections, but just not a large quantity. I got a Newcastle, I think it was 5 bucks. I didn't really mind though because the place is so cool it makes up for it.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
The new location is a definite upgrade! 

Don't be alarmed about parking because it is now Downtown (off of Broadway) and in the new SoBro district... there is an attached free lot and tons of off-street and affordable lot options that surround this spot. 

We popped in last night for a low-key hang to celebrate a dear friend's birthday and enjoyed ourselves. Some great music was on the gorgeous stage and the acoustics were certainly on point. The staff and our server were super friendly and made some suggestion off the diverse cocktail menu.... which also happens to include "Skinnies" - drinks under 125 calories. Hello diet-friendly cocktail. 

Prices were fair on both drinks and bites and I happened to love the layout of this joint. 
It is spacious yet still offers a cozy vibe. And, I'm absolutely smitten over the rustic lighting fixtures - perhaps I have watched too much of HGTV lately? Either way, this is a great spot for a meal, drinks, catch live music, host an event, or dare I say - to just hang out!

I dig it.

TIP: The patio offers up pretty sweet views of downtown. Great place to relax and enjoy!

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: (Horrible)  where to start..  I travel 8 months out of the year.  For me to take the time to write a review is really bad.  Food, well it's disgusting along with the service.  Bar tender along with all other employees are quick to bring you a drink for the most part.  Food however, forget it.   Not to mention you truly don't want what they're serving!  Ordered their standard house burger with lettuce and tomato.  Came without both.  Asked for medium rare, was told sorry it's frozen..  Got the Philly with order too.  That amount of got peppers is a sure sign that meat is bad.  Because why otherwise would you ruin a simple steak & cheese with so much none tasty spice?  Not to mention the ridiculous chain smoking.  If you're looking for live music and a friendly local vibe.  Please don't go through what I have. Go somewhere else!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great bar, great music and awesome drinks!! Best part, Jake the bar tender awesome we will be back very soon!! Our new favorite bar!!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I was surprised how small it was but what you get is a very personal and authentic experience. Also, there is nobody rushing you around the exhibits. Some great historical items to be seen and a few excellent audio visual displays. I learned a lot about the man and I'm so glad that I paid a visit. (Very welcoming staff as well) Happy to part with $17 to learn more about this giant of music.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Love Kid Rock...not so much the bar. Music was so load you couldn't have any type of conversation. Service not that good. Had to go to the bar for beers. Hopefully they can get better.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I'm not a die-hard Johnny Cash fan, but this was one of my favorite things we did on our trip to Nashville. I've always been into his greatest hits and had enjoyed the Walk the Line biopic, but I left with a much deeper appreciation for his contribution to music and his legacy. Tons of memorabilia; everything from lyric sheets and love letters to candid photos and on-stage costumes. Staff was friendly and enthusiastic throughout. As other reviewers mentioned, the last section of the museum features his Hurt video, which was filmed just a few months before he died. Not a dry eye in the house. Be sure to spend the few extra dollars to get your photo "taken with Johnny". The museum staff encouraged us to take the attached shot, and as you can see, it was worth every penny.

name: 360 Burger
text: Eye wateringly expensive for what you get. An app, dinner for two, and a few drinks came close to $100.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
The Listening Room Cafe was the quintessential Nashville experience during our last trip.  Our brief experience with the Listening Room Cafe was great.  This review is only for the music and bar, as we did not have any food.  

We ran across it as we had some time to spare before concerts at LP, and this place is right near the entrance of the bridge.  There is not much around it, but we could clearly hear the music from outside, so we decided to check it out.

When you walk in, it is an open, brick room with a bunch of tables and a stage.  Pretty stripped down place, with a basic bar menu with a bunch of drinks.  Service at the bar was great.  

It was clear from the start that this place was about the music.  No gimmicks or distractions.  Just a couple of folks on a small stage playing great original country.  

Sure, at the bars, you get great music, but music there seems peripheral; at LRC, the music is paramount and just feels important.

name: 360 Burger
text: One of the best burgers I've had at a restaurant in a long time great service. Extremely nice staff. Your drink will never go empty or table ignored there

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Easily one of the worst restaurants I've ever been to. We sat for 20 minutes without a waiter even coming to our table or being given menus. Finally after asking for a server twice, a waitress came over. We ordered the bottomless mimosas. They were basically just orange juice, very small, slow to be refilled, and not at all worth the $15. We then ordered some food from their incredibly short and unappetizing menu (vegetarians beware, there is one option for you and it's disgusting). The food came out and all of it was incredibly awful. I've had better food in dirty roadside diners, where I question whether or not I'm eating chicken or rat. As for the music, it wasn't bad. But the jerk making tranny jokes needs to just not. Way to be an ignorant piece of crap. Save yourself the trouble and go anywhere else.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
TERRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE! There are definitely more enjoyable ways to spend your time and money in Nashville. 

My wife and I visited with our baby, and the moment we stepped inside our baby started having a melt down. We asked if we could step back out for a moment and the attendant at the entrance rudely stated that we had to go all the way through and exit at the end due to the fire code (which made no sense). After making our way through the packed exhibit as quickly as we could with a screaming baby, I stopped back at the front desk to ask if we could re-enter later after we got our son calmed down. Despite me explaining the situation, the guy at the desk even more rudely stated that that there was no way we could re-enter because we already went through and that the policy. I stepped away before losing it on the jerk, and after we got our son calmed down we went back and demanded to to speak with the manager. She reluctantly agreed to give us a refund, but didn't even bother apologizing much less acting like she cared when we complained about the way her staff treated customers. I thought the South was supposed to be known for its hospitality, not to mention the fact that this place is in the tourism/hospitality industry. 

The little museum looked like it had some pretty neat stuff if we would have had the chance to enjoy it, but the terrible customer service totally wrecked it for us. So all things considered, I would recommend skipping the museum. Just watch the movie at home later, because there are a lot better ways to enjoy spending your time and money in Nashville.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This place is awesome if you ever come to Nashville - unbelievable customer service Frankie & the band was amazing

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Out of our entire trip to Nashville this was by far our favorite part.  We bought some tickets online ahead of time and it was quick and easy. We got there 20 minutes before the show and were seated right away. The waitress was nice and attentive. The show started 20 minutes late but it was so excellent we didn't mind.  The singers and musicians were awesome and the kids eyes didn't leave the stage. The food was a 4/5. Small portions but good flavors for the most part. Buffalo chips were not good and are the only thing I wouldn't do all over again. The performers were so nice and made themselves available after the show. A Nashville must!!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: This is my favorite place to catch a writer's round in town! Even though this is a music venue, the menu and food is great. Every time I've been here the staff has been great! Definitely a "must do" on any trip to Nashville.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Really loved the atmosphere! We were with a group of 5 women ranging from 22 to 82. My daughter and my 2 sisters stood at the bar for 20 minutes talking and having good conversation waiting to order. They eventually tried getting a bartenders' attention but were totally ignored. We then asked a waitress passing by if we could order a drink and she (a bit abruptly) told us we could not order from her. It was a Wednesday, a little crowded but not crazy. We were just asking for a drink to sip and enjoy the music. Did not happen so we left. Our group was from Houston, Austin and Charleston, so we are accustomed to crowds and waiting and don't mind. But service just wasn't going to happen at all here. However, fun place though and the band was great!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: What an amazing collection of memorabilia.  The interactive exhibits are also very cool. One star deduction for the lack o crowd control - they really need to limit admission a little bit - but other than that an first rate, 5 star experience. Highly recommend.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
We're here for the first time in Nashville. This bar is so cool. The band is amazing. Frankie our server is so cool and so attentive. 

We hit every bar in broadway and this is the  best  and most fun a must visit

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Visited during CMA Fest 2018. Great service from Jake at the downstairs bar...best bartender we met all weekend! Custom drinks mixed at fair prices. Fun setting with live music.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
A terrific collection. 
I'm not a big fan of museums, but I do and did enjoy the music of Johnny Cash. Ultimately fans will enjoy the most.   It's modern and you can easily spend twenty minutes or a couple of hours. Primo location on third.  Highly recommend.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The atmosphere and show was amazing, the service was slow and the food was horrible. I ordered the prime rib medium rare with green beans and Gouda mac. The prime rib was completely seared/burnt on one side which was odd to me, like it was a pre cut piece of meat cooked to order and not an actual whole prime rib. The Gouda mac was good but ice cold and the green beans where super salty. The other 4 members in our groups enjoyed the show but agreed the food was bad. Oh and their soda fountain wasn't working so the soda tasted really bad and the server didn't know what to do to fix it.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
"It took 5 phone calls, 2 emails, and 25 days to receive a $20 check (not even the entire amount I was overcharged).
I paid $25 to park, $22 to get in the door, and $50 for a sandwich and 2 beers to be afforded this experience.

Like I said, the music was good and the place was cool, 
but Nashville is eaten up with cool music places."

The place is cool. The music was great. The food was bad.
The service was horrendous, and then a few days later I saw where I had been overcharged for more than $20.

And, when I say horrendous, I mean nearly 30 minutes before we saw a server (the place was not busy). We saw her when the food came, but never saw her again. We had to flag down someone else to ask for another beer and water, though the water never came. Then, we waited a good bit at the end of the evening trying to catch a glimpse of her to get a check, eventually just going to the front of the place and asking for it. 

Then, of course, charged $50 on a $24 bill.

I talked to a manager by phone who sounded pretty aggravated to field the call. Their calls roll to their personal phones. Service industry don't live in the office...
It wasn't the attitude you would expect on calling to report an overcharge, and there was even a tone at one point like I might be making this stuff up or something.

I didn't hear back from him for 5 days, at which point I contacted the owner. 
He was sympathetic and accommodating at first, 
and agreed to refund the entirety of my bill. 

I waited for 2 weeks, but the check never came. 
I contacted him again and he was less than caring.
A reply email that he meant to mail it 2 weeks ago; but had an emergency; but actually did just run across it yesterday and it was on its way.

The check did arrive after another request, but not only was it not for the entire bill, it was not even for the entire amount of the overcharge. 

He did include 2 tickets to get in the door; like I would want to experience this again.

Both of these guys double-talked so much they couldn't keep it all straight, not for some schmuck like me. It was palpable when you talked to them and evident in their actions.

It took 5 phone calls, 2 emails, and 25 days to receive a $20 check (not even the entire amount I was overcharged).
I paid $25 to park, $22 to get in the door, and $50 for a sandwich and 2 beers to be afforded this experience.

Like I said, the music was good and the place was cool, 
but Nashville is eaten up with cool music places.

Spend your money somewhere else.
This place does not care about its patrons; plenty of tourists in Nashville.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
The place seems to be about revenue generation.....

We were saddened as we think Johnny Cash would be underwhelmed by this money pit museum. The whole till/ticket purchase layout is poorly executed and it seems if you can flog an item with his name on then let's do so..... 

Give it a miss.....buy a CD for $20 from an independent store and appreciate what the man came from and created.....

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: A great addition to the downtown area! The full menu gives plenty of options, both healthy and more indulgent. The Mac and Cheese with chicken is beyond incredible, as well as the Kale and Quinoa salad. Their signature cocktails are super tasty, as well. Make sure you check out the rooftop, which is the tallest on Broadway. The staff is great, and I would def recommend trying it out!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: What a great experience. Good memorabilia and movie clips. Enjoyed learning about him and his family. Very clean and well organized museum.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: For a tourist destination type set-up, we were impressed by the menu and quality of the food. They did their best to accommodate our multiple food restrictions. The venue is excellent for the performers and not bad to enjoy them. The vibe is light and feels more intimate than the cavernous space would suggest.  However...it was freezing!  The only thing that put a blot on my memory and will keep it a one time affair is the lack of suitable heating. I hope it's air-conditioned in the summer or be prepared to shed layers as decency allows, because it's a  family friendly.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Came out with a group of friends around 10pm on a Saturday night in mid-May for a drink or three on the rooftop. The place was packed, drunk people everywhere. You have to walk up five or six flights of stairs to get to the top. Sloppy bachelorettes, aggressive bachelors and a lot of twerking going on. Not my scene. 

But if I were a bachelor or bachelorette, or interested in meeting one of those then this is the place to be at..

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Amazing place. We were the first table sat on what was the first full night open. Heather was our server, the sweetest! Manager Chase checked in on us a few times and even opened the merch store for us and got us t shirts and other items that were still in boxes. Mike, security, gave us a tour of the VIP section, second floor and rooftop! Food was great. Beer can chicken was so good we ordered two, and artichoke dip I even finished off with a spoon when the pita chips ran out. And then the music! Amazing. Great job, Heather, Chase and the rest of the team. Already planning our trip back! Tip it on back y'all!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: 545 pm June 2 2018  looking forward to getting a good seat and having a nice cocktail 15 minutes before the piano bar activities started, however my friend and I were greeted rudely at the bar when we were asking about the particulars of the Liquor used in certain cocktails.  Customer service is sub par and lacking.  We left. Hope the music made up for the bar service.  #dissapointed

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text: This small but seriously original music venues are fantastic and original. The hippy country vibe is wonderful. You will find yourself having a great time.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Love the bar, food and music! 5 stars on that. My complaint is the bartenders and the shady stuff they did to me. So my wife and I were there the past weekend drinking for a few hours. We were ordering Tito's and soda water for 23$ a round. I was paying cash each round and leaving a 2$ tip. After maybe 7-8 rounds, I ran out of cash and had to order our next round with my debit card. When the bill came it was 22.77$. I look and they had a 77 cents charge for using the card. Not a big deal, but then I began to think that when the bartenders were charging me 23$ a round when it should have been 22$. They were adding the electronic fee even when I was paying cash. I inquired about it to the bartender and all she said was that she made a mistake. To me, it seemed like they were trying to scam an extra 1$ on each round. I can only imagine how much they do that on a busy night.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Awesome time, great music and drinks on 2nd floor. Made our trip. Group of 14, very accommodating . Will come back

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Dierks' Whiskey Row is extremely well done! The interior is beautiful and clean, and they did a great job preserving the old building. The food is delicious - highly recommend the mac n cheese and fried pickles! Great varied music on all 3 levels with quality sound, and amazing country bands! Can't wait to go back :)

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Mini burgers were awesome. Drinks and music typical for a honky tonk. Would eat here again.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
I cannot believe there are bad reviews of this place. It is amazing the 1st level is rock/country  and 2nd level was 90's and early 2000 rock. 

 Food was excellent. The bartender ladies  especially on the 1st floor are smoking hot. 

 The bands were just incredible both levels.  

Hit this place up early on for the music. And then about 9 30 10 o'clock head to the Back Corner dance club in Germantown. Dance the night away awesome R&B  Non stop music from 10 to 3:00 a.m.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Awesome spot!  It was a blast. Great bands and atmosphere. Good beer and drink selection. They were out of Badass Lager on the weekend which was disappointing but many other beers to choose from.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: When I visited Nashville, this was one of my favorite things we did! The museum was really interesting- I learned a lot about Johnny Cash- and we had a blast. Tickets were about $20, and we spent a good amount of time in the museum. The gift store was pretty solid, and the cafe was so-so (I wouldn't plan on eating at the cafe as a destination, just as convenience). I enjoyed how interactive the museum was, for example there is an exhibit where you could listen to his songs organized by decade. Definitely a place to visit when you are in Nashville!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Wish I knew about this place sooner!

Who needs Broadway?  When I'm back in Nashville I'll come to the listening room multiple times. 

Such talented singer songwriters!!!

Left wanting MORE MORE MORE!!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I agree with other reviews, go for the music. Went the night Sarah Ames, Josh Dorr, Sam Ashworth, and Bruce Wallace were playing. They were wonderful. However I was disappointed by the pulled pork steak. Mine was dry and overlooked. The waitress saw me cutting into it and offered a steak knife. Then I ordered the strawberry shortcake which was a lot better. Thumbs up to the staff. The service was wonderful.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Being from out of town and visiting Nashville this is a cool place to visit if you want to see a awesome view of the city.  The roof top bar is amazing and worth the hike up the 4 flights of stairs.  The food was not bad and they had a nice variety.  We ate on the second floor as the first floor was pretty packed with people enjoying their dinner and listening to the live music.  The night we went they did not have live music on the second floor.  Also on the second floor they do not have servers, so while you are able to order food you do have to order it at the bar.  They were not that busy and we were easily able to walk up to the bar but on nights when they are busier I could see it being an issue.  Would visit again though.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: This is right in the middle of music row and by far the loudest on the strip.  The music was actually really good much more southern rock than country (which I love)!  It's a huge bar with at least 3 levels.  It's really Nice inside very modern.   It's packed even when the strip wasn't that busy.  The reason for the 3 stars is this isn't a true honky Tonk which is really what we were looking for.  It's more commercialized with a double level stage lighting etc.  if that's your thing this is your place.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Came here for drinks and for the music! This place was packed on a saturday evening, and great cover bands galore! On this strip of music bars, this is probably one of the better ones. careful, there is a casual dress code, so no athletic shorts. Great drinks, upstairs area, great music, i recommend visiting!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Not very impressed with this busy and overcrowded museum. I would have enjoyed it more if I could have seen what was in the museum. Less people better time, I would suggest calling to see when the slowest time is to visit and hopefully you will have a better experience than I did.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Typical museum. Lots to see and read. $18 a ticket. Clean. Videos movies his suits etc. Get there.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Only one bartender who is really slow.  We spent 2 hours here because the band was good, but the bartender/owner stayed down at one end and couldn't keep up.   After waiting 30 mins for a drink, I waved my arms at her, and she completely flipped out, so we got up to leave, and then she got worse and actually ran to the door guy to have us thrown out as we were leaving.  It was like "you can't walk out, I'm throwing you out".  She then called out to my wife "you fkn b@tch", even though she never said a single word to her.  I know menapause is rough, but holy cow!!  If you can't handle it, sell the bar for God's sake.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
This review is for the venue - not the food!

We were bar hopping on Broadway on a Friday night and we passed through some places that were mostly misses. We almost passed by this place, as you can't see all that's inside from the front door, but then we saw all the people dancing, drinking, and singing through the window. So we stepped back in. It was so fun! They have a huge stage and the people who were playing were great. We did not try the food but the bar was great and the venue was lit!!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
If I've learned one thing about Nashville, it's that nobody believes in elevators!! Or maybe it's just telling me to get my a** back into shape....

   This was a cool little rooftop bar to chill out on during the day. There was a DJ playing, party music, and a bar right in the middle. There wasn't a whole lot of room for seating that wasn't at the bar, with just a handful of tables and a couple couches. 

   I don't really see anything that was Dierks Bentley related about this bar, but whatever. They had some fun drinks but they were a bit expensive. I tried the Redbull Frose' and it was really good! $11 was a bit high thought for the size of it. 

   We ended up claiming one of the couches and they were very enjoyable to sit and look at the pretty view of downtown Nashville. They even had huge fans blowing, which was perfect for the 90 degree weather that we had.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Fun Romp Through Johnny Cash Memorabilia

SITREP

This is an excellent stop in Nashville, and a must-do (really) for anyone who is a fan of the fan.  The museum tour is $15 and there are all sorts of great memorabilia items for sale for those who want to take a piece of the man back home with them.

AND SODA!

These guys thought of everything!  They even sold my diet Pepsi in a nice adjunct refrigerator just when I need some cool refreshment.

THE SETUP

There was also a haunting theme for me this whole trip of mine while in Nashville - I kept on running into moments drenched in Johnny Cash and/or Nine Inch Nails (NIN).   

* At bars & music venues - such as at Tootsies - I kept hearing Johnny Cash or NIN music played by the bands;
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/ysb-uye-gs-up-hoes-down-town-nashville-pub-and-bar-crawl-nashville?select=Bbit4aziG6MXbw3jnh4bsw#Bbit4aziG6MXbw3jnh4bsw

* At the United Record Pressing tour, we witness a new pressing of NIN's album "Pretty Hate Machine"! 
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/yelp-spring-break-event-tour-of-united-record-pressing-nashville?filter_by_userid=True&select=QWEtZLqDk_boTWAEBmW1Og&userid=3mNz5nQFTIBQm0oU5mBR0w#QWEtZLqDk_boTWAEBmW1Og

* And then as I walked into this store, not a minute passed by and they were playing Johnny's haunting cover of NIN's song, "Hurt".

THE LOWDOWN

I love this place and it was also a serendipitous sign that continued throughout the weekend as I kept running into flashes of Johnny Cash at other music venues, over restaurant music speakers, and flyers & billboards that had the man's likeness plastered all over Nashville...

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We came in for an appetizer and a quick drink on a Friday night. Our waitress was nice and service was quick. The Bavarian pretzel was actually really good. Enjoyed the live band.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I thought I knew a decent amount about Johnny Cash..but I did not! This museum was a great stop on a cold winter day in Nashville.

The price of entry is not the cheapest but I think it was worth the cost. We spent a solid 1.5-2 hours here and really read into all of the displays and watched the multimedia presentations. There was some really cool stuff and a few interactive displays as well. It was also amazing to see so many cool Cash (and more) memorabilia items.

The coffee shop and gift shops are also in the same building and have a decent amount of cool stuff in them as well. While I didn't buy anything I saw a few things that could make cool gifts for big time fans!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This place opened a few years ago and I never checked it out. Big mistake. The staff is awesome ( especially Kayla ) she always takes good care of us. Great live country music. Games and entertainment. If you like to dance this place is it!! Great food, great music, great people!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Another cool little bar on Broadway in downtown Nashville. 

The music was fun on Tuesday evening when we stopped in. It was also nice and cool with the air conditioning while it was 95 degrees outside. 

Live music that you can hear from the street if you can't make it in. 

I just find these places to all be regular run of the mill dive bars, nothing great but nothing bad either. This was one of the better ones in my opinion.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
I asked the band to play a song.... i handed the artist $40 bucks and she said told me it would cost me $100. it was a lynard skynard song which they were fully capable of playing. I asked for managers and they said they couldn't help. 

Lame bands. Good service but the live bands weren't worth my cash. Take your money to Tootsies. At the bands and servers were nice

name: The Basement East
text:
My friend got us some tickets to see the Prince tribute at Basement East, so we hit up Lyft and got ourselves over to the East side for the evening.

We got there early so we could hopefully get something to eat. Around back of the venue is a bar area that has tables inside as well as a nice deck with tables outside. We ordered food and drinks at the bar and sat outside to shoot the shit and wait. Their menu has some interesting selections - bahn mi with pork, spicy pickled carrots; grilled chicken with some sort of spicy sauce; tacos; etc. The bahn mi was actually really good, definitely had some spice, and was served with a small handful of tortilla chips. It wasn't too big and hit that sweet spot of not so much food you were stuffed and unable to catch a buzz and not so little food that you got wrecked drunk and had to get carted home. The specialty drinks they had going on for Bonnaroo weekend were also good and only $5 for blood orange vodka and Red Bull Red.

Once we paid up, we went around to the front to go inside the venue. The stage was on the right as you walked in, bar straight ahead. Some tables were set up in the middle of the room and there were barstools in front of the bar. There was also a small mini-bar set up on the wall beside the hallway to the restrooms that had beer and a small selection of liquor drinks. The size pretty nice and luckily it was kind of empty that night so everyone could get a good look at the band playing Prince jams. Smoking outside on the deck. Bartenders were fast, I suggest using the mini bar if they have your drinks as that's less busy and much more convenient.

Overall a good venue and I look forward to seeing other shows here!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: It's a plain establishment in my eyes, but one thing that always stands out in my eyes is the venue is always the loudest on the block. Great musicians sing good songs, and they actually interacted with the guests when I was there. No complaints from me, definitely.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: The bouncer called me a faggot and that I couldn't get in with a tank top. I looked inside the bar and several females and the band had tank tops or spaghetti straps on. I found it very offensive.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
What makes this place great are the singer/songwriters that perform here. I love the fact they also serve food however it was pretty mediocre. First off, I'd like to say that our server was amazing. She truly went out of her way and made sure we got what we had asked for. If it wasn't for her amazing service I'd give it 3.5 stars. The kitchen got our order wrong multiple times regardless of sending it back. I had gotten the BBQ platter pulled pork and the meat was very dry. I enjoyed the green beans and Brussels sprouts. I'd skip the Mac and cheese as it was very bland in my opinion. 

If you're trying to meet your $15 min, maybe try the wings? It was apparently the performer's favorite. I would've done so but I had already placed my order when they decided to share that piece of information.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: This was one of the coolest experiences of my life. The sculptures were so accurate. Staff members were above and beyond, especially this sweet lady running the photo shoot portion of it. She made our experience from a 4 to the full 5 stars.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: There were a lot of cool things to see. I really wish that for the money, there would have been more of a "tour" feel. Also wish that there would have been some kind of markings on things to tell if they were real or replicas. All in all it was ok, but I can check it off of my list of things to do in Nashville.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Wonderful live music and our waitress was the most on the ball server I have ever seen! A fun stop on the Honky Tonk Highway.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: We just went to the General Jackson Showboat lunch Christmas show.  The price for the cruise and lunch was 65.00 including Tennessee state tax.  The salad and desert were at the table when you set down at your assigned table, we were at table 25 a side table by the window.  Our seat was great I loved looking out the window while we ate our lunch.  The meal consisted of Turkey, mash potatoes, gravy, green beans, and dinner rolls.  The meal was served to us by our servers and we had ice tea and coffee to drink.  The service was excellent and our seats still had a good view of the show even though it was on the side.  The desert was peppermint cheesecake with chocolate sauce drizzled on the plate.  The entertainer was excellent with 6 entertainers who all were very talented.  It was a great day to cruise about 45 degrees and relatively clear for a December day.  All in all I would recommend attending the General Jackson Christmas show.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Very good food great service. Only thing that was sketchy is that this place doesn't explain why there is a "tech fee"   It's not on menu and posted no where. You are subject to pay it depending on how much your bill is.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
After reading roughly 40 one star reviews that illustrate the physical and verbal aggression that the security guards have used towards many human beings, I am not sure why I am even bothering to write this review. It is very apparent that the establishment knows their security guards are very LARGE and aggressive men who immediately resort to physical violence when a simple spoken sentence to someone could completely change the outcome of a situation. This is the most disgusting place I have ever stepped foot in. Again, this review will change nothing, as it is clear by the many reviews that speaking up about the immediate physical and verbal aggression occurring here has not changed. These men are still forcibly putting their hands on sober, 100 pound young women, literally THROWING them outside, and then calling them a B****. There is never a situation where this should be happening. 

PS - Kevin. Don't bother copy and pasting your cookie cutter response to all your one-star reviews. Instead hire staff members who do not PHYSICALLY ASSAULT PEOPLE. It's amazing that I even have to say that.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
We did the lunch cruise.  We ate as soon as we boarded...before even leaving the dock.  Buffet was  ok nothing great but good enough. Salad, grits, mashed potatoes,  chicken,  pork tenderloin,  corn bread and dessert. 
Show was very entertaining. Jusst lots of hits by lots of different people. 
Definitely would recommend as a tourist :-)

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Stopped in the afternoon for a drink, came back at night for more drinks.  Bartenders both times were very friendly and not hard to get their attention, in fact, they were usually asking me for a refill.  Acoustic performers were all very good, entertaining, and engaging with the audience on open mic night.  Did not have the food, but it did look pretty good.  Night bartender was very friendly.  Enjoyed our visits very much.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
YeeHaw, Kid Rock! Great addition to Nashville's vibrant Honkey Tonk scene. Such a fun atmosphere. Well laid out. Engaging staff. Rocking band. What more does a staycationing girl need?? Even on a Wednesday at 2pm, this place was happening. Here's why I like it compared to other Honkey Tonks:
1-Prosecco. Because, Prosecco. 
2-ample seating
3- elevated stage for easy band viewing 
4-the kitchen got my order right! Burger/Med Rare.. and it was actually medium rare! Oh, it was good, too!
5-attentive clean up crew. Every time we finished a glass or a plate, it was promptly cleared. 
6-I wasn't the oldest one here ;)
If you are visiting Nashville, I can recommend this one as a true taste of a Lower Broadway Honkey Tonk and I have been to them all. I may start here from now on when I bring friends to see what this unique Nashville scene is all about.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Mixed review Alert! While the music and entertainment was absolutely Awesome all night long . The food was just dreadful, Kid Rock if you read this ... if your gonna have the words Steakhouse in your name.. have decent steaks.. yes I did order steak at a bar.. bad mistake the $38 ribeye tasted like it came from Walmart and my dad cooked it. PBR is $7 so have a buzz before ya come . Again.. entertainment was top notch.. Food was garbage and grossly overpriced

name: The Basement East
text: We went to a show at The Basement East but as soon as got there we realized we were hungry so we popped over to The Beast Pub for a quick sandwich and noticed that it was also happy hour. We went up to the bar and the bartender was probably the nicest bartender I've ever seen in Nashville! He told us to find a seat and if he took too long getting out to us that we could come up to the bar to order. We were in a bit of a hurry so we decided just to order with him at the bar and the drinks and food came out super quick. Our drinks were I think $7 each and they were doubles since we were there during 2 for 1's. Both drinks (tito's and tonic and jack and coke) were both great! Then the sandwich came out, I don't remember what it was called but it had ham, jalapeño bacon, cheese on an amazing sandwich bun, seriously, one of the best sandwiches I've had in awhile. We were able to quickly pay and get over to catch the show. If all venues had bars/sandwich shops connected I would probably go to more shows. This made the show even more enjoyable, a full stomach and a lightly dizzy head! haha!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Very interesting museum dedicated to Johnny Cash. Admission is a bit pricy - $16 per adult. It pretty much covers Cash's entire career and family life. Very interesting for a Cash fan. I found the competing audio clips to be very annoying at times, but it was tolerable.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Very cool multi level bar. Bartenders all have uniforms & look put together. Fair drink prices, fair pours & entertainment on every level.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
For those who need a short review- do not bother with this restaurant.
For those others that want the drama that unfolded this evening- please keep reading. I purchased a Groupon for this restaurant today with the plan that we would visit this evening before the weekend started. I have been a server before and know that taking care of tables with coupons can be a hassle. However, having said that, I know how to take care of my server monetarily regardless of what the ticket looks like. After we sat down, it took quite a while for our waitress to come back and take our order.We ordered an appetizer in addition to the two entrees and beer flight that our Groupon included. While the bartender is pouring our beers, he is loudly bitching to our waitress and another client about "coupon people". The conversation continues for close to 5 minutes about us only 5 feet away! Then our entrees arrive before our appetizer because according to the waitress, she forgot. In order to be fair, our burgers were ok. However, our "specialty fries" were a let down. My "stadium" cheese fries had cheese from a jar poured on them and my husband's parmesan fries had the commercial, green container parmesan sprinkled on them. The appetizer, when it arrived, was another poor representation of this restaurant. Then, to top it off, the beer was... "off". I am a huge fan of our local brewery, Yazoo. However, when we tasted that in addition to some other unknown brews, I couldn't finish my Dos Perros. My guess is that they haven't cleaned their taps or their lines in a long time, therefore, giving the beer an undesirable flavor/finish. By the time our meal ended, I was furious and in the process of leaving a scathing note for the bartender, however, my husband dissuaded me saying "Don't even bother... this place won't be open in two months". Hopefully, I have given you a clear picture of your potential meal. 

-Natasha

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Location: I love street parking..when there's no meter. I hate dumping my change purse out, but I promised to meet a friend here at 3 and the meters still tik till 5. I love the area, but damn I wish parking was better.

Environment: I've seen Belcourt Taps advertised and based off their website, I'm imagining a young and fun original restaurant. When I got there, the place is very original, but I felt like I was in the backwoods of Wilson County. I live in Mount Juliet, so I like going "into town" (if you will) to get away. When I arrived, there was absolutely no one there, and the server was chilling with her grandchild, a couple of months old. Our drinks were served in a red solo cup (minus beer). Their performance stage is extremely small, which some could call intimate but I would call inconvenient if I were to be there at night. Maybe my timing had to do with it. Okay, so my timing had everything to do with it. Goes to show, no matter what city you're in, 3:00 on a Monday is going to be dead as a door knob (besides Fido's). The actual look of the restaurant is cute and country vintage looking.

Food: I got a house salad and the Hangover. I felt the house salad, which was $6, was a bit much for just lettuce, onions, and cheese. The Hangover was so excellent! I really did enjoy the bourbon onions on the salad and was happy they were on the burger. I've had a food truck's stuffed burger once and it was so sloppy that the cheese came out like juice. Belcourt Tap's was perfect, enough flavor and no messiness. Granted, it's a HUGE burger, it is kind of messy, just not the same. The pretzel bun is amazing and made it easy for me to eat in 4's (hope that makes sense). Fries were awesome too! I felt like the $12 for the Hangover was worth it.

Service: Despite having to take care of her grandson while working, our server was awesome. She was always on point with things and never missed anything. 

Overall the food was great, and if I came back, it would definitely be for the food, but probably not for anything else. Well, besides the service :)

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Easy to purchase tickets online, even the day before...midweek.  A mammoth room but you don't feel like you're one of 2000 people.  Big screens all over the room.  Great speaker system.  Padded bench seating with backs (like church pews).  They are really organized.  Easy in and out for the show.  Worst part....mall parking was miserable.  It was packed driving in and driving out.

name: Third Man Records
text:
A very cool, quirky, off-beat and trendy vinyl shop. I loved the White Stripes and I love everything Jack White does, which was the main reason I visited the store front. What he is doing for music and vinyl promotion is amazing. Check out his CBS Morning and Dan Rather interviews. I expected it to be an overpriced record store and was delightfully surprised that everything from the trinkets, t-shirts to the vinyl was reasonably marked. This is a great place for Third Man Records artist items and just a great place to put on your tour of Nashville list. The performing monkey machine is pretty cool along with the old recording booth. They also have live events at TMR.

Also, if you ever get to see Jack White in concert--he is worth every cent! I saw him perform in Nashville with special guest Loretta Lynn and it was the best concert that I have ever been to by far.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great beer list, solid food. I was a big fan of the make your own flight to really have a chance to experience the different beers they had on the menu. Being that I'm not from town, I rolled through the selections of local rotating taps. Our waitress was really great at providing some direction and I actually think I ended up liking what she suggested better than what I picked myself. For food, I shared a pizza and a goat cheese salad. The solid was a fair sized portion but exactly what one would expected if you poured together some lettuce, goat cheese, onions, and walnuts from their plastic bags at the grocery store.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: I'm writing this because of the reply Ms. Kelli's put on my first review and I am not able to reply to her. She replied two months after I posted my review and said we had to wait for her to unlock the doors in the freezing cold due to a car accident "last night" and that was a lie. It was two months ago. Everyone was inside standing around and she was refusing to unlock the door and refusing to wait on us when we got inside. She also said I post a lot of negative reviews which is also a lie. I post mostly five star reviews and actually don't like leaving a negative review except for when I think people should know about it. So just know that this place is rude, obnoxious and ungrateful. To call me a nitpicker is completely unprofessional and no legitimately run business that appreciates their customers would do this. If you say you open at 8pm and you are inside with all your staff then open at 8pm instead of watching your customers stand outside in the freezing cold. If you are a karaoke place and you have ten people wanting to sing then don't make them sit there and listen to your DJ hog the show for an hour before they can sing. If you are wasted you will probably have fun here or anywhere else. But if you are alert and aware you will see how rude they are. It's typical situation where they have so many tourists coming that they can get away with being arrogant because there will always be a new batch of people coming. Just read the other one star reviews.

name: Music City Tippler
text: Had a great Sunday brunch, fabulous cocktails..the gin mule is highly recommended.great good and atmosphere

name: Anthem
text:
Anthem is the go-to venue for any nightlife enthusiast,multi level club with top notch DJ's and mixologist. VIP is the perfect place for a more relaxed, private ambiance, offering a bird's eye view of the Main Floor. They play EDM, Hip-Hop, R&B, and Pop music. 
It's the best place to come for all of you new to Nashville, and not into the country scene.
I always have a great time!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Overrated is about all I can say.  Vince Gill played 2 songs, Little Big Town played 2 songs.  You sit through 2 1/2 hours of old timers and hosts trying to be funny, not to mention all the advertisements.  Once we left at the end of the show we spent more time leaving the parking lot than the top 2 headliner acts combined.  Really, 2 songs from the headliners?  Drinks are $9 dollars each.....really?

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great little spot, was doing a road trip from Rochester down to Key West and this was the dinner spot when we reached Nashville. Good service, good food (not amazing blow your mind delight, but currently living in NYC I can vouch for the fish and the burgers being above my expectations). Reasonably priced drinks (was rather funny hearing a few folks complain about a 5 dollar margarita...). I will definitely be coming back!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Arrived around 9:00 had to move to a different table. The one we were seated at was filthy. Local brew (Yazoo Dos Peros )was flat. Our server was not attentive. Probably wanted to get out of there faster than us. Talked to the manager he was more concerned with flat beer than cleanliness. All in all it was a bust. Stay in printers alley if ya want to hear the blues

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
GO!!!! That's all I can say!!!

To see a show and do the backstage tour was around $150 for 2 people. I think this was the best $150 we spent on our trip. The show was a lot of fun. The tour was great. I feel like I have an even bigger appreciation for the Opry and country music after visiting.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Definitely checked this off my bucket list with my wife! If your anywhere in the area you should go. There was people from Canada, England, and all over the states. It's a very clean, nice, respectful, historic establishment that will leave you looking at Country music even better than before!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
A typical chain store selections, atmosphere and crowd....but it's Nashville TN, there is live music,  fun service, the food products are good ,just not special. 
No real draw other than name and entertainment seems more our style. 
Had chicken wings, catfish nuggets, collar greens, tomato soup, and fried pickles. ..
I'd order them again...

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: We were visiting Nashville for New Years so needless to say, downtown was packed. My boyfriend loves craft beer so we found this place walking distance from downtown, but far enough away to not have the crowds that the downtown bars do. It has a great atmosphere to drink and have conversations. I'm not a big beer drinker but even I was able to find something I enjoyed on their extensive menu. We will definitely be going back next time we are in town!

name: Third Man Records
text: So frigging cool! How neat is it that you get to play with EVERYTHING in this place?! Including a GRAMMY! Thank you, Jack!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Tremendous Venue.  Great party.  Very good music.  Even the food and beverages was pretty good here.  The atmosphere is outstanding,  Great energy with good people.  The venue itself is tucked away from the bright lights on Broadway but down the side street of 2nd Ave.    Great entertainment place to have some laid back fun.  Nice stage, multiple bars.  Definitely will check out again when visiting.

Grade: B

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Worst place for a bachelorette party - don't come here! They do not care about their guests. The food takes forever! The management, Lacie, gives zero shits.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
Ate dinner and Attended the New Years party


Firstly, my party was caught off guard with a prefixed menu that contained no prices. Nowhere on the website was a prefixed menu mentioned. With only three options to choose from it was still difficult choosing what to eat because the waiter knew nothing about the menu. It seemed like the only words he knew were "I don't know". So, through my own personal experimentation, I found that the only appetizer worth getting is the pork belly. Entrees were poor; steaks weren't cooked to order and the bouillabaisse contained clams that weren't even open. With a meal that wasn't fit to serve a guinea pig, the bill still came out to be $110 per person.  

Now, the New Years event was even worse. They promised a live DJ and a burlesque show starting at 9pm. They stuffed people in the Tippler like cattle with little room to move around and the music didn't even start until 10pm, but only the people that paid an additional $140 could hear him. The speakers didn't turn on in the main floor until 10:30pm. Even then, the speakers flickered off and on intermittently. The Tippler's event planning and execution was absolutely horrible, nothing about this "party" was done properly. We could only view most of the burlesque show through a tv because the stage was in the vip section (also not mentioned). After midnight, everyone left just as confused and angry as myself looking for another bar that could possibly salvage this ruined New Year's Day.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Our waiter was nice and the band was amazing but it took way too long for us to get our food. After asking multiple times about where our food was, our waiter finally explained that the kitchen lost our ticket. Overall, it took over an hour and a half to get our food. While the music and atmosphere was awesome, the food and service was disappointing.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The music was great and the music was great!! Trey was a great server as well!! Anytime in Nashville come check this spot out!!!!!

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: I'm super loyal to Lipstick Lounge for Nashville karaoke, but thus isn't a bad option if you're downtown and get the itch to belt one out. We stopped in after the art crawl on a cold night out and both the crowd and the bar were warm and inviting. Good mix if talent levels and genres and the man running the show was super nice. Solid bar service and a good selection of beers on tap.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Place has a nice homey feel but that is as good as it gets.  Bar tender was extremely inattentive despite the lack of customers.  Took 15 minutes and asking twice to get water.  Took forever to get my food ordered and then the food was mediocre and not even what I ordered. And there were billing issues.... Never going back

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
We were here a couple of months ago, and I just realized in all my Nashvillian reviews I neglected to do one on the Opry. We saw Vince Gill and Pam Tillis as the headliners that night as well as going on the backstage tour. The show was great, I really had no idea what to expect, as my grandma is really into country music, and I'm not-so-much. My grandma adored all the older acts, and my sister and I got a kick out of the younger ones. Vince Gill was amazing, even for someone who knows very little of his work outside of his 1990s Christmas album. Pam was funny, and a great show host as well. She did a nice job of keeping her segment moving, and even gave a shout out to MinneSOta because her piano player was from here! My only complaint is with the pews. I totally get the church vibe is intended (I had toured the Ryman earlier that day) but they really pack you in close. There's very limited leg room, and not a whole lot of seat room, either. It makes it pretty uncomfortable for anyone taller than 5'2" and weighing more than a buck20.

The backstage tour was super informative, but I don't know that I'd want to do it after the evening's show again because we didn't end up getting outta there until nearly 11 pm and granny was pretty tired by then.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
This is one of the worst, possibly the worst, restaurant I've ever been to. Literally inedible. The pulled pork was the driest meat I've ever tasted in my life. It was like eating tree bark. Tasteless, inedible. Texas toast wasn't toasted. Hush puppies were so dry they turned to dust when I bit into one. Literal dust. The "tarter sauce" tasted like mayonnaise. I think I saw a minuscule piece of pickle in there, but by and large it was just mayo. Burgers were all cooked to the consistency of shoe leather -- shriveled dry hockey pucks of meat (we asked for medium). Cole slaw consisted of large dry squares of cabbage with chipotle flavoring sprinkled on. Ever gnaw on a chunk of dry cabbage? Super gross. To add insult to injury, they gave the meal of one member of our party to another table. We were done eating by the time she received her meal. 

One star for the fresh fruit cup. If you like grapes, this is the restaurant for you.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: I love the flying saucer- and I come here everytime I go to Nashville! They have the best pretzels I've ever had. We love it so much that we had our after party here after our wedding. the GM, Kacey, even kept the whole place open (even the kitchen!) an extra hour so we could party with our friends eating pretzels and drinking beer after our wedding. The staff was attentive, and the quality of the beer/food is always there. We'll be back!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I'll go back for the service, atmosphere and live music but will eat before I go. If you just need a late night snack, the food wasn't awful but just not the meal worthy quality we like.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: I have to say, the girls today at DawgHouse, AMAZING!  thank you Abby and Jules for being the best bartenders in the city.

name: Third Man Records
text: While cool and theory, and with an amazing building and good graphic design, Third Man is nothing but a self-made, over-priced museum to Jack White next to the ghetto. $20 for a 45? No. $200 for photographs? No. If you don't worship the ground Jack White walks on, just no.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
This is probably one of the coolest non-touristy bars in Nashville. Even though I have a strong love for country music, they don't shove it down your throat here like they do on Broadway. The building it's located in is extravagant - it reminds me of an abandoned Victorian age train station (which there's also an abandoned train right outside.) it's pretty big and spacious inside, with many tables and a lounge area with lots of comfy looking couches. Plastered on every inch of the wall are thousands of saucers, which is really interesting to look at. Especially because many of them are of different places and attractions. 

   The coolest thing about this place is their drink selection. 200 beers to choose from. If you try all 200, you get a saucer with your name on it put on the wall. If you complete this challenge more than once, you'll get a different colored saucer. How. Awesome. Is. That.

  This place is so cool y'all. A great place for a more local vibe.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: I love this place regardless of the fact that I do not get a long with some of the former staff.  I still recommend this bar as the top karaoke joint in all of Nashville!  Great staff, great prices, and great karaoke!

name: Anthem
text:
To me, this is a step in the right direction, inviting Nashville to diversify it's venues. As far as similar decent club experiences go, there is only South and Seen, so this is a step up in the classy/trendy club direction. I hope others follow suit and up the ante so they all improve.

Anyway, I've been here 3 times, twice for shows and once at the end of a night. It's usually the same clubby environment, with loud music, primarily house. I really like the music, so it works for me. I've also actually tried their food, since I didn't have dinner before going out one of the nights, and it's not bad actually. Sure, it's a bit pricey, but nothing too bad considering you're in a CLUB. 

The music is pretty great as well, assuming you like the genre. Definitely something energetic to dance to, and with good transition to keep people going. It's also really interesting how they divide up the space, with a top and bottom floor, and a small bar area with different music that's almost sound isolated so that you can talk even if there is a crazy show going on 10 feet away. I like.

Overall, this place is pretty great as far as Nashville goes - sure, it doesn't come close to clubs in the other major cities (Miami, NYC, LA), but it is a step in the right direction. Kudos.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Good food. Fun atmosphere! Loved their house band! Suggest seeing them if you want some classic blues!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: A great small venue with great food...burgers, BBQ and pizzas.  Awesome venue for listening to some of Nashville best singers/songwriters.  A must stop when visiting Nashville.  Entertainment nightly.  Not many tourist but you are sure to meet some fun locals.  Nice patio out front as well!

name: Belcourt Taps
text: Polite service, nice selection of beers on tap, awesome sweet potato fries, fun cozy college bar atmosphere. We were very satisfied.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Wonderful! Went before a comedy show. I would definitely recommend this place to anyone who wants to listen to live music and enjoy the pretty good food.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Hidden little gem, hard to locate but great little joint. Local craft beer on tap. I had the black bean corn burger and house made chips, it really hit the spot. Hubby had a turkey burger and fries. Better than chain restaurants! Great service.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I had a chance to go to BB King's with my wife and we enjoyed ourselves! I was not too hungry so I got a cup of Beer Chili and Crawfish poppers (appetizer) she had the pulled pork sandwich with sweet potato fries. We both came to the conclusion that our food was OK. Not great definitely not bad just pretty good/ok. There was a local trio performing they were really good and apparently they perform there often. They were really good. Our waiter was in and out sometimes there sometimes no where to be found. I would go back here I love music and I realize this place is what it is. I think they try to have great food but it doesn't the food is just good/ok (THE FOOD WAS NOT BAD just nothing great) but what they lack in food they make up for it in music. I would definitely go back but temper you expectations with the food. Music A+. We enjoyed ourselves.

name: Music City Tippler
text:
This bar was needed and it's obvious that other agree with me because the times that I've been there, it's been packed. The age group seems to be young professionals, mid-late 20's to 30's. 

I love nice cocktails but the whole "excuse me while I go grow a lemon tree" thing grates me. Tippler manages to turn out quality drinks, fast. We visited when it was slammed and I pulled out the "make me something with Fernet" card and they delivered, fast. To me that is the definition of a good cocktail bar: quality concoctions that don't take all night to mix.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: This place is a lot of fun but you do have to get over the karaoke guy being a total jerk. He didn't totally ruin it but is definitely a mean guy. Just don't ask him about how many people in front of you, and if you don't want people to go ahead of you in line, give him a bigger tip. He yelled at me for asking when I was up, (people that signed up after me went in front of me, but I still asked very nicely) and then said that others gave him a $20 tip so they got ahead. It was pretty crazy actually, I did not expect him to be so mean I was simply asking. It might be a soup nazi kind of thing, have to ask in a certain way or he will yell at you I don't know. The bartender girl is awesome (and a talented singer too!) but that guy was just so mean.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: The bar tender shook a drink all over me. I'm pretty sure she was dunker than I was. The place was nasty and the service was horrible. Skip this crappy hole in the wall and head to Lipstick Lounge.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: A must see for anyone living in or visiting Nashville!  I am not even a fan of country music, but the building and the tour was fun and very interesting.  It is only around a hour and costs $20, but you learn and see a lot in that time and it was fun!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
My husband and I ended up coming back here a few times during our trip to Nashville for this year's CMA Fest. 

We first came up from the riverfront to cool off and have a bite to eat between sets, but when we arrived and saw the extensiveness of the beer menu, we caved.

Being from out of town, we tried a couple different local beer, of which they had plenty on tap. After our first two pints, we decided to opt for the "Flights" instead - a sampler of five 5 oz. beer that you could either order from their menu, or build yourself.

During our first visit, we got the rocket tots and hummus and pita as an appetizer. The rocket tots were piping hot - deep fried and filled with jalapeños and cheese, and the pita for the hummus appetizer was super warm, soft and fresh. I ordered the grilled chicken breast and greens. The portion was hearty, but I found the chicken and bacon a little overdone and dry. Otherwise, the ingredients were  good and the dressing came on the side, which was nice since I always find my salads end up swimming in dressing. 

During our second visit, we came strictly for the beer, and during our third visit we opted to try their much acclaimed soft pretzels, which were incredible, not too salty and still super fresh even at 11:30 p.m. (considering the NYC pretzels I'm accustomed to [read: hard as concrete and more salt than pretzel - this was astonishing to me). By our third visit, we had tried a good selection of their on-tap beers, having ordered the Hops 101 Flight, Local Flight and U.S.A. Flight. We even ended up choosing favorites from our selections.

The restaurant itself has a great vibe. It's comfortable and inviting, with huge picnic tables and couches in the sunroom area where we spent our time. There are also plenty of tables inside the main bar area. I can't forget to mention the pristine bathroom conditions and amazing service we received, especially considering the insanity of CMA Fest week, since thousands of people flood downtown Nashville, requiring many restaurants to have their waitstaff work 12-15 hour days for four days straight.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
This place is cool. Laid back for as crowded as Broadway gets.  My daughter couldn't recall if she ordered onion rings and our server was like no worries, we'll get you some on the house. 
Really friendly. 
Thanks Ellen, Matt, and Cate. 
The food and drinks were great.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Amazing atmosphere! We were looking for something just a little different. Great Blues bands playing. Wonderful service, our bartender was Jasmine and she was wonderful and so personable! We will definitely be back.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Wow I have to tell you this towns food is out of this world. And the service continues to blow me away. Here is the thing that is nuts tonight was the lowest tab and the best night of all. If you come to Nashville and don't make it to B. B. Kings you will have missed out.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Finally got around to come here last month, after having heard that it was great from several friends. Actually came here as a part of a HUGE group, (40ish) with a lot of coworkers. It was a great environment to talk and eat, but at the same time listen to the music played live, which I'm happy to say was not country.... definitely a nice change of pace from the usual downtown places in Nashville. 

Anywho, I ordered a dish, I forget what it was called, but it was essentially a large serving of macaroni and cheese with a tasty fried piece of chicken. Now that sounds pretty simple, but some friends suggested it, and MAN am I glad they did. The macaroni and cheese has this delicious non-standard flavor, maybe since it was white (not yellow) and appeared to be made with different cheeses.... Eithery way, it was tasty, as was the chicken, which despite being fried and crunchy on the outside, it was juicy and tender on the inside. 

Overall, this place is awesome for large parties, can be a nice relaxing environment or social, and its refreshing to have a popular place in downtown Nashville that plays blues instead of country music. Would come back.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: We had a group of 12 and were there on a Tuesday night. Service was slow, our server Mary was inattentive and frustrated about our requests for drinks other than beer. She actually bordered on rude. The food was average at best. I had grilled cheese and tomato bisque and honestly Campbell's soup is better. Lower your expectations before going.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Pleasant atmosphere, okay food. It's just glorified bar food (nothing wrong with that), but it was not priced like bar food. The waiter was trying his hardest to upsell some stuff we didn't want. I understand, it was lunch and quite slow, but you will not create repeat customers by being pushy. Long time customers are what sustain businesses, of which we will not be. First and last time visiting this establishment. Sorry restaurant, just being honest.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Ah, the Saucer.

There's no better place for a bite and a beer. 

With over 200 something beers, you'll never be at a loss to try something new! 

Trying them all gets you about $3,000 in the hole, but a fabulous plate (saucer) on the ceiling to brag about for years to come! 

Get the warm pretzel appetizer, play some darts and have a blast!

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Great burger with blue cheese completely melted. All the fries were crunchy and amazing. Eli was a good waiter and he said the fries were fried twice. Staff seem to have a really good working relationship. Prices are reasonable. Since I was from out of town, I had to wander around until I found the Back Alley Diner, but it was worth it. I will eat there again tomorrow before I head home.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: Awesome choice! Great food at a great price. Really friendly and Fun staff. Richard was great and helpful. 5 stars!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Food was better than what we expected! Pulled pork was fresh and flavorful. It melted in your mouth and fell apart easily. Ribs literally fell off the bone and had just the right amount of sauce. Their chopped salad with chicken was great for a lunch meal. The chicken was freshly made and not frozen. Drinks were ok and service was a bit slow that's the only reason I'm giving a 4 out of 5.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text:
the bar was almost empty when I got there and yet it took almost 15 minutes to get served. The waitress didn't know the drink menu and the food was horrible. 

I never plan to go back

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text:
I expected better because there were decent word of mouth reviews...
We tipped them to jump on the list and one hour later, not even called to sing. Nashville tourists, there are plenty other karaoke bars that honor a good tip. Skip this one.

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
We moved to Nashville about 4 months ago and have checked out many bars and restaurants in the area since moving here. We checked out this place on a whim. It was quite the discovery! There was live music when we walked in (that was very good) and the place was filled. We sat at the bar and were served promptly. After we'd been there a little bit, the owner of the bar came over and talked to us for awhile. She was so kind and welcoming! 

The place has character and a warm feel - we'll be back for sure! Favorite bar find so far.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: I was in Nashville for work.  This diner was recommended by the hotel. It was with in walking distance from the hotel which was great.  The restaurant had a fun atmosphere and friendly staff. I was dining for lunch and ordered the BBQ sandwich.  Sandwich was ok. Not something I would recommend. Looks like this place would be much better for dinner. Next time I am in town I will try it out for dinner.

name: Anthem
text:
Anthem is extremely cramped and makes a major deal out of selling "VIP" tickets. I did not buy VIP tickets but was able to walk up to VIP instantly not knowing where I was going. 

The club promoters and their pals were allowed to dance on the stage while the bouncer pulled others off. In all my years and cities and clubs, I have never experienced something like that. Generally in "edm" it's the fans that are supposed to matter. Not the drug dealing fiending promoters who will phase out in the next 3 months.

My suggestion..considering how expensive the drinks are and how cramped the space is..if you want to keep show kids coming back then change the attitude of this place. 

Don't make the music about the money.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: Stay away from the mac and cheese!!! Ive been having great foods in the vicinity here in Nashville and figured this place has a great bartender/Staff for drinks so lets try the food...  I saw the menu and it had the choice of macaroni... brisket beef , pork or chicken... chose the pork... pork was ok... mac was wth!? Kraft type mac n cheese...? Really?!‍ literally that mac was straight out the box!? I would have expected the creamy goodness that the South provides freely through its comfort foods... but this was no comfort! This was Monsanto! Please stay away from the mac...unless yer looking for that good box flavor... cause thats not the price I would be charging for kraft type mac... yeek! Just saying cause if ya dont know, ya need to know..

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: They play good music but keep your check if you pay with a debit/credit card. I left a cash time but paid my tab with my debit card. Bartender decided to put an extra tip for himself so instead of paying $34 for 4 lemon drop shots, I paid $41 plus the cash tip I left him. Not happy about that one bit. But I'll just have to pay cash from here on out when I go to this bar.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Went today for lunch and didn't have such a great experience.  Overcooked chicken fingers, two were not even edible just chunks of fried yuk, and my co-worker got the chili and said that was poor too.  Great place to drink beer and play trivia, but probably won't be back for food anytime soon.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: In Nashville for NYE.  I'm a wing snob.  Decided to try this place based on the menu.   Buffalo wings were excellent!   I always order extra crispy and extra wet.  Cooked perfectly.   Moderate heat but good flavor.  Nice atmosphere.   Tons of beers!!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: My family members are not country music fans, but this was great! Each artist did three songs.  Some bluegrass, some traditional country, some gospel, some new country.  Wednesday night summer show was a good value with really good seats available directly from the Opry.  It is a stage show and a radio show.  A nice way to sample great performers.  We all agree we would do it again and it was a major highlight of our trip.  As someone once told me, always see the best at something do what they do best, even if you are not sure you'll like it; you won't be disappointed and might find you like it after all.

name: BB King's Blues Club
