text: The atmosphere, music, location, and food was all perfect! Really, really great!! The only reason I'm giving four stars instead of five is because of our waiter. First he came up to my boyfriend and I and said "Hi ladies!" As soon as he looked up he realized she was a he LOL but he never apologized which I thought was rude. He also seemed to have forgot about us towards the end. But the tables are really uniquely painted and the decorations are neat! Hefty bill but what do you expect? My boyfriend also got a complimentary souvenir beer glass since he ordered a tall beer! I'd definitely return.

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text:
Sat at the bar for 15 minutes. Made eye contact with bartender and waved down many times after being ignored to try to get my first drink of the night. The bartender deliberately served all the women around me while knowing I was waiting for a drink for 15 minutes.  So I Left. Yeah you, black plugs, black hat backwards with tats up your arms. Your the worst. Your also the slowest bartender I've seen on broadway.

Also, half full bar and karaoke host over inflated time to sing to receive tips for getting a faster sing time. This place is a joke.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Amazing experience that everyone should have at least once! Venue is very easy to get to as far as parking and entering/exiting the building. Our seats were in Section 15, Row Z, which is the last row on the floor level, and we still had a great view. Definitely recommend for anyone visiting Nashville.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: This place was so awesome.  We had a large party and we were taken care of.  The staff was friendly and respectful.  There was live music.  And the food was amazing.  5 out of 5 for sure.  Did not disappoint.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: My go-to place for a solid lunchtime Burger downtown. Just be sure to show up early during lunch to ensure you can get a table.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Entertainment was good. It had a rustic feel. The wings were okay. The drinks were good but the new bartender gave my husband a top shelf margarita with a gin base instead of tequila and it was terrible. But other than that the server was nice and the music was on point. I love live bands with people who can sing instead of screaming.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Great place to hang and drink beer! 
The Flying Saucer is historic and filled with a great casual and fun environment. All my friends and I go in on Monday.
Why Monday? Monday is Pint Nite!
On Pint Nite, almost all beers are only 3 bucks. I have been doing this for the past 2 years and probably have tried over 100+ beers through this place!
They also have a "UFO club" that helps you track what beers you have drank and lets you work towards a goal of 200 beers. Once you get there, you get a reward, but not quite sure what the reward is. 
The food here, however, is pretty meh. On Wednesdays, they do half off food, but its really not special. 

Overall, great place to hang and drink beer, alright place to eat food. Enjoy!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The music was great, but the service was slow and the food was meh. I ordered the chicken fried chicken and the chicken was delicious, but the vegetables (squash, zucchini and carrots) very mushy. It also came with "baked" Mac and cheese. I have never been so disappointed. It definitely was not baked and it tasted like melted American cheese.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: The Jalapeno Poppers at B.A.D. were delicious and the martinis were also great! I loved the hummus plate and pita chips as well! B.A.D. was my favorite place to visit, with the live music, and relaxed decor B.A.D was a great place to hang out any day of the week! Service was great as well and as the night went on it felt like everyone who was dining or drinking was hanging out together and interacting with the live musician. I would recommend B.A.D. to anyone visiting the Nashville area.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Perfect spot to go before the Frist Museum. All taps are $4 from 4-7, M-F. 

Sweet Tea is a doll and very knowledgeable about the exhibits at the museum.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We absolutely loved attending the Grand Ole Opry House.  We added a tour of the backstage area.  I would encourage you to add this tour to your package.  The seats at the show are just a wood bench (like in an old church). There are numbers on the top part of the wood to identify where you are to sit.  The benches did have a cushion.  If you are looking to see a big act, check out Tuesday night. The big acts make their money on weekends.  If you have never heard the type of music they have, download the app for Grand Ole Opry and enjoy!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Literally patronize this place all the time. And THIS is what they give me. This basket is supposed to be full of fries and they gave me whatever scraps they had left. Wont be recommending to any of my friends because as loyal as I was to B.B. kings, they were disloyal in customer satisfaction. If you do right by the customer, the customer will do right by you. Literally, what's difficult to understand about this?

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: The food is always awesome! Keith is always super friendly, and definitely my go to lunch spot!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: If you're looking for overpriced food with no taste then you've found the right spot.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text:
Staff at the door was super friendly but we weren't 100% impressed.

The place reeked of smoke, so if this bothers you, it's not the place for you. 

It's a karaoke bar... We got up to sing karaoke, but when we can back, all our drinks had been cleared at the table we were at and were forced to buy new ones. What a rip off! Seemed like a scam to get you to spend more money. 

It was fun as a one-time spot but I don't think I'd frequent here regularly.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
What can I say? It's the Grand Ole Opry, it's historic and I'm so honored to have been able to experience a performance at the venue. From the minute you walk in you can tell how incredibly important this venue is, not only to Nashville, but to country music as a whole. Before the concert they played a moving video on the history of the Grand Ole Opry and the significance of performing there and it was great to see.

In addition to that, there are NO bad seats in this venue at all. Seriously! Any where you sit in the venue you will have a fantastic view of the stage. Once you're seating down prepare yourself for a mind-blowing performance because it seems like everyone who performs here is completely proud to play here and will give you one HELL of a performance. So happy to have been a witness to this and be able to mark this off my bucket list.

name: Belcourt Taps
text: After reading all the reviews from the groupon purchases I ignored my instincts and tried it anyways. Lesson learned now. The place is quaint and the service was good but beyond that it sucked. Maybe two out of the ten beers was decent the others were awful tasting and were not even worth drinking. We also got pretzels with the groupon. My husband had the plain pretzel which was decent but a little dry. I had the garlic parmesan which was awful,they used garlic powder for flavoring and gave you a dipping side which tasted like a garlic vinaigrette dressing and it was also dry and over cooked. Next time I will listen to my instinct and not make bad groupon purchases. :(

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: DESTROYED MY PROPERTY!!! The worst experience I've ever had at a bar in Nashville. "Manager" was unapologetically rude and service was terrible. I wish I could give this place a negative star. Avoid at all costs. They damaged my personal property by tampering with my driver license to the point where I will now have to get it replaced. This place will pull the laminate off your license! BEWARE!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: The grand ole opry house is a must see when you come to Tennessee. Our roots can be found here whether it's through dancing or the sounds of country music. Be sure to wear cowboy boots when you're attending a show

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text:
Great place to stop by, specially if you are with your kids, we definitely had so much fun at this place!
We'll definitely coming back lol

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text:
You have to take this place for what it is... it's basically a redneck bar and proud of it.

I popped by for some drinks and to listen to some music. Both were great and the service was swift.

Warning: If you're looking to have an intimate conversation, this is not the place... downstairs is as loud as hell, but hey... that's what your here for.

The establishment is located at the center of where you want to be on Broadway.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: The Carl Stewart band was great. He is such a pro ! But the young Chef was the real surprise!  We got the catfish and shrimp platter. The fish was lightly battered and lightly fried to perfection. None of this overly battered stuff. Very tasty and not heavy. The young guy is also a real pro.Raquel was a friendly server too!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: First time visiting, this was such an incredible experience. The history behind the building is so perfectly preserved, and there is a ton of memorabilia scattered throughout the house. I was expecting something totally different, but from looking around, I don't think there is a seat in the house that would be a "bad seat". The sound is incredible and the building has a natural acoustic feature so it really allows the audience to hear the sound perfectly without flaw. The bands were incredible, and everyone was so friendly! There is a gift shop with tons of different souvenirs you can buy for yourself and others. So blessed to have been able to experience this and make something off my bucket list as well as see Mason Ramsey live! Thank you for being so inviting!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I entered a world I did not know existed anymore. 
First of all, apparently they do a simulcast on am radio. If you are under the age of 60, as I am, you may not know that am radio exists. Apparently, it still does. 
Each 30-minute segment is bookended with two solid full minute commercials for crappy restaurants and health insurance companies spoken by a deep-voiced announcer, who is not doing this ironically. They are hosted by an octogenarian who makes the kind of jokes one remembers from watching Lawrence Welk with your long-dead grandmother. 
My experience started with a number by said octogenarian mc, followed by a trio of women in their late 60s accompanied by their father who made jokes about how he was saddled by having all girls. Apparently something he hasn't gotten over in 60 plus years. Why? Because girls statistically succeed more than boys in 2018? I suppose they wouldn't know that given their advanced age. 
Their number was followed by another octogenarian guy who wrote some song I think I've heard before about being a piece of coal but could be a diamond, his drunken rambling, his next incoherently slurred song and his drunken exit. 
The mc then did a spoken word number, with backup singers who struggled to hold a tune on a countryfied hymnal, which honestly could be a regular SNL skit. 
Closing out this set was the Opry square dancers, a medium meant for radio - like Irish step dancing without the choreography. 
The final set was mc'd by an octogenarian woman who made weirdly sexual jokes, which was not at all like my long dead grandmother watching Lawrence Welk. 
She introduced a heavily made-up, bleached blonde who told a story about now she'd come to Nashville and tended bar, then sang a song that she wrote (but did not play any instrument on) about being a pretend friend as a bartender. 
The female octagenarian mc sang two songs that were not sung particularly well. Then she introduced a hunk who she made more sexual jokes about and said we'd know better as so and so. I assumed from the show Nashville, which I have never seen. Some people screamed but 2/3 of the audience was bewildered. He wasn't very good.
All and all it was a worthless overpriced terrible show. On a Saturday night they didn't have anyone worth seeing in the whole show and format made it unwatchable. I would never do this again.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Literally the most racists  establishment I've ever been to. Dave Griffith is the main culprit and is a terrible human being. Because you manage a bar doesn't mean you get to discriminate against people you don't care for in a bar. Thanks for judging your actions on someone's skin color! Classy!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: What a nice place ! We scheduled an impromptu last minute night out to the GOO and were not disappointed. This place is pure class. A full evening of entertainment. Lots of history. And very well decorated. Spend the money, see the show, love the history. It's worth it.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Ryman Theatre
3:30 show
Great time!
Freezing cold outside (wait)
Dustin Lynch & Schonda Pierce and others Great!
Cost worth it. But was our most expensive adventure in Nashville. (Besides parking $$$)

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Monday is pint night, Tuesday is trivia, Wednesday take home a glass from your favorite brewery, Thursday is American pint night, Sunday is local draft night. Always and occasion to drink at the Saucer. Make sure your beers count for something and join the UFO club! Nothing like having a plate (or 7) on the wall!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: AVOID AVOID AVOID. Do yourself a favor and walk passed this place. How dare the owner even have the guts to call someone a he/she. Isn't this 2015? And isn't this Nashville?

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Great food and great atmosphere. Live music too. We came here for lunch while in Nashville and this was one of my favorite places. 
Great old building that is perfect for a blues club. 
This will be one I return to any time I'm in Nashville.

name: Back Alley Diner
text: After being asked by Back Alley Diner to revise my review, I checked their site again and it does state their hours are until 10pm for food on Sat. I must have read the incorrect hours on a different link. I could not remove my previous review for some reason... Only update it. I never got a chance to eat here but I've heard it is good.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great food and even better music with Mike Hayes Band.  Ribs just fell off the bone and fried chicken fabulous!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: We caught a show here and we were lucky enough to do a backstage tour and we got to go on stage! This venue is an institution and has featured just about every name in country music. The people who run this place are very passionate about what they do. It's a must do in Nashville!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: In town for the week and heard that we needed to see a show over here. The experience was like no other. So many different acts in 2 hours. Never grew up a country fan, but this gave me such a new appreciation of the genre. By far the coolest thing I have done in Nashville and a must for anyone.

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Avoid this place. Would I've it zero stars if I could. MC was obviously more interested in playing songs for his friends than the actual paying customers. We saw numerous round of MC's friends come in after us and have their songs played while our songs were never played. Much better places to spend your money.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: The food was good, but the service was terrible. This is the kind of bar were the servers spend more time flirting with female patrons and ignoring the men. On a slow Sunday evening, we waited 10 minutes before we asked to see menus, then another 15 minutes before or orders were taken. There are a bunch of other restaurants in the area (had they been open, we would have left), spend your time elsewhere.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text:
Absolute GEM of a honky tonk!

This small place definitely has a more cozy, intimate feel than the other spots along Broadway, but that makes for a great interactive music experience. 

If have the pleasure of stopping by on a weekend to see Noah Garner, you're in for one hell of a show (dancing on the bar included!). Ladies--you'll fall in love. Gentlemen--watch your girls!

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
I found this lovely establishment by chance while looking for a place to eat dinner. Half price wings this Tuesday night so I definitely got myself some wings, but I also made sure to sample the BBQ pulled pork sandwich with baked beans. The wings were super crispy and were flavored with the traditional Nashville Hot Chicken seasoning. The exterior was dry, which was surprising, and the wings were super crispy. There was also a hint of sweet to them. The pork was delicious served with a side of BBQ sauce to go on my sandwich. The sandwich also had coleslaw and bacon on it. Everything is better with bacon. There was no imagination in the original bun. Wish I had something a little more like a hoagie roll for the bun but it still worked. 

The misstep of the evening was the mix up almost resulting in me not getting my wings. Thankfully that was quickly rectified. Would definitely come back and recommend to friends.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Ryman Theatre
3:30 show
Great time!
Freezing cold outside (wait)
Dustin Lynch & Schonda Pierce and others Great!
Cost worth it. But was our most expensive adventure in Nashville. (Besides parking)
A hint for parking - search public library parking building.  It is $14?for day.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: There really isn't a bad seat in here. I had a great time here on a Saturday night. While the seats are pew style there was enough room between people. I liked the balcony view and while it doesn't allow for amazing pictures, at the Opry, no matter where you are sitting you are allowed to walk down to the stage and take photographs. I also took the backstage tour after the show. You can take pictures and get to see all the dressing rooms, the green room, go on stage and get pictures at the microphones, etc. Definitely a cool experience and a fun evening. Parking at the Opry can be far, but it is free. Arrive early and go check out the inside of the Opryland hotel. There are lots of restaurant options inside.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Wasn't there long . Welcomed us in sat down at a table. Waited 10 minutes no one came to ask us for a drink or menu. Then went to the bar to order 2 drinks got carded . Didn't bring my ID in with me while we bar hop on Broadway. They wouldn't serve me because the State cracks down on them for under age drinking.  
I guess at 52 I must be looking really good.  lol 

The BB King in Memphis was so nicer than this place. 
So if you go to Broadway in Nashville , don't forget your ID

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
I was here recently with a group of work colleagues for dinner during some training in Nashville. I thought the food was pretty good for bar food (the primary offering is a selection of burgers, but they had great sides), and it's nice that they have the big patio for warm weather. Like most places in Nashville, they have live music, but I actually thought the venue was too small for the band they had. It's not a big location, and the music was pretty overwhelming. It's basically just one room (unless you go outside), so there was no place to escape the music and just talk with your party.

Overall, it was a success for our party (~20 people, and they let us stand around a group of tables for food and drinks), but I likely won't be going back on return trips to Nashville.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Do not believe a word you are told by the Opry Call Center that sells tickets for performances at both the Ryman and the Opry House.  I was prepared to go in person to buy tickets, but I was assured by the sales person at the Opry Call Center that the price was exactly the same if our tickets were purchased from her over the phone.  And what convenience!!  She also offered to send our tickets by email 48 hr. before the show.  Apparently they lie their heads off and will say anything to make a sale.  We have not received our tickets and are now told that they do not have the capacity to send tickets by email.  We have other commitments before our concert and may be standing in the Will Call line or security line when our concert starts because we were lied to by  the Opry Call Center.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Great music. Good food as you would expect...but buyer beware. Prices published on their menu is not what they charge.  Good wines advertised at $6 a glass are out of so they can get you to buy the actual house wine "Lucille" advertised at $6 but actually $8 a glass.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text:
Stopped here for dinner. It was a $5 cover per person to enter for dinner. The staff was incredibly slow. There was next to no one here and it was surprising how slow and inattentive the staff actually was. We ordered two beers and a mixed drink and waited for almost 25 minutes to get them. 

We ordered two appetizers and again very slow service and once the expediter brought them to our table we didn't see the waiter again until the table next to ours was seated. At that point we request the bill and left.

name: Back Alley Diner
text:
Back Alley Diner was the first place we ate after arriving in Nashville. Starving, we wandered across the street from our hotel and happily stumbled onto this place! It was late afternoon, so our large party easily found a place to sit. Our server was very nice, though a member of our group didn't like her because she refused to serve him alcohol. I don't blame her at all because 1. We quickly found out that Nashville has very strict carding rules and 2. it's his own damn fault for having an expired ID. 

At first glance, B.A.D. looks grimy like the name implies, but it's actually kind of cute after you settle in and look around. I had the catfish po'boy, which came with hushpuppies and my choice of baked beans. Hello, delicious Southern food! The jam for the hushpuppies was a great addition, but I should have gotten fries instead of the beans. Beans were fine, but a taste of someone else's fries filled me with Fry Jealousy. Portions were generous and everyone at my table was very pleased with the food. 

B.A.D. isn't good enough to trek all over town for, but if you're close definitely check it out. And bring a current ID.

name: Third Man Records
text:
A must-stop shop while visiting from out of town if you love (1) music, (2) vinyl, (2) Jack White/White Stripes/Raconteurs/Dead Weather, (3) enjoy the symbolism of the number 3 (placement intentional).

We swung by right after they opened on a Sunday (10 am). To be candid, the area was a little sketchy as we drove up; lots of vagrant folks were meandering about nearby. Other reviewers didn't seem so kind to the area either, but we felt safe throughout.

This place is definitely unique from any other record store I've been to so far. Going in, you understand the connection to Jack White & his music (big fan), but also the other artists on their recording label (same name - Third Man) that continue to grow in number and stature. All of the vinyl they sell is exclusively Third Man releases, heavy on JW/WS reissues. I was hoping to find any Vault or other TMR exclusives (like the recent Cubs/Pearl Jam 45), but no dice. 

I found the store to be more of a museum than a traditional brick/mortar record store - tons to look at, investigate, and marvel. I sincerely appreciate their effort(s) to make this a one-of-a-kind shopping experience. We checked out the listening room/booth, while also envious of the recording station too. Lots of TMR merch, collectibles, and apparel to choose from if so inclined. We made a few smaller music selections and bought a store sticker (drats!). 

If you are a music enthusiast and vinyl lover/collector, I'd recommend stopping by, regardless of your musical tastes or the type of collector or stage in your collection you find yourself. It's not too far from Grimey's, either, so that is a plus. 

It's a very original place and I look forward to TMR releases in the future!

name: Ms. Kelli's Karaoke Bar
text: Was enjoying the place and then when we got up to watch my niece sing, they cleared our table, along with the kooxie that was on my beer. When we told them what happened, they denied that it happened. I found the koozie in the garbage and left, never to return.

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: This place has  great food, awesome sports bar and the hottest spot for Sunday Funday where you can find the fun 80s band Spazmatics.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
As a fair-weathered country fan, I even found this tour interesting. I imagine that any huge country fans would be loosing their ish if they went on this!

You get to walk where all the country stars have gone- into the deluxe dressing rooms, up the celebrity back entrance, on the stage and on the little wood circle in the center of it where they all sing. 

The coolest part was the mini mail room. Apparently, fans can send the Grand Ol Opry mail for any of their favorite stars. The Grand Ol Opry saves it and hands it to the stars when they enter. Such a cool tradition! 

The dressing rooms are gorgeous and super fancy. It's cool to see which celebrities choose which dressing room. You also get to take a picture on the stage and there's a great gift shop.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: I love this place. Love hearing about the history and the backstage tour is full of interesting information. The videos of Blake Shelton are a plus, too :) Standing in that circle on stage sure is special. We only did the tour this time around because all of the recent shows were at the Ryman, but I can't wait to come back and catch another show here in the future!

name: DawgHouse Saloon
text: Amazing staff and service! Came in today before the crowd hit looking for a chill Sunday after a late Saturday out. Was served by the only guy bartender I saw in the building and I can honestly say I've never met a more friendly face behind the bar! Drinks were great, service phenomenal and the atmosphere was wonderful. Can't wait to come back!!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text:
As the below review reads "take this for what it is" that couldn't be any more true. 

Redneck Rivera is exactly what you would think it would be. It's a promising bar, not much thrill to it but not terrible either. The live music was pretty good though! I also got a kick out of when I asked for a water and she pointed at a gatorade cooler behind me. 

I would probably go back. But not super eager too.

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: Tries to stand out as a strong supporter for the military but doesn't know how to check a military ID??? $6.50 for a can of bud light? Consider this a one beer and move on location at best.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I have heard about The Grand Ole Opry my entire life.  So, when my wife & I found ourselves coming through Nashville and it turned out that there was a show, it seemed like something we should do.

We are not big country music fans, but the show could not have been more fun!  It was a real slice of Americana.  Everyone was extremely welcoming and friendly.  The fact that when we bought our tickets we had not idea who would be on the venue added to the adventure.  We enjoyed every artist and were pleasantly surprised when the final headliner was The Band Perry (If I die Young.)

It is not cheap, but not outrageous for top scale live entertainment.  The crowd tended to the old side, but it was a full-family attraction with all ages well represented.  Parking was ample.  The seats are bench-style, but well padded and there is not a bad view in the house!  Even a huge thunderstorm could not dampen the evening.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: First time to Nashville and loved it. The Grand Ole Opry was wonderful. It was quite an interesting experience. We had handicap seats that were excellent. My husband is not a country fan but really enjoyeD it. The history  is remarkable.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
The 4-day weekend that was Yelp Spring Break 2014 officially ended for me Sunday at noon. That gave me pretty much a whole day to run around Nashville & get to all the places I'd heard about while in town but hadn't been to yet.

"You have to go check out Flying Saucer." I'd heard that over & over again the week I was in Nashville. At the taproom near where I was staying. At each craft brewery I visited. It always came up, sooner or later, in conversations: Flying Saucer's 80+ taps of quality craft beers.

So on my last full day in Nashville, I finally made my way over for a little lunch & a lot of beer. This place bills itself as Nashville's draft emporium & yes, yes it is. Lunch time on a Sunday was slow & most of the place (& it's a really big place) was empty. I sat at the bar. 

The bartender was very attentive & accommodating. Although it wasn't busy, Sundays are a great day to visit Flying Saucer. It's $3.50 pints on all TN beers. Looks like I'm drinking local. For bites to go with my brews, I had the Rocket-Tots & those were screamin' good!

Looking over a calendar they had posted, Sunday $3.50 TN pints was just the beginning. Flying Saucer does all kinds of weekly specials & events. I was really starting to wish I'd be in town longer so I could come back.

My advice for any craft beer enthusiast visiting Nashville... "You have to go check out Flying Saucer." & go early while you're in town so you'll have the chance to go back again. Mondays are $3.00 pints on almost every beer in the house, you don't want to miss that.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
This historic and culturally significant venue is a true beauty. Some of the biggest stars have stood on the stage and gave some of their greatest performances. 

What is love about the Grand Ole Opry is the layout; no matter where you are sitting there are no bad seats. You will have a great view throughout the entire venue. 

Be sure to pick up a few sourvenirs from the gift shop, and to take the behind the scenes tour for $24 bucks. You get to learn the history of the Grand Ole Opry, go backstage, check out the dressing rooms, and walk the halls that some of the greatest names in country music have walked. Its truly a magical experience.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I had heard of this of course, but had no idea what it really was.  

A live radio show... Complete with live commercials from local merchants. 

We enjoyed all of the artists, the beauty and traditions of The Grand Ole Opry and the banter of the Master of Ceremonies. 

It is a must see if you are near Nashville.  I would go again, even though Country music is not really my fav;) 
The whole experience is awesome.  

Next time I would look into a VIP pass to see the inner working of the back of the house;) 

YeeHaw!

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Great to experience being here but not my favorite concert to come to.   Very fast show and not much music for one artist. But I'm glad I got to experience it.  Just not what I fully expected.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: No longer a $3 cover on Friday and Saturday nights, yippee!!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: This terrible establishment failed to protect a patron from an angry customer. She proceeded to punch, scratch and completely disrespect a family of customers. This was atrocious all because we asked if she was done at her table so we could spread out to more seats with our large party. We did not force her out but simply asked the question

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
Awesome spot to grab a drink in a relaxed, chill atmosphere!  Their beer list is amazing--they have something like 100 beers available.  Their wine and cocktail lists are a bit smaller, but still good.  I had the Tennessee cocktail and I will say it didn't taste like there was much alcohol in it.
As others mentioned, not super friendly friendly as compared to other places in Nashville, but the vibe is such that it's nice to just chat and lay back on their comfy couches (amazing) w/o having someone come by all the time.  Also, their food is great!  Get the jalapeno tots (comes w/ cheese, bacon, fried egg) and the pretzels (the sauces are amazing).

name: Belcourt Taps
text:
Oh my god, this place was so disappointing. An old friend was in town and we made the horrible mistake of bringing her here, I was embarrassed for Nashville to be represented by them to my friend. 

Service: our waitress was obviously new, which was fine... She mentioned taking an abc class recently and made small talk with us about how scary the class was and about how important it was to see every customers I.D's.... She took our beer orders....and DID NOT I.D. a single one of us, we were kind of dumbfounded...

Food: horrible. I'm talking probably the worst food we've had in over a year. We ordered the nacho plate which consisted of low quality chips, nasty pickled jalapeños and the MOST DISGUSTING queso I have EVER had. It wasn't even hot, it was cold and thick and over everything. Absolutely disgusting. My stomach actually hurt after eating it. The other plate we got was the fried pickle appetizer, it wasn't nearly as bad but was hardly memorable. 

Considering the restaurant is advertised as a "tapas" restaurant we assumed they might actually give a damn about their food. It was laughable, they should be ashamed they even served that.

name: Third Man Records
text: Let's just say I couldn't find the newest Kenny Chesney!

name: John Rich's Redneck Riviera
text: Terrible experience here! Went last night with a group of people and the bouncer didn't let me In when i had different forms of ID's i'm 23 years old. Highly recommend on getting new bouncers there so rude. You just lost business

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
Beautiful concert hall. Very intimate, and great acoustics. I came to see Kem in concert and left a very happy lady. 
If you have trouble walking, please arrive Extra early. There's quite a bit of walking and stairs to climb. We didn't opt to use the elevator due to the long wait time.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Sometimes you find the perfect place and Tennessee Brewing was and is the prefect place. The beer was good the staff was amazing the food was delightful.  The atmosphere was perfect.  The upper deck allowed for a picturesque view of the city. The lower decks and patios gave the feel of your own back yard with family and friends. The staff was so helpful with explaining about their beers.  They took the time to describe their beers and how their flights should be drank to get the most enjoyment from flavors.  Once we settled into a spot and began to soak in the view and tease our taste buds with some down home great beers our food showed up. We were just knocked of our feet with the flavors and visual presentation of meal.  It was our last night in town and the experience at Tennessee Brewing was spectacular.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: So this place is IT. This was my favorite place for live music in Nashville. It wasn't typical honky tonk nor was it classic rock or top 40 hits. The band we saw had a cello and violin and it was just DIVINE! It's very divey, but comfy, inviting, great seats for viewing the band, and a really neat atmosphere.

name: Ole Red
text: I wish I could say that we actually tasted anything served here, but we did not. Instead, my best friend was harassed because her I.D. expired THE NEXT DAY. FOR HER 50TH BIRTHDAY. Will never return.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
This is the bar we ended our trip to Nashville in, and we ended up staying for longer than we were planning to because of the awesome band performing and the great atmosphere. We got here at around midnight and were lucky enough to grab a seat on the second floor overlooking the band performing below. The music was absolutely amazing, decorations in the bar were fun, and overall we wished we had went to Layla's for more than one night. 

Definitely recommend this location. It has a different feel from the other bars - a bit more laid back perhaps - and we enjoyed it immensely.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: The food is really heavy, fried and cream based. The prices are high at least $12 an order no alcohol included. The beer is great. Recommend stopping for a drink and show but no food.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: So glad we had our company retreat here! What an honor to listen to Gordon Kennedy -Grammy award winning songwriter. Staff was fantastic!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I can't attest to the hockey experience at Bridgestone which is after all why it's here to begin with--I do know the local fans are enthusiastic to say the least (though many are heartbroken at the moment over the Cup they almost snagged). I just haven't been to see one as I'm not much of a hockey fan but one of these days I might give it a shot. I have now seen two live rock shows at Bridgestone which is what my review will reflect.

First of all---it is a general rule for me that live music is best in small-medium venues where you can see the act from the floor in your line of sight. As such I've see many up and coming and (in my mind) established and proficient acts of many genres in the many other venues scattered throughout the city since my move to the area a few years ago. You can see great shows at Marathon, Exit/In, 3rd & Lindsey, The End, etc. But there are simply some acts that will not play such a modest venue and when it comes to an arena act, Bridgestone is a solid, in many ways superb, choice. For one thing there's not really a bad seat in the house. On the floor, in the stands, even in the top left or right stands, the stage and set up is always in your line of sight wherever you sit. For another, because it's an ICE HOCKEY ARENA this place is not sweltering and damp. Some venues will have you feeling like you're in a sweat lodge but things remain comfortable and even somewhat chilly here at Bridgestone no matter how packed or active a show. To top it off, the crew and staff are remarkable at working a crowd through the line at a remarkable pace--safely and securely. You have no problem getting through a line and to your seat in plenty of time. Even leaving your seat to hit the restroom and get back in time for the next act (or to get a snack or drink) is painless.

As for negatives, it's doubtful that any are unique to Bridgestone and aren't just part of every arena experience--no decent parking that isn't $25 and up (depending on the surge) in the area (but even then you're in and out of nearby lots pretty quickly), insane concession prices ($10 for a 'refillable' cola, I can only imagine the beer prices), etc. All in all though, if a major act is coming to the area Bridgestone is a good place to catch them,

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Came back a second time on a second trip. Always great beer and food. Will come back again soon.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
On a vacation, the temptation might be to invest wisely, like Warren Buffett, but in Nashville, the temptation is more likely to leave you drinking like Jimmy Buffett.  I actually don't drink, but as a fan of his music for many, many years, I've been to over a dozen Margaritaville's so on a recent trip to Nashville for a Paul Simon concert, of course I had to stop by this one for lunch.  

Live music is a common feature of Margaritaville, but not often during lunchtime, so I was pleasantly surprised to see a performer when I arrived at just before noon on a Saturday.  He was working his way through a mix of cover songs (think the theme song from The Dukes of Hazzard) & I was quickly seated by a welcoming hostess.

While I have been to many of their restaurants, most Margaritavilles do have one or two unique area dishes (e.g. their take on the po' boy in New Orleans), but at this location, I opted for the French Dip & Sweet Potato Fries & settled in to watch some old Buffett performance clips on one of the many tv screens hanging in the restaurant while I waited for my meal.  

It arrived quickly enough, as did a refill on my drink order, & the food was excellent.  The space in the venue is such that it's not too noisy that you can enjoy a conversation & still hear the music being played & the service I experienced was quite good.

After lunch, I visited the retail shop & while I was a bit bummed on the lack of locally themed merchandise (I have enough t-shirts for the rest of my life that I was hoping for a little more variety), most casual visitors should walk away happy.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Great selection of concessions. Seating is terrible. People were leaving and going to the ticket office to request reassignment because the seats were extremely small. It was amazing that an arena that was recently updated has such tight seating. They were very good about trying to accommodate the people, but when you pay $60+ for a ticket you expect to be able to sit in the seat.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: A very crazy place! Very friendly bartenders and great music. We mostly had drinks but also the fried shrimps and it was amazing!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Best band we found on Broadway all weekend! Not too crowded and the service was great!

name: National Underground
text: Hopped in here on a 2nd trip to Nashville. Was harassed by a worker about using the bathroom first before buying a drink. I thought it was odd. He continued until my friend gave her credit card up to buy a drink. He still continued and lectured me after I got out of the bathroom. I find the place rude and won't be coming back.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: My only complaint is how early they close on Friday nights! 10 PM seems a little too early for me...BUT we did really enjoy this place! They had a unique beer selection and we enjoyed each of the drinks we had. I also really liked how they had games available, from old school games, to multiple darts boards. There was plenty of seating, from their two patios to the double stories. I also liked how you could look out into their brewery area and walk through it.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: This place was crazy packed and extremely loud. When we walked in no empty tables or chairs were there. We listened live band music in standing. It was Friday late evening on Broadway, Nashville. The band was pretty good, even if it was not country music.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: One of the better places to drink a variety of local brewed beer in town especially if you're a tourist staying in close proximity to downtown and don't want to venture too far outside the city to checkout other breweries like Fat Bottom (East Nashville) and would rather not sit in a big tourist trap like Big River. The beer is pretty good, some are a bit adventurous for my taste (Basil Ryeman), but I just don't like herbs in my beer. The full bodied and citrusy Southern Whit is top notch and for me the best they have to offer. The small, yet reasonably priced menu is probably the most "sophisticated" any local brewery has to offer. The sandwich section consists of a burger and hot dog gilded with boutique garnishments that would make a Whole Foods proud. The entrees are mostly French culinary standards masquerading as southern staples, but what it lacks in innovation and creativity it makes up for in value. The frog legs were eccentric, but tasty. Definitely worth checking out when you're checking out Nashville

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: The 5 beer burger and seasoned fries were ridiculously good. Cool vibe and the Travel Channel was shooting a special there while we were drinking so it has to be good!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Bridgestone is a great venue for concerts, as I've been here twice for the Maroon 5 and Bruno Mars concerts. 

I do agree with Sheena T. that musical groups don't sound so good performing live here. It was hard to hear the live performer because the music was way too loud. I went to a Bruno Mars concert at the Fox's Theater in Atlanta two years ago and the sounding was much better (Of course Bruno's singing is still godly!). However, the lighting was awesome! The lightning is what I love best about this place. 

I was lucky to grab floor seating for the Bruno Mars's concert. I was placed in these tiny chair closely placed next to each other. Although the chair was comfortable, I wish they didn't put the chairs so close together or get bigger chairs (I am pretty petite so that says something!). At the concert, this one obese lady was siting next to me and she literally sat on her chair and 30% of my chair...her "boyfriend" put his arm around her neck and kept hitting my shoulder (and tried to hit on me too -__-). I barely had room to stand or dance when standing up because she hogged the space (no pun intended). 

The food was average to me. My friend liked the fried chicken tenders a lot but I thought it was bland. Also, they don't let you carry water/soda in a bottle. Any drinks have to be put in a cup so the crazy fans can't throw the bottles around. 

Traffic is horrible every time there is a big event. Arrive here 1 hour early to avoid the traffic and find parking as most of the closer parkings are filled up quickly. I was late for the last concert and had to park 2 blocks away from Bridgestone (behind Hume Fogg HS) and it was pretty safe to walk. It costed $15 to park till the next day. 

2013/#72

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: The BEST hot chicken sandwich EVER. I did not want it to end. My husband had the burger. It was almost as good as the chicken. Cool place, free parking, off the beaten path and good beer. Visiting from out of town and so happy we found this place through Yelp!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We were wandering around aimlessly downtown, looking for somewhere to go that has live music and good drinks. Jimmy Buffet's had an open area of seating and live acoustic music so we decided to stop in. There were 2 guys doing some cover songs which made for good background music. Buffet's music was everywhere...in the menu, written on the walls, on the tv, etc. Our server, Monte, was really nice and was on top of everything. I would give him 5 stars but I can only give Jimmy Buffet's 3 for being so mediocre. I ordered a cheeseburger and for almost $11, it was comparable to fast food. I ordered a hurricane which was very weak. This is a very touristy spot. As a local, I've learned my lesson and will try somewhere else for a good cheeseburger and stronger drinks. This place is nice for live music and people watching if you sit in the front out in the open.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Staffing people to prevent patrons from exiting at the end of a capacity event is unsafe. Minus one star for each of the two exits staff people told me I could not exit this past Tuesday. 

Minus another star when floor staff person asked me for tickets to prove my seats were on the floor, when half an hour earlier he had checked my tickets for our initial entry. That must have been the cause of the line. Hey ushers and arenas! It's not patrons fault paperless tickets are the norm and we don't have paper tickets in hand.

Minus another star for $20 for a double mixed drink (before tip).

Decent facility but price gouging, no arena parking, and ridiculous staffing make this a place in need of some improvement!

name: Ole Red
text: Nice place, cool vibe. Had lunch. Food is ok, not great but not awful. But the gnats! So many! Gnats in our faces, poking at our drinks, tasting our food.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Fantastic brew pub. Great food, awesome beer, and fantastic service. I genuinely felt like the staff was committed to assuring I had a great experience.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text:
Oh Winners, you fascinating little Midtown gem.  Many nights have been spent here, listening to karaoke (avidly avoiding the singing on stage part myself), enjoying buckets of cold brews, singing and dancing along with the crowds.  I always find it ironic that you're less crowded than your neighbor Losers, but you're always busy on a weekend night and you offer the fantastic Whiskey Jams on Monday nights, showcasing local talent and surprise guests.  

I can honestly say there has never been a night where I've come here and not been entertained or amused.  You're quick with the drinks, you have a great patio, and a prime location.  I'm not sure much else needs to be said.  You're a great little Nashville haunt, a fun place to go on any night; though I'd appreciate it if you outlawed the singing of slow songs after midnight (can we say fun sponging?).

name: UV Nightclub
text: Don't waste your time. Bad drinks. Bartenders in bad moods.  Dirty atmosphere with a dance floor that is partially covered with nasty carpet. Nashville offers  so much more at other venues. Do not even waste your time for one drink.

name: Ole Red
text:
Southern as PBR.  Ok that's not completely accurate.  The atmosphere is decidedly music focused.  They have live music everyday and almost the entire time they are open, tip the performers - Lower Broad tradition is they all play just for tips.  

We stopped in for lunch with the kids.  The food was southern influenced and felt filling if not heavy on the stomach.  We opted to try several appetizers and share them at our table.  All were good and could have been a meal on their own.  

The bar was open and in full swing at 11am when we arrived.  If you enjoy a cocktail with your meal they have a fairly long list of options, along with several beers on tap.  

There is also a gift shop if you aren't hungry or thirsty you can always pop in and grab an Ole Red shot glass or tshirt.  

We are locals and this is one of those places we will return to for performances and when out of town guests come to visit.  A nice addition to the Lower Broad scene.  

The building is pretty fun too, google it.  It once housed a quite famous shop and now has 5 floors of space open via the Ole Red venue.

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
This is such an amazing venue! It was beautiful, the acoustics were incredible, and no matter where you sat you had an awesome view! I'm very disappointed in myself for never having been before! This first trip was to see the Video Games Live concert. It. Blew. My. Mind! If they bring this back yearly, I think it could bring more interest from younger generations that don't have exposure to classical style orchestral music. It's safe to say that I will be attending more shows here in the future! 

The only problem is that I saw on the local news that the Schermerhorn is going into bankruptcy! Say it ain't so! Days after finding this gem I hear this terrible news! If the hall survives this I will certainly be buying season passes. The arts deserve our support, and make no mistake this is at at it's finest.

On the night I went they had free parking at LP field with a $3 shuttle to take you to and from the center. I don't know if that is for every show, but if it is, that's a great parking deal!

Also, for those that didn't know, free concerts in the park for the community are held during the summer. Check it out!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: This is my favorite restaurant and every time I come there I am greeted by the hostess, Shacora. She is very pleasant and gives my family and I the best seating possible. She has a very great attitude which brings my family and I back everytime

name: Ole Red
text: Fantastic bar with great drinks! Live music! Bartenders Randi and Brandi were great! Great place to cool off in Nashville summer heat!

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Winners really ought to post something, somewhere, on their website that says they're only 21+. With a website that promises a "great culinary experience", my boyfriend and I (who are 20 and were visiting Nashville) decided to try it out and catch some football/grab some lunch in December. We got there at noon, hardly anyone else there, and a waitress who didn't give us her name comes up and says, can I see your IDs? We were confused, but gave them to her and she says, "um, you people are too young. You need to leave right now." We were shocked, as a place marketing themselves as a bar and grill with a decent menu selection is rarely 21+ at all, let alone at noon. Total letdown, and even though we'll be over 21 next time we visit, we certainly won't be heading to Winners or Losers.

name: Ole Red
text: We sat on the 5th floor. We did not realize when booking our reservation that there was a limited menu on the top floor (appetizer only). This would be great if it was communicated when booking. We had the seafood platter, baked pretzel, burrata cheese. All decent, but nothing to brag about.  The crab legs were served with no claw crackers which made them very hard to eat normally. Could have used 2 more servers. Busy for a Saturday night so it took extra time to get drinks, silverware, and plates. This place is new so I will assume they are working out the details of running a successful roof top restaurant and bar in Nashville.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Proximity to the Ryman was the initial draw to this restaurant.  We had valeted the car there and with the frigid temperatures, we wanted something close by.  As soon as we stepped through the doors, we felt good about the choice.  
We were seated immediately and the life music was wonderful.    Our server was reasonably attentive and even told us about other events going on in the area.  
I ordered the shrimp trio and enjoyed it but since the grilled shrimp was my favorite of the trio, I was wishing that I'd just ordered those. 
It is definitely somewhere that we'll go again.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Best part - the band played started at 9:30 and went almost until 1:00. They were great and kept the audience engaged. The dance floor was never empty - everyone heard something they could dance to. 

Service - we were a group of four and we were seated promptly after we walked in. We got lucky with timing and got a table right in front of the stage. 

Food service - was extremely slow and each round of food (appetizers and main course) ended up being served after a long period  waiting. Almost 45 minutes between our order and receiving the food. 
We also wanted to order dessert but when I tired to our server said they're not serving dessert anymore. I wish she informed us they were changing their menu. 

Food - decent shrimp dishes. Everything else tastes mediocre. 

Drinks - decent drinks although I've had better margaritas. Most of them ended up being more sour than I expected (blueberry margarita, watermelon margarita, tranquil waters, and last mango in Paris. )

Although it was a great place with a talented band, the service did not match up to it.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
This was my first time coming to the Bridgetown Arena for a concert in Nashville. The venue was big enough for the band and honestly I had no idea who they were until my niece asked to go. 

They did have plenty alcohol options. Their food options were ok, what you expect at a music event. The staff were very professional and helpful. 

Great concert venue.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Insanely busy! But what would one expect from doing the "Broadway scene" in Nashville? Stood in line at the bar for about 15 or so minutes to get a drink when I asked a waiter that walked by if there's a quicker way to get a drink. He explained that we could take a table in the dining/ entertainment area. We took a table down front near the Dance Floor area. The band was great! The drinks were good and the service was reasonable considering how busy they were. In comparison to the Vegas Margaritaville it is much smaller, but all the bars on Broadway are pretty small in Nashville... At least the ones I saw and entered. The atmosphere was on point and I would most definitely go back again.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We were here on a Monday at lunch. The place was nearly empty when we arrived, and yet it took over 2.5 hours to complete lunch. The world's slowest service. Live country music (not one Jimmy Buffet song in the bunch). Sub-par food (stale chips, soggy chopped salad, taco meat worse than Taco Bell's). Good burgers and drinks.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: Solid bar and grill. Ate dinner and had drinks during whiskey jam. Food was good, service was great too. Drinks weren't over priced nor was the bill. All alcohol wasn't under done, which made for perfect drinks.

name: National Underground
text: I went with friends that are musician and were playing.  I got a Tuna Melt and it was okay nothing to complain about for the food.  What I did not appreciate was the drunk sound guy telling me the band sucks and that he hated the lead singer and like to "F@ck with her."  To get a drink I had to walk to the bar, but the bartender was a very sweet girl.

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
Simply beautiful.

This is the perfect home for the Nashville Symphony; a classy and very elegant space, with comfortable seats, great views and stunning acoustics.  It is hard to find a bad seat at the Schermerhorn, or to not enjoy the inside and outside of this remarkable campus.  This really is an exceptional venue space and Nashville landmark.

We came here for the first time to see Kathy Griffin, and we're already excited to come for a symphony performance or concert.  We found the ushers and staff to be helpful and friendly, and the interior of the building to be large enough to accomodate everyone comfortably, without long lines or that uncomfortable crushed feeling that sometimes accompanies venues like this.  The seats are tiered in such a way that everyone seated on the floor can see the stage easily, and the venue is small enough that no matter where you're seated, you can still see the faces of every performer and the strings on every instrument.

How lucky are we to have such a wonderful space to hear exceptional music and experience comedians, dancers and other entertainers?!  We'll definitely be returning.

name: Ole Red
text: Very new place to having good time!   Good for Drinks&Food and Music and Music and Music

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Margaritaville is a great place to stop on Broadway for a sit-down meal with a full menu, without missing out on the fun of live music. My husband and I had lunch here while in Nashville and were not disappointed. The food was an appreciated change from hot chicken and tater tots that can be ordered at most bars on Broadway. The food boasted both quality and quantity; be sure to come here hungry! Our server Karah was super attentive and very pleasant. Overall this was an excellent dining experience, and we will surely be back our next time in Nashville.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: LOVE THIS PLACE!!!  Tucked away in a neighborhood you wouldn't expect, but the place is nice and has awesome beer!  Definitely do a Beer Flight.  The Basil Ryeman is my favorite!  Service was good and to top it off, our server learned it was our anniversary and gave us our Pints FREE!!!  Great service and did a little extra with giving us a free pint of beer. We will definitely be back to imbibe some more with FANTABULOUS BEER!!!

name: National Underground
text: Very inviting from the sidewalk with patio space for us ladies and our pup. The white whiskey moonshine was a good starter on a hot day especially on vaca. The service and food are also worth the trip.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Tour lasted less than 15 minutes, no excitement or enthusiasm from these brewmasters!

name: Ole Red
text: Atmosphere was great...as was the live music.  The food was just "ok." Not a very big menu.  Fried pickles and cornbread were our two favorites.  Also had the Fried chicken and pork cops...which were underwhelming.  The service was good and friendly...and relatively quick.  Would probably only go back for drinks and skip the food.

name: Nashville Symphony
text: Beautiful venue, and excellent customer service.  Had a great experience hearing the Nashville Symphony play alongside Leann Rimes last night.  Would recommend to anyone to visit this place.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I saw the Predators play the Capitals on 1/16 so this review is for the hockey experience. 

Let me start off by saying I'm from Chicago, so we've been a hockey city for a MUCH longer period of time than Nashville. 

The arena is very nice and quite large. Concessions are priced about average to what I'd pay at any other NHL venue, but the ticket prices were EXTREMELY CHEAP compared to other stadiums. My tickets cost by about 3/4 less then what I would pay here in Chicago (again different market) and were great seats. 

Parking for us sucked, as there really isn't a true parking lot used for the arena; more you have to find a parking structure nearby, and ours was about a 15 minute walk. That wasn't so bad as you get to walk through down town Nashville and take in the bar scene and music scene, but I'm sure for families with kids it could get dicey. 

The atmosphere itself was rather "minor-league" feel. Very quiet during games, and when it wasn't, the team had these lame college chants that felt like they dragged on forever, for different in game situations.  I mean due to the Nashville still trying to grow their fan base, they need to do these things, but at times it felt like overkill. 

All in all, I liked the stadium and the view we had, as well as the atmosphere outside the arena. The in game atmosphere left a lot to be desired as was more minor league than NHL.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
My experience was AWESOME when attending a concert at Bridgestone Arena. I attended a concert over Easter weekend with a large group of family- including children. Safety was a huge concern for us, but the large amount of security manning the arena made us feel safe.

The seats aren't too bad. For our concert, we sat in the nose bleed sections and did not feel claustrophobic in the seats- a huge plus for "crappier" seats. The sound in the arena was fantastic.

Leaving the arena proved to have its difficulties. The escalators stopped working at one point during our exit which made a huge halt in the traffic pattern and ultimately took a good thirty minutes to get from our seats to the front doors. 

Another important thing to add, though it is not the arena itself responsible, is that traffic around the arena is a mad house. The parking was not cheap for a spot roughly a half mile from the doors- $20 per vehicle.

name: Ole Red
text:
This is the best music venue in town. Loved the layout and the ability to see the stage from everywhere. The bands were fantastic!  Bar service was prompt
And very friendly. 

Had we left when we got hungry, I would rate this place. 10. Sadly, we didn't want to miss the band so are there. It was terrible. I ordered the grilled ham and cheese sandwich  and the bread was burnt beyond recognition. Inedible. And the waitress said she was sorry but no offer to fix and it appeared on the bill. Would have made a bigger deal but we were done.  

Go For the music and drinks. Eat at Luke Bryan's. Where the music and drinks were also fantastic.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Busy place. Grumpy bartender. If you're going to work in the bar business in a town like Nashville you should try to enjoy people. Maybe he was just having a bad day. Fish tacos were very good. Fins up margarita was all sour mix and not very good.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Went during CMA Fest and had such a good time. David was great and our food was so tasty!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I'm a big fan of this arena, especially during the Preds games. Food is really good and reasonably priced. My go-to is the Kayem's hot dog with fries combo. $7.75 but as a season ticket holder, I get a dollar off! Plenty of food at a great price; you can't be that. Also, I prefer to get my beer at the bar on the 200 level; the beer selection is more to my taste (i.e. Sierra Nevada Pale, Yazoo selections, etc.) and has a full bar. A craft bottle here costs you 6.75 compared to a $10 20 oz can of Bud at concessions. (No thank you.) And, as a season ticket holder, you get a discount as well! Also worth mentioning, the bartenders are pretty cool and courteous, as is all staff in and around the arena. Keep up the good work Bridgestone!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: We met the beautiful, beefy, bald headed, bartender Jeremy here and got $2.50 PBRs. Can't be beat for the prices in Nashville.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: Came to Nashville specifically for the Preds/Lightning game. Unfortunately, I think our home arena in Tampa has spoiled me. Entering the facility and getting through security was a breeze, and the interior of the arena is very eye-catching, but that's where the wow factor ended. While walking to the seats, it was evident that the arena had not been thoroughly cleaned after the last event; there was garbage underneath the majority of the seats and just looked dirty. The seats are also very narrow to some standards, similar to a cheap airline; the woman next to our group was somewhat portly and 'spilled over' into one of our seats. The prices of the beer and food were fair (considering you're at a sports arena). Other than that, great location with tons of hotels nearby for visitors, but some room for improvement.

name: Ole Red
text: Came to Nashville, our second day back, atmosphere here is great all friendly people.  You share your table which is fun.  The couple who shared our table bought us drinks for the nite, who can beat that.  We went to mostly all the top clubs on Broadway.  We think Ole Red is by far the best for food, drinks and good old country music.  Many bands play Big dance floor which we like.

name: Ole Red
text: Probably the worst place in Nashville .  Music so loud you can't talk. Macaroni and cheese and baked bees were terrible. No Tobasco So called dance floor had food and drinks spilled all over it

name: Marathon Music Works
text: The only reason this was not a one rating is because 311 was awesome. I don't know how you can have a concert with no air conditioning. Sweat was pouring off everyone's faces. My fiancé who meet goes to concerts had a bad experience all because it was 100 degrees in a concert. The only thing that would have made the concert better is if it was at a different venue.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: If you go there you have to ask for Chris Anthony best service we have received in at least 6 months. Chris made this meal a great experience.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Lots of choices along Broadway...we were lured by the southern rock blues vibe playing inside.  We stopped in for a quick refreshment.  Chatted it up with a great bartender who was genuinely personable, super friendly and pretty cute.  Band pulled in other singers and performers and music was loud enough to talk  over.  Recommend for casual, enjoyable experience.

name: Ole Red
text: Checked out this new place today and just loved it!!  The second of Blake Sheldon's restaurants named after his song. Great atmosphere!  Aaron from Texas was our server and he was fabulous. Gave us some great recommendations and info on the nighttime bands, building of the place, etc.  Live music was great. Not too loud for a lunch time atmosphere. Food was very very good.  I would recommend!!!

name: Ole Red
text: Came in went upstairs to bar. Totally not busy. Totally ignored by a female bartender as I sat with a credit card in my hand. Sorry Blake, but your place needs better service. The guy singing was awesome tho.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: $10 for a shot of bourbon in a plastic cup. So worth it! The music was amazing. The location was quaint. Like an old dive bar. A bit grungy. Not too crowded, but still hopping. They have security at the door which is great. Being a girl, all alone, honky tonking, Layla's was the place I felt the safest.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: I used to go here about once a month for a happy hour event.  I will never go here again.  I was assaulted by the staff at the neighboring bar "Losers."  The staff lied to the police about the incident, and the in house video was suspiciously "broken" when a detective returned to retrieve the evidence. Three staff members participated in beating me unconscious.  I left in an ambulance.  The incident cost me thousands of dollars.  I witnessed a similar incident at Winners a few years ago. When I asked what happened then, I was told to "mind my own business or I could join him." I sincerely regret my silence.  Being a bouncer is not an entitlement to assault people.  I would not recommend either establishment to my worst enemy.  Winners and Losers should both be out of business.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: The venue itself is cool. Looks awesome.......just don't go there expecting a great listening experience. Easy parking a huge plus. But the purpose it serves is self defeating because the acoustics are terrible. Saw Stryper last night and I could not get over how such a great band could sound so deplorable. . Low end was pure unadulterated MUD. Acoustically this place is pretty much a gymnasium......and it sounded like one.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Chris in retail is awesome! Super friendly. Drinks were good quality. Food and service was great. Good tourist spot. I'm local and still like to come down for the music.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: I go to concerts a lot in Nashville, but I recently visited Marathon for the first time. I have to say, it was a wonderful and spacious venue. I love how they have multiple bar locations. Very convenient. They even had three dollar tacos! The only thing I really disliked was the fact that there are bathroom attendants. It's not a classy restaurant or anything so why did they need to be there? The woman in the lady's room was very harsh and tried to force her help on you. I'm perfectly capable of pumping soap and getting a paper towel on my own, thanks though. Overall super neat venue!

name: Ole Red
text: It was very disappointing. The decor was not a country atmosphere. It was very modern, staff was not friendly.  How could someone put a place like this in the middle of a historic district.  The new restaurants was not even busy but the old established ones were packed. We asked one musician to play an old country song by Ray Price. He said love the song but don't play in that era which I thought how would you even be here if not for the history of country music.

name: Ole Red
text: Went here for dinner while at a conference, no expectations. Nice corner location on Broadway. It has a large open main floor area with a great band playing. It was lively but not too loud. Nashville hot biscuit sandwich was delightful but I must comment in the sweet potatoes tots! Oh my word! Delish! Great place to eat, take in a band and then head out for other adventures on Broadway.

name: Ole Red
text: This was my first visit to Nashville, and I had to check out Ole Red. My friend and I were at the restaurant when it opened for lunch and were seated promptly and welcomed by our awesome waitress Nira. Before we even placed our order, I was in need of caffeine bad and she made me a fresh pot of coffee! Everything on the menu sounded great, it was hard to decide what to choose. I went for the Nashville Hot Chicken Biscuit with a mini wedge salad and my friend got the Half Fried Chicken bucket with a side of mashed potatoes. Our food came quickly and was so yummy! The Nashville Hot Chicken Biscuit was huge, the size of a hamburger and I got the tater tots as a side (such a good choice). The fried chicken was served in a bucket, full to the rim and came with biscuits and scrumptious milk gravy (bottle that up and sell it in the gift shop)!  A few minutes after we started eating, my friend's mouth started to tingle and she realized there must've been pickles in the brine of the fried chicken. She's allergic to pickles and didn't think to ask and of course left her medicine at our hotel! Nira and the manager Sean were so great and responsive to help my friend. They quickly removed her meal and went searching for Benadryl. In fact, Sean went to a drug store close by and bought Benadryl for my friend, that's A+ service if you ask me! She ordered another (non pickle brine) meal - the pork steak (ginormous) and we ate, drank and listened to great music for the next 5 hours! The vibe and food are great at Ole Red, but for us, it was the impeccable service that will bring us back the next time we visit Nashville.

name: Ole Red
text: Great entertainment and great food! Pimento Cheese appetizer was the best!! Huge portions - consider sharing! The bucket of chicken is literally a bucket of chicken!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: so disappointed, service was horrible. i ordered cheeseburger and bread was stale. the perfect margarita was the only good part. The waitress was totally out of it

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: LOVE this bar! The food, the drinks, the music, the bartenders/waitresses. Prob my fave place to be anytime we're in town! We love being here! It's a throwback to what Nash used to be and I love it!

name: Ole Red
text:
Wow.... this place SUCKS.
Went to see our neighbor sing, waited two hours with our name on the list. Surrounded by at least 15 empty tables. The tables that were seated were not getting their drinks for 10-15 minutes. Servers moved like snails. When asked the hostess and MANAGER why there were empty tables and we were still waiting they were hesitant and said "I don't really know". This place needs to get it together or they will have no business. Would not recommend. Music was great though.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Our first night in Nashville we found this gem! Great food and beer plus live bluegrass music! A wonderful spot to hang out and enjoy Music City USA! We will be back for sure.

name: Ole Red
text: Great rooftop on a sunny day. Cute vibe. Loved it!!! Would return! Didn't experience lower levels. Roof was awesome.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I've eaten here 3 times now.  Twice back in February and it was Fantastic.  I tend to not venture out too much once I find something I like.  All three times I've gotten the Fajita Taco Salad which normally comes with beef but substituted chicken instead.  It comes with the dressing already mixed up in the salad and it was superbly blended.  However, I ate the same thing just recently and it was just mediocre.  I was disappointed.  Overall though, the service was excellent, we were able to walk right in and sit down at the bar and it was on a weekend when we went.  We did get there early though.  I would still recommend this place!

name: Ole Red
text: We dined 6/30 right at opening (11am) and came in with the waiting wave of people. We were seated quickly although most of the staff seemed to be in a bad mood. The menu is very specialized, meaning not a ton of choices, none of the appetizers really seemed our cup of tea but we did both order the Tennessean burger, it came with pimento cheese and the usual toppings. The husband got fries and they come out seasoned well and thick. I substituted  with a mini wedge salad that was really good and fresh. We both cleaned our plates! We actually had no idea this was Blake Shelton's restaurant, we popped in the day before and it was packed but stuck out because it was super clean, air conditioned and didn't reek of old smoke and beer! Definitely a good burger, we will be back and next time we will get the tots and poutine!! A little attention from the staff, refills etc. would be great and the bluegrass band playing was a nice touch! I would give it a try and if you are vegan they have quite a bit to choose from!

name: Ole Red
text: Crazy tourist trap. Rude staffers. Do not waste your time, they do not want or need your money

name: Ole Red
text: What a deal. We had a blast. The music was top notch,  atmosphere great and bartender best!  Have fun.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I went to see Mary J Blige & Nas. We had great seats and the staff was friendly. This was my second time attending an event here and I definitely will be back.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: This place is awesome. Service was outstanding beer was great and the food was off the hook great flavor profile

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Need to update my review. Because of my last review the manager was kind enough to reach out to me. I don't write this review because of any type of influence. On 5/31 we visited again. Kira was our server. Her service was spot on for the point of being excellent. Food was good. I wish yelp allowed 3.5 stars. Food was better than average but what you would expect from a chain. Based on this experiment I would absolutely go back. Obviously they have their thing, island drinks and appetizers. While we did not have them the nachos are huge and look pretty good.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
This was my second time visiting TN Brew Works. The first time I thought this brewery was just OK since the selection of beers wasn't my style. However, the most recent time I went (back in October), my sister and I each loved our beers. She had 1927 (IPA) and I had Basil Ryeman (Saison). 

The best part was the hummus. Odd, I know. But the white bean and curry hummus paired with texas toast was just perfect. It may have just been a seasonal item but if you can grab this when you're here you wont regret it!

The staff was friendly and knowledgeable. The set-up is pretty cool, ample seating with a second floor and a deck. I'll be back for sure!

name: Ole Red
text: This meal was really filling, price was reasonable. My friends got tater tots as their side and I immediately regretted getting the normal French fries. The tater tots were fluffy, crispy, delicious. The mushroom burger I order was great, the bbq sauce tasted sweet and tangy. The atmosphere of the restaurant is really fun, the entire restaurant itself is huge..two levels with live music. There was a wait for one hour but we ended up getting a text that our table was ready after about 10 minutes! You should check this place out, there's a few vegan options as well which I was really excited about.

name: Ole Red
text: The nachos are amazing! One tray is more than enough for 4people. Great music! Nice venue Blake Sheldon

name: National Underground
text: The most authentic and non-touristy places we visited in this neighborhood. Loved the Hot Chicken and great craft beer selection. Great vibe to the place, awesome band, and friendly door staff. Robert the bartender gave us great suggestions for where else to go (East Nashville, who knew?). Loved this place.

name: Marathon Music Works
text: Literally the worst place to host an event. The staff were rude. They acted essentially as fun police. Don't dance or act like a fun person at all or you will probably get kicked out. I'd give them zero stars if it was an option.

name: Ole Red
text: Fun place. Went for drinks and appetizers. Good band. Service was very good. Nachos were really good.

name: Ole Red
text: This bar is terrible, the bounces think that are bit shit. One bounce is like 5' 4 and will kick you out if he feels threatened. So no go here, there are about 100 other bars to go to

name: Ole Red
text:
