We really enjoyed the vibe here, but the food was mediocre at best. We really enjoyed the live music, the central location, the fun/happy-go-lucky atmosphere here, but it seemed a little franchise-y with the inside store. Also, the draft beer selection was awful...lots of mass produced beers, very little craft beer options, and no draft IPAs.

I had the quesadilla and don't recommend it. The table next to us got a bunch of burgers which looked BIG and juicy and delicious -- so maybe get that!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
I can't so much about this place, since the co-workers and I came here for just drinks.  And it was just 1 drink.  Since we were a large group, they sat us in the back with the other large groups.

For the most part, it looked decent.  It had nice ambience with enough lighting.  It had nice decorations around the place with palm trees, pictures, etc.  Overall, it wasn't too bad.  

Rating
Food:  n/a
Service:  4
Price:  3
Ambience:  3
Overall:  3

 Would probably come back if I come to Nashville.

name: Ole Red
text: First visit and, although seating was slow & hostess was grumpy, we had a nice visit; drinks and food were excellent; music was fabulous; prices reasonable; outstanding decor & friendly waitstaff. The Ole Red Onion burger was one for my top-ten burgers list; it was really exceptional. We will return!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
I wanted to try this restaurant because I love margaritas and I like Jimmy Buffett. I thought the decor was awesome it gave you an island feel. There were fake palm trees fake lanterns and a tiki area. I thought the gift shop was overpriced $16 for a 10oz coffee cup . 

The drinks were ok but not great or perfect considering I was at a Jimmy Buffett themed restaurant and he is know for margaritas. I've had better at a steakhouse and I paid 1 price for a margarita and it came in the shaker so I can refill my glass at my table. So go figure I paid almost $20 for 2 drinks that weren't as great as expected and at the steakhouse I could of paid maybe $15 with enough drink to equal both of the ones I had tonight. I think I'd been better off just grabbing a beer and drinking it with my meal. 

Now to the food this was completely unexpected from a well know restaurant with a song called Cheeseburger in Paradise because burger was not this. I ordered it well and it seemed too dry and no flavor at all. The fries were ok but it's hard to mess up fries but I've kinda slacked on eating them anyways. My husband ordered the garlic bacon burger and he didn't have any garlic flavor at all and the only flavor he got was from the ketchup. Our fried pickles didnt have any flavor either just battered pickles with no seasoning. Here is the kicker of the meal. My daughter said her chicken tenders were too greasy. This is a kid who loves her chicken and fries and if she doesn't like the food it's a no go. 

The waitress was nice and it didn't take long to get seated but kinda took awhile to get our food after we ordered and it wasn't too busy. This was around 5p on a Monday night with WWE Monday Night Raw in town at the arena. Location is awesome being within walking distance to the arena and our parking garage but I think this is how they attract the tourist that come to town. I know next time I will research the local restaurants near the area before I decide based on a name. I know this is one place we will not go back to unless its just for a couple of drinks before an event.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Arriving to town early, I couldn't check in to my hotel yet so I walked the Gulch & found myself cooling off at TN Brew Works. 
As a frequent visitor to NashVegas, I've had TNBW beers before & since I've never been to the actual brewery before, I decided to check it out. 
The beers themselves are good but nothing mind blowing. What gives them the 5 stars is the quality of service. Everyone working the taproom was exceptional & were quick to chat. Some of the staff gave me tips on other Nashville establishments that I haven't went to as well as informing me that Jack White's Third Man Records was within walking distance, which I ended up checking off the bucket list as well! 
The next time I'm in town, TN Brew Works will definitely be on my radar.

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: This place has a lot of potential, but the lack of customer service here was very surprising. Was here with a group of 20 ppl and requested a game be put on one of two TVs on the roof, one of which was airing the end of a horse race. There were two other small tables on the rooftop, and the bartender insisted someone was watching the already over horse race. After asking the other two tables if they cared (which they didn't), we went and requested them to change it again. They instead changed it to Nascar because the bouncer wanted to watch it. We left shortly after with our deep pockets.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: We came here for a work event and went on a brewery tour and had light bites and drinks. The food was really good! Definitely steps above simple "bar food", as they had a really delicious kale, beet and burrata salad, and wings, tacos, burgers, fries, etc and much more. They also had a couple kombucha options which were delicious for those that don't drink. I would definitely recommend this place for a corporate event, light bites/drinks or even a casual dinner spot. They also had live music!

name: Nashville Symphony
text:
Who doesn't love Christmas movies at Christmas time?
(Husbands who've been subjected to countless hours of Hallmark Channel please lower your hands, we understand) 
So what a brilliant idea it was for the symphony to host an evening viewing of an all time favorite - Home Alone. 
They seamlessly blended the live music directly over the score for the film & blew us away with a choir for the few songs in it.
The only negatives on the night are that the seating isn't what we've all become used to in modern movie theaters & I spent the majority of intermission in line to get a couple of bottles of water & returned to my seat empty handed at the bell with yet a dozen people between me & the bar.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I recently visited here with a group of 6 and shortly after dinner, two members of our group who had eaten the taco salad we're sick to their stomach and spent a large portion of the rest of the night vomiting with food poisoning. Aside from that, we also had serving staff that was less than thrilled to serve us and seemed annoyed by the few minor requests that we had. I am not one to typically leave reviews but being that I often take other's reviews into consideration when choosing a restaurant, I wanted to inform others of our experience. We visited Margaritaville with high hopes but we were certainly let down. With all of the other great places to eat in Nashville, I definitely wouldn't recommend this one!

name: Winners Bar and Grill Nashville
text: A local friend of mine said to meet her and some friends here for Whiskey Jam on Thursday. It looked like a good time so we trekked it this way after dinner. Downstairs was packed for the jam sesh so we didn't actually spend a ton of time down there, but we did hang on the roof for a while. Luckily we snagged a table fairly early and even though it got busy, I could always get a round of drinks without a wait. It was a fun area to bounce around as we went to Losers next and then on to Kung Fu. Fun times on a Thursday night!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I love Margaritaville. The service was great just like at every other Margaritaville. Booze in a Blender is always good.  Live music is great too.

name: The Night Owl
text:
When the BF said he had some high school friends that were playing at The Night Owl, I thought "Where the hell is that?" Then I thought, "Sounds like an adventure!" So we went out there to check it out.

We get there and see a ton of people outside having some smokes. I went on in and had some fun jokes with the bouncer at the door while he was checking my ID. Friendly guy. Then we get us a table as far back as we can. This place isn't as big as I thought it would be, so it wasn't very far back at all and was very smushed in with the other tables. There's a bar area for ordering your drinks and food if there is no waitress. And there is a pool table behind the seating tables.

Turns out this dive is legit! Reasonably priced drinks, friendly bartenders, fun crowd. The bands make it loud as fuck in there but hey, it is a small place, and you kinda came to see the music no? We had the Kitchen Sink wings which are apparently of all the different flavors and I have to admit those things were pretty good (and I usually don't like wings). There's a sliver of floor in front of the band for dancing if you feel like it also. Oh, and they have jello shots for purchase. I mean, that's pretty cool and fun!

Basically this is a cool little dive off the beaten path in a nondescript area of town. Check out some live bands, try the wings, and have a jello shot just for fun!

name: National Underground
text:
So there we were, some local Nashvillians downtown.  (I know... what?)  We were going to eat at ACME, but saw that it was closed.  What's this place next door?  Hmmm... seems interesting.  Then a guy standing outside tells us we should eat there.  The burgers are amazing, he says.  He claims they are the best burgers, voted on by the Nashville Scene (any local will immediately tell you this is false.)  Even though I knew this dude was BS-ing, I thought we'd give it a shot.  He also said he enjoyed it because, "they let me bring my dog and sit outside."  I looked the place up online as we sat down and as it turns out, this dude is the freakin' owner!  Dude, just tell me you own the place.  Don't make up a bunch of lies just to get us in your place.  Just say you own it.  If you don't believe in the quality of your own restaurant in order to give it to me straight, that says quite a bit about your character and your faith in your establishment.  

So we sat down.  Our service was awful.  Our waitress would take half of our order and then leave.  So my food arrived before friends had even ordered even though we were all sitting there.  

They made a big deal over splitting checks as well.

Oh, the food... right.  Decent.  Definitely not the best burger or wings.  Friends enjoyed the hot chicken, but not the best in town.  

I can't recommend a place that tries to deceive people.  Also, the bit at the top of your menu about the tap water being bad?  C'mon.

name: Ole Red
text: We only stopped in for a couple drinks and listen to live band but we only stayed for 1 drink. We went to the bar and where there were only 3 people sitting but we were never greeted by the young brunette bartender. I had to look at her and ask if I could order a beverage where she said , sure what would you like. She got our drinks and 2 of her friends arrived and she proceeded to talk about her boyfriend issues and his travel schedule. Our drinks were empty and she never asked for another drink so we left . I completely respect if they are busy and tending to many patrons but in this case that was not a factor. Atmosphere was a 5* but the service was 1* which makes it a never return for us.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I really loved this place.  Three floors of dining tables, bars, pool tables, with a huge dance floor in the middle. 

Bands play live for an hour or so, with an intermission where they teach line dancing while the band takes a break. 

The food was like TGIFridays...Nashville Style.  BBQ and Fried Pickles were yummm. 

Very touristy, but I loved it.  Would go back multiple times. 

PS look at their event schedule.  While we were there, they were closed more nights than not for a special convention event for Snap On Tools, the filming of the show Nashville, and a concert with paid seating.   We had to coordinate the night so we could go on a night we could get in on a general night.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
I too was lead to Soulshine by Scoutmob's 50% off deal, and my overall opinion was "(shrug), meh" ... 

Our server was great, I was excited to see they had three Fat Bottom brewery selections, and the building itself was pretty cool.  I feel Soulshine's laid back "jam band" vibe is a nice addition to mid-town's stale Vandy bro AND music row pushers scene.  All that being said, the food was pretty unsatisfying.  My girlfriend and I split a bowl of crawfish bisque, small pulled pig nachos, and got two small 8" pizzas (the Bourdeaux and the hamburger pie).  Crawfish bisque tasted like canned cream of mushroom soup with four scant crawfish tails thrown in as a garnish, the nachos were greasy, gooey cheesieness with BBQ sauce and a bit of pork, but were completely uninspiring, and the pizza was the biggest let down.  My girlfriend was excited about the wheat dough option, which along with the MULTIPLE BBQ pie options, I thought were both an insult to the pizza gods.  While I admire their creative effort in adding jerk chicken to a pie and calling it the "Bob Marley", one does not just simply "dazed and confusedly" throw random ingredients on a pie and create a new menu item.  

I will go again, but not to eat.  It will be to escape the douchebaggery of midtown, grab a Fat Bottom Rye Pale Ale and watch some live music.

If you want good pizza, go to Bella Nashville in the farmers market.  Chicken little know pizza.

name: Twin Kegs
text: Average burgers, and cheap beer. Fine if you are looking for that. I had hoped for more based on reviews, but the burgers seemed like frozen patties cooked up.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: For atmosphere for informal music and food venue this place can't be beat. I was surprised to find it on the tourist-Hell strip in Nashville. Great service. And the food was better than expected. I hope to come back to see more artists performing on the big stage. The food is not cheap. The fried baloney sammich was as expected. (Next time I'll ask for whole wheat bread.) The fried pickles were great. The spicy ones ARE spicy. Burgers are just fine. Kale salad was also very good. No idea whether it's worth taking dance lessons, but I will seriously consider it with my GF the next time I'm in town and have time.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: We came here late one night just for a few drinks. We didnt eat at all. We sat on the roof top terrace and listened to the live band. This little experience gives them 4 stars. That terrace is really nice. Its a good place to relax, people watch and listen to music.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
I was in Nashville for a convention and walked down to this place and enjoyed the music and atmosphere. 

My wife had a pulled pork sandwich and I had a pulled pork plate. The beans were great and the BBQ sauce was great also

name: Twin Kegs
text:
Awesome food, try the Spice burger and fried pickle chips yum with cheap beer too!
Great dive bar

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Well, that was a little disappointing. The space is very nice. Unfortunately,  the food and service leave plenty to be desired.  Service was pretty slow. My $9.00 martini, when it finally came, arrived in highball glass. The food was fine-not great or in any way memorable, but fine. I'm really just left with no reason to visit again.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Huge stage & seating area for concerts. Nice little store attached with souvenirs that has very reasonable prices. Only stopped in for an appetizer, which was great, but would come back again. Later at night a line starts to form so there may be a wait. Wouldve been nice to have a larger selection of craft beer. You have to try Line Dancing lessons before you leave!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Soulshine Pizza is a great place to catch live music, have a quality beer, and eat some of the best pizza in Nashville!

Soulshine sponsored my softball league through Nashville Sports Leagues.  My team lost in the championship game, but got a $50 gift card to use.  After getting stiffed on league fees by a couple of players, I had no qualms about taking the my wife to dinner with them.  Ha...

We arrived and drove around the parking lot a couple of times to find a spot.  This is the only negative experience of the night.  The parking is tight.  They do valet, but I think it's $5 to go that route.

When we walked up, the band was going and we were seated downstairs.  The band was upstairs.  That wasn't a bad way to go as we could still hear them and the tv monitors showed them if you wanted to watch.  We could also talk without yelling at each other. 

We both ordered the crawfish soup and it was excellent--very creamy, but not too spicy.  My wife and I then split a medium pizza.  Half was the 5-cheese and half was the Don Vito.  They are cool about doing that if the base sauce is the same.  The Don Vito is fantastic and I'd highly recommend it.  The pizza and crust are really well done--definitely one of the best pies in Nashville.

The beer list wasn't great, but they get high marks for including local brewers.  Yazoo, Blackstone, Fat Bottom, and Jackalope were all on the beer menu.  I tried the Jackalope Red Rompo for the first time last night.  It was very good.  I'd like to see a few more craft selections, but it's still very cool that they provide such a wide variety of local stuff.

Soulshine Pizza is excellent.  The pizza is great and the restaurant provides and awesome environment to enjoy yourself.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Mediocre BBQ but atmosphere was really great.  Loved upstairs and really great cover band.  Exactly what you would expect from a place named Rippy's on Broadway.

name: Nashville Palace
text: We stopped in awhile back and was kinda late but had one of the best chicken Quesadillas I had ever had. That late at night the place was kinda crazy and has a very eclectic crowd there was plenty of entertainment there! Lol

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Came here while in Nashville for a conference. The pizza was delicious. Our waitress was awesome. We would high recommend this for anyone.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
This place looks small from the outside, but is really big on the inside. 

There is not a bad seat in the house. The first floor has low tables in the front, hightop tables in the back, bar seating and a second floor so everyone has a view of the stage. 

There are three bars all conveniently located. The bathrooms are not obvious. I am not sure how the staff and service is as I was there for a very early professional development session.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Saturday, August I 2nd, I worked all day and decided I want to have dinner at an Awesome restaurant and have some great pizza..so I decided on Soulshine....I have never had my daughter here before and I wanted her to have some great food and check out a great building...I love how they remodeled this restaurant..it is an old warehouse style building that has been remodeled and revamped...

I LOVE THE BUILDING..
I LOVE THE DECOR....
I LOVE THIS RESTAURANT...

We got there about 7ish..and we were able to park in their lot. I love the fact that they have a private parking lot in an area near Vandy where it is hard to park anywhere...lol!!!

The place was SO NOISY..but hey its Saturday night and you are in a college area..so YES expect the noise..if you don't want noise...stay home !!!! ((( lol))))
Our waitress I believe was Anita, I really couldn't hear her name very well. I opted to sit upstairs where it seemed to be a little more noiser by the way, but I love that staircase ...so you want to climb them...

We sat ourselves at a high top table for four...We were greeted immediately and gave our drink order..Tony took a PBR, Noel iced tea and myself..Coca Cola...tall and cold please !!!! and keep them coming..!!!

Noel decided on the 8 inch small Shrimp Alfredo and Tony and I opted to share a medium "The Jacksonian" which is a chicken with Alfredo sauce ...so soo sooo good. I had to try Noel's choice also...it was good as well but I am not a sun dried tomato fan...and that ingredient was on hers...

We had a wonderful dinner. Their was sports on all the tvs..the band never played while we were there...I loved this dining experience..we had a nice dinner..

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Disappointment! I've been here dozens of times and hosted many group events here. That was before all of the changes. The new building renovation looks like a New York bar with the horse figures remaining a sad reminder of fun times.  I could have forgiven that if the food was still great. The BBQ beef and chicken thighs were dry and tasteless. Service was terrible, seats too close together. Wish I didn't know how great it used to be.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Should be called Ripoffs! We live in Nashville and happen to be going to a show at Bridgestone Arena. On the way we decided to have a few cocktails and walked into Rippy's. I looked over the menu and first noticed the Bushwhacker (my favorite), I ordered one and was told that the machine was not working. I then asked for a White Russian and again informed that they had no milk, bummer. I took a relook at the menu and ordered the Spray Tan, this drink consists of Tito's Vodka and some other delicious items. As I'm watching the bartender make my drink I noticed that she was pouring Skol Vodka, which is lower grade and from the well. When I asked if the drink was supposed to be made with Tito's she replied "you have to request that"....to that I responded...."but it's on the menu, you mean that even though it says it comes with Tito's on the menu you have to request it???"......she replied "yep". Whatever, I asked for the tab and received a bill for $25.00.....this consisted of two shots (which we did order) and one drink (that wasn't even made as the menu said)......that's pretty steep. I didn't fight it......we paid and left. But I am writing this today because I feel that if they did this to me, they must do it to others. Get an itemized bill and watch what you order!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Fun place to spend the evening! Decent food and drinks and good music! Three levels, so plenty of room to spread out. They've got line dance lessons for people who don't know how to do country.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
We came here for our first honky-tonk experience with the kids. Because we stayed at a Marriott hotel we were able to get in for free on a Thursday night. ($6/ adult cover). 

Large dance floor with lots of seats and bar areas surrounding. 2 stories of views. Large stage. Live music and line dancing lessons. 

We didn't have any food so we can't comment on that.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: My boyfriend and I had dinner here when we stopped in Nashville for an evening. They have live entertainment which was so fun! The server was very nice and attentive. The food was delicious and even though it was busy we got our food within 10 minutes of ordering! Highly recommend!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
TOURIST TRAP!

Went expecting something else.

You know its a TT when they ask you if you want your whiskey and coke in a souvenir glass.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
You come to Rippy's not for the food or music but the upstairs open air patio.  These guys have some of the best views of Broadway Street.  Here you can cool off under the fans and people watch.  

The food is your typical bar food.  Nothing special though not terrible.  They normally have very loud, very average cover bands playing on the patio.  It's nice to hear some okay music and sip some ice cold Hap and Harry's beer in bottles.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Giddee Up! This country bar was rocking on a Friday night when we busted during the 2014 CMA Festival. The energy was fun and upbeat.

There was a country cover band playing on stage, which kept the crowd dancing and singing during our meal.

The bar's service was attentive and we didn't have to wait long to place our food and drink orders.

The BBQ was above average, not the best; but still much better than some other bar establishments.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
I don't know how this place only has a 3 star rating- Great atmosphere- live music without being obnoxiously loud, fantastic service- our bartender was so helpful and patient with us while allowing us to substitute different things, I felt like a pain in the butt, but it was SO worth it!  Boyfriend and I got the sampler with the ribs, pork loin, pulled pork,sausage (with cheese?), macaroni and cheese and "corn cakes" Their pulled pork was amazing! Absolutely fabulous with their sweet bbq sauce! Mac and cheese was delicious and the corn cakes were really good, although a strange concept- corn bread that's like a pancake...?  Tasty, but would've been better as actual cornbread, pancake thickness just felt like something was missing.  I have no idea why they served blocks of cheese to go with the sausage, it didn't really make sense to me.  The ribs were a bit dry for my liking, but I like them dripping with sauce so I think that was just a personal preference. 
We really enjoyed this place and will definitely be going back on our next visit. Hopefully we get the same bartender because she was awesome!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: We just came in for drinks and appetizers while we wait for our concert to start the evening. Great good and nice atmosphere.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Let's just start by agreeing that all of the horses (particularly the ones that are upside down on the ceiling) can be a bit much.  Mostly in a good, fun way, but the ones by the bathrooms are a little weird.  Moving on...

My first experience at Wildhorse was for a concert (Sister Hazel, it was of course fantastic, but that's beside the point).  We had reserved seats, which were not significantly more expensive than GA and very much appreciated.  That night, we didn't eat at Wildhorse, but we did drink.  My only complaint was that you can't get the specialty drinks except for in the "specialty (souvenir) glasses" which makes them way more expensive.  But they're so good.  And to be honest, while I though they were particularly ridiculous at the time, the glasses are actually mason jars and I use them around the kitchen all the time. 

Now, as we're planning our wedding, we've been looking at Wildhorse as the venue for one event that weekend and they've been great to work with so far.  The events staff is responsive and very professional. Today we had a tasting there, and we were all very happy with the quality of the food (and the quantity.  OMG the quantity).

Do check their schedule before you go - while most nights do not, some events require tickets.  I look forward to going back for the line dancing!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Rippy's is as casual of a dining experience as you can get. However, the food tastes good and the service is excellent. My favorite server Melody is as good as they come-ask for her by name.
The live music both upstairs and down is always good. If you're ever in Nashville, make sure to stop by and enjoy.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Awesome! Each time we stopped in (on Friday, on Saturday and on Sunday) this past weekend it felt like home. The CMA Fest was going on so there were an extra 80,000 people running around town, but each day we came in with our group of 6 we were greeted with huge smiles and shout outs from Joni, Liz, Smalls and everyone working the 2nd floor bar. Ice cold beer, great food and awesome people...who wouldn't want to hang out here? See you'll next time for sure!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: It's OK. I went mostly because I had my young son and this was rated "good for kids". The food did not blow me away, however it was a nice atmosphere.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Tony and I went here for lunch today...another Sunday in Nashville...and yes another Pizza Joint...I am on a pizza kick right now...So we opted to try Soulshine Pizza Factory and we were glad we did..

It is located down near Vandy...closer to Vandy than Broadway...but easy to find...gets plenty of food traffic from the University students..It is a two story location. We were greeted and seated immediately on the first floor. Our waiter arrived quickly. Tony ordered a Budweiser Bottle and I ordered a soda...
We looked through the menu..I already knew I wanted pizza..so we ordered "the Kitchen Sink" small and appetizer of Garlic bread and marinara sauce..it arrived very quickly.
Our waiter was very friendly and told us before we leave to go up and check out the upstairs and the outdoor upper level patio where they are sitting up a live band..
We walked up there after we ate...
OMG...I loved it up here...so light bright and airy...definitely going to eat upstairs next time.
I loved the interior..the service and the food..

Everything including tip, taxes food and drink...$24
Not bad..I tipped him 18% for a sunday afternoon party of 2 at noon!!!
Not bad!!!
I will go there again!!!
DEFINITELY!!!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Check your bank statements. I went there last night with party of 7 which were 3 separate checks. He brought them in bifold book so there couldn't have been any confusion. He charged my meal and also charged the other on my account as well as charging them. Whether he voided it or did by accident never mentioned hey I accidentally ran other check but I voided it out. Also you can't just call up to speak to a manager to resolve this. Everything is automated and you can't speak to a live person. Aside from that service sucked took 20 minutes to get drinks everybody's food came out and ours was another 10 mins having ordered the same time due to waiters error. Also phone service inside is terrible but they do have wifi catch is you have to check-in as being there to get access. Go to BB Kings instead better music food price and service.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Food was AMAZING. The pulled pork was so good especially with the sweet BBQ sauce. It melted in my mouth! The service however was AWFUL. The guy was rushing around so much he forgot his customer service skills at home (especially friendliness). The way he asked our table if we were ready to order was "ready? Lets go." I felt like I was inconveniencing him. I always tip 20% but he got what he earned.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: 3 adults 1 child 50.00 which isn't bad for the location and live music. Burgers are huge. My son loved his chicken wrap. My only negative is that they charge over 2.00 for ice tea and serve it in small plastic cups.  We were thirsty and our poor waitress had to work hard to keep our drinks full.  We will go back.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: My mediocre rating is probably more due to my expectations than the venue. I was here on business many years ago. At that time is was very rustic looking with old wooden beams and a "barn dance" kind of atmosphere. Now that my wife and I are visiting the area I couldn't wait to take her back to see what I loved on that visit. Sadly, it isn't here anymore. My wife summed it up best when she said her impression of the decor was "cafeteria". We had a beer ($7) and left. We didn't order any food, so we can't comment on that. The band playing was not great, and wasn't playing any country tunes. Seems like Wildhorse isn't the place to go anymore for country music or a country feel.

name: Twin Kegs
text: I came with a friend for the dive bar experience.  I see hipsters talk about the place which was weird but it was just older southern men there.  We played some shuffleboard while drinking some beer.  We were asked to let others play before our first game was even over.  I don't get the appeal.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Martins food is much better. Ok if u are looking for something on broadway but not the best for BBQ

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Place is crowded and the service is terrible. I tried to order a beer 4 times and the server was gone before I would get a chance to tell her what I wanted. The food is a joke, their pulled pork was dry, coleslaw was dry, and their baked beans tastes like Busch's baked beans... I wouldn't recommend this place.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
It's a great place to meet a friend, good trivia night, pretty good pizza, but the thing that stands out to me is the customer service. 

I had left my credit card at a nearby bar the night before and casually mentioned it to the bartender John. Without missing a beat, he called the nearby bar, walked over, and personally picked it up. 

I was really touched by this and will be coming back for sure. Also hope the owner Chris reads this because John js the kind of guy I'd want to manage my restaurant.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: Very nice venue to see a show. If I lived in Nashville (or even close by) I would be spending a lot more time there watching shows!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Great drink selection. The pizza is quite delicious, but the other few dishes I've had were meh. Overall a great happy hour place for friends!

name: Twin Kegs
text: Beers and burgers. Nice location and away from the "trendy" tourist traps that plague this city. They even have a nice pinball machine! Might make it a favorite place to unwind.

name: Twin Kegs
text:
We were excited to try out our neighborhood dive bar, and I liked it, but I don't think it'll become a regular spot for us! 

The good? Classic dive bar. Shuffle board. Couple of small TVs - but not a full on sports bar with TVs everywhere! They were playing great music while we were there. Great drink specials during Happy Hour ($7/8 pitchers of PBR). They have karaoke and trivia (depending on the night). Beers on tap and canned/bottled. (I had a pint of Bombshell Blonde, and my fiance had a Black Abbey draft beer.) They also have food (we didn't try any on our visit visit)!

The not so good? SMOKY. Just learned that you can still smoke inside bars in Nashville (just moved here from Texas). I'm pretty headache-prone when stuck in a smoky room, so this is the main reason that Twin Kegs isn't going to be our normal spot. Too bad! 

A cool spot - but we probably won't be regulars!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great food, prices, and live music. The smoked pulled pork sandwich is to die for. The service left something to be desired though.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Talk about a country-filled night! Came here on a Friday night and danced my cowboy boots off learning how to line-dance. The energy was palpable, the range of skill-set was noticeable, and the music was blaring. It was just a really fun experience honestly! 

They also have an arcade/game area upstairs. This part was pretty empty when I went, but the bottom floor was packed with people who had ordered food and drinks. I didn't get a chance to try their food, so I can only speak about the general entertainment atmosphere, which I found to be promising.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Went to the wild horse tonight for the 80's dance party to end Alz and was incredibly disappointed by the lack of response or interest of the serving staff in our section of the 2nd floor.  We ended up going to the bar to order our first round of drinks and food. When I asked one server if she had our table she said no but she would get our server. Never saw her.. then when she did get close enough to me, I tapped her on her shoulder. She spun around and very rudely told me not to touch her.. seriously??? I was trying to get her attention so we could get some service... her name was Mercedes. Stay clear of her if you visit there.  Her unprofessionalism definitely put a damper on the evening. Our previous visit the day before was pleasant, the place is very clean.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
The music -- by Nathan Belt and the Buckles  -- was really great, very versatile and talented musicians. They played a nice mix of traditional country, rock and roll oldies, and very little contemporary.  I liked how they chose songs to spotlight the various band members  (guitarist,  pianist,  drummer) I was REALLY surprised to hear they play only for tips. Wow, the competition must be stiffer in Nashville,  because they could have had a paying gig elsewhere I'm sure. There's not much of a dance floor, but a few couples made do with space available. 

We'd checked out the menu beforehand so knew what to expect (mostly bar food with a couple home cookin' dishes). The Longhorn salad was surprisingly good (who orders salad at a honky-tonk bar, right?) -- steak done perfectly  and a nice variety of fresh greens.  Dixie chicken portion was huge.  Onion rings were ok, a little cold.
Now as to the service ... it was a Saturday night, but it was easy to find a table in the restaurant where the band was playing.  Our server, Brittany, greeted us right away,  but it was 5 minutes  before she was able to take our drink order. She was friendly and professional, though,  came back right away and took our food order. About 20 minutes later, she came over to explain that there was an event in the theater area, and the kitchen was swamped with orders, but she would check on the order. About 10 minutes later, she came back and said the kitchen was still swamped but she would talk to the manager about how long the food was taking (40 minutes by then).  We asked for some pretzels or nuts (it was 8:30 and one of us hadn't eaten since lunch), and she brought us some chips and said she was personally going to track down the order. About 5 minutes later, the manager (Tara?) came over with an order of chicken tenders and said that somehow, in the big stack of orders, the kitchen had lost ours. She apologized and said the food was being prepared now. She comped the tenders, the chips, and another beer. Brittany came back to refill drinks and apologized again.  The food came shortly thereafter. 
So here's the thing  -- mistakes happen,  orders get lost, especially when its really busy. But when the server and manager explain what happened,  apologize,  and try to make it right, what more can you expect? They took the time to talk to us personally,  it was clear they cared. So kudos to them for that. And hey. we had great music to entertain us while we waited.  I'd  recommend this place,  but maybe suggest timing your visit for a less hectic time.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: Alway have a great time coming here. Tonight's show Kinky Boots has been awesome so far can't wait for act two.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Wonderful food for the price!  The ribs were so good, they really didn't require a sauce, and the pulled pork was so tender.  The side room of the joint could be better cooled down in the hot months.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Had a decent time here. Really it was our only choice since we had my 18 year old cousin with us and it was the only place that allowed under 21 since they are a restaurant. 

There was a decent band playing and we ordered some drinks. The food looked okayish and none of us where too hungry so we decided to opt out. We got one appetizer of beans with some tortillas that was pretty good. I ordered a mixed drink and it tasted like a bunch of juice and no alcohol. Overall all we had a decent time.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Good food and line dance lessons.  Yes touristy, but clean and brighter than most of the other venues in the music row area.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good for a quick bite. I split a pulled pork sandwich and onion rings with a friend. They were good and just enough food before the evening festivities. My friends got ribs. They were dry but again way better than I expected for bar food. And there were a lot of ribs to share!

name: Nashville Palace
text: Music was fantastic and entertaining. I wish it didn't take over 2 hours and our waitress continually telling us our food will be right out.  Needless to say we never did get to eat here since after 2 hours we had to cancel our order in order to make it to the Grand Ole Opry before the show started.  I would not try eating here unless you are only coming for the music.  Our beer came out quick and was cold.  If it wasn't for the music, I would have rated it a 1 star.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Took a group here to experience some "Nashville" scenery...the cover charge of $6 is totally ridiculous. We waited at the bar on the right side of the stage and it took for ever to get a drink from the pissed of bar tender behind the bar, and drinks are very expensive here. The band was great though and the women's bathroom was fabulous! I've never been to a bar that busy and had such a clean restroom.

name: Big Machine Brewery & Distillery
text:
Great spot to slip in and have a drink. 
Wait staff is always busy and rude. 
I have been twice now once they weren't so busy same service and attitudes. 

Frozen lemonade is delicious, but not as delicious as the whiskey mule.

Opted for a plastic cup so I didn't have to leave my ID it took long enough to get a drink. 

Great spot, but don't be in a hurry and prepped for a rude attitude! Cheers.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Excellent place to come to eat, drink and have a very good time, do not forget to try the French toasts are from beyond and the chicken fried chicken ... OMG
Excelente lugar para venir a comer, tomar y tener un muy buen tiempo, no dejen de probar las tostadas Francesas son del mas allá y el pollo frito pollo...OMG

name: Nashville Palace
text:
I had zero idea of this place's existence until my friend drug me here for some dancing. What initially was going to be a night of two-step (no idea what that is) turned out to be a night of swing dancing to rock-a-billy. My friend was a bit disappointed, but nonetheless, I full embraced it as I love east coast swing dancing. I do it frequently as my time allows it. 

There are two different stages. One when you first enter the establishment and another one in the back of the establishment. One this particular evening, they had rock-a-billy on both stages. This is greatly due to a convention going on at the Opryland Hotel Resort located near the Nashville Palace. I am not sure if my friend researched this before our outing. Regardless, we all enjoyed the music. 

My friend had a visitor in town whom she had danced with for years. They were basically professionals. Despite the music, they made a point to show off their expertise on the dance floor. Spectators applauded them once they finished one of the dances since the band was still warming up, but still played what I would consider a danceable song. He was flipping her around and on the floor; it was purely amazing! 

He later danced with me and showed off his moves.  I feel like I can't dance well unless I have a strong lead, and he was a great lead. It was very apparent that he and I were used to different dancing styles.

My friends ended up getting drinks and enjoyed what they got. I am not sure what the costs were, but I took a sip of my friend's cosmo, and it was tasty. There was no table service, but instead, they went up to the bar and got their drinks. 

The place is extremely spacious. We were in the back with a full-on dance floor with a stage for the band and plenty of room for standing and sitting to watch the band if you didn't wish to dance. It is also great for people watching. People were dressed up in full attire for the dance. Think, Dukes of Hazard prom attire meets Nashville Palace. It was definitely different from anything I had ever seen. 

I would definitely come back. We didn't pay a cover to get in and to be able to watch live bands without charge is always a plus in my book. Plus, after finding out that this place is so legendary gives me just that much more incentive to check it out again soon.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Went in tonight and sat at the bar. The bartender acknowledged everyone around me, some twice and just ignored me. We made eye contact and he turned away and asked the folks around me if they were ok. I wonder why???

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Rippys was awesome! Only reason I can't give it a 5 star review is because they didn't have options to do things like 1/2 chicken and ribs. You can only choose one meat for a dinner plate. The ribs were delicious and everything is finger licking great! The ambiance, decor, vibe, and live music made you feel like a local. The best part of my Rippys experience was the impeccable service! Melody is a rockstar! She gave me a birthday shot, also showed and took a pic of her lipstick for my friend because she was curious of the color she was wearing! We all joked with a group chant, 'maybe it's maybeline.' And it was! Oh.. She also found the time to get our drinks and food at just the right time. Melody you're awesome and congrats on the engagement! Her fiancé is an actual rockstar! So stop by, ask for her, and then go see her fiancé play! Rippys BBQ. Nashville at its best!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Good food, awesome atmospher. 
Very expensive, probably not for everyone. It will have to be an occasion

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Absolutely the most wonderful time. This place is hip AF! Great food, drinks, and atmosphere! Truly a "not so hidden dream"! We loved all the celebrities we saw there (and we even met a few!) On a scale of 1-10 this place is a 100! Cannot wait to come back!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The WORST bar I have ever been to in my life. I am TWENTY-THREE years old and they denied because they thought my ID was fake. I had a 2nd, 3rd, and 4th form of ID and they still would not let me in. The African American security guard even threatened my boyfriend for saying to call the police to verify. REALLY classy Rippy's. ARE YOU KIDDING ME?! Actually, thank you, because I would not want to spend a dime at this place. Came from Legend's across the street and wish I would have stayed there. Also, have fun being reported to the Better Business Bureau! Yes, I'm from Indiana, and you best bet I know the laws!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: I ordered the breakfast Mac and they didn't tell me that they were out until they served everyone else at the table their breakfast. Others at my table had biscuits and gravy and they didn't bring the biscuits until 10 minutes later. They forgot the syrup for my mother in laws pancakes. Had to wait 5 more minutes for that. Hash browns were served cold, eggs were supposed to be over medium and they were runny. Coffee was full of coffee grounds. Very disappointed on our first Nashville breakfast.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This is the worst place I have ever been. The service was horrible and the food tasted like it was a day old and microwaved. The fries were stale, the pork was old, the brisket smelled foul and the wings were ice cold when brought to the table. Don't even get me started on their drinks. I got a margarita and it was watered down. If I wanted to pay $16 for water I would have stayed at home. On top of all the horrible food our server came over to the table at the end and had the nerve to speak back to me about the tip I had left her. I explained to her that the food was horrible and she rudely answered me and said she had never had any complaints rolled her eyes and walked away. I don't recommend this place to anyone visiting Nashville and they definitely left a sour taste in my mouth for this city.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Huge restaurant with large garage doors that can be opened for an open air feel. There is a large stage one end opposite the large bar area for musical guests to sing. While we had dinner there was an acoustic singer performing which was nice during dinner. It sounded like they had a line up all night of 3-4 different people.

We ordered the queso as an app. Queso was ok... I pretend to know cheese, but I know liquid cheese and this queso wasn't top notch but never the less we still ate it and enjoyed the chips that came with it. 

For meals we had a Nash burger, meatloaf and salmon dishes. All were actually surprising good! My burger was amazing, although I wish they would have asked how I liked it cooked instead of well done. 

The reason I gave a 4 was because our server wasn't super friendly and because they use iPods or something electronic in their hand to order food electronically it seems a little weird when you are ordering and they are busy typing in stuff rather than making eye contact, etc. He did recommend the meatloaf though, which my mom loves... so good job!

Overall, I think I will definitely come back with friends or family especially if we're going to A concert at the Bridgestone! The location can't be beat!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Passing by we were looking for a place to eat and we came across Wildhorse Saloon. The place was AWESOME!!! Very cool atmosphere, great entertainment and customer service. The food was pretty good. In my opinion a little too pricey for what you get. I got a house salad added grilled chicken. The chicken was 3 bucks extra and it was cold. Kind of confusing. However, he had the brunch burger and LOVED it. For an app we had fried pickles and they were A M A Z I N G!!!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
I think NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon is alright. It's very close to my Nashville office, so I have visited for lunch while there. I haven't been blown away by any part of the experience, but it's convenient, and not terrible, so it's likely I'll be back. 

On my most recent visit with a co-worker we opted to sit outside, because the weather was nice. Perhaps it's due to the fact that we were outside, but our service wasn't great. The restaurant definitely wasn't busy during our visit, so this was a bit frustrating. Our table was also very lopsided, and though we pointed this out we weren't given the option to move, though we were the only two people sitting outside. 

I ordered a Coke and opted for the Grilled Catfish Tacos, which were served with pickled vegetables, white bbq sauce, and avocado, and they came with a side of fries. The food was pretty good, but it wasn't anything special. I struggled getting my drink refilled, which goes back to the service issues we were experiencing. 

Overall, I'd say if you're in the area and looking for a lunch or dinner spot, I think there are likely better options around than NashHouse.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Great ambience, service and food! I went during lunch with a coworker. The server was awesome and gave us a quick run down of the menu. We both ordered the grilled catfish tacos. It's included two tacos with grilled catfish, pickled vegetables, white bbq sauce, avocados and of course french fries. I never had grilled catfish tacos before but it was love at first bite. You definitely want to go and get those amazing tacos!!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
We love to come here on Fridays for happy hour. They have lighting 100 come in and broadcast live and they have trivia and fun games with great prizes. They also have half hour apps and draft beer until 6.  
The food is good, and they have an Ok draft list. 
We have a blast playing games and winning prizes!

One complaint I have is that every single time we've been here, we've had to get up to track down our waiter to pay our tab. Once the radio station event is over, the waiters seem to completely disappear-sometimes for a solid 30 minutes. It is so frustrating. We've even tried closing our tab early to avoid the rush at the end of event, but even that didn't help. I think a lot of it has to do with the splitting of checks with big groups. I'd recommend the waiters talk to the group at the beginning of the evening and asking how they want to handle to check so at the end it can go much smoother. 

Other than that, we love it here and will continue to come back!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Went to watch the Mayweather v. McGregor fight last night. Watched a brown guy get kicked out. All my brothers should frequent this establishment. They are down with the cause.
#BlueLivesMatter

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
The restaurant is at a decent location, and the environment is pretty chill but the food is subpar. Did not meet my expectations of Nashville barbecue at all.

Choices:
Beignets
BBQ brisket sandwich
BBQ pork plate
BBQ sauce is clumpy, would've rather had generic brand

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Had a great time at the Wild Horse!  Oscar behind the bar was awesome!   He made sure all our girls had a drink and laughs!   Highly recommend going to!!

name: Twin Kegs
text: (Almost) lifetime resident. Best burger I've had in Nashville, hands down. And it's consistently on the highest level every single time I go.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
My girlfriend and I came to Nashville for a weekend getaway, and we happened to come across the Wildhorse Saloon while walking through the city. It's a huge place with 3 levels and plenty of seating. The stage area was impressive. It's a great place to watch a show and most of the patrons seemed to enjoy the line dancing. 

But this place gets a 1-star from me because I'm convinced that it's just a fancy tourist trap. The food and drinks were horrendous. I ordered the fried chicken with a side of baked beans and mac and cheese, while my girlfriend ordered smoked sausages and BBQ chicken. Our food was out in less than 5 minutes. The food seemed like they went to a local grocery store deli. It was all lukewarm, bland, and dry. The baked beans came out barely warm. The mac and cheese tasted like it came from a Kraft box. I tried their apple brown betty. They took pieces of generic sliced bread, and put baked apples over it with a small scoop of whipped cream. There were also no raisins in it at all like it said on the menu. It was pretty awful and I couldn't finish it.

This place is a scam. The prices are way too expensive for the quality of the food we received. Thankfully we got there just before they started the $6 cover charge. Stay far away from this place if you're just looking for a place to eat. There are much better and cheaper options.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Nice new place. Good stage for live music. Got a table right away but the service was lacking. Chicken was decent but not $22/chicken. Out of very common bottled beers .  PA is could come down 15db . Mix for the room not the packed house it was not.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Bartender is the most bad ass bartender I ever met! She made our whole experience! Shout out to Elle for giving us the best time at the bar! It was so busy because of first Georgia game and she was able to give everyone the attention they needed!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Atmosphere was great, our seat was next to opened French doors on second floor, so was able to watch was going out side. 
   Food was excellent, and portions were very large, more than enough. Service was good, it was packed, but the server was great. 
    Great time, and will eat there again!!!

name: Nashville Palace
text: Great Saloon atmosphere. The waitstaff is extremely friendly and a pleasure. The music is fantastic without being overbearing

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: So, I feel compelled to give a shout out here for customer service, kindness and of course, great shows. My family and I buy 4-5 shows per season had a little mix up with one of the shows, and when you're talking 7 seats, that's a good deal of coin, suffice to say, the Senior Manager Akil Lyle absolutely made right, the wrong and...was a total doll about it. Highly recommend taking your kids/young people to a live show, TPAC has something for everyone and, they truly DO care about you and want you to enjoy the show. BEST customer care I have ever received.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Watch the band Two Way Crossing. Great show bar. Large dance floor, great food good prices. Will definitely come back! Pictures aren't the best because of lighting.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Do not waste your hard-earned money on their dinner show.  The food was NOT worth the high ticket price.  The show was mediocre in variety and quite frankly, monotonous and boring.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: The best thing Tpac has to offer is the staff. They are wonderful. However, the broadway group for Phantom couldn't beat the staff. Christine was nasal, didn't mesh with the phantom understudy. And his acting was sub par. The opera house owners were great and showed a great relationship of work. Carlotta stole the show with the best voicwhich created an odd experience. People need to understand broadway isn't the be all end all. It's the beginning.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Rippy's is a RIP-OFF!! Their regular drink was in like a 6oz plastic cup for $10! Ordered a double and on my bill it was freakin $21 unreal !  They should pay their bands to play if they are charging prices like this.  We talked to other visitors from London that were also disgusted with their food and drink prices.  They had a great band( Mantzel bros from WI).  Next time we come we will order water.  Too bad you can't  be a decent and reasonable establishment. You shoukd chance your name to " Rippy's you off".

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Not bad for a breakfast place for a hotel in the downtown of a metropolitan city.  Either you get a free continental breakfast or overpriced.  No free continental breakfast at the Cambria and thus my review.  The service was excellent. Coffee bitter, portions very small.  Again standard downtown practice for most areas. Not bad, but not a destination breakfast

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: My college experience in Nashville would not have been the same without this place. It's not the cheapest bar on Broadway but it has the best music and the best energy. Must visit if you're in town!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great dance floor and music but good luck getting a drink. I've been here 45 minutes and tried to get a drink from 2 separate bartenders to no avail. Completely ridiculous at this point.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Stayed at the dining area, less noisy but still could listen to the band. Pulled Pork (that comes either w/ salad and/or sandwich) is delicious. Side fries are very good too. Good selection of local brews. We liked the place and food.
Ps. I came with my wife and 6 years old daughter.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
A unique venue with a fun atmosphere and plenty of country music vibes. Place is HUGE - has three levels that are accessible - and on peak nights can get completely packed out. So with that mind, there is sometimes a bit of a wait to get food or drinks. Has an upper billiards level and bars on each level. 

I would recommend going on a night when they are teaching a line dance or any night with live music. Food and drinks can be a bit pricey, but it is in the tourist trap area of downtown, so this is expected. Be sure to stop in and take a look at the great decor if you have never been inside.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Good food and good local bands, need I say more.  If you want to feel like a local come on in and have a beer and live music. Service is great too!  Wife had a Malibu pineapple that was awesome. I had a Yazoo Hopry  Hazy IPA. man was it good, and by it I mean 3 or 4 :).

Pro
Locals hangout
Good music
Good beer
Good food

Cons
None at all. Great place!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Fantastic service!! Friendly staff and great local music! Local talent is awesome! Pork was tender and delicious! Beer selection was delicious and recommended by Raegan, thank you for your recommendation and wonderful service!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Four stars for the second floor, open air space. I'm glad that the bottom level was all full, because it was definitely better to be upstairs with the freeze, over looking Broadway street, and there is still live music. I can't comment on the food because all I got was a corndog and fries, but it seems like pretty typical stuff.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: I was there after lunch and the restaurant was absolutely empty. Despite being the only one there for lunch it took forever for a waiter to come to my table. The waiter was not helpful with suggestions, so I ordered an IPA and Shrimp & Grits. The overpriced shrimp & grits were awfull. The shrimp was overcooked and sauce was way too overpowering. I like strong flavors but this tasted like someone spilled the black pepper into the sauce by accident.  Terrible.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Service was good.  Decor was very cool country Nashville Vibe.  Service was good.  Food was good, we had burgers and they were very flavorful.  I would have eat there again.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We visited the Nash House twice while we were in Nashville.  The food was amazing.  The desserts are over the top.  The Nash pie is to die for~ it's a must try.  Live music and an incredible staff is a reflection of Andy, the front of the house manager, style.  This is a must visit while you are in Nashville.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: At Wildhorse Saloon for free beer and hot wings live at night. Seats couldn't have a much more obstructed view. Can see maybe half the stage. Buddy has a view of the sign. Seats 1 and 2 suck.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This bar is far from a "lounge" this is a hopin' hustlin' 4 level rodeo bar with fantastic live music on every floor. The top floor had the best music all day long- it's a staple to go visit if you come to Nashville! The beer is cold and people are tourists but very friendly and fun! 

Also the roof top looks over the entire strip which is totally awesome! Grab your cowboy boots and friends and ride on in to this fun place!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Good time for a Thursday! Came in after a bus ride into the city. Mi Madre found this place looking up late night eats in the area. The band was JAMMING! The prices gave Chicago a run for the money. $3.50 for a PBR & too damn much for a Miller Lite.

The patty melt was good, but the fries were definitely freaky-fried

Also, never seen a bathroom attendant in a dive bar before.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: I really liked this place as an out-of-towner visiting Nashville's strip. It was laid back with a good band. There were skee ball and basketball to play with friends, ample space to weave in and out of people, unusual decor (trailer park theme) and the people seemed to low-key.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Not only does the place a great music and food, it is a really cool atmosphere. A must stop. I had the potroast with mashed potatoes. Awesome. My wife had corn cakes, eggs and jalepeno bacon. So good. My son and I sampled the hot sauces. Eachwas unique and very good. Service was top notch.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Found out about this place through a co-worker. Said they had good food and a nice atmosphere. I checked it out with my fiance' this Memorial Day since we were off. We went around brunch so it was pretty much empty. Waited probably 15-20 minutes before a waiter approached us so that sucked. Finally ordered and the food was good. I had the smoked brisket tacos which are filled with flavor and heat. My fiance had the BIG Ole BLT that was loaded with bacon. We both enjoyed the food but service was really lacking.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Paradise Park lives up to its name when it's 2:30 A.M., you're hammered, and need something good and greasy to soak it up.

This trailer park themed bar and grill has a lot of charm, happy vibes, beer, booze, and greasy food. I stumbled in and immediately wanted to take on "Big Al's Challenge" which consists of eating a "Big Al Burger" featuring five beef patties and five slabs of cheese with a side of chili cheese fries or tots. 'Merica! F*ck yeah!

I'm about 6' and 190 pounds of pure salt, sugar, and general apathy. As I was about to order I turned to the side and noticed a man in overalls waiting for his order. This man was shorter than me, but easily was pushing 380 to 400 pounds. He was truly twice my size. And then it hit me. Ding! Ding! Ding!

(Drunken) Archie: Are you Big Al?

(Very) Large Man: Yes. That's me.

(Drunken) Archie: They named a challenge after you. That's so cool!

Big Al: Did it once. Never again, kid.

(Drunken) Archie: I am going to try it. And I am going to add bacon.

Big Al: C'mon, kid. Have fun in Nashville. Don't hurt yourself.

The way he looked at me with concern you'd think I was attempting to ride a tricycle off a cliff or something. But it made me change my order to a simple bacon cheeseburger with a side of chili cheese tots. Hit the spot. And I couldn't finish. I tapped out with a few bites to go. The "Big Al's Challenge" would have destroyed me.

Thank you to Paradise Park for (almost) sobering me up. And an extra special thank you to Big Al for saving me from potential internal injuries, obesity, diabetes, and heart disease. 'Merica! F*ck yeah!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Tom Morales restaurants always do well in Nashville. I think they are the most popular ones. I always like the atmospheres, and generally like the food. The same can be said here. I love what they've done trying to preserve the historicalness of the site with photos from sit-ins and reconstruction of the old diner feel. Good food too. But nothing unique enough to grab a fifth star.

I would go back. This will be a good place to bring Nashville visitors for lunch, or brunch. A space where children are welcome, but you can also grab a decent cocktail.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Great place to go to if you want a live band certain nights. Food is good. The setting is great as they have a upstairs and downstairs bar. Check the downstairs out.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: In town for work we stopped in and got an amazing show, good drinks and an amazing crowd! Well worth the trip! It was so packed we couldn't get past the first 6 feet of the bar, but that meant we were right by the stage the whole time. It was super fun and I wish I could have had more time to explore all the pictures on the wall and the rest of the bar. It looked awesome.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
By far my favorite spot on Broadway. The interior is set to look like a trailer park, setting the stage for a divey end-of-the night beer (or three), with a side of fireball and (of course) live country music. 

Stand on the elevated stage across from the performance stage at  2 am and watch dramatic fights break out between drunk southern bells. 

Laugh as you try to lift your feet from the sticky floors and reminisce about your favorite frat parties from back in the day.

Buy a corn dog from the food window, or walk next door to the restaurant for some sit-down service. 

Play Big Buck. Play Pac Man. 

Buy a personal pitcher of beer for less than a New York City pint and relish in all that is Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Fun bar for live music. 3 levels and 3 different stages with different music. A little bit for all tastes.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Very weird themed bar. Artificial grass on the ground. It was our last stop for the night, it was basically empty besides a few others that wandered in & out. The band played for a virtually empty place. They took requests which the two older ladies sitting next to me took advantage of. There was a checkered-floored hallway that led off the another section of the bar, I'm assuming the kitchen or somewhere to order food, decided not to take a stroll down it. 
Positive- They do have a good selection of draft beers.

name: Tin Roof
text: Tin roof has very consistent quality and very good food. The salads are very well cared for, not just a bunch of iceberg thrown on a plate. The quesadilla's are amazing. Good bar, too. I very much appreciate the consistency of the food.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
We went to see the show on Wednesday December 27th .We waited outside starting at 3 o'clock for the 5 o'clock show ,the temperature was about 30°, and we still BARELY made the cutoff for the 12 seats they have available that aren't reserved.The show was GREAT we had to order from the bar, I ordered the catfish and chips which was pretty damn awesome . The atmosphere was that of a very small bar with good service and the show was absolutely FANTASTIC ! 
We heard : Neal Carpenter, Dylan Altman , Kate Bowen and Austin jenkes .
I must say Dylan Altman was AMAZING !! 
I recommend going at LEAST 2 hours prior to make sure you get a seat . After all we were there at 3:00 and we were number 8 and 9 of 12.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: When in Nashville...I had to check out the Bluebird Cafe.   Went to the early show on a weekday.  Good thing, as I was a few minutes late.  Only several pew seats were still available.  No cover, but a $10 minimum for drinks/food.  Show had 4 singers in a round robin format.  The unplugged format is great!  Less than 40 feet at most from the stage, listening to music this way is so intimate & powerful!  The audience was very supportive and  respectful of the musicians.  Nary a sidebar conversation or cell phones during the performance.  Highly recommend, and I can't wait to go back!  Might need to try a 9 pm show w/cover next time!  The highlight of my Ft Campbell/Nashville trip!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Wonderful little restaurant/bar/music venue.

When my friends in Nashville asked where our group was going and I mentioned The Stone Fox they all remarked on how isn't that the place on the West side?  Which is true.  The Stone Fox might be something that you would expect to see over near The Pharmacy but rather is on the other side of town near...nothing.  It's in a residential area.  In fact, The Stone Fox is made from an old house.

The beauty of this is the benefit of the porches.  In addition, the inside has a very homey feel to it, like the front room that has small lighting and large antique maps covering the walls.  The food is a delight, with their late night menu serving healthy apps like the kale and onion hummus pizza (gluten free).  

I would go so far as to say that this place is a hidden gem.  Because it is still newer and in a non-commercialized part of town not very many people have heard about it or been to it yet, meaning you can slip into it on a late evening and catch a really amazing live show on their inside small stage and eat really tasty, healthy food or just shoot the shit on the porch area with friends (back porch is bigger).  The night we went there was a really great 2 piece band from Mississippi playing.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
It was a cold, cold night during the Songwriter's Festival and I had the pleasure of claiming a barstool at the bar, the night Tom T. Hall performed.
The room was completely filled, not a seat to be had.
Dixie, Tom's wife sat at the table, in front of me.
He performed, he told stories, he interacted with the audience for 2 hours.
It was magical.
After his show, the place emptied out and I sat at the bar, just taking it all in.
The aesthetics, the ambiance, the sound...  I was sitting in a pretty famous place...

And then something magical happened.
Mr. Hall came over to me, took both my hands, looked into my eyes and thanked me for coming out in such awful weather.
Dixie, his wife turned around to see who he was talking to, and she flashed me a great big southern smile and thanked me, as well....
I thanked him for coming out in the awful weather, as well....
And then we all walked out together, him holding his wife's hand.
We said goodbye and then I drove off and never felt so amazing, like I did that evening.....

This is truly a fun, magical, historical place to go to at least once, while you're visiting Nashville. You never know who will be in the audience, with you.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Came in one afternoon for a quick bite- sat in the mezzanine and had the best sandwich. Squash fritter poboy that I wish i could eat almost everyday. 
Boone was a great bartender. Attentive but not too much in your face. 
Keep it up

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
I had the Polska here, was really good topped with sautéed onions and peppers an mustard. The portion size was pretty big which I liked the kielbasa was longer than the roll which was nice I prefer that ratio opposed to shorter. It came with fries which were ok just fries. 

The service was good did not have to wait to be helped and the food came out fast. Of course there was live music for lunch which was great.

I also came back at night and realized they have a stage on the second floor as well and both stages were playing live music. I got a apple pie shine shot it was really good but I don't know how much was actually alcohol haha that was $7. Te bar tenders were super attentive and always made sure all the customers were helped. 

The night music was fun the band was large and some members were on the stage while one or two would be on the bar counter, it was a fun environment and every night they were packed!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Tried the chicken and waffles today for brunch. Amazing decision! The bourbon syrup really topped it. New favorite brunch spot. Also tried the sangria - it was ok. Should have stuck with bottomless mimosas.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Fun, fun, fun... Walked into this dive local bar on a Thursday night band was , upstairs band was good made it up to the third-floor, band was great and saxophone player was standing on the bar blowing his horn!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
If you are from out of town and want some fun but to avoid the downtown craziness this is your place. Outstanding food , great service and real good local bands. This is a good taste of Nashville. I love the whole vibe and down stairs there are Billards in the place next door. some real fun.
p.s. That is the best club I have ever had.
The sweet potatoe hummus is ridiculously good as well.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: First place we ate out at during our stay in Nashville. Located on Broadway so it was right in the heart of all the action. There was live music and we got to sit on their rooftop patio. Beautiful views, typical bar food, great vibe!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
A shining star in Nashville. French philosopher Henri Bergson's principle of duration explains how once we acknowledge the greatness of something, we kill it. The Stone Fox makes me think of this, because I am a bit weary of praising the sweetness that is The Stone Fox lest I jinx it. It's one of those things you hope never changes, but you can't help but fear that something--some outside force or something internal--will cause it to lose that spark. This place has amazing shows, fantastic food and drinks, incredible decor (lots of maps; you won't be able to miss it, but make sure to take a look at the huge mural map of the United States on the back wall) and accommodating staff. It wonderfully meshes a classy restaurant with a grungy bar-house. It's a place you can take your grandparents to (Monday nights: Bingo!) and also your party-prone friends. William Tyler, an amazing local musician, owns the place along with his sister. This must be how they book so many incredible musicians. I can't stress enough how much I enjoy their lineups. It never disappoints. The only thing that I don't like about The Stone Fox is that it's so far away from my house. 


Also, when you see the staff and the people who frequent this place, you'll know it's called The Stone Fox for a reason. Wowza!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Loved the upstairs outdoor deck area! Very nice and fun to have a few drinks.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Occasionally there is a decent singer/songwriter on the first floor, but overall the place is a dump and full of tourists that don't know any better.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: A must-go in downtown Nashville.  Super cool atmosphere you just know there is so much country music history made here. Their Apple Shine specialty shot tastes like apple flavored goldschlager.

name: The Stone Fox
text: The best brunch in town.  The owners, Elise and William Tyler, are real locals who put a lot of time and energy into their food and welcome EVERYONE.  This tends to be a musicians hangout.  Great front porch and the back patio is the place to be during nice weather.  Their annual  Pardi Gras Crawfish Boil, in February, is the most fun I've had in a long time.  They know how to do it right!!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: After flying into town I stopped into Tootsie's at 10:30am on a Saturday for the first time. It was a great experience and introduction to Nashville! The bar decor of old photographs was really unique and gave it a dive bar feel. The place was surprisingly busy that early in the morning and the audience was a loud fun crowd that would request songs and sing along with the band. The band playing wore cowboy outfits and had a great sound. I didn't realize until after I left that there was a different band playing on the next level of the bar. I will definitely be going back to Tootsie's before I leave town!

name: Riverfront Park
text: We were in town for a weekend and thought this would be one of the places we should see since Nashville is also a river town.  Meh...I've seen better.  The Cumberland River itself is not very wide.  That LP field is just so hard to miss.  It is really not a pretty sight unless you are a Titans fan.  The park itself is not big.  There is not much open grassy area.  We saw a group of squatters or drifters congregating under one of the few shaded areas in the park.  The riverbank was unkempt and growing wild with tall weeds.  If you are on Broadway, I guess you should make a short stop around the corner to see the park.  But there is no need to make a special trip to the riverfront.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Been here several times for drinks, dinner, and Sunday brunch.  Everything has been really good.  The menu changes up enough to keep it interesting and fresh.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: My husband and I went with our three kids ages 8-14 on a Saturday night. We all loved it. The music was great. The staff was pleasant and the food was fine. Would go back for sure.  The kids got a little restless toward the end but behaved nicely.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
The menu is WAY over priced for what you get as an overall experience including food quality. The service was awesome, attentive, timely and she was a nice girl. After looking at the menu and history of the restaurant online, I was completely thrown off when we sat down. 
Example: Brussels sprout appetizer was $8, $3 to add (what we got was) 1/2 oz of bacon with approximately 6 Brussels sprouts cut in half. 
Probably won't return.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great, fun atmosphere with great bands, and a free cover!  Drinks were average priced for the Broadway area.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
I'm all about shopping local when I can and I use to go to The Well a lot.  Wifi is fast and I like the random furniture.  They have lots of local items for sale which is neat, coffee is decent and the local pastries are good.  The sandwiches are pretty poo though. 

Speaking of poo, the women's bathroom is the most disgusting bathroom I've seen in Nashville. I would post a photo but I'll save you the excitement to see it in person, ladies.
