I've used porta-johns at beer festivals around town that I felt cleaner in and I'm not joking. I've sent them an email, a FB message and told the staff in person.  No one seems to care which in turn keeps me not caring to ever go back.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I absolutely appreciate Katy and the team that assisted her in addressing me and my families concerns and giving us a fair resolve. She not only listened to our issues but acknowledged our feelings, which really meant a lot. AND SHE WAS ON IT! It took a second for her to respond and get caught up, but once she did she didn't miss a beat with following up with me and providing a resolve. Thank you soo much Katy !

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Hit this place every time We're in town. Hope to be relocating to Nashville, on the near future. Any up and coming acts that need a bass player hit me up!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Paradise Park Trailer Resort is a honky-tonk bar and restaurant that opened on Lower Broadway in downtown Nashville in 2007. I visited this past Friday night and learned, later on in the weekend, that this place is closing soon. It's supposed to close this month (July 2018) so I wanted to get my review out before they closed.

We showed up just before midnight on Friday and this place was packed. The line to get in wasn't very long, but it was very crowded inside, especially on the first floor. There were two bands, one on the first floor (ground level) as soon as you walk in and one inside on the rooftop (fourth level). I believe both bands were cover bands (definitely the band on the top floor; I remember one song they sang was the Alien Ant Farm version of Smooth Criminal). Both bands were pretty good and most people seemed to be having a good time.

There are a lot of lights and neon signs on Broadway. You can't miss Paradise Park's sign because it's one of the biggest. It's green and red and spans over two stories. It's one of the most prominent signs on the street. The space has colorful and kitschy decor (neon signs, string lights, Christmas lights, a disco ball, and more). Just inside the entrance is a photo booth and Skee-Ball. During our visit, the second and third floors were closed. The second floor was home to a dueling piano bar called The Big Bang.

We spent most of our time on the rooftop patio which was a lot more laid back and relaxed than downstairs. The rooftop has both an interior and exterior bar. The outdoor portion of the rooftop is covered in artificial turf with picnic tables, lawn/porch chairs, and high tops for seating. There was always a game of cornhole going on while we were up there. The highlight, to me, is the view from the rooftop. You get to see the beautiful downtown Nashville cityscape as well as all of the activity below on Broadway. Paradise Park seems to be in the center of it all. If it's not closed by the time you read this, the rooftop is definitely worth checking out.

If you want to use the elevator and it's not working, try punching in 0114 (authorization code). Otherwise, you'll have to get an employee to help you or just take the stairs.

On June 13, 2018, the Nashville Business Journal reported the building (411 Broadway) sold for $27 million last summer (https://www.bizjournals.com/nashville/news/2018/06/13/the-goldberg-brothers-are-closing-this-downtown.html) and will close in July 2018. The owners of the building and Paradise Park, who also own a bunch of restaurants in Nashville, are planning to open a new concept which will utilize all four stories of the building. It's supposed to open in 2019.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: If you visit, you pretty much have to go to Tootsies to check it off your list. Front bar gets really crowded, but upstairs is a little less congested. We spent time in both areas and each of the bands were really good performers. They do tend to play the same songs though, obviously a lot of crowd favorites. Drinks were expensive, but it was about as expected considering the Broadway area and the popularity of Tootsies.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
They serve beer in mason jars...

Hipster apocalypse! 

I really liked this little joint. I'm practically never on the westside...Stone Fox may have given me a reason to venture there now. We came for a friends show and I was sorely disappointed that we did not eat dinner here. Instead we just stood around and drank our cold mason jar beers. As a former geography major graduate I have to say I'm semi obsessed with the American wall map on the wall near the stage. I also loved the very pinteresting idea of using pallets as a fence for their rear patio, complete with herbs in between the slats. I really hope that during meal service they don't allow smoking back there. 

I will definitely come to see small gigs at The Stone Fox. I heard that it used to have better acoustics but honestly I feel like if the band knows what it's doing, it shouldn't matter too much.

Anyway worth going to for surely! Can't wait to try some grub!

name: The Stone Fox
text: The service here can be a little slow sometimes, but they make hands down the best burger I have had in Nashville and have a great selection of beers. Also, they host free/fun events such as bingo night and have a house bluegrassy band on Sundays. I think is one my favorite places in Nashville to grab a bite to eat, have a beer, and enjoy the evening!

name: World Music Nashville
text: Been here a few times buying things for my husband. They know what they are talking about and have helped me in my purchases. However, my husband took a guitar here to get a free estimate on fixing it. They never called with an estimate but only called to tell us it was fixed. We never approved them fixing it as we hadn't decided this is where it should get fixed. We had to pay to get the guitar back. The work seems fine but this is not how businesses should run. Very frustrating.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Great atmosphere. Food is fun and delicious. There's two different scenes to keep you entertained. A must see

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This was our second to last bar we visited on our girls weekend to Nashville & it was just as fun as everyone said it was! We went straight upstairs to the 3rd floor & got a drink (4 shots of well tequilla $28) (don't judge me for ordering a well brand). 

We listened to the band for a bit, which like every band we heard this past weekend was amazing. Then we went outside to the front patio which had the best view of downtown Nashville, we loved being up there. 

The only warning is try not to use the bathroom on the 2nd floor because there was an extremely rude bathroom attendant that was screaming at everybody who walked in about anything & everything. She was also very over the top with asking for tips because she says she only works for them but there would be no way I would tip somebody who made going to the bathroom so uncomfortable for everyone in our group.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Got to see Thom Schuyler, Fred Knobloch, Tony Arata, and Jelly Roll Johnson play in the round during a special NYE show. Being from New Orleans, I think I have fairly high standards for live music, and this was one of the coolest shows I've ever seen. The music wasn't overpoweringly loud. The songs and the stories behind them, told by the songwriters were the center of the show.

name: Tin Roof
text: Amazing live music!!!! I was blown away by the band Saturday night. Cool little place!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Gotta give it a 5 star for tradition and Lindsey at the second floor bar. Stiff drinks and much appreciated. Music? Of course and muy bueno. Must see must visit.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Music on all 3 floors 
Service and music both excellent crowded but worth it view from roof top at night very nice 
A line to get in but it moves quick well worth the wait 
Drinks a little pricey but it is a tourist spot
Sit chill and enjoyed all the music and fun

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: We were downtown just being tourists on a Thursday afternoon, and we were amazed at how lively it was in the middle of the day, so we felt inspired to duck into a honky-tonk. I remembered this place's epic decor/theme from a long-ago trip, and from the street, it did seem like the least crowded -- and maybe the most sincere? I mean, if you can have the most sincere pumpkin patch, can Nashville have the most sincere honky-tonk? While it lays the redneck ambience on a little thick, it never seems too clever about it -- to us, it felt very down to earth. The bartender was very nice and very attentive, and she suggested a local beer we ended up loving. We opted to order our food at the counter and pick it up there -- that made it feel a little more real. I had the hot chicken, and while it wasn't Hattie B's, it was not lacking in heat, a heat that really snuck up on you. My husband really liked his burger. The fries were like I make at home, except AWESOME. There was a very relaxed vibe, and the people who did come in were a diverse crowd (hipsters, rednecks, investment bros, a 20something girls' weekend). The live music was very laid-back/stripped-down and a good range of songs, and both musicians were very friendly. Basically, this was EXACTLY what I wanted from a honky-tonk experience -- and that we were able to have fun here in the middle of the afternoon only reinforces to me what a fun town Nashville is.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: 3 stars for a wednesday night visit, but oh, how i'd love to come back on a weekend.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Come for the band!!! Period ! I can literally stop my review right here.  I mean the place has really not much going for it but it manages to PACK a massive crowd.  Monday night at 10pm and the place was shoulder to shoulder.  Walls and floors are caked in sticky-icky shit... but people seem to not mind that stuff so ehhh - to each their own.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Monday Open Mic Night at the Bluebird was the highlight of my Nashville trip for sure! The deal here is you either book tickets far in advance before they've sold out or you take your chances at Open Mic Night. We did not plan ahead, but hey were there on a Monday so why not? 

THE WAIT - We read all the reviews that said be there an hour early and thought we'd be extra cautious, so we go there 2 hours early instead.  Tourist Fail! They hire security to ensure you aren't loitering in the parking lot early and disturbing other businesses. We were shoo' d away rather quickly. We came back exactly 56 minutes before doors open and we were already numbers 35 and 36 in line. They really mean an hour early. By 45 minutes to opening there were already 80 people in line and the venue was a capacity. Note that it's the same line for those wanting to be part of the audience and those wanting to perform, so get there early. Also, pack sunscreen, I fried in the sun waiting in the parking lot line (so worth it)! 

THE ATMOSPHERE - Great little venue, true listening room (so be quiet). Tables are push as close up to the front of the stage as possible. If you are lucky enough to score the front row, you feel like you are practically on stage with the artists. Great sound throughout the entire venue. Don't let the strip mall exterior fool you, this place has a great vibe. 

THE FOOD - Limited menu  but the prices are more than fair and the food they do provide is good. Mostly snacky items and lighter meals. We had the edamame and sweet potato fries, both were tasty. They have a full bar, including my personal favorite cider. 

THE SERVICE - Service was friendly and efficient. I'd totally come back! 

THE ENTERTAINMENT - I have to say, I was really surprised at how much I enjoyed this. Open Mic nights can be hit or miss.  There were literally artists from all over the world that had really traveled to either moved to Nashville or just came in for the week for a chance to sing at the Bluebird. Almost everyone we say had real talent. It was a great show!  

I would consider this a must if you are in Nashville. Granted, it's a trek from downtown tucked away in Green Hills (suburbia). A little bit of walking and one bus ride will get you there. Or it's about a 20 minute taxi from Honkey Tonk Row.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Stopped in here with some girlfriends to grab a bite to eat.. had chicken tenders from what I remember they were good, ha!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I had as good as a time as I expected from what everyone had told me. Truly a uniquely Nashville experience.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Really good breakfast and entertainment on a Saturday. Chicken and waffles good but suggest you try other options more creative. Bloody Mary bar works well and lots of items to make each BM your favorite.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Very original performances from humble emerging artists usually with their own written material. When I went, there were performances from country, pop country, and bassist artists. Astounding performances and I would highly recommend anyone interested in music to attend. If you haven't reserved tickets in advance, go about 2 hours early to reserve a spot the day of. It's worth it to see a free show from these emerging artists.

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text:
I have only recently experienced all the beautiful goodness that is The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel. Now I seem to be a frequent attendee of the events on their schedule.

Old Crowe Medicine Show along with a concert pairing with Broadway notable and actress Idina Menzel with the Nashville Symphony left a nice aftertaste last year but it is 2013's schedule that has solidified The Woods as a notable outdoor live entertainment venue in my book. 

I have already enjoyed The Black Crowes and Old Crowe and still have One Republic, Alabama Shakes, FUN, and Sigur Ros left. I love the diversity of acts that are booked here ranging from Harry Connick Junior to Imagine Dragons, a little something for most audiophiles. 

Lawn parking is FREE and easy to access and there is a bit of pre-show tail-gating going on too! I generally valet and grab a cocktail at Cafe Fontanella which is located on the grounds before the show too. The beautiful backdrop of nature and greenery make you feel as if you've been whisked to a faraway place while the layout of the stage and grounds are thoughtfully executed. You can choose to layout on a blanket, bring a chair, stand or mill around, or opt to upgrade to the VIP boxes which sit high on a hill and overlook the crowd. 

The casual vibe is weaved together with local food trucks parked on the grounds and fairly priced concessions throughout. 

Overall, this is a wonderful place to catch a show during favorable weather and seasons. My only suggestion is if you plan to imbibe, bring a designated driver or to carpool since the winding roads and location are a bit of a stretch and a cab ride won't be cheap unless you live in the area. 

if you're into the great outdoors and a casual concert experience, join 4500 of your Nashville neighbors and head out to the unlikely space where country crooner Barbara Mandrell's old estate was housed. Only in Nashville, folks. Only in Nashville...

TIP: This venue may also be rented for private events and corporate functions too!

name: Tin Roof
text: Definitely a do-able bar, the staff, in my opinion, always takes too long and most of the time seems put out to have to wait on you. decent patio and decent food. everything is just ok. not awful, not great - best thing about it is the location.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
If there's one activity that needs to be on your list when in the area, it has to be going to the Bluebird! 

There is not a bad seat in the house and the talent that graces the stage is second to none. 

You can make reservations a week in advance which is highly recommended! I lucked out and got 2 seats the day of by constantly checking the website for possible cancellations! This saved me from having to stand outside for a couple hours! 

The staff is super friendly. The only downfall is the parking lot, but you can park across the street at the mall and walk over! 

Best show you'll see no matter who's playing the night you go!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Visited Nashville a couple of months ago, and we all made a note of it to stop at Tootsies. And boy, did it not disappoint! When you first walk in, it is very crowded. However, once you find a spot, you're good! We luckily got a spot right in front of the stage. The band was INCREDIBLE! In my opinion, the night we visited Tootsies was my favorite night in Nashville! The bar service was good, and the bathroom attendant was pretty awesome as well! Next time I go to Nashville, I know we're I'm heading first! I would highly recommend Tootsies to anyone who is visiting Nashville!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Heard this place was the place to go, but I wasn't impressed. The place was packed, barely room to move about. Drinks were weak and served in plastic cups. Can't hear the band upstairs very well. Cleanliness was not up to par either.
Now I can say I came, I saw and then I left.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Disgusting!!! I had the veggies burger it's rice and black beans in a patty, it's soft, squishy with no flavor. The hand cut fries were cold! Yuck.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great music and attentive bartenders.  Seating is limited, but you will want to be on your feet enjoying the music anyway

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: When I go to Nashville, I always and I mean always will stop at Tootsie. The music is great the service is great. Its one of the funnest places in Nashville.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Definitely understated. Cheap beer and friendly bar staff. The music was better than most.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Took my team up the street for lunch on Monday.  Fried chicken sandwich was phenomenal.  Exceptional food, service, and atmosphere.  This makes the regular rotation.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I'm only taking 1 star off because the process to get booked here is so difficult and I've easily booked every other venue in town at least once...but alas, the Bluebird is a Nashville original! Just a word to the wise...do NOT talk..this is a listening room! You will never have a bad night of music here...it is very tiny so if you're claustrophobic this may not be your thing...I think sunday nights are great but any night there's a good show..

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: How does this establishment need reviews?! It's blow the top off, no reason to leave amazing!  Pick a floor, settle in, listen, be enlightened by the great music.   Did. Done. Would do it a thousand times over! You're welcome.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Live music all the time - cool. $4 yeungling - not. Filthiness - not. Mediocre service - not. Uncomfortable seating - not. Super-touristy crowd - not.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Goodnight. If you like crowded, loud, hot bars that smell like they haven't been cleaned over the years (years that no doubt included drunks puking now and again), then it's your place. If you don't like that -- particularly on a Saturday, midday, then stay away -- even with its history. There seemed to be only two types of people in the bar: 1) 20somethings looking to get drunk, and 2) 40somethings looking to prove they were still 20somethings. Call me a curmudgeon, I just didn't want to spend any more time there than I did.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Well, the booze and food were fantastic. Pretty good prices and I loved all the retro kitchen tables. Service was pretty lousy. The place wasn't that busy to have been ignored by our server, maybe she was having an off night. The door guy, on the other hand, was too preoccupied with chatting up his hipster cronies to even do his job. He wasn't very sly about bad mouthing customers either, we heard him loud and clear as we stepped on the porch to smoke. My travel companion and I are from Chicago where pretty much everyone is a jerk, but the staff here kinda blew us away. Stone Fox, get yourself a better crew of kids who actually want to work and you'll be an A++ establishment.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
This place is made famous thanks to the show Nashville which is the only reason I know about it.  I am coming to Nashville with a group for my sister's bachlorette and we wanted to check this place out.  This means that I had to wake up at 5:50 a.m. my time to go online to reserve spots.  They say you can only reserve 6 people and we had more than that so my mom and sister were at home sitting in line as well.  I clicked in right exactly at 6 a.m. the time they were made available for the following Friday night.  When I got to the selection there was only a couple seats left at every table. How is this even possible if I was right in at exactly the time they said while my mom and sis are still in the queue.  Doesn't seem they make everything available.  I selected and then when my mom and sis got in they got sold out.  I sent them an email saying to cancel the reservation I made and that I'm sorry that because of their system we wouldn't be able to check out their place during our visit.  They wrote back - 
                     
              Thank you for reaching out to us. We are happy to assist with the cancellation of your reservations. Please remember that we are unable to refund the amount you were charged at the time of your reservations (Service Fees, Taxes, or Pre-Pays) but you should not see any additional charges in regards to your cancelled seats.

Awesome, so not only am I out of luck but you also charged me $3 to even try to reserve for a free concert.  What the hell?  People talked about pretentious - I think that is a perfect word for this place.  Get over yourself Bluebird Cafe.  We will likely enjoy great music at better places in Nashville.

Oh and thanks for making me wake up super early and ruin my Monday morning!  Not like you care one bit.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Went here for happy hour on a Friday, and had a great time! We started upstairs and then transitioned to the downstairs cellar, which was a more refined, chill space to relax. The cocktails were all a little sweet for me, even the old fashioned, but they were a great deal for being 1/2 off (making most of the cocktails $5). The manager and our server were both wonderful and went out of their way to make sure we had a good experience. Would go back again, but probably for happy hour only.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: hoenstly the live music is not very good and you cant really dance cause there are too many pepole around. they  also do not give free chasers which is a reall bummer.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Had never been to this part of Nashville and thought it was great. There was an incredible number of bars to hear some really great music. Everyone said to go to Tootsie's and I wasn't disappointed. The bartender Sarah was the nicest young lady, very pretty and sweet. She made the night for me. The band was great and I loved that the woman singing got on top of the bar and sang! It was a really fun place and I was even more impressed with my visit here after visiting other bars with much less enthusiasm and service. The view on the top gave a fantastic view of the street. Again Sarah was great and very thoughtful to make sure I enjoyed my visit. Definitely with come here again and bring friends.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: This was the chosen happy hour spot today and let's just say I didn't do the choosing. I ordered a melrose mule first and it was forgettable. But the cucumber cooler was so outstanding that I dubbed it the most refreshing drink I've ever had. Imagine the perfect day by the lake with the sun kissing your skin ever so slightly and this is the drink that can take you there. I am giving this place two stars solely for the cucumber cooler. Go get one! Now the appetizer...the brisket nachos. Just say no to dry brisket. Just say no to broken cheese sauce. Just say no to under seasoned food. This place has potential to be a real winner but the execution and the need to cut corners in food prep stunt the potential.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Went on a Thursday night around 8, super crowded,    Average bands, drink prices same as most on Broadway... nice that they have heaters on roof patio.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
I went to this bar with a couple of coworkers and clients during a conference I was attending in town... I consumed $87 in drinks on my credit card. When I got home to look at my credit card statement I noticed that I've been charged twice, once for $140 and a second time for $35!!!
I had to file a dispute through my credit card company because it's just impossible to reach this joint by phone...

Never going back!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
The key is to hop online and get "in line" for their ticket system. Definitely get on the ticket page a few minutes before the clock starts counting down. I was able to get 2 seats at table 9, which was literally touching the stage. It was perfect. There is a seating chart on the website if you're curious how seating works. Reservations are the only way to go. I can't imagine standing outside (especially in the Nashville summer heat) and waiting for a seat that likely won't happen. 

Food is nothing special, but it's nice to have a few options if you need a little something. They have beer, wine, and your standard cocktails available. Great prices too. 

Overall, such a fun experience and definitely worth it if you can get tickets!

name: Tin Roof
text: We were walking around Broadway mid afternoon and the band lured us in. They were very good so we decided to stay for lunch. Service was friendly but kept feeling like this place may be sort of tourist trappy but that's just what we were in Nashville so we decided to soak it in. Food was ok nothing to rave about. We had pulled pork sandwiches for about $14 each and had some chicken scratch beer. We were definitely there for the entertainment and the crowd wasn't bad either. We had a good time!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Beautiful small music venue.  We were lucky enough to get tickets for table 4/5.  We shared our table with a mom and daughter from England.   We listened to four really talented musicians playing "In a row".   They each took turns singing their original music.  The show lasted about an hour and forty minutes and then they stayed for pictures.  Great experience!!!  I wish they would have let us spend our $10 each mandatory fee on merchandise instead of food.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
First time in Nashville in probably 20 years.  Also first time at Tootsies.  My father use to sing here years ago and I've always wanted to visit.  

My wife and I only wanted to stop in for a drink and then explore more establishments on Broadwsy; however,  we ended up ordering lunch and spending a couple of hours there listening to the band. 

I ordered the burger and the wife ordered the pulled pork sandwich, as both were recommended.   We had them cut in half so that we could share.  The pork was goid, but we both felt the burger was best.

Great experience.   Recommend everyone visit Tootsies.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This past Sunday, my wife and I witnessed a Cuban American mom (about 5' tall and under 110 lbs.) being dragged 20 feet in a choke hold by a large African American bouncer with a large diamond zirconia earring in his left ear - just for kneeling on a chair in order to see.

We followed them out with two nice men (whom were patrons for 10+ years) to ensure she and her husband were OK. 

This was clearly assault, the gal also appeared to be targeted. She said that she was willing to leave but wanted to wait for her husband to return as he had stepped away. This obviously put quite a damper on our Nashville visit. I don't like submitting negative reviews, albeit this guy should be facing assault charges. I feel obligated to warn others in the event this should happen again.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Love this bar!  Both stages always have amazing performers.  Drinks are reasonable, bartenders are friendly.

The negatives I have to give are:  the bathrooms!  So small and difficult to get to!  The other is a good/bad.  It gets packed!  So much so that you can't move and it begins to be hard to enjoy yourself.  If you need space, go upstairs and hang out behind the stange, it seems to have a decent amount of space.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tennessee staple Honky Tonk. It was really busy and you have the option of three different floors and live music to pick from. Very top has a beautiful view of the NashVegas strip and heat lamps for when it's chilly!

name: Throwbacks Bar & Grill
text: Great place. I stopped in because I saw this little sign on the road advertising Chicago Italian Beef sandwiches. A couple of years ago my wife and I went to go see the Rolling Stones in Chicago, and since then we have been unable to find a place here that made them like the legendary Al's Italian Beef. Until now. Throwbacks nailed it.It's not listed on the menu, so you won't see it on the website, but trust me, it was great.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I had heard/read so many things about the Bluegrass Brunch, so I decided to try it out when some friends from out of town came to visit. I read enough reviews to know that I should be prepared to wait a bit. Luckily, once we checked in we were able to go ahead and order our bottomless mimosas to enjoy. The bar area can get pretty packed, but with a mimosa in hand, I wasn't too stressed about it. Plus you have live music to listen to while you wait. I also like that they get your number and text you when your table is ready. You are also sent a link to a site that lets you see what number you are in line-SO helpful! When we got our table, the waiter was very friendly. He immediately asked us if we were planning to truly take advantage of the bottomless mimosas, to which we unequivocally replied YES! That being said, we managed to put down a serious quantity of mimosas, making it totally worth the $15. The food was also good. I had the breakfast tacos (you can't go wrong with bacon, eggs, and avocado). I also loved that we were never rushed, despite there being a wait. I definitely recommend the brunch! Good times were had by all!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsie's is the place you have to go to at least once just to say you've been. I prefer the top floor, it has much more room. I don't like the first floor at all...very crowded and so packed you can't even move. Top floor is very cool and seems to be just slightly less tourist-y.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
My girlfriends and I came to the Sutler on a Saturday for brunch. We were able to get right in around 1:30 PM and they immediately served us some fresh biscuits with sorghum butter and jelly. So good. I ordered the BLT. It was piiled with thick cut bacon and the usual suspects. I tried the hash that my girlfriend got and it was delicious. They offer unlimited mimosas for $15 and the sangria looked refreshing too. I'll be back to try that! 
Overall- it's a good brunch spot. Inexpensive and who doesn't like unlimited mimosas on the patio? Did I mention they have a patio? Yep.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: One of the most iconic bars in the entire country. This is the place to be in Nashville, amazing bar, amazing people. I did not even try and got about five girl's numbers here just by being friendly. It is sometimes hard to hear in the place its loud but you have to have skills. It had a few locals but its mostly a tourist bar with legendary country music framed pictures on the wall. Southern women are easy to talk and this is the best bar on the Broadway strip by far. Only downsize is that it is not that big and its packed and its hard to move around.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Yes, the reputation is deserved.  

We went there on a Friday evening to the first show.  The songwriters' circle was excellent; there were some truly talented voices and I enjoyed hearing about their life experiences and how they factored into the song.  Food wise service was very fast and friendly.  The food is nothing special, but it's totally edible, reasonably priced, and fast (and you don't come here for the food anyway, do you?).  

It's a hole in the wall and a little bit of a ride from downtown, but it was totally worth it.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
I had to write an update after coming back for dinner and loving it! I had heard not so great reviews about their brunch from friends, BUT I'm hoping that maybe its just they are busier at brunch and they were still new?

Either way, my friend and I came in for dinner before a show, and ordered drinks and food in the back fenced area. Our waitress was awesome and sure to keep our glasses full. I sampled a couple of cocktails that were really really great and I had a black bean bowl and my friend had a cheeseburger with curly fries. Both were delicious and we ate every bite! Food was seriously delicious! 

Seems like they change up the menu a good amount since my black bean dish is no longer on the online menu :( sad! However I see that they have replaced it with a couple other items that look pretty amazing in comparison. 

Maybe coming here for dinner is the trick, but I'll give it a shot for brunch too!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
Fun Stop In The Western Nashville Area

SITREP

I was brought here by friends for a nice evening of some munchies, great drinks, and Monday-night *BINGO!* and was not disappointed.

THE SETUP

Located on 51st Avenue, just a bit outside the Downtown arena, the Stone Fox provides some seriously vibes!

*THE FOOD

Delicious food that we had:

* The Kale Pizza; and,
* The BBQ Pork Chipolte Sliders

Each on their happy hour menus for just about $10-$12.

*THE DRINKS

I got myself the Paper Plane, which was a wonderfully refreshing cocktails consisting of Kentucky Bourbon, so it did not disappoint!

*BINGO!*

Monday is bingo-night, and the action was fast-paced as the participants tried to keep up with the "caller".  It makes for a great retro-fun experience, and the crowd was mainly a very hip cadre of 20/30 somethings.  So not your typical bingo crowd.

TOM SELLUCK

There's an oil painting of the man up there right in the middle of the restaurant.  I do NOT know why.  Next time I'm there, I will ask!

THE LOWDOWN

The Stone Fox is cold stone fun!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: What can I say about a place that is that established... The drinks are good the beer prices a little high.. but the music and the staff are great. The chili dogs are awesome...

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Well where do I start. I had the fried chicken and first bite took me back to my grandmothers house frying chicken in her kitchen. She would fry it in an iron skillet. The collards were equally amazing and let's not even talk about how good the Mac n cheese is. Thanks for taking me back 30 years!!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Went on a Saturday night. Place was packed but be sure to take advantage of the several different floors including the rooftop.  They had a band with a sick fiddle player and they did a lot of popular stuff with a twist.  We only drank beers so I can't speak for the mixed drinks.

name: Tin Roof
text:
Tin Roof is tucked down at the bottom of the ever changing Demonbreun (street?) and has somehow managed to outlast a good number of other bars on this strip of businesses, so they must be doing something right! I find a good number of people planning to go here, but it's just never my go-to place. Drinks are about what you'd expect and I can't remember the food, so that tells me it's probably OK. Just seems rather middle of the road all around. They have a lovely patio area and a "green room" that they've added on that is nice. 

Tin Roof also has live bands and music and can be a fun night out. Maybe now that my BF lives in the Gulch I'll head over here more... we'll see!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: First time here, in from Chicago for business. Great place to get a 1/2 burger with sweet potato fries. Sunday night visit about 7:45pm. Not a long wait. Definitely will ve back.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: the tots are the best thing to ever happen to my life i wanna order 8 more orders rn. then i wanna roll in a basket of them and cover myself in tots and ketchup and never look back

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Very fun, great night out.  The food wasn't very good but the experience was outstanding.  Very Nashville with great music, and very laid back crowd.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: very cool 3 story bar/restaurant with live music. blackberry moonshine was awesome. Nachos just ok. But definitely a place I would revisit for drinks and music!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Sitting here observing the cleanliness practices at the bar on the third level. Watching Sasha on Jan 28, 2018 at 730p cough repeatedly into her hand, braid her hair, and then eat at the bar. Never saw her wash hands and then she handled ice, cups, and alcohol. Now she's rubbing her fingers on her lips. Yikes.

name: Tin Roof
text:
Went for the first time a couple weeks ago. Have always heard good or indifferent things about this place and wanted to check it out for myself. I don't typically go out to bars much, but sometimes a girl just wants to dance. 

We got there a little early, I would say around 930-10. Was not super packed, took a while to get bartenders attention to get drinks. Sat at a table listening to the music. Not many people were dancing at the time. Once the time djs swapped, the music got better and brought a ton of people to the dance floor. By 11 the place was packed and we were having a blast. 
The other side wasn't packed earlier in the evening and I honestly forgot about the other side. On our way out, we walked through the other side. I stopped for about three songs. Loved the live music on that side.

I would come back.

name: The Stone Fox
text: Seen some of the best shows since I've been in Nashville here. The interior is Twin Peaks(the show)with a modern kick which is awesome. The back porch area has a great atmosphere. I have eaten here once and the BBQ Nachos were layered with BBQ so every chip had some toppings, and the fried pickles were delicious. Very cool

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: GREAT acoustic venue. Food is good and service is as well. It's a little small but that adds to the intimate feel. Great place to really go LISTEN to some great music.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I'm not a huge country music fan, but I had an absolutely fantastic time at Tootsie's.  I would consider some of the songs played as more main stream than Country, but Country is prevalent.  It's a simple formula, great music, libations and wonderful service.  Check it out before the crowds become too overwhelming.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We had a great dining experience at the Sutler. I was curious to try their take on the horseshoe, as it's a favorite in my home state of Illinois. I made a reservation online, which was an easy process, but was a bit disappointed to find that we still had to wait 10-15 minutes upon our arrival. They'd run out of the cocktail I was really hoping to try, but our waiter was quick to make an alternate recommendation. The food took some time to arrive, but I didn't think the wait was anything out of the ordinary for Nashville. The staff was very courteous and gave us frequent updates. I have to say, that horseshoe was well worth the wait! It was simply delicious. To make up for our wait time, they gave us a complimentary dessert, which was really thoughtful and spoke to their dedication to customer service. I will definitely return to the Sutler and would recommend it to anyone looking for a good meal (especially the elusive horseshoe!) in Nashville.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
I don't know where to start on this review. Let's go basic: Food.

The food is good. Very good - if you're in the breakfast/brunch mood, pick the sweet potato pancakes with bourbon butter and jalapeno bacon. If you're in a light lunch mood, you can't go wrong with the fried chicken salad. It comes with white hominy and is amazing.

But actually you should come here because of what this place was and what it means now. This is where the Nashville sit ins happened and in the second seat from the end is where a black man was arrested instead of a black man having an opportunity to eat.

Sitting at that same counter, thinking about what all has and hasn't changed in our country, made me cry all the way through my meal. The history is palatable here. The staff knows it, the owner sure as heck knows it and no one is afraid to talk about it, share memories and stories and celebrate the opportunity to be a different place, in the same place, as part of a new time.

Go. Eat a meal. Ask questions. Think.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Sro. Standing to the side of the stage, got pushed into table to my right. Female singer very off key
 Left after 10 min. Should have a crowd control. So much for my excited anticipation of this wonderful legendary starmaker.
Victoria Nellums

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Every time I walk into Paradise Park I get transported back to an era where 90's version of Billy Ray Cyrus rocked a mullet and sang "Achy Breaky Heart". Make no mistake, P-Park is playful with the redneck decor (i.e. there is a Christmas tree made out of tires spray-painted green) but it gives this bar a fun atmosphere with a Joe Dirt-like character. It is kitschy and slightly over-the-top but not offensive. I've spent hours here since the trailer park theme draws you in, the cheap beer in the bathtubs catches your attention then the bands get you to stay. The bands are some of the best I've seen on Broadway. Although I've mentioned some of the highlights and appeal there are even more things I enjoy about this joint.

The service is great. The bartenders are super nice and I've never had a problem with the service. The food is an intoxicated person's dream. They have all those foods you crave late at night--mac n' cheese, hand dipped chicken tenders and tater tots smothered in nacho cheese (yes I've tried all of them and they are amazing). On a night when the main bar area isn't completely packed you can order with the bartender and sit at the bar to eat or one of their tables in the back. They have a section of the bar that looks like the outside of a double-wide and you can order food there and eat on the restaurant side of P-Park as well. 

In summary, P-Park is a place that I recommend seeing if you find yourself on lower Broadway. I always take visitors here and they find it to be a "hoot". Grab a $6 pitcher with some friends, listen to their amazing artists and have a good ole' time.

name: Tin Roof
text: Good night time bar.  If you are a smoker you can go outside and smoke.  You may see a country music star occasionally.  Big mixed drinks.  Cabs are always available.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: A MUST do in Nashville.  I am not a country music fan but that does not matter here, when someone has talent, the music has no boundaries.  This place is small, intimate and the talent that is show cased is never short of exceptional!!  If you have ANY interest in music, you MUST go.  Anytime I come to Nashville now, the Bluebird cafe is a MUST.  Now, getting tickets is another story but I would not hesitate standing in line for 3 hours for a chance to see another show!  And I typically don't do lines!  GO, you WILL NOT be disappointed!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I am a Hispanic male from Southern California. Thursday night, I visited Tootsies with my GF and  some friends. As I approached the entrance of the bar, I was asked for my ID. I pulled my wallet out, and pulled out 2 ID's (drivers license and State ID) I handed what I thought was the bouncer, my Drivers license and then he asked me "Is the other ID your Green Card?" I turned to him in disbelief and asked him did he really ask me that. I immediately walked in and asked for the manager. We were approached by a dark haired man with glasses who said he was the manager. We walked down to confront the bouncer only to find out the bouncer was a Sheriff. In the midst of speaking to the Sheriff and manager, a large black man (real bouncer)walks up to me and pushes me. I tell the man to keep his hands off me, and the manager proceeds to tell me I am no longer welcomed in the bar. The Sheriff had to separate the bouncer and manager from me. This is the first time in my life that I have experienced racism directly and wouldn't imagine it would occur in an establishment of this magnitude. I've been to this place a couple times on other visits to Nashville and even attended the bar earlier in the day before the incident! I know this incident is a sign of the times and this will no way effect their business but hopefully the "management" at Tootsies will consider some training on how to handle these types of situations in the future, as I am sure this won't be the last time this happens here!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: You guys, this is a Nash must!! If you don't get reservation tickets ahead of time get there at least 2 hours before the show starts. To stand in line for the first come seating. We got there right at 5, for a 6:30 show and by the time we got closer to the door, there was only 1 seat left in the whole place. My hubby wouldn't let me not go in so I went in solo. They let him come in and out and stand at the door to watch a few songs, which was nice. It was definitely a cool experience and the baked Brie was super yummy!

name: Throwbacks Bar & Grill
text:
We were really excited when Throwbacks first opened.  We have given this place many second chances even though it is consistently plagued with food and service issues.  This past Tuesday night was the last straw and needless to say, we will not be back.  It started with the typical lack of service (neither server/bartender knew the drink specials, our friends waited over 15 mins for ice water, the food came out incorrectly and my husband's burger was cold).  It ended when the male bartender/server (who has been fired before but for some unapparent reason was rehired) came over, and in a confrontational tone and posture, wanted to know what the problem was.  My husband told him the wait for the food, drinks, water and general lack of service was the problem.  The bartender/server apparently did not like the answer he received so he continued demanding to know what the problem was and what he needed to do.  My husband, getting a bit agitated at this point, told him that what he needed to do was just leave him alone.  This was not good enough for the bartender/server.  After more attitude from him my husband said leave me alone, we will never be back.  To which the bartender/server responded with "That's what you said last time; feel free to leave now."  and that is exactly what we did.  In the spirit of full disclosure, we did say the last time that we wouldn't be back based on the same bartender/server's confrontational attitude however we unfortunately wasted our time and gave Throwbacks one more try.  Trust me when I say, that it was the last.

It's also worth mentioning that the female bartender said it was her first night behind the bar, that everyone else called out so when she came in to have a drink on her night off, the male bartender/server asked her to help him out.  He was apparently the bartender, server and cook for the evening yet he found plenty of free time to sit at the bar and smoke while drinking white wine.

If you want to go somewhere where they are consistently out of menu items, their drink specials change but they don't update their website, is a sports bar but will have comedy/music/poker rather than sports and has rude and inattentive servers/bartenders then Throwbacks is the place for you.  Otherwise, save yourself the unpleasant experience and check out Alley Pub (across the street) or Brewhouse West.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This is a Landmark in Nashville.  

A lot of country music stars have preformed here over the years.    And you never know who will drop in unexpectedly 


The rooftop area is awesome and a place to hang out.   You would be disappointed!    We will be back for sure

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Went here on a Friday night.  It was a really great vibe!  The performers were top notch and the drinks were pretty good.  The acoustics are fantastics and the band honored requests (for a small, reasonable donation).  The only thing I'd criticize is that the stage is by the door and that makes the entrance to the place get extra crowded as people are coming in and out, but also standing around to listen to the band.  So other than the narrow cramping, it really is a fantastic place for music.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Who wouldn't love Tootsie's? It's one of (if not the) oldest bars on Broadway in Nashville and a must-visit place! It's not an upscale place, food is bar food and servers don't seem overly happy to help, but I that's part of it's charm. The music is completely amazing, and the next group is always better than the last (or you think they are because you've been day drinking since 10am). Make sure you have cash for the bands--they aren't paid by the bars to play, they make all their money from tips. A few will take Venmo, but most only take good ole cash. The tables and chairs all wobble and there's not always a place to sit (always packed on every level--especially on weekends). The later it gets into the night, the better the people watching gets, but once the large groups of bachlorette parties start coming in, look out. For reasons unknown, they can't seem to hold their liquor and it turns into a bit of a shit-show--but again, if you know what you're getting into, sit back, watch, giggle and have another drink and enjoy the amazing music. Try to catch one of the groups with a fiddler--they are truly fun to watch and have so much talent! Will visit here every time we're in town!!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Lunch Box, the Paradise Park manager on duty, was more than helpful when I was asking about the ingredients in their chili (I have a food allergy and thought the chili would be safe for me to eat). Lunch Box then informed me of the ingredients and how the rest of their food was made- he was awesome, incredibly helpful, and very informative; he was more than willing to accommodate my food allergy and make sure what I was eating was safe for me to eat. I could not recommend this place more. Yummy food and awesome service. Letty, one of the kitchen staff, also went above and beyond to help me out and find a manager for me to talk to. Without her great attitude and willingness to help,  I could have easily wound up sick. Thankfully the staff at Paradise Park is incredible.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The bartender threw out my full beer while I was using the restroom. I get keeping things clean but if you cover your beer that means I'm coming back for it. Plus the bathroom had roaches. Dont fall for the tourist trap much better places on Broadway to visit than them.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
We were in Tootsie's on a Friday at 3 p.m. in the place was packed. Jam-packed. I mean call the fire marshal there was 6 lb of crap in a 3lb bag packed. However that didn't stop us from getting some beers and listening to some good country music.

For six beers it ended up being $42. I don't mind paying a little extra but $7 a beer for Bud Light? That's how you know you're on the strip I guess. Be way it works and most of these Honky Tonks is they will play pretty much any song you want one if they know it too if you're a hot looking cowgirl in 3 if you have 20 bucks

We were enjoying ourselves and having a pretty darn good time when all of a sudden Here Comes a bartender who is about 5 foot nothing and came out and yelled at all of us were standing in front of the stage. It's not like we had any place to go we really couldn't move the only way for us to go without she was trying to push us back into the bar and there was simply no place for us to go. She went and got mr. Bouncer man who also came in and try to get us to move back and once we showed him there was simply nowhere to move he kind of shrugged his shoulders went back outside and took care of moving the Beggars out from front of the store. After the song we were listening to is over we decided to leave. We found it there is a couple more cost-effective Honky Tonks Off the Strip.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: PLEASE COME BACK.! We miss you.! I need some late Mac n cheese and chicken strips and tots and a great mullet wall.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: If you are going to the bluebird for the menu then you have completely missed the point. Not that it is bad, but you go for the music and the vibe. It feels like an absolute Nashvilles staple, with a writers-in-the-round set up, reasonably priced drinks, and a fine food menu. It is great for couples or small groups, or if you just love music.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Love at first sight......This is my kind of place!!  My friend and I rang in the New Year here with some new friends.  I loved the atmosphere and unique decor.  Being NYE it was obviously busy but the service was still top notch!!  I defiantly will be back to enjoy some PBR tallboys next time I'm in town.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We loved this place! We came here for my daughter's birthday for brunch and just had a fabulous time! The music was great, food was excellent, and the whole ambiance was wonderful! I can't recommend this place any more! Rachel, our waitress, was the cherry on top! She truly made us have the best time! Thank you!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The Brisket Tacos are excellent for Taco Tuesday ! The service was fast! And my bartender Morgan was friendly  and down to earth! The delicious food and Morgan's friendly smile and attentiveness to her customers makes the Sutler a number one stop for lunch!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: My review is based solely upon standing in line and not actually entering the Bluebird. We came on a Sunday at 5 pm when they are due to open according to their business hours, and the line was 20 people deep. Our fault: we didn't realize you need to make a reservation to stand a chance of getting in. Neither did everyone else in line. There is no one from the Bluebird corralling people or providing any kind of direction, so after standing in line for 45 minutes in the blazing sun with zero movement in the line (literally, no one went inside that didn't have a reservation) we decided to leave. I would highly recommend making a reservation to avoid this situation. The staff could also make some improvements by coming outside and educating people on what to expect with the line.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Really enjoyed our brunch here. They band was great and despite sitting directly next to the stage we could still hear each other. The food didn't blow us away but we were all happy enough with our orders. I'd come back for the music and mimosas!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Pretty disappointed to write this review as I really enjoy the bar and it's live entertainment. We have been several times with great service in the past. But last night an incident happened with the employees that clearly is no mistake.  As I purchased my beers, on the 2nd floor from one of the beer buckets, I handed over $100 bill, she commented "$100" and looked at it in the light to check if it was fake (you know. The usual). Than proceeded to get me change and the two beers I ordered. Got to my table to realize I was shorted on my change. I walked up to let her know, and within 5 seconds 4 security guards where booting me out the back door. 
    I'd love to believe that it was an accident on her part, but after talking to another patron that this happed to, and the way I was quickly forced out of the bar, I'm thinking this is a scheme they pull off on drunks all night long.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Made the trip to Nashville to attend an "in the round"  show at the Bluebird Cafe: John Cowan, Bill Lloyd, Pat Simmons Jr., Jonell Mosser and Tom Brit.  At $15 per person, plus a two-drink minimum, this has to be one of the best entertainment values I've seen in recent years.

Tiny storefront in a little strip shopping center - definitely nothing special from the outside.  Next door is a hair salon, I seem to recall.  

Food and drink options are average bar fare (but service was brisk and professional).  We looked over the menu online before we went, and decided to have a nice dinner elsewhere before the show.

But this isn't about the menu:  it is all about seeing a show in a very intimate, iconic venue.  Some seats are so close you could reach out and touch the performers (but don't - that's kind of creepy).

This is definitely a "plan ahead" place.  Most shows sell out in minutes, since venue is small, I'd guess it seats maybe 50-60 people?  You purchase tickets online, and generally need to be ready to make a reservation the minute tickets go on sale.  And you only have a minute or so to complete the transaction, so have your credit card out, and print out the searing chart and be ready with a list of your preferred seats.

You -can- show up the day of the show - they set aside a very small number of seats to sell at the door, and there is the occasional no-show for a reservation, but the night I went there was a line for last minute seats, and I don't know if everyone got in.

One of a kind place.  I can't wait to go back.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Ticketing process is a joke. Don't waste your time.

Its pretends to be democratic but is presumably rigged for friends because their technology makes it impossible to actually reserve a ticket.

You get up early, you wait in a virtual line, your turn comes up, and then the site breaks...EVERY time.

Lot of great music in Nashville so don't start your trip getting frustrated with this disaster of a process.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: On vacation in Nashville and Tootsie's came highly suggested. My group & I decided to check out Tootsie's on a Saturday from approximately 11-5/6. We had a table on the rooftop. The view was perfect. The heaters by the door helped us to remain comfortable and it was November 9th. Drinks were great & ice cold (just how we like it). The food was wonderful; we enjoyed the sampler, nachos, and a pulled pork sandwich. The service was a bit slow as the bar was packed so this was understandable. If we wanted our drinks faster all we had to do was go to the bar which was completely fine. The only dilemma was the traffic to the bathroom. Its location was not ideal and caused traffic to back up on the stairs. Overall a great enjoyable experience for all.

name: Tin Roof
text: Slow service over priced food. Good service = Good tip. Crap service and the bar tender had a crappy attitude and playing on your phone half the time does not warrant a good tip. 10/10 would not go again. Stay away.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Visited the rooftop bar while strolling Broadway.  The band was really nice considering the crowd was only about 8 people in the afternoon. They kept asking for requests and were not asking for tips even though most artists do during the show. We got to hear a few requests and made sure to tip them on the way out. The bartender was not very friendly and made it feel less than welcoming. The band and venue made up for it though.

name: The End.
text: Me and The Squad rolled up looking REAL nice after getting sorted out with some real good bean rolls at The Gold Rush and we had matching Dilly Bar Squad t-shirts but we weren't wearing them at the time but the show was great and our friend Matt really loved Jeff Rosenstock's set like Matt was going off down in front but anyway bye for now.............

name: The End.
text:
I feel I should start by saying I have been here only once and for a Jeff the Brotherhood show, which is an experience in and of itself.  The End is located in an alley in Elliston.  It feels like s shanty inside.  It's low ceiling-ed and cramped and it sells cheap beer and the scent of cigarette smoke leaks in from its small fenced-in patio.  It doesn't take much to sell out this small shack and it becomes difficult to move or breathe.

And its freaking awesome.

The energy at the shows here is just so much fun.  Its such a different venue from the other ones about town.  It enjoys its own filth and it gets wild in here.  I'm sure there are plenty of more low-key shows but there's nothing like a rock-fueled sold out experience here.  It's a dive bar music hole in the wall and I absolutely love it.  No frills, nothing fancy, just good music, cheap beer, and a unique atmosphere in the face of a becoming-too-fancy Nashville.  I'd recommend throwing caution to the wind and coming here at least once to see a band you might normally not see.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Place was half-empty when we walked in, and we were told there'd be a 20 minute wait.  Saw at least 2 managers or expediters just standing around, as well as 2 waiters who didn't seem too busy.  Maybe one of them could have waited on tables and cut down on that wait time...Cobb salad was only okay and half the cheese on the nachos wasn't melted.  Go to the Memphis location to eat and stop by here just to pick up your pins.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Great bar! Bands were awesome and staff kept the place running smooth. Never a long wait at the bar and stupid annoying drunks were "handled" by security. Will be back!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Came here during the daytime after a day of shopping on broadway.  It's a big place with, of course, a big stage.  The dance floor is pretty spacious, and they have nice decor (I like the big guitar on the back wall).  They have an upstairs area as well, and a sectioned off elevated dining area on the side.  

The place was packed for a monday but pretty clean.  They do charge for water, so drink beer.

Jk

name: The Valentine
text:
This is such a refreshing establishment to have on broadway. Although they stay true to their roots with live country music on the first 2 floors in a building that has had 2 tenants in the last 100 years, a boot store and a blacksmith; they offer a more non touristy feel on the 3rd floor for a dj or the roof top for a open air cocktails. 
All of the apps that i havd had were amazing. This place is definitely worth a trip

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Beautiful accommodations. Loved the balcony off our room overlooking the courtyard. Found an amazing deal on the hotel tonight app. Comfy beds. The best feature of this hotel is the $10 shuttle that takes you to Broadway. I would patronize this hotel again.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
The Stage is a great time! 

I like that they play a mixture of music, not just obscure country songs that I don't know, and the crowd is lively and fun. Although, it can be a bit TOO packed for my taste on weekend nights. The drinks are about what you expect on Broadway, not crazy expensive or cheap either, about middle of the line.

A couple things to remember:

- The Stage WILL be filled with out of towners and people visiting, so don't expect a lot of Nashville locals. 
- There is typically a line out front that is crazy long, so go to the back ally way for a shorter/sometimes no line. 

I like the Stage and come here when I'm in the mood to play tourist!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The bar was only 1/4 full but we struggled to get one of the four bartenders standing around to make us drinks.  When she did, it can with a snotty attitude and our drinks were in small plastic cups, mostly filled with ice.  $11 a piece.  Even when you said," thank you," they didn't respond.   Even though we were sitting at the bar, we couldn't get refills.   It's a shame because the venue was comfy and clean, and the cover band was great.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The hotel was beautifully decorated for the holidays.  We were pleasantly surprised considering the price.  They have a nice restaurant/bar in the lobby and an indoor pool.  Our room was spacious with a little patio.  Definitely going back when I'm in Nashville again.

name: The Valentine
text: Go there for the drinks and live music. The service from waitress was less than expected. A group of 8 went there and the atmosphere is fantastic. We did decide to eat there as we made reservations. When the waitress walked up and asked what did we want, I replied please get a note pad. She told me she had been doing this a long time so I agreed with her. We got food brought out a little at a time as others waited. The waitress left off 2 hamburgers, fries and then told us we didn't order that. So I guess she thought that 2/3rds were eating but the others weren't. We did have a good time and will go back when in Nashville. The owner did come out and apologized, gave us the meals and did make it up to our party. If I can give any suggestions is waiters and waitresses, I do not care how good you think your memory is. Please take a note pad as too much is going on and you do get distracted. Other than that I loved the place.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Pretty average country bar in downtown Nasville.  We sat upstairs, where the bartender was less than friendly, but otherwise enjoyed ourselves.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Was at this hotel for about 4 days for a conference and everything was really good. The hotel is a little older but well managed. Love it that every room have a balcony. I would in deed stay hear again.

The service was really good as well but was a little slow cleaning my room and understand the hotel was pretty full. May need to brain extra staff when hotel is about full.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Best bruschetta I've had anywhere! My cousin and I always make it a point to hit up the Hard Rock in every city. Staff was very friendly. Great location!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I was walking around downtown nashville trying to find a good place to eat. This is our first time downtown. An male employee was standing outside telling his specials to walkers but gave us an unfriendly nod. I really hope this is a diverse restaurant. You had great reviews however that caused us to keep walking.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Great variety of whiskey, knowledgeable bartenders, live music, and central location. I definitely would come back if I'm ever back in town!

name: The 5 Spot
text: Good ol fashioned fun!!  Motown Monday was awesome! So much dancing, sweating, laughter, good music and great energy! Wish what places like this back home!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Pulls in a decent interactive crowd with their live music.  Space to both listen and to dance.  Drinks are average, bartenders only know traditional drinks and aren't the friendliest.  The crowd is fun though, very mingly.  There is a seating area too.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Rudest staff ever!  Loved how they took the guy's 100 dollars then asked him to get off stage and leave.  Most terrible place ever! Avoid! . Absolutely the worst place ever. can't wait to get back to arizona.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
This was our first stop on Broadway, and it may have been my favorite. The band that was playing was super fun and played Zac Brown Band per my request, which I am all about.  They were really good, too! 

It was relatively busy, but still pretty early in the night. We got a seat on the balcony, but quickly moved downstairs when a table opened up. The beer selection wasn't the most stellar, but I'll let it pass. This was truly a Nashville experience. Come here if you are visiting.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: We hit up The Stage on Broadway on our first night in Nashville! The music was great, the drinks were cold and the people were awesome. It was the perfect amount of people (not to crowded but not empty either) and the wait staff and security were great.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: No refrigerator in a $200 room, air won't go under 72 period, king club access useless, coffee machine messed up 2 days straight, staff unsure of packages added to room for anniversary or honeymoon, I've stayed in Days Inn's that were quieter, every move next door or in hall you hear, bathroom really small, lobby nice and room clean other than that a $80 a night hotel and I had a king club room $550 for 2 nights, robbery!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Best drinks in town!  Our bar tender/ waitress Faith was fantastic...friendly, mixes the best drinks in Nashville and a great waitress too.  We each had a Jack Daniels Low Rider... Totally wonderful !! The banana-strawberry Coloda was tasty too!
We had veggie burgers with salad. The burger had a huge, fresh portobello mushroom on it. The burgers were quite large and cooked  just right.  The salad was full of dried cranberries and bacon. Everyone was in costume for Halloween!!this is a 'must go' place when we are in Nashville,TN !

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Above average service, exceptional memorabilia, very clean, and flavorful food with valuable portion sizes.  Biggest down falls is very little country music and no items priced under $11.  Two levels with adequate space.  Definite place to go for a drink and big meal.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Spent 4 nights here as part of a Haunter's Convention. yes, you read that right HAUNTERs. You know, people who run haunted houses.  The hotel is large, it actually wraps around itself and so getting lost is possible, but you will find your way back, eventually. 

The lobby is spacious and quite pretty, the elevators are at the oddest angles but stately and proud.  I was on the 2nd floor, which happens to be the club floor - We'll talk about the club lounge in a moment. 

While I was not in a Club Room, I had a friend who had one, so I was able to see the differences.  My room was 2 beds, with a lot of extra room, but the view, well, there wasn't much of one, except of the air handling units. Still I had a balcony.. *shrug*

My friend had a club room, King sized bed LOTs of excess room and a balcony that over looked the pool - Winter, so no one was out in it. And it was in need of a cleaning, but still, a better view than I had.  Because he had the club room, he invited me to the club lounge, the first thing I noticed in there was the overwhelming stink of the garbage can.  It needed to be attended to both times I visited.  Other wise, they provided a nice breakfast, with pastries, hot entrees and drinks as well as coffee and lattes for those at the club level. 

The hotel handled the convention very well.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: At first we were disappointed to find that this wasn't actually located downtown, but the service and for the price of the rooms it worked out well. The receptionist checking us in was very kind and helpful. She got us in early, but gave us the option of waiting to have a nicer room. We declined just so that we could freshen up and get started on the day. The room was a good size and had 2 armchairs, where most hotels might just give you one. We also got a balcony with a view of the pool. This wouldn't be good if you wanted to avoid hearing people outside there, but we were barely around. The bathroom was a bit tight, but it did the job. The fitness center enabled me to get my cross-fit work out of the day in.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: This hotel was average as far as cleanliness and the location was random, but if you don't mind those things then you're fine, stay here. If you are traveling with a dog and think you have found the hotel for you, THINK AGAIN. We were told at check-in there would be a $100 fee if a complaint was made about our dog barking and we could not get there in a reasonable time to calm her down. They also claimed they would check on the room to confirm the complaint. INSTEAD, the hotel called us and said a complaint was made so we will INSTANTLY be charged a fee. We arrived within 10 minutes and our dog was not barking AT ALL when we arrived. My husband talked to the staff and they told him they didn't hear her barking either....but we were still being charged. If this hotel just wants to charge at automatic $100 pet fee, that's what they should call it up front. That way pet lovers will find elsewhere to stay. ADDITIONALLY, don't leave any items behind in your room. Sadly, I left my hair straightener behind and I called the hotel the next day, they told me I had to leave a voicemail with lost and found and they would contact me promptly. I called lost and found every other day for over a week and received NO call back. I finally had to force someone to talk to me on the phone and they said they might have my item. I told them I left a black Sedu hair straightener behind and 24 hours later they finally called me back about my REVLON CURLING IRON. Yeah, not exactly my Sedu hair straightener. Obviously I know you should always check your room before you leave, but I have left items behind at hotels on a few occasions and the staff saved my items for me. No such luck at this hotel.

name: The Valentine
text: Some of the best times we have had downtown nashville, there are so many different venues to choose from, but the Valentine nailed it. There are some amazing people that work there GREAT service an the food was amazing an very well priced! Thank you Nashville.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: Pretty good spot. I believe they have the most spicy quesadillia in town. I had the cheeseburger and it wasn't bad at all! We really didn't like the fact the parking lot was chained off.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text:
You got 4 stars just for you Brisket Sandwich. So after all my fellow yelpers said you had great brisket i decided to give it a try last nite. 

Smoke Ring was very nice
Smoke Flavor was Very nice
Perfectly sliced
I like the way you combined the fatty end with the lean end on the sandwich which gave a nice balance.

Guys, sorry but you need to have mom teach you something about tater salad LOL.Basically i did not need it after the sandwich

Thanks yelpers....

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: We were walking by and decided to stop in and were so happy we did. Such a cool place and Rochelle is one of the best bartenders ever! She's just the cutest and so incredibly NICE! Felt like we were best friends by the time we left. Got to hear some great music while we were in too. If we didn't have to leave for the airport, no telling how long we would've stayed! Can't wait to come back!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: My wife, two kids and myself all stayed here at the Sheraton Music City Hotel in Nashville, TN for a week. The rooms were extremely comfortable, the staff super friendly and the restaurant and room service were F-A-N-T-A-S-T-I-C. Truth be told, the breakfast buffet is over priced, but the other meals were extremely fair price wise, so it averaged out.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The band plays a diverse genre! And the security is so cute  ladies, don't miss out! I went to the bar on February 28 and one of the security guys caught my attention... Best people best security best guys one security with a straw hat caught my attention you'll know who I'm talking about when you see him

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
We drove to Nashville from our area, three plus hours away, to eat here. My son wanted to eat at this location since he'd eaten st the location in Atlanta. He loved it so I was excited to experience it with him in Nashville. The atmosphere wasn't what I thought it would be, probably my fault as I was feeding off of his 16 year old excitement. The staff was friendly and the food was good, just good though.
We wanted to buy something for my daughter since she didn't make the trip with us but the selection in the restaurant was uber small so we were told that they bigger "gift shop" was not in the restaurant, but down at the end of the parking lot. That was different but the selection was indeed better. We did end up buying an over priced hat pin. We'll do a little more research before our Next trip. As I said, I think my expectations were too high. It was just good food and nice staff, nothing super special.

name: Limelight
text: I am a huge fan of Limights Friday night happy hour. The establishment is a huge warehouse and when you walk in it can be overwhelming, but after taking advantage of their 3-4-1 drinks (before 7 I believe) I'm sure you'll be able to relax and unwind from the week. I love the DJ who spins old school and new school faves, so you can definitely catch yourself a line dance or two or just people watch! Hungry? Need to coat your stomach? They have fresh, hot, delicious food that's definitely worth the wait in line. It gets more and more crowded as the night goes on but it's always a guaranteed good time :)

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text:
Not bad. 

We decided on this place because we wanted to sit outside on a lovely night but the 4 person band playing outside was quite loud, so we opted to have dinner inside instead. Our group of three had a bit of an issue ordering; I think our waitress was the only one working inside and she had a number of tables, but once we snagged her we ordered the fried jalapenos, hot dry rubbed wings, brisket, ribs and sausage. 

Everything is a la carte and the sides cost $2 and some change extra and they are not large portions at all.  I wasn't blown away with the cowboy beans as a side, and whatever you do, DON'T order the corn on the cob. It is not grilled but rather dumped into boiling water and cooked. Oh, and it's tiny. I enjoyed my wings but I have to say I prefer the smoked wings at Neighbors better...sorry. The brisket is pretty spectacular and I enjoyed the ribs as well. 

Overall, food was pretty good but the highlight of the meal for me was the fried jalapenos. Those were killer. But...should those really be the highlight of the meal? I think not.

I'd come back but would focus on the brisket or choose another dish instead.

name: The Bridge
text: I ordered two sandwiches and fries. I asked for ranch. I got one pack. The fries weren't even cooked. I expect SOOOOO much more for $40 of sandwiches. I will NEVER order from this place again!!!! It was absolutely HORRIBLE!!!!!!!!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Never order the nachos, for they have little to NO toppings on them. Paid $9 extra for steak for there to be the smallest amount of steak I could have possibly been given. Josh was my waiter and was extremely rude and slow about refills. When I told him my meal was wrong he said that I was in the wrong for not asking him about when I first ordered and my meal was not changed.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: I had planned to attend a conference for a week in April. I canceled the reservation and they charged me. I have called the hotel all morning. No one answer's the phone, they have transferred me around to 4 different call center's and I can't seem to talk to a live person.
