No one call's me back to entertain my question or try and resolve my situation. Tried all morning to contact Mary Roman or Charley Morales. This hotel is chaos, avoid it!!! Will never stay in a Sheraton or Marriott hotels, ever.............

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Saturday night was the most fun I've ever had in this bar!! Love music, all the write songs!! The crowd plays off of each other's energy! We spent hours here drinking and dancing! Most fun bar we hung out in our entire weekend trip!! I love that the bars in Nashville have a jug of water with a stack of cups next to it to help yourself and to cut the bar lines down.

name: The 5 Spot
text: I came here for QDP over the weekend and had SO much fun!! They had free bottles of water, awesome perk. The music was great, the vibe was everything you'd hope a dance party would be, and the people were too much fun. They had a photo booth and a small stage to dance on. I can't wait to come back. East Nashville never disappoints!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Great little bar. Love the vibe and the atmosphere. Super nice staff. Great music!!! Will be back!!!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Three levels of live country music. Ample space for groups of people just wanting to dance, sing and drink to some good music.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
California Crew here. 

Great music, Staff is great.

I'd like to give a specific shout out to Grace at the topside bar. There's a bunch of us west coasters in Nashville for the first time and she's truly a rockstar amongst a bunch of great folks.

Thank you lass for putting up with us and be better at your job than almost everyone we met on the bar scene in NSH. 

Looking forward to coming back!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Worst ever literally 40 mins and still counting for our damn check and its not that busy.  Completely unacceptable time is money and I don't have time to waste.  Stay far away from this place, its really not even that good "Hard Rock" is just a name!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
I really enjoyed the 3 piece band!  They were playing requests and the crowd was very enthusiastic.  The bartender was friendly and prompt and my drink was affordable.
I very much enjoyed my 30 minute stop in.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
The security wouldn't let us in on CMA Fest. We had planned to spend the evening there (from 5 til close) drinking and eating with bartender Mallory.

We were denied entrance per the Security Guard. We decided to go down to Tootsies instead and stayed there until 1am.

I WOULD NOT recommend this bar if you are looking to have a good time.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
Here for funky music $10 cover 
Bring id
Wow we came for a show on Saturday night and was suppose to start at 9pm but it was 1030 and hasn't started yet! They were still trying to set up and it was for funky music yet since it was Cinco de mayo -- they were just playing the "themed" music. We waited until 1030 and realize that they were stalling this whole time. 

My local friends love this place and took us here because they usually come on Sundays and they were as outraged and thrown off as we were that this was acceptable.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The hotel has a beautiful lobby and that's about all I can say good about this hotel.  There is only one set of elevators that you can use a luggage cart on.  Hallway after hallway of rooms,  be prepared to walk a long time.  It's hotter than can be inside.  Ordered 4 cans of soda,  an ice cream sundae,  and a bowl of banana pudding.  $41!!!  And they weren't that good.  It's Nashville,  find something else.  You'll be a while lot happier.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
I was supposed to be walking back to the hotel. I was seduced by a saxophone, as one is. Rarely have I heard saxophone on Broadway, so I took a chance and went in. It has that divey feel but turns out, it seems like Sunday nights are unofficial social swing dancing nights at Whiskey Bent. A phenomenal band playing *real* country music (not the pop stuff), and fun-as-all-get-out swing dancers hanging out. If you're looking for where the locals hang out, this is it. 

I had a fantastic time, the dancers recognized right away that I wanted to dance. Everyone is so friendly, right down to the bouncer. I loved the various whiskey-themed art on the walls. Everyone packed up around 10:30pm to head to Robert's Western World, so I followed suit. I can't wait to come back.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I just wish they would clean their ceilings.   This is actually a collection of dust and mold. Anyways had to leave bc my friend had an asthma attack. Otherwise God Bless

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: This was good, not great. The food and service was decent, but really expensive. Steak was prepared as ordered, but was too heavily seasoned.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: They have the worst customer service I've ever encountered. Their lack of organizational abilities lost them a lot of business tonight from many different people. Don't stay here!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Awesome service and great music. Highly recommend the moonshine drinks. Get there early as it seemed to get packed around 7pm

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: My son and his friend are musicians and were so excited to have lunch here today! We have been to at least 10 locations in other cities and had great experiences. This was a bad experience. The food was mediocre, some of the food was served cold and the service was horrible! I asked for a manager who never came. I asked for the check and it took 20 minutes for them to get around to providing it. We live in Franklin and will not be back!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
The Sheraton Music City hotel was one of the official hotel partners of Yelp Spring Break Nashville 2014. The official hotel partner rate was $139 per night but I ended up booking with Living Social for only $109 per night which included a $30 dining voucher per night. Because I am a Starwood Preferred guest Gold Member, I was upgraded to a junior suite and even received complimentary cocktails coupons up to $15 each. In total I paid $128.12 per night for the three night stay which included $90 in dining credit and $45 in drink credit. Definitely a great value!

The hotel amenities include a complimentary airport transfer service, outdoor pool, 24 hour gym, jacuzzi, and an indoor heated pool. There's also an on-site restaurant and lounge. Food service stops promptly at 12 midnight even though the bar is open much later.  Not even cold items are available after 12 midnight.

One slight draw back is that the hotel is located about 15 minutes from the downtown area. The hotel has two shuttles which could easily schedule complimentary shuttle service to the downtown areas at certain times of the day. Other than that it's a fantastic hotel and I would definitely stay here again!  

Thanks so very much Janece for LS & Daniel at the Front Desk!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Sorry guys, once again a bar waiter that would much rather puts around the bar dancing with other employees that wait on customers; when did they quit emphasizing customer service; I don't pay for customer avoidance!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: My salad was very bland and old also my chicken was very overcooked and dry. I expected more based on other reviews but it was a dissapoinment. Go try the restaurant before you look at reviews it might be good to some and not to others.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Bartender on the top floor on 11/09/18 around 10:15 pm was so nasty. I doubt I am the 1st to tell you that. She needs to go.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
After many years as a Sheraton customer I doubt I would ever book again. The hotel itself is in a good location and the room was clean and spacious. In fact everything was fine, until about 9PM when the entire hotel lost power. Guest began to run amok in the courtyard screaming and yelling. Pitch black darkness in the room. A call to the front desk yielded little information. With nothing else to do my wife and I tried to sleep through the night. There was no AC so it was super hot and uncomfortable. 

The power seems to have been restored around 5:30AM. After getting some sleep I went to the front desk to find out if they would be offering any compensation for the loss of service.  I was told there was no discount or vouchers be given because it was a regional blackout. I asked if there was a generator. I was told yet, but it failed to power up and give power to the hotel.

For the price I paid, I expect the hotel to have a generator. And I expect it to work. If not I expect to be compensated. I called Sheraton corporate hoping for a resolution. They took down my complaint and passed it on to the hotel and said they would be getting back to me.

Guess what they never did? Not a call back. Nothing. No apology. No measly discount off a future stay or anything. Poor customer service. Too cheap to give me half off one nights stay during which I lost expected services and now the company will likely miss out on thousands of future revenue from this guest.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: I've eaten in and taken out and have loved the food both times. The food is very smoky so if you like that this is your place. My favorite is the smoked mushrooms which I haven't yet seen anywhere else in Nashville. My only concern is that I haven't yet seen the restaurant crowded, I'm not sure what's keeping others away, hopefully they just don't know about it yet.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Our stay here couldn't have been better, perfect everything!  :D



ps- every room has a private balcony!

name: The Valentine
text: Prob one of fave bars on broadway! Highest rooftop and awesome view! Best customer service & their menu is amazing! Gotta have the chicken sandwich!!!! Hands down awesome staff & entertainment too!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: small but loud! T-shirt's are a bit pricey and beer was 5.50 each...it was like a big party in there

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This venue is by far the best and most fun on the strip. We stopped in several of the hot spots and they were over crowded and the drinks were $12 for a tiny plastic cup. This place is on spot with an amazing band that plays non stop. The drinks were very affordable and strong pours. I can't wait to return for another fun evening. The staff also looks so happy and it makes the vibe feel alive.

name: Ray Stevens CabaRay Showroom
text:
Having no idea what to expect, not really being too familiar with Ray Stevens I was very pleasantly surprised. 

We were taking the In-Laws to celebrate their Birthday and they also seemed to really enjoy themselves.

The food itself was pretty good, and it arrived pretty quickly after we were seated (as well as an abundance of rolls).  It's not the best meal you've ever had, but for Dinner Theater food I presume this to be up to snuff.

The truly confusing part is this. Since you are prepaying for the DINNER, the gratuity is not included in that because Drinks and Dessert are NOT included. As a result, the waitstaff, to avoid being short changed deliver a bill that includes the price of the meal (But not the show) as well as any drinks or dessert you ordered. This is confusing and makes it look like you are being charged a second time for the food, but they do this simply to produce a ticket that includes the correct Gratuity guide. Otherwise the hardworking staff would be tipped on 6 dollar Bourbons and 5 dollar Banana Puddings for 2 dollar tips instead of 7 dollar tips for 40 dollars of food, drinks and desserts. 

The best part for me was that dinner seating starts PROMPTLY at 6, the show starts PROMPTLY at 7:30 and ends PROMPTLY at 9.

The show itself was wonderfully fun and I look forward to coming back!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Nachos were great and beer made me happy... our server and new friend key, is awesome!!!! Worth the visit especially to take a look at the memoribilia

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: First time in Nashville and this bar is my favorite! Great live music and bartenders are amazing! Venue is perfect for loud music!

name: The 5 Spot
text:
This place is soooooooooooo much fun!!! 
I swear I've never had as much fun as I've had in the bar. The bartenders are super nice and the drinks come out great. I happily paid my $200 tab because I was thoroughly entertained . I will definitely be coming back to this place every time I'm in Nashville. Thanks for the good time 5spot

name: The Bridge
text: I am RAVING. This place is absolutely amazing. After a not so stellar customer service experience at the actual Renaissance Hotel, our service at The Bridge Bar & Restaurant was probably the best service I've ever received-- anywhere. I travel for business and pleasure all year long, from LA to Boston, and never experienced this level of customer care. Judy was so sweet right from the start. When we told her about my friend's unfortunate experience here in Nashville, from losing her cell phone/wallet, to getting locked out of our room in the middle of the night, Judy was SO sympathetic to everything we had been through, and immediately offered us an appetizer on the House. We ordered 2 (much needed) glasses of wine, and within a few minutes, John Campbell, the Director, came over and told us that Judy told him all about our stressful trip, and he had arranged for us to get a ride to the airport with the hotel's driver, free of charge! We really needed some positive vibes, and these two were like angels sent to save us! It doesn't stop there either ya'll, our drinks were on the House, as was our meal. I'm crying. Food, drinks, service, EVERYTHING was exceptional. I 100% recommend this Bar/Restaurant to anyone in the Nashville area. I will be coming back every time I'm here! Love, love, love.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: This place is great. Lots of good moonshines to try. Jalapeño one is definitely my favorite. There's always good music in this bar.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
Despite the London Fog-style smoke hovering at all times and the super small and kind of stuffy space, I love the 5 Spot.  Seriously, I do.  It's some sort of hidden gem of musical amazingness and I have yet to go here and leave having not enjoyed myself immensely.  The first time I went was when a friend asked me if I wanted to hear this awesome new band called the Alabama Shakes.  I don't regret that next long day of work at all.  

I have seen so many fantastic acts since that remind me of everything that is amazing and fun about living in Nashville.  From a guy quite literally standing on while playing his upright bass to a drummer practically dancing into the audience while playing, the 5 Spot has provided me with the opportunity to see some of the most fun musical acts I would have never heard of otherwise.  And they have so many other special events, like 80s dance parties.  Seriously, can more places do that?  

The bartenders do a great job trying to stay on top of the orders of demanding patrons, so be patient.  It's always inexpensive to go (like the time it was a $10 cover but I got the bands new record as part of my admission) and always a good time.  Be prepared to sweat and reek of smoke and not care because you're having a blast.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
A great place to listen to music.  They specialize in great acoustic acts until 6pm, then good bands.  Tuesday night is 80's Rock night - "Twang Free Tuesday" with Randy Nations - terrific guitarist.
No food, but a super friendly bar staff, and a great sounding room.  The animals on the walls and floor (bear) were all killed by a bow, if you want some trivia.
Sunday Funday starting at noon with Shawn Mayer and Mark Dooley is a must see - Shawn is an amazing singer/songwriter.  Try to catch Kinsey Rose when she sings here.  Brin, Laura, Shawna, Molly, Charley, and Sara are great bartenders!
Great bar for music and whiskey!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: We stopped in for drink and to listen to some good music. It was just an okay experience. The band was pretty generic, honestly. And then they were passing the tip bucket around before even finishing the first set. Just not a lot of personality in this one.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We stopped in here for dinner because we wanted to get away from the strip and the bar scene. We picked Hard Rock because we've always gotten good food and service at any location we've stopped in to. The service was very slow and it wasn't because they were busy. The food did not look or taste fresh. It tasted like something they had sitting on a burner in the kitchen for hours. We ordered ribs and they were almost inedible. It was so difficult to get our server's attention, we gave up on complaining, we just wanted to pay our bill get back to our hotel. Summary: We spent almost 100.00 for 2 people ordering just a meal each, an appetizer and a couple of non alcoholic drinks - A high price to pay for disappointment.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The most rude, arrogant, bullying door staff of any venue on Lower Broad. Stay far away from this place unless you enjoy being assaulted for simply asking them a question.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
This is really an airport hotel, but you wouldn't know it by it's amenities, food venues and size.

It's huge... and the employees are top notch.

There are a lot of large group events held here, but don't let that scare you away. They have ample staff to assist at a moments notice.

Rooms are nice and big, as is the lobby, restaurant and bar.

Good choice if you don't want to trek downtown.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: So far my favorite spot on broadway! Band on the first floor was sooo good last night we didn't want leave to check  out other spots! We are definitely will back tonight! Drinks and crowd were good too!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: My complaint is in regards to reservations.  They are the worse to deal with. The reason for my travel was because my father had a stroke and I'm driving. I made a reservation and called back to cancel within less than an hour. They will not cancel and are charging me the full rate of $189.  This was a family emergency not a leisure family time.  I realized when I arrive it will be at 5am in the morning arrival and would have to leave a few hours later.  There customer service along with management is extremely poor.  I will never do service with them again.  Extremely poor management and waited an hour to deal with a supervisor and still no feedback.  Amazing how they stay in business and being so heartless in this time.  If I could give them no stars I would.

name: The Valentine
text: Probably my favorite spot on Broadway! Went on a Thursday afternoon and they had AMAZING live music on the rooftop (s/o to Spencer Jordan Music!) The bartender was super sweet, it wasn't overly packed, and the drinks were yummy. Stayed till the band left and had a blast!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Ordered my burger well done and it came out rare. For the price they charge here you'd think they could cook your food correctly. Also wanted to sub Mac and cheese for the fries and it came out with fries.  The nachos were okay.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Great patio overlooking broadway and the manager, Molly, was extremely friendly! I would recommend coming here for a meal or casual drink to anyone looking for a fun spot!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: As a resident of downtown I hosted a group of friends in town at The Stage. There was a huge crowd, a lot of pushing and 2 of our phones were stolen. We asked a bartender who proceeded to tell us that was the 6th time that night a phone was stolen. I went to buy a drink and found my ID and credit card were stolen out of my purse attached to my body. The person went immediately to GH mall and spent $10,000. I mentioned this to my neighbors who said The Stage is known for pick pocketing. As a resident of downtown I want to make tourists aware of this as it is a known problem and The Stage has not addressed it. BE CAREFUL!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: We were unaware there was some sort of "dog show/convention" going n during our stay. So between the allergies (we are allergic to dogs) and the constant barking, our stay was less than pleasant. It would have been nice if the hotel had both notified guests of the dog show/convention since they would have known in advance, and kept the dogs in a specific area of the hotel in consideration of the rest of the paying guests.

name: Robert's Western World
text: My favorite Honky Tonk in town. Along the Broadway strip, your typical night can be very hit or miss-- but not Roberts. Always fantastic music with a crowd actually interested in listening. For a proper Nashville experience, it's a must.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Was doing the Broadway thing and slid into Roberts after starting out at Silver Dollar. The band was serving a serious slice of blues with a young lad on lead guitar slaying his axe. They went into a long Allman bros. song with an incredible solo. After the tip jar went around they started a C/W set. Before I could lament the loss of the blues, our fine young lad was tearing up the licks. Please don't miss Roberts - it's the real deal. Oh yeah - cheap beer too.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place to see some country/western music in Nashville!  (Less of a tourist location compared to the other spots close by) Since you didn't come here for the bbq get a fried bologna sandwich and enjoy the great music. Tip the staff and the musicians(there is no cover)! Will definitely go back if I am in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Really fun place. Great band. Not sure her name but i had a blonde bartender that was great and really attentive. The fried bologna sandwich is the thing to eat but I didn't love it. Just my preference. I still recommend trying it just for the experience.

name: Legends Corner
text:
Man, our bartender 
Really jacked up our drinks so
No thanks to Legends

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I am not sure why this place has 3.5 stars. In my opinion, it's a guaranteed good time with fab food! We had a bachelorette dinner there for 18 girls who flew in from several different cities throughout the country. I wanted to make sure the bride to be and the other gals had delicious food, good ambiance & service, and great live music. That is exactly what we got. Since we had such a large party we had to choose one of the many pre fixe options. We were able to adjust the menu we selected since we had a handful of vegetarians, to two veggie entrees (veggie lasagna and Portobello quinoa- YUUMM) and two meat (the steak was perfectly charred). Each dish was so unique and worth every cent (which wasn't much!). To top it off with the trio dessert, let's just say we were craving more. The toffee chocolate ball was to die for. Tiffani, who helped arrange the menu was a pleasure to work with and even personalized the menu for us! Natalie served us the entire evening and put up with our antics. :) She was such a great server.The band was fun and entertaining as well. The bride got to go up on stage and chat with them, it was a riot.   I am giving it a 5 on every level! Made our Nashville experience all that much better!

name: Legends Corner
text:
During our Broadway bar crawl this spot hands down had the most consistent line up of amazing live music. 

Every time we stopped in we were completely blown away by the singers on stage. 

It's a great bar for people watching as well. The bartenders here are very polite and actually pour pretty great drinks. 

This should be a stop during your Nashville adventures! Cheers! 

Stop in and request some of your favorite county songs!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great night, food was great with a wide selection. The entertainment on the night was awesome. Only problem was we never booked a table and had to sit at a bar area, a first come bases. Had a great view of the band however so wasn't to bad!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Cheap beer.  Great atmosphere. Live music in Nashville is awesome  and Tin Roof keeps the vibe going.

name: Robert's Western World
text: F*ck every other bar on Broadway after coming to Roberts western world. Bartenders are always amazing to me, bands are amazing and no BS country, just the real sh*t. Fried bologna sandwiches, makers mark on the rocks, with some killer live music and you have me sold.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Mine and my boyfriends favorite place to go to in nashville for a special night out. It's great food and always love music, only thing I dislike is I feel like the tables are on top of each other, if you're looking for something a little more private or romantic I would suggest somewhere else

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: First place we stopped in on our trip through Nashville.  Great music, no cover charge, cold beers, good service and good crowd.  What's not to like about this place.  Didn't have any food.

name: Legends Corner
text: Tonya and Issac was behind the bar and slinging drinks, the band was entertaining and fun, met some really cool locals. Overall a great experience and will be a regular stomping ground whenever i am in town.

name: Robert's Western World
text: The bartenders are amazing here especially Becky at the far end. I didn't even watch the band I just watched her work. Bands are really good. The bar has a lot of energy. And a lot of people eat here From what I can tell.

name: Legends Corner
text: My wife and I really enjoyed the music here today.  Harold

name: Music City Center
text: EW, EW, and more EW! So was there for a military ball, and I get it you probably gave us a discount. . .whatever. Food was HORRIBLE chicken was raw, NO not undercooked, not to "our" liking RAW. One piece was still bleeding and when it was brought to manager? supervisor? S attention we didn't get any concern or care, just oh want another piece? UMMM no thanks dying or getting sick on raw chicken and who knows what else it touched not my idea of a good night. Couldn't even enjoy the veggies those were also undercooked and had a bad vinegar sauce on them. so left early and had tacobell for dinner. Really thought we were in for a great night at a great venue, boy was I proven wrong.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Good time.  Good music.  Food was served fast.  Limited menu.  Cheeseburger just right- nice and greasy.  Fries and onion rings also good.  Like a little hole in the wall- just what I was looking for.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Had a great time. chose the guided tour and our guide was not only witty but very informative. amazing history and a must see by any fan of music period. LOVED coming here.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Overall disappointing. With all of the AMAZING places around Nashville, Sambuca has to step it up. Service was wonderful and the manager was very apologetic, but the food took nearly 2 hours and arrived cold. I don't recommend it, honestly.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Loved this auditorium. Just being there, I could understand the whole country music history.
Hope I can watch a show there. Introductory movie they are showing at the Ryman was impressive. Well done movie.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This place is super fun. We stopped by here on the YSB UYE bar crawl this past Friday, I believe it was.

Apparently the musicians don't get paid, so make sure to tip them well - their only payment is tips. 

We all congregated on the top floor, which was a *tiny* bit quieter than the bottom floor, which was nice.

I'd come here again if ever in the area!

name: Legends Corner
text: One hell of a bloody mary. Great music too. We went around lunch time too. Bartender was nice too.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I've been here multiple times for my favorite shows in town. The Ryman is legendary for a reason. I've never been to a place where the audience respects the bands and which holds a communal reverence as well as the Ryman.

For example, in comparing the Ryman to the Tabernacle in Atlanta, the venues are about the same capacity and have about the same-level acts come through. However, shows at the Ryman have a way of capturing the audience's love and respect that makes you feel like you're face-to-face with the performer paying them their personally owed respects for their time and efforts. It's a really unique feeling that I only get at the Ryman.

I could go on and on about the details of the place but you really must go experience a show here if you haven't already. Yes, the pews aren't super comfortable and they pack the audience in but you don't care about those things once the show starts.

Pros:
Best concert venue I've ever been to. The sound, atmosphere, history, and audience all add up to the best concert experience you can imagine.

Cons:
It was under construction when I went to see Ben Howard so it wasn't quite as pretty as it normally is.

Overall:
Go. Just go.

name: Robert's Western World
text: You cannot find better music! The food (for bar food) is great. I had a wonderful hamburger and fries. They make real drinks. You do not have to wonder if the bartender really added alcohol to your rum and coke. Back to the music, if you do not want get up and dance it must be intermission. The crowd is fun and oh did I mention that the music is the best on Broadway?

name: Robert's Western World
text: Service is great! Burgers are ok but the fries and grilled sandwiches are on point. Live music is one of the best on Broadway!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Good music, quick snack. 

Stopped in here towards the end of the night for a baloney sandwich.  Comes with a bag of chips and PBR but we upgraded to whiskey.

name: Musicians Corner
text: Free music festival, food trucks, bars, gorgeous setting - honestly, what else could you ask for? The kids zone is a great spot for the little ones to burn off some energy. Exceptional lineup all month. Get yourself to Centennial Park to listen to some tunes, sip a Mint Julep or Yazoo and revel in summertime

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Historic? Yes. Great sound? Yes. Great acts? Yes. But, it is hands down the most uncomfortable venue to see a concert. They oversell the church pew benches so you are smashed together. I'm not a big person, but it seems like everyone else is - and I prefer a bit of personal space, especially if I'm sitting for hours. I've seen a dozen shows there, but I give up. I will not go back until they update the seating or stop overselling the venue.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I would return to Sambuca based off of service alone. Tyler, our server was beyond attentive and was definition of southern hospitality. The food was amazing as well. I had the Shrimp and Crab Scampi, it was delicious and filling. A few people in our group ordered the scallop dish and it was devoured by all. You should definitely get the creme brulee, it was SO GOOD!!! If you're visiting Nashville and need a good spot for food and music add this spot to your list!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Wow! I love this place. I make sure I stop in when I am in Nashville. The show tonight was fantastic and the food is good. Simple, delicious bar food straight from the flat top.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: With many music choices in the live seeing, they have two bands playing alternatively through the night. While the food was decent the chicken sandwich was more like for food but the salad was very good the music more than made up for it

name: Nashville Municipal Auditorium
text: This venue has a pretty old and musty feel to it.  I'm definitely not a huge fan.  For as old as it is though, it's clean and the drink prices are a a dollar or 2 less than Bridgestone Arena.  I wouldn't not go to a show here due to the venue but it's not somewhere I'm dying to go back to either.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
First night in Nashville ever. Wandered in for dinner with the kids because the vibe sucked me off the street. Good service but very casual. Band playing were solid and tolerating a few annoying drunks. NFL games playing on a number of screens which is a bonus. Good price, serving Mexican mostly. 
Wished the kids were at the hotel so I could of enjoyed this place a lot more!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Drinking a Hop Perfect IPA...Great beer and listening to the Don Kelly Band. When in Nashvegas, one of many places to visit!

name: Legends Corner
text: Another great bar on Broadway. A lot of good energy and good music. There's not much which separates this one from the others, but for no cover, good music, and a nice atmosphere you can't go wrong with Legends.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Stopped back in this place just for a night cap and dessert -- the bar area upstairs is open seating.  We had another phenomenal time.  Great music, great service, great drinks and dessert.  I'd recommend this spot to anyone looking for great live jazz and a fun atmosphere to celebrate something.

Just FYI, if you don't do valet the pay lot up the street is now $15 for the evening.

name: Legends Corner
text:
Awesome dive-ish bar on Broadway! 

Yes, Broadway is the tourist-y strip in Nashville, but it's worth checking out, esp. if you're a tourist.

(Make sure you check out the rest of the city though, too.)

Legends: live music, strong drinks, ample space, fun/kitschy "Music City" décor.

Nice ladies' bathrooms! Solid bartenders. 

Not too much else to say, really.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We stopped in here to grab some drinks before lunch. Overall it was a nice place to grab quick food and listen to music. I will say that the music was very loud, so if you plan to have a conversation with the people at your table, this might not be the best place to go. We ordered drinks and appetizers, and sat on the second floor since the first floor was packed. The food we ordered was pretty standard bar food, nothing spectacular.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We did a self guided tour here & it was really nice! This was a great place to see! I'd recommend a visit.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Came here with my family and girlfriend during Christmas leave from overseas.  They do have a military rate and the Ryman is an attractive building...... Although I was sorely disappointed that we were rushed through a "self guided" tour.  The security people were very rude and pushed us through the walkway like cattle closing the doors behind us each section we barely viewed.  I understand that you may have an event to setup for but we were there well before closing time.   My money would of been better off supporting the Country Music Hall of Fame Museum.  


Congrats you get One Star!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We came for the drinks and dessert and we were thoroughly delighted with both. Cory, our waiter, also let me "make my own drink"--the strawberry purée mojito....with no mint. It's called The Brooke, and it tastes like a Sonic drink so be careful; it's a bit too easy to slurp those suckers down with no inhibition. Cory was awesome. We basically became friends by the end of our stay. Loved this place. When I'm back in Nashville, this will be a place I come to.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
We attended the late Opry show at the Ryman on a Saturday.  We showed up at 9:10pm and were left out in the cold night until 9:30pm.  The show was suppose to start at 9:30pm but started around 9:45pm.  There was a fine mist and around 33 degrees that night.  We had my elderly father with us.  Standing in line to get in the door in the wet cold air.  I was extremely worried about my father's health.  I think they were waiting for everyone to get out from the early show.  I have no other explanation on why we were out in the cold air for so long.  I wish I had known we would have to wait outside and would have made different decisions.  Thankfully, to date my father hasn't gotten ill but I have.  I know it is from standing out in the cold mist for so long.  Next time we attend Opry in the winter months we will go to the early show so not to be in the cold so long.

The show itself is like stepping back in time.  The seats are pew style and as Americans are getting bigger they are tight.

We returned later in the week for the back stage tour.  I don't know if we would do it again.  Really the self guided tour gets you everything you learn on the back stage tour.  The tour allows you to see the dressing rooms and stand at the side of the stage.  The entire tour was about 30 minutes.  Everything the guide told us can be read in the self guided tour.  The closest parking lot cost us $20.  I am sure there are other places to park but again with my Dad we wanted to be as close as possible.

The history here is special.  Worth a visit.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
What a waste of money. Nothing printed on my tickets about limited view. I went to guess services and the gentleman looked at a seating chart and replied that my seats were fine. I showed him this photo and he still wouldn't assist me. 

Sounded like a great show and I bet most seats are a great view. Shame.

name: Legends Corner
text:
This place was a little odd, but I liked it.  It's located on a corner (hence the name), right next to Tootsie's and down the block from the Ryman.

My husband and I stopped in for a few drinks on a Saturday afternoon after escaping the 24/7 bachelorette party of Tootsie's.  It wasn't very crowded, which was a nice break.  We were able to settle in at a table and drink some cheap Miller Lites.

The entertainment when we visited was this guy named Buck McCoy.  I guess you could call him a Tim McGraw impersonator?  Musically, he was just ok, but he put on a decent show and was very entertaining.  He also brought on this TERRIBLE Elvis impersonator... which was kinda weird, but again, entertaining.

If you are on Broadway, I'd definitely check this place out.  They have all sorts of country music memorabilia on the walls, which is cool.  It's also a long, narrow space, so you can be all the way at the back bar and still see/hear the band.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place has a cool western vibe. Live music, plenty of bar space, staff is very friendly and knowledgeable of the menu. Drink specials are awesome. Fried bologna is very good as well as the onion rings. If you're looking for a place to grab a drink with some friends, I would recommend this 100%.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Ryman Auditorium has some interesting history and the tour is a must! They bring you in a room and a presentation plays that is very entertaining and educational! The building has so much history! Highly recommended!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Love this place, it's beautiful and a must see while in Nashville but the stage performances and advertising push seems a bit dated, which was sad to see.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Our favorite bar on Broadway - this coming from a girl who has trouble listening to any country made after 1995. We came here for fun after my wedding, and it was the perfect place for a little after-party dancing! What's more, I was wearing my great-grandmother's bracelet (priceless) and after getting home that night, realized it had fallen off. With little hope, I called RWW the next morning and, lo and behold, they had found it and kept it in a safe place until I was able to come get it. Needless to say, I'll be a patron for life.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Mother Church! Amen. What an inexpensive no frills tour that takes you back in time!
 
Arrive on time, make it safely through the TSA-style Security checkpoint and head up stairs.
You file into a small room with multiple benches and a large screen surrounded by old school concert posters. This room - packed with tourists - definitely needed a fan or air conditioning as it got a bit toasty during the opening film.

I learned so much about The Ryman and it's beginning during this video. So, pay attention! It's very well done. Next, you'll move through the double doors and WOW there it is ... the iconic auditorium! Amazing and breathtaking.

It's an easy self-guided tour that will take you as long as you want to spend admiring The Mother Church and the displays donated by artists and their estates.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We had a late lunch at Tin Roof on the first day of our first visit to Nashville and it was a wonderful experience of the Nashville, Broadway music scene.  The food was excellent.  We had a great burger and yummy beef and mushroom quesadilla.  The frosting on the cake was the band, a trio that did a mix of older and newer country songs.  Pedal Steel Guitar, Bass and Guitar were perfect in this space.  It was quiet at lunch, the band took requests and we almost stayed all day.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Nice old fashioned mom and pop operation with good music, tasty fried baloney sandwiches and disgusting wine in a plastic cup.....and our bartender was proud of it when she proclaimed "y'all ain't gonna get no fancy wine in this town"

name: Robert's Western World
text:
omg... $2.50 domestic beer
great live music 
fried bologna sandwich, burgers,  pork chop sandwich....great food at reasonable prices.
don't miss robert's!!!!!

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text: In a city where people are genuinely nice I was unpleasantly surprised by the unprofessional general attitude in this establishment. Rude is an understatement. There are certainly better places to go see musical acts and definitely better food. The menu is tiny and the bartenders make the food???  Okay so maybe you aren't going for food just to see some good music. Technically they are completely disorganized and the place is dark and smells musty.  When I say dark I mean like you can't see dark and the place is a mess. There are certainly better places to go see musical acts. I would skip this place and try somewhere else.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
This place was pretty good. The music was very loud (which I think is typical for Nashville). It's almost hard to hear yourself think. We stopped in for
A snack-we had the loaded tator tots. They were to die for! We had the ranch dressing on the side which was a good idea as there was a lot of cheese on the tots. The service was good and the people were very friendly. I would definitely return for drinks and a snack.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: My wife and I had our Valentine's dinner on 2/13/16.  All the food except our dessert was exquisite.  For starters we had chicken samosas in puff pastry and buca beignets, and for dinner had red snapper bouillabasse and scallops.  The first two drinks we ordered were also exceptional - Sambuca 75 and coconut mojito.  All the food and drinks to this point were creative and delicious.  Less exceptional were the other two drinks we ordered because we got things that were way too sweet, and the cheesecake sopapilla dessert was nothing to get excited about.  The ambiance is very cool and romantic.  There was live music at the front with tables laid out theater-style. We're not fans of loud music where we can't talk to each other, so this was perfect for us - very talented musicians, Tiffany Johnson & Soul Confidant, with a great sound balance that was loud enough for us to be fully engrossed in the music but not so loud that we couldn't carry on a normal conversation.  The service was also very good.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: So some friends asked me to go on an adventure to this new place on Nolensville Rd for lunch today. I had no idea what to expect but was surprised off the bat when I showed up to the old Kroger and saw what they had done to the exterior! It looked great! When we went in there were little shops and kiosks everywhere selling everything from absolutely beautiful Quinceanera dresses to International trinkets to cell phone cases. The food area is set up like a food court with a stage at one end. There were about six walk up food stops and one sit down place at the other end. I went to the place that serves esquites street corn naturally and also got carnitas nachos. All I can say is yum! And as I looked around It looked like all of the portion sizes are great!! They have live music every night! Wednesdays they Wine and Rewind night where they play live 80s and 90s music?!?! Um, sign me up!  Check this place out! It's worth it!

name: Robert's Western World
text: It's a great place, just make sure you're outta there by sundown. At sundown, they basically just turn the amps up to screaming levels and pretend they are as good as the afternoon band, which is not true. The afternoon band plays with purpose and sensitivity and is very tight. The feature band is not tight at all, although they are loud as hell, which apparently is all you need to be to fool this generation of morons.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
This is one of our favorite places to visit for fun drinks, good food and great music ALL of the time. Their music starts earlier than most bars on Broadway and they play a mix of everything including some Country Rock n Roll. Our server Maggie was friendly and brought us our bar drinks pretty quickly. She took our food order and brought out everything just as we wanted. We shared some food and we tried some tacos and sandwiches. The burger was juicy and the toppings were fresh. The Pulled Pork sandwich was just sweet enough and not too stringy for a pulled meat. We really liked the street corn and wished the portion was a little bit bigger for a side order. Nothing gourmet but we just wanted good bar food while we listened to the singers/bands. That is exactly what we wanted. 
This is a chain restaurant/bar and they are opening a location very close to our home. We mentioned to our server how excited we were to be getting a Tin Roof soon and asked if she had any other information for us on when it would be opening. She actually sent over to our table a gentleman named Wes (corporate guy) who gave us some great information. Fingers crossed that we will become regulars to the new Delray Beach, Fl. location and still enjoy our Nashville getaways and visit here when we are in town. 
Thanks for the fun times this past weekend!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
In Nashville Memorial Day weekend with some girlfriends and had to check out Robert's Western World.  One of my good friends from college is an Okie who is old school country to the bone.  He assured us that Robert's was the ONLY real honky tonk on Broadway, so of course, we had to oblige.

The house band was incredible.  The lead singer knew every word to EVERY requested song by heart.  He was the only one all weekend that did NOT have any sort of reference to cheat from while he sang (ipad, iphone, etc).  Of the many bars we checked out, EVERY other singer had an ipad.  Clearly this band REALLY knows their stuff.  Plus they were legit.

Drinks were made well and affordable, and the friend pickles were DELISH.

What a fun afternoon, we had a great time and made some awesome memories.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I'll start with the positives:
1) atmosphere was awesome. The lighting was sophisticated and romantic. The live band was also a great touch and not too loud. We sat upstairs so we have a really nice view. 
2) the service was great. Our waiter was attentive and knowledgeable about the menu. He made some great recommendations to my husband for his whiskey drink and beers.  

The negatives: 
1) for the price, the food was UNDERWHELMING at best.  We ordered the calamari as a starter and it was bland. I'm not sure if Applebees has a calamari dish, but if they do, I'd imagine this would be it. No flavor and rubbery. At this point I was apprehensive about ordering dinner, but we proceeded. My husband ordered the ribeye and I ordered the seabass. Both were pretty bland, and again for the price, I was expecting to be blown away. 
2) our food took close to 40 minutes to come out. A group of six women that came in at least 25 minutes after us got their food before us. 
3) the drinks, while tasty, were WEAK. Again, for the price I was expecting much much more. 

Overall, if a friend was having a birthday party at this establishment I would probably go back. With that said, I'd eat before and just order wine.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I planned my best friend's bachelorette party dinner here and it was more than I could ever ask for. The hosts were so sweet and knew the bride by name, and they put us by the stage and the singer honored our bride to be. Our server, Maxfield, was perfection, recommending so many incredible dishes-- the mozzarella beignets and the shrimp and crab dip were amazing, and the ribeye was the best I've ever had hands down. We came for the ambiance but left happier than we ever could've imagined.  It's a must-try if you're looking for a great night on the town that's not the over-done Honky Tonk stuff!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We did the backstage tour of this place and it was amazing!!!  A must in Nashville!!  It really settles you into the history of country music!!!  After the tour yesterday, we saw Josh Turner & Little Big Town in concert and what an experience!!!  There not joking when they say they have the 2nd best acoustics in the country!!!  WOW...this is an extremely special place to see a concert!  What an honor!  Definitely see something here if you can, you will not be disappointed!!!!  It seats about 2,100 people.  We had lower level tickets, but I think I would try the balcony next time.  There definitely isn't a bad seat in the place, but I would just change it up!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Located right in the middle of Downtown Nashville with so many places to choose from.  What drew me here was the live music that was being played.  It was modern music with an attractive looking band.  The bar itself was nice and had plenty of seating.  I ordered a drink at the bar and I love that the bartenders were really nice.  I sat down at a booth and when a table closer to the band opened up I moved up.  

The vibe of this place was so fun.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
This place is THE BEST!! I never been somewhere so unique, different, but quality in every way.

Food: it's a good court styled place, so you have 4 or 5 different restaurant options. El Gaucho Argentinian food is my favorite, but all are delicious. I think my favorite thing about El Gaucho is the sauces. The chimichuri is killer and just makes everything you put it on 'pop.' Bright and fresh, it's delicious! The nacho potatoes they have there are very different but in a good way. I think of them like potato braves (from a Spanish tapas spot) on steroids. The potatoes are perfectly cooked but have the sear and crunch on the outside that seals the deal.

Entertainment: wow oh wow. This place has it all. Salsa lessons. Fire dancers. Aerial dancing. Singers and bands. Truly a sight for sore eyes, no matter when you go. 

People: the kindest. Everyone is friendly and wants you to have fun and experience something new.

I beg of you all, please check this spot out. You will not be disappointed.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
Things I love about this place:
1. SALSA THURSDAYS! Come early on Thursday evening for a free salsa dance lesson and stay to continue dancing all night long!
2. This place is a huge mall full of everything that you could possibly need: food, shopping, groceries, performances, etc. 
3. THE POPSICLES. The popsicle shop is cheap af and they serve delicious popsicles of all kinds of flavors.
4. You can just grab a drink and walk around the mall! 
5. THE CULTURE! Everything here has Mexican culture in it (clearly, by the name), and everyone is incredibly friendly. I had a really great time at this place.

Things I was meh about:
1. The prices of food (not the popsicles). I ordered some pork belly and oysters. The portions were small (but delicious) and our bill came to like $40. It seems a bit over-priced for the area.
2. It seems as if there is still some construction going on in the building, as they continue to fill it with new stores. So you may notice some unfinished work on the opposite side of the building as you walk around.

Overall, I had a great time, and I definitely plan on going back here for some late-night dancing! Excellent space!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I felt like the menu was limited for gluten free.  They were accommodating to alter some of the items. The atmosphere was great with the live band. I will say the band was a bit loud to where we couldn't have a conversation with my family.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: It's been a few years since I came here and recalled it being very nice. Even tonight,  the band is awesome. We were promptly seated. The restaurant was less than half full. However, the promptness in which a server came to take our order was not good. Our party waited 30 minutes for our drink order to ne taken. Jeez...

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: The food - they are not kidding when they say their steak and seafood is really good here. Arielle is the best waitress ever. If you have a chance to request her - do it. She's wonderful. The filet is so awesome - I added shrimp to mine and the Brussels sprouts and the Mac n cheese. The appetizers we had were also amazing. We had the shrimp and crab dip and artichoke with goat cheese and beignets. Everything was incredible but Arielle made the experience all the better.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
If I could give this bar a zero stars I would after the spinless way they fired the best band in town! How do you do that by a text with no explanation?? Adults don't conduct themselves
 like that! How unprofessional!! I can only say it was a huge mistake to get rid of money makers like Eileen Rose and the Silver Threads!!! Hope they can eat stupidity! I can see business going down hill!!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Was there for a couple for my birthday dinner on a Saturday night. The atmosphere was great. Had a live band while we was there & they were wonderful. Definitely a date night, laid back kind of place to go once in a while. I would recommend this place for anyone that just want to enjoy some good floor and live music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Great vibe. Romantic. Sexy.
Decent food. Definitely not of the highest quality but good enough.
Excellent music. Phenomenal band.

Primary complaint: Very slow service. The waiter purposely asked everyone in my large work party of 12 if they wanted soup or salad prior to their order (after we had already ordered several appetizers). It felt manipulative and as a strategy to stretch our wallet when we wouldn't ordinarily a soup or salad in addition to a bunch of appetizers and entrees.

I *think* I'd still come back. But what started off as an excellent night ended up being a very long 3+ hour very
 expensive dinner --$1300 w drinks. When we asked him for the bill, he told us that we "stressed him out." Get it together guy--not good to show your stress publicly.

Don't get me wrong--I pay top money for amazing food and service but although the entertainment was excellent the service missed the mark.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Food is great and the atmosphere is amazing. Great hospitality. I would recommend the street corn and the southern biscuits.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Very friendly staff, good music and a really good cheeseburger for 6:50. It's almost impossible to find a burger this an expensive in Downtown Nashville. Especially one that's good. It's a honky tonk so don't expect fancy furniture and China. But I strongly recommend Roberts.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place is way cool and especially on a hot day. Old school flat top behind bar serving delicious fried bologna. Very nice only bottle beer selection.

name: Legends Corner
text: Classic..loved the music and atmosphere. So Nashville. The band was awesome. We just got drinks there

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Good music, decent food - very affordable. Long history 
Went on a Monday, so kind of quiet.  Decent cheeseburger- good beer selection 
I bet it's hopping on a weekend

name: Robert's Western World
text: Good old country music. Enjoyed every second of it. Nice crowd!!! A must while in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text: True Country and nice staff! Saw Brazil Billy the other night and the fiddle player was amazing! Back in here again as I loved it so much!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Roberts Western World is a dimly-lit, no-frills, real-deal Honky Tonk. It's the perfect place to pull up to the bar and let the fantastic (and loud) live music carry your cares away. This is my favorite Nashville bar.

name: Robert's Western World
text: OMG! Have the fried bologna sandwich! So good. This is a relic, one of the few left in  Nashville! Good food and good drink!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We dined here for lunch and the service and food was great!  The live bands were excellent.  The bathrooms were clean and tidy.  Really nice experience.  Would definitely eat here again!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: The garden burger and sweet potato fries were delicious! Enjoyed the band and the prices were reasonable! Will definitely return when we visit Nashville again!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Bartender HUNTER was rude and unprofessional. He was sarcastic and gave smart a** answers when approached with feedback regarding orders.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Sambuca has a great menu selection! We visited for a a birthday dinner. The food was fabulous. The service was not amazing. We had to wait 30 minutes to get our checks. Also the music was very nice but almost too loud to be able to have a conversation. I will be returning however, the food was really that good!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
So much fun! If you're lucky enough to catch beyond wings circus you are in for an absolute treat. There always seems to be something entertaining going on. It's very family friendly, but wouldn't be bad for a date night either!
The food there is so delish. There are a lot of options, but I'm a big fan of tres gauchos. It would be difficult to make a bad food choice there!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This is a hidden gem!  We were in Nashville with a large group & we bought the 7 attraction city sightseeing pass......had no idea what this place was; but it was on the list & close by so we thought we'd check it out. It is a beautiful auditorium that has so much history & they still have music acts that perform here in the present day.

It starts out with a cute multi-screen film detailing the building's history with lots of great video clips & photos of famous  performers.  There are lots of displays with photos & memorabilia from former performers.  There is also a booth where you can record a recording keepsake.  

The auditorium is beautiful with church pew style seating.  You also have opportunities for photos with instruments right up on the stage.  Cool place!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great line up, great atmosphere, best place in downtown Nashville if you're looking for good music. Don't expect sophisticated cocktails. Fried pickles and Voodoo chicken fingers are very good.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: If you want to see a place rich in history that by grace of some wonderful people was kept alive so all could enjoy then don't miss the Ryman. We did the self guided tour and took away a deep appreciation for all who brought this gathering place together and revived it after many years of neglect.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Nice outdoor seating in the thick of it. Over-priced menu for the average quality of the food. We did enjoy the seared tuna appetizer, but were so disappointed that the ice machine was broken and they could not make some of those tasty-sounding drinks on the menu. I had a very overly sweet passion fruit Mojito. The mint was not at all muddled- which drives me crazy. Yo, bartenders: MINT MUST BE MUDDLED IN MOJITOS!! Over-priced drinks, too. The Havarti tater tots did not taste as if they had any cheese in them, nor could I detect any garlic, as promised. Too bad, they have live music and a good ambiance....but the food does not deliver.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
The cost of the food vs the portion size was unfortunate! Although what little we got tasted good I would have much rather went somewhere else where I could pay less and receive more. I ended up paying for another meal to supplement. 

The restaurant itself was nice and has a very relaxed atmosphere.  The live band was nice but it was a bit more laid back than we wanted to be.

name: Musicians Corner
text: Cool setup! A lot of food truck. You could definitely spend a few hours here if the weather is nice.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Went here to see Shinedown. 
Great place with a lot of nostalgia 
Sound system was very good. Could here them singing even without the microphone 
Pews were a little cramped. But once you stand up you can spread out some.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Due to a last minute trip for valentines weekend, we didn't have a dinner reservation. We went to the tin roof for a couple of drinks and some bar food. The service was great (and fast)! The food was okay. You have great music to listen to while you're here too!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: On Friday November 8th my group & I sat down at a table and enjoyed a couple drinks while listening to very talented singers. It was perfect. The food was delicious, I especially loved the cornbread. It was a perfect location downtown. A place I would highly suggest.

name: Second Fiddle
text: On Friday November 8th during the evening my group & I stopped by second fiddle to have a couple drinks and listen to the talent. The band was very talented and also knew how to entertain a crowd and was excellent at involving the crowd. I even purchased a beer koozie which saldly I had forgotten to take home with me that night. The next day I stopped by the bar, explain my mishap and they gave me my koozie which I was relieved to have again. They are adorable beer koozies. The only downfall to second fiddle is that they did not serve food. We ended up having to leave this establishment in search of food. Just a suggestion for the future. Overall great time, great atmosphere, and great music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great food and atmosphere a must visit in Nashville.  Music is awesome, your girl deserves to be treated to this!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This "mother church of country music" is a sensational place to see a show. I attended an Opry at the Ryman concert, which was great fun and very much enhanced by the venue. It does feel somewhat like a church, with the stained glass in the back of the auditorium and the exquisitely uncomfortable pews for the seating. It positively oozes with history and the acoustics are incredible. Also, for a building seating over 2300, it feels quite intimate. There's a modern lobby with new and clean restrooms and a bar. A gift shop is attached. (Tip: If you enter the gift shop at intermission, you will need your ticket to get back into the show.) Price depends on where you sit, but the view is fine even towards the sides where the tickets are less expensive. (It appears they don't sell the most extreme sides for most events, where the view would be obstructed.)

Seeing a performance here is a must-do Nashville activity.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We were not sure if we were going to enjoy our visit here but it was a pleasant surprise. This is the original grand old Opry location. It includes a video of the history of Ryman Auditorium and they have a display of items that our favorite country western singers wore. You too will be pleasantly surprised

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Called Sambuca days prior to see what they do in terms of a 'birthdays.' I was told that the band can do a 'shout out.'

Reservations were made for the wife's birthday and to just simply 'acknowledge' her birthday, no expectations.

Our waitress and the band, Patton James & the Synchromatics went above and beyond.  The band not only did a 'shout out,' but did a customized version of 'Happy Birthday' for the misses. 

Our waitress, Cody, was attentive, pleasant, and when we ordered dessert; she came back with a lit candle in the desert with 'Happy Birthday' in chocolate icing along the plate.
 Something they didn't have to do.

Also, a lot of the reviews state the food is overpriced?! Compared to what? Applebees or Ocharleys? I guess you would call it overpriced if those restaurants are your frame of reference. The free live music/show is easily worth the price of the food.

My only gripe, is that all the patrons around me, were so self-absorbed in their conversation is that they couldn't appreciate good music or the saxophonist killin' it.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I was able to get the last seat available to see an acoustic Shinedown show and was blown away by the character of this place.  As the old venue for the Grand Ole Opry, the auditorium has a special meaning for the performing artists and because it is small, there is a special connection with the audience.  It appears as a small modern building in the front, but upon entering, you realize you are in a for a unique experience inside a piece of history.  The acoustics are perfection and allow for musicians to perform potentially with no plugs.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: History rich and quite an experience. Hard to describe the reverence in the air. Enjoyed our time here!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
What a beautiful space! 
We took the backstage tour of the Ryman and found it interesting. I think the backstage mostly just brings you in each dressing room (and they show videos in some), but other wise you see the same as a self guided tour. 

Don't forget to exit through the gift shop ;)

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Perfect location and really good food. You're in the best spot for bar hopping in Nashville (without being on the overly populated touristy spots). Music is great too.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: I won't be dining here again. Rachel was our server and the service was almost non existent.  The restaurant was not very busy but the other waiters had to cover for her. The food and wine is mediocre at best.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I can't believe it took me this long to finally see a show at the Ryman. We went to see Jenny Lewis in February, more for the experience of the auditorium than for the choice of musical act (though she's great, too). Now, I'm super excited to come back for another concert soon.

You already know it's an old church with wooden pews. The acoustics, as advertised, were phenomenal. The history just seeps through the walls, and I was impressed how the crowd really respected the atmosphere and the music throughout the night.

If there are any drawbacks, it's probably the lack of more restrooms. But the Ryman can elevate a good performance into something almost mystical. There's no better place to see a show.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This is Nashville. Mother church of country music. I wish I saw a performance here but I was only able to do the tour and that alone was amazing. 
You can feel the history. The old wooden pews, the amazing acoustics its chilling. I really enjoyed the video at the beginning of the tour, I had no idea there was so much behind this place! I history on how it came about was amazing, really tells you the true significance of the Ryman. 
So many picture opportunities but I really had to take my photo "in the circle". It's tradition right? 
To think the Ryman was almost demolished! Thankfully it's history inspired the community and a number of investors to keep it going & have it restored.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: One of our favorite Nashville restaurants--every dish is terrific, service is friendly and wonderful, live music is always fun! Will return, highly recommend.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place on busy Broadway. The waitress was super friendly, nice and attentive. The music - two older men that were in their 80s probably - did a great job entertaining the crowd. It was so much fun seeing how much they enjoyed singing and entertaining the crowd. There was a special New Years menu so not as much to choose from as normal. We had fried bologna and french fries. It just sounded so funky we had to try it and it was not bad at all. Good place to hang out for a while.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Great movie and great AC.   If grew up on Grand Oe Ovary, it is a must visit.  Very educational about its history.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: We stumbled into the Tin Roof after hearing some of the music outside. They had great bands and there was actually room to walk around and breathe in contrast with tootsie's next door. Drinks are reasonably priced, would come again.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: I went to Tin Roof with my friends. We were all 21, and the bouncer kicked us out because he said "we didn't look 21". We showed them our IDs and told them to scan them but they said they didn't care. I bought a drink from there and they took my drink away from me and kicked my friends and I out even though I paid for my drink and showed them my ID. This is the most disrespectful place I've ever been to. I will never go here again, and I recommend never going to this bar.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Was seated at a nice table on the patio. Waitress was very friendly and attentive.  Drinks took way too long to come out.  
Apps were the cheese balls and the fried cauliflower.  Both were average.  We were then told there was a 15 top and an 8 top that are blocking up the kitchen.  Food wouldn't be out for a while.  30 min later we got our food.  The greek bowl was awful.  Raw cauliflower, chick peas and artichokes straight out of the can.  Didnt even take the time to add salt.  Side of carrots was literally 8 carrot chips.
Offered us a free dessert we chose the toffee pudding.  10 min later she comes out and says they are all out.
Check please.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Wow. Few places in America have as much impact, as this little auditorium does.  The birthplace of the Grand Ole Opry, this place has a lot of significance to the history of Country music. I didn't make it out for a show (I have been here 2x and haven't had the luck to take in a show) but I did take the self guided tour and it was definitely a place that feels/smells like it has seen a thing or two.
Love the old stained glass, the intro movie was informative and I really  love the old Hatch posters of all the bands who has performed here. Anyone who is anyone has performed here. What a great venue. I love old performance venues and I'm glad I made it out and took the tour. It is a magnificent building and really a cornerstone to making Nashville into the Music City it is known for today.
A must see for anyone looking to explore the history of this glorious City and the artists that inhabit it.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The self guided tour is as long or short as you want it to be. The Ryman Auditorum is a cool place to visit but we thought the extras you get to see on the tour are not worth the money. Mainly, just a few cases of artifacts that are covered up during the performances. We would recommend attending a concert there instead.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
HOLY MOLY, now this is some DAMN good Home Country Cooking.  I had some great Fried Chicken, wonderful Catfish and amazing Country Ham.  

Our Server was the best, he was on top of things, funny and didn't miss a beat with anything we needed.  

The best thing, we happened to see Billy Ray Cyrus and Johnny Van Zant while we were there...Hell, if it's good enough for them, it's good enough for me.

I was really thinking about going back there for dinner every night....it was that good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is how you do country breakfast, and it doesn't help when it's at the end of you road.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Ate here the other night.  Still being on ny time we get that about 5:45 and we had no line.  There were 4 in our party, 2 adults and 2 kids.  My youngest eats nothing so be ordered macaroni and cheese with a side of mac and cheese from the kids menu which was delicious.  The rest of us ordered different dishes and sides to taste everything.  Nothing disappointed us.  Keith, the manager, stopped at our table and when he learned that we were from ny and tasting all southern food, he brought us samples of some of the things we did not order.  Keith also brought us a molasses/agave type of spread that is available to all but you need to request it.  Keith taught us to mix this with butter and spread on a biscuit.  This was amazing!  So was the hasbrown casserole, creamed corn, fried chicken, hot chicken, stringbeans, pork and catfish.  We liked the city ham better than country ham.  Skip the fried green tomatoes.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We had a great time last night at the City winery . We enjoyed the music with Andrew Ripp and the food we had was really good . We had the risotto balls , hummus plate, flat bread, chicken, and slaw with cranberries, almonds and Brussels. Everyone enjoyed their food. My only complaint is hard seats which is an issue when you are sitting for hours.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Iconic. Classic. Consistently good on all levels. What's not to love? There are places that do individual things better, but few that pit out a comparable total package. Just be prepared to wait a bit on most nights, or use their take-out or catering services.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Get there early, the other reviews are right on about that. It can take a year and a day to get a table, but that's not why I rated it so low. I anticipated the end all be all breakfast when I looked over the menu, and what I got was a glorified Cracker Barrel. I can get eggs, biscuits, and meat anywhere, and these biscuits aren't even close to being the best metro Nashville has to offer. Not worth the wait, not worth the hype, not worth the money.

name: Big Shotz
text: We stopped in for $5 double shots. All delicious. We left because it was like 7pm and empty. But definitely good for a start of the night double shot!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Long wait. Huge portions. The Sunday special was smoked brisket. Simply the best I've ever had. The creamed corn side was similarly memorable. Great food at a modest price at a Nashville institution.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This cafe is awesome.  Cute decor, polite servers, amazing biscuits. We loved it so much we came back the next day for breakfast round two.
I loved the peach jam, pulled pork bbq, biscuits and hash brown casserole. 
Loveless gets pretty busy somehow we beat the crowds both days.  A must see if you find yourself in Nashville.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I've been here now 3 times and have been consistently impressed with the food and the service.  From great appetizers like the giant pretzel to the cheese fries, you are in for carbohydrate heaven.  The sausages, the sauerkraut and schnitzels have all been great.  
The Bierhaus is very open and nicely draped with hops and murals.  It seats over 600 so you should be able find a seat, but may share the table with others.  The restaurant is set up as a proper beer garden.  
They have excellent German beers from well known German breweries with a variety of glass sizes.
Don't come if you're on a diet.  You'll leave stuffed and happy.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: After moving to Nashville & hearing all the raving reviews about loveless, I was really excited to try it. Unfortunately, loveless did not live up to my expectations. The food was average. They wanted to charge over $3 for an 8 oz (maybe 12 at best) of Apple juice. The biscuits were ok as well. However, the staff was nice. IMO, you won't miss anything if you choose not to go.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Fourth of July visit! We had to wait to be seated but the food was every second worth it!! :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I love loveless cafe because of the history and atmosphere, but recently it's gone a little downhill. The biscuits and homemade jam are always good and the chicken n dumplins they serve on Wednesdays are delicious. Unfortunately everything else is just average.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The bad:
White corn grits were soupy and tasteless, even with cheese. 

The good:
Fried chicken was yummy, but missing something.... Salt? Heat?
Fried green tomatoes were good. 

The great:
Love the biscuits with peach preserves! The pork was yummy too.  
The hash brown casserole didn't blow my mind until I got home and reheated it. 
Peach tea, half sweet and half unsweetened was pleasantly flavorful without being too sweet. 
The moonshine bloody Mary was good and the tiny souvenir Jar was a nice touch. 

If I come back, I'm going to the store for peach preserves and biscuit mix!!!

name: The Basement
text:
Very cool venue, but it has the absolute worst layout of any music venue I've ever visited.  The bar is tucked away in the back corner, and it's damn near impossible to get a drink.  The layout dictates that the bar line cuts straight through the middle of the venue, inconveniencing the people trying to watch the show AND the people trying to get a beer.

Incredibly awkward and counter-intuitive layout, and not a very comfortable place to watch a show, but four stars because of the cool vibe and the incredible bands they book.  The mix on the music always sounds great, too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We enjoyed our visit very much everyone was very friendly the place was very neat to look at all the pictures of the famous people there it was fun just sitting around the area they told us 45 minute wait it took about 55 pretty good on judging time just a little disappointed there was no really big gift shops it looks like they had plenty of room but they just weren't there otherwise we had a beautiful day and would definitely go back

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Fantastic southern food, huge variety, and great drinks to boot. It's just a shame that so many people know about this place; there's always a huge wait (I've never waited less than 30 mins, and sometimes as much as 2 hours). On occasion I find it worth the wait, but usually I'll just go elsewhere.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: It's been 6 months since I went to the Loveless and I'm counting down the days til I can return. Everything we ordered amazing: Southern sampler, country ham, fried chicken, fried green tomatoes and of course biscuits and jam!! As an NJ resident, dreaming of returning, keep up with Loveless Cafe on social media, they are very interactive and post beautiful food pictures that have me checking the prices on flights to Nashville on a regular basis!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: It is solid and the biscuits are perfect, but the wait can be a bit tedious after a certain hour in the morning.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
From one meal at Loveless, I can see why this place has the reputation it does. 10:00 am on a Thursday and the wait was 35 minutes long. Luckily, they give you a buzzer so that you can wander the multiple gift shops on the property while you wait. Before we knew it, our outdoor table was ready and a huge pile of biscuits was plopped on our table. Holy hell, they are addictive! Served with unbelievably fantastic peach preserve, as well as strawberry and blackberry preserve and sorghum syrup...honestly I would have been happy just eating these as my meal! 

But then our gigantic plates of food arrived, meats and eggs and grits and cheesy hash brown casserole.
