Everything was excellent and we stayed full and in a food coma until 6 pm that night, I kid you not. The Loveless staff was excellent and a few servers came by and chatted with our table. We loved the food and hospitality!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Honestly I would have given loveless cafe a 5 star and they should get it for there food. However, the reason I'm giving the 4 stars is for the rude hostess, Brittany. She had ruined the experience at first because she was giving us attitude from the beginning when we walked in. However the wait was worth it because the food was amazing. Large portions that were made to perfection. Our waitress Cindy was amazing and suggested great entrees to try. I had the bbq breakfast and it was so savory an delicious I highly recommend it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: One of the best breakfasts I have ever had. I really enjoyed my pork chops, but the highlight were the biscuits. LOVED THEM!!!  Great friendly service too. I can't wait to visit again. Too bad I live in CA.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Overall, I had a very pleasant experience at the Loveless Cafe last weekend. I was there on a double date with old friends. The wait (starting at 5 PM on a Saturday) was an hour and a half, but we had planned ahead and showed up well before we were hungry. We killed the wait by playing corn hole and checking out the shops. 

The biscuits were solid. They didn't beat the homemade biscuits that my southern family makes, but the blackberry, peach and strawberry jam that they were served with was delicious. 

We each got the drink special of the night, a Strawberry sipper. It was essentially lemonade with strawberry rye whiskey and was fairly sweet. It was perfect for my taste, but not for the guys'. 

Our waiter was friendly and hilarious. The service was fast and each of us enjoyed our meals. I got the catfish sandwich with grits and it was certainly well done. 

If you go there with good company and expecting a long wait, the Loveless Cafe is a good place to grab some southern food. I'm not sure I would go there over the summer though because most of the waiting areas are outdoors and a long, hot wait would have made us miserable.

Addition: We did not feel rushed at all while we there. In fact, we actually felt that the restaurant did not have the focus on volume that other places had. While we were there, we commented that we appreciated how much space they had put in between the tables.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If you take the time to go anywhere to eat in Nashville this should be your number one choice! The biscuits were the best I've ever had and they are free!! There is always a long wait, but if you go during nonpeak hours it's not too bad. Plus they have a little shop to look around in while you wait.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A favorite for us. Chicken tenders are some of the best and we always get decent to great service. Our out of town visitors love it here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Uhhh... biscuits, biscuits, and more biscuits! Took about 45 mins to get seated, but you have the chance to wander around the place and check out all the cute little shops in the area.

Once seated you are promptly give delicious, buttery soft biscuits with a variety of jams. My fav jam was the peach one. 

Per the recommendation of the guy at the BBQ pit place, I got the BBQ pork omelet. It was just perfect! Usually I find omelets to be too filling, but they had the right ratio of eggs to meat in there. Super tasty. Everyone else thoroughly enjoyed their food and we were even able to pack the rest of our biscuits to take away.

Service was nice and friendly and the place was very clean. You can even take a look at the kitchen through windows on the way to the bathroom. 

Defo make this a food stop if you are in Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: All the notoriety surrounding this restaurant is true...it is worth coming to because the food is excellent, the atmosphere is great, and the service is top-notch.  The store they have in their compound has a lot of cool souvenirs and provides and opportunity to kill some time if you have to wait in line which is always a possibility here.  I've been here once and surprisingly only had to wait for 15 minutes which I'm told is unheard of.  Anyways, do yourself a favor and check this place out if you're in the Nashville area!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The Loveless Cafe was everything I had expected and more.  The food was fabulous and plentiful.  You will not leave her hungry.
http://yallcomeoninthedoorsopen.blogspot.com/2014/08/cousins-gather-at-loveless-cafe.html

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
DEFINITELY worth the hype.

I had no idea about this amazing place UNTIL I checked Yelp and found this fantastic brunch location.  We were in Nashville for a fun weekend. The Loveless Cafe is a drive from downtown, but totally worth it. Be prepared to wait for your delicious, eating experience. No fear, they have already anticipate this, and LC has an entire tourist town for you to explore and shop while you wait for your buzzer to go off.

Finally. We are seated. The interior of this cafe is suuuuper charming. I got the signature plate with the "red eye gravy." Definitely an acquired taste, but I'm glad we were able to try it. I had meal envy over what the hubs ordered. A pulled pork masterpiece (photographed).

The buttermilk muffins that are served while you wait for your entree are reason enough to some here. And the Bloody Mary's made with moonshine are great (if you like Bloody's).

Since we had already made this 'south' drive outta Nashville, we continued down to  Jack Daniel's distillery. An entire day of amazement.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I live in the area so it's great to have a new options. This place is sort of neat, but it also feels kind of like an amusement park. Just not authentic. Some of the foods are interesting, as are some of the beers. I find the tables and chairs to be cool looking, but quite uncomfortable.

If my only choice were inside Opry mills, this spot would land towards the top of the list. Other decent options in the area include Chuy's, Mission barbecue, and scoreboards over across the street. The hot chicken at scoreboards is worth the trip.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Tuvimos que esperar una hora para sentarnos a comer, pero valió la pena! La comida estuvo deliciosa y la atención muy buena. El café tiene tienditas a los lados donde te puedes entretener mientras esperas.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Had a very enjoyable time here after shopping at Opry Mills.  Set up like a traditional beer hall in Germany it is one of the few places to experience German food in this part of the country.  Had a pork schnitzel and bier cheese soup.  Both were very good.  A little disappointed with the apple strudel compared to others I have experienced.  Choice of German and local beers was good.  Entertainment was touristy but good.  Servers were excellent and attentive.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My wife and I had the fried chicken.  The chicken was great.  I would compare it to White Fence Farm in Illinois.  The biscuits and jam were fantastic!  Best biscuits I have ever had!  We had creamed corn, fried green tomatoes, grits and mashed potatoes as sides.  Best creamed corn I have ever had.  Fried green tomatoes were great as well.  A must try in Nashville.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Positive: The atmosphere is great. Table and venue decor is great. Love the way it looks! Server was very sweet. 
Negative: Food! The offer a $20 very limited and sub par buffet. I went the route of ordering off the menu = rock hard inedible biscuits, cold food that seems like it sat on expo for a little too long. Extra well dome crispy burgers. 

I really wanted to love this place because of it's great atmosphere, but just didn't do it for me!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Our family loved the fried chicken, fried green tomatoes, collared greens. But the smoked pork chops with peach jelly stole the show. Everyone is so friendly down here we took home souvenirs too!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The Loveless Café was the most disappointing restaurant I have been too. We have been looking forward to going there for almost 3 years and we finally got the opportunity and were disappointed at every turn. The place is cute, quaint. and has a lot of history but the waiting staff is rude and you feel like you're inconveniencing them by just being there.   The food is absolutely nothing special nothing that you can't find at a local Cracker Barrel or mom-and-pop diner.  We have no reason to return

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
A cute, clean, well maintained Ma and Pa kinda feel, restaurant. Cute little stores that sell their homemade jams and jellies, bbq and of course their biscuits. It is worth a morning drive. 30 minutes from Nashville. Have a great little bbq smokehouse right on property. Busy but keep
Things moving. Excellent, friendly service.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My husband and I went to dinner and a concert here and left unimpressed.  We ordered a good sampling of the menu.  My lobster chowder was overly smoky and salty, with very little lobster.  The bread basket (which was $6!) was completely stale.  (I am talking, crumbly, need a drink of water stale.)  My husband's cheeseburger was quite good (that was the highlight of the night) but my duck confit left a lot to be desired.  First, the presentation was completely unappetizing.  Everything was brown and drab looking.  The taste wasn't much better.  Everything on the plate was salty and heavy.  There was no brightness or "pop" to the dish, and it sorely needed one.  It honestly reminded me of a chicken dinner plate at Denny's!  (But at least at Denny's it would have cost me $10, not $24.)  Finally the chocolate stout cake was small and stale.  All in all, a very disappointing, very expensive meal.

The concert venue was also disappointing.  While I found the acoustics good, the chairs were incredibly uncomfortable. They were like the chairs you'd find in a cheap office lunchroom -- metal and plastic and stackable.  Except instead of sitting in them for a 10-minute lunch, you sat in them for 90 minutes or more, constantly shifting to try to find a comfortable position.

I had high hopes for City Winery but left disappointed.  I think this is a great concept for a restaurant and music venue, so I hope they'll improve their menu and get some new chairs!  :) If so, I'll be back to give it another shot.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Used to be great but food quality has went way down. More of a site seeing place now.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The place is nice but the food is sub par at best.  Small portions for big prices and nothing leaving you with a reason to come back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I'd have to agree with others that this cafe might not necessarily be worth the wait time. My friend & I came on a Sunday (before Memorial Day) around 6:30pm and didn't get seated until almost 8pm. We walked around the little store and checked everything out. Two separate weddings were going on so it was neat to see the brides posing under the Loveless neon sign out front while we waited. Our waiter was real friendly and attentive. He brought us their famous biscuits with 3 different flavored jams right when we sat down. Now if anything, the wait was worth these biscuits with butter-n-jam! My friend & I both ordered the fried chicken with mashed potatoes and gravy. She got the collard greens and I opted for the green beans. Both were really good. I honestly thought the white meat, fried chicken could've been more moist, but I don't really eat fried chicken like ever, so I'm not the best at deciphering from good/bad fried chicken. All-n-all, it was a decent experience. Our waiter comped our desserts which was nice. My friend just had a slice of the apple pie and I had a small portion of their banana bread pudding. My friend said the pie was so-so. The bread pudding was decent, but I was so full from my meal that I couldn't eat anymore than a few fork-fulls of it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is a unique gem just outside of Nashville. Everything I have tried has been wonderful Nd always filling. Take  look at the pictures your eyes will it lie!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Delicious!   Our family of four ordered 3 entrees and we still had leftovers!  Steak and eggs, southern ham and eggs, and the southern combo platter.  We all had the hashbrown casserole, which was cheesy and tasty.  The ham was a bit salty for my northern palette.  The sausage gravy, the made from scratch biscuits, and the homemade preserves were all excellent.  

Don't forget to stop by the cute shops to pick up a jar of preserves for home or as a gift for a loved one!  Biscuit mix also available, along with cute souvenirs, home decor, t-shirts, and stuffed animals.  Wish we could bring home cajun bacon that we saw at the shop.  They do have a shipping option.

name: Rocketown
text: I saw August Burns Red here last night and I liked how there wasn't any alcohol sold at the venue and foul language wasn't permitted either. However, later on in the show I was afraid I was going to end up really disliking this venue because of the crowd rules. I noticed a guy crowdsurfing and I immediately waited for him to get kicked out (which never happened, to my surprise). I then noticed there was actually a pit in the center of the crowd away from where I had been standing and the rest was history. There was even a guy in a power chair in the pit with us and that made it even better. I really respect this place and I love that a fellow West Virginian originally started it. I drove over three hours from my house in Jefferson City and I'll definitely be back.

name: Big Shotz
text: This was an ok bar. I did not notice this was a smoking bar. The service was decent. The drinks were blah... there was no music playing. They have drink specials but nothing that was all that great.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits were great.  The chicken so so and the fries the typical frozen type.  Very average.

name: Big Shotz
text: Live music & the best jello shots of my life!! What more can one ask for?!? Just go and enjoy a blue raspberry jello shot for me! Oh and don't forget to shake it on the dance floor me too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Not close to downtown, this iconic spot still serves it like food is the main business. We love it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
If there was ever a destination restaurant- this is it! What a great place to visit!! So many adorable trinkets and souvenirs, even the drive from Nashville is enjoyable!
I wish I would have known about this place before.. I can't wait to go back!
The food, the service, the grounds, literally everything about this restaurant is awesome! Down to the crossword puzzle place mats!
I should mention that we went with a large of group of about 15 people and they literally stayed open for us to eat, they were extremely accommodating and gave us about 40 of their heavenly biscuits to go!!! I truly cannot describe what a great experience we had at the loveless cafe! All of their preserves and all of their homemade honey and jams were to die for, I strongly recommend spending an evening there and support their amazing locale!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The drive to get here made us wonder,the food removed all concern.our waitress Susan was fantastic we were served quickly and correctly.
Every dish was fantastic from the jams and biscuits to the country ham. Portions were large and all tasty.
  The biscuits were endless and waitress gave us what we didn't it to take home.
Everything was great

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Horribly annoying performers making racket the entire time we were there... nearly impossible to even relatively enjoy the average beer and food they have available.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
AMAZING!!!

We were visiting from out of town for the CMA music fest. We drove 45 min in the rain to get here and it was worth it! We only had to wait about 20 min for a table and our waiter TALOR was awesome. He got us set up with mimosas and bloody marys, and  the food was the best breakfast food I have ever had!! The hash-brown casserole was delicious and the biscuits, well they are famous for a reason!

I suggest everyone go there if you get the chance! I will definitely be back again as soon as I can.  xoxo

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Some of the best German food I have ever had. Outstanding atmosphere and service. Huge place with great vibe...fun, fun, fun....

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is the sweetest place and our server Jeff was wonderful and accommodating! I would highly recommend the spot, go for a Natchez Trace drive afterwards, and make sure you ask for Jeff.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Insane waits on the weekend. Waited over an hour on Friday for a take-out order (including the 30 min drive over there). Can't see what the fuss is. Will have to try to make it out on a Tuesday or Wednesday and see if it's actually possible to get a table. Not impressed with the food I got- have definitely had better in the area.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Can I give this 6 stars? The food is delicious, plentiful and excellent value for money. The service is efficient and friendly. This is maybe the best Southern cooking I've ever had. We'll be back!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Disappointed-Heard such great reviews and that this was a landmark restaurant. Ordered chicken tenders and they were overlooked and tasteless. Fried green tomatoes were undercooked. Not good at all. Seemed like a dingy old restaurant that needs some major Clorox wipes and a clean up. Flies were all over the place and hair was in my menu. Overpriced greasy spoon. I've had better chicken at KFC. Will not be returning.

name: Rocketown
text: I came here for a concert, I saw Hey Monday and someone else. It was a big open area, there isn't much to say...it seems fine. Will I go here again? Sure why not. It wasn't a very closed in space, I liked that

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Awesome place, the biscuits were delicious and all you can eat. I had the bbq Sammy and my wife had the fried chicken and waffle.  Both were great and at a reasonable price. Our server (Morgan) was excellent.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Man do I want to hate this place.  Everything about it says TOURIST TRAP.   And some items aren't as good as the others, but they do so much well.  I know that the blackberry jam is suppose to be the item, but the Peach is soooo Good.   In a way, it does kind of remind me of what Cracker Barrel was like in the 70's when the staff wore red bandana shirts.  I have gotten into a habit of taking co-workers from out of town out here to eat.  So far, everyone has gone on and on to others about it.   I just wish I would quit ordering the sampler plate with 3 meats.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Growing pains... I was in Munich last fall for October  fest, and if you come here to get a taste of that experience you'll get it. But they are working out the bugs that come with opening a new place, staff knowledge of menu and bar items were most noticeable. I have no doubt they will get it all worked out, I'll be back! The attention to detail inside is impressive.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I cried when I found pulled pork that I enjoyed more than my own.  George rolls in at 3:30 and starts smoking meat, for the love of god.  I know this because that's when we showed up...and waited until they opened.  George was real friendly to three random men showing up at the smokehouse before dawn, looking for BBQ.  He was cool with us napping in the car and playing catch in the parking lot.  

We were the first ones in the door and they throw biscuits in your face when you get inside, served with homemade jams that makes Smucker's look like Suckers.  BOO-YA.  George swears by the biscuits and I won't say he's wrong.  They were excellent.

The exact moment my life changed is easy to recall, it's the second the pulled pork hoe cakes arrived; heaping, steaming, and screaming at my soul.  People, the pork melted in my mouth.  Has that ever happened to you?  Be real here.

Oh, the service was good and the staff was friendly.  They hooked up a free plate of biscuits and jam to go as we left.  We also shared a nice conversation on Chicago style pizza which they adore; I think after the food and service a frozen za should find it's way to Loveless from "the boys who went camping."

A true labor that is not without love produces a product that fills my heart and tummy tum tum with the truest form of adoration.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wow. I'd been to this place twice before and was just as satisfied as I was this time. I was visiting Nashville again with a friend and she said she wanted a hearty southern meal and we ended up here! We both ordered the quarter chicken with cheesy smashed potatoes (amazing). The biscuits are great and I was so completely stuffed when I left, yet we still contemplated the desserts. Great place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Was in town for business, thought I'd check out the Loveless again as it had been a few years.   The biscuits were incredible, as were the 3 jams.  Had the fried chicken plate (dark).   Quarter chicken was generous...2 legs and a back/thigh.  Came out very hot and fresh.  The crust is not overly salty nor greasy, but the chicken was cooked just a few minutes too long.  Even the leg meat was a bit tough.  The turnip greens with pot liquor were excellent, as was the pot liquor.  The fried okra was disappointing...the coating too thick and bready.   I remember having this several years ago and it was a different cornmeal coating that was much lighter and crisper.   Have they changed the recipe?   Came around 5:30 on Monday night and the restaurant was pretty empty.   Used to seeing this place being packed.   Service was quick and friendly.  I ended up walking out full but feeling a little let down...not the same as I remembered.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
My first and only visit (so far) at this place was nothing short of amazing. For Christmas my friends and I traveled from Memphis to see John Waters' Christmas show. Initially we had balcony seating. Upon checking in we asked if we could upgrade our seating. The gentleman helping us was extremely helpful and friendly. He upgraded us to stage side seating at no extra charge. We literally got to sit mere feet away from John as he delivered a hilarious show. 
Our server was attentive and polite and answered all of our questions in a knowledgeable and helpful manner. 
I ordered the house Rosé and amongst the three of us we split Wild Mushroom & Risotto Balls, the Hummus Plate (this is a must! It was so delicious and fresh!), the fried Brussels Sprouts, and the Margherita Veggie Flatbread. The entire experience left me feeling completely satisfied and overwhelmed with joy. I know it had a lot to do with how giddy I was from meeting John Waters and being in his presence for the duration of the show. But the food, ambience, hospitality, and wine,  exponentially added to our experience. I was left with a glow for a few days afterwards and dreaming of the tapas and wine. 
I would most definitely like to return to experience the food and another show.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing biscuits, definitely the best I've ever had! Their blackberry jam is outstanding. Service is great as well. Watermelon ribs, fried chicken, fried green tomatoes, and mashed potatoes with gravy are some of our favorites!! Definitely  must stop here when you're in Nashville!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
"Biscuit Poisoning? YES PLEASE! "
5 of 5 stars Pending review
If you are visiting Nashville, make the drive to this wonderfully taste of history! But be aware they bring you a plate of the most buttery biscuits with an assortment of jams, preserves and honey. Stop at one...or you will get too full of the yummy goodness. Then make sure that what ever your family orders as the main dish you all order a different side, because there is ALOT to share. From Mac and Cheese to the BEST turnip green and mashed potatoes. My husband had the house chicken, I had the meat loaf and my daughter had the roast beef we each got 3 sides, we took so much home, so good, And we each ordered dessert to go. You could of rolled me out of that wonderful place!!! But don't leave till you visit all the shops and learn about its origins. It's a very nostalgic place. After dinner.... Take a drive through the parks. Truely beautiful.

Visited August 2015

name: City Winery Nashville
text: We came for brunch, so it wasn't very busy and we didn't see a live show.  The inside is very nice and spacious.  I love the staircase of wine bottles !   The food wasn't great.  I had a salmon salad wrap, which was salty n bland at the same time. The potatoes were seasoned well, but also salty. The flight (wine samples) were all good. I like the display of them.  Honestly, the best part was the fire place we sat next to.  They lit it up and we were so warm ! Thanks !!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Awful food.  Service was amazing and biscuits but that is it.  Our food was cold and just not good...breakfast was a bust

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless was a ride outside the city but worth the trip.  They have built their own little community where you can shop at stores while you wait and even ship home your items!  We had an hr and a half wait to eat so we did shop and enjoyed their own community.  Their chicken and waffles was good.  But their gravy was even better!  Their biscuits were good but it was really cool to watch them make them through the glass window on your way to the bathroom. If you have kids make sure you check it out!  The mashed potatoes were delish! Worth the trip outside town and the wait! I have to say it was the best food we had the whole trip.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Wow wow wow. I love the biscuits. I love the preserves. But most of all, I love that Southern hospitality, ya'll. We waited over an hour for a table on a Saturday for brunch but it was so worth it. The venue itself is an attraction alone - a little bluegrass was being played by an endearing small group of musicians to patiently waiting customers in the 90+ heat (many of us were waiting under shady trees and sauntering in and out of the air conditioned gift shops full of Loveless goodies). Once we got our table (inside, phew! Too hot out!) we were treated so well by the gorgeous Susan- she was genuine and sweet; took the time to talk through the menu when we asked questions etc. Our coffee (filtered) was delish and never ran dry. Hot chocolate was the BEST! I was totally overwhelmed with the well-priced menu and quick pleasant service too. If you are a tourist visiting Nash, you gotta just do this- it's a rite of passage- those biscuits alone smothered in peach preserve will make it worth all that long wait in the summer humidity.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
When near Nashville this is a foodie must!  

Excellent biscuits and other southern favorites including fried fish and chicken gizzards!  

We have had both breakfast and dinner and no complaints!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The most Amazing biscuits!!! Cute place and the food is great. Service was quick.  The ham and jam store right across is great to find cute little gifts to take home.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We waited for an hour and 45 minutes. Not worth that long of a wait. Under an hour, do it.
The service was pretty good, they were obviously very busy.
Right away they will bring you biscuits. Dig in because they're famous for a reason. Try the peach jam. They will bring you more so keep them coming and you can take some home to go!
We had omelets which were yummy. The pulled pork one was fun and good. Cheese and garden omelets were standard.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Worst. Meal. Ever. 

My mind is blown. I've been so excited to see Nashville's food scene become on par with larger cities. However, in my 30 years as a Nashvillian I've never had a worse meal. It was like a middle schooler plated our charcuterie plate with store bought Bologna. The aioli was neon yellow and bread was like wonder bread. On to the cheese board that had one particular mystery cheese no one wanted. The food allergy we told the waiter was subsequently disregarded causing a plate to be sent back. 

The food was terrible and waiter blissfully unaware. I will never be back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Took the 1 hour drive from Lebanon just to get some biscuits and it was very much worth it. Our waiter was the best. Super quick and friendly even though we got there only about 25 minutes before they closed. Only had dessert (pie) and biscuits, and then stopped at the store. Eat the biscuits. Take some to go. The preserves they are served with are excellent as well, especially the strawberry.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is good, but super rich. We came here for breakfast, and it's typical, heavy, American fare. They start you out with a pile of biscuits and jam. The biscuits are super tasty, but I guess they are about 50% butter. I impulsively bought the chicken and waffles, and they were also super rich. The chicken was great and had a nice crispy shell. The waffle was also good, not too much to say about it.

The service was amazing, my dad spilled coffee everywhere and they were quick to help us out.

Overall it's great food in a casual southern atmosphere. It's just a bit too rich and they don't really serve lite fare, so I'm going to give it a 4.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We had our hopes to high for this place but we weren't impressed. Their biscuits indeed are one of the best we've ever had!! They bring four biscuits and three different jams and WOW... really delicious. We had ham and eggs, the ham was very salty. We also had chicken and waffles, the chicken was really dry and the waffle was ok. The service could be a little bit better. Our waitress was not friendly ( kinda rushing us even though it was our first time there) and didn't tell us about the daily specials but she did tell other tables the specials. Other waiters/waitresses were nicer than ours (tall guy). The place is kinda cute.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Fantastic food, charming decor, friendly service (thanks, Katie!). I now see why it's on everyone's "must" list when checking out Nashville's sites.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place was only so-so.  Food is no better than any of the run-of-the-mill breakfast chains (not even the biscuits). The service is absolutely appalling and just skirts being downright rude.  The wait was ridiculous and I can't help but think that it is grotesquely overestimated in an effort to get people to shop at all of the other little shops on the premises.  The grounds are pretty decent though and the hostess was at least thoughtful enough to suggest ordering takeout to eat at one of the picnic areas.  Would advise against using the app to order takeout. The front end staff admittedly have no idea whatsoever about any takeout orders placed via app. They only know about any app orders when/if the back end staff bring completed orders up front.  Would also advise triple checking pick up orders (before leaving) for things like having complete meals, drinks, syrups, sauces, sides, utensils, etc... In a nutshell, I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here again or consider it a must do event if family/friends are in town.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I might rate this 3 stars if it weren't for the 5-star hype. It was all "OK" cafe food at best - NOTHING special.

Biscuits? They were good - but very small. If you want a real biscuit, get off the trace at Hwy 72 and go to Corinth, MS for Abe's or Lloyd's - nothing to see here. Preserves were pretty good and the sorghum was good.

World's best fried chicken? Hardly. Dry and over-cooked and - that poor thing musta been a chick - littlest pieces I've ever seen.

Meatloaf was cold. Not stone out of the fridge, but not warm. Taste of it was average.

Green tomatoes were too thickly cut and got soggy fast.

Mashed potatoes? Stirred potatoes. Like from a box? Red eye gravy? Mix?

Wanted to try some pie, but $33 in for very "eh" food - I didn't wanna risk it.

This place is evidently surviving on past reputation. I didn't get the hype.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Loveless Cafe has gone through several ownerships, but the place stemmed from Lon and Annie Loveless, who were known to pass out fried chicken and biscuits to travelers who were traveling on Highway 100.  They serve items such as the country ham, pork bbq, omelets, fried chicken, catfish, pancakes, sandwiches, salads, and desserts.  My sister and I shared the 'Famous Loveless Country Ham,' which was a 7oz sliced ham that came with 2 eggs and a side of red-eye gravy.   You also have a choice to have homefries or hash brown casserole, and the platter is also served with biscuits (sorghum and honey are offered upon request).  The ham itself was tasty, but way too salty (even for my taste).  Even without seasoning the eggs and eating it with the ham, it still didn't balance it out.  I really enjoyed the hashbrown casserole, as it was wonderfully cheesy and creamy - yum!  I could have eaten this all day!  We also tried the Pimento Cheese & Fried Green Tomato Biscuit - it came with a nice generous dollop of pimento cheese with a perfectly fried sliced green tomato, all in their homemade biscuits - it was delicious!  I also really enjoyed their biscuits as it had a nice little crispy top with a lovely soft interior; great on its own or with butter - you can add honey, sorghum, or any of the jellies that they also provide you with.  There are plenty of parking spaces, and there's also a cute gift store that you can check out across the lot - they sell the Loveless's strawberry vines decor on platters, cookbooks, kitchen accessories, home decor, etc.  I'm glad I was able to check this place out!

+DELICIOUS BISCUITS!!!
+hashbrown casserole
+Pimento Cheese & Fried Green Tomato Biscuit

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My husband has not stopped talking about those biscuits now 8 months later. It's a bit out of the way if you're downtown, but worth it! Yum!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Grounds are lovely and lots to do while you wait - and you're going to wait. Biscuits are overrated. They're more like buttery dinner rolls. Service was excellent, they had lots of friendly and attentive staff. But I wouldn't come back for the food. Fried chicken was underwhelming, and the pancakes and waffles were very sweet. However, the pork was really good. It tasted like sweet, smoky pork - it didn't need a sauce or any other cover up.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Biscuits are no kidding great. Loved the chicken the pork and the pies look great. Too full to order pie. This was some good cooking. Worth the extra trip. Great wait staff lots of enthusiasm from everyone there.   
A little touristy but still lots of fun. I will be back for the biscuits!!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Loved this new restaurant in the Opry Mills Mall. The food was awesome and the entertainment was so good. Our waitress was Allison, she was so cute and very knowledgeable of all the beers and the food!!!! We will be back!!!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: By far the best biscuits. Top them with the peach jelly and you have a winner. Overall great southern food and that friendly southern service you hear about.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We stopped by at 8:30 on a saturday morning and it was perfect timing as we got seated right away. Our server was friendly and attentive and gave great recommendations since we were first time visitors. I got the bbq pork eggs which came with 2 buried pancakes. Helpings were generous and the food was tasty too. My friend got the chicken biscuits which were delicious. The house biscuits lived up to their legendary status. This place is well worth the drive!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Not really much to say that hasn't already been said.

First of all, the fried chicken is the best around...maybe some of the best I've had.

They are known for the biscuits and jam, which are just ok to me.  I compare everything to my mom's homemade biscuits and jam, and nothing comes close.

There is one thing you can always count on with Loveless Cafe that may not have been previously mentioned...the music on their playlist is solid country gold.  Merle, Possum, Waylon, and all the hits from the 90's. 

I'd like Loveless so much more if it was a hidden gem.  It's popularity creates a long wait for a table.  If going on a weekend, arrive before 8:00 and you won't have much of a problem. After 8:00, and especially after 9:00, you should plan on at least an hour.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The Loveless Cafe experience was worth the scenic drive and wait!  Excellent, friendly customer service with every employee we encountered.  Jason made amazing suggestions! Thanks for a lovely Sunday!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Tourist trap meat-and-three.  Biscuits are mediocre...they mass produce them, so that they are just a "step" about fridge "grands".  My homemade baking powder biscuits are better.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: After reading the reviews I decided to check this place out for breakfast before our ride back home to North Carolina. We, my wife and I, felt the nostalgia as soon as we pulled in. We were greeted and brought to one of many rooms; very comfy. The menu was loaded with a lot of nontraditional breakfast items, very non-typical of a breakfast menu. My wife got coffee and French toast, I got coffee and Southern Omelet (3 Eggs, Diced Country Ham, Bacon or Sausage with Onions, Peppers and Cheddar Cheese). While the omelet was good sized, the fillings were non-existent and the cheese was clumped in the middle. $10.00 for an omelette with no side like potatoes is way too expensive. $7.00 for three pieces of French toast, regardless of how good, is also expensive for no bacon or sausage. No way would I come back here again at these prices for NO reason... oh, and the coffee was weak and overpriced too...thankfully the Loveless Cafe is close to Interstate 40 and the Natches Trace Parkway.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I have been here four times with hope each time we would have better service. Each visit has been made at lunch time so there has only been maybe 10 parties dinning at the same time so not that busy. Each time it's has taken about an hour and a half because the service is soooo slow. On one occasion we gave up on telling the waitress what we wanted because it would take her 10 minutes to get back to us and I hope you aren't thirsty because that is not a priority. If I were rating on just the service this would be a one star. The food is wonderful I haven't ordered anything I haven't liked and the large pretzel is huge enough to share. I do suggest you try it just be warned that the service will be slow!!


Update- so we tried again and was very happy this time! As always the food was great but, our server was very attentive and helpful.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
The Venue is beautiful.  But the service sucks.  Management was not friendly at all.  I think I spoke to the GM about why the food was cold and he did not try to get me another plate or offer to comp my meal.   I think with this is going to have a lot of bad reviews if the management doesn't get changed.  
As the rest of the community has discussed the parking situation is not favorable.  I was their for a corporate party is how they handled where to go was not organized.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Oh my word. This place is hog heaven. Not for hogs, of course, cuz they're getting smoked out back. But all manner of cooked hog--bacon, sausage, country ham, pulled pork--is here for you. We also spent some time talking with Eric, the pitmaster. He brought us into the smoke house and talked with us about the process, showing us pork butts, briskets and chickens in the smoker. This dude loves his job and does it well.

Back inside, they gave us a mess of biscuits to start. After we were done they gave us another mess of biscuits to go, along with the preserves. Here's a tip. Ask for the sorghum for your biscuits. And while you're at it, mix a little in with your grits. Oh my word.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Went for Super Bowl party.  The wines for tasting were not good.  The hummus plate was not good. Some store bought hummus with pickled cauliflower and flavorless cracker bread. The mushroom pizza was AWFUL. Servers were great. The big screen TV was great.  Venue has potential but the food and wine were meh.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Destination Restaurant! If you are visiting Nashville this place is a must... The food, the service, the grounds, the country ham and their preserves... Yum their peach preserve is amazing... I even thought of liking the jar :/ it was that good. Their portions are gigantic so you will be better off sharing a couple of dishes... Easy drive from Nashville and beautiful scenery on the way here...

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Convinced my family to go while visiting Nashville.  Thought it would be "touristy" but made the trip.  WOW!!!  The biscuits with the preserves are worth the trip alone.  The hot chicken...definitely THE best. My son, who just got the fried chicken, said if he ever was on death row, THIS would be his last meal.  Spinach Alfredo soup, a must order! The service was AMAZING.  Susan (sp) went above and beyond and was friendly as could be.  Y'all need to go!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Overall, I had a really good experience. Loved the live music the day I went, as well as my food and my server Gemaal. Great service! Definitely would go back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: So, I had major expectations for this place because of all the hype from everyone. The best biscuits ever? No. And they weren't even warm. My husband & I agreed that the best thing about the biscuits were the 3 homemade jams that came with them. Those were fantastic. My cinnamon raisin French toast was good, but nothing fantastic. The bacon was great though & I'm not even a bacon eater, typically. My husband's omelet didn't have much flavor. It was a good breakfast, but we kind of expected a great one, especially after waiting an hour & 40 minutes.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Loved City Winery! The wine was fantastic and the food was even better. I got the grouper and my boyfriend got the steak. Both were delicious, we didn't want them to end! You can tell everything here is made with quality ingredients. We stopped back for brunch with family, it was also delicious. Make sure you ask for Kimberly, she was by far the best server we've ever had!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits alone are worth the wait that you generally encounter when visiting. Their fried chicken is excellent every time and the hashbrown casserole is a must! Try going early to skip the crowd- they're basically busy the entire afternoon on the weekends in my experience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Yummmmmmmmmm

I suggest going first thing in the early AM to get a good table on a weekend- but that said- still worth the wait if you hit it mid church rush!

Love the pancakes here, the biscuits are delish and my husband loves the country fried steak that they have on the menu.

Really quaint little restaurant- like such that you might find the floor uneven in spots. :) Part of its character.

that said- the mini biscuits and the preserves are delish and they are very generous they do not skimp.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Worth the hype. Amazing biscuits, amazing jam... my husband got pulled pork and eggs and loved every bite! I got the ham and eggs! If we're ever back in TN we will definitely be coming back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place lives up to the hype. Great food, service and atmosphere. We only had to wait 20 minutes for our table. Definitely worth it. We'll come back again if we're ever in the area. Great fried chicken!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Went to City Winery for an event last weekend. Besides the sub par food, the atmosphere really rounds out your entire experience. Couldn't really see myself frequenting to this establishment if I didn't have a reason too. Examples, event/concert. The drinks were over priced and the food was just ok. My girlfriend and I decided to split a flatbread. The crust was exceptional. However, the flavors that were included didn't really compliment each other. Hopefully I can give this place another try because it really does have the potential.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Food is very good even though the restaurant is annexed to the mall.  Don't let that deter you if you have a craving for German food & beer!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Best biscuits! Biscuits with jams are complimentary. Be sure to get there early. If there is a long wait, there are several cute shops to peruse. Great place to pick up a gift. A game a corn hole is available as well as plenty of outdoor seating to wait on. You can also see into their kitchen where they make the biscuits from scratch.

Very homey decor and feel. Tables looked a bit squished together but I didn't notice this being a problem. Great friendly waitstaff. Breakfast menu had everything you'd want for a traditional breakfast. I decided to go with French toast with a side of bacon. Perfection on a plate! It was a great introduction to Tennessee home cookin for my first trip to Nashville. Great environment for family and kids.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits and preserves were the best part of the meal. Don't know if I would travel more than a few minutes for them though. Guest ordered the special which was peach-bbq smoked chicken with mac and cheese and mashed potatoes and his verdict is that the sauce was the best part. Chicken was said to be kind of dry and there was a shoulder shrug when asked about the sides. I ordered ham and eggs with hash browns and turnip greens. The hash browns were the best and came recommended by our nice waitress. The turnip greens had great flavor. The ham was a very large portion but was a little hard and chewy and was my least favorite part. The experience may have been better had we gone to the museum and the store etc. Maybe next time and maybe one more star. But it's gonna be a solid 3 for me.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This is a stop worth the wait.  It's a great experience if you've never visited here.  We got there at 12:15 pm on a gorgeous autumn Sunday.  Ninety minute wait for a table.  We passed the time by exploring the interesting shops and walking the grounds.  Our lunch menu included hash brown casserole, hush puppies,ham, meat loaf, pulled pork, turnip greens and THE biscuits.  These Texas women didn't care for the biscuits at all. Tough, bland biscuits.  Turnip greens were cold and very stringy--no pot liquor as promised.  Meat loaf was bland.  High points-- hash brown casserole, ham, hush puppies.  Got the homemade banana pudding--made with sugar cookies instead of vanilla wafers--nothing special.  We're glad we took the time to visit, but I don't need to go back unless I'm in Nashville for extended time.  If you're traveling south out of Nashville, take the Natchez Trace.  Beautiful drive!  Have a full tank of gas before hitting the Trace...gas stations are few and have to ask Siri for gas locations.  The Trace has sporadic internet connection.  Go to Loveless at least once in your life!  No regrets!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I will find any excuse to eat here when I'm close to Nashville. The breakfast is amazing. For lunch the fried chicken and mashed potatoes actually taste homemade. This is one of my favorite places to eat.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
While the location is nice and adds a little class to Nashville the training of the wait staff is underwhelming.
If you use wine in your name your people had better be the best they can be when it comes to wine and this is not the case. 
The staff were very nice, however, it is just that they have not been given the tools to be as aware and knowledgable as they should be.
The night was very quiet and the overall service was suspect.
Food quality was mediocre and not to the quality expected.
This is not the place to eat or drink until they learn to step up their game.
Too bad, we were initially excited and were let down on our first dinner in Nashville for NHL All Star weekend.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
32 bucks for breakfast is a wee too high.

food was great, service was great.

just can't get over the price.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best place in Nashville for country ham, eggs, biscuits, preserves.  Only wish they still had the homemade butter and a little thinner cut on the country ham.  Their lunch and dinners are fantastic as well. Meatloaf or chicken n'dumplings are both winners.  The homemade salad dressings are fabulous.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: First time here. Fun. Good brats and awesome pretzels. Indoor beer garden tables. They have a live band in evenings. Outdoor patio. Kept it simple this time but definitely want to explore the menu more. Full service restaurant with Coke products. Everyone enjoyed their meal.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless is (apparently) one of those Nashville institutions, and since breakfast is one of OUR family institutions, we decided to hit the place on the way out of town. Because we enjoy traveling while in a coma, we opted for the family-style breakfast, which, roughly translated, means "we come to your table and stuff you like a Thanksgiving turkey until you can't take anymore." Eggs, grits, hash brown casserole (very light -- not), bacon, ham (yummy, but WAAAY too salty), and the star of the show -- biscuits that will make you slap your grandma. At first taste, I wasn't that impressed, but after the 7th or so I concluded that maybe they were pretty good. And served with delicious preserves and sausage gravy. Needless to say, there was no lunch consumed that day. Good coffee and great service. Be prepared for a significant wait during rush times.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The Best Bisquits I've Ever Had

The place was a zoo on a Sunday, with nearly an hour wait--but worth it.  It serves the most amazing bisquits I've ever had--you take a bite, put your tounge up against the underside, and the bisquit just melts like cotton candy.  These bisquits are like crack.

I can't comment on the rest of the food.  It was good, but so overshadowed by the bisquits that even mentioning other food would distract from the real feature at this place.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
The first thing I thought was odd was the $5 up front valet fee...I usually pay more on the back end and this really turned me off.
The location is beautiful and service was great.
I tried several items on the menu:
Beef bone marrow...just to say I've had it once...best thing I can compare it to is beef-flavored snot...one and done with this one
Hamburger and fries...excellent! 
Sausage pasta dish...tasted like a salt lick...even my sodium addict wife said it had entirely too much salt..very disappointing.
Flat bread pizza was great too!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My mother and I first time Nashville. We just wanted some good ol country food. When we walked it was so cute with the wall of fame. We were ordering take out because the wait was very long to be seated. We didnt have time to waiting. So when it came down to ordering the hostess Hiley was sooooo rude. When she had to take our order, when we were sitting down (starring at us so ugly), and when we were getting our food. I never felt so uncomfortable. I was so mad but i didnt say anything because i didnt want to cause a seen. But they with be getting a call and a letter. Thanks Hiley for ruining our first time in Nashville.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Stumbled upon this place by accident but so glad I did. Had the smoked pork chops and the onion soup. Both food and service were excellent. And the brews, don't get me started on the brews. So good!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Not sure where I heard of this place, but I know I had heard of it. We stopped here on a road trip out west. It's a very cute place; was an old hotel, I believe. We ordered food on the phone ahead of time and then picked it up. We ate it in the car. The food was okay, but that may be because I ordered a salad. The biscuits are good, but I'm from the south, so I wouldn't say it was anything spectacular. Definitely think it's worth a shot, but I think I may have missed something about it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Food was great, biscuits were hot and fresh out of the oven, and our server (Mark) was awesome! Highly recommended

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Good food that did appear to be "scratch made" I have the biscuits n gravy.  The gravy did taste scratch made and not from. Mix.  
Biscuits were really tasty. 
The jams were good but the strawberry was
Extremely runny so not very jam like.  The peach really didn't taste overly peachy to me.  
The blackberry was By far my personal fav of the the 3.
Luke was our server. He was attentive And provided us with great service and just the right about of chit chat. 
Nice way to start the day. 
I'd return but might make reservation in advance.  We waited about 1 hour this sunny Sunday morning.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
City Winery has been overlooked and underrated for far too long.  It's time to give them their props. Though this establishment is relatively new to Nashville the clientele who frequent are some of Nashville's finest.  And there is a reason for that.  The service continues to be exceptional.  Yes, truly exceptional.  Wait staff and bartenders take the time to engage and form relationships with diners.  The service is timely, accommodating and personalized.  Ryan Nelson is a staff member who goes above and beyond to make patrons feel not only catered to but at home.
  The change in Chef may have altered the menu, but this establishment has not skipped a beat as far as dishing out delicious choices.  Chef Garrett Pittler brings a much welcomed Buffalo flair to the Southern kitchen.  The Burger on Weck (Menu item: "Black Hawk Farm Burger") does his native town justice.  The Kummelweck roll is perfectly seasoned and baked (no small feat for those who understand this savory sandwich bread - which may be easily crafted but is temperamental to store - therefore, fresh is a must!)  This burger boasts beautifully grilled onions and a horseradish aeoili that tingles the tastebuds.  The Grilled Cheese goes above and beyond in a gourmet Texas Toast style - bringing comfort in a layered combination of two cheeses and fresh thick tomato. Accompany these choices with the Smoked Salt & Vinegar Fingerling Frites to add a tasty compliment.
Top these dishes off with the House Zin - a delicious, fruit and jam forward flavor with a lingering dry finish - and arguably you have a perfect lunch.
Another excellent option is the Kale Caesar flavorful and zesty - an anchovy lovers salad experience!
Much like their sister properties in NYC, Chicago and Napa, this location is now producing their own featured wines. Happy hour at City Winery is a quality experience for visitors and locals alike - a wonderful value!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I've officially set my mom up for failure with a visit to Loveless Cafe two days before Thanksgiving!!  Friendly service, amazing meatloaf and delicious sides.  This little gem was the icing on the cake for our day trip to Nashville.  My only regret... Not saving room for dessert!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is VERY touristy -- for example, there are *multiple* gift shops -- but the food is absolutely worth it. The biscuits are, of course, famous, but their BBQ deserves to be equally well-known. The BBQ pulled-pork omelette was so flavorful, moist, and delectable. You can get a plate of biscuits with four different toppings for variety -- I LOVED the pimiento cheese and fried green tomato biscuit. Their country-style ham is excellent -- it tastes like a thick-cut slice of prosciutto. I'll also note that our server was very friendly and helpful. 
Pro-tip: one of the gift shops has a freezer with Jeni's ice cream in it. :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I visited the Loveless Cafe twice on my recent trip to Nashville. This restaurant never disappoints. The pulled pork and Bloody Marys are wonderful. The granola (might be a side item) is good. I wouldn't recommend the French Toast. But, of course, my favorite part of the meal were the BISCUITS!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: While in town for a conference, I coordinated an evening event to be catered here. The food was great, and the staff were semi-helpful. I would like to have seen a little more hospitality and communication from there. Otherwise, a great experience.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Very delicious. Everything was good. Had the Leberkase. Eggs were cooked perfectly. Also had red cabbage and potato salad. All food was very tasty and they have a nice selection of beers but not extensive. I gave only 4 because I asked for a glass and was given a dirty one. I will return again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Extra long wait during the weekend, but yummy chicken and biscuits!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I attended City Winery New Year's Eve and that evening KIM was my server and she was fantastic. I've been to City Winery a few times and by far Kim provided the best service of any visit. I am not a fan of the wine but the experience she provided certainly helped with that! :) Thanks KIM!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The long lines are for the famous name, but the food is actually delicious.  I'm not sure it was worth the long wait, but once we got in, it was good.  Service was top notch.  The breakfast was satisfying, with basics like eggs, bacon, hashbrown casserole, biscuits and gravy.  My favorite was the pillowy biscuits brought out first with the assortment of jellies.  My daughter got the chicken and waffles and she was not impressed.  I would go back, however, if we were in town again.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Excellent news.. The $15 burger with potato chips was cooked to order and actually tasted good..   A lot of money for a burger, granted, but if you're going to eat there, it's good.  Take my word for it..   The rest of the food is blah.

Seating is still difficult.  You pull your chair out into the aisle, so you can watch the stage and you are up against the other person, at the other table, behind you... and you're fighting for the aisle..  That's still a problem.  A lady and I were practically in one another's laps, trying to view the stage from the aisle........  Thank God she didn't smell.

So.. concerts here are (on a scale from 1-10) about a 3-4 unless you're in the first seats against the stage.
Food (on a scale from 1-10) is a simple 1. unless you have the $15 burger with potato chips.  If you HAVE to eat, the burger is good.  The brussels sprouts have sugar.  Just be warned.

I'm thinking if you sit upstairs on the high tops, you don't have to fight people for the aisle to get a good view of the stage.  You won't be in someone else's lap.  You have more room.  
I'll try that, one of these days.

Going to the Burlesque show tonight....  Again, down on the floor. But I chose a seat that shouldn't have anyone in front of me and I hopefully won't have to fight over the aisle for a view.

This place really is mediocre.. Unfortunately...
Thank God the A/C works.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Found the Loveless Cafe online while looking for restaurants before my wife and I took a trip to Nashville and boy am I glad I did! 

While pulling up I didn't think much of the exterior until I walked in and saw a nicely renovated place with autographs on the walls from nearly 30 years worth of country music acts. We had a roughly 45 minute wait (a testament to how good the food is!) that we spent sitting on a bench outside watching a family play Corn Hole. 

Once inside our waiter Matt was attentive and really nice. He had a personality with out being overbearing and took really good care of us.

 Their signature item is biscuits - they are served with everything. The biscuits were good, not amazing but nothing bad to say about them. Their jam on the other hand was amazing!  For our main course my wife and I both ordered the fried chicken.  It was the best fried chicken I have ever had. It was AMAZING. 

If I didn't live a 13 hour drive away I would be a regular here.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: One of my favorite places in Nashville. Great service, friendly staff, and good music. If you want great German food and lots of good beer, look no further.

name: Big Shotz
text: We stumbled upon on Big Shotz on Friday and we couldn't get over how nice and sweet the Bartender was she took time to get to know us and our drink order! The band was really great! We felt like the Prices for drinks and shots was very reasonable! We made sure to make Big Shotz our first stop on Saturday night and as soon as we walked the sweet bartender not only remembered us from the night before but remembered our drink order as well! Before calling it a night we had to stop back in!! We truly felt like this place is definitely underestimated! We have been telling everyone about it! So if y'all out in Nashville stop by Big Shotz you won't be disappointed!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Absolutely the best German restaurant we've eaten at! The portions are huge!!! The red cabbage was amazing. The service was excellent and the staff was so friendly and hospitable. We will definitely come back!!

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Finally got here for a show--and there is much to like in that format. Good service--thanks Debbie. A solid Old Fashioned and hey put it in perspective--solid concert food. The farm burger with bacon: nicely done. But come here for dining? Probably not, too many better options just minutes away. Also not impressed with the welcome experience here. Never fun when staff are obviously bothered that you don't know what to do. Yet I enjoyed my evening and will take in more shows in the future.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I was visiting Nashville and I had to come here. It's a bit far, 25 mins outside the city but a nice scenery drove. The place was busy but moved quickly with service. The waitresses are polite and attentive. Food is pretty good and biscuit is a bit different then what I was expecting but still good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: They just made it on the tv show 36 where they shared their tip with viewers: put chunks of pink watermelon on smoked ribs and finish off in a 400 degree oven for 30 minutes. The hosts both raved. I will go soon.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Wine for days! Went to dinner since I'd never been. Had a couple of the small plates, pumpkin gnocchi, fries and kale salad and the beet and bacon flatbread. All good, but they are changing the menu, so there are a couple of things that are not carrying anymore. I would like to come back to see a show.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Adorable, iconic, and so tasty! 

Feels like you're eating at your grandmas house. The food was so yummy. Their known for their biscuits and for good reason. My favorite item was the pimento cheese breakfast (listed in the starter section) it was so strong and savory! 

A bit far out but it's a pretty drive so go for it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The food was amazing!!!!! The best creamed corn I have ever eaten!  Peach and strawberry jam are excellent.  Peach jam was like peach pie filling! 
We ordered the fried chicken which was juicy and very good. Great mashed potatoes!!! Fried green tomatoes not that great.  We will definitely be back. The pancakes looked great too!! It's out of the way but worth the drive!!!!!!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: There isn't much to say. This place is amazing. We know that it is a kind of quasi- hipster concept. To bring a German drinking hall to Nashville, complete with polka, and lederhosen, but it isn't ironic at all. In fact, this restaurant is genuine. No weird east Nashville fusion fad recipes. Old school, German recipes like Grandma from the old country made. This is by far my favorite restaurant in Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I am a recent move to Nashville, and like other post, was suggested to go here. I like home style cooking as much as the other place, but this place missed the mark. I got the fried chicken. But, for me, it didn't have enough seasoning. I cannot remember what side I ordered, but I know I was not satisfied with it.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Holy smokes!! Jalapeno and Cajun flavored bacon! Who knew bacon could get better? Biscuits are delicious and the pit bbq pork is excellent!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I love love love their biscuits and homemade jams. If you come here expect to wait anywhere from a few minutes to a few hours. It is definitely a high volume restaurant. We enjoyed walking around the grounds to the little shops while we waited for a table (2ish hours). The food was pretty good but the jam and Biscuits were by far the star of the show. They had a ton of delicious looking pies on display though we did not partake in any of them. I'm not sure we'd go back unless an out of town family member or friend wanted to go because of the usually long wait times but it was pleasant enough experience. Nice attentive service and plenty to look at.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Nice strong coffee. After breakfast I wanted to take a nap in the corner. Homemade everything is hard to really dislike. The potato casserole rivaled my grandmothers and the biscuits. They were basically crack.
Of course friendly southern attitudes complete the experience.. Great breakfast spot. Can't wait to try it for dinner.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Maybe it's because I have been raised around Southern food that I wasn't blown away. Everything just didn't live up to the hype, and I am honestly a little disappointed that I got so excited to eat here. The service was pretty good, and our drinks were always immediately filled. That's probably the reason I feel bad giving Loveless Cafe less than three stars. However, the food... meh. I've had better food from local restaurants from my town (e.g. Beacon Light Tea Room). The biscuits were good, but again, Beacon Light Tea Room has better ones. The fried chicken I ordered tasted a little dry to me, and it caused my stomach to be upset that night. It was nice to say I've had the experience, but I probably will not be returning.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits are fantastic. And the jam/preserves (peach) are equally wonderful. This place is out of the way but absolutely  worth the drive for the biscuits alone. The food is pretty good as well! Fried chicken was a touch too greasy for my liking but still yummy nonetheless.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Went there for a combined Father's Day / German World Cup match early on Sunday morning. They were unprepared for the crowd they got, but in spite of a few moments of confusion we were seated with the entire family and quite enjoyed ourselves. The staff (for the most part) was attentive and pleasant, but a special shout-out to the manager on duty - he ran a tight ship and took care of the initial issues like a pro. The weisswurst and knackwurst were a little bland, but the rest of the food we overall pretty good for a place this size.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Seriously the best. Always a wait but worth it.
Biscuits and homemade jams to start.  Unfortunately you can't just eat those. You have to order food from their variety filled menu items. Chicken and waffle - chicken breast is bone in.  Waffle is hearty. I think it has wheat germ in it.  Don't hold me to my guess . Important part is fluffy means it is hearty and good. 
Southern plate I think it looked good. My friend had the whole thing ate by the time I poured my syrup on my waffle. Must've been good. . 
Biscuit sampler they are biscuit sliders. Choose four from the choices.  
Sausage gravy.  Not the best I've had but I would order it again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Just drove 20 minutes out of the way and had lackluster fried chicken at loveless cafe. Famous for fried chicken?? Booooo.   No seasoning. 

Biscuits tough

Blueberry preserve was excellent, however

BBQ sauce too sweet (on meatloaf and pulled pork)

Paula Deen fried chicken in Pigeon Forge waaaaay better

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The best biscuits ever!! Watermelon ribs are amazing and their jams are sooo good!! Everything we had was wonderful.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I had been wanting to go here for about 2 years now. It did not live up to my expectations. The service was good until we were done eating, stacked all of out plates and 20 min later the server asked how we wanted out check. So it got real slow after 10am when a lot of other people came in. The food was ok, typical southern food. It was a little overpriced but I guess you are paying for the experience. I will not go back unless someone is visiting me and really wants to go. There are much better breakfast places a lot closer to Nashville.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
A lot of hype and super long wait for an average breakfast. The biscuits and preserves are worth the hype, but not worth the wait. Order to go and sit at a picnic table on the property is the way to go.

The atmosphere was cool. They had a band playing some bluegrass. It was a pretty day to sit on the steps and enjoy. 

When I ordered, I asked for the bacon to be cooked crispy. The waitress said all the bacon is cooked crispy, but it came out limp and fatty. 

Overall, it was decent but been to better.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The biscuits!!!! Delicious! We ordered the family style "all you can eat"....the sausage was tasty, the jams were good. Good service..All in all, a great family place for breakfast.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: 3 shows under our belts here, supper club...dining, drinking, music and chit chat.  It is lovely, not a bad seat in the house.  Our preference is upstairs in what they call VIP area.  Great view and easier to chit chat.  Go downstairs if you want to make new friends as you sit close.  Food is good, me loves the Kale salad and risotto cheese balls.  Super satisfactory on all levels.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I would give this place 5 stars if I didn't have to wait two hours to eat...but I will say that it was worth the two hours!  The food was amazing!  We were from Chicago and wanted real country cooking and we got it. The staff is amazing too.  Only downside is I wish they had some more stores to shop in :)

name: City Winery Nashville
text: Excellent. First of all, the space is incredible. It acts as a restaurant and an event space with two venues (one smaller, one larger). Got to see that they make wine in house, as well. There's nothing I love better than authenticity. There is ample seating here, from multiple patios to a main dining area. I came with a big party and we were accommodated very well. Also, I came for a birthday and the staff made sure we received a free bottle of champagne to celebrate. This kind of courteousness goes a long way. The staff handled our huge party very well and had everything out to us in a timely manner. This place is great for a date night, a birthday party, and event, or a wedding. Loved my time here.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I have not seen a show here so can only speak on the dining experience. I took my mother there for her birthday to try some of the wines and share appetizers. You wouldn't think this would be such a let down. The food was a TERRIBLE let down. we first ordered a flatbread which was supposed to have parmesan, mushroom confit, red onion, apple butter, and red pepper olive oil. When it came out it also had some kind of greens on it....guessing collard. If you are going to put ingredients on a flatbed, you need to have it on the menu. Even though it took a long time to come out, it was still overly doughy with a strange bitterness taste. We sent that back immediately. 

While looking over the menu to find anything else to eat while we drank our overly priced wine, we thought maybe we would share a bottle of wine. The sommelier came over to us to go over some of them. You would think he would go into detail about a few wines, but instead asked a question or two of what we liked, pointed to a page for us to look over, and then pointed to the most expensive bottle of wine on the page. 

Still wanting to give it a chance, hoping that the flatbread was a fluke, we ordered the risotto balls (a recommendation by our server). They were BLAND. If you live in the south or are going to have a restaurant in the south, learn how to season your food! We heard the chef came from Holland House so I was really excited to see what it was about. Total Let down. I will NEVER go back. 

Another thing to mention is the LBTD tax (%15 added on to the wine on the tap) that they slip in there. There is small print on the menu letting you know this, but it is very small. 

I wouldn't even waste my time.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If you're a savvy traveler, you would have already seen Loveless cafe on all the top lists "What to do" and "What not to miss" in Nashville. With so much publicity and fame, you would have thought this place to be a tourist trap. CONTRARY. It is the most "homey" and welcoming atmosphere! PLUS their food is OUT OF THIS WORLD. Fried chicken for breakfast? While a norm in Nashville, Loveless' take is far from the norm. THIS IS A MUST.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Paid a visit for breakfast and I was stuffed after the biscuits! The biscuits are absolutely amazing along with their spreads. I highly recommend visiting if the opportunity presents. Staff was incredibly friendly, family friendly and fun environment. Shopping also on property.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Based on the reviews, I was expecting something good. Sadly, it was not. It felt like a touristy chain restaurant with Americanized German food.

The giant pretzel did not seem fresh (and I know a fresh handmade pretzel can be delicious), and the beer cheese dip was flavorless. (I think they just used the beer cheese soup as the dip.) The sausages were fine - nothing special. The best thing I ate was the red cabbage, which was pretty good. The whipped mashed potatoes appeared to be instant potatoes. The potato dumpling was rubbery and for some mysterious reason had a crouton hidden in the middle (which is apparently a traditional thing?).

Service was fine, no complaints there. Space was huge and seemed to be clean and orderly. Prices were moderate, but the food was not worth it.

I wanted to like it and wish I could have better things to say, but I was totally unimpressed. :(

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Good food. Good service. Maybe expected more from having almost a 2 hour wait. Really anticipated to be wowed. 
Typical southern food. My gf and I split the fried pork chops w/ eggs (Sunnyside up bcuz what respectable self proclaimed food critic wouldn't) and the Southern Sampler (Fried chicken, meatloaf and BBQ). The chicken was good and so was the BBQ. The meatloaf seemed greasy and plain. Our sides were the Mac n cheese (the real deal!!!), fried ocra (avg) and the hashbrown casserole (basic and under cooked). We ordered the fried green tomatoes as an app which were tied with the Mac n cheese for amazing.
I'd say overall the food was average but maybe people go there more for the experience than the food. I will say Ms. Anne and Rock in the store were the best and would be the only reason to give a four or five

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: The food was tasteless and the waiter, grumpy.  I had the fish & chips - a waste of time and money.  One big piece of fish that was tough and over cooked.  I couldn't even eat the "fries," which were soggy lumps of undercooked potatoes.  We ordered the potato pancakes as an appetizer - they were cold, hard and tasteless as well.  We won't be going back again.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: What a fun music venue. We saw Bobby Bare and Bobby Bare Jr a couple of weeks ago and it was a fantastic show. It's nice to have dinner options beyond the standard bar fare (ahem, 3rd and Lindsley). The wine selection is as good as you'd expect from a place called "winery". A few gripes - we bought VIP tickets and must have been the only ones, because they didn't open that section. They gave us decent seats, but didn't offer to reimburse us. The tables are community, so we got seated with some obnoxious college kids constantly snapping selfies. Service seemed to still be working out the system. But a great show will save a lot of service sins.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I worked in a fine dining German restaurant years ago, so I am going to try to not rate this place based on that. As usual, I will cover the good and bad, and try to avoid the ugly. I should note that I did not have the full experience, as I was with my daughter who was yucking German food at the time, so my in-house experience was in the bar waiting for food.

One thing that struck me was how much the employees, bar and floor, were spending with another employee who was at a table in the bar area, rather than focusing on customers. I understand it is a slow night, but had I not paid my bill right when I ordered, I would have had a difficult time getting any type of attention. I hope this was an off night.

First, the atmosphere is on point for a German bierhaus, except perhaps a bit too bright and a less communal feel in many ways. The beer comes in standard European sizes, all the way up to a liter stein. And, while I did not see anyone drinking out of one, they have steins for regulars in their own little lockers. Did not see a Stammtisch, so not sure if they have that type of designation for strong regulars.

The food? I had the King Ludwig Patter so I could try a bunch of different foods. The rouladen was good, but a bit dry (overcooked?). The Kassler Ripchen was nicely smoked and the highlight of the meal. A chop and the two krauts would have been a nice meal. The cut is a bit thinner than I have had in the past, but very nice flavor and well cooked. I did not get to try the Knackwurst that came with the plate, as it was missing when I got home (my spidey senses were tingling to check before I left, but I ignored them, so I put this on me). 

As for the sides. Pretty standard sauerkraut and the red cabbage is not the overly sweet crap I have had at some German restaurants. As for the whipped potatoes and gravy, I felt they were rather fake feeling and would have much rather had some Spätzle than the potatoes. Honestly, the downpoint of the meal.

I also grabbed an Apfelstrudel for dessert. Not the style I am used to (had a topping), but very tasty. I would much rather have a drier version, like I am used to, but different strokes?

I really would have like to try a wurst of some type, so I am a bit saddened they had a lack of quality control that night. Yes, perhaps I should have contacted management to get it fixed, but I live on the other side of Nashville, so I am not sure when I will get my next chance to travel over (but if they read this and keep a list, I would still like to try the wurst).

I will likely get back at some time and try a schnitzel next round. I would also like to Spätzle.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We went on a Friday morning and got seated right away. Service was good. The biscuits were great and the food was really good. The southern omelet was loaded. Prices were pretty decent for breakfast too. If you like strong coffee it was pretty strong. Definitely cute and lives up to the expectations.
