name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Friends and I came here for breakfast on our first morning in Nashville and were not disappointed! 

Biscuits and homemade preserves to start off a meal?! Yes, please!
Moonshine in your Bloody Mary?! Of course!
One of the best southern breakfasts ever?! For sure!

I loved the Southern Plate (eggs, bacon, sausage, country fried ham and hasbrown casserole). It was the perfect amount of food and gave me a taste of what Loveless is known for.

Our waitress was great, the host was even better! If you're in Nashville, this is a must visit piece of Americana history.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Excellent service, excellent biscuits, great atmosphere.  I'm not much of a jam/jelly person, but all three I tried with my biscuits were above average...ok they were all yummy!  I'll be back!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I took my staff to lunch at Loveless to celebrate a co-worker's birthday.  It was a big hit.  Many of us were new to Nashville and really enjoyed this staple.  As a true southerner, I would say that the biscuits are a little overhyped but they were still quite good.  It's just a matter of personal taste though.  I will definitely go back and take more friends in the future.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Not sure why anyone would leave a Negative review about this Restaurant its AMAZING food and service !!!! Nothing beats Great service Thank you Brittany for that but Great food and this place has both a must try in Nashville don't pass this one up !!!

name: Dirty Little Secret
text:
Venue - One of the only Vegas style club here in Nashville that I've seen. Place is cool with that Speakeasy/Underground feel to it when you see it from outside. The inside is a decent size, with a decent size bar . 

Door people - Staff here is hella chill and not all stuck up like Cali, Miami,  etc places as they are actually nice and helpful. 

Price - Not sure what they charge as I was a hotel guest and had free entry. 

Dress code - They do have a slight dress code especially on shoes,  they want people to have that club attire look.

Music - Music was chill when I went but it was dead so the main dj wasn't on yet, and it was at the beginning of the night.

Crowd - A bit mixed of a crowd. 

Overall cool spot and would be back to check it out on the next visit.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless Cafe has a country vibe! Their biscuits are amazing and you must order them! The waitress and staff are super sweet! If you're in Nashville, gotta check this place out!

name: Big Shotz
text: The place was smoky and not friendly. I would not recommend spending your money. I tried the Collier & McKeel Bourbon, not impressed.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: The acoustics were great and I enjoyed the show.  The drinks were overpriced.  The menu online did not match the menu, which was disappointing as the item I planned to order was not available.  The food we did order was just bad.  I ordered a steak which was over cooked and over seasoned.  My friend ordered a pasta dish which was dense and lacked flavor.  I will go back for shows, but will not order food again.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
So far as atmosphere goes? Just lovely - absolutely perfect! All else needs a little more work to get there. You can tell the food is inspired, but just isn't quite... good, to be frank. Or if it is good, it is just good, and certainly not great. Poorly seasoned, odd flavors, everything we ordered was missing something or had too much of another thing. I cant remember if we had a waiter or waitress, they paid us so little mind. Won't be on the list of places we re-visit unless maybe for a glass of wine before a show... we'll see

Edit: As promised, the manager did contact us. No change in my review, but it's always good to know that concerns are being heard and not falling on deaf ears. This kind of commitment, I'm sure, will lead to improvement.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Bavarian Bierhaus in Opry Mills is an authentic German restaurant/bar exuding the spirit of Oktoberfest.  It's impossible to miss the huge building as it proudly displays the name with their emblem of a lion holding a stein in the classic royal blue and white, as the colors of Bavaria. The style inside is reminiscent of a Munich bierhall with large communal tables and benches to sit on and a stage for live music. Near the entrance past a small gift shop and colorful mural they also have a bar area with smaller bar tables and chairs and an outdoor patio area. 

Although this is a bierhaus they have a full bar. If you are unsure what type of German beer you'd like to get you could opt for a flight of 6 beers, 4 oz each. They will give you 4 of the famous beers then you can pick the other 2 for the flight. These are served on a large wooden paddle. If you want one certain type of beer they have 3 sizes to choose from--.3 liter, .5 liter, or 1 liter of beer. I got the .5 liter of the Paulaner Premium Pils which was refreshing and really good. Somehow it is also more fun to drink beer out of a huge stein than just a regular pint class. If you want to be THAT person who gets wine at a bierhaus you can order to your liking as they have 4 different reds and whites each.

The food menu has many of the German staples such as wurst (sausage) or schnitzl (breaded chicken or pork that is pan seared). We got a giant pretzel ($9) that comes with mustard and we also got a side of the warm bier cheese ($3). The cheese is worth it to get with the pretzel and our server told us as much--it was great! The pretzel was a good choice to soak up all that beer we were drinking as well! 

I was really impressed by this gem of a place in the Opry Mills. Parking is easy as there is a huge lot and they are open until midnight I believe on Fridays/Saturdays so it can be a great place to go hang out and have a few drinks with friends. Whether you come to have a few beers, a meal or to hear live music it is a good spot for large groups as they have plenty of room.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: New place but pretty fun. The bar tenders were prompt and pleasant. I've had the patty melt and breakfast sandwich. No complaints food wise. I could definitely see this as a great pregame place for preds or titans games. I'm looking forward to see this place in full swing come this summer. The outdoor bar looks like a lot of fun in nice weather.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Their biscuits are life, but I've been Keto for three months  so I had to branch it and try new things. So my staple fried chicken, fried fish, fried pork chops, had to go. So I mixed up this visit: Sunday brisket, cucumbers and onions, and turnip greens. It's a WIN!
The only complaint would be that the pieces had a bit too much fat, but they were still good. Good color, awesome hickory flavor, tender the au jus really set it off. A really good meal with a really good price.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Ok people, listen up. If you are in or near Nashville, you NEED TO EAT HERE!! I give this place 25 stars, but Yelp only offers 5, but just know it's really 25. My husband and I came to Nashville on our honeymoon, and people told us 100 different places to eat, (most of which sucked). Then, we took a carriage ride and asked the driver where he likes to eat. He said the Loveless Cafe, and so we were like it can't be any worse than the other God awful tourist traps we went to. Oh. My. God. Y'all. The food tastes like little baby Jesus came down from heaven and cooked the food Himself. I had the 1/2 fried chicken, fried okra, and mashed potatoes. My husband had the chicken livers, fried green tomatoes, and hash brown casserole. Oh, and THE BISCUITS!! LORD JESUS, the homemade biscuits!! I took one bite and the hallelujah choir started singing. I imagine it's what the food must taste like in heaven, and I'm not a really religious person. Seriously, go. It's like 30 mins outside of Nashville, but it's worth the drive. You won't regret it!!

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
This is for January 22, a Monday, early afternoon so it was slow. But with the interior, list of activities & drink list I can see that it probably gets super busy at night. 
The chips and salsa were really good. Best tortilla chips I've ever had, nice job. I got Philly  sandwich and fries. It was ok. The chicken strips the kids ordered looked really tender and breaded good. What I wish I'd ordered after seeing them lol. 
My son had turkey club he seemed to like it but still hungry after eating it. 
Service was ok. There seemed to be workers everywhere then gone to who knows where when wanted to ask for something. But maybe it. As prep time for evening or something. They were nice and we had a good lunch. 
Place is very clean. They do great on that. 
As we were leaving I saw they had a corn hole game, that's always a fun one.

name: Drifters
text: Visited here a couple times recently for their ribs.  They always fall off the bone and some of the best I have tried in Nashville.  I have only visited during lunch and the waitress/bartender is awesome and has a great personality.  Looking forward to my next return!

name: Drifters
text: Wow little hole in the wall looking with great staff very informative our waiter said they use a dry rob on their brisket & a little bit of wet rob just before they take it out.... we got the brisket plate it came with black beans, slaw & fries.... it was great thanks

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Phenomenal environment! The shrimp po boy was amazing! Sampler platter had a great variety! Food was excellent!!!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: We sure do love to keep things local here in Nashville! If you ever become a member of anything in this town, be sure to join at the Belcourt! You get reduced admission prices and a discount in concessions. PLUS, you get to watch any and all of the great movies that come through here; movies we wouldn't normally get to see in any other theater around here and I'm so grateful for that!

name: Drifters
text: Was visiting Nashville and happened upon Drifter's by accident in my search for BBQ after a much closer restaurant was out of chicken, ribs and practically everything else but the BBQ sauce. However, Drifters was the most pleasant surprise in a visit filled with great meals!  Drifters looks like both a dive bar and a down home restaurant at the same time, and as out of towners we appreciated the comfortable, informal environment. The staff were welcoming and friendly and very attentive. Leah our server was great and by the time we left we were hugging the Manager goodbye - it wAs that kind of place! In terms of the food, it was nothing short of spectacular. We had the half baby back ribs dinner and a pulled chicken salad and both were great. The ribs were perfectly cooked and the meat fell off the bone. Drifters has a BBQ sauce bar so you can choose your preference for your ribs - I liked the Smoke Fire best, which was a Texas style sauce with some chipotle kick to it! Also had the tots, the baked beans and the cole slaw, all of which were superb. I did leave there a little disappointed, but only because I don't live nearby and can't come back any time soon. However, I am definitely going to tell all my Nashville friends about it, and look forward to visiting on my next trip!!!

name: EXIT/IN
text:
Bands/performers: 
Security and staff was kind of weird and a bit rude. I was doing merch for a well known band and they made it complicated for the band members to get back stage. Make sure to bring your contract, they misplaced out & it was a bit complicated to get our buyouts before they found the contract. Also make sure to do sound check because things got complicated when request where made to have the musicians sound like the band wanted to.

name: Drifters
text: I can't even begin to explain how disappointing was.  I got the bbq sampler platter, so I tasted all the main stays.  All of it was flavorless and dry.  The chicken was the worst.  Then the pork. The ribs were sad.  The sausage was fine - I think they source it elsewhere, which makes sense. The service was good - not their fault.

name: Drifters
text: We stopped in here for a drinks. The location was convenient as it was just a short walking distance from our restaurant. We did not eat any of the food because we were waiting on our restaurant to call us with an open table. The service was prompt and pleasant. Their beer menu was decent. Their are no cocktails on the menu and for good reason...the one I asked them to make tasted like cough syrup.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: I'll start by saying I'm a bit biased. I'm a new board member. The Belcourt is one of our local treasures. The beautiful theatre and the incredibly talented and dedicated staff honor its tradition. Between the wonderful film selection (new films are added weekly!), special events, great popcorn and bar-yes, I said-bar, becoming a member of the Belcourt gives back-tenfold. Bring a group of friends, see the midnight movie series. It's money well spent.

name: Springwater
text:
I ducked in here last year and was too early for the show but hung out in a very funky room with a very cool group of performers until we had to head out for another commitment.  Everyone was so cool AND welcoming, it was on my return trip list fo sho.

So, this year, we found ourselves roaming the neighborhood, looking for a white bbq sauce fix, and we decided, why not put the two together!?!  

We stuck a head in and asked it they were cool with carry out carry ins, and they totally were.  We ran next door, grabbed the addictively enslaving turkey sammie from Hog Heaven, and came right back to sit at the bar and enjoy a few adult bevs with said sammie.  It was a match made in Nashville heaven.  The barkeep was attentive and welcoming, which should maybe be this city's new motto.  

I didn't notice any smoke until my post-bbq, cigarette-sucking dining companion lit up, happy as a clam, and announced he was home.  He was blowing smoke at me, though, for affect, so that was key re: my noticing smoke.  Smoking never quite "took" for me personally, but I thoroughly appreciate a little touch of smoker's haven while imbibing. 

Next year, third time has to be a charm, and I need to catch a band PERFORMING here.

Thanks for the great time!

P.S. I used the bathroom and was not scarred for life.  Don't get me wrong, I'm a huge fan of creature comforts, but I was also secretly raised a townie, so I've used the bathroom next to a tractor pulling a hayride wagon.  But, compared to that, this was a dream.  Its all about perspective, kids.

name: The Country
text: Awesome atmosphere! Lots of great beers on tap. Outdoor space with garage door that opens into indoor space. Very country chic!

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
Awesome place! Visited from New Orleans and came here to check out the LSU Tigers for the College World Series.
Great atmosphere, excellent beer selection, and delicious  food.
Special shout out to Jenna and Jot for top-notch customer service even though the power went out for a minute or two we had a blast and they made me feel like home. 
I will surely  be back and recommend it to everyone.

name: EXIT/IN
text: If you're short like me, get there early to get a spot on the small raised platform. It helps!

name: Drifters
text:
Our first meal in Nashville. It was great!!  Perfect atmosphere. Perfect service. Perfect hush puppies. 
Two for one happy hour beers was a nice Friday night surprise. 
Ribs are nice. Smoked nicely. Pulled pork and brisket done nice. Sweet bean side nice. Nachos very good. Fried pickles very good. 
Cole slaw a little to "creamy". Sausage good. 
Overall, great pub feel with great food and service.
Add: big whisky selection. Nice effort.

name: The Country
text: Super mediocre. Mac and cheese was good, Korean pork tacos had a huge bone shard in them, drink was unnecessarily sweet- almost undrinkable, music was ok, but sound was bad. Service was lovely. Product unfortunately not so much.

name: Drifters
text: Nice low key atmosphere.  Outdoor dining.  Live music.

name: The Local
text:
Very cool spot with a heavy focus on music. Pros: clean, great stage and sound system, neat decor. 
Cons: not incredibly inviting staff, hard to get a drink, very expensive beer.

name: Springwater
text: This bar is one of the oldest bars in Nashville and has been open since 1897.  It has such a feel of quaintness and old time goodness.  The band hadn't started playing but the venue is small and I think would have given you the feel of a personal concert since the tables were less than 2 ft from the stage. They only serve beer and soft drinks, but it is a local hangout if you are looking for something other than the nightmare of Broadway.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text:
I've been to several shows at the Cannery, and I've always thought the house sound was unnecessarily loud. I bring earplugs to rock shows, but last night I saw The Wind and the Wave - basically mildly amped acoustic. The volume level was insane! My ears are still ringing. Butch Walker played a great set after, but I went around the corner and listened through layers of brick to enjoy it.

This isn't Spinal Tap. No need to put everything on 11. I've been watching live shows since 1970, and there's absolutely nothing gained by setting the sound board on stun!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
Amazing venue!
I've only visited for the Rifftrax Live events, and they have always been impressive.  Great service and presentation.  The staff seems genuinely happy to host the event.

Great place for unique events.

(Frequent traveller from out of town)

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: This was my first concert experience in music city and I'm hoping this place isn't representative of what Nashville has to offer. The most important things to know are that parking is actually $10 cash and you should dress light because there is essentially no air flow in what in all honesty is just an old warehouse. Security was efficient, but not too friendly. I was treated like my out of state ID was fake which felt silly and unnecessary. Bartenders were similar. Canned tallboys are $5-7. Yuengling was cheaper than Budweiser, which was uncanny but convenient. Doors said they'd open at 8, actually opened around 8:45. Show started right on time. Sound was good, but not great. Floor isn't inclined so it's not easy to see the band because the place holds like 1,000 people. Leaving the parking lot wasn't too terrible for a sold out show. I wouldn't go back unless I really, really liked the band. It was just too humid and claustrophobic and felt like way too many people for what I'm pretty sure was the second floor of a very old building.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
There is always something worth going to watch at the Belcourt. I've been coming here since I was an annoying teenager, before I could appreciate its awesomeness or partake in their adult beverages. The old theatre atmosphere is so warm and fun that it's even worth going to see a bad movie here. You'll still leave happy with the whole experience. And they do in fact play some terrible movies on occasion, because some cult classics are so awful that they just have to been seen (The Room, for one). 

As I mentioned, they serve beer and wine, which is a treat. And I always get the impression that the folks who work here truly enjoy their jobs. Everybody wins.

name: Drifters
text: Stopped in for an early dinner on my way through Nashville. I sat on the patio with my dog and ordered the sampler plate. It included 3 oz of brisket, 3 oz pulled chicken, smoked sausage, 1/3 rack of ribs and 2 sides. The ribs fell off the bone and the sausage was fantastic. I wasn't too impressed with the chicken, but the smoky brisket, perfectly crispy tater tots and tasty slaw made up for it. And they offered 5 varieties of sauces with varying heat and sweetness. Waitstaff was excellent, took great care of my pup and included wet wipes and plasticware with my to-go box. Don't let the dive-bar feel throw you. This place is legit and definitely worth checking out.

name: Drifters
text:
Fun bar with trivia on Monday nights and friendly bartenders. The bartender helped me save a drunk fly by putting it outside - how nice is that? 

Wasn't particularly impressed with the BBQ though, a bit dry. I liked that their menu had options for vegetarians as well.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: I have a love-hate affair with Cannery.  The bands they book here are incredible.  I've seen Mat Kearney, Grace Potter and the Nocturnals, Alt-J, Punch Brothers...you name it...I've honestly lost track of how many times I have been here.  So why don't I LOOOOVE it you ask?  Its the layout.  It's that simple.  There are currently three different venues within the Cannery Row complex, with the Ballroom being the biggest.  The stage is far back within the open space.  The bar runs along the far wall.  But the problem is that unless you are right in front of the stage you are pretty much guaranteed to be off to the right, in some cases they very far right, and good luck seeing anything whatsoever from that angle.  The sound as a result of the odd positioning isn't always on point either.  Even with the massive bar it can take a long time to get a beverage.  But yet the acts are so fantastic.  They really are.  I grumble every time I see someone I love playing here, but I go anyways and hope I can get close enough to actually see them.  The space can also be rented for private parties and weddings, and for those sorts of things it works really really well.  I enjoy special non-concert events here very much.  But just be aware that you might be visually impaired at any show unless you get the coveted spots directly before the stage.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
They have redone the lobby and now it feels like a shot fun style entrance. They repositioned the doors so that they face the parking lot and that is nice. The new bathrooms are a huge improvement as well.
However, they have not replaced to original seats. The first three I sat in were broken. They do not compare to a new theater in terms of comfort. The result is that you get some of the old and some of the new. We will see more movies here in the future.

name: Drifters
text: As far as East Nashville BBQ joints go, this  one is the best. Their smoked chicken quesadillas are phenomenal. (I've eaten them twice this week... Don't judge me.) When you add great drink specials and a low key outdoor patio (that's pup friendly) to the fantastic BBQ, it is easily one of my favorite places to eat out in East Nashville.

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
Mercy Lounge, it has been twice now that you have provided an awesome drinking experience. Whiskey fueled dancing, furious drinking, laughing and tom foolery. 

This place is a host to an excellent music venue. The crowd both times was, fun, enthusiastic, non-violent, and raging or maybe that was just us.. bonus.

The new years eve event was fucking awesome. Sweet ass 90's cover band destroyed the venue. And as I am attempting to recall the night through a whiskey tinted memories. One thing is for sure.. We had a blast.. and will return.

name: The Local
text: Jamie is the best!! She is so friendly and welcoming and pours a great drink. Pretzel bites were so good we ordered a second basket. Our welcome to Nashville has been the best, we will be back! Thank you Jamie for getting our trip off to an awesome start!

name: Drifters
text: Super cozy spot with awesome food. Had the homemade massive corn dogs that are spot on. Thick layer of hush puppy batter. Best tater tots I've ever had on the side. Chips and queso on point to start. Homemade sauce bar all with a different tastes and temperatures. Tried some of my friends brisket and the Mac and cheese as well without disappointed. 2 massive corn dogs with a Mountain of tater tots for I believe under $8! Definitely would go back and definitely recommend!

name: The Family Wash
text: Met a friend here for pint and pie night. Ordered the meatloaf - yum! The music was great. I really liked how cozy this spot was and will probably return.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: One of my favorite venues in nashville. I've seen some of my favorite bands here and have never been disappointed. The venue is big enough to fit a large number of people but still small enough to be an intimate show. The only problem we had was that we had gotten one pbr from the bar and our tab was $14. Which is a little sketchy. But oh well.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: What a fun bar! Plenty of seating, nice and spacious, lots of TV's, and it was nice to see that they attract so many people of differing ethnicities! I'll definitely go back :)

name: Experience Nashville Tours
text: My husband and I took a walking tour of Nashville with our tour guide, Kaysie Young.  Great inside information.  Kaysie was very friendly and knowledgeable. Based on some of these inside tips, we changed up our schedule and the rest of our trip went much more smoothly.  Highly recommend this tour as part of your Nashville experience.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: I will first say that I was brunching with a large group, however, we waited over TWO AND A HALF HOURS for our food. Four people in our group never never ended up getting their food (two order were not even put in), and one plate had a hair in the food. ON TOP OF THAT, one person of my group told the owner about our horrible service. The owner responded by calling the member of my group a horrible person. What type of OWNER does that?! This is such a poorly run establishment. I will never return, and I would never recommend this place.

name: Commodore Grille
text:
Most people seem to be reviewing this place for dinner and live music, but I came here for the breakfast buffet. At $11.99 for a slightly upscale continental breakfast, I wasn't impressed.

Compared to the East Coast, food in Nashville is so cheap. I can get a massive dinner for $10 in Nashville so the price for a mediocre buffet was too high. I had a bagel, bacon, eggs, pancakes, and an apple pastry. The bagel and eggs were on par with what a Quality Inn would serve on a continental breakfast. The bacon was actually quite good as were the pancakes. The apple pastry was pretty good too. But if you stay somewhere like a Hyatt Place, you will get a better breakfast, and it will be included in the room cost. 

The saving grace of this place was the wait staff. I ate at the bar, and the guy taking care of me was really friendly. The whole staff was dressed up for Halloween, which was cute. 

I wouldn't come back here for anything other than the live music, personally.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
2 stars off for counter service: $8 for 2 lilliputian tamales that were about 1.5 inches short and dry as chalk in your mouth on a summer day in the Chiapas. I was told "they were good" and I'd get a decent amount. In other words.... screwed over by otherwise usually accommodating and very genuine staff.

The experiemce wasn't in line with the general brand and experience which, if consistently applied in ALL their affairs, would get the 5 stars. 

It's the little things, (apparently like their artisinal community yoga goat-crafted, gold-flake, small-batch powdery ol' tamales,) which count. And whoever's counting how much $ they make off of delivering cusomers a thing, which is ... absolutely nothing worth putting down your throat-hole.

If the profits were all going to a just cause other than the overhead of the theatre, yah, I'd be prepared. But this just felt dirty. Gritty, and dirty. In the mouthal area, sure, but also like I'd been touched funny back THERE when I wasn't looking.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Went here on a Tuesday night to see Joe Jonas and DNCE, first visit ever. We did have to wait in line as others mention but it didn't take that long at all. Inside is just an open space. It's essentially a contest of who is the rudest person in the room. People shoving and stepping on you trying to get closer to the stage. If someone tall is in front of you, too bad, you can't see at all. And yes, it was hot. But my biggest grievance is that there was a tiny section carved out by the bar for 21+. Corralled into about 1/8th of the venue, we had to stay over there to drink. Luckily for us, this is where the giant poles are located. Was this just a thing for DNCE? The 21+ area was PACKED. So I am not the only "old lady" there!

name: Frisky Frog's
text: This is Now called Live Oak. It's under totally new management and is Amazing. Super friendly with great food and place to watch any game. Also the patio has a putting green.

name: Drifters
text: Pretty good BBQ. Drifters is half dive bar, half barbecue restaurant with a cool outside area where they feature really good musicians. I ordered brisket and it looked more like pulled pork, but I shut up and ate it and it was good lol. I enjoyed the sauce, as well, and the service was on point.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: Don't go!!!! They collect a cover and the band played 1 minute of a last set. Not worth making the trip to the Gulch!!!

name: The Local
text: Great little spot with music of course. We got lucky and had multiple players doing some bluegrass. They have a nice outside patio for the warm days. Staff seemed be really engaged with the customers. Looked like they actually cared.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
I had some time to kill before checking into the room I rented, and I was in the neighborhood shopping, so I decided to stop in and see a movie at the Belcourt. If I lived in Nashville I'd probably have a membership. The staff were friendly and there's plenty of parking for patrons.

I saw a show in the late afternoon, so there were only a dozen or two people in the theater. Prices are very reasonable, and they show a great collection of art and indie films that can be hard to find at mainstream theaters--I saw Obvious Child when I visited, and I can't even find that being shown in Chicago outside one theater. It's not a run-down place; it may not have the fancy seating that brand new theaters have, but it's perfectly comfortable. If you're visiting, have a couple hours to spare, and are in the area, check out the schedule. And if you're local, you have no excuse!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: quaint theater! always have interesting/new/foreign/obscure movies! would love to be a member here!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Deff one of the bigger honky tonks on the broadway strip. I mean theres actually some space to move in this place. When we got here there was no music on any of the floors. Maybe we can during the bands break but even still there was no music playing at all. It was easy getting drinks here, and a good spot for bigger groups, but might have less of the Nashville charm as other places.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
For live music- 5 stars! Has a huge stage for performers and it's a large bar for group gatherings but as much as I appreciated the entertainment, I would be happy going to a smaller more intimate bar where it's easy to get a drink and you can enjoy the music with out being surrounded by a loud environment. 

For food, it's bar food. The service is nothing special. The margarita special for 5 dollars was watered down. I would definitely go hit up a BBQ joint then eat here if you are looking for dinner. 

For night life it's like a college party. Crazy, crazy lines with a younger crowd so I would just walk down until you don't have to wait in line and can actually breathe in whatever bar you get into. Maybe it's because I'm getting older but if you're a tourist, it's worth being able to get a sense of live music in those smaller bars.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: First trip to Nashville and first place we stopped at. The music was very good but the service was awful. We sat at the bar got 2 beers, bartender took credit card and never acknowledged us again. We tried waving her down multiple times but nothing. We finally decided to eat somewhere else and had to find another worker to get our card so we could cash out.  Pretty sad for this place because I only heard good things.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: First time in Nashville on a girls trip. Super friendly staff and awesome food. Saw Isaac Mathews.  Honestly never a country fan. Man he changed my mind. Truly AMAZING voice!!! Lucky enough to meet him, sweet person. Highly recommend.

name: The Back Corner
text:
This place is unique to the area, and an establishment for future lounge/clubs in the city that is Nashville. How convenient to have a place  right across the street from where you live, can grab a drink when you get off from work, before the stressed come out to get loose. 

I was on soon enough to read the review of the patron who complained of the manager. I was in the vicinity of the encounter. With the place being as crowded and busy as it was, the manager could not have handled the situation anymore professionally than she had, given the circumstances. To add, the place was congested with people, and the fire alarm was going off. Given those circumstances, you can imagine the hand dealt.

As is with a patient, they sometimes think they are the only one the doctor has to tend to. That was the case with these patrons who were being irrational, and also drunk. I was there, near the entire incident, and the manager did not just instantly call them a bitch. In fact, she asked a question, after accidentally bumping into them. The women said, "did you just push me,bitch?" And the manager replied, "Did you just call me a bitch?" Any reasonable person can see how that can get misconstrued. 

With the place as busy as it had been, and that particular group as incorrigible as they were, the manager could not have handled the situation any better. They were a small part of a large whole-which was the entire place packed with people. She excused herself from bumping into them, as it was crowded. They chose to escalate the situation when she tried to resolve it. Given the circumstances, which was the place being packed, she had no choice but to have them removed. They were not within reason.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
We stumbled across this place while walking on Broadway. 

The music was loud and everyone inside looked like they were having a great time. 

We walked in and there were a ton of people dancing on the first floor and the tables were full. We went upstairs and another band was playing! 

There were a few empty tables, so we grabbed a seat. The music was great, the atmosphere was fun and the waitress was friendly. 

The food was ok and the price was very reasonable. I would go back for sure!

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: Dive bar without the grime. Great warm place with music to be heard. Good place to hang for a beer.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
My past few visits to Nashville I've found it to be consistently the best bar on Broadway. 
3 levels and 3 stages with live bands. Fun crowd. People watching. 
The bands on the main stage are great!

name: Live On The Green Music Festival
text: I only got to Live on the Green once this summer but looking forward to returning next year. We had VIP tickets, so we were treated to lots of delicious food and enjoyed the show from the towers at the side of the square, which offered great views of the stadium, river, other parts of Nashville and yes, the stage. The music might have gotten a bit lost as I happily devoured appetizers such as candied bacon and bacon-wrapped peppers. But, this free festival is just one of the many things that makes Nashville so great. The audience range in age from young to old, babies, dogs, hippies and businessmen. Just a lot of different people coming together for some great music outside. I love this town.

name: The Station Inn
text: While in Nashville for vacation, we were looking for somewhere with a bluegrass set and did we find it! Sunday night is their bluegrass jam session- this place was packed with people from all over the world. Super cool place to have a beer and listen to some raw talent (old and young) just enjoy playing music together. I highly recommend making a stop here if you love live music and would like to get away from all the lights of the broadway strip!

name: The Station Inn
text: If you are in Nashville, it's a must to come to the Station Inn. Plain and simply, it is the greatest music venue on the planet!

name: The Cowan
text:
3.5 stars.

We saw The Fixx here last weekend and drove up from Atlanta to do it.  The sound was excellent, you could see from just about anywhere, the staff generally friendly and the drinks surprisingly inexpensive.  We paid for VIP tickets in hopes of snagging a balcony seat (there are only a few stools against the rail) but were unsuccessful.  You really have to show up 1+ hour before doors open to even hope to get one for popular shows.  Even then, they line everyone up in the same line (VIP and non) even though the balcony entrance is in TopGolf itself.  Thankfully they seem to limit the amount of VIP/balcony tickets sold, so if you're willing to stand there's plenty of room and good vantage points.  Otherwise, once the balcony chairs fill up you can not see the stage from the remaining booth seating.  There is a private bar but it's limited, so for more selection you'll end up going downstairs anyway.  You'll also end up using the bathroom downstairs because the ones upstairs in TopGolf are surprisingly small.  There were menus on the tables but it was unclear how and from whom you were supposed to order.  All this may make the VIP upcharge not worth it for some people.  As others have mentioned, parking is a zoo between this, TopGolf and (the night we were there) any nearby Titans game.  If you're staying downtown, take Uber or Lyft - the Cowan's own website suggests this!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great atmosphere, great singers and great waitresses! Tons of energy there! We will definitely come back!

name: The Station Inn
text: Great low key "hole in the wall" place. Definitely more locals than tourists and such a relaxed feel to the place. Not a place for food, but fun and unique atmosphere.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place has a great roof top bar area with live music, there is also a downstairs. It gets crazy packed inside but service was fast and friendly upstairs, downstairs seemed a lot busier and hard to get the bartenders attention. We had a great time listening to live music after the Titans game on a 75 degree Sunday in December on the roof!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: One of my worst experiences in Downtown Nashville. Over crowded. Slow bar service. Very very dirty. On the top floor there were only single restrooms and I stood in line for 20 minutes to use it. Once I got in there it was covered in urine and feces. I couldn't even wash my hands because of all the trash and beer bottles in the sink. To top it all off they were out of my favorite beer, Blue Moon. The only good thing is you can step out on the balcony to breathe fresh air instead of the horrible odors through out the building.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
New Years Eve at the Nashville Underground was nothing short of a disaster and total disappointment! 

Upon arrival we were greeted with a closed door! Security guard on inside secured the door so we could not open it to get in and sit at our $1055.00 table we paid for! It was 11 degrees outside and a huge line of customers that paid to get in were made to sit and freeze. All the while Joey DeGraw (one of the partners) sat just inside the door, laughing at the irrate patrons. I guess no one told him how business works...treat the the customer with respect because they pay your bills! 

We were told prior to our arrival that there would be two lines...one for VIP and one for General tickets...that didn't happen. Though they said we could not enter because of capacity issues (which all seats were presold and accounted for before NYE so I am not sure how they over shot capacity) once inside it was surprisingly light on people! We arrived to our seat just moments before midnight and were given a single drink even though we prepaid for two plus a champagne toast (which we never received) and a charcuterie board we prepaid for but never got! To top it all off the fire alarm went off the entire night. We had our fill of being mistreated and made our way to FGL House where we we treated amazingly! Nashville Underground is not destin for longevity at this rate...we won't be back unless we get a refund and apology!

name: Famous Nashville
text: Good music! Service is good and waiter was funny.... food was pretty good 4stars but overall a 5

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This was our favorite bar on our trip to Nashville! I wish I could remember the name of the guy who was performing on the first floor last night because he was amazing! This place had the best atmosphere and fast service for being crowded. We absolutely loved it.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Tried to give homeless teenager money from inside and was asked to leave. Business stated they did not care about homeless teenager begging for money in the street. I was escorted out like a criminal by their wannabe security personnel.... very unfortunate because this young man made several dollars and was very happy with my donation! Shame in you honkey tonk!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
Go when Isaac Matthews is playing!

The service here is great and the people are really nice. They have some pretty quirky signs up which made the experience even more fun. We didn't order anything crazy but there was always someone ready to take our order and answer our annoyingly stupid questions like do you have bottled beer. (They do. There's a row of them above the bar so you can easily make your selection.)

I would highly recommend this place for locals or tourists.

name: Famous Nashville
text: My family and I were in town for vacation and we ended up here on the rooftop. It was a blast. They had a DJ cranking out the tunes and people drinking and having a great time. It's nice to go somewhere and actually have a DJ and not live music.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Very lively and chill. It has two floors. The first floor is always full of people but if you need some space there is always the second floor. There is live band music on both floors but if you need some quality time with your family, friends or significant other go to the second floor.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Ok have to rate on the food. It's not bad for a bar. I had chicken sandwich with tater tots. Course the band and love music is the best.

name: Nashville Underground
text: We attended CMA Fest last weekend and before going, we heard all about Nashville Underground - how it was such great food, music and a friendly atmosphere. We decided to check it out ASAP and are SO glad we did; we LOVED it! The food was amazing, the music enjoyable and the service awesome! We even sat on the patio and with how hot it was, the waitress was on top of our water, other needs and continued fun conversation too. Nashville Underground was definitely a highlight of our trip and we'll for sure be back!

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Tarps are back up on the fences.
They don't want the locals watching from the street.
Will find a roof to enjoy the concerts from because I'm not paying their exorbitant prices for outdoor seating.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Great evening last night with Long Players and special guests to re-enact Fleetwood Mac.

One of the best shows ever!

Food was also very good as was the service.

Love it.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: With so many great bars on Broadway, there's no reason to go here. The "cocktails" were way overpriced for what you get, which is a subpar mixed drink (vodka and lemonade for $9) in a dinky little plastic cup (think what you would find to use for water in a waiting room). Food is even worse. I got the pulled pork sandwich, the pork was dry and lacking flavor, and the chipotle BBQ sauce looked like something one would find in a baby's diaper. My friend got the chicken tenders and they were cold inside. To seal the deal on this place being a terrible experience, the waitress shorted me on change. Save yourself the poor experience here and go down the block to Tequila Cowboy, they have significantly better food and drinks and better prices (my drink there was twice the size, much better quality, and cost me less.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Fun times, as long as you're drinking and not uptight. It's very crowded on the wknds and you have to be ok with drinks, crowds, and loud, obnoxious people! Always good music, but take your own flask, as alcohol in downtown Nashville is incredibly expensive!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Great spot for drinks and live music. Great band called Lower Broadway band performing.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I went here while I was on vacation in Nashville. I loved this place! The band that was playing was awesome. Great view of Downtown Nashville. I can't say much for the drinks since I don't drink... BUT if you don't drink, I highly recommend the Sweet Tea. It was honestly some of the best I ever had. Definitely a fun time here!

name: Alley Taps
text: Great selection of beer, great happy hour (11-5 on a Sunday?!), and an awesome vibe. Low lights, and the best smelling bar I've ever been to. No joke, it's not just that it doesn't smell BAD, it actually smells GOOD. It feels like a modern speakeasy! Hailing from Seattle, we'll definitely be back!

name: Alley Taps
text: The BEST small bar off of Broadway. Live music every night. We really enjoyed TheNashMash615 on Sunday night. Multiple artists and great music. It is a full bar with a great bourbon selection.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: You will likely have joiners at your table. I went with my dad and the couple at our table kept referring to me us as husband and wife no matter how many times they were corrected ( YUCK and so awkward) they turned out to be swingers and followed us after we moved seats. The show was cool. Worst nachos and tater skins I've ever had.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Not a bad bar to hang out in. The staff on the other hand are not nice at all. The impression is they are not happy workers. Ordered a few drinks without a smile and attitude. Well to say the least there. Are many more places that will actually appreciate our being here and business. Advice move on there are other places to have a good time. This place seriously needs a bar rescue episode.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Every floor has something amazing. And then you get the the roof and the views are amazing. Great friendly staff, clean bathrooms, mechanical bull, dance floor, fireplace. Anything you want, they have it.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
This was a quick lunch spot for us while we were out and about in Nashville on a short weekend trip. There wasn't many options for parking as there were only about 10 spots infront. There was a lot next door that charged a $10 fee. I do think parking can probably be tricky at most places in downtown Nashville so this wasn't surprising.

There was a huge stage inside for live music. We got to see a few really good acts. It is loud so I wouldn't suggest this place if you are wanting to go out somewhere and chat with people. It's more for watching/listening the musical acts.

We came with my husband, parents and 3 kids. They didn't have a highchair which kind of stunk so our little one at to eat on our lap. They also didn't have a kids menu. Kids are allowed but I wouldn't consider this a kid friendly place.

The server was friendly and helped us find something on the menu that the kids would like. The food was pretty typical American food. Not bad but not outstanding or anything. Typical bar food. I think I would have enjoyed this place more if I had a few hours to kill (without my kids) and drink a few beers while enjoying some good local Nashville music.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I requested the melodic excellence of Oasis from the band on the third floor.  They said they would play the song, TOOK MY HARD EARNED MONEY to play the song then told everyone at the bar I was lame for requesting Oasis because it was clear I was out of town.  That's correct, I am from out of town and the four scum stole my money and faith in music.

Everyone know Oasis is great except for the bigots on stage who decided to play racially fueled hate music.

If you are from out of town, don't go here because it is clear they just want to steal your money and screw you over.

name: Nashville Underground
text: De used to eat dinner here ...regrettably...the chicken tasted like it had been fried in a vat of old oil with fish.  Service was horrible.  The fact nonone was eating in there should have been the sign

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This place was packed when I visited on a Monday evening.  And I can see why.  The music here on all levels (literally, on all levels) was fantastic.  The food here (I tried the wings) was really delicious.  The drinks were good, and the service was wonderful. 

Back to the music, which may be why you visit -- the band that was performing here did rock, pop, and country hits, and they were fantastic.  They did versions and covers of Fleetwood Mac, Billy Joel, and Pat Benatar, among others, and really hit it out of the park.  There is plenty of room here, so the capacity here is huge.  A great find during a visit to Nashville.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This was our first stop on Broadway... and dang it was fun! Three stories of live music, food, and drinks. We enjoyed listening to a band out of KY who performed a little country and southern rock n roll! Definitely up our alley! For apps my husband and I shared SW chicken egg rolls and wings. The rolls were superb and the wings were Nashville hot! Definitely loved this joint!

name: Alley Taps
text:
A hidden gem in the heart of downtown Nashville's historic Printers Alley. A Steelers' bar (original owner is from Pittsburgh) and they have Guinness on tap!
The wings are mouth watering and the hot dogs on toasted Hawaiian bread will knock your socks off.
Great ambiance, friendly bartenders and dozens of craft beers!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: Everything you'd expect and more! Attended the time jumpers show on Monday. The show started at 8, but crowd shows up hours early to hold down tables for the evening. If you want a table with service, you probably have to arrive like 90+ minutes before the show. We sat at the bar and had a great time and great service. Music was fun and like an educational lesson. Onion rings were good. Didn't try other food. Prices for drinks are right. Enjoyed this Nashville treasure!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
As absolutely ridiculous as it is to admit, I didn't know where 3rd & Lindsley was.* Yes. I know. But I knew that it was a staple in the Nashville live music scene and that I needed to check it out. What better timing, then, was it to have a friend come in from out of town who wanted to see a live show? Perfect. Done.

The first thing that you'll notice about 3rd & Lindsley is that there's breathing room. I get the 'intimate' nature of a lot of live music venues is what draws crowds. I don't like smelling strangers. Having some room to manspread is a-okay with me. You can choose from tables downstairs to stools upstairs (and at the bar). That said, 3rd & Lindsley isn't so cavernous that you'll feel lost or have a hard time hearing/seeing what's going on onstage. After paying a $10 cover, we walked in, grabbed a table and sat down to enjoy some good tunes. The atmosphere was extremely laid back. I don't know that the band had a huge following, but it seemed that everyone in the venue was having a good time (and a few ladies were having a *very* good time). Besides that, their talent was undeniable. There are *so* many good musicians in this town. It's unbelievable.

Since the place wasn't overrun with people, we decided to hit the bar rather than wait for table service. On the Thursday night we were here, there was only one waitress and she looked to be in the weeds. Since I paid cover, my friend got the drinks. I don't know whether there's a cocktail menu from which to choose but this doesn't seem to be a cocktail kinda place. He got a beer and I got a Jack and Coke. The pour wasn't exceptionally strong or large but I don't know how much he paid for it. We had just come from dinner so we didn't look at the food options although I don't know that I'd ever, willingly, eat at a music venue.

I'd come back. The website calendar is very easy to navigate, the cover price was fair, the staff were nice, and the vibe was very laid back. Oh, and the sound quality was fantastic. Professionals play and work here, without a doubt. Given its location, I don't know how much random foot/tourist traffic it gets but given the quality of performer the venue is able to book and the ease with which a patron can see/hear what's happening onstage, I'm not at all surprised with the popularity of the venue from music lovers in the know. 

*To my credit, my grizzled rideshare driver blanked as well and we both felt very dumb when we realized where it was.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: I will never return as the prices for concessions were robbery .  9,00 for a bottle of water !  Cop - homeless - searching belongings - metal detectors .  And the performer asked for the audience to come closer and the gestapo would not allow.  How embarrassing for Lucinda Williams !  Nope never again !

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Honky Tonk Central is one of the best bars in Nashville. This is a MUST visit for Nashville nightlife. The live music, DJ's, and drink specials are great. You can't go here and not have a great time. I came here on a conference for work and went to this venue as part of the bar crawl. It was definitely a great time and totally worth visiting. The name speaks for itself when you think of Nashville and Country music. Go and have a great time!

name: The Back Corner
text: What an epic venue tucked away and exclusive to budding artists in Nashville! Loved seeing Charlotte Sands perform live and can't wait to visit this again!

name: Nashville Underground
text: I went to Hattie Bs and the wait was 2 hrs, so my group decided to walk around broadway we found this place! Not only was the live music amazing but the hot chicken was fantastic!! The waitress was so good I enjoyed myself!!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: On the corner of forth avenue and Broadway, can't miss it! They have a live band every night which is great entertainment and there is no cover at any of the bars (something I'm not used to as a Chicagoan). I LOVED the yee haw drink (very sweet, has a hint of coconut and pineapple). If you're 21+, I'd recommend going here! Pretty pricey but definitely worth the experience.

name: Nashville Underground
text: BRING CASH HERE!!!!   So, I am really confused.   I came there, and the staff was amazing.  So nice.  But when I went to pay my tab, they asked me whether I wanted to use a card or cash.  Apparently there is a huge difference.  Why?   I know there are credit card fees.  But why is my tab 20 percent higher if I use a card?!?   Is this place actually paying their taxes???? Or, is this just a way to make more money?   As a local, I want everyone to pay their share of taxes.  Because I do......

name: The Station Inn
text:
Indeed one of the hottest place on the planet for going to see bluegrass and acoustic/folk music. Sure the sign says "World Famous Station Inn" and guess what? It really *is* world famous to musicians and acoustic music lovers. Bluegrass fans travel from all over the world to catch a show here.

Caveat: the neighborhood that has sprung up around The Station Inn is nothing like the bar itself. The Station Inn is old, dilapidated, run-down, usually over-crowded. It's endearing. What's sprung up around it is hipsterville, young, urban, trendy, outrageously expensive. High rises being built within a stone's throw. The two are at odds. 

If you like a great dive bar with world class music, you'll find it here. If not, the rest of the neighborhood will suit you just fine. Beer is the main order here. Rest of the neighborhood? No trouble finding a menu with dozens of martini options. 

Privately I have to wonder how much longer the owners can hold out. 20-30 years ago you were risking it parking here. Now? Main danger now is no parking due the crowd of Lexas, Hondas, Mercedes and Beamers. What used to be a colorful and eerie part of town is now more. The land the bar sits on is worth a gold mine.

But what the hell. Come here for the music and be glad you visited. I did for the first time in about 20 years and really enjoyed my stay. I hope to return once again in the future. If you're in it for the music, it's happening here on a regular basis. If you're looking for just a place to have a cocktail, might be best to move on. This is my kind of old-time music joint and it's just fine.

name: Music City Male Revue
text: This show was more funny than what I was expecting. First off the show was suppose to be at 5pm and they sent an email saying it had to be moved to 4pm the week of. Who sees a male show that early? Went for my bachelorette party and the host completely ignored my group the entire time! He asked who came out the farthest and we said San Francisco and some other group said Florida and he goes Florida is definitely the farthest! Does this guy need a geography lesson? I am hurt and upset he ignored our group the entire time because this was something I was looking forward to the most and it was the most disappointing. You can tell the guys are very new and nervous. The only good one is the black guy who really made the show! The rest half assed it and when they were dancing to Backstreet Boys all completely off beat and not in sync! There was no grand finale and I was left feeling disappointed and unwanted at the show when this was suppose to be my special day and I felt the opposite. This place has a lot of potential but they need a new host, the guys need way more practice and they need to work on their choreography. Guess I am just used to Vegas shows! Guys are good looking though.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Ascend amphitheater has an amazing view of the city and is particularly great during the sunset. However, the staff there over reactive to everything. I think I've seen people kicked out for just about every reason possible. Don't smoke unless you're in the smoking section. They will confiscate your e cig vapes or you can leave the premises. Their beers cost $16 and the cheapest one was $13. The food is outrageously expensive. I haven't even begun to talk about the sound issues. This is a town of audio engineers. The sound should be amazing! Unfortunately, the music is played way too loud and there is lots of audio distortion, with clicks and pops happening frequently throughout Dwight Yokum's set. The vocal wasn't loud enough during Lucinda Williams set either. Overall, I wasn't very impressed with this last concert. I've never liked their customer service. It's a pretty setup though if they fix some things.

name: Nashville Underground
text: I mean if I could give this place zero stars, I would. I get it you're a new bar but why in the FUCK would you sell that many tickets for $50  ON NEW YEARS EVE when you can't allow that many people in your bar? Use your head... you let over 100 people wait outside in 13 degree weather AND not to mention me and my friends didn't even get in so I will be getting my money back because YOU don't know how to plan New Year's Eve in downtown Nashville... that's very embarrassing.  I hope in the meantime (before your bar gets shut down) that you all as a staff will be able to use a little more common sense and treat your guests like guests. Don't tell me I'm gunna get food and a champagne toast when I didn't even get in

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We came here for a bachelorette party and had a great time up on the third floor. One of the girls in our group has multiple sclerosis and has a really difficult time walking downstairs because she feels unsteady. When we were ready to leave, she walked to the elevator and asked if she could ride down because she didn't feel safe walking down the stairs. The employee at the elevator was rude enough  to look her up and down and say "You don't look disabled to me". When she tried to explain her situation, his unwillingness to help and aggression in response were appalling. We were absolutely outraged at his behavior! We're not sure what she would have needed to do to "appear more disabled", but perhaps the employees at this establishment could benefit from some training on the American Disability Act.

name: 360 Burger
text: Best beer & burger spot in Antioch

name: 360 Burger
text: Food is delicious, but the service was a bit lacking. Waited for 20 minutes for a drink refill while our server was standing at the corner of the bar talking with other staff. I had to actually ask him to come and refill our drinks. Hoping it was just an off day, because I plan to come back.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Okay, as a very huge Johnny cash fan, I FREAKED when I saw this on a trip over the summer. I immediately dropped by. I walked in to a rather small giftshop and looked around a bit. They have everything. Huge collection of shirts, CDS, books and even signed memorabilia and baby onesies you can buy. 

I walked up and purchased my ticket which was fairly priced and went inside. This collection of his memorabilia is UNBELIEVABLE! Not only do they have all his gold and platinum records, stage outfits, wedding outfit, personal fan club items, etc. but they also have a lot of June Carter's stuff as well. They even had a little heart shaped box of chocolate John wrote a love note on in sharpie on display. 

The coolest little place I've been to in Nashville. I recommended for anyone who likes Johnny.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Great show! We had a fantastic time at the Listening Room Cafe.  The online reservation process was easy. The website is very well done and all the information you would need or want is there. There is complimentary valet parking which is a plus!
We took our 10, 14, and 17 year old with us and they all said it was a fun experience. There's no smoking and for the most part it is family friendly. The show is very good and worth going alone! 
The food is just okay and nothing to write home about but we didn't eat anything we absolutely did not like. 
Our waiter was just okay and wasn't super attentive to us. I could tell he was very attentive to the tables around us that ordered alcohol (we only ordered water and some sodas). Even so, we loved the show and would go again when in Nashville!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: This is a great venue to hear great live music from the songwriters themselves. It's a quiet place so you can hear the acoustics perfectly that is different from the live bands you hear on Broadway. It is about a mile walk from Broadway or you can take a quick drive or uber/Lyft ride there. The food isn't bad either. I had the Alfredo pasta and it was great. Also has good ribeyes. A must stop to hear premium good music.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Good environment with a great band playing the day we went. Less crowded than some of the other restaurants on Broadway. As far as gluten free, not a huge selection but managed to get a burger with no bun.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great lineup of songwriters and singers when we went. The food is okay, perhaps some of the dishes overpriced, but the drinks are solid. It's worth it because they don't charge a cover for the music. I was surprised to hear some recent hits as sung by the people who wrote them for artists like Tim McGraw, Blake Shelton, Chris Young.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: They don't monitor how many people they let in. The first section you couldn't move, it was hard to maneuver through out the museum.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
This museum was fantastic! I don't know why Lonely Planet makes it sound so poor. Prices were relatively high (15$) but it was worth it. 
It is a very modern, interactive museum with an amazing array of personal items, e.g. letters, clothes, furniture and instruments. 
It's a good mix of his personal life and his career as a musician and also as an actor. 
Johnny Cash fans will probably need at least two hours.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
"It took 5 phone calls, 2 emails, and 25 days to receive a $20 check (not even the entire amount I was overcharged).
I paid $25 to park, $22 to get in the door, and $50 for a sandwich and 2 beers to be afforded this experience.

Like I said, the music was good and the place was cool, 
but Nashville is eaten up with cool music places."

The place is cool. The music was great. The food was bad.
The service was horrendous, and then a few days later I saw where I had been overcharged for more than $20.

And, when I say horrendous, I mean nearly 30 minutes before we saw a server (the place was not busy). We saw her when the food came, but never saw her again. We had to flag down someone else to ask for another beer and water, though the water never came. Then, we waited a good bit at the end of the evening trying to catch a glimpse of her to get a check, eventually just going to the front of the place and asking for it. 

Then, of course, charged $50 on a $24 bill.

I talked to a manager by phone who sounded pretty aggravated to field the call. Their calls roll to their personal phones. Service industry don't live in the office...
It wasn't the attitude you would expect on calling to report an overcharge, and there was even a tone at one point like I might be making this shit up or something.

I didn't hear back from him for 5 days, at which point I contacted the owner. 
He was sympathetic and accommodating at first, 
and agreed to refund the entirety of my bill. 

I waited for 2 weeks, but the check never came. 
I contacted him again and he was less than caring.
A reply email that he meant to mail it 2 weeks ago; but had an emergency; but actually did just run across it yesterday and it was on its way.

The check did arrive after another request, but not only was it not for the entire bill, it was not even for the entire amount of the overcharge. 

He did include 2 tickets to get in the door; like I would want to experience this again.

Both of these guys double-talked so much they couldn't keep it all straight, not for some schmuck like me. It was palpable when you talked to them and evident in their actions.

It took 5 phone calls, 2 emails, and 25 days to receive a $20 check (not even the entire amount I was overcharged).
I paid $25 to park, $22 to get in the door, and $50 for a sandwich and 2 beers to be afforded this experience.

Like I said, the music was good and the place was cool, 
but Nashville is eaten up with cool music places.

Spend your money somewhere else.
This place does not care about its patrons; plenty of tourists in Nashville.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: LOVED this museum! I thought it was a little pricey for being so small but still worth it! Loved all the artifacts and readings on them. Really loved the station where I could hear one of Cash's songs in different types of taping- amazing how the sound is so different. Loved the staff there! They would chime in and add to things to what you were reading or saying. One even started dancing with me haha!

name: 360 Burger
text: I love the burgers and fries! I went here on a date and was thrilled by the quality of the food and the prices. I've went to several gourmet burger places that charged way more for mediocre service and food. So, I was pleasantly surprised by this place. There was a very laid back atmosphere, music, and great food. I hope to go there again, soon.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
This was an awesome experience. I would recommend getting there a little early to get a good place in line if you have tickets already. We got seated at a high table along the side of the room. I'm on the shorter side so I was excited that I would be able to see the stage well.

I did not eat so I can't speak for the food. The menu looked like your typical Nashville items, fried everything. I read other reviews that said to eat beforehand so that's what we did. As for the drinks, I had a thyme warp. Similar to a Moscow Mule but with a thyme flavor added in. It was good and large!

The entertainment was AMAZING. Songwriters playing some of their best. I recognized every song and it was so cool to hear them sung by the people who actually wrote them as opposed to the ones who recorded them. They gave back stories and a little information about where they're from. 

This place is a MUST SEE in Nashville. Order tickets beforehand.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
I have been here a few times - mostly during Songwriter's Festival.
I have always had a good seat, whether it was on the couch, a big overstuffed chair, or a barstool.
Music always sounds great.
I have never felt like the place was so crowded I couldn't enjoy the performers.
In fact, every time I have been here, I have always gotten a great seat and no one standing in front of me, to block any views.

I really like this place.
Food isn't bad, either.
Good beer.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
Two stars because the boat didn't sink. Service was poor to spotty. Dinner was acceptable. Trying to get a cup of coffee was sort of an ordeal. The dessert was served only to the people seated who did not go outside to see the bottom of broadway. They never came back to serve the dessert. We asked 3 times before we got one for my wife. 
I suppose I would recommend not doing the dinner for $90.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I got a Groupon for this but that was a while ago so I can't say if it's there or not anymore. That made for a great outing for me and my husband already! We really enjoyed the exhibits. I feel like the first part of the exhibit from the early part of Johnny Cash's career was a bit narrow (meaning it was hard to move around...the exhibit itself was great) considering a lot of patrons wanted to stand there and read absolutely everything displayed there. After that initial part all else was good. My husband is a musician and enjoyed seeing the many guitars on display. To get trough the entire museum takes at least a couple hours of you take the time and enjoy it, so it's definitely worth it even if you don't have the Groupon. 
The gift shop was nice enough. High prices as one would expect but if you're a fan it's worth a look around.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Great bartender Dennis! Delicious fried pickles and chicken tenders. Great chill vibe.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Kenny the bartender was great.  The piano players were also amazing!! However your waiter was not so great. It's wasn't even busy when we went in. It was a Thursday night. Not friendly at all. Not on top of getting your drinks. I walked up many times to the bartender just to get another drink. When the waiter did come over he expected a tip. You had maybe 20 people in the bar dude. Wouldn't want to see you on a busy night.

name: 360 Burger
text: We stopped in Nashville overnight and, after driving all day, were looking for something good for dinner. 360 Burger came up first on Yelp and a burger and a beer are always a good idea so we went there. It was a great choice! I had the Sliders and a beer and my husband had the Pretzel Bun Barbeque Bacon Burger. They were both delish! The server was friendly and attentive. He told us that the meat for the burgers is locally grown, very fresh. Awesome! As we were getting ready to leave, a live band was setting up to play. If we come through Nashville again, we will definitely stop here again. The only bad thing I can mention is that someone was smoking right outside the door and when people came into the restaurant, big clouds of smoke would come with them. But the food was terrific, the service was great and , except for the smoke, we really enjoyed our visit.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Excellent layout!! Great museum and was easy to get lost in a world of music. Cool gift shop, didn't have the coffee but it smelled amazing.

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text:
Blue Bar has the makings of a very bad choose-your-own-adventure experience. For a $10 cover charge on New Year's Eve, you had two options: turn left (I suppose this is the Rack Room side) and you can sit in a brightly lit white room that has the feel of an old basement and pay $1 per song if you want to hear any music. Had I had the opportunity and the jukebox had the song, I would have torturned the crowd with back-to-back playings of "What's New, Pussycat" or some Spice Girls song.

Turn right, and you go down a long hallway to what appears to be the Blue Bar side of the house. No offense to schizophrenics, but I'm afraid the DJ that night was suffering from a bad case of music-schizophrenia. Just as people were getting into the groove, he'd change the tune and tempo and it just killed any mood. Perhaps it's just me, but guys dancing in suits is just weird. There was plenty of that. 

As if those issues weren't enough, asking $7.50 for a Jack and coke is ridiculous...and a poorly made Jack and coke at that. I mean, it's ONLY two ingredients. I'd rather pay the extra $4.50 at Patterson House down the street for an infintiely better cocktail, but that would be comparing apples to crap. 

During past visits to this place, the music was just OK and the staff was just OK, but after a hiatus from this place for a few years, I'm reminded why I should never return.

name: 360 Burger
text:
This is a great local restaurant. They have a wide variety of hamburgers and other food. Everything is very fresh, hot, and the service is great. The quality of the food can't be beat. They make a mean burger.

Another thing I like is that we have 3 small children and they do not complain about splitting plates.

My biggest complaint is they stopped serving their baked beans. 

Keep in mind that everything is prepared to order, so you have to wait a bit, but it is a wait that is well worth the freshly prepared food you get in return.

Finally let me say if you want Antioch to rebuild, it will take businesses like this. That depends on you supporting them, and this is one worthy of support.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: This used to be a favorite spot to take people who come to visit.  Highly disappointed that they chose to only sell bottled water during CMA Fest.  Every other bar gave out free water or had stations set up.  The music was also not as good as normal for this place, we didn't stay long.

name: 360 Burger
text: Incredibly tasty!!! I dined here for the first time tonight. I had the opportunity to enjoy the turkey burger with habanero cheese and fries. I found it flavorful and juicy. To top it off the bar had Angry Orchard apple cider, which made my meal even better. The bartender was attentive and pleasant and overall I would count this as a positive dining adventure.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Talk about a shitty place. I only say shitty, because there's literally one bathroom on the ground floor during peak times and there's nowhere to go, and trying to get a drink at a bar is impossible.

 We hear there are more bathrooms upstairs, but then we have to wait in line and when we didn't realize this, the bouncers were complete assholes. I actually heard them call a bachelorette party a "bunch of cunts". 

This place is worse than the music that Dierks Bentley makes. In some respects, it's the same exact bar as every other downtown Nashville bar (crazytown, honkytonk central, etc), but the staff at other places seems much more professional. For contrast, Nashville Underground also recently opened, and the staff there is extremely pleasant. Of the country named bars downtown, like FGL house, AJ's Good Time Bar, and the George Jones Museum, Dierks' bar is the worst. Hopefully it loses money and shuts down soon.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I loved the Johnny Cash Museum! I know the tickets are a little steep at $19pp, but I wanted to pass along that I found a Groupon for $20 for 2 people or $38 for 4 people - and I had an extra ticket after our party of three, so I was able to give it to someone else in line.  The museum took about 1-1.5h to get through, and I'd recommend it for adults, but may not be interactive enough for kids depending on the age.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Excellent time Well worth the trip to 4th and Broadway

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text:
So, I found myself at this bar on a Sunday night.  I can't comment on the food, I didn't eat anything.  I CAN comment on the experience.

First, they had a live band that took requests from the audience periodically, and played a good mix of new and classic country.  The band also had a few people from the audience play, with the highlight being Keith Whitley's son playing some of his dad's tracks.

The drinks were fair priced for Opryland, and the bar was 100% the local spot for drinking.  As an FYI - you can smoke in here, so, yeah, it's not for bringing your children.  

We had Hope and John Boy as our tenders for the night.  Both were attentive and regularly checking on everyone there.  This is exactly what I was looking for: local bar close to the hotel that was a no-frills watering hole.  

Last thing: If you are staying at the Gaylord and are looking for upscale/fancy dining, don't come here and bitch.  This bar is for people who aren't paying 27 bucks a day to valet their Escalade.

Hope you enjoy it as much as we did!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Who are we kidding here,.....? I'd visit the place Johnny Cash washed his clothes at! It's music history son,..... enjoy!

name: 360 Burger
text:
I really wanted to enjoy my lunch at 360 Burger. I was thrilled that there was some life being pumped back into Hickory Hollow, and after recently learning that some of the chefs studied at Johnson & Wales (my alma mater), I was pumped. The sad truth is that my lunch was a letdown.

I ordered the 360 burger with gouda on the pretzel roll, medium rare. I received a well-done burger on a giant, tough pretzel roll, which muted the flavors of the burger and toppings within. After I removed the top bun and was able to taste the meat, it was noticeably "off" - tasting gamey and I daresay, perhaps old? Apart from that, the meat was unseasoned and boring. 

I will say, they got the sweet potato fries right - they were cut like shoestring fries, well cooked and well seasoned, and served with a great spicy aioli. 

Will I come back? Maybe for fries and a beer, but I'm not at all impressed with the burger.

name: 360 Burger
text:
Found them on Yelp. New to the area. First time walking in. The place looks great, very clean looking. Menu was nice and variety. Easy to read and not overwhelming. Was greeted first as we walked in. Drinks ordered first thing when we sat. 
Food was very presentable and a lot to eat. I ordered Cilantro Guacamole burger. Amazing. The cilantro was in the burger meat blended and had flavored. Cooked right and fries were great.
Our server was cute and she kept watch and filled drinks just as any server should do. I could have the worse meal and if she tops off my drink and stops to checkup a few times, I'm happy. She did just that, think her name was Katie.
Overall great experience for first time. Will be back.
