I ordered the spicy chicken biscuit sandwich which was just the right amount of spice. You have to try the fried pickles because they are amazing! My son got the bucket of chicken and he said it was really good. It's a lot of chicken so a bucket for the whole table is enough. This place is clean and a great time!!

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I have had the opportunity and/or privilege to see a number of acts play at the Bridgestone Arena over the past Twenty-two  years. Last night was no exception when we saw the Backstreet Boys perform here.

I have to say that I was very impressed with their show. Even 26 years later, these guys still sound great and put on a heck of a show.

The overall experience was very nice. We had great seats, listened to some great music, and a good time all around

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
***Reviewing this place as a venue***

I came here for a CD release party for a friend of a friend. They had rented out the whole bar as a music venue. The way this bar is set up is pretty cool. There is a stage towards the front of the bar, and then the taps are in the back. It is large enough that everyone was able to move around comfortably.

My favorite part of the bar was upstairs. There are bar games and a wall of windows that overlook the breweries. There is a smaller bar upstairs for you to get your beer fix. 

TBW offers a great variety of beers with many options for your preferences. I think this is a great venue for a party to rent out for a social or a fundraiser. The staff was attentive and great, and it was overall a wonderful experience!

name: Ole Red
text: Came here with our kids for lunch. Kid friendly place during the day. Great atmosphere and amazing food. We asked our server for food suggestions, as former servers we knew they would have the beat info. We chose from her suggestions and were happy we did. Tater tot poutine is a must. Champagne of chicken-half portion was enough for 2 and we actually would have had left overs if we were local and going home to a fridge.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Had the clam and corn chowder, sat by the window people watching while the live music played along. Loved this place. It was less hole in the wall and more standardized restaurant compared to other stops along that street. Loved the music, excellent waiter who helped guide us as to what places ee should be seeing during our stay in nashville. Go to place if u need good food and a second to relax from the noise.

name: Ole Red
text:
We bought $100 p/p tickets to Ole Red's 4th of July rooftop bar and unfortunately the only highlight of this night was the fireworks that were offered for free by Nashville. 6 of us were down in Nashville for the weekend, and decided to get tickets to the 4th of July rooftop bar offer from Ole Red. What a mistake!!! We paid $600 to watch fireworks!  

There was limited seating, they offered passing hor d'oeuvres which was just that passing. There was one hostess "running" around with a tray on occasion.

We were entitled to one drink with that pricetag, and the drink was limited to a cocktail list chosen by Ole Red, which by 7:30 pm was only down to a selection of 2 drinks, which neither was worth drinking. If you paid for drinks, they were outrageously priced and not that good. 

Nothing worth going back to this bar for!

name: Ole Red
text: The service is slow and inattentive on the roof. Waited 15 minutes than had to chase down server to order a drink. Than waited another 20 for the drink to show up without the other drink and water  we ordered. Server acted like she was doing me a favor. Avoid plenty of other options. Nothing special about this location.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: A definite honky tonk bar!  Loved it!!  And there are thousands of license plates from all over hanging from the ceiling.  A lot to look at while you sipping down your drinks or listening to the bands playing.  Friendly people working there, and customers.  Was glad I stopped into this place for a quick drink.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: love my rock &roll but i have to say this is a bad place to hold a rock show everybody is on there butt country town what else can i say back to indy a rockin crowd ..just have to say walking down town and stopping in all the great and famous bars was awesome.i will be back only to have a good time but i will never waste my money at this place again...

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I don't know what some of you people are talking about this place is AMAZING!!  Great environment to grab a delicious craft beer or stuff your face with one of their tasty pizzas!  I highly recommend the Wild Bill or the Bob Marley.  Also as one of the biggest Widespread Panic fans ever...I loved when I walked in and saw the big painting of JB right by my table, even got to hear "Ain't life grand" while I was enjoying a Fat Bottom Black Betty and a cup of y'alls cream of crawfish soup (YUM!).  Will definitely be back to try more things on the menu, and as a Midtown regular for years, WELCOME TO THE NEIGHBORHOOD!!

name: Twin Kegs
text: Just came in to try their cheeseburger & fries because I'd heard good things and live nearby. Nothing fancy, or creative, no eggs on top or anything, just a good burger. This is a smoky bar, so if you don't smoke you might want to get it to-go as I did. But the best thing I've had here is the chicken wings. Not buffalo, just barbecued wings that are quite tasty.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I ate there on a Sunday afternoon for dinner during the CMA fest. I sat at the bar and had the pulled pork plate with beans and slaw--- all delicious, the portion was large, and served quickly!  Wait staff behind the bar was super friendly, attentive, and a Wisconsin fan!  Food on the menu was reasonably priced and bottled beer was $6 like other places downtown. I did not order a mixed drink, but if I did I would probably ask the price before ordering!!  Live country music from a 5 piece band was good, although loud.  If in town again I will certainly check out Rippy's for BBQ!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
My 8 best girlfriends & I were in Nashville this past weekend & we stopped here 2 of the 3 nights because we had so much fun. The cover band was PHENOMENAL & the atmosphere was a blast, we would absolutely recommend it.

The only reason we couldn't give 5 stars is because of the absolute piece of trash bouncer that was so very rude at closing time. We were aware we got there near closing time Saturday night so we decided not to get a drink but just listen to the band. Before the band even finished standing up to be done for the night the bouncer started screaming & cursing at every person at the bar. He was physically pushing people out & even picked up some boy who turned around to try to find his friends, knocking into people. It was EXTREMELY unnecessary & unfortunately left us very upset. 

Yes, we know bouncers have tough jobs. We have stayed at many bars til closing time, some of us work at bars but we have never seen such an overreaction to a closing 15 minutes before 3 am. We say definitely enjoy your stay at Rippy's but LEAVE an hour before they close.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Slooooowwwww. Decent food but not outstanding. Wonderful music. Ribs were the best yet not fall off the bone.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: We were here last night for dinner and it was Status quo for southern bbq.  Wasn't overly impressed, but it was still good.  My husband had the half rack of ribs, and I had the smoked pulled pork.  My husband said the pulled pork was the best he's ever had, but I didn't agree.  He said his ribs were standard, nothing special.  Fall off the bone though!  Coleslaw and baked beans tasted identical to KFC's.  Lol.  French fries were nothing special.  Chili was decent!  Major downfall is that I don't think they make their own bbq sauce which I would expect in Nashville.  We saw a huge bottle of KFC Masterpiece bbq sauce on the server stand.  We were bummed.  Food was served on paper lined baskets which is cool, but once the paper gets soggy from the meat, it starts to shred into the meat.  Yuck!  I'd recommend using a different kind of paper!!  Service was pretty bad.  Server was busy and the place was packed so we were very forgiving.  Amazing atmosphere though and the entertainment....ONE OF A KIND!!  Only in Nashville!!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Quite the hidden gem. Best to come around 7:00pm when its live and full of energy. Family was worried that a venue like this would cost a lot. LUCKILY we were able to come in for free because we are staying in a mariott hotel instead of paying the normal 6$ a head. Loads of fun for me an the family, siblings and i are big music and dancing fans so the large dancefloor was fun. Great experience for us filipinos from Maryland on our road trip down to Nashville!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This is supposedly THE venue for music headliners and crowds. It was lame, the crowd didn't even clap for the performers and it was impossible to get service at the bar. The space is huge and looks like it has potential, but I just don't see it being the place for fun and music.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
Well, TPAC is the only place to bring the Musicals and other grand mid-sized performers to Nashville, so you know - its good for that, but I've never left being wowed by the venue or service itself; a show yes. The venue; never. 

To start - why doesn't the main floor host a restroom? Wait, what? I have to walk into the bowels of the lower levels (which house a museum in the daytime) past the darkened museum pieces? (creepy!)

Second - signage - I've been here a good 20 or more times in my life in Nashville and still get confused on what 'loge' or 'balcony' I need to que up for. 

Thirds - its just dated yo. This place could use a solid facelift into the 2000's. Hear that fancy donors? You people love to remodel. Remodel TPAC! I was in the nosebleeds for a recent show and all the lights were burnt out. I couldn't read my program. Comical almost. The main door way needs more direction, too. It is a MESS every time you try to escape that place with the fancy people lining up for their cars literally blocking the exit.

Other than that everything is just totally average. The overpriced concessions, the friendly retired ushers - everything you'd expect from a performing arts center...

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: My friend recommended me this bbq joint. It was my first night in Nashville and I have to give it 4 stars. I ordered the pulled chicken platter that came with 2 sides. Mac and cheese and potato salad. Chicken was very good. But the sides I had was average nothing special. Atmosphere was loud but amazing typical broadway bbq joint.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Just got to Nashville after a long flight in so I stopped here with my family to get something to eat.  Well I never did get anything to eat and so did many others in the restaurant!   I waited for 15 minutes and never saw a waiter!  This was around 2 in the afternoon and there was hardly anyone in there!  We got up and left!!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Me and a few girls went here on our Nashville trip. Ordered the Chicken Sandwich (hot) and Fried Pickles. The food was great! The chicken was so juicy and had just the right 'kick' to it. The fried pickles were a perfect blend of batter to pickle ratio. It all paired great with a Blue Moon. There was live music and in between sets they would teach line dancing. Loved the atmosphere of this place. The service, however, not so great. Our girl disappeared for ever. She wasn't the one to bring us our food. We had to ask several other waitresses for items that we needed and when we were done and ready for the check I believe we waited for over 20 mins. Maybe she was having an off day. This won't keep me from coming again. Just hope the service isn't like that all the time. I enjoyed my time there but I feel like it was a little too much extra time. Luckily I'm not an impatient person.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Throughly Enjoyable!  The band was rocking.  The food was good.  The portions are huge!  Sharing a plate would not be a bad idea.  The service was amazingly fast.  Prices are reasonable.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
The crust!! Oh mama this is how a good pizza is made.
My absolute favorite is the one with chicken and buffalo sauce (of course) I usually choose it as a calzone, but it's really good either way.

I like their outdoor patio too, especially at night with the cute lights and just absorbing the music Row action. 

If you get a chance go see one of their live music acts! Really good music is served with excellent food and drinks. 
I was told they had to make changes and remodel to make sure not too much of their live music would be heard by some annoyed neighbors. That makes me wanna shake my head! I live in the neighborhood and this is music city, if live music annoys you, live somewhere else. 
Annywho...

Service is always friendly and sometimes they are slammed but they do a good job keeping you updated and refilling your drinks. 

This is the best pizza in the neighborhood for sure!!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Thought this place was very awesome. We had a private party here and they really look care of us. From entertainment to the bar service - top notch. How they can put that many drinkers into one building and still keep up with it... awesome! Would recommend!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Got there on a Saturday afternoon.  The place was packed, and the live music was loud.  When the waiter asked what we wanted to drink, I said, "Scotch and soda".  The waiter said that this place was a honky-tonk bar, and didn't have scotch.  I thought that was quite odd, because any bar should have a cheap scotch in the well, but I ordered a Jack & coke.

My buddy and I split the sampler platter:  ribs, onion rings, sausage, wings, pork loin, and a few other things.  It was tasty and the portion size was more than adequate.

I'm here on business, and will try as many different places as I can.  There are so many other places along Broadway I want to try, so I don't know if I'll come back here any time soon.  It wasn't a bad place, not at all.  It's just that I want to try new things.

name: Nashville Palace
text: The food was Okay. But it was hot inside, doors were open so there were flush flying around while we were trying to eat. The Singer wasn't very good. He kept singing stupid songs nothing good. And we waited for a Long time for our food. I would go back here again

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Stopped in for lunch on a Monday. Not crowded. Sat no the 2nd floor, listened to some good music. Pulled pork sandwich with a side of onion rings and pork loin with Cole slaw and potato salad. All well cooked and delicious.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
This was a great first food stop in Nashville! Being the first time I had been to Nashville I was pleasantly surprised.  The place was packed to the rook, literally there is seating upstairs on the outdoor roof area.  Staff was running around like crazy but were very attentive to our table and never let our drinks run dry.  Our table order are large pizza and it was more than enough for 3 people.  

Will definitely come back!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: A true example of Southern Hospitality, one of very few places allowing kids after 6 pm. Great staff, great musicians and great cocktails.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great music, friendly and fast service, food is delicious!  Not sure why only 3 stars. Maybe I'm a jaded East Coast Girl who doesn't know good southern vibes but all is good here!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
OMG! My tastebuds just took a trip down memory lane! I ordered the Bolgna sandwich to go and boy was I in for a treat when I got back to my office.  The sandwich was so good, it reminded me of the sandwiches we had growing up as kid during the summer months.  Do yourself a favor and order yourself one.  It is a really big sandwich, so go ready to eat with your game face on.  The only thing I woud suggest is to request toasted bread, but thats a personal preference because of how Mom and Dad made it for me and my brothers!  

Great sandwich guys, and thank you for my trip down memory lane!

DJ

name: Nashville Palace
text: Great service and a fun little place.  Listened to some good country singers.  I would have like it if they were more current.  I thought the drinks were a bit over priced.  We only ordered fried pickles and Onion rings and they were both  very good.  The mixed drinks were just right .  I am hoping to get back here while in town.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I've only gotten the beer here which is all right and the music performances are good. It is kind of hard to find a table. It is  on division so there are a lot of other bars and scene nearby

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Three different levels, three different bands. It was like a Goldilocks situation where each level serves it's own purpose. The higher up you go, the crazier and more crowded it gets, and the better the bands get. We started on the lowest level having drinks at a table where it was less crowded. The band was fine but the entertainment value came more from how hammered the lead singer was. After face planting off the front of the stage, she continued to insist she was fine dancing around and getting into it with the crowd. Eventually they turned her mic off and she still continued to sing into it. You could tell her band members were so sick of her shit.

We then skipped the second level and went straight upstairs to meet friends up top. The upstairs band really had the crowd going and it was pretty packed up there. Had some drinks, got my groove on and partied til close.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This place is a fine touristy music venue which allows you in for free if you are staying at a Marriott resort.  We ended up going before 10pm and there were a lot of teenagers on the dance floor dancing provocatively to Taylor Swift which made me feel old as the hills and uncomortable.  After 10pm everyone who look prepubescent left the building and the venue became rather dead on a Saturday night.  Some moron having one too many drinks upstairs spilled a cocktail on our table below but the waitress was kind enough to take care of it.  They have line dancing classes but the music everyone was learning how to line dance to sounded too much like a country version of Justin Bieber.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Came in for lunch and stuck around for a good while.  The food is pretty good and staff is fun.  We hit over 15 bars over the weekend and best bartender hands down in downtown Nashville is Annalise W.  Personality thru the roof and so much fun not to mention easy on the eyes.  We will return!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: The pizza was decent if not a little over cooked but our problem was generally with the service.  Our waiter was clearly busy which is fine, but when he approached our table, he immediately started making fun of one of his other tables for their taste in beer (the fact that they didn't know what exactly they wanted was what was taking up all of his time).  It made us all really uncomfortable, but he wouldn't let up.  Finally when our food was dropped my salad order was wrong (and the salad and pizza came out at the same time).  They did replace it but there were no apologies.  They also forgot to bring silverware and plates.  Even by the time the new salad came out we still didn't have anything to eat with.  When we asked for them, our waiter only brought plates back but was in such a hurry that we couldn't ask him for silverware.  We finally asked two more people (one who forgot about us) and got silverware.  Once we asked our waiter about it, he got out his key chain and was waving a key in my husband's face saying he was the only one in the restaurant with that key and people kept asking him for it, which is why he didn't have time to come to our table.  We tried to talk to two more people about the poor service we had received, all of whom just made excuses about the restaurant being too busy.  I've never seen such horrible customer service in my life.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Pretty underwhelming food at high prices. First- we sat ourselves and had to wait about 15 minutes before anyone even came to us with menus or to even talk to us. Then the pizza was eh. 

But the atmosphere was fun and lively. People seemed to be enjoying themselves. When we finally were served, our server was nice and attentive.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Not impressed with the food at all. The BBQ pork wraps were sub par. The slaw was not fresh. I think it was days old if not longer. The onion rings are frozen and tasteless. The wings and fries were pretty good. The condiment bottles on the table were dirty and had not been wiped off. The contents had dropped down the sides of the bottles and had crusted around the rim. One condiment bottle didn't even have a lid on it. Overall, I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone. On a positive note, the server was great.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
A positive: huge space and we easily found a table upstairs for our party of 7. 

The downside: our service was not great. Our waitress sat our beers on the table and said "here's your beer" and walked away. No handing it to who ordered each one, no glasses or oranges for our blue moons. In general we seemed like an annoyance. No smiles. My water was empty most of the meal. When one of us got the wrong meal (pork instead of chicken) the person giving it to us literally picked the bun off of each of our sandwiches sitting in front of us on the table to see if we had the chicken. With his bare hands! 

Food was okay. Two of us got the chicken tender meal and had a ton of food that they enjoyed it. For the pulled pork/chicken sandwiches - the bread was sort of soggy. Cole slaw was dry not creamy. I wish we wouldn't have wasted our Nashville meal on this place.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I made the trip up from Atlanta to catch the Summerland tour, and was pleasantly surprised by this place.  It has a nicely laid out floor plan, with a lot of seating on three floors of space, all with a decent view of the raised stage.  A medium sized venue nestled in the midst of 2nd avenue on Nashville, a popular street for nightlife, one can catch a variety of acts here, and have a decent dinner to boot.  And if you love the place enough, there's no shortage of memorabilia you can take home from the gift shop.

The saloon has a deal with local Blackstone brewery, and they carry some of the local brews, including one beer brewed specifically for this place.  A number of signature cocktails can be ordered as well, either by themselves or, for the touristy souvenir, in trademarked take home glasses.  Drink prices were average, with lots of bar space for those inclined to belly up.  The selection of other brews was a bit light, but I'd rather try something local, so I was happy.

The fare is that of the traditional American bar and grill.  I tried the chargrilled chicken sandwich, which is served with a ranch sauce well infused with avocado.  The chicken was decent, on the dry side, but the aforementioned sauce was very good.  All of the sandwiches come with fries, and these were crispy without being thin, and had an excellent flavor.  I've been trying to dial down on cheese lately, so I chose this one, but many of the other entrees were tempting, including a burger with jalapenos in a jalapeno sauce with a jalapeno infused cheese.  OK, now that I typed it, I think I should have ordered it...

When I entered, to be honest, I did not expect much from the sound system.  Much to my surprise, the acoustics of the place were quite good, and the sound man was on last night.  Vocals were crisp and clear, while the rock was loud without being overpowering.  My table was fairly close to the stage, but wandering around, it seemed to me the sound was excellent pretty much everywhere.  

For the number of tables they have, a veritable legion of wait staff can be seen flitting about the restaurant.  My waiter was great, with a good knowledge of the menu, and plentiful refilling of waters and soft drinks, and regularly checking on alcoholic beverage desires from those drinking.  He was personable and professional, and in hindsight I should have tipped him more for waiting on me for 5 hours during the concert.  At one point he even brought me a drink I ordered to where I was on the dance floor.

Overall, the Wildhorse was a very nice experience for me.  Is it a bit touristy?  Yes.  More than a bit.  But the food was decent, local beers were available, good service was to be had, and good music could be heard well.  Oh, and unbelievably, they actually serve Diet Mountain Dew, a great rarety and my soft drink of choice.  The only real detractor, and I'm nitpicking perhaps, were the restrooms.  In a venue this size, it would be a struggle to keep them respectable, but nevertheless, by the end of the night it was not great.  Also, the women's room needs expansion, as there was quite the line for what I am told were only a few stalls.  But venue restrooms are never acceptable, so don't let that scare you off from trying a show here.  And maybe take a picture with the titular Wildhorse statue!

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Traditional country music at it's finest. This venue has two separate stages. Several bars, to obtain your favorite beverage in a timely fashion.  I didn't try the food, but people looked happy to receive it!

The band in front (Larry Hamilton Band)  had five main artists that had played/toured for at least 20-30 years each with numerous accolades and credits to their trade.  It was fun, and engaging.  They also got the visiting artists involved by inviting them up to sing a few songs as well. Wonderful vibe and variety. 
I'm fairly certain the owner was persuaded to share his talents as well. We heard him sing and play a few tunes through a little bit of coaxing ;-). Vocals and musicianship were on point!

Great bands in the back as well. Lots of great  seating to keep it intimate with the artists. Bluegrass artist Rhonda Vincent, and Country artist Daryle Singletary were pumping out the hits for the  CMA Fest crowd last night.  They we're up close and personal here. Not a bad seat in the house.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The food was AMAZING! My husband and I had a front row seat for live music for lunch and it couldn't have been better. Very inexpensive and totally worth it. Plus they had some hilarious tshirts for sale and an equally funny staff. Definitely go here if you're looking for a place to go.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Meh. Tourist trap.. 
Apps are good, drinks are ok. 
Free cover for military or if your staying at the Gaylord Opryland resort!
Thanks for the dance lessons! I don't think I'd come back here but was a ok place!
Headed to printers alley

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: If I could give  zero stars I would have. We PREPAID for the Taste of Tennessee event. Only to be forced to wait in line with others that did not prepay to attend.  Never attend a special event at the Wildhorse Saloon. They do not know what they are doing. Over 50 people just walked in to eat. Either you have a special event or you don't.  You cannot successfully hold a special event and have regular dining.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: They have a large upstairs area for night life on the weekends. I didn't order any of their pizza, but I had a drink. The drinks seemed to be a bit pricier than other nearby bars. They also had a band, but it was pretty typical bar band music. This place seems alright for any one young or older.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great place! The line dancing lesson was a blast and the atmosphere is very family friendly. I haven't lived here long but I WILL be a frequent face here.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Sat here for about ten minutes after the George Jones tribute concert, no server, no staff at all seemed present, so we left. What a waste.

name: Houston Station
text: Off the beaten path but not far from good stuff in Nashville. Went to an adult birthday party there and had a fantastic time. Clean venue, friendly help and surprisingly good acoustics. Definitely recommend Houston Station for private functions.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: We wanted dinner and they charged us a cover.... I've never been charged a cover to go eat dinner somewhere... They had line dancing lessons and then a band. Both were cool. We wanted to watch the Blackhawks playoff game and they made sure they sat us right in front of a TV and then changed the channel to the game for us. Waitress was really friendly and chatted with us about Chicago. Food was good, too.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Tourist trap. Horrible food. So many better options in Nashville. Ribs tasted like car exhaust. Overall, the food was like cafeteria style slop.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Really disappointed. Booked for private events two nights in a row. We called the first night and they said it was going to be open normal hours today. Planned our whole day around the lessons only to arrive and find locked doors and a sign that said "we will return at 11am" it was 5pm and they were clearly closed for yet another private event.

They should have better communication. Huge disappointment

My mother travelled ALL THE WAY from Ireland for this

name: Nashville Palace
text: I like this place! It's touristy but you know what? That's alright with me because the people, both patrons and staff, are friendly. It's the kind of place where everyone smiles at each other. They have old time live country groups playing seven days a week and it's a family friendly place. The bartenders don't stiff on poured drinks which is refreshing from the downtown Nashville scene. This place is simple, wholesome and fun. I'll cruise through here in the future when in town.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Avoid this place.  Service sucked both times I've been here.  You're either waiting for a table watching people that came in after you get seated or you get seated and the waitress doesn't even know you're there so you have to ask to be served.  Oh and a $6 cover charge for the luxury of being treated this way.  BS!  No wonder it's the only place on Broadway you can get a table at 8p on a Friday night.  Last time for this guy.  Time to shut the place down and let someone that knows how to run a place like this do it.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Came here during a crowded Predators game. The wait time was about 30 minutes to get seated for food. I ordered a bbq wrap with onion rings. The flavor of the wrap was very good, although it was a pretty small portion. I enjoyed the live music. Overall, good experience.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: This place is definitely a blast. A bit of a tourist trap but I think that sometimes that can be just what you need on your first night in a new city. We stopped in for dinner on a Monday night and the place was pretty busy. It's a huge venue with a restaurant, at least three bars, a large dance floor and a stage. A band was performing when we arrived which was really cool. We were seated quickly. I didn't expect the food to be good but it was actually really good. They have a mix of barbecue food. The pimento cheese we ordered was served with this really tasty bacon jam. It was really delicious. I enjoyed the fact they served three types of fries all together, curly, seasoned and crinkled. All my fry needs were met. They offered line dancing lessons in between band sets and my little nieces really enjoyed dancing with the group. We had a really great time and I would recommend this restaurant to anyone who wants a quick taste of Nashville.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Music was cool. Dinner took a very long time to arrive and when it did it was just ok. The ribs were practically flavorless. Unless you soaked them in BBQ sauce it was pointless to eat. The best thing I can say is that it's food.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Food was not good. Worst burnt hamburger ever. Very slow service. Music was good if you like older tunes.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Place got crowded real fast. Ordered a few angry orchards and just enjoyed people watching. First time in Nashville figured I should eat something BBQ considering every restaurant was that type of food. Pulled chicken had great flavor, potato salad was tasty seemed yellow mustard based, which I don't mind. Live Music can be heard from every bar, not a fan but it all sounds the same to me. If your into this scene this is heaven.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Had a large group and were trying to grab something that everyone liked before the Predators hockey game. We walked in and the placed was already pretty packed ... Ended up going upstairs (which was equally as busy).

The food was good but nothing to write home about. I had the pulled pork with baked beans and cole slaw ... pretty standard stuff. The ribs looked good, the pulled chicken got some rave reviews. We also ordered a bunch of apps beforehand. A few of the dinners came out wrong but the server quickly got us squared away.

Good food, good drinks, cool honky tonk atmosphere, but best of all they got us in and out pretty quick in time for the game next door.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Country Line dancing lessons brought us here early. The lessons lasted about 10 minutes. This was followed by a boring band and you couldn't apply what you learned at the lesson. 

Quite honestly, you must need to come later, because early is boring.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Ribs - good rub but ribs are dry as hell. Pulled park dry as well. Cole slaw wasn't good . Beans are good. I would never eat there again. 36 bucks for crappy bbq

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Awesome experience for our family!  Great entertainment, good food, amazing atmosphere.  Definitely a family fun destination restaurant.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
What a gem TPAC is to the city of Nashville!  We are so lucky to have this venue, featuring a wide variety of shows, concerts, comedians and so much more, on several different stages.  TPAC is home to the Andrew Jackson Hall (where several large-scale productions are held), the Tennessee Rep and the Nashville Ballet.  I've seen productions from all three companies and they are all top-notch.  I particularly enjoyed seeing Cabaret by the Tennessee Rep 1 1/2 years ago - the small hall was perfect for this intimate show, and the show was beautifully sung, acted, danced and costumed.  I bit the bullet this year and purchased my first set of season tickets and have enjoyed every show I've seen.  

About parking - I purposely purchase tickets for Sunday shows so I can take advantage of parking in around Legislative Plaza.  I never pay a cent to park and nearly always find reliable and safe parking 2-3 blocks from TPAC. 

I'll continue to enjoy all that TPAC has to offer, that's for sure!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Waited over an hour and a half after ordering with no food and no update when asking the bar. Never received food.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Terrible, don't waste your money. Same food you'd find in the freezer section of your grocery store. Chicken fingers were hard as a rock, mac and cheese barely edible. Chicken wrap chicken was hard as a rock as well. Curly fries old and hard. Service was terrible as well. Took 15 minutes after receiving food for waitress to come back so we could ask for ranch. Another 7 to get it. Meanwhile our drinks were empty. Waitress was seen walking around eating. Smh. McDonalds would have been better.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: 4 of my friends of mine and I dined here today. We waited over 20 minutes for our pizza. When we got our orders, my boyfriend's pizza didn't come. We asked about his pizza 3 different times. It never came. We all finished our meal, and asked for our checks. Still no pizza. Finally we talked with a manager, she got his pizza to go. THEY STILL CHARGED HIM $2.74 FOR HIS DRINK!!!!! It was not our server's fault but the manager needs to learn about customer service. Bottom line: HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Really cool place if you're willing to withstand the overpriced drinks. The band was great, but that's typical of what you get on Broadway. My wife would've stayed the whole night, but I wanted to see what else Nashville had to offer. Bartender was friendly and very attentive. I'd go back! Try that Jaco Daniels Fire, one of the only states it's available right now!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Much to be desired. Pulled pork was bland. Nashville "hot chicken" was good. Sides were ok but not great in a place known for great southern food. Big screen to watch the game. Live entertainment at night. Room for improvement.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great atmosphere! Service was very good and awesome bands! We had the fried pickles and then bbq brisket with baked beans and greens. Everything was delicous!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Typical Sysco food and inattentive service. Just good enough, but won't be going back. Beer selection is very limited.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Soulshine has become a fantastic place to catch live music or go hang out and grab some drinks and a bite to eat before you head out for the night on Division. They have a fantastic beer selection and their pizza is awesome.

My wife and I always opt for the wheat crust pizza :) The Carinvore is always my go to choice.

The seating in the balcony upstairs and outside is first come first serve but it is always pretty easy to find a seat at the bar downstairs as well if the wait is a little long. People come and go so typically you do not have to wait for seating too long.

Definitely recommend to any local or tourist looking for a place to hang out.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Mediterranean Pizza = To DIE For
Good Beer
Good Prices
Friendly staff
GREAT Music
Parking can be difficult at times

I really enjoyed my time at Soulshine. I will be returning soon to see if it is consistently this good!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The food was quite good and you got a lot of it. We had a very large group last night.  Had a chance to taste several of my coworkers food.  Wish we had a more experienced-server though.  Not good when you ask how the catfish is and that person tells you to order the ribs.  And he couldn't tell anyone of us who he beer was good.  Several of us just went straight to the bar and ordered.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Sunday, May 6:   We were looking for good BBQ downtown and saw Rippys.  Decides to give it a try.  Our server was fantastic.  He was attentive and polite the entire time.  The bbq was so-so. Not very meaty for the price, but the sides were good.   I thought $10 for mozzarella sticks was a little much though.  The biggest complaint I have was regarding the live music.   We were on the second level, a mother/daughter duo with a male singer were performing.  They were very good.  However, I was appalled that the male singer started goin from table to table with the tip bucket, literally asking for tips!  I understand they make their living from tips, I work for tips too, but I would NEVER make my clients uncomfortable by asking for a tip.  It's the choice of the patron based on the performance or service as to whether they'd like to leave gratuity!  I was not happy about his approach and he noticed (while my husband was digging for cash to give this guy), he said to me " well if you feel that strongly about it you don't have to tip. But that's the way we make our living.  I told him I also work for tips and was still speaking when he got his money and walked away from me. Also- we saw four other live music acts the night before and we tipped every one of them, by choice.  Rippys needs to have a conversation with this guy.  His behavior was 100% unacceptable!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: For live music and a good time I give this place 5 stars. I did not eat here and the food looked like you should expect at a pub serving BBQ. This place is all about the constant live music and entertainment and great staff. The staff hustles around in the hot sun as you kick your feet up and listen from a roof top deck to some amazing performers play Kid Rock-Miranda Lambert, I am not a country lover, but I loved me some Rippy's- the place to go in dt Nash!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: UK alumni held a Pep rally and UK vs UL b-ball watch party prior to the bowl game. Woefully understaffed. 2 Bartender's and the line took over 30 minutes.  Additionally they had very few staff to take food orders. We tried to order and could never find anyone. Then staff tried to deliver other people's food to us 3 times.  Apparently they didn't know that BBN travels well.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We stayed in the Cambria (hotel above this restaurant). It was so convenient for us to head downstairs, have some DELICIOUS southern/ American food, and enjoy some AMAZING TALENT. Their hot chicken, Mac n cheese, pickle flights, desserts, and drinks were fabulous. We ate here 5 times during our stay. The staff is incredible, very attentive, friendly and accommodating. Would recommend 10/10. Would return 1000 times over.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Just sat at the bar for ten minutes. The bartender (dirty blonde hair, glasses) was not very busy yet walked passed me several times and looked at me, then kept walking. I was never addressed, never greated. I walked out. On the way out she walked passed me and did a double take like she realised I was walking out, yet said nothing. What a shame because this place is world famous and I was looking forward to a good experience. Instead, I'll go back to Florida with a bad taste in my mouth (which is the only thing I was served here). What a shame.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Haven't eaten here but went to the concert event drivin and cryin and it was awesome! Great service and nice local beer choices at good prices. I'll be back.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
My girlfriends and I loved this place for the Friday night happy hour with Lightning 100. We plan to come back again! 

The service, at the height of the Friday rush, was exceptional. Our waiter was attentive, helpful with menu and is drink suggestions, and never made us feel rushed to leave despite the crowd. A++ 

We tried several pizzas- the Palermo and the Bob Marley were our favorites. The crust is tasty, thin, and available in both white and whole wheat (we liked them both). 
Several beers were on draft and only $2 during happy hour.

The music was loud and a great backdrop for revelry after a busy work week, but be prepared to shout. We loved the games and DJ antics as well, from 5-7- there are many chances to win concert tickets and other prizes. There is a local act that takes the stage at 7pm for a free show, so it's just another wonderful way to find new music. 

We got there at the magic hour after business traffic was gone, and party goers were not yet out and about, so we were able to find street parking nearby. Given the congestion of Division street, I imagine this isn't always the case, so be forewarned.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Wow, a great place to stop in. The atmosphere was good, the waitress was attentive and friendly, and the decor gave me plenty to take it. We enjoyed the music and the drinks and would love to stop back in. I knocked off a star because I wasn't impressed with the food options, hot dogs and fried bologna isn't my thing. The burger did look fantastic when one went by though.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
I thoroughly enjoyed my visit to Soulshine Pizza... but I also admit I wasn't in any hurry and my husband and I were looking for a relaxing evening. Service was fine... no one was in much of a hurry, but neither were we. I thoroughly enjoyed my pizza, and my husband loved his red beans & rice. 

Personally, I see this as a great happy hour hangout spot. Dunno that I'd come for a speedy dinner. (We parked on the street, and I fed the meter for 2 hours. We got out and had only 5 minutes left on it. We didn't realize we were there that length of time, and we were actually shocked it took that long. Not a big deal for us that day, but still a surprise.) It's a casual, laid-back place. I'd recommend only coming if that's exactly what you want.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great Lower Broadway spot with live music and wide open windows to enjoy the weather. Would get the coveted five-star rating if they served Ketel One. #KetelTastesBetter The only food item we ordered on this visit was beer battered mushrooms, which were fine... Typical frozen bar fare, but the pork and ribs on the menu smelled good on their way out to other tables.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: One star is way too much for this establishment. After paying a $6 cover charge to enter the restaurant/bar I was informed that guests under 21 years of age do not pay cover. Please explain to me how someone of age- who pays to DRINK alcohol pays to enter. In my experience it's the other way around. Guests of age who will spend more money and tip workers do not pay to enter. This is absolutely ridiculous. Not to mention paying $6 per guest to enter and wait 45 minutes to be seated to eat. This is the most overrated place in Nashville I have been. As a veteran visiting 2-3 times a year to my favorite city, I will not be returning to this dump. Can you say tourist trap?

name: The Rutledge
text: Had a great time listening to 3 great bands with friends. First time here but what a cool venue. I will definitely be back.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Long story short. crowded area. bouncer pushes me out of his way and into somebody else.  Not knowing it was a bouncer, I step backward pushing him back.

after talking to him, a manager, and a cop I was escorted out. 

certain people in my party couldn't even return to the table to pay their tab.

mountains out of molehills kind of thing from a security team that suffers from little man syndrome. Maybe he didn't have time to finish watching the movie "Road House" for the millionth time while day dreaming that he could have made it in the secret service if they just gave him one shot.

the chicken fingers were on point tho.

name: Houston Station
text: Only giving 3 stars because of parking. Other than that this place is absolutely lovely. Not only do I conduct business here but I also attended a wedding here. One if the loveliest weddings I've been too.  I heard a new restaurant called Hemingways has opened. I've heard great reviews but haven't had the chance to try yet.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Five stars for entertainment! There was a cover to get in which our group originally found strange considering EVERY bar on the strip has live music with no cover or drink minimum...but turns out this was a more legitimate band, not a young group trying to get their name out there. Great musicians and the lineup thy have for the summer includes a number of radio favorites. The line dancing was a unique twist to the evening considering we did not find any other bars doing it. They had multiple dancers there to show you the steps. They keep them fairly simple so everyone can pick it up, but spice them up so each one is a little different from the next. The decor with all the horses is pretty cool too and makes for many photo-shoot opportunities.

Three stars for food. I was way less than impressed with the meal. The brisket was decent, pulled pork was bland but fell apart nicely, and Kraft makes a wayyyy better Mac and cheese. I think I would have been better off sticking to the apps menu. The spicy fries pickles were delicious!

But surely make this a stop on you trip! The whole experience was one of my favorite parts of the weekend. Everyone needs to line dance at least once to live country music!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
There's a good reason why the Wildhorse is world famous. In fact, the way I became aware of this place was through a dear friend of mine who does shows here frequently. Maggie Baugh is her name, and all you need to know about her is that her talent level has piqued the interest of Sony Music. I'll give you my three reasons why Wildhorse Saloon is the place to be when y'all come to Nashville. 

1). The atmosphere. There aren't a lot of places that balance class AND fun. Wildhorse is one of those rare gems. A beautiful, three level music venue with a giant stage where staff and patrons alike can learn to line dance. I dare you to not smile when you set foot in this piece of heaven! 

2). The customer service. What can I say? The customer service here is top notch! The staff here want to talk to you and aren't worried about social status. Everyone is welcome at Wildhorse. You will come in a visitor and leave as part of the family. To say anything less would be downright foolish! 

3). The food. When I first came in to dine, I ordered the Nashville Hot Chicken sandwich. While Prince's invented the culinary delight, Wildhorse perfected it. I have never sunk my teeth into a sandwich that balanced the sweet with the heat so beautifully. It wasn't just a sandwich. It was a work of art! The fiery boldness of the habanero mixed with the sweet and sensible sweet tea brine waltzed along my tastebuds as a symphony of flavor played deep into the night. I left the saloon with a big smile on my face. 

My one small gripe is that the options are a bit pricey. However, when you go to the Wildhorse, you get what you pay for: an experience like no other! 

Nashville, Wildhorse Saloon better stick around. Because the it will be a very sad day if it goes under.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Celebrating our daughter's 17th birthday so needed something fun to do with teens. We started with an early dinner downtown then headed over to the Wildhorse for some line dancing. Our group of 7 girls had a blast! They did the 7:00 lesson and mostly stayed on the dance floor until the 9:00 lesson was finished. All the girls loved it and it was something unique they had not done before. Excellent live music on a Saturday night and we got in free because we arrived just before 6 PM.  The environment was very family friendly but we did leave around 10. At 10:30 it switches to 21 and over.  Wrapped up the night at the Legendary Milkshake Bar for a fun birthday night downtown!  Get to the Wildhorse by 7:30 for best seating choices to enjoy the live music and watch the line dancing.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Excellent drinks and food! Amazing entertainment! Hands down best on the street! If you are in town, don't miss this place for excellent entertainment! Service was excellent, as well.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
Everyone knows my love for pizza, so of course I had to give Soulshine a try. In fact, I was even excited! Their menu looked great online.

So maybe it was my subconscious fear that I might ACTUALLY like a place in Midtown that ruined it... but really, it wasn't.

My friend and I ordered a wheat crust pizza and before any one of you say, "That's where you went wrong! Get the regular crust next time," I'm going to stop you right there and point my finger to Mellow Mushroom and their delicious wheat option. It can be done well. After a couple of bites of my slice, the toppings and cheese slid off and I was left with seeing gray crust. Is that normal? There went my appetite that was already disappointed.

You'd have to really convince to try Soulshine again. On one hand, I did go within weeks of their opening, but then again... it's a chain. They've established their recipes. So no, thanks. Vandy and Belmont kids can have their pizza.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Last night was awesome!!! We went to Soulshine for my 30th birthday dinner. I had about 30 people with me, the wait was a little long but worth it. We basically took over a whole section. Our server Ryan (or Bryan, sorry I forgot) was AWESOME! I know it can be stressful having such a large group, but he was great! He kept checking on me and brought out my food first because it was my birthday, and some yummy bread pudding!!! We all had a blast, thanks to him. It turns out he's only been serving for a month! TERRIFIC job Ryan (or Bryan)!!!!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I went to Rippy's with my father last night before the Predators Rangers hockey game. We sat at the bar and had two beers each and ate dinner... Perfectly respectable restaurant guests. When it came time to pay, my father set out a 20% tip for the bartender, plus an additional almost $2 in quarters and dimes that were in his pocket. The bartender then came over, separated out the change from the dollar bills, shoved it back across the bar at my father, and told my father to keep his change because it's 'rude and shitty' to give loose change to a bartender. I have never had a server or bartender at any restaurant say that or be so rude. Rippy's management should take a closer look at who they're hiring and what kind of things their bartenders are allowed to say to decent, well tipping, respectful customers. I won't be going back, and that bar tender is certainly not smart as she turned down money just because it was loose change rather than dollar bills or a credit card slip.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Never went in because the security guard at the front said our friend was stumbling in. She had 2 drinks and a beer and had been looking for line dancing the entire night during cma fest. Coming from California, we were looking for some good dancing, instead receive a cold shoulder.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Easily the best brisket aside from my moms home smoked that tastes like an heirloom... Super cool atmosphere and a seriously rocking decor! As a restaurant consultant I give them a 5 stars

name: Houston Station
text: This is my favorite venue in Nashville for any event. The space is beautiful and unique, online anything else in Nashville. It is also in a secluded area, great if you need privacy. The staff is so wonderful and will help make your special event there absolutely perfect.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Great band and view from the top! Ribs are good, always a good time. Hard to get a table or bar tender.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: If I could give more stars I absolutely would. I've got the same things both times: bacon queso, fried okra, meat loaf, and mashed potatoes. The gravy that comes with the meat loaf and mashed potatoes clearly has some sort of addictive substance in it because nothing that good can be 100% natural.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: These guys made a rainy afternoon so fun! Loved it each time one of them sang something original.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Their Famous Fried Pickles should be famous! These deliciously thinly shaved pickles are gently fried. They're light, tasty and we'll worth it. We also got the deviled eggs and they were delicious too! Light and tasted, not heavy and overbearing eggy. Great appetizers.
I got the brisket plate, and I was a little disappointed, and why this is only 4 stars. It _tasted_ good but dry, more dry than I'd like. Smothering it in BBQ sauce made it better but then I lost the flavor of the well smoked meat. 
Wife got the shrimp and grits, and I was jealous. So good! Highly recommend the shrimp and grits!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
When you're hitting the downtown Nashville music and food scene, Rippy's should be a stop on your journey. Whether you just want a drink, food or listen to good music, there's a place for all. They have quite an expansive area for eating, drinking or watching bands. My wife and I ventured to the top floor where we'd seen some very talented artists performing. The music acts change frequently so there's a good chance you'll see a few performers if you're there for a hour or 2. 
They have a good craft beer menu as well as drink specials. I had the BBQ pork wrap which was pulled pork, BBQ sauce and cole slaw in a tortilla wrap along with curly fries. Very tasty and filling. For my vegetarian wife, there wasn't too much to choose from so she ended up with chips and salsa. 
The bands work mostly for tips so if you see one you like, be generous.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: After a long day around Nashville we were struggling on where to eat.  Everywhere on broadway seems to have the same menu.  My mom wanted ribs at the moment so we ended up here. It also wasn't as loud as some of the other venues.  We sat on the first floor and were helped immediately. We ordered a full slab of ribs to share with curly fries and onion rings - we were literally starving.  The food came out so fast. So fast. Which I didn't mind since hangry!!!  We ended up finishing everything except the onion rings and didn't even try the cornbread. 2 well drinks and the ribs was $46.  Wasn't the best meal ever but didn't disappoint. I wouldn't choose to come back.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Fried Pickles great, bbq sauce great, host staff, warm and welcoming. We were there for two different bands. The first was a guitar trio and one band member had their mic turned up to the point where the singing was annoying. The second was a full band who hand a person dedicated to their sound mixing and they were very good. The food is mediocre at best. Dry pulled pork, dry brisket, bitter greens, alright pork loin sandwich. Had the biggest beef with the bar tender. Bar tender would not serve drinks from the bar, made us go through the waiter (who was busy). She than stood there and literally did nothing.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Great food and atmosphere. Not that long of a wait for being a popular place and awesome live music. The wings and fries were excellent. And, for those who care, the bathroom was super clean. Definitely want to go back the next time I'm in Nashville!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Great service and food! We had a large group and service was quick and accurate. The food was very good and we enjoyed the live music while we dined. The music was loud enough to hear but didn't hinder our conversation. I recommend stopping by for a great meal at a cool spot!

name: Big Machine Brewery & Distillery
text: This place was amazing. My friends and I came in here to taste the vodka lemonade slushies and we stayed for 4 hours. I'd highly recommend this place to anyone in town. Ali and Jacob were top class bartenders and had so much fun with us. Definitely a must is you're visiting Nashville!

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We had a great meal and heard two talented aspiring singer songwriters at Nash House on a recent Sunday night. The wait staff were super friendly and attentive. We were surprised there wasn't a bigger crowd. The deviled eggs were our favorite and the blueberry cobbler a close second.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I was surprised by how crowded Rippy's was on a random Sunday night! It's a good thing they have plenty of space here. Didn't get to try any food, so I can't comment on that. The best part about this place was the band (led by Ty Parkin). Other than the music though, this place was just average.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Just left after having dinner, 3 adults and 2 kids. On the plus side, our kids loved getting to dance and the band was great. The negatives: our waitress didn't bring us water, we asked for water, she brought half of us water. The hot chicken sandwich was good chicken, the wedge salad was not good (how?? The lettuce was brown and there was zero bacon, just weird...), the bbq brisket and sausage was blah. Husband ate half and walked away from it. Just a real bummer on the food and service bc it's such a cool place.  Waitress finally came back around w our check and we were out.

And for that bbq plate, a salad, a sandwich (plus a side of Mac) and tip (bc even if they don't show up, we do) we totaled out at $99. Dang.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: We ended up here on a whim, as it was pouring on our way to Broadway and they were the first doorway we reached. It was a Thursday afternoon and they had a lice cover band. Food was excellent! I had a pulled pork sandwich with coleslaw on it and homemade potato salad as a side. Generous servings of both and super tender pork. Good ambiance and a great time!

name: Nashville Palace
text: Don't change a thing.  Good food, relaxed atmosphere, not overly crowded for lunch, and good traditional country music!  We heard Jon Byrd and Mike Oldham last week and enjoyed both.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Hands down BEST BBQ on Broadway! the service was very impressive. We were seated immediately upon entering the building. Our hostess was super nice. Our waiter came to the table WITH water  and took our drink order. He came back quickly with drinks in hand,  they both tasted great! and then he took our food order! OMG when i say he wasn't even gone FIVE minutes after taking our order when our order came out! CORRECT, may I add, and DELICIOUS!!!    I would say they should change their name to "Quikky's" LOL but overall, it was an awesome experience. Will definitely return for the drinks, food and atmosphere!!

name: CMA Fest
text: This event is an absolute nightmare for anyone who works downtown. The organization is pretty sketchy and the cops will shut down any road they see fit without notice. People wander around drunk and I've had to dodge more than one tourist with a Bud Light in the middle of the road. This thing used to be in Centennial Park and I think it needs to move back, purely for safety's sake. It's HIGHLY unsafe and unrealistic to hold this massive event in the small 10 city blocks of downtown. If you're going, be aware and stay safe.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Went one night for dinner and was thrilled at what I saw. The venue has a large restaurant area and a huge stage. As I walked in a young lady was playing the guitar and she was excellent. 

I saw down and noticed right off the bat they had a great beer selection. I am a fan of drinking local and they did not disappoint. The server was very helpful with her suggestions and I went for the Nashville hot chicken, boneless breast. I was a bit disapointed that they didn't have the bone in any more as I always prefer bone-in since it has more flavor. It was very tasty. It came with some slaw but only a little bit.

The live entertainment was amazing. I stayed for the second act which was a woman on keyboard.

The only negative, and the reason I didn't give five starts is that the server could've been a little more attentive. It took almost 10 minutes after I paid for her to come back.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Horrible service.... Took 10 minutes to get a beer. Too many choices on Broadway to be that bad.

name: Twin Kegs
text: Eight of us at work this evening ordered take out and  most had the BBB with ether tots or fries. We were all in agreement that it was the worst we've had from  twin kegs, everything from over spiced, over cooked and very salty could not have enough ketchup to hid it. Very disappointed !

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Absolutely the worst. Asked for four shots of a whiskey that's usually the cheapest whiskey at a bar and the total was 45 dollars. Between the ridiculous prices and the filth, nobody should ever go here.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text:
I have been a season ticket holder for TPAC's Broadway series for three years now and I have never been disappointed in a show.  Whether it's the opera, ballet, or traveling musical I always love coming here.  The sound is incredible, the staff unbelievably friendly and you can bring wine in with you to the performances.  YES!

If you find musicals enjoyable (and there are many out there that are fantastic) I'd suggest becoming a season ticket holder.  You can spread out your payments for your season if needed and you get discounts on other shows, plus its cheaper than singular tickets and you can get better seats at a better price.  I've gotten to see some great shows that I had heard of and some of the best shows I had never heard of.

The Nashville ballet and the Nashville opera also do shows here and they put on some amazing performances.  If you haven't seen the Nashville Nutcracker ballet at the holidays make it a must this year.

As its downtown make sure to give yourself enough time to get to your show as parking can be a pain, or just come early and enjoy a pre-show cocktail.  They also sell snacks to munch on while you wait for the show to start.  TPAC is not far from Broadway but it's a little bit of a walk so be aware of that as well if you decide to do dinner downtown first.  
TPAC has two theaters inside, Jackson Hall which is larger, and James K. Polk, which is smaller.  Sometimes they have shows running simultaneously so again, something to think about when planning a night here.  

I've never had a bad time here and always enjoyed the performances.  Amazing artists, amazing staff, and again, you can bring your cocktails in the theater with you (and they usually have a specialty drink to go with the show you're seeing).  So get dolled up and head to TPAC, you'll thank me later!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Rippy's marries 2 long bars, 2 live stages, and Barbecue without any major dysfunction. 

Downtown Nashville is an fantastic place for live music, but surprisingly there aren't just too many barbecue joints to pick from. Jack's has a prominent place on Broadway across the street but I left a bit appointed so I decided to dial up Rippy's a few days later to see if I couldn't find a winning 'Cue. More a concert venue than just a straight up barbecue house, Rippy's is big enough that there are actually multiple sections with separate live bands. The walls must be pretty well insulated, because I couldn't even hear the other band from my side of the restaurant. The crowd is rather wild and loud - if not just bone ass wasted - but the service was still excellent. 

I opted for the 1/2 Chicken Barbecue plate and what came from the kitchen was more than I bargained for as it flaunted the mentioned 1/2 Chicken that is seasoned and then slow smoked. The meat had a great smoke level, which matched perfectly with the evident smoke ring yet remained moist and juicy especially in the dark meat areas. The Curly Fries were standard issue and a bit overly salted but that did little to keep me from nibbling on them every few bites. The Chili on the other hand was flat and contained Beans - a pet peeve of mine. I would skip the Chili altogether on the next go around. 

Naturally the party atmosphere is what most patrons come to Rippy's for but the food isn't a slouch when you weigh in the nearby options of the genre and while Rippy's wasn't the best barbecue I've ever had, but it was certainly passable. I'd go back for the drinks and music any day, although I'd likely order a Burger instead.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Went here because it was close the the Marriott.  Glad that we did.  The food was great   and the prices were good.  Good selection of TN draft beer too.  Love the huge screen TV and the entertainment.  Listened to Haleigh Martin who was pretty good.  Too bad she had to start on a slow Sunday night.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
Sadly this place was awful...we waited an HOUR to be seated (busy night and we had no reservations so I get it no worries) But to then wait an hour to get Apps and still have no main entree after an hour and 20 min...we left...despite being told it was "coming right out" by our poor waiter (who we still tipped 20% for the drinks and Apps after all the piss-poor kitchen staff was NOT his fault) no manager to complain to to be seen (likely cowering in the back office as we were NOT the only people leaving, or complaining) 
I had heard good things and we were looking forward to enjoying it...instead we left frustrated and hangry.  Spitting nails and warning others about the horrid ticket times.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: A great selection of food, beer, and music. We came here for an event, and really enjoyed the band, and the sandwiches. The spicy fried pickles were awesome, and it was nice to try some of the local beer while listening to live country music. The band played all kinds of country from new to classic, which was great! If I had to recommend something it would be to put spicy, fried pickles in the sandwiches. It's a little trick I learned.  The service was super nice, and everyone was really cool. The location is great too.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: I haven't even had the main course but our server, Amy A said they have the best fried pickles. She was Right. The best fried pickles EVER.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Found this place on Christmas night by chance.  Had a table of 9 and service was fabulous.  Food was delicious.  We had the chicken fried chicken, meatloaf, and shrimp and grits.  Everyone loved their food.  The NashHouse pie was unbelievable.  Highly recommend this establishment.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text:
We are staying at the JW across the street. We passed by several times and decided to give this place a try. I am SO glad we did. Sky was our server and was outstanding. He was attentive, had great suggestions, and was personable. 

We started with the fried pickles. They were great. They were served with white bbq sauce and he also brought out ranch. 

We then shared chicken fried chicken and an order of biscuits and jam. CFC was fantastic! It came with a biscuit stuffing. So good! The biscuits came with 4 different kinds of jams. So good! 

We have been to several places while visiting this time and we have been so disappointed with our service until tonight. We are going back for breakfast tomorrow. Definitely go check them out. You'll be glad you did!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Made it to the famous Blue Bird on Hillsboro Pike. Woo! I love places like this because it's not what you think from the outside.  From the outside it just looks like a taco shop back in San Diego that has like 4 tables.  But it seats about 70 at a strip mall.  How's that for not judging a bird by it's bird cage?! 
     This is where the magic happens. I luv being around artist who are paying their dues and trying to make it. This place is so legendary they don't take reservations and they pack in all the time for Songwriters Nights. There's a wall of a lot of people who have played there. This is where the "Songwriters" perform who wrote and created hits for other artist and themselves . Everyone from Taylor Swift, Keith Urban, Faith Hill and omg Carol KING!!! Carol King played here. "gasp!" So awesome. And now Mel M from Yelp has took a pic in front of the entrance at the Bluebird Cafe =)  If you're into Country and or love music and always wanted to visit Nashville.  You will want to stop here for street cred.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We walked in and immediately felt the spirit of our wonderful Nashville town! What a cool place! They smoke all the meats, food is spot on! What??? My wife finally found her illusive "Grilled Romaine Salad!!!" Needless to say the food more than matches the wonderful atmosphere! We just found our place!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsie's...more like poopsies 

Things to keep in mind as you decide what bars you want to visit on Broadway:

1. The bouncers seemed inexperienced and unnecessarily rude. They cracked my friend's legal ID. A separate bouncer told us he could not let anyone onto the rooftop due to capacity but then prompted to let a group of 40+ dudes up 

2. Drinks / music were fine but comparable to other bars that don't have sad excuses for bouncers

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: After the bars when you're looking for that greasy goodness they got what you need. Burgers, dogs and fries oh my!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Celebrated my birthday here, the food was fantastic, the restaurant was a bit loud, maybe because of the space.   The patrons seemed to lack respect for proper dress, this is not a Cracker Barrel!  But a piece of history, revamped into a nice restaurant.  Our server, probably belonged at a pancake house, but the food was very good, the wine very good, many good choices.   Restrooms very clean, altogether a nice spot!  We went downstairs after dinner for the music and it did not disappoint, the man downstairs was EXCELLENT!!  The venue perfect, perhaps the Hostess could do more to sell the downstairs.  I'll go back looking to try other menu items....

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I'll start by saying I'm a 25+ year Nashville resident, with a clear understanding of the challenges that come with our population boom, and staffing issues around the restaurant explosion in particular. That said, the experience I had today was dreadful to the point that I feel compelled to share it. Side note: I am loathe to complain in restaurants, and this is my first negative review. I've also been a patron of the Sutler (old and new) off and on for many years.

I went in for lunch, sat down at the bar alone around 12:30.  The place was less than half full.
I ordered a Saloon Burger with fries, and caught up on the football scores.  The burger was so oversalted it was absurd. Dripping with grease, tough, off-flavored, really nothing redeeming about it. Fries were nearly as bad....limp, soggy, just not good food.  

When I told the bartender how salty it was, her response was, "oh, I'm sorry" as the check was put in front of me. Most of the food was clearly uneaten and still on the plate, but there was not the slightest attempt to make things better...wow! 

I've eaten all over the world, and am realistic enough not to expect culinary miracles at The Sutler. But a decent burger with fries at a fair price ($16.95 w. fries?) is not too much to ask of any professional food establishment. Is Nashville growing too fast to keep a close eye on the basics these days?   Enter at your own risk.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This place is amazing!  Three floors of live music.  Bartenders on 3rd floor are awesome!  Highly recommend stopping by if you're ever in downtown Nashville.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
I live in East Nashville, within easy walking distance of both Bongo Java and Barista Parlor, and biking distance of Sip, Portland Brew, and Ugly Mugs. I also get to Dose pretty regularly because it's near my son's daycare and my work. I should be more than satisfied with my coffee shop selection, but none of them have quite hit my sweet spot. Here's my list of coffee shop ideals:

1) Locally roasted coffee (sorry Dose and Barista Parlor)
2) Not Drew's Brews (just don't love it - sorry Sip and Ugly Mugs)
3) Option to get individual cuppings in a French Press, Pourover, Chemex, Aeropress, Clever dripper, or something. (Sorry Bongo Java and Portland Brew)
4) Soothing, homey atmosphere that isn't snotty (sorry Barista Parlor and Portland Brew)
5) Reasonable (not cheap - I know good coffee is expensive) prices
6) Decaf options for my second or third cup (sorry Barista Parlor and Dose - decaf espress just won't do for me)

Things I (personally) don't really care about or know anything about:
1) Coolness (in fact, too much cool is a turnoff)
2) Espresso drinks - I drink black brewed coffee
3) Food choices - I'm there for coffee
4) Really anything but the coffee and the comfort

All this to say, The Well is my favorite coffee shop in Nashville, which is extremely surprising given its Green Hills location. A huge selection of coffee from Just Love means there's plenty of variety in single origin or blends, whatever your roast preference (as a City roast fan, I think I have 10+ coffees to choose from!). They will make it with a pour over cone, a Chemex, an Aeropress, or a French Press - a wealth of options. I've had the pour over and the Aeropress, and both were executed quite well, creating clean and flavorful cups. 

The tables are large, the wood everywhere inside leads to a comfortable feeling, and there are couches and squishy chairs if you want comfort over utility. The wifi is reasonably fast (I'm posting this review on it!) 

And prices are reasonable - $2 for 12 oz cups made to order, with refills coming in at just a dollar! That wouldn't be cheap for coffee brewed in a giant pot, but for single-cup brewing it's an amazing deal.

Yes, the Baristas are a little slow and unprofessional-seeming, but they know how to make good coffee. Yes, the bathrooms are kind of gross. Yes, the building needs work - there are some leaks in the hallway leading to the bathroom on this rainy day. No, they don't have good food choices. But I, personally, don't care. They hit everything on MY list, which makes them my favorite. I will certainly give them patronage whenever I have the opportunity, and will be much more reluctant to go to my local East Nashville shops knowing this exists.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
The atmosphere is like a step back into time.  This two floor venue is very loud.  It is hard to hold a conversation and even our waiter had trouble hearing us.  Service was very slow and waiter was not attentive.  The menu is pricey and limited at dinner.  I had the filet mignon with brussel sprouts and mashed potatoes for $39.  The filet was a generous cut and cooked perfectly.  Mash potatoes were good.  I have had better brussel sprouts.  There were only three on the plate.  My companion got the seafood gumbo.  She liked it but thought it was too spicy.  However, a would expect it to be as it has andouille sausage in it. The bad news is her gumbo came out from kitchen but my food did not.  The waiter went to check on it and came back to say it was coming but it took probably 15 more minutes.  In fact, I had called a manager to the table to inquire about my meal since my companion was finished with hers.  My food finally arrived and we were offered one free dessert.  Very sad offer for such an event.  Forgot to mention they do offer bread when you sit down.  The basket had cheese biscuits and one piece of sweet cornbread.  The cornbread looked as if it had a bite or two taken out of it. We had sweet and unsweet tea to drink.  At one point the waiter refilled our tea and put sweet tea in both glasses.  This glass of tea tasted like a fruit tea.  Upon inquiry we were told it might be mango tea.  Definitely need to get their act together. 

Attaching photos of inside main floor and movie screen.  They show old movie clips without sound on the screen.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Very affordable and divey. Lots of college aged people spilling drinks on each other and getting a little rowdy at night. The service is friendly and the food is well priced with decent portions. Nothing here wowed me, but the short line for bathrooms stands out on a Friday night on Broadway!

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text: This place is awesome! The staff is friendly, no charge for parking, the crowd is chill, just a great back drop for music shows. The food and drink is a bit pricey. Oh, and big screens would be a huge plus IMO. But a fantastic spot for music.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
