text: This place was recommended to me by a friend as the best spot to hit while visiting Nashville. We were only in town for the one night, and it was a Tuesday, but the service we got from Jacqui behind the bar was great. She was extremely pleasant and helpful for the duration of the evening. Would and will recommend it to others, and will definitely stop back on my travels in the future.

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text:
We are extremely spoiled in Nashville. We don't lack in music venues right in my backyard, so to drive 20 minutes might not seem like much, but for us spoiled people it seems like a feat. Especially when you are stuck in traffic on a 1 lane road adding an extra 10-15 minutes to the trip. But I digress..

The venue itself is very pretty with stringed lights and a picturesque atmosphere. But the concession lines are LONG. And getting to the port-a-potties in the dark during a show is not exactly easy. I would prefer some better signage in the dark cause I got lost getting from the seated area. 

It was a sold out show when I attended and it was very crowded. If you are going to get general admission tickets, you have to have very low chairs, so plan on either a blanket or check your chairs accordingly. Also, get there early or else you aren't going to get a spot. 

We left the show early and still waited in line to exit the venue. But, they did a pretty good job of getting us out of there. Overall, this is a place that is nice if you are hanging out all day or plan on getting there early and taking it easy, but it's just not my favorite music venue.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Came with one of my girls for brunch on Sunday. We got there a little before they opened and there was already a line outside. Once doors opened, place quickly filled up. We got sat at a bar top on the middle of the place. Was a little skeptical about being sat there, but we had a great view of the band that was playing. We did sit for a while before we were greeted and got drinks. Our server was really nice and stayed busy. We never got biscuits before or meal, as all other tables did. Off the bat we ordered bottomless mimosas, because I mean what is brunch without mimosas?!  
We both ordered the chili chicken hash. I had never had hash and was excited to try it. It was okay, was a little spicier than I expected. I don't normally eat a lot of fried foods, so naturally the fried potatoes didn't settle well in my stomach. Obviously not their fault. 
Our server stayed on top of keeping our mimosas filled up. We asked for some biscuits a little later and they were delicious. 
Bathroom is downstairs down a hallway, I assume it's a shared bathroom with another place. Decor in the place was neat. Lots of knick knacks on the walls. Boots on back wall of band and boots hanging from ceiling going down the stairway. 
Cute place for brunch.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
We stood in line for the 9:30 show for about 2 hours, but it was absolutely worth it. It was the In the Round show and the musicians were mostly songwriters for big country music names. It's such a great experience to hear these songs from the people who actually  wrote them - and for whom they mean something deeply meaningful. 

The bluebird provides an awesome, intimate experience where it feels like you're sitting in a living room and listening to them jam. Also a great intro to country music for us.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: This meal was outstanding!!! The pork chop was extremely tender and was paired with blackened peas and cabbage. The meatloaf was the bomb digitey!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Over rated total Dive bar.  Felt dirty coming out of there just looking for a place to stand. What's all the rage about??

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I have never been to a worst place than this place. We came in to have a drink, and after 30 minutes security came to check id's, we gave them our id'e and the guy says those white girls have to go. Security told us to leave the the venue because we weren't  spending enough money at the bar. Honestly, we were have been having an amazing time in Nashville, and this place ruined it. I have never seen just discrimination.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Awesome place! My boyfriend and I came here before a Predators game and I'm glad we did. Food was super cheap and really good. There were two sides, one had the bar and stage and the other was more quiet where families can eat. If you wear your Predators gear you can get a free bud light.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
We came here for Sunday brunch after attempting to go to another place that had an hour wait. Got there just before they opened at 10 and there was already a line of at least 50 people. We were sat almost immediately, the space is quite large. The servers are NOT stingy with their bottomless mimosas :-). We had chicken and waffles (savory waffle with chives I believe) and pork hash, both were delicious. 
They have the weekend routine down very well. Food was all coming out quickly for having such a rush in the morning. There is also a bluegrass band that plays during brunch, which is an added bonus! The sound and noise level was perfect to have conversation and enjoy brunch.

name: Tin Roof
text: Awful wait staff and bartenders. chubby blonde girl .. awful. would not recommend this.bar to anyone! find a new bar!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Seemed cool until the artists were horribly bigoted and mysoginistic. I regret spending money here. It's not funny to make fun of gender disparity, or to write & perform blatantly sexist lyrics about women. The bluebird should do more to keep their artists in check.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Door what is a piece of s***. Great music great atmosphere but please upgrade your doorman new year new start seriously upgrade it f****** stupid

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Duane really ruined our experience. The food was good, and the drinks were fine, but Duane felt the need to flex his nuts as the all powerful 'bouncer' and ruined the fun for everyone. Duane, chill out.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Okay, so let me preface this with I am 23, I've waited tables over 3 years, and I'm a fairly frequent bruncher. The food here was decent and pretty affordable. I got the breakfast biscuit but honestly I would have been just as happy with McDonald's. The bottomless mimosas were barely refilled and tasted like straight orange juice. Waste of $17. The server seemed really irritated the whole time. We ordered coffee to which she responded "all the cups are dirty." And apparently they were all dirty for the hour we were there. Keep in mind, I'm a server. I try to give servers the benefit of the doubt when i eat out, but she was just plain rude and unaccommodating. It really took away from our experience and overall it was frustrating, I would not recommend this place to anyone.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Loved walking back in time to this iconic place. Sitting at the counter and taking in the scene was so surreal.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The Sutler has returned to Melrose and it does not disappoint. The drinks are prepared with a lot of attention to detail and the food is really good. We had the horseshoe BBQ plates and the hamburger. All of them were very good. The only reason I'm not giving the Sutler 5 stars is when you go to the bar downstairs, there is a distinctive cigarette smell. Because the Sutler doesn't allow smoking, it must be from a previous tenant of the space.

name: Throwbacks Bar & Grill
text: I went there on comedy night Thursday.  The drinks were nice and strong, I've never really seen a bartender work so hard.  The people there were nice, wasn't too crowded, and the comedians were definitely funny.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Yeah 5 stars, cause why the heck not. Yeah maybe pricey drinks, but there's no cover charge...so I feel like it's well worth it. Don't have to get smashed to have a good night here, the music does it!

name: Tin Roof
text: I did not have any food here, but the service was spectacular (Fenway shirt behind bar) as well as our server.  She was good with timing on drinks and kept a watchful eye on low drinks.  On  my trip to Nashville, i was most happy with this establishment for their service, as well as the quality of live music they had going on at pretty much anytime we went in.  We visited this place 3 times on the trip, usually after trying somewhere else.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Let's just say this first..
you don't go here for the quick service or good food haha. Limited menu, which is overpriced. I think it took us about an hour to get chicken fingers. NO BIGGIE THOUGH... because after the hour wait outside to get into another hour wait line to get inside, we were used to waiting :)

Loved the place. So cool to see in person. It's cozy, for sure. We went on a open mic night and saw about 33 people play one song a piece. Acts varied by...wow I never want to hear that sound again to ..oh I bet we'll see her again! Was super entertained and were seated with two lovely strangers who made it even more fun.

It's worth the wait :)

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The employees at this place are major assholes...as the bar was starting to shut down the nice bartender at the top told me I could use the restroom downstairs but as soon as I walked down the security guard starts yelling at me extremely aggressively and telling me the restroom is closed. I explain to him that the bartender upstairs had just now told me I could use the lower restroom but he said he didn't care and I had to go. Keep in mind that this whole time I'm  100% sober - I  haven't even drank alcohol since January. Then as I'm trying to leave a cop is blocking the path talking to a drunk guy. I politely wait instead of trying to push through the cop and he just mimics the security guard, trying to rudely  herd me through the 4 inch space between him and the drunk guy. The only reason I give this place 2 stars is because the venue and music was awesome - but nothing is worth being treated like an incompetent idiot by stupid overly machismo asshole security guards and cops.  I will be letting everyone know about the disappointing experience and warning them about this place. Again, nothing is worth blatantly disrespecting a client and both the management and employees need to seriously re-evaluate their behavior.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
hm.... drink was $6 ordered a few, paid $6 per drink on my card PLUS i tipped on the card. My bank shows I was billed $7.20 per drink plus my tip... WTF!! PAY CASH HERE

Other than that, its fun place. Bands are hit or miss, but allover its a cool little dive.

Just pay cash.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Let me start off by noting that my review has absolutely zero to do with the food they serve here. It might have been great, it might have been terrible, I absolutely don't remember. What is important is that it is absolutely one of the finest music listening rooms in Nashville, which is kind of saying something. I first went when my younger brother came to visit and I was trying to find cool activities for him to experience outside of the obligatory Grand Ole Opry experience. My roommate recommended Bleubird and I am forever in his debt. You should expect to show up early and wait in line for nightly shows. It is a small venue and it is worth the wait. I ended up coming back three more times after my initial visit and would have liked to be a more frequent visitor if school obligations and financial constraints hadn't been such spoil-sports. Don't expect to come here and chat with your friends, this is a place to listen, not to speak.

Pro-tip: Try and come on a singer/songwriter night and hear the stories behind the lyrics, very enjoyable!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Sometimes you're downtown, and you're in a hurry and don't have time for a sophisticated meal. Well, Paradise Park works, and puts out thoroughly edible, if not inspiring, food at a fair pace. One downside: if any artists are playing, don't expect to carry on a conversation with anyone. The acoustics of this place are such that even if you sit at the furthest possible location your ears will still be annihilated. In spite of this place's devotion to MEAT, my vegetarian friend said the veggie burger was at least passable.

Passable...sometimes that's all you need.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Bartenders are the absolute best.  Bands are entertaining.  Just a fun place to listen, people watch, and have a few longnecks.

My best suggestion - don't grab the front row seats, unless you enjoy "eau de Ladie's room".

Live feed on a webcam, with about a 50 second delay.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Best music, fun, energetic atmosphere. Love the view from the rooftop. Of course it gets crowded but where doesn't it in Nashville- for as many people that do come in those doors- they manage them well.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Yes, it's a dive bar, but I heard a great blues band here tonight!  Lots of tap beer!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great place to begin (or end) your night of bar-hopping. The great thing about all the honky tonks on Broadway is that it's super easy to pick up and jump somewhere else when you get tired of sitting. Great musicians, fun crowd interaction, and cheap, cold beer. What more could you ever ask for?

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: (6/23/2014) It's trashy, sticky, gimmicky, and I thought I'd hate this place, but ended up there two nights in a row.  There's plenty of space, we enjoyed the band, the drinks were cheap.  There was basically and 80s/90s cover band playing your usual frat party faves from a spectrum of country/Southern rock/alt rock.  So wish I had enough room for a corn dog, love that there's basically a fry shack in the middle of the bar, and a beaten down convertible (warning, you're going to need to decon if you get in that thing).  Monday is apparently 2-for-1 beer night (did I mention place is cheap)?  Enjoy cuttin' the astroturf rug.

name: Tin Roof
text: No

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Love this place!! It is a must every time I go to Nashville. Perfect combination of food and bar without being too crowded and annoying like some places in downtown Nashville. Plus they have a full size car inside the bar just for fun!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This place should go through bar rescue. They were busting the bags of ice they use in drinks on the pavement bumpy the alley entrance. Totally against food safety regulations. And I have no idea why the fire marshal hasn't shut them down for occupancy violations yet. 
The music was good but it was so packed you couldn't even dance.and by packed I mean people crushing together chest to back.

name: The Stone Fox
text: So disappointing! I've experienced two lousy brunches, and I would never go back! There is no treason to wait an hour for cold mediocre food.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: A must see if you're ever in Nashville. I gave it four stars for the atmosphere and the music. I felt pressured order food so got some chips and salsa. Don't go there for the food just go there for the drinks and music.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great time in the back room.  Band was good, singer was good, I was entertained.  It's what you'd expect from a bar.  Overpriced drinks and a fun loving, boot stomping group on the stage, plus drunk people ogling the bartenders.  Had fun and I'd go back, but I'd leave early again because I don't like being claustrophobic.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Amazing service! They are quick and extremely friendly!  We just happened to stumble across this looking for a place without an hour and half wait! Food was great! I would recommend this historical and yummy place!

name: Riverfront Park
text:
Riverfront Park is right on Broadway St. It overlooks the river. This is a nice place to relax, read a book or get some sun. There are these big concrete stairs that you can sit on. If you decide to walk down the stairs there are a few more benches for you to sit and enjoy the view.

However, the park is not very big it is a little on the small side and there is not much grass. It's mostly concrete. It is not an ideal location for a picnic or to play a sport. If you are searching for a cab in Nashville this seems to be the central location where you can find a cab. Also, you can rent bikes within this central area as well.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Delicious and a nice surprise- interesting decor although a bit dark for me for lunch. BUT that would be the only negative. My salad was perfect including all of my favorites. Creamy goat cheese, candied pecans, sweet potatoes, grilled chicken with a maple vinegarette dressing. The service was attentive but not intrusive. 4 refills of my Arnold Palmer was appreciated! Beautiful bar and interesting decor. Would recommend!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Really fun place with an awesome rooftop patio. Perfect for day drinking. 

I don't usually drink anything besides beer...but this place has a fantastic strawberry daiquiri that I highly recommend. 

Service was ok. It was busy so it's understandable they were moving a little slower. 

The live bands were tremendous!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Stopped in for a late night burger and ordered the bacon cheeseburger. It was pretty middle of the road. Nothing special at all. Probably won't be back. There are much better options in the area.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Everyone kept telling us to grab a drink at Tootsies and I'm guessing it was out of nostalgia? Super packed and drinks were nothing fancy. Live music was awesome but after my vodka soda with well (Popov? I'm guessing) vodka we were ready to move on. Definitely a been there done that kind of place.

name: The Stone Fox
text: I have had some good, GOOD food at The Stone Fox. I regret to say I've only been there maybe twice in all the while it's been open, and with all of the excitement that has surrounded it since it did open.   The ambience is great and unusual.  The food really is the star, though. And the eclectic music, if that's what you're there for.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Tootsie's is a three floor venue with live music on every floor. Although it's crowded on the first floor as soon as you walk in, don't despair, go up to the third floor where it is most likely roomier and cooler. 

They take advantage of the fact that they have been around so long because their prices are higher than most in Downtown Nashville. $7 for bottle beer, but the entertainment makes it worth it. 

Thursday afternoon 7/27, beginning at 2:30, we saw perhaps the best band in the three days in Nashville. It was a 6 member band that was unnamed. Lauren on vocals and Katrina playing the fiddle. They were joined by various male singers at times. This group had more range and material than the other bands we had seen.

Music City USA. You have to visit this place.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I got their buffalo shrimp appetizer as a meal with a side of Mac n Cheese.  Both were outstanding.  I was a little surprised when shrimp lettuce wraps arrived because of the dollop of celery salad, which I did not expect, but it was a great compliment to the fried spiciness of the shrimp.  Also had a few happy hour drinks that were delicious as well.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text: Ehhh, it's ok. I've been twice, the first time for a black coffee and the second for an extra dry cappuccino. I wasn't impressed, and the place is definitely overpriced (a common Green Hills failing). I was a barista for more than eight years, and I know my way around a cup, but this place is drinkable at best. I'd honestly rather go to Starbucks, so that says something.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
AVOID at ALL Costs-FOOD POISONING and Bad Customer Service

Me and my family arrived at Sutler Saloon on Monday afternoon. I was super excited because the website looked awesome. 

My family arrived 15 min before me. Once I arrived my family had their Apps, I looked over the menu and found what I wanted. 5 min passed and then 10min. I was thirsty even a glass of water would have sufficed..but no NOTHING!. I had to go find another server who stated that original server had been cut and but she could help us. He didn't check on his table or anything. Just did his side work while we sat with no server. That wasn't even the beginning. 

* It was so cold we had to bring in jackets into the establishment, we even asked for the fans to be turned off and our request was dismissed by the male server who forgot about us. Another lady came in and asked and it was turned off. HMMM
* We had to bus our own table
* Sangria was horrible we told original server but again who would expect him to do anything from the amount of customer care he has already displayed.
* The manager was whipping down tables, on his computer answering the phone and then was at the prep station placing food to the plates WITH NO GLOVES
* The server wasn't focused and messed up all the checks so we had to write down all the orders on separate pieces of paper to help. 

NOW HERE COMES THE DOOZY!

THEN 3 OF US GOT SICK FROM FOOD POISONING. My sister immediate had to use the restroom and was throwing up for 2 days. 
I had stomach aches but no biggie couldn't eat for the rest of the night no biggie right.. WRONG the next morning woke up THROWING UP! On the flight home THROWING UP on the PLAN. Had to take a day off of work. I am diabetic so when I get sick it is a different beast and I have to monitor myself so DKA won't occur. 
My other friend had diarrhea for 2 days

PLEASE DON'T GO THROUGH WHAT WE WENT THROUGH!  We even called and didn't they care UMM NO! Please the experience nor the food is worth the pain me and my sister are going through. I am just so glad my 5 year old niece wasn't effected.

name: Tin Roof
text:
This is mostly for the Friday Night Fight event on 8/26 which was coordinated with JRCLive. 

We bought VIP tickets for the Mayweather v McGregor Fight Night Block Party at Tin Roof. The VIP tickets cost about $20 more than a standard ticket ($35 vs. $15 in advance) and had a number of alleged advantages. First, VIP ticket holders had access to a restricted area closer to the screen for "optimal viewing." The VIP area had its own dedicated bar and bathroom areas (more on this later), and were allegedly sold in "limited numbers" to keep lines for both short. The screen was "the biggest in Nashville." 

To put it mildly, the reality was a bit different than the expectation. For starters, the "VIP" area was absolutely jam packed. There was less room to move around the VIP section than there was in the general admission section. There were a few folding chairs in the middle, but for the most part, it was just crowds of people standing and hoping to get something resembling a decent viewing angle (not easy to do because the VIPs were in the front and the giant screen wasn't easy to see from most spots- actually better from the General Admission section). 

The lines for the bar were terrible. like 20+ minutes to get a drink. The lines for the bathrooms were worse. Also, the VIP "bathrooms" were 4 porta potties that got REALLY gross. Lines in the general admission section were shorter. We ended up walking further to go up there for drinks and bathroom runs. 

On the positive side, the screen was huge, it was fun to watch it as part of a big crowd like that, and the drink prices weren't bad. The staff remained friendly and helpful even though they clearly were overwhelmed (anybody in their shoes would be). Though to be fair, I'm not sure whether the outside bartenders were from Tin Roof or the event planning group (JRC Live).

After the fight we went inside (the bracelets got you in for no cover) and left almost immediately after because there was a huge fight on the dance floor and someone was literally dragged out. No thanks. I like divey and even a little rowdy, but this was downright trashy. Maybe it's better on a non-event night, but it was rough.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
We went to Woolworth on 5th during a trip to Nashville and were pleasantly surprised! The selection is good and all of the food was southern comfort food. The staff was lovely, our waitress was very friendly and attentive. 

We got shrimp and grits, gumbo and both were great. The vegetarian options were really creative and nice for the vegan in our group.

Definitely worth checking out for the history when you're in Nashville!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Fun vibe.  We stopped by late night on Friday, and then returned again on Saturday. Really enjoyed all 3 floors.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Wow! What a awesome way to start off my Nashville trip. I'm glad I listened to everyone. Its a three level bar with live bands on each levels which includes a roof top bar. Drinks and bartender are wonderful. It's a must try experience.

name: Riverfront Park
text:
When you're ready to take a break from the hustle & bustle of Broadway, stroll down to 1st Avenue & check out Riverfront Park.  

On a beautiful Saturday afternoon, I watched kayaks, bass boats, & a Pontoon Saloon cruise the Cumberland.  & Everyone was zooming in on Nissan Stadium across the river, preparing for an NFL Exhibition game against the Bears the next day.  

I liked that the Park was laid out to allow seating on the steps & elevated grassy areas.  Yes, I know it's "small" (5 acres) ~ but it's not like you can move 1st Street back, ya know?  Now the Memphis Riverfront along the Mississippi River is a whole different story!

I rode one of the Free Electric Buses parked here that made a loop to the Bicentennial Capitol Mall State Park via 4th & 5th Aves.  Many attractions along this route or a couple of blocks off.  A very helpful amenity.

name: Tin Roof
text:
They don't allow colored people into the bar. EspeciallyIndian (India) people. I was sober and still kicked out.

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text: My husband got us expensive tickets to a Willie Nelson and Alison Krauss & Union Station concert. We went mainly to see Alison Krauss & Union Station. We are from Birmingham, AL and made the trip to Nashville to stay the weekend. We had dinner in Nashville before the concert & left a little later than we wanted, but still had plenty of time to get there by start of the concert. When we got a couple of miles away, as I could see on the map, traffic was totally stopped. It inched along for an hour. When we finally turned into the parking area, it was insane! None of the parking attendants knew what the heck they were doing. A few of the cars in front of us were directed to a lot near the street. We were directed to the very back of the lot, near the stage. When we got to that lot there were about five parking attendants all standing together and when they started directing us, one directed us one way and another directed us the other way! They were totally clueless! We then saw why it was taking so very long for all the cars to get into the lot. These morons! When we finally got parked & started walking to our seats, we noticed that we had to walk back, all the way to the front of that lot to get in. It was blocked with fence close to where we were. When we FINALLY got to our seats, Alison Krauss & Union Station were over an hour into their set. We got to see their last 40 minutes. During intermission to change the stage, my husband and I started talking about getting out after the concert and how terrible it was going to be to get out since we were parked in the lot farthest from the street. Then I started reading reviews on here and saw that we were right in thinking that way. We ended up leaving after one song of Willie Nelson so we wouldn't get stuck for another 2 to 3 hours in traffic trying to get out. I have been to hundreds of concerts at many different venues & I've never encountered something like this. Bad experience and a waste of a lot of money. Will never go here again.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Nice Nashville bar. The security was relaxed and that was nice considering some can be gun happy. The bartender greeted us right away and got us drinks quickly for the amount of people in there. The mixed drink was delicious and it wasn't watered down so thumbs up to that. Band was great. They took song requests and got right to singing the songs. They rocked that little stage.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Incredible dining experience from start to finish! We went for dinner last night, and we're already planning our next visit to the Woolworth. Allow me to give you a breakdown of our very memorable evening:
Ambience: As soon as you walk up to the building, you can feel the history this beautiful building has to offer. The owners did a remarkable job with the restoration, salvaging the original floors, the staircase, and the mezzanine. The aesthetics are top notch throughout, from the beautiful antiqued mirrors to the retro wallpapers. I spent most of the night obsessing over all the decor. The entire restaurant had perfectly dimmed mood lighting with a warm vibey feel. I can't wait to come back to have cocktails at the upstairs mezzanine bar that overlooks the downstairs. 
Service: From the second we walked in, we were greeted with friendly smiling faces. The hostesses were very kind and attentive. The bartenders were very knowledgeable about the beverages and quick to take our drink orders when we visited the bar. Once we were seated for dinner, we had very prompt and polite service from our server and SA. Benjamin was great to check on us and keep our table clean and free of empty plates. All of our appetizers and entrees came out in a very timely manner. Overall, we thought the service was great! 
Cocktails: The cocktail menu is very inventive, full of solid choices. I had quite a few of the rye whisky cocktail called 1930 and finished my night with the Love Pinot Noir. Both were very satisfying and paired well with our dishes. My table also ordered several cocktails off the menu, and everyone was very happy with their choices. 
So now the food: Oh the food! To start, everything on the dinner menu sounds amazing! I would label the cuisine as creative Southern comfort food, with a few dishes having a little Cajun feel. I wanted every appetizer on the menu, but we kept it to 4. The fried cheese curds and gumbo were my favorites, but all our starters were delicious! I'm dying to come back for the harissa chicken thighs and the Brussel sprouts! Then the entrees....sooo good! I ordered the braised short ribs and also tried all of my friends dishes. The short ribs were excellent and the portion was quite generous. The fried chicken was absolutely legit. Living in Nashville, it's not often that I get to have fried chicken that isn't labeled as "Hot Chicken," but I loved this fried chicken so much. It was authentic Southern buttermilk fried chicken that granny would make...if you're granny was a 5 star chef, that is. Not greasy, not too heavy, and perfectly breaded. Our table really enjoyed the fish and the ribs, as well! After our entrees, we were completely stuffed (due to the sizable portions) but could not pass up the dessert menu. So we indulged, and we were NOT disappointed. We tried several but my favorites were the chocolate pudding with the peanut brittle and the caramel pecan pie. They were amazingly decadent and were the perfect finish to a wonderful night.  Overall the entrees and apps were very flavorful and well seasoned, and the desserts were everything a Southern gal could ask for. I can guarantee you won't find anything bland or boring on this menu. I recommend you go make your reservations now before everyone discovers this new hotspot. It will definitely be a new staple of Nashville. 
PS Sorry there are no pictures. We dug in as soon as the food arrived. At best, I could have uploaded pictures of empty plates licked clean

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tried most of the honky tonk bars on Broadway and Tootsie's was easily our favorite.  The place was packed on all three floors and for good reason.  I'd suggest checking out all three floors and find the band you enjoy and go for it. The beer is ice cold and we found the bartenders provided really good pours on the mixed drinks.  Hey, it's not the bar at the Ritz, but it's not trying to be.  This is a honky tonk; expect that atmosphere and you'll get the most out of this place.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text: Love this place! Totally local flavor with a hip environment!  The drinks are great and they just added food.  Love that they offer gifts where the proceeds benefit different causes. The staff is always friendly!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Had a great time here last night! We were there for a blues show with the Mike Henderson band and they were awesome! No reservations for the Monday shows, so we started lining up about an hour before the doors opened and we were around 10th in line. Drink prices were reasonable and the service was decent. We ended up sitting dead center directly in front of the stage, so we had a great view of the band. Would definitely come back!

name: The Stone Fox
text: I really enjoyed brunch on a Sunday. There was a wait so I ate at the bar. I had quick, super friendly service and delicious food.  The scrambled tofu needed lots of help though, just a bit of seasoning would have helped. That's really the only reason I'm not giving Stone Fox 5 stars.  The homemade biscuits had great flavor with a perfect flakiness. The Tres Leches with coconut icing was beyond any I've had at the neighborhood Panaderia.  John at the bar was so warm and attentive. I'll go back for Monday night BINGO!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I'm not one for Honky-tonks, but the historical significance of this place in the 70's and 80's got me interested.  Not much by way of decor here -- walls are plywood with graffiti encouraged by the management, concrete or wood floors, and stools to sit on, and wooden tables.  The draw is the music, not the decor, and while every bar on the street has a live band, Tootsie's sports 3 -- one on every floor of the building.  Don't like the song their playing, hit the stairs ........ like tuning the radio.  Craft brews on this whole street are pretty hard to come by, but Tootsie's had Fat Tire in the bottle for $5 a pop, so we hung out for a while.  Conversation is quite strained, because the music is really loud, and the crowd is really raunchy -- country girls have no qualms about grinding up against you if they like the way you look.  The other thing that surprised me here -- although they aren't alone on Broadway with this -- is that after every set of songs, the band sends one of it's members into the crowd with a tip jar to "take up a collection".  While their conversation with you is friendly and good natured, the jar is being shaken right under your nose, and I did feel a little brow-beaten by the guy after his third trip around the bar during our visit.  Where I come from, the bars pay the band with the jacked up prices for booze, and you tip the musicians on your way out if they played a song you like, or requested.  Here, it seems that the bar jacks up the booze prices anyway, but the bands are forced to "sing for their supper".  "Gotta earn a livin' ", he said more than once as he rattled his pickle jar in my face.  Put me off a little bit, but not so much that I wouldn't recommend them.  Just know what you got as you enter.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We would give it more stars but they asked us to leave our booth unless we paid $1000.00 because it was after 6:30pm on a Monday night. So all 20 of us whose flight was cancelled will spend our money somewhere else in Nashville!! Have fun we will somewhere else where they want to make $$$!!

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text: I love a great coffeehouse. This is definitely a cute gem in the heart of bustling and busy Green Hills. I came on a weekday afternoon, and it was quiet, but many people were there-- students, professionals meeting with coworkers, etc. The coffee choices are many. Very low-key environment.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: This place is a great place for brunch, nice vibe and a great bluegrass band. Rachel was our waitress and she was great!! Always made sure our mimosas were filled. I had the smoked brisket and it was pretty good. Also had the cheese grits...AMZING!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Cool history. Awful business. Ive known several people to work and play here over the years and they have all said how horribly they treat people. Sky high prices. No room to move. This is a tourist trap plain and simple.

name: Tin Roof
text: I had fun. My boyfriend thought it to be a frat bar. But I meet some awesome people there. Service was friendly. I would go back.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Since I live around the corner, I am worried how successful this place is going to get and it will be a huge success, because it's absolutely wonderful!  The owner renovated the interior maintaining its historical significance during Nashville's Civil Rights movement.  And the food is fantastic - at least what my friends and I have had thus far!  Crispy fried chicken livers (light on the exterior; rich interior!), fried flounder (great sauce), hearty brussel sprouts (except can the restaurants not come up with something new!), and great biscuits!  I should also say their bar seems top notch; at least the Manhattan I had was!  Food prices are great; bar prices standard.  Enjoy!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
So this was quite the throwbacks for me.  Stopped in for lunch last Sunday before leaving for the airport.  Sat at the counter and got fast and friendly service.  My server recommended the sweet potato pancakes and they did not disappoint.  There was live piano music playing in the background, which made for a pleasant backdrop.  There are TVs playing and ample space for diners, whether at the counter or tables.  The place also sells some souvenirs but it's a small portion of the place, nothing obstructive or intrusive.  

Overall, I enjoyed my visit and trip back down memory lane.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsies is a must see while in Nashville! Awesome music on every floor. Drinks are still expensive however I am ok paying a little more when I am entertained. People and staff were friendly, crowd was a little older (very few college kids). We felt very safe there unlike some other bars.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Point of service is critical to any business, and if you can't take an order every 30 seconds with a line out the door... well you suck.  

I waited in line what seemed over 30 minutes with about 20 to 25 people infront of me.  If someone isn't teady, just say "next" like Frau Farbissina from Austin Powers screaming "Scott". They should open another register.  

I also git cut by a bunch of groupie chick's who inserted themselves with their boy toys. I didn't want to say anything and cause a fight, but there should be some sort of security with a line like this.  Fights start this way.  

The food here is decent,  but not worth the wait.  I'm sure there's another place that can fill your arteries with grease at 2am.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Good music. Food.....Meh. Fun roof top with great views. Mercedes was a great waitress. Drinks were good, prices not horrific. Our only problem was with their rule that the outside heaters do not get turned on until 4:30! Well, iI'm sorry we were cold at 4pm!  EXCUSE US!   That is ridiculous.  Our waitress made it happen and we were thankful but the gentleman that turned it on did ask us where we were from and insisted that we shouldn't be cold because we were from a northern state and it was 55 degrees in Nashville.   As if there is a cut off for a certain time or temperature that we are allowed to be cold!!!!

name: Riverfront Park
text:
Nashville..i didn't know you had some sort of relief from the honky tonk and loud street of Broadway.  It was a little area where you could probably snuggle with your sweetheart and be away from the hustle and bustle.

Lighting could be better considering it's a park.  You are able to talk to your friend or sweetheart without shouting.  You can see the Stadium (for the Tennesse Titans) and you get to meet other strangers visiting.

I wish it was earlier and we could have walked around more but the lack of lighting prohibits me and my Nashville cohort to wander far from the crowd.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Roaches crawling around like they own the place! But other than that it is cheap, greasy, food you can get after a night of drinking in Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Music is great, but can't figure out why the board of health doesn't shut them down .  Ladies bathroom is intolerable, while some attendant helps a young patron who consumed too much get sick. Line out the door to use the facilities, but employees get to jump in front of everyone.  And some pseudo security guard watching all of this.  Go for the music.....but beware!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
This past Friday, I gathered a few friends in hopes of doing something different and going to the Wilson County Fair. Well some of my friends were less than thrilled about the idea of driving to Lebanon to eat corn dogs and funnel cake, so I said "Ok, I'm in for something else if we pick somewhere unique and fun that I have not been." My friend Amber suggested Sutler and even made the bold claim that it was her favorite bar in town. 

Amber really needs to get on yelp, because I thought her raving review was spot on!  We started upstairs for a drink and dinner. For dinner, I had a delicious grilled cheese with tomato soup. The waitress suggested it over the other two sandwiches I was debating, and she was right! It had four kinds of cheese and bacon. But the tomato soup and pesto sauce were my favorite part!  My husband got the brick chicken and enjoyed it as well, but it seems those of us that got the hot chicken bite appetizers and grilled cheese sandwiches were a little more impressed with our meals. 

After dinner, we went to the downstairs bar where there was a totally different speakeasy type vibe. If you are just going for drinks, I would definitely recommend the downstairs. The drink menu is the same as upstairs just with a more unique atmosphere! I had the Melrose Mule and another cocktail with blackberry moonshine that were both excellent but also not insanely overpriced like many places around town have become. I mean you pay $8- $10 for a drink here, but it will actually be worth it in my opinion. They also have a great beer and wine selection.

Sounds like many of the complaints about this place come with the parking. We actually took an Uber from home knowing that we would each have a few cocktails, so it seems our $7 Uber from home was well worth not having to pay valet or hunt for a spot. 

I will definitely be going back to Sutler. I though it was the perfect spot for a group of friends. It had enough variety on the menu to please everyone, and the two different floors allow you to change up the atmosphere as if you are headed to two different places.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
I LOVE that I finally fit in a visit to The Well.  I really enjoyed the coffee I had  - the Mayan Mocha, with almond milk.  I'm very looking forward to see what other concoctions The Well has to offer.  Especially because... they seriously have every Monin syrup known to man.  I am not exaggerating, take a look for yourself... they have EVERY FLAVOR in existence!

The Well has a couple of cute 'n attractive T-shirts I'd like to buy at some point, as well as coffee beans for sale.  I think a really big attraction of The Well is the ambience - it was so peaceful, comfortable.  I sat in a comfy couch, and there are plenty of tables and chairs.  There's no rushed feeling.  

Of course, I was there at 8p at night.  Oh! And that leads me to mention that they're open 'til 10.  Wish they were open right now (at 1a)...

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I'll just say it - this place is weird.  I like the classic feel but not the modern pricing.  The food simply doesn't live up to it.  I had the pork chop, it was ok, not anything special.  We had multiple servers, multiple people stop by and ask us if everything was ok (before food arrived), even gentleman wearing dishwashing aprons came by to interrupt our conversation.  I get it, this place is new.  But I don't know, just an awkward dining experience overall that will prevent me from returning.

name: Tin Roof
text: I attended a winter onsie party this place hosted and I had a blast! I appreciate the lively experience they facilitated. The drinks were good and the service decent. I didn't try any food while I was there so I'm not sure how it is.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Beyond disappointed !!! I came here tonight to have a great time for my little sisters 21st birthday. I was ided, let in. Mind you I'm from California. My boyfriend hands them his id, also from California,and the SHERIFF had the audacity to say "Oh I know your type, are you even LEGAL, is one of those IDs your green card." Let me just say my boyfriend is Colombian. He is an American citizen. I can not believe this is 2017 and he is being labeled as an illegal because of the color of his skin. No! This is not ok ! I am half white half Mexican even though I look white. Why was I not harassed?  Because of the color of my skin? What type of establishment is being ran here??? The manager whose slim with glasses did nothing ! Instead when told how out of line the comment was, he had security push my boyfriend out to the street. If you are Mexican do not come here ! You will be discriminated against and have security used for the wrong reasons. The message was told to us loud and clear today what Tootsies REPRESENTS. So disappointed tootsies. You DISGUST me! I will NEVER be back!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
A certain kind of woman's paradise for sure, but that woman is me. I came to Paradise Park looking for a relaxing evening for one after a past few days of too much honky tonking and networking. 

Paradise Park contains, among other things: gross carpet, a bit of a smoke smell, an old car, and some old  television parts. In other words, it's basically my grandfather's basement. I figured this would be a laid back, less crowded place and while I was right, this certainly does not mean it was not fun. I ended up having an unexpected blast, rocking out to the cover band  that refused to play country and watching people of all types dance like crazy with enough room to do so. I didn't try try the food but  Paradise Park had a decent amount of drafts and a super friendly staff. I was told it gets pretty crowded on weeknights, but on a quiet Wednesday, this disgustingly carpeted place was full of good times with plenty of breathing room.

But II hope I didn't breathe too much of the mildew from the green carpet. 

...I know. I'm obsessing. I spent the first portion of my night here alone-plenty of time to concentrate on the carpet. 

...I wrote a yelp talk thread trying to find out the name of this place, because yes, I had such a good time, I didn't bother to learn the name. Nobody remembers the carpet so I really hope I'm not dreaming it. How could I?

...I'll stop complaining. If the carpet does indeed exist, please don't get rid of it, I won't know how to get back otherwise. :(

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great place until security without no reason took my gf out by the neck, what type of place drags women out like that, I will make sure that place never does that to women ever again, that's abusive and discriminative.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: I have waited years to go to The Bluebird Cafe. It needs no introduction. The intimate space and talent that they book converted my friend who does not care about music (I know who doesn't like music - well here is one) who came with me to buy the album on iTunes and listened to the album for days. Of course I bought souvenirs. The food is very average and the service from the server was below average. She knew what she was doing but didn't want to do it anymore; "it" meaning serving.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We stopped in on a Thursday afternoon for a beer. We loved the music playing and lively atmosphere. A great spot!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We enjoyed our visit!! There are 3 floors with 3 different bands even at 11a. The fried pickles were delicious but the drinks were kind of small for $9. Over all, enjoyed our time and the roof top bar, even in the rain!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
The iconic Tootsie's Lounge. It's a 3-story dive bar with a very unique crowd. It gets really crowded, it was packed on Saturday but was a lot better on Tuesday. 

It's a little pricey for what it is but so is everything on Broadway. 

One tip: bartender told us they charge the same ($9) for any whiskey and mixer, but if you just say whiskey and coke they'll give you house. I found that to be beneficial so we started ordering the good stuff haha. 

This place is really cool to come and check out and say you've been there.  The live music usually consists of 3 different bands, one on each floor which is really cool and best of all, it's free.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Great bar in Nashville! Truly lives up to its name. Three floors of live music. One night we went Kid Rock made a late night appearance!!!
Sub par bar food- but no one goes there for the food. However, I have heard there are a few items that are great after a few too many. People go there for the live music, lively atmosphere, and good times. This was the bar we normally started our night off and ended it at. Always packed, but a stop you must make when on Broadway!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Does a mans heart good to see such musical joy. Four song writers performing and raising money for an area hospice.  Good local IPA brew and tasty seasoned chicken fingers with fries.  Touching evening. Highly recommended.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Word of advice - be patient to wait in line, it will be a long wait, but it's fun.  If you're with someone, take turns going across the street to get something to drink/eat.  Also, if it's a first come, first serve night, hope you are within the first 100 to get in.

Once you're in, find a seat and take it! There is a minimum food/drink order, but that's no problem.  Enjoy the show, it's all about the experience and to say I've been there is pretty awesome.

Yes, if you watch Nashville, you'll see parts of the club where they shot.

name: The Stone Fox
text:
I don't think I will go out of my way to go to The Stone Fox....actually, I might go out of my way to avoid.  

Good: Seated quickly at the bar during a seemingly busy brunch hour

Bad: Food.  Bland and underseasoned.  I ordered a BLT with an egg.....underwhelming and was left thinking about my next meal.

Ugly: Sanitary practices.  I asked for a lemon for my water.  The bartender, who had been touching all of the random surfaces, dirty plates from other customers, and writing utensils......just reaches with her bare hands into the lemon container and just hands it to me (like a hand to hand transfer).  Needless to say, I was grossed out and didn't want the lemon anymore.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: This dump is way overrated and over-hyped and not worth the effort of standing in line. You are far better off enjoying the various venues on lower Broadway!

name: The Stone Fox
text:
The fox is an odd place... Trying entirely too hard to appear as if they're not trying at all. From the kitschy decor, to the apathetic staff gliding around oozing general disdain... This place wants so badly to be "authentic" it makes one almost feel bad for it.

We dropped in on Sunday morning and joined the small crowd gathered at the doors awaiting their opening. We were quickly seated at a repurposed diner table and promptly were assaulted with entirely-too-loud hank Williams by a hipster Lou Diamond Phillips look-alike manning two old record players on the stage. It's 10am and we struggled to speak over the din, having to yell out order to the server. 

We politely asked that it be turned down a touch so we didn't have to shout. Lou Diamond Hipster dropped it a hair, then slowly bumped it back up even louder. We eventually retreated back to the bar to get away from the speakers. It helped, somewhat. 

In general, the staff were very disconnected and borderline rude, harboring a "too cool to be bothered" attitude that doesn't jive with their choice to work in the service industry. 

The food... Solid but unspectacular. I had the chicken and waffles, and was served a couple chunks of dry white meat heavily battered and fried past done. The waffle was average, helped by tech yolk spilling from the optional egg atop it. My girlfriend's BLT was solid, propped up by a couple slices of their excellent local bacon. Another in our party raved about the fried french toast. 

Their Bloody Mary mix is house made, and excellent. 

The decor and concept has promise... But IMO it misses the mark. I've been to many places along these lines that execute the Idea much more effectively. 

I would be remiss to not mention the sanitation issues we saw behind the bar and around the main room in general. We were not afforded a look into the kitchen, but I fear it matching the upkeep of the bar area. 

We won't be back.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
I am pleased to report that Nashville has a truly interesting, affordable and delicious restaurant added to the downtown scene. I thought that the theme would be somewhat gimmicky: an old Woolworth's with an historic lunch counter now turned into a slick contemporary upscale diner. But I think they really pulled it off. The whole space is open and bright, but comfortable and warm. Staff was exceptional, from the bartenders, valet, hosts and servers. We had appetizers and craft cocktails, all reasonably priced and delicious. The deviled eggs are made with smoked trout and they are excellent. Salads were also excellent. We had fried chicken dinners and the fresh fish of the day, a blackened cobia served over succotash. The cobia received raves from our table mates and the chicken was what a fried chicken dinner is supposed to be: Very moist half chicken fried in pieces, very crispy and flavorful. The chicken was served with mashed potatoes, creamy and buttery (no gravy). It is also served with stewed green beans, great flavor with a nice peppery bite, as well as mac and cheese, pretty traditional with a little bit of heat from some red chiles. 
Although there were pricier items on the menu, including a couple of steak entrees and pork chops, the half chicken dinner is under 20 dollars. The menu is varied but not overly ambitious. There are several vegetarian and gluten free options, for those of you high-maintenance types (I'm not talking about you, Alex). 
It is clear to me that the chef is trying and succeeding at taking diner and bistro standards, cooking, serving and pricing them just right. Nice job!

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text:
Hate to do this, but....it's no Red Rocks.  But nothing is, really.  I'm forever spoiled for any other outdoor venues.

However, this is a nice little venue and beats the heck out of a corporate mega-arena.  The grounds were really nice (would have loved to see them in the daylight) and there are lots of trees and cricket/cicada noises to add to "the woods" ambiance.  And hiking trails too!

When we were here for Sigur Ros, the entire grass area was general admission.  Because we were traveling, we weren't properly equipped with lawn chairs and the like but luckily had a blanket to sit on.  If you do opt to not bring chairs, be sure to get there early and get a seat where the ground is somewhat sloped.  Seating is also somewhat willy nilly (no defined rows) so make sure you have a landmark before you venture out to the restroom or you might not find your way back.  Speaking of restrooms, these ones were strange.  All porta-potties, but an oddly permanent inside sink set up outside set-up.  At any rate, your trip to the restroom is guaranteed to be an adventure!

Beer selection was surprisingly decent.  The food looked terrible, but that's par for the course at an outside venue with no actual kitchen.  Be sure to have snack in your car as you may have to wait a bit to leave (we were in the car for close to an hour afterwards).

Another nice feature would be a screen to better see the performers.  Because the ground is relatively flat and we didn't arrive as early as we had hoped, it was hard to see.  And finally, smoking seem to be permissible throughout the entire seating area.  I get that it's outside, but a bit of a shock for me.

But really, you can't beat seeing one of your favorite bands in "the woods."

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Can't speak to anything at Tootsie's other than the awesome band that happened to be playing the night we were passing through Nashville. We made our way to the top floor where the band was rocking. Although it was pretty packed, we managed to push our way towards the stage and ended up right in front of the lead singer. Once we established our space on the dance floor, we had a blast singing and dancing to every song. The band did a great job balancing country music, which Nashville is obviously known for, with other genres. We only ordered one drink while we were at Tootsie's for fear of losing our spots in front of the band and the drink was average strength and average price for Broadway.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I always have a good experience when I come to The Sutler. The vibe is trendy-but-not-too-trendy. It's nice that this place isn't located in the hub-bub of hipster Nashville. The food is great and the drinks are delicious! I'm a fan of the Guacamole Trio (appetizer) and the Melrose Mule (drink). The tacos are great too! On Thursday nights, they have a "live karaoke" band where you get to sing with the band...lyrics are on a screen. It's fun and oh so entertaining! If you sit at the front of the restaurant (near the windows), the live music isn't obtrusive. The Sutler is kid-friendly, but don't worry, it's not ever packed with little ones! (I have a 4-year old and a 7-year old that come for the kids' mac-n-cheese!) Parking can be a challenge, but there's valet available at the corner.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: So this place is famous, and a lot of people stop in because of that. And just like those other people, I was drawn in by the allure of fame. Once inside, I realised that they didn't have good drinks or good drink specials. Adding insult to injury, they had no (or at least no local) beer. Thanks, but no thanks. The music is good, but they have 2 live bands playing at the same time and that is confusing. There are plenty of bar choices on Broadway. Stop in, if you love the band playing, stay, if you don't, keep walking.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
The Bluebird is awesome and worth the wait in the long lines to get in. I would give it a five except for the lines. It would be nice if they just sold tickets so people didn't have to wait for hours.

We arrived around 4pm for a 7:30 show (doors at 6:30) and the line was already about 10-15 deep. The walkway where you wait isn't entirely shaded, so it can be quite hot and sweaty. 

All that being said, once you're in, the Bluebird is charming and has a great ambience. The staff is friendly and fun. The music is excellent and you get a lot of it.

They have a nice drink selection. The food menu is minimal, but everything we had was good. Homemade potato chips are highly recommended!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: If you have never been to Nashville, you have to come here just to say you did. I like it best during the day, it tends to still get pretty crowded. You don't come here for the cleanliness, that is for sure. We were able to snag a bar stool at the top floor bar, right near the stage which was great. Bar staff was very attentive and friendly however the prices are a but ridiculous. $10 bucks for a SMALL vodka soda and $6 for Miller Lites. But I guess they know what they are doing! Music was great as usual and all around a decent time.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Definitely a unique place at a central downtown location. Prices are reasonable for food portions. Skip the tea as it has a very unique burnt taste. Prompt service, waiter needs not be so serious all the time, it makes you feel like you are a hassle for them. I hear the fried chicken is the best thing on the menu. None of us ordered that. The turkey sandwich was amazing. Patty melt not so much. I would not order that again.
Definitely a unique place with a lot of character and history. If not for the location and the music scene, we would have never considered visiting it.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: The bouncers literally shut down the hallway twice because they couldn't properly escort a drunk guy out, overcrowded and nothing special from what I saw. Three or four floors of shoulder to shoulder sweaty southerners, no thanks.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Definitely went just straight for the food so I have no idea on what to say about the bar (bar hopped elsewhere). Five alarm burger is pretty good but reminds me a bit like I'm eating buffalo wings in a burger rather than hitting that heat wave. 

THING TO NOTE: For people with allergies like mine you're going to be the awkward step child. Asked them if their tots or sweet potato fries were made with peanut oil since they're pretty visual on telling you their fresh cut fries are...They are. So if you've got a peanut allergy... just hope you only wanted their burgers + dogs.

name: Tin Roof
text: Tin Roof Demonbruen is easily one of my favorite stops when I'm going out! It's been around forever and arguably has the most inexpensive drinks on the West side. Live music almost every night of the week! It's nice that they have three bars fully staffed, so you're not waiting too long to get a drink. Chill atmosphere, lively band and cheap drafts -- what more do you need?

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The food and service upstairs is great. The 1 star is for the bartender downstairs. I've been twice and both times this bartender has been rude and inattentive. Bad service.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I am only giving two stars because it is a cool looking place... Even though it was very hard to find parking there were only a few people in there. We had the idea to try the sutler after going to two other places that were too long wait because they were packed... We were excited to go there and looking forward to trying it out... we got in immediately were seated and waited about 10 minutes and no one came to our table... My wife got up and asked the bartender if we could order appetizer and two drinks while we waited but they told us we had to order from a waiter... We waited 10 more minutes... No waiter. We were hungry so we decided to leave and go across the street to a restaurant... It was packed but they found us a table and we had a good dinner. I was disappointed I really wanted to like that place... I think they need to step it up if they're going to make it with all the great places popping up...it's too easy to go somewhere else where you know that they are glad to have your business and want you to be pleased. A night out to dinner like that is too expensive not to have a good experience...

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Had the quarter fried chicken. The Mac n cheese was delicious! Love the vibe. It was definitely an experience

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: No sitting room for anyone dining in because everyone with one drink takes up the available booth seating. Literally had to eat my food on the floor. How hard is it to put "reserved for dining customers only" signs on the tables. On the other hand, seems about right considering how short sighted the downtown sporting club concept is. Just really shouldn't be that difficult to see people sitting on the floor with food and fix the issue.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
happily checked off my bucket list. I made it! I couldn't get a reservation a week before (forgot to get online until the afternoon...) so I got there around 5 and stood in line.  there were already about 20 people in front of me though, but I was one of the last few people that made it in!

you don't pay to get in, you just need to spend $10 a person on food/drink. the wines were great, and may I strongly suggest the baked brie?  it may be one of the best ones I've ever had.  

musicians were GREAT.  I did not know any one of them, but they were all awesome - funny when they chatted, genuine when they played, and the songs were so good that they brought me to tears a couple of times.  

anyone, that's into the music, has to go visit if you ever visit Nashville!  thank you bluebird - thank you Nashville ABC!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
I've wanted to visit the Bluebird for about eight to ten years now, since I was in college to earn my music management degree. The Bluebird is in a nondescript strip mall next door to a dry cleaner; you could easily drive by without realizing it. It's a tiny place, but it was a great show. I know now they take reservations online; I was there the week before this was rolled out. Hopefully that will be a benefit to people. I visited with a coworker when we were in town for a conference. We stopped in on Tuesday night and got there about an hour before the early show began, so we may have gotten lucky just because of the day of the week. We didn't have reservations or anything but were able to sit in the pews, and since we were at the end of the line got a spot in the first pew.

There were others there who had reservations, but I couldn't find how to do that for this show--it said that they didn't take them. Luckily, it was fine. We were there for an In The Round session, so we heard from the four artists in the round plus a bonus song from a collaborator of one of those artists. The night I was there those in the round were Vee Lasher, Madison Marie Armour, Paul Sikes, and Tony Zavitson. Vee's song plugger was in the audience too (who, judging by surname, is mother or other relative of one of the artists), so you know industry people stop in too. The show lasted an hour and a half or so, I think; long enough for each of the artists to do 4-5 songs each. It was well worth it: The music was great, the show was intimate, and everyone had a good time. I think some people might turn their nose down at the early show, thinking that it's going to be subpar; keep thinking that if you want. It'll make it easier for the rest of us to get in.

I don't know about any of the tables, but the sight lines from the pews were perfect. Use the restroom before going, if you can; there are two single-use bathrooms here, one for each gender. There's a $7 minimum per person but that's an amazing deal to hear such high quality music. If you're sitting in the pews, be careful what you order since there's nowhere but your lap or hand to put your food.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I thought the entertainment was great so my boyfriend and I went for our last night in Nashville as we thought it would top off the trip, instead I had the most frightening and aggressive bouncer physically grab my boyfriend and I for trying to finish my drink on the side before heading out onto the streets (no open container law). I have never been more terrified by a man in my life as my boyfriend and I are both very passive and understanding people.. i've never experienced something so terrible in my life.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
good luck trying to get tickets. the website is way below par, and pretty much blocks you from even having a chance. The Bluebird needs a massive site upgrade, to support thier fan base. disappointed for sure going to website to tickets and the door can not even handle the request.. I did get lucky and for past the select a seat page only to be rejected at the checkout page.. FAIL..  call your web/IT admin or get a new one..


Update 5.31.2018
So I FINALLY got tickets it took me a week of trying to get tickets but i got some. if you can get through the web process... going there and seeing an in the round live... unbelievable... 

would be 5 stars but getting tickets will possibly drive you crazy

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Holler and swaller! This place is awesome every time. We went today with our luggage right from the airport. We thought that it would be too crowded, but the nice guy outside told us to come on in. We perched on the stairs and tucked our rolling suitcase on the top step. Perfect view of the entryway band. There were 5 people on the front window stage and one girl on the bar. There was a woman playing a violin that was fantastic! She was boss and killed it.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: A great and truly unique addition to Nashville's many dining options. The food was excellent- my blackened salmon was maybe the best I've ever had. Our waiter provided excellent service and we loved the setting and appreciated its historical significance. Check out all three floors. It's fun to walk around. We'll be back.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Saw a Sunday writers round last week. The girl I sat next to was one of the performers. I noticed they force the performers to pay a minimum of $10. It was an okay show but I don't like that the performers have to pay to play even if it's only $10. Seems like the bluebird is more about money than quality performances.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Flew in from good ol Htown (that's Houston for you non Texans) and decided to stop for lunch, great vibes and atmosphere in a Friday afternoon. The Chili wasn't the Texas chili (our mistake, wasn't even thinking about it). Anyone know who the solo artist is here on Friday's?? Awesome upbeat chill acoustics. I wonder if he has a soundcloud....

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
If I was able to give 3.5 stars I would. 3 would not accurately portray since The Sutler isn't "average," and we'll likely return. 

First off, the venue was cool. The restaurant area was very stylish, but that "speak-easy" feel to the bar downstairs was awesome. 

The service was a letdown. Although our waitress was upbeat and helpful when she was at our table, unfortunately, she consistently let way too much time go between checking on empty drinks...from the time we sat down to the point we got up.  Another note on the service was the bartender downstairs. After dinner we grabbed a drink. I'm going to chalk up his recommendation off the drink menu as not hearing me correctly because the drink I received was not remotely what I stated I wanted. Great selection of craft beers which I ordered to help get the drink down. 

Food was very good. The four of us got something different (fish, burger, pulled chicken and pulled pork). All of us enjoyed it. I felt the pulled chicken portions were a little off. I received LOTS of fries (which they're very good) but not as much chicken as I would've liked. It was delicious and I would've paid more to have a larger portion. The burger was great and "fun" in the dunk. The pulled pork was also very good. It may have been an optical illusion, but it seemed like there was more pork on that plate than on the chicken plate. Lastly, the fish was raved about too. Order it without the head if you're the faint of heart as our person was. 

Overall, it was a good time, not great. I'm hoping it was an off night regarding service. It was definitely good enough to give it another try.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Overpriced, Overrated, Overlook it! 2 beers, a Miller High Life and an Angry Orchard was $14. Music was subpar. Do yourself a favor and head To Roberts next door.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Probably the worst place I've ever eaten.. There was mold on the bread on my egg sandwich... didn't bother telling the managers they were too busy or just not in sight. Really liked this place when it first opened but now it's just started to get ran down. Won't be returning

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
If you are a fan of the show, Nashville, Bluebird Cafe is a must visit!

Located in the outskirts of the main Nashville area in a small strip mall. Very tiny parking lot. The actual venue is really small as well. Inside also looks like it only seats a limited amount of people.

They open at night only so I did not get a chance to come see any live music during my visit. Seems like you need to plan ahead if you want to actually get inside.

Great music has come out of this tiny cafe, worth a visit!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
This place was totally fine! I was kind of worried given some of the recent negative reviews, but for 109+tax the result was completely reasonable. I checked with no problems around 11pm on a Friday night. It's a pretty accurate statement that this Sheraton has more personality than most hotels as the lobby has tons of stuff and a patio overlooking the courtyard is a nice addition to the experience. I got my room upgraded since I have SPG gold and it's pretty spacious, much more so than the Sheraton in Boston that I just got back from. The fitness center is probably the largest Sheraton one I've seen thus far and there is plenty of space and equipment. The pool is pretty decently sized and there is a hot tub available as well.

As far as food goes, it's pretty run of the mill. I got a turkey burger and fries from the restaurant for about $15 bucks. Nothing to write home about, but nothing that made me regret eating here. There is a shuttle that runs to and from the airport back to Sheraton, but service stops around 11pm so I couldn't utilize it on my way in.

The staff were super nice, rooms were clean, and I would definitely stay here again.

name: The Valentine
text: I come here often. Have gotten to know the staff and thoroughly find it to be one of the most fun, sanitary, inviting places in downtown Nashville, specifically on Broadway. Brunch on Sunday mornings is INCREDIBLE. Not to mention bringing in great company with me that can laugh, joke and mesh well with their incredible team of bartenders, bouncers, and management. I would and do constantly highly recommend this place as our go to EVERY TIME friends or family come to town. Thank you to the Valentine team for being so amazing!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Molly M waited on me. I explained I needed a HRC pin for my shadow box that would match the other pins.  She went above and beyond to help me.  After I signed my receipt, I gave her my pen in appreciation!!!

name: Limelight
text: Other than getting frisked to get in, I had a great time. The music was appropriate and 3 for 1 drinks weren't bad at all. They also had a free buffet on the Friday I went.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
When our flight was delayed causing us to miss our connecting flights with no hope of reaching out final destination u quickly hopped on the Starwood SPG website to find a good rated hotel in the area. The rate-to-quality of this hotel was a fantastic value. And it was cheaper booking direct compared to an online travel site. 

The hotel was of good Sheraton quality and the staff was fantastic. The room was clean and nice. Although being an airport hotel you did hear the planes frequently overhead. 

My wife needed some apple cider vinegar from room service, and while I was uncertain if they could, they not only delivered but extremely quickly. They said it would take a bit with a few orders in front of us so I requested if it would be done in about 30 minutes. It was less than 10 minutes before we had it at the door. 

The lobby was beautiful as well as the courtyard. Although I wish we had more time to enjoy this property itself. If staying from any length of time, schedule some time to just enjoy the property. 

The only thing that came up was that our last minute reservation done on their website didn't make it to the hotel before we arrived so they ended up having to rebook me locality. The rate was the same.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We had been to the HR last weekend and our server sold us on the HR's NYE private party. We decided to go with the least expensive ticket at $75 per person since we had to buy 3. We were told we would be outside, but it would be covered, heated and have a table/seating. It would also include access to the HR Café itself and the bathrooms. Luckily we had eaten prior to arriving at the HR for NYE. We were supposed to be let in at 8pm. After waiting in line the HR security finally let us in at 8:15pm. There was a very small covered area with 2 heaters. The area where the tables/seating was not covered nor were there any heaters. There was one bar and absolutely zero wait staff. We were given 2 drink tickets, but after we used those tickets we were only allowed to order from the limited bar outside. The HR had security at every door and would not allow us into the café, the bar inside or the store. We could only go to the bathroom and then had to leave. About 15 mins before midnight I went to the bathroom again and saw they were giving out champagne to the people inside. There was none provided outside nor were we given the option to purchase a glass. This was the only time in the night there was not security at the door guarding the café, so I walked into the bar and asked the bartender if I could get a couple of glasses of champagne. He looked at me in disgust and said "yeah, if you paid for it" and walked away. My badge clearly said "club level" so he knew I was not part of the $125 ticket for inside. I was completely offended. After I had just spent $100 eating there with my family on Sunday night, then another $300 for NYE. I was treated so poorly. I wasn't asking for it for free, I would have happily purchased it. I live in Nashville and am appalled that someone in our city would treat paying customers so poorly. There were 2, yes 2 heaters outside for about 100 people. It was ridiculous. Yes, we had a great view of the main stage, and yes we didn't have to fight for a bathroom, but after spending $400 at the HR in one week I would have expected to have been treated better. I was also told that the people with the $200 tickets were unhappy because they ran out of propane for the heaters upstairs on the balcony and they said the food was nothing special. Overall we had a good time, but the "private party" was a bit disappointing.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Great small venue to listen to live music and grab a drink. I walked up and down Broadway and Whiskey Bent is the bar I chose to sit into. Glad I did! The bartenders were awesome, friendly and attentive. The bands that happened to be playing were great and I had a wonderful afternoon sipping on drinks and listening to great live music.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Had most wonderful time here last nite with my girl. Music was just amazing crowed was very mature would definitely recommend coming here n next time coming back with my more girls time.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Fantastic service from Letitia at the bar. Great drinks, and all around friendly staff!

name: Bootleggers Inn
