text: My mom and I came to Nashville for a few days for vacation. We're not into the big touristy spots or spots where drunk people congregate.  We wanted to find a great place with music. We first came to bootleggers and we're very pleased with the music performances they had. The music is typically one-two singers and a guitarist. If you're looking for something more low key with amazing talent and friendly service (Janet was so sweet), then bootleggers is the place for you.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Great sound. Great food and nice drink.  Could spend the rest of the trip here.     Very impress with location and overall.   Staff really nice.  Thanks

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: What was once a shining star in the barbeque world is, as of this writing, for sale and not worthy of a visit until a new owner takes over.  Our visit started with not one, but two disappointments.  The liquor license expired, so they could no longer pour, and they ran out of the smoked Texas sausage (read: they aren't going to get any more).  Having no choice but to eat, the usually reliable brisket was dry and overcooked.  The service was good, but you have to feel for them; having to deal with the reality of a place on life support.   Here's hoping a new owner brings this back to its former self, but until then, stay away,

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
I am giving it 4 stars, because I really do not recall much. It was about 4pm on cinco de mayo, since noone does the Mayo here in Redneckville, it didnt matter. I had fun, i think.

The drinks are bit pricey for Redneckville, but I am sure it is because it is a tourist trap :)
Still cheaper than in Las Vegas for tourists haha

name: FooBar
text: inexpensive locals bar. lots a reviews complained of the smoke but fret no more; smoking is outside only, in their newly fenced in back yard /patio area.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Just saw Luke Combs here!!! What a blast. Beers are reasonably priced. Venue is great for any band in Nashville. Had to wait online in the rain for an hour before he went on though. Other than that place is awesome. Highly recommend!!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Awesome bar with live music right on Broadway. There are so many places to choose from and I was having major sensory overload, but so happy we stopped here!

My family was so tired after a long day of doing as many touristy things as possible. We didn't want a jam packed bar but still wanted he live music scene. There was a great cover band that was very interactive with the crowd. Take note that we were out on a Monday night and it was still poppin'. 

Drinks: Lots of drink choices to choose from except for the fact that they don't make a Hot Toddy. Disappointing because it's not that hard to make one. 

Seating: There's an upstairs and downstairs that give you a great view of the band no matter where you're at. Plenty of room for everyone!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Two years ago I had a terrible time at a Sheraton in Florida. This week was my first return to one of their hotels.  I can't say enough good things about my experience. From check in to check out everything was taken care of, all of our needs met. Clean, maintained, great service and advice from many staff members, especially Tammy in the lobby area and Terrell in the Club Room.  So good that I had them book me a room for tonight in Birmingham.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Sunday afternoon fun!!! 
This was our fav bar on Broadway (out of the 5 we went to.) I didn't know what I wanted, asked the bartender to surprise me. No hesitation, except to ask if I like a particular flavor, and she went to work! Delicious cocktails. GREAT band, who I wish I could remember the name of, and fun atmosphere. Bartenders were on top of their game! A+

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
We booked this hotel via Hotwire.com and got a great deal.  When reading about the hotel, we saw that it was pet friendly so we were happy to know that we could bring our dog, since we were arriving here after visiting family in NC.  When we checked in, I asked if there was anything special I should know since we had our dog and they made me sign a form and said that we couldn't leave our dog in the room unattended, so that really put a damper on the entire trip because we were very limited on where we could go.  

I wish this was posted on their website so that we wouldn't have brought our dog on the trip.  

Otherwise everything was very nice, staff was good, rooms were nice and it was within reasonable distance from everything (driving not walking)

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Pretty large venue this one, with mostly good bands, at least when I've been. The drinks are reasonable and it gets packed with tourists on weekends. There is usually a super long line outside so go around the back to the alley and enter at the rear, you will save loads a time.  Bar staff are very efficient you won't wait long for your beer. Well worth stopping in this place for that true Nashville experience, you won't be disappointed.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Great place for drinkin' and watchin' live music. Intimate settin', stage is not so high that you feel disconnected with the band. Friendly bartenders and decent drink prices. Good times.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: With a skeleton crew on for Thanksgiving, our waitress was working hard. She did a good job, considering. So did the kitchen. Food was out surprisingly fast, and we had no complaints. The menu seemed awfully limited and had no local feel. I had hoped to go to a non-chain eatery, but many of them were closed for the day. Better planning, next time!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Blow away by the awesome service!!! On a whim, we decided to give Hard Rock a try. Having our 3 yr old is always tricky, and since we were surrounded by bars, we figured we better play it safe.. So glad we did!!! 

We were able to get a table right away. Our server, Morgan was right there to greet us and take out order. The atmosphere was fun.. Music was great!! It had our 3 yr old dancing. Will definitely go back on our next trip to Nashville!!!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
I've been to the Sheraton Music City twice, both times were for the Nashville cat show. I've never stayed at the hotel and my rating is only on the convention center part of the hotel. 

From the look of the hotel, I'd say this place was built in the 1980's maybe; but it's been well kept. The location of the hotel isn't downtown, it's more of an airport hotel, which is good and bad. Good being close to the airport and bad because there isn't much in the way of entertainment or restaurants. 

The convention/expo center has its own entrance on the north side of the building. There is a small lobby/foyer before you enter the ballroom area. Along the ballroom there's a hallway that leads down to the other ballrooms and conference rooms. The bathrooms are located along this hallway. 

In the foyer area is a small concession stand that sells sandwiches and salads, along with drinks during events. This is a great space for the Nashville Cat show.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: The best thing about the hotel was the bed was so comfortable and the staff was very friendly! So friendly that they told my husband you can come out to Tennessee and buy two boots and get one free! Very pleasant! Next time we visit we will be back to enjoy a bit longer!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
PARKING: street parking. 
OUTSIDE: visiting from CA so I had to check out downtown Nashville at night. I haven't been down here in at least 10 years at night. 

You can see from outside through the open door that there were a good amount of people inside with a live band playing and hear the good music and singer. 

INSIDE: free cover for men and women! YEEHAW says the hand stamp on my wrist. How appropriate for going into a country bar. Cowboy faces on the right wall painted. Live band directly on your right when you walk in. Ample floor space for dancing but only one couple dancing. 
Music was great so I wish more people were dancing. 

Everyone else was sitting or standing by he bar or the tables and chairs. Or upstairs where you can look down and see downstairs. One guy was dropping ice on a friend down below haha. 

BATHROOMS: decent, toilet paper and no bad smells, which is always a plus when out at a bar at night. 

MUSIC: LOVED the girl singer and the second band of guys. I'm no country music expert at all so he fact that I liked the music means a lot. They were taking requests and asking for tips of course but I know some bands don't take requests. Seems they knew a ton of songs. And if they couldn't play your song then they'd give your tip money back haha! 

OVERALL: I would come back for sure. Liked the stools at the bar instead of having to stand awkwardly with your drink all night. Music was live and not just a run of the mill DJ pressing buttons. No cover charge! Guy even re stamped the YEEHAAAW on my hand when I asked him to on my way out.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: We stopped in while waiting for a nighttime trolley tour so we were only in there for about 20 minutes at 6:30pm. We had fantastic moonshine drinks! There was a terrific band playing and it just had a good vibe of a local, semi-dive bar. On Friday night I ventured down to Tootsie and man was that a mistake! For one I wasn't drunk and two, i was alone, anyway after leaving and zig zagging my way through the hoards of people down Broadway to fin somewhere else to go, I found myself back at Bootleggers and it was kind of empty but I just had a fantastic time! Again, another great band playing, had a few local beers and ended up staying until about 1:30am! Service was good, vibe was great. Chatted with a lot of others who were visiting from out of town. Just all over good vibe and a great place to go if the jammed packed bars of Broadway are too overwhelming.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Do not go here on a Friday or Saturday night. Actually all of Broadway gets CRAZY at night. We went there our first night out (on Thursday) and it was PERFECT. There was a band and a good crowd, but not crazy packed that you were getting knocked over. If I ever come here again, I will not be on Broadway during the weekend.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This place was pretty cool! Very much like the Tardis, in that it is much bigger on the inside than it looks on the outside. The first floor was overwhelmingly packed, but we soon found out that there were 3 other levels to explore! Each level was as fun as the next, and there was definitely more room to dance a little :) drinks weren't too overpriced and we didn't pay a cover to get in, so that was great. I've been looking for some actual line dancing places downtown for a while and can't seem to find one. Even though The Stage didn't fit the bill when it came to line dancing of any kind, I still had a lot of fun :)

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Just went here to be a tourist and grab a beer, but it was awesome! The bartender was very engaging, and the atmosphere was amazing! I was by myself, and had never just gone to a bar for a beer by myself, but I felt very comfortable. Good beer, friendly bartender, how could anything go wrong?

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
Came here strictly for moonshine! It was delish! I had the water melon kind which they mixed into a margarita, and also a apple one and it was very tasty. They had a really fun band rocking the house on a Monday night.

Cleared out around 2, so wouldn't say it was quite happenin'. Loved the prohibition vibe inside and decor, bartender was super attentive. Many tables were extremely wobbly, and I was worried the elbows of my campanions would make it slide right off. Other than that, great spot in downtown.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: 5 stars for what it is. The drinks were reasonably priced. The local resident bands were not bad. What made this bar was the rooftop patio/bar. It overlooked downtown and was a great spot to relax, drink, listen to local music and have a good time.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
This bar is great b/c it isn't one of the main attractions do you aren't packed in like sardines! However because it isn't a main bar, the music may not always be top notch. The last band I saw in there played Pearl Jam so they were a winner in my book!

We discovered this bar several years ago during a girls' trip and have gone back during each subsequent trip. In fact in this last trip, we went back both nights we were in town!

This is where I was introduced to Oatmeal Cookie Moonshine and my life will never be the same! It is delicious over ice and goes down way too easy. My friend loves the Bloody Mary with Jalapeño Moonshine!

name: The 5 Spot
text:
I used to love this place, but the craftsmanship on the outdoor bar is a total disaster...uneven cuts on the lumber?! How can I trust these people to make my drink correctly?!
I doubt I'll ever come here again until my gig next Tuesday

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Looking for some of that good 'ole Honky Tonk in the heart of Nashville??? Look no further, you've found your place! Always lively, lots of energy, locals and transients alike are here. Bartenders are hot and sexy too. There's security just in case someone consumes too much Fireball and gets out of hand, but everyone here is pretty friendly so it's unlikely that would happen.

The live music is a great, and they play a wide range of old and new. This is a MUST visit, even if you don't drink, that's okay. You have to visit this place when you're in Nashville!!! Seating around the sides and in the back, and an upfront dance floor for the more adventurous.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
I went there on Dec27,2019 Friday
I ordered drinks  and they kept my Visa card
When I went home I forgot my Visa card
The next day I check my charges
And I was going to go pick my card up
Someone from The bar charged over $800 at the mall and I had to cancel my visa I see now why they want to keep your visa card
Lesson learned never ever let them keep your visa card pay as you go or pay cash I did call the establishment about it but they never called me back yet about this theft

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: As previous reviews state, this is a chain restaurant so you will get the chain food with the chain service. Way over priced, lack in flavor, & poor customer service. This location was no different than the other chains. You're left on your own to find parking in the street. Good luck! If you want the chain restaurant experience, that's all it is.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Terrible Service!
The only reason why we went in there was because I was walking around broadway with kids and none of the places would allow them in, except here. 
The place has 2 floors and we were told they had live music on the top floor so we asked the hostess to give us a table there. She said we had to wait 20 minutes. 
When the 20 minutes passed, We went up and the place was empty! She didn't even walk up with us but rather told us we could go up now, so we didn't get a table assignment. There was a band playing and a couple of tables with customers. The Batman didn't even notice us, and I tried going up to him to ask where we could sit but he didn't even acknowledge I was there. 
We decided to sit outside on the terrace. The waitress came over and took our order. It took her 10 minutes to bring the drinks out which were a lemonade and waters. Another 10 or 15 minutes went by and we asked if the food was going to take much longer because the kids were very hangry by now. She said the kitchen was swamped but was going to check. We had to ask another waiter about our food and our waitress because she never returned. He said he was going to check on the food, but we told him to come back, we didn't want to lose another server. When he returned he said he didn't know how long it was going to take, that he couldn't find out. At this point, we decided to leave the place. We wasted close to an hour just waiting in this place. They need more servers, kitchen staff, I don't know why else but it is not acceptable to wait for food and for a table at an empty restaurant that long!
Only reason I don't give it a 1 star is the location and the fact that they accept kids

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Whenever we come into town we eat here! We love the staff, food and environment. Its a great place with good music.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: SAD! The failing hard rock cafe took over an hour to bring appetizers. Then the $20 chicken tenders took another 45 minutes. Wouldn't recommend.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
Started out with a great band, great music until 10pm then these punk ass kids show up ( a supposed band)  waited for 45 mins while these jackasses set up.  I had a gut feeling it wasn't going to go well.  This is NASHVILLE !!!!   Not senior prom.   Anyway they started singing bouncing around the stage and acting like they were some famous wanna be boy band.   Who the F*+# is Jerry Jacobs?   He isn't country !   Not the country I've heard. My whole like.  Damn I'm getting old .....My kids can sing better than this idiot !!!!   Finished my drink and left.  They ruined my experience tonight !!!   The Stage hired some talentless morons that sang crap!!!!
Like I mentioned the 1st group we could have stayed listening to them all night , but cocky wanna be talentless think their hot shit punks don't belong in this venue.  So many better bands we saw tonight.  Anyway,  they should go to LA and find their fame along Hollywood Blvd where they are better suited.  This was not country !    Oh
Well,   Hopefully they see this post and try singing lessons. If you see skinny jeans and punk hairdos and unwarranted attitude ......walk away.   Lol

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
This hotel offers airport parking that I've purchased several times. Each time it's complete chaos. They advertise a shuttle to/from your car, however, they sometimes will flat out refuse to take you to your car. The long-term parking lot is about a 1/4mile walk. Being forced to walk a 1/4mile downhill with luggage while wearing heels in 30 degree weather after flying on a redeye all night is absolutely absurd. 
If the hotel doesn't intend to offer a shuttle service to customers vehicles, perhaps they shouldn't ADVERTISE the shuttle! 
Parking here is just chaotic. You have to pull your car up to the valet attendant each time, as opposed to going straight to park like every other parking facility. Then you have to drive down to the long term lot and wait for a shuttle driver to come pick you up in no designated spot. And most of the time the driver never bothers to show up.
Also, when calling the hotel to request the shuttle at the airport, no one answered the phone for nearly 20 minutes. I had to keep calling repeatedly.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
We did the self-guided Ryman Auditorium late morning & wanted to eat somewhere on Broadway. The music sounded really loud at some places & the parking was too far for a one-legged fat boy like me. Hard Rock has relatively quiet, had valet parking & since my name is Rock I've always wanted a Hard Rock baseball cap. 

I knew going in that the food wasn't highly regarded. We split a half-pound burger with fries & a smoothie. It was plenty for two. A souvenir pint glass came with the smoothie to add to our collection.  

It was not bad at all, but other than the destination has & the valet parking it was unremarkable. I don't regret doing it, but I've got my hat & my pint glass so I don't need to go again.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: My must visit bar when I'm in Nashville. After a night at the Ryman what could be better. Nashville downtown is tremendous and the big guitar outside leads you to the Hard Rock Cafe. You will love it here. Even though I've never been disappointed at a Hard Rock Cafe in any city, this one in Nashville will always be my favorite.

name: The Valentine
text: I went here on a Wednesday evening to hang out and have some dinner. The band was enthusiastic, but the country was a little too old school for me. I enjoyed their gummy bear shot (which was the special of the day) and got a really good veggie wrap featuring some kind of spinach dip in the wrap. The Mac and cheese was mediocre and the place was a little on the emptier side for Broadway.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: One of my favorite places in Nashville.  Sunday Funday with Shawn Mayer and Mark Dooley (12-3) is some of the best live music around.  Shawna Hornbeck bartends every Sunday with her faithful partner Molly Bird.  They always make my cocktail just the way I like it, and are super fun.  There is no place else to be on Sunday afternoon!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: My first time bar hopping in Nashville and wandered into this place. The bar was ok, but honestly the band was just awful. I'm a musician myself and after all the talk about how great the Nashville music scene is, I was appalled that they let such a crappy band on stage on a Friday night. However the place was pretty empty so maybe the person booking will realize the error of their ways. One beer and we were gone.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: I had a great time at this venue. This the drinks were very delicious and not water down. The pricing is not that bad.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Service was good but the food was lackluster. Luke warm, wilted fries and a tasteless club sandwich. My daughter did not care for her salmon salad as well.

name: The Valentine
text:
2.5

The good things to start: the employees are wonderfully nice. Everyone from security to the door guys to the bartenders... super nice. I think many of the problems I had/have with The Valentine are due to the fact that it's new. BUT if it's open to take my money and is located on Broadway (ground zero in the tourist traffic game), I think it's fair to expect that it would have its act together from the very beginning.

I came here with a good friend in late spring. I was excited to spend time with her and to show off a new business. She, being from TN, was dubious about going out on Broadway but she indulged me. I left with egg on my face. We walked in to find a, largely, empty huge space. 'Well, it's Sunday so maybe it needs some time to amp up.' Thing is, even though it may be Sunday, it's still Broadway. Most establishments weren't hurting for a crowd. We walked in and thought about getting a bite to eat. The menu, at that time, wasn't quite ready. We'd thought about having salads and sandwiches. At the time, though, all they had to offer were chicken tenders and pretzel bites. Hmm. Okay. Drinks. We're in a bar. We'll get drinks. I got a Stiegl Grapefruit and my friend ordered a white wine... which came in a plastic cup and was a small pour. Hmm. Okay. We tried to make the best of it (the bartender was very sweet as she apologized about items that were unavailable) but as we started talking, the band started up. I hate to yuck someone's yum but this band was not the most talented. But they were loud. Very loud. The emptiness of the bar didn't help the noise or talent level. Wanting to escape the madness, we tried to salvage our time there by going to the roof. Since it was such a slow night, the venue was closed past the second floor. I get it. I do. But rooftops are Broadway bars' bread & butter in food weather. After the first floor, the rooftop should always be open. My friend, patient and sweet as she is, was nearing her breaking point. We gulped our drinks and took off to see what else Downtown had to offer.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
We went last night, Thursday, at 10:30pm when Jesse Cain band came on. They check everyone for ID at the door. We found seating right at the bar. The band played everything from Johnny Cash, Charlie Daniels, and Garth Brooks. The dueling fiddle players were crazy good. The band was really entertaining, very talented singers and musicians.

The patrons were a lot of fun, and the $8.50 Captain and cokes were good.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
First, the hotel is pretty nice. The customer service is what I have issue with. 

When you pay for a hotel, you pay for certain aminities. When I arrived, after a 6 hour drive, I had 10 minutes if AC before a citywide blackout. 

Now, I know that is an act of God which is unpredictable but our first night in the hotel was sans air in July. It was miserable. The only thing my best friend and I could do was open the balcony door to let some night air in the room. By doing this, we could hear (all night) a group of very loud men in the pool/balcony area. At 1am, I went down to complain and ask the status of the outage.  I was told that they would find the men who were keeping us awake and have them hold it down. I was also told the outage was being resolved.

At 5am, we just couldn't take it anymore. No one had resolved the loud guest problem and we were so uncomfortably hot, we decided to go find breakfast somewhere.

About that time the power came back on.

Today, when I checked out, I asked if they would discount the room. Let's face it, it may not have been controllable but you had guests that didn't sleep and paid ahead of time for amenities that we didn't receive.

Instead of being polite, the front desk guy rudely told me no, I would not receive any discount. I was merely asking a question. A reasonable question. And I wasn't being a jerk. I paid money that I worked hard for and was uncomfortable an entire night to the point that I did not sleep.

When I told the guy that I planned to contact his corporate office, he said "Well you do that. You weren't the only person inconvenienced. 23,000 other people were affected." He said it snarky. Again, I was simply asking a question and as a paying customer, I expect better service than that. I do not appreciate being talked to like a spoiled brat. 

I do NOT recommend this hotel to anyone. It might be okay if your trip is uneventful... But should something inconvenience your stay, don't expect Sheraton to do anything about it and surely don't ask the guest services people about it or risk being treated rudely.

name: The Valentine
text:
This is one of my favorite places on Broadway because they have a roof top and you can see all downtown. BUT you have to walk up those stairs. 
They have music downstairs. There are a few levels. I don't know if they have music on each level at the same time. 
We had a really nice time on a Friday afternoon listening to nice music on a bright sunny day eating hummus and vegetables while the teenagers had chicken nuggets. Yes, they let them in during the day. 
They serve the wine in a plastic cup to remind you that you are on Broadway. They have several vegetarian options which are good for the Gluten intolerant friends. Drinks are very reasonable too. 
Put on the list to visit and you WILL see a bachelorette party.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Not sure why this hotel isn't ranked higher. It is at minimum a 4. 
The lobby and building was in excellent condition with 5 star customer service. The room was exceptionally clean and the workout room was the best one I've been to in a bonvoy chain. 2 pools and a hot tub, free parking, 12 noon check out. 
My only complaint is I could smell cigarettes . Not sure if I was near smoking rooms or a break room but it was distinguishable

name: FooBar
text: I don't know, maybe some people like dark, smoked-fill hipster dungeons that wreak of vomit and STD's, but not this guy. And if that weren't enough - let's turn the heavy metal up to 11 so that the patrons have to scream at each other. And make sure the bathrooms doors don't lock, people love that. The live music venue may be the only redeeming factor here, but the sound guy must be deaf - again, way too loud. In a place where I could've easily caught something worse, I suppose I should be thankful I only left with tinnitus.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Really great staff, good food and not far from the heart of The District in downtown. I really enjoyed my meal here and I didn't feel rushed to eat and leave as you do at several other downtown restaurants! I will definitely come back here

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
If you want to eat here so that you can say you did, then go ahead. Otherwise, I would eat elsewhere. 
The service was good. Our waitress was really sweet. 
Food wise, it was average. I've had just as good or even better at any cheaper chain restaurant like Applebee's. 
Sadly, I didn't look at the price of a soft drink and was shocked when I got the bill. $3.79! Maybe in NY City, but Nashville?!?! That's ridiculous. I got the sweet tea. It was actually terrible. I don't mean just average. I mean terrible. 
Husband got hamburger and said it was good. Not great, just good. I paid extra for flavored fries. A complete waste of money! I could barely taste the difference between the regular fries and the "flavored" ones. 
So go buy  a t-shirt in the gift shop and eat somewhere else.

name: Ray Stevens CabaRay Showroom
text: Ray Stevens was amazing. He put on a show with all the hits as well as stories behind them. He is a true entertainer. After the show, Henry with fans which was awesome. His singers even mingled with the crowd after and my five year old son loved them. I highly recommend the show to anyone who is a fan.

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text:
I had a good experience here.  Just one visit, so I'll keep it short - but I liked it and will be back.

The Southwest Salad with chicken (an add-on option) was really excellent.  The chicken was very well seasoned and full of flavor.  I'm not sure what the dressing was, but I supplemented with some of their hot BBQ sauce and it worked really well.

I liked the atmosphere (sat outside) and laid-back attitude, and our server was friendly, quick, and professional.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
We checked into this hotel the night of my birthday. It is a very beautiful establishment, close enough to the city (15 min cab ride to downtown nashville) and far enough from all the craziness.

The check in process was quick and easy, my lady booked a king sized bed room and it was quite a ways from the elevator. Once we walked in our room we realized we got a double bed room, which was not what we asked for, we called the front desk and were told to speak with Hailey.

Hailey took care of us and gave us our king room with an outside deck entrance to their outdoor pool. She also gave us complimentary breakfast buffet passes for our entire stay for the inconvenience, very cool! I told her it's my bday so she also gave us two free passes for cocktails at their lobby bar.

The room was big, great amenities, good working a.c., everything was clean, up to date and also had a mini fridge and a big TV. The outdoor deck was an added bonus, being able to walk to the pool from our bed is always a great way to spend a lazy day. 

This hotel is definitely large, they have cool Johnny cash memorabilia, great amenities like a jacuzzi, an indoor pool past their gym, the outdoor pool, a bar, decent buffet and they also have shuttles to and from the airport. As well as a friendly and helpful staff.

This is definitely a great hotel to stay in even if you want to spend most of your stay in downtown Nashville.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: It is a Hard Rock Cafe in another city. Good for Tourists looking for Nashville stuff in the gift shop. Nothing stands out that I have to say because I live in Nashville. The Hard Rock Cafe in Vegas a different story. I can get collectibles at Walmart in Nashville..so really the tourist location loses it luster here on me. Prices are a bit pricey for average chain food grub. If not a local, maybe stay away. Why pay for parking when you can get average food down the street for free parking. NOW this is NOT to say this is not a place to visit when you visiting Nashville. It has COOL stuff only Nashville will have. If I had someone come to visit and ask specifically about the Hard Rock, of course I would take them. Otherwise, not so much. Not against this place, just not for it as a local.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: To the bouncer that decided to man handle my sister tonight.  What an eye opener that things like this truly can happen to anyone at anytime.  To most a simple, please don't do that would do.  But for him he seemed it necessary to grab her arm and pull her out of the bar with force.  Trust me I am not naive and understand drunk patrons do a lot of things.  But I'm one of many witnesses that will say she was doing nothing wrong.  So I could cuss them out and I could raise my voice but what's the point.  All I ask is for people to realize it's NEVER okay to grab a woman the way he did and I'd say the same thing If he was a man being mistreated.  It's 2018.  Get your shit together.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: The best service ever Chevy was our waitress, she was the bomb!  Very personable,  the Manager was running his Bum off ,  i guess there was a grease fire the day before and so the food was running slow but the Manager on Monday the 26th night wasn't, LOL.  I told my husband i bet when he started this Morning He was 400 lbs. Now Hes just a string bean.   But We spent our 2nd Anniversary there!!!   It was perfect

name: The End.
text: If you're wanting to book a show here, move along. They don't communicate well at all and the last time I put a touring act there, the staff treated them like shit. Always shady about pay too. As an audience member it's just ok.....Nashville has far better places to see live music.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
There is nothing not to love about "The Mother Church of Country Music" As a true fan of country music I am still in awe of this place after my third visit. 

One of Marty's guests, Dale Jett, a relative of the Carter family, absolutly brought the house down IMHO singing the Classic Carter Family song, "Will You Miss me when I'm Gone". This old guy cried his eyes out listening to every word of that song. 

Oh yea, that Stapleton guy was pretty good as well . ;)

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
BLUF: Friendly staff, good music, not a bad place to hang out.

I spent a day wandering around downtown Nashville and ended up spending a good deal of that time at Tin Roof. I came in around 11 to hear Kevin and Luk play (I'd never heard of them prior to this). Despite a little bit of construction work being done on a new stage at the front of the restaurant, they weren't hard to hear at all. They played well and were more than willing to take any requests anyone could throw at them. Unfortunately for them, I was the only one there for the first couple hours and I couldn't think of a single song to ask for, so they were stuck trying to come up with more ideas themselves. 

After just sitting and enjoying the music for a bit, I decided to order some lunch. I had the Rodeo Burger and fries. Everything was good, but nothing to write home about. If you're at Tin Roof for a show it's worth getting something to eat, but it's not a place I'd tell someone to go specifically for their food. 

At around 2:30, I got up and left (Kevin and Luk were still playing, though by this time there were plenty of other customers to hear them) to wander Nashville for a bit. Despite how long I'd been just sitting around with nothing but my water, none of the staff ever seemed impatient or unpleasant with me (probably partially because they weren't particularly busy), which played a large role in why I decided to return later that same day.

I returned around 4:30 to hear the Lower Broadway Band and take advantage of Happy Hour. I don't recall exactly what the discount was, but I know drafts were all cheaper, so I had an Angry Orchard Crisp Apple and a Little Harpeth Brewing Chicken Scratch. I think I paid about $4 each for those, not sure what the normal price is. The bartenders I interacted with were all helpful and quick to offer me another drink when they noticed me finishing up mine, despite the place being packed and extremely loud at that point. After finishing my drinks, I headed out to get dinner elsewhere rather than eat a second meal there.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Nice little divey honkey tonk. Nothing fancy here. Just basic food done right and good music for a good price.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: How can one simply review the Mother Church? The history here is rich and the sound, flawless. Highly recommend catching a show here and having a good look around. Also, buy a limited Hatch Show Print upstairs!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
If you venture into the 'honky tonk' district, and nudge your way through the tourists downtown, then you may find yourself near Robert's Western World.  Here's the deal, most of the nearby honky tonks are pretty miserable for people who really are into music.  I've heard enough fake southern accents from performers in downtown Nashville to turn Hank Williams Sr over in his grave.  Robert's is the rare exception.  The few times I've been here it was crowded with people of all ages, but somehow it didn't seem that hard to get a drink.  The 3-4 different artists Ive heard play here ranged from 'pretty damned talented' to 'holy hell, that guy's about to go viral'.  
  If you don't really give a damn about good music, then there are plenty of downtown options for you and your group of tanked up knucklerumblers.  But if you want to take a chance on hearing that rare performance from someone before they make it really big, the Robert's is your best bet on Broadway.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Easily the best music venue in town, one of the best in the world.  The acoustics are incredible, and the history in this venue is unbelievable.  Do yourself a favor and get there early to take a walk around if you've never been before.  Only complaint is that the seats are pretty uncomfortable, but that's just part of the experience.  10/10 would recommend seeing a show at the Ryman.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
The food was good and our waiter was lovely, but those were the only redeeming parts of our experience at Sinema.

Dinner took almost three hours and the manager seemed unwilling to accept any blame, and only came over to apologize to us after we asked for him. Drinks were extremely overpriced (seriously, $12 for a rail drink?) and dinner wasn't exactly affordable either. The main dining room was extremely dark and the place was practically empty on a Saturday night (not a great sign). There are way better places to spend your money.

name: Legends Corner
text: Bands on both Friday and Saturday night were mediocre at best...Crowded and no room to even walk

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Ok....I was invited to sambuca for a surprise anniversary party which was amazing I have been previously before and it was just as a amazing so you can't got wrong with this restaurant the live band is nice and the restaurant itself is very intimate once I got there I felt a little out of place with everyone having a significant other but I made it work...I ordered the Blackened red snapper etouffee which was delicious and some wine which was great as well our server was very knowledgeable about the menu and very attentive to everyone needs we sat upstairs in the balcony where you can look over the stage it was really nice this is a good place for a perfect date night and enjoy some good music .

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Went here for dinner, drinks, and a live band with my boss and supervisor after work. We got to sit on the main floor in front of the live band and enjoyed a great cover band of country music. Still surprised most of these musicians in downtown live off of tips, so please tip them well. 

Now on to the food and drinks that we ordered. I had the local brewery's beer, Yazhoo Hop IPA, which was a good craft beer that I've had in the past. But please note that all the beers served here are in bottles. NO DRAFT BEER. Not a big minus but I do prefer draft over bottle. The price of the beer was also good for bottle beer, ranging from $4 to $6.50

The food menu was very short and simple but good selections of western traditional food. My supervisor got the burger, which he noted was really great. And my boss and I ordered the fried bologna with cheese. Wow! was it great. The guest who's table we took after they paid, made the recommendation to order this sandwich and glad we listened to them. In order to have a reference of what this sandwich would taste like think of a grilled cheese with bologna or ham. It was a really great blend of flavor. For the three of us with two beers each we paid only $30. Order this and enjoy!

name: Legends Corner
text: Love this place! Great music and drinks! Will definitely be back. John Karl sang while we were there. He was awesome!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Appetizers: 
- Smoked Salmon
- Shrimp & Crab Dip

Entree: 
- Sea Bass

Dessert:
- Cheesecake

One of the best meals I've had.  Couldn't stop eating.  The music was a nice backdrop to the meal.  One of the more expensive places that I've been, but certainly worth a visit.  I visited on a business trip, so I got my money's worth!

name: Musicians Corner
text:
This is such a wonderful event that appeals to people of all ages and musical tastes. Although we attended on a rainy day (May 30), we had a wonderful time. The rain probably prevented a lot of people from coming, so we were able to easily find parking and a picnic table for our group of 8. We moved the table under a tree to protect us (and our food) from the off and on again rain. 

There were about 8 food trucks there offering a range of food from barbecue, burgers and grilled cheese sandwiches to ice cream and snow cones. The lines were not long, again thanks to the rain, so we were able to get our food in about 15 minutes. Although I was not familiar with any of the musical acts, I thoroughly enjoyed all the music that ranged from indie pop to folk. 

They have a wonderful kids area that is roped off, providing lots of room for kids to run around and play. They had a variety of toys including balls, hula hoops and big, soft toys for the younger kids and toddlers. There was also a craft table set up where the kids could make pictures. Although I don't have kids, there were several in our group, and that was such a nice area for them. 

I also enjoyed browsing the artisan booths selling jewelry, home decor and clothing, to name a few. This is a free event and well worth visiting. The Spring series takes place from 12-5:30 every Saturday and ends the weekend of June 27, with a Sunday event on the 28th as well.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Food is a bit pricey for what you get, but the ambience and live music make up for it. I had a very enjoyable time. Ordered the beignets (wow! what a contrast in taste and I forgot they were filled by the time they arrived), the crab dip (awesome), and 2 other appetizers that I can't remember now. For entrees, I got the sea bass, while my friend got the chili scallops. Both were quite delicious, although the portions were smaller than expected.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: First time in a long time I ate at Sambucca. It hast changed much which is both good and not so good.  I had the scallops which were good not great.  I did like the artichoke app we had but not so much the lobster app. Our server was really good considering there was 8 of us.  He stayed on top of the drinks and was there when you needed him.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
It's clean and nice enough, but WAY overpriced. Get over yourselves. As a statistic test sample I bought 7 Dewars White Scotch and this one was $11! 

By far the highest, and the environment was just ok. Go to Tootsies or Crazy Town. Much better prices. Get over yourself Tin Roof

name: Robert's Western World
text: Average bar venue, with entertainment,  to get a "quick" (*see below), bite to eat for lunch downtown. Busy place, nothing fancy, nothing real special. Seating on bar stools at small tables, or at the bar. Their fried bologna sandwich is their signature. They were training a new cook, and it took almost 45 minutes to get our food. This may not be the place to go, if you are in a rush! Or I just caught them on a "bad day."

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This music is what we came to Nashville to hear!  John England and the Western Swingers were playing. Oh my gosh, what a great group. This place is the real deal.
Food wise - okay. We had chicken strips and onion rings. The O rings were great, chicken strips were okay. We did not come for the food, but it was okay. The music was awesome!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This is one of my favorite bars on Broadway. Came here last night for the first time in a lonnnng time and was reminded why I love this place so much. Great music, two story bar (which is awesome and you don't feel trapped like a sardine), and awesome drinks! We popped in and were all able to order our drinks in a timely manner, which was surprising because it was a busy Saturday night. Beer is super cheap and overall, a really fun place to come with visitors and friends!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Visiting the "Mother Church Of Country Music" was a must for me on my to-do list while in Nashville. That said,  it was definitely fun to see all of the back stage dressing rooms where legendary artists like Dolly Parton, Elvis, Johnny Cash spent their time getting ready before the show, having the opportunity to take a picture on the stage (which came at an extra fee I might add) but it was certainly not the highlight of my trip. Fun? Yes. Rich in history? Sure. 

I suggest you visit the Ryman to watch a show and get a real Country experience rather than touring the place. 

$20 admission.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This is my favorite spot on Broadway. 
Best music and friendly staff.  First time to Nashville and Robert's band was the best !

name: Robert's Western World
text: Mixed feelings about this one. Great entertainer- had a more fun approach to his singing than most of the bands on Broadway. Nice atmosphere. Food was very slow. We ordered onion rings and chicken strips and it took a while which was disappointing. They were hot when we got em though! Only had one or two cooks so I get it but unfortunately we stepped in to Robert's for something fast. Our mistake. But like I said, fun atmosphere

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Hot damn! This place is so action packed! Great food, uplifting music, and entertainment everywhere! Must check this out. Something for everyone!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I toured the Ryman about a month ago and it was very informative! Last night I went to my first concert there to see Bryan Adams bare bones show. The venue is amazing and the acoustics are second to none! Will definitely try to see another show there in the future!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Located steps from the famed Ryman Auditorium, Robert's Western World is the quintessential Honky Tonk where many up and coming Country Music stars have cut their teeth, Upon a recent visit, I had the privilege of watching studio musicians jamming to some classic country numbers - some of which they actually played on during the original recordings. A highlight of the evening was witnessing one of Elvis's background singers step on to stage and sing a rendition of Suspicious Minds which elevated the already high level of quality music. Check Robert's Western World out on the Broadway strip for good beer, good people and great music!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Ja var börjar man sin beskrivning angående denna legendariska konsertlokal. Kort är det i den här f.d. kyrkan som country musiken utvecklades och frodades under flera decennier (då Grand Ole Opry höll till här).

Alla klassiska country artister som hade karriärer under 40-50-60-70 talen har spelat här och oftast själva varit begaistrade av det faktum att de platsade att beträda denna anrika scen. Om man tilläts framträda här, så var oftast en country musik artists lycka gjord. Ett bevis på att du och din musik var accepterade, beundrade och älskad.

Men något regelrätt museum har det lyckligtvis inte omvandlats till och att leva på gamla meriter duger som bekant inte i dessa dagar. Så desto mer glädjande att man fortfarande har världsartist bokade här. Akustiken och intimiteten är rena lyckan för både artister och vi i publiken.

Om du har möjligheten så se gärna en live konsert här. Annars kan man besöka under dagtid och bara gå runt och se både de underbara lokalerna och diverse montrar med historiska material. Möjlighet finns även att få en guidad rundtur i logerna bakom scenen och själv få stå på den klassiska scenen och låta sig fotograferas bakom mikrofonen (de lånade t.o.m. ut en gitarr till mig för det ändamålet).

name: Legends Corner
text: En original bar - det er her legenderne opdages, en fantastisk stemning og man bliver nemt revet med. Vi var 3 gutter der havde en fantastisk aften, den går aldrig i glemmebogen. De bands der spillede var både autentiske og gode (vi var andre steder hvor kvaliteten var knap så god) - stemningen kunne få selv den ringeste drink til at smage godt...

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Very nice steaks but still a bit pricey. Service from Dimi was excellent and personable. We had no alcohol and split a dessert and saved some money. Trying to avoid sugar and carbs. Rachel Rodriguez and her band started playing and she was incredible. We should have stayed longer but headed back in the rain to the hotel around the corner. Most of Nashville seemed out of town for the Christmas holiday. We may come back but there are so many good restaurants in Nashville, it really had to be outstanding to want us to come back. I would come back for drinks and music.

name: Legends Corner
text: IDK, overproduced band didn't know what they wanted to play. Pop country at it's best prefer the other places on the block.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: The music brought us in this place. We ordered a drink each and kept the tab open thinking we would stay for the music and have more drinks. We closed the tab and left after one drink. The drinks were not good, don't think there was any vodka in my vodka soda. Bartender was on his phone the whole time. Go somewhere else! Lots of other choices with good music and better service and better drinks.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Flight Cancelled...you're stuck in Nashville for a night.  Get in a cab, tell them you want to get your honky tonk on and arrive at Robert's.  Then have a fantastic night!  So goes my story. 

Good music, cheap beer, good music, limited food selection, good music,. 

I don't even like country music and I had a great time and thought the music was great.  I would recommend it and go back in a second if I were in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Cold beer, burgers, fries, amazing onion rings, good band.  

Touristy for sure, me included...but a lot of fun!

Food took a bit to get but the crowd was huge. 

This place is everything that I expected and hoped for for my first trip to Nashville

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Went with friends before an evening at TPAC and it was delightful!

We started with the goat cheese stuff artichoke - a combo I have never had but really enjoyed!

My table companions had the shrimp, the veggie lasagna, and the chili-rubbed scallops, and they all munched way quite happily.  The scallops were a very pretty dish - with risotto "discs" under each scallop that had been shaped and seared to resemble scallops too. fun.
I went with a Gorgonzola salad (sooo good) and then the 3-side combo because the sides all looked so good.  The crunch broccoli was good, but I wish they said onions and peppers in the description (not my fav), the prosciutto mac and cheese was creamy goodness. but the BRUSSELS SPROUTS - oh my, wish I'd gotten 3 of those.  If you like Brussels sprouts, you must try! and if you don't THINK you like them, this might just change your mind.

For dessert we shared the Sticky Toffee Pudding...and wow, it was amazing.  Not too sweet, almost a savory bread pudding with warm toffee inside---man, out of this world.

Great service from Matthew and we made it to the show on time.

The was a light rock band (sorry did not catch the name) that was really excellent as well.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Need a quick burger. The burger is good enough  but the band was a pleasant surprise- for somebody who visits Nashville for the first time and has her first full meal in the city. Lovely posters too

name: Robert's Western World
text: Good bar with excellent band. Not too crowded. Drinks reasonable.  Good service.  Highly recommend.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: This place is a such a great addition to Nashville. I was very impressed when we went here for lunch with some friends. They have a large food court area with lots of different food options. I loved the live music and rich culture of Plaza Mariachi. You can tell that a lot of time, money and care went into building this place. My favorite part would definitely be the the popsicles. No explanation needed - they are amazing! This is a perfect spot for friends and families to go and enjoy good food, drinks and music!

name: Music City Center
text:
What a great venue. I've been to a view events here, most recently being the auto show. Now it does suck they jack up pricing for parking for "special events." It's normally $6 to park, but they charge $15 for anything going on. It was convenient parking in the garage and we didn't have far to walk to go inside. It's really a spacious place with tons of light, cool light fixtures and state of the art facilities. The main space is HUGE! Hence, the auto show was there! Now, I didn't see any food options. We were so thirsty from walking around and when I went up to the concession stand, they were "closing" at 3pm when there were 2 more hours of the show left. Just know that going in, bring your water bottle! Convenient to Omni and Country Music Hall of Fame. This place has really cleaned up that side of Broadway and put Nashville on the map in terms of attracting good shows and conferences. 
Great place!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
This place is a cool divey Honky Tonk Bar and Grill! It stays packed, does not charge a cover, considers itself to be the "Home of Traditional Country Music". Keep in mind it is very popular and stays crowded. Be prepared for a wait to get inside. Robert's Western World is a unique Nashville treasure that boasts great live country bands, cheap but decent drinks, ridiculously low priced food at the Honky Tonk Grill with beer specials (such as the $5 Stimulus Package - all beef hot dog, chips, & Miller Lite and $5 Recession Special - a fried bologna sandwich, chips & PBR), and an array of interesting people mingling with each other. 

The coolest feature for me was the upstairs area that overlooks the entire bottom half of the bar and stage. The dim and red lit area has plenty of seating and standing areas that have great vantage points of the entire place. I also learned that the top floor has a back exit that is less congested than the front. I was surprised to find that most bars on Broadway have back entrances and exits. As the folks in Nashville say, "Always leave out the back door when your bar hopping downtown!"

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
First time seeing a show here.  Not even a CM fan but man, this was a very cool experience.  I enjoyed every minute. Even the dude doing the radio commercials was pleasant to listen to.  Very professionally executed.  Congrats on 90 years GOO!  And Cheers to all the amazing staff that give people great entertainment for their hard earned money.
Almost forgot to mention, when you purchase your tickets be sure you avoid obstructed view.  Happened to be a live screening this past Friday evening and cameraman was blocking 50% of our view.   Staff gladly moved us to the front pews and we were very pleased.  Thank you for that !

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great band with an awesome variety of songs; friendly staff ready to make your experience great; good, affordable drinks; awesome atmosphere on Broadway. A fabulous find on our Friday night out exploring Broadway in search of bars with live music. A must do for all on broadway. No cover- so tip the staff & musicians!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: The wife and I sat near the stage area. The band they had was totally amazing! The band's name was the Chris Weaver Band. The food was decent. The drinks were okay as well. But what got us was the air conditioning seem to be out when were there last Friday night! It was extremely hot inside. We don't like eating hot food when the thermostat is set to Hell. We were sweating profusely! We only come here occasionally and parking is valet tip plus $5.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Here on s Friday night. Overcrowded. Took well over 30 minutes for any  music and the and the band to come on....awkward silence for a good amount of time

name: Robert's Western World
text:
If you want to hear quality, traditional Western Swing and Country (the music on which Nashville was built), this is your place. 

Always a good band, and if you don't like them, a new one will take the stage in about an hour. 

But you'll like 'em all

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Fun fun fun! We just stopped in for a beer and stayed for 4 hours! The music was awesome, and the service was spot on.,we will be going back today!

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text: Went to Douglas Corner Cafe  on 11/2/13 with group of 14, ranging in ages from 21 - 75.  Saw Rich Fagan, Bobby E. Boyd and Pamela McNeill.   We loved every minute!  The music was fantastic and the DCC staff was great.  The place may be no frills and the menu limited but don't let that stop you.   Douglas Corner Cafe is a real gem.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Probably one of the finest acoustic settings in the country. Unique seating on wooden pews (surprisingly comfortable) that stretches wide so there are many great seats. A formidable lineup of outstanding acts. The snack stand had some terrific popcorn prepackaged fresh in boxes. And they also had cocktails, beer and wine, as well as other treats that you can take into the theatre. I would look for an excuse to come here again!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
AMAZING! Best venue I've ever been to for live music. Beautiful, historical building with gorgeous stained glass, great views from pretty much everywhere. Cool church-pew-like seats, not much legroom but whatevs, it's a cool and nostalgic form of seating. We sat in the balcony, which I had read had the best views, and I definitely agree -- even the back seats would be fine. Awesome acoustics as well. Just an overall great musical experience with some Music City historical charm thrown in. 
[Boring info: There's a gift shop on the first floor with country music/Nashville stuff, and refreshments for sale somewhere that I didn't use. I can't speak to the restrooms as I didn't use them either. No parking that I know of; we took a Lyft.] 
LOVE IT!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
If you're visiting in the winter as we are, then the Opry is held at Ryman Auditorium and you're very lucky. The sound is amazing and the intimate vibe of the place, incompatible. 

We've never been to a show like this and we've been to a lot of show. The line up was great - four sections each with two acts and a host. In between acts there are announcements as it is after all a radio show and they have to plug their sponsors. Bill Anderson was a brilliant host for the second quarter, very charming.

We feel very lucky to have seen the variety of talent we did. From artists who've been Opry members for 30, 40 years to artists on their second Opry bill. The standout was Chris Jansen who I wish if heard more from but will look him up. He had fantastic energy. Artists feel very honoured to play this show and you can tell, this is one of the highest accomplishments you can have as a country performer. That makes for a brilliant vibe, the fact that they all want so much to be there.

What an amazing show. An absolute joy.

name: Legends Corner
text:
Great location for a drink and country music. Never know who may show up on the stage. Food service is minimal pizzas from a warming oven. They get 4 stars only for the history and music that they provide. All entertainers play for tips which is common for the area. Many of these performers are looking for a start in the music industry. The ambience is the draw that will grab you when you visit. 
Evenings get very crowed so go during the day.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We visited Robert's on a Friday night in Nashville over Spring Break - it was packed but we had a great night, watching the house band Brazilbilly and soaking up the atmosphere. Will definitely return if we're back in the area, This is a Nashville must-see.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
The beer is ice cold and the servers are friendly. It's a very limited menu even for a bar so I wouldn't plan on a full "meal" here, more along the lines of "snacks" with my drinks while I'm listening to the live music. 

With my cold beer and the live music I grabbed the Pollo Del Sol Quesadilla which was really good - just because the menu is very limited doesn't mean that what it does have on it will not be tasty! 

Thumbs up!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Although we do not hit the night life as much as we used too...we love swing dancing and Sunday night is the night to go to Sambuca!!! Our favorite band is Patton James and the Synchromatics but every Sunday night the place has a group of regulars that go to all the dance stops around town and Sambuca has a great swing band on Sunday nights. If we are up for dancing and an evening out and wishing to catch some old dance friends, we go to Sambuca.

name: Second Fiddle
text: I was visiting for CMA fest 2015. This place had great music, beer, and friendly staff. I would definitely recommend this place to a friend. We had a lot of fun at The Second Fiddle and look forward to going back when we come back to Nashville.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
This classy plaza is basically a mini mall with essentially an upscale food court (Greek, Latin, coffee shop, juice bar) and several shops (boutiques, grocery market with fresh meats/seafood, hot food & small pharmacy, restaurant, art gallery, spa). Looking forward to more shops here.

Live entertainment in the food court - Latin music, fire juggler, and aerial dancer. You can have a beer and walk around the plaza.

The outside is well landscaped with seating areas in center green space and awesome outside bar off the main restaurant. Plenty of free parking.

Kid and stroller friendly. Tito's is in the plaza too which is an arcade and has kid slide. There is a private event room there also for parties.

Happy to have this addition to our neighborhood!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Pretty ridiculous place, cheap beers and alot of fun.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Just had appetizers and drinks for happy hour, both were very good.  We recommend the cheese beignets and the shrimp/crab dip.

Wish we had found this place earlier would have liked to catch one of the weekend bands.  Great stage & dance floor area.

name: Legends Corner
text:
Love, love, loved it! I stopped by with my girlfriends on a Sunday night, and we had the best time. 

As a 30-something Nashville visitor, I felt overwhelmed by a lot of the honkeytonks with their long lines and cramped spaces. Legends was roomy, the people were friendly, and the band was awesome. I couldn't get enough of the singer's voice and she fulfilled as many requests as possible. She even dealt with a drunk heckler who was on a mission to hear "Sweet Home Alabama."

I would absolutely return on my next visit.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great music and food it was expensive but I think it was better than Ruth Chris! Our waiter knew the answer to all my questions and had recommendations on what food was best. Would love to go back soon. I had the sea bass and my boyfriend had the pork chop we had the chuterie  appetizer. Highly reccomend!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Ordered a drink, the waitress never came back with it and ignored our table for a good 30 minutes. We left. I'll never come back

name: Legends Corner
text: Favorite honky tonk on Broadway. We caught Buck McCoy on Saturday afternoon and loved it so much, we went back and saw him again on Sunday.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We took the backstage tour that was excellent!  Our guide really knew his stuff!  This place is amazing!  I could feel the presence of all the old acts that used to grace the stage.  It's kind of how you feel when you go to Arlington Cemetery or Little Big Horn!  Don't miss the video either...it was fabulous!  I am so glad we got to go in. I wished we could have seen a show there. Do not miss seeing this place!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I don't think i fully understood or appreciated the fact that I was going to a performance at Ryman Auditorium. Arriving early and getting an opportunity to walk around the outside and start to take in some of the historical markers.....Birth of Bluegrass for starters. Going on to explain that in 1945 Bill Monroe and his mandolin brought to the Ryman Auditorium stage a band that created a new American musical form. As you start absorbing everything that has happened here the realization sets in that this is going to truly be a unique experience at one of the most historical venues.

As you walk in there is an amazing gift store with all kinds of commemorative items to satisfy almost any collectors souvenir needs. 

The staff was phenomenal and eager to help any way they could. From the aisle attendants to the bartenders to the souvenir stands they all were happy and smiling throughout the night.

As Paramore took the stage to close out their tour in their hometown and Haley Williams leaned down to kiss the stage before performing, it became very evident that this place is also very special to the performers that come through. 

I had a seat in the upper balcony, and couldn't have been more pleased. I think it's safe to say there isn't a bad seat in the place! Sound quality is amazing and the stage is plenty large enough to accommodate elaborate band set ups.

So glad that I was able to finally come to Ryman and attend such an amazing performance. Wouldn't hesitate to come back and attend another event in the future. If you haven't been you really need to add this to a list of musts....it's something that should be experienced by everyone!

name: Robert's Western World
text: A must see in Nashville! Amazing live music...the band was so good I almost converted to country music :) great decor also...boots showcased on one side of the wall and country music memorabilia all over.  Best part of my trip to Nashville! I wanna come back for more and walk down Broadway to check out all the live music bars and venues!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Classic honky tonk. If you like old school country music - think George Jones and Buck Owens - hit this spot late night. The house band is really fantastic and knows about any paid request you put in to them. Dance your heart out with anyone nearby - know 'em or not. Great service you won't go thirsty. Good bar food. 

Oh, and be sure to tip the band as well as your server! Nashville is a no cover town. Tips are how they make a living providing great country music entertainment.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Yes, the Ryman is historic. Yes, it has hosted many many musical legends. Yes, the place offers a lovely aesthetic that many other musical venues in Nashville hold, but despite all this, I wasn't crazily impressed by it. 

From the perspective of a concert goer, I felt the way they have us congregating into the place is a bit disorienting. There were no defined lines. The person checking purses did not do a thorough job of inspecting them. They do have a metal detector, but I just didn't feel the security of the place was very strong. That makes me nervous when going into large scale venues in this day and age. 

Again, this is just personal preference, but the pews inside are painful to sit in for long extended periods of time. I value the originality to maintain the integrity of the venue and being that it is what came with the Ryman when it was first established. As someone who loves historical architecture, I value this very much! But, my back wasn't having it at all and it really sucked sitting there for 2.5 hours. Take an anti-inflammatory before you roll in there if you also have back issues. The entire venue has pews for seating. When the Ryman was first built, it was created as a tabernacle. 

Expect price gouging. A soda or bottled water will run you $5. Sorry, but not sorry and no thanks. I am cheap when it comes to that I guess. I just can't justify it in my mind. 

Parking around the venue is rough $10-$20 in parking garages or paved lots. I parked a few blocks away in a free spot and walked in the cold wet rain to get there. I just wasn't going to do that. Next time, I will likely uber and save myself the pain altogether, but at the time this seemed the most practical. 

On an ending note, the Ryman really is a pretty place. It is a historic relic to downtown Nashville and has cemented itself into the fabric of the music scene of the city. I value it for its history and integrity, not practicality.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: horrible service. literally stood in front of a male bartender as he served at least 4 men before finally asking for my order. and the 3 of the men had just walked up. the area where you stand to listen to the band/dance is SO small. the indianapolis location is better!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: We love coming to Plaza Mariachi with friends to enjoy the music, atmosphere, and the food.  Our one gripe is the price of the alcohol.  My friends ordered two shots of tequila, and almost fainted when the waitress said $26.  Of course, they paid as requested, but it sure put a bad taste in their mouth for ordering alcohol while enjoying the other things offered at this wonderful venue.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Best bar on Broadway!  Make sure Slick Joe Fick is playing, he's the show!!!  Great bologna sandwich too!  Drink prices are the same as the other bars -- high -- considering the bar isn't paying the band, they work for tops.  Kind of a sweet deal for the bar owners!  Regardless, it's a great place with great music!!!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: OMG. Such good food! Kinda pricey but totally worth it! My son and I were starving and had nachos, steak tacos, chicken tacos (we both liked the steak better but they ran out), and burritos. After he ate, my son enjoyed the arcade. I enjoyed the live music while he played. Awesome family atmosphere, and great adult fun at night. There were dessert and gyro vendors too, although we didn't try them yet; too full off the Mexican food!!! They also had some shoppes where you could buy trinkets and t-shirts, etc. Way better than the Kroger that used to be in this retail space!!! We live close and will be back!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
On a recent trip to Nashville we were looking for a good Honky Tonk to bring kids to in the afternoon. Robert's Western World was perfect. It had a different feel than many of the shinier bars lining Broadway.

John Shepherd, who has been performing for decades, was on stage taking requests, with encyclopedia knowledge of country music. We sat next to his wife Lois, and enjoyed the show.

Beer is cheap, and the food is surprisingly good. I had the recession special, including a fried bologna sandwich. The sandwich was actually really good. 

I would come back, just a comfortable classic atmosphere.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
Of all the places I hit up on Broadway, Tin Roof was my least favorite.  

At risk of sounding like an old lady, this place was just too loud.  The band was both bad and deafening when we went on a Friday afternoon.  We opted for the bar upstairs in order to avoid losing hearing at a premature age.

Once we got upstairs, the service pretty much sucked.  I'm not sure if the bartenders were in between shifts or ours was just plain disinterested.  At any rate, getting our beers from him proved to be a lackluster experience.

The one pro for Tin Roof was surprisingly the food.  The pork nachos were very solid bar food.  You can't really mess that up I suppose, and after hitting up several other honky tonks before, they were just what the doctor ordered.

Tin Roof wasn't the worst bar I've ever been to by any means, but it was definitely my least favorite of the honky tonks I visited on Broadway.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Wow what a place. Went to the Grand Ole Opry at the Ryman and loved every min of it. Sat in the upper part dead center. Great seats. The music was just what i thought it would be. Its so cool being there and soaking in the history of the building. If you have a chance go while at the Ryman. Little Jimmy Dickens came on and had the eveyone rolling in the floor. He's a funny guy.

visited in Nov 2011

name: Robert's Western World
text: Very busy, slow service and average burgers. Great music and party environment. The entertainment is more of a reason to visit than the food. Amazing people and if you just want to have a few drinks with friends and experience true Honky Tonk Nashville then this is the place.

name: Robert's Western World
text: If you truly want to experience Nashville, this spot is pure gold! My companion and I stopped in for all of 20 minutes prior to heading to a concert at The Ryman and it was overwhelmingly my favorite part of the whole evening. (And that's saying a lot). We had already eaten at some utterly forgettable tourist-trap restaurant down the street (take a look at my other reviews if you're curious to see which one), and I would've given my kneecaps to have sidled up to the bar and ordered an anything-but-fancy burger and a beer here instead, if for no other reason than to soak up the atmosphere. The music was some of the best live music I've ever heard (and it was a Wednesday night!) and the ambience is unbeatable. It's a dive, but a dive with some serious soul! It will be a "must" for any pilgrimages to Music City I make in the future.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I feel like the Ryman and Opry are a must see for any country music fan visiting Nashville.

The Ryman is smaller and has less comfortable seats than the Opry. But the smaller venue makes it feel like a more intimate show.

I was lucky enough to see Vince Gill in the Bluegrass series on my first ever visit to the Ryman. He put on a phenomenal show.

I was unlucky enough to be sitting behind a tall guy with a broad frame...glad my husband didn't mind me invading his space because I was really excited to see Vince.

It's a great experience, beautiful building, fun atmosphere. Worth your time and money.

Would have loved to tour it but they weren't offering any guided tours on the weekend we visited. You don't get as much from the self guided tour plus Nashville requires a lot of walking and we were pooped.

name: Douglas Corner Cafe
text: Fabulous spot for live music! Came here for a record release "Nashlantis" and absolutely loved the venue- has great vibes and the acoustics are outstanding. I'm not much of a beer drinker- so I ordered the "Blue persuasion"- it was delicious- our sever Sheree was so nice and friendly as was her sister Rhonda who was behind the bar. They both were friendly and helpful- even loaned me a sharpie to get a shirt signed. If You have the opportunity- go- listen to some great live music and have a beverage or two!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This is fantastic venue..... historic, intimate, great acoustics, lots of reasons to come here. But I gave Ryman 1 star to get their attention and possibly spare others from the same angst we had. 

We travelled 500 miles to Nashville to see Ringo and His All Star Band for nostalgia. We were stunned by the unexpected exceptional musicianship. These aging top notch performers haven't lost their touch and are still incredibly at the top of their game!!! I'm in my 60's and this was the best concert I was ever at!!!  

The reason for the 1 star..... my companion forget the tickets she bought on stubhub. Though we had photos showing the barcode in our phones, we tried to avoid a potential situation by calling the theater and even going there in person prior to the concert to ensure they would let us in. We repeatedly offered to leave should anyone else claim our seats (of course that couldn't happen unless the stubhub seller scammed us). The Ryman staff was downright unhelpful and insisted that we had have the stubhub tickets physically in our hands to get into the theater. This soured my companion's mood for the day as they could easily have made this a non-event. As it turned out, we got in line at show time, showed the scanned tickets on our phones and went right in without a getting any attention. 

Shame on you Ryman there was no reason to treat us this way!!!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text:
Here in Music City we are richly blessed with an over abundance of fine restaurants, but just as people mistakenly think of Nashville's music scene as Country, it would be similarly egregious to overlook the wonderful ethnic eating experiences on offer by focusing solely on the fine dining establishments. 
Plaza Mariachi promises to make a party from an evening of casual dining. 
The moment we arrived live music was playing throughout the parking lot from the stage inside hosting Songwriters Night. 
Stepping into this converted grocery store you're virtually transported to a cozy village square with cafe hemming it's edges much more so than a food court. 
They're still filling in a number of the mall shops with tenants but you can already tell from the early entrants that they're committed to making your visit an enjoyable one. 
I'm looking forward to my next trip back there to pick up some special items from the MazFresco Market & you have to stop by Paletas Tocumbo for some of their homemade ice creams, just be sure to leave some Coconut for me.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I would give no stars if I could! We were there last week and they had NO WORKING BATHROOMS and people were still going in the bathrooms and the men were using the women's because the men's was horrible!! The staff was told and shrugged it off and said the manager was notified and not doing anything about it. I can't believe in such a touristy area they would allow such filth and unsanitary conditions .

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great food and amazing customer services.  The restaurant's atmosphere was very classy and the music performance was beautiful with a mixture of Blues and Jazz. We ordered a lot of food and drinks. The Scallop dish and the shrimp/crab dip were amazing! Their drinks were on point and we ordered two rounds of drinks which doesn't happen often. The only downside was some of the shrimps were slightly overcooked. Even so, our server and manager were very attentive and they didn't charge us for the specific dish. Their desserts were delicious! I highly recommended this restaurant and we will come back again!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We decided to follow a friend's recommendation while in Nashville for a quick trip for a wedding - I am SO glad we did! While it isn't in the downtown area, it was certainly worth the drive.
