The biscuits lived up to their billing and the veggies were fresh and delicious. Unfortunately, we did not have room for dessert, but be sure you get some when you go. If you're in the neighborhood, treat yourself to a good meal - but order dessert before your meal since they run out quickly.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Excellent! I had the bbq pork omelet.  Their biscuits are great! 

Well worth the wait, there's plenty to do on their property while you're waiting.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Super great breakfast spot! Love the drop biscuits and the jam was good too! Portion size was ample and service was excellent! No complaints at all- really enjoyed this spot.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Absolutely LOVE this place! We had a party for a travel hockey team this past Saturday, and everything was perfect.  Our waitress Tia did a fantastic job taking care of 16 adults and even more 10-11 year old kids always with a smile on her face.  Highly recommended

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
My best friend and I enjoyed our brunch meal at Loveless Cafe. 

We're tourists and made this our "on our way out of town" meal since we knew Loveless is known for having long waits (and especially on a Sunday!). We had a party of two and were quoted a 1 hr. and 20 min. wait time - and we waited exactly that! We had no problem, though. After all, we had nothing to do but drive back home that Sunday. It also helped us work up an appetite! 

I want to give the brunette hostess her props, she kept a smiling face on and greeted every guest that walked in with a positive attitude and smile. I know that for myself, that would've been hard considering she deals with person after person, same question after same question! 

The biscuits definitely lived up to expectations! They had a sweet taste - different than biscuits you'd get from Cracker Barrel or your typical southern restaurant. Don't fill up on them, though! The food is where it's at. 

Cons: Not a lot of waiting room in the actual restaurant building which sucked when it rained, however, there were plenty of places on property to walk around and look at while bored waiting. Unfortunately, rain doesn't make for good photo opportunities outside so that was unfortunate. 

TIP: They don't take reservations on weekends. Get there early.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great food, and fabulous service! The hostess was very welcoming, and our server was on it! Just expect a wait time almost anytime of the day, especially on weekends. We ended up waiting only 20 minutes on a weekday around 2pm. On Sunday we went for brunch and it was over an hour wait. But that's to be expected at such a popular place. What's great is that as you wait, you can walk around the property to the shops and so forth!

name: Dirty Little Secret
text: I spent enough time in here to determine that I wouldn't want to come back. I attended an after party here after a gala I attended. Drinks were pricey and music were terribly weak, security mayhem ensued, and left little to care to remember. I can't say that this is something I would want to return to. Believe me when I say there is no secret to the fact that this place did leave me feeling dirty because of the money spent on weak mixed booze.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I had looked forward to going here for months since I heard it was opening. I was so disappointed when I did. First off it took nearly five minutes before I could get a server and it wasn't even the one responsible for our table. Then the server that was supposed to be ours decides to show up with teas that we didn't even order but not our beers. The the Doner Kebab that I do loved in Germany and was on the online menu was no longer available. I was so upset I just walked out.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food was so good. The service was pleasant and fast. Everyone was well trained and seemed to work as a team. The fast paced flow was flawless and uncompromising. When you get good service and you see good service being presented it makes your meal that more enjoyable.  I had steak and eggs. The cook or someone from the kitchen brought my meal out with a smile and seemed to have great pleasure in presenting her plate. The food was delicious.  When you have a great steak you don't need sauce.  That's blasphemous.  While the steak could have used a little more seasoning for my taste, it was still good and I did not grab the A1 bottle.  What can be said about the biscuits and jam that hasn't already been said. mmmmm...Heaven!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Really wanted to like this little place, however it is overrated. The wait was 2hrs. Bathroom needed cleaning to the point I had to go outside to get some fresh air. On top of that once I received my food there was a long strand of dark hair fried into my fried green tomatoes. Biscuits were great!! If it wasn't for the waitress being attentive, I would have given this place 1 star. Beware. Find a Cracker Barrel. Not worth the wait at all.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: They had me at wine on tap. I came in on a Monday night for dinner and was excited to find that parking was free. This is usually not the case although valet is $5-8. There was no wait and we were quickly seated and quickly wined. Our server was fantastic and knowledgable about wine. I ordered the lamb shank osso bucco with vegetable root hash. It was perfectly fall off the bone.  My partner in crime had the trout on a bed of raisin couscous that was good but not quite to the level of the osso bucco. Im excited to learn that City Winery allows you to buy the wine on tap in a growler type (but clearly not) fashion. I recommend trying the Obsidian Ridge Cab Sauv on tap.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
So I have been back another time since the glaad concert. Again to see Meghan Linsey. Surprise surprise.

The second time was Meghan Linsey with Sawyer Fredericks.

Parking this time was not nearly as wonderful as last. I waited and waited and waited by the valet station - where they were all standing and fetching cars for others from the show prior... And no dice. I would estimate 15-20 minutes before I reversed enough to turn my car around to leave. 

Luckily there was a spot within walking distance as it was raining. Still strange no one wanted my money... And I always too well...

Again the seats were excellent. I was at a table next to the stage. Three seats in. With a group of acquaintances and some strangers. The tables are long so you're often mixed up close with people you don't know... But I didn't find it too bothersome. 

The guy next to me ordered a few cokes and some sort of appetizer. I had a glass of wine.

Why am I mentioning what this stranger next to me ordered? Because it appeared on my tab and was unable to be taken off.

I waited a long time to do this review on purpose. As the review is not about getting it fixed. But about the attitude at the time. As though I was lying about this single male next to me not being with me because I was a single female. 

The venue is still nice. Service seems to have gone down on most accounts.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This place is alright! The location and atmosphere allow for a fun place to get together with a big group where you can chat loudly without having to worry about bothering anyone around you. On Friday nights they have live german music which is fun. I ordered the chicken schnitzel sandwich and wasn't too big of a fan. It was okay, but I probably wouldn't order it again. The fries were good though! My husband got the currywurst and loved it. The prices here are pretty high compared to similar places around. Overall, not too bad!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This is in the Opry mills mall.  Good beer drinking environment with the layout consisting of octoberfest tables and the liter beer mugs.  A German style band was playing while we were there making a fun interactive environment. The food on the other hand is mediocre at best.  I am German and was hoping for some decent German dumplings and sauerkraut.  Neither were very good at all.  So this is why they only get 3 stars from me.  Step up the food game and I would give a 4.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Southern cooking at its finest!!!
Biscuits and jams to die for! The best catfish I've ever had! 
Food came out quick and hot!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Would recommend to anyone! No wait. Food was out quickly and delicious at that! Friendly staff and homey environment. They have the best biscuits in the entire world. Great price for the amount of food we got!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: First time in Nashville had to make the short drive to the Loveless. It reached and surpassed our expectations! A definite must see and do for anyone visiting. Our wait time for a table was less than ten minutes. The atmosphere is incredible and our server was so sweet. The food is good old country diner fare  and the biscuits are great. They must be because they make 7000 a day. Thanks Loveless for making our first stop in Nashville one of the most memorable.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The food that I ordered made this cafe seem very overrated. I picked up my friend from the airport and we drove 30 minutes to the restaurant. Luckily, we didn't have to wait, probably given that we were there at 8am on a Friday morning.

The biscuits were indeed delicious, and they were so buttery that there was no need to spread butter on them. The homemade jams were also yummy. However, the fried chicken that came with the waffle was neither juicy nor tender. Rather, it was dry and overcooked.

Not sure if I'd drive 30 minutes to visit again, but at least the scenery was beautiful on the way out there.

name: The Basement
text: Went to The Basement on a whim with some friends while visiting Nashville! The band was pretty good, but it was extremely packed...like I don't know if it was even legal for that many people to be there. The bar area was extremely crowded, which made it hard to get a drink.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Came early on a Friday morning, so the place was pretty empty and quiet.  The wait staff is fantastic! The ladies and gentlemen at the front of the house are very kind and friendly. My server, Lucas, really went out of his way to make it a personal experience for myself and my husband.  The parking lot is easily accessible and there is plenty of room for parking and visiting the surrounding retail shops Loveless owns.  

Lucas was prompt in greeting us and was able to answer all of our questions with honest answers, which is very refreshing! He was attentive but not in our faces while we ate... Again... So refreshing to have a server who understands balance! 

We ordered the Southern Breakfast Sampler, which comes with two eggs, their specialty ham, bacon, sausage, and your choice of hashbrown casserole, fried potatoes or fruit.  I ordered hashbrown casserole and Lucas made it possible for my husband to order more meat instead of a side.  A coffee, a hot tea, and two breakfast samplers = ~ $35.   Reasonably priced and, we did not mind spending the money because the service we received was great.  

First: let me rave about the hashbrown casserole.  Oh my god, it is so decadent! Creamy, tangy, cheesy, and with hot sauce, its perfect.  Some of the best hashbrown casserole I've had.  My next favorite item: the ham!  It was absolutely perfect, though I wish I had more of it on my plate!  It's tender, juicy, slightly sweet, salty, and perfect.  The bacon, when its fresh, is also very tasty.  Crispy, salty, and smoky.  I wasn't fond of the sausage by itself, but with the blackberry preserves, it was awesome.  

The biscuits were okay.  I was very enticed by the sound of them by all the reviews here.  But sadly, I was slightly disappointed when I tried them this morning.  They were a little chewy and dense, but again, with the preserves or gravy they were decent.  That's why instead of 5 stars I gave 4 stars.  The hype is a little high for this place, but I still enjoyed my breakfast.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
After some awesome hikes along the Natchez Parkway this place hits the spot! I was tired and just wanted some good comfort food and then we realized how close we were to Loveless...so excited! At 4pm it was already busy but we got right in and our server was so friendly and helpful! We decided on just sharing the chicken fried chicken and then added some extra sides. 
First the biscuits came out...for some reason I've been on a real biscuit kick lately so I've had my fair share and these are some of the best. They have a good flake and a slightly salty, buttery taste; add the butter and jams and they are almost a dessert. Then the food came out and everything was spot on. I didn't think that the fried okra would taste fresh but it was some really fresh tasting okra!! The side of the day was garlic mashed potatoes and those things were garlic-y, which in my world you can never have too much garlic so they were perfect. The food all came out quickly and was still warm, a major bonus!
This place is every bit worth the hype it receives. It's good comfort food with really good friendly service.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Don't know where they came up with the name loveless because this place is full of love (insert your groan here). I chose to have my birthday dinner here on the way out of Nashville after hearing so much about it and didn't regret it one bit. Our waitress gave me my dessert with a candle on it and announced to everyone that it was my bday so everyone sang to me.

Long wait during dinnertime but well worth it. You can pass the time quickly by exploring the shops around it or playing cornhole out front. Great southern food and hands down the best biscuits I've ever had. I ended up buying their mix to make my own at home (plus a lot of other items I didn't need -  oh Loveless Cafe, you sure are smart with your marketing).

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Stopped in based on reviews and we were amazed.  I'm from Milwaukee and we have great authentic German restaurants.  Bavarian Bierhaus kicked the crap out of them.  I'm German and know what laberkasse is, theirs was fantastic. I do not suggest that for most Americans. My wife ordered the pork schnitzel and it was authentic and perfection to say the least.  An odd restaurant to find in Nashville, but damn is this place good.  

Great and I mean great service.
Amazing beer selection.


Go here, you won't be sorry that you did.  I will be back!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The Loveless Cafe was such a great experience that I find myself wanting to change my address just so I can dine here again soon. I learned about this place while planning our trip to Memphis.

Let's start with our sweet waitress, who quickly offered suggestions when we were struggling with what to order. (The menu options were bountiful and mouthwatering.) My husband and I both ended up ordering the Southern Sampler Platter and my son ordered pancakes. Let's just say that it was a good thing we hadn't eaten all day.

For my sampler, I ordered fried catfish, fried chicken and pulled pork BBQ, along with fried green tomatoes and creamed corn. (Yes, that's a lot of fried foods but I was on vacation.) I loved everything--especially the creamed corn. Yum! The fried chicken breast was tender and juicy, the catfish was lightly breaded and flaky, and the pulled pork was so tender I almost didn't need to chew.

Even though we were stuffed (and couldn't finish our entree), my husband and I decided to split a piece of their chocolate chess pie. It was rich and utterly sinful.

The next time you're in Nashville, TN, and you're looking for some good 'ol Southern cooking and hospitality, stop in at the Loveless Cafe. Your taste buds will thank you! Bon appetit!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Ate late lunch today around 1:30. Food was fresh, hot and plenty of it. Susan our waitress was friendly and gave great recommendations. The place was clean and organized and prices were reasonable. Only five miles off the interstate and easy to get to. Definitely worth a detour. Homemade biscuits and jams are to die for. Go if you're in the neighborhood and want great home cooking.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing! Amazing! Amazing! Went here with my mother and the place lived up to it's hype! Make sure you give yourself plenty of time (our wait was estimated to be two hours but was a little over an hour). The drive was scenic and they have tons of activities, chairs, and cute gift shops to keep you busy while you wait. The food was to die for (the biscuits were out of this world) and the atmosphere was quaint! Couldn't have had a better brunch :)

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: As locals we usually stay away from the touristy spots but I'm glad we didn't with here! The atmosphere is wonderful! The service was a little slow but he had several tables. We started off with the giant pretzel and ordered the warm bier cheese along with the mustard. The pretzel was the best we've ever had. He ordered the wurst plate and I tried the regular brat and the smoked brat and both were on point. I've never liked saur kraut but liked theirs. I ordered the jager schnitzel and it was delicious. I ordered the fries with mine and they were good as well. Their beer selection was really good and didn't disappoint. We will be returning to listen to some live music.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: First time here. Great atmosphere with authentic music and clothing. Served by a very cute girl named Allison. Always smiling and very knowledgeable of the menu. An overall great experience.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We accidentally arrived at a peak time, so we weren't able to be seated (and we were starving.)

Good news, though! The gift shop next door also sells food! We walked around the property a bit, poked our heads inside the main dining room to take in its charm, then headed over to the shop across the parking lot. It was darling, lots of Southern-inspired knick nacks and foodstuffs. 

We were able to get a dozen biscuits with butter and jam AND some BBQ. We ate in the car like animals, but we didn't even care how it looked. It was so good! The biscuits were the perfect size (small enough to justify going back for seconds, and thirds, and fourths...) I highly recommend you order some, even if you're not able to eat inside. 

Next time I'm in town, I'll plan accordingly and come back!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We went for breakfast and it was delicious! I had a bbq pork omelette and a biscuit with a fried green tomato and pimiento cheese. There is definitely a bit of wait (a little over an hour for 8 people) and they require your whole party to be there to put your name on the list. There are cute shops around the restaurant with souvenirs, coffee, snacks, art, jewelry, etc. to wander in while you wait. Plus, they make their own hot sauce!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Great place to have an authentic German meal. Live music, good food and excellent service. Charles took care of us. He was fantastic! Ask for Charles when you go there.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is an ABSOLUTE MUST VISIT when you're in Nashville. Wow is Loveless a revelation. It's about a 20 minute drive from downtown, and there can be a wait, but the food and atmosphere is well worth it. The Southern hospitality here is incomparable: the servers are warm, kind, and attentive. And this food is finger-lickin' good. Come hungry, because the portions are HUGE.

The feast begins with their famous biscuits, which are buttery, savory, and addictive...and have FREE REFILLS. Better still are that they come with sweet preserves, a perfect accompaniment for the biscuits. My friend and I then ordered the pulled pork BBQ and fried chicken respectively. The BBQ was some of the best I've ever had: tender, rich, and flavorful. The Mac and cheese and coleslaw on the side were also excellent. The fried chicken was superb - crispy on the outside, and juicy on the inside. And while I loved the food...I could barely finish because the portions were so big. 

Loveless is an absolute treat, and it's a must visit for Nashville first timers.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Cannery Ballroom-sardine sweat shop. So hot it must have been in the eighties last night for Rival Sons. Unenjoyable to the point of no return. It's not me Cannery Ballroom it's you and we won't be seeing each other anymore.

name: Commodore Grille
text:
In town and staying at the Holiday Inn, I wanted to get a quick bite to eat before heading out for the famous Nashville music scene so stopped at the hotel restaurant to eat.  It was the Commodore Grill on a Wednesday night.  The food was good, service was good, but the music was great!  Groups of three singer/songwriters took the stage for three songs each then left for another group of three.  Found out it was "Songwriters Night".  When I asked what was the gig, (really, Holiday Inn?), was told, "welcome to Nashville" in a smooth Tennessee drawl.  

Awesome experience ended up parking at the Commodore for the rest of the night and am looking forward to a return visit.   I'm not a country music fan but these live performances were great.  For anyone looking for a real Nashville experience by performers who really put it out there, check out the Commodore Grill.

name: Drifters
text: Had the woodchuck cider and a tofu sandwich. Big heavy sandwich, in a good way. Tofu fried, a little bland in terms of the breading, but great texture/moisture level, and bland tofu breading works as a good base for their variety of sauces, many of them spicy in unique ways. Good outdoor seating with good lighting. Parking's a pain but its a pain for any business in this area.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
Film, food and wine, and special events.  Car parking free when you get your ticket and number for the parking machine.  Wish they would do the Lord of the Rings uncut Trilogy lock-down again. What fun that was.  Perhaps a Harry Potter lock-down soon...or even something a bit more serious all day/nighter.
Belcourt East any time soon please to save us the trundle across the river.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Love the Belcourt! I, unfortunately, don't go as frequently as I'd like (but, that's only because my wallet is tight). That said, though, their movie tickets are SO well priced...and a bar inside?...most excellent. Just a short 7minute walk from house, I couldn't ask for a better landmark in my neighborhood.

name: Drifters
text: The sampler was one of the best bbq i ever had, it is a bit costly, but there was plenty of food left over on my wifes plate. None on mine. I like to eat. The service was great. If i go back to nashville, i will be eating at this place again.

name: Drifters
text: Drifters, oh Drifters. I love you so. From your amazing two for one drink specials to your BBQ tofu you make me infinitely happy.

name: The Family Wash
text:
Without a doubt, my favorite pub/restaurant/hangout place in Nashville.  We've been coming here for about 5 years and always enjoy ourselves on our rare date nights.  Great atmosphere, good music, fantastic beer selections, and the menu (while small) always delivers.  Hard to pass up the shepherd's pie, but if you can...try the meatloaf and mac & cheese.  

We also see families in here quite often so it is pretty kid friendly.  In fact, they have kids nights at least once or twice a month.

Passionate owners who care about service and their restaurant.

name: The Family Wash
text:
Cool atmosphere....good beer selection!
Chicken pot pie = fantastic
Meatloaf = stupid good

name: EXIT/IN
text: I had no clue what to expect upon my arrival at Exit/In, but I was MORE than thrilled when I walked in.  Intimate, but not too small or cramped.  Larger than High Watt, but smaller than Mercy Lounge, this venue is perfect for rising stars in the Nashville (and beyond) scene.  I can't wait to check out another show here!

name: Frisky Frog's
text: I used to LOVE this place, but this one experience will forever ruin Frisky Frogs. I'd gone before, for preds game and such, but I went for brunch with my girlfriends and some friends from out of town. I made a reservation beforehand for 11:30am.  We get there and the guy at the front (later found out he was one of the managers) tells me I am early and "I guess I can sit you"...as there was a table already reserved for us with my name on it. Then he tells us we are not allowed to order before 12:30p so the kitchen can get set up. Weird, but we ordered unlimited mimosas anyway. Finally ordered food...waited....waited....waited...food never came.  WE WAITED FOR 3 HOURS. No joke. Turns out they cancelled our order because the group at the other half of the table (who arrived after us) got their food so they thought that was the whole table. Got the manager over, told him we get it, half of us work in food service, but still that was unacceptable. This one manager (they are twins, one brother is SUPER NICE, but the other one, the one we dealt with, was a super ASS) tells us he is sorry but this is just something that happens and we can wait for our food or he would be happy to cancel our orders. We asked about our drinks and he said he could give us 10% off, but that is the best he could do. 10%...are you serious! I told him straight up we were getting up and walking out, not paying for anything, and made sure our waitress (who was super overworked and was basically doing the whole place by herself) was not on the hook for any of this. We gave our waitress a big tip and left.  Will never walk back in that place again. I apologize to the other brother I did not have the pleasure of meeting, please know all these bad reviews are because of your brother.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: I had the gumbo nachos and added shrimp. They were great!! So were the 2 for 1 drinks. The best part was the music, they played all the hits!! Casey, the bartender was very friendly and nice to talk to!!! I will be back!!

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: Went there last night for the first time to see Smith and Myers and I thought the place was the worst small venue I've been to downtown Nashville. No circulation of air throughout the place made for everyone around my wife and I sweating our asses off. Level of the floor to the stage left viewing at a minimum. People at the bar ignore you. Just overall a horrible experience. I will not be back there for anything again.

name: Frisky Frog's
text:
Stopped in Thursday night after having dinner in the Gulch. None of our group had ever been. We had originally thought we were going to stop into the Tin Roof, but all they had was hockey on the TV. Walked down to Frisky Frog and the music we heard sounded good and we decided to stop in. Place was not super busy, but lets be honest, it was a Thursday. We grabbed some drinks and sat close to the band. The  band was great! Such a variety of music, including rap. Great music to sing and dance along to. Drinks were good and strong. 
We enjoyed ourselves so much that we ended up going back again Friday night after making some rounds.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: This movie theater might not have reclining seats but it has amazing movies and a whole downtown area right down the street. I love going to lunch and then the movies right after. They play old and new movies. The area couldn't be more perfect. The prices are very reasonable and everybody is very friendly.

name: Drifters
text: Hard to find but well worth the effort. Had the half pulled pork and brisket sandwich. 4 oz. each and super flavorful, Try the super hot sauce. Fries were hot and seasoned to a T.

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
3.5

As an event venue, Mercy is a bit tight. As a music venue, it's intimate. Does that make sense? Enjoyment of the space will entirely depend on what brings you out. 

To try & enjoy ML as an event venue with many people moving about, the space tends to get very cramped, very quickly. It's hard to pay attention to a variety of things at once because it's rather difficult to move around. It's the sort of space that if you are planning on having an event, you should plan for either something small or something progressive that allows guests to get in and get out to another space. Spending a few hours in the confines can be a touch claustrophobic.

As a music venue (its intended and best use), Mercy Lounge makes much more sense. The space that's cramped as an event venue becomes intimate for a musical performance. That has much to with the fact that, typically, for a performance people aren't milling about. They're staying still and being respectful to the performers, other guests and to the venue. For shows, the bartenders are quick and friendly. The beers are $5 a draft pull and the acoustics lend themselves well for concentrating on one thing (with lots of voices and feet bouncing around everywhere, with a lot going on, it can be a bit overwhelming in another setting).

Come for the music. Think carefully about an event. Enjoy your time.

name: Drifters
text:
Drifter's is a classic dive joint.  From the minute you walk in you get an instant low key laid back local vibe.  People at the bar knew each other, knew the bartenders and didn't seem to have a care in the world.  Had it not been a dreary rainy day, I would have brought my pup and sat outside to enjoy some brews since they had a nice patio as well.  

I can't speak much for the BBQ as I'm a vegetarian, but the hush puppies were on point.  I enjoyed mine with some BBQ sauce, as I didn't care much for the dipping sauce that was served with them.  I also got some chips and salsa.  Now being a TX girl, I knew this was risky, but I was told the salsa was made in house, so I gave it a go.  Not sure if I'd call it salsa, as it was more like pico.  You know big chunks of tomato and diced onion.  But it was still good.  My man got the ribs and I did try the tiniest of bites, just so I could say I tasted it.  Wow - SMOKEY!  These meaty bones were defiantly slow cooked over a smoke pit for sho!  My man enjoyed them.  The baked bean were just that - nothing wowed me about them.  And I'd say the same for the coleslaw.  Overall food wasn't bad, but not sure I'd call it the best!  They did have some veggie options, but they seemed rather predictable and not worth the try for me.  I would have loved to see some BBQ setan on the menu or something at least trying to run with the BBQ theme.  My man said to give it 4 stars, but being a southern girl, I just wasn't that impressed.

They had some nice brews on tap, which made me content.  And the staff was fantastic.  I could see this as a great place to hang out and drink some cold ones.  But I'd be up for looking for some other BBQ places to try out.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
This theatre deserves nothing less than 5 stars. It's a lovely old movie house, lush velvet seats and all, originally opened as a silent film house in the '20s. (Renovated since then, of course - nothing looks particularly shabby.)

I visited on a late Monday afternoon and it was calm, quiet, and awesomely air-conditioned. I assume they have more moviegoers at a more normal time - the location is excellent, right off the Vanderbilt campus. Programming includes repertory, cult classics, indie/foreign, kids films, second run, etc. Plus lots of special programming: outdoor films in their parking lot, midnight screenings... Sometimes they do some first-run stuff as well. It's basically everything anyone wants if they're choosing not to go to a multiplex! 

Later this month they'll be screening the hilariously brilliant Japanese horror cult classic "House." Watching this on the big screen is a necessary life experience. 

All tickets before 6pm every day are matinee priced: $7.75! Ahhh glorious. They automatically gave me with the receipt a free parking pass for their lot.

Two women in the row in front of me actually took care to sit slightly toward the left so they wouldn't block my view - so thoughtful!

Worth a visit as a tourist? Yessir, especially if you need some peace and a temporary change of scenery via silver screen. If you're a local? Get yourself a membership!

name: The Country
text:
We came on a Sunday afternoon looking for a patio to enjoy the sunshine. This place is huge and someone put a lot of money into it- it's pretty! They have lots of beer and some good looking cocktails. They have live music Mon-Thurs. Very laid back vibe and good for groups.

We have the pretzel and Brussels sprouts to snack on. The pretzel and cheese sauce was particularly good.

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
Awesomeness place came thru last night 
A free concert was playing they have multi
Stages and the crowd was very hip the 
Gentleman at the front desk was very 
Polite and professional great place to visit

name: EXIT/IN
text: The EXIT/IN was a great place to catch a show! I went here on a Wednesday night to see the awesome band Superorganism. Tickets were cheap which I always appreciate. It kills me to go to a big venue like Bridgestone, spend $150+ on tickets, and be up so far you can barely even see the performer. The EXIT/IN allows you to get up close and personal with the band performing. Parking can be a little tricky but we were able to find free parking on a side street close by. The check-in process was quick and easy. Have your IDs with you, even if you bought tickets online. I did see security around but they didn't say anything or bother me the whole night. Maybe they have listened to the feedback or maybe this was a smaller show so they didn't have to be on such high alert? The feel of the place is a classic dive music venue. I loved it. Behind the bar, they have a list of names of people who have performed at the venue before. Cool touch. I didn't check out their drink menu too much because I had a sore throat, but they had a good selection of beers and mixed drinks. The stage is raised so you can have a good view from anywhere in the room. There is also a balcony if you really want the bird's eye view. We were pretty close to the stage because it wasn't a super packed show and we arrived on time. The opener ended up cancelling so the band performed a little earlier than expected. I felt bad for people who came later because they probably missed half the show. That's why I'm always on time! The sound was awesome. The band was of course great. One thing that kind of put a damper on the concert was the video stopped working. The band had really cool video work for their background and for about 4 songs it didn't work. The venue had to shut off all of the lights and reboot everything it looked like. At one point the band was almost playing in the dark. I get it, these things happen. The band was cool with it and cracked jokes with the audience. Overall, it was a fun venue that lets you really experience the band for an unbeatable price. I would 100% go back to check out another show!

name: Springwater
text: This place is as divey as it gets. Driving by, most people wouldn't even realize it's there, or that it's open. After reading that it was the oldest bar in the entire state of TN, and realizing it was walking distance from where I live, I had to check it out. It was relatively empty around 7:30 on a Friday night - one booth of people, and a few people at the bar. The bartender was friendly, and quickly served us up some draft beers. The place is dark and grungy, in a comfortable kind of way, with torn booths and a stage for performances. There's also darts, music playing, and some outdoor seating. It was a fun spot to grab a beer before dinner.

name: The Station Inn
text:
This place is a bit rustic, but if you like bluegrass...it's a great place. The food isn't much, however..... The hotdog with pimento cheese is surprising pretty good.
Not really a dinning establishment... Rather it is know for some great music.   Seating is somewhat of a challenge. (Folding tables and chairs)
So come early to get a good spot of prepare to stand.
The draw here is the music. Small venue makes the sound incredible.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Came here with some friends in the middle of the day to enjoy some food and live music. We sat up on the third floor which was nice because it wasn't as packed as the others.

The live music was pretty good and enjoyable with some drinks and food. The mixed drinks are tiny for how expensive they are. I would skip them and just get a beer instead if you want a drink. The fried pickles were really good and came with a lot so it was perfect to share between 7 other girls. For lunch I split a buffalo chicken wrap with my friend. It was the perfect amount of food to split as they gave fries with the wrap as well.

Overall the place was okay. Okay drinks, decent food and some good music. Also we got our pictures taken with the honky tonk sign which was a nice feature! I would tell anyone to stop by and  see it at least once while in Nashville.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Awesome live music! Cash was flying for those Southern strings. Come here if you are looking for somewhere fun to spend your Friday night in Nashville

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: You can't miss with anything on Broadway! Live music everywhere, no cover and cheap drinks! This should be the new marketing slogan for Nashville. My favorite place that I can remember is Honky Tonk Central! This was a 3 level bar with live music on every level. The biggest thing about Nashville is that free live music at a bar is amazing! The talent is beyond good and I don't even like country music. This bar didn't disappoint with several bachelorette parties on each level, beers under $5 and no cover!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Favorite bar I discovered in town. Nice prices and friendly people. Drinks were strong and music was great. They have one guy there almost every day and he is fantastic

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
When ascend you to a food place, you should go there. You'll be glad that you did.

I have such great memories of this place. When I was young and reckless, I went to a Dixie Chicks concert here. I got lost in the building and ended up exploring the innards of it. I climbed up into the rafters and then I managed to ascend to the top of the building, and down into the balcony, and eventually made my way to the expensive seats plenty of which were still available and then watched the Chicks getting it on. This was actually before the days of the whole backlash against them, but I don't want to say that out loud because I don't want you guys thinking I am old.

Anyway the bottom line is that this is a beautiful venue and has wonderful memories for me.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: One of the best local music spots in Nashville. Food is just ok and the cover charge isn't always what's stated on the website. Beware.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: We went here both nights that we visited Nashville. It has a younger crowd and amazing bands. The first night the band played a 90s mash up that was pretty fun. They also played a lot of newer country. The second night they played rock n roll and country (new and old). There is no cover and the bands request $20 to request a song. Not bad considering there is no cover and there is nothing better than listening to your favorite song live! Also the view from the 2nd level perfectly shows downtown. Definitely would recommend this place if you want a fun night out on the town.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great live bands! Seems like a local hang out. Food looked good but typical bar food.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
I really enjoy this bar on non Peak days rather than the weekend. This bar is unparalleled when they play good acoustic music without all the electric and full band overlay. The bar is comfortable the seating is private and it's a good mix of Ages people who are locals and visitors from out of town

I suggest the beef or chicken skewers they are cooked well healthy and flavorful.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Gave it 5 stars because Tim Bridges is sizzling hot! Going back next weekend!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place rocks in town for my 40th and by fat best place 3 floors 3 different bands outside atmosphere great service a must when in town!

name: The Station Inn
text:
Loved, loved, loved, my experience here. The band was amazing. (Frank Solivan and Dirty Kitchen) True musical excellence. Worth every penny at a modest $12 cover. Bartenders as well as door staff were very nice. As the other reviewers mention your alcohol choice is only beer. But they have goo goo clusters! 

Skip the cover bands and mediocre bars on the strip and treat yourself to something real.

name: The Station Inn
text: I went here with a friend who is a Nashville local. He recommended the Doyle and Debbie show as "like seeing George Jones and Tammy Wynette, but on mescaline". they did not disappoint. the music was great, and the act was hysterically funny. it's a sort of Stephen Colbert style social satire. the venue is superbly decrepit. they only serve beer and "coolers" (Smirnoff Ice) so you may want to pre-game, but be sure to support the place and buy some drinks while you're here.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: We've wanted to go to 3rd & Lindsley for years! Finally made it out the Tuesday before Thanksgiving for an MV2 night with some of their young artists. Nora Collins is going to be a good one! We had a blast! Highly recommend this place!!

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text:
Love Bobbys.  It's a great dive bar off the beaten path.  I love how they have song writers night and also have other nightly activities (comedian night etc) 

Highly recommend for a good local time!!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: The food here is so bad. I've eaten the strawberry pecan salad (thumbs down), the spinach-artichoke dip (ew! How do you mess up spinach-artichoke dip??), the potato skins (meh), the philly cheese steak (two thumbs down), and the chicken wings (very mediocre and the ranch was lumpy). The mozzarella sticks were alright. Do yourself a favor and eat before you go. This place must only stay in business because you're trapped at a table for the concert, so you may as well eat there. Don't fall for it.

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text:
The War Memorial Auditorium is a majestic and beautiful historic building. 

After climbing many levels of long marble steps, you're greeted with enormous white columns and a huge courtyard. This is truly one of the most beautiful buildings in Nashville. 

The auditorium was built as an incredible memorial for the fallen soldiers who gave their lives for our country in World War I. For more information on this incredible building, you may find this link helpful :

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_Memorial_Auditorium

( The State Capital stands behind the Auditorium making it even more impressive. The lighting and the beauty of these two landmarks is absolutely breathtaking. )

Now for my review on the auditorium itself:

We purchased VIP tickets for the Cowboy Jack Clement tribute benefiting musicians without health insurance. ( I've known Cowboy all my life, so this was one tribute I wouldn't have missed for anything. ) 

I could go on and on about the line up of incredible artists, how great the show was, and how much I enjoyed it,  but this review is about the auditorium.

Our seats were in the balcony ( 3rd floor) which gave us a great view of the stage
but the elevator only goes to the main floor. If you have trouble walking up stairs, buy your tickets for the main floor.  

The interior of the auditorium is beautiful, even the ceiling is something to admire.
The stage is more than ample  for a very large band, choir or even orchestra. Unfortunately the sound wasn't great which is a shame because the atmosphere is amazing. 

The auditorium sells drinks which include sodas, beer, mixed drinks and water. 
( no wine) On the third floor, the "bar" is basically a closet with a counter and one girl operating it as a "cash only" bar. ( a small beer - $8.00, large - $15.00 )

Now for the worst part....the ONLY restrooms in the building are in the BASEMENT. 
This may not be an issue for some people, but for me it was a real inconvenience. 

Every time I needed to make a trip to the ladies room, it involved going down 3 floors to the basement and 3 floors back to our seats.
( approximately 100 stairs each way.) Recent knee surgery made this a painful inconvenience. 

Another problem is the seating. I'm 5ft. 3in. and I had absolutely no leg room. My son and husband are over 6 ft. 3 in. and were so uncomfortable it caused us to  stand in the stairway a few times. ( my purse was in my lap the entire time -no room on the floor by my seat.) I felt like I was sitting on an airplane. 

It was very cold and windy that night so we used valet parking. ( Parking is also an issue here.)  
If there's another event at the auditorium that I absolutely don't want to miss, I'd definitely get tickets on the main floor.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
HTC is another country music bar on Nashville's main drag.  This is another multi-tiered bar that is perhaps built a little better than the other re-purposed buildings nearby.  Crowd was a good mix of ages with college kids, bachelor/ette parties, and also old folks just listening to music.  The bands vary by floor but we just stayed on the ground level.  Both bands we saw were alright with the second one being a bit obnoxious with people on cell phones; I agree that you shouldn't be on a phone if you're right next to the band, but if you're in the back of the room and the singer calls you out then he's just a jackass (he did this multiple times to different people).

Bar prices seemed a bit higher here than in some of the other bars.  Beer selection was decent with the list having ~half domestic options with a number of local microbrews thrown in.  Bartenders are decent given the volume of people they have to deal with.  The male bathroom attendant was hilarious but also a bit pushy; didn't bother me but I can see some people getting uncomfortable.  Overall this is a worthwhile place to stop by but not worth a specific visit when in town.

name: The Back Corner
text: Really cool place!! Have been here a couple of times and had great experiences. Didnt catch the bartenders name the last time I was here but she was an absolute doll. Will definitely be back!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Ow!!!  Honky Tonk Central on a Saturday night celebrating my niece's outstanding accomplishments.  I can say Honky Tonk and Honky all I want and no one will be upset because that's what it's called. Three levels of locals and tourists packed and overflowing off the balconies. Yeah buddy! This place has that Nashville energy and live music right in the heart of it all.  This is where the action is and what you hear every visitor rave about.  Come here and you know you are in Nashville.  Woo!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Stopped in for an appetizer after a visit to the Hall of Fame. This was our first Nashville Country bar experience! Food is Really good for bar food standards! Annoying they don't allow substitutes on the app platter which sucks! 

I have this place 4 Stars because the band was really Awesome, and for what it is, a country bar, its definitely doing everything right. 

The band knew just about every cover song and played on request! Cute little female singer who could really sing, token fat guy with a great voice and a second guitar player who could sing as well! Shot out to "Hoss Skelton and his band"

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text:
I came here for the TFIOS event this past Thursday. I was media so I was able to snag a reserved seat in the balcony ... felt bad for the poor teens standing near the stage!

I can't speak for the venue as a concert place, but for TFIOS it was fine. Easy to see the actors + writer (John Green! *fangirls out*) from where we were in the balcony. Good acoustics although I don't think it was meant to play movies/clips from movies.

I'd like to explore this place more if ever back in Nashville.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Do not come here! !!! I am on a Bachelorette party from Chicago,  2 of of the 10 girlss had their phones and wallet stolen from their purse, along with other women from the bar.  Security did nothing to help us, would not even call the police for us and told us to do it ourselves.  This place is criminal infested with terrible security that is worthless!!!!!

name: The Station Inn
text:
Went in for the comedy show...seemed sorta dark an didn't seem like our vibe. 

So my gf an I went on to downtown and drooled over $400.00 boots....yeah we didn't get any. 

And they only take cash here at this place.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great music, food, customer service and atmosphere! Note that the music is loud and the place isn't for people who want to be calm or quiet, but if you want live country music, the occasional two step dance and a low key but fun atmosphere, this place is perfect.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: I was visiting Nashville two weeks ago with two girlfriends of mine. One of the girls I was with was leaning against the wall texting, and the bouncer accused her of being drunk and threw her outside. When I asked him what his problem was he proceeded to yell in my face that I could chug my 11$ drink and "get the f#*% out". He then grabbed my hand that was holding the full drink and threw the drink down my shirt, and without letting go of my hand he literally threw me outside of the building, where him and his friend flipped me off while they were closing the door. I spent the rest of my night soaking wet and smelling like booze. I would not suggest wasting any time at this over priced shit hole.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
What and interesting spot. Like most places in Nashville the non-descript exterior hides a warm, fun filled environment on the inside. Since the name of the place is also it's cross streets, if you can't find this place, you have had too much to drink and need to go home. With that said, the musical performance by The Time Jumpers is sure to bring smiles to those familiar with archetypal southern favorites and newbies alike. The crowd is a mix of Nashville locals , travelers and a few younger people like me.  Everyone was friendly. 

The food is basically upgraded bar food with some good entrees as well. I felt like a patty melt tonight and damn was it good. The menu indicated "Angus beef" and it was and epic combination of sautéed onions, Swiss and rye. Fries have some sort of seasoned salt but there is something really good about them that I can't identify.  My partner in crime had the prime rib dinner which was also very good. 

Parking is slightly better than most places in Nashville with a few nearby businesses not needing their parking lots at night. Bring a Mini Cooper to fit in small places. Also get here early if you want a decent table, or a table at all for that fact. Some friendly stranger indicated she paid someone to be here at 5 to secure her a front row table by the stage. That's dedication people.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Overall a pretty good music venue. I'm here now for a concert. It is a smoke free, not! People smoking all around me. You would think they would take the necessary steps to enforce the no smoking rule but no. The stench of cigarettes is why I'm only giving it 2 stars. 
On a positive note, prices for food and drinks aren't that bad.  In line with other venues.

name: Live On The Green Music Festival
text:
I guess I'll be that person that breaks the 5 star trend. I remember going to Live on the Green when it first started and it was amazing. Being able to just sit and relax while listening to music was awesome. Now, not so much. I fear, dear Nashville, this event has outgrown its tiny space. I went mainly to see City & Colour and while I'm glad I toughed it out to the end, it was not pleasurable for the most part.

At first, yes many people were lounging on blankets and enjoying the opening band but as the night progressed it got considerably more crowded. Those with blankets and lawn chairs seemed to just give up after awhile and retreat to other places or leave all together. We were CONSTANTLY being pushed or bombarded with "excuse me I need to get by" as people walked over others to stand towards the front. Soon it was no longer a fun, live show but instead of was the dodging of the beer and cigarette smoke as people moved around you, most with no sympathy to your presence whatsoever. 

Lots of great local food trucks, companies and beer vendors but getting to these stands were a gamble of either losing your spot on the lawn (if lucky enough to have one) or braving sending one or two of your party to navigate through the crowd. The lines were outrageous, mainly just groups of people standing in whatever fashion they deemed fit. While, from what I saw, prices were quite reasonable for a "concert" event, the lines just weren't worth it.

Most of the artists that play this event are not the "lets all dance and move to the beat" kind of artists, at least on this night. City & Colour is a perfect example of the type of music this event was made for! It would have been awesome to just sit and be able to listen to the heavenly vocals of Dallas Green while enjoying a beer but instead you have to settle for listening to the music while filtering out every single social hour conversation going on around you. If you just want to hear the music and don't care about actually being able to see the artist, then find a spot a good distance away and you'll be fine. 

I feel like this event could be amazing, if run more efficiently. Possibly moving the beer tents and such away from the stage vicinity would help thin out the crowd of those patrons that make you think "are they waiting in line or just watching the show?" Before you go, ask yourself this: Do I want to be constantly stepped around, over or pushed aside by what seems to be every single person who has crawled out of East Nashville's hipster woodworks? Do I enjoy having my feet stepped on, beer spilled on my shoe and cigarette smoke being blown in my direction by countless people with no decency for those around me? Do I want to see great artists for free but sacrifice my comfort as I stand for 5+ hours? If so, then this is the event for you! I appreciate the fact it's a free show and I guess this is what you should expect with a show like this but guys, this isn't Bonnaroo. You do not have days to spend socializing and getting messed up as you listen to the music. It's a concert full of regular people who may or may not enjoy the fact you are plastered on a local pale ale as you smoke your billionth cigarette of the night. Most of us just wanted to be able to enjoy a great night of music but, at least in my opinion, this time it fell very short.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: Awesome new venue.  Design and sound are great.  Sat on the lawn with a beach chair.  Great evening.

name: Live On The Green Music Festival
text:
This is seriously one of the coolest events in Nashville! 

I saw Gin Wigmore, ZZ Ward and Matt & Kim a few weeks ago, and my mind was blown! Who knew that space could hold so many happy music fans?? What an awesome set-up! I got to grab a blanket and relax with some friends while listening to some kickass music. Life in Nashville is dang good!

It is so dang good in fact, that I chose all of my MBA classes based on the LOTG schedule; so no Thursday classes for me in the Fall!

If you haven't hit up LOTG, you need to free up your Thursdays and head on over! It is not to be missed!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
One of the things about the various listening rooms in Nashville is when you get to see so many mind-blowing bands, musicians and singers. The space becomes associated in my brain with the musical magic that happens so consistently inside it.  I'm a huge Time Jumpers fan (I've been 8 or 9 times now since moving to Nashville in 09).  I recommend to everyone - come to Nashville. Stay over Monday Night. See the Time Jumpers.  Guaranteed. 

Another thing about amazing venues like 3&L is how popular they become. Of course - amazing talent will draw crowds.  So getting in line early (like hours before doors) and waiting another couple hours (time to sample the extensive but for the most part ordinary bar/fried food menu.  It's certainly a magnitude of order better than the menu at the Station Inn (Time Jumper's former venue) but not amazing enough to warrant 5 stars. I'll keep trying it, though, and guaranteed you won't go hungry (unless you're vegan). It's just not very foodie-ish. Nashville has a lot of amazing culinary talent doing interesting things.  You don't come to this venue for dinner, though, you come for the music and have decent barfood dinner/snacks. 

Take note of the seating; You'll be in seats for several hours. On the main floor the chairs are wooden with no arm rests and have short square backs. The chairs on the balcony are wooden with no arm rests but have padding on the seats. There are also padded stools on the balcony.

Sound is great throughout the room, too.  Be assured, you will have an amazing musical experience at 3rd and Lindsey. You just won't remember the food.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This was our favorite bar in Nashville. The bartender was great and the music was fantastic!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Honky Tonk Central has always been one of my favorite places in Nashville. It doesn't have the old school legendary character of a lot of the places on Broadway, but what it lacks in heritage, it makes up for in good times. 

The open air 3 story bar has live music on every level. So you can freely roam floor to floor listening to a different live band. We enjoy visiting the other venues on Broadway, but it always seems like we find ourselves back relaxing at Honky Tonk Central overlooking the city & listening to some awesome bands.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
We went there last night and it was such a cool experience!
The Time Jumpers are a band of 9 older men (including Vince Gill) that usually play Mondays for $20. The venue is smaller so in order to get a table, get there at 6:00 and have dinner and drinks before the show starts at 9:00. 
The band is bluegrass and they pulled groups on stage (pre planned) to perform. Last night, Kacey Musgraves came and played with them.
One of the best experiences during my time in Nashville!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: The owner hit my female friend in the face. He was drunk and violent. Never go there if you have respect for yourself. There is video footage.

name: The Station Inn
text: Bluegrass DREAM!  Sunday night keeps it rocking.  Love this bar and the atmosphere.  Nothing beats a dive bar where you can walk right up to people jamming.  The pictures on the wall display the history of this establishment.  What a gem!  The popcorn and cheap pitcher beers will keep you going all night

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: This place is popular in Nashville the food is bar food so don't expect to much place it's old but nice parking was full but across the street is a public parking for $10 all night we went Wednesday night they have 2 great performers the sound was excellent the show was great if you want to see new artists give a chance to 3rd&lindsley for sure you aren't gonna be dissatisfied

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: It was a decent place. The live music this afternoon was very good! Both of the singers were excellent, our waitress was very attentive and nice but the food was subpar. Got a burger and it was a frozen patty, disappointing. But seemed like a decent place to hang out otherwise- just don't eat!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place was great! They had an awesome band playing while we were there, the waitress was attentive and available, but not overbearing. This was nice since we wanted to listen to the band. The food wasn't gourmet or spectacular by any means, but that's not why we went -- we got some wings and a buffalo wrap. Like I said, both were good and I felt like the prices were pretty reasonable. It's a big place, too.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: We clearly went to this establishment for the music and we were not disappointed whatsoever.  The show was fantastic.  We saw a tribute to David Bowie and while we were not that familiar with the music the band and singers were amazing.  The atmosphere was that of a club and perfect to listen to music.  In terms of food, typical pub food and pretty average quality.  I wouldn't go here for the food but for the music, absolutely.

name: The Station Inn
text:
The finest bluegrass in Nashville! No pretense, just world-class music. Always worth the cover charge. 

The Station Inn as as casual as it gets in Nashville. That being said, it's primarily a listening room; that is, people come to hear the music and respect the musicians by not chatting while they are playing. 

About food and drink: if you don't like ballpark food, then you should probably eat before arriving (shows usually begin at 9pm anyway). It's a hot dog, pizza, beer, and soda kind of place. If you drink beer, go for whatever local Yazoo is on tap. Bottled water available. 
People come here for the music, not the libations.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Multi level bar with entertainment on every level. No Johnnie black & no bulliet bourbon. This seemed to be the only bars on broadway without these liquors. We were also charged two different amounts for two different rounds with the same items.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This place is awesome!! The live music is awesome!! The food, drinks and atmosphere is great! All the bartenders are very attentive! Expect to spend a lot of money because the drinks are HIGH!! But had a great time!

name: Live On The Green Music Festival
text: I can't believe this music festival is free! get here early and you can get five dollar parking. Amazing selection of food trucks that have won best of Nashville awards for many years. Such a great atmosphere and even Festival T-shirts are only 15 or $20. Everyone should come here at least once though I guarantee you if you come here you're going to want to come back every Thursday!

name: Famous Nashville
text: It's a shame this place looks so good when they are either short staffed ( all the time ) or workers who don't care.    Music is good, food is good, drinks are good when you can get them.   There are too many other places with the same thing including good service.   Don't waste your time here

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great bar, I was there twice on my visit to Nashville and the music was really good both times, it's a tourist spot, but an enjoyable one! I'd recommend it.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
I've visited Honkey Tonk Central a few times and it's always a total blast. It's definitely more of a chill atmosphere earlier in the evening, but as soon as the sun goes down the real party starts. I absolutely love grabbing a beer and hanging out on one of the third floor balconies. It's great for people watching over Broadway! 

The music varies, but they generally have some very talented acts who play all of the country classics. 

It tends to get very crowded in the evening - it's definitely a bachelor/bachelorette haven, but as long as you go in with that mindset it's not that bad. 

The bathrooms have always been clean when I used them and the drinks are (in my opinion - coming from Orlando, FL) fairly priced.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Visited this location when me and my roommate were new to Nashville and looking for a new hangout spot. Giving it a one star is very generous of me! Service was terrible, management was even worse!! 
It took over 17 minutes to get mine and my roommates beer. I order their Mac and cheese and it came out cold, and tasted like it had been sitting for quite a while. My roommate order their burger, after being told they were out of TWO of her first choices. Burger was terrible, ordered medium and came out well. 
After mentioning to my server about how disappointed I was with the whole evening, all she did was offer me a free dessert and did not try to fix the situation at all. 

The music was so loud our server was having to yell at us and I left with a massive headache. 
The service was horrendous and the young blonde manager who gave me a dirty look after I complained, was so rude. 

The restaurant was dirty, the food was terrible, and the staff was worse!

Please save your time and money by not even entering this establishment!!!

name: The Station Inn
text: This place is AMAZING! We are from the LA area and we would never be able to experience something like this back home.  We went on a Sunday, open jam session. What a surprise! Amazing musicians playing Bluegrass and an equally great crowd!! NASHVILLE has such a unique music scene and the people make the experience even better. Will definitely be back!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Very modern and comfortable venue.  We were there the second day after their opening.  On the 1st floor they have a few couches up front by the stage along with comfortable booth and table seating.  Nice bar area too.  They have a large variety of cold beer on tap (28.6 degrees) and a nice variety of food selections.  Had the Chicken Caesar Salad and the  Goo Goo Cluster Brownie Sundae - both were good.  See their menu online at their site.  Server was friendly and efficient and gave good  food suggestions.  The acoustics were good also.  Planning on going back this weekend!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Mediocre food and an hour wait for a table. The night we went here there was a big football game on and the crowd could have cared less about the live music. This lack of engagement made the band bored. So it wasn't the best situation. Hopefully it's more fun on a regular night!

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
As of today I have attended 4 concerts at Ascend Ampitheater and each and everyone has been fantastic and AFFORDABLE! 

Getting to the heart of downtown nashville and parking is usually the most expensive and annoying part of any of our great downtown venues but Ascend is right on the river and you can park for all concert across the bridge for $5, thats hard to beat!

After concerts you are walking distance to broadway and SoBro, so you can always find something to do downtown.

As for the food inside it was all actually good too, the frozen lemonades were the best i've had at any entertainment event, and the food was quick and not too overpriced.

If you are going here for a concert I would recommend getting seats closer to the stage as the Lawn fills up quick, but there really isnt a bad view in the house.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Disappointing. The hot chicken sandwich was a huge disappointment. I'm not sure there was chicken on the sandwich, it was a flat piece of breaded, fried something covered in hot sauce. Fries were good but you can get them at half the cost at any fast food place. The pickles? Delish! When I commented how good the pickles were, the bartender brought me extra. 

And the bartending staff was also disappointing. There were two young guys who had zero skills in the noticing there were people needing drinks department. If it weren't for for bartender Lauren, I would have sent back the food and left. She was professional tho I suspect she knew the food was sub-par but her attentive and friendly personality made me still want to pay the bill. 

The location is good...towards the end of the rowdy Broadway crowd. The 7-9 pm band was great (earlier band not so much). I'm confused by the entire experience.

name: Music City Male Revue
text: Our group of bridesmaids took our wonderful bride to the Male Revue as part of her bachelorette party, and we all had so much fun! Having a drag queen narrate was the highlight, and the dancers were all so energetic and fun! (Not to mention easy on the eyes.) This really added to our trip to Nashville, and I would do this again. Make sure to get a table - it's worth paying a little more.

name: The Station Inn
text:
Well thank heavens.  I've been "saving" my 200th review for something Bicentennial-Worthy and this is definitely it!  
Hubby and I are rarely home together during the week as we both business travel a lot.  This week we decided to finally check out one of the classic Nashville attractions, The Doyle & Debbie show at The Station Inn.  OK, the bar itself would get a 4 from me and I'm sure there are those who would trash it to pieces.  However, it is what it is and it's not pretending to be anything else ( much the same way as John A's over in Music Valley).  Bring cash, don't expect fancy drinks or an extensive menu of apps, get over yourself and have a good time.  The prints on the walls reflect some of the great talents that play or have played here.  I hope it never changes.

Now, for the show.  I was excited to see it although I was kind of dreading a night of jokes that might take digs at some of my opinions that don't necessarily line up on the same side of the aisle as some folks around these parts.  I mean, I can hang...but it gets tiresome.  I had nothing to fear as it turns out.  This show is just flat out funny.  Oh my...the in your face humor/satire is great but it's the subtleties that really get you.  The uneasy smiles, fidgeting and general awkwardness are hysterical!  And the show...oh my...I don't want to give anything away but it's some of the best satire ever.  The kind that has you wondering if it really IS satire at all.  It's that good.  I'm going to drag every guest we have from out of town to The Station Inn for this show.  Go and have fun.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Bu far my favorite bar in Nashville. Cheap drinks with an amaxing atmosphere and people. The bands and levels on each floor keep it interesting while the writing on the walls allows you sketch your name into history. Beautiful views, beautiful people, and only great times!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Kevin the bartender is the best!! I recommend this place for before dinner drinks or late night!

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Great little place. Good bands and drinks. If you are looking for a chill place this is it.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This is the best place in town.  Great bands and outstanding service. Everybody is very kind. Sound system has good quality.   Definitely a must see spot in Nashville.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: This venue is beautiful! Nashville did a great job making a comfortable, well lit, nicely staffed and right on the water home for their newest venue. We saw the 3rd show at The Ascend and this was the 4th concert we had traveled to in a week and of all the venues and shows we saw this week this amphitheater tops the cake for enjoyable and comfortable viewing.  The city served as a beautiful backdrop to the perfectly lit stage. Staff was nice and we witnessed a few partiers be comforted on their trips in a way we viewed as positive for anyone in their situation. Happy show goers are a great thing to have at a venue as the positivity spreads far in these things. The bathrooms were kept clean and checked upon by staff frequently through the evening. I only witnessed the women's bathroom and was very pleased to have such a clean restroom (and while on the road I must say is still the cleanest I have seen), but I was told the men's room experienced longer wait times and supposedly have less stalls then the women's, but overall were still nice. We very much enjoyed this experience and although we live far away we will definitely be back! Thank you also to Live Nation!™ for your helpful and friendly staff, this experience was furthered by all your employees on 8/4/2015.

name: The Station Inn
text: This really was one of the coolest experiences that we had in Nashville. Reading about the cool things to do here, we kept hearing that the Station Inn would provide a unique Bluegrass Experience. We stumbled in for a Bluegrass open mic night so to speak, and were blown away. There in the middle of this small place was a circle of artists that ranged in age from children to grandpas playing their respective instruments harmoniously. We grabbed a couple of seats - which aren't fancy by any means and enjoyed the show. The bar is really divey - most of the seating is standard metal folding chairs. There are a couple of double seats along the back wall if you are looking for something more comfortable and you have a date. There is a snack stand that sells beer by the bottle and other drinks. For snacks they have pizza, nachos, popcorn and some other random pre-packed items. Nothing fancy about this place - but it will be an awesome experience. As we sat there, we saw person after person walk in and join this ever-growing jam session. Station Inn is right in the middle of the Gulch, and music starts at 8. So a prefect after-dinner spot.

name: Nashville Underground
text: NYE at Underground in Nashville was one of the worst experiences getting in to the place for the 20 guest we had so called VIP table which was horrible to get that cost 4000 to rent. I complained about a horrible door guy to Tom D. who was my contact supposely only heard from him once and said a Kelley was going to call to give me details never contacted me. Get to Underground and Tom is the door guy rude as anything just asked I have a 4000 table and my guest frozen outside. He ignores me and complain straight to Tom D today just to keep it to themselves and I and he is rude again in his email trying to blame my group for not coming all together. I would not get any VIP table at this place no matter if Nashville is sold out

name: Nashville Underground
text: Their Nashville fries taste like arbys fries, but they are straight. Fricken bomb.com y'all. Salads are humongous and super yummy. I got the chicken caesar, muy bueno. Chicken tenders were okay. They were saltier than expected. Roof top is the bee's knees. Good view of all of Broadway since it's at the end of the street.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Stopped here on a Sunday night and Monday afternoon. I'd say this place was almost as equally packed both times. We were able to get seats both times, once at a large table, after about 15 minutes of looking for one and the second time at the back end of the bar. We didn't eat here, just came to enjoy drinks and music. The music here was great! They played a lot of crowd favorites and were very entertaining.

My complaint about this place would be the slow service, when we were at a table it took sooooo long for our waitress to come back...on Monday when we sat by the bar it was easy to see why...the waitresses spent 1/3 of their time working and 2/3 of their time standing around, complaining about customers and watching the basketball game! I mean, it was really uncomfortable hearing them make fun of a patron because they didn't want a lot of cranberry juice in their drink, or asking for something else specific. The waitresses would throw glass and empty cups into the trashcan behind us and send ice and other bits of trash flying into the air and onto the floor. When we sat down the one bartender completely ignored us, I assumed her job was to only take orders from the waiters because it was blatant, but then I saw her serving the customers right next to us so it was clear she just doesn't like money. We stayed for one drink and left, it wasn't worth the hassle of listening to the rude waiters and dealing with the staff. Being on Broadway you can find a great caliber musician at one of the many bars there, you would think they would fight a little harder to keep customers happy!

Personally we liked the music at other places better, so if this place is full you are better off somewhere else!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
It was a worst experience they kick us out thinking we were the condensation coming from the air
But if your ever visiting Tennessee this is the worst spot ever

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text: First time at 3rd and Lindsley, specifically to catch Vince Gill with the Time Jumpers. Unfortunately, Vince didn't make the show, but am awesome show nonetheless. I actually don't think Vince would have added anything to the experience since the band was amazing. Our server Garret was very attentive and polite. This venue fills up quick on a Monday night so get there early. We arrived a little after 6:00 for an 8:00 show and seating was filling up quick.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
The bartender upstairs was very personable and changed one of the screens to the desired football game that was on. Their bloody Mary's are hands down one of THE best bloody Mary's I have ever had, as they are homemade and not some Mr. T's mix. 

They have a pretty decent selection on their menu, but I ordered their seasoned fries and beer cheese dip. My friend got the mac & cheese bites, but I guess they weren't too good since she only ate a couple and ate my fries.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
We went in there on Wednesday, May 11th and I liked it right away.  This place has 3 floors and each floor has a huge bar and a stage for live music.  I was surprised that they had bands playing in the middle of a weekday there.  That was great.  We are from San Jose, Ca.  and I wish we had a place like that here. 
     We didn't order any food there so not sure what they serve but since it's a bar and grill you can pretty much guess what they have.  The second floor was closed for some reason I don't know.  But both bands on the first and third floor were playing country music and they were really good.  
     The bartender on the third floor was very attentive.  She didn't make us wait to order our drinks which I really liked.  So many bar and grills I've been to where the bartender kind of ignores you for 10 minutes while they bullshit with people at the other end but the barkeeps here don't do that.  They help you immediately.  If you get there and the first floor has no place to sit down simply go upstairs and you can find a spot at the bar.  
     I will definitely go back there when in Nashville.   Great place.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Was here with a group of 9 on Friday night. We decided not to go back on Saturday or Sunday. There are better places to grab a drink and hear great live music. Our table order some food and the waitress added an 18% gratuity to our tab. I get it at a restaurant but not when you are ordering bar food and buying drinks ( and a lot of them too!) She pulled the same stunt when she brought us a round a shots. YOU WANT $18 TO BRING US SHOTS FROM THE BAR TO OUR SEATS WHICH TAKES ABOUT 30 SECONDS OF YOUR TIME???!!!! GET REAL! Never had that happen anywhere before and won't happen to me again because I will not be back. Try Tin Roof or The Stage. Those places don't try to hose their patrons.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: So they have a extensive beer selection as well as over 20 on draft. The food was just ok. I had s brisket melt that was good but with a little more work would have been fantastic. My mans burger was also good but the party was more like a frozen patty. Now his coleslaw was super fresh and obviously home made and he lived it. I had there o ion rings and they melted in my mouth. A solid bar good place

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: While this is obviously a tourist centric bar (being in the heart of Broadway) I still loved this place and was by far my favorite stop on my trip to Nashville. Obviously not the best choice in alcohol (basic mixed drinks and beer) but the atmosphere was great. Three levels of live music with friendly bar tenders at each stop.
