There were plenty of seats, food, and good music to go around. I recommend the top floor as its a little less crowded than one and two. The place is loud but not ear drum shattering. I could clearly understand the band and had a blast singing and dancing to all the songs. Great stop if you're on Broadway and want a cheap drink and great entertainment.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Typical overpriced Nashville bar, drinks were good but holy cost Batman. We were on the rooftop which has an excellent view of the river, but it's really only good for one drink.

name: Nashville Underground
text: First time to Nashville, just had to come downtown to Broadway. We stumbled across Nashville Underground and it was beyond the best taste of Nashville that we could have ever asked for. We went up to the rooftop and met our bartender, Bobby Two Times, he has the heart and soul that we were looking for in the Music City!! The Hot Chicken was to die for and wish that I could enjoy it on a regular basis but our service superseded all! Thank you Bobby Two Times for putting such a wonderful impression of this lively city!

name: Nashville Underground
text: We hit Broadway on our Nashville trip and were blown away by how busy it was! We walked all of the way down to the what looked like the end and found this place. Turns out that was best because this place is so much fun! Great food and a super friendly staff! We had a great time there and wanted to share!

name: The Station Inn
text:
This place was great!! The music was excellent. It's definitely a neighborhood divey-kind of bar (clean, but not fancy at all) but very enjoyable.
I'd definitely recommend getting there early -- less than 45mins in advance and you'll have trouble finding a place to sit.

name: Nashville Underground
text: The bartender Bobby 2 Times made our evening an experience to remember. Don't know what you want to drink? He will create you a one of a kind beverage. Great time! Will be back.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Our daughter lives in Nashville. We visit Honky Tonk every visit. We always love the music and love that this place is huge and can handle the crowd volume without seeming crowded. It is on the corner and is three floors with balconies that over look Broadway. The last two times we have been lucky to have the same bartender by the name of Jordan. She is great. She makes great mixed drinks which is hard to sometimes find on Broadway. We also heard a great up and coming singer by the name of Jackson Capps. We stayed for his entire set. Look him up and visit him on stage at HTCentral. Also, look for Jordan!

name: Famous Nashville
text: Delicious Manhattan made by our favorite bartender, Emellee.  The Famous Saloon has a nice, clean atmosphere.  Guitar pick murals are unique enough to stop by and grab a drink.  Heard a great new artist, Chris Cole.  He was great and had plenty of talent to rock out requests on a whim. I will definitely stop back to this place when I am in town again.

name: The Station Inn
text: One of the best things about hosting first-time Nashville visitors is we're compelled to do touristy things we might not otherwise do. As a 7 year resident of this area, a visit to the Station Inn was long overdue. I'm not really even a bluegrass fan, but the two bands we saw (both from Indiana, ironically) were great. Almost all seats were taken by the time we arrived, but we found a place to stand that wasn't in the way and offered a great view of the stage. This is definitely a must-visit for anyone visiting Nashville, or those of us who have lived here a long time and never been.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Yet another fun stop on the Honkey Tonk Strip! This place has no cover, just like all the other bars on the strip. I think that this place was only one floor, but I'm not 100% sure. This place is on the corner with the entrance toward the front of the room alongside the stage. So it was easy to com in and start dancing without having to muscle through a crowd of people. The night I was there the band was amazing, hopefully they were a regular band, and they were a request band. There was plenty of dancing going on here. The bar was in the center of the room, so there wasn't much overcrowding while waiting to order a drink.

name: Famous Nashville
text: The rooftop had the best view of the city and Cumberland River. Moscow Mules were delicious!

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
4.5

When living in Music City, you expect great music and great concerts. All genres of music come here and I'm always on the look out for some great shows. This summer the Ascend Amphitheater has a pretty amazing line up and when my boyfriend told me he bought tickets for Portugal. The Man, I was pretty excited. However, I was a little nervous about two things. One, he got the lawn seats so I didn't think the view would be great. Two, it's an outdoor venue so the experience all depends on the weather that day. I just crossed my fingers and hoped for the best!

We went to the concert on a Saturday night. The venue is in a really nice location. There is $5 parking across the pedestrian bridge so it's just a short walk over. We were pretty early so we were able to grab a drink downtown and then walk to Ascend when we were ready. We got to Ascend around 6:30 so make sure we got a good enough seat for the show at 7:30. Check-in was quick and easy. They check your bags so don't try to sneak anything in. There is food and drink for sale but of course everything is pretty expensive. At first I was shocked to see the price of beer at around $15, but then I realized the cans were pretty big. I think they were 24 ounces so really you're paying $7.50/beer. That's not much worse than a beer downtown. I didn't look at the food options but I did see a food truck or two. I was pleasantly surprised by the lawn seats. The lawn is on a slope so seeing the stage is no problem. We got a seat right at the front of the lawn and had a perfect view. We just brought towels to sit on but you can bring low chairs or rent chairs. I was worried about the people constantly walking back and forth between the lawn and the seats, but security does a nice job of keeping people moving along. They don't allow people to sit on the ledge of the lawn. They don't allow people to linger or watch the show in the walkway. People might complain about this but the people in the lawn paid money to see the show too so not blocking our view is just common courtesy. The sound of the show was very loud and I had no problem seeing the stage. The lawn seats are a pretty good deal! They are about half the price of the normal seats. I had a blast at this show and would definitely come to another show here! 

Now here is the warning. It's an outside venue. Sometimes it rains. That's the risk you take with going to a show here. They don't reschedule shows so if it's raining, the show goes on. If it's lightning, the show might get delayed. We had some lightning in the distance so I thought it was going to pour on us. Luckily, the weather stayed clear and we had a perfect night. I think if it was raining the lawn would be a mess and it would be hard to enjoy the show. My advice, bring a poncho just in case and bring plastic bags for electronics. Do a stay-away rain dance and hope for the best! If you get a clear day/night, you will really enjoy this venue!

name: The Back Corner
text: Super chill venue with a great atmosphere to it. I came to The Back Corner for a private show, and wasn't expecting it to be too amazing, but I was blown away! I loved the set up of the venue as well as the sound. I look forward to attending more events here in the future!

name: Nashville Underground
text: The service sucks. One in our party never received his meal even after we asked multiple times. Another in our party, the meal was so over done it was like leather. The manager sucks. Need to fire the management team.  They eventually provided the missing meal. The manager adjusted our bill. Even with the credit does not excuse the extremely poor service. I do not recommend. There are too many other locations to patronize.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: My home away from home when I am in Nashville. Best place to watch a Packer's game is upstairs.

name: Nashville Underground
text: What a great experience! The food was delicious. Fried pickles and Hot Chicken Sandwich and fries were so good. And the kids said they were the best chicken tenders they've ever had! The mechanical bull was a blast. Plus everyone who worked there was so helpful and patient with our large group. Dakota was the epitome of southern hospitality. Thank you so much for a great time.

name: The Cowan
text: Far too much to post without making it a book. Piss poor customer service, don't buy VIP tickets as they're a complete scam, and the bar only has two bartenders. Good sounding venue but absolutely horrible service.

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Where to begin? For starters: They don't allow smoking! Thank the Good Lord & Baby Jesus.

For the con's: Let me put this early in the review - do NOT go for the food. It is all microwaved/deep fried FREEZER food from Sam's Club. It. Is. Terrible. Sure the prices aren't horrendous, but the food IS. The cheese sticks are straight up the "Farm Rich" ones from the green and white freezer bag. Yeah, you know the ones I'm talking about. Pre-packaged, not fresh burgers. Even the waitress said nothing was made in-house. Everything is from cans, bags, and came out of the freezer. All the other review are correct also, the service is SLOWWWW. They also got our order wrong twice.

For the pro's however: The venue is very neat. Used to be a TON smaller, and it appears in the last few years they've bought the place next door and knocked out a whole wall, doubling their size and moving the stage out another 30-40 foot. This is a cool place to come watch talented acts on a super small stage. Decent seating from the floor, ok seating in the balcony sections, however if you get the wrong table on either side, you'll be looking at the speaker boxes all night.

All-in-all, very neat, small, and intimate venue to see true Nashville talent and artists for a pittance of a price. Go! (Just eat before or after the show...)

name: Nashville Underground
text: Pretty standard Broadway bar.  Food is pretty generic.   Service is unattentive.   Nice tap list.  Live music.  Given the number of options available, I would pass on this joint.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Our uber driver warned us of this. This bar will try and double charge you. Happened to our group with 3 different servers and bartenders even when we paid cash they gave back incorrect change. We had to correct every purchase we made as they double charged us. FAKE NEWS! Sad! Folks, please double check your receipts.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
The only place hopping on a Sunday night.  With 3 floors to choose from, you can expect to find your desires flavor of... country music.  Actually, the band on our floor did play some other soft rock hits (journey, etc).  Since I'm not really a country buff (shhh), this was a pleasant surprise.

Bartenderess was friendly, and we found a TV with a soccer game on.  The bottom floor was the liveliest, with folks dancing and a very busy bar.  The top floor was a little more mellow.  Drinks are served in clear plastic cups, which might give you an idea how cheap this place is.

In the bar scene of Nashville, Honky Tonk Central remains King as the biggest and the best, catering to the widest audience.  No wonder it's the only place on Sunday to have more than a few people in it :)

name: Nashville Underground
text: DON'T GO HERE!! And definitely DON'T give them your credit card!! Had the worst restaurant/bar experience of my life. Ordered fries with gravy that were never delivered even after asking 4 times over an hour period. Mac and cheese came out after 50 minutes and sat on the bar counter in front of us for 10 minutes getting cold before we could get the barback's attention & ask them to give it to us. The bartender lied to us and said there was no way to contact the manager & lied about what his manager even looked like & then the barback was able to call the manager on a walkie-talkie. Manager was the opposite of helpful & basically said there was nothing that could be done. Left after 1.5+ hours, never got the fries at all, was told they were taken off check, paid for what we actually had and then was DOUBLE CHARGED for that order anyway (way more than what the fries were)!!! They also continue to have 2 $5 holds on my credit card that I can't get taken off the until they process....apparently just so they can literally steal more money. No apology nothing from anyone there except the Barback who was very nice. This establishment cares nothing about customers and is dishonest. It's in a great location but there are TONS of other great places around. I've never had service nearly this bad in Charleston, Boston, NYC, or any other large city I've been to. Please don't give this place your credit card so they can steal your money and put fraudulent charges on it too!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great atmosphere! We went on a Monday night. I am pregnant and was very happy not to be bombarded by sloppy drunk people. We also sat at the bar and ate chicken fingers which were delicious! Neither of is felt like having a drink and we still got excellent service!

name: Famous Nashville
text: The bartenders are great! The drinks are cheaper here than most bars in Nashville. The band ended at 10:00pm ... the bar stays open til 3:00am. I would have stayed longer, but there was no music.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: What more can i say then this is a great bar, with decent food. No matter what time of day it is you will hear live music. Music was great, bartenders were great, just a laid back chill spot that i could stay for hours!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Honky Tonk Central is proof that Nashville has a *lot* of tourists. Don't get me wrong: I appreciate the fact that HTC helped to revitalize lower Broad (I remember when there wasn't much Downtown that wasn't on 2nd Ave) but this sort of Nashville experience is definitely one you're going to want to wait and bring your out of town friends or hit up as part of a lower Broad crawl. I can see the appeal HTC has for tourists but it's the local landscape that has me a bit confused.*

By now, you know the score: no cover (much appreciated), multiple levels, big crowds of folks committed to woo-hooing their way to a good time, live music that may or may not be pleasing to the ear, tvs, drinks of fluctuating strength, etc. You know what to expect. If, for some reason, you find yourself drawn to HTC, make your way to the balcony. The breeze and view are the star attractions at this Downtown Nashville mainstay. To be able to look out and see the sea of humanity bathed in neon and walking the street in droves is a pretty powerful scene for anyone who can remember a time when such a scene wasn't common. HTC may not be my cup of tea (or, jug of moonshine) but I recognize its importance in the Downtown Nashville landscape and appreciate its role in changing a dead scene into a thriving one. It may not be a place I'd go every weekend but when I have friends in town, I wouldn't doubt that I'll be sucked into its orbit... along with the rest of you. You can't fight the moonlight.

*Which brings me back to my opening sentence: there are so many tourists coming to Nashville, HTC doesn't have to worry about a locals contingent.

name: Famous Nashville
text: We went up to the rooftop for a change of scenery from the bars on Broadway. The views are nice, and there was a DJ spinning top-40 style music, so it was definitely different from the live country music everywhere else. The bartenders were awesome and the chicken fingers were actually very good...I'm not really a "chicken fingers" person, but these were great. I would definitely come back.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
I'm not a country music fan, and after walking down all of the honky tonk, it was refreshing to hear top 40 music blasting through the street. When we walked to the door bouncer checked our ID's (like any club or bar would) and began to hold up my ID to the light, he  bent and twisted it, he even asked the bouncer if it looked real. I'm not sure how things are around here, but in the Tri-State area I'm accustomed to bouncers scan your ID. Perhaps it's a thing Nashville to invest in doing as well.

It's a shame that my first impression wasn't very good, because this place was an otherwise really good bar. We were there early so it wasn't crowded but people were slowly making their way down the honk-tonk. 

This place has an elevator so after a whole day of walking it was nice to use that instead of stairs. Their outdoor patio was really nice and you get a view of the Nissan Stadium from it. Again, the music was far better, imo, then most of the country music playing at some of the other places.

name: Alley Taps
text:
Alley Taps is located in Printers Alley but on the East side of Church around the corner from the Courtyard Marriott.  

Just opened a few months back and the inside is very nicely refurbished - a stage to the left, long L shaped bar along the wall and a front room that has cozy leather furniture. 

Entertainment is no cover, 7 days a week and a bit different vibe than Broadway - more of a jazz blues vibe that is nice.   Note the bands work for tips only so keep that in mind and feed their jar accordingly.  

Full bar, limited local beer ... but our favorite West Coast IPA was on draft which was a plus.  Full bar, 2 for 1 happy hour 3-7pm was a perk.  

Plenty of servers behind the bar kept drinks flowing so that was appreciated. 

The total area is engulfed by the music so that could be good or bad - for us we couldn't chat or talk to bartender as we sat at the bar.  The Mgt may want to consider a bit of volume control.  

The menu is limited and very much bar food. We ordered a pretzel that was over micro waved and not very good.  I would not recommend coming in hungry unless things change (or your drunk and have to  eat).  

Overall nice place, good music, decent happy hour.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Awesome rooftop bar pulling great beers. Great view and games. But the highlight was our bartender Bobby Two Times. He was personable and funny. When we told him we were from out of town he wrote out a personalized list of places we should visit in Nashville, many of which were the highlights of the trip. Can't recommend this place enough!

name: 3rd And Lindsley
text:
Great music...

...but as a restaurant: below average food, below average cleanliness, amateurish, average service. 

Go for the music but eat somewhere else. Unimaginative bar food.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Had tickets for Doobie Brothers/Steely Dan show for May 20, 2018. Show was to start at 7:30. At around 6:00 there was a Severe Thunderstorm  in the area. By 7:30 there was still rain and lightning in the area. At 8:00 with rain still falling Ascend chose to open the gates at 8:15 with yet more rain on the way. 

This was a poor decision by management. There are many music venues here in Nashville. Avoid Ascend.

name: Nashville Underground
text: 3 girlfriends and I came to town for a long girls weekend. It was recommended that we go to Nashville Underground. We made reservations for 8:30pm. Once we got inside we waited about 5 minutes for someone to come to the hostess stand. We were met by a very rude and abrasive guy who told us he had no tables available for us and that it would be at least 20 minutes before something opened up. He said he would go check to see if he could fine one. While he was gone a very friendly security guard came to us to make sure we had been helped. He told us there were plenty of tables opened on the second floor and that we should just go up there and grab one which is what we did. After 30 minutes of sitting at a table with no staff we were finally told it would at least 45 minutes before we could even place an order and much longer before we could get our food.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
While the venue manages to attact some of the better acts in town, tickets are incredibly overpriced. $100+ for some shows to sit in the grass and have your view blocked by people constantly moving & stealing spots? No thanks.

On top of that it just seems pointless to have an outdoor only venue in Nashville. This really should have been built as an indoor-outdoor venue, like stadiums with rectractable roofs. There's a high chance of rain basically constantly in Nashville...and if you're lucky enough for it to not rain you're going to have at least 95 degree heat and full humidity most of the summer. Then you have the entire winter season when they can't do shows. Plus with it being totally outdoors they've become a major headache for people who live in that area of downtown and even toward Donelson (not me, I'm not dumb enough to move by a stadium, but just saying). They're also terrible at communication when it comes to weather delays...they don't seem to ever cancel and instead think it's acceptable to push an opening act back to 10:30pm! 

Parking has been another issue...it's a major headache to get in and out and parking anywhere near there is at least $30 most shows.

Not to mention it has recently come out that supposedly the venue was built with money that was meant to go to flood victims...wouldn't surprise me in the slightest.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: This was my first bar in the city and I loved it! Actually, I wish I stayed longer...the burger was ok, drinks were good but the band was awesome! I liked how cozy it was...of course it was only like 3pm lol

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Took a small group for brunch. Bottomless mimosas were rarely refilled. They had two brunch menus that didn't agree. People were charged for sides that should've been included. B&G were lukewarm.

They fixed the bills, but it took them a while.

Seems like the locals know to avoid this place for brunch...

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: So I came in the day before Thanksgiving, right after I walked out of Kanye West's concert early (seriously, why the diatribe?) Cute place, not raucous party central but I prefer my bars quiet and cozy. Tiffany and Jimmy were hanging out there and were very good company. Take off a star because $7.50 for a cocktail? Come on.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: I'm a local and was looking for something different.  Friendly staff. Great entertainment. Beer was $5 a bottle.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This is a honky think and a place to go for drinks and hooping and halloring. We did order the hummus appetizer to go with our drinks and it was mediocre with the celery being dried on the ends and the hummus being very warm. The wine options are also mediocre but the band was great. Know why you're there. Get a beer and enjoy the music.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Loved the musicians and songs and the format of each musician sharing a story and singing one of their songs. Loved everything about the show. Our waitress was terrific tho the service can be slow at the start since a hundred drink orders go in at once. Understandable. Not a big deal.  The crowd was extremely respectful of the performers and everyone quietly enjoyed the show or sang along.  

The only exception is the waiter working the far left of the room the night we went, Friday, May 25. He'd sit down at his tables and he would talk very loudly for minutes at a time (his customers spoke so quietly I couldn't hear them) during the performances.  Distracting and unnecessary, the neighboring tables would turn to glare; he kept going. After the third or fourth time this happened I tapped him on the shoulder and asked if he could keep it down. He was incredibly inappropriate in his response. Even came by a few times afterward to taunt me. The manager needs to go monitor this behavior. Horrible. This guy needs better training or to find a job at a different kind of bar.


I updated the rating after hearing from the owner. Thank you for the response.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Every time I have friends or family in Nashville i take them here first, The bartender Horse is the person who helps entertain the evening for my guests and me lately. I dont feel like im in a tourist trap here like the rest of Broadway. We always say we are gonna be here for one drink as a group. Yet, somehow end up closing the bar down every time regardless of wich group of people are visiting lately. The bands on the first floor always rock it which is great for my family. Then for my friends who come up from Atlanta love the second floor and the roof top vibes. All in all its the perfect place for tourist and locals. I just wish Horse was workin last night to get to hang with my family. Luckily they are in town till Tuesday.

name: 360 Burger
text: i really wanted to give an extensive review about how good this place is, but sadly it was only mediocre to me :( we had an awesome server & the environment was cool & casual. the beef they use comes from grass-feed cows which I think is awesome, but i don't know I've just had better burgers.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I was in there with a couple friends on a Tuesday night drinking with some friends. I'd been a couple times before, but my bartender Jasmine made this night exceptional! She not only made sure I was taken care of but was very attentive to my friends and surrounding customers. Every time I returned to the bar she made sure I got what I needed and it was fairly busy. Will be returning, thanks Jasmine!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: This is another great live music venue in Nashville, but it is a lot cleaner and hipper than the honky-tonks on Broadway. Although the food menu is a little limited, most everything we tried was good, including the local beers on tap. I had the fried ravioli and waldorf salad while my friend had the calamari and black-and-blue salad. The salads were awesome and the ravioli was tasty but the calamari was nothing special, if not a little plain. We went around dinner time and got to see some GREAT performances by some young singer/songwriters all the way from the UK! I would highly recommend this place if you actually want to enjoy some good food and music but want to get away from the noise of the main strip.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Putting the Listening Room on our weekend itinerary was easily the best decision we made on our trip to Nashville. It's a great change of pace from the Honky Tonks on Broadway. These musicians are amazing. My wife and I were truly blown away. The drinks and food prices are more than reasonable and tasty too.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: OK so this is a must see for any fan but only have shirts up to a 2x. Also I believe everything should have museum on it not just Johnny Cash most other shops had same stuff. Staff was friendly place was clean but a coffee place inside???? Still being a fan loved it.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: One of the best times to have in Nashville. This is what music city is about. Watching brilliant, versatile artists hop from one genre to the next, from slaying one instrument to another, and even the bartender hopping on stage to murder an original rendition of CeeLo Green. The performers tell you to request anything. Really. They mean anything. :) come here to boogie with your friends and listen to a wider selection than most of the bars on the strip / anything your heart may desire. Whenever I have friends come in town, I take them here absolutely.

name: 360 Burger
text: I just got done eating at 360 burger and it was so fantastic that I had to get right on yelp and write a review. I consider myself a food connoisseur and am very critical when it comes to my judgement of food and restaurants. 360 burger is in an odd location tucked away in hickory hollow. It is a small joint with a bar that only seats a few but the interior is done very well and it has a nice ambiance. There was a live band when I went, very very loud, band was great I must add but don't plan on having much of a conversation. Good thing was once my burger came to the table I didn't need to speak. It was cooked perfectly, the pretzel bun was great, and the burger was very filling. For $7.95 it was a bargain, sweet potato fries included. I got the cilantro avocado burger, it had habanero cheese and all of the flavors came together to create a memorable experience with every bite. I usually eat very fast but I took more than 20 minutes to enjoy each and every bite of that burger. Well done! I will be back.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Wonderful music combined with good food. Relaxed atmosphere with prompt service. I enjoyed the blpt (?)sandwich. Service was good and the entertainment is wonderful. We went to see our friends Jaime O'Neal and Rod Good do a song writers showcase. There is a $15 min per person. Oh yeah, try the cheesecake. We really enjoyed it.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: We found a pretty good deal on Groupon that we took advantage of and after going, it was an even better deal than I initially thought.  If you are a Johnny Cash fan, even a casual one, I would say that visiting this museum is a must!!! Heck, I think that even if you've never really listened to Johnny Cash that this museum would be a great experience, as long as you have an appreciation for music.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: If you love Johnny Cash, you'll love this place!  It was so cool to see pictures, letters and even school yearbooks from when he was a kid....even letters from later in his life. What a treasure!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: OK, so we expected Chow-Line food, and pretty much was as expected.  Plentiful, but fairly low quality, rush through the line and finish eating before the boat moves.  We were not expecting a great meal, but did expect the music to be "Nashville" quality and maybe even hear something you had heard in the past.   The dance and choreography was unique, but after 5 minutes, nothing special.   Kate Smith would be rolling in her grave to hear the way they sang "God Bless America".  We were at a table of 10, all strangers, and we were the only 2 that remained at the table until entertainment was finished.   Walk down Broadway in Nashville and lively music pours onto the street from 30-40 bars that rate above this presentation.  They were all talented, clean, and crisp, just never had the attention of the audience.  Sorry, Nashville, you need to fix this venue.  The multi caravan of Ski-doo's playing in the wake of the paddle wheel was more memorable than the food or music.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Such a fun spot to hit in Nashville! Live acoustic county music and great food. Make a reservation and enjoy the whiskey and good vibes!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Never thought id ever end up in nashville w my familly shelly cory and me the franco's.we visited the meuseum of johny cash, now on our way to memphis to see elvis house..

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This museum did not disappoint.  I came with my mom who grew up watching Johnny Cash and we both learned a lot.  There was a lot of neat memorabilia.  It is on the small side but it was nice to get through it in 45 minutes.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Can't comment on the food. Frozé was a little disappointing. I came just for the view and WOW! The rooftop bar was spectacular! Great views, awesome atmosphere. Live music on first floor was fun and traditional Nashville. I much preferred the style of the room on the 2nd floor with the DJ. Such a fun space that works great in the day and I'm sure is even better at night. Would definitely recommend!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great atmosphere, good selection of drinks, and great service from Danielle! The live music was fun and energetic!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Awesome! There were so many awesome things! We got to see a short video on all the film work that Mr. Cash worked on--I never knew he was in so many movies! The chair he sat in on the "Hurt" video was there and the actual video was playing as well. It is a must for any fan! We also got to take pics with the man himself--with a green screen, of course.

name: 360 Burger
text: Ordered a to go order yesterday about 15-20 minutes away. There was only one table there and when I arrived my order was still not ready. Weird. It was amazing though. I wish it had more fries, but I hadn't eaten all day so it was devoured. I highly recommend the pretzel bun burger with salmon and raspberry jalapeno jam. You can thank me later. I wish they did events like a sports night or music night like they used to...it has a cute vibe and staff is always kind. I would personally set up a music night if they'd let me, because I think it's a great place for it and could bring in lots of business. A sports night, like maybe half priced burgers on sundays or Mondays would be great...2-4-1 drinks or something to draw in business..this place has potential and if they are doing those things, I wouldn't know because  there's no marketing. I've never had a bad meal here. Biggest problem here is deciding...do I get waffle fries or sweet potato fries?? Oh the struggle.

name: 360 Burger
text: Great beer selection and price.  Staff are always friendly.  Burgers are quality.  Fried pickles were a scosh too salty but the fact that there is a retro arcade next  door kind of offsets that.  Hickory Hillow needs more places like it, thankfull they are leading the way.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
We noticed there was a cover charge as we were walking up, we quickly turned around and started walking away. They said forget about the cover and just come on in and check it out.

Man this place was dead. Must've been an off night. We ended up grabbing a round of drinks and grabbed a few tables for the group. The band was pretty good, played a mix of genres and songs. 

We decided to leave after a few songs ... too many other places we wanted to check out on Broadway.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Less than a block off the main drag of Broadway, mostly the same as the other hole in the wall bars, but my group had a good time, good band, good bar service, clean individual restrooms.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Went here on a Friday night after 10 so we were only charged $6.00 to get in. It was ok, but like another reviewer wrote, they cater to the ones that keep throwing up the $20's and up. I didn't tip at all, once I could see what was going on.The later it got , the crowd started to get kinda wild, so we called it a night. The one and only time I've ever been, I may go again and then again I may not. It wasn't bad, so I'd recommend if asked for something a little different to do in Downtown.

name: Silver Dollar Saloon
text: Had a great time, tried another local Bourbon call "Bella Meade". Not bad, It had a little bite. Not to much flavor.

name: 360 Burger
text: Cilantro Avocado Burger on pretzel bun  (and organic sautéed spinach) - hella good - the hubs had the PBJO (burger with peanut butter & jelly with grilled onions!)

name: 360 Burger
text: The food is amazing, but service usually fails. This place was way better with live music. I highly recommend the salmon burger on a pretzel bun. Their fries are killer too.

name: The Basement East
text: This is my favorite venue in town! It's a great size, the sound is great, the sound guy really knows how to get the best sound out of each band, regardless of the style. The drinks are affordable and are pretty stout! This is the best place to see live music in Nashville!

name: 360 Burger
text: This place is awesome. The servers are awesome and super friendly. It was random find in Nashville and I'm happy I went!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
We have been on the General Jackson 3 times now. It has really gone down hill!

The best part of the cruise for us was being able to go out and watch the lights of the city come into view after dinner, now with the later dinner time, we actually missed it because we were eating. 

Food was decent. It is a shame that they took the buffet away, some things I just don't care for.

The show hasn't changed much in the last 3 years. It is passable. 

This is a company retreat every year. I am so glad I had the chance to experience it before the dinner format change!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: So far not good. Waiting for 15 min for drinks. Had a hair in my water. Waiting on food. We will se

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I was really really excited to visit this Museum! It is definitely a smaller museum, but there are a TON of artifacts from Johnny Cash's life and his time with Sun records. I enjoyed walking around and reading about his life and seeing such great items on display. I really enjoyed reading about his relationship with other notable singers like Jerry Lee Lewis, Elvis, Roy Orbison, etc. Music is life and brings people such enjoyment. Just walking around I was able to see so many people smiling and enjoying their time at the museum. The reason I am knocking off a star is because I think they have too many people in the museum at a time. I would have been fine waiting to get inside if that means I could have more room to browse. It just seems to be very congested in the museum which made it difficult for me to read everything I wanted to read. I think I was there for 1.5 hours, but I know I could have stayed much longer if there weren't as many people. 

I am glad I visited this museum and I do think you should go check it out if you have time. It's within walking distance to tons of bars and restaurants too so you can go here and then grab a drink or walk around some other shops downtown.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: After a much anticipated visit, we unfortunately had a very disappointing experience. After ordering drinks and food, the bouncer came over to us and told us to quiet down despite a live band playing in the background. The manager of the bar then came over and made negative comments as well about our noise level.  Coincidently, our group included the only black person in the bar. I don't want to assume this was a racial issue; however, both the bouncer and manager made it pretty obvious that it was as our group did not raise our voices beyond the average bar noise level. I will not be returning to this bar.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: I did both the cafe for coffee and the museum.  The cafe au lait was good.  The gift shop had some nice things, but hot damn is it expensive.  Who would pay $32.00 for a tank top?  The interior is nice.  The museum is cool, $18.00 is a bit pricey, but you can probably find discounts if you plan ahead.  The tour is self-guided.  There are quite a few neato things in the museum.  Guitars, gold records, outfits, letters, vidoes, photos.  Lots to look at.  It's mostly done chronologically, and separated by medium.  There are videos of his acting projects.  There is a small section devoted to Sun Records and other artists who started around the time of Johnny Cash.  The last thing is the video of "Hurt" played on loop.  I blubbered like a baby, it really is one of the best songs and videos.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text:
Sat on top floor. Live music was good, prices affordable. Had pulled pork platter which fed both myself and my wife. Had 3 local beers which I enjoyed very much.

Only think I didn't like was that I could hear the live music downstairs at the same time.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Great small but mighty museum!! Love the amount of historical items and information, easy to wonder, read and enjoy. Makes us appreciate Johnny Cash even more as a singer, human being and a positive influence on others. Take the time for this when you visit.

name: 360 Burger
text:
Both burgers were delicious, and the onion rings were crispy on the outside and tender on the inside- just like they should be. 

Our only complaint was that the entire restaurant reeked of spray paint.  Apparently one of the neighboring businesses is doing some renovation and it was polluting the air.

This place is now closed.

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text: the music is pretty much all hip hop and rap, theres a lot of smoke around and not that many people go on the dancefloor. pretty depraved

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Good food, great live music, fast service during the show!!! We saw three amazing singer-songwriters perform!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The reason they receive a 1 star is because 0 is not an option. Went tonight with a group of 12 and food was TERRIBLE! Spent over $1000 and they had the nerve to charge us $28 for a credit card fee! Cost of doing business idiots! Food was absolutely horrible for ALL of us! I would NEVER go back.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The only reason I'm giving it two stars is because the venue itself is cool and has such potential to be amazing. The staff is super friendly and were really accommodating but the food was not good :( I'm sure that this place is fabulous for drinks and live music at night time but for that only. They should hire a creative chef and this place could be a 5 star worthy establishment!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The buffet was $18 of nothing. Everything was empty. I just had old eggs and a nasty Bloody Mary. How do you fail on a buffet?

name: 360 Burger
text:
So let me say this first, I normally don't do reviews RIGHT after eating. Also I had a few other lunch plans fall through and was in the area alone and not wanting a chain burger. I had heard about this place on another site (newschannel 5's story about the new hockey rink expansion). I do take this review with a grain of salt, literally, because a burger is a burger is a burger. That aside, I know that there are a TON of things going on in this area as far as expansion and revitalization, and this is a good step in the right direction. 

To the foooooooood! I kept it simple and ordered the 360 with everything on it. It arrived promptly with regular shoestring fries perfectly cooked and NOT over salted. My first bite into this burger was an explosion of salty, savory, and meaty goodness and I didn't get a lot of the pretzel roll. However the second bite gave me the home-run rating that I crave as a foodie. There was a nice 'snap' of the pretzel crust with a fluffy yet chewy roll. They definitely knocked it out of the park with the bun! The ingredients were good, blended well, and none really overpowered the other. I am not sure what kind of onions they use, but they tasted perfect for burgers! 

Anyway I digress, this was a bit expensive for lunch, my tab being around $10. Then again I'm one who doesn't care about spending a great amount for great food.

Thanks again for reading, and if you're in the area... check it out.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Absolutely the best bar on lower broadway! Plan on spending a few hours here. The entertainment is truly outstanding  . Will be back as a soon as possible. Thankyou for making my families last nite in Nashville the best!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
This is without a doubt the GREATEST music museum I've ever been to! So many great displays & things to see, so much history & interesting. Johnny Cash was a great man & this place does him & his legacy a lot of justice. It cost me about $22 to go in & I think it's worth every penny by far!
I've been to lots of music museums but this one blew me away. I can't say enough good things about it.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text: Stopped here on vacation with a couple of friends. Great place to take fun pictures. Wasn't as big as I thought it would be, but still had fun.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: This was a great experience. You are signing up for a very touristy experience but that is what you need to do sometimes. The General Jackson is an authentic riverboat and you will sail along the banks of the Cumberland River taking in the sights and pace of life of the south. The food is good and authentically southern but it is the music the blew me away. We saw the Sunday in the South which offered up rock, country, blues, and gospel. It was amazing with anyone of the performers having the ability to headline their own shows - and I'm sure some of them do. Do yourself a favor and book some time on his boat - you will be glad that you did.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I would let Johnny Cash purr me to sleep every night if I were June. Oh, hush your judgment. Who could deny that deep voice and sad meets mysterious meets rebel demeanor? Obviously, not this girl.

On many o' Smith family road trips you'll find us taking our places with Cash songs like Daddy Sang Bass, Mama Sang Tenor, The One On The Right Is On The Left or one of my favorites, If I Were A Carpenter (and you were my lady). So it was much to my delight to find clever plays on Cash lyrics in the museum store - for instance, a bar of soap properly named: A Bar Named Sue. There were also other expected items like t-shirts (great female selection), records and the like. The space was fairly small but they somehow seemed to squeeze a custom chopper in there. Next time I'll be making my way through the museum now that I know it's only a few steps from the Las Vegas of Tennessee. 

Please note: This review is solely for the gift shop - unfortunately, I didn't get a chance to check out the museum (this time).

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Just to get a picture with Johnny was worth it. Plus don't miss his rendition of 'Hurt' at the end.  Worth the read.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: I came here with 8 of my good friends to celebrate a bachelorette, birthday, and anniversary. We went to order drinks at the bar and the bartender was a RACIST. It was Sunday at 730pm on June 25th. He told my wife that "she was on the wrong side of the border". WTF?! Never coming back to this place again. The drinks are terrible as well. Do not spend your money here.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great service, waitress was outstanding, food/drinks very good, but the Merch lady was horrible. Been around people selling Merch for 20 years, including Dierks when he came to Fort Worth and she was not only rude, not helpful, acted like we were a inconvenience, we bought nothing. Unlike Luke's, Blake's, And Jason`s where we bought items. I have a friend who's friends with DB, don't think I won't pass it on! Thanks!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Music was incredible!!! Loved the show!!!

There is a $15 minimum for F&B...which is ok. For the best experience...order 2 drinks after seating because you're not likely to see your server again. Eat somewhere else...we were a group of 6...all thumbs down on the food...

name: The Basement East
text: Great venue, great sound, amazing night. HOWEVER they wouldn't let my friend come in due to him RESEMBLING someone who is banned from the premises. I was disappointed to hear he couldn't come along to enjoy last nights show all because of a resemblance to someone else. Are you going to kick out every bearded long haired mid twenties man? There goes your demographic.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: We really enjoyed our ride on the General Jackson! The staff were very friendly and extra accommodating. The music was fantastic and the cruise up river was fun. The buffet lunch was ok. The food was pretty good, not amazing.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: If you are in Nashville then you must go to Dierks Bentleys Whiskey Row. Good food, good music, great service. Frankie was our server and she was the best. If I am ever back in town you know I'll be at Whiskey Row

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
Fun way to spend the afternoon.  We took the 2 1/2 hour midday Sunday cruise.  The buffet is ready as you board the boat.  Some reviewers have panned the food offerings, but I really don't understand why.  Maybe they were expecting individually prepared meals. It's a buffet, folks.  Enjoy.  Pulled pork BBQ, BBQ chicken, mac and cheese, beans, salads and dessert.  All very good and plenty of it.  Wait staff were as friendly as could be.  They kept our water and iced tea glasses full, which is not to be taken casually on warm days when hydration is important.  There is of course a full bar (several of them in fact) as well.  

The show starts about thirty minutes after boarding giving everyone a chance to eat.  It goes about 50 minutes.  The show itself is OK.  It's a musical revue and the performers are good, but the musical selections didn't wow us and we've certainly experienced better acoustics.  Still, it's a fun experience and we have no complaints.  If you want world class music and acoustics, go to the Ryman or the Opry House.  If you want a riverboat experience, this is the place.  One reviewer complained about the costuming.  Geez, get a life.  It's stage costuming and nothing out of line.  It's a family oriented event and no one will be corrupted by the experience.    

By the time the meal and show conclude, you've cruised down the Cumberland to downtown Nashville.  The crowd moves from the air conditioned main cabin to the outside decks to take in the views.  Lots of great pictures to be had.  Kind of fun and different was the legion of jet skiers that followed us doing jumps and other aquabatics in the wake of the big stern wheeler.  Up on the hurricane deck is more musical entertainment and another bar.  Spend the hour cruise back to dock listening to music, watching the jet ski entertainment, taking in the views, or going back into the air conditioned main cabin if the heat gets to be too much.

Go and have fun.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Originally I suspected this place to be "too big name" but found the entertainment was on points- 3 floors to choose from, good was great, customer service was friendly.  This place delivered.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: For starters Jenna is the most amazing bar tender! I was consistently and attentively attended to. My experience with Jenna made my Nashville experience. She was profession, watched out for other women's safety, and was genuinely kind. I highly recommend this bar!!!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: If you are a Johnny Cash fan this is a MUST see. So many artifacts and memorabilia of Johnny Cash and his family. I loved listening to how his songs have progressed with the ages and learning more about his younger life. I think everyone I was with left learning something new and appreciative of Johnny Cash and his music. I wish the Johnny Cash kitchen was open, however it looks as though they are still working on it.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Really good food and live music with @ASeier. My husband and I had a great time!! We ordered the scramble bowls--definitely a must see in Nashville's music scene.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: First time to Nashville and wandered past this place and the music was awesome! Wound up spending the rest of the night there. It's got 4 different levels with 3 different bands. We stayed downstairs at the bar because Hannah G was taking care of us and there was no way we were leaving her - she was the best!!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Such a great time and GREAT music. For semi home bodies like me, I recommend the se one floor. Small but still get to enjoy the music and mini bar

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Loud and fun place a little much for 1 in the afternoon our server Ashley was good. It's a check of the box type of place in a tourist trap street.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Pretty cool museum. There's a ton of things that were in his house that they displayed. There's headphones to listen to some of the music. Albums all over the wall and all historic information. The cost for 2 adults was a little under $45. Pricey & nothing included. You can take a picture with Johnny Cash down through digital imaging, but for an additional charge. We didn't do it, but I believe it was $20 more

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: They literally told us we each had to spend $25 because we were a large party (it was my friends bachelorette) and fed ALL of us drinks that had diluted alcohol. We literally couldn't taste the alc in our drinks and the shots hardly burned our throats (v telling). They ended up not making us pay the $25 because we complained. The atmosphere was cool tho !!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: Overall my group & I enjoyed Losers Bar & Grill during our vacation to Nashville. We came across Losers on Saturday evening where we decided to hang out on the 3rd floor. The performers Tori Allen & Les Hall were absolutely incredible. We enjoyed them so much we decided to go back on Sunday evening to watch Les Hall perform again. We able to enjoy cocktails and food while at Losers. There was a mix up on Saturday evening with one of the individuals food but thankfully that was resolved. On Sunday there was a mix up but the bartender apologized and we were grateful to resume our nice evening. I suggest this bar to anyone stopping by Nashville and for locals. You need to see Tori Allen & Les Hall perform. We were blow away by their talent!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: My favorite place to go in broadway. Always GREAT, live music. Fantastic drinks worth your money, a good, crowded area up near the stage if you want to dance/sing a long, but more space and chairs in the back if you're in the mood to relax and talk. Nice staff, have never been disappointed here!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: A dress code on Broadway? I'm sweating my buns off on boardway and I cant wear shorts without a belt loop?

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: A few thing went wrong, we had a server Alexis N who looked like she disinterested in her job.  She didn't make eye contact with her customers.  She appeared to be tired. Secondly I'm not sure what a 3% tech tax is.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I honestly don't know why this place only has three and a half stars. This was hands down the best place I saw in Nashville. My family and I tried to get into the bluebird cafe twice to no avail, and we found this place by chance online. We bought tickets online an hour before the show with no problem, and I am so glad we did. The food was great, but the food doesn't even matter compared to the singers. The three artists I heard were incredible, the vibe was incredible, I just loved it so much and left feeling so inspired and happy. Please, please come here. Take your friends, your family, come by yourself even, you will not be let down, I promise.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Good place to hear music talent in Nashville. However service food and cocktails poor

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
If I could give zero stars, I would because, based on our experience, this place doesn't even deserve one star. We ordered drinks and two appetizers and the total came out to $49 before tax and tip, and we were told the total was $60 even. With only four people in our party, the tip should not have been automatically added since that's only done for parties of 6 or more. And the service fee/ tech fee of 3% would not add up to the additional charges we had to pay. 

When we asked for an itemized receipt, our server said she couldn't do that and insisted she "wasn't overcharging" us. 

My only regret besides coming to this establishment, was not getting our servers name. I definitely would not recommend this place and would not come back.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Omg absolutely loved it here.  Great service.  We got stuck in rain storm and they weren't open yet.  They let us in.  Such amazing workers.  No one else on broadway opened there doors.  They gave us menu and smiled.  More people came in. Service and food was awesome. It was Thursday and they gave us the brunch menu.  Omg it was so good.  Service was impeccable wish I knew our waitresses name.  She was so sweet. Place filled u fast. Everything that came out looked very appetizing

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
An alternative to the Bluebird Cafe, the Listening Room offers a more spacious spot to listen to up and coming artists in Nashville. 

We enjoyed the country/folk music and stories from the four performers, with two of them standing out for their talent. They played for about 90 minutes and stayed for pictures and signing or to chat a little. The nice thing about small venues and people who don't have big heads is this personal touch. While you only pay about $5 to get in, there's a $15 food and drink minimum, which is a little hard when you don't drink. The menu items are also not too expensive. The food menu is not that extensive and nothing to write home about, though the Brussels sprouts were okay.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Amazing.   Love the music and the artifacts that were portrayed here.  Loved what he did for prison reform.  It's really small.  They bring you through his whole life here up u til his very last music video for "Hurt"

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Kate McGaffin is the best and sweetest waitress!! My fri new and I always have a great time at this bar and are always treated well and with efficiency when we go! High recommend checking this bar out!!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
We booked the evening cruise, the first hour was on the deck and a band played for us.then,  we went downstairs where the show and dinner are being held.
The show only runs for the last hour and it was ok, not professional as the other shows I have been to. Even though we were supposed to be served steak and we got chicken, the chicken was good and the food was perfect. The service was the best thing in our experience. The boat is located just across the street from opry mills, so the parking is not an issue and if you are a guest at Gaylord opry hotel, there is a shuttle runs to the show.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: My favorite bartender Jackie hooked me up with my crown apple & ginger ale!!! Made my night!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Today was Whiskey Rows first day open. We came in from the freezing cold to a warm and lovely atmosphere. They had a great country band playing (expected when in Nashville). We drank plenty of good cold bottle beer as they do not have any draft taps. The service was great, food was even better. I highly recommend the garlic fries! So yummy!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I am appalled by the lack of compassion carried out by the employees of this establishment.  We chose this restaurant out of all the fine establishments on the Broadway strip and the way we were greeted was in a passive aggressive way being told that we were not able to enter because we had our luggage accompanying us. It then proceeded to downpour and we had no where to go, and the staff stared at us and did not let us in. This is absurd, as Nashville is a main tourist attraction.  This establishment is not a good reflection of the great man, Dierks Bentley.

name: 360 Burger
text:
O. M. G. We discovered this restaurant using my smartphone and I can't wait to return! The food and ambiance were phenomenal, exceeded only by the service. Taylor our server was on the spot, anticipating our needs and meeting them. I had a new full glass of soda before the old one ran out. Simply outstanding! 

We had the 360 burger and fries. It was awesome, and justbig enough to fill you up. Not too big, not too small; and the portion of fries was generous. 

If I had any complaint or suggestion for the owners, it would be to consider music other than obscure blues. While it certainly lends character to the restaurant, it was also a little loud and distracting. Not enough to lose a star over, for sure. 

All said, we will definitely return soon!

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: Small crowd.  Friendly bar.  Entertaining country band.  What else could you ask for.  I'll be back.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Great environment , great music both night we were around . We only heard rock music , so it may be a rock and roll bar which is fine . The first band we saw was fantastic , great stage presence. If you want a large spot with multiple levels and great rock music , definitely Come check it out

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We went back to Dierks on our visit again this year. Jake still bartends and remembered us from last year, impressive memory. Once again great bartender who took great care of us and made our visit that much more enjoyable. We will be back next time on Broadway.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: I give this place 3 stars only because there is no place to sit...not even at the bar...or little benches against the walls...otherwise I could stay there all night and drink and listen to music

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: First stop at losers!  Awesome food, live country music!.  Not as noisy as the other bars, but a little quietness here and there doesn't hurt.  Had their fried catfish.  But what got to me was their fried hush puppies.  It was perfectly crispy with a touch of heat!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We arrived as the next band was setting up and sat at the bar.  20 minutes later they came by and took all the bar stools.  We left our drinks and headed out.  Incredibly rude!  Not all of us are 21 and drinking Bud Lite. They should have at least told us that we wouldn't be able to sit there.  Also, the double standard "dress code" where men can't wear tank tops but women can wear anything.  Just not the place I want to spend my money!!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: An inspiring tribute to a great artist. Displaying many unique artifacts and allowing for comparisons of different musical eras and types this museum is an incredible journey. The only lingering question I have is, who keeps that much stuff their whole life?

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: I don't know whom is responsible but this is by far the cleanest bar in Downtown Nashville! This is the first thing that I noticed about the establishment. The staff is very friendly and the drinks come quickly. No having to wait for the barmaid or tender to flirt with someone. The music was on point as well. Over all I would have to say this is a hidden gem in downtown Nashville.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: By far my favorite bar on broadway. The stage setup is awesome and the sound system is rockin! Most bands have a better variety of music when compared to the rest of broadway. Service is good too.

name: Live Oak
text: We came out to this bar on Sunday for the Patriots game because it's the best Patriots Bar in Nashville and we're from New England and love our team. We got there about 50 minutes before kickoff and the bar and tables were PACKED. That was our bad, should have figured and went there for brunch instead of down the road. I give 3 and not 5 stars for one reason only - our bartender. It was a blonde female with a colorful trucker hat working the left side of the bar. First of all she just looked pissed off the whole time - that's fine I guess as long as you are serving drinks and food without issue... but we had one huge problem with her that had nothing to do with her not so friendly personality. The Nashville Patriots fan club had a singer for the National Anthem before the game (she was phenomenal). Everyone in that bar got on their feet, took their hat off and gave respect... EXCEPT HER. Not another bartender moved but she kept her hat on and continued popping bottle tops off bottles... literally the only person in that bar not paying respect. You want to Colin Kaepernick (or however you're spell his name) and take a knee go for it... but to keep moving and making noise was so disrespectful I wanted to scream. If it wasn't the beginning of the game and the fact that we wouldn't get another drink after I would have spoken my mind but I held my tongue. I hope management sees this and says something to her about it. Unacceptable.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Ive never been so mortified about a bar/restaurant in my life. I came to Nashville for my 40th bday and just wanted to have a good time, yet everyone was so aggressive and abrasive. People wanted to start fights everywhere my friends and I turned. We even gave this bar a second chance our second day in Nashville and low and behold it was the same thing. Not only do patrons get aggressive, so do the Bouncers. I accidentally bumped a bouncer while he was cleaning off our table and he got in my face. Then he tried to be aggressive toward my cousin for my bump. So inappropriate and not necessary. Then the bartender sells me $75 in beers and we get told we have to leave, unable to finish beers that were just sold do us. Don't sell beers if we aren't allowed to drink them. So disgusted and disappointed. I didn't think Dierks Bentley would approve of this reputation. I will never return.

name: 360 Burger
text: Service was good but none of use were impressed by the food. It was good but didn't live up to the hype everyone was making it out to be.  Small little place with live music and a bar. It was ok but not amazing.

name: Madame Tussauds Nashville
text:
Wax figures was never my thing. This is the first time I visited any Madame Tussaud's Museum and this may not be my last!

The figures here are so realistic. I love how they were set up with the perfect spot lights. They were also staged in that exact moment that make them iconic!

Musical theme ROCKs! Photo friendly made the experience so much fun. Pretend you are part of the crew/performers did make the experience more interactive.

Purchasing tickets from their websites would save you a few bucks. We ended up just standing at the entrance ordering the tickets while the actual ticket office was empty.....

Locate inside Orpy Mills so quite convenient as you can do some shopping after the visit too!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
My wife and I were on vacation in Nashville and a friend of mine recommended the Johnny Cash Museum. So cool!

The place is on the main drag in Nashville and it was packed! We had a Groupon, so we saved some money.

It starts off with some hostory on the walls, but after experiencing it, I would almost go from the end to the front.

The best part of the museum is a station where you can listen to other bands cover Cash songs. You could spend 2 hours there if you wanted to.

They also have a cool wall with every album cover displayed. They also showed some of his theatre expositions from the 60's and 70's.

I would have loved to see a Highwaymen concert with him and Willie and Kris. A definite must see in Nashville!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
Really nice rooftop patio. Had both playoff hockey AND the Raptors playoff game on, so as a Canadian that was surprising and great! 

To be honest the reason for the 3 stars is because the rooftop bad legitimately sucked. All 5 members of my party agreed on this. The lead singers voice was not nearly as good as their pianist, I just wanted him to shut the hell up. They played way more rock than country (rock is my favourite) and yet the guy kept playing slow, non-party songs. Like it bummed the crowd whereas every other bar around is bumping (as were the floors below, to be fair). 

The first few floors legit had bands playing music so loudly it hurt my 25 year old ears. I never in my life thought I'd complain about music being too loud, but knowing Kid Rock I can totally see him telling the manager, "Make sure we are the loudest damn bar on the strip!" 

The food didn't look amazing - oddly it was standard bar food and not southern bbq (like every other bar on the strip). Seemed odd to be different and yet boring. My buddy actually got a beef sandwich of some sort (can't remember which one) and said he liked it, so there's that.

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: Cheap beer.  Food is great!  Love their nachos, pizza and homemade fries!  But we really come for all the great bands they have that feature so many talented artists!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: My husband is a huge fan of Johnny Cash, so we of course had to make a stop here. When it comes down to the nitty gritty, I guess it is a cool place and the price point is decent. My main complaint is that we went midweek in the off-season and it was absolutely packed to the rafters and it is not a large space by any means so I didn't feel as though he really got to enjoy it and take his time looking at everything. Tourists can be a pushy bunch so seeing each individual exhibit was dicey. If this museum was moved to a larger venue with a better layout, I could see it being a 5 star attraction for us. At the end of the day, definitely go see it if you are a fan but make sure you take your expectations down a notch.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
This place was kind of a miss for us this time around. I contacted them almost two months ago to inquire about reserving a table and never heard back from anyone. I called a few days prior to our arrival and the voicemail stated they did not take reservations and opened at 6pm. We arrived at 8 and were able to get a table against the first wall when you walk in. We had an okay view of the stage. 

For the most part we just weren't really impressed with the music and entertainment. I've been to a few other piano bars, Bobby McKey's in the National Harbor and Croc Rocks in Myrtle Beach, and I just don't think this one compared. I think I expected a lot out of the musicians and being in Nashville and what not but they were just ok. 

The service here was good, our waitress was handling a lot of tables but she was very attentive and fast, we didn't have to wait long for her to come and check on us. 

This place gets really crowded, by 10pm it was standing room only, and with our seat location we could no longer see the stage so we left.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Had a great experience!   Ordered the chicken wings, Mac and cheese and garlic fries, all excellent.  Drank the bourbon drink, Dierks Dram, great cocktail.   Entertainment was very good, overall a great experience.   Will recommend to friends and will return.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We stopped in several times during our week in Nashville. The bands were consistently great, the bar was consistently crowded, and everyone there seemed to be having a great time. My only complaint was they need more restrooms, and need cleaned more frequently on busy nights.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Had such a great time listening to great music and our server Hollee was absolutely amazing. Hollee never let our drinks run out and was very attentive to our needs... will definitely be back .THANKS HOLLEE

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Went for lunch with the kids. Live music was great. Drink special buy any well get the next for a dollar. We had the fried tomato's and the fried crawfish both had a good corn meal taste. My sister had the Tuna sandwich and they did over cook it but all around good.  Fun tables

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
Great place to see a concert. Of course. The history alone is reason enough to go see. Unfortunately the idiots running the ticket office is reason enough not to attempt a show. 
They went through the effort to put out a full page add in the local paper to promote a play. Offered two tickets for the price of two. Not a quick line or promo code on a website. A full page add that went to print in the paper. Great deal right?  Not exactly. When giving them the promo code that was printed in the paper, I was told that it's only for 10% off each ticket. No explanation. No acknowledgement that I'm staring at something describing a very different offer. Not even a solution to the issue. After talking to a rude ticket sales person and a bored manager who audibly sighed on the phoned after asking how you could not possibly honor a promotion that had to have been proof read by multiple people before printing, I unfortunately had to give up. 
The Opry will forever be a great place to go see an event. Unfortunately it's become more of a typical tourist trap and less of the historical icon of TN.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Beer heaven, there is a lot of space for groups here. The bar / restaurant is hidden behind the Union Station hotel.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: Wonderful tour and rich history! Guided tour lasts roughly an hour and very informative and interactive!

name: WannaB's Karaoke Bar
text: WannaB's is my absolute favorite bar in Nashville! It's a hidden gem of a place with fantastic people all around you. You get to sing on stage and enjoy the night without feeling any judgment from the patrons. My girlfriends and I took over the bar when we came in for a bachelorette party and had the best night of our lives! The drinks were cheap and there is a little window next door that sells pizza.. it's a must. Go and have a fabulous time any day of the week!

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: Was looking for a low key spot to spend with the girlfriend for our anni. This place was perfect! We were greeted by an extremely friendly doorman named Ronnie who led us into what would be an epic night. There is a $10 cover fee but it def keeps the hoodlums out. We found a spot at the center of the bar and had a perfect view of the stage. We ordered the slab of ribs with baked beans and slaw. The ribs were pretty damn good, had to get some extra sauce to go with it though. The beans were as good as beans get and the slaw was not too heavy on the mayo. But the food was not the highlight of the spot it was more so the atmosphere. At first I felt out of place, me and the girlfriend were literally the only Asian people in here. It was mainly an older crowd as well. But the band crushed the performances and everyone was up and dancing, old and young. This encouraged me to get on the dance floor and just dance. We ended up dancing the rest of the night away and went home with full bellies. Def check it out of you don't want to deal with the madness on Broadway Street of drunk bachelorette and want something more intimate.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text:
I've seen the Opry at the Ryman, and I've seen it from the back of the stage at the Opry House, but this was the first time I've seen the Opry from the seats of the Grand Ole Opry House. 

You don't have to be a country music fan to enjoy the Opry.  My BiL was visiting, so we took him to the Opry.  He's never been into country music, but we all had a great time.  I got the tickets a couple of days before the show, and all the better seats were already gone.  The screens were helpful, but I wish we'd been closer.

But even from our seats, we could see the circle on the stage that had been taken from the Ryman.  It is a great tradition.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: The worst. In a mall across from a Dave and busters. The parking lot was unmarked which left half the showgoers roaming around after a dreadful show. $150. A ticket and the show had 6 unknown performers and two older stars. Seats were church benches. Commercials for Humana were run constantly. Each performer did two songs and there were commercials between each performance. Never go there.staff was annoyed, music was lousy.total rip.off..blech

name: Third Man Records
text:
This place is off the beaten path and not your typical tourist trap. 

Awesome gift options. Listening and photo booths are nice interactive touches. 

An awesome stop for any music lover. You'll get to see Jack White's Grammy's, too!

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text: Great place, better than the San Antonio location, which me and the wife do love. Friendly waitstaff, the dude on duty knew his brews and was quite friendly despite us arriving at near closing on a sunday. Would recommend.

name: Flying Saucer Draught Emporium
text:
The location is huge! I've been to the Flying Saucer in Charlotte, which was still sizeable, but this location is beautiful and historic, much like the Union Station hotel next to it. Besides those two gems, the other businesses by it appear to be offices with pricey parking decks. 

I sat at the bar, perused their menu of beers and was so happy to see that they were the only ones to offer Highland Brewing's Cold Mountain Ale and Catawba Brewing White Zombie. For $5. I sat next to other people who were on their own so I began chatting with them. 

This is a great place for dinner, friends, or families - yes, I think so! Great staff and wonderful ambiance transports you into the past.

I thought about deducting 1 star for the parking - you have to park a bit farther on the street and even then, it's a bit hard to find parking. However, I found parking and I didn't mind walking 1/4-1/2 mile.

name: Grand Ole Opry
text: This was the best show we have ever been to. My wife and I made this our first stop in Nashville for our honeymoon. The staff was amazing and courteous. We picked our tickets up at will call and it was a seamless process. Entry was quick once they opened the doors for the show. It was hot outside so be sure to wear something you are comfortable in. Once inside the air was kicking and the show started right on time. Our seats were the best in the house. Seeing country greats perform live was breathtaking. This is a must stop if you're coming to Nashville.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: We stopped in on a whim this Sunday afternoon. We were seated promptly, and our waiter was quick to the table to get our drink orders. We ordered the ribs. These were hands down the best ribs I've had in years. These are not bony, stick robs with leathery meat. They are large succulent ribs with plenty of tender, flavorful, juicy meat. The sauce they slather on the ribs is outstanding (and we bought some on the way out).  The sides weren't special, just your standard beans and cole slaw, but I didn't really need anything to take way from the ribs, they were that good. We will be back.

name: BB King's Blues Club
text: I'd go 3.5 stars. If you're looking for the nashville blues vibe without the packed madhouse that that surrounds the honky tonks,  this is the place to go.  Great option when travelling with older people (due to the hostess /seating that is missing in the bars and a little elbow room). The house band was great!  And the floor was bouncing from the club downstairs.  It is crazy loud in there,  don't expect much conversation.  Our server was even wearing ear plugs. Food was on point,  smothered chicken with Mac and cheese was amazing!  Specialty drinks were decent.  I'll definitely come back next time I'm in the area.

name: Third Man Records
text: Super tiny. Thought they would be selling more records-- nestled into kind of a shady area. We rode bikes but would recommend driving if you can.

name: Dan McGuinness Irish Pub
text:
Live music outside, so we went inside and drank there and never went back outside. Nice move, us.

The bathroom could use some work but given this is an Irish pub I don't think that should be expected. No offense to the Irish. I know some Irish. They probably have nice bathrooms too.
