Came in on a Tuesday night because the outside sign said "Master Chef at Layla's", sat at a table across the bar, ordered drinks and then asked the bartender, Sammy,  what the "Master Chef" was for....she had no idea. She even went outside and looked up at it only to still not have a clue. Was there for a few hours and listened to a live band that was good but she still offered no insight to the marque...she just laughed it off-Oh well, I guess. 

After the first 30-45 mins, Sammy saw that we weren't going anywhere and then became attentive to our cocktails. 
It was my 1st time in Nashville and the band was SUPER loud and conversation was difficult even at the back of the bar but not pissed about it. Tis live music. Whaddaya gonna do?!?! Had a good time and enjoyed myself.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: This place was so much fun. I'm not even that much into the kind of music they played but it was just such a fun atmosphere, the band was nice, the people were all really interesting - very Rockabilly - and the drinks were average price. Really fun place to go. It's packed on a weekend.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: Sent my contact info to finsfeedback THAT DAY never heard a thing...review stands. and is reinforced

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: We visited here on vacation and stopped by with a toddle.  First of all I love a brew place that can accommodate a toddler.  The waitress was very nice and was able to adjust the grilled cheese sandwich to not include the preserves.  We got the charcuterie board with the beer bread, it was so good I could have eaten in all day.  I also got a beer and burrata salad...you had me at burrata.  This was amazing and had great flavors.  We got the beer flight, our favorite was the Southern Wit!  I would go back here again if I could!

name: 12th & Porter
text:
My girlfriend and I bought tickets to see Humming house during the grand re-opening weekend of 12th & Porter. We decided to dine at the restaurant before hand.

I have nothing but praise for this renewed establishment. The interior is hip, trendy, and welcoming. The staff is very attentive and friendly.

I had the pulled pork nachos, while the girlfriend tried the classic burger with sweet potato fries. Both tasted fantastic!

My only regret is the lack of foresight to take pictures of the food before diving in. I will definitely be returning to this establishment!

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
when I think about Margaritaville I think about vacationing as its typically the only time I'd stop in one.  We were downtown for a show and wanted to grab dinner and it was near by and seemed not to be over crowded as it was a Tuesday evening. 

My wife and I ordered 2 margaritas which seemed really watered down.  The service was a bit slow and again "it wasn't too busy on this Tuesday evening".  The food came out and was fairly decent but not memorable.  There are several options within walking distance I'd choose before coming back.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: This was the worst Margaritaville I've been to .The service was bad and the food was tasteless.  It took 20 minutes to get out drinks after we ordered them . Someone ordered a soda and waitress never did bring that . We had to ask another employee to bring us one .  Someone ordered the seafood Mac and cheese and it did not have a taste at all ,no spices, the cheese had no taste like it wasn't real cheese . I ordered the flatbread and also was tasteless.  Someone ordered the nachos which were plentiful but all the cheese was on the top of the mound so after the top layer there was nothing in them .  We ordered margaritas and there was no salt on the rim and were syrupy sweet. We were there on a Wednesday night in November so it wasn't during peak season when it was packed .  I guess this restaurant thrives on its location rather than its quality of service and food.

name: Ole Red
text: I wish I could have reviewed this place properly, but I was turned away at the door at 8:30pm when Broadway was kicking! I guess they don't like visitors. Oh, by the way, I called up see what time they close the kitchen.  10pm.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: What cool place two story's of yummy beer and live music on a Sunday.. a good joint to make good memory's

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: What a disappointment!  Jimmy Buffet would be appalled!  We were in Nashville for the weekend, and decided to visit Margaritaville.  We walked right in and our party of 4 was seated. That was the only positive thing about this experience.  When our server approached us, I asked for a bucket of loaded Coronas, something we always order when we visit Margaritaville.  Not once did she ask the other members of our party what they would like to drink.  She returned about 10 minutes later to ask for their drink orders.  Another 10 minutes before she returned with the bucket of Coronas.  We took a drink, and they were horrible.  When we were finally able to flag the waitress down, she insisted they were correct, and argued with me.  They were not filled with Lime tequila, and the tequila added was a very short pour.  When she finally decided to make them right, she returned with only 3 beers in the bucket, not 5.  Service was horrible, even though the restaurant was not busy.  When our check arrived, it was $85!!  For a bucket of beer and an appetizer!  I asked to speak to the manager, explained my issue, and he took the bill and walked away.  The waitress returned about 5 minutes later with a new bill that was $45, no explanation from anyone.  If this is how business is always done at this location, it would explain why it wasn't crowded.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: Service was great! All the bartenders were friendly and quick with drinks. The music was great ! I would recommend this place for a drink and good music they have food but it is simple bar food. I will be back!

name: National Underground
text: Ok, Hot Chicken BUT no tap ice water AND two dollars for a bottle!!  Nuts .. AND we left.. Would not AND will not recommend to anyone.. Go anywhere else for better service . RIPOFF... And I asked twice for tap ice water. Band wasn't a band.. Again go someplace else.

name: Ole Red
text: Multiple floors with a rooftop bar just like every bar in Nashville. This venue is on the smaller side compared to the other new celebrity bars. Rooftop was closed for a private event the night we were there. Sat at the second floor bar and split the redneck nachos. Very disappointing, basically a huge portion of over cooked potato chips. The nacho toppings like the chicken, cheese, barbecue sauce, and  others were very skimpy. Really just tasteless, none of the toppings were layered. Just placed on top of the chips. The 3 stars are for the bartender. He was friendly and efficient. Zero stars for the redneck nachos.

name: Ole Red
text:
Music was great ambiance was cool and service was wonderful. Food was pretty good if you like southern fried food. I wouldn't say "you have to go here"
But if your close and it's not a huge wait check it out!

name: The East Room
text: Saw Datenight here on Friday. The high ceilings and mezzanine are cool, the show was $5 at the door, and the music was pretty good. The place isn't too large, so it's always easy to get a drink at the bar and the staff are all pretty chill. There's a nice outdoor smoking area in the back where you can get away from the crowd between shows. The only bad thing is the bathrooms, there were fairly substantial lines between shows, especially the women's room.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Bridgestone Arena is a fantastic stadium located smack dab in the middle of all of the downtown Nashville action. 

I was lucky enough to escape my corporate summit in Nashville long enough to watch the Predators host the Boston Bruins on a Thursday night and I will be the first to exclaim that the Preds Arena is an exceptional one. They keep the stadium spotless and the accessibility to each floor is unmatched thanks to the fast moving escalators that are seemingly everywhere. Better yet is the seating - there truly isn't a bad seat in the house and you can get on on the cheap as $50.00 tickets nets a mid rink sightline. Of course the Beers are pricey (weighing it at $10.00 a pop for a large) but welcome to the world of professional live sporting events, right?

The locals also add a lot to the atmosphere as Predators fans may be some of the friendliest in the National Hockey League and in true Nashville style there are live bands to revel in between periods. After the game the party really kicks in as the backside of the venue spills into Broadway which is the epicenter of Music City. You will watch the entire stadium empty into the Nashville bar scene before your very eyes, it is an incredible sight to behold. 

I was very impressed with Bridgestone Arena and would definitely recommend a visit to any local or visitor alike if you get the chance to watch a game, event, or concert at this gem in the Nashville skyline.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
I've been to Bridgestone arena before and knew it would be a special experience for my daughter! So I sent my 8 year old on a fun trip to watch a Preds game with her cousins. She was so excited to go to her first hockey game!! I packed her bag (small backpack because a little girl can't remember to keep a purse on her shoulder... and frankly purses are uncomfortable) with her wallet, extra sweaters, chapstick and a pair of p.j.s just in case the game ended late. When she finally got there her aunt sent me a very happy picture of her before entering. Now once she got in was an entirely different story. At the entrance she was asked to empty her bag and throw it away. They did tell my 8 year old who was now sobbing that she could walk it all the way back to the car and come back... how nice. However, that's unrealistic for a child who has hip problems to make the treck once. It was either she throw the bag away or go home (there were 4 other kids with her so home wasn't an option). So, a very sad little girl threw her bag away and sat at a Preds game with her belongings spilling over in her lap. 

Lastly, If she brought a purse she could have walked it in. I think it's a little unfair to boys/men who wouldn't carry a purse. I think your policy is very one sided and could use relooking at. Either you make it an all around fair policy of no bags or you check bags better. There is no reason for anyone to throw their belonging away especially if it's not on your policy online! Very disappointed in how you handled things.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Had a flight. Beer was great. We liked the basil ryman but they all were all tasty. We got the hot chicken sandwich. It was ok but NOT hot like Nashville hot chicken should be. We got another sandwich with a hard-to-remember name. It had ham, an egg, curry powder, and some type of preserve on it. It was awesome! The ambience was cool and the service was great. Would recommend!

name: Ole Red
text: We went to this bar on Monday last week mid day. There was maybe a ten minute wait which I was excited about having heard lines could've long. We were seated upstairs. Server gave us menus and never returned. We luckily still had our drinks from downstairs bar we got during the wait. On our way out I saw the server and she smiled...?!  I thanked her for the water we had asked for. She said you're welcome. I then told her she never came back. She walked away. Not a good start. Super disappointed. I work for Marriott and can't really send my valued guests to an establishment with my name on it that can't remember to wait on guests. We sat there 40 min. On a positive note it's a pretty place and the music was good. Hope they get it together....

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: We went for the beer which was good but were blown away by the food. The 5 beer burger was in a league of its own. It has totally messed with my emotions.

name: Ole Red
text:
Music is why we came here 
Music is good
Food is average 
It's loud but fun
I don't know what else to say so I'm just typing til I can end comments

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I came here with a friend who had previously had a great experience at the location in Destin, FL. I had never been, but was optimistic. I was also excited for live music and food in Nashville, but that is not the experience I received. When we first arrived there wasn't anyone at the host stand for over 5 minutes. We waited and eventually were seated. There were two of us but we were only given one menu and no silverware. Our waitress came over ten minutes later to finally get our drink order (water and sweet tea). The waitress brought out two waters and no tea. We ordered appetizers and I asked for my tea. She came back with the tea which was very bad. And asked us if we had ordered anything yet. We said yes repeated our appetizers. Twenty minutes later we received our appetizers and ordered our dinner entrees. We also asked our server for silverware. We waited five minutes. At this point we were out of water and still had not received silverware. My steak came out. Still no silver ware. No water. I got up and walked to the host stand to ask for silverware after asking a different server and still not receiving any. My steak was cold by the time I was able to eat it. I ordered a Caesar salad with my steak, but never received it. The mashed potatoes were awful. I love potatoes and this was my least favorite part of the meal. Our server never came back. I sat my card on the table to indicate we were ready to pay. Twenty minutes went by. She still did not pick up the card. I went to the host stand again to see if they could locate our waitress. She finally came by ten minutes later. Still no water. I am very disappointing. I was looking forward to the live music and decent food and I was extremely let down.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
My boyfriend and I were in Nashville this past weekend for a family reunion.  After the Saturday afternoon family festivities, we decided to venture over to Broadway to get some dinner and have a drink or two.  Being that we are both vegetarian, sometimes it is hard to find places to dine out when we're out of town.  We wandered up and down Broadway for awhile, checking out menus that were posted in the windows of a few different restaurants.  Finally we settled on Jimmy Buffett's Margaritaville because we saw that they had a few vegetarian options.
The place was very crowded but we spotted a couple of empty seats at the bar.  There was a cover band on stage and the music was very loud, but pretty good.  We were greeted promptly by one of the bartenders, given a couple of menus, and we decided to have a couple beers while we waited.  The beer selection wasn't the best, but any cold beer on a muggy night like Saturday was good enough for me.  
We decided to order a couple of veggie burgers to take back to the hotel for dinner.  I ordered the El Diablo Burger (sub-veggie patty) and my boyfriend ordered the Barbecue Bacon Cheeseburger (no bacon, sub-veggie patty).  While we waited for our order, we were entertained by the other bartender on duty doing a variety of glass-tosses and bottle flipping.  It was actually really fun to watch.  Our order took bit longer than I had expected, but it was understandable considering how busy the restaurant was that night.  We each had one more beer, paid for our order (the price was reasonable), and headed back to the hotel.
We finally got back to the hotel and sat down to eat.  The presentation was nice and our server/bartender made sure that napkins, condiments, and silverware were all included in out to go bag.  The burgers were good, but not great.  The hand formed patties were a little small for the buns and a little under done for my taste (for those of you that have never tried a veggie burger, they really need to be cooked well done so that they are not mushy in the middle).  I did like the big chunks of carrot, edamame, peppers, and peas in the patties.  The El Diablo Burger was way, way too spicy for the both of us, and we generally really like spicy foods.  The Barbecue burger was fantastic.  The barbecue sauce was smoky and sweet, and the onion strings were good and crispy.  
All in all it was a good meal.  The service and atmosphere was great and the food was ok.  It's probably not a restaurant that I would frequent, but good for an occasional visit.  I would liken it to about any other chain restaurant; not the best, but good enough.  I'd say it was worth for what we paid, and definitely worth the three star rating.

name: Ole Red
text:
I generally do NOT review or post anything.  My experience this weekend at Ole Red has forced me to post a review.  As a resident of Nashville with friends visiting from out of town we found ourselves at Ole Red.  Hopes were high, results were low and I will never visit Ole Red again and I will make sure that EVERY person that I know that visits Nashville will not pay patronage to Ole Red.  Sad place, self serving and selfish.  

We stopped at Ole Red to have a drink.   With an 11 year old child, it is tough to "stop and have a drink" because children cannot sit at a bar.  I would never encourage that and agree with the general rule.  That said, you have to actually take a table.   We got our table pretty quick and settled in for a drink and an order of fries.  

We were promptly notified by "Jesse" (our server) that we have to eat food.  Okay, well we ordered fries for the kid.   Jesse was kind enough to tell me - well your splitting hairs and that is not food and we were going to be moved.  

We opted to leave.  On the way out i asked the hostess - are you guys backed up for tables?   I see 4 open empty tables and our server stipulated that people were waiting for tables.  They indicated a 20 -30 minute wait.  Not sure how you have a 30 minute wait with empty tables -  perhaps just low staffing.

Either way - doesn't matter.  At the end of the day - High Hopes, Low Results.    New moniker for Ole Red - HHLR

I will make sure that NO ONE I KNOW will ever visit this place.

If you do visit - Ask for Server Jessie - he is the sharpest tool in the shed.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: We enjoyed the music and atmosphere.  Ordered the fish and chips and they were very good.  Our server Josie was amazing!

name: Ole Red
text: Ole Red opened May 1 and it's quite nice!   Signs of Blake Shelton everywhere and there's even a phone that is for incoming calls only from Blake!  I ordered a white sangria that was fantastic and we had appetizers - tater tots with cheese and biscuits.    They have an in house chef that is amazing.  All the breads are made from scratch.   The biscuits came with blackberry jam and bourbon butter.    Can't wait to go back and try more food!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: (Was there a few years ago but I just found this saved in my drafts so I thought I'd post it!) G reat bar.  i bet it's terrifying in the daytime but it's adorable at night with it's fat colored xmas lights, license plates and red stools.  Live bluegrass most days of the week and the band that was playing when we were there (jypsi) was great.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I've never been to a Margaritaville before and had a great time. The food was great and had the BEST server. Her name is Christina and she was awesome! Very attentive without being overbearing. I'm from South Carolina and she is the reason our experience was so great. Loved it and her! We will be back 100% the next time we're in Nashville.

name: Ole Red
text: The Bar itself was immaculate, the bartenders Jericho and Tim were amazing., Great conversation, and very knowledgeable. Make sure you go to the third floor for Oysters and see Kaylie..

name: Bridgestone Arena
text: I've always been a fan of Bridgestone Arena. It's a great venue in a nice location right off of Broadway near all the bars and such. I like that security is so tight and the employees that work elsewhere in the arena are always so friendly and will often joke with you and hold a conversation. I would definitely recommend catching a concert or show here.

name: Bridgestone Arena
text:
Nice venue. Clean and seemingly easy to navigate. Didn't have to wait to use the restroom, not a single time. One draft beer was $11, and it was about a pint of beer. A 20-oz bottle of water cost $5. These prices and these remarks cover the Bon Jovi concert on February 18, 2017.

It's been a lamentably long time since I've been to a live concert--like 30 years.  The Bridgestone Arena was a great place to break that dry spell.  We were in section 101, straight ahead from the stage, a bit left of center from that perspective, and about 8 rows up.  These were great seats.  If I weren't getting older and blindy, they would have been even better seats, but for the things I couldn't eyeball, I simply had to gaze upwards to the large monitor.  Anything would have been better than the churning jumble of the people in the floor seats, where folks had to stand the entire concert in hopes of seeing anything.

I imagine that even the nosebleed seats had a splendid view of the stage, because the Arena really isn't very large.  We heard and read that the Bon Jovi concert broke attendance records for a concert at this venue, but it did seem laid back during the concert.  That's most likely because of the performer and the relatively advanced age of the attendees.  But that's a supposition...which shares most of its letters with "suppository", so take that for what it's worth.

Upon decamping the spectacle, we hiked about 4 blocks south and 2-3 blocks west before summoning an Uberide (a newly-discovered elemental wonder), because the general area was chaotic.  Broadway, which was likely already crowded, suddenly had nearly 20,000 hyped-up concert-goers dumped on it.  We got out of Dodge and retreated to the respite of the 1808 bar at the hotel next door to our hotel.

All in all, I'd like to go to another concert at the Bridgestone Arena.  It is a comfortable, clean place with short concession lines and quick bathroom access...the ultimate and penultimate qualities of a great venue.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Good beer. There's plenty to choose from.
Good food. With some vegetarian options.
Great patio. It's huge. Plenty of space for you and your tribe.
Live music. Great atmosphere.
I'm glad we stopped in while we were in town. I'm a fan.

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text:
Was in Nashville for a few days on a road trip with the girlfriend. We stopped here while wandering around Broadway late on a Monday night.

Most places in Nashville were pretty dead at that time, but Layla's was definitely alive. They had a great bluegrass band, cheap drinks, and a lot of locals and people dancing (line dancing, I think. Definitely was not skilled enough to join in). We even made a few new local friends while at this bar. This bar is one of the best places on Broadway.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: I try to find the best in every restaurant, some are just harder that others. To be fair, I went to Margaritaville on a Saturday night, after 11:00 p.m.,  after a show. I felt like our waiter just gave up. Everything was so slow. I ordered the Cheeseburger in Paradise and apparently the chefs gave up too. Zero seasoning. Now, for the good part: the French fries. They were on point. Look, if you like watching drunk bridesmaids dance to mediocre 90's country songs, have at it. If you want decent food and service after 11:00 pm, you may want to try Waffle House.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text: The drinks were amazing, the food was so so for the price, but it was worth the money for such great service. Ethan from FL was our server who was kind, efficient, and fast working. He made it feel like home and was attentive to our needs. Thank you Ethan!

name: Layla's Honky Tonk
text: This is a great place to chill out and escape the crowds that are woooooooing it up on the strip.   It's not very smoky or full with clubbing crowds. Instead it's laid back vibe with some great classic country music.  Reasonably priced drinks and no cover- the bands play for tips.   If your taste in music runs towards Dwight Yokum and Cash then this is the place for you.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Went here only cause one of my college friends from out of town wanted an 'authietic' margarita, even though we tried to talk her out of it, as there are so many great places around Honkey Tonk Row. Margaritaville on Lower Broadway - why? why? why? when you MARVELOUS BBQ places like Rippy's or Jack's BBQ.  If you're in Nashville do what they do.  We were told a 30-minute wait, which is normal for the area, but it went beyond an hour - why wait that long for a chain restaurant available in every city.   I know waits can be long at popular times, but I'd rather wait for something exceptional or unique to the area.

Our server was super, I think it was Jonnel!  But I sure wish he moved on to a place that isn't like the McDonalds of 'have fun' faux tropic restaurants.  It must be soul robbing. 

The wait in line was a crazy amount of time for an average burger and cold sweet potato fries.  Our waiter was apologetic about the fries and offered to re-do, truthfully,  I just wanted to get the devil out of there.  The  'authentic' margarita crew were happy. Beer was cold, but that's hardly a unique find in a Nashville bar or really any bar.

FYI there's now Margaritaville retirement communities.  Also could do without the shop full of  good-time tacky souvenirs, I live vicariously through other people's lives stuff - like a CrackerBarrell, maybe since Margaritaville is moving into the retirement community game, they'll be selling tropical-themed grampers in the gift shop. On to Margaritaville Tulsa, Syracuse and Cleveland!!!

name: Ole Red
text: I'm giving 4 stars because our reservation was bumped from dinner to lunch. Apparently the upstairs was booked for a private party. Big imposition for us but they redeemed themselves with great service, drinks and entertainment. They comped us an appetizer and gave us a great front row table. The food was hearty and surprisingly good. Make a reservation as this place gets crowded

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: My boyfriend and I decided to check out the Sunday live jazz sessions at Tennessee Brew Works. It was our first time there and I must say the ambiance and seating of the venue really was patron friendly. My boyfriend was able to order a draft beer right away and luckily there was a table available near the music. They have many seating options: at the bar, tables both up- and downstairs, as well as outdoor seating. It was a sweltering 90+ degrees outside so we opted for inside seating, however, I will definitely try the outdoor seating when the weather gets cooler. Overall it has a great vibe, reasonably priced beer, and a nice live music scene on Sundays. They also do tours!

name: Marathon Music Works
text:
Great Venue! 
Old warehouse. Plenty of parking in the area. 
(Both paid and unpaid in the area.)

Stage was high enough you could see no matter the area you were in. I've been to a rock concert as well as an r&b show the sound works for both genres.

Only complaint was the line situation out front was confusing and could have been better handled.

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
Overall a bad representation and disappointment. We had a group of 11 in town for the weekend after Thanksgiving and we wanted to go out and sight see. My wife's parents are big Buffet fans and wanted the start with late lunch and margaritas. We sat down just a few mins after 2pm and left about 4;15pm, not by choice. 

The downstairs had a medium crowd and upstairs was mostly open when we got there and we needed 1 high chair but it took 10 mins to find one. We then got settled and ordered drinks. One end of our table got forgotten about and our server took off to put drinks in and the first round took 15 mins and they didn't get to order until he came back. 

We then realized we should put all our food orders in to hope it was just a drink issue. Unfortunately, It was not. Our food sporadically came out and with most being burgers, sandwiches and salads. Three burgers came out overcooked, mine so dry it crumbled when I bit into it, and 1 missing toppings. Out of 10 orders the only one with just a salad with chicken breast came out 15 mins later than the rest, and we were missing a side of onion rings. None of us really wanted to order more drinks. 

Ate that point we were ready to move on and asked for the checks. When we voiced that we were disappointed with our experience and the server was very nice and really seemed to be trying. He was shaking and kept telling us the kitchen was the fault. He said he'd take the bills to the manager to see what could be done, he came back 10 mins later with the bills, no change and no explanation lol. I said something to the managers both on the way out and they seemed to be totally shocked sarcastically. Offered us a voucher or a chance to look at the checks again as we were walking out. We declined and just wrote it off as a loss. Good luck.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
Checked this place out one evening after dinner. 

Beer sampler:
Definitely a fan.  $10 for the sampler, which has 5 samples on it.  All the beers were tasty.  I tend to leave behind the IPA's because they are usually a little too hoppy for me...but I know that Nashville seems to enjoy the hops.  

Growlers:
They actually have a growler filling station as you come in the door and technically it is a "separate" business.  This is for tax purposes.  We took a growler of our own in, which they had no problem filling and rinsed before they did so.  We purchased a growler of Ryeman.  Good beer :)  They put a little stamped tag on it so we would know what we were taking with us.  Pricing was good as well.

Seating:
Lots and lots of seating!  They have a lower level and an upper level.  The lower level has an area that apparently often has live music and did while we were there.  The upper level has tv monitors to watch the game on.  Both levels look out onto the brewery floor so that it kinda cool as well!

Tours:
The tours are $12 and that includes the tour and a beer sampler...so essentially the tour is only $2 :)  Good deal!

Staff:
Friendly and helpful :)

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: I'd say the distillery tour we took was more exciting, but I can stomach the taste of beer more than whiskey. At the end of the tour we got to pick a complimentary beer. I like hefeweizens, so I chose the Southern Wit. Highly recommended.

name: Ole Red
text:
Ole Red gets a high 3 stars, maybe a low 4.  I'll explain.  

So, we were looking for a nice dinner before we went out onto the strip for the night and decided to check out Ole Red.  First of all, the place looks great!  It had a modern and hip look.  That red dog posted all over the place is pretty cool.  You can tell it's definitely a newer restaurant (which I will talk more about in a bit), and in my opinion it has the one of the best looking stages in Nashville.  It's quite impressive how big the place is, the main floor is huge and the balcony might be just as big. Got to see a great artist and band play that night, Cort Carpenter.  Check him out!

But, the service, well... let's just say they still have some kinks to work out.  I will give it to them, they were very busy the night we went and I know what it's like to work in the food service industry, so I am a little forgiving.  

First, we got there and waited about 30 minutes for a table.  Not a problem.  We were finally told to make our way to the upstairs balcony because that is where we will be sitting.  It would've been nice to be escorted to the upstairs area, but we got up there just fine.  We needed a table for four, so we were a bit surprised when the hostess up top brought us to a table that was literally wedged in between two others.  The people at the other tables even gave us a look like "yeah, that's not going to happen".  Not to mention, the table was dirty still.  The hostess put our menus down and walked away.  I was kind of in shock.  I had to flag down another server and tell her we were going to sit at the table down the way because this table is dirty and there was no way all four us were going to be able to sit down.  She said that was fine.  We sat down at a different table and our server didn't seem to thrilled about that.  I apologized, and she seemed okay after a while.  We put in our food and drink orders.  If there is one pet peeve of mine, it's when the appetizer comes merely minutes before the main dish.  We felt like we had to wait about 25 minutes before getting our appetizer.  But, like I said, they were busy and we were enjoying the band.  No big deal.  When she brought out the food and walked away, there was no silverware.  Granted it was a lot of finger food, but it's hard to eat tater tot poutine without a fork.  Had to once again flag her down and ask for silverware.  

The food though?  It was very good!  We got the redneck  nachos for an appetizer which was great and super filling.  A friend got the southern tater tot poutine, which was very delicious while the rest of us got burgers.  The burgers were great!  If I had to compliment them for something, it's their tater tots.  I'm used to the little golden yellow nuggets that every restaurant tends to use, but you can tell they make theirs from scratch.  Crispy brown on the outside, but soft on the inside.  I could've eaten that all night.  

So, they still have some kinks to workout, but overall a good experience and great food!

name: The East Room
text:
Grungy is the right word for this dark space, very plain, dark, with a stage, a small bar with a wide selection of beers, and 1970's style pleather stools. 

We went for a stand up comedy show featuring local comedians. The show was about 2 hours long with a $10 cover. They did tell us over the phone the cover was $5 but oh well, still pretty cheap. Those dudes have to make a living some how. 

Comedians were funny, crowd was laid back. Pretty cool music too. Very unpretentious.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text:
What a phenomenal brewery!

TBW is one of my favorite craft breweries in Nashville, offering some fantastic selections like the Basil Ryeman, Walk the Lime, and Country Roots. These are really great quality beers that experiment in pretty creative directions, and it totally, totally works. If you're a first-timer, try the 5-beer sampler for $10.

Beyond the beer, TBW is an awesome place to hang out. There's live music, plenty of balcony seating with nice views of downtown Nashville, and tons of board games (including a giant Connect Four!) What a great place to get together with friends and hang out, or just relax with that special someone--either way, TBW is a good time. Definitely recommend it, and absolutely will be back.

name: Ole Red
text:
Most of you will go for the ambiance, the rooftop views, drinks and music, but I did not (one day...). I was there for a pre-construction tour and again today for a luncheon and let me tell you, meeting planners, the mashed red potatoes must be made with angels tears, and blessed offerings of a cow treated so gently that it willingly gave its best cream and butter. They are amazing and I wish I'd had a Ziploc bag in my purse because I would have embarrassed my peers by stuffing some in my bag.

The others at the table raved over the baked chicken and I heard it was the best one person had ever had. My wings were eh though I rate the pulled pork highly,  especially with the white bbq sauce. 

The greens were decent. But can I tell you about the banana pudding? It was so doggoned fresh and light and gorgeous. It's like getting the essence of bananas because they were smooshed and smoothed in the middle layer. And I got the unexpected pleasure of a hint of chocolate, just a smidge of shavings perhaps over the whipped cream top.

In conclusion, yum!

name: The Night Owl
text: Seriously great local stop. Super convenient location w easy parking. The live music (AK Live) was awesome! Great burgers and awesome service. Will be back

name: Margaritaville - Nashville
text:
This is a good go to when you know you want a good diner and good service.  There was live entertainment in the bar- a seated country music artist with a guitar.  He was ok.  Some people dressed up as key political figures where standing in front of the place waving at everyone and kind of were more entertaining that the actual music.  
I always get the cheeseburger in paradise and it was cooked perfectly but I had to ask for the 57 sauce!  . I had the perfect margarita but I have to say the uptown top shelf margarita is better.  The perfect margarita was suggested because it has fresh lime but I think I would rather have the Cointreau.  All in all, it was a good experience on a very busy night.

name: Tennessee Brew Works
text: Great place!  A spacious area with an upstairs and really cool vibe!  The beer is very interesting for sure - the flavors are just as described so if you are not into drinking a beet or root or whatever it says don't get it because it tastes exactly like what it says - a very enjoyable place to hang out and the food looked really good!

name: Ole Red
text: Great music and a place for drinks and music. Will not eat here again. Ordered the nachos they threw a whole chicken filet on the top of the nachos. It was like dark brown/black in color. The waitress was appalled herself and did take it off our bill. Asked for a vegan patty on a regular burger bun. It came out with a gluten free bun, my side of pickles never came out. Have been at our table 2.5 hours still haven't gotten receipts. Waitress was very kind but not good with checking on our table or in a timely manner. Kept disappearing.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
This is a must stop if you're in Nashville.  The service is very good; food is average.  My "world famous" fried pickles were pasty; portion was generous.  The brisket sandwich with the sweet BBQ sauce was was nice and tender.  There is also an option of a mustard BBQ sauce if you prefer.  Sandwich is served with unremarkable chips ... This is an opportunity for improvement.

Don't be dissuaded if there is a line.  Tables are turned pretty quickly.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Love this place! One of our first stops every time
We come to Nashville! Great food and even better live country music!!!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Freaking love this place. Massive club with a lounge feel which doesn't make sense but if you go and sit at a table at one of their bars with some friends, you'll find yourself at some point looking up into a horse head and over to the big ass dance floor and you'll say to yourself "oh yeah! I'm in a massive dance club!". Great staff and drink selection too. Go get lost in this place next time you're in Nashville!

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: There are certain places in Downtown Nashville which are a must for visiting. The show Nashville helped places like the Bluebird (not in downtown) gain notoriety. Places like Tootsies and Nudies are classic and live off their reputations. The Wildhorse Saloon is the "real deal". Set up like a mini Ryman, there's plenty of room for dining, dancing, parties, etc. There's a second floor in addition to the main area. My colleagues and I only came for the music and drinks. Doug McCormick was the entertainment and was excellent. The large stage with multimedia effects makes this more of an entertainment venue than a restaurant or bar. The staff was very friendly and the place was exceptionally clean.

name: Twin Kegs
text:
Went in, was approached immediately by a spritely bar tender with blonde hair.
Ordered the burger and wings, enjoyed both! 
"...cheapest beer prices in Nashville"
True.
Lots of variety too! 

I will be back.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
I'd recommend checking this place out whether you're a tourist or a resident. My favorite thing about Wildhorse is that they give guided instructions on how to line dance in between the sets of the live bands. They also play pop music too so there's something everyone, or at least anyone that likes to go out dancing, can enjoy if you're going with a large group.

The last time I was here was in the middle of the week. I'd say this is kid friendly because there were a lot of what I assume were high schoolers on the dance floor. One cute couple dressed in cowboy hats and boots was dancing along with their baby!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This place is uncomfortably packed! 2 stars for the patio and one star for the very nice bartender. I would recommend this place as a tourist trap only :-/

name: Twin Kegs
text: This place could really use some remodeling, but that's the only bad thing I have to say about it... The bartender was a delight , and the food was delicious! I got the BB Burger... Very very delicious and flavorful. Will be back for another Burger when I'm in the area. The fries were also delicious!

name: CMA Fest
text:
This is a fairly decent music festival with less than crazy foot traffic. The city does things right and closes off Broadway for foot traffic. However, for some reason the intersections are still open? So, you will meet with insane lines when the lights turn red. Of course, this event brings Ina ton of tourists, so if you're a local bent on discovering niche festivals, this will not be your cup of tea. However, if you're willing to brave the crowds, there's great free music and freebies in the mix for you during the daytime. Vendors seen super speedy and friendly earlier during the day towards the opening of the festival, but I'm not sure that I would recommend going later in the day. Nashville summers are unforgiving, and the menacing combination of body heat, humidity, and sun screams irritated visitors. I was also sunburnt after 30/50 minutes walking to and fro around noon. 

Be prepared with sunscreen and with a tolerance for cowboy boots and you'll be more than fine.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Stopped here while sight seeing...and stayed four hours! The bands were amazing and kept us quite entertained. 

Ordered the super sampler BBQ platter and two of us couldn't finish it! It came with a tin bucket filled with enough condiments for any taste. The ribs were smoky and meaty, the sausages fantastic, spicy good taste on the wings, but beware -- those peperoncini's have quite a kick! The pork loin was good, but pales in flavour next to the other meat selections. The cheese chunks and onion rings rounded out a great (in no way healthy!) feast. 

We were well taken care of by our bartender who custom made Tootsie's moonshine shooters for us -charred cinnamon and apple pie. Awesome. Also had the local brewery Yazoo Hefeweizen which was tasty. 

If you are worried about heading out after all that, the bar has a "blow before you go" breathalizer at the door. What more could you ask for?

name: Twin Kegs
text: Checked out Twin Kegs last week for the first time after kickball and it was awesome!  It's a very small place but the beer was cold and the food was good.  I had the Big Bad Burger (BBB) and it was exactly as the name states, Big and Bad (Bad meaning good though).  It was a cool bar atmosphere which made it kind of hard to talk at times, but it was all around a good time.  I'm definitely gonna go back!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Went to this bar last night, and the bartender was awesome!  I unfortunately did not catch her name (it was super packed and very busy) but she was outstanding.  Fast, made good drinks, and was very cool.  After visiting other places, she was hands down, one of the most friendly, and the best at her job.  Music was good.  We ordered a bunch of food here, and while it wasn't life-changing, it was good.  Overall, a very good experience here.  Would come here again.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Visited with a group of friends during the day on Saturday. Live music was cool and had plenty of table space. Service wasn't very friendly and bartenders were a little hard to track down, but it was a cool environment with a group of friends. They have an upstairs area which was cool and watched little kids dance to the live music. Beer is a little pricier since you're on Broadway so maybe a weekend place for live music, but not a frequent place for me.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: BBQ Brisket was okay, not the beat i've tasted.  Just meat with sauce.  Fried pickles were great!  Sliced covered with batter.  Crispy anf hot.  I'm not a bug fan of country music so i was getting sleepy while we were listening to the band that was playing that evening.  Typical bar food is served.  Fast service!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Pulled chicken was amazing as was the Mac n cheese (I totally love ma Mac n cheese)..atmosphere great with country band in background and windows open blowing in a warm breeze...service was great and staff was extremely friendly in that southern way... great time overall would only request some more local beers on tap

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Excellent beer and they are in special. Start with the tamales I strongly recommend them. We also shared a pepperoni pizza and it was great and filling. Trent Daniels was the best server. Thank you so much

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text:
My overall reaction to this place is "meh" - the service was okay, the food was okay, the ambience was okay. Nothing was really special about it. I'm a little confused about who they're catering to. For a pizza place, they seemed remarkably non kid-friendly - which is fine, but I wish I'd known in advance. The whole wheat crust was a nice option, but didn't taste very good. The waiter seemed befuddled that we just wanted a cheese pizza (really? that's unusual?). Their menu was actually kind of confusing - so many options that it was a bit overwhelming. 

Pros:
*Lots of options?
*Nice patio (if it's not totally full, like it was the day we were there)

Cons:
*Food wasn't that good
*Front staff seemed actually unhappy to have a kid there
*So many options that it was hard to sort out what to order (but not in a good way)
*Huge TVs in every corner so you can't get away from whatever sports are on
*Seemed unclear on what customer base they were going after
*Their valet lot is so small that it was "full" on the day we were there for lunch

Kid-friendly scale:
*Wouldn't come back again with our 3yo. They seemed not interested in kids at all. That's totally fine - but if you're a pizza place, kind of weird. 

Vegetarian-friendly scale:
*Eh, it's a pizza place, so yes.

name: Nashville Palace
text: My wife and I went there the last Saturday in February. We did not want to get mixed up in the crowds on Broadway and this was close to our hotel. The services was very good we were promptly seated and our drink order taken. They had a fairly big bar with only 4 beer taps. Their food standard bar food, burgers, wings etc. The beer and food was reasonably priced, surprising really for a tourist spot. The band was ok at best. The patrons were on the older side and the band played older country for this crowd. Several people got up and 2-stepped and certain songs they clogged. It was fun evening and I can recommend it unless you are in your 30's or less.

name: Twin Kegs
text: This is a very small location. Looks dirty on the outside but not too bad inside. I have not eaten here yet, but they say the burgers are good. My husband justed wanted to grab a beer and myself a soda..but we will try the food and I will give a review about it then.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Beware!!! Had relative come to town. Was at Rippys and was assaulted by 2 bouncers! I would stay away.. there are seriously way to many good bars on Broadway. I have read similar reviews about Rippys. Management needs to address an obvious issue!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Bartenders are the worst. Couldn't give a crap about anything or anyone. Give me a tip and get out of my face, is the attitude.
Think they are hot...LOL! 
They don't know what bar tending is. Shot and beer hookers.
What a waste of money. There are plenty of places where the bartenders are friendly.
Keep moving!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good pulled pork, not great. Really good sweet tea. Service was interesting. Our waiter was quick but we had to flag him down to get our order taken. But once we did our food came out to the table within 5 min. The music (not live) was TOO loud. I would have liked for them to turn it off so we could have soaked up the sounds coming from the street. Loved eating upstairs and overlooking Broadway!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: At the table we had ribs, pulled chicken, and pulled pork- ribs are dry smoked but very good. Music was good, ambience reminds me of a college town bar.... Hit the spot before our concert.

name: Nashville Palace
text: We went to Nashville Palace last night for dinner. There were 8 of us so we were unable to sit inside. We decided to sit on front porch where we could see and hear the band. The food and music were both very good. The band played for over two hours without stopping. What we didn't know was that they were having a Burlesque Festival in part of the building. It was quite a parade into the building. Not appropriate for the children sitting on the patio eating dinner with their parents.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: I would give four start to the entertainment and the place but I came here to eat and I was hoping for some good BBQ but instead the meat was dry and blend. I am from California and I had better brisket there than at the Wildhorse.....

name: Twin Kegs
text: Don't waste your time. Worst dive in Nashville. Worst on the inside than the outside and that's saying a lot. Busted up my front bumper coming into the gravel parking lot. Waited 30 minutes for an average burger.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
First, ask for Blake. You're welcome. He's an awesome waiter!! 2nd, order the Blue Ridge Collins if you're drinking. 100 proof made with moonshine and the best tasting drink I've ever had. A little pricey but worth it. But be careful, it doesn't taste like alcohol and is dangerous!!

The food is excellent. I HATE pickles, but I found myself eating fried pickles one after another. Brisket sandwich is great, and the Mac 'n cheese is delicious.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: The worst country bar I have ever been to.  It is owned by the Gaylord so they don't care about having a crowd.  And during CMA fest they make you wait in line for hours and no one is inside.  It is dead an no good.  I have been to country bars all over the world and it is the worst.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Spicy [jalapeño] fried pickles were on point. The brisket and chopped pork were also delicious. Good atmosphere/ambiance.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Need some soul and good food! Great vibe great music sit outside and enjoy. Best place in Nashville

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text:
Amazing!!!!!  Staff is awesome.  Food is also Amazing. 

Crowd is respectful usually.  Great place.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Lines out the door on the weekend so try to check this place out during the week if you are planning to go. I went on a Sunday night for dinner - $6 cover. The band wasn't great, but I wanted to see the country line dance lesson - it only lasted 15 minutes but was still cool to have done that in Nashville. The fried pickles were fantastic, but I wasn't impressed with my sweet tea pork entree. It was also incredibly loud and the lighting made it difficult to even see my food.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
WORSE CUSTOMER SERVICE EVER! 
Myself and 3 others came to Rippy's on a Sunday evening. They were honestly not that busy. We headed upstairs and sat at the bar. Of the 3 bartenders there, no one acknowledged us. Again...they were not busy at all! So after about 10 minutes, we decided we would get a table. We stood at the entrance is the dining area wondering if we needed to be seated or we could seat ourselves and there wasn't a single person we could ask. One of my guy friends went to the bar to ask and while he was gone, I was able to finally grab someone who told us we could seat ourselves, but when my friend came back, he was told by the girl at the bar that we had to wait to be seated. We finally sat ourselves and it took about 5 minutes or so for our waitress to come to our table. She was sweet and attentive. She put in our drink order and came back to order our food and was apologetic that the drinks were taking so long to be made. As far as the food goes, we ordered ribs and brisket. The main entrees were really good, but the sides were just okay. So I'm giving one star for the waitress's attentiveness and another star for the good entrees, but other than that, I wouldn't come here again. The poor customer service will make you lose your appetite.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Venue awesome! Band sucked balls. Still had fun! Good for dancing and watching old men creep on minors.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: Good drinks, great band,lots of dancing. Staff was very accomodating and definately put customers first. Love the renovations. Much more open and easy to move around in.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The ribs were pretty good. Part of dining out it service and it was just ok. The bartender looked bored and offered very little in reply when I asked questions. The beer was cool, not cold. Went to Jacks across the street and that was a way better experience.

name: Nashville Palace
text: Sandy was great today. She was very personable and prompt. She was honest about the menu and friendly as all heck to myself visiting my mother who recently moved here. I could see how this place could get hoppin but during the lunch hour- you could probably turn the speakers down a little bit. As much as we enjoyed the musician and her selections- it was hard to hear each other even on the patio. Recommend the quesadilla and Sandy.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: This place by far was our favorite bar on Broadway, strictly due to the amazing bands we heard there each time. It's large inside and I believe there are three stories. We never made it upstairs because we loved the bands downstairs. Our servers were great and I recommend a drink called "yeehaw". I can't speak about the food because we didn't eat there although from the looks of the menu it's standard bar food, nothing fancy.

name: Tennessee Performing Arts Center
text: For the second time in a row ive had trouble purchasing tickets. It has taken over 30 mins both times. The tech dept needs to be over hauled!! The first time I called Leeroy was no help. Boo to the online and call in experience.

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Was looking for a place I could listen to some live music and enjoy some food and a drink. But did not want to go to a concert venue or any place I'd to pay a cover charge just to get in.

The Nashville Palace served me perfectly. Easy in, easy out. Attentive waitress, real good live country music and cold beer and some food.

The food is bar food, really basic stuff - so don't come here if you're looking for a wider range or/and attractive choices. But if you're happy with a burger and some fries along with your beer while listening to the band playing - they'll deliver exactly this.
Okay, the same quality type of burger MC Donalds  will give you for almost half the price, but hey - MCD won't service you at your table and of course will not have the live music.

I also liked the atmosphere in this place. The interior and the whole place just looked exactly right for the type of music played here.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Pizza here is good, but nothing so spectacular that it warrants putting up with the horrible parking situation around Division street. Prices are fair in the restaurant itself, but expect to pay at least $6.00 - $10.00 for parking if you're not lucky enough to find somewhere on the street nearby (which you probably won't). Save yourself the stress and hassle - there are many places in Nashville with good or better pizza and service and where parking is much cheaper and more available.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I liked this spot. My pizza and salad were good. Our waitress remained cool and attentive even though it was clear she either had a lot of tables and/or rough day. The outside area is pretty chill. Would go again.

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I had the muffuletta and was disappointed. It was pre-packaged lunch meat with no flavor. The server was great and the vibe was very nice. Food however was less than so-so.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I LOVED this bar!! This was my last stop on my nightlife tour of Nashville, and I'm so glad we stopped in. There were 3 different live country bands playing in different sections of the bar that were all amazing. The drinks were reasonably priced, I had the Yazoo Heif because when in Nashville you should probably try a Nashville brew. One of the things I really loved about this bar was the diverse crowd of people here. There was the newly 21 crowd, couples of all ages, bros in their 50s, I could go on and on, but this place basically covered all demographics. And the best part was, everyone was having an amazing time! I would go here again in a heartbeat, and I kinda wish we had something like this in Boston.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
The best pulled pork sandwich ever.

I LOVE this place!  While it admittedly is a bit tourist-y, the food here is some of the best you can get in the area.  In particular... the pulled pork sandwich.  Top it with their spicy BBQ sauce and you are in pulled pork heaven.

They frequently have live musicians who (like most in Nashville) are truly talented.  The location as well cannot be beat, and is walking distance everything you would want access to!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: Sam waited on us, really helped me find the beer to match my tastes.  Quick, knowledgeable and respectful EVERYTHING I want in a waiter at a restaurant I am trying for the first time.  Will go back, and THANK YOU!

name: Soulshine Pizza Factory
text: I'll keep this short and sweet!  COOL SPOT!  Great choices of food/pizza, live music, inside and outdoor seating options, location is good, staff is friendly...that's pretty much what you want in a bar/restaurant IMO!

name: Nashville Palace
text:
Well I must say if I would have read some of the reviews ahead of time and hadn't been so hungry I probably would have driven past.  Then again maybe the Dukes of Hazard museum next door would have been enough to draw me, well no I guess not. 

This is a bar in a out of the way place. I don't mean this in a bad way but the bartenders scared me, no need to go into details but I wouldn't sit at the bar again. It's close to the G.O.O and a huge hotel/convention center but nothing else really around. The music was very OK and for a place like Nashville there seems to be a hundred better choices to see live music.  Now the smoked wings were pretty damn good.  Well smoked and tasty, then again I was very hungry. 

Overall not worth the stop in my opinion.  If you want live music go downtown, it's not that far!

KT

name: Twin Kegs
text:
I love it when a friend says, "Let's go dive bar hopping!" Don't mind if we do...at ALL. I have been dying to come to this place for a long time (even if I always mistakenly call it Twin Peaks...uh...wrong joint) and finally I got to go. Yay me! 

So this place is just a big square room with a bar at the back. Tables in the middle and TVs on the walls. Perfect for us to look at the Olympics opening ceremonies while also drinking some cold beer. Yes, cold beer, and pretty cheap too. Shuffleboard. Fun patrons. Smoke 'em if you got 'em. 

The best thing was karaoke. God, I love a dive bar with karaoke. YES PLEASE! No stage or anything, you just stand up by the KJ near the hallway to the bathroom and rock out. I immediately started signing up for songs. The clientele ran a little younger than me and they were singing a bunch of 90s songs but it was awesome. Everyone clapped even if you were a not-so-good singer. I rocked all my jams and had a FUCKING BLAST. Also, one dude from Venezuela or Brazil or somewhere sang a damn Robbie Williams song. Who the hell knows him around here? I loved it.

Look, the dive bars in Nashville are slowly going away to be replaced by condos, townhouses, parking lots, and whatever else. You can't make dive bars like this, they have to already be there...so let's just all bow down to the awesomeness that is Twin Kegs and patronize it all the time so that it will stay around FOR-EVAH.

name: The Cobra
text:
Tried to escape the bullshit of touristy Nashville and couldn't because the DJs drunk friend on 7/30/2019 - Tuesday. He heckled me after I gave a suggestion to the DJ AFTER HE WENT HOME NOT FOR THE NIGHT.

The DJs very drunk girl friend also shoved me when my boyfriend  confronted the DJs friend. It should be noted I only had 2 drinks and was very sober...

Find a new DJ who can handle their friends and friends girlfriends... Nashville has plenty of them.

name: Nashville Palace
text: We just walked in here because it was close and looked fun.  We came back three times on our short vacation just to see waitress TAMMY.  She is fun and she is the ONLY one of all the actual bar tenders that got our drinks right.  When we went for 3rd time she wasn't working so we just ordered beer.  She is a great asset to your business!!!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Stopped into this place right after the Predators ice hockey game.  Was just across the street and looked good.   Live music was playing, which is typical here in Nashville.  I must say, Nashville has surpassed Austin, TX for the live music capitol of the world.  Lots more live music venues and bars, but then again, lots of them are country, where Austin has a various mix.

Any ways, back to the food.  We were just grabbing a late night drink and bite after game, and were craving the barbecue.  We went with Rippy's Super Sampler Platter of all kinds of meats. Wings were good, and the ribs fell off the bone.  Really enjoyed that.  The sausage and pork loin wasn't that special, but still good.  We were expecting more for the price, but still wasn't too bad.  But, I've had better.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: A good and family friendly place with live music and line dancing lessons.  Food is fine, but it's the atmosphere that makes for a great experience.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: We stopped by the NashHouse looking for a relaxed brunch atmosphere and found just that! Our group of 7 all enjoyed our food and dining experience as our waiter was very attentive. The music videos being shown on the large screen was a great touch and we had no problem getting seated on a Sunday morning. Overall a great experience and a place that I would recommend to others!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I went there last night. They had a great lively atmosphere. The workers there are just awful and hateful. I bought two beers and it was $9.50 and I gave the little blonde bartender $10 and said don't worry about the change. I always tip my bartenders after the night with a larger sum. This bartender said "really fifty cents, you think I need your fifty cents" and threw two quarters on the bar. No I didn't think she needed my fifty cents, I was just trying to save her a trip back to me to deliver fifty cents. Needless to say I did not give a better tip at the end of the night as my party of 15 and I left and took our business elsewhere. I've never been treated with such disrespect! I will never recommend this place. Honky Tonk Central is much more friendly!!

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Rippy's has potential to be a great bar. It's not. $4.75 for domestics make it one of the most expensive on the strip. The cost of food is nowhere near reasonable. For 10 bucks I got wings. The wings had no meat and them and were mostly batter. When I say no meant on them, I mean I saw mostly bone on the drumsticks. When I asked the server about it, she took care of it right? NO. Instead, she went ahead an added gratuity to our table of 5! Food is bad. Won't be back. Sorry to say as a Nashville native.

name: Wildhorse Saloon
text: I was in town visiting. I figured, hell, might as well check out how they dance down here. Its REALLY big inside, looks are deceiving from the outside. Sure enough, by the time I got in, there were already peeps dancing. I think overall it was a pretty cool experience, if not for the garbage bar tender who when I asked for a drink of water (cause I'd been drinking all day and needed to sober up/hydrate) responded with "I'm in the middle of an order here, so you're just going to have to wait, OK?? Pretty amazed at his response, given that I was hella nice in asking him and not being all demanding and shit. Congratulations a$$hole, you just gave the Wildhorse Saloon 1 star on Yelp.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: I was in Nashville for the night and decided to go out and explore the downtown area.  There was a lot going on and I was a little bit overwhelmed. However, after walking around for a bit I decided on Rippy's. Based on the reviews and the photos I should have left immediately, but I just really wanted to eat. I wanted to Tennessee Hot chicken but that wasn't on their menu. For drinks i got the honky tonk tea (really good) and the Tropical something(i can't remember the full name, but i didn't enjoy it. It tasted like cheap liquor and Red Bull). For food i ordered the pork loin with a double side of Mac & cheese. It kind of reminded me of school lunch. I think i was most shocked by the Mac. I was under the impression because i was in the south i was going to get some really good Mac. This  one tasted like crafts.

name: NashHouse Southern Spoon and Saloon
text: Had dinner there for the first time last night before the Preds game.  Service was slow even through there were a lot of servers standing around, and the place was at less than 50% capacity.   Burger and Chicken sandwich took 40 minutes to arrive, then we waited another 5 to get silverware.  Food was cold and my wife's burger was burnt black on the bottom.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: Good barbecue.  Live country music, a nice place to stop for a meal.  Friendly staff.  Walking distance from the convention center and close to the hockey arena.  Seat yourself.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text:
Just Because .." Hello are you eating ? " Great Greeting huh..? Come In , Listen to music , have a few drinks , cause its BAR FOOD , They call it BBQ ...But its BAR FOOD ... Listen to music few brinks , More BAR FOOD..  Decent portions, Plastic dinnerware , bucket of sauces table side. Lotz of Napkins . Their ribs are over smoked with flavor TooMuch , pulled pork was ... ,However their grilled chicken was very good.  Im guessing cause that was made fresh to order, and nicely spiced . 

With that we are heading out to Honky Tonk & Nudies , too see whats going on there ..

name: Nashville Palace
text:
This place is great.  Free to get in, within walking distance of the hotel we were staying at.  On Friday and Saturday when we were in town they had Larry Hamilton Band (fantastic band), which we really enjoyed dancing to.  

Nice there is a place to go to listen to good, traditional country music.  Good priced beer and great food.

We come here every time we come to town.  Another plus, there is no smoking inside, unlike another bar down the street from there.

Look forward to coming here again next time we are in town.

name: Nashville Palace
text: We stopped in to have lunch yesterday. We walked in and the office door was open and 2 women had their feet up on the desk, chatting. We stood for a while trying to figure out if they were open. There were people cleaning in the dining area, so I walked into the bar and asked the bartender if they were serving food. She just stared at me like I was speaking a foreign language. We finally turned around and walked out. We recommend getting better service and you might have business.

name: The Cobra
text:
Go to No Quarter, Mickey's, Duke's, Dino's... literally anywhere else. 

I was there this past Sunday to see a friend do stand-up. One of the bartenders was so rude to us that I thought that she was kidding. It was absurd. The friend that I was there to see later pointed out that she got his drink wrong (which we both agree is no big deal, it totally happens), but he didn't even want to say anything about it because he didn't want her to blow up on him. Almost every customer at that bar was under 35 and probably worked in the service industry too... I don't know anybody in that room who would treat their customers like that. She might've been tired, whatever- I hope she doesn't talk to everyone like she talked to us. It was awful. Just awful. 
I will not go back. Ridiculous.

name: The Cobra
text:
Tonight the DJs drunk friend shoved me after i confronted him when he said rude things to my girlfriend suggested a song to the DJ ONCE HE GOT HOME. The DJs friends girlfriend also shoved my girlfriend.

We went to Broadway this night and this was somehow the worst bar we visited... liked this bar a lot before this happened but never going back now.

name: Rippy's Bar & Grill
text: The bbq there was delicious!!!  Decent price. I wish the service was a little bit better. They do come around. But when you do need someone no ones around. The live music was entertaining.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I love this place. There's several floors and live music all week long. It's a Nashville staple.  The bands are fantastic. You have to try this place if you're here and looking for a good time.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
I can't comment on anything inside the restaurant.
As a fan of the tv show Nashville, I made my husband stop here while we were driving through town.  We were unable to stay for a show, but I did want my pictures in front of the sign.
It's odd that it's in the middle of a strip mall.  It also looks a lot smaller then I would expect it to be. There are a lot of scary signs about copyright infringement all over the doors.
However, it does look like a great place to see some great talent.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
While out searching for apartments, I was in dire need of caffeine, a bathroom and internet (in that order).  The Well delivered and then some.  (OK, bathroom wasn't great, but it was clean enough and it worked)

I had an iced soy chai - it was lovely.  Much better than Sbux.  Plenty of seating, although some was less than comfortable.  Service was a bit slow, but I appreciate that they took the time to make drinks right.  

It wasn't until I read the other reviews on here that I even knew about the religious slant.  But I appreciate that it wasn't pushy.

Drink menu was pretty big - I look forward to returning!

name: Tin Roof
text: Stopped in for dinner and a drink. It was a Tuesday and kind of quiet, but I can see how this place can get hopping. Food was good, decent bar fare with a little twist on things. Service was good and drinks were solid. Affordable solution to the overpriced tourist traps on Broadway.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
It's all about the history and atmosphere 
Came here for some jack, music and look at the pics ...wasn't disappointed !!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: This is a really cool place! (Though I was it was cleaned up a bit) The food/drinks are reasonable and the talent is unmatched. Get the baked Brie and whatever dessert they have that evening.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: My wife and I visited this cafe this evening and saw a very good show put on by the Sweethearts of the Rodeo.  We enjoyed the entertainment as well as the venue which was made popular by the show Nashville which we both enjoy watching. We would welcome doing a return trip to this location during another future visit.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I am a Hispanic male from Southern California. Thursday night, I visited Tootsies with my GF and  some friends. As I approached the entrance of the bar, I was asked for my ID. I pulled my wallet out, and pulled out 2 ID's (drivers license and State ID) I handed what I thought was the bouncer, my Drivers license and then he asked me "Is the other ID your Green Card?" I turned to him in disbelief and asked him did he really ask me that. I immediately walked in and asked for the manager. We were approached by a dark haired man with glasses who said he was the manager. We walked down to confront the bouncer only to find out the bouncer was a Sheriff. In the midst of speaking to the Sheriff and manager, a large black man (real bouncer)walks up to me and pushes me. I tell the man to keep his hands off me, and the manager proceeds to tell me I am no longer welcomed in the bar. The Sheriff had to separate the bouncer and manager from me. This is the first time in my life that I have experienced racism directly and wouldn't imagine it would occur in an establishment of this magnitude. I've been to this place a couple times on other visits to Nashville and even attended the bar earlier in the day before the incident! I know this incident is a sign of the times and this will no way effect their business but hopefully the "management" at Tootsies will consider some training on how to handle these types of situations in the future, as I am sure this won't be the last time this happens here!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Over rated place. We got in quick and bartender was very attentive as soon as we walked in, but too crowded due to the hype of it being the "spot" to go. We ended up at Legends and Layla's which was less crowded and music just as good.  Not a bad experience but def a place to stop me say you were there. Nothing incredible.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: No matter how much time you have in Nashville or who is performing that night make sure you get out to the blue bird cafe. This was my favorite place in Nashville. I came on a night where they had a round circle of singer songwriters performing. They were all friends and chatted between each song giving some background about what they had written. It was so cool to get up close and get a better understanding of why a song was written and what it means. I think they have a lot of variety in the styles of their performances and whether or not the evening is ticketed so check out the line up ahead of time. I can't wait to come back again!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
I was so excited about coming to Nashville and Tootsie's was on the top of my list. My husband and I went on a Wednesday night and I was shocked of how packed it was. It's a great venue with three stories of live music. The entrance and bottom floor was much smaller than I expected it to be. We spent most of our time on the third floor which had the roof top bar. Drinks are reasonably priced and my husband said the beer was nice and cold. 
The reason I am giving Tootsie's 3 stars is for the service and attitude of the bartenders. I have never met more rude woman behind a bar in my life! The three in particular on the roof I wish I had gotten there names but they were horrible. I wasn't drinking that night and I ordered a water and it was like I was a bother to them for ordering water. Some people don't drink!!!!! I live in Los Angeles and have been to some of the best bars and restaurants LA has to offer. I never received service like that. We eventually went back downstairs because those girls were just miserable. Rolling there eyes when people ordered drinks! Come on now! If you want a great honky tonk on broadway with great friendly service walk right next door to Legends! That was our favorite on all of broadway

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
2nd honky tonk bar that we chose to visit during our mini vacation. This was as good as it gets! Rowdy! Great band! Awesome service! We were packed in like sardines! Everyone was happy! We grabbed two open seats right in front of the band. We just slid in there when someone got up and met all kinds of tourists from around the globe. There were folks my age, folks 20 years older than me and folks 30 years younger than me. We all had one purpose - party like it's 1999! And party we did! Always had a beer in our hands - bartenders raced about making sure we were all satiated. I never smiled so big! We clapped! We sang! We cheered! We swam in a bowl of happiness!

WooHoo!

name: The Stone Fox
text: This place is not worth the wait and the service is absolutely terrible. Waited an hour+ for a table that we were told would take 30 mins. Server didn't come until 20 mins after we were seated. Even then they got the food order wrong. One star because they didn't charge me for my order, which was the right thing to do. Don't intend to return.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great band...very crowded but a must see while in town!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: fun place. crowded. all good singers. have a good time!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Had a great time at Tootsies!  We loved the 3rd floor bar and outside deck!  We visited your establishment on Friday night and felt right at home.  We came back on Saturday night because we loved the bartender!  She was quick and friendly.  Very good personality.  Love her!  Thank you, Chelsea for being so good to us!  You are a great bartender!  So glad they gave you the chance to sling drinks two years ago with no experience!  You're great at it!  If we ever get back to Nashville from Chicago again, we will certainly stop in to see you!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
Went for a brunch on a Saturday morning. Of course we expected a long wait for a group of 4 at 11:00, and we were lucky to have bottomless mimosas to accompany us as we waited. The bar staff was very diligent and friendly to refill our mimosas very promptly! I'm not going to say we were drunk by the time we sat down, but... well... crap happens. 
Anyway, we ordered the big ole biscuits and gravy and the sweet potato pancakes with some coffee to sober us up. The food was incredible! The wait staff was so friendly and they continued to fill our mimosas as the bluegrass band played.. This place was amazing and we had a great time!

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: I am not sure whether to review this place as a bar, or as a restaurant. My wife and I went here on a week night and while as a "bar" it was good to very good. The atmosphere I think was fun and it was lively enough...but not so packed you couldn't move. Probably the only thing that brings it down from 5 to 4 stars is that the band that was playing was ok, but not as good as some of the others on Broadway. As a restaurant it was very good also. The hot dog wrapped in bacon was probably the best hot dog I have ever had. Their Frito and chili was very good also. The hamburgers looked great...but I will have to come back another time to find out.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Super fine touristy spot! We stopped in during the day on NYE. It was cold but they still had the rooftop open with heaters of course. It was busy but the bartenders were very quick to get drunk orders. The beers were cold and drinks were super yummy! The music was loud enough to jam to but not too loud you couldn't hold a conversation.  I would for sure go back if we were in town!
