The only complaint I have is we ordered a vodka red bull and they did not inform us that it wasn't real red bull and my husband who is allergic to artificial sweeteners had a bad reaction.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
So, I had never been inside of Tootsie's and my beau felt like I needed to experience it.  I will say this...it was a Friday night and super crowded.  I think for some that would be a plus, and for others it may be a deterrent.  I was mixed on how I felt about this place.  The live music was good, but they should work on overlapping the set times so that there is never a time when all the stages are empty/on break.  That happened to us and we were waiting for the music to start back up for half the time we were there.  The wait time on getting a drink was super fast, especially since they have beer tubs with bartenders set up around the bar areas.  I most enjoyed listening to the live music in the front room and also checking out all of the pictures on the walls of people who have been there in the past.  
I should mention that it was free!  :)  That is always a plus.
Overall I am glad to say I have been to Tootsie's even though heavy crowds are not my favorite thing in the world.

name: The Stone Fox
text: We went for Sunday brunch and there was a 30 wait which was no big deal.  We finally got seated and our order was taken.  Didn't have to wait long on the drinks (the only plus was the Bloody Mary!). But the wait for the food was ridiculous and then to get it cold made it even worse!  I got the breakfast tacos and the cheese was hard as a rock since it had been melted and then cooled off.  The potatoes and bacon were cold too.  When I let the waitress know she was extremely rude about it and said that's not possible bc all the food comes out immediately. When the waitress came back out with our bill they did take our meal off and she asked that we would give them a second chance when not so busy?!? Um, we won't be going back anyway!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Wow, where do I start, I should have left after I saw the red flags but I really wanted to have lunch on their patio, so after struggling to get a seat , no one ever acknowledged us, waited for 10 - 15 min.  Finally just got up and left,  it was not busy,  saw bartenders / waitresses just standing behind the bar. Never again

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Look... This place aint bad, it's just not my choice of places to grab a drink and listen to live music. My fiance and I went based on it's popularity and so did everyone else in the area from out of town. Im not big into the tourist traps so... Yeah.

PRO TIP: Dont bring stools away from tables and sit in the middle of the room. Im talking to you man in the green shirt (he'll never see this)!

name: Tin Roof
text: Got into town for the first time at 11am on a Thursday and went to Tin Roof for a beer and good live music. Had a great time

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: What was once a classic gem of Music City is now a sticky-floor beer pit designed to sell as much alcohol as possible. All the historic adornments on the wall are vandalized and during peak hours it's too crowded to move inside. If you must, poke your head in to say you did but please I encourage you to find something more genuine Nashville has to offer.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: I came here for just a casual lunch with my significant other and it was a great time in my opinion. The place looked a lot better in the inside than I had initially expected. The food was fantastic and the service was pretty good. They are a little proxy though. Also My SO is pretty picky and and tends to be an "difficult customer" and he was still able to find something on the menu to his liking which is amazing in my opinion. The servers did seem to get annoyed with him but I can't really blame that on them.  They also have souvenirs which where pretty nifty. They have different menus throughout the day if just depends when on when you get there. Over great place to eat.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: What an amazing place to visit and the bartenders are always nice especially gunner and avery and the waitress scarlett is very nice, just kinda on the shy side. Oh btw what time does Deacon Claybourne play? I would love to see Rayna James and Deacon sing on that stage!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Oh gosh, if you really had just one day in Nashville, where would you go that evening for live music, the Grand Ole Opry or the Bluebird Cafe? That's a tough call, but since neither Jamie W. nor I have ever been to Nashville before, we went with the Opry with no regrets. An excellent concert that turned out to be the pinnacle of time management as the show was done at 9:15PM sharp. Did we dare try to traverse the city for a half-hour to attempt to catch the 9:30PM show at the Bluebird? Why not, what did we have to lose? After all, we were leaving town in the morning.

So off we went to discover that the Bluebird Cafe is in a strip mall off Hillsboro Pike. Like Joseph and Mary in baseball caps, we were hoping there could be room for us. We wouldn't have minded standing next to the restroom, but alas, there was a handwritten sign taped on the glass door that said no one else would be allowed in since they were sold out. It reminded me of that scene in "Hans Christian Andersen" when Danny Kaye got locked in the closet by Farley Granger, an ironic point since both actors were in the Hollywood celluloid closet if you know what I mean. Danny was put in the closet to prevent him from giving the slippers to his beloved ballerina, the subject of his unrequited love.

I didn't have any shoes on me to give to performer and well-regarded composer Gary Burr, but we were able to peek through the window and see a bit of his performance that night. The owners were kind enough to have speakers out into the parking lot (photo:  http://bit.ly/1IL4WQ4). I know who Burr is because he's now in a country trio with his wife and my old favorite Kenny Loggins. "Even though we ain't got money, I'm so in love with ya, honey." Burr has an almost-as-pleasing voice. All we needed were a couple of naugahyde recliners from Bradford's Furniture next door except they were closed. Too bad there was an agitated guy on his cell thoroughly upset that he couldn't get in. Chill bro, this is Nashville. Good music is everywhere.

name: The Woods Amphitheater At Fontanel
text: Holding people at the gate til about 30 minutes before the concert starts seems silly.  Food and beverage vendors inside could have been selling a lot more if we were allowed to walk in.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I had a really great time here as a solo traveler! It was a fairly low key Sunday night, but the bands were fantastic and it was easy enough to snag a single seat on each of the different floors. My favorite spot was the second floor- there are seats behind the stage that are perfect for someone who wants to quietly observe and enjoy!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: What a fun evening!  The bands were awesome!  It was crowded but we were there to mingle.  The drink prices are way too high.  $7 for a Yuengling beer. And $11 for a G&T plus tips.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Not really what we expected.  Caveat that I'm not into modern country music, and there was lots of that, but it was also a bit crowded and there were Kid Rock posters everywhere (I have no idea why).  Lots of white "bro" guys and the women who like them.  But maybe that's the Nashville demographic.  Not a bad experience, but don't think it lives up to the hype and there are other bars in the area that are just as good. We were there last Friday night, and I was particularly impressed with one very good male singer on the second floor.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Cool bar, good live music, packed butts-to-nuts though, so expect that. Pretty sure the place was over-capacity. However, really historic and lively.

name: Tin Roof
text: I had the shrimp basket...time they opened up. The shrimp were extra crispy and a bit overcooked. We were the first orders to come out. The fries, I added cheese on them for .75. They apply this white, thin cheese sauce on the fries that you barely see and barely taste. So it's not smothered or what you think of when you read "cheese fries". The waitress was short and uninviting...not very welcoming at all. Dropped our food off and went to go sit back down. I thought she was going to get our silverware, not realizing they have plastic ware on the table, but I wanted some ranch so i had to wait until she made her way back to 'check' on us. First time here...not that pleasant. I'll leave this to the college kids and night life.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Food was amazing for a bar! Burgers were awesome! Great vibes with the live band and trailer park themed decor!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Had to check this place out as it is one of the more popular places in Broadway. There are several floors and each floor has a different band playing. 
A bit older crowd but fun to have a drink.

name: The Well Coffeehouse
text:
I had been curious to try this non Starbucks coffee shop in Green Hills and came in on Sunday for a pick me up. 

I really enjoyed the decor and that there is PLENTY of space to lounge and read, study, or work. Finding out it used to be a Burger King made sense! The counter top is long and definitely fast foodish, but they have done a great job giving it a make over. 

I decided to order differently and had an iced Fireside; a vanilla and cinnamon latte. I was pleased to discover they offer both soy and almond milk, I love variety! 

My drink was..odd. I'd get random patches of sweetness mixed with a bitter espresso flavor. It was different, and in a way that I would not order it again. I'm thinking the drink was set up that way, but it just wasn't for me. 

I wasn't blown away by my first experience, but maybe I had an off drink. I will come back and order my regular latte and see how that goes!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
One of Nashville's original Honkey Tonks.   Just loved the place.  Tons of pictures of people that have played there in he past.  
2 bands playing on 2 different levels and both filled with talented musicians.  Couldn't sit still on the bar stool.   Random stars' band members showing up throughout the night.  The night we were there a member of Tim McGraw's band sang a song and Frankie Ballard's drummer who preformed as well!  Can't imagine the talent that shows up on CMA weeks or on the weekends.  
Crowded?! Absolutely, and I can't imagine what it's like on weekend night as we were there on a Tuesday night.   I will say however, that we rarely waited long for a drink there.   The bartender, Chelsea, was on it!!!  
The bathrooms were completely horrible.   Especially the one on the lower level heard that the one upstairs was better though. 
It's definitely a must visit for anyone coming to Nashville!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Just the most history rich honkeytonk in Tennessee. What I love about this little music shack is that it always has a great crowd. You find yourself singing along and if you leave without a smile it's your own damn fault. Drinks are expensive, seating is limited, cover bands galore- and I still love it.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
Paradise Park is the place to be! Their food is a 5 EASILY! My boyfriend and I came to Nashville for the first time, and Paradise Park was the first place we went! Bacon Cheeseburger with fries is what I got and he got tater tots! Mouth watering. Our ticket number was2, so I'm thinking we may have been the 2nd order of the day, but the customer service was 5 as well! The perfect welcome to Nashville! 
So we decided to go Saturday night after a fun night out (to also see if we were just hungry and to confirm our thoughts on how amazing this place is) well, the customer service was not very good. She was short and rude, which is why I have to knock it down a star because you have to beware if you aren't going when they first open! But the food was still a 5 nonetheless. The venue is a 5 as well! It's a trailer inside the building, which is pretty cool, and at night the side where they play live music is pretty awesome! I would definitely go again!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsie's is overrated. Been here a couple of times with my friends and it's nothing special. Was once escorted out because my friend misfired a mayonnaise packet and the group behind us that it hit asked the bouncer to escort us out and he did, even though we apologized and explained it was an accident. Staff isn't friendly or understanding, bands really aren't very good. Check out ANY OTHER bar on Broadway.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: We came to Nashville for a bachelorette party and we found ourselves on the doorstep of Tootsies. I cannot express just how fun this bar is. The people are super friendly, the band was great, and the atmosphere was awesome. I would like to give a special shout out to the door man David. David is a genuinely sweet guy! He is charismatic and warm and knows how to make people feel safe and welcome!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Love the indoor and outdoor seating! They also usually have the best bands playing! It's one of the original spots on Broadway and deserves a visit! Drinks are a bit pricey due to the large amount of tourists. There was also an older crowd since we came in during the early evening.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
All I can say is so much fun! Out of all the honky tonks my friends and I visited, this one was my favorite!

Every level had a band, and the top floor had a gorgeous deck overlooking Broadway. It was packed, but we still had adequate room to dance and sing with the band. 

Great time!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Always one of my favorite honky-tonks to visit when I'm in town.  Top-notch music any time of day.  Fairly-priced drinks.  The old bearded guy who plays bass in every band.  Lovely girls playing fiddle.

But seriously, the talent here is some of the best in the city and you're missing out if you don't stop by.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: My husband and I truly loved the Bluebird. Maybe partially because its iconic, but mostly because it was a quaint, low-key, intimate venue. The performers were incredible and you felt like they were playing just for you. The food was ok, nothing to really write home about, but they had a good selection of drinks and it was very reasonable and they were all extremely nice. It was a great experience. A little tough to get in, but if you are on the site at 8am Monday you can get seats .

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: A disappointment. This new restaurant/bar is actually two doors down from where the original Sutler was. We were seated and no one came to our table for fifteen minutes. Several servers walked by us but no acknowledgment of us even being there. The place was half empty and I couldn't manage to wave anyone down. My husband and I sat another five minutes until I had to walk up to a passing server and ask for assistance. He said he'd tell our server. Ten more minutes went by with no sign of any one to take our drink or food order. We gave up and left. The hostess looked surprised we were leaving. I told her that no one came to the table. She just gave me a blank stare. Won't be back.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Tootsie's is a damn good time with different live music on every level. It has a hole in the wall feel with a lot of personality. Great live music, friendly staff, and as always you'll definitely walk out with a few more friends than you arrived with.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: There are so many great places to eat in Nashville sad to say service and food was adverage at best and way over priced. I went there for the nostalgia unfortunately I would have to say the decor is a 21 centry version of what wonce was a place where average Nashvillians gathered for lunch and a on February 13, 1960, a group of mainly college students from historically black universities walked in sat down at the lunch counters and asked to be served.This is lost in the glitz

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Being a huge fan of the show, Nashville, I couldn't wait to get tickets to see some songwriters and singers.  As everyone has said the process for getting tickets is daunting and frustrating.  We had 5 in our party and that wasn't possible so just two of us were able to snag tickets.  I have to say the pain was worth it.  It was an amazing experience from start to finish.  The singers did not disappoint.  The venue was cozy and inviting!! The atmosphere is just heaven.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Things to note: I had 6 tickets for tonight. One person in my group was running late and they still let her in after the singing started. The waitresses will still take orders after the singing starts too. I was at the 6pm show and it ended around 7:45.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Great dinner.  I travel to Nashville periodically for work and often eat alone.  I will definitely come back here.  The restaurant is a beautiful homage to the old Woolworth lunch counter and honors the civil rights history with the restoration and historical photos.  Music is soul, nice change up from country.  Tonight I ordered meatloaf, it was amazing.  Also real mashed potatoes and roasted Brussels sprouts were excellent.  Everything was GREAT. Nice atmosphere.  Nice bar.  Nice service.  Highly recommend.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Some friends and I came to this establishment and were told at the door that we were not welcome because this was not a bachelorette party type of establishment. We all came from different states and were very excited to come here! Yes we were on a bachelorette party but this was our first stop because we wanted somewhere low key. We were instantly judged and not welcome and told this was not the place for us...what kind of establishment turns away guest. We were also told there was no seating but as we glared through the glass there were open tables. The group in front of us was let in (with no reservation). Welcome to Nashville!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
I waited to get back home to write about my awful experience at your establishment.  The events of Sunday 2/12 have shaken me up and not only made me feel embarrassed, violated but for the first time I've felt singled out in discrimination.  My only crime that night was to place my knee on a bar stool. 

I am a petite 5.3" woman, 115 lbs., sitting at the back of the bar enjoying the band and only to get a better view of the band I placed my knee on a stool.  I was asked not to do that by a tall bouncer, and I removed my knee, only that the music got the better of me and I placed my knee on the stool a second time to get a better look.  Just seconds after the bouncer reappeared and said I had to leave, I said "fine I will go, let me wait for my husband" who was at the bar ordering drinks, at that point the bouncer forced me out by grabbing my arms behind my back and dragging me out, when I tried to resist his abusive manner of grabbing me and I was pleading with him to stop and asked "what did I do wrong" begging him to let me go, he grabbed me by my neck and violently dragged me out to the sidewalk. 

At this point I broke down, I was in disbelieve that this is how I was being treated as a patron that was paying good hard earned money at your establishment.  I am from Miami and in my many years of visiting bars, restaurants and clubs in Miami, I have never in my life been treated with such disrespect and abuse.   Sad to say that when the manager came out her response was "he was doing his job".  Well everyone has a job to do, but mistreating someone is not the way to do any job. 

I want to thank the kind people who came to my defense, they saw the way I was being treated was not right, and spoke out of their disgust.  If something positive is to come from this, I hope no one else should endure such horrible treatment. Tootsies needs to evaluate this bouncer, no one who feels they must grab a woman by her neck should be a bouncer and they must find another approach to properly remove someone.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Food is great. Whatever time it is the food is consistently good! The prices are super fair and the food is super fresh. Def a place to eat before you go out drinking or after a night of drinking. The place itself is a little dingy but the food is top notch. Would come back for the hot chicken and the cheese burgers.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: Love the food and the atmosphere. You just never know when this place is open or when they are changing out the menu. The last 4 times I've tried to get food I have been unsuccessful on different days and times, so I'm afraid I will not patronize The Sutler. It's unfortunate, it could be a great place to hang.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text: Always a great stop for a scrumptious burger.  Nothing fancy ... Food is served in paper food trays and kitchen roll towels serve as napkins on the table.   Don't pass up the sweet potato fries, though mine weren't as hot as they could have been.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Darn?!?XO!

This should be a 5 star review!  After all I showed up in Nashville for one night and was able to get into the famous fabulous Bluebird Cafe with no reservation!  

But we saw an old blues guy, who insisted on just playing 12 bar blues songs and he wasn't very good.  I hope, he was having a bad day or I was not in the mood.

There was a reason why we were able to get in without a reservation.

That said, I loved my experience......  even waiting in line in the rain wasn't too bad.  The food, drink, and the service were very nice.

But the tip is look at the website and make sure it is worth waiting in line.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: This a great spot for a party. So many stars have played and sung here. The bar is a little cramped and when it's busy it can be impossible to move around but if you go in the afternoon for some day drinking there's always a good local live musician playing! Make sure you leave a good tip for the bands on the way out!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
This place has a super cool set up: upstairs - was the traditional dining room set up; downstairs was more suited for lounging.  I came during happy, so it was half off their signature/specialty cocktails as well as some other drink specials.

I had two of the specialty/signature cocktails: Don't Ask Rye & The Gambler.  They both were pretty good but if I had to pick the Gambler was the better of the two.  To snack on we tried the wings and the mac n cheese - green chicken chili.  The wings were better than average but nothing spectacular.  The mac n cheese was a very unique combination that went together well.  Usually I steer away from restaurant mac n cheese unless a trusted source gives me the ok but I'm glad I took a chance on it. **The menu did not indicate that the mac n cheese  had tomatoes on it; so if you're allergic or don't like tomatoes be mindful of that.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
100% worth the wait.  My husband and I decided fairly last minute to try to get into the early show on a Tuesday.  We waited in the 90 degree, sunny weather for a little over an hour and barely made the cut, but it was soooo worth it!  

Pro tip: you can make reservations a week out, do that.

Food and drinks were decent and the music was fabulous.  This is exactly what we wanted when we came to Nashville, not the craziness of lower broadway.  This place is a must go.

Also, if you watched the TV show Nashville this might now be what you expect.  But in a great way (in my opinion).

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: A great bar on Honky Tonk Row. Great scene on even a Monday night! The live music was spectacular! The bar service was speedy. The vibe here was a lot of fun, great scene with a small stage right in the window. This place was packed, selection was good they even had cider.

name: Tin Roof
text:
I would do five stars based on the beer selection, great food, the bar environment, music, etc.

But, what I will say about my overall experience, cover the top of your glass.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: It was fun to stop in for a drink at a Nashville institution like Tootsie's. There was live entertainment with the singer walking down the actual bar during her set. I only stayed on the bottom floor, but the place kept going up to the rooftop.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Hands down the funnest bar in Nashville! There's a variety of music and live bands to choose from. There are 3 floors plus a little outdoor section. The vibe on each floor varies, I found that the first floor you can go and just hang out with friends or on a date and listen to music and relax. As the floors get higher, I guess so does your level of intoxication cause the 3rd floor was the dance party. So much fun, I totally recommend--And there's no cover.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: If you are looking for a trendy  fancy place.... this is not for you. Now, if you are looking for a good old bar,  full of history , great live music,  and a good stiff drink at a decent price... This is your place! Their bloody Mary did not look the best, but I was Pleasantly surprised at how good they made it. Definitely recommend this place, lots of history, it's a must go to if you're in the area just to say you've been there.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Incredible location in the heart of downtown in a beautifully restored and historically rich space. Atmosphere had a really nice, simple elegance while still feeling extremely relaxed and familiar. Host staff were warm and inviting. Sitting at the bar was a great call as the bartenders were welcoming and knowledgable.  Mikey, Freddy, Adam, and Fletcher made sure we had an amazing experience, and the food and drinks were excellent! Can't wait to try everything! Hightlights: Five and Dime (cocktail), pickled shrimp (app), cheese curds (app), corn pudding (side), black eyed peas (side), fried flounder (entree), bourbon caramel pecan pie (dessert)

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Well, be assured that  the wait to get in or the hassle you survive to get tix is worth it. Of course, most folks go for the music which never fails to surprise, intrigue, and entertain, but the requirement to spend a certain minimum on food is actually a good thing because otherwise people would miss out on what is surpisingly tasty fare!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Nice view from rooftop,  multiple levels and bars on every section keep the drinks going.  Music was good with different acts on every stage but still overcrowded for me.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Loved it!  Great food and service.  Cool history too.  Recommend !!!  My first Nashville chicken and it was great!  HOT but, great.  Will return on my next visit.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: We didn't get tickets but waited in line for 1 1/2 and scored two seats inside. Was worth the wait and really cool to see. Very small inside and they pack the house.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Super cute bar! Very old but has a lot of history behind the honky tonk. Great live music - loved the upstairs and rooftop. Fun place to go at night or during the day. I will be back!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: LOVE this place!  Always a good show where you also make new (very close)friends. A Nashville trip is not complete without three things: Roberts Western World, Station Inn and The Bluebird...and Loveless, must have Loveless.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
I have lived in Nashville for 5 years and finally made it over to the Sutler. I've consistently heard locals rave about this place (particularly because of their bottomless brunch mimosas). My roommate and I were hungry, and decided to make our way on over to this notorious eatery. It was a bit packed, granted it was a Friday night, but we were able to snag one of the only open booths left. It's seat your self, so keep that in mind when going there!

Live music was playing, which is always nice on a weekend in Nashville, bonus points because it was a recent Voice contestant leading the live music. We started off with drinks, the strawberry-lemonade sangria pitcher was our choice, and it was pretty delicious, I would definitely order it again. My friend ordered a club sandwich and mac and cheese, she raved about the sandwich, but was a bit underwhelmed by the mac and cheese. I wasn't too hungry but got the whipped pimento, which was pretty tasty (nothing crazy amazing though). I have a pretty big sweet tooth so I also ordered the chocolate jar...it was huge--but hit the spot.  

The service was great, our waitress was so helpful, so attentive despite how packed it was. We ended the night by going right downstairs where they have a cocktail bar called, Rambler. They also have a billiards bar which we didn't have enough time to check out. So much to do in such a small space, I'll have to come back and check it out again!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
So worth the wait!! 

This cute little cafe is located in a strip mall and it is super famous because of the show Nashville (sorry never watched it but a friend dragged me along to this venue). We got there at 3:45PM  an waited in line close to 2 hours. It was a little hot outside and we were not exactly prepared but made friends with others in line and the time flew by. They even brought water for us as we were waiting (which was so nice). 

Once we got in we got seated in the benches in the back of the room. The venue was very small and intimate and we both absolutely loved the show. The food was not bad either - also very reasonably priced!

name: SongBird Tours
text: This tour is AMAZING!! One of the best tours I've ever been on (and I work in the tourism industry). Two incredibly talented songwriters and the tour guide lead a tour of Music Row and the songwriters perform the newest songs they have written and their greatest hits on the bus. The songwriters on our tour, Paul and Trey, have written many hits for artists like Carrie Underwood, Keith Urban, Randy Travis, Faith Hill, and so many more! They tell the stories behind the songs before they perform them and it's an incredibly moving and raw experience. Both are SO talented and have beautiful voices. We were truly moved. Even the tour guide, Lexie Hayden, jumped in at one point to sing and oh my goodness, she was wonderful! I highly recommend this tour!! There's no better way to see Nashville and learn the secrets of Music Row! Thank you for an awesome experience!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Love Tootsie's!  The band is always pretty good and willing to take requests.  

PSA: Bring some cash for tip money.  I like to remind folks to bring cash because so many people don't carry cash anymore but when going out to the Nashville bars, tips are often how musicians make their money!

Well, back to it!  If you don't like crowded places or people possibly bumping into you or touching you, this probably isn't the place for you!  

Tootsie's is often crowded at anytime of the day.  It is one of the original bars in Nashville and is iconic!!!!  I have never had a bad time, though have found it difficult to get in during busy times!!  If you are visiting Nashville, I would definitely say you should make a trip to visit Tootsie's!!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I had so much fun here! Great venue and live music was mind blowing.  Jackson, Courtney and their band were first class.  Crowd was a bit rowdy but added to the energy.

name: SongBird Tours
text: LOVED this tour! Tray, Taylor and Lexi are fantastic. Loved the songs - especially "97 Malibu!!! Great entertainment and informative. I highly recommend it.

name: True
text:
I've stayed here a number of times and while the hotel is nice, the restaurant is horrible.  Consistently the food is horrible and the breakfast portion size is a joke.  For $14 you can get 2 2" chicken tenders on two mini waffles... the egg white omelette was soaked in so much grease I asked the waitress to take it back and just bring me scrambled eggs and toast.  I was still charged the full price but I tried to eat the omelette and couldn't.  

There's a lot of good food near the hotel within walking distance.  I won't eat here again.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Stopped in just for a beer and music. Loved the place. Intimate setting and outstanding band.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: Went on a Thursday night around 7pm and I was shocked how empty this place was.  We started off with almost every appetizer and the deviled eggs were the best!  I ordered the steak and it was cooked to perfection, awesome flavor.  This place is perfect, not crazy but great food.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: The food was fantastic, and we received great service from our waitress Kim! I recommend getting the Patty Melt. Their milkshakes are handmade and were so good!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
I enjoyed breakfast here, with friendly service and historical roots. I made a reservation for 10:15am but didn't need it. After getting our table we were forgotten about for 5-10 min but once the staff realized that error we were served quickly. 

The breakfast menu isn't huge but there are several hearty options. The only real gluten-free option is the eggs, bacon, and home fries, and pray the seasoning doesn't have wheat maltodextrin. Next trip to town we will stop for lunch or dinner.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text: It is a great place and a short walk from TPAC so you do not need to move your car if going to both. My last meal here in this building was about 1959 before I left Nashville for another university and was also working at Cain-Sloans on the corner of 5th and Church. My friend and i had jambalaya and the meat loaf for entrees. My jambalaya was fabulous and the meat loaf seemed to have been frozen before it was cooked and was very mediocre for this main dish. Definitely not the taste I remember when coming there for years before I was 19. There also was no bread with the  meat loaf and vegges. The dessert bread pudding with a warm whisky brown sugar sauce was terrific with ice cream. This had been suggested by our very friendly and efficient waiter. I gave it a 4 instead of a 5 as the meat loaf was such a disappointment, but try it and take your children and grandchildren for a history lesson as well as a good meal in a lovely atmosphere..

name: The Stone Fox
text: The food was great! However, our service was not. Once we got our food, we didn't see our server. We waited longer to get our check than to get our food. Once we received it, we waited another ten minutes to have it picked up with our credit card. We finally put cash on the table and left.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: You can't beat the price on the endless mimosas! My friends and I went during brunch on a Saturday so of course it was busy, but we were able to start on our mimosas while we waited for our table. Our server was attentive and friendly. My mimosa glass was rarely empty because she was on top of the refills! My food was good, so I'll definitely be going back.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: If I could give this bar a -10, I would.  This is by far the most overcrowded, hot, noisy, and annoying bar.  Everything is filthy, you can't move inside and you feel like you're packed in like sardines, it smells awful, etc.  There are three stories to this place, and each story is the same thing.  I stayed there for about 10 minutes and the whole time I got bumped into, couldn't move, and couldn't hear any of my friends. Oh, and the drinks are small and overpriced. NOBODY should be spending their time here while in Nashville, to put it nicely.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
We went for dinner on Saturday night, and had absolutely wonderful experience. We had reservations, but plans changed, and we got there almost 90 minutes early. The girls up front, were totally accommodating, got us in right away. "Come on, we'll feed you!!" Is what we were told!!
Got immediately greeted by Eddie, who made all of us feel immediately comfortable and relaxed. He got us seated, introduced himself, made us all smile, and made it seem effortless.
He was attentive, fun and made great recommendations!
The food was amazing, everything came out correctly, and fast.
I had the bacon wrapped meatloaf, my wife the burger, and her dad, the shrimp and grits. It was all delicious, but the highlight may have been the pork belly appetizers!
Don't skip those!
10 out of 10 will be back
Great people and a historic location make this a must visit!!

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: What an amazing night. So happy and lucky to have got tickets on line. Wow. Sons of daughters playing in this intimate setting. A memory to treasure for a lifetime.  I'm so thankful and grateful to have sat with some amazing people during this experience. I really enjoyed the food and amazing music.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Had a great time there yesterday. Awesome music just an over all good time wit 60 plus of my new best friends

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: We came here because it was walking distance from our Air B&B and I would say it was okay, they had one really refreshing and delicious drink that had cucumber in it. But he food was only okay, nothing really all that special, in fact, the experience was kind of forgettable. My fiance got a burger that he was really excited about and ended up getting another burger the next day from somewhere else because he didn't feel his craving for burgers was satisfied. I had the pork mac and cheese and it was oddly sweet. I was not a fan at all, half the noodles were crunchy and the flavor was just not pleasing to me. The girl who served us was pretty nice and we liked that there was live music playing while we ate, but, that's pretty much every bar in Nashville

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I don't know how this place works but the door guy made fun of my husband for holding onto a tote bag we had just bought at a show at the Ryman. I was annoyed.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Fun place. Good music and signature drinks. Beautiful on the roof top.  Good service too.

name: Tin Roof
text:
Came here as part of a "pub crawl" that was anything but. Basically paid 20 bucks for a sheet of paper with a list of bars on it and told it was self directed. It was one of the lamest most cash grabby things I've ever seen. The organizer worked at this bar so I blame them. They even had inaccuracies printed on their piece of paper. It felt like such a scam. 

I ordered this sandwich. The B n C Medley or something like that. Described as beef brisket with queso and peppers. I basically got a bun with a little cheese sauce, some pepers, and probably a half ounce of meat. A half ounce of meat. A half ounce of meat. Another blatant ripoff that. 12 bucks for a sandwich with less meat that a single slice of cold cuts. 

I ordered the fried green tomato appetizer. This was actually good, and came with plenty of pimento cheese, but only 4 tomato slices. 

Drinks were pricy and not very strong. Service was fine. Not the waitresses fault her bosses are so greedy.

When it appears a business' number one goal is not quality or service but the extraction of the maximum amount of cash while providing the minimum in return, I definitely would never be back.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: A must-see if you are visiting Nashville and love music (even if you are not as familiar with country music). I loved the intimate setting of the "in the rounds" setup--each artist took turns playing, and it was like getting to sit in on a group of talented friends/ musicians sharing their stories through music. My only complaint is that the online reservations ran out so quickly (within minutes of opening 1 week prior)! Thankfully, we got in after arriving early at 430pm to line up for a stand-by spot as the 13th,14th, and 15th people in line and were seated in the pews, which was still great. So glad we got in, because this was definitely a highlight of the trip.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: My wife and I got here at midday and were able to cozy right up to the bar with a great view of the stage. The musicians, namely the lady lead singer, were quite good and very entertaining. I'd go back, but made a difference that we were able to get a seat and stick around awhile.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
This place was mediocre at best! I understand it is an iconic place, it is a staple here in Nashville, but it looks and feels dirty. 

There are three levels. Which we didn't know at first, so when we arrived we thought it was so crowded we weren't going to find a place to sit. 

Once we walked up the stairs to the second level we were presented with another full bar, tables, and a stage. We decided to have a seat. We ordered appetizers: Buffalo Chicken Wings, Fried Spear Pickles, and Supreme Nachos with Chicken. 

There was nothing original about the food. The performances weren't that good, off key at times, and the tables and walls had lots of writings on them. As if it was 'a thing' to write your name down or a message. Before I could express my thoughts on that, my mother scratched BZ-PZ into the table. Well I guess they happened. Haha 

Sitting at the table I felt like I couldn't have gotten a sliver bc it was so worn down. I also felt like with the moisture sitting in the table the writings that were there could have gotten on my clothes and ruined them. 

Our food which was plated in paper plates, I get it but also....where does the money go? Clearly this place is profitable. However it doesn't show at all in the decor, food, or performances. 

Anyway, after finishing our food, I walked up to the third floor to see what that looked like. Well it was a lot of stairs and the nicest level at a quick glance. There was a patio which looked cool but I was 'Tootsie-d'  out by this point and just wanted to bounce. 

Overall, it is a 'been there done that, don't have to ever go again' kind of a place for me.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
We had to go here! There is so much history here. I was with a group from work and this was a must stop for us.  There was live country music on every level, we went straight to the top.  They have a rooftop patio which affords beautiful views.  We had to make a mark...literally...wrote our names on the wall.

I loved the ambience here.  It was true country.  There were couples slow dancing, friends line dancing and the singer of the band dancing on the bar.  It was everything that I pictured Nashville to be.

Go there!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Great music joint...don't come here for the food...just drinks music and great ole time

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Walked in expecting an eclectic take on fine dining. Has a kinda classy feel. Reminded me of the Merchant Tavern in St. John's, NL, a restored, classic brick bank building. Unfortunately, Woolworth's is still Woolworths. Uninspired menu, terrible wait staff. Rushed us from the moment we sat down. (Never bring a main when appetizers were only served 5 mins earlier.) Either poor kitchen coordination or intentional table turning. In any case, if looking for something with similar atmosphere while in St. John's, the Merchant Tavern is 5 star on all accounts. 

Not impressed.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Nothing screams True Nashville like the Bluebird Cafe! If you're lucky enough to score a ticket to their singer/songwriter concert series, it's a must-do! You can thank me later. The Bluebird sells out every night, it is a legendary venue that has reared many of country music's biggest hit songs. 
If you're in Nashville, get on their website to check for showings and to buy tickets. During each show, there are a few pew seats available on a first come first serve basis, but the line for those seats begins hours before the show. 
This was truly an incredible experience! I oils love to come here on a date, hopefully that will happen in the near future :)

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Perfect down and dirty Nashville bar with flowing drinks and great live music! Liked having the option is explore a few floors of music/bar options and the views of Broadway from the rooftop deck.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: The music is good. But the food is typical greasy bar food. Nothing amazing. The BLT the bread was greasy and kind of burnt. Also they need more gf and keto options.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Too crowded, lots of levels but so does everything else in Nashville, I don't get the nostalgia behind this bar but ok.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Such an absolute pleasure to have been able to visit Tootsie's! When we came, it was jammed full of people, but nothing that we couldn't handle. It was an incredible experience to come watch live music for the first time in Music City! We only stayed for a few songs because we had other places to be, but I'm sure glad we stopped in! The decorations amongst all the walls were really neat and gave us a glimpse into the history that made Nashville what it is today. It's very cool to think about the artists that once graced the stage here and have made it big. A family member purchased a T-shirt here for me without my knowledge and that was a great surprise and great way to remember where I'd been. The building itself is beautiful inside and out, and has been very well taken care of. I can't wait to one day visit again!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: Offered the band naming rights to my 2nd child for a Queen song (preferably "somebody to love" or "Bohemian" and they only knew "Fat bottom girls".  Not what we were looking for.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text: I was here for Cinco De Mayo & the Predators were in the play off's. such a huge scene & the staff was still speedy & accommodating. We even managed to wrangle a table on the roof. Such a shame we had dinner reservations & had to give it up but boy howdy it was a blast & great views of the hysteria below.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text: Welcome to Nashville! Let me guess, you came here to "be discovered and get a record deal"?! Well, you should probably just stop while you're ahead and go to DSC and get a drink from Tyler Bennet, because you're gonna need it with those kinds of hopes and dreams!

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
My husband and I went for lunch. I ordered a Caesar salad and a cup of sweet potato and black bean soup. My husband ordered the burger and fries. 

Everything was really good . I loved the Caesar dressing and the soup was good. The soup is more like a chili though. 

My husband said his burger was good. They bring you their homemade sauces to try. All of them are good. The fries were good nothing special. 

I like the restaurant will definitely go back to try other items.  The staff is very nice too.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
Cool. What an experience.

Having done the whole loud Broadway for a couple of nights, we were looking for something chill to do. That's when Bluebird cafe popped up on my yelp search.

Situated randomly in a plaza (across from the Whole Foods and other stores), Bluebird cafe sits. We went on a rainy Sunday night for songwriters night, hosted by Steve Goodie. No reservations are taken for the night-it's a first come, first serve.

We parked in the furniture store lot next door and walked over to stand in line. Almost two hours we stood and luckily, when the time came, the line started moving.. And the doors closed right behind us.  We were the last two people to get in for the night!

We were seated in the pews in the back (most people got tables, but I think it's because we were the last ones) and were served right away. We got some local brews and nachos to share.. And sat back to listen.

Steve Goodie is an awesome host- he's hilarious, musically talented, and full of charisma. And then the songwriters came up to stage- from young to old, to guitars to accordions, to singles to married folk, the range was endless. And it even ended with a famous songwriter (who wrote songs for Faith Hill, Keith Urban, etc) But overall, they were all solid and great. The crowd appreciated the music too (much different than what you see on Broadway) and it was just overall a great night. 

If you're looking for a chill place in Nashville to hear some great singers/songwriters and are willing to wait in line for it, definitely check out Bluebird Cafe- what a gem in Nashville.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Nashville's venerable music hall and bar is a must see for any visitor to the Broadway scene in Music City. 

Chances are it won't take long for you to find your way to Tootsie's Orchid Lounge as the lines are usually the longest, the music the loudest, and the crowd the most heavily served. 3 floors worth of music await you, each featuring their own band, long bar, and mass of revelers. In fact, it almost feels like 3 separate clubs in one building. Sure, the drinks are on the expensive side for the locale but I would argue the ambiance is worth the extra coin; especially on the open rooftop located on the 3rd floor. Oh, and watch those steps ladies - I witnessed a few close calls on my visit. 

I should also point out that Tootsie's Orchid Lounge seems to attract the best talent in Music City. Every act in the area competes for stage time thanks to their seemingly always packed house. Don't forget to tip - the house doesn't pay the bands whatsoever. 

You haven't truly visited Nashville without the stop at Tootsie's Orchid Lounge so you may as well get it in early since they are the bar set for the nightlife scene on Broadway.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
To begin, this place is filthy. Ask for plastic silverware if you dare to eat here; the rolled silver actually had dried food on it. Plus the glasses were cloudy, so I am fairly certain that they were unwashed as well. 
The quality of the food was poor. My husband got the cheeseburger and was thoroughly disappointed; the patties were thin and significantly over-cooked. I tried two of their specialty cocktails and both of them were ultra-sweet. Its like they were syrup- instead of spirit-based. That might have been fine if whatever syrups they had used were even slightly well made; they weren't. My husband loves bourbon and, from the look of the menu, the Sutler carried many of his favorites. Yet this too proved deceptive; three of the bourbons he requested weren't available, in spite of them being listed on the menu. When my husband finally found a bourbon that they did have in-house, the price on our bill was $4 more per drink than the price listed on the menu. We might not have noticed had the server not left the over-sized menus on our table throughout our entire visit - long after we had ordered. The giant things were in our way all night. 
Most of the staff we encountered were as distasteful as the food and the lack of cleanliness. The manager was actually standing near the food window and shouting expletives at other staff members. Some staff seemed to deserve to be shouted at, as they didn't seem to care much about their customers or the restaurant in which they were working. While our server fell into this category, there was one brunette server that was kind to us. Sadly, she wasn't assigned to our table. 
Avoid this place. Even with a cool-looking stage that we thought world be appealing, we found the music to be an afterthought. The artist playing made us think we were anywhere other than Nashville. Nearly all other music venues in town offer outstanding music; the Sutler not so much.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
I love music and am not exactly a country fan per say ...but this place was amazing. 

 Four people sit in a circle/square (let's not be technical) and take turns singing songs they wrote. There is great dialogue between them and the crowd and the songs sung were absolutely fascinating/impressive on the evening I went given the atmosphere/vibe. 

I think this place is a must visit if you are ever in the nashville area.

name: The Bluebird Cafe
text:
We planned to get tickets for this but they are elusive. We arrived around 7:30pm to line for the late 9:30 show. It was worth the 2 hour wait. We chatted up with others in line.

We got really lucky and was seated right next to the performers.

The bluebird has had so many song writers come through over the years. This is a very intimate setting. The performers are seated in the middle of the room and small tables form around them and it fans out. 

There was a $15 cover charge, but well worth it. The food menu was also decent with a wide selection of appetizers, food and salad options.

If you're coming from out of town this is a must visit.

name: Woolworth on Fifth
text:
Woolworth on 5th is a must s when visiting Nashville, simply for the rich history of the Civil Rights movement and counter sit-ins.  

The building and restaurant has expanded and completely been renovated, but they preserved the stools and the markings of where the counter and stools used to be (before they were moved) are still there.  

They've got a nice menu, but we shared a chocolate malt while sitting at the counter and taking it all in.  

Great malt, lovely service and something everyone should experience.

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Though not my favorite Honky Tonk on the NashVegas strip, it's up there. It's a must-stop bar blasting country songs that needs to be a part of your bar crawl.

Sureeeeee there are some cheaper bars and sureeeeee it's way crowded, but c'mon! It's right there smack dad in the middle of the action! You'll stop here - whether you like it or not!

name: Tootsie's Orchid Lounge
text:
Walked through this historic Nashville watering hole as part of our "Walkin' Nashville Music City Legends Tour". 

As it was a hot day, I saddled up to the bar for a quick Jack & Coke.

The bartendress asked "Who is that guy?", referring to our tour guide. "He comes through here every day at about the same time with a bunch of people just to use the bathroom."

I explained we were on a walking tour and he was our guide.

She said out of all the time she has worked there, I was the first on the tour to ever buy a drink.

I told her it takes a New Yorker to break the ice.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: I made reservations for last night, and it did not go well. After a long uber ride, we were sat down and given menus. We waited. And waited. And waited. Then a woman comes over and tells us that due to a flood in the basement they are unable to feed any other people, then asks us if we wanted drinks. We say yes... And wait. And wait. And wait. No server came over the entire time we were there. We go to the bar to order drinks there, the bartender tells us they had let call 10 minutes ago.... So we leave. I understand it was a poor situation, but they could of handled us properly and appropriately. Big let down.

name: Paradise Park Trailer Resort
text:
I ordered the Chicken Fried Chicken burger with Sweet Potato fries and a Sweet Tea. I then proceeded to the pick up counter, where literally a minute later my order was ready. I was pleased with the fast service as I was hungry, but didn't question why it was so fast for a Chicken burger. I filled up my drink and sat down to eat and I noticed the food looked like leftovers, it wasn't until my boyfriend tried some chicken and fries and mentioned how it looked like it was old, had either been sitting in the kitchen or refried and was pretty cold considering a few minutes had only past. I wasn't going to return it as I don't like making a big fuss but my bf said he would since I paid for it and shouldn't get leftovers. 

When he politely told the lady at the pick up counter about it she turned to me and yelled 'I gave this to you 10 minutes ago of course it's cold' (definitely wasn't 10 minutes ago) then she told me 'I got you' and went to the cook at the back who then came out and stared me down. After he re-made my food, he came out with it and then had a go at me telling me that if I waited 10 minutes then of course it would be cold and continued to basically tell me I was wrong. I didn't argue back, instead I looked at him as I was already uncomfortable with how they were acting.  

The food this time, was great. The Chicken was more golden then brown, cold and burnt and the fries were steaming hot unlike the previous bunch. Obviously they thought I wouldn't notice if they just sent out an order already made, which was ready in 2 minutes from ordering, compared to when they remade my food which took more than that. 

As a server myself at a great brunch restaurant located in downtown, I have never been so appalled by such service. If a customer pays for a meal and they are not happy with it (in my case not because I'm picky but I don't appreciate leftovers) you don't come out and yell at them for your idiotic mistake, you re-make the order and get on with your day. 

I get its stressful, I'm in the same environment but if a customer is unhappy with a meal you fix it and remain polite. 

The food was actually great when they cooked it fresh but sadly the service from the back of house was disgusting from both the female and older male, therefore I won't be returning and will spread the word about my experience so no one else gets treated such a way for a mistake the cook made by serving leftovers.

Because the food was good they get two stars, otherwise I would've rated it Zero.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: This was one of my favorite spots. We waited 2 hours for breakfast only to be told once we were seated that there were no more hash browns or grits. With such a limited  brunch menu there wasnt a lot of choices. We left after an hour drive. Total waste of 4 hours of our day.

name: SongBird Tours
text: Great tour. Intimate setting to hear original songwriters story and song. Trey, Lexi and Carly were great! Nice way to see and hear some of Nashville's music history.

name: The Sutler Saloon
text: First off their bottomless mimosas are only $17 and there's no time limit! There was a long wait when I got there but the bar downstairs let's you start the bottomless while you wait and you can play all sorts of different games in the bar. Live music and the staff was so sweet! Food was also delicious! I got the chicken fried biscuit and made it hot (because it's Nashville)  Also I'm assuming there's always a wait on the weekend so take that into consideration!

name: The Sutler Saloon
text:
What a cool place! I came here on a Friday night with my date around 10pm to grab a couple drinks and they had a really great cover band playing an eclectic mix of songs (including their own renditions of Red Hot Chili Peppers and R. Kelly). It's called a saloon, but it's not really a saloon. I liked that it wasn't just another honky tonk place.

What surprised me most about this bar is that they have two more bars downstairs underground - one's a lounge and one's a pool hall! The DJ at the lounge was doing a fantastic job playing a great selection of music. I was also really impressed by the cluttered cowboy boots hanging down from the top of the stairwell on the way down toward these two underground bars.

The Sutler gets Five Stars in my book for its live music, the lounge DJ's music downstairs, its overall atmosphere, its many eclectic surprises, and its awesome decor!
But I give the Sutler Three Stars for its service and food quality. I had to wait an unreasonably long time for a waiter to come to our table at the saloon part of the bar. And our drinks down in the lounge took an unreasonably long time to make and/or come to our table. Additionally: We wanted to order dessert at the Saloon, but they were out of their (only) two dessert options, and the potato hummus appetizer we ordered instead was not that great. The chips were oily and hard, and the dip (which wasn't anything to rave about) needed a bigger bowl for the size of those chips!

I still had a lot of fun there and highly recommend people check it out, at least for the fun of the music and the exploration of the underground bars. I also want to come back on a Sunday for their bluegrass brunches!

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: SO FUN! were in Nashville for a bachelorette party and stayed there most of the night. Awesome music and great drinks.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Worth it! Little pricy, but burger was excellent. Drinks were yummy. Good customer service all around. Really neat atmosphere with the music and memorabilia. Not the biggest hard rock I've ever been to, but not terribly small. I recommend going! You won't be disappointed!

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: One of my favorites on Broadway! Good moonshine shots and drinks. The bands are always great. I've been here several times and two times they've been accommodating to Chicago Blackhawks fans and even the bands had hawks jerseys on. Fun place to get the party started!!!

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text: Great place with excellent music, stiff drinks but most importantly, an honest staff and clientele.  My girlfriend left her purse, and the manager, recovered it, called me from her phone (thank God she doesn't lock it, lol) and even charged it when we picked it up for the morning walk of shame.  All cash and cards in place.  Thank you, we'll be back.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Cons: No in room safe and no mini fridge, and the only customer accessible microwave I found was in the gift shop. The walls are on the thinner side. Wifi is paid (to get free internet you have to use the computers in the lobby). Pepsi products only, no Coca-Cola. There is no soundwall between the freeway and the hotel (only a problem if your room faces it, which mine did) and still don't understand why they didn't put heavier curtains on the windows to muffle the sound better. 

Pros: The bed is extremely comfortable at least! I was also pretty pleased with the fact that they had two sitting chairs and an ottoman, especially since most hotels usually have only one sitting chair and a desk chair. Really close to the airport (selling point for us, but could be a con for others).

The overall service was good. They delivered a toothbrush to the room when the front desk ran out of the toothbrushes that they kept up there, and included toothpaste as well. They also rebooted the printer immediately when I couldn't get it to print my boarding passes.

name: The Bridge
text:
I've always come here during show cases for Country shows.
Its just a bar that serves food and is smack right in downtown Nashville.
Has a cool view over the street and the busy life of the hotel guests as well as tourists.
One thing for music is that it ECHOS so bad. It's hard to have a conversation and whoever is singing has a natural reverb in the place.
I did order some food while listening. You pay def. more for hotel prices but it got me through the night and a few drinks.
It is a great place to visit, meet at a local noticeable area if you get lost, meet at the Renaissance hotel!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
Was at this hotel for about 4 days for a conference and everything was really good. The hotel is a little older but well managed. Love it that every room have a balcony. I would in deed stay hear again.

The service was really good as well but was a little slow cleaning my room and understand the hotel was pretty full. May need to bring extra staff when hotel is about full so when you get a break your room will be clean....

name: The 5 Spot
text: We went Sunday night to hear Heath Haynes' cover band. It was perfect: great music in a divey sort of atmosphere -- exactly what we wanted out of the place. There was no cover charge, and our drinks averaged $5 a piece (beer and whiskey). If you like hearing Waylon Jennings, the Allman Brothers, Elvis, etc., Heath and his band are your fellows.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: You pay a luxury hotel price for a fairly standard hotel.  Not worth it.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
We had an amazing time here! 

Ended up here on a Saturday night because all other bars were too crowded to walk. This had the perfect amount of people in it. 

The band was amazing, Moonshine Outlaws. Good music, good beers, and friendly people make for a fun night. I will be bac

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: First time in Nashville, and we just had a great time and AMAZING food here! Tommy our server was very hospitable and engaged genuinely with us! Molly came by to check on us and she was also very genuine. Great food and great service is a WIN WIN for me! Keep it up team!

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text:
*DO NOT TRUST THIS HOTEL TO SHIP ANYTHING OR DEAL WITH FEDEX, UPS, ETC* 
I would give this hotel a ZERO if I could...
 
I needed to ship out a large, heavy pelican case containing expensive equipment. Last Sunday, before taking off to the airport, I went to reception to have this taken care of. The hotel did NOT have any FedEX Ground slips so I left my info on an express slip + my email.
I asked MEGAN if she could just schedule a ground pick up with the info I gave & email me the tracking number. She said that wouldnt be a prob. Come to find out by another employee... she is new in that dept and totally messed up.

Now I'm dealing with PEGGY. Horrible customer service. Guys - I left this package last Sunday.. its Friday and im STILL chasing a tracking #. 

I've been calling, emailing, this is just ridiculous. They promise to get back to me by a certain time & never do. I've probably called and explained my story 20 times.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: It was a amazing stay and service, we had a late check in and everything was exactly what we needed. There food and service was amazing. We will come back. Parking is free and there front desk is always happy to help.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: The butterscotch moonshine is to die for.  I got the Peach which wad good; however, the wife had the butterscotch and it was awesome.

name: The Valentine
text: Such a fun honky tonk (i will use this term this one time in my life, because it was nashville)! The atmosphere was very fun and enjoyable, decent beer selections, friendly people, great music, and lots of dancing! The place completely changed vibe after 11 pm, with the awesome country music band (which, to point out, played some incredible riffs including pink floyd and others) packing up and the music switching to club like, at which point we left. Still, really enjoyed the spot, and highly recommended for good music and a chill honky tonkin' vibe (i lied above, i used that term again)!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Super food, super wait staff.  Noise level is high, but enjoy the experience, that is part of it.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
A fun place in Nashville. I was there around the Country music awards. This place was a lot of fun and packed full of people listening to country music( live ).

Except for the wait to get in is was a fun time and drinks were reasonable priced.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: We went here after Tootsies (my apologies! :)) But it had a ton of great performers and plenty of room which I liked. It is dark in there so I could have probably taken a nap, not realizing how nice it was outside! But liked the venue feel to the place! Bartending staff was super nice and quick to our orders! Definitely a place you should check out if doing the Broadway thing!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: The dining room was virtually empty but the food took more than an hour to arrive. When it did everything was stone cold. Heard a couple at a table behind us complain that their food was also cold. Too expensive for the serving size and mediocre food. Service was friendly, though slow. It did take a while before our water was refiled and the appetizers came out with the main dishes. Would not recommend.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: This hotel is awesome! I gave it four stars because the pillows were really soft and didn't give my neck support. It was a bit uncomfortable for me even if I doubled up my pillows it was just too flat. The mattress was pretty good, nice and firm. The bed sheets were very soft and good quality.  The hotel itself is super clean and elegant. I loved the breakfast buffet and the room service is outstanding. We ordered room service for dinner and everything was ready it 20 minutes. They have a great dinner menu lots of veriety. Hubby and i ordered the Tennessee bbq pulled pork sandwich, it was great but a bit too sweet for me. We also ordered the chicken panini and it was very good and it came with fries. The Bread pudding was also good. I have no complaints as for food, and atmosphere. Location is a plus it's close to downtown. I will return and it's a pet friendly hotel with no pet fee. They even give you a doggie bags to dispose their waste. Our room was super clean, they even had an orchestra playing live music in the lobby. I wish I could have given this hotel 4 1/2 stars instead of 4. We shall return.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: We ordered the nachos appetizers and the half roast bbq chicken....huge portions! And delicious! The bbq chicken was alright, but the nachos were excellent. I haven't been to many Hard Rock cafes but I enjoyed the experience at the Hard Rock Nashville. There were photographs of famous country singers adorned on the walls and great, live music...really made you feel like you were in music country!

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: My quest to try brisket everywhere I can continues on. The brisket here is very smokey and spicy form the dry rub. It's very tasty, but just not my favorite way to enjoy brisket. I got one piece of the brisket sushi and it was pretty good although I probably wouldn't order it again. I also got the brisket nachos and they were good as well. Service was a little slow because a table of 20 had just been seated before us. Our waitress was friendly and apologetic and even bought us 2 beers on her for having to wait. It's a cool place and I would totally go back if someone else wanted to.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
Heard some awesome music coming from here so had to stop in. Ended up staying for almost three hours listening to Brit Stokes. 

It was early afternoon and it ended up being a great place to stop and take in some great music. Friendly and attentive bartenders. Local beer. Comfortable barstools, not the cheesy, uncomfortable metal ones that so many places have. 

Loved the variety of music that was played. You could even carry on a conversation if you wanted to. 

Whiskey Bent ended up being one of my favorites on Broadway.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
I live in Orlando, so we have fairly large Hard Rock's here and I was expecting the same while I was here. This wasn't so. It was fairly small, there was no area for a live band (that I could see), which I thought was strange considering we were in the music capital of the world. 

However, the staff was friendly, especially the valet who was more than happy to help direct us to our next venture. The server was kind of pushy when I didn't order a drink, but I think she was just trying to be friendly, but I was a little put off by it, because it made me feel a little guilty for not getting one, even though I was the designated driver. But the hamburger I ordered was fantastic and it was quiet besides the music playing. But it wasn't obnoxiously loud. As these places tend to be. 

I wish their store was a little bigger and had more merchandise. They didn't even have the special shot glass for their store! 

But otherwise, it was pretty much the same as all the others. I kind of feel like, if you've been to one, you've been to them all, but still a great place to eat.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Alexis was great taking our order
With a cheerful smile and recommended the souvenir glass to take home - thanks I love cup collections and the food was good.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: My biggest issue had to do with the manager and our server. Pointed out that the shots served were light. They claim there is a certain amount for a shot. Snotty server poured out plastic cup shot, in front of manager into shot glass and indeed it was short. Manager was not a nice guy at all. I told him his customer service was not good. He asked if I wanted to step outside to discuss it further. My friend also indicated his buddy or bouncer was ready to help and looked like he wanted to hit me.  I told the manager that I did not want to discuss this further. Proof was already too clear. Moral. Enjoy the music. Great. Booze of course is good. But don't point out a fault. They can't handle it. Lots of choices in Nashville fortunately. I simply can't recommend a place that employs people in customer service with bad attitudes. Go next store or across the street. Or wait a month I'm sure neither worker can last long there and hopefully they don't grace another place with their style of service. Sorry Bootleggers perhaps you should help your manager from this past Saturday night. He needs some training or a leather boot ride.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: This was my first time visiting Nashville and I tried most of the bars on the main strip of Broadway and this was by far my favorite. Although the drinks are a tad pricier than the other bars (or at least it seemed that way), it was still a great time. I was impressed with the bands they had and also the place is open and space compared to all the surrounding bars. Loved it here!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Burgers are huge.  I would suggest sharing.  Love the variety of rock music playing. Onion rings are great;however, the burgers were to be cooked medium well and these were cooked more then well done.  Very burnt and not good.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Love this hotel, it wasn't over priced and the look and feel of this hotel was luxurious! I actually wish I could of stayed longer to enjoy it more. Their food was good and customer service was very friendly and welcoming. Only downfall for me was their parking lot is just in front and it feels like a longer walk if you have a lot of bags.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I'm not the bar hopping type but in Nashville you must. There's live music everywhere! Some better than others but overall great. We decided to be deaf here the longest. We left because the singer changed. It's packed with energetic people dancing and singing. The style is similar to a concert. Everyone faces the stage and sings along and dances in their spots while being considerate of their surroundings.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Decent Sheraton, the public areas are better than the rooms. A little off the beaten path, but convenient to the airport. Staff was friendly but a tad slow. Overall, a pleasant stay, and a little more character than the average Sheraton.

name: The Valentine
text: I had a great time at the Valentine! I was able to get my dance on! The DJ  did a great job of playing a variety of music including top 40. A group of us came out on a Friday Night and it was awesome. The ambiance was eclectic and perfect for a great Night Club Scene. So if you want to get your groove on then get ready to get your dancing shoes on.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: Fantastic spot on Broadway. A gem! We came to hear J. Edwards play and he was marvelous. Get the oatmeal cookie moonshine. Out of this world. So much better than the huge bars on broadway.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
My life is like a series of ADHD moments. You got into one thing with a good intention and then it snowballs into something completely different than the direction you were going for. This is exactly what happened to me on Monday night when I was sitting in the Starbucks near my home where my complete was open ready to do homework. 

The guy next to me at said Starbucks started talking to me about one thing and we landed on the subject of swing dancing. He told me that dancing was going to take place that night at The 5 Spot. I had never heard of it nor did I know of its dancing. I had only been swing dancing at one spot so far here and though I enjoyed it, I was looking for something that offered something more. I considered going to Brentwood, but it is my understanding they are a bit of a more babyboomer crowd. I love dancing with them, but I enjoy a mix of all ages versus it being lopsided in the aging of dancers.

I packed up my laptop, ran home to change and off I was to The 5 Spot. I arrived before 9pm where I got free entry. After 9, it costs to enter and dance. They call it Motown Mondays, but truly is a mix of all genres from the 50s to 70s. They offered more traditional swing and rock n roll until 10:30pm before turning it up to some other stuff. I loved it. The crowd evolved with the music. Once the swing dancing music concluded, many of those people dispersed and a new type of crowd appeared. It was extremely lively and fun. Everyone had a great time, especially me! I didn't leave until nearly midnight. This was on a Monday, too, as I said!

Drinks were reasonable. I didn't have anything, however, after talking to a few fellow dancers and getting to know them - they vouched that the bartenders served up some booze heavy pours. All drinks are under $10.

Parking might be a bit painful, but if you get there early like me - you won't have any issues. Just leave all valuables in the trunk of the car or leave them at home since they really do not have a place for you to store them. 

What to wear - wear comfortable shoes! Ladies typically wear weekend attire or period clothing of the era of swing dancing. I personally always wear a dress with leggings because if I am spinning around, I sure don't want any of my stuff being shown. Guys wear jeans usually or slacks along with a casual shirt or button down. Again, this vastly depends on how deep you are into the swing dancing scene. People later in the evening wore clothes that were more suited for going out than for deliberate dancing like the earlier crowd. 

This particular night I went, they did have a DJ. This would seem pretty obvious from the above statements, but the 5 Spot does have live music as well. I look forward to when I will have the chance to check that out and dance to them.

5 Spot, I look forward to you becoming my weekly habit!

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text:
Service terrible.

Food cold.

Server was in the bathroom on the phone the entire time.

I have very few words about this experience.

name: The Valentine
text:
Stopped in last Thursday afternoon because we heard the great live music while walking down broadway. We had two beers each while we listened to the band play. They were really great. The venue is very pretty and is two floors. It has a very pretty large chandelier in the center of the ceiling and had a large bar downstairs and one or two bars upstairs. 

The only reason I am giving this place three stars is because when I came back on Saturday night they did not have live music. They had a DJ and a girl playing the violin. On Broadway with so many venues playing live music they should have had some kind of band playing. I was a little disappointed because on Thursday afternoon it was great!

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text: I had high hopes for this place, but was very disappointed.  I did not like the ribs at all, they were way more tender than ribs should be (literally fell off the bone), and did not have much flavor to them at all.
