The ribs were so bad I didn't even bother finishing the portion I got on my sampler platter.  I've never had ribs before that were so bad I had no desire to finish them.  The only fairly good thing I had in the sampler platter was the Texas sushi- a jalapeno popper wrapped in brisket, and the brisket was fairly lackluster.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Don't go to this place with a large group.  They struggled with the service and timing of the meal.  I don't know if it was the size of the group or what, but they cook their steaks way too fast.  Rare to medium rare is the best you'll get.  Medium  to well doesn't happen, even if you send it back.  Drinks, like all other places in downtown Nashville are way overpriced and not much of a selection.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: I went there during the day and it was only about 25% full. But, the lack of people made it even more fun. The band worked hard to get people involved and they were a lot of fun.

name: The 5 Spot
text:
Came for a Lightnin 100 event. It was filled with tons of people, but they have plenty of standing room and a handful of tables with stools to choose from.

Tons of beer choices to choose from with good prices. The downside was that the female restroom was flooded.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Not really a fan of eating at Hard Rock but it was close to the strip and we needed nourishment so we dined in.  The food was decent enough and the service was good.  Food isn't particularly fresh or foodie worthy at all but it was a big clean restaurant.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: First time in Nashville and it was late in the evening on a Friday night, last month. We were not sure where to eat. We saw Hard Rock and thought, "ok we will go there, Hard Rock always has decent food". Boy were we wrong. We should have realized... no line like everywhere else... run. But.. its the Hard Rock, cant be that bad... We went in and were seated right away. I think we were one of five tables. The waiter was great, excellent service. The music was great as well. The drinks were horrible and very overpriced. Still, no big deal. We ordered three huge fajita nachos and two burgers with fries. The burgers with fries were just okay, a little bland. The Nachos, thats where we went wrong. By the time they got to the table they were very cold. One plate had nearly raw fajita meat on it, a little brown on the outside, red and dripping with blood on the inside. They did not ask how the meat was to be prepared. We sent it back as the person would not have been able to eat blood-soaked chips. The second person ate a few chips off the enormous plate and stopped eating. The third person, She started eating and went to get her fork from under neath the edge of her plate and felt something odd. When she lifted her plate there was food literally baked on to the half of the bottom of the plate. It had been there for a bit. We still had not gotten the third nachos back from the kitchen. We showed the waiter the dirty plate, he was pretty embarrassed and apologized. We told him to cancel the third one. As he walked away he was telling a coworker about the dirty plate and showing it to her. The third plate of nachos was coming out as he was walking back. When they arrived at the table you could clearly tell the kitchen did not appreciate the food being sent back. The meat was burned and the whole top of the stack of nachos was burned black. I am guessing they were just making sure that the meat was done and not raw, right... So the waiter apologized and said he would talk to the manager. As we were waiting for the check I needed to use the ladies room. I walked in, it was appalling. There was wet toilet paper strung across the bathroom floor. The stall itself was not even hover-able. I could understand if this was a busy establishment, but it was pretty empty. Staff was just sitting around at the bar pretty much doing nothing. Someone could have easily checked the conditions of the restroom. The manager never did come out. The waiter advised us that the manager took the nachos off the bill. Our bill for two burgers and fries and about six cocktails... $120 before the tip... Save your money and stay far away from this nasty establishment.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text:
A big bar but usually full, not uncomfortably busy but about right. The bad was good and this place has Dickel so I was happy.  As we were walking in the singer was in the middle of something about George Strait and a drunk voice in the crowd yelled, "If you don't like George Strait- Get the F**k OUT"..I had to laugh.

 They have this big mural on the wall and I could identify all but one, the old chubby guy on the bottom. I was told he was a Grand Old Opera star back in the day, probably before i was born. I've been here a few times and have always had a good time.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: Great place to stay. Very clean, polite staff. We did have an issue with our room when we first arrived and it was a bit of a headache but the manager took care of it and upgraded us to a room across the hall and everything was great. The pool area was super nice and has been very well kept. The restaurant was great, great food and service. Our server Tessa was amazing and Andrew at the front desk was so very helpful.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text:
I can't begin to explain how great of a time we had hanging out at the bar listening to Brandon Holden sing/play his guitar on Saturday. First of all, this place looks like a small bar from the outside and very unassuming. It is anything but that! There are some bar height tables against the wall and a pretty long bar top with bar stools plus enough room for some dancing while enjoying the music. They have like 30 flavors of moonshine which could easily make hundreds of different combinations. The drinks are reasonably priced and they have a big variety of everything from Bourbon to Vodka and plenty of very cold bottled beers. The insides are a little dark but it gives off that saloon feel like the old country days. As for Broadway bars, they have the cleanest bathrooms and that is a plus when you drink a few beers.
The daytime girls behind the bar serve up more than just drinks. They are super friendly and totally funny to talk to. While we were there, we got to know Jess since it was not very busy. She is the best. The other girl, Deanna has an amazing voice and it is a special treat when she gets on stage to sing a duet with Brandon. On Sunday morning there is a musician who plays his own original music and though he is a bit loud, his music is very good. Glad we visited here and can't wait to return in 6 mos. for our next vacation.

name: The Valentine
text: I went to Nashville with friends for the weekend and of course popped in and out of bars all day. We decided to go in to the valentine and I'm glad we did! We went to the rooftop area, there wasn't many people at first, but there was live music the whole time (awesome bands btw), Sean was the best bartender I've had in a while and the others were also very attentive. My friend and I try nachos everywhere we go and there's were some of the best we've had. Once it came closer to game time it started to fill up but the staff was still just as awesome, they even brought out a table and chairs for a disabled vet. By far one of my favorite memories from that weekend, we stayed pretty much all day! Only downside is that it's a Georgia bar. GEAUX Tigers!! 12/10 recommend

name: The Judge's Vinegarroon
text:
Got the sampler plate.
1) brisket was really good. texture was excellent. tender. nice flavor, good smoke ring.
2) sausage. good. garden variety smoked sausage.
3) wings. good. 
4) ribs. ***  they gave me a butt end that was like shoe leather and inedible.
they gave me 1 meaty rib from the middle of a slab.. it was downright tasty and pull off the bone tender. It's really too bad they didn't throw the butt away - instead of putting it on a plate and expecting someone to attempt to eat it.
5) onion rings.  I'm going to guess and say that they use gluten flour to batter. The batter stuck to my teeth and was gummy..  I literally had to scrape it off.  
6) smoked green beans.  I once had a mother in law that thought that opening a can of green beans and cooking it in a sauce pan for 45 minutes constituted a vegetable.  These green beans were just as bad.  They need to change up the recipe and the cooking time.  They were awful.
7) They gave me two jalapeno's that were stuffed with sausage, some cheese, rolled in sliced brisket and toothpicked.  They were two large to shove in my mouth, and difficult to cut up...  Think they were a waste.

I had a dark ale called "The Special."  Quite good.  I highly recommend.

Would I come back here?  I think I would do take-away and just order the brisket.  
Maybe stick around for a beer.  The brisket is worth ordering.. 

They need some fixin..  They have a good anchor, they just need to fix some recipes.
Atmosphere is comfy.
Plenty of seating.
Good for groups.

* Call them up, order the brisket, have a beer, leave.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Great music bar on Broadway with no cover charge. I'm used to paying for anywhere with live music so this was a nice surprise. The music was great and the crowd got really into it which made it fun.

name: Whiskey Bent Saloon
text:
This little bar on Broadway is one of the best for live bands.
They must be very picky about who they hire because I have not seen a bad band here, in fact some of the best pickers in town will be on stage any day of the week.
The bar is comfortable and the bartenders quick to serve and very polite.
A highly recommended stop on a trip down Broadway.

name: Sheraton Music City Hotel
text: A little far from downtown, but a very nice hotel to stay at. Ample parking, friendly front desk and our room came with a cute little patio. We booked through hotels.com and got a fantastic deal! We will definitely stay here again if we get the chance.

name: Bootleggers Inn
text: MOONSHINE, MOONSHINE, MOONSHINE. That is literally all you need to know.  The bartenders are awesome and very friendly.  Casual, laid back bar.  One of my favorites on Broadway.  Is pretty small so can get fairly packed on the weekends.  And the bands they have playing there are top quality, and play lots of older country.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: The Stage is great! The locals that play here are fantastic! I hit a lot of bars while in Nashville and by far this was the best place for me. Outdoor patio with great views, ground floor bar, acoustic bar, and top floor bar. Staff was very quick and friendly. Definitely a place to stop into when in town and check out.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Extremely slow service and overpriced food. Never asked if we wanted refills and saw server only twice entire meal.

name: Hard Rock Cafe
text: Ok experience , staff somewhat indifferent but will try again.  Food was good, took a minute but satisfied upon arrival.  Parking a bit of a chore, but it's downtown and expected.  Street performers a bit distracting but once inside felt more comfortable .  Looking forward to some brunch another day.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: First I loved this bar first time I'm in Nashville.  Was enjoying myself listening to the Chris Weaver band until this woman in a hockey shirt and braided pigtails with a baseball cap decided that she wanted to pick a fight with my girlfriend and I.  All we were doing was dancing and she accidentally elbowed my friend several times.  It happens the place was crowded.  We are patient people.  But of course she was highly intoxicated. All we did was ask her if she could try to stay in her own personal space with a smile.  She came after my friend, she moved so she decided to come after me.  Luckily there was a 6'6" man with his wife watching the whole thing.  He intervened and talked to her husband and then she stopped.  Well I thought until she threw a beer bottle at my legs.  We left and told the bouncer on our way out.  He was very nice and listened.   I would of gladly given the bar 5 stars but your local drunks ruined it for us.  Very disturbing.

name: The Stage on Broadway
text: Ordered a mixed drink here that had pineapple juice in it. I watched the bartender make it & she used the entire can of pineapple and a little more from another can. All it tasted like was juice. I had to ask for another shot on the side to go with my juice. Lol. I bartended also so I know the pours and this was definitely under the standard. It also took a few minutes to get service because she was on her phone before realizing we were there.

name: The 5 Spot
text: Great place for live music and a drink! The cover charge has taken me by surprise a few times, but it's worth it.

name: FooBar
text: What? You live in Nashville and don't have allergies? You want to know how it feels to have rheumy eyes? Come here. I'll give Foobar this much - it lives up to its name! I'll also give it this - if you aren't from around there, you really have no business hanging out there. It's a strictly locals only place that is as inviting as an oyster with its trap shut. I saw people (it could be the light, but I only saw white folks) walk in, slap each other on the backs, hug, dance and have a great time. A supremely loud band was banging out on the nearby stage in the adjacent room to an audience of about 6 people. Suddenly a health inspector walked in with a cop in tow, and went about pointing his flashlight everywhere, looking for something. Then, a bouncer came in and yelled, "Who has a black Acura?" One dude raised his hands, and the bouncer said, "Someone rear ended into your car." After half an hour, I went out to take a call, and I found the place swarming with cops, a dude being arrested, and cop cars going up and down the road. That's when I figured that this place must be Magic Kingdom to a bunch of people for they see something in here that I don't, and I need GTFO.

name: Robert's Western World
text: By far the BEST bar in Nashville for awesome-old school- country.  Filled with memorabilia, simply but tasty menu. Service is busy.....with location being popular, but they were very friendly and attentive.  We stop in every night we are here just to listen to the music we love.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Hard to say what hasn't been said about the Ryman. It's literally one of the best places in the country to hear live music as it was built as a church before the days of amplified acoustics.

A few tips: the first two rows of the balcony are some of the best seats in the house. The first two front rows on the floor are folding chairs. When seeing a show the merchandise area is on the second floor; get there early if you want one of the limited edition hatch print show prints of your show as they sell out quick.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Super Fun!  Went to Roberts on a Thursday night, after being at the Wildhorse Saloon.  What a fun surprise!  The crowd was a blast, the music was great! Wish I'd spent my night here instead of the Wildhorse.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We started our Nashville weekend at Roberts. It was supposed to be one of many stops on our first day! Problem is we never left. Great music, great drinks, fantastic $4 Fried Bologna & Cheese Sandwich and the best bartenders ever (Rachel & Shyann)!!!!! You must stop here while in Nashville; stop for one or stay 5 hours like we did!!!!

name: Legends Corner
text: This is my favorite bar downtown. It's the vibe and the music. Lots of room to get around and they play great bands. Quick to get drinks as well. This bar feels like more of a 30's and up crowd where like tootsies is more 20s. Now don't get me wrong there all all ages everywhere and there is always a mix it does tend to fell this way.

name: Music City Center
text:
This is a gorgeous convention center that is well located in downtown Nashville.  It's right by all the Nashville attractions, and there are a bunch of upscale business hotels nearby so that conference goers can wrack up their points.

It is so big that there are pockets where cell phone reception is rather rotten.  I'm glad that there was sponsored free wifi for my conference.

Also, there's a huge capacity in the 4th floor ballroom, but there aren't a ton of escalators or elevators, so it becomes a cluster f getting out of there.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Great place for original country music!!
Listening to John Shepherd. They have great bar food, like fried bologna sandwiches!!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I was here for a large party,  limited menu,  company dinner. The filet was great as was the pork chop. The salad was a great mix of greens and a sweet dressing. 

The place is in a cool neighborhood and the locals say was all warehouses years ago. Service was good and the restroom was tidy. The band was fantastic. I was worried I would hear all country music and when the played Sinatra and other standards it made for a great atmosphere for dinner.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Birth of the Bluegrass, 1945! The history in this place is incredible. I was only in downtown Nashville for 12 hours and experiencing this venue was one of the funnest nights of my life. I've learned my lesson and will purchase tickets early next time because there is no general admission, which might be obvious for some events but not always the case when a rock band is playing.

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Them popsicles are poppin. Your friends are fake asf if they haven't dragged you here yet.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We tried to eat lunch here today, but were turned away because we had our water bottles in our bag.  We are here for CMA fest and it's over 90 degrees.  Even the music venues let you bring them in and encourage you to keep them filled.  So no burgers & beers for us.  We went to another place down the street.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: We went to the Gulch for a nice meal.  Sambuca had great entertainment, nice food, and great drinks.  We had an excellent time.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
If you are a music history buff, and especially if you love all things country, the Ryman Auditorium should be a definite stop on your list! This was where the Opry began and the home of bluegrass. We took a self-guided tour ($20/person) and spent as long as we wanted strolling through the auditorium and soaking up the energy of musicians who made the place what it is today. There's an eerie kind of energy that permeates the place - sort of spiritual. I especially liked seeing the displays of costumes on the lower floor in the back of the theatre. I opted to get my picture snapped on stage and for ten bucks, it's a great souvenir. For a few dollars more you can get a guided tour which takes you backstage to dressing rooms and the like. We thought the time we spent was plenty.
I almost - almost - opted for my own private studio recording time. For an extra $20 you can sing one of several songs and get it recorded in their studio. I just didn't see any songs that I thought I could adequately sing! (That's my story and I'm sticking to it).
They are back to live performances here - if you get the chance to see a show, DO IT! I'm told the acoustics in this theatre are some of the best in the world. And who knows, you might just sit next to Dolly for a show or see the ghost of Conrad Twitty...

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Really frustrated by this visit, planned months in advance for my birthday. The food quality was decent though the filets our party ordered were average at best and served cold. The salad was excellent. Also, I ordered a side is asparagus not knowing the filet was served over asparagus. The server should have mentioned this. Also, I couldn't get my drink refilled until my meal was almost done.

But the biggest issue was the 70s rock band who, in the middle of a Springsteen song, stopped and the lead singer said bourbon was more important than Springsteen as the band did double shots. Then they laughed they forgot the lyrics and took a break. If you were planning a break  you couldn't wait until the song was over to snort up the booze? This is really unprofessional when you have a room full of dinner guests subjected to juvenile behavior by grown men. Felt like they cared more about their drinking then the paying customers.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I cannot even fathom how this place has anything less than 5 stars. 

The first time I came here was about 4 years ago on a family vacation to Nashville. All of us absolutely LOVED it. The atmosphere, live music and food were all amazing. I don't typically remember meals but I remember those scallops perfectly because they are truly the best I've ever had. 

Fast forward 4 years and I'm back visiting Nashville with my boyfriend. I hyped up Sambuca and said it was one place we HAD to go to while in town. After checking Yelp and seeing 3.5 stars I was nervous it had gone down hill. We got to sambuca at about 8pm on a Wednesday night. We were told the dining room was reserved all night but could grab a seat in the bar area. We had great seats with a perfect view of the amazing funky blues/jazz/soul band that was playing. Our bartender, Clayton, was incredible. Such a nice guy and gave us outstanding service. 

I didn't even have to look at the menu because I had been dreaming of having these scallops again for the past 4 years. They did not disappoint!! I was sooo happy that they were as amazing as I remember. Seriously worth a stop if you're in the area!!! You will not be disappointed.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Review as a music venue: I just went to my very first concert at the Ryman this week, and it was everything I thought it would be. It's an amazing experience to hear an artist perform in this 100+ year old church turned music venue that has heard and seen the greats of music and film and theater and politics and everything else on the stage. Great acoustics. Great seating - hard to find a bad seat in the house (I think the worst seats may actually be the very first rows on the orchestra floor, because you might have your view blocked by people ahead of you and you have to look up at an angle to see the stage)! We sat on the balcony, and our seats were great. We had a great view of the act we were there to see (Elle King). The pew/seats were more comfortable than I thought, but (no biggie) you do have to get up and out of the seats to let people through, because the pews are a bit too close together to allow someone to walk in front of you. They sell beer and wine and cocktails (and let you take them into the venue), but they're pricey. My advice: get a drink at Cafe Lula (just outside the Ryman - just before the metal detectors at the back entrance where you go in for concerts)! Their beer and other drinks are cheaper (my beer was $5, rather than the $8+ inside at the Ryman), and they let you take them into the Ryman. All in all, seeing a show at the Ryman is such a cool experience! I know I'll be back!

Review of the tour: When my friend from Austin came to visit me in Nashville, I was looking for activities we could do around the city. Touring the Ryman was at the top of my list! We went on a Saturday afternoon for the self-guided tour. It was so worth it! I didn't know anything about the history of the Ryman, and the self-guided tour starts with an entertaining and informative video. I had NO idea that the Ryman was almost torn down and was vacant for years after the Grand Ole Opry moved from the building! After the video, you can walk around the Ryman, sit in the pews, take photos of the amazing architecture, including the gorgeous stained glass. In the stairwell of the auditorium, there are several panels that detail the history of speakers and performers at the Ryman over the years! Once you get down to the first floor of the auditorium, they have dresses, guitars, hats, etc. worn by famous performers at the Ryman. The self-guided tour is $20 - but it's worth it! It's one of the most fun things I've done in Nashville! I learned a lot about the city, the Ryman, and country music! (There's also a guided backstage tour that is $30.) Tons of fun! Highly recommended!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Awesome time portal to the Golden Age of music. What a treat. Filled with memorabilia.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Amazingly enough this great little dive bar with a good band had the best fried green tomatoes I've ever had... I cannot come back to Nashville to come to this place!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: The Arcs are going to rock the church tonight. Always venerable venue keeps us coming back. Love love love the Ryman.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Without a doubt, the best, most genuine honky tonk in town. Always cheap, always amazing music. ALWAYS take your family or friends visiting in town here.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great vibe and wonderful service! A very chill place for great live music. Attracts an older (wilder) crowd, which adds to the charm and appeal of this place. Hope, our bartender was very attentive and made our night with a steady flow of good drinks.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Came with a group for a late night dinner, ambiance outside was nice, I had the crab and shrimp scampi (minus the shrimp) and it was pretty good. I went to order a 2nd drink and was told the bar was closed, yet I noticed another server coming out with a round for the table next to us, not to mention some folks at our table joined us after, with drinks they bought at the bar. They closed early for a Friday night. Felt like our server was just done, and wanted out.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: SO fun! this bar was the first bar we went to while in Nashville. The live music was awesome and the drinks didn't cost an arm and a leg. The giant Jenga they have in the back was really fun along with the photo booth. We had such a good time here. And their QUESO was AMAZING.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
My brother and I decided to go here for some food and drinks before a show at the Ryman a couple weeks ago. Read the reviews on here and decided it looked like a pretty decent place.

The atmosphere is AWESOME. Everyone else has described it, so I don't think I can really add on to it that much. I'm not really a country music fan, but the bands that they have there really know how to play, and there's no cover charge, which is always a plus. I also loved the decor, it was great. There were a ton of cowboy boots and dollar bills on the walls and it just seemed like a really fun place.

They have a great amount of beers available (even though I only got a Blue Moon) and everything was decently priced so that was great. My brother and I did get some food as well. I had the Mushroom Swiss burger with onion rings, and my brother had the Cheeseburger with fries. The food was decent, but it's something that they obviously don't really focus on so I didn't expect it to be of really high quality.

The bartenders and everyone there was super friendly and always had a smile on their face. Overall, this is definitely a must visit for anyone that's not from here or new to town. Even lifelong residents would enjoy this place!

name: Robert's Western World
text:
If you come to Nashville and get down to Music Row don't you have to stop in here? I think so because it is such an institution. Always good live music playing its a real honkytonk. They are famous for their $4 fried bologna sandwich. I had one this week and will tell you it was very good and well worth it (4). With lettuce and tomato and a lot of bologna it brought back my childhood days when we would make these all the time. You also get a bag of chips so you can make a meal on it or just a good snack. 

With all the pictures and posters on the wall there is a lot of history here. Come in and enjoy.

name: Robert's Western World
text: OBSESSED. Was one of my favorite bars in Nash. Suuuper cheap drinks and great live music!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Took my boyfriend here for his birthday. They sat us two tables from the stage.  The jazz band playing was great. Definitely set the mood, and they were also taking requests. We ordered the shrimp and crab dip for starter and it wasn't anything special but was good. Our entrees were really awesome though. The waiter recommended the Blackened Red Snapper and is was incredible, the flavors were spot on! My boyfriend ordered the Shrimp and Crab Scampi, another winner. But by far the dessert was the best: Cheesecake Sopapilla. I would go back just based on the desert alone. Are waiter was awesome, very friendly and definitely directed us to the better choices on the menu. Definitely plan on returning!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
There are a lot of things going for Sambuca: free valet, really hot music, and arresting visual displays. The food, however, leaves me perplexed.

Food is my primary measure for evaluating a restaurant, but I have to take a moment to comment on the ambiance of this place. With its generous use of draped red and purple cloth and weird light fixtures. The interior design is sort of how I would imagine what an upscale Turkish brothel would look like. I can't say that that's either a good or a bad thing, but it's certainly interesting. I have to say, though: I am all for mood lighting, but this place is exceptionally dim. At one point, I watched a waiter forced to identify a soup by using a flashlight. If the lighting is bad enough to interfere with your employees' ability to do their jobs, I think it's time to go back to the drawing board.

As for the food, I was pretty optimistic after the first course: the bisque was well-balanced and quite tasty. Furthermore, their side-dish, prosciutto mac&cheese, was remarkably light. I thought I was headed for a thoroughly 4-star meal, but alas, it was not to be. I admit that I broke one of my own commandments of restaurant eating, which is "Don't order a chicken breast or a pork chop unless someone has specifically recommended it." As punishment for my sins, I spent my evening chewing through an overcooked, though relatively well-seasoned, pork chop. Remarkably, they managed to pull off the opposite feat with their vegetables. Now, I prefer many vegetables, like broccoli and carrots, to be on the "al dente" side. However, bell peppers and onions do NOT fall into this category: it was remarkably bitter. I will say, though, that because they were undercooked it made for good eating the next day after I nuked them in the microwave. I didn't try too much of my tablemates' food, but at least two folks commented that the lobster enchiladas were not particularly lobster-y and that the portions were a bit stingy.

This meal showed some moments of promise, but I was expecting a bit more. Perhaps one should only order items with cream in it.

name: Robert's Western World
text: I got a greasy burger like I like it with some greasy fries.  Listened to awesome music and had great service.  Best part was I didn't hear one song by Luke Bryan or any of his cohorts.

name: Musicians Corner
text:
What a great festival! 

We had gorgeous weather, really good music (mostly blues when I was there recently) which my friend who attends regularly said was bit out of the norm. There were food trucks and vendors. And activities for the kids and the pets.

Coming from NOLA, I thought it was nice that there was a beer garden but odd that you had to be fenced off from the populace in general. The beer must not escape the picket fence!

Loved that there were some mature trees to offer shade and that there was plenty of space. Did not love dog owners who cannot control their pets.

name: Legends Corner
text: This was the first place we checked out on Broadway street while visiting Nashville, really liked their Southern Sangria. The energy is great, people always dancing around the stage. They have different bands so it's not always country. We came back a few more times for their drinks.

name: Robert's Western World
text: my favorite honky tonk on lower Broad! the best! best music! a must for anyone doing the tourist thing that wants to hear great music.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Great experience at this place! They accommodated a party of 15 for a bachelorette party with a special prix fix menu because of the size, and the food was delicious! One of our party got dripped on from an AC unit and they re-sat us in a private room and comped some of our meal. It was handled immediately and professionally. Our server Jesse was great, he humored us and made sure the bride had a great time. We were all very happy!

name: Legends Corner
text: Love the blues??? You must go.  And for a blues joint the food was decent.  I'll be back.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Great bar, gets super crowded though. the band was awesome, the drinks were great. I will definitely be going back here. Definitely not a place to go if you are looking to have your personal space.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Amazed at the history here.   Did the tour and back stage pass.  So glad we did.  Highly recommend.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This was my favorite and last stop on Broadway. I would have loved to stay longer if my friends weren't ready to go home for the night. The band played a medley of 80's-00's hip hop for most of the time I was there. It was very nostalgic for me. Reminded me of middle school and high school dances. There was a much younger crowd here. Didn't hear any country music. It was a Saturday night. Didn't catch the name of the band. Only crowded on the dance floor. Plenty of places to sit in the back.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: It was average. Was in Nashville for the weekend, we have a Tin Roof back home but we still decided to check it out (we actually mistook it for another bar.) But nonetheless, we sat upstairs because it was nice out, they had opened windows & half of the roof was open. Not sure it was open on purpose, the half that was covered, was covered with ply-wood. It began to rain which scattered the half that wasn't covered. Stayed for a few beers & mules & left.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Loved seeing the place where the Grand Ole Opry started!! Emerging artist and those tried and true! Don't miss this when checking out Nashville, from music, comedy, square dancers, young and old!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Definitely a crowd for the older folks or those who like the oldies. Not a typical Nashville bar. Cheap alcohol tho but not much room.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We ended up going here several times during our trip to Nashville. Every time a great band was playing. Even at 6 or 7 pm we stood around and waited by the bar for a seat but the music was worth it. I wouldn't eat dinner here but the fried pickles were delicious-we got them all 3 times we visited. It's a dive bar but every tourist should be going here at least once.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Unfortunately we were unsure when we'd be arriving, so OCMS shows on and before NYE were sold out, so we just went for a daytime tour by redeeming 1/4 of our Access Pass. Beautiful space, but they really need to include a demo of the acoustics as part of it. Will certainly attend a show if back in Nashville.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Always a good time, fantastic live music...drinks are a little pricey, but I would choose going here over quite a few other along the strip, because the layout feels less cramped.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This is not just any historic venue,  this is hollowed ground for country music!  It's THE church!  The pews,  the floors, the ceiling is all original which provides amazing acoustics.  Now I know why bands still play here and find it an honor in doing so.  The video introduction is amazing and educational for the self- guided tour.  When you come to Nashville, you must see this place along with the Grand Ole Opry.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We were told by multiple Tennesseans that Robert's was the best bar on Broadway so we had to check it out for some day drinking. We scored a table right up near the stage and were lucky enough to catch Eileen Rose and her band playing some great country hits. We had the best time, sipping our beers, munching our fried bologna sandwiches (order immediately as they take an hour to arrive at your table!), and singing along to the wonderful music. Great energy and atmosphere at Robert's.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Most of the time, when we visit a new city with a classic music venue, they end up having bands we have no interest in... not this time. Rufus and Martha Wainwright rolled into town for their Christmas show, and we enjoyed every minute of it.

The venue itself definitely has character and some obvious flaws (that are probably unavoidable for such an old spot). Roughly 75% of the seating in the lower section is under the balcony and doesn't get a "great" view of the stage, but they aren't really obstructed either. The acoustics are amazing, so much so, that Rufus sang without a microphone for a rendition of "O Holy Night" which was worth the price of admission alone.

The only downsides are the concessions, in terms of what items are available, and the location of the restrooms as the doors were open most of the night for smokers and it was frigid outside.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We went to a Grand ole Opry performance here and it was an unforgettable experience!  We had balcony seats and still felt so close to the stage. The seats resemble church pews so not the most comfortable but the sound of music in the auditorium more than makes up for it! Had such a wonderful time and would recommend it to anyone visiting Nashville and likes country music!

name: Second Fiddle
text: Fun place, great music and drinks. Funky, and historic decor. Came here from Reno, Nevada with my honey and we had a great time! Our first stop in Nashville was a 10!

name: Nashville Municipal Auditorium
text: Horrible horrible venue. Came for a show November 21st to see the 1975. Still outside at 8:12 with a line about half a mile long. They couldn't open the door sooner! The opening act is all ready on stage and performing. This place stinks.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
This was the last dinner I had during my trip to Nashville. We had a reservation and were sat on the balcony above the stage. A jazz band played some light music starting at 6:30pm. It was a really awesome set up and had such a trendy cool vibe. I had a couple of Dirty Martinis (best ones I had in Nashville) and we tried a few of their apps to start. the Mac and Cheese with prosciutto, the buschetta and 2 orders of the Buca Beignets. All fantastic. We order the right about for the 7 of us to share. 

I had the special which was sea bass wrapped in bacon with risotto. Different but delicious. A very unique dining experience. We had a great time!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
this would probably be cool if you were into old timey country music. we paid for the backstage tour. you should do that if you want to see shitty dressing rooms built in the 90s and hear kind-of stories from a tour guide who "doesn't know for sure, but probably." taylor swift MIGHT have been in this dressing room.

the old costumes are pretty legit, and this place would be cool for a concert.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Really enjoyed this place. Menu is small and simple. I went out on a limb and tried the fried bologna sandwich and was pleasantly surprised! From the locals I spoke to there, one being a musician himself, this is a great place to hear some of the best local music, which I was able to do while there. Definitely worth a stop in.

name: Second Fiddle
text: This place is one of my favs on Broadway if you're looking to just hang out, have some drinks, and listen to some good music.  The past two times I came to Nashville this was the bar we hung out at before we went out to get wild.  The staff is super friendly as well.

name: Legends Corner
text: Great spot, tons of history, random memorabilia throughout (check out the hallway on the way to the restrooms), reasonably priced drinks & approachable bartenders.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Okay, these five stars come with a bit of a caveat. It is not 5-star food. It's not really 5-star service either, though the staff is impossibly sweet if you treat them the same. These five stars are because when you go to Nashville you have to experience something truly honky tonk -- like really, really honky tonk. 

If you're lucky enough to be in town on a Monday, definitely go check out John England & The Western Swingers, a staple at RWW. They're super genuine, mega-talented, and worth the effort.

While you're there, order a fried bologna sandwich (and while they're making it for you, try your best to dispel what you think this amazing treat might be -- it'll be worth it!) ... We also had the chicken strips which were pretty much of the generic drop-and-fry variety, but good nonetheless.

Again, nothing about this place is 5-star, but if any place should get 5 stars on Yelp, it's this one.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: the food was really good, the service - justine - was really, really good and the entertainment was over the top.  a great break from the cma's.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Beyond expectations! If you are in Nashville, this is a must! This place has the best of everything! I can't tell you how amazing the food is here. Martin makes sure that you are taken care of and that you leave happy!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
This place is like Candy to a fat kid, Crack to a druggie or rubbing alcohol to Kitty Dukakis. 

Amazing time watching Greg Allman. I had side seats and thought it would be troubling to see but it wasn't. 

The acoustics, the lights, the shear fact of being in the Ryman made this one of the best places I've seen a concert. 

Staff was great (will call and greeters), place to get a drink was very convenient and the people was a great mix of young and old. This was, and IS, the place for me to get a music groove on.

name: Robert's Western World
text: We visited from California this week. Such a fun bar. Great bands both times we stopped in and loved the fried bologna sandwiches and onion rings!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great fried bologna sandwich! Good drinks and fun music. This isn't one of the super popular places so it's a little easier to get into. Loved it!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Recession Special = PBR, fried bologna, a bag of Lays, live honky tonk in the morning and smiles!

name: Robert's Western World
text: What a fun place to eat some junk food, drink beer and listen to an old style country band with a fiddler!!  I had the fried bologna sandwich with onion rings and loved it!  The drawback, it needs a good deep cleaning!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great music. Food was than acceptable but the service was absolute horrendous. Unless you went up to a bar you were blatantly ignored.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
Came here a few nights ago with a large party.

Let me start with the good - essentially, the only reason why I didn't give this place 1 star. Those at my table who ordered a drink said that the drinks were good, and the atmosphere at the place is pretty cool as well. 

First of all, we sat down around 7 and it took over an hour for our salads to even come. We were starving by this point, they refused to even bring us some bread or chips. The server was VERY rude, giving everyone an attitude when they asked for something simple, like a refill.

By the time our salads came, I didn't even care that there was barely any dressing on it... I ate it anyway. We waited another hour almost for our meals to come.

I ordered the chicken and beef skewers, which were disgusting. They were extremely cold and absolutely tiny. The "vegetables" were sad mushy squash and zucchini. Some of my coworkers ordered the steak, which was good. I should have ordered it!

Dessert came - I skipped it, but my coworkers said that it was fine.

Definitely would never come to this place again by choice, which is unfortunate, because the vibe is cool and it seems like they might have better food if you're in a smaller party. But if you have a big group - don't come here unless you want to spend 2 1/2 hours for dinner.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Came here for a work dinner with approx 100 colleagues. We had rented out the sky loft and had a fixed menu. The service was great, however, the food was cold when we received it. I understand that there were quite a few of us, however. I ordered a steak medium rare but it came out well done. Will give this place another shot when I come back to Nashville (without 100 other colleagues:))

name: Robert's Western World
text: Why is that bologna sandwich so good? It just is! And it's even better to have it with a brew while enjoying some great music! Of all the spots on Broadway, this was easily among my favorites.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: We loved our self-guided tour of the Ryman! The video knocked our socks off, we were definitely not expecting it to be as amazing and interesting as it was! This venue has so much history and it really is a fascinating spot to wander through. All of the staff people we encountered were very friendly and helpful as well! Especially the gentleman who took the time to explain all of the photos outside the theater room! Loved it!

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Wow! Loved the atmosphere. Came here late night on a Sunday night - had really good small plates & the live jazz was so awesome! Definitely returning

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I really liked the timeline in the Ryman telling about the history of the building, it's occupants, and the Opry. It helped piece things together. This and a few other exhibits are part of the self guided tour. 

The guided tour add on is way to go - it is only $4 more. You can do the self guided museum before and/or after the guided tour that allows you to see backstage. Granted the views are not amazing - and you can't take  pictures behind stage - but the guide is full of knowledge. Each dressing room you visit is themed and full of pictures and the guide goes through all the pictures with you telling you the story of the singers pictured.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The venue is classic. it's a wonderful building and the acoustics are great.

The only thing that I am not a fan of is some of the acts they book. Rock concerts are not meant for this venue. There are pillars obstructing the view and I felt awful listening to some of the lyrics of these rock bands coming out of their mouths as I stood in a church pew. If you are to buy tickets, your experience would be well worth your money if you bought closer to the stage, for sure.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Went here for a girlfriend's bachelorette party. They were super nice even though the bride got stuck in traffic and was a half hour late. Our food was all really good. My favorite part was the upstairs bartender, Eric! He made the whole night better. We had a few drinks and an app. upstairs with him while waiting on the bride and the rest of the party. He was a lot of fun, very helpful with the menu, and made the night great!  Thanks Eric!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great place for an inexpensive meal.  Limited menu but really good food and entertainment.  Yucca fries were the big winner in our group.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: I would have rather stopped in for a drink to listen to the band and gone elsewhere for our meal. The bartender paid no attention even when drinks were empty and never checked in once the food arrived. There were only two others at the upstairs bar so the beer got restocked instead. The food was just ok. If I would do it again I would stick to an appetizer at best and move on for better food.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
Petty cool experience on a Friday night.  We ordered the Fried Bologna sandwich and Mozzarella sticks.. mehh nothing to brag about there.
If you take the cool atmosphere and live music into consideration, overall, we had a fun time.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Exactly what I was looking for. Great aspiring band, friendly and observant bartender, and delicious low-priced food. Basic sandwiches, appetizers, and domestic/import bottles, this place is an easy stop along Broadway. A beer and burger will run you just over $10.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
First time here and very impressed. The food was amazing, the atmosphere awesome, live music very entertaining, and Jordan our waiter was attentive. World class customer service and quality restaurant. Would definitely come back and recommend to anyone in town!!! 

Appetizer- shrimp and crab dip! (Great taste and portion) 
Meal- pork chop (flavorful and well made) 
           Flat iron steak (quality meat with taste) 

Today is a Friday night and the band is keeping everyone engaged!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
The Mother Church of Country Music! We really enjoyed this being unfamiliar with the history of the Ryman. The video with holograms that you start out with was the perfect length of time and detail in my opinion. The building is beautiful. We did the self guided tour and enjoyed being able to listen/read as much as we wanted. 

They do have a AAA discount I think it's 2$ off per person. 

We went soon after opening which it wasn't crowded yet which I'm sure led to such a positive experience for us. 

We chose to go here over the country music hall of fame museum and glad we did!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Hands down best honky tonk on Broadway. Superb musicians, cold beer, and hot grilled bologna sandwiches.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Nice bar. Was in Nashville over the fourth and went here a couple times. Fun band, friendly staff, yummy food. Pretty spacious and good upstairs 'outdoor' area that's unique.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Music was good. Food was fair. I had a chicken Cobb salad. The chicken was bland. It needed more seasoning. The other couple shared the teriyaki chicken wings. They said they were tasty but smothered in sauce. The fish and chips were also only fair. The chips came out ice cold and undercooked. They did make new fries which were hot but a little on the hard side. Cole slaw was inedible.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: The worst food ever. I had to actually spit out the coke slaw it was rancid! I have never spit out food before! I ordered the Mac and cheese with bacon... came cold and trust me I LOVE Mac and cheese. I did not even eat it! Worst Mac and Cheese ever! Hubby got the voodoo hoagie and average at best! Don't spent your money on food here. The server did not even ask why we did not eat the food....... totally bummed! Skip it!!

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: This was one of the more fun spots on Broadway that I visited recently, mostly because I felt like the crowd here was better than at some of the other honky tonks. Like others, Tin Roof had great live music, strong drinks, and a cool atmosphere lighted by strings of Christmas lights across the ceiling. Didn't eat anything, but enjoyed the strong dranks!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Not a very kid friendly place. Didn't have access to silverware- to cut a hotdog for my baby. Also, no changing table in bathrooms.   Hamburger was less than good. The group playing music made the place earn my stars.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Delicious food but their reservation system is currently not pulling open table reservations so call to confirm. Thankfully we had out reservation confirmation so they helped us out and found a way to get us seated in a full house! Server had a little attitude but overall did a good job. Trendy and enjoyable ambiance, good was delicious and they have a little something for everyone!

name: Legends Corner
text: Great place to start your downtown experience, we went on a Saturday afternoon the band playing was great.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Always love coming here and seeing the history of this place even beyond the country music!! Recommend coming if your in town!!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Great Spot to stop into for some live music, drinks and food. Drinks are fairly priced and the food is cheap. I had a bologna sandwich "Delicious", my boyfriend had a burger with onion rings. Onion rings were so good, we had to order an additional basket. The Service was great and the atmosphere was friendly. Definitely a "GoodTime". I'm hoping to stop by before my visit ends.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: What can I say about this historic building that has not already been said? This place has the vibe of greatness. Everyone who's anyone has performed here over the last 100 or so years. It's updated at the entrance and in the lobby but the theater itself still has the old pews. We saw Jeff Foxworthy here and I want to come back to see a music act and hopefully the spirit of Minnie Pearl!

name: Robert's Western World
text: The music is outstanding. The bartenders are friendly, and the food is awesome. There are decent vegetarian options, and the fried cheese sticks rule. The atmosphere is fun and the crowd is always diverse, made up of  many generations from all over! This is not a bar to have a conversation at, it's perfect for listening to great musicians, people watching, and drinking!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Amazing place to visit if you're a country music fan. Standing in the auditorium where country music became what it is today is an amazing feeling. The Ryman is well kept and the exhibits were great to see. The introductory video was very cute. Everything was very clean.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text: Great for hanging out and getting drinks. The food wasn't very good. I'd go back for a night out but not for a meal.

name: Robert's Western World
text: This place was fun,  lots of great cheap food & drink choices.  We are here and had a fried bologna sandwich.  It was very good.  Sweet tea kept flowing and the live music was perfect.

name: Second Fiddle
text: Pretty much the standard crazy bar on Broadway. Band playing the night I was there was awesome which made the place. Get the wrong band in there and it wouldn't be anything special.

name: Center Stage
text: One stars feels generous for this place. They run a shady business and don't maintain their property. Not sure why anyone goes here, particularly in a city full of great bars.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Hands Down one of the coolest spots I have been to. This is the epitome of the Downtown Nashville experience. Cant wait to go back

name: Nashville Municipal Auditorium
text: Strange stadium set-up. I went there to watch a Queens of the Stone Age concert when I immediately realized this was not the preferred design for a rock concert. This place is much more suited for conventions, as a roller rink, or sporting arena. The acoustics are not great and the dome from the inside is off-putting and makes the entire place look run-down.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Beautiful, historic, legendary. Do the tour and see a show. Then head down to Robert's for a "stimulus package."

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
I have been to Sambuca several times and each time the food has been amazing! The service is almost always amazing as well, although we have had so-so service on occasion. 

The Chicken Samoas are amazing but I do wish they came in a larger size. Their cocktails are unique and fun, I love the Mojito! 

The vibe is what keeps me coming back again and again; it's the perfect place for a date night, a celebration, or to wow out-of-town guests!

name: Robert's Western World
text: Just got back from a Nashville trip, and this bar was the most fun we had while we were there.  My boyfriend & I are NOT country music fans ("Then why were you in Nashville?") but we popped into Robert's and listened to The Silver Threads play and they were INCREDIBLE.  Not only were they a solid band, but they really knew how to work the crowd.  It's not a 5-star establishment by any means, but I wouldn't call it a dive, either.  We ate the fried bologna sandwich, and that was quite tasty :)

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: Came here last weekend to celebrate my friend's upcoming nuptials. Everything was amazing! Our table was waiting for us when we arrived so we did not have to wait. The band, ambiance, drinks, and food were all up to par. Loved this place! I highly recommend the crap dip, it was soooo good! If ever, in the area check this place out!

name: Plaza Mariachi
text: Just go sit, eat, listen to live music, watch acrobatics. For kids, teens, and adults. FUN

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Ryman Auditorium is a beautiful theater right in the thick of things, right off of Broadway. It started as a church in 1885 and is still called "The Mother Church" by those from near & far.

After a renovation a couple of years ago, they now have a little cafe connected to the building, a big box office & gift shop plus a new area for the tours they do. I'd love to come back for a tour at some point. 

The night I went, all my dreams came true as I saw Andy Cohen, a man I love and adore, along with one of his besties Anderson Cooper. The show brought me to tears (literally. i have problems.) but the venue was pretty magnificent, as well.

Ryman wasn't quite as a big as I envisioned and that actually made it seem like a very intimate environment for a show. Google tells me it seats 2,362 which is surprising because it felt like there was just 500 people! haha I had to google Grand Ol Opry because that felt way bigger to me and that seats 4,400. 

I feel like most seats on the main floor are fairly good however there are a bunch of pillars and one such pillar was right in my view-line. That kind of sucked and I wish I would have known so I booked a different seat. 

Ryman itself is a gorgeous place though! Lovely venue and every worker I encountered was pretty friendly. I was also impressed with their local draft beer selections. They had a good variety and prices weren't too inflated for a music venue. Bravo!

I would definitely see future shows at the Ryman!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Amazing place to visit. It was more than the Grand Ole Opry to us. The history and back stage tour far surpass the GoO. If you get a chance take this tour while in Nashville.

name: Tin Roof Broadway
text:
do not go here...I
. repeat do not go here. The bartender on the roof top floor was very disrespectful and had vulgar language and an attitude when I asked for for service after waiting 15 minutes. when I approached management for the bad service they did not apologize but simple asked me to go to another part of the bar for service and pointed me to a server on another level. I felt as my business was not appreciated and not welcomed. I left after the verbal abuse and continued down Broadway and had a great time, if you have a choice please skip this bar and enjoy yourself among the other great establishments.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: I did a self-guided tour which was informative and fun. First you get to see a 10min film which was great. Then you walk around the theatre to see displays and videos filmed with famous people talking about history of Ryman. Price is a bit high given how small the place is but I enjoyed learning all the histories about Tom Ryman and Sam Jones, Lula(I admire her intelligence and toughness), and the renovation.

name: Legends Corner
text: Legends is a must see spot in Nashville! It's a tight space like many others with good drinks and live music. You can't miss it!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
I only came here for a tour and not a show, but I loved it. Tip, they have a AAA discount, so don't forget to use it. 

The very best part of the tour is the interactive movie and I loved every second of it. It kept my attention and left me wanting to learn even more about the Ryman. While I was visiting, they were setting up for their New Years Eve show and there was a lot of hustle and bustle on the stage. I enjoyed seeing how they pull everything together and thought that was an extra special perk. 

I loved touring such a legendary place and I vowed to return next time and to see a show. 

There are endless picture opportunities and people were taking thousands of selfies. No pictures were off limits, except during the movie. 

In total, I spent about 1.5 hours here, but I could have easily spent more time.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text:
This place is a joke. I don't understand how it has so many positive ratings. I booked a reservation on OpenTable based on the positive reviews here and there. The band that played was onstage maybe 20 minutes of my dining experience (I arrived at 7 pm, not a tall ask at that time), the service was atrocious, and the portions were laughably small. If your portion size is small, I better at least think it was the best few bites of food I've ever put in my mouth. 

They care more about presentation and aesthetic than the food itself. Save your money, please go somewhere else.

name: Sambuca Restaurant
text: If you are anywhere close to this place you are doing yourself a disservice by not coming in. The food. The ambience. The staff. The Music. I'm a Worldly traveler and believe u me this is a top notch place on my List.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text:
Absolutely a great place to tour, we took the self guided tour & could not have been happier. The staff are extremely helpful & it was a dream come true to stand on the stage. 

It is about a hour & a half to see the site including the initial video which is very informative. The costumes, photography's & atmosphere make it a must see when you are in Nashville.

name: Robert's Western World
text: Entertainment was a joke. This guy has been singing to his wife sitting in a booth since approx 1974. One waitress for the entire restaurant and entire bar. She was nice enough but completely frazzled. Cheapest PBR we found on Broadway tho. Reg cans for $2.50. Watched several bologna sandwiches and burgers being made on the grill. Did not look appetizing at all. Quickly finished our beer and left.

name: Robert's Western World
text:
When yelp hands you lemons, the Nashville yelp community made lemonade for us!

Coming to Robert's with a million other amazing yelpers was hands down, no questions asked the BEST part of my Nashville experience. I loved talking to every single person I met! 

The bar itself is awesome too. Beers were very reasonably priced, and the live music was unreal. I wish I could import some of their sound in to DC! The staff was super nice, and for the most part it was pretty clean. 

I was worried the Broadway area would be a tourist trap much like Fisherman's Wharf is in San Francisco, but I was happy to be completely wrong. Really cool music poured out of every bar and people were just enjoying life. 

If you're from out of town, don't miss this place - you'll really enjoy it!

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: This was a cool place! I'm not a huge country music fan, but I do enjoy it. I liked most that you get a good history lesson and it's very cool that this place honors the past. I would certainly recommend this to all who visit Nashville.

name: Ryman Auditorium
text: Show was great. Attendants were rude upon leaving. As we saw the exit door was headed directly outside we headed for a different door to use the restroom and were told no re-entering. We never left! The two women said to go to a nearby cafe. Disappointing as the tickets were pricey.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: I really enjoyed the Bavarian Bierhaus. Tried the flight of beers and the brats platter (Werstelier?) and the cheese and meat plate app. On top of great food they had a great act playing. I'd definitely go again soon. You've got to check this place out!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food was forgettable, and it's not exactly in the middle of town. They do have decent biscuits, if you're into that sorta thing, but don't expect much from the rest of the menu. My eggs were over cooked and it was probably the worst "steak" I've had in 10 years. Pretty much a tourist trap. Meh.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My friend brought me here when I was visiting  Nashville, and wow this place is a gem! It was pretty far out of the way (it felt like we were in the car for 20 minutes from midtown?), and the wait was long (she said that it's usually longer), but it was worth it. I could make a meal out of the biscuits and preserves alone!! This place had amazing customer service, and even though it seemed everything on the menu was basic, everything just tasted better here. Even my scrambled eggs were the best I've ever had! I liked this place because it felt like I was sitting in my grandma's kitchen...you know, if my grandma hung up hundreds of autographed celebrity photos on the walls! I recommend this place to everyone visiting Nashville, just because you have to say you've been to the Loveless Cafe at least once, right?

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Me and my friend go here about once every few months because we love the beautiful  ride over for the coffee and biscuits.. I always order catfish... Although I am from the MS delta where catfish is our middle name, I still enjoy their catfish... The turnip greens are great with pepper sauce and the crinkle fries never disappoint nor satisfy. The okra is out of a box... Server told me that one! 
I just don't get what the hoot is all about... I guess you say it's a Nashville thing but I've been to shacks on the side of the road with better home cooked food. I have a love/hate relationship with this place. I want to love it because of the beautiful location and home feel but it's just becoming to "franchisee" without being a chain.. People come from all over to see this place and celebrities as well... I don't get it... Like I said I come every few months for the scenery and hopes that the food gets better... Service is for the most part lovely

name: Loveless Cafe
text: THE BEST meal we had in Nashville.  The fried chicken was amazing, homemade biscuits and jams, chicken fried steak, the mac & cheese.  This will be the first stop on our return trip!  There are also cute little shops you can walk to while waiting for your table.  Crafts, foodie stuff, etc

name: City Winery Nashville
text: I came here during Nashville burger week. Their special was the porcini pork burger on a squid ink bun. It was good but my friend ordered the regular burger on the menu and it was even better than the special. Our server was Gemaal and he took care of us. He knew the menu inside and out. Most of all he was one of the most attentive servers I have had in Nashville. I will be back if only to have his humor at the table again

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I rarely give a place five stars but this cafe is amazing.  It is a bit of drive and worth it. Everything I order was great tasting. They start you with you a plate of biscuits, which they're famous for. The plate comes with three Jelly's, peach, strawberry and blackberry.  Their all made in house and you can buy them or ship them. With the meal you get more biscuits and grits, which I love. Theses are the best grits I have ever had. The gravy is good with sausage in it. I had bacon, sausage and ham with eggs and a hashbrown casserole (excellent). I cannot tell you how good this place is, once again everything is awesome.  You may have to wait in line but it is worth it. You will love this place, you must go. I highly recommend it and will be back.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
This is not fine dining German food and it's a kitchy Oktoberfest theme, but it's a fun night out. I came here with some family and we had a great time.

The beer selection is really good and they go great with the giant pretzels. Can't stress enough how good the pretzels are. Really hit the spot.

The waiter highly recommended the Jaegerschnizel which is a breaded pork cutlet with mushroom gravy on top of noodles. It was not bad, the pork was a little dry and it would have been much better if they put the mushroom gravy on the noodles as well as on top of the entire thing. But it was decent enough. 

Now the highlight was the entertainment, a lovely woman playing the according and keyboards and just making it a fun night. There are plenty of TVs in the space so if you want to keep up with the Nashville sports, this is a great place to watch the game.  Also has a huge bar so you don't even have to grab a table. 

So if you're looking for a great meal and that's the focus of dinner, skip the Bierhaus. If you're looking for a fun evening out with friends that revolves around beer and kitchy entertainment, this will do nicely. I had a lot of fun here.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Worth the long drive and wait for a table!! We had a large group and being our first time at Loveless we ordered a little bit of everything! The biscuits and gravy where to die for and the fried chicken was amazing!!! Also had the fried green tomatoes, grits and hash brown casserole and I would recommend them all!! Staff was fast and friendly!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This place is awesome! The food tastes authentic, and the live entertainment is amazing.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place was recommended to my hubby and I by our Airbnb host and let me tell you! Their biscuits were to die for and they serve them with three different types of preserves-peach being my fav (I actually bought some to bring home). Everything we tried was delicious and one of my favs was their fried green tomato biscuit with pimento cheese. I also got some pimento cheese to take home because it was SO GOOD. The service matched the excellent food and was provided with a smile every visit. We went three times while we were in town and were warmly welcomed and fed til we were stuffed each time. It's a must try when in Nashville! We will most definitely be back!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I asked for some yellow mustard with my biscuits and they brought it to me......umhumm.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Not a bad place.  The atmosphere is not quite as cool as the New Port, Kentucky location.  And it is a fat cry from the real one in Munich. The entertainment was not up to par.    But it is new and has potential.  

My waitress, Jennifer was very friendly and did a great job.

The food, I ordered the wurstellet sampler, was good but not great.  

I have dietary restrictions and was not happy to find a rule against substituting one side for another even though the sides  by themselves are all the same price.  

Will I be back?  Probably, but I will give them a while to become better established first.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Loved Loved..would go again.  We were lucky to sit outside. Staff was great 
food was good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Thank you Food Network / Travel Channel!!!!

The biscuits were to die for.  The server was so nice and he knew we were from California right from the beginning.  This might have helped because he kept giving us biscuits and the jelly (amazing).  When we got to the food we weren't even that hungry.  The food was average, but the real reason this is 5 stars is due to the biscuits and especially the jelly.

Please treat yourself and order something small or split a meal and just get the biscuits and jelly.  The biscuits were soft and good, but it was the jelly that was superb.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
I went to see Art Alexakis lead singer of Everclear and a special guest Leigh Nash from Six Pence. Great Venue. Based from New York this is the 4th location.
They will start making their own wine in a few months. They just been around since October 2014.
This was dinner and music and great atmosphere. I found this show through "bands in town" app on my phone and popped up. Glad I did and glad Art picked this place.

My server was great. Connor. Seemed all the servers that night were on it, when looking around. I actually came in with my wheelchair and they accommodated me. Staff was nice.
I was greeted and offered a beverage. That came out fast and he had knowledge of wine and suggested. Food came out fast and flat bread was plenty big!! Enough for 1 or three to share. But for a 2 hour show it lasted me the night. 

They do serve Sat and Sun brunch. Burgers look amazing and will have to try next time I'm in.
Their regular menu is different than their "Show menu" so keep that in mind.
You won't find a burger if you're craving during a show. Save that for lunch or dinner time on a non show night.

Pros: 
-great for friends, pop in and have a glass of wine, or something to eat. great atmosphere and cool hang out.
- Great artists too they have playing there from all around big or small.
-State of the art sound system, digital and Line Array speaker system. 
-You can see no matter where you sit.

Cons:
-parking limited. Valet is $5. Nice its cheap to park but if I'm already coming in to spend $10 on a glass of wine or more plus a meal walking out paying over 50 bucks. At least cover parking if you're limited!!? But again, 5 bucks isn't much.

-Food looks great but flat bread I got was bland. I had to spice it up. But don't get me wrong it was great, just needed little more flavor!

Over all great experience and will be back!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Except for giant dumpling everything was great.  Great selection of German beer on tap, and great sausage.  Going back for the Pork shank which was sold out.  Interesting place to eat.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We stopped here on our drive from Nashville to Memphis. I liked the experience here,  but didn't absolutely love the food. If I could just rate the biscuits, they would get 5 stars. 

Even on a Monday around 10am, this place was still pretty crowded. Our server was very nice, but the service was super slow. We got two plates of biscuits, one before our food came and one when our food came. We split the Southern omelette and country ham. The omelette was average and the ham was flavorful, but a little dry. The biscuits were perfection - not too big or buttery, and just a little flaky. Melt in your mouth deliciousness. 

They also have some shops on site, where they sell some of their preserves and mixes. 

Worth a visit for the experience for sure!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Decorated in the style of Hof Brau in Munich. Had the schnitzel which was very good. Spaetzl was soft and I remember it being more firm and fried in Munich. Had the Dunkel beer and liked it. Similar to beer in Germany, still has that American "bite".  Service and music was good. I would come back again!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: If it's out of the way, make the drive.   If there is a line,  wait!   So glad we took the trek from downtown.   We got the sampler with chicken,  meatloaf,  and bbq pork.   The sweet potatoes were what sweet potatoes were meant to taste like.   The mac n cheese was OK.  The hashbrown casserole was delicious.   The biscuits. ....we went to the shop and bought the mix and preserves to take home. ...so good.  We were happy we took the trip  out and wish this place was back at home.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This is is awesome! Long wait but lots of seating and plenty to see. There is a BBQ shack in the middle that hands out free samples that are to die for! Also lots of cute shops! Bring a bottle of champagne and ok to drink mimosas while you.
 Worth the trip!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Unreal breakfast! Amazing biscuits and jelly and jams. Great service a must stop if your in Nashville

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Music venue is great

Service was way off again! Party of six, 2 meals come out lukewarm, the other 4 plates start to trickle out 17 minutes later. They tried to deliver plates that we did not order three different times. Ordered espresso and the cookie plate, espresso comes out Luke warm and cookies come out 14 minutes later.
It seems like the kitchen really let the wait staff down again. We left 20% because we know how hard servers work but we will not be ordering anything to eat here again
The people that were crushed next to us also had the same horrible service. We were all laughing about it by desert.

Six different main courses ordered and the standout was the shaved kale salad....big miss on the food but it is hard to get a clear feel for the food when all the plates showed up lukewarm or cold

Super disappointing! 

Saw one review stating "best food in Nashville" my advise is go to City House, Sinema or Adele's and then recant your statement respectfully

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: We arrived to another country,  Germany. Waiters are all dressed appropriately :). My husband enjoyed the beers got one in all sizes .03, .05 & 1ltr. Nice outside area! Really enjoyed the band who spoke and sang in German. Will be back.  Enjoyed our food he got the sausage platter, & pretzel. I got potatoe pancakes and donor kabab!! Not sure of the bread but the meat and salad but was great and flavorful. Spent about 2hrs there..

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Had dinner at the Bavarian Bierhaus tonight, food was great, and Terry's German music played on an accordion and other cool instruments, was the perfect compliment to a really fun evening! Thank you Terry!! If I ever come to Tennesse again I will definitely stop here again

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
While in Nashville three weeks ago we dropped in for a late lunch. The food was fantastic. Our server was not attentive. We both remarked how we wish we had been seated in another section as the other tables were getting amazing service. 
Back to the food. I ordered the BLT (the T being fried green tomatoes). It was very good. The bacon was just right and the fried green tomatoes had a nice crunch to them. I had a side of mac -n- cheese which was good (not great but good). The biscuit was wonderful and the strawberry preserves were fantastic. So good that after we ate we walked over to the Loveless market and each picked up a jar to take back. 
My mom had breakfast, two fried eggs, sourdough toast, bacon, hash browns, and the city ham. The ham was great. 
I was surprised on my way to the bathroom to pass two open window kitchens, one that show cased biscuit making. That was very cool. 
I would definitely come back and I highly recommend going. I would have loved to give 5 star but I just couldn't with such poor service.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Virginia was an awesome server very good food and it is the first  stop on the Natchez Trace.. Very one stops and takes their picture at the sign...

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless Cafe is amazing. The biscuits are out of this world and the fried chicken and fried catfish are delicious. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Ask for Virginia - she is a great waitress.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loveless Cafe was awesome! Everyone I knew recommended I go on a recent trip.  The food was amazing and though there was a wait, as expected, it was only 30 minutes and gave us time to check out the little shops they have there which we enjoyed as well!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Our waitress was a doll and the biscuits was great. Some of the very best cheddar grits I have ever had. We come for the first time on a Sunday & it was a 2 hour wait so we left. We returned the following a Tuesday at 11 and only had to wait 10 minutes for a table. This place is worth the drive but not a wait of 2 hours on the weekend.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: The Hofbrau house in Cincinnati is much better.  I ordered the Jager Snitzle, honestly the ones I make at home are much better.  If you plan on having a conversation in the place forget it.
