There is a singer and the microphone picks up all the conversations.  Horrible echo throughout the place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
While visiting Nashville, Loveless was one of the top places on my list to visit. It was about a 20 minute drive from the city but it did not disappoint. We came on a Friday late afternoon and there was still an hour wait. Not to worry, there's a very scenic drive near by and you can kill time that way. Or just explore the grounds, there's two different gift shops with lots of goodies to buy. 

When we were finally seated, we noticed there was moonshine on the menu. How could you pass up on that? I had a Watermelon Crawl (watermelon, Lemonade, Sprite and a Moonshine Sidecar in a Souvenir Loveless Mini Mason Jar). The little souvenir mason jar was too cute! The moonshine did kick my butt!

For food we ordered the Loveless Fried Chicken (Quarter Chicken) with a side of macaroni and cheese, slow cooked green beans, fried green tomatoes, and hashbrown casserole. Before our meal came out they brought out their signature biscuits and they were buttery and light, just the way I like them. Everything else was really good. I loved the fried chicken, the batter wasn't too heavy or oily. The only side dish that I didn't care for were the fried green tomatoes. I've had better and they were so small.

We were so stuffed after our meal that we skipped out on dessert but now I'm regretting that decision! If I'm ever back in Nashville I'll have to make room for their desserts!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Have you ever had a food experience that you still remember to this day?  Loveless Cafe created that experience for me.  It's not fair to other comparable restaurants.  Oh wait a minute there no comparable restaurants.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The food is always amazing here! The staff is always nice and warming. The prices are great and the amount of food is very generous!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is epic. If you looking for a place with a home town feel you have found it. The biscuits are the best and the service is amazing.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Great atmosphere and decent service. One particular part of the menu is disappointing. They advertise vegetarian dumplings but use animal products to make them. This is seriously false advertisement, and can make people who can't have animal products sick, like myself. 

Not a great place for vegetarians.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I visited this amazing place on my first trip to Nashville because I read that this was a must-see. I was visiting from Florida to see the Vandy/UF game and felt so at home while dining here. The southern vibe was amazing and Loveless Cafe hands down has the best biscuits (mmh, homemade jelly!) and fried chicken that I've ever had. Whoever tells you to consider coming here on your next trip, please listen. Although the place is a few minutes out of town, the drive is very scenic and worth the time.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Points off for miserable sound system with scratchy noise; band was screaming.  Food was good.  Server very inexperienced.  He forgot our rye bread.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Biscuits were yummy!  Love the three different types of preserves that came along with them.  Also, enjoyed the rest of my breakfast: 2 pork chops, grits, scrabbled eggs with a mimosa. Had enough left over to eat later in the day.  Definitely glad we stopped here while we were in TN!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The hype is valid... (Although a bit out of the way, well worth the drive).
We only came for dessert and coffee since we had had dinner before heading over to Loveless.... (Big mistake).  Our party of four ordered the chess pie, fudge pie, banana pudding, and strawberry rhubarb cobbler... Everything was fresh and delicious. I only wish we would have tried some of the food.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Martha Stewart wasn't kidding when she said it's the best breakfast in America. I'm not sure why they call it the loveless cafe because all I felt here was love. I don't think I have ever had better breakfast food than what I ate here. The service was amazing and quick. We were in and out in about an hour. 

The biscuits came out first and I didn't think anything else could live up to those biscuits. Then the food came. I ordered the chicken and waffles and it was the most perfect meal I have ever had. The waffle was fluffy and light while the chicken was fried just beautifully. If you are in Nashville or even if you aren't I highly recommend making the trek out to Loveless Cafe.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Amazing place. We walked in expecting a long wait because the place looked super busy. The hostess said you two follow me.  We were sat and greeted immediately with a plate of biscuits. The best biscuits Ever. Everything we ordered was amazingly good. Highly recommend this place.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Always enjoy coming here when I visit my sister! The wait can be extremely long so don't come starving, because you will have to wait! But there are little shops and games you can play while waiting! Food was delicious! So anything on menu is amazing! I had grilled chicken sandwich with green beans... Delicious!! The biscuits they serve you before your meal is to die for! Love the jam that comes with it!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: On our last day in Nashville, we visited Loveless Cafe. My mom and I both had a great breakfast, but the biscuits were by far the best part. I loved the jellies and could have easily had an entire breakfast of just biscuits. Would love to go back the next time I visit Nashville!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
To die for!! Well worth the 30 minute wait. Adorable setting with cool 
Tennessee hill breezes in the middle of July.  Shopped the four shoppes while we waited. Games of corn home on the front lawn. 

Food consisted of amazing biscuits and jams. I had the grilled catfishes with mashed potatoes. Cream corn and hush puppies !!! Amazing !!

Kat...Great waitress!! Looked like a rockabilly angel with big blue eyes :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: These are the best biscuits I've ever had. When I think of southern eating this is the place to be. I would recommend this place, it's a great atmosphere.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
When you google places you must see/do in Nashville, The Loveless Cafe comes up as one of the top 5.  With it also being our last name, we were excited to see what it was all about.

We drove from St. Louis to Nashville for a weekend and came hungry as this was our first stop once in Tennessee.  We were greeted by an associate, very friendly, who was eager to take our pictures around the grounds esp with our last name being highlighted.  We put our name on the waiting list and looked around the shops, the Barn and other parts of the grounds.

Our waiter was extremely helpful and knowledgeable and excited that another Loveless namesake had stopped in.  We started with sweet tea and their homemade biscuits with the various jams and preserves.  I got the fried chicken with two sides and my husband got the sampler with 3 meats and sides.  Needless to say we were not disappointed.  They were advertising national dessert month and their homemade goodies so we had a piece of their turtle pie...not to miss!

We did get a little something to remember our time there and have already started thinking about our next visit whenever we're in Tennessee again.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I don't even know where to begin. I guess in the order it happened! Blueberry pickers: something we'll try to recreate at home. Biscuits and strawberry jam: perfection. The other two flavors were good, but the strawberry was phenomenal. Macaroni and cheese: best I've ever had in a restaurant. Cucumbers and onion: a little too sweet for my taste, but still good. BBQ pork: tender, flavorful. Good sauce. Meatloaf: delicious. I haven't tried my fried chicken yet, it's in my to-go box for later (with half of my meatloaf and most of my pork). There were three of us, and we all loved everything. 

This was out of our way, and we couldn't be happier that we made the side trip. It's fun like this that keeps me sticking to my motto on road trips: why not??

name: Loveless Cafe
text: A co-worker recommended this place. What a great treat! We had their peach rub BBQ chicken and pulled pork. We also had creamed corn, cheese grits, turnip greens and sweet potatoes. Every bit of food was amazing! Definitely stop by!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The atmosphere feels like someone's cozy grandma's house to me (not mine though, I didn't have cozy grandmas), which is nice. The food is good when you're craving some country cooking. I've had various things here, from the pancakes (love) to brisket (pretty good) to a cheeseburger (a bit disappointing, but okay) to salad with fried chicken (good salad, the fried chicken is really good), and more. The biscuits are great of course...love the creamed corn, which isn't one of my usual go-to choices. We tend to go during non-peak times/days, so we don't usually have to wait very long. We wouldn't go there if we had to wait more than 20-30 minutes, but that's because we live near by and can go any time. I think it's worth a bit of a longer wait for a fun little tourist experience, if you're on the fence about it. The service is pretty good, sometimes things have to be sent back to kitchen for being cold or something but the servers always handle things well. In summary, I recommend eating here...because it's good and quirky and like (someone else's) grandma's house...in a good way.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Great little quaint place for breakfast. Service was fast and efficient. Food was excellent and truly southern comfort food. There are also gift shops and areas to buy jam and they will even ship it to you. Overall highly recommend this Nashville staple!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
So I surprised my wife with a trip to Nashville to celebrate her inexplicable love of country music and visiting the Loveless was high on her to-do list.  

Thank god!

You may be able to get a breakfast this good in New York, but I couldn't tell you where and I'm sure you'd pay a small fortune for it.  Despite the ridiculous wait (1.5 hour) and vertigo inducing pitch of the floor (a bit uneven) the meal was phenomenal with a capital "PH."

The biscuits were unique, even by Nashville standards.  Small and light, they didn't require any condiments to satisfy, though that didn't stop me from drowning them in the best Sausage gravy I've ever had.  My wife had the Chicken and a Waffle and declared it the single best piece of chicken she'd ever eaten.  I had to dive into the "Pit-Cooked Pork Barbecue & Eggs, One to the Left and One to the Right" which came with a pancake and the greatest iteration of breakfast potatoes created: the Hash brown Casserole.  Besides being some of the best pulled pork, the remainder of the meal was equally exquisite.  The eggs just seemed fresher and the pancake fluffier than any I'd ever had elsewhere. 

Know going in on a weekend that you will wait and wait and wait to be seated.  This is partially due the tourist destination nature of the establishment and partially by design as there are multiple souvenir shops on the premises. You've been warned.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: In love with this place! We decided to eat here before attending a show at the Grand Ole Opry. We arrived at 5:30 and seated right away as this is a humongous restaurant! The waitress greeted us and took our drink order. She was attentive and polite the whole time. Out of our group, beer was ordered and enjoyed but I had a glass of Riesling which was also good. For appetizers, we had cheese fries, pretzel and beer cheese soup. We loved all of it! Everyone enjoyed their meals and agreed we would definitely be back. The polka band started playing around 6 and they were really fun to listen to! I would definitely recommend this place. Although we left our kids home on this trip, we plan on returning with them because we know they would also love the food, music and atmosphere:)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: The family style breakfast was awesome. The food came out hot. The coffee never stopped. The famous biscuits and homemade jelly were to die for. The waitstaff was great, friendly and attentive.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: This place was alright. Definitely a good spot for drinks and appetizers with friends, however, it's very overpriced. It's 10 dollars per person for a wine tasting, and on top of that, if you buy a bottle, they will only wave one fee (all the wineries I have been to.. which have been a lot... they will wave the group tasting fee.) Also, their wine was good.. but I've definitely had better. Especially when one of the cheapest is 25 dollars a bottle. Again, it's a really really cute looking place.. it definitely has a fun vibe, it's just way over priced. We didn't get any appetizers while we were here (because of the price) so I can't attest to how good the food was. I will probably try some next time, but you definitely need to be prepared to spend a pretty penny.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Food was decent at best. Beer selection was fairly good, for German beers that is. Certainly not as great as the German food I was accustomed to back home in the Midwest, but for Nashville it was pretty good. Certainly not a place I would go to all the time, as the prices were a bit high for what you get, but for a quick German fix i would prefer this place over Gerst Haus.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Having been to City Winery for several shows now, I thought that it was about time to give this place a review.  
Sitting snuggly, a block or so, behind the Convention Center on Lafayette, you can, as I have, drive right past this place but once you find it, it is a lovely space to spend an evening.  Parking is valet only, unless you are savvy at finding street parking nearby (which I am and no I won't give away my secret locations).  If you can't find street parking, no worries, the cost to valet park will not shock your wallet.  It's a lovely building with a wine grape vine growing around the front.  The inside is spacious and has an open, welcoming feel.  
I thoroughly enjoy the variety of performances that this venue books.  Initially, I thought that it was just going to be yet another "Nashville-esque" venue with the same talent popping in and out but I've been introduced to a number of acts that I would probably not have found otherwise.  Kudos to them for this!  The prices for the shows are extremely reasonable.  The more popular the talent, the more the ticket will cost, of course, but even the priciest ticket that I've purchased has been reasonable.  
I love the ambiance of the performance area, wide open with plenty of seating.  I will say choose wisely for the shows, I'm not a fan of passing waiters/waitresses during a show but this is not a deal breaker.  
I am absolutely a wine lover but for whatever reason, I'm never in the mood for wine when I come here.  I have perused the wine list and it's nice.  The mixed drinks are decent and are priced maybe a little less than some of the trendier spots in the city.  If beer is your thing, they do have a small selection.  The food is good.  It's not the best in the city but it's on par with other restaurants.  So far, I've had the risotto balls, the duck flatbread, and the caramelized pork belly.  None have disappointed.  
The staff has always been attentive and very professional.  It can be a challenge at times, to get another drink once the venue is full and the show has started but I will not hold that against them.  If a drink is needed as soon as your glass is empty, there is a bar in the back.  
FYI - If a show is ever cancelled, they go above and beyond taking care of you for the inconvenience.  I received a personal phone call when they realized that I hadn't checked my email to alert me to a cancelled show.  In the email, they offered me a full refund or City Winery credit and 2 complimentary tickets to another show.  I mean seriously, how many other venues would do this!  
I'm thinking that I need to start ordering the wine and finally become a vinofile.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Loved it! We showed up on Monday around 2 and were advised that a 40 minute wait was head of us. Really we only waited about 20 minutes and during that time there was plenty to check out on the property. I ordered the fried chicken and my fiancée got the pulled pork. Both were absolutely amazing. The biscuits and sides all were just great. I got a sweet tea and a shot of moonshine. Go big or go home right. Portions are large and our waitress was super nice. I have nothing but good things to say about loveless. My only regret is I won't get to try everything.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: This was legit authentic German cuisine!  And the atmosphere was great. Had a lady playing an accordion and singing Bavarian music. I got the 6 beer flight and was not disappointed. The food was tasty. The wait staff were awesome. Give this place a try. You won't regret it!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place was given a lot of hype. I was looking forward to tasting the fried chicken I have heard so much about. Don't get me wrong the chicken was cooked perfectly but it was lacking flavor. The green beans and mashed potatoes were awesome though. The sweet potatoes were bland and the mac and cheese was subpar. The peach and strawberry preserves were awesome but I was disappointed in the biscuits. For a place that advertises their biscuits like crazy they were just ok. The sweet tea was not sweet which is shocking from what I've experienced so far down here in the south. Prices were a little pricey but not over the top. It's pretty much what I have come to expect from Nashville food. Lots of hype but really just ok. I might go back to try some of the other dishes. I am a sucker for country cooking. I'm just hoping another dish will blow me away. Where is the mouth watering food Nashville?

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I have never had a more delicious breakfast in my life. Never. I would like to swim in a pool of their preserves, then take a nice nap in a bed of their biscuits. Well, after eating a bunch of them. Yeah, the wait was brutal, but we knew what to expect, brought a Sunday paper and did some poking around at the shops. The wait was worth it. Great service, too.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
It was good, but was a bit too hyped up... We came for a late lunch, but even though, there was a line and a LONG wait. 1 hour and 30 minutes to be exact. Luckily, they have a number of stores around the restaurant and corn hole to keep people entertained while waiting. There is a country store-type store that sells Loveless Cafe souvenirs and an store that sells locally made art. The stores are cute, but a bit on the pricey side, which is expected. 
FINALLY our buzzer went off! I was absolutely starving by this point! They brought out a large plate of biscuits and damn, those were really good! I really wish that I had thought to buy some biscuit mix. They were butter, fluffy and warm. They also brought out a dish of preserves. I liked the strawberry best, but that might be because I really like strawberries. I liked that the jam wasn't too sweet, which sometimes happen. 
I split the 3-meat sampler with a friend and got an extra side. Our 3 meats were the pork, fried chicken, and fried catfish. Our sides were the okra, fried green tomatoes, and the grits and cheese. The grits really were cheesy. In fact, it was more like melted cheese with some grits. It was good, but a bit rich for my taste. I think that I prefer the grits to be in a broth rather than just slathered with cheese.  The catfish was good as was the pulled pork. I was less of a fan of the fried chicken. The batter could have used a bit more seasoning (pepper?). I think that my favorite part of the meal were the biscuits.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I was raised in North Georgia in a poor family in the 1970's. Every night Mom would cook supper and Dad, my three brothers, and I would enjoy what ever Mom was able to put on the table. It was traditional food cooked by the southern poor for over a hundred years. When I was tall enough to see the top of the stove she started teaching me how to cook the same way. Over the years I have tried to change and cook healthier while using the basic knowledge I learned. 

When I first heard of Loveless Cafe I was a bit skeptical and thought it was another place that served food that people "thinks" is Southern food. I was quite surprised.

I ordered fried chicken meal and a fried pork chop as well just so I could try it. Mashed potatoes with gravy, and creamed corn. My wife ordered her goto favorite  fried catfish with mac and cheese and fried okra. The only thing that appeared not completely from scratch and hand prepared was the okra. It was pre-breaded but still tasty. If anything served was not prepared in their kitchen it would be an extreme surprise to me. 

This meal transported me back to that dining room table with 6 people surrounding it. Mom that was there to take care of us daily, Dad, the hard working man that worked sometimes three jobs to make sure we had what we needed. Not always what we wanted but always what we needed. My three brothers and me. We never really knew we were poor but we always knew we were loved in good times and in bad. No matter what we knew where home was.... and still is. 

As I sat there with my wife talking and laughing with our server that first night, a tear welled up in my eye as I realized I was as home with my family as I could be....

Yes, it's that good, it's home.....

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Our favorite place in Nashville! Barbara is such a sweetheart. She is always so friendly and the service is amazing. The southern fried catfish and the fried chicken is so delicious!! Oh and the warm buttered biscuits YUMM!! Always 1-2 hours wait during the morning weekends and nights but only 20-30 mins of wait btw 2-4ish during the weekends. Can't wait to go back again next month! 10% military discount too! :)

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Excellent service and the food was outstanding. Our party got the garden/vegetarian omelette and the southern omelette .   Both were solid choices

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Really busy at three in afternoon .  Nice staff.  Clean.  Great flavorful food.  Worth the wait.  Portions  are huge

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I always enjoy eating at the Bavarian Bierhaus.
The pork shank was not only delicious, but it was also huge.  The red cabbage was also great.  We sat at the bar and service there was fantastic!  Everything I have eaten here is good.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Food here was good. Atmosphere and service is great. Decent beer. I'd definitely return. I'll go out on a limb and say of all the restaurants at Opry Mills, this is one you should go to.

name: Analog at Hutton Hotel
text:
The space is beautiful but lacks adequate seating proportionate to the number of tickets sold for events there.  I attended Writers for Wishes.  Paying ticket-holding attendees were told to wait in line outside the venue until doors opened, but guests of the event artists ~people who weren't performing~ were bumped to the head of the line despite my girlfriend having stood at the very front of the line in 4" heels for 20 minutes in effort to get a decent seat & the artists' guests having shown up literally two minutes before doors were scheduled to open.  (Despite that, those attendees acted put off by the fact that they even had to wait until the doors opened to enter the venue.)  Once commoners were permitted entry, we found that literally every sofa or seat without an obstructed view was marked "reserved".  So Analog hosted a charity event for Make-A-Wish, during which aspiring artists performed, yet they alienated potential donors and fans with poor and preferential treatment.  In the words of Pretty Woman's Vivian Ward, "Big mistake.  Big.  Huge."

Again, seats aren't super easy to snag, but the venue doesn't have servers offering drinks or food.  The only way to order is to go to the bar, but in doing so you risk losing your seat if you've been lucky enough to get one.  We waited until about halfway through the show to go to the bar, which cost the bar at least a first round of drinks that my girlfriend and I would have ordered otherwise (if not more).  We asked to see a wine list and were met with a blank expression.  The bartender said "Um, I think all I have right now is a Pinot Noir, a Chardonnay, and a Rose."  A list with names, wineries, origins, tasting notes... would still have helped us decide if we wanted to order any of those.  The bottle of Pinot Noir sitting on the back area of the bar was half empty, having been opened who knows when, and had a screw cap.  Since no wine list was available, we asked to see a cocktail menu.  The bartender replied apologetically, "Um I don't think I have one of those right now either."  Um, okay...  Somewhere like Analog at The Hutton doesn't find it prudent to make wine and cocktail lists consistently available?  Smh.  We ordered the screw cap Pinot Noir and were promptly handed a tab for $12.43 per glass and asked to tip.  When we returned to our seats, a group of four other attendees had gathered round them and seemed to be debating how to divvy our two seats between them.  They feigned surprise when we said they were our seats despite both of us having left our 8.5"x11" printed-at-home tickets unfolded on the seats of both of our chairs and my girlfriend having added some loot from her purse (lip gloss, hand sanitizer, lotion) to each seat just to avoid any uncertainty about the seats being taken.  The vultures then asked if we'd mind if they moved the table several feet so their view while standing uncomfortably close to us would be less obstructed.  Of course the way they wanted to move the table would have made mine and my girlfriend's views *more* obstructed.

We wouldn't necessarily refuse to return to Analog under any circumstance, but it would take a really stellar act we couldn't pass up to get us back there, and our expectations for the overall experience would be pretty low.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Perhaps the cafe is overrated. Of course if you're going on the weekend be ready for a two-hour wait; it's quite smart of them to have a little village of shops to spend your time in while waiting. I bought their amaretto honey butter which is amazing (but so sweet only a dab will do ya). 
I ordered steak & eggs which were decent, but the side of hashbrown casserole was amazing (an LC specialty to be sure- don't go without trying it). I couldn't wait to try their oh-so-famous biscuits and ordered the biscuit sampler.  I found the pimento cheese/fried green tomato biscuit to be very good and the pulled bbq pork biscuit made me curious for their bbq dinners (the bacon and fried chicken biscuits are nothing to speak of). But the plain biscuits served with breakfast lack any flavor- Jim & Nicks' muffins cannot compare, even Red Lobster cheddar biscuits are much better lol. I certainly had enough leftovers for a second meal, but left the plain biscuits behind.
The service is friendly and all the famous Nashville celebs cover the walls as visitors but for me to wait two hours it's got to be outstanding.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
The new Nashville. This place puts it all together.

Intimate setting, plenty of room, purpose built music venue, great food, great wine list, full bar and prompt service. 

What more could you ask for?

Here first time for Leon Russell. Quite surprised about this place. Like sitting in a restaurant with restaurant menu and servers only 50 feet from the stage.

The food was really good. Pan seared mackerel was a favorite for our table. Perfectly cooked and expertly paired with purple Brussel sprouts, lentils and a cranberry purée. 

The wine selection was ample and we never even looked at the reserve list. The sprits list was also plentiful with plenty of bourbon selections among others.

Once the music started the acoustics worked well and the sight lines were excellent. Everyone remained comfortably seated throughout the performance.

This place is worth visiting regardless of who is performing and can only be improved by the level of talent on stage.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Wish we could give 4.5 stars - it was almost perfection. Came with friends and we had a great time. Loved the atmosphere, the beer, and the food. The food was fantastic! Would love to come back on a busy weekend night with all the music. The one small complaint we had was addressed promptly by one of the owners. Would definitely recommend and be back!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: German restaurants aren't easy to find, and it's even more difficult to find one that can accommodate gluten-free and dairy-free options.  So it was awesome to be able to eat here as they were accommodating and the food was delicious!  The hostess was also very helpful.  I ate there with people who had lived in Germany and they enjoyed it too.  Thank you!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
I really enjoyed my experience at the cafe! The food was fresh, brought out quickly, and I had a very kind server. I enjoyed a waffle (which I could only eat half of because it was so big). The waffle was a bit dense, versus light and fluffy like I like them. I also had their cheesy hasbrown casserole (I could have ordered this alone and been SO happy!)... SO delicious!! I also had the ham and bacon, but they were both way too salty for my taste. The homemade biscuits were to die for though! Coupled with the peach jam (which I normally don't eat). Very very tasty! 
One last thing, be sure to eat before you go. Our wait was around an hour and 40 minutes, but there's plenty of shopping around to keep you occupied.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Best breakfast ever! Hands down, no contest. The biscuits and homemade jam were amazing! I highly recommend the BBQ pork and eggs. Good ol' southern hospitality! Our server Trey was the best!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
As someone who has visited German beer halls in Germany I can say emphatically this place captures the feeling. From the hall design to the soccer goal in the urinals this place has it all. 

Kathleen, our server, was more than helpful. Even offering her last ibuprofen to my wife to alleviate her headache. I just wish her coworker, maybe a manager, with the gauged ear piercings had been so pleasant. When I asked if he could set the TV channel for us he held his finger up to me in silence without uttering a word as if I were disrupting him. Sorry to be a nuisance but you're in the service industry and I expect words not callous gestures. 

I can say I will be back, but I hope not to see this person again as they had no manners.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My wife and I stopped here because she looked up things to do in Nashville. It was a pretty cool place if you have time to kill a few hours. The biscuits you get before your meal were hot & fresh. You get peach, blackberry, and strawberry preserves to go on them. (We bought some biscuit mix & blackberry preserves in the gift shop while we waited to be seated.) For our meal we split the southern sampler (fried chicken, catfish, and meatloaf.) The chicken and catfish were great but the meatloaf was pretty average. Don't waste your meal on the meatloaf when there's plenty of other good things on the menu. The hashbrown casserole and mac&cheese were both really good for sides. This place reminded me of cracker barrel but with more history. Would definitely go back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
TWO WORDS - TASTELESS CAFE! I was as disappointed as a child on Christmas who didn't get what she asked for from Santa. 
When I learned my husband was coming to Tennessee for business, the first thing I did was scout out places to eat. He and I are both self proclaimed foodies. Anyway, Loveless Cafe was top on the list. I skimmed through the reviews and was impressed by what I was reading. 
When we finally arrived in Nashville, I asked the lady, who checked us into the hotel, what she thought of Loveless Cafe, she raved about the biscuits. She said they're like nothing she ever tasted before. At this point, I'm boiling over with excitement. 
On our way to the restaurant, the traffic was horrible; however, I didn't mind. I knew the payoff would be SO worth it - not so much. 
Lemme just say, my husband and I are from Alabama. We know some good, southern cooking. It's what we were raised on in grandma's kitchen. ... OK, back to the review. 
We arrived and were immediately seated. I believe the positives stop about there. Yup, immediately seated - the only positive. 
The waitress came over hyping the food up. The pork is smoked 12 hours... we're known for our pork, fried chicken and biscuits... On and on and on... Lemme just say, she played her role as the hype girl - give her a raise! 
I digress... 
I'd already decided on the sampler weeks before we arrived. I knew we'd want to taste a little bit of err'thang! 
Ah, I wish I'd taken a picture of the food. The chicken wings and hush puppies looked like they'd been cooked in old grease. You could clearly tell it was time to change it. If the looks weren't enough to make the determination, the taste sealed the deal. The fish was also tasteless. I don't believe any seasoning was used. The 12 hour slow smoked pork - all I can do is shake my head! It was cold, hard, awful and served on top of what looked like a pancake which looked and felt like it had been sitting under a light all day. All the moisture and life was sucked right out of it - poor pancake! 
Now, to the raved review biscuits... The biscuits at the Cracker Barrel in Alabama taste better. I'm sure they're the same everywhere, but I can't vouch for anywhere else since I haven't been... There's nothing special, or spectacular about these biscuits. In fact. I've had a better biscuit at Jack's - a fast food chicken restaurant.
Here's my advice - save your time, gas, coins, and taste buds! It's definitely NOT worth the hype. YOU'RE WELCOME!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Oh my I would come here just for the biscuits. Absolutely the best!!!! Service was great.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: My daughter has lived in Nashville for almost 10 years so if don't do breakfast at Loveless it is not a good trip! We went during the week so we're seated right away. Before you even order out come the hot, melt in your mouth biscuits! You add a cuppa joe and you are in literally in  hog heaven! My daughter got the French Toast with bacon and I got my "usual" two eggs with bacon with hash brown casserole. We shared the two plates for the best of both worlds. They will refill not only your coffee cup but biscuits too!  They are known for their Country ham, takes one home to remember this epic visit.  They never rush you, even if there is a line out the door.  Sit a spell and enjoy a nice Southern breakfast.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Hewww weee honey! Bring your comfy crocs cause the line is looong! Oh and a crossword would be a good idea too. Ever heard of those Heavenly Hams they have at the fancy kroger or in the shoppin mall???? Well Loveless puts those hams to SHAME honey! They have heavenly ham, and boy oh boy did I butter my biscuit! But was it worth the 2 hour wait Yvette? Yes. Yes honey it was. Only thing I would say is, the bathroom isn't very escapable in a terror/hostage/tornada situation. For that I deducted a star, but, I'd put a step ladder in there to reach a window for old gals like me and it'd be a 5 star rating!!! A++++ food and service!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: For me, the food was just ok, and barely that. The pretzel was great but very salty. The mustard it was served with was sticky and sweet rather than sharp and spicy like I was expecting. I ordered the meat and cheese board and the beer cheese soup. The meat was just awful. It had an overwhelming iron and geletin flavor and the quality was in par with Oscar Meyer. The cheese lacked flavor entirely. The soup had a gritty texture and should have been smooth.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text:
They sat us quickly and accommodated us since we had a stroller. Our waters were brought out without being asked. We ordered our food and unfortunately it took about 45min- 1 hour to be brought out (2 cheeseburgers and 2 orders of chicken tenders). The milkshake we ordered was melted. We didn't receive one of our meals (we were sharing so we were all still able to eat). Our server Ian was rushing to help multiple tables with little to no help from anyone. He was very apologetic and never once was rude. We ended up returning our milkshake and never getting that 4th meal. I wish he had more help since it was a very busy Sunday lunch rush. 

5 starts to our server Ian, 0 stars for management.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: We were charged more for two eggs and 2 slices of bacon than we would have been charged for an entire breakfast meal - why didn't the server tell us that? The prices are ridiculous, and for the life of me I don't understand why people rave over their biscuits - they're not even flaky! McDonald's and other fast-food places have better biscuits. Their chicken & dumplings taste like those you buy in a can at Kroger - not gross, but not homemade either. And their vegetable casseroles are too greasy. If people think the food is good I think it is because they can't cook themselves and don't really know what good home cooking tastes like. I'M NOT A FAN OF LOVELESS CAFE!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
We visited Loveless for about the 15th time last weekend.  I learned a little more about it this time.  

Our first visit here was in around 1999 when Donna McCabe still owned it.  It was so charming then.  Like eating in a house.  This was before Loveless was expanded with more tables, professional kitchen, new restrooms, the stores, the barn, etc.  

It lost much of its charm when the McCabes gave it up.  But as I think about it, the things that have been done needed to be done.  Any business needs to make money or why have it?

A couple things I miss from the old Loveless.  They used to bring out biscuits in a round pan.  Now they are made in a large rectangular pan and served on a plate.  You just get a few and usually have to ask for more.  As I recall, the biscuits seemed better made the old way, even though it's the same recipe.  Also, the preserves used to be on the table in bigger glass containers.  Now they bring them out in tiny cups.  

Also, they used to grind up the ham for their omelets instead of chopping the ham.  Much better the old way.  Big difference.

But overall, I have to say the product is still good.  We waited for 2 hours last time.  It's not worth a 2-hour wait.  Cracker Barrel is not as good, but it's good.  If you have to wait more than an hour, screw it.  Come back another time.  

To me, this is a breakfast place.  They push the fried chicken at lunch and now have BBQ, but even when Donna owned it, the chicken was not that good.  Loveless is a breakfast place.

We have to give credit and a big thank you to the people who bought it from Donna.  I was told they are relatives of the Frist family of Nashville.  Good for them for saving this piece of our Tennessee culture.  

This place is not exactly as it used to be, but thanks to the new owners we still have it and it is very good.

Would prefer they use Tennessee-made meats, though.  Also, the sausage gravy here is less than spectacular.

name: Big Shotz
text: Layne Mathis is literally amazing! It was extremely busy and Layne was able to really hold it down. Much love and greatly appreciated! Thanks Layne!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Wanted to try this place but decided not to based on the purposeful lack of organization. 

My wife and I walked in and were told if we wanted to sit in the restaurant there would be a wait, but if we wanted to sit at the bar we could right away. We elected to wait. 

Q: How long is the wait?

A: I really can't say. We're understaffed and have had a number of large parties walk in without a reservation. 

(There are several people waiting - looks like at least two parties.)

Q: Ok, can you put our name on a list?

A: Oh no, my General Manager doesn't allow me to make a list. I'd get in trouble if I made a list. You'll just have to stay around here. 

So while we're standing there, more people come in and are told the same thing. No no, we can't make a list. 

By this point it was clear there were going to be several parties, some before us and some after. 

Who's responsibility is it to keep track of who is first or second, etc? This young lady who hasn't given us a number, taken a name, didn't seem to be paying much attention at all to us or the other people waiting?

So we left. I'll go spend my money somewhere where the management is interested in providing for a reasonable accommodation of (gasp) logically dealing with crowds of customers in parties of varying size. You know - with something the rest of the restaurant world uses - a list.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This restaurant should be on everyone's bucket list for authentic Southern food.  Forget healthy...forget cholesterol.  Just enjoy the awesome food here and eat a salad and workout tomorrow!

name: Big Shotz
text:
Why have a minimum? Why isn't one drink enough? No wonder it is dead here. Bad management/owner.
Out of business soon...go to a better bar. Lots to choose from.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
This place is SO GOOD and SO CUTE. I loved, and I mean loved the southern vibes this place gives off. It's just really charming. 

The biscuits and preserves were dangerously good. I would've been happy just eating biscuits the entire morning. They're buttery and rich and delicious. I like how they were on the smaller side, too. And don't get me started on the preserves..they were out of this world.

I ended up getting a vegetable omelette and it was really fresh! They chopped up the vegetables into super tiny pieces which I loved because a lot of places don't do that. And the coffee was great too! There's also a really cute gift shop next to it as well. This was easily one of my favorite stops while I was visiting Nashville!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
they handled a large (100+) group (with reservations) of hungry, tired, cranky guests and did so with grace and class...OH and the food was outstanding and everlasting ...did I mention the food was so very tasty and plentiful...because it WAS!!
A+++

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
Came here with a lot of family members - large family reunion. Good place with lots of seating and space. I ordered the schweinshaxe (pork shank). It was better than I expected. Most German fare I've had seemed dull, but this was very flamboyant: very crispy skin, tender meat, tasty lard, briny fried pork taste mixed with the sourness of the red cabbage and spice of the horseradish and creaminess of the gravy. 

Food didn't take too long to arrive. Price was a little on the high side for quantity and quality, but it is consistent with the local tourist area and shopping mall.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: City Winery always has the  best events, tonight was the West Sonoma Coast Vintners...we did the VIP ticket which allowed us an hour early entrance to taste wine and the charcuterie board which was amazing, pictures will be attached!!! Some of my favorite wineries were Dumol, Ernest Vineyards and Peay Vineyards. Keep a look out for their events, top knot!!!

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Came with the family for a nice German experience. Good beer! Giant hot pretzel as an appetizer was crisp on the outside and fluffy inside. Ambiance was cool, after the small bar there are rows and rows of tables with bench only seating. Perfect for making new friends if you're there during the dinner rush. Their food was good for the most part, would've gotten more stars from me if I didn't have to send my sliders back for being raw. When they came back out lo and behold they were still raw. The manager and server were super apologetic though and took it off the bill happily. The place also has live and festive music, complete with an accordion. Also bonus points given that everyone working there wore German costume. Would I go back? Maybe. Probably not my first pick though. Not too bad because the prices weren't awful!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: This place is an event. There are multiple buildings for souvenirs, buying food to take home, and the smoke house. The restaurant is also massive and the staff so friendly; the manager personally reviewed the menu with my wife to discuss food allergies. The portions are massive, including the endless side of biscuits and jam. The amount of meat you get is the same whether it's a plate, or a dish with that meat! The pulled pork was good, not great, but I had enough leftovers for dinner and breakfast the next day! I'd go back.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, jam, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, biscuits, BISCUITS! 

Oh, yeah, they have other food, too, and a very friendly staff.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Stopped in on our way through Nashville.  It was a good choice. It was good food and quick.  Our waiter, FatJohn was good and funny. We enjoyed our meals.  The four of us had the giant pretzel with beer cheese for an app. The main courses were Black Forest schnitzel, curry wurst, wurst plate with jalapeño cheddar sausage, and spinach salad and onion soup.  All were good but here are some fine details...... the beer cheese was good but not great.  The jalapeño cheddar sausage was not spicy. The spinach salad dressing was a little gelatinous but still tasty. It was a texture thing. The sampler platter was ordered for dessert. The best thing on it was a toss up between the apple strudel and the pretzel bread pudding. Overall not a bad stop.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text: Great beer, food, and experience! Don't let the location deter a visit. Dishes are authentic, as well as the brews. Multiple visits have always been good.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
With the drive and worth the wait. In fact I enjoyed the wait and took the time to tour the property and buy souvenirs. 

Owen made my day, he is a dream.

The food was amazing I chose a dinner sampler for brunch because it offered more choices. Chicken was well seasoned, catfish was amazing, and I always love country ham.  I wish I could have tried the bbq! Oh and the drinks were actually good I had something with whiskey, strawberries and lemonade...skip the mimosa and go for this drink it actually goes great with brunch.

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
The goods:  Beautiful bar, restaurant, venue.  The musicians that played were run of the mill singer/songwriters, but the sound was good (although it was really light, mainly acoustic music).  Every member of the staff I encountered was a lovely person.

The bads:  Overpriced.  Do you like paying $8-10 per glass of wine or beer?  Cause that's the lowest priced stuff.  Do you enjoy paying $9 for black bean dip that can barely be shared by two people?  Not to mention the chips that came with it were super thin and crumbled everywhere, and were gone by the time we were halfway through the dip.  All of the other reviews I've read here say the valet is $7, but it was $5 the night we went (Thursday).

So that's it. Everything was pretty much just okay.  I will probably stick to the smaller clubs with cheaper drinks and better bands.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Oh my goodness...seriously! I'm pretty sure the biscuits have crack in them...we just couldn't get enough! The best biscuits, hands down! The homemade jams that went with the biscuits (you get three to taste) were a perfect compliment to the biscuits. I had the BBQ pork and it was wonderful! And...since it's 'go big or go home' give the Mac and Cheese a try for a side! It was well worth the calories-absolutely delicious! And since no country meal is complete without dessert...might I suggest the coconut? It was delicious-even on a full stomach ! My only regret was not trying the banana pudding-I hear it's the bomb-diggety-I guess I will need to go back someday! We rolled out of the restaurant (literally) and was so glad we found this little gem on Pinterest! Give it a whirl!!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
For a cafe that's named loveless, the place be showing us some mad love!

Loves:
+ Comp'd biscuits. They are def worth the hype OK!
+ I loved my chicken. Hopefully someone in your party will get some and share the wealth.
+ Owen was our waiter and he was an absolute delight.
+ Cute decor. I'm a fan.
+ Little shops for you to peruse while you wait for your table.

Not so loves:
- About 45 min outside of Nash.
- There'll most likely always be a wait.

Overall this place is wonderful and worth the drive AND the wait. Thank you to the cafe for delighting us with some good cooking and thank you Owen for being a kind soul.

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
The Loveless Café has the most amazing biscuits I have ever eaten! I mean seriously, I can make the biscuits my entire meal with their own preserves, honey, and butter. I cannot emphasize enough the biscuits alone are totally worth the wait at this place (my family has waited over 2 hours before for a table here - but there is plenty to do between walking around the on-site shops and playing cornhole by the picnic tables outside while you wait). 

Aside from the world's best biscuits, The Loveless Café services up all your classic country favorites. Their fried chicken is delicious - fresh, crispy, seasoned just right, and complimented by your choice of sides. I'd also recommend the fried catfish or the smoked beef brisket. Breakfast is served all day here if that's what you're in the mood for. 

The service is as top notch as the food here. Friendly southern hospitality at it's finest. And they've always been very attentive on refilling the biscuit basket - that's instantly 5 stars from me!

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Loveless is a solid 4 stars. Why is that, you might ask? Well, the biscuits are out of this world and they come with 3 different types of homemade preserves. It was buttery, sugary heaven. If I had those alone, it would have been 5 stars.

The food itself, however, was really just a 3. I got one of the omelettes and, although the portions were big (though not quite as big as the people there) it was a very average omelette. My friend got the pulled pork breakfast, which he loved. The meal was literally the day's sustenance for us. But i just keep dreaming about those biscuits...

The service was average. The waitress was not that attentive and forgot that I had ordered the honey and sorghum (which basically looked and tasted like just honey). Regardless, just go and order a plate of biscuits. You won't be sorry you did.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text:
Friendly service and great rockabilly music, but that's where it stops. 
I had the turkey dinner, and the turkey was bone dry despite being drowned in gravy. I might come back for drinks and live music, but not to eat.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Perfect. I don't think anything could be better then breakfast Loveless. The wait may suck, you have to have most, if not all, of your party with you and then still wait 30+ minutes no matter the time of day. But with the gift shops and everything around it really is not too bad. Perfect pit stop if you are just coming through and tired of eating at Cracker Barrel.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Cute place and a must see if you're visiting the area in my opinion. It seemed like everywhere we went someone mentioned we should visit there. The kitchen store part had a lot of cutesy gifts that weren't overly cheesy which was nice. I got the pulled pork omelette my oh my was it rich but interesting and tasty! Pro tip - if you like sweet grits ask for the sorghum and pour it in your grits. So delicious! Went on a Tuesday afternoon around 1 and didn't have reservations. They said it was a good time where they weren't as busy and could take walk-ins.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Lots of good food and great service.  Had eggs, ham, pancakes and casserole .  All good !

name: Loveless Cafe
text:
Best breakfast I've had in a long time! First off...I wish I could remember the name of our waiter (tall guy with strawberry blonde hair-you know who you are!), because he was WONDERFUL and definitely made our experience even more enjoyable! 
The biscuits were to die for...Melt in your mouth! And the jams were delectable!
The waiter was amazing at giving suggestions! He led us all in the right direction based on what we were hungry for! 
The restaurant was so clean and well kept - but still had that historical charm to it. 
Loved every minute of my experience here! It truly felt as though I was having a meal with one big family

name: City Winery Nashville
text:
Reviewing this mostly as a music venue: This is one of those reviews that it's kind of painful to look at that two stars, but I'll try to justify it since there's no 2.4 star option.

Valet parking - despise it, despise it more when it takes forever in the freezing cold because of a valet issue, which it did after the show.

Friends bought us tickets to see a show there. We had front-table seats,  this should have been great. Unfortunately the assigned seating up there meant I spent the time faced almost completely away from the performers. I was jammed next to a couple I didn't know, had very little space behind me, so turning my chair was not particularly a feasible option. Very little room behind or to the sides.

I took a break from looking at the stage after a while because my neck hurt so much from craning it. I noticed there were plenty of free and open seats and tables, and the aisles they had constructed were huge so they could have given people a lot more space at the tables simply by not allowing 4 people to walk side by side in the aisles.

If we'd just had enough space to turn the chairs 90 degrees in the viewing situation would have been pleasant. We were packed in the sardine fashion, which was absurd because there were plenty of free tables.

Got up a couple of times to hit the restroom, just stayed standing off at the side of the stage until I felt like getting into the table pit again.

The food was alternately great and just ok, but the prices for everything were on the pricey side. I'll remind I was there for the performance, not for the food. My neck, back, and ears were annoyed by nearly everything at about five songs in.

Basically a slightly layout change to the tables would solve most of it, open seating after a certain point would have been nice, ability to get the car parked and unparked sans valet would be great.

By the time I left I was in a mood. For a music venue they could be so great, but it's just not set up for that and the way they have the up front seating. It was a very expensive, neck pain inducing night.

Maybe I should just say I'm old, this music venue made me grumpy. Get off my lawn. Food was tasty though. Not on my lawn!

name: Loveless Cafe
text: AMAZING!!  The meatloaf and smoked turkey are sublime!  Let's not even get started on the biscuits and jams.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: I was visiting Nashville with my boyfriend and we was told this was the place to go to! We went and put in our names, we ended up waiting 2 hours to even get seated. Once we WERE seated, our waitress, I believe her name was Skye, kept giving up glares the entire time we were being waited on. Did not seem very friendly at all towards us and we did not understand why as to she was being very well to the tables surrounding us. The food however was pretty good.. not sure if it was 2 hour waiting worthy, but it was decent. VERY largely portioned. I order the Music City Platter and everything was great except the ham is VERY salty.

name: Fat Kat Slim's
text: I can't figure out what they are.  Is it a bar mainly?  Or Are they a 50's diner?  They have the decor but doesn't seem kid friendly or have shakes or malts etc and the menu has no real theme - kind of a hodgepodge and I don't recall seeing appetizer options but I could have missed that.  We were there for lunch.  One side of menu is all alcoholic drinks, martinis etc which doesn't rally seem to go with the 50's diner motif.  The acoustics are very bad and was hard to hear the person sitting next to me (and there was no live music etc).  As for food Onion rings were very salty.  Burger was average.  The chili frito pie lacked meat and was reheated but not all the way through even.  . It was also a small portion for $14 but that didn't matter since we didn't eat due to lack of flavor and temp.  The waitress did remove the charge from the bill so I will give them thumbs up for trying to keep us happy.  Am posting this mainly so Mgmt will see it and help them improve.  Would love to see them succeed and maybe the rooftop will do well when weather is nicer.  It's a great location - was hoping it could be someplace we could stop on way to Preds games with the family but not so sure unless some changes made.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: Long wait, it was New Year's Eve and busy. We waited over an hour. The shops were cute but ran out of things to do quickly. Once we sat, the service was fast and the food was great! Biscuits were amazing.

name: Loveless Cafe
text: One of our Nashville favorites. When company visits, we like to take them here. Their homemade biscuits and jam are out of this world. The shops are fun and cute. And you will have time to shop because the wait is usually 1-2 hours. But it is worth the wait. We usually leave for Loveless Cafe before we are actually hungry.

name: Bavarian Bierhaus
text:
I'd give zero stars if I could. 

First time here and it will be my last. Very low customer to server ratio but it still took over 30 minute to receive our pretzel app.  Beer cheese tasteless and my biergarten burger is like biting into a 1/4lb ground beef with zero flavor and very dense texture. 

Server was atrocious - did not offer condiments, drink refills and when given an empty pepper grinder, he ran off to refill it in the kitchen. I grabbed one off a nearby table so I could finally start lunch after waiting so long for it to come out of the kitchen.

name: City Winery Nashville
text: My boyfriend and I loved this restaurant.   We had a wonderful experience. Nathan behind the bar was great!!!!   Morgan helped us get tickets to see a show and was a pleasure.  Hope to return to Nashville and visit again.

name: The Country
text: Went to see Hexagon Presents (which I highly recommend) and surprisingly the food was great!  I had the brussel sprouts and warm kale salad (which did not get shared) and my s.o. had the chicken and biscuits.  We'll definitely be back especially for Hexagon Presents.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: The Belcourt is great. They show the smaller films, the indie films, and the foreign films that the big theaters don't. Prices are reasonable. Seats are comfortable. Unlike some smaller theaters, Belcourt has high quality movie projectors so the picture quality is fantastic!

name: The Country
text: My friend was visiting and of course wanted to hear some live music. She had already experienced Broadway on previous trips, so we managed to compromise on trying The Country. It was a Tuesday night so I was happy to find live music somewhere other than downtown. The location is in the Vanderbilt/Parthenon area which is always a relief for me because parking is manageable. The bar itself is pretty nice. Had a big patio area with lights that was cute. The inside is very open and dark, but not too dark. What I would expect from a bar. The decor is actually really nice. I mean, not a ton to it but you can tell it's fairly new. Good beer selection. The only kink was they weren't serving food that night...don't know why because the bartender was very short with us. Not exactly service with a smile, but I guess they don't put their "A" team on a slow Tuesday night. It was fine. We got our beer, listened to some music, but then had to go somewhere else to find some food. I would definitely be down for trying this bar again on a weekend, especially if visitors are in town.

name: Springwater
text:
It's a dive bar. Correction, it is a dive, CASH only bar (with an ATM onsite). Beer was reasonable, clientele was... well, "divey". Pool tables, a few drunks, attentive bar tender and the possibility of live music. Not bad! I am a fan!

A few of the less than sober occupants did tell me this was the oldest bar in Nashville?

name: Drifters
text: We chose this place based on the reviews and it did not disappoint. Quaint bar with a neighborhood feel, service was friendly and fast. Answered all questions we had and was a good conversationalist without being annoying when you wanted to have a private conversation.  BBQ was great. Highly recommend the sampler platter! Great option to try multiple items. Great selection of BBQ sauces.

name: Mercy Lounge
text:
I enjoy this venue quite a lot. They get a good amount of acts I really want to see, so that's always good. 

Spacious and never too crowded.

name: Frisky Frog's
text: Came in for the Funday at the Frog event last week and saw a DJ there- he was awesome! Paulo with the hat. After that, the party died down, but it was still fun. Bartender was super nice and made delicious drinks. I didn't try the food yet but I'll go back if I see that DJ on the event flyer again.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: We went on a Monday during the 8 on 8th band promotion time period. It was a great place to get a local music feel. Drinks were affordable.

name: Drifters
text: Fried pickles were awesome! Beef and pork were deliciously smokey. Casual atmosphere, large outdoor seating area.

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: We went to the Postmodern Jukebox show last week. I liked that we were able to get right next to the stage and almost touch the musicians. If a group we likes plays there we will be going back

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
Nashville needs more places like this. The amount of culture and genuine entertainment that a place like the Belcourt creates is incredible. They are constantly throwing events (like outdoor movies and midnight classic showings) and the staff is always friendly and seem eager to serve and assist you. Not to mention the movie selection... I have yet to see a film I didn't like at the Belcourt. Each film seems to be hand picked for greatness.

The sound system and general aesthetics of the theatre are excellent. Everything feels classy, but cozy. I could come here every day.

name: Drifters
text: Great east Nashville watering hole with an eclectic offering of live music every weekend including Pal Sheldon and His Awesome Friends - they play here in warmer months every month. Super friendly and casual vibe. Every time we go there we always see someone we know. Yummy wings, beans, brisket, burgers, salads and some fine vegetarian food and it's not overpriced! Good for the pocket! It's our fave local semi dive bar.

name: Drifters
text: I was immediately addressed by everyone on shift. Great beer selection and I went with their signature pulled pork sandwich "The Drifter" and was blown away. Great meat, great bread, and I'm from Texas. Would recommend even if they were cheering for Alabama.

name: Drifters
text: So so yummy that I came here twice in one night! They have 2 for 1 drinks on happy hour and the bbq is delicious! Like any good place, they make all of their own sauces and offer a variety of them. It's a nice local joint to get some good food and drinks with many other places to hang out nearby.

name: The Country
text: Hidden gem in west end. Came in on a Saturday and had a great time. Bartender super friendly, the band playing that night was good.

name: Drifters
text: Yesss!!! Bring Nashville to the table!!  First off the happy hour specials are great.  Either a double well drink or 2 beers for 1.  The service was so awesome.  The gentleman that waited on us was on point and full of great suggestions.  The food was tasty specifically the pulled brisket and pork.  The coleslaw was done perfectly.  The beans were delicious.  I will be back.  The place was the perfect price!!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: Yes! Finally something that gives Nashville a true cosmopolitan vibe! Somewhere to find great independent movies, documentaries and foreign films that encourages diversity and ignites the mind. Also, It is a bargain for sure with decent parking and is walking distance to great bars and restaurants. It is an absolute perfect place for a stimulating evening out. Long live the Belcourt Theatre!

name: Experience Nashville Tours
text: At the last minute we decided to see if we could get on a walking tour of Nashville. After researching a bunch on Yelp, it seemed many of the tours did not operate on Mondays. Lucky for us Experience Nashville Tours was scheduled to do one tour on Monday and we were able to confirm a spot on Sunday evening. We met our tour guide Kaysie along with a few other travelers and it was well spent couple hours. This lady is so high energy and enthusiastic that it really makes the tour a wonderful experience. You can tell she has a great passion for the artists and history of the town and she took us to several very interesting venues with lots of background stories. It was a fun couple hours and very affordable. I'd highly recommend booking a tour with Kaysie!

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: The Belcourt has a special place in my heart. From the unique films to the drinks and friendly staff... this place always makes me happy. It's historical significance tops everything and I hope it stays around for a long time. Do yourself a favor and see a movie at the Belcourt.

name: The Country
text:
Came here alone on a Thursday night for dinner and free music.  Very satisfied with the experience.

Staff: Bartender was very nice.  I'm told it's a Southern thing, but very patient while I pondered my beer options. 

Food: Had their grilled cheese and chips. Nothing special, but satisfying and reasonably priced.

Booze:  Beers on tap.  Recommend the Kentucky Bourbon Barrel if you get the chance (Serving size is smaller, but it's higher percentage and tasty.  Price and size were similar to what I got when I ordered the same at The Listening Lounge).  Kudos to The Country for having a reasonable selection.  

Ambiance: Very relaxed. Clean and updated decor. Place was not full.  Thankful that it felt comfortable enough to sit alone, intermittently reading a paper and listening to the music. As for the music, I liked one person more than the other.  The crowd was very subdued, but at least the first artist rocked out and had a good time. 

Price: Pretty reasonable.  I think it was $23 for dinner and 2 of their most expensive beer on tap.  And the 1.5 hr of free entertainment.  

Overall: I wanted to go back, but we ran out of time in Nashville.  Would've liked to try a few of their appetizers.  If you're in the area and looking for something easy without a big crowd, consider this place.

name: The Family Wash
text: We loved this place. Casual, friendly, attentive service and good food- not too pricey! Good food. And live music! Shepherd's Pie was excellent. Did I mention that all the food is good?

name: Drifters
text: Great place to stop in and get a drink with food. I was able to be seated quickly at the bar. Great selection of drinks and beers on draft. The food was amazing, highly recommend the nachos with brisket.

name: EXIT/IN
text: Great setting for live music. Long long list of stars that have been through on the wall! Better than expected beer selection.

name: Drifters
text: I honestly don't understand how they have 4 stars... we were cool with the atmosphere of the restaurant, but when I went to the bathroom I saw the kitchen. FILTHY!! Prep table was open and gross AF! Things that should have been refrigerated weren't.. and the cooks were not wearing gloves to say the LEAST! We just canceled our order and left before getting the food.

name: Drifters
text: Went here on a recommendation of a local as we are from out of state and we where looking for where locals go. Waitress took our and it arrived fast, but the pork ribs where really dry and over cooked. We talked to the waitress and they drought us some fresh one and they where awesome. We don't care for spicy food or sauce and they had 5 sauces to choose from from sweet to spicy. The staff was great and the atmosphere is the type we really enjoy.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
Since moving to Middle Tennessee in late 2014, I have probably been to the Belcourt close to 30 times and I've never once had a bad experience.  The staff is friendly, the popcorn is delicious, and most of the time I will leave intellectually stimulated by whatever film I just saw. It's a stark contrast to your typical multiplex experience to say the least. 

But most importantly, as a basically lifelong film fanatic, I can assure that you are going to be surrounded by other audience members who have a true mutual respect for the viewing environment.  Before every film begins, a message comes on the screen that strictly forbids talking or cell phone use of any kind, and that if this rule is violated, a staff member will take care of it if it's brought to their attention.  In my two dozen plus times at The Belcourt, I have never once seen this ruled violated by an audience member.  This is hands down the best theater not only in Nashville, but Middle Tennessee in general, and a true haven for dedicated movie lovers.  I'm extraordinarily anxious to leave Murfreesboro and live in Nashville, so I will have the opportunity to come far more often and join their membership program.  

A couple things of note:  The parking lot is usually full, but you'll probably find street parking on Belcourt Ave, or the next street over on Acklen. 

It's a tired joke of how outrageous concession prices are at any cineplex you go to, but I always make a point of getting a popcorn and soda at the Belcourt, and I encourage you to also make a concession purchase when you visit.  As mentioned before, the popcorn is delicious, but more importantly The Belcourt is offering the Nashville community a truly invaluable product that would be almost non-existent in the area without the theater's presence, which are interesting and diverse films throughout the entire year.  I'm the type that makes Top 10 lists at the end of every year, and almost every entry in my personal list of 2018 was something I saw at The Belcourt.  So remember when you're passing by the stand, you would be supporting a non-profit that continues to make The Belcourt an irreplaceable cultural mecca of the city, as opposed to just filling the wallets of some rich executive with no connection to Nashville.

I absolutely love this theatre, and it would be so hard to fill the void of finding a comparable place if I ever left Middle TN.

name: Drifters
text: Now this is what I call a home away from home! I could eat twenty plates of the bbq brisket nachos and rock out to the kid rock cover bands! They have great two for one draft beer specials that will make any beer girl get out of her snuggie! They also have great vegetarian options for all you hippies.

name: Mercy Lounge
text: My mom, fiancée, and I saw the Ultimate Garth Brooks Tribute this Saturday. We had a wonderful time. The band was fantastic and the staff was amazing! My mom needs to use a wheelchair because of arthritis in her knee. Eron was very kind and made sure that we were comfortable. They personally escorted us from the elevator to the stage area and made sure my mom had a great view of the performance. Additionally, the staff is extremely responsive via email. My fiancée emailed the venue in advance to make sure that the space was wheelchair accessible. The staff responded immediately. Thank you, Eron, for making our first country music concert and visit to Nashville so memorable.

name: Drifters
text: This place was super laid back. The live music was good and great as background or just to listen too. The musician played for several hours without a break and only stopped to pack up. The BBQ fell off the bone and the side portions were big enough to not feel cheated and small enough to not take away from the best ribs I've had in a while. Lots of locals and the staff was awesome, checking in just enough to meet your needs and not make you feel ignored.

name: Springwater
text:
Beer
Food
Music

Built on top of a spring, what else do you want?

1896 built at the same time as the Parthenon! 
Password no longer required ;)

name: Drifters
text: This bar restaurant had a great atmosphere.   A variety of Tex mex and BBQ along with Vegan options.   The portions were huge and more than generous.    The BBQ was mediocre and did not have very much flavor.   They had a vast selection of BBQ sauce which was helpful for helping out the meat.   Our server was awesome and attentive.    Just wish the BBQ has been better.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
Oh they have really changed the look of this wonderful Theater 
Looks completely renovated and their prices are lower than most others and I really enjoyed the movie with natilie portman 
Playing John Kennedy wife ..a great place to check out

name: The Local
text:
Thanks for fixing the issue! Appreciate it.


The music and beer selection here are good. We went in on a Friday night. It was pretty quiet, not a huge crowd. The reason for our original 2 star review is upon checking our credit card statement we found the bartender gave himself a higher tip than the one we gave him for two beers. It's pretty shady to change the tip amount on the receipt. I don't know that we will be back. But if you go, pay in cash.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text:
I heart this place so much.

The movies are inexpensive and original (lots of indie flicks.) You can buy beer and popcorn. I think that's it. That's really all you need to know. You can also catch live shows and talks from time to time. Midnight Movies is cool. But I really think cheap tickets, old theater, beer, and popcorn - 'nuff said.

name: The Local
text: Love the local vibe. Local musicians and song writers  this is probably one of my favorite spots in Nashville so far. Typically they have two bartenders on so you do have to order from the bar as they get quite busy but I typically sit at the bar anyway haha the food is good too!

name: Cannery Ballroom
text: I was here tonight to see Theory of a Deadman. I had VIP tickets and my husband and I settled in our spot right in front of the stage. I started feeling light headed and the room was spinning. Thinking it was low blood sugar I sent my husband for a sugary drink. I want to add that I had ZERO alcohol in my system so I was not drunk . As he stepped back up beside me I was passing out and fell into him. He got security and their concern for me was overwhelming and so sweet. The security guy left and brought back some juice and water and expressed to me that I should step away and sit down or get some air, but I was determined to not give up my awesome spot in the front...... I'm stubborn ‍ and I was optomistic that I would be better once the juice kicked in. He let me know that if I needed ANYTHING to let him (or one of the other security personnel that he pointed out) know. I started to feel better, but then I started getting weak, nauseated, and dizzy again after a short while so my husband led me to a sitting area where he left me to find security again. Eron came. He was so nice, very professional, very concerned, and went so far beyond what I ever expected. He called an ambulance and had two of his female security officers stay with us and help me outside when I felt able to walk out to meet the ambulance. Those ladies were also very sweet and helpful--complimenting my makeup to make me feel better and fanning me with a clipboard to cool me off. Eron checked back in with us while we waited and then I left in the ambulance. I was able to get back to the concert and see the last 4 songs AND Eron was at the entrance when I got there and had us escorted backstage! I may have missed 3/4 of the concert, but I was over the moon because of his gesture. I was greeted with a hug from one of the ladies that helped me, too. I wish I knew everyone else's names, but there are parts of the night that are fuzzy. Thank you so much to everyone for all of your help and concern. The staff here went above and beyond and are simply amazing.

name: Belcourt Theatre
text: I spend so much time here that I've nicknamed it my home away from home. They are doing a serious service to our community. Everything they put out is high quality. The staff is very nice. The prices are great. This place keeps me going.

name: EXIT/IN
text: If you want to be treated like absolute trash, definitely check this place out. We had an awesome, amazing time in Nashville for my husband's 40th (reviews to follow), but this place was the one and only loser of our trip.  I pre-purchaed tickets for the Sept 1 Sam Holz concert.  The bouncers/doormen/henchmen let some of us in (the females) without ID's (in San Francisco we don't go out with ID's at 40 but apparently in Nashville they're super strict so beware and bring your ID's) and denied the husbands, only to take their and our money first. They then came inside, lifted the females bodily and threw us all out when one of the husbands called them out for only requiring ID's of the men. These bouncers are the kind of guys who have no power in life so they wield whatever ounce of self-importance they can muster.  The ambiance was OK, the drinks were OK, venue would have been fine if the bouncers hadn't been so nasty and stolen our money. Love Nashville and we will be back, but I've never had a worse experience at a bar. Too bad they didn't know who we know in Nashville. If we'd had a good night they would have had a country music legend in their midst.  Be careful who you treat like waste matter, you never know! We were sure to pass along to our Nashville friends where NOT to go.

name: EXIT/IN
text:
One of my favorite Nashville venues! 
My main concern with this locale is parking. 

To be such an intimate place, the Staff could brush up on politeness. 

I've seen indie to rock at this legendary spot! It suits most all genres and the sound quality it great! 

Def like their FB page- they have ticket giveaways!

name: Nashville Underground
text: Had a really good time here with my wife and nephew. It's new so it's super clean. The wings were killer. The ring of fire sauce is actually really hot. They put the Titans game on for us and the staff was really pleasant and chatted with us. In the men's room, you can see the bar and televisions from the urinals through the windows so that was really cool. We're local and this is the nicest place on Broadway. We'll be back!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: If I could give less that a star, I would. Love the music, but the service was God-awful. I have never been treated so poorly by a bartender (and I'm from New York)... I very politely asked for water (on a day when it had been 90+ degrees and dehydration was a real possibility), was consistently ignored, until she finally slammed down a bottle of water and told me they don't serve tap water. Maybe it's because I'm from out of town, but I had never heard of such a thing, so when I questioned it, she had security escort us out. Seriously? We will not be returning.
