name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Came from Philly to Nashville to check out this spot. Very well lit. Good food.. Try the fish tacos they are my favorite. The drinks are well made and very reasonable.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
This three floor honky tonk had three different bands and a huge variety of music. 

It was crowed, but easy to navigate.  Found it a difficult to get drinks on the 1st, but no issues on the other two. 

We were invited to grab some open seats at table and enjoyed watching the bands and their interactions with the audience. 

This is a place you must stop at while walking down Broadway.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This is a nice bar to hang out . It's more for single people. But it has nice balconies and is huge!!!. Not the best price in drinks but have diferent groups playing in each floor.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Great place with great bands. Solid lineup compared to most places on Broadway. Always a good time.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Not sure what the craze is with this place. Seemed very similar to all the other bars except for the fact the beers were way more expensive than anywhere else we went. Not my favorite of the night but a cool place nonetheless!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: A little too "gritty" for my taste, with only a token, rotgut wine on the menu. But I appreciate that they aren't trying for an upscale vibe and I am clearly not their target audience! The band we saw was lively and talented, but it was hot and sweaty and condensation from the ceiling was dripping on my head so I had to move on to the next stop. Let's just call it... "Authentic."

name: War Memorial Auditorium
text:
A decent, but small venue.

The small size likely makes some events nice because of the relative intimacy of the venue, but it also has a serious downside.  That is that the floor seating consists of uncomfortable folding chairs, that over the course of a show of any length, will consistently remind you that you've been sitting in a folding chair for a while.

I would absolutely see another show here, but I would certainly be more interested in seating on the second floor which is entirely built for this purpose.

name: Famous Nashville
text: Was extremely excited to attend their NYE event. Unfortunately the top floor flooded and we were not allowed in. We were promised a refund by the management and now they are not refunding any of the customers who didn't make it in due to the flooding. Extremely poor management in my opinion.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
We enjoyed this location, a band on every floor is always great because if you don't like one you can just make your way to the next. The balconies on every floor is definitely one of the best parts about this bar. It's great to see the chaos on the street down below while you're comfortably standing in a bar listening to great music. It's also smack dab in the middle of Broadway so you get a great taste of the vibe of the city. 

Only thing I didn't necessarily like was that this bar has bathroom attendants. I don't need someone to put soap in my hand or rip my paper towel, and I don't need small talk while taking care of business. 

Other than that, great bar.

name: The Station Inn
text: I had high hopes for this place. However, we walked in and were immediately greeted with stares from everyone there. Then we find out there is a $12 cover charge- on a Monday night. Considering every other place we went to didn't have a cover charge, this is a little steep. The music seemed great and I wish I could've enjoyed it, but we decided to leave after being awkwardly confronted after making it halfway to the bar to be told there was a cover charge. Not only that but they made it uncomfortable and were rude. Maybe this place is better for locals than visitors but i felt like they could've shown a little more courtesy in the way they spoke to us regardless of who we were. Otherwise, the actual place seemed like a cool little spot and what little we heard of the music was nice.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Love, love this place. Rocking music all day long, good food and fantastic staff! Go Tara!

name: The Station Inn
text: This place rocked. Great bluegrass and mountain music on a thursday night in January.  The aesthetic is perfect- divey, southern and authentic. Much better alternative to the insanity of Broadway downtown. I felt it was worth the $12 cover.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: This bar was so much fun! We went here two nights in a row! The fried pickles and fried chicken were very good as well as the drinks and live music. The Yee Haw drink was my favorite and the country bands were so good! I was dancing the whole night. There are three floors and on every floor there is a country band.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Total Downtown Nashville experience. Got pulled on stage by the lead singer of the band for a dance contest for single girls - completely mortified, but had an amazing night. Never seen so many combos of fireball recipes ((dangerous)) lol

name: Alley Taps
text: We found a great little bar along printers row and were pleasantly surprised! Beautiful inside. Prices are good and the atmosphere is fantastic. You almost feel like a local the minute you walk in the door. Natalie the bartender was fantastic and we met some really cool people while we were there. We will definitely be back!

name: The Station Inn
text:
This place was awesome!  Though the decor of the building has the feel of the 60's, you shouldn't be alarmed.  For just $15 we saw a great group (18 South).  The beer prices are reasonable for Nashville ($4) and the staff is friendly.
We'll go back without a doubt!

name: Live On The Green Music Festival
text:
Awesome music venu and a must do if you're in Nashville. Parking can be a bit tough, but what's new if you're from Nashville. 

Make sure to see the Mummies as they're amazing!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Crowded bar with multiple floors. Live music setup on each floor playing covers. The bar can get crowded at times so the wait for a drink might be a little but there are other bars to move between. The views of Broadway from the balconies is nice. The bathroom lines can get crowded and messy

name: Alley Taps
text:
Took a chance in Printer's Alley to get off of Broadway for a little while.  

This place is quaint and had a decent crowd and pretty good band for Wednesday night.  

We didn't eat there so I can not give 5 Stars. Good draft beer selection and good service. 

Take a chance and get off the strip and check this place out on Printer's Alley.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Honky tonk was a bar we went for New Year's Day to watch football. Had a big group of friends and were having a great time. One of my friends got cut off and as I went over to get him out of the bar, a security guard sucker punched me and put me in a choke hold. I have a busted lip and couple marks on my face. Even the bartenders had my back and said I didn't do anything wrong. I called the police and filed a complaint. But never once did a manager come out and talk to me. I will never recommend this place to go if they have this aggressive security guard working there. He assaulted me and got sent home. It is all on camera and I will proceed with legal actions. Ruined my trip to Nashville.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: While touring around with family from out of town we stopped in to give them a taste of the touristy part of Nashville. We had the fried bologna sandwich which was tasty but definitely a gut buster. Waitress was nice and efficient. The bathroom attendant has a hoot! The band was Ok but nothing special. I would include it as a stop on a downtown crawl but not as a destination.

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text:
This was my first trip to Nashville and first time at benchmark. The bar was pretty nice. It's small and there is limited seating. There was no cover charge and of course there was live music. The music was awesome. There were no waiting staff so we had to go to the bar. This is where the issues I had came into play. The bar opens tabs but keeps your card. I opened the tab and they kept my card. I went about my evening and when I went to close my account prior to leaving I found they had given my card to another patron. 

I couldn't fathom how the staff would not check the name on the card before giving it to someone. That's a first for me. The bartender initially said she gave it back to me and I explained my tab was still open and she confirmed that it was. They looked all over the bar before realizing they swapped two cards mine and the other patron. 

Needless to say I was a little upset. I had to call and cancel my card and lock my account. The staff somehow reached out to the patron who had my card and he came back at bar closing and gave the card to the staff. I spoke with him and thanked him for returning it but at that point everything was closed and locked anyway.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: FUCK THIS PLACE.. The security guard told me to fuck off. Was looking for a first drink... I guess not here. The guard was wearing mask. I hope the owners can his disrespect self.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: Donny Lee rocked the house. Stopped in for one beer, but spent 4 hours. Great time. Will definitely add Honky Tonk Central to most fun bars in Nashville.

name: The Station Inn
text: We wanted live music, and BOY did we get it. We happened in on a night when there was incredibly gorgeous Bluegrass music being joyfully played and sang by a mix of a regular band plus their friends from the audience. I think it was perfect: we got a little something different than what happens most nights, but it was exactly what we hoped for.

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text:
Someone must have read my review because they took that dreadful black tarp off the fence..
That was a ridiculous move, to begin with.
If you're going to build an outdoor concert venue in downtown, expect local residents to watch from the other side of the fence..

name: Famous Nashville
text: It could be an awesome place , but is WAY too loud! It is painful in the bar. Either turn it down or install sound dampening in the ceiling. As it is, I can't stand to be in the bar more than 30 minutes at a time. It's a shame cause it's an awesome bar....

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Initially walked past this place but the music made me step back and walk in. Adam Rauscher was playing with Dominique Hutchinson. My husband d and I ended up staying for 4 hours enjoying the great service and great entertainment!

name: The Back Corner
text: I just got through listening to Jesse Kinch's performance of "After All These Lovers," one of Jesse's originals, at The Back Corner.  Unbelievable acoustics surrounding great talent!  For music events, it's clear that The Back Corner is the place to go in Nashville.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
Attempted to come to Honkey Tonk to ring in the new year after paying $80 for their "NYE Fast Pass" which supposedly would allow you to skip the line into Rippeys and Tootsies as well as here. This was our first stop at 9:30pm (much before the rush to get into places before midnight) and we were still told we needed to wait in line. 

Essentially myself, as well as 7 of my friends, were collectively scammed out of $560 for absolutely NOTHING. Additionally, the passes could only be paid for in cash, so I highly doubt that the large profit this bar is making on scamming its patrons will ever be reported on their tax return. 

Please reconsider before paying to attend any special events at the Honkey Tonk.

name: Honky Tonk Central
text: My boyfriend and I came by last night and the music was great. The female guitarist who just turned 21 is a damn rockstar. Purple rain!! Only downside was the creepy pinky ring dude who kept trying to high five me and my boyfriend between naps who needed to be to be cut off. He is probably nice sober though. 5 stars.

name: Nashville Underground
text: I dont write negative reviews yet we wont be going back. To many great restaurant options available.  Waited 50 minutes for a chicken salad and a small hot chicken dinner.  Chicken dinner may of been the worst I've had. Thank goodness the fries were good.

name: Nashville Underground
text:
Come here for the club and music, but avoid the food.

Nashville Underground is located at the end of Broadway street in Nashville. It's a solid location that's a bit away from the usual raucous you'll see on Broadway. 

One thing that I like about this place is that it contains a bit of something for everyone. There's a live music section/pub style restaurant on the first floor. The second contains a mechanical bull (which I rode and fell off).  The third contains an LED dance floor. A rooftop bar and private spaces for parties. If you come here to drink, club, and have a good time, you'll love this place.

But I'll have to remove a star due to the terrible food experience here. My friends and I ordered a variety of things so I know it wasn't just a single dish. Food ordered below:

-G's Southern Steak Salad: The steak wasn't precut and it was placed on top of the salad. The steak was so rough that we couldn't cut it with the knife provided. I asked the waitress for a steak knife and we still had trouble. Gave up on trying to eat this.
-Jumbo Wings: Forgot the sauce we got it with this, but the sauce came out too...sweet with a peculiar flavor. My friend that ordered this shared it with the rest of our group hoping that she didn't have to touch it anymore.
-Build Your Own Burger: A simple burger that's super hard to mess up. Fries were a bit unseasoned.

4/5. Honestly, the clubbing experience was so solid here that it saved this place from a lower rating.

name: Alley Taps
text:
We came here early on a Saturday night and it was a welcome respite from the shoulder-to-shoulder busy bars of Broadway and other Printer's Alley bars. 

The theme is a Prohibition-era Speakeasy. They have a really neat little house band that plays good music and dresses in period. The walls of the bar are combination exposed brick and rock, giving you the feel that you're underground. The lighting is low, romantic and charming. I would have loved to see the bartenders dress in period as well!

We stayed long enough to have a few beers and listen to the band finish. Definitely a fun spot that we will return to occasionally!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
We came in on Sunday night at 8pm. The place was packed, standing room only. The only reason we stayed is because of the awesome band. A female was upfront with a 10 year old killer drum player and 17 year old crazy guitar player. They played everything from AC/DC, Tom Petty, Led Zeppelin, Neil Diamond, etc.

There is a long wait to get a drink at the bar but for $10 you will get a double pour in your drink.  About 40 minutes a partial table cleared and we got a seat but there was no table service.  It took about an hour for someone to come to clear up the table but did not take drink orders.

name: The Cowan
text:
Saw a show with The Maine, as was severely underwhelmed by the mix in the room. I agree with D.H. below about the vocals being literally indistinguishable when in the first 1-8 rows of standing room. Their Speaker Line Array either needs to add one or two more or simply put some front of house speakers for the people who want to be close. It's an intimate venue so that should be a no brainer...I moved to the middle & back of the venue and it sounded solid there.

You have one job as a live music venue, Cowan, HAVE GOOD SOUND. Unfortunately, you guys missed the part where you walk the room and listen to the mix to ensure consistency. Don't just mix from back of house. My God. Amateur Hour here with Top Golf's "Music Venue". Just because you do Golf, doesn't mean you should be doing music.

The band however was AWESOME.

name: Alley Taps
text:
What an awesome spot! And it's the only Pittsburgh Steelers' bar in the city! Great spot for weekends, rad ambiance and super friendly bartenders! Game day they have 2-4-1 beers! The live music is a nice change from the Broadway honky tonks. The hot dog is STELLAR! 
Truly a hidden gem!

name: Honky Tonk Central
text:
All you have to know about Honky Tonk Central is....$6 for a freaking PBR.
Mediocre bands playing the same old songs you hear back home on a Monday night (unless you've come to Nashville to hear Bon Jovi covers).
The bar caters to the Frat and Bachelor/Bachelorette Party crowd.
Do yourself a favor and go across the street to Robert's and hear real country music played by amazing musicians (and only pay $2.50 for a PBR)

name: Benchmark Bar & Grill
text: Stopped in here on Saturday 8/8/2015 and listened to an amazing band!! If anyone knows the name of them please let me know. They played great together and amazing acoustic by the lead singer!!

name: Ascend Amphitheater
text: HAD A PHENOM TIME!!!! Vampire Weekend had my total respect. Everything at this venue is top notch. My favorite venue in Nashville to see a concert (and I've seen over 50). Go!!!!!!!!! I impore you.

name: Nashville Underground
text: Came to the underground for the first time with my Family and we were not disappointed. The manager Teddy was amazing and showed us the whole restaurant. On the roof, our bartender was Bobby and he was awesome, super personable, quick service and BOMB drinks. SHOUT OUT TO BOBBY 2TIMES! Thanks for an awesome experience!

name: The Back Corner
text: One of my favorite clubs in Nashville. The only place that doesn't play country music which I love. I love when they play hip hop & top 40's. You can check out the calendar to see what they're playing for the night, the ambiance in there is great-definitely a mix of LA & New York. It's a mix crowd which I love. The manager & all the staff there are very welcoming, I normally reserve a table there when I go & the prices are very reasonable.

name: The Cowan
text: Went to a concert here, and the doors were supposed to open at 7:00! After sitting in the cold and the rain, they delayed opening the doors with little apology. Super disappointing!

name: Bobby's Idle Hour Tavern
text: This place is a gem. The staff is the very best and you're going to learn something new when you start talking to the person sitting next to you.

name: Famous Nashville
text: I would have to say this place has some of the best food for a bar with live music just off Broadway. But I have to say I am skeptical of their happy hour practices. I ordered a house wine which I was told was on the happy hour menu but they were out so I could order the full priced option? My friend ordered a beer two for one. When he went to order the second one was told it was to late. When I did get the bill the wine was not on happy hour at all. I had to question the bill and was able to reach a reasonable expectation but it was more work than dinner and a drink should be.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: My wife and I stumbled upon this place in Nashville after dinner at Husk. The music is top notch and it is a way different vibe than the typical Broadway scene in Nashville. Apparently you need to make reservations. Luckily, the nice lady at the door let us stand in the back and we were able to nab some chairs. We didn't have the food, but what was coming out of the kitchen looked pretty good.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I really liked the Johnny Cash Museum. Was in and out in about 30-45 minutes. The museum was kindof small but good for what it was. 

TIP:  Watch for Groupons for 1/2 off!!

They had a lot of cool old things of Johnnys.  There were also iPads that made the information a bit more interactive. There was handwritten letters, clothes and many other items to view. 

There is also a museum store for you to grab your Johnny merch.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: My SO and I decided to break up a road trip with a stop in Nashville specifically to visit this museum. I purchased a Groupon that guaranteed admission for two for the low price of $19 and was blown away by the high quality experience we received for our money. This museum is an obvious must see for all Johnny Cash fans, but the exhibits also provide an education into the evolution of rock n' roll for all music enthusiasts. The facility is clean and well-lit, displays are thought out and plaques/signage are easy to read. The staff members are professional, attentive and knowledgeable about the exhibits. With ample parking nearby, there is no excuse to skip this delightful Nashville gem of a museum while you're in town and pay some respect to the Man in Black!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Pass on Brunch...
It's not in my nature to be cruel but in adherence to the traveler mantra I have a duty to warn others in regards to this brunch.  Don't go!  We heard good things about the music that happens at night but if that's true, fine, but the brunch service has a ways to go.  

The rest of this review will be for management, hopefully they'll take steps to improve.  
Service: our apathetic waiter was at best, vacant. He took 20 mins to greet us at our table because he was "making coffee"...  So either the hostess should not have sat us at his station or maybe coffee should already be made (we arrived at 10:15, opening time is 10). The best was when we asked if we could get a to-go cup, he said he'd check. Came back ten mins. Later and when I asked again about the To Go, he said "probably, I'll check!"

Food:  I've seen better buffets at Country Buffet.  Cold, soggy, tiny waffles; hockey puck sausages, sausage gravy eew, rubbery eggs.  The seafood? Dip was good as was the fruit plate. The rubbery, hard eggs, waffles and sausages aren't surprising when they sit in a chafing dish for forty minutes.  Kudos to the kitchen for having food ready at ten a.m. But the service staff isn't helping you when it takes a party of four almost forty minutes to get plates to eat...btw, there were only eight customers (including us four) in the place!

Cost:  for three buffets, three drinks and one bottomless mimosa (eew) and a bagel sandwich the tab was almost $150.  We're from Chicago, we KNOW high prices but that was absolutely ridiculous considering the venue, service and quality of food.  If the restaurant wasn't so far away from everything we would have left but decided to stick it out and give it a shot. Lesson learned, listen to your gut and run!

I suppose we're just tourists and there's no chance we'll greatly affect this place but they should seriously re-consider the brunch trade because at this point they are just hurting themselves.

Again, I feel bad to leave a negative review but when the only good thing you can say about a restaurant is that no one got food poisoning, things need to change!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Hands down an Great music venue

Food quality was less than ideal and a bit pricy for what you get.  Did not finish salad entrée, just did not taste fresh.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
We came here on a Saturday night to the early seating and did not have to wait very long to get in since we got there about 15 minutes early. We were seated at a great table with a great view. Our server was good, but they were out of many of the items on the menu (and we were the first seating of the night). Also, once the show started, she barely came around.

The show itself was awesome and the atmosphere was great! There were 4 artists who all had written songs for famous people. Their own music and voices were also great. We took our kids and they had high chairs and one artist even snag a children's song (coincidence). this would have been a 5 star review had the menu been fully available as the food was decent.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: The General Jackson Showboat was pretty nice. The boat goes from Opryland to Downtown Nashville. It provides plenty of great spots for pictures. They did a performance that was basically the history of country. It was a great experience to see as I was not a big country fan. The food was okay. It seemed satisfactory. The desert was great. It was an interesting twist in strawberry shortcake.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
Wow! What a remarkable journey down the Cumberland river in nashville. One thing I loved about it was being able to see on the outskirts of the city. It was a treat to see the river and the side of Nashville off road. The nighttime view of city was remarkable, very beautiful sailing underneath the pedestrian bridge. 

There's a show at the end of the night on your way back to the dock which I was very impressed with. The entertainment was amazing, it takes you all the way back to when country first began and had a great timeline that shows you best of country hits of each decade. The flow of the show was just perfect they did great, but the last 10minutes did seem to drag a little because your getting a little tired around ten.

The downside was the drinks were crazy EXPENSIVE for a single beer of a local brewery. 14.50$ Whaaaat???? There insane to ask that much for a 16oz beer. The food was average not like mamas home cooking food and service a bit slow but very pleasant. 

Ultimately if your looking for a good southern country entertainment and love country music this would be something great for you and your family to check out. Very family oriented!

name: 360 Burger
text:
I stumbled across this place after spending a few hours at Game Galaxy Arcade a few doors down with my little brother. The burgers are delicious and offer a lot of bun and topping options I haven't seen at other places. 

The cheesy goodness burger is a classic cheeseburger with three cheeses and perfectly satisfied my classic burger cravings. My fiancée got a cilantro avocado burger that was spicy and different and delicious. My brother had sliders that totally filled him up. There's also a good variety of fries and onion rings and two for one draft beer every day! On top of that, the two times I've been, I've had excellent service. This isn't the spot you'd expect to find such a good burger joint, but it's well worth the trip.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text:
We had walked by on a Friday night and loved the music coming through the open window but we had other plans.

Saturday, after the Country Music Hall of Fame, we were looking for lunch and music.  Again, the sounds coming out of the open window drew us in.  Carlton Anderson was playing that afternoon and did a great job working the crowd and singing standards with his guitar!  Good luck in the music business.

We ordered 2 orders of Southwest eggrolls and 2 burgers with tots.  The bar mistress was attentive to our drink and food orders.  The Southwest egg rolls portions were generous and yummy.  The burgers were great and the tots were crispy & yummy.  Plus, a great food value in downtown Nashville.

name: 360 Burger
text:
Let me start by saying that I want to give 4 stars, but the inconsistency makes me give 3 stars. The last time I went, my fiance and I couldn't get well done burgers for the life of us. Granted, the owner bought a round of drinks for us for the inconvenience, but it sucks that we couldn't get a well done burger to save our lives, and they kept giving us cool, pre-cooked fries from a bowl of fries sitting on the counter. The owner had to go back back and tell them to drop fresh fries.

However this time I got a chicken sandwich and vegetables instead beef and french fries, so there was no issue with cold fries or medium well done burgers instead of well done burgers, as ordered. And I wish I could remember my servers name, but he was fantastic. I asked him to watch my plate and drink while I went to the restroom, and he and other servers literally set up a perimeter around my table. How hilariously good is that?!  I drink a lot of water, and my water glass was never empty for long. Also, if you go tried the bomb pop drink. It is fantastic and really reminds you of a bomb pop from the ice cream truck. The service today was great, but because I've had a couple of times where the service was mediocre and the food was average, I am reluctant to give it 4 or 5 stars.

If I go again and get the same service (I really wish I could remember his name) as I got today, I would not hesitate to upgrade the star rating.

name: 360 Burger
text:
This place has some great attributes - cool decor, friendly staff, craft brew, and garage doors.  Now on to the food - started with the onion rings which were tasty but not very hot.  With the speed in which they served our skeptical nature thought food lamps were in the mix - boo on that.

Burgers were very good - opted for the pretzel bun and sweet potato fries.  Fries were a bit soggy but tasty.  The aioli dipping sauce was great!

Overall it's a good addition to the neighborhood!!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Went for lunch based on yelp, it was terrible. Service took forever!! Food was blah. The only high point was the outdoor patio. Don't bother!!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We love you Dierks and your new place is really cool.  Music groups are awesome.  Unfortunately your bar tenders are horrible.  They are not well trained, service is extremely slow and it was not even that busy.  We all know money is made with serving booze.  You need more help and your folks need to be trained on how to make drinks more efficiently.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
We held a private event at the Listening Room Cafe and I feel compelled to write a superb review for their excellent and attentive service. 

When trying to find the right space in Nashville for our party, I stumbled across the Listening Room Cafe by pure chance but it was exactly the place I was looking for to host our event. The decoration is rustic interiors with brick background, wood beams and elevated ceilings. The sound system is amazing and they have a projector as well to use for tv or your own a-v hookups. There is also plenty of parking for your guests which is a HUGE plus in the downtown area considering there are parking lots at every turn and corner. The outdoor patio has a nice view of the Nashville skyline and is a great place to catch a drink on a cool evening. 

The Owner was a pleasure to work with and helped work through every little request I had. He even helped the kitchen prepare a custom menu with a authentic home recipe for our guests which came out incredible. We created a customized menu and bar menu for our guests and they were willing to accomodate all of my requests.  I especially enjoyed the local Yazoo beers on tap. I got to try a lot of the offerings on the menu and highly recommend the fried pickles, southern fried chicken, whiskey salmon, and broccoli casserole.  Our guests left the evening with an awesome and authentic Nashville experience and I even got on stage and played a song to close out the evening. 

If you are searching for a place with character, a place where you can support a local business owner with a vision and dream of the perfect singer-songwriter venue, and a place that just gushes with that local Nashville flavor then I highly recommend the listening room cafe. The sound system is awesome in here and really gives the musicians a platform to perform their trade. I look forward to coming back soon and enjoying the listening room cafe another time. Support Local!!!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Great museum dedicated to the Man in Black. TONS of memorabilia, neat interactive videos, recordings, and instruments. We used our Nashville city pass to get us in, and I definitely found it interesting & insightful. Only downfall was that it was incredibly crowded, but I guess that comes with the territory of going to a touristy spot on a weekend.

name: 360 Burger
text:
Quite impressed!  From the warm greeting at the door by Justin to the suggestions and menu explanations. Food was great -the sweet potato fries, awesome! 

Don't discount this Antioch diamond in the rough...can't wait for my next visit.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We got there and bought a drink then the band stopped playing.  45 minutes later we finally gave up on music and left.

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text: I love this place. I find myself continually coming back week after week just to see what's going on. The atmosphere fits the Midtown vibe and the staff is always friendly and attentive. During the week it's a great place to grab a happy hour beer and watch espn. On the weekends it's an all out dance party. The jock there, Darren B, plays some of the best tunes of every flavor in town. If you're looking for live music I hear Sundays are the best time to go. Reasonably priced drinks and fast, friendly service will have me visiting Blue Bar whenever I'm in midtown.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
If your a Johnny Cash fan this is the place to go! About two months ago I came to Nashville for the first time from New Jersey and HAD to come here and I ma so happy I did! It reached my expectations completely! From the memorabilia, the records, the music the whole experience was amazing! 

In general, it's a small museum but there is so much in there! I thought I knew a lot about Johnny Cash before going in there, but when I came out I learned so much more! So many great things to look at!  More than enough to keep you busy for an hour or two. And the best part is, your allowed to take all the pictures you want!  The price was also a great bargain and was easy to find!  

My boyfriend who is not even a Johnny Cash fan had a great time and actually wound up coming out of there a fan! This is not a place to miss when visiting Nashville!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: Great cruise, show was good.  We didn't do the dinner cruise, so we relaxed on the deck and took in the views.  One thing I would say is that the Opryland Hotel didn't have good signage for getting to the boarding area.  Massive hotel with bad signage.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: SO much fun!  I really enjoyed how the pianists alternated every so often - so you got a different style and personality mixed in.  They ALL were great. Interacted with the crowd, darn near played every song thrown their way. FUN bumper stickers.  Not as crowded as other places on Broadway - which was nice to be able to dance about a bit.

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: Great place!! Wonderful service!! Our very large group was well accommodated and we had a great experience! Thank you! We had a good time!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text:
A perfect Broadway gem!  We ducked into this place several times because we seemed to find the only empty seats each time we peeked in. 

The food was fast, fresh, and piping hot.  We didn't order anything elaborate, but it was yummy every time.

The entertainment was spot on and the guys playing were a good time as well as accomplished, polished performers.  Each staff member we encountered each day was friendly, welcoming and accommodating.  One day while we were sitting the bartender passed out bottle cozies, which I thought was a nice, hospitable touch.

Thanks for the many good times--we loved it!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: A must-do for any fan of the Man in Black. Seeing the relics of his life and work, both musical and religious, was awe-inspiring. Don't miss this if you're in Nashville! (One star off only because it's rather small.)

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: I thought this was a great venue.  All the musicians were talented, very impressed with them moving from piano to guitar to drums.  I thought the drinks were good, and reasonably priced.  Thoroughly enjoyed this visit.

name: Silver Dollar Saloon
text: One of my favorite bars in Nashville! The bartenders are so friendly and really know their drinks! Not to mention they have some of the best live music downtown!  I ALWAYS stop by Silver Dollar whenever I'm downtown!

name: 360 Burger
text: Was so excited to come and try this restaurant, as the grass fed beef is such a great seller. As I walked in it seemed there were only two servers for the full restaurant, so as you can imagine, the service lacked in parts. Im sure if they had one more server to help, I wouldn't have to say that, though.  I ordered the Cilantro avocado burger and was less than impressed. For the pricing they have, as well as the crowd, I was disappointed. Food took almost 40 minutes to come out and I was on my lunch break, so had to eat it out of a to go box. Might try it a 2nd time, who knows. Hopefully the next experience will be better.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great intimate setting to hear REAL music in Nashville. It was amazing! Minus one star because the food was just OK

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Had high expectations for this place since it is so well known! Came in on a Saturday morning around 11:15. It was pretty quiet, though the space is pretty large. Ordered brunch and some drinks. Drinks were good, brunch was a let down. French toast was mediocre. I got scrambled eggs, potatoes, and bacon, and was really disappointed. They first forgot my meal, then when it came the eggs were cold and just tasted flat out bad. The potatoes were a bit hard and under-cooked. Friends of mine ordered the 2 for 1 mimosa deal they had - each getting one. When the bill came they charged them both full price mimosas and then said they couldn't split the deal between seats - something they should've explained before. Luckily they fixed it, but it was a bit off-putting. The only plus was that there was live music. I would say maybe come in for drinks or a snack to check out the place and hear some music, but pass on the Brunch.

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: We both had a lot of fun here.  The food was fine, and the drinks were well priced.  We were there on a Sunday night and it wasn't busy, but the live music was incredible (Carlton Anderson (sp?)). Jalapeno burger was fine, and the philly cheesesteak was actually pretty good.  We both enjoyed our time here and LOVED the live music-- it really gives you the Nashville feel.

name: The Basement East
text: Like the other reviewer mentioned, this place used to be a neighborhood favorite for us. Great sandwiches, casual bar, nice outdoor deck, great beer selection. But to wait a month of brats/dogs for the "new menu", which is basically eggs all day (Brunch menu) and less-than-inspired bar food for the "late night menu" is a sad state of affairs indeed. I was ready to make this our Sunday NFL headquarters until this turn of events. I get there are some people who don't get out of bed to eat until after Noon, but seriously - egg burritos until 3pm Sat & Sun?! I had eggs at 7AM, thanks. I'm good. Fix me up that delightful Cuban pork sandwich and we're friends for life. Until then.......farewell my friend.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
I had a GREAT time here!  I am not a giant fan of country music but it was so fun to sit and listen to amazing talent perform their songs.  i was thoroughly entertained the entire show.

i did eat before I came because i heard the food wasnt the best.  I did order the fancy lemonade which was awesome and the fried pickles but I didnt love those as much mainly because they had a little too much kick for my palette.

Im not sure I would recommend coming for food but I 100% recommend coming for live music, definitely worth the price of admission :)

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
We loved this place!
I'll admit I was a bit hesitant because of comments about it only being 2 rooms of stuff. Yes, it is a smaller location than it obviously used to be, but it is a LOT of stuff crammed into the small space.
I dare say it's not enough space. But, it's obvious watching The Hurt video that it used to be in a larger space.

If you're into music at all it's a great museum. If you're into Johnny Cash, it's a must-see!!

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
Been going to the Bang since they opened the first one in St. Louis. After only a half hour or so, the impression one gets is that these musicians know most every song composed from the past two centuries.  Their competence while doing the standard piano bar setup and moving to the small band format is entertaining to watch. They are all wonderful singers to boot. They work very hard to try and get to every request made each night and their patter between tunes is quite funny. 
The food is quite good. The Rock 'n Roll Salad is a favorite of mine along with the pulled pork sandwich.  Being a non-drinker, I'm not one to pass judgment on the beers and what seems to be a well stocked selection of mixed drinks. I know Coca Cola owns Middle Tennessee, but a cold Pepsi would better suit my taste. 
The concept of the piano bar is not new and, nationally, there are other brands out there. However, I find The Big Bang Bar to be one of the good ones whose staff really does take care that a good time is had by all.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
I wasn't a massive country music fan, but I always did like Johnny Cash when I heard his music.  Given that I was in Nashville, walked by the museum several times, and saw ads for it everywhere, I decided to be a tourist and check it out.  The museum has a cafe and gift shop in front.  The gift shop is overpriced however the gear is unique and cool, which makes it somewhat worth it (I grabbed a tank top).  Museum admission is similiarly pricey at $16--especially given the total size of all exhibits--however as even a casual fan I found it worth it.

While the space is limited, it's packed with worthwhile exhibits and content.  From the recordings strewn through the space, the chair from the "Hurt" music video, dozens of costumes and a butt-load of history, there is plenty to engage with.  And what's there is worth engaging with.  Johnny Cash had a fascinating life which, while not always rosy, was very well lived.  The care put into this tiny museum shows and can easily be appreciated.  You can zip through the place in 15 minutes if you wish, but instead you'll probably find yourself spending closer to an hour.

I find myself listening to Johnny Cash a lot more nowadays.  Unless you're diehard against country (and if you are, why are you in Nashville), given this a visit if you're in town.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I needed to go to the potty. No line in the men's so I went with it. Literally got chased out by an employee (a tiny little "man")  for using a restroom with no line. He pounded on the door. Not because there was a line, but because he could. I'd avoid this place when there are several other places to go where you will be treated more kindly.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This place was amazing. If you love Johnny Cash you will enjoy this place. We had so much fun and enjoyed glimpsing into his life and things and learning new facts about him. The pictures at the end where so fun and cute enough to put up in the house. I would go back again.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Very neat to see the history of his life through time:  well put together museum.  I would make this a must see while visiting Nashville.

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: The band is the only thing I enjoyed at this place. The place smelled of smoke. The bathroom was gross and we stopped a drunk leaving the bar that was wanting to drive home. Went to get assistance from bartender for cab for him and was surprised by their lack of help in detaining this guy or getting him a ride. Can't they be held liable if something were to happen?

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This place is a must for any Johnny Cash fan. I picked up a magnet sun records for our fridge. Lots of great history and things owned my the man in black and June. Well worth the price of admission. Gift shop was nice but a little spendy.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: We started off having a great night until the bouncer kicked us out without a reason.  We were there with all of my aunts and uncles and just settled a $400+ tab.  I asked for the manager and he was this dopey geeky little guy that didn't care.  We let them know we also had civil servants with us and he was completely ignorant.  There are so many bars on the strip that do not have this $6/person cover.  Save your time/$6 and dignity and find yourself a real Nashville country bar.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Awesome place to hear new music, and the food is great. Song Suffragette shows on Mondays are really cool.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Great place to see higher quality music in nashville. Music started at 7pm on Friday with three singer songwriters. One had a big hit song for rascal flatts so this was real talent. Good sound quality. It is a full restaurant with small tables surrounding the stage.  The food is decent.  I suggest the fried pickles.  They have a nice selection of sandwhiches and a few entrees. The greenbeans that i had on the side were exceptional. Sangria was awesome but the music was awesome!  Second band had so much energy and had a maroon 5 vibe. This is a great place if you want great music, solid food, and an actual table while you listen.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Loved the atmosphere and the musicians. So nice to see how people migrate to this town for their love of singing and songwriting. Fun place for an evening in Nashville and less touristic than many other places in town

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: This place is not my scene but the bar itself is a pretty innovative and cool idea. I will give them 4 stars for coming up with a new fresh cool idea. I would recommend trying the place out to see if its your scene, this place is a lot different than a lot of other bars in Nashville and across the US.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: This was a great place to hear some up and coming artists, grab an inexpensive drink, and hang out! The food options looked tempting but we had already eaten, so I can't speak to that. Our experience was positive, though!

name: Silver Dollar Saloon
text: Nice place, good music, and they have Miller Lite. Someone just told me I didn't need to drive this far south from Chicago for a miller lite.... Who knew?!

name: 360 Burger
text:
Interesting menu.  Not at all what i expected.

Visited mid afternoon on a Saturday. Good crowd, but not packed out.  Even so, it took a good 15 minutes for server to take our order and then another 20 minutes or so to get it to the table.

Our server was pleasant, but obviously overextended.  Looking around, i think she was the only one working.

I might try one more time, but if experuence is not better, this one goes off my list.

name: The Basement East
text: Awesome venue for live music. Big enough to fit a good size crowd but small enough that it still feels intimate.  Also I was very pleased that there was a vegan option on their food menu on the pub side.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: It was very interesting to see different parts of Johnny Cash's life in the museum. There is a lot to see, hear, and experience. The only downside is that the museum itself was jam packed with people so I couldn't take my time reading everything, and it was pretty pricey to go in to the museum itself.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Found my new hang out spot in lower Broadway!! Came here with an open mind & had the BEST experience!! A group of friends & I came New Year's Eve to get table service & I had the best customer service provided, awesome energy & music and drinks. Will be back to try some of the food i saw some good feedbacks on

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: I loved it! Me and my husband went for drinks! They had live bands! It was awesome! The talent was great!  This place was so cool! Prices for drinks were very reasonable! I definitely recommend this place!  It was awesome! The place was packed! It's definitely something to experience!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I found this place by internet search, and checked on yelp, seems the feedback are quite positive.. so purchased the tickets on line.. it's inexpensive.. we went there from walking from broadway, it's quite some walk, the venue is pretty sizable, and on a Tuesday evening, we have 4 artist joined.. they sing one by one, and each of them will also introduce their song and how they wrote it.  So it's quite good if u are open to some young artist.. the food is ok.. my chicken breast is quite dry and the fried Brussels spout is pretty good, i don't think i can make it myself. The hummus is good too.. they also gave me 50% off on my hummus with yelp check in.. my husband ordered cobb salad with their chili soup.. he seems very happy with the performance and food as he gives a 25% tip!! That's a little tricky though, as the 25% is the first tip choice right after no tip, next is 20%, 15%.. haha..

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Came here for a bachelorette and it was lively. The drinks were not expensive. The shots came in a lighted small glasses

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text:
I'd like to comment on my experience here but our entire party of 5 was not granted entrance at the door due to us having one African American gentleman with us. The door man's reason was discriminatory, racist and hypocritical as every white man that walked in past us was dressed identically. I'm sure the establishment is successful but the door man's actions & excuse is a poor reflection of management and sadly, a reflection of his close-minded self. 

You know what they say, when you have a good experience, you'll share it with one or two people. When you come across a bad experience, you'll share with a multitude of people. Needless to say, we won't be returning.

name: General Jackson Showboat
text:
Expensive, cheesy, not many amenities. It gets hot here in Nashville, you'd think there'd at least be water for people paying $60 a ticket. You won't be in the a/c until you're in the dining room. 

Service on the deck for drinks was pretty spotty. A beer is $14. Food inside was okay (beans, Mac n cheese, bbq were good). 

The show was definitely a show! I already knew going in it wouldn't be my favorite music (this was all for my visiting family) but man I have to say I would appreciate it if the ladies on stage would wear a bit more clothing. Honestly, they're on an elevated stage, cleavage out, short dresses and twirling, shaking their butts. I just felt like it was completely inappropriate. I would not take anyone else here. 

More a/c options and water for guests would make this a lot more enjoyable.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Great food- had filet cooked to perfection! Service was great and the music was awesome! Seen James Dean and Rachel(?) 7/22/19 they both had a lot of talent!!

name: 360 Burger
text:
With so much word around about this place I tried it out for the first time tonight. I had a simple bacon cheeseburger with habanero cheese along with sweet potato fries. The burger was very good but pretty greasy, yes I understand a burger is supposed to be greasy but this was bun being soggy from the grease. The mood from the room was quite chill and relaxing., beer prices are a bit expensive for this type of setting, my overall rating for this place was very good. Will I be back? Yes 
Would I recommend this place? Yes 
I read reviews about the service not being upto par, I sat at the bar so service reviewing is out on this one. I'd give it at least 3.5 out of 5. I'll be back to add more when I eat here again.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Very interesting. Lots of artifacts. Believe it's a little high priced. Would recommend if you like Johnny Cash

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: My friends and I decided to stop in Whiskey Row for New Years Eve before we met up with the rest of our group downtown, and we had so much fun that we just made everyone come meet us there!!! The staff was so friendly and welcoming, and seemed to be having just as much fun as the people actually there to party! There were groups that rented out VIP booths and the girls taking care of those tables had light wands and kegs and bottles and were coming out on shoulders and dancing on tables.. I felt like I was in a Vegas club!!! But of course, with the perfect Nashville twist on it. I 10000% recommend Whiskey Row! We are already looking into booking a table for my birthday! Y'all check it out!

name: General Jackson Showboat
text: We did the Dinner Cruise last night.   The entertainment was great and the meal was good.   On the downside the waiter was rude.  He yelled in my ear several times when addressing the table, no one at the table could understand what he was staying because of his accent, he kept reaching across the table to refill water glasses, he never brought additional dinner rolls and he took forever to bring coffee for the other guest. We were seated at table 26

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: My wife and I enjoyed this place both for the music by John Riggins and company as well as the food.  Harold

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I went to To Dierks Whiskey row Nashville, on New Years Eve, and I have to say, hands down, one of the best times I've had while visiting Nashville! There was no other place like this on broadway. Every floor had its own unique vibe. My Favorite floor was the second floor, where Whiskey row offered Flight service. The presentations of the flight service coming out to my table was unbelievable and the energy was outrageous. Everyone, from the staff, to the patrons, throughly was enjoying themselves. I was extremely impressed with everything this establishment had to offer. I can't wait to be back and I will be back !

name: 360 Burger
text:
Great food good local beers (FAT BOTTOM BREWERY FTW!)
they need a better display of beer menu (FREE MARKETING TIP) 

sometimes the music is better than others but its always a pleasure to be there

name: 360 Burger
text: Super friendly and quick service. Delicious, and fresh, oysters. Creative burger options which are also delicious, and yummy cocktails. I would like better happy hour specials, but still highly recommend.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: My friend and I had a great time tonight at the New Year's Eve opening in Nashville. The staff was friendly and welcoming. The bartenders kept the drinks flowing, and the wait staff did a great job. We were especially impressed with Nicole. She was friendly, personable, and took a moment to pose for a picture with us. The security staff had their hands full with all of the "amateurs" out on New Year's Eve, but from what I saw, they handled each incident professionally. The band's sound on the first floor was well mixed and balanced throughout the space. With their prime corner location I'm sure that Whiskey Row will quickly become a popular choice among the many options on Lower Broadway.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Wow!  The pork steaks were off the charts.  Not going to find these anywhere in TN or any states around.  I was floored to find them as I grew up eating these in Illinois and have not seen them on a menu since moving to TN three years ago.

We have some friends in town and took them on "Broadway" last night.  They were disappointed that everything was covers and loud and packed.  We brought them to the "Room", and they are in love with Nashville!

a hidden gem in this town.  love the Bluebird but this is today's place to be.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: This was a fun spot for soccer and live music. The service was five stars.  The drinks were excellent. My 3 stars is because the food wasn't super.  Drink and sing but eat elsewhere.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Super cool place - but definitely more of a destination for cocktails. The menu isn't too small but they were sold out of the first 2 things I wanted to order. We went to the 8:30 show and the artists were awesome and other patrons were lovely (the tables seat 4 so if you're a party of 2 you may be paired with new faces!). Check in was a bit disorganized and the valet line was super long, so get there early and Uber if you can! Definitely would return but would get dinner somewhere else before & just get drinks at the show

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Really liked this place. Brought the in laws here when they came to visit.  There's a lot more to Johnny Cash than what I thought I knew.  Was pretty crowded, that's the only negative.

name: Rack Room Blue Bar
text: It is a small little back bar. But it is great place to hang out. We only stayed for a little bit but the bartender was very nice. I wouldn't have even knew if this was in the back if my friend didn't know. It is in the back of the bar by the bathrooms. Cheap fireball shots too!

name: 360 Burger
text: Great burger!! Owner was extremely nice. Good music and a atmosphere that just yells family. We'll be back.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Male bartender from 11-2pm was amazing.  He served so many people without a hiccup.  Thank you for your attention to everyone's needs and your speed.  
Dierk's, he is definitely a keeper.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Went on Feb13, where Valentine's day special 3-course meal was the only option for dining.

Music and the ticket fee were fine - the atmosphere reminded me of the times in American college, but seriously the food was so bad that I wouldn't have come if it weren't for the lack of information.

For starter, figs were burnt. For the main, meat were burnt. For the dessert, they were out of sorbet making me doubt when they started this whole event - and then the 'flourless chocolate cake' turned out to be not flourless at all. Lastly - I don't know why - but the wine glasses smelled of some unpleasant odor that I thought of presenting deodorant. This was at 65 per each person.

I mean, it was for experience but not the best one. I wouldn't give a star to be fair. Needs imminent improvement.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: I couldn't even walk in the music was soooo load not enjoyable...and I like my music turned up

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Love Whiskey Row! Nashville needed something like this. Definitely the new hot spot. BILL BUTLER is the MVP. Fav bartender!! They play a variety of hits from every genre. Great energy and upbeat atmosphere. The staff is very professional and always accommodating. We don't usually have to wait long for drinks. Bartenders are on top of their game and make quality drinks. Check it out!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: First, I want to commend Greg the chef for being so kind to his customers. I emailed Greg before coming here because I have a fish allergy. Greg not only assured me he would take care of me through email, but he also came out to our table to make me feel even more comfortable. The Mac and cheese was AMAZING, and my dad loved his smoked wings too. This place is SO awesome

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I had such high expectations for this place. And it met every single one. The architecture of the building is amazing. The guitar chandelier, the lights, the space itself. The food is phenomenal. A wide variety of tastes and their brunch on the weekends is my FAVORITE. The bartenders are fast, friendly and aided to their customers needs. Live music is always very involved with the crowd and the DJ (night time) is probably one of the best I've ever heard. Overall, it's not like most bars on broadway. You can tell this place is constructed and run by a FAMILY, and everyone works together well to meet the needs of their customers. I highly recommend this to be a place to visit when coming to Nashville.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: Every time I come here I have a GREAT time! The service is great and the drinks are always strong! It's upstairs above another bar so it's kind of hard to fine. Other than that it's a great place to relax, listen to some music, and have some good drinks!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
I was in Nashville for work and caught a Titans game (SO fun). I followed the crowds over a bridge back to downtown Nashville on Broadway in search of dinner and drinks. I found no food, but I did find Dierks. Now I'm not a huge country fan, but I have a friend who loves Dierks Bentley so after a short wait in a line, I was in. The downstairs was crowded, but still managable to move. The bar was out of a lot of basic domestic beers so I settled for a Music City beer the waitress recommended. I stood nearby and listened to a great cover band, but found it really hard to meet or get to talk to anyone. I moved around, found a few different spots, but just couldn't blend in with the vibe. I went to the bar to get another drink and the bartenders were slammed. It just wasn't happening.

I'd give it another try on maybe a slower night, but all in all just not my favorite.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: Awesome place Pretty cool bar,  just opened and they are still working out on  things

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: We had so much fun here! The band was great! I'd give it five stars except that our waitress kept disappearing. We had the artichoke appetizer and drinks.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
This is a must see/do whilst in Nashville. There is nothing like this where I'm from and to my knowledge, anywhere else though I could be wrong.

Beers are cheap, they do food too. The vibe is very, very cool but not too cool for school. You can sit back, drink your Bud Lime and just chill into the atmosphere;

Two guys playing piano opposite each other, accompanied by a band. Are they any good? Does Dolly Parton have big boobs?! Yes, they're good. In fact, they're great. Talented and skilled musicians who've got their job down pat. You want live music in Nashville? You've got it. A mix of tunes from all genres, they'll give anything a go - if you request and tip them.

Remember, they're starving musicians and have seven kids to feed at home. If you're generous with them, they'll play anything... But seriously, this is their bread and butter and if you don't tip you're an ass. Don't be p*ssed if they don't know the whole song, it's impossible to know every song. They may know another song by that artist. Whichever the case, they'll make it fun and have a laugh about it. The higher the tip, the sooner your song gets played. $20 gets yours on next. I wish we'd been able to tip more. We couldn't be too frivolous with our cash unfortunately.

The banter between the band and sometimes bartender who gets up to sing a few is brilliant; funny, slick, cheeky. So you get a real mix of entertainment. 

As I said, drop by for a bottle of Bud or two and see for yourself. We spend about three hours there because we couldn't bring ourselves to leave wondering what they were going to play next. Awesome.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Not a bad place to have a drink and listen to music.  Their hand crafted signature drinks were very good. Pricey but typical pricing for the area. I just don't get why on the main floor do they only have one unisex bathroom. Bad planning.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: Nice place.  Pretty cool artifacts.  Truly enjoyed that he married his first wife in San Antonio TX.

name: 360 Burger
text: Staff very friendly and the food was good at first. My medium burger was placed on my friends well done burger. Fries were not cooked fully. Food tasted amazing but you can't be a burger place and mix up burgers. The server when told got defensive and blamed the kitchen and nothing was done about the check. My entire order was wrong and I paid for everything fully. This place needs to get at least the service right. Customers should pay for a complete messed up order.

name: The Basement East
text:
I thought I'd caught a show here before until I arrived the other night (turns out I was thinking of the East Room). 
So, I'd wondered how 5 full bands would pull off a set in a basement setting (which is what the above mentioned venue really is and that's not a knock either, seen some cool music there) only to realize this is a full size (for up to 400 anyway) modern music venue. Great affordable beers and shots, clean bathrooms, great sound system. Cool security (thanks for letting me put my merch in my car so I could thorougly enjoy the pit), good (and fast) bartenders. 
And...venue owners who know how you are supposed to behave at a metal show. Thanks for letting us rip the pit the way the show intends.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: I came to Nashville for a conference and snuck away for a dinner one night. This was a great find. There was a cover charge but I thought the musical entertainment was worth it. I think the most memorable part of this restaurant is the exposed brick interior, live music, friendly staff, and the mac & cheese. I'd recommend others to go if they're in town.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Food was good. Staff was attentive. Music was great. We came on a Monday night and heard the song suffragettes. Awesome singer/songwriters. Loved it.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
The performance was amazing!!! I'm not a country music person but these guys were so good I may even download a couple of their songs. 
The only reason 4 out of 5 stars was service. It was very slow. We waited over an hour for food and had empty drinks a majority of the evening. Our server was mia and would come back reeking of cigarette smoke. But I would still go back!

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: They don't validate parking so you have to pay separately for that. Theres a lot in the back of the building with meter parking. Its a cool little trip down history and memory lane. A must do if youre a Cash fan

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text:
Unfortunately, I have to write a negative review on Yelp for the first time, but this review is warranted. I would first like to respond to John's review below from 9 days ago, and mention that this security worker is still employed at this establishment as of 2 days ago, and he was absolutely rude and unprofessional. 

However, as it was impossible to make it upstairs on a Saturday night during the summer in Nashville, my friend and I decided to give Dierks another try yesterday 7/14. We met up with a large group of girls we know from school and were having a grand time on the dance floor. About 30 minutes into our groove, a female approached my friend and told her that an "executive" of the bar wanted us to come join them and dance on the bar at their VIP booth because he thought we were "attractive." Thus, we joined them at the booth, and began dancing along the top of the booth, as is customary, or so it seemed. 

Unfortunately, about an hour and a half in, our experience took a turn. Now, I will fully admit that I am responsible for my actions, however I do not feel what ensued was warranted. I had stepped off of the bar/booth for a bit to use the restroom, meander, etc. During this time, my friend and I got separated. I was standing near the outside of the booth, and made the poor choice of standing on top of the outside of the same booth/rail we were invited to, in order to get a better view of the dance floor to try to find my friend. A security gentleman, repeatedly tapping my waist, not only told me to get down, but then abruptly and rudely said to me "Get out. I can either ask you to leave nicely or I can throw you out" when all the while I was completely cooperative, most likely due to the shock of not even receiving a warning, but immediately being kicked out. All I was saying to him was I am waiting for my friend, who was right behind him. 

Now, again, I was completely at fault for standing on the outside of the booth, however, it was the same booth that we had been invited over to by an "executive" to dance. In addition, earlier in the night, a different security personnel had nicely told me that I cannot request a song from the DJ, and that was that; I did not try to approach the DJ again. I have been to many other establishments in Nashville and throughout the world, and never have I ever been so disrespected and made out to seem like a degenerate. I was at a bar in Nashville, so naturally I was drunk, however, I was by no means trashed or "sloppy" or unruly. 

In addition, our friend from school, whom we met up with there, had a similar security horror story the night prior. She had tried to get into Dierks with 13 other girls she traveled to Nashville with, and for whatever reason, a security guy refused to let her in. Only her. Leaving her alone on the street. Fortunately, we were on broadway so she didn't have to be alone. And again, she was drunk, but fully composed. No stumbling, vomiting or anything else to that effect. 

When the previous reviews stated that this bar is sexist, I actually agree. Very rarely do I ever call a person or establishment sexist. If an owner or manager does not reach out to me via Yelp, I will be contacting someone via phone or email on the website. Moreover, I am curious to find out what the Better Business Bureau will think of this repeated behavior in your establishment, based on my multiple first-hand experiences, and SEVERAL of these reviews. Fellow Yelpers, take your business and time to Luke's instead, you will be treated humanely and have a better time, anyway.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great time!!! Friendly staff and great music.   Well decorated!   Loved hanging out here.

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text:
Wow what a fitting tribute to one of the best in the business.

This museum is jam packed with so much stuff from the life and career of Johnny Cash. But not so much that it's too much.

A very well organized museum with displays from his earliest years until his death.

Personal belongings, photos, letters, records and so much more to see and explore.

name: The Basement East
text: That sushi appetizer... What great dreams are made of... Like nothing I've ever had.  They have Deep Eddy Grapefuit vodka too!  (Nachos are mediocre, sadly.)

name: Johnny Cash Museum
text: This was my dream! This place is awesome they have clothes, furniture, records, hand written notes!! They have a picture guy you can get your photo with Johnny next to you. It was great!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: We had lunch here today. Great food, friendly staff and amazing music. A must see if you're visiting Nashville

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: This is my favorite night life spot in Nashville! The talent these guys have is unbelievable; I don't know how they do it! It's a spot where you can (usually) sit down, have some great drinks, and be thoroughly entertained all night. The bar staff is great and the entertainers are top notch. I read a few reviews that lowered their rating because there's a cover...it's $6.00, and it's 100% worth it in my opinion! Plus, I just saw that if you check in on Yelp you get a $2.00 discount! I wish I'd known that before this weekend; we went both Friday and Saturday. We couldn't get enough!

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: Johns the man behind the bar! Good food and great drinks at reasonable prices! Worth the stop for great live music and open late with a late kitchen. 10/10 recommend.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text:
Well, I'll start by saying I loath leaving bad reviews. But this is a case that it is called for. 

First off, they charge cover - which is fine ($6 on a Saturday night) but they obviously pick and choose who they charge. My friends were split up upon entrance. Half charged, half were not. Just seems a bit shady. 

Second, the drinks were fine. We had a lovely bartender who promptly served us and was super friendly. I wish I remembered her name because she deserves 5 stars. 

However, one of the guys on the piano was so utterly rude to a member of my party. I was honestly appalled. 

They take requests, so we wrote our song request and put a tip on stage. At one point there was a lull in music and my friend shouted out to the guy "play back that a** up! (Our song choice) in a friendly manner. They had just been playing mania rap songs. And then all of a sudden the piano man decided to snap. He shouted "listen drunk girl I'm not playing that song I have a bachelors degree in music I'm not playing that sh!t" while he obviously played the piano and sang the song afterward in an aggressive and angry way. Even the security guard standing near him seemed offended for us. The crowd got a bit silent and everyone looked around at each other in a "what the heck just happened manner". We got our tip back and left soon after. 

Needless to say I will never return to this establishment and I hope their "artists" who are so proud of their collegiate achievements find a better job than performing for a plethora of bachelorette party's and drunk co-eds. He may have a bachelors degree but Juvenile had a chart-topping single so, I would say one is doing better than the other.

name: Music City Bar and Grill
text: Great drink prices. Music was awesome. We didn't eat but didn't come to eat. Great place to unwind. Highly recommend if you're looking for laid back place to have a good time and listen to good ol' country music.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: The most incredible music venue I've been too! The musicians were super entertaining and very talented. Only bad review was that the server waited to check on us for long periods at a time, so we would need something or run out of water and then have to wait till he was out again. Then the food itself wasn't horrible, but wasn't great either.. I got the Cranberry walnut salad and it was pretty good but the chicken tenders my friend got not-so-good. Other than that, there was free valet parking, the venue was clean, and the music was INCREDIBLE!

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Worst experience , great music.  My wife and I are here for a convention and had an hour in a half to go find lunch.  My wife ordered a Kale and Quinoa salad and I a Burger with no bun on top of lettuce.  We waited about 35-40 minutes for our food and when it arrived the salad had no Kale, very little ingredients and the burger was one of those frozen looking Costco patties and it was ice cold.  The waitress brought the manager over and he assured they'd remake them etc.  My wife's salad came out almost immediately but still not what she remembered since she had ordered the same thing last year.  I however waited and waited and even 20 minutes after my wife had finished.  Almost 40 minutes after receiving our bad food, I still had no burger.  By this time we were already late for our convention and we had to leave and I ended up with no meal.  Incredible how poor the service and quality of food are.  Save your money and go somewhere else.  The music however was great.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: All the way out here from California and we love this place. The band was amazing, drinks great and service was excellent. We have been here in Nashville 2 days and have visited this bar more than 5 times! Great experience and will always come back!! If you are looking to experience Nashville this place is a must visit!!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
Stopped in while friends we in town. We really enjoyed the plane and the bands rocked. We didn't try any food but we will definitely come back to try it out. 
 The staff was super nice and fun as well.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Had so much fun here!   Hollee is amazing.  Made us feel more welcome than anywhere on Broadway.  Service second to none on the rooftop!

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text:
Great Atmosphere!! Good food!  We stopped in to checkout Nashville we on our way across the country of watching Angela Marie & Donny Lee!! 
Could not have asked for a better experience!! Kid Rock's Honky Tonk Kicks Ass!!

name: Losers Bar & Grill -Downtown
text: This is a great place when you want to get off of busy Broadway. The beer was cold and the selection was great. Service was good at the bar, spotty from the waitress. Food also good, we split several apps, which were all to our liking. The entertainment was also good. A very homy, neighborhood bar kind of place.

name: Big Bang - Dueling Piano Bar
text: This was by far the most fun and interactive thing we did while in Nashville.  The musicians were absolutely amazing.  They were very talented and we were amazed by the huge variety of songs they knew.  I would recommend this bar to absolutely anyone visiting Nashville.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Unfortunately, this place missed the mark.  The talent of the singers/songwriters was probably great, however when in the private area you are not provided access to enjoy them.   You are provided with a nice credit card fee for choosing the establishment for your group.  We had to meet a minimum, which would be understandable- other than the fact the food quality does not come anywhere close to the tab that needed to be achieved.    Nashville has so much to offer, I definitely won't add this to my list on future visits.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: Great music. Service is slow- but so is all the other restaurants on the row. We did not eat here- but had a few beers.

name: Listening Room Cafe
text:
Fantastic idea, poorly executed.
Hot beer, cold food. They have a disclaimer about running out of food but they ran out of fries, chili, sent us a brisket end sandwich that was hard as a rock, then greasy ends of the brisket as "replacement". 
We were the last table - a curtain between us and where they throw dirty dishes so we not only listened to music, but also the sound of silverware dropping and plates stacking and a dropped glass on the floor. 
We were told by the manger we were comped for dinner since we were from out of town (in lieu of a rain check for the next time) but were still asked to pay a full bill from the server. 
Even if everything had gone smoothly,  forget enjoying the last set. The wait staff is everywhere in the way with their little computers to make sure you pay bc that was "the best and only time to do it".  
This place is a great idea... in theory. We won't be back and I suggest you don't waste your money.

name: The Basement East
text: Basement East did us dirty. I know Tennessee is strict on IDs but seriously... a passport and social security card? They kicked my fiancé out who is 28 because I bought him a beer... he had his ID stolen last week. Tough break. Missed a great band which we already bought tickets for. Wouldn't of been so bad if we were treated kindly.

name: Kid Rock's Big Honky Tonk and Rock n' Roll Steakhouse
text: The sound system in the place is amazing!  Big beautiful place with a great view of the strip.  Good to make a home base for meeting people.  I went here a few times while visiting the strip.  Drink prices were average for the area.  Good place to watch bands play, on any floor.  I recommend to at least stop by if your in the area.

name: Dierks Bentley's Whiskey Row
text: I come to Nashville often and after spending NYE here (and lunch the next day) I can say that I will DEFINTELY be back each trip! Best spot on broadway with the highest rooftop!

name: Listening Room Cafe
text: Go for the music, not necessarily for the food.
